The Jesuit order was suppressed in 1773 under pressure from the Catholic powers. Berthier's French troops entered in February 1798 and proclaimed a Roman Republic; Pius VI died in exile in France, and Neapolitan arms restored Pius VII in 1800. French troops returned in 1808 and absorbed Rome into Napoleon's empire, carrying off its treasures and holding the pope in France until his return in 1814; the Congress of Vienna confirmed the restored Papal States.
zh:
罗马跨在台伯河畔的七丘之上。它曾是罗马帝国的都城，哥特战争后缩成一座在废墟间谋生的小镇；756年起由教皇治理，作为教宗国的驻地，科隆纳和奥尔西尼等贵族家族据守塔楼互相攻杀。1300年的首次禧年招来约两百万朝圣者，但1309年教廷迁往阿维尼翁，随后的西方大分裂使罗马荒废于派系仇杀。1418年康斯坦茨公会议结束分裂，出身科隆纳家族的玛定五世把教廷带回罗马。1444年，恩仁四世治下的罗马仍是一座废墟、葡萄园与朝圣者并存的小城，人口或仅两万，却重新成为教廷的稳定驻地。

1447年当选的尼各老五世创办梵蒂冈图书馆，历任教皇着手重修城墙、教堂和街道。儒略二世和良十世时代，伯拉孟特动工兴建新圣彼得大教堂，米开朗基罗绘制西斯廷教堂天顶画，拉斐尔为教廷套房绘制湿壁画；出资者有阿戈斯蒂诺·基吉这样的银行家；工程的耗费和教皇的腐败也是激起宗教改革的原因之一。1527年5月6日，查理五世麾下欠饷的德意志雇佣步兵攻破罗马，教皇克雷芒七世在瑞士卫队拼死掩护下逃入圣天使堡，被拘到赎金付清才脱身。劫掠、瘟疫和逃亡使罗马人口从约5.5万降到1万，文艺复兴的黄金时代戛然而止。

1545年特伦托公会议开幕后，罗马成为天主教改革的大本营，罗马宗教裁判所在此审判焦尔达诺·布鲁诺，并于1600年在鲜花广场将他处以火刑。思道五世在1585至1590年间开辟新路、修复输水道，新圣彼得大教堂1626年祝圣，贝尔尼尼和波洛米尼则用喷泉和立面塑造了巴洛克的罗马。1773年，耶稣会在各天主教强国压力下被取缔。1798年2月，贝尔蒂埃率法军入城，宣布成立罗马共和国；庇护六世死于法国流放地，1800年那不勒斯出兵帮助庇护七世复位。1808年法军再至，罗马被并入拿破仑的帝国，珍藏遭劫，教皇本人被拘在法国，直到1814年返回；维也纳会议确认了重建的教宗国。

en:
Ancona occupies two hills on a promontory of the Adriatic's western shore, where Greek exiles from Syracuse founded a town around 387 BC; its harbour, the nearest to Dalmatia, was the finest on that coast. Trajan enlarged it with his architect Apollodorus of Damascus, and the marble arch raised in his honour in 115 stands at the head of the quay. Above the town the cathedral of San Ciriaco crowns the Guasco hill, a grey-stone Greek-cross church on the site of the Greek acropolis, completed at the end of the twelfth century. From the eleventh century Ancona was a maritime republic ruled by six Elders, coining its own agontano and usually allied with Ragusa and Constantinople against Venice, which grudged it a rival in the Adriatic. An imperial army failed to starve the town out in the siege of 1173, remembered for the widow Stamira, who sallied from the walls and set fire to a siege engine; the Malatesta were the city's only signori and held it only from 1348 to 1383. In 1444 the oligarchic city, under papal suzerainty, lived by the Levant trade; its most famous son was Cyriac of Ancona, a navigator and antiquarian who travelled the eastern Mediterranean recording its monuments.

Ancona kept its self-government until 1532, when papal troops issued from the citadel Pope Clement VII had been allowed to build against a Turkish threat and occupied the city; Antonio da Sangallo the Younger's five-bastioned fortress then commanded town and harbour. A papal safe-conduct drew Greek, Turkish, Jewish and Iberian merchants, and Ancona became the busiest port of the Papal States. Under Paul IV twenty-six Portuguese Sephardim who refused baptism were hanged and their bodies burned in 1556, and later, when the Papal States expelled its Jews, Ancona was one of only three cities where they might remain. In 1732 Pope Clement XII made it a free port and set Luigi Vanvitelli to rebuild the harbour; the pentagonal Lazzaretto rose on an artificial island. French troops set up the Anconine Republic in 1797, Napoleon took the city into his Kingdom of Italy in 1808, and an Anglo-Austrian siege in 1815 returned it to the popes.
zh:
安科纳建在亚得里亚海西岸一处难得的海岬上，城区占着两座山丘；约公元前387年，叙拉古的希腊流亡者在此建城。这里的港口是意大利一侧距达尔马提亚最近的港口，也是西岸最好的天然良港。图拉真命建筑师大马士革的阿波罗多罗斯扩建港务，115年为纪念他而建的大理石凯旋门就立在码头尽头。城上的瓜斯科山顶立着圣奇里亚科主教座堂，这座灰色石材的希腊十字式教堂建在希腊卫城旧址上，12世纪末完工。11世纪起，安科纳成为由六名元老治理的海上共和国，铸造自己的阿贡塔诺银币，通常与拉古萨和君士坦丁堡结盟，共同对抗把它视作对手的威尼斯。1173年帝国大军久围不克，寡妇斯塔米拉冲出城防火烧攻城器械，事迹因此传世；马拉泰斯塔家族是这里唯一的领主，统治期只有1348至1383年。1444年的安科纳是寡头执政的城市，名义上臣属教宗，靠黎凡特贸易为生；航海家兼古迹学者安科纳的基里亚科是本地人，他遍历东地中海，把沿途古迹记录下来。

安科纳的自治维持到1532年：教宗克雷芒七世先以防备土耳其人为由获准修建城堡，这年教宗军队从堡中涌出占领全城，小安东尼奥·达·桑加洛设计的五棱要塞就此扼住城市与港口。教廷颁发通行证，招徕希腊、土耳其、犹太和伊比利亚商人定居，安科纳成为教宗国最繁忙的港口。1556年，二十六名拒绝改宗的葡萄牙塞法迪犹太人在保禄四世治下被处绞刑后焚尸；后来教宗国驱逐犹太人时，安科纳仍是仅有的三个允许他们居留的城市之一。1732年，克雷芒十二世将此辟为自由港，命路易吉·万维泰利改建港口，他设计的五角形检疫站建在人工岛上。1797年法军到来，成立安科纳共和国，1808年拿破仑把它并入意大利王国，1815年英奥联军围城，城市重归教宗。

en:
L'Aquila crowns a high shelf of the Abruzzi Apennines, facing the Papal States across the mountains. Frederick II of Hohenstaufen founded it as a royal town, gathering ninety-nine mountain villages into one walled settlement; each mother-village kept its own borough, and the Fountain of Ninety-nine Spouts, built in 1272 with jets along three walls, records the union. Manfred destroyed the young town and the Angevins rebuilt it, closing the walls early in the fourteenth century, and L'Aquila grew into the second city of the Kingdom of Naples. Its wealth came from the saffron fields of the Aterno valley and transhumant flocks moving between the high pastures and the Florence road. In 1294 the hermit Pietro da Morrone was crowned Pope Celestine V in Santa Maria di Collemaggio and proclaimed the Perdonanza indulgence there, the rite from which the papal Jubilee developed. After a thirteen-month siege by the condottiere Braccio da Montone, the royal army defeated him beneath the walls on 2 June 1424 and he died of his wounds three days later. In 1444, under the newly victorious Alfonso of Aragon, the self-governing city was at the height of its wealth, and Saint Bernardino of Siena died there on 20 May.

A basilica rose over Saint Bernardino's shrine, receiving his body in 1472 after the earthquake of 1461. In 1481 Adam of Rottweil, a pupil of Gutenberg, set up one of Italy's earliest printing presses. The Aquilans opened their gates to French armies in 1494 and again in 1527; after the French collapse the Spanish viceroy Filiberto of Orange sacked the city and annulled its privileges, and the townsmen had to raze a quarter and pay a hundred thousand ducats a year for the massive Forte Spagnolo, begun in 1534 above the Florence road. Plague carried off much of the population in 1656, and on 2 February 1703 a great earthquake flattened the city and killed more than six thousand; baroque rebuilding took half a century. In 1799 the townsmen rose for King Ferdinand under General Salomone; Napoleonic rule after 1806 abolished feudalism and the old sheep-drove privileges, and in 1815 L'Aquila returned to the Bourbons.
zh:
拉奎拉雄踞阿布鲁齐亚平宁山脉的一片高台，隔着山岭与教宗国相望。霍亨斯陶芬的腓特烈二世把九十九个山村合并为一座有城墙的王家新城，每个母村在城里各占一区；1272年修成的九十九孔喷泉，喷水口沿三道墙排布，纪念的就是这次联合。曼弗雷迪摧毁了这座年轻的城市，安茹王朝将它重建，14世纪初城墙合龙，拉奎拉发展成那不勒斯王国的第二大城。它的财富来自阿泰尔诺河谷的藏红花田，以及在高山牧场和通往佛罗伦萨的大道之间转场放牧的羊群。1294年，隐修士莫罗内的彼得在科莱马焦圣马利亚圣殿加冕为教宗雷定五世，并在那里发布「佩尔多南扎」大赦令，教宗的禧年制度就从这一仪式发展而来。雇佣兵首领布拉乔·达·蒙托内围城十三个月后，1424年6月2日王家军队在城下将其击败，他伤重三日后死去。1444年，在新胜的阿拉贡的阿方索治下，这座自治城市正值富庶的顶点，锡耶纳的圣伯尔纳定于5月20日在此辞世。

圣伯尔纳定圣殿在他的墓地上建起，1461年的大地震撼动工程，他的遗体于1472年移灵安放。1481年，古腾堡的门徒罗特韦尔的亚当在此开设意大利最早的印刷所之一。拉奎拉人1494年、1527年两度向法军开门；法国失败后，西班牙总督奥兰治亲王菲利贝托洗劫城市、废除其特权，市民还被迫铲平一个街区，每年缴纳十万杜卡托，在通往佛罗伦萨的大道旁的高地上修建庞大的西班牙要塞，工程1534年动工。1656年瘟疫夺去大量人口；1703年2月2日的大地震把城市夷平，六千余人遇难，巴洛克式的重建持续了半个世纪。1799年，市民在萨洛莫内将军率领下起兵效忠费迪南德国王；1806年后的拿破仑政权废除封建制和古老的牧道特权，1815年拉奎拉重归那不勒斯的波旁王室。

en:
Napoli fills the shore of its wide bay and climbs the hills behind a Greek street grid, for it began as the Cumaean colony of Parthenope and was refounded as Neapolis in the sixth century BC. Virgil was partly educated there and later lived in its environs. After 1282 the Angevins made it the capital of their southern kingdom; Frederick II had founded his university there back in 1224. Alfonso V of Aragon drove out René of Anjou in 1442. In 1444 Napoli was the capital of an Aragonese, Neapolitan-speaking Catholic kingdom, a crowded court city and grain port serving one of Italy's largest monarchies. Its cathedral kept vials said to hold the blood of San Gennaro, a fourth-century bishop beheaded at Pozzuoli and patron of the city, whose liquefaction drew crowds three times a year.

Charles VIII of France overran the city in February 1495 on his Angevin claim and had left by July; after a secret partition treaty in 1500, Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba's Spaniards took it in May 1503 and sealed the conquest at the Garigliano on 29 December. Spanish viceroys then ruled for two centuries. Pedro de Toledo, from 1532, drove Via Toledo through the old city, rebuilt the Sant'Elmo fortress and gathered the courts in Castel Capuano; in 1544 Barbary corsairs carried off some 7,000 people from the kingdom into slavery. By the next century Napoli was Europe's second-largest city after Paris: Caravaggio painted for its churches, and the Neapolitan Giambattista Vico wrote his New Science there. In July 1647 the fisherman Masaniello led a tax revolt that grew into a French-backed republic, and Spanish troops did not return until April 1648. Plague in 1656 killed roughly 200,000 people. Austria replaced the viceroys in 1707; Bourbon troops took the city in May 1734 and won Bitonto on the 25th. The young King Charles opened the Teatro di San Carlo beside the royal palace in 1737, and the kingdom was recognised in 1738. The French-backed Parthenopaean Republic briefly displaced Ferdinand IV in 1799. Joseph Bonaparte entered in February 1806 and was proclaimed king on 30 March; Joachim Murat ruled from 1808 until his defeat at Tolentino in May 1815. Ferdinand returned that June, and in December 1816 Naples and Sicily were joined as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
zh:
那波利（今通译那不勒斯）坐落在宽阔的海湾边，城区从岸上爬上背后的丘陵，老城仍留着希腊人的街格：它最初是库迈人建立的帕耳忒诺珀殖民地，公元前6世纪扩建为尼阿波利斯。维吉尔少年时在此求学，后来又住在城郊。1282年后，安茹王朝把它作为南意大利领地的都城；腓特烈二世早在1224年就在此创办了大学。1442年，阿拉贡的阿方索五世赶走安茹的勒内。1444年的那波利是一个阿拉贡王朝统治、说那波利语的天主教王国首都，一座人口稠密的宫廷城市和谷物港口，服务于意大利境内最大的君主国之一。主教座堂里收藏着相传盛有圣雅纳略之血的玻璃瓶，这位4世纪在波佐利被斩首的主教是城市主保圣人，他的圣血每年三次液化，引来大批信众。

法国国王查理八世以安茹继承权为名，1495年2月占领城市，7月即撤离；1500年的秘密瓜分条约之后，贡萨洛·费尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦的西班牙军队1503年5月入城，12月29日在加里利亚诺锁定胜局。此后两个世纪由西班牙总督统治。1532年起，总督佩德罗·德·托莱多在旧城里辟出托莱多路，改建圣埃尔莫堡，把法庭集中到卡普阿诺堡；1544年柏柏尔海盗从王国掳走约7000人为奴。到下个世纪，那波利已是仅次于巴黎的欧洲第二大城市：卡拉瓦乔为这里的教堂作画，本地出生的维柯在此写成《新科学》。1647年7月，渔民马萨涅洛领导抗税起义，后来演变为法国支持的共和国，西班牙军队直到1648年4月才重新入城。1656年的鼠疫夺去约20万人的生命。1707年奥地利取代西班牙总督；1734年5月波旁军队攻占城市，25日在比通托取胜。年轻的国王卡洛斯1737年在王宫旁建成圣卡洛剧院，这是欧洲持续演出最久的歌剧院，波旁王国则于1738年获得承认。法国支持的帕尔泰诺佩共和国1799年曾短暂取代费迪南多四世。1806年2月约瑟夫·波拿巴入城，3月30日被宣布为国王；若阿基姆·缪拉1808年继位，1815年5月在托伦蒂诺战败。费迪南多于6月返回，1816年12月，那波利与西西里合并为两西西里王国。

en:
Salento is the heel of the Italian boot, a flat peninsula between the Adriatic and the Ionian; at Otranto the Italian coast comes within sight of Albania, the nearest point between the two shores. Taranto, its capital, sits on a narrow spit between the open Mar Grande and the enclosed Mar Piccolo, whose shallow waters have long been farmed for mussels. Founded as the Spartan colony of Taras in 706 BC, it became in 1088 the seat of the Norman Principality of Taranto, first granted to Bohemond, Robert Guiscard's son and later a leader of the First Crusade. The last great prince, Giovanni Antonio Orsini del Balzo, held Taranto with Bari and Lecce and was among the richest lords of the Kingdom of Naples; when he died without an heir in 1463 his fiefs reverted to the crown. In 1444 Salento had been Aragonese for two years: a Catholic, Neapolitan-speaking land of olive groves and vineyards, walled ports and baronial castles, with Greek still spoken in a cluster of inland towns.

Otranto suffered the peninsula's worst disaster of the age. On 11 August 1480, after a two-week siege, an Ottoman army under Gedik Ahmed Pasha stormed the town, had its captain sawn in half and beheaded some 800 men who refused to convert; the Turks held it for thirteen months and withdrew in September 1481, after Mehmed II died marching on Italy. The coastal towns rebuilt their walls against further raids: Charles V gave Lecce a castle and a new circuit of walls, and the present Aragonese castle at Taranto, a seven-tower fortress attributed to Francesco di Giorgio Martini and finished in 1496, repelled an Ottoman attack in 1594. Barbarossa's fleet retook Otranto briefly in 1537. From about 1630 Lecce raised the densely carved churches and facades of Salentine baroque out of its soft local limestone, and came to be called the Florence of the South. French-backed legislation ended feudal jurisdiction in the Terra d'Otranto in 1806.
zh:
萨伦托是意大利靴形半岛的鞋跟，夹在亚得里亚海与伊奥尼亚海之间；奥特朗托海峡这边能望到阿尔巴尼亚，是意大利离巴尔干最近的海岸。首府塔兰托坐落在开阔的大海与封闭的小海之间一条狭长地岬上，小海的浅水里久有贻贝养殖。它本是公元前706年斯巴达人建立的殖民城塔拉斯，1088年成为诺曼人塔兰托亲王国的首府，首任亲王博希蒙德是罗伯特·吉斯卡尔之子，后来也是第一次十字军的首领之一。末代强藩焦万尼·安东尼奥·奥尔西尼·德尔·巴尔佐兼领塔兰托、巴里和莱切，是那不勒斯王国最富有的领主之一，1463年无嗣而终，封地收归王室。1444年时，萨伦托归入阿拉贡统治已两年：这片信奉天主教、讲那不勒斯语的土地上遍布橄榄园、葡萄园、设防港口和男爵城堡，内陆还有一片城镇仍讲希腊语。

奥特朗托遭遇过那个时代半岛上最惨重的祸事。1480年8月11日，格迪克·艾哈迈德帕夏的奥斯曼军队围攻两周后破城，城防长官被锯成两截，约八百名拒绝改宗的男子被斩首；土耳其人占据十三个月，1481年9月因穆罕默德二世在进军意大利途中病死而撤离。沿海各城纷纷重修城墙防备再袭：查理五世为莱切修筑城堡和新城墙；塔兰托的阿拉贡城堡由弗朗切斯科·迪·乔治·马蒂尼设计，七座塔楼，1496年建成，1594年击退了一次奥斯曼进攻。1537年，巴巴罗萨的舰队曾短暂重占奥特朗托。约从1630年起，莱切用当地松软的石灰岩，盖出一批雕饰繁密的教堂和立面，人称「南方的佛罗伦萨」。1806年法国支持下的立法废除了奥特朗托地区的封建司法权。

en:
Reggio sits on the Aspromonte side of the Strait of Messina, facing Sicily across the narrow sea lane that travellers and fleets used between the Tyrrhenian and Ionian waters. Its Greek predecessor Rhegion was one of the major cities of Magna Graecia, and long Byzantine rule left Basilian monasteries, mulberry groves and silk working in the valleys. Reggio later headed the Calabrian giustizierato under Norman and Hohenstaufen kings, but its choice of sides in the Neapolitan succession cost it dear: after backing René of Anjou against Alfonso V of Aragon, it lost the provincial seat to Catanzaro in 1442. In 1444 Reggio was therefore a port in the newly Aragonese Kingdom of Naples, Catholic at the high altar but still home to Greek-rite monks, a Jewish quarter, fisheries and silk merchants.

Ferdinand I restored Reggio's capital status in 1465, and the Jewish quarter gave European printing one of its notable dates when Abraham Garton printed Rashi's commentary on the Torah there in February 1475, the first dated Hebrew book. After the French wars for Naples, Spanish viceroys governed Calabria from 1504, while Genoese, Venetian, Spanish, Dutch and English buyers kept the market for Reggio silk busy; bergamot orchards also spread around the coast in the eighteenth century. Raids exposed the same open shoreline that made the port rich. Hayreddin Barbarossa burned Reggio in 1534 and carried off about eight hundred people, and Barbary raiders returned in 1558 to enslave many inhabitants. Earthquakes wrecked the medieval harbour in 1562 and devastated southern Calabria in 1783. French troops took the city in 1806 and made Reggio a military command and a duchy under Napoleonic Naples.
zh:
雷焦位于阿斯普罗蒙特山麓，隔狭窄的墨西拿海峡与西西里相望；舰队和旅人往返第勒尼安海与伊奥尼亚海时，常取道这条水路。其希腊前身雷吉翁是大希腊最重要的城市之一，漫长的拜占庭统治则在山谷间留下巴西略修会修道院、桑园和丝织业。诺曼与霍亨斯陶芬君主统治时期，雷焦长期是卡拉布里亚司法区首府，但它在那不勒斯继承战争中支持安茹的勒内、反对阿拉贡的阿方索五世，因而在1442年把省级治所让给卡坦扎罗。1444年，雷焦是刚归入阿拉贡体系的那不勒斯王国港口，官方崇奉天主教，城中却仍有希腊礼仪修士、犹太区、渔场和丝绸商人。

1465年，费尔南多一世恢复雷焦的首府地位。1475年2月，亚伯拉罕·加顿在当地犹太区印成拉希的《托拉》注释，这是第一部有明确日期的希伯来文书籍。法国争夺那不勒斯之后，西班牙副王自1504年起治理卡拉布里亚；热那亚、威尼斯、西班牙、荷兰和英格兰买主维持着雷焦丝绸的生意，香柠檬园也在18世纪沿海一带扩展开来。同样的海岸带来财富，也把掳掠者送到城下。1534年，赫伊尔丁·巴巴罗萨焚毁雷焦，掳走约八百人；1558年，柏柏尔袭掠者又返回此地，把许多居民掳为奴隶。1562年的地震毁掉中世纪港湾，1783年的大地震重创南卡拉布里亚。1806年，法军攻占雷焦，使它成为拿破仑体系下那不勒斯的军事司令部和公国。

en:
Messina guards the Sicilian side of the narrow, current-swept strait that carries its name. Greek settlers developed its sickle-shaped harbour of Zancle and renamed the town Messana around the early fifth century BC. Arab forces destroyed the city in 843, and Roger I of Hauteville took the site in 1060 during the Norman reconquest. In 1347 Genoese galleys fleeing the siege of Kaffa brought the Black Death into this harbour, their crews already dead or dying on board, and from Messina the plague crossed into mainland Italy. After the Sicilian Vespers the city became a second royal capital beside Palermo under the Crown of Aragon, its senate, merchants and silk workers enriched by a port linking the Tyrrhenian and Ionian seas, while fishermen harpooned swordfish in the strait's currents. In 1444 Messina was a Catholic, Sicilian-speaking Aragonese city, wealthy and proud enough to rival Palermo.

Its most famous painter, Antonello da Messina, worked in the Netherlandish oil technique, and his paintings influenced the school of Venice. Greek refugees from the Peloponnese settled here in 1533-34, fleeing Ottoman expansion and keeping their Greek rite. In 1548 Ignatius of Loyola founded the first Jesuit college in the world here, the seed of the University of Messina. In 1571 Don John of Austria sailed the Holy League fleet out of this harbour and defeated the Ottomans at Lepanto on 7 October; Miguel de Cervantes, wounded in the battle, recovered for a time in Messina's Grand Hospital. The city was then at its peak, counted among the ten largest in Europe, but rivalry with Palermo and resentment of Spanish rule drove its senate to revolt in July 1674. French aid kept it free until April 1678; after the Peace of Nijmegen the Spaniards retook and sacked the city, abolished its senate, university and ancient privileges, and built the Real Cittadella to overawe the port. Plague returned in 1743. Utrecht assigned Sicily to Savoy in 1713, Austrian rule followed in 1720, and the Bourbons secured the island in 1734-1735. Earthquakes that began on 5 February 1783 shattered much of Messina, leaving only the citadel standing among the ruins. The Bourbons kept Sicily through the Napoleonic wars and joined it to Naples as the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in December 1816.
zh:
墨西拿扼守着水流湍急的同名海峡的西西里一侧。希腊殖民者经营镰刀形的赞克勒港，在公元前5世纪初前后将城镇改称墨萨拿。843年，阿拉伯军队摧毁城市；1060年，欧特维尔的鲁杰罗一世在诺曼收复中夺取此地。1347年，从卡法围城战中逃出的热那亚桨帆船把黑死病带进这个港口，船上的人已经成批死去，鼠疫随即从墨西拿传入意大利本土。西西里晚祷之后，它在阿拉贡联合治下成为与巴勒莫并列的第二都城，元老院、商人和丝织工匠依托连接第勒尼安海与伊奥尼亚海的港口致富，渔民则在海峡急流中叉捕剑鱼。1444年的墨西拿是一座天主教、说西西里语的阿拉贡城市，富庶而自负，足以同巴勒莫相争。

本地最有名的画家安东内洛·达·梅西纳采用尼德兰式油画技法作画，他的作品影响了威尼斯画派。1533至1534年，为躲避奥斯曼扩张，伯罗奔尼撒的希腊难民到此定居，保留了自己的希腊礼。1548年，依纳爵·罗耀拉在此创办世界上第一所耶稣会学院，即后来的墨西拿大学。1571年，奥地利的堂胡安率神圣同盟舰队从港内出发远征，10月7日在勒班陀击败奥斯曼舰队；在战斗中负伤的米格尔·德·塞万提斯曾在墨西拿大医院养伤。当时的墨西拿正处在全盛期，名列欧洲十大城市，但与巴勒莫的竞争和对西班牙统治的怨恨驱使元老院在1674年7月起义。法国援助使城市坚持到1678年4月；《奈梅亨和约》后，西班牙人收复并洗劫城市，废除元老院、大学和古老特权，又修建雷亚尔城堡压制港口。1743年鼠疫再度袭来。《乌得勒支和约》1713年将西西里交给萨伏依，1720年转为奥地利统治，1734至1735年波旁家族取得该岛。1783年2月5日开始的地震群摧毁墨西拿大片城区，废墟中只有城堡矗立。波旁王朝在拿破仑战争中守住西西里，1816年12月把它与那不勒斯合并为两西西里王国。

en:
Palermo curves around a broad Tyrrhenian gulf beneath the Conca d'Oro, the fertile plain whose vineyards, orchards and grainfields fed one of Sicily's best harbours. Phoenician settlers called their port Ziz, and Greek speakers knew it as Panormos. Arab forces took the city in 831 and made it the seat of Sicilian government. Robert Guiscard's Normans needed a five-month siege to enter it in 1072, and Roger II was crowned king there in 1130. His Palazzo dei Normanni housed the royal court and the Palatine Chapel, whose mosaics, marble panels and painted wooden ceiling joined Norman, Arab and Byzantine workmanship. The Hohenstaufen emperor Frederick II later kept his Sicilian court in the palace and supported the poets later called the Sicilian School. After Angevin rule drew the court toward Naples, the Sicilian Vespers of 1282 began in Palermo and brought the island under Aragon. In 1444 Alfonso V of Aragon ruled from Naples, which he had taken in 1442, but a viceroy and the Sicilian parliament remained at Palermo; its merchants shipped grain, sugar and Conca d'Oro wine.

Spanish rule after 1516 put the island under Habsburg viceroys, while Palermo nobles built town palaces with revenues from grain, silk and sugar. Famine and heavy excise taxes turned that order upside down in 1647. The first rising, in May, was led by the miller Nino La Pelosa after prisoners were released from the city jail; he was soon executed. Giuseppe D'Alesi, who had watched Masaniello's revolt in Naples, returned in August and was elected captain by the people. His followers brought cannon against the royal palace, drove the viceroy to flee by sea, preserved the public bank and drew up forty-nine chapters for greater Sicilian control of the kingdom. Noble factions then turned on him with the accusation that he meant to hand Sicily to France, and D'Alesi was beheaded on 22 August.

The Peace of Utrecht gave Sicily to the House of Savoy in 1713, Spanish troops reoccupied Palermo in 1718, and Austria held the island from 1720. Charles of Bourbon conquered it in 1734 and was crowned at Palermo the next year, but the royal court remained at Naples. Ferdinand of Bourbon took refuge there from the French in 1798 and again in 1806, the second time under British protection. A Sicilian constitution was proclaimed at Palermo in 1812, then set aside when the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies was formed in 1816 with its capital at Naples.
zh:
巴勒莫环抱第勒尼安海的宽阔海湾，后方是阿拉伯人所称的「金盆」沃土；葡萄园、果园和粮田供养着西西里最好的港口之一。腓尼基定居者把这里称为齐兹，希腊语居民则称之为帕诺尔莫斯。831年阿拉伯军队攻占城市，把它设为西西里政权的驻地。1072年，罗贝尔·吉斯卡尔率领诺曼人围城五个月才入城；1130年，鲁杰罗二世在此加冕为王。他的诺曼王宫容纳王室宫廷和帕拉蒂纳礼拜堂，礼拜堂里的马赛克、大理石镶板和彩绘木顶结合了诺曼、阿拉伯与拜占庭工艺。后来，霍亨斯陶芬王朝皇帝腓特烈二世把西西里宫廷设在宫中，并资助后来被称为西西里诗派的诗人。安茹王朝把宫廷重心移向那不勒斯后，1282年「西西里晚祷」起义在巴勒莫爆发，西西里岛转归阿拉贡。1444年，阿拉贡的阿方索五世从1442年取得的那不勒斯发号施令，但一位副王和西西里议会继续驻在巴勒莫；商人从这里输出谷物、蔗糖和「金盆」葡萄酒。

1516年后，西西里由哈布斯堡西班牙的副王统治，巴勒莫贵族则靠谷物、生丝和蔗糖的收益在城中修建宅邸。1647年，饥荒和沉重的消费税打乱了这套秩序。5月，囚犯被放出城监后，磨坊工尼诺·拉佩洛萨领导了第一场起事，但他很快被处死。朱塞佩·达莱西曾在那不勒斯观察马萨涅洛起义，8月回到巴勒莫，被民众推举为统领。他的追随者把大炮推到王宫前，逼得副王从海上逃走；起事者保护公共银行，还拟定四十九项条款，要求让西西里人更多管理本岛。贵族派系随后反咬他企图把西西里交给法国，达莱西于8月22日被斩首。

1713年，《乌得勒支和约》把西西里交给萨伏依家族；西班牙军队1718年重新占领巴勒莫，奥地利自1720年起统治此岛。1734年波旁家族的查理攻取西西里，次年在巴勒莫加冕，但王室宫廷继续设在那不勒斯。1798年和1806年，波旁的费迪南多两度为躲避法军逃到巴勒莫，第二次还受到英国保护。1812年，西西里宪法在巴勒莫颁布；1816年两西西里王国成立、定都那不勒斯，这部宪法随即被搁置。

en:
Malta is a small, stony island group sixty miles south of Sicily, lying across the narrow channel that joins the eastern and western Mediterranean. Its Grand Harbour is one of the safest anchorages between Sicily and the Tunisian coast, and the old capital Mdina sits on high ground inland, looking down on the roads to it. An Aghlabid army sacked Byzantine Melite in 870, and the Arabic-speaking settlers who followed left their language on the islands; Roger of Sicily brought Malta under Norman rule in 1091, and after 1282 it passed with Sicily to the Crown of Aragon. A Hafsid raid besieged Mdina in 1429 and carried numbers of islanders into slavery. In 1444 about ten thousand Catholic, Maltese-speaking people lived here under an Aragonese governor and the town council in Mdina, fishing the surrounding waters while their low coasts stayed exposed to corsairs.

The long age of fortification began in 1530, when Charles V enfeoffed Malta to the Hospitallers for an annual tribute of one falcon. The knights, driven from Rhodes eight years earlier, made fortified Birgu beside the Grand Harbour their seat rather than Mdina. In 1551 Dragut's Ottomans raided Gozo and carried most of its people into slavery. Suleiman the Magnificent sent a far larger force in 1565: roughly five hundred knights and six thousand soldiers held Birgu and the harbour forts for nearly four months, until a relief army landed from Sicily and the Ottomans re-embarked. The knights then built a new capital on the Sciberras peninsula and named it Valletta after Grand Master Jean Parisot de la Valette, ringed the harbour with bastions, and sent their galleys cruising against Ottoman shipping for two centuries while Baroque churches and palaces rose behind the walls. The 1693 Sicily earthquake shook down much of medieval Mdina, and Lorenzo Gafà rebuilt its cathedral between 1697 and 1703. Napoleon took Malta on his way to Egypt in June 1798, but the Maltese rose within months and, with British and Neapolitan help, blockaded the French garrison for two years; its surrender in 1800 opened British rule, confirmed by the Treaty of Paris in 1814.
zh:
马耳他是西西里以南约六十英里的石质群岛，横亘在连接地中海东西两段的狭窄航道上。大港是西西里与突尼斯海岸之间最稳妥的锚地之一，旧都姆迪纳高踞内陆台地，俯瞰通往大港的道路。870年阿格拉布军队洗劫拜占庭的梅利特，随后迁来的阿拉伯语定居者把语言留在了群岛上；1091年西西里的鲁杰罗把马耳他纳入诺曼统治，1282年后它随西西里归属阿拉贡王权。1429年哈夫斯入侵者围攻姆迪纳，掳走不少岛民为奴。1444年，约一万名信奉天主教、操马耳他语的岛民由阿拉贡总督和姆迪纳的市镇公会治理，在周围海域捕鱼为生，低矮的海岸却始终暴露在海盗威胁之下。

漫长的堡垒时代始于1530年：查理五世把马耳他封给医院骑士团，年贡为一只猎鹰。骑士团八年前被逐出罗得岛，这次没有进驻姆迪纳，而在大港旁防备森严的比尔古设下总部。1551年，德拉古特的奥斯曼军队袭击戈佐岛，把大部分居民掳为奴隶。1565年，苏莱曼大帝派来远为庞大的军队：约五百名骑士和六千士兵坚守比尔古及港中堡垒近四个月，直到西西里援军登陆，奥斯曼人才登船撤走。骑士团随后在希伯拉斯半岛上修建新都，以大教长让·帕里索·德·拉·瓦莱特之名命名为瓦莱塔，又在大港周围筑起棱堡；此后两百年，骑士团桨帆战舰巡弋海上、截击奥斯曼航运，城墙之内巴洛克教堂和宫殿次第兴建。1693年西西里大地震震毁中世纪姆迪纳的大片建筑，洛伦佐·加法在1697年至1703年重建主教座堂。1798年6月，拿破仑在远征埃及途中夺取马耳他，但不出数月马耳他人便揭竿而起，在英国和那不勒斯援助下围困法军两年；1800年法军投降开启了英国统治，1814年《巴黎条约》予以确认。

en:
Sassari grew up a few miles inland from the Roman harbour of Turris Libisonis, now Porto Torres, whose people abandoned the exposed coast for the hills during the Saracen raids; the merged villages are first named in a document of 1131. It became the richest city and last capital of the Giudicato of Torres. Its last strongman, Michele Zanche, was murdered in 1275, and Dante placed him in the fifth bolgia of the Inferno, among the barrators. After Genoa broke Pisan power at Meloria in 1284, Sassari ruled itself as a free commune allied to Genoa, under statutes of 1316 written in Latin and Logudorese and noted for their mild penalties. In 1323 its citizens opened their gates to the Infante Alfonso of Aragon; the town then counted some 10,000 people, and in 1331 it became a royal city of the new Kingdom of Sardinia. Brancaleone Doria seized it for the Giudicato of Arborea in 1391, and in 1420 William III of Narbona sold the last Arborean rights, Sassari with them, to Alfonso V for 100,000 gold florins. In 1444 the Catalan castle raised to guard against the town's own revolts watches over a royal city, while Barbary corsairs hound its sea trade.

French troops under Renzo da Ceri sacked Sassari in 1527, and plague thinned the city in 1528 and again in 1652. It recovered under Spanish rule: in 1562 the Jesuits opened Sardinia's first university and the town acquired its first press, and the historian Giovanni Francesco Fara gathered a humanist circle about him. Between 1603 and 1606 Genoese craftsmen built the Fountain of the Rosello down by the valley, the city's emblem, and the old Aragonese castle housed the Spanish Inquisition. Sardinia passed to Austria in 1713 and to the House of Savoy in 1720. In December 1795 the peasants of the Logudoro marched on the city against feudal dues, behind the judge Giovanni Maria Angioy, who entered it with viceregal powers; the rising collapsed in 1796 and Angioy died in exile in Paris in 1808. The Savoyard court weathered the Napoleonic wars from the island, and in 1821 Sassari was a city of the Kingdom of Sardinia.
zh:
萨萨里兴起于罗马港口图尔里斯利比索尼斯（今波尔图托雷斯）几英里外的内陆：萨拉森海盗袭扰时，港人弃海岸退入丘陵，合并而成的聚落首见于1131年的文献。它后来成为托雷斯吉乌帝卡提最富庶的城市和末代都城。末代强人米凯莱·赞凯1275年被杀，但丁把他写进《神曲·地狱篇》第二十二歌，放在地狱第八圈第五恶囊的贪官之列。1284年热那亚在梅洛里亚海战击垮比萨后，萨萨里成为与热那亚结盟的自由城邦，1316年颁行拉丁文和鲁古多罗方言双语法典，刑罚之宽缓在中世纪少见。1323年，市民向阿拉贡的阿方索王子开城，当时全城约有一万人；1331年，它成为新生的撒丁王国的王属城市。1391年，布兰卡莱奥内·多里亚替阿尔博雷亚攻占此城；1420年，纳博讷的纪尧姆三世把阿尔博雷亚的剩余权利连同萨萨里，以十万金弗罗林卖给阿方索五世。1444年，为防备本城反叛而修的卡塔兰城堡俯瞰着这座王属城市，海上贸易则饱受巴巴里海盗侵扰。

1527年，伦佐·达·切里率领的法军洗劫萨萨里，瘟疫又在1528年和1652年两度使人口锐减。西班牙统治时期城市复苏：1562年耶稣会士开办撒丁岛第一所大学，城里也有了第一台印刷机，历史学家乔瓦尼·弗朗切斯科·法拉周围聚起一个人文主义圈子。1603至1606年，热那亚工匠在山谷边建起罗塞洛喷泉，这是城市的标志；古老的阿拉贡城堡里则设着西班牙宗教裁判所。撒丁岛1713年归奥地利，1720年转归萨伏依王朝。1795年12月，鲁古多罗的农民为反对封建赋役进军萨萨里，首领是带着副王全权入城的法官乔瓦尼·马里亚·安焦伊；起事1796年瓦解，安焦伊流亡巴黎，1808年死在那里。拿破仑战争期间，萨伏依朝廷在岛上支撑下来，1821年的萨萨里是撒丁王国的城市。

en:
Klagenfurt lies in the Klagenfurt basin, where the Glan carries the waters of the Wörthersee to the Drau, and German and Slovene villagers shared the surrounding countryside. The Spanheim dukes of Carinthia laid out a market here, first recorded as 'in foro Chlagenvurth' in 1192–99, and Duke Bernhard moved the flood-prone settlement to safer ground in 1246; it received its charter in 1252. Carinthia, a duchy since 976, passed to the Habsburgs in 1335 and was ruled together with Styria and Carniola as Inner Austria. In 1444 Klagenfurt was still a modest market town overshadowed by St. Veit, the seat of the duchy's Estates, though the forges of the Görtschitz valley already worked the iron of the Hüttenberg, prized here since the age of Roman Noricum.

The town's founding legend tells of a lindworm that haunted the marsh and devoured anyone who came near, until the villagers chained an ox fitted with an iron hook to a tower as bait and killed it; the beast entered the town's coat of arms and later the Lindwurm fountain on the Neuer Platz, its dragon carved from a single six-ton block of slate and hauled there in 1593 by three hundred white-clad youths. Ottoman raiders crossed the Seeberg into the Jaunfeld in 1473 and returned four more times before 1483, against leagues the peasants had formed for their own defence. After a fire destroyed the town in 1514, Emperor Maximilian I gave Klagenfurt to the Carinthian Estates in 1518, and they made it their capital: the Italian architect Domenico dell'Allio laid out the chessboard streets, the Lend canal reached the Wörthersee in 1527, the mint moved from St. Veit in 1529, and the Estates' Landhaus rose from 1574, its Great Hall of Arms finished in 1578 with painted arms and princes' portraits. By the end of the century Klagenfurt was the most modern and strongest fortress town in the region. Nearly all the Estates were Lutheran by then, but Archduke Ferdinand's Counter-Reformation closed the Trinity church in 1600 and gave it to the Jesuits. French troops entered without a fight in 1797 and occupied it again in 1805 and 1809, when the walls were blown up and the border of Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces ran just to the west.
zh:
下克恩滕的克拉根福地处克拉根福盆地，格兰河把沃尔特湖的湖水引入德劳河，周围乡间德意志与斯洛文尼亚农户杂处。克恩滕公爵施潘海姆家族在此设立市集，1192至1199年间的文献首次以克拉根福市集（in foro Chlagenvurth）之名记载其地；1246年伯恩哈德公爵把屡遭水患的聚落迁往高处，1252年获得城市特许状。克恩滕自976年起为公爵领地，1335年归于哈布斯堡家族，与施泰尔马克、卡尼奥拉合并，按内奥地利治理。1444年的克拉根福还只是座不起眼的集镇，声势在公爵领地等级会议驻地格兰河畔圣法伊特之下，唯有格尔奇茨河谷的铁匠铺已在冶炼许滕贝格的铁矿，这种铁自罗马诺里克时代起便备受珍视。

相传克拉根福的建城传说中，有一条林德虫盘踞在沼泽里，凡靠近的人都被它吞食；村民在塔上拴住一头挂着大铁钩的公牛作诱饵，才把恶龙杀死。龙的形象进了城徽，后来又立在新广场的喷泉上：石龙由整块六吨重的板岩雕成，1593年由三百名白衣青年拖到广场。1473年，奥斯曼袭扰军越过塞贝格山口攻入尧恩费尔德，到1483年又先后四度来犯，农民自行结社自保却不堪一击。1514年全城毁于大火，皇帝马克西米利安一世1518年把克拉根福赐予克恩滕等级会议，后者将其建成自己的首府：意大利建筑师多梅尼科·德利·阿利奥规划棋盘式街道，1527年伦德运河连通沃尔特湖，1529年君主的铸币厂从格兰河畔圣法伊特迁来，1574年起兴建等级会议大厦，大纹章厅1578年完工，厅内绘满纹章和历代克恩滕君主的肖像。到16世纪末，克拉根福已是这一地区最现代、最坚固的要塞城市。那时等级会议几乎已全体皈依路德宗，费迪南德大公推行反宗教改革，1600年封闭三一教堂并转交耶稣会。1797年法军不战入城，1805年和1809年又两度占领；1809年旧城墙被炸毁，拿破仑伊利里亚行省的边界就划在城市以西不远处。

en:
Krain, Kranjska in Slovene and Carniola in English, covers the upper Sava and the forested limestone country between Carinthia and Istria. Kranj and Kamnik were its early seats, but in 1256 Duke Ulrich III of Carinthia moved his residence to Laibach (Ljubljana), a market town on the road from the Adriatic toward the Danube. The Habsburgs took Carniola in 1335, and Rudolf IV raised it to a duchy in 1364. In 1444 German-speaking nobles and burghers held the walled capital while Slovene villagers pastured livestock in its valleys; the Catholic Habsburg land lay inside the Holy Roman Empire, close to the Ottoman frontier.

Emperor Frederick III set up the Diocese of Laibach in 1461. After the severe earthquake of 1511 the city was rebuilt in the Renaissance style with new walls, and in 1515 the great Slovene peasant revolt broke out across the province: about 80,000 villagers demanded their old customs and trading rights until imperial mercenaries crushed the five-month rising. Protestant teaching took hold after 1529; the Carniolan reformer Primož Trubar founded the Protestant Church of Carniola and wrote the first printed books in Slovene, while Laibach supported a Protestant secondary school, public library and printing house. The Protestants were driven out in 1598, Bishop Thomas Chrön had eight cartloads of their books burned in public, and the Jesuits brought the town back to Catholic practice. From 1809 to 1813 Laibach was the capital of Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces. In 1821 the emperors of Austria and Russia met there with their allies for the Congress of Laibach, which authorised Austrian troops to suppress the liberal rising in the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
zh:
克拉尼在斯洛文尼亚语中称克拉尼斯卡，英文常作卡尼奥拉，地处萨瓦河上游、克恩滕与伊斯特里亚之间森林覆盖的石灰岩山地。它早期的治所在克拉尼和卡姆尼克；1256年，克恩滕公爵乌尔里希三世把驻地迁到莱巴赫，即卢布尔雅那，这座商镇位于亚得里亚海通往多瑙河流域的道路上。哈布斯堡家族1335年取得卡尼奥拉，鲁道夫四世1364年将其升为公国。1444年，讲德语的贵族和市民据守设防的首府，斯洛文尼亚村民在山谷间放牧牲畜；这片天主教的哈布斯堡领地属于神圣罗马帝国，紧邻奥斯曼边境。

皇帝腓特烈三世1461年设立莱巴赫教区。1511年的强烈地震后，城市以文艺复兴风格重建并新筑城墙；1515年，大规模的斯洛文尼亚农民起义席卷全省，约八万名村民要求恢复旧有惯例和贸易权利，五个月后被帝国雇佣军镇压。1529年后新教教义在此扎根：卡尼奥拉宗教改革家普里莫日·特鲁巴尔创立卡尼奥拉新教教会，写成最早的斯洛文尼亚语印刷书籍，莱巴赫也办起新教中学、公共图书馆和印刷所。1598年新教徒被逐出城，主教托马日·赫伦下令当众烧毁八车新教书籍，耶稣会随后使城市回归天主教。1809年至1813年，莱巴赫是拿破仑伊利里亚行省的首府。1821年，奥地利皇帝和俄国皇帝率各国盟友在此召开莱巴赫会议，授权奥地利出兵镇压两西西里王国的自由派起义。

en:
Istria is the large triangular peninsula that reaches into the northern Adriatic between the Gulf of Trieste and the Kvarner, taking its name from the Histri, pirate tribes whom Rome needed two campaigns to subdue in 177 BC. At Pola, the chief town, the Romans left one of the best-preserved amphitheatres of the ancient world. Slavic settlers occupied the interior in the seventh century, while the coastal towns kept their Romance speech. In the later thirteenth century those towns passed one by one to Venice, and Pola became part of the Stato da Mar in 1331; meanwhile the castle country inland around Mitterburg, the German name for Pazin, had fallen to the Habsburgs. In 1444 the Istrian coast was Venetian ground. Its harbours watered the galleys sailing between Venice and the Levant, the pans at Pirano produced salt, and the wine and oil of the coastal slopes went north in Venetian holds.

War and sickness wore Venetian Pola down: Genoese, Hungarian and Habsburg raids, then plague, malaria and typhus, left scarcely 3,000 inhabitants by the 1750s among ruins overgrown with ivy. Its shipping lived in fear of the Uskoks, Slavic irregulars based at Senj who raided merchantmen under Austrian protection; Venice's campaign against them opened the Uskok War in 1615, fought around Gradisca and the Istrian frontier. Dante, who had visited the town, gave Pola a line in the Divine Comedy, beside the gulf that marked the edge of Italy. When the Republic fell in 1797 the Treaty of Campo Formio gave Istria to the Habsburgs. Napoleon attached it to his Kingdom of Italy in 1805 and to his Illyrian Provinces in 1809, which brought the Code Napoleon, roads and schools. Austrian troops reoccupied the peninsula on 20 September 1813, and after 1815 it was administered within the Habsburg Kingdom of Illyria.
zh:
伊斯特里亚是伸入亚得里亚海北部的三角形大半岛，夹在的里雅斯特湾与克瓦内尔湾之间，得名于希斯特里人；这个以海盗为业的部族让罗马人连打两场仗，才在公元前177年将其征服。首城普拉留存着古代世界保存最完好的竞技场之一。7世纪时斯拉夫人定居内陆，沿海诸城仍讲罗曼语。13世纪后期，这些城镇相继落入威尼斯之手，普拉1331年并入「海洋之国」；而内陆以米特堡（帕津）为中心的堡寨地带，此前已归属哈布斯堡。1444年的伊斯特里亚海岸是威尼斯的疆土：各港为往返威尼斯与黎凡特的桨帆船补给淡水，皮兰盐田产盐，沿海坡地的葡萄酒和橄榄油则随威尼斯商船北上。

战争和疫病耗尽了威尼斯治下的普拉：热那亚人、匈牙利人和哈布斯堡先后来袭，随后是鼠疫、疟疾和伤寒；到1750年代，这座古城只剩约三千居民，残垣上爬满常春藤。港中船家还要提防乌斯科克人，这些以塞尼为基地的斯拉夫非正规兵在奥地利庇护下劫掠商船；威尼斯出兵讨伐，1615年引发乌斯科克战争，战场就在格拉迪斯卡和伊斯特里亚边界一带。但丁到过普拉，在《神曲》里写到这座毗邻海湾、标志意大利边界的城市。1797年威尼斯共和国灭亡，《坎波福尔米奥条约》把伊斯特里亚交给哈布斯堡。1805年拿破仑将半岛并入意大利王国，1809年又划入伊利里亚行省，带来《拿破仑法典》，修起道路和学校。1813年9月20日，奥地利军队重新占领半岛；1815年以后，它归哈布斯堡的伊利里亚王国管辖。

en:
Zagreb grew from two hills on the southern slopes of Mount Medvednica above the Sava; the Roman town of Andautonia once stood nearby at Šćitarjevo. In 1094 King Ladislaus of Hungary founded a diocese on the eastern hill, Kaptol, where the cathedral and the canons' quarter took root, while craftsmen and traders settled Gradec on the neighbouring height. The Mongols sacked both towns in 1242, and Béla IV's Golden Bull of that year made Gradec a free royal city with its own walls and courts. The two neighbours never got on: for four centuries they feuded across the Medveščak brook over its mills and jurisdiction, with excommunications and street fighting, and the wooden bridge between them took the name Krvavi most, the Bloody Bridge. In 1444 Zagreb belonged to the Croatian-Hungarian crown. Its Catholic craftsmen wove cloth and its merchants ran the markets of Zagorje, while beyond the southern hills the Ottoman advance through the Balkans was drawing close.

As the southern frontier collapsed, the kingdom's institutions gathered at Zagreb: the Sabor convened at Gradec, the town is called Croatia's capital in documents from 1557, and the ban took up residence there in 1621. The strain of the Turkish wars helped ignite Matija Gubec's peasant revolt in Zagorje against Baron Ferenc Tahy. It broke out on 28 January 1573 and ended twelve days later, when on 9 February the baronial army broke Gubec's ten thousand men at Stubičko polje and left about three thousand dead. On 15 February Gubec was brought to St Mark's Square, where tradition says he was forced to wear a red-hot iron crown in mockery of a 'peasant king' and was then quartered. The Jesuits, who had opened a grammar school in 1607, built the baroque church of St Catherine in 1620–32 and later an academy of philosophy, theology and law. The Zrinski–Frankopan plot against Vienna ended on the scaffold: Ban Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan were beheaded at Wiener Neustadt on 30 April 1671. Fire and plague scourged the town as cruelly as war, and in 1776 the royal council moved from Varaždin to Zagreb.
zh:
萨格勒布发源于萨瓦河畔、梅德韦德尼察山南麓的两座小山，附近的什奇塔尔耶沃曾坐落着罗马城镇安达通尼亚。1094年，匈牙利国王拉斯洛一世在东山卡普托尔设立主教区，大教堂与法政牧师区在此扎根，工匠和商人则聚居于相邻的格拉代茨高地。1242年两地同遭蒙古人洗劫，同年贝拉四世颁发金玺诏书，把格拉代茨辟为自由王城，许其自筑城墙、自设法庭。两镇素来不睦，为梅德韦什查克溪上的磨坊和管辖权争斗了四百年，绝罚与巷战不断，溪上木桥因此得名「血桥」。1444年的萨格勒布属于克罗地亚—匈牙利共主邦联：天主教工匠织布，商人掌着扎戈列的市集，而在南部群山之外，席卷巴尔干的奥斯曼兵锋正步步逼近。

随着南部防线土崩瓦解，克罗地亚王国的各套机构陆续聚到萨格勒布：萨博尔议会在格拉代茨召开，1557年起的文献已称其为克罗地亚都城，总督1621年在此开府。土耳其战争的重负引燃了扎戈列的民变：1573年1月28日，马蒂亚·古贝茨率众起义，反抗费伦茨·塔希男爵；12天后的2月9日，贵族军队在斯图比查原野击溃古贝茨的上万人马，义军战死约三千人；2月15日，古贝茨被押到圣马可广场，相传被逼戴上烧红的铁冠，嘲弄他这个「农民国王」，随后被处车裂。1607年已在此开办文理中学的耶稣会，1620至1632年建成巴洛克风格的圣凯瑟琳教堂，日后又办起教授哲学、神学与法律的学院。兹林斯基—弗兰科潘反维也纳密谋以断头收场：总督彼得·兹林斯基与弗兰·克尔斯托·弗兰科潘1671年4月30日在维也纳新城被斩首。火灾与瘟疫对城镇的摧残不亚于战争，1776年王国御前会议从瓦拉日丁迁至萨格勒布。

en:
Judenburg lies on the Mur at the edge of the Aichfeld, the broad grain basin of Upper Styria, where the road over the Obdach Saddle runs south to Carinthia. It first appears in a 1074 charter as mercatum Judinburch, a market below Eppenstein castle named for its Jewish merchants, and held town rights by 1224. Its wealth came from the Erzberg at nearby Eisenerz, Austria's largest iron mountain: miners had worked its surface ore since the twelfth century, water-powered hammers refined it in the valleys, and an iron ordinance of 1448 divided the markets, sending Innerberg iron to northern Europe and Vordernberg iron by way of Venice to the Levant. Judenburg also traded in speik, an Alpine herb sold in Venice as perfume, and Frederick III gave the town a monopoly of that trade in 1460. Ruled from Graz with the rest of Inner Austria, it was in 1444 a Catholic German-speaking Habsburg town living on Erzberg iron and Aichfeld grain.

War came up the Mur in the later fifteenth century: Hungarian troops held much of Upper Styria in 1479, and Ottoman raiders burned Judenburg and Bruck the next year; in 1496 Maximilian I expelled the Jews of Styria, ending the community from which the town took its name. During the Peasants' War of 1525, miners and peasants out of Salzburg took Schladming and captured the governor, Siegmund von Dietrichstein, before Niklas von Salm retook the town and burned it. Lutheran preachers won most of the valleys after 1530, but Ferdinand II expelled them in 1598, and only crypto-Protestant farmers held out in the high dales until Joseph II's Tolerance Patent of 1781. In 1625 Ferdinand II merged the Erzberg forges into the Innerberger Hauptgewerkschaft, which employed two or three thousand men and produced some five thousand tons of iron a year, the largest ironworks of its age. On 7 April 1797 Napoleon made Judenburg his headquarters and signed an armistice there with Archduke Charles, opening the talks that ended at Leoben.
zh:
尤登堡位于穆尔河畔，地处上施泰尔马克广阔的艾希费尔德谷物盆地边缘，翻越奥布达赫山口通往克恩滕的大路经过这里。1074年的文书首次以「尤登堡市集」（mercatum Judinburch）之名记载这座埃彭施泰因城堡下的市集，地名就来自在此经商的犹太人；1224年它已拥有城市权。尤登堡的财富靠附近艾森埃尔茨的埃尔茨山，那是奥地利最大的铁矿山：12世纪起人们开采山表矿石，河谷里的水力铁锤负责锻冶，1448年的冶铁令划分了销路，内山的铁销往北欧，福德恩贝格的铁经威尼斯运往黎凡特。尤登堡还经营一种叫「施派克」的高山草本植物，在威尼斯当作香水出售，1460年腓特烈三世把这项贸易的垄断权授予该城。它随内奥地利其余土地听命于格拉茨，1444年是一座讲德语的天主教哈布斯堡城市，靠埃尔茨山的铁和艾希费尔德的谷物为生。

15世纪后期战火沿穆尔河而上：1479年匈牙利军队占领上施泰尔马克大片土地，次年奥斯曼袭扰军焚毁尤登堡和布鲁克；1496年马克西米利安一世把犹太人逐出施泰尔马克，城名所自的社群就此终结。1525年农民战争期间，来自萨尔茨堡的矿工和农民攻占施拉德明，俘获总督西格蒙德·冯·迪特里希施泰因，尼克拉斯·冯·萨尔姆随后夺回城池并纵火焚毁。1530年后路德宗牧师争取到多数山谷的信众，费迪南德二世却在1598年将他们驱逐，只有高山谷里的秘密新教农户坚持到1781年约瑟夫二世颁布《宽容敕令》。1625年，费迪南德二世把埃尔茨山各铁厂并入内山总冶铁会，用工两三千人，年产铁约五千吨，是当时世界最大的冶铁企业。1797年4月7日，拿破仑以尤登堡为大本营，在此与卡尔大公签订停战协定，随后的谈判在莱奥本收官。

en:
Ob der Enns, the land above the Enns, runs along the Danube through old border country. The Roman fort of Lentia stood on the hill above the river bend where Linz now stands; the name first appears in 799, and in 1205 or 1206 Duke Leopold VI of Babenberg bought the town and its castle from the lords of Haunsperg. Linz ranked with Enns, Steyr and Wels among the prince's market and toll towns. In 1444 it was a German-speaking Catholic town of the Habsburg Duchy of Austria, its Danube fields shipping grain and river barges carrying the trade of the interior.

Linz Castle became a Habsburg residence: Frederick III rebuilt it as a palace from 1477 and kept his court there from 1489 until his death in 1493, and the Frederick Gate carries the date 1481 and his A.E.I.O.U. cypher. Ferdinand I married Anne of Bohemia and Hungary in the town in 1521, and his son, the future Ferdinand of Tyrol, was born in the palace in 1529. Rudolf II rebuilt the palace from 1600 and added the Rudolf Gate. From 1490 the estates held their regular diets at Linz, making it the capital of the land above the Enns. Protestant teaching entered after 1520 and most townspeople were Protestant within a generation, until Rudolf II and Matthias pressed the Counter-Reformation after 1600. The estates joined the Bohemian revolt in 1619, Bavarian troops occupied the country from 1620, and in 1626 Stefan Fadinger's peasant army besieged Linz for weeks; perhaps 40,000 rebels took up arms and some 12,000 died before the rising collapsed.

From 1612 to 1626 Johannes Kepler was district mathematician at Linz; a printer he brought from Erfurt produced the first book printed in the town in 1615, and his Harmonice Mundi, setting out the third law of planetary motion, appeared here in 1619. His house and press outside the walls burned in the peasant siege, and he moved to Ulm. The wool manufactory founded in 1672 became the largest in the Austrian lands, and the Trinity plague column was raised on the main square between 1717 and 1723. In January 1742 Field Marshal Khevenhüller retook Linz and forced its French garrison, 10,000 strong, to capitulate. In November 1783 Mozart wrote a symphony in four days for Count Thun's concert and premiered it in the town, the work later called the Linz Symphony. In 1809 Masséna stormed the bridge and castle at Ebelsberg below the town. The Linzer Torte, named after the town, is the oldest cake named after a place, and its earliest known recipe, kept in an Admont abbey codex, dates to 1653.
zh:
「恩斯河上游」意为恩斯河以上之地，多瑙河穿过旧日的边疆地带。罗马人的伦特亚堡就建在林茨城址所在的河湾山丘上；林茨一名首见于799年，1205或1206年，巴本堡的利奥波德六世从当地领主手中买下这座城镇和城堡。林茨与恩斯、施泰尔、韦尔斯等同属诸侯的市场与关税城镇。1444年，它是哈布斯堡奥地利公国一座讲德语、奉天主教的城镇，多瑙河畔的农田运出谷物，河上的商船转运内陆货物。

林茨城堡后来成为哈布斯堡的宫廷所在：腓特烈三世1477年起把城堡改建为宫殿，1489年起在此驻跸，直到1493年去世；腓特烈门上镌有1481年的年款和他的「A.E.I.O.U.」花押。1521年，斐迪南一世在城中迎娶波希米亚和匈牙利的安娜，他们的儿子、后来的蒂罗尔的斐迪南1529年生于宫中。鲁道夫二世1600年起重建宫殿，增建鲁道夫门。1490年起，地方等级固定在林茨召开会议，使它成为恩斯河上游的首府。1520年后新教传入，一代人之后多数市民已改宗新教；1600年后鲁道夫二世和马蒂亚斯推行反宗教改革。1619年等级加入波希米亚叛乱，1620年起巴伐利亚军队占领此地；1626年斯特凡·法丁格率农民军围攻林茨数周，起事者约有四万之众，约一万二千人死亡，叛乱终告失败。

1612至1626年，约翰内斯·开普勒在林茨担任地方数学家；他从埃尔福特请来印刷工，1615年印出林茨的第一本书，阐述行星运动第三定律的《世界的和谐》也于1619年在此出版。1626年围城时，他在城外的住宅和印刷所焚毁，随后迁往乌尔姆。1672年创办的毛纺厂后来成为奥地利诸邦最大的工场；1717至1723年，集市广场上立起圣三瘟疫柱。1742年1月，克芬许勒元帅收复林茨，迫使城中一万人的法国守军投降。1783年11月，莫扎特为图恩伯爵的音乐会用四天写成一部交响曲并在此首演，即后来的《林茨交响曲》。1809年，马塞纳强攻林茨下游埃伯斯贝格的桥梁和城堡。以林茨命名的林茨蛋糕是以地名命名的最古老糕点，现存最早的配方出自1653年。

en:
Vienna sits on the Danube just east of the wooded Vienna Hills, on the site of Vindobona, the Roman camp that guarded the Pannonian frontier. In 1155 Henry II of Babenberg made the town his dynasty's residence, and in 1221 it won staple rights, forcing every merchant sailing down the Danube to offer his goods there; Venetian wares and the wine of the surrounding hills filled its market. The Habsburgs took Austria in 1278; Rudolf IV, 'the Founder', chartered the university in 1365 and raised the Gothic nave of St Stephen's, and after Albert V was elected king of the Romans in 1438 Vienna was an imperial residence. In 1444 Frederick III held it, unable to curb roving mercenary bands, and his burghers repeatedly turned to his rivals; even so, tolls and taxes made it the richest city of the Austrian lands.

Vienna became a bishopric in 1469, with St Stephen's as its cathedral. Matthias Corvinus of Hungary starved it into surrender on 1 June 1485 and held it until his death in 1490. Its people turned Protestant early, but the Jesuits Ferdinand I summoned in 1551 made the city a headquarters of the Counter-Reformation. Suleiman the Magnificent besieged it in vain in 1529. The second Ottoman attempt came much closer: on 14 July 1683 Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa invested the city, and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg's garrison held until 12 September, when John III Sobieski of Poland led the allied charge down the Kahlenberg, the largest cavalry charge on record, and overran the Ottoman camp. Legend credits the defender Jerzy Kulczycki with opening the first café from beans the Turks left behind; the first documented one belonged to the Armenian Johannes Diodato in 1685. Plague killed nearly a third of the people in 1679 and returned in 1713.

The rebuilt city took on its baroque face under Fischer von Erlach and Hildebrandt, and Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven made it the capital of European music. Napoleon occupied Vienna in 1805 and 1809; it had become the capital of the new Austrian Empire in 1804, and the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire was proclaimed there in 1806. In 1814–1815 the crowned heads and ministers of Europe gathered at the Congress of Vienna to redraw the map after Napoleon.
zh:
维也纳坐落在多瑙河畔、维也纳林山东麓，罗马人文多博纳军营的故址，当年这座军营守卫着潘诺尼亚边境。1155年，巴本堡家族的亨利二世把王朝驻地迁到此城；1221年维也纳取得堆货权，沿多瑙河而下的商人都必须在城中开市售货，威尼斯来的货物和城郊林丘的葡萄酒挤满市集。哈布斯堡家族1278年入主奥地利，「奠基者」鲁道夫四世1365年创办大学，又为圣斯蒂芬教堂修起哥特式中殿；1438年阿尔布雷希特五世当选罗马人的国王后，维也纳成为皇帝驻地。1444年统治这里的是腓特烈三世，他约束不住四处劫掠的雇佣兵，市民一再倒向他的对手；尽管如此，关税和商税仍使维也纳成为奥地利领地最富庶的城市。

1469年维也纳设立主教区，圣斯蒂芬教堂成为主教座堂。匈牙利国王马加什一世围城断粮，1485年6月1日城降，维也纳被匈牙利占至1490年马加什去世。市民很早就改宗新教，但斐迪南一世1551年召来的耶稣会士把这里变成反宗教改革的大本营。1529年苏莱曼大帝围攻不克。第二次奥斯曼围攻凶险得多：1683年7月14日，大维齐尔卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏围城，守将施塔亨贝格率守军苦撑到9月12日，波兰国王扬·索别斯基率联军从卡伦山冲下，发动有记载以来规模最大的骑兵冲锋，踏破奥斯曼大营。相传突围求援的波兰人库利奇茨基（Jerzy Kulczycki）用土耳其人遗下的咖啡豆开出维也纳第一家咖啡馆；有案可查的第一家则是亚美尼亚人迪奥达托1685年开的。1679年鼠疫夺去近三分之一居民的生命，1713年瘟疫再度袭来。

重建后的维也纳在菲舍尔·冯·埃拉赫与希尔德布兰特手中换上巴洛克面貌，海顿、莫扎特和贝多芬则让它成为欧洲音乐之都。拿破仑1805年和1809年两度占领维也纳；维也纳1804年已成为新奥地利帝国的首都，1806年神圣罗马帝国的终结也在此宣告。1814至1815年，欧洲各国君主与大臣齐聚维也纳会议，在拿破仑之后重划欧洲版图。

en:
This is the far western corner of Hungary, where the wooded Alpine foothills fall to the Rába and the marshy flats of the Moson, beside the road to Vienna. Sopron, the Roman Scarbantia, was the seat of one of the first counties founded under King Stephen I. The Bohemian king Otakar II seized it in 1273, and when the town opened its gates to Ladislaus IV in 1277 it was raised to a free royal town. Kőszeg guards the hill road to the south; Charles I made it a royal town in 1328 after breaking the Kőszegi lords who had run the hills as their own. The towns lived on the grain of the Rába plain, the wine of the Sopron hills and the carrying trade to Vienna. In February 1441 the widowed Queen Elisabeth pawned Sopron and the country round it to the Emperor Frederick III for 8,000 gold florins, so in 1444 the borderland is pledged to the empire and waiting to be redeemed, while the Ottoman threat still lies far to the south.

Matthias Corvinus redeemed the pledge in July 1463, paying 80,000 florins for the return of the Holy Crown and the pawned lands; Kőszeg, lost to Austria in 1445, came back to Hungary only in 1647. Suleiman's host ravaged Sopron in 1529, and three years later it seemed unstoppable on the Vienna road. At Kőszeg, between 5 and 30 August 1532, the Croatian captain Nikola Jurišić and some 800 Hungarians, Croats and Germans beat back nineteen assaults by an army of over 100,000, until Janissary unrest forced the Sultan to turn home; tradition says the last Ottoman troops were withdrawing as the clocks struck eleven, and Kőszeg's church clocks have read eleven o'clock since 1777 in memory of the siege. Refugees from occupied Hungary swelled Sopron, which hosted several national diets, while its German-dominated council struck Hungarian from the town records in 1594. Bocskai's rebels sacked the town in 1605, plague thinned its people, and the great fire of 1676 cleared the ground for a new baroque inner city. In the Rákóczi war Kőszeg served the kuruc rebels as a western stronghold and Sopron fell to János Bottyán. Hungary's first coal mine opened at Brennberg, near Sopron, in 1753.
zh:
这里是匈牙利最西的一角，阿尔卑斯山东麓的林丘在此俯临拉巴河与莫雄沼泽，紧挨通往维也纳的大道。索普朗的前身是罗马城市斯卡尔班提亚，伊什特万一世立国时最早的州治之一便设在这里。1273年波希米亚国王奥托卡二世夺取该城，1277年城市向拉斯洛四世开城，随后受封自由王家城市。克塞格扼守南边穿过丘陵的大道，查理一世1328年翦灭割据丘陵的克塞吉家族后，把它也封为王家城镇。这些城镇靠拉巴平原的谷物、索普朗丘陵的葡萄酒和运往维也纳的转运生意为生。1441年2月，寡后伊丽莎白把索普朗及周边地区以八千金币抵押给皇帝腓特烈三世，因此1444年这片边地押在皇帝手中，等待赎回，而奥斯曼的威胁还远在南方。

1463年7月，马加什国王花八万弗罗林赎回圣冠和这批抵押的土地；1445年落入奥地利之手的克塞格则要到1647年才随和约归还匈牙利。1529年苏莱曼的大军洗劫了索普朗，三年后这支军队在进军维也纳的路上看似无人能挡。1532年8月5日至30日，克罗地亚守将尼古拉·尤里希奇率约八百名匈牙利人、克罗地亚人和德意志人坚守克塞格，击退十万余众的十九次总攻，最后耶尼切里军哗变，苏丹被迫班师；相传最后一支奥斯曼军撤离时钟正敲十一点，自1777年起，克塞格教堂的钟为纪念此役一直停在十一点。匈牙利沦陷区的难民涌入索普朗，城市多次承办国会，德意志裔主导的市政会却于1594年把匈牙利语剔出市政文书。1605年博奇考伊的起义军洗劫该城，瘟疫又使人口大减，1676年的大火之后，人们建起新的巴洛克内城。拉科齐战争中，克塞格是库鲁茨起义军在西部的要塞，索普朗被博特扬·亚诺什攻克。1753年，匈牙利第一座煤矿在索普朗附近的布伦贝格投产。

en:
Split occupies a Dalmatian peninsula and grew up around the palace the Emperor Diocletian built near his home town of Salona for his retirement. Begun around 295, the fortified compound housed his court and garrison; after he abdicated in 305 he lived out his years there, and when the emperors begged him to resume power he answered that the cabbages he planted with his own hands were worth more than a throne. He died in the palace in 312, and his mausoleum later became the Cathedral of St Domnius. The palace also sheltered Julius Nepos, the last Western emperor recognised at Constantinople, who was murdered near Salona in 480. After the Avars and Slavs sacked Salona in 639, Roman refugees moved within the palace walls, bringing the relics of St Domnius, and their town lived on as a commune between Byzantium, Croatia, Hungary and Venice. In 1409 Ladislaus of Naples sold his claim to Dalmatia to Venice for 100,000 ducats, and by 1420 the Republic ruled Split. In 1444 it was a Catholic Venetian port governed by a Venetian count and captain, its people mostly Croatian and its sea trade worth more to Venice than its old privileges.

The city's Renaissance found its voice in Marko Marulić, born in Split in 1450: his Judita, finished in 1501 and printed in Venice in 1521, was the first long epic in Croatian, and contemporaries called him the Christian Virgil. As Ottoman armies reached the hinterland, Split became a fortified border port; the Ottomans took Klis, which commands the pass inland, in 1537, yet the town's merchants sent cloth and salt through that pass to the Ottoman interior, and the port throve on the traffic. Venice won more of the hinterland after the Morean War in 1699. In 1764 Robert Adam published measured drawings of the palace in London, carrying its forms into European neoclassicism. The fall of Venice gave Split to Austria in 1797; Napoleonic France took it in 1805 and placed it in the Illyrian Provinces in 1809, until an Austrian and British force occupied the city in November 1813 and the Congress of Vienna confirmed Austrian rule in 1815.
zh:
斯普利特地处达尔马提亚的一座半岛，整座城围绕戴克里先皇帝为退位养老修建的宫殿发展起来，宫殿就在他的故乡萨罗纳附近。约295年开工的设防宫苑住着他的朝廷和驻军；305年退位后，他在宫中安度余年，后来众帝请他重新掌权，他回答说自己亲手种的卷心菜比皇位更值得留恋。312年他在宫中去世，他的陵寝后来改为圣杜尼乌斯大教堂。宫殿还收留过君士坦丁堡承认的末代西罗马皇帝尤利乌斯·尼波斯，他480年在萨罗纳附近遇刺。639年阿瓦尔人和斯拉夫人洗劫萨罗纳后，罗马难民带着圣杜尼乌斯的遗骨避入宫墙，把宫殿当成了城；此后这里作为自治公社，在拜占庭、克罗地亚、匈牙利和威尼斯之间周旋。1409年，那不勒斯的拉迪斯劳把自己对达尔马提亚的权利以十万杜卡特卖给威尼斯，到1420年斯普利特已受共和国统治。1444年，这里是威尼斯治下的天主教港口，由威尼斯派来的伯爵与长官治理，居民多为克罗地亚人；对威尼斯而言，它的海上贸易比城市的旧特权更要紧。

城市的文艺复兴在马尔科·马鲁利奇笔下发声：他1450年生于斯普利特，1501年写成的《尤迪塔》1521年在威尼斯印行，是第一部长篇克罗地亚语史诗，时人称他为「基督徒中的维吉尔」。奥斯曼大军抵达腹地后，斯普利特变成设防的边境港口；克利斯扼守通往内陆的山口，1537年落入奥斯曼之手，可商人仍把布匹、盐和其他货物经山口运进奥斯曼腹地，港口就靠这路买卖兴旺。1699年摩里亚战争后，威尼斯夺得更多腹地。1764年，苏格兰建筑师罗伯特·亚当在伦敦出版宫殿的实测图集，把戴克里先宫的形制带进欧洲的新古典主义建筑。1797年威尼斯灭亡，斯普利特依《坎波福尔米奥条约》归属奥地利；1805年拿破仑法国取得此地，1809年划入伊利里亚行省；1813年11月奥英联军占领城市，1815年维也纳会议确认奥地利统治。

en:
Ragusa, called Dubrovnik by its Slavic neighbours, occupies a rocky strip of the southern Dalmatian coast, with a sheltered Adriatic harbour and roads running inland toward Balkan mines and caravan routes. Venice controlled the city from 1205 to 1358; after the Treaty of Zadar its patricians kept their councils and laws under the distant Hungarian crown. They bought Primorje in 1399 and took Konavle in the 1420s, giving the small republic farmland and a compact stretch of coast. In 1444 Ragusa was a Catholic Dalmatian city-state ruled by noble councils. It had made short-term agreements with the Ottomans in 1430 and 1442, and its merchants were already turning Ottoman proximity into access to inland markets.

The ruling families backed this diplomacy with practical urban institutions. A pharmacy opened in 1317, a quarantine station followed in 1377, and Onofrio della Cava brought spring water into the city in 1438 and built its two public fountains. The Ottoman treaty of 1458 fixed the larger relationship: Ragusa paid tribute, set at 12,500 gold coins a year from 1481, but kept its laws, flag, courts and low customs duties. Ragusan factors entered Ottoman ports and the Black Sea, while ships carried Balkan metals, hides, wax and salt to Italy and Flanders; some Ragusans reached Portuguese Goa in the 1530s. The city also became a centre of Croatian poetry and drama.

The earthquake of 6 April 1667 ended that prosperous period. Between 3,000 and 5,000 people died, including Rector Simone Ghetaldi, and more than three quarters of the public buildings collapsed. The patriciate rebuilt the city in Baroque form, but Atlantic routes and Ottoman-Venetian wars had reduced its old carrying trade. Ragusa accepted Habsburg protection in 1684 and ceded Neum and Sutorina to the Ottomans in 1699 so that Venetian territory would not surround it by land. Neutrality kept its ships at sea in the eighteenth century, until French troops under General Jacques Lauriston occupied the city in 1806 and Marshal Marmont abolished the republic on 31 January 1808. A Ragusan rising with British help in 1813 opened the way for Austria, whose troops entered in January 1814.
zh:
拉古萨在斯拉夫语中称杜布罗夫尼克，位于南达尔马提亚的岩石海岸，拥有亚得里亚海上的避风港，道路从这里通往巴尔干矿场和商队路线。1205至1358年它受威尼斯控制；《扎达尔条约》后，本地贵族在遥远的匈牙利王权下保留了议会和法律。1399年购得滨海地区，1420年代又取得科纳瓦维，使这个小国获得农田和一段紧凑海岸。1444年的拉古萨是贵族议会治理的天主教达尔马提亚城市国家。它已在1430和1442年同奥斯曼订立短期协议，本国商人也把邻近奥斯曼变成进入内陆市场的便利。

统治家族用实用的城市制度配合外交。药房1317年开业，检疫站1377年设立，属于欧洲最早的一批；奥诺弗里奥·德拉·卡瓦1438年把泉水引入城中，并修建两座公共喷泉。1458年的奥斯曼条约确定了双方关系：拉古萨纳贡，1481年起年贡为一万二千五百枚金币，但保留法律、旗帜、法庭和低关税。拉古萨商人得以进入奥斯曼港口和黑海，商船把巴尔干金属、兽皮、蜂蜡和盐运往意大利与佛兰德，1530年代还有人抵达葡萄牙治下的果阿。城市也成为克罗地亚诗歌和戏剧的中心。

1667年4月6日的地震结束了这段富裕时期。三千至五千人遇难，时任执政官西莫内·盖塔尔迪也在其中，四分之三以上的公共建筑倒塌。贵族们以巴洛克风格重建城市，但大西洋商路和奥斯曼—威尼斯战争已经削弱了旧日的转运贸易。1684年拉古萨接受哈布斯堡保护，1699年把内乌姆和苏托里纳割给奥斯曼，以免陆上边界全被威尼斯领土包围。18世纪的中立政策让船只仍能航行，直到雅克·洛里斯顿将军率法军在1806年入城，马尔蒙元帅于1808年1月31日废除共和国。1813年，拉古萨人在英国帮助下起义，随后在1814年1月为奥地利军队打开道路。

en:
Zeta covers the Zeta valley, the Morača lowlands and the approaches to Lake Skadar, guarded by the Crnojević fortress of Žabljak. It had been a Nemanjić crown land and then the realm of the Balšići before it passed to the Serbian Despotate in 1421. As Despot Đurađ Branković's authority weakened, the local vojvoda Stefan Crnojević moved from Despotate service to an alliance with Stjepan Vukčić Kosača and then to Venetian suzerainty, and on 2 March 1444 he and his sons joined Skanderbeg's League of Lezhë. In that year Zeta was an Orthodox Serbian pastoral country of clans, pastures and livestock, with Stefan already its real master; he returned to the Despot's suzerainty only in 1448.

Stefan spent his last years under Venetian supremacy, and his son Ivan fought the Ottomans until they took Žabljak while besieging Shkodër; Ivan then moved his court to Cetinje beneath Mount Lovćen and founded the monastery there. Under his son Đurađ the monks of Cetinje, led by Hieromonk Makarije, ran a printing press, and the Oktoih of 1494, printed in red and black, became the first book in Serbian Cyrillic; four more liturgical books followed before the Ottomans took direct control in 1496 and organised Zeta as a vilayet within the Sanjak of Skadar. The mountain clans kept their arms and most of their autonomy, and in 1516 they elected Bishop Vavila at Cetinje, beginning the rule of the prince-bishops; the Ottomans for their part set up a Sanjak of Montenegro under Ivan's Islamized son Staniša, called Skender. The clans defeated the expeditions sent against them at Lješkopolje and under Arslan Pasha, but the lowland forts stayed in Ottoman hands. In 1697 Danilo Petrović became bishop and turned to Russia for arms and money; he was wounded at Carev Laz in 1712, and two years later Ottoman troops burned the Cetinje monastery. Petar I, bishop from 1784, gave Montenegro its first law code, and in 1821 he led the mountain clans while Ottoman garrisons still held Žabljak and the lowland approaches.
zh:
泽塔领有泽塔河谷、莫拉查低地和斯库台湖附近地带，由茨尔诺耶维奇家族的扎布利亚克要塞扼守。这里曾是尼曼雅王朝的王室领地，后来成为巴尔希奇家族的疆土，1421年转归塞尔维亚专制国。随着专制公久拉吉·布兰科维奇的权威衰落，本地军事首领斯特凡·茨尔诺耶维奇从专制君主麾下转而结盟斯特耶潘·武克契奇·科萨察，随后接受威尼斯宗主权，并于1444年3月2日率诸子加入斯坎德培领导的莱什联盟。在这一年，泽塔是一片由部族、牧场和牧群支撑的东正教塞尔维亚土地，真正的主人已是斯特凡；他直到1448年才重新承认专制公的宗主权。

斯特凡在威尼斯的最高权威下度过晚年，他的儿子伊万与奥斯曼人苦战，土耳其人围攻斯库台时夺取了扎布利亚克；伊万随后把宫廷迁到洛夫琴山下的采蒂涅，在那里修建了修道院。他的儿子久拉吉在位时，以修道司祭马卡里耶为首的修士们在采蒂涅办起印刷所，1494年红黑两色印成的《奥克托伊赫》成为第一部塞尔维亚西里尔文印本书；此后又印出四部礼仪用书，1496年奥斯曼人直接接管，把泽塔编为斯库台桑贾克境内的维拉耶特。山地部族保留了武装和大部分自治权，1516年在采蒂涅选出瓦维拉主教，开启了主教治国的传统；奥斯曼人则设立黑山桑贾克，交给伊万改宗伊斯兰教的儿子斯塔尼沙（斯肯德）管辖。部族在列什科波利耶和对阿尔斯兰帕夏的作战中击败前来讨伐的军队，但低地堡垒始终在奥斯曼手中。1697年，达尼洛·彼得罗维奇成为主教，转而向俄国求取军火和金钱；1712年他在察雷夫拉兹受伤，两年后奥斯曼军队烧毁了采蒂涅修道院。佩塔尔一世1784年就任主教，为黑山制定了第一部法典；1821年，他领导着山地部族，扎布利亚克和低地通道仍由奥斯曼军队驻守。

en:
Hum, the medieval Zahumlje, is the hilly country astride the upper Neretva, between the Adriatic shore and the mining towns of central Bosnia. Ragusan traders drove pack-trains up its valley with salt and coastal goods, and Orthodox, Bosnian-Church and Catholic families lived intermingled, the Franciscans having come in the 1340s. The local lords were the Kosača, whose cliff-top fortress of Blagaj looked down on a wooden bridge over the Neretva guarded by two towers; the small settlement at the crossing did not yet bear the name Mostar. In 1444 the land belonged to Stjepan Vukčić Kosača, Grand Duke of Bosnia, who ruled it as its master and had lately backed the anti-king Radivoj against King Tomaš.

Four years later Stjepan styled himself herceg, the duke, of Saint Sava, and his dominion came to be called Herzegovina. In 1452 his son Vladislav rose against him and seized Blagaj together with the two bridge towers, the first written trace of the bridge-town. The Ottomans overran Bosnia in 1463, Stjepan died in 1466, and about 1468 the crossing fell to them; they called it Köprühisar and laid out a craftsmen's čaršija and residential mahalas around it, and by the early sixteenth century it was the seat of the Sanjak of Herzegovina. The town took its name from its bridge-keepers, the mostari. In 1566, on Suleiman the Magnificent's order, Mimar Hayruddin, a pupil of Sinan, replaced the wooden span with a single stone arch leaping twenty metres above the river from rock to rock. Evliya Çelebi, who said he had passed through sixteen countries, wrote that he had never seen so high a bridge. By then Mostar held some 10,000 people, before the eighteenth century brought long stagnation.
zh:
胡姆古称扎胡姆列，是内雷特瓦河上游的丘陵之地，夹在亚得里亚海岸与波斯尼亚中部的矿镇之间。拉古萨商人赶着驮队沿河谷北上，运去食盐和沿海货物；东正教徒、波斯尼亚教会信徒和天主教徒杂处而居，方济各会修士1340年代已到此地。本地的主人是科萨察家族，他们在崖顶的要塞布拉加伊俯瞰着内雷特瓦河上一座由双塔守护的木桥；渡口小镇当时还没有莫斯塔尔之名。1444年，这片土地归于波斯尼亚大公斯捷潘·武克契奇·科萨察，他以主人的身份统治胡姆，前不久还支持伪王拉迪沃伊与国王托马什争位。

四年后，斯捷潘自称圣萨瓦的「赫尔采格」（公爵），他的领地后来被称作黑塞哥维那。1452年，其子弗拉迪斯拉夫起兵反叛，夺取布拉加伊和桥头双塔，这是这座河桥镇最早的文字记载。奥斯曼1463年攻灭波斯尼亚，斯捷潘于1466年去世，约1468年渡口也落入土耳其人之手；他们称它克普吕希萨尔，在桥周围辟出匠人集市和居住的教坊街区，到16世纪初它已是黑塞哥维那桑贾克的治所。城名来自守桥人「莫斯塔里」。1566年，奉苏莱曼大帝之命，锡南的门生米马尔·哈伊鲁丁把木桥换成一座独拱石桥，自河面凌空二十米，从一岸岩石跨到另一岸岩石。自称走遍十六国的旅行家爱维亚·瑟勒布写道，他从未见过这么高的桥。此时莫斯塔尔已有约一万居民，随后的18世纪是漫长的停滞。

en:
The lowlands where the Usora runs into the Bosna were the northern approach to the Bosnian kingdom, covering the medieval lands of Usora and Soli. Soli, 'the salts' in the old Slavic tongue, took its name from the brine springs around the later town of Tuzla, and the salt was carried down the Bosna valley; Usora, ruled from the cliff fortress of Srebrenik, is first named in a Hungarian bull of 1244 and was reclaimed by Stjepan II Kotromanić in 1324. Below them stood the royal fortress of Doboj, guarding the road from the Hungarian border into the kingdom. In the spring of 1415 its walls were rebuilt in Gothic fashion, with a five-storey donjon and a cannon platform, while Ragusan engineers laid its cistern. That August, beneath the fortress, the Bosnian army of Hrvoje Vukčić Hrvatinić and Isa-Beg's Ottoman horsemen fell on some 15,000 Hungarians under John Garai and routed them, carrying off much of the Hungarian nobility for ransom. In 1444 King Tomaš still ruled the region, and the keeps of Doboj and Srebrenik watched a frontier pressed between Hungarian Syrmia and the Ottomans.

The kingdom collapsed in May 1463: the last duke of Usora, Tvrtko Stančić, fell fighting, and King Stjepan Tomašević was put to death. The northern forts held out a little longer, and Doboj opened its gates without a fight in early summer 1476. In the summer of 1490 the Ottomans rebuilt its fortress, fifteen hundred men working for some fifty days under the master builder Ibrahim, and stationed a permanent garrison there from 1503; official records count at least eighteen times the place was burned or plundered. At the old salt springs, Soli became the garrison town of Tuzla, its brine a steady source of imperial tax. The long Austro-Ottoman border wars then beat upon the valley: after Zenta, Eugene of Savoy's raiders crossed the Bosna in 1697 on their march to Sarajevo, and in 1716 the Austrians burned Doboj town without taking its keep. The treaties of Belgrade in 1739 and Sistova in 1791 restored the frontier each time, leaving the Doboj captaincy in Ottoman hands.
zh:
乌索拉河注入波斯纳河的低地，是波斯尼亚王国的北大门，涵盖中世纪的乌索拉与索利两块土地。索利在古斯拉夫语中意为「盐」，得名于后来图兹拉城一带的盐泉，所产食盐沿波斯纳河谷外运；乌索拉以悬崖要塞斯雷布雷尼克为治所，其名首见于1244年的匈牙利诏书，1324年由斯捷潘二世·科特罗马尼奇收复。下游多博伊的王家要塞扼守着从匈牙利边境进入王国的道路。1415年春，城墙按哥特样式重修，建起五层高的主楼和炮台，蓄水池由拉古萨工程师修造。同年8月，就在要塞之下，大公爵赫尔沃耶·武克契奇·赫尔瓦蒂尼奇的波斯尼亚军队与伊萨贝伊的奥斯曼骑兵夹击约翰·加拉伊率领的约一万五千匈牙利军，将其击溃，大批匈牙利贵族被掳走勒索赎金。1444年，托马什国王仍统治着这片地方，多博伊和斯雷布雷尼克的城堡监视着夹在匈牙利锡尔米亚与奥斯曼之间的边境。

1463年5月王国倾覆：末代乌索拉公爵特尔特科·斯坦契奇战死，国王斯捷潘·托马舍维奇也被处死。北方诸城又坚守了一段时日，多博伊于1476年初夏不战开城。1490年夏，奥斯曼人重修要塞，匠师易卜拉欣指挥约一千五百人施工五十天，1503年起常驻守军；据记载，这座城堡历史上至少十八次遭焚毁或劫掠。古老盐泉上的索利变成驻军城镇图兹拉，盐税成为帝国一笔稳定的进项。随后漫长的奥土边境战争反复冲刷这条河谷：森塔大捷后，欧根亲王的突袭部队1697年越过波斯纳河，向萨拉热窝进军；1716年奥地利人烧毁多博伊城镇，却未能攻下城堡。1739年的《贝尔格莱德条约》和1791年的《锡斯托瓦条约》两度恢复旧边界，多博伊防区始终留在奥斯曼手中。

en:
Smederevo lies on the right bank of the Danube below Belgrade, where the Jezava joins the river. When Belgrade went back to Hungary in 1427, Despot Đurađ Branković chose an empty stretch of riverbank for a new capital and from 1428 raised a vast triangle of walls between the Danube and the Jezava, one of the largest water-girt fortresses in the Balkans; its inner court with the palace was ready by 1430. The new court bound his family to both neighbouring powers: his daughter Mara was married to Sultan Murad II, and in 1435 he signed a treaty of friendship with Venice in the fortress audience hall. Marriage did not save the town, for Murad's army besieged it in 1439 and hunger forced surrender after three months, while his sons Grgur and Stefan were carried off and blinded in 1441. The Peace of Szeged restored Smederevo in 1444, when it was again the Orthodox Serbian capital on the Danube frontier, its grain fields feeding the border between Hungary and the Ottomans.

The long forced labour on the walls entered folk memory through Đurađ's wife Jerina, born Irene Kantakouzene, whom tradition blamed for the levies and taxes, calling her Prokleta Jerina, Damned Jerina. The walls repelled Mehmed II in 1454 and 1456, and around 1449 the Hungarian commander John Hunyadi was held in the fortress dungeons until ransomed. In 1459 the town surrendered without a fight under Stephen Tomašević, and the medieval Serbian state ended with it. The Ottomans made Smederevo a garrison town and the seat of the Sanjak of Smederevo, adding four low artillery towers in 1480. After Belgrade fell in 1521 it ceased to be a front line and grew into a Danubian market. It changed hands in the later Habsburg-Ottoman wars, and during the First Serbian Uprising the rebel council sat there from 1805 to 1807. Ottoman rule returned in 1813; the Second Uprising of 1815 opened the road to autonomy, though an Ottoman garrison remained behind the walls in 1821.
zh:
斯梅代雷沃位于贝尔格莱德下游的多瑙河右岸，耶扎瓦河在此汇入多瑙河。1427年贝尔格莱德归还匈牙利后，专制公久拉吉·布兰科维奇选中一段空旷河岸另建新都，1428年起在多瑙河与耶扎瓦河之间筑起三角形的庞大城墙，是巴尔干规模最大的环水要塞之一；带宫殿的内廷1430年落成。这座新城把他的家族同两个强邻绑在一起：女儿马拉嫁给苏丹穆拉德二世，1435年他又在要塞觐见厅与威尼斯签订友好条约。联姻没能保住城市，穆拉德的军队1439年来攻，三个月后城中因饥荒投降，他的儿子格古尔和斯特凡被掳走，1441年被刺瞎双目。1444年《塞格德和约》把斯梅代雷沃归还塞尔维亚，这一年它重新成为多瑙河防线上的东正教塞尔维亚都城，周围粮田供养着匈牙利与奥斯曼之间的边境。

长年筑城的苦役留在了民间记忆里：相传久拉吉的妻子耶里娜（本名伊琳娜·坎塔库泽娜）强征夫役、横征暴敛，百姓称她为「受诅咒的耶里娜」。城墙1454年和1456年两度挡住穆罕默德二世；约在1449年，匈牙利名将匈雅提·亚诺什曾被关在要塞地牢中，直到匈牙利人付赎金赎出。1459年，城市在斯特凡·托马舍维奇手中不战而降，中世纪塞尔维亚国家随之告终。奥斯曼人把斯梅代雷沃变成驻军城镇和斯梅代雷沃桑贾克的治所，1480年又增建四座低矮的炮兵塔楼。1521年贝尔格莱德陷落后，它不再是前线，发展为多瑙河畔的集镇。此后在哈布斯堡与奥斯曼的战争中数度易手，第一次塞尔维亚起义时，起义政权的政务会议1805年至1807年设于此城。1813年奥斯曼统治恢复，1815年第二次起义为自治打开道路，但到1821年，城墙之内还驻着奥斯曼军队。

en:
Corfu, called Kerkyra by its Greek inhabitants, guards the mouth of the Adriatic, a day's sail from the Epirote coast; the walled town takes its western name from the twin peaks of its citadel, Korypho in Greek. After Roman and Byzantine centuries it passed from the despots of Epirus to the Angevins of Naples, and in 1386 the island, left without a ruler, offered itself to Venice, which acquired formal sovereignty in 1401. The Republic made the town its chief naval base in the Ionian Sea, the 'Door of Venice'; Catholic nobles sent from Venice ruled an Orthodox Greek people of fishermen, sailors and vine-growers who shipped wine, oil and raisins into the Adriatic. An Ottoman raid under Ali Bey was beaten off in 1431, and in 1444 Corfu was the Republic's forward bulwark against the Turkish fleet.

The relics of Saint Spyridon reached Corfu after Constantinople fell in 1453, brought by a Corfiote monk named Kalohairetis, and the islanders came to credit their patron with delivering the town from plague and with shielding it in its sieges. In August 1537 an Ottoman army of 25,000 landed, ravaged the island and carried off some 20,000 captives, yet the citadel held through twelve days of assault; Ottoman landings in 1571 and 1573 also failed, and the Venetians raised the New Fortress to secure the town. The last great siege came in 1716, when 33,000 Ottomans landed against about 8,000 defenders under Count von der Schulenburg and were driven off after twenty-two days; a story ran through the Turkish ranks that a monk with a flaming torch threatened the assault columns, and Venice ordered an annual litany on 11 August. Vivaldi wrote his oratorio Juditha triumphans for the victory, and the Teatro San Giacomo, opened in 1693 and staging opera from 1733, was the first theatre and opera house of modern Greece. Venetian rule ended with the treaty of Campo Formio in 1797; after French and Russo-Ottoman occupations and the short-lived Septinsular Republic, Corfu became in 1815 the seat of the British protectorate of the United States of the Ionian Islands.
zh:
科孚，希腊居民称之为克基拉，扼守亚得里亚海入口，与伊庇鲁斯海岸仅一日航程；这座有城墙的城镇，西文名称得自要塞的双峰，希腊语称「科里福」。历经罗马与拜占庭的漫长统治后，它从伊庇鲁斯专制公之手转入那不勒斯安茹家族治下；1386年，失去宗主的科孚自行归附威尼斯，威尼斯于1401年取得正式主权。共和国把此城经营为伊奥尼亚海最重要的海军基地，号称「威尼斯之门」；来自威尼斯的天主教贵族，统治着由渔民、水手和葡萄农组成的希腊东正教居民，岛上出产的葡萄酒、橄榄油和葡萄干行销亚得里亚海。1431年阿里贝伊率领的一次奥斯曼袭掠被击退，1444年的科孚正是共和国抵御土耳其舰队的前沿屏障。

君士坦丁堡1453年陷落后，一位科孚修士把圣斯皮里东的遗骨带到岛上，岛民逐渐相信这位主保圣人曾使城镇免于瘟疫，又在历次围攻中护佑城池。1537年8月，两万五千奥斯曼军队登陆蹂躏全岛，掳走约两万人，但要塞在十二天的猛攻中守住；1571和1573年奥斯曼军两度登陆又告失败，威尼斯人随后增筑新要塞。最后一次大围攻在1716年：三万三千奥斯曼大军登陆，舒伦堡伯爵麾下约八千守军迎战，二十二天后将其击退；土耳其营中传言，有个手持火炬的修士威吓攻城队伍，威尼斯遂定每年8月11日举行巡礼。维瓦尔第为这场胜利写下清唱剧《犹滴凯旋》；圣贾科莫剧院1693年开幕、1733年起上演歌剧，是近代希腊第一座剧院兼歌剧院。威尼斯统治随1797年《坎波福尔米奥条约》告终，历经法国与俄土占领和短命的七岛共和国后，科孚于1815年成为英国保护国爱奥尼亚群岛合众国的首府。

en:
Vlorë sits on one of the Adriatic's best natural anchorages, a wide bay beneath the Ceraunian heights, and above the town the castle of Kaninë commands the road from the coast into the interior. Greeks, Romans, Normans, Venetians and the Angevin kings of Naples held it in turn, and after Stefan Dušan's Serbian conquest of 1345–46 it became the capital of the Principality of Valona, whose despot John Komnenos Asen grew rich on the trade passing to Venice and Ragusa. Balša II, who held the city by marriage, fell fighting the Ottomans at Savra in 1385; his widow Comita and daughter Rugina offered Vlorë to Venice more than once and were refused, and the sultan's troops took it in 1417. An Albanian rising drove out the garrison in 1432, but by 1444 Vlorë, now Avlonya, was again an Ottoman sanjak centre and naval port, its Orthodox Albanian townsmen shipping inland wool and bay salt to Italy.

The port drew merchants. The Ottomans settled a Jewish community here from 1426, later joined by exiles from Spain, and the censuses of 1506 and 1520 counted 528 families, about 2,600 people, handling spices, leather and mohair between Italy and Istanbul, a trade that withered after Lepanto in 1571. The local Vloraj family held the sanjakbey's office almost without a break from 1481 into the eighteenth century. Suleiman the Magnificent had the octagonal sea-fortress built in 1531, and the Muradie Mosque went up in 1542. A Venetian fleet took Vlorë in 1690 and lost it to an Ottoman siege the next year, when the town held some 10,000 inhabitants. In 1812 Ali Pasha of Ioannina seized it after the murder of the local bey, and in 1821 the bay formed the Adriatic flank of his pashalik.
zh:
发罗拉坐落在亚得里亚海最好的天然锚地之一，喀罗尼亚山岭下一处宽阔海湾，城后高地上的卡尼纳城堡扼守着海滨通往内陆的道路。希腊人、罗马人、诺曼人、威尼斯人和那不勒斯的安茹王室先后占据此地；1345至1346年斯特凡·杜尚的塞尔维亚军队攻下它之后，这里成为发罗拉公国的都城，专制君主约翰·科穆宁·阿森靠往来威尼斯和拉古萨的贸易致富。凭姻亲入主的巴尔沙二世1385年在萨夫拉战死对奥斯曼的战役，遗孀科米塔和女儿鲁吉娜多次提出把发罗拉献给威尼斯均遭拒绝，苏丹的军队最终于1417年入城。1432年阿尔巴尼亚起义者逐出了守军，但到1444年，改称阿夫洛尼亚的发罗拉重新成为奥斯曼的桑扎克中心和军港，信东正教的阿尔巴尼亚市民把内地羊毛和海湾盐装船运往意大利。

港口吸引了商人。奥斯曼人1426年起把一个犹太商人群体安置于此，后来又有西班牙流亡者加入，1506年和1520年的普查登记了528户、约2600人，在意大利与伊斯坦布尔之间贩运香料、皮革和马海毛，这门生意在1571年勒班陀海战后凋敝。当地的发罗拉家族自1481年起几乎不间断地把持桑扎克贝伊之职，直到18世纪。苏莱曼一世1531年下令修建八角形海堡，穆拉迪耶清真寺1542年落成。1690年威尼斯舰队拿下发罗拉，次年就在奥斯曼围城中失守，当时城中约有一万人。1812年，当地贝伊遇害，约阿尼纳的阿里帕夏夺取此城；1821年，这片海湾构成他帕夏领地的亚得里亚海侧翼。

en:
Epirus is the mountain country between the Pindus range and the Ionian Sea, and Janina is its stronghold, built on a rocky promontory that juts into Lake Pamvotida, with the small island in the lake within sight of the castle walls. After 1204 Michael I Komnenos Doukas made the city a capital of the Despotate of Epirus and settled refugees from the fallen Constantinople; Serb lords and the Italian Esau de' Buondelmonti held it in turn, and in 1411 the citizens called in Carlo I Tocco, count of Cephalonia, who reunited the Epirote realm and died in Janina in 1429. When his bastard sons fell out and appealed to the Ottomans, the city opened its gates to Sinan Pasha on 9 October 1430, after he promised to respect its churches and property. In 1444 Janina was the seat of an Ottoman sanjak, its Greek Orthodox burghers and the Vlach shepherds of the high pastures alike living by the wool shipped out through the Adriatic ports.

The peace held until 1611, when Dionysius the Philosopher, a deposed bishop of Larissa, led a peasant march on the city and the janissary commander Aslan Pasha crushed it; Christians were expelled from the citadel and the Aslan Pasha Mosque was raised on the ground they left. Janina nonetheless grew into the foremost school city of the Greek world: the Maroutsaia school, where Eugenios Voulgaris taught, drew students from across the Balkans, and Janina merchants paid for four Greek printing houses in Venice. In 1788 Ali Pasha of Tepelenë, the Albanian chieftain called the Lion of Yanina, made the citadel the capital of a pashalik that stretched from Albania down to the Gulf of Corinth, and Karaiskakis, Androutsos and Botsaris all served at his court before they led the Greek revolt. Sultan Mahmud II declared him a traitor in 1820 and sent an army to besiege Janina; Ali withdrew to the old monasteries on the lake island, and the siege was still running when the Greek revolution broke out in 1821.
zh:
伊庇鲁斯是品都斯山脉与伊奥尼亚海之间的山地，重镇约阿尼纳建在伸入帕姆沃蒂达湖的岩岬上，湖中的小岛与城堡墙头遥遥相望。1204年后，米哈伊尔一世·科穆宁·杜卡斯把此城建为伊庇鲁斯专制侯国的都城，安置从沦陷的君士坦丁堡逃出的难民；塞尔维亚王公和意大利人埃索·德·布翁代尔蒙蒂先后据有该城。1411年，市民请来凯法洛尼亚伯爵卡洛一世·托科，他重新统一伊庇鲁斯旧疆，1429年在约阿尼纳去世。他的庶子们争位，向奥斯曼人求援，1430年10月9日，辛南帕夏承诺尊重教堂与财产，城市开城。1444年的约阿尼纳是奥斯曼桑贾克的治所，希腊东正教徒市民和高山牧场上的弗拉赫牧人都靠羊毛为生，羊毛经亚得里亚海各港外销。

太平维持到1611年：被废黜的拉里萨主教「哲人」狄奥尼修率领农民向约阿尼纳进军，禁卫军指挥官阿斯兰帕夏将其镇压，基督徒被逐出城堡，腾出的地方建起了阿斯兰帕夏清真寺。尽管如此，约阿尼纳仍成长为希腊世界首屈一指的学堂之城：叶夫根尼奥斯·武尔加里斯执教过的马鲁齐亚学校吸引着整个巴尔干的学生，约阿尼纳商人还出资在威尼斯办了四家希腊文印刷厂。1788年，人称「约阿尼纳之狮」的阿尔巴尼亚首领台佩莱纳的阿里帕夏把城堡作为帕夏辖区的都城，势力从阿尔巴尼亚一直延伸到科林斯湾，卡赖斯卡基斯、安德鲁措斯、博察里斯都曾在他的宫廷效力，后来成了希腊起义的领袖。1820年，苏丹马哈茂德二世宣布他为叛逆，发兵围攻约阿尼纳；阿里退守湖中小岛上的古老修道院，围城仍在继续，1821年希腊革命已经爆发。

en:
Mystras occupies a steep spur of Taygetus above the Spartan plain, its Frankish keep crowning the slope and the walled town climbing below it. William II of Villehardouin, prince of Achaea, built the fortress in 1248-49 after subduing Laconia; it passed to Byzantium in 1262, and from 1349 was the capital of the Despotate of the Morea, the appanage of imperial sons. The Palace of the Despots stood on its terrace, and the churches and monasteries of Hagia Sophia, the Pantanassa and the Peribleptos were covered in frescoes. Gemistos Plethon taught here for decades and tutored Despot Theodore II; at the Council of Florence in 1438-39 his lectures on Plato were heard by Italian humanists, among them Marsilio Ficino, who called him the second Plato. In 1444 the despot holding court at Mystras was Constantine Palaiologos, the future Emperor Constantine XI; the town was a Greek Orthodox stronghold while Venetian harbours and Ottoman armies ringed the peninsula.

When Constantine left for Constantinople in 1449, the despotate went to his quarrelling brothers, above all Demetrios Palaiologos, its last ruler here. Mehmed II overran the Morea after the imperial capital fell, and Demetrios surrendered Mystras in 1460. Plethon had died there a few years before, and in 1466 his Italian followers, led by Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta, took his bones from the town and buried them in the Tempio Malatestiano at Rimini. Under the Ottomans the town became the seat of the sanjak of Mezistre; western travellers, finding it inhabited above the empty Spartan plain, mistook it for ancient Sparta. A Venetian army took it in the Morean War and held the town from 1687 to 1715. In 1770 Mystras joined the Orlov revolt, and Ottoman Albanian troops sacked it and killed the metropolitan Ananias, who had sheltered several of their men during the rising. Much of the town was left in ruins and its people drifted away over the following decades.
zh:
米斯特拉斯踞守塔伊盖托斯山伸入斯巴达平原的一道陡峭支脉，法兰克式主堡高居坡顶，带城墙的城区沿坡而下。亚该亚亲王纪尧姆二世·德·维拉杜安平定拉科尼亚后，于1248至1249年间修筑这座要塞；1262年它转入拜占庭之手，1349年起成为皇子封地摩里亚专制国的都城。专制君主的宫殿坐落在台地上，圣索菲亚等教堂和修道院布满壁画。格弥斯托士·卜列东在此讲学数十年，曾教授专制君主狄奥多尔二世；1438至1439年的佛罗伦萨公会议上，他讲论柏拉图，马尔西利奥·费奇诺等意大利人文主义者在座，费奇诺称他为「第二个柏拉图」。1444年，在米斯特拉斯临朝的专制君主是君士坦丁·巴列奥略，即后来的皇帝君士坦丁十一世；威尼斯人的港口和奥斯曼军队环伺半岛，这座城仍是希腊东正教的重镇。

1449年君士坦丁前往君士坦丁堡即位后，专制国落入他彼此不和的诸弟手中，其中末代统治者是季米特里奥斯·巴列奥略。帝都陷落后，穆罕默德二世横扫摩里亚，季米特里奥斯于1460年献城。卜列东几年前已在此去世，1466年，他的一批意大利追随者在西吉斯蒙多·潘多尔福·马拉泰斯塔带领下从城中取走遗骨，葬入里米尼的马拉泰斯塔圣殿。奥斯曼时期，这里成为迈齐斯特雷桑贾克的治所；西方旅人见它仍有人烟、高踞空旷的斯巴达平原之上，常把它错当作古斯巴达。摩里亚战争中，威尼斯军队攻占此城，占据至1715年。1770年，米斯特拉斯响应奥尔洛夫起义，奥斯曼阿尔巴尼亚部队洗劫全城，杀死了曾在起事时庇护过若干阿尔巴尼亚人的都主教阿纳尼亚斯。城区大半化为废墟，此后数十年间居民陆续迁离。

en:
Athens is the plain and harbour district of Attica, with the Acropolis rising between the town and Piraeus, called Porto Leone in 1444. Attic grain moved through that harbour, while the citadel on the rock controlled town and port. Trade was modest; the ancient buildings above the houses set the town apart. The Parthenon had served as a Greek temple and Orthodox church before the dukes created by the Fourth Crusade made it their cathedral and palace. Otto de la Roche, a Burgundian knight, took the Acropolis in 1205 and founded the Duchy of Athens. In 1311 Walter V of Brienne tried to dismiss his unpaid Catalan Company after hiring it against Epirus; the mercenaries killed him and much of the Frankish cavalry in a battle in southern Thessaly and ruled Attica for decades. The Florentine Acciaioli family seized the duchy in 1388. In 1444 Nerio II Acciaioli ruled Greek Orthodox townsmen from the rock; after campaigning with Constantine Palaiologos, Despot of the Morea, he lost Thebes and became Constantine's tributary.

Nerio died in 1451, leaving a child duke under the regency of his widow Chiara Zorzi, and Acciaioli feuds opened the way for Ottoman intervention. In 1456 Turahanoğlu Ömer Bey overran Boeotia and the lower town of Athens; in 1458 Mehmed II came to Athens and received the Acropolis. He was struck by the ancient monuments and issued a firman against looting them, while the Parthenon became the city's main mosque. Athens shrank into a provincial market town. From the reign of Ahmed I it was assigned to the imperial harem and administered through the Kizlar Agha, chief black eunuch of the palace. Ottoman garrisons stored gunpowder on the Acropolis.

Lightning detonated a store in the Propylaea in 1640. On 26 September 1687, during Francesco Morosini's Venetian siege, a shell struck the Parthenon magazine and destroyed much of the temple. The Venetians held the ruins for only a few months before abandoning Athens in April 1688, and Ottoman rule returned until the Greek rising of April 1821. The Athenians took up arms and the Ottoman garrison withdrew into the Acropolis, beginning another siege on the same rock.
zh:
雅典是阿提卡的平原与港口地带，卫城耸立于城镇和比雷埃夫斯之间；1444年时，比雷埃夫斯称作「狮子港」。阿提卡谷物从这个海港运出，岩石上的要塞则控制着城镇与港口。这里贸易规模不大，真正醒目的是屋舍上方的古代建筑。帕特农神庙曾是希腊神庙和东正教教堂，第四次十字军后建立的公爵政权又把它改作主教座堂和府邸。1205年，勃艮第骑士奥顿·德·拉罗什占据卫城，建立雅典公国。1311年，布里耶讷的戈蒂埃五世雇加泰罗尼亚佣兵团对伊庇鲁斯作战，却想在欠饷情况下将其遣散；佣兵团在色萨利南部的一场会战中杀死他和大批法兰克骑兵，随后统治阿提卡数十年。1388年，佛罗伦萨的阿奇亚奥里家族夺取公国。1444年，内里奥二世·阿奇亚奥里在卫城上统治信奉东正教的希腊市民；他随摩里亚专制君主君士坦丁·巴列奥略出兵后丢掉底比斯，成了君士坦丁的纳贡者。

内里奥二世1451年去世，幼子在遗孀基亚拉·佐尔齐摄政下继位，阿奇亚奥里家族的内斗给了奥斯曼干预的机会。1456年，图拉汗奥卢·厄梅尔贝伊攻占维奥蒂亚和雅典外城；1458年穆罕默德二世亲临雅典，接受卫城投降。他为古代建筑所动，下令不得劫掠破坏，帕特农神庙则被改作城内主清真寺。雅典缩成一个行省集镇。艾哈迈德一世在位以后，城市被划给苏丹后宫，由宫中的黑人宦官总管吉兹拉尔阿迦管辖。奥斯曼守军还把火药储存在卫城上。

1640年，雷击引爆山门里的火药。1687年9月26日，弗朗切斯科·莫罗西尼率威尼斯军队围攻卫城，一发炮弹击中帕特农神庙内的火药库，神庙大半被毁。威尼斯人只占据废墟数月，1688年4月便弃城撤走，奥斯曼又统治到1821年。当年4月雅典人举事，奥斯曼守军退入卫城，同一块岩石上再次展开围城。

en:
Thessaly is the great plain enclosed by the Pindus, Ossa and Olympus and watered by the Peneius, whose grain, horses and wool were famous long before the Ottomans arrived. At its western edge stands Trikala, and above the town rise the rock pillars of Meteora, where hermits settled in the ninth century and monks began to build monasteries in the fourteenth; Athanasios the Meteorite founded the Great Meteoron in 1356 under the protection of the Serbian emperor Simeon Uroš, and in time twenty-four houses perched on the pillars, reachable only by jointed ladders or the rope net that hauled visitors up the cliff. The Ottomans took Trikala in 1395, and in the 1420s Turahan Bey made the town, called Tırhala, his seat, settled Muslim colonists, founded Tyrnavos and led from there the raids that carried Ottoman arms into the Morea. In 1444 Trikala was the capital of the Sanjak of Tirhala, and the woollen cloth of its Greek weavers already sold across the province.

The first Ottoman census, in 1454–55, counted 251 Muslim and 212 Christian households in the town, which Turahan and his son Ömer Bey provided with mosques, a medrese, hammams and caravanserais; late in the sixteenth century the governor Osman Shah had Mimar Sinan build him the lead-domed mosque that carries his name.
