Canton, the Chinese city of Guangzhou, stands at the head of the Pearl River estuary, where seagoing junks could pass from the South China Sea to the old city of Panyu's offices and warehouses. It was already a Lingnan seat under the Han and became the capital of the Southern Han kingdom in the tenth century. Arab and Persian merchants lived in a foreign quarter in Tang times, when the port handled Indian Ocean shipping. The early Ming sea bans narrowed lawful commerce to tribute embassies and examined ports, leaving Canton as the place where most foreign trade was checked. In 1380 Zhu Liangzu rebuilt the walls across Yuexiu Hill and raised the five-storey Zhenhai Tower above them. In 1444 Ming officials, Cantonese merchants and Southeast Asian traders dealt in spices, incense and forest goods behind the walls.

Portuguese contact turned into war in the estuary: Ming fleets defeated Diogo Calvo's ships at Tunmen in 1521 and won another action at Xicao Bay in 1522. Trade resumed after the Luso-Chinese agreement of 1554, and from 1557 the Portuguese stored goods at Macau downriver. The port revived after the sea ban was lifted in 1567, but the Ming-Qing transition brought two severe captures. The Shaowu Emperor was enthroned at Canton in December 1646 and executed when Li Chengdong took the city the next month; in November 1650 Shang Kexi's Qing army sacked it, and tens of thousands died in the Gengyin calamity. Zhenhai Tower burned during the Three Feudatories' revolt and was rebuilt in 1687. After Taiwan fell in 1683, European East India ships returned to the Whampoa roadstead. In 1757 the Qianlong Emperor confined most European trade to Canton, and from 1760 the Cohong merchants managed it from the Thirteen Factories outside the walls. Tea, silk and porcelain went out; silver came in, followed by growing quantities of opium. The first American ship in the trade, the Empress of China, anchored at Whampoa in 1784.
zh:
广州位于珠江口内侧，海船可从南海直抵番禺旧城的官署和货仓。汉代这里已是岭南都会，10世纪时还做过南汉国都。唐代阿拉伯、波斯商人聚居蕃坊，港中船只连通印度洋海路。明初海禁把合法贸易压缩到朝贡使团和指定口岸，广州成为多数外商接受盘验的港口。1380年，朱亮祖把城墙修过越秀山，并在城头建五层镇海楼。1444年，明朝官员、广州商人和南洋商人在城墙内交易香料、熏香和南洋林产品。

葡萄牙人到来后，珠江口很快转为战场：1521年明朝水师在屯门击败葡萄牙舰队，1522年又在西草湾取胜。1554年葡中议定通商后贸易恢复，1557年起葡人在下游的澳门堆放货物。1567年海禁解除后广州重新恢复往来，但明清易代给城池两次重击。1646年12月绍武帝在广州即位，次月李成栋破城，绍武被俘遇害；1650年11月尚可喜率清军攻入，庚寅之劫中死者数以万计。镇海楼在三藩之乱中焚毁，1687年重修。1683年台湾平定后，欧洲各国东印度公司的船只回到黄埔锚地。1757年，乾隆帝把多数欧洲贸易限制在广州；1760年起，公行商人在城外十三行经营这项贸易。茶叶、丝绸和瓷器从这里出口，白银随后大量流入，鸦片数量也日渐增加。1784年，第一艘来华贸易的美国船「中国皇后号」在黄埔下锚。

en:
Macau, then called Haojing, was a group of fishing coves on the southeastern tip of the Xiangshan peninsula, linked to the mainland by the narrow Lotus Stem sandbar. It had belonged to Xiangshan County since Southern Song times, where Tanka boat-dwellers and Hakka villagers fished and made salt. Ming sea bans left little legal shipping on the coast, and in 1444 there was still no town here, only an anchorage among islands facing the water later called Taipa.

The Portuguese entered that anchorage after their defeats at Tunmen in 1521 and Xicao Bay in 1522. In 1553 they obtained leave to land by saying they needed to dry soaked cargo; Chinese sources describe a bribe paid to the coast intendant Wang Bai. In 1557 the Ming posted a guard officer over the settlement and accepted an annual rent, fixed at five hundred taels of silver from 1571. The Portuguese called the harbour Macau after the bay of A-Ma, the sea goddess Mazu.

Macau became the first permanent European settlement in China and a port of call on the Portuguese carrack route to Nagasaki and Manila. The diocese was created in 1576 and the municipal council in 1583. The Jesuit College of St Paul, founded in 1594, prepared missionaries for China and Japan; the adjacent Church of St Paul was built from 1602 to 1640. The Jesuits also built Monte Fort between 1617 and 1626. On 24 June 1622, after a three-day battle, outnumbered defenders drove off a Dutch fleet attacking the beaches, the only major engagement fought chiefly between European powers on the Chinese mainland.

Japan's closure in 1639 and the Dutch capture of Malacca in 1641 cut through the old carrack routes. Early Qing sea bans left Macau with limited foreign trade, and after Guangzhou customs was established in 1685 the peninsula served European ships waiting to go upriver. From 1757 Europeans had to report at Macau before trading at Canton. By the later eighteenth century it was also a staging point for opium carried to Whampoa.
zh:
澳门旧称濠镜澳，是香山县东南端的一组海湾渔村，半岛与大陆之间只靠莲花茎狭长沙堤相连。南宋以来这里属香山县，蜑家船民和客家村民以捕鱼、煮盐为生。明初海禁下，沿岸合法商船很少；1444年这里还没有城镇，只有一处夹在岛屿间、面向日后氹仔水域的锚地。

葡萄牙人在1521年屯门和1522年西草湾战败后，转而进入这处锚地。1553年，他们自称需要晾晒浸湿的货物，中文资料记载其贿赂广东海道副使汪柏，获准登岸；1557年明朝设官管理这个聚落并收取年租，1571年租额定为白银五百两。葡人由供奉海神妈祖的妈阁湾把这里称作澳门。

澳门成为中国土地上第一座欧洲人常住城镇，也是葡萄牙大帆船前往长崎和马尼拉航线上的停靠港。1576年教区设立，1583年议事会成立。1594年耶稣会创办圣保禄学院，为前往中国和日本的传教士授课；相邻的圣保禄教堂建于1602年至1640年。1617年至1626年，耶稣会又修筑大炮台。1622年6月24日，兵力居劣势的守军经三天战斗，把进攻海滩的荷兰舰队击退；这是中国土地上唯一主要由欧洲两支军队交手的大战。

1639年日本锁国，1641年荷兰攻占马六甲，旧有大帆船商路大受打击。清初海禁中，澳门只保留有限对外贸易；1685年粤海关设立后，半岛成为欧洲船只等待上驶内河时的停泊地。1757年以后，欧洲商人须先到澳门报备，才能前往广州贸易。到18世纪后期，这里也成为鸦片运往黄埔的中转地。

en:
Fuzhou lies at the mouth of the lower Min River, where the junk trade of Fujian's inland valleys meets the sea. Wang Shenzhi made it his capital when he founded the Min kingdom in 909, opened the Gantang anchorage and set up Fujian's first maritime trade office; the northern migrants he led in were remembered as the eighteen surnames that followed the Wang. The city walls built in that age enclosed three hills, and in 1065 the prefect Zhang Boyu had banyans planted by every household, which gave Fuzhou the name Banyan City. Song yards here built ocean-going ships, and the great hall of Hualin Temple, raised in the tenth century, is the oldest timber building in south China. In 1396 thirty-six Fuzhou seafaring families were sent under Ming order to settle in the Ryukyu kingdom, and the Changle anchorage downstream provisioned Zheng He's fleets between 1405 and 1433. In 1444 Fuzhou was the Ming provincial capital of Fujian, full of sailors who knew the Ryukyu and Nanhai routes, while private sea trade was hemmed in by the maritime prohibitions.

In 1474 the Fujian maritime trade office was moved to Fuzhou, and Ryukyu tribute missions were lodged at the Rouyuan Hostel. Wokou raided the prefecture hard in the Jiajing decades, and Qi Jiguang twice brought troops into Fujian to clear the coast. At the end of 1624 the Jesuit Giulio Aleni introduced Catholic teaching in the city. In 1645 Fuzhou became a Southern Ming capital: the Prince of Tang, Zhu Yujian, was enthroned there as the Longwu emperor and renamed the city Tianxing Fu as his travelling court; Qing armies destroyed the regime and took Fuzhou the following year. In 1674 the feudatory prince Geng Jingzhong rebelled from Fuzhou and held out until 1676, and the Qing coastal evacuation emptied shoreline villages until the policy ended in 1684. After that, licensed trade with Ryukyu and shipping to Japan carried Fuzhou through a wealthy eighteenth century.
zh:
福州地处闽江下游入海口，福建内陆各河谷的船运从这里出海。909年王审知建立闽国，定都福州，开甘棠港，设福建第一个市舶司；随他入闽的中原移民号称「十八姓从王」。五代时扩建的城池把乌山、于山、屏山圈入城中，福州别称「三山」；1065年知州张伯玉令家家户户种植榕树，满城榕树又为它赢得「榕城」之名。宋代福州是造船中心，10世纪所建华林寺大殿是南方最古老的木构建筑。1396年，三十六姓福州船户奉旨移居琉球；1405年至1433年郑和下西洋，下游的长乐太平港是船队停泊和采办的基地。1444年的福州是明朝福建省城，城中水手熟悉琉球与南洋航路，民间海上贸易却被海禁束住手脚。

1474年，福建市舶司移驻福州，琉球朝贡使团被安置在柔远驿。嘉靖年间倭寇大举寇掠福州府，戚继光两度率兵入闽平定。1624年底，耶稣会士艾儒略将天主教传入福州。1645年福州成为南明都城：唐王朱聿键在此称帝，改元隆武，升福州为天兴府，作为行在，次年清军便攻灭隆武政权、占领福州。1674年靖南王耿精忠据福州起兵反清，支撑到1676年；清初迁界又使沿海村落为之一空，直到1684年政策结束。此后对琉球的特许贸易和往来日本的商船，支撑福州度过了富庶的18世纪。

en:
Ganzhou holds the upper Gan River, where the Zhang and Gong streams meet before running north through Poyang Lake to the Yangtze. Its brick walls, first raised in the fourth century and faced with stone under the Northern Song, enclosed the chief city of the Jiangxi hills. South-west of the city the Meiling road, cut through the Dayu ranges in 716 for the Tang minister Zhang Jiuling, crossed the southern watershed to the Beijiang and Canton, so that most inland trade to and from the great port went over this pass. Above the city rose the Yugu terrace, made famous by a ci of the Southern Song poet Xin Qiji that begins 'Below the Yugu terrace the clear Jiang flows'. The surrounding hill country was Hakka land, its terraced fields and clans spreading across the four-province border. In 1444 Ganzhou was a Ming prefectural seat and the busiest staging town on the road between the Yangtze and Canton.

The broken border country drew a special command, the Nan-Gan grand coordinator, whose charge ran across Jiangxi, Guangdong, Fujian and Huguang. Its best-known holder was Wang Yangming, who in 1517 stormed the bandit fastnesses of Hengshui and Tonggang in the Dayu ridges and set up Chongyi county to settle the pacified country. The pass trade was then at its height: between 25,000 and 50,000 kilograms of silver crossed north each year to pay for Jingdezhen porcelain, which porters carried from the Gan over Meiling to Canton for Portuguese and Dutch ships, and the pass's thirtieth-duty alone came to 43,000 taels in 1567. When the Ming fell, Ganzhou held for the Longwu court under the name Zhongcheng, 'the loyal prefecture', until the Qing took it in 1646. Hakka clans in the hills built fortified stone manors called wei, the Guanxi New Wei near Longnan among them, and in 1793 the Macartney embassy travelled the old post road over Meiling on its way to the Canton factories.
zh:
赣州据赣江上游，章、贡二水在此相会，北经鄱阳湖入长江。城墙始筑于4世纪，北宋时以砖石包砌，围起的是江西南部最重要的府城。城西南的大庾岭路为唐相张九龄于716年凿通，越过分水岭接上北江、可抵广州，内陆与这座大港之间的往来，大半要走这道梅关。城中高地上的郁孤台，因南宋词人辛弃疾的名作而传遍天下，其《菩萨蛮》起句便是「郁孤台下清江水」。周围山地是客家人的聚居地，梯田和宗族遍布四省交界。1444年的赣州是明朝赣州府治，也是长江与广州之间最繁忙的中转重镇。

四省交界的山区难治，明朝专设南赣巡抚，辖区横跨江西、广东、福建、湖广。最有名的一任是王守仁，1517年他攻破大庾岭横水、桶冈的山寨，奏设崇义县安插归顺的人。此时梅岭商路正当盛时：每年有2.5万至5万公斤白银从广州北运，支付景德镇瓷器的货款，脚夫把瓷器挑过梅岭，在广州装上葡萄牙、荷兰商船；1567年梅关三十税一，一年关税即达4.3万两。明亡时，赣州为南明隆武朝廷坚守，改名忠诚府，1646年才被清军攻破。山间客家大族修建石砌围屋自保，龙南的关西新围是其中代表；1793年，马戛尔尼使团沿旧驿道逾梅岭南下，前往广州商馆。

en:
Changsha lies on the lower Xiang River, whose boats carry the produce of the Dongting lake plain north to the Yangtze. Pottery was the city's first famous export: the Tang kilns at Tongguan fired the earliest known underglaze polychrome wares, carried to Southeast Asia and the Persian Gulf. In 907 Ma Yin made Changsha capital of his Chu, one of the Ten Kingdoms; peace with the northern dynasties let him send Hunan tea north, and the region's tea became famous. The Yuelu Academy was founded at the foot of Yuelu Hill in 976. In 1015 the Song emperor Zhenzong summoned the headmaster Zhou Shi and gave the academy his calligraphy for a gate plaque; in 1167 Zhu Xi and Zhang Shi lectured to crowds whose horses were said to drink a roadside pond dry. When the Mongols besieged Tanzhou in 1275, the Song governor Li Fu slew his family and leapt into a well rather than surrender; hundreds of academy students died in the fallen city. The Ming renamed the city Changsha Prefecture in 1372. In 1444 it was a busy river port trading in tea and lake-plain grain; Yuelu Academy, ruined in the late Yuan wars, had been repaired with private funds in 1432.

By the late Ming Changsha was one of China's four great tea markets, and the young Wang Fuzhi studied at Yuelu before the dynasty fell. In 1664 the Qing made the city seat of the Huguang Right administration. Wu Sangui's revolt began in December 1673 and reached Hunan in 1674; the provincial governor abandoned Changsha, and the city stayed in rebel hands until early 1679, when Qing forces retook Yuezhou, Changde, Hengzhou and Changsha. The academy, rebuilt in 1668, was destroyed again and rebuilt from 1684; the Kangxi Emperor granted a plaque in 1687 and the Qianlong Emperor another in 1743. Hunan became a separate province in 1723-1724 with Changsha as its capital. The riverfront became the foremost of the four great Qing rice markets, as Huai salt came up from the lower Yangtze and Hunan rice went back in its place. In 1792 the headmaster Luo Dian built a pavilion among the red maples above the academy, renamed Aiwan by the governor-general Bi Yuan after a maple-at-dusk line of Du Mu.
zh:
长沙位于湘江下游，洞庭湖平原的物产由湘江船队北运入长江。长沙最早出名的物产是陶瓷：唐代铜官窑烧出已知最早的釉下多彩瓷器，碗、壶等器物远销东南亚和波斯湾，与越窑、邢窑并称唐代三大出口瓷窑。907年，马殷以长沙为都建立楚国，位列五代十国；他对北方政权保境安民、通商往来，把湖南茶叶运到北方交易，湖南茶开始名闻天下。976年，岳麓书院在湘江西岸的岳麓山下创立。1015年宋真宗召见山长周式，赐下亲书的书院匾额；1167年朱熹、张栻会讲，听讲者车马之多，据说把道旁池水都喝干了。1275年元军围攻潭州，湖南安抚使李芾举家投井、不肯投降，岳麓书院数百书生也死于城破之时。1372年明朝改置长沙府。1444年的长沙是繁忙的河港，经营茶叶和湖区平原的粮食；岳麓书院在元末战乱中毁坏，1432年已由民间集资修复。

晚明时，长沙位列中国四大茶市，青年王夫之在明朝灭亡前曾在岳麓书院求学。1664年，清朝以长沙为湖广右布政使司驻地。1673年12月吴三桂起兵，次年部将攻入湖南，湖南巡抚弃长沙而走，城池在吴军手中数载，直到1679年初清军连克岳州、常德、衡州和长沙。书院1668年刚刚重修，战乱中再毁，1684年起重建，康熙帝1687年赐匾「学达性天」，乾隆帝1743年再赐「道南正脉」。1723年至1724年湖南成为独立省份，长沙定为省治。此后沿江一带成为清代四大米市之首，淮盐自长江下游而来，湖南稻米又随回程船东去。1792年，岳麓书院山长罗典在山上的枫林间建亭，湖广总督毕沅取杜牧诗中枫树薄暮的名句，将它改名爱晚亭。

en:
Wuling, the country around Changde, lies where the Yuan and Li rivers break out of the Wuling Mountains into the reed marshes of Dongting Lake, a gap old geographies called the throat of Sichuan and Guizhou. Timber and other mountain goods from Guizhou came down the Yuan this way to the Yangtze, and the wharves of Changde lived by the traffic. Up the river, in the hills of the county called Taoyuan, was the setting men gave to Tao Yuanming's Peach Blossom Spring; its fisherman was a man of Wuling, and shrines and pavilions to the tale were raised there from the Tang dynasty. West of the lake plain the ranges belonged to native chieftains, the Peng lords of Yongshun and Baojing above the rest, whose Tujia followers held the ridges. In 1444 Wulin city was a Ming prefectural seat between a registered river country and the tribal hills.

A prince came in 1508, when Zhu Youshu took up his fief as Prince of Rong at Changde. The hills' troops had their day in 1555, when the young Yongshun chieftain Peng Yinan led three thousand Tujia soldiers to the coast and helped destroy a Wokou host at the battle of Wangjiangjing. Wuling itself produced Yang Sichang, the grand secretary in overall charge of the late-Ming anti-rebel wars, who died on campaign in 1641. In 1643 Zhang Xianzhong's army swept Hunan, and the last Prince of Rong fled with his mother up the Yuan to Chenxi and was never heard of again. When Wu Sangui rebelled, the Peng chieftains led their troops against him for the Qing at the Chenlong Pass; between 1727 and 1729 the Yongzheng court abolished their eight-hundred-year-old chieftaincies and put Yongshun and Baojing under regular officials.
zh:
武陵是常德府城周围的一片地方，沅、澧二水在这里穿出武陵山脉，进入洞庭湖的芦荡沼泽，旧地志称这一带为「川黔咽喉」。贵州山中的木材等山货顺沅水而下，经此运往长江，常德城的码头和商民就靠这条水路为生。上游桃源县境内沅水畔的山陵，相传就是陶渊明《桃花源记》的原型，文中打鱼人本是武陵人；自唐代起，当地人在那里建起祠庙亭阁供奉这篇名作。湖沼平原以西的群山归土官管辖，永顺、保靖的彭氏势力最大，领有的土兵多为土家族。1444年的武陵城是明朝常德府治，一边是编户纳粮的水乡，一边是土官治下的山地。

1508年荣王朱祐枢就藩常德，这里成为亲王封国。山地土兵也有自己的功名：1555年，年轻的永顺宣慰使彭翼南率三千土兵远赴东南沿海，在王江泾会同各路兵马大破倭寇。武陵本地走出了明末督师镇压民变的阁臣杨嗣昌，1641年他在军中病故。1643年张献忠军席卷湖南，末代荣王朱慈炤奉母沿沅水逃到辰溪，不知所终。吴三桂叛乱时，彭氏土司出兵助清，在辰龙关与叛军作战；1727年至1729年雍正改土归流，彭氏八百年的土司统治告终，永顺、保靖改由流官治理。

en:
Zhenyuan lies where the road from Hunan climbs onto the Yunnan-Guizhou plateau and the Wuyang River bends through a narrow valley. Dong and Miao villages held the country before the Southern Song opened a frontier commission here. Under the Ming the town carried both civil and military offices, with the prefectural city on the north bank and the guard city on the south, facing each other across the river's S-shaped bend. Work at Qinglong Cave began in 1388; Buddhist and Daoist shrines, the Ziyang study hall and Wanshou Palace later filled the Zhonghe cliff above the river, while Zhusheng Bridge crossed the water below. In 1444 prefecture and guard shared one garrison town on the Ming route into the Miao hills.

The civil seat became Zhenyuan County in 1498 after the prefecture had been briefly reduced and restored. During Wu Sangui's revolt in 1673, Gan Wenkun, governor-general of Yun-Gui, failed to hold Guiyang and fell back on Zhenyuan, where he was killed. The Qing kept a regional military commander in the town, but its hinterland remained unsettled. When Shi Liudeng launched the great Miao rising in north-eastern Guizhou in 1795, Miao communities in Zhenyuan's Forty-eight Streams took up arms, and troops from seven provinces were mobilized before the rising was put down.
zh:
镇远位于湖南入云贵的古道上，舞阳河在峡谷中绕出一道弯。本地原有侗族、苗族聚居，南宋在此设沿边溪洞招讨使司。明代的镇远兼管民政与军务，北岸是府城，南岸是卫城，两城隔河相对。洪武二十一年（1388年），青龙洞开始营建，后来在中和山崖壁间陆续建成佛寺、道观、紫阳书院和万寿宫，又有祝圣桥跨河而过。1444年的镇远府、卫同城，是明军进入苗疆路上的军镇。

弘治年间镇远府一度降为州，随后恢复；弘治十一年（1498年）设镇远县。1673年吴三桂起兵，云贵总督甘文焜守不住贵阳，退到镇远后身亡。清代继续在此派驻总兵，但城外山地仍不平静。1795年石柳邓发动黔东北苗民起事，镇远四十八溪的苗民响应，清廷从七省调兵，才把起事镇压下去。

en:
Guiyang occupies a mountain basin on the Nanming River in central Guizhou. Under the Yuan the town was called Shunyuan, and in 1292 the Eight Fan and Shunyuan military headquarters was placed within its walls. The Ming made it the seat of the new Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission in 1413, when the town was still known as Guizhou. Military guards and civilian offices shared the basin, while Yi, Miao and Bouyei chiefs held most of the surrounding hills. In 1444 Guiyang was therefore a provincial capital barely thirty years old, a Ming garrison watching the roads into Shui-Xi and the Miao country.

Jiang Dongzhi, governor of Guizhou, gave the city its best-known landmark in 1598 by building Jiaxiu Pavilion on the Aoji reef in the Nanming River and linking the reef to the south bank; the name asked for literary success. The pavilion burned in 1621 and was rebuilt by Zhu Xieyuan, then recovered its old name under Tian Wen in 1689. War reached the river before that rebuilding: in the second month of 1622, the Yi rising led by She Chongming and An Bangyan brought some 100,000 men against Guiyang and besieged it for more than ten months. When Wang Sanshan's relief army entered in spring 1623, famine had already broken the city. The Qing stationed the governor of Guizhou here in 1659 and moved the Yun-Gui governor-general to Guiyang in 1666.
zh:
贵阳位于贵州中部南明河畔的山间盆地。元代这里称顺元城，至元二十九年（1292年），八番顺元宣慰司都元帅府设于城中。永乐十一年（1413年），明朝在当时仍称贵州城的地方设贵州等处承宣布政使司，使它成为新行省的会城。卫所和民政衙门同处盆地，周围山地大多仍在彝族、苗族和布依族土司手中。1444年的贵阳设省才三十余年，是一座监视水西与苗疆道路的明军边城。

万历二十六年（1598年），贵州巡抚江东之在南明河鳌矶石上筑堤连接南岸，并建甲秀楼，楼名取「科甲挺秀」之意。此楼天启元年（1621年）焚毁，总督朱燮元主持重建；清康熙二十八年（1689年）巡抚田雯重修，恢复旧名。比这次重修更早，战祸已到城下：天启二年（1622年）二月，奢崇明、安邦彦领导的彝族起事以约十万众围贵阳逾十月。天启三年（1623年）春王三善援军入城时，城中已因饥荒残破。清顺治十六年（1659年），贵州巡抚驻贵阳；康熙五年（1666年），云贵总督也移驻于此。

en:
Wumeng occupies the Wumeng Mountains on the Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan border, above the gorges of the Jinsha and Niulan rivers. The old Five-Foot Road crossed these hills on its way from the Sichuan basin into Yunnan. Under Nanzhao and Dali the country belonged to the Wumeng Yi, and the Yuan created Wumeng Route in 1278. Fu Youde, Lan Yu and Mu Ying brought Ming armies through in 1381, after which the dynasty set up Wumeng Military-Civilian Prefecture under Sichuan. In 1444 appointed county magistrates did not govern these ridges: a hereditary Yi chief ruled the mountain villages, formally enrolled on the Ming frontier while keeping authority at home.

Direct Qing rule arrived through war. Ortai, who directed the replacement of native chiefships in the southwest, transferred Wumeng to Yunnan in 1727 and moved to install appointed officials. The greed and cruelty of garrison commander Liu Qiyuan helped drive Lu Wanfu into revolt; Liu and several local officers were killed, and Ortai called in troops from Yunnan, Guizhou and Sichuan to suppress the rising. The Qing established En'an and Yongshan counties in 1728. Three years later Wumeng Prefecture was renamed Zhaotong, a name taken to mean bright and open, with its seat moved to En'an, the core of the later city.
zh:
乌蒙位于云南、贵州、四川交界处的乌蒙山区，金沙江、牛栏江在群峰间切出深峡。古道五尺道穿过这里，把四川盆地与云南连接起来。南诏、大理时期，其地属乌蒙部；元朝1278年置乌蒙路。1381年，傅友德、蓝玉、沐英率明军经过此地，随后明朝设乌蒙军民府，划归四川管辖。1444年，普通州县流官尚未深入这些山岭，世袭的彝族首领在名义上编入明朝边疆秩序，实际仍统辖山中村寨。

清朝的直接统治由战争带来。主持西南改土归流的鄂尔泰1727年把乌蒙划归云南，准备改设流官。总兵刘起元贪暴残忍，逼得禄万福起兵；刘起元和多名地方官被杀，鄂尔泰随后调集云南、贵州、四川三省军队镇压。1728年，清廷设恩安、永善二县；三年后改乌蒙府为昭通府，取「昭明宣通」之意，并把府治移到恩安，也就是后来昭通城的核心。

en:
Shigatse, long known to Tibetans as Samdrubtsé, lies where the Nyang River runs into the Yarlung Tsangpo, holding the road from Lhasa into western Tsang. Its dzong, the fortress on the ridge above the river, was raised by the Phagmodrupa rulers in the fourteenth century, and the town grew up beneath it. By 1444 the Rinpungpa, formerly Phagmodrupa governors in a side valley, held the real power in Tsang. Their lord Norbu Zangpo kept it by balancing the fading court at Nedong against the great Sakya and Gelug monasteries, and the Samdrubtsé fortress was the strongest place in his western lands.

In 1447 Gendun Drup, a disciple of Tsongkhapa later counted as the First Dalai Lama, founded Tashi Lhunpo below the town's Sun Hill with money from local nobles; Norbu Zangpo let the work proceed, and the Gelug order had its first major monastery in Tsang. In 1565 the Shigatse governor rose against the Rinpungpa and opened the Tsangpa period, and in 1618 the Tsangpa made the town their capital after defeating Gelug forces and ruling most of Ü-Tsang. Güshi Khan's Mongol army took Shigatse in 1642, ended Tsangpa rule, and granted wide lands around the town to the Fourth Panchen Lama, Lobsang Chökyi Gyaltsen; Tashi Lhunpo became the seat of the Panchen Lamas. The Kangxi Emperor recognized the Fifth Panchen Lama as Panchen Erdeni in 1713. When the Sixth Panchen Lama died in Beijing in 1780, a feud over his estate helped draw the Gorkhas of Nepal into Tsang; they sacked Tashi Lhunpo in 1791 and gave back the plunder only after a Qing-Tibetan campaign drove them to the outskirts of Kathmandu, where they promised tribute every five years.
zh:
日喀则藏语旧称溪卡桑珠孜，简称桑珠孜，地处年楚河注入雅鲁藏布江处，扼守从拉萨通往后藏西部的道路。14世纪，帕木竹巴政权在河畔山冈上筑起桑珠孜宗堡，城镇就在堡下成形。到1444年，原在一条侧谷任帕竹家臣的仁蚌巴已成为后藏实际的统治者；家主诺布桑波在衰弱的乃东宫廷与萨迦、格鲁两大派寺院之间周旋，桑珠孜堡是他西部领地中最坚固的据点。

1447年，宗喀巴的弟子根敦珠巴（后来被追认为一世达赖喇嘛）靠当地贵族捐资，在日光山南麓创建扎什伦布寺；诺布桑波没有阻拦，格鲁派在后藏有了第一座大寺。1565年，日喀则宗本起兵推翻仁蚌巴，开启藏巴汗时期；1618年，藏巴汗击败格鲁派联军，以日喀则为都，统辖卫藏大部。1642年，固始汗的蒙古军队攻下日喀则，终结藏巴汗政权，把城镇周围大片土地赐给四世班禅罗桑曲结，扎什伦布寺成为历代班禅的驻锡地。1713年，康熙帝册封五世班禅为「班禅额尔德尼」。1780年六世班禅在北京圆寂，随后的遗产之争成为廓尔喀入藏的诱因之一；廓尔喀军队1791年洗劫扎什伦布寺，直到清朝与西藏的联军反攻到加德满都近郊，才交还财物，答允每五年进贡一次。

en:
Lhasa sits in a high valley on the Lhasa River beneath Red Hill. Pilgrims make for the Jokhang, the temple Songtsen Gampo founded in the seventh century for images brought by his Nepali and Tang brides; the Jowo Shakyamuni later kept there is Tibet's most revered Buddha statue, and the Barkhor path around the shrine drew monks and traders long after Lhasa ceased to be a royal capital. In the early fifteenth century Tsongkhapa and his disciples founded Ganden, Drepung and Sera in 1409, 1416 and 1419, placing three large Gelug monasteries around the valley. In 1444 the city still owed allegiance to the Phagmodrupa gongma Drakpa Jungne at Nedong, while the Rinpung lords were gaining ground in Tsang. Lhasa itself was ordered more by its temples, pilgrimage circuit and monastery estates than by a royal court.

The Great Fifth changed that. In 1642 Güshi Khan overthrew the Tsangpa dynasty and handed Tibet to the Fifth Dalai Lama, the first Dalai Lama to hold both spiritual and political leadership. His Ganden Phodrang administration moved to Lhasa, work on the Potala began on Red Hill in 1645, the White Palace was in use by 1649, and the Red Palace was added in 1690-1694 after the Great Fifth's death. The Barkhor had become a market for foreign goods by the time Ippolito Desideri reached Lhasa in 1716: he met Mongol, Chinese, Muscovite, Armenian, Kashmiri, Nepali and northern Indian traders, and saw musk, gold, medicinal plants, furs and yak tails exchanged for tea, sugar, saffron, turquoise, amber and coral. Dzungar troops sacked the city and killed Lhazang Khan in 1717; a Qing army installed the Seventh Dalai Lama in 1720 and stationed ambans there. After the ambans killed the regent and died in the riot of 11 November 1750, the Qing court created the Kashag council in 1751. The Gurkha war brought the Twenty-Nine Articles of 1793, placing the garrison and the Golden Urn for reincarnations under amban supervision. In 1821 the Potala above the Jokhang marked Lhasa as the fixed Dalai Lama capital under Qing oversight.
zh:
拉萨位于拉萨河的高谷中，城北是红山。香客前往的核心是大昭寺：7世纪松赞干布为安置尼泊尔、唐朝两位公主带来的佛像而建，后来供奉其中的觉卧释迦牟尼像成为藏地最受尊崇的佛像。吐蕃王权没落后，拉萨很久不再是王都，但绕大昭寺的八廓转经道仍吸引僧人与商贩。15世纪初，宗喀巴及其弟子分别在1409年、1416年和1419年创建甘丹寺、哲蚌寺和色拉寺，三座格鲁派大寺围在河谷周边。1444年，拉萨仍在名义上臣服于驻在乃东的帕木竹巴贡玛札巴迥乃，仁蚌巴首领则在后藏扩张。此时支配拉萨的主要是寺院、转经道和寺院领地，而不是王庭。

第五世达赖喇嘛改变了这种局面。1642年，固始汗推翻藏巴汗王朝，把西藏交给第五世达赖喇嘛；他也是第一位同时掌握宗教与政治权力的达赖喇嘛。甘丹颇章政权移驻拉萨，1645年红山上的布达拉宫动工，白宫1649年投入使用，红宫则在第五世达赖喇嘛圆寂后的1690至1694年增建。德西德里1716年抵达拉萨时，八廓街已是外来货物市场，他见到蒙古、汉地、莫斯科、亚美尼亚、克什米尔、尼泊尔和北印度商人，麝香、黄金、药材、毛皮和牦牛尾在这里换走茶叶、糖、藏红花、绿松石、琥珀和珊瑚。1717年准噶尔军队洗劫拉萨并杀死拉藏汗；1720年清军册立第七世达赖喇嘛，并在当地设置驻藏大臣。驻藏大臣杀死摄政后，自己也在1750年11月11日的暴乱中丧命，清朝朝廷遂于1751年设立噶厦。廓尔喀战争后，1793年的《钦定藏内善后章程二十九条》把驻军与认定转世的金瓶掣签置于驻藏大臣监督之下。1821年，大昭寺上方的布达拉宫标示出拉萨已是达赖喇嘛的固定都城，处在清朝监管之下。

en:
Dartsedo, Dajianlu in Chinese records, is wedged into a steep valley more than 8,000 feet high, where three gorges meet and two rivers join below the town while snow peaks tower thousands of feet above its walls; the road from Chengdu climbs through this gap into the Tibetan country of Kham. It was the seat of the kings of Chakla, whom the Yuan confirmed as native chieftains and whom later Qing accounts counted among the Four Great Native Chiefdoms of Kham. In 1407 the chief Ngawang Gyaltsen submitted to the Ming and received a bronze seal from the Yongle Emperor as Pacification Commissioner of Changhexi, Yutong and Ningyuan. The town lived by tea: porters and mule caravans carried brick tea up the trails from Ya'an and Chengdu and traded it for Tibetan horses, wool and medicinal herbs. In 1444 Dartsedo was already the busiest market on the whole Sino-Tibetan frontier.

In the 1620s the armies of Lijiang overran much of Kham but were thrown back from Chakla. The quarrel that cost the kings their town was with Lhasa, which kept a tax commissioner here; in 1700 that commissioner, backed by Khoshut Mongol power, murdered the king and seized Dartsedo. A Qing army stormed the town on 28 January 1701 and restored the Chakla house, then secured the road by ordering an iron-chain suspension bridge thrown over the Dadu at Luding below the town; the Kangxi Emperor's bridge was finished in 1706. The dead king had left no son, so his widow ruled the chiefdom; when she too died without an heir her daughter, already running the neighbouring Muping chiefdom, held the Chakla seal as well. The Qing detached Chakla from Lhasa's claims in 1725 and placed a subprefecture at Dajianlu in 1730. On 1 June 1786 an earthquake of magnitude 7.75 levelled the town, and the Sichuan governor reported that not one merlon of its walls was left standing; a landslide dammed the Dadu, and when the earthen dam gave way the flood scoured the valley below. The tea market was rebuilt and remained the town's livelihood.
zh:
打箭炉，藏语称达折多，嵌在海拔八千多英尺的深山峡谷中：三道峡谷在此相凑，两条河水在城下相汇，雪山高出城墙数千英尺，成都方向的官道正是穿过这道山口进入康地藏区。这里是察拉王国（汉文史书作明正土司）的治所，元代便册封当地首领为土官，清代文书将其与巴塘、里塘、德格并称康区四大土司。1407年（永乐五年），土酋阿旺坚参内附，受封长河西鱼通宁远宣慰使，获赐铜印。小城以茶为生：背夫和马帮把雅州、成都的砖茶沿山路驮来，在此换取藏地的马匹、羊毛和药材。1444年的打箭炉已是整条汉藏边地上最热闹的市集。

17世纪20年代，丽江土司的军队横扫康区大部，却在察拉被击退。真正给国王招来祸事的是与拉萨的冲突：西藏甘丹颇章政权在打箭炉设有征税营官，1700年（康熙三十九年），营官倚仗和硕特蒙古之势攻杀土司蛇蜡喳吧、占据城镇。1701年1月28日清军破城，恢复了察拉土司，随后又下令在城下泸定的大渡河上修建铁索悬桥以安稳这条大路，康熙帝钦准的泸定桥于1706年建成。蛇蜡喳吧死后无嗣，由其妻工喀署理事务；工喀1710年去世仍无继承人，其女桑结本在署理邻近的穆坪土司，便将明正司印务一并兼管。1725年清廷将察拉划出拉萨管辖，1730年（雍正八年）置打箭炉厅。1786年6月1日发生7.75级大地震，全城尽毁，四川总督奏报城垣全行倒塌、不存一雉；山崩壅塞大渡河，土坝溃决后洪水横扫下游河谷。茶市事后重建，依旧是这座小城的生计所系。

en:
Chengdu sits on the Chengdu Plain, whose rivers Li Bing tamed with the Dujiangyan waterworks in the third century BC; the irrigation made the basin a land of abundance, and the city has kept its name and site since Qin general Zhang Yi walled it in 311 BC. Its most famous product was Shu brocade. A Han brocade office supervised the tribute cloth and gave Chengdu the name Brocade City; under the Southern Song the plain supplied more than two thirds of the silk sent to court. In 1021 the city's merchants began using the jiaozi, the first paper money anywhere, and the Song later opened an official office to print it.

Chengdu was the capital of Liu Bei's Shu Han in the Three Kingdoms, and of the Former Shu and Later Shu kingdoms in the tenth century. Meng Chang of the Later Shu had hibiscus planted all along the city walls, giving Chengdu its other name, the Hibiscus City. Two Tang emperors took refuge here from rebellion, Xuanzong in 756 and Xizong in 880. The poet Du Fu built a thatched hut beside Flower Rinsing Creek in 759 and wrote 240 poems there in four years, and the Wuhou Shrine honoured the Shu Han chief minister Zhuge Liang. Under the Ming, Chengdu held the Sichuan provincial administration and the court of Zhu Chun, the Prince of Shu, whose palace rose on the old inner city. In 1444 it was the southwest's political and mercantile centre, living on silk and grain.

In 1621 the Yi chieftain She Chongming rebelled, killed the provincial governor and besieged Chengdu for 102 days. Zhang Xianzhong's army took the city in 1644 and he proclaimed himself emperor of the Great Western, calling Chengdu Xijing; two years later the city was burned in the fighting and largely emptied. For years the Qing provincial administration sheltered at Langzhou, and the Three Feudatories' revolt of 1673 brought war back to Sichuan. The Qing then brought in settlers under the filling Sichuan from Huguang migration and returned the provincial government to Chengdu. By the eighteenth century the plain again shipped grain, silk and tobacco out of its chief city.
zh:
成都位于成都平原。公元前3世纪李冰主持修建都江堰，驯服平原上的河水，使四川盆地成为「天府之国」；自公元前311年秦将张仪按咸阳形制筑城以来，城址和城名再未变过。成都最出名的物产是蜀锦：汉代设锦官督造上供的织锦，成都因此又叫「锦官城」；南宋时成都上交的丝绸占全国七成以上。1021年，成都商人开始使用世界上最早的纸币「交子」，宋仁宗时官府又设交子务负责印行。

成都先后做过三国时蜀汉和五代时前蜀、后蜀的都城。后蜀孟昶命人在城墙上遍种芙蓉，成都于是又有「芙蓉城」之称。唐代两位皇帝避乱入蜀，先有756年的唐玄宗，后有880年的唐僖宗。759年，诗人杜甫在浣花溪畔搭起草堂，四年间写下240首诗；成都还有祭祀蜀汉丞相诸葛亮的武侯祠。明代，成都是四川承宣布政使司治所，明太祖第十一子朱椿受封蜀王，在旧子城上建起蜀王府。1444年的成都，是西南的政治和商业中心，以丝绸和粮食致富。

1621年，彝族土司奢崇明起兵反明，杀死巡抚徐可求，围攻成都102天。1644年张献忠率军入城，自立为大西皇帝，改成都为西京；两年后全城在战火中焚毁，人口几乎逃散一空。清朝的四川布政使司多年寄居阆中，1673年三藩之乱又把战火烧回四川。此后清廷以「湖广填四川」大举移民，把省会迁回成都。到18世纪，成都平原重新向外输出粮食、生丝和烟草，成都也恢复为西南首要都会。

en:
Chongqing commands the confluence of the Yangtze and the Jialing, where the walled town climbs a steep peninsula between the two rivers. After Qin conquered Ba in 316 BC, Zhang Yi stationed a garrison and built a fortress at Jiangzhou by the Chaotianmen crossing, the first recorded city on the site. Under the Sui the town became Yu Prefecture, the source of its abbreviation Yu, and in 1189 the newly enthroned Emperor Guangzong raised Gong Prefecture to Chongqing Fu, the double celebration that gave the city its name. Around 1238 the Song prefect Peng Daya carried the walls down to the Jialing against the Mongols, fixing the outline later walls followed. Chongqing's one turn as an imperial capital came with Ming Yuzhen, a Red Turban commander who entered Sichuan through the Wu Gorge and in 1363 proclaimed himself emperor of Great Xia, making Maitreya worship the state teaching and casting his own copper coins. He died in 1366 and was buried at Ruiling north of the Jialing; his young son Ming Sheng surrendered to the Ming in 1371 and was exiled to Korea the next year. In that same year the guard commander Dai Ding rebuilt the walls with seventeen gates, nine open and eight closed. In 1444 Chongqing was a heavily garrisoned river hub between the Sichuan basin and the Yangtze gorges.

In 1621 the Yongning tusi leader She Chongming seized Chongqing and made it the capital of his Daliang regime, then marched on Chengdu for a siege of 102 days; he was not killed until 1629. Zhang Xianzhong's army took the city in 1644, and war, massacre and flight emptied much of eastern Sichuan, and the Three Feudatories' revolt after 1673 fought over the ruins. The Qing migration called filling Sichuan from Huguang then brought farmers, boatmen and merchants upriver, many of them landing at Chongqing's wharves. On the lower Jialing, Ciqikou grew into a porcelain-making market town, and by the early nineteenth century the city was again the main transshipment point between the basin and the gorges, not yet opened as a treaty port.
zh:
重庆城坐落在长江与嘉陵江相汇处一道陡峭的半岛上，城墙沿江岸起伏。公元前316年秦灭巴，张仪在朝天门一带屯兵修筑江州城，这是史籍所见重庆建城之始。隋代改置渝州，重庆简称「渝」即来自这一古称；1189年，刚受禅登基的宋光宗取「双重喜庆」之意，升恭州为重庆府，城市因此得名。1238年前后，南宋知府彭大雅为抵御蒙古，把城垣拓展到嘉陵江边，后世城池基本沿用这个轮廓。重庆唯一一次做帝国都城是在明玉珍时：他率天完红巾军由巫峡入蜀，1363年在重庆称帝建大夏，奉弥勒教为国教，自铸铜钱。1366年明玉珍病死，葬在嘉陵江北岸的睿陵；幼子明昇于1371年向明朝投降，次年被流放朝鲜半岛。同年，重庆卫指挥使戴鼎重修城垣，设九开八闭共十七座城门。1444年的重庆，是四川盆地与长江三峡之间驻有重兵的河港枢纽。

1621年，永宁宣抚使奢崇明袭占重庆，以此为大梁国都，随即出兵围攻成都102天；他本人直到1629年才败死。1644年张献忠军攻占重庆，战乱、屠杀和逃亡使川东大片地方人口一空，1673年后的三藩之乱又在废墟上反复拉锯。清廷推行「湖广填四川」，农民、船工和商人沿江西上，多从重庆各码头登岸。嘉陵江下游的磁器口发展成烧瓷和赶集的市镇；到19世纪初，重庆重新成为四川盆地与三峡之间最主要的货物转运港，此时尚未开为通商口岸。

en:
Yichang, the Ming subprefecture of Yiling, stands at the mouth of the Xiling Gorge, where the Yangtze breaks out of the Three Gorges into the lakeland of the Jianghan plain. Every junk sailing between Sichuan and the middle river had to stop here: trackers hauled the boats up through whirlpools and reef-strewn rapids, crews were changed at the wharves, and Sichuan salt and hill tea changed hands before the run down to Jingzhou. The Ming turned Xia Prefecture into the Yiling subprefecture under Jingzhou in 1376. In 1444 it was a small walled town of boatmen, porters and fishermen, living off the gorge traffic at the foot of the mountains that divided Hubei from Sichuan.

In the gorge above the town stood the old Yellow Ox Shrine, its hall to Yu the Great rebuilt by Ming officials in 1618. These mountains became the last Ming holdout on the mainland. After the Qing conquest, loyalist bands called the Kuidong camps kept the Sichuan-Hubei border ranges, and Li Laiheng, adopted son of Li Guo, a nephew of Li Zicheng, built his fort on Maolu Mountain above Xingshan. In 1662 the court sent 200,000 troops against the camps; within two years Li's was the only band left, encircled by 100,000 men behind wooden walls and trenches. His men shot and killed Su'erma, the third son of the Manchu general Mulima, and held out for months before food ran out and every breakout failed. In August 1664 Li killed Li Youshi, a former comrade sent to talk him into surrendering, saw his old mother to safety, and burned himself to death with his wife and children. The Qing gave Yiling a homophone written name in 1648, and in 1735, after the Rongmei chiefdom in the western hills came under regular rule and Hefeng Subprefecture was founded, raised the town to Yichang Prefecture. White Lotus sects rose in these same hills in 1796 and fought on until 1804.
zh:
宜昌即明代的夷陵州，城在西陵峡口，长江在此冲出三峡、进入江汉平原的湖网地带。往来四川与中游的船只都要在此停靠：纤夫把船拉过漩涡暗礁密布的险滩，水手在码头换班，川盐和山里的茶叶在此转手，再放船东下荆州。1376年明朝改峡州为夷陵州，隶属荆州府。1444年的夷陵是一座船夫、脚夫和渔夫聚居的小城，靠着川鄂分界群山脚下的峡江过活。

峡中江边的黄牛祠即后来的黄陵庙，是江上最有名的古庙，主殿禹王殿于1618年由明代官府重建。这片群山后来成了南明在大陆最后的据点。清军入关后，号称夔东十三家的明军余部据守川鄂边境山地，李过（李自成之侄）的义子李来亨在兴山茅麓山筑寨。1662年清廷发兵二十万三省会剿，两年后诸营或破或降，只剩李来亨一部被十万清军团团围住，外有木城壕沟。守军击毙满洲将领穆里玛的第三子苏尔马，相持数月，终因粮尽、突围不成，1664年8月李来亨杀死前来劝降的旧识李有实，遣走老母，与妻子儿女举火自焚。1648年清廷把夷陵改写作「彝陵」；1735年西山容美土司改土归流、设鹤峰州，彝陵州升为宜昌府。1796年白莲教又在这片山里起事，战火一直延到1804年。

en:
Wuchang and Hanyang face each other across the Yangtze at the mouth of the Han, the crossing between the middle Yangtze and the roads north and south. Wuchang's walls went up in 223 with Sun Quan's Xiakou fort, and a watch tower at the Yellow Crane jetty became the Yellow Crane Tower. Tang poets made it famous across China: Cui Hao wrote his great poem on the tower, and Li Bai, seeing Meng Haoran off to Yangzhou here, gave the three settlements the name River City in a later verse. Ming commanders rebuilt the tower in 1371-1381; after it burned in 1566 it went up again in 1571. The Southern Song general Yue Fei garrisoned Wuchang for eight years and campaigned against the Jin from here, and was later enfeoffed as Prince of E. Under the Yuan the city became the seat of Huguang province. In 1370 the Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed his sixth son Zhu Zhen, born in Wuchang the year his army took the city, as Prince of Chu, and the Chu palace rose beside the provincial offices. In 1444 Wuchang was the political centre of Huguang, the older Hanyang faced it across the river, and the marshy bank that would become Hankou held no market town.

Under the Chenghua emperor the Han shifted north of Guishan hill and left a sheltered north-bank anchorage, where Hankou grew into a town within a generation. By the Wanli reign it shipped the tribute grain of Huguang and transshipped Huai salt up the Yangtze for Hunan and Hubei, and in 1635 a long dyke was raised to protect its river streets. In 1643 Zhang Xianzhong's rebel army stormed Hanyang and Wuchang, drowned the Chu prince Zhu Huakui in the Yangtze, and proclaimed himself King of the Great West before carrying his regime into Sichuan. Under Qing rule Hankou entered its busiest age: merchants of the Shanxi, Shaanxi, Huizhou and Jiangxi guilds dealt in salt, pawnbroking, rice, timber, cloth and medicines, the six great trades of the town. Hankou was ranked with Zhuxian, Jingdezhen and Foshan as one of the four great market towns of the empire, and the Yangtze-Han crossing was known as the thoroughfare of nine provinces.
zh:
武昌与汉阳隔长江相望，汉水就在这里入江，这处渡口把长江中游与南北各路连通。223年东吴孙权筑夏口城，城西黄鹤矶上的望楼便是黄鹤楼。唐代诗人使它名扬全国：崔颢在此写下平生最得意的一首《黄鹤楼》，李白又从这里送孟浩然东下扬州，他笔下长江与梅花的诗句还让三镇有了「江城」的别称。1371年至1381年，明初将领主持重建黄鹤楼；楼1566年焚毁，1571年再度建起。南宋时岳飞驻防鄂州（今武昌）八年，几次从这里出师北伐抗金，身后追封为鄂王。元代武昌成为湖广行省治所。1370年，明太祖封第六子朱桢为楚王，朱桢生于1364年，正逢大军攻克武昌，楚王府后来与湖广布政使司同驻城中。1444年的武昌是湖广政治中枢，老城汉阳隔江相望，后来长成汉口的那片低洼江岸还没有商镇。

成化年间汉水改从龟山以北入江，北岸留下风浪较小的停泊地，汉口只用几十年就长成市镇。到万历年间，湖广漕粮在这里装船东下，淮盐溯长江而上，分销湖南、湖北；1635年又筑起长堤，护住沿江街市。1643年，张献忠的军队攻破汉阳、武昌，把楚王朱华奎沉入长江，自称「大西王」，随后率部进入四川。入清以后，汉口进入最繁忙的年月：山西、陕西、徽州、江西各帮商人经营盐、典当、米、木材、棉布、药材，号为镇上六大行业。汉口与朱仙镇、景德镇、佛山镇并称天下四大名镇，两江相会的渡口也有「九省通衢」之称。

en:
Nanchang lies on the lower Gan River at the edge of the Poyang Lake plain, the natural hub of Jiangxi; the river road carries Jiangxi paper and porcelain south to Canton. The Han made it seat of Yuzhang Commandery in 201 BC, and Tang Hongzhou was known for its shipyards and paper. Its landmark is the Tengwang Pavilion of 653, made China's most famous pavilion by Wang Bo's preface of 675. Zhu Yuanzhang took it from the Yuan in 1362, and his Ming made it Nanchang Prefecture, the seat of Jiangxi. In 1444 the provincial administration shared the city with Zhu Quan, seventeenth son of the Hongwu Emperor: first enfeoffed at Daning on the northern frontier, he was swept into the Jingnan war by his brother the Yongle Emperor and then moved to Nanchang with his guard disbanded, spending his later years on the zither, tea and the theatre.

The ground before the city settled the founding of the Ming. In 1363 Chen Youliang attacked with an army said to number 600,000, and Zhu Yuanzhang's nephew Zhu Wenzhen held the walls eighty-five days with fewer than ten thousand men. When the relief army reached the lake, Chen was killed in the battle there, his tower ships burned by fire ships.

A second princely revolt ended far faster. In 1519 Zhu Chenhao, Prince of Ning, rose from his mansion, and the grand coordinator Wang Shouren, the philosopher known as Wang Yangming, put him down in forty-three days and caught him on Poyang Lake; the Tengwang Pavilion burned in the fighting and was rebuilt in 1526. Matteo Ricci sojourned here while seeking leave to enter Beijing, and under the Wanli Emperor imperial clansmen resettled here made up about a quarter of the city's people. In 1648 the surrendered Ming generals Jin Shenghuan and Wang Deren turned back to the Southern Ming; Tantai's Qing army besieged Nanchang for eight months and sacked it when it fell in 1649, and the pavilion burned again, rebuilt in 1654 and in 1789. The painter Bada Shanren, born here in 1626 as Zhu Da of the imperial house, became a monk after the conquest and returned to paint his cold, staring birds and fish in Nanchang until his death in 1705.
zh:
南昌位于赣江下游、鄱阳湖平原边缘，是江西的天然枢纽，溯赣江而上的商路把本省的纸张、瓷器运往广州。汉代于公元前201年在此设豫章郡治，唐代的洪州以造船、造纸闻名。城中的地标是653年始建的滕王阁，675年王勃一篇《滕王阁序》使它名扬海内。1362年朱元璋从元朝手中夺取南昌，明初改置南昌府，为江西布政使司治所。1444年，与布政使司同城的还有明太祖第十七子宁王朱权：他初封北方边地大宁，靖难之役中被兄长燕王朱棣裹胁起兵，朱棣即位后被改封南昌、削去护卫，晚年只以琴学、茶事和戏曲著述度日。

南昌城下还打过一场决定明朝开国的大战。1363年，陈友谅率号称六十万的大军来攻，朱元璋之侄朱文正以不足万人坚守八十五天；援军进抵湖口后，陈友谅在鄱阳湖水战中中箭而死，楼船被火船焚毁。

第二次藩王起兵败得快得多。1519年宁王朱宸濠在南昌举叛，南赣巡抚王守仁（即后世所称的哲学家王阳明）仅用四十三天便将其讨平，在鄱阳湖将他俘获；滕王阁毁于兵火，1526年重建。利玛窦谋求进入北京期间曾留居南昌；万历年间被安置到此的朱氏宗亲约占城中人口的四分之一。1648年，已降清的明将金声桓、王得仁在南昌反清归明，谭泰率清军围城八个月，1649年城破后大肆屠戮，滕王阁再遭焚毁，1654年重建，1789年又一次重建。画家八大山人1626年生于南昌，本名朱耷，出自明朝宗室；明亡后出家为僧，晚年回到南昌，画他那些翻着白眼的鱼鸟，1705年卒于此。

en:
Hangzhou sits at the southern end of the Grand Canal, where it meets the Qiantang River and Hangzhou Bay. The Sui linked the city to the canal in 589; it was capital of the Wuyue kingdom and then, as Lin'an, the working capital of the Southern Song from 1138 until the Mongols entered in 1276. This was the city Marco Polo supposedly visited and called Quinsai, greater than any other in the world, its markets crowded with silk, paper, books and porcelain. Its most honoured grave is on West Lake: the general Yue Fei, recalled from his advance against the Jin and framed by the chief minister Qin Hui, was put to death in a Lin'an prison in 1142, and a temple was raised over his tomb in 1221; Bai Juyi and Su Shi built the lake's causeways. Zhu Yuanzhang captured Hangzhou in 1366, and the Ming made it the seat of Zhejiang province. In 1444, two years after a drought dried West Lake, the city was still the wealthy Wu-speaking terminus of the canal trade.

One local son already in office was Yu Qian of Qiantang: after the Tumu disaster of 1449 he organised the defence of Beijing and headed the Jingtai Emperor's government, only to be executed when Yingzong returned in 1457; his tomb was raised beside West Lake. Wokou raiders struck Hangzhou Bay between 1553 and 1558, at times pressing close to the walls. In 1513 the commander Li Long set bronze kneeling figures of Qin Hui, his wife and their accomplice before Yue Fei's tomb, and pilgrims beat the statues to pieces; they were recast in iron in 1594. Qing forces entered Hangzhou in 1645, and in 1650 a walled Manchu banner garrison rose in the western city; under the Qing the Hangzhou weaving bureau joined those of Suzhou and Jiangning as one of the three great imperial silk centres of Jiangnan. The Kangxi Emperor first saw West Lake in 1689 and wrote plaques for its Ten Scenes in 1699; the Qianlong Emperor followed with six southern tours from 1751 to 1784, and his verses helped make Longjing tea a court favourite. In 1782 a manuscript copy of the Siku Quanshu was placed in the Wenlan Pavilion on Gushan.
zh:
杭州在大运河最南端，运河到此与钱塘江、杭州湾相接。589年隋朝把它接入运河；五代时它是吴越国的都城，南宋时改名临安，1138年起成为实际行都，直到1276年元军入城。马可·波罗相传到过这里，把他称为行在（Quinsai）的杭州记为天下第一等的富庶城市，市上满是丝绸、纸张、印本和瓷器。它最受尊崇的墓在西湖畔：名将岳飞在北伐抗金的战场上被朝廷强令召回，受宰相秦桧构陷，1142年在临安狱中被杀，1221年墓上建起祠庙；白居易和苏轼则主持修筑了西湖的堤岸。1366年朱元璋攻取杭州，明代以杭州府为浙江布政使司治所。1444年的杭州，虽在两年前刚经历西湖干涸的大旱，仍是运河贸易南端最富庶的吴语城市。

杭州人于谦此时已在朝中为官：土木堡之变后，他组织了1449年北京对蒙古的保卫，主持景泰朝政，英宗1457年复辟后却被处死，他的墓也在西湖畔。1553至1558年倭寇反复袭扰杭州湾，有时兵锋直逼城墙下。1513年，都指挥李隆在岳飞墓前铸起秦桧夫妇及其同党反绑双手的跪姿铜像，凭吊者把铜像砸得粉碎，1594年像被改用铁重铸。1645年清军进入杭州，1650年城西建起墙垣环绕的八旗驻防城；清代杭州织造局与苏州、江宁并列，是江南三大官办丝织中心之一。康熙帝1689年初游西湖，1699年为西湖十景题匾；乾隆帝1751至1784年六次南巡，他的咏茶诗使龙井茶成为宫廷爱物。1782年，一部《四库全书》抄本入藏孤山文澜阁。

en:
Yangzhou guards the junction of the Yangtze and the Grand Canal. In 486 BC Fuchai of Wu dug the Han Canal here to carry supplies north against Qi, and the city grew up at the canal's mouth. Under the Tang it was the richest emporium in China, with Arab, Persian and Korean merchant quarters, and contemporaries ranked it first and Yi Prefecture second among the cities of the age. From its Daming Temple the monk Jianzhen made six attempts to cross to Japan and reached it in 753, blind, to found the Toshodai-ji in Nara. Yuan Yangzhou still kept foreign communities: Marco Polo claimed to have governed the city for three years, though no Chinese text mentions him, while the Vilioni tomb of 1342 shows that Italian traders were really here. Under the Ming the city became the exchange for Huai salt, rice and silk, and new walls went up against the wokou. In 1444, with the court at Beijing and the tribute-grain fleets moving up the canal, Yangzhou sat at the busiest trade crossing in the empire.

When the Ming collapsed, the Southern Ming grand secretary Shi Kefa held the city for the dynasty; Prince Dodo's Qing army took it on 20 May 1645 after a short siege and killed him when he refused to submit, and the ten-day sack that followed emptied it, recorded by the survivor Wang Xiuchu. Salt rebuilt Yangzhou. The Lianghuai salt administration sold the Huai coast's salt here for Anhui, Jiangxi, Hubei and Hunan, and the salt duty long supplied some two-fifths of the empire's revenue; Huizhou merchant houses laid out gardens held to be the finest in China, and in 1655 the Dutch envoy Nieuhof already found the city restored to its old splendour. The Kangxi and Qianlong emperors toured those gardens, and in 1757 the salt commissioner Gao Heng built the Five-Pavilion Bridge across Slender West Lake for a southern progress. The Eight Eccentrics made Yangzhou a centre of painting, lacquer and jade workshops and block-printing houses lined the canal, while the Wenhui Pavilion, completed in 1780 beside the Tianning Temple, housed a manuscript copy of the Siku Quanshu.
zh:
扬州扼守长江与大运河的交汇处。公元前486年，吴王夫差为北上伐齐在此开凿邗沟转运粮草，城市就兴起在邗沟入江处。唐代它是天下最富庶的商埠，阿拉伯、波斯和新罗商人在城中侨居，时人以「扬一益二」把它排在天下城市之首。高僧鉴真从大明寺出发，六次尝试东渡，753年双目已盲的他终于抵达日本，在奈良创建唐招提寺。元代扬州仍有外来商团：马可·波罗自称曾治理扬州三年，中国史籍却无记载，而1342年维利奥尼家族的墓碑说明意大利商人确曾在此聚居。入明以后，扬州成为淮盐、稻米和丝绸的大集散地，又新筑城墙防备倭寇。1444年朝廷已在北京，漕粮船队沿运河北上，扬州是全国商船往来最繁忙的码头。

明亡时，南明大学士史可法据守此城，多铎的清军1645年5月20日短暂围城后破城，史可法拒降被杀，随后的十日屠戮使城市为之一空，幸存者王秀楚把经过写成《扬州十日记》。让扬州复兴的是盐业：两淮盐运使把淮南海盐在此批销安徽、江西、湖北、湖南，盐税长期约占全国岁入的四成；徽商家族修筑的园林被推为天下之冠，1655年荷兰使臣尼霍夫已见城市恢复旧观。康熙、乾隆两帝屡下江南游览这些园林，1757年两淮盐运使高恒为迎驾在瘦西湖上建起五亭桥。扬州八怪使这里成为绘画中心，运河两岸漆器、玉器作坊和刻书坊林立，1780年在天宁寺旁落成的文汇阁入藏了一部《四库全书》抄本。

en:
Anqing guards the north bank of the lower Yangtze where the river, pressed between the Dabie range and the hills of northern Jiangxi, narrows to a defile, the stretch later called the throat of the long Yangtze and the first frontier between Wu and Chu; every fleet moving between Nanjing and Huguang had to pass under its walls. The walled city was a frontier work of the Southern Song: in 1217 the prefect Huang Gan, a disciple of Zhu Xi, petitioned to build it at the Yicheng ferry after Jin armies broke through upstream, and Ma Guangzu rebuilt it on the same site in 1260. Zhu Yuanzhang took the city in the wars that founded the Ming. In 1444 it was a six-county prefecture of Nanzhili and a heavily garrisoned river stronghold.

In 1568 the Zhenfeng Pagoda rose within Yingjiang Monastery above the water, named to rouse the wind of letters and used as a landmark by every junk that passed. With rebel armies closing on the late Ming, the court in 1637 placed a special governor at Anqing over four prefectures, and when the new province of Anhui was carved from western Jiangnan under the Qing, its provincial government moved to Anqing in 1760. The prefecture's greater fame in these centuries was literary. Tongcheng county gave the Qing its dominant school of prose: Fang Bao (1668-1749) laid down its principles, Liu Dakui (1698-1779) carried them forward and Yao Nai (1732-1815) brought them together, and Tongcheng models set the standard for the age. Tongcheng also produced the grand secretary Zhang Tingyu (1672-1755), chief editor of the History of Ming and the only Han Chinese minister of the Qing admitted after death to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; his father Zhang Ying had earlier settled a family lawsuit over a boundary wall with a poem urging his household to give up three feet, the neighbours yielded three as well, and the gap became the famous Six-Foot Alley. Deng Shiru (1743-1805) of Huaining, the seal-script master who renewed Qing calligraphy and seal carving, was another son of the prefecture.
zh:
安庆踞长江下游北岸，大别山与赣北丘陵在此夹江，江面收束成峡，旧称「万里长江此封喉，吴楚分疆第一州」，往来于南京与湖广之间的舰队都要从城下经过。府城本是南宋的边防工程：1217年金军破光州，朱熹弟子、安庆知府黄干奏请在宜城渡筑城，1260年马光祖又在原址重筑；朱元璋在开国战争中攻取此城。1444年的安庆领六县、隶属南直隶，是重兵驻守的江防要塞。

1568年，迎江寺内的振风塔在江边落成，取「以振文风」之意，往来舟船都拿它做江上航标。明末起义军逼近，朝廷于1637年在安庆专设巡抚，统辖四府；清代从江南西部分出安徽省后，省级衙署于1760年移驻安庆，此地成为安徽省会。这几百年里，一府之地更出名的是文章。桐城县贡献了清代居主流的古文流派：方苞（1668—1749）立定义法，刘大櫆（1698—1779）承前启后，姚鼐（1732—1815）集其大成，桐城古文成为一时准绳。桐城还出了三朝重臣张廷玉（1672—1755），他是《明史》总纂官，也是清代唯一死后配享太庙的汉臣；其父张英早先因家人与邻争墙，作诗劝自家让出三尺，邻家也退三尺，中间的巷道便是传名的六尺巷。怀宁县人邓石如（1743—1805）以篆书、篆刻另开一路，为清代书法与印章之别派开山者。

en:
Nanyang fills the broad basin between the Funiu Mountains and the Han River, where roads from the Central Plains pass into Hubei and Shaanxi. Its chief city, Wan, was the seat of Nanyang Commandery under the Qin and under the Han one of the five great metropolitan cities of the empire, crowded with state iron foundries; the registers counted 47,547 households serving the government workshops, and the iron lances of Wan were feared for their sharp points. The Gengshi Emperor was enthroned on the bank of the Bai River here in AD 23, and Liu Xiu raised the Eastern Han on Nanyang men and Nanyang money, many of his twenty-eight Cloud Terrace generals coming from the commandery; as the dynasty's 'southern capital', Wan ranked second only to Luoyang. The commandery also produced the astronomer Zhang Heng, maker of an armillary sphere and a bronze seismoscope, and the physician Zhang Zhongjing, who compiled the Shanghan Lun. Local tradition places Zhuge Liang's thatched farm at Wolong Ridge west of the city, the scene of Liu Bei's three visits. The early Ming made Wan the seat of Nanyang Prefecture and enfeoffed Zhu Jing, twenty-third son of the Hongwu Emperor, as Prince of Tang, with a great palace in the city; the green jade of nearby Dushan Hill kept its jade workshops busy. In 1444 the Prince of Tang held court here, and Nanyang was the political and market centre of south-western Henan.

The late Ming rebellions reached the basin in 1633 and again in 1638, and both times Zuo Liangyu beat Zhang Xianzhong back from the walls. In November 1641 Li Zicheng stormed the city and killed the reigning Prince of Tang on Qilin Ridge; he took firm control in 1642, and Qing troops arrived in 1645. Under the Qing the post road from Beijing to Hunan, Guizhou and Yunnan ran through the Wancheng station outside the east gate, where northern pack trains met river boats; Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants built their guild hall there in the Kangxi years. On the eastern lowlands Zhoujiakou, the river harbour at the meeting of the Jialu and Shaying rivers, had grown by the late eighteenth century into a town of tens of thousands, sending grain and goods north to the Yellow River and south to the Yangtze.
zh:
南阳地处伏牛山与汉水之间的宽阔盆地，中原通向湖北、陕西的道路穿境而过。首府宛城秦代即为南阳郡治，汉代与洛阳、邯郸、临淄、成都并称「五都」，官营冶铁作坊林立，载入户籍的工官、铁官人户有四万七千五百四十七户，宛地的铁矛以锋利闻名。公元23年，更始帝在城南淯水之滨登基；刘秀靠南阳的人和财货起家，云台二十八将中不少人出自本郡，南阳成为东汉的「南都」，城邑规模仅次于洛阳。这一带还出了制成浑天仪、候风地动仪的天文学家张衡，和著成《伤寒杂病论》的医家张仲景。城西卧龙岗相传是诸葛亮躬耕之处，也是刘备三顾茅庐的地方。明初于宛城设南阳府，明太祖第二十三子朱桱受封唐王，在城中建起宏大的王府；城外独山产绿玉，玉作作坊常年忙碌。1444年，唐王在此就藩，南阳是豫西南的政治与商业中心。

明末战乱于1633年、1638年两度波及盆地，张献忠两次攻城，都被左良玉击退。1641年11月李自成攻破南阳，在城西麒麟岗杀唐王朱聿鏼；1642年他再攻并控制南阳，1645年清军进入这一地区。清代北京通往湖广、云贵的驿道经过城东的宛城驿，北方驮队与南方河船在此交接，康熙年间山陕商人建起会馆。东部低地上的周家口地处贾鲁河、沙颍河交汇处，到18世纪末已发展成数万人的河港，粮食货物北走黄河、南达长江。

en:
Kaifeng lies on the flat south bank of the Yellow River, whose silt has raised the bed above the plain and made levees the city's constant care. Wei made it its capital as Daliang in 364 BC, and the Bian River of the Sui Grand Canal linked the Yellow River to the Huai and made the city a great entrepôt. As Dongjing, the Northern Song capital, it was the richest city in China, its night markets and riverside crowds painted in Zhang Zeduan's 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival'. Above the north-eastern wards rose the Iron Pagoda, a glazed-brick tower of 1049 named for its iron-coloured bricks, raised after the master builder Yu Hao's wooden pagoda was lost to lightning. The Jurchen took Dongjing in 1127 and the Mongols after them. In 1381 Zhu Su, fifth son of the Hongwu Emperor, took up his fief as first Prince of Zhou and built on the old Song palace site; he had more than four hundred edible wild plants grown and painted for his illustrated famine herbal, the 'Jiuhuang Bencao'. In 1444 Kaifeng was the seat of Henan province, flooded five times since 1375, and home to a small Jewish community whose synagogue dated from 1163.

A stele of 1489 lists fourteen clans, and in 1605 a Kaifeng Jewish juren, Ai Tian, told Matteo Ricci in Beijing that his 'Yicileye', Israel, congregation numbered about a thousand; by the late Ming it held some 4,000 people. Li Zicheng besieged Kaifeng three times in 1641 and 1642. In the first assault the Prince of Zhou, Zhu Gongxiao, paid the defenders from his treasury and Li took an arrow in the left eye. The third siege, from April 1642, starved much of the city until the Ming relief army was routed at Zhuxian to the south-west. In October the rain-swollen Yellow River, which both sides had tried to use against the other, burst the dikes and buried the city: of some 370,000 people about 30,000 survived, and the flood destroyed the synagogue and most of its scrolls. The Qing rebuilt the walls in 1662 and kept Kaifeng as the provincial seat, but its trade and crafts never regained their Ming level.
zh:
开封地处黄河南岸平原，黄河挟带的泥沙把河床淤得高出两岸，修堤防水是此城世代的大事。前364年魏国迁都于此，名为大梁；隋代大运河的汴河连通黄河与淮河，使这里成为水运要冲。北宋以此为东京，是当时中国最富庶的城市，夜市和汴河两岸的人流都画进了张择端的《清明上河图》。城东北耸立着铁塔，这座1049年建成的琉璃砖塔因砖色如铁而得名，建在名匠喻浩的木塔遭雷击焚毁之后。1127年金军攻陷东京，以后又入蒙古之手。1381年，明太祖第五子朱橚就藩开封，在宋故宫旧址建起周王府；他把四百多种可食的野生植物种在府中，命画工绘图，著成图谱式的救荒专书《救荒本草》。1444年的开封是河南省会，自1375年以来已五次遭黄河水淹，城中还住着一支犹太人社群，他们的会堂始建于1163年。

1489年的碑刻列出了十四个犹太姓氏；1605年，开封犹太举人艾田在北京告诉利玛窦，他的「一赐乐业」会众约有千人；到明末，这支社群约有四千人。1641至1642年，李自成三次围攻开封。第一次攻城时，周王朱恭枵拿出王府存银犒赏守军，李自成左眼被箭射伤。1642年4月起的第三次围城使城中大半人饿死，明朝援军在城西南的朱仙镇被击溃。10月，交战双方都曾想借黄河水淹对方，被秋雨涨满的河水冲决堤防，开封全城没于水中，三十七万人仅存三万，犹太会堂被毁，经卷大多散失。清朝于1662年重修城墙，仍以开封为河南省治，但城中的商业和手工业再没恢复到明代的水平。

en:
Hanzhong is the long river basin locked between the Qinling range and the Daba Mountains, the Han River running east through its rice fields. Its roads are plank ways cut into the cliff faces of the gorges, and the basin is the gate between the Guanzhong plain and Sichuan. After the fall of Qin, Liu Bang held it as King of Han with his seat at Nanzheng; on an altar in town he raised Han Xin to grand general, and Han Xin's ruse of mending the plank roads while marching secretly on Chencang won Guanzhong back. The dynasty Liu Bang founded took its name from this fief. Chenggu was the home county of Zhang Qian, the envoy who twice crossed the Western Regions under Emperor Wu and opened the Silk Road. In the Three Kingdoms period Wei and Shu fought hard for the basin: in 219 Huang Zhong killed the Wei general Xiahou Yuan at Dingjun Mountain, and Zhuge Liang, who launched his northern expeditions from Hanzhong, asked in his last will to be buried there; his Wuhou tomb lies at the foot of Dingjun. The Ming made it Hanzhong Prefecture in 1370 and posted a guard to watch the road into Sichuan, so in 1444 it is a quiet garrison town, its markets living on basin rice and the tea, timber and mountain goods carried over the plank roads.

In 1627 Zhu Changhao, fifth son of the Wanli Emperor and Prince of Rui, took up residence in a palace more than twenty years in the building, its grounds covering about a third of the walled city, and he added salt levies and other taxes the people could ill afford. A peasant rising broke out in the prefecture in 1637, and through the 1640s the armies of Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong moved back and forth along the old road to Sichuan. The prince fled to Chongqing, where Zhang put him to death in 1644, and the townspeople stripped and dismantled the palace he left behind. The White Lotus rising of 1796—1804 swept the mountains where Sichuan, Hubei and Shaanxi meet, keeping imperial armies in the Qinling valleys for nine years.
zh:
汉中是夹在秦岭与大巴山之间的长条盆地，汉江横贯东流，两岸都是稻田。进出盆地要走峡谷崖壁上架木修成的栈道，这片盆地也是关中平原通往四川的门户。秦亡之后，刘邦受封汉王，以南郑为都；他在城中设坛，拜韩信为大将，韩信佯装修复栈道，暗中却取道陈仓出兵，打开了重回关中的路。刘邦建立的王朝，国号就来自这个封国。城固县是张骞的故里，这位使臣在汉武帝时两度出使西域，开通了丝绸之路。三国时魏蜀激烈争夺汉中：219年，黄忠在定军山斩杀魏将夏侯渊；诸葛亮数次北伐都以汉中为基地，临终遗命安葬于此，他的武侯墓就在定军山下。1370年明朝改设汉中府，派驻军卫把守入川大道，1444年的汉中是一处安静的卫所城镇，市面靠着盆地米粮和栈道运来的茶叶、木材、山货维持。

1627年，万历帝第五子、瑞王朱常浩就藩汉中；瑞王府修了二十多年，约占府城三分之一，他又加派盐税等名目，百姓不堪重负。1637年府内爆发农民起事，整个1640年代李自成、张献忠的军队沿入川古道往来不断。瑞王逃往重庆，1644年被张献忠处死，留在汉中的王府被当地人拆抢一空。1796—1804年的白莲教起义席卷川、鄂、陕交界的山地，清军在秦岭峡谷里打了九年。

en:
Qingzhou lies in central Shandong on the road from Jinan to the Jiaodong peninsula, its seat at the walled town of Yidu. Its name comes from the Yu Gong, 'between the sea and Mount Dai lies Qingzhou', one of the Nine Provinces of antiquity. Its single spell as a dynastic seat came in 399, when Murong De, ruler of the Xianbei state of Southern Yan, made the fortress of Guanggu his capital, the only dynastic capital on Shandong soil. In 410 Liu Yu's Eastern Jin army stormed Guanggu and razed it; two years later the pilgrim Faxian, returning from India by sea, landed at nearby Laoshan and came here to translate his scriptures. On Tuoshan, Camel Mountain, outside the town, 638 Buddhist images were cut into the cliff from Northern Zhou times on, Shandong's largest such group. Through the Song, Jin and Yuan, Yidu remained the chief town of eastern Shandong. The Ming made it Qingzhou Prefecture and briefly the capital of Shandong, until the provincial seat moved to Jinan in 1376. Zhu Fu, seventh son of the Hongwu Emperor, held the fief as Prince of Qi until he was deposed for good in 1406, leaving his palace empty. In 1444 Qingzhou was still one of Shandong's foremost prefectural towns, though no princely court remained.

In 1499 Zhu Youhui, seventh son of the Chenghua Emperor, took up residence as Prince of Heng, and his descendants held the fief until the Ming fell. The dynasty ended here in the Qingzhou Incident of 1644: Zhao Yingyuan, one of Li Zicheng's officers, seized Yidu and killed Wang Aoyong, the Qing commissioner for Shandong, by dismemberment; Qing troops retook it within months. The last Prince of Heng, Zhu Youzou, had already surrendered; he was taken to Beijing and executed in 1646 with eleven other Ming princes, among them the Hongguang Emperor. In 1729 the Yongzheng Emperor stationed a banner garrison general here with 2,000 cavalry and 400 infantry; when its walled Manchu city was finished in 1732, the general Emida led the first bannermen from Beijing. In 1761 the post was reduced to a vice-commander, who also supervised the banner garrison at Dezhou.
zh:
青州地处山东中部、济南通往胶东半岛的官道上，府治在益都城。州名出自《尚书·禹贡》，「海岱惟青州」，是古九州之一。它唯一一次成为王都，是399年鲜卑慕容德建立南燕、以广固城为都，这是山东土地上唯一的王朝都城。410年刘裕率东晋军久攻破城，夷平广固；两年后，西行求法的僧人法显由印度渡海归来，在附近的崂山登陆，随即到这里翻译带回的经卷。城外的驼山上，638尊佛像自北周起陆续雕成，是山东最大的摩崖造像群。宋、金、元三代，益都都是山东东部的首城。明代设青州府，并一度以该城为山东省治，1376年省治迁往济南。明太祖第七子朱榑受封齐王、就藩于此，1406年被彻底废为庶人，王府就此空着。1444年的青州仍是山东数一数二的府城，只是再没有藩王宫廷。

1499年，明宪宗第七子朱祐楎就藩青州，是为衡王，其子孙在此传国直至明亡。1644年发生青州之变：李自成部将赵应元占据益都，将清廷派来招抚山东的官员王鳌永肢解处死，清军数月之内夺回城池。末代衡王朱由棷此前已降，仍被执送北京，1646年与弘光帝等十一名明朝藩王一同遇害。1729年，雍正帝在青州派驻防将军，领马甲两千、步甲四百；1732年满城筑成，将军鄂弥达率首批八旗兵自北京南下进驻。1761年将军一职降为副都统，兼辖德州驻防。

en:
Jinan lies where the southern hills meet the Yellow River plain, with Mount Tai not far to its south. Springs feed Daming Lake and the seventy-two named springs that give it the name City of Springs. Under the Song it became a superior prefecture in 1116; two celebrated poets, Li Qingzhao and Xin Qiji, were born here and both fled south after the Jurchen conquest. While serving here as a Yuan official, the painter Zhao Mengfu depicted the two low peaks north of the city in Autumn Colours on the Qiao and Hua Mountains. Ming armies took Jinan in 1368, and in 1376 the Shandong provincial government moved here from Qingzhou. The city's best-known siege came in 1400, during the Jingnan campaign: the rebel Prince of Yan Zhu Di breached a dike to flood the walls, yet Tie Xuan and the general Sheng Yong held out for three months, first feigning surrender to drop an iron portcullis at the prince, then hanging tablets bearing his father's posthumous title on the ramparts so he dared not bombard the city. Zhu Di withdrew; after he took the throne in 1402, Tie Xuan was put to death by dismemberment. In 1444 Jinan was the provincial capital on the post road running south from Beijing.

Long peace made Jinan one of the richest cities of northern China in the Jiajing and Wanli decades; Li Panlong, born at Licheng in 1514, led the Later Seven Masters of letters. War returned at the dynasty's end. In the fourth Manchu inroad Dorgon's raiders sacked Jinan early in 1639: the left administration commissioner Zhang Bingwen, the investigating censor Song Xuezhu and the prefect Gou Haoshan died in its defence, the Prince of De Zhu Youshu was carried off captive, and his palace burned. Later courts honoured Tie Xuan, the Southern Ming and then the Qianlong Emperor granting him posthumous names. In 1644 Jinan passed first to Li Zicheng's Shun regime and then to the Qing; in 1666 the ruined De palace was rebuilt on a smaller scale as the Shandong governor's yamen. Its trade recovered slowly under the Kangxi Emperor, and Jinan remained the provincial capital.
zh:
济南位于南部丘陵与黄河平原相接之处，南距泰山不远。泉水汇入大明湖，城中有七十二名泉，济南也因此别称泉城。1116年北宋升齐州为济南府，李清照、辛弃疾两位名家都出生于此，女真南下后两人相继南渡。元代书画家赵孟頫在济南做官时，画下城北两座矮峰，成了名画《鹊华秋色图》。1368年明军攻入济南，1376年山东布政使司自青州移驻于此，济南成为山东省会。1400年靖难之役中，济南打了一场最出名的保卫战：燕王朱棣掘开河堤灌城，铁铉与大将盛庸却死守三个月，先遣人诈降、暗放铁板伏击燕王，再在城头高悬写着其父皇尊号的牌位，使燕军不敢开炮。朱棣解围而去，1402年登基后，铁铉被处以磔刑。1444年的济南是北京通往南方官道上的山东省会。

承平日久，嘉靖、万历年间济南成为北方最富庶的城市之一；1514年生于历城的李攀龙主盟文坛，为「后七子」之首。战祸在明末重来：1639年初清军第四次入塞，多尔衮所部攻破济南，山东左布政使张秉文、巡按御史宋学朱、知府苟好善守城而死，德王朱由枢被掳北去，德王府付之一炬。后朝追念铁铉的忠义，南明和后来的乾隆帝都给他上了谥号。1644年济南先归李自成的大顺，随后入清；1666年焚毁的德王府缩建成山东巡抚衙署。康熙年间商贸缓慢恢复，济南终清之世都是山东省会。

en:
The country at the foot of the Taihang range, where the Qin River leaves Shanxi for the Yellow River plain, was called Yewang in Qin times and Henei from the Sui, and a Huaizhou garrison sat here from the fifth century. It was the birthplace of the late Tang poet Li Shangyin (c. 813-858), remembered for his dense, allusive 'Untitled' poems. In December 1126 the Jin general Wanyan Zonghan stormed Huaizhou after the Song garrison fought to the end; its commander Huo Anguo refused to surrender and was put to death with his whole household. Under the Mongols it became Huaiqing Route, and in 1368 the new Ming dynasty set Huaiqing Prefecture over six counties, with its seat at Henei on the lower Qin. Its well-watered fields made it grain country, and in 1443 the court moved the Prince of Zheng, Zhu Zhanjun, to Huaiqing from Fengxiang; the prince entered his new fief in 1444.

The Zheng fief's most famous son was Zhu Zaiyu (1536-1611), heir of its prince, a mathematician, astronomer and music theorist who in 1584 worked out the mathematics of twelve-tone equal temperament. Huaiqing also lived by its drugs: rehmannia, Chinese yam, achyranthes and chrysanthemum, the 'four Huai medicines', whose dealers, the Huai merchants, built guild halls in the great drug markets of the north. In the late 1630s the rebellions reached Henan, and Li Zicheng's army destroyed the Ming forces in the province before his Shun dynasty briefly held it in 1644; Qing armies then took Huaiqing, kept the prefecture, and later added Yuanwu and Yangwu to its six counties.
zh:
太行山南麓、沁河出山西入黄河平原之处，秦代称野王，隋代起改名河内，5世纪以来便是怀州治所。晚唐诗人李商隐（约813—858年）就出生在这里，他以意象繁密、托旨幽微的《无题》诗闻名。1126年12月，金将完颜宗翰攻克怀州，宋朝守军力战到最后，守将霍安国坚决不降，被完颜宗翰灭了满门。元代称怀庆路，1368年明朝改置怀庆府，府治设在沁河下游的河内县，领六县，沁河灌溉的良田以产粮著称。1443年，朝廷将郑王朱瞻埈从陕西凤翔改封怀庆，郑王于1444年就藩。

郑藩最出名的人物是朱载堉（1536—1611年），郑恭王嫡子，身兼数学家、天文学家和乐律学家，1584年以精密计算首创十二平均律。怀庆还靠药材立身：怀地黄、怀山药、怀牛膝、怀菊花号称「四大怀药」，经营怀药的怀商结成怀邦，在北方各大药都修建会馆。1630年代末民变波及河南，李自成军歼灭了省内的明军主力，1644年其大顺朝一度据有此地，随后清军攻取怀庆，沿用府治，后来又把原武、阳武二县划入，共领八县。

en:
Taiyuan occupies the upper Fen River plain, where the Fen leaves the hills and enters the central Shanxi basin. Jinyang, its first walled city, was founded in 497 BC; in 453 BC Zhao broke a siege by opening the Fen on the army of Zhi, and later dynasties kept Jinyang as a northern capital. After conquering Northern Han in 979, the Song emperor Taizong had the old city burned and flooded, and in 982 a new walled town was laid out on the present site. Ming forces under Xu Da took it from the Yuan in 1368. The Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed his third son Zhu Gang as Prince of Jin, and the Jin palace became the largest of the Ming princely courts. The general Xie Cheng enclosed the town with walls about fourteen kilometres around, while Zhu Gang built Chongshan Temple for his mother, Empress Ma. In 1444 Taiyuan supplied the northern garrisons with iron and weapons; Shanxi merchants, earning salt sales rights by delivering frontier provisions, were already building commercial networks from the basin.

Late Ming wars reached Taiyuan in 1644, when Li Zicheng's Dashun army stormed the city on its march from Xi'an toward Beijing. Shanxi governor Cai Maode killed himself as the city fell, and the Jin palace and Chongshan Temple burned in the fighting that brought Qing rule. South-east of the walls stood the twin brick pagodas of Yongzuo Temple: Wenfeng Pagoda was completed in 1599 and Xuanwen Pagoda in 1612. Under Qing peace, Taiyuan's iron, sulphur and coal trades supported a wider commercial region. Pingyao, Taigu and Qi in Taiyuan Prefecture produced the Shanxi draft banks that financed tea caravans to Mongolia and Russia, while the prefectural city handled northern trade and handicrafts.
zh:
太原位于汾河从山地进入晋中盆地的上端平原。公元前497年，晋阳城已在此筑成；公元前453年，赵氏决汾水反灌围城的智氏军队，此后多个政权把晋阳作为北方都城。979年宋太宗攻灭北汉后焚毁、淹没晋阳城，982年又在今太原一带另筑新城。1368年徐达从元朝手中夺取太原。明太祖封第三子朱棡为晋王，晋王府成为明代王府中规模最大的一处；谢成主持扩建城垣，城墙周长约十四公里，朱棡又为生母马皇后修建崇善寺。1444年，太原为北方驻军提供铁货和兵器，山西商人也因向边镇运送粮饷、换取盐引，开始从盆地向外建立商路。

晚明战火在1644年烧到太原，李自成的大顺军从西安向北京进军途中攻破城池，山西巡抚蔡懋德城破后自缢。随后清军定晋的战事中，晋王府和崇善寺都毁于火灾。城墙东南立着永祚寺双塔：文峰塔1599年完工，宣文塔1612年完工。清代承平期间，太原的铁、硫磺和煤炭支撑着周边商业。太原府境内的平遥、太谷和祁县出现晋商票号，为前往蒙古、俄罗斯的茶叶商队办理汇兑；太原城本身则经营北方贸易和手工业。

en:
Pingyang fills the broad Fen River valley of south-western Shanxi, the fertile corridor between the Luliang and Taiyue ranges, with its seat at Linfen. In 309 the Xiongnu leader Liu Yuan made the city the capital of his Han state, and through the Sui, Song and Yuan it remained the chief town of the Fen valley. Its sheltered basin suffered less than the open plains in the late Yuan wars and grew crowded with people. From 1373 to 1417 the Ming organised eighteen official migrations, assembling the settlers at the Great Pagoda Tree of Hongtong before sending them out to repopulate the war-scarred North China Plain; families across northern China have since traced their ancestors to that tree. In 1444 Pingyang was one of the most densely settled prefectures of the Ming, living from the cultivated fields of the Fen valley.

At Hongtong, on the southern slope of Huoshan, stands the Guangsheng Temple, founded in Han times. The buildings of its lower temple went up under the Yuan and preserve Yuan wall paintings of theatrical performances, and the temple kept a Jin-dynasty Buddhist canon later known as the Zhaocheng Tripitaka. Its glazed Feihong Pagoda, built from 1515 to 1527, survived both the great Huaxian earthquake of 1556 and the Linfen earthquake of 1695. That shock, on 18 May 1695, reached degree eleven on the Chinese seismic intensity scale, affected more than 120 counties across eight provinces, and killed an estimated 52,600 people. The same basin had already taken one of the deadliest earthquakes in China's recorded history, at Hongtong in 1303. In 1724 five of the prefecture's subprefectures were put directly under the province and a sixth followed under the Qianlong Emperor, leaving Pingyang with one subprefecture and ten counties; Linfen remained its seat.
zh:
平阳占着晋西南开阔的汾河谷地，是吕梁山与太岳山之间的肥沃通道，府治设在临汾。309年，匈奴首领刘渊建立汉国、定都平阳；隋、宋、元各代，这里一直是汾河流域的首城。盆地有群山屏蔽，在元末战乱中受损比中原平原轻，人口日益稠密。1373年至1417年，明朝组织了十八批官方移民，先在洪洞大槐树集结，再迁往遭兵火破坏的华北平原填补人口，北方各省的家族纷纷把祖先追溯到这棵槐树。1444年的平阳是明朝人烟最稠密的府之一，靠汾河谷地的耕地为生。

洪洞境内、霍山南麓的广胜寺始建于东汉。下寺多为元代建筑，保存着元代戏曲壁画，寺中还藏有金代雕造的大藏经，后世称《赵城金藏》。寺内通体琉璃的飞虹塔建于1515年至1527年，历经1556年华县大地震和1695年临汾大地震而未毁。1695年5月18日的地震最高烈度达十一度，波及八省一百二十余州县，约五万二千六百人遇难。同一盆地在1303年已经遭遇过洪洞大地震，那是中国有记载以来死人最多的地震之一。1724年，府属五个州升为省直辖的直隶州，乾隆年间又有一州升走，平阳府缩为一州十县，临汾始终是府治。

en:
Hejian lies in the flat, river-cut country south of Beijing, in land named for the waters that divide the plain. The Ming converted the old Yuan route into Hejian Prefecture in 1368 and placed it in the Northern Metropolitan Region the next year. In 1444 its walled seat was the first prefectural city on the main road south from the capital. The prefecture also reached east through Cangzhou to the Bohai shore, where tidal flats belonged to the Changlu salt country. Salt-boiling households there produced sea salt for a major Ming northern revenue source.

Under the Ming, the salt commission at Changlu town supervised twenty-four saltworks strung along the Bohai coast. Salt and official traffic moved between the shore, Cangzhou, Hejian and the capital region, while the prefecture's registered population passed 400,000 by the late sixteenth century. The Qing kept Hejian County as the prefectural seat after 1644. In 1731 they transferred Cangzhou to Tianjin Prefecture, putting the coast and salt district under a different administration from the inland city of Hejian.
zh:
河间位于北京以南的平原水网地带，地名来自诸河之间的土地。1368年，明朝把元代河间路改为河间府，次年划入北直隶。1444年，河间府城是北京南下官道上的第一座府城；辖区又经沧州伸向渤海，海边滩涂属于长芦盐区。灶户在那里煮海晒盐，供应明朝北方一项重要官盐收入。

明代，长芦镇的盐运机构统管渤海沿岸连成一线的24处盐场。食盐和公务往来在海岸、沧州、河间与京师之间流动；到16世纪后期，全府登记人口已超过40万。1644年清朝接管后，河间县仍是府治。1731年，沧州改属天津府，海岸和盐区便与内城府城河间分属两个行政区。

en:
Baoding lies below the eastern face of the Taihang Mountains, where rivers run east toward Baiyang Lake and the plain opens toward Beijing. Mongol troops destroyed Baozhou in 1213, and Zhang Rou, a Jin general who had submitted to the Mongols, rebuilt the city in 1227. In 1275 Shuntian Route was renamed Baoding, a name referring to the defence of the capital. The Ming made it Baoding Prefecture in 1368 and moved the Daning military commission there in 1403. In 1444 the seat at Qingyuan County was a prefectural city and garrison on Beijing's southern flank. In the hills to the northwest, Zijing Pass stood with Juyong and Daoma as one of the Three Inner Passes. The old Quyang kilns farther west had supplied the thin white Ding porcelain admired in the Northern Song, although production had ended under the Yuan.

Zijing Pass showed its worth in 1449. After the Tumu disaster, Esen's Oirats forced the pass and advanced on Beijing, using the Taihang valley to turn the capital's outer defences. The Ming appointed a Baoding grand coordinator in 1515, and the city kept soldiers and officials close to the roads between the capital, Shanxi and the southern plain. Under the Qing the Zhili governor moved from Zhending to Baoding in 1669, and the office became the Viceroyalty of Zhili in 1724. The Lotus Pond Academy opened in 1733, giving the garrison city a well-known centre for classical scholarship.

The Qing also brought imperial tomb building to Yi Prefecture. Work began at Yongning Mountain in 1729 after the Yongzheng Emperor chose the site for his mausoleum, and the Tailing was completed in 1737. It became the first tomb of the Western Qing necropolis in the northwestern hills guarding Baoding's flank.
zh:
保定位于太行山东侧，诸河东流注入白洋淀，平原向北京展开。1213年蒙古军摧毁保州，降蒙的金将张柔在1227年主持重建。1275年，顺天路改称保定路，地名与护卫京师有关。1368年明朝设保定府，1403年把大宁都司移驻于此。1444年，清苑县治既是府城，也是北京南侧驻军之地；西北山中的紫荆关与居庸关、倒马关合称内三关。更西边的曲阳古窑曾为北宋烧造胎体轻薄的白釉定瓷，到元代已经停烧。

1449年，紫荆关的价值直接显现。土木之变后，也先的瓦剌军攻破此关，沿太行山谷进逼北京，绕向京师外围防线。1515年，明朝设置保定巡抚；城中长期驻有军队和官员，看管北京、山西与南部平原之间的道路。清朝时，直隶巡抚在1669年由真定移驻保定，1724年改设直隶总督。1733年，莲池书院开办，使这座军镇又有了知名的经学场所。

清朝还把皇家陵寝设到易州。1729年，雍正帝选定永宁山为陵址后工程开工，泰陵于1737年完工。它是清西陵的第一座帝陵，位于屏护保定侧翼的西北山岭中。

en:
Datong fills the northern Shanxi basin where the Sanggan and Yu rivers lead out toward the Mongolian Plateau. Chinese farming towns and Mongol pastures met here, and horses were the frontier's most valuable trade goods. Pingcheng, inside present-day Datong, was the Northern Wei capital from 398 to 494; the emperors' Buddhist caves at Yungang were cut into the sandstone cliffs west of the city from 460 onward. In 1044 the Liao made the town their Western Capital, and the Ming kept that border role. Xu Da rebuilt the old walls in brick in 1372. By 1444 Datong was one of the Nine Border Garrisons, with a Ming princely fief inside the city, passes toward Mongolia under its watch, and a garrison put as high as 136,000 soldiers and 50,000 horses.

In 1449 Esen's Oirats came through this sector on the invasion that drew the Zhengtong Emperor into the Tumu campaign. The Ming army was destroyed and the emperor taken, and Ming frontier policy around Datong and Xuanfu stayed on the defensive. Raids and licensed horse trade alternated for generations. In 1570 a family quarrel sent Altan Khan's grandson across the border; the Xuan-Da commander Wang Chonggu and Datong grand coordinator Fang Fengshi used the incident to negotiate tribute relations and frontier markets, which softened the border wars. At the Ming-Qing transition Jiang Xiang killed the rebel officer Zhang Tianlin and surrendered Datong in 1645, then turned against the Qing. Dorgon's army took the city in 1649 and carried out a massacre; rebuilding began in 1652. The Drum Tower and the glazed Nine-Dragon Wall still marked the rebuilt streets.
zh:
大同位于山西北部盆地，桑干河、御河从这一带向北通向蒙古高原。农田、城墙和草原牧场在这里相接，马匹则是边境上最值钱的货物。大同城区内的平城曾在398年至494年为北魏都城；460年起，北魏在城西砂岩崖壁上开凿云冈石窟。1044年，辽朝把这里建为西京，明代延续了它的边防地位，徐达又在1372年将旧城加筑为砖城。到1444年，大同已是九边军镇之一，城中有藩王府，境外通向蒙古的关隘受其监视，兵额号称13.6万名军人、5万匹战马。

1449年，也先率领瓦剌军从这一路入犯，把明英宗引向土木堡。明军战败，皇帝被俘，大同、宣府一带的边政此后长期取守势。此后数十年，蒙古骑兵入犯和官府许可的马匹互市交替出现。1570年，俺答汗之孙因家族纷争越境投明，宣大总督王崇古与大同巡抚方逢时借这件事议定封贡和边境互市，边战才缓和下来。明清易代之际，姜瓖杀死农民军将领张天琳，于1645年献城降清，随后又反清。1649年，多尔衮率军破城并下令屠城；1652年城中开始重建，鼓楼和琉璃九龙壁立在修复后的街巷间。

en:
Ningxia joins two landscapes. In the north the Yellow River runs below the Helan range, facing the Ordos: Han canals turned this arid edge into the 'Jiangnan beyond the passes', and the Huamachi salt lakes supplied the Shaanxi markets. In the south the Liupan hills, old Yuanzhou, hold the road between the Guanzhong plain and the steppe; Western Han stud farms grazed cavalry horses there, and Han Wudi and Tang Taizong both came to inspect the frontier and its herds. In 1038 the Tangut Li Yuanhao founded his Western Xia at Xingqing on the northern plain. In 1227 Genghis Khan died at his camp in the Liupan hills while the Mongol armies closed on Xingqing, and the conquerors afterwards named the land Ningxia, 'the pacified Xia'. Under the Ming five guards held the plain and Ningxia became one of the Nine Border Garrisons. Zhu Zhan, the Hongwu Emperor's sixteenth son, took up his fief here in 1397 and compiled the first Ningxia gazetteer. In 1444 his son holds court amid military farms and salt-certificate markets, the Mongols just beyond the wall.

In 1468 Man Si, chief of the settled Mongol 'local Tartar' clans below the Liupan, held the cliff fortress of Shicheng with 20,000 followers; Xiang Zhong and Ma Wensheng starved it through a winter, razed it, and sent Man Si to Beijing for execution. A Ming supreme commander sat at Guyuan over the three garrisons of Ningxia, Yansui and Gansu, moving to Huamachi each autumn against Ordos raiders. In 1592 the retired Mongol-born vice commander Bobei mutinied in Ningxia, killed Grand Coordinator Dang Xin and took forty-seven forts; only Xiao Ruxun's small Pinglu fortress held out. Li Rusong and Ma Gui ringed it with earthworks and flooded it from the Yellow River, and in the ninth month Bobei killed himself, the first of the Wanli reign's Three Great Campaigns. Qing troops came in 1645. In 1697 the Kangxi Emperor used Ningxia as the base of his last campaign against Galdan, sending Fiyanggu and Maska out with two columns. On 3 January 1739 a magnitude-eight earthquake wrecked the Yinchuan plain and killed over 50,000 people.
zh:
宁夏由两片土地拼成：北边是黄河绕着贺兰山、面向鄂尔多斯的冲积平原，南边是六盘山下旧原州的黄土丘陵。北部平原自汉代引黄河水开渠，把这片干旱边地溉成「塞上江南」，东缘花马池的盐湖出产池盐，运往陕西市集；南部草场自西汉起官营养马，汉武帝、唐太宗都曾亲到这一带巡视边防、察看马政。1038年，党项首领李元昊在北部平原的兴庆府建立西夏。1227年，成吉思汗在六盘山的营帐中病逝时，蒙古大军正合围兴庆；战后征服者把这片土地命名为宁夏，取「平定西夏」之意。入明以后平原上设五卫，宁夏列为九边之一。明太祖第十六子朱栴1397年就藩于此，修成宁夏第一部方志。1444年，嗣位的庆王在军屯与盐引市集之间开府，长城之外便是蒙古诸部。

南边并不总是太平。1468年，落籍六盘山北麓的蒙古「土鞑」首领满四聚众两万，据守悬崖上的石城；项忠、马文升围城一冬，断其水草，破城后捣毁石城，满四被押赴北京处死。明廷后来在固原设总制，统辖宁夏、延绥、甘肃三镇，每年秋后移驻花马池，防备鄂尔多斯骑兵。1592年，已致仕的蒙古裔副总兵哱拜在宁夏镇起兵，杀巡抚党馨，连陷河西四十七堡，只有参将萧如薰坚守平虏城不降；李如松、麻贵筑围围城，决黄河水灌城，九月哱拜自尽。这一仗是万历三大征的第一征宁夏之役。1645年清军入据，1697年康熙帝以宁夏为最后一次亲征噶尔丹的基地，费扬古、马斯喀分率两路大军出塞。1739年1月3日，一场约八级的大地震摧毁银川平原，压死五万余人。

en:
Lanzhou occupies a narrow basin where the Yellow River breaks east through the mountains, the last great crossing on the Northern Silk Road before the Hexi Corridor. Han armies founded Jincheng, the 'Golden City', here to guard the crossing, and in 583 the Sui renamed it Lanzhou after Mount Gaolan south of the walls. The Tibetan Empire overran it in 762 and Zhang Yichao recovered it for the Tang in 848, after which it passed through Western Xia, Jin and Mongol hands. Under the Ming it was reduced to a county of Lintao prefecture, but kept a large garrison and became a princely seat: Zhu Ying, fourteenth son of the Hongwu Emperor, moved here as the first Prince of Su in 1399, and his descendants kept their riverside palace to the dynasty's end. In 1385 the garrison officer Yang Lian moved the Zhenyuan crossing to the foot of White Pagoda Mountain, chaining boats into a pontoon bridge tethered to iron pillars cast under the founding generals Feng Sheng and Deng Yu, later called the 'generals' pillars'; for five centuries it was the only bridge on the upper Yellow River. In 1444 Lanzhou was a fortified frontier town of Ming Shaanxi, its soldiers farming military colonies and filling granaries for the posts farther west.

Lanzhou became a subprefecture again in 1477. After retiring in 1541, Duan Xu, a local official who had served in the south, introduced the southern water wheel to his home town: large wheels on the Yellow River bank lifted water into the fields, and more went up along the reach in later years. In 1643 Zhang Xianzhong's rebels stormed the city and killed Zhu Shihong, the last Prince of Su, ending the princedom. Under the Qing, Gansu became a province separate from Shaanxi in 1666, with Lanzhou its capital. In 1738 the Lintao prefecture seat moved inside the walls and the city became Lanzhou prefecture; in 1764 the governor-general of Shaan-Gan moved his yamen from Xi'an, making Lanzhou the headquarters of the entire north-west.
zh:
兰州位于黄河切穿山地东去的狭长河谷盆地，是北方丝绸之路进入河西走廊前最后一个大渡口。汉军在此设立金城县，取「金城汤池」之意，扼守渡口；583年隋代因城南的皋兰山改名兰州。762年吐蕃攻占兰州，848年张议潮举陇右归唐，此后又经西夏、金朝和蒙古相继统治。明代兰州降为临洮府属县，却驻有重兵，还是藩王封国：明太祖第十四子朱楧初封肃王、就藩甘州，1399年移封兰州，子孙在黄河边的肃王府一直住到明末。1385年，兰州卫指挥杨廉把镇远浮桥移到城北白塔山下，以铁缆连锁战船为桥，两岸拴缆的铁柱由开国功臣冯胜、邓愈监铸，后人称作「将军柱」；此后五百年间，它是黄河上游唯一的桥梁。1444年的兰州是明朝陕西边防上的军镇，卫所军士屯田积谷，供应更西边的城堡。

1477年，明廷升兰县为兰州。1541年，在南方做过官的兰州人段续致仕还乡，把南方的水车引入兰州，黄河岸边架起提水灌田的大水车，以后沿河又添了不少。1643年，张献忠的军队攻破兰州，末代肃王朱识鋐被杀，肃藩除国。入清以后，1666年甘肃从陕西分出设省，定兰州为省会；1738年临洮府治移入驻城，改称兰州府；1764年陕甘总督衙门自西安迁来，整个西北的军政衙署都集中到了兰州。

en:
Xi'an, the ancient Chang'an, lies in the Wei valley where the Silk Road entered China proper. The Han founder Liu Bang made it his capital in 202 BC. Tang Chang'an held about a million people: Xuanzang ran a board translating the Indian scriptures he had brought home, the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda went up in 652 to hold them, and a limestone stele of 781 recorded the Church of the East in Chinese and Syriac. With the fall of Tang the city was wrecked and its people forcibly marched to Luoyang. Ming armies took it in 1369 and renamed it Xi'an, 'Western Peace', and from 1370 a new wall and moat girdled the much smaller city. In 1384 the Bell Tower went up where the four main streets met, hung with a Tang bell of 711, and in 1392 the Hongwu Emperor rebuilt the Muslim quarter's Great Mosque in Chinese temple style, facing Mecca to the west. In 1444 Xi'an was the chief city of Shaanxi, a fortified north-western bastion guarding the road to the Hexi Corridor and the caravan trade with the western regions.
