全州是朝鲜半岛西南湖南平原的首邑，全国最丰足的稻米产地，全罗道监营就设在此城。892年，叛将甄萱以当时的完山为都，建立后百济。四十年后，他的儿子甄神剑起兵将他推翻，囚禁在金山寺；甄萱逃脱后投奔老对手王建，又随高丽大军回到全州，于936年攻灭后百济。新王朝把这里视作王室本贯之地：朝鲜开国君主李成桂出身全州李氏，1380年他在荒山击败倭寇后，在先祖穆祖旧居所在的梧木台设庆功宴。太宗于1410年建庆基殿供奉太祖御真，1439年又建实录阁收藏王朝实录。1444年，全罗道监司在这座城墙环绕的城中统辖全道。

1592年，日军为夺取全罗的稻米而来。8月14日，权栗以约千人据守梨峙，挡住小早川隆景约一万五千人的军队，封住了从金山通向全州的道路；次年他又指挥了幸州之战。第二次入侵时全州终究不守：1597年9月南原陷落后，日军进占全州，直到撤退。全州本实录是被本城人救下来的：日军逼近时，庆基殿参奉吴希吉与儒生安义、孙弘禄把太祖御真和实录移入内藏山，其余三部实录都毁于兵火。庆基殿于1614年重建；后来朝廷以全州本为底本新印五部，分藏各处山中史库。

en:
Sakam was Siraya land on the coastal plain behind the Tayouan sandbar, where Taiwan-fu and later Tainan took shape. Its villages had close ties with Sinkan and faced the shallow Taikang inlet, which separated their fields from the anchorage beyond the sandbar. Villagers farmed the coastal plain, hunted deer in the grasslands and managed access to the landing places through their own village affairs. In 1444 no larger island ruler controlled the lagoon; Siraya communities held the landings, deer grounds and fields around Sakam.

The Dutch East India Company put the Tayouan anchorage to use in 1624 by building Fort Zeelandia as its base for trade with China and Japan. On 20 January 1625 Governor Marten Sonck bought a tract at Sakam from the Sinkan people for fifteen pieces of flowered cloth and laid out the Provintia settlement. After campaigns against neighbouring Siraya villages in 1635-36, the company brought in Chinese farmers, who turned much of the plain into rice paddies and sugar fields; deerskins, rice and sugar moved out through the Dutch forts. The Guo Huaiyi rising of 1652 was put down with Sinkan help, and Fort Provintia was built at Sakam in 1653.

Zheng Chenggong entered the lagoon through the Luerhmen channel in 1661, took Provintia and forced Zeelandia to surrender on 1 February 1662. Sakam became the seat of his Kingdom of Tungning, and in 1665 the Zheng administration built Taiwan's first Confucian temple there. Qing forces took the island in 1683, and Taiwan Prefecture was established the next year as its walled city spread over old Sakam. During the Lin Shuangwen rebellion of 1787-1788, rebels overran much of the surrounding countryside while Taiwan-fu held out until Fuk'anggan's army crossed from the mainland and restored Qing control.
zh:
赤崁是大员沙洲内侧滨海平原上的西拉雅地域，后来的台湾府和台南就在这里成形。这里的村社与新港社关系密切，村田外是水浅的台江内海，潟湖之外才是沙洲外的锚地。居民耕种滨海平原、在草地猎鹿，并通过村社事务管理登陆地。1444年，岛上还没有更大的政权控制这片潟湖，西拉雅诸社掌握着赤崁一带的登陆地、猎场和农田。

1624年，荷兰东印度公司利用大员锚地修建热兰遮城，作为对中国、日本贸易的基地。1625年1月20日，台湾长官宋克以十五匹花布向新港人购得赤崁一片土地，开辟普罗民遮。1635至1636年征讨邻近西拉雅村社后，公司招来汉人农民，把大片平原改造成稻田和蔗田；鹿皮、米和糖经荷兰人的城堡外运。1652年郭怀一起事被荷兰人联合新港等社镇压，1653年普罗民遮城在赤崁建成。

1661年，郑成功从鹿耳门水道进入台江内海，先取普罗民遮城，再迫使热兰遮城于1662年2月1日投降。赤崁成为东宁王国的治所，1665年郑氏官府又在这里建成台湾第一座孔庙。1683年清军取得台湾，次年设置台湾府，府城在旧赤崁一带扩展。1787至1788年林爽文抗清时，起事者控制了城外大片地方，台湾府城坚守到福康安率军从大陆渡海，才恢复清朝的控制。

en:
Known in older Chinese records as Shule, Kashgar is the oasis below the Pamirs where roads from Ferghana, the Tarim Basin and the high mountain passes meet. Its rivers water fields and bazaars in otherwise arid country. In 1444 this Sunni Muslim Turki merchant town was rebuilding after Timurid wars: the Eastern Chagatai khanate had recovered it in 1432, while Dughlat emirs kept much local power. The Id Kah Mosque had been built two years earlier by Saqsiz Mirza and incorporated parts of a religious complex from 996, giving Kashgar a large new congregational mosque for its Friday prayers. The oasis had been an early Muslim city of the Turkic east under the Karakhanids, then passed through Qara Khitai and Chinggisid realms before Timur's armies took it. Wool, livestock and caravan supplies changed hands in its bazaars.

Dughlat control ended in 1514, when Sultan Said Khan defeated Mirza Abu Bakr, founded the Yarkand khanate and kept his first court at Kashgar before moving it to Yarkand. Later, rival Naqshbandi networks known as the White Mountain and Black Mountain khojas divided the cities of Altishahr. In 1680 the White Mountain leader Afaq Khoja called in Galdan's Dzungar army; the Chagatai khans became puppets, and Tsewang Rabtan later imposed direct Dzungar rule. Qing forces took Kashgar in 1759 while suppressing the revolt of Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan, then stationed a garrison and imperial councillor there. Id Kah was rebuilt as a golden-brick mosque in 1798. By 1821 Kashgar was a guarded Qing market on the Pamir roads, with Kokand and exiled khojas beyond the mountains.
zh:
喀什噶尔在汉文古籍中称疏勒，是帕米尔脚下的绿洲，费尔干纳、塔里木盆地和高山山口的道路在此相接。绿洲河流浇灌着干旱地带中的农田和巴扎。1444年，这座逊尼派突厥语穆斯林商城正从帖木儿系战争中恢复：东察合台汗国1432年收复此城，杜格拉特埃米尔仍掌握大量地方权力。艾提尕尔清真寺刚在两年前由沙克色孜·米尔扎建成，建筑还并入了996年宗教建筑群的一部分，为喀什噶尔提供了举行周五聚礼的大型清真寺。喀喇汗王朝时期，这里已是突厥语东方较早的穆斯林城市之一，后来又经历西辽和成吉思汗系政权，最后被帖木儿的军队攻占。羊毛、牲畜和商队补给都在巴扎交易。

1514年，萨亦德汗击败米尔扎·阿布·伯克尔，建立叶尔羌汗国，先在喀什噶尔设庭，后来才迁往叶尔羌，杜格拉特人的控制到此结束。此后，纳合昔班底教团中的白山派与黑山派和卓网络彼此敌对，分裂了回疆诸城。1680年，白山派首领阿帕克和卓引来噶尔丹的准噶尔军队，察合台系汗王沦为傀儡，策妄阿拉布坦后来又改为准噶尔直接统治。1759年，清军在平定波罗尼都和霍集占之乱时攻占喀什噶尔，随后驻军并派遣参赞大臣。1798年，艾提尕尔清真寺以黄褐色砖重建。到1821年，喀什噶尔仍是清朝在帕米尔道路上设防的商市，山外有浩罕和流亡和卓活动。

en:
Chanderi stands on the border of Malwa and Bundelkhand, among hills, lakes and forest south-west of the Betwa River, where the road out of Malwa runs north toward the Ganges plain. The town lives by cloth: Koli weavers settled there in the mid-1300s, and their handlooms made its name for sheer cotton and silk, later sold as Chanderi saris, while Jain merchants built a cluster of temples. Sultan Mahmud Khalji I of Malwa took the town in 1438 after a siege of several months, so in 1444 it is a fresh frontier acquisition of the Malwa sultanate. Passing through in 1445 after beating the Jaunpur army at Kalpi, the sultan ordered the seven-storey Koshak Mahal, a Mandu-style palace of which only three floors were ever finished.

The fort's hardest years came with the break-up of Malwa. Medini Rai, a wazir of Sultan Mahmud II who had gone over to Rana Sanga of Mewar, made Chanderi the capital of the Rajput kingdom the Rana gave him. After beating Rana Sanga at Khanwa, Babur stormed the fort in January 1528: that night the defenders' women burned in jauhar, and at dawn the men smeared the ashes on their foreheads, put on saffron kesariya robes and rode out to die in the rite called saka. Puran Mal retook the fort in 1529, and through the 1530s and 1540s it changed hands among Bahadur Shah of Gujarat, Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, who made it a Sur frontier post. Akbar's armies took it with the rest of Malwa in 1562 and made it a sarkar of the Malwa subah. The Bundelas seized it before the end of the century and held it under Ram Sab, a son of Raja Madhukar of Orchha; Devi Singh Bundela became its governor in 1646, and his line kept the town until 1811, when Jean Baptiste Filose captured it for Daulat Rao Scindia of Gwalior.
zh:
钱德里地处摩腊婆与本德尔肯德交界、贝特瓦河西南的丘陵湖泊林间，摩腊婆北上恒河平原的大路从这里经过。这座城靠织布立足：14世纪中叶科利族织工到此定居，手工织机织出的轻薄棉布和丝绸远近知名，后来以「钱德里纱丽」行销；耆那教商人也在城中建起成群庙宇。摩腊婆苏丹马哈茂德·卡尔吉一世围攻数月，于1438年拿下此城，所以1444年的钱德里还是苏丹国新到手的边镇。1445年，苏丹在卡尔皮击败江布尔军队后途经此地，下令修建七层的科沙克宫；这座曼杜风格的宫殿最终只建成三层。

堡垒最纷扰的岁月随摩腊婆的瓦解而来。梅迪尼·拉伊本是苏丹马哈茂德二世的维齐尔，投奔梅瓦尔的拉纳·桑加后，受封以钱德里为都的拉杰普特王国。巴布尔在坎瓦击溃拉纳·桑加后，于1528年1月强攻此堡：当夜守军女眷行乔哈尔投火自焚，黎明时分男人们把灰烬抹上额头、披上藏红色的凯萨里亚战袍，出城赴死，是为「萨卡」。普兰·马尔1529年收复堡垒；1530至1540年代，它在古吉拉特的巴哈杜尔·沙、胡马雍和舍尔沙之间几度易手，舍尔沙把它作为苏尔王朝的边防据点。阿克巴的大军1562年征服摩腊婆全境，钱德里成为摩腊婆苏巴下辖的一个萨卡尔。本德拉人在16世纪末夺取此城，由奥尔查王公马杜卡尔之子拉姆·萨卜据守；1646年德维·辛格·本德拉受任城主，其家族一直保有此地，直到1811年让-巴蒂斯特·菲洛斯为瓜廖尔的道拉特·拉奥·辛迪亚将它攻占。

en:
Cumaná stands at the mouth of the Manzanares, where the river enters the Gulf of Cariaco; in the speech of its first inhabitants the name was said to mean 'union of sea and river'. In 1444 the coast belonged to the Cumanagoto and Chaima, peoples whose forebears had come from the Orinoco basin, and divers gathered pearls on the beds off the island of Cubagua.

The pearls brought the first Spaniards. From 1500 the pearl fishers of Nueva Cádiz on Cubagua came to the river for fresh water, and Franciscan friars opened a station they called Puerto de las Perlas, the first mission on the Spanish Main. On 3 October 1515 Cumanagoto led by the cacique Maragüey burned the convent and killed the friars in revenge for slave raids. Gonzalo de Ocampo answered with a punitive expedition and a fort named Nueva Toledo, and Bartolomé de las Casas arrived there in 1521 hoping to colonise without soldiers, only to leave after quarrelling with Ocampo. Refounded more than once, the town took its lasting form in 1569, when Diego Fernández de Serpa made it the capital of New Andalusia under the name Cumaná.

Across the gulf the salt pans of Araya drew Dutch fleets loading salt for the North Sea herring trade. In 1622 more than forty Dutch warships came to seize the peninsula and were driven out, after which Spain fortified Araya to keep the Dutch from settling. French buccaneers sacked Cumaná in 1676, and four years later the corsair Michel de Grammont took the town with fifty men. Antonio José de Sucre, the Gran Mariscal de Ayacucho and one of the principal generals of South American independence, was born here, and on 15 July 1811 Cumaná declared against Spanish rule.
zh:
库马纳位于曼萨纳雷斯河注入卡里亚科湾的河口，据说这个名字在最早居民的语言里意为「海与河的交汇」。1444年，这片海岸属于库马纳戈托人和柴马人，他们的祖先来自奥里诺科河流域；近海的库瓦瓜岛一带有珠贝床，潜水人在此采珠。

是珍珠引来了最早的西班牙人。1500年起，库瓦瓜岛新加的斯城的采珠人来河口取淡水，方济各会修士在此开辟「珍珠港」，这是西班牙人在美洲大陆上的第一个传教站。1515年10月3日，酋长马拉圭伊率领库马纳戈托人为报复猎奴袭击，焚毁修院、杀死修士。冈萨洛·德奥坎波以讨伐作答，修起名为新托莱多的要塞；1521年，巴托洛梅·德拉斯卡萨斯来到这里，想不靠士兵和平拓殖，却因与奥坎波反目而离去。城镇此后几经重建，到1569年迭戈·费尔南德斯·德塞尔帕将它定名库马纳、设为新安达卢西亚首府，才稳定下来。

海湾对岸的阿拉亚盐田引来荷兰船队，为北海的鲱鱼腌制业运盐。1622年，四十多艘荷兰战舰来夺取半岛，被西班牙人击退，王室随即在阿拉亚修筑要塞，以防荷兰人在此立足。1676年法国海盗洗劫库马纳，四年后海盗米歇尔·德格拉蒙仅率五十人就攻下此城。有「阿亚库乔大元帅」之称的安东尼奥·何塞·德苏克雷是南美独立的主要将领之一，就出生在库马纳；1811年7月15日，库马纳宣布脱离西班牙统治。

en:
At Angostura, the 'narrows' far upstream from the Orinoco's delta, the great river contracts from a broad floodplain into a rocky gap barely 800 metres wide, the surest crossing on its lower course. This was Carib country in 1444: river villages planted cassava and fished the eddies, canoe traders passed between the coast and the interior, and no raiding party could slip through the strait unseen. The crossing belonged to the peoples of the river.

Spain's first town on the lower Orinoco, Santo Tomé de Guayana, was founded near the Caroní in 1576 and sacked by Dutch raiders three years later. Antonio de Berrío refounded it in 1595, and in 1617 Walter Raleigh's last expedition to Guayana stormed the place; his son Wat was killed in the assault, and Raleigh was beheaded in England the following year. The rebuilt town was burned by English and Dutch raiders in the 1620s and again by the Dutch in 1637. Only in 1764 did Joaquín Moreno de Mendoza fix the town permanently at the narrows, as Santo Tomás de la Nueva Guayana de la Angostura del Orinoco, soon shortened to Angostura, capital of Guayana Province. Alexander von Humboldt passed through in 1800. In the wars of independence Manuel Piar's patriots broke Miguel de la Torre's royalist army at San Félix, on the Chirica tableland, on 11 April 1817; the royalists abandoned Angostura in July, and the town became the republic's provisional capital. Piar, the general who had conquered Guayana, then fell out with Bolívar: a court martial condemned him, and on 16 October 1817 he was shot against the wall of Angostura's cathedral on Bolívar's order. On 15 February 1819 Bolívar opened the Congress of Angostura there, which proclaimed Gran Colombia before the year ended and sat on until 1821.
zh:
安戈斯图拉意为「狭口」，在奥里诺科河三角洲上游很远的内陆，浩荡河面在此从开阔的泛滥平原收束成一道仅800米宽的岩石水道，是下游最可靠的渡口。1444年，这里是加勒比人的地方：河畔村落种植木薯、在涡流中捕鱼，独木舟商人往来于海岸与内陆之间，任何袭掠队伍都无法悄悄穿过狭口。渡口掌握在河畔原住民手中。

西班牙人在奥里诺科河下游建立的第一座城镇圣托梅·德·圭亚那，1576年设在卡罗尼河附近，三年后就被荷兰袭掠者洗劫。安东尼奥·德·贝里奥1595年重建此城；1617年，沃尔特·雷利最后一次远征圭亚那时猛攻此地，儿子瓦特在攻城中战死，雷利本人次年在英格兰被斩首。重建的城镇1620年代被英荷袭掠者焚毁，1637年再遭荷兰人放火。直到1764年，华金·莫雷诺·德·门多萨才把城址永久定在狭口，全名为「奥里诺科河狭口的新圭亚那圣托马斯」，很快简称安戈斯图拉，为圭亚那省首府。1800年，亚历山大·冯·洪堡途经此地。独立战争中，1817年4月11日，曼努埃尔·皮亚尔的爱国军在奇里卡台地的圣费利克斯击溃米格尔·德·拉·托雷的保王军；保王军7月弃城，安戈斯图拉成为共和国的临时首都。为共和国拿下圭亚那的皮亚尔随后与玻利瓦尔反目，军事法庭裁定他有罪，1817年10月16日，他奉玻利瓦尔之命在安戈斯图拉大教堂墙前被枪决。1819年2月15日，玻利瓦尔在此召开安戈斯图拉议会，议会年底宣布成立大哥伦比亚，会期延续到1821年。

en:
The Essequibo rises in the Acarai Mountains and runs 1,014 kilometres through forest, savanna and tidal islands to the Atlantic, the largest river between the Orinoco and the Amazon. In 1444 its lower banks and swampy shore were Lokono country, the mainland Arawak people. Villagers farmed, fished and travelled by canoe, carrying river and coastal produce while no European fort commanded the mouth.

European ships reached the estuary in 1498. The river became a route into Guiana for seekers of El Dorado, especially after Lawrence Kemys, Walter Raleigh's second-in-command, followed it in 1596 toward waters he mistook for Lake Parime and the gold city of Manoa. In 1616 Zeelanders under Joost van der Hooge began Fort Kyk-Over-Al at the meeting of the Essequibo, Mazaruni and Cuyuni channels; its Dutch name referred to the view over the rivers, and by 1672 it was a two-storey brick post. Dutch traders dealt with Lokono communities, while enslaved Africans worked cotton, indigo and cacao plantations and later sugar fields. British forces took the colony in 1665, French raiders plundered it, and Zeeland retook it two years later; it changed sides again during the wars of the 1780s. By 1800 Essequibo and neighbouring Demerara held about 380 sugarcane plantations, and the Treaty of London confirmed British rule in 1814.
zh:
埃塞奎博河发源于阿卡拉伊山脉，穿过森林、稀树草原和潮汐岛屿，奔流1014公里注入大西洋，是奥里诺科河与亚马孙河之间最大的河流。1444年，河下游两岸与沼泽海岸是大陆阿拉瓦克人洛科诺人的土地。村民务农、捕鱼，乘独木舟往来，转运河上与沿海物产，当时河口还没有欧洲堡垒。

欧洲船只1498年到达河口。这条河后来成了寻找黄金国者进入圭亚那的通道；1596年，沃尔特·雷利的副手劳伦斯·凯米斯溯河而行，把所见水域误认作帕里梅湖和黄金城马诺阿。1616年，约斯特·范德霍赫率领泽兰人在埃塞奎博河、马扎鲁尼河与库尤尼河汊道相接的位置修建凯克-奥弗阿尔堡，堡名来自荷兰语中俯瞰诸河的意思，到1672年已是一座两层砖石要塞。荷兰商人同洛科诺社群交易，被奴役的非洲人则在棉花、靛蓝、可可种植园和后来的甘蔗地里劳作。1665年英军夺取殖民地，法兰西袭掠者随后洗劫此地，泽兰两年后收复；18世纪80年代的战争中，控制权又数次易手。到1800年，埃塞奎博与邻近的德梅拉拉共有约380处甘蔗种植园，1814年《伦敦条约》确认英国统治。

en:
The Demerara River rises in the central Guiana rain forest and flows 346 kilometres north through tidal creeks to a shallow Atlantic estuary. Its Lokono name meant the river of letter wood, a darkly marked hardwood used for bows and fine woodwork. In 1444 Lokono communities fished, planted and moved by canoe along its banks, using the waterway to pass between rain forest, savanna and coast. No European fort or sugar mill then stood on the shore.

Dutch traders were using the river by 1691. On 18 October 1745 the Dutch West India Company made Demerara a separate colony on the unused eastern side of the Essequibo claim, and its founding orders told settlers to keep peace with Amerindians and respect their freedom and lands. Sugar arrived with the first planter, Andries Pieterse: within six months 18 large sugar plantations and 50 smaller holdings had been laid out. Enslaved Africans cleared the fields, cut the cane and worked the boilers, while planters smuggled supplies and people from the English Caribbean when the company could not meet demand. In 1755 the administration moved upriver to Borsselen Island and the lower guard post grew into Stabroek. When Cuffy's Berbice revolt began on 23 February 1763, Governor Laurens Storm van 's Gravesande allied with Lokono, Kalina, Warao and Akawaio fighters, kept the rising out of Demerara and sent 50 soldiers east. Nearly 200 plantations lined the river by 1780, shipping sugar, coffee and cotton through the estuary; the colony's cane gave Demerara sugar its name.

The Napoleonic wars turned that estuary into a repeated prize. British forces took Demerara without fighting in 1781, French forces seized it in 1782, and the 1783 Treaty of Paris returned it to the Dutch. A West Demerara slave revolt was crushed in 1795. The British took the colony again in 1796, handed it back under the 1802 Peace of Amiens, retook it in 1803 and received formal cession in 1814. Stabroek was renamed Georgetown in 1812.
zh:
德梅拉拉河发源于圭亚那中部雨林，向北流经346公里的潮汐河汊，注入水浅的大西洋河口。它的洛科诺语名称意为「蛇纹木之河」；蛇纹木纹理深暗，可制弓和精细木器。1444年，洛科诺人在河两岸捕鱼、耕作，乘独木舟往来，把这条水道当作进出雨林、稀树草原和海岸的通路。此时岸边还没有欧洲堡垒或制糖作坊。

1691年时，荷兰商人已经在使用这条河。1745年10月18日，荷兰西印度公司在埃塞奎博属地东侧尚未开垦的土地上设立德梅拉拉殖民地，建殖命令要求定居者与印第安人和平相处，尊重他们的自由和土地。第一个种植园主安德里斯·彼得瑟到来后，甘蔗种植迅速铺开；六个月内，当地已划出18座大型甘蔗种植园和50处较小农庄。被奴役的非洲人砍伐林地、收割甘蔗并操作煮糖锅；当公司满足不了需求时，种植园主还从英属加勒比走私物资和人口。1755年，行政中心迁到上游的博瑟伦岛，河口哨站发展为斯塔布鲁克。1763年2月23日科菲领导的伯比斯起义爆发后，总督劳伦斯·斯托姆·范·斯赫拉夫桑德同洛科诺、卡利纳、瓦劳和阿卡瓦约战士结盟，把起义挡在德梅拉拉之外，并派出50名士兵东援。到1780年，河两岸已有近200座种植园，蔗糖、咖啡和棉花经河口运出；德梅拉拉糖也因这块殖民地得名。

拿破仑战争使这个河口反复易手。英军1781年兵不血刃占领德梅拉拉，法军1782年将其夺取，1783年《巴黎条约》又把它归还荷兰。1795年，西德梅拉拉的奴隶起义被镇压。英军1796年再度夺取殖民地，1802年依《亚眠和约》交还，1803年再次占领，并于1814年正式获得割让。1812年，斯塔布鲁克改名为乔治敦。

en:
Paramaribo stands on the west bank of the Suriname River, about ten kilometres from the Atlantic, on a low coast cut by creeks and lined with mangroves. In 1444 Lokono (Arawak) communities grew cassava on raised village mounds, fished the river mouth and traded along the shore, while Kalina (Carib) groups moved between the coast and the inland savanna. Dutch seamen found an indigenous village near the mouth called Parmurbo, and the town that grew on the spot kept its name. The canoe routes up the river still belonged to the peoples who used them.

Traders of several nations tried posts at the river mouth; the first colony to last was English. In 1650 settlers sent by Francis Willoughby, governor of Barbados, landed here, and their strongpoint above the river became Fort Willoughby. During the Second Anglo-Dutch War a Zeeland squadron under Abraham Crijnssen sailed up the Suriname and bombarded it until the English ran out of ammunition, three hours after the first shot. The Peace of Breda in 1667 let each side keep what it had conquered: the Dutch kept Suriname, the English kept New Amsterdam, the future New York. The fort was renamed Fort Zeelandia, and Paramaribo became the chief town of the Society of Suriname, the chartered company that from 1683 ran the river plantations where enslaved Africans cut sugar and grew coffee, cocoa and cotton. Thousands escaped the estates for the rainforest; the long Maroon wars ended in treaties that left the inland rivers in Maroon hands. British troops occupied the colony from 1799 to 1802 and again from 1804 to 1816. Paramaribo was built almost entirely of wood, and in January 1821 a fire destroyed more than 400 houses in a single night.
zh:
帕拉马里博在苏里南河西岸，距大西洋约十公里，城外是河汊纵横、红树林连绵的低海岸。1444年，洛科诺（阿拉瓦克）人在堆高的土岗上建村、种木薯，在河口捕鱼并沿岸交易；卡利纳（加勒比）人往来于海岸与内陆草原之间。荷兰水手后来在河口见到一个叫帕尔穆尔博的原住民村落，兴起于河畔的城镇便沿用了这个名字。那时溯河而上的独木舟水路仍属于使用它们的原住民。

河口先后有各国商人试设贸易站，第一个站住脚的殖民地却是英国人建的。1650年，巴巴多斯总督弗朗西斯·威洛比派来的移民登岸，河畔据点定名威洛比堡。第二次英荷战争中，亚伯拉罕·克莱因森率领泽兰舰队溯苏里南河而上，炮轰三小时后英军弹尽。1667年《布雷达和约》规定各方保留战时夺占的土地：荷兰人保有苏里南，英国人保全新阿姆斯特丹，也就是后来的纽约。堡垒改名泽兰迪亚堡，帕拉马里博成为苏里南协会的首城；这家1683年获许成立的特许公司经营沿河种植园，役使非洲奴隶收割甘蔗、种植咖啡、可可和棉花。数以千计的奴隶逃出种植园、进入雨林，漫长的马龙战争最终以一系列和约告终，内河一带留在马龙人手中。英军曾在1799—1802年、1804—1816年两度占领殖民地。帕拉马里博几乎是一座全木之城，1821年1月的一场大火一夜之间烧毁400多栋房屋。

en:
Cayenne occupies an island where the Cayenne and Montsinéry rivers meet the sea, behind a wall of mangroves. In 1444 Kali'na (Galibi) communities held the shore and the coastal islands, while Arawak and Palikur groups fished the beaches and creek mouths. They planted cassava and moved along the coast by dugout; the riverside hill bears the name of Cépérou, the Galibi chief who later sold it to the French. Spanish ships reconnoitred the coast but never settled, and no European house yet stood on the island.

In 1643 Charles Poncet de Brétigny landed with 400 settlers, bought the hill from the Galibis and raised Fort Cépérou. He brought slavery with him and treated the indigenous people so harshly that they rose against the French; by 1648 only 25 settlers were alive. Dutch traders occupied the ruins and built sugar works around Fort Nassau, until French forces under La Barre and Tracy secured the colony in 1664. It did not stay quietly French: raiders from English Suriname sacked the town in 1667 before the Peace of Breda gave it back, and in 1676 a Dutch fleet under Jacob Binckes captured Cayenne, only for Jean d'Estrées to storm it in a night attack that December. Plantations then spread around the town, worked by enslaved Africans growing sugar, indigo, cotton and spices. The Convention abolished slavery in 1794 and the decree was proclaimed in Guiana on 14 June; Napoleon restored it in December 1802. In those years the Directory used Guiana as a place of deportation for beaten politicians, and Jean-Charles Pichegru, the republican general sent to Cayenne after the coup of 1797, escaped and made his way to London. An Anglo-Portuguese force took the town in 1809 and administered it from Brazil until the last occupiers withdrew in 1817.
zh:
卡宴城在卡宴河与蒙特西内里河共同入海处的一座岛上，前方是一道红树林海岸。1444年，卡利纳（加利比）人据有海岸和近岸岛屿，阿拉瓦克人与帕利库尔人在滩涂和河口捕鱼。他们种植木薯，乘独木舟沿岸往来；河畔山丘以加利比首领塞佩鲁的名字命名，法国人后来正是从他手中买下山头。西班牙船只勘察过这片海岸却没有定居，岛上也还没有一间欧洲人的房屋。

1643年，夏尔·庞塞·德·布雷蒂尼率400名移民登岸，从加利比人手中买下山丘，筑起塞佩鲁堡。他带来奴隶制，又严酷压榨原住民，原住民愤而反抗；到1648年，移民只剩25人。荷兰商人占据废墟，在拿骚堡周围办起制糖作坊，直到1664年拉巴尔和特拉西率领的法军拿下殖民地。但它没能安稳地留在法国手里：1667年，来自英属苏里南的袭掠者洗劫此城，《布雷达和约》又把它归还法国；1676年雅各布·宾克斯率荷兰舰队攻占卡宴，让·德斯特雷随即在同年12月趁夜强攻收复。此后种植园在城镇四周铺开，非洲奴隶在园中种植甘蔗、靛蓝、棉花和香料。1794年国民公会废除奴隶制，法令于6月14日在圭亚那公布，拿破仑却在1802年12月予以恢复。这几年间，督政府把圭亚那当作流放政敌的地方，共和派将领让-夏尔·皮舍格吕在1797年果月政变后被押到卡宴，后来越狱，辗转逃到伦敦。1809年英葡联军攻占卡宴，由巴西方面管理，最后一批占领军1817年才撤离。

en:
The mangrove shore and seasonally flooded plains of Amapá run along the north side of the Amazon delta, with rainforest rising behind the coast. In 1444 the land belonged to Arawak- and Carib-speaking peoples, among them the Tucuju who gave the shore its early name, as well as the Waiãpi, Palikur and Maracá-Cunani. They farmed raised earth plots, fished the tidal channels and tended groves of bacaba palms; the fruit gave Macapá its Tupi name macapaba, 'place of many bacabas'. Their rivers reached straight into the Amazon mouth, but no European town or garrison stood on the coast.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón sighted this shore in February 1500, off a river mouth so wide the sea water ran fresh, and Francisco de Orellana later claimed the whole coast for Spain as Nueva Andalucía after descending the Amazon. English and Dutch traders built posts there in the early 1600s, among them the forts of Nassau and Muturu, until expeditions from Pará drove them out; in 1637 the Portuguese Crown created the Captaincy of Cabo do Norte. The French pressed in from Cayenne, and although the Treaty of Utrecht fixed the border with French Guiana in 1713, French settlers and soldiers kept crossing it. A Portuguese military post set up in 1738 grew into the town of São José de Macapá. From 1764 the crown built a riverside fortress there as part of the Marquis of Pombal's Amazon defence, on a scale matched only by the Real Forte Príncipe da Beira; Indian labourers sickened and black slaves escaped, so the walls took eighteen years to finish. In 1808 and 1809 Luso-Brazilian troops and a British squadron used the area as a base for their campaign against Cayenne.
zh:
阿马帕的红树林海岸与季节性泛滥平原沿亚马孙三角洲北岸展开，岸后是连绵的雨林。1444年，这里的居民是说阿拉瓦克语和加勒比语的诸族群，包括为海岸赢得早期名称的图库鲁人，以及瓦亚皮人、帕利库尔人和马拉卡-库纳尼人。他们垒起土台耕作，在潮水河汊里捕鱼，经营巴卡巴棕榈林；马卡帕的名字就来自图皮语的马卡帕巴，意为「巴卡巴果繁多之地」。内陆河汊直通亚马孙河口，但此时岸上还没有欧洲人的城镇和驻军。

1500年2月，维森特·亚涅斯·平松望见这片海岸，船外是一个宽到海水变淡的河口。弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳顺亚马孙河而下后，曾替西班牙把整条海岸命名为新安达卢西亚。17世纪初，英国和荷兰商人在此设立据点，其中包括拿骚要塞和穆图鲁要塞，最后被来自帕拉的远征军逐走；1637年，葡萄牙王室设立北角都督辖区。法国人从卡宴方向不断进逼，1713年《乌得勒支和约》划定了与法属圭亚那的边界，法国移民和军队却照样越界。1738年设立的葡萄牙军站后来发展为圣若泽·德·马卡帕镇；1764年起，葡萄牙王室在这里修建河畔要塞，作为庞巴尔侯爵亚马孙防御工程的一环，工程规模巨大，印第安劳工染病、黑奴逃亡，城墙修了十八年才完工。1808至1809年，葡属巴西军队和一支英国分舰队以这一带为基地，出兵进攻卡宴。

en:
Guajará Bay, where the Guamá River meets the Pará channel beside Marajó Island, opens onto the mouth of the Amazon. The Tupinambá knew the broad water as Guaçu Paraná, and in 1444 their canoes worked the igarapés and flooded forests between fishing grounds, gardens and camps; the Pacajá lived along the same shores. Marajoara exchange networks had for centuries carried pottery and forest produce between the islands, but no European ship had yet rounded Marajó, and no fort commanded the water road from the great river to the Atlantic.

The Portuguese built one to keep rivals out. In January 1616 Francisco Caldeira Castelo Branco, sent from Brazil to stop French, Dutch and English traders entering the Amazon, anchored in the bay and ran up a thatched wooden fort he named Presépio, the Crib. Around it grew Feliz Lusitânia, later called Belém. The Tupinambá stormed the fort in January 1619 under their chief Guaimiaba, and fighting over the settlement ran on to 1621. In 1625 the crown set up the Haver-o-Peso post to weigh and tax everything that passed, from European cloth and iron to cacao and the barks, roots and seeds the Portuguese called drogas do sertão. Sugar, cattle, rice, cotton and coffee each had their turn as the district's staple. In 1772 the town became capital of the State of Grão-Pará and Rio Negro, a colony answering directly to Lisbon, and only in 1775 was it joined to Brazil. From 1793 the October Círio de Nazaré drew canoe-loads of river people into the town for the candle procession of Our Lady of Nazareth.
zh:
瓜雅拉湾在瓜马河汇入帕拉河道处，隔着马拉若岛朝向大西洋，是亚马逊河的入海口之一。1444年，图皮南巴人把这片宽阔水域称作瓜苏巴拉纳，独木舟穿行于溪流和泛滥林间，往来渔场、园圃和营地；帕卡雅人也住在同一带岸边。马拉若人的交换网络数百年来在各岛间转运陶器和林产品，但此时还没有欧洲船绕过马拉若岛，也没有要塞守着这条大河通往大西洋的水路。

葡萄牙人来此，为的是把这条水路对别人关上。1616年1月，弗朗西斯科·卡尔代拉·卡斯特洛·布兰科奉命从巴西北上，阻止法国、荷兰和英国商人进入亚马逊河；他在瓜雅拉湾停泊，筑起一座茅草顶木堡，取名普雷塞皮奥，意为圣诞马槽。堡周围发展出幸福卢西塔尼亚定居点，后来改名贝伦。1619年1月，图皮南巴人在首领瓜伊米阿巴率领下攻下堡垒，围绕定居点的战事一直打到1621年。1625年，王室设立阿韦罗佩索税馆，过港货物一律称重征税，既有欧洲的布匹和铁器，也有可可和葡萄牙人称为「林野药料」的树皮、根茎和种子。蔗糖、养牛、稻米、棉花和咖啡先后成为这一地区的支柱产业。1772年，贝伦成为格劳帕拉与里奥内格罗国的首府，这块殖民地直属里斯本，1775年才并入巴西。自1793年起，每年十月的纳扎勒圣烛游行都会把一船船沿河居民载到城里，持烛前往纳扎勒圣母像前。

en:
Maranhão is the island-and-bay coast where the Mearim, Pindaré and Itapecuru reach the Atlantic around Upaon-Açu, the large island the Tupi knew by that name. Mangrove channels cut the shore, and seasonally flooded plains stretch inland from the river mouths. In 1444 Guajajara, Urubu and Tupinambá communities farmed and fished on the island and mainland, while Timbira and Sakamekra groups held the inland forests and savannahs. Canoes moved through the estuaries, but no European fort or factory yet stood on the coast.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón sighted the shore in 1500, and the Portuguese crown included it in the Maranhão grants from 1535. The first lasting settlement was French: Jacques Riffault left men on Upaon-Açu in 1594, and Daniel de La Touche and François de Razilly founded Saint-Louis in 1612 as the seat of Equinoctial France. A Portuguese expedition from Pernambuco took the town in 1615 and renamed it São Luís. In 1621 it became capital of the Estado do Maranhão e Grão-Pará, the base for missions and expansion toward the Amazon; the Dutch West India Company occupied the island from 1641 to 1644. Planters and traders later clashed over crown rules for Indigenous labour and the monopoly of the Maranhão Trading Company, issues behind the Beckman revolt of 1684. Cotton spread through the lowlands in the late eighteenth century, grown largely by enslaved African workers, and São Luís became a busy cotton port before the boom faltered after 1800.
zh:
马拉尼昂是一片岛屿与海湾交错的海岸，梅阿林河、平达雷河和伊塔佩库鲁河在图皮人称作乌帕翁阿苏的大岛周围注入大西洋。岸边分布着红树林水道，河口以内是季节性泛滥平原。1444年时，瓜雅雅拉人、乌鲁布人和图皮南巴人等图皮语社群在岛上与大陆农耕捕鱼，廷比拉人和萨卡梅克拉人等热依语群体则占据内陆林地和草原。独木舟在河口间往来，但欧洲人的要塞或商馆还没有出现在这片海岸。

比森特·亚涅斯·平松1500年望见这段海岸，葡萄牙王室从1535年起把它纳入马拉尼昂封赐。最早存留的定居点来自法国人：雅克·里福1594年把人员留在乌帕翁阿苏岛；1612年，达尼埃尔·德·拉图什和弗朗索瓦·德·拉齐利建立圣路易，作为赤道法兰西的治所。1615年，一支从伯南布哥出发的葡萄牙军队夺取该城，改名圣路易斯。1621年，它成为马拉尼昂与大帕拉国的首府，也是传教事务和向亚马逊扩张的基地；荷兰西印度公司在1641年至1644年占据此岛。种植园主和商人后来围绕王室的印第安劳力规定和马拉尼昂贸易公司的专营权发生冲突，这些矛盾引发1684年的贝克曼叛乱。18世纪末，棉花在低地推广，主要由被奴役的非洲劳工种植，圣路易斯成为繁忙的棉花输出港，这场繁荣在1800年后转弱。

en:
Crato lies below the Chapada do Araripe, where springs feed the Granjeiro and Jaguaribe-Mirim valleys and make a humid Cariri district inside the dry northeastern interior. In 1444 Kariri, Aquijiró, Guariú, Xocó and Quipapaú villages kept fields and hunting grounds along those watercourses. The steady springs and deeper soil gave their country an advantage rare in the surrounding sertão.

Portuguese settlers entered the district mainly through missionary villages. The Capuchin Carlos Maria de Ferrara gathered Kariri communities at the Miranda mission, also called the Mission of the New Kariris, on the Itaitera River; manioc, grain, sugar cane and cattle did well in its moist bottomlands. A church dedicated to Our Lady of Penha was begun in 1745, the parish followed in 1762, and Vila Real do Crato was installed on 21 June 1764. Its sharpest colonial crisis came in 1817, when the Pernambucan revolt reached Ceará. The young priest José Martiniano Pereira de Alencar proclaimed independence from the pulpit on 3 May. Royalist landowners crushed the rising within a day and sent the prisoners to Fortaleza and Salvador.
zh:
克拉图位于阿拉里皮崖壁北麓，泉水注入格朗热罗河与雅瓜里比-米林河，在干旱的东北内陆滋养出湿润的卡里里地带。1444年，卡里里人、阿基罗人、瓜里乌人、绍科人和基帕帕乌人的村社沿这些水道开辟农田和猎场。稳定泉眼和较深的肥土，使这片地方比周围干旱腹地更适于居住。

葡萄牙人主要通过传教村落向这里渗透。嘉布遣会士卡洛·玛丽亚·德·费拉拉把卡里里诸村聚集到伊泰拉河畔的米兰达传教村，这里又称新卡里里传教村；木薯、谷物、甘蔗和牛群都适合在湿润低地生长。1745年，供奉佩尼亚圣母的教堂开工，1762年设立教区，1764年6月21日克拉图皇家镇正式成立。殖民时代最激烈的变故发生在1817年，伯南布哥革命传入塞阿拉。年轻神父若泽·马蒂尼亚诺·佩雷拉·德·阿伦卡于5月3日在讲坛上宣布独立，保王派地主当天就镇压了起事，并把俘虏押往福塔莱萨和萨尔瓦多。

en:
In 1444 the dunes and river mouths of the Ceará coast, with the dry sertão stretching inland, were Indigenous country. Tupi-speaking Potiguara, whose name means 'shrimp-eaters', had lately spread along the shore; the maritime Tremembé ranged the beaches to the north-west, and Tabajara, Kariri, Anacés and other peoples held the Ibiapaba ridge, the wet valleys and the inland highlands. No European fort stood anywhere on the coast, though by the end of the 1500s French ships would be anchoring off these beaches to load brazilwood for the dye-works of France.

The French came first: in 1590 a French captain set up a trading post on the Ibiapaba ridge, bartering metal tools for brazilwood with the Tabajara. In 1603 the Portuguese sent Pero Coelho de Sousa up from Pernambuco with soldiers and Tupi auxiliaries; he stormed the ridge and, falling back to the coast, raised a palisaded fort by the Ceará river, but the drought of 1605-09 and constant attacks drove him out, and he died in poverty in Lisbon. Martim Soares Moreno built Fort São Sebastião on the same shore in 1612 and held it through an alliance with the Potiguara. Dutch forces took the post in 1637 and lost it to an Indigenous attack in 1644; their captain Matias Beck then built Fort Schoonenborch on the Pajeú stream, which passed to Portugal with the fall of Pernambuco in 1654 and was renamed Fortaleza de Nossa Senhora da Assunção, the nucleus of the town of Fortaleza.

Behind the coast the sertão went over to cattle. In the eighteenth century leather and dried beef paid for nearly everything, and the shore settlements ran charqueadas that shipped jerked beef south from Aracati, until the droughts of 1790-93 killed off the herds. Kariri, Tremembé, Anacés and other peoples held out for almost fifty years in the fighting the Portuguese called the Barbarians' War. Ruled from Pernambuco since 1680, Ceará became a captaincy on its own in 1799, administered from Fortaleza.
zh:
1444年，塞阿拉海岸的沙丘与河口之外，是大片干旱内陆，全境仍是原住民的土地。说图皮语的波蒂瓜拉人其名意为「食虾人」，新近沿海岸扩张而来；善于航海的特雷门贝人游猎于西北海滨，塔巴雅拉人、卡里里人、阿纳塞人等族群据有伊比亚帕巴山、湿润山谷和内陆高地。岸上还没有一座欧洲堡垒，但到十六世纪末叶，法兰西装运巴西红木的商船便会到此停泊。

法国人先动手：1590年，一名法兰西船长在伊比亚帕巴山上设商站，用金属工具与塔巴雅拉人交换红木。1603年，葡萄牙人从伯南布哥派佩罗·科埃略·德·索萨带兵北上，随军还有图皮盟军；他攻下山头，撤到海岸后在塞阿拉河边筑起木栅堡垒，但1605至1609年的大旱和原住民持续的袭击逼他撤离，他本人后来在里斯本穷困而死。1612年，马蒂姆·苏亚雷斯·莫雷诺在同一海岸修建圣塞巴斯蒂昂堡，靠与波蒂瓜拉人的盟约守住据点。荷兰军队1637年夺堡，1644年又在原住民攻势中失守；荷方首领马蒂亚斯·贝克随后在帕热乌溪畔筑起斯霍嫩博赫堡，1654年伯南布哥陷落，堡垒转入葡萄牙之手，改名圣母升天堡，福塔莱萨城即从它周围长成。

海岸背后的干旱内陆成了牧牛之地。十八世纪，皮革和肉干几乎能换来一切，沿海聚落开办肉干作坊，从阿拉卡蒂把肉干南运，直到1790至1793年的大旱使牛群倒毙。卡里里、特雷门贝、阿纳塞等部族在葡萄牙人所称的「野蛮人战争」中抵抗了近五十年。塞阿拉自1680年起受伯南布哥管辖，1799年成为独立的都督辖区，治所设在福塔莱萨。

en:
Oeiras sits in the Canindé valley in the southern Piauí sertão, where caatinga scrub thins into cerrado and carnaúba palms line the watercourses. In 1444 Ge bands hunted and planted along the streams, and no Portuguese herd had yet entered the country. The Portuguese came with cattle in the 1670s: Domingos Afonso Mafrense, a rancher from Mafra known in the sertão as Domingos Afonso Sertão, opened the Canindé and Parnaíba valleys and strung more than thirty ranches along their rivers, and his Fazenda Cabrobó on the Riacho Mocha grew into the Vila da Mocha.

When Mafrense died in 1711 he left his ranches to the Jesuits, who drove the Piauí cattle trade that supplied Maranhão and the sugar coast of the Northeast. John V made Mocha a vila in 1712, and when Piauí was detached from Maranhão in 1718 the king named it the new captaincy's capital. A Jesuit seminary opened in 1749, the first secondary school in the region, and the first governor only reached the town in 1759. Two years later the settlement was raised to a city and renamed Oeiras in honour of the Count of Oeiras, the minister later known as the Marquis of Pombal. Pombal had already turned on the Jesuits: expelled in 1760, they lost the ranches to the Crown as the Fazenda Real Fisco, and the estates fell into decay. In 1821 Oeiras was still the capital of Piauí, a cattle town gathered about its parish church and seminary.
zh:
奥埃拉斯坐落在皮奥伊南部荒原的卡宁德河谷，卡廷加灌丛渐稀，过渡为塞拉多草原，水道两旁长着巴西蜡棕榈。1444年时，热依人的群体沿溪狩猎、垦地种粮，葡萄牙人的牛群还没有进入这片土地。1670年代，葡萄牙人赶着牛来了：出生在马夫拉的牧主多明戈斯·阿方索·马弗伦塞在荒原上人称「荒原的多明戈斯·阿方索」，他开辟卡宁德河与巴纳伊巴河谷，沿河串起三十多座牧场，莫沙溪畔的卡布罗博牧场后来发展成莫沙镇。

马弗伦塞1711年去世时把牧场留给了耶稣会，会士经营的皮奥伊牛群供应着马拉尼昂和东北的甘蔗海岸。若昂五世1712年将莫沙升为镇，1718年皮奥伊从马拉尼昂分出，国王定莫沙为新都督辖区的首府。1749年耶稣会神学院开学，是当地第一所中学，首任都督却迟至1759年才到任。两年后莫沙升格为市，改名奥埃拉斯，向奥埃拉斯伯爵致敬——这位重臣就是后来的蓬巴尔侯爵。蓬巴尔此时已经对耶稣会下手：1760年会士被逐，牧场作为「皇家税庄」没入王室，田庄日渐败落。1821年时，奥埃拉斯仍是皮奥伊的首府，一座围着教区教堂和神学院的牧城。

en:
Rio Grande covers the northeastern corner of Brazil around the mouth of the Potengi, the wide river Portuguese mariners called the Great River. In 1444 Potiguara villages held the dunes, mangroves and canoe anchorage at the bar, while Cariri and Tarairiu peoples lived farther inland toward Seridó and the Chapada do Apodi. Coastal canoes carried fish, manioc flour and brazilwood, and no European fort yet guarded the entrance.

French traders used the anchorage for decades, buying brazilwood through their Potiguara allies. The Portuguese Crown granted the captaincy in 1534, but the expedition organized for the donatary João de Barros collapsed after heavy losses, and the bar remained unfortified. Work on the Barra fortress began on Epiphany 1598 and finished on 24 June; its builders named it for the Three Kings, and Natal was founded beside it on Christmas Day 1599. Sugar mills and cattle ranches spread behind the new town. A Dutch assault failed in 1631, yet two years later the garrison fell. The occupiers rebuilt the earthen fort in stone as Castle Keulen and called Natal New Amsterdam. The Cunhaú and Uruaçu killings of 1645 opened a wider Catholic and Calvinist war, and Portuguese forces drove the Dutch out in 1654. In 1817 the sugar planter André de Albuquerque Maranhão seized Natal for the Pernambucan revolution; he was overthrown within a month, wounded and imprisoned in the Three Kings fortress, where he died on 26 April.
zh:
里奥格兰德位于巴西东北转角，环绕波滕吉河口；葡萄牙海员因河口宽阔，把这条图皮语原意为「虾河」的河流称为大河。1444年，波蒂瓜拉人的村社占据河口沙坝旁的沙丘、红树林和独木舟锚地，卡里里人与塔赖里乌人住在塞里多和阿波迪高地一带的内陆。沿海独木舟转运鱼、木薯粉和巴西木，河口还没有欧洲要塞把守。

法国商人利用这个锚地数十年，通过波蒂瓜拉盟友收购巴西木。葡萄牙王室1534年封出都督区，但受封者若昂·德·巴罗斯组织的远征队损失惨重，河口仍无防备。河口要塞1598年主显节动工、6月24日完工，修建者以三王为它命名；1599年圣诞节，纳塔尔在要塞旁建立，甘蔗磨坊和牧牛场随之向城外扩展。荷兰1631年的进攻被击退，但两年后守军失守。占领者把土筑要塞改建成石砌的克伊伦堡，并将纳塔尔改称新阿姆斯特丹。1645年库尼亚乌和乌鲁阿苏惨案引发更大规模的天主教徒与加尔文宗信徒战争，葡萄牙军队1654年赶走荷兰人。1817年，糖坊主安德烈·德·阿尔伯克基·马拉尼昂为伯南布哥革命夺取纳塔尔；他不到一个月便被推翻，受伤后关入三王堡，于4月26日死在堡中。

en:
The Paraíba do Norte River reaches the sea at the eastern bulge of Brazil; Ponta do Seixas, close by, is the easternmost point of the American mainland. In 1444 Potiguara villages held the estuary, shore and wooded plain behind it. The Potiguara grew manioc, fished the coast, and later traded brazilwood to French ships for metal tools, while Kiriri and Ariú bands occupied the drier slopes leading toward the Borborema Plateau. French vessels used the Bay of Traição as an anchorage, so the river mouth became one of the places where Portugal's contest with France over dyewood turned into war.

Potiguara warriors encouraged by the French destroyed the Tracunhaém sugar settlement in 1574, opening the Potiguara War. Portuguese campaigns relied on Tabajara rivals as allies, and in 1585 the victors founded Filipeia de Nossa Senhora das Neves, Brazil's first royal city under the Habsburg kings. Sugar mills spread up the valley, while the fort of Santa Catarina at Cabedelo covered the river mouth and anchorage. A Dutch assault failed in 1632, but a fleet of 29 ships returned in November 1634, took the forts of Santa Catarina and Santo Antônio, and entered abandoned Filipeia on Christmas Eve. Under Dutch Brazil the town became Frederikstadt; Portuguese forces recovered it in 1654.
zh:
北帕拉伊巴河在巴西东部凸出部入海，附近的塞沙斯角是美洲大陆最东点。1444年，波蒂瓜拉人的村落据有河口、海岸和后方林木平原。他们种植木薯、在海边捕鱼，后来又用巴西木向法国船交换金属工具；基里里人和阿里乌人则占据通向博尔博雷马高原的干旱坡地。法国船可在特赖桑湾停泊，这个河口也成了葡萄牙与法国争夺染料木时最先开战的地点之一。

1574年，得到法国人支持的波蒂瓜拉战士摧毁特拉库尼亚恩蔗糖定居点，波蒂瓜拉战争爆发。葡萄牙远征军与和他们敌对的塔巴雅拉人结盟，1585年获胜后建立「降雪圣母菲利佩亚」，这是哈布斯堡君主统治巴西期间第一座由王室直辖的城市。糖坊沿河谷扩展，卡贝德卢的圣卡塔琳娜要塞则扼守河口与锚地。1632年荷兰人的进攻被击退，但1634年11月，一支二十九艘船组成的舰队重返此地，连克圣卡塔琳娜和圣安多尼要塞，并在圣诞前夜进入已被放弃的菲利佩亚。荷兰巴西时期，这座城改称弗雷德里克城，1654年被葡萄牙军队收复。

en:
In 1444 the coast later called Pernambuco was a string of Caeté and other Tupi-Guarani villages between a reef-bound shore and a rainforested escarpment. Villagers planted manioc in the red massapê soil, drew fish from the inlet that became Recife, and fought ritual wars for captives. Brazilwood groves covered much of the slope behind them. Cape Santo Agostinho marked the coast to the south, and the reefs off Olinda sheltered one of the few useful anchorages on this open Atlantic shore.

Vicente Yáñez Pinzón landed at Cape Santo Agostinho on 26 January 1500, the first recorded European landing in Brazil. Portugal claimed the shore under the Treaty of Tordesillas, and after a French trading post was driven out, Duarte Coelho entered his hereditary captaincy in 1535; Olinda became a town two years later. Sugar, grown on engenhos worked by enslaved African and Indigenous labour, made Pernambuco the richest captaincy in Brazil and one of the world's largest sugar-producing regions by 1600. Its wealth drew James Lancaster's English privateers to Recife in 1595. A Dutch army took Olinda and Recife in 1630. From 1637 John Maurice of Nassau built canal-cut Mauritsstad beside Recife, brought scholars and painters such as Frans Post and Albert Eckhout to Dutch Brazil, and allowed the Kahal Zur Israel synagogue, the first recorded synagogue in the New World.

Portuguese planters rose against Dutch rule in 1645. Their forces won at Guararapes in 1648 and 1649 and retook Recife in 1654. Recife's merchants, called mascates, had prospered while Olinda's mill owners fell into debt, and the feud produced street fighting in the Mascate War of 1710-11. Pernambuco rebelled again in 1817, replacing the Portuguese governor with a short-lived republic; royal troops executed its leaders and detached southern Alagoas as punishment. In 1821 the Beberibe convention drove out the Portuguese garrison.
zh:
1444年，后来称作伯南布哥的海岸还是一连串卡埃特等图皮-瓜拉尼语村落，夹在礁石海岸与雨林崖地之间。村民在红色马萨佩沃土上种植木薯，在后来形成累西腓的海湾捕鱼，也为俘获人牲而进行仪式战争。村落后方的坡地遍布巴西木。圣阿戈斯蒂纽角标示着南侧海岸，奥林达外的礁石则为这段开阔的大西洋海岸提供了少数可用锚地。

1500年1月26日，比森特·亚涅斯·平松在圣阿戈斯蒂纽角登陆，这是欧洲人在巴西有据可考的第一次登陆。葡萄牙依据《托尔德西里亚斯条约》取得这段海岸；法国人商站被逐走后，杜阿尔特·科埃略于1535年接管世袭都督辖区，奥林达两年后设镇。糖坊使用非洲奴隶和土著劳力，到1600年前后，蔗糖已使伯南布哥成为巴西最富庶的都督辖区，也是世界最大的蔗糖产区之一。财富把詹姆斯·兰开斯特的英国私掠船在1595年引到累西腓。1630年，荷兰军队攻占奥林达和累西腓。1637年起，拿骚的约翰·毛里茨在累西腓旁营建水道纵横的毛里茨城，把学者和弗兰斯·波斯特、阿尔贝特·埃克豪特等画家带到荷兰巴西，还允许设立新大陆有记载的第一座犹太会堂卡哈尔·祖尔·以色列会堂。

葡萄牙种植园主1645年起兵反抗荷兰统治，1648和1649年两度在瓜拉拉佩斯取胜，1654年收复累西腓。累西腓商人被称作「马斯卡特」，他们在奥林达糖坊主负债时发家，双方仇怨最终演成1710至1711年巷战不断的马斯卡特战争。1817年，伯南布哥再度起事，以短命共和政府取代葡萄牙总督；王军处死其领袖，并把南部的阿拉戈斯划出作为惩罚。1821年，贝贝里布会议驱逐了葡萄牙驻军。

en:
Bahia faces the Bay of All Saints, one of the largest sheltered anchorages on the Brazilian coast. The Tupinambá called it Kirimurê, the 'great inland sea', and in 1444 their villages occupied the mangrove shores and the fertile Recôncavo behind them. Families cleared manioc fields around thatched longhouses, fished from dugout canoes and traded or feuded between independent villages. No European ship had yet entered the bay.

A Portuguese castaway gave the coast its first durable link with Europe. Diogo Álvares, called Caramuru by the Tupinambá, settled among them in 1509, married Tupinambá women and later acted as an intermediary for the crown. An early captaincy under Francisco Pereira Coutinho collapsed under settler violence and Tupinambá attacks, but on 29 March 1549 Tomé de Sousa laid out Salvador on the bluff above the anchorage as the first capital of Brazil. The upper town held the governor, Jesuits and, from 1551, the first Brazilian bishopric; the lower town served the port and market. Sugar engenhos spread through the Recôncavo, and Salvador became one of the New World's busiest ports for the African slave trade.

Its wealth drew the Dutch. Jacob Willekens and Piet Hein stormed the city for the Dutch West India Company on 10 May 1624. A Luso-Spanish armada of fifty-two ships and almost fourteen thousand men under Fadrique de Toledo blockaded the bay and forced the Dutch out on 1 May 1625; John Maurice of Nassau-Siegen besieged Salvador without success in 1638. The colony's capital moved to Rio de Janeiro in 1763, but the regent John landed at Salvador on his voyage south in 1808 and signed the decree opening Brazilian ports to friendly nations there.
zh:
巴伊亚濒临万圣湾，那是巴西海岸最大的避风锚地之一。图皮南巴人称这片海湾为基里穆雷，意为「巨大的内海」。1444年，他们的村落占据红树林海岸和后方肥沃的雷孔卡沃；居民在茅草长屋周围开辟木薯田，划独木舟捕鱼，在彼此独立的村落间贸易或仇杀。此时还没有欧洲船只驶入这座海湾。

一名葡萄牙遇险者最先把这片海岸与欧洲长期联系起来。迪奥戈·阿尔瓦雷斯于1509年流落图皮南巴人中间，被称作「卡拉穆鲁」；他娶图皮南巴女子为妻，后来为葡萄牙王室充当中间人。弗朗西斯科·佩雷拉·科蒂尼奥的早期都督辖区因殖民者施暴和图皮南巴人反击而覆灭，但1549年3月29日，托梅·德·索萨在俯瞰锚地的高崖上营建萨尔瓦多，作为葡属巴西的第一个首府。高城驻有总督和耶稣会士，并从1551年起设巴西第一个主教区；低城则服务于港口与市场。甘蔗种植园和榨糖作坊遍布雷孔卡沃，萨尔瓦多成为新大陆贩运非洲黑奴最繁忙的港口之一。

这笔财富引来了荷兰人。1624年5月10日，雅各布·威廉肯斯与皮特·海恩代表荷兰西印度公司攻陷城市。1625年5月1日，法德里克·德·托莱多率领一支拥有五十二艘船、近一万四千人的西葡联合舰队封锁海湾，迫使荷兰人撤出；拿骚-锡根的约翰·莫里斯又于1638年围攻萨尔瓦多，仍未得手。1763年，殖民地首府迁往里约热内卢；1808年，摄政若昂南下途中在萨尔瓦多登岸，并于当地签署向友好国家开放巴西港口的敕令。

en:
The island-dotted coast around the Bay of Ilhéus, where the Cachoeira and Almada rivers meet the Atlantic, takes its name from the many ilhéus, the islets strung along its shore. Tupi-speaking peoples moving down from the Amazon had driven the older Tapuia into the interior around the year 1000, and in 1444 the coast belonged to the Tupiniquim, who fished and hunted in the Atlantic Forest and kept gardens above the sheltered anchorages later called São Jorge dos Ilhéus.

On 26 June 1534 John III granted the fifty-league shore as the hereditary Captaincy of Ilhéus to Jorge de Figueiredo Correia, a royal scribe who never left Portugal and sent the Spaniard Francisco Romero in his place. Romero settled on Tinharé in 1535 and then moved his seat to the Bay of Ilhéus, naming the town São Jorge after the absent donatário. Sugar was the first export crop; Tomé de Sousa, the first governor-general, called the bay the best ground on the whole coast for a plantation, and the Engenho de Santana, later worked by the Jesuits, had first been granted to Mem de Sá, the third governor-general of Brazil. After Figueiredo's death Aimoré raiders struck the plantations, and in 1559 the Tupiniquim killed three Portuguese to avenge a kinsman. Mem de Sá's reprisals ended at Cururupe beach in the fight called the Battle of the Swimmers, where Tupiniquim warriors waded into the sea and fought to the death against his Tupinambá allies. A French raid was beaten off in 1595, and the little Santo António fort at the harbour mouth was rebuilt in stone and lime in 1611. The town stayed poor for the rest of the colonial years. Amazonian cacao reached the southern Bahian rivers after the Frenchman Louis Frédéric Warneaux brought seed from Pará and planted it on the Rio Pardo, and by the late eighteenth century the Itaípe canal, cut by the naval engineer François Gaston Lavigne for cocoa canoes, carried the crop from the Almada down to the port.
zh:
伊列乌斯湾一带岛礁散布，卡舒埃拉河与阿尔马达河在此注入大西洋，「伊列乌斯」一名来自沿岸众多的小岛。约1000年，来自亚马逊方向的图皮语族群把较早的塔普亚人逐入内陆；1444年，沿岸属于图皮尼金人，他们在大西洋林地中渔猎，也在后来称圣若热-杜斯-伊列乌斯的避风锚地附近开辟园圃，此时葡萄牙人尚未到来。

1534年6月26日，若昂三世把这段五十里格长的海岸作为世系都督府授予王室书记官若热·德·菲格雷多·科雷亚；受封者始终没有离开葡萄牙，派西班牙人弗朗西斯科·罗梅罗代为经营。罗梅罗1535年先驻蒂尼亚雷岛，随后把治所迁到伊列乌斯湾，以不在场的受封者之名把小镇命名为圣若热。甘蔗是最早的出口作物；首任总督托梅·德·索萨称这处海湾是整条海岸上最适宜办种植园的地方，后来由耶稣会士经营的圣安娜糖坊，最初便授给了巴西第三任总督梅姆·德·萨。菲格雷多死后，艾莫雷人频频袭击种植园；1559年，图皮尼金人杀死三名葡萄牙人，为死去的族人报仇。梅姆·德·萨的报复在库鲁鲁佩海滩收场，是役称「泅水者之战」：图皮尼金战士冲入海中，与他的图皮南巴盟军死战到底。1595年法国人的一次袭击被击退，港门口的圣安多尼小堡于1611年改用石块和石灰重建。殖民时代余下的年月里小镇一直穷困。法国人路易·弗雷德里克·瓦尔诺从帕拉带来可可种子、种在帕尔杜河畔，亚马逊可可随之传入巴伊亚南部河流。到18世纪末，海军工程师弗朗索瓦·加斯东·拉维尼为运可可独木舟开凿的伊塔伊皮运河，已把阿尔马达河上的可可运往伊列乌斯港。

en:
The Goias uplands fill the basin between the upper Tocantins and the middle Araguaia, a wide run of cerrado savanna cut by ribbons of riverine forest. On the Araguaia the river splits around the Ilha do Bananal, some twenty thousand square kilometres of seasonally flooded ground and the largest purely riverine island in the world. The river-fishing Karajá and their Javaé kin kept villages there and along the banks, while Xavante and Xerente bands of the Jê family hunted the grasslands between the two rivers. The Goiá, who later gave the whole region its name, lived by the Rio Vermelho in the south. These nations planted maize and manioc and took fish from the rivers, and in 1444 no European had yet entered this part of the interior.

Gold pulled the frontier in from the south: the bandeirante Anhanguera's strikes on the Rio Vermelho in 1725 opened the Vila Boa mines just beyond the southern hills, drawing settlers and slave raiders into Goiá country. The northern sertão held out much longer, and Portuguese 'pacification' columns wore down the Xavante only in the campaigns of 1794-1798, breaking their villages and settling survivors in supervised aldeamentos. Jesuits had met the Karajá on the Araguaia as early as 1658, but the river stayed outside Portuguese control. In 1812 a presidio, Santa Maria, went up on the lower Araguaia to guard a chartered river-trading company, and on 11 February 1813 allied Xavante, Xerente and Karajá stormed it and drove the garrison downstream.
zh:
戈亚斯高地位于托坎廷斯河上游与阿拉瓜亚河中游之间，是一片开阔的塞拉多稀树草原，林带沿河蜿蜒。阿拉瓜亚河在中游分岔，环抱约两万平方公里、随季节涨水的巴纳纳尔岛——世界上最大的纯河成岛。以河渔为生的卡拉雅人及其近亲雅瓦埃人在岛上和两岸立村，沙万特人、谢伦特人等热依语族群的队伍在两河之间的草原游猎，后来为整个地区命名的戈亚人住在南方的红河一带。这些部族种植玉米和木薯，也在河里捕鱼；1444年，还没有欧洲人进入这片内陆。

把边疆拖进来的是南方的黄金：被称为「阿年古埃拉」的旗手1725年在红河挖到富矿，南山另一侧的博阿镇矿区随之开张，拓殖者和掳奴队跟着进入戈亚人的土地。北部腹地坚持了更久，葡萄牙人的「绥靖」纵队直到1794至1798年的征讨才压垮沙万特人，打散他们的村落，把幸存者编入受监管的村屯。耶稣会士早在1658年就在阿拉瓜亚河畔接触过卡拉雅人，但这条河始终不在葡萄牙人控制之下。1812年，葡方在下游建起圣马利亚要塞，为一家特许河运公司护航；1813年2月11日，沙万特人、谢伦特人和卡拉雅人联手攻破要塞，把守军逐向下游。

en:
Diamantina occupies the cold upper ridges of the Serra do Espinhaço, where streams divide between the Jequitinhonha and São Francisco systems. In 1444 Macro-Jê groups camped, hunted and planted along these watercourses. The quartz gravels later dug for diamonds were untouched by Portuguese miners, and no road or colonial camp yet linked the Serro Frio highlands to the coast.

Gold prospectors from the Serro settlements founded Arraial do Tejuco in 1713 and raised a chapel to Saint Anthony on the slopes of the Serra da Lapa. Diamonds appeared in the gold washings and were sold secretly for several years before Governor Lourenço de Almeida reported the find to Lisbon in 1729. The Crown created the Diamond District and Intendency of Diamonds in 1734, leased extraction to contractors after 1740, and replaced the contracts with direct Royal Diamond Extraction under the Marquês of Pombal in 1771. Officials checked travellers, goods and markets, while soldiers and informers pursued diamond smugglers. Enslaved Africans opened the lavras and washed the gravel. João Fernandes de Oliveira, the principal diamond contractor, lived with Chica da Silva, a freedwoman whose wealth and influence made her the most famous resident of Tejuco. Because the Crown feared disorder in a diamond town, Tejuco remained under Serro's jurisdiction and became a parish and municipal district only in 1819.
zh:
迪亚曼蒂纳位于埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉寒冷的上部山脊，溪流分别流向热基蒂尼奥尼亚河与圣弗朗西斯科河。1444年，大热依语系族群沿水道扎营、狩猎和耕作。后来被翻找钻石的石英砾石还没有葡萄牙矿工动过，也没有道路或殖民村落把塞鲁弗里乌高地同沿海连起来。

来自塞鲁聚居点的淘金者1713年建立特茹科村，在拉帕山山坡建起供奉圣安多尼的小堂。淘金层中出现钻石后，原石被秘密买卖数年，直到1729年总督洛伦索·德·阿尔梅达把发现上报里斯本。1734年，葡萄牙王室设立钻石区和钻石监督署，1740年后把开采包给承包商，1771年又在蓬巴尔侯爵主持下废除承包，改为王室直接开采钻石。官吏盘查旅客、货物和市场，士兵与线人追捕钻石走私者。被奴役的非洲人开凿矿坑、淘洗砾石。首席钻石承包商若昂·费尔南德斯·德·奥利维拉与获得自由的奇卡·达席尔瓦共同生活，后者的财富和影响使她成为特茹科最有名的居民。由于王室担心钻石城镇生乱，特茹科长期归塞鲁管辖，直到1819年才成为堂区和市政辖区。

en:
Porto Seguro lies on the forested coast of southern Bahia, around the mouth of the Buranhém River. Tupi-speaking peoples had pushed older Jê-speaking Tapuia bands into the interior centuries earlier, so in 1444 Tupiniquim villagers farmed manioc and fished from dugout canoes along a harbor they called Nhoesembé, while Tapuia hunters kept the woods behind the Monte Pascoal hills. No European sail had yet appeared off the beach.

This coast became the first recorded Portuguese landing place in Brazil. Pedro Álvares Cabral's India fleet sighted the hump of Monte Pascoal on 22 April 1500, landed the next day and anchored in the sheltered roadstead on 24 April, naming it Porto Seguro, or 'safe harbor'. Two days later Frei Henrique de Coimbra said the first Mass on Brazilian soil at Coroa Vermelha, the reef-fringed cove south of the anchorage. The fleet's scribe, Pero Vaz de Caminha, described the people, rivers and brazilwood in the letter he sent back to the Portuguese king.

Gonçalo Coelho raised the first permanent Portuguese post, a small fort, in 1504. In 1534 the crown granted fifty leagues of coast as the hereditary captaincy of Porto Seguro to Pero do Campo Tourinho, who installed the town in 1535. Brazilwood gave the captaincy its first export; sugar plantations then spread with enslaved Indian and African labour. Jesuits put a church and college on the upper town in 1551, the captaincy passed to the Duke of Aveiro in 1559, and its fort was strengthened during the seventeenth-century wars. The old lordship was incorporated into the captaincy of Bahia in 1761.
zh:
塞古罗港位于巴伊亚南部林木繁茂的海岸，地处布拉年河口一带。数百年前，图皮语民族把早先居住此地的操热语塔普亚诸部逐入内陆；因此到1444年，图皮尼金人在他们称为尼奥恩森贝的港湾沿岸种植木薯、划独木舟捕鱼，塔普亚猎人则据有蒙特帕斯科阿尔丘陵后方的丛林。此时海滩外还没有出现欧洲船帆。

这片海岸是有记载以来葡萄牙人首次登上巴西土地的地方。1500年4月22日，佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔前往印度的舰队望见蒙特帕斯科阿尔的山影，次日登岸，并于4月24日在避风锚地下泊，将其命名为塞古罗港，意为「安全港」。两天后，恩里克·德·科英布拉神父在锚地以南、礁岩环绕的科罗阿韦梅利亚小湾举行巴西土地上的第一场弥撒。随队书记员佩罗·瓦兹·德·卡米尼亚则在呈给葡萄牙国王的信中，描述了这里的居民、河流和巴西红木。

第一个葡萄牙永久据点建于1504年，由贡萨洛·科埃略筑起一座小要塞。1534年，王室把五十里格海岸封给佩罗·多·坎波·图里尼奥，作为世袭的塞古罗港都督辖区，他在1535年正式设城。巴西红木是这里最早的出口货，随后甘蔗种植园依靠印第安和非洲黑奴劳力扩张。耶稣会士于1551年在高城修建教堂和学院；1559年，都督辖区转入阿威罗公爵手中，要塞也在17世纪的战争中加固。1761年，这片老牌封邑被并入巴伊亚都督辖区。

en:
The Bay of Vitória is a sheltered harbour set with islands below the Atlantic Forest escarpment, and in 1444 it had no Portuguese town. Tupinambá and Temiminó villagers farmed and fished much of the coast; Aimoré and Goitacá groups of the Jê family kept the forests, the Doce valley and the southern sertão. The islands and mainland trails belonged to one indigenous world with no single ruler over it.

In June 1534 John III granted the fifty leagues of coast between the Mucuri and Itapemirim rivers to Vasco Fernandes Coutinho. He landed at the Prainha anchorage on 23 May 1535, Whit Sunday, and named his settlement Vila do Espírito Santo, the Town of the Holy Spirit, after the feast; the landing place grew into Vila Velha. Amerigo Vespucci had already surveyed this coast on the 1501 voyage. Indigenous wars, French interlopers and feuding grant-holders made the mainland shore unsafe, so about 1549 the settlers moved behind the bay waters to Santo Antônio Island, and after a Portuguese victory on 8 September 1551 the new town was renamed Vitória. José de Anchieta was among the Jesuits who set out to convert the coastal villages. The island beat off two famous raiders, Thomas Cavendish in 1592 and Piet Heyn's Dutch squadron in 1625; local accounts single out Maria Ortiz, a young woman said to have fought at the barricades against the Dutch. In 1692 Antônio Rodrigues Arzão found small gold deposits near Castelo, and the tracks his miners opened became the road from the coast into the Minas country.
zh:
维多利亚湾是一处避风良港，湾内岛礁散布，背后是大西洋林地的陡崖；1444年，这里还没有葡萄牙人的城镇。海岸大部分地方住着图皮南巴人和特米米诺人，他们耕作、捕鱼；艾莫雷人和戈伊塔卡人等热依语族群则据有林地、多西河谷和南部内陆。湾中岛屿和大陆上的小路同属一个原住民世界，没有谁统管一切。

1534年6月，若昂三世把穆库里河到伊塔佩米林河之间的五十里格海岸封给瓦斯科·费尔南德斯·科蒂尼奥。1535年5月23日五旬节，他在普拉伊尼亚锚地登陆，以节日把定居点命名为圣埃斯皮里图镇，意为圣神之镇；登陆处后来发展成维拉韦利亚。亚美利哥·韦斯普奇已在1501年的航行中勘测过这段海岸。印第安战争、法国闯入者和受封者之间的仇杀使大陆海岸很不安全，约1549年，居民退到湾内的圣安多尼岛上隔水自保；1551年9月8日葡萄牙人取胜后，新镇改名维多利亚。若泽·德·安谢塔是最早向沿海村落传教的耶稣会士之一。这座岛击退过两拨有名的袭掠者：1592年的托马斯·卡文迪什和1625年皮特·海因的荷兰舰队；当地记述特别提到一名年轻女子玛丽亚·奥尔蒂斯，据说她在街垒后与荷兰人作战。1692年，安东尼奥·罗德里格斯·阿藏在卡斯特卢附近发现少量金矿，矿工踏出的小路成为海岸通往米纳斯地区的道路。

en:
São Tomé is the low coast east of Guanabara, where lagoons, sandspits and the Paraíba do Sul floodplain lie between the sea and the forested highlands. In 1444 Tupinambá fishing villages ringed the Araruama lagoon and made salt there; the cape itself was called Gecay. Goitacá hunters held the Campos plains to the west, and Puri bands lived in the forests farther upriver. No European factory or cane field had yet been planted.

A Portuguese expedition under Gaspar de Lemos, with Amerigo Vespucci aboard, sighted the cape in 1501 and named it for Saint Thomas. In 1503 a party left by Vespucci's voyage set up a brazilwood factory guarded by 24 men on the Araruama bar; Tupinambá warriors destroyed it in 1526. Pero de Góis later landed with colonists and sugarcane from São Vicente, founding Vila da Rainha on the Itabapoana, but Goitacá and Puri attacks forced the captaincy's abandonment. The French moved into the gap and built a stone fort in 1556 to load brazilwood. It held until the Cabo Frio war of 1575, when Rio de Janeiro's governor Antônio Salema brought forces from Guanabara, São Vicente and Espírito Santo against the French alliance with the Tamoio.

Slave raids and a smallpox epidemic spread by colonists devastated the Goitacá as settlers opened the plains. On 29 May 1677 the Vila de São Salvador de Campos was founded on the Paraíba flats, and the Portuguese crown bought the old captaincy in 1752. Salt pans around Araruama, sugar mills on the flatlands and whaling stations at Búzios supplied Rio de Janeiro and the Minas Gerais gold camps. In 1821 the district sent salt, sugar and whale products to those same markets.
zh:
圣多美是瓜纳巴拉以东的低海岸，潟湖、沙嘴和南帕拉伊巴河冲积平原夹在大海与林木覆盖的高地之间。1444年，图皮南巴渔村环绕阿拉鲁阿马潟湖，并在当地晒盐；他们把海角称作格凯。戈伊塔卡猎人占据西侧的坎波斯平原，普里人群住在更上游的森林里。海岸上还没有欧洲商站，也没有甘蔗田。

1501年，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯率领、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇随行的葡萄牙考察队望见这座海角，以圣多默为它命名。1503年，韦斯普奇航程留下的人员在阿拉鲁阿马沙洲设立一座由二十四人守卫的巴西木商站；1526年，图皮南巴战士摧毁了商站。佩罗·德·戈伊斯后来率殖民者登陆，带来圣维森特的甘蔗，在伊塔巴波阿纳河畔建立维拉达赖尼亚，但戈伊塔卡人和普里人的进攻迫使这块领地荒废。法国人随后进入空隙，1556年修建石堡装运巴西木。1575年卡布弗里乌战争中，里约热内卢长官安东尼奥·萨莱马调集瓜纳巴拉、圣维森特和圣埃斯皮里图的军队，击破法国人同塔莫伊人的同盟，石堡才被拔除。

殖民者开辟平原时，奴隶猎捕和殖民者带来的天花使戈伊塔卡人遭受重创。1677年5月29日，圣萨尔瓦多-迪坎波斯镇在帕拉伊巴平原设立，葡萄牙王室又在1752年买下旧领地。阿拉鲁阿马周围的盐田、平原上的蔗糖作坊和布齐奥斯的捕鲸站，向里约热内卢与米纳斯吉拉斯的淘金营地供货。1821年，这片地区向同样的市场输出盐、糖和鲸产品。

en:
Guanabara, the great bay of the Brazilian coast, was ringed by the villages of the Tamoio, a Tupinambá confederation who farmed manioc on its islands and fished its calm water. The granite cone of the Sugarloaf stood at the bay mouth, and behind the shore rose the forested Serra do Mar. In 1444 no European had yet entered the bay. The first Portuguese ships, led by Gaspar de Lemos with Amerigo Vespucci aboard, did so on 1 January 1502, mistook it for a river mouth, and named it Rio de Janeiro, the January River.

The bay became the one place in Brazil where Portugal and France fought a colonial war. In 1555 the French admiral Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon landed 500 colonists, many of them Huguenots, on an island in the bay and built Fort Coligny, the centre of his France Antarctique, in alliance with the Tamoio. Governor Mem de Sá stormed the fort in 1560, and his nephew Estácio de Sá founded the town of São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro in 1565, named for Saint Sebastian, patron of King Sebastião. On 20 January 1567 a Portuguese army broke the French and their Tamoio allies outside the town; Estácio was wounded and died a month later, and the French were driven out of Brazil.

Sugar and the African slave trade built the town after that. French corsairs kept coming: in September 1711, during the War of the Spanish Succession, René Duguay-Trouin's squadron fought into the bay; four Portuguese ships were lost and Rio paid a heavy ransom to save its defences. When gold and diamonds were found up in Minas Gerais, Rio was the nearest outlet for them to the Atlantic, and in 1763 the colonial capital moved there from Salvador. In 1808 the Portuguese court of Queen Maria I and the Prince Regent John, fleeing Napoleon's armies, arrived with the Lisbon nobility, the only European court ever to move its seat into its own colony. Townspeople were evicted to house the arriving nobles, and the court founded the Royal Library and the Botanical Garden and licensed Brazil's first newspaper, the Gazeta do Rio de Janeiro. The Valongo wharf, open from 1811, landed shiploads of enslaved Africans on whom the city rested, making Rio the greatest slave port in the Americas. It was still the capital when the court sailed back to Lisbon in 1821.
zh:
瓜纳巴拉是巴西海岸的大海湾，湾周遍布塔莫伊人的村落。塔莫伊人是图皮南巴人的一个联盟，在湾中岛屿上种植木薯，在平静的水面捕鱼。湾口矗立着糖面包山的花岗岩奇峰，岸后是森林覆盖的马尔山。1444年，还没有欧洲人驶入过这座海湾。1502年1月1日，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯率领、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇随行的葡萄牙船队首次到此，把海湾误认作河口，取名里约热内卢，即「一月之河」。

这座海湾后来成了巴西唯一一处葡萄牙与法国正面争夺殖民地的战场。1555年，法国海军将领尼古拉·迪朗·德·维尔加尼翁把500名殖民者送上湾中一座岛屿，其中不少是胡格诺派教徒；他在岛上筑起科利尼堡，与塔莫伊人结盟，作为「南极法兰西」的核心。巴西总督梅姆·德·萨1560年攻陷该堡，他的侄子埃斯塔西奥·德·萨1565年建城，以塞巴斯蒂昂国王的主保圣人圣塞巴斯蒂昂命名，称圣塞巴斯蒂昂-杜里约热内卢。1567年1月20日，葡军在城外击溃法军及其塔莫伊盟友，埃斯塔西奥受伤，一个月后死去，法国人也被逐出巴西。

此后撑起城市的是蔗糖和非洲奴隶贸易。法国海盗不断来袭：1711年9月西班牙王位继承战争期间，勒内·迪盖-特鲁安率法国舰队强攻海湾，四艘葡萄牙战船损失，里约付出巨额赎金才保住防御工事。米纳斯吉拉斯发现黄金和钻石后，里约是这批财富前往大西洋最近的出口，殖民地首府于1763年从萨尔瓦多迁此。1808年，玛丽亚一世女王和摄政若昂的葡萄牙宫廷为躲避拿破仑大军，带着里斯本的贵族抵达，这是唯一一次欧洲宫廷把驻地迁进自己的殖民地。数百名贵族需要安置，市民被赶出住宅腾房，宫廷又开办皇家图书馆和植物园，准许出版巴西第一份报纸《里约热内卢报》。1811年启用的瓦隆戈码头一船船运来被奴役的非洲人，城市建立在他们之上，里约也成了美洲最大的奴隶港。1821年王室启程返回里斯本时，里约仍是首都。

en:
Between Guanabara and the island of São Vicente, the forested Serra do Mar runs almost into the sea, leaving a narrow coast of steep green islands, deep channels and Tupinambá villages. The Bertioga channel, held between Santo Amaro island and the mainland, gave sheltered anchorage to the canoes plying the shore, and the rivers behind Ubatuba and Caraguatatuba were the only breaks in the mountains on the way to the plateau. In 1444 this coast belonged to the Tupinambá alone.

The Portuguese came for the channel, the safest anchorage on the run south to São Vicente. Martim Afonso de Sousa raised a watchtower at Bertioga in 1531, and in 1534 John III granted the shore behind it as the hereditary captaincy of Santo Amaro to Pero Lopes de Sousa. A palisade that replaced the tower in 1547 was stormed and burned by the Tupinambá four years later, so in 1560 the crown built the Forte de São Tiago there, later called São João, the first royal fortification in Brazil; it crossed its fire with the Forte de São Filipe across the channel to cover the approaches to the port of Santos. A whale-oil works at the mouth of the channel and Jesuit missions among the Indians were almost all the colony ever mustered here, for Santo Amaro had neither mines nor a road to the plateau. From the 1620s it shared its lord with the neighbouring captaincy of São Vicente, and in 1709 the crown bought both and folded them into the new captaincy of São Paulo e Minas de Ouro.
zh:
在瓜纳巴拉与圣维森特岛之间，林木覆盖的马尔山几乎直逼入海，只留下一道狭窄海岸，散布着陡绿的岛屿、深水水道和图皮南巴人的村落。圣阿马鲁岛与大陆夹峙的贝尔蒂奥加水道，为沿海往来的独木舟提供避风锚地；乌巴图巴和卡拉瓜塔图巴背后的河流，则是穿山前往高原仅有的缺口。1444年，这段海岸完全属于图皮南巴人。

葡萄牙人看中的正是这条水道，它是南下圣维森特沿途最安全的锚地。马丁·阿方索·德·索萨1531年在贝尔蒂奥加建起瞭望塔；1534年，若昂三世把塔后的海岸封给佩罗·洛佩斯·德·索萨，设为世袭的圣阿马鲁领。1547年代替瞭望塔的木栅寨，四年后被图皮南巴人攻破烧毁，王室于是在1560年就地修建圣雅各要塞（后称圣若昂要塞），这是巴西第一座王家防御工事，与水道对岸的圣腓力要塞炮火交叉，封锁桑托斯港的入口。水道口的鲸油作坊和在印第安人中传教的耶稣会，几乎是殖民地在这里经营的全部，因为圣阿马鲁既没有矿藏，也没有通往高原的道路。1620年代起，它与邻近的圣维森特领同封一主；1709年，王室买下两块领地，并入新设的圣保罗与黄金米纳斯领。

en:
The wooded highlands where the Sabará River joins the Rio das Velhas were Macro-Jê country long before the Portuguese spoke of Minas Gerais. Xakriabá, Puri and kindred peoples used the river fords, hunting grounds and village lands, moving along inland trails far from the markets of the Brazilian coast. In 1444 there was no European town, tax house or mining camp here; the streams and hills belonged to the Indigenous peoples whose world the Paulista expeditions would enter more than two centuries later.

The first Portuguese came looking not for gold but for Sabarabuçu, a legendary mountain range said to be made of silver and emeralds. In the 1670s Fernão Dias Pais's expedition combed the country near the Serra do Espinhaço, and his son-in-law Manuel de Borba Gato opened the camps of Sumidouro and Roça Grande, whose people were among the first to find gold in the streams. Borba Gato kept the strike secret for years, but once the news leaked the rush was on, and by about 1700 the Arraial da Barra do Sabará was one of the largest and busiest supply camps of the mining region, set on the Estrada Real.

Gold also set Paulista pioneers against the Portuguese and Brazilian newcomers they called emboabas, and in the War of the Emboabas of 1707 to 1709 Sabará was one of the districts fought over. After the outsiders' victory the crown placed a town at the end of each road into the mines to curb gold smuggling; in 1711 it chose Sabará, settled chiefly by Portuguese-born miners, over the Paulista camp of Roça Grande, and created the Vila Real de Nossa Senhora da Conceição do Sabará, seat of a comarca from 1714. A royal smelting house opened there in 1734 to take the crown's fifth on every batch of gold, and the town held one of the largest enslaved populations of the period. The gold paid for the parish church, the churches of Our Lady of Ó and the Rosary, and the stone fountains along its steep streets; the Municipal Theatre opened in 1819.
zh:
萨巴拉河汇入旧河一带的林木高地，在葡萄牙人说出米纳斯吉拉斯这个名字以前很久，就是大热依语族各民族的土地。沙克里亚巴人、普里人及同族各群使用这里的渡口、猎场和村地，沿内陆小路往来，与巴西海岸的市场没有什么相干。1444年时，这里没有欧洲人的城镇、税馆或淘金营地；河流与群山属于原住民，要等两百多年后，圣保罗的远征队才进入他们的世界。

葡萄牙人最初进山，为的是萨巴拉布苏，传说中一座由白银和绿宝石堆成的山脉。17世纪70年代，费尔南·迪亚斯·派斯的远征队在埃斯皮尼亚苏山附近搜遍山野，他的女婿曼努埃尔·德·博尔巴·加托开设了苏米多鲁和罗萨格兰德两处营地，营里的人是最早在溪流中找到黄金的一批。博尔巴·加托把金矿的发现瞒了好几年，消息一走漏，淘金者蜂拥而来；到1700年前后，萨巴拉的巴拉营地已是矿区人最多、最热闹的补给营地之一，坐落在皇家大道上。

黄金也使圣保罗拓殖者同他们口中的「恩博阿巴斯」，即葡萄牙本土和巴西其他地区来的新到者动起刀兵；1707年至1709年的恩博阿巴斯战争中，萨巴拉是双方争夺的矿区之一。外来者获胜后，王室在每条通往矿区的道路尽头设镇，以堵截黄金走私；1711年，王室选中以葡萄牙本土出生的矿工为主的萨巴拉，而不是圣保罗人盘踞的罗萨格兰德，设立萨巴拉圣母受孕皇家镇，1714年又成为司法辖区驻地。1734年，镇上的皇家熔铸厂开工，每一批黄金都要在这里缴付五分之一金税，镇上的奴隶人口也是当时最多的地方之一。黄金换来了本堂教堂、多座修会教堂，以及陡坡街道旁的石砌喷泉；市立剧院于1819年落成。

en:
Off the coast of São Vicente lies a sheltered island anchorage, separated from the mainland by a narrow tidal channel. Behind it the Serra do Mar rises sharply, and native tracks over the escarpment lead to the Piratininga plateau, a country of Atlantic forest and open grasslands. Tupiniquim and Tupinambá groups held the shore in 1444, while Guaianá people moved across the plateau above. The island had no Portuguese name.

The Portuguese made it their first firm foothold in this part of Brazil. Gaspar de Lemos sighted and named the island in 1502, and Martim Afonso de Sousa founded Vila de São Vicente in 1532 under orders from John III to check French traders. Its councilmen were elected the same year, making the town the first formally organized settlement in Portuguese America. The Engenho dos Erasmos, probably built in 1534, became one of the colony's earliest sugar mills. A few years later, Spaniards from the Plate entrenched themselves at Iguape and sacked São Vicente before they were driven south.

The route from the coast to the Piratininga plateau decided more than the island's own fields did. In 1554 Manuel da Nóbrega, José de Anchieta and other Jesuits established the College of São Paulo de Piratininga, which grew into the town of São Paulo. Tupiniquim fighters under Chief Tibiriçá beat off a Tamoio siege in 1562. Paulista bandeiras then pushed into the sertão, capturing Indigenous people and reaching the Minas Gerais goldfields. The captaincy's seat moved from São Vicente to São Paulo in 1681, and after the War of the Emboabas the crown bought the captaincy in 1709 and reorganized it as São Paulo e Minas de Ouro.
zh:
圣维森特海岸外有一处可避风浪的岛屿锚地，同大陆只隔一条狭窄潮汐水道。岛后马尔山陡起，原住民山径翻越崖壁，通向大西洋森林与疏林草原交错的皮拉蒂宁加高原。1444年，图皮尼基姆人和图皮南巴人据守海岸，瓜亚纳人在高原上往来，岛屿还没有葡萄牙名字。

葡萄牙人把这里建成他们在巴西这一地区的第一个稳固据点。1502年，加斯帕尔·德·莱莫斯望见并命名圣维森特岛；1532年，马丁·阿方索·德·索萨奉若昂三世之命建立圣维森特镇，以遏制法国商人。同年镇议会举行选举，使这里成为葡属美洲第一个正式建制的城镇。约1534年建成的埃拉斯莫斯糖坊，是殖民地最早的糖坊之一。几年后，来自拉普拉塔的西班牙人在伊瓜佩筑垒，洗劫圣维森特，随后才被逐往南方。

海岸通向皮拉蒂宁加高原的道路，比岛上农田更能决定后来的归属。1554年，曼努埃尔·达·诺布雷加、若泽·德·安谢塔等耶稣会士建立圣保罗德皮拉蒂宁加学苑，后来发展为圣保罗镇。1562年，酋长蒂比里萨率领图皮尼基姆战士击退塔莫伊人的围攻。圣保罗旗队再深入内陆，掳掠印第安人，并抵达米纳斯吉拉斯金矿区。1681年，领主治所从圣维森特迁往圣保罗；恩博阿巴战争之后，王室于1709年购入该领地，改组为圣保罗与黄金米纳斯领。

en:
Ortelsburg sits among the forests and lakes of southern Masuria, in the old Galindian wilderness that the Teutonic Order called the Wilderness. Between 1350 and 1360 Ortolf von Trier, Komtur of Elbing, raised a wooden border fort on the strip between two lakes, and in 1360 settled Masovian beekeepers beside it; their hamlet was called Beutnerdorf after their craft, the fort Ortulfsburg, in time Ortelsburg. Kęstutis's Lithuanians burned the wooden fort in 1370 and the Order rebuilt it in stone. It stood on the trade road from Warsaw to Königsberg, a frontier strongpoint against Lithuania and Masovia, and Polish troops held it after Grunwald in 1410. In 1444 it was still a small garrison post, with a Polish-speaking village at its gates.

In 1454 the town joined the Prussian Confederation and was incorporated into Poland, and after the Thirteen Years' War the peace of 1466 left it to the Order as a Polish fief. It passed to the Duchy of Prussia in 1525, and its people were Polish-speaking Masurians: in 1538 only five burghers are on record as knowing no Polish. The old fort was falling into ruin when Duke George Frederick rebuilt it as a hunting lodge from 1580, having taken the country for his hunting ground, and the craftsmen drawn by the works founded the town in 1581. A quarrel over beer-brewing rights with neighbouring Passenheim grew so bitter that the two fought a pitched battle in the fields between them; Elector John Sigismund settled it on 23 March 1616 by granting the town its charter. In 1629 Elector George William met Crown Prince Władysław Vasa here to prepare the truce that ended the Polish-Swedish war. Plague and a Tatar raid struck together in 1656, and plague returned in 1709 to 1711. From 1744 a Prussian jäger corps was garrisoned in the town, and the Ortelsburg Jägers made their name as scouts and marksmen. In the winter of 1806 Frederick William III and Queen Louise sheltered here from the French; on 1 December the king issued the Ortelsburg Publicandum ordering the reform of his army, and French troops sacked the town on the last day of the year.
zh:
奥特尔斯堡地处马祖里南部的林湖之间，原是古普鲁士加林迪亚部落的荒野，条顿骑士团径直称之为「荒原」。1350至1360年间，埃尔宾长官奥特洛夫·冯·特里尔在两湖之间的陆颈上筑起木制边防堡，1360年又从马佐夫舍迁来养蜂人安置在堡旁；村落因养蜂这行得名「养蜂人村」，城堡则称奥特卢夫斯堡，日后讹转为奥特尔斯堡。1370年科斯图提斯率立陶宛人烧毁木堡，骑士团改用石头重建。它坐落在华沙通往柯尼斯堡的商路上，是防备立陶宛和马佐夫舍的边境据点，1410年格伦瓦德战役后被波兰军队占领。1444年时，这里仍是一座小小的驻军要塞，城门外住着一个说波兰语的村落。

1454年该镇加入普鲁士联盟、并入波兰王国；十三年战争后，1466年的和约把它留给骑士团，作为波兰的封邑。1525年它转归普鲁士公国，居民都是说波兰语的马祖里人：据记载，1538年全镇只有五名市民不懂波兰语。旧堡日渐倾颓，把这一带当作猎场的格奥尔格·弗里德里希公爵从1580年起把它改建为狩猎行宫，应工程而来的工匠于1581年建起奥特尔斯堡镇。后来因啤酒酿造权与邻镇帕森海姆结怨，两镇人竟在之间的田地上大打出手；1616年3月23日，选帝侯约翰·西吉斯蒙德颁授城市特许状，了结这场争执。1629年，选帝侯格奥尔格·威廉与波兰王储瓦迪斯瓦夫·瓦萨在此会晤，筹备结束波瑞战争的停战协定。1656年瘟疫和鞑靼劫掠一同袭来，1709至1711年瘟疫再至。1744年起，一支普鲁士猎兵部队驻防本镇，「奥特尔斯堡猎兵」以侦察和枪法打出名声。1806年冬，弗里德里希·威廉三世与路易丝王后在此躲避法军，国王于12月1日颁布《奥特尔斯堡公告》，下令改革军队；法军在当年最后一天占领并洗劫了镇子。

en:
Guayrá is the forested plateau between the Paraná, Iguazu and Tietê rivers. The Paranapanema, Tibagi, Ivaí and Piquiri drain its Paraná pine woods, and the Peabiru track runs along its southern edge toward Santa Catarina and Asunción. In 1444 Kaingang bands held much of the hunting country, while Avá-Guarani villagers farmed the river banks and disputed the forest paths; Tupi lands began beyond the Tietê. The track carried Indigenous travellers, but no Spanish town or mission yet stood in the region.

The first Spanish settlements came from Asunción: Ontiveros in 1554, Ciudad Real del Guayrá in 1556 and Villa Rica del Espíritu Santo in 1570. Jesuits followed after a royal order of 1608, when José Cataldino and Simón Mazeta founded Loreto and San Ignacio and then built more than a dozen Guarani reductions along the northern rivers. The missions drew the Paulista bandeirantes, who raided for captives. Antônio Raposo Tavares and Manuel Preto built a fort on the Tibagi in 1628, and the attacks turned into an invasion. In late 1631 Antonio Ruiz de Montoya gathered the surviving Guarani on about 700 rafts; roughly 12,000 people left Guayrá and about 4,000 reached safety downstream, where the exiles refounded their missions. Ciudad Real was destroyed in 1638, and the Treaty of Madrid assigned the land to Portugal in 1750. In 1821 Guayrá remained a thinly held São Paulo forest frontier.
zh:
瓜伊拉是巴拉那河、伊瓜苏河与铁特河之间的森林高原。巴拉那帕内马河、蒂巴日河、伊瓦伊河和皮基里河穿过巴拉那松林，原住民的佩阿比鲁路沿南缘通往圣卡塔琳娜和亚松森。1444年时，卡因冈游群据有大片猎场，阿瓦-瓜拉尼村民在河畔耕作并争夺林中道路；铁特河以北是图皮人的地域。佩阿比鲁路上有原住民旅人往来，但瓜伊拉境内还没有西班牙城镇或传教站。

最早的西班牙人定居点来自亚松森方向：1554年的翁蒂韦罗斯、1556年的皇家瓜伊拉城和1570年的圣灵比亚里卡。1608年王室下令后，耶稣会士何塞·卡尔塔尔迪诺与西蒙·马塞塔建立洛雷托和圣伊格纳西奥，又在北部各河流域建起十多座瓜拉尼归化区。这些传教镇引来圣保罗旗队掳人为奴。1628年，安东尼奥·拉波索·塔瓦雷斯和曼努埃尔·普雷托在蒂巴日河畔筑堡，袭击随后演变为入侵。1631年底，安东尼奥·鲁伊斯·德·蒙托亚把幸存瓜拉尼人集中到约七百只木筏上；约一万二千人离开瓜伊拉，只有约四千人抵达下游，流亡者在那里重建传教区。皇家瓜伊拉城于1638年被毁，1750年《马德里条约》把这片土地划归葡萄牙。到1821年，瓜伊拉仍是圣保罗治下人口稀少的森林边地。

en:
Beyond the Serra do Mar, more than nine hundred metres above the Atlantic, the Curitiba plateau mixes open grasslands with forests of Paraná pine. Kaingang and Xoclengue hunters used the northern woods, while Mbyá and Nhandeva Guarani farmed and hunted around the headwaters of the Iguaçu to the south. The Tupi name Curitiba refers to an abundance of pine nuts. In 1444 only native trails crossed these campos.

Gold seekers from São Vicente climbed up from Paranaguá in the mid-seventeenth century, following the old Caminho de Queretiba; Eleodoro Ébanos Pereira led the first official mining expedition in 1649. A thatched chapel to Our Lady of Light gave the little settlement of Nossa Senhora da Luz dos Pinhais its name, Gabriel de Lara erected its pillory in 1668, and Mateus Martins Leme raised it to a vila in 1693. The gold gave out within a generation and miners left for Minas Gerais. In 1720–21 the royal judge Rafael Pires Pardinho renamed the vila Curitiba and required leave to cut trees along the rivers. After 1730 the cattle road from Rio Grande do Sul by way of Sorocaba to Minas Gerais turned the grasslands into breeding and wintering ground for tropeiro herds, and in 1812 Curitiba became seat of the comarca of Curitiba and Paranaguá.
zh:
越过马尔山，库里蒂巴高原高出大西洋九百多米，草甸与巴拉那松林交错。卡因冈人和肖克伦人在北部林地狩猎，姆比亚、南德瓦等瓜拉尼群体则在南方伊瓜苏河源一带务农兼狩猎。「库里蒂巴」是图皮语地名，意为多松籽之地。1444年，只有土著小道穿过这些草原。

17世纪中期，圣维森特的淘金者从巴拉那瓜翻山而来，沿古老的克雷蒂巴路寻找砂金；埃莱奥多罗·埃巴诺斯·佩雷拉于1649年率领第一支官方采矿队。供奉光明圣母的茅草小堂形成了「松林光明圣母」小村，加布里埃尔·德·拉腊1668年在此立起镇柱，马特乌斯·马丁斯·莱梅又于1693年将其升为镇。黄金不到一代人便告采尽，矿工转往米纳斯吉拉斯。1720至1721年，王室法官拉斐尔·皮雷斯·帕尔迪尼奥将镇名改为库里蒂巴，并规定砍伐河岸林木须经许可。1730年后，从南里约格兰德经索罗卡巴通往米纳斯吉拉斯的牛道，把这片草原变成赶牛队伍的繁育和越冬地；1812年，库里蒂巴成为库里蒂巴-巴拉那瓜司法区治所。

en:
Braslaw occupies Castle Hill on the narrow strip between Lakes Dryvyaty and Navyata, in the Baltic lake country. The water routes and pastures made it a useful border post: a castle of the Principality of Polotsk is mentioned there in 1065, and archaeologists have found traces of a Viking settlement nearby, probably connected with mercenaries guarding the frontier. It entered the Grand Duchy of Lithuania in the fourteenth century and watched the uneasy border with the Livonian Order. During the civil war of the 1430s, Švitrigaila gathered his Lithuanian, Livonian and Tatar supporters at Braslaw before his defeat near Wiłkomierz in September 1435. In 1444 it was a Lithuanian frontier castle, set among Orthodox Ruthenian villages whose people grazed cattle around the lakes.

The castle's best-known resident was Helena Ivanovna, daughter of Ivan III of Moscow and widow of Alexander Jagiellon. Alexander granted limited town rights while staying at Braslaw in 1500. After his death in 1506 Helena received the castle and estate; she had refused to convert from Orthodoxy, and her marriage had given Moscow a pretext for intervening in Lithuanian affairs. She settled here, founded an Orthodox convent on Castle Hill, and died in 1513. The Habsburg envoy Herberstein passed through in 1517 and noted the great lake beside the town. Later centuries were quieter: Stanisław August granted a coat of arms in 1792, the Third Partition assigned Braslaw to Russia in 1795, and Marshal Michel Ney kept a short headquarters there during the 1812 French campaign.
zh:
布拉斯拉夫坐落在德里维亚特湖与纳维亚塔湖之间的狭长地带，城堡山扼守波罗的海湖区的水路和牧道。1065年文献已提到这座波洛茨克公国城堡；考古学者还在附近发现维京人定居点，认为可能与守卫边境的雇佣兵有关。14世纪它并入立陶宛大公国，监视同立窝尼亚骑士团之间不安的边界。1430年代内战中，斯维特里盖拉在布拉斯拉夫集结立陶宛、立窝尼亚和鞑靼部众，1435年9月在维尔基米日附近战败。1444年，这里是立陶宛边境城堡，周围是说罗塞尼亚语的东正教村庄，村民沿湖放牧牛群。

城堡最有名的住客是莫斯科的叶莲娜·伊凡诺芙娜。她是伊凡三世之女、亚历山大·雅盖隆契克的遗孀。1500年亚历山大驻跸布拉斯拉夫时，授予城镇有限自治权。1506年丈夫死后，叶莲娜获得城堡和领地；她始终不愿放弃东正教改宗天主教，这段婚姻也让莫斯科有了干预立陶宛事务的借口。她定居此地，在城堡山修建东正教女修院，1513年在此去世。1517年，哈布斯堡使节赫伯斯坦路过，记下城边的大湖。此后几个世纪较为平静：1792年斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特赐下纹章，1795年第三次瓜分把布拉斯拉夫划归俄国；1812年法国战役期间，米歇尔·内伊元帅曾把司令部短暂设在此地。

en:
Vitebsk grew up around the harbour at the Vitba's mouth on the Western Dvina, where boats could move between the Dvina system and Dnieper portages. It is first recorded in 1021 and became the seat of its own principality in 1101. Its transfer to Lithuania came through a marriage: Algirdas married Maria, daughter of the last prince of Vitebsk, and inherited the town in 1321. By 1351 the Upper and Lower Castles and a princely palace stood above the rivers. In 1441 Vitebsk was listed among the fifteen largest cities of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Three years later it was a major Orthodox Ruthenian trading town, with merchants, boatmen and craft suburbs below its stone forts.

Early in the sixteenth century Vitebsk became the seat of its voivodeship, and in 1597 it received Magdeburg law and a coat of arms. Religious division then brought its worst internal crisis. On 12 November 1623 Orthodox burghers killed Josaphat Kuntsevych, the Uniate archbishop of Polotsk, and the Crown punished the whole town by withdrawing its city rights until 1644. A Jesuit collegium ran a school theatre there from 1641, but the Thirteen Years' War brought a Russian and Cossack siege in 1654; the Truce of Andrusovo returned Vitebsk to the Commonwealth in 1667. By the later eighteenth century it was the second-largest town in the Belarusian lands after Mogilev. The First Partition assigned it to Russia in 1772, and it became the seat of Vitebsk Governorate in 1802. On 26-27 July 1812 Russian rearguards under Konovnitsyn and Pahlen fought on the Luchosa outside the town, holding Napoleon long enough for Barclay de Tolly's army to slip away toward Smolensk. The French then occupied Vitebsk.
zh:
维捷布斯克兴起于维季巴河注入西德维纳河的河口港，船只可在这里进入西德维纳水系，并经水陆联运接上第聂伯河商路。它1021年首见记载，1101年成为独立公国的治所。它转入立陶宛之手与一场婚姻有关：阿尔吉尔达斯娶末位维捷布斯克公爵之女玛丽亚，于1321年继承此城。到1351年，河畔高地上已经建起上堡、下堡和王公宫殿。1441年，维捷布斯克名列立陶宛大公国十五座最大城市。三年后，这里已是一座重要的东正教鲁塞尼亚商镇，石堡下方住着商人、船工和各行手工业者。

16世纪初，维捷布斯克成为本省省治，1597年获得马格德堡法和城徽。宗教分歧随后给它带来最严重的内部危机。1623年11月12日，信奉东正教的市民杀死波洛茨克东仪派大主教约萨法特·昆采维奇，王室以褫夺全城城市权作为惩罚，直到1644年才恢复。1641年起，耶稣会学院在此办有校园剧场；十三年战争期间，俄军和哥萨克军队于1654年围城夺取此城，1667年安德鲁索沃停战协定又把它归还联邦。到18世纪后期，它已是白俄罗斯土地上仅次于莫吉廖夫的第二大城。1772年第一次瓜分把它划给俄罗斯，1802年成为维捷布斯克省省会。1812年7月26至27日，科诺夫尼岑和帕伦率领的俄军后卫在城外卢乔萨河阻击拿破仑，为巴克莱·德托利的主力撤向斯摩棱斯克争取到时间，随后法军占领维捷布斯克。

en:
The Uruguay River makes a broad bend at Paysandú, its east bank broken by wooded stream valleys behind open grazing country. The name is Guaraní: the Bavarian Jesuit Bernardo Nusdorffer, a missionary in the eastern reductions, wrote of the river island of Y Paucando, 'the island set in the river', and a Jesuit map of 1749 marked Paisandú at this crossing. In 1444 no European had yet seen it. Charrúa, Chaná and Minuane bands spent the summers fishing on the river and the winters inland, hunting deer and rheas with bolas and bows; the crossings and pastures were shared ground, not a frontier.

Spain and Portugal settled the ownership of this bank in a long string of treaties and raids. Colonial papers called the place the Paso de Paisandú by 1754, and after the Treaty of San Ildefonso fixed the border in 1777 the landing became a river port with a saladero, where cattle were slaughtered for tasajo and hides. A parish followed in 1805, and Benito Chain laid out the town in 1810. José Artigas crossed here in 1811 from the Argentine bank to lead the Oriental revolution, and in 1815 he ran his war from a mud rancho beside the old church. The priest Damaso Larrañaga found an Indian village of twenty-five households that was, as he noted in his travel diary, 'provisionally the capital of the Orientals', because Artigas, his staff and the deputies of the other towns were all camped in it.
zh:
乌拉圭河在派桑杜一带拐了个大弯，东岸开阔牧场背后是林木茂密的溪谷。地名来自瓜拉尼语：在东部传教区传教的巴伐利亚耶稣会士贝尔纳多·努斯多费尔曾记下河中有岛，名唤「伊保桑多」（Y Paucando），意为「河中插入的岛」；1749年的一张耶稣会地图已在这处渡口标出派桑杜。1444年时欧洲人还没有到过这里，查鲁亚、查纳和米努安人的游群夏天在河边捕鱼，冬天带着流星锤和弓箭进入内地猎鹿和美洲鸵；渡口和草场是共用之地，不是边界。

西班牙和葡萄牙靠一连串条约与袭扰确定了这段河岸的归属。到1754年，殖民地文书已把这里称作派桑杜渡口；1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》划定边界后，这个登陆点发展成河港和腌肉场，宰杀牛只制作肉干、收集皮革。1805年这里设立教区，1810年贝尼托·查因规划了城镇。1811年，何塞·阿蒂加斯从阿根廷一侧渡河到此，领导东岸革命；1815年，他在老教堂旁一间土坯茅舍里指挥战事。神父达马索·拉腊尼亚加在旅行日记里写道，这个只有二十五户人家的印第安村落「暂时是东岸人的首都」，因为阿蒂加斯、他的参谋班子和各镇代表都驻在村里。

en:
The far east of the Banda Oriental is where the grasslands meet the Atlantic: dunes and coastal lagoons run down to the Cerro de San Miguel south of the Laguna Merin, and a narrow strip of dry ground between the Castillos hills and the sea carries the only overland road from the Rio de la Plata to Brazil. In 1444 it was Guenoa country, one of the peoples the Spanish sources group with the Charrúa, whose bands followed game across plain and lagoon shore.

Cattle escaped from the early Europeans ran wild here in great herds, and by the eighteenth century their hides drew slaughter gangs and smugglers to the eastern grasslands. The two empires set about blocking the coastal road with forts. A Spanish fieldwork went up on the Cerro de San Miguel in 1734; the Portuguese took it three years later and built the present four-bastion stone fort from 17 October 1737, a Vauban-style star worked in rough stone with a garrison of a hundred. The Treaty of Madrid let Portugal keep the Castillos line in 1750. When war reopened, the Portuguese threw up the Fortaleza de Santa Teresa at the Angostura defile in October 1762, its timber hauled thirty kilometres through swamps from San Miguel; Pedro de Cevallos took both forts in April 1763 and marched on into Rio Grande. The Portuguese commander Tomas Luis Osorio was court-martialled for the loss and hanged in Lisbon, until the evidence his widow produced cleared his name. Bernardo Lecocq strengthened the works in 1775, and the Treaty of San Ildefonso confirmed them to Spain in 1777.
zh:
东岸的最东端是草原与大西洋相接之处：沙丘和沿海潟湖一直延伸到梅林潟湖以南的圣米格尔山；卡斯蒂略斯山地与大海之间有一条狭窄的干地，是从拉普拉塔通往巴西的唯一陆上通道。1444年时，这里是格诺阿人的土地，西班牙文献把格诺阿人归入查鲁亚诸族；他们的游群在平原和潟湖岸边追逐猎物迁徙。

早期欧洲人带来的牛只在这里野化，形成庞大的牛群；到18世纪，牛皮把屠宰队和走私者吸引到东部草原。两个帝国着手在沿海通道上设堡封堵。1734年，圣米格尔山上先有一座西班牙野战工事；三年后葡萄牙人将其夺取，并于1737年10月17日起修建现存的四棱堡石堡，采用沃邦式星形布局，粗石砌成，驻军百人。1750年《马德里条约》允许葡萄牙保留卡斯蒂略斯防线。战事重开后，葡萄牙人于1762年10月在安戈斯图拉隘口赶建圣特蕾莎要塞，木材要从圣米格尔穿过沼泽拖运三十公里；佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯1763年4月连夺两堡，继续向里奥格兰德推进。守将托马斯·路易斯·奥索里奥因失守被军事法庭判处绞刑、在里斯本处死，后来他的遗孀拿出证据，才洗清他的罪名。贝尔纳多·勒科克1775年加固工事，1777年《圣伊尔德方索条约》确认两堡归西班牙所有。

en: Al-Junaynah, El Geneina, the 'little garden', is a watered basin on the Darfur-Wadai road, in the Masalit country of Dar Masalit. In 1444 its farmers and herders answered to the Tunjur, who had taken the old Daju lands and linked Darfur with Ouaddai; the rulers still kept to their own cults and Islam touched only the leading families. In 1635 Abd al-Karim of the Maba overthrew the last Tunjur king, Daud, founded the Kolak dynasty at Wara, and bound the Masalit and Dajo to him by marriage. After Muhammad Sabun made Wadai a power in 1804, royal caravans took the road through Ennedi and Kufra to Benghazi, and the livestock, ivory and captives of this western borderland went north with them.
