zh: 朱奈纳（Al-Junaynah，阿拉伯语意为「小花园」）是达尔富尔通往瓦达伊的路上一处有水的盆地，地处马萨利特人的家园达尔马萨利特。1444年，这里的农民和牧人臣服于通朱尔人；他们夺取旧达朱人的土地，把达尔富尔和瓦达伊连成一片，统治者仍保留自己的信仰，伊斯兰教只在显贵家族中流传。1635年，马巴人阿卜杜勒·卡里姆推翻末代通朱尔国王达乌德，在瓦拉建立科拉克王朝，并以联姻把马萨利特和达朱两族拴在自己一边。1804年穆罕默德·萨本使瓦达伊强盛后，王室商队取道恩内迪、库夫拉前往班加西，这片西部边地的牲畜、象牙和掳掠的人口也随之北上。

en:
In 1444 the bay of Asunción, on the east bank of the Paraguay River near its meeting with the Pilcomayo, belonged to Cario groups of the wider Guaraní world. Their maize fields, fishing camps and river crossings occupied the bank where Spanish ships later anchored. The river led north toward swamps and the routes to Upper Peru, and south toward the Río de la Plata. Cario leaders made alliances through kinship and marriage, a system that shaped the colony as soon as European soldiers entered the bay.

Juan de Ayolas passed up the river around 1537 while looking for a route to Upper Peru. Juan de Salazar y Espinosa found the Cario friendly and raised the fort of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción on 15 August 1537; Domingo Martínez de Irala established the cabildo that made it a city on 16 September 1541. After the first Buenos Aires failed, its settlers moved here, and Asunción became the oldest continuously occupied Spanish town in the basin, called the Mother of Cities for the expeditions that later refounded Buenos Aires and founded Santa Fe, Corrientes, Córdoba and Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Early alliances followed the Guaraní cuñadazgo, by which chiefs gave women to newcomers; after 1541 forced round-ups called rancheadas overshadowed that custom. Irala, elected commander by the settlers in 1538, later acknowledged nine children by seven Guaraní women. The 1603 Synod of Asunción ordered missionaries to work in Guaraní.

Conflict over imperial office made Asunción an early centre of revolt. José de Antequera y Castro, sent to investigate Governor Diego de los Reyes Balmaseda, took the governorship himself in 1721 and defeated royal forces before he was arrested and executed in 1731. His comunero followers fought on until 1735. On the night of 14-15 May 1811, plotters meeting in Juana María de Lara's house moved against Governor Bernardo de Velasco. Two years later Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia began his long rule of independent Paraguay.
zh:
1444年，亚松森河湾位于巴拉圭河东岸，靠近皮科马约河注入巴拉圭河的地方，属于瓜拉尼人群中的卡里奥人。他们的玉米田、渔场和渡口占据着后来西班牙船只停泊的河岸。巴拉圭河北通沼泽和前往上秘鲁的道路，南下拉普拉塔河。卡里奥首领靠亲属关系和婚姻结盟，欧洲士兵进入河湾后，这套制度很快改变了殖民地的面貌。

约1537年，胡安·德·阿约拉斯为寻找通往上秘鲁的道路溯河而上。胡安·德·萨拉查·伊·埃斯皮诺萨发现卡里奥人态度友善，于1537年8月15日建起圣母升天堡；1541年9月16日，多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉设立市政会，把要塞变成城市。第一座布宜诺斯艾利斯失败后，居民迁到亚松森，使这里成为拉普拉塔河流域最古老且持续有人居住的西班牙城镇。从亚松森出发的远征队再建布宜诺斯艾利斯，又建立圣菲、科连特斯、科尔多瓦和圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，因此它得到「诸城之母」的称呼。早期同盟遵循瓜拉尼人的姻亲制度，首领把女子送给新来者以结成亲属；1541年后，被称为「兰切阿达」的大规模暴力掳掠压倒了这种安排。1538年被移民推举为指挥官的伊拉拉，后来承认自己与七名瓜拉尼妇女生有九名子女。1603年的亚松森主教会议要求传教士使用瓜拉尼语。

围绕帝国官职的冲突，使亚松森早早成为起事之地。何塞·德·安特克拉·伊·卡斯特罗奉命调查总督迭戈·德·洛斯·雷耶斯·巴尔马塞达，却在1721年自任总督，击败王师，最后被捕并于1731年处死。他的公社追随者一直作战到1735年。1811年5月14日夜间至15日，密谋者在胡安娜·玛丽亚·德·拉拉家中集合，向总督贝纳尔多·德·贝拉斯科动手。两年后，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚开始长期统治独立的巴拉圭。

en:
In 1444 the wooded Paraguay River banks around Concepción had no Spanish fort or market town. Guaraní-speaking farmers kept villages east of the river, while Mbayá bands moved through the northern Chaco and the upper Paraguay. They called themselves Eyiguayegis, people of the palm. The river linked these worlds: raiders, fishermen, kin parties and traders crossed at familiar bays. After Spaniards entered the basin, those crossings became a military frontier between Asunción and Portuguese Brazil.

War came before permanent settlement. In 1542 Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca led Guaraní allies against Mbayá raiders northeast of Asunción. Within a century Mbayá bands had horses and iron tools, raided Guaraní villages and Spanish holdings, and destroyed a reduction in Itatín in 1661. Some bands made peace while others kept fighting, leaving the northern bank unsafe for decades. Belén, the first moderately successful mission among the Mbayá, opened east of the future Concepción in 1760. Governor Agustín Fernando de Pinedo founded Villa Real de la Concepción in 1773 as a military town against Portuguese advance; soldiers received land grants, and the settlement remained a garrison post until its cabildo opened in 1812. In 1813 Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia established the penal settlement of Tevego farther north, posting convicts and guards on ground colonial forces had never firmly controlled.
zh:
1444年，康塞普西翁一带林木茂密的巴拉圭河畔还没有西班牙要塞或集镇。讲瓜拉尼语的农民在河东居住，姆巴亚人群则在北查科和巴拉圭河上游移动。他们自称埃伊瓜耶吉，意为「棕榈之人」。巴拉圭河连接着这些人群：袭掠者、渔夫、亲族和商人都在熟悉的河湾往来。西班牙人进入流域后，这些渡口成了亚松森与葡属巴西之间的军事前沿。

战争早于永久定居点到来。1542年，阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡率领瓜拉尼盟友，进攻亚松森东北方的姆巴亚袭掠者。不到一个世纪，姆巴亚人已有马匹和铁制工具，袭击瓜拉尼村社与西班牙据点，并在1661年摧毁伊塔廷的一处传教村。有些群体议和，另一些继续作战，使北岸数十年不得安定。1760年，贝伦传教村在后来的康塞普西翁以东设立，是姆巴亚人中第一个稍有成效的传教点。1773年，总督阿古斯丁·费尔南多·德·皮内多建立王家康塞普西翁镇，把它当作抵御葡萄牙推进的军镇；士兵获得授地，居民点一直承担驻军职能，到1812年才设立市政会。1813年，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚在更北处设立特韦戈流放地，把犯人和守卫放到殖民军队从未牢牢控制的地带上。

en:
At the bend where the Paraná turns south, about fifty kilometres below its meeting with the Paraguay, seven stone points run out into the river and throw up rough water; the Spaniards named their settlement Ciudad de Vera de las Siete Corrientes, the city of the seven currents, while the Guarani called the place Taragüí. In 1444 this was Guarani country: large communal villages, the tekoá, lined the Paraná and the Uruguay, whose people grew maize and manioc, fished the river and raided their old enemies the Charrúa to the south-east, with Kaingang bands holding the eastern woods. Sebastian Cabot's ships first entered the Paraná in 1527. On 3 April 1588 the adelantado Juan Torres de Vera y Aragón, helped by Alonso de Vera y Aragón and Hernandarias, planted a way-station on the flood-free high bank, a natural harbour on the long river road between Asunción and Buenos Aires; its 148 first settlers came from Asunción and Concepción del Bermejo. A wooden cross raised outside the new fort gave the town its founding legend: in a fight with the Guarani in May 1588 fire and thunder were said to burst around it, and the Spaniards' arquebus flashes were taken for the god of the cross speaking; the episode was remembered as the Miracle of the Cross.

The town stayed small, but its shipyards built vessels for the whole viceroyalty and its hides went downriver to market. Corrientes kept a rebellious streak, rising against Asunción in the comunero troubles of 1732 and 1763. The Cazadores Correntinos militia went south to defend Buenos Aires during the English invasions of 1806 and 1807. In 1810 the cabildo joined the May Revolution as Belgrano's small army passed through on its way to Paraguay, and in 1814 an open cabildo recognized Artigas as Protector of the Free Peoples. From 1818 to 1819 the province was governed by Artigas's Guarani foster son Andrés Guazurarí, known as Andresito, the only caudillo of fully indigenous origin in the independence wars. In December 1821 the province adopted its first constitution.
zh:
巴拉那河在与巴拉圭河汇合后下行约五十公里处折向南流，七道石岬伸入江中，激起湍急的水流；西班牙人把新城命名为「七急流的贝拉城」，后简称科连特斯，瓜拉尼人则称之为塔拉圭。1444年，这道河湾还是瓜拉尼人的土地：巴拉那河与乌拉圭河畔坐落着名为特科阿的大型村社，村民种玉米、木薯，下河捕鱼，不时奔袭东南方的宿敌查鲁亚人，东边丛林里则是卡因冈人的游团。1527年，塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特的船队首次驶入巴拉那河。1588年4月3日，殖民督办胡安·托雷斯·德·贝拉-亚拉贡在阿隆索·德·贝拉-亚拉贡和埃尔南达里亚斯协助下，在不受洪水威胁的高岸设驿建站，作为亚松森与布宜诺斯艾利斯之间漫长水路上的天然良港，最早的148户居民来自亚松森和贝尔梅霍河畔的康塞普西翁。新城堡外竖起的一座木十字架引出了建城传说：相传1588年5月与瓜拉尼人交战时，十字架周围火光雷声大作，西班牙人火绳枪的爆闪被当成十字架之神显灵，此事后来被称作「十字圣迹」。

城镇长期不大，造船厂却为整个总督辖区造船，兽皮也顺河运往市场。科连特斯人素来不服亚松森管束，1732年和1763年两度卷入公社派起事。1806至1807年英国入侵拉普拉塔时，「科连特斯猎兵」民团南下参加保卫布宜诺斯艾利斯。1810年，市议会加入五月革命，贝尔格拉诺的小股部队正取道这里出征巴拉圭；1814年，开放市政会拥戴阿蒂加斯为「自由人民保护者」。1818至1819年主政该省的是阿蒂加斯的瓜拉尼人养子安德列斯·瓜苏拉利，人称「小安德列斯」，也是独立战争中唯一纯印第安血统的地方领袖。1821年12月，科连特斯颁布了这一带第一部省宪法。

en:
The Río de la Plata is the broad freshwater estuary where the Paraná and Uruguay rivers pour into the Atlantic, its southern shore opening onto the flat grassland of the pampas. In 1444 no European ship had entered it. Charrúa bands moved along the northern shore, and Querandí hunters held the country behind the future Buenos Aires, running down guanaco and rhea on foot and hobbling the animals with the boleadora. Inca power ended far to the north in the Andes, so nothing on the river answered to any master.

Juan Díaz de Solís sailed in for Spain in 1516 and called the water the Mar Dulce, the freshwater sea, before Charrúa warriors killed him on the Uruguayan shore. Sebastian Cabot explored up the Paraná in 1527, got silver trinkets from the Guaraní and heard of a silver mountain inland; he named the water the River of Silver, and the name outlived the legend. Pedro de Mendoza planted Puerto de Nuestra Señora del Buen Ayre on the shore in 1536, but famine and Querandí attacks drove the settlers out, and in late June 1541 they burned the post themselves and withdrew to Asunción. The town that held was founded on 11 June 1580 by Juan de Garay, who came down the Paraná with some three hundred settlers, most of them Guaraní families.

Buenos Aires had been meant to guard the route of Potosí silver, but the Crown let legal goods travel only through Lima and Seville, so the porteños lived by contraband with Brazil, paid for in hides stripped from the feral cattle that overran the pampas; organised hunts killed them by the thousand for leather and tallow. In 1680 a force from the town crossed the water and seized the Portuguese Colonia del Sacramento within months of its founding. Made capital of the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776, Buenos Aires threw out British invaders in 1806 and again in 1807 under Santiago de Liniers. On 25 May 1810 the cabildo deposed Viceroy Cisneros and set up a junta, opening the war that ended Spanish rule.
zh:
拉普拉塔河是巴拉那河与乌拉圭河注入大西洋汇成的宽阔淡水河口，南岸连着平坦无垠的潘帕斯草原。1444年，还没有欧洲船只驶入这条大河：查鲁亚人的游群活动在北岸，克兰迪猎人据有日后布宜诺斯艾利斯背后的土地，他们徒步追猎原驼和美洲鸵，用流星索将猎物绊倒。印加人的势力远在北方安第斯山中便告终止，河上的一切不受任何人统辖。

1516年，胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯代表西班牙驶入河口，把这片水域称为「淡水海」，不久便在乌拉圭岸上被查鲁亚武士杀死。1527年，塞巴斯蒂安·卡博特溯巴拉那河而上，从瓜拉尼人手中得到银饰，又听说内陆有一座银山，便把这条水道命名为拉普拉塔河，意为「银河」；银山的传说后来消散，河名却留了下来。1536年，佩德罗·德·门多萨在岸上建起「善风圣母港」，饥荒和克兰迪人的袭击却逼走殖民者，1541年6月底他们自己烧毁据点，撤往亚松森。真正扎下根的城市由胡安·德·加赖在1580年6月11日建立：他顺巴拉那河而下，带着约三百名移民，其中多为瓜拉尼人家族。

布宜诺斯艾利斯本是为守护波托西白银的出路而设，王室却规定合法货物只能绕道利马和塞维利亚，港口人于是靠与巴西的走私为生，付给对方的是潘帕斯草原上泛滥的野牛皮；人们组织围猎，成千上万地宰杀牛群，取走皮革和油脂。1680年，一支从该城出发的军队渡河南下，在葡萄牙人建成萨克拉门托殖民地几个月后便将其夺取。1776年，布宜诺斯艾利斯成为新设拉普拉塔总督辖区的首府；1806年和1807年，圣地亚哥·德·利尼耶斯率军两度击退英国入侵者。1810年5月25日，市政会议废黜总督西斯内罗斯，另立执政委员会，终结西班牙统治的战争随之展开。

en:
The Tandilia and Ventana hills break the grass plains between the Salado River and the Atlantic, at the southern end of the country the Spaniards called the Pampas. In 1444 small bands of Serranos moved through their glens and the empty coast beyond. They were northern Tehuelche groups, counted by the Jesuit Thomas Falkner among his Het and called Puelches by the Spaniards: nomadic hunters who ran down guanaco and rhea, threw the bolas, lived in leather toldos and fought the Pampas bands to the north. No European ship had yet touched the shore.

Magellan's fleet passed along this coast in 1520. Horses and feral cattle from the Spanish settlements on the Rio de la Plata later changed the hunt, and by the eighteenth century the glens held one of the region's great gatherings. At the Chapaleofu fair, the 'poncho fair' recorded by the Jesuits, people from the pampas, northern Patagonia and both sides of the Andes met to trade ponchos, cattle and hides. Falkner, an English Jesuit physician who spent nearly forty years among these peoples, knew the hills himself: in 1746 he and Jose Cardiel opened the mission of Nuestra Senora del Pilar beside the coastal lagoons, and it was abandoned five years later. Back in England he published his Description of Patagonia, the fullest European account of these peoples. A Spanish expedition crossed the ranges and reached Tandil about 1770. In 1821 no Spanish town yet stood on these hills.
zh:
坦迪利亚山与本塔纳山突起在萨拉多河与大西洋之间的草原上，是西班牙人所称潘帕斯草原的南端。1444年，塞拉诺人的小股游群往来于山谷和更南边荒无人烟的海岸之间。他们是北特维尔切人的一支，耶稣会士托马斯·福克纳把他们归入自己所说的海特人，西班牙人则称之为普埃尔切人：逐猎原驼和美洲鸵的游牧猎人，擅长投掷流星索，住在兽皮帐篷里，常年与北方的潘帕斯诸部交战。此时还没有一艘欧洲船靠过这段海岸。

1520年，麦哲伦的船队从这段海岸外驶过。拉普拉塔殖民点的马匹和野化牛群后来改变了他们的狩猎方式，到18世纪，这些山谷里有了这一带最盛大的集会之一。耶稣会士笔下的「篷乔集市」设在查帕莱奥富，潘帕斯、北巴塔哥尼亚和安第斯山两侧的人们来此交易篷乔、牛只和皮革。福克纳是英国籍耶稣会士兼医生，在这些部族中生活了近四十年，亲自走过这片群山：1746年，他和何塞·卡迭尔在滨海潟湖畔建起皮拉尔圣母传教所，五年后即告废弃。回到英国后，他出版了《巴塔哥尼亚志》，这是当时欧洲人记述这些部族最详尽的一部书。约1770年，一支西班牙探险队越过山岭抵达坦迪尔。到1821年，山间还没有一座西班牙城镇。

en:
The salt-white shores around Bahía Blanca mark the southern edge of the Pampas, where streams and shallow estuaries cut through dry lowland. In 1444 small Gününa küna bands moved along this coast; Mapuche-speakers called them Puelche, people of the east. They hunted guanaco, rhea and Andean deer with bows and boleadoras, gathered wild fruit and seeds, and camped in skin tents near fresh water under family elders. No Spanish post stood on the bay, and its whitish banks had not yet been fixed on a reliable chart.

The coast remained poorly mapped into the late eighteenth century. Epidemics then cut deeply into the Gününa küna, and survivors joined Mapuche, Het and Tehuelche communities. In 1805 the Spanish crown ordered an official survey of the shoreline. After 1810, indigenous leaders and Criollo traders moved through the region as patriot and royalist forces contested the pampas, but the bay itself had no permanent Spanish garrison by 1821.
zh:
坎德拉里亚（布兰卡湾一带）盐白色的海岸是潘帕斯草原南缘，溪流和浅河口切过干旱低地。1444年，小型居努纳·库纳游群在这一带海岸活动；马普切语使用者称他们为普埃尔切人，意为「东方的人」。他们用弓箭和投石索猎取原驼、美洲鸵和安第斯鹿，采集野果与种子，由家族长者带领，在淡水旁搭起兽皮帐篷。海湾边没有西班牙据点，发白的崖岸也还没有出现在可靠海图上。

直到18世纪末，这条海岸仍缺少精确测绘。随后的疫病使居努纳·库纳人口锐减，幸存者并入马普切、海特和特维尔切社群。1805年，西班牙王室下令正式勘测海岸线。1810年后，随着爱国者与保王派军队争夺潘帕斯，原住民首领和克里奥尔商人也在这一地区往来，但到1821年，海湾边仍没有西班牙常设驻军。

en:
Puerto Deseado occupies a narrow ria roughly twenty miles long where the Deseado River meets the Atlantic, one of Patagonia's most reliable anchorages. In 1444 the dry hills and shoreline were Aónikenk Tehuelche country. Bands wintered on the coast for fish, shellfish and seals, then followed guanaco and rhea into the open steppe and uplands in summer. They moved with the seasons rather than building a town, and the deep inlet served as a landing place before European ships reached it.

European ships used the anchorage early, but settlements failed there repeatedly. Driven in by a storm, the Magellan-Elcano expedition entered the inlet in March 1520 and named it Bahía de los Trabajos Forzosos after the labour the weather cost the crews. Thomas Cavendish sailed in on 17 December 1586 aboard the Desire and called the anchorage Port Desire after his ship; Tehuelche arrows wounded several crewmen, and he left after ten days. The headland at the mouth took the name Punta Cavendish. John Narborough claimed the coast for England in 1670 without leaving an occupation. Antonio de Viedma's Spanish camp of 1780 lasted seven months, even with a wooden fort, a scurvy hospital, a forge and a bread oven. In 1789 the Real Compañía Marítima tried a permanent fishing station, building a chapel, hospital, fields, salting works and the Todos los Santos and San Carlos forts. No whales were found, sea lions could not pay for the station, supplies and desertions drained it, and the company withdrew in 1803; the last soldiers left in 1807.
zh:
德塞阿多港在德塞阿多河注入大西洋处，是一条约32公里长的狭窄河口湾，也是巴塔哥尼亚少见的可靠锚地。1444年，干旱丘陵和海岸属于阿奥尼肯克·特维尔切人的活动范围。他们冬季在岸边扎营，捕鱼、拾贝、捕猎海豹，夏季追随原驼和美洲鸵进入开阔草原与高地。人们按季节迁徙，不建城镇；欧洲船只到来前，深水湾已是可供停泊的登陆地。

欧洲船很早便利用这个锚地，定居尝试却一再失败。1520年3月，麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺探险队被风暴吹入湾中，因船员在恶劣天气下付出大量劳役，将它命名为「苦役湾」。1586年12月17日，托马斯·卡文迪什乘「欲望号」进湾，按船名把这里称作欲望港；特维尔切人的箭射伤数名船员，他十天后便离去，湾口岬角后来得名卡文迪什角。1670年，约翰·纳伯勒为英格兰宣称这片海岸，却没有留下占领军。1780年，安东尼奥·德·别德马设立的西班牙营地维持了七个月，营中曾有木堡、坏血病医院、铁匠炉和面包炉。1789年，皇家海事公司尝试建立常设渔业站，建起小堂、医院、农田、腌渔场以及诸圣堡和圣卡洛斯堡。附近没有鲸，海狮收益不足以维持站点，补给和逃亡又不断耗损人力物力；公司于1803年撤出，最后的士兵在1807年离开。

en:
Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego lies beyond the Strait of Magellan at the southern edge of the Americas. Its northern half is treeless, wind-scoured steppe; its southern edge is a broken maze of channels and islands. In 1444 the northern plains and the interior belonged to the Selk'nam, whom their neighbours called Ona, land nomads who hunted guanaco with bows and kept no fixed villages. A related people, the Haush, held the rainy Mitre Peninsula to the southeast, while canoe-going Yahgan and Kawesqar lived from the colder southern channels. The Selk'nam called the island Karukinka, 'our land.' They wore little against the cold and kept fires burning day and night, even carrying embers in their bark canoes; the smoke of those fires gave the island its European name.

Ships, not settlers, made its early European history. On 21 August 1520 the Magellan-Elcano expedition saw the line of fires from offshore and first charted the coast as Land of Smoke, until Charles I of Spain renamed it Land of Fire. On 1 November the fleet found the All Saints' Strait, the passage now called the Strait of Magellan, and took nineteen days tracing the island's northern shore, believing it a coast of the supposed southern continent. In 1578 storms drove Francis Drake south of the islands into open water, the passage that now carries his name, which showed the land was no continent; Juan de Alderete in 1555 and Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa later both gave up attempts to conquer the island, beaten by its climate. In January 1616 Jacob le Maire and Willem Schouten rounded Cape Horn, named for their ship Hoorn, and opened the high-latitude route most later sailers preferred to the narrow strait. The first Europeans who actually lived on the island were castaways: after the Purísima Concepción was wrecked in 1765, 193 survivors spent three months building a boat at Puerto Consolación and sailed her to Buenos Aires. James Cook surveyed the northeast coast in 1769 and, with the naturalist Joseph Banks, met Haush people at Buen Suceso Bay while taking on wood and water. Through 1821 no European power had raised a permanent town on the island.
zh:
火地岛位于麦哲伦海峡以南、美洲大陆的最南端，北半部是无树多风的草原，南缘是支离破碎的水道与岛群。1444年，北部平原和内陆是塞尔克南人（邻族称他们为奥纳人）的活动范围：他们是陆上游牧者，用弓箭猎原驼，没有固定村落。亲缘相近的豪什人住在多雨的东南米特雷半岛，驾独木舟的雅甘人和卡韦斯卡尔人则在更寒冷的南部水道谋生。塞尔克南人称此岛为卡鲁金卡，意为「我们的土地」。他们衣着单薄，靠昼夜不熄的火堆御寒，连树皮独木舟里也带着火种；欧洲人后来以这些火堆的烟为这座岛命名。

这座岛最早的欧洲史是一部航船史。1520年8月21日，麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺探险队在海上望见连绵的烟火，最初把这片海岸命名为烟地，西班牙国王卡洛斯一世后来改为火地。11月1日，船队发现诸圣海峡，即后来的麦哲伦海峡，沿岛屿北岸走了十九天，当时还以为这是传说中南方大陆的海岸。1578年，风暴把弗朗西斯·德雷克吹到群岛以南的开阔海面（这片海域后来以德雷克命名），人们这才看清这里不是大陆；1555年的胡安·德·阿尔德雷特和后来的佩德罗·萨米恩托·德·甘博阿都曾试图征服火地岛，都败于气候而退。1616年1月，雅各布·勒梅尔和威廉·斯豪滕绕过合恩角（角名得自他们的船「霍伦号」），走出一条高纬度航路，后来的船只大多宁可走这里，也不走狭窄的海峡。真正在岛上住过的第一批欧洲人是海难者：1765年「至圣受孕号」失事后，193名幸存者在安慰港花三个月造出一艘船，驾船回到布宜诺斯艾利斯。1769年，詹姆斯·库克测绘东北海岸，在好运湾补给木水时，博物学家约瑟夫·班克斯随他一同与豪什人接触。直到1821年，没有任何欧洲强国在岛上建起永久城镇。

en:
Kawésqar country runs from the Gulf of Penas south to the Strait of Magellan, a wet succession of islands, channels, fjords and shores along the Brunswick Peninsula. Wellington, Santa Inés and Desolación islands lie along the western approach to the strait, with no towns, roads or fixed fields. The families called themselves Kawésqar, their word for a person; Alacaluf was a later name taken from Yahgan. In 1444 they travelled by canoe, gathered shellfish, hunted seals and sea lions, and coated themselves in sea-lion oil under close capes against the rain and cold.

Magellan's ships entered the strait in 1520, yet the first recorded sighting of people likely to be Kawésqar came on 22 April 1526, when García Jofre de Loaísa's Spanish expedition passed the western end of the passage. The strait let ships sail between the Atlantic and Pacific, while the network of side channels stayed in indigenous hands. From the late eighteenth century, British and North American whalers and sealers entered those waters more often. They traded with canoe camps and sometimes abducted people; introduced diseases did greater damage. In 1821 most side channels were still travelled mainly by Kawésqar canoes.
zh:
卡韦斯卡尔之地北起佩尼亚斯湾，南至麦哲伦海峡，由湿润的岛屿、水道、峡湾和不伦瑞克半岛沿岸连成一片。惠灵顿岛、圣伊内斯岛和德索拉西翁岛位于海峡西端外海，岛上没有城镇、道路或固定农田。各家族自称卡韦斯卡尔，这个词在他们的语言中指「人」；「阿拉卡卢夫」是后来从雅甘语借来的他称。1444年，他们乘独木舟迁徙，采集贝类，捕猎海豹和海狮，并在贴身斗篷外涂抹海狮油脂，抵挡雨水和寒冷。

麦哲伦的船只1520年驶入海峡，但首次有记录望见可能是卡韦斯卡尔人的居民，是1526年4月22日加西亚·霍弗雷·德·洛艾萨的西班牙探险队经过海峡西端时。这条航路让船只能够往来大西洋与太平洋，旁侧水道组成的水网则仍掌握在原住民手中。18世纪末起，英国和北美捕鲸船、猎海豹船更频繁地进入这些海域。他们和独木舟营地贸易，有时掳走居民；外来疾病造成的破坏更大。1821年，多数旁侧水道里往来的仍主要是卡韦斯卡尔人的独木舟。

en:
Huillimapu, the great southern land of the Huilliche, runs from the Bueno River country toward Reloncaví Sound and the sea approaches to Chiloé. In 1444 Cunco groups held the rainy coast and wooded foothills, while Huilliche communities on the eastern flatlands grew potatoes, maize, quinoa and beans. Rivers, sea inlets and forest trails linked their fishing grounds and fields, and local chiefs answered to no outside governor.

García Hurtado de Mendoza founded San Mateo de Osorno in 1558, on low ground between the Rahue and Damas rivers. Alonso de Ercilla, later author of La Araucana, marched in the same expedition. Gold washings, farms and trade with Chile and Peru made Osorno a rich southern town, and an earthquake damaged it in 1575. After Pelantaro's Mapuche force ambushed and killed Governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola at Curalaba in 1598, the southern towns rose against Spanish rule. Huilliche fighters besieged Osorno and destroyed it in 1604, and most surviving settlers withdrew to Chiloé. For nearly two centuries the closed country gave rise to Spanish stories of a lost City of the Caesars. Military pressure and diplomacy reopened the route under Governor Ambrosio O'Higgins; the 1793 Parliament of Las Canoas accepted incorporation into the Spanish Empire and allowed Osorno to be rebuilt, with Fort Reina Luisa on the Rahue guarding the settlement.
zh:
维利马普是维利切人的南方大地，范围从布埃诺河流域延伸到雷隆卡维湾和通往奇洛埃的海路。1444年，库恩科诸部占据多雨海岸与林木山麓，东部平原上的维利切社群种植马铃薯、玉米、藜麦和豆类。河流、海湾和林道连接渔场与农田，各部首领不受外来总督管辖。

1558年，加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨在拉韦河与达马斯河之间的低地建立圣马特奥·德·奥索尔诺；后来写成《阿劳卡纳》的阿隆索·德·埃尔西利亚也随军南下。淘金、农田和同智利、秘鲁的贸易使奥索尔诺成为富庶的南方城镇，1575年地震又使它严重受损。1598年，佩兰塔罗率领的马普切军队在库拉拉巴设伏，击杀总督马丁·加西亚·奥涅斯·德·洛约拉，南方诸城随即起兵。维利切战士围困奥索尔诺，1604年将其摧毁，幸存的西班牙居民大多退往奇洛埃。此后近两百年，西班牙人从这片封闭土地传出失落的恺撒之城的故事。安布罗西奥·奥希金斯任内，军事压力与谈判重新打开道路；1793年拉斯卡诺阿斯议会接受并入西班牙帝国并允许重建奥索尔诺，拉韦河畔的雷娜·路易莎堡护卫这座新城。

en:
Pehuenmapu is the high Andean country of the Pehuenche, the 'people of the pewen'. The pewen is the monkey-puzzle tree whose pine nuts were their staple food on slopes above about a thousand metres. On the eastern side of the Andes their country ran from the Diamante River south to Lake Aluminé; the Pehuenche Pass and nearby trails crossed the cordillera to Chile. In 1444 families wintered in the lower valleys and climbed to the high woods in summer, gathering pine nuts between March and May and hunting guanaco. They kept no permanent towns, and local chiefs controlled the mountain routes independently.

Jerónimo de Bibar recorded Pehuenche groups in 1550, and the colonial wars later showed the value of their passes. In 1657 mountain raiders crossed the Pehuenche Pass to estancias in Maule and Cuyo, reaching southern Mendoza without going through Concepción. Pehuenche and Huilliche fighters sacked San Luis in 1712, and Pehuenche bands joined Cangapol's allied raid of 1740, which crossed the Luján district and reached Magdalena near the Río de la Plata. The rising led by Lebián and Pilmigerenantu in 1769 brought malones to Mendoza. A displaced band settled by the Malargüe River the next year and attacked Fort San Carlos, newly built to hold the southern Mendoza frontier. The 1771 Parliament of Negrete ended the fighting on the Chilean side, while the eastern valleys remained under indigenous chiefs. By then Mapudungun had become the common Pehuenche language.
zh:
佩温马普是佩温切人的安第斯高山领地。族名来自马普敦贡语中的「佩温」，也就是在千米以上山坡成林的智利南洋杉，松子是他们的主食。东坡领地北起迪亚曼特河，南至阿卢米内湖；佩温切山口和邻近小路越过山脉，通往智利坡地。1444年，各家族冬季住在低谷，夏季登到高处，在3月至5月采集松子、猎取原驼。这里没有常设城镇，各酋长分别掌握山路。

1550年，赫罗尼莫·德·比瓦尔已记录下佩温切诸部；殖民地时期的战事后来显出这些山口的价值。1657年，山地战士经佩温切山口袭击马乌莱和库约的牧场，不必经过康塞普西翁就能抵达门多萨南部。1712年，佩温切人和维利切人洗劫圣路易斯；1740年，他们又加入坎加波尔的联合突袭，越过卢洪一带，打到拉普拉塔河畔的马格达莱纳。1769年，莱维安和皮尔米赫雷南图领导大起事，战火烧到门多萨。次年，一支被逐出故地的群体在马拉圭河畔落脚，并攻打为巩固门多萨南境而新建的圣卡洛斯堡。1771年的内格雷特议会结束了智利一侧的战事，东坡山谷仍由原住民首领掌握。到这时，马普敦贡语已是佩温切人的常用语言。

en:
Carmen covers the lower reaches of the Río Negro, where the river crosses dry steppe to reach the Atlantic. In 1444 its banks and crossings were Chechehet country. This nomadic Het group moved between the Colorado and Negro rivers after guanaco, rhea and deer, used boleadoras and gathered wild seeds. Camps stood by fresh water close enough to meet Puelche and Tehuelche bands; no Spanish fort guarded the river mouth.

The Spanish pushed this far south as a planned outpost, not as a large city. On 22 April 1779 Francisco de Viedma y Narváez founded the Establecimiento del Río Negro on the south bank, with a fort and colonists sent from Spain. A flood on 13 July swept away the first huts, and the survivors crossed to the left bank at Carmen de Patagones. When ships began arriving in October, many Galician colonists found no promised houses and dug cave dwellings into the barranca. A small garrison, subsistence farms and trade with native peoples kept the isolated post alive, since ships were its only link with Buenos Aires. In April 1812 royalist prisoners seized the fort and held it for Montevideo until 23 December 1814, when it passed to the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata.
zh:
卡门位于内格罗河下游，河水穿过干旱草原注入大西洋。1444年，河岸和渡口是切切赫特人的土地。这个海特人游牧群体在科罗拉多河与内格罗河之间追踪原驼、美洲鸵和鹿，使用投石索并采集野生种子。营地设在淡水旁，也足以同普埃尔切、特维尔切游群往来；河口当时没有西班牙堡垒。

西班牙人把势力推到这么南的地方，为的是一座计划中的边防据点，而不是大城市。1779年4月22日，弗朗西斯科·德·别德马-纳瓦埃斯在河南岸建立「内格罗河定居点」，配有一座堡垒和从西班牙送来的移民。7月13日洪水冲走最初的棚屋，幸存者迁到左岸的卡门-德帕塔戈内斯。10月船只陆续抵达时，许多加利西亚移民未见承诺的住房，只在崖壁里挖出洞屋栖身。小驻军、自给农庄和同原住民的贸易维持着这个孤立据点，海路则是它与布宜诺斯艾利斯之间唯一的联系。1812年4月，保王派囚犯夺取堡垒，替蒙得维的亚据守，到1814年12月23日转入拉普拉塔联合省手中。

en:
Picunmapu was the central Chilean country of the Picunches, the Mapudungun-speaking 'people of the north.' Their hamlets and irrigated fields spread through the transverse valleys from the Aconcagua to the Biobío: they worked stone and metal, made pottery and answered to their own lonkos. The strongest of the southern groups, called Promaucaes by the Incas, held the rich land between the Maipo and the Maule. In 1444 the Inca frontier stopped around the Choapa valley, and these villages took no orders from Cuzco.

The Inca push came late in the fifteenth century under Túpac Inca Yupanqui. Garcilaso de la Vega's chronicle describes a three-day battle at the Maule in which the Promaucaes and their allies checked the Inca army, which never campaigned farther south; the hilltop Pucará La Muralla remained its southernmost known outpost. Pedro de Valdivia's Spaniards ran into the same kind of resistance after founding Santiago, holding three years of campaigning to little. In 1544 the Promaucaes burned their own villages and fields and withdrew toward the Maule, where the southern groups shut them out; Spanish grain estates took over their ditches and terraces, and encomienda labor and resettlement in pueblos de indios wore the Picunche communities down. One man carried the war back to the Spanish nevertheless: Lautaro, a Mapuche boy taken young and put to work in Valdivia's own household as groom and stableman, learned cavalry and Spanish tactics there, escaped and was chosen toqui. His warriors killed Valdivia at Tucapel in 1553, and Promaucae bands from these valleys joined his march on Santiago the following year. The Spanish surprised his camp at Peteroa in 1557 and killed him there.
zh:
皮昆马普是智利中部皮昆切人的土地，「皮昆切」在马普切语中意为「北方的人」。他们的村落和灌溉农田散布在阿空加瓜河至比奥比奥河之间的横断山谷里，加工石器和金属，制作陶器，各村落听从自己的酋长。南方最强的一支居于马伊波河与马乌莱河之间的沃土上，印加人称他们为普罗马乌卡人。1444年，印加疆界止于乔阿帕河谷一带，这些村落不听命于库斯科。

印加人的推进在15世纪后期到来，时当图帕克·印卡·尤潘基在位。史家加西拉索·德·拉·维加记下了马乌莱河畔一场持续三日的会战：普罗马乌卡人与盟军挡住印加大军，后者再未向南用兵，山顶的拉穆拉亚堡是其已知最南的前哨。佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚建立圣地亚哥之后，西班牙人也撞上同样的抵抗，三年征讨收效甚微。1544年，普罗马乌卡人焚毁自己的村庄和田地，向马乌莱河方向南撤，却被南方诸部拒之门外；西班牙人的谷物庄园接管了他们的沟渠和梯田，委托监护制的劳役和迁入印第安人村镇又逐步拆散了皮昆切社区。但有一个人把战争带回了西班牙人面前：劳塔罗少年时被掳，在巴尔迪维亚本人家中做马夫和饲马人，在那里学会骑兵战术和西班牙人的战法，逃走后被推为军事领袖。1553年，他的战士在图卡佩尔杀死巴尔迪维亚；次年，这些河谷的普罗马乌卡队伍加入他进军圣地亚哥的行列。1557年，西班牙人突袭他在佩特罗阿的营地，将他杀死。

en:
Angoche occupies a cluster of low islands set in mangrove creeks where the African coast bends toward Mozambique. Muslim merchants had lived and traded there since the late first millennium, and by 1444 the town was the southernmost of the Swahili sister-cities that looked to Kilwa, a free emporium beyond the reach of any European power. Dhows took aboard ivory, ambergris and gold brought from the Zambezi fairs and the lands of the Mwenemutapa, and the straw mats and hats woven by its craftsmen were bought all along the shore. The mainland behind the islands belonged to the Makua, whose caravans fed its market.

A tradition recorded at Angoche tells how the sultanate began. Hassani, a refugee from Kilwa, died while visiting Mussa on Mozambique Island and was buried nearby; when Mussa came to the grave he judged Angoche a finer site than Quelimane and installed Hassani's son Xosa as its first sultan, around 1485. Vasco da Gama sighted the islands in 1498, and early in the next century Duarte Barbosa still listed the town among the vassals of Kilwa. The Portuguese required every coastal dhow to buy their trading license, but Angoche went on dealing without one, until Zambezi factories and Maravi tolls wore it down. By the end of the 1500s the island kept a Portuguese factor and a priest for its fifteen hundred people; the priest was murdered in 1627, and the trade that remained was leased in 1709 to an Indian merchant. When Francisco Moraes Pereira visited in 1752, the sultan had just been restored with Portuguese help after a raid by an ex-slave and his bandits, and the town had been rebuilt on a new site after quarrels with the Makua. Mascarene plantation demand then swelled the traffic in ivory and slaves, and by 1821 Angoche was again an independent emporium, growing rich outside any European system.
zh:
安戈谢坐落在非洲海岸折向莫桑比克处的一组低矮岛群上，四周环着红树林水道。穆斯林商人自公元第一个千年晚期便在此居住贸易；1444年时，它是拥戴基尔瓦的斯瓦希里姊妹诸城最南端的一座，也是欧洲势力够不着的自由商港。独桅帆船在这里装上象牙、龙涎香和来自赞比西集市、姆韦尼·马塔帕之地的黄金，本地工匠编织的草席和草帽沿岸都有人买。岛后的大陆属于马库阿人，他们的商队为岛上市场供货。

安戈谢当地记下的口传，讲了苏丹国的由来：基尔瓦流亡者哈萨尼到莫桑比克岛拜访穆萨时死在那里，葬在附近；穆萨到墓前看过后，认定安戈谢是比克利马内更好的港址，便于1485年前后立哈萨尼之子肖萨为第一代苏丹。1498年达·伽马看到了这片岛群；16世纪初，杜阿尔特·巴尔博萨仍把这座城列为基尔瓦的附庸。葡萄牙人强迫沿海每艘独桅帆船购买通商许可，安戈谢却无照经商，直到赞比西商站的兴起和马拉维人的抽税把它拖垮。到16世纪末，岛上为一千五百名居民驻有葡萄牙商馆代表和一名神父；神父于1627年被杀，残余的贸易在1709年包租给一名印度商人。1752年弗朗西斯科·莫赖斯·佩雷拉到访时，苏丹刚在葡萄牙帮助下从一名叛奴匪帮的洗劫后复国，城镇也在与马库阿人交恶后放弃旧址、另择新址重建。此后马斯克林种植园的需求使象牙和奴隶贸易膨胀，到1821年，安戈谢再度成为一座独立商港，在任何欧洲体制之外发财致富。

en:
The well-watered coastal hills of northern Natal fall from the Nkandla heights toward the Indian Ocean. For centuries before 1444 Nguni cattle-herders and growers of sorghum and millet lived there in scattered homesteads, iron smiths worked the forges of the chiefs, and ivory already moved north along the coast to the trading stations on Delagoa Bay. Among the northern Nguni clans were the Mthethwa, 'the rulers'.

The man who raised them high was Dingiswayo, born Godongwana, a Mthethwa prince condemned by his father King Jobe; he escaped the executioners and spent years in exile before coming back to seize the kingship. He built a paramountcy of some thirty northern Nguni chiefdoms, drawing neighbours in by treaty and marriage as often as by war. In exile he had learned from the Tembe chiefs of Delagoa Bay how much a port could earn, and as king he sent ivory north to buy Portuguese firearms, the first Nguni ruler to arm his regiments that way. Young men were enrolled in age-set regiments that answered to him rather than to the chiefs of their home villages.

One of his commanders was Shaka, the rejected son of Senzangakhona, chief of the small Zulu clan, who had grown up under Dingiswayo's protection. When the Zulu joined the confederacy around 1811 Shaka became the paramount's favoured general, and when Zwide of the Ndwandwe captured and killed Dingiswayo in 1817 the Mthethwa regiments went over to his former pupil. Shaka kept the age-set system but drilled the regiments into a disciplined standing army, and the wars of his reign drove the upheaval later called the Mfecane across southern Africa. In 1818 he held Gqokli Hill against Zwide, and in 1820 he broke the Ndwandwe alliance on the Mhlatuze River; the old Mthethwa hills became the centre of the Zulu kingdom that ran from the Pongola to the Tugela.
zh:
纳塔尔北部水草丰美的滨海丘陵，从恩卡德拉高地斜斜伸向印度洋。1444年之前数百年，恩古尼牧人和种植高粱、谷子的农人便在这里的分散村落中生活，铁匠在首领的炉前打铁，象牙沿海岸北运到德拉戈阿湾的贸易站。族名意为「统治者」的姆泰特瓦人，便是北部恩古尼诸部之一。

把姆泰特瓦带上强盛之路的是丁吉斯瓦约。他本名戈东瓦纳，是姆泰特瓦王子，被父王约贝论死，却从刽子手手中逃脱，流亡多年后归国夺位。他以盟约、联姻与战争并用，把约三十个北部恩古尼部族结成一个盟主政权。流亡期间，他从德拉戈阿湾的滕贝首领那里看清了港口贸易之利，即位后便用象牙北去换取葡萄牙火器，是第一个这样武装兵团的恩古尼统治者。他把青年按年龄编入兵团，士兵听命于他本人，而不是出身村落的首领。

他麾下有一员年轻将领恰卡。恰卡是弱小祖鲁部族首领辛赞格科纳不被承认的儿子，在丁吉斯瓦约庇护下长大。约1811年祖鲁部加入联盟，恰卡成为盟主最倚重的将领；1817年恩德旺堆首领兹维德俘杀丁吉斯瓦约，姆泰特瓦的兵团转而听命于这位旧日主君的门生。恰卡保留年龄兵团的旧制，却把他们操练成纪律严明的常备军，他在位时的连年大战把后世称为姆费卡内的大动荡推向整个南部非洲。1818年，恰卡在戈克利山挡住兹维德，1820年又在姆拉图泽河畔粉碎恩德旺堆联盟；旧日的姆泰特瓦丘陵就此成为祖鲁王国的中心，国境北起蓬戈拉河，南抵图盖拉河。

en:
Chaco Austral is the southern sweep of the Gran Chaco, dry thorn forest and palm savanna crossed by the Salado, Dulce and Bermejo. In 1444 its inland camps belonged to Guaycuru-speaking nations, the Toba and Mocoví among them, who hunted with bows, fished, gathered honey and carob and moved with the seasons. On the south-western floodplains the Tonocoté lived in palisaded villages, watering maize, quinoa, beans and squash from the annual floods, herding llamas and rheas and burying their dead in large urns. An Inca expedition sent by Túpac Yupanqui could not fight its way through the thorn woods.

The first European to cross the country was the Portuguese castaway Alejo García, who in 1524 marched west with a Guaraní war band, reached the Inca frontier beyond the Chaco and came back with silver before being killed on the Paraguay; his haul started the legend of the Sierra de la Plata, and Cabot and Ayolas followed on the same rumour. Juan de Ayolas crossed the thickets on that quest and was killed with all his men by the Payagua in 1538. Spanish settlement clung to the south-western rivers. Francisco de Aguirre refounded the short-lived El Barco as Santiago del Estero in 1553, the oldest Spanish town in Argentina; parties sent from it founded Tucumán, Córdoba, Salta and the other cities of the north-west, earning it the name Mother of Cities. Farther east, Concepción, founded in 1585, was abandoned under attack in 1632, and the Jesuit mission of San Fernando del Río Negro failed as well. In 1821 the Toba, Wichí, Mocoví and the other mounted nations still held the whole interior.
zh:
南查科是大查科向南展开的部分，干旱刺林与棕榈草原相连，萨拉多河、杜尔塞河和贝尔梅霍河穿行其间。1444年，内陆的营地属于托巴人、莫科维人等瓜伊库鲁语族群，他们用弓狩猎、捕鱼，采集蜂蜜和角豆，随季节迁移。西南河泛地上，托诺科特人住在有栅栏的村落里，借每年泛水浇灌玉米、藜麦、菜豆和南瓜，牧养羊驼和美洲鸵，死后用大瓮安葬。图帕克·尤潘基派出的印加远征军没能穿过这片密林。

第一个穿越大查科的欧洲人是葡萄牙沉船幸存者阿莱霍·加西亚：1524年，他随一支瓜拉尼武装西行，穿过查科抵达印加边境，带着银器返回，却在巴拉圭河畔被杀；他带回的银子引出「银山」传说，卡博特和阿约拉斯后来都是追着这个传说而来。胡安·德·阿约拉斯为寻路穿过密林，1538年和全队一起被帕亚瓜人杀死。西班牙人的定居点只在西南河畔站住脚：弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷在短命的埃尔巴科旧址上于1553年改建圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗，这是阿根廷境内最古老的西班牙城镇；远征队从这里出发接连建立图库曼、科尔多瓦、萨尔塔等西北诸城，它也因此被称作「诸城之母」。更东面，1585年建立的康塞普西翁在1632年的进攻中废弃，圣费尔南多-德尔里奥内格罗的耶稣会传教区也没能维持。到1821年，托巴人、维奇人、莫科维人等已掌握马匹的族群仍据有整个内陆。

en:
The mountain valleys of Catamarca, Quimivil, Hualfín and Andalgalá among them, lie between the high puna and the dry plains that fall away toward the Chaco, greened by snowmelt streams. In 1444 they belonged to rival Pazioca chiefdoms, the peoples the Spanish later called Diaguitas: Capayanes in the southern valleys, Olongastas in the southeast, Cunza-speaking Atacameño communities in the high northwest. Irrigated maize fields, llama herds and stone villages lay below hilltop strongholds, and no outside governor yet ruled the valleys. The name Catamarca is Quechua for a fortress on a slope, and it arrived with the Incas. In the 1470s Túpac Inca Yupanqui's armies drew the western valleys into Qullasuyu and built El Shincal de Quimivil into a provincial centre on the Inca road over the San Francisco Pass to Chile; the Pucará de Aconquija was among the largest forts on the empire's southern edge.

Diego de Almagro's men crossed the San Francisco Pass in 1536. The first Spanish town held only briefly: in June 1558 Juan Pérez de Zurita founded Londres de la Nueva Inglaterra in the Quimivil valley, named for Mary Tudor, the English wife of Philip II. The town was moved, renamed and abandoned more than once, while Chile and the new Peru-based Governorate of Tucumán disputed its jurisdiction. In the great Calchaquí rising of 1630 the cacique Juan Chalimín led the warriors who destroyed it, and the refounded settlement kept coming under attack. Only in 1683 did Fernando de Mendoza y Mate de Luna establish a lasting town, San Fernando del Valle de Catamarca, in the central valley on the track between Santiago del Estero, Tucumán and La Rioja. The image of Our Lady of the Valley, venerated earlier at nearby Valle Viejo, was placed in the town's new church in the 1690s and drew pilgrims from across the northwest. Catamarca later passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata and the intendency at Salta, and in 1821 its council proclaimed provincial autonomy and chose Nicolás Avellaneda y Tula as first governor.
zh:
卡塔马卡的山谷以基米维尔、瓦尔芬和安达加拉为代表，夹在西北的普纳高地与东南渐入查科的干旱平原之间，靠融雪溪流成为绿野。1444年，这些谷地分属帕西奥卡人互相敌对的酋邦，西班牙人后来把他们统称迪亚吉塔人：卡帕扬人在南部谷地，奥隆加斯塔人在东南，讲库恩萨语的阿塔卡马人社群在西北高地。灌溉玉米地、大羊驼群和石砌村寨下方即是山顶堡垒，此时还没有外来的总督统治这些谷地。卡塔马卡这个名字出自克丘亚语，意为山坡上的堡垒，是随印加人一起来的。1470年代，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的军队把西部谷地并入科利亚苏尤，把基米维尔的辛卡尔（Shincal）建成印加道路上的行省中心，这条道路越过圣弗朗西斯科山口通往智利；阿孔基哈堡则是帝国南境最大的要塞之一。

1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的部下越过圣弗朗西斯科山口。第一个西班牙城镇只维持了很短时间：1558年6月，胡安·佩雷斯·德·苏里塔在基米维尔谷建立新英格兰的伦敦镇，名字取自费利佩二世的英格兰妻子玛丽·都铎。城镇几经迁移、改名和废弃，智利与以秘鲁为靠山的新设图库曼督辖区又争夺它的管辖权。1630年卡尔查基人大起义，酋长胡安·查利明率部摧毁此城，重建后的城镇仍不断遭袭。直到1683年，费尔南多·德·门多萨·伊·马特·德·卢纳才在中央谷地建起持久的圣费尔南多-德尔巴列-德卡塔马卡，正处在圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗、图库曼和拉里奥贾之间的通道上。山谷圣母像此前已在附近的旧谷（Valle Viejo）受拜，1690年代迎入新城的教堂，吸引阿根廷西北各地的朝圣者前来。卡塔马卡后来划入拉普拉塔总督辖区，归萨尔塔监政区管辖；1821年，市议会宣布省自治，选出尼古拉斯·阿韦利亚内达·伊·图拉为首任省长。

en:
The Copiapó River runs through a long oasis in the Atacama Desert. Its watered meadows gave the local name Copayapu, usually explained as green pasture or turquoise sowing land. In 1444 Copayapu farmers and herders lived in compact villages on the river banks and kept watch from hilltop pucaras. They worked copper, shaped black-on-red pottery painted with stylized llamas, and exchanged river and highland goods for fish and shellfish brought from the Pacific. Cuzco's armies and roads had not yet reached the valley.

The Incas annexed Copayapu around 1470 and moved mitma families from the Elqui and Huasco valleys into the middle and upper basin. Forts, tambos, shrines and mining posts then followed the Inca road across the province. At Viña del Cerro, Diaguita and Inca metalworkers smelted copper from about 1470 until the Spanish arrival; the site may also have been used for ceremonies and solar observation. By the time Pedro de Valdivia entered the valley, two lords, Aldequin and Gualenica, ruled its lower and upper districts under a dual chieftaincy. Diego de Almagro had first crossed the Andes by the Comecaballos pass and reached Copiapó on 21 March 1536. Valdivia arrived on 26 October 1540, heard Mass, took possession for the Spanish crown, and named the place the Valley of Possession. A Spanish town nevertheless came late: José Manso de Velasco formally founded San Francisco de la Selva de Copiapó only on 8 December 1744.
zh:
科皮亚波河流经阿塔卡马沙漠中的一带狭长绿洲，水草丰美的河漫滩赋予当地「科帕亚普」之名，通常解释为绿色牧地或绿松石播种地。1444年，科帕亚普农牧民在河畔聚居成村，并在山巅堡垒设防。他们炼铜，制作绘有风格化羊驼纹的黑彩红陶，还用河谷和高原物产交换太平洋沿岸带来的鱼、贝。库斯科的军队和大道此时尚未进入河谷。

约1470年，印加吞并科帕亚普，把来自埃尔基河谷和瓦斯科河谷的米蒂马家庭迁到流域中上游，堡垒、坦博驿站、神庙和采矿点也随印加道路分布到这一带。约1470年至西班牙人到来前，迪亚吉塔工匠和印加工匠在比尼亚德尔塞罗冶炼铜；研究也认为，这里可能承担过祭祀和太阳观测功能。佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚进入河谷时，阿尔德金和瓜莱尼卡两名首领正按双头首领制分管下游与上游。此前，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗已取道科梅卡瓦约斯山口越过安第斯山，于1536年3月21日抵达科皮亚波。1540年10月26日，巴尔迪维亚到达此地，举行弥撒并代表西班牙王室宣布占有，将其命名为「领有谷」。但西班牙人的城镇出现得很晚：何塞·曼索·德·贝拉斯科直到1744年12月8日才正式建立圣弗朗西斯科·德拉塞尔瓦·德·科皮亚波。

en:
Iquique takes its Aymara name Iki Iki, a place of rest or dreams. In 1444 the shore below the rainless Tarapaca desert was a Camanchaco landing place rather than a town; Spaniards later called these fishermen Changos. They put to sea on rafts made of sea-lion hides, gathered shellfish, salted fish and scraped guano from the old islet by the beach. A short way inland, Colla farmers used the ravines and oases to grow crops and trade dried fish, maize, cloth and highland goods with Aymara lordships. The lords of Chucuito had strong ties to that network before Inca armies reached Tarapaca.

After the Inca annexation, Cerro Esmeralda became the site of a capacocha sacrifice. Excavations found two girls, one about eighteen and the other nine or ten, with gold and silver bracelets, Spondylus shell, fine textiles, pottery, gourds and snuff tablets; the burials date from 1475 to 1499. Under the Viceroyalty of Peru, the encomiendas of San Lorenzo de Tarapaca and Pica drew indigenous labour into the colonial economy, while Iquique itself stayed a small guano and fish landing at El Colorado. The eighteenth-century silver mines of Huantajaya and Santa Rosa brought traffic to the province, but most metal went overland to Arica. San Lorenzo became the jurisdiction's seat in 1768, and a warehouse at Iquique became a customs post in 1788. Local legend says two indigenous men discovered nitrate earth when their campfire set the caliche alight; the priest of Camina tested the samples and watched the residue make plants grow unusually fast. Documents of 1811 already record the first saltpetre shipments, and the little port was still part of southern Peru when independence was proclaimed on 28 July 1821.
zh:
伊基克的艾马拉语原名「伊基伊基」，意为休息或入梦之地。1444年，这片紧邻无雨塔拉帕卡沙漠的海岸还不是城镇，只是卡曼查科人的登陆点；西班牙人后来把这些渔民称为昌戈人。他们驾海狮皮皮筏出海，采集贝类、腌制鱼干，也在海滩旁的旧小岛挖取鸟粪。稍往内陆，科利亚农人利用沟谷和绿洲种植，再把鱼干、玉米、织物和高原货物同艾马拉诸领主交易。印加军队抵达塔拉帕卡之前，丘基托的领主已同这条交换网络关系密切。

印加吞并后，埃斯梅拉达山成为卡帕科查祭祀地。发掘者在山上发现两名少女遗骨，一名约十八岁，另一名九到十岁，随葬金镯、银镯、海菊蛤、精美织物、陶器、葫芦和嗅药板；墓葬测年为1475年至1499年。秘鲁总督辖区时期，塔拉帕卡的圣洛伦索和皮卡两个委托监护辖区把原住民劳力纳入殖民经济，伊基克本身则长期只是埃尔科罗拉多装运鸟粪和鱼货的小码头。18世纪万塔哈亚和圣罗莎银矿给这一省带来人流，但多数白银仍经陆路运往阿里卡。1768年，圣洛伦索成为治所；1788年，伊基克的一座仓库被改成海关站。当地相传，两名原住民男子生起营火时点燃了含硝的钙积土层，卡米尼亚的神父检验样本，又发现残余物让植物长得异常快，硝土才被辨认出来。1811年的文献已经记载首批硝石外运；1821年7月28日秘鲁宣布独立时，这座小港仍是秘鲁南部的一部分。

en:
Jujuy is a fertile high valley where the Xibi Xibi joins the Río Grande, at the southern mouth of the 155-kilometre Humahuaca canyon, the road from the plains up to the Altiplano. The Omaguaca studded that canyon with pucarás; the largest, the Pucará de Tilcara, held more than two thousand inhabitants and commanded a long stretch of the road from a hill above Tilcara. In 1444 this was Diaguita country, where the Jujuí and Omaguaca herders, kin to the Calchaquí of the western mountains, grew maize on the flats, drove llama trains up the canyon and answered raiders from their fortresses; Inca armies took the canyon only late in the century under Túpac Yupanqui, garrisoning the pucarás to guard nearby silver and copper mines. Spaniards met them early: in late 1535 a foraging party of Almagro's Chile expedition was killed here and eighty men had to storm a local fortress.

Two earlier Spanish towns burned, Nieva in the cacique Juan Calchaquí's rising of 1563, and San Francisco seven months after it was planted in 1575. On 19 April 1593, the Monday after Easter, Francisco de Argañaraz y Murguía founded San Salvador de Velazco with forty soldiers, and the town grew as the staging post on the mule road from Tucumán to the silver mines of Potosí. It belonged to the Viceroyalty of Peru until 1776, when it passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and on 3 March 1781 Gregorio de Zegada beat off a Chaco war party in the Zapla hills.

From 1810 Jujuy stood on the main front of the independence war. Manuel Belgrano reached it on 19 May 1812 to take over a demoralised Northern Army, outnumbered two to one by Pío Tristán's royalists advancing down the Humahuaca road. Instead of fighting, he ordered the district stripped: at dawn on 23 August 1812 the whole population left with him for Tucumán, a march of about 250 kilometres, driving their cattle ahead while houses, crops and even iron goods were burned so that the royalists found nothing. The scorched-earth march is remembered as the Jujuy Exodus.
zh:
胡胡伊是希比希比河汇入格兰德河处的肥沃高谷，位于全长155公里的乌马瓦卡峡谷南口，这条峡谷是从平原登上高原的道路。奥马瓦卡人在峡谷中遍筑普卡拉堡垒，其中最大的蒂尔卡拉普卡拉踞守蒂尔卡拉旁的山丘，一间间小石屋里住有两千多人，俯瞰着脚下长长一段峡路。1444年时这里是迪亚吉塔人的土地：河谷中的胡胡伊人与奥马瓦卡牧人和西山的查尔查奇人同源，他们在滩地上种玉米，沿峡谷驱赶驼队，遇有袭扰便据堡垒应战；直到该世纪末，图帕克·尤潘基麾下的印加大军才拿下峡谷，并把这些普卡拉充作守卫附近银矿、铜矿的前哨。西班牙人很早就与他们交手：1535年末，阿尔马格罗智利远征队的一支搜粮小队在此被杀，一支八十人的部队强攻才夺下当地一座堡垒。

西班牙人早先的两处城镇都付之一炬：涅瓦城在1563年酋长胡安·查尔查奇领导的起义中被毁，1575年建立的圣弗朗西斯科城仅七个月后便被烧光。1593年4月19日，即复活节后的星期一，弗朗西斯科·德·阿加尼亚拉斯·伊·穆尔吉亚率四十名士兵建成圣萨尔瓦多·德·贝拉斯科，这座城镇作为从图库曼通往波托西银矿的骡马道补给驿站兴盛起来。1776年之前它隶属秘鲁总督辖区，此后划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区；1781年3月3日，格雷戈里奥·德·塞加达在萨普拉丘陵击退一支来自查科的部落武装。

1810年起，胡胡伊一直处在独立战争的最前线。1812年5月19日，曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺抵达这里，接掌士气低落的北方军，面对沿乌马瓦卡峡路南下、兵力两倍于己的皮奥·特里斯坦所部保王军。他没有选择迎战，而是下令坚壁清野：1812年8月23日黎明，全城居民赶着牲畜随他撤向图库曼，走完约250公里的路程，房屋、存粮连同铁器一概烧毁，不给保王军留下任何东西。这场行军史称「胡胡伊大出走」。

en:
Potosí is a cold Charca basin over 4,000 metres up in the Andes, beneath Sumaq Urqu, the cone later called Cerro Rico. Aymara farmers and llama herders knew its silver veins but held the peak to be a sacred huaca and left the metal in the rock. A legend recorded by the chronicler Arzáns says that when miners sent by Huayna Capac opened a vein, a thunderous voice told them in Quechua that the silver was reserved for men who would come from across the sea; the Inca left the hill, renamed Potojsi, 'it thunders'. In 1444 there was no city here, only the grazing grounds, shrines and small settlements of the Charca world.

In 1545 an indigenous herder named Diego Huallpa, chasing a runaway llama, lit a fire on the mountain for the night; the flames showed a white thread of pure silver, and Captain Juan de Villarroel claimed the hill that April. The rush built the Villa Imperial de Potosí. A census under Viceroy Francisco de Toledo counted 120,000 people in 1573, and by 1625 the city held about 160,000, more than Seville and second only to London. 'Worth a Potosí' entered Spanish for a great fortune, and Cervantes named its mines in Don Quixote. The royal mint struck the pieces of eight that llama and mule trains carried to the Pacific and across Panama to the treasure fleets; other loads went east to Buenos Aires or sailed from Acapulco to Manila. Between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries about four-fifths of all silver mined on earth came from this one mountain.

The metal was dug by Andean hands: Toledo's mita conscripted about 13,000 men a year, one in seven adult men from a district running from Quito to Buenos Aires, to carry 100 to 300 pounds of ore up shaft ladders; mercury, cold and falls killed many. During the independence war Potosí changed hands again and again, and when Manuel Belgrano retreated he ordered the Casa de la Moneda blown up; townspeople crept in and cut the fuse. The mines and mint were still being fought over in 1821.
zh:
波托西是查卡人寒冷的高原盆地，地处安第斯山海拔四千多米处，坐落在克丘亚语称作苏马克乌尔库的锥形山峰下，西班牙人后来称这座山为里科山。说艾马拉语的农民和骆马牧民早知山中多银，却把峰顶奉为神圣的瓦卡，任由银子留在岩中。编年史家阿尔桑斯记下一则传说：瓦伊纳·卡帕克派去的矿工刚凿开矿脉，便听到雷鸣般的声音用克丘亚语告诉他们，这些银子是留给从大海彼岸来的人的；印加人弃山而去，将山改名为「波托赫西」，意为「打雷了」。1444年时这里还没有城市，只有查卡世界的牧场、神殿和零星聚落。

1545年，印第安牧人迭戈·瓦尔帕追赶一头走失的骆马，夜间在山上生火取暖，火光照出一缕纯白的银线；同年4月，胡安·德·比利亚罗埃尔上尉占下此山。蜂拥而来的淘银者建起波托西皇家城。1573年托莱多总督的人口普查录得12万人，到1625年全城约有16万人，多于塞维利亚，仅次于伦敦。「值一个波托西」成了西班牙语里形容巨富的说法，塞万提斯也在《堂吉诃德》里写到这里的银矿。造币厂铸造的八里亚尔银币由骆马和骡队运上太平洋岸，过巴拿马转上珍宝船队，另一些则东运布宜诺斯艾利斯，或从阿卡普尔科运往马尼拉。16至17世纪，全世界开采的白银约有五分之四出自这一座山。

银子是安第斯人的双手挖出来的：托莱多设立的米塔制每年强征约1.3万人，征发范围从基多一直延伸到布宜诺斯艾利斯，每七名成年男子就有一人应役，背着100至300磅矿石沿竖井梯子向上攀爬，水银中毒、严寒和坠井让许多人丧命。独立战争期间，波托西在保王军和爱国军之间反复易手；曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺撤退时下令炸毁王家造币厂，市民却潜入厂内剪断了引信。直到1821年，矿山和造币厂仍在争夺之中。

en:
Arica sits where the Azapa and Lluta valleys reach the Pacific below a steep rocky headland, the Morro; one Aymara explanation of its name describes a place beside that hill. In 1444 Camanchaco fishermen worked the shore, while valley farmers kept llamas, grew maize and exchanged fish, shellfish, textiles and highland goods across different altitude zones. Aymara lordships from the altiplano also placed colonies in the upper valleys. That network gave the coast value before any Spanish warehouse existed, while Inca power was close but had not yet firmly fixed its rule over Arica.

After the indigenous miner Diego Huallpa found Potosi silver in 1545, Spanish traffic turned toward this natural roadstead. From the 1560s, mercury from Huancavelica landed at Arica and Potosi silver moved back through its warehouses and mule trains. The settlement was probably formally titled San Marcos de Arica in 1584; contemporary accounts name Francisco Hernandez Nazarino as the settler who built houses and storerooms and organized the mule trade. The cargoes brought English and Dutch raiders, including Francis Drake, Joris van Spilbergen, Bartholomew Sharp, William Dampier and John Clipperton, while earthquakes repeatedly wrecked buildings exposed to the bay. On 28 July 1821, when Peru proclaimed independence, Arica remained a southern port serving Arequipa and Upper Peru.
zh:
阿里卡位于阿萨帕谷和柳塔谷通向太平洋之处，陡峭海岬「莫罗」俯瞰海湾；艾马拉语对地名的一种解释，把它说成海岬旁的地方。1444年，卡曼查科渔民在岸边谋生，谷地农人牧养羊驼、种植玉米，并在不同海拔之间交换鱼、贝、织物和高原物产。来自高原的艾马拉领主也在上游谷地设置移民点。西班牙货栈出现以前，这套往来网络已经让海岸有了价值；印加势力已经逼近，却还没有稳固控制阿里卡。

1545年，原住民矿工迭戈·瓦尔帕发现波托西银矿后，西班牙人流和货流转向这个天然锚地。16世纪60年代起，万卡韦利卡的汞在阿里卡上岸，波托西白银则经这里的货栈和骡队回头运出。约1584年，定居点正式获得「圣马科斯·德·阿里卡」的城市头衔；当时记载提到，殖民者弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·纳萨里诺营建房屋、仓库并组织骡运。这些货物把英国和荷兰袭掠者引到阿里卡，弗朗西斯·德雷克、约里斯·范·斯皮尔贝亨、巴塞洛缪·夏普、威廉·丹皮尔和约翰·克利珀顿都在来袭者之列，地震也一再摧毁面向海湾的建筑。1821年7月28日秘鲁宣布独立时，阿里卡仍是一座服务阿雷基帕和上秘鲁的南端港口。

en:
Oruro is a cold mineral country of the central Altiplano, nearly 3,800 metres high around the Uru Uru hills. The Uru, herders and fisherfolk of the highland lakes, were subdued first by the Aymara kingdoms and then by the Incas, who ruled this part of Qullasuyu from Paria, building a Sun temple, storehouses and tambos on the royal road. In 1444 the district had no town of any size: scattered Uru and Aymara settlements grazed llamas within the Pacajes highland world, with Caracara its best-remembered place, while the silver and copper in its rocks was worked only at a trickle.

The first Spaniards came in 1535, when Juan de Saavedra's vanguard of Almagro's Chile expedition camped at Paria. For seventy years prospectors searched the Uru Uru range; the rush came only in 1605, when the priest Francisco Medrano and his partners struck rich silver at San Cristóbal. On 1 November 1606 the oidor Manuel de Castro founded the Real Villa de San Felipe de Austria, named for Philip III. By 1618 twenty ore mills ringed the town, and a 1678 census counted 75,920 people, nearly half of them Spaniards or creoles, making Oruro the second city of Upper Peru; the veins gave out after 1680 and the town shrank. Its later fame was rebellion. In 1739 Juan Vélez de Córdova drew up a manifesto of grievances for a plot that a denunciation betrayed before it could rise, and on 10 February 1781 Sebastián Pagador and Jacinto Rodríguez de Herrera raised the Oruro revolt during the great Andean rising; royalists crushed it by 1783 and shipped its leaders to Buenos Aires. In 1789 miners found a small image of the Virgin in a hollow of the Pie de Gallo hill, and the cult of the Virgen del Socavón began. Oruro rose under Tomás Barrón on 6 October 1810 and stayed a contested royalist garrison, Olañeta's headquarters after Falsuri, while the war ran on past 1821.
zh:
奥鲁罗坐落在安第斯高原中部、乌鲁乌鲁群山一带，海拔近3800米，是一片寒冷的多矿之地。乌鲁人本是高原湖畔的牧人和渔人，先被艾马拉诸王国征服，后又受印加统治；印加人从帕里亚管辖科利亚苏尤的这一部分，在王家大道旁修建太阳神庙、仓库和坦博驿站。1444年时，这一地区还没有像样的城镇：乌鲁人和艾马拉人的零散聚落在帕卡赫斯高原世界里放牧骆马，卡拉卡拉是其中留名最多的地方，山中的银铜矿脉只有零星开采。

西班牙人最早在1535年到来，胡安·德·萨阿维德拉率领阿尔马格罗智利远征军的前锋在帕里亚扎营。此后七十年间，探矿者搜遍乌鲁乌鲁群山，热潮却迟至1605年才到来：神父弗朗西斯科·梅德拉诺等人在圣克里斯托瓦尔找到富银矿；1606年11月1日，查尔卡斯检审庭法官曼努埃尔·德·卡斯特罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略建立奥地利圣费利佩皇家城，以国王费利佩三世命名。到1618年，城周已有二十座选矿场；1678年的人口普查录得75,920人，近半是西班牙人和土生白人，奥鲁罗成为上秘鲁第二大城，只是1680年后矿脉枯竭，城市随之凋敝。它后来以反叛闻名：1739年，胡安·贝莱斯·德·科尔多瓦草拟申诉文告，密谋尚未发动便因告发而败露；1781年2月10日，塞巴斯蒂安·帕加多尔和哈辛托·罗德里格斯·德·埃雷拉趁安第斯大起义举事，保王党在1783年前将其镇压，把首领们押往布宜诺斯艾利斯。1789年，矿工在公鸡山的一处岩洞中发现一尊小圣母像，坑道圣母的信仰就此发端。1810年10月6日，奥鲁罗在托马斯·巴龙领导下起兵；整个独立战争期间它都是双方反复争夺的保王军据点，法尔苏里之战后还成了奥拉涅塔的司令部，战事一直持续到1821年以后。

en:
Mbwila, Ambuíla to the Portuguese, was a small Mbundu state in the rugged hills at the headwaters of the Lukala River, where a mountain gap joined Kongo with Ndongo and carried both kingdoms' trade caravans. Its rulers bore the title Ndembu, and the Portuguese called the string of hill polities the Dembos, buffers disputed between Angola and Kongo. Its capital stood on the heights above the valley, almost unassailable; Kongo and Ndongo both claimed it and neither ruled it, villages growing grain under local hill lords. In 1444 it passed as the remote southern march of the Manikongo.

After Luanda's foundation in 1575, three powers pressed on the gap. Mbwila swore vassalage to Angola in 1619–1620 and then ignored it, sometimes leading other Dembo rulers. It backed Queen Njinga of Ndongo in 1627–1630 and joined her again when a Dutch fleet seized Luanda in 1641. After Portugal retook Luanda in 1648, Lisbon traded its claims on Mbwila to Kongo for a mining concession King António I refused to honour.

A local succession quarrel then brought the armies in. In late 1664 António expelled the regent, Dona Isabel, and the country's lord; they fled to Luanda claiming the king meant to block the roads, and an Angolan army entered the gap. On 29 October 1665, in the Ulanga valley south of the capital, Portuguese musketeers with two light cannon, flanked by Imbangala and Brazilian allies, met a Kongo host of some fifteen thousand archers, shielded heavy infantry and a few hundred musketeers. António was killed leading the last charge, and his seven-year-old son was captured. The victors buried his head in the chapel of Our Lady of Nazareth on Luanda Bay and sent the Kongo crown and sceptre to Lisbon. Tradition makes the princess Aqualtune, who led a battalion in the battle, one of the captives sent to Pernambuco's sugar mills; her son Ganga Zumba and grandson Zumbi later led the runaway kingdom of Palmares. Kongo itself slid into half a century of civil war. Campaigns in 1692–1693 won only nominal vassalage, and in 1758 a Portuguese fort went up at Encoge, south of Mbwila, to stop slave caravans through the gap reaching Dutch, French and English ships north of Kongo.
zh:
姆布维拉（葡萄牙人称为安布伊拉）是卢卡拉河源头山区的一个姆本杜人小国；分隔刚果与恩东戈的山脉在这里裂开一道隘口，两国商队都经此往来。当地统治者称「恩登布」，葡萄牙人把这一线山地小国统称登博斯，安哥拉和刚果为这群半独立的缓冲邦争了两百年。姆布维拉的首府坐落在河谷上方的高地上，几乎无法攻取；刚果与恩东戈都宣称对它拥有主权，却都无法真正统治，各村种植谷物，听命于本地山酋。1444年，它算作刚果国王治下遥远的南疆。

1575年罗安达建城后，三股势力都压向这道隘口。1619至1620年，姆布维拉向安哥拉称臣，随后便置之不理，有时还统领其他登博斯邦主；1627至1630年恩东戈的恩津加女王作战时它站在女王一边，1641年荷兰舰队夺取罗安达后它再次投奔女王。1648年葡萄牙重克罗安达后，里斯本以一项采矿特许权为交换把对姆布维拉的主张让给刚果，安东尼奥一世却拒绝履行。

一场本地继承之争把两国大军引进了隘口。1664年末，安东尼奥驱逐了摄政唐娜·伊莎贝尔和姆布维拉邦主，二人逃到罗安达，声称国王准备封锁道路，安哥拉军队随即开进隘口。1665年10月29日，在首府以南的乌兰加河谷，携两门轻炮的葡萄牙火枪兵与因班加拉人、巴西盟军列阵，迎战由约一万五千名弓箭手、持盾重步兵和数百火枪手组成的刚果大军。安东尼奥在最后一次冲锋中被杀，他七岁的儿子被俘。胜利者把他的头颅葬在罗安达湾的拿撒勒圣母礼拜堂，刚果的王冠和权杖送往里斯本。相传在阵中率队参战的公主奥夸通也在俘虏之列，被押往伯南布哥的甘蔗种植园；她的儿子冈加·尊巴和孙子祖比后来领导了逃奴王国帕尔马雷斯。刚果本土则陷入半个世纪的内战。1692至1693年的战事只换来名义上的臣服；1758年，葡萄牙人在姆布维拉以南的恩科热筑起要塞，堵截奴隶商队借隘口驶向刚果以北海岸的荷、法、英商船。

en:
In 1444 the Chaco Boreal was a spread of dry thorn forest, palm savanna and seasonal floodplain north of the Pilcomayo and west of the Paraguay. Chiquito and Chané communities lived near its western openings, while Ayoreo and Yshyr or Chamacoco groups moved through the interior and Mbayá-Caduveo and Qom bands used the river edges. People followed game, water and seasonal harvests along paths that linked the Paraguay, the Pantanal and the Andean foothills. No imperial road or fixed frontier crossed the plain; outside armies found a population that could move around them.

Alejo García, Domingo Martínez de Irala and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca all crossed the Chaco or its margins in the early sixteenth century while seeking routes toward the Andes. A lasting Spanish wedge appeared only on 26 February 1561, when Ñuflo de Chaves marched from Asunción and founded Santa Cruz de la Sierra on the edge of Chiquitos country, about 220 kilometres east of the city's later position. Itatine attacks killed Chaves in 1568, and the settlers moved the town west in 1590 and again in 1595; the old and new populations were not united until 1622. Jesuits opened another frontier from 1691, gathering Chiquito groups into reductions with farms, churches and instruction in European music. Eleven mission towns stood by 1760, but the Spanish Crown's expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 broke up their organisation. Santa Cruz rose against Spanish rule on 24 September 1810. In 1821 the new republics held parts of the western and riverine edges, while Guaycuruan and Mbayá horsemen still controlled the open Chaco.
zh:
1444年，北查科是皮科马约河以北、巴拉圭河以西的干旱棘林、棕榈稀树草原和季节性洪泛地带。奇基托人与查内人住在靠近西部通道的地方，阿约雷奥人和伊希尔人（查马科科人）穿行内陆，姆巴亚—卡杜韦奥人和科姆人则利用河边地带。各个人群沿小径追逐猎物、水源和季节收成，这些小路连接巴拉圭河、潘塔纳尔和安第斯山麓。没有帝国道路或固定边界穿过平原；外来军队面对的是能够绕开他们移动的居民。

16世纪初，阿莱霍·加西亚、多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉和阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡都曾在寻找通往安第斯的道路时穿过查科或其边缘。1561年2月26日，纽弗洛·德·查韦斯从亚松森出兵，在奇基托斯边缘建立圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，位置在后来城区以东约220公里，西班牙人才有了持久的落脚点。1568年，伊塔廷人的攻击杀死查韦斯；居民在1590年和1595年两度西迁，新旧居民直到1622年才合在一起。耶稣会从1691年开辟另一条边疆，把奇基托人集入有农田、教堂并教授欧洲音乐的传教村。到1760年，这里共有十一座传教镇；1767年西班牙王室驱逐耶稣会，这套组织随之瓦解。1810年9月24日，圣克鲁斯起事反对西班牙统治。1821年，新生的共和国只掌握西部和河边的部分边缘，瓜伊库鲁与姆巴亚骑手仍控制着开阔查科。

en:
Chiquitos is the tropical savanna between the Amazon and the Gran Chaco, open grassland broken by rivers and strips of gallery forest. In 1444 it had no single ruler: Piñoco, Tao, Manasi and other peoples farmed maize and manioc, hunted, fished and made pottery in villages organized by kinship and language. The humid yungas on the eastern Andean slopes stopped Inca armies, and the grasslands lay beyond Spanish reach as well; the newcomers later grouped all these varied peoples together as Chiquitos.

Spaniards first came with the old town of Santa Cruz de la Sierra, founded in 1561 on the savanna's eastern edge, but colonial control stayed thin. In 1637 Brazilian bandeirantes crossed the Paraguay and raided toward the future San José de Chiquitos, opening decades of slave hunting. The Jesuits were the ones who settled in. José de Arce founded San Francisco Xavier in 1691, the first of eleven reductions built by 1760; around their churches the mission Indians ran cattle, wove cotton cloth and spoke a shared Chiquitano language, and every town kept singers and instrument makers for mass. The Swiss Jesuit Martin Schmid reached that first mission, by then called San Javier, in 1730 and stayed thirty-seven years. He set up its music school, had organs, harps and violins built, and designed the carved wooden churches of San Javier, San Rafael de Velasco and Concepción, their twisted columns and altars cut from local hardwood by Chiquitano craftsmen. With almost no Spanish settlers, the fathers ran the towns as self-governing parishes and as a buffer against Portuguese slavers. After Charles III expelled the order in 1767, the Paraguayan reductions emptied, but the Chiquitos townspeople kept their churches open and their feast-day singing; under the secular clergy who replaced the Jesuits, the mission population fell below 20,000 within two years.
zh:
奇基托斯是亚马孙与大查科之间的热带稀树草原，河流与林带穿插在开阔草地间。1444年，这里没有统一的统治者：皮尼奥卡、陶、马纳西等族群在村落里种植玉米和木薯，狩猎捕鱼并制作陶器，村落按血缘和语言组合。安第斯山东麓湿润的云加林挡住了印加军队，这片草原也在西班牙势力之外；后来的西班牙人把这些各不相同的草原居民统称为奇基托斯人。

1561年，圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉旧城在草原东缘建立，西班牙人随之而来，但殖民控制始终薄弱。1637年，巴西旗兵渡过巴拉圭河，袭扰到后来的圣何塞-德奇基托斯一带，开启了数十年的奴隶掳掠。真正扎下根来的是耶稣会。1691年，何塞·德·阿尔塞建立圣弗朗西斯科·哈维尔，这是到1760年为止十一座归化传教镇中的第一座；传教镇的印第安人在教堂周围牧牛、织棉布，使用统一的奇基塔诺语，每座镇子都有为弥撒伴奏的歌手和乐器匠。瑞士耶稣会士马丁·施密德1730年抵达这座当时已称圣哈维尔的传教镇，一住三十七年。他开办音乐学校，命人制作管风琴、竖琴和小提琴，还设计了圣哈维尔、圣拉斐尔-德贝拉斯科和康塞普西翁的木雕教堂，扭曲柱和祭坛都由奇基托斯工匠用当地硬木凿成。这里几乎没有西班牙移民，神父们把传教镇办成自治教区，也充当抵御葡萄牙奴隶贩子的屏障。1767年卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会后，巴拉圭的传教镇纷纷人去镇空，奇基托斯的镇民却维持着教堂开放和节日歌唱；接替耶稣会的世俗神父治理无方，两年之内传教区人口便降到两万以下。

en:
The Cochabamba valleys take their name from the Quechua Quchapampa, 'lake plain', and lie between the cold Altiplano and the eastern lowlands. Maize ripens on the lower valley floors while llamas graze the high ground, and in 1444 the Quta, Chui, Sipi-Sipi, Sura and their neighbours still farmed the country under their own chiefs, for Inca armies had not yet crossed the yungas. Their maize fields were the prize, since the cold highland could not grow enough grain.

The Inca Topa Yupanqui conquered the valleys late in the fifteenth century, and Huayna Capac turned them into state maize lands: he brought in some 14,000 mitmaq farmers and filled about 2,400 circular storehouses on the hillsides, whose contents went by llama caravan to the army and to Cuzco. Garci Ruiz de Orellana became the first Spaniard to hold land in the valley in 1542, Viceroy Francisco de Toledo ordered the founding of Villa Real de Oropesa in 1571, and the town was laid out afresh around its present plaza in 1574. Through the Potosí silver boom the valleys supplied the mines with grain, meal and timber, and in 1786 Charles III renamed the town Cochabamba. Its best-known fight in the independence wars came on 27 May 1812, when the patriot army was away and the women of Cochabamba climbed the Coronilla hill, led according to tradition by Manuela Gandarillas with sticks, stones and a few swords, and held off José Manuel de Goyeneche's royalists until they were ridden down; Gandarillas was killed at their head.
zh:
科恰班巴诸谷的名字来自克丘亚语「湖原」（Quchapampa），夹在寒冷高原与东部低地之间。下谷地的玉米成熟时，高处坡地还放着羊驼；1444年，库塔、丘伊、西佩西佩、苏拉等族群仍在各自首领名下耕种这片地方，印加军队还没有穿过云加林。他们的玉米田正是旁人觊觎的目标，因为寒冷高原长不出足够的粮食。

15世纪末，印加王图帕克·尤潘基征服诸谷，瓦伊纳·卡帕克把这里改成国家玉米产区：他迁来约一万四千名米特马克农民，在山坡上布满约两千四百座圆形仓库，仓里的粮食由羊驼队运往军队和库斯科。1542年，加西·鲁伊斯·德·奥雷利亚纳成为最早在谷地置产的西班牙人；1571年，总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多下令建立奥罗佩萨皇家镇，1574年城镇又在日后广场的位置重新规划。波托西银山繁荣期间，诸谷向矿区供应粮食和木材，1786年卡洛斯三世将城镇改名科恰班巴。独立战争中这里最出名的一仗发生在1812年5月27日：爱国军在外作战，科恰班巴妇女登上科罗尼利亚山，相传由曼努埃拉·甘达里利亚斯率领，手持棍棒、石块和寥寥几把刀剑，抵挡何塞·曼努埃尔·德·戈耶内切的保王军，最终被骑兵冲垮，甘达里利亚斯死在队伍前列。

en:
Chuquiabo, in Aymara Chuqiyapu, the golden farmland, is a steep green valley cut into the cold Altiplano by the Choqueyapu River beneath the ice of Illimani, its terraces dropping toward the coca-growing yungas. Aymara-speaking Colla farmers worked the terraces long before 1444, washing gold from the streams and carrying cloth and metals along the road between the Titicaca basin and the eastern lowlands, while the older ruins of Tiwanaku stood on the nearby plain. In 1444 the valley was still Colla country under its own lords, with Inca armies from Cuzco pressing into the Collao. Spanish horsemen first crossed it in 1535 with Almagro's march on Chile.

On 20 October 1548 Captain Alonso de Mendoza, acting for Pedro de la Gasca after the defeat of Gonzalo Pizarro's revolt, founded Nuestra Señora de La Paz at the village of Laja and moved the town into the valley three days later; the name marked the peace just won, and Charles V granted it a coat of arms in 1555. La Paz sat on the road carrying Potosí silver from the high mines toward Lima, and mule trains made the town rich. It passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. In 1781 Julián Apasa, an Aymara trader in coca and cloth who had taken the name Túpac Katari from two earlier rebel leaders, brought some 40,000 highlanders against the town, made his camp on the El Alto heights, and blockaded it for six months, until troops advancing from Lima and Buenos Aires broke the siege, at a cost put at 20,000 dead. He was hanged and quartered, and one of his severed limbs was displayed on a height above the town as a warning; Aymara oral tradition keeps his last words: 'I die, but I return as thousands upon thousands.' On 16 July 1809 Pedro Domingo Murillo proclaimed a junta in La Paz, the first open break with Spain in Spanish South America; royalist troops retook the town and hanged him on 29 January 1810.
zh:
丘基亚博，艾马拉语称丘基亚普，意为「产金的田」，是乔克亚普河在寒冷高原上切出的深翠河谷，抬头便是积雪的伊伊马尼峰，层层梯田朝盛产古柯的云加低地铺落。1444年之前很久，说艾马拉语的科拉农人已在此耕作，从溪中淘金，沿连通的的喀喀湖盆地与东部低地的道路贩运布匹和金属，更古老的蒂亚瓦纳科遗址就矗立在附近平原上。1444年，这里仍是本族首领治下的科拉土地，库斯科的印加大军正步步进逼科利亚奥高原。1535年，西班牙骑兵随阿尔马格罗远征智利，首次穿过这道河谷。

1548年10月20日，阿隆索·德·门多萨上尉受命于佩德罗·德拉加斯卡，在拉哈村建立「和平圣母城」；贡萨洛·皮萨罗的叛乱刚平，城名便是纪念这场和平，三天后城址迁入丘基亚博河谷。1555年，卡洛斯五世赐下城徽。拉巴斯坐落在波托西白银运往利马的大道上，往来的骡队使这座城镇富足，它于1776年划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。1781年，做古柯和布匹生意的艾马拉商人胡利安·阿帕萨·尼纳取两位先前义军首领之名，自称图帕克·卡塔里，率约四万高原部众攻城；他在埃尔阿尔托高地上扎营，围城六个月，利马和布宜诺斯艾利斯开来的援军才将包围打破，围城期间死者约两万。他被处绞刑后车裂，一条残肢被悬在城旁高地示众；艾马拉口传留下他最后的话：「我死，但我将化为千万人归来。」1809年7月16日，佩德罗·多明戈·穆里略在拉巴斯宣布成立执政委员会，这是西属南美洲第一次公开与西班牙决裂；保王军队重占城市，于1810年1月29日将他绞死。

en:
Moxos, written Mojos in Spanish sources, is the seasonally flooded Beni savanna crossed by headwaters of the Mamoré and Madeira. Long before 1444 its peoples raised a hydraulic landscape of artificial mounds, raised fields, ponds, canals and causeways that let villages live, travel and farm through the annual flood; the mound country around Casarabe, east of the later town of Trinidad, held one of the most elaborate of these societies. In 1444 Arawak-speaking Moxo communities and neighbours such as the Itonama, Cayuvava, Canichana, Tacana and Movima lived among rivers, lakes and gallery forest under local chiefs, beyond the reach of the Inca.

A Spanish probe from Lima under Pedro de Candía reached the savanna in 1538 and withdrew, and the lowlands kept their independence for another century and a half. The Jesuits Pedro Marbán and Cipriano Barace came from Santa Cruz de la Sierra in 1675 and won followers with iron tools and medical care; the first reduction, Nuestra Señora de Loreto, dates from April 1682, and Barace founded Trinidad on the Mamoré in 1686. The mission towns gathered many peoples around church, plaza and craft quarters, teaching weaving, writing and liturgical music, and a Baroque repertory composed there by Jesuit and indigenous musicians survives in manuscripts of more than four thousand pages. Barace, founder also of the Baures mission, was killed on the forest frontier with Brazil in 1702. Fifteen villages existed when the order for the Jesuit expulsion arrived in 1768; they passed to secular clergy and lost people and trade in the decades that followed.
zh:
莫克索斯在西班牙文资料中写作莫霍斯（Mojos），中文通行称作莫霍斯平原，是马莫雷河、马代拉河上游贯穿的季节性洪泛贝尼草原。早在1444年之前，这里的居民就堆造出一片人工地貌：土丘、台田、池塘、渠沟和堤道，让村落能在一年一度的大水中居住、通行和耕作；后来特立尼达以东卡萨拉韦一带土丘密布，是这些社会中工程最繁复的之一。1444年，操阿拉瓦克语的莫克索斯社群与伊托纳马、卡尤瓦瓦、卡尼查纳、塔卡纳、莫维马等邻族，在河流、湖泊和林带之间各由本地首领治理，印加的势力到不了这里。

1538年，佩德罗·德·坎迪亚从利马派出的西班牙试探队曾到达草原又撤走，低地的独立又维持了一个半世纪。1675年，耶稣会士佩德罗·马尔万和西普里亚诺·巴拉塞从圣克鲁斯德拉谢拉进入，靠铁器和医药赢得信众；第一座归化村镇洛雷托圣母建于1682年4月，巴拉塞又于1686年在马莫雷河畔建立特立尼达。传教城镇把许多族群聚在教堂、广场和工匠区周围，教他们纺织、识字和教堂音乐；耶稣会士与本地乐师在那里谱写的巴洛克曲目，留存下四千多页抄谱。巴拉塞还建立了包雷斯传教站，1702年在与巴西交界的森林边疆被杀。1768年驱逐耶稣会的命令抵达时，这里共有十五座传教村镇；村镇转交世俗神职人员后，人口和商贸在随后几十年里不断流失。

en:
The Puno highlands cover the cold plains north-west of Lake Titicaca, around Hatuncolla and Lake Umayo. After Tiwanaku's decline, Colla chiefs built pukaras on the hills and raised tower-like chullpas at Sillustani for noble families. Llamas and alpacas grazed the plain, potatoes and quinoa grew in high fields, and lake routes connected Hatuncolla with lands holding gold. In 1444 Chuchi Capac ruled from Hatuncolla, but its many fortified settlements were divided by rivalry and faced both the Lupaqa and Pachacuti's expanding Inca forces.

The Colla–Inca War of 1445–1450 ended in Pachacuti's victory. Chuchi Capac waited at Ayaviri, then withdrew to Pucara after a long battle; Inca troops took the fortress and captured him, after which local leaders submitted at Hatunqulla. The conquered country became part of Qullasuyu. Francisco Pizarro granted local lands in encomienda in 1535, and silver prospectors later reached the lake road. In 1657 José de Salcedo registered the rich Laykakota silver vein, and San Luis de Alba grew nearby, with its own priest by 1665. Factional killings and executions during the Laicacota conflict destroyed the mining settlement. In 1668 the Viceroy Count of Lemos moved its population to San Carlos de Puno, laid out on the road linking Arequipa, Cuzco, La Paz and Potosí.
zh:
普诺高原位于的的喀喀湖西北岸，环绕哈通科拉和乌马约湖。蒂亚瓦纳科衰落后，科拉首领在山丘上筑起名为普卡拉的堡垒，并在西路斯塔尼为贵族家族修建塔状的楚尔帕墓。大羊驼和羊驼在寒冷平原放牧，马铃薯和藜麦生长在高田里，湖上道路把哈通科拉同产金土地连接起来。1444年，楚奇·卡帕克以哈通科拉为统治中心，但众多设防聚落彼此竞争，外部还要面对卢帕卡人和帕查库特克扩张中的印加军队。

1445—1450年的科拉—印加战争以帕查库特克获胜告终。楚奇·卡帕克先在阿亚维里列阵，久战后退守普卡拉；印加军队攻下堡垒并俘虏他，各地首领随后到哈通科拉归降。被征服的土地成为科利亚苏尤的一部分。1535年，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗把当地土地授予监护征赋主，银矿勘探者后来也进入这条湖畔道路。1657年，何塞·德·萨尔塞多登记了富饶的莱卡科塔银脉，圣路易斯·德·阿尔瓦随之兴起，并在1665年获得常驻神父。莱卡科塔的派系仇杀和处决冲突破坏了这座矿业聚落。1668年，莱莫斯伯爵总督把居民迁往圣卡洛斯·德·普诺，新城设在连接阿雷基帕、库斯科、拉巴斯和波托西的道路上。

en:
The Chili Valley carries mountain water from the Andean foothills toward a dry stretch of Peru's southern coast. Yarabaya and Chimba farmers, together with Collagua and Cabana villages, cut irrigation canals along the river terraces and grew maize in ground that received little rain. The Inca state treated the valley as a southwestern frontier and posted mitma settlers there, but it did not build a city on the later Spanish model. In 1444 the settlements later called Yanahuara, Cayma and Characato were farming hamlets on the edge of Tawantinsuyu, linked by tracks to highland pastures and the Camaná shore.

Spanish newcomers moved the council and households of Villa Hermosa de Camaná into the valley on 15 August 1540 and refounded them as Arequipa; Charles V recognized the town as a city the next year. Its wheat, maize, wine and brandy supplied the Caylloma and Potosí mining circuits, and roads ran down to the sea at Quilca. White volcanic sillar became the material of its churches and convents. The Dominican Monastery of Santa Catalina, consecrated in 1579, housed nuns from wealthy criolla and mestiza families inside a walled precinct of narrow streets.

On 19 February 1600 Huaynaputina produced the largest eruption recorded in South America. People in Arequipa watched ash darken the sky, while falling volcanic debris buried fields across the region and killed perhaps 1,000 to 1,500 people. Santa Catalina was damaged again by earthquakes in 1604 and was later rebuilt. Arequipa remained a royalist stronghold in the independence war: Mateo Pumacahua and Vicente Angulo seized it in November 1814, and Juan Ramírez de Orozco's royalists recovered it less than a month later. When Peru's independence was proclaimed in 1821, the city was still under royalist control.
zh:
奇利河谷把安第斯山麓的雨雪和融水引向秘鲁南部的干旱海岸。亚拉瓦亚人和钦巴人同科利亚瓜、卡瓦纳人的村落一起沿河阶开渠，在少雨的土地上种植玉米。印加国家把这片谷地当作西南边境，迁来米特马屯垦者驻守，却没有建立西方式城市。1444年，后来称为亚纳瓦拉、凯马和查拉卡托的聚落还是印加边缘的农村，有小路通往高地牧场和卡马纳海岸。

1540年8月15日，西班牙人把卡马纳美丽镇的市政会和居民迁入奇利河谷，重建为阿雷基帕；次年，查理五世承认它为城市。当地的小麦、玉米、葡萄酒和白兰地供应卡伊约马与波托西矿区，货物再沿道路运到基尔卡出海。白色火山凝灰岩成为教堂和修道院的主要建材。1579年祝圣的圣卡塔利娜修道院是一座围墙环绕的宗教城区，狭窄街巷里住着出身富裕克里奥尔和梅斯蒂索家庭的修女。

1600年2月19日，瓦伊纳普蒂纳火山发生南美有记录以来规模最大的喷发。阿雷基帕人看见火山灰遮暗天空，落下的火山碎屑掩埋周围农田，约1000至1500人丧生。圣卡塔利娜修道院又在1604年地震中受损，之后得到重建。独立战争时期，阿雷基帕长期倾向保王派：1814年11月，马特奥·普马卡瓦和比森特·安古洛攻占该城，胡安·拉米雷斯·德·奥罗斯科的保王军不到一个月便将其收复。1821年秘鲁宣布独立时，阿雷基帕仍受保王派控制。

en:
Nazca covers a chain of narrow river valleys in Peru's southern desert, between the Pacific shore and the Andean foothills. Rain is scarce, so Paracas and Nasca communities built puquios, sloped filtration galleries, underground channels and vertical shafts that carried groundwater to fields in the Aja, Ingenio and Grande valleys. The dry pampa beside those fields holds their geoglyphs, made between roughly 500 BC and AD 500 by stripping dark surface pebbles from lighter soil; straight lines run for kilometres beside figures of birds, fish, a monkey, a spider and plants. Inca officials reached the coast around 1438 and tied the valleys to Cusco by road. In 1444 Nazca was a recently annexed frontier, valued for irrigated maize, fish and the desert route south.

Colonial chronicles date the Spanish founding of Santiago de la Nasca to 28 October 1548, when Alonso de Mendoza acted for Pedro de la Gasca; another tradition places the formal foundation in 1591 under Viceroy García Hurtado de Mendoza. Grapes became the valleys' profitable crop. Jesuit colleges in Cuzco and Lima held large estates in the Ingenio Valley, where enslaved African workers made wine, grape brandy and the big ceramic botijas used to ship them. When Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767, the Crown took the estates. On 14 October 1820 Manuel Rojas Argerich led 250 patriots in a surprise attack on Colonel Manuel Quimper's royalist detachment; the town swore independence two days later and received its formal town government on 29 August 1821.
zh:
纳斯卡位于秘鲁南部荒漠，是太平洋岸与安第斯山麓之间一连串狭窄河谷。雨水稀少，帕拉卡斯人和纳斯卡人修建普基奥斯，用有坡度的渗水廊道、地下渠道和竖井把地下水引向阿哈、因赫尼奥和格兰德河谷的农田。河谷旁的干燥荒原上分布着他们的地画：约在公元前500年至公元500年间，人们刮去深色表砾，露出浅色土层，划出长达数公里的直线，以及鸟、鱼、猴、蜘蛛和植物图形。约1438年，印加官员抵达海岸，用道路把诸谷连接到库斯科。1444年，纳斯卡是刚并入印加的边地，价值在灌溉玉米、鱼类和南通的荒漠道路。

殖民地编年史把圣地亚哥·德·拉纳斯卡的建城时间记为1548年10月28日，由阿隆索·德·门多萨奉佩德罗·德·拉·加斯卡之命完成；另一种说法把正式建城放在1591年总督加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨任内。葡萄后来成为诸谷地最赚钱的作物。库斯科和利马的耶稣会学院在因赫尼奥河谷拥有大型庄园，役使非洲奴隶生产葡萄酒、葡萄白兰地和运输用的大陶瓮。1767年卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会后，这些庄园收归王室。1820年10月14日，曼努埃尔·罗哈斯·阿尔赫里奇率250名独立派士兵突袭曼努埃尔·金佩尔的保王分队；两天后，城镇宣誓独立，并于1821年8月29日正式设立镇政机构。

en:
Abancay lies in a warm grain valley on the eastern Andean slope, beneath Mount Ampay and just north of the Pachachaca river. Quechua farmers held villages here before the Incas, and the Pachachaca was the border country facing the Chancas on the far bank; the place took its name from the amancay, a white mountain flower. In 1444 it was a sensitive frontier of Cuzco, where the road out of the highland capital split between the southern mountains and the routes down to the coast.

Those roads brought the conquistadors' own civil war to the valley on 12 July 1537. Alonso de Alvarado, sent by Pizarro to relieve Cuzco, held the Abancay bridge and ford against Rodrigo Orgóñez, Almagro's lieutenant; Pedro de Lerma's desertion carried the fight for the Almagrists, who captured Alvarado and most of his men, the opening round of a quarrel that ended with Almagro's defeat at Las Salinas in April 1538. The Spanish town of Santiago de los Reyes de Amancay was formally founded only on 3 November 1574. Its encomiendas planted sugar cane for aguardiente, and mule trains made the place a freight link between the coast and the southeastern Andes. Micaela Bastidas, born to one of the district's muleteer families in 1744, became Túpac Amaru II's wife and chief organiser: she raised troops and ran the revolt's supplies and correspondence until its collapse, and was put to death in Cuzco on 18 May 1781, the same day as her husband.
zh:
阿班凯位于安第斯山东坡一个温暖的谷物河谷，在安佩伊山下，紧邻帕查查卡河以北。印加人到来之前，克丘亚农人已在此结村而居，帕查查卡河对岸就是昌卡人的地界；地名得自阿曼凯，一种白色的山花。1444年，这里是库斯科敏感的前沿，从高原都城伸出的道路在此分岔，一条通向南部山地，一条通往沿海。

1537年7月12日，这些道路把征服者自己的内战引进了河谷。阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多奉皮萨罗之命驰援库斯科，扼守阿班凯桥和渡口，迎战阿尔马格罗的部将罗德里戈·奥戈涅斯；佩德罗·德·莱尔马临阵倒戈，阿尔马格罗一方击溃并俘虏了阿尔瓦拉多和他的大部分人马。这场争斗最后以1538年4月阿尔马格罗在萨利纳斯战败收场。直到1574年11月3日，西班牙人才正式建立圣地亚哥·德·洛斯雷耶斯·德·阿曼凯镇。监护地里种起甘蔗酿造烧酒，骡队则把这里变成沿海与安第斯东南部之间的货运节点。1744年，米卡埃拉·巴斯蒂达斯出生在本地一个骡夫家庭，后来成为图帕克·阿马鲁二世的妻子和最主要的助手：她征募军队，统筹起义的补给与文书，起义失败后于1781年5月18日在库斯科被处死，丈夫也在同一天赴死。

en:
Cuzco lies high in a valley of the eastern Andes, the navel of the Inca world. The Killke people raised the first walls on the hill above it around 1100, and after 1438 the Sapa Inca Pachacuti made the old town the capital of Tawantinsuyu, laying it out as a puma with the plaza of Haucaypata at its breast. The puma's head was the citadel of Sacsayhuamán, raised by 20,000 labourers: three dry-masonry terrace walls, their blocks hauled thirty-five kilometres from the quarries, some over a hundred tonnes yet fitted so tightly that paper will not pass between them. Roads ran from the city's quarters to every suyu, and the Coricancha, the temple of the Sun, was sheathed in gold. In 1444 Pachacuti was extending Inca power from the richest and holiest city of the Andes.

Atahualpa's men had only just taken it in the civil war when Pizarro's Spaniards entered on 15 November 1533 and stripped the palaces and the gold plates from the Coricancha; he refounded it after the Spanish fashion on 23 March 1534. In May 1536 Manco Inca seized Sacsayhuamán, fired the thatched roofs with burning arrows and hot stones, and penned some 190 Spaniards around the square for ten months; Juan Pizarro was killed by a stone in the assault that retook the fortress. Manco withdrew to Vilcabamba, whose last Inca, Túpac Amaru I, was beheaded in Haucaypata in 1572. The victors' feud ended at Las Salinas on 6 April 1538, when Almagro was defeated and executed in the city that July; they quarried Sacsayhuamán block by block for their houses, and only the stones too huge to move were left. Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, born here in 1539 to a Spanish captain and an Inca princess, learned Quechua and the reading of quipus here before writing the Comentarios Reales in Spain.

A baroque cathedral and La Compañía church rose on Inca foundations, until the earthquake of 1650 levelled most of the city and spread the cult of the Lord of Earthquakes. On 4 November 1780 the kuraka Túpac Amaru II put the corregidor Arriaga to death at Tungasuca and raised the Andes in revolt; his army failed before Cuzco in 1781 and he was quartered in the plaza on 18 May, after which Charles III banned the Comentarios Reales in Peru as dangerous. The Angulo brothers and Mateo Pumacahua rose in 1814 and were crushed within a year, and in 1821, as Lima proclaimed independence, Cuzco still held for the king.
zh:
库斯科坐落在安第斯山东麓的高谷之中，是印加世界的肚脐。约1100年，基尔克人率先在城北山丘上筑起墙垣；1438年以后，萨帕·印卡帕查库特克把这座老城定为塔万廷苏尤的都城，按美洲狮的形状规划全城，以豪卡伊帕塔大广场为狮胸。狮首是城北的萨克塞瓦曼城堡：帕查库特克和后继者征发约两万名役夫修筑三道锯齿状阶墙，石灰岩巨石从三十五公里外的采石场拖来，最大的重逾一百吨，石块不施灰浆，接缝严密得连一张纸都插不进。大道从城区通向帝国四大苏尤，太阳神庙科里坎查遍覆金板。1444年，帕查库特克正从这座安第斯最富庶、最神圣的城市向外扩张印加的势力。

阿塔瓦尔帕的将领在内战中夺城未久，1533年11月15日，皮萨罗麾下的西班牙人便开入城中，洗劫各处王宫，剥下科里坎查的金板；1534年3月23日，皮萨罗按西班牙式样在同一广场周围重建城市。1536年5月，曼科·印卡夺取萨克塞瓦曼，用烧红的石弹和火箭点燃茅草屋顶，把约一百九十名西班牙人围困在广场一带达十个月；胡安·皮萨罗带队反攻城堡时被石头击中头部，伤重而死。曼科最终退往比尔卡班巴，1572年，这个小朝廷的末代印卡图帕克·阿马鲁一世在豪卡伊帕塔广场被斩首。征服者之间的仇怨于1538年4月6日在拉斯萨利纳斯了断，皮萨罗兄弟击败阿尔马格罗，他于同年7月在城中被处死。战胜者随后把萨克塞瓦曼拆石建房，最后只剩下大得搬不动的巨石。史家印卡·加西拉索·德拉维加1539年生于库斯科，父亲是西班牙军官，母亲是印卡公主；他在库斯科长大，说克丘亚语、能读奇普，后来前往西班牙，写成《印卡王室述评》。

巴洛克式大教堂和耶稣会教堂在印加地基上陆续建起，1650年的大地震把殖民城区几乎夷平，城中兴起「地震之主」的崇拜。1780年11月4日，酋长图帕克·阿马鲁二世在通加苏卡处死地方长官阿里亚加，震动安第斯的大起义随之爆发；1781年他的大军进逼库斯科却未能破城，5月18日他在广场上被车裂。起义之后，卡洛斯三世以「危险」为由在秘鲁禁毁《印卡王室述评》。1814年，安古洛兄弟与马特奥·普马卡瓦再度举事，不到一年即告失败；1821年利马宣布独立之时，库斯科仍为西班牙国王坚守。

en:
The Rímac, Chillón and Lurín water green valleys through the coastal desert of central Peru. Above the sea at Pachacámac stood the holiest shrine of the Peruvian coast: for more than a thousand years pilgrims climbed to consult the oracle of the creator god Pacha Kamaq, and even the Incas, when they later took the site and built a Temple of the Sun there, let its priests keep their independence. Around it spread the adobe towns and huacas of the Ichma, heirs of the older Lima and Maranga cultures, Cajamarquilla and Pucllana among them, in a densely peopled countryside. In 1444 the Ichma still ruled the valleys from these mud-brick centres, beyond the reach of Cuzco.

After Cajamarca, Francisco Pizarro sent his brother Hernando and fourteen horsemen to Pachacámac for its gold, but the priests had carried off more than four hundred loads of it and the treasure was never found. Pizarro founded his capital on the lands of the Ichma lord Taulichusco on 18 January 1535, naming it the City of the Kings for the Epiphany, though the native name of the valley prevailed as Lima. In August 1536 an Inca army under Quizu Yupanqui stormed the new town while Cuzco itself lay besieged, and was beaten back. Made capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1543, with Callao harbouring the silver fleets, Lima had San Marcos, the first university chartered in South America, from 1551 and its first printing press, worked by the Italian Antonio Ricardo, from 1584. The founder did not grow old in his capital. On 26 June 1541 Almagro's men burst into his palace and cut Pizarro down after he had killed two of them.

Earthquakes wrecked the city in 1586, 1687 and 1746, the last sending a wave over Callao, and Viceroy Manso de Velasco rebuilt both city and port; the walls raised in the 1680s faced the Pacific corsairs. A mural of Christ painted on an adobe wall by a slave brought from Angola stood through the earthquakes of 1655, 1687 and 1746, and the Lord of Miracles came to draw October processions of penitents in purple; the city council named the image patron of Lima in 1715. In 1776 the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata took Lima's monopoly over the silver of Upper Peru, and on 28 July 1821, after San Martín landed and the viceroy withdrew to the mountains, the city proclaimed independence.
zh:
里马克河、奇永河与卢林河在秘鲁中部的沿海沙漠中浇灌出片片绿野。海边高地上的帕查卡马克是整个秘鲁海岸最神圣的朝圣地：一千多年里，朝圣者登山求问造物神帕查·卡马克的神谕；后来印加人拿下圣地、加建太阳神庙，也仍任由神谕祭司保持独立。圣地周围散布着依其马人的土坯城镇，他们是更古老的利马文化与马兰加文化的继承者，卡哈马基利亚、普克利亚纳等瓦卡圣地星罗棋布，乡野人烟稠密。1444年，依其马人仍以这些土坯城为中心统治各河谷，库斯科的势力尚未到达。
