卡哈马卡之役后，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗派弟弟埃尔南多率十四名骑兵前往帕查卡马克索取黄金，祭司们却已运走四百多驮金子，这批财宝再无人找到。1535年1月18日，皮萨罗在依其马首领陶利丘斯科的土地上建立新都，为纪念主显节取名「诸王之城」，但河谷的土著名字最终流行开来，称利马。1536年8月，库斯科尚在围困之中，基苏·尤潘基率领的印加军队猛攻新城，被击退。1543年利马成为秘鲁总督辖区首府，卡亚俄是白银船队停泊的外港；南美洲第一所奉敕设立的大学圣马尔科斯大学1551年在此开办，意大利人安东尼奥·里卡多1584年又在这里开动了南美洲的第一台印刷机。开创这座城市的人并没能在此安享晚年。1541年6月26日，阿尔马格罗一党冲进他的宫殿，皮萨罗亲手杀死两名袭击者后被砍倒。

1586年、1687年和1746年的地震三度重创利马，最后一次还让巨浪吞没卡亚俄，总督曼索·德·贝拉斯科主持重建城港；1680年代筑起的城墙对着太平洋上的海盗。一名被掳自安哥拉的黑奴在土坯墙上绘成的基督壁画，历经1655年、1687年和1746年三次地震而不毁，「奇迹之主」引来越来越多身穿紫袍的忏悔者在10月游行；市议会1715年已奉这幅圣像为利马的主保。1776年，新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区夺走了利马对上秘鲁白银的垄断；1821年圣马丁率军登陆、总督退入山区后，利马于7月28日宣布独立。

en:
Huancavelica takes its name from Wankawillka, the Quechua 'sacred stone', the hill above the cold Ichu River, a tributary of the Mantaro. Its high pastures were the country of the Angaraes, wedged between the Huanca towns of the Mantaro valley and the warlike Chanca confederation. Villagers had long dug red cinnabar from the hill of Chacllacatana and ground it into pigment, working it on and off until about 1460. In 1444 local Quechua lords still ruled, for the Inca wars against the Chancas had only just reached these valleys; within a generation Pachacuti's armies brought it, with the Huanca country, into the Tawantinsuyu.

Conquistadors crossed the highlands in 1533-34, and the Huancas of the neighbouring valleys allied with Spain against Cuzco. The hill's worth emerged later. In 1559 the prospector Enrique Garces recognised mercury ore on Wankawillka, and around 1563 the curaca Gonzalo de Nahuincopa showed the rich lode to the encomendero Amador Cabrera, who registered it on 1 January 1564 as La Descubridora; the mine was renamed Todos los Santos and, in the eighteenth century, Santa Barbara. Viceroy Toledo had Villa Rica de Oropesa founded on 4 August 1572, and the next year took the mines for the Crown under a mercury monopoly. Santa Barbara was the only large quicksilver mine in the Americas. Mule and llama trains carried its mercury to Potosi, Oruro and Cerro de Pasco, and even to New Spain when the Almaden mines in Spain could not keep up; a miners' guild ran the workings from 1577.

The metal that refined all that silver was dug at a heavy price. The mita sent thousands of native labourers into the tunnels, and a mass for the dead was said before every shift went down. In 1648 the viceroy in Lima called Potosi and Huancavelica 'the two pillars that support this kingdom and that of Spain', adding that Spain could sooner spare the silver of Potosi than its mercury. Tunnel collapses cut output through the eighteenth century and the mines stopped work in 1813. The next year local men under Marino Castano joined Mateo Pumacahua's revolt.
zh:
万卡韦利卡其名来自克丘亚语的万卡维尔卡（Wankawillka），意为「圣石」，指伊丘河上方的那座山；伊丘河水寒，注入曼塔罗河。这片高原牧场曾是安加赖斯人的土地，夹在曼塔罗河谷的万卡诸邦与南方好战的昌卡联盟之间。当地人早就在查克利拉卡塔纳山开采红色辰砂、研磨成颜料，矿脉断断续续采到约1460年。1444年，本地克丘亚酋长仍在统治，因为印加对昌卡的战争才刚波及这些谷地；不出一代人，帕查库特克的军队便把这片土地和万卡之地一并纳入塔万廷苏尤。

1533至1534年，征服者穿过这片高原，邻近河谷的万卡人站到西班牙一边，共同对抗库斯科。这座山的价值后来才显出来。1559年，探矿者恩里克·加塞斯在山上认出汞矿石；约1563年，酋长贡萨洛·德·尼亚温科帕把富矿脉指给委托监护主阿马多尔·卡夫雷拉，后者于1564年1月1日把矿山登记为「发现者」（La Descubridora），矿山后来更名「诸圣」，18世纪又改称圣巴巴拉。1572年8月4日，托莱多总督下令建立奥罗佩萨富镇，次年将矿山收归王室，实行水银专营。圣巴巴拉是美洲唯一的大型水银矿，骡子和羊驼驮队把水银运往波托西、奥鲁罗和塞罗德帕斯科，连新西班牙也在西班牙阿尔马登产量不继时得到接济；1577年起，矿工行会经营这座矿山。

提炼那么多白银所用的水银，开采代价惨重。米塔制把成千上万名土著劳工送进矿道，每班人下井之前都要先做一台追思弥撒。1648年，驻利马的秘鲁总督把波托西和万卡韦利卡称作「支撑本王国与西班牙王国的两根支柱」，还说西班牙宁可舍弃波托西的白银，也不能没有这里的水银。18世纪矿道接连坍塌，产量下滑，矿山于1813年停工。次年，马里尼奥·卡斯塔尼奥带领本地人加入马特奥·普马卡瓦的起义。

en:
Jauja lies at the head of the Mantaro valley, the broadest vale in the Peruvian Andes, where the Xauxa-Wanka grew maize on terraced fields and ran great llama herds long before the Incas. Their town stood above the river on the royal road from Cuzco to Quito, and Wanka fighters had a name as the toughest in the mountains. In 1444 they still ruled themselves, with the Chanca wars only just behind them.

Pachacuti's armies took the valley after hard fighting, and around 1465 Túpac Inca Yupanqui built Hatun Xauxa as an imperial centre, with a temple of the Sun, an acllawasi and storehouses large enough to feed an army; only Cuzco outranked it. When Huayna Capac died at Quito, his body rested at Xauxa on the road south, an honour for a city whose men had been among his most loyal troops in the northern wars. The Xauxa backed Huascar in the civil war and made the city his headquarters. Atahualpa's general Challco Chima stormed it, kept the captive Huascar in its fortress and had him drowned in the Andamarca river. Hernando Pizarro later found Challco Chima camped here at the head of 35,000 men and tricked him into leaving his army on a false summons from Atahualpa; Francisco Pizarro, reaching Xauxa in 1533, had the general burned on suspicion of messages to Quizquiz.

On 25 April 1534 Pizarro founded Santa Fe de Hatun Xauxa as the first Spanish capital of Peru. His men opened Inca storehouses heaped with food, clothing and treasure and found they could live for months without working; that memory, fixed in a green and gentle valley, produced the país de Jauja, the Spanish land of Cockaigne, and the saying 'Esto es Jauja' for any easy plenty. The capital lasted a year, since Lima was founded nearer the sea in 1535, and in 1565 the town was moved to its present site. Tarma and then Huancayo took the valley's trade, yet Jauja's dry mountain air kept filling its hospital with ailing Spaniards. From 1742 to 1756 the forests to the east rose under Juan Santos Atahualpa.
zh:
豪哈地处曼塔罗河谷北端，这是秘鲁安第斯最宽阔的河谷。早在印加人到来之前，绍克萨-万卡人就在这里的梯田上种玉米、牧养成群的羊驼；他们的城寨高踞河畔，正临库斯科通往基多的王家大道，万卡武士的悍勇也闻名山间。1444年时，昌卡战争的烽烟才刚散去，万卡人仍然自己管着这片土地。

帕查库特克的军队经苦战拿下河谷，约1465年，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基建起瓦敦万萨作为帝国的行政中心：城中有太阳神庙、选妃宫和足以供养大军的仓库，地位仅次于库斯科。瓦伊纳·卡帕克在基多去世后，灵柩南运途中曾在万萨停驻，因为这座城派出的士兵是他北方战事中最忠诚的一支。绍克萨人同样站在王廷一边，内战中支持瓦斯卡尔，把万萨作为他的大本营。阿塔瓦尔帕的将领查尔科·奇马攻破此城，将被俘的瓦斯卡尔囚于城中要塞，又把他溺死在安达马卡河。后来埃尔南多·皮萨罗在万萨见到查尔科·奇马和他的三万五千大军，便假传阿塔瓦尔帕的命令把他骗离军队；1533年弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗抵达万萨，又怀疑他与基斯基斯暗通书信，将他烧死。

1534年4月25日，皮萨罗建立圣菲·德·瓦敦万萨，作为西属秘鲁的第一个首府。部下打开印加的仓库，里面堆满粮食、衣物和财货，发现自己几个月不用操劳也能度日；这座青翠和煦的河谷在西班牙语里就此成了「豪哈之乡」，也就是安乐乡的代名词，西班牙人还用「这简直是豪哈」（Esto es Jauja）来形容轻易到手的富足。首府只维持了一年：1535年利马在更靠海的地方建起，1565年城镇又迁到今址。河谷的贸易先后被塔尔马和万卡约接走，但豪哈干燥的山风仍把患病的西班牙人不断送进当地医院。1742至1756年，东面的丛林在胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕领导下起事。

en:
At the mouth of the Moche River, where Andean water runs out into the coastal desert, the Chimú built Chan Chan, the largest adobe city in the Americas. By 1444 ten walled palaces, one raised for each dead king, spread across some twenty square kilometres, their mud walls moulded with fish, nets, pelicans and crabs. Canals carried mountain water to fields of maize and cotton on the rainless plain, and forty thousand people or more lived off them; thousands of craftsmen worked gold, silver and the burnished black Chimú pottery, their trades fixed by law. At Huanchaco, the city's port, fishermen went out on reed canoes, and Spondylus shell travelled down the coast from Ecuador. The kings ranked the Moon above the Sun and were buried with their courts in the palaces; Chimú oral history traced the dynasty to Taycanamo, who crossed the sea on a balsa raft. In 1444 the kingdom's coast ran from Paramonga almost to Tumbes.

Around 1470 Túpac Inca Yupanqui's armies cut the mountain canals above the valley, and with the fields drying the Chimú had to surrender. Their king Minchançaman was carried off to Cuzco, the artisans were resettled under the mitma system, and Chan Chan's gold went to adorn the Qurikancha sun temple. Beside the half-empty capital Diego de Almagro marked out a Spanish town on 6 December 1534 and named it Trujillo, after Pizarro's birthplace in Extremadura; Pizarro installed its first town council on 5 March 1535, and in 1537 Charles V made it the first city in Peru granted a royal coat of arms. The conquerors looted the abandoned royal compounds, and one tomb yielded gold entered in the records at 80,000 pesos. An earthquake all but destroyed the town on 14 February 1619, and between 1687 and 1690 it girdled itself with an elliptical wall against the pirates raiding the Pacific coast. Sugar and wheat brought fresh wealth, and on 29 December 1820 the intendant José Bernardo de Tagle proclaimed Trujillo's independence, the first such declaration in Peru.
zh:
莫切河入海口处，安第斯山水消失在沿海沙漠里，奇穆人在这里建起昌昌——美洲最大的土坯城。到1444年，十座带围墙的王宫在约二十平方公里内铺展，每一座都为一位故去的国王而建，土坯墙上塑着鱼、渔网、鹈鹕和螃蟹。灌溉渠把山雪水引到无雨平原上的玉米田和棉田，城里城外有四万多人；数千名匠人加工金器、银器和奇穆乌亮的黑陶，职业由王法限定。外港万查科的渔民划着芦苇舟出海，厄瓜多尔沿海的海菊蛤也沿海路南运到此。国王们把月亮看得比太阳还重，死后连同随员葬入王宫；据奇穆口传，王朝始祖塔凯那姆是乘木筏渡海而来。1444年，奇莫的沿海疆土从帕拉蒙加一直延伸到近通贝斯一带。

约1470年，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的大军切断河谷上方的山间水渠，田地干涸，奇穆人被迫投降。国王敏查卡曼被押往库斯科，工匠按米特马制度被迁走，昌昌的金器被送去装点科里坎查太阳神殿。1534年12月6日，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗在半空的旧都旁圈出一座西班牙城镇，以皮萨罗在埃斯特雷马杜拉的故乡命名为特鲁希略；1535年3月5日皮萨罗为它设立首个市政会，1537年卡洛斯五世赐下城徽，它是秘鲁第一座获此恩荣的城市。征服者洗劫废弃的王宫，一座王陵出土的金器在账册上登记为八万比索。1619年2月14日的大地震几乎毁城；1687至1690年间，为防御袭扰太平洋海岸的海盗，城外围起一道椭圆形城墙。甘蔗与小麦带来新的财富，1820年12月29日，地方长官何塞·贝尔纳多·德·塔格莱宣布特鲁希略独立，这是秘鲁的第一份独立宣言。

en:
Cajamarca sits in a fertile highland basin of the northern Andes, at about 2,750 metres where the Mashcón and Chonta rivers meet, with hot springs a short ride from the town. Its people were potters first of all: from about 200 BC they fired fine vessels of white kaolin at more than a thousand degrees, ware that has turned up in Wari cities near Cuzco and in Moche tombs on the coast. By the fifteenth century the valley was the chief seat of the lord Spanish accounts call Cuismanco, whose ruler bore the title Guzmango Capac. In 1444 Cajamarca was still a highland kingdom outside the Inca world, living by ceramics, llama herds and exchange with the coast, and the armies of Cuzco had not yet crossed the mountains.

The Inca generals Capac Yupanqui and his nephew Tupac Inca Yupanqui took the valley between 1463 and 1471, garrisoned it and rebuilt Kasha Marka on Inca lines, making it a quartering place on the highway between Quito and Cuzco. The war between Huascar and Atahualpa split its lords, and in November 1532 Atahualpa himself was camped at the hot springs after defeating his brother. On the 16th fewer than two hundred Spaniards under Francisco Pizarro drew his unarmed following into the plaza, killed thousands within hours and carried off the Sapa Inca. From his room he promised to fill one chamber with gold and two more with silver, and precious metal poured in from every corner of the empire. Once it was melted down, he was baptised and strangled in Cajamarca on 26 July 1533.

Under Spanish rule the native lords kept their seven guarangas for a time, while their people owed rotating labour at the Chilete silver mines in the nearby hills. Reforms in 1574 and 1784 placed the town under the administration of Trujillo, and on 19 December 1802 Charles IV granted it the rank of city and seat of its province.
zh:
卡哈马卡坐落在安第斯山脉北部一片肥沃的高地盆地，海拔约2750米，马什孔河与琼塔河在这里汇合，出城不远就是温泉。这里的人首先以制陶立身：约自公元前200年起，他们用白色高岭土在千度以上高温中烧造精美陶器，这类器物在库斯科一带的瓦里城市和沿海的莫切墓葬里都有出土。到15世纪，谷地已是西班牙记载所称奎斯曼库领地的首邑，统治者号古斯曼戈·卡帕克。1444年的卡哈马卡还是印加世界之外的高地王国，靠陶器、美洲驼群和与沿海的交换为生，库斯科的大军尚未越过山岭。

1463至1471年间，印加将领卡帕克·尤潘基与其侄图帕克·印加·尤潘基攻占谷地，驻军屯守，按印加样式改建卡沙马卡，把它变成基多与库斯科之间大道上的屯驻要地。瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕的内战分裂了当地首领；1532年11月，刚击败兄长的阿塔瓦尔帕正驻营于温泉。11月16日，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗手下不到两百名西班牙人把他手无寸铁的随从诱入广场，几小时内杀死数千人，掳走了这位萨帕·印卡。被囚于一室期间，他答应用黄金填满一间房、再用白银填满两间房，金银从帝国各个角落源源运来。财物熔尽之后，他在受洗后于1533年7月26日在卡哈马卡被绞死。

西班牙统治下，当地首领一度保留七个瓜兰卡的建制，其部众则须轮班到附近山里的奇列特银矿服役。1574年和1784年的改制把此镇划归特鲁希略管辖；1802年12月19日，卡洛斯四世赐其城市地位，并定为省治。

en:
Huanuco covers the high corridor between the Marañón and the Huallaga, where cold pasture drops through maize valleys towards the Amazon forests. At Kotosh stands the Temple of the Crossed Hands, raised around 2500 BC and among the oldest ceremonial buildings in the Andes. The lords of Yarowilca built a regional power on these heights and barred the road up from Cuzco, so in 1444 the country was still in local hands and no Inca garrison sat on it.

The Incas broke in later in the century and laid out Huánuco Pampa on a plateau above the Vizcarra river, ringed by ravines, on the Cuzco–Quito highway. Storehouses and an ushnu platform stood around its great square, and officials posted there ruled at least five subject peoples; the maidens of Pillco were sent south to Cuzco as acllas. The Spanish town Gómez de Alvarado founded beside the ruins in August 1539 lasted barely a year, abandoned to the raids of Manco Inca's captain Illa Túpac and to the plateau's cold. Pedro Barroso re-founded it 140 kilometres away in the warm Pillco valley among the Chupacho on 2 February 1541, and after the conquistadors' wars emptied it again Pedro de Puelles settled it for good in 1543 as León de Huánuco; Charles V granted it arms and the style 'Most Noble and Most Loyal' that August. Its valleys became a granary of the intendancy of Tarma. In 1812 the district's Indians rose, criollos and clergy joined them and a junta sat in the town until royal troops put it down; on 15 December 1820 Huanuco proclaimed independence.
zh:
瓦努科位于马拉尼翁河与瓦亚加河之间的高原走廊，寒冷的牧场向下过渡为种植玉米的河谷，再往低处便是亚马孙丛林。科托什的交叉双手庙约建于公元前2500年，是安第斯最古老的礼仪建筑之一。亚罗维尔卡人的首领在这片高原上建起地域性政权，长期封住从库斯科北上的道路，因此1444年时这片土地仍在本地人手中，没有驻扎过印加军队。

15世纪后期，印加人攻入此地，在比斯卡拉河上方、四围深沟的高原上营建瓦努科潘帕；它坐落在库斯科至基多的王家大道上，大广场周围设有仓库和乌什努祭台，驻守的官员统辖至少五个臣属族群，比尔科的少女则被送往南方的库斯科充任太阳贞女。1539年8月，戈麦斯·德·阿尔瓦拉多在遗址旁建起西班牙城镇，但只维持了不到一年：曼科·印卡的将领伊利亚·图帕克不断袭扰，高原上又寒气逼人，定居者弃城而去。1541年2月2日，佩德罗·巴罗索在140公里外温暖的比尔科河谷、楚帕乔人之地重建此城；征服者的内战使它再度荒废，直到1543年佩德罗·德·普埃列斯才把它最终安定下来，定名莱昂·德·瓦努科，同年8月查理五世颁赐城徽和「最高贵、最忠诚」的称号。这里的河谷后来成为塔尔马监政区的粮仓。1812年，本地印第安人起事，土生白人和教士相继加入，还在城中成立自治政权，最终被王军镇压；1820年12月15日，瓦努科宣布独立。

en:
The Nanay, Amazon and Itaya rivers and Lake Moronacocha enclose a country of blackwater channels, forest flooded for months each year and raised groves that keep above the water. At European contact the Napeano, also called Yameo, and the Iquito lived along these waterways in small seasonal camps, fishing, hunting and moving with the river's rise and fall; in the Iquito language their name means 'a multitude separated by the waters'. They kept no roads or towns, and kin groups shifted freely between rivers. In 1444 canoes were the only traffic on these channels, and no outsider ruled the forest.

From 1638 Jesuits sent from Quito gathered the peoples of the Marañón basin into reductions, moving a village upstream or downstream as war, sickness or better ground demanded and rebuilding it, often under the same name. Father José Bahamonde founded a string of Iquito missions from 1740. His station of San Pablo de los Napeanos, set on the Nanay by 1757, ran to poultry pens, cattle, goats and pigs, a mill crushing cane for molasses and brandy, a carpenter's shop and a school for the children. The village was moved to its later site in 1764 and renamed San Pablo de Nuevo Napeanos. Three years later Charles III expelled the Jesuits from Spanish America; without their fathers the missions emptied, the Napeano families drifted away, and by the end of the century the place was known simply as the hamlet of Iquitos. In 1821 it was still a scatter of mission huts and river landings on a forest edge no garrison had ever bothered to hold.
zh:
纳奈河、亚马孙河、伊塔亚河与莫罗纳科查湖环抱的低地，布满黑水河汊、一年被水淹上数月的林子和几处高出水面的树丛。欧洲人到来时，纳佩阿诺人（又称亚梅奥人）和伊基托斯人沿水道而居，住小型季节性营地，捕鱼打猎，随河水涨落搬迁；在伊基托斯语里，「伊基托斯」的意思是「被水分开的人群」。他们没有道路和城镇，亲族群体在各条河之间自由迁居。1444年，水道上只有独木舟往来，森林不受外人统治。

1638年起，基多派来的耶稣会士把马拉尼翁盆地的诸族归入传教村；遇上战事、疫病或更好的土地，就把整村往上游或下游搬，换个地方还常沿用旧名重建。何塞·巴哈蒙德神父从1740年起连建数座伊基托斯传教站。他在纳奈河畔的纳佩亚诺斯的圣巴勃罗站到1757年已养起家禽、牛、山羊和猪，设有榨甘蔗制糖蜜和烧酒的磨坊、木工坊和一所儿童学校。村落1764年迁到后来的城址，改名新纳佩亚诺斯的圣巴勃罗。三年后卡洛斯三世把耶稣会逐出西属美洲，传教站没了神父日渐空落，纳佩阿诺家庭陆续散去，到世纪末这里只叫伊基托斯小村。1821年，它仍是森林边缘一片零散的传教茅屋和河边泊点，从无驻军愿意来此把守。

en:
Tumbes lies at the mouth of its river on the Gulf of Guayaquil, the northernmost town of the Peruvian coast. Its people, the Tumpis, were the ablest seafarers of that shore: they fished and traded far along the Pacific on balsa rafts and carved the red, spiny Spondylus shells carried as offerings across the Andes. By the fifteenth century their valley had been absorbed into the Chimú state, and in 1444 Tumbes was its outpost facing the still-free peoples to the north. Within a generation Inca armies reached the gulf; the emperors garrisoned the frontier there, and Huayna Cápac had roads, houses and palaces built. In the war between Huáscar and Atahualpa the Tumpis took Huáscar's side, and Atahualpa's troops wasted their lands.

In 1528 Francisco Pizarro landed at Tumbes on his second voyage, the first well-built Inca town his men had seen; two local boys, Felipillo and Yacané, learned Castilian there and became his first interpreters. When he came back in 1532, putting in at Puerto La Leña, the curaca Chilimaza met him with a fight at the Manglares, and Pizarro afterwards set a cross on the beach now called La Cruz. The crown attached Tumbes to the Audiencia of Quito by the decree of 1563, and it stayed a quiet frontier town until its people proclaimed independence on 7 January 1821 and chose to join Peru.
zh:
通贝斯位于通贝斯河注入瓜亚基尔湾的河口，是秘鲁沿海最北端的城镇。当地的通皮斯人是这片海岸最出色的水手，乘巴尔萨木筏在太平洋上远航捕鱼、互通贸易，还雕刻红色多棘的海菊蛤贝壳，这种贝壳作为供品远销安第斯各地。15世纪，通贝斯谷地被并入奇穆国家；1444年时，它是奇穆面向北方未臣服诸族的前哨。不出一代人，印加大军开抵海湾，皇帝们在此屯守边疆，瓦伊纳·卡帕克还下令修筑道路、房舍和宫殿。瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕开战后，通皮斯人站在瓦斯卡尔一边，阿塔瓦尔帕的军队践踏了他们的土地。

1528年，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗在第二次远航中登陆通贝斯，这是部下见过的第一座规整的印加城镇；本地少年费利皮略和亚卡内在此学会西班牙语，成了他最早的两名译员。1532年他从莱尼亚港重返时，酋长奇利马萨在红树林一带迎战，战后皮萨罗在后来得名拉克斯的海滩竖起十字架。1563年的王室敕令把通贝斯划归基多检审法院，此后它一直是座安静的边镇，直到1821年1月7日宣布独立、选择加入秘鲁。

en:
The temperate basin where Cuenca stands, 2,550 metres high and crossed by four rivers, was the country of the Cañari; their name joins kan, the serpent, and ara, the macaw, the two animals their stories made the ancestors of the people. They farmed the valley in a dense scatter of villages and sent its gold, copper and coca down to the coast, a loose confederation of caciques who fortified the ridges facing Cuzco. Their chief town, Guapondelig, means a plain as wide as the sky. In 1444 the Cañari still ruled themselves, one of the strongest peoples of the northern Andes, and no Inca road yet crossed their land.

Túpac Yupanqui's armies ended that. United under a chief named Dumma, the Cañari held the high passes and beat off the first Inca attack near Saraguro; they yielded only when the Inca brought up reinforcements from across the empire and demanded their leaders' children as hostages. Cuzco then rebuilt Guapondelig as Tumebamba, the 'second Cuzco', with palaces and temples, and there Huayna Cápac, son of Túpac Yupanqui, was born. On the bare uplands north of the city the garrison at Ingapirca guarded the road to Quito; its elliptical sun temple was built without mortar around a single living rock. In the war between Huáscar and Atahualpa the Cañari chose Huáscar, and after Atahualpa's victory at Chimborazo he reached Tumebamba, executed their leaders and sacked the city. The survivors served Pizarro as guides and auxiliaries through the Andes.

On 12 April 1557 Captain Gil Ramírez Dávalos, acting on the viceroy's order, founded Santa Ana de los Ríos de Cuenca beside the ruins, naming it after the city of Cuenca in Spain, with the local caciques in attendance. The town grew rich on textiles and metalwork, became a diocese in 1769 and a gobernación under the Viceroyalty of New Granada in 1777. The French Geodesic Mission arrived in 1730, and Charles Marie de La Condamine surveyed and described Ingapirca in 1739, the first European to do so. On 3 November 1820 the Cuencans disarmed their Spanish garrison and proclaimed independence; royalist troops retook the town before the year was out.
zh:
昆卡所在的温和盆地海拔2550米，四条河穿流其间，古时是卡尼亚里人的故土。他们的名字由「kan」（蛇）和「ara」（金刚鹦鹉）拼成，口传故事把这两种动物奉为族人的祖先。盆地里村落密布，出产的黄金、红铜和古柯顺山路销往沿海；各酋邦结成松散联盟，在面向库斯科的山脊上遍筑堡垒。主城瓜庞德立格的意思是「宽如天空的平原」。1444年的卡尼亚里仍由自己的酋长统治，是安第斯北部最强悍的族群之一，印加的道路还没有伸进他们的土地。

图帕克·尤潘基的大军结束了这种局面。卡尼亚里人共推敦马为首领，扼守山口，在萨拉古罗附近击退了印加人的第一次进攻；直到对方从帝国各地调来援军，并要求各酋长送儿子为质，他们才归降。库斯科随后把瓜庞德立格改建为图梅班巴，号称「第二库斯科」，宫殿神庙林立，图帕克之子瓦伊纳·卡帕克就出生在这里。城北方荒凉的高地上，因加皮尔卡（Ingapirca）的驻军把守着通往基多的道路，卫城中的太阳神庙不用灰浆，绕一整块原生岩石凿成。内战中卡尼亚里选择了瓦斯卡尔，阿塔瓦尔帕在钦博拉索取胜后进抵图梅班巴，处死他们的首领，洗劫了这座城。幸存者为皮萨罗充当向导和辅助兵，引他穿越安第斯山。

1557年4月12日，希尔·拉米雷斯·达瓦洛斯上尉奉总督之命，在废墟旁建立圣安娜·德·洛斯·里奥斯·德·昆卡，以西班牙的昆卡为新城命名，本地酋长也到场参加。城市靠纺织和金属加工富足起来，1769年设教区，1777年成为新格拉纳达总督区治下的州。法国大地测量队1730年到达昆卡，夏尔·马里·德·拉孔达米纳1739年测绘并记述了因加皮尔卡，是第一个这样做的欧洲人。1820年11月3日，昆卡人制服西班牙驻军，宣布独立；当年年底之前，王党的军队又夺回了城池。

en:
Canelos begins east of the Andean gap at Baños, where the Pastaza, Puyo, Pindo and Bobonaza rivers run through forested foothills toward the Amazon. In 1444 the riverside clearings held the farmers, fishers and potters later drawn together as the Canelos Quichua, while Zápara, Achuar and Jívaro-speaking bands moved through the same basins. The woods yielded the aromatic cinnamon bark the Spaniards called canela, and they named the country after it; dugout canoes on the rivers, not Andean roads, carried what trade there was.

Dominicans came over the Baños trail early in the seventeenth century, and Sebastián Rosero, who opened the route, had baptized thirty-five local people by 1631. The mission led a hunted life. Jívaro raids forced the village to move twice, and later shifts followed the best cinnamon grounds and fishing water. The families never settled at the station for long and spent much of the year at their riverside farm plots, the purina; a 1707 account found Canelos empty for most of the year, and around 1712 Father Ignacio de Santa María gathered the people on the Bobonaza under Saint Joseph after an unhealthy site and an epidemic had driven some twenty-five families downstream. In 1725 the Dominicans sent twenty Canelos families to open a new mission on the Curaray. Through that century Canelos was a meeting ground for the peoples of the Andes and the forest, drawing Zápara families from the Napo and Curaray, Achuar refugees who married into the village, and occasional Shuar visitors. The Dominicans were called back to the mission in 1821.
zh:
卡内洛斯起于安第斯山口巴尼奥斯以东，帕斯塔萨河、普约河、平多河与博博纳萨河流经林覆山麓，奔向亚马孙。1444年，河畔林中空地上住着后来融合成卡内洛斯克丘亚人的农人、渔民和制陶人，萨帕拉、阿丘阿尔和操希瓦罗语的游群也往来于同一水系。林子里出产香气浓郁的肉桂皮，西班牙人叫它「卡内拉」，就用它给这片地方命名；往来贸易靠的是河上独木舟，而不是安第斯山路。

17世纪初，多明我会士沿巴尼奥斯山道而来，开辟这条路的塞瓦斯蒂安·罗塞罗到1631年已为三十五名当地人施洗。传教站屡受冲击，希瓦罗人的袭击迫使村落两度迁移，后来几次搬迁则追着最好的肉桂林和渔场走。居民本也不长住站上，一年里大半时间待在河畔的自耕地「普里纳」；1707年的一份记述称卡内洛斯一年多数时候空无一人。约1712年，一处居址环境恶劣又闹疫病，约二十五户人家顺流迁走，伊格纳西奥·德·圣玛丽亚神父才把众人聚到博博纳萨河畔，以圣若瑟为主保。1725年，多明我会派二十户卡内洛斯家庭前往库拉赖河另开新传教站。整个18世纪，卡内洛斯是安第斯山民与森林诸族的会合地，吸引从纳波河和库拉赖河来的萨帕拉家庭、与本村通婚的阿丘阿尔难民，还有偶尔到访的舒阿尔人。1821年，多明我会士又被召回主持这个传教站。

en:
The marshy shores and mangrove channels where the Guayas River opens into its gulf were the country of the Huancavilcas, whom their Manteño kinsmen called the southern Manteños, with the Chonos holding the river mouths. They fished, built rafts and traded on large balsa craft as far south as Peru and, it was said, north to Mexico, paying in copper axe-money and in the red Spondylus shell their smiths treated as sacred, and their goldsmiths also cast gold masks. Neither Quito nor Cuzco ruled their islands, and in 1444 the villages answered to their own caciques.

The first Spaniards came from Paita with Sebastián de Benalcázar in 1534; the Chonos burned their town and killed nearly half its people. Hernando de Zaera rebuilt it in 1536 and Francisco de Orellana moved it in 1537, but a league of Chonos and Punaes besieged it for six months in 1541, the Huancavilcas destroyed it in 1543, and only on 25 July 1547 was Santiago de Guayaquil, named for the chono cacique Guayaquile, fixed on its final site. Its timber and sheltered water made it the principal shipyard of the Armada del Mar del Sur in the seventeenth century and a port of call in the Manila galleon trade between Acapulco and Callao. That wealth drew Cavendish in 1586 and the Dutchman l'Heremite in 1624; Dampier's party burned much of the town in 1684, French corsairs sacked it and fired its main buildings in 1687, and the town was then rebuilt behind forts on the hills. Rogers and Dampier returned in 1709 and withdrew before a yellow-fever outbreak. From the 1770s the cacao estates made Guayaquil one of the world's largest cacao ports, known as the city of cacao.

On 9 October 1820 townsmen backed by a battalion of the garrison arrested the Spanish authorities almost without bloodshed, and on 8 November the Free Province of Guayaquil was proclaimed, with José Joaquín de Olmedo at its head.
zh:
瓜亚斯河注入海湾处，沼泽海岸与红树林水道纵横，这里是万卡维尔卡人的土地，曼特尼奥亲族把他们叫作「南曼特尼奥人」，河口一带还住着乔诺人。他们捕鱼、造筏，驾着大型巴尔萨木筏南下秘鲁、据说北抵墨西哥通商，交易用铜铸的斧币和工匠视为圣物的红色海菊蛤贝壳，金匠还铸有金面具。基多和库斯科都管不到这些岛屿，1444年时各村庄只听命于自己的酋长。

1534年，塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝纳尔卡萨尔从派塔率首批西班牙人来此定居，乔诺人烧毁村镇，杀死近半居民。埃尔南多·德·萨埃拉1536年重建，弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳1537年再迁城址；1541年乔诺人与普纳人联手围城六个月，1543年万卡维尔卡人把城彻底摧毁，直到1547年7月25日，圣地亚哥·德·瓜亚基尔才固定在最后的城址，城名来自乔诺酋长瓜亚基莱。丰富的木材和避风的水面，使它在17世纪成为南海军最主要的造船厂，也是阿卡普尔科与卡亚俄之间马尼拉大帆船贸易的停靠港。这份财富引来一批又一批海盗：卡文迪什1586年来袭，荷兰人勒里米特1624年来袭，1684年丹皮尔一伙放火烧掉大半个城，1687年法国海盗洗劫之后又把主要建筑付之一炬，城市这才迁到山丘要塞之后重建。1709年罗杰斯与丹皮尔再度来攻，却因黄热病流行撤走。1770年代起，可可种植园让瓜亚基尔成为世界最大的可可输出港之一，人称「可可城」。

1820年10月9日，市民在驻防军一个大队的支持下逮捕西班牙当局，几乎兵不血刃；11月8日，瓜亚基尔自由省宣告成立，由何塞·华金·德·奥尔梅多领导。

en:
At more than 2,800 metres on the eastern skirts of the Pichincha volcano, the Quito basin is a high, cold and fertile valley of the Guayllabamba. Since the sixth century the Quitu, a loose confederation of small chiefdoms akin to the Cara, had farmed its terraces and carried obsidian down to the coast, and the deep painted tombs of La Florida show the wealth of their lords. In 1444 the country was still a patchwork of rival highland lordships beyond the Inca frontier. Túpac Yupanqui's armies crossed it later in the century and Quito became the Incas' northern stronghold; when Huayna Capac died, his son Atahualpa held the north from here against Huascar in Cuzco.

After Atahualpa's execution the rumour that his treasure lay at Quito drew two Spanish expeditions, Alvarado's from Guatemala and Belalcázar's from the south. The Inca general Rumiñahui burned the city and hid its gold before the Spaniards reached it, and under torture he never said where it lay. On 6 December 1534 Belalcázar founded San Francisco de Quito beside the ashes. In 1541 Gonzalo Pizarro outfitted an expedition here in search of the cinnamon country and El Dorado; his lieutenant Orellana descended to the Amazon and followed it to the sea. Philip II made Quito the seat of a Real Audiencia in 1563.

The city grew rich on the woollen cloth of its obrajes, shipped to New Spain and Peru, and on religious art. The Franciscan Jodoco Ricke opened a school of arts in 1552 that trained Indian sculptors and painters, and the polychrome saints of the Quito School, above all the work of Manuel Chili, called Caspicara, were bought even for European churches; Charles III said that if Italy had Michelangelo, he had Caspicara in his American colonies. In 1736 La Condamine, Bouguer and Godin, with the Spaniards Jorge Juan and Ulloa, arrived to measure a degree of the meridian on the equator. A rising against the Bourbon tobacco and brandy monopolies drove the royal officials from the city in 1765. On 10 August 1809 the criollo elite set up an autonomous junta in the name of the deposed Ferdinand VII, among the earliest such moves in the Spanish empire; royalist troops retook Quito and in August 1810 killed the junta's leaders and some three hundred citizens, and the city still held for the king in 1821.
zh:
基多盆地海拔超过2800米，坐落在皮钦查火山东麓，是盖亚班巴河流域一片高寒而肥沃的谷地。自6世纪起，基图人这个由小酋邦组成、与卡拉人相近的松散联盟便在此耕种梯田，把黑曜石贩运到沿海，拉佛罗里达的彩绘深墓显示出其首领的财富。1444年时，这一带仍是彼此争雄的高原小邦犬牙交错之地，处在印加边界之外。该世纪晚些时候，图帕克·尤潘基的大军越过边界，基多成为印加的北方重镇；瓦伊纳·卡帕克死后，其子阿塔瓦尔帕正是以这里为据点，同库斯科的瓦斯卡尔相争。

阿塔瓦尔帕被处死后，他的财宝藏在基多的传闻引来两支西班牙远征队，一支是阿尔瓦拉多从危地马拉出发，一支是贝拉尔卡萨尔从南方而来。印加守将鲁米尼亚维在西班牙人到达前焚城并藏起黄金，被俘后遭受酷刑，却始终不吐露藏宝之处。1534年12月6日，贝拉尔卡萨尔在灰烬旁建立圣弗朗西斯科·德·基多。1541年，贡萨洛·皮萨罗在这里装备远征队，去寻找肉桂之乡和黄金国，他的副将奥雷利亚纳顺河而下，驶入亚马孙河并直达河口。1563年，腓力二世在此设立检审庭。

城市靠织造作坊的毛呢销往新西班牙和秘鲁而致富，宗教艺术同样出名。方济各会士里克1552年开办工艺学校，培养印第安雕塑家和画家；基多画派的彩色圣像连远在欧洲的教堂也来求购，其中尤以曼努埃尔·奇利（人称卡斯皮卡拉）的作品最为抢手，卡洛斯三世曾说，意大利有米开朗基罗，他在美洲的殖民地就有卡斯皮卡拉。1736年，拉孔达明、布格、戈丹偕西班牙军官豪尔赫·胡安与乌略亚抵达，在赤道上测量子午线的一度。1765年，反对波旁王朝烟草与烧酒专卖的起义把王室官员逐出城市。1809年8月10日，土生白人上层以被废黜的费尔南多七世之名成立自治执政委员会，这是西班牙帝国境内最早的同类举动之一；保王军队重占基多，于1810年8月杀害委员会领袖和大约三百名市民，而1821年时基多仍在保王军手中。

en:
Quijos covers the wet cloud-forest valleys below the Antisana volcano, where the Quijos River runs into the Coca and then the upper Napo on the way to the Amazon. The Quijos farmed these slopes, hunted in the forest below and carried cinnamon bark and other forest goods up to the mountain markets, so that Quito knew the country beyond the eastern passes as the Cinnamon Country. They were warriors first: Spanish parties learned to return by different routes rather than meet Quijos spears twice. Inca power had reached only the edge of these valleys and spread some Quichua among them, but in 1444 local chiefs still ruled their own valleys and held the forest crossings on the road from Quito to the Napo.

In time gold joined cinnamon in the rumours coming out of the forest, and in 1540 Gonzalo Pizarro left Quito with several hundred Spaniards and several thousand native porters to conquer the Cinnamon Country and find El Dorado. Around Sumaco the expedition found only scattered cinnamon trees of poor quality; it struggled down the Coca to the Napo and there lost its second-in-command, Francisco de Orellana, sent ahead to find food. He was carried downstream so far that on 12 February 1542 he reached a river no European had sailed, the Amazon, and followed it all the way to the sea. Gil Ramírez Dávalos founded Baeza in 1559, the first Spanish town of the Ecuadorian Amazon, and the colonists enslaved the Quijos who had built it. Their answer came on 29 November 1578, when the war chief Jumandy led the villages in a general rising and burned Ávila and Archidona. Baeza held out, the highland chiefs the Quijos counted on turned against them, and Jumandy was taken and hanged and quartered in the San Blas square of Quito. A new rising planned for 1590 was betrayed before it began; the Quijos then chose flight over servitude, descending the rivers into the Peruvian forest or scattering south toward Canelos, and the old chiefdoms broke apart. Jesuits later ran the Napo missions from Archidona until the crown expelled them, while Baeza shrank to a half-empty staging post. In 1821 the forest still answered mostly to its own people.
zh:
奎约斯在安蒂萨纳火山东坡湿润的云雾林谷地，奎约斯河流入科卡河，再入纳波河上游，通向亚马孙。奎约斯人在坡地上耕作，到下方林中狩猎，把肉桂皮和其他林产物背到山地市集出售，基多人因此把东山口外的这片地方叫作「肉桂之乡」。他们首先是战士：西班牙队伍学会了换一条路撤回，免得二次撞上奎约斯人的长矛。印加势力只到达这些谷地的边缘，给他们带去一些克丘亚影响，但1444年时各谷地仍由本地酋长统治，基多通往纳波河路上的林中渡口也握在他们手中。

后来传出林子的消息里，黄金和肉桂并列。1540年，贡萨洛·皮萨罗率数百名西班牙人和数千名土著挑夫离开基多，要征服肉桂之乡、找到埃尔多拉多。远征队在苏马科一带只找到稀稀落落、品质低劣的肉桂树，沿科卡河挣扎到纳波河，还在那里失去了先行找粮的副将弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳。他顺流越走越远，在1542年2月12日抵达一条欧洲人从未航行过的大河，即亚马孙河，一路跟随它到了入海口。1559年，希尔·拉米雷斯·达瓦洛斯建立巴埃萨，这是厄瓜多尔亚马孙地区第一座西班牙城镇，殖民者随后把建城的奎约斯人沦为奴隶。1578年11月29日，战事首领胡曼迪率领各村总起义，烧毁阿维拉和阿奇多纳；巴埃萨守住了，奎约斯人寄望的高地酋长倒戈，胡曼迪被俘，在基多的圣布拉斯广场被处以绞刑并肢解。1590年，一次新的起义还没发动就被告发，奎约斯人宁可逃亡也不做奴隶，他们顺河而下进入秘鲁丛林，或四散南奔卡内洛斯方向，旧有的酋邦就此瓦解。后来耶稣会士以阿奇多纳为基地主持纳波传教区，直到被王室驱逐，巴埃萨则败落成半空的中转站。1821年，这片森林大体仍由本地人自己做主。

en:
The Caquetá lands run from the foggy eastern foothills of the Andes down to the black-water rivers of the Amazon forest. The Caguán, Orteguaza and Mocoa rivers tie its scattered villages together, but in 1444 no road, mission or encomienda reaches them. Autonomous Andaquí, Koreguaje, Tama and Macaguaje communities hold the forest and its waters, and the foothill ground later called Mocoa is known to the Kamëntšá as Shatjok.

The hunt for El Dorado brought the first Spaniards. Hernán Pérez de Quesada entered these forests in 1542, with Georg Hohermuth von Speyer crossing the same ground, and after two years Quesada marched out again with no treasure and no lasting post. Captain Gonzalo H. de Avendaño founded Mocoa as San Miguel de Agreda de Mocoa on 29 September 1563, but the frontier held him poorly: Andaquí warriors burned the town almost to the ground in 1630, and the survivors moved it to the banks of the Mocoa. The independence leader José Acevedo y Gómez ended his life here. He had drafted the text of the act of independence of 20 July 1810 and was called the Tribune of the People; hunted by the royalists, he died in 1817 near Belén de los Andaquíes, sheltered in his last illness by an indigenous family.
zh:
卡克塔从云雾低垂的安第斯东麓延伸到亚马逊雨林的黑水河地带，卡关河、奥尔特瓜萨河和莫科阿河把分散的村落串在一起。1444年，这里还没有道路、传教站或监护领地，林中与河畔居住着安达基、科雷瓜赫、塔马和马卡瓜赫等自治族群；后来得名莫科阿的山麓之地，卡门查人称之为沙特霍克。

寻找黄金国的热潮带来了第一批西班牙人。1542年，埃尔南·佩雷斯·德·克萨达进入丛林，格奥尔格·霍赫穆特·冯·施派尔也穿过同一地带；两年后克萨达空手撤出，没有留下任何据点。1563年9月29日，贡萨洛·H·德·阿文达尼奥船长建立圣米格尔·德·阿格雷达·德·莫科阿，但这条边疆并不容他站稳：1630年，安达基战士几乎将莫科阿焚毁，幸存者把城镇迁到莫科阿河畔。独立运动领袖何塞·阿塞韦多-戈麦斯也死在这片土地上。他执笔起草了1810年7月20日独立法令的文本，人称「人民护民官」；为躲避保王派追捕，他1817年在贝伦·德·洛斯安达基斯附近病故，临终由一户原住民家庭收留。

en:
The province follows the Cauca through its broad middle valley, a warm belt of maize fields and river gold between the Western and Central cordilleras, then crosses the wet western slope to mangrove estuaries on the Pacific. The Gorrones held much of the valley before the Spaniards came and traded with the Quimbaya to the north; the Jamundí and Petecuy peoples controlled lands farther south, while earlier Calima chiefdoms had farmed maize and yuca and worked gold along smaller rivers. Beyond the cordillera, Chocó-speaking families fished the coastal lagoons. In 1444 the valley was divided among village chiefs, with gold ornaments but no Spanish towns.

Sebastián de Belalcázar entered the valley from the south in 1536 after taking Quito. The Petecuy brought together a large indigenous army, and the Jamundí fought the invaders with poisoned arrows, but Spanish arquebuses and swords broke the resistance. Belalcázar founded Santiago de Cali on 25 July 1536 north of its later site, and Captain Miguel Muñoz moved the town the next year. Because the Cauca valley lay outside the Inca Empire, Belalcázar claimed it as his own jurisdiction rather than as part of Pizarro's Peruvian conquest. Cali first served as seat of the governorship of Popayán, until Belalcázar moved the administration to higher, cooler Popayán in 1540. In the same year Juan Ladrillero opened the Pacific anchorage of Buenaventura. Indians destroyed that early settlement before 1600, but a colonial mule road later linked the rebuilt port with Cali and the mining valleys. Cattle ranches and sugar haciendas spread around Cali; Indian communities and enslaved Africans did most of the forced labour, and runaway-slave palenques were raiding roads near the city by 1580.

Cali moved quickly in the wars against Spain. Its junta of 3 July 1810 acted seventeen days before Bogotá, and the linked towns of the Cauca valley defeated a royalist army at Bajo Palacé on 28 March 1811, the first pitched battle of the New Granadan independence movement. Pablo Morillo's expedition restored royal control by 1816. Simón Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 let the creoles of the valley take lasting control.
zh:
考卡这片地方沿考卡河中游展开，西安第斯山脉与中科迪勒拉山夹出一带暖热的农田和砂金河道；向西翻过湿润的山岭，则是太平洋沿岸的红树林河口。西班牙人到来前，戈龙人占据谷地大部，与北方的金巴亚人交易；哈蒙迪人和佩特库伊人控制南部土地，更早的卡利马酋邦长期种植玉米和木薯，并在小河旁制作金器。山岭西侧，说乔科语的族群在潟湖捕鱼。1444年，河谷由各村卡西克分治，有金饰而无西班牙城镇。

1536年，塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔夺取基多后从南方进入谷地。佩特库伊集合起一支庞大的印第安军队，哈蒙迪人则用毒箭抵抗，但西班牙人的火绳枪和刀剑击溃了他们。7月25日，贝拉尔卡萨尔建立圣地亚哥·德·卡利，地点在后来城址以北；次年米格尔·穆尼奥斯上尉把城镇南迁。由于考卡河谷不在印加帝国境内，贝拉尔卡萨尔把它当作自己的辖区，而不是皮萨罗征服的秘鲁的一部分。卡利最初是波帕扬督军辖区的治所，1540年贝拉尔卡萨尔才把行政机构迁到更高、更凉爽的波帕扬。同年，胡安·拉德里列罗在太平洋岸开辟布埃纳文图拉锚地。早期定居点在1600年前被印第安人摧毁，后来一条殖民骡道把重建的港口与卡利和各采矿河谷连接起来。卡利周围出现牧牛场和甘蔗种植园，强迫劳役主要落在印第安社群和黑奴身上；到1580年，逃亡黑奴的帕伦克已在城边道路上袭扰。

反西战争开始后，卡利行动得很快。1810年7月3日，当地成立洪达，比波哥大早十七天；1811年3月28日，考卡河谷结盟城镇在下巴拉塞击败保王军，这是新格拉纳达独立运动的第一场对阵战。巴勃罗·莫里略的远征军到1816年恢复了王室统治。1819年玻利瓦尔在博亚卡取胜后，河谷中的克里奥尔人掌握了持久控制权。

en:
The middle Magdalena valley is a hot lowland watered by the Gualí and Mariquita rivers below the Cordillera Central, and in 1444 it was Panche country. The Panche, whom their neighbours also called Tolimas, were a warlike people culturally close to the Caribs, whose raids reached the Muisca highlands to the east. At the Salto de Honda, rapids break the navigation of the great river, and indigenous traders had long trans-shipped cargo there between the Caribbean lowlands and the Andes; the villages at the landing belonged to their Gualí and Ondaima kinsmen and answered only to their own caciques.

Conquistadors entered the region in the late 1530s, and in 1551 Captain Francisco Núñez Pedroso founded San Sebastián de Mariquita, naming it after the local cacique Marequita. Gold and silver mines made the town's fortune, and Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada, the conqueror of New Granada, died there in 1579 and was buried in its church before his remains were later carried to Bogotá. Below the town lay the river port of Honda, where every passenger and cargo between Cartagena and Santafé changed vessels around the rapids; in 1643 the port's merchants paid 5,000 pesos to have it raised to a villa by Philip IV. The warm climate made Mariquita the viceroys' favourite summer retreat. In 1783 Charles III seated his Royal Botanical Expedition there under José Celestino Mutis, who studied the local flora with criollo naturalists including Francisco José de Caldas, and the educational reformer Francisco Antonio Moreno y Escandón was born in the town. During the Patria Boba the Province of Mariquita declared independence, with José León Armero as president and Honda as its capital, until royalist forces retook it in 1815.
zh:
马格达莱纳河中游是一片炎热低地，瓜利河与马里基塔河在中部山脉脚下穿流而过；1444年，这里是潘切人的土地。潘切人又称托利马人，勇武好战，文化上接近加勒比人，兵锋曾远及东面的穆伊斯卡高原。马格达莱纳河在翁达险滩断航，早在欧洲人到来之前，土著商人就在此将货物换船，往来于加勒比低地与安第斯山之间，滩头的村落属于潘切人的瓜利和翁达伊马亲族，只听命于本族酋长。

1530年代末，西班牙征服者进入这一地区。1551年，弗朗西斯科·努涅斯·佩德罗索船长建立圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·马里基塔，以当地酋长马雷基塔的名字命名。金银矿开采让城镇富足起来：1579年，新格拉纳达的征服者贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达在此去世，葬在当地教堂，遗骨后来才迁往波哥大。城下方的河港翁达扼守险滩，往来卡塔赫纳与圣菲波哥大的旅客货物都要在此换船；1643年，港中商人凑了5000比索，从费利佩四世处买到市镇封号。温暖的气候让马里基塔成为总督们偏爱的避暑地。1783年，卡洛斯三世把皇家植物考察队设在这里，由何塞·塞莱斯蒂诺·穆蒂斯主持，他与弗朗西斯科·何塞·德·卡尔达斯等土生白人学者一道研究当地植物；推动教育改革的弗朗西斯科·安东尼奥·莫雷诺-埃斯坎东也出生于此。「傻瓜祖国」时期，马里基塔省宣布独立，何塞·莱昂·阿梅罗出任总统，以翁达为都，1815年被保王派军队收复。

en:
The cool Bogotá savanna is a high basin ringed by the eastern Andes, where Chibcha-speaking Muisca kept maize fields and potato plots and were divided between the zipa of the south and the zacque of the north. In 1444 the zipa held court at Funza, within the chief territory called Bacatá. The Muisca worked no gold or emerald mines of their own: women rendered salt from brine, and four-day markets moved salt, cotton mantles and goldsmiths' work for the gold brought in by neighbouring peoples and the emeralds of the Muzo hills. At Lake Guatavita in the mountains to the north-east, a new zipa was rowed out on a rush raft coated in gold dust, and gold and emeralds were thrown into the water as offerings; Spaniards who later heard the tale called him El Dorado, the gilded man.

Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada climbed from the Magdalena into the highlands in 1537 and broke the zipa's power within months. Tisquesusa, the last independent zipa, was overtaken and killed, and his successor Sagipa died under torture without giving up the hidden treasure. On 6 August 1538 Quesada founded Santafé on the edge of the savanna; a Royal Audiencia sat there from 1550, and the town became capital of the New Kingdom of Granada. The treasure hunt moved to Guatavita: Lázaro Fonte and Hernán Pérez de Quesada cut a breach in the lake's rim to lower the water and gathered gold pieces from the exposed shores, yet the gilded king's hoard never surfaced. Santafé remained the seat of government when the Crown created, suppressed and restored the Viceroyalty of New Granada between 1717 and 1739. On 7 August 1819 Bolívar won the Battle of Boyacá nearby and entered the city three days later; viceregal rule collapsed, the old name Bogotá was restored, and the town became capital of Gran Colombia.
zh:
凉爽的波哥大高原是安第斯东脉环抱的高山盆地，说奇布查语的穆伊斯卡人在这里耕种玉米和马铃薯，族群分由两位首领统辖：南部的西帕和北部的萨克。1444年，西帕的宫廷设在巴卡塔境内的丰萨。穆伊斯卡本地不产金、不产祖母绿：妇女从盐卤中煮盐，四日一集的集市上用盐、棉布和金工，换取邻族带来的黄金和穆索山区的祖母绿。在东北山间的瓜塔维塔湖，新西帕继位时要乘芦苇筏入湖，全身涂满金粉，金器和祖母绿随之投入水中献祭；后来听到这个故事的西班牙人把他叫作埃尔多拉多，意为「镀金之人」。

1537年，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达从马格达莱纳河攀上高原，几个月内便击垮西帕的势力。末代独立西帕蒂斯克苏萨被追兵杀死，继他而立的萨希帕受尽酷刑，始终没有交出藏匿的宝藏。1538年8月6日，克萨达在高原边缘建起圣菲城；1550年起皇家审判院驻此，圣菲成为新格拉纳达王国的首府。寻宝者随后来到瓜塔维塔：拉萨罗·丰特和埃尔南·佩雷斯·德·克萨达挖开湖岸缺口降低水位，从出露的岸边拾得金器，金王投入湖底的大宗宝藏却始终没有出现。1717至1739年间，王室几度设立、裁撤又恢复新格拉纳达总督区，圣菲一直是首府。1819年8月7日，玻利瓦尔在附近赢得博亚卡战役，三日后入城；总督政权崩溃，城市恢复波哥大旧名，成为大哥伦比亚的首都。

en:
Chocó reaches from the Gulf of Urabá and the lower Atrato across some of the wettest forest on earth to the San Juan and Baudó rivers on the Pacific slope. In 1444 Guna villagers held the gulf and lower Atrato, Wounaan fished the San Juan, and Emberá groups such as the Baudó and Citarará lived upriver. They planted maize and yuca in clearings, hunted, fished, and washed gold from river gravel. Dugout canoes, not roads, joined their villages, and no Andean-style paramount chief ruled the region.

Rodrigo de Bastidas surveyed this coast in 1501. From nearby Santa María del Darién, Vasco Núñez de Balboa later crossed the isthmus to reach the Pacific, yet the rainforest kept Spanish settlers out of the upper rivers for more than a century. Franciscans received Emberá land at the future Quibdó in 1648, and missionary outposts, lumber camps and plantations slowly followed, often under attack and often worked by enslaved Africans. The crown organised the province of Chocó in 1739, with Nóvita as its capital, because river gold had become worth the cost of occupation.

The mines depended on enslaved labour. In 1728 a slave named Barule joined Antonio and Mateo Mina at the Tadó palenque, where about 120 cimarrones proclaimed him king; royal troops defeated the settlement and shot its leaders on 18 February. The same rivers carried grains of platinum, treated mainly as an impurity in gold workings until Antonio de Ulloa observed its mining during his voyage of 1735 and took samples to Spain. Chocó declared independence in 1813, royalist officers retook the mining towns during the reconquest, and patriot rule returned only after Boyacá in 1819.
zh:
乔科从乌拉瓦湾和阿特拉托河下游起，穿过地球上最湿润的几片雨林，向西直到太平洋坡的圣胡安河与包多河。1444年，库纳人住在海湾和阿特拉托河下游，沃南人在圣胡安河捕鱼，包多人、西塔拉拉人等埃姆贝拉支派居于上游。他们在林间空地种玉米和木薯，狩猎捕鱼，也从河砂中淘金。连接村落的是独木舟而不是道路，这里也没有安第斯式的至高首领。

1501年，罗德里戈·德·巴斯蒂达斯勘察这一带海岸。后来巴尔沃亚从附近的圣玛利亚·拉安提瓜·德尔达连出发，穿过地峡到达太平洋；但在此后一百多年里，雨林仍把西班牙移民挡在上游各河之外。1648年，方济各会在后来的基布多取得埃姆贝拉人的土地，传教站、伐木营和种植园才慢慢出现，它们屡遭攻击，劳作则常由黑奴承担。1739年，王室设立乔科省，以诺维塔为省会；河砂里的黄金已经值得西班牙人付出占领的代价。

矿区依靠奴隶劳动。1728年，黑奴巴鲁莱与安东尼奥·米纳、马特奥·米纳兄弟在塔多帕伦克聚集约一百二十名西马龙人，巴鲁莱被拥为王；保王军攻破据点，于2月18日枪杀了这些首领。这些河流还带出白金颗粒，在安东尼奥·德·乌略亚1735年航行途中见到开采并把样本带回西班牙以前，矿场多把它当作黄金里的杂质。乔科1813年宣布独立，再征服期间保王军官夺回矿镇，直到1819年博亚卡战役后爱国军才恢复统治。

en:
In 1444 the canyon of the Cauca and the neighbouring valleys of western Antioquia were the country of the Nutabe, who farmed maize, beans and cotton on the hillsides, fished the rivers and washed alluvial gold from their gravels; the Tahamí lived beyond the Porce, between it and the Magdalena. All the region's gold was still in indigenous hands.

Spaniards came for that gold. In August 1541 Jerónimo Luis Tejelo, a captain of Jorge Robledo, entered the Valle de Aburrá, its fields and gold-bearing Medellín river still worked entirely by indigenous hands, and that December Robledo founded the town of Antioquia in the Ebéjico valley. Hostile peoples drove the settlement from site to site, and after Robledo founded a second town, Santa Fe, in 1546 he was captured and put to death near Pácora by order of his rival Sebastián de Belalcázar, governor of Popayán, in their feud over the conquest. Gaspar de Rodas re-established Santa Fe and carried the mining frontier north through Cáceres and Zaragoza. After the Governorate of Antioquia was separated from Popayán, a royal cédula of Philip II on 30 October 1584 made the merged town, now called Santa Fe de Antioquia, the provincial capital. Its gold paid for luxuries carried up from Cartagena; the town received a cathedral in 1799 and became a bishop's see in 1804.

The famine of 1807 to 1809 had deepened the province's poverty when a provincial junta met at Santa Fe in 1810. A constitution was sworn at Rionegro in 1812, and on 11 August 1813 the dictator Juan del Corral proclaimed absolute independence. Colonel Warleta's royalists retook the province in 1816 and burned Remedios, until José María Córdova defeated them at Chorros Blancos, near Yarumal, in February 1820.
zh:
1444年，考卡河峡谷与安蒂奥基亚西部的一道道山谷是努塔韦人的家园。他们在坡地上种植玉米、菜豆和棉花，在河中捕鱼，从河沙里淘取砂金；塔阿米人住在波尔塞河与马格达莱纳河之间。这一带的黄金此时还全部掌握在土著人手中。

西班牙人正是为黄金而来。1541年8月，豪尔赫·罗夫莱多麾下的赫罗尼莫·路易斯·特赫洛进入阿武拉山谷，谷中农田和产金的麦德林河还完全由土著人经营；同年12月，罗夫莱多在埃韦希科谷建立安蒂奥基亚镇。土著的袭扰让新城几度迁址。1546年罗夫莱多另建圣菲镇，不出数月就在征服土地的管辖权之争中被对手、波帕扬省督塞巴斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔下令逮捕，在帕科拉附近处死。加斯帕尔·德·罗达斯重建圣菲，把采矿前沿经卡塞雷斯和萨拉戈萨向北推进。安蒂奥基亚都督府脱离波帕扬后，1584年10月30日费利佩二世颁布皇家敕令，将合并后的城镇（此时已称圣菲-德安蒂奥基亚）定为省城。此地出产的黄金偿付了从卡塔赫纳溯流运来的奢侈品；城镇1799年建起大教堂，1804年成为主教驻地。

1807年至1809年的饥荒让全省愈发贫困。1810年，各镇代表在圣菲组成省洪达；1812年在里奥内格罗宣誓颁布宪法；1813年8月11日，独裁官胡安·德尔科拉尔宣布完全独立。1816年，瓦莱塔上校率保王派焚毁雷梅迪奥斯、重新占领全省，直到1820年2月何塞·马里亚·科尔多瓦在亚鲁马尔附近的乔罗斯布兰科斯战役中将其击败。

en:
Cartagena Bay opens between the mouths of the Magdalena and the Sinú, one of the safest anchorages on the southern Caribbean shore. In 1444 its islands and inlets were held by Carib-speaking Mocana villagers: the Kalamarí on the sandy island where the walled city later rose, kindred villages on Tierrabomba, Barú and at inland Turbaco. They fished the bay, built circular huts with high roofs behind wooden palisades, and traded with the gold-working peoples up the Sinú. No European sail had yet entered these waters.

Pedro de Heredia founded Cartagena on the Kalamarí ground on 1 June 1533, naming it for Cartagena in Murcia. Guided by India Catalina, his men stripped the Sinú tombs of their gold; one haul held a solid-gold porcupine weighing 132 pounds. The town became the warehouse of the Carrera de Indias, where Potosí silver gathered for the Atlantic crossing and enslaved Africans were sold in the Plaza de los Coches. French raiders sacked the open town in 1544, and Francis Drake burned some two hundred houses and the cathedral in 1586, leaving after a month's ransom. Philip II then set Bautista Antonelli to plan the walls and the Castillo San Felipe de Barajas on San Lázaro hill, both raised over two centuries and finished in 1654. The Inquisition sat here from 1610 and read its sentences in the main plaza; in 1697 the Baron de Pointis's French fleet stormed the sea forts and plundered the city for a month.

The largest assault of all failed. In 1741 Edward Vernon arrived with about 180 ships and 25,000 men, 2,000 of them North American colonists, among them George Washington's half-brother Lawrence, who later named Mount Vernon for him. The defence rested on Blas de Lezo, an admiral who had lost an eye, a leg and the use of his right arm. His garrison repulsed the assault on San Felipe on 20 April, leaving eight hundred British dead, and Vernon sailed away. Cartagena declared independence on 11 November 1811 and the Inquisition closed with the old regime. Pablo Morillo retook it in December 1815 after a starvation siege that gave it the name Heroic City; Mariano Montilla's troops and José Prudencio Padilla's ships freed it on 10 October 1821.
zh:
卡塔赫纳湾开口在马格达莱纳河与锡努河的河口之间，是南美洲加勒比沿岸最安全的锚地之一。1444年，湾中的岛屿和水湾归说加勒比语的莫卡纳诸村：卡拉马里人住在后来老城区所在的沙岛上，铁拉邦巴岛、巴鲁岛和内陆的图尔瓦科还有同族村落。他们在湾中捕鱼，在木栅栏后盖起高顶圆屋，并与锡努河上游以金器闻名的族群贸易。此时还没有欧洲船帆驶入这片水域。

1533年6月1日，佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚在卡拉马里故地建立卡塔赫纳，以穆尔西亚的同名港口为它命名。他由印第安女子卡塔利娜引路，掘开锡努人的墓葬掠取黄金，一次所得中有一尊132磅重的纯金豪猪。不出一代人，此城成为西印度航线上的大仓库：波托西的白银在此集中，跨大西洋运往西班牙，非洲黑奴在马车广场上买卖。法国袭掠者1544年洗劫了不设防的城镇，弗朗西斯·德雷克1586年焚毁约两百座房屋和大教堂，收了一个月赎金才撤走。腓力二世遂命巴蒂斯塔·安东内利主持城防，城墙此后两百年间陆续修筑，圣拉萨罗山上的圣费利佩·德·巴拉哈斯城堡1654年完工。宗教裁判所自1610年在此设庭，在主广场宣读判决；1697年，普安蒂男爵的法国舰队连破海上要塞，洗劫城市达一个月。

规模最大的一次围攻却以失败收场。1741年，爱德华·弗农率约180艘船、2.5万人抵达，其中有两千名北美殖民地士兵，乔治·华盛顿的异母兄长劳伦斯也在其中，他后来便以弗农之名命名自己的庄园。守城的是布拉斯·德莱索，这位海军将军失去过一只眼睛、一条腿，右臂也无法活动。守军4月20日击退对圣费利佩城堡的强攻，英军陈尸八百，弗农只得扬帆撤走。1811年11月11日，卡塔赫纳宣布独立，宗教裁判所随旧政权一同关闭。1815年12月，巴勃罗·莫里略经饥饿围城夺回城市，卡塔赫纳因此得名「英雄之城」；1821年10月10日，马里亚诺·蒙蒂利亚的陆军与何塞·普鲁登西奥·帕迪利亚的舰队解放该城。

en:
The Caribbean shore and forested northern slopes below the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta were Tairo country, part of the wider Tairona group of Chibcha-related chiefdoms. Stone-paved paths and terraces joined coastal fishing and salt-making villages, yuca and maize fields, and high hamlets. Teyuna, the large settlement later called Ciudad Perdida, held 169 terraces, circular plazas and stone roads above the Buritaca River. In 1444 no single ruler commanded the whole country; each valley had its cacique, and families exchanged salt, pottery, stonework and gold objects between coast and sierra.

Spanish ships arrived in 1498, and Rodrigo de Bastidas founded Santa Marta on a nearby bay in 1525. Colonists soon demanded porters, gold and a road toward the highland savanna, and the frontier turned to war. In 1551 Pedro de Ursúa's expedition was broken at the Paso de Origua, with only thirteen soldiers returning. Tairona warriors burned Santa Marta several times, took Fort Bonhida and traded with English and French corsairs. Governor Juan Guiral Velón campaigned through the valleys in 1599 and 1600, executing caciques and assigning captured villagers to encomiendas around Santa Marta. Teyuna was abandoned during those years. Communities that withdrew into the highest ranges kept their laws and rituals, and their descendants include the Kogi, Wiwa, Arhuaco and Kankuamo peoples.
zh:
玛格达莱娜的加勒比海岸与圣玛尔塔内华达山脉北坡的森林山地，是泰罗人的土地，属于范围更大、同属奇布查语系的泰罗纳诸酋长领地。石铺道路和台地连接沿海捕鱼、制盐的村落，木薯与玉米田，以及高山居民点。后来被称为「迷城」的泰乌纳是其中的大型聚落，在布里塔卡河上方拥有169层台地、圆形广场和石路。1444年，没有一位统治者统辖全境；每个河谷各有酋长，沿海与山地之间流通着盐、陶器、石器和金器。

西班牙船只1498年到达，罗德里戈·德·巴斯蒂达斯1525年在附近海湾建立圣玛尔塔。殖民者很快索要挑夫、黄金和通往高原稀树草原的道路，边疆随之陷入战争。1551年，佩德罗·德·乌尔苏阿的远征队在奥里瓜隘口被击溃，仅十三名士兵返回。泰罗纳战士数次焚毁圣玛尔塔，夺取邦伊达堡，还同英格兰和法兰西私掠者贸易。1599年至1600年，总督胡安·吉拉尔·韦隆逐谷用兵，处死诸酋长，并把俘获的村民分给圣玛尔塔一带的监护征赋主。泰乌纳也在那些年被废弃。退入最高山区的社群保留了自己的法律和仪式，科吉人、维瓦人、阿尔瓦科人和坎夸莫人都是他们的后裔。

en:
Maracaibo lies on the western side of the narrow channel joining Lake Maracaibo to the Gulf of Venezuela, the only sea entrance into the large inland waterway. In 1444 Añú families fished from stilt villages along the lake shore, including Santa Rosa de Agua; the Coquivacoa held the narrows, Wayuu kinsmen herded and traded across the dry plains to the north, and Carib groups lived on the eastern shore. Fish, salt and canoe routes supported the villages, while no stone fort or Spanish town yet blocked the bar.

On 24 August 1499 Alonso de Ojeda, Juan de la Cosa and Amerigo Vespucci became the first Europeans known to enter the lake. The houses raised over the water put Vespucci in mind of Venice, and the Spaniards called the coast Venezuela, or 'little Venice'. Under the Welsers' concession, Ambrosius Ehinger fought the Coquivacoa and founded Neu-Nürnberg on 8 September 1529. Nikolaus Federmann removed its few settlers to Cabo de la Vela in 1535. Alonso Pacheco's Ciudad Rodrigo of 1569 was also abandoned during indigenous risings, and Pedro Maldonado founded the lasting town of Nueva Zamora in 1574 for Governor Diego de Mazariegos.

Raiders tested the channel for the next century. The Dutch corsair Henrik de Gerard plundered Maracaibo in 1614 and William Jackson in 1642, while the Spanish built San Carlos de la Barra Fortress in 1623 with limestone from Toas Island to cover the pass. L'Olonnais captured the fort and sacked the town in 1665. In March 1669 Henry Morgan destroyed or captured three Spanish warships while leaving the lake, then feigned a night land attack to get past San Carlos. Michel de Grammont pushed inland as far as Trujillo in 1678. The protected anchorage nevertheless made Maracaibo a transshipment port for produce from the southern lake and Venezuelan Andes bound for the Caribbean. In 1777 it passed to the Captaincy General of Venezuela. The province stayed loyal to the Crown in 1810 and housed the captaincy general after Caracas fell to the republicans; a garrison rising in 1821 carried the independence war onto the lake.
zh:
马拉开波位于马拉开波湖通往委内瑞拉湾的狭窄水道西侧，这条水道是进出广阔湖水的唯一海口。1444年，阿纽人在湖畔桩屋村落中捕鱼，圣罗莎德阿瓜便是其中一处；科基瓦科阿人据守湖口，瓦尤人在北方干旱平原放牧通商，东岸则有加勒比语族群。鱼、盐和独木舟航路供养着这些村落，湖口还没有石堡或西班牙城镇。

1499年8月24日，阿隆索·德·奥赫达、胡安·德·拉·科萨和亚美利哥·韦斯普奇成为已知最早驶入此湖的欧洲人。架在水面上的房屋让韦斯普奇想起威尼斯，西班牙人遂把这片海岸称为委内瑞拉，意为「小威尼斯」。德意志韦尔泽家族取得殖民特许权后，安布罗修斯·埃因格同科基瓦科阿人作战，于1529年9月8日建立新纽伦堡。1535年，尼古劳斯·费德曼把城中寥寥居民迁往瓜希拉半岛的贝拉角。阿隆索·帕切科1569年建立的罗德里戈城也在土著起义中废弃；1574年，佩德罗·马尔多纳多奉总督迭戈·德·马萨列戈斯之命建成长存的新萨莫拉。

此后一个世纪，袭掠者不断试探这条湖口水道。荷兰私掠者亨里克·德·热拉尔1614年洗劫马拉开波，威廉·杰克逊1642年再度来犯；西班牙人则在1623年修筑圣卡洛斯·德拉巴拉堡，从托阿斯岛运来石灰岩封锁湖口。1665年，洛洛奈攻下堡垒并洗劫城镇。1669年3月，亨利·摩根离开湖泊时击毁或俘获三艘西班牙战船，又佯作夜间陆路进攻，从圣卡洛斯堡前脱身。1678年，米歇尔·德·格拉蒙深入内陆，一直攻到特鲁希略。尽管如此，受遮蔽的锚地仍使马拉开波成为转运港，湖南岸和委内瑞拉安第斯山区的物产经这里运往加勒比。1777年，马拉开波划归委内瑞拉都督府。1810年，该省继续效忠西班牙王室；加拉加斯落入共和派之手后，都督府迁到这里。1821年，一场驻军起义把独立战争带上湖面。

en:
The valley of Caracas lies a short way inland from the Caribbean, cut off from the sea by the forested Ávila ridge and watered by the Guaire. In 1444 its maize plots and scattered villages belonged to the Caracas, Teque and Mariche, and the cacique Guaicaipuro had drawn the valley's peoples into a confederacy strong enough to meet Spanish intruders with arms.

The first intruder was the mestizo Francisco Fajardo, who between 1555 and 1562 twice tried to plant a settlement from the coast at La Guaira, and the confederates destroyed both attempts. On 25 July 1567 Captain Diego de Losada defeated the villages one by one and founded Santiago de León de Caracas, named for the valley's people. Governor Juan de Pimentel made the town capital of Venezuela Province in 1578. The mountains kept Caribbean corsairs out until 1595, when Amyas Preston and George Somers led English privateers over a little-used pass of the Ávila while the defenders watched the usual road, and sacked and burned the undefended town. Wheat paid for the early years, but from the 1620s cacao, grown on the surrounding haciendas with African slave labour, made the fortune of Caracas. The earthquake of 1641 levelled most of the town, and in 1728 the crown vested the cacao trade in the Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas.

This mountain city also produced the men who undid Spanish rule. Francisco de Miranda, who had fought in the American and French revolutions and is called the precursor of South American independence, was born here, as was Simón Bolívar, on 24 July 1783. A junta on 19 April 1810 and the declaration of 5 July 1811 opened Venezuelan independence in the valley. On Maundy Thursday 1812 an earthquake destroyed much of Caracas and killed thousands, and when the first republic fell two years later thousands of its people fled east. The city came back to patriot hands only after Bolívar defeated the royalists at Carabobo in June 1821.
zh:
加拉加斯（卡拉卡斯）谷地离加勒比海岸不远，阿维拉山林木葱郁的山脊把它与海洋隔开，瓜伊尔河穿谷而过。1444年，谷中的玉米地和散落村落属于加拉加斯人、特克人和马里奇人；酋长瓜伊凯普罗把谷地各部结成联盟，足以以武力迎击来犯的西班牙人。

最早来犯的是混血的弗朗西斯科·法哈多。1555至1562年间，他两度从海岸上的拉瓜伊拉伸入谷地建立据点，都被联盟各部摧毁。1567年7月25日，迭戈·德·洛萨达上尉将各个村落逐个击破，建起圣地亚哥·德·莱昂·德·加拉卡斯，城名取自谷地的原住民。1578年，省长胡安·德·皮门特尔把委内瑞拉省的首府设到这里。山岭曾把加勒比海的海盗挡在外面，直到1595年，阿米亚斯·普雷斯顿和乔治·萨默斯率英国私掠船员从阿维拉山一条少有人走的隘口翻越而入，守军盯着的却是惯常的大路，他们遂洗劫并烧毁了无备的城镇。早年的加拉加斯靠小麦赚钱，1620年代起，周围庄园役使非洲奴隶种植可可，为城市挣来财富；1641年的大地震把大半个城镇夷为平地，1728年王室把可可贸易特许给加拉加斯吉普斯夸公司。

这座山城也走出了推翻西班牙统治的人。参加过美国独立战争和法国大革命、被称为南美独立先驱的弗朗西斯科·德米兰达出生于此，西蒙·玻利瓦尔也于1783年7月24日出生在这里。1810年4月19日的执政委员会和1811年7月5日的独立宣言，使委内瑞拉独立在这条谷地里开场。1812年圣周四，一场大地震摧毁了大半个加拉加斯，数千人丧生；两年后第一共和国覆灭，又有成千上万的市民向东逃亡。直到1821年6月玻利瓦尔在卡拉沃沃击败保王军，加拉加斯才回到爱国者手中。

en:
The highland basin of Hunza, later Tunja, was the northern seat of Muisca power on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense. Its ruler bore the title hoa or zaque, and from the fenced settlement at Hunza he received the homage of the chiefs of Boyacá. Chibcha-speaking farmers grew maize and potatoes on the high plains, and trains of human carriers moved salt, cotton cloth, goldwork and emeralds between Hunza, Bacatá (the future Bogotá) and the priestly centre of Suamox, later Sogamoso. In 1444 Hunza and Bacatá were the two chief seats of the Muisca, with Suamox the religious centre to the east.

Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada reached Hunza in August 1537. His men found the aged zaque seated alone on his chair and dressed in gold while his court fled; they carried him off to Suesca and emptied his compound of gold, emeralds and cloth. Captain Gonzalo Suárez Rendón laid out Spanish Tunja on the site on 6 August 1539, with its main square, church and house lots; his own Casa del Fundador is the oldest building left from those years. Encomiendas of indigenous labour made the early townsmen rich, and the Franciscans, Dominicans, Augustinians and Jesuits each founded convents in the century after the conquest. Juan de Castellanos, a soldier turned priest who died in Tunja, wrote the Elegías de varones ilustres de Indias, a verse chronicle of the conquest and of Muisca life. In 1781 Comunero rebels marching on Santa Fe stopped to sack the tobacco office. Tunja declared independence on 9 December 1811 and housed the congress of the United Provinces until the royalists retook it on 29 November 1816. On 7 August 1819 Bolívar's army caught Colonel Barreiro's division at the Boyacá bridge on the road to Tunja and broke it in two hours, opening the road to Santa Fe and ending Spanish rule in New Granada.
zh:
罕萨盆地后来成为通哈，是穆伊斯卡人在昆迪博亚卡高原北部的权力中心。这里的统治者称霍阿或萨凯，在围栏围起的城镇里接受博亚卡诸酋长朝贡。说奇布查语的农民在高原种植玉米和马铃薯，人的驮队把盐、棉布、金器和祖母绿运来运去，往来于罕萨、后来成为波哥大的巴卡塔与祭司中心苏阿莫克斯（后来的索加莫索）之间。1444年，罕萨和巴卡塔是穆伊斯卡人两个并立的权力中心，苏阿莫克斯则是东方的宗教中心。

1537年8月，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达抵达罕萨。部下见到年老的萨凯独坐椅上、一身金饰，随从都已逃散；他们把他掳往苏埃斯卡，将其居所中的黄金、祖母绿和织物劫掠一空。1539年8月6日，船长贡萨洛·苏亚雷斯·伦登在旧址上规划西班牙人的通哈，建起主广场、教堂和分给征服者的宅地；他本人的奠基者之宅是那个年代留存下来的最古老房屋。委托监护制下的印第安劳役让早期市民致富，方济各会、多明我会、奥斯定会和耶稣会在征服后的一个世纪里先后建起会院。行伍出身、后来成为神父的胡安·德·卡斯特利亚诺斯卒于通哈，著有《Elegías de varones ilustres de Indias》，用韵文记述征服经过和穆伊斯卡人的生活。1781年，向圣菲进军的公社起义者路过通哈，捣毁了烟草税署。1811年12月9日，通哈宣布独立，直到1816年11月29日保王军夺回之前，联合省议会一直设在这里。1819年8月7日，玻利瓦尔的军队在通往通哈的博亚卡桥截住巴雷罗上校的师，两小时内将其击溃，打开了进军圣菲的道路，终结了西班牙在新格拉纳达的统治。

en:
Algoa Bay lies on the sea route from the Cape toward India, with fresh water at the Baakens mouth and an anchorage between Cape Recife and Cape Padrone. Behind it, dry valleys and thornveld rise toward the Sneeuberg. In 1444 San hunters used the shore and mountains, while Khoekhoe herders and Xhosa-speaking cattle keepers moved stock between seasonal pastures. The bay had no European post then, only camps, cattle paths and watering places.

Bartolomeu Dias reached the bay in 1488 and planted a wooden cross on St Croix Island; Vasco da Gama later noted Bird Island. Portuguese captains valued the water, but no town followed for three centuries. The Dutch East India Company founded Graaff-Reinet in 1786 to draw trade from the interior, and competition for cattle and the Zuurveld soon pulled the district into the Xhosa wars. In 1795 Graaff-Reinet's burghers rejected company rule and proclaimed their own short-lived republic, shortly before British forces took the Cape. British troops built Fort Frederick above the Baakens in 1799 to prevent a French landing in support of the inland rebels, and its guns never fired a shot. Frontier fighting later drove Xhosa communities beyond the Fish River; the prophet Nxele's attack on Grahamstown failed in 1819. The next year about 4,000 British settlers landed beneath the fort, where Rufane Donkin laid out Port Elizabeth.
zh:
阿尔戈阿湾位于从好望角通向印度的航路上，巴肯斯河口有淡水，累西腓角与帕德龙角之间是可泊船的开阔海湾。湾后方干旱谷地和灌丛草原逐渐抬向斯尼乌山。1444年，桑人猎人在海岸和山地活动，科伊科伊牧人与操科萨语的牧牛群体按季节转牧场。湾畔还没有欧洲人的据点，只有营地、牧牛小径和补水处。

1488年，巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士抵达海湾，在圣克罗伊岛竖起木十字架；瓦斯科·达·伽马后来又记录了伯德岛。葡萄牙船长看重这里的淡水，但此后三百年间没有形成城镇。荷兰东印度公司于1786年建立格拉夫-里内特，以吸纳内陆贸易；对牲畜和祖尔费尔德草场的争夺很快把这一地区拖入科萨战争。1795年，格拉夫-里内特市民拒绝公司统治，宣布成立一个短命共和国，不久英军便占领开普。1799年，英军在巴肯斯河畔高地修筑弗雷德里克堡，以防法军登陆支援内陆叛军；堡中火炮后来一炮未放。边疆战事后把科萨社群驱过大鱼河，先知恩克斯莱1819年进攻格雷厄姆斯敦失败。次年，约四千名英国移民在堡下登岸，鲁凡·唐金在此规划伊丽莎白港。

en:
The Barinas savannas climb from the Apure plains toward the wooded piedmont of the Mérida Andes, cut by the Santo Domingo river and other streams off the mountains. In 1444 the people here lived in the Osoid manner, fishing and maize villages of Arawak speakers and groups linked to the Tunebo and the Andes, with mounded settlements and raised causeways that carried maize and cassava between floodplain and hills; chiefs held the river crossings. Barinas is an indigenous word for the strong wind that blows off the Santo Domingo valleys in the wet season, and also for a low thorny shrub with yellow flowers common on the high plain. No Spanish town stood there yet.

Georg von Speyer's Welser expedition crossed in the 1530s, but the first town came only in 1577, when Captain Juan Andrés Varela founded Altamira de Cáceres. Tobacco earned the small settlement a name and cattle ranches spread into the plains; the llanero horsemen who later made up the bulk of both armies' cavalry in the independence wars learned their trade on the ranches of Barinas and Apure. The townspeople moved twice, to Nueva Trujillo de Barinas in 1628 and to the present site in 1759, a transfer confirmed by royal decree in 1762. Charles III made the town capital of a new Province of Barinas in 1786, and it became a patriot stronghold: Cristóbal Mendoza, first president of the First Republic of Venezuela, had lived and practised law there. Royalists retook the city in 1814, José Antonio Páez recovered it in 1817, and with the rest of Venezuela it entered Gran Colombia in 1821.
zh:
巴里纳斯草原由阿普雷平原向梅里达安第斯山林木覆盖的山麓抬升，圣多明各河等山溪顺坡而下。1444年，这里的居民延续奥索伊德传统：操阿拉瓦克语的渔猎玉米村落，与同图内博人和安第斯人群有关的部族共居；他们筑土墩而居，修起高架堤道，在泛滥平原与丘陵之间运送玉米和木薯，渡口由各酋长把持。巴里纳斯本是印第安语词，指雨季从圣多明各河谷吹来的强风，也指高原上常见的一种开黄花的矮刺灌。当时这里还没有西班牙城镇。

格奥尔格·冯·施派尔代表韦尔塞公司的远征在1530年代穿过此地，但第一座城镇迟至1577年才由胡安·安德烈斯·巴雷拉上尉建立，取名阿尔塔米拉·德·卡塞雷斯。烟草让这座小定居点有了名气，牧牛场随后遍布平原；独立战争中交战双方骑兵的主力都是草原骑手，他们牧牛御马的手艺最初就是在巴里纳斯和阿普雷的牧场上练出来的。居民两度迁城：1628年迁为新特鲁希略·德·巴里纳斯，1759年再迁至现址，1762年获王室敕令确认。1786年，卡洛斯三世设立巴里纳斯省并定此城为首府，它后来成为爱国者的据点：委内瑞拉第一共和国首任总统克里斯托瓦尔·门多萨曾在此居住、当律师。1814年保王军夺回此城，何塞·安东尼奥·派斯1817年将其收复，1821年它随委内瑞拉并入大哥伦比亚。

en:
The Pacific shore around the Gulf of Panama was Cueva country on the eve of European contact. Cueva-speaking villagers planted maize, cacao and root crops, fished the coastal shallows, and used river and forest trails toward the Caribbean side of the isthmus. The bay took its Spanish name from a nearby Cueva ranchería called Panama. In 1444 no European town stood here; scattered palm-thatched hamlets occupied the littoral, and no outside power yet controlled the route between the two seas.

Pedro Arias Dávila moved his colony from Santa María la Antigua del Darién to this bay and founded Nuestra Señora de la Asunción de Panamá on 15 August 1519, the first permanent Spanish city on the American Pacific shore. Charles I granted it a city title and council in 1521. Ships, men and supplies left here for Francisco Pizarro's conquest of Peru, while Peruvian gold and silver crossed the isthmus to the fairs at Nombre de Dios and Portobelo. The town gained convents, a hospital and a cathedral by the early seventeenth century, and its wealth drew privateers across the isthmus. Henry Morgan landed on the Caribbean coast with about 1,400 men, crossed the jungles and sacked Panama on 28 January 1671. Spanish accounts blame Governor Juan Pérez de Guzmán for the great fire, saying he ordered the powder stores blown up. Antonio Fernández de Córdoba rebuilt the town in 1673 on a defensible peninsula 8 kilometres to the southwest; the burned settlement was left as the ruins later called Panamá Viejo. In 1821 the city broke from Spain and joined Gran Colombia.
zh:
欧洲人到来前，巴拿马湾的太平洋沿岸是库埃瓦人的土地。操库埃瓦语的村落种植玉米、可可和块根作物，在近岸浅海捕鱼，并沿河流与林中小路通往地峡的加勒比一侧。海湾的西班牙名称来自附近一个叫巴拿马的库埃瓦人村落。1444年，这里还没有欧洲人的城市，沿岸只有分散的棕榈顶村落，也没有外来势力控制两洋之间的通路。

佩德罗·阿里亚斯·达维拉把殖民地从圣玛丽亚·拉安蒂瓜·德尔达连迁到这片海湾，于1519年8月15日建立圣母升天巴拿马城，这是美洲太平洋岸第一座永久西班牙城市。1521年，卡洛斯一世授予城市头衔并设市议会。船只、人员和补给从这里出发，支持弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗征服秘鲁；秘鲁的金银则横越地峡，运往农布雷-德迪奥斯和波托韦洛的集市。17世纪初，城中已有修道院、医院和主教座堂，财富也把私掠者引过地峡。亨利·摩根率约一千四百人在加勒比海岸登陆，穿过丛林，在1671年1月28日洗劫巴拿马。西班牙记载把大火归于总督胡安·佩雷斯·德·古斯曼，称他下令引爆火药库。1673年，安东尼奥·费尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦在西南8公里一处易守的半岛上重建城市；焚毁的旧城留下，后来称为旧巴拿马城遗址。1821年，该城脱离西班牙，加入大哥伦比亚。

en:
Chorotega covers the eastern shore of the Gulf of Nicoya, from Tivives and Chomes to the Tempisque lowlands and the Guanacaste foothills. In 1444 this coast formed the southern edge of Mesoamerica. Chorotega villages under Gurutina and other chiefs grew maize on the coastal plains and exchanged Nicoya polychrome vessels, jade ornaments and carved ceremonial metates along northern routes. Older Corobicí and Huetar communities lived nearby, a Nahua group occupied the Bagaces area, and the stronger kingdom of Nicoya lay across the gulf. No single town ruled all these shores.

Spanish ships entered the gulf with Gaspar de Espinosa in 1519, and Gil González Dávila crossed the district from Tivives in 1522. Encomienda grants then split the native villages. Spanish anchorages had short lives: Juan de Cavallón founded Villa de los Reyes and Puerto Landecho at Tivives in 1561; Alonso Anguciana de Gamboa founded Espíritu Santo, later Esparza, in 1574; and Diego de Artieda opened Caldera harbour three years later. Esparza lived by Pacific traffic with Panama, while its parish church and the San Lorenzo convent served a district reaching from the Aguacate mountains to the Tempisque. Pirates sacked the town in 1685 and burned it in 1686, driving survivors inland to Las Cañas and Bagaces. Cattle ranches then spread across the Tempisque plains, and the settlement of Guanacaste formally founded in 1769 later became Liberia. Spanish rule in Costa Rica ended in 1821.
zh:
乔罗特加位于尼科亚湾东岸，从蒂维韦斯、乔莫斯一直延伸到滕皮斯奎低地和瓜纳卡斯特山麓。1444年，这片海岸处在中美洲的南缘。古鲁蒂纳等首领治下的乔罗特加村落在沿海平原种植玉米，并沿北方商路交换尼科亚彩陶器、玉饰和雕有纹饰的仪式用石磨盘。更早的科罗维西人、韦塔尔人社区住在附近，巴加塞斯一带有纳瓦人群体，海湾对岸则是更强大的尼科亚王国。没有任何一座城镇统治整片海岸。

1519年，加斯帕尔·德·埃斯皮诺萨率西班牙船只进入尼科亚湾；1522年，希尔·冈萨雷斯·达维拉从蒂维韦斯穿过这一地区。随后，监护征赋授予把原住民村落分割开来。西班牙人的港口历时不长：1561年，胡安·德·卡瓦永在蒂维韦斯建立雷耶斯镇和兰德乔港；1574年，阿隆索·安吉西亚纳·德·甘博阿建立圣埃斯皮里图，即后来的埃斯帕尔萨；三年后，迭戈·德·阿尔铁达启用卡尔德拉港。埃斯帕尔萨依靠与巴拿马的太平洋贸易维持，教区教堂和圣洛伦索修道院服务的辖区从阿瓜卡特山脉一直到滕皮斯奎。1685年海盗洗劫城镇，次年又将其焚毁，幸存者被迫退入内陆的拉斯卡尼亚斯和巴加塞斯。牧场随后扩展到滕皮斯奎平原，1769年正式设立的瓜纳卡斯特聚落后来成为利韦里亚。1821年，西班牙在哥斯达黎加的统治终结。

en:
In 1444 this part of Nicaragua was a volcanic lake country on the Pacific slope. Mangue-speaking Chorotega communities, Sutiaba above all, held the plain between Lake Xolotlán and the cone of Momotombo, while Nahua speakers from the southern lakes kept towns of their own in the district. Farmers, fishers and local lords occupied a chain of towns and ceremonial grounds on the fertile volcanic soil, paying tribute to no one beyond their own rulers, and no Castilian had yet entered the lakes.

After Gil González Dávila's entrada of 1522 opened the lake country, Francisco Hernández de Córdoba founded Santiago de los Caballeros de León on the southwestern shore of Xolotlán in 1524. He enjoyed his city for only two years: Pedrarias Dávila, the aged governor who had led the taking of Panama, had him beheaded in the main square in 1526 during the War of the Captains and made León the seat of Spanish government in Nicaragua; enslaved Indians were shipped from its roads toward Panama and Peru. The volcano then drove the city out. After the earthquakes of 1610 the citizens voted to abandon the lake shore and rebuild some 30 kilometers west beside Sutiaba; the shocks had not flattened the old town, but Momotombo's ash slowly buried it in the years after. The new León raised the Assumption church from 1706 to 1740 and opened its university in 1812, only the second in Central America. On 11 October 1821 the city's council signed the act taking Nicaragua and Costa Rica out of the Spanish monarchy.
zh:
1444年，尼加拉瓜这一角是太平洋坡地上的火山湖区。说曼格语的乔罗特加社群占据索洛特兰湖与莫莫通博火山锥之间的平原，苏蒂亚巴是其中最大的一个；南方湖区的纳瓦语人群也在这一带有自己的城镇。农夫、渔民和地方首领在肥沃的火山土上经营着一连串城镇与仪式场所，只服从自己的统治者，卡斯蒂利亚人还没有踏入湖区。

1522年吉尔·冈萨雷斯·达维拉的远征打开湖区后，弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦于1524年在索洛特兰湖西南岸建立圣地亚哥·德·洛斯·卡瓦列罗斯·德·莱昂。他只在自己的城里享了两年：1526年，曾主持夺取巴拿马的老总督佩德拉里亚斯·达维拉在「首领战争」中把他斩首于城主广场，并把莱昂设为西班牙在尼加拉瓜的统治中心；被奴役的印第安人从这里经陆路被运往巴拿马和秘鲁。逼走这座城市的是那座火山。1610年连串地震后，居民投票决定离开湖岸，西迁约30公里，在苏蒂亚巴旁重建城市；地震并没有夷平旧城，但此后莫莫通博的火山灰渐渐把它埋住。新城的升天堂建于1706至1740年，大学则开办于1812年，是中美洲的第二所大学。1821年10月11日，莱昂市政会议签署法令，使尼加拉瓜和哥斯达黎加脱离西班牙君主统治。

en:
Mosquito is the middle reach of the Mosquito Shore, around the lagoons and cays where the Coco, the river the Miskito call Wangki, reaches the Caribbean at Cabo Gracias a Dios. In 1444 small Miskito-speaking communities farmed and fished along these river basins, travelling by dugout canoe between the forest, the shore and the sea-turtle grounds; Sumu- and Paya-speaking peoples held the neighbouring districts the Spanish later named Taguzgalpa and Tologalpa. A chief's authority seldom reached beyond his own village, and no European had yet reached the coast.

Columbus rounded the cape after a storm on 12 September 1502 and gave it its thanksgiving name. Four Castilian conquest licenses between 1545 and 1594 and repeated Franciscan missions won nothing lasting, so the shore instead gave shelter to Dutch, English and Welsh privateers, Henry Morgan and William Dampier among them. From the 1630s the Providence Island Company dealt with Miskito leaders as kings, and a king's son visited London. In 1641 survivors of a wrecked Portuguese slaver settled by the Coco and married into the coast, beginning the Miskito Sambu; King Oldman was in turn received in England and returned with a laced hat and a commission to shelter English castaways. Sambu war bands later raided as far as Yucatán and Costa Rica, selling their captives on to Jamaica. King Edward I signed an alliance with Britain in 1740 and a British superintendent arrived in 1749, but Britain evacuated the shore under the 1786 Convention of London. Spain shipped in some 1,200 settlers, war resumed in 1797, and the Miskito drove the Spanish from Bluefields on 4 September 1800; in 1821 the coast still answered to its own Miskito king.
zh:
莫斯基托是莫斯基托海岸的中段，周围是潟湖与礁岛；米斯基托人称作旺基河的科科河，在格拉西亚斯-阿迪奥斯角注入加勒比海。1444年，说米斯基托语的小型村社沿各条河谷农耕渔捞，乘独木舟往来于雨林、岸边和海龟渔场之间；操苏穆语、帕亚语的族群住在邻近地带，西班牙人后来把那里称作塔古斯加尔帕和托洛加尔帕。首领的权势很少越出本村，欧洲人也还没有踏上这片海岸。

1502年9月12日，哥伦布在风暴后绕过这个海岬，为它取了感恩的名字。卡斯蒂利亚在1545至1594年间四次颁发征服许可，方济各会又屡次深入传教，都未能持久立足，海岸反而庇护了荷兰、英格兰和威尔士私掠者，亨利·摩根和威廉·丹皮尔都曾在此落脚。1630年代起，普罗维登斯岛公司把米斯基托首领以国王相待，一位国王之子还访问了伦敦。1641年，一艘失事葡萄牙贩奴船的幸存者在科科河畔定居通婚，形成赞布米斯基托人；国王欧德曼也曾到英格兰做客，带回一顶镶边帽和一份接济遇险英人的委任状。赞布武装后来袭掠远至尤卡坦和哥斯达黎加，把掳获的人口转卖到牙买加。1740年，国王爱德华一世与英国签订同盟条约，英国又在1749年派来海岸监督官，但依1786年《伦敦公约》，英国人撤出了海岸。西班牙随后运来约一千二百名移民；1797年战事再起，1800年9月4日米斯基托人把西班牙人逐出布卢菲尔兹，到1821年，这片海岸仍归米斯基托人自己的国王管辖。

en:
The Pacific lowlands between the Paz and Lempa rivers are Pipil country. Nawat-speaking Nahua migrants entered from central Mexico around 900 and settled among older Maya, Lenca and Xinca populations; by the thirteenth century their city-states had united, and by 1400 Cuzcatlán was ruled by a hereditary monarchy that kept a standing army. It was less a single city than a network of noble towns and tribute districts. Its wealth sat on the Pacific plain: irrigated cacao orchards behind Acajutla, Sonsonate and Izalco, cotton fields, salt pans and fisheries, and the shore later called the Balsam Coast, whose aromatic resin reached Europe in the seventeenth century. Woven cotton and cacao moved along the regional trade routes. In 1444 Cuzcatlán was one of the strongest lordships in the region.

Pedro de Alvarado invaded from the Guatemalan Highlands in 1524. At Acajutla on 8 June his feigned retreat drew the Pipil army within cavalry charge and it was killed to a man, but an arrow passed through Alvarado's leg and left him with a permanent limp; six days later he watched the battle of Tacuzcalco from a hill while his brothers led the charges. The fortified cities of Cuzcatlán and Izalco still held, and when he demanded their surrender the mountain warriors answered that if he wanted their arms he must come and take them. Local legend calls that lord Atlacatl, though no contemporary chronicler names him. After seventeen days Alvarado withdrew to Guatemala.

Gonzalo de Alvarado founded the first San Salvador in 1525, and the general Pipil rising of 1526 destroyed it. Diego de Alvarado returned with three hundred Indian auxiliaries from Soconusco, re-founded the town on 1 April 1528 and granted encomiendas to his followers. The last strong point was the Peñol de Cinacantan, a sheer rock above Tamanique with one guarded approach: two assaults were beaten back in a single day before a wooden siege tower was pushed up to the walls and the fort breached. The country was counted pacified by 1539. Encomienda labour, epidemics and work on cacao and indigo holdings thinned the Pipil towns, though an archiepiscopal survey in 1772 still recorded Nawat in 64 towns and 56,292 speakers. Spanish rule lasted until independence in 1821.
zh:
帕斯河与伦帕河之间的太平洋低地是匹普人的土地。约900年，说纳瓦特语的纳瓦移民从中墨西哥进入此地，定居在更早的玛雅、伦卡和辛卡族群之间；到13世纪，他们的城邦已结为一体，1400年时库斯卡特兰由世袭君主统治，并保有一支常备军。它由贵族统治的城镇和贡赋区结成网络，并非一座单一城市。财富集中在太平洋平原上：阿卡胡特拉、松索纳特和伊萨尔科背后是灌溉可可园，另有棉田、盐池和渔场；后来称作香脂海岸的地带出产芳香树脂，17世纪时已远销欧洲。棉织物和可可靠区域商路外运。1444年，库斯卡特兰是这一带最强盛的领主国之一。

1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多从危地马拉高地攻入。6月8日在阿卡胡特拉，他以假退把匹普军队诱入骑兵冲锋的距离，将其尽数歼灭，但一支箭射穿了阿尔瓦拉多的腿，使他终身跛行；六天后的塔库斯卡尔科之战，他只能在山丘上观战，由几个弟弟率部冲锋。设防的库斯卡特兰和伊萨尔科仍未攻下，阿尔瓦拉多要其投降时，山里的战士回话：想要我们的兵器，就上山来取。当地传说把这位首领称作阿特拉克特尔，不过没有任何同时代的编年史家提到他。十七天后，阿尔瓦拉多退回危地马拉。

贡萨洛·德·阿尔瓦拉多1525年建起首座圣萨尔瓦多，1526年匹普人全面起事将其摧毁。迭戈·德·阿尔瓦拉多率三百名来自索科努斯科的印第安援军重返，1528年4月1日重建城镇并向部下分封监护地。最后的据点是塔马尼克上方的西纳坎坦岩要塞：岩壁陡峭，只有一条重兵把守的通路，西军一天内两次强攻都被击退，直到把木制攻城塔推到墙边才破城。到1539年，这一地区已被视为平定。监护制劳役、疫病和可可、靛蓝种植使匹普诸城人口凋零，但1772年的大主教巡查仍记载64个城镇使用纳瓦特语，使用者有56292人。西班牙统治一直延续到1821年独立。

en:
The province called Honduras wraps around the Bay of Trujillo on the Caribbean shore. The Guaimoreto lagoon lies sheltered behind a deep roadstead, and the wooded hills of Capiro and Calentura rise a short way inland. In 1444 the Papayeca and Chapagua peoples held this coast, their villages, fields and fishing grounds under local headmen; the Papayeca numbered Nahua speakers among them, whom the conquistadors later took for Mexicans. No Christian town or fort stood on the bay, whose deep water was known only to the people who fished its cays and rivers.

Christopher Columbus anchored in that roadstead on 14 August 1502, on his fourth voyage, and went ashore at Punta de Caxinas, the first time he stood on the Central American mainland; his crews sounded bottomless water and named the coast Honduras, the depths. Cristóbal de Olid, sent by Hernán Cortés, founded Triunfo de la Cruz beside the lagoon in 1524 and then tried to keep the country for himself. Francisco de las Casas defeated him, and Juan de Medina founded Trujillo by the harbor on 18 May 1525. The town became the first capital of Honduras and the outlet for gold and silver from the interior, while the Papayeca chiefs Mazatl and Pizacura fought the conquistadors until their resistance was broken.

Around 1550 native labor raised the Fortaleza de Santa Bárbara on the bluff above the bay, named for the patron saint of gunners; in time it mounted fourteen cannon, yet it never made Trujillo safe. French raiders burned the town in 1558, the Dutch sacked it in 1633, an English force under William Jackson took it in 1643, and in 1683 the largest pirate gathering ever seen in the Caribbean assembled offshore. By the eighteenth century Spain had nearly withdrawn from a port it judged indefensible, and the government of Honduras had removed inland to Comayagua. In 1797 the British shipped about 2,500 defeated Black Caribs, later called the Garifuna, from St Vincent to Roatán; they crossed to the mainland and built their fishing villages along the beach below the fort. A thin Spanish garrison held Trujillo until Central American independence in 1821.
zh:
名为洪都拉斯的这个省份环抱着加勒比海岸的特鲁希略湾：瓜伊莫雷托潟湖藏在一道深水锚地之后，卡皮罗山和卡伦图拉山的林木丘陵在内陆不远处隆起。1444年，帕帕耶卡人和查帕瓜人据有这片海岸，村社、田地和渔场由本地首领管辖；帕帕耶卡人中还有纳瓦语使用者，后来的征服者把他们当成了墨西哥人。湾畔没有基督教城镇或要塞，这片极深的海水只有在礁岛和河流间打鱼的本地人熟悉。

1502年8月14日，哥伦布第四次远航时在这片锚地停泊，在卡克西纳斯角登岸，第一次踏上中美洲大陆。水手们测不到海底，便把这一带海岸命名为洪都拉斯，意为「深渊」。1524年，埃尔南·科尔特斯派来的克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在潟湖旁建立特里温福·德拉鲁斯，随后便想把这片土地据为己有；弗朗西斯科·德·拉斯·卡萨斯将他击败，胡安·德·梅迪纳于1525年5月18日在港畔建立特鲁希略。此城成为洪都拉斯的第一个首府，也是内地金银外运的港口；帕帕耶卡首领马萨特尔和皮萨库拉率众抵抗征服者，直到失败。

1550年前后，原住民劳工在海湾上方的崖地上筑起圣巴巴拉要塞，以炮兵主保圣人命名；要塞后来配备十四门大炮，却没能让特鲁希略变得安全。1558年法国袭掠者焚毁城镇，1633年荷兰海盗将其洗劫，1643年威廉·杰克逊率领的英国武装将其占领；1683年，加勒比规模最大的一次海盗集结又在湾外出现。到18世纪，西班牙几乎放弃了这座被认为无法防守的港口，洪都拉斯的统治机构也已内迁科马亚瓜。1797年，英国把约2500名战败的黑加勒比人（后来称加里富纳人）从圣文森特岛押往罗阿坦岛；他们渡海来到大陆，在要塞下方的海滩边建起渔村。直到1821年中美洲独立，特鲁希略始终只有一处兵力单薄的西班牙驻军。

en:
The province labelled Guatemala in 1444 is the eastern end of Soconusco, a narrow strip of Pacific piedmont squeezed between the Sierra Madre and the sea around the Suchiate river. Volcanic ash and rain nearly all year grow cacao prized across Mesoamerica; the beans left the coast together with achiote, cotton mantles, quetzal feathers and jaguar skins, along the road that ran north toward Tehuantepec and the markets of central Mexico. A string of small competing towns lay along that road, most of them Mixe-Zoque-speaking, with the dialect later called Tapachultec around the settlement that became Tapachula. The K'iche' kingdom of Q'umarkaj coveted the cacao towns but never ruled them, and in 1444 the coast answered to no highland king.

The coast kept its independence until 1486, when the Mexica emperor Ahuitzotl sent his captain Tiltototl to found Tapachollan as a garrison and tribute town. Soconusco then paid in cacao, cotton clothing, bird feathers and jaguar skins, and two revolts early in the next century brought Moctezuma II's armies back to put them down. Pedro de Alvarado passed through on his march to highland Guatemala in 1524, and disease and flight cut the native population of the cacao towns to a fraction within a generation. The Crown made Soconusco a province soon afterwards; its cacao was famous enough in Spain that Miguel de Cervantes, later the author of Don Quixote, petitioned the king for a post governing it, without success. In 1568 the province was attached to the Captaincy General of Guatemala. In 1794 Tapachula replaced Escuintla, wrecked by a hurricane, as provincial capital, and when independence came in 1821 the town declared for Mexico rather than Guatemala.
zh:
1444年游戏里的「危地马拉」省，实为索科努斯科的东端：马德雷山脉与太平洋之间夹着一条狭窄山麓，苏恰特河流经此地。火山灰和终年雨水滋养出在中美洲备受珍视的可可；可可豆和胭脂果、棉毯、格查尔鸟羽、美洲豹皮一起，沿通往特万特佩克和墨西哥谷地的海岸商路北运。商路沿岸是一连串彼此竞争的小城邦，居民多说米塞-索克语，后来塔帕丘拉城一带的方言被称作塔帕丘尔特语。库马尔卡赫的基切王国觊觎这些可可城镇却未能得手，1444年的海岸不奉任何高地国王为主。

海岸诸邦的独立在1486年告终：墨西卡皇帝阿维索特尔派将领蒂尔托托特尔建立塔帕乔兰驻军城镇，索科努斯科此后以可可、棉衣、鸟羽和美洲豹皮纳贡；16世纪初两度叛乱，蒙特祖马二世两次派兵回剿。1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多进军危地马拉高地途中经过海岸，疫病和人口逃亡在一代人之间使可可城镇的原住民锐减。西班牙王室不久将索科努斯科划为行省；当地可可在西班牙名声太大，连后来写成《堂吉诃德》的米格尔·德·塞万提斯都曾向国王请求出任索科努斯科的官职，未能如愿。1568年，索科努斯科划归危地马拉都督府。1794年，塔帕丘拉接替遭飓风摧毁的埃斯昆特拉成为省治；1821年独立时，塔帕丘拉宣布并入墨西哥，而不是加入危地马拉。

en:
Petén is a vast low plain of rainforest, savannah and shallow lakes in northern Guatemala. The great Classic Maya cities of the region had stood empty for centuries, but around Lake Petén Itzá the Itza kept a Postclassic kingdom whose king bore the title Kan Ek'. Their capital, Nojpetén or 'great island', occupied an island in the lake behind defensive walls along the shore, and canoes were the only way in. The Itza had begun moving south after the fall of Mayapán in 1441 and divided their island into four quarters by lineage; in 1444 they were making the lake their stronghold, tied by marriage, trade and war to the Kowoj, Yalain and other lake Maya groups.

Hernán Cortés crossed the lake country in 1525 on his march to Honduras, with 140 Spaniards and thousands of Mexican warriors, and visited Nojpetén as Kan Ek's guest. He left behind a cross and a lame horse; the Itza, who had never seen a horse, fed it poultry, meat and flowers as if it were a god, and when it died they carved its statue. When Franciscans from Mérida returned in 1618 they found the horse idol still standing, and friar Juan de Orbita smashed it on the spot. Kan Ek' spared the visitors but would not convert, saying Itza prophecy fixed another time, and the friars were expelled the following year. A military entrada in 1622 ended with the friar Diego Delgado and his party killed, and the lake was then left alone for most of the seventeenth century. The last campaign came from Yucatán: Martín de Ursúa y Arizmendi cut a road south from Campeche, launched assault boats across the lake and took Nojpetén on 13 March 1697. With the island fell the last independent native kingdom in the Americas, and the settlement there became the Spanish post of Flores.
zh:
佩滕是危地马拉北部一片广阔低地，遍布雨林、稀树草原和浅水湖。当地古典时代的马雅大城已荒芜数百年，伊察人却在佩滕伊察湖畔维持着一个后古典期王国，国王称卡内克。都城诺赫佩滕意为「大岛」，坐落在湖中小岛上，沿岸筑有防御墙，外人只能乘独木舟抵达。1441年马亚潘陷落后，伊察人开始南迁，按氏族把岛城分为四区；1444年，他们正以湖区为据点，通过联姻、贸易和战争与科沃赫、亚莱因等湖畔马雅群体周旋。

1525年，埃尔南·科尔特斯进军洪都拉斯，带着140名西班牙人和数千墨西哥战士穿过湖区，以卡内克客人的身份访问诺赫佩滕。他留下一个十字架和一匹跛马；伊察人从未见过马，把它当神看待，喂它禽肉和鲜花，马死后还为它雕了像。1618年梅里达的方济各会士再来时，马像还供在岛上，修士胡安·德·奥尔维塔当场把它砸碎。卡内克饶了来客的性命，却拒绝改宗，说伊察人的预言指定了别的时间，修士们第二年也被驱逐出境。1622年的武装远征以修士迭戈·德尔加多一行被杀告终，此后大半个17世纪湖区无人过问。最后一场攻势从尤卡坦发起：马丁·德·乌尔苏亚·阿里斯门迪从坎佩切向南开路，驾攻岛船队渡湖，于1697年3月13日攻陷诺赫佩滕。随着岛城陷落，美洲最后一个独立的原住民王国灭亡，岛上定居点成为西班牙人的据点弗洛雷斯。

en:
Corozal Bay and the mouths of the Hondo and New Rivers, sheltered behind cays and mangrove, made this coast a meeting ground for Yucatán canoe traders.
