Its chief town, Chactemal, usually identified with the ruins at Santa Rita, held the river routes inland to Lamanai and the Petén lakes and dealt in cacao, cotton and salt. The province answered to Mayapán until that city's supremacy collapsed in 1441, and in 1444 Chactemal was an independent lowland Maya polity run by Putún-connected merchants and farmers.

The province's best-known figure was a Spaniard. Gonzalo Guerrero was wrecked off the eastern Yucatán coast in 1511 with a handful of survivors, enslaved first in Uaymil and taken into the service of Chactemal's ruler Nachan Kan a few years later. He rose to command the ruler's warriors as a nakom, had his face tattooed and his ears pierced, married Nachan Kan's daughter and raised children counted among the first mestizos of the Americas. When Cortés sent word in 1519 offering rescue, Guerrero refused; his shipmate Jerónimo de Aguilar went, and became the translator who served Cortés beside La Malinche. Guerrero instead organised the defence that drove off Francisco de Montejo's entrada of 1527 and 1528, and he died in 1536 fighting the Spanish in Honduras, where he had sailed with fifty war canoes from Chactemal, killed by an arquebus shot. In the 1540s Gaspar Pacheco's bloody campaign broke the province and attached its survivors to Spanish Yucatán. Spanish settlement stayed thin, and from around 1640 English logwood cutters worked the river mouths for the dyewood European weavers wanted. The 1783 Treaty of Versailles granted Britain logging rights between the Hondo and Belize rivers, the basis of British Honduras.
zh:
科罗萨尔湾和翁多河、纽河的河口有群岛与红树林遮蔽，是尤卡坦独木舟商人汇集的海岸。当地首邑查克特马尔通常被比定为圣塔里塔遗址，扼守通向拉马奈和佩滕湖区的内陆河路，转销可可、棉花和盐。1441年马亚潘霸权崩溃以前，这一政区听命于马亚潘；1444年，查克特马尔已是一个独立的低地马雅政权，由与普屯人有渊源的商人和农人主事。

此地最出名的人物是个西班牙人。1511年，贡萨洛·格雷罗乘船在尤卡坦东岸外海失事，与少数幸存者先在瓦伊米尔为奴，几年后转入查克特马尔统治者纳昌·坎麾下。他凭战功升为统领战士的「纳科姆」，纹面穿耳，娶纳昌·坎的女儿为妻，所生子女被视为美洲最早的混血儿之一。1519年科尔特斯派人送信邀他归队，格雷罗拒绝了；同船的赫罗尼莫·德·阿吉拉尔应召而去，后来和拉·马林切一同为科尔特斯做翻译。格雷罗则组织防御，击退了弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍1527年和1528年的远征；1536年，他率查克特马尔的五十艘战舟远赴洪都拉斯对西班牙人作战，中火绳枪身亡。1540年代，加斯帕尔·帕切科的血腥征剿灭亡了这个政区，幸存人口被并入西属尤卡坦。西班牙移民始终稀少，约从1640年起，英国伐木工进入各河口采伐欧洲织布业需要的染料木。1783年《凡尔赛条约》允许英国在翁多河与伯利兹河之间伐木，这就是后来英属洪都拉斯的前身。

en:
The Zapotecs called themselves the 'people of the clouds' and farmed the three arms of the central valleys of Oaxaca long before 500 BC. Their hilltop capital of Monte Albán ruled the valleys for roughly a thousand years; after the Mixtecs took it, Zaachila in the southern valley became the last Zapotec capital, named for the ruler Zaachila Yoo. In 1444 its coquitao still governed the valley towns from Teitipac to Mitla, whose people traded salt, maguey products and small amounts of cochineal, while the Mixtec kings of Tututepec and Tlaxiaco pressed in from the west and the Mexica of Tenochtitlan looked south.

Mexica armies first raided under Moctezuma I, then in 1486 raised a garrison fortress on the hill of Huaxyácac to hold the road to Tehuantepec, and Ahuitzotl stormed Zaachila in 1495. King Cosijoeza, whose name meant 'storm of knives', strengthened the walls of Guiengola, defeated the Mexica force sent against him, then made peace with Tenochtitlan. When word came that Tenochtitlan had fallen, he ordered his people not to fight, and Francisco de Orozco entered the valleys on 25 November 1521 with almost no bloodshed. The Spanish town laid out beside the old Mexica fort was named Antequera and raised to a city by Charles V in 1532; Dominicans made it a centre for converting the Mixtecs and Zapotecs, and Cortés held the surrounding country as Marquis of the Valley of Oaxaca. Disease cut the native population to a tenth by 1650, though cochineal kept the valleys wealthy.
zh:
萨波特克人自称「云之人」，早在公元前500年以前很久就耕作着瓦哈卡中央谷地的三条支谷。他们的山顶都城阿尔班山统治谷地约一千年；阿尔班山落入米斯特克人之手后，南谷的萨奇拉成为末代萨波特克都城，得名自首领萨奇拉·约奥。1444年，萨奇拉的国王仍统辖着从特伊蒂帕克到米特拉的谷地诸镇，居民以盐、龙舌兰制品和少量胭脂虫交易；西边图特佩克和特拉西亚科的米斯特克诸王不断进逼，特诺奇蒂特兰的纳瓦人则把目光投向南方。

纳瓦军队最早在蒙特祖马一世治下来攻，1486年又在瓦基亚卡克山筑起驻军要塞，扼守通往特万特佩克的道路，阿维特索特尔则在1495年攻陷萨奇拉。国王科西霍埃萨（名字意为「刀之风暴」）加固吉恩戈拉的城墙，击败前来征讨的纳瓦军队，随后与特诺奇蒂特兰议和。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落的消息传来，他命族人不得抵抗，1521年11月25日，弗朗西斯科·德·奥罗斯科几乎兵不血刃地进入谷地。西班牙人在旧纳瓦要塞旁建起城镇，取名安特克拉，1532年由查理五世立为城市；多明我会以此为向米斯特克人和萨波特克人传教的中心，科尔特斯则以瓦哈卡谷地侯爵的身份领有四周乡野。到1650年，疫病使原住民人口减至十分之一，但胭脂虫仍维持着谷地的富庶。

en:
The low limestone shore of the Bay of Campeche has no rivers, so its Maya towns grew up around wells; older cities such as Edzná stood inland. War between the Cocom and Tutul-Xiu from 1441 tore apart the League of Mayapán and broke the peninsula into rival chiefdoms; the priest-ruler Ah k'iin Peech founded his own on this coast, Kaan Pech. In 1444 it was an independent Yucatec-speaking town of temples and cotton tribute, trading along a shore where no European ship had yet anchored.

The first one came on 22 March 1517, when Francisco Hernández de Córdoba landed to fill water casks, the first Spaniards to stand on Yucatán. The local lord asked whether they came 'from where the sun rises' and spoke the word 'Castilán'; his priests lit copal and reeds and told the strangers to leave before the fire burned out. They did, and Bernal Díaz del Castillo later thought the town had held perhaps 36,000 people. A Spanish post founded in 1531 was abandoned, and on 4 October 1540 Francisco de Montejo the Younger laid out San Francisco de Campeche, the base from which the Spanish finished the conquest of Yucatán.

The port shipped palo de tinte dyewood, salt, sugar and timber and built ships, and its wealth drew Dutch, English and French raiders for nearly 160 years; the sacks of 1633 and 1663 were only the worst of many visits, and Henry Morgan was among the captains who took prizes in the bay. In 1685 Laurens de Graaf, 'Lorencillo', seized the town and held it two months loading silver and jewels, then threw his plunder overboard to outrun three Spanish frigates. Work on the walls began the next year to the plan of French engineer Louis Bouchard de Becour. Finished in 1704, they ran 2,560 metres around the town in an irregular hexagon with eight bastions and four gates, and the older Fuerte de San Miguel and the Fuerte de San José el Alto, finished in 1762, crowned the hills covering the land approaches. Charles III made Campeche a city in 1777, and in September 1821 it declared for the Plan of Iguala.
zh:
坎佩切湾沿岸是低平的石灰岩海岸，地表没有河流，玛雅城镇多依水井而建，更古老的埃兹纳等城市则坐落内陆。1441年开始的科科姆人与图图尔-休人之战撕裂了马亚潘联盟，半岛分裂为彼此征战的城邦，祭司统治者阿·金·佩奇在这一带海岸建立了自己的坎佩切。1444年，它是一个讲尤卡坦语的独立城邦，有神殿、棉布贡赋和沿海贸易，欧洲船只还不曾在此停泊。

第一艘欧洲船1517年3月22日到来，弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦上岸补充淡水，这是西班牙人第一次踏上尤卡坦。当地首领问他们是否「从日出之处而来」，还说出了「卡斯蒂兰」这个词；祭司们点燃柯巴脂和芦苇，命这些外人在火熄灭前离开。西班牙人随即离去，贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯·德尔·卡斯蒂略后来估计，这座城镇约有三万六千人。1531年西班牙人设立的据点很快放弃；1540年10月4日，小弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍营建圣弗朗西斯科·德·坎佩切，西班牙人正是以这里为基地完成了对尤卡坦的征服。

这座港口输出染木、盐、蔗糖和木材，还发展造船业，财富也引来了荷兰、英国和法国袭掠者近一百六十年的侵扰；1633年和1663年的两次洗劫只是众多袭击中最惨重的，亨利·摩根也曾在湾中劫走船只。1685年，绰号「洛伦西略」的劳伦斯·德格拉夫攻占城镇，占据两个月，拼命装载银器和珠宝，撤离时为甩掉三艘西班牙护卫舰的追击，把赃物抛进海里。筑城工程次年动工，由法国工程师路易·布沙尔·德·贝库尔设计，1704年完工：城墙周长2560米，围出不规则的六边形，八座棱堡、四座城门；较早建成的圣米格尔堡和1762年完工的圣何塞阿尔托堡雄踞城外高地，控制陆路通道。卡洛斯三世1777年将坎佩切升格为城市；1821年9月，坎佩切宣布拥护伊瓜拉计划。

en:
Sotuta was a Yucatec Maya kuchkabal in the plains of north-central Yucatán, founded on a blood feud. The Cocom family had headed the league of Mayapan for more than two hundred years, keeping members of the other noble houses in the capital as virtual hostages, until 1441, when Ah Xiu Xupan of the rival Xiu family had the Cocom household killed and Mayapan sacked and burned. One Cocom heir survived because he was away trading in Honduras; on his return he built Sotuta, and its halach uinik ruled as his descendant and claimed descent from Kukulkan. The peninsula broke into warring city-states, and in 1444 the young polity was fighting the Tutul-Xiu of Maní, Ah Kin Chel and Hocaba.

Of the Maya lords who faced the Montejos' conquest, Nachi Cocom of Sotuta, whom the Spanish called el Señor de Sotuta, held out the longest. He was defeated at the ruins of T'ho in 1542, the ground on which Mérida was then founded, and accepted baptism as Juan Cocom; his town passed into the encomienda. Resistance near Sotuta was not finished. In November 1761 Jacinto Canek, a Maya baker born Jacinto Uc who had taken the old Itza royal name Canek, raised the village of Cisteil against Spanish rule and had himself crowned in its church with a saint's crown. Militia stormed Cisteil on 26 November and burned it with about five hundred of its defenders. Canek was captured and, on 14 December 1761, broken and burned in the main plaza of Mérida, his ashes scattered.
zh:
索图塔是尤卡坦半岛中北部平原上的尤卡坦玛雅城邦，它的建立源于一场灭门血仇。科科姆家族作为玛雅潘联盟的首领统治了两百多年，把其他贵族家族的成员留在都城中形同人质。1441年，仇家休氏的阿赫·休·舒潘诛灭科科姆全族，玛雅潘也遭劫掠焚毁。一位科科姆继承人因远在洪都拉斯经商而幸免，归来后建起索图塔，历代首领以哈拉奇·维尼克的身份统治，自称库库尔坎的后裔。半岛就此分裂成互相攻战的城邦，1444年的索图塔正同马尼的图图尔-休、阿金切尔和奥卡巴交战。

在迎击蒙特霍家族征服的玛雅首领中，被西班牙人称为「索图塔大人」的纳奇·科科姆抵抗最久。1542年他在特奥遗址战败，西班牙人随后在这片土地上修建梅里达；纳奇受洗改名胡安·科科姆，索图塔被划入监护征赋制。但这一带的抵抗并未结束。1761年11月，出生时名叫哈辛托·乌克的玛雅面包匠哈辛托·卡内克在索图塔附近的西斯泰尔村起事反西，他借用伊察王族古老的名号卡内克，还在村中教堂里用圣像的王冠为自己加冕。殖民民兵11月26日攻破西斯泰尔并放火烧村，约五百名守者死于火中。卡内克被俘，1761年12月14日在梅里达大广场被打断骨后焚死，骨灰遭扬散。

en:
The Mixteca Costa is the hot, wet Pacific slope below the Mixtec highlands, with the lower Río Verde valley at its centre. The Mixtec codices tell how Eight Deer Jaguar Claw led a band of highland Mixtecs to the coast around 1083 and built Tututepec, Yucu Dzaa in Mixtec and Totopec in Nahuatl, the 'hill of the bird'. He and his successors subdued dozens of towns from the Chatino country to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, and cacao, feathers, slaves and soldiers flowed to the capital as tribute while conquered rulers stayed in place under governors sent from Tututepec. By 1444 it was the strongest of the four great Mixtec lordships, and the only Mixtec state that had never submitted to the Aztec Empire while Mexica armies pressed into Oaxaca.

Aztec armies never broke it. Tizoc and Ahuitzotl sent expeditions against the coast, and the lords of Tututepec fought Ahuitzotl in alliance with the Zapotec king of Zaachila; Moctezuma II campaigned there from 1503 to 1511 and took only outlying towns such as Tlaxiaco. In 1522, after the fall of Tenochtitlan, Pedro de Alvarado marched south with Zapotec allies from Tehuantepec and took Tututepec, capturing its lord, extorting gold worth thirty thousand pesos and leaving him to die in captivity. That March Hernán Cortés had the town refounded as Segura de la Frontera. Through the rest of the colonial period the humid lowlands were planted with cotton, and their trade ran to Acapulco rather than the city of Oaxaca, until the coast entered independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
米斯特卡海岸是米斯特克高地下方炎热多雨的太平洋坡地，下贝尔德河谷居中。米斯特克手抄本记载，约1083年，「鹿八日虎爪」率领一批高地米斯特克人来到海滨，建立图图特佩克；它在米斯特克语中称尤库扎阿（Yucu Dzaa），纳瓦特尔语称托托佩克（Totopec），意为「鸟山」。他和后继者征服了从查蒂诺人（Chatino）地区到特万特佩克地峡的数十座城镇，可可、羽毛、奴隶和士兵作为贡赋源源送往都城，被征服者的君位得以保留，但要接受图图特佩克派来的官员监督。到1444年，它已是米斯特克四大政权中最强的一个，也是墨西卡军队逼入瓦哈卡时唯一不曾臣服阿兹特克帝国的米斯特克国家。

阿兹特克军队始终没能打垮它。蒂索克和阿维特索特尔先后向沿海发兵，图图特佩克君主与扎奇拉的萨波特克国王联军迎战阿维特索特尔；蒙特苏马二世1503年至1511年在此作战，也只夺下特拉希亚科（Tlaxiaco）等边镇。1521年特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多1522年会同特万特佩克的萨波特克盟军南下，攻陷图图特佩克，擒获其君主，勒索价值三万比索的黄金后任他死于囚中。同年3月，科尔特斯下令将此城改建为塞古拉德拉弗龙特拉。殖民时期余下的年代里，湿润低地广种棉花，贸易多走阿卡普尔科而非瓦哈卡城，直到1821年海岸并入独立的墨西哥。

en:
Tohancapan covers the Gulf shore between the Cazones and Tecolutla rivers and the cedar-covered Sierra Papanteca ridges later centred on Papantla. El Tajín had stood in these hills from about 600, a city of temples, palaces and many ballcourts, with the Pyramid of the Niches rising above its plazas. It controlled routes along the Veracruz coast until fire and Chichimec pressure destroyed it early in the thirteenth century. Totonac survivors founded Papantla around 1200, while Tuzapán remained the stronger Postclassic town. In 1444 this was free Totonac country: fishing villages worked the shore, and the forests supplied cedar, cotton, cacao, honey, fruit and the vanilla orchid that became the region's most valuable export.

Moctezuma II later added Papantla to the Mexica tribute province of Tochpan; its towns sent mantles, chilies and maize, and Tuzapán sent warriors against Tlaxcala. The Totonacs allied with the Spaniards in 1519, and Papantla was refounded as Papantla de Santa María de la Asunción; vanilla from its forests soon reached European buyers. In 1785 Diego Ruiz found the overgrown Pyramid of the Niches while searching for illegal tobacco fields, and his report in the Gaceta de Mexico brought El Tajín to the attention of New Spain's antiquarians. During the independence war Serafín Olarte gathered Totonac guerrillas around Papantla. From 1813 until his capture and execution in 1820 he kept royalist forces out of parts of the sierra, while insurgents used Tecolutla to land arms.
zh:
托安卡潘位于卡索内斯河与特科卢特洛河之间的墨西哥湾海岸，以及后来以帕潘特拉为中心、雪松遍布的帕潘特拉山地。埃尔塔欣约自600年起立城于这些丘陵间，城中有神庙、宫殿和许多球场，壁龛金字塔高踞广场之上。它曾控制韦拉克鲁斯沿岸道路，13世纪初毁于战火和奇奇梅克人的压力。约1200年，托托纳克幸存者建立帕潘特拉，图萨潘则是后古典时代更强的城镇。1444年，这里仍是独立的托托纳克土地：渔村利用海岸资源，森林提供雪松、棉花、可可、蜂蜜、水果和香荚兰，后者后来成为当地最有价值的出口物。

蒙特苏马二世后来把帕潘特拉并入墨西加的托奇潘纳贡省；各城镇缴纳披布、辣椒和玉米，图萨潘还出兵协助攻打特拉斯卡拉。1519年，托托纳克人与西班牙人结盟，帕潘特拉以圣玛丽亚·德·拉·阿森松·德·帕潘特拉之名重建，当地森林的香荚兰很快卖给欧洲买主。1785年，迭戈·鲁伊斯在查缉私种烟草时发现被丛林掩没的壁龛金字塔，他在《墨西哥公报》上的报告使埃尔塔欣受到新西班牙古物学者注意。独立战争期间，塞拉芬·奥拉特在帕潘特拉周围聚集托托纳克游击队。1813年至1820年被俘处死前，他使保王军无法完全控制部分山地；起义军还利用特科卢特洛接运登陆武器。

en:
The Tlapanecs, who call themselves Me'phaa, farm the steep Pacific slope of
Guerrero east of Acapulco. Around the great semicircular bay lived their
close kin the Yopi, whose country bore the Nahua name Yopitzinco;
Acapulco itself means 'place of the big reeds'. They grew maize, cotton and
cacao in the hot coastal pockets, worked gold and precious stones in the
mountains, and worshipped Xipe Totec, the flayed god whose cult the Mexica
learned from them. The Yopi were bowmen and stubborn fighters: ringed by
Aztec power, they kept their independence and even attended coronations in
Tenochtitlan as honoured guests. In 1444 Acapulco was a scatter of fishing
and cotton villages around one of the finest anchorages on the South Sea,
paying tribute to no one.

Ahuitzotl's armies campaigned here for four years at the end of the
century and set up a military post, but the Yopi kept the land and the post
never took hold. Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte led the first Spaniards
ashore on 13 December 1523, and in 1528 the crown took the bay directly as
the 'City of the Kings'. Cortés laid out shipyards and the first road to
Mexico City, and thirty Spanish families settled beside the port in 1550.
After Andrés de Urdaneta found the westerly track across the Pacific in
1565, the Manila galleons, known in New Spain as La Nao de China, made
Acapulco their terminus from 1571. Each year a galleon crammed with
Chinese silk and porcelain, spices and ivory exchanged its cargo for
Mexican silver at the fair, and the town tripled for the market; Acapulco
became the second port of New Spain after Veracruz. In January 1614 the
Japanese embassy of the samurai Hasekura Tsunenaga landed here, more than a
hundred Japanese Christians with two dozen samurai, on their way to Europe.

The galleon cargoes drew raiders. A Dutch fleet sacked the town in 1615 and
was driven off only after hard fighting, and the Fort of San Diego rose
above the bay to guard the next fair. It was wrecked by the earthquake of
1776 and rebuilt within seven years. In the wars of independence Morelos'
insurgents burned the town and took it on 12 April 1813, and the fort
surrendered on 16 August. Royalists retook both on 12 April 1814; the
galleon run, cut by the fighting, never resumed. Acapulco joined the
Mexican Empire on 15 October 1821.
zh:
特拉帕内克人自称梅帕人，在阿卡普尔科以东、格雷罗陡峭的太平洋山坡上耕
作。半圆形大海湾周围住着他们的近亲约佩人，这片地方的纳瓦语名字叫约佩
钦科；「阿卡普尔科」本身则意为「大芦苇之地」。他们在炎热的滨海低地种
植玉米、棉花和可可，在山里采炼黄金和宝石，敬奉剥皮之神西佩托特克，墨
西卡人正是经由他们才知道这一信仰。约佩人善射剽悍：虽被阿兹特克的势力
包围，仍保住独立，甚至作为贵客前往特诺奇蒂特兰参加君主加冕礼。1444年
的阿卡普尔科，只是南海一处上佳锚地旁散落的渔村和棉乡，不向任何人纳
贡。

世纪末，阿维措特尔的军队在此征战四年，设下一个军站，但军站始终没能扎
稳，土地仍在约佩人手中。1523年12月13日，胡安·罗德里格斯·德·维拉富
埃尔特率第一批西班牙人上岸；1528年王室直接接管海湾，称「诸王之城」。
科尔特斯在此修建船厂和通往墨西哥城的第一条道路，1550年三十户西班牙家
庭移居港畔。1565年安德烈斯·德·乌尔达内塔找到横跨太平洋的东返航路后，
在新西班牙被称作「中国船」的马尼拉大帆船从1571年起以阿卡普尔科为终
点。每年大帆船满载中国丝绸、瓷器、香料和象牙进港，在市集上把货物换成
墨西哥白银，城镇人口因市集膨胀到平时的三倍，阿卡普尔科成了新西班牙仅
次于韦拉克鲁斯的第二大港。1614年1月，武士支仓常长率领的日本使团在此
上岸，百余名日本基督徒与二十多名武士取道前往欧洲。

大帆船上的货物也引来劫掠者。1615年一支荷兰舰队洗劫城镇，苦战后才被击
退，圣迭戈要塞随即在海湾上方建起，以护卫来年的市集。要塞毁于1776年地
震，七年后重建。独立战争中，莫雷洛斯的起义军焚毁城区，1813年4月12日夺
取全城，8月16日迫使要塞投降；王师于1814年4月12日将两者一并收复。大
帆船航路已被战火切断，再未恢复。1821年10月15日，阿卡普尔科并入墨西哥
帝国。

en:
Tlaxcala was a Nahua confederation on the altiplano east of the Valley of Mexico, made up of four towns, Tepeticpac, Ocotelolco, Tizatlan and Quiahuiztlan, which had joined forces in the fourteenth century. The Mexica of Tenochtitlan never broke it. Yearly flower wars between the two states were fought to take sacrificial captives rather than to conquer, while Aztec armies swallowed the peoples around it and cut the Tlaxcalans off from Gulf-coast cotton and salt. In 1444 the four towns were a crowded independent enclave inside the Aztec orbit, each under its own tlatoani, living on the maize lands of the upper Atoyac. In Nahuatl the name means 'place of the corn tortillas'.

Cortes entered the Tlaxcalan passes in September 1519 and beat off the attacks led by Xicohtencatl the Younger; his father, the old lord of Tizatlan, was among the rulers who then took the Spaniards into alliance. Tlaxcalan warriors marched on Tenochtitlan that November and sheltered the broken Spanish army after the Noche Triste of 1520. For the final siege the shipwright Martin Lopez had thirteen brigantines prefabricated here, and Tlaxcalan porters carried the pieces over the pass to Texcoco, where they were reassembled on the lake. Xicohtencatl the Younger, who had turned against the alliance, left the camp before the siege and was hanged on Cortes's orders in 1521. Tlaxcalan troops made up most of the army that destroyed Tenochtitlan that August.

The Spanish laid out Tlaxcala town in 1522 as a centre of evangelization, and Franciscan friars arrived two years later, raising one of the first four Franciscan monasteries in the Americas on a hill above the town. For their part in the conquest the Tlaxcalans kept their native cabildo and their tribute exemption through three colonial centuries. Charles V granted the town a coat of arms in 1535, and when the crown lagged on its promises the lords answered with the Lienzo de Tlaxcala, a painted codex setting out all they had done for Spain. Cochineal red dye made local merchants' fortunes, and in 1591 some four hundred Tlaxcalan families moved north to settle the Chichimec frontier, taking their tribute exemption with them. Tlaxcala entered independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
特拉斯卡拉是墨西哥谷以东高原上的纳瓦人同盟，由特佩特克帕克、奥科特洛尔科、蒂萨特兰和基亚维斯特兰四镇在14世纪结成。特诺奇蒂特兰的墨西加人始终没能打垮它：双方年年进行荣冠战争，为的是俘获人牲而非灭国；阿兹特克军队吞并周边诸族后，又切断了特拉斯卡拉人通往墨西哥湾沿岸的棉花与食盐之路。1444年，四镇在阿兹特克势力的包围中守着一块人烟稠密的独立飞地，各由自己的特拉托阿尼统领，靠阿托亚克河上游的玉米地为生，其名在纳瓦语中意为「玉米饼之地」。

1519年9月，科尔特斯率军突入特拉斯卡拉山口，击退小希科滕卡特尔率领的阻击；他的父亲、蒂萨特兰的老首领是随后决定与西班牙人结盟的几位首领之一。当年11月，特拉斯卡拉战士随科尔特斯进军特诺奇蒂特兰，1520年「悲痛之夜」后又收容了溃败的西班牙军。为了最后的围攻，造船匠马丁·洛佩斯在当地预制了十三艘双桅帆船，特拉斯卡拉脚夫把船件翻过山口运到特斯科科，在湖边重新组装。反对结盟的小希科滕卡特尔在围城前离开营地，1521年被科尔特斯下令绞死；同年8月攻陷特诺奇蒂特兰的大军，主体就是特拉斯卡拉战士。

1522年，西班牙人规划特拉斯卡拉城作为传教中心，方济各会士两年后抵达，在城边小山上建起美洲最早的四座方济各会修道院之一。因征服有功，特拉斯卡拉人在殖民时期三百年间保留了土著市政会和免贡特权。卡洛斯五世1535年颁赐城徽；当王室迟迟不兑现承诺时，首领们以《特拉斯卡拉画布》作答，用这部彩绘抄本列明他们为西班牙立下的功劳。胭脂虫红染料让本地商人致富，1591年约四百户特拉斯卡拉人家带着免贡特权北迁，前往奇奇梅克边疆屯垦。1821年，特拉斯卡拉加入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Zacatula, Zacatotlán in Nahuatl, sat at the mouth of the Balsas River, where the hot Tierra Caliente plain opens onto the Pacific. Cuitlatec farmers and fishermen lived among its lagoons and river bars, and the shore track made the place a stopping point for peoples moving up and down the coast. In the fifteenth century both the Purépecha and the Aztecs pressed on the Cuitlatec dominion; Aztec armies stormed Cuitlatepan in 1497 and folded this coast into the tributary province of Cihuatlán.

Spaniards soon valued the river bar for another reason. After Tenochtitlan fell, Cortés sent Gonzalo de Umbría and Juan Álvarez Chico to scout the gold here, and in 1523 Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte and Simón de Cuenca destroyed the old settlement and founded the Villa de la Concepción with 122 Spaniards, the first Spanish municipal seat on New Spain's Pacific coast. Beside the Barra de Zacatula they built the fortified Puerto de Santiago, New Spain's first Pacific shipyard, where brigantines were fitted out to explore the Mar del Sur. Sacked and burned in the later sixteenth century, the town was rebuilt in the seventeenth century beside the Hacienda de la Orilla at the river mouth, where a new shipyard made it a naval staging post again. During the independence war José María Morelos, the parish priest who commanded the insurgents in the south, put Zacatula into his province of Técpan in 1811, and in 1814, after his defeats at Coyuca and Acapulco, he reorganized three hundred men here while preparing the constitution sanctioned that year at Apatzingán.
zh:
萨卡图拉，纳瓦特尔语称萨卡托特兰，位于巴尔萨斯河入海口，铁拉卡连特的炎热平原在此直面太平洋。库伊特拉特克农民和渔民住在潟湖与河口沙洲之间，沿岸通道使这里成为人群沿海岸往来的落脚点。15世纪，普雷佩查和阿兹特克都向库伊特拉特克人的领地施压；1497年阿兹特克军队攻陷库伊特拉特潘，把这片海岸并入朝贡省份西瓦坦。

西班牙人很快看上了这块河口沙洲的另一种价值。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，科尔特斯先派贡萨洛·德·翁布里亚和胡安·阿尔瓦雷斯·奇科来此探查金矿；1523年，胡安·罗德里格斯·德比利亚富埃尔特和西蒙·德·昆卡毁掉旧聚落，率一百二十二名西班牙人建立康塞普西翁镇，这是新西班牙太平洋沿岸第一个西班牙市镇治所。他们在萨卡图拉沙洲旁修筑设防的圣地亚哥港——新西班牙太平洋上的第一座船厂，双桅帆船在这里装配出航，探索「南海」。该镇在16世纪后期遭洗劫焚毁，居民17世纪时在河口的奥里利亚庄园旁重建，新船厂让它重新成为海上集结地。独立战争中，由教区神父成为南方起义军统帅的何塞·马里亚·莫雷洛斯1811年把萨卡图拉划入他设立的特克潘省；1814年，在科尤卡和阿卡普尔科接连战败后，他在此重整三百人的队伍，同时筹备当年在阿帕钦甘通过的宪法。

en:
The Mexica were latecomers to the Valley of Mexico. In 1325 they built
Tenochtitlan on a marshy island in Lake Texcoco, at the promised sign of
an eagle on a cactus, then enlarged it with chinampa gardens and three
causeways to shore. They served Azcapotzalco as mercenaries until Itzcoatl
and the exiled Nezahualcoyotl overthrew that city in 1428 and, with
Tlacopan, formed the Triple Alliance; Moctezuma I, ruler from 1440, made
his city its senior partner. Above the roofs rose the Templo Mayor, twin
shrines to the war god Huitzilopochtli and the rain god Tlaloc, rebuilt six
times. By 1444 chinampa maize and tribute fed the island, and Tlatelolco's
market drew merchants from across central Mexico, with cacao beans passing
as small change.

After the floods of the 1490s Ahuitzotl rebuilt both city and temple on a
grander scale. When Cortés entered on 8 November 1519, Tenochtitlan held
perhaps 200,000 people, among the largest cities on earth. He seized
Moctezuma II, was driven out on the Noche Triste of 30 June 1520, and
returned with Tlaxcalan allies to starve it in a ninety-three-day siege.
Cuauhtémoc surrendered on 13 August 1521; the victors razed the temples
and built Mexico City over the same canals and causeways, a Spanish grid
around the Plaza Mayor ringed by indigenous San Juan Tenochtitlan. The
viceroyalty of New Spain followed in 1535. Juan Pablos printed the first
books in the Americas in 1539, and the royal university was chartered in
1551.

The lake that fed the city also threatened it. The great Desagüe drainage
works could not stop the inundation of 1629, when streets stood under water
for five years and the court spoke of moving the capital. Rioters twice
stormed the viceregal palace over grain prices and church quarrels, chasing
out the Marquess of Gelves in 1624; famine mobs burned it in 1692. The
Metropolitan Cathedral rose beside the Zócalo over more than two centuries
and was finished in 1813. The poet Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, the 'Tenth
Muse', spent her last 27 years in the Jeronymite convent of San Jerónimo,
writing verse and defending women's learning. The engraving school founded
in 1781 became the Royal Academy of San Carlos, first of its kind in the
Americas.

Hidalgo's insurgents beat the royalists at Monte de las Cruces in September
1810, close enough to see the capital, yet turned away. The city held to
the crown until Iturbide entered at the head of the Army of the Three
Guarantees on 27 September 1821.
zh:
墨西卡人是墨西哥谷地的后来者。1325年，他们在特斯科科湖的沼泽岛上建起
特诺奇蒂特兰——正是神谕所示鹰栖仙人掌之地，又用奇南帕园圃扩岛，以三条
长堤连接湖岸。他们曾作为雇佣兵为阿斯卡波察尔科效力，直到1428年伊兹科阿
特尔与流亡的特斯科科君主内萨瓦尔科约特尔联手攻灭该城，又和特拉科潘结成
三邦同盟；1440年即位的蒙特苏马一世把这座城市经营成同盟之首。屋顶上方
矗立着大神庙，两座塔顶神殿分别供奉战神威齐洛波契特里和雨神特拉洛克，神
庙先后重建六次。1444年，奇南帕玉米和属邦贡赋养活湖岛，邻城特拉特洛尔科
的大市集吸引中墨西哥各处的商人，可可豆在摊位上当零钱使用。

1490年代的洪水过后，阿维措特尔把城市和大神庙都按更宏大的规模重建。
1519年11月8日科尔特斯入城时，特诺奇蒂特兰约有二十万人，是当时世界上最
大的城市之一。他囚禁蒙特苏马二世，1520年6月30日「悲痛之夜」被逐出
城，随后率特拉斯卡盟友回师，围城九十三天，以饥饿困取该城。夸乌特莫克于
1521年8月13日投降；征服者拆毁神庙，在原有运河与长堤的格局上建起墨西哥
城：马约尔广场周围是西班牙式棋盘街区，外圈是土著的圣胡安·特诺奇蒂特
兰。1535年设立新西班牙总督区。1539年胡安·帕布洛斯印出美洲的第一批书
籍，皇家大学于1551年奉敕设立。

养活城市的湖水也威胁着城市。宏大的德萨格埃排水工程未能挡住1629年的大
洪水，街道被淹达五年之久，宫廷甚至讨论迁都。民众因粮价和教会争端两次攻
入总督府：1624年赫尔韦斯侯爵被逐出城外，1692年饥荒中的民众烧毁宫殿。都
主教座堂在索卡洛广场旁修了两个多世纪，到1813年才完工。有「第十缪斯」之
称的诗人胡安娜·伊内斯·德·拉·克鲁兹在圣赫罗尼莫修道院度过最后二十七
年，在那里写诗、为女性求知的权利辩护。1781年创办的雕刻学校后来成为圣卡
洛斯皇家学院，是美洲第一所这类学校。

1810年9月，伊达尔戈的起义军在蒙特·德·拉斯·克鲁塞斯击败王师，战场近
得可以望见都城，他们却转身撤走。墨西哥城一直效忠王室，直到1821年9月27
日伊图尔维德率三保证军入城。

en:
Tlapacoyan sits in the Nautla country of Veracruz, where streams off the eastern highlands gather into the Bobos River and run down to the Gulf coast. Its Nahuatl name is read locally as the place where a person is washed and purified. The district belonged to Totonacapan, the Totonac country that stretched between the Cazones and Papaloapan rivers; Totonac farmers had tilled vanilla orchids there since before 1200, using the pods as temple perfume and as flavouring, and cotton grew in the warm lowland fields. In 1444 the villages here were still Totonac speaking, tied to their neighbours by markets and by the road climbing from the small port of Nautla into the highlands. Mexica armies reached the district only in 1472 and held it for forty-seven years; villagers kept their Totonac tongue, and Nahuatl spread little beyond the local nobility. When Cortés landed in 1519 the Totonacs joined his march against Tenochtitlan, and the road past Tlapacoyan to Nautla was later associated with his route inland.

Spanish families built a sugar mill beside the old native settlements in 1608. Two neighbouring villages, Zacayucan and Chilacan, were resettled around it and remain the town's Santiago and San Pedro wards, Totonac and Mexica in origin; in 1610 the old community of Santa María Yohualtlacualoyan took the name Tlapacoyan. A viceregal grant of one year's tribute exemption in 1683 paid for its parish church. Sugar, cotton and, from about 1739, organized tobacco plantations tied the town to coastal trade: flour, maize, timber, vanilla, bananas and tobacco went down the Bobos to Nautla and on to Veracruz, and the roadside inns lodged travellers and their pack animals between the port and the plateau.
zh:
特拉帕科扬地处韦拉克鲁斯的瑙特拉一带，东部高地的溪流汇成博博斯河，流向墨西哥湾。其名是纳瓦特尔语，当地释为「洗涤、净化人身之地」。这片地区属于托托纳卡潘，即夹在卡索内斯河与帕帕洛阿潘河之间的托托纳克人之地；1200年以前，托托纳克农人已在此栽种香荚兰，把豆荚用作庙里的香料和食物的调味，温暖的低地还出产棉花。1444年时，此地村落仍通用托托纳克语，靠市集和一条自小港瑙特拉通向高地的道路与邻地往来。墨西卡军队1472年才进入此地，统治四十七年；村民一直说托托纳克语，纳瓦特尔语几乎只在当地贵族中通行。1519年科尔特斯登陆后，托托纳克人随他进军特诺奇蒂特兰，经过特拉帕科扬通往瑙特拉的道路后来也被认为是他内陆行军路线的一部分。

1608年，西班牙家庭在旧土著聚落旁建起甘蔗榨制场。邻村萨卡尤坎和奇拉坎被安置在场边，即后来的圣地亚哥坊和圣佩德罗坊，两村分别源自托托纳克人和墨西加人；1610年，旧聚落圣玛利亚·约瓦尔特拉夸洛扬改名特拉帕科扬。1683年，总督准许全镇免贡一年，用这笔钱修建教区教堂。甘蔗、棉花和约1739年起成片种植的烟草，把小镇系在沿海贸易上：面粉、玉米、木材、香荚兰、香蕉和烟草顺博博斯河运到瑙特拉，再转往韦拉克鲁斯；路旁的客栈接待往返于港口和高原之间的旅人及其驮畜。

en:
The province covers a stretch of Pacific coast and the wooded Sierra Madre
behind it, from the broad bay of Banderas to the mangrove coves that became
San Blas. The shore belonged to the kingdom of Xalisco. Its Pinomes, the
'Nahuas of Nayarit', grew maize on the coastal plain, fished the Pacific,
and traded cotton, salt and the feathers of the western forests. Xalisco's
rulers kept their seat in the Matatipac valley at the foot of Coatépec hill
above Tepic, and sent coastal produce up to central Mexico. South along the
coast lay the Tecos kingdom of Colimán, while Coras and Huicholes held the
northern mountains. In 1444 this was the western edge of the Mesoamerican
world, a line of fishing towns and island coves within the Xalisco sphere.

The kingdom's last ruler was a queen. Pupualtzin was the only heir of the
tlatoani captured and sacrificed while fighting for Colimán against the
Purépecha in the Saltpeter War, and she held the regency from 1508 before
taking the throne. Under her Xalisco absorbed Sayula, the home country of
the Sayultecas, and the neighbouring señoríos. She received Francisco
Cortés de San Buenaventura, Cortés's cousin, in peace in 1525. Nuño de
Guzmán gave the west a harsher conquest: he burned Xalisco in 1530, hunted
the queen through the Sierra, defeated her army near Aguamilpa and had her
publicly hanged at Tepic in 1532, while founding Santiago de Compostela as
the capital of his Nuevo Reino de Galicia. The country rose again in the
Mixtón War of 1540; Pedro de Alvarado died in its fighting before the
viceroy's army broke the revolt.

San Blas was a late-colonial creation. José de Gálvez founded the port in
1768 as the naval base and shipyard for expeditions to the Californias. One
of its ships, the schooner Sonora, carried Bodega y Quadra as far as the
Alaskan coast in 1775. It was a poor harbour all the same: mangrove swamps
hemmed it in, no more than four vessels could anchor at a time, and fevers
were endemic. Alessandro Malaspina found the place so unhealthy that in
1791 he moved his squadron south to Acapulco. When the wars of independence
reached the west, San Blas declared for the Plan de Iguala on 25 July 1821.
zh:
本省涵盖一段太平洋海岸和背后林木茂密的西马德雷山脉，从宽阔的班德拉斯湾
一直到后来成为圣布拉斯的红树海湾。这片海岸属于哈利斯科王国。境内的皮诺
梅人即「纳亚里特的纳瓦人」，在滨海平原种玉米，在太平洋上捕鱼，贩卖棉
花、湖盐和西部山林的禽羽。哈利斯科的统治者以特皮克上方、科阿特佩克山麓
的马塔蒂帕克谷地为中枢，把滨海物产送往中墨西哥。沿海岸向南是特科斯人的
科利曼王国，科拉人和维乔尔人则据守北部山地。1444年，这里是中美洲世界的
西缘，一串渔镇与岛礁海湾都处在哈利斯科的势力范围内。

王国最后一位统治者是位女王。普普阿尔钦是国王的独女，其父在「硝石战
争」中协助科利曼对普雷佩查人作战，被俘后献祭而死；她自1508年起摄政，
后来继位。在她治下，哈利斯科吞并了萨约尔特卡斯人的家乡萨乌拉以及邻近的
酋长国。1525年，她和平接待了科尔特斯的堂弟弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣
布埃纳文图拉。努尼奥·德·古斯曼给西部带来的则是另一种征服：1530年他焚
毁哈利斯科城，把女王追进深山，在阿瓜米尔帕附近击败她的军队，1532年将
她公开绞死在特皮克，同年建立圣地亚哥·德·孔波斯特拉，作为新加利西亚王
国的首府。1540年全境在米什顿战争中再度举兵，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多死在
此役中，最后由总督的大军镇压了起义。

圣布拉斯是殖民时代晚期才建起的港口。1768年，何塞·德·加尔韦斯在此建
港，作为经略加利福尼亚的海军基地和船厂。港中装备出的斯库纳帆船「索诺
拉号」1775年载着博德加·夸德拉一直驶到阿拉斯加海岸。但这里实在算不得
良港：红树沼泽环伺，一次最多停泊四艘船，热病常年流行。亚历杭德罗·马拉
斯皮纳嫌这里太易致病，1791年把自己的船队南移到阿卡普尔科。独立战争波及
西部后，圣布拉斯于1821年7月25日宣布拥护《伊瓜拉计划》。

en:
Between the forested Sierra del Nayar and the Pacific lagoons, the coastal plain from the Río Piaxtla to the Río Santiago belonged to the Totorames, whose chief town was Chiametlán. Heirs of the Aztatlán settlements that grew up on this coast around 900, they planted maize, beans and chile on river fields, took fish and shrimp with weirs, dried their catch and gathered salt to trade with the Cora and Huichol villages in the hills. In 1444 their small chiefdoms answered to no overlord: the Mexica of the central plateau never reached this coast, and southern towns such as Tepic paid tribute only to the lords of Xalisco.

The first Spaniard reached the coast in 1526, when Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura, nephew of Hernán Cortés, took the submission of the local lords; the conquest came with Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán's brutal march of 1530–31. In 1531 Guzmán founded Santiago de Compostela, the first capital of Nueva Galicia, but after the encomendero Juan Ruiz de Arce was killed in 1540 the Spanish town was moved inland, and its old site became Tepic. The Cora in the hills rose in the Mixtón War and were not subdued until 1722. In 1768 Charles III ordered San Blas made a deep-sea naval port, the station for ships bound for California and Sonora; Manila galleons put in there and a royal shipyard built and repaired the crown's vessels. In the 1770s ships out of San Blas carried Juan Pérez to Nootka Sound and Bodega y Quadra to the Alaskan coast, sent to forestall Russian posts farther south. Junípero Serra sailed from San Blas on 12 March 1768 to open the missions of Baja and Alta California. In November 1810 the priest José María Mercado seized Tepic and San Blas for the insurgents, but was defeated and killed on 31 January 1811, and the coast stayed royalist for the rest of the independence war.
zh:
在林木覆盖的奈亚尔山与太平洋潟湖之间，从皮亚斯特拉河到圣地亚哥河的沿海平原属于托托拉梅斯人，首镇是奇阿梅特兰。他们是约900年兴起于此海岸的阿斯特兰诸聚落的后裔，在河畔田地里种玉米、菜豆和辣椒，用鱼梁捕捞鱼虾、把渔获晒干，还煮海为盐，与山区的科拉人和维乔尔人村落交易。1444年，这些小酋邦没有君长：中部高原的墨西加人从未到过这段海岸，特皮克等南方城镇只向哈利斯科的君长纳贡。

第一个西班牙人1526年来到海岸：埃尔南·科尔特斯之侄弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉接受了当地君长的归附；真正的征服伴随努尼奥·贝尔特兰·德·古斯曼1530至1531年的残酷进军而来。1531年，古斯曼建立圣地亚哥·德·孔波斯特拉，这是新加利西亚的第一个首府；1540年监护主胡安·鲁伊斯·德·阿尔塞被杀后，西班牙人城镇迁往内陆，旧址成为特皮克。山区的科拉人在米斯特翁战争中起义，直到1722年才被征服。1768年，卡洛斯三世下令把圣布拉斯辟为深水军港，驻扎前往加利福尼亚和索诺拉的船只；马尼拉大帆船在此停靠，王家船厂为王室修造舰船。1770年代，从圣布拉斯驶出的船把胡安·佩雷斯送到努特卡海峡，把博德加-夸德拉送到阿拉斯加海岸，以防俄国人的据点继续南下。1768年3月12日，胡尼佩罗·塞拉从圣布拉斯启航，前往开创南下、上加利福尼亚的传教区。1810年11月，神父何塞·马里亚·梅尔卡多为起义军夺取特皮克和圣布拉斯，却在1811年1月31日兵败身亡，海岸在独立战争余下的时间里始终效忠王室。

en:
The grassy sierras around the Cerro de la Bufa stand on the high cold plateau the Spaniards later called La Gran Chichimeca, the country of the Zacatecos, one of the Chichimeca peoples. Their Nahuatl name means 'people of the grass': bands of hunters who also worked small plots, moving their camps between waterholes, painting their bodies for war and paying tribute to no one. They already dug silver and lead out of their hills and carried the metal south to trade, so the ore under their hunting grounds was known to be rich before any European reached them. In 1444 the Zacatecos, with the Guachichiles to their east and the Caxcanes to their south, were among the free warrior peoples beyond the Mesoamerican frontier.

In 1546 Juan de Tolosa came down from the Cerro de la Bufa with silver ore, guided there by a native, and a mining camp was founded in 1548 as the Real de Minas de Nuestra Señora de los Zacatecas. The San Bernabé vein was struck at once, and after the finds at Vetagrande, Pánuco and the El Edén mine, Indians, black slaves and adventurers poured in by the thousand. Tolosa's own marriage showed the mixed world of the rush: in 1550 he wed Leonor Cortés Moctezuma, the daughter of Cortés and of Isabel Moctezuma, daughter of the Aztec emperor. The silver went south to Mexico City by armed mule convoy, and from 1550 the Zacatecos and their kinsmen spent half a century raiding those convoys in the Chichimeca War, until presidios, treaties and resettlement bought an uneasy peace. The town became the missionary base for the far north, and friars set out from it for California and Texas. Philip II named it the Very Noble and Loyal City in 1585, and by 1600 only Mexico City was larger in New Spain, its silver underwriting the Habsburg wars in Europe. Mining fortunes paid for the baroque cathedral of carved quarry stone whose walls run from pale pink to burnt orange in the sun. Insurgents under Ignacio López Rayón took the town in 1811, and it swore independence in 1821.
zh:
布法山周围牧草覆盖的群山坐落在高寒高原上，西班牙人后来把这片高原称作「大奇奇梅卡」，萨卡特科人是奇奇梅克诸族之一，世居于此。这个纳瓦特尔语名字意为「草上之民」：他们分成游群，狩猎之余也种小块田地，营地逐水源迁移，战时在身上绘彩，不向任何人纳贡。他们早已在群山里开采银和铅，把金属运到南方交易，所以还没等欧洲人到来，猎场地下埋着富矿就已不是秘密。1444年时，萨卡特科人与东面的瓜奇奇尔人、南面的卡克斯坎人一样，是中美洲边疆之外自由的好战民族。

1546年，胡安·德·托洛萨在一名土著带路下从布法山带回银矿石；1548年，采矿营地正式建立，名为「萨卡特卡斯圣母雷亚尔银矿镇」。圣贝尔纳贝矿脉当年即告发现，贝塔格兰德、帕努科和埃登矿又陆续出矿，成千上万的土著、黑奴和冒险家蜂拥而至。托洛萨本人的婚事也看得出这场淘金潮里新旧世界的交错：1550年，他娶了莱昂诺尔·科尔特斯·蒙特祖玛为妻，她是科尔特斯与阿兹特克皇帝之女伊莎贝尔·蒙特祖玛的女儿。白银由武装骡队南运墨西哥城，从1550年起，萨卡特科人及其亲族用了约半个世纪在奇奇梅克战争中袭掠这些车队，最后靠要塞、和约与重新安置换来勉强的和平。这座镇又成为向遥远北方传教的基地，修士们从这里出发前往加利福尼亚和得克萨斯。1585年腓力二世封它为「至贵至忠之城」，到1600年，它在新西班牙已仅次于墨西哥城，出产的白银支撑着哈布斯堡在欧洲的战争。采矿带来的财富还建起凿石砌筑的巴洛克式大教堂，石墙在阳光下从浅粉变成焦橙。1811年，伊格纳西奥·洛佩斯·雷翁率起义军占领此镇，1821年镇上宣誓独立。

en:
Guachichil covers the dry Potosino highlands east of Zacatecas, where cactus plains, scattered waterholes and the valley later called El Gran Tunal break up travel across the plateau. In 1444 its namesake people were one of the most widespread Chichimeca nations, moving in nomadic and semi-nomadic bands over lands that later became Zacatecas, San Luis Potosí and adjoining deserts. They lived by hunting and gathering, followed war leaders rather than one court, and carried long bows capable of piercing Spanish armour. Their rites centered on local spirits, waterholes and hunting grounds, and neither Aztec tribute collectors nor Spanish miners yet occupied the plateau.

Silver brought soldiers and pack trains across those hunting grounds. After Zacatecas's mines opened, Guachichil raiders made the road a repeated target in the Chichimeca War from the mid-sixteenth century: war parties struck convoys and withdrew into the semidesert. Military campaigns cost men and money without securing the route, so Viceroy Luis de Velasco used Miguel Caldera and the Franciscan Diego de la Magdalena to negotiate, distribute gifts and settle families in fixed towns. In 1591 about 400 Tlaxcalan families were brought north, with Purépecha families following, to farm and offer a model of settled Christian life. Caldera's men verified gold and silver at Cerro de San Pedro in March 1592. The hill lacked water, so San Luis Minas del Potosí was founded in the valley on 3 November 1592, with Juan de Oñate as its first magistrate.
zh:
瓜奇奇尔位于萨卡特卡斯以东的波托西干旱高原，仙人掌荒原、分散水洼和后来被称作大仙人掌谷的河谷使穿行变得困难。1444年，得名所自的瓜奇奇尔人是分布最广的奇奇梅克族群之一，以游猎和半游猎群体活动于后来的萨卡特卡斯、圣路易斯波托西及邻近荒漠。他们狩猎采集，追随善战首领，没有统一宫廷，所用长弓能够射穿西班牙盔甲。各群体的仪式围绕本地神灵、水洼和猎场，阿兹特克收税官和西班牙矿工当时都还没有进入这片高原。

银矿把士兵和驮队带进了这些猎场。萨卡特卡斯开矿后，瓜奇奇尔袭掠者从16世纪中叶起在奇奇梅克战争中反复袭击这条道路：战队攻打车队后便退回半荒漠。军事征伐耗费人力和钱财，却不能保证道路安全，总督路易斯·德·贝拉斯科于是派米格尔·卡尔德拉和方济各会修士迭戈·德拉·马格达莱纳谈判、分发礼物，并把各群体安置到固定城镇。1591年，约400户特拉斯卡拉家庭被迁往北方，普雷佩查家庭随后也加入；他们在当地农耕，作为定居基督教生活的范例。1592年3月，卡尔德拉的人在圣佩德罗山验明金银矿。由于山上缺水，圣路易斯·米纳斯·德尔·波托西于1592年11月3日在河谷建城，胡安·德·奥尼亚特任首任地方长官。

en:
The humid coastal plain around the mouth of the Pánuco, threaded by the Tamesí and other slow rivers and shut off from the sea by long lagoons, was the northern edge of Mesoamerica and the country of the Huastec, the Téenek, whose Mayan tongue had split from its sister languages millennia before. They farmed maize and cotton in the bottomlands under a scatter of local lords rather than a single king, and their towns, set with small temple-pyramids, were known around the gulf for painted pottery and shell work. The river village of Tampico took its name from their word for 'place of otters'. In 1444 the señoríos still governed themselves, though Mexica power was rising to the south.

A generation before the Spanish arrived, the armies of Moctezuma I defeated the Huastec, who paid tribute to Tenochtitlan thereafter while keeping their own lords. Francisco de Garay, governor of Jamaica, sent Alonso Álvarez de Pineda to chart the northern gulf coast; in 1520 Huastec warriors threw his landing party back from the Pánuco. After the fall of Tenochtitlan, Cortés secured the river in 1522. Garay himself arrived with six hundred men to plant a rival colony, lost his legal quarrel with Cortés and died at Mexico City the following year. Nuño de Guzmán's slavers and the first epidemics emptied the old towns. San Luis de Tampico, founded for the Franciscan Andrés de Olmos, lasted until 1684, when pirate raids drove the settlers south of the Pánuco. In 1746 the viceroy granted the empty coast to José de Escandón as the colony of Nuevo Santander, and two years later his settlers began planting a chain of villas from the Pánuco to the Rio Grande. The revolt of 1810 pulled the coast into eleven years of war, which ended Spanish rule in 1821.
zh:
塔毛利帕斯的帕努科河口周围，潮湿的沿海平原被塔梅西河等缓流穿织，又被长长的潟湖与外海隔开。这里是中美洲的北缘，也是瓦斯特克人（自称特埃内克人）的故土，他们的玛雅语在数千年前便与各姊妹语言分家。他们在低地种植玉米和棉花，没有统一的国王，而是由一批各据一方的小邦君主治；镇中有小型神庙金字塔，彩绘陶器和贝器闻名于整个墨西哥湾。河畔小村坦皮科的名字来自瓦斯特克语，意为「水獭之地」。1444年，这些小邦仍自行其政，尽管墨西卡人的势力正在南方兴起。

西班牙人到来前不久，蒙特祖马一世的军队击败瓦斯特克人，他们此后向特诺奇蒂特兰纳贡，却保留了自己的君长。牙买加总督弗朗西斯科·德·加赖派阿隆索·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·皮内达测绘墨西哥湾北岸，1520年，登陆队在帕努科河畔被瓦斯特克战士击退。特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，科尔特斯于1522年控制该河；加赖亲率六百人前来另建殖民地，在与科尔特斯的权属之争中落败，次年死于墨西哥城。努尼奥·德·古斯曼手下的奴隶贩子和最早的疫病使旧日城镇凋零。为方济各会士安德烈斯·德·奥尔莫斯设立的圣路易斯·德·坦皮科存续到1684年，海盗袭掠迫使居民迁往帕努科河南岸。1746年，总督把空旷的海岸封给何塞·德·埃斯坎东，建为新桑坦德殖民地；两年后，他的移民开始从帕努科河到格兰德河建立一串城镇。1810年的起事把海岸卷入长达十一年的战争，西班牙统治于1821年终结。

en:
At the northern edge of Mesoamerica, the Sierra Madre Occidental falls toward a hot coastal plain cut by the Culiacán, Mocorito and Sinaloa rivers. Here lived the Tahues and Guasaves, Cahita-speaking villagers akin to the peoples farther north, with Acaxee farmers in the eastern mountains. They built no cities: autonomous extended families put up flimsy huts on the flood land and moved when the rivers rose, growing maize, beans and squash, hunting deer, weaving cotton mantles and burying their dead in urns. Salt, dried fish and shells moved between coast and sierra, and the ballgame ulama was played beside every sizeable village. In 1444 these valleys answered to no empire, only to their own elders and war leaders.

Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán reached them early in 1531, marching north from Chametla with four hundred Spaniards and eight thousand Indian allies, and founded San Miguel de Culiacán. On the way his men entered riverside villages where they found only women, and for a time believed they had reached a country of Amazons; the men were away gathering to fight. Silver opened the country: in 1563 Amador López opened the Real de Minas de Cosalá, the first great mines of the northwest, and from 1564 Culiacán and Cosalá were governed as a remote exclave of Nueva Galicia. In 1583 Pedro de Montoya founded the Villa de San Felipe y Santiago on the Sinaloa river, later called Sinaloa de Leyva, where the Jesuits Gonzalo de Tapia and Martín Pérez arrived in 1591 and built missions up the river valleys; Andrés Pérez de Ribas later wrote the history of that work. The mountain Acaxee rose under Perico in December 1601 and forty-eight of their leaders were executed. In 1610 Diego Martínez de Hurdaide raised the Fuerte de Montesclaros on the northern frontier against further revolt. During the insurgency José María González Hermosillo, sent north by Hidalgo himself, attacked El Rosario in December 1810 but was beaten at San Ignacio de Piaxtla on 7 February 1811, and the province stayed in royalist hands until independence.
zh:
这里是美索亚美利加的北缘：西马德雷山脉向炎热的沿海平原倾斜，库利亚坎河、莫科里托河和锡那罗亚河纵横入海。河谷里住着塔韦人和瓜萨韦人，他们是与更北方各族有亲缘的卡希塔语村民，东部山区则是阿卡塞农人。他们不建城市：自治的大家族在河滩搭起易拆的茅屋，河水涨起便迁走，种玉米、菜豆和南瓜，猎鹿，织棉布，把死者葬在陶瓮里。盐、鱼干和贝壳在海岸与山区之间往来，稍大的村落旁都有玩乌拉马球戏的球场。1444年，这些河谷不归任何帝国，只听从本族长老和战时首领。

1531年初，努尼奥·贝尔特兰·德·古斯曼率四百名西班牙人和八千名印第安辅助兵，从查梅特拉北上打到这里，建立圣米格尔·德·库利亚坎。途中他的部下走进一些河畔村落，只见到女人，一度以为自己到了传说中全是女人的部落；其实男人们都外出聚兵迎战去了。打开这片地方的是银矿：1563年阿马多尔·洛佩斯开出科萨拉雷亚尔银矿，这是西北部最早的大矿；1564年起，库利亚坎和科萨拉作为新加利西亚遥远的飞地管辖。1583年，佩德罗·德·蒙托亚在锡那罗亚河畔建立圣费利佩-圣地亚哥镇，即后来的锡那罗亚德莱瓦；耶稣会士贡萨洛·德·塔皮亚和马丁·佩雷斯1591年抵达，沿河谷建起传教站，安德烈斯·佩雷斯·德·里瓦斯后来把这段事业写成史书。1601年12月，山区阿卡塞人在佩里科率领下起义，四十八名首领被处死。1610年，迭戈·马丁内斯·德·乌代德在北部边疆筑起蒙特斯克拉罗斯堡，以防再乱。独立战争中，伊达尔戈亲自派往北方的何塞·马里亚·冈萨雷斯·埃尔莫西约1810年12月攻打埃尔罗萨里奥，却在1811年2月7日败于圣伊格纳西奥·德·皮亚斯特拉，全省直到独立始终掌握在保王派手中。

en:
The Tepehuán, who called themselves Ódami, held the eastern ridges and high valleys of the Sierra Madre Occidental, with the broad, well-watered Valle de Guadiana at their centre. In dispersed villages above the desert they grew maize, beans, chile and cotton, governed by elders in peace and chosen war leaders in war; their name in Nahuatl means 'lords of the hills'. The related Acaxee and Xixime lived to their west, nomadic Chichimecs roamed the arid plains to the east, and they were probably the most numerous people of the sierra. In 1444 no European had yet entered their valleys.

Silver seekers entered the Valle de Guadiana in the 1550s, and Francisco de Ibarra founded the Villa de Durango there on 8 July 1563, seat of the new province of Nueva Vizcaya. Mines and cattle haciendas pushed into the hills, and repeated epidemics in the mission villages may have cut the native population by four-fifths. Jesuit missions at Santa Catarina, Santiago Papasquiaro and El Zape had gathered the survivors when, in 1616, a baptized prophet named Quautlatas raised a broken cross and promised that the old gods would make the Tepehuán prosperous again once the Spaniards were driven out. On 16 November his men seized a wagon train near Santa Catarina and killed about a hundred people in the church at El Zape, and ten missionaries died in the rising. Governor Gaspar de Alvear answered with a war of 'fire and blood', and the last war chief, Gogoxito, fell before the revolt was declared over in 1620. The Jesuit Andrés Pérez de Ribas called it the greatest outbreak of violence New Spain had seen since the conquest, and it cost more than two hundred Spanish and perhaps four thousand Tepehuán lives. The Jesuits were expelled in 1767, and in 1821 the province passed with the rest of New Spain into independent Mexico.
zh:
特佩瓦人自称奥达摩人，据有西马德雷山脉的东缘山脊与高山谷地，以开阔湿润的瓜迪亚纳河谷为中心；在纳瓦特尔语里，其名意为「山岭之主」。在俯瞰荒漠的散布村落里，他们种植玉米、菜豆、辣椒和棉花，平时由长老主事，战时推举军事首领。西边住着与他们相近的阿卡塞人和希希梅人，东边干旱平原则有游猎的奇奇梅克人往来。他们大概是西马德雷山区人数最多的族群；1444年时，还没有欧洲人进入过他们的山谷。

1550年代，寻找白银的探矿者进入瓜迪亚纳河谷；1563年7月8日，弗朗西斯科·德·伊瓦拉在此建立杜兰戈镇，作为新设新比斯开亚省的首府。矿场和牧牛庄园随后涌入山区，传教村镇里反复流行的瘟疫可能使原住民人口减少了五分之四。幸存者被并入圣卡塔琳娜、圣地亚哥·帕帕斯基亚罗和埃尔萨佩等耶稣会传教站。1616年，受过洗礼的先知夸乌特拉塔斯举起一柄断十字架，宣称只要赶走西班牙人，旧神便会让特佩瓦人重获富足。11月16日，他的部下在圣卡塔琳娜附近截获一支车队，又在埃尔萨佩的教堂里杀死约一百人，十名传教士在起义中遇难。总督加斯帕尔·德·阿尔韦亚尔以「火与血」开战，最后一位军事首领戈戈克西托战死，1620年起义被宣布平定。耶稣会士安德烈斯·佩雷斯·德·里瓦斯称，这是征服以来新西班牙最猛烈的一场暴乱，两百多名西班牙人和大约四千名特佩瓦人在战乱中丧生。耶稣会于1767年被驱逐，1821年，新比斯开亚随新西班牙并入独立的墨西哥。

en:
Coahuila is the high desert east of the Bolsón de Mapimí, where the ranges of the Sierra Madre Oriental enclose dry basins and a handful of springs. In 1444 it had no towns. Chichimec bands, above all the Guachichiles, hunted with the bow, gathered mesquite and prickly pear, shifted camp with the rains and raided the settled country to the south; the springs at Saltillo marked the northern edge of their range, and Spaniards later called them indios bárbaros. They traded and feuded among themselves and answered to no outside lord.

Santiago del Saltillo, founded beside those springs by Alberto del Canto in 1577, was the first Spanish town, and the Chichimeca War nearly killed it: within ten years fewer than twenty Spaniards remained. In 1591 the viceroy shored it up with seventy-one Tlaxcalan families, settled in their own township beside the Spanish one. At Parras, Lorenzo García planted vines in 1597 that began the oldest wine estate in the Americas. Monclova, out in the northern desert, was founded, abandoned and refounded eleven times between 1577 and 1689 before Alonso de León's settlement held; it became capital of Coahuila province and the base of the presidio line against Apache raiders.

The desert also swallowed Mexico's first insurgency. Fleeing north after their defeat at Puente de Calderón, Hidalgo, Allende and the other rebel leaders stopped at the wells of Acatita de Baján in March 1811 at the invitation of Ignacio Elizondo, a royalist officer who had pretended to join them. His men ambushed the column there; Allende's son was killed in the firing, and the captives were marched to Chihuahua and shot. Independence was sworn at Monclova on 15 June 1821.
zh:
科阿韦拉是马皮米洼地以东的高原荒漠，东马德雷山脉的山岭环抱着一个个封闭盆地和为数不多的泉水。1444年这里没有城镇。奇奇梅克诸游群以瓜奇奇尔人为首，持弓狩猎，采集豆灌木和仙人掌果实，随雨水移营，不时南下劫掠定居地区；萨尔蒂约的泉水是他们活动范围的北界，西班牙人后来把他们叫作「野蛮印第安人」。各族群彼此贸易、相互仇杀，不奉任何外来的君主。

阿尔韦托·德尔·坎托1577年在这片泉水旁建起第一个西班牙城镇圣地亚哥·德尔萨尔蒂约，它险些被奇奇梅卡战争扼死：十年后城中剩下不到二十名西班牙人。1591年，副王调来七十一户特拉斯卡拉人家，安置在西班牙城镇旁边的独立村镇，才算把它撑住。在帕拉斯，洛伦索·加西亚1597年在这里栽下葡萄藤，办起美洲最古老的酒庄。北方荒漠里的蒙克洛瓦在1577至1689年间十一次建立、废弃、再建，直到阿隆索·德·莱昂这一次才站稳脚跟；它后来成为科阿韦拉省省会，也是要塞防线抵御阿帕奇袭掠者的基地。

这片荒漠也吞没了墨西哥的第一场起义。1811年3月，伊达尔戈、阿连德等起义首领在卡尔德龙桥战败后北逃，被假意投诚的保王军官伊格纳西奥·埃利松多邀到阿卡特塔·德·巴汉的水井边停下。埃利松多的部队在那里伏击了队伍，阿连德之子在交火中被杀，俘虏们被押往奇瓦瓦处死。1821年6月15日，蒙克洛瓦宣誓独立。

en:
Yaqui is the lower Yaqui River country and the Gulf of California shore of Sonora, homeland of the Yoeme, who were perhaps 30,000 strong in about eighty rancherías spread through a valley sixty miles long. Yearly floods renewed fields of beans, maize and squash, villagers wove cotton, families at the river mouth fished the gulf, and desert and mountain bands lived by hunting and gathering. Their fame as fighters guarded the valley's edges. In 1444 the Yoeme followed their own elders and war leaders, and no Spanish road had yet reached the river.

Captain Diego de Guzmán reached it on 4 October 1533. On a level plain an old Yoeme leader drew a line in the dirt, told the Spaniards not to cross and refused them food; in the fight that followed the intruders pulled back. Francisco de Ibarra failed to plant a settlement in 1565, and the valley's lack of silver did more than its bows to keep colonists away for decades. Diego Martínez de Hurdaide's expedition was trapped and nearly broken in 1607 and got away only by a ruse; from that war the Yoeme called outsiders yori, people who do not respect the traditional law, and made peace in 1610. In 1617 they invited in Jesuits Andrés Pérez de Ribas and Tomás Basilio, who gathered them into eight mission towns. For roughly a century the Yoeme kept their communal lands, took baptism alongside their own rites and adopted wheat, cattle and horses; distance and their fame as fighters shielded them from settlers and slavers, and the epidemics that emptied other missions largely missed the valley. Miners and settlers pushed onto its lands in the 1730s, and in 1740 the Yaqui rose with Mayo, Pima and Opata allies. The missions never recovered, and after the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the Franciscans sent to replace them never won the same trust. When Mexico's independence war began in 1810, the Yaqui held back: they still counted themselves a separate nation.
zh:
亚基位于索诺拉的亚基河下游与加利福尼亚湾沿岸，是约梅人的家园；当时约梅人约有三万，八十来座农猎村落散布在一条近百公里长的河谷里。每年河水泛滥，重新滋养菜豆、玉米和南瓜田，村民纺织棉布，河口人家在湾中捕鱼，沙漠与山地的群体则以狩猎采集为生。善战的名声守着河谷的边界。1444年，约梅人仍听命于本族长老和军事首领，西班牙人的道路尚未通到亚基河。

1533年10月4日，迭戈·德·古斯曼队长抵达河边。在一片平坦原野上，一位约梅老人在地上划下一道线，叫西班牙人不得越过，又拒绝给他们食物；交战之后，入侵者退走。弗朗西斯科·德·伊瓦拉1565年在此建立据点失败，而河谷里没有白银，这比弓箭更有效地让殖民者几十年里不愿前来。1607年，迭戈·马丁内斯·德·乌尔戴德的远征队被围困、几乎被打垮，只靠一条诡计脱身；这场战争后，约梅人把外来者称为「约里」，即不尊重传统律法的人，并于1610年议和。1617年，他们主动迎入耶稣会士安德烈斯·佩雷斯·德·里瓦斯和托马斯·巴西略，两人把居民归并为八座传教村镇。此后约一个世纪，约梅人保留公有土地，在接受洗礼的同时保留自己的仪轨，也种起小麦、养起牛马；偏远的位置和尚武的名声使垦民和奴隶贩子退避，掏空其他传教区的瘟疫也大体放过了这条河谷。1730年代，矿工和垦民闯入河谷土地，1740年亚基人联合马约人、皮马人、奥帕塔人起义。传教区再未恢复，1767年耶稣会被逐后，接替的方济各会始终没有赢得同样的信任。1810年墨西哥独立战争爆发时，亚基人没有卷入：他们仍自认是一个独立的民族。

en:
The arid mountains and basins of northern Chihuahua, running up to the Rio Grande at El Paso, were Suma country. They lived as a set of autonomous bands, with no chief over all of them, hunting and gathering across the desert and sowing almost nothing. Their ancestors had lived in the Jornada Mogollon pueblos of the same country until about 1450, when those villages were abandoned and their people went back to moving between waterholes. In 1444 Suma camps shifted with the seasons, trading and raiding with the neighbouring Concho, Manso and Jumano.

Antonio de Espejo met more than a thousand Suma near the Rio Grande in 1583 and was received peacefully; he called them the Caguates, and the name Suma appears in Spanish records only from 1630. Franciscans opened a mission for them at El Paso in 1659 and another near the city of Chihuahua in 1663. Apache raids then split the bands: some settled under Spanish protection while others joined the raiders. The Pueblo revolt of 1680 drove thousands of Spanish refugees into El Paso; famine followed in 1683–84, the Suma revolted and fled, and through the next century bands repeatedly left the missions for the mountains. Smallpox in the 1780s killed most of the Suma living at the San Lorenzo mission, and the survivors merged into frontier towns and Apache bands.
zh:
奇瓦瓦北部干旱的山地与盆地，向北一直到埃尔帕索一带的里奥格兰德，是苏马人的土地。他们分成若干各自为政的游群，没有统辖全体的君长，在沙漠中游动狩猎采集，几乎不种庄稼。其祖先原是同一片土地上霍尔纳达·莫戈永文化的村民，约1450年那些村落被放弃，人们重新回到逐水源而居的生活。1444年，苏马人的营地随季节迁移，和邻近的孔乔、曼索、胡马诺人或交易、或冲突。

1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍在里奥格兰德附近遇到一千多名苏马人，受到友好接待；他把他们称作卡瓜特人，「苏马」这个名字到1630年才见于西班牙记载。方济各会1659年在埃尔帕索为他们设立传教站，1663年又在奇瓦瓦城附近设了一处。随后阿帕奇人的袭掠使各游群分化：一些人在西班牙保护下定居，另一些加入了袭掠者。1680年普韦布洛起义把数千名西班牙难民赶进埃尔帕索，1683至1684年饥荒随之而来，苏马人起事并逃离传教站；此后一个世纪里，不断有游群离开传教站、躲进山里。1780年代的天花使住在圣洛伦索传教站的苏马人病死大半，幸存者融入边疆市镇和阿帕奇诸部。

en:
The Río Conchos gathers the water of a wide desert country in central Chihuahua and carries it north to join the Rio Grande, and its valley and tributaries were the home of the Concho, who called themselves Yoli. These semi-nomadic Uto-Aztecan speakers were split between the Chinarras, the Chisos and many smaller bands, with no chief over all of them. In 1444 their camps followed water and game along the river, next to Suma, Toboso and Tarahumara lands.

Expeditions out of the San Bartolomé valley in 1570 and 1574 opened routes up the Florido, San Gregorio and Conchos rivers. In 1604 Fray Alonso de la Oliva founded a Franciscan mission on the river and named it for the small shells, conchas, in the bed; it grew into San Francisco de Conchos. Concho, Toboso, Chizo and Tarahumara people were brought there in turn, and at its height the settlement held more than four thousand Indians. In 1645 local people burned the mission and killed friars Tomás de Zigarán and Francisco Labado, and it was resettled in 1677. A trial in 1684 heard a Mamita headman claim leadership over dozens of named Concho bands, and three years later the Spanish put the settlement under a military presidio.
zh:
孔乔斯河汇集奇瓦瓦中部广大沙漠地带的水流，向北注入里奥格兰德；河谷及其支流是孔乔人的家园，他们自称约利。这些半游牧的犹他—阿兹特克语居民分成奇纳拉、奇索和许多较小的游群，没有统辖全体的君长。1444年，他们的营地沿河追逐水源和猎物，与苏马、托沃索和塔拉乌马拉人的土地相邻。

1570年和1574年，圣巴托洛梅谷地派出的探险队沿弗洛里多河、圣格雷戈里奥河和孔乔斯河而上，打开了通路。1604年，修士阿隆索·德·拉·奥利瓦在河畔建立方济各会传教站，因河床里的小贝壳（孔查）得名，后来发展为圣弗朗西斯科·德·孔乔斯。孔乔、托沃索、奇索、塔拉乌马拉等族群先后来到这里，聚落极盛时安置了四千多名原住民。1645年，当地人焚毁传教站，杀死修士托马斯·德·西加兰和弗朗西斯科·拉巴多；1677年传教站重新安置。1684年的一场审判中，一名马米塔游群的头人声称自己统领着数十个有名可查的孔乔游群；三年后，西班牙人把该聚落置于军事要塞管治之下。

en:
The Cochimí wandered the central desert of Baja California, from El Rosario in the north to San Javier in the south, a country of bare sierra and gulf shores. They had neither towns, fields nor herds; small bands followed fish and shellfish, game and wild seeds, and the year turned on the summer pitahaya harvest, the season of flowers and plenty. Their guamas, or shamans, kept the ceremonies and the sacred places. They could give no account of the painted animals and hunters on the walls of the sierra caves, holding them to be the work of an earlier, taller people who had vanished. In 1444 these trails and seasonal camps were untouched by outside rule, and no European ship had mapped the gulf shore.

Francisco de Ulloa's ships reached the head of the gulf in 1539 and showed that Baja was joined to the mainland, though cartographers went on drawing California as an island for another century; Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo and Sebastián Vizcaíno later surveyed the Pacific coast. Sustained contact began with Eusebio Francisco Kino's short-lived San Bruno settlement of 1683-1685. Juan María de Salvatierra opened Loreto among the neighboring Monqui in 1697, and Francesco Maria Piccolo founded San Javier among the Cochimí in 1699. Over the next seventy years Jesuit missions ran north through Mulegé, San Ignacio and San Borja, and the stone church raised at San Javier between 1744 and 1758 was counted the finest of the peninsula's mission churches. Mission congregations, a changed diet, measles and smallpox cut the desert bands down by about three quarters in the first twenty years of evangelization. The Jesuit expulsion reached Baja California in 1768. Junípero Serra's Franciscans opened San Fernando Velicatá the following year, the Dominicans reached El Rosario in 1774, and by then the surviving Cochimí communities had been greatly reduced.
zh:
科奇米人在下加利福尼亚中部沙漠中游徙，范围北起埃尔罗萨里奥，南至圣哈维尔，地上是光秃的山岭和海湾岸线。他们没有城镇、农田和畜群，各小队追逐鱼贝、猎物和野生种籽，一年的节奏围绕夏季的仙人掌果采收展开，那是花开而食物丰足的时节。瓜马（巫师）主持仪式、守护圣地。山岭洞穴的壁上画着动物和猎人，科奇米人说不出这些画的来历，认为是一群早已消失、身材更高的先人所作。1444年，这些小径和季节性营地不受外来政权统治，也还没有欧洲船只测绘过海湾岸线。

1539年，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚的船队航行到海湾尽头，证明下加利福尼亚与大陆相连，但此后一个世纪里制图家仍把加利福尼亚画成岛屿；胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略和塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯开诺后来又分别考察了太平洋沿岸。持续接触始于尤塞比奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺1683至1685年短暂维持的圣布鲁诺定居点。1697年，胡安·玛丽亚·德·萨尔瓦铁拉在邻近的蒙基人中建起洛雷托；1699年，弗朗切斯科·玛丽亚·皮科洛在科奇米人当中创立圣哈维尔传教站。此后七十年，耶稣会的传教链经穆莱赫、圣伊格纳西奥和圣博尔哈向北延伸；圣哈维尔1744至1758年间建起的石砌教堂，被视为半岛传教教堂中最精致的一座。传教集居、饮食变化、麻疹和天花使这些沙漠群体在传教最初二十年间减少约四分之三。1768年，驱逐耶稣会的命令送达下加利福尼亚，胡尼佩罗·塞拉率领的方济各会次年开设圣费尔南多·贝利卡塔；多明我会1774年抵达埃尔罗萨里奥，那时幸存的科奇米社群已大幅衰微。

en:
The Guaycura held the tail of the Baja California peninsula, from near Loreto south to Todos Santos and the Bay of La Paz: about 25,000 square kilometres of austere desert and mountains with few springs. They were no chiefdom but a dozen or so independent bands of a few hundred people, each with its own ground and sometimes at war with the rest. Their language resembled no other Native American tongue, a sign to linguists that their ancestors had lived isolated on the peninsula for thousands of years after other peoples pushed them south. They hunted mule deer and bighorn sheep, took turtles and shellfish on the shore, and roasted agave hearts in pits the year round; in late summer the pitahaya cactus fruit let whole bands gather at once. In 1444 the people may have numbered about 5,000, moving between brush camps under shamans.

What first drew Spaniards to this coast was pearls. In 1533 the mutineer Fortún Ximénez sailed into the Bay of La Paz, found pearl oysters with unusually large pearls, and was killed there with several of his crew in a fight over the plunder. Hernán Cortés came himself in 1535, named the bay Santa Cruz, and tried a colony that starvation forced him to quit; pearl boats kept visiting for another 150 years. The Jesuits reached La Paz in 1720, siting their Airapí mission partly as a rest stop for Manila galleons, then added Dolores, Todos Santos and San Luis Gonzaga. The Uchití band joined the Pericú revolt of 1734, killing Jesuits and Spanish sailors, and from 1748 the southern bands were forcibly concentrated at Todos Santos, where children were kept at the mission to hold their parents. The Alsatian Jesuit Johann Jakob Baegert, at San Luis Gonzaga from 1751 to 1768, left the fullest account of Guaycura life, and the sourest: page after page calls his charges lazy, lying and thievish. When the Jesuits were expelled in 1768, 746 surviving northern Guaycura were marched to Todos Santos; more than 300 died of measles within a year, and by 1808 only 82 remained. The separate culture dissolved at about that time.
zh:
瓜伊库拉人住在下加利福尼亚半岛的尾端，北起洛雷托附近，南至托多斯桑托斯和拉巴斯湾，是约二万五千平方公里淡水稀少的贫瘠沙漠与山地。他们没有统一的酋邦，而是十几个各自独立、各有地盘、彼此有时交战的小队，每队几百人。瓜伊库拉语与其他任何美洲原住民语言都不相像，语言学家认为这说明他们的祖先在被别族挤到南方之后，已在半岛上孤立生活了数千年。他们猎骡鹿和大角羊，在海岸捕龟拾贝，一年到头在坑中烤龙舌兰心；夏末皮塔哈亚仙人掌果成熟的几个月里，全队人才得以聚到一处。1444年，瓜伊库拉人可能共约五千，在萨满主持下从一处灌木营地迁往下一处。

最早把西班牙人引到这段海岸的是珍珠。1533年，哗变的领航员福尔图恩·希门尼斯驶入拉巴斯湾，发现珠母贝里有异常大的珍珠，又因劫掠与当地人冲突，他和几名船员被杀。埃尔南·科尔特斯1535年亲自前来，把海湾命名为圣克鲁斯，试图建立殖民地，却因饥荒撤出；此后一百五十年间珍珠船仍不断到来。耶稣会1720年进入拉巴斯，在艾拉皮设传教站，部分用途是给马尼拉大帆船作停歇补给地，后来又增设多洛雷斯、托多斯桑托斯和圣路易斯·贡萨加三站。乌奇提队加入了1734年的佩里库人起事，杀死耶稣会士和西班牙水手；1748年起，南部各队被强行集居到托多斯桑托斯，传教站扣下孩子，以此留住他们的父母。阿尔萨斯籍耶稣会士约翰·雅各布·贝格特1751至1768年驻在圣路易斯·贡萨加，留下了关于瓜伊库拉人生活最详尽也最刻薄的记录，通篇骂他们懒惰、说谎、偷窃。1768年耶稣会被逐，七百四十六名幸存的北方瓜伊库拉人被押往托多斯桑托斯，一年内三百多人死于麻疹，到1808年只剩八十二人，其独立文化也在这时前后解体。

en:
The Cahuilla lands lay between the San Bernardino and San Jacinto ranges and the Colorado Desert, about 2,400 square miles of canyons, passes and dry basins. Clans camped around permanent springs and in the oases of California fan palms, eating the palm fruit and working its leaves into baskets, sandals and roof thatch. Their legends remembered a great freshwater lake in the Coachella basin, fed by the Colorado, which dried up when the river changed course before 1700. East across the desert, the Mohave, Pipa a'ha macave or 'people who live by the water', held the Colorado from Black Canyon south toward the Parker valley and followed trails as far as the Californian coast to gather clams. In 1444 there was no Spanish mission, town or garrison anywhere in this country; springs, river crossings and desert paths belonged entirely to the peoples who knew them.

Spaniards first reached the river in 1540, when Melchor Díaz crossed it on the Coronado expedition and named it Rio de Tizón, while Hernando de Alarcón sailed into its mouth from the gulf; Díaz died on the retreat. Juan de Oñate marched through Mohave country in 1605 looking for a route to the sea, but no Spanish post followed. In 1774 Juan Bautista de Anza crossed Cahuilla territory to open the first overland road from Sonora to Monterey, and the Franciscan Francisco Garcés, who met the Mohave in 1775, later followed one of their trails across the desert; he was killed in the Quechan uprising on the lower Colorado in 1781, which closed the road. A few Cahuilla later took baptism and traded with Hispanic ranchos, but when Mexico inherited Spain's claims in 1821, the desert clans still governed their own springs, trails and crossings.
zh:
卡维拉人的土地夹在圣贝纳迪诺山脉、圣哈辛托山脉与科罗拉多沙漠之间，是一片约2400平方英里的峡谷、山口和干盆地。各氏族围绕常年不竭的泉眼和加州蒲葵绿洲而居，食用蒲葵果实，把叶片编成筐篮、凉鞋和屋顶苫席。他们的传说记得科切拉盆地里曾有一片科罗拉多河补给的大淡水湖，后来河流改道，湖水在1700年以前干涸。沙漠以东，自称「依水而居之人」（Pipa a'ha macave）的莫哈维人占据着从黑峡谷向南延伸到帕克谷地的科罗拉多河段，还沿着小径远至加利福尼亚海岸采集蛤蜊。1444年时，这片土地上没有西班牙传教站、城镇或驻军；泉眼、渡口和沙漠小径完全属于熟悉它们的人。

西班牙人1540年第一次到这条河：梅尔乔·迪亚斯随科罗纳多远征队渡过科罗拉多河，把它命名为蒂松河（Rio de Tizón，意为火炭），埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔则从海湾驶入河口；迪亚斯在归途中死去。1605年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特为寻找出海通道率军穿过莫哈维地区，却没有留下任何西班牙据点。1774年，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·安萨穿过卡维拉地区，开出第一条从索诺拉通往蒙特雷的陆上道路；方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯1775年会见莫哈维人，后来沿他们的一条小路横穿沙漠，1781年在科罗拉多河下游的克尚人起义中被杀，这条陆路也随之封闭。此后少数卡维拉人受洗，与西班牙裔牧场贸易；1821年墨西哥继承西班牙的权利主张时，沙漠诸氏族仍自行管理着泉眼、小径和渡口。

en:
The Chumash hold the Santa Barbara Channel coast from Morro Bay to Malibu, with San Miguel, Santa Rosa and Santa Cruz among their island lands. In 1444 more than 150 independent villages occupied the shore, the northern Channel Islands and the Santa Ynez valley. Their most distinctive craft was the tomol, a sewn-plank canoe up to thirty feet long, reliable enough for open water and swordfish hunting. Boat builders formed a specialist guild, and leading families passed the canoes down as heirlooms. Craftsmen also drilled Olivella shell beads into currency for trade networks reaching east beyond the Colorado River, while fish, deer and acorns moved between island, coastal and inland villages. Each village had its own chiefs and shamans.

Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo's ships entered the channel in 1542; he saw so many plank canoes drawn up at one wealthy village that he named it the pueblo de las canoas, later associated with Malibu. Cabrillo died that winter and was buried on San Miguel Island. Sebastián Vizcaíno named the channel Santa Barbara in 1602, but permanent Spanish occupation began only after the 1769 Portolá expedition. Between 1772 and 1804 Franciscans opened missions at San Luis Obispo, San Buenaventura, Santa Barbara and Santa Inés. Governor Felipe de Neve began the Royal Presidio of Santa Barbara in April 1782, the last royal presidio Spain built in its American colonies, and Junípero Serra blessed the site. The December 1812 earthquake and tsunami wrecked Mission Santa Barbara, which was rebuilt by 1820, a year before Mexican independence replaced Spanish rule.
zh:
丘马什人的土地沿圣巴巴拉海峡海岸展开，北起莫罗贝，南至马里布，圣米格尔、圣罗莎和圣克鲁斯等北海峡群岛也在其中。1444年，一百五十多个互不统属的村庄分布在海岸、北海峡群岛和圣伊内斯河谷。他们最有特色的技术是托莫尔缝板舟：这种船最长约9米，能进入外海捕剑鱼。造船者有专门的「独木舟行会」，望族把船当作传家财产。工匠还把小榧螺壳磨成贝珠，作为货币流通到科罗拉多河以远；渔获、鹿肉和橡子则在海岛、海岸和内陆村庄之间交换。每个村庄各有酋长和萨满。

1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略的船队驶入海峡；他在一个富庶村庄岸边看到大量缝板舟，便称之为独木舟村，该地后来通常被认为是马里布。卡布里洛在当年冬天去世，葬在圣米格尔岛。1602年，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯卡伊诺把海峡命名为圣巴巴拉，但西班牙人的长期占领要到1769年波尔托拉远征后才开始。1772年至1804年间，方济各会先后建立圣路易斯-奥比斯波、圣布埃纳文图拉、圣巴巴拉和圣伊内斯传教所。1782年4月，总督费利佩·德·内韦开始修建圣巴巴拉王家要塞，这是西班牙在美洲殖民地修建的最后一座王家要塞，胡尼佩罗·塞拉为址祝圣。1812年12月的地震和海啸摧毁圣巴巴拉传教所，建筑到1820年重建完成；次年墨西哥独立，西班牙统治结束。

en:
T'epot'aha'l is the Salinan name for the lower Salinas Valley, the Santa Lucia Range and a broken coast around San Simeon and Lucia. The Salinan language had no known relatives, and the people called themselves the People of the Oaks. In 1444 Antoniano bands in the valley, Miguelino groups on the upper river and Playano families on the shore lived without a central chief. They gathered acorns from valley oaks, hunted deer in the mountains, took fish and shellfish from the sea and left shell middens along the coast. No European ship had yet anchored close to their shore.

Spanish ships passed the coast in 1542, but Spain did not enter the valley until Gaspar de Portolá's overland expedition of 1769. Junípero Serra founded Mission San Antonio de Padua among the Antoniano on 14 July 1771, the third Franciscan mission in Alta California; it also saw the first use of fired roof tiles in Alta California. Miguel Pieras and Buenaventura Sitjar stayed to build it, and 158 Salinans had been baptised by the end of that year. The first Christian marriage in California followed there in May 1773. No town grew around the remote mission. Fermín Lasuén founded Mission San Miguel Arcángel on 25 July 1797 beside the Salinan village of Vahca, adding a stop on the route between San Luis Obispo and San Antonio. San Antonio held about 1,300 native neophytes in 1805, mostly Salinans with Yokuts and Esselen among them, but only 178 remained in 1810. At Mexican independence in 1821, the missions still controlled the valley.
zh:
特波塔哈尔是萨利南人对这片土地的称呼，范围包括萨利纳斯河下游河谷、圣卢西亚山脉，以及圣西米恩和卢西亚一带曲折崎岖的海岸。萨利南语与任何已知语言都没有亲缘关系，他们自称「橡树之人」。1444年，河谷中的安东尼亚诺群体、河流上游的米格尔尼奥群体和海边的普拉亚诺家庭分成小群自治，没有最高酋长。他们采集谷地橡树的橡子，在山中猎鹿，从海中获取鱼和贝类，并在海岸留下贝丘。那时还没有欧洲船只在附近停泊。

西班牙人的船1542年曾从海上驶过，但直到1769年加斯帕尔·德·波尔托拉陆上远征，西班牙人才进入河谷。1771年7月14日，胡尼佩罗·塞拉在安东尼亚诺人中间建立圣安东尼奥·德·帕多瓦传教所；它是上加利福尼亚的第三座方济各会传教所，也是上加利福尼亚最早使用烧制屋瓦的传教所。米格尔·皮埃拉斯和布埃纳文图拉·西哈尔留下主持营建，到1771年底已有一百五十八名萨利南人受洗。1773年5月，这里举行加利福尼亚的第一场基督教婚礼。这座偏远传教所周围没有发展出城镇。1797年7月25日，费尔明·拉苏恩在萨利南村庄瓦卡旁建立圣米格尔·阿坎赫尔传教所，为圣路易斯-奥比斯波与圣安东尼奥之间的路程增加一处落脚点。1805年，圣安东尼奥约有一千三百名原住民新信徒，以萨利南人为主，也有约库特人和埃塞伦人；到1810年只剩一百七十八人。1821年墨西哥独立时，传教所仍控制着这座河谷。

en:
The Lakisamni were a Northern Valley Yokuts people of the lower Stanislaus River, where the water runs west out of the Sierra foothills into the San Joaquin Valley; their villages and fishing grounds stretched from the later crossing at Ripon upstream to Knights Ferry. They shared this oak and river country with the Miwok Tawalimnu. Like other Yokuts they took fish with spears and basket traps, hunted deer and elk, and lived on acorn mash pounded in the mortar holes that mark the river rocks at Knights Ferry; they gathered salt from salt grass, and tobacco was the only plant they cultivated. Shell beads from the coast served as money, while valley salt, steatite and obsidian moved the other way. Yokuts tribes then numbered four to six hundred people each, and in 1444 the Lakisamni answered to no outside power.

No Spanish soldier entered this part of the valley until Gabriel Moraga's official expeditions of 1806-1808. On the 1808 march he took twenty-five soldiers to scout mission sites and pursue runaways who had carried off horses, cattle and weapons; he named the river Río de Guadalupe, while other Spaniards called it the Laquisimes after these people, and the meetings were hostile on both sides. In 1821 mission padres came to the Laquisimes for Cucunuchi, a young man born on the river about 1798. His younger brother had gone to Mission San José the year before and had been baptized Orencio; on 24 September 1821 Cucunuchi reached the mission with his wife, daughter and mother, his father refusing to go, and was baptized Estanislao. At the close of Spanish rule that year, no mission or pueblo yet stood on the river.
zh:
拉基萨姆尼人是北谷约库特人的一支，住在斯坦尼斯劳斯河下游；河水自内华达山脉山麓西出，流入圣华金谷。他们的村落和渔场从日后里彭的渡口沿河上溯到奈茨费里，河畔岩石上的臼洞标示出当年舂捣食物的地点。他们与塔瓦利姆努米沃克人共享这片橡树与河川之地。和其他约库特人一样，他们用鱼叉和鱼篓捕鱼，捕猎鹿和马鹿，以在臼洞中舂出的橡实泥为主食，从盐草上取盐，栽种的作物只有烟草。海岸来的贝壳珠充当货币，谷地的盐、皂石和黑曜石则反向运往海岸。当时每个约库特部落约有四五百到六百人，1444年的拉基萨姆尼人不受外来权力管辖。

直到加夫列尔·莫拉加1806至1808年的官方远征，西班牙士兵才进入谷地这一段。1808年，他率二十五名士兵查勘传教站选址，追捕带走马匹、牛只和武器的逃亡者；他把这条河命名为瓜达卢佩河，另一些西班牙人则由拉基萨姆尼之名改称拉基西梅斯，双方几次相遇都怀有敌意。1821年，传教士到拉基西梅斯来要一个名叫库库努奇的年轻人，他约1798年出生在河畔。他的弟弟前一年已先到圣何塞传教站，受洗取名奥伦西奥；1821年9月24日，库库努奇带着妻子、女儿和母亲抵达传教站，父亲拒绝同行，他本人不久受洗，取名埃斯塔尼斯劳。这一年西班牙统治结束时，河上还没有建起一座传教站或村镇。

en:
Pomo country runs from the Pacific shore to Clear Lake, across the redwood coast and the Russian River valley. The Pomo were never one nation: about seventy independent bands spoke seven related but mutually unintelligible languages, and at contact they numbered between 8,000 and 21,000 people. They took salmon and waterfowl, gathered shellfish and seeds, and pounded acorns in stone mortars. Their women wove baskets by plaiting, coiling and twining, some tight enough to cook in, with conical burden baskets for the acorn harvest and even basket boats for crossing rivers. Clamshell discs and cylinders of red magnesite, mined locally, served as money across much of central California; the same trade brought steatite from Catalina Island and obsidian from Mount Konocti into Pomo villages. In 1444 no stranger had yet reached it by sea.

The strangers came in 1812. Ivan Kuskov of the Russian-American Company sailed into Bodega Bay with twenty-five Russians and eighty Native Alaskan hunters, and fifteen miles up the coast chose Metini, a seasonal camp of the Kashaya, the coastal Pomo of that shore; Fortress Ross was dedicated there on 11 September 1812, its name taken from Rossiya. The company wanted sea-otter pelts and grain and meat for its colonies in Alaska, and the outpost became the southernmost Russian settlement in North America. Kashaya families lived beside the Russians and the Alaskan newcomers, working and trading with them, while Spanish missions were already pressing north beyond San Francisco Bay. Kuskov governed Fort Ross until 1821.
zh:
波莫人的土地从太平洋岸边延伸到清水湖，横跨红杉海岸与俄罗斯河谷。波莫人从来不是一个统一的民族：约七十个彼此独立的群体操七种互不相通的亲属语言，欧洲人初遇时总人口在8000到21000之间。他们捕捞鲑鱼和水禽，采集贝类和种籽，用石臼舂橡实为食。妇女用编、盘、缠三种技法编织筐篓，有些密实得可以直接在里面烹煮；收获橡实靠圆锥形大背篓，渡河时甚至使用篮筐扎成的小船。蛤壳圆片和本地开采的红色镁石管珠在加利福尼亚中部大部充当货币；同一张贸易网还把卡塔利娜岛的皂石和科诺克提山的黑曜石带进波莫人的村落。1444年，还没有外来者从海上到来。

外来者在1812年到来。俄美公司的伊万·库斯科夫率领二十五名俄国人、八十名阿拉斯加原住民猎手驶入博德加湾，在海岸以北约二十四公里处选中滨海波莫支系卡沙牙人的季节性营地梅提尼；1812年9月11日，罗斯堡在那里举行落成礼，堡名取自「俄罗斯」。公司要的是海獭皮，以及供应阿拉斯加殖民地的谷物和肉食，这座据点成了俄国在北美最靠南的定居点。卡沙牙家庭同俄国人、阿拉斯加新来者比邻而居，为其劳作，彼此交易；与此同时，西班牙传教站也已越过旧金山湾向北进逼。库斯科夫一直担任罗斯堡主管，直到1821年。

en:
Sha'yuushtl'a, the Siuslaw homeland, centres on the river of the same name where it breaks through the Coast Range into a narrow tidal estuary on the Pacific. Autonomous villages of cedar plank houses lined the lower river, linked by family ties, canoe landings and trails over the mountains to the Willamette and Camas valleys. Families took Chinook and coho salmon and lampreys at the weirs, gathered shellfish, seals and waterfowl from the estuary, and collected berries and roots inland. Wealth was counted in dentalium shells, woodpecker scalps and polished clam-shell disks, and a headman's worth lay in feeding his villagers from that store. The Siuslaw shared a language with the Lower Umpqua to the south but kept their own river and fishing grounds. In 1444 only Siuslaw canoes use the estuary.

On the evening of 26 January 1700 a subduction earthquake of magnitude approaching 9 shook the whole coast and drove a tsunami into the river-mouth villages, smashing houses, weirs and winter stores; the same wave crossed the Pacific and washed onto the Japanese coast, where officials wrote it down. Bruno de Heceta's Spanish ships surveyed the Oregon coast in 1775, but contact at the Siuslaw stayed indirect for years, with pelts passing through neighbouring villages. The American James Baker bought sea-otter furs from the Lower Umpqua for about twelve days in 1791, and Hudson's Bay Company trappers made the first recorded overland contact in 1820. In 1821 no European post stood at the river mouth.
zh:
赛乌斯劳人的自称是沙尤什特拉，家园以同名河流为中心：河水穿出海岸山脉，经一条狭窄的潮汐河口注入太平洋。下游两岸分布着各自独立的雪松板屋村落，彼此靠姻亲、独木舟码头和翻山小路相连，山路通向威拉米特谷地和卡默斯谷地。人们在鱼梁上捕捞奇努克鲑、银鲑和七鳃鳗，在河口采贝、猎海豹和水禽，在内陆采集浆果和根茎。财富用角贝、啄木鸟头皮和磨制的蛤壳圆片计算，村长是否称职，要看他能不能用这些储积养活村民。赛乌斯劳人与南边的下安普夸人语言相通，却守着自己的河流和渔场。1444年，河口往来的只有赛乌斯劳人的独木舟。

1700年1月26日夜，一次近9级的俯冲带大地震震动整条海岸，海啸扑入河口村落，冲毁房屋、鱼梁和过冬储仓；这道海浪还横越太平洋，冲上日本海岸，被当时的官吏记录下来。1775年，布鲁诺·德·埃塞塔率领西班牙船考察俄勒冈海岸，但此后多年，赛乌斯劳河口的接触仍多经邻村转手。1791年，美国人詹姆斯·贝克向下安普夸人收购了约十二天海獭皮；1820年，哈德逊湾公司的捕兽者首次留下经陆路接触的记载。1821年，河口仍没有欧洲商站。

en:
Tsinuk commands the mouth of the Columbia, where the Great River pushes through shifting bars and lines of breakers to meet the Pacific. Even in fair weather the entrance can break a ship, and the river behind it stayed hidden from European captains for decades. Lower Chinook villages stood on Baker Bay and behind Chinook Point on the north bank. Their red-cedar plankhouses held extended families, and dugout canoes carried fishermen to the salmon and sturgeon grounds and hunters after elk in the coastal hills. Rank ran from successful traders, warriors and shamans down to slaves taken in coastal raids, and free families bound infants' foreheads between boards so a flattened skull marked them off from captives. In 1444 the estuary was Chinook water, its canoes trading salmon, cedar and elk under the river's own rules, and no ocean-going ship had yet crossed the bar.

Bruno de Heceta sighted the headlands in 1775 and guessed a river lay behind them, but sickness aboard kept his ship outside; James Cook sailed past in 1778 and George Vancouver missed the mouth in April 1792. On 11 May 1792 Robert Gray took his ship Columbia across the breakers, traded near the point later named for the Chinook, and left his vessel's name on the river. Lewis and Clark reached Chinook Point in November 1805 and wintered across the estuary at Fort Clatsop, where Comcomly, the one-eyed principal chief of the Lower Chinook, came to meet them. John Jacob Astor's Pacific Fur Company raised Fort Astoria in 1811, and by then most of the estuary's trade passed through Comcomly's hands. In July 1813 he married a daughter to the post's manager, Duncan McDougall, and when the British sloop Racoon approached that autumn he gathered his warriors to defend the fort. The Astorians had already sold it in October to the Montreal-based North West Company, which renamed it Fort George; the Hudson's Bay Company inherited the post in 1821.
zh:
奇努克之地守着哥伦比亚河口，大河穿过游移的沙洲和成排碎浪注入太平洋。即便天气晴好，这个入口也能毁船，河门此后在欧洲船长的海图外藏了几十年。下奇努克人的村庄坐落在贝克湾和北岸的奇努克角后方，红雪松木板长屋里住着扩大家庭，独木舟载着渔人前往鲑鱼和鲟鱼渔场，载着猎人到滨海丘陵猎麋。社会等级从成功的商人、战士和萨满一直排到沿海劫掠中得来的奴隶；自由人家用木板把婴儿的前额夹平，以扁平头型区别于俘虏。1444年，整个河口都是奇努克人的水面，独木舟按本地规矩交易鲑鱼、雪松和麋鹿，还没有一艘远洋船越过那道沙洲。

1775年，布鲁诺·德·埃塞塔望见两岸岬角，猜测后面藏着一条大河，但船员患病，他的船只能停在外海；詹姆斯·库克1778年从旁经过，乔治·温哥华1792年4月也没找到河口。1792年5月11日，罗伯特·格雷驾「哥伦比亚号」越过碎浪，在后来以奇努克命名的岬角附近交易，河便以他的船得名。刘易斯与克拉克1805年11月抵达奇努克角，在河口对岸的克拉特索普堡过冬，下奇努克人的独眼大酋长康科姆利曾到营中相见。1811年，约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的太平洋毛皮公司建起阿斯托里亚堡，那时河口贸易大半要经康科姆利之手。1813年7月，他把一个女儿嫁给商馆主管邓肯·麦克杜格尔；同年秋天英国炮舰「浣熊号」逼近，他又集结战士准备协防。可阿斯托里亚人已在10月把商馆卖给蒙特利尔的西北公司，堡垒改称乔治堡，1821年由哈德逊湾公司接管。

en:
Duwamish country gathers around Elliott Bay and the lower Duwamish River, where glacier-cut tideflats open into the eastern reach of Puget Sound. The ebb laid bare wide mudflats thick with clams, salmon turned up the river each year, and cedar and fir covered the rising ground behind the shore. The Duwamish, whose Lushootseed name means 'people of the inside', lived in cedar longhouses in villages strung along the bay, the river and the lake behind them, and their canoes carried them to potlatches and trade meetings with other Coast Salish communities. In 1444 these were long-settled villages on a sheltered inland sea, and no European post lay within a thousand miles.

Diseases carried up from distant contacts reached the sound in the 1770s, and one village emptied after smallpox. George Vancouver's British ships anchored off the future site of Seattle on 19 May 1792, and his surveyors spent weeks taking the measure of the sound; on 4 June Vancouver claimed it for Britain and named it for Lieutenant Peter Puget. His lookouts had already spotted the great snow peak to the southeast, which he named Mount Rainier after his friend Rear Admiral Peter Rainier. The boy Sealth, later called Chief Seattle, was growing up in these villages while the ships worked the sound. Maritime fur traders soon learned the Strait of Juan de Fuca approach, swapping metal goods for pelts bound for China, but none built a post on Elliott Bay. From the early 1800s northern raiders, the Lekwiltok and other Kwakwaka'wakw, crossed the sound in long canoes to carry off slaves and plunder. The Anglo-American convention of 1818 made the Oregon Country a jointly occupied land, and in 1821 Duwamish villages still held the river.
zh:
杜瓦米什之地围绕埃利奥特湾和杜瓦米什河下游展开，冰川刻出的滩涂在这里汇入普吉特湾东段。退潮时大片泥滩裸露，贝类密布，鲑鱼每年溯河而上，岸后的高地上长满雪松和冷杉。杜瓦米什人的卢舒特塞德语名称意为「内在之地的人」，他们住在一座座雪松长屋里，村落沿海湾、河流和背后的湖泊分布；独木舟载着他们去参加夸富宴，与其他海岸萨利什村镇交易。1444年，这片遮蔽良好的内海上是定居已久的村庄，千里之内还没有欧洲人的据点。

远方接触带来的疫病1770年代传到海湾，一座村庄在天花过后荒弃。1792年5月19日，乔治·温哥华的英国船队在未来西雅图城所在的海岸外停泊，测量员花了几周测绘海湾；6月4日，温哥华以海军上尉彼得·普吉特之名为海湾命名，并宣布归英国所有。此前瞭望员已望见东南方那座积雪的大峰，温哥华以友人、海军少将彼得·雷尼尔之名称之为雷尼尔山。船队在湾中作业的那些日子，后来成为西雅图酋长的男孩西亚特尔正在这些村落里长大。海上毛皮商很快摸清了取道胡安·德富卡海峡的航路，用金属器换取运往中国的毛皮，却没有人在埃利奥特湾旁设立据点。19世纪初起，北方夸扣特尔诸部，包括莱奎尔托克人，驾长独木舟跨海而来，掳走奴隶和财物。1818年英美条约把俄勒冈地区划为共同占有，到1821年杜瓦米什村庄仍守着自己的河。

en:
Tachii'nii is the canyon country of Tséyiʼ, a Navajo name meaning 'inside the rock', east of the Hopi mesas; the stream leaving the canyon mouth gives Chʼíńlį̄, Chinle, its name. Ancestral Puebloan farmers built their towns into the sandstone walls: the White House stood in a cliff five hundred feet high from about 1060 to 1275, its upper rooms coated in white plaster, while Mummy Cave held close to seventy rooms in two alcoves three hundred feet above the floor. Drought emptied the canyons around 1300, and the people moved toward the Little Colorado River and Black Mesa; Hopi families afterwards kept seasonal fields and pilgrimage routes here into the late 1600s. In 1444 Diné, Navajo, bands ranged the wider plateau, hunting, gathering, growing corn, beans and squash, and trading at the Pueblo towns. The steep walls, seeps of water and empty cliff dwellings made the canyons a refuge rather than anyone's frontier post.

Around 1700 pressure from rival peoples drove Navajo families south-west into Tséyiʼ. They brought the sheep and goats acquired from the Spanish, grazed them along the rims and planted corn and peaches on the canyon floor beside the old ruins. Long raiding wars followed with the Rio Grande colonists and other Indian nations. On a winter day in 1805 Lieutenant Antonio Narbona led a Spanish expedition into Canyon del Muerto against Navajos fortified in a rock shelter; after an all-day fight he reported 115 killed and carried off thirty-three captives. The shelter is remembered as Massacre Cave. A peace was made that May, but Chinle remained a place of trade and reprisal for the rest of Spanish rule.
zh:
塔奇尼是霍皮台地以东特塞伊峡谷一带的峡谷之地，「特塞伊」是纳瓦霍语，意为「岩石之内」；流出峡口的溪流给峡外的钦利（Ch'inli）起了名字。古普韦布洛农民把村镇修进砂岩峭壁：白屋（White House）嵌在约一百五十米高的崖壁中，约1060年至1275年间有人居住，上层房舍抹着白灰；木乃伊洞（Mummy Cave）的两处岩龛高出峡底约九十米，有近七十间房舍。约1300年的大旱使峡谷空置，居民迁往小科罗拉多河和布莱克台地；此后霍皮家庭继续在此耕种季节性农田、保持朝圣路线，直到17世纪后期。1444年，迪内人（纳瓦霍人）的游群活动在更广阔的高原上，狩猎、采集，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，并到普韦布洛村镇贸易。陡壁、渗水的泉眼和空置的崖屋使这片峡谷成为避难所，而不是谁的边疆据点。

约1700年，敌对部族的压力把纳瓦霍家庭逐向西南，进入特塞伊。他们带来从西班牙人社会获得的绵羊和山羊，在崖顶放牧，在峡底的旧崖屋旁种植玉米和桃树。此后是同里奥格兰德殖民者及其他印第安民族之间漫长的袭掠战争。1805年冬季的一天，安东尼奥·纳沃纳中尉率西班牙远征军进入穆埃尔托峡谷，攻打据守在一处岩棚中的纳瓦霍人；激战一整天后，他报告杀死115人，掳走33人。这处岩棚后来被称为屠杀洞。同年5月双方议和，但在西班牙统治的余下岁月里，钦利始终是贸易与报复交织之地。

en:
Yavapé was the western country of the Yavapai, an Upland Yuman people who ranged over some ten million acres of west-central Arizona, from the San Francisco Peaks toward the Colorado and back to the Salt and Gila rivers. Four bands, the Yavapé, Wipukepa, Tolkepaya and Kewevkepaya, moved through mountains, plateaus and desert washes without a capital or a single chief; archaeologists trace them to Patayan groups that moved east from the Colorado around 1300. They raided and traded with the Western Apache, fought the Akimel O'odham over saguaro harvest grounds, and kept an on-and-off peace with the Pai, their kin to the north. In 1444 no Spaniard had yet entered their hills.

The first recorded Spaniard came in 1583, when Hopi guides led Antonio de Espejo to copper-bearing hills near Jerome; he had come looking for gold and went away disappointed. In 1598 Hopi guides brought Marcos Farfán de los Godos to the same mines, and he named the people cruzados for the crosses painted on their heads. Juan de Oñate crossed the country that same year and again in 1604-1605, seeking a road to the sea that the Yavapai had told him of, but no mission or presidio followed. Through the next two centuries Yavapai and Western Apache bands raided south for livestock and traded captives to the Spanish settlements for metal goods, horses and guns, while smallpox carried off about a quarter of the people. The Franciscan Francisco Garcés lived among Yavapai groups in 1776, and when New Spain's rule ended in 1821 the bands still held their trails and waterplaces.
zh:
亚瓦派是亚瓦派人西部群体的土地。亚瓦派人属高地尤曼语族群，在亚利桑那中西部约一千万英亩的土地上游徙，范围北起圣弗朗西斯科峰，西近科罗拉多河，南抵索尔特河与希拉河一带。他们分亚瓦佩、维普克帕、托尔克帕亚和克韦夫克帕亚四部，穿行于山地、高原和沙漠旱谷之间，没有都城，也没有统一的首领；考古学者认为，他们是约1300年从科罗拉多河畔东迁的帕塔扬人群的后裔。他们与西阿帕奇人时而贸易、时而联手劫掠，为仙人掌果的采集地同阿基梅尔·奥奥德姆人交战，和北方同族的派人时和时战。1444年时，还没有西班牙人进入过这些山地。
