有记载的第一个西班牙人是1583年由霍皮向导带到杰罗姆附近含铜山地的安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍，他本想寻找黄金，结果失望而归。1598年，霍皮向导又把马科斯·法尔凡·德·洛斯·戈多斯带到同一处矿山，他因当地人头上画着十字而称他们为「十字人」。胡安·德·奥尼亚特同年以及1604至1605年间两度经过这里，寻找亚瓦派人告诉他的出海通道，但传教站和要塞都没有随之而来。此后两个世纪里，亚瓦派与西阿帕奇群体南下劫掠牲畜，把俘虏卖到西班牙定居点，换取金属器、马匹和火器；天花又夺走约四分之一人口。方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯1776年曾在亚瓦派群体中生活；到1821年新西班牙统治结束时，各部仍掌握着自己的小径和水源地。

en:
The Akimel O'odham, 'river people' as the Spanish later rendered their name, Pimas, kept open ranchería villages along the Gila and Salt rivers of southern Arizona. In this dry land they drew river water through canals into fields of maize, beans and squash, wove cotton cloth and baskets, and carried their surplus to neighbouring peoples. Apache and Yavapai raiders tested the villages, though some bands also traded and intermarried with them. In 1444 the Akimel were settled farmers with no European mission or garrison anywhere near them.

The first Spaniard to reach the villages was the Jesuit Eusebio Francisco Kino, who rode through in 1694 on journeys that mapped Pimería Alta and brought wheat seed and livestock; no resident mission was built on the Gila. Settlers and miners pressing into O'odham land then provoked the 1751 revolt, led by Luis Oacpicagigua of Sáric, who drew at least fifteen thousand O'odham into one plan. On 20 November rebels killed eighteen settlers lured to his home, and over a hundred more across the Pimería Alta, including at Tubac. Oacpicagigua surrendered in March 1752 and died in a Spanish prison in 1755, and the crown built three presidios to hold the country, among them Tubac. When Mexican rule began in 1821, settlements and troops were still few along the Gila.
zh:
阿基梅尔·奥奥德姆意为「河畔的人」，西班牙人后来把他们的名字叫成皮马。他们在亚利桑那南部吉拉河与索尔特河畔开阔的牧场式村落里生活，开渠把河水引进玉米、菜豆和南瓜田，织造棉布与篮筐，再把剩余物产带到邻族那里。阿帕奇人和亚瓦派人不时袭掠这些村落，也有一些队群同他们贸易通婚。1444年，阿基梅尔人是定居的农人，附近没有任何欧洲传教站或驻军。

第一个进入这些村落的西班牙人是耶稣会士尤塞比奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺：他在1694年骑马经过，沿途测绘了上皮马利亚，也带来麦种和牲畜，但吉拉河畔始终没有建起常驻传教站。随后殖民者和矿工涌入奥奥德姆人的土地，引发1751年起义。萨里克的路易斯·奥阿克皮卡吉瓜把至少一万五千名奥奥德姆人联成一个计划，11月20日，起事者在他家中杀死十八名被诱来的定居者，上皮马利亚各地又有一百多人被杀，图巴克也在其中。奥阿克皮卡吉瓜于1752年3月投降，1755年死在西班牙人的监狱里；王室随后建起三座要塞镇守此地，图巴克是其中之一。1821年墨西哥统治开始时，吉拉河沿岸的居民点和军队仍然稀少。

en:
Kinyaa'aanii is the English spelling of Kinyaa'áanii, the Towering House clan, one of the four traditional Diné clans, whose name marks this canyon-and-mesa country on the eastern edge of Dinétah, between the Chuska Mountains and the upper Rio Grande. In 1444 Diné families moved between seasonal farmsteads and hunting camps, growing corn, beans and squash and carrying bison meat and hides to nearby Pueblo towns in exchange for maize and woven cotton. Authority rested with family and clan leaders, and no Spanish settlement yet occupied the frontier. After contact the Diné took up Spanish sheep and goats: the mountain flocks grew large, sheep became a form of wealth paid at weddings and in trade, and Diné women spun the wool into blankets that New Mexican buyers prized.

Spanish records before 1600 grouped these Southern Athabaskan speakers with Apaches or Quechos. In the 1620s Fray Jerónimo de Zárate-Salmerón wrote Apachu de Nabajo for people beyond the Chama; the word came from Tewa and meant 'a large area of cultivated lands', and by the 1640s the Spanish were calling them Navajo. Raiding back and forth with the New Mexican settlements brought expeditions into the Mount Taylor and Chuska Mountain country in the 1770s, after which Navajo, Spanish and Hopi parties kept a rough common front against Apache and Comanche bands for about twenty years. In 1800 Governor Chacón led five hundred men to the Tunicha Mountains and twenty Diné chiefs asked for peace; mutual expeditions in 1804 and 1805 ended in another agreement in May 1805. When Mexico became independent in 1821, it inherited the same round of raids, trade fairs and treaties.
zh:
金亚阿尼是纳瓦霍语高屋氏族（Kinyaa'áanii）的英文拼写。高屋氏族是迪内人四大传统氏族之一，省名即用来标识迪内塔东缘、丘斯卡山与格兰德河上游之间这片峡谷与方山交错的土地。1444年，迪内家族在季节性农田和狩猎营地间迁徙，种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，把野牛肉和兽皮带到邻近的普韦布洛城镇，换取玉米和棉布；权力在家族与氏族首领手中，边境上还没有西班牙人的居民点。接触西班牙人之后，迪内人接过了他们的绵羊和山羊：畜群在山里不断扩大，羊成为婚嫁和交易中支付的财富，迪内妇女纺出的羊毛毯也受到新墨西哥买主看重。

1600年以前的西班牙文献把这些说南阿萨巴斯卡语的人归入阿帕奇人或凯乔斯人。1620年代，修士赫罗尼莫·德·萨拉特-萨尔梅龙用「阿帕丘·德·纳瓦霍」称呼查马河以外的人群；这个词来自特瓦语，意为「大片开垦的土地」，到1640年代，西班牙人已通称他们为纳瓦霍。同新墨西哥居民点之间的相互袭掠，引来1770年代远征队攻入泰勒山和丘斯卡山一带；此后约二十年，纳瓦霍、西班牙和霍皮几方大致联手，对付阿帕奇和科曼奇队群。1800年，查孔总督率五百人进抵图尼查山，二十名迪内首领求和；1804和1805年双方互相远征，1805年5月再订和议。1821年墨西哥独立时，继承的还是袭掠、互市与订约一轮一轮的循环。

en:
The Ndee, 'the people' in Western Apache, held the broken mountains and watered valleys of east-central Arizona by the fifteenth century, the western edge of the country later called Apachería. Family bands kept to seasonal rancherías, hunting and gathering and tending small maize fields, and carried bison meat, hides and stone to Pueblo towns in exchange for woven cotton. Authority rested with local kin leaders, and no chief spoke for all the bands. In 1444 no Spaniard had yet entered these mountains.

The first Spanish account of any Apache people dates to April 1541, when Coronado met Querechos on the plains east of the pueblos and called them 'dog nomads': they followed the bison herds, lived in tents of tanned hide, and loaded their tent poles and baggage onto dogs. References to mobile peoples west of the Rio Grande appear by the 1580s. Horses then lengthened every journey, and by the late seventeenth century Apache raids reached Sonora while Spanish patrols answered with reprisals and captive-taking. Through the eighteenth century Comanche bands from the plains and the New Mexican frontier pressed the Ndee from two sides, but in 1821 the mountain paths of east-central Arizona remained theirs.
zh:
恩德（Ndee）在西阿帕奇语中意为「人民」。15世纪时，他们占据亚利桑那中东部崎岖山地和有水的谷地，这里处在日后所称阿帕奇利亚的西缘。家族队群住在季节性营地里，狩猎采集，也种小块玉米地；他们把野牛肉、兽皮和石器原料带到普韦布洛城镇，换回棉布。权力在地方亲族首领手中，没有哪个酋长能代表所有队群。1444年，还没有西班牙人进入这些山地。

西班牙人对阿帕奇人的最早记载是1541年4月：科罗纳多在普韦布洛地区以东的平原遇到凯雷乔人，称他们为「狗背上的游牧人」：他们随野牛群迁徙，住鞣皮帐篷，帐篷杆和行李都由狗驮运。到1580年代，西班牙文献开始提到格兰德河以西的流动族群。马匹随后延长了每一段行程，17世纪后期，阿帕奇人的袭击已抵达索诺拉，西班牙巡逻队则以报复和掳人回应。整个18世纪，平原上的科曼奇队群和新墨西哥边境从两面挤压恩德人，但到1821年，亚利桑那中东部的山地通道仍归他们所有。

en:
Ohkay Owingeh is a Tewa pueblo on the Rio Grande, at the mouth of the Rio Chama. It was founded around 1200, as the old Pueblo communities of the north consolidated into the plaza towns of the Tewa Basin; its people farmed maize, beans and squash on irrigated bottomland, and a kindred pueblo, Yúngéh, the 'place of the mockingbird', stood on the opposite bank between the two rivers. In 1444 it was one of the independent Tewa towns of the upper Rio Grande, and more than half a century would pass before Spaniards entered the valley.

Coronado's expedition passed through the Rio Grande pueblos in 1540–1542, but conquest came only in 1598, when Juan de Oñate was welcomed at Yúngéh and renamed Caypa, across the river, San Juan de los Caballeros. San Gabriel de Yunque, on the bank offered to the Spaniards, served as the first Spanish capital of New Mexico, until Pedro de Peralta moved the government to Santa Fe in 1610; missions and forced tribute followed. In 1675 the governor arrested forty-seven Pueblo medicine men on charges of sorcery, and among those flogged and imprisoned was Po'pay, a religious leader of this pueblo; Pueblo leaders marched on Santa Fe in force and secured his release. From Taos he planned the rising, and knotted cords went out to every pueblo, one knot to be untied each morning until the day appointed. When two Tesuque runners were caught and the Spaniards learned the date, Po'pay brought the revolt forward a day, and on 10 August 1680 the pueblos rose together, killed some 400 Spaniards, twenty-one of them Franciscan friars, and besieged Santa Fe until the governor cut his way out and led the survivors south to El Paso. New Mexico stayed in Pueblo hands for twelve years, and Po'pay ordered the churches pulled down and the old names and ritual baths taken up again. Diego de Vargas retook the valley in 1692, and San Juan remained one of the principal pueblos under Spanish, and later Mexican, rule.
zh:
奥凯奥温盖是格兰德河畔的一座特瓦人普韦布洛，位于查马河汇入格兰德河处。它约建于1200年，时值北方古普韦布洛社群聚合为特瓦盆地广场式村镇的年代；居民在灌溉农田上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，同族的云格村坐落在对岸两河之间，村名意为「反舌鸟之地」。1444年时，它是格兰德河上游独立的特瓦村镇之一，西班牙人还要半个多世纪才会进入这条河谷。

1540至1542年，科罗纳多的远征队曾穿行格兰德河沿岸的普韦布洛；征服迟至1598年才到来，胡安·德·奥尼亚特在云格受到接待，把对岸的凯帕村改名为圣胡安·德·洛斯·卡瓦列罗斯，让出的云格村改称圣加夫列尔·德·云格，成为西属新墨西哥的第一个首府。1610年，佩德罗·德·佩拉尔塔把治所迁往圣菲，传教和强征贡赋随之而来。1675年，总督以行巫术的罪名逮捕四十七名普韦布洛祭司，本村的宗教领袖波·依受了鞭刑并入狱；各普韦布洛首领率众进逼圣菲，才把他救出。他在陶斯策划起义，打着绳结的绳子送往各个普韦布洛，约定每天早晨解开一个结，到最后一个结解开之日同时举事。两名特苏克信使被抓、西班牙人得知日期后，波·依把起义提前一天。1680年8月10日，各普韦布洛一同起事，杀死约四百名西班牙人，其中二十一人是方济各会士，并围攻圣菲，逼得总督突围而出，带着幸存者南撤埃尔帕索。新墨西哥在普韦布洛人手中维持了十二年，波·依还下令拆毁教堂，恢复旧名和仪式沐浴。1692年，迭戈·德·巴尔加斯重新占领河谷，圣胡安在此后西班牙及墨西哥的统治下，一直是主要的普韦布洛之一。

en:
Tsiahahéndé is the Rio Grande valley around Teypana, a Piro pueblo on the west bank above the Jornada del Muerto, the ninety-kilometre desert crossing where travellers found no water. The Piro spoke a Tanoan tongue, and in the fifteenth century they held a river corridor about ninety-seven kilometres long through what is now Socorro County, their maize fields and towns packed into the green bosque along the bank while desert lay beyond. They may have numbered 7,000; their largest town, San Pascual, was later counted at roughly 1,500 rooms and 2,000 people. Mescalero and other Apache families moved through the surrounding mountains and basin, gathering mescal, hunting, trading and sometimes raiding the river towns. In 1444 Teypana, Pilabó, San Pascual and Senecú were still wholly Indigenous pueblos.

In June 1598 Juan de Oñate's settlers emerged from five waterless days on the Jornada del Muerto, and the people of Teypana fed them and gave them drink; the Spaniards renamed the pueblo Socorro, 'help'. Around 1626 a mission, Nuestra Señora de Perpetuo Socorro, was opened at nearby Pilabó, and mines were already working in the nearby mountains; a friar counted about 600 people in the district. Epidemics and Apache raids cut the Piro pueblos down so far that later local risings came to nothing, and when the great Pueblo Revolt broke out in 1680 it took place without them. Several hundred Piros and Tiwas left with the retreating Spaniards for El Paso, where Piro refugees founded Senecú del Sur in 1682; none of the old riverside pueblos was ever reoccupied by its own people. By the Spanish reconquest of 1692 Socorro stood in ruins, and governors ordered its resettlement more than once before the first settlers returned, in about 1815.
zh:
齐亚哈亨德是特帕纳周围的里奥格兰德河谷。特帕纳是一座皮罗人的普韦布洛，在河西岸，南面便是长约九十公里、全程找不到水源的沙漠旱路霍尔纳达德尔穆埃尔托，意为「死者之旅」。皮罗人说一种塔诺语族的语言。15世纪时，他们据有今索科罗县境内约97公里长的河谷走廊，玉米田和村镇挤在河畔绿色林带中，林带之外便是沙漠。他们的人口可能有7000；最大的圣帕斯夸尔后来被清点出约1500间房舍、两千名居民。梅斯卡莱罗等阿帕奇家庭在周围的山地和盆地间游走，采集龙舌兰、狩猎、贸易，有时也袭掠河畔村镇。1444年，特帕纳、皮拉博、圣帕斯夸尔和塞内库仍完全是印第安人的普韦布洛。

1598年6月，奥尼亚特率领的殖民者在霍尔纳达德尔穆埃尔托熬过五天无水的行程，走出沙漠时，特帕纳人给他们送来食物和饮水；西班牙人便把这座普韦布洛改叫索科罗，意为「援助」。约1626年，邻近的皮拉博建起永助圣母传教站，附近山区的矿坑也已经开工；有修士清点出当地约600人。疫病和阿帕奇袭击使皮罗诸村人口锐减，后来几次局部起事都归于失败，1680年大普韦布洛起义爆发时，皮罗人已经无力参加。数百名皮罗人和蒂瓦人随撤退的西班牙人前往埃尔帕索，皮罗难民于1682年在那里建起塞内库德尔苏尔；河畔的旧村镇再没有被原居民重新居住。到1692年西班牙人重新征服时，索科罗已成废墟；历任总督几次下令重新设殖，第一批移民直到约1815年才返回。

en:
The Llano Estacado, the Staked Plains, is a vast grassy tableland ringed by caprock bluffs between the Canadian River and the Pecos, standing high above the surrounding desert. In 1444 Apache bands who called themselves the Mashgaléndé, 'the people near the mountains', pitched their skin lodges across it. They followed the bison herds with their whole households, dogs hauling poles and bundles on travois; they cut the meat thin to dry in the sun, pounded it and mixed it with fat to carry on the march, and came back to the desert edge to roast the sweet hearts of mescal agave. No European had yet seen the southern plains, and the horse was still unknown to them.

Francisco Vásquez de Coronado crossed the tableland in 1541, marching east from the Rio Grande in search of Quivira, and found a Querecho camp of some two hundred hide lodges among uncounted bison; his men were the first Europeans to look on the Great Plains. The Spanish later called these Apaches Mescaleros, after the agave that fed them. Mounted on Spanish horses, they raided deep into New Mexico and Nueva Vizcaya, but early in the eighteenth century the expanding Comanche drove them off the tableland, which became part of the Comancheria. Hugo O'Conor, the red-haired commandant the Apache called the Red Captain, harried them through the 1770s without ever breaking them.
zh:
埃斯塔卡多平原是一座被崖岸环绕的辽阔草甸台地，横亘在加拿大河与佩科斯河之间，高踞四周荒漠之上。1444年，自称马什加伦德（意为「靠近群山的人」）的阿帕切诸部在台地上支起皮帐。他们带着全家老小追随野牛群，狗用滑橇拖着木杆和行囊；肉切薄片晒干、舂碎拌上油脂，便于行军携带，回到荒野边缘再烘烤龙舌兰甘甜的茎心。此时还没有欧洲人见过南部大平原，他们也还不知道马。

1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多为寻找基维拉从格兰德河率军东进，越过台地，在数不清的野牛中间发现一座约有200顶皮帐的克雷乔人营地，他的部下是第一批望见大平原的欧洲人。西班牙人后来以供养他们的龙舌兰为名，把这些阿帕切人称作梅斯卡莱罗人。骑上西班牙人的马后，他们深入新墨西哥和新比斯开袭掠；但18世纪初，扩张中的科曼奇人把他们赶下台地，埃斯塔卡多并入科曼切里亚。被阿帕切人称为「红队长」的红发司令乌戈·奥康纳在1770年代反复追剿，却始终没能压服他们。

en:
From the cedar canyons of the Edwards Plateau south to the oak grasslands cut by the San Antonio and Nueces rivers stretched the country of the Lipan, the easternmost of the Apache peoples, who called themselves the Łebaį́ Ndé, the Light Gray People. In 1444 they moved with the bison and white-tailed deer, hauling hide tipis on dog travois, and their rancherías grew corn, beans and pumpkins in cleared ground. They had no horses yet, and no European had entered their plains.

The Lipan had Spanish horses by 1608 and became the raiders every supply train feared on the road from Coahuila to San Antonio; their name first appears in Spanish records in 1718, after they struck that town. Pressed by the Comanche, two Lipan chiefs made peace at San Antonio in 1749, and the Spanish built Mission Santa Cruz de San Sabá for them in 1757. No Lipan ever settled in it, but it told the Comanche that Spain had taken their enemy's side, and in 1758 some 2,000 Comanche, Tonkawa, Bidai and Hasinai warriors burned the mission to the ground. It was the only mission in Texas destroyed outright by native attackers; the presidio built beside it was left alone. The mission's patron, Pedro Romero de Terreros, later had the destruction painted, and the picture finished in 1765 was the first painting of an historical event made in Spanish Texas. A punitive column of more than 500 Spaniards and Lipan under Diego Ortiz Parrilla marched north in 1759 and was beaten at a moated, stockaded Taovaya village on the Red River, leaving two cannon behind. The Candelaria and San Lorenzo missions were deserted by 1767, the year the Marqués de Rubí ordered a war of extermination against a people thinned by the smallpox of 1764. Lipan scouts nonetheless kept serving the Spanish crown, and in 1811 they were with the royalist column that seized the rebel priest Miguel Hidalgo at Acatita de Baján.
zh:
切沙从爱德华兹高原雪松丛生的峡谷向南，直到圣安东尼奥河与努埃塞斯河切过的橡树草原，是利潘人的土地。利潘人是阿帕切诸族中位置最靠东的一支，自称韦巴因·恩德，意为「浅灰色的人」。1444年，他们随着野牛和白尾鹿迁徙，用狗拉滑橇拖着皮帐，营地的清地上种玉米、豆类和南瓜。此时他们还没有马，也没有欧洲人踏入这片草原。

到1608年，利潘人已得到西班牙人的马，科阿韦拉通往圣安东尼奥的路上，每支补给车队都怕他们袭掠；1718年他们攻打圣安东尼奥，利潘的名字第一次出现在西班牙文书中。迫于科曼奇人的压力，两名利潘酋长1749年在圣安东尼奥议和，西班牙人1757年为他们修建圣萨瓦圣十字传教站。利潘人从不住进去，但这座传教站让科曼奇人认定西班牙站到了仇敌一边。1758年，约两千名科曼奇、通卡瓦、比达伊和哈西奈战士把传教站焚为平地，这是得克萨斯唯一一座被原住民彻底毁掉的传教站；旁边的要塞他们没有动。传教站的资助人佩德罗·罗梅罗·德·特雷罗斯后来请人把这场焚毁画了下来，1765年完成的这幅画是西属得克萨斯第一幅描绘历史事件的画作。1759年，迭戈·奥尔蒂斯·帕里利亚率领五百多名西班牙士兵和利潘人北上讨伐，在雷德河畔一座环有壕沟、立着木栅的塔奥瓦亚村落前战败，丢下两门火炮。坎德拉里亚和圣洛伦索两座传教站到1767年也告废弃，就在这一年，鲁维侯爵对刚遭1764年天花削弱的利潘人颁下剿灭令。利潘斥候仍继续为西班牙王室效力，1811年他们随保王军纵队在阿卡特塔·德·巴汉俘获了起事神父米格尔·伊达尔戈。

en:
Auia is the Karankawa name preserved in Spanish records for the low Gulf shore between Galveston and Corpus Christi bays, where the lower Brazos and Colorado rivers reach the sea behind a chain of barrier islands. In 1444 it was no single chiefdom: the Capoque, Coco and other related Karankawa bands moved with the seasons, fishing and gathering shellfish in the passes and hunting deer and bison on the coastal prairie. Their language is usually classed as isolated, canoes carried them between island camps, and trade linked the shore dwellers with peoples far inland.

Pineda's Spanish ships were the first to chart this coast, entering Corpus Christi Bay in 1519 with the first documented European claim to the Karankawa shore. A closer meeting followed in 1528, when survivors of Pánfilo de Narváez's Florida expedition, Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca among them, were wrecked on Galveston Island and cared for by the Capoque. Cabeza de Vaca lived among the coastal peoples for seven years, supporting himself as a healer and trader, and wrote the first European account of them. In 1685 La Salle planted Fort Saint-Louis on Matagorda Bay, hundreds of kilometres west of the Mississippi mouth he had aimed for. After the French seized Karankawa canoes, the band waited until La Salle had walked inland, where his own followers murdered him on the Brazos in 1687, and then killed the settlers left in the fort and took five children alive. Alonso de León reached the ruins for Spain in 1689. A French boy raised by the Karankawa later testified that they ate the flesh of slain enemy warriors but would not touch the French dead. Spain built the La Bahía presidio in 1721 and the Espíritu Santo mission beside it in 1722, then moved the post to the Guadalupe River in 1726; disease, mission life and frontier war wore the bands down. In 1817 the privateer Jean Lafitte set up his Galveston Island camp of Campeche, and in 1821 Spanish Texas passed to newly independent Mexico.
zh:
奥亚是西班牙文献中保留下来的卡兰卡瓦语名称，指加尔维斯顿湾与科珀斯克里斯蒂湾之间的低平湾岸，布拉索斯河、科罗拉多河下游在一连串障壁岛之后入海。1444年，这里并非统一的酋邦：卡波克、科科等彼此亲缘的卡兰卡瓦群体随季节迁移，在潮汐水道捕鱼采贝，到沿海草原猎鹿和野牛。他们的语言通常被归为孤立语言，独木舟往来于海岛营地之间，贸易把湾岸居民同远在内陆的人群联系起来。

皮内达的西班牙船队最早测绘这段海岸，1519年驶入科珀斯克里斯蒂湾，这是欧洲人对卡兰卡瓦湾岸最早有记载的权利主张。更直接的接触发生在1528年，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯佛罗里达远征的幸存者在加尔维斯顿岛遇险，阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡也在其中，卡波克人收留并照料了他们。卡韦萨·德·巴卡在湾岸人群中生活了七年，靠行医和做买卖为生，写下欧洲人对他们最早的记述。1685年，拉萨尔在马塔戈达湾建起圣路易堡，地点偏离他原定的密西西比河口数百公里。法国人夺取卡兰卡瓦人的独木舟后，卡兰卡瓦人等到拉萨尔远行内陆（他1687年在布拉索斯河畔被自己的同伙杀死），便攻进堡垒杀死留守的定居者，只留下五个孩子的性命。1689年，阿隆索·德·莱昂代表西班牙找到堡垒废墟。一个被卡兰卡瓦人养大的法国男孩后来作证说，他们会吃战场上被杀敌人的肉，却不肯碰法国死者的遗体。1721年西班牙修建拉巴伊亚要塞，1722年在旁边设立圣神传教站，1726年又把据点迁到瓜达卢佩河畔；疾病、传教区生活和边境战争逐渐耗尽了这些群体。1817年，私掠船长让·拉菲特在加尔维斯顿岛设立他的坎佩切营地；1821年，西属得克萨斯转入独立的墨西哥之手。

en:
Gulgahén, an Apache name for the people of the open plain, covers part of the Llano Estacado, a high, nearly treeless tableland stretching across eastern New Mexico and the Texas Panhandle and ringed by caprock bluffs; the Spanish later called it the Staked Plain. Water is scarce on the flat grassland, and in 1444 Apache bison hunters knew the few draws that cut through the escarpment to reliable springs. They moved with the herds in skin lodges, used dogs to pull travois, sliced bison meat thin to dry in the sun, and pounded it with fat to carry on the march.

Francisco Vázquez de Coronado's army, striking east in 1541 in search of Quivira, was the first European force to cross the tableland, and its chroniclers found a camp of about two hundred skin lodges belonging to hunters they called Querechos, the name the people of Pecos Pueblo used for these Apache. Horses spread over the Southern Plains after the 1680 Pueblo Revolt scattered Spanish herds, and mounted Comanche bands pushed the Apache off the Llano soon afterwards; by the early eighteenth century the plain was the western reach of Comanchería, with Comanche war trails running south-west toward the Pecos and the Rio Grande.
zh:
古尔加亨是阿帕奇语里对开阔平原居民的称呼，省境据有埃斯塔卡多平原的一部分。这片高台地横亘新墨西哥东部与得克萨斯锅柄地带，几乎无树，四周环着岩帽陡崖，西班牙人后来称之为「立桩平原」。台面草原水源稀少，1444年时，阿帕奇野牛猎人认得少数切穿崖壁、通往稳定泉眼的旱谷。他们住兽皮帐篷，随牛群迁徙，用狗拖拉沃伊橇；野牛肉切薄片晒干，再春碎拌上油脂，带在行军路上食用。

1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多率军东进寻找基维拉，成为第一支穿越台地的欧洲武装；随行史官在草原上见到约两百座兽皮帐篷的营地，营中猎人被他们称作「克雷乔人」，这本是佩科斯普韦布洛人对这些阿帕奇人的叫法。1680年普韦布洛起义打散西班牙马群后，马匹传遍南部平原，骑马的科曼奇群体随即将阿帕奇人赶下台地；到18世纪初，这片平原已是科曼奇里亚的西缘，科曼奇人的袭掠路线向西南通往佩科斯河与格兰德河。

en:
The blackland prairies of the middle Brazos, broken by oak groves and pale limestone bluffs, were the country of the Waco, a Wichita people whom the earliest Spanish reports called the Yscani. Their principal village stood on this stretch of the river, a permanent town of conical, grass-thatched lodges ringed by granaries and brush-fenced fields of maize, beans, pumpkins and melons. Two Tawakoni villages, El Quiscat and the Flechazos, stood close by, and the men left on seasonal hunts after bison out on the plains. The Waco tattooed their faces and spoke a Caddoan tongue. In 1444 neither horses nor Europeans had reached their towns.

The Teyas farmers whom Coronado met on the plains to the west in 1541 may have been ancestors of the Waco. Epidemics and pressure from the Osage and Apache drew the Wichita bands south, and by 1730 the Waco and their Tawakoni kinsmen had settled their villages on the Brazos; Guillaume de L'Isle's map of 1718 already marks a 'Quainco' who were probably the Waco, and La Harpe travelled among villages like theirs in 1719. A French-brokered peace with the Comanche in 1746 made the Wichita towns into busy trading places, and in 1759 Wichita and Comanche warriors threw back a 500-man Spanish column under Parrilla at the fortified Twin Villages on the Red River, taking two cannon. The Tawakoni chief Quiscat went down to San Antonio to seek peace in 1772. Smallpox swept the Wichita towns in 1777 and 1778, but the Waco kept their Brazos village, which was still occupied in 1820.
zh:
布拉索斯河中游的黑土草原上，橡树林与浅色石灰岩崖壁交错，这里是韦科人的土地。韦科人是威奇托人的一支，最早的西班牙文书称他们为伊斯卡尼人。他们的主村就在河的这一段，圆锥形草顶屋组成一座定居大村，村外是一座座谷仓和灌木围篱圈起的田，种着玉米、豆类、南瓜和甜瓜。紧邻着他们的是埃尔基斯卡特和弗莱查索斯两座塔瓦科尼村落，男人们按季节到平原上猎野牛。韦科人纹面，说卡多语族的语言。1444年，马和欧洲人都还没有到达他们的村镇。

科罗纳多1541年在西边平原上遇到务农的特亚人，他们可能是韦科人的先祖。疫病和奥塞奇人、阿帕切人的压力把威奇托诸部向南驱赶，到1730年，韦科人和塔瓦科尼亲族已在布拉索斯河畔定居；纪尧姆·德·利勒1718年的地图上已标出一个「宽科」（Quainco），多半就是韦科人，拉阿尔普1719年穿行过的村落也可能是他们的。1746年法国撮合威奇托人与科曼奇人议和，威奇托诸镇成了热闹的交易场；1759年，威奇托与科曼奇战士在雷德河设防的双子村击退帕里利亚率领的五百人西班牙纵队，缴获两门火炮。塔瓦科尼酋长基斯卡特1772年南下圣安东尼奥求和。1777年和1778年天花横扫威奇托诸镇，韦科人却守住了布拉索斯河畔的村子，1820年那里仍有人居住。

en:
The prairies between the Brazos and Colorado rivers later bore the name Tickanwa'tic, the Tonkawa word for 'real people'; Tonkawa itself is a Waco name meaning roughly 'they all stay together'. In 1444 no fixed chiefdom ruled the grassland. Small bands followed buffalo and deer with skin lodges and dog travois, while Caddo-speaking farmers held the pine country to the east. The people later called Tonkawa were then still far to the north: Spanish records place them in northwestern Oklahoma in 1601, and Apache and Wichita pressure had driven them south to the Red River by 1700. They crossed into central Texas only at the end of the seventeenth century.

Some bands settled among the Yojuane at the San Gabriel missions in the 1740s, and a mission opened for them in 1756 drew almost no converts. Two years later Tonkawa fighters joined Comanches, Yojuanes, Bidais and Hasinais in an army Spanish estimates put at 2,000 men that burned Mission Santa Cruz de San Sabá. The mission had been built on the San Saba River for the Lipan Apache though no Apache ever lived there, and it was the only Texas mission destroyed completely by Indians; the nearby presidio went untouched. The Tonkawa made peace with Spain in 1770 and traded bison and deer hides and tallow for firearms, and a Spanish count in 1778 numbered 300 warriors. In 1821 they remained a power on the Texas frontier, holding to shifting alliances rather than mission life.
zh:
布拉索斯河与科罗拉多河之间的草原后来得名蒂坎瓦蒂克，这是通卡瓦语中「真人」的意思；而「通卡瓦」本身是瓦科人的叫法，大意是「他们聚居在一起」。1444年，这片草原上没有固定的酋邦，小群体带着兽皮帐篷、靠狗拉拖橇追逐野牛和鹿，东面的松林地带则掌握在说卡多语的农人手中。后来被称为通卡瓦人的人群此时还远在北方：1601年的西班牙记载把他们记在今俄克拉荷马西北部，到1700年，阿帕奇人和威奇托人的逼迫已把他们赶到雷德河一线。直到17世纪末，他们才进入得州中部。

1740年代，一些群体到圣加布里埃尔传教站与约胡安人比邻而居；1756年专为他们开设的传教站几乎无人皈依。两年后，通卡瓦战士与科曼奇人、约胡安人、比代人和哈西奈人合兵，据西班牙人估计有两千人之众，焚毁了圣克鲁斯·德·圣萨瓦传教站。这座传教站修在圣萨瓦河畔，本为招抚利潘阿帕奇人而建，却从没有阿帕奇人进去住过；它也是得州唯一一座被印第安人彻底摧毁的传教站，旁边的要塞倒没有受到攻击。1770年，通卡瓦人与西班牙议和，用野牛皮、鹿皮和油脂换取火器；1778年西班牙人清点出他们有三百名战士。1821年，他们仍是得州边境上的一支力量，凭的是反复改换的盟约，而不是传教站里的定居生活。

en:
The Ishak, 'the people' in their own tongue, were called Atakapa by the Choctaw, a name meaning 'people-eater', for their war custom of eating the flesh of slain enemies, and French writers later took the name from the Choctaw. Their marshy prairies and bayous ran from Galveston Bay and the Trinity River east to the Calcasieu, Mermentau and Vermilion rivers, where the Akokisa, Bidai and other related bands lived independently and spoke an isolated language. They fished and hunted small game, gathered roots and berries, and sent dried fish, shark teeth, hides and salt dug at inland salt domes along the Gulf trade routes to Caddo, Chitimacha and Karankawa neighbours. In 1444 their world held no Europeans; deerskin clothing, tattooing and portable camps suited a coast of tides, passes and river mouths.

Europeans first documented these bands in November 1528, when castaways of Pánfilo de Narváez's expedition reached Isla de Malhado near Galveston and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca wrote the earliest account of them. French traders entered with the founding of Louisiana in 1699. The man-eating name found a fresh witness in 1719, when the French officer François Simars de Bellisle was shipwrecked near Galveston Bay: he spent eighteen months as an Akokisa captive and watched his captors butcher and eat a slain enemy warrior during a bison hunt, until Hasinai traders carried a letter from him to the French commander at Natchitoches, who sent a rescue party in 1721. After Louisiana passed to Spain in 1762, Acadians led by Joseph Broussard were settled among the bayous in 1765. Their cattle ranches drew Eastern Atakapa families into the steer trade, registering brands at Poste des Attakapas, where a census counted 409 inhabitants in 1766. After the Louisiana Purchase of 1803 American officials organised Attakapas Parish in 1805; by then planters were taking communal land along the Mermentau and Vermilion, and John Sibley put the number of Atakapa men left in Louisiana at about fifty.
zh:
伊沙克在他们自己的语言里意为「人」，乔克托人却称他们为阿塔卡帕，意思是「食人者」，因为他们有在战时吃被杀敌人之肉的习俗，后来的法国人也从乔克托人那里沿用了这个名字。他们的沼泽草原与河湖水乡从加尔维斯顿湾、特里尼蒂河向东延伸到卡尔克苏河、梅门托河和弗米利恩河，阿科基萨、比戴等亲缘群体各自生活在这些流域，使用一种孤立语言。他们捕鱼、猎取小动物、采集根茎和浆果，把干鱼、鲨鱼牙、兽皮和在内陆盐丘挖得的盐，沿湾岸商路卖给卡多、奇蒂马查和卡兰卡瓦邻人。1444年，他们的世界里还没有欧洲人；鹿皮衣、纹身和便于迁移的营地，适合潮汐、水道与河口交错的海岸。

欧洲人最早在1528年11月留下关于这些群体的记载，当时潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯远征的落水者抵达加尔维斯顿附近的厄运岛，阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡写下关于他们的最早记述。法国商人随1699年路易斯安那的建立进入此地。「食人者」之名在1719年等来新的目击者：法国军官弗朗索瓦·西马尔·德·贝利勒在加尔维斯顿湾附近遇海难，被阿科基萨人掳走18个月，在一次野牛围猎中目睹俘获他的人肢解并吃掉一名被杀的敌族战士；最后哈西奈商人把他的一封信带到纳基托什的法国长官那里，救兵于1721年将他接走。路易斯安那1762年转交西班牙后，约瑟夫·布鲁萨尔率领的阿卡迪亚人于1765年被安置到这片河湖地带。他们的牧场把东阿塔卡帕家庭带入菜牛买卖，到阿塔卡帕驿站登记自家牛只的耳记，1766年的人口普查在当地数出409名居民。1803年路易斯安那购地后，美国官员于1805年设立阿塔卡帕堂区；那时种植园主正在取得梅门托河与弗米利恩河沿岸的共有土地，约翰·西布利统计路易斯安那剩下的阿塔卡帕男子只有约五十人。

en:
Nawunena, 'the Southern People', was the southernmost of the Arapaho divisions, but the Arapaho were nowhere near this dry shortgrass plain in 1444. Its pedestrians were Apache hunters, the people later called Querechos: they pitched bison-hide lodges, hauled their goods on dog travois, sliced meat thin to dry in the sun and pounded it with fat into pemmican, and dealt with strangers in Plains sign language. The Arapaho proper then lived far to the northeast, an Algonquian farming people of the western Great Lakes who grew maize and hunted beside the group later known as the Gros Ventre in the Red River valley.

In 1541 Coronado's army crossed this part of the High Plains in search of Quivira and came on a Querecho camp of some two hundred hide lodges on the Llano Estacado, the first Europeans to set down how the plains nomads lived. The chroniclers watched troops of dogs hauling lodge poles, noted meat dried like leaves and blood carried to drink in a bison gut, and wrote that the people moved camp like the Arabs, with their tents and dog teams. Early in the eighteenth century Ojibwe gunmen pushed the Arapaho and the Gros Ventre out of the Red River country toward the upper Missouri, where the two peoples parted. Arapaho bands turned south into Wyoming and Colorado, took up horse nomadism, and became plains middlemen, trading bison meat and hides to the Arikara, Mandan and Hidatsa farming towns for maize and beans; the Pawnee word for 'trader' is one likely root of the name Arapaho. Allied with the Cheyenne from about 1811, the southern camps had coalesced as the Nawunena by 1821, running horses and furs between the Platte and the Arkansas.
zh:
纳乌内纳（Nawunena）意为「南方人」，本是阿拉帕霍人最南的一支，但1444年时阿拉帕霍人离这片干旱的短草平原还很远。在这里徒步行走的是阿帕奇猎人，也就是后来被称作克雷乔（Querecho）人的群体：他们搭野牛皮帐篷，用狗拉橇搬运家当，把肉切薄晒干，再拌上油脂捣成肉糜饼，与外人打交道时使用平原手势语。那时真正的阿拉帕霍人还远在东北方，是五大湖以西的阿尔冈昆农耕者，在雷德河谷种玉米、打猎，邻着后来被称为格罗斯文特人的族群。

1541年，科罗纳多的军队为寻找基维拉穿过这一带高地平原，在拉诺埃斯塔卡多遇到一座约有两百顶皮帐的克雷乔营地，欧洲人这才第一次记下草原游牧者的生活。随军编年史家看到成群的狗拖着帐杆，记下他们薄如叶片的干肉和灌在野牛肠子里随身饮用的血，还写道这些人带着帐篷和狗队拔营迁移，如同阿拉伯人一般。18世纪初，持有火枪的欧及布威人把阿拉帕霍人和格罗斯文特人逼出雷德河地区，推向密苏里河上游，两族在那里分手。阿拉帕霍诸支转而南下怀俄明和科罗拉多，过上骑马游牧的日子，又做起草原中间商，用野牛肉和皮革到阿利卡拉、曼丹和希达察人的农耕村镇换取玉米和豆类；波尼语里意为「商人」的词，很可能就是阿拉帕霍一名的来源之一。约1811年起他们与夏延人结盟，到1821年，南方各营已合为纳乌内纳一支，在普拉特河与阿肯色河之间贩运马匹和皮货。

en:
Tokinahyup is a sweep of shortgrass plains between the Arkansas River and the small streams of southern Kansas. In 1444 it belonged to the Caddoan world of the Wichita and their Pawnee kin: families farmed corn, beans and squash in river-bottom fields, joined communal bison hunts on foot, and gathered in villages of grass-thatched lodges that might hold a hundred or two hundred houses. The Wichita marked their faces and bodies with straight tattooed lines, so later Spaniards called some of them the Rayados, 'striped ones'. At the Great Bend of the Arkansas their well-watered fields were already the country those Spaniards would hear of as Quivira, and downstream stood Etzanoa, 'the Great Settlement', a Wichita town that may have held 20,000 people in the two centuries after 1450.

In 1541 Francisco Vázquez de Coronado reached the Arkansas with thirty horsemen. A Plains guide the Spaniards called the Turk had drawn him north with stories of a bearded king who wore gold, but Coronado found straw-roofed villages and a chief with a copper necklace; before marching back to New Mexico he had the Turk garroted for the deception. Friar Juan de Padilla returned to preach and was killed by Quivirans soon after. Other Spanish parties reached the same towns in 1594 and 1601, and the French officer Bourgmont visited the Great Bend with Kaw companions in 1724. Plains Apache pressure and smallpox thinned the Wichita during those years as horses spread among the southern plains nations. The country passed from France to Spain in 1762, back to France, and to the United States in 1803; by then the Kiowa and their Naisha Apache allies were moving south towards these hunting grounds, and in 1821 no settler had yet taken the land.
zh:
托基纳休普是阿肯色河与堪萨斯南部诸溪之间的一片短草平原。1444年，这里属于威奇托人及其波尼亲族所在的卡多语世界：各家族在河谷低地种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，结队徒步围猎野牛，聚集时住在茅草覆顶的村落里，有的村子有一两百座屋舍。威奇托人在脸和身上纹出直线条，后来西班牙人因此把其中一些人称作拉亚多人，意为「带条纹的人」。他们在阿肯色河大拐弯一带溪流纵横、田地肥沃，那就是后来西班牙人听说的基维拉；下游方向还有埃察诺阿，意为「大聚落」，这座威奇托城镇在1450年后的两百年间可能住过两万人。

1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多率三十名骑手抵达阿肯色河。把他引向北方的是一个被西班牙人称为「土耳其人」的平原印第安向导，此人声称有一位身披黄金的长髯国王；科罗纳多见到的却是茅草顶村落和戴铜项圈的酋长，撤回新墨西哥之前，他下令以欺瞒之罪将「土耳其人」绞杀。胡安·德·帕迪利亚修士重返此地传教，不久被基维拉人杀死。后来又有西班牙队伍在1594年和1601年抵达这些城镇，法国军官布尔蒙则在1724年与堪萨斯人同伴一起到访大拐弯。那些年里，平原阿帕奇人的压力和天花使威奇托人人口锐减，马匹也在南部平原各族中传开。1762年，这片土地由法国转交西班牙，后来归还法国，1803年售予美国；此时基奥瓦人和他们的纳伊沙阿帕奇盟友正向南趋近这片猎场，到1821年，还没有任何定居者占下这片土地。

en:
Naisha keeps Ná'ishą, the Plains Apache autonym, said to mean 'takers' for their skill at stealing horses. The camp name Jicarilla is Mexican Spanish for 'little basket', after the sealed water-baskets made by the Eastern Apache bands who hunted the grassland between the Canadian and Arkansas rivers. In 1444 Southern Athabaskan bison hunters crossed these short-grass pastures and cottonwood bottoms on foot, dragging loads on dog travois; they dried meat and hides, knew the seasonal waterholes, and traded plains produce to the farming villages on either side, before horses or Europeans had reached the Southern Plains.

Francisco Vázquez de Coronado's army marched along the Canadian, which he called the Río Cicuyé, in 1541, chasing the gold of Quivira and finding none, and Juan de Oñate followed the same river east in 1601. Horses spread after the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, and mounted Comanche bands pressed the Apache hard through the next century. The Ná'ishą, never more than a few hundred people (their number was put at about four hundred in 1780) and allied with the Kiowa in Plains Indian Sign Language, lived around the upper Missouri early in the 1700s and made this part of the Southern Plains their main range only around 1800. In 1821 the grassland was still Indian country, claimed only at a distance by newly independent Mexico.
zh:
省名纳伊沙保留了平原阿帕奇人的自称 Naisha，据说意为「掠取者」，得自他们盗马的本领。首府名希卡里亚是墨西哥西班牙语「小篮子」的意思，来自东阿帕奇群体制作的密封水篮；这些人也在加拿大河与阿肯色河之间的草原游猎。1444年，南阿萨巴斯卡野牛猎人步行往来于短草牧场和三角叶杨河谷，用狗拖拉沃伊橇；他们晒制肉干、加工兽皮，熟悉各处季节性水洼，把草原物产拿到两边的务农村镇交换，那时马匹和欧洲人都还没有到南部平原。

1541年，弗朗西斯科·巴斯克斯·德·科罗纳多的军队沿加拿大河东进，他把这条河称作西库耶河；他们追寻基维拉的黄金，却一无所获。1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特又沿同一条河东下。1680年普韦布洛起义后马匹扩散，在接下来的一个世纪里，骑马的科曼奇群体紧紧逼迫阿帕奇人。纳伊沙人始终只有几百人（1780年估计约四百人），与基奥瓦人结盟，靠平原印第安手语交谈；他们在18世纪初住在密苏里河上游一带，约1800年才把南部平原这一带作为主要活动范围。1821年，这里仍是印第安人的土地，只被独立之初的墨西哥远远宣称管辖。

en:
Kitkit'ish keeps Kitikiti'sh, the name the Wichita gave themselves. In 1444 their towns lined the Arkansas and its Walnut River tributary around the Great Bend, the farming country archaeologists call the Great Bend aspect: round, grass-thatched lodges stood by large granaries, women raised maize, beans, squash and sunflowers on the floodplains, and bison hunts crossed the prairie beyond. At the centre of several towns lay a council circle, a patio ringed by four semi-subterranean lodges; the imported objects dug up there suggest the chiefs kept them. The Wichita tattooed straight lines around their eyes, so the Spaniards called them Rayados, the 'striped ones'.

Coronado's army reached the Arkansas on 29 June 1541, looking for the golden province of Quivira, and found about twenty-five farming villages of up to two hundred houses, rich in maize but with no gold or silver. A Wichita captive the Spaniards called the Turk had talked them into the march with tales of gold; under torture he confessed he had meant to lead the army to its ruin on the plains, and Coronado had him garroted before marching away in August 1541. In 1601 Juan de Oñate came to Etzanoa on the Walnut River, the 'Great Settlement', and counted more than twelve hundred round houses; excavators have found chain mail and Spanish iron axe-heads at these town sites.

Disease and Apache and Osage raids thinned the towns through the 1600s. Quivira was abandoned early in the 1700s, French visitors in 1719 found the Wichita already shifting south, and by 1757 their main villages stood on the Red River. The Louisiana Purchase carried the region to the United States in 1803, and the Adams-Onís Treaty, in force in 1821, made the Arkansas the frontier with Mexico.
zh:
基特基蒂什保留了威奇塔人的自称 Kitikiti'sh。1444年，他们的村镇沿阿肯色河及其支流沃尔纳特河分布，环绕大弯一带，即考古学者所说的「大弯文化」农业圈：草顶圆屋旁是大谷仓，妇女在河滩种玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵，男人到远处草原猎野牛。几座大镇中心有「议事圆环」，一座庭院围着四座半地穴式屋舍；出土的外来器物多集中在这里，推测归首领收藏。威奇塔人在眼周纹出直线，西班牙人因此称他们为雷亚多人，即「纹线之人」。

1541年6月29日，科罗纳多的军队抵达阿肯色河，寻找遍地黄金的基维拉，见到的却是约二十五座务农村镇，每座至多两百座房屋，盛产玉米而没有金银。一个被西班牙人称作「土耳其人」的威奇塔俘虏先前用黄金的故事诱他们远征；他在酷刑下供认想把军队引到平原上等死，1541年8月科罗纳多撤离前将他绞杀。1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特来到沃尔纳特河畔的「大定居点」埃特萨诺阿，数出一千二百多座圆屋；考古学者在这些城镇遗址中挖出了锁子甲和西班牙铁斧头。

整个17世纪，疫病加上阿帕奇人和奥塞奇人的袭掠不断削弱这些村镇。基维拉在18世纪初被废弃，1719年的法国访客发现威奇塔人已在南移，到1757年他们的主要村镇已立在雷德河畔。1803年路易斯安那购地使这片地区名义上转归美国，1821年生效的《亚当斯-奥尼斯条约》把阿肯色河定为同墨西哥之间的边界。

en:
The Chitimacha, whose name means 'people who live on the Grand River', held the Atchafalaya Basin, the maze of swamps, bayous and lakes between the Mississippi and the Gulf. Their villages stood on ground so tangled that no enemy could reach them, so they built no palisades; each held about five hundred people in pole-and-mud lodges under palmetto thatch. Women grew many varieties of corn, beans and squash and stored the harvest in raised granaries; men took deer, turkey, alligator and fish, armed with bows, blowguns and darts tipped with cane or fish bone. Dugouts hollowed from single cypress logs, some carrying fifty men, linked the villages, and surplus grain went north to middlemen such as the Avoyel in exchange for the flint their delta lacked. Parents bound their sons' foreheads flat in infancy, and adults covered themselves in tattoos. Rank ran so deep that nobles and commoners spoke different dialects, and their tongue was a language isolate; descent passed through the mother, and women elders approved the hereditary chiefs. In 1444 the four Chitimacha bands held one of the continent's most abundant estuaries.

European diseases reached them long before Europeans did: the four bands numbered perhaps 20,000 around 1500 and only about 4,000 by 1650. Direct French contact came at the end of the century, and in 1707 the Louisiana French opened a long war that drove the Chitimacha from their Bayou Lafourche villages and sold many captives into slavery. In 1730 the French at New Orleans turned on their Chawasha neighbours and all but destroyed that band; its survivors joined the Chitimacha, who later also took in remnants of the Taensa and some Houma. After the British took Acadia, Acadian exiles began settling the basin in the 1760s, and Chitimacha families married among these Cajun newcomers and turned Catholic, a small people holding on along Bayou Teche.
zh:
奇蒂马查人的名字意为「住在大河上的人」，他们占据着阿查法拉亚盆地，即密西西比河与墨西哥湾之间由沼泽、河汊和湖泊织成的水网。村落周边地形盘错，外敌无法靠近，所以他们不设栅栏；每村约有五百人，住在糊泥木架、蒲葵叶顶的屋子里。妇女栽种多种玉米、菜豆和南瓜，把收成存进高架谷仓；男子猎鹿、捕野火鸡和短吻鳄、下河捕鱼，武器是弓、吹箭筒和装着藤镞或鱼刺的镖枪。整根柏木剜成的独木舟可载五十人，把各村彼此相连，多余的谷物向北经阿沃耶尔人这样的中转商，换回三角洲所缺的燧石。父母把男婴的额头捆扎成扁平形状，成年人则通体文身。等级森严，贵族与平民各说不同的方言，而他们的语言是一门孤立语言；世系按母系传递，世袭酋长须经女性长老认可。1444年时，奇蒂马查人的四个族群据有北美大陆最丰饶的河口之一。

欧洲人带来的疫病比欧洲人本人先到：1500年前后四族合计约有两万人，到1650年只剩约四千。与法国人的直接接触迟至17世纪末，1707年，路易斯安那的法国人发动旷日持久的战争，把奇蒂马查人逐出拉福什河汊的村落，许多俘虏被卖为奴隶。1730年，新奥尔良的法国人转而对查瓦沙邻族下手，几乎将其灭族，幸存者并入奇蒂马查；此后他们又接纳了坦萨人的残余和部分霍马人。英国夺取阿卡迪亚后，阿卡迪亚流亡者从1760年代起迁入盆地，奇蒂马查人家族与这些卡津新来者通婚、改宗天主教，作为一个小小的民族在泰什河汊一带坚持了下来。

en:
The Kadohadacho were the northernmost of the three Caddo confederacies, four communities holding the Great Bend of the Red River, where the water loops through the Piney Woods on the edge of the southern plains. Caddoan mound centres and farming villages had stood in these bottomlands from about 1000, and the Kadohadacho planted maize, beans and squash, gathered pecans in the river woods, and traded their bows and pottery to neighbouring towns. In 1444 their villages lay beyond European reach, tied to the other Caddo, Hasinai and Natchitoches towns by language, ceremony and exchange.

A party from the de Soto expedition met Kadohadacho travellers in 1541 without entering the Red River villages. In 1687 the Kadohadacho sheltered the survivors of La Salle's French venture on the Texas coast and afterwards traded with French Louisiana. Early in the eighteenth century Chickasaw raiders struck the Great Bend villages, killing or enslaving many people; the survivors drifted west and south to the Nasoni and Natchitoches, and by the end of the century the last Kadohadacho had left the bend for their kinsmen around Natchitoches.
zh:
卡多哈达乔是卡多三大联盟中位置最北的一支，四个社群据有红河大弯；河水在这里绕过松林地带，紧邻南部平原的边缘。约1000年起，这片低地上已有卡多语族群的土墩中心和农耕村落。卡多哈达乔人种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在河畔林中采集山核桃，所制的弓和陶器销往邻近诸城。1444年，他们的村落远在欧洲人势力之外，以语言、仪式和交换与卡多、哈西奈、纳基托什诸城相通。

1541年，德索托远征队的一支队伍遇到卡多哈达乔游群，但没有进入红河畔的村落。1687年，卡多哈达乔收留了拉萨尔在得克萨斯海岸的法国远征幸存者，此后与法属路易斯安那贸易。18世纪初，奇克索袭击者攻打大弯诸村，许多人被杀或被掳为奴；幸存者陆续西迁、南投，投奔纳索尼人和纳基托什人，到18世纪末，最后的卡多哈达乔人已离开河弯，前往纳基托什一带依亲族而居。

en:
Anilco was a Mississippian farming province on the lower Arkansas, about thirty-five miles above where the river joins the Mississippi. Its chief town is usually placed at the Menard–Hodges site, two platform mounds over bottomlands settled since the Baytown period of 300–700. The Arkansas carried the district's maize and its shell, chert and other goods between local plaza towns and the river provinces of Casqui and Pacaha upstream. In 1444 the people of Anilco planted the floodplain soils and fished the backwaters under a chief the Spanish chronicles met only once.

The Hernando de Soto expedition entered the lower Arkansas in 1541. In May 1542, while de Soto lay dying at a nearby town, his men sacked Anilco on a report that its chief meant to join Quigualtam downstream, and killed many of its people. When Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet passed in 1673, the French knew the riverside villages as Akansea, and the old mound locality had become the Quapaw village of Osotouy.

In the summer of 1686 Henri de Tonti, La Salle's Italian-born lieutenant, built a wooden trading post beside Osotouy: Poste de Arkansea, the first European settlement on the entire Mississippi. Tonti wore a metal hook in place of the hand a grenade had taken, and the river peoples believed the appliance gave him special powers. John Law's Mississippi Company landed German settlers and about a hundred slaves and indentured servants in 1717 to grow grain for Louisiana, then collapsed with the Mississippi Bubble and withdrew within seven years. Payamataha's Chickasaw raiders, 150 strong, struck the post in 1749, and floods and Chickasaw threats moved it three times along the river. Under Spanish rule, on 17 April 1783, James Colbert led British partisans and Chickasaw allies against it in the only battle of the American Revolution fought in what became Arkansas. The post passed to the United States in 1803 and was the first capital of Arkansas Territory from 1819 to 1821.
zh:
阿尼尔科是阿肯色河下游的密西西比文化农业酋邦，位于河口上游约35英里处。其主邑通常被定为梅纳德—霍奇斯遗址：两座台墩矗立在低地上，这一带自300年至700年的贝敦时期便已有人定居。阿肯色河把本地出产的玉米和贝壳、燧石等货物，运往卡斯基、帕卡哈等上游河上酋邦的广场城镇。1444年，阿尼尔科人在河漫滩上种玉米、在回水汊湾捕鱼，受一位酋长统辖；西班牙人的行记后来只记载过他这一次。

1541年，德索托远征队进入阿肯色河下游。1542年5月，德索托在附近城镇病重时，部下听信阿尼尔科酋长打算同下游的基瓜尔坦联手的传言，洗劫阿尼尔科并杀死许多居民。1673年雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃经过时，法国人把河畔诸村称作阿肯色，古墩一带已成了夸帕人的奥索图伊村。

1686年夏，拉萨尔的意大利裔副手亨利·德·通蒂在奥索图伊旁建起一座木制商站阿肯色站（Poste de Arkansea），这是整个密西西比河上第一个欧洲人定居点。通蒂被手榴弹夺去一只手，代之以铁钩，河畔各部相信这只铁器赋予他异乎寻常的力量。1717年，约翰·劳的密西西比公司运来德国移民和约百名奴隶与契约仆役，为路易斯安那种粮；公司随密西西比泡沫破产，七年内便告撤走。1749年，帕亚马塔哈率150名奇克索战士袭扰商站；洪水与奇克索人的威胁又使站点沿河三迁。西班牙统治时期的1783年4月17日，詹姆斯·科尔伯特带英国游击队和奇克索盟友来攻，这是后来的阿肯色境内唯一一场独立战争战役。商站于1803年归入美国，1819年至1821年成为阿肯色领地的第一个首府。

en:
Yscani is an early spelling of Iscani, one of the Caddoan-speaking Wichita bands; the name was later also used for the Waco. This is prairie-and-oak-edge country, where the southern grasslands meet the Cross Timbers around the Salt Fork of the Arkansas; groves of walnut and bur oak break the open bison range. In 1444 hunters moved through it on foot with dog travois, before horses reached the Southern Plains, while related Wichita towns to the north kept maize, bean and squash fields in the river bottoms. The Teyas whom Coronado met on the plains to the west in 1541 may have been ancestors of these people.

In 1601 Juan de Oñate crossed from the Canadian to the Salt Fork and found an Escanjaque camp of six hundred round lodges and more than five thousand people. The lodges were dressed with bison hides and ran as wide as twenty-seven metres; their owners planted nothing and lived by the hunt. They told Oñate that the great Rayado town of Etzanoa lay twenty kilometres away and led the Spaniards north, hoping for allies against their own enemies, then attacked the column on its way back. Whether these Escanjaques were the ancestors of the Iscani is uncertain, but Iscani warriors are named among the Wichita gathered at the Taovaya twin villages on the Red River in 1759: behind a moated palisade flying the French flag, with French muskets and Comanche horsemen, they beat off Diego Ortiz Parrilla's Spanish column and captured both its cannon. Smallpox weakened the Wichita towns in 1777–1778. The Louisiana Purchase of 1803 gave the United States no more than a paper claim here, and in 1821 no European town yet stood on this oak-fringed prairie.
zh:
阿斯卡尼（Yscani）是伊斯卡尼（Iscani）的早期拼法，指一支说卡多语族语言的威奇塔群体，这个名字后来也用于韦科人。这一带是草原与橡树林交错的边缘，南部草原在阿肯色河索尔特支流一带接上十字林；胡桃林和大果栎林散布在开阔的野牛草原上。1444年，在马匹传到南部平原以前，猎人们步行迁移，用狗拖拉沃伊橇，北方的威奇塔亲族村镇则在河滩种玉米、豆类和南瓜。科罗纳多1541年在西方草原遇到的特亚人，可能就是这些人的先祖。

1601年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特从加拿大河转至索尔特支流，发现一座有六百座圆屋、五千多人的埃斯坎哈克营地。圆屋覆以鞣制野牛皮，最宽达二十七米；主人不种庄稼，以狩猎为生。他们告诉奥尼亚特，雷亚多人大镇埃特萨诺阿在二十公里外，并引导西班牙人北行，想借其力量对付仇敌，却在队伍返程时发动袭击。这些埃斯坎哈克人是否为伊斯卡尼人的先祖尚无定论，但到1759年，伊斯卡尼战士已名列雷德河畔塔韦哈什双子村的守军之中：他们据守悬着法国旗、外有壕沟栅栏的寨子，靠着法式火枪和科曼奇骑兵击退了迭戈·奥尔蒂斯·帕里利亚的西班牙纵队，还缴获了对方的两门火炮。1777年至1778年的天花削弱了威奇塔诸镇。1803年的路易斯安那购地只让美国得到一纸名义主权，到1821年，这片橡树林环绕的草原上仍没有欧洲人的城镇。

en:
Casqui was a fortified Mississippian province on the St. Francis and Tyronza rivers of eastern Arkansas. Its chief town is identified with the Parkin site, a seventeen-acre palisaded village at the confluence behind a moat fed from the river. One large substructure mound and six smaller mounds ringed its plaza, and about twenty-one Parkin-phase villages spread through the surrounding maize fields, pecan groves and fishing waters. Archaeology puts continuous occupation of the site at more than five centuries. In 1444 its people lived behind the timber walls through a long feud with Pacaha.

Hernando de Soto's expedition reached Casqui in 1541. The chief walked out more than a mile with his people to welcome the Spaniards, several villagers accepted baptism, and the townspeople helped raise a tall wooden cross on the central mound. When the expedition moved on to Pacaha, Casqui's men followed and sacked their old enemy's town as its people drowned trying to reach a river island. De Soto then threatened to march with Pacaha in revenge, the plunder came back, and he sat the two chiefs down to a peace dinner. Seven-layer glass beads, two falconer's bells and musket balls later dug up at Parkin match equipment the expedition carried. The village was abandoned around 1650, and by the 1670s Quapaw-speakers held the river country, leaving Chief Casqui named only in the Spanish journals.
zh:
卡斯基是阿肯色东部圣弗朗西斯河与蒂龙扎河一带设栅设防的密西西比文化酋邦。其主邑被定为帕金遗址：两河汇流处一座17英亩的木栅村镇，镇外有一道引河水灌入的壕沟；一座大台墩和六座小土墩环绕广场，周边约21个帕金阶段村落散布在玉米田、山核桃林和渔场之间。考古表明该遗址已连续使用五百多年。1444年，由于同帕卡哈长期敌对，人们仍栖身于木墙之后。

1541年，德索托远征队抵达卡斯基。酋长带着族人走出一英里多迎接西班牙人，几名村民受洗，镇民又帮着在中央土墩上竖起一座高大木十字架。远征队转往帕卡哈时，卡斯基人尾随而至，趁帕卡哈人逃往河中岛屿、有人溺亡之际洗劫这座旧敌城镇。德索托威胁将同帕卡哈联手报复，战利品这才送回，他又安排两位酋长共进和解宴。帕金后来出土的七层玻璃珠、两只驯鹰铃和火枪弹，与远征队携带的器物相符。这座村镇约在1650年废弃，到1670年代，河谷已由使用夸帕语的人群占据，卡斯基酋长之名只保存在西班牙人的行记中。

en:
Kanza covers the lower Kansas River valley, where the river runs east through tallgrass prairie to the Missouri. The river later took its name from the Kanza, or Kaw, a Dhegiha Sioux people also called the 'People of the South Wind'; the state of Kansas is named for them in turn. In 1444, before the Kanza had moved up the Missouri, Caddoan-speaking Pawnee bands farmed corn, beans and squash on the bottoms, hunted buffalo on the surrounding plains, and wintered in villages of earth and grass lodges.

Coronado crossed central Kansas in 1541 looking for the golden province of Quivira and found only farming villages. The Kanza first appear on French maps late in the seventeenth century; Bourgmont found them in one large village near Doniphan in 1724. In 1744 the French built Fort de Cavagnial on the Missouri bluffs, the farthest-west post on the river, a stockaded fort with four bastions whose garrison drew high-grade furs from the Kanza. The French garrison pulled the post down and withdrew in 1764 after Louisiana passed to Spain. Lewis and Clark could still make out chimney stumps and the fort's outline in 1804, when they put the Kanza at about 1,500 people, 'reduced by war with their neighbors'; their main village then stood on the Kansas near the mouth of the Big Blue.
zh:
坎扎位于堪萨斯河下游河谷，河水向东穿过高草草原，注入密苏里河。河名得自坎扎人，又称卡乌人，是德吉哈苏语族群的一支，也被叫「南风之人」，后来的堪萨斯州同样以他们命名。1444年，坎扎人尚未沿密苏里河西迁，说卡多语的波尼群体在河滨低地种玉米、豆子和南瓜，到周围草原猎捕野牛，冬天住进土屋和草屋村落。

1541年，科罗纳多穿过堪萨斯中部，寻找遍地黄金的基维拉，只见到务农的村落。坎扎人最早见于17世纪末的法国地图；1724年布格蒙到访时，他们住在唐尼芬附近一座大村落里。1744年，法国人在密苏里河畔崖地建起卡瓦尼亚勒堡，这是当时密苏里河上最靠西的据点，一座四角设棱堡的木栅要塞，守军用坎扎人供给的上等毛皮做贸易。路易斯安那转归西班牙后，法国驻军在1764年拆堡撤走。1804年刘易斯与克拉克经过时，仍能辨认出烟囱残基和堡墙轮廓；他们估计坎扎人约有1500口，已「因与邻部交战而减少」，那时他们的主村在堪萨斯河近大布鲁河口处。

en:
The Osage River winds through the wooded northern Ozarks, and here the Pahatsi, the Upland band of the Osage, kept their permanent villages on open hilltops above the bottoms; the French would call them the Great Osage. They were one division of a people who call themselves the Wazhazhe, the Children of the Middle Waters. Women raised corn, beans and squash by the lodges, men hunted deer in the oak forest and twice a year struck out after buffalo on the western plains, on foot, for the horse was still unknown in 1444. Clans split into Sky People and Earth People, and the force of Wakonda ran through every animal and stream. No European neighbour existed then; the world turned on kinship, ceremony and the blood feud.

Marquette and Jolliet put the Osage on their map of the Mississippi in 1673, and horses reached the bands before 1700. Claude-Charles Du Tisné led the first official French expedition to the Great Osage villages in 1719; the Osage called these bearded newcomers the Heavy Eyebrows. Six years later Osage chiefs crossed the Atlantic, were presented to Louis XV at Versailles and hunted with him in the royal forest. Allied with France, they harried the Illiniwek and by the middle of the century had broken the Caddoan villages to the south, holding sway between the Missouri and the Red rivers. In 1795 the Chouteau brothers of St Louis, holding a Spanish monopoly on the trade, built Fort Carondelet inside the Great Osage village itself, 350 miles southwest of St Louis. Smallpox swept the bands early in the new century and killed perhaps 2,000 Osage; Lewis and Clark in 1804 found the Great Osage on the Osage River and put the whole nation at about 5,500. The treaty made at Fort Osage in 1808 ceded their Missouri lands, and the Treaty of St Louis in 1818 stripped away more of the old grounds, opening the long retreat towards Kansas.
zh:
奥塞奇河蜿蜒穿过林木葱郁的欧扎克北部山区，帕哈齐人是奥塞奇的山林一支，把永久村落建在河滩之上开阔的山顶，法国人后来称他们为大奥塞奇。他们所属的民族自称瓦扎热，意为「中游之水的儿女」。女人们在屋舍旁种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男人在橡树林中猎鹿，每年两度徒步西征大平原围猎野牛，因为1444年时马还没有传入。氏族分作「天人」与「地人」两个半偶族，瓦孔达的力量穿行于每一头走兽、每一道溪流之间。那时他们没有欧洲邻居，世界靠亲属、仪典和血仇维系。

1673年，马凯特与若利埃把奥塞奇人标上密西西比河地图；到1700年前后，马已传入各支。1719年，克洛德-夏尔·迪蒂内率第一支法国官方远征队到访大奥塞奇诸村，奥塞奇人把这些大胡子新来者叫作「浓眉人」。六年后，奥塞奇首领们渡过大西洋，在凡尔赛觐见路易十五，并随他在王室森林行猎。与法国结盟后，他们攻伐伊利诺伊人，到18世纪中叶又击破南方的卡多语村落，称雄于密苏里河与雷德河之间。1795年，圣路易斯的舒托兄弟凭西班牙当局授予的贸易垄断权，把卡龙德莱特堡直接修进大奥塞奇人的村子，距圣路易斯三百五十英里。新世纪初天花横扫各支，约两千名奥塞奇人病死；1804年，刘易斯与克拉克在奥塞奇河畔找到大奥塞奇人，估算整个民族约有五千五百人。1808年在奥塞奇堡签订的条约割走了他们在密苏里的土地，1818年的《圣路易斯条约》又削去大片故地，开启了迁往堪萨斯的漫长过程。

en:
The Tamaroa were an Algonquian-speaking band of the Illiniwek confederacy, and they held the busiest stretch of the upper Mississippi, the river on both banks around the mouths of the Illinois and the Missouri. About 3,000 people lived in mat-covered lodges, planting corn, beans and squash on the floodplain and going out on to the prairie after bison. Their chief village stood on the east bank beside the grass-grown mounds of a city abandoned centuries before. In 1444 boats of Illinois bands, Siouan peoples and parties from the lower Mississippi all met at the meeting of the three rivers, and no European had yet seen it.

Jolliet and Marquette passed the mouths in 1673, and La Salle counted some 600 lodges at Tamaroa in 1682. Father Pinet built the Mission of the Holy Family next to the village in 1696, and the Cahokia band came to settle beside them; disease and liquor cut the two groups to ninety dwellings within a few years. In 1703 the Tamaroa moved to the mouth of the Kaskaskia River, where a French town was growing into the wheat and fur mart of the Illinois Country. The Odawa chief Pontiac, who had besieged Detroit and fought the British for three years, was killed near Cahokia by a Peoria warrior in 1769, in the troubled years after France gave up the east bank. Jean-Baptiste de Coigne, son of a Tamaroa mother and a French trader, led a Kaskaskia, Tamaroa and Cahokia alliance. He helped George Rogers Clark take Kaskaskia in 1778 and later travelled to Virginia, where he smoked a peace pipe with Governor Thomas Jefferson and afterwards kept up a correspondence with him. In 1818 five Tamaroa leaders signed the Treaty of Edwardsville, ceding about half of Illinois to the United States, and the survivors were counted among the Kaskaskia.
zh:
塔马罗厄人是伊利尼韦克联盟中说阿尔冈昆语的一支，据有密西西比河上游最繁忙的一段河身，即伊利诺伊河与密苏里河河口附近的两岸。他们约有三千人，住在草席覆顶的棚屋里，在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，又远赴草原猎捕野牛。主村位于东岸，挨着一座数百年前便已废弃的古城留下的、长满野草的土丘。1444年，伊利尼各支、说苏语的族群和密西西比河下游来的队伍都在三河汇流之地往来，欧洲人尚未到此。

1673年，乔利埃特与马凯特驶过河口；1682年，拉萨尔在塔马罗厄数到约六百座棚屋。1696年，皮内神父在村旁建起圣家传教站，卡霍基亚一支也前来同住，没过几年疫病和烈酒就把两支人削减到只剩九十处住所。1703年，塔马罗厄人迁往卡斯卡基亚河口，一座法国城镇在那里成长为伊利诺伊地区小麦与皮货的集散地。渥太华首领庞蒂亚克曾围攻底特律、与英国人打了三年仗，1769年在卡霍基亚附近被一名佩奥利亚战士杀死，时值法国交出河东土地后的动荡年月。让-巴蒂斯特·德·夸涅的母亲是塔马罗厄人、父亲是法国商人，他后来统领卡斯卡基亚、塔马罗厄与卡霍基亚联盟，1778年协助乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克夺取卡斯卡基亚；他还曾远赴弗吉尼亚，与州长托马斯·杰斐逊共吸和平烟斗，此后两人保持通信。1818年，五名塔马罗厄首领在《爱德华兹维尔条约》上签字，把大约半个伊利诺伊割让给美国，幸存者则被计入卡斯卡基亚人之中。

en:
The Platte runs through this province in wide, shallow braids, and its low river terraces later held the cornfields and earth-lodge towns of the Tsawi. The Tsawi were the Chaui, 'People in the Middle', whom French traders called the Grand Pawnee; the other three Pawnee bands ranked their chiefs first in the nation. Its women planted corn, beans and squash in the bottom fields, and each summer priests carrying the sacred bundles led the whole village out on foot for the buffalo surround. In 1444 all this still lay ahead: the Chaui lived far to the south on the Arkansas, and no horse had yet reached the Platte.

Late in the seventeenth century mounted Apache raiders and gun-carrying Osage and other eastern tribes fell on the southern Pawnee villages. So many captives were carried down the Mississippi and sold in French Canada that Panis, the French form of Pawnee, became the common word there for an Indian slave; a Panis is on record in Montreal as early as 1670. After France gave up Louisiana in 1763, Spanish trade restrictions cut off the southern bands' supply of firearms, and the Osage pressed them out of the Arkansas. The Chaui led the retreat north: a Spanish report placed them in Nebraska by 1777, and their main town rose on the Platte where Central City later stood. To assert precedence over the Skidi on the Loup, the Chaui sent a hunting party north of the Platte within sight of their villages. The war that followed, about 1770-75, ended in the Skidis' defeat and their acceptance of Chaui chiefs as heads of the Pawnee. In 1818 the Grand Pawnee signed their first treaty with the United States at St Louis.
zh:
普拉特河在这片地方分成又宽又浅的多股水道，低阶地上的农田和土屋村落后来都属于察维人。察维人即乔伊人（Chaui），意为「中间人」，法国商人称他们「大波尼」，波尼其他三支都承认其酋长在全族中居首。妇女在低地田里种玉米、豆子和南瓜，每年夏天，祭司捧圣束带队，全村徒步出猎，合围野牛。但这都是后来的事：1444年时，乔伊人还住在遥远南方的阿肯色河畔，普拉特河也还没有见过马。

17世纪后期，骑马的阿帕奇人和持火枪的奥塞奇人等东部部落接连袭击南部波尼村落。大批俘虏被沿密西西比河运到法属加拿大卖掉，以至于「帕尼」（波尼的法语叫法）成了那里对印第安奴隶的通称；早在1670年，蒙特利尔就有帕尼奴隶的记录。1763年法国让出路易斯安那后，西班牙人的贸易限制切断了南部各支的火器来源，奥塞奇人又步步进逼，把他们挤出阿肯色河。乔伊人率队北撤，1777年的一份西班牙报告已记载他们到了内布拉斯加；他们的主村建在普拉特河畔，后来的森特勒尔城就起在村址上。为压服卢普河畔的斯基迪人、确立首领地位，乔伊人故意把猎队派到普拉特河北岸、对方村外可望见的地方。约1770至1775年战争爆发，斯基迪人战败，承认乔伊酋长为全波尼之首。1818年，「大波尼」在圣路易斯与美国签订了第一个条约。

en:
The province keeps the name the Missouri gave themselves: Niutachi, 'people of the river mouth'. They spoke a Chiwere Siouan tongue, close kin of the Otoe, and in the fifteenth century their permanent villages stood along the lower Missouri, chiefly beside the mouth of the Grand River and at the great river's own confluence with the Mississippi. Their own tradition says the Missouri and the Otoe had once been one people and parted over a love affair between the children of two chiefs. The Missouri farmed the bottoms, hunted bison on the prairie and held the entry to a river whose upper course no outsider had ever seen. In 1444 their villages still commanded both mouths.

Jacques Marquette met the Missouri in 1673, and the French trade that followed brought guns and goods, and smallpox with them. Étienne de Bourgmont, a French officer who had married a Missouri chief's daughter, built Fort Orleans at the Grand's mouth in 1723, the first European fort on the Missouri. From it he set out in 1724 to cross the plains and make peace with the Padouca, an Apache people far to the west. The post was abandoned only two years later. In 1730 a Sauk and Meskwaki attack on the Missouri villages killed hundreds and all but ended the people; most survivors joined the Otoe, others the Osage and Kansa. When the lower Missouri country passed to the United States in the Louisiana Purchase of 1803, the Missouri were a small band living among the Otoe. The French had already given their name to the river.
zh:
省名保留了密苏里人的自称纽塔奇（Niutachi），意为「河口之人」。他们说奇维雷语支的苏语，与奥托埃人是近亲；15世纪时，他们的常住村落分布在密苏里河下游，主要在格兰德河河口以及大河注入密西西比河的河口一带。按他们自己的传说，密苏里人和奥托埃人本是一族，因两位酋长的子女相恋而分裂。密苏里人在低地耕作，到草原猎捕野牛，把守着一条外人尚未见过其上游的大河入口。1444年，他们的村落仍据有这两处河口。

1673年，雅克·马凯特与密苏里人相遇，随之而来的法国贸易带来了火枪和货物，也带来了天花。法国军官艾蒂安·德·布尔蒙娶了一位密苏里首领的女儿，1723年在格兰德河口修建奥尔良堡，这是欧洲人在密苏里河上建的第一座堡垒；1724年，他又从这里出发横穿大平原，到远在西方的帕杜卡人（阿帕切人的一支）那里议和。仅仅两年后，这座据点就被废弃。1730年，索克人和梅斯夸基人袭击密苏里人的村落，杀死数百人，几乎使这个部族覆灭，幸存者大多投奔奥托埃人，其余加入奥塞奇人和坎扎人。1803年密苏里河下游地区随路易斯安那购地转归美国时，密苏里人已是寄居奥托埃人之中的一小支。法国人早已把他们的名字给了这条大河。

en:
Omaha is named for a Missouri River crossing above the mouth of the Platte, where wooded river bottomlands give way to the open bison plains. In 1444 the country belonged to the Central Plains village world of Caddoan speakers related to the Pawnee: families raised maize, beans and squash on the river terraces, lived in earth lodges, and left the valleys on seasonal communal hunts. The Omaha themselves, Dhegihan Siouans whose name means 'upstream', were still a woodland people far to the east, near the Ohio and Wabash; they reached the upper Missouri only at the end of the seventeenth century.

French reports first placed them on the Big Sioux in 1700, in a village of roughly four hundred dwellings and four thousand people, and in 1718 Guillaume Delisle mapped them on the upper Missouri as 'the Maha, a wandering nation'. About 1734 they built their first village west of the river on Bow Creek, and around 1770 they became the first people of the northern plains documented as mounted bison hunters. From his big village, Tonwantonga, Chief Blackbird ran the upper Missouri fur trade, drawing French and Spanish traders and receiving a Spanish post nearby, until the smallpox epidemic of about 1800 killed a third of the tribe and the chief with it. Blackbird was buried on a bluff above the river, and Lewis and Clark were led to the grave in 1804. Manuel Lisa opened his fur post of Fort Lisa nearby in 1812.
zh:
奥马哈得名于普拉特河口以北的密苏里河渡口，林木覆盖的河畔低地在这里让位于开阔的野牛平原。1444年时，这片地方属于中央平原上与波尼人相近的卡多语村民世界：人们在河畔阶地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，住在土屋里，并按季节离开河谷集体出猎。奥马哈人本是德吉哈语支的苏语林居族群，族名意为「上游之人」，当时仍远在东方的俄亥俄河与沃巴什河一带，直到17世纪末才迁到密苏里河上游。

1700年，法国报告首次把他们标在大苏河畔，那是一座约四百座住所、四千居民的村庄；1718年，纪尧姆·德利尔把他们绘入密苏里河上游，标注为「流浪的马哈人」。约1734年，他们在密苏里河以西的鲍溪建起第一座村庄；约1770年，他们成为北方平原有记载的第一批骑马野牛猎人。黑鸟酋长坐镇「大村」托恩万通加，把持密苏里河上游的毛皮贸易，引来法国和西班牙商人，西班牙人还在附近设立商站。约1800年的天花夺去约三分之一族人的性命，黑鸟也在其中；他葬在河畔高崖之上，1804年刘易斯和克拉克被人带到墓前。1812年，曼努埃尔·利萨在附近开设毛皮站利萨堡。

en:
The Wahpetunwan, the Leaf Village, were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands of the Seven Council Fires. Their country lay among the northern lakes at the edge of the woodland: in 1444 their camps gathered wild rice in the shallows, fished from canoes and hunted deer in the forest, then traveled out on seasonal buffalo hunts where the plains opened to the west.

Radisson and Groseilliers made the first recorded French contact with the Dakota in 1659-60. Daniel Greysolon, sieur du Lhut, traded through this country in 1679 and talked the Dakota and Ojibwe into a peace; he counted forty Dakota villages around Mille Lacs. The peace did not hold. Ojibwe war parties carrying French muskets pressed south through the eighteenth century, and Ojibwe oral tradition tells of the storming of Kathio, a great Dakota village on Mille Lacs, about 1750, after which the northern woods belonged to them. The Wahpetunwan camps pulled back to the upper Minnesota and the Red River prairies, where horses and the beaver trade had changed camp life by 1800.
zh:
沃珀顿（Wahpetunwan）意为「叶村」，是七营联盟东达科他四支之一。他们的地方在北方湖群、林地的边缘：1444年，营地的人在浅水里收野米，划独木舟捕鱼，进森林猎鹿，西边平原敞开来时再按季出去猎野牛。

1659至1660年，拉迪松与格罗塞耶留下了法国人与达科他人接触的最早记载。1679年，迪吕穿过这一带贸易，说和达科他人与奥吉布瓦人停战；他在米拉湖周边数到40座达科他村落。和平没有维持住。整个18世纪，拿着法国火枪的奥吉布瓦战队不断南压；奥吉布瓦口传讲，约1750年他们攻破米拉湖畔的达科他大村卡希欧，经此一战北方林地归了奥吉布瓦人。沃珀顿的营地退向明尼苏达河上游与雷德河草原，到1800年前后，马匹和河狸皮贸易已经改变了营地的日子。

en:
In 1444 the prairies and wooded valleys of the Iowa River were late Oneota country. Farmers worked light soils near water, raised corn, beans and squash, hunted bison and deer, and stored surpluses in underground pits; their villages made the globular, shell-tempered pots archaeologists use to trace the culture. Moving through this Chiwere world were the Báxoje, 'grey snow people' in their own Siouan tongue; the Dakota were said to call them the 'sleepy ones', ayuxbe, which the French wrote as Ioway. From the fifteenth to the eighteenth century the Báxoje lived around the red pipestone quarry of south-western Minnesota, neutral ground where many nations dug catlinite for ceremonial pipes, and their villages were already drifting south towards the eastern plains.

Europeans enter the written record on 17 June 1673, when Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met Illinois parties on the nearby Mississippi. La Salle claimed the whole Mississippi valley for France in 1682, and two years later Nicolas Perrot negotiated peace among the upper Mississippi nations. By then the Báxoje, perhaps 1,000 to 1,500 strong, were the dominant people of the Iowa country. Horses reached them through plains networks in the 1720s; Sioux pressure pushed their villages west in the 1760s, while French and later British traders brought metal goods and marriage ties. Smallpox had cut them to about 800 people by 1804, when Lewis and Clark visited their settlements on the Platte. Marie Dorion, a Báxoje woman, was the only woman to cross to the Pacific with the Astorian overland party of 1811, and she survived the journey.
zh:
1444年，艾奥瓦河流经的草原与林木河谷属于晚期奥内奥塔文化圈。农人在近水处耕作松软土地，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎野牛和鹿，余粮存入地下窖穴；各村落烧制贝壳羼和料的球形陶罐，考古学家凭这种陶器辨认这一文化。在这个奇维雷语世界里迁徙的是巴霍杰人：他们的苏语自称意为「灰雪之人」，据说达科他人称他们为「困倦的人」（ayuxbe），法国人把这个名字写成艾奥瓦。15至18世纪，巴霍杰人住在明尼苏达西南部的红管石采石场一带，那里是各族共有的中立地，人们开采卡特林石雕制仪式烟斗；此时他们的村落也已在陆续南移，趋近东部平原。

欧洲人第一次出现于文字记载，是1673年6月17日雅克·马凯特与路易·乔利埃特在附近的密西西比河畔会见伊利诺伊人。1682年，拉萨尔代表法国宣布整个密西西比河流域归法国所有；两年后，尼古拉·佩罗又在上密西西比诸族之间调停议和。此时巴霍杰人约有一千至一千五百，已是艾奥瓦一带最强的族群。1720年代，马匹经平原上的交换网络传来；1760年代苏人的压力迫使村落西迁，法国及后来的英国商人则带来金属器物与通婚关系。到1804年，天花已使巴霍杰人口减至约八百，刘易斯与克拉克在这一年访问了他们在普拉特河畔的村落。巴霍杰女子玛丽·多里翁是1811年阿斯托利亚陆路远征队中唯一的女性，她随队抵达太平洋沿岸并活了下来。

en:
The Ithanktunwanna, better known as the Yanktonai, 'Little Village at the End', were Western Dakota rather than Lakota. In 1444 they were pedestrian bison hunters who moved with the seasons between Mni Wakan, the sacred water later mistranslated as Devils Lake, and the headwaters of the Sheyenne and James rivers. Parties of Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara came up to the lake to trade their corn for meat and hides, and the Yanktonai carried pelts and dried meat between the Missouri villages and the northern forests.

Horses reached them in the eighteenth century and lengthened every hunting and raiding round; in 1794 the French trader Jean Trudeau named the James the Riviere aux Jacques. Their best-known chief of these years was Wanata, the Charger. As a youth of eighteen he followed his father Red Thunder to fight for the British in the War of 1812, served at the siege of Fort Meigs in 1813 and was wounded in a charge on the American works at Sandusky, the fight that gave him his name. The British gave him a captain's commission and took him to England. The Louisiana Purchase and the border convention of 1818 drew the United States frontier up to his country without a soldier entering it, and in 1821 Yanktonai camps still held the lake and the rivers.
zh:
扬克托奈人（Ithanktunwanna，意思是「尽头处的小村庄」）是西达科他群体，不是拉科他。1444年，他们还是徒步猎牛的人，随季节在米尼瓦坎（意为「灵水」，后来被误译成魔鬼湖）与夏延河、詹姆斯河上游之间迁徙。曼丹人、希达察人和阿里卡拉人的队伍来到湖畔，用粮食换肉和皮革，扬克托奈人则把毛皮和肉干贩运于密苏里河畔的村落与北方森林之间。

18世纪马匹传到这里，拉长了每一次狩猎和征战的路程；1794年法国商人让·特鲁多把詹姆斯河命名为雅克河。这一带最出名的首领是瓦纳塔，意为「冲锋者」。1812年战争中，十八岁的他随父亲雷德桑德为英国作战，1813年参加莫米堡围城，又在桑达斯基强攻美军工事时负伤，他的名字就来自这场战斗。英国人授他上尉军衔，还带他去了英国。路易斯安那易手和1818年的边界条约把美国边疆推到他的家乡旁，却没有一个士兵进入这里；到1821年，湖畔与河畔仍是扬克托奈人的营地。

en:
This stretch of South Dakota is open grassland cut by the Missouri, which swings between bluffs and timbered bottoms. In 1444 earth-lodge farming villages stood along the river while nomadic bands hunted buffalo on the plains around them. The province bears the name of the Yankton, the Ihanktunwan or 'Village at the End', who then lived more than two hundred miles to the east in the Minnesota lake country, at the end of Spirit Lake near Mille Lacs.

Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries musket-armed Ojibwe war parties pressed the Dakota south and west, and the Yankton in time moved out onto these plains and took to horses and tipis. The first Europeans known to have reached here were French: on 30 March 1743 the La Verendrye brothers, on an expedition that had pushed west from their Assiniboine posts, secretly buried a lead plate stamped with the French royal arms on a bluff above the Missouri, heaped a stone cairn over it, and told the local people the cairn marked only their passing. In late August 1804 Lewis and Clark met the Yankton in council at Calumet Bluff on the river, where the captains smoked the pipe with the chiefs and handed out American medals and gifts.
zh:
南达科他这一带是开阔草原，密苏里河在陡崖与林木夹峙的低地间蜿蜒流过。1444年，河畔分布着土屋农耕村落，四周草原上则有游猎群体追逐野牛。本省得名于扬克顿人，即伊汉克顿万（Ihanktunwan），意为「尽头的村落」；那时他们还住在两百多英里以东的明尼苏达湖区，米勒拉克斯湖附近灵湖的尽头。

整个17、18世纪，手持火枪的奥吉布瓦战队不断把达科他人赶向南方和西方，扬克顿人最终迁到这片草原，改用马匹和梯皮帐篷。已知最早来到这里的欧洲人是法国人：1743年3月30日，拉韦朗德里兄弟从阿西尼博因河畔的据点一路西来，在密苏里河畔的崖上暗埋一块铸有法国王室纹章的铅板，又在上面堆起石冢，只对当地人说石冢是为了纪念他们路过。1804年8月下旬，刘易斯与克拉克在河畔的卡柳梅特崖与扬克顿人议事，两位队长和首领们共吸烟斗，分发美国的奖章和礼物。

en:
The Sisithunwan, the Sisseton, were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands, and their name is read as 'Fishing Grounds Village'. Their country followed the upper Minnesota River: in 1444 camps netting fish and gathering wild rice could move west through the Traverse Gap between Big Stone Lake and Lake Traverse and pitch camp on the buffalo plains. The gap is a level break in the continental divide, Lake Traverse draining north toward Hudson Bay and Big Stone Lake south to the Mississippi, and in great floods water has crossed from one basin to the other.

Pierre-Charles Le Sueur ascended the Minnesota in 1700 to dig the blue-green clay of the Blue Earth River, which a French chemist had certified as copper ore; Fort L'Huillier guarded the dig until tests in the south showed the clay worthless and a Meskwaki attack in 1703 drove the garrison out. Through the eighteenth century Ojibwe war parties pushed the Sisseton west of the gap, where horses and beaver pelts tied their camps to plains commerce. The Anglo-American convention of 1818 fixed the imperial border at the 49th parallel; until then the gap itself had separated British ground in the north from French and later American territory in the south, and in 1821 Dakota camps still held the lakes.
zh:
锡塞顿（Sisithunwan）是东达科他四支之一，名字一般解作「渔场村」。他们的地方沿明尼苏达河上游展开：1444年，营地在河上捕鱼、采野米，再向西穿过比格斯通湖与特拉弗斯湖之间的特拉弗斯隘口，到野牛草原上扎营。这道隘口横切北美大陆分水岭，地势平坦：特拉弗斯湖水向北流入哈得孙湾，比格斯通湖水向南经密西西比河出海，洪水大时水会越过分水岭，在两个流域之间串流。

1700年，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔沿明尼苏达河上行，采掘蓝土河的蓝绿色黏土，一位法国化学家曾断定它是铜矿，利利耶堡就是为守矿而建；后来送到南方化验，证明黏土一文不值，1703年梅斯夸基人（狐族）进攻，守军弃堡。整个18世纪，奥吉布瓦战队把锡塞顿人逼向隘口以西，马匹和河狸皮把他们的营地系在草原贸易上。1818年英美公约把国界划在北纬49度；在那之前，特拉弗斯隘口本身就是北方英国领地与南方（更早是法国）领地的分界，到1821年，湖沼仍掌握在达科他营地手中。

en:
The Nueta, 'our people', was what the Mandan villagers on the Missouri's west bank called themselves. In 1444 they were the settled trading people of the upper Missouri and its Heart and Knife tributaries, living in fortified towns of round earth lodges forty feet across, each set around a central plaza. Women grew corn, beans and squash on the river flats and dried the surplus in cache pits, and the plazas were the marketplace of the central plains: Mandan corn left for bison meat and fat, while goods brought in had travelled from the Pacific coast, the Gulf of Mexico and the Tennessee River. Huff Village held 115 lodges and more than a thousand people.

Pierre Gaultier de La Vérendrye, the first European to reach them, was carried into a Heart River village in 1738; he counted nine palisaded towns, about a thousand lodges and perhaps 15,000 Mandan who set their own terms for trade. Horses bought from the Apache widened their hunting range. The smallpox that came out of New Spain reached the northern plains in 1781 through Comanche and Shoshone camps, cutting the Mandan from thirteen clans to seven; the survivors drew into two villages and were raided in their weakness by Lakota and Crow war parties. In the winter of 1796 the Welshman John Evans came chasing the old European tale of Welsh-speaking Indians, found nothing and left. Lewis and Clark built Fort Mandan beside the villages for the winter of 1804–05; there they took on Sacagawea for the journey west and carried Chief Sheheke east to meet President Jefferson. Sheheke had lived through the great epidemic but was killed in a quarrel with the Hidatsa in 1812. In 1821 the two reduced villages still drew trading parties up the upper Missouri.
zh:
努埃塔（Nueta，意为「我们自己人」）是密苏里河西岸曼丹村民的自称，外人更熟悉的名字是曼丹。1444年，他们是密苏里河上游及哈特河、奈夫河一带定居经商的人：一座座设防村镇里，直径约12米的圆形土屋围着中央广场。妇女在河滩种玉米、豆子和南瓜，余粮晒干后藏进窖坑；广场就是中部平原的市集，曼丹玉米换出去，进来的是野牛肉和油脂，还有从太平洋岸、墨西哥湾和田纳西河远道而来的货物。霍夫村有115座土屋、一千多居民。

1738年，第一个来到这里的欧洲人皮埃尔·戈尔捷·德·拉韦朗德里被抬进哈特河畔的村庄；他数到九座栅栏村镇、约一千座土屋，曼丹人约有一万五千之众，贸易的条件由他们自己定。马匹从阿帕奇人那里买来，扩大了狩猎的范围。1781年，出自新西班牙的天花经科曼切人和肖肖尼人的营地传到北部平原，曼丹氏族由十三个减到七个，幸存者并入两座村庄，虚弱时又遭拉科塔人和克劳人袭掠。1796年冬天，威尔士人约翰·埃文斯为寻访欧洲传说里「说威尔士语的印第安人」而来，一无所获地离去。1804至1805年，刘易斯与克拉克在村旁修建曼丹堡过冬，远征队在这里带上萨卡加维亚西行，又带首领谢赫克东去会见杰斐逊总统。谢赫克躲过了大瘟疫，却在1812年与希达察人的冲突中被杀。1821年，这两座凋敝的村庄仍吸引着商队走上密苏里河上游。

en:
Makoua covers the fir woods and lake maze behind Superior's north shore, from Lake Vermilion to Gichi-onigaming, the Great Carrying Place. In 1444 Eastern Dakota hunters used much of the interior, Cree travelers knew the northern waters, and Anishinaabe families from the lake shore followed the eastern portages. Wild-rice beds, fish runs, moose yards and beaver ponds supported seasonal camps rather than towns.

The eight-and-a-half-mile Grand Portage bypassed falls and rapids on the lower Pigeon River and joined the Superior watershed to Rainy Lake and the rivers flowing toward Hudson Bay. French traders reached western Superior in the 1650s, and Daniel Greysolon du Lhut used the lake country in 1679 to make peace between Saulteur and Dakota parties. In 1729 the Cree guide Auchagah drew Pierre de La Verendrye a map of the route to Lake Winnipeg. Voyageurs then brought interior furs to Fort Charlotte, carried the packs over the trail, and exchanged them at Superior for goods from Montreal.

Under British rule the North West Company made the bay one of its main inland depots, with a palisaded post, storehouses and a Grand Hall for the summer meeting of canoe brigades. The 1783 Treaty of Paris put the shore in the United States, and in 1802 the company voted to dismantle its eighteen buildings and raft the materials north to the new Fort William. By then Lake Superior Ojibwe bands, later grouped as the Bois Forte, had become the main Indigenous power in these woods.
zh:
马夸位于苏必利尔湖北岸后方，是从维尔米利翁湖延伸到「大搬运地」吉奇奥尼加明的冷杉林与湖网。1444年，东达科他猎人使用大片内陆，克里旅人熟悉北部水道，湖岸的阿尼什纳比家庭则行走于东部搬运道。野米床、鱼汛、驼鹿场和河狸塘供养的是季节性营地，而不是城镇。

长达十三点七公里的大波蒂奇绕开皮金河下游的瀑布和急流，把苏必利尔流域与雷尼湖及通向哈得孙湾的河网连接起来。法国商人在1650年代到达苏必利尔湖西端；1679年，达尼埃尔·格雷索隆·迪吕在湖区促成索尔托人与达科他人和解。1729年，克里向导奥查加为皮埃尔·德·拉韦朗德里绘出通往温尼伯湖的路线图。此后，内陆船夫把毛皮运到夏洛特堡，再背过大搬运道，在苏必利尔湖畔换取来自蒙特利尔的货物。

英国统治时期，西北公司把这座海湾建成主要内陆补给站之一，设有木栅据点、仓库和大商馆，供独木舟船队夏季会合。1783年《巴黎条约》把湖岸划入美国；1802年，公司决定拆除十八座建筑，把材料北运，修建新的威廉堡。到这时，后来归入布瓦福特人的苏必利尔奥吉布瓦诸部，已是这片林地中最主要的原住民力量。

en:
Baawitigon is the Anishinaabe name for the rapids where the St. Marys River carries Lake Superior into Lake Huron. The province takes in the south bank and the Upper Peninsula trails running west toward the Menominee River and Noquet country. Canoes had to unload around the broken water, while Ojibwe fishing camps took sturgeon in spring and whitefish in autumn. During the runs, a camp of perhaps 150 or 200 people could become a much larger Algonquian gathering. Inland families also gathered wild rice and blueberries, hunted moose and trapped beaver. In 1444 the rapids were a fishery, carrying place and meeting ground, not a European-style town.

Étienne Brûlé was the first European known to reach the rapids, around 1620. French missionaries followed, and in 1668 Claude Dablon and Jacques Marquette founded the south-bank Jesuit mission that became Sault Ste. Marie, the oldest permanent European settlement in Michigan. Three years later Saint-Lusson staged the Pageant of the Sault there: before representatives of fourteen Indigenous nations, a cross and France's arms were raised and the Lake Superior country was claimed for Louis XIV. Louis Le Gardeur de Repentigny established a small French seigneury and post in 1751, but British traders and soldiers soon controlled the crossing. Although the Treaty of Paris assigned the south bank to the United States in 1783, British forces stayed until 1797. By then Ojibwe, French, Métis and Scottish families were linked around the rapids by the fur trade; a joint commission after the War of 1812 fixed the border along the river.
zh:
巴维蒂冈是阿尼什纳比人对圣玛丽斯河急流的称呼，苏必利尔湖的湖水经此流入休伦湖。此省包括急流南岸，以及上半岛上向西通往梅诺米尼河与诺奎特人之地的林地步道。独木舟到急流边必须卸货转运，奥吉布瓦渔村则在春季捕鲟鱼、秋季捕白鱼。鱼汛期间，一两百人的营地可能扩大成阿尔冈昆诸族的大会。内陆居民还采集野米和蓝莓，猎驼鹿、捕河狸。1444年，这里是渔场、搬运道和会盟地，不是欧洲式城镇。

约1620年，艾蒂安·布吕莱成为已知最早到达急流的欧洲人。法国传教士随后而来；1668年，克洛德·达布隆和雅克·马凯特在南岸建立耶稣会传教站，后来发展为密歇根最早的欧洲人永久定居点苏圣玛丽。三年后，圣吕松在此举行「苏圣玛丽典礼」，在十四个原住民民族代表面前竖起十字架和法国纹章，宣布苏必利尔地区归属路易十四。1751年，路易·勒加德尔·德·勒庞蒂尼在此设立法国领地和小据点，但英国商人与军队很快控制渡口。1783年《巴黎条约》把南岸划给美国，英军却留到1797年才撤离。到那时，毛皮贸易已把奥吉布瓦、法裔、梅蒂和苏格兰家庭联结在急流周围；1812年战争后的联合委员会把边界确定在这条河上。

en:
The Osaakiiwaki are the Sauk, an Algonquian people; Osaakiiwaki is the Ojibwe name the French wrote down as Sac, 'people of the outlet'. Their principal town stood at the mouth of the Fox River, where it opens into Green Bay. The Sauk planted maize, beans and squash, hunted big game through the summer and split into winter trapping camps, while clans named for the bear, beaver, eagle and wolf ordered the village. Closest of their allies were the Meskwaki, the Fox, up the same river. In 1444 no European had yet entered Green Bay, and the Sauk traded and feuded with the Ho-Chunk, Menominee and Dakota around them.

French priests and traders reached the bay in the 1660s, and Claude-Jean Allouez founded the mission of Saint-Francois-Xavier at the Fox River rapids in 1671. For half a century the Sauk kept the peace with New France even while the Fox fought it, until in 1733 they sheltered Fox survivors of the second Fox War; French reprisals drove both peoples out of Green Bay. The Sauk moved to the Mississippi and around 1750 built Saukenuk at the mouth of the Rock River, a corn town above the rapids that Jonathan Carver in 1766 called the largest and best-built Indian town he had ever seen. The warrior Black Hawk grew up there. The Sauk and Fox also dug lead in the country east of the upper Mississippi and traded the ore with their furs, and they kept their British alliance into the War of 1812, when Black Hawk's band fought the Americans beside the redcoats.
zh:
奥萨基瓦基人即索克人，属阿尔冈昆族群；奥萨基瓦基（Osaakiiwaki）是奥吉布瓦人对他们的称呼，意为「水口之人」，法国人转写作萨克（Sac）。他们的主镇坐落在福克斯河注入格林贝的河口。索克人种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，夏季结队猎捕大兽，冬天分散成设陷阱的捕猎营地；熊、河狸、鹰、狼等氏族维系着村落的秩序，同河上游的梅斯克瓦基人（即福克斯人）是他们最亲近的盟友。1444年时，欧洲人尚未进入格林贝，索克人与周边的霍春克人、梅诺米尼人、达科他人贸易往来，也彼此争战。

法国神父和商人在1660年代抵达格林贝，1671年克洛德－让·阿卢埃在福克斯河急流处建起圣方济各·沙勿略传教站。此后半个世纪，尽管福克斯人屡与法国交战，索克人始终与新法兰西相安无事。1733年他们收留第二次福克斯战争后幸存的梅斯克瓦基人，法国人的报复把两族一同逐出格林贝。索克人迁到密西西比河一带，约1750年在罗克河口建起索克努克；这座险滩上方的玉米城，被1766年到访的乔纳森·卡弗称为他见过最大、营建最好的印第安城镇，武士黑鹰就在这里长大。索克人与福克斯人还在密西西比河上游以东开采铅矿，铅矿石和毛皮一同外销；他们一直维系着与英国的同盟，1812年战争中黑鹰的队伍随英军对美作战。

en:
The province named Meskwaki covers the lower Wisconsin corridor, where the river meets the Mississippi beneath wooded bluffs at the prairie later called Prairie du Chien. The Fox-Wisconsin route made these crossings worth holding: a short portage between the Fox and Wisconsin rivers carried canoes from Green Bay on Lake Michigan all the way to the Mississippi. In 1444 Chiwere-speaking Oneota villagers farm corn, beans and squash on the bluff-tops and bottoms, gather wild rice, fish the rivers and hunt deer and bison. Sauk, Ho-Chunk, Ioway and Illinois bands share or contest the surrounding prairies.

Jacques Marquette and Louis Joliet canoed through in June 1673, the first known French party to use the crossing, and found a Meskwaki band led by Alim; the French read his name as 'dog' and called the prairie Prairie du Chien. Nicolas Perrot built a trading post there in 1685 and in 1689 proclaimed the Fox, Wisconsin and Mississippi waters for France. The Meskwaki commanded the Fox River and the passage west, and their hold on it brought on the two Fox Wars. The first ended in 1716. The second opened in 1728 with a royal decree ordering the people's destruction, and in September 1730 about 900 Meskwaki attempting to break eastward were killed or seized by French and allied warriors; captives were sold as slaves in the French settlements, and the survivors joined the Sauk. Prairie du Chien passed to Britain in 1763 and stayed a British frontier post despite the 1783 peace treaty. The British captured Fort Shelby there in July 1814 and withdrew after 1815, and the Americans built Fort Crawford in 1816 to hold the crossing.
zh:
名为梅斯夸基的省份覆盖威斯康星河下游走廊，河水在林木崖壁下、于后来称普雷里德欣的草原旁汇入密西西比河。福克斯—威斯康星水道让这些渡口值得占据：福克斯河与威斯康星河之间只需短途陆运，独木舟便能从密歇根湖畔的格林贝一直划到密西西比河。1444年，说奇维雷语的奥内奥塔村民在崖顶和河畔种玉米、豆类和南瓜，采野米，在河中捕鱼，猎鹿和野牛；索克、霍春克、艾奥瓦和伊利尼游群在周围草原上共处或争地。

1673年6月，雅克·马凯特与路易·若利埃划独木舟经过，是已知最早利用这一渡口的法国队伍；他们遇到阿利姆率领的梅斯夸基游群，法方把他的名字理解为「狗」，这片草原便叫普雷里德欣。尼古拉·佩罗1685年在此修建贸易站，1689年又宣告福克斯河、威斯康星河与密西西比河水域归法国所有。梅斯夸基人扼守福克斯河和西行通道，对通道的控制引来两次福克斯战争。第一次1716年议和。第二次1728年开启时，法王甚至下了消灭这族人的诏令；1730年9月，约九百名试图向东突围的梅斯夸基人被法国及其原住民盟军杀死或俘获，俘虏被卖到法国人的拓殖地为奴，幸存者投奔索克人。普雷里德欣1763年转入英国之手，尽管1783年和约已把它划归美国，它仍是英国的边疆据点。1814年7月英军攻占当地的谢尔比堡，1815年后撤离；美军1816年修建克劳福德堡，守住渡口。

en:
The Ho-Chunk are a Chiwere-speaking Siouan people of the Green Bay country, their lands running from Lake Winnebago up the Fox and Wisconsin rivers and south to the Rock. They call themselves Hoocągra; neighbouring Algonquians called them Winnebago, 'people of the fetid water', and the French rendered this as les Puants. They are successors to the Oneota villagers who raised thousands of effigy mounds across the southern prairies, and in 1444 they lived in bark-and-mat villages under twelve clans, grew maize and wild rice, sugared the maples and took sturgeon from Lake Winnebago. They were the dominant power between Lake Michigan and the Mississippi, several thousand strong.

Jean Nicolet came ashore at Red Banks in 1634, the first European the Ho-Chunk had seen, and was feasted at a gathering he put at 5,000 warriors. Within a generation the people were nearly gone: accounts tell of hundreds of warriors drowned in a lake storm, of European fevers sweeping the villages and of Illinois raiders killing many more, so that by the late 1650s barely 500 remained. The Beaver Wars then carried Algonquian refugees into their country, and French traders returned to Green Bay at the end of the 1650s. The Fox Wars of 1712 to 1733 brought French campaigns to the bay villages. Once the fighting stopped, the Ho-Chunk recovered inland, from 700 people counted in 1736 to more than 2,900 by 1806, though smallpox swept through again in 1757 and 1758.
zh:
霍春克人是说奇维雷语支苏语的民族，世居格林贝一带，乡土从温内贝戈湖沿福克斯河、威斯康星河延伸，南抵罗克河。他们自称霍春克（Hoocągra）；邻近的阿尔冈昆人称之为温内巴戈，意为「浊水之民」，法国人译作「臭人」（les Puants）。他们是奥内奥塔文化村民的后裔，先民在南部草原上堆起成千上万座象形丘。1444年时，他们分十二个氏族，住在树皮和草席搭成的村落里，种玉米和野米，熬枫糖，在温内贝戈湖捕捞鲟鱼，是密歇根湖与密西西比河之间最强盛的势力，人口有数千之众。

1634年，让·尼科莱在红岸登岸，成为霍春克人见到的第一个欧洲人；霍春克人设宴款待，尼科莱称聚集的武士有五千之众。但仅仅一代人之后，这个民族便几近消亡：有说法称数百名武士在湖上风暴中溺亡，欧洲传来的热病席卷各村，伊利诺伊袭击者又杀死许多人，到1650年代末幸存者只剩五百左右。海狸战争随后把大批阿尔冈昆难民推入他们的乡土，法国商人也在1650年代末重返格林贝。1712至1733年的福克斯战争把法国人的兵锋带到湾畔村落。战事平息后，霍春克人内迁休养，人口从1736年查点的七百回升到1806年的两千九以上，只是天花又在1757和1758年两度流行。

en:
Peewareewa is Peoria country along the middle Illinois River, where the river widens into the long sheet of Peoria Lake. The Illinois knew this water as Pimiteoui, and the country around it was known for fat game; other tribes are said to have come here to hunt through the winter. The Peoria, who called themselves peewaareewa, were one of the Algonquian-speaking peoples of the Illinois Confederation. In 1444 their seasonal villages occupied wooded river land beside open prairie, with cornfields around the lodges, hunting parties crossed the grass after bison, and canoes on the lake linked them to the other Illini bands.
