Louis Jolliet and Jacques Marquette came up the river in 1673 on their way back from the Mississippi. In January 1680 La Salle and his lieutenant Henri de Tonti raised Fort Crèvecoeur on the east bank, the first French fort built in the West. Tonti had lost his right hand to a grenade in the Sicilian wars and wore an iron hook under a glove, which gave him his Indian name of Iron Hand. On 16 April 1680, as Iroquois war parties pushed into the Illinois valley, the garrison mutinied, pulled the fort down and deserted. Tonti returned in 1691 and built Fort St Louis du Pimiteoui near the lake, a fur post that was never abandoned and became the settlement later called Peoria. War with the Iroquois and epidemic disease cut the Illinois from about 10,500 at intensive European contact to fewer than 500 within a century. After France ceded its lands east of the Mississippi in 1763, many Peoria withdrew to the west bank. Americans built Fort Clark by the lake in September 1813, and the Treaty of Edwardsville in 1818 ceded the Peoria lands in Illinois to the United States.
zh:
佩瓦雷瓦是伊利诺伊河中游的皮奥里亚人土地，河道在这里展宽，形成一长条皮奥里亚湖。伊利尼人把这片水面称作皮米特威，湖滨野兽肥壮，据说外族人也会来此过冬打猎。皮奥里亚人自称佩瓦雷瓦，是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟成员之一。1444年，他们的季节性村落设在林木繁茂的河滩与开阔草原之间，屋舍周围种着玉米，猎队穿过草地猎捕野牛，湖上独木舟把他们与其他伊利尼群体连在一起。

1673年，路易·若利耶和雅克·马凯特从密西西比河返程时溯河而上。1680年1月，拉萨尔和他的副手亨利·德·通蒂在东岸建起克雷夫科尔堡，这是法国人在西部修筑的第一座要塞。通蒂在西西里战争中被手榴弹炸掉右手，手套里戴着铁钩，河谷里的印第安人因此叫他「铁手」。1680年4月16日，易洛魁战队进逼伊利诺伊河谷，守军哗变，拆毁堡垒后逃散。1691年通蒂回到湖边，另建圣路易·德·皮米特威堡，这座毛皮据点再未废弃，发展成后来的皮奥里亚定居点。对易洛魁的战争和疫病使伊利尼人从欧洲人密集接触初期约一万零五百人，在一个世纪内减到不足五百。1763年法国割让密西西比河以东土地后，许多皮奥里亚人撤往西岸。1813年9月美国人在湖边修建克拉克堡，1818年的《爱德华兹维尔条约》把伊利诺伊境内的皮奥里亚土地割让给美国。

en:
Kaskankaham covers the lower Kaskaskia River bottoms where that stream meets the Mississippi: oak woods and tallgrass prairie above the floodplain, deep alluvial soil along the water. It takes its name from the Kaskaskia, Kaaskaaskia in Miami-Illinois, one of the Algonquian-speaking bands of the Illinois Confederation. In 1444 their women planted corn, beans and squash in the bottomland fields, hunting parties pursued bison across the prairie, and dugout canoes carried dried meat and pelts along the Mississippi. No European had yet entered the river.

Jacques Marquette and Louis Jolliet met the Kaskaskia in 1673 at the Grand Village on the upper Illinois River, where a Jesuit mission took root two years later. Iroquois raids scattered that town, and about 1703 the Immaculate Conception mission was refounded on the Mississippi at the place that became Kaskaskia. The mixed French and Illinois settlement held some 2,200 people by 1707. Its farmers shipped wheat and flour south to New Orleans, whose Gulf coast could not grow grain, while lead mines across the river in Missouri were worked with enslaved African labour after 1719. Nearby Fort de Chartres, first raised in 1719 for John Law's Company of the West, became the seat of French government in the Illinois Country and was rebuilt in limestone in the 1750s. King Louis XV sent the parish a church bell in 1741.

After France ceded the east bank in 1763, French and Illinois families crossed by the hundred into Spanish-held Missouri. On 4 July 1778 George Rogers Clark's Virginians took Kaskaskia without a fight, and the parish rang the old French bell in celebration; Kaskaskia people have called it the liberty bell ever since. The town became capital of Illinois Territory in 1809 and the first capital of the state of Illinois in 1818, losing the seat to Vandalia the next year.
zh:
卡斯坎卡哈姆是卡斯卡斯基亚河下游汇入密西西比河处的低地，泛滥平原上方是橡树林和高草草原，水边是深厚的冲积土。省名来自卡斯卡斯基亚人，他们是说阿尔冈昆语的伊利尼联盟一支。1444年，妇女在河畔田里种玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎队在草原追猎野牛，独木舟沿密西西比河运送肉干和毛皮；此时欧洲人还没有到过这条大河。

1673年，雅克·马凯特和路易·若利埃在伊利诺伊河上游的大村遇到卡斯卡斯基亚人，两年后耶稣会传教站在那里落脚。易洛魁人的袭击冲散了大村，约1703年，圣母无原罪传教站在密西西比河畔重建，地点后来发展为卡斯卡斯基亚。到1707年，这座法国人与伊利尼人混居的聚落约有二千二百人。农场把小麦和面粉南运新奥尔良，那里的墨西哥湾沿岸长不了粮食；河对岸的密苏里铅矿在1719年后使用非洲奴隶劳动。附近的沙特尔堡初建于1719年，为约翰·劳的西方公司而修，后来成为法国伊利诺伊行政当局的驻地，18世纪50年代又用石灰岩重建。1741年，路易十五给教区送来一口教堂钟。

1763年法国割让密西西比河东岸后，许多法国和伊利尼家庭渡河西入西班牙属密苏里。1778年7月4日，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克率领的弗吉尼亚部队未经战斗拿下卡斯卡斯基亚，教区敲响那口法国旧钟庆祝，此后当地人便称它为「自由钟」。该镇1809年成为伊利诺伊领地首府，1818年成为伊利诺伊州第一个州府，第二年首府迁往万达利亚。

en:
Cahokia lies on the east bank of the Mississippi, in the stretch of bottomland lakes, woods and prairie later called the American Bottom. In 1444 the great earthworks a few miles north of the later village were already old: the Mississippian town there had peaked in the thirteenth century and lain abandoned for generations, and its builders had no known link to the Illini clans then living along the river. The Cahokia, Kahokiaki in Miami-Illinois, were one of those clans.

In late 1696 Father Pinet and the Quebec Seminary of Foreign Missions raised a log church among the Cahokia and Tamaroa, and the river village of Cahokia grew around their Holy Family mission. It became one of the largest French towns in the Illinois Country, a market for furs and Indian goods of roughly 3,000 people, while habitants planted wheat across the fifty miles of lowland toward Kaskaskia; a French colonial courthouse went up about 1740. After France ceded the east bank in 1763, many Catholic families crossed to Ste Genevieve and the new village of St Louis. On 20 April 1769 the Odawa war chief Pontiac, who had besieged Detroit six years before, was killed in or near Cahokia by a Peoria warrior. George Rogers Clark held a court there in 1778 and took the loyalty of 105 Cahokia household heads, and after 1787 the old French courthouse served the Northwest Territory's St. Clair County, enlarged in 1801 and 1809 until its jurisdiction reached the Canadian border.
zh:
卡霍基亚位于密西西比河东岸，河迹湖、林地与草原交错的这片泛滥平原后来被称为阿梅里肯洼地。1444年，后来村北几英里处的巨大土丘已是陈年遗迹：丘上的密西西比文化城镇在13世纪规模达到顶峰，荒废已有几代人，其建造者与当时沿河而居的伊利尼诸氏族没有已知的关联。卡霍基亚人便是这些氏族之一。

1696年末，皮内神父和魁北克外方传教会神学院在卡霍基亚人与塔马罗亚人中盖起一座木教堂，河村卡霍基亚就围绕圣家堂传教站发展起来。它后来成为伊利诺伊地区最大的法国城镇之一，是毛皮和印第安货物的市集，人口约三千；法国定居者在通往卡斯卡斯基亚的五十英里低地上种植小麦，约1740年又建起一座法国殖民地风格的法院。1763年法国割让东岸后，许多天主教家庭渡河西往圣热纳维耶夫和新建的圣路易斯。1769年4月20日，六年前围攻底特律的奥达瓦军事首领庞蒂亚克在卡霍基亚或附近被一名皮奥里亚战士杀死。1778年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克在此设庭，收下一百零五名卡霍基亚户主的效忠誓约；1787年后，那座法国老法院转供西北领地的圣克莱尔县使用，该县1801年和1809年两次扩界，辖区一直抵到加拿大边界。

en:
The Chickasaw Bluffs are four stretches of high bank on an otherwise low and swampy reach of the Mississippi; the Chickasaw called the great river the Sakti Lhafa' Okhina, the 'scored bluff waterway'. One of the bluffs carried a Mississippian mound town, whose empty houses gave the ground its later name of Chucalissa, 'abandoned houses' in the Chickasaw language. By the fifteenth century the town had long stood deserted, and the country west of the Tennessee River had become hunting ground for the Chickasaw, whose own towns lay to the south in the upper Yazoo and Tombigbee valleys. In 1444 no fort rose on the bluffs; Chickasaw hunting parties camped there and crossed the river by canoe.

Hernando de Soto's Spaniards wintered among the Chickasaw in 1540 and 1541, and after they looted native stores a Chickasaw night raid on their camp nearly destroyed the expedition. In May 1541 de Soto crossed the Mississippi near these bluffs, the first European to reach them. La Salle's canoes stopped here in 1682; while his men searched for a lost hunter they threw up a stockade named Fort Prudhomme, the first French structure in Tennessee, used for only ten days, and La Salle himself lay ill there for forty days on his way back upriver.

Armed through their trade with Carolina, the Chickasaw beat off Bienville's first attack at Ackia in 1736, and his second attempt ended on the fourth bluff. In 1739 he gathered more than 3,000 French, African and Indian troops there and built Fort Assumption, named for the feast day on which it was finished, with three bastions towards the land and seven terraces climbing the slope from the river. Over the winter disease, desertion and drink broke the army, which marched away in March 1740 and left the Chickasaw unbowed. Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby bought all Chickasaw land east of the Mississippi in the Treaty of Tuscaloosa in 1818, and the next year Jackson, John Overton and James Winchester laid out a town on the fourth bluff and named it Memphis, after the old Egyptian city on the Nile.
zh:
奇克索崖是密西西比河这一段低洼多沼的河岸上仅有的四段高崖，奇克索人把大河称作萨蒂尔哈法奥希纳（Sakti Lhafa' Okhina），意为「刻痕崖水道」。其中一道崖上曾有密西西比文化的土丘村镇，空屋使这片地方后来得名丘卡利萨，在奇克索语中意为「废弃的房屋」。到15世纪，镇子久已荒废，田纳西河以西成了奇克索人的猎场，他们自己的村镇在南边的亚祖河与汤比格比河上游。1444年的崖上没有要塞，只有奇克索猎手在此宿营、划独木舟渡河。

1540至1541年冬，埃尔南多·德·索托的西班牙人在奇克索人那里过冬；西班牙人劫掠了当地人的粮仓，奇克索人便夜袭西军营地，几乎把这支远征队打垮。1541年5月，德·索托在这几处崖附近渡过密西西比河，成为最早到达此地的欧洲人。1682年，拉萨尔的独木舟队在此停泊，队员为寻找一名走失的猎人赶筑栅栏堡普鲁多姆堡，这是法国人在田纳西修建的第一处建筑，只使用了十天；拉萨尔返航途中还在堡中养病四十天。

奇克索人靠与卡罗来纳的贸易得到火枪，1736年在阿基亚击退边维尔的第一次进攻，他的第二次出兵又止步于第四道崖。1739年，边维尔集结三千多名法军、黑人士兵和印第安盟军来到崖下，建成圣母升天堡，以竣工日的宗教节日命名，堡垒朝陆地一面有三座棱堡，河岸到崖顶开出七层台地。整个冬天，疾病、逃亡和酗酒拖垮了军队，1740年3月法军撤走，奇克索人仍未屈服。1818年，安德鲁·杰克逊与艾萨克·谢尔比在《塔斯卡卢萨条约》中买下密西西比河以东的全部奇克索土地；次年，杰克逊与约翰·奥弗顿、詹姆斯·温彻斯特在第四道崖上规划新城，仿照尼罗河畔的埃及古城取名孟菲斯。

en:
Chickasha is the black-soil hill country of the Chickasaw, stretching across the upper Yazoo and Pearl River valleys of northeast Mississippi. Proto-Chickasaw groups left the Tombigbee country in the fifteenth century after the collapse of the Moundville chiefdom and settled their maize towns on this higher ground. In 1444 no single ruler governed them: towns were organized through matrilineal clans and two moieties, women held most property, and hereditary leadership passed through the mother's line.

The first Europeans to test those towns met a sharp defense. Hernando de Soto's expedition wintered in Chickasaw country in 1540 and 1541; when he demanded two hundred bearers, Chickasaw warriors burned the Spanish camp at night and nearly destroyed his force before it reached the Mississippi River. Traders from Carolina began supplying guns after 1670, and Chickasaw raiders sold captives taken from the Choctaw until the French armed the Choctaw in reply. France then tried to remove the British-aligned towns by force in the First Chickasaw War: one army was repulsed at Ogoula Tchetoka on 25 March 1736, and Bienville's French and Choctaw column was bloodily beaten at the palisaded town of Ackia on 26 May. The Chickasaw kept their hills through France's withdrawal east of the Mississippi in 1763, set their first boundary with the United States in the 1786 Treaty of Hopewell, and still held their homeland in 1821.
zh:
奇克谢是奇克索人的黑土丘陵地，横跨密西西比东北部亚祖河与珍珠河上游。15世纪，蒙德维尔酋邦瓦解，原奇克索群体离开汤比格比地区，把玉米城镇建在这片较高的土地上。1444年，这里没有一位共主：各城镇按母系氏族和两个半族组织，大部分财产归女性所有，世袭领袖也沿母系传承。

最早试探这些城镇的欧洲人，很快遇到了强硬抵抗。1540年至1541年，埃尔南多·德·索托的远征队在奇克索之地过冬；他强征两百名挑夫，奇克索战士趁夜烧毁西班牙营地，几乎歼灭这支队伍，残部才逃往密西西比河。1670年后，卡罗来纳商人开始供应火枪，奇克索袭掠者把从乔克托人那里掳来的俘虏卖给殖民者，法国则以武装乔克托人回应。法国随后试图用武力清除这些亲英城镇，发动第一次奇克索战争：1736年3月25日，一路军队在奥古拉切托卡被击退；5月26日，比安维尔率领的法国与乔克托部队又在栅栏坚固的阿基亚村惨败。1763年法国退出密西西比河以东后，奇克索人仍保有自己的丘陵；1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》首次划定他们与美国的边界，到1821年，这片家园仍在他们手中。

en:
Chahta is the Choctaw name for the central Mississippi country between the upper Pearl River and the Chickasawhay. In 1444 its prairies and creek bottoms held farming towns of late Plaquemine background, with maize fields, summer houses, corn stores and round winter houses. The old platform mound at Nanih Waiya, built centuries earlier, later became the Choctaw sacred place of origin. Towns and matrilineal clans handled most of their own affairs, and rival groups sometimes settled disputes at stickball, a hard game called the 'little brother of war'. By the time French records name the Choctaw, these villages had formed three great divisions: Okla Falaya in the west, Okla Tannap in the east and Okla Hannali in the south.

Hernando de Soto crossed the northern edge of this country in 1540 and 1541 without recording the Choctaw name; Iberville made the first documented French contact in 1699. French muskets helped Choctaw towns answer Chickasaw slave raids, and Choctaw warriors joined the campaign that broke the Natchez rising in 1730 before marching with Bienville against Ackia in 1736. The contest between British and French traders then split the nation in a civil war from 1747 to 1750, from which the pro-French party emerged on top. The 1786 Treaty of Hopewell fixed the Choctaw boundary with the new United States. Years later Pushmataha rejected Tecumseh's call for a general alliance and led Choctaw warriors on the American side at New Orleans in 1815. The treaties of Fort Adams in 1801 and Doak's Stand in 1820 had already opened millions of acres to planters, so the Choctaw entered 1821 with their old country pressed on every side.
zh:
查塔是乔克托人对自己密西西比中部家园的称呼，范围在珍珠河上游与奇克索海河之间。1444年，草原和溪谷低地上分布着普拉克明文化后期的农耕城镇，有玉米田、夏季住房、储玉米的棚屋和圆形冬季住房。纳尼怀亚古土丘早在许多世纪前建成，后来成为乔克托人神圣的起源地。各城镇和母系氏族自行处理大部分事务，对立群体有时用激烈的棍球赛解决争端，这种比赛被称为「战争的小兄弟」。法国记载明确提到乔克托人时，这些村镇已形成三大部：西部的奥克拉法拉亚、东部的奥克拉坦纳普和南部的奥克拉汉纳利。

1540年至1541年，德·索托从这片土地北缘经过，却没有记下乔克托之名；1699年，伊贝维尔与他们首次有了可考的法国接触。法国火枪帮助乔克托城镇回击奇克索人的掳奴袭击，乔克托战士1730年参加了击垮纳奇兹起事的战事，1736年又随比安维尔攻打阿基亚。英国和法国商人的争夺后来使这个民族在1747年至1750年陷入内战，亲法一派最终占上风。1786年的《霍普韦尔条约》划定了乔克托人与新生美国之间的边界。多年后，普什马塔哈拒绝特库姆塞提出的广泛联盟，率乔克托战士在1815年的新奥尔良战役中站在美国一方。1801年的《亚当斯堡条约》和1820年的《多克斯坦德条约》已把数百万英亩土地开放给种植园主，因此乔克托人进入1821年时，故土已四面受压。

en:
Ishenoca covers the lower Mississippi above the delta, around the Bayagoula village by Bayou Goula in Iberville Parish, on the west bank of the river. The tribe's Choctaw name means 'bayou people'. Earlier societies left burial mounds on the parish ground. In 1444 these banks were a chain of related towns, Bayagoula, Mugulasha, Quinipissa and Houma, whose maize fields, hunt camps and canoe trade served the river traffic between the gulf and the interior; no European had yet built on the river.

La Salle passed in 1682 and claimed the whole valley for France, but the first French visitor was Iberville in 1699. Among the Mugulasha he found the chief wearing a blue serge coat and keeping a French letter that Henri de Tonti had left with the Quinipissa fourteen years before. The Bayagoula and Mugulasha shared one village, yet in the spring of 1700, after a winter in which the Houma raided them, the Bayagoula fell on their village-mates and destroyed them. The survivors' turn came in 1706: Taensa guests turned on their hosts, and a Tunica ambush near the village killed most of the rest. Smallpox killed more of them; about forty warriors were counted in 1715, and by 1739 the handful left lived between the Houma and Acolapissa and was being absorbed. The river banks changed rulers without another battle, from France to Spain in 1763, and to the United States with the Louisiana Purchase in 1803.
zh:
伊谢诺卡位于密西西比河三角洲以上，即伊贝维尔堂区境内贝尤古拉一带的巴尤古拉人河畔村落，地处大河西岸。部名在乔克托语中意为「河汊之人」。更早的社会在堂区土地上留下过墓葬丘。1444年，这一岸是巴尤古拉、穆古拉沙、基尼皮萨、霍马等相近部族连成的村镇带，玉米田、狩猎营地和独木舟贸易服务着海湾与内陆之间的河上往来；河岸边还没有欧洲人的建筑。

拉萨尔1682年经过此地，代表法国宣布占有整个河谷，但第一个到访的法国人是1699年的伊贝维尔。他在穆古拉沙人那里见到酋长身穿一件蓝色哔叽大衣，还保存着一封法语信，那是亨利·德·通蒂十四年前留给基尼皮萨人的。巴尤古拉人与穆古拉沙人本共居一村，可是在遭霍马人袭击的那个冬天过去后，1700年春，巴尤古拉人突然对同村的穆古拉沙人下手，将其消灭。幸存者的劫难在1706年到来：客居的坦萨人反戈相向，图尼卡人又在村外设伏，余下的人大多被杀。天花接着夺去更多人命：1715年清点时他们只剩约四十名战士，到1739年，寥寥残存者住在霍马人与阿科拉皮萨人之间，正被逐渐吸收。这片河岸此后再未经一战便两度易主：1763年法国让给西班牙，1803年又随路易斯安那购地归入美国。

en:
Tohome covers Mobile Bay and the lower Mobile River, where the river meets a sheltered arm of the Gulf of Mexico. In 1444 the Mobile and Tohomé towns held the bay shores and river bluffs, farming maize, fishing the shallows and trading by canoe along the coast; their speech supplied much of Mobilian Jargon, the Choctaw-based trade tongue later used from the Mississippi to peninsular Florida. No European ship had yet anchored in the bay, though a Spanish chart made during Álvarez de Pineda's voyage of 1519 already traced this shoreline.

France came with the Le Moyne brothers. Iberville entered the bay in January 1699, and in 1702 he and Bienville founded Fort Louis de la Louisiane on a bluff twenty-seven miles up the river, with the town of La Mobile below it; for nine years this was the capital of French Louisiana. In 1704 the ship Pélican brought twenty-three young women to the colony, but passengers had picked up yellow fever at a Havana stopover, and after the landing the disease carried off colonists and neighbouring Natives alike; a supply ship from Saint-Domingue brought Mobile its first African slaves the same period. Around 1709 the Mobile and Tohomé were allowed to settle beside the fort. Floods and sickness drove Bienville to move the town down to the bay in 1711, and the old site was burned so no enemy could use it; the brick fort begun there in 1723 took the name Fort Condé.

The post then changed masters with every war around the gulf. Britain took it from France in 1763 and renamed the fort Fort Charlotte for the queen; 112 French residents kept their homes, and the new rule's religious tolerance brought Sephardic Jewish merchants from Savannah and Charleston. Bernardo de Gálvez, the Spanish governor at New Orleans, besieged Fort Charlotte and captured it in 1780, and Spain held Mobile until 1813, when General James Wilkinson occupied it for the United States during the War of 1812.
zh:
托霍梅覆盖莫比尔湾与莫比尔河下游，莫比尔河在此注入墨西哥湾一处隐蔽的湾臂。1444年，莫比尔与托霍梅人的村镇据有湾岸和河畔崖地，种玉米、在浅滩捕鱼、乘独木舟沿海岸贸易；他们的语言后来构成莫比尔行话的主要成分，这种以乔克托语为基础的贸易通语，通行范围从密西西比河一直到佛罗里达半岛。此时湾中还没有欧洲船抛锚，不过西班牙人皮内达1519年远航时绘制的海图，就已经描下这段岸线。

法国人随勒穆瓦纳兄弟而来。伊贝维尔1699年1月驶入湾中，1702年与弟弟边维尔在河上游二十七英里的崖地上建起路易斯安那圣路易堡，堡下的城镇叫拉莫比尔，此后九年都是法属路易斯安那的首府。1704年，「鹈鹕号」给殖民地送来二十三名年轻女子，但乘客在哈瓦那停靠时染上黄热病，登岸后疫病夺走许多殖民者和邻近原住民的性命；同一时期，一艘从圣多明各来的补给船给莫比尔带来第一批非洲奴隶。约1709年，莫比尔人与托霍梅人获准在要塞旁定居。洪水和疾病最终促使边维尔1711年把城镇下移到湾畔，旧址被付之一炬，以免为敌所用；1723年在新址动工的砖砌要塞得名康德堡。

此后每一场海湾战争都让这座据点换一次主人。1763年英国从法国手中取走此地，以王后之名把要塞改称夏洛特堡；112名法国居民留下未走，新政权的宗教宽容还引来萨凡纳和查尔斯顿的塞法迪犹太商人。新奥尔良的西班牙总督贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯1780年围城拿下夏洛特堡，西班牙据有莫比尔直到1813年，詹姆斯·威尔金森将军在1812年战争中为美国占领了它。

en:
Santa Rosa Island guards the mouth of Pensacola Bay, whose deep water made it one of the finest anchorages on the northern shore of the Gulf of Mexico. In 1444 the bay and the creeks behind it belonged to a Muskogean people later called the Pensacola; dugout canoes linked their village landings to fishing grounds and to Bottle Creek, the mound ceremonial centre fifty-odd miles to the west, where eighteen earthworks stood around a plaza. Creek traders came overland from the north, but no European sail had yet entered the bay.

The first Spanish attempt showed how dangerous the coast was. In August 1559, six years before St Augustine was founded, Tristán de Luna brought eleven ships and about 1,500 colonists from Veracruz to found Santa María de Ochuse; a hurricane five weeks later sank six ships with most of the stores, and the survivors gave up within two years. Spain returned only in 1698, building the presidio of Santa María de Galve to check French expansion down the Mississippi. A French force from Mobile under Bienville took Pensacola in 1719 and handed it back under the peace treaty, and repeated hurricanes later moved the garrison from Santa Rosa Island to a fort on the mainland. Britain acquired Florida in 1763 and made Pensacola the capital of West Florida. In March 1781 Bernardo de Gálvez closed on the town with nearly 8,000 men brought from Havana and Mobile. When his fleet commander refused to risk the channel, Gálvez took his own small ship, the Galveztown, through it under British fire, and Charles III later granted him the words Yo Solo, 'I alone', on his coat of arms. A two-month siege followed; on 8 May a howitzer shell blew up the magazine in Fort Crescent, Fort George surrendered on 10 May, and over 1,100 British and Loyalist men went into captivity, the peace settlement confirming West Florida to Spain. Andrew Jackson took Pensacola in 1814 and again four years later, and in 1821 he entered the town as the first American governor of Florida.
zh:
圣罗莎岛横在彭萨科拉湾口，湾内水深，是墨西哥湾北岸最好的锚地之一。1444年，海湾和后方的河汊属于一支说穆斯科格语的人群，后来被称为彭萨科拉人；他们的独木舟把村落登陆点同渔场、同西边五十多英里外的博特尔克里克土墩礼仪中心连在一起，那里的广场四周立着十八座土墩。北方的克里克商人从陆路来此贸易，但此时还没有欧洲船驶进过这座海湾。

西班牙人的第一次尝试，正好显出这片海岸的凶险。1559年8月，比圣奥古斯丁建立还早六年，特里斯坦·德·卢纳率十一艘船、约一千五百名殖民者从韦拉克鲁斯前来，建立圣玛丽亚·德·奥丘塞；五周后的一场飓风击沉六艘船，大部分物资随之沉没，幸存者不到两年便撤走。西班牙人迟至1698年才重返，修建圣玛丽亚·德·加尔韦要塞，以阻遏法国人沿密西西比河南下。1719年，边维尔率莫比尔的法军夺取彭萨科拉，又依和约归还；此后飓风不断，驻军从圣罗莎岛迁到大陆上的要塞。1763年英国取得佛罗里达，把彭萨科拉定为西佛罗里达首府。1781年3月，贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯率近八千人从哈瓦那和莫比尔合围彭萨科拉。舰队司令不敢冒险进入航道，加尔维斯便亲自驾驶自己的小型战船「加尔维斯城号」冒着英军炮火穿过，查理三世后来准许他把「唯我」（Yo Solo）二字刻上纹章。围城持续两个月，5月8日一发榴弹击中新月堡（Fort Crescent）的火药库，乔治堡于5月10日投降，一千一百多名英军和亲英派士兵被俘，和约确认西佛罗里达归西班牙。安德鲁·杰克逊1814年攻占彭萨科拉，四年后再次进占；1821年他以佛罗里达首任美国总督的身份进入这座城镇。

en:
The middle Alabama winds through cane bottoms and fertile red bluffs between the fall-line hills and the coastal plain. The towns of Tawasa and Atagi, whose name meant pure water, stood in this stretch. Their people grew maize and beans after the older mound-building chiefdoms of the valley had broken apart, and old earthworks still marked the river terraces. Trade and marriage tied them to the Alibamu upstream and the Choctaw to the west, but no single chief ruled all the towns. In 1444 the Tawasa settlements managed their own affairs, and no European had yet entered the Alabama valley.

Hernando de Soto's army reached central Alabama in 1540. At Mabila, a fortified town whose exact site is still debated, Chief Tuskaloosa concealed more than two thousand five hundred warriors in the houses. The Spaniards were at first driven out with their baggage trapped inside, then they burned the town and overran the defenders after a day of fighting. In 1560 starving colonists from Tristán de Luna's failed Pensacola settlement occupied the abandoned river town of Nanipacana before their expedition collapsed. Around 1707 slave raiders seized Tawasa captives. One of them, Lamhatty, reached Virginia, where a list of sixty words taken from him became the only surviving record of the Tawasa language, possibly related to Timucua. France raised Fort Toulouse in 1717 at the forks of the Coosa and Tallapoosa, and about sixty Tawasa joined the Alibamu beside the fort before entering the Creek Confederacy. In 1814, after the Red Stick defeat at Horseshoe Bend, the Treaty of Fort Jackson on the same site imposed a large Creek cession and scattered the remaining Tawasa among Creek, Seminole and other neighbouring communities.
zh:
中亚拉巴马河穿过河蔗密布的滩地和肥沃的红色崖岸，两侧是瀑布线丘陵与沿海平原。塔瓦萨、阿塔吉等城镇位于这一河段，阿塔吉一名意为清水。较早的筑丘酋邦瓦解后，这里的居民种植玉米和豆类，河岸阶地上仍留有旧土墩。他们通过贸易和婚姻与上游的阿拉巴马人、西边的乔克托人往来，却没有统辖各城镇的共同首领。1444年，塔瓦萨人的聚落各自处理自己的事务，欧洲人还没有进入亚拉巴马河谷。

1540年，埃尔南多·德·索托的军队到达中亚拉巴马。设防城镇马比拉的确切城址长期没有定论，首领塔斯卡卢萨把2500多名武士藏在屋舍中。西班牙人一开始被赶出城，辎重也困在里面；随后他们放火烧城，经一天战斗压垮守军。1560年，特里斯坦·德·卢纳在彭萨科拉的殖民受挫，饥饿的殖民者占据废弃的河畔城镇纳尼帕卡纳，但远征最终仍告溃散。约1707年，奴隶袭掠者掳走一批塔瓦萨人。俘虏之一拉姆哈蒂辗转到达弗吉尼亚，人们据他的口述记下60个词，这成了塔瓦萨语仅存的记录；这种语言可能与蒂穆夸语有关。1717年，法国在库萨河与塔拉普萨河汇流处修建图卢兹堡，约60名塔瓦萨人到堡旁投奔阿拉巴马人，后来加入克里克联盟。1814年，「红棍」在马蹄湾战败后，同一地点签订的杰克逊堡条约要求克里克人大片割地，余下的塔瓦萨人也分散到克里克人、塞米诺尔人和邻近族群之中。

en:
Coweta lies on the lower Chattahoochee, among river-bottom fields of maize, beans and squash just below the river's fall line. In 1444 the valley held the farming towns of a South Appalachian Mississippian chiefdom, their plazas and platform mounds worked by Hitchiti-speaking villagers; Coweta and its neighbour Tuskegee were later arrivals. Kinship and an old trade in shell and copper tied the towns together, and no European had yet reached the Chattahoochee.

The de Soto expedition passed east of the valley in 1540, and the epidemics behind it broke the old chiefdom, whose towns shrank and regrouped. In 1685 the towns welcomed the English trader Henry Woodward; after Spanish reprisals most of them moved east in 1690 to the Ochese Creek post on the Ocmulgee, where English muskets and the deerskin trade made them the Ochese Creeks. They raided the Florida missions in 1704, turned on Carolina in the Yamasee War of 1715, and afterwards fell back to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Creeks, with Coweta their principal trading town.

In May 1718 Brims, mico of Coweta, called British, French and Spanish agents to his town and declared Creek neutrality, setting the three empires to bid against each other until his death in 1733. Coweta kept that balance through Georgia's early years: Mary Musgrove, daughter of an English trader and a Creek mother, was James Oglethorpe's interpreter from the colony's founding in 1733, and by the 1750s Savannah shipped as many as 50,000 deerskins a year. The American Revolution split the towns, and in 1790 Alexander McGillivray, son of a Scottish trader and a Creek mother, schooled in the Carolina low country, signed the Treaty of New York with Washington. In the Red Stick War of 1813-14 William McIntosh, mico of Coweta, led the Lower Creeks with Andrew Jackson; after Horseshoe Bend on 27 March 1814, the Treaty of Fort Jackson took 22 million acres, and in 1821 McIntosh signed the first Treaty of Indian Springs, opening the first Lower Creek lands to the cotton frontier.
zh:
考维塔地处查特胡奇河下游，河滨滩地里玉米、豆类和南瓜相连，北面不远便是河流的瀑布线。1444年，河谷中散布着南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化的农耕城邦，广场与高台墩之间住着操希奇蒂语的农人；考维塔和邻近的塔斯克吉都是后来才迁入河谷的。各镇以亲缘相联，又靠流通贝壳与铜器的古商道彼此往来，此时欧洲人尚未抵达查特胡奇河。

1540年德索托远征从河谷东边经过，随之而来的疫病瓦解了旧邦国，诸镇人口锐减、重新组合。1685年，各镇接纳了英国商人亨利·伍德沃德；遭西班牙报复后，多数城镇于1690年东迁到奥克马尔吉河畔的奥切塞溪商栈，靠英军火枪和鹿皮贸易被称为奥切塞克里克人。1704年他们随英军劫掠佛罗里达布道所，1715年在雅马西战争中反戈攻打卡罗来纳，战后退回查特胡奇河，成为下克里克人，考维塔则是诸城的首要商镇。

1718年5月，考维塔酋长布里姆把英、法、西三国代表召到镇上，宣布克里克中立，让三大帝国竞相拉拢，直到1733年去世。佐治亚草创的年代里，考维塔仍维持着这一平衡：英国商人与克里克女子之女玛丽·马斯格罗夫自1733年殖民地建立起便为詹姆斯·奥格尔索普担任翻译，到1750年代，萨凡纳每年输出的鹿皮多达五万张。美国独立战争使诸镇分裂，1790年，苏格兰商人与克里克女子之子、在卡罗来纳低地受教育的麦吉利夫雷与华盛顿签订《纽约条约》。1813至1814年红棍战争中，考维塔酋长麦金托什率领下克里克人随安德鲁·杰克逊作战；1814年3月27日蹄铁湾之战后，《杰克逊堡条约》割走2200万英亩土地，1821年麦金托什又签署第一个《印第安斯普林斯条约》，首批下克里克土地向棉花种植边疆开放。

en:
The Ais lived on the barrier islands and mainland shore of the long lagoon the Spanish called the River of Ais, now the Indian River. Their towns ran from Cape Canaveral south to the St. Lucie Inlet, with the chief town at Ais or Jece, whose paramount spoke for settlements along much of that sheltered coast. The brackish water supplied fish, turtles and shellfish, and sabal palms and cocoplums gave fruit, so the people kept no fields and still had a dependable food supply. In 1444 European ships had not entered this Florida coast, and the lagoon chiefs managed their own alliances and local wars from their canoe landings and fishing weirs.

Spanish ships learned the shore after Juan Ponce de León sailed past in 1513, but the lagoon was not easy to hold. Pedro Menéndez de Avilés visited Ais in 1565 after founding St. Augustine and accepted the chief's oath to Philip II; the small post he left there collapsed within months amid hunger and fighting, and peace came five years later. At the end of the century Governor Gonzalo Méndez de Canço reported that the Ais chief could put more warriors in the field than any other Florida chief. The lagoon also drew shipwrecked Europeans and, later, fugitive slaves from Spanish settlements. Jonathan Dickinson, wrecked on the coast in 1696, left the fullest European account of Ais dress, food and customs after his party was passed along the shore towns on the way to St. Augustine; Franciscans sent three years later baptized no one. After 1700, slavers from Carolina and their Indian allies burned and captured the coastal towns. About 88 people recorded as 'coast Indians' were moved to northern missions in 1726, and only 52 remained in 1728. In 1763 the people still recorded as Ais left for Cuba with the Spaniards and Calusa; another fragment had moved toward Alabama and later joined the Seminole.
zh:
艾斯人住在西班牙人称作「艾斯河」的长潟湖沿岸，障壁岛和大陆岸边都有村镇，这片水域即今印第安河。其地北起卡纳维拉尔角，南至圣露西入海口；酋镇艾斯又称杰塞，镇中大酋能号令这条遮蔽海岸上的多处聚落。咸淡水中出产鱼、龟和贝类，箬棕与可可李结实可食，所以他们不开田地，也有稳定的食物来源。1444年，欧洲船只尚未进入这段佛罗里达海岸，潟湖诸酋在独木舟泊地和鱼梁之间安排自己的联盟与战事。

1513年胡安·庞塞·德莱昂驶过海岸后，西班牙人才知道这条潟湖，但要守住它并不容易。1565年，佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯建立圣奥古斯丁后造访艾斯镇，接受首领向腓力二世宣誓；他留下的小据点数月后便因缺粮和冲突瓦解，双方五年后议和。16世纪末，贡萨洛·门德斯·德·坎索总督报告，艾斯首领能投入战场的武士多于佛罗里达其他任何首领。潟湖一带还吸引过遇险的欧洲人，后来也有西班牙殖民地的逃亡黑奴来投。1696年，乔纳森·迪金森一行在海岸遇险，被沿海岸村镇辗转带往圣奥古斯丁；他的日记成了欧洲人记载艾斯服饰、食物和习俗最详尽的资料。三年后派来的方济各会修士没有施洗一人。1700年后，卡罗来纳奴隶贩子及其印第安盟友焚毁并掳掠沿岸村镇。1726年，约88名被记作「沿海印第安人」的人被迁往北方传教站，1728年只剩52人。1763年，仍被记作艾斯人者随西班牙人和卡卢萨人前往古巴；另有一支早先迁往阿拉巴马，后来加入塞米诺尔人。

en:
Timucua is the country between the Suwannee and Santa Fe rivers held in 1444 by the Northern Utina, the Timucua speakers whose dialect the Spanish later called Timucua proper. Scattered farming villages answered to local chiefs, and the principal town was perhaps at Fig Springs; across the Suwannee lived the closely related Yustaga. Hernando de Soto marched through in 1539 and thought the Northern Utina more populous than any people he had yet met. He seized Chief Aguacaleycuen as a hostage, and after an ambush and a battle near Napituca he executed the chief and his other hostages before moving on.

Franciscans entered the chiefdom in 1597, and San Martín de Timucua, likely at Fig Springs, became the leading station of the Timucua mission province. The Northern Utina led the Timucua Rebellion of 1656; Spanish soldiers burned their towns and moved the survivors onto the royal road between St. Augustine and Apalachee. Creek and Yamasee raiders in the pay of Carolina then carried people off year after year, and epidemics thinned those who remained. When Spain ceded Florida to Britain in 1763, the handful of Timucua left near St. Augustine sailed for Cuba with the Spanish.
zh:
1444年，萨旺尼河与圣菲河之间的土地由北乌蒂纳人占据，他们操蒂穆夸语的一支方言，西班牙人后来称之为「正宗蒂穆夸语」。分散的务农村落各有酋长，主要村镇可能就在菲格泉；萨旺尼河对岸是关系密切的尤斯塔加人。1539年埃尔南多·德·索托率军穿过，认为北乌蒂纳人比他此前见过的任何族群都多。他把酋长阿瓜卡莱昆扣为人质，在纳皮图卡附近遭到伏击、打了一仗后，处死这名酋长和其他人质，随后继续进军。

1597年方济各会进入这一酋邦，很可能设在菲格泉的圣马丁·德·蒂穆夸成为蒂穆夸传教教区的首要传教站。北乌蒂纳人是1656年蒂穆夸叛乱的主力；西班牙军队焚毁村镇，把幸存者迁到圣奥古斯丁与阿巴拉契之间的王家大道沿线。后来，受雇于卡罗来纳的克里克和亚马西袭掠者连年掳人，疫病又使留下的人不断减少。1763年西班牙把佛罗里达割让给英国时，聚在圣奥古斯丁附近的少数蒂穆夸人随西班牙人乘船前往古巴。

en:
In 1444 Apalachee was the most populous and tightly ruled native country in Florida, a Muskogean-speaking land between the Aucilla and Ochlockonee rivers behind Apalachee Bay. Its farming villages answered to powerful chiefs, kept large stores of maize, wore copper ornaments and raised platform mounds for their rites, and Anhaica was the head town. Timucua speakers lived just beyond the Aucilla to the east.

Pánfilo de Narváez marched in on 15 June 1528 and met such resistance that he fell back to the coast. Hernando de Soto seized Anhaica eleven years later and wintered there in 1539 and 1540 while Apalachee raiders killed his horses. Franciscans arrived around 1600, and in 1656 San Luis de Talimali became the western capital of Spanish Florida, with Apalachee grain and cattle sent from the province to feed St. Augustine. In January 1704, during Queen Anne's War, the former Carolina governor James Moore led about fifty colonists and a thousand Creek warriors through the missions; the fight at Ayubale was the only large stand. Moore carried off roughly 1,300 surrendered Apalachee, some of them resettled on the Savannah and Ocmulgee rivers, and another thousand as slaves. The Spanish themselves burned San Luis and abandoned the province, and only a small band came back near St. Marks in 1718.
zh:
1444年的阿巴拉契是佛罗里达人口最多、统治最严的原住民地区，这片穆斯科格语土地位于奥西拉河与奥洛克洛尼河之间，背靠阿巴拉契湾。务农村落听命于有权势的酋长，储存大量玉米，佩戴铜饰，夯筑土墩举行仪式，安海卡是首镇。奥西拉河以东不远就是蒂穆夸语人群。

1528年6月15日，潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯进入此地，遭到顽强抵抗，只得退回海岸。十一年后埃尔南多·德·索托攻占安海卡，在阿巴拉契人不断袭杀马匹的情况下于1539年至1540年在此过冬。约1600年方济各会传教士到来，1656年圣路易斯·德·塔利马利成为西属佛罗里达的西部首府，阿巴拉契出产的谷物和牲畜从这里运往圣奥古斯丁供应该城。1704年1月安妮女王战争期间，前卡罗来纳总督詹姆斯·摩尔率领约五十名殖民者和一千名克里克战士横扫各传教站，阿尤巴莱一战是仅有的大规模抵抗。摩尔带走约一千三百名投降的阿巴拉契人，其中一些被安置到萨凡纳河和奥克马尔吉河畔，另有约一千人被掳为奴。西班牙人自己焚毁圣路易斯，放弃整个教区，只有一小群人在1718年回到圣马可斯附近。

en:
In 1444 the Guale lived on the Georgia coast and its Sea Islands, among the tidal creeks and salt marshes between the Altamaha and Savannah rivers, with towns on St. Catherines and Sapelo. Their chiefs, called micos, ruled through town councils and matrilineal clans, and the towns held plazas and platform mounds in the coastal Mississippian tradition. Families grew maize and beans, hunted deer on the mainland, and took fish and oysters from the estuaries; island and river towns traded food and shell and exchanged marriage partners.

Spanish missionaries from St. Augustine entered the Guale towns in the 1560s, a few years after the first French ships had called there. The friars baptised and taught, but their missions also fed St. Augustine and sent drafts of Guale men to work its fields and walls under the repartimiento labour system. In 1597 five Franciscans were killed across the towns in a single rising. Spanish accounts blamed Juanillo, a chief who defied the friars' ban on polygyny, though rivalries among the micos fed it as well; a sixth friar, Francisco de Avila, was held for ten months before Governor Canzo's burning expeditions and Spanish-backed rivals brought Juanillo down. The missions recovered, but epidemics, Westo slave raiders armed from Carolina, and pirates wore the province down until Spain withdrew its last coastal stations in 1684. Most Guale then entered the Yamasee confederacy and filled its Upper Towns; armed by the Scots of Stuarts Town on Port Royal Sound, Yamasee raiders sailed south to carry off Florida mission villagers. James Moore's South Carolinians overran the coast in 1702, and after the Yamasee War of 1715 the survivors scattered among the Lower Creeks and the Florida missions. When James Oglethorpe founded Georgia in 1733 the Guale no longer held the islands.
zh:
1444年，瓜莱人住在佐治亚海岸和它的海岛上，活动在阿尔塔马哈河与萨凡纳河之间的潮汐河汊与盐沼之间，圣凯瑟琳斯岛、萨佩洛岛上都有他们的村镇。酋长称为米科，依靠镇议会和母系氏族施政；镇中建有广场和土墩，是沿海密西西比文化的传统。居民种玉米和豆类，在大陆猎鹿，在河口捕鱼采蚝，海岛与河畔村镇交换粮食、贝壳并互通婚姻。

圣奥古斯丁的西班牙传教士在法国船只最先来访几年之后，于1560年代进入瓜莱村镇。修士们施洗讲道，传教站却还要供养圣奥古斯丁，按劳役摊派制度征调瓜莱男子去那里耕田筑城。1597年，五名方济各会士在各村的同一次起事里被杀。西班牙记载把主谋归于违抗多妻禁令的酋长胡安尼略，但米科们之间的争斗也是起因；第六名修士弗朗西斯科·德·阿维拉被囚十个月，坎索总督出兵焚毁村镇，加上西班牙支持的对头出手，才把胡安尼略除掉。传教区一度恢复，但疫病、得到卡罗来纳火器的韦斯托掳奴者和海盗不断消耗这里，西班牙终于在1684年撤走最后几座海岸站点。此后多数瓜莱人加入亚马西联盟，构成其「上镇」的主体；在罗亚尔港斯图尔特镇苏格兰人的武装下，亚马西袭击者南航，掳走佛罗里达传教村镇的居民。1702年詹姆斯·摩尔率领南卡罗来纳人横扫海岸，1715年亚马西战争后幸存者分别投奔下游克里克人和佛罗里达传教区。1733年詹姆斯·奥格尔索普建立佐治亚时，瓜莱人已不再保有这些海岛。

en:
The fall-line hills of the lower Chattahoochee are the country of Kasihta and the other Lower Creek towns. Their Muskogean-speaking villagers came out of the South Appalachian Mississippian world: maize fields climbed the river terraces below platform mounds that carried temples and chiefs' houses, and after the old mound centres broke up each town ran its own affairs. Creek oral tradition traced Kasihta and its neighbour Coweta to settlers from the Ocmulgee around AD 900-1000, and the two ranked as the oldest towns on the Chattahoochee. Kasihta was a 'white town', a town of peace, where councils met and blood could not be spilled. In 1444 its people traded along the ridge paths and had never seen a European.

Franciscans and soldiers reached the Chattahoochee from Apalachee in 1638, and by the 1670s the town's deerskins were going through Florida to Havana while English traders from Charleston appeared at Coweta. Slave raids and the rivalry of Spain and England pulled most of the towns east to the Ocmulgee, where Carolina called them the Ochese. Kasihta and Coweta people fought in the Yamasee confederacy, raiding for slaves on Carolina's behalf, until debt and the traders' abuses drove the towns to rise on 15 April 1715. The Yamasee War killed about seven percent of South Carolina's settlers and nearly wiped the colony out; when the Cherokee took the colonists' side in 1716 the coalition broke, and the towns went back to the Chattahoochee as the Lower Towns of the Creek confederacy. For a century Kasihta shared in the deerskin trade with Carolina and Georgia, a white town that took in refugees as smaller peoples folded into the Creek world. The American Revolution and the treaties after it ate into the town lands, and Andrew Jackson's defeat of the Upper Towns in the Creek civil war of 1813-14 forced the defeated nation to surrender its Georgia country; by 1821 the old Kasihta lands were open to American settlement.
zh:
查特胡奇河下游的瀑布线丘陵，是卡西塔和其他下克里克城镇的土地。这里讲穆斯科格语的村民出自南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化：玉米地沿河畔台地拾级而上，平顶土丘上建有神庙和酋长的居所；古老的墩台中心瓦解后，各城镇自行处理内部事务。克里克口传把卡西塔和邻镇考维塔追溯到约公元900至1000年从奥克马尔吉河迁来的移民，两镇并列为查特胡奇河畔最古老的城镇。卡西塔是一座「白镇」，也就是和平镇：议事在此举行，镇上禁止流血。1444年，居民沿山脊小路与远近邻族贸易，还从未见过欧洲人。

1638年，方济各会修士和士兵从阿巴拉奇抵达查特胡奇河；到1670年代，这里的鹿皮已经佛罗里达远销哈瓦那，查尔斯顿来的英国商人也出现在考维塔。贩奴袭扰加上西班牙与英国的争夺，把大多数城镇向东引向奥克马尔吉河，卡罗来纳把他们称作奥切斯人。卡西塔人和考维塔人随亚马西联盟出战，替卡罗来纳掳人为奴，直到债务和商人的凌虐把诸镇逼反：1715年4月15日，亚马西战争爆发。这场战争杀死了南卡罗来纳约百分之七的殖民者，殖民地几乎覆灭；1716年切罗基人倒向殖民者一边，联盟瓦解，诸镇退回查特胡奇河，组成克里克联盟的下镇。此后一个世纪，卡西塔参与对卡罗来纳和佐治亚的鹿皮贸易，作为白镇收留难民，看着较小的族群陆续并入克里克世界。美国独立战争及战后条约不断蚕食城镇土地；1813至1814年克里克内战中，安德鲁·杰克逊击败上镇，战败的联盟被迫交出佐治亚故土，到1821年，古老的卡西塔土地已向美国拓殖者敞开。

en:
The mountain-fringed valleys of the upper Coosa River were the seat of Coosa, the greatest of the South Appalachian paramount chiefdoms. Its capital, the site archaeologists call Little Egypt, stood on the Coosawattee with a plaza and three platform mounds at the head of eight villages of perhaps 2,500 to 4,650 people. From there the mico drew tribute from seven or more subject chiefdoms strung four hundred miles along the Appalachians, about 50,000 people in all, as far north as Chiaha on the French Broad, whose raised houses looked over fields of maize, beans, squash and tobacco. In 1444 Coosa's merchants and war parties were known from the Tennessee to the Alabama piedmont.

Three Spanish expeditions reached Coosa inside thirty years. De Soto came in the summer of 1540, his chroniclers spelling the name Coça and finding not one city but a chain of villages with fertile gardens and full granaries; Tristán de Luna followed in 1560 and Juan Pardo in 1566-68, who built five forts in the interior, Fort San Pedro beside Chiaha and his main fort, San Juan, at Joara. In 1568 the Indians rose and killed the garrisons, all but one of Pardo's soldiers dying, and Spain made no further attempt on the interior. Disease proved deadlier than the soldiers: by 1600 the Coosa heartland was largely abandoned, the survivors withdrawing into small fortified villages down the Coosa in Alabama, one of them a palisaded town of 47 houses, while Cherokee warriors from the mountains took the empty northern valleys. The name Coosa lived on as one of the four mother towns of the Creek confederacy among the Upper Towns, deep in the deerskin trade of the eighteenth century. Andrew Jackson's defeat of the Upper Towns in the Creek civil war of 1813-14 brought forced cessions that stripped the old Coosa country of its self-rule.
zh:
上库萨河群山环抱的河谷，是南阿巴拉契亚诸最高酋邦中最强大的库萨的根本之地。其首府（考古学家称小埃及遗址）坐落库萨瓦蒂河畔，镇中有广场和三座平顶土丘，统辖八座村落、约两千五百至四千六百人。大酋长向沿阿巴拉契亚山脉绵延四百英里的七个或更多臣属酋邦索取贡赋，总人口约五万，势力最北抵达弗伦奇布罗德河畔的奇亚哈；那里架空而起的房屋俯瞰着玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟田。1444年，从田纳西到亚拉巴马皮德蒙特，各地都知道库萨的商队和战队。

三十年间，三支西班牙远征队先后抵达库萨。1540年夏德索托到来，随行记事把名字拼作Coça；他们没有见到雄城，只见到一串田园肥沃、粮仓充盈的村镇。特里斯坦·德·卢纳1560年继至，胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年再来，在内地修筑五座要塞：圣佩德罗堡立在奇亚哈旁，主堡圣胡安堡设在乔阿拉。1568年，印第安人起事，歼灭各堡驻军，帕尔多的士兵仅一人生还，西班牙再也没有尝试深入内陆殖民。比士兵更致命的是疫病：到1600年，库萨腹地已大半荒废，幸存者退入库萨河下游亚拉巴马境内设防的小村，其中一座围栅镇有47座房屋；山里的切罗基战士则占有了空旷的北方谷地。「库萨」之名延续下来，成为克里克联盟四大母镇之一，位列上镇，深深卷入18世纪的鹿皮贸易。1813至1814年克里克内战中，安德鲁·杰克逊击败上镇，随后的强迫割地终结了古老库萨故土的自治。

en:
Issati is the Santee country, where the Congaree and Wateree meet to form the Santee and the river crosses a hundred miles of South Carolina coastal plain to the Atlantic. The Santee were a small Catawban-speaking people whose villages, burial mounds and hunting grounds lined the middle river, and in 1444 canoe and foot trails tied them to the Winyah, Congaree and Catawba while no European ship had yet sounded the river mouth.

Spaniards of Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón's expedition touched this coast in 1526, and Francisco de Écija, sent from St Augustine in 1605 and 1609, noted Santee villages along the banks. After the English founded Charles Town in 1670 the Santee were drawn into the deerskin and slave trades; in 1700 John Lawson found their settlements running for miles along the river. They rose with the Yamasee against the colony in 1715, when a census counted only two villages and forty-three men, and in late 1716 militia with Etiwan and Cusabo allies took the river villages and sold many of the men into West Indian slavery.

During the Revolution the British stockaded Fort Watson on the Santee to guard the link between Charleston and their inland posts. In April 1781 Francis Marion's militia and Henry Lee's Continental force besieged it without artillery; unable to storm the palisade or cut the garrison off from the river, the Americans hewed a rough log tower higher than the walls, set riflemen on its platform and shot the defenders off the parapets until the fort surrendered on 23 April. The Santee Canal, authorised in 1786 and opened in 1800, ran twenty-two miles from the Santee to the Cooper River, carrying upcountry produce to Charleston by a shallow inland route.
zh:
伊萨蒂是桑蒂人的土地：资河与沃特里河汇成桑蒂河，河水穿过南卡罗来纳沿海平原上百里，注入大西洋。桑蒂人是人口不多的卡塔万语族群，村落、墓冢和猎场沿中游两岸排开；1444年，独木舟航线和小路把他们同温亚人、康加里人和卡托巴人连在一起，欧洲船只还没有测过河口的水深。

1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永远征队里的西班牙人到过这段海岸；1605年和1609年，圣奥古斯丁派出的弗朗西斯科·费尔南德斯·德·埃西哈两次记录了河畔的桑蒂村落。1670年英国人建立查尔斯镇后，桑蒂人被卷入鹿皮与奴隶贸易；1700年，约翰·劳森看到他们的聚落在沿河数英里内绵延。1715年，他们随雅马西人起兵攻打殖民地，战前的人口调查只数出两座村落、四十三名男子；1716年底，民兵联合埃蒂万人和库萨博人攻下河畔村落，把许多男子贩往西印度群岛的奴隶市场。

独立战争中，英军在桑蒂河畔筑起沃森堡，扼守查尔斯顿与内陆据点之间的水陆通道。1781年4月，弗朗西斯·马里昂的民兵和亨利·李的大陆军部队围攻该堡；他们没有火炮，强攻木栅和断水都不奏效，便砍木搭起一座比围墙还高的粗木塔，让射手站上塔顶平台，把守军从雉堞后一一打退，堡垒于4月23日投降。桑蒂运河1786年获准开凿、1800年通航，长二十二英里，连通桑蒂河与库珀河，内陆物产沿这条浅水航路运往查尔斯顿。

en:
The rolling Piedmont of the Wateree and Catawba rivers is the homeland of the Iswa, Ye Iswa, 'people of the river', later written Catawba. In the fifteenth century its mound towns answered to the mico of Cofitachequi, whose capital Talimeco stood on the Wateree. Its greatest mound carried a temple holding the bones of dead rulers, heaps of freshwater pearls and rooms of weapons; Garcilaso the Inca later wrote of twelve life-size, club-wielding statues guarding its door. Long wars with Ocute in Georgia had emptied the Savannah, Saluda and Broad basins into a waste the Spanish called the Despoblado, leaving Cofitachequi in 1444 the strongest power between the mountains and the coast.

Spanish ships raiding Winyah Bay in 1521 carried off some sixty captives. One, Francisco Chicora, learned Spanish and told Peter Martyr in Spain of Datha, a tall, pale, pearl-rich king carried on his subjects' shoulders. In 1540 de Soto followed a captive boy's tale of a gold-rich land ruled by a woman, crossed two weeks of the empty Despoblado, and reached Cofitachequi. Its ruler, the Lady of Cofitachequi, met him at the river on a litter draped in white cloth. The Spaniards took her hostage while hunting gold, found none, and she escaped on the road to Joara. Juan Pardo in 1566-68 found the chiefdom much weakened and called its town Canosi; his forts were burned within two years.

Westo and Occaneechi slave-raiders harried the region through the later 1600s, though Henry Woodward met an 'emperor' said to field a thousand bowmen in 1670, who had visited Charleston. In 1701 John Lawson found only Congaree hamlets where Talimeco had stood, and the survivors drifted into the Catawba confederacy. As the Catawba the river people became the Piedmont's leading tribe, allied with Carolina, their women shaping river-clay pottery in a craft reaching back to Woodland times. Smallpox swept them in 1738 and again in 1759, the second outbreak killing nearly half the nation. Shawnee raiders killed their chief King Hagler near his village in 1763, the year South Carolina confirmed the Catawba 144,000 acres on the river. They fought for the revolutionaries, withdrawing to Virginia when British troops came in 1780 and returning after Guilford Court House in 1781.
zh:
沃特里河与卡托巴河流经的起伏皮德蒙特，是伊斯瓦人的家园：耶伊斯瓦（Ye Iswa）意为「河上人」，英国殖民者后来把这个名字写作卡托巴。15世纪时，这一带的土丘城镇都听命于科菲塔切基的大酋长，首府塔利梅科位于沃特里河畔。最大的土丘顶上建有神庙，供着历代统治者的遗骨、成堆的淡水珍珠和一间间武器库；印卡·加西拉索后来据多年后的转述写道，庙门口立着十二尊手持大棒、与真人等高的雕像。与佐治亚奥库特的长期战争使萨凡纳河、萨卢达河和布罗德河流域人烟断绝，化为西班牙人所说的「德斯波布拉多」荒野，到1444年，科菲塔切基已成了山地与海岸之间最强的势力。

1521年，西班牙船在温约湾掳走约六十人。其中一个叫弗朗西斯科·奇科拉的人学会西班牙语，在西班牙宫廷向彼得·马特讲述：有位名叫达塔的国王，肤色白皙、身材高大，坐拥珍珠，出行由臣民肩扛而行。1540年春，德索托听信一个被俘少年所说「有片黄金之地由女人统治」，在空旷的德斯波布拉多荒野里走了两个星期，抵达科菲塔切基。统治者是一位女性，西班牙人称她「科菲塔切基女主」，她乘铺着白布的肩舆到河边相见。西班牙人搜寻黄金时把她扣作人质，结果黄金没有找到，她在前往乔阿拉的路上逃脱。胡安·帕尔多1566至1568年再到时，酋邦已大为衰弱；他把这里的城镇称作卡诺西，所修要塞两年内全部被烧。

17世纪后期，韦斯托人和奥卡尼奇人的贩奴队伍不断袭掠这一地区，但亨利·伍德沃德1670年仍见到一位据称能出动上千弓箭手的「皇帝」，此人还到访过查尔斯顿。1701年约翰·劳森路过时，塔利梅科旧地只剩康加里人的小村落，幸存者陆续汇入卡托巴联盟。以卡托巴之名，河上居民成为皮德蒙特最强大的部族，与卡罗来纳结盟；妇女用河泥制陶，这门手艺可一直追溯到林地时期。1738年和1759年天花两度袭来，后一次夺去近半数族人的生命。1763年，肖尼袭扰者在村边杀死首领哈格勒王，同年南卡罗来纳为卡托巴人确认了沿河14.4万英亩的保留地。独立战争中他们支持美方，1780年英军过境时暂避弗吉尼亚，1781年吉尔福德县府战役后返回家园。

en:
The gorges and tablelands of the upper Cumberland were, in 1444, a border country between peoples. The Yuchi, who call themselves Tsoyaha, 'children of the sun', in a language with no known kin, held the Tennessee valley to the south and ranged across these headwaters, planting corn in the river bottoms; Shawnee hunters from the Ohio country knew the Cumberland as Wasioto. Deer and elk filled the hills, and no European had yet crossed the ridges to the east.

Hernando de Soto's men, crossing the Tennessee valley in 1541, heard of the Yuchi as the Uchi and described them as a powerful tribe. The first English party over the Appalachian divide reached the western rivers in 1671, when Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam were sent out from Fort Henry by Abraham Wood. By then the upper country was emptying fast: in the 1670s Iroquois war parties fighting for the fur trade drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, and in 1714 the Cherokee destroyed the Yuchi town of Chestowee at the urging of two English traders from South Carolina; the surviving Yuchi drifted south to the Savannah and the Chattahoochee. For two generations the headwaters were left to passing hunters. In March 1775 the Cherokee sold the Kentucky and Cumberland country at Sycamore Shoals to Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company, and Daniel Boone blazed the Wilderness Road through Cumberland Gap; by the end of the century settlers' stations had taken root along the upper river.
zh:
1444年，坎伯兰河上游的峡谷与台原是几支人群相邻而居的边地。尤奇人用他们那种与任何语言都不亲缘的语言自称「措亚哈」，意为「太阳之子」；他们据有南方的田纳西河谷，游猎踪迹遍及这一带河源，在河滩种植玉米，来自俄亥俄方向的肖尼猎人则把坎伯兰河称作瓦西奥托。山林中鹿和麋鹿成群，东面的山脊还不曾有欧洲人翻越。

1541年，埃尔南多·德·索托的队伍穿过田纳西河谷，听说过尤奇人，记作「乌奇」，并称他们是一支强大的部落。英格兰人最早翻越阿巴拉契亚分水岭是在1671年：亚伯拉罕·伍德从亨利堡派出托马斯·巴茨和罗伯特·法勒姆，抵达西向的河水。此时上游地带正在迅速变空：1670年代，为毛皮贸易作战的易洛魁武装把肖尼人逐出肯塔基；1714年，切罗基人受两名南卡罗来纳英格兰商人怂恿，摧毁尤奇城镇切斯托维，幸存的尤奇人向南退往萨凡纳河与查特胡奇河。此后两代人，河源一带只剩往来的猎手。1775年3月，切罗基人在锡卡莫尔浅滩把肯塔基与坎伯兰的土地卖给理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司，丹尼尔·布恩随即开辟穿过坎伯兰峡的荒野之路；到18世纪末，移民据点已在上游河畔扎下根。

en:
The Chiaha were a Dallas-phase Mississippian chiefdom of the lower French Broad River valley in East Tennessee, farming maize, beans, squash and tobacco in the Appalachian bottoms. Their principal village, Olamico, stood on an island in the river behind a wooden palisade, the first fortified town Hernando de Soto's men met on their march, with a thirty-foot platform mound rising above its plaza. Chiaha marked the northern edge of Coosa's reach, and its people spoke a Muskogean tongue related to Koasati. In 1444 the island town still commanded the valley's maize lands, and no European had crossed the mountains.

De Soto reached Olamico in June 1540 and was welcomed: the chief lent him his own house, and the villagers brought sofkee corn gruel, honey and a sweet sauce of bear fat. The goodwill ended when de Soto demanded thirty women; the elders cleared the town and withdrew to another island upstream, and he settled for porters instead. Juan Pardo came in 1567, and his men built Fort San Pedro nearby, one of six garrisons strung west from Joara. In 1568 the inland towns rose at once, burned the forts and overwhelmed the garrisons; of Pardo's 120 soldiers across the six forts, only one lived, and Spain never tried the interior again. Disease thinned and rearranged the valley towns, so that when the Virginians James Needham and Gabriel Arthur crossed the mountains in 1673 looking for the Tomahittans, the French Broad country was passing under the Cherokee, whose speakers already held the hills between Chiaha and Joara.
zh:
奇亚哈人是东田纳西弗伦奇布罗德河下游谷地的达拉斯期密西西比文化酋邦，在阿巴拉契亚的滩地上种植玉米、豆类、南瓜和烟草。主镇奥拉米科坐落在河心岛上，围以木栅，是德·索托远征队一路上见到的第一座设防城镇，镇中广场上矗立着一座三十英尺高的平顶土墩。奇亚哈地处库萨势力范围的北缘，居民操与科阿萨蒂语相近的马斯科吉语。1444年，这座岛上重镇仍统辖着河谷的玉米地，欧洲人还没有翻山而来。

1540年6月，德·索托抵达奥拉米科，起初颇受礼遇：酋长把自己的住宅让给他住，村民送来索夫基玉米粥、蜂蜜和熊脂调成的甜酱。德·索托索要三十名女子，长老们当即把妇女全部撤走、避往上游另一座小岛，他只好改口要了一队脚夫。1567年胡安·帕尔多到来，部下在附近建起圣佩德罗堡，是从乔阿拉向西串联的六座驻军要塞之一。1568年，内陆诸镇同时起事，焚毁要塞、击溃驻军，帕尔多派驻六堡的一百二十名士兵仅一人生还，西班牙再未尝试深入内陆。疫病使河谷诸镇人口凋零、聚落重组，1673年弗吉尼亚人詹姆斯·尼达姆与加布里埃尔·阿瑟为寻找托马希坦人翻山到来时，弗伦奇布罗德一带正渐入切罗基人之手，而切罗基语人群早已据有奇亚哈与乔阿拉之间的山地。

en:
Joara, settled around AD 1000 in the upper Catawba valley at the foot of the Blue Ridge, within sight of Table Rock, was the largest Mississippian town in the country that became North Carolina. A twelve-foot earthen mound stood above the plaza on the west bank of Upper Creek, and its people traded copper and salt through the hills and grew maize in fertile bottoms no coastal European had seen. In 1444 Joara was still a full mound chiefdom, one of the few inland towns ruled by a mico, a great chief, rather than a lesser orata, and untouched by Europe.

De Soto's chroniclers recorded Joara in 1540. In January 1567 Juan Pardo wintered there, renamed the town Cuenca and built Fort San Juan, the first European settlement in the North Carolina interior, nearly twenty years before the English Roanoke colony and forty before Jamestown; he meant to open an overland road to the silver mines of Mexico, believing the Appalachians were a Mexican mountain range. Five more forts ran west from San Juan to Chiaha. In 1568 the towns rose together and burned all six, and of Pardo's 120 garrison soldiers only one survived; Spain gave up the southeastern interior. Disease emptied the upper Catawba soon after, and when John Lederer passed through in 1670 he found a Sara town nearby whose people dug cinnabar for purple face paint and traded cakes of salt. The survivors, the Sara or Cheraw, drifted east to the Yadkin and Dan and were absorbed into the Catawba Nation between 1726 and 1739. English, Scots-Irish and German farmers took the abandoned valley later in the eighteenth century.
zh:
乔阿拉约于公元1000年兴起于蓝岭山麓的卡托巴河上游，抬头可见桌山，是后来北卡罗来纳境内最大的密西西比文化城镇。一座十二英尺高的土墩矗立在上溪西岸的广场旁，居民以铜和盐同山地各部交易，在欧洲人还不知道的肥沃滩地上种植玉米。1444年的乔阿拉仍是一个完整的土丘酋邦，是内陆少有的由米科大酋长而非小首领奥拉塔统辖的重镇，也未曾接触欧洲。

1540年，德·索托的书记官记下了乔阿拉。1567年1月，胡安·帕尔多在此过冬，将镇子改名昆卡，筑起圣胡安堡，这是欧洲人在北卡罗来纳内陆的第一个定居点，比英国人的罗阿诺克殖民地早了近二十年，比詹姆斯敦早四十年；帕尔多打算从这里开出一条通往墨西哥银矿的陆路，因为西班牙人误把阿巴拉契亚山脉当成了墨西哥的山系。圣胡安堡以西又修五座要塞，一直连到奇亚哈。1568年，诸镇同时起事，六堡尽毁，帕尔多麾下一百二十名驻军仅一人生还，西班牙就此放弃东南部内陆。疫病很快使卡托巴河上游人口流散，1670年约翰·莱德勒路经此地时，在附近见到一座萨拉人城镇，居民开采辰砂调制紫色面彩，还以盐饼交易。余部即萨拉人，又称切罗人，向东退入亚德金河与丹河流域，于1726至1739年间并入卡托巴联盟。18世纪后期，英格兰、苏格兰-爱尔兰和德意志农户接手了这片荒废的河谷。

en:
The pinewoods and river bottoms between the North Carolina coast and the Piedmont are Tuscarora country. Their name, Skarù·ręˀ, means 'hemp gatherers', after one of the three tribes of their Iroquoian confederacy, and the wild hemp gave fibre for cord and medicine. Their large towns stood on the Roanoke, Tar, Neuse and Pamlico, where dugout canoes ran from inland villages down to the coastal sounds, and seven matrilineal clans, Bear, Beaver, Turtle and Wolf among them, bound the towns together. In 1444 these were populous, self-ruling towns, kin in language to the Iroquois far to the north and untouched by any European.

For more than fifty years after the first English settlers came in 1653 the Tuscarora lived at peace with them, until slave raiding and the seizure of river lands drove the southern chief Hancock to war. In 1711 his men killed John Lawson, the English surveyor whose book on Carolina had guided colonists and who had helped found New Bern, and allied towns struck in coordinated raids at the farms and the town of Bath along the Roanoke, Neuse and Trent. South Carolina answered with two armies of a few dozen white men and hundreds of Indian allies: John Barnwell's in 1712, then James Moore's, nearly a thousand strong. The neutral northern chief Tom Blount seized Hancock, whom the settlers executed in 1712, and Moore's army stormed Fort Neoheroka in 1713, a palisaded strongpoint built against firearms and artillery whose defenders had no cannon of their own; about 950 people died there or were carried off and sold in the Caribbean or New England. Blount's followers took a 56,000-acre treaty tract on the Roanoke in 1718, chartered in 1722 as Indian Woods, and in that same year the Iroquois admitted the migrating Tuscarora as their sixth nation. The last band left North Carolina for New York in 1804.
zh:
北卡罗来纳海岸与皮德蒙特之间的松林和河滨低地，是斯卡鲁雷（塔斯卡洛拉人）的家园。族名斯卡鲁雷意为「采麻者」，原是其易洛魁语三族联盟中一支的名字，野麻用来取纤维、搓绳和制药。他们的大镇坐落在洛亚诺克河、塔尔河、纽斯河和帕姆利科河畔，独木舟从内陆村落顺流直达海岸潟湖；熊、河狸、龟、狼等七个母系氏族把各镇联结在一起。1444年的塔斯卡洛拉各镇人烟稠密、自主其政，与遥远北方的易洛魁人语言相通，欧洲人却尚未到来。

1653年第一批英国定居者到来后，塔斯卡洛拉人与他们和平相处了五十多年，最终被贩奴袭掠和对河畔土地的侵占逼反。1711年，南支首领汉考克的部下处死了约翰·劳森，这位英国测量官写过一本指点殖民者前往卡罗来纳的书，还参与建立了新伯尔尼；随后结盟各镇协同出击，攻掠洛亚诺克河、纽斯河和特伦特河畔的农庄与巴斯镇。南卡罗来纳两度派来几十名白人加数百名印第安盟友的军队：1712年约翰·巴恩韦尔一路，其后詹姆斯·穆尔又率近千人前来。保持中立的北支首领汤姆·布朗特拿下汉考克，殖民者于1712年将他处死；穆尔的军队1713年攻破内奥赫罗卡堡，这座木栅要塞为抵御火枪火炮而筑，守军却没有自己的大炮，约950人战死，或被掳往加勒比和新英格兰卖为奴隶。布朗特的部众1718年依约得到洛亚诺克河畔5.6万英亩土地，1722年划为印第安伍兹保留地；同年，易洛魁联盟接纳北上的塔斯卡洛拉人为第六族。1804年，最后一支人离开北卡罗来纳，迁往纽约。

en:
The sheltered waters of the Pamlico River and Pamlico Sound, guarded from the Atlantic by the long line of the Outer Banks, were the country of the Pamlico, a Carolina Algonquian people whom Raleigh's men recorded in 1585 as the Pomoui. They planted corn and beans in riverside fields and drew shad and herring from the sound, sharing its inlets and shoals with the Croatan, Machapunga and Secotan, their kin in language and trade. In 1444 no European sail had yet crossed this horizon; the inlets later charted as Wococon and Hatteras were known only to the canoe men who fished them.

Ships of the Roanoke voyages had shown the English these waters, yet settlers did not take up the Pamlico River until the 1690s, English farmers and French Huguenots among them. The naturalist John Lawson helped lay out Bath, chartered in 1705 as the first town in North Carolina, which lived by naval stores, furs and tobacco. A smallpox 'great mortality' in 1696 shattered the Pamlico, and when Lawson visited in 1710 he found a single village of perhaps fifteen fighting men. Swiss and Palatine Germans under Christoph von Graffenried founded New Bern the same year, and on 22 September 1711 the southern Tuscarora and their Pamlico allies struck Bath, New Bern and the plantations along the Neuse and Trent, opening the Tuscarora War; Lawson was among the killed, and more than a hundred settlers died round New Bern. The Pamlico who survived the war were absorbed into the Machapunga and Tuscarora. The pirate Blackbeard settled at Bath in 1718 and took the king's pardon, but put to sea again; on 22 November Virginia forces under Lieutenant Robert Maynard overtook him at Ocracoke Inlet and killed him. New Bern, with its new governor's palace, became the colony's capital in 1770.
zh:
帕姆利科河与帕姆利科湾水面平静，外滩群岛如长堤横在外面，挡住大西洋的风浪。这里是波莫伊克（帕姆利科）人的土地，他们操卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆语，雷利的手下1585年把他们记作「波莫伊」。他们在河畔田地里种玉米和豆子，在湾中捕捞西鲱和鲱鱼，与语言相通、贸易往来的克罗阿坦人、马查邦加人和塞科坦人共用各处水口和浅滩。1444年，欧洲人的船帆还没有出现在海平线上；后来被标作沃科康和哈特勒斯的水道口，那时只有打鱼的独木舟船夫知晓。

罗阿诺克远航的英国船只早已熟悉这片水面，但直到1690年代，英格兰农户和法国胡格诺教徒才陆续迁居帕姆利科河畔。博物学家约翰·劳森参与规划了巴斯，这座1705年获许建城的小镇是北卡罗来纳第一座城镇，靠柏油松脂、毛皮和烟草为生。1696年一场被他们称为「大死亡」的天花重创帕姆利科人，到1710年劳森来访时，只剩一个小村子，能作战的人不过十五名上下。同年，克里斯多夫·冯·格拉芬里德率领瑞士人和普法尔茨德意志人建起新伯尔尼；1711年9月22日，南部图斯卡罗拉人联合帕姆利科等盟邦袭击巴斯、新伯尔尼以及纽斯河、特伦特河沿岸的种植园，图斯卡罗拉战争爆发，劳森也在遇害者之列，新伯尔尼一带有一百多名殖民者被杀。战后幸存的帕姆利科人并入马查邦加人和图斯卡罗拉人。海盗黑胡子1718年在巴斯安家、接受国王赦免，却很快重操旧业；同年11月22日，罗伯特·梅纳德中尉率领弗吉尼亚部队在奥克拉科克水口追上他，将他击毙。建起总督府的新伯尔尼1770年成为殖民地首府。

en:
The Pennyrile, the country of the Kaskinampo, is a rolling karst tableland between the lower Cumberland and the Green, its limestone split by sinkholes, springs and river caves. Its most famous ground lies on the Green: Mammoth Cave, the longest cave system known, whose dark passages Indians had entered for thousands of years, leaving cane torches, gourd bowls and woven grass slippers behind them. In 1444 the tableland was the southern country of the Shawnee; their bark-covered houses and cornfields stood in the bottoms, their hunters followed deer and bison to the salt licks, and the lower Cumberland appeared on later French maps as the Riviere des Chaouanons, the River of the Shawnee. No European had yet set eyes on either river.

In the 1670s Iroquois raids waged for the fur trade drove the Shawnee out of Kentucky, leaving the tableland to passing Cherokee and Chickasaw hunting parties. Thomas Walker crossed the mountains to the south-east in 1750 and gave the Cumberland its name. The long hunters followed: in the later 1760s James Smith's party traced the Cumberland down to the Ohio through this country, while Kasper Mansker, Isaac Bledsoe and Uriah Stone marked its licks and trails. The Cherokee sale at Sycamore Shoals in 1775 brought the tableland into Richard Henderson's Transylvania purchase, and settlers' stations began to take root.

The cave enters the written record in 1797, when as the story goes a hunter named Houchin chased a wounded bear into its great mouth. Valentine Simon registered the land the next year and worked its saltpeter, and after the embargo of 1807 cut off foreign saltpeter the cave earth became a strategic commodity. In July 1812 Charles Wilkins and Hyman Gratz bought the cave and put seventy slaves to leaching calcium nitrate on an industrial scale for the gunpowder mills of the War of 1812. With peace the workings closed, and paying visitors were soon touring the galleries by lamplight.
zh:
卡斯基南波所在的彭尼罗尔，是坎伯兰河下游与格林河之间一片起伏的喀斯特台原，石灰岩上遍布落水洞、泉眼和临河溶洞。这片地方最出名的所在是格林河畔的猛犸洞，已知最长的洞穴体系；印第安人早在几千年前就已进入漆黑的洞道，留下芦秆火把、葫芦碗和草编的鞋。1444年，台原是肖尼人南部的活动之地，树皮覆顶的房屋和玉米地坐落在河谷低地，猎手追着鹿和野牛前往盐渍地，坎伯兰河下游后来出现在法国人的地图上，标作「肖尼人之河」。此时欧洲人还不曾看见这两条河。

1670年代，为毛皮贸易而来的易洛魁袭掠把肖尼人逐出肯塔基，台原上只剩切罗基和奇克索的猎手往来。1750年，托马斯·沃克从东南翻山而过，为坎伯兰河命名。随后而来的是「长猎人」：1760年代后期，詹姆斯·史密斯的队伍沿坎伯兰河穿过此地，一直探到俄亥俄河口，卡斯珀·曼斯克、艾萨克·布莱德索和尤赖亚·斯通则记下沿途的盐渍地和小径。1775年，切罗基人在锡卡莫尔浅滩出让土地，台原归入理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚购置，移民据点开始扎下根。

1797年，据传一个姓霍钦的猎人追一头受伤的熊，追进了猛犸洞巨大的洞口。次年瓦伦丁·西蒙登记这块土地并开采硝石；1807年的禁运切断海外硝石来源后，洞里的硝土成了紧俏的军需物。1812年7月，查尔斯·威尔金斯和海曼·格拉茨买下洞穴，驱使七十名奴隶大规模淋取硝酸钙，供给1812年战争的火药厂。战事结束后矿坑关闭，没过多久便有游客提灯入洞游览。

en:
Kentahke is the flat western tail of Kentucky, where Green River bottoms and open barrens slope down to the meeting of the Ohio and Mississippi; every canoe passing between the Gulf of Mexico and the continental interior had to pass this fork. Mississippian farmers held the country first. Wickliffe, a mound town occupied until about 1350, had two platform mounds facing a plaza, a hereditary chief, stored maize and trade links reaching Wisconsin and the Gulf. Those chiefdoms had broken up before any European ship reached the coast, but in 1444 hunters and farmers still used the river landings and cane flats; the Shawnee name later read as Kentucky was glossed as 'at the prairie'.

By the late seventeenth century epidemics and the Beaver Wars had thinned the interior and folded its Algonquian villagers, the Kispoko among them, into the Shawnee. English longhunters and surveyors came next: Thomas Walker crossed in from Virginia in 1750 and Christopher Gist followed the year after, and the 1768 Treaty of Fort Stanwix threw the country open to colonial claims. In 1780 George Rogers Clark built Fort Jefferson on the Mississippi just below the Ohio's mouth, although Governor Thomas Jefferson's warrant had required buying the ground from the Chickasaw; Clark built without asking. Chickasaw warriors besieged the stockade until the garrison burned and left it in June 1781. When Chickasaw chiefs opened peace talks the next year, they told the Americans that this was the place where they had been made to suffer most. Kentucky became a state in 1792, but its western end remained Chickasaw hunting ground until Andrew Jackson and Isaac Shelby signed the Treaty of Tuscaloosa in 1818, buying the tract for 300,000 dollars paid over fifteen years. By 1821 surveyors were running their lines through the purchased prairie.
zh:
肯塔基地处肯塔基西部的平坦尾端，格林河河洲和开阔的贫瘠地朝俄亥俄河与密西西比河的汇流处倾斜；往来墨西哥湾与大陆腹地的独木舟都必须经过这道河口。最早据有这片土地的是密西西比文化的农民。威克利夫是一座延续至约1350年的土墩城镇，两座台墩对着一座广场，由世袭首领统治，存有玉米，贸易往来远达威斯康星和墨西哥湾。这些酋邦在欧洲船抵达海岸前已经瓦解，但1444年仍有猎人和农民使用河边登陆点与藤丛平地；肖尼语里后来读作肯塔基的名字，被解释为「在草原上」。

到17世纪后期，疫病和海狸战争已使内陆人口凋零，基斯波科等说阿尔冈昆语的村社并入肖尼人。英国的长途猎人和测量员随之而来：托马斯·沃克1750年从弗吉尼亚翻山进入，克里斯托弗·吉斯特次年跟进，1768年的《斯坦威克斯堡条约》把这片土地向殖民索求敞开。1780年，乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克在俄亥俄河口下方的密西西比河畔修建杰斐逊堡，而托马斯·杰斐逊州长的批准令本要求向奇克索人购地，克拉克却未征得同意便动工。奇克索战士围攻栅栏堡，守军在1781年6月焚堡撤离。次年奇克索首领议和时对美国人说，正是在这个地方，他们让美国人吃了最大的苦头。肯塔基1792年建州，但西端仍是奇克索人的猎场，直到1818年安德鲁·杰克逊和艾萨克·谢尔比签订《塔斯卡卢萨条约》，以三十万美元、分十五年付清买下这片土地。到1821年，测量员已在购得的草原上拉线划界。

en:
Ouasioto was an older name for the Cumberland ridge country at Kentucky's eastern edge, where the Cumberland River winds out of the mountains on its way to the Ohio. The Shawnee called that river Wasioto, and hunters followed its valleys to the V-shaped notch in the ridge where Kentucky, Virginia and Tennessee meet, one of the few breaks in the Cumberland wall at about 1,630 feet. In 1444 the ridges held no European road or post, only game, furs and native trails, and the country was tied to the Chisca and Yuchi peoples whom the Spanish later met on the upper Tennessee.

Abraham Wood's Virginia traders left the first written report of the notch in the 1670s. The next recorded crossing came in 1750, when the Virginia physician Thomas Walker crossed it and named the river for the Duke of Cumberland, the British commander at Culloden four years earlier. In March 1775 Richard Henderson's Transylvania Company bought Cherokee lands beyond the ridge and sent Daniel Boone with a party of axemen to cut a road through the gap. The trace became the Wilderness Road, and between 200,000 and 300,000 settlers crossed it into Kentucky and the Ohio Valley before 1810. Cherokee raids through the wars of 1776–1794 made the road a war path as well, and after the Treaty of Tellico Blockhouse in 1794 it was widened for wagons.
zh:
奥瓦西奥托是肯塔基东缘坎伯兰山岭一带的旧称，坎伯兰河从群山间流出，一路奔向俄亥俄河。肖尼人称这条河为瓦西奥托；猎人沿河谷前行，可抵达肯塔基、弗吉尼亚和田纳西交界处山岭上一道V形缺口，海拔约1630英尺，是连绵坎伯兰山岭中少有的断口之一。1444年时，山岭间没有欧洲人的道路或商站，只有猎物、毛皮和原住民小路，这片地方同后来西班牙人在田纳西河上游遇到的奇斯卡人和尤奇人联系在一起。

17世纪70年代，亚伯拉罕·伍德派出的弗吉尼亚商人留下了关于这道山口的最早文字记录。下一次有记载的穿越是在1750年，弗吉尼亚医生托马斯·沃克穿过山口，以四年前在卡洛登统兵的英军将领坎伯兰公爵为这条河命名。1775年3月，理查德·亨德森的特兰西瓦尼亚公司买下山岭外侧的切罗基土地，派丹尼尔·布恩带一队伐木工在山口开路。这条小径后来成为荒野之路，到1810年已有20万至30万移民经它进入肯塔基和俄亥俄河谷。1776年至1794年战争期间切罗基人的袭扰也使这条路成了战道；1794年《特利科堡条约》之后，道路被拓宽到可通马车。

en:
Waayaahtanwa is the middle Wabash country of the Wea, whose Miami-Illinois name comes from waayaahtanonki, the 'place of the whirlpool'. In 1444 their bark-covered lodges and cornfields occupied the wooded bottoms between present Terre Haute and Logansport, the stretch of river that later held Ouiatenon near Lafayette. The Wabash carried their canoes to the Ohio and the Mississippi, and trails linked them with the Miami, Piankeshaw, Pepikokia and Illini; French traders and missionaries had not yet come within reach of them.

The Wea enter written records in 1673, after the Beaver Wars had scattered the Miami-speaking peoples. In 1717 Francois Picote de Beletre built Fort Ouiatenon on the Wabash, a palisaded fur post that was the first fortified European settlement in Indiana, meant to hold the Wabash corridor against English expansion. Wea villages settled across the river, and by mid-century five Wea and two Kickapoo villages traded at the post. On 1 June 1763, early in Pontiac's War, Wea, Kickapoo and Mascouten warriors walked in and took it without a fight. The post was ceded to the British, abandoned, and then burned by Charles Scott's American militia in June 1791. The Wea made peace at Greenville in 1795. On 7 November 1811 William Henry Harrison marched a thousand men on Prophetstown on the nearby Tippecanoe, the headquarters Tecumseh and his brother Tenskwatawa, the Prophet, had raised for their tribal confederacy; Tecumseh was away recruiting allies. Warriors attacked the camp before dawn and were beaten off after more than two hours, and the Americans burned the town and its winter stores. Tecumseh's confederacy never recovered. The 1818 Treaty of St Mary's took most of the remaining Wea land, and in 1820 the band agreed to leave the Wabash for Missouri and Arkansas.
zh:
瓦亚坦瓦是韦阿人在沃巴什河中游的土地，族名来自迈阿密—伊利尼语的瓦亚塔农基（waayaahtanonki），意为「漩涡之地」。1444年，他们覆着树皮的屋舍和玉米田分布在今特雷霍特到洛根斯波特之间林木繁茂的河漫滩，后来乌亚塔农堡所在的拉斐特一带也在这段河上。沃巴什河的独木舟可通向俄亥俄河与密西西比河，陆路则把他们与迈阿密人、皮安克肖人、佩皮科基亚人和伊利尼人相连；那时法国商人和传教士还没有到过这里。

韦阿人最早在1673年见诸文字记载，此前海狸战争已使说迈阿密语的各族流散。1717年，弗朗索瓦·皮科特·德·贝莱特尔在沃巴什河畔修建乌亚塔农堡；这座木栅毛皮贸易站是欧洲人在印第安纳的第一个设防据点，用来扼守沃巴什走廊、阻挡英国扩张。韦阿村落搬到堡子对岸定居，到18世纪中叶已有五个韦阿村落和两个基卡普村落在此贸易。1763年6月1日，庞蒂亚克战争初起，韦阿、基卡普和马斯库滕战士走进据点，兵不血刃地将它拿下。该堡随后割给英国又遭废弃，1791年6月被查尔斯·斯科特的美国民团烧毁。韦阿人在1795年《格林维尔条约》后议和。1811年11月7日，威廉·亨利·哈里森率兵一千，进逼附近蒂珀卡努河畔的先知镇；那是特库姆塞和兄长、先知滕斯克瓦塔瓦为各部联盟营建的大本营，当时特库姆塞正外出联络盟友。守军在黎明前袭击营地，激战两个多小时后被击退，美国人随即烧毁先知镇和储备的冬粮，特库姆塞联盟再也没能恢复。1818年《圣玛丽斯条约》割走大部分残存的韦阿土地，1820年这支人同意离开沃巴什，迁往密苏里和阿肯色。

en:
In the fifteenth century the headwaters of the Maumee were Atchakangouen country, the land of the Miami band later called the Crane. Their chief town, Kekionga, stood where the Saint Joseph and Saint Marys join to form the Maumee, on the western edge of the Great Black Swamp; its Miami name described the great blackberry brambles around it. A six-mile carry from the Maumee to the Little River linked Lake Erie with the Wabash and the Mississippi, and furs, food and shell beads already moved along that path. The people planted maize in the bottoms and hunted beaver and deer in the woods, and in 1444 no European had yet entered the country.

Beaver Wars raiding drove the Miami west to Lake Michigan before French guns and trade goods brought the Crane band back to the Maumee about 1700. Jean-Baptiste Bissot de Vincennes built a post and fort at Kekionga in 1704. Smallpox emptied the village in 1733. In 1749 the pro-British chief Memeskia, called La Demoiselle, led his followers a hundred miles southeast to found Pickawillany on the Great Miami; on 21 June 1752 French-allied warriors destroyed that town and killed him, while the French rebuilt Fort Miamis at Kekionga. The village joined Pontiac's rising in 1763 and seized its British garrison, then accepted British posts by 1765. By 1790 Kekionga sent out some two thousand packs of pelts a year, worth about £24,000, twice the value of any other trading district around Detroit.

The frontier wars of the new United States soon reached the town. In 1780, after Augustin de La Balme's raiders had sacked Kekionga, Little Turtle's Miami destroyed the whole force nearby. The confederacy he led defeated Josiah Harmar's army in 1790 and Arthur St. Clair's in 1791, killing some nine hundred Americans, the worst loss the United States Army ever suffered to Native forces. Anthony Wayne's victory at Fallen Timbers in 1794 opened the portage; Wayne built Fort Wayne on Kekionga's site, and the Treaty of Greenville in 1795 took the carry for the United States. Further treaties in 1817 and 1818 ceded the rest of the country around the fort.
zh:
15世纪时，莫米河源头一带是阿恰坎戈恩人的土地，即后来所称鹤部的迈阿密支派。他们的主村凯基翁加位于圣约瑟夫河与圣玛丽斯河汇成莫米河之处，紧挨大黑沼泽西缘；迈阿密语村名说的是村四周大片的黑莓灌丛。从莫米河到利特尔河的六英里陆运道把伊利湖同沃巴什河、密西西比河连起来，毛皮、粮食和贝珠已沿这条路往来。人们在低地种玉米，在林中猎河狸和鹿；1444年，欧洲人尚未进入此地。

海狸战争中的袭击把迈阿密人西驱到密歇根湖一带，后来靠着法国火器和贸易货物，鹤部约在1700年回到莫米河。1704年，让—巴蒂斯特·比索·德·万塞讷在凯基翁加建起贸易站和堡垒。1733年天花使村民撤离一年。1749年，亲英首领梅梅斯基亚（人称拉·德穆瓦泽勒）率众向东南行约一百英里，在大迈阿密河畔另建皮卡维兰尼；1752年6月21日，与法国结盟的武士摧毁此村并将他杀死，法国人则在凯基翁加重建迈阿密堡。1763年，该村加入庞蒂亚克起义，拿下驻守的英国守军，到1765年又接受英国据点。到1790年，凯基翁加每年输出约二千包毛皮，价值约二万四千英镑，是底特律周围其他任何贸易区产值的两倍。

新生美国的边疆战争很快波及这座村镇。1780年，奥古斯丁·德·拉尔姆的袭击队洗劫凯基翁加后，「小乌龟」率领的迈阿密人在附近将其全歼。他领导的联盟1790年击败乔赛亚·哈马尔、1791年击败阿瑟·圣克莱尔，美军约九百人丧命，是美国陆军在与原住民武力交战中最惨重的失败。1794年安东尼·韦恩在福伦廷伯斯获胜，打通陆运道；韦恩在凯基翁加旧址修建韦恩堡，1795年《格林维尔条约》把这条联运道割给美国。1817年和1818年的后续条约又割让了堡垒周围其余土地。

en:
The lower Michigan peninsula runs between Lake Michigan and Lake Huron, its
southern prairies and oak openings cut by rivers that drain west into the
lake. In 1444 it is Algonquian country. The Bodewadmi, whom the French
called Potawatomi, hold the southwestern reaches as 'keepers of the fire',
youngest brother of the Council of Three Fires with the Ojibwe and Odawa;
Mascouten and Miami villages lie beyond. Their bands winter in bark-mat
lodges on the river bottoms, raising maize, beans and squash, spearing fish
through the ice and gathering wild rice and maple sugar with the seasons.
The Old Sauk Trail and other native tracks cross the peninsula, and the
beaver taken in its woods moves along them to the east.

The trails and the furs drew the French, but the Beaver Wars came first:
Iroquois raiders pushed the Bodewadmi west to Green Bay before the 1660s.
They drifted back after the Great Peace of 1701, the year Cadillac founded
Detroit, and their villages gathered beneath its walls and along the St.
Joseph River. French posts had already risen on that river: La Salle built
Fort Miami at its mouth in November 1679, and in 1691 a permanent Fort St.
Joseph went up on the lower river near present-day Niles, beside the ford
where the Old Sauk Trail crossed the Grand River Trail. Grown out of Claude
Allouez's Jesuit mission, the post anchored the southern Lake Michigan fur
trade among Potawatomi and Miami villages, its garrison only ten soldiers
with a blacksmith, a priest and an interpreter. The Bodewadmi fought beside
the French through the colonial wars, then turned on the British in
Pontiac's rising of 1763 and seized Fort St. Joseph, taking every frontier
post in the region except Detroit. In 1781 a Spanish raiding party captured
the fort and briefly claimed the St. Joseph River for Spain.
zh:
密歇根下半岛伸在密歇根湖与休伦湖之间，南部草原和橡树林地间分布着一条条向
西入湖的河流。1444年，这里是阿尔冈昆人的土地。博德瓦德米克人（法国人称波
塔瓦托米人）据有半岛西南部，自称「守火者」，是与奥吉布瓦人、奥达瓦人结成
的三火议会中的幼弟；更远处是马斯库滕人和迈阿密人的村庄。他们的居群在河畔
低地的树皮席小屋过冬，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，凿冰叉鱼，按季节采集野米、熬
制枫糖。索克古道等陆上小径纵贯半岛，林中猎得的河狸皮就沿这些小路向东外
运。

这些小径和毛皮引来的首先是法国人，但河狸战争先一步到来：1660年代以前，
易洛魁袭掠者已把博德瓦德米克人向西赶到格林贝。1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》
后，他们陆续东归，同年卡迪亚克建立底特律，博德瓦德米克人的村庄聚到城墙脚
下和圣约瑟夫河畔。法国人更早便在这条河上设点：1679年11月，拉萨尔在河口
修筑迈阿密堡；1691年，永久性的圣约瑟夫堡在下游今奈尔斯附近建成，就在索克
古道与格兰德河步道汇合的渡口旁。城堡从阿卢埃神父的耶稣会传教站发展而来，
守着密歇根湖南部的毛皮贸易，周围是博德瓦德米克人与迈阿密人的村庄，驻军不
过十名士兵，另配铁匠、神父和译员。历次殖民地战争中，博德瓦德米克人都与法
国并肩作战；1763年庞蒂亚克起兵，他们转而攻打英国人，攻克圣约瑟夫堡，湖区
边疆据点除底特律外尽数落入其手。1781年，一支西班牙突袭队攻下要塞，短暂宣
布圣约瑟夫河归西班牙所有。

en:
Michigami takes its name from the Anishinaabe word for the great lake at its western edge, but this province is the river country behind that shore: forest and oak openings drained west by the Grand River, called Owashtanong by the Odawa and later La Grande Rivière by the French. In 1444 its trails belong to the Anishinaabe lake world, where Bodéwadmi (Potawatomi) bands and Mascouten neighbours move between hunting camps and river-bottom fields. They raise maize, beans and squash, take sturgeon and whitefish, gather wild rice and maple sugar, and trap beaver.

The Beaver Wars of the mid-seventeenth century scattered the peninsula's villages, and by the late 1600s Odawa bands had settled the Grand River rapids at the later site of Grand Rapids. French voyageurs worked the lake-and-river route, yet the valley stayed Indigenous fur country: France ceded Michigan to Britain in 1763 and Britain handed its lower lake posts to the United States in 1796 without a settler town appearing here. In 1806 Joseph and Madeline La Framboise opened the first trading post in West Michigan, near where the Thornapple joins the Grand. Joseph was fatally stabbed that autumn by a Potawatomi, and Madeline, whose mother was Odawa and who spoke Odawa, Ojibwe, French and English, ran the business for more than a decade, holding her own even against John Jacob Astor's competition. By 1810 Chief Noonday's village at the rapids held about 500 Odawa; Noonday fought beside Tecumseh at the Thames in 1813. In 1821 the Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi signed the Treaty of Chicago and ceded the lands south of the Grand River to the United States.
zh:
密歇加米得名于阿尼什纳比语中对西边大湖的称呼；这个省份写的却是湖岸背后的河乡：林地与橡树草原之间，格兰德河向西汇水入湖。奥达瓦人称它奥瓦什塔农，法国人后来称它「大河」。1444年，这里的陆路属于阿尼什纳比人的大湖世界，波塔瓦托米游群与马斯库滕邻人往来于猎营和河畔田地之间。他们种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，捕捞鲟鱼和白鱼，按季节采集野米、熬制枫糖，并猎捕河狸。

17世纪中叶的河狸战争打散了下半岛村落；到17世纪末，奥达瓦游群已在格兰德河急流一带定居，地点就是后来大急流城的所在。法国船夫沿湖河航路往来，但河谷仍是原住民的毛皮之乡：法国1763年把密歇根割让给英国，英国1796年又把下游湖堡交给美国，这里都没有出现定居者的城镇。1806年，约瑟夫与马德琳·拉弗朗布瓦兹在山楂河汇入格兰德河处附近开设西密歇根第一座贸易站。同年秋天约瑟夫被一名波塔瓦托米人刺死，母亲为奥达瓦人的马德琳通晓奥达瓦语、奥吉布瓦语、法语和英语，独自把生意经营了十几年，连约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的竞争也没能把她挤走。到1810年，诺戴酋长在急流边的村庄约有五百名奥达瓦人；1813年诺戴随特库姆塞参加泰晤士河战役。1821年，奥达瓦人、奥吉布瓦人和波塔瓦托米人签订《芝加哥条约》，把格兰德河以南的土地割让给美国。

en:
Hotaawathipi is the northwestern Ohio country between the Maumee and Sandusky rivers, where oak ridges and prairie islands rise out of the Great Black Swamp and the water drains north to Lake Erie. Miami-speaking bands camped and planted maize on the higher ground, took fish and waterfowl from the marsh and beaver and deer from the woods, and followed river trails west to Kekionga, north to the lake and south into Shawnee country. In 1444 no European had entered the swamp; it was still a world of village councils, hunting grounds and old exchange paths.

Iroquois raids during the Beaver Wars made the Ohio Country a contested fur ground, and Miami bands returned only around 1700 with French backing. In the late 1730s a Wyandot band from Detroit settled on Sandusky Bay, where Nicholas Orontony founded Junundat, courted British traders and tried to raise an anti-French coalition, making him a forerunner of later Ohio leaders from Pontiac to Tecumseh. An English post built beside the bay in 1745 was the first European post in the Ohio Country, and the French put up one of their own a few years later. In May 1763 the Sandusky Wyandot seized the British Fort Sandusky at the start of Pontiac's War and killed most of its garrison; the town was burned in reprisal and the people moved upriver to Upper Sandusky. Native delegates met there in September 1783 to form the confederacy that fought the Northwest Indian War, until Anthony Wayne broke it at Fallen Timbers in 1794 and the Treaty of Greenville let American forts and farms into the country. The Treaty of Fort Meigs in 1817 confined the Wyandot to a reservation around Upper Sandusky.
zh:
霍塔瓦西皮是俄亥俄西北部莫米河与桑达斯基河之间的土地，橡树林高岗和草原洲从大黑沼泽中隆起，水流全都向北汇入伊利湖。操迈阿密语的群体在高地上扎营、种玉米，从沼泽获取鱼和水禽，从林中猎取河狸与鹿；河路西通凯基翁加，北达伊利湖，南入肖尼人地区。1444年时还没有欧洲人走进这片沼泽，这里仍是村落议事会、猎场和古老商路的世界。

河狸战争中易洛魁人的袭掠，使俄亥俄地区成为各方争夺的毛皮战场，迈阿密诸部约1700年才靠法国支持返回。1730年代末，一支怀安多特人从底特律迁居桑达斯基湾，首领尼古拉·奥龙托尼在那里建立朱嫩达特（Junundat），结交英国商人，又试图组织反法联盟，成为庞蒂亚克、特库姆塞等后来领袖的先声。1745年英国人在湾边设立的据点是俄亥俄地区第一座欧洲人商站，几年后法国人也建起自己的据点。1763年5月庞蒂亚克战争爆发时，桑达斯基的怀安多特人袭取英军桑达斯基堡，杀死大部分守军；村镇随即被报复焚毁，居民沿河上迁到上桑达斯基。1783年9月，原住民代表在上桑达斯基集会，组建后来投身西北印第安战争的联盟，直到安东尼·韦恩1794年在福伦廷伯斯将其击败，《格林维尔条约》使美国堡垒和农庄得以进入这一地区。1817年《梅格斯堡条约》把怀安多特人限制在上桑达斯基周围的保留地。

en:
Kentaientonga is the western Erie country around Presque Isle Bay, where a sandspit peninsula almost closes off one of the best anchorages on Lake Erie. Its Iroquoian villagers, the people the French called the Cat Nation after the wildcats of their woods, lived in palisaded towns, raised maize, beans and squash on the Erie Plain, and hunted deer and beaver in the forest behind the shore. Trails ran south from the bay to the Allegheny portages and the Ohio headwaters. In 1444 no European ship had entered the bay; the Erie still held every path along the lake.

War with the Haudenosaunee ended that. In the summer of 1654, after five days of retreat, about 2,000 Erie warriors with their women and children made a stand inside a hastily built palisade; 1,200 Seneca and Onondaga, many carrying Dutch muskets, came against them. The Erie loosed poisoned arrows so thick that the attackers held up canoes as shields and used them as ladders, but the palisade was carried, and by 1656 the Erie confederacy had ceased to exist, its surviving women and children adopted into Seneca and Onondaga families. French soldiers returned to the shore in 1753 and built Fort Presque Isle, the first post in the chain that ran south to Fort Duquesne; they burned it when Niagara fell in 1759. The British rebuilt it, and in June 1763 about 250 Ottawas, Ojibwas, Wyandots and Senecas closed around it. The sixty-man garrison held out for two days, surrendered on a promise of safe conduct to Fort Pitt, and was mostly cut down as it came out. Americans laid out the town of Erie on the bay, and in 1813 Oliver Hazard Perry built and fitted his squadron behind the sheltering peninsula. On 10 September his nine ships captured the whole British squadron on the lake, reopening the way to Detroit and to the battle that broke Tecumseh's confederacy.
zh:
肯泰恩通加是普雷斯克岛湾周围的伊利人西部土地，一道沙质半岛几乎把伊利湖上最好的锚地之一围合起来。住在栅栏村镇里的易洛魁语村民被法国人称为「猫族」，得名于他们林中众多的野猫；他们在伊利平原种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在湖岸后方林中猎鹿与河狸。小径从湖湾南通向阿勒格尼水陆联运道和俄亥俄河源。1444年时还没有欧洲船只进入这座湖湾，湖边的每条小路都掌握在伊利人手中。

终结这一切的是与豪德诺索尼的战争。1654年夏，约两千名伊利战士带着妇孺撤退五天后，在一道仓促修成的栅栏里死守；来攻的是一千二百名塞内卡人和奥农达加人，许多人拿着荷兰人的火枪。伊利人的毒箭射得极密，进攻者把独木舟顶在前面挡箭，又把它们当作云梯攀墙，但栅栏终被攻破；到1656年伊利联盟已不复存在，幸存的妇孺多被塞内卡和奥农达加家庭收养。1753年法军回到这片湖岸，修建普雷斯克岛堡，这是他们向南一直连到迪凯纳堡的堡垒链上第一座据点；1759年尼亚加拉陷落后，法军将它烧毁。英军重建此堡，1763年6月，约二百五十名渥太华、奥吉布瓦、怀安多特和塞内卡战士合围而来；六十名守军坚守两天，以获准撤往皮特堡为条件投降，出堡时大部分被杀。美国人在湾畔规划了伊利镇，1813年奥利弗·哈泽德·佩里在挡风的半岛背后建造并装备舰队；9月10日，他的九艘战舰在湖上俘获整支英国分舰队，重新打开通往底特律的道路，也通向击垮特库姆塞联盟的那场战役。

en:
Ohiyo is the upper Ohio's run through wooded hills where western Pennsylvania gives way to the Virginia frontier, the stretch later centred on Wheeling. In 1444 this was late Fort Ancient country, a river world that memory ties to the Shawnee. Bark-covered villages and maize fields occupied the fertile bottoms, and canoes carried shell, tobacco, furs and travellers between the Mississippi system and trails climbing toward the Alleghenies, while hunters took deer and turkey in the hills. No European had mapped the water the Seneca called Ohi:yo', the Good River.

Virginian parties crossed the Alleghenies into the valley in the 1670s and brought back the first reports of it. French claims followed: in 1749 Céloron de Blainville buried a lead plate at the mouth of Wheeling Creek to mark France's claim to the river. Britain won the Ohio Country soon afterwards, and the Treaty of Fort Stanwix drew the Ohio as the southern edge of Native territory, a line Virginia settlers crossed anyway. Ebenezer Zane had staked his claim on the Wheeling bottom when Fort Fincastle, soon renamed Fort Henry for Patrick Henry, was raised there in June 1774. Shawnee, Wyandot and Mingo fighters attacked it in September 1777, the fight in which Samuel McColloch, cut off outside the fort, rode his horse over a sheer bluff and escaped unhurt with the animal; the leap grew in retellings. They came back with Loyalist support in 1782, and when the garrison's powder ran low, Betty Zane ran to her brother's house nearby, carried a barrel of gunpowder back through the fire and kept the defence supplied. The Ohio became the southern boundary of the Northwest Territory after the war, and in 1818 the National Road reached Wheeling, linking the river landing with the Potomac.
zh:
俄亥俄（Ohiyo）指上俄亥俄河穿过林木丘陵的一段，即西宾夕法尼亚转入弗吉尼亚边疆之处，这一带后来以惠灵为中心。1444年时这里属于晚期堡古文化圈，是一片记忆中与肖尼人相联系的河上世界。树皮屋村落和玉米地占据肥沃河洲，独木舟载着贝壳、烟草、毛皮和旅人，往来于密西西比水系与通向阿勒格尼山脉的小路之间，猎人则在丘陵间猎鹿和火鸡。欧洲人还不曾测绘这条被塞内卡人称为俄希约（Ohi:yo'，意为「好河」）的大河。

1670年代，弗吉尼亚人翻过阿勒格尼山脉进入河谷，第一批关于这里的消息由他们带回。法国人的领属宣言随之而来：1749年，塞洛隆·德·布兰维尔在惠灵溪口埋下一块铅牌，标明这条河属于法国。英国不久赢得俄亥俄地区，《斯坦威克斯堡条约》把俄亥俄河划为原住民领地的南界，弗吉尼亚定居者照样越界。埃比尼泽·赞恩早已占下惠灵的河洲，1774年6月芬卡斯尔堡在那里动工，不久改名亨利堡，以帕特里克·亨利命名。1777年9月，肖尼、怀安多特和明戈战士攻打此堡，塞缪尔·麦卡洛被隔断在堡外，纵马跳下一道陡崖，人马均无伤；这次跳跃在流传中越说越险。1782年，他们在效忠派支援下再度来攻，守军火药将尽时，贝蒂·赞恩跑到附近兄长家中，抱回一桶火药穿过火线，使守军得以支撑。战后俄亥俄河成为西北领地的南界，1818年国家公路通到惠灵，把这个河港与波托马克河连在一起。

en:
Monacan country is the rolling Virginia piedmont between the falls of the James and the Blue Ridge. Its principal town Rassawek stood at the fork where the Rivanna joins the James, while Mowhemencho guarded the path upriver just above the falls. These Siouan-speaking farmers planted corn and beans on the bottoms, buried their dead in earthen mounds raised beside the towns, and handled the copper that moved along the upland trails. Below the falls the Algonquian Powhatan confederacy held the Tidewater and were their hereditary enemies; the Monacan shared the high ground with their kinsmen the Manahoac. In 1444 no European had yet crossed the falls.

Christopher Newport crossed them in November 1608 with forty Jamestown men, although the Pamunkey chief Parahunt had warned him that Monacan country meant war. The two towns he found, Massinacak and Mowhemencho, simply ignored the visitors, so his men seized a headman for a guide; one in the party thought the Monacan language sounded like Welsh. When John Lederer came that way in 1670 the same towns held only about thirty bowmen, and they now carried muskets. Their chief Surenough signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation after Bacon's Rebellion, and in 1700 Virginia settled Huguenot refugees on the old fields at Manakin. The remnant merged with the Nahyssan and Saponi, and as Tutelo-Saponi they were adopted by the Cayuga of the Iroquois League in 1753.
