Families netted mackerel and herring, took lobster and seal off shores marked by their shell middens, and hunted moose and caribou inland in season. The island was one half of the Mi'kma'ki district Epekwitk aq Piktuk, governed by local saqamaq and a women's council under the Grand Council, and part of the Wabanaki confederacy with the Wolastoqiyik, Passamaquoddy and Abenaki. In 1444 no European ship had entered the gulf.

Jacques Cartier sighted the island in late June 1534, on his first voyage, and in 1604 France claimed it with the rest of Acadia as Île Saint-Jean, a claim the Mi'kmaq never accepted. France kept it at Utrecht in 1713, when peninsular Nova Scotia passed to Britain, and in 1720 Port-la-Joye became a garrisoned seat of government for Acadian settlers; Jean Pierre Roma held a fishing and trading station at Three Rivers on the east coast. New Englanders out of newly taken Louisbourg burned both posts in 1745. The next summer a French and Mi'kmaq party surprised and routed some two hundred New Englanders foraging on the Hillsborough River. Acadians fleeing the expulsions in Nova Scotia then swelled the population to nearly five thousand.

After Louisbourg fell again, Colonel Andrew Rollo landed five hundred men in August 1758, built Fort Amherst above Port-la-Joye and deported most of the island's population. Three transports, the Violet, Duke William and Ruby, went down in the December crossing, drowning more than eight hundred people; the Duke William alone lost more than 360. Ceded to Britain in 1763, the island was surveyed into sixty-seven lots assigned by a London lottery in 1767, most of them to absentees. In 1769 it became the separate colony of St. John's Island, with the new town of Charlottetown as its capital, and in 1798 it was renamed Prince Edward Island for the Duke of Kent.
zh:
埃帕戈伊特格纳格（埃佩奎特克）的米克马克语名通常译作「浪涛摇荡的摇篮」。这是圣劳伦斯湾中一座地势低平、红土遍布的岛屿，与大陆只隔一道狭窄的诺森伯伦海峡，米克马克人又称它米尼古。人们在贝丘所在的岸边捕捞鲭鱼、鲱鱼、龙虾和海豹，当季再转入内陆猎取驼鹿和驯鹿。本岛是米克马克基七区之一「埃佩奎特克-皮克图」的一半，由各村酋长和妇女议事会在大议事会下治理，并与沃拉斯托基伊克人、帕萨马科迪人、阿布纳基人同属瓦巴纳基联盟。1444年，还没有欧洲船只驶入过这片海湾。

1534年6月底，雅克·卡蒂亚在第一次航行中望见此岛；1604年，法国把它与阿卡迪亚其余土地一并宣称占有，命名为圣让岛，米克马克人始终没有接受这一宣称。1713年《乌得勒支和约》后法国保住了该岛，而半岛上的新斯科舍落入英国之手；1720年，拉乔伊港成为驻有守军的法国治所，迁来阿卡迪亚移民，让·皮埃尔·罗马则在东岸三河经营一处渔栈和商站。1745年，从刚攻下的路易斯堡出发的新英格兰人把两处据点都烧毁。次年夏天，一支法军和米克马克人的队伍在希尔斯伯勒河畔奇袭并击溃约两百名征集给养的新英格兰士兵。随后，逃离新斯科舍驱逐行动的阿卡迪亚难民使岛上人口增至近五千人。

路易斯堡再度陷落后，安德鲁·罗洛上校于1758年8月率五百人登陆，在拉乔伊港上方修筑阿默斯特堡，把岛上大部分居民驱逐出境。维奥莱特号、威廉公爵号和鲁比号三艘运输船在12月的航程中沉没，溺亡者超过八百人，仅威廉公爵号就有三百六十多人丧生。1763年该岛正式割让给英国，经测绘分成六十七块份地，1767年在伦敦以抽签方式分配，大部分落入身在外地的业主之手。1769年它成为独立的圣约翰岛殖民地，以新建的夏洛特敦为首府，1798年为纪念肯特公爵改名为爱德华王子岛。

en:
Segepenegatic is the Mi'kmaq district of Sipekne'katik, the wooded centre of peninsular Nova Scotia, lying between the upper reaches of the Bay of Fundy and the deep sheltered water of Chebucto Bay, the harbour later called Halifax. Its name means a place rich in wapato, the water plant whose tubers grew in the wet ground of the Shubenacadie river country. Mi'kmaq families summered on the harbour for its fish and shellfish, moved inland for winter hunting, and their district chief sat in the councils of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444 this was a country of seasonal camps and canoe portages, without Acadian farms or European blockhouses.

Mission Sainte-Anne was opened on the Shubenacadie in 1699. After Port-Royal fell to a British siege in 1710 and Utrecht confirmed the peninsula to Britain, the mission became the meeting point of French and Mi'kmaq resistance in a country the British claimed but could not control. Jean-Louis Le Loutre, the priest who led the Acadian and Mi'kmaq war effort, arrived in 1738 and ran the station as chapel, supply point and raiding base. In 1746 the Duc d'Anville brought the largest French force yet sent across the Atlantic; storms and three months at sea left the ships crowded with sick men when they reached Chebucto, the duke died in the harbour, and the projected assault on Annapolis Royal came to nothing. British settlers founded Halifax beside the water in 1749, and through Father Le Loutre's War Mi'kmaq warriors canoeing down the Shubenacadie raided the new town and its outpost at Dartmouth. British troops burned Mission Sainte-Anne in October 1755, with the Acadian deportation already under way.
zh:
塞格佩内加蒂克是米克马克人的锡佩克内卡蒂克地区，位于新斯科舍半岛中部林地，一边通向芬迪湾上游，一边连着切布克托湾那片幽深的避风深水港，也就是后来哈利法克斯所在的港湾。地名意为瓦帕托丰生之地，这种水生植物的块茎长在舒贝纳卡迪河流域的湿地里。米克马克家族夏天在港湾捕鱼采贝，入冬转入内陆狩猎，地区酋长则参加米克马克基的议事会。1444年，这里只有季节性营地和独木舟搬运道，还没有阿卡迪亚农庄或欧洲人的堡垒。

1699年，圣安妮传教站在舒贝纳卡迪河畔设立。1710年皇家港被英军攻陷，《乌得勒支和约》又把半岛确认给英国，此后这座传教站便成了法国人与米克马克人抵抗活动的会合点：这片土地英国声称拥有，却无力控制。1738年，领导阿卡迪亚人和米克马克人作战的传教士让-路易·勒卢特尔来到这里，把传教站兼作礼拜堂、补给点和出击基地。1746年，昂维尔公爵率领法国迄今派过大西洋的最大一支舰队前来；风暴和三个月的海上颠簸使舰队驶入切布克托湾时满船病员，公爵本人死在港中，进攻安纳波利斯罗亚尔的计划也化为泡影。1749年，英国移民在港湾边建立哈利法克斯；勒卢特尔神父战争期间，沿舒贝纳卡迪河划独木舟而下的米克马克战士不断袭击这座新城和它在达特茅斯的前哨。1755年10月，阿卡迪亚大驱逐已经开始，英军焚毁了圣安妮传教站。

en:
The Petkootkweak, or Petitcodiac, runs through wooded ridges to Shepody Bay at the head of the Bay of Fundy and doubles back in a great right-angle bend, the elbow later called The Bend. Its tide is one of the sights of the Fundy shore: twice a day a wall of brown water roars upriver with a sound the Mi'kmaq heard as thunder, and Petkootkweak means ‘the river that bends like a bow’. The valley belonged to Siknikt, ‘the drainage place’, the south-eastern district of Mi'kma'ki, where families wintered near the headwaters, crossed by a carry over to the Shubenacadie, and took salmon, sturgeon and waterfowl from the river and its salt marshes; their kinsmen the Wolastoqiyik held the Saint John to the west. In 1444 the bay knew only that seasonal round.

Acadians from Port-Royal were the first settlers. In 1698 Pierre Thibodeau founded Chipoudie on Shepody Bay and Guillaume Blanchard opened Petitcoudiac; with Memramcook the three villages made up the Trois-Rivières, whose farmers dyked the marshes with aboiteaux and worked their way upriver to the elbow. They were the ‘neutral French’, who never swore the unconditional oath Britain demanded after Utrecht, and the collapse came with the Seven Years' War. After Fort Beauséjour fell in June 1755 Major Joseph Frye sailed up with two hundred militia to burn the Trois-Rivières. At Village-des-Blanchard, while his men set the church alight, Charles Deschamps de Boishébert fell on them with Acadians, Mi'kmaq and Maliseet; in three hours' fighting behind a dyke twenty-two militiamen were killed and six wounded, and Frye drew his men back to the boats. It was the first French success of the war in Acadia. Joseph Broussard, known as Beausoleil, kept up the partisan war on this river until 1758, while Boishébert led hundreds of homeless villagers to camps on the Miramichi, where famine thinned them through 1756–1758. Freed after the peace, Broussard led the first party of exiles to Louisiana in 1765, where the Acadians became the Cajuns. The next year eight families of Pennsylvania Germans, among them Heinrich Stief, settled the empty elbow as The Bend, the beginning of Moncton.
zh:
佩特库特奎阿克河（法国人写作Petitcoudiac，后作Petitcodiac）穿过林木丘陵，注入芬迪湾湾头的希波迪湾，在下游折出一个直角大弯，这个河弯后来被叫作「弯镇」。河口涌潮是芬迪湾畔的奇景：一天两次，一道黄褐色的水墙逆河而上，轰鸣如雷，米克马克人说的佩特库特奎阿克正是「弯如弓弦之河」的意思。河谷属于米克马克基东南的希格尼克特区，意为「排水之地」；氏族在河源一带过冬，经一条联运道通往舒贝纳卡迪河，又在河面和盐沼间捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼，猎取水鸟，西边圣约翰河上住着同族的沃拉斯托基伊克人。1444年，湾畔只有他们随季节来去的踪迹。

最先来定居的欧洲人是从罗亚尔港迁来的阿卡迪亚人。1698年，皮埃尔·蒂博多在希波迪湾畔建立希波迪村，纪尧姆·布朗沙尔开辟佩蒂特库迪亚克，二者与梅拉姆库克合称「三河」；村民用带泄洪闸的海塘围垦沼泽，农庄沿河上溯到河弯处。这些人是《乌得勒支和约》后仍不肯向英国无条件宣誓效忠的「中立法兰西人」，灭顶之灾随七年战争到来。1755年6月博塞茹尔堡陷落后，约瑟夫·弗莱少校率两百名民兵溯河而上焚毁三河；在布朗沙尔村，当兵丁放火烧村教堂时，夏尔·德尚·德·布瓦埃贝尔率领阿卡迪亚人、米克马克人和马勒西特人猛扑过来，隔着海塘打了三个钟头，民兵22人毙命、6人受伤，弗莱只得把队伍撤回船上。这是开战以来法国一方在阿卡迪亚的第一场胜仗。绰号「美阳」的约瑟夫·布鲁萨尔在这条河上坚持游击战到1758年；布瓦埃贝尔则把数百名无家可归的村民带往米拉米希的难民营，1756至1758年饥荒在营中蔓延。战后获释的布鲁萨尔于1765年率领第一批流亡者前往路易斯安那，迁去的阿卡迪亚人后来被称为卡津人。第二年，八户宾夕法尼亚德意志移民（其中有海因里希·施蒂夫一家）在空置的河弯处落脚，把此地叫作「弯镇」，蒙克顿就是在这片河弯上兴起的。

en:
Gespegeogag, 'the end of the land' in Mi'kmaq, is the wooded finger of the Gaspé Peninsula, where the Appalachian hills run into the Gulf of St. Lawrence around Gaspé Bay. In 1444 it was Mi'kmaq country: family bands summered on the bay and its offshore islands, fishing mackerel and salmon and taking seal and walrus, then moved inland after moose and caribou, their bark camps following the season. No European had yet charted the bay, and the first French sail arrived ninety years later.

On 24 July 1534 Jacques Cartier lost an anchor in a storm, put into the bay and raised a ten-metre wooden cross bearing the arms of Francis I and the words Vive le Roi de France, the first French taking of possession in what became Canada; before sailing home he took the two sons of Stadaconan chief Donnacona with him. For more than a century Europeans came only for the fishing season, spreading cod on the beach stones to dry, until Pierre Denys de la Ronde opened the first permanent fishing post in 1676. Around 1740 the whole peninsula held only about five hundred settlers, with Pabos its chief fishing post. In September 1758, after Louisbourg fell, Wolfe and Hardy sailed into the bay with nine ships and burned Gaspé, Grande-Rivière and Pabos, destroyed some two hundred fishing vessels and carried the fishermen off to France. The coast passed to Britain in 1760; Acadians escaping the expulsions and, after 1784, Loyalists settled its coves. Jersey merchant houses then ran most of the coast's cod trade, sending dry fish to the West Indies and bringing back rum, molasses and sugar.
zh:
盖斯佩盖奥加格在米克马克语里意为「陆地的尽头」，是加斯佩半岛林木覆盖的尖端，阿巴拉契亚丘陵在此伸入圣劳伦斯湾，山峦环抱出加斯佩湾。1444年，这里是米克马克人的土地：各家族群夏天在海湾和海岛上捕鲭鱼、鲑鱼，猎取海豹和海象，入冬转入内陆追逐驼鹿和驯鹿，树皮帐篷随季节搬移。此时还没有欧洲人测绘过这个海湾，第一面法国船帆要到九十年后才出现。

1534年7月24日，雅克·卡蒂亚在风暴中损失一只锚，停进加斯佩湾，在岸边竖起一根十米高的木十字架，上刻弗朗索瓦一世的纹章和「法兰西国王万岁」字样，这是法国在后来的加拿大第一次宣示占有；启航回国前，他还把斯塔达科纳酋长多纳科纳的两个儿子带走。此后一个多世纪，欧洲人只在渔季前来，把鳕鱼摊在海滩石上晾晒，直到1676年皮埃尔·德尼·德·拉龙德开设第一个常住渔业据点。1740年前后，整个半岛只有约五百名定居者，帕博是最大的渔业据点。1758年9月路易堡陷落后，沃尔夫和哈代率九艘船驶入海湾，焚毁加斯佩、格朗德里维耶尔和帕博，毁掉约两百艘渔船，把渔民掳往法国。1760年海岸归入英国，逃避大流放的阿卡迪亚人、1784年后又有效忠派，陆续在各个小湾安家。泽西岛商号随后把持了海岸鳕鱼贸易的大半，把干鱼运往西印度群岛，换回朗姆酒、糖蜜和蔗糖。

en:
Onguhiara takes its name from Onguiaahra, an Attiwandaron village on the Niagara River where water runs from Lake Erie toward Lake Ontario. In 1444 the Niagara Peninsula belonged to the Attiwandaron. French writers later called these Iroquoian villagers the Neutrals because they could deal with both the Wendat and the Haudenosaunee. Maize fields occupied the fertile lowland, deer were hunted in the surrounding woods, and furs and dressed deerskins moved along the river. The falls and gorge stopped through traffic, so canoe parties unloaded and carried their goods around the rapids. That portage and the river mouth gave a small village value out of proportion to its size.

Étienne Brûlé crossed the region around 1615, and the Récollet Joseph de La Roche Daillon wintered with a Neutral chief in 1626-1627. Epidemics and Haudenosaunee attacks dispersed the Neutral confederacy in 1651. France then tried to hold the river mouth with forts. La Salle built Fort Conti there in 1678 and Louis Hennepin visited the falls from the post; the Marquis de Denonville placed a hundred-man garrison on the site in 1687, but only twelve survived the winter before the stockade was pulled down. In 1720 Louis-Thomas Chabert de Joncaire obtained Seneca permission for the Magasin Royal trading post, and in 1726 Gaspard-Joseph Chaussegros de Léry built the machicolated stone house that became the core of Fort Niagara. The French enlarged the fort in 1755 and surrendered it to Sir William Johnson's British force in 1759.

During the American Revolution, Fort Niagara served British troops, Loyalist refugees and Seneca allies. The west-bank settlement founded as Butlersburg in 1781 became Newark, the first capital of Upper Canada in 1792. John Graves Simcoe moved the government to York in 1797 because Newark stood directly on the new border, and Fort George was built beside the town in 1796-1799. Isaac Brock was killed at Queenston Heights on 13 October 1812 while defeating an American crossing; Mohawk warriors led by John Norton fought in the British line. In 1813 Laura Secord walked out of American-held Niagara to warn a British post. American forces took Fort George in May, burned Niagara in December, and lost Fort Niagara to a British night attack on 19 December.
zh:
昂古希亚拉得名自阿蒂万达伦人的昂吉亚赫拉村；村庄位于尼亚加拉河畔，河水从伊利湖流向安大略湖。1444年，尼亚加拉半岛属于阿蒂万达伦人。后来的法兰西作者称这些说易洛魁语的村民为「中立人」，因为他们能同时与温达特人和豪德诺索尼人往来。肥沃低地上分布着玉米田，周围林地可供猎鹿，毛皮和鞣制鹿皮沿河运送。瀑布与峡谷切断直航水路，独木舟队必须卸货，绕过急流后再上船。这条转运道和河口使一座小村获得了远超其规模的价值。

艾蒂安·布吕莱约在1615年穿过这一地区；1626年至1627年冬，重整派修士约瑟夫·德·拉罗什·达永在一位中立人首领处过冬。疫病和豪德诺索尼人的进攻使中立联盟在1651年溃散。此后法兰西试图以要塞控制河口。1678年，拉萨尔在河口修建孔蒂堡，路易·亨内平从这座据点前往观看瀑布。1687年，德农维尔侯爵在当地派驻一百名守军，却只有十二人活过冬天，栅栏随后拆除。1720年，路易-托马·沙贝尔·德·容凯尔取得塞内卡人同意，设立王家商馆；1726年，加斯帕尔-约瑟夫·肖斯格罗·德·莱里建成一座带投石孔的石楼，后来成为尼亚加拉堡的核心。法兰西于1755年扩建堡垒，1759年又把它交给威廉·约翰逊爵士率领的英军。

美国独立战争期间，尼亚加拉堡为英军、效忠派难民和塞内卡同盟提供据点。西岸的定居点1781年初建时称巴特勒斯堡，后改称纽瓦克，1792年成为上加拿大第一个首府。约翰·格雷夫斯·西姆科因纽瓦克紧邻新划定的边界，于1797年把政府迁往约克；1796年至1799年，乔治堡建在城镇旁。1812年10月13日，艾萨克·布洛克在昆士顿高地击退美军渡河时阵亡，约翰·诺顿率领的莫霍克战士也在英军阵线中作战。1813年，劳拉·塞科德走出美军占领的尼亚加拉，向英军据点报警。美军5月攻占乔治堡，12月焚毁尼亚加拉，12月19日又在夜袭中丢掉尼亚加拉堡。

en:
Attignawantan was the country of the Bear People, the largest nation of the Wendat confederacy, on the wooded peninsula between Matchedash Bay and Nottawasaga Bay. Wendat farmers had moved north from Lake Ontario by the late thirteenth century. Their bark-covered longhouse villages stood behind palisades, with fields of maize, beans and squash beyond the hunt paths, and in the fifteenth century the Bear People joined their Cord neighbours to the southeast in the first Wendat league. By 1444 their peninsula was a settled western core of Wendake, tied to Algonquin fur routes that ran through Lake Nipissing to the Ottawa River.

Étienne Brûlé may have reached this country before 1615; that summer Samuel de Champlain and the Récollet Joseph Le Caron were at the Bear village of Carhagouha, where Le Caron said the first recorded Catholic mass in the Wendat country. Ossossané was the leading Wendat town of its day, and in 1636 Jean de Brébeuf watched the great Feast of the Dead there, a ceremony in which the bones of the dead were gathered and reburied in a common pit. Jesuits had worked among the Wendat since 1626, and in 1639 they raised the fortified mission of Sainte-Marie near the Bear village of Quieunonascaranas, the first European settlement in Ontario; the Bear nation then had thirteen villages. Measles and smallpox swept the towns from 1634 to 1640 and carried off between half and two-thirds of the Wendat.

In March 1649 Haudenosaunee raiders overran the villages of Saint-Ignace and Saint-Louis; Brébeuf and Gabriel Lalemant, seized at Saint-Louis, were tortured to death at Saint-Ignace. The French burned Sainte-Marie themselves rather than leave it to the raiders, and the survivors who wintered on Christian Island starved there before fleeing toward Quebec in 1650. Ojibwe families later hunted the emptied shore. A fur post opened on Matchedash Bay in the late 1770s, and the British treaties of 1785, 1798 and 1815 cleared the way for the Penetanguishene Road and the garrison at its end.
zh:
阿蒂格纳万坦是熊族之地。熊族是温达特联盟中最大的族群，住在马奇特达什湾与诺塔瓦萨加湾之间的林木半岛上。13世纪后期，温达特农人已从安大略湖北迁，树皮长屋的村落外筑着木栅，猎路尽头是玉米、菜豆和南瓜田。15世纪时，熊族和东南邻的绳族结成温达特最早的联盟。到1444年，这座半岛已是温达克定居的西部核心，连着取道尼皮辛湖通往渥太华河的阿尔冈昆毛皮商路。

艾蒂安·布吕莱可能在1615年以前就到过此地；同年夏天，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰和重整奥斯定会修士约瑟夫·勒卡龙在熊族村落卡尔加古阿（Carhagouha）驻足，勒卡龙在那里主持了温达克有记载的第一场天主教弥撒。奥索萨内是当时温达特首屈一指的村镇，1636年让·德·布雷伯夫在此观看盛大的亡者之宴，典礼上死者的遗骨被收集起来，合葬进同一座墓坑。耶稣会士1626年已开始在温达特人中传教，1639年他们在熊族村落基厄诺纳斯卡拉纳斯（Quieunonascaranas）附近建起设防的圣玛丽传教站，这是安大略第一处欧洲人定居点；当时熊族共有十三座村落。1634年至1640年，麻疹和天花横扫各镇，温达特人死去一半到三分之二。

1649年3月，豪德诺索尼战团攻陷圣伊尼亚斯和圣路易两村；布雷伯夫和加布里埃尔·拉勒芒在圣路易被俘，在圣伊尼亚斯被酷刑处死。法国人自己放火烧掉圣玛丽，不把它留给敌人；幸存者在克里斯蒂安岛过冬，大批饿死，1650年逃往魁北克方向。后来奥吉布瓦家族在空出的湖岸游猎。1770年代末马奇特达什湾开出一家毛皮站，英国1785年、1798年和1815年的条约修通佩内唐吉申道路，路的尽头驻下军队。

en:
Attigneenongnahac was the country of the Cord People, the Hatingeennonniahak, 'makers of cords for nets', one of the oldest nations of the Wendat confederacy. They lived on the well-drained rises of Mount St. Louis Ridge, between the Sturgeon and Coldwater rivers, where palisaded longhouse villages looked out over maize, bean and squash fields on the light upland soils. In the fifteenth century the Cord People and their Bear neighbours formed the first Wendat league, and by 1444 their ridge was the southeastern farming core of the confederacy, with tracks running west to Bear towns and east and south to other Iroquoian peoples.

When Champlain travelled through Wendake in 1615 the Cord were one of its four nations, and in 1640 three principal villages stood in their territory. Jesuits passed through in the 1630s, before the epidemics of 1634 to 1640 thinned the towns and the Haudenosaunee invasion of spring 1649 broke them. In summer 1650 more than 300 Wendat survivors reached Quebec under Father Paul Ragueneau; among the scattered groups, the Cord alone refused the next spring to move away from the protection of Fort Saint-Louis, and they became part of the Huron community that settled at Lorette. Their ridge was left largely empty; Ojibwe families later crossed it on their travels, and the British treaties of 1798 and 1815 opened the country around Penetanguishene and Lake Simcoe.
zh:
阿蒂格内农纳哈克是绳族之地。绳族温达特语称哈廷根农尼亚哈克（Hatingeennonniahak），意为「编网绳的人」，是温达特联盟中最古老的族群之一。他们住在斯特金河与科尔德沃特河之间圣路易斯岭排水良好的高地上，木栅环绕的长屋村外，是轻质壤土上的玉米、菜豆和南瓜田。15世纪时绳族与相邻的熊族结成温达克最早的联盟；到1444年，这片山岭已是联盟东南面的农耕核心，小路向西通往熊族村镇，向东、向南连接其他易洛魁语族群。

尚普兰1615年穿行温达克时，绳族已是联盟四大族群之一；1640年其境内有三座主要村落。耶稣会士1630年代经过这里，随后1634年至1640年的疫病削弱了各村，1649年春豪德诺索尼人入侵，将联盟击散。1650年夏，保罗·拉格诺神父带领三百多名温达特幸存者抵达魁北克；流散的各族群中，第二年春天唯有绳族不肯迁出圣路易堡的保护范围，他们后来成为定居洛雷特的休伦社群的一部分。绳族的山岭大体荒弃，后来只有奥吉布瓦家族往来经过；英国1798年和1815年的条约使佩内唐吉申与锡姆科湖一带开放。

en:
Maisouna covered the lower valley of the river later called the Saint-Maurice. Two islands split its mouth into three channels where it enters the St. Lawrence, and the French named the site Trois-Rivières, halfway between Quebec and Montreal. In 1444 Laurentian peoples farmed maize, beans and squash in longhouse villages along the bank, while Algonquian-speaking hunters moved through the forests and river crossings; later French records place the Maisouna between the villages of Stadacona and Hochelaga. Jacques Cartier stopped here in 1535 on his way upstream and planted a cross on Île Saint-Quentin, and when French traders returned around 1600 the Laurentian villages had vanished.

The Sieur de Laviolette founded the permanent post in 1634, the second town in New France after Quebec, and Saint-Maurice pelts made it the fur market between Quebec and Montreal. Mohawk raiding kept the palisaded town under arms: in 1652 a war party seized the young Pierre-Esprit Radisson outside the walls and carried him into Iroquoia, where a Mohawk family adopted him. He made his way back after nearly two years, and with his brother-in-law Médard des Groseilliers he reached Lake Superior before any other Europeans and helped found the Hudson's Bay Company. The raiding wars ended with the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In 1730 the Forges du Saint-Maurice opened upstream, the first successful ironworks in New France, turning local ore into pots, stoves and ironware. After the British conquest of 1760 an American invasion ended in the marshes outside the town, when a local farmer led General Thompson's Continentals off the road on 8 June 1776; the British scattered them and took Thompson prisoner in the last battle fought on Quebec soil.
zh:
迈索纳位于后来得名圣莫里斯河的下游。河口被两座岛屿分作三道水口注入圣劳伦斯河，法国人把这里取名三河城，地处魁北克与蒙特利尔之间。1444年，劳伦提亚人在河畔的长屋村落里种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，阿尔冈昆语猎人则穿行于森林和渡口；后来的法国文献把迈索纳人置于斯塔达科纳与奥谢拉加两个村落之间。1535年，雅克·卡蒂埃溯河上航途中在此停留，在圣康坦岛竖起十字架；等到法国商人1600年前后重返，劳伦提亚人的聚落已经消失。

1634年，拉维奥莱特老爷在此建立永久据点，这是新法兰西继魁北克之后的第二座城镇，圣莫里斯河的毛皮使它成为魁北克与蒙特利尔之间的毛皮市场。莫霍克人的袭掠让这座栅栏城镇常年戒备：1652年，一支战队在墙外掳走少年皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松，把他带往莫霍克地界，由一户人家收养。近两年后他设法归来，随后与连襟梅达尔·德·格罗塞耶成为最早抵达苏必利尔湖的欧洲人，并参与创立哈德逊湾公司。1701年，《蒙特利尔大和平》结束了漫长的袭掠战争。1730年，圣莫里斯锻铁厂在河流上游开办，是新法兰西第一座成功运营的铁厂，把当地铁矿铸成锅具、炉灶和铁器。1760年英国征服后，美军的入侵在城外沼泽中告终：1776年6月8日，一名当地农夫把汤普森将军的大陆军领离道路，英军将其击溃并俘虏汤普森，这也是魁北克土地上的最后一场战斗。

en:
Lake Nipissing is a broad, shallow water between the Ottawa River and Georgian Bay, emptying into Lake Huron through the French River. Two great canoe routes met on the lake: by the Mattawa and Ottawa a traveller reached the St Lawrence and the French towns, while the French River led west to Huronia and the upper lakes. The Nipissing, an Anishinaabe people of Ojibwe and Algonquin kin, kept villages on its shores and islands, took sturgeon from its shoals and passed the northern forests' furs along that corridor. Their medicine men so impressed the first French visitors that maps long marked the water as Lac des Sorciers, the Lake of Sorcerers. In 1444 no European had yet entered their country.

Étienne Brûlé, travelling with Huron bands, was the first European to reach the lake about 1610, and Samuel de Champlain crossed it in 1615 on his way to Huronia. Jean Nicolet ran a cabin and trading house on the shore through the 1620s, and the Jesuit Claude Pijart spent nine years among the Nipissing and gathered a small Christian flock. In 1649–1650 the Iroquois overran the country, and the Nipissing fled with the Amikwa all the way to Lake Nipigon, where Claude Allouez found them in 1667; within a few years they were back on their own lake. Voyageurs then made the crossing a link on the Montreal fur road, and around 1780 the North West Company raised Fort La Ronde on the shore. The post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company with the merger of 1821.
zh:
奥迪什夸加米格，即尼皮辛湖地区，湖泊宽阔而水浅，地处渥太华河与乔治亚湾之间，湖水经弗伦奇河注入休伦湖。两条独木舟大水道在湖上相接：走马塔瓦河、渥太华河可抵圣劳伦斯河上的法国人市镇，走弗伦奇河则西通休伦尼亚和上游诸湖。湖畔居民是尼皮辛人，一支兼有奥吉布瓦与阿尔冈昆渊源的阿尼什纳贝人，村落在湖岸和岛上，在浅滩捕捞鲟鱼，把北方森林的毛皮沿这条走廊转销出去；他们的巫师给最初的法国来客留下极深印象，以致此后多年地图上都把此湖标作「巫师湖」。1444年，欧洲人还没有进入他们的地界。

1610年前后，随休伦人队伍游历的艾蒂安·布吕莱成为第一个见到此湖的欧洲人；1615年，萨米埃尔·德·尚普兰在前往休伦尼亚的途中渡过此湖。让·尼科莱在1620年代常驻湖畔经营木屋商馆，耶稣会士克洛德·皮雅尔则在尼皮辛人中待了九年，聚集起一小群信徒。1649至1650年，易洛魁人攻破这片地方，尼皮辛人随阿米克瓦人一直逃到尼皮贡湖，克洛德·阿卢埃1667年在那里找到了他们；没过几年，他们已回到自己的湖边。后来的船夫把这段水路当作通往蒙特利尔毛皮干道上的一站，1780年前后西北公司在湖畔建起拉龙德堡；1821年两家公司合并，这座贸易站归入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
The Weskarini, Wàwàckeciriniwak, the 'people of the deer' in Algonquin, were the band the French called La Petite Nation, the Little Nation, to set them apart from the Kichesipirini of the upper Ottawa. Their hunting grounds ran along the north bank of the Ottawa and up the Lièvre, Rouge and Petite-Nation rivers, the last of them named for the band. The Ottawa was the main canoe route from the St. Lawrence settlements to the upper Great Lakes, and Weskarini beaver pelts went down it to French traders; in season they hunted, fished and gathered across the Laurentian valleys. Deep in their country rose the forested mountain they called Manitonga Soutana, the mountain of the spirits, which they said rumbled and moved underfoot, and the French named Mont Tremblant, the trembling mountain. In 1444 these valleys belonged to the Weskarini alone, and no European canoe had yet entered the Ottawa.

Champlain met Weskarini bands on his way up the river in 1613, and they became French allies, trading at the river mouths and wintering with their Wendat friends. The Beaver Wars ended that life: when the Haudenosaunee struck in 1654 the main band was cut to pieces in the hills near Mont Tremblant, and survivors fled toward Trois-Rivières, where the Jesuits sheltered only those who accepted baptism. By the later seventeenth century the Weskarini no longer appear as a people, their kin merged into other Algonquin communities. On 16 May 1674 the French West India Company granted the emptied country as the seigneury of La Petite-Nation, the westernmost seigneury in New France, to François de Laval, bishop of Quebec. Laval planned an Algonquin mission there, gave it up, and passed the grant to the Séminaire de Québec in 1680. Joseph Papineau bought the estate in 1801 and 1803, put a sawmill on the river and brought in New England lumbermen, and in 1817 it passed to his son Louis-Joseph.
zh:
韦斯卡里尼人自称瓦瓦克齐里尼瓦克，阿尔冈昆语意为「鹿族」；法国人称他们为「小民族」（La Petite Nation），以区别于渥太华河上游的基奇西皮里尼人。他们的猎场沿渥太华河北岸展开，深入列夫尔河、鲁日河和小民族河流域，小民族河便因他们得名。渥太华河是圣劳伦斯河畔定居点通往五大湖上游的主要独木舟水路，韦斯卡里尼人的海狸皮顺河而下卖给法国商人，他们又按季节在劳伦琴山谷中狩猎、捕鱼、采集。领地深处矗立着林木覆盖的山峰，他们称作马尼通加·苏塔纳，即神灵之山，相传山体会发出轰鸣、在脚下晃动，法国人因而叫它蒙特朗布朗，意为「颤抖的山」。1444年时，这些山谷只属于韦斯卡里尼人，还没有欧洲人的独木舟进入渥太华河。

1613年，尚普兰溯河而上时遇见韦斯卡里尼游群，他们后来成为法国盟友，在各条河口贸易，与交好的温达特人一同过冬。海狸战争终结了这种生活：1654年豪德诺索尼人来袭，主体队伍在蒙特朗布朗附近的山里被击溃，幸存者逃向三河市，耶稣会只收留接受洗礼的人。到17世纪后期，韦斯卡里尼作为一个族群不再见于记载，余部并入其他阿尔冈昆社群。1674年5月16日，法国西印度公司把这片空地封给魁北克主教方济各·德·拉瓦尔，是为新法兰西最西端的「小民族领地」。拉瓦尔原想在此设立阿尔冈昆传教站，后来作罢，1680年将领地转给魁北克神学院。约瑟夫·帕皮诺1801年和1803年买下产业，在河上建起锯木厂，招来新英格兰伐木工人；1817年产业传给儿子路易-约瑟夫。

en:
The island beneath Mount Royal lies where the Ottawa River joins the St.
Lawrence, just short of the Lachine Rapids; Osheaga, its Iroquoian name,
means the 'big rapids'. The rapids end ocean navigation, so goods moving
between the Atlantic and the upper Great Lakes must change vessel here. In
1444 St. Lawrence Iroquoians work one of the river's richest fisheries and
tend maize, beans and squash around stockaded villages of bark-covered
longhouses. Hochelaga, girdled by its palisade on the slope of the mountain,
is the greatest of these towns.

Jacques Cartier landed on 2 October 1535 while searching for a route to
Asia, visited Hochelaga the next day and named the hill above it Mount
Royal. When Champlain came in 1603 the Iroquoian villages were gone, emptied
by warfare and dispersal. He laid out a fur post below the rapids in 1611,
and in 1642 Maisonneuve founded Ville-Marie on the island, where Jeanne Mance
ran the Hotel-Dieu hospital from the first year. For decades the settlers
lived behind palisades under Iroquois attack; in 1689 raiders destroyed the
village of Lachine a short way upstream. Holding the head of the canoe
route, Ville-Marie became the warehouse of the western fur trade, and
Jolliet, La Salle and the Verendryes all outfitted here before pushing into
the continent. In August 1701 some 1,300 indigenous delegates gathered on
the shore to conclude the Great Peace of Montreal with the French, burying
hatchets and exchanging wampum belts. Stone walls later ringed the town,
which served as France's military headquarters in the colonial wars; after
Quebec fell, Vaudreuil surrendered it to Amherst on 8 September 1760. Under
British rule the North West Company made Montreal its base, and its
voyageurs carried the fur trade far into the western interior.
zh:
皇家山下的岛屿坐落在渥太华河注入圣劳伦斯河之处，上游不远处便是拉欣急流，易
洛魁语地名「奥谢阿加」意为「大急流」。急流拦住了海船的去路，大西洋与上游
五大湖之间的一切货物都要在此换船。1444年，圣劳伦斯易洛魁人在河上经营全流
域最丰饶的渔场，在木栅环绕的树皮长屋村外种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，奥什拉加便
是其中最大的村镇，木栅顺皇家山坡而建。

1535年10月2日，为寻找通往亚洲水道而溯河上行的雅克·卡蒂埃登岛，次日进入
奥什拉加，把村旁的山丘命名为皇家山。1603年尚普兰再来时，这些易洛魁村庄已
在战乱与流徙中消失。1611年，他在急流脚下辟出毛皮贸易站「皇家广场」；1642
年，迈松纳夫在岛上建立维尔马利，让娜·芒斯从第一年起便在此主持主宫医院。
此后数十年，居民在木栅后抵挡易洛魁人的攻袭，1689年上游不远的拉欣村即遭摧
毁。扼守独木舟航路起点的维尔马利成了西部毛皮贸易的货栈，若利埃、拉萨尔和
拉韦朗德里等探险家都在此置办装备，再深入大陆。1701年8月，约一千三百名原住
民代表聚到岸边，与法国人缔结《蒙特利尔大和约》，埋葬战斧、交换贝壳珠带。
小镇后来环以石墙，在殖民地战争中充当法国的军事指挥中心；魁北克陷落后，沃
德勒伊于1760年9月8日向阿默斯特投降。英国治下，西北公司以蒙特利尔为基地，
它的船夫把毛皮贸易一直带到西部内陆深处。

en:
Stadacona stood where the St. Lawrence narrows between Cape Diamant and the heights opposite, which the Algonquin called Kebec, 'where the river narrows'. The St. Lawrence Iroquoian town stood on the Saint-Charles behind maize fields; their word for a village, kanata, later gave Canada its name. Cliff and narrows made it the strongest fortress site on the river, which every fleet bound inland had to pass. In 1444 no European sail had yet entered the gulf, and the river belonged to such towns.

Jacques Cartier wintered here from September 1535; scurvy killed a quarter of his men until the Stadaconans showed him annedda, a white-cedar brew that cured the rest. In May 1536 he carried chief Donnacona and his two sons to France, and none returned. He returned in August 1541 with five ships and founded Charlesbourg-Royal on the Cap-Rouge, France's first North American settlement, abandoned in June 1543. When Champlain reached the narrows, the town had vanished in war and disease, and only Innu and Algonquin bands still fished eel there. Champlain built his Habitation beneath the cape on 3 July 1608; the Kirkes seized it in 1629, France got it back in 1632, and he died there in 1635.

Quebec became capital of royal New France in 1663 and a bishop's see in 1674; Augustinian nuns arriving in 1639 ran the Hôtel-Dieu, the first hospital north of Mexico. When Phips demanded its surrender in 1690, Frontenac answered with 'the mouth of my cannons' and beat him off. In 1759 Wolfe's men climbed the heights by night; on 13 September they beat Montcalm on the Plains of Abraham in about an hour, both generals mortally wounded; the city surrendered five days later. Lévis won at Sainte-Foy in April 1760 but failed to retake the city; France ceded Canada in 1763. The Quebec Act of 1774 let the French keep faith and law; the American New Year's Eve assault of 1775 died with Montgomery in the snow, and the siege ended in May 1776. Quebec became capital of Lower Canada in 1791, and early in the next century it was North America's third-largest port, crowded with timber ships.
zh:
斯塔达科纳坐落在圣劳伦斯河骤然收窄之处，钻石角与对岸高地夹水而立，阿尔冈昆语称此地为凯贝克（Kebec），意即「河流变窄之处」。这座圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的城镇在圣夏尔河畔，镇外是玉米田；他们表示村庄的词「卡纳塔」（kanata）后来成了加拿大的国名。峭壁加窄水，使这里成为整条河上最险固的要塞，所有深入内陆的船队都必须从崖下经过。1444年时，欧洲人的船帆还没有驶入海湾，大河属于这样的村镇。

1535年9月起，雅克·卡蒂亚在城边过冬，坏血病夺走他四分之一的人手，直到镇民教他用白雪杉熬制安内达（annedda）汤剂，其余人才被治愈。1536年5月，他把酋长多纳科纳和他的两个儿子带回法国，三人均未生还。1541年8月，他率五艘船重返此地，在卡普鲁日筑起法国在北美的第一个定居点皇家夏尔堡，1543年6月即被放弃。尚普兰抵达窄峡时，此城已毁于战争和疫病，只有因努和阿尔冈昆游群还来捕鳗。尚普兰1608年7月3日在钻石角下建起「居所」；柯克兄弟1629年夺城，法国1632年将其收回，他1635年在此去世。

1663年魁北克成为王家新法兰西的首府，1674年成为主教区；奥古斯丁修女会1639年抵达，她们主持的主宫医院是墨西哥以北的第一所医院。1690年菲普斯要守军投降，弗龙特纳克答以「我大炮的炮口」，将其击退。1759年，沃尔夫的部队乘夜攀上高地，9月13日约一小时内在亚伯拉罕平原击败蒙卡尔姆，两人均伤重而死，城市五天后投降。莱维1760年4月在圣福瓦取胜，却未能夺回城市；1763年法国割让加拿大。1774年《魁北克法案》保住法裔的信仰与法律；1775年新年前夜美军的强攻随蒙哥马利死在雪里，围城于1776年5月收场。1791年魁北克成为下加拿大首府，19世纪初已是北美第三大港，挤满运木材的船。

en:
Toutouskak is the bay the French called Tadoussac, where the dark water of the Saguenay fjord meets the St. Lawrence estuary. In 1444 it was summer ground of the Innu, whom the French later named the Montagnais: they camped on the shore to hunt seal and meet the canoes that came down the Saguenay with furs. Jacques Cartier stopped there in 1535 and found their sealing parties on the beach. By the end of the century Basque whalers flensed their catch on the strand and boiled the blubber into oil, while every summer more than a thousand Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin gathered to barter beaver pelts with the European ships. They held back from the first captain to arrive and waited for rival bidders to push the price up, and by 1600 this was the busiest fur market in North America.

In 1600 Pierre de Chauvin and François Gravé Du Pont, holding Henri IV's fur monopoly, built a trading house at the river mouth; sixteen men wintered and only five survived, but Tadoussac became France's first lasting settlement in Canada. At a solemn summer feast in 1603 Gravé and Champlain made alliance with the Innu, Algonquin and Etchemin. In 1608 Basque captains answered Gravé's monopoly claims with cannon fire and wounded him before Champlain arranged a truce. Récollet friars opened a mission in 1615, and for thirty years Tadoussac was the only seaport on the St. Lawrence. Settlers whaled out of the bay from 1632, and the small mission chapel raised in 1747 served the post for the rest of the French regime.
zh:
塔杜萨克（因努语称图图斯卡克）位于萨格奈峡湾深色江水与圣劳伦斯河口湾相接之处。1444年，这里是因努人（法国人后称蒙塔涅人）的夏日之地：他们在岸边扎营捕猎海豹，接应从萨格奈河载着毛皮顺流而下的独木舟。1535年卡蒂亚途经此地，见到的正是捕海豹的因努人。到16世纪末，巴斯克捕鲸人在海滩上解剖鲸尸、熬炼鲸油，每年夏天还有上千名因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人聚集于此，用河狸皮同欧洲商船交易。他们不肯把头货卖给最先到的船长，专等几艘船竞相出价、把价钱抬高；到1600年，这里已是北美最繁忙的毛皮市场。

1600年，持亨利四世毛皮垄断权的皮埃尔·德·肖万与弗朗索瓦·格拉韦·迪蓬在河口建起贸易屋；十六人留下过冬，仅五人生还，塔杜萨克却就此成为法国在加拿大第一个延续下来的定居点。1603年夏天，迪蓬与尚普兰在一场隆重的宴会上同因努人、阿尔冈昆人和埃切明人结盟。1608年，巴斯克船长们用炮火回应迪蓬的垄断要求、将他击伤，最后由尚普兰谈成休战。1615年方济各重整派修士开设传教点；此后三十年，塔杜萨克是圣劳伦斯河上唯一的海港。1632年起，定居者从湾口出航捕鲸，1747年又建起一座传教小教堂。

en:
The Oumamiwek were the western of the two Montagnais bands that summered around Uashat, the great bay the French would call Sept-Îles; their own coast ran west past the mouth of the Sainte-Marguerite. Each spring families came down from the inland forests to spear salmon in the rivers, take seal in the bay and harpoon whale offshore, then turned back upcountry for the winter caribou hunt through the land they called Nitassinan. By 1444 Basque whalers had begun sailing these waters each season, but the shore itself held no European house or post, and the year still followed the Innu round.

Jacques Cartier entered Uashat in August 1535 and charted the seven islands as the Ysles Rondes, finding Basque fishermen already at anchor. Samuel de Champlain stopped off the Sainte-Marguerite in 1603; the Jesuit Jean de Quen opened the Ange-Gardien mission on the bay in 1651, and the merchant François Bissot set up a fur post there in 1661. The coast's place in European records was fixed by a disaster. On 22 August 1711 Admiral Hovenden Walker's expedition against Quebec, short of pilots and sound charts and feeling its way through fog, was driven onto the Île-aux-Œufs reefs west of the bay. Seven troopships and a storeship broke up, and 890 soldiers, sailors and women drowned, one of the worst naval disasters in British history; the headland facing the reefs was named Pointe-aux-Anglais, the English Point. The Sept-Îles post was later run by the North West Company and passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821.
zh:
奥马米韦克人是在乌阿沙特大海湾（法国人后来称之为七岛）度夏的两支蒙塔涅人中偏西的一支，其海岸向西越过圣玛格丽特河口。每年春天，各家从内陆森林来到海边，在河里叉鲑鱼、在湾中捕海豹、在外海标鲸，入冬再溯河返回他们称作尼塔希南的故地猎驯鹿。到1444年，巴斯克捕鲸船已开始逐季驶来这片水域，但岸上没有一间欧洲人的房屋或商站，一年的作息仍循着因努人的老节律。

1535年8月，雅克·卡蒂亚驶入乌阿沙特，把七座岛屿绘作圆岛，而且发现已有巴斯克渔民在湾中锚泊。1603年，尚普兰在圣玛格丽特河外停留；1651年耶稣会士让·德康在湾畔创立守护天使传教所，1661年商人弗朗索瓦·比索又在此开设毛皮站。让这段海岸写进欧洲记载的，是一场浩劫。1711年8月22日，海军上将霍文登·沃克远征魁北克，舰队缺少领航员和可靠海图，在浓雾中摸索前行，被风浪推上湾西的蛋岛礁群。七艘运兵船和一艘补给船碎裂，八百九十名士兵、水手和随船妇女溺亡，是英国历史上最惨重的海难之一；正对礁群的海角得名英格兰角。七岛商站后来由西北公司经营，1821年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Chisedec was the name later given to the Innu band of Uashat, the great bay that became Sept-Îles, and Mishta-shipu, the Moisie River, the Great River in their language. It runs 410 kilometres south through spruce and birch forest to the Gulf of St Lawrence, its strong current broken by rapids, and ranks among the finest salmon and trout waters in eastern North America. In 1444 its people, whom the French later called Montagnais, moved between the coast and the boreal interior in portable skin tents, taking salmon and seals in season and following caribou and moose through Nitassinan, their homeland. No European mission or trading post stood on the bay.

Jacques Cartier sailed past the islands in 1535 and left the first written record of them as the Ysles Rondes, the Round Islands; he met Basque fishermen already crossing every year for cod and whales, and named the Moisie the River of Horses. Fishing and furs drew the French to the anchorage. The Jesuit Jean de Quen founded the L'Ange-Gardien mission in 1650, fur traders opened a post soon after, and Louis Jolliet, back from mapping the Mississippi with Jacques Marquette, set up another in 1679. Chisedec hunters were drawn into New France's commerce and its wars against the English and the Haudenosaunee. After Britain took Canada in 1763, the North West Company took over the Sept-Îles post in 1802; in 1821, with the merger into the Hudson's Bay Company, the bay became a company post.
zh:
切斯迪克是后来文献对一支因努人群的称呼，他们住在乌阿沙特大湾与米什塔希普大河一带；前者日后成为七岛，后者即穆瓦西河，因努语意为「大河」。穆瓦西河全长410公里，穿过云杉与桦木林地南流入圣劳伦斯湾，水流湍急、险滩相接，是北美东部最好的鲑鱼和鳟鱼河流之一。1444年，这些后来被法国人称作蒙塔格奈人的居民带着可搬运的兽皮帐篷，在海岸与北方森林内陆间往返，渔季捕捞鲑鱼和海豹，狩猎季在故土尼塔希南内追逐驯鹿与驼鹿。那时海湾边还没有欧洲传教站或贸易栈。

1535年，雅克·卡蒂埃驶过群岛，首次留下文字记载，称之为「圆岛」；他遇到年年横渡大西洋而来的巴斯克渔民在此捕鳕和捕鲸，又把穆瓦西河命名为「马河」。渔业和毛皮把法国人吸引到这个锚地。1650年，耶稣会士让·德·康创立「守护天使」传教站，毛皮商人随后也开了贸易栈；曾随雅克·马凯特测绘密西西比河的路易·若列，在1679年另设一处。切斯迪克猎人也被卷入新法兰西的商业，以及它同英格兰人和易洛魁联盟的战争。1763年英国夺取加拿大后，西北公司于1802年接掌七岛贸易栈；1821年西北公司并入哈德逊湾公司，海湾边的据点成为公司商栈。

en:
Qikirmiut takes its name from the Qikirtamiut, the Inuit islanders of the Belcher Islands, some 1,500 treeless islands spread across the south-eastern corner of Hudson Bay. Dorset hunters lived here between 500 BCE and 1000 CE, and Thule people arrived between 1200 and 1500. In 1444 their Inuit descendants travelled by kayak and umiak among the islands and sea ice, taking seals and walrus, Arctic char and beluga, eiders and caribou; the islands bear only willow scrub and tundra, and no European chart or boundary had yet reached them.

Henry Hudson sighted the archipelago in 1610, and in 1670 Charles II's Hudson's Bay charter folded it on paper into Rupert's Land; the Europeans who later mapped it probably gave the islands the name of an early company captain, James Belcher. The Anglo-French wars for the bay were fought elsewhere, around the Nelson and Albany rivers, and no company post or mission was built on the Belchers during this period, so the islanders kept to their seasonal rounds on ice and open water. Early in the nineteenth century the island caribou herds disappeared, and the Qikirtamiut made their winter clothing from the down of the eider ducks nesting on their shores.
zh:
基蒂克美奥特得名自基基尔塔米乌特人，即贝尔彻群岛的因纽特岛民。约一千五百个没有树木的岛屿散布在哈得孙湾东南角，岛上只有柳树灌丛和苔原，不成林木。多塞特人在公元前500年至公元1000年间居住于此，1200年至1500年间图勒人来到群岛。1444年，他们的因纽特后裔乘皮艇和木架皮舟往来于岛屿与浮冰之间，猎捕海豹、海象、北极红点鲑、白鲸、欧绒鸭和驯鹿；欧洲人的海图和边界都还没有延伸到这里。

亨利·哈德逊1610年望见这座群岛；1670年查理二世颁发哈得孙湾公司特许状，在纸面上把它划入鲁伯特地。后来绘制地图的欧洲人大概以公司早年的船长詹姆斯·贝尔彻为群岛命名，一说为海军将领爱德华·贝尔彻。英法争夺海湾的战争都在别处进行，战场围绕纳尔逊河和奥尔巴尼河；整个这一时期没有公司商栈或传教站建在贝尔彻群岛，岛民依旧依季节在冰面和开阔水域间往来营生。19世纪初，岛上的驯鹿群消失，基基尔塔米乌特人便用在海岸筑巢的欧绒鸭的绒羽缝制冬衣。

en:
Cisasipi is a spelling of Cisâsîpî, 'Great River', the East Cree name for the La Grande and for the country around its mouth on the rocky eastern shore of James Bay. In 1444 no Atlantic ship had yet entered the bay, and East Cree families kept a seasonal round: summer fishing camps on the coast, autumn goose hunts over the shore flats, winter trapping and caribou hunting in the inland forest. The rivers were the only roads, frozen solid for months each year.

Henry Hudson sailed into James Bay in 1610, and after the Nonsuch's fur voyage of 1668 Charles II granted the Hudson's Bay Company a charter over the whole bay. The Company's ships bought beaver at the river mouths without going inland, but this East Main shore was the one coast it could never close off: French and independent traders came overland from the Saint Lawrence and met the Cree canoes before they reached Company posts. The HBC did not build on the Great River until 1803, when it put up Fort George near the mouth. Cree hunters carried pelts to the post, yet in 1821 most families still wintered inland rather than settling beside it.
zh:
奇萨西比（Cisasipi）是克里语Cisâsîpî的异写，意为「大河」，东克里人用它称呼拉格朗德河以及詹姆斯湾岩石东岸河口一带的土地。1444年，尚无来自大西洋的船只驶入海湾，东克里家族按季节往来：夏天在海边营地捕鱼，秋天到岸滩猎雁，冬天进内陆森林设陷阱、猎驯鹿。河流是唯一的通路，一年里有好几个月河面封得严严实实。

1610年，亨利·哈德逊驶入詹姆斯湾；1668年诺萨奇号毛皮航行获利后，查理二世颁发特许状，把整个海湾交给哈得孙湾公司经营。公司的船停在各河口收购河狸皮，不深入内陆，但东岸这片「东梅因」海岸是它始终封锁不住的一段：法国商人和独立商人从圣劳伦斯方向由陆路赶来，在克里人的独木舟抵达公司商站前就截下了毛皮。公司直到1803年才在大河口附近建起乔治堡。克里猎手把毛皮送到堡中，可到1821年，多数家族仍旧进内陆过冬，没有在商站旁定居。

en:
Iyiyiw is a spelling of iiyiyuu, 'human being', the name the East Cree, or Eeyou, give themselves. Their taiga-and-lake country southeast of James Bay is part of Eeyou Istchee; its canoe routes run by the Eastmain and Rupert rivers to Lake Mistassini, 'big rock' in Cree, the great lake of the interior. In 1444 there was neither town nor fixed border here: families summered by the lakes taking fish and waterfowl, then scattered to inland hunting grounds for caribou, beaver and marten. Cree and Innu travellers already knew the portage chain that climbed from the Saguenay over to the Rupert, a back way from the Saint Lawrence straight to James Bay.

That chain became a French road to the coast after Henry Hudson's 1610 voyage let the English in by sea. In 1663 Guillaume Couture's party, guided by Indigenous travellers, took forty-four canoes up the Saguenay to Mistassini and on toward the Rupert. In 1671 the French official Jean Talon sent the Jesuit Charles Albanel with Paul Denys de Saint-Simon to open the route for France; they wintered among the Mistassini band, baptised roughly a hundred adults and as many children, and reached James Bay on 28 June 1672, the first French party to get there overland. The English seized Albanel on the Rupert two years later and shipped him to England. Posts around the lake moved several times before the Hudson's Bay Company fixed its own at Mistissini in 1821.
zh:
伊伊尤（Iyiyiw）是东克里人（自称Eeyou）对自己的称呼iiyiyuu的异写，意思是「人」。他们的土地在詹姆斯湾东南，泰加林与湖沼交织，是东克里祖地埃尤乌伊斯特奇的一部分；独木舟路线沿东梅因河和鲁珀特河伸向米斯塔西尼湖，湖名在克里语里意为「大岩石」。1444年，这里既无城镇也无固定边界：家族在湖畔度夏，捕鱼和水鸟，入秋后散入内陆猎场，猎驯鹿、河狸和貂。克里人和因努人早已知道一条水陆联运路线：从萨格奈河上溯，再翻到鲁珀特河，等于一条从圣劳伦斯直通詹姆斯湾的后门。

亨利·哈德逊1610年的航行使英国人从海路进入海湾后，这条联运路线就成了法国人通往湾岸的陆路。1663年，纪尧姆·库蒂尔一行在原住民向导带领下，乘四十四艘独木舟上溯萨格奈河，经米斯塔西尼湖驶向鲁珀特河。1671年，法国官员让·塔隆派耶稣会士夏尔·阿尔巴内尔与保罗·德尼·德·圣西蒙北上，为法国打通这条通道；他们在米斯塔西尼人群中过冬，为约一百名成人和同样数目的儿童施洗，1672年6月28日抵达詹姆斯湾，是第一支从陆路走到海湾的法国队伍。两年后，英国人在鲁珀特河抓住阿尔巴内尔，把他押往英格兰。湖畔商站几经迁移，哈得孙湾公司最后在1821年把商站定在米斯塔西尼。

en:
At Baawitigong, the 'place of the rapids', the whole discharge of Lake Superior races down the St. Marys River into Lake Huron. The Ojibwe kept a permanent village of 150 to 200 people beside the white water: sturgeon came in the spring and whitefish in the autumn, when the bank swelled to thousands as families of the surrounding Anishinaabe nations, the Odawa and Potawatomi among them, gathered to fish and trade. The rapids were both the barrier every canoe had to pass between the two lakes and the meeting place of the upper-country peoples, and the catfish-named Marameg were one of the bands of this country. In 1444 its people knew nothing as yet of Europeans.

Étienne Brûlé, with Huron guides, was the first European to see the rapids, in 1623 by French reckoning, and French maps soon marked them Sault de Gaston, after the brother of Louis XIII. In 1668 Claude Dablon and Jacques Marquette founded a Jesuit mission and renamed the place Sault Sainte-Marie; five years later Marquette set out with Louis Jolliet to trace the Mississippi. On 4 June 1671, after the trader Nicolas Perrot had gathered chiefs of fourteen nations and some two thousand people, Saint-Lusson raised a great cross bearing the arms of France, lifted his sword with a handful of earth and cried 'Vive le roi', claiming Lake Huron, Lake Superior and all the country between the seas for Louis XIV. In 1736 Louis Denys de La Ronde opened a shipyard at Pointe-aux-Pins on the north shore and launched the first decked vessel onto Lake Superior, sent to search for copper along its shores. After the conquest the North West Company made the rapids a post around 1790 and built the first lock past the white water in 1798. On 20 July 1814 an American raiding party burned the company depot and the lock, but the north bank stayed British.
zh:
巴维蒂冈在奥吉布瓦语里意为「瀑布之地」：苏必利尔湖的全部来水经圣玛丽斯河奔泻入休伦湖。奥吉布瓦人在白水边设有一座150到200人的定居村落，春天捕捞鲟鱼，秋天捕捞白鱼；白鱼季一到，河岸会聚集数千人，周围阿尼什纳贝各族都来捕鱼交易，奥达瓦人和波塔瓦托米人也在其中。这处急流既是两湖间一切独木舟都要越过的险阻，又是上游诸部族人相会的地方，以鲶鱼为名的马拉梅格人就是这一带的一支。1444年，这里的人还不知道欧洲人。

据法国方面记载，1623年艾蒂安·布吕莱在休伦向导带领下第一个见到这处急流，法国地图很快按路易十三之弟加斯东的名字把它标作加斯东瀑布。1668年，克洛德·达布隆和雅克·马凯特在此建立耶稣会传教站，将此地改名圣玛丽瀑布；五年后，马凯泰和路易·若利埃一同出发去探查密西西比河。1671年6月4日，商人尼古拉·佩罗召集十四个部族的首领和约两千人到场，圣吕松竖起镌有法兰西纹章的大十字架，举剑抓起一把泥土，高呼「国王万岁」，把休伦湖、苏必利尔湖直到各海之间的广袤土地尽数宣告为路易十四所有。1736年，路易·德尼·德·拉龙德在北岸潘角开设船坞，造出第一艘驶入苏必利尔湖的甲板船，派它沿湖寻访铜矿。英国接手后，西北公司约1790年在此设站，1798年又修成绕过急流的第一座船闸。1814年7月20日，一支美军突击队焚毁公司货栈和船闸；北岸仍在英国人手中。

en:
Shallow, island-dotted Lake Abitibi lies on the Clay Belt between the Ottawa valley and James Bay; its outlet, the Abitibi River, runs northwest into the Moose River and so to the bay. Canoes travelling between Montreal and James Bay went this way, up the Ottawa and Lake Timiskaming, across the lake, then down the Abitibi to the coast. The Abitibi people gathered at Pointe Abitibi by the Duparquet River to fish through the summer, and scattered in winter to hunt moose and caribou through the surrounding forest; French sources explain their name as the people of the dark-water lake. In 1444 the lake country was entirely in Indigenous hands, and no European fort or boundary had reached it.

The first Frenchmen to cross the lake were soldiers. In 1686 the Chevalier de Troyes led about a hundred men along the canoe route on a march against the English posts on James Bay; France and England were still at peace, and the surprise attack took Moose Fort, Rupert House and Fort Albany. Among his officers was Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville, who later led the French campaigns that nearly swept the English from Hudson Bay. De Troyes built a post on the shore, and as the halfway station between the Ottawa and James Bay routes it stayed open through the whole French period. After Britain took Canada in 1763 the lake became a free traders' stronghold working against the Hudson's Bay Company. The Company answered with Abitibi House in 1794, could not win the local competition, and abandoned it in 1811; after the merger with the North West Company in 1821 it took over the rival's post on the lake instead.
zh:
水浅多岛的阿比蒂比湖横卧在渥太华河谷与詹姆斯湾之间的黏土地带上，湖水从阿比蒂比河向西北流入穆斯河，再通往海湾。往来蒙特利尔与詹姆斯湾的独木舟都走这条路线：溯渥太华河而上，经蒂米斯卡明湖横穿阿比蒂比湖，再顺阿比蒂比河北上。阿比蒂比人在迪帕尔凯河畔的阿比蒂比角聚夏捕鱼，入冬便分散到周围森林，猎取驼鹿和驯鹿；法文资料把他们的名字解作「深色湖水之人」。1444年，湖区完全在原住民手中，欧洲人的堡垒和疆界都还没有到这里。

第一批横穿湖区的法国人是军人。1686年，特鲁瓦骑士率约百人沿这条独木舟路线奔袭詹姆斯湾上的英格兰商站；当时英法两国尚在媾和之中，这场奇袭连克穆斯堡、鲁珀特屋和奥尔巴尼堡。他的部将中有皮埃尔·勒莫因·迪贝维尔，此人后来指挥的法国攻势几乎把英国人逐出哈得孙湾。特鲁瓦在湖畔筑了一座商站，因地处渥太华线与詹姆斯湾各站的中途，整个法国统治时期都维持不辍。英国1763年夺取加拿大后，这座湖成了自由商人与哈得孙湾公司抗衡的据点。公司1794年开设阿比蒂比屋应战，仍争不过对手，1811年将其放弃；1821年与西北公司合并后，公司改为直接接手对手设在湖畔的商站。

en:
Mosoni is a form of Môsonî, the name the Moose Cree, or Ililiw, give to their country around the mouth of the Moose River at the southern end of James Bay. In 1444 they had no fixed town, following the same round year by year: summer canoe parties fishing and gathering berries, autumn goose and duck camps along the bay shore, winter lodges inland for big game, beaver and marten, spring hunts as the birds flew north. The broad Moose carried the winter's catch down to the estuary, and no European had yet entered the bay.

Pierre-Esprit Radisson scouted these shores from Rupert House before the Hudson's Bay Company built Moose Fort here in 1673, its second post in North America. The fort stood on Moose Cree land, partly to keep French traders coming up from the Saint Lawrence off the bay; Cree hunters brought pelts, provisions and labour to it, and its takings cut into the New France fur trade. In March 1686, with France and England still at peace, the Chevalier de Troyes led thirty French soldiers, seventy Canadian volunteers and Indigenous guides more than 800 miles in eighty-two days from Montreal by the Ottawa, Abitibi and Moose rivers. Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville was in the assault party that surprised the sleeping garrison. The French renamed the place Fort St Louis and went on to take Rupert House and Fort Albany as well. The English retook and burned the fort ten years later, and the Treaty of Utrecht confirmed the bay to Britain in 1713. A new fort went up a mile upstream in 1730; a kitchen fire destroyed it five years later and the rebuilding took seven more. When the Company merged with the North West Company in 1821, the post spread outside its palisade as Moose Factory, the Hudson's Bay Company's main base on James Bay.
zh:
莫索尼（Mosoni）是克里语Môsonî的异写，驼鹿克里人（Ililiw）用它称呼自己在麋河口、詹姆斯湾最南端一带的土地。1444年，他们没有固定城镇，年复一年循着同一个周期生活：夏季结队乘独木舟捕鱼、采浆果，秋季在湾岸设营猎雁鸭，冬季住进内陆棚屋，猎大型野兽、捕河狸和貂，春天水鸟北返时再猎一场。宽阔的麋河把一冬的收获运到河口，欧洲人此时还没有进过海湾。

皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松先从鲁珀特商站出发侦察过这片海岸，1673年哈得孙湾公司在此建起麋河堡，这是它在北美的第二座商站。商站设在驼鹿克里人的土地上，一半用意是挡住从圣劳伦斯方向北上的法国商人；克里猎手把毛皮、粮食和劳力带到堡中，商站的进账让新法兰西的毛皮生意吃了亏。1686年3月，法国和英国尚未开战，德·特鲁瓦骑士却带着三十名法国士兵、七十名加拿大志愿兵和原住民向导从蒙特利尔出发，沿渥太华河、阿比蒂比河和麋河行军八十二天，走了八百多英里。皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔就在突袭队里，趁夜拿下睡梦中的守军。法军把这里改名圣路易堡，接着又连克鲁珀特商站和奥尔巴尼堡。十年后英军夺回并焚毁了这座堡，1713年《乌得勒支和约》把海湾划归英国。1730年，公司在上游一英里处建起新堡；五年后一场从厨房起的火把它烧毁，再建又花了七年。1821年公司与西北公司合并后，商站越出栅栏发展为驼鹿工厂，成为哈得孙湾公司在詹姆斯湾的主要基地。

en:
Attawapiskat takes its name from the Swampy Cree, or Mushkegowuk, name Āhtawāpiskatowi ininiwak, 'people of the divided rocks'. Their country followed the Attawapiskat River from inland lakes to Akimiski Strait on James Bay, facing Akimiski Island, the largest island in the bay. In 1444 the river mouth was a spring and summer gathering ground where bands met for the fishing runs; in winter families dispersed to the shore flats, inland woods and the island itself, trapping, hunting and gathering roots, berries and nuts. Canoes, toboggans and snow trails linked the camps, and no European post stood on the river.

After Henry Hudson opened James Bay in 1610, the fur trade reached this river only from posts farther down the coast. The nearest was Fort Albany to the south: French raiders seized it with the Company's other bay forts in 1686, and in 1693 James Knight sailed in with four ships, whereupon the five French defenders abandoned the fort and its fur stocks without a fight. The returned English post drew Mushkegowuk hunters south with pelts, though Company canoes came this way only rarely. The HBC tried a wintering post on Attawapiskat Lake under George Budge in 1814 and gave it up by 1821. In that year the river mouth was still chiefly a summer fishing camp.
zh:
阿塔瓦皮斯基特（Attawapiskat）出自沼泽克里人（Mushkegowuk）的称呼，意为「岩石分隔之地的人」。他们的土地沿阿塔瓦皮斯基特河，从内陆湖沼延伸到詹姆斯湾的阿基米斯基海峡，与湾中最大的阿基米斯基岛隔海峡相望。1444年，河口是各群体春夏聚集、趁鱼汛捕鱼的地方；入冬后家族分散到岸滩、内陆林地甚至岛上，设陷阱、打猎，采集根块、浆果和坚果。独木舟、平底雪橇和雪路把各处营地连在一起，河上还没有欧洲人的商站。

亨利·哈德逊1610年驶入詹姆斯湾后，毛皮贸易只能顺着更南方的商站传到这条河。最近的是南边的奥尔巴尼堡：1686年法国袭湾部队把它和公司其他要塞一起拿下；1693年，詹姆斯·奈特率四艘船逼近，五名法国守军不战而弃堡垒和库存的毛皮。英国人重占商站后，沼泽克里猎手带着毛皮南下交易，但公司的独木舟很少走到阿塔瓦皮斯基特河。1814年，公司派乔治·巴奇在阿塔瓦皮斯基特湖试办冬站，到1821年还是放弃了。那一年，河口仍主要是一片夏季捕鱼营地。

en:
The Nelson and Hayes rivers break the swampy south-western shore of Hudson Bay, carrying the waters of the Saskatchewan and Red River countries through tidal flats and muskeg to the ice. The people of the coast call themselves Mushkegowuk, 'people of the muskeg', the western Swampy Cree. They summered on the bay, fishing and hunting goose in the salt marshes, and wintered inland at the caribou hunt, and their bark canoes were the only craft that mastered that river network. In 1444 no European had entered their waters, and the furs of the interior moved along their canoe roads without passing a single foreign post.

English ships came soon after the bay was found. Thomas Button reached the Nelson in 1612, buried his sailing master at its mouth, wintered at Port Nelson and named the coast New Wales. In 1684 the Hudson's Bay Company raised Fort Nelson there as its first headquarters, and then built York Factory on the Hayes, a river handier for canoes. Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville made the new fort his recurring target. Driven off in 1690, he took it in 1694 and renamed it Fort Bourbon, lost it to an English counter-attack the next year, and on 5 September 1697 fought three English warships with his single ship Pelican and sank the Hampshire, in the greatest sea fight the bay had ever seen; the fort surrendered to him eight days later, and France held it until Utrecht returned the coast to the Company in 1714. Henry Kelsey had already gone inland from York in 1690, the first European to reach the Saskatchewan plains and their bison herds. After him the coastal Mushkegowuk, the Company's 'Homeguard Cree', provisioned the yearly ships and ran the canoe trade that pulled the furs of the Saskatchewan country down to the bay. In their own language the post was Kihci-waskahikan, the Great House.
zh:
纳尔逊河与海斯河在哈得孙湾西南岸的沼泽低地上切开缺口，把萨斯喀彻温河、雷德河流域的来水穿过潮滩与泥炭沼送入冰海。沿岸居民自称穆什凯戈乌克人，意为「泥炭沼之人」，即西部沼泽克里人。他们夏天到海湾捕鱼、在盐碱滩猎雁，冬天退回内陆猎驯鹿；能驾驭这方水网的，只有他们的树皮独木舟。1444年，还没有欧洲人进入这片水面，内陆的毛皮沿他们的独木舟之路外运，沿途没有一座外人商栈。

海湾被发现后，英国船很快循迹而来。托马斯·巴顿1612年驶抵纳尔逊河，把领航员葬在河口，在纳尔逊港过冬，并把这片海岸命名为新威尔士。1684年，哈德逊湾公司在河口筑起尼尔森堡，作为公司的第一个总部，随后又在更便于独木舟航行的海斯河上修建约克堡。皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·迪贝维尔把这座新堡当成了反复较量的对手：1690年他被英舰击退，1694年将它攻陷并改名波旁堡，次年又被英军反攻夺回；1697年9月5日，他率单舰「鹈鹕号」在湾中迎战三艘英国战舰，击沉「汉普郡」号，打了哈得孙湾有史以来最大的一场海战，八天后要塞向他投降。法国一直占据此地，直到《乌得勒支和约》把海岸归还公司，时为1714年。亨利·凯尔西走得更早，1690年就从约克堡深入内陆，是第一个抵达萨斯喀彻温草原、见到大群野牛的欧洲人。在他之后，沿海的穆什凯戈乌克人，即公司所称的「卫堡克里人」，为每年到来的船只供应给养，经营着把萨斯喀彻温腹地的毛皮拖向海湾的独木舟贸易。在他们自己的语言里，这座商栈叫基赫奇瓦斯卡希坎（Kihci-waskahikan），意为「大屋」。

en:
West of Hudson Bay the forest ends and the Barren Lands begin: treeless tundra cut by the Kazan River and strewn with lakes, swept each year by the great caribou migration. The Ahiarmiut, the Ihalmiut or 'people from beyond', hunted that herd along the inland rivers, while other Inuit wintered on the coast taking seal, walrus and beluga; Chipewyan Dene, caribou-eaters from the taiga edge, also ranged east to the bay shore. In 1444 this was a country measured by the caribou walk, where no ship had yet watered.

The first ships were Danish. In 1619 Jens Munk, searching for the Northwest Passage for Christian IV, brought two vessels into the Churchill River and wintered at a spot he named Nova Dania, 'New Denmark'; cold, famine and scurvy killed almost all his 64 men, and only three sailed home aboard the little Lamprey. The Hudson's Bay Company built the Churchill River Post in 1717 and raised the star-shaped stone Prince of Wales Fort there between 1731 and 1741, after a Chipewyan peace with the Cree opened the inland fur trade. Through that century, as the caribou herds failed, the Dene drew south and Kivallirmiut bands took to wintering inland year-round.

The fort was the base for Samuel Hearne's northern journeys. In 1770 he set out with Chipewyan guides under Matonabbee, crossed the Kazan and Dubawnt barrens to the Coppermine, and on 17 July 1771 watched his Dene companions massacre an Inuit camp at Bloody Falls. Eleven years later, as the fort's governor, he surrendered it without a shot to the French admiral La Perouse, whose three warships had found only 39 civilian defenders behind the walls.
zh:
哈得孙湾以西，森林走到尽头，便是「不毛之地」：没有树木的苔原被卡赞河切开，湖泊星罗棋布，驯鹿群一年一度的大迁徙扫过旷野。阿希亚尔米尤特人自称伊哈尔米乌特，意为「来自远方之人」，沿内陆河流追逐鹿群；另一些因纽特人在海岸过冬，捕猎海豹、海象和白鲸；来自泰加林边缘、以驯鹿为食的奇佩瓦恩迪纳人也向东活动到湾岸。1444年的这片土地以驯鹿的脚步丈量，还没有一条船在这里补过淡水。

最先到来的是丹麦船。1619年，为丹麦国王克里斯蒂安四世寻找西北航道的延斯·蒙克率两艘船驶入丘吉尔河，在一处他命名为「新丹麦」的地方过冬；严寒、饥饿和坏血病几乎夺去全部64名船员的性命，只有3人驾着小船「七鳃鳗号」返国。哈得孙湾公司1717年建起丘吉尔河商栈，又在1731至1741年间筑成星形石砌的威尔士亲王堡；此前奇佩瓦恩人与克里人议和，内陆毛皮贸易随之打开。同一世纪里，驯鹿群减少，迪纳人逐渐南撤，基瓦利尔米乌特人转为终年内陆生活。

这座石堡是塞缪尔·赫恩北方之行的出发地。1770年，他由马顿纳比率领的奇佩瓦恩人做向导，越过卡赞河与迪邦特湖一带的荒原，抵达科珀曼河；1771年7月17日，同行的迪纳人在血腥瀑布突袭一处因纽特营地，大开杀戒，赫恩只能在一旁看着。11年后，已是堡中总督的赫恩未发一枪便向法国海军将领拉佩鲁斯投降，后者的三艘战舰面对的，只是城墙内39名非军职人员。

en:
Rainy Lake, Gojiji-zaaga'igan to the Ojibwe after its many inlets and Tekamamiouen to the Cree for the rain that sweeps it, drains westward by the Rainy River into the Lake of the Woods and the Winnipeg River, the canoe road from Lake Superior into the far interior. Its people, the Gojijiwininiwag, were Saulteaux of the Monsoni country, living on fish and the wild rice of its bays and passing furs along that road; the Cree dwelt to the west and the Sioux to the south, and war parties from the south were never far away. In 1444 the lake was entirely their own.

Jacques de Noyon became the first European to reach Rainy Lake in 1688 and threw up a temporary post, and Fort Tekamanigan, which Robutel de La Noue built there in 1717, was soon abandoned under Sioux pressure. The post that lasted came out of the La Vérendrye expansion. When the explorer reached Grand Portage in the late summer of 1731 his men refused to press farther into unknown country so late in the year; his nephew Christopher Dufrost de La Jemeraye took a few willing hands on, reached Rainy Lake before freeze-up and raised Fort Saint-Pierre at its outlet, the first French post west of Lake Superior. La Vérendrye came through the next summer and pushed on to the Lake of the Woods, where he built Fort Saint Charles. A Cree chief, La Colle, made his camp beside the fort and helped the French hold the Sioux, though open war with them came anyway in 1741. The post served the western trade until 1758. The North West Company built Fort Lac la Pluie on the same ground between 1775 and 1787, and the Hudson's Bay Company set up Lac la Pluie House there in 1818, three years before the two companies were joined.
zh:
雷尼湖在奥吉布瓦语里称戈吉吉湖，因湖岸多湾而得名；克里人则称之为特卡马米温，意思是横扫湖面的雨。湖水向西经雷尼河注入伍兹湖和温尼伯河，这条水路正是从苏必利尔湖通往西部内陆深处的独木舟干道。湖畔的戈吉吉维尼尼瓦格人是蒙索尼一带的索尔托人，以捕鱼和采收湖湾里的野稻为生，也沿这条水路转卖毛皮；他们西边住着克里人，南边住着苏人，南方来的袭击小队从不曾真正远去。1444年，这座湖还完全属于他们自己。

1688年，雅克·德努永成为第一个到达雷尼湖的欧洲人，搭起一座临时驿站；1717年罗比泰尔·德拉努在那里修起特卡马尼冈堡，不久就因苏人的威胁弃守。真正扎下根的驿站出自拉韦朗德里的西进：1731年夏末，这位探险家走到大波蒂奇时，手下人不肯在这么晚的季节再深入陌生之地；他的外甥克里斯托夫·迪弗罗·德拉热默赖带着几个愿意前行的人继续赶路，在封冻前抵达雷尼湖，在湖口建起圣皮埃尔堡，这是苏必利尔湖以西第一座法国驿站。第二年夏天拉韦朗德里经此西进，直抵伍兹湖修建圣夏尔堡。克里人首领拉科勒把主营扎在堡垒附近，帮法国人牵制苏人，但对苏战争还是在1741年爆发。这座驿站经营西部贸易直到1758年。1775至1787年间，西北公司在同一地点建起雨湖堡；1818年哈德逊湾公司又在此设立雨湖商馆，三年后两家公司合为一体。

en:
The Red River comes down out of the plains to Lake Winnipeg, and where it meets the Assiniboine lie the Forks, a canoe meeting ground and trading place used by First Nations for thousands of years. The great lake to the north was winipīhk, 'muddy water', in Western Cree. Corn grew in fields along the Red before contact, and the two rivers joined the bison hunters of the plains to the fishing and trapping camps of the forest; Cree, Anishinaabe, Assiniboine and Dakota all met at the Forks. In 1444 no European had seen the lake, and the goods changing hands were furs, hides, dried meat and pemmican.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company may have been the first European to sight Lake Winnipeg, in 1690. In 1738 the French under La Vérendrye built Fort Rouge at the Forks, their first post on the Red River. After the British conquest the two rival fur companies posted themselves on the same stretch of river: the North West Company built Fort Gibraltar at the Forks, and in 1812 the Hudson's Bay Company raised Fort Douglas a little downstream, beside which Lord Selkirk planted his Red River Colony of Scottish settlers. The colony lived on pemmican supplied by mounted Métis buffalo hunters, yet in 1814 its governor Miles MacDonell forbade its export, an order the Métis and the North West Company read as a grab for their trade. In March 1816 HBC men pulled Fort Gibraltar down. On 19 June, Cuthbert Grant led about sixty mounted Métis past Seven Oaks with a pemmican train, and Governor Robert Semple marched out with fewer than thirty men to stop them. The fight lasted about fifteen minutes: Semple and twenty of his men were killed, for one Métis dead. That night, in the camp on Frog Plain, the Métis singer Pierre Falcon wrote the song that carried the fight's name. The two companies merged in 1821, and their long feud at the Forks ended with it.
zh:
雷德河自草原北流入温尼伯湖，在与阿西尼博因河汇合处形成「福克斯」河汊，是原住民使用了数千年的独木舟会舟之地和贸易场所。北边的大湖在西克里语中称温尼皮赫克，意为「浑水」。与欧洲人接触之前，雷德河沿岸已种有玉米，两条河把草原上的野牛猎人与林间捕鱼设阱的营地连在一起，克里人、奥吉布瓦人、阿西尼博因人和达科他人都在河汊往来。1444年，还没有任何欧洲人见过这座湖，易手的货物只有毛皮、兽皮、肉干和肉糜饼。

1690年，哈得孙湾公司的亨利·凯尔西可能是第一个望见温尼伯湖的欧洲人。1738年，拉韦朗德里麾下的法国人在河汊建起鲁日堡，这是他们在雷德河上的第一座商栈。英国人接管后，两家互为对手的毛皮公司在同一段河上设站：西北公司在福克斯修起直布罗陀堡；1812年，哈得孙湾公司在不远处筑起道格拉斯堡，塞尔扣克伯爵的苏格兰移民就在堡旁建立雷德河殖民地。殖民地靠骑马的梅蒂野牛猎人供应肉糜饼过活，1814年殖民地总督迈尔斯·麦克唐奈却下令禁止肉糜饼外销，梅蒂人和西北公司认为这道命令是要夺他们的生意。1816年3月，公司的人拆毁了直布罗陀堡。6月19日，卡斯伯特·格兰特率约六十名骑马的梅蒂人护送一队肉糜饼经过七株橡树，总督罗伯特·森普尔带不到三十人出城拦截。战斗只打了约一刻钟：森普尔和部下二十人被杀，梅蒂一方仅死一人。当晚在蛙原的营地里，梅蒂歌手皮埃尔·法尔康写下传唱这场战斗的歌。1821年两公司合并，河汊上的长期争斗也随之收场。

en:
Lake Winnipeg, wīnipēk or 'muddy water' in Cree, is a vast, shallow remnant of glacial Lake Agassiz. Its eastern shore rises into the Atikaki, 'caribou country' in Anishinaabe: granite ridges and black spruce where the Bloodvein, Berens and Poplar rivers come down out of the Shield, and First Nations petroglyphs and rock paintings mark cliffs above the Bloodvein. Cree bands netted whitefish and sturgeon on the lake and hunted moose and caribou in the woods; Anishinaabe peoples lived to the south-east and Assiniboine on the prairie edge. In 1444 the lake's long sand beaches were empty of Europeans.

Henry Kelsey, travelling out from York Factory, is thought to have been the first European to sight the lake in 1690. The French came from the opposite direction forty years later: Jean-Baptiste de La Verendrye, son of the explorer, was stopped by ice within twenty miles of the shore in 1733 and reached the lake in 1734, when his party mapped it as Ouinipigon and built Fort Maurepas near the Red River mouth at its southern end. The lake country's beaver then went to Montreal rather than the bay. Traders first descended the Berens from the Severn country in 1767, and in 1814 the Hudson's Bay Company opened a post at the river mouth; the river, like the post, took its name from Joseph Berens, the company's governor. The lake route ran from York Factory to the Red River.
zh:
温尼伯湖的克里语名温尼佩克（wīnipēk），意为「浑水」，是冰川时代阿加西斯湖残留的一片广阔浅湖。湖东岸地势隆起，便是阿蒂卡基，阿尼什纳比语意为「驯鹿之地」：花岗岩脊与黑云杉林间，布拉德维恩河、贝伦河、波普勒河从加拿大地盾奔流而下，布拉德维恩河畔的崖壁上还留有原住民的岩刻与岩画。克里人部落在湖上捕捞白鱼和鲟鱼，在林中猎驼鹿与驯鹿；东南方住着阿尼什纳比人，草原边缘则是阿西尼博因人。1444年，长长的湖滩上还没有一个欧洲人。

一般认为，1690年从约克堡方向而来的亨利·凯尔西是最早见到此湖的欧洲人。40年后，法国人从相反方向而来：探险家拉韦朗德里之子让-巴蒂斯特1733年前进到距湖仅二十英里处被浮冰挡住，1734年抵达湖岸。法国人把大湖记作韦尼皮贡，在南端雷德河河口附近建起莫勒帕堡，湖乡的海狸皮改运蒙特利尔，不再流向海湾。1767年，商人首次从塞文河地方顺贝伦河而下；1814年，哈得孙湾公司在贝伦河河口设立商栈，河名与商栈都取自公司总督约瑟夫·贝伦。这条湖路一头连着约克堡，一头通向雷德河。

en:
Lake Manitoba lies between the grasslands to the south and the boreal woods to the north, its two basins narrowing at the shallow strait called The Narrows. Cree and Ojibwe speakers heard a spirit in the wind-driven water there; their names for the strait, manitou-wapow and manidoobaa, gave Manitoba its name. Reed beds along the shore supplied fish and waterfowl for Assiniboine and Cree camps, while parties from the plains brought bison meat and hides to the lake. A short carry from the Assiniboine River put canoes into this lake, from which the lake chain led toward the Saskatchewan country. In 1444 the fish camps, portages and canoe routes belonged to those nations alone.

La Vérendrye's French parties entered the lake from Fort La Reine in the mid-1730s and called it Lac des Prairies while exploring a route toward the Saskatchewan. Forts built on Cedar Lake and the Saskatchewan River gave the linked lakes a place in the French fur trade, as traders tried to draw western furs away from Hudson Bay. In 1767 French fur traders built the second Fort Dauphin on nearby Dauphin Lake. Hudson's Bay Company and North West Company posts later competed on the same lake until the two companies merged in 1821.
zh:
马尼托巴位于南方草原与北方针叶林之间，马尼托巴湖的两座湖盆在浅水的大窄口收束。克里人和奥吉布瓦人相信风浪拍过窄口时能听见神灵的声音，他们对海峡的称呼马尼图瓦波和马尼多巴后来化成马尼托巴这个名字。湖畔芦苇荡为阿西尼博因人和克里人的营地提供鱼和水禽，草原队伍则把野牛肉和兽皮带到湖边。独木舟从阿西尼博因河经一段短途陆运便可进入此湖，再沿相连湖链前往萨斯喀彻温地区。1444年时，这些渔场、陆运道和独木舟航路只属于当地各部族。

1730年代中期，拉韦朗德里的法国队伍从拉雷讷堡进入马尼托巴湖，把它称作草原湖，并寻找通往萨斯喀彻温河的路线。法国人随后在锡达湖和萨斯喀彻温河畔修建堡垒，使这串相连湖泊进入毛皮商路，试图把西部毛皮从哈得孙湾方向引开。1767年，法国毛皮商人在邻近的多芬湖畔修建第二座多芬堡。后来哈德逊湾公司和西北公司都在湖畔设立商栈相争，直到两家公司于1821年合并。

en:
Kinougeoulini covers the wet forest corridor where the Saskatchewan River leaves the boreal woods, spreads into Cedar Lake and passes Grand Rapids on its way to Lake Winnipeg. Lake Winnipegosis lies immediately to the south. At Opaskwayak, the wooded narrows near The Pas, Swampy Cree families gathered each summer for sturgeon and whitefish and for the rites of the Midewiwin, while moose and beaver were taken in the surrounding forest. Canoes carrying western and northwestern furs came down the same river. In 1444 the lakes, narrows and fishing stations were Cree country; the open grassland beyond the woods belonged to their Assiniboine allies.

Henry Kelsey travelled through the district between 1690 and 1692, the first recorded European on the Saskatchewan. The La Vérendryes then tried to hold the canoe route with a chain of posts: Fort Dauphin on Lake Winnipegosis, Fort Bourbon on the lower river and Fort Paskoya on Cedar Lake, later moved upstream to The Pas. Their purpose was to buy furs before canoe brigades reached the English on Hudson Bay and to test whether the river led toward a western sea. Anthony Henday, the only British trader known to have visited one of these far French posts before the conquest, called Paskoya a hogsty in 1754. French forces burned or abandoned the chain as New France collapsed in 1758 and 1759. Independent winterers and the North West Company later reopened the sites, and the Hudson's Bay Company took them over after the merger of 1821.
zh:
杰诺利尼是温尼伯湖以西一片湿润的森林走廊：萨斯喀彻温河走出针叶林后汇入锡达湖，再经大急流流向温尼伯湖，温尼伯戈西斯湖就在南侧。帕斯附近林木环抱的河窄处称奥帕斯夸亚克，沼泽克里人各家族夏天到此捕捞鲟鱼和白鱼、举行米德维温仪式，也在周围森林猎驼鹿和河狸。西部与西北部的毛皮同样乘独木舟顺这条河而下。1444年时，湖泊、窄口和渔场都是克里人的地界，森林外的开阔草原则属于他们的阿西尼博因盟友。

1690年至1692年，亨利·凯尔西经过这一带，是已知最早来到萨斯喀彻温河的欧洲人。拉韦朗德里父子后来试图用一串堡寨控制这条独木舟航路：温尼伯戈西斯湖畔的多芬堡、下游河畔的波旁堡、锡达湖畔的帕斯科亚堡；帕斯科亚堡后来上移到帕斯。法国人想在独木舟队抵达哈得孙湾的英国人手中之前买下毛皮，也想探明这条河是否通向西方大海。1754年，安东尼·亨迪把帕斯科亚堡称作「猪圈」；在法国统治结束前，他是已知唯一访问过这座遥远法国堡垒的英国商人。1758年至1759年新法兰西崩溃，法国人焚毁或放弃了这串堡寨。后来个体冬猎者和西北公司重开旧址，1821年公司合并后由哈德逊湾公司接管。

en:
Satsuma covers the Satsuma Peninsula and the East China Sea coast of southern Kyushu, the western half of the later Kagoshima mainland. Its sheltered inlet at Kagoshima looks toward Sakurajima, while coastal villages, iron-bearing hills and mountain valleys feed traffic into Kinko Bay. The court province was separated from Hyuga after a Satsuma-Hayato rising in 702, and its old provincial seat stood near Satsumasendai. The Shimazu had served as military governors since the Kamakura period, and by the late 1300s their Shimizu Castle at Kagoshima was the chief warrior base. In 1444 the old provincial administration had already given way before the Shimazu, whose ships and retainers tied the province more closely to the bay than to the old court offices.

Kagoshima brought Christianity into Japan when Francis Xavier landed at nearby Gionnosu on 15 August 1549. Under Shimazu Takahisa and Yoshihisa, the Shimazu brothers united Satsuma, Ōsumi and Hyūga, crushed the Ōtomo at Mimigawa and defeated the Ryūzōji at Okitanawate; for a time they held nearly all Kyushu. Toyotomi Hideyoshi's Kyushu campaign of 1587 forced them back to their home provinces. The Shimazu joined the western army at Sekigahara in 1600 yet kept their lands, and Shimazu Iehisa began Kagoshima Castle the next year.

In 1609 a Satsuma expedition captured Shuri and King Shō Nei in Ryukyu after fighting through the islands. The Amami Islands came under Satsuma, while the Ryukyu court kept its throne and its tributary trade with China. That arrangement allowed Chinese and Southeast Asian goods to keep reaching Kagoshima even after the Tokugawa maritime restrictions. Sengan-en, the Shimazu villa garden, was laid out for Shimazu Mitsuhisa in 1658. Satsuma remained one of the largest outer lordships in 1821.
zh:
萨摩位于九州南部的萨摩半岛和东海沿岸，相当于后来鹿儿岛本土的西半部。鹿儿岛海湾遮蔽风浪，与樱岛相望；沿海村落、产铁山地和山谷中的物产都汇集到锦江湾。702年萨摩隼人叛乱后，该地从日向国分置为令制国，古国府靠近萨摩川内。镰仓时代以来，岛津氏担任守护；到14世纪后期，鹿儿岛的清水城已成为其主要武家据点。1444年，旧国衙体制早已让位于岛津氏，把萨摩联系起来的是家臣团以及鹿儿岛湾里的船只。

1549年8月15日，方济各·沙勿略在鹿儿岛附近的祇园之洲登陆，开始在日本传教。岛津贵久、义久在位时，岛津兄弟统一萨摩、大隅和日向，在耳川击败大友氏，又在冲田畷击破龙造寺氏，一度控制九州大部。1587年，丰臣秀吉发动九州征伐，将他们压回本国诸郡。1600年，岛津氏在关原之战中加入西军，却保全了领地；第二年，岛津家久开始修筑鹿儿岛城。

1609年，萨摩军沿琉球各岛作战后攻陷首里，俘虏尚宁王。奄美群岛改由萨摩控制，琉球朝廷则保留王位和对中国的朝贡贸易。凭借这种安排，即使德川幕府施行海禁，中国和东南亚货物仍能运抵鹿儿岛。1658年，岛津光久营建岛津氏别邸庭园仙岩园。到1821年，萨摩仍是最大的外样大名领地之一。

en:
Cheongju lies in the Musimcheon valley in central Korea, where the road from Hanyang to the south-western provinces crosses the grain country of Chungcheong. The mountain fortress of Sangdang Sanseong has guarded the heights above it since Baekje times, and below it Unified Silla laid out Seowon, one of its five secondary capitals, in 685; Goryeo gave the town the name Cheongju in 940. The town's surest title to fame is a book. In 1377 monks at Heungdeok Temple printed the Jikji, an anthology of Zen patriarchs' teachings, with movable metal type, the oldest surviving book printed that way, seventy-eight years before Gutenberg's Bible. An iron flagpole from Yongdu Temple, cast in 962, still stands on the old temple site in the town centre. In 1444 Cheongju was a quiet prefectural town beneath its fortress, sending its grain up the road to Hanyang.

Cheongju was fought over twice under the Joseon kings. Early in 1592 Kuroda Nagamasa's division took the town and the Chungcheong defence commissioner fled. Cho Hon, a former magistrate of Okcheon, raised a thousand civilian volunteers, and the monk Yeonggyu joined him with five hundred warrior monks; about fifteen hundred men stormed the west gate and retook Cheongju, the first victory of the war won by righteous army and monk-soldiers together. Cho Hon and Yeonggyu both fell later that year at Geumsan, and Sangdang Sanseong was repaired in 1596. In March 1728 Yi In-jwa's Soron and Namin rebels seized Cheongju Castle as the first move of the Musin Rebellion against King Yeongjo, claiming the king was not the true heir. The royal army retook the castle within weeks, Yi In-jwa was captured and executed, and the rising collapsed.
zh:
清州位于朝鲜中部的无心川谷地，汉阳通往西南诸道的大路穿过忠清道的产粮区，打这里经过。上党山城自百济时代起就扼守着城北的高地；685年，统一新罗在山下设西原小京，为五小京之一，940年高丽改其名为清州。清州最出名的是一本书：1377年，兴德寺僧众用金属活字印出禅门祖师法语集《直指心体要节》，这是现存最古老的金属活字印本，比古腾堡圣经早七十八年。城中的龙头寺旧址上，立着一根962年铸造的铁幢杆。1444年的清州，是山城脚下一处安静的州治，所产谷物沿大路运往汉阳。

朝鲜时代，清州两度沦为战场。1592年开战之初，黑田长政所部攻占清州，忠清道防御使弃城而逃。玉川前县监赵宪募集义兵一千，灵圭率僧兵五百来会，两军共约一千五百人猛攻西门，收复清州，这是义兵与僧兵首次联手告捷。赵宪与灵圭后来都在同年的金山之战中战死，上党山城也于1596年重修。1728年3月，李麟佐率少论派与南人叛军袭取清州城，作为反对英祖的戊申乱第一着，声称英祖并非正当的王位继承人。官军数周内夺回城池，李麟佐被俘处死，各地叛乱随之瓦解。

en:
Bungo occupied eastern Kyushu, from the Kunisaki Peninsula and the harbour of Funai to the mountain valleys bordering Hyuga and Higo. Old Toyo was divided into Bungo and Buzen in 701, and in 1185 Minamoto no Yoritomo sent the Otomo clan east from Kanto as shugo to subdue pro-Taira warriors in Kyushu. The clan held Bungo through the Kamakura and Muromachi centuries, ruling from Funai over a timbered, deeply indented coast; in 1444 local gentry and shrine and temple estates still kept much of the countryside in their own hands.

Bungo's Nanban years centre on Otomo Sorin. Francis Xavier visited him at Funai in 1551, after which Portuguese, Chinese and Ryukyu shipping made the port one of the busiest in Kyushu. The Portuguese surgeon Luis de Almeida founded an orphanage there and in 1556 a hospital with wards for surgery, internal medicine and leprosy, the first in Japan to practise Western medicine. Jesuit records called Sorin the King of Bungo, and the Tensho embassy sent by the Christian lords of Kyushu sailed for Rome in 1582. Baptised in 1578 with the name Francisco, he pulled down Buddhist temples and Shinto shrines and pressed his subjects to convert, but defeat by the Shimazu at the Mimikawa later that year broke Otomo power. Shimazu armies overran Bungo in 1586 and took Funai, where Almeida's hospital was destroyed in the invasion; Sorin appealed to Toyotomi Hideyoshi, whose Kyushu campaign restored his son Yoshimune, though Sorin himself died in 1587 before the fighting ended. Yoshimune later renounced Christianity and was dispossessed for cowardice in the Korean wars, and under the Tokugawa Bungo was divided between shogunal land and the small domains of Funai, Kitsuki, Usuki and Saeki.
zh:
丰后在九州东部，从国东半岛和府内港湾延伸到毗邻日向、肥后的山地河谷。701年，旧丰国被分为丰前和丰后；1185年，源赖朝为压制九州的亲平氏武士，把出身关东的大友氏派任守护。大友氏历经镰仓、室町时代保有丰后，以府内为本据统治这片森林密布、海岸曲折的土地；1444年，地方豪族和寺社庄园在乡间仍掌握很大实权。

丰后的南蛮时代以大友宗麟为中心。1551年，方济各·沙勿略到府内与他会面，此后葡萄牙、中国和琉球的商船使府内成为九州最繁忙的港口之一。葡萄牙外科医生路易斯·德·阿尔梅达先在府内开办孤儿院，又于1556年建起分设外科、内科和麻风病科的医院，这是日本第一所施行西医的医院。耶稣会文献称宗麟为「丰后之王」，九州基督教大名派遣的天正遣欧使节也于1582年启程前往罗马。1578年他受洗，取教名方济各，随后拆毁佛寺神社、强令领民改宗；同年在耳川之战中败于岛津氏，大友家由盛转衰。1586年岛津军攻占丰后、拿下府内，阿尔梅达的医院毁于战火；宗麟向丰臣秀吉求援，秀吉发动九州征伐，恢复了其子大友义统的领国，宗麟本人却在1587年战事结束前病殁。义统后来弃教，又在朝鲜之役中因怯战被除封；德川时代，丰后被分为幕府天领和府内、杵筑、臼杵、佐伯诸小藩。

en:
Okinawa is the chief island of the Ryukyu chain, lying between the East China Sea and the Pacific about 640 kilometres south of Kyushu. Its gusuku lords formed the three realms of Hokuzan, Chuzan and Nanzan, with Chuzan holding Shuri and the neighbouring port of Naha. Ming investiture tied the court to the Chinese tribute system, and Fujianese families settled in 1392 supplied diplomats, interpreters and shipbuilders. Shō Hashi united the three realms in 1429 and made Shuri Castle the royal seat. In 1444, only fifteen years later, Naha junks carried silver, swords, ceramics, spices, sappanwood and sugar between China, Japan, Korea and Southeast Asia, while noro priestesses kept the island rites at the Shuri court.

Naha's harbour works soon matched that trade. In 1451 a Chinese engineer built the roughly one-kilometre Chōkōtei causeway to link the port islands with Okinawa and receive Ming envoys; warehouses and the Mie and Yarazamori forts covered the anchorage. In 1458 the court hung the newly cast Bell of Many Nations in Shuri's main hall, its inscription presenting Ryukyu as a maritime intermediary. The Second Shō dynasty took power in 1469. Under Shō Shin, who reigned from 1477 to 1527, local lords were brought to Shuri, the priestesses were placed under court order, and Ryukyu extended its control over the Sakishima Islands and, by 1571, the northern Amami group.

Satsuma invaded in 1609 and met stiff resistance on almost every island on the route before taking Shuri and King Shō Nei. The Fifteen Articles placed Ryukyuan diplomacy and commerce under Satsuma supervision, and the Amami Islands were ceded, but Shuri kept its throne and most internal government. The court also continued its tributary missions to China, which let Chinese goods pass toward Kagoshima under the Tokugawa maritime restrictions. Naha's Tsuboya potters established their enameled Ryukyuan ware in 1682, and the Shuri court still administered Okinawa's internal affairs in 1821.
zh:
冲绳是琉球群岛的主岛，位于东海与太平洋之间，北距九州约640公里。岛上按司曾形成北山、中山、南山三个政权，其中中山据守首里和邻近的那霸港。明朝的册封把琉球宫廷纳入朝贡体制，1392年定居的福建人后裔则为王府提供外交官、通译和造船工匠。1429年，尚巴志统一三山，以首里城为王都。1444年，距统一仅十五年，那霸的帆船已在中国、日本、朝鲜和东南亚之间运载白银、刀剑、瓷器、香料、苏木和糖；祝女则在首里宫廷维持岛上祭祀。

那霸的港埠设施很快跟上贸易规模。1451年，一名中国工匠主持修筑长约1公里的长虹堤，把港中诸岛与冲绳本岛连接起来，以便迎接明朝使节；仓库和三重城、屋良座森城拱卫泊地。1458年，王府把新铸的万国津梁之钟悬挂在首里城正殿，铭文把琉球称作海上往来的津梁。1469年，第二尚氏取得王位。尚真1477年至1527年在位期间，各地按司被集中到首里，祝女也被纳入宫廷秩序；琉球将先岛群岛纳入治下，到1571年又控制了奄美群岛北部。

1609年，萨摩军队入侵，在航线上的几乎每座岛屿都遇到顽强抵抗，最终攻陷首里、俘虏尚宁王。《掟十五条》把琉球的外交和贸易置于萨摩监管之下，奄美群岛被割让，但首里朝廷保留王位和大部分内政。琉球继续向中国派遣朝贡使节，中国货物也因此能在德川海禁之下输往鹿儿岛。1682年，那霸壶屋工匠烧出釉彩琉球陶器；直到1821年，冲绳内政仍由首里朝廷管理。

en:
Ha Tinh is the narrow shelf where the Hong Linh hills press the coastal road against the Gulf of Tonkin. At its southern end the Hoanh Son range runs into the sea, and the Ngang pass is the one level road between the northern plain and the lands beyond; inland are rice fields, and the coast faces fishing inlets and salt pans. The Ming ruled Dai Viet from 1407, but in 1418 Le Loi raised the Lam Son revolt just to the north, and in 1424, taking a lieutenant's advice, the rebels came down this coast to seize Nghe An, the base from which they drove the Ming out in 1427. In 1444 Ha Tinh is the southern march of the restored Later Le, a line of soldier-settler villages, salt pans and fishing harbours guarding the road south.

Every army moving between the Red River plain and the southern coast used that road. After the Mac seized the throne, the men of Thanh Hoa and Nghe An kept the Le cause alive. Nguyen Hoang, whose elder brother had been killed by their brother-in-law Trinh Kiem, had his sister, Kiem's own wife, plead for a distant posting, and in 1558 he led the men of Thanh-Nghe south through the Ngang pass to hold Thuan Hoa, the march that grew into the Nguyen lordship. For a century Ha Tinh lay just behind the Trinh-Nguyen front, its coast crowded with troops and supply junks; in 1774 Hoang Ngu Phuc took 30,000 men down the road to storm the Nguyen capital Phu Xuan, and Tay Son armies marched it in both directions. Tien Dien village here was the ancestral home of the poet Nguyen Du. Born in 1766, he served through the fall of the Le and then the Nguyen, led the embassy to the Qing in 1813 and 1814, and recast the Chinese novel Jin Yun Qiao as a 3,254-line verse tale in nom, The Tale of Kieu, before his death in 1820.
zh:
河静是洪岭余脉把沿海官道挤向北部湾的一道狭长海岸，南端横山直插入海，横山关是北方平原与南来之地之间唯一平缓的通道；内陆开稻田，海边列着渔港和盐田。1407年起明朝统治大虞，1418年黎利在北面举兵蓝山，1424年义军纳部将之计沿这条海岸南下夺取乂安，并以此为根基在1427年逼退明军。1444年的河静是复国后黎朝的南陲，一连串军屯村寨、盐灶和渔港守着南下的大路。

往来红河平原与南方海岸之间的军队，都要走这条路。莫氏篡位后，清化、乂安的军民支撑着后黎残局。阮潢的兄长被姐夫郑检所杀，他由身为郑检之妻的姐姐求情，求得外放边地；1558年，阮潢率清乂子弟过横山关南下镇守顺化，这支人马后来长成阮主基业。此后百余年，河静紧贴郑阮前线，沿岸挤满兵马与粮船；1774年黄五福率兵三万沿这条路攻克阮都富春，西山军又在道上来回奔波。本省仙田村是诗人阮攸的祖籍，他1766年出生，历事后黎与阮朝，1813至1814年出使清朝，把中国小说《金云翘传》改写为3254句的喃字长诗《传翘》，1820年病故。

en:
Suō occupies the south-western tip of Honshu on the Seto Inland Sea, with sheltered harbours looking across to Kyushu, Korea and the China coast. Its provincial capital of the law-code age stood at Hōfu, seat of the Tamanooya Shrine, the province's ichinomiya. From the fourteenth century the land belonged to the Ōuchi, a warrior house that claimed descent from the kings of Baekje and grew rich on the tally trade with Ming China and Joseon Korea, shipping out copper, sulphur and swords and bringing back silk and porcelain. In 1360 Ōuchi Hiroyo moved the clan seat to Yamaguchi, a new town laid out on Kyoto's grid and later called the 'Kyoto of the west'; its five-story Kōshaku-ji pagoda, raised for Ōuchi Yoshihiro, was completed in 1442. In 1444 Ōuchi Mochiyo rules a trading city whose wealth draws monks, scholars and merchants fleeing Kyoto's wars.

The Ōuchi pushed their way into national politics. Masahiro led the western host through the Ōnin War from 1467, and his son Yoshioki marched on Kyoto in 1508 and restored the deposed shogun Ashikaga Yoshitane. The ink painter Sesshū, lately returned from the Ming ports, worked in Yamaguchi under the clan's patronage. Their feud with the Hosokawa over the China trade came to blows at Ningbo in 1523, after which Ming cargoes moved mainly on Ōuchi ships. Under Ōuchi Yoshitaka the city was Japan's main meeting point with foreign learning, and the Jesuit Francis Xavier was received there in 1550 and given leave to preach. Yoshitaka then planned to move the emperor and his court from war-torn Kyoto to Yamaguchi; his generals took it for court intrigue, rose under Sue Harukata in 1551 and forced him to kill himself. Mōri Motonari, another former vassal, destroyed Sue at Itsukushima in 1555 and took Suō two years later.

After Sekigahara in 1600 the victorious Tokugawa cut the Mōri down to Suō and Nagato, and the clan built its new capital at Hagi on the Sea of Japan coast, the domain later known as Chōshū. Yamaguchi shrank to a posting town between Hagi and the port of Mitajiri. The Kikkawa, kinsmen of the Mōri, kept Iwakuni, and in 1673 raised the five-arched Kintai Bridge over the Nishiki River.
zh:
周防地处本州西端，面朝濑户内海，良港隔海望向九州、朝鲜和中国沿海。律令时代的国衙在防府，一之宫玉祖神社坐落于此。14世纪起周防归大内氏统治；这一武家自称百济王族后裔，靠对明朝和朝鲜李朝的勘合贸易致富，运出铜、硫磺和刀剑，换回丝绸与瓷器。1360年大内弘世把本据迁到按京都条坊营建的山口，这里后来有「西京」之称；大内氏在香积寺为纪念大内义弘而建的五重塔1442年落成。1444年大内持世在此统治，贸易之财把躲避京都战火的僧侣、学者和商人吸引到这座城里。

大内氏既插手全国政局，也经营文化。政弘自1467年起统率应仁之乱的西军，其子义兴1508年进兵京都，拥戴被废的将军足利义稙复职。刚从明朝港口归国的画僧雪舟，受大内氏庇护在山口作画。与细川氏争夺对明贸易的冲突1523年在宁波爆发，此后对明贸易主要由大内的船只经营。大内义隆时，山口是日本接触海外学问的主要去处，耶稣会士方济各·沙勿略1550年在此谒见义隆，获准传教。后来义隆想把天皇和朝廷从战火中的京都迎到山口，家臣认定这是公卿弄权，1551年拥陶晴贤起兵，逼他自尽。另一家旧臣毛利元就1555年在严岛攻灭陶晴贤，两年后平定周防。

1600年关原合战后，得胜的德川氏把毛利氏减封到周防、长门两国，毛利氏在日本海沿岸的萩另建居城，即后来的长州藩。山口沦为萩与三田尻港之间道路上的宿场町。毛利一门吉川氏领有岩国，1673年在锦川上建起五拱的锦带桥。

en:
Izumo faces the Sea of Japan on the San'indo coast of western Honshu, where short rivers running off the Chugoku mountains water small coastal plains. It is the sacred country of the Izumo Taisha, shrine of Okuninushi, the god who built the land and binds human marriages, counted among the oldest shrines in Japan; after the Yamato court brought Izumo under its rule the shrine kept its priestly standing, and local belief held that in the tenth month all the gods gathered there, so Izumo called that month kamiarizuki while the rest of Japan called it kannazuki. The same rivers carried iron sand, which tatara furnaces smelted into steel for swordsmiths and armourers. The medieval shugo, Sasaki, Yamana and finally Kyogoku, rarely came to the province; in 1444 the Kyogoku lived in distant Omi while their deputies the Amago ruled from Gassan Toda, a mountain castle above the coast.

Expelled for seizing manors, Amago Tsunehisa retook Gassan Toda by surprise in 1486 and built the clan into Sengoku lords holding Izumo and Hoki and the steel trade; under his grandson Haruhisa, shogun and court named him shugo of eight San'in and Sanyo provinces in 1552. Haruhisa's sudden death opened the way for Mori Motonari, whose blockade starved Gassan Toda into surrender in 1566, when Amago Yoshihisa was led captive to Aki. The loyal retainer Yamanaka Yukimori, shown in later portraits with a crescent moon on his helmet, raised restoration armies from 1569 in the name of Amago Katsuhisa and fought on until he was captured and killed after Kozuki Castle fell in 1578.
