Tuareg oral tradition holds that Buktu, the woman who gave Timbuktu its name ('Buktu's well'), came originally from Essouk. Through the fifteenth century the Kel Taddemekat fought the incoming Iwellemmeden confederation, and by mid-century the newcomers grazed their herds from Lake Faguibine to the approaches of the Aïr. When Judar Pasha's musketeers overthrew Songhai at Tondibi in 1591, the Adrar des Ifoghas was wholly Tuareg country, and the caravan city lived on only in the name of the Kel Taddemekat.
zh:
塔得迈卡意为「类麦加」，又称苏克，即「集市」，坐落在伊福加斯山地的埃苏克河谷，东北距廷巴克图五百公里。9至15世纪，它是撒哈拉中段商路上的主要转口城：商队穿过大沙漠后在此休整，备下水和粮食，再南下苏丹地带。1068年贝克里写道，天下诸城以它最像麦加，又说它营建胜过加纳和加奥，城名即「类麦加」之意。居民是蒙面的柏柏尔穆斯林，食肉，也吃不耕自生的谷物，高粱由苏丹地带运来，商路远达塔赫尔特、瓦尔格拉等易巴德派城市。1083—1084年穆拉比特人联合加纳来攻，大概就是在此役之后，该城由易巴德派改奉马立克派逊尼教义。古城沿干河两岸及河心小岛分布，墓地里立着11世纪的阿拉伯文墓碑，河谷岩壁上刻有库法体和提非纳文铭文；城址附近还发现一种提纯黄金的工艺遗迹：把金料与玻璃一同熔化，杂质混入玻璃，留下纯金。到1444年，此城已过盛时。商队改投廷巴克图，凯尔·塔德梅卡特部图阿雷格人在旧城墙间放牧，只对桑海保持松散臣属。

图阿雷格人的口述传统称，廷巴克图其名（意为「布克图之井」）所自的妇人布克图，相传本是埃苏克人。15世纪里，凯尔·塔德梅卡特人与新来的伊韦勒梅登联盟争战，到15世纪中叶，新来者的牧场已从法吉宾湖一直伸展到阿伊尔高原边缘。1591年朱达尔帕夏的火枪手在通迪比推翻桑海时，伊福加斯山地尽是图阿雷格人的天下，这座商队城市只留在凯尔·塔德梅卡特的名字里。

en:
Macina is the Inner Niger Delta, the wide floodplain between the Niger and its tributary the Bani. Each wet season the rivers rise far over their banks and turn the country into a shallow lake; as the water falls it leaves a maze of lakes and channels. The peoples of the delta have long divided the work by this water: the Marka grow rice, the Bambara millet and sorghum, the Fulani drive cattle out to the fresh floodplain pasture, and the Bozo and Somono fish the channels and carry their catch to the market at nearby Jenne. Fulani pastoralists from Termess, south of Hodh, founded a sultanate here about 1400, but the delta's chiefs were more often vassals than masters. In 1444 Macina belonged to the merchant city of Jenne, and its rice, cattle and fish all moved through Jenne's wharves.

The overlords changed with the fortunes of the Niger bend. In 1477 the Mossi emperor Naba Nasséré raided through and made Macina his, until the Askia kings of Songhai drew the floodplain into their empire; after the Moroccan victory at Tondibi in 1591 the Arma musketeers of Timbuktu collected its dues, and in the eighteenth century the Bambara of Segu made the Fulani chiefs their tributaries. In 1818 a preacher from a minor scholar family, Seku Amadu, raised a jihad against the Bambara. The Fulani chief Ardo Amadu gathered a host put at a hundred thousand men to crush him, but at Noukouma about a thousand jihadists routed it. Seku Amadu took Jenne the same year and in 1820 built a new capital at Hamdullahi, a name meaning 'praise God'. Ruling with a grand council, he made the delta the seat of the Fulani caliphate of Massina: his judges applied sharia, a code settled how herders and farmers might share the floodplain, and mosques were built low and plain without decoration or minarets.
zh:
马西纳就是内尼日尔三角洲，尼日尔河与支流巴尼河之间的一片广阔河泛地。每逢雨季河水大涨、漫出河岸，把整片乡野变成浅湖；水退之后，地上留下纵横交错的湖泊与水道。三角洲的居民早就按这片水分了工：马尔卡人种稻，班巴拉人种粟和高粱，富拉尼人把牛群赶上新淹出的河泛牧场，博佐人和索莫诺人在水道里捕鱼，渔获送到附近杰内的市场出售。约1400年，来自霍德以南泰尔梅斯的富拉尼牧人在此建立苏丹国，但三角洲的酋长们多半时候是附庸而非主人。1444年，马西纳归商城杰内所有，稻米、牲畜和鱼都从杰内的码头外运。

主人随着尼日尔河套的局势更替。1477年，莫西皇帝纳巴·纳塞雷袭掠此地，把马西纳据为己有；后来桑海阿斯基亚王朝的国王们把河泛地并入帝国；1591年摩洛哥在通迪比取胜后，收贡的换成廷巴克图的阿尔马火枪兵；到18世纪，塞古的班巴拉人又把富拉尼酋长们变成附庸。1818年，出身小经师家庭的教士阿赫马杜·洛博发起反对班巴拉人的圣战。富拉尼酋长阿尔多·阿赫马杜集结号称十万的大军前来围剿，却在努库马被约一千名圣战者击溃。阿赫马杜同年拿下杰内，1820年另建新都哈姆杜拉希，意为「赞美真主」。他与大议事会共治，把三角洲变成富拉尼人马西纳哈里发国的中枢：法官施行沙里亚法，颁下法典规定牧人和农户怎样共用河泛地，清真寺也按他的规矩造得低矮素净，不加装饰、不建宣礼塔。

en:
Timbuktu stands about twelve miles north of the Niger, at the edge of the Sahara. About 1100 it was a summer camp of Maghsharan Tuareg at a well, then grew into the meeting point of the Taghaza salt caravans and the gold brought up from the southern rivers: North African merchants from Ghadames and Awjila brought cloth and horses and carried off gold, slaves and ivory. Mansa Musa of Mali annexed the town peacefully on his way back from Mecca and had the Djinguereber mosque raised in 1327; scholars drifting east from Walata made the Sankore quarter a seat of learning, and by 1375 the town was marked on the Catalan Atlas. As Mali weakened, a Tuareg chief, Akil ag-Amalwal, made himself master. In 1444 Timbuktu was a self-ruling trading city under Tuareg lords, its warehouses stocked with cloth, books and gold, and the Sidi Yahya mosque begun in 1400 was completed in 1440.

Sunni Ali of Songhai took the city in 1468, and when his soldiers fell on the Sankore quarter many scholars fled back to Walata. Under Askia Muhammad, who seized power in 1493, Timbuktu had its best years while Gao remained the imperial capital: the Sankore madrasa drew students from across the western Sudan, the book trade throve beside the salt and gold markets, and Leo Africanus saw gold plate on the ruler's table and noted a load of Taghaza salt selling for eighty ducats. On 30 May 1591 Judar Pasha's musketeers, fresh from Tondibi, took the city for the Saadian sultan of Morocco and made it their seat of government. In 1593 the new rulers purged the scholars, and Ahmad Baba, the city's greatest teacher, was carried off to Marrakesh with his books, not returning until 1607. After 1612 the Arma, descendants of the garrison, chose their own pashas, and more than a hundred short regimes followed. The Bambara of Segu made the city tributary under Biton Coulibaly and again under Ngolo Diarra; in 1787 the Tuareg entered Timbuktu and reduced the pashalik to dependence, and the gold and slave trade had long moved down to the Atlantic coast.
zh:
廷巴克图位于尼日尔河以北约十五公里、撒哈拉沙漠的南缘。约1100年，这里只是马格沙兰图阿雷格人在一处水井旁的夏季营地，后来成了塔加扎盐队与南方河金汇合的地方：来自古达米斯、奥吉拉的北非商人带来布匹和马匹，换走黄金、奴隶和象牙。马里的曼萨·穆萨朝觐归来途中和平接管此城，1327年下令修建津加里贝尔清真寺；从瓦拉塔东迁的学者把桑科雷区变成讲学之地，到1375年，这座城已被标进《加泰罗尼亚地图集》。马里衰落后，图阿雷格首领阿基勒·阿格-阿马尔瓦勒自立为主。1444年，廷巴克图是图阿雷格贵族治下的自治商城，仓库里堆满布匹、书籍和黄金，1400年动工的西迪·叶海亚清真寺已于1440年落成。

桑海的桑尼·阿里于1468年攻取此城，军队在桑科雷区施暴，许多学者逃回瓦拉塔。1493年夺权的阿斯基亚·穆罕默德治下，廷巴克图迎来最好的年月，帝国都城仍设在加奥：桑科雷伊斯兰学校吸引整个西苏丹的学生，书市与盐市、金市并盛，利奥·阿非利加努斯看到统治者案上的金盘，还记下一驮塔加扎盐卖到八十达克特。1591年5月30日，朱达尔帕夏的火枪手在通迪比获胜后拿下此城，为摩洛哥萨阿德苏丹所有，并把这里作为统治中心。1593年，新主整肃学者，城中最负盛名的教师艾哈迈德·巴巴带着藏书被押往马拉喀什，直到1607年才返回。1612年以后，驻军后裔阿尔马人自行推举帕夏，短命政权更迭上百次。塞古的比通·库利巴利和后来的恩戈洛·迪亚拉先后迫使此城称臣纳贡；1787年图阿雷格人入城，把帕夏国降为附庸，而黄金和奴隶贸易早已转到大西洋沿岸。

en:
Gao stands on the left bank of the Niger where the river meets the Tilemsi valley, the southern end of a trans-Saharan caravan road. Arab geographers called the town Kawkaw and described two settlements facing each other across the river: a market town of merchants and warehouses, and a royal town where the king lived beside his mosque, with the common prayer ground between them. Boats and caravans carried slaves, copper and cloth through its wharves, and buyers paid in cowries. Mali conquered Gao in 1325; when Ibn Battuta stayed a month in 1353 he found one of the finest, biggest and most fertile cities of the Sudan, supplied with rice, fish, milk and chickens, and he left with a caravan bound for Takedda that drove hundreds of slave girls north. A war with the Tuareg of Takedda wrecked the town late in the fourteenth century, after which the Sunni kings threw off Malian rule. In 1444 Sunni Sulayman Dama ruled from Gao, capital of a small kingdom on the eve of its great expansion.

Sunni Ali Ber, who reigned from 1464, made Gao the capital of the Songhai Empire, taking Timbuktu and Jenne. In 1493 his general Muhammad Ture seized the throne as Askia Muhammad and went on pilgrimage to Mecca; on his return he raised the pyramidal mud-brick tomb that still marks the skyline, seventeen metres high, said to be built of clay and timber carried back from Mecca by a caravan of thousands of camels. Leo Africanus, visiting between 1506 and 1510, found the town unwalled but full of rich merchants, its market square crowded with slaves for sale, where a girl of fifteen fetched about six ducats. The empire fell a day's march north of the city at Tondibi. On 13 March 1591 Judar Pasha's four thousand Moroccans, many carrying arquebuses, met a far larger Songhai army, which drove a thousand cattle ahead to break the Moroccan line; the gunfire and cannon turned the herd back into the Songhai ranks, and the fight lasted about two hours. Gao was evacuated, the Moroccans made Timbuktu their capital, and Gao became an Arma garrison town. About 1770 the Tuareg took it.
zh:
加奥位于尼日尔河左岸、河流与蒂莱姆西谷地相接的地方，是一条穿越撒哈拉的商道的南端。阿拉伯地理学家称它为考考，记下隔河相对的两座聚落：商人货栈所在的市场城，和国王傍清真寺而居的王城，两城之间是公共礼拜场。船只和商队在码头转运奴隶、铜和布匹，买卖用宝螺结算。1325年马里征服加奥；1353年伊本·白图泰在此住了一个月，称它是苏丹最美好、最大、最丰饶的城市之一，稻米、鱼、牛奶和鸡肉都很充足，他最后随一支开往塔凯达的商队北返，队中赶着数百名女奴。14世纪末，与塔凯达图阿雷格人的战争毁了这座城，桑尼诸王随后摆脱了马里的统治。1444年，桑尼·苏莱曼·达马以加奥为都，此时的桑海还是个小国，大扩张尚未开始。

1464年即位的桑尼·阿里·贝尔把加奥定为桑海帝国的都城，攻取廷巴克图和杰内。1493年，他的将领穆罕默德·图雷夺取王位，称阿斯基亚·穆罕默德，随后赴麦加朝觐；归来后他建起那座十七米高的金字塔形泥砖陵墓，高出全城屋顶，相传所用泥土和木料由数千峰骆驼的商队从麦加运回。利奥·阿非利加努斯1506至1510年间到访，见此城没有城墙，却满是富商，集市广场上挤满待售的奴隶，一个十五岁的少女能卖到约六杜卡特。帝国亡于城北一日行程的通迪比。1591年3月13日，朱达尔帕夏的四千摩洛哥军迎战人数远多的桑海大军，军中许多人持有火绳枪；桑海人赶千头牛冲在阵前，想用牛群冲乱敌阵，枪炮声却把牛群惊回，反冲乱自家队伍，战斗只持续了约两个小时。加奥人弃城撤走，摩洛哥人改以廷巴克图为都，加奥成为阿尔马人的驻防城。约1770年，图阿雷格人占领了它。

en:
Djenné sits in the floodplains of the Inland Niger Delta, where the Bani joins the Niger and the waters spread over the country from August to February; canoes then take the place of roads and the town becomes an island. The present town grew after 1000, as older Djenné-Djeno, settled since around 200 BC, was abandoned nearby. By the fifteenth century Djenné was a walled market city-state, loosely tributary to Mali, where salt from Taghaza and gold from Bitu changed hands with slaves, copper, cotton, dyed cloth, rice and fish. Its first mosque went up in the thirteenth or early fourteenth century, when the sultan Kunburu became a Muslim, pulled down his palace and built on its site; later rulers added the towers and the surrounding wall, and Askia Muhammad rebuilt it. In 1444 the Jenne-koi ruled a prosperous, largely independent river town, Muslim merchants and scholars tied its markets to Timbuktu, and in 1447 the Genoese Antonio Malfante, writing home from the Saharan oasis of Tuwat, became the first European to report the town from traders' accounts.

Sonni Ali of Songhai took Djenné in 1471 only after a siege of about six months: the Bani flood protected the town but also let him bring up a river fleet and starve it out. Its sultan died during the siege, his young son made peace, and the boy's mother married Sonni Ali. Under the Askias Djenné held some 40,000 people and a Jenne-mondio collected customs duties. The Portuguese captain Duarte Pacheco Pereira heard around 1507 of a walled city of 'great wealth of gold', and João de Barros wrote that Djenné had once been more famous than Timbuktu; Leo Africanus saw merchants paddling narrow canoes to Timbuktu during the flood.

After the Songhai defeat at Tondibi in 1591, Judar Pasha's Moroccan musketeers crossed the Sahara and sacked Djenné, and in 1599 they defeated a Mali army outside its walls. Trade outlived the conquest: in 1655 the chronicler al-Sadi still called Djenné one of the great markets of the Muslims, where salt from Taghaza met gold from Bitu. Moroccan control faded after 1630, and early in the eighteenth century Biton Coulibaly's Bambara state at Ségou drew the city into its empire. In 1818 Seku Amadu founded the Fulani state of Massina and his jihad brought Djenné under the government ruling it in 1821.
zh:
杰内坐落在内尼日尔三角洲的洪泛平原，巴尼河在这里汇入尼日尔河，每年8月到次年2月洪水漫过乡野，独木舟取代道路，城镇成了岛屿。现存的城镇1000年以后才兴起，邻近早在公元前200年左右就有人定居的杰内－杰诺则遭废弃。到15世纪，杰内已是一座有城墙的商业城邦，松散地向马里纳贡，塔加扎的盐、比图的黄金与奴隶、铜、棉花、染布、稻米和鱼在此转手。第一座清真寺建于13世纪或14世纪初：苏丹昆布鲁皈依伊斯兰教后拆毁宫殿，在原址建寺，后来的统治者添建高塔和围墙，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德又加以重修。1444年，杰内科伊统治着这座富庶且大体独立的河畔城镇，穆斯林商人和学者把它的市场同廷巴克图连在一起；1447年，热那亚人安东尼奥·马尔方特从撒哈拉绿洲图瓦特写信回乡，根据商人的讲述首次向欧洲报告这座城镇。

1471年，桑海的松尼·阿里围城约六个月才攻下杰内：巴尼河的洪水护住了城，却也让他调来河上舰队，把城困到粮尽。围城中苏丹去世，年幼的儿子议和，孩子的母亲嫁给了松尼·阿里。阿斯基亚王朝时，杰内约有四万居民，杰内蒙迪奥负责征收关税。葡萄牙船长杜阿尔特·帕谢科·佩雷拉1507年前后听闻这是一座有城墙、「多黄金」的城市，若昂·德·巴罗斯则写道杰内曾比廷巴克图更有名；利奥·阿非利加努斯见过商人在涨水期划着窄独木舟前往廷巴克图。

1591年桑海在通迪比战败后，朱达尔帕夏的摩洛哥火绳枪兵越过撒哈拉洗劫杰内，1599年又在城下击败一支马里军队。贸易比征服更持久：1655年，编年史家萨迪仍称杰内是穆斯林的大市场之一，塔加扎的盐与比图的黄金在此相会。摩洛哥人的控制1630年后瓦解，18世纪初，比通·库利巴利以塞古为中心的班巴拉国家把杰内并入版图。1818年，塞库·阿马杜建立富拉尼人的马西纳国家，他的圣战使杰内转入1821年统治这里的政权之手。

en:
Yatenga is the northern Mossi country beyond the upper Volta rivers, a dry grazing land where cattle and horses bred the cavalry on which a naaba's power rested. The kingdom took shape among the Mossi states in the fourteenth century, tradition naming Naaba Yadega as its founder, and it grew strong by swallowing Zondoma, the country around Gursi, also written Gourcy. Its horsemen raided as far as the Niger bend and twice occupied Timbuktu; Sonni Ali of Songhai spent his last campaigns on this frontier and died on one of them in 1492. In 1444 Yatenga kept the old Mossi cults, answered to its own warrior king, and lived by livestock, tribute and raiding rather than the trade of the Muslim river cities.

Askia Muhammad ended the long border war with a crushing victory in 1498, but Yatenga kept both its independence and its hostility to Islam. By the mid-eighteenth century the crown had weakened: about a dozen naabas had followed one another in half a century while the provincial nakomse chiefs held the real power. Naaba Kango, driven into exile at Ségou by his cousin Wobgo, came back in 1757 with Bambara soldiers carrying flintlocks, the first firearms seen in Yatenga; he won the civil war, curbed the nakomse and built himself a new capital at Ouahigouya. After Kango died in 1787 the succession quarrels returned, yet in 1821 Yatenga still stood alone, a Mossi kingdom on horseback with Fulbe jihad armies gathering beyond its northern border.
zh:
雅滕加是沃尔特河上游以北的莫西人国度，干旱草场牧牛养马，繁育出支撑「纳巴」王权的骑兵。王国14世纪在诸莫西政权中成形，相传纳巴·亚德加是开国之君；它后来兼并宗多马，即古尔西（Gursi，亦作Gourcy）一带，国力随之壮大。雅滕加骑兵远征尼日尔河河湾，曾两度占领廷巴克图；桑海的松尼·阿里最后几次征战就在这条边地，1492年死在征途中。1444年的雅滕加保留莫西旧信仰，听命于尚武的本族国王，靠牲畜、贡赋和抄掠为生，不靠尼日尔河穆斯林城市的买卖。

1498年，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德以一场大胜结束漫长的边境战争，但雅滕加既保住独立，也保住对伊斯兰教的敌意。到18世纪中期，王权已经衰弱：半个世纪里换了十几位纳巴，实权落到地方首领「纳孔塞」手中。纳巴·坎戈被堂亲沃布戈逐到塞古避难，1757年带着使用燧发枪的班巴拉士兵归国，那是雅滕加第一次见到火器；他打赢内战、压制纳孔塞，在瓦希古亚另建新都。坎戈1787年死后，继承纷争重起，但1821年的雅滕加仍是一个马上的莫西王国，独自面对北方边外集结的富尔贝圣战大军。

en:
Gurma is the wooded savanna east of the Volta basin, home of the Gourmantché, or Gulmanceba, whose language and chiefdoms were close to those of the Mossi but whose open frontier faced the Niger. Early in the thirteenth century Diaba Lompo founded Bingo, the nucleus of later Fada N'Gourma; Bilanga, where the 1444 ruler sat, was also remembered as an early capital of the country. Ivory, cattle and grain moved through its markets, and the roads from Dendi carried news of the empires beyond the river. In 1444 a Gourmantché king keeping the old local cults ruled from Bilanga, on the exposed southern edge of the Songhai world.

The storm came in the sixteenth century, when Songhai armies marched repeatedly into Gourma and Askia Ishaq II twice campaigned there in person. After the Saadians destroyed his army at Tondibi in 1591, the defeated askia was deposed and driven south; he sought shelter at Bilanga, one of the towns he had himself raided, and on his first night there the townspeople broke into the house and killed him. Gourma outlived the empire that had harried it, and through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries Fada N'Gourma, whose Hausa name means 'residence of the chief of Gourma', was the center of a Gourmantché state. In 1821 its kings still ruled from there, independent and unconverted, between the Niger successor states and the Volta peoples.
zh:
古尔马是沃尔特盆地以东的林木草原，住着古尔曼切人，又称古尔芒塞巴人；他们的语言和酋邦与莫西人相近，敞开的边地却朝向尼日尔河。13世纪初，迪亚巴·隆波建立宾戈，即后来法达恩古尔马的雏形；比朗加也曾是古尔马早期的都城之一，1444年的统治者就驻在这里。象牙、牲畜和谷物在当地市集流转，登迪方向来的道路带来河外诸帝国的消息。1444年，信奉本地旧信仰的古尔曼切国王从比朗加发号施令，国土正对着桑海势力暴露的南缘。

风暴在16世纪到来：桑海军队一再开进古尔马，阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世还曾两度亲征。1591年萨阿德人在通迪比摧毁他的军队后，这位战败的阿斯基亚被废黜、逐向南方，到比朗加寻求庇护，那正是他本人抄掠过的城镇之一；到镇上的第一夜，居民便冲进住处把他杀死。古尔马比侵扰它的帝国存续得更久，16至17世纪，法达恩古尔马（豪萨语意为「古尔马酋长居所」）是古尔曼切政权的中心。1821年，那里的国王依旧独立、未改宗，夹在尼日尔河诸后继政权与沃尔特各族之间。

en:
Wagadugu, also called Wogodogo, lies on the grain-bearing central plateau of the White Volta basin, among the millet fields of the Mossi heartland. The Nyonyonse founded the first settlement, Kombemtinga, in the eleventh century. Mossi tradition traces the royal line to the princess Yennenga, who fled her father's house disguised as a man, and Rialé, a Mande elephant hunter; their descendant Oubri took the town, which was renamed Wogdgo, 'come and honor me'. In 1441 Naba Niandéfo made it his capital, though the kings long kept moving their court between favored villages. In 1444 it was still a raw new seat of the mogho naba, the Mossi high king, maintained by cavalry levies, court elders and ancestral rites.

The empires of the Niger bend knew the Mossi as raiders: in the fifteenth century Mossi horsemen seized Timbuktu and sacked the trading post of Walata. Askia Muhammad answered in 1497 with an Islamic holy war, defeated the Wogodogo army, yet could take neither the kingdom nor its old cults. When the Saadians broke Songhai after 1591 the pressure from the north lifted, and trade with Fula and Malian lands grew through the eighteenth century. When Naba Doulougou let the town's first mosque be built early in the nineteenth century, the court kept its ancestral ceremonies beside it. In 1821 Wagadugu remained the strongest of the Mossi monarchies, its king ruling with his council while Fulbe jihad states formed around it.
zh:
瓦加杜古又称沃戈多戈，位于白沃尔特盆地盛产谷物的中央高原，四周是莫西腹地的粟田。尼尼翁塞人11世纪在此建立最早的聚落孔贝姆廷加。莫西传说把王室世系追溯到女扮男装逃离父家的娅南加公主，和曼德象猎人里亚莱；他们的后裔乌布里夺取此城，城改名沃格多戈，意为「来向我致敬」。1441年，纳巴·尼昂德福定都于此，但国王们很久之后仍在喜爱的村落间迁徙宫廷。1444年的瓦加杜古还是莫戈·纳巴（莫西大王）一个全新的驻地，靠骑兵征发、宫廷长老和祖先祭祀维系。

尼日尔河湾的诸国都把莫西人当作抄掠者：15世纪，莫西骑兵一度攻占廷巴克图，洗劫商站瓦拉塔。1497年，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德以伊斯兰圣战回应，击败沃戈多戈的军队，却没能征服王国、改掉旧祭。1591年后萨阿德人击灭桑海，北方压力随之消解；18世纪，与富尔贝和马里地方的贸易增长。纳巴·杜卢古19世纪初允许城内修建第一座清真寺时，宫廷在寺旁奉行的还是祖先典礼。1821年，瓦加杜古仍是最强大的莫西王国，国王与宫廷会议共同执政，周围则有一个个富尔贝圣战政权成形。

en:
The rain forest between the Pra and the Ofin is Akan country, laced with rivers that wash gold out of the hills. Its villages were organized through matrilineal clans, and authority sat with lineage stools and the shrines that guarded them; farm produce, kola nuts and gold dust linked the forest to the coast and to the northern markets. In 1444 no single court ruled the whole region, and the eastern lands around Akyem Kotoku belonged to local Akan chiefs, while Denkyira and Akwamu overshadowed their neighbours. By 1629 Dutch maps called this eastern district Akim, the Great Acani, and later in the century Akyem was an inland power in its own right, holding the goldfields and the roads that led south to European ships.

The power that finally overtopped them began a little way west, at Kumasi. Osei Tutu founded the town in the 1680s, and tradition puts the choice of site on his priest Okomfo Anokye, who planted two kum seeds and declared that whichever sprouted would mark the capital; Kumasi means 'under the kum tree'. Osei Tutu made the town his seat in 1695, and Anokye gave the new union its emblem when, according to legend, he called the Golden Stool down from the sky to land on the king's lap, a seat believed to hold the soul of the Asante nation. The Asante army crushed Denkyira in 1701, opening the roads from the goldfields to the Dutch and other European traders on the coast.

Akyem bloodied the new power more than once. Its men fought beside Denkyira against Osei Tutu and killed the king themselves in 1717, ambushing him as he crossed the Pra. The next year the Aowin king Ebirimoro sacked Kumasi itself, until Opoku Ware I drove the invaders out; he then turned on Akyem and broke it in 1742, after which Abuakwa and Kotoku went their separate ways. Akyem had its revenge of a kind in 1764, when it joined Fante, Dahomey and Oyo to beat the Asante at Atakpame, though Osei Kwadwo's victory the following year reopened the road to Accra. In 1817 Kumasi was the capital of an Asante empire commanding the gold-bearing forest.
zh:
普拉河与奥芬河之间的雨林是阿肯人的土地，河川从山里冲刷出砂金。村寨按母系氏族组织，权力系于各氏族的凳子和守护祖龛；农产品、柯拉果和金砂把这片森林同海岸和北方市场连在一起。1444年全境没有共主，阿基姆·科托库周围的东部土地归各地阿肯酋长所有，登基拉和阿夸穆则凌驾于邻邦之上。到1629年，荷兰地图把这一东部地区标作阿基姆，即「大阿卡尼」；该世纪后期，阿基姆已是一支内陆强权，据有金矿区和通往南方欧洲商船的道路。

最终压过它们的强权，起家于稍西的库马西。奥塞·图图于1680年代建城，相传选址出自他的祭司奥孔福·阿诺基耶之手：他种下两粒库姆树籽，宣布哪一粒发芽，都城就设在哪里，而库马西的意思就是「库姆树下」。1695年奥塞·图图定都于此。据传说，阿诺基耶召来金凳子自天而降，落在国王膝上；这张金凳被视为阿散蒂民族魂魄所寄，是新联盟的标志。1701年，阿散蒂军队击灭登基拉，打通了金矿区到海岸荷兰等欧洲商人之间的道路。

阿基姆不止一次让这个新强权流血。它先与登基拉并肩对抗奥塞·图图，又在1717年亲手杀死他：奥塞·图图渡普拉河时中了阿基姆人的埋伏。次年，阿温王埃比里莫罗洗劫库马西，奥波库·瓦雷一世将入侵者逐出，随后转攻阿基姆，于1742年将其击败，阿布阿克瓦和科托库此后各自分立。1764年，阿基姆联合芳蒂、达荷美和奥约，在阿塔帕梅击败阿散蒂，但奥塞·夸杜沃次年取胜，重新打通前往阿克拉的道路。1817年，库马西已是控制含金雨林的阿散蒂帝国都城。

en:
The Gold Coast takes its name from the gold dust Akan traders carried south through the forest to the Gulf of Guinea. At its eastern end in 1444, the Accra plain belonged to the Gã-Adangbe, fishing and salt-making towns ruled by a king from inland Ayawaso. Salt and dried fish went north in exchange for gold, though the busiest beaches were still Ada and Prampram to the east, and the heavy surf kept European ships from landing.

The Portuguese built a small fort at Osu in the 1550s, but the townspeople destroyed it and trade returned to the beach. Other powers then crowded the shore. The Dutch raised Fort Crèvecœur, the Swedes built a fortified lodge at Osu in 1652 that their former agent Carloff seized for Denmark in 1658 and enlarged as Fort Christiansborg, and the English built James Fort. The kingdom of Accra grew rich on the traffic until the Akwamuhene Ansa Sasraku sacked Ayawaso and beheaded King Okai Koi in 1677; four years later his armies burned the coastal towns and drove the king's heir into exile, after which captives replaced gold as the staple export. In 1693 the Akwamu broker Asameni took men into Christiansborg disguised as merchants buying goods, overpowered the fever-thinned garrison and kept the castle for a year, flying the Danish flag while trading with ships of every nation; he then sold it back to the Danes for fifty marks of gold. Akyem forces overthrew Akwamu in 1730, and in 1742 Opoku Ware of Asante conquered Akyem, after which the Asante kings collected ground-rent and tribute from the Accra forts for the rest of the eighteenth century.
zh:
「黄金海岸」得名于阿肯商人穿过森林南运到几内亚湾的金沙。1444年，东端的阿克拉平原属于加-阿丹格贝人，这些以渔盐为业的村镇由国王在内地的阿亚瓦索统辖；食盐和咸鱼北运换取黄金，不过最繁忙的海滩还在东边的阿达和普兰普兰，汹涌的拍岸浪使欧洲船只无法靠岸。

葡萄牙人1550年代在奥苏建了一座小堡，不久就被当地人摧毁，贸易重新回到海滩上。随后其他列强沿岸相继建堡：荷兰人筑起克雷夫科尔堡，瑞典人1652年在奥苏筑成设防商馆，原先替瑞典人效力的卡尔洛夫1658年转而替丹麦夺下它，扩建成克里斯蒂安斯堡，英国人则建起詹姆斯堡。阿克拉王国靠贸易富足，直到1677年阿夸穆国王安萨·萨斯拉库攻陷阿亚瓦索、处死国王奥凯·科伊；四年后他的军队又焚毁沿岸城镇，迫使王储流亡，此后俘虏取代黄金成为主要出口。1693年，阿夸穆商人阿萨梅尼带人扮成进货的商人混入克里斯蒂安斯堡，制服了被热病削弱的守军，把城堡据有一年，挂着丹麦旗和各国船只交易，最后以50马克黄金卖回给丹麦人。1730年阿基姆联军攻灭阿夸穆，1742年阿散蒂国王奥波库·瓦雷征服阿基姆，此后直到18世纪末，阿散蒂国王一直向阿克拉各座商堡收取地租和贡赋。

en:
The country between the Abomey plateau and the coastal lagoons was the land of the Aja and the Fon. Aja migrants from Tado on the Mono River founded Allada, called Great Ardra, probably around the 13th century, and its kings ruled the surrounding plain from the town of the same name. In 1444 Allada was the strongest power of this hinterland, its towns and villages living off the farms of the plateau; the Fon country around Abomey, inland to the north, was still in its shadow.

Portuguese traders reached Allada in the 1470s, and Great Ardra grew rich selling captives to European ships, with perhaps 30,000 people in its capital at the height of the trade. On the Abomey plateau a rival Fon dynasty built its own kingdom. King Houegbadja founded Abomey in the mid-17th century and laid out the walled royal palaces, a cluster of courts where each later king added his own buildings and recorded his victories on polychrome earthen bas-reliefs. His grandson Agaja made Dahomey a military power: his armies took Allada itself in 1724 and the slave port of Whydah in 1727, putting the coast and its European trade under the crown's control.

Dahomey's armies were famous for their women's regiment, the Mino, 'our mothers' in Fon; Europeans called them Amazons. It began under Houegbadja as a corps of elephant hunters, and tradition credits his daughter Queen Hangbe with a female royal guard; the Mino fought in the assault on Whydah. The long wars with Oyo ended around 1740 with Dahomey paying tribute, but under Tegbesu the sale of captives through Whydah became the crown's chief revenue, paying for the standing army, the women's regiment and the annual royal Customs held at Abomey. In 1818 Ghezo seized the throne and turned the regiment from a palace guard into a full fighting corps.
zh:
阿波美高原与沿海潟湖之间是阿贾人与丰人的土地。相传阿贾人从莫诺河畔的塔多迁来，约在13世纪建起名为「大阿尔德拉」的阿拉达，其王以同名都城统治周围平原。1444年，阿拉达是这片内陆最强的政权，城乡都靠高原上的农田为生；北方内陆阿波美一带的丰人仍活在它的势力之下。

1470年代，葡萄牙商人来到阿拉达，大阿尔德拉靠向欧洲商船出售俘虏致富，贸易最盛时都城人口约有三万。阿波美高原上，一支对立的丰人王族建起自己的王国。国王乌埃格巴贾在17世纪中叶创建阿波美，规划了围墙环绕的王宫；这是一片宫院群落，后来每位国王都在其中增建宫室，把自己的胜绩绘在彩色泥塑浮雕上。其孙阿加贾把达荷美打造成军事强国：1724年攻陷阿拉达本土，1727年又夺取奴隶贸易港维达，把海岸和对欧贸易都置于王室控制之下。

达荷美的军队以女子军团闻名，丰语称之为米诺，意为「我们的母亲」，欧洲人则叫她们「亚马孙人」。这支部队在乌埃格巴贾时本是一队猎象人，相传他的女儿汉格贝女王养了一支女子卫队；攻打维达时，她们已经上阵。与奥约的长期战争约在1740年以达荷美纳贡告终，但特格贝苏在位时，经维达出售俘虏成为王室最大财源，供养着常备军、女子军团和阿波美每年一度的王家祭典。1818年盖佐夺取王位，把这支部队从王宫卫队扩编为正式的作战军团。

en:
Whydah is no harbour: sandbars seal its lagoon from the surf, and everything landed here came through the breakers by canoe. In 1444 the Hueda, a Gbe-speaking people, farmed and fished these beaches in small towns under a king ruling at Savi, within the loose orbit of the Aja kings of Allada; the port itself was called Glēxwé, the Farmhouse. Lagoon canoes carried salt and dried fish along the Slave Coast, and no European factory yet stood on the shore.

Portuguese ships first called in the 1580s, and by the 1680s the kings of Whydah had made the open roadstead one of the great markets of the Atlantic slave trade. The English Royal African Company secured a permanent factory in 1684, later William's Fort, and Brandenburgers, Dutchmen and Frenchmen built rival lodges beside it; unlike the stone castles of the Gold Coast, these were flimsy posts of mud and straw, whose guns were fired more often in salute than in anger. In 1716 the crew of the slaver Whydah Gally found this the second-busiest port on the coast when they bought five hundred captives from King Haffon for Jamaica. Haffon, whose crown was a gift from Portugal, granted the Portuguese land for Fort São João Baptista in 1721. His reign ended in March 1727, when Agaja of Dahomey's army overran Savi and Whydah without warning, burned the king's town and carried off forty European traders to his camp at Allada, freeing seven of them a fortnight later. The long wars with Oyo that followed left Dahomey an Oyo tributary, and the European lodges became rent-paying tenants of Dahomey's viceroy while captives kept shipping through the surf for the rest of the century. In 1818 the Brazilian trader Francisco Félix de Souza helped Ghezo seize the throne and took the title of chacha, master of Whydah's trade.
zh:
维达根本没有港口：沙洲把潟湖与大海隔开，一切货物都得靠独木舟穿过拍岸浪运上岸。1444年，讲格贝语的惠达人在这些海滩上耕作捕鱼，村镇由驻在萨维的国王统辖，大致处在阿拉达的阿贾诸王势力范围内；港口本身叫格莱韦，意思是「农舍」。潟湖中的独木舟把食盐和咸鱼贩运到奴隶海岸各处，岸上还没有欧洲商馆。

葡萄牙船只最早在1580年代到访，到1680年代，维达诸王已把这段开阔锚地经营成大西洋奴隶贸易最大的市场之一。英国皇家非洲公司1684年在此设常设商馆，即后来的威廉堡，勃兰登堡人、荷兰人和法国人也在旁边建起互争短长的商馆；和黄金海岸的石头城堡不同，这些只是泥木搭成的简陋商站，大炮鸣放礼宾的时候多，真正开火的时候少。1716年，贩奴船「维达号」的船员向哈丰国王买下五百名俘虏运往牙买加，此时维达已是这段海岸第二繁忙的奴隶港。哈丰的王冠是葡萄牙所赠，1721年他又划地给葡萄牙人修建圣若昂·巴普蒂斯塔堡。1727年3月，达荷美国王阿加扎的军队出其不意攻陷萨维和维达，焚毁王城，把四十名欧洲商人掳到他在阿拉达的大营，十四天后放了其中七人。此后达荷美与奥约长期交战，最终沦为奥约的纳贡国，各国商馆则成了向达荷美总督纳租的房客，整个18世纪，俘虏仍源源不断穿过拍岸浪装船外运。1818年，巴西商人弗朗西斯科·费利克斯·德·索萨帮助盖佐夺取王位，受封「恰恰」，执掌维达贸易。

en:
Dendi means 'down the river' in Songhai, and this is the stretch where the Niger leaves the desert: below Gao the valley opens into farming country, and as the floods withdrew, millet and rice went into the fields. Riverain Songhai and the older Tyenga villagers fished, farmed and carried grain, salt and kola nuts to Borgu and Hausaland; the river markets around Gaya were the province's chief places. Governors came from the court at Gao, but the river chiefs kept much of their own authority, and the river cults outlived the Islam of the towns. In 1444 Dendi was the southernmost province of the Songhai state under the Sonni kings, Muslim at court, with the villagers still largely given to the old rites.

Dendi gave the dynasty its most famous king and the empire its last refuge. Sonni Ali, who came to power in 1464 and took Timbuktu and Djenné, had grown up among his Dendi mother's people, reared in the downstream traditions. In March 1591 the Saadian army broke the Songhai host at Tondibi, and Askia Nuh, a son of Askia Dawud, led the surviving court and thousands of Songhai downstream, founded a capital at Lulami south of Say, and wore out Moroccan expeditions until 1599. The pasha Mesaoud sacked Lulami in 1639, during the reign of Askia Ismail, yet the askias held on for centuries more in small Muslim chiefdoms, and Dendi traders kept the old caravans moving to Borgu and Hausaland.
zh:
登迪在桑海语中意为「河的下游」，尼日尔河正是在这一段离开沙漠：过了加奥，河谷展宽为农耕之乡，洪水退去后，粟和稻播进田里。沿河桑海人和更早的廷加村人捕鱼耕作，把谷物、盐和可乐果运往博尔古和豪萨兰，加亚一带的河埠是本省的首镇。长官由加奥朝廷派出，河酋却保留着大半权威，河畔村落的河水崇拜也比城里的伊斯兰更为久长。1444年，登迪是松尼王朝桑海国家最南端的行省，宫廷是穆斯林的天下，村民则大多仍守旧礼。

登迪为王朝送出了最有名的君主，也为帝国留下了最后的退路。1464年即位、攻取廷巴克图和杰内的松尼·阿里，幼年便在登迪籍母亲的族人中按河乡旧俗长大。1591年3月，萨阿德军队在通迪比击溃桑海大军，阿斯基亚·达乌德之子阿斯基亚·努赫率残存朝廷和数千桑海人顺河南下，在赛以南建都卢拉米，与摩洛哥远征军周旋到1599年。1639年，帕夏梅萨乌德趁阿斯基亚·伊斯梅尔在位洗劫卢拉米，但诸阿斯基亚在若干穆斯林小酋长国里又延续了数百年，登迪商人也照旧把商队赶往博尔古和豪萨兰。

en:
Borgu is the rolling savanna watered by the middle Niger and its tributaries, home of the Bariba, or Borgawa. Mounted Wasangari lords ruled a loose confederacy of three kingdoms from their walled towns: Bussa, Nikki and Illo. Bussa, the oldest of the three, stood at the limit of navigation on the Niger, just above the rapids where caravans from the north met canoes coming upriver; Wasangari kings kept Karabonde earth-priests at their courts, and the richer market town of Nikki often overshadowed it. In 1444 the Borgu kings still held to the old gods and guarded the trade routes against the Muslim empires to the north.

War filled Borgu's next three centuries. When Nupe crushed Oyo at the end of the 15th century, the Alaafin Onigbogi took refuge at the Borgu court, and the two allies built up their cavalry together. Songhai came anyway: Sunni Ali's invasion was badly mauled in the 1490s, and Askia Muhammad's army of 1505 briefly held Bussa before the Borgawa drove it out. After Songhai collapsed in 1591, Oyo turned on its former ally and reduced Borgu to vassalage, until a Borgu victory in 1783 restored its independence.

The Bussa rapids gave Borgu its best-known European visitor. In 1806 the Scottish explorer Mungo Park, following the course of the Niger on his second expedition, ran his boat onto a rock in the narrows below the town. Warriors gathered on the bank and loosed arrows and spears at the party; Park and his officers jumped into the Niger and drowned, and only one of their guides lived to give an account. His journal was never recovered. Park's first journey of 1795 to 1797 had taken a European as far inland as Segou, and the book he published afterwards made the Niger known to readers across Europe.
zh:
博尔古是尼日尔河中游及其支流滋润的起伏稀树草原，居民是巴里巴人，又称博尔加瓦人。骑马的瓦桑加里贵族以设防城镇为根基，统治着布萨、尼基、伊洛三个王国组成的松散联盟。三国之中布萨最古老，城在急流上游、尼日尔河通航的尽头，北方商队在这里与溯河而来的独木舟换货；瓦桑加里诸王的宫廷中任用卡拉邦德地祭司，而更富庶的市集城镇尼基常常盖过它的风头。1444年，博尔古诸王仍信奉旧神，据守商路，与北方的穆斯林帝国抗衡。

此后三个世纪，博尔古战火不断。15世纪末努佩击败奥约，奥约的阿拉芬·奥尼格博吉逃入博尔古王廷避难，两个盟友一同扩建骑兵。桑海仍一再来犯：桑尼·阿里的入侵在1490年代遭重创，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德1505年的大军一度占领布萨，最终被博尔加瓦人击退。1591年桑海崩溃后，奥约反戈攻打旧日盟友，把博尔古降为属国，直到1783年博尔古一战获胜才恢复独立。

布萨急流还带来了博尔古最出名的欧洲访客。1806年，苏格兰探险家蒙哥·帕克第二次沿尼日尔河下行考察，船在布萨城下的窄道撞上礁石。岸上聚集的武士朝船队放箭投矛，帕克和同伴跳入尼日尔河溺亡，只有一名向导活下来讲述经过，他的日志再也没能找回。帕克1795至1797年的第一次考察曾让欧洲人深入到塞古，回国后出版的旅行记风行欧洲，也让欧洲读者第一次知道尼日尔河。

en:
Oyo-Ile, the walled capital of the Oyo Empire, stood in the northern Yoruba savanna, where horse-buyers from the Niger bend met traders carrying kola and cloth south to the forest. Tradition calls Oranmiyan, a prince of Ile-Ife, its founder around 1300: at Bussa a local chief gave him a snake with a charm at its throat, and the king built where the serpent stopped. His successors ruled as Alaafin, 'owner of the palace', from the Afin beside the Akesan market. Shango, Oranmiyan's son by a Nupe princess, was later worshipped as the god of thunder. By 1400 tribute from neighbouring towns and the long-distance markets had made Oyo a formidable inland power. In 1444 its rule reached no further than metropolitan Yorubaland, and the Alaafin drilled cavalry in the manner of the peoples to the north.

The Nupe cut that power short: around 1535 they sacked Oyo-Ile and drove the Alaafin into exile in Borgu. The dynasty returned eighty years later with armour and cavalry, ruling first from Oyo-Igboho. Eguguojo conquered nearly all Yorubaland, and his sister Orompoto, the first female Alaafin, used horses bought in Borgu to drive the Nupe back in 1555 and formed a cavalry corps. Early in the seventeenth century Abipa rebuilt Oyo-Ile. Cavalry could not take Benin, where the Ekiti hills broke the charge, but southward raids began in 1682, and after eleven campaigns Dahomey accepted tribute in 1748. The eighteenth century was Oyo's peak, fed by horses, captives and European goods from the coast; Muslim clerks kept the Alaafin's records in Arabic. Palace politics then undid it: from 1754 the Bashorun Gaha forced four Alaafins to ritual suicide, sending each the parrot's egg that commanded death, until Alaafin Abiodun put him to death in 1774. Campaigns against Borgu and Nupe ended in defeat, and in 1795 the war-lord Afonja sacked Apomu, a market town of holy Ife, at Alaafin Awole's command, then marched on Oyo-Ile and forced Awole to suicide. In 1817 Afonja declared Ilorin independent with Fulani and Muslim allies, and as 1821 opened Fulani raiders were pressing into Oyo's northern villages.
zh:
奥约伊莱（旧奥约）是奥约帝国的城墙都城，矗立在约鲁巴北部的稀树草原上，从尼日尔河湾来买马的商人与南运柯拉果、布匹入森林的商人在此交易。相传约1300年，伊费王子奥兰米扬营建此城：他在布萨受当地酋长指点，跟随一条颈悬符咒的大蛇前行，在大蛇停下的地方筑都。后继诸王以「阿拉芬」（意为「宫殿之主」）为号，在阿克桑市场旁的阿芬宫理政。奥兰米扬与努佩王妃所生的儿子尚戈，后来被约鲁巴人奉为雷神。到1400年，邻邦贡赋和长途商市已使奥约成为内陆强国。1444年时，它的统治还不出约鲁巴腹地，阿拉芬正仿效北方各族操练骑兵。

努佩人打断了这股势头：约1535年，努佩军队洗劫奥约伊莱，阿拉芬流亡博尔古。八十年后，王朝带着铠甲和骑兵卷土重来，最初以奥约伊格博霍为都。埃古古奥朱征服了几乎整个约鲁巴兰，他的姐姐奥龙波托是第一位女性阿拉芬，用从博尔古买来的马在1555年击退努佩人，并组建骑兵军。17世纪初，阿比帕重修奥约伊莱。骑兵在埃基蒂丘陵前冲不动，攻贝宁无果，但南征从1682年开始，经过十一次征战，达荷美于1748年称臣纳贡。马匹、俘虏和海岸来的欧洲商货让18世纪成为奥约的顶峰，穆斯林书吏以阿拉伯文为阿拉芬掌文书。随后宫廷政治毁了帝国：1754年起，首辅加哈向每位失势的阿拉芬赐下命令赴死的鹦鹉蛋，逼迫四位阿拉芬相继仪式性自杀，直到1774年阿拉芬阿比奥敦将他处死。征博尔古、讨努佩又接连战败。1795年，军阀阿丰贾奉阿拉芬阿沃莱之命洗劫圣地伊费的市镇阿波穆，随后进军奥约伊莱，逼阿沃莱自尽。1817年，阿丰贾联合富拉尼人和穆斯林势力据伊洛林独立；1821年开始时，富拉尼骑兵已在袭掠奥约北方的村庄。

en:
The Nupe country fills the basin between the Niger and the Kaduna, where the canoe road to the Niger bend meets the tracks coming south from Hausaland. Its towns farmed the fertile floodplain, fished the river and kept long markets in cloth, grain and iron; Nku is remembered as the earliest Bini settlement. In 1444 they still answered to separate chiefs. The man tradition names as their unifier was Tsoede, a prince of the Attah's court at Idah, born to a Nupe mother, who fled down the Niger to his mother's people.

Tradition places his conquests in the middle and later fifteenth century: Tsoede, also called Edegi, subdued the river towns one by one and took the title Etsu, 'king', making Nupe a power between the two rivers. Within a century Nupe armies could sack Oyo-Ile and drive the Alaafin out of his capital. The later Etsus ruled through the chiefs of the river towns until Etsu Jibiri, about 1770, became the first Muslim ruler. Etsu Ma'azu held Nupe at its greatest strength, but in the 1790s rival claimants, Jimada and Majiya II, split the kingdom, and from 1806 the Sokoto jihad crossed its borders under Abdullahi dan Fodio. When Ma'azu died in 1818 the succession wars that followed left the old kingdom under the control of Gwandu.
zh:
努佩之地位于尼日尔河与卡杜纳河之间的盆地，通往尼日尔河湾的水路与从豪萨兰南下的商道在此相接。一座座城镇在肥沃的河漫滩农耕、在大河中捕鱼，维系着布匹、谷物和铁器的长途市集；恩库被追认为比尼支系最早的定居点。1444年时，各城镇仍由各自的酋长统治。传统中统一努佩的人叫措埃德，他本是伊达阿塔王庭中的王子，母亲是努佩人，后来沿尼日尔河逃到母亲的族人中间。

相传他的征服在15世纪中后期：措埃德又名埃代吉，逐个降服沿河城镇，取号「埃措」（意为「王」），使努佩成为两河之间的强国。不到一百年，努佩军队便能攻陷奥约伊莱，把阿拉芬逐出国都。后来的埃措们依靠沿河城镇的酋长统治，直到约1770年，埃措·吉比里成为第一位穆斯林君主。埃措·马阿祖在位时努佩最为强盛，但1790年代吉马达与马吉亚二世争立，国家分裂；1806年起，阿卜杜拉希·丹·福迪奥率索科托圣战军攻入其境。1818年马阿祖死后，继位纷争中的旧王国落入格万杜控制。

en:
Ile-Ife lies among the forest hills of inner Yorubaland, the holiest city of the Yoruba, who hold that the world began there when Oduduwa scattered the first handful of earth over the primordial waters. A wall some seven kilometres round was built from the tenth or eleventh century, and behind it the dynasty of Oduduwa has ruled as Ooni ever since. From Ife's gates went out the princes who founded the other Yoruba kingdoms: Oranmiyan gave Benin its Oba dynasty and then rode north to found Oyo. Between 1200 and 1400 the casters of Ife made the naturalistic bronze, brass and terracotta heads for which the city is known, working for King Obalufon II, who is said to have invented brass casting; its glass beads have been found as far away as Mali and Mauritania. A five-metre stone monolith called the Staff of Oranmiyan stood in a grove where the founder was said to have died. By 1420 the workshops had fallen quiet as power and trade moved to Benin and Oyo, and in 1444 Ife was a walled city of priests, farmers and craftsmen, its Ooni still the spiritual father of every Yoruba king.

No Alaafin of Oyo dared march on Ife, for every one of them swore at his crowning never to attack the city. The oath was broken in 1795, when the war-lord Afonja sacked Apomu, Ife's market town, on Alaafin Awole's order and then turned his army against Awole himself, the sacrilege from which Oyo never recovered. Ife held back from the wars that afterwards tore Yorubaland apart, but in 1821 its army marched with the Ijebu against Owu Ipole, opening the Owu war that filled the roads with refugees and closed the age of the old Yoruba cities.
zh:
伊莱伊费深藏在约鲁巴腹地的森林丘陵间，是约鲁巴人最神圣的城市；按他们的信仰，世界就从这里开始，奥都杜瓦把第一把土撒向洪荒的水面，陆地才隆起。约10至11世纪，这里建起一道周长约七公里的城墙，奥都杜瓦的王朝便以「奥尼」之号在城内统治。各约鲁巴王国的开创者都出自伊费的宫门：奥兰米扬为贝宁建立奥巴王朝，随后北上建立奥约。1200至1400年间，伊费匠师为奥巴卢丰二世铸出写实逼真的青铜、黄铜与赤陶头像，相传黄铜铸造法就是这位国王发明的；伊费的玻璃珠远输马里和毛里塔尼亚。一根高约五米的整石柱「奥兰米扬杖」立在一片林苑中，相传那里是奥兰米扬去世之处。到1420年前后，作坊沉寂，权力和商路转往贝宁与奥约。1444年的伊费是一座城墙环绕的城市，居民是祭司、农夫和工匠，奥尼仍是所有约鲁巴君主的精神之父。

奥约的阿拉芬无人敢犯伊费，每位阿拉芬登基时都立有不攻此城的誓言。誓言在1795年被打破：军阀阿丰贾奉阿拉芬阿沃莱之命洗劫伊费的市镇阿波穆，随即挥师反噬阿沃莱本人，奥约再未从这桩渎圣之举中恢复。此后约鲁巴兰战乱不已，伊费本想置身事外，但1821年还是与伊杰布联兵攻打奥乌伊波莱，奥乌战争随之爆发，道路上尽是逃难的人群，古老约鲁巴城邦的时代走到尽头。

en:
Benin is the Edo forest country around Oredo, the palace quarter of Edo, the walled capital later called Benin City. The early Ogiso rulers united the villages of the region, and after a period of kingship backed from Ife the Oba dynasty established itself in the thirteenth century. Oba Ewedo moved the royal palace into Edo, and Oba Ewuare, who seized the throne in 1440, made the city an armed capital: he rebuilt it after his coup, raised an eleven-kilometre inner rampart and moat with nine fortified gates, laid out broad avenues and led Benin's armies into neighbouring lands. Outer earthen walls run for thousands of kilometres through the surrounding farmland, marking the bounds of towns and fields. Traders entered the city under toll and inspection, while hereditary guilds worked ivory and brass for the Oba; the brass casters of the Igun quarter cast palace plaques and royal heads by lost wax, a craft traced by tradition to Ife. In 1444, four years into Ewuare's reign, a militarised court at Edo controlled the ivory and pepper of the forest behind the most elaborate earthworks in West Africa.

The Portuguese reached Edo in 1485 with Joao Afonso de Aveiro, in the reign of Ozolua, later called the Conqueror, who sent an embassy to Lisbon seeking firearms; missionaries followed in 1514 and did not stay. Around 1504 Esigie won the throne in war against his brother, and in 1515 he and his mother Idia defeated an Igala invasion at Idah; Idia became the first Iyoba, the queen mother, and her ivory mask is Benin's best-known work. Pepper, ivory and brass casts made the sixteenth century wealthy, and the bracelet-shaped manillas sold by Portuguese merchants fed the casters' furnaces. In 1691 a Portuguese captain could still describe Edo as larger than Lisbon, its houses so safe they had no doors, but the Dutch trader David van Nyendael found many of them half ruined in 1701 or 1702. After the succession wars of the early eighteenth century Akenzua I restored strong royal rule, and the palace with its guilds remained the centre of Benin's power as European merchants moved on to newer ports along the coast.
zh:
贝宁是奥雷多周围的埃多人雨林腹地，奥雷多是埃多的宫城区，这座有城墙的都城后来称贝宁城。早期奥吉索统治者联合了各地聚落；经过一段由伊费支持的王政时期，奥巴王朝在13世纪确立。奥巴·埃韦多把王宫迁入埃多，1440年夺取王位的埃瓦雷则把城市变成尚武之都：他在政变后重建都城，筑起周长十一公里、设有九座城门的内城墙与壕沟，辟出宽阔大道，并率军征伐邻地。郊外的土工外墙绵延数千公里，圈出城镇与田野的界线。商人入城须纳税受检，世代相承的行会专为奥巴制作象牙和黄铜器物；伊贡街区的铸匠以失蜡法铸造宫殿饰板和先王头像，这门手艺据说传自伊费。1444年，埃瓦雷即位仅四年，埃多的尚武宫廷控制着雨林的象牙和胡椒，城西非最繁复的土工工事拱卫。

1485年，葡萄牙人随若昂·阿方索·德·阿韦罗抵达埃多，当时在位的是后来被称为「征服者」的奥佐卢阿，他向里斯本遣使寻求火器；1514年传教士前来，却没有久留。约1504年，埃西吉在与兄弟的战争中夺得王位；1515年，他与母亲伊迪亚在伊达击退伊加拉人的入侵，伊迪亚成为第一位「伊约巴」，即王太后，她的象牙面具是贝宁最著名的作品。胡椒、象牙和黄铜器物造就了16世纪的富足，葡萄牙商人贩来的手镯形黄铜环成了铸匠的原料。1691年，一名葡萄牙船长仍称埃多大过里斯本，城中人家夜不闭户；但荷兰商人达维德·范尼恩达尔1701或1702年已看到许多半毁的房屋。18世纪初的继承战争之后，阿肯祖阿一世恢复了强有力的王权；随着欧洲商人转投沿海的新港口，奥巴宫廷和各行会仍是贝宁权力的中心。

en:
Gobir was the northernmost of the seven true Hausa states, and Hausa tradition expected its kings to shield the rest from raiders out of the Sahara. Between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries the Gobirawa held settlements in the Aïr Mountains, until the Tuareg sultanate of Agadez arose early in the fifteenth century and displaced them. They moved south by stages, from Maigali to Goran Rami near Sabon Birni, while the town of Birnin Lalle, whose Hausa name means 'city of henna', commanded the southern country they were entering. Leo Africanus, writing in the early sixteenth century, described many villages of herdsmen and a busy trade in linen textiles and shoes, made, he claimed, like those of the ancient Romans, which Wangara traders carried as far as Timbuktu and Gao. In 1444 Gobir was a Muslim Hausa kingdom living by its herds, forges and looms, while Tuareg pressure kept narrowing its northern lands.

The long retreat kept Gobir at war. Around 1715 its riders joined Agadez and Zamfara to break the supremacy of Kebbi, and the kings then turned against Katsina, Agadez and Zamfara in turn. Early in the eighteenth century the court settled at Birnin Lalle. Under Babari the Gobirawa destroyed Birnin Zamfara and built a new walled capital, Alkalawa, on the Gulbin Rima. The conflict that undid the kingdom began on its own ground: about 1774 Bawa invited the preacher Usman dan Fodio to settle at Degel, and dan Fodio shared in the education of Bawa's nephew Yunfa before his preaching against the exactions of the Hausa elite turned the court against him. Sarki Nafata restricted his followers, and when Yunfa took the throne in 1803 and failed to have his old teacher killed, the Fulani War broke out. Gobir's cavalry had the better of the early fighting at Tsuntua, but in October 1808 Sokoto forces stormed Alkalawa and killed Yunfa. Most of Gobir passed into the Sokoto Caliphate, while survivors of the old dynasty kept fighting from lands to the north.
zh:
戈比尔是豪萨七邦中位置最北的一个，豪萨人的传统是由它的国王替各邦挡住从撒哈拉来的袭掠者。12至14世纪，戈比拉瓦人在阿伊尔山地建有聚落，15世纪初图阿雷格人的阿加德兹苏丹国兴起，把他们挤向南方。他们分批南迁，经迈加里到萨本比尔尼附近的戈兰拉米，比尔宁拉莱（豪萨语意为「散沫花城」）则控制着他们正要进入的南部地带。16世纪初的利奥·阿非利加努斯写到，此地到处是牧人的村落，亚麻织物和鞋履买卖繁忙；他还说那些鞋的样式和古罗马人穿的相仿，由万加拉商人一直贩运到廷巴克图和加奥。1444年，戈比尔是一个靠畜群、铁匠炉和织机立足的穆斯林豪萨王国，北方土地在图阿雷格人的压力下不断收缩。

漫长的南迁让戈比尔始终在打仗。约1715年，它的骑兵与阿加德兹、赞姆法拉联手打破凯比的霸权，随后又依次与卡齐纳、阿加德兹和赞姆法拉交战。18世纪初，王廷设在比尔宁拉莱。巴巴里在位时，戈比拉瓦人攻毁比尔宁赞姆法拉，在古尔宾里马河畔另筑有城墙的新都阿尔卡拉瓦。最后倾覆王国的冲突起于自己境内：约1774年，巴瓦把传道者奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥请到代盖尔定居，丹·福迪奥还教过巴瓦的侄子云法，后来他抨击豪萨权贵的盘剥，王廷转而与他为敌。国王纳法塔限制他的信徒，云法1803年继位后又试图除掉这位旧日老师而未成，富拉尼战争就此爆发。戈比尔骑兵在聪图阿的早期战斗中占了上风，但1808年10月索科托军队攻破阿尔卡拉瓦，杀死云法。戈比尔大部并入索科托哈里发国，旧王朝的余部在北方土地上继续作战。

en:
Katsina sits on the open Hausa savanna where the caravan roads between Gobir, Zamfara, Kano and Daura meet, in country good for cotton, millet, guinea corn and cattle. Tradition places the walled town's beginnings around 1100, and among the seven Hausa states Katsina and Daura were remembered as the two kings of the markets. The royal compound of Gidan Korau is dated to 1348, its Kofar Soro gate opening behind earthen ramparts. In 1444 a Muslim sarki ruled from that palace, and his gates controlled the roads that carried cotton cloth, hides, leather, salt and kola nuts between the Sahara, Hausaland and the southern forests.

The fifteenth century gave the town the Gobarau Mosque, its fifteen-metre mud minaret rising above the roofs; Muhammad al-Maghili, a scholar from Tlemcen, taught in Katsina and tradition connects him with the building, which was inspired by the mosques of Timbuktu. It ran as a madrasa that drew students across Hausaland, and the city produced scholars of its own, above all Muhammad ibn al-Sabbagh, known as Dan Marina, whom the Sokoto caliph Muhammad Bello called 'the teacher'. Askia Muhammad of Songhai conquered Katsina in 1512, and it broke from Gao after the fighting at Karfata in 1554. Its rivalry with Kano ran to an eleven-year war during the reign of Muhammad Rumfa, another offensive in the 1570s and later campaigns around Karayi; after Songhai weakened, Katsina turned to Bornu and sent a hundred slaves at each royal enthronement. By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it was the largest of the seven city-states, with specialised trade quarters and leather workshops. In 1807 Umaru Dallaji's Fulani army overthrew the Wangarawa and made Katsina an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate; the defeated nobles fled north to Maradi, and Dallaji ruled from the old city as its first Fulani emir in 1821.
zh:
卡齐纳坐落在开阔的豪萨草原，戈比尔、赞法拉、卡诺和道拉之间的商路在此相会，周围土地适宜种植棉花、粟和高粱，也宜牧牛。相传这座有城墙的城镇始于约1100年；在豪萨七邦中，卡齐纳和道拉并称两个掌市场的王。王宫科劳宫的传统纪年为1348年，科法尔·索罗门开在土墙之内。1444年，一位穆斯林萨尔基在这座宫殿执政，他的城门把守着商路，棉布、兽皮、皮革、盐和柯拉果沿这些路在撒哈拉、豪萨地区和南方森林之间往来。

15世纪，城里建起戈巴劳清真寺，十五米高的泥筑宣礼塔高出一片屋顶；特莱姆森学者穆罕默德·马吉里曾在卡齐纳讲学，相传建寺也与他有关，寺院的式样受廷巴克图清真寺启发。清真寺兼作伊斯兰学校，吸引豪萨各地的学生；卡齐纳也出了自己的学者，首推穆罕默德·伊本·萨巴格，人称丹·马里纳，索科托哈里发穆罕默德·贝洛称他为「老师」。桑海的阿斯基亚·穆罕默德1512年征服此城，卡齐纳在1554年卡尔法塔之战后脱离加奥。它与卡诺的争霸包括穆罕默德·鲁姆法在位时的十一年战争、1570年代的又一次进攻和后来卡拉伊一带的战事；桑海转弱后，卡齐纳投向博尔诺，每有新王即位就献上一百名奴隶。到17和18世纪，它已是七邦中最大的城邦，拥有专门的商区和皮革作坊。1807年，乌马鲁·达拉杰的富拉尼军队推翻万加拉瓦王朝，把卡齐纳变成索科托哈里发国的埃米尔国，战败的贵族北逃马拉迪；1821年，达拉杰作为首任富拉尼埃米尔在旧城执政。

en:
The Zamfarawa farm the heavy-soiled plains between the Rima and Ka rivers, some of the best grain land in western Hausaland; Heinrich Barth later called it almost the most flourishing country of Negroland. Zamfara was counted among the older Hausa kingdoms, whose early kings ruled from Dutsi and drew the neighboring chiefdoms into one state. Traders carried leather and cloth along the Hausa roads, and the town of Yandoto drew scholars as well as merchants. Tradition also derives the kingdom's name from Fara, a Gobir princess lost in the bush and brought home by Zamfarawa hunters. In 1444 Zamfara was still a small kingdom ruled from Dutsi, its people keeping the old Hausa spirit cults.

Early in the 16th century the kings moved north to the Gagare river and built Birnin Zamfara, whose wall ran eleven miles and opened through fifty gates. Songhai's Askiya had already carried his campaigns through Hausaland: Leo Africanus heard that the king of Zamfara was slain and the country made tributary, though by the mid-1500s Zamfarawa raiders were riding south as far as Yauri. About 1715 Sarkin Zamfara Babba and his son Yakubu joined Gobir and Agadez against their overlord Kebbi, captured its king Muhammadu dan Giwa, and made Zamfara a first-rate power. Gobirawa expelled from Asben by the Tuareg had been given farmland here, and they proved fatal guests: around 1756 Sarkin Gobir Babari destroyed Birnin Zamfara. King Mairoki fled to the hill-fortress of Kiawa, where Bawa Jan Gwarzo besieged him for fifteen years before taking him. In 1804 Usman dan Fodio opened his jihad from a base at Sabon Gari in Zamfara, and the old kingdom was absorbed into the Sokoto Caliphate.
zh:
扎姆法拉人耕作着里马河与卡河之间黏重土壤的平原，这里是西豪萨兰最好的谷物产地之一，后来的海因里希·巴尔特称它几乎是黑人之地最丰饶的乡野。扎姆法拉被算作较早的豪萨古国，早期诸王以杜齐为都，把周围酋邦并成一国。商人沿豪萨商路贩运皮革和布匹，扬多托城既招客商也招学者。当地传说还把国名溯源于一位名叫法拉的戈比尔公主，她在丛林中迷路，被扎姆法拉猎人救下并送回。1444年的扎姆法拉仍是以杜齐为都的小王国，百姓信奉豪萨旧有的精灵崇拜。

16世纪初，诸王北迁加加雷河畔，兴建比尔宁扎姆法拉，城墙绵延十一英里，开有五十座城门。那时桑海的阿斯基亚已用兵豪萨兰：莱奥·阿非利加努斯听说扎姆法拉王兵败被杀、全国称臣，可到16世纪中叶，扎姆法拉骑兵已自行南下劫掠，远及亚武里。约1715年，扎姆法拉王巴巴与王子雅库布联合戈比尔和阿加德兹进攻宗主克比，生俘克比王穆罕默杜·丹·吉瓦，扎姆法拉一跃而为一等强国。被阿加德兹图阿雷格人逐出阿斯班的戈比尔人曾获准在此领田务农，这批来客却成了致命的仇人：约1756年，戈比尔王巴巴里攻毁比尔宁扎姆法拉。扎姆法拉王迈罗基逃入基亚瓦山寨，巴瓦·詹·格瓦佐围城十五年才将他擒获。1804年，奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥以扎姆法拉境内的萨邦加里为基地发动圣战，古国随后并入索科托哈里发国。

en:
Bonny is a low island town in the mouth of the Bonny River, where the Niger Delta opens into the Bight of Biafra. Ibani Ijaw fishermen were its first settlers; they called it Okoloama, after the curlews that nested on the flats, and their king, the amanyanabo, ruled through canoe houses, each with its own fleet and chiefs, that commanded the water lanes between the inland markets and the sea. In 1444 Bonny was still a small fishing town, though the deep water off its beaches already gave it one of the finest anchorages in the delta.

Portuguese ships sailing for Fernão Gomes reached the bight around 1472, and Bonny spent the next three centuries as one of the busiest slave ports on the Slave Coast, serving Portuguese, Dutch and English captains in turn. Under the Pepple dynasty of the eighteenth century the canoe houses kept war canoes on the approaches, their bows mounting heavy guns and each vessel carrying as many as 140 men. In 1790 alone some 20,000 captives, most of them Igbo brought down from the interior, were loaded for the Americas. When Britain abolished the trade in 1807, Bonny's houses kept their fleets and sold palm oil, kernels, ivory and Guinea pepper instead.
zh:
邦尼是邦尼河口一座低洼的海岛城镇，位于尼日尔河三角洲注入比夫拉湾处。最早来定居的是伊巴尼部伊乔渔民，他们称此岛为奥科洛阿马，名字来自在滩涂上成群栖息的杓鹬；首领称「阿马尼亚博」，通过一座座独木船屋施行统治，每座船屋各有船队和首领，掌控着内陆市场通往大海的水道。1444年的邦尼还是一座小渔镇，但岛外水深，已是三角洲上最好的锚地之一。

1472年前后，为费尔南·戈麦斯效力的葡萄牙帆船驶入比夫拉湾，此后三百年间，邦尼一直是奴隶海岸最繁忙的奴隶港之一，先后接待葡萄牙、荷兰和英格兰船长。18世纪佩普尔王朝治下，各船屋在入海通道上部署作战独木舟，船头架着重炮，每艘可载多达一百四十人。仅1790年，就有约两万名俘虏被装船运往美洲，其中多为从内陆贩来的伊博人。1807年英国废止奴隶贸易后，邦尼的各船屋保留了船队，改卖棕榈油、棕榈仁、象牙和几内亚胡椒。

en:
Idah stands on the east bank of the Niger, just below the confluence where the Benue comes in, the oldest royal seat of the Igala people. Their kings, the Attahs, ruled from it over yam farms and hunting grounds between the two rivers, and the town served the middle Niger as a fishing port and market where canoe traders paid in bronze rings and cowries. The dynasty had strange beginnings: tradition makes the first Attah a Jukun princess, Ebuluejeonu, daughter of the king of Jukun, who led her people to Idah in the fifteenth century and was enthroned there. Idah's name also ran upriver, for Nupe tradition makes Tsoede, the first Etsu, a man of the Attah's court who fled down the Niger to found his own kingdom. In 1444 the Attah ruled from Idah as a power of war-canoes at the Niger-Benue confluence.

The great trial came in 1515–1516, when Attah Ayegba Oma Idoko sent his canoes across the Niger against Benin, called in by Benin nobles at odds with Oba Esigie over his Portuguese alliance; the war was fought for command of the river trade. Esigie won with Portuguese firearms, and Benin tradition adds that a servant of the queen mother Idia killed the Igala general before the fighting turned. Igala memory keeps the Attah's daughter Inikpi instead: the oracle said Idah could be saved only if she were buried alive by the river, and she consented, so the story runs, that her people might live; the Benin soldiers saw the flames of the sacrifice and, thinking the town already burned, fell back. Igala afterwards paid tribute to the Jukun confederation of Kwararafa until the seventeenth century. Its later wars fed the canoe trade of the lower Niger, where captives of the middle river were sold on towards the Delta slave ports.
zh:
伊达位于尼日尔河东岸、贝努埃河汇入口下游，是伊加拉人最古老的王城。历代「阿塔」在此设朝，统治两河之间遍布薯蓣田和猎场的国土；伊达也是尼日尔河中游的渔港和商埠，独木舟商旅在此以铜环和贝币交易。这个王朝的开端颇为奇特：相传第一位阿塔是朱昆公主埃布卢埃杰奥努，朱昆王之女，她在15世纪率族人迁至伊达并在那里登位。伊达的名声也溯流而上，努佩传说称第一代埃措措埃德本是阿塔王庭中的人，他沿尼日尔河逃走，另建王国。1444年，阿塔以伊达为都，凭战船在两河汇流处称雄。

大考在1515—1516年到来：阿塔·阿耶格巴·奥马·伊多科应贝宁国内反对奥巴·埃西吉对葡结盟的贵族之请，派战船渡尼日尔河攻伐贝宁，战事为争夺河上商路的控制权而起。埃西吉靠葡萄牙火器取胜，贝宁传说还称太后伊迪亚的一名仆从在战局扭转前刺杀了伊加拉主将。伊加拉人记住的却是阿塔的女儿伊尼克皮：神谕说唯有把她活埋河畔，伊达才能得救，相传她甘愿赴死，以换族人存活；贝宁士兵望见献祭的火光，以为城池已焚，便退兵了。此后伊加拉向朱昆人的夸拉拉法联盟纳贡，直到17世纪。后来的战争又为尼日尔河下游的独木舟商路提供俘虏，中游的人口经此被转卖向三角洲的奴隶港。

en:
The open savanna between the Benue and the hills of the Jos plateau is Alago country, the country of the salt towns. The Alago say they came west from Apa, seat of old Kwararafa, with their Jukun kin, and their leader Andoma founded the kingdom of Doma in 1232; Keana, where brine springs feed the salt-boiling pans that draw traders from all sides, counts itself a twelfth-century foundation. Doma, Keana, Obi and their sister towns each kept their own king, and porters carried their salt and grain by market track south to the Benue and north toward Bornu. In 1444 these chiefdoms still ruled the country, shared with the Koro and Gwandara farmers around them.

The town called Lafia did not yet exist. Muhammadu Dunama, a Kanuri leader from Bornu, founded it only in the late eighteenth century, camping with his people south of Shabu village and laying out a Muslim market town on the road between Bornu and the Benue. From 1804 the Fulani jihad overturned the country to the north and planted emirates at Bauchi and Gombe, but the Alago kingdoms of Doma, Keana and Obi kept their independence through the wars, their salt pans still feeding the caravan tracks.
zh:
贝努埃河与乔斯高原丘陵之间的开阔稀树草原是阿拉戈人的土地，即「盐镇之乡」。阿拉戈人自称随朱昆亲族从古老夸拉拉法的都城阿帕西迁，首领安多马于1232年建立多马王国；基阿纳的盐泉上盐锅林立，引得四方商贩前来，相传是12世纪的基业。多马、基阿纳、奥比等姊妹城镇各奉其王，脚夫沿商道把食盐和谷物南运贝努埃河、北贩博尔努。1444年，这片土地仍由这些酋邦分治，与四围务农的科罗人和关达拉人共居。

名为拉菲亚的城池此时尚不存在。18世纪末，来自博尔努的卡努里首领穆罕默杜·杜纳马率部在沙布村以南扎营，在博尔努通往贝努埃河的路边建起一座穆斯林商镇，这才有了拉菲亚。1804年起，富拉尼圣战席卷北方，在包奇和贡贝立下埃米尔国；多马、基阿纳和奥比等阿拉戈王国却在战火中保住独立，盐锅里的盐依旧供应着各条商路。

en:
Zazzau was the southernmost of the seven true Hausa states, on the open plains south of Kano and Katsina, and its early kings ruled from Turunku, strongest of the hill chiefdoms above Kufena. As the Hausa march facing the lands of the Niger and Benue, it lived from the slave trade: raiders drove captives up from the south to the markets of Kano and Katsina, where trans-Saharan caravans paid for them in salt, and grain went north by the same roads. In 1444 Zazzau was still ruled from Turunku, its farmers keeping the old Hausa spirit cults; Islam had not yet crossed the border from Kano.

Clerics and traders from Kano brought Islam around 1456, but it long remained a town religion beside the rural rites. In the late 15th century the Turunku ruler Bakwa seized Kufena, and early in the next century a new capital rose east of the old hill, named Zaria after Bakwa's daughter. The kingdom's fame belongs to Amina, Bakwa's daughter and its greatest general: Hausa tradition gives her thirty-four years of campaigns through Bauchi and Nupe to the edge of Kwararafa, and the earthen ramparts she raised at her camps are still called Amina's walls. The Chronicle of Abuja says she brought forty eunuchs and ten thousand kola nuts from Nupe to Hausaland, and tradition adds that she died in battle far to the south and her body was never brought home. In later years Zazzau paid tribute at different times to Songhai, Bornu and Kwararafa. The Fulani jihad took Zaria in December 1808: the last Hausa king, Muhammadu Awwal Makau, fled south to Abuja, where his line kept the title Sarkin Zazzau at Suleja, while a Fulani emir held the old city under Sokoto.
zh:
扎造是豪萨七个正宗邦国中最靠南的一个，位于卡诺和卡齐纳以南的开阔平原上，最早的王廷设在图龙库——库费纳山上那群山地酋邦中最强盛的一个。作为朝向尼日尔河与贝努埃河之地的豪萨前哨，它靠奴隶贸易立足：掳掠者把俘虏从南方一路驱赶到卡诺和卡齐纳的市场，跨撒哈拉商队在那里用盐买人，谷物也沿同一条路北运。1444年的扎造仍以图龙库为都，农户奉行豪萨旧有的精灵崇拜；伊斯兰教还没有从卡诺越境而来。

约1456年，卡诺来的学者和商人传入伊斯兰教，但它长期只是城市里的宗教，与乡间祭礼并存。15世纪末，图龙库之主巴克瓦夺取库费纳；下一世纪初，旧山以东建起新都，以巴克瓦之女命名为扎里亚。扎造的名声系于阿米娜，巴克瓦的这个女儿是它最能征善战的将领。豪萨传说称她征战三十四年，率军穿过包奇和努佩，直抵夸拉拉法边缘；她在各处营地筑起的土堤仍被叫做「阿米娜墙」。《阿布贾编年史》说她把四十名阉奴和一万枚柯拉果从努佩带回豪萨兰，传说还讲她战死在遥远的南方，遗体没能运回家乡。此后扎造先后向桑海、博尔努和夸拉拉法称臣纳贡。1808年12月，富拉尼圣战军攻占扎里亚：末代豪萨王穆罕默杜·阿瓦勒·马考南逃阿布贾，其后人在苏莱贾保留「扎造王」称号，旧城则由索科托麾下的富拉尼埃米尔统治。

en:
Kano grew up beneath Dala Hill in the Hausa savanna, where iron-working villagers lived before the first kings. The Kano Chronicle dates its dynasty to Bagauda in 999; the third king, Gijimasu, began the earthen city wall in 1095 and his son Tsaraki completed it. Wangara Muslims brought Islam under Yaji I in the fourteenth century. The city linked caravans from Bornu and the Sahara with Gonja and the southern forests. In 1444 the sarki Abdullahi Burja, ruling since 1438, governed a Sunni market town whose merchants dealt in salt, cotton, leather, kola nuts and indigo-dyed cloth; farmers outside the walls grew rice, grain and citrus.

Muhammad Rumfa, sarki from 1463 to 1499, gave Kano its richest age. He enlarged the walls and the Gidan Rumfa palace, laid out Kurmi Market, invited scholars and pressed leading families to convert; the Kano Chronicle credits him with twelve innovations, from the kakaki trumpet to ostrich-feather shoes at court. He married Auwa, a daughter of Askia Muhammad of Songhai, who later became the first woman to hold the title Madaki. Indigo dyers worked the Kofar Mata pits beside the gate of that name, and Kurmi Market drew traders from Ghadames, Tripoli and the western Sudan, slaves among its goods. A generation later Leo Africanus described wealthy merchants, skilled craftsmen and strong cavalry, while Kano's long war with Katsina ended without a victor.

Later reigns endured Katsina raids, Jukun attacks from the south and Fulani pressure as weaving, dyeing and leatherwork carried on. Usman dan Fodio's reform movement challenged the Habe rulers from the 1790s, and Fulani jihad forces took Kano in 1805; the last sultan was killed in 1807, and the city became an emirate of the Sokoto Caliphate. Famine struck from 1807 to 1810, yet cloth, dyes and leather again went north to Tripoli and across to Lake Chad and Timbuktu, making Kano the caliphate's richest commercial province by 1821.
zh:
卡诺兴于豪萨草原的达拉山下，最早的国王到来之前，山下已有从事冶铁的村落。《卡诺编年史》把王朝开端系于999年的巴高达；第三王吉吉马苏1095年开始修筑土城墙，儿子查拉基将其完工。14世纪亚吉一世在位时，万加拉穆斯林把伊斯兰教带入卡诺。卡诺把来自博尔诺和撒哈拉的商队同贡贾及南方森林连接起来。1444年，1438年即位的萨尔基阿卜杜拉希·布尔贾统治着这座逊尼派商业城镇，商人经营盐、棉花、皮革、柯拉果和靛蓝染布，城墙外的农民种植稻米、谷物和柑橘。

1463年至1499年在位的穆罕默德·鲁姆法给了卡诺最富庶的年代。他扩建城墙和鲁姆法宫，开辟库鲁米市场，延揽学者，力劝望族皈依；《卡诺编年史》把十二项革新归于他，从卡卡基号角到宫廷里的鸵鸟羽鞋。他迎娶桑海阿斯基亚·穆罕默德之女奥瓦，奥瓦后来成为第一位拥有「马达基」头衔的女性。靛蓝染匠在科法尔·马塔门边的染坑劳作，库鲁米市场吸引古达米斯、的黎波里和西苏丹的商人前来，奴隶也在买卖之列。一代人之后，利奥·阿非利加努斯记载这里有富有的商人、熟练的工匠和精锐骑兵；卡诺与卡齐纳的长期战争则没有赢家。

此后的统治者接连应付卡齐纳入侵、南方朱昆人的袭掠和富拉尼人的压力，纺织、染色和皮革业维持了下来。1790年代起，奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的改革运动挑战哈贝统治者，富拉尼圣战军1805年攻下卡诺，末代苏丹1807年被杀，卡诺成为索科托哈里发国的埃米尔国。1807年至1810年饥荒肆虐，但布匹、染料和皮革重新北运的黎波里，转销乍得湖和廷巴克图，到1821年，卡诺已成哈里发国最富庶的商业省份。

en:
Damagaram is the Sahelian plain south of the Ténéré, where caravan trails from Agadez and the salt oases of Kawar run on to the Hausa cities. In 1444 it was a thinly peopled marchland of Hausa farming villages and Tuareg dry-season camps, with wells where the camels drank on the road between the Aïr and Kano under loads of salt, dates and cloth. No chief yet ruled it from a walled town, and the camps mostly managed their own affairs.

A state arrived here late. In 1731 a party of Muslim nobles moved south under a leader called Mallam and settled near Mirriah, nominally under Bornu, and in 1736 they moved their seat to the village of Zinder. Its walled Birni, with the Tuareg trading quarter of Zengou growing up beside it, became the chief market on the road from Tripoli to Kano. Damagaram grew rich on caravan tolls, on the salt evaporation pans of western Bornu, on ostrich feathers sold to Europe and on slaves, with the Kel Gres Tuareg camped nearby as allies. When Usman dan Fodio's jihad overran Gobir and the other Hausa kingdoms after 1804, the defeated animist nobles took shelter here and went on to found refugee states such as Maradi to the west; Damagaram kept its markets open to the Sokoto Caliphate all the same, and caravans kept passing through Zinder.
zh:
达马加兰姆是泰内雷沙漠以南的萨赫勒平原，阿加德兹和卡瓦尔盐洲通往豪萨诸城的商道从这里经过。1444年时，这里是人烟稀疏的边地，散布着豪萨人的农庄和图阿雷格人的旱季营地，沿途一口口水井供驮着盐、椰枣和布匹往来于阿伊尔与卡诺之间的骆驼歇脚。还没有哪个首领在带城墙的城镇里发号施令，各处营地大半自行其是。

这里的国家出现得很晚。1731年，一伙穆斯林贵族在被称为马拉姆的首领带领下南迁，在米里亚附近落脚，名义上奉博尔努为宗主；1736年，他们把治所迁到津德尔村。带城墙的比尔尼和旁边生长起来的图阿雷格商人街区曾戈，成了的黎波里通往卡诺商路上最大的市集。达马加兰姆靠商队税、博尔努西部盐田的出产、销往欧洲的鸵鸟羽和奴隶致富，凯尔·格雷斯图阿雷格人在附近扎营为盟。1804年以后，乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥的圣战攻灭戈比尔等豪萨古国，落败的多神教贵族来此避难，后来在西边建起马拉迪等流亡政权；达马加兰姆与索科托哈里发国之间的商路却没有断，驼队依旧穿过津德尔。

en:
Bornu is the dry plain south-west of Lake Chad, cut by the seasonal Komadugu Yobe, where the Sao of an earlier age built their walled towns. The Kanuri who farm and herd there became the heartland people of the Sayfawa dynasty after about 1380, when the Bilala drove the court out of Njimi in Kanem, across the lake. The kingdom rebuilt itself in Bornu, but the Dawudid and Idrisid branches feuded so constantly that fifteen mais followed one another between about 1390 and 1470, and no fixed capital existed: the mai's camp moved from site to site, stopping for years at a time at places such as Garu Kime, while caravans carried slaves, salt and cattle north along the Saharan roads. In 1444 Bornu was a Muslim kingdom recovering from another succession war, its horsemen raiding Mandara and Kotoko to the south.

The winner of the feud, Mai Ali Gaji, ended the wandering about 1472 when he walled a new capital, Ngazargamu, between the Yobe and the Komadugu Gana in the middle of a salt-making district, at the southern end of the trans-Saharan roads. For three centuries it was the chief city of the central Sudan; a later chronicle counts 660 laid-out streets and four Friday mosques, each said to hold twelve thousand worshippers, and its markets drew caravans from Tripoli, Tunis and Cairo that sold Venetian paper and glass beads, Middle Eastern silk and books, and brought kola nuts and gold up from the south. Under Idris Alooma, from about 1570, Turkish instructors drilled his musketeers and the armies campaigned as far as the Fezzan; his chief imam, Ahmad ibn Fartuwa, wrote the chronicle of his wars, and qadi courts were set apart from the ruler's own officials. After Alooma the empire slowly lost ground, and in 1808 Fulani jihadists took and destroyed Ngazargamu. The scholar and commander Muhammad al-Amin al-Kanemi led the recovery, took the title shehu in 1814 and founded Kukawa, leaving the Sayfawa mai a figurehead.
zh:
博尔诺在乍得湖西南，是一片被季节性的约贝河切开的干旱平原，更早的萨奥人曾在这里筑起城寨。约1380年，布拉拉人攻陷卡奈姆的恩吉米、把赛法瓦朝廷逐过乍得湖后，在此农耕放牧的卡努里人成了王朝的腹地之民。王国在博尔诺重建，达乌德系和伊德里斯系却内斗不休，约1390至1470年间有十五位迈接连登位，也没有固定都城：迈的营帐四处迁移，曾在加鲁·基梅一类地方驻留多年，商队则沿撒哈拉商路把奴隶、盐和牲畜运往北方。1444年的博尔诺是个刚从又一场继承战争中缓过来的穆斯林王国，骑兵向南袭掠曼达拉和科托科。

内斗的胜利者迈·阿里·加吉约于1472年结束了迁徙：他在约贝河与科马杜古加纳河之间的一片产盐区中央，筑起有城墙的新都城恩加扎尔加穆，正扼跨撒哈拉商路的南端。此后三百年间，它是中苏丹的中心城市；后世一部史籍数出城里有六百六十条修整过的街道、四座聚礼清真寺，据说每座能容一万两千人礼拜；市集吸引的黎波里、突尼斯和开罗商队，贩来威尼斯的纸张和玻璃珠、中东的丝绸和书籍，又从南方运入柯拉果和黄金。约1570年起在位的伊德里斯·阿劳马请来土耳其教官操练火枪手，兵锋远达费赞；他的首席伊玛目艾哈迈德·本·富尔图瓦记下他的历次征战，卡迪法庭也与君主自己的官员分设。阿劳马之后帝国节节退缩，1808年富拉尼圣战者攻占并摧毁恩加扎尔加穆。学者兼将领穆罕默德·阿明·卡涅米主持复国，1814年取号「谢胡」、建立库卡瓦，赛法瓦的迈成了空头君主。

en:
Kanem is the parched country north-east of Lake Chad, where the road down from the Kawar oases comes to the lake. It was the first homeland of the Sayfawa mais, Muslims since the eleventh century. Their capital Njimi, whose site has never been located, drew the trans-Saharan caravans that carried slaves, ivory and animal hides north and filled the royal treasury with customs dues. The Bilala, a pastoral people of the lake fringe, warred on the Sayfawa through the fourteenth century, killed the mai Dawud Nikalemi about 1363, and about 1380 forced the court of Umar I across the lake to Bornu. The Bilala kept Kanem and built a kingdom strong enough to rival Bornu. In 1444 a Bilala sultan held the country, and the caravan road between the Fezzan and the Chad basin ran through his hands.

Early in the sixteenth century the Bornu mai Idris Katakarmabe, son of Ali Gaji, led the Sayfawa armies back across the lake. He defeated the Bilala ruler Dunama bin Salma at Gharni Kiyala and entered Njimi, then turned on the usurper A'dim bin Salma, beat him at Jugulgul and took his oath of submission. Kanem became a Bornu province in name, but Katakarmabe left the Bilala chiefs in place as vassals and kept his own court at Ngazargamu west of the lake. About 1630 the rising Wadai sultanate drove the Bilala out altogether; they withdrew east to Lake Fitri, where their later sultans ruled at Yao. Tunjur raiders moved in behind them until a Bornu army under Dala Afuno secured the country, and Dala's Kanembu kinsmen, the Dalatoa, governed it as viceroys for the next two centuries. Their hold was seldom firm, with Wadai, Tuareg and Arab raiders pressing on every side, and by the later eighteenth century caravan traffic up the oasis road had dwindled and Kanem was a troubled march between Bornu and Wadai.
zh:
卡奈姆是乍得湖东北的干旱之地，卡瓦尔绿洲南下的道路从这里通到湖畔。这里是赛法瓦王朝诸迈最早的家园，11世纪已改宗伊斯兰教。都城恩吉米的具体位置已不可考，却吸引跨撒哈拉商队把奴隶、象牙和兽皮运往北方，王室靠关税充实府库。湖畔的游牧族群布拉拉人与赛法瓦交战了整个14世纪，约1363年攻杀迈达乌德·尼卡勒米，约1380年又迫使迈乌马尔一世的朝廷西渡乍得湖、迁往博尔诺。布拉拉人占住卡奈姆，建起的王国国力足以同博尔诺抗衡。1444年，布拉拉苏丹据有此地，费赞通往乍得盆地的商路就从他手中经过。

16世纪初，博尔努迈阿里·加吉之子伊德里斯·卡塔卡尔马贝率赛法瓦大军重返湖东。他在加尼基亚拉击败布拉拉君主杜纳马·本·萨勒马，进入恩吉米，随后回师征讨篡位者阿丁·本·萨勒马，在朱古尔古尔将其击败，受其臣服。卡奈姆名义上成为博尔努的一省，但卡塔卡尔马贝仍让布拉拉酋长作为附庸留在原地，自己的朝廷设在湖西的恩加扎尔加穆。约1630年，崛起的瓦达伊苏丹国把布拉拉人彻底逐出，他们东撤到菲特里湖，后世苏丹在亚奥立国。通朱尔袭掠者趁虚而入，直到博尔努将领达拉·阿福诺率军平定此地；达拉的卡涅姆布亲族「达拉托阿」作为总督，在此统治了此后两个世纪。他们的控制很少稳固，瓦达伊、图阿雷格和阿拉伯袭掠者从四面施压；到18世纪后期，绿洲古道上的商队已经稀少，卡奈姆成了博尔努与瓦达伊之间动荡的边地。

en:
Southeast of Lake Chad, the plains north of the Chari are the country of the Bagirmi, whom their neighbours call the Barma. They farm millet, herd cattle and gather ivory in a scatter of village chiefdoms on the southern fringe of the Kanem world. In 1444 no kingdom yet stands at Massenya, but the ivory of these plains and captives taken in the lands further south are already moving north with the caravans that link the Chad basin to Tripoli.

Tradition dates the kingdom that grew out of these chiefdoms to 1480 or 1522, under Mbang Abd al-Mahmud Begli or Mbang Birni Besse. Its mbangs built Massenya of clay houses around a palace and a mosque of hewn stone, and paid their way in the trans-Saharan trade with captives, ivory, hides and cotton, bringing back copper and cowries. Under Mbang Abdullah the court accepted Islam late in the sixteenth century, while most of his people kept their old rites. Bornu's greatest mai, Idris Alooma, reduced Bagirmi to tribute, and Abdullah's revolt drew him south on his last campaign: he died there in 1602 or 1603, reportedly killed by a man of the Gumergu. In its stronger years the kingdom raided north to the shores of Lake Chad, and under Mbang Muhammad al-Amin it shook off Bornu's overlordship in the later eighteenth century. Wadai proved a harder neighbour. In 1805 its army sacked Massenya, killed the mbang and his family, and carried off some 20,000 people to sell in the northern markets, setting the dead mbang's son on the throne as a tributary.
zh:
乍得湖东南、沙里河以北的平原是巴吉尔米人的土地，邻族称他们为巴尔马人。他们种植小米、牧牛、采集象牙，生活在加奈姆世界南缘一群互不统属的村社酋邦中。1444年的马塞尼亚还没有王国，但这片平原的象牙，加上从更南方掳来的俘虏，已随连接乍得盆地与的黎波里的商队源源北上。

按当地传说，由这些酋邦合并而成的王国建于1480年或1522年，开国君主或作姆邦·阿卜杜勒-马哈茂德·贝格利，或作姆邦·比尔尼·贝塞。历代姆邦建起马塞尼亚：土坯民居围绕石砌的王宫和清真寺；国家以俘虏、象牙、皮革和棉花参加跨撒哈拉贸易，换回铜和贝壳。16世纪末姆邦·阿卜杜拉在位时宫廷接受伊斯兰教，多数民众仍守旧礼。博尔努最有作为的马伊伊德里斯·阿卢马迫使巴吉尔米纳贡；阿卜杜拉反叛，他最后一次南征就死在这里，时在1602或1603年，据说是被一名古梅古人所杀。王国强盛时一度北掠至乍得湖畔，姆邦·穆罕默德·阿尔-阿敏在18世纪后期摆脱了博尔努的宗主权。东邻瓦达伊却更为难挡：1805年瓦达伊军队洗劫马塞尼亚，杀死姆邦及其家人，约两万人被掳往北方市场贩卖，胜者立死去姆邦的儿子为纳贡之君。

en:
Mandara is the volcanic Mandara Mountains country on the Bornu frontier, south-east of the plains ruled from Ngazargamu. Wandala-speaking Mandarawa farmed the highland valleys in a strictly ordered society known for iron working and horse raising, and mountain raiding supplied captives for the slave caravans of later centuries. Later tradition traced the ruling line to a queen, Soukda, and a non-Mandarawa hunter named Gaya shortly before 1500. The name first appears outside the region on Fra Mauro's Venetian world map of 1459, and Leo Africanus, who knew the country as Medra, called its people rich and industrious and praised its rulers' love of justice. In 1444 the later Muslim sultanate had not yet taken shape: highland clans followed their own elders and war leaders, while Kanem-Bornu, rebuilding its power, overshadowed the plains to the north.

For its first century the young kingdom fought its neighbours on every side. After conquering the Dulo it moved its capital to Dulo around 1580 under Sankre, a war leader whose dynasty then held the throne. When the Dulo disputed the succession, Bornu backed Aldawa Nanda of Sankre's house; the mai of Bornu installed him in person, which gave Bornu lasting hold over the Mandara court. Around 1715 the twenty-fifth ruler, Bukar Aji, accepted Islam from visiting teachers and made Mandara a sultanate, and one tradition names the teachers as two Moroccans of Fez on their way home from Mecca. Under Bukar Guiana the Mandarawa defeated Bornu in a great battle around 1781, and by the turn of the century about fifteen chiefdoms paid them tribute. In 1809 Modibo Adama, a Fulani disciple of Usman dan Fodio, led a jihad into the mountains and briefly held Dulo before a Mandara counterattack drove him out; the victory brought Mandara and Bornu together again against the Fulani.
zh:
曼达拉是博尔努边境上的曼达拉火山山区，在恩加扎尔加穆所治平原的东南方。讲万达拉语的曼达拉人在高地河谷耕作，社会等级森严，以冶铁和养马闻名；进山掳掠得来的人口还供应了后世的奴隶商队。后世传说把王族世系追溯到1500年以前不久的一位女王苏克达，和一个非曼达拉族的猎人加亚。这个名字最早在外界出现，是在1459年威尼斯的弗拉·毛罗世界地图上；利奥·阿非利加努斯称此地为梅德拉，说当地人民富足勤勉，统治者秉公好义。1444年时，后来的伊斯兰苏丹国尚未成形：山地氏族听从各自的长老和军事首领，正在复兴的卡奈姆-博尔努则笼罩着北方平原。

建国后的头一个世纪，这个年轻王国四面与邻族交战。征服杜洛人后，约1580年在军事首领桑克雷主持下迁都杜洛，其后王位由桑克雷王朝掌握。杜洛人争夺继承权时，博尔努支持桑克雷家族的阿尔达瓦·南达，博尔努君主亲自将他扶上王位，也因此长期把持曼达拉宫廷。约1715年，第二十五代王布卡尔·阿吉从来访的导师受教皈依，曼达拉成为苏丹国；一说两位导师是从麦加返乡、途经此地的非斯摩洛哥人。布卡尔·圭亚那在位时，曼达拉人约在1781年的一场大战中击败博尔努，到世纪之交约有十五个小邦向他们纳贡。1809年，乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥的富拉尼弟子莫迪博·阿达马率圣战军攻入山区，一度占领杜洛，曼达拉反击将他逐出；这场胜利让曼达拉与博尔努再度联手对付富拉尼人。

en:
Bauchi is high savanna on the northern edge of the Jos Plateau, but the walled town of Bauchi did not exist in 1444. Bolewa farmers had settled along the Gongola by the thirteenth century, while Gerawa, Warji and other Chadic-speaking villagers kept the later Bauchi country as farmland and hunting ground. To the south lay the Jukun power of Kwararafa, whose world reached up to the plateau through the Bolewa ancestral cult of Konon Akku. No Muslim city-state ruled here in 1444; scattered farming and hunting communities followed their own religions.

The Sokoto jihad reached the plateau under Yakubu dan Dadi, a Hausa scholar who had studied under Usman dan Fodio and became the only non-Fulani commander to hold a flag in the caliphate. From 1809 to 1818 his campaigns subdued the highland villages and brought them into an Islamic state tied to Sokoto. In the first year of the war he founded Bauchi and girdled it with walls 10.5 kilometres in circumference; tradition says the name honours Baushe, a hunter who told him to build west of Warinje Mountain, and the town was also called Yakoba after its founder. Yakubu ruled from it as the first emir of Bauchi.
zh:
包奇是乔斯高原北缘的高稀树草原，但1444年时尚无城墙环绕的包奇城。博莱瓦农人13世纪已在贡戈拉河沿岸定居，格拉瓦人、瓦尔吉人和其他使用乍得语支语言的村民，把后来的包奇地区开垦为农田和猎场。南方是朱昆人的夸拉拉法势力，博莱瓦人的孔农·阿库祖灵崇拜把这片高原也纳入朱昆人的世界。1444年这里没有穆斯林城邦，只有奉行各自传统宗教、分散而居的农耕与狩猎社群。

索科托圣战随雅库布·丹·达迪来到高原。他是豪萨学者，曾师从乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥，后来成为索科托哈里发国中唯一执掌军旗的非富拉尼裔将领。1809至1818年，他的征战降服高原村落，把它们纳入依附索科托的伊斯兰政权。开战第一年他便建起包奇城，修筑周长10.5公里的城墙；传说城名是为纪念猎人鲍谢，正是他建议在瓦林杰山以西建城，这座城也以建城者得名雅科巴。雅库布在此定都，成为包奇第一任酋长。

en:
Wukari is the country between the Donga and the Benue, flat floodplains cut by salt-bearing streams. Hausa traders to the north called the pagan peoples of the Benue basin Kororofa, 'the salt people', and salt, ivory and slaves went north by caravan through Bauchi to Katsina, Kano and Bornu, while horses came south the same way. In 1444 the land belonged to Kwararafa, a loose multi-ethnic confederacy whose cavalry had already tested the Hausa states: Kano had destroyed its early ritual centre of Santolo and taken an annual tribute of slaves, and Kwararafa paid tribute to Zazzau for much of the fifteenth century. What bound its different towns together was less a court than the Aku Uka, a divine king treated as God's representative on earth. Oral tradition names a hunter, Katakpa, as the founder of Wukari, which in 1444 was not yet the fixed Jukun capital it later became.

A severe defeat by Bornu at the end of the fifteenth century brought refugees from the Muslim north into the Benue valley, and salt profits paid for a rebuilt cavalry. Kwararafa revived under King Kenjo until about 1610, and Jukun migrants moving up from the south became the leading people around Wukari. Its armies became the scourge of the Hausa cities: they forced Kano's ruler into exile in 1653 and drove the people of Kano to take refuge in Daura in 1671, and in 1680 they struck Katsina and Zazzau, then pushed on into Bornu and sacked its capital Ngazargamu before Mai Ali drove them out, reportedly sending three captives back with their ears cut off and hung around their necks. Drought, internal quarrels and pressure from the Chamba wore Kwararafa down during the eighteenth century, and by its end it paid tribute to Bornu. Its last king, Adi Matswen, was driven into exile around 1810 in the Fulani wars, while Wukari survived as the main Jukun ritual centre under its Aku Uka.
zh:
武卡里地处栋加河与贝努埃河之间，平坦的洪泛平原上分布着含盐湖溪。北方的豪萨商人把贝努埃河流域的非穆斯林诸族称作「科罗罗法」，意为「盐民」；盐、象牙和奴隶经巴乌奇由商队北运至卡齐纳、卡诺和博尔努，马匹则沿同一条路南来。1444年，这片土地属于夸拉拉法，一个松散的多族群联盟。联盟骑兵早已同豪萨诸邦交过手：卡诺摧毁了它早期的祭祀中心桑托洛，每年索取奴隶为贡，而15世纪大部分时间里，夸拉拉法又向扎造纳贡。把各城镇维系在一起的与其说是王庭，不如说是阿库·乌卡，这位神王被视为真主在人间的代表。相传一位名叫卡塔克帕的猎人创建了武卡里，此时它还不是后来那个固定的朱昆人都城。

15世纪末夸拉拉法惨败于博尔努，穆斯林北方的难民涌入贝努埃河谷，盐业的收益又重建了骑兵。联盟在肯乔王治下复兴，直至约1610年；约自1600年起，从南方迁来的朱昆移民逐渐成为武卡里周围的主导族群。联盟军队成了豪萨诸城的克星：1653年迫使卡诺统治者流亡，1671年又使卡诺居民逃入道拉避难；1680年他们先攻卡齐纳和扎造，继而攻入博尔努、洗劫其都城恩加扎尔加穆，最后被阿里迈伊击退，据说他送还三名俘虏，耳朵被割下挂在脖子上。18世纪，干旱、内争和昌巴人的压力拖垮了夸拉拉法，到世纪末它已向博尔努纳贡。末代王阿迪·马特斯温约于1810年在富拉尼战争中被逐，武卡里则作为阿库·乌卡治下朱昆人主要的仪式中心留存下来。

en:
Calabar, Akwa Akpa in Efik, fills the mangrove country where the Calabar and Cross rivers run into the Bight of Biafra. The Efik had moved down from the lower Niger to fish and farm the creeks, and they lived in large stockaded towns, the greatest of them Creek Town, Old Town and Duke Town, led by the Duke and Eyamba families in a loose league with no paramount ruler. Behind the chiefs stood the Ekpe society, the leopard-men: masked members in graded titles who enforced debts and judgements from the Ekpe house. In 1444 the towns were still fishing settlements, and no European ship had yet entered the bight.

The first European vessel on record came in 1625 and found the Efik already settled at Creek Town and Old Town. Calabar then became an international slave port, its merchants bartering captives brought from the interior for copper bars, manillas and Danish guns. Between 1725 and 1750 about 17,000 men and women were sold there to European captains, and from 1772 to 1775 the figure passed 62,000; Duke Town and Creek Town became the two greatest slave marts on the bight. The enslaved preacher John Jea, whose autobiography was printed in 1811, wrote that he had been born in the Calabar country before slavers carried him off as a boy. Ekpe rites crossed the Atlantic with the captives and were carried to the Spanish Caribbean. After Britain abolished the trade in 1807 exports moved to palm oil and kernels, though Spanish and Portuguese ships still bought captives at Duke Town. In 1815 the frigate HMS Comus sailed in and seized seven such ships at anchor.
zh:
卡拉巴尔，埃菲克语称阿克瓦阿克帕，地处卡拉巴尔河与克罗斯河注入比夫拉湾的红树林水网之间。埃菲克人从下尼日尔河一带南迁到河口渔耕，住在设有栅栏的大镇里，最大的是克里克镇、奥尔德镇和杜克镇，以杜克、埃扬巴两大家族为首，各城镇松散结盟，不立共主。首领背后还有埃克佩豹社：佩戴面具、按等级授衔的成员在豹社会所里主持追债和裁判。1444年的诸镇还只是渔村，海湾里也没有出现过欧洲帆船。

有记载的第一艘欧洲船1625年才来，那时埃菲克人已在克里克镇和奥尔德镇定居。卡拉巴尔随后成为国际奴隶港，商人用从内陆贩来的俘虏换取铜条、马尼拉币和丹麦火枪。1725至1750年间，约有一万七千名男女在此卖给欧洲船长；1772至1775年，售出人数超过六万二千，杜克镇和克里克镇成为比夫拉湾上最大的两处奴隶市场。被掳为奴的布道师约翰·吉（John Jea）在1811年印出自传，自称童年被掳前出生在卡拉巴尔一带。埃克佩的仪式随俘虏渡过大西洋，被带到西属加勒比。英国1807年废止奴隶贸易后，出口转为棕榈油和棕榈仁，但西班牙和葡萄牙商船仍到杜克镇购买人口。1815年，英国军舰「科马斯号」驶入港内，一次缴获七艘贩奴船。

en:
Cameroon takes its name from a mangrove river, the Wouri estuary on this coast, whose swarming shrimp Portuguese sailors would soon turn into a place name. In 1444 the river mouth was Sawa country, the shore of coastal Bantu fishermen and farmers, and Duala tradition remembers the Bakoko and Bassa living there before the Duala came. No European ship had yet entered the estuary.

Fernão do Pó, sailing for the Lisbon merchant Fernão Gomes, entered the Wouri around 1472 and named it the Rio dos Camarões, the River of Shrimps, and Cameroon kept that name. Duala speakers trace their line to Ewale, who led his people to the east bank, and by the sixteenth century they were the leading brokers of this coast, buying ivory and captives from the Bakweri, Mungo and Bassa of the interior and selling them aboard European ships for guns, gunpowder, alcohol, textiles and mirrors. In the eighteenth century the Wouri villages that Europeans called Cameroons Town formed one of the principal slave marts on the bight. The settlements remained rival houses: in 1814 the chief Ngando Mpondo styled himself King Akwa against the Bell lineage of Ndumb'a Lobe, and the estuary was still a string of separate villages, Deido, Akwa, Njo and Hickory Town, with Akwa and Bell feuding over the river trade.
zh:
喀麦隆的名字来自一条红树林河流，即本省海岸的武里河河口；葡萄牙水手很快因河中虾群密布，把它变成了地名。1444年，河口两岸是萨瓦人的土地，即沿海班图渔民和农夫的家园，杜阿拉人的传说记得，在他们迁来之前，住在河口的是巴科科人和巴萨人。那时还没有欧洲船驶入过河口。

1472年前后，为里斯本商人费尔南·戈麦斯效力的航海家费尔南·多波驶入武里河，称之为「里奥多斯·卡马罗因斯」，意为虾河，喀麦隆的名字便从这条河传开。杜阿拉人把世系追溯到埃瓦莱，说是他率族人迁到河口东岸；到16世纪，他们已是这片海岸头号中间商，从内陆的贝克威里人、蒙戈人和巴萨人手中买下象牙和俘虏，转卖到欧洲船上，换回火枪、火药、酒、布匹和镜子。18世纪，欧洲人所称的「喀麦隆城」，即武里河畔的一组村落，已是海湾上主要奴隶市场之一。各村落始终各立门户：1814年，酋长恩甘多·姆庞多自称阿克瓦王，与恩敦巴·洛贝的贝尔家族分庭抗礼；河口仍是戴多、阿克瓦、恩乔和希科里镇一串分立的村庄，阿克瓦与贝尔两家为河上贸易争斗不休。

en:
The Gabon of the charts is the broad estuary where the Komo River breaks out of the rainforest into the Atlantic just north of the equator. By the fourteenth century the Vili kings of Loango had pushed their trading supremacy along this coast as far as these waters, while the wooded banks of the estuary itself belonged to Myènè Bantu fishermen, the clans later called the Mpongwe, who lived by fishing and the canoe trade with inland peoples. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered their roadstead.

Lopo Gonçalves and Rui de Sequeira reached the estuary in 1473 or 1474, on the voyage that made Gonçalves the first European sailor known to have crossed the equator. They named it the Gabão, after the hooded cloak its branching, sleeve-like waters were said to resemble, and the name passed from the river to the coast and later to the country. Mpongwe clans settled its banks in the sixteenth century and became brokers between the interior and the ships, taking ivory, ebony, beeswax and captives from the Bakèlè and Séké and selling them to Portuguese, Dutch and English traders for cloth, mirrors, iron machetes and firearms. Cheap imported ironware arrived in such supply that the local blacksmiths lost their living. The Mpongwe's own canoes ran sixty feet long under palm-frond sails and carried eight or ten tons along the shore. From about the 1770s the brokers dealt increasingly in captives. In 1821 the estuary was still divided among rival Mpongwe clans, and no European had yet built a permanent post there.
zh:
地图上的加蓬，是科莫河穿出热带雨林、在赤道以北注入大西洋的宽阔河口。14世纪时，卢安果的维利诸王已把贸易霸权沿海岸向北推到这一带；河口林木葱郁的两岸属于梅内语的班图渔民，即后来所称的姆蓬韦人诸氏族，以捕鱼和与内陆族群的独木舟贸易为生。1444年，还没有任何欧洲帆船驶入这片锚地。

1473或1474年，洛波·贡萨尔维斯与鲁伊·德·塞凯拉抵达河口，正是在这次航行中，贡萨尔维斯成为已知第一个越过赤道的欧洲水手。他们见河口分叉的水面宛如衣袖，形似水手所穿的带帽斗篷「加庞」，便以此命名，这个名字后来从河名扩及海岸，再扩及整个国家。16世纪，姆蓬韦各氏族在河口两岸定居，成为内陆与海船之间的中间商：从巴克勒人和塞凯人手中取得象牙、乌木、蜂蜡和俘虏，卖给葡萄牙、荷兰和英格兰商人，换回布匹、镜子、铁砍刀和火枪。进口铁器便宜量大，本地铁匠因此断了营生。他们自己的独木舟长达六十英尺，张着棕榈叶编成的帆，可载八到十吨货物沿海岸往来。约从1770年代起，他们开始卷入奴隶贸易。到1821年，河口仍由彼此竞争的姆蓬韦氏族分据，欧洲人还不曾在此建起一处永久商站。

en:
The Atlantic coast north of the Congo River was the land of the Vili, a branch of the Bakongo, who shared it with the Yombe, the Lumbu and the forest Babongo. In the fifteenth century no single power ruled it: Mayumba, Kilongo, Piri and Wansi were small chiefdoms that 'made war on each other' while trading ivory, raffia cloth and copper from the Mindouli mines inland, and Kakongo to the south was a vassal of Kongo. In 1444, then, the country that would become Loango was a string of Vili chiefdoms on Kongo's northern fringe, woven into the cloth and copper trades but unknown by name to European ships.
