Dutch visitors later recorded its founding tradition: a chief called Njimbe, from Kakongo, overcame the rival chiefdoms late in the sixteenth century through a web of alliances and set his capital at Bwali in Piri, the province that gave the Vili their older name of Muvili. Njimbe also ordered the succession, a rotation among the rulers of four provinces, and for a long time Loango's kings followed it.

In the seventeenth century Loango's power ran from Cape St Catherine almost to the Congo mouth. Copper from Mindouli went to Europe, and thousands of metres of raffia cloth went even to Portuguese Luanda; Vili caravans travelled inland to Teke country and beyond, while the royal trade officials called mafouks made every European ship anchor offshore and allowed no permanent factory. Kongo had sent priests to convert the new power, and in 1663 the Capuchin Bernardo d'Ungheria baptised the king as Afonso with some 6,000 of his people; after the king's death a civil war ended in 1665 with the Christian party defeated, and its exiles carried the quarrel abroad, one of them, Miguel da Silva, winning the rule of neighbouring Ngoyo. Slave exports then grew year by year, and Vili quarters appeared in distant markets, at São Salvador and in the Mbundu lands, where Queen Verónica of Ndongo-Matamba promised by treaty to stop trading with them but could not. In 1701 an English merchant found the government in the hands of a queen-regent, Mucundy. The coast also sheltered a small black Jewish community with no ties to any other, first reported by Europeans in 1777. French missionaries found interregna lasting seven years, run by regents called Mani Boman, and when King Buatu died in 1787 the old rotating succession died with him, and no settled constitution took its place.
zh:
刚果河以北的大西洋海岸是维利人的土地。维利人是巴刚果人的一支，与约姆贝人、伦布人和森林中的班邦戈人共居此地。15世纪时没有任何单一政权统辖这里：马永巴、基隆古、皮里、万西等小酋邦「彼此攻战」，同时买卖象牙、拉菲草布和内地明杜利矿的铜，南面的卡刚果则是刚果王国的属邦。因此1444年时，后来的卢安果还只是刚果北缘一连串维利酋邦，已经卷入布匹和铜的贸易，欧洲船却叫不出它的名字。荷兰来访者后来记下了它的开国传说：16世纪后期，一个来自卡刚果、名叫尼任贝的首领凭合纵连横降伏各敌对酋邦，定都皮里的布瓦利，维利人的旧称「穆维利」便来自皮里；尼任贝还定下四省诸侯轮流继统的规矩，此后很长时间卢安果国王都按此产生。

17世纪鼎盛时，卢安果的势力北起圣凯瑟琳角，南抵刚果河口附近。明杜利的铜销往欧洲，成千上万米拉菲亚布甚至卖到葡属罗安达；维利商队深入特约人地区乃至更远的内陆，王室贸易官马富克则让欧洲商船一律停泊在近海，不许设立商馆。刚果曾派神甫来这个新强国传教，1663年嘉布遣会修士贝尔纳多·敦加里亚为国王施洗，取名阿方索，同受洗的约有六千人；国王死后内战爆发，1665年基督教派战败，流亡者把纷争带到国外，其中米格尔·达席尔瓦后来成了邻国恩戈约的统治者。此后奴隶出口逐年增加，维利人的侨居区出现在遥远的市集：在圣萨尔瓦多，也在姆本杜人的土地上——恩东戈-马塔姆巴的维罗妮卡女王曾立约承诺不再与他们通商，却拦不住维利人继续扩散。1701年，英国商人发现国政掌握在女摄政穆昆迪手中。沿岸还住着一个与外界全无往来的黑人犹太小社群，欧洲人1777年才首次记述它。法国传教士见到的则是长达七年的王位空悬期，由马内·博曼摄政处理国事；1787年布阿图国王死后，旧的轮替继承法随之失灵，再没有稳定的建制取而代之。

en:
Luanda lies on a deep Atlantic bay in the Mbundu lands between the Lukala and Kwanza rivers. In 1444 its shoreline held only fishing villages ruled by local sobas, while inland the kingdom of Ndongo was taking shape under rulers titled ngola; tracks from the bay led toward the Kwanza and the trade routes of the interior, and no European ship had yet anchored there.

Portuguese ships reached the Congo in the 1480s. Paulo Dias de Novais, grandson of Bartolomeu Dias, founded São Paulo da Assunção de Luanda in January 1576 under a royal grant, bringing a hundred settler families and four hundred soldiers. War with Ndongo broke out almost at once; the Portuguese pushed up the Kwanza, built the inland fort of Massangano, and ringed the town with fortresses, of which Fort São Miguel, raised in the 1630s, keeps the hill above the harbour. In 1621 Nzinga Mbandi came to Luanda as her brother the ngola's envoy, negotiated a treaty and was baptised Ana de Sousa; after her brother's death she ruled Ndongo and Matamba, joined the Dutch when they took the town in 1641 and renamed it Fort Aardenburgh, and fought the Portuguese to a peace in 1656. Salvador Correia de Sá's Luso-Brazilian expedition drove the Dutch out in 1648. Luanda then became the centre of the slave trade to Brazil: Brazilian ships crowded the roadstead, Mbundu and Imbangala merchants brought captives down from the interior, and by 1751 between 5,000 and 10,000 enslaved people were sold there every year.
zh:
罗安达位于卢卡拉河与宽扎河之间姆本杜土地上的一处大西洋深水海湾。1444年时，沿岸只有受各地「索巴」首领管辖的渔村，内陆的恩东戈王国则在称「恩戈拉」的统治者手中逐渐成形；海湾有小路通向宽扎河和内陆商路，还没有欧洲船只在此停泊。

15世纪80年代，葡萄牙船只到达刚果。巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士之孙保罗·迪亚士·德·诺瓦伊斯凭王室特许状，于1576年1月建立圣保禄·达·阿松桑·德·罗安达，带来一百户移民和四百名士兵。葡萄牙很快与恩东戈开战，军队沿宽扎河深入，筑起马桑加诺要塞，又在城镇周围大修堡垒，建于17世纪30年代的圣米格尔堡扼守着港口上方的山头。1621年，恩津加·姆班迪作为兄长恩戈拉的使者来到罗安达，议定条约并受洗，取名安娜·德·索萨。兄长死后，她统治恩东戈和马坦巴；1641年荷兰攻占罗安达、改名阿尔登堡，她与荷兰人联手，对葡萄牙作战直到1656年议和。1648年，萨尔瓦多·科雷亚·德萨的葡萄牙—巴西远征军把荷兰人赶走。此后罗安达成为向巴西贩运奴隶的中心：港中挤满巴西船只，姆本杜和伊姆班加拉商人把掳来的人口从内陆送来，到1751年，每年有五千至一万人在此被卖为奴。

en:
Mbamba was the southern march of the Kingdom of Kongo, a coastal province on the Atlantic between the Congo estuary held by Soyo and the Mbundu frontier beyond Mbwila. Its people were Bakongo villagers of fishing and farming settlements; its governor, the Mwene Mbamba, was one of the great electors of the manikongo, and the province had been part of the kingdom since its rise around 1390. Long the crown's shield against the lands to the south, Mbamba also held the open beaches where inland ivory was traded on toward the sea. In 1444 the Mwene Mbamba ruled this frontier in the king's name: his villages paid fish, grain and ivory, and his war bands watched the border country where Kongo's power thinned out.

After the court's conversion the province's dukes became kingmakers: early in the seventeenth century Duke António da Silva placed Bernardo II on the throne and then replaced him with Álvaro III. In 1622 a Portuguese army from Luanda with Imbangala mercenaries overran the south and at Mbumbi killed the new Duke of Mbamba and the Marquis of Mpemba; the former duke Pedro II, now manikongo, led the royal army south, broke the invasion at Mbanda Kasi the following January, freed the subjects the Portuguese had carried off, and wrote to the Dutch Estates General proposing an alliance to take Luanda. In 1641 a Mbamba contingent fought beside the Dutch when they seized that city. At Mbwila in 1665 the Portuguese killed King António I and broke the kingdom; São Salvador was sacked in 1678, and for forty years the Kimpanzu and Kinlaza houses fought over the ruins, selling defeated rivals down slave routes that ran north through Loango and south to Luanda. The Kimpanzu kept a court at Luvata, and order returned only in 1709, when Pedro IV reoccupied São Salvador. Mbamba saw another major war in the 1730s, and its coast remained one of the sources of Kongo slaves through the rest of the century.
zh:
姆班巴是刚果王国的南方边省，西临大西洋，北接索约所据的刚果河口，南连姆布维拉以外的姆本杜边境。居民是巴刚果人，住在以渔耕为生的村落里；省长姆韦内·姆班巴是马尼刚果手下最有权势的选侯之一，这片土地自1390年前后刚果兴起以来就是王国的一部分。姆班巴长期充当王权抵御南方的屏障，又有开阔的海滩，内地市集的象牙从这里转运出海。1444年，姆韦内·姆班巴奉国王之名镇守边疆：村落缴纳鱼、谷物和象牙，战士戍守着刚果王权渐趋稀薄的边境地带。

王室皈依基督教后，姆班巴公爵成了拥立新王的人：17世纪初，公爵安东尼奥·达席尔瓦先把贝尔纳多二世推上王位，随后又换成阿尔瓦罗三世。1622年，罗安达的葡萄牙军队带着因班加拉雇佣兵横扫南方，在姆本比杀死新任姆班巴公爵和姆彭巴侯爵；出身姆班巴公爵的马尼刚果佩德罗二世亲率王军南下，于次年1月在姆班达卡西击溃入侵者，救回被掳走的臣民，还致信荷兰联省议会，提议结盟攻取罗安达。1641年荷兰人夺取罗安达时，姆班巴的军队就和他们并肩作战。1665年，葡萄牙人在姆布维拉杀死国王安东尼奥一世，王国随之崩解；圣萨尔瓦多于1678年遭洗劫，此后四十年间金潘祖与金拉扎两派在废墟上厮杀，战败的政敌沿贩奴路线被卖往北方的卢安果和南方的罗安达。金潘祖一派在洛瓦塔维持朝廷，秩序直到1709年佩德罗四世重占圣萨尔瓦多才告恢复。1730年代姆班巴又经历一场大战，此后直到18世纪末，这里的海岸始终是刚果奴隶的来源地之一。

en:
Anziku was the Portuguese name for the Tio kingdom of the Teke people, whose king held the title makoko. His capital stood on the open Mbe plains north of the Congo River; the country's wealth lay to the south at Pool Malebo, the wide, lake-like reach where canoe cargoes from the deep interior had to be unloaded, since falls on the lower river blocked the way to the sea, and carried overland by caravans from the Atlantic coast. In Kikongo the name Teke means 'to sell', and neighbours knew the Tio first as merchants who took tolls at the Pool and tribute of copper and ivory from the river villages. Smithing went with kingship: six ritual anvils stood near the Lefini Falls, dwelling place of the national spirit Nkwe Mbali, and the royal-anvil rites of Loango and Kongo are thought to derive from Tio practice. In 1444 the makoko was the great inland rival of the manikongo, and Kongo's eastward wars had already come to a stop against his northern marches.

Kongo never found an answer to the Tio. In 1491 the manikongo asked the Portuguese for help against them, and King Henrique I was himself killed fighting the Tio in 1568. When Olfert Dapper described the country in the mid-seventeenth century, the makoko at his capital Monsol was said to count thirteen lesser kings beneath him, and two roads ran from the Pool to the sea, one through Loango and one through Portuguese Luanda. Tio merchants kept Europeans away from the Pool: Italian missionaries who reached its bank in the seventeenth century were threatened and turned back, never allowed to cross to the makoko, for the merchants feared baptism would cost them their tolls. Around 1700 charm-boxes called nkobi spread among the northern lords, granting power without the crown, and the lord Nzã Mbã grew rich on the Loango route, keeping musketeers and elephant hunters who were sold as slaves if they came back empty-handed. Royal campaigns against Boma came to nothing in 1710 and 1740, but about 1810 King Opontaba fought the northern lords to a draw at Idzwa and had the nkobi redistributed, and the authority of Mbe was briefly reaffirmed.
zh:
安齐库是葡萄牙人对特克人特约王国的称呼，国王号称马科科。王都设在刚果河以北开阔的姆贝平原，财脉却在南方的马莱博湖：河面在此展宽成湖，下游瀑布又阻断河运，海船无法上溯，来自内陆深处的独木舟商货只能在此上岸，换由大西洋海岸来的商队驮运。在刚果语里，「特克」就是「卖」的意思，邻人眼中的特克人首先是商人：他们在湖畔抽取过境税，向滨河村落收取铜和象牙作为贡赋。锻冶与王权相连，勒菲尼瀑布附近供着六座仪式铁砧，那里是国神恩奎·姆巴利的居所；据研究，卢安果和刚果宫廷的王权铁砧仪式都源自特约。1444年，马科科是马尼刚果在内陆的最大对手，刚果向东的战争已在他的北疆前止步。

刚果始终拿特约人没有办法：1491年马尼刚果请求葡萄牙人出兵相助，1568年连国王恩里克一世本人也死于对特约人的战事。17世纪中叶达珀记述这个国家时，定都蒙索尔的马科科据说下辖十三位小王；当时马莱博湖有两条商路通往海边，一条经卢安果，一条经葡属罗安达。特克商人长期把欧洲人挡在马莱博湖之外：17世纪抵达湖畔的意大利传教士遭到威胁和驱赶，始终不被允许渡河觐见马科科，因为商人担心洗礼会让他们丢掉过境税。1700年前后，名为恩科比的神龛匣在北方领主中传开，无需王冠就能赋予权力；领主恩赞·姆班凭卢安果商路致富，蓄有火枪队和猎象人，猎象空手而归者会被卖为奴隶。1710年和1740年对博马的两度用兵都无果而终；1810年前后，奥蓬塔巴国王在伊兹瓦与北方领主打成平手，随后将恩科比重新分配，姆贝的王权一度重振。

en:
Mpemba is the high ground around M'banza Kongo, the royal heartland of the Kingdom of Kongo. Around 1390 Lukeni lua Nimi, founder of the Kilukeni dynasty, built his capital on the Mongo dia Kongo, a hill where inland trade routes met in conquered Mpemba land. Kings moved war captives to the town, and by the mid-fifteenth century M'banza Kongo was a crowded walled capital, supplied with iron and grain by Mpemba's villages; the first Portuguese thought it as large as Évora. In 1444 the manikongo ruled his core provinces from this hill.

Diogo Cão reached the Congo mouth in 1483, and eight years later priests baptised the manikongo Nzinga a Nkuwu as João I. His son Afonso I won the succession war of 1509, saying Saint James and the Virgin had appeared to him in the fighting; he gave Kongo a Christian coat of arms, made Catholicism the royal cult, and his son Henrique became a bishop in 1518. A two-storey palace and stone churches rose by the old royal enclosure, one later becoming São Salvador Cathedral. Kongo paid in palm cloth, copper and ivory and, increasingly, in slaves; in 1526 Afonso was already protesting to Lisbon that his own people were kidnapped for sale. In 1568 the Jagas sacked the capital and drove out Álvaro I, who returned with Portuguese aid and ceded them Luanda, source of the nzimbu shells used as Kongo's money.

Disaster came at Mbwila on 29 October 1665, when a Portuguese-Angolan army killed the manikongo António I and took his head. The Kimpanzu and Kinlaza lineages fought for forty years; the capital was sacked and abandoned in 1678, rival kings holding mountain fastnesses such as Kibangu. Kimpa Vita, born in those hills c. 1684, taught that Jesus and the saints were Kongolese, and in 1705 she led thousands of peasants back into the ruins and lodged in the gutted cathedral, until Pedro IV had her burned as a heretic the next year. His troops retook the city in 1709; a reduced Kongo lived on, though José I fielded 30,000 men there in 1781 and the wars kept slaves flowing out through Soyo and Luanda.
zh:
姆彭巴是姆班扎刚果周围的高地，刚果王国的王畿。约1390年，基卢肯尼王朝的开创者卢肯尼·卢阿·尼米在蒙戈·迪亚·刚果山上建起都城，此山扼守商路交会处，地处被征服的姆彭巴故地。历代国王把战争俘虏迁居都城，到15世纪中叶，姆班扎刚果已是城墙之内人烟稠密的都城，姆彭巴各村为它供应铁器和粮食，最早到来的葡萄牙人说它有葡萄牙埃武拉那么大。1444年，刚果之王马尼刚果就在这座山上统治王国的核心诸省。

1483年迪奥戈·康抵达刚果河口，八年后神父为马尼刚果恩济加·恩库武施洗，他取教名若昂一世。其子阿方索一世在1509年的继统之战中取胜，自称圣雅各与圣母在战中向他显灵；他为刚果设计基督教纹章，把天主教立为王室信仰，儿子恩里克1518年成为主教。旧日王寨旁建起两层王宫和石造教堂，其中一座后来成为圣萨尔瓦多主座教堂。刚果用棕布、铜和象牙支付，后来越来越多地用奴隶；1526年阿方索已在致信里斯本，抗议本国百姓遭掳走贩卖。1568年雅加人洗劫都城、逐走阿尔瓦罗一世，他靠葡萄牙援军还都，把罗安达割让给对方，当地出产的贝壳是刚果的货币。

大难在1665年10月29日降临，葡属安哥拉军队在姆布维拉击杀马尼刚果安东尼奥一世，取下他的首级。金潘祖与金拉扎两个王族随后打了四十年内战；都城于1678年遭劫废弃，争位的国王们退守基班古山一类山寨。约1684年生于这些山地的基姆帕·维塔宣称耶稣和诸圣徒本是刚果人，1705年她率数千农民重回废墟，住进被掏空的主座教堂，次年佩德罗四世将她以异端罪烧死。佩德罗的军队1709年收复城市，一个大为缩小的刚果继续存在，1781年若泽一世仍能在此一战投入三万大军，而战争让奴隶不断经索约和罗安达流出。

en:
Ndongo is the Mbundu country between the Dande and Kwanza rivers, backed by the Angolan highlands. From the fourteenth century iron ritual emblems called ngola gave authority to their guardians, and the king took the title ngola a kiluanje, from which the Portuguese formed the name Angola. In 1444 the highland settlement of Kabasa, also called Caculo Cabaça, was the seat of a ruler advised by a council of nobles and served across the villages by chiefs called sobas. Mbundu farmers and smiths supplied the court, which bound its villages through zumbi ancestors and ilundu land spirits. Two servile orders, the land-tied ijiko and the saleable abika, made the country vulnerable once European ships reached the mouth of the Kwanza.

The first Portuguese mission arrived in 1520 at Ndongo's own request, but Kongo still claimed the country as its vassal; around the middle of the century Ndongo broke from Kongo, and war with Portugal opened in 1579 after an ambush of a Portuguese column. Paulo Dias de Novais, grandson of the navigator Bartolomeu Dias, built the fort of Massangano on the Kwanza in 1582, and an assault on Kabasa in 1590 was crushed. In 1617 Portuguese and Imbangala forces sacked the capital and drove Ngola Mbandi to the Kindonga islands. In 1621 he sent his sister Nzinga to negotiate at Luanda: offered only a mat while the Portuguese governor sat in a chair, she had an attendant kneel and used her as a seat, spoke to the governor face to face, and accepted baptism as Ana de Sousa. She took power in 1624 and, driven out four years later, conquered Matamba and made it her base. When the Dutch seized Luanda in 1641 she joined them against Portugal, and with Dutch reinforcements routed a Portuguese army at Kombi in 1647. A treaty in 1657 recognized her as queen of Ndongo and Matamba. The client king of the rock fortress Pungo a Ndongo rebelled in 1670, and after a long siege the rocks fell in 1671; Ndongo's sobas then passed into the slave-trading colony of Portuguese Angola.
zh:
恩东戈是丹德河与宽扎河之间、背靠安哥拉高地的姆本杜人之地。从14世纪起，名为恩戈拉（ngola）的铁制宗教象征赋予其守护者权威，国王采用「恩戈拉·基卢安杰」的称号，葡萄牙人正是从恩戈拉叫出了「安哥拉」这个名字。1444年，山地聚落卡巴萨（亦称卡库洛·卡巴萨）是王都，国王有贵族会议辅佐，通过各村的索巴首领统辖地方；姆本杜农民和铁匠供应宫廷，祖姆比祖先与伊伦杜土地神灵维系着各个村落。依附于土地的伊吉科和可以买卖的阿比卡构成两等依附者，欧洲船只一到宽扎河口，这种身份区分就招来了大祸。

1520年，第一个葡萄牙使团应恩东戈自己的请求而来，但刚果仍声称对它拥有宗主权；16世纪中叶，恩东戈摆脱刚果独立，1579年恩东戈伏击一支葡萄牙纵队，战争就此爆发。航海家巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士的孙子保罗·迪亚斯·德·诺瓦伊斯1582年在宽扎河修筑马萨加诺要塞，1590年强攻卡巴萨被击退。1617年，葡萄牙人与因班加拉人联军洗劫王都，把恩戈拉·姆班迪赶到金东加群岛。1621年，他派妹妹恩津加赴罗安达谈判：葡萄牙总督坐着椅子，却只给她一张席子，恩津加便让一名侍女跪下以身为座，与总督平视交涉，并受洗取名安娜·德·索萨。她1624年掌权，四年后被逐，随后征服马塔姆巴并以之为根基。1641年荷兰夺取罗安达，她与荷兰结盟共同对付葡萄牙，1647年靠荷兰援军在科姆比击溃葡萄牙军队。1657年，条约承认她为恩东戈和马塔姆巴女王。岩石要塞蓬戈·安东戈的附庸国王1670年起兵，经长期围攻，岩山于1671年陷落；恩东戈诸索巴随后被纳入葡属安哥拉这个奴隶贸易殖民地。

en:
Benguela lies on the bay where the Catumbela River comes out of the central Angolan highlands. In 1444 the shore and the plateau behind it belonged to the small Ovimbundu polity the Portuguese later called the Kingdom of Benguela, whose caravans carried cattle and copper down to the coast; local rulers and merchants from the highlands gave the open roadstead its value, and no European had yet settled there.

The Portuguese crown created a separate captaincy of Benguela in 1615, chiefly to reach the copper country of Sumbe Ambela. Two years later Manuel Cerveira Pereira sailed south from Luanda with 130 men and founded São Felipe de Benguela on Baía das Vacas, with a fortress by the beach. Dutch West India Company troops took it in 1641 and held the bay until Salvador Correia de Sá's expedition retook it in 1648. The rammed-earth fortress, 300 by 150 metres, was completed in 1661 and later held convicts deported from Portugal. A French naval raid in 1705 nearly destroyed the town. Between such wars Benguela lived from the trade in people: ships from Brazil and Cuba anchored a mile offshore and loaded captives brought from the interior, and the town became, after Luanda, the busiest slaving port on this stretch of the south Atlantic coast.
zh:
本格拉坐落在卡通贝拉河从安哥拉中部高地入海处的海湾边。1444年时，海岸和后方高原属于葡萄牙人后来称为本格拉王国的奥文本杜人小政权，高原商队把牲畜和铜贩运到海边；空旷锚地的价值来自本地首领和从高地下来的商人，欧洲人还没有在此定居。

1615年，葡萄牙王室单设本格拉都督区，主要为了打通松贝安贝拉的铜产地。两年后，曼努埃尔·塞尔韦拉·佩雷拉率一百三十人从罗安达南下，在瓦卡斯湾建立圣菲利普·德·本格拉，海滩旁筑起要塞。1641年，荷兰西印度公司军队攻占此地，占据海湾直到1648年萨尔瓦多·科雷亚·德萨的远征军将其夺回。夯土要塞长三百米、宽一百五十米，1661年建成，后来还用来关押从葡萄牙流放来的犯人。1705年法国海军的一次袭击几乎摧毁城镇。在历次战争的间隙，本格拉靠人口生意维持：巴西和古巴船只在离岸一英里处下锚，装上从内陆掳来的人，使这里成为仅次于罗安达、这段南大西洋海岸上最繁忙的奴隶贸易港。

en:
Ezorongondo is the Herero name for Walvis Bay, the Whale Bay of Dutch and English sailors. The province runs south along the Namib shore as far as the cove the Portuguese mapped as Angra Pequena. Behind Pelican Point lies the only sheltered deep-water roadstead on this coast, where southern right whales gathered to feed and breed. In 1444 Khoisan-speaking hunters and herders moved between fog, dunes, salt pans and the dry mouth of the Kuiseb, camping wherever the waterholes allowed. Herero pastoralists had not yet entered the land, and no outside power knew the bay.

Bartolomeu Dias anchored his São Cristóvão in the roadstead on 8 December 1487 and named it O Golfo de Santa Maria da Conceição; on the same voyage he charted the cove to the south as Angra Pequena, but the Portuguese fortified neither anchorage. English fishing boats and then Dutch and English whalers came for the fish and the whales, yet the desert behind the beach could not feed a permanent town. At the end of the eighteenth century Dutch East India Company ships used the bay as a stopover between the Cape and Europe, and after a short Dutch occupation it passed under British control in 1795. In 1821 Ezorongondo was still only a calling place for ships, its desert interior left to Khoisan travellers and herders.
zh:
埃佐龙贡多是鲸湾港的赫雷罗语名称，荷兰和英国水手把这个港湾叫作「鲸湾」。这片省份沿纳米布海岸向南，一直延伸到葡萄牙人测绘为安格拉·佩克纳的小湾。鹈鹕角环护着这一带海岸唯一的避风深水锚地，南露脊鲸成群到此觅食育幼。1444年，讲科伊桑语的猎人和牧人在雾气、沙丘、盐沼和奎斯布河干河口之间往来，哪里有水洼就在哪里宿营；赫雷罗牧民尚未进入此地，也没有外部势力知道这个海湾。

1487年12月8日，巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士率「圣克里斯托旺号」在锚地停泊，将其命名为圣母受孕湾；同一次航行中，他把南面的小湾测绘为安格拉·佩克纳，但葡萄牙人在两个锚地都没有修筑工事。先是英国渔船，后来又有荷兰和英国捕鲸船，为鱼群和鲸群而来，可海滩后方是沙漠，养不起一座常住城镇。18世纪末，荷兰东印度公司的船只把这里当作好望角与欧洲之间航线的中途停靠站；经过短暂的荷兰占领，海湾于1795年转归英国控制。1821年的埃佐龙贡多仍只是船只停靠之处，沙漠内陆往来的仍是科伊桑猎人和牧人。

en:
Lesser Namaqualand covers the Nama coast between the lower Orange and the Olifants rivers: foggy Atlantic shore, granite hills and sparse Kamiesberg grazing. The Nama, the strongest Khoekhoe group in the region, moved sheep and cattle between seasonal waterholes, while San hunters lived in the more broken country. Nama smiths already worked native copper. In 1444 power belonged to Nama captains who knew the wells, and a clan's standing rested on livestock, copper and access to water after the brief rains.

Copper first brought Cape expeditions into this dry country. Trekboers seeking pasture had reached the Vanrhynsdorp area by about 1662, and in 1685 Governor Simon van der Stel travelled north after seeing Nama copperware. His party reached the Koperberg near the later Springbok, where copper ore lay in the hills, but ox wagons could not make mining pay across the desert. Farms spread only slowly along the better-watered high ground. Christiaan Albrecht opened missionary contact in 1809, and Heinrich Schmelen of the London Missionary Society established the Steinkopf station among the Nama in 1817. The copper at Koperberg remained known but unworked on any large scale.
zh:
小纳马夸兰指下奥兰治河与奥利凡茨河之间的纳马海岸一段，有多雾的大西洋海岸、花岗岩丘陵和卡米斯山的稀疏牧场。纳马人是当地最强的科伊霍伊族群，赶着牛羊在季节性水眼之间迁移；桑人猎人则生活在更崎岖的山野。纳马工匠已经会加工天然铜。1444年，权势属于熟悉各处水井的纳马首领；短暂雨季之后，一个氏族的地位要看牲畜、铜器和取水权。

最早把开普探险队引到这片干旱地带的是铜。约1662年，寻找牧场的游牧垦民已抵达范伦斯多普一带；1685年，开普总督西蒙·范德斯特尔见到纳马铜器后亲自北上。他的队伍到达后来斯普林博克附近的科珀山，在山里找到了铜矿石，可是牛车穿越荒漠的成本使采铜无利可图。农庄只在水源较好的高地缓慢扩展。1809年，克里斯蒂安·阿尔布雷希特开始与纳马人传教接触；1817年，伦敦会的海因里希·施梅伦在纳马人中建立斯泰因科普夫传教站。科珀山的铜矿虽已为人所知，却仍未得到大规模开采。

en:
The Roggeveld is a high, cold plateau on the northern edge of the Karoo. Its western rim is the escarpment that drops to the Tankwa Karoo; its highest peak rises to 1,739 metres and carries snow in winter, and the plateau around the later town of Sutherland numbers among the coldest country in South Africa. Khoisan hunter-gatherers camped at its springs and left ostrich-eggshell fragments around stone-packed shelters, while Khoekhoe herders kept cattle and sheep in stone kraals. In 1444 no colonial power ruled here, and people moved with the game and the grazing, among stands of the wild rye Secale africanum that later gave the plateau its name.

Trekboers from the Cape reached the Roggeveld early in the eighteenth century and the first loan farm, Uitkyk, was granted in 1746. Most holdings were summer posts: flocks wintered in the lower Karoo and returned to the high pasture in summer, while San stock raids kept the frontier dangerous. Carl Peter Thunberg, a Swedish naturalist and apostle of Linnaeus later called the father of South African botany, was the first to write the name down, in 1774, explaining it as wild rye. Hinrich Lichtenstein found parts of the plateau depopulated in 1803, and when William Burchell crossed it in 1811 some settler families still lived in wagons, tents and reed huts.
zh:
罗格菲尔德是卡鲁北缘一片高寒高原，西缘是俯临坦克瓦卡鲁的断崖，最高峰海拔1739米、冬季积雪，后来萨瑟兰一带的高原是南非最冷的地方之一。科伊桑猎人在泉边扎营，石砌挡风遮蔽所周围散落着鸵鸟蛋壳碎片；科伊科伊牧人在石圈畜栏里饲养牛羊。1444年时还没有殖民政权到此，人们追逐猎物和牧场迁徙，穿行在野生黑麦（Secale africanum）丛间，这种野麦后来给高原取了名。

18世纪初，开普的游牧布尔人进入罗格菲尔德，第一处借地牧场乌伊特凯克于1746年批出。多数地产只是夏季牧点：畜群在低地卡鲁过冬，夏天赶回高原，桑人盗畜也使边疆处处危险。瑞典博物学家、林奈的弟子卡尔·彼得·通贝里被称为南非植物学之父，1774年第一个写下罗格菲尔德这个名字，解释其意为野麦。1803年欣里希·利希滕施泰因看到高原部分地方已经流散；1811年威廉·伯切尔路过时，仍有移民家庭住在大车、帐篷和芦苇棚里。

en:
The Cape is the peninsula below Table Mountain, with Table Bay on its Atlantic side and False Bay beyond the mountains. Fresh water runs off the mountain toward the Salt and Liesbeeck rivers through ground used as pasture. In 1444 Goringhaiqua and other Khoekhoe clans moved cattle there and traded stock with neighbouring San hunters. No European fort, garden or permanent landing place occupied the bay.

Bartolomeu Dias rounded the peninsula in 1488 and opened the sea route that later Portuguese captains followed to India. The shore was not easily taken: in 1510 Goringhaiqua fighters killed Francisco de Almeida, the Portuguese viceroy, and more than sixty of his men at the Salt River. After the Dutch ship Nieuwe Haarlem was wrecked in Table Bay in 1647, its crew's favourable report persuaded the Dutch East India Company to use the bay as a refreshment station. Jan van Riebeeck landed on 6 April 1652 with about ninety people and built a clay-and-timber fort, gardens and pens for passing East Indiamen. Free burghers received Liesbeeck farms in 1657, enslaved labour arrived the next year, and the first wine harvest came in 1659, when Doman led Khoekhoe resistance. The five-bastioned stone Castle of Good Hope replaced the old fort between 1666 and 1679. Under Simon van der Stel, farms spread to Stellenbosch, and Huguenot settlers strengthened the wine estates from 1688.

The wars against France turned the provisions port into a naval prize. British forces took it after fighting at Muizenberg in 1795, returned it to the Batavian Republic under the Peace of Amiens in 1803, and landed again in 1806 to defeat Batavian troops at Blaauwberg. In the 1814 peace settlement the Cape became a permanent British possession.
zh:
开普是桌山下的半岛，西临桌湾，山后是福尔斯湾。桌山的淡水流向盐河与利斯贝克河，沿岸土地是牧场。1444年，戈林海夸等科伊霍伊氏族在这一带放牧牛群，并与邻近的桑人猎人交易牲畜。桌湾还没有欧洲人的堡垒、园圃或固定登陆点。

1488年，巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士绕过半岛，打开了后来葡萄牙船长前往印度的航路。但这片海岸并不能轻易占据：1510年，戈林海夸战士在盐河击杀葡萄牙总督弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达及其六十余名部下。1647年荷兰商船「新哈勒姆号」在桌湾失事，幸存船员带回的好评促使荷兰东印度公司把这里设为补给站。1652年4月6日，扬·范·里贝克率约九十人登岸，修筑土木堡垒、园圃和畜栏，为往来东方的商船供应物资。1657年，自由市民获得利斯贝克河畔农场；次年奴隶劳力被运入；1659年第一批酿酒葡萄收获，同年多曼领导科伊霍伊人抵抗。1666年至1679年，设有五座棱堡的石砌好望堡取代旧堡。西蒙·范德斯特尔任内，农庄扩展到斯泰伦博斯；1688年起，胡格诺派移民增强了葡萄园产业。

对法战争使这个补给港成为海上战利品。1795年，英军经梅曾贝赫之战夺取开普；1803年依《亚眠和约》归还巴达维亚共和国；1806年英军再次登陆，在布劳贝希击败巴达维亚军队。1814年的和约安排中，开普成为英国的永久属地。

en:
The Great Karoo is a wide semi-arid basin between the Great Escarpment and the Swartberg, where low shrubs and drought grass live on uncertain rain and scattered fountains. Khoekhoe pastoralists once moved cattle and sheep across these flats, and San hunters knew the springs and game paths around the place later called Beaufort and painted on sheltered rock faces in the surrounding ridges. In 1444 there was no town or colonial frontier here; when the grazing failed, whoever held a fountain could stay on with their stock.

European loan farms had reached the Nuweveld foothills by 1760, when Abraham and Jacob le Clercq, later De Klerk, were granted Hooyvlakte. Competition for its fountains brought repeated stock raids and fighting between settlers, San bands, Xhosa cattle keepers, runaway slaves and outlaws. The settlers long called the dry country Droogeveld, and only in 1794 did the Cape Political Council first write Caro, a word taken from Khoe speech meaning dry or hard land. In 1818 Lord Charles Somerset's government founded Beaufort on Hooyvlakte and named it for his father the Duke of Beaufort, sending a magistrate and a church to farms that had until then answered to no fixed authority.
zh:
大卡鲁是大断崖与斯瓦特山之间一片广阔的半干旱盆地，低矮灌木和耐旱牧草只靠不稳的年雨和零星泉水生长。科伊科伊牧人曾赶着牛羊走遍这些平原，桑人猎人熟悉后来博福特一带的泉眼和兽道，还在周围山脊有遮蔽的岩壁上绘下岩画。1444年时这里没有城镇，也没有殖民边疆；牧草枯萎时，谁占住一处泉水，谁才能带着牲畜留下。

到1760年，欧洲人的借地农场已推进到努韦尔德山脚下，亚伯拉罕·勒克莱尔和雅各布·勒克莱尔（后来改姓德克勒克）在这一年获得霍伊弗拉克特。泉眼之争引来一次又一次盗畜和交战，移民、桑人团伙、牧牛的科萨人、逃亡奴隶和亡命者都卷入其中。移民早先把这片干地叫做「德罗赫菲尔德」（Droogeveld），直到1794年开普政治委员会才第一次写下「卡罗」（Caro）一名，这个词来自科伊语，意为干旱或坚硬的土地。1818年，查尔斯·萨默塞特勋爵政府在霍伊弗拉克特设立博福特，以其父博福特公爵命名，为这些向来不受固定官府管辖的牧场派来法官和教会。

en:
Swellendam lies below the Langeberg, where Overberg wheat country rises toward the dry Little Karoo and streams feed the Breede. In 1444 Hessekwa and Attaqua Khoekhoe grazed cattle on seasonal veld around the Buffeljags and Koringlands rivers, while San hunters used the mountains. No Dutch drostdy, wagon road or town yet occupied these valleys.

Cattle traders from the Cape entered the valleys after 1652. The Dutch East India Company laid out Swellendam in 1745, naming it for Governor Hendrik Swellengrebel and his wife Helena ten Damme, and placed a drostdy on its eastern frontier. Artisans and wainwrights settled around the official residence, and wagons carried grain and livestock between the inland farms and the Cape. Anger at Company prices and maladministration turned the district into a small republic on 17 June 1795, with the Swellendam-born farmer Hermanus Steyn as president. A commando rode to Muizenberg before British occupation ended the republic on 4 November. Merino bloodstock from Spain reached the Cape in 1789, and descendants were brought to Swellendam in 1803 to improve local wool sheep. In 1812 the London Missionary Society settled about 300 to 400 surviving Hessekwa and Attaqua at Suurbraak under Johannes Seidenfaden; five years later German Separatists founded the Little Karoo mission village of Zoar.
zh:
斯韦伦丹坐落在朗厄山麓，奥弗贝赫的麦作地带逐渐抬向干旱的小卡鲁，沿途溪涧汇入布里德河。1444年，赫塞夸与阿塔夸两支科伊霍伊人在布费尔亚赫斯河和科林兰兹河一带的季节性草原牧牛，桑人猎人则在山间活动。这些谷地还没有荷兰人的政务官公馆、马车路或城镇。

1652年开普建立补给站后，牲畜商贩进入这些谷地。荷兰东印度公司于1745年规划建立斯韦伦丹，以总督亨德里克·斯韦伦格雷贝尔及其妻子海伦娜·滕·达默命名，并把政务官公馆设在这条东部边线上。工匠和造车匠在公馆周围定居，马车把内陆农庄的谷物和牲畜运往开普。对公司收购价和弊政的不满，使这一地区在1795年6月17日成为一个小共和国，出生于斯韦伦丹的农场主赫尔马努斯·斯泰恩被推举为总统。一支民团骑马前往梅曾贝赫；11月4日英国占领开普，共和国结束。来自西班牙的美利奴种羊1789年运抵开普，其后代在1803年被带到斯韦伦丹，用以改良毛用绵羊。1812年，伦敦会把约三百至四百名幸存的赫塞夸人和阿塔夸人安置在聚尔布拉克，由约翰内斯·塞登法登主持；五年后，德意志分离派信徒建立了小卡鲁传教村庄措阿尔。

en:
This is the Transkei, the green river valleys and surf-bound coast beyond the Kei, home to Xhosa-speaking nations such as the Gcaleka, Thembu, Mpondo and Bomvana. Nguni cattle-herders and grain-growers had settled the Eastern Cape by the early centuries of the era and absorbed Khoekhoe and San clans; Xhosa royal genealogy begins with Tshawe, founder of the royal house before the fifteenth century. In 1444 the land was ordered through homesteads, cattle enclosures and chiefly councils, and a man's standing was counted in cattle; no European ship had yet passed this shore.

After Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape in 1488, this coast became a graveyard for the Portuguese carracks of the India run. In April 1554 the São Bento, a 900-ton ship homeward bound from Cochin with spices, silk and porcelain, drove onto the rocks of the Wild Coast. Her captain was Fernão Álvares Cabral, son of the man who had claimed Brazil for Portugal, and the survivors' long march north gave the Portuguese one of their best-remembered shipwreck narratives. In the same century Nxeko united the Thembu around Dedesi in the Mthatha country as a kingdom in their own right.

War pressed in from the southwest. The first Cape frontier war between the Xhosa kingdoms and the Cape colonists broke out in 1779, and even the campaigns that ended in 1819 carried British power no farther than the Fish and Keiskamma rivers, well short of the Kei. In April 1819 the prophet Makhanda, councillor to Chief Ndlambe, led thousands of warriors against the British garrison at Grahamstown and was beaten back; imprisoned on Robben Island, he and thirty other prisoners tried to swim to freedom on Christmas Day 1820, but only four men made the crossing alive and Makhanda drowned. Clans fleeing the Zulu wars were taken in beyond the Kei and became the amaMfengu, 'the wanderers'. In 1820 Hintsa came to the Xhosa royal seat beyond the Kei, and in 1821 every chiefdom beyond the river still ruled itself.
zh:
这里是特兰斯凯，即凯河以外绿色河谷与浪涛拍岸的海岸，盖卡莱卡、滕布、姆蓬多、姆瓦纳等操科萨语的部族都住在这一带。恩古尼牧人和农人在纪元最初几个世纪已定居东开普，牧牛养羊、种植谷物，并把科伊霍伊和桑人诸部吸收进来；科萨王室的谱系从查韦开始，他在15世纪以前开创了查韦王族。1444年时，维系这片土地的是村落、牛栏和首领议事会，一个人的身份高低以牛群计算，欧洲船只还没有经过这段海岸。

1488年巴尔托洛梅乌·迪亚士绕过好望角以后，这段海岸成了葡萄牙往返印度大帆船的葬身之地。1554年4月，900吨的「圣本笃号」从科钦满载香料、丝绸和瓷器归国，在狂野海岸触礁；船长费尔南·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔是为葡萄牙夺得巴西的佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔之子，幸存者长途北行的经历后来成为葡萄牙最有名的沉船故事之一。同在16世纪，恩谢科以代德西和姆塔塔一带为中心统一滕布人，建立了自己的王国。

战争从西南方向逼近。科萨诸王国与开普殖民者之间的第一场边境战争爆发于1779年；到1819年战事结束，英国势力也只推进到大鱼河和凯斯卡马河，离凯河尚远。1819年4月，首领恩德拉姆贝的谋士、先知马卡纳（Makhanda）率数千战士攻打格雷厄姆斯敦的英国守军，被击退；他被囚于罗本岛，1820年圣诞节与另外三十名囚犯泅水逃亡，三十一人中只有四人生还，马卡纳溺死。为躲避祖鲁战乱西逃的诸部在凯河以外被收留，称为阿马芬古（amaMfengu），意为「流浪者」。1820年欣察（Hintsa）即科萨王位，王庭设在凯河以外；1821年，凯河以外的各部仍由自己的首领统治。

en:
Green hills and a sheltered lagoon on the coast of Natal drew Nguni farmers and cattle-keepers southward from the early 1300s, while the earlier San hunter-gatherers were absorbed or drifted off toward the Drakensberg. Around the Bay of Natal lived clans remembered as the amaLala and amaMbo, sowing millet and sorghum, tending chiefly herds and working iron. In 1444 only local fishermen and the occasional coastal trader knew the bay; no European sail had yet been sighted there.

What Europeans learned of Natal for a long time came from shipwrecks. On Christmas Day 1497 Vasco da Gama, bound for India, sighted the green shore and named it Natal, the Portuguese word for Christmas. In June 1552 the great carrack São João, limping home from Cochin, broke up on the south coast: roughly five hundred people got ashore and set out on the six-hundred-kilometre walk to Delagoa Bay, but only about twenty-five reached it alive. Among the dead were her captain, Manuel de Sousa Sepúlveda, and his wife Leonor, daughter of Garcia de Sá, the governor of Portuguese India. In 1686 the Dutch East Indiaman Stavenisse was lost off the bay and her crew lived for months under the protection of the Abambo, whose country they called Embo; the galiot Noord fetched them away in 1689, and the Cape government even signed a paper buying the bay, though no Dutch settlers ever followed. The old chiefdoms ended in the Mfecane, when Zulu armies crossed the Tugela after 1818 and scattered, absorbed or expelled Natal's clans, leaving the bay and its hinterland nearly empty of people by 1821.
zh:
14世纪初起，青葱丘陵和一处风浪不兴的潟湖港湾吸引恩古尼农人和牧人南迁；更早的桑人猎民或被融合，或渐渐退入德拉肯斯贝格群山。纳塔尔湾周围住着后来被称为拉拉人和姆博人的诸部，他们种植谷子和高粱，为首领牧牛，也会冶铁。1444年时，知晓这座港湾的只有当地渔民和偶尔路过的沿岸商人，海上还从未出现过欧洲船帆。

欧洲人最初认识纳塔尔，留下的几乎全是沉船记录。1497年圣诞节，驶往印度的瓦斯科·达·伽马望见这片翠绿海岸，以葡萄牙语的「圣诞节」一词称之为纳塔尔。1552年6月，从科钦艰难归国的大帆船「圣若昂号」在南海岸解体：约五百人登岸，徒步北上六百公里前往德拉戈阿湾，最后只有约二十五人走到。船长曼努埃尔·德·索萨·塞普尔韦达和妻子莱奥诺尔都死在路上，莱奥诺尔的父亲正是葡属印度总督加西亚·德·萨。1686年，荷兰东印度公司商船「斯塔瓦尼塞号」在湾外遇险，船员被阿班博人收留数月，他们把这片土地称作恩博；1689年快艇「诺德号」将人接走，开普当局甚至签约买下港湾，却始终没有移民前来。纳塔尔诸部最后毁于姆费卡内大动荡：1818年以后祖鲁军队渡过图盖拉河，诸部或溃散、或被吞并、或被逐走，到1821年，港湾及其腹地已几乎没有人烟。

en:
Delagoa Bay is a wide, island-studded lagoon opening to the Indian Ocean, with the Espírito Santo estuary of the Matola, Tembe and Umbeluzi rivers feeding its western shore. Ronga-speaking clans fished the shallows, tilled the hot coastal flats and herded cattle along the banks. The Matsolo, whose name later passed to the Matola river and town, held the country behind the estuary, while the Tembe dominated the sandy shores and islands to the south. Tembe chiefs grew rich on ivory brought down from the interior, paying for beads, brass and cloth and keeping war bands in their service. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered the lagoon.

The first Portuguese ship came in 1502 with António de Campo, one of Vasco da Gama's captains, and in 1544 the trader Lourenço Marques charted the estuaries and gave the bay its name; for two centuries the Portuguese kept no more than a few small, intermittently held stations. In 1721 the Dutch East India Company built Fort Lijdzaamheid on the shore, a fever-ridden post that the English pirate John Taylor briefly seized in 1722, a year after he took the retiring viceroy of Goa's treasure ship in the Mascarene Islands; the Dutch abandoned the fort altogether in 1730. In the late 1770s William Bolts brought an Austrian company to the bay, shipping as much as 75,000 pounds of ivory a year until Portuguese warships from Goa expelled him in 1781. To keep other powers out, the Portuguese then raised a fortress of their own named Lourenço Marques, at whose gates Tembe and Matsolo chiefs went on selling ivory; French, British and American whalers also called there for provisions in the early nineteenth century.
zh:
马措洛位于德拉戈阿湾一带；德拉戈阿湾是一片宽阔、岛屿错落的潟湖，通向印度洋，西岸有马托拉河、滕贝河与翁贝卢济河汇成的圣埃斯皮里图河口注入。说龙加语的诸部在浅滩捕鱼，在炎热的海滨低地耕作，沿河两岸牧牛。马措洛人据有河口背后的土地，他们的名字后来给了马托拉河与马托拉城；滕贝人称雄南面的沙岸和岛屿，首领们靠内陆南下的象牙致富，换得珠子、黄铜和布匹，还能豢养自己的武装。1444年时，还没有欧洲船驶入过这片潟湖。

1502年，瓦斯科·达·伽马麾下的船长安东尼奥·德·坎波最先驶入海湾；1544年商人洛伦索·马克斯勘察各河口并为海湾定名，此后两百年间，葡萄牙人只维持着几处时设时废的小商站。1721年，荷兰东印度公司在岸边筑起莱德扎姆海德堡，那里瘴气横行，1722年被英国海盗约翰·泰勒一度占据——此前一年，他刚在马斯克林群岛劫走果阿卸任总督的宝船；荷兰人最终在1730年弃守。1770年代末，威廉·博尔茨代表一家奥地利公司来到湾边，每年运出的象牙多达7.5万磅，直到1781年被果阿派来的葡萄牙战舰赶走。为防别国再打海湾的主意，葡萄牙人随即筑起自己的堡垒，以洛伦索·马克斯为名；滕贝和马措洛的首领照旧在堡门口出售象牙，进入19世纪，又有法国、英国和美国的捕鲸船前来补给。

en:
Inhambane lies on a deep Indian Ocean inlet where the small Mutamba River enters a bay enclosed by two sandy headlands, one of the few safe harbours on this straight stretch of the Mozambique coast. Dhows from Kilwa and the Swahili coast had called there since the eleventh century, trading cloth and beads for pearls and ambergris and coasting north to Chibuene. Bitonga villagers grew cotton and wove it themselves; Karanga chiefs, who had overrun the coast before the Portuguese arrived, took tribute from the Tonga communities and kept most of their dealings with Muslim merchants in their own hands. In 1444 Inhambane was therefore an African port inside the Indian Ocean trading world, with no European yet settled there.

Vasco da Gama replenished his ships in the bay in January 1498 and was received well enough to name the coast Terra da Boa Gente, the 'Land of the Good People'. A ship sent by Francisco de Almeida was wrecked south of the bay in 1505, and the episode gave the Portuguese their first meeting with the Karanga chiefs. A permanent feitoria followed in 1534, and six years later Inhambane became the site of the first Jesuit mission in south-eastern Africa. The port did its busiest trade in the eighteenth century, when Indian merchants handled much of its ivory and slaves. From about the 1730s Tsonga groups pressed south into the Tonga lands, and by 1760 their raids reached the beaches near the town; after the 1770s the sugar and coffee islands of the French Mascarenes drew still more slave cargoes out of the bay.
zh:
伊尼扬巴内位于印度洋上一处深水海湾，穆坦巴小河在此入海，两道沙咀合围出天然良港，是这段平直的莫桑比克海岸上少有的避风处。早在11世纪，来自基尔瓦和斯瓦希里海岸的独桅帆船已在此停泊，用布匹和珠子换取珍珠、龙涎香，还北上奇布埃内贸易。比通加村民自种棉花、自行纺织；葡萄牙人到来之前，卡兰加酋长已征服海岸，向通加社群收取贡物，把持着他们与穆斯林商人的大部分生意。1444年的伊尼扬巴内因此是印度洋贸易圈里的一座非洲港口，还没有欧洲人在此定居。

1498年1月，瓦斯科·达伽马在此补给，因受到友好接待，把这一带命名为「好人之地」（Terra da Boa Gente）。1505年，弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达派出的一艘船在湾南失事，葡萄牙人借这次事故第一次见到卡兰加酋长。1534年葡萄牙人设立永久商站，六年后又把伊尼扬巴内建成他们在东南非的第一个耶稣会传教站。18世纪是港口最繁忙的年代，象牙和奴隶生意多由印度商人经手。约18世纪30年代起，聪加诸部向南压入通加人土地，到1760年前后袭扰已波及城边海滩；18世纪70年代以后，法属马斯克林群岛的甘蔗和咖啡种植岛又从湾中运走更多奴隶。

en:
In the granite hills south of the Zimbabwe Plateau stand the dry-stone walls of Zimbabwe, the Karanga Shona 'houses of stone'. The Great Enclosure rises in walls eleven metres high, the Conical Tower stands within it, and above the town looms the older hill complex with its shrine of Mwari. Karanga ancestors built all of it without mortar from the 11th century onward, and set eight soapstone birds on pillars the height of a man above the eastern enclosure; the birds are thought to show the bateleur eagle, the messenger of god in Shona belief. As capital of the kingdom of Zimbabwe the city drew gold from the southern mines down the Save and Runde rivers to Sofala, and Chinese porcelain, Persian pottery and Arab coins have been dug from its houses. At its peak perhaps 10,000 people lived across an area the size of medieval London. In the 15th century the gold routes bent north through the rising Mwenemutapa state; tradition says the prince Nyatsimba Mutota led part of the population away in search of salt. In 1444 the old capital lay under Mwenemutapa overlordship, its court long gone, though people still lived in the valleys.

The Portuguese on the coast never saw the city and wrote from hearsay. Diogo de Alcáçova described its walls in a letter of 1506; António Fernandes twice crossed the hinterland in 1513–1515 and noted mortarless stone strongholds; Vicente Pegado, captain of the Sofala garrison, recorded in 1531 a fortress of stones 'of marvellous size', which the Shona called Symbaoe, their word for a royal court. Two reports even spoke of an inscription over the gate in characters no Arab merchant who had seen it could read, and João de Barros wrote that the Shona themselves held the walls to be the devil's work. Such stories fed the legend of Ophir and the Queen of Sheba. Power on the plateau meanwhile passed to Changamire Dombo, perhaps a Mwenemutapa governor who built a following on the royal cattle; he crushed a Portuguese army, conquered Butua around 1683, massacred Portuguese traders in the 1690s and cleared every Portuguese off the plateau before dying around 1696. His Rozvi successors barred Europeans from their country and kept the ruins and the old goldfields through the 18th century. During the great drought of 1795–1800 Changamire Rupandamananga was said to let his people starve, and the civil wars ran on until at least 1808. By 1821 the valleys beneath the walls were empty.
zh:
津巴布韦高原以南的花岗岩丘陵中，矗立着津巴布韦的无浆石墙，卡兰加绍纳人称之为「石屋」。大围场的石墙高达十一米，墙内立着圆锥形石塔，城后更高的山丘上是年代更久、供奉姆瓦里的圣殿。卡兰加人的先祖自11世纪起不施灰浆筑起这一切，还在东围场上方立起八只皂石鸟，每只安在一人高的石柱上，一般认为雕的是短尾雕，绍纳人相信它是神的使者。作为津巴布韦王国的都城，石城把南方金矿的黄金经萨韦河与伦德河引向索法拉，房屋遗址中出土过中国瓷器、波斯陶器和阿拉伯钱币。极盛时约有一万居民，城区面积抵得上中世纪的伦敦。15世纪，黄金商路北折，改走新兴的穆韦内穆塔帕；相传王族尼亚钦巴·穆托塔率部分部众北上寻找盐源。1444年，这座旧都已在穆韦内穆塔帕治下，王廷早已迁走，谷地中却仍有人居住。

海岸上的葡萄牙人始终未曾亲见此城，只能凭传闻落笔。迪奥戈·德·阿尔卡索瓦1506年的信描述过它的石墙；安东尼奥·费尔南德斯1513至1515年两度穿行内陆，记下无浆石砌的堡垒；1531年，索法拉驻军司令维森特·佩加多记载，有一座「大得惊人的」石块垒成的要塞，绍纳人称之为辛巴韦，即他们语言中的王宫。还有两则传闻说，城门上方刻着铭文，见过它的阿拉伯商人没有一个认得那些字；若昂·德·巴罗斯则写道，绍纳人自己都相信这些墙是魔鬼所造。这些说法后来养出了俄斐与示巴女王的传说。高原上的权力转入昌加米尔·多姆博之手，他可能本是穆韦内穆塔帕的总督，用王室的牛群聚起部众，随后击溃一支葡萄牙军队，约1683年征服布图阿，1690年代又屠杀葡萄牙商人、把所有葡萄牙人逐出高原，约于1696年死去。他的罗兹维继任者不许欧洲人入境，在整个18世纪守住了石城废墟和古老金矿。1795至1800年的大旱中，昌加米尔·鲁潘达马南加据说坐视子民挨饿，引发的内战至少延续到1808年。到1821年，石墙下的谷地已经空无一人。

en:
Butua was the Kalanga country, the western Shona lands around Khami and the goldfields west of Great Zimbabwe. Early in the fifteenth century traders from Angoche opened a route up the Zambezi through Ingombe Ilede to these western workings, and the gold traffic that had fed Great Zimbabwe began to flow past it instead. At Khami a Leopard's Kopje chiefdom grew into the Torwa kingdom; its first remembered mambo was Madabhale, with the praise name Chibundule, 'the sounding of the war horn'. By 1444 Butua was a power in its own right, rich in cattle, ivory and gold, whose rulers kept the favour of Mwari, the high god of the Shona.

Khami was their stone capital for two centuries from about 1450. The Torwa lived on raised dry-stone terraces above the huts and cattle kraals of the commoners; the Hill Complex held the royal enclosure, and a retaining wall six metres high and sixty-eight metres long was dressed across its whole face with a checkerboard pattern in dark and light stone. Caravans carried Butua's gold first to Muslim and later to Portuguese traders, who called the kingdom the 'Mother of Gold', and Ahmad ibn Majid left its first mention in writing in 1502. In the 1490s the Torwa backed Changamire I's revolt against Mutapa; in 1493 their mambo sent the Mwenemutapa four thousand cattle and a gift of gold, and war between the two states ran on until 1512.

In the 1640s the mambo's brother, married into a family of Muslim traders called the Mwenye, drove him out, and he returned in 1644 with the soldiers of a Portuguese prazo-holder; Khami's Hill Complex was burned in the fighting. Around 1683 Changamire Dombo overran Butua and abandoned Khami for Danamombe, the capital of his Rozvi Empire. Kalanga tradition remembers the last Chibundule as a king with magic powers, beaten only after a bride sent by Dombo cut the horn-like braid in which his strength lay; by 1696 Dombo held all the old kingdom's goldfields.
zh:
布图阿是卡兰加人，即西绍纳人的土地，在卡米和大津巴布韦以西的金矿区一带。15世纪初，安戈谢商人开辟商路，经因贡贝伊莱德沿赞比西河深入西部金场，过去滋养大津巴布韦的黄金贸易改为绕古城而过。卡米的一个豹地文化酋邦随之壮大为托尔瓦王国；人们记得的第一位王叫马达巴莱，颂名奇本杜莱，意为「战角之声」。1444年，布图阿已自成一强，牛群、象牙和黄金富足，国王还维系着绍纳至高神姆瓦里的恩宠。

从约1450年起的两百年里，卡米是托尔瓦的石头都城。王族住在干砌石墙垒起的高台上，台下是平民的茅屋和牛栏；山丘建筑群里是王室围院，一道六米高、六十八米长的护墙，整面用深浅石块拼出棋盘格纹。商队把布图阿的黄金先运给穆斯林商人，后来又运给葡萄牙人，后者称这个王国为「黄金之母」。1502年，艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德第一次在文字中提到布图阿。15世纪90年代，托尔瓦支持昌加米雷一世反叛穆塔帕；1493年，国王向姆韦尼穆塔帕送上四千头牛和一批黄金，两国之间的战争一直打到1512年。

17世纪40年代，国王的兄弟娶了穆斯林商人家族姆文耶家的女子，借对方势力赶走国王；1644年，国王靠一位葡萄牙普拉佐领主的军队复位，卡米的山丘建筑群在战火中被焚。约1683年，昌加米雷·敦布攻占布图阿，废弃卡米，另以达纳蒙贝为他所建罗兹维帝国的都城。卡兰加口述传统把末代奇本杜莱说成拥有神力的王，只因敦布送来的妃子剪掉了他那束维系力量的角状发辫才被击败；到1696年，敦布已掌握旧王国的全部金场。

en:
Sofala lies on the low, mangrove-fringed shore of the Buzi estuary, the southernmost great emporium of the Swahili coast. Merchants from Mogadishu founded the post in the 10th century and for generations kept its gold a secret from their rivals in Kilwa. Dhows carried the metal up the Buzi and the Save from the markets of Manica and the mines behind Great Zimbabwe, and in the 1180s Sultan Suleiman Hassan of Kilwa brought the town into his empire. Sofala kept its own counsel all the same: its Swahili merchants paid tribute to the Mwenemutapa, whose land it formally was, while the Kilwa governor answered only for the resident Muslims. The city ran its own affairs, kept outposts as far south as Cape Correntes and across the channel in Madagascar, and was the dominant port south of Kilwa. In 1444 its sheikh ruled a rich and prickly city-state, though the old goldfields were already running down.

The first European known to reach it was Pêro da Covilhã, who slipped into the town disguised as an Arab trader in 1489 and sent Lisbon word of its gold. When Portuguese ships entered the harbour in 1502, the elderly sheikh Isuf was at odds with Kilwa, where the minister Emir Ibrahim had murdered the ruling sultan and seized the throne, so he took the newcomers as allies against the usurper. In 1505 Pêro de Anaia raised Fort São Caetano from stone shipped out from Portugal, the second Portuguese fortress on the East African coast, but malaria gutted the garrison, and in 1507 its captain moved the men and trade to healthier Mozambique Island. The roadstead, said once to hold a hundred vessels, let ships in only at high tide over a shifting sandbar; the goldfields had moved north, and Sena and Quelimane on the Zambezi drew off the traffic. Portuguese chroniclers meanwhile identified Sofala with the biblical Ophir, King Solomon's gold port, and tied its old rulers to the Queen of Sheba. The Buzi's shifting sands slowly swallowed the old town, which by 1821 was little more than a malarial outpost.
zh:
索法拉位于布济河口低洼、红树林环绕的海岸，是斯瓦希里沿岸最南端的大商埠。10世纪，摩加迪沙商人在此设立商站，此后几代人都对基尔瓦的竞争对手守着黄金的秘密。阿拉伯帆船经布济河与萨韦河，把马尼卡市集和津巴布韦腹地金矿的黄金运到此处；1180年代，基尔瓦苏丹苏莱曼·哈桑将此镇并入他的国家。索法拉照旧自行其是：斯瓦希里商人向此地名义上的君主穆韦内穆塔帕纳贡，基尔瓦派来的长官只管穆斯林居民。城邦自主处理事务，商栈远至南边的科连特斯角和海峡对岸的马达加斯加，是基尔瓦以南首屈一指的港口。1444年，当地谢赫统治着这座富庶而倔强的城邦，只是古老金矿的产出已在下滑。

已知最早抵达的欧洲人是佩罗·达·科维良，他在1489年乔装成阿拉伯商人混入城中，把黄金港的消息送回里斯本。1502年葡萄牙船驶入港口时，年迈的谢赫优素福正因基尔瓦之事恼怒：大臣埃米尔·易卜拉欣弑君篡位，优素福拒不承认，便把新来者当作对付篡位者的盟友。1505年，佩罗·德·阿纳亚用葡萄牙运来的石材建起圣卡耶塔诺堡，是葡萄牙人在东非海岸的第二座堡垒；但疟疾拖垮了驻军，1507年要塞指挥官把人员和贸易迁往更宜居住的莫桑比克岛。这片锚地据说曾容得下上百艘船，却横着一道移动的沙洲，船只只能趁涨潮进港；金矿产地已然北移，赞比西河上的塞纳和克利马内又分走了贸易。葡萄牙编年史家则把索法拉比附为《圣经》里的俄斐，即所罗门王的黄金港，又把它古代的统治者和示巴女王的传说扯在一起。布济河的流沙渐渐吞没老城，到1821年，这里只剩一个疟疾横行的小据点。

en:
Sena holds the chief crossing of the lower Zambezi, where dhows from the Indian Ocean met the land caravans carrying gold down from the Zimbabwe plateau. By the fifteenth century it was a Muslim Swahili bazaar on the northern edge of the Mutapa state: merchants from Angoche and the coast landed Indian cloth, beads and porcelain and bought gold and ivory under the protection of the Mwenemutapa, while Tonga farmers and fishermen worked the banks around the wharves. In 1444 the town lived by that protected trade, its landing place busy with Swahili craft.

After taking Sofala the Portuguese pushed up the Zambezi and in 1531 raised a fortified feira at Sena and another at Tete, supplanting the Muslim merchants. When the Jesuit Gonçalo da Silveira was strangled at the Mwenemutapa's court in 1561 on the urging of Muslim traders, his body thrown into the Musengezi river, a Portuguese expedition swept the Zambezi a few years later and ended the Swahili presence; Sena became a garrison town with a Dominican church. Francisco Barreto gathered his army there in 1571 for the march against the rebel Samungazi Tonga, came back empty-handed, and died on the Zambezi two years later. The river country kept fighting the newcomers: settlers fled to Sena during Kapararidze's anti-Portuguese rising of 1631–32, and the Tonga rose around it again in 1669–72. Sena later became the first seat of the captaincy of the Rivers of Sena, before the governor moved upriver to Tete; around the town stretched the prazo estates, whose Portuguese and Afro-Portuguese lords kept private armies of armed slaves and shipped ivory and gold down to the coast.
zh:
塞纳扼守赞比西河下游最重要的渡口，印度洋来的单桅帆船在此停泊，通往津巴布韦高原金矿区的陆路商队从这里出发。到15世纪，这里已是穆塔帕国家北缘的斯瓦希里穆斯林集市：安戈谢和沿海商人运入印度布匹、串珠和瓷器，在姆韦尼穆塔帕的庇护下收购黄金和象牙，通加农民和渔民在码头两岸劳作。1444年，这座城镇靠受庇护的贸易为生，河埠上斯瓦希里商船往来不断。

葡萄牙人夺取索法拉后溯赞比西河而上，1531年在塞纳和太特各设一处设防商站，取代了穆斯林商人。1561年，耶稣会士贡萨洛·达·西尔韦拉被穆斯林商人进谗，在姆韦尼穆塔帕宫廷遭人勒杀，遗体抛入河中；几年后葡萄牙讨伐队扫荡赞比西河，清除了斯瓦希里势力，塞纳成为驻有多明我会教堂和守军的要塞城镇。1571年，弗朗西斯科·巴雷托在此集结军队，进剿反叛的萨蒙加齐通加人，却无功而返，两年后病死在赞比西河上。沿河之地反抗不断：1631至1632年卡帕拉里泽反葡起事时，殖民者逃到塞纳，1669至1672年通加人又在城周起兵。塞纳后来成为塞纳河总督区的首个治所，之后总督迁往上游的太特；市镇周围是大片普拉佐庄园，葡裔与混血园主蓄有武装奴隶组成的私军，把象牙和黄金运往下游海岸。

en:
Massapa was the market country below the Mutapa Empire's gold-bearing northern plateau, on the road inland from the Zambezi. Caravans came upriver from Sena and Tete and then overland to its feira, swapping Indian cloth, beads and metalware for gold panned from the northern streams. There was no single rich town: the Mwenemutapa's power kept the roads safe, his provincial chiefs policed them, and every load paid duty at the king's market. In 1444 this was Shona country governed through those chiefs, long before any Portuguese captain held office in the interior.

The royal court drew the first missionary here. In 1561 the Jesuit Gonçalo da Silveira reached the zimbabwe of the Mwenemutapa Negomo, baptised him after the king dreamed of the Virgin Mary and then baptised hundreds of his court; Muslim traders and traditionalist nobles turned Negomo against him, and Silveira was strangled and thrown into the Musengezi River. From the 1580s the Portuguese made Massapa their leading inland fair, and its captain filled an old court office, the 'captain of the gates', counted among the king's 'great wives'. In 1629 Kapararidze's army was beaten at Massapa by a Portuguese force raised in Tete and Sena; the new king Mavhura accepted vassalage, the Captain of Masapa sat in his zimbabwe to be consulted on war and peace, and 1.28 kilograms of gold went to the Captain of Mozambique every three years. Prazo wars gnawed at the empire for the rest of the century. In 1693 Changamire Dombo's Rozvi army sacked the fairs, destroying Dambarare and its church first and then burning Massapa; only the fair in Manyika survived.
zh:
马萨帕是穆塔帕帝国北部产金高原脚下的商站之地，处在赞比西河通往内陆的大路上。商队从塞纳和太特溯河而上，再走旱路来到这座集市，用印度布匹、珠子和金属器换走北方溪流里淘出的黄金。这里并没有一座单独的富庶城镇：是姆韦尼穆塔帕的王权护着商路平安，各地酋长负责巡护，每批货物都在国王的市场上纳税。1444年，这里是由诸酋长直接管理的绍纳土地，葡萄牙商站队长进入内地还是很久以后的事。

第一个传教士是王宫本身引来的。1561年，耶稣会士贡萨洛·达·西尔韦拉来到姆韦尼穆塔帕内戈莫的都城；国王梦见圣母后接受洗礼，数百名廷臣也随之受洗。穆斯林商人和守旧贵族随即说动内戈莫反目，西尔韦拉被人勒杀，尸体扔进穆森盖济河。从16世纪80年代起，葡萄牙人把马萨帕经营成首要内陆集市，商站队长还充任王廷旧职「城门队长」，被算作国王的「大妻」之一。1629年，卡帕拉里泽的军队在马萨帕被太特和塞纳纠集的葡萄牙武装击败；新王马夫拉接受藩属地位，马萨帕队长驻在他的都城中，战和大事须与其商议，每三年还要向莫桑比克长官献上1.28公斤黄金。此后整个世纪，普拉佐的私战不断侵蚀帝国。1693年，昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维军队洗劫各商站，先毁丹巴雷雷及其教堂，接着放火烧掉马萨帕，只有马尼卡的商站留存。

en:
Shangwe was the Shona-speaking cattle and woodland country of the Mafungabusi Plateau, the high ground between the Zambezi lowlands and the Sanyati River, later called the Gokwe region. Miombo woodland covered the heights, feeding wild bees and elephant herds; its people gathered honey, hunted ivory and counted their wealth in cattle. Shona oral tradition makes Mutota, the first Mwenemutapa, an elephant hunter from this country, which puts the plateau early among the lands sending gold and ivory down to the Zambezi. In 1444 Shangwe was a north-eastern borderland of Butua, nearer the rising power of Mutapa than Khami, the stone capital of the Torwa kings.

No royal town stood here; villages, grazing grounds and hunting paths made up the country. In the 1690s Changamire Dombo, who had raised his Rozvi following with the Mwenemutapa's royal cattle herds, massacred Portuguese traders on the plateau and drove every Portuguese off it. A Rozvi band led by Chireya then overcame the Shangwe Confederacy on the Mafungabusi and settled a branch of the Changamire dynasty among the northern Shona. Portuguese goods could only move through Zumbo, a feira founded around 1720 on the Zambezi by the Luangwa mouth; African intermediaries carried them up into Rozvi lands, which no Portuguese might enter. The great drought of 1795-1800 and the succession wars after it loosened the Changamire's hold, leaving Shangwe a tributary frontier by 1821.
zh:
尚圭是马丰加布西高原上说绍纳语的牧地与林乡，这片高地夹在赞比西低地与萨尼亚蒂河之间，后来被称作戈奎地区。米翁博林地布满高地，林间有野蜂和象群；居民采蜜、猎取象牙，以牛群计算财富。绍纳口传传统把第一代姆韦尼穆塔帕穆托塔说成出身此地的猎象人，高原也因此很早成为向赞比西河输送黄金和象牙的地方之一。1444年时，尚圭是布图阿的东北边地，离兴起中的穆塔帕更近，离托尔瓦王廷所在的石城卡米更远。

这里没有王城，一地只有村落、牧场和猎道。17世纪90年代，昌加米雷·敦布借姆韦尼穆塔帕的王室牛群拉起罗兹维部众，在高原上屠杀葡萄牙商人，把他们尽数驱逐。奇雷亚率领的一支罗兹维人随即在马丰加布西攻灭尚圭联盟，昌加米雷王朝的一支就此定居在北绍纳人中间。葡萄牙货物只能经宗博进出：这座商站约1720年设在赞比西河上、卢安瓜河口附近，由非洲中间人运入罗兹维境内，葡萄牙人则不得入内。1795年至1800年的大旱和随后的继承战争削弱了昌加米雷的掌控，到1821年，尚圭只是一块纳贡边地。

en:
Far up the Zambezi, below the escarpment where the Luangwa comes in from the north, lies the land of Chikova, the remote north-western march of the Mutapa state. Tonga farmers kept the banks and hunters brought ivory down from the elephant country on both sides of the river; the hills behind Chikova were also said to hold silver. In 1444 the Mwenemutapa's authority ran thin so far upstream, and the country paid its tribute chiefly in tusks.

The silver rumours drew the Portuguese inland. In the mid-1570s Vasco Homem, marching on the Chikova mines after his campaign in Manyika, was cut down with almost all his men. At the end of the century Zimba raiders, mercenaries of the Maravi ruler Lundu, crossed the Zambezi and seized gold-bearing land until the armies of the Mwenemutapa Gatsi Rusere drove them out. Early in the eighteenth century the Portuguese founded a feira at Zumbo, the farthest market up the river: its traders bartered cloth and beads for ivory up the Luangwa and as far as Lake Bangweulu, and some settled across the water at Feira. In 1723 the Mwenemutapa moved his court down from the plateau into the valley, to Chikova. A rival's blockade of the feira was broken by a Rozvi army in 1772. In 1804 a chief called Mburuma sacked Zumbo and the feira stood abandoned for sixteen years, its trade ruined by drought and disorder.
zh:
赞比西河上游、卢安瓜河自北方汇入处下方，是奇科瓦之地，穆塔帕国家偏远的西北边陲。通加农民在两岸耕作，猎手从河两边的大象之乡运来象牙，奇科瓦后方的山里还传说出产白银。1444年，姆韦尼穆塔帕的权势溯河至此已经很弱，此地主要以象牙纳贡。

银矿的传闻把葡萄牙人引向内陆。16世纪70年代中期，瓦斯库·奥梅姆从马尼卡回师后进兵奇科瓦银矿，所部几乎被全歼。世纪末，马拉维君主伦杜麾下的津巴雇佣兵渡过赞比西河，攻占产金之地，最后被姆韦尼穆塔帕加齐·鲁塞雷的军队逐出。18世纪初，葡萄牙人在宗博设立商站，这是赞比西河上最远的集市：商人用布匹和串珠沿卢安瓜河深入，远至班韦乌卢湖换取象牙，还有人渡到对岸的费特定居。1723年，姆韦尼穆塔帕把王庭从高原迁入河谷，移驻奇科瓦。1772年，一支罗兹维军队击破了争位者对商站的封锁。1804年，酋长姆布鲁马洗劫宗博，商站废弃了十六年，旱灾和动乱使贸易凋敝。

en:
Tete lies on the right bank of the Zambezi, about halfway between the Shona goldfields and the sea; its Nyungwe name means 'reed', after the beds along the shore. In the fifteenth century the riverside was a feira, a trading ground inside the widening power of the Mwenemutapa. Swahili merchants from Angoche and the coast met Tonga fishermen, porters and canoemen there, sending ivory and gold from the plateau downstream to Sena and Quelimane and carrying Indian cloth and beads back upstream. In 1444 the country answered to Mutapa, and the river traffic was in African and Swahili hands.

News of the Mwenemutapa's gold drew the Portuguese up the Zambezi, and they built a settlement at Tete in 1531. When the Jesuit Goncalo da Silveira was killed at the Mutapa court in 1561, a thousand-man expedition of 1568 broke the Swahili hold on the feira. The square Fort Sao Tiago Maior, raised in 1575 with round bastions at its corners and restored in 1686, became the military anchor of the station. By the mid-seventeenth century Tete was a market for ivory and gold ringed by prazos, large leased estates whose Portuguese and Afro-Portuguese owners kept private armies of slaves and fought one another, the Mutapa court and the river chiefs for the Zambezi traffic. The remote garrison even reached print in Europe: the Marquis de Sade set an episode of his novel Aline et Valcour at the Fort of Tete.
zh:
太特位于赞比西右岸，大致处在绍纳金矿区与外海之间；尼扬圭语里其名意为「芦苇」，得名于河岸成片的芦苇荡。15世纪时，这片河畔是一处商站，处在姆韦尼·马塔帕不断扩张的势力范围内。来自安戈谢和沿海的斯瓦希里商人在此与通加渔民、挑夫和船夫交易，把高原的象牙和黄金顺流送往塞纳和克利马内，再把印度布匹和珠子运入上游。1444年时，这一带受穆塔帕统辖，赞比西商路掌握在非洲人和斯瓦希里人手中。

姆韦尼·马塔帕坐拥黄金的消息把葡萄牙人引上赞比西河，他们于1531年在太特建起定居点。1561年耶稣会士贡萨洛·达·西尔韦拉在穆塔帕宫廷被杀，1568年一支千人远征军摧毁了斯瓦希里人在商站的势力。1575年修筑、1686年修缮的方形圣雅各·马约尔要塞四角设圆形棱堡，是这座据点的军事支柱。到17世纪中叶，太特已是象牙和黄金的集散地，周围遍布普拉佐，即大片租佃地产；其葡萄牙人和葡非混血主人豢养奴隶组成私军，为争夺赞比西商路，彼此、对穆塔帕宫廷和沿河酋长不断攻战。这座偏远要塞还进了欧洲人的书本：萨德侯爵在一部小说里写到过太特要塞。

en:
Quelimane began as a Swahili Muslim trading town on the Rio dos Bons Sinais, a short river that reaches the Indian Ocean through the Zambezi delta. Dhows from Kilwa and Sofala unloaded cloth and beads at its anchorage and took on ivory brought upriver from Makua and Maravi lands, and the river mouth let ocean-going ships trade with canoes without crossing the surf. It was already one of the oldest Muslim towns on this stretch of coast when Vasco da Gama reached it in 1498 on his first voyage to India; he took its safe anchorage as a sign that he was on the right course, and named the river the River of Good Signs. One tradition explains the town's own name from the answer field hands gave his men when asked what the place was called: kuliamani, 'we are cultivating'. In 1444, under Sofala's sway, it was a small Muslim port living chiefly on ivory.

Permanent Portuguese occupation is recorded only from 1544. In 1631 Muzura's Maravi army attacked Quelimane, the only Portuguese town north of the Zambezi; its defenders held out, and a Portuguese counter-attack drove the Maravi out in 1632, after which the Makua chiefs around the port sought Portuguese protection. During the eighteenth century Quelimane became a major market for ivory and slaves brought from the Zambezi hinterland. An earth-and-brushwood fort had been begun by 1740 to cover the anchorage; the settlement was raised to a town in 1763 and the fort completed the next year, but fifteen years later it lay in ruins and the governor of Mozambique ordered a new work built near the river mouth.
zh:
克利马内起初是斯瓦希里穆斯林商人在好兆头河（Rio dos Bons Sinais）畔建立的贸易城镇，小河穿过赞比西三角洲注入印度洋。来自基尔瓦和索法拉的单桅商船在锚地卸下布匹和珠子，装上马库阿、马拉维地方顺河运来的象牙；河口使远洋船不必冲过浪涌，就能与独木舟交易。1498年瓦斯科·达·伽马首次远航印度抵达此处时，它已是这段海岸上最古老的穆斯林城镇之一；达·伽马把安稳的锚地视为航向正确的征兆，河便得名好兆头河。关于城名也有个说法：他的手下问田里的农夫此地何名，对方以为在问自己在做什么，答以「库利亚马尼」，意为「我们在耕种」。1444年时，此城在索法拉势力之下，是一座主要靠象牙为生的小港。

葡萄牙人的永久占据据记载迟至1544年才开始。1631年，穆祖拉的马拉维军队进攻克利马内，当时这是赞比西河以北唯一的葡萄牙城镇；守军守住城池，葡萄牙人在1632年反攻，将马拉维人逐出，港口周围的马库阿酋长随后也请求葡萄牙庇护。18世纪里，克利马内成为赞比西腹地运来的象牙和奴隶的大市场。1740年，一座土木要塞已经动工，用以拱卫锚地；聚落于1763年升为镇，要塞次年完工。仅仅十五年后要塞已成废墟，莫桑比克总督只得下令在河口附近另筑新垒。

en:
Menabe is the red laterite plain of western Madagascar between the Mangoky and Tsiribihina rivers; its name means 'great red'. Morondava, the chief anchorage on the surf-beaten shore, sits at a river mouth whose Malagasy name means 'long coast'. Its people descend from Austronesian seafarers who settled the island between the fifth and ninth centuries and Bantu farmers who crossed from the mainland in the ninth. In 1444 fishermen, rice-growers and cattle-herders lived in small riverside villages and sold provisions, cattle and slaves to Swahili and Arab dhows. No king ruled the whole plain, but the Maroserana lords of Fiherenana to the south, 'those who own many ports', were pushing north along the coast.

On 10 August 1500 the Portuguese captain Diogo Dias, blown off course on the voyage to India, became the first European to sight Madagascar, and Dutch, English and Portuguese ships began calling on the western shore. The slave trade gave the Maroserana firearms, and the firearms gave them a kingdom. In the first half of the seventeenth century Andriamisara built a chiefdom in the Fiherenana valley, and his son Andriandahifotsy, 'the White Prince', carried his arms north to the Manambolo and set his capital at Bengy in the Mangoky valley. His sons pushed on to found Boina near Mahajanga, which became the greatest slave port on the island. By the early eighteenth century Menabe was the strongest power in Madagascar; its raiders swept the coasts and crossed to the Comoro Islands for captives, and the Sakalava held the island's slave trade in their hands until the end of the century. In 1719 the Dutch ship Barneveld found the paralytic king Ranaimo ruling at Andakabe, the future Morondava. Menabe's power peaked between 1730 and 1760 under Andrianinevenarivo; in 1820 and 1821 the armies of Radama I of the Merina ravaged the plain twice.
zh:
梅纳贝是马达加斯加西部的红色砖红壤平原，夹在曼戈基河与齐里比希纳河之间，其名意为「大红」。这段拍浪海岸上的主要停泊地穆龙达瓦位于一处河口，地名在马尔加什语中意为「长岸」。当地人是5至9世纪定居该岛的南岛航海者与9世纪自非洲大陆渡来的班图农民之后。1444年，渔民、稻农和牧牛人住在沿河小村，向斯瓦希里和阿拉伯独桅帆船出售补给、牛只和奴隶。当时还没有统御整个平原的君主，但南方菲赫雷纳纳的马罗塞拉尼亚领主，意为「拥有众多港口者」，正沿海岸向北扩张。

1500年8月10日，葡萄牙船长迪奥戈·迪亚斯在前往印度途中被风暴吹离航线，成为第一个望见马达加斯加的欧洲人，荷兰、英国和葡萄牙船只此后开始停靠西海岸。奴隶贸易给马罗塞拉尼亚人带来火枪，火枪又为他们打出一个王国。17世纪上半叶，安德里亚米萨拉在菲赫雷纳纳河谷建立酋长势力；其子安德里安达希福齐（「白王子」）挥师北上直抵马南博洛河，定都曼戈基河谷的本吉。他的儿子们继续北进，在马哈赞加附近另建布伊纳王国，马哈赞加后来成为全岛最大的奴隶港。到18世纪初，梅纳贝已是马达加斯加最强的政权，掳掠者横扫沿海，还渡海远征科摩罗群岛抓捕人口；直到该世纪末，全岛奴隶贸易都掌握在萨卡拉瓦人手中。1719年荷兰商船巴内维尔德号抵达时，瘫痪的国王拉奈莫正在日后穆龙达瓦的前身安达卡贝主政。梅纳贝的国势在1730年至1760年安德里亚尼内韦纳里沃在位时达到顶点；1820年和1821年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世的军队两度蹂躏这片平原。

en:
The coast between Mahajamba Bay and the Manambolo River is a flat shore of mangrove creeks, fishing villages and dry savanna. In 1444 the clans later called Sakalava herded zebu inland and worked the shallows, with no prince over them; Muslim merchants from the older trading towns to the north beached their dhows here and bartered beads, cloth and metalware for cattle, tortoiseshell and rice. This land was Ambongo, a stretch of the sea road between the Muslim ports beyond Mahajamba Bay and the Menabe country only taking shape far to the south, around Morondava.

The Sakalava kingdoms grew on the slave trade: their chiefs sold cattle and captives to Arab and Swahili merchants for muskets no neighbour could match. About 1685 Andriamandisoarivo, a son of the Menabe king Andriandahifotsy, was driven out by his brother and marched his followers north through Ambongo, going on to conquer the Muslim Antalaotra ports of the north-west and found the kingdom of Iboina. Ambongo became a march between Menabe and his new monarchy, sometimes counted as Boina's southern province, more often a patchwork of small chiefdoms under their own lords; Besalampy became the chiefs' seat and Maintirano their port, where cattle and captives were sold into the Indian Ocean trade. In 1820 and 1821 the British-trained armies of Radama I of Imerina marched against Menabe, but Ambongo never submitted to Antananarivo, and its scattered valleys still answered to their own Sakalava lords.
zh:
马哈詹巴湾与马南布卢河之间，是一道地势平坦的海岸，红树林溪湾、渔村和干旱草原相间。1444年，后来被称作萨卡拉瓦人的诸氏族在内陆牧放瘤牛、在浅海谋生，不奉任何君长；来自北方古老商埠的穆斯林商人把独桅帆船拖上这里的滩头，用珠子、布匹和金属器皿换取牛只、玳瑁和稻米。这片土地叫安邦戈，是马哈詹巴湾以远的穆斯林港埠与梅纳贝之地之间的一段海路，那时梅纳贝还在遥远南边的穆龙达瓦一带成形。

萨卡拉瓦诸王国靠奴隶贸易起家：诸酋长把牛只和俘虏卖给阿拉伯和斯瓦希里商人，换来四邻都没有的火枪。约1685年，梅纳贝国王安德里安达希富齐之子安德里亚曼迪苏阿里武被兄长逐出国境，率部众北上，穿过安邦戈，去征服西北的穆斯林安塔劳特拉港埠、建立伊博伊纳王国。安邦戈就此成了梅纳贝与他的新王国之间的边地，时而被算作伊博伊纳的南境，更多时候则是林立的小酋长国，各有君长：贝萨兰皮成为首领们的居城，迈因蒂拉努是他们的港口，牛只和俘虏在那里被卖入印度洋贸易。1820年和1821年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世由英军训练的军队两度南征梅纳贝，安邦戈却从未向塔那那利佛称臣，分散在条条山谷里的居民仍听命于自己的萨卡拉瓦领主。

en:
The Island of Mozambique is a coral isle some three kilometres long, lying about five kilometres off the mainland in Mossuril Bay, with the open Mozambique Channel beyond it. By the fourteenth century a Swahili stone town stood on its northern end, founded, by local tradition, by settlers from Kilwa, and its sheikhs married into the ruling houses of Angoche and Quelimane. Dhows loaded there with gold from the Zambezi fairs and the lands of the Mwenemutapa, ivory from the Makua country and ambergris, then made sail for Kilwa, Gujarat and Arabia. In 1444 the town was the northern anchor of Kilwa's chain of Muslim cities, and its own people called it Muipiti.

Vasco da Gama dropped anchor off the island in March 1498 on his first voyage to India and dealt with its ruler, Sultan Mussa Bin Bique; the island took its name from him, and in time the whole mainland country did too. The Portuguese seized the island in 1507 and made it the chief port and naval station of the Carreira da India, the yearly fleets sailing to and from Goa, which watered and repaired here. They raised the Chapel of Nossa Senhora de Baluarte in 1522, held to be the oldest European building in the Southern Hemisphere, and late in the century built Fort São Sebastião on the island's tip, the strongest Portuguese fortress on the Swahili coast. Dutch East India Company fleets attacked it twice, in 1607 and 1608, the first siege lasting six months, and the garrison under Dom Estêvão de Ataíde beat them off both times. From 1570 the island was the capital of Portuguese East Africa and a missionary centre from which priests went into the Zambezi interior.

In the eighteenth century the island dealt more and more in people. Dhows and caravans out of the Makua interior brought captives by the thousand, with ivory and gold, for the Mascarene sugar islands and for Brazil, and Mozambique became one of the busiest slave markets on the east African coast. The caravans were still arriving in 1821.
zh:
莫桑比克岛是一座长约三公里的珊瑚岛，坐落在莫苏里尔湾中，距大陆约五公里，岛外便是开阔的莫桑比克海峡。14世纪时，岛的北端已立着一座斯瓦希里石城；据当地传说，建城者是来自基尔瓦的移民，岛上的谢赫与安戈谢、克利马内的统治家族联姻。来自赞比西集市和姆韦尼·马塔帕故地的黄金、马库阿地方的象牙和龙涎香在此装上独桅船，扬帆驶往基尔瓦、古吉拉特和阿拉伯。1444年，这座城镇是基尔瓦穆斯林城市链最北端的一环，岛上本地人称之为穆伊皮蒂。

1498年3月，瓦斯科·达·伽马首次远航印度，在岛外下锚，与岛上的苏丹穆萨·本·比克打交道；岛名便来自这位苏丹，后来整片大陆上的国家也沿用了这个名字。葡萄牙人1507年夺取该岛，把它建成「印度航路」上的首要港口和海军站，往返果阿的年度船队都在此补水修船。1522年，巴拉尔特圣母礼拜堂落成，被视为南半球最古老的欧洲建筑；该世纪后期，岛端又筑起圣塞巴斯蒂昂堡，是斯瓦希里海岸上最坚固的葡萄牙要塞。荷兰东印度公司舰队两度来攻，1607年一围六个月，1608年再攻，唐·埃斯特旺·德·阿塔伊德率领的守军两次都将其击退。1570年起，莫桑比克岛成为葡属东非的首府，也是一座传教中心，神父们从这里进入赞比西内陆。

18世纪，岛上越来越多地做起人口买卖。独桅船和来自马库阿内陆的商队把数以千计的俘虏连同象牙、黄金一起运来，卖往马斯克林蔗糖群岛和巴西，莫桑比克成了东非海岸最繁忙的奴隶市场之一。1821年，贩奴商队仍在源源上岛。

en:
Kilwa Kisiwani, a low coral island a short sail from the Rufiji shore, holds the greatest of the Swahili stonetowns. The Kilwa Chronicle tells how Ali ibn al-Hassan, a Persian prince of Shiraz whose mother was, by that account, an Abyssinian slave, bought the island from its mainland king in the tenth century for as much cloth as would ring it, then cut the tidal causeway to the mainland. About 1190 his successors seized Sofala, the southern emporium through which the gold of Great Zimbabwe reached the sea, and gold made the city: the sultans minted their own coinage for five hundred years, and their coins have turned up in the ruins of Great Zimbabwe. Early in the fourteenth century Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman built the cliff-top palace of Husuni Kubwa with its octagonal bathing pool, and enlarged the Great Mosque; Ibn Battuta, visiting in 1331, called Kilwa one of the world's most beautiful cities. In 1444, under the Mahdali dynasty, the sultan still claimed lordship over the coast from Mombasa to Sofala, and Kilwa stood at the height of its wealth.

Vasco da Gama's ships passed Kilwa in 1498, and on 24 July 1505 Francisco de Almeida stormed the town, gave it over to plunder and built Fort Santiago before sailing on to Mombasa. A revolt of Arab mercenaries drove the Portuguese out in 1512, and the old sultanate broke into rival cities. In 1587 the Zimba, fresh from taking Sena and Tete on the Zambezi, stormed Kilwa and killed some 3,000 of its people; the Portuguese retook the island before the century ended, but it never recovered its place in the gold trade. After Mombasa's Fort Jesus fell to Oman in 1698 Kilwa passed to the Yarubi imams, whose governors the townsmen repeatedly expelled; for much of the eighteenth century an independent Kilwa sold slaves and ivory to French ships from the Mascarenes. In 1785 the Bu'Saidi sultan of Oman garrisoned the Gereza, the coral fort whose Swahili name means 'prison', built to hold captives for the slave ships; the gold age was over, and the island lived on the traffic in people.
zh:
基尔瓦基西瓦尼是一座低矮的珊瑚岛，离鲁菲吉河口的海岸只有一水之遥，斯瓦希里诸石城中最宏大的一座就坐落在这里。《基尔瓦编年史》讲述，10世纪时，设拉子的波斯王公阿里·伊本·哈桑（书中说他的母亲是一名阿比西尼亚女奴）向大陆首领买下此岛，代价是足以绕岛一周的布匹，随后凿断了退潮时连接大陆的堤道。约1190年，他的继承者夺取索法拉这座大津巴布韦黄金出海的南方商埠，黄金成就了这座城：苏丹们自行铸币达五百年，他们铸出的钱币在大津巴布韦遗址也有出土。14世纪初，苏丹哈桑·伊本·苏莱曼在崖顶建起胡苏尼库布瓦宫，宫中带有八角浴池，并扩建了大清真寺；1331年到访的伊本·白图泰称基尔瓦是世界上最美的城市之一。1444年，在马赫达利王朝治下，基尔瓦苏丹仍对从蒙巴萨到索法拉的海岸拥有宗主权，城市的富庶正值顶峰。

瓦斯科·达伽马的船队1498年驶过基尔瓦海面，1505年7月24日，弗朗西斯科·德·阿尔梅达攻陷城市，纵兵大掠，又筑起圣地亚哥堡，随后驶往蒙巴萨。1512年阿拉伯雇佣兵起义赶走葡萄牙人，旧日苏丹国分裂为彼此争战的诸城。1587年，刚拿下赞比西河上塞纳和太特的津巴人攻破基尔瓦，杀死约三千居民；葡萄牙人在16世纪结束前重新占据该岛，但它再没能找回在黄金贸易中的位置。1698年蒙巴萨耶稣堡落入阿曼之手后，基尔瓦转入亚鲁卜伊玛目治下，居民屡次驱逐其任命的总督；18世纪的大部分时间里，一个独立的基尔瓦把奴隶和象牙卖给来自马斯克林群岛的法国船。1785年，阿曼的布·赛义德苏丹在格雷扎堡驻军；这座珊瑚堡的斯瓦希里名字意为「监狱」，为关押等候贩奴船的俘虏而建。黄金时代已经结束，全岛靠人口贸易维持。

en:
Mzizima, 'the town of plenty', was a string of fishing and farming villages on a deep, sheltered harbour, the kind of bay where a ship could ride out any monsoon. The anchorage saw little trade in the fifteenth century; the dhows plied between the stone towns of Kilwa and Mombasa, and in 1444 the village elders answered, loosely, to the sultan of Kilwa.

Portuguese fleets swept the coast and sacked Kilwa in 1505, the old order dissolved, and Omani Arabs took the shore in their turn. Mzizima stayed a fishing village. Zaramo oral tradition tells how, early in the nineteenth century, Kamba raiders from the north pressed the Shomvi clans here, who called in Pazi, a warrior from the hinterland; he drove the raiders off and asked for salt, cloth and luxuries as his fee. When the Shomvi could not pay, they settled him and his kin among them against an annual tribute, and the people who grew from that following took the name Zaramo. By 1821 Mzizima was still no more than a fishing village.
zh:
姆齐齐马意为「丰饶之镇」，是一处深水避风良港边上散布的渔村和农庄，这样的海湾任凭多大的季风都能泊船。15世纪时这座锚地没什么生意，单桅帆船往来的是基尔瓦、蒙巴萨那些石头城；1444年，村里的长者松散地听命于基尔瓦苏丹。

葡萄牙舰队扫荡海岸，于1505年洗劫基尔瓦，旧秩序随之瓦解，海岸转入阿曼阿拉伯人之手，姆齐齐马却始终是个渔村。扎拉莫人的口传故事说，19世纪初，北方的坎巴袭掠者进逼这里的绍姆维氏族，后者从内陆请来武士帕齐；他击退袭掠者，索要食盐、布匹和珍货作为酬劳。绍姆维人拿不出来，便把他和他的亲族安置在自己人中间，每年纳贡，由这支追随者繁衍成的人群便称扎拉莫人。到1821年，姆齐齐马仍不过是一座渔村。

en:
Lindi is one of the older Swahili towns of this coast, settled in the eleventh century at the mouth of the Lukuledi, where a deep inlet gives safe anchorage to dhows; its original Swahili name was never written down. In 1444 it was one of the lesser Muslim partners in Kilwa's loose confederation of trading cities, and its people lived by fishing and farming while its boats carried ivory and provisions from the Mwera hinterland into the monsoon trade that the island of Kilwa commanded.

Lindi's fortunes followed those of its overlord. In July 1505 a Portuguese fleet stormed Kilwa and burned it, and the smaller ports on Lindi Bay lost the power that had sheltered them and much of their trade. In 1588 warbands the Portuguese called Zimba, moving up from the Zambezi, sacked Kilwa and swept on along this shore; the friar João dos Santos later wrote that they killed and ate three thousand people taken in the city, a claim modern historians put down as legend. In the seventeenth century Omani Arabs made themselves masters of the coast, and they gave the town its present name, Lindi, 'the deep channel'. Under their rule its harbour became a shipping point for ivory gathered in the interior and for growing numbers of slaves, carried north to Zanzibar and the markets of Arabia.
zh:
林迪是这片海岸上较古老的斯瓦希里城镇之一，11世纪建于卢库莱迪河口，一道深水海湾正好为独桅帆船提供锚地；它最初的斯瓦希里名字没有被记下来。1444年时，它是基尔瓦松散商业城邦联盟中较小的穆斯林成员，居民以捕鱼和耕种为生，海船把姆韦拉内陆的象牙和食粮运进基尔瓦岛掌控的季风商路。

林迪的命运随宗主基尔瓦沉浮。1505年7月，葡萄牙舰队攻陷并焚毁基尔瓦，林迪湾一带的小港失去庇护，贸易大减。1588年，被葡萄牙人称作津巴人的武装从赞比西方向北上，洗劫基尔瓦后横扫这段海岸；修士若昂·多斯桑托斯后来写道，他们在基尔瓦杀死并吃掉了三千人，现代史家把这个说法归为传闻。17世纪里，阿曼阿拉伯人成为海岸的主人，正是他们把此城改名林迪，意为「深水航道」。在他们治下，这座港湾成了输出内陆象牙的口岸，还有越来越多的奴隶，一并北运桑给巴尔和阿拉伯市场。

en:
The anchorage that became Bagamoyo lies on the Zanzibar Channel, within sight of the island. Five kilometres to the south, Kaole was settled in the eighth century as a trading town whose coral-stone ruins, two mosques and about thirty tombs among them, date from the thirteenth to the sixteenth centuries. Stone pillars mark some of the graves, said by local tradition to hold the diwanis, the local rulers descended from the sheikh Ali Muhamad al-Hatim al-Barawi; Chinese porcelain found among the ruins shows what the dhows brought back when they carried off Kaole's ivory, ebony, sandalwood and mangrove poles. By the fifteenth century Kaole was fading, and around 1444 Bagamoyo itself was a small satellite village of Zaramo and Swahili fishermen and farmers, trading fish, salt and gum within Kilwa's loose maritime confederacy.

Kaole's stone town fell to ruin in the sixteenth century, after Portuguese fleets broke the old Swahili order, but the anchorage lived on. About the middle of the eighteenth century Shomvi clans from the Malindi shore settled here, by their own oral account; Omani kinsmen of the sheikh Shamvi la Magimba followed and taxed the local trade and the salt of Nunge. The village became a caravan halt and took the name Bagamoyo, 'lay down your heart', a porter's phrase for setting down his load at the sea. From the 1810s, as Oman made Zanzibar the emporium of the western Indian Ocean, Nyamwezi caravans from as far as Lake Tanganyika ended months of marching here with ivory and gum copal, shouldering loads that ran to seventy pounds, and took back Indian cloth, guns and copper wire. By 1821 Bagamoyo was the rising market of the Mrima coast.
zh:
巴加莫约的锚地在桑给巴尔海峡上，与海岛遥遥相望。以南五公里的考莱8世纪已是一座商镇，其珊瑚石遗址可追溯至13至16世纪，存有两座清真寺和约三十座墓葬，一些墓前立着石柱；当地人相传，墓中长眠着迪瓦尼，即谢赫阿里·穆罕默德·哈提姆·巴拉维的后裔、世代在此的统治者。遗址里出土过中国瓷器，可见当年单桅帆船运走象牙、乌木、檀香和红树桩时，带回来的是什么。到15世纪考莱渐衰，1444年前后，巴加莫约本身只是依附它的一座小村，扎拉莫人和斯瓦希里人在此捕鱼、制盐、采胶，在基尔瓦主导的松散海上联盟里做些小本买卖。

16世纪葡萄牙舰队击碎旧有的斯瓦希里秩序，考莱石城沦为废墟，但这座锚地延续了下来。18世纪中叶，按绍姆维人自己的口述，他们从北方的马林迪海岸南迁至此；谢赫沙姆维·拉·马金巴的阿曼亲族随后而来，向当地贸易和嫩盖出产的食盐抽税。村子成了商队驿站，得名巴加莫约，意为「放下你的心」，是脚夫走到海边卸下重担时的话。1810年代起，随着阿曼把桑给巴尔经营成西印度洋的商业中心，远自坦噶尼喀湖的尼亚姆韦齐商队走几个月到这里歇脚，驮来象牙和柯巴脂，担子重达七十磅，再换走印度布匹、火枪和铜丝。到1821年，巴加莫约已是姆里马海岸上升的商埠。

en:
The coast below Mombasa breaks into coral reefs and mangrove creeks and runs south to the bay of Tanga. By 1444 its chief town was Vumba Kuu, a Swahili stone town facing Wasini Island at the southern limit of the world of coral mosques and Indian Ocean dhows. Its merchants shipped ivory brought down from the interior and took back Indian cloth, glass beads and Persian and Chinese ceramics, and archaeology dates the town to the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries. Further south stood Tongoni, a Swahili town of the fifteenth century, where a Friday mosque and some forty stone tombs still looked over Mtangata Bay. Rival Shirazi towns competed around them for the trade, while Digo clans farmed the ridges behind the coast and kept to the old spirits. Vumba Kuu had its own diwan and stood on the southern edge of Mombasa's sphere.

Vasco da Gama passed this coast in April 1498 and anchored off Tongoni; he found the local oranges better than any in Portugal and came back the following year for a fifteen-day stay. Portuguese fleets soon made the towns submit to the customs house at Mombasa, though Tanga itself stayed no more than a small trading post. Early in the seventeenth century the Vumba, led by Mwana Kyambi Ivoo with their Digo allies, made war on the Shirazi towns and overran them one by one; their last capital, Tumbe, fell around 1640 and was left a ruin. When Omani armies drove the Portuguese out of Mombasa at the end of the century, the Vumba diwanate lived on though Vumba Kuu was already abandoned, its lords still enthroned beside the graves of their ancestors. From the 1750s the caves at Shimoni held captives for the coastal slave trade, and the Digo grew rich carrying ivory and slaves between shore and interior. By 1821 the whole coast answered to Muscat and the rising power of Zanzibar.
zh:
蒙巴萨以南的海岸散成一片珊瑚礁和红树林水道，一直延伸到坦噶湾。1444年时，这一带的首镇是与瓦西尼岛隔海相望的斯瓦希里石城温巴库（Vumba Kuu），正处在珊瑚清真寺与印度洋独桅帆船世界的南端。城中商人把内陆运来的象牙装船，换回印度布匹、玻璃珠以及波斯和中国的瓷器，考古测定城址的年代在14至15世纪。更南面还有一座繁盛于15世纪的斯瓦希里商镇，留下一座星期五清真寺和约四十座石墓，俯临海湾。互为对手的设拉子城镇在四周争夺商利，身后沿海的丘陵山脊由迪戈人耕作，他们仍敬奉旧神。温巴库由自己的迪万治理，处在蒙巴萨势力范围的南缘。

1498年4月，达·伽马驶过这片海岸，曾在这座商镇外停泊；他说当地的橙子比葡萄牙的还好，次年又来停留了十五天。不久葡萄牙舰队迫使诸城镇臣服，听命于设在蒙巴萨的海关，坦噶本身则始终只是一个小贸易站。17世纪初，温巴人在姆瓦纳·坎比·伊沃率领下，与盟友迪戈人一同对设拉子人开战，把他们的城镇逐一攻陷；最后的都城通贝约于1640年前后陷落，沦为废墟。该世纪末阿曼军队把葡萄牙人逐出蒙巴萨时，温巴库城虽已荒废，温巴迪万政权仍延续下来，首领照旧在先祖墓旁即位。1750年代起，希莫尼的洞穴用来关押奴隶贸易中的俘虏，迪戈人靠在海岸与内陆之间转运象牙和奴隶致富。到1821年，整条海岸都已臣服于马斯喀特和崛起的桑给巴尔。

en:
Zanzibar, an Arab name meaning 'coast of the blacks', is the green island of Unguja, set a day's sail off the Swahili shore behind a fine natural harbour. Bantu fishermen and farmers had settled it by the middle of the first millennium, and by the tenth century Unguja Ukuu and Kizimkazi in the south and Tumbatu in the north numbered among the Swahili exchange points where Gulf and Indian merchants gave Indian cloth for gold, ivory and ambergris. Patrician houses rose in coral stone, and the mosque at Kizimkazi carries a kufic inscription dating it to 1107, one of the oldest Islamic buildings on the coast. In 1444 Zanzibar was one of many autonomous Muslim city-states, its ruler among those who acknowledged the loose overlordship of Kilwa, then at its zenith.

Vasco da Gama called at Zanzibar in 1498, and in 1503 or 1504 Captain Rui Lourenço Ravasco extracted tribute from its sultan, opening nearly two centuries of loose Portuguese rule that never ran much beyond a trade depot: when the English ship Edward Bonaventure watered here in 1591 it found neither fort nor garrison, and the local 'king', predecessor of the Mwinyi Mkuu of Dunga, still managed the island's affairs. Strangled trade led the Swahili towns to call in Oman, and after the fall of Mombasa's Fort Jesus in 1698 Zanzibar passed to the Yarubi imams. Arab merchants settled the harbour quarter of Stone Town, while the Mwinyi Mkuu went on ruling the villages from Dunga, and a revolt against Omani rule was put down in 1784. Early in the nineteenth century, under the Bu'Saidi sultans, Arab planters laid out the first clove shambas and the harbour trade in slaves and ivory swelled year by year; by 1821 Stone Town was already a busy Omani emporium built on cloves, ivory and slaves.
zh:
桑给巴尔的阿拉伯语名称意为「黑人海岸」，它就是绿意盎然的温古贾岛，隔海与斯瓦希里海岸相望，岛后藏着一座优良的天然港湾。班图渔民和农民在一千纪中叶已在此定居，到10世纪，岛南的温古贾乌库、基济姆卡济和岛北的通巴图都已跻身斯瓦希里人的贸易据点，波斯湾和印度商人用印度布匹换取黄金、象牙和龙涎香。望族的住宅以珊瑚石砌成，基济姆卡济的清真寺存有库法体铭文，纪年为1107年，是沿海最古老的伊斯兰建筑之一。1444年，桑给巴尔是众多自治的穆斯林城邦之一，在基尔瓦权势鼎盛之时，它的统治者也承认其松散的宗主权。

瓦斯科·达伽马1498年到访桑给巴尔，1503或1504年，鲁伊·洛伦索·拉瓦斯科船长向岛上苏丹强索贡赋，开启了葡萄牙人近两百年的松散统治，其统治范围几乎不超过一处商馆：1591年英国船「爱德华·博纳文彻」号在此补给淡水时，发现岛上既无堡垒也无守军，本地首领（即后来栋加的姆维尼·姆库）仍在处理岛务。贸易受压的斯瓦希里诸城请来阿曼人，1698年蒙巴萨耶稣堡陷落后，桑给巴尔转入阿曼亚鲁卜伊玛目治下。阿拉伯商人在石头城的港区定居，姆维尼·姆库则继续在栋加统治各村落，1784年一场反抗阿曼统治的起义遭到镇压。19世纪初，在布·赛义德王朝治下，阿拉伯种植园主开辟了最早的丁香园，港中奴隶与象牙的贸易逐年膨胀；到1821年，石头城已是一座建立在丁香、象牙和奴隶之上的繁忙阿曼商埠。

en:
Mombasa fills a coral island beside a sheltered harbour on the Indian Ocean. Local lineages trace the town to Mwana Mkisi, a queen of the pre-Islamic age who founded Kongowea, and to Shehe Mvita, who built its first stone mosque. The Mnara mosque on the island was raised around 1300, and Ibn Battuta stopped for one night in the fourteenth century and found Shafi'i Muslims and expertly built wooden mosques. Within Kilwa's orbit, the town shipped ivory, gold, millet, sesame and coconuts to the Red Sea, Arabia and India, and its harbour held vessels from Sofala, Cambay, Malindi and Zanzibar. In 1444 its old Mvita families and its ocean trade made it the leading rival of nearby Malindi.

Mombasa fought the Portuguese harder than any other Swahili town. Vasco da Gama met a chilly reception in 1498, the town was sacked in 1500, and Portuguese fleets returned in 1505 and again in 1528, when Nuno da Cunha destroyed much of it. The Ottoman captain Ali Bey seized it in 1585, and within a few years Zimba raiders overran the island and slaughtered its Muslim population before the Segeju stopped them at Malindi. The Portuguese came back in 1589 and built Fort Jesus above the old harbour between 1593 and 1596. The Italian architect Giovanni Battista Cairati designed a square Renaissance fortress with four corner bulwarks, shaped like a man seen from the air, and Swahili masons carried out the work. In 1631 the ruler Yusuf ibn al-Hasan, brought up by the Portuguese as Dom Jeronimo, killed the garrison and took to the sea as a pirate; a Portuguese army retook the fort the next year.

In 1696 Saif bin Sultan of Oman laid siege to Fort Jesus, and his army took it in December 1698 after nearly three years of blockade. Portugal won the fort back briefly in 1728 and 1729, but from the 1740s the Mazrui governors held both town and fort on their own account and refused rule from Oman. Ivory, provisions for passing ships and the traffic in enslaved people fed the island, and in 1821 Abdallah ibn Ahmad al-Mazru'i still governed from Mombasa.
zh:
蒙巴萨位于印度洋上一座珊瑚岛，坐拥一处遮蔽良港。当地世族把建城史追溯到前伊斯兰时代建孔戈韦阿的女王姆瓦娜·姆基西，以及建起第一座石构清真寺的谢赫·姆维塔。岛上的姆纳拉清真寺约建于1300年；伊本·白图泰14世纪在此留宿一夜，见到的是沙斐仪派穆斯林和营造精良的木构清真寺。在基尔瓦的势力范围内，蒙巴萨把象牙、黄金、小米、芝麻和椰子运往红海、阿拉伯和印度，港中停泊着索法拉、坎贝、马林迪和桑给巴尔来的船。1444年，古老的姆维塔世族和远洋贸易已使它成为近邻马林迪最大的对手。

在所有斯瓦希里城邦中，蒙巴萨抵抗葡萄牙人最为顽强。瓦斯科·达·伽马1498年在此受到冷遇，城市1500年遭洗劫，葡萄牙舰队又两度来攻：1505年一次，1528年努诺·达·库尼亚更摧毁了大半个城市。奥斯曼将领阿里贝伊1585年夺取蒙巴萨；不出数年，津巴武装席卷该岛、屠戮穆斯林居民，最后在马林迪被塞格朱人挡住。葡萄牙人1589年重返，于1593年至1596年在旧港上方修建耶稣堡。这座方形文艺复兴风格要塞四角设棱垒，由意大利建筑师乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·凯拉蒂设计，俯瞰形似一个仰面朝天的人，施工则由斯瓦希里工匠完成。1631年，被葡萄牙人养大、教名堂·热罗尼莫的统治者优素福·伊本·哈桑袭杀驻军，此后出海为盗；葡萄牙军队次年夺回要塞。

1696年，阿曼的赛义夫·本·苏丹围攻耶稣堡，近两年封锁之后，其军队在1698年12月破城。葡萄牙人1728年至1729年曾短暂夺回，但自18世纪40年代起，马兹鲁伊家族的总督割据城邦与要塞，拒不接受阿曼统治。象牙、过往船只的给养和奴隶贸易养着这座岛，1821年时阿卜杜拉·伊本·艾哈迈德·马兹鲁伊仍在蒙巴萨主政。

en:
Malindi lies on Malindi Bay at the mouth of the Galana River, where Bantu-speaking farmers and fishermen smelted iron long before the first stone houses went up.
