Dzungar armies sacked the Syr Darya towns in 1723-1727, and old Sozaq was among the cities they destroyed.
zh:
所扎克在13世纪的文献中称作胡扎克，是卡拉套山北麓、穆云库姆沙漠以南一座有城墙的商队城镇，锡尔河绿洲通往钦察草原的道路从这里穿过干旱草原。城址约19公顷，叠压着五层建筑遗存，最早可到10世纪，发掘中还出土过铜钱、陶器和房屋残迹。1444年，它正处在阿布海尔汗日益扩张的乌兹别克联盟兵锋之前；1446年，该城与瑟格纳克、阿库尔干一起自愿归附，使阿布海尔的兀鲁思在锡尔河防线上站稳脚跟。

阿布海尔1468年死后，成吉思汗系苏丹克烈与贾尼别克以锡尔河诸城建立哈萨克汗国，哈萨克传统把所扎克列为1465至1469年的第一个汗廷驻地。在与昔班尼王朝的长期战争中，贾尼别克的长子马赫穆德为哈萨克人夺取此城；1511至1521年哈斯木汗在位时，汗廷再次设在这里。16世纪余下的时间里，它作为锡尔河诸城之一，屡见于哈萨克汗、布哈拉昔班尼汗与南方帖木儿统治者的争夺。1723至1727年，准噶尔军队洗劫沿河诸城，所扎克古城也在被毁之列。

en:
Sighnaq, whose ruins are now called Sunakata, stood about twenty kilometres north of the Syr Darya under the Karatau range, on the caravan road between Isfijab and Jand; in Turkic its name means Shelter. From the tenth century it was a half-settled Oghuz border town where steppe hides and stock changed hands for the goods of the Muslim south, and the Hudud al-'Alam notes that its bows were made for export. The country round it was Dar al-Kufr, the Abode of Unbelief, which ghazis from Khwarezm raided in 1152 and 1195, and in the twelfth century the town was the capital of the still-pagan Kipchak khanate. Genghis Khan's men took it after a siege in 1220 and killed the population. The rebuilt city became a capital of the Blue Horde, with a mint, mosques and madrasas under Urus Khan, and Muslim writers called it the land harbour of the Kipchak steppe. Baraq Khan defeated a Timurid army and held it from 1427; after his death it reverted to Shah Rukh, and in 1444 Sighnaq sat on the Timurid frontier with Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbeks massing beyond it.

Abu'l-Khayr took the city in 1446, and in 1457 Kalmyk raiders defeated him at Kuk Kashanah seven kilometres to the south and dictated their peace. Muhammad Shaybani, the refounder of Uzbek power, was born in the Sighnaq region; he stormed the town several times in the 1490s. After the Uzbek state broke apart it passed to the Kazakhs, who kept it as a capital from 1521 to 1620. War with Bukhara nevertheless reached its walls in the 1570s, when Baba Sultan and then Abdullah Khan II seized the town, and in 1598 Abdullah issued a grant to the mausoleum of Ziya al-Din while Karakalpak clans were already settling nearby. By the later seventeenth century the caravan road had moved away and Dzungar and Uzbek raids had emptied the old town, whose central ruins served as a graveyard; it lingered only as a name on Remezov's map of Siberia drawn in 1698.
zh:
斯格纳克（又译昔格纳克）遗址今称苏纳卡塔，位于锡尔河以北约20公里、喀拉塔乌山南麓，在伊斯菲贾卜与詹德之间的商路上，突厥语意为「避难所」。10世纪时，它是乌古斯人的半定居边镇，草原的皮革和牲畜在此换取南方穆斯林地区的货物，《世界境域志》记载当地制造弓箭用于出口。城周地区被称为达尔库夫尔，即「不信者之地」，花剌子模的加齐1152年和1195年两度来袭；12世纪，这里是尚未皈依的钦察汗国都城。1220年，成吉思汗的军队围城破城，屠尽其民。重建后的城市成为蓝帐汗国都城，兀鲁思汗在位时设有铸币厂、清真寺和经学院，穆斯林作者称它为钦察草原的陆地港口。1427年，巴拉克汗击败帖木儿军队，占据此城；他死后城市复归沙哈鲁。1444年，斯格纳克扼守着帖木儿的边境，城外就是阿布海尔集结的乌兹别克人。

1446年，阿布海尔攻占斯格纳克；1457年，卡尔梅克袭击者在城南7公里的库卡沙纳击败他，逼他接受议和。乌兹别克势力的重建者穆罕默德·昔班尼就出生在斯格纳克一带，他在1490年代又数次猛攻此城。乌兹别克国家崩解后，斯格纳克转入哈萨克之手，1521—1620年作为哈萨克汗国都城。与布哈拉的战争还是追到了城下：1570年代，巴巴苏丹和阿卜杜拉汗二世先后夺城；1598年，阿卜杜拉向齐亚丁圣陵颁赐封地，当时附近已有卡拉卡尔帕克部族落脚。到17世纪后期，商路改道，加上准噶尔和乌兹别克诸部不断袭掠，旧城空废，城中遗址沦为墓地；只有1698年列梅佐夫绘制的西伯利亚地图上，还留着斯格纳克这个名字。

en:
At the great bend of the Don the Volga and the Don come within seventy versts of each other, and the narrow portage between them has carried boats and goods between the Caspian and the Black Sea since ancient times. In the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries the Golden Horde city of Beljamen, perhaps the Bezdezh of Russian chronicles, stood on the Volga bank where Dubovka now lies, a rich market on the caravan road. Timur's armies sacked it at the end of the fourteenth century and it never recovered. In 1444 its ruins stood in Great Horde pasture, Tatar herds grazed around them, and boatmen still hauled their craft across the portage.

After Muscovy took Kazan in 1552 and Astrakhan in 1556 the Volga trade revived. A seasonal guard of fifty streltsy watched the portage from 1579, and in July 1589 voivode Grigory Zasekin founded the permanent fortress of Tsaritsyn at the mouth of the little Tsaritsa River; its nearest sister fort, Voronezh, lay more than five hundred versts away across the steppe. The garrison held an exposed post. The Volga's right bank was called the Crimean side, and in raiding years the soldiers could pasture their cattle only on Sarpinsky island in mid-river.

For more than a century rebels and steppe raiders took turns at the walls. In 1607 the garrison joined the pretender False Peter and was stormed by Shuisky's troops. Stepan Razin dragged his boats over the portage to the Volga in 1667 for his Caspian cruise, and in April 1670 his Cossacks entered Tsaritsyn after the fortress musketeers opened the gates; the loyal voivode was put to death, and the town changed hands again once Razin was defeated. Bulavin's Cossacks held it in 1708. In August 1717 the Crimean serasker Bakhti Gerai, on the great Kuban slave raid, blockaded the fortress and drove fifteen to thirty thousand people off along the Penza-Saratov-Tsaritsyn line. The Tsaritsyn watch line was begun in 1718, the Volga Cossack Host was settled at Dubovka in 1734, and Yemelyan Pugachev's assault was beaten off in August 1774. From 1780 Tsaritsyn was an uyezd town, a grain and salt port on the lower Volga.
zh:
顿河在此拐出大河曲，伏尔加河与顿河相距不过七十俄里，两河之间狭窄的连水陆路自古便是船只和货物往来里海与黑海的通道。13至14世纪，金帐汗国的城市别利亚门（或即罗斯编年史中的别兹杰日）就坐落在今杜博夫卡所在的伏尔加河畔，是商道上富庶的市场。14世纪末，帖木儿的军队洗劫此城，它再未恢复。1444年，故城废墟躺在大帐汗国的牧场上，四周是鞑靼牧群，船工仍把船只拖过这条连水陆路。

1552年莫斯科征服喀山、1556年征服阿斯特拉罕后，伏尔加商路重新繁荣。1579年起，五十名射击兵组成的季节性哨队在此看守连水陆路；1589年7月，督军格里戈里·扎谢金在察里察小河口建起永久要塞察里津，最近的友军要塞沃罗涅日远在五百多俄里外的草原另一端。守军的处境凶险：伏尔加河右岸被称作「克里米亚岸」，入寇的年份里，他们只能把牲畜赶到河中的萨尔平斯基岛上放牧。

此后一个多世纪，叛乱者和草原入寇者轮番攻打这座要塞。1607年，守军投奔伪彼得，被舒伊斯基的军队攻破。1667年，斯捷潘·拉辛把船拖过连水陆路进入伏尔加河，开始他的里海之行；1670年4月，城内射击兵哗变开门，他的哥萨克进占察里津，不肯归顺的督军被处死，拉辛败亡后该城再度易手。1708年，布拉文的哥萨克占据该城。1717年8月，克里米亚塞拉斯克巴赫季·格莱发动库班大掠奴，封锁要塞，沿奔萨—萨拉托夫—察里津一线掳走一万五千至三万人。1718年俄国开筑察里津警戒防线，1734年伏尔加哥萨克军被安置到杜博夫卡，1774年8月叶梅利扬·普加乔夫强攻要塞被击退。1780年起，察里津成为县城，是下伏尔加的粮食与食盐港口。

en:
The southern Udmurts, the 'meadow people' whom the Russians called votyaki, farmed the forest-steppe between the Vyatka and the Kama on rye, cattle and forest honey; the Ananyino burial ground by the river named the Iron Age culture of the region. Their southern ary clans had paid tribute to Volga Bulgaria and kept princes who served first Bulgar and then Tatar governors; their country was the Arsk land. At the Kama crossing rose Alabuga, a Bulgar border stronghold founded under Emir Ibrahim around the end of the tenth century; a white-stone fortress-mosque with eight towers followed in the twelfth, modelled on the mosques of Bilyar and Bolgar, to guard the caravan road up to the Visu fur country. In 1444 the Arsk land belonged to the khanate of Kazan, and Udmurt villages rendered grain, honey and pelts to the khan.

Moscow took Vyatka and the northern Udmurts in 1489. When Kazan fell in October 1552 the tsar's regiments swept the Arsk side for ten days, and the Udmurts became yasak peasants paying pelts and honey. Russian settlers filled the Kama clearings: Sarapul appears in the 1579 census as a refuge of peasants fleeing the Perm country, and Yelabuga grew beside the Bulgar ruins as a palace village, with a Trinity monastery built on the old fort site in 1614 to 1616. The one surviving tower of the fortress-mosque was called Shaytan's castle, and the early seventeenth-century Book of the Great Map marks 'the Devil's town, Yelabuga likewise'. Both towns throve on grain and fish floated down the Kama. In 1773 Pugachev's rebels sacked Sarapul, and the southern Kama peoples rose with him the next year. In 1780 Catherine II made Yelabuga and Sarapul district towns of the new Vyatka viceroyalty.

Sarapul raised the best-known soldier of these parts. Nadezhda Durova, the commandant's daughter, left the town in 1806 and enlisted in a cavalry regiment as a man. She fought at Friedland and Borodino, where she was wounded, and was Kutuzov's orderly; when her secret came out Alexander I pardoned her in person and let her serve on under the name Aleksandrov. In 1816 she retired to Yelabuga.
zh:
南部的乌德穆尔特人是「草地之人」，俄罗斯人称之为沃季亚克人，在维亚特卡河与卡马河之间的森林草原上耕种，以黑麦、牲畜和林间蜂蜜为生；卡马河畔发掘出的安纳尼诺墓群，成了整个地区铁器时代文化的名字。他们的南支「阿尔人」曾向伏尔加保加利亚纳贡，本族王公先后听命于保加尔和鞑靼长官，这片土地故称阿尔斯克之地。卡马河渡口上矗立着阿拉布加，是10世纪末前后埃米尔易卜拉欣所建的保加尔边境要塞；12世纪又在那里筑起一座八塔白石清真寺堡垒，仿照比利亚尔和保加尔城的聚礼清真寺，扼守通往「维苏」毛皮之乡的商队大道。1444年，阿尔斯克之地属于喀山汗国，乌德穆尔特村庄向汗缴纳谷物、蜂蜜和毛皮。

1489年莫斯科拿下维亚特卡，北乌德穆尔特人随之归入大公治下。1552年10月喀山城破，沙皇的军队横扫阿尔斯克之地十日，乌德穆尔特人沦为缴纳毛皮和蜂蜜的雅萨克农户。俄罗斯农民占满卡马河畔的开垦地：1579年的册籍中，萨拉普尔是逃离彼尔姆之地的农民的落脚处；叶拉布加在保加尔古城址旁兴起，成为宫廷村落，1614至1616年在旧城址上建起圣三一修道院。清真寺堡垒只余一座孤塔，人称「魔王堡」，城也得了「鬼城」的别号，17世纪初的《大地图册》就把此地标作「鬼城，即叶拉布加」。两座城镇都靠顺卡马河贩运谷物和鱼产兴旺。1773年普加乔夫的起义者洗劫萨拉普尔，第二年南卡马的各族民众群起投奔他的队伍。1780年叶卡捷琳娜二世改制，叶拉布加和萨拉普尔成为新设维亚特卡总督辖区的县城。

这一带最有名的军人出自萨拉普尔。司令官的女儿娜杰日达·杜罗娃1806年从城中出走，化名男子加入骑兵团，打过弗里德兰和博罗季诺，在博罗季诺负伤，还当过库图佐夫的传令官；身份暴露后，亚历山大一世亲自赦免了她，准她以亚历山德罗夫之名继续服役。1816年她退役，到叶拉布加定居。

en:
Urgench is the grain country of southern Khwarazm, flat fields watered by canals drawn from the lower Amu Darya, later including the Shavat channel, where Sunni farmers sowed wheat, rice and millet. The walled town that now carries this name did not exist in 1444; the great city of the delta was still Gurganj, farther north among the old channels. Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbeks had taken Gurganj in 1430 or 1431, so these southern canal villages and their granaries stood on the Uzbek edge of Timurid Khwarazm, between the Kyzylkum pastures and the trade roads toward Khiva.

Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks conquered Khwarazm in 1505, and after he fell at Merv a Safavid garrison held the oases until the Sunni nobility called in Ilbars and drove the Qizilbash out in 1511. The khans of Ilbars's Arabshahid line ruled from Vazir and then Gurganj; Bukhara overran the country in the 1590s, and Haji Muhammad returned from Safavid exile only in 1598. During the seventeenth century the Daryaliq channels failed and the northern cities began to empty. Abu al-Ghazi, khan from 1643 after ten years in Persian exile, was a historian as well as a ruler: he wrote his genealogies of the Turks and Turkmens in Chagatai while settling Gurganj's survivors in the southern oasis and founding Yangi Urgench, the 'new Urgench'. Nader Shah occupied Khiva for six years from 1740, and the Qongirat dynasty that took power in 1763 repaired the canals and tightened its hold over the delta; in 1811 Muhammad Rahim Khan subdued the lower channels.
zh:
乌尔根奇是花剌子模南部的谷物之乡，阿姆河下游引出的灌渠（后来包括沙瓦特渠）浇灌着平坦农田，逊尼派农户在水边种植小麦、稻米和粟。1444年，后来称作乌尔根奇的这座城墙城镇还不存在，三角洲的大城仍是更北面、旧水道之间的玉龙杰赤。阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克人已在1430年或1431年攻占玉龙杰赤，南方这些渠边村落和粮仓便处在帖木儿王朝花剌子模的乌兹别克边境，一边是克孜勒库姆的牧场，一边是通往希瓦的商路。

1505年，穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人征服花剌子模；他在梅尔夫战死后，萨法维驻军接管绿洲，直到当地逊尼派贵族迎立伊尔巴斯，于1511年逐走克孜勒巴什。伊尔巴斯一系的阿拉伯沙希王朝诸汗先以瓦济尔、后以玉龙杰赤为都；1590年代布哈拉攻占花剌子模，哈吉·穆罕默德流亡萨法维波斯，1598年才得以返回。17世纪，达里亚雷克各渠水量衰退，北方城市人口流散。1643年即位的阿布·哈齐曾在波斯流亡十年，他既是汗也是史家，用察合台文写下突厥人与土库曼人的系谱，同时把玉龙杰赤的幸存居民安置到南方绿洲，建立了杨吉·乌尔根奇，意为「新乌尔根奇」。纳迪尔沙自1740年起占领希瓦六年；1763年掌权的昆格拉特王朝整修灌渠、收紧对三角洲的控制，1811年穆罕默德·拉希姆汗征服了下游各水道。

en:
Yedishkul is the open steppe of the lower Dnieper below the rapids, looking south across flat country to the Perekop isthmus and the Crimea. In 1444, three years after Hacı I Giray founded the Giray khanate, these pastures belonged to the Crimean khan. Tatar herders moved between the Volga grasslands and the peninsula along tracks leading to Perekop, and Dnieper landings served the ferries; no stone town stood anywhere in the land.

From 1478 the Crimean khanate was an Ottoman vassal. Through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries Zaporozhian Cossacks pushed down the river, setting up winter camps and palanka districts, and the settlement of Bilchowisce appears on Beauplan's map of 1648. In 1728 the Yedishkul Nogai horde, driven west by the Kalmyks from the Emba by way of the Volga and the Kuban, entered the steppe under Crimean protection; the region took its name from them. Field Marshal Münnich's Russians built the Alexander redoubt here in 1737 and gave it back at the Peace of Niš in 1739. Russian troops returned in 1771, the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca detached the steppe from the khanate in 1774, and the Nogais were moved off to the Kuban, where their last rising was crushed in 1783.

Russian rule arrived in the shape of a shipyard. On 18 June 1778 Catherine II founded Kherson on the high Dnieper bank, named after the ancient Greek city of Chersonesos in the Crimea. It was Grigory Potemkin's project, built beside Münnich's old redoubt by his engineer Ivan Gannibal, and on 16 September 1783 the yard launched the 66-gun Slava Yekateriny, the first ship of the line of the Black Sea Fleet. Suvorov supervised the town's fortifications during the war of 1787-1791. Potemkin himself was buried in St Catherine's Cathedral in 1791, and in 1803 Kherson became the seat of the Kherson governorate.
zh:
叶迪什库勒是第聂伯险滩以南、第聂伯河下游的开阔草原，原野尽头南望彼列科普地峡与克里米亚。1444年，即哈吉一世·格来建立格来王朝三年后，这片牧场归克里米亚汗所有。鞑靼牧人沿通往彼列科普的牧道往返于伏尔加草原与克里米亚半岛之间，第聂伯河上只有若干渡口，全境没有一座城池。

1478年起，克里米亚汗国成为奥斯曼帝国的附庸。16至17世纪，扎波罗热哥萨克沿河而下，设立冬营和「帕兰卡」营区，比利霍维奇（Bilchowisce）居点出现在1648年的博普兰地图上。1728年，叶迪什库勒诺盖斡耳朵受卡尔梅克人逼迫，从恩巴河经伏尔加河、库班西迁，进入克里米亚汗庇护下的草原，地区也因这支斡耳朵得名。1737年，陆军元帅米尼希麾下的俄军在此修筑亚历山大堡垒，1739年依尼什和约归还。1771年俄军再度占领，1774年库楚克开纳吉和约把这片草原从汗国手中夺走，诺盖人被迁往库班，他们最后的反抗于1783年在那里被镇压。

俄国给这片土地带来的是一座船坞。1778年6月18日，叶卡捷琳娜二世下令在第聂伯河高岸上建赫尔松，城名取自克里米亚的古希腊城市赫尔松涅斯。这是格里戈里·波将金主持的工程，由他的工兵将领伊万·甘尼巴尔在米尼希旧堡垒旁营建；1783年9月16日，船坞下水六十六炮战舰「叶卡捷琳娜荣耀号」，这是黑海舰队的第一艘战列舰。1787至1791年战争期间，苏沃洛夫主持城防工事。1791年，波将金本人葬于圣叶卡捷琳娜大教堂，1803年赫尔松成为赫尔松省省治。

en:
Shetland is a bare, deeply indented archipelago where the North Sea meets the Atlantic, about 220 kilometres west of Norway. Norse farmers and fishermen occupied its sheltered sounds from the late eighth century, and the island names still record that settlement. In 1444 the Catholic, Norse-speaking islanders belonged to the Norwegian Crown within the Kalmar Union. They kept sheep and small farms and fished from the voes, while Scalloway on the Mainland served as their older centre. Bressay Sound already had a fine anchorage, but the future town of Lerwick did not yet exist.

The islands changed crowns through a royal dowry. On 28 May 1469 Christian I pledged Shetland to James III of Scotland for 8,000 Rhenish guilders as security for the dowry of Margaret of Denmark. The money was not repaid, and Scotland annexed the islands in 1472. Scottish institutions followed slowly: a sheriff of Orkney and Shetland was appointed in 1541, and general Scots law replaced local practice in 1612. At Scalloway, Patrick Stewart, Earl of Orkney, built his stone tower from 1600 with workers summoned from the parishes. Island lairds complained of his rule, and he was executed in 1615.

Lerwick grew with the Dutch herring fleets that gathered in Bressay Sound during the seventeenth century. The Scots raised an artillery fort above the anchorage in 1652-1653; its thin garrison bluffed a Dutch fleet in 1667, and the ungarrisoned works were burned in 1673. Rebuilt in 1781 and named Fort Charlotte, it guarded a town that had replaced Scalloway as the island capital in 1708. After the 1707 Union, salt duties weakened the old North German fish trade, and Shetland merchant-lairds fitted out their own vessels. Roughly 3,000 Shetlanders served in the Royal Navy during the Napoleonic Wars; of 120 men taken from Fetlar, only twenty returned.
zh:
设得兰群岛是北海与大西洋之间一座裸露而海湾深切的群岛，东距挪威约220公里。8世纪末起，诺斯农民和渔民占据各处避风海湾，岛上地名仍保留着这段定居史。1444年，这些说诺斯语的天主教岛民属于卡尔马联盟中的挪威王权。他们经营小农场、牧羊，并在峡湾状的近海水域捕鱼；主岛上的斯卡洛韦是旧中心。布雷塞湾已有良港，但未来城镇勒威克尚未出现。

群岛因一笔王室嫁妆易主。1469年5月28日，克里斯蒂安一世把设得兰抵押给苏格兰国王詹姆斯三世，作为丹麦的玛格丽特嫁妆中8000莱茵古尔登的担保。这笔钱没有偿还，苏格兰遂于1472年吞并群岛。苏格兰制度推进得很慢：1541年才设立奥克尼与设得兰治安官，1612年苏格兰一般法律取代当地旧规。在斯卡洛韦，奥克尼伯爵帕特里克·斯图尔特从1600年起征召各教区民夫修建石造塔楼。岛上地主控诉他的统治，他最终在1615年被处死。

17世纪，荷兰鲱鱼船队聚集布雷塞湾，勒威克随之发展。苏格兰人在1652年至1653年于锚地上方修筑炮兵要塞；1667年，薄弱的守军唬退了一支荷兰舰队，1673年无人驻守的工事又被烧毁。要塞于1781年重建并命名为夏洛特堡，护卫着这座已在1708年取代斯卡洛韦的群岛首府。1707年联合后，盐税削弱了旧有的北德鱼货贸易，设得兰商人地主开始自行装备船只。拿破仑战争期间约有3000名设得兰人在皇家海军服役；费特勒岛被带走的120人中只有20人返乡。

en:
The Faroes are a steep, treeless island group between Shetland, Norway and Iceland, where sea cliffs and narrow sounds set the limits of farming. Norse settlers established their general assembly on Tinganes, the rocky peninsula that divides Tórshavn harbour, and the annual thing drew a market. In 1271 the Norwegian Crown arranged regular sailings from Bergen with salt, timber and grain, making the harbour the islands' main trading place. In 1444 Catholic West Norse islanders under the Norwegian Crown in the Kalmar Union kept sheep, fished and took sea birds, bringing wool and dried fish to Tórshavn even though no built-up town had yet been recorded.

Sources first mention a permanent settlement after the Lutheran reform of 1539. Magnus Heinason, a Faroese trader and privateer who had served William the Silent in the Dutch Revolt, built the Skansin fort around 1580 after pirates and slave raiders nearly caught him at the harbour. The little battery guarded the anchorage, and in 1584 Tórshavn had only 101 inhabitants. Heinason was later arrested on the orders of the Danish official Christoffer Valkendorff and beheaded in Copenhagen in 1589; a noble assembly declared the sentence void the next year and restored his name after his death.

In 1655 Frederick III enfeoffed Kristoffer Gabel with the Faroes, and from 1662 Gabel's family controlled the trade monopoly, paying islanders low fixed prices for their goods. A gunpowder store exploded on Tinganes in 1673, burning houses and old island records. The Crown took over the monopoly in 1709, the year smallpox killed about 250 of Tórshavn's roughly 300 people. Niels Ryberg later used the royal warehouses for entrepôt trade and experiments with salted cod and herring. Tórshavn Cathedral was built in 1788, and after the Treaty of Kiel left the Faroes under Denmark in 1814, the Crown suspended the Løgting in 1816.
zh:
法罗群岛是设得兰、挪威与冰岛之间一组陡峭少树的岛屿，海崖和狭窄海峡限制了农耕范围。诺斯移民把全体岛民的议会设在分隔托尔斯港的岩石半岛廷加内斯，年度庭会也吸引来市集。1271年，挪威王权安排船只从卑尔根定期运来盐、木材和谷物，使这座港口成为群岛主要贸易地。1444年，卡尔马联盟中挪威王权治下信奉天主教的西诺斯语岛民牧羊、捕鱼、捕捉海鸟，把羊毛和风干鱼带到托尔斯港，但当时文献尚未记载这里已有成片城镇。

1539年路德宗改革之后，资料才首次提到常住居民点。法罗商人兼私掠船船长马格努斯·海纳松曾在荷兰起义中为沉默者威廉效力；约1580年，海盗和掳奴者险些在港中截住他，他随后修建斯坎辛要塞。这座小炮台守卫锚地，而1584年托尔斯港只有101名居民。海纳松后来被丹麦官员克里斯托弗·瓦尔肯多夫下令逮捕，1589年在哥本哈根被斩首；次年贵族会议宣布判决无效，在他死后恢复名誉。

1655年，弗雷德里克三世把法罗群岛封给克里斯托弗·加贝尔；1662年起，加贝尔家族控制贸易垄断，以低廉的固定价格收购岛民货物。1673年，廷加内斯一处火药库爆炸，烧毁房屋和古老岛志。1709年王室接管垄断贸易，同年天花夺去托尔斯港约300名居民中约250人的生命。尼尔斯·吕贝尔后来利用王室仓库经营转口贸易，并试做腌制鳕鱼和鲱鱼。托尔斯港主教座堂建于1788年；1814年《基尔条约》把法罗留在丹麦治下后，王权又在1816年中止勒格廷议会。

en:
Bornholm is a rocky granite island far out in the southern Baltic, closer to the coasts of Sweden and northern Germany than to the Danish mainland, and sailors and raiders have fought over its harbours since Viking times. Its four round churches, the largest at Østerlars, went up around 1160 with a fortified top storey and shooting slits, as much strongpoints against Wendish pirates as places of worship. In the thirteenth century the archbishops of Lund raised Hammershus on the cliffs of the northern tip, the largest medieval fortress in Scandinavia; Danish kings stormed it again and again in their quarrels with the archbishopric, yet it remained a clerical stronghold into the 1500s. Rønne, on a natural harbour on the west coast, became the island's chief market town in 1327, and merchants of Greifswald kept a trading post there around 1400. In 1444 Bornholm was a Catholic Danish fief held by the Archbishop of Lund, its people living by herring and the Baltic carrying trade.

In 1525 Frederick I pawned the island to Lübeck for fifty years, and the city's governors ran it from Hammershus until the Danish crown redeemed Bornholm in 1576. Swedish forces under Carl Gustaf Wrangel stormed the fortress during the Torstenson War in 1645, and the Peace of Roskilde ceded the whole island to Sweden in 1658. Swedish rule lasted less than a year: on 8 December 1658 a party of islanders led by Jens Pedersen Kofoed shot the Swedish commandant, Johan Printzensköld, in the streets of Rønne and sent word to Copenhagen that Bornholm had returned to its old king; the Treaty of Copenhagen confirmed the return in 1660. Hammershus then became a state prison. Corfitz Ulfeldt and his wife Leonora Christina were held there in 1660 and 1661, and the German theologian and alchemist Johann Conrad Dippel was its prisoner from 1719 to 1724. The fortress was abandoned in 1743, leaving Rønne as the island's garrison and administrative centre.
zh:
博恩霍尔姆是远悬南波罗的海的一座花岗岩岩岛，距瑞典和北德海岸反比距丹麦本土更近，自维京时代起，水手和袭掠者就为它的港口争夺不休。岛上四座圆形教堂约建于1160年前后，最大的一座在厄斯特拉斯（Østerlars）；教堂顶层设有防御工事和箭眼，既是礼拜场所，也是抵御文德海盗的据点。13世纪，隆德大主教在岛北端的悬崖上修筑哈默斯胡斯，这是斯堪的纳维亚最大的中世纪要塞；丹麦国王在同大主教区的争斗中几度攻破此堡，它却始终是教会的堡垒，直到16世纪初。伦讷坐落在西岸的天然良港旁，1327年成为全岛首镇，1400年前后格赖夫斯瓦尔德的商人在此设有商站。1444年，博恩霍尔姆是隆德大主教持有的天主教丹麦封邑，岛民靠鲱鱼和波罗的海航运为生。

1525年，腓特烈一世把岛屿典押给吕贝克，期限五十年，吕贝克的总督据哈默斯胡斯统治全岛，直到1576年丹麦王室才将其赎回。1645年托尔斯滕森战争中，卡尔·古斯塔夫·弗兰格尔率瑞典军攻破要塞；1658年《罗斯基勒条约》把全岛割让给瑞典。瑞典的统治不到一年：1658年12月8日，延斯·佩德森·科福德（Jens Pedersen Kofoed）带领一批岛民在伦讷街头击毙瑞典长官约翰·普林岑舍尔德，并向哥本哈根报信，宣布博恩霍尔姆回归旧主，1660年《哥本哈根条约》确认了这次回归。哈默斯胡斯此后改为国家监狱：科尔菲茨·乌尔费尔特和妻子莱奥诺拉·克里斯蒂娜于1660年至1661年关押于此，德意志神学家兼炼金术士约翰·康拉德·迪佩尔则在1719年至1724年被囚于此。1743年要塞废弃，伦讷成为全岛的驻军和行政中心。

en:
Blekinge is a broken Baltic coast of granite hills, oak woods and skerries. Danish kings held it as their eastern march, governing through Sölvesborg and Lyckeby castles while the landsting under Scanian Law met at Hjortsberga. Ronneby was the busiest port, with its 12th-century Holy Cross Church and town privileges from 1387. The forests behind the town supplied timber and tall oak for shipbuilders, and the narrow coastal roads gave Swedish raiders an easy target in every Nordic war. In 1444 Blekinge remained Danish, poor in towns but valuable for ships' masts, timber and defended anchorages.

The Northern Seven Years' War produced the province's most notorious atrocity: on 4 September 1564 Erik XIV's Swedish army stormed Ronneby and killed townspeople in the Ronneby Bloodbath. In 1611 the young Gustav Adolf surprised Kristianopel, the fortified town Christian IV had planted near Lyckeby. After Roskilde ceded Blekinge to Sweden on 28 February 1658, the Swedish crown rebuilt the coast for its fleet. Karlshamn was chartered in 1664 beside a Baltic harbour and given forts designed by Erik Dahlbergh; pro-Danish snapphanar attacked it during the Scanian War. On 10 August 1680 Charles XI founded Karlskrona on the island of Trossö, an ice-free base closer than Stockholm to Denmark and Sweden's Baltic provinces. Ronneby lost its town rights and many inhabitants were moved to the new city, while shipwrights were brought from Ostrobothnia and Stockholm. The yard employed about 1,100 workers in 1711, and by 1750 Karlskrona had roughly 10,000 people and ranked among Sweden's largest cities.
zh:
布莱金厄是一段丘陵、橡树林和岩岛交错的破碎波罗的海海岸。丹麦国王把它当作王国东境，由瑟尔沃斯堡和吕克比两座城堡统辖，行斯科讷法的地区庭在约茨贝加召开。龙讷比是最大的港口，拥有12世纪的圣十字教堂，1387年获得城市权。城后森林出产造船用的木材和高大橡木，而狭窄的滨海道路也使它在每场北欧战争中都容易遭到瑞典人袭击。1444年，布莱金厄仍属丹麦，城镇不多，却因船桅、木材和可设防的锚地而有价值。

北方七年战争给这里留下最出名的暴行：1564年9月4日，埃里克十四世的瑞典军队攻破龙讷比，杀戮市民，史称「龙讷比血案」。1611年，年轻的古斯塔夫·阿道夫突袭克里斯蒂安四世设在吕克比附近的设防新城克里斯蒂安诺佩尔。1658年2月28日罗斯基勒和约把布莱金厄割让瑞典后，瑞典王室为舰队改造这条海岸。卡尔斯港1664年在一处波罗的海良港获特许，埃里克·达尔贝里设计的炮台负责防卫；斯科讷战争期间，亲丹麦的自由射手曾进攻这里。1680年8月10日，卡尔十一世在特罗瑟岛建立卡尔斯克鲁纳，取其冬季不冻，且比斯德哥尔摩更靠近丹麦和瑞典的波罗的海行省。龙讷比被取消城市权，许多居民迁往新城，船匠则从厄斯特罗波的尼亚和斯德哥尔摩调来。1711年，船坞雇工约一千一百人；到1750年，卡尔斯克鲁纳约有一万居民，已跻身瑞典最大城市之列。

en:
Lolland and Falster, joined by the narrow Guldborgsund, lie almost completely flat between Langeland and Zealand; Danes call Lolland the 'pancake island'. Their loam is the most productive in Denmark, yet nearly every acre belonged to a manor, and the nobles held the peasantry tighter than anywhere else in the kingdom. A castle raised at Nykøbing in the late twelfth century guarded the sound's narrowest stretch against Wendish pirates; Lübeck stormed and burned it in 1253, and the Hanseatic cities besieged it again in the Dano-Hanseatic War of 1368 to 1370. Nakskov, on the western fjord, grew from a fishing village into the islands' leading market town, its oldest surviving privileges dated 1266. When the crown pawned Denmark in the mid-fourteenth century, the islands passed to the Holstein count John the Mild, and the deposed Christopher II died in a house at Sakskøbing. A Bridgettine abbey was founded at Maribo in 1416. In 1444 Lolland and Falster were Catholic crown lands, their wealth in grain, cattle and fisheries.

In 1446 the Lolland landsting enacted the Lollands Vilkår, strengthening the lords and, for the first time in Denmark, binding tenant farmers to the estates they worked. Lübeckers burned Nakskov in 1510, and in the Count's Feud of 1534 Nykøbing sided with the deposed Christian II; the Reformation closed the islands' monasteries later in the decade. The new Renaissance castle at Nykøbing housed Sophie of Mecklenburg, widow of Frederick II, who ruled all Lolland-Falster from 1588 until her death in 1631; Christian IV often stayed there to hunt on Falster. In 1658 Charles X Gustav's army crossed the ice from Langeland. Legend says the Nykøbing priest Jesse Jessen preached so fiercely to the Swedish king in the monastery church that he spared the town the fire he had planned. Nakskov did not escape: after a long siege in 1659 the Swedes sacked it, and the town lost half its people in the years that followed. In 1674 Nakskov became one of the first Danish towns where Jews were allowed to settle. From the 1780s the magnate C. D. F. Reventlow directed the crown's agrarian reforms, ending compulsory labour on the manors and setting tenants on the way to owning their farms.
zh:
洛兰与法尔斯特由狭窄的古尔堡海峡相连，是朗厄兰岛与西兰岛之间两座几乎全平的岛屿，丹麦人把洛兰称作「煎饼岛」。两岛的壤土是丹麦最肥沃的耕地，田亩却几乎尽归庄园，贵族对农民的管束也比王国其他任何地方都紧。文德海盗袭扰这片海岸，12世纪末，尼克宾在海峡最窄处筑起城堡设防；1253年吕贝克军队破城焚镇，1368年至1370年的丹麦-汉萨战争中，汉萨诸城再度围攻。西岸峡湾旁的纳克斯考由渔村发展为两岛首镇，现存最早的城市特许状出自1266年。14世纪中期丹麦王室典押土地时，两岛划归荷尔斯泰因伯爵「温和者」约翰，被废黜的克里斯托弗二世最终在萨克斯克宾的一所宅子中终老。1416年，圣布里吉特会在马里博创立修道院。1444年，洛兰与法尔斯特是信奉天主教的王属岛屿，财富出自谷物、牛只和渔业。

1446年，洛兰地方法庭颁行《洛兰规约》，强化贵族的权利，并首次在丹麦把佃农束缚在所耕种的庄园上。1510年吕贝克人焚毁纳克斯考；1534年伯爵战争中，尼克宾站在被废的克里斯蒂安二世一边，1530年代后期宗教改革又使岛上修道院相继关闭。尼克宾新建的文艺复兴式城堡成为腓特烈二世遗孀梅克伦堡的索菲的驻地，她从1588年起统辖整个洛兰-法尔斯特，直到1631年去世；克里斯蒂安四世也常为法尔斯特的猎场驻跸此地。1658年，卡尔十世·古斯塔夫的军队从朗厄兰踏冰登岛。相传尼克宾的一位神父在修道院教堂向瑞典国王厉声布道，使国王放弃了焚城的打算。纳克斯考未能幸免：1659年瑞典军久围之后攻破并洗劫了城镇，此后数年镇民损失了一半。1674年，纳克斯考成为丹麦最早允许犹太人定居的城镇之一。1780年代起，本地大贵族雷文特洛主持王室的农业改革，废除庄园劳役，让佃农逐步走上购地自营之路。

en:
North Jutland wraps around the Limfjord, the sound severing the peninsula's northern tip from the mainland. At its narrowest point stands Aalborg, where traffic crossed between Himmerland and Vendsyssel; by the fifteenth century salted Limfjord herring, Jutish cattle and Norwegian timber passed through a port whose royal trading privileges went back to 1342, with Budolfi Church above the quays. Inland stood Viborg, a bishopric from about 1060 with five monasteries and seat of the Landsting, the assembly where every newly elected Danish king had been approved since the eleventh century; Erik Menved tried to overawe it with a royal castle, but the stronghold was demolished at Christopher II's accession in 1320. In 1444 the province was a Catholic country of herring boats, cattle fairs and wealthy market towns.

Reformation and civil war then struck North Jutland harder than the rest of Denmark. Hans Tausen preached in Viborg in 1525-1529, and a parish church there became the first in Denmark given leave to hold Lutheran services. In 1534 Skipper Clement, a merchant skipper born at Vedsted in Vendsyssel and once vice-admiral to the deposed Christian II, raised the Jutish peasants, who burned the gentry's manor houses. His farmers, stiffened by German landsknechts sent by Count Christopher of Oldenburg, routed the Jutish noble army near Svenstrup on 16 October 1534, leaving fourteen prominent nobles dead. Johan Rantzau's royal army drove him back on Aalborg and stormed the town on 18 December, with as many as 2,000 dead in the sack. Clement was taken at Storvorde a few days later and beheaded, quartered and exposed at the Viborg Landsting in September 1536.

Aalborg then entered its merchant age. The herring-salting monopoly of 1516 and the guild's Hanseatic trade made it the kingdom's second port after Copenhagen by the early seventeenth century; the half-brothers Jørgen Olufsen and Jens Bang raised their sandstone mansions there in 1616 and 1624, and Christian III built Aalborghus Castle around 1550 for his tax collectors. Imperial troops held the town from 1627 to 1629, fire gutted it in 1663, and the Viborg fire of 1726 destroyed the cathedral and most of the old city. In 1814 Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden, and Aalborg lost its three-century-old Norwegian trade.
zh:
北日德兰环抱利姆海峡，这条水道把日德兰半岛北端与大陆隔开。海峡最窄处是奥尔堡，南来北往的人货在此往返于希默兰与温叙塞尔之间；到15世纪，腌制的利姆海峡鲱鱼、日德兰牛和挪威木材经这座港口转运，其王室贸易特权可追溯到1342年，圣布多尔菲教堂就矗立在码头旁。内陆的维堡是更古老的中心：约1060年成为主教驻地，有五座修道院，又是兰斯廷大会的所在地，自11世纪起每位新选丹麦国王都要在这个北日德兰议会上获得认可；埃里克六世曾想用一座王家城堡压服议会，城堡却在1320年克里斯托弗二世继位时被拆毁。1444年，这片省份是天主教的乡土，靠鲱鱼船、牛市和富庶的商业城镇立足。

宗教改革和随之而来的内战，对北日德兰的打击超过丹麦其他地区。1525年至1529年汉斯·陶森在维堡布道，当地一座教区教堂成为丹麦第一所获准举行路德宗礼拜的教堂。1534年，克莱门特船长号召日德兰农民起事：他出生在温叙塞尔的韦兹斯特，曾是被废国王克里斯蒂安二世的海军中将，农民军焚毁贵族庄园，又靠奥尔登堡的克里斯托弗伯爵派来的德意志雇佣兵助阵，于10月16日在斯文斯特鲁普附近击溃日德兰贵族军队，十四名显贵贵族战死。约翰·兰曹率王军把他逼回奥尔堡，12月18日攻破城市，屠城中多达两千人丧生。克莱门特几天后在斯托沃德被俘，1536年9月在维堡兰斯廷大会上被处斩，肢解后悬尸示众。

此后奥尔堡进入商人的年代。1516年的腌鲱鱼垄断权加上行会与汉萨同盟的贸易，使它在17世纪初成为仅次于哥本哈根的王国第二大港；异母兄弟约恩·奥卢夫森和延斯·邦先后在1616年和1624年建起砂岩宅邸，克里斯蒂安三世则在1550年前后为征税官修建奥尔堡城堡。1627年至1629年帝国军队占领城市，1663年大火烧毁大片城区，1726年维堡大火又毁了大教堂和大半个旧城。1814年丹麦将挪威割让给瑞典，奥尔堡随之失去经营三百年的对挪贸易。

en:
Närke is the small inland province of plains and woods between Lake Hjälmaren and Lake Vättern. Its peasants paid grain, butter and pork, and the northern hundreds worked osmund iron for Bergslagen. Örebro grew on a gravel bank where the Svartån could be forded and bridged: roads from Västergötland, Värmland, Bergslagen and the Mälaren basin met there, and Hjälmaren carried boat traffic east. The market held town privileges by 1404, guarded by a royal fortress on an islet in the river, probably raised under Magnus Eriksson in the mid-1300s to gather taxes and hold the western roads; it weathered several sieges. Engelbrekt's rebels took it in 1434, and he held Örebro as a fief until his murder by Måns Bengtsson at Hjälmaren in May 1436. In 1444 this was Catholic Sweden's fortified bridge town on the road into the interior.

Gustav Vasa's men retook Örebro from the Danes on 30 January 1522, and in 1529 the Örebro Synod met there, the first evangelical church assembly in Sweden, though it stopped short of a break with Rome. Under Duke Charles, the future Charles IX, the townsmen received a monopoly of the regional iron trade, shipping Bergslagen iron out and carrying food back to the mines. The medieval keep was rebuilt as a Renaissance castle in 1596–1605, an arms works opened around 1600, and riksdags met at the castle through 1602–1617. Famine and conscription drove about fifteen Närke crofters to the short-lived Morning Star rising of 1653. The town's dynastic moment came in 1810, when the riksdag assembled there elected the French marshal Jean-Baptiste Bernadotte crown prince; he later ruled as Charles XIV John and founded the Bernadotte line of Swedish kings. On 18 July 1812 Britain and Russia concluded their peace treaty in the same town.
zh:
内尔克是耶尔马伦湖与韦特恩湖之间一片不大的内陆省份，多平原与林地。农户缴纳谷物、黄油和猪肉，北部百户区为贝里斯拉根冶奥斯蒙德铁。厄勒布鲁起于斯瓦特河上一处可涉渡、可架桥的砾石滩：西约特兰、韦姆兰、贝里斯拉根和梅拉伦湖区的道路在此相会，耶尔马伦湖又有舟楫东去。这座市集在1404年前已享城市特权，河心小岛上的王家要塞据守着它；要塞可能建于14世纪中期马格努斯·埃里克松在位时，用来征税并控守西行道路，曾顶住数次围攻。1434年，恩厄尔布雷克特的起义军夺取要塞，他本人受封厄勒布鲁，直到1436年5月在耶尔马伦湖畔被贵族芒斯·本特松杀害。1444年，这里是天主教瑞典通往内地道路上一座设防的桥梁城镇。

1522年1月30日，古斯塔夫·瓦萨的部下从丹麦人手中夺回厄勒布鲁；1529年，厄勒布鲁会议在此召开，这是瑞典第一次福音派教会会议，不过尚未与罗马决裂。在后来即位为卡尔九世的卡尔公爵治下，市民取得地区铁业专卖权，把贝里斯拉根的铁运出，再把粮食运回矿区。中世纪主楼在1596至1605年被改建成文艺复兴式城堡，约1600年又兴办兵工厂，1602到1617年间历届议会多次在城堡召开。1653年，荒年和兵役驱使约十五名内尔克佃农发动转瞬即败的晨星起义。1810年，议会在厄勒布鲁推举法国元帅让-巴蒂斯特·贝尔纳多特为王储，他后来即位为卡尔十四世·约翰，开创了瑞典的贝尔纳多特王朝。1812年7月18日，英国与俄国又在同一座城镇签订和约。

en:
New Caledonia centres on Grande Terre, a narrow, mountainous island some 400 kilometres long, ringed by reefs that enclose broad lagoons with deep anchorages; on a south-western peninsula lies the sheltered roadstead of future Nouméa. Lapita potters, makers of dentate-stamped red pottery, reached the Koné coast in the north-west around 1300–200 BC, among the first settlers in the remote Pacific; their descendants, mingled with later Melanesian arrivals, became the Kanak clans. In 1444 the clans fished the lagoon, grew yams on ridge terraces and watered taro in irrigated fields. Authority ran by clan and customary land rather than from any island-wide ruler, while exchange voyages linked neighbouring districts and the outlying islands.

Outside ships found the islands late. On 4 September 1774 James Colnett, aboard HMS Resolution, sighted Grande Terre, and James Cook named it New Caledonia after Caledonia, the Roman name for Scotland; Cook's own father was Scottish. The expedition met Kanaks at Balade and followed the east coast south to the Isle of Pines, at a time when the Kanak population of the islands has been estimated at around 70,000. In 1788 Lapérouse probably examined the west coast shortly before he and his ships vanished. D'Entrecasteaux brought a rescue expedition in 1792–93 and charted stretches of the coast without finding a trace of him. A few more European ships passed in the decades that followed, but through 1821 no fort, mission or trading post stood in the islands, and the future Nouméa roadstead remained Kanak water.
zh:
新喀里多尼亚以格朗德特尔岛为中心，这座狭长多山的大岛长约400公里，四周礁群环抱，潟湖中多可避风浪的深水锚地；岛西南一处半岛外的隐蔽深水区，就是后来努美阿所在的港湾。约在公元前1300年至前200年，制作红色齿纹陶器的拉皮塔陶工抵达岛屿西北的科内海岸，这里是远太平洋最早的人类定居点之一；他们的后人与后来的美拉尼西亚移民融合，形成卡纳克诸氏族。1444年，氏族居民在潟湖捕鱼，在坡垄上种薯蓣，引水浇灌芋艿梯田。社会按氏族和传统领地运行，没有统辖全岛的首领，各地区与外围岛屿之间靠交换航行往来。

外来船只发现这里很晚。1774年9月4日，随「决心号」航行的詹姆斯·科尔内特先望见格朗德特尔岛，詹姆斯·库克随后以苏格兰的拉丁古称喀里多尼亚将其命名为新喀里多尼亚；库克的父亲正是苏格兰人。远征队在巴拉德与卡纳克人接触，再沿东海岸南下到松树岛；据估计当时群岛上约有七万名卡纳克人。1788年，拉彼鲁兹很可能在失踪前不久察看了西海岸。1792年至1793年，当特尔卡斯托率搜救队前来，测绘了部分海岸，却没有找到他的踪迹。此后几十年又有零星欧洲船只经过，但直到1821年，岛上仍没有要塞、传教站或商馆，努美阿外的锚地依旧是卡纳克人的水域。

en:
The Society Islands cross the central South Pacific in two clusters. The Windward group holds Tahiti, the largest of the high islands, and Moʻorea; the Leeward group runs through Raʻiātea, Huahine and Bora Bora. On Raʻiātea stands Taputapuātea, the greatest marae of eastern Polynesia, where priests and voyaging chiefs met for roughly a thousand years; the cult of the god ʻOro, marked by sacred red feathers, spread from there across the ocean. High chiefs claimed descent from the gods and ruled through councils, but no single chief held the whole chain. In 1444 Tahiti, Raʻiātea and Bora Bora were rival chiefdoms whose people shared one language, marriage ties and long canoe voyages.

European ships arrived late. Samuel Wallis landed on Tahiti in 1767 and took it for Britain as King George's Island. Bougainville followed in 1768, and in 1769 Cook set up an observatory at Point Venus to time the transit of Venus, then named the Leeward cluster the Society Islands. Breadfruit, the islanders' staple, drew the Bounty: William Bligh's ship lay here for five months in 1788–89 collecting young breadfruit trees for the West Indies, and the crew's ties with Tahitian women helped bring on the mutiny of April 1789; when HMS Pandora came for the mutineers, fourteen were seized on Tahiti while Fletcher Christian's party hid on Pitcairn. The London Missionary Society landed in 1797 on the Duff and backed the Pōmare chiefs. Pōmare II won the battle of Te Feipī in 1815, and Tahiti and Moʻorea became the core of a Christian kingdom; the missionary William Pascoe Crook laid out Papeete on its sheltered roadstead in 1818. When Pōmare II died in 1821, Raʻiātea, Huahine and Bora Bora remained independent.
zh:
社会群岛横跨南太平洋中部，分为两群。向风群岛以最大的火山岛塔希提和莫雷阿为主，背风群岛由赖阿特阿、胡阿希内、波拉波拉等岛组成。赖阿特阿岛上的塔普塔普阿泰是东波利尼西亚最大的马拉埃，约一千年来一直是祭司和航海酋长集会之地，以神圣红羽为标志的「奥罗」神崇拜也从这里传向周围大洋。大酋长自称神裔，与议事会共同治国，但没有哪位酋长能统有整条岛链。1444年，塔希提、赖阿特阿和波拉波拉分属相互竞争的酋长领地，居民共用一种语言、互通婚姻，并掌握独木舟远航的技艺。

欧洲船来得很晚。1767年，塞缪尔·沃利斯在塔希提登陆，以英王乔治之名把该岛归为英国所有。布干维尔1768年随后来访。1769年，库克在金星角架设观测台测定金星凌日，随后把背风岛群命名为社会群岛。岛民的主食面包树引来了「邦蒂号」：1788至1789年，威廉·布莱的船在此停泊五个月，采集面包树苗运往西印度群岛，船员与塔希提女子结下的关系成为1789年4月哗变的诱因之一；「潘多拉号」后来追捕哗变者，在塔希提抓走十四人，弗莱切·克里斯蒂安一伙则躲到了皮特凯恩岛。1797年，伦敦传道会乘「达夫号」登陆，支持波马雷家族的酋长。波马雷二世1815年在特费皮战役获胜，塔希提和莫雷阿成为一个基督教王国的核心；1818年，传教士威廉·帕斯科·克鲁克在避风锚地旁规划了帕皮提。波马雷二世1821年去世时，赖阿特阿、胡阿希内和波拉波拉仍保持独立。

en:
Rapa Nui is a small triangular volcanic island at the south-eastern edge of Polynesia, and one of the remotest inhabited islands in the Pacific. Polynesian voyagers settled it around 1200, and oral tradition names the chief Hotu Matuʻa as its founder, landing at Anakena on the north coast. The clans carved more than nine hundred moai, the giant stone figures of deified ancestors, mostly between 1250 and 1500. They cut them at the Rano Raraku quarry, hauled them to coastal stone platforms called ahu and set the faces inland over their own clan lands, some crowned with red stone pukao; tradition said the statues walked to their platforms by their own mana. The largest erected, Paro, rose nearly ten metres, and an unfinished figure in the quarry would have reached twenty-one. By 1444 the lineages had formed two rival confederations, the western and northern Tuʻu with their royal Miru line at Anakena, and the eastern ʻOtu ʻItu; chiefs and priests still ordered the raising of statues.

Statue-raising ended as island wars worsened. From about 1680 rival clans toppled one another's images in the huri moʻai, breaking them in the fall to kill the mana they held, and prestige shifted to the bird-man contest at Orongo, where swimmers raced to the islet Motu Nui for the season's first sooty tern egg. On Easter Sunday, 5 April 1722, the Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen became the first European to land, and in a clash on the beach his men shot dead about a dozen islanders; he named the place Easter Island. From 1724 to 1750 the ʻOtu ʻItu fought the Tuʻu for control of the island. A Spanish squadron under Felipe González de Ahedo came in 1770, charted the coast, named the island San Carlos and claimed it for Spain without leaving a garrison. Cook in 1774 found several statues already fallen and, through Hitihiti, a Polynesian from Bora Bora in his crew, learned that the figures commemorated former high chiefs; La Pérouse followed in 1786. In 1821 no European flag yet flew over Rapa Nui, whose clans and bird-man ritual still held local power.
zh:
拉帕努伊是波利尼西亚世界东南尽头一座三角形火山小岛，也是太平洋上最偏远的有人岛之一。波利尼西亚航海者约在1200年定居于此，口传传统说最早率众登岸的是酋长霍图·玛图阿，登陆处在北岸的阿纳基纳。各氏族雕了九百多尊摩艾石像，大多成于1250年至1500年，石像代表被神化的祖先。它们在拉诺拉拉库采石场凿成，被拖到海边称作阿胡的石台上，面朝内陆守望本氏族的土地，有些头顶还加红色石质的普卡奥；岛民相传石像是凭自身神力走到台上的。已立起的最大一尊「帕罗」高近十米，采石场里还有一尊未完工的，若雕成可达二十一米。到1444年，各血缘群体组成两个敌对联盟：西部和北部是图乌，王室米鲁世系以阿纳基纳为中心；东部是奥图伊图。酋长和祭司仍在主持竖立石像。

随着岛上战事加剧，竖石像的时代结束。约从1680年起，敌对氏族互相推倒对方的石像，即「胡里摩艾」，并让石像摔碎以灭其神力，权威转向奥龙戈的鸟人竞赛：参赛者游到莫图努伊小岛，取回当季第一颗乌燕鸥蛋。1722年4月5日复活节，荷兰航海家雅各布·罗赫芬成为第一个登岛的欧洲人，滩头冲突中他的部下开枪打死约十二名岛民，他把该岛命名为复活节岛。1724年至1750年，奥图伊图与图乌为控制全岛交战。1770年，费利佩·冈萨雷斯·德·阿埃多率西班牙舰队到来，测绘海岸，把岛屿命名为圣卡洛斯并宣布归属西班牙，却没有留下驻军。库克1774年再来时，已有几尊石像倾倒，他靠船上一名来自波拉波拉的波利尼西亚人做翻译，得知石像是为纪念历代大酋长而立；拉彼鲁兹1786年随后来访。1821年，拉帕努伊上空还没有任何欧洲旗帜，氏族和鸟人仪式仍掌握着本地权力。

en:
Muʻa faces the eastern lagoon of Tongatapu, its village of Lapaha fronting the water from which Tongan voyaging canoes sailed the central Pacific. Here dwelt the Tuʻi Tonga, sacred king of a maritime polity whose name reached Fiji, Samoa, ʻUvea, Futuna and Niue, and whose chiefs brought tribute at the annual ʻinasi first-fruits ceremony. Around Lapaha rise the langi, royal tombs of coral slabs quarried along the coast, cut to fit with barely a gap and stacked three tiers or more; the greatest were raised for ʻUluakimata Teleʻa. At nearby Heketā stands the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui, a thirteenth-century trilithon of three coral stones; tradition says the hero Maui carried them from ʻUvea in a giant canoe. In 1444 the islands' wealth moved in canoes, fishponds and plantations, and the Tuʻi Tonga still ruled from Lapaha.

Around 1470, after the Tuʻi Tonga Takalaua was murdered by men from ʻUvea and Futuna, his son Kauʻulufonua I made his brother Moʻungāmotuʻa the first Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua, who took the work of government; the Tuʻi Tonga remained a sacred, untouchable figure at Lapaha, his followers the inland-road people and the new court's the low-road people. Around 1600 a third line, the Tuʻi Kanokupolu, arose. The Dutch ship Eendracht made the first recorded European visit in 1616, Abel Tasman called at Tongatapu and Haʻapai in 1643, and James Cook, entertained at an ʻinasi in 1773, named Tonga the Friendly Islands. In April 1799 Fīnau ʻUlukālala II's faction killed the harsh Tuʻi Kanokupolu Tukuʻaho at the ʻinasi in Muʻa, opening fifty years of civil war. In 1806 Fīnau's men seized the British ship Port-au-Prince at Lifuka in Haʻapai; twenty-two of its twenty-six crew were killed, and fourteen-year-old clerk William Mariner was spared. He spent four years at Fīnau's court as Toki ʻUkamea, the Iron Axe, and his dictated account of 1818 is the chief European record of pre-Christian Tonga. Fīnau used the ship's cannon against Nukuʻalofa's fortress in 1807, and after his death in 1809 Haʻapai and Vavaʻu broke away under his son. In 1821 Muʻa kept its sacred king, but rival chiefs held the power.
zh:
姆阿位于汤加塔布岛东侧潟湖畔，其中的拉帕哈村临水而立，汤加人的远洋独木舟正是从这片水域驶往中太平洋。图伊汤加，即神圣的汤加之王，就驻跸在拉帕哈；这个海上政权的声名远及斐济、萨摩亚、乌韦阿、富图纳和纽埃，各岛首领每年在「伊纳西」初果礼上进贡。拉帕哈一带耸立着朗吉王陵：沿海采来的珊瑚石板被切割得彼此几乎严丝合缝，垒成三层或更多层级，最大的几座为图伊汤加乌鲁阿基马塔·特雷阿所建。附近赫克塔的哈阿蒙加·阿毛伊是一座由三块珊瑚石搭成的三石门，建于13世纪；相传英雄毛伊把这些石头用大独木舟从乌韦阿运来。1444年，群岛的财富随独木舟、鱼塘和种植园流转，图伊汤加仍在拉帕哈发号施令。

约1470年，图伊汤加塔卡拉瓦被来自乌韦阿和富图纳的人刺杀，他的儿子考乌卢丰阿一世把日常政务交给弟弟蒙加莫图阿，即第一代图伊哈塔卡拉瓦；图伊汤加留在拉帕哈，成为神圣而不可触碰的人物，他的从属称「内陆路人」，新朝廷的人则称「低路人」。1600年前后，第三支王族图伊卡诺库珀鲁兴起。荷兰船「团结号」（Eendracht）1616年最早留下欧洲人到访的记录，1643年亚伯·塔斯曼到访汤加塔布和哈阿派，1773年詹姆斯·库克在「伊纳西」礼上受款待，把汤加称作友谊群岛。1799年4月，菲瑙·乌卢卡拉拉二世一派趁「伊纳西」礼在姆阿刺杀了暴虐的图伊卡诺库珀鲁图库阿霍，开启约五十年的内战。1806年，菲瑙的人在哈阿派的利富卡夺下英国船「太子港号」，二十六名船员中有二十二人被杀，十四岁的文书威廉·马里纳获免。他在菲瑙的宫廷住了四年，得名托基·乌卡梅阿，意为「铁斧」；他口述的见闻1818年成书，是欧洲人记载基督教传入前汤加的主要文献。1807年，菲瑙用船上的火炮攻打努库阿洛法要塞；他1809年死后，哈阿派和瓦瓦乌在其子治下脱离汤加塔布。1821年，姆阿仍住着神圣的国王，实权却在相互争战的首领手里。

en:
Tuvalu is a string of nine low islands, three reef islands and six atolls, scattered across the central South Pacific with hundreds of kilometres of open sea between them, yet holding barely twenty-five square kilometres of land in all. Polynesian voyagers out of the Samoa-Tonga sphere settled eight of them, which gives the group its name: Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', and Niulakita stood outside that older pattern. Communities lived from coconuts, fish and the reef, sailing canoes linked atoll with atoll and ran on to Samoa and Tonga, and the founding ancestor of Niutao, Funafuti and Vaitupu is said to have come from Samoa while Nanumea's came from Tonga. Islanders told of the Eel and the Flounder, who made the islands: the flounder gave the atolls their flat shape, the eel became the model of the coconut palm. In 1444 the group appeared on no European chart.

Álvaro de Mendaña made the first recorded European contact on 16 January 1568, when he sighted Nui and charted it as Isla de Jesús without landing; on his second Pacific voyage he passed Niulakita in 1595 and named it La Solitaria. Other Spanish and British navigators crossed the neighbouring waters in the centuries that followed, but few made out the group clearly and none came ashore. In May 1819 Arent Schuyler de Peyster, an American sailing the British brig Rebecca, named Funafuti Ellice's Island after Edward Ellice, member of Parliament for Coventry and owner of the ship's cargo, and hydrographers extended the name to the whole archipelago. Through 1821 contact stayed brief and accidental, and no European had settled on any of the nine islands.
zh:
图瓦卢由九座低矮岛屿组成，三座礁岛、六个环礁散落在南太平洋中部，岛与岛之间隔着数百公里海面，全部陆地加起来不过25平方公里。波利尼西亚航海者从萨摩亚、汤加一带出发，在其中八座岛上定居，群岛之名即来源于此：「图瓦卢」意为「八座并肩而立」，尼乌拉基塔不在其列。各社群以椰子、渔获和珊瑚礁为生，独木舟往来于各环礁之间，远航可至萨摩亚和汤加；纽陶、富纳富提和瓦伊图普的始祖相传来自萨摩亚，纳诺梅阿的始祖则来自汤加。岛民相传鳗鱼与比目鱼造了这些岛屿：比目鱼化出环礁的平坦形状，鳗鱼化作椰子树的原型。1444年时，欧洲人的海图上还没有这组群岛。

1568年1月16日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚完成了有记载的第一次欧洲接触：他望见努伊，标为「耶稣岛」，但没有登陆；第二次远航太平洋时，他又在1595年经过尼乌拉基塔，命名为「孤岛」。此后几个世纪里也有西班牙和英国航海家经过附近海域，但少有人看清这组群岛，更无人登岸。1819年5月，驾驶英国双桅船「丽贝卡」号的美国人阿伦特·斯凯勒·德佩斯特把富纳富提命名为埃利斯岛，名字来自考文垂议员、船货的主人爱德华·埃利斯，后来的海图编制者又把这个名称扩及整个群岛。直到1821年，接触仍短暂而偶然，九座岛上没有一个欧洲人定居。

en:
Tarawa is an atoll of the Tungaru or Gilbert chain, its islets strung around a broad lagoon with one unusually wide ship passage; the name Tarawa means that passage in Gilbertese. In the islanders' creation story the spider god Nareau divided sky from sea and left Tarawa as the first land. Gilbertese seafarers settled the chain by about 200 BC, sailing between atolls in canoes they built themselves and steering by the stars and the shape of the swells. Tarawa had no permanent chiefs: elder councils and the descent groups holding each strip of land ran the villages, which lived on lagoon fish, coconuts, pandanus and swamp taro. In 1444 its people were tied to neighbouring atolls by marriage, feud and voyaging, and no European had yet come near.

Pedro Fernandes de Queiros sighted the northern atolls of Butaritari and Makin in 1606, and John Byron anchored off Nikunau in 1765. On 20 June 1788 Thomas Gilbert, master of the East India Company ship Charlotte, reached Tarawa and gave Europeans their first description of it without landing; he named an islet Matthew Island and the lagoon Charlotte Bay. Charlotte, sailing in company with John Marshall's Scarborough, was a storeship of the British First Fleet, bound from Botany Bay to Guangzhou for tea after landing her convicts. In 1799 the whaler Ann and Hope called at Nikunau, the first of that trade, and in 1820 Adam Johann von Krusenstern gave the whole chain Gilbert's name. No foreign administration followed.
zh:
塔拉瓦是通加鲁（吉尔伯特）群岛中的一座环礁，小岛环列在宽阔潟湖四周，中间有一条异常宽大的航道，塔拉瓦的名字在吉尔伯特语中就是「航道」的意思。岛民的创世故事里，蜘蛛神纳雷阿乌（Nareau）分开天与海，把塔拉瓦留作最初的陆地。吉尔伯特航海者约在公元前200年已定居这串群岛，他们驾驶自造独木舟往来各环礁，凭星象和涌浪的形状掌舵。塔拉瓦没有世袭首领，长老议事会和掌握各条土地的世系群管理各村，村人以潟湖渔获、椰子、露兜树和沼泽芋为生。1444年，婚姻、仇怨和航行把他们和邻近环礁连在一起，欧洲人还不曾靠近这里。

1606年，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·奎罗斯望见群岛北部的布塔里塔里和马金；1765年，约翰·拜伦在尼库瑙外海停泊。1788年6月20日，东印度公司商船「夏洛特号」船长托马斯·吉尔伯特抵达塔拉瓦，首次向欧洲人描述这座环礁，但没有登岛，只把一座小岛命名为马修岛、把潟湖命名为夏洛特湾。「夏洛特号」和约翰·马歇尔的「斯卡伯勒号」同为英国第一舰队的运输船，遣送流放犯人后由植物学湾驶往广州贩茶。1799年，捕鲸船「安与霍普号」停靠尼库瑙，是这行生意的第一艘；1820年，亚当·约翰·冯·克鲁森施滕以吉尔伯特的姓氏命名整个群岛，外来统治却没有随之而来。

en:
Nauru, Naoero in its own language, is a small raised coral island far out in the central Pacific, hundreds of kilometres from its nearest neighbour. Long isolation gave the islanders a language of their own and a society of twelve clans, each tracing descent through the mother's line. They farmed fish as well as the land: families caught juvenile milkfish, acclimatised them to fresh water and raised them in the sheltered Buada Lagoon, with coconuts and pandanus fruit to fill out the diet. In 1444 the reef, lagoon and clan lands were run entirely by Nauruans, and no outside power held any part of the island.

The first European sighting came in 1798, when the British captain John Fearn sailed past in the trading ship Hunter and named the place Pleasant Island for its green, attractive appearance; he did not stay. Ships remained rare for decades afterwards, and through 1821 the island had neither a European resident nor any foreign fort, mission or store.
zh:
瑙鲁在本族语中称诺埃罗，是中太平洋一座隆起的珊瑚小岛，离最近的邻岛也有数百公里。漫长的孤立让岛民发展出自己的语言，社会分为十二个氏族，血统都按母系追溯。岛民既种地也养鱼：各家捕捞幼虱目鱼，让它们适应淡水，养在受遮蔽的布阿达潟湖里，再以椰子和露兜树果实补足口粮。1444年时，珊瑚礁、潟湖和氏族土地全由瑙鲁人自己管理，岛上没有任何外来势力的据点。

欧洲人第一次望见瑙鲁是在1798年：英国船长约翰·费恩乘商船「猎手」号经过，见岛上葱翠好看，取名快乐岛，却没有停留。此后几十年里船只仍很少见，直到1821年，岛上既没有欧洲居民，也没有外人修筑的要塞、传教站或商号。

en:
The Marshalls are twenty-nine coral atolls in two parallel chains: Ratak, the sunrise chain, and Ralik, the sunset chain. Majuro, the capital, is sixty-four islets around a lagoon of nearly 300 square kilometres. Early settlers brought coconuts, breadfruit, giant swamp taro and chickens; the wetter southern atolls grew taro and breadfruit for sizeable villages, while the drier north lived mainly on pandanus and coconuts. Marshallese sailors crossed open water in walap canoes sewn from breadfruit planks with coconut fibre, finding atolls below the horizon by reading how swells bent around their reefs. Stick charts mapped those swell patterns, but they were teaching aids and were left ashore before a voyage. Land belonged to chiefs called iroij, and each chain answered to a paramount iroijlaplap. In 1444 tattooed Marshallese lived under this order with no outsider in their waters.

Spain found the islands early and then kept away. In 1526 Alonso de Salazar, in the one surviving ship of the Loaisa expedition, sighted a northern atoll, probably Taongi, and named it San Bartolome, but strong currents stopped him landing and he sailed on to Guam. Alvaro de Saavedra went ashore in 1528 on an uninhabited atoll and met tattooed islanders, whom the Spanish called Los Pintados; in 1565 the pilot Lope Martin, after seizing the San Jeronimo in a mutiny, was retaken at Ujelang and marooned there with twenty-six men. The Manila galleons then used a sea lane farther north and provisioned at Guam. Contact resumed only in 1788, when John Marshall and Thomas Gilbert, bound from Botany Bay to Guangzhou in their First Fleet ships, traded peacefully at Mili. When Otto von Kotzebue arrived in 1817 he found thatched huts, woven mats and the rule of the iroij almost untouched.
zh:
马绍尔群岛由二十九座珊瑚环礁组成，排成平行的两串礁链：拉塔克意为日出，拉利克意为日落。首府马久罗由六十四座小岛围出近300平方公里的潟湖。早期定居者带来了椰子、面包果、大沼泽芋和鸡；湿润的南部环礁种沼泽芋和面包果，养出较大的村落，干旱的北部主要靠露兜树和椰子过活。马绍尔水手驾驶瓦拉普独木舟远渡大洋，船板取自面包果树，用椰壳纤维绳缝成；他们辨认涌浪绕过礁体后的折转，找出地平线以下的环礁。木棒海图标出涌浪的格局，但那只是教学用具，出海时留在岸上。土地归于称作伊罗伊杰（iroij）的酋长，每条礁链又各有一位最高酋长伊罗伊杰拉普拉普（iroijlaplap）。1444年，纹面的马绍尔人在这套秩序下生活，海域里还没有外人。

西班牙人早早发现了这片群岛，之后却一直避而远之。1526年，洛艾萨远征队唯一幸存船上的阿隆索·德·萨拉萨尔望见北部一座环礁，可能是塔翁吉，将其命名为圣巴托洛缪，但海流使他无法靠岸，只得继续驶往关岛。1528年，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉登上一座无人环礁，遇见纹身的岛民，西班牙人把他们叫作洛斯平塔多斯，意为画身之人。1565年，领航员洛佩·马丁发动哗变夺取「圣赫罗尼莫号」，后来在乌杰朗被夺回，他和二十六名同伙被遗弃在岛上。此后马尼拉大帆船只走更北的航道，在关岛补给。再接触要等到1788年，约翰·马歇尔和托马斯·吉尔伯特乘第一舰队的船从植物学湾驶往广州，在米利环礁与岛民和平交易。1817年奥托·冯·科策布抵达时，看到的还是茅屋、草席和伊罗伊杰的统治，几乎没有变化。

en:
Wake is a waterless coral atoll north of the Marshalls, three islets around a shallow lagoon, with Utirik, the nearest inhabited island, almost 1,000 kilometres away. Archaeologists have found no ancient artifacts there, but the Polynesian rat reached it somehow, and Marshallese tradition tells of Anen Kio, the island of the kio flower, where canoe parties from the southern atolls hunted seabirds and gathered albatross bones to use in tattooing. It was a hunting ground, not a home. In 1444 Wake was uninhabited, but Marshallese pilots still knew the way there.

Alvaro de Mendana de Neira made the first recorded sighting on 2 October 1568, sailing north after the Solomon Islands; on the eve of the feast of Saint Francis he named it San Francisco, and his log describes a low barren ring with seabirds and bushes but no coconuts. James Cook later tried to re-find the island from Mendana's figures and reached the Hawaiian Islands instead. Captain Samuel Wake of the merchant ship Prince William Henry came upon the atoll in 1796 and left it his name, and Charles William Barkley of the fur brig Halcyon arrived soon after to name it Halcyon Island independently. Through 1821 no power occupied Wake or built on its reef.
zh:
威克是马绍尔群岛以北一座没有淡水的珊瑚环礁，三座小岛围着浅水潟湖，最近的有人岛乌蒂里克也在近1000公里之外。考古学家没有在岛上发现古代遗物，波利尼西亚鼠却不知怎么上了岸；马绍尔人的口传里有一座基奥花之岛（Anen Kio），南部环礁的独木舟队渡海到那里捕猎海鸟，收集信天翁的骨头用作纹身器具。那里是猎场，不是家园。1444年的威克无人居住，马绍尔领航员却仍认得去那里的航路。

1568年10月2日，阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚·德·内拉离开所罗门群岛北航时首次有文字记载地望见威克；那天是圣方济各节前夕，他把岛命名为圣弗朗西斯科，航海日志里写的是一座低平贫瘠的环状岛，只有海鸟和灌木，没有椰子。后来詹姆斯·库克拿着门达纳的数据重新寻找这座岛，反而找到了夏威夷群岛。1796年，商船「威廉·亨利王子号」船长塞缪尔·威克途经这座环礁，以自己的姓氏命名；不久后毛皮贸易双桅船「哈尔西恩号」的查尔斯·威廉·巴克利也到了这里，在不知情的情况下另起名哈尔西恩岛。直到1821年，仍没有任何势力占领威克或在礁上营建。

en:
Pohnpei is a high volcanic island in the eastern Carolines, ringed by a reef and lagoon and drenched by some of the heaviest rainfall on earth. In 1444 it was the seat of the Saudeleur dynasty, which had united the island under one court at Nan Madol, off the eastern shore. The capital stood on 92 artificial islets between the coast and Temwen Island, its platforms and walls of columnar basalt divided by tidal canals; later visitors called it the Venice of the Pacific. Its name means 'within the intervals', and older tradition named it Soun Nan-leng, the Reef of Heaven. Pohnpeian legend credits twin sorcerers, Olisihpa and Olosohpa, with levitating the basalt logs with the help of a flying dragon, and Olosohpa became the first Saudeleur. Five tribes were each led by two principal chiefs, and tribute, raiding and banishment upheld chiefly power over an island of perhaps 25,000 people. No European chart yet marked Pohnpei.

The later Saudeleur were remembered as harsh and greedy rulers who offended the island's gods. About 1628 a semi-mythical invader, Isokelekel, overthrew them, kept Nan Madol for a time, and bequeathed the more decentralized nahnmwarki chiefships to his successors, who abandoned the stone city to the tides. Spanish ships had already sighted Pohnpei: on 14 September 1529 Álvaro de Saavedra charted it as San Bartolomé and named the surrounding islands Los Pintados, the Painted Ones, for their tattooed people, and on 23 December 1595 Pedro Fernandes de Queirós passed without landing. No foreign post followed, and in 1821 the island still answered to its own chiefs and the flooded ruins of their royal city.
zh:
波纳佩是东加罗林群岛的一座火山岛，四周环着礁盘与潟湖，山区年雨量居全球前列。1444年时，全岛处在绍德雷尔王朝治下，王朝以东岸外的南马都为唯一的朝廷。这座都城建在海岸与泰蒙岛之间的92座人工小岛上，玄武岩石柱垒起的台地和石墙被潮汐运河分隔，后人常称它为「太平洋的威尼斯」。「南马都」意为「间隔之间」，更古老的名字叫「天堂之礁」。波纳佩传说，两位孪生术士靠一条飞龙把巨石凌空运到工地，两兄弟中的一位后来成为第一位绍德雷尔。全岛分五个部落，各由两名大首领统领，约两万五千岛民靠贡赋、袭掠和放逐维系首领的权威。此时欧洲人的海图上还没有波纳佩。

后来的绍德雷尔在传说中横征暴敛、冒犯岛神。约1628年，半神话的外来者伊索克勒克推翻王朝，他一度留居南马都，后人改行更为分权的南姆瓦尔基首领制，把这座石城弃给潮水。西班牙船只此前已经望见此岛：1529年9月14日，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉把它标为圣巴托洛梅，又因岛民纹身，把周围岛屿命名为洛斯平塔多斯，即「画身人」；1595年12月23日，佩德罗·费尔南德斯·德·基罗斯经过而未登陆。欧洲人没有随后设立据点，到1821年，波纳佩仍听命于本地首领和他们那座任潮水漫过的石城废墟。

en:
Palau's western Carolinian group centres on Babeldaob, a high volcanic island facing the smaller, crowded island of Koror across a narrow channel. Austronesian seafarers had settled its coasts by the last millennium BC, and over the centuries they cut hillside terraces, raised basalt and coral platforms, and linked compact villages with stone paths. Every village turned on its painted bai, the meeting house whose beams carried its people's stories. The caves of southern Babeldaob and northern Koror held crystalline limestone, and Yapese canoe expeditions crossed 400 kilometres of ocean to quarry it. They shaped the stone into disks, the biggest 3.6 metres across and four tonnes in weight, and towed them home on bamboo rafts along a current route of more than 1,000 kilometres. These rai stones were Yap's ceremonial wealth, and even a disk lost at sea kept its value, because ownership lived in the oral record rather than in the stone itself; Yapese tradition sends the discoverer Anagumang south from Yap on a god's bidding five or six centuries before. In 1444 Palauan chiefs and villages ruled themselves.

Europeans were slow to reach the islands. The Spanish expedition of Ruy López de Villalobos may have sighted them in 1543, though historians dispute the identification. After Palauan castaways reached Samar in 1696, a map they helped compose brought Jesuit missions to the islands, and the mission of 1710 ended with two priests killed on Sonsorol. Sustained contact began with a shipwreck. In 1783 the East India Company packet Antelope grounded off Ulong, and Captain Henry Wilson's crew spent three months among the Palauans before making their way home. Wilson took with him Lee Boo, second son of Abba Thulle, the ruler of Koror. The young man reached London in 1784, went to school with the Wilsons and was feted by society, but smallpox killed him that December at the age of twenty, and he was buried at Rotherhithe. Wilson's journals, edited by George Keate as An Account of the Pelew Islands, went through more than twenty translations. No power had posted a garrison here by 1821.
zh:
帕劳群岛位于加罗林群岛西端，主岛巴伯尔道布是一座火山岛，与狭小而人烟稠密的科罗尔岛只隔一道窄水道。南岛语族航海者至迟在公元前一千纪已定居海岸；此后许多世纪里，他们开辟山坡梯田，垒筑玄武岩和珊瑚石台地，用石路串起紧凑的村落，每个村落都围着绘满图画的会所运转，梁上画着本族人的故事。巴伯尔道布南部和科罗尔北部的洞穴出产晶质石灰岩，雅浦人的独木舟队横渡四百公里海面来此采石，凿成圆盘，最大的直径3.6米、重四吨，再用竹筏顺洋流拖回一千多公里外的雅浦。这种石币是雅浦人的礼仪财富，就连在海上失踪的圆盘也照样有价值，因为所有权记在口述传承里，不在石头本身；雅浦传说，五六百年前一支探险队受神祇指引南行，发现了帕劳的采石场。1444年时，帕劳由本地首领和村落自治。

欧洲人来得很慢。鲁伊·洛佩斯·德比利亚洛沃斯的西班牙船队可能在1543年望见群岛，但后人对这一辨认仍有争议。1696年帕劳漂流者抵达萨马岛，他们协助绘制的地图引来耶稣会传教团，1710年的传教却以两名神父在松索罗尔被杀告终。持续接触始于一场沉船：1783年，东印度公司邮船「羚羊号」在乌龙附近搁浅，亨利·威尔逊船长的部下与帕劳人共处三个月后启程返航。威尔逊带走了科罗尔统治者阿巴·图勒的次子李布。年轻人1784年抵达伦敦，在威尔逊家上学，受到社交界追捧，却在当年12月死于天花，年仅二十，葬在罗瑟希思。威尔逊的航海日记由乔治·基特整理成书，先后译成二十多种文字。到1821年，还没有任何强国在此驻军。

en: Midway is a small atoll at the remote north-western end of the Hawaiian chain, where Sand, Eastern and Spit islands make a rough, incomplete ring around a sheltered lagoon. Hawaiian names for the place are Kuaihelani, 'backbone of heaven', and Pihemanu, 'the loud din of birds', but the islets never held a permanent settlement: no chief, marae, village or fishing fleet was based here, and the Hawaiian voyaging world centred on the larger islands far to the south-east. In 1444 the beaches were left to albatrosses, monk seals and turtles. No European or American ship is known to have entered the lagoon in the whole 1444-1821 period, and Midway stayed an unoccupied anchorage without a colonial claim or resident people, its reef absent from every chart.
zh: 中途岛是夏威夷岛链西北端的偏远小环礁，沙岛、东岛和斯皮特岛在潟湖周围围出不完整的圆环。夏威夷人以Kuaihelani（意为「天之脊梁」）和Pihemanu（「群鸟喧闹」）称呼这里，但岛上从无永久定居点：没有酋长、马拉埃、村落或渔船队，夏威夷人的航海世界以东南方远处的大岛为中心。1444年，海滩交给信天翁、僧海豹和海龟。1444年至1821年间，没有任何有记载的欧洲或美洲船只进入这片潟湖，中途岛始终是无人占据、也无殖民宣称的锚地，所有海图上都找不到它的礁群。

en:
Christmas Island is a steep, forested island south of Java, its central plateau ending in sheer sea cliffs. Seabirds nest on the rocks and red crabs share the monsoon forest, but in 1444 no people lived there: the island had no harbour, no ruler and no settled anchorage, and it lay well off the sailing routes between the Indies and the Indian Ocean.

Europeans found it late and only passed it by. Captain William Mynors of the East India Company ship Royal Mary named it on Christmas Day 1643, and Dutch charts soon carried it under the label Mony. In March 1688 the English navigator William Dampier, aboard the Cygnet, was blown east while making for the Cocos Islands from New Holland; two of his crew waded ashore at the Dales on the west coast, the first recorded landing, and Dampier found the island empty. Later captains did no more than add soundings and sightings. Through 1821 Christmas Island had neither settlers nor administration, and belonged to nobody.
zh:
圣诞岛是爪哇以南一座陡峭的林木之岛，中部高原尽头是直插海面的悬崖。海鸟在岩礁上筑巢，红蟹栖息在季风雨林中，但1444年岛上无人居住：没有港口，没有统治者，也没有可用的锚地，整座岛远离东印度与印度洋之间的航线。

欧洲人很晚才发现它，又都从海上掠过。1643年圣诞节，东印度公司船只「皇家玛丽号」船长威廉·迈纳斯为它命名，荷兰海图很快以「莫尼」之名把它标入图中。1688年3月，英国航海家威廉·丹皮尔乘「西格尼特号」从新荷兰前往科科斯群岛途中被风吹向东面，两名船员在西岸的戴尔斯涉水登岛，这是最早有记录的登岛，丹皮尔看到的只是一座荒岛。此后的船长至多补充几处测深和目击记录。直到1821年，圣诞岛仍没有定居者，没有官府，不属于任何人。

en:
The Cocos, or Keeling, Islands are two low coral atolls in the open Indian Ocean: the single island of North Keeling and a horseshoe-shaped southern atoll around a lagoon, twenty-seven islets in all. Coconut palms and seabird colonies had the low beaches to themselves. In 1444 the islands had no people, no ruler and no port, and they lay south of the ordinary sailing tracks between Sumatra and India.

Captain William Keeling of the East India Company sighted them in 1609 on a voyage home from the Indies, and the group took his name. The islands were hard even to find: in 1688 William Dampier, sailing from New Holland, meant to make the Cocos but was blown off to Christmas Island instead. A Swedish captain sketched North Keeling in 1749 and British hydrographers later put the atolls on their charts, but no trader or planter came ashore to stay before 1821. The islets remained uninhabited through the whole period.
zh:
科科斯岛（科科斯〔基林〕群岛）是开阔印度洋上的两座低矮珊瑚环礁：一座是单独的北基林岛，一座是马蹄形、围着潟湖的南环礁，共27座小岛。低矮海滩上只有椰林和海鸟群落。1444年，岛上没有人、没有统治者，也没有港口，位置偏在苏门答腊与印度之间的常用航线以南。

1609年，东印度公司船长威廉·基林从东印度返航时望见这组群岛，群岛便以他的名字命名。要找到它还得凭运气：1688年，威廉·丹皮尔从新荷兰出航，目标本是科科斯，却被风吹到了圣诞岛。1749年一名瑞典船长画下北基林岛，英国水文师后来把环礁绘入海图，但直到1821年也没有商人或种植园主上岸长住。在这一时期里，这些小岛始终无人居住。

en:
The Galápagos are a group of arid volcanic islands straddling the equator, roughly 900 kilometres west of the South American coast. Most shores offer little fresh water, yet giant tortoises, marine iguanas and seabirds bred there in vast numbers, and the archipelago took its name from the tortoises the Spaniards called galápagos. No grave, building or permanent camp has been found to prove pre-Columbian settlement: a Spanish chronicler claimed Túpac Inca Yupanqui had visited the islands, but the Incas were not deep-sea sailors and the story is generally treated as legend. In 1444 the islands were uninhabited, hidden so often by fog that early Spaniards called them the Encantadas, the enchanted isles.

They enter written history by accident. On 10 March 1535 Tomás de Berlanga, Bishop of Panama, was sailing to Peru to settle the quarrel between Francisco Pizarro and Diego de Almagro when calms in the doldrums drove his ship off course; the crew ran so short of water that two men and ten horses died, and the survivors chewed cactus pads to stay alive. Berlanga sent his account to Charles V, and maps by Ortelius and Mercator marked the islands around 1570 as the Turtle Islands. From Richard Hawkins's call in 1593, English pirates used the coves to lie in wait for Peruvian treasure ships. William Ambrosia Cowley charted the chain in 1684 and gave sixteen islands their English names, and the goats his kind of visitors left behind overran several of them. After James Colnett surveyed the islands in 1793, whalers anchored here to provision, stacking live tortoises in the holds because the animals survived for months without food or water, and crews left letters in a barrel on Floreana for any passing ship to carry home. Through 1821 no power had planted a lasting colony.
zh:
加拉帕戈斯群岛是横亘赤道的干旱火山群岛，在南美洲海岸以西约九百公里的大洋中。多数岸边几乎没有淡水，大海龟、海鬣蜥和海鸟却成群繁衍，群岛的名字就来自西班牙人对龟的称呼「galápago」。没有发现墓葬、建筑或长期营地能证明哥伦布到来之前有人定居：曾有西班牙编年史家声称图帕克·印卡·尤潘基到过群岛，但印加人并不远海航船，此说通常被当作传说。1444年时群岛无人居住，还常被海雾遮蔽，早期西班牙人叫它「恩坎塔达斯」，意为魔幻之岛。

群岛进入文字记载纯属偶然。1535年3月10日，巴拿马主教托马斯·德·贝兰加乘船前往秘鲁，调解弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗与迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的争端，船在赤道无风带遇滞风偏航；淡水耗尽，两名船员和十匹马渴死，余下的人靠嚼仙人掌叶片活命。贝兰加把见闻呈报查理五世，奥特柳斯和墨卡托1570年前后的地图把这里标作「龟岛」。1593年理查德·霍金斯到访后，英国海盗常借这些海湾潜伏，袭掠从秘鲁运金银回国的西班牙宝船。1684年，威廉·安布罗斯·考利测绘群岛，给十六座岛取了英文名，海盗留下的山羊后来在好几座岛上泛滥。1793年詹姆斯·科尔内特考察之后，捕鲸船到此补给，把活海龟堆在船舱里，因为这种动物不吃不喝也能活几个月；船员还把信件放在弗洛雷阿纳岛的一只木桶里，托过路船捎回家。直到1821年，没有任何政权在这里建立持久殖民地。

en:
The Ktunaxa hold the valley of the Kootenay River and the forests around Kootenay Lake, in the long trench between the Rockies and the ranges to their west. Their speech is a language isolate, with no proven kin to any neighbour's. The bands moved with the seasons, taking fish with traps and weirs and hunting deer, bear and waterfowl, and they travelled the waterways in a light bark canoe of a distinctive sturgeon-nosed design that neighbouring groups also used. The upper bands crossed the Rockies each summer to run bison on the plains and fought the Blackfoot over hunting grounds; their portable tipis and summer Sun Dance had more in common with plains peoples than with the coast. In 1444 no European had yet seen these mountains.

Smallpox crossed the passes ahead of the traders, carried back by bands returning from the plains, and thinned the parties that hunted east of the mountains. The Ktunaxa first appear on a European chart on Alexander Mackenzie's map of about 1793. In 1807 David Thompson sent Jaco Finlay to build Kootanae House near where Toby Creek joins the Columbia, the North West Company's first post in the Columbia Basin and Thompson's base for his later surveys of the region. Ktunaxa bands brought their furs there until Peigan war parties closed the Howse Pass route from the plains, and the post was abandoned in 1812.
zh:
克图纳哈人（Ktunaxa，即库特奈人）的家园在库特内河河谷与库特内湖周围的山林，地处落基山脉和西侧群山之间那条长长的地沟。他们的语言是孤立语言，与四邻的语言都没有确证的亲缘。各部随季节迁徙，用鱼梁和陷阱捕鱼，猎鹿、猎熊、猎水禽，水上往来乘坐一种轻便的树皮独木舟，船头做成独特的鲟鱼鼻式样，邻近各族也有使用。上游群体每年夏天翻过落基山到平原围猎野牛，为猎场与黑脚人交战；他们便于搬移的梯皮帐篷和夏日太阳舞，与平原各族的共同点比与海岸各族更多。1444年，还没有欧洲人见过这片群山。

天花赶在商人之前翻过山口，被从平原归来的队伍带回，使东猎的部落人口锐减。克图纳哈人第一次出现在欧洲人的地图上，是约1793年亚历山大·麦肯齐绘制的地图。1807年，戴维·汤普森派雅科·芬利在托比溪汇入哥伦比亚河处附近建起库特奈商站，这是西北公司在哥伦比亚河流域的第一处商站，也是汤普森后来测绘这一带的基地。克图纳哈各部把毛皮带到这里交易，直到皮甘武士从平原方向封锁了豪斯山口通道，商站于1812年被放弃。

en:
The Kainaa, 'Many Chiefs' in the Blackfoot tongue, hold the shortgrass plains between the Bow and Oldman rivers, with the Belly and St. Mary watering their camps. Their Plains Cree enemies called them mihkowiyiniw, 'stained with blood', which English traders shortened to the Blood. With the Siksika and Piikani they make up the Niitsitapi, the Blackfoot Confederacy. In 1444 they had neither horses nor guns. Bands of ten to thirty lodges wintered in wooded valleys and gathered each summer as the chokecherries ripened for the Okan, the Sun Dance, and for great communal bison drives: hunters ran the herds into pounds and over cliffs, women dried the meat with berries into pemmican, and men made their names in the warrior societies. Bulls' tongues were the delicacy offered at the ceremony.

Horses reached the Niitsitapi around 1730, called ponokamita or 'elk dogs', and the mounted Kainaa soon raided south against the Shoshone, overrunning most of their range within two generations. In the autumn of 1754 Anthony Henday of the Hudson's Bay Company reached a great Blackfoot camp after nearly 3,000 kilometres by canoe and 1,400 on foot, and invited its chiefs to carry furs to the bay. They refused: the road ran through Cree and Assiniboine country. The trade came to them instead, as company posts rose along the North Saskatchewan on the edge of their range, where Kainaa parties brought pemmican and bison robes rather than beaver.
zh:
凯纳（Kainaa，中文维基译盖恩纳）在黑脚语中意为「众酋长」，据有弓河与奥尔德曼河之间的短草平原，贝尔河与圣玛丽河滋养着他们的营地。仇敌平原克里人叫他们 mihkowiyiniw，意为「染血之人」，英国商人简称为「血部落」。他们与西格西卡人、皮卡尼人合称尼特西塔皮，即黑脚联盟。1444年时，他们既没有马，也没有火器：十来座到三十座帐篷组成的小队在林木河谷过冬；夏天稠李成熟，全族聚集，举行奥肯节（太阳舞），并展开大规模集体围猎：猎人把牛群赶入围栅、逼下悬崖，妇女把肉和浆果晒成肉糜饼，男子则在战士会社中挣得名声。牛舌是祭典上敬献的珍馐。

约1730年，马传到尼特西塔皮人这里，他们称之为 ponokamita，意为「麋狗」。骑上马背的凯纳人很快南下攻掠肖肖尼人，不过两代人便夺占其大部分游猎地。1754年秋，哈得孙湾公司的安东尼·亨德先乘独木舟走了近三千公里、再徒步一千四百公里，抵达一座庞大的黑脚营地，邀请酋长们把毛皮运到哈得孙湾交易。酋长们拒绝了：去海湾的路要穿过克里人和阿西尼博因人的地盘。后来贸易主动找上门来，公司在他们游猎范围北缘的北萨斯喀彻温河畔设起商栈；凯纳人拿去交易的多是肉糜饼和野牛皮袍，河狸皮反倒很少。

en:
Assapasca is the aspen parkland between the Touchwood Hills and the Qu'Appelle River, where aspen groves and pothole lakes break the grassland as the boreal forest gives way to open plains. In 1444 no towns or posts stood here. Small bands on foot, the people later recorded as Cree and Assiniboine or Nakota, fished the lakes, trapped beaver in the ponds and moose in the woods, and hunted buffalo where the parkland opened southward, their lodges dragged by dog travois. The Qu'Appelle took its name from a story of these people: travellers on the river heard a voice call ka-tepwet, 'what is calling?', and when they answered, only the echo came back, which French ears caught as qu'appelle. The North West Company trader Daniel Harmon heard the tale from local people in 1804.

The first European to reach the parkland was Henry Kelsey, sent inland from York Factory with hatchets, beads and tobacco; after some 600 miles of river and thirty-three portages he wintered near The Pas, went south on foot with Cree in 1691, probably as far as the Touchwood Hills, met Assiniboine hunters, and on 20 August wrote of a 'great store of buffalo' and silver-haired bears, the first European account of the northern herds and the grizzly. He tried to make peace between the Assiniboine and a people he called the Naywatame, and failed. French traders came in from the east after La Verendrye built Fort La Reine on the Assiniboine in 1738, and Cree and Assiniboine bands of the Iron Confederacy were soon trading furs and pemmican for muskets and kettles; horses from the Blackfoot country changed the buffalo hunt by mid-century. In 1787 the North West Company built Fort Esperance on the lower Qu'Appelle, a stout post in open buffalo country kept chiefly as a pemmican depot that fed the canoe brigades further north. Rival posts crowded in beside it, and the Hudson's Bay fort was burned in 1816 in the violence that culminated at the Battle of Seven Oaks. The old depot was abandoned two years before the merger of 1821, when what remained passed to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
阿萨帕斯卡是图奇伍德丘陵与卡佩勒河之间的杨树林草原，白杨林和锅形湖散布在草地上，北方针叶林在此过渡为开阔平原。1444年，这里没有城镇，也没有商栈。后来被记作克里人和阿西尼博因人（纳科达人）的小队伍徒步迁徙，在湖中捕鱼，在池塘捕海狸、在林中猎驼鹿，到林缘向南敞开处猎野牛，帐篷靠狗拉拖橇搬运。卡佩勒河的名字来自当地人的一个故事：河上的旅人听见有声音呼喊「卡泰普韦特」，意为「谁在叫」，回喊之后只听到回声，法国人把这喊声听成了「卡佩勒」。西北公司商人丹尼尔·哈蒙1804年从当地人口中听到这个传说。

第一个走到这片林缘草原的欧洲人是亨利·凯尔西。他带着斧头、珠子和烟草从约克厂出发，逆河行船约六百英里、经过三十三处陆运，在帕斯附近过冬后，于1691年随克里同伴南下，很可能到了图奇伍德丘陵，遇见阿西尼博因猎人；8月20日，他写下「野牛极多」和「银色毛发的熊」，这是欧洲人对北部野牛群和灰熊最早的记载。他还想在阿西尼博因人与他称为内瓦塔梅人的部族之间讲和，没有成功。1738年拉韦朗德里在阿西尼博因河畔建起拉雷讷堡，法国商人随即自东而来；加入铁联盟的克里和阿西尼博因队伍不久便以毛皮和干肉饼换取火枪与铁锅，到18世纪中叶，黑脚之地来的马又改变了野牛狩猎。1787年，西北公司在卡佩勒河下游建起埃斯佩朗斯堡，这座坚固商栈立在开阔的野牛之乡，主要充当干肉饼仓，供给更北面的独木舟商队。周围很快挤满竞争的商栈；1816年，哈得孙湾公司的商栈在最终酿成七橡树之战的冲突中被焚毁。老干肉饼仓在两年后废弃，1821年两家公司合并时，残余设施归了哈得孙湾公司。

en:
Ashalaho, 'Many Lodges', was the name of the Mountain Crow, the largest of the Apsáalooke bands. Their country was the upper Yellowstone, which the Crow call Elk River, where the Absaroka and Bighorn ranges look over cold plains cut by beaver streams. In 1444 the people who would become the Crow were still settled villagers on the Upper Missouri, raising crops and hunting bison like their Hidatsa kin; these western valleys then belonged to Shoshone and other northern Plains hunters, who moved their camps on dog-drawn travois.

The Crow broke from the Hidatsa and moved west in the late seventeenth century. Crow tradition keeps the leader No Intestines, who dreamed of sacred tobacco and led the Ashalaho on a long search until they reached the upper Yellowstone; they drove Shoshone bands west over the mountains and took to mounted bison hunting. Horses spread among the Plains peoples from about 1730, and the Crow bred and traded them so well that their herds drew raids by Blackfoot and Gros Ventre parties. In 1805 the North West Company trader François-Antoine Larocque travelled for two and a half months with a Crow camp on its way home to the Yellowstone, and his journal is the first close European record of Crow life. In 1807 Fort Raymond was built near the mouth of the Bighorn, traded with the Crow until about 1813, and drew the mountain valleys into the Upper Missouri fur trade.
zh:
阿沙拉霍意为「多营盘」，是山地克劳人的名称，也是阿普萨鲁克（Apsáalooke，克劳人自称）各支里最大的一支。他们的地方在黄石河上游，克劳语把这条河叫作麋鹿河；阿布萨罗卡岭与大角山俯临寒冷平原，河狸出没的溪流切开谷地。1444年时，后来的克劳人还是上密苏里河畔的定居民，和希达沙亲族一样种地、猎牛；更西边的这些河谷当时属于休休尼人和其他北方平原猎手，他们用狗拉拖架搬营。

17世纪晚期，克劳人与希达沙人分离，向西迁移。克劳人的传说里，首领无肠梦见圣烟，带着阿沙拉霍人长途寻觅，一直走到黄石河上游；他们把休休尼部落逐过山岭，自己也成了骑马猎牛的人。约1730年马匹在平原各族中普及，克劳人养马、贩马很出名，马群也因此招来黑脚人和格罗斯文特人的袭掠。1805年，西北公司商人弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克跟着一处迁回黄石河的克劳营地走了两个半月，他的日记是欧洲人对克劳人生活最早的近距离记录。1807年，雷蒙德堡在大角河河口附近建起，与克劳人贸易至约1813年，把这些山谷拉进了上密苏里的毛皮贸易。

en:
The Sahnish, whom French and later American traders called the Arikara or Ree, speak a Caddoan tongue and are close kin of the Pawnee; their ancestors split from the Skidi Pawnee around the fifteenth century and carried village life up the Missouri. The name Arikara is usually read as 'horns', for the two upright bones men wore in their hair, though some translate it as 'corn eaters'. On terraces above the river in what is now central South Dakota they built fortified towns of earth lodges, and the Arzberger site holds the remains of more than forty-four. Women tended fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, nomadic camps came down to the river to trade meat for the harvest, and twice a year long parties set out on the bison hunt. In 1444 the Sahnish were the settled corn farmers of the middle Missouri. When Omaha and Ponca attacks in the late seventeenth century ended in peace, Omaha women learned to raise earth lodges from Arikara women.

In 1743 two sons of La Vérendrye reached a Sahnish village on this stretch of the river and buried an inscribed lead plate claiming the country for France. Smallpox swept the Missouri in 1780–1782, and of thirty-two Arikara villages only two were left; excavators later found seventy-one mutilated bodies in one village burned in those years, and Lakota raids pressed the survivors hard. Lewis and Clark met the remnant in 1804, and a delegation they urged east in April 1805 ended with Chief Ankedoucharo dying in Washington; his people held the Americans responsible. In 1821 the two surviving villages still kept their cornfields and ditchwork on the Missouri.
zh:
萨尼什人（Sahnish）被后来的法国和美国商人称作阿里卡拉人或里人，说卡多语，与波尼人是近亲；他们的祖先约在15世纪与斯基迪波尼人分开，把村落农耕生活沿密苏里河一路带上游。「阿里卡拉」通常解作「角」，来自男人插在发间的两根直立骨饰，也有人译为「食玉米者」。在今南达科他中部的河畔阶地上，他们建起土屋组成的设防村镇，阿茨伯格遗址就保存着四十四座以上的屋基。妇女种植玉米、豆子、南瓜和向日葵，游牧部落到河边用肉类换粮食，每年还有两次大队出动的长途猎牛。1444年，萨尼什人是密苏里河中游定居的种玉米的人。17世纪末奥马哈人和篷卡人来攻，议和之后，奥马哈妇女还向阿里卡拉妇女学会了建造土屋。

1743年，拉韦朗德里的两个儿子来到这一段河畔的萨尼什村庄，埋下一块刻字铅碑，以法兰西的名义占有这片土地。1780至1782年天花席卷密苏里河，三十二座阿里卡拉村庄只余两座；后人在一座被焚毁的村庄里发现了那一年代的七十一具残缺遗体，拉科塔人的袭击又紧逼幸存者。1804年，刘易斯与克拉克遇到残存的萨尼什人；他们劝派出的东行使团在1805年4月成行，酋长安克杜查罗却在华盛顿病故，族人认定美国人要为他的死负责。1821年，仅剩的两座村庄仍守着密苏里河畔的玉米田和壕沟。

en:
The Missouri cuts through the northern South Dakota grasslands, taking in the Grand River and other small timbered streams. In 1444 its terraces held the northern towns of the Caddoan-speaking earth-lodge villagers, kinsmen of the Sahnish or Arikara. Palisaded towns of domed lodges overlooked fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, and the surplus grain went by dugout to the bison hunters of the open plains. Beyond the river timber stretched short-grass country where the great herds ran, and winter cold could kill anyone caught far from shelter.

Horses reached the river early in the 18th century. The smallpox epidemic of 1780–1782 cut the Arikara villages on the Missouri from thirty-two to two, and raiders burned a fortified town on this stretch of the river; the ruins later dug over as the Larson site held the bodies of seventy-one men, women and children. Lakota bands crossed into the emptied country, and the Sihasapa, the 'Blackfoot' Lakota, no kin of the Blackfoot Confederacy of the northern Rockies, made the Grand River valley their range. Lewis and Clark held council with the surviving Arikara near the Grand's mouth in October 1804 and sent a chief, Ankedoucharo, on to Washington, where he fell ill and died, turning his people against the Americans for years. After 1807 Manuel Lisa's fur traders pushed their posts up the Missouri.
zh:
密苏里河穿过南达科他北部的草原，纳入格兰德河等几条林木丛生的小河。1444年，河畔阶地是卡多语系土屋村民分布的北缘，他们是萨尼什人（即阿里卡拉人）的亲族。圆顶土屋组成的栅栏村镇俯瞰着玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵田，余粮乘独木舟运给开阔平原上的猎牛人。河林之外是短草荒原，庞大的野牛群在那里奔走，严冬能冻死任何来不及躲避的人。

马匹在18世纪初传到河畔。1780至1782年的天花大流行把密苏里河沿岸的阿里卡拉村镇从三十二座削减到两座，袭击者又焚毁了这一段河畔的一座设防村镇；后来被考古学者发掘的拉森遗址废墟中，留有七十一名男女和儿童的遗骸。拉科塔各部渡河进入空虚的土地，锡哈萨帕人，即意为「黑脚」的拉科塔人（与北落基山的黑脚联盟并无亲缘），把格兰德河谷当作自己的活动地。1804年10月，刘易斯与克拉克在格兰德河口附近同残存的阿里卡拉人议事，并派首领安克杜查罗前往华盛顿，他却在那里病逝，使族人此后多年与美国人为敌。1807年后，曼努埃尔·利萨的皮货商把贸易站向密苏里河上游推进。

en:
Oglala is the short-grass country west of the Missouri's great bend above later Pierre, where river terraces face the distant Black Hills. In 1444 the valley belonged to the Middle Missouri world of earth-lodge farmers and bison hunters; the Arikara were then splitting from the Skidi Pawnee. Below later Pierre stood the fortified Arzberger village, more than forty-four lodges behind a stockade and twenty-four bastions, one of the last works of the older Initial Coalescent village builders on this stretch of the river.

In 1743 the La Vérendrye brothers reached an Arikara village near Pierre, the first written record of these reaches, and on a bluff over the Missouri they buried a lead plate stamped with the arms of France, claiming the country for the French king while telling villagers the cairn merely marked their passage. In those years the Oglala were becoming a distinct Lakota division: after taking horses from the Cheyenne around 1730, they moved with the Brulé into the James River valley and held the Missouri's eastern bank by about 1760. The smallpox of 1780–1782 cut the Arikara villages on the river from thirty-two to two and shattered the Mandan and Hidatsa as well; the crossing the farmers had barred stood open, and Lakota bands moved onto the High Plains. Lewis and Clark met armed Lakota on the river in 1804, at a parley that nearly came to a fight, and the fur posts built afterward tied the Oglala to European goods.
zh:
奥格拉拉是密苏里河大河弯以西的短草之地，在后来皮尔以上的河段，河畔阶地遥对远方的黑山。1444年时，河谷属于密苏里河中游土屋农夫与野牛猎人的世界，阿利卡拉人正与斯基迪波尼人分化。后来皮尔下游坐落着设防的阿兹贝格村，四十四座以上的房屋围在木栅与二十四座棱堡之内，是这一段密苏里河上较古老的「初始融合文化」村社最后的工程之一。

1743年，拉韦朗德里兄弟抵达皮尔附近的阿利卡拉村庄，这是这一河段最早的文字记录；他们在俯瞰密苏里河的高崖埋下一块铸有法国王徽的铅碑，为法兰西国王领有这片土地，却对村民说石堆只是法国人路过的记号。那些年里，奥格拉拉人正形成独立的拉科塔分支：约1730年从夏延人那里得到马匹后，他们与布鲁埃人进入詹姆斯河流域，约1760年已控制密苏里河东岸。1780—1782年的天花使河畔的阿利卡拉村庄从三十二座减为两座，曼丹人和希达察人也遭重创；村民们据守的渡口就此敞开，拉科塔各群体进入高平原。1804年，刘易斯和克拉克在河上遇到武装的拉科塔人，谈判几乎演成交战，此后建起的毛皮商站把奥格拉拉人与欧洲货物拴在了一起。

en:
Pequot country takes in the sheltered shore of southeastern Connecticut, where the Thames, Mystic and Pawcatuck rivers enter Long Island Sound. The Pequot spoke an Algonquian dialect close to Mohegan, and their palisaded villages, fishing stations and canoe paths linked inland hunting grounds with the coastal exchange between Niantic country to the west and Narragansett country to the east. In 1444 no European ship had entered the sound; its fish and shellfish and the estuary crossings belonged to the Pequot alone.

The first European to map these waters was Adriaen Block, who entered the sound and the Connecticut River in 1614. Smallpox swept the Pequot towns in 1633, and the killing of trader John Oldham in 1636 gave the English colonies and their Mohegan and Narragansett allies their pretext for war on the sachem Sassacus. Before dawn on 26 May 1637 John Mason's men and their allies surrounded the palisaded village at Mystic and set fire to it, killing 400 to 700 Pequots. The 1638 Treaty of Hartford dissolved the nation, forbade even the name Pequot, and gave the survivors to the allies or sold them into slavery; small reserves were later held at Mashantucket in 1666 and Pawcatuck in 1683. John Winthrop the Younger founded an English town on the harbor in 1646 and named it New London in 1658, and its wharves sent out privateers during the Revolutionary War. On 6 September 1781 Benedict Arnold, who had grown up a few miles up the Thames, led a British force that burned much of New London and stormed Fort Griswold across the river; after William Ledyard's garrison surrendered, many of its men were shot. It was the last major battle in the northern colonies, about six weeks before the Franco-American siege of Yorktown.
zh:
佩科特人的土地在康涅狄格东南，是泰晤士河、米斯蒂克河和波卡塔克河注入长岛海湾的一段遮蔽海岸。佩科特人说与莫西干语相近的阿尔冈昆方言，栅栏村落、渔场和独木舟水路把内陆猎场同海岸往来连成一片，西去是奈安蒂克人的地界，东面是纳拉甘西特人的地界。1444年，还没有欧洲船进过这片海湾，鱼群、贝场和河口渡口全归佩科特人。

第一个绘下这片水域的欧洲人是阿德里安·布洛克，1614年他驶入长岛海湾和康涅狄格河。1633年天花横扫佩科特村镇，1636年商人约翰·奥尔德姆被杀，英格兰殖民地便带着莫西干和纳拉甘西特盟友，向萨萨库斯酋长的部族开战。1637年5月26日天亮前，约翰·梅森所部和盟友围住米斯蒂克的栅栏村放火，400至700名佩科特人遇害。1638年《哈特福德条约》解散这个部族、禁止再用「佩科特」之名，幸存者或分给盟友，或卖为奴隶；直到1666年和1683年，后人才分别在马尚图克特和波卡塔克保有小块保留地。1646年小约翰·温思罗普在港湾建起英格兰城镇，1658年定名新伦敦，独立战争中这里的码头派出大批私掠船。1781年9月6日，在泰晤士河上游不远处长大的本尼迪克特·阿诺德率英军烧毁大半个新伦敦，又渡河强攻格里斯沃尔德堡；威廉·莱德亚德率守军投降后，仍有许多人被枪杀。这是北美北部殖民地最后一场大战，约六周后便是法美联军围攻约克镇。

en:
This province is the Shenandoah Valley, the long corridor between the Blue Ridge and the Allegheny ridges, where the forks of the Shenandoah run north to the Potomac. In 1444 its bottomlands belonged to the Senedo, farming people whose language no record preserves; they planted the river flats and left the earthen mounds later opened above the bends. The valley was also a war road. Seneca and Lenape raiders filed down it from the north to strike the Catawba far to the south, and Catawba war parties followed the same track back.

Early settlers heard that the Senedo had themselves been wiped out by Catawba raiders before 1700. Governor Alexander Spotswood's Knights of the Golden Horseshoe crossed the Blue Ridge at Swift Run Gap in 1716, Adam Miller staked the first farm on the south fork in 1727, and through the 1730s German and Scots-Irish families came down the old Indian path, the Great Wagon Road; Winchester and Woodstock grew among their settlements. The Iroquois, who had long used the valley as a raiding corridor, sold their claim to it for 200 pounds in gold at the Treaty of Lancaster in 1744, and the Shawnee camped near Winchester withdrew over the Alleghenies in 1754. In the Revolutionary War the valley sent the Continental army wheat and riflemen alike.
