Ming records called the realm Yili-bali, but no garrisoned capital had replaced Almaliq.

The Dzungars later brought a settled court back to the valley. Near Ghulja their rulers kept brick buildings, Buddhist monasteries, warehouses and irrigation channels; Russian reports also mention four cannon at the seat. Farmers moved from the southern oases planted wheat, barley, millet, melons, grapes, apricots and apples. Qing armies broke the Dzungar regime in 1755 during the fighting around Amursana. The Qing then made the Ili a military frontier: Ming Rui took office as the first General of Ili in 1762, Huiyuan Cheng was built on the river in 1763, and Ningyuan received farmers and merchants from the south. Together with neighbouring forts they formed the Nine Cities of Ili, whose garrisons and granaries dominated the valley in 1821.
zh:
特克斯河与巩乃斯河汇合后称伊犁河，在天山与博罗科努山之间冲出一条宽阔河谷，再向西流向巴尔喀什湖。葛逻禄商人与牧人在盆地中建起阿力麻里，城名来自周围成片的野苹果林。14世纪中期，秃忽鲁·帖木儿把这里作为察合台汗廷和伊斯兰教传播中心，但景教徒墓葬和天主教传教士的活动说明城中仍有其他信徒。战乱和游牧秩序的恢复使旧城大半荒废。1444年，也先不花的蒙兀儿汗廷依靠部族首领、骑马牧人和夏季牧场控制伊犁；明代史籍称这个政权为亦力把里，此时却没有一座驻有军队的都城取代阿力麻里。

准噶尔人后来把定居汗廷带回这片河谷。他们在固勒札附近维持砖造建筑、佛寺、仓廪和灌溉渠，俄国报告还提到汗廷驻地有四门火炮。来自南疆绿洲的农户种植小麦、大麦、黍、甜瓜、葡萄、杏和苹果。1755年，清军在阿睦尔撒纳引发的战事中击垮准噶尔政权。清朝随后把伊犁变成军事边疆：1762年明瑞出任第一任伊犁将军，1763年惠远城在伊犁河畔建成，宁远城则安置南疆农户和商人。它们与邻近堡垒合称伊犁九城，到1821年时，驻军和粮仓仍支配着这片河谷。

en:
Kuqa occupies one of the best-watered oases below the Tian Shan, on the caravan road running north of the Taklamakan from Aksu toward Korla and Turpan. This was ancient Kucha, the largest city-state listed in the Hanshu's account of the Western Regions, with 81,317 inhabitants. Fourth-century visitors described triple ramparts, a lavish royal palace and thousands of Buddhist stupas and temples. The monk Kumarajiva was born here in 344; after the Former Qin general Lü Guang took Kucha in 383, Kumarajiva was carried east, and from 401 he led translation work in Chang'an that made Sanskrit sutras available in Chinese. Kuchean music, copper, iron and lead also gave the oasis a name among caravans. Uyghur settlement and Chagatai rule later changed its language and faith, and in 1444 the Sunni Turki town lay in the Moghul realm of Esen Buqa II, while the Dughlat amirs who held Kuqa and nearby Bai kept much of the local power.

Chinese records place Kuqa under the Eastern Chagatai khans in 1468 and under the Yarkand Khanate in 1533. Rulers on the northern Tarim road needed its water, provisions and taxes, and Chagatayid princes and Sufi teachers moved through it with the caravans. Older Buddhist monastery ruins remained around the Muslim town, but political life centred on the oasis and its road to Turpan. Galdan's Dzungar campaigns brought Kuqa under Dzungar rule with the rest of Altishahr in 1680. Qing armies took the oasis in 1758 while breaking Dzungar power.
zh:
库车位于天山南麓水源充足的一片绿洲，扼守塔克拉玛干沙漠北缘、从阿克苏通向库尔勒与吐鲁番的商路。这里是古龟兹，《汉书》所记西域城郭诸国中最大的一国，人口有81317人。4世纪的到访者称它有三重城墙、华丽的王宫，以及成千上万座佛塔和寺院。高僧鸠摩罗什344年生于此；383年前秦将领吕光攻下龟兹后将他带往东方，401年起他在长安主持译经，把梵文佛经译成汉文。龟兹乐和铜、铁、铅也让往来商队记住了这片绿洲。回鹘迁入和察合台统治后来改变了这里的语言与信仰；1444年，这座逊尼派突厥语城镇处在也先不花二世的蒙兀儿势力范围内，占有库车和邻近拜城的杜格拉特异密则掌握着大量地方权力。

汉文史料记库车1468年归东察合台诸汗统治，1533年归入叶尔羌汗国。控制塔里木北道的统治者需要这里的水源、给养和税入，察合台王公和苏菲导师也随商队往来。穆斯林城镇周围仍留有古老的佛教寺院遗址，政治生活则围绕绿洲和通往吐鲁番的道路展开。1680年，噶尔丹发动准噶尔战事，库车与阿尔蒂沙尔诸城一并受准噶尔统治。1758年，清军在击破准噶尔势力时夺取这片绿洲。

en:
Hami, called Kumul in Uyghur, is the first large oasis west of the Jiayu Pass. Caravans leaving the Gobi passed its fields before choosing the routes north or south of the Tian Shan. Streams and underground channels watered grain land, vineyards and melon plots, and Chinese travellers already noted Hami's melons, raisins and wine. After Yuan rule collapsed, the Chagatayid prince Gunashiri founded the small kingdom of Kara Del here. The Ming invested his successor Engke Temür as Zhongshun Wang in 1404 and set up the Hami Guard in 1406, yet neither stationed regular tax officials nor replaced the local ruler. In 1444 the Buddhist Chagatayid khan stood between Ming garrisons and Esen's Oirats, ruling Uyghur cultivators, Muslim merchants and Mongol herdsmen. The Ming envoy Chen Cheng found a small walled town with orchards and a mixed Mongol and Muslim population.

That exposed position made Hami a repeated object of frontier wars. Ming troops under Ren Li entered the oasis during disorders in 1446 and moved 1,230 people inside the Jiayu Pass. A pro-Mongol faction overthrew the khan in 1463, and Ming attempts to restore Gunashiri's house did not hold. Mansur Khan of Turpan captured Hami in 1513 and annexed it in 1515; Islamic rule replaced the Buddhist kingdom, and Turpan armies used the oasis as a base for raids toward the Jiayu Pass. Hami later passed under Dzungar overlordship until its chief Ebeydulla submitted to the Qing in 1697 and his followers were enrolled as a banner the next year. Qing authorities built adjoining Muslim and Chinese garrison towns, and after the conquest of Xinjiang made Hami a subprefecture in 1759. Sweet Hami melons were already being sent to Beijing as tribute fruit.
zh:
哈密在维吾尔语中称昆莫勒，是嘉峪关以西第一片大绿洲。商队走出戈壁后，先到哈密的农田，再分赴天山南北各路。溪流和地下渠道灌溉着粮田、葡萄园和瓜田，中国使臣早已提到这里的甜瓜、葡萄干和葡萄酒。元朝崩溃后，察合台后裔兀纳失里在这片绿洲建立小国哈密国。1404年，继位的安克帖木儿被明朝封为忠顺王；1406年明廷设哈密卫，但没有派遣常规税官，也没有取代本地君主。1444年，信奉佛教的察合台系汗王夹在明朝驻军与也先的瓦剌之间，治下有畏兀儿农人、回回商人和蒙古牧民。明朝使臣陈诚看到的是一座有果园的小土城，蒙古人与回回人杂处其中，礼俗各不相同。

这种暴露的位置使哈密一再卷入边地战争。1446年哈密生乱，明将任礼率军进入绿洲，把一千二百三十人迁入嘉峪关内。1463年亲蒙古的一派推翻汗王，明朝多次复立兀纳失里的后裔，都没能稳住局面。吐鲁番的满速儿汗1513年攻占哈密，1515年正式吞并；伊斯兰统治取代了佛教王国，吐鲁番军队又以哈密为基地，多次进逼嘉峪关。哈密后来受准噶尔控制，直到1697年首领额贝都拉归附清朝，部众次年被编为札萨克旗。清朝在相邻处修筑回城与汉城，1759年平定新疆后设哈密厅。哈密甜瓜当时已作为贡果送往北京。

en:
Qakilik, the Charklik oasis at the foot of the Altyn Tagh beside the shrinking salt lake of Lop Nur, was the seat of Shanshan, the kingdom the Han first knew as Loulan. The road from Dunhuang forked here, north to Korla and west to Khotan, and Han and Xiongnu contested it for generations. In 77 BCE the Han envoy Fu Jiezi came with gifts of gold and stabbed the drunken Loulan king; the court placed his brother Weituqi on the throne, renamed the realm Shanshan and moved the capital south to Wuni in this oasis. The new king asked for a Han garrison at Yixun, the Miran of later ruins, and soldier-farmers were settled there. In 73 CE Ban Chao, finding a Xiongnu delegation there already, killed its envoys by night and showed their heads to King Guang, who submitted. Buddhist stupas and monasteries stood at Miran from the second to the fifth century; Faxian, crossing from Dunhuang in 399, reckoned more than four thousand monks in the country, all Hinayana. The kingdom died with its rivers: the Han colony at Loulan was abandoned in 330 when the Tarim changed course, King Bilong fled west to Qiemo in 442, and around 630 the last Shanshan people migrated to Hami; Xuanzang in 644 found only a town he called Nafubo. Miran was a Tibetan fortress in the eighth and ninth centuries, holding the pass into Tibet, before the sands emptied it. By 1444 only a small Turki-speaking oasis remained under the Moghul khan Esen Buqa II, its caravans running between Hami and the Khotan oases.

In the early sixteenth century Mansur Khan led Moghul ghazis east from Turpan against Hami and Dunhuang, raiding the Ming frontier. Later in that century the Yarkand Khanate gathered Turpan, Hami and the southern oases, after which Charklik passed to the khojas and then the Dzungars, who made the last Moghul khans clients in Galdan's 1680 campaign. When Qing armies crushed the Khoja brothers' rising in 1759, the southern route passed under Qing control; Charklik stayed a minor caravan halt beneath the Altyn Tagh.
zh:
若羌（维吾尔语称卡克里克）是阿尔金山脚下、临着日渐干涸的盐湖罗布泊的绿洲，曾是鄯善国的王都，汉朝最初称这个国家为楼兰。从敦煌而来的道路在此分岔，一支北向库尔勒，一支西向和阗，汉与匈奴为控制两道争夺了好几代。前77年，汉使傅介子带着黄金财物抵达楼兰，在酒宴上把醉酒的楼兰王刺死；朝廷立其弟尉屠耆为王，改国名为鄯善，王都南迁到这片绿洲上的扜泥城。新王畏惧故王诸子，请求汉朝在伊循，也就是后来的米兰遗址驻军，汉廷便派将士和屯田卒前来。73年，班超带少数随从出使到此，发现匈奴使者已经先在；他当夜袭杀匈奴使者，把首级拿给鄯善王广看，鄯善随即归附。2至5世纪，米兰的佛塔和伽蓝立于商道之旁；399年法显从敦煌穿越大漠后到此，估计国中有僧四千余人，全习小乘。这个王国随河流一起衰亡：330年塔里木河改道，楼兰的汉人屯田据点废弃，442年国王比龙西奔且末，约630年最后的鄯善人北迁哈密，644年玄奘只找到一座他称作纳缚波的小城。米兰在8至9世纪成为吐蕃人的要塞，扼守南通吐蕃的山口，随后也被流沙废弃。到1444年，蒙兀儿汗也先不花二世治下只剩一个说突厥语的小绿洲，商队往返于哈密与和阗诸绿洲之间。

16世纪初，满速儿汗率蒙兀儿圣战者从吐鲁番东攻哈密和敦煌，屡犯明朝边塞。该世纪后期，叶尔羌汗国把吐鲁番、哈密与南路诸绿洲并入一国，卡克里克此后先归和卓统治，又落入准噶尔之手，1680年噶尔丹远征后末代蒙兀儿诸汗沦为附庸。1759年清军平定大小和卓之乱，天山南路转入清朝治下，卡克里克依旧是阿尔金山脚下一处不起眼的商队歇脚地。

en:
Yarkand is the oasis on the southern rim of the Taklamakan, watered by the Yarkand River as it comes down from the Karakoram and Kunlun ranges. Its canals supported cotton fields and orchards, while its roads ran west toward the Pamirs, south to Ladakh and east along the desert to Khotan and China. Chinese records called the place Suoju. Marco Polo passed through around 1273 and found Muslims, a smaller Nestorian community and plentiful provisions, especially cotton. After the Chagatai settlement, Dughlat emirs controlled the oasis cities. In 1444 Yarkand was a Sunni Turki Muslim town under Dughlat lordship, supplying wool, cotton, food and animals to caravans on the southern Tarim road.

Sultan Said Khan defeated Mirza Abu Bakr in 1514 and, after an early court at Kashgar, made Yarkand the capital of his new Chagatai state. The khan's city became the principal market of the Tarim oases. Said's raiders crossed the Karakoram into Ladakh and Kashmir, and the khan died at Daulat Beg Oldi in 1533 while returning north. Late in 1603 the Portuguese Jesuit Bento de Gois reached Yarkand with a Kabul caravan and waited about a year for the next party toward Cathay. The king sold command of that caravan to chiefs who then held authority over its merchants, and Gois, on the first known European overland journey from India toward China, saw Yarkandi jade ranked among the most prized goods. Rival White Mountain and Black Mountain khojas weakened the khanate before Galdan's Dzungars took the city in 1680 and installed a puppet khan; around 1700 Tsewang Rabtan ended the Chagatai line and imposed direct Dzungar rule. Qing armies secured Yarkand in 1759 while suppressing the revolt of Burhan-ud-din and Khoja Jahan, and in 1821 it remained a garrisoned frontier market on the roads to Ladakh and Kokand.
zh:
叶尔羌位于塔克拉玛干沙漠南缘，叶尔羌河从喀喇昆仑山和昆仑山流下，滋养出这片绿洲。渠水浇灌棉田和果园，道路西通帕米尔，南至拉达克，又沿沙漠东连于阗和中国内地。汉文古籍称这里为莎车。马可·波罗约在1273年经过，看到居民多为穆斯林，也有人数较少的景教徒，物产充足，尤其盛产棉花。察合台系分封之后，杜格拉特埃米尔控制了各座绿洲城。1444年，叶尔羌是杜格拉特贵族治下的逊尼派突厥语穆斯林城镇，为塔里木南道上的商队供应羊毛、棉布、食物和牲畜。

1514年，萨亦德汗击败米尔扎·阿布·伯克尔，先在喀什噶尔设庭，随后把叶尔羌定为新察合台系国家的都城。汗廷所在使这里成为塔里木诸绿洲最重要的市场。萨亦德的军队越过喀喇昆仑山进入拉达克和克什米尔，他本人则在1533年北返途中死于斗拉特别奥里地。1603年底，葡萄牙耶稣会士鄂本笃随喀布尔商队抵达叶尔羌，等待约一年才随新商队前往契丹。汗把商队指挥权出售给首领，这些首领沿途管辖同行商人；鄂本笃正在进行已知第一次欧洲人从印度陆路前往中国的旅行，他也看到叶尔羌玉石被列为最受珍视的货物之一。白山派与黑山派和卓相争，削弱了汗国。1680年，噶尔丹的准噶尔军攻占叶尔羌，另立傀儡汗；约1700年，策妄阿拉布坦终结察合台系汗统，改为准噶尔直接统治。1759年，清军在平定波罗尼都和霍集占之乱时控制叶尔羌；1821年，它仍是通往拉达克和浩罕道路上一座有驻军的边疆商市。

en:
The Kochkor valley lies high in the inner Tian Shan, a grassy basin 1,800 to 2,500 metres up walled by the Kyrgyz Ala-Too, Kyzart and Jumgal ranges. Its road runs north to the Chu and south over the Torugart pass towards Kashgar, the route caravans used between the Tarim and the steppe. Saka and Wusun burial mounds show the basin was grazed in antiquity; Islam came with the Karakhanids, and after the Mongol conquest the country passed to the Chagatai ulus and then to Moghulistan. Tughluq Timur made Islam the khans' religion, but the highland clans kept most of their old beliefs. In 1444 Kochkor was summer pasture of Kyrgyz tribes on Moghulistan's remote Tian Shan edge, valued for horses, sheep and wool rather than for towns.

Through the sixteenth century Kyrgyz clans rode to war with the Kazakh khans against Yarkand and the Uzbeks. The Dzungar blows began in 1643, when a 50,000-strong army under Batur drove them from eastern Zhetysu, and the great invasion of the 1720s scattered the highlanders into Fergana, leaving only those who submitted by Lake Issyk-Kul. After Qing armies broke the Dzungars in 1755–57 the Kyrgyz climbed back to their old jailoos, fought Abylai Khan's Kazakhs over the recovered grass, and made peace in 1780. Early in the nineteenth century the Khanate of Kokand, expanding north, made the northern Kyrgyz tribes its tributaries, and Kyrgyz horsemen became the core of its armies.
zh:
科奇科尔谷地深藏天山腹地，是海拔1800至2500米的草原盆地，为吉尔吉斯阿拉套、克扎尔特与朱姆加尔山脉环抱。谷中道路北通楚河，南越图噜噶特山口直抵喀什，是塔里木与草原之间商队往来的通道。萨卡人与乌孙人的墓冢说明盆地自古便是牧场；伊斯兰教随喀喇汗王朝而来，蒙古征服后这里先后归入察合台汗国和东察合台。秃黑鲁·帖木儿把伊斯兰教立为汗室的信仰，高山部落却大多保留旧俗。1444年的科奇科尔是吉尔吉斯部落在东察合台天山边陲的夏牧场，所重的是马匹、绵羊和羊毛，没有城镇。

整个16世纪，吉尔吉斯诸部随哈萨克诸汗出征，同叶尔羌和乌兹别克作战。准噶尔人的打击始于1643年，巴图尔珲台吉率五万大军把他们逐出七河东部；1720年代的大入侵又把高地人驱散到费尔干纳，只有臣服者留在伊塞克湖畔。1755至1757年清军击灭准噶尔后，吉尔吉斯人重返旧日的夏牧场，为收复的草场同阿卜赉汗的哈萨克人交战，至1780年议和。19世纪初，向北扩张的浩罕汗国把北方吉尔吉斯诸部收为藩属，吉尔吉斯骑兵成为浩罕军队的核心。

en:
The Chu runs between the Kyrgyz Ala-Too and the steppe on its way to the Muyunkum desert, and its valley held some of the richest caravan towns on the Silk Road. Suyab, whose ruins lie west of Tokmok, began as a Sogdian merchant settlement and became the chief capital of the Western Turkic khagans. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang passed through in 629 and found its markets crowded with foreign traders; Tang China built a fortress there in 679, a walled town of twelve gates, long one of the Four Garrisons of the Anxi protectorate. Li Bai, one of the most celebrated poets in Chinese, is said by some accounts to have been born in Suyab. The town was overtaken by Balasagun, capital of the Karakhanids, where the poet Yusuf Khass Hajib was born around 1019; his Kutadgu Bilig is one of the earliest surviving works of Turkic Islamic literature. Beside the city stands the eleventh-century Burana minaret, forty-six metres high when new, its upper half later lost to earthquakes. The Kara-Khitai took Balasagun in 1134 and the Mongols in 1218, and when William of Rubruck followed the Chu in 1253 he found only ruins. In 1444 the valley belonged to Moghulistan, and Kyrgyz and Moghol nomads moved across its pastures.

The valley also gave the Kazakh Khanate its start. Two Jochid sultans, Kerei and Janybek, broke with Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek khanate and led their clans east into Moghulistan to live as qazaqs, frontier seceders who kept themselves by hunting and raiding. The Moghul khan Esen Buqa granted them pastures along the Chu, and around 1465 their followers proclaimed a khanate there; qazaq, first a name for such frontier bands, became the name of a people. Through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries Kyrgyz and Kazakh clans campaigned together against Yarkand and the Oirats, until the Dzungars broke into Zhetysu in 1643 and again in the 1720s, when the valley was largely abandoned. Kyrgyz and Kazakh herdsmen flooded back after the Qing crushed the Dzungars in 1755–57, then fought each other over the empty grass until a truce in 1780. By the early nineteenth century the expanding Khanate of Kokand was pushing north towards the Chu and making the northern Kyrgyz tribes its tributaries.
zh:
楚河在吉尔吉斯阿拉套山与草原之间流向穆云库姆沙漠，河谷里曾坐落着丝绸之路上最富庶的几座商镇。托克马克以西的碎叶本是粟特商人的聚落，后来成为西突厥可汗的首要都城。629年，唐朝僧人玄奘途经此处，见到市镇上胡商云集；679年唐军在此筑城，城墙四面开十二座门，碎叶长期位列安西四镇之一。中国最著名的诗人之一李白，相传就出生在碎叶。后来碎叶让位于喀喇汗王朝的都城八剌沙衮：诗人优素福约1019年生于此城，所作《福乐智慧》是突厥语伊斯兰文学最早传世的经典之一；城旁立着11世纪的布拉纳塔，原高四十六米，上半截后来毁于地震。喀喇契丹1134年攻取八剌沙衮，蒙古人1218年再度占据；1253年鲁布鲁克沿楚河而行，所见已是废墟。1444年的楚河谷地属东察合台，吉尔吉斯与蒙兀儿游牧人在草场上往来迁徙。

楚河谷地也是哈萨克汗国起家之地。两位术赤系苏丹克烈与贾尼别克脱离阿布勒海尔的乌兹别克汗国，率部东入东察合台，在边境上过着「哈萨克」式的生活：脱离旧主，以射猎和劫掠为生。蒙兀儿汗也先不花把楚河沿岸的牧场封给他们，约1465年，他们的部众在此拥立汗国；「哈萨克」本指这种边境流民的生活方式，后来变成一个族群的名字。16至17世纪，吉尔吉斯与哈萨克诸部联兵对抗叶尔羌与卫拉特，直到准噶尔人1643年攻入七河，又在1720年代大举来犯，河谷大半荒废。1755至1757年清朝击灭准噶尔后，吉尔吉斯与哈萨克牧民蜂拥而回，旋即为空旷的草原互相攻伐，至1780年议和。19世纪初，扩张中的浩罕汗国向楚河方向北进，把北方吉尔吉斯诸部收为藩属。

en:
Yashilkul is a freshwater lake 3,734 metres up in the Alichur Pamir, held between the North and South Alichur ranges where a mountain fall once blocked the river; the Alichur flows in and the Gunt flows out toward the Panj. Wide grassy uplands ring the shore, and Kyrgyz herders drive sheep and yaks up from the lower valleys to summer there. The Ming envoy Chen Cheng, crossing to the Timurid court in the Yongle era, may have recorded the lake as Yixi-ke'er, possibly its first Chinese name. In 1444 the high country was the remote fringe of the Moghul khans of the eastern Chagatai line; their descendants founded the Yarkand khanate in 1514, and the Dzungars overran Altishahr between 1678 and 1705.

In the summer of 1759, after Kashgar and Yarkand fell, the Qing general Fude hunted the khoja brothers Burhan al-Din and Khwaja Jahan through these mountains. At the lake the brothers made their last stand: Khwaja Jahan held the ridge east of the water with ten thousand men while Burhan al-Din waited on the west with the families and baggage. Qing attacks up the slopes stalled, until Fude sent forty picked musketeers to scale an unguarded height above the Khoja position and fire down into it, while Uyghur beks serving the Qing raised their banners and called on the rebels to surrender, and the Khoja army melted off the ridge. The brothers fled into Badakhshan with some three hundred followers, where Sultan Shah seized them. The Qianlong emperor had a victory stele in Manchu, Chinese and Turki raised east of the lake, and kept a Qing garrison at nearby Suman.
zh:
叶什勒池清代称伊西洱库尔淖尔，是阿尔楚尔帕米尔的高原淡水湖，湖面海拔3734米，夹在北阿尔楚尔山与南阿尔楚尔山之间，原为山崩堵塞河道而成；阿尔楚尔河注入湖中，湖水西流为贡特河，奔往喷赤河。湖周是宽阔的高山草场，柯尔克孜牧人从低地山谷赶着羊群和牦牛上来度夏。明代永乐年间出使帖木儿朝的陈诚，可能已在《竹山集》中以「亦息渴儿」记下此湖，这或许是它最早的汉文名称。1444年，这片高寒之地处在东察合台系蒙兀儿汗廷遥远的边缘；其后人于1514年建立叶尔羌汗国，1678至1705年间准噶尔人征服了天山南路。

1759年夏，喀什噶尔与叶尔羌既下，清将富德深入山中，穷追大小和卓波罗尼都、霍集占。和卓军在湖畔据守：霍集占以万人扼守湖东山岭，波罗尼都带着老弱辎重留在西岭。清军仰攻东岭受挫，富德遂选四十名精锐火枪手攀上和卓军疏于防守的高处，自北岭居高俯射；降清的回部伯克鄂对、霍集斯等人树起回旗喊话招降，和卓军纷纷下山归降。大小和卓只带三百余众逃入巴达克山，被巴达克山首领素勒坦沙擒获。乾隆皇帝下令在湖东立满、汉、维三种文字的纪功碑，并在附近的苏满驻兵戍守。

en:
Tsaparang was the citadel-capital of Guge, which held the Sutlej valley of far western Tibet after the old Tibetan empire collapsed. Around 910 Kyide Nyimagon, great-grandson of the persecuting king Langdarma, fled to Ngari, and the branch of his line that settled the Sutlej valley became Guge. King Yeshe-Ö founded Tholing in 997 and sent the translator Rinchen Zangpo to study in India, and in 1042 the Indian master Atiśa came at the royal invitation; from these valleys Buddhism's 'upper revival' spread across the rest of Tibet. The monasteries grew rich on the India-Tibet trade road and the gold of Ngari, and the kings piled their capital onto a single rock: a pyramid of weathered earth five to six hundred feet high, honeycombed with caves and tunnels, the village at its foot, the White and Red chapels on the lower terraces, a stair-tunnel past the royal apartments to the summer palace on the summit. It absorbed Purang in 1378 and once ruled Ladakh; in 1444 Guge was still a confident Buddhist power under its ancient dynasty.

By the seventeenth century its kings had long acknowledged the Rinpungpa rulers of Tsang as overlords. In 1626 the Portuguese Jesuit António de Andrade reached Tsaparang, the first known European to cross the Himalayas; the last king, Tashi Drakpa, let him preach, gave him a house at the foot of the rock and allowed a second church at Rudok, hoping to counter his brother, the kingdom's chief lama. The monks rose in 1633 and called in Senge Namgyal of Ladakh; a Ladakhi army blockaded the rock for months and starved the fortress into surrender in 1635, and the king and his royal kin were put to death. Brother Manuel Marques, Andrade's old companion, returned in 1640 to reopen the mission, was seized, and sent one last letter to Agra begging rescue before he vanished. Ladakh held Guge for nearly half a century, until 1679-1680, when the Fifth Dalai Lama's general Galdan Chhewang drove the Ladakhis out with a Mongol-Tibetan army and annexed Guge to Lhasa. Tsaparang never recovered: with the dynasty gone the citadel emptied, its tunnels and chapels left to the sand.
zh:
札布让是古格王国的堡寨都城，古格据有吐蕃崩溃后西藏西部的象泉河谷。约910年，灭法之王朗达玛的曾孙吉德尼玛衮西逃阿里，其后人领有象泉河的一支便是古格，王统出自吐蕃王室。益西沃于997年兴建托林寺，派大译师仁钦桑布赴印度求法；1042年，印度高僧阿底峡应王室之请入藏，藏传佛教的「上路弘法」便从这些河谷传向西藏各地。寺院的富庶靠的是古老的印藏商路和阿里的黄金；历代国王又把都城垒上一座孤山：这座高约一百七十五米的风蚀土山形如金字塔，山体被洞窟和暗道掏空，山脚是民居，下层台地坐落着白殿、红殿和僧舍，一条隧道石阶绕过王宫寝宫，直通山顶的夏宫。古格1378年吞并普兰，还曾一度统治拉达克；1444年的古格在旧王朝治下，仍是个底气十足的佛教政权。

到17世纪时，古格王早已承认藏地仁蚌巴政权的宗主权。1626年，葡萄牙耶稣会士安东尼奥·德尔·安德拉德抵达札布让，成为有记载最早翻越喜马拉雅山的欧洲人；末代国王赤扎西扎巴德准他传教，在宗堡脚下赐屋建堂，又允许他远赴日土另建一寺，想借传教士制衡出家为僧、身为宗教领袖的王弟。1633年僧侣发动叛乱，引来拉达克王森格南杰的军队围困土山数月，1635年这座石山要塞粮尽出降，国王与王室成员被杀。当年随安德拉德翻山的一名修士1640年重返古格，试图恢复传教，被守军擒获，只向印度阿格拉发出最后一封求救信，此后不知所终。拉达克统治古格近半个世纪；1679至1680年，五世达赖麾下的噶丹泽旺率蒙藏联军赶走拉达克人，把古格并入拉萨治下。札布让再未复兴，王统既绝，堡城空了，洞窟与佛殿没入黄沙。

en:
The forested valleys around Nyingchi are the western core of Kongpo, where the Nyang River breaks out of the eastern Himalayan gorges to join the Yarlung Tsangpo. Monsoon rain reaches far up them: timbered slopes rise above river flats sown with grain, and high pasture lies above the trees. Kongpo kept its own kings long after the Yarlung dynasty ruled from Lhasa. They claimed royal blood: after the eighth king, Drigum Tsenpo, was killed in a palace feud, his son Nyatri fled to Kongpo and was raised as its king, and a rock inscription of the imperial period at Demo records the standing of his line. Buchu Monastery south of the Nyingchi flats was founded under Songtsen Gampo in the seventh century as one of the eight 'demoness-subduing' temples, built by geomancy on the right elbow of the ogress whose body covered Tibet; it was the oldest Buddhist sanctuary in Kongpo and belonged to the Nyingma school. In 1444 the valleys still belonged, on paper, to the Phagmodrupa regime of Drakpa Jungne, but its recent succession war had left the local lords and monasteries with the real power.

The yogi and engineer Thang Tong Gyalpo, who strung iron chain bridges across Tibet, knew these valleys: he founded Manmogang Monastery in Kongpo and took the iron for some of his bridges from mines here. In the wars of the following reigns Kongpo sided with the Rinpungpa and the kings of Tsang, who governed it through dzong forts. After Gushi Khan's victory in 1642, the Ganden Phodrang government granted the Nyingchi lands to the noble houses of Ngapoi, Jiangzhong and Jiala, and Gelugpa monks were already sharing Buchu with its older Nyingma community by then. The dzong administration of Kongpo, broken in the disorders, was restored under the Jiaqing emperor between 1796 and 1820.
zh:
林芝周围森林密布的河谷是工布的西部核心，尼洋河在这里冲出喜马拉雅东段的峡谷，汇入雅鲁藏布江。印度洋的水汽沿河谷深入：林坡之上出产木材，河边阶地种植谷物，林线以上是高山牧场。雅砻王朝迁都拉萨以后很久，工布仍有自己的王。工布王出自吐蕃王统：第八代赞普止贡赞普在宫斗中被杀后，王子聂赤逃到工布，被拥立为工布王，第穆一带一方吐蕃时期的摩崖石刻记载了这一支的地位。林芝阶地以南的布久拉康建于7世纪松赞干布时期，是镇伏魔女的八座神庙之一，依风水压在魔女的右肘上，为工布最古老的佛教道场，原属宁玛派。1444年，这些河谷在名义上仍归札巴迥乃的帕木竹巴政权，但刚过去的继承纷争已经让地方首领和寺院掌握了实权。

在西藏各处架设铁索桥的瑜伽师、工匠汤东杰布熟悉这些山谷：他在工布修建了门莫岗寺，造桥所用的铁有一部分就采自当地矿山。此后的教派战争中，工布站在仁蚌巴和藏巴汗一边，由他们设宗管辖。1642年固始汗取胜后，甘丹颇章政权把林芝一带封给阿沛、江中、甲拉等贵族；那时布久拉康里已有格鲁派僧人与旧有的宁玛派共处。战乱中废坏的宗制，在清嘉庆年间（1796—1820年）得到恢复。

en:
Qamdo, Chab-mdo in Tibetan, takes its name from the meeting of the waters: the Dza and Ngom rivers join below the town to form the Mekong, and the caravan roads out of Sichuan and Yunnan all funnel through this gap on the way to Lhasa. Tea, salt and wool changed hands beneath its cliffs, yet the town's real master was the monastery on the terraced hill above it. In 1373 the sixteen-year-old Tsongkhapa, travelling from Amdo, spent a night at the river junction and dreamt of the arhat Bakula; he foretold that a great house of learning would one day stand there. His disciple Sherab Sangpo, counted among the six 'banner-holders' who upheld the teaching on the borderlands, founded Jampaling in 1437 (1444 by another account), the first Gelugpa monastery in Kham. In time it ran twelve monastic colleges, held more than five thousand monks and oversaw seventy dependent houses. In 1444 it was still a young house, sharing a fractious Kham with local chiefs who answered to no distant king.

Its abbots were at first appointed from outside, until in 1594 the third Pakpalha incarnation became the fourteenth abbot; the Pakpalha tulkus then ruled Jampaling as its lamas and the district's princes, through monastic and civil officials who administered five small dzongs and eighteen estates. The Bon king of Beri sacked the monastery's main buildings during his raids across Kham, and when Güshi Khan's Khoshut Mongols destroyed Beri in 1639-1640 the fourth Pakpalha received a patent ordering all central Kham to obey him. The sixth Pakpalha aided the Kangxi Emperor's surveyors bound for the Kailash range and in 1719 received an imperial title and a copper seal, the first of the Qing patents that registered the lineage among the great reincarnating hierarchies of the frontier. The caravans never stopped below the terraced halls, and every year the monks laid out their butter sculptures and performed the masked Guqing dance.
zh:
昌都，藏语意为「两江汇合处」：扎曲与昂曲在城下相汇成澜沧江，四川、云南往拉萨去的商道都要从这道山口穿过。茶、盐、羊毛在崖下易手，城镇真正的主人却是坡上台地上的大寺。1373年，十六岁的宗喀巴从安多赴拉萨学经，在两河交汇处夜宿一晚，梦见十六罗汉中的巴古拉，便预言此地日后当建一座大道场。他的弟子、位列「边远护持圣教六大旗手」之一的西绕松布，后来于1437年（另说1444年）创建强巴林寺，这是康区第一座格鲁派寺院。寺院最盛时下设十二座扎仓，僧众五千余人，下辖七十座属寺，号称康东第一大寺。1444年的它还年轻，与各地头人分治着纷乱的康区，无人听命于远方的君王。

建寺之初法台由外聘高僧出任；1594年第三世帕巴拉活佛就任第十四任法台，此后历世帕巴拉既是寺中教主，又是昌都的行政首领，设僧官、俗官两套衙门，管辖五个小宗、十八个甲本区。白利土司横扫康区时，强巴林寺的主要建筑被其捣毁；1639至1640年固始汗率和硕特蒙古攻灭白利，第四世帕巴拉获颁照票，命中部康区各地听其号令。第六世帕巴拉因配合康熙帝派往冈底斯山勘界的人员，1719年受封「阐讲黄法额尔德尼那门汗」并赐铜印，帕巴拉世系列入清朝册封的边疆大活佛。台地殿宇之下商队往来不绝，寺中每年陈列酥油花、跳古钦神舞。

en:
Markam, Smra-khams or the 'goodly land' in Tibetan, fills the high pastures and gorges where the upper Mekong cuts through the Hengduan ranges at the meeting of Sichuan, Yunnan and Tibet, facing the Bathang country across the Jinsha to the east; later Chinese gazetteers noted that most of its people lived by their herds and tilled no fields. Its fame was salt. At Tsakalo, the 'salt wells' of Yanjing in the southern gorges, brine had been drawn from shafts by the Mekong since the days of the Tibetan Empire: salt-makers carried it up from the riverside in wooden tubes, poured it into rows of terraced roofed pools along the banks and let wind and sun do the rest, and the yellow salt of the east bank and the red salt of the west bank travelled across Kham on yak backs. The Sichuan-Tibet road ran through the country and the Yunnan caravan route joined it. In 1444 the local chiefs held Ming tusi titles, but Markam, like the rest of Kham, obeyed no single ruler.

In the late Ming the Naxi chiefs of Lijiang pushed up the Jinsha and held the Bathang country, the salt wells with it, for about seventy years, until Güshi Khan's campaign of 1639-1640 against Beri gave the country to the Khoshut, who posted sde-pa officials to Bathang and Lithang to collect taxes. In 1719 the Qing general Yue Zhongqi marched two thousand men on Bathang and its sde-pa surrendered; in 1726 the court delimited the three-province border along the Ningjing Hills, set up a marker stele and assigned Bathang to Sichuan. Markam kept its place as a stage on the great road into Tibet, and the riverside terraces went on making salt.
zh:
芒康，藏语意为「善妙之地」，地处横断山脉腹地、川滇藏三地交界处，澜沧江上游的高原牧场与深山峡谷多在其境内，东隔金沙江与巴塘相望。后来的汉文方志记载，当地居民多以牧畜为生，不事田亩。这里以盐出名。南部河谷中的察卡洛，汉语称盐井，自吐蕃时期便从澜沧江畔的竖井汲取卤水：盐民把卤水装进木筒背上岸，倒入两岸一排排架起的屋顶式盐池，借风日晒干，东岸出黄盐、西岸出红盐，再由牦牛驮队贩运康区各地。川藏大路穿境而过，云南来的商道也在此接入。1444年，当地首领虽受明朝土司封号，芒康却与整个康区一样，没有统辖全境的君王。

明末，丽江木氏土司势力越过金沙江北上，统治巴塘地方约七十一年，盐井也在境内；固始汗1639至1640年攻灭白利后，地方归于和硕特蒙古，第巴分驻巴塘、里塘征税。1719年，清将岳钟琪率兵两千进逼巴塘，巴塘第巴归降；1726年清廷沿宁静山勘定川滇藏边界，立碣为界，巴塘划归四川。此后芒康仍是川藏大路上的台站，江边层层盐田也一直照晒不误。

en:
Dege lies in northern Kham, where the upper Yangtze cuts through steep gorges below high yak pastures. In 1444 it was a small Vajrayana Buddhist kingdom ruled by the Gar clan, a family that traced its line to Gar Tongtsen, minister to Songtsen Gampo, and had held estates here since the thirteenth century. Barley farmers worked the river valleys, nomads pastured yaks on the high ground, and Derge metalworkers gave the court a practical name as well as a Buddhist one. The royal seat took shape at Gengqing in 1448, when Bota Tashi Sengge moved his household there and joined Thang Tong Gyalpo in founding the Tanggya chapel. Gongchen Monastery later became the Sakya temple closely tied to the royal family.

War helped enlarge the kingdom. In 1639 Güshi Khan's Qoshot Mongols marched into Kham against the Bon king of Beri; Derge forces joined the campaign, and after Beri fell its rulers took the title of Dharma King and expanded until the kingdom held twelve to fifteen thousand households. Qing recognition came in 1728 with a tusi title, while Dege's wider fame came from its press. Tenpa Tsering founded the Parkhang beside Gongchen in 1729, his son enlarged it, and carvers cut blocks for the Kangyur, Tengyur, Nyingma tantras, Sakya treatises and Bon texts. By the end of the century the printing house held more than two hundred thousand blocks. The court also patronised Situ Panchen, a scholar, painter and physician, and two queens ruled in their own right. The last, Tsewang Lhamo, commissioned the collected Nyingma tantras before her death in 1812. In 1821 monks, carvers and metalworkers still made Dege one of the busiest religious centres in eastern Tibet.
zh:
德格位于康北，金沙江上游切过陡峭峡谷，高处是放牧牦牛的牧场。1444年，这里是噶尔家族统治的金刚乘佛教小王国；该家族自称出自松赞干布的大臣噶尔·东赞一系，从13世纪起便领有当地庄园。河谷居民种植青稞，高原牧民放牧牦牛，德格工匠的金属手艺也让这个王庭兼具宗教与实务之名。1448年，博塔·扎西森根把家族驻地移到更庆，并与汤东杰布共同修建汤甲经堂，王都的格局开始形成。后来的贡钦寺是萨迦派寺院，也与德格王室关系密切。

战争扩大了这个王国。1639年，固始汗率和硕特蒙古军队进入康区，讨伐信奉苯教的白利王；德格军队参战，白利败亡后，德格统治者采用法王称号，并把领地扩张到有一万二千至一万五千户的规模。1728年，清朝授予德格王土司头衔；让德格声名远播的则是印经院。却吉·登巴泽仁1729年在贡钦寺旁创建德格印经院，其子加以扩建，刻工为《甘珠尔》《丹珠尔》、宁玛派密续、萨迦派论书乃至苯教经文雕版。到18世纪末，院藏经版已超过二十万块。王庭还赞助过兼通学问、绘画和医术的司徒·班钦，并有两位女王亲自执政。末代女王策旺拉姆在1812年去世前主持刊印宁玛派密续总集。1821年，僧人、刻工和金属工匠仍使德格保持为卫藏以东最繁忙的宗教中心之一。

en:
Rebgong is the Rongwo River valley in Amdo. Its Tibetan tribes keep sheep, yaks and horses on high pastures above the Yellow River, while barley fields and painters' villages occupy the lower ground. Monasteries across Amdo knew the valley for Regong art: villagers in Wutun and nearby hamlets painted thangkas, made sculptures and appliqué hangings, and prepared bright mineral colours for religious walls and scrolls. A Sakyapa shrine called Zhikha Lhakhang stood on the site of Rongwo Monastery from 1301. In 1444 the twelve Rebgong tribes still followed their own chiefs and lamas, and the Ming court held them through titles rather than resident officials.

Rongwo Monastery gave the valley its lasting form of government. Samten Rinchen rebuilt it in 1462, and his brother Lodro Sengge received a Ming National Preceptor title after becoming abbot; later lamas ruled as monks and chiefs together. The monastery joined the Gelug order in 1605 and received a Tianqi reign plaque in 1622. Its first Shartsang incarnation, Kaldan Gyatso, opened the dialectical college in 1630 and, under the title Erdeni Nangso, governed the twelve tribes of the Rongwo valley and the Zekog pastures. Regong painters carried their thangkas and appliqué work to monasteries across Amdo, while the Qing-era Shartsang incarnations continued the old preceptors' rule.
zh:
热贡是安多隆务河流域的河谷。藏族部落在黄河上游的高山牧场放牧绵羊、牦牛和马，低地分布着农田和画师村落。安多各处寺院熟悉这里的热贡艺术：五屯及附近村寨的画师绘制唐卡，制作塑像和堆绣，也为宗教壁画与卷轴调配鲜亮的矿物颜料。1301年，萨迦派小寺智卡贡康已立于今隆务寺所在地。1444年，热贡十二部族仍听从本族头人和喇嘛，明朝只以封号维系，不派常驻官员。

隆务寺后来成为这片河谷的政教中心。1462年，三木旦仁钦重建寺院；其弟罗哲森格继任法台后获明朝封为国师，此后的寺僧兼具僧侣与首领身份。隆务寺1605年改宗格鲁派，1622年获天启年间赐匾。1630年，第一世夏日仓活佛蔼丹嘉措设立显宗学院，并以「额尔德尼昂锁」的身份统辖隆务河谷和泽库草原的十二部族。热贡画师把唐卡与堆绣送往安多各处寺院，清代的夏日仓活佛系统则延续了旧日国师的统治。

en:
Garzê sits in the highland barley valleys of the upper Yalong, in the northern Kham country called Hor, or Tréshö. Tibetan histories give its lords a Mongol forebear: when Phagpa passed through in the 1260s, a Mongol prince sent with him by Kublai Khan fathered a son, Hor Namgyal, on a woman of the country, and Hor Namgyal's descendants subdued the neighbouring tribes. These same pastures had earlier produced Düsum Khyenpa (1110-1193), the first Karmapa and founder of the Karma Kagyu order. In 1444 the Trehor and Dzakhok clans herded their yaks and sowed barley along the river, their castles guarding the northern caravan road, while the ancient Achak Dru house that had long ruled Tréshö was nearing the end of its male line.

That line failed before the century was out, and Namkha Gyaltsen, heir of Hor Namgyal, married his son to the Achak Dru heiress and joined the country from Dzakhok in the west to Draggo and Dawu in the east; on his death his sons divided the lands into the Five Hor States, Mazur, Khangsar, Trehor, Draggo and Beri, whose castles ringed the growing Garzê market. Fiercest was Bon Beri: under Dönyö Dorjé its raiders reached Qamdo, Riwoche and Markam, wrecked Jampaling's main halls and harried the Gelug monasteries, until at the call of the Fifth Dalai Lama and the Panchen Lama, Güshi Khan of the Khoshut marched into Kham in 1639 and, aided by Derge, destroyed Beri within a year and put its king to death. About 1642 the Khoshut founded Kandze Monastery on the hill above the Mazur and Khangsar castles, its pilgrim circuit nearly eight kilometres long; it came to hold fifteen hundred monks and ranked with Qamdo's Jampaling among the greatest houses in Kham. In 1728 Beri and the other Hor chiefs submitted to the Qing and were enrolled as tusi, and the barley valley of Garzê remained a caravan stage on the northern road into Tibet.
zh:
甘孜位于雅砻江上游的青稞谷地，属康北称「霍尔」（藏语作「哲雪」）的地方。藏文史籍给当地首领记了一位蒙古先祖：13世纪60年代八思巴经过此地时，忽必烈派来随行的一位蒙古王子与当地女子生下霍尔南嘉，他的后裔逐步臣服周边部落，是为霍尔诸部的先祖。更早的时候，这片牧场还出生过第一世噶玛巴杜松虔巴（1110—1193），噶玛噶举派的创始人。1444年，朱倭、扎科的氏族在雅砻江边放牧牦牛、种植青稞，寨堡守着北路商道，而久主哲雪的古老氏族阿察布鲁男嗣将绝。

该氏在15世纪末绝嗣，霍尔南嘉的后人南喀坚赞让儿子娶阿察布鲁家的独女，把西起扎科、东到炉霍、道孚的土地合为一国；南喀坚赞死后，诸子分家，形成麻书、孔撒、朱倭、章谷、白利五大霍尔土司，寨堡环立在日渐兴盛的甘孜镇边。五部中最强悍的是奉苯教的白利：土司顿月多吉的骑兵远达昌都、类乌齐、芒康，捣毁过强巴林寺的主要殿宇，四处攻掠格鲁派寺院。应五世达赖喇嘛和四世班禅之请，固始汗于1639年进军康区，在德格土司相助下一年内攻灭白利，擒杀顿月多吉。约1642年，和硕特蒙古在麻书、孔撒两寨上方的山头兴建甘孜寺，转经山道将近八公里长，最盛时僧众一千五百人，与昌都强巴林寺并称康区最大的寺院。1728年，白利与霍尔各部首领归附清朝，受封长官司等土司世职，青稞丰饶的甘孜谷地仍是川藏北路上的商队要站。

en:
Xuanhua lies in the basin of the Yang River between the Inner and Outer Great Wall, the last strong place on the road from the steppe to the Juyong Pass and Beijing. Its walls began in the Tianbao reign of the eighth century as the Xiongwu fortress An Lushan raised at Feihu; under the Liao it was the seat of Guihua Prefecture, and under the Jin and Yuan a small garrison behind an earthen rampart. The Ming turned it into a city of soldiers. In 1394 Zhu Hui, Prince of Gu, enlarged the town to a walled circuit of more than twenty-four li with seven gates; five years later, when he was stripped of his princedom in the Jingnan civil war, three gates were sealed and only four remained. In the Zhengtong reign the censor Luo Hongxin faced the crumbling rammed-earth wall with grey brick and gave it barbicans, enceintes and a moat. In 1444 Xuanhua was the headquarters of the Xuanfu Garrison, one of the Nine Border Garrisons and seat of the high command coordinating Xuanfu, Datong and Shanxi, a crowded town of troops, military households and camp traders living off the garrison and the basin's grain fields.

Five years later border war reached Xuanhua. In 1449 Esen's Oirats destroyed the imperial army at Tumu Post, in the Xuanfu sector, and led the Zhengtong Emperor away captive; through the panic the walled towns of the command held, and the dynasty weathered the crisis behind Yu Qian's defence of Beijing. For the rest of the Ming, Xuanhua kept its martial character, its Zhenshuo and Qingyuan towers rising over the central avenue. Under the Qing the wall ceased to be a frontier. In 1693 the Kangxi Emperor turned the old garrison into a civilian prefecture, Xuanhua Fu, 'proclaiming civilisation', the first prefectural city west of the capital; in 1757 nearly a hundred and twenty thousand taels were spent renewing its crenellations, gun platforms and rampart walks.
zh:
宣化地处洋河河谷盆地，夹在内、外两道长城之间，是草原通往居庸关和北京的大路上最后一处可守的重镇。其城始于8世纪唐天宝年间安禄山在飞狐塞修筑的雄武城，辽代为归化州治所，金、元两代只是土墙后面的一处屯驻军。明代把它变成一座兵城：1394年，就藩于此的谷王朱橞展扩城池，城墙周长超过二十四里，开有七门；五年后靖难之役爆发，他被削藩，三道城门遭封堵，只留四门。正统年间，都御史罗亨信给容易倾颓的夯土城墙外包灰砖，又添筑瓮城、月城和城壕。1444年的宣化是九边重镇之一宣府镇的驻地，也是节制宣府、大同、山西三镇的军门重地，城中挤满驻军、军户和随军商贩，靠着军镇和盆地里的粮田过活。

五年后，边事烧到了宣府。1449年，瓦剌也先在宣府镇地界的土木堡击溃御驾亲征的明军，俘走明英宗；混乱之中，防区内的城寨守住了，朝廷靠于谦主持北京守备度过危局。此后有明一代，宣府始终不改尚武本色，镇朔楼、清远楼矗立在城中干道上。入清以后，长城不再是边防线。1693年（康熙三十二年），康熙帝改宣府镇为宣化府，取「宣扬教化」之意，号称「京西第一府」；1757年又耗白银近十二万两，新修垛口、海墁和炮台。

en:
Daming lies on the grain plain where southern Hebei meets Henan and Shandong, and the Wei River, the old course of the Sui-Tang Yongji Canal, carries boat traffic through its fields. Under the Tang its city, Weizhou, was counted among the six 'grand prefectures' of the empire. After the An Lushan rebellion it became the headquarters of the Weibo, or Tianxiong, military governorship, the strongest of the three Hebei garrisons that answered to no court; in 782 the governor Tian Yue raised Weizhou to a prefecture and named it Daming, taking a line from Sima Qian, 'Wei is a great name'. The place had a hand in several dynasties: Li Cunxu proclaimed himself emperor at Weizhou on his way to founding the Later Tang, and Guo Wei marched south from his post at Yedu to found the Later Zhou. Nearby Yuancheng was the home of the Wang clan from which Wang Mang rose to seize the Han throne in AD 9. The Northern Song made Daming its auxiliary capital Beijing, the bulwark facing the Liao capital at Yanjing and the greatest city in Hebei, called the lock and key of the northern gate. The Jin kept it as a prefectural seat and the Yuan as a route. In 1401 floods on the Zhang and Wei swamped the Song city and buried it in silt; the commander Wu Mi built a new walled seat north of Aijiaokou. In 1444, therefore, Ming Daming was still a young city in the Northern Metropolitan Region, with Yuancheng County attached and its markets fed by plain grain and Wei River boats.

Under the Ming, Prefect Xiong Xiang built towers over the four gates in 1472, and in 1565 Prefect Yao Ruxun had the walls faced with brick and stone. The early Qing planned to seat the governor-general of Zhili, Shandong and Henan here in 1648, and the restored viceroy of Zhili kept his residence at Daming from 1661 until the office was abolished in 1669. Readers of the novel Water Margin know the city as the home of Lu Junyi, the 'Jade Qilin', whom the Liangshan outlaws rescue in the chapters on their great assault on Daming Prefecture.
zh:
大名位于冀南与河南、山东相接的产粮平原，卫河即隋唐永济渠故道，舟船穿境而过。唐代这里称魏州，列为天下「六雄」之一。安史之乱后，魏州是魏博（天雄军）节度使驻地，为河朔三镇中最强的一镇；782年节度使田悦升魏州为府，取《史记》「万，盈数也；魏，大名也」一句，定名大名。五代时这里几度牵动皇统：李存勖在魏州称帝，进而建立后唐；郭威也从邺都南下，建立后周。邻近的元城是王莽家族的故里，族中王莽于公元9年代汉建新。北宋以大名府为陪都北京，北对辽朝燕京，是河北最大的城市，号称「北门锁钥」。金代仍为府治，元代设大名路。1401年漳河、卫河洪水灌城，宋城淤没于泥沙之下，都指挥使吴宓在艾家口镇北另筑新城。因此到1444年，明代北直隶治下的大名还是一座年轻的府城，元城县附郭，城中市集靠平原粮食和卫河舟楫支撑。

明代，知府熊祥于1472年修建四门城楼，1565年知府姚如循又将城墙包以砖石。清初的1648年，朝廷预定以大名府为直隶山东河南三省总督驻地；1661年复置直隶总督，驻节大名，至1669年裁撤。在小说《水浒传》里，大名府是「玉麒麟」卢俊义的故乡，梁山好汉搭救卢俊义、兵打大名府的几回写的就是这座城。

en:
Wuding is the flat grain country of the northern Shandong plain, where the Tuhai River runs north towards the mudflats of the Bohai coast. Under the Ming it was Le'an, a sub-prefecture of Jinan Prefecture, and the new dynasty settled fresh villages on land the wars had emptied. In 1420 it produced the strangest rising of the early Ming: Tang Sai'er, a martial master's daughter from Putai, preached the White Lotus teaching and called herself the Buddha Mother. She gathered followers at Xieshipeng, took the towns of Ju and Jimo and defeated several imperial forces before her army was broken at Anqiu; after the defeat she slipped away among the sympathetic villagers and was never caught.

Le'an also held the fief of Zhu Gaoxu, the Yongle Emperor's second son and a hard-riding cavalry commander of the Jingnan campaign. In 1426 he rebelled there against his nephew the Xuande Emperor, who on Yang Rong's advice took the field himself; the prince surrendered within a month and Le'an was renamed Wuding. Held prisoner in Beijing, he later hooked the emperor's leg and threw him to the ground during a visit, for which he was put to death by burning. In 1444 Wuding was a quiet grain-growing sub-prefecture under Jinan. It passed to Li Zicheng and then to the Qing in 1644, became an independent sub-prefecture in 1724, and in 1734 was raised to Wuding Prefecture, with the new county of Huimin as its seat.
zh:
武定是鲁北平原上的平坦粮乡，徒骇河北流入渤海湾的滩涂海岸。明代这里是济南府乐安州，新王朝在战乱抛荒的土地上招民垦殖，建起新村。1420年，明初最奇特的一场民变起于此地：蒲台人唐赛儿是武师之女，传白莲教，自称「佛母」。她在卸石棚聚众，攻下莒州、即墨，连败官军，所部后来在安丘被击溃；兵败之后她混在乡民之中脱身，始终没有被抓到。

乐安还是朱高煦的封地。他是明成祖第二子，靖难之役中以敢打硬仗的骑兵将领闻名；1426年他在这里起兵反叛侄子明宣宗，宣宗纳杨荣之谏御驾亲征，不到一个月朱高煦就出城投降，乐安州随即改名武定州。被囚在北京时，他又在宣宗探视之际伸脚把皇帝勾倒，最终遭炮烙处死。1444年的武定是济南府治下安静的粮作州城。1644年它先归李自成，随后归清；1724年升为直隶州，1734年再升武定府，以新设的惠民县为府治。

en:
Laizhou's prefectural seat was Ye County, a walled port on the eastern shore of Laizhou Bay, the southern bight of the Bohai Sea. Han administrators placed Donglai Commandery there, the Sui gave the prefecture its present name in 585, and the Ming made it Laizhou Prefecture in 1376, with authority over the eastern Shandong peninsula. In 1444 fishing boats and salt barges worked the shallow bay, while coasters carried Shandong grain, fish and salt between ports around the Bohai. Behind the anchorage, Ye County's walls made it the nearest major prefectural city west of Dengzhou.

The city's hardest test came in the Wuqiao mutiny. Kong Youde and Geng Zhongming, former officers under Mao Wenlong, rebelled in the winter of 1631, took Dengzhou early in 1632 and turned on Ye County. Prefect Zhu Wannian held Laizhou with the governors Xu Congzhi and Xie Lian. Rebel cannon killed Xu in the fourth month; in the seventh Kong offered a false surrender, and Zhu and Xie were seized when they came out to announce the pardon. Zhu refused to call the garrison out and was killed, while Xie died later that year, but Laizhou never opened its gates. Ming armies broke the revolt in 1633, and Kong crossed the Bohai with his surviving men to join the Manchus. Manchu raiders under Abatai reached Laizhou and Dengzhou in 1642, and after the Ming collapse in 1644 the prefecture passed to the Qing.
zh:
莱州府的治所是掖县，一座位于莱州湾东岸的海港城。莱州湾是渤海南部的大海湾，汉代已在此设东莱郡，585年隋代改置莱州，1376年明朝升为莱州府，管辖山东半岛东部。1444年，渔船和盐船在浅湾往来，沿岸海船把山东的粮食、渔获和海盐运销渤海各港；锚地后的掖县城池，则是登州以西最近的重要府城。

吴桥兵变是掖县城最严酷的一战。1631年冬，毛文龙旧部孔有德、耿仲明举兵反叛，1632年初攻占登州，随后进围莱州。知府朱万年与山东巡抚徐从治、登莱巡抚谢琏登城守御。四月，徐从治死于叛军炮火；七月，孔有德诈降，朱万年、谢琏出城宣谕时被俘。孔有德命朱万年劝降，朱万年不从被杀，谢琏也在当年死去，莱州却没有破城。1633年明军平定叛乱，孔有德率残部渡渤海投奔后金。1642年阿巴泰入塞时，清军掠至莱州、登州一带；1644年明朝灭亡后，莱州府归入清朝。

en:
Yanzhou covers the rolling country of southern Shandong, with its seat at Ziyang, the old town of Xiaqiu, and borrows its name from one of the Nine Provinces of the Yu Gong. Two things gave the prefecture its weight. The Grand Canal crossed it at Jining, carrying the southern grain tribute north to Beijing, and within its bounds lay Qufu, the home of Confucius, and Zouxian, the home of Mencius; the Duke Yansheng, Confucius's direct heir, kept the family temple at Qufu. It was also a princely fief. In 1385 the Hongwu Emperor enfeoffed his tenth son Zhu Tan there as Prince of Lu. A patron of scholars who wrote poetry, Zhu Tan died in January 1390 after taking alchemical elixirs that poisoned his eyes, and the court gave him the unsparing posthumous name Huang, 'the Dissolute'; his son held the fief for sixty-four years. In 1444 Yanzhou was one of Shandong's foremost princely seats, guarding the south of the province.

In 1499 lightning struck the Temple of Confucius at Qufu and burned the Great Completion Hall with more than a hundred and twenty bays of buildings; the court rebuilt it over five years at a cost of 150,000 taels. The Ming itself ended here in the fifth Manchu inroad: in the tenth month of 1642 Abatai's army stormed Yanzhou, killed the Prince of Lu Zhu Yipai, and burned three of the city's four gates in a single day. Two centuries of treasure piled up in the Lu palace were carried off. The dead prince's younger brother Zhu Yihai escaped, and after the fall of Beijing he fled south to lead the Southern Ming resistance as prince-regent, fighting on along the coast until his death in 1662. Under the Qing, Yanzhou kept its standing. In 1684 the Kangxi Emperor came in person to sacrifice to Confucius at Qufu, where the sixty-fourth-generation descendant Kong Shangren lectured before him; he later won fame for the play The Peach Blossom Fan. Lightning fired the temple again in 1724, and the Yongzheng Emperor had it rebuilt over six years.
zh:
兖州是鲁南的起伏乡野，府城设在滋阳，即旧城瑕丘，州名借自《禹贡》九州之一。这座府城的分量来自两样东西。大运河在济宁穿过府境，把南方漕粮运往北方的北京；府中还有孔子故里曲阜和孟子故里邹县，孔子嫡裔衍圣公世守曲阜的孔氏家庙。这里同时是藩王封地。1385年明太祖封第十子朱檀为鲁王，就藩兖州。朱檀礼待文士、能写诗歌，却在洪武二十二年十二月（1390年1月）服食丹药，毒发伤目而死，朝廷给了他毫不留情的谥号「荒」；其子嗣位，在藩长达六十四年。1444年的兖州是山东最重要的藩府之一，镇守鲁南。

1499年，雷电击中曲阜孔庙，大成殿连同一百二十余楹建筑烧成灰烬；朝廷历时五年重修，耗银十五万两。明朝本身也在这里走到末路：1642年十月清军第五次入塞，阿巴泰所部攻陷兖州，杀鲁王朱以派，四座城门有三座在同一天烧毁，鲁王府二百余年积蓄的财物被洗劫一空。死者之弟朱以海逃出，北京陷落后南下，以鲁王监国统领南明抗清，退守沿海，直到1662年去世。入清以后兖州仍保其地位。1684年康熙帝亲临曲阜祭孔，孔子六十四代孙孔尚任在御前讲经，他后来以剧作《桃花扇》闻名。1724年雷电再次引燃孔庙，雍正帝历时六年将它重修。

en:
Xuzhou, the ancient Pengcheng, guards the gap between the Shandong hills and the North China Plain where four provinces meet, on the old confluence of the Si and Bian rivers. It is the homeland of the Han imperial house: Liu Bang was born at Pei within its borders, and in 206 BC Xiang Yu made Pengcheng the capital of his Western Chu. The princes of Chu went to nearby tombs in gold-threaded jade suits; the Shizishan tomb held the rebel Liu Wu of the Seven States Rebellion. Under the Northern Song the Liguo works north of the city became one of the empire's greatest iron centres, with thirty-six private smelters and thousands of foundrymen, and in 1077 Su Shi raised the Su Embankment against a Yellow River flood. The Jurchen took the city in 1129, and in 1352 the Yuan chancellor Toqto stormed it, crushing the Red Turban rebel 'Sesame Li' and reopening the grain route; he renamed the city Wu'an. After the Yellow River turned into the Huai, Ming Xuzhou lived by the Grand Canal, with a great state granary and one of the seven customs barriers; tens of thousands of corvée boatmen and rapids haulers dragged junks through the Xuzhou and Lüliang rapids below the walls. In 1444 it was a rich, flood-prone transport hub where iron and tribute grain changed hands at the wharves.

The Yellow River undid that prosperity: after the 'flush the silt with clear water' policy of 1579 piled silt against the city, its embankments stood as high as the walls by the 1590s. In 1605 the new Jia Canal drew the main canal route off to the north-east to bypass the rapids, most junks abandoned the wharves and trade drained away. In 1624 a breach buried the walled city under four metres of water and sediment. One of the Southern Ming's Four Jiangbei Garrisons, Xuzhou fell to Qing armies in mid-1645; the scholars Yan Ermei and Wan Shouqi refused to serve the new dynasty and were remembered as the Two Ming Loyalists of Xuzhou. The Tancheng earthquake of 1668 wrecked much of what remained. The Qing later made Xuzhou a prefecture seated at Tongshan, ruling the border counties of four provinces.
zh:
徐州古称彭城，扼守山东丘陵与华北平原之间、四省交界的缺口，古为泗水、汴水交汇处。这里是汉朝皇室的故乡：刘邦生于境内沛县，公元前206年项羽以彭城为西楚都城；汉代楚王死后着金缕玉衣葬在城外山陵，狮子山楚王陵的主人就是七国之乱中的叛王刘戊。北宋时，城北的利国监是全国最大的冶铁中心之一，三十六处民营冶场、工匠数千；1077年苏轼主持修筑苏堤，抵御黄河洪水。1129年金兵攻占徐州；1352年元丞相脱脱攻破州城，镇压红巾军首领「芝麻李」、重开漕运粮道，并把徐州改名武安。黄河夺淮以后，明代的徐州靠大运河为生，城中设有大型官仓和全国七处钞关之一；数以万计的民夫和洪夫在城下的徐州洪、吕梁洪间挽舟过险。1444年的徐州是富庶而多水患的漕运枢纽，铁器和漕粮在码头转手。

黄河最终冲掉了这方家业：1579年推行「蓄清刷黄」，泥沙在徐州城边越积越多，到1590年代堤防已经与城墙齐高。1605年泇河完工，把大运河主航道引向东北以避开险滩，多数舟楫不再经过徐州，市面随之萧条。1624年黄河决口，洪水和泥沙把州城深埋四米。徐州是南明江北四镇之一，1645年年中被清军攻取；乡绅阎尔梅、万寿祺坚不仕清，并称「徐州二遗民」。1668年郯城大地震又毁掉大半城郭。清代后来升徐州为府，以铜山县为府治，管辖四省交界的州县。

en:
Huai'an sits on the North Jiangsu plain where the Grand Canal crosses the old course of the Huai River. In 486 BC the king of Wu, Fuchai, cut the Hangou Canal here to carry his fleets from the Yangtze northward, and the place has lived by water ever since. In 1128 Song troops breached the Yellow River dikes to stop a Jin advance; the river then seized the Si and lower Huai channels, its silt building coastal flats toward the sea and swelling Hongze Lake, so floods became the city's permanent burden. Ming Huai'an Prefecture reached east to the salt-boiling and fishing coast around Yancheng. The Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan, who ran state grain transport for thirty years under the Yongle Emperor, dredged the old Sha River channel into the Qingjiangpu in 1410 and built four locks; four state shipyards and rows of imperial granaries made the town the throat of the grain-fleet route. In 1444 Huai'an is the canal's grain-transport hub: the grain barges were built and repaired in its yards, and travellers changed here from southern boats to northern horses.

North-bank Huaiyin was the home of Han Xin, a poor local youth who became the Han dynasty's greatest general in the war against Xiang Yu. River commissioners sat in Huai'an too, and the Wanli-era Pan Jixun fought the Yellow River's silt with long dikes that penned the current to scour the bed, and kept raising the Gaojia weir above Hongze Lake. The city's most famous writer was Wu Cheng'en (1506–1582) of Shanyang, who composed Journey to the West here and gave Chinese fiction its Monkey King. The wars of the Ming-Qing transition swept up and down the canal, and under the Qing, Haizhou and the northern counties were split from Huai'an, though both the grain-transport and southern-river director-generals kept their seats here, the Qingjiangpu yards and warehouses stretching for miles. In the 1760s the Qinghe county seat, wrecked by flood, moved into busy Qingjiangpu, by then the true pivot of canal traffic.
zh:
淮安在苏北平原上，正当大运河穿过淮河故道的地方。公元前486年，吴王夫差在此开凿邗沟，把舟师从长江引向北方，这座城此后一直靠水立足。1128年，宋军为阻挡金兵掘开黄河大堤，黄河随即夺泗水和淮河下游入海，泥沙在东边淤出大片滩地，也垫高了洪泽湖，水患成了淮安世世代代的负担。明代淮安府辖地向东一直伸到盐城一带煮海为盐、以渔为业的海滨。平江伯陈瑄为永乐皇帝总督漕运三十年，1410年循沙河故道挑浚成清江浦，建起四道闸门；四大官营船厂与成排的皇家仓廒，使淮安成为漕船航路的咽喉。1444年的淮安是大运河上的漕运总枢：漕船在当地的船厂修造，旅人则在这里下南船、换北马。

北岸的淮阴是韩信故里，他后来成了汉朝击败项羽的第一名将。治河大臣也常驻淮安，万历年间的潘季驯以长堤束水攻沙，一再加高洪泽湖一线的高家堰。城里最有名的文人是山阳县人吴承恩（1506—1582），他在这里写成《西游记》，为中国小说造出一个孙悟空。明末清初的战火沿运河来回席卷；入清以后，海州与北部各县被析出，但漕运总督和南河总督仍驻节淮安，清江浦的船厂仓廒绵延数十里。1760年代，毁于洪水的清河县城迁入热闹的清江浦，那时这里已是运河上真正的总枢。

en:
On the middle Huai, Fengyang was the ancient Zhongli and later the seat of Haozhou, an obscure county town until it gave China a dynasty. Zhu Yuanzhang was born here in 1328 to a poor farming family. When famine and plague carried off his family in 1344, he took vows at the Huangjue Monastery before joining the Red Turban rebels who made him the Hongwu Emperor, founder of the Ming. Ruling from Nanjing, in 1369 he ordered a 'Central Capital' built beside Haozhou to the standard of an imperial capital, with Li Shanchang superintending the works; its plan later served as the model for the palace cities the Ming built at Nanjing and Beijing. He raised the Huangling Mausoleum over his parents' grave and moved thousands of families in from Shandong, Shanxi, Hebei, Guangdong and the Taihu country. In 1375, shaken by resistance among the conscripted craftsmen and alarmed at the cost, he abandoned the nearly finished Zhongdu, though the new prefecture and county kept the name Fengyang he had given them. In 1444 the grand walls enclosed a half-empty city, in truth a mausoleum garrison under the vast Fengyang Prefecture of South Zhili, where princes had once drilled troops and Zhu Wengui, son of the dethroned Jianwen Emperor, had been confined since the Yongle reign.

The quiet of the imperial necropolis ended with the collapse of the late Ming. In 1635 the rebel armies of Gao Yingxiang, Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong marched on Fengyang to humble the dynasty and took the city in under ten days, beating the prefect Yan Rongxuan to death and killing sixty court eunuchs and four thousand garrison troops; the city's guardian Zhu Guoxiang fought to the end and killed himself. The rebels freed the prisoners, looted the stores and burned both the Huangling Mausoleum and the Huangjue Monastery. Under the Qing, Fengyang Prefecture passed from Jiangnan Province to Anhui. The Zhongdu palaces were never rebuilt; the county town took over their walls and gate platforms or left them to crumble, while the Huangling's stone figures stood in fields south of the town.
zh:
凤阳地处淮河中游，古为钟离，隋唐以后是濠州治所，本是个不起眼的小县，直到这里走出了一位开国皇帝。1328年，朱元璋出生在当地一户贫苦农家；1344年灾荒和瘟疫夺走他的亲人，他入皇觉寺出家，后来投奔红巾军，成了明太祖。定都南京后，他把无上的荣耀堆给故乡：1369年下诏在濠州以西营建规制一如京师的中都，由李善长主持工程，后来南京、北京的宫城都以它的规划为蓝本；又在父母墓前修建皇陵，并从山东、山西、河北、广东和太湖一带强迁数千户来此充实。1375年，迫于应役工匠的抗争、又惊于工程劳费，他在中都将成之际下诏罢建，新府、新县仍用他赐下的名字——凤阳。1444年的凤阳，宏伟城墙圈着一座半空的城，名为南直隶凤阳府首县，实质是座皇陵驻军之城；皇子诸王曾在此练兵，被废的建文帝之子朱文圭自永乐年间起一直幽禁在皇城里。

皇陵之城的沉寂在明末大乱中终结。1635年，高迎祥、李自成、张献忠等路农民军为挫明朝声威直取中都，不到十日便攻破城池，将知府颜容暄杖杀，又杀宦官六十人、官军四千，留守朱国相力战不敌、自杀而死。农民军开狱放囚、搜刮财物，纵火焚毁明皇陵，连朱元璋曾出家的皇觉寺也付之一炬。入清以后，凤阳府先属江南省，后划归新设的安徽省。中都的宫殿再未重建，城墙和城门台基或被县城沿用，或任其倾颓，皇陵神道两旁的石人石马立在城南的田野间。

en:
Where the Ying River crosses the North Anhui plain to join the Huai, the Qin set up Ruyin County, and in 523 the Northern Wei made the town the seat of Yingzhou, the name it kept for most of the next thousand years. The fighting that made its name came in 1140, when Liu Qi, holding the newly renamed Shunchang Prefecture with fewer than twenty thousand men of his Eight-Character Army, beat off a Jin host put at over a hundred thousand under Wuzhu, one of the Southern Song's most celebrated defensive victories. Ouyang Xiu, the great Northern Song man of letters, retired to Yingzhou, boated on its West Lake and died there in 1072. At the end of Yuan rule the plain produced the rising that undid the dynasty: in 1351 Liu Futong, a Yingzhou man, raised the Red Turban standard here on the strength of White Lotus and Maitreya teaching, and later installed Han Lin'er, the 'Little King of Light', at the head of his Han Song regime. Under the Ming, Yingzhou was a sub-prefecture of Fengyang Prefecture in South Zhili; in 1444 it was an unassuming farming county whose grain was floated down the Ying to the Huai.

Under the Qing it rose in standing. In 1735 the Yongzheng Emperor raised Yingzhou to a full prefecture, Yingzhou Fu, and created Fuyang County as its seat, the first appearance of the name Fuyang. The new prefecture took in the sub-prefecture of Bozhou and five counties across the flat, crowded north-western corner of Anhui, country Qing administrators rated 'busy, worn and hard to govern'. Through the Qing it stayed one of the granaries of the middle Huai, its markets thick along the Ying. The West Lake Ouyang Xiu had written of fared worse: from the Jiaqing reign onward, repeated Yellow River bursts carried silt into it, and the old lake slowly silted up and the resort fell into decay.
zh:
颍河横穿皖北平原，向东南注入淮河。秦代已在此置汝阴县，523年北魏设颍州，此后近千年大半沿用此名。1140年，刘锜率不足两万人的八字军驻守新改的顺昌府，挫败金兀术麾下号称十余万的金军，是南宋最出名的防御大捷之一。北宋文宗欧阳修晚年退居颍州，常游颍州西湖，1072年长逝于此。元末，这片平原走出了掀翻王朝的起义：1351年，颍州人刘福通借白莲教与弥勒信仰聚众，在这里举起红巾军义旗，后来又迎立韩林儿为韩宋政权的小明王。明代，颍州是南直隶凤阳府下辖的散州；1444年的颍州是个朴实的农耕州县，粮食顺颍河运往淮河。

入清以后，颍州的地位上升。1735年（雍正十三年），雍正帝升颍州为颍州府，增设附郭阜阳县为府治，「阜阳」之名第一次出现。新府领亳州和五县，覆盖皖西北平坦稠密的平原，清代考语为「繁、疲、难」，是出名难治的地方。整个清代，这里都是淮河中游的粮仓之一，颍河两岸市集相望。欧阳修吟咏过的颍州西湖却没能保住胜景：嘉庆以后黄河屡次决口，泥沙灌入湖中，湖面渐渐淤塞，当年的名胜衰败下去。

en:
Zhenjiang, the old Jingkou and Runzhou, holds the south bank of the Yangtze where the Grand Canal comes down to join the river, opposite Yangzhou. Grain junks sailing from the delta to the northern capitals and cargoes crossing the Yangtze all had to pass this point. In 209 Sun Quan built a fortress on the Beigu bluff above the ferry, later called the iron-walled city, to guard the approach to his capital upstream. The Song gave the place its present name in 1113, and it kept its name as a battlefield: when Wuzhu's Jin army withdrew north after raiding the south, Han Shizhong and his wife Lady Liang, called Liang Hongyu in later operas, fell on it at the Huangtiandang reach with eight thousand men, and tradition has her beating the war drums from the flagship while the ships blocked the Jin fleet. In the river off the city rose Jinshan with its temple, founded under the Eastern Jin and given the name Jiangtian Chansi by the Kangxi emperor on a southern tour. In 1444 Zhenjiang was a Ming garrison and canal port of Nanzhili, where tribute grain and silk changed hands between river craft and canal boats.

When Southern Ming resistance collapsed downriver in 1645 the city passed to the Qing. In 1659 Zheng Chenggong and Zhang Huangyan sailed a fleet up the Yangtze, seized Zhenjiang and came close to Nanjing before the expedition failed. The Qing then planted a permanent garrison at Jingkou under a vice-commander, Chinese bannermen at first and a Mongol banner force after 1763, whose officers and families took up nearly half the walled city. Through the eighteenth century its wharves stayed one of the busiest trans-shipment points between the Grand Canal, the Yangtze crossing and the sea-going junks trading along the coast.
zh:
镇江古称京口、润州，扼守长江南岸，大运河在此入江，北岸就是扬州。江南粮船北上两京、南北货物横渡长江，都要经过这一处。209年，孙权在渡口旁的北固山高地上筑起军城，后世称铁瓮城，拱卫上游的都城。北宋1113年改润州为镇江府，此地仍以战场闻名：金兀术率金军掳掠江南后北撤，韩世忠与夫人梁氏（后世戏曲中称梁红玉）率八千淮军在黄天荡江面截击，相传她亲自在楼船上擂鼓督战，宋军船队堵住金军退路。城外江中的金山上有金山寺，东晋时始建，康熙帝南巡时赐名江天禅寺。1444年的镇江隶属南直隶，是河防驻军所在和运河港口，漕粮、丝货在这里由江船转驳运河船。

1645年南明沿江防线崩溃，镇江归入清朝。1659年，郑成功、张煌言率水师入江，攻克镇江，进逼南京，北伐最终失败。清朝随后在京口设副都统，常驻重兵，初为汉军八旗，1763年以后改调蒙古八旗，官兵连同家眷占去城内近一半地面。整个18世纪，镇江码头始终是大运河、长江渡口与沿海海船之间最繁忙的转运点之一。

en:
Ningguo is the mountain country in the south-east of Nanzhili, where streams from the Huangshan ranges gather into the Qingyi River and run north to the Yangtze. The prefectural seat Xuancheng stood below Jingting Hill, known as the poetry hill of the south: Xie Tiao governed Xuanzhou at the end of the fifth century and wrote of the hill beyond the walls, and Li Bai climbed it seven times in the Tang age. The prefecture's wealth came from paper. Workshops in Jingxian had made paper since Tang times, when Xuanzhou tribute paper reached the court, and their xuan paper, soft under the brush, moth-resistant and said to last a thousand years, together with the local writing brushes, became the stock on which painters and calligraphers relied. In 1444 Ningguo was a six-county Ming prefecture living by these workshops and by the pack-road trade over its passes into Zhejiang.

Learning outshone arms in the Qing centuries. Mei Wending (1633-1721) of Xuancheng, the foremost astronomer and mathematician of the early Qing, wrote more than eighty works that reconciled the Chinese computational tradition with the Jesuit astronomy newly brought from Europe. In the years of the Ming-Qing transition the monk-painter Shitao, a scion of the fallen Ming imperial house, spent more than ten years at Guangjiao Monastery below Jingting Hill; the landscapes he painted of the Ningguo country and the Huangshan peaks became a model for Qing painters long after he left.
zh:
宁国是南直隶东南的山乡，黄山余脉的溪涧汇成青弋江，向北流入长江。府治宣城坐落在敬亭山下，此山号称「江南诗山」：5世纪末谢朓任宣城太守，写过城边这座山，到了唐代，李白又七度登临。宁国府的名产是纸。泾县纸坊自唐代已开始造纸，宣州贡纸当时便进入宫廷；泾县宣纸受墨温润、久藏不蠹，号称「纸寿千年」，加上同样出名的宣笔，历代书画家挥毫多靠这两样。1444年的宁国府领六县，靠纸坊和翻过山口通往浙江的驮路商贸易为生。

入清以后，此地的名声在学问而不在武功。宣城人梅文鼎（1633—1721）是清初首屈一指的历算名家，著书八十余种，把中国传统算学与欧洲传教士带来的天文历算之学打通。明清易代之际，明宗室后裔、画僧石涛在敬亭山下的广教寺住了十余年，他笔下的宁国丘壑与黄山群峰，在他离去很久以后仍是清代画家取法的范本。

en:
Huizhou fills the narrow valleys of the Huangshan range, short of farmland but long on crafts. The Qin set up counties here, and in 1121 the Song fixed its six, Shexian, Xiuning, Wuyuan, Qimen, Yixian and Jixi, borders that then held for eight hundred years. The thin soil shaped how its people lived: a Ming gazetteer reckoned the harvest fed little more than a tenth of them and that nine households in ten lived by a craft or by peddling goods in other provinces. When Zhu Yuanzhang entered the mountains at the end of the Yuan, Zhu Sheng (1299-1370) of Xiuning gave him the counsel to build high walls, store grain and be slow to claim the throne. Wuyuan was the ancestral home of Zhu Xi (1130-1200), and his Neo-Confucian teaching filled the lineage schools of every valley. Its craftsmen were already famous: the ink maker Li Tinggui, son of Xi Chao and granted the imperial surname by the Southern Tang lord Li Yu, made Xin'an ink a treasure Song collectors prized above gold. In 1444 Huizhou was a Ming prefecture of six counties.

The trading exodus gathered after the salt reform of 1505, when salt licenses could be bought for silver: Huizhou men crowded the salt yards of Lianghuai and Liangzhe and made Yangzhou their base, and by the Wanli reign they stood level with the Shanxi and Shaanxi merchants, no market town complete without a Huizhou man. The pirate coast made and broke two of them. Wang Zhi of Shexian ran an armed fleet from Hirado in Japan until he was beheaded in 1560; Hu Zongxian (1512-1565) of Jixi, supreme commander against the wokou raids, was caught in the fall of Yan Song and died in prison. Learning kept pace with trade: Dai Zhen (1724-1777) of Xiuning, the leading evidential scholar of the Qing, served on the Four Treasuries in Beijing, and Xu Xiake twice climbed Huangshan and named it the strangest mountain under heaven. In 1790 Gao Langting led his Sanqing opera troupe from Yangzhou to Beijing for the emperor's eightieth birthday, and three more Huizhou troupes followed; their erhuang opera was later counted an ancestor of Peking opera.
zh:
徽州是黄山群峰中的山府，川谷狭窄，田少而瘦，手艺与学问却极一时之盛。秦代已在此置县，1121年北宋定名徽州，领歙县、休宁、婺源、祁门、黟县、绩溪六县，这道辖境八百年基本不变。薄田决定了当地人的活路：明代《徽州府志》说，本地一岁所入养不活十分之一的人，十户人家倒有九户靠手艺或挑贩到外省谋生。元末朱元璋兵入山中，休宁人朱升（1299—1370）献上「高筑墙、广积粮、缓称王」三策，为其所纳。婺源是朱熹（1130—1200）的祖籍，他的理学后来充塞了各条山谷里的宗族书院。匠作也早已成名：晚唐奚超父子避乱南来制墨，其子廷珪得南唐后主李煜赏识，赐姓李，李廷珪的新安墨到宋代已成藏家看得比金子还重的珍品。1444年的徽州，是明朝下辖六县的府。

外出经商的大潮在1505年盐法改行开中折色后涌起，商人可在运司纳银领取盐引，徽州人于是挤满两淮、两浙的盐场，以扬州为根基，到万历年间已与山陕商人势均力敌，市井间遂有「无徽不成镇」的说法。东南海疆一造一毁了两个徽州人：歙县人汪直以日本平户为据点统领武装海商集团，1560年被处斩；绩溪人胡宗宪（1512—1565）总督东南、剿平倭寇，却在严嵩倒台时受牵连，1565年死于狱中。学问与商路并进：休宁人戴震（1724—1777）是清代考据学的宗师，晚年在北京的四库全书馆任纂修官；徐霞客两度登临府境上的黄山，誉为「天下第一奇山」。1790年，高朗亭率扬州三庆班入京为乾隆帝贺八十大寿，另外三大徽班随后北上，他们带去的二黄声腔后来被看作京剧的远祖。

en:
Shaoxin, usually written Shaoxing, lies on the shore of Hangzhou Bay where the Kuaiji hills come down to the Qiantang estuary. Early in the fifth century BC, after Goujian of Yue came back from captivity in Wu, his minister Fan Li built a triangular fortress here, the seed of later Shanyin and Kuaiji. Under the Eastern Jin the city was the seat of the governor of Kuaiji: Wang Xizhi, later called the sage of calligraphy, held that post, and in 353 he and his friends gathered at the Orchid Pavilion in the hills southwest of town for the spring purification rite, where he wrote the preface later honoured as the finest work of running script in China. When the Song court fled the Jurchen, Emperor Gaozong took refuge here, and in 1131 his new Shaoxing reign period gave the city its name; Yuezhou became Shaoxing Prefecture and an auxiliary capital of the Southern Song. In 1444 it was a wealthy Ming prefecture of eight counties, with Kuaiji and Shanyin sharing one walled canal city, known for its rice wine, its examination families and the paper moving on its canals.

Its scholars carried the prefecture's name across the empire. Wang Shouren, born in Yuyao in 1472 and usually called Wang Yangming, built the teaching of the School of Mind between official posts that also took him to frontier commands, and in 1519 he suppressed the Prince of Ning's revolt. The painter and playwright Xu Wei was a Shanyin man. After Nanjing and Hangzhou fell to the Qing, Ming loyalists installed Zhu Yihai, Prince of Lu, as regent in Shaoxin on 7 September 1645; his court never worked with the rival Longwu emperor in Fuzhou, and in the summer of 1646 Qing troops crossed the Qiantang and Zhu escaped by sea to Zhoushan. Under the Qing, Shaoxing men staffed the legal offices of officials empire-wide as the Shaoxing masters; Wang Huizu of Xiaoshan, a private secretary who rose to a county magistracy, was held up as the model of that calling, while rice wine and examination households kept the old city busy into the early nineteenth century.
zh:
绍兴位于杭州湾南岸、会稽山北缘，城在钱塘江入海处的水网之间。公元前5世纪初，越王勾践自吴国获释归来，大夫范蠡在此筑起三角形的城邑，即后来山阴、会稽的雏形。东晋时这里是会稽内史的治所：被后世尊为书圣的王羲之曾任此职，353年三月初三，他与友人在城西南兰渚山下的兰亭行修禊之会，乘兴写下后世推为「天下第一行书」的《兰亭集序》。宋廷避金军南下，宋高宗驻跸越州，1131年改元绍兴，越州因年号升为绍兴府，并作南宋陪都。1444年的绍兴府下辖八县，会稽、山阴两县同治一座水网城垣，城中以黄酒、科举世家和运河上的纸张贸易闻名。

绍兴的士子把府名带到全国。1472年生于余姚的王守仁（世称王阳明）在仕途之外立起心学，也曾在边疆统军，1519年平定宁王朱宸濠的叛乱。书画家、戏曲家徐渭是山阴人。南京、杭州陷清后，坚持抗清的明臣于1645年9月7日在绍兴迎立鲁王朱以海监国；鲁王朝廷与福州的隆武帝互不相下，1646年夏清军渡过钱塘江，朱以海由海路逃往舟山。入清以后，绍兴人以刑名师爷的身份在各地官署掌理案牍，人称「绍兴师爷」；萧山人汪辉祖由幕宾做到知县，被这一行奉为典范，黄酒与科举世家则维持着府城到19世纪初的市面。

en:
Ningbo stands at the mouth of the Yong River, on the east edge of the Ningshao Plain, behind the sheltering Zhoushan islands. The Tang set up Mingzhou in 738 and moved its seat to Sanjiangkou in 821, where a walled inner city formed the core of the port; a Song maritime trade office opened in 999, and Mingzhou junks sailed to Goryeo and Japan carrying merchants and Zen monks. The Ming gave the city its present name in 1381, Ningbo, 'calm waves'. In 1444 its maritime office licensed trade with Korea and Japan and received the Japanese tally missions, while coastal garrisons multiplied and the sea bans closed in around Wu-speaking sailors, fishermen and shipwrights.

In May 1523 two Japanese missions, from the rival Hosokawa and Ouchi houses, clashed in the streets over their tally credentials; they killed Ming officers and plundered the countryside, and Beijing answered by closing the Zhejiang and Fujian trade offices. Trade then moved to Shuangyu, an island anchorage south of Zhoushan where Japanese, Portuguese and Southeast Asian merchants dealt goods from 1524 until Ming troops under Zhu Wan destroyed it in 1548; the Portuguese called this coast Liampo. The wokou wars brought Yu Dayou and Qi Jiguang's campaigns to the Zhejiang coast. In 1645 Ningbo's Ming officials surrendered to the Qing, but Zhang Huangyan of Yinxian fought on with a fleet for nearly twenty years until his capture and execution in 1664.

Books gave Ningbo its other name. Fan Qin built the Tianyi Ge library in 1561 and stocked it with more than seventy thousand juan; his heirs kept the books as family common property, never to be divided, and it is the oldest private library still standing in China. In 1676 Huang Zongxi became the first outsider allowed upstairs to read it, and with Quan Zuwang he made the city the centre of the Eastern Zhejiang school. The Qianlong Emperor later had Tianyi Ge measured and copied as the model for the imperial libraries that housed the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries. Qing evacuation orders and sea bans hurt the port, and Ningbo merchants carried their trading networks inland.
zh:
宁波在甬江入海口、宁绍平原东缘，舟山群岛横在外海，为港口挡住风浪。738年唐朝设明州，821年州治移到三江口，筑起内城，港城的核心就此定下；999年北宋设市舶司，明州海船往来高丽、日本，禅宗僧侣也搭商船往返传法。1381年，明朝取「海定则波宁」之意改明州为宁波。1444年，宁波市舶司掌管对朝鲜、日本的勘合贸易，日本贡船一律在此入港；海防卫所不断增设，海禁日益收紧，城里多是操吴语的水手、渔民和造船工匠。

1523年5月，日本细川、大内两家的贡使为勘合符真伪在宁波械斗，杀死明朝军官，又纵兵劫掠城外；朝廷随即裁撤浙江、福建两市舶司。中外商船转而聚到舟山以南的双屿岛澳，1524年至1548年间，日本、葡萄牙和东南亚商人在此互市，直到朱纨派明军把这座私市踏平。此后倭患大起，俞大猷、戚继光都曾在浙江沿海用兵。1645年宁波明朝官员降清，鄞县人张煌言却率水师继续抗清近二十年，1664年被俘就义。

宁波的另一个名声在藏书。辞官回乡的范钦1561年建起天一阁，藏书最多时超过七万卷；范氏后人立规要求藏书由子孙共有、不得分散，这是中国现存最古老的私家藏书楼。1676年，黄宗羲成为第一个获准登楼读书的外姓人，他和全祖望又把宁波做成浙东学派的中心。乾隆皇帝后来命人测绘天一阁，照它的形制修建文渊阁等皇家藏书楼，收藏《四库全书》。清代迁界令和海禁使港口受挫，宁波商人便把商路向内地伸展。

en:
Jinhua, the old Wuzhou, sits in the Jin-Qu basin of central Zhejiang, where the Dongyang and Wuyi rivers join to form the Wu River and run on through Lanxi into the Qiantang system. After the Wu state placed the seat of Dongyang Commandery here in 266, the town grew into a collecting point for rice, bamboo and timber coming out of the hills and going by water toward the southern end of the Grand Canal. Its most famous goods were cured hams, made here since the Tang and listed as tribute under the Song; they used the local two-end-black pigs and kept well on river journeys. Zhu Yuanzhang took Wuzhou in 1358, renamed it Ningyue for a time, and established Jinhua Prefecture in 1360. In 1444 its seven counties made a bookish inland grain prefecture, with hams, rice and mountain goods moving downriver from its wharves.

The prefecture produced scholars as well as hams. Song Lian of Pujiang (1310-81), the leading prose writer of the founding Ming, directed the compilation of the History of Yuan and tutored the crown prince, until the Hu Weiyong case swept him up in old age and he died on the road to exile. In 1646, after Bolo's Qing army broke the Southern Ming line along the Qiantang, the grand secretary Zhu Dadian refused to surrender and held Jinhua; the city fell in the seventh month, and local accounts record a massacre that killed about fifty thousand people. Under the Qing, Jinhua stayed an eight-county prefecture, its hams again listed as tribute and its wharves gathering rice, bamboo and timber for the Qiantang route, the agricultural and river-trade market of the central Zhejiang basin through the eighteenth century.
zh:
金华古称婺州，地处浙江中部的金衢盆地，东阳江与武义江在城边汇成金华江，再经兰溪流入钱塘江水系。266年孙吴在此设立东阳郡治所，此后山城成为稻米、竹材、木材下水运往大运河南端的集散地。这里最出名的物产是腌腿：唐代已开始制作，宋代列为贡品，原料是本地的「两头乌」猪，腌制风干后耐于储运，正宜走水路。1358年朱元璋攻取婺州，改称宁越府，1360年设金华府。1444年的金华府下辖七县，是文风很盛的内陆产粮之区，火腿、稻米和山货都从江边码头外运。

金华既出火腿，也出文人。浦江人宋濂（1310—1381年）是明初文章大家，主持纂修《元史》，又做过太子的老师；晚年卷入胡惟庸案，被贬赴蜀，死在途中。1646年，清将博洛的军队突破南明钱塘江防线后，大学士朱大典拒降据守金华；七月城陷，据地方文献记载，屠城死难者约有五万人。清代金华仍为辖八县的府城，火腿再度列为贡品，码头继续集散稻米、竹材和木材，供应钱塘江水路，整个18世纪都是浙中盆地的农业市集与河运转运之地。

en:
Poyang faces China's largest freshwater lake, where the Gan and several other rivers gather before draining to the Yangtze through a narrow channel in the north. The walled town on the lake's east shore was the seat of Raozhou prefecture, whose seven counties included Fuliang with its porcelain town of Jingdezhen. The lake once settled the fate of a dynasty: in 1363 Chen Youliang, who had long besieged Nanchang with a huge fleet of tower ships, was met on the water by Zhu Yuanzhang with far smaller vessels. The fleets fought for weeks, until Zhu's men sent fire ships into the packed enemy line and burned the tower ships out; Chen was killed before the fighting ended, the last great battle before the founding of the Ming. In 1444 Poyang was a Ming prefectural seat, its harbour busy with the lake and river craft that carried Raozhou's porcelain toward the Yangtze.

The porcelain came from Jingdezhen, named in 1004 for the Jingde reign era and already running the Yuan court's porcelain bureau. Blue-and-white ware made the town's name, and in 1369 the Ming opened an official pottery there, followed under the Xuande emperor by the imperial kiln that fired palace ware for the rest of the dynasty. Ming potters later produced the contending-coloured doucai of the Chenghua reign and the bold five-coloured wares of Jiajing and Wanli, and Jingdezhen was counted with Foshan, Hankou and Zhuxian among the four great towns of the age. Its cups and dishes went down the Chang River into the lake and on to the Yangtze, or south over the Meiling pass to Canton, where Portuguese and Dutch ships carried them on to Europe and silver flowed back in payment. Under the Qing the court posted supervisors to the kiln; under Yongzheng and Qianlong the bannerman Tang Ying (1682-1756), who had learned every stage of the potter's craft himself, directed the works, and the soft-coloured fencai and 'Tang kiln' wares of those years rank with the finest porcelain ever fired there.
zh:
鄱阳在鄱阳湖东岸。这片中国最大的淡水湖收纳赣江等多条河流，湖水只经北侧一道狭窄水道泄入长江，湖畔的府城便是统辖七县的饶州府治，浮梁县及其属下的景德镇都在境内。湖面曾决定过王朝归属：1363年，陈友谅以楼船巨舰组成的庞大舰队久围南昌，朱元璋率较小的船队入湖迎战，双方混战经月，最后朱元璋放出火船冲入挤作一团的敌阵，焚毁楼船巨舰，陈友谅兵败身死，这是明朝开国前最后一场大战。1444年的鄱阳是明朝的饶州府城，港中往来的多是把饶州瓷器运往长江的湖船与河船。

瓷器出自景德镇。该镇1004年以宋真宗景德年号得名，元代已在此设浮梁瓷局供应宫廷，青花瓷器令它名满天下。1369年明朝在镇上设陶厂，宣德年间又设御窑厂，终明一代烧造宫廷用瓷：成化的斗彩、嘉靖与万历朝的五彩相继称绝，景德镇与佛山、汉口、朱仙并称天下四大名镇。杯盏盘碗顺昌江入湖、转长江，或南越梅岭抵达广州，由葡萄牙、荷兰商船载往欧洲，换回来的是整船白银。清代向御窑厂专派督陶官，雍正、乾隆年间，内务府旗人唐英（1682—1756）躬亲窑务、通晓每道工序，他督造的粉彩与「唐窑」器物被视为历代官窑中的上品。

en:
Jianning fills the mountain-rimmed upper valley of the Min in northern Fujian. The Han set up Jian'an county here in AD 196, one of the first four Chinese counties in Fujian, and the Wu made it the seat of a commandery ruling almost the whole region and the site of one of their largest shipyards. In 943 Wang Yanzheng, a son of Min's founder, declared himself emperor of Yin at Jianzhou; Southern Tang armies sacked the city two years later. Song times carried the prefecture to its height. The Beiyuan plantations sent the court its dragon-and-phoenix cake tea, the Jianyang kilns fired thick black-glazed bowls for whisked tea, and the Fujian scholar Cai Xiang praised their bluish-black hare's-fur glaze as beyond rivalry elsewhere. Japanese monks carried the bowls home as tenmoku, and five Southern Song examples rank among Japan's national treasures. The book town of Masha in Jianyang sold its woodblock editions across the empire, and Zhu Xi taught at Kaoting in the same county. Jianzhou became Jianning Prefecture in 1162, the first fu in Fujian, and Marco Polo, passing late in the thirteenth century, knew it as Quenlinfu, a city of three long bridges and quantities of silk. In 1444 it was a crowded Northern Min-speaking prefectural town of tea gardens, kilns and bookshops.

In 1455 the court enfeoffed a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi as hereditary Erudite of the Five Classics and built his mansion beside the Master's shrine. A new tea trade then opened from the Wuyi hills: pine-smoked black tea, the first of its kind, went down the Min to the coast, and Dutch ships brought it to Europe in 1610, where Wuyi bohea became the taste of the age. War ended the old order in 1648, when Qing armies stormed the prefectural city against Zhu Changhu, the Ming prince of Yunxi, and sacked it; of the people of the twin county seats of Jian'an and Ouning, fewer than a hundred survived. The hill country recovered on tea in the following century, as Wuyi black tea found buyers across Europe.
zh:
建宁占据闽江上游群山环抱的谷地，是闽北最古老的中心。196年，汉朝在此设建安县，为福建最早的四县之一；孙吴以建安为郡治，统领几乎全闽，这里也是孙吴最大的造船基地之一。943年，闽国建立者之子王延政在建州称帝，国号大殷，两年后南唐军攻破建州。宋代是这座府城的全盛时期：北苑茶山造好送往宫廷的龙凤团茶，建阳窑烧造点茶用的厚胎黑釉茶盏，闽人蔡襄称其青黑的兔毫釉为别处所不及；日本僧人把茶盏带回国内，称作天目，五件南宋茶盏被列为日本国宝。建阳麻沙的书坊将刻本卖遍全国，朱熹也在同县的考亭讲学。1162年建州升建宁府，是福建第一府；13世纪末马可·波罗路过时称它为建宁府（Quenlinfu），记下三座长桥和成匹的丝绸。1444年的建宁，是闽北语通行的繁庶府城，茶园、窑场和书坊相依。

1455年，朝廷封朱熹九世孙为世袭翰林五经博士，在朱子祠旁建起博士府。此后武夷山一带开出新生意：以松烟熏制的红茶是红茶之祖，顺闽江运到沿海，1610年由荷兰商船带回欧洲，武夷茶（bohea）一时成了风尚。1648年，明清易代的战火打到府城：清军为讨伐明宗室郧西王朱常湖攻破城池、大肆屠戮，建安、瓯宁两县同城而治的百姓，幸存者不足百人。入清以后，武夷红茶在欧洲销路日广，茶山之利让这片山地重新殷实起来。

en:
The mountains of western Fujian are Hakka country, and Tingzhou was the first prefectural seat the court built for Hakka migrants. When the upheavals of the fourth century drove northern families into these valleys, the Tang created Tingzhou in 736 to settle them and placed its seat at Changting on the Ting River, which runs south out of the hills to join the Han and meet the sea at Chaozhou. The prefecture lived by that current, floating paper, bamboo and timber downstream as rafts, and the land kept a frontier temper: under the Song, armed bands gathered after the autumn harvest and moved across the border country of Fujian, Jiangxi and Guangdong, and troops put local risings down again and again. Changting's craftsmen made the fine white Yukou paper already presented to the Southern Song court as tribute, while the plainer maobian paper supplied printers across the south. After the Mongol years the Ming made it Tingzhou Prefecture in 1368, ruling eight Hakka counties. In 1444 it was a crowded Hakka-speaking Confucian land of bamboo groves, paper troughs and river rafts.

Ming peace filled the remaining valleys, and Changting became the market of a three-province border country. An emperor's end played out inside the prefectural yamen: in 1646 the Longwu emperor Zhu Yujian, abandoned by his admiral Zheng Zhilong as Qing armies entered Fujian, was captured at Tingzhou and killed, and his court dissolved. Under Qing rule the eight counties kept their Hakka speech and their old trades, and families from these crowded valleys joined the migrants floating down the Han to Chaozhou and onward overseas, carrying the old-country name of Tingzhou to settlements across Southeast Asia.
zh:
福建西部的群山是客家人的家园，汀州是朝廷为客家移民设立的第一座府城。4世纪的大乱把中原人家赶进这片山谷后，唐朝于736年设汀州安置他们，州治放在汀江畔的长汀；汀江南流出山，汇入韩江，从潮州入海。汀州靠这条水道为生，纸张、竹木都放排而下；此地也长期带着边地脾气：宋代秋收之后，常有武装人群在福建、江西、广东交界的山地间流动，本地起事一再被官兵镇压。长汀工匠造出细腻洁白的玉扣纸，南宋时已是进献宫廷的贡品，普通些的毛边纸则供给南方各地的印书作坊。元代之后，明朝于1368年改置汀州府，下辖八个客家县。1444年的汀州，是客家人聚居、通行客家话的儒教之地，竹林、纸槽和溪上的木排就是它的生计。

明代太平年月里，余下的山谷也渐渐住满，长汀成为闽粤赣三省边地的商埠。一位皇帝的结局就发生在府衙里：1646年，隆武帝朱聿键在清军入闽时被水师首领郑芝龙抛下，逃到汀州被俘遇害，隆武朝廷随之瓦解。入清以后，汀属八县保住了客家话和旧营生，人满为患的山谷中，一户户客家加入沿韩江而下、经潮州出洋的人流，把汀州这个旧乡名带到南洋各处聚落。

en:
The rainy province of Tamsui covered the northern coast between two useful landing grounds: Kelang's sheltered deep-water harbour and the mouth of the Tamsui River. Basay people and related Ketagalan villages lived by fishing, shifting cultivation and barter. Senar stood above the river landing later called Hobe, and canoes carried deerskins, sulfur and food between Kelang, the river and other villages. In 1444 no outside army garrisoned either harbour; village leaders controlled access to the anchorages, sulfur grounds and hunting lands.

Spaniards sailing from Manila reached Kelang on 16 May 1626 and built San Salvador on Heping Island. Merchants from Fujian were already sailing to Tamsui to barter with local people, and in 1628-29 the Spanish raised Fort Santo Domingo near Senar while Dominican and Franciscan friars preached among the Basay and Kavalan. In 1636 villagers angered by taxation attacked and demolished the fort; the Spanish rebuilt it in stone in 1637, then abandoned Tamsui in 1638. A Dutch force from Tayouan captured Kelang in 1642 and rebuilt the river post as Fort Antonio in 1644, the fortress Chinese settlers later called Hongmao Cheng. Dutch ships loaded sulfur, deerskins and provisions at the northern harbours.

After Koxinga ended Dutch rule in southern Taiwan in 1662, the Dutch reoccupied Kelang in 1663, but Zheng forces drove them from the northern coast in 1668. Qing authority reached this rainy frontier only slowly. In 1723 settlers from Zhangzhou in Fujian began opening land at Kelang and laid out its first street, while Qing officials established the Tamsui coastal defense jurisdiction in the same year. A naval patrol post at Tamsui followed in 1808.
zh:
淡水这片多雨的土地位于北台湾海岸，连接两处实用登陆地：鸡笼有避风的深水港，淡水河口则有后来称为沪尾的河口码头。巴赛人和关系相近的凯达格兰诸社以渔捞、游耕和交易为生，圭柔社位于河口上方；独木舟在鸡笼、淡水河口和其他村社之间运送鹿皮、硫磺和食物。1444年，两处港湾都没有外来军队驻守，村社首领控制着锚地、硫磺地和猎场。

1626年5月16日，来自马尼拉的西班牙人抵达鸡笼，在和平岛修建圣萨尔瓦多城。福建商人此前已常到淡水与当地人交易。1628至1629年，西班牙人在圭柔社附近修筑圣多明哥城，道明会和方济各会修士向巴赛人、噶玛兰人传教。1636年，当地人因税赋攻毁城堡；西班牙人1637年以石料重建，仍在1638年放弃淡水。1642年，大员的荷兰军队攻占鸡笼，1644年在淡水原址改建安东尼堡，汉人移民后来称它为红毛城。荷兰船只在北方港湾装载硫磺、鹿皮和粮食。

1662年郑成功结束荷兰人在南台湾的统治后，荷兰人于1663年重占鸡笼，1668年被郑氏势力逐离北海岸。清朝的统治缓慢抵达这片多雨边地。1723年，福建漳州移民开始入垦鸡笼并形成最早街肆，清廷同年设立淡水海防建制。1808年，清水师又在淡水设置巡防据点。

en:
Middag was the Dutch name for a chiefly network on Taiwan's central-western plain, around the Dadu River and the country of modern Taichung and northern Changhua. Its villages belonged to Papora, Babuza, Pazeh and Hoanya peoples, and their headman arbitrated disputes, received the first game of the hunt and led ritual rather than ruling like a king. The Dutch called him Keizer van Middag, the 'Emperor of Midday'; his own people called him Lelian, the Sun King. David Wright, a Company agent living on Taiwan in the 1640s, counted seventeen towns obedient to him and noted that ten more had earlier thrown off his rule; the chief went about with one or two attendants, let Christians pass through his lands but never settle in them. In 1444 the river mouth, farmlands and deer plains were held by the villages alone, before Chinese farmers or European factories reached them.

The Company learned of the alliance from pirate reports in 1638. Pieter Boon's first expedition, in 1644, was beaten back by Papora fighters; returning in 1645, his men destroyed thirteen resisting villages, and Kamachat Aslamie accepted a cane at a Dutch landdag as the mark of Company overlordship. The Company then leased village lands to Chinese farmers. Aslamie died in 1648 and his nephew Kamachat Maloe succeeded him, but the villages kept their half-independence until the Dutch left the island.

Koxinga's troops came in 1661, while the siege of Zeelandia was still on, seizing grain and planting military colonies; the commander Yang Zu fell with about five hundred men, said to have died to a man, and the Zheng general Huang An later ambushed and killed the Dadu headman. In 1670 Liu Guoxuan's campaign against the Salic village left only six of its people alive. Qing rule brought heavier corvée, and in 1731 the Dajia West Society rising spread to Dadu after soldiers killed five Dadu villagers carrying grain under submission; Qing troops and Anli allies put it down in 1732, and Middag's supra-village leadership ended with it.
