巴米扬海拔2550米，地处喀布尔与哈烈之间的高原，河流在红色崖壁间切出一道翠绿谷地，商队多经此翻越兴都库什山。数百年来，它是丝绸之路西段最负盛名的佛教中心：僧侣在崖壁洞窟中苦修，6世纪时崖上凿成高53米和35米的两尊立式大佛，周围环绕数百座绘满壁画的洞窟和廊道。大佛像曾被涂成胭脂红色，小佛像饰以数种色彩。约630年玄奘在此停留十五日，见到伽蓝数十所、僧徒数千人，他在《大唐西域记》里写大佛「金色晃曜，宝饰焕烂」。伊斯兰教先随萨法尔王朝传入，伽色尼的马哈茂德将其立为谷地之教；古尔王朝治下，巴米扬在1155至1212年间是一个北抵乌浒水的王国的都城。1221年成吉思汗围城，城上一箭射死他最疼爱的孙子、察合台长子木阿秃干，城破后居民尽数被杀，残丘后来得名沙赫尔·古勒古勒，意为哀号之城。数十年后谷地中才重新出现城镇，帖木儿时期略有重建。1444年的巴米扬是帖木儿治下喀布尔道上一处安静的边地，两尊古老的大佛立于巴扎上方。

1504年巴布尔攻取喀布尔后，巴米扬便随喀布尔一同沉浮，归入巴布尔的莫卧儿后裔。胡马雍之子米尔扎·哈基姆以近乎独立之主的身份兼领喀布尔与巴米扬，直到1585年去世，阿克巴的官员才把该省收归直辖；古道上的戍军监视着乌兹别克人。奥朗则布在兴都库什用兵时，下令用大炮轰击大佛，两尊造像却没有倒。17世纪后期帝国控制松弛，周围山地的哈扎拉诸部自行其是。1747年以后，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼的骑兵把谷地纳入新生的阿富汗帝国，向诸部征兵索贡，只是高山险隘仍让巴米扬自成天地。

en:
Jalalabad covers the plateau where the Kabul and Kunar rivers meet, just west of the Khyber road that descends to Peshawar and the Indian plains. Long before the Mughal city stood here, the district was known as Nagarahara or Adinapur; its Buddhist monasteries at Hadda drew the Chinese pilgrims Faxian around 400 and Xuanzang in 630. The warm Nangarhar plain grew oranges, dates and sugarcane, and its old fort gave travellers and troops their last controlled halt before the pass. In 1444 Afghan tribes held most of the countryside around Adinapur, while the Timurid governors of Kabul claimed a suzerainty that meant little outside the garrison.

Babur knew the valley from his raids through the Khyber and in 1508-09 laid out the Bagh-e Wafa, the Garden of Fidelity, below Adinapur. His grandson Akbar founded the present city in 1570 and named it Jalalabad from his own name Jalal-ud-din. Mughal governors used the new fortress and posting-stage to guard the road between Kabul, Peshawar and the imperial cities of India. Nader Shah's army came this way in 1738 on its march toward Delhi, and ten years later Ahmad Shah Durrani added Nangarhar to his Afghan empire. Timur Shah liked the mild winter climate enough to keep his winter court at Jalalabad. The plain beside the road also served as a battlefield in the Durrani succession wars: on 29 June 1809 Mahmud Shah defeated Shah Shuja near Nimla and drove him into exile.
zh:
贾拉拉巴德位于喀布尔河与库纳尔河汇合处的台地，东面便是经开伯尔山口下行至白沙瓦和印度河平原的道路。莫卧儿城市建立以前，这一带称那揭罗曷或阿迪纳布尔；哈达的佛教寺院曾在400年前后迎来到访的法显，630年玄奘也来此巡礼。温暖的楠格哈尔平原出产柑橘、椰枣和甘蔗，古城堡则是旅人、军队进入山口前一处可控的落脚点。1444年，阿富汗部落掌握着阿迪纳布尔周围的大部分乡野，喀布尔的帖木儿总督只在驻军所及之处保有宗主权。

巴布尔在取道开伯尔山口奔袭时熟悉了这片谷地，并于1508—1509年在阿迪纳布尔下方辟建「忠诚园」。他的孙子阿克巴1570年在现址建城，取自己的名字贾拉尔丁，称贾拉拉巴德。莫卧儿总督把这座新要塞和驿站用于控制喀布尔、白沙瓦与印度诸帝都之间的道路。1738年，纳迪尔沙的军队经此向德里进军；十年后，艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼把楠格哈尔纳入阿富汗帝国。帖木儿沙喜爱这里温和的冬季，便把冬朝设在贾拉拉巴德。城旁平原也卷入杜兰尼王统战争：1809年6月29日，马哈茂德沙在尼姆拉击败沙·舒贾，迫使后者流亡。

en: Kunduz lies where the Kunduz and Khanabad rivers meet on the irrigated Tokharistan plain, north of the Hindu Kush. The ancients knew the place as Drapsaka, a prosperous Buddhist centre in the third century; under the Timurids it was called Kuhandiz, Persian for 'old fort', later Qunduz. In 1444 its walled town belonged to the Timurid Empire and covered the eastern approaches to Balkh on the roads toward Badakhshan and Kabul. After Muhammad Shaybani's Uzbeks took Balkh in 1506 the valley came under Uzbek rulers, and in the eighteenth century it was absorbed into the Durrani Empire. In 1815 the Uzbek chief Muhammad Murad Beg made Kunduz the seat of his own khanate, took Badakhshan from Mir Yar Beg and pushed his power across the Amu Darya to Kulab, from Balkh to the foothills of the Pamirs.
zh: 昆都士位于昆都士河与汗阿巴德河交汇处，地处兴都库什山以北灌溉便利的吐火罗斯坦平原。古时这里称德拉普萨卡，3世纪时是繁荣的佛教中心；帖木儿时期得名库汉迪兹，波斯语意为「古堡」，后演变为昆都士。1444年，这座有城墙的城镇属于帖木儿帝国，扼守从巴尔赫东去巴达赫尚、喀布尔的道路。1506年穆罕默德·昔班尼的乌兹别克人攻取巴尔赫后，河谷转入乌兹别克统治者之手，18世纪又并入杜兰尼帝国。1815年，乌兹别克首领穆罕默德·穆拉德·贝格以昆都士为都建立自己的汗国，从米尔·雅尔·贝格手中夺取巴达赫尚，势力跨过阿姆河抵达库洛布，西起巴尔赫，东到帕米尔山麓。

en:
Maymana sits on the Maymana River, a tributary of the Murghab, among the hills and steppes between Herat and the Amu Darya. Thick walls, towers and a moat ringed the town, whose citadel has roots in the early Iron Age. Caravans coming up from Herat and Iran on the road into Turkistan changed animals and stocked up in its bazaars. Iranian villagers and the settled descendants of Arab garrisons worked the oases, while Aimaq nomads pastured their flocks on the surrounding grasslands. In 1444 Maymana was a Sunni Muslim frontier district of the Timurid Empire, a modest market that lived mainly from that passing trade.

Uzbek power arrived with Muhammad Shaybani's early-sixteenth-century campaigns toward Herat and Turkistan; the Safavids defeated Shaybani, but Uzbek chiefs stayed on as the ruling military class. From 1621 the Ming tribe held the governorship, and when Nader Shah's empire collapsed in 1747 Hajji Bi Ming made Maymana the seat of an independent Uzbek khanate. With Andkhoy, Sheberghan and Sar-i Pol it made up the four little principalities south of the Amu Darya known as the Chahar Wilayat, and its bazaars throve on the carrying trade between Herat and the cities north of the river. After Ahmad Khan died in 1814 Sar-i Pol broke away; in 1821 Maymana remained the seat of the Ming khans.
zh:
梅马内位于穆尔加布河支流梅马内河畔，处在赫拉特与阿姆河之间的丘陵草原上。城周绕有厚墙、塔楼和壕沟，城中城堡的渊源可上溯至早期铁器时代。从赫拉特和伊朗前往突厥斯坦的商队，在此更换牲畜、补给货物。绿洲由伊朗语村民和定居的阿拉伯戍兵后裔耕作，艾马克游牧民在周围草原放牧。1444年，这里是帖木儿帝国的逊尼派边地，一座主要靠过路商队维持的小型市集。

16世纪初，穆罕默德·昔班尼远征赫拉特和突厥斯坦，乌兹别克势力随之而来；萨法维人击败了昔班尼，乌兹别克首领却留居当地，成为统治阶层。1621年起明部世袭梅马内长官，1747年纳迪尔沙的帝国瓦解，哈吉·比·明以梅马内为都城建立独立的乌兹别克汗国。它与安德胡伊、希比尔甘、萨尔普勒并立，是阿姆河以南四个小邦之一，四邦合称「四地」（Chahar Wilayat）；城中巴扎靠赫拉特与阿姆河以北诸城之间的转运贸易兴盛。1814年艾哈迈德汗死后萨尔普勒脱离，1821年的梅马内仍是明部汗王的驻地。

en:
Bost stood at the meeting of the Helmand and Arghandab rivers, on the low Garmsir road that runs towards Kandahar. Arab armies took it from the Zunbil kings in the 650s, and under the Ghaznavids it became the winter capital of Mahmud of Ghazni's empire. At Lashkari Bazar, the 'soldiers' market' by the later town, Mahmud and his son Masud raised a south palace a hundred and seventy metres long along the river, faced with painted stucco, frescoes and carved marble, and a hundred-metre market street joined the palace complex; seven kilometres to the south the Qala-e-Bost fortress guarded the river crossing, its richly carved eleventh-century arch surviving from a mosque of the old city. Bost was also a seat of learning: Ibn Hibban al-Busti, born here in 884, returned in 951 to found a madrasa that paid its students a stipend. The Mongols sacked the town in 1220 and Timur destroyed it in 1383, later ordering it rebuilt. By 1444 it was a small fortress-town on the southern marches, its pastures and crossings held by Afghan herders under the loose reach of the Mihrabanid maliks of Sistan.

By the later sixteenth century Bost was held by the Safavid shahs. As the western bulwark covering Kandahar, it shared that city's long quarrel with the Mughals: Akbar gained Kandahar by treaty in 1595, the borderlands changed hands more than once, and in the winter of 1648–1649 Shah Abbas II's armies retook Kandahar and beat off every Mughal counter-siege. The district joined Mirwais Hotak's Afghan rising in 1709; Nader Shah's army passed through Bost on the way to the siege of Kandahar in 1738, and from 1747 it formed part of Ahmad Shah Durrani's Afghan empire.
zh:
巴斯特位于赫尔曼德河与阿尔甘达卜河汇流处，地当加尔姆西尔低地通往坎大哈的道路。7世纪50年代，阿拉伯军队从尊比尔王公手中夺取该城。加兹纳维王朝时期，它成为马哈茂德帝国的冬都：在后世城旁的拉什卡里巴扎（意为「军营市场」），马哈茂德与儿子马斯乌德沿河岸建起长达一百七十米的南宫，墙面饰以彩绘灰泥、壁画和大理石雕，一条约百米长的市场街与宫苑相连；往南七公里的巴斯特堡扼守渡口，雕饰华丽的11世纪拱门是旧城一座清真寺的遗存。巴斯特也是治学之地：884年生于此地的伊本·希班951年回乡，创办了一所向学生发放津贴的经学院。1220年蒙古人洗劫该城，1383年帖木儿再度毁城，后来又下令重建。到1444年，它只是南边一座小堡镇，牧场和渡口由阿富汗牧民掌握，仅受锡斯坦米赫拉卜马利克们松散控制。

16世纪后期，巴斯特为萨法维沙阿所有。作为掩护坎大哈西路的屏障，它随该城卷入与莫卧儿的长期争夺：1595年阿克巴以订约方式取得坎大哈，这片边地此后几度易主，1648至1649年冬沙阿·阿拔斯二世的军队攻克坎大哈，莫卧儿历次反攻围城均被击退。1709年此地随米尔维斯·霍塔克举事，1738年纳迪尔沙取道巴斯特进围坎大哈；1747年起，它成为艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼阿富汗帝国的一部分。

en: Chakhansur is the main settlement of the Khashrud, the desert delta in north-eastern Sistan where the Khash river loses itself among reed-beds and shifting dunes. Sand has buried the canals and field boundaries of a populous medieval oasis, perhaps the Saruzan that the geographer al-Istakhri placed on this road; flocks, dates and the rough carpets of its Balochi herders went down the river road to Zaranj. In 1444 the delta was the north-eastern march of the Mihrabanid malik's Sistan, and it followed the province through each later change of master, from the Uzbek raid of 1507 and Safavid rule to the Hotak conquest of 1717 and Nader Shah's recovery of Sistan in 1738; after 1747 it passed to the Durrani Afghans.
zh: 恰汉苏尔是哈什鲁德沙漠三角洲的首镇，在锡斯坦东北部，哈什河在此消失于芦苇荡与流动沙丘之间。流沙掩埋了古渠和田埂，底下是中世纪一座人烟稠密的绿洲，地理学家伊斯塔赫里记载的萨鲁赞可能就在此地；畜群、椰枣和俾路支牧民织的粗朴地毯顺河道运往扎兰季。1444年，这片三角洲是米赫拉卜马利克治下锡斯坦的东北边地，此后随全锡斯坦几经易主：1507年乌兹别克人入寇，继而萨法维统治，1717年霍塔克王朝攻占，1738年纳迪尔沙收复锡斯坦；1747年后归入杜兰尼阿富汗。

en:
Bela stands just inland from Sonmiani Bay, where the Porali River, the Arabius of Alexander's historians, leaves the hills and crosses the Las plain toward the sea. In 325 BC Alexander found the Oreitan town of Rhambacia here and thought the site promising enough to leave Hephaestion behind and build a city. Arab sources called the place Armabil, and the Chachnama ranks it as the second port of Sindh after Debal; Muhammad bin Qasim passed through on his conquest of Sindh in 711. The Hingol valley nearby held the Hinglaj cave shrine, which continued to draw Hindu pilgrims under Muslim rule. In 1444 Bela was a small Sunni town of date gardens and fisheries, and the first reliable stopping place on the road out of Sindh into Makran.

A local dynasty took shape in 1742, when the Jamote chief Jam Ali Khan Korejo founded Las Bela with Bela as its capital. Nasir Khan I of Kalat later invaded and bound the Jam to his confederacy. The dynasty's outlet to the sea was Sonmiani, whose boats worked the pearl banks and whose merchants sent goods from Kandahar and Kalat toward Muscat and Sindh. The Jam ruled the Lasi tribes of the plain from Bela, paying tribute when Kalat could enforce its overlordship and managing his own affairs when the khan's reach weakened.
zh:
贝拉位于松米亚尼湾稍靠内陆的地方，普拉利河（亚历山大史家笔下的阿拉比乌斯河）从山地流出，穿过拉斯平原奔向海岸。公元前325年，亚历山大在这里见到奥里塔人的城镇兰巴基亚，认为此地适于建城，便留下赫费斯提翁主持营建。阿拉伯文献称这里为阿尔马比勒，《恰奇纪事》把它列为信德仅次于德巴尔的第二处港口；711年穆罕默德·本·卡西姆征服信德时也曾途经此地。附近欣戈尔河谷中的欣格拉杰石窟神庙，在穆斯林统治时期仍吸引印度教徒前来朝觐。1444年，贝拉是一座以椰枣和渔获为生的逊尼派小城，也是从信德进入莫克兰后第一处可靠的歇脚地。

1742年，贾莫特部首领贾姆·阿里·汗·科雷霍建立拉斯贝拉政权，以贝拉为首府。卡拉特汗纳西尔汗一世后来入侵，把贾姆纳入自己的部落联盟。这个王朝的出海港口是松米亚尼，船只在附近采珠，商人把坎大哈和卡拉特的货物运往马斯喀特与信德。贾姆家族从贝拉统辖平原上的拉西诸部：卡拉特能够施压时便纳贡，汗廷控制减弱时则自行处置部务。

en:
Kharan is a high sandy desert cut off from coastal Makran by the dark ridges of the Siahan range. Its usable wealth consisted of wells, old gabr-band dams, seasonal watercourses, and grazing for sheep and camels. Caravan tracks crossed the waste toward the Rakhshan valley, Kalat, Kandahar and Makran, so the roads often mattered more than any town. Islamic sources first call the country Buqan in 674, usually naming it with Qiqan, the future Kalat, and Kufic inscriptions from the early Islamic centuries have been found in its oases; local tradition attributes the older dams to Zoroastrian builders. At Mashkhel, nine domed tombs near Qila Ladgasht mark the Nausherwani, whose genealogy claims Khorasani origins and the Mongol Arghun chief Nikodar Oghul, converted in 1282 as Sultan Ahmad Khan. In 1444 Sunni Baloch clans held the wells and pastures, and no local chief kept a large court.

During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the Nausherwani drew revenue from the Kandahar-Kalat-Makran caravan trade and made the fortress at Kharan their seat. When Mir Ahmad Khan founded the Khanate of Kalat in 1666, the desert country lay on the edge of his Brahui confederacy. Nasir Khan I later invaded Kharan and secured the submission of its nawab. Nausherwani chiefs continued to hold the fortress. They acknowledged Kalat's demand for tribute when an army could reach the desert, and kept their own council when the khan's court was occupied elsewhere.
zh:
卡兰是一片高耸的沙质荒漠，西亚汉山脉暗色山脊把它同南方沿海的莫克兰隔开。当地人能够倚赖的财富是水井、古老的加巴尔班德拦水坝、季节性水道，以及放羊和骆驼的牧场。商队穿过荒漠，前往拉赫尚河谷、卡拉特、坎大哈和莫克兰，因此道路往往比城镇更要紧。伊斯兰文献在674年首次称这里为布甘，常把它和日后卡拉特所在的齐齐干并称；绿洲中发现过伊斯兰早期数世纪的库法体铭文，民间则把更古老的水坝传为祆教徒所修。马什凯勒的加拉·拉德加什特附近有九座穹顶墓，属于诺希尔瓦尼人；他们的谱系自称出自呼罗珊，并可追溯到蒙古阿尔浑部首领尼库达尔·兀鲁勒，此人于1282年改宗伊斯兰教，改名苏丹·艾哈迈德汗。1444年，逊尼派俾路支诸部掌握着水井和牧场，本地首领没有宏大的汗廷。

17、18世纪，诺希尔瓦尼人从坎大哈、卡拉特和莫克兰之间的商队贸易中取得收入，并把卡兰要塞作为驻地。1666年米尔·艾哈迈德汗建立卡拉特汗国时，这片荒漠还处在布拉灰联盟的边缘。纳西尔汗一世后来攻入卡兰，迫使当地纳瓦布臣服。此后诺希尔瓦尼酋长仍据守要塞：卡拉特军队能进入荒漠时，他们承认纳贡义务；汗廷被别处事务牵住时，卡兰便由各部自行议事。

en:
Chabahar lies on a sheltered bay of the Makran coast, where the monsoon keeps the weather mild enough for its Persian name to mean 'four springs'. Five kilometres northwest is Tis, the ancient Tiz, the older harbour on this shore. Cargoes from India were landed there and carried on into Iran, Central Asia and the Caucasus; al-Muqaddasi described its trade in the tenth century, Kermani wrote of it in 1188, and al-Biruni placed the beginning of the Indian coast at Tiz. Mongol raiders wrecked the port around 1223, and it never regained that trade. In 1444 Tiz was a fishing village above a ruined harbour, while Baloch families around Chabahar bay lived from fish and dates.

A Portuguese fleet seized Tiz and Chabahar in 1616 and held them until 1621. The headland fort later called the Portuguese castle covered the anchorage: the Persian account describes a walled work about 54 by 26 metres, with towers toward the sea and a watchtower visible well out on the water. After the withdrawal the bay returned to Makran's Baloch chiefs, first the Buledais and later the Gichkis, while the governors of Bampur claimed a loose overlordship from the north. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Chabahar remained a group of fishing hamlets on a good anchorage, sending out dried fish and dates while larger cargoes went through Muscat and the Indian ports.
zh:
恰巴哈尔位于莫克兰海岸一处避风海湾，受季风影响，气候温和，波斯语地名意为「四个春天」。城西北五公里是提斯，古称梯兹，是这段海岸更早的港口。印度货物曾在这里上岸，再转往伊朗、中亚和高加索；穆卡达西在10世纪记述过它的贸易，克尔曼尼1188年也写到这座港口，比鲁尼则把梯兹作为印度海岸的起点。约1223年，蒙古袭掠者摧毁了梯兹，此后它再未恢复旧日贸易。1444年，提斯只是废弃港池上方的渔村，恰巴哈尔湾一带的俾路支家庭以渔获和椰枣为生。

1616年，一支葡萄牙舰队夺取提斯和恰巴哈尔，盘踞到1621年。海角上后来被称为葡萄牙人城堡的堡垒控制着锚地；波斯文记载说，这座带围墙的工事长约54米、宽约26米，临海一侧设有塔楼，还有一座在海上远处就能看见的瞭望塔。葡萄牙人撤走后，海湾重归莫克兰的俾路支首领，先是布莱迪家，后来是吉奇基家，北方班布尔的长官也只保持松散的宗主权。17、18世纪，恰巴哈尔仍是优良锚地旁的一组渔村，输出鱼干和椰枣；更大宗的货物则经由马斯喀特和印度港口流通。

en: Rafsanjan lies on a high, semi-desert plain between Kerman and Yazd, on the caravan road that linked the two cities. Qanats watered its cotton fields and garden villages, and its old name Rafsangan is read as 'copper mine' in Old Persian, after the copper-bearing hills around it; rugs woven here were sold under the Kermani name. Local tradition puts its old bazaar in Muzaffarid times, and Timur's armies sacked the town on their way through. In 1444 Rafsanjan was a Persian-speaking Sunni market town of the Timurid Empire, modest in size but kept busy by the road, its cotton and its copper; in later years its cotton was carried as far as India and Russia. The Afghan invasion at the end of Safavid rule wrecked it again, and in 1787 the town opened its gates to Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar without a fight.
zh: 拉夫桑贾位于克尔曼和亚兹德之间的半沙漠高原，在连接两城的商旅大道上。坎儿井浇灌着棉田和村落花园；按当地解释，旧名「拉夫桑甘」在古波斯语里意为「铜矿」，名字来自四周产铜的山地。这里也织地毯，却一直打着克尔曼地毯的名号出售。当地传说老巴扎在穆扎法尔王朝时期已经存在，帖木儿的大军经过时还洗劫过此城。1444年，拉夫桑贾是帖木儿帝国一座说波斯语的逊尼派集镇，城邑不大，路上的行旅、棉布和铜料却让它十分热闹；当地的棉布后来远销印度和俄罗斯。萨法维末年阿富汗入侵者再次毁城。1787年，拉夫桑贾不战而开城，归附阿迦·穆罕默德汗·卡扎尔。

en:
Sabzevar lies on the western Khurasan road, between the Iranian plateau and the routes to Mashhad and Herat. Its orchards, mills and caravan traffic made it a useful provincial centre after the Mongol invasions, and the old fire temple at Azarbarzin remained a landmark above the plain. The town is best known as the capital of the Sarbadars. Their revolt began at Bashtin with the killing of a tax official, and in 1337 the rebels under Abd al-Razzaq seized Sabzevar. The name Sarbadar meant 'head on the gallows'. Their government brought together armed villagers, artisans and dervishes; Hasan Juri preached the return of the Twelfth Imam, while military amirs held the fortresses and troops. The regime gave the city its Shia reputation, but the two sides repeatedly fought for control. In 1381 Khwaja 'Ali-yi Mu'ayyad submitted to Timur at Nishapur and was kept as governor. Sabzevar avoided the destruction visited on other rebel cities. By 1444 the Sarbadar state had disappeared, and the town belonged to Timurid Khurasan.

The frontier still drew armies and claimants. Around 1600 the Safavids recovered Sabzevar from the Uzbeks together with Herat and Farah. In the Safavid collapse of the early eighteenth century, Nader Qoli, general of Shah Tahmasp II, pursued the suspicious shah through this district and blockaded him in Kohne Sangan fort. Tahmasp kept his title, while Nader kept control of the army; the siege was one stage in his rise before the campaigns of Herat and Isfahan. Sabzevar itself remained a stopping place on the same road.
zh:
萨卜泽瓦尔位于呼罗珊西部大道上，地处伊朗高原通往马什哈德与赫拉特的道路之间。蒙古入侵之后，这里的果园、水磨和商队贸易使它成为一处有用的地方城镇，阿扎尔巴尔津古火庙仍是平原上的标识。这座城市最出名的身份，是萨尔巴达尔政权的都城。暴动起于巴什廷，起因是一名税官被杀；1337年，阿卜杜勒·拉扎克率领叛军夺取萨卜泽瓦尔。「萨尔巴达尔」意为「绞架上的头颅」。其政权靠武装村民、手工业者和德尔维希支撑；哈桑·朱里宣传第十二伊玛目归来，军事埃米尔则掌握堡垒和军队。这一政权让城市有了什叶派色彩，但两派一再为控制权交战。1381年，霍贾·阿里·穆阿亚德在内沙布尔向帖木儿臣服，并被留任总督，萨卜泽瓦尔没有遭到其他反叛城市那样的毁灭。到1444年，萨尔巴达尔政权已经消失，城镇归属帖木儿系呼罗珊。

这条边疆仍不断引来军队和王位争夺者。约1600年，萨法维王朝从乌兹别克人手中收复萨卜泽瓦尔，连同赫拉特和法拉一并夺回。18世纪前期萨法维崩溃时，塔赫玛斯普二世的将领纳迪尔·库里经这一带追击心存猜忌的君主，把他困在科赫内桑甘要塞。塔赫玛斯普保住了名号，军队却掌握在纳迪尔手中；这场围城是纳迪尔出征赫拉特和伊斯法罕之前崛起过程中的一段。萨卜泽瓦尔本身仍是同一条大道上的歇脚地。

en:
Bojnord belongs to the mountain edge of Khurasan. The Aladagh foothills and the gaps through the Kopet Dag link the Mashhad plain with Astarabad and the Kara Kum; here the springs and pastures mattered more than a single city site. Local tradition assigns the camps here to the Qarai Turks after the Mongol invasions of the thirteenth century. In 1444 there was still no large town at Bojnord. Timurid governors claimed the frontier, nomads moved their flocks between mountain and plain, and caravans and raiders could both use the passes.

The walled town that took shape here was a Safavid answer to raids from the desert. Ismail I moved Kurdish families into Khurasan, and Tahmasp I continued the policy early in the sixteenth century. From 1598 to 1601 Abbas the Great settled another 45,000 Kurdish families and organized five Kurdish domains stretching from Astarabad to Chenaran. Bojnord became the seat of the Shadiyan tribe. Tribesmen held land in return for military service on the border, and their town was enclosed by a defensive wall, with eleven quarters, bazaars and four mosques inside.
zh:
博季努尔德属于呼罗珊的山地边缘。阿拉达格山麓与科佩特山脉的山口把马什哈德平原同阿斯塔拉巴德、卡拉库姆连接起来；在这里，泉眼和牧场比一处城址更重要。本地传统认为，13世纪蒙古入侵之后，这些营地归卡拉伊突厥人使用。1444年时，这里还没有大城市；帖木儿总督名义上统辖边地，游牧民在山坡与平原之间转场，商队和袭掠者都能利用山口进出。

后来形成的设防城镇，是萨法维王朝应对沙漠袭掠的办法。伊斯玛仪一世首先把库尔德家族迁到呼罗珊，塔赫玛斯普一世在16世纪初继续这一做法。1598年至1601年，阿拔斯大帝又安置四万五千户库尔德人，在阿斯塔拉巴德到切纳兰之间编成五个库尔德领地。博季努尔德成为沙迪扬部落的驻地。部落民分得土地，为萨法维君主服边境军役；他们的城镇外围有城墙，内部分为十一个街区，设有巴扎和四座清真寺。

en:
Takrur was the kingdom of the middle Senegal River, the fertile strip of floodplain later called Futa Toro. Its earliest rulers are remembered as the blacksmith-kings of Dya'ogo, said to have brought iron-working to the valley, and a Soninke line from Wagadu, the Manna, took power in the ninth or tenth century. In 1035 King War Jabi imposed sharia law, the first ruler in the Sahel to adopt Islam outright, and his son allied the kingdom with the rising Almoravids; cavalry from Takrur may have served with them as far as the battle of Sagrajas in Spain in 1086. Takrur grew rich on the river posts between the salt coast of Awlil and the goldfields of Bambuk. Civil war in the thirteenth century let Mali install military governors around 1286, and as Mali faded the valley passed through Fula and then Jolof hands. In 1444 it was a Muslim land of Fula farmers and fishermen, newly overrun by the Jolof emperor Tyukuli N'Diklam, who divided it among his governors.

By 1506 those governors were at war with one another. Koli Tenguella, a Fula warlord from Futa Jallon, conquered the valley in 1512, fixed his capital at Tumbere-Jiinde and founded the Denianke dynasty, whose satigis remained pagan kings ruling over a Muslim people and drew tribute from Gajaaga and Bambuk after the Jolof defeat at Danki in 1549. The Char Bouba war of the 1670s dragged the dynasty into civil war, and through the eighteenth century the Trarza Moors with Moroccan backing and the French of Saint-Louis raised and pulled down satigis almost at will as they contended for the river's gum arabic. In 1776 a Torodbe revolt led by Sulayman Bal overthrew the Denianke and set up the Imamate of Futa Toro. Its first almamy, Abdul Qadir ibn Hammadi, defeated the emirates of Trarza and Brakna, and for a time Futa Toro was one of the stronger Muslim powers of the Senegal valley.
zh:
特克鲁尔是塞内加尔河中游的王国，即后来被称作富塔托罗的肥沃河谷。人们记得最早的统治者是迪亚奥戈王朝的铁匠诸王，相传冶铁术就是他们带到河谷来的；9或10世纪，来自瓦加杜的索宁克曼纳王朝取而代之。1035年，国王瓦尔·贾比推行沙里亚法，是萨赫勒第一个公开奉伊斯兰教的统治者，他的儿子又使王国与兴起的穆拉比特人结盟；1086年西班牙的萨拉卡战役中，穆拉比特军中可能就有来自特克鲁尔的骑兵。特克鲁尔占据河畔据点，把滨海奥卢勒的盐和邦布克的金连在同一条商路上，因贸易而富。13世纪内战后，约1286年马里派来军事总督；马里势力衰退后，河谷先后落入富拉尼人和沃洛夫人之手。1444年，这里是一片富拉尼农夫和渔民的穆斯林土地，刚被沃洛夫皇帝蒂乌库利·恩迪克拉姆攻占，分给众总督治理。

到1506年，众总督已混战成一团。来自富塔贾隆的富拉尼军阀科利·滕格拉于1512年征服河谷，定都通贝雷-金德，建立登尼扬克王朝。登尼扬克的萨蒂吉们是统治穆斯林民众的异教君主；1549年沃洛夫在丹基战败后，加贾加和邦布克都向他们纳贡。17世纪70年代的沙尔·布巴战争把王朝拖入内战；整个18世纪，有摩洛哥撑腰的特拉尔扎摩尔人和圣路易的法国人争夺河畔的阿拉伯胶贸易，几乎随意废立萨蒂吉。1776年，苏莱曼·巴尔领导托罗德贝人起事，推翻登尼扬克，建立富塔托罗伊玛目国。首任阿尔马米阿卜杜勒·卡迪尔·本·哈马迪挥师击败特拉尔扎和卜拉克纳两个埃米尔国，富塔托罗一度成为塞内加尔河谷较强的穆斯林强权之一。

en:
Kantor is the upper Gambia river country, where the stream bends east towards the goldlands of Bambuk. Mandinka farmers shared its banks with Wolof, Bainuk and Jula settlers. Local tradition traces its name to the mid-thirteenth-century expedition of Tiramakhan Traore, Sundiata's general: the quarrels of his men here gave the Mandinka phrase kana-ntoro, 'do not trouble me', and when peace was restored they founded Songkunda, the 'place of agreement'. From the fifteenth century the chief market was Sutuco, where three roads met: up the Sandugu Bolong, east through Bundu to the Niger, and south-east through Tanda into the Fouta Djallon. Caravans brought Bambuk gold and ivory down to the wharves and carried coastal salt back inland. In 1444 the country was a western tributary of the Mali mansa, and as Mali weakened the Buurba of the Jolof was already moving in to claim its homage.

The Portuguese reached it early: Diogo Gomes sailed up as far as Kantora in 1456, and in 1506 Duarte Pacheco Pereira found Sutuco a walled town of some 4,000 people with a great fair, where Mandinka traders with trains of asses paid for red, blue and green cloth, brass bracelets and beads in gold; five or six thousand doubloons of good gold went down to Portugal in good years. In the 1520s Mansa Jalali Wali made the north bank independent as the kingdom of Wuli, founded his capital at Jalalikunda, fought off an invasion from Futa Toro and fell in battle against Niani, leaving the strongest state on the river. Kantora itself for a time became a province of Kaabu. When Richard Jobson visited in 1621 the king of Wuli held Sutuco, by then a seat of marabouts and Koranic learning as well as trade, served by its river port downstream at Fattatenda. Mungo Park later passed through Wuli on both of his journeys up the Gambia in search of the Niger.
zh:
坎托尔地处冈比亚河上游，河道从这里折向东方的班布克金矿区。曼丁卡农人在河畔而居，另有沃洛夫人、拜努克人和朱拉商人聚居。相传地名源于13世纪中叶松迪亚塔麾下将领蒂拉马汉·特拉奥雷的远征：他的队伍在此屡起争端，曼丁卡语「卡纳恩托罗」意为「别惹我」，后来纷争平息，部下建立松昆达村，村名意为「立约之地」。自15世纪起，苏图科（今苏图科巴）是这条河上首屈一指的市集，三条商路在此会合：沿桑杜古博隆北上、向东经邦杜通往尼日尔河、向东南经坦达深入富塔贾隆。商队把班布克的黄金和象牙运到码头，再把沿海的食盐运回内陆。1444年，此地是曼萨治下马里西陲的附庸；随着马里衰落，沃洛夫的布尔巴也已开始来索取它的朝贡。

葡萄牙人很早就到了这里：迪奥戈·戈梅斯1456年溯河而上，最远抵达坎托拉；1506年，杜阿尔特·帕切科·佩雷拉看到的苏图科是一座约有四千居民的设防城镇，市集中赶着驴队的曼丁卡商人用黄金购买红、蓝、绿各色布匹、铜镯和珠子，太平年份每年有值五六千达布隆的足色黄金运往葡萄牙。1520年代，曼萨贾拉利·瓦利在北岸建立独立的伍利王国，定都贾拉利昆达，击退来自富塔托罗的入侵，后来在对尼亚尼的作战中战死，留下了这条河上最强盛的国家。坎托拉本地则一度成为卡布帝国的一个省。1621年理查德·乔布森到访时，苏图科已归伍利国王管辖，那里既是贸易重镇，也是马拉布特聚居、讲授古兰经的学术中心，由下游河港法塔滕达吞吐货物。后来蒙戈·帕克两次沿冈比亚河寻找尼日尔河，都曾取道伍利。

en:
Siine is the Serer country behind the creeks and palm groves of the Saloum delta, a land of farming villages on Senegal's Petite Côte. Before the Guelowar arrived, councils of lamans, priest-chiefs who guarded both land rights and Serer rites, governed its villages. In the fourteenth century a Guelowar maternal clan fleeing defeat in Kaabu won asylum here. Serer nobles married Guelowar women, their children became Serer kings, and Maysa Wali, chosen by the laman council, ruled from Mbissel as the first Maad a Sinig. In 1444 Siine formed part of the Jolof confederacy, while its court kept the old Serer religion.

Portuguese ships reached the coast in the 1450s, and Alvise Cadamosto recorded the ruler as Bur-ba-Sine; European maps turned the title into Barbacim. The best-remembered king of these years was Mbegane Ndour, born into the Guelowar royal line and linked by marriage to a princess-priestess of Baol. Oral accounts credit him with poisoning Moussa Eli Bana Sall, a Takruri marabout who controlled Saloum. Mbegane then founded the kingdom of Saloum and ruled it together with Siine. Around 1520 Siine and Saloum became the first Jolof vassals to renounce the Buurba's overlordship, nearly thirty years before Danki. When Nasr ad-Din's movement crossed Senegambia in the 1670s, Serer troops from Saloum helped Cayor overthrow clerical rule, while the Guelowar kings at Mbissel kept their throne and old rites through the eighteenth century.
zh:
塞尼是萨卢姆三角洲溪汊与棕榈林后方的谢列尔人之地，村落分布在塞内加尔小海岸的农田间。盖卢瓦尔人到来前，各村由拉曼会议治理；拉曼既是掌管土地权利的首领，也是谢列尔旧仪的守护者。14世纪，一个盖卢瓦尔母系氏族在加布的内争中失败，到此寻求庇护。谢列尔贵族迎娶盖卢瓦尔女子，他们的后代成为谢列尔人的国王；迈萨·瓦利被拉曼会议推举，以姆比塞尔为都，称第一代马阿·西尼格。1444年，塞尼属于卓洛夫联盟，王廷仍守谢列尔旧教。

1450年代，葡萄牙船只抵达海岸，阿尔维塞·卡达莫斯托把君主头衔记为布尔巴西内格，欧洲地图后来把它转写成巴尔巴辛。这一时期最常被提起的国王是姆贝甘·恩杜尔。他出身盖卢瓦尔王室，又娶巴奥勒的公主兼女祭司以巩固名分；口述传说称他毒死了控制萨卢姆的塔克鲁尔族马拉布特穆萨·埃利·巴纳·萨尔，随后建立萨卢姆王国，并与塞尼联合统治。1520年前后，塞尼与萨卢姆最先拒绝布尔巴的宗主权，比丹基之战早了近三十年。1670年代纳西尔丁运动席卷塞内冈比亚时，萨卢姆的谢列尔军队帮助卡约尔推翻教士政权，姆比塞尔的盖卢瓦尔诸王则在整个18世纪保住王位和旧仪。

en:
Galam, also called Gajaaga, was a Soninke kingdom on the upper Senegal, holding both banks from the country around Kayes downstream to Bakel and straddling the Falémé at the edge of the Bambuk goldfields. Its rulers, called tunka, took their fame from gold: 'Galam' means gold in Wolof, and the kingdom was known as the Land of Gold. Its Bathily dynasty, the Bacili of Manding tradition, came up from the Inner Niger Delta between the eighth and eleventh centuries, subdued the local Gaja Soninke and fixed their rule in the thirteenth; as heirs of Ghana they kept the old snake cult of Wagadu. Gold panned in Bambuk passed through the tunka's markets into caravans crossing the Sahara. In 1444 Galam paid tribute to Mali.

Songhai attacks in 1506 broke Mali's hold on the Sahel, and by the late sixteenth century Galam gave only nominal tribute to the Denianke of Futa Toro; around the middle of the seventeenth it was perhaps the strongest power on the upper river. In 1690 the tunka granted a holding to Malick Sy, a Torodbe cleric from Futa Toro, who settled it with kinsmen and Muslim refugees and built it up as Bundu; Bundu took land from its former overlord, and Gajaaga soldiers killed Sy in an ambush in 1699. The French built Fort Saint-Joseph in 1700, and for decades most of the slaves shipped out of Saint-Louis came through Galam. Raids by the Trarza Moors and Kaarta, together with long succession wars, wore the kingdom down; a joint invasion by Kaarta and Khasso in 1750 was beaten off but showed its weakness to all its neighbours. In 1820 the French returned to the upper river and rebuilt their post at Bakel.
zh:
加兰又名加贾加，是塞内加尔河上游的索宁克王国，疆域自卡耶一带顺流而下至巴凯尔，据有大河两岸，又地跨法莱梅河，紧邻邦布克产金地。统治者称通卡；「加兰」在沃洛夫语中意为黄金，当时人又称这个王国为「黄金之地」。巴蒂利王朝（曼德传统中称作巴西利）在8至11世纪间从内尼日尔三角洲北上，征服当地的加贾索宁克人，13世纪真正站稳脚跟；作为加纳的后继者，他们保留了瓦加杜古老的蛇神崇拜。邦布克淘出的黄金经通卡治下的市集进入横跨撒哈拉的商队。1444年，加兰向马里纳贡。

1506年桑海的进攻打碎了马里对萨赫勒的控制，到16世纪末，加兰只在名义上向富塔托罗的登尼扬克人纳贡；17世纪中叶，它或许已是河上游最强的政权。1690年，通卡把一块封地赐给来自富塔托罗的托罗德贝神职人员马利克·西，他率族人和穆斯林难民前往定居，把它经营成邦杜；邦杜反过来从旧主手中夺取土地，1699年西在加贾加军队的伏击中被杀。法国人1700年建成圣约瑟夫堡，此后数十年，从圣路易运出的奴隶大多经由加兰。特拉尔扎摩尔人和卡尔塔不断袭掠，继承战争长年不休；1750年卡尔塔与哈索联手入侵，虽被击退，王国的虚弱却暴露在所有邻邦眼前。1820年，法国人重返河上游，在巴凯尔重建据点。

en:
The estuaries between the Geba and Rio Grande de Buba were Biafada country. Its fishing villages and mangrove channels belonged to three kingdoms, Biguba, Guinala and Bissege; Biguba and Guinala were subject to the Mandinka mansa of Kaabu, heir to Mali's old power in Senegambia. Guinala had a port town, an inland seat at Bruco, and a large weekly market at Bijorei. In 1444 canoes carried salt and dried fish from the coast, pepper and kola nuts from the forest, iron, and Mandinka cotton cloth; European ships were only beginning to know the shore.

Alvise Cadamosto reached the coast in 1455 and Diogo Gomes in 1456; Portugal claimed the region from the 1450s, but Biafada rulers kept the river villages. About the middle of the century Guinala defeated a Fula armed migration led by Dulo Demmba. In the sixteenth century Guinala became the leading Euro-African port here, exporting on average 3,000 enslaved people a year to the Americas. In the 1580s lançados built the fort of Porto da Cruz nearby; after Bijagos raiders struck it in 1610, they withdrew upstream to Bolola, near later Buba. The captive trade continued through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, fed by wars involving Kaabu and Futa Jallon, while Portuguese authority scarcely reached beyond scattered coastal posts.
zh:
热巴河与布巴河之间的河口湾是比亚法达人的土地，红树林水道纵横，渔村分属比古巴、吉纳拉和比塞盖三个王国。比古巴和吉纳拉都向加布的曼丁卡曼萨纳贡，后者在塞内冈比亚承续着马里的旧日势力。吉纳拉在布巴河一条支流上设有港口商镇，统治中心在内陆的布鲁科，还在比若雷办有这一带最大的周市。1444年，独木舟往来贩运沿海的盐和鱼干、林中的胡椒与柯拉果、铁条和曼丁卡人织的棉布；葡萄牙人的卡拉维尔帆船这时才刚学会走这些水道。

1455年，阿尔维塞·卡达莫斯托抵达这段海岸，迪奥戈·戈麦斯次年也到来。葡萄牙从15世纪50年代宣称占有此地，但比亚法达统治者仍掌握着河畔村落。约在15世纪中叶，吉纳拉击败了杜洛·登巴率领的富拉人武装迁徙队伍，这股势力此前曾连破数个沃洛夫和曼丁卡政权。16世纪，吉纳拉成为这段海岸上最重要的欧非贸易港，平均每年向美洲输出3000名奴隶。实际经营贸易的是兰萨多斯，即被放逐到非洲的葡萄牙流亡者和新基督徒：他们定居在比亚法达人中间，与当地统治家族通婚，形成一个充当译员和中间商的欧非混血精英阶层，其规模最大的聚居地就在布巴和布巴河一带。16世纪80年代，为防备法国海盗，他们修筑十字港要塞；但1610年比热戈斯群岛的独木舟袭击者洗劫该堡后，他们退往上游的博洛拉，也就是后来布巴城的所在。此后两个世纪，俘虏贸易仍在继续，加布与富塔贾隆之间的战争不断提供人口，葡萄牙人的势力却始终没有越过几座零散的海岸商站。

en:
The coast between Sherbro and Cape Mesurado is one mangrove corridor after another, broken at Cape Mount by a thousand-foot granite headland and the tidal lagoon behind it, Fisherman's Lake; Piso, the local name, means 'pigeon's hole'. The Mafa, Mano and Gallinas rivers wind through Gola forest on their way to the sea. In 1444 Gola fishing and farming villages lived off the creek trade, bartering salt and kola nuts with Mande-speaking travellers from upcountry. Dense mangrove gave the shore few anchorages worth a European chart, and no chart had yet fixed its names.

Pedro de Sintra mapped the headland in 1461 and named it Cabo do Monte, and Portuguese pilots logged the channels behind it as the Rio das Galinhas. Around 1545 Mane-Sumba war bands came down the Mano and Moa, broke the old coastal order and spread Mande ways of war. Mandinka of the Camara clan married into Gola villages, and their descendants became the Vai, whom Dutch records first place by Cape Mount in the early seventeenth century. The Dutch trading post built on the cape was hard to defend and never fed itself; its supplies came by sea from Elmina, about 750 miles away. From the 1620s the Mande coalitions called Quoja and Karou made themselves masters of the shore, and Karou raiding parties worked the country between the Mafa, Mano and Gallinas for another hundred years. Cape Mount became an anchorage for slavers, while the remoter Gallinas creeks drew the trade in strength only late in the eighteenth century. After Britain banned the trade in 1808 those same creeks hid the last illegal slavers, and in 1821 no European power yet owned the coast.
zh:
谢尔布罗到梅苏拉多角之间的海岸是一条接一条的红树林走廊，到大角山才被一座高约千英尺的花岗岩岬角截断；岬后是潮汐潟湖「渔夫湖」，当地名称皮索意为「鸽子洞」。马法河、马诺河和加利纳斯河穿过戈拉人的林区蜿蜒入海。1444年，戈拉人的渔村农庄靠河汊贸易过活，用盐和柯拉果同内陆来的曼德语旅人交换。红树林太密，这一带海岸少有值得欧洲人绘制的锚地，海图上也还没有固定的地名。

1461年，佩德罗·德·辛特拉测绘这座岬角，命名为山角（Cabo do Monte），葡萄牙领航员把岬后的水道记作母鸡河（Rio das Galinhas）。约1545年，马内-松巴战团沿马诺河和莫阿河南下，打破旧有海岸秩序，也带去了曼德人的战法。卡马拉氏族的曼丁卡人与戈拉村落通婚，后人形成瓦伊人，荷兰文献在17世纪上半叶首次把瓦伊人记在大角山一带。荷兰人在岬角上设过贸易站，却难以防守、无法自给，补给全靠约750英里外的埃尔米纳走海运送来。17世纪20年代起，夸贾和卡鲁两个曼德人联盟成为沿海的主人，卡鲁战团此后一百年间在马法河、马诺河和加利纳斯河之间的腹地四处征战。大角山成为贩奴船的锚地，更偏僻的加利纳斯河汊直到18世纪末才涌来大量贸易。英国1808年禁止奴隶贸易后，这些河汊藏起了最后的非法贩奴船；到1821年，还没有任何欧洲政权占有这段海岸。

en: The dry pastures of Termes centre on the wells of Awdaghust, whose ruins at Tegdaoust mark an early southern terminus of the trans-Saharan caravan road, fifty stages south of Sijilmasa. In the ninth century al-Yaqubi described a Berber Sanhaja town whose king raided the lands of the Sudan and took tribute from more than twenty of their rulers, and Ibn Hawqal noted that Ghana's kings depended on the salt that passed through its markets. Al-Bakri, writing before the Almoravid attack, found a flourishing town of markets, date palms and henna trees. In 1054-55 Abd Allah ibn Yasin's Almoravids stormed Awdaghust and seized its people and goods because the town obeyed the ruler of Ghana. A century later al-Idrisi saw only a small desert place short of water, whose inhabitants lived from their own camels. By the early thirteenth century Walata, 360 kilometres to the east, had taken over the caravan routes. In 1444 Muslim Soninke herders watered their flocks at the old wells on a remote edge of weakening Mali.
zh: 泰尔姆的干旱牧地以奥达古斯特的水井为中心，泰格达乌斯特的废墟是撒哈拉商道早期的南端商站，位于锡吉勒马萨以南五十个驿站之遥。9世纪时雅库比记载，这座桑哈贾柏柏尔人城镇的君主南征黑人之地，接受二十多位小邦统治者的贡赋；伊本·豪卡勒也提到，加纳诸王离不开经此转运的盐。白克里在穆拉比特人来袭之前写道，这里市集兴旺，长满椰枣和散沫花。1054至1055年，阿卜杜拉·伊本·雅辛的穆拉比特军队攻破奥达古斯特，因此城臣属加纳王而掳掠其人口财物。一个世纪后伊德里西见到的只是一座缺水的沙漠小镇，居民靠自养的骆驼过活。到13世纪初，以东360公里的瓦拉塔接管了商道。1444年，穆斯林索宁克牧人在这些古井旁饮畜，身处衰落中马里的遥远边陲。

en:
The Tagant is a long sandstone plateau rising out of the desert of central Mauritania, its southern cliffs looking over the dry bed of the old Aoukar lake basin. Its Berber name means 'forest', for the highland catches enough rain for acacia scrub, pasture and date-palm oases. Stone villages line the cliffs from the time of the Tichitt culture: millet farmers settled there some four thousand years ago and built the oldest stone settlements south of the Sahara, possibly the ancestors of Ghana, and hundreds of rock paintings of animals and hunting scenes remain on the rocks. The villages were abandoned as the climate dried around 500 BC. Caravans brought people back to the plateau, and the town of Tichitt was founded in the twelfth century on the road from Oualata to Chinguetti and Sijilmasa; local legend says seven towns have risen on the same spot. In 1444 no prince ruled the Tagant, where Sanhaja Berber clans and Fula pastoralists moved between wells and oases.

From the mid-seventeenth century groups moving down from the Adrar pushed the plateau's Toucouleur inhabitants south toward Futa Toro. Out of the Char Bouba war the Idaw Aish, an Idawish clan, built the Emirate of the Tagant with Tidjikdja as its capital, and the walled ksour of Tichit, Rachid and Tidjikdja lived on dates, caravan dues and Islamic learning. The new emirate soon went to war with its neighbours: a Brakna army besieged the Idawish for three months at Dhahr Tagant and rode off only after receiving forty horses. The emirs were strongest through the eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, but feuds inside the ruling houses never stopped; succession disputes from the later 1700s split and wore down the emirate, as they did the other Moorish emirates around it.
zh:
塔甘特是毛里塔尼亚中部沙漠中隆起的长条砂岩高原，南缘悬崖俯临奥卡尔古湖盆的干涸湖床。其柏柏尔语名意为「森林」，因为高地所得雨水足以养育金合欢灌丛、牧场和椰枣绿洲。崖壁上分布着提希特文化的石砌村落：约四千年前，种粟的农人到此定居，建起撒哈拉以南最古老的石砌聚落，他们或许就是古加纳先民的一支；岩壁上还留有数百处描绘动物与狩猎场面的岩画。约公元前500年气候变干，村落被放弃。商队让人重返高原，12世纪，提希特城建在瓦拉塔通往欣盖提、再到西吉勒马萨的商路上，当地相传城址上先后叠建过七座城镇。1444年的塔甘特没有君主，桑哈贾柏柏尔部族和富拉尼牧人在各处水井与绿洲间转徙。

17世纪中叶起，从阿德拉尔南下的部族把高原上的图库洛尔人逐往南方的富塔托罗。沙尔·布巴战争之后，属伊达维什人的伊达乌·阿伊什部族建立塔甘特埃米尔国，以提吉克贾为都；提希特、拉希德、提吉克贾等设防枣城靠椰枣、商税和伊斯兰学问为生。新埃米尔国很快与邻邦交兵：卜拉克纳军队曾在塔甘特崖下围困伊达维什人三个月，收下四十匹马才撤走。整个18世纪和19世纪初埃米尔势力最强，但统治家族内讧不歇；18世纪后期起，继承之争不断分裂、消耗着这个国家，周围其他摩尔人埃米尔国也走了同样的路。

en:
Wagadu was the Soninke name of old Ghana; the province's own town, Dia, lay farther south on the Diaka channel at the western edge of the Inner Niger Delta. Three settlement mounds cover a town older than nearby Djenné, where Bozo fishermen, Marka rice growers and northern traders used the water road between the delta and the Sahara. Ibn Battuta, crossing Mali's domains in the fourteenth century, heard of the place as Zagha, whose people were 'old in Islam' although its chief still obeyed the mansa. By 1444 the jurists ran Dia themselves and called it Balad Allah, the town of God: the mansa of Mali did not dare enter it, and anyone who reached its walls ceased to be counted a Mali subject. Under the scholars' Muslim rule, Bozo fishing rites and Marka cults continued as before.

In 1494 or 1495 Askia Muhammad's Songhai army took Zaagha and drew the clerical town into Songhai's western marches. Long after Songhai power ebbed, Dia stayed in the hands of a local non-Muslim warrior house, the Diawara or Traore, while its marabouts kept the name Balad Allah. When Seku Amadu founded the Fulani Islamic state of the Dina in Macina in 1818, Dia submitted; the new rulers removed the Marka family and handed the town to the maraboutic Koreissi, putting an end to the long balance of Muslim scholarship and old cults.
zh:
瓦加杜是索宁克人对古加纳的称呼；本省的城镇迪亚更靠南方，位于尼日尔河内陆三角洲西缘的迪亚卡水道上。三座居址土丘下埋着一座比邻近杰内更古老的城镇，博佐渔民、马尔卡稻农和北方商人借连通三角洲与撒哈拉的水道往来。14世纪伊本·白图泰行经马里疆土时，听说此处名叫扎加，居民「早已奉教」，首领却仍听命于曼萨。到1444年，迪亚由宗教学者自行治理，自称「真主之城」巴拉德安拉：马里的曼萨不敢入城，谁到了城边就算不得马里的臣民。在学者的穆斯林统治之下，博佐人的渔猎仪式和马尔卡旧祭仍照旧延续。

1494或1495年，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德的桑海军队攻取扎加，把这座学者之城纳入桑海的西部边地。桑海势力退去很久以后，迪亚仍由本地非穆斯林武士家族迪亚瓦拉（又称特拉奥雷）掌握，城中的学者则继续使用「真主之城」的名号。1818年塞库·阿马杜在马西纳建立富尔贝人的伊斯兰国家迪纳，迪亚归服；新政权废黜马尔卡家族，把城镇交给宗教学者世家科雷西，宗教学问与旧祭长期并存的局面就此结束。

en:
The arid pastures of Baghena surround Koumbi, whose ruins at Koumbi Saleh may be the lost capital of Ghana, the empire that grew rich taxing the gold moving north across the Sahara. Al-Bakri knew it as two towns six miles apart: a stone city of Muslim merchants with a Friday mosque, and a nearby royal residence where the salt and gold of the caravan road changed hands; in the eleventh century the capital held perhaps 30,000 people. Almoravid forces took it in 1076, and around 1240 Sundiata Keita's army of a rising Mali seized and destroyed it. By 1444 the mosque and stone houses stood in ruins around wells used by Muslim Soninke herders and Tuareg camel nomads. Since the Tuareg took Timbuktu in 1430 and Walata in 1433, Koumbi counted only as a pasture frontier, not a caravan city.

Mali lost Baghena and neighbouring Wagadu to Mossi raiders around 1470. Under the Askia dynasty the country became a military province under an officer titled the Baghena-fari. On 12 March 1591 Judar Pasha's Saadian army broke Songhai power at Tondibi, and within the year the Baghena-fari Bokar ben Askia Muhammad Benkan rose against the new Moroccan order. His revolt failed, and Baghena drifted into the loose frontier of the Timbuktu pashalik, its worth now in flocks rather than in the old royal markets.
zh:
巴吉诺的干旱牧地环绕着库姆比，昆比萨利赫的废墟可能就是加纳古都的所在，这个帝国靠对北上撒哈拉的黄金征税致富。白克里记下两座相距十公里的城镇：一座是石造的穆斯林商人城，城中有聚礼清真寺；另一座是附近的王宫，商道上的盐和黄金在此转手。11世纪时这座都城约有三万居民。穆拉比特军队1076年攻占该城，约1240年，兴起中的马里由松迪亚塔·凯塔率军夺取并摧毁了它。到1444年，清真寺和石屋都已成废墟，水井旁是穆斯林索宁克牧人和图阿雷格骆驼游牧民。图阿雷格人1430年取廷巴克图、1433年取瓦拉塔之后，库姆比只算一道牧地边疆，不再是商队城市。

约1470年，马里在莫西人的袭扰下失去巴吉诺和邻近的瓦加杜。阿斯基亚王朝时，这里成为军事行省，由称「巴格纳法里」的长官管辖。1591年3月12日，朱达尔帕夏的萨阿德军队在通迪比击溃桑海；不出一年，巴格纳法里博卡尔·本·阿斯基亚·穆罕默德·本坎起兵反抗新来的摩洛哥秩序，终归失败。巴吉诺随后落入廷巴克图帕夏辖区的松散边地，值钱的是畜群，不再是旧日的王城市集。

en:
Hodh, el-Hodh or 'the Basin' in Arabic, is the dry Aoukar depression enclosed by the Tichitt-Walata and Tagant cliffs, where some of West Africa's oldest stone settlements stand on rocky headlands above the desert. Its oasis was first called Biru, a Mande name, and in Ghana's day it lay on the southern edge of that empire; early in the thirteenth century it replaced Aoudaghost as the southern end of the trans-Saharan road. Caravans out of Sijilmasa reached it after the salt mines of Taghaza, and the town grew into a market and a seat of Muslim learning, perhaps two or three thousand strong, before passing to Mali in the fourteenth century. Ibn Battuta spent about fifty days there among Muslim Massufa Sanhaja: he found groundwater, date palms with watermelons sown in their shade and plenty of mutton, and was struck by the respect and freedom the women enjoyed; the Berber name Iwalatan was already overtaking the old Mande Biru. From the later fourteenth century Timbuktu drew the caravans away, and after the Tuareg took Walata in 1433 the oasis entered 1444 as a smaller Tuareg-held station, living from wells, flocks and dates.

The Mossi broke the peace in 1480. Nasséré, king of Yatenga, had crossed the Niger three years earlier and ravaged the Malian borderlands; his men took Walata after a month's siege and sacked it, but the townspeople rallied, chased the raiders into the desert and rescued many of the people carried off. When Leo Africanus passed through in 1509-10 he found a small Songhai tributary kingdom of three large villages among the palm groves, its people speaking Songhai and friendly to strangers. Its prince had fled into the desert before making peace on a yearly tribute to the ruler of Timbuktu. Early in the seventeenth century Hassaniya Arabs settled in the town, and the Lemhajib, three Soninke families absorbed into the Berber and Arab milieu, ran its politics for the next century and a half.
zh:
霍德在阿拉伯语中称「霍德」，意为盆地，是干旱的奥卡尔洼地，提希特—瓦拉塔崖壁和塔甘特崖壁环抱四周，西非最古老的几处石砌聚落就坐落在俯临沙漠的岩角上。洼地里的绿洲最初叫曼德语名字比鲁，加纳时代位于帝国南缘，13世纪初取代奥达古斯特，成为撒哈拉商道的南端终点。锡吉勒马萨的商队经过塔加扎盐矿后来到这里，城镇发展成市集和伊斯兰教学问中心，居民可能有两三千人，14世纪并入马里。伊本·白图泰曾在信奉伊斯兰教的马苏法桑哈贾人中间停留约五十天：这里有地下水，椰枣树下种着西瓜，羊肉充足，而女性享有的尊重和自由让他吃惊；柏柏尔名字伊瓦拉坦也已在取代旧曼德名比鲁。14世纪后期起，廷巴克图把商队陆续引走；图阿雷格人1433年夺取瓦拉塔后，这座绿洲在1444年是图阿雷格人手中的较小驿站，靠水井、畜群和椰枣为生。

1480年，莫西人打破了平静。亚滕加国王纳塞雷此前三年渡过尼日尔河，蹂躏马里边地；他的军队围城一个月后攻破瓦拉塔并大肆洗劫，但市民重新集结，追入沙漠，救回许多被掳走的人。利奥·阿非利加努斯1509至1510年路经此地时，瓦拉塔是桑海的小附庸国，棕榈林间只有三座大村，居民改说桑海语，对外乡人很友善。其君主先逃入沙漠，后来以每年向廷巴克图统治者纳贡为条件议和。17世纪初，讲哈桑语的阿拉伯人迁入城镇；莱姆哈吉布是三个索宁克家族，融入柏柏尔和阿拉伯环境后，在此后一个半世纪里主持当地政事。

en:
The grassy uplands between the Sankarani and the upper Niger were the land called Dô, one of the oldest Mande countries. Arab geographers knew it early: al-Bakri heard of the land of Daw and its neighbour Malal near the goldfields, and al-Idrisi in 1154 set the two four days' journey apart in a river valley leading down to the Niger. Oral tradition remembers Dô as a kafu of twelve towns ruled by the Condé clan, and the Sundiata epic ties the Condé land to the dynasty's birth: Sogolon Condé, the mother of Sundiata Keita, came from Dô. After Sundiata beat Soumaoro Kanté at Kirina about 1235, tradition places the proclamation of the empire's charter, the Kouroukan Fouga, on a field near Kangaba. The highland pastures were cattle country, and tracks linked the villages with Niani and the goldfields of Bouré and Bambuk. In 1444 Dô was a Mandinka province of the mansa.

Songhai armies reached the Manding in the next century, and the kanfari Dawud sacked Niani in 1545 without holding it. After Mansa Mahmud IV's defeat at Jenne in 1599 Keita power broke into chiefdoms, and the last mansa, Mama Maghan, failed in his siege of Ségou in 1670 and withdrew to Kangaba, a local chief with nothing but the royal name. The sacred Kamablon was built there in 1653, a circular mudbrick hall in the town square where griots gathered at each re-roofing to recite the oral history of the old empire. In 1751 Biton Coulibaly's Bamana army took Niani and made its mansa a vassal, and from the later eighteenth century Fulbe armies out of the new almamyate of Futa Jallon pressed north into the Manding. In 1821 Dô was a raided borderland between Ségou and the Fulbe highlands, its old towns taking orders from Bamana courts.
zh:
桑卡拉尼河与尼日尔河上游之间的草丘高地称作多，是曼德最古老的地方之一。阿拉伯地理学家很早就听说它：贝克里把「道」和邻邦马拉尔记在金矿附近，1154年的伊德里西则说，两地相距四日路程，同在一条通向尼日尔河的河谷里。口述传统中，多是孔戴氏族统有十二座城镇的卡富；松迪亚塔史诗也把这片孔戴人的土地与王朝的诞生连在一起：松迪亚塔·凯塔之母索戈隆·孔戴就来自多。约1235年松迪亚塔在基里纳击败苏毛罗·孔戴之后，相传帝国的根本大法《库鲁坎富加》就在康加巴附近的原野上宣布。高地草场牧放牛群，小路把村落与尼亚尼以及布雷、班布克金矿区相连。1444年，多是曼萨治下的一个曼丁卡省份。

下个世纪，桑海军队打进曼丁，坎法里达乌德1545年洗劫尼亚尼，却没有久占。1599年曼萨·马哈茂德四世兵败杰内之后，凯塔政权瓦解为诸酋长国；末代曼萨马马·汉1670年围攻塞古失败，退回康加巴，守着王族的名号做了地方酋长。1653年，城里建起神圣的卡马布隆，这是一座立于公共广场的圆形泥砖大厅，每逢重新铺顶，格里奥们便汇聚于此，诵唱旧帝国的口述史。1751年，比通·库利巴利的班巴拉大军攻占尼亚尼，把那里的曼萨降为附庸；18世纪后期，新兴富塔贾隆阿尔马米国的富拉尼军队又向北进逼曼丁。1821年，多是塞古与富拉尼高原之间屡遭攻掠的边地，旧日城镇都听命于班巴拉人的宫廷。

en:
Sibiridugu is the river country of the rapids where the upper Niger drops out of the Manding hills into the middle valley, the district of Barouéli and Niamina with Bamako at its main crossing. The rapids break the river's through passage, so the crossing became a place where cargoes changed hands: Bozo and Somono fishermen worked the fords and pools, Mandinka farmers tilled the banks, and porters carried gold, ivory, kola nuts and salt between the southern Manden and the Sahel. Ghana ruled the land first, then the mansas of Mali, who still held it in 1444.

In the sixteenth century the Niaré, a family of Soninke origin, built the kafu of Bamako at the rapids. Tradition names the hunter Simballa Niaré as the man who chose the site and his son Diamoussa as its founder, who laid out the town's first quarter, Niaréla; Muslim Touré and Drave families, clerics and merchants, settled beside them. In Bambara the town's name means 'crocodile river'. Bamako grew as a client of the rising Bambara power at Ségou, and Biton Coulibaly's campaigns between 1712 and 1755 brought the whole Sibiridugu under Ségou, the Niaré chiefs keeping their town as vassals. Mungo Park passed through on his second Niger journey in 1805 and 1806 and counted about 6,000 people, a busy market at the trans-shipment point between Ségou and the Manden. In 1821 Bamako remained a Bamana town of the Ségou empire, while Seku Amadu's Fulbe caliphate was overrunning the delta downstream.
zh:
锡比里杜古是上尼日尔河闯出曼丁丘陵、跌向中游谷地的急流地带，领有巴鲁埃利和尼亚米纳一带，主要渡口巴马卡就在此处。急流切断了河道的直通航行，渡口便成了货物换手的地方：博佐和索莫诺渔民在渡口与鱼潭间劳作，曼丁卡农人耕耘两岸，脚夫把黄金、象牙、柯拉果和食盐往返搬运于南曼丁与萨赫勒之间。这片土地先归加纳统辖，后来归于马里的曼萨，1444年仍在其治下。

16世纪，索宁克出身的尼亚雷家族在急流边建起巴马卡卡富。相传猎人辛巴拉·尼亚雷选定城址，其子迪亚穆萨主持建城，划出城里最早的街区尼亚雷拉；世代以教士和商人为业的穆斯林图雷、德拉韦两族也在旁边安家。在班巴拉语中，城名意为「鳄鱼河」。巴马卡作为兴起于塞古的班巴拉强权的附庸逐渐发展，1712至1755年间，比通·库利巴利的连年征战把整个锡比里杜古纳入塞古的势力，尼亚雷酋长作为藩属照旧保有城镇。1805至1806年，蒙戈·帕克第二次探查尼日尔河途经此地，数出约六千居民；在塞古与曼丁之间，这是一处货物转运的热闹市集。1821年，巴马卡仍是塞古帝国治下的班巴拉城镇，而塞库·阿马杜的富拉尼哈里发国正在席卷下游三角洲。

en:
South of the Bani and west of Djenné lies the Bendugu, the 'country of grass' in Bamana, an old province of the Mali Empire. Its Bozo fishing camps grew into the market town of San at a ford where the river road from the Inner Niger Delta met the track to the goldfields of the south. Oral traditions disagree whether the town, which arose around 1400 as a dependency of the kingdom of Daa, was founded by Marka from Dia or Dyula from Djenné. Twelve local kings, mostly of the Traore lineages, ruled its villages under a governor called the yaw. In 1444 the Bendugu answered to the mansa, and the markets of San dealt in iron, river rice and the mud cloth its weavers were known for.

Songhai never digested the province: Askia Ishaq I defeated a Malian army there in 1542 and Askia Daoud raided it in his turn, but the twelve kings kept their villages until the defeat at Tondibi swept imperial rule away. In the eighteenth century the country lay on the loose edge of the Ségou empire of Biton Coulibaly, and in 1739 Famaghan Ouattara of Kong destroyed San while intervening in a Bamana civil war; the townspeople rebuilt it a little to the north. Every year the whole town gathered at the Sanké pond for the Sanké mô, a collective fishing rite on the second Thursday of the seventh lunar month, held to mark the founding of the town. In 1818 Seku Amadu's jihadists won at Noukouma beyond the Bani, and by 1821 the caliphate of Hamdullahi had reached the fords of the Bendugu.
zh:
巴尼河以南、杰内以西是本杜古，班巴拉语意为「青草之乡」，原为马里帝国的旧省。博佐人的渔村在一处渡口旁长成桑镇：内尼日尔三角洲的水路在此接上通往南方金矿区的旱道。这座约1400年兴起、臣属达阿王国的商镇，究竟是迪亚来的马尔卡人还是杰内来的朱拉人所建，口述传说说法不一。本地十二位小王多出自特拉奥雷氏族，在名为亚夫的中央任命官吏管辖下治理各村。1444年的本杜古奉曼萨为君，桑镇市集上买卖的是铁器、河米和织工出产的泥染布。

桑海始终没能真正吞下这片旧省：1542年阿斯基亚·伊沙克一世在此击败马里军队，阿斯基亚·达乌德后来又来攻掠，但十二位小王一直保有村庄，直到通迪比一战把帝国统治整个卷走。18世纪，这里处在比通·库利巴利的塞古帝国松散边缘；1739年孔国的法马甘·瓦塔拉插手班巴拉内战，摧毁桑镇，居民后来在稍北处重建新城。每年第七个月的第二个星期四，全镇人聚到桑凯塘举行「桑凯蒙」集体渔祭，纪念建城。1818年，塞库·阿马杜的圣战者在巴尼河彼岸的努库马获胜；到1821年，哈姆杜拉希哈里发国的势力已抵达本杜古的渡口。

en:
Lobi is the country south of the upper Black Volta, farmland and hunting grounds with no single royal town. At Loropéni in the south, stone walls ringed a fortress settlement, the best preserved of ten such enclosures in the area; Lohron and Kulango traders held it and grew rich carrying gold toward the trans-Saharan routes, and it stood at its height between the fourteenth and seventeenth centuries before being abandoned early in the nineteenth. In 1444 Gan, Lohron, Kulango and other Gur-speaking villagers held most of the country, while the related peoples later grouped as Lobi still lived mainly east of the river.

Around 1770 those Lobi groups began crossing the Black Volta from the country around Wa, settling among the Gan, Kulango and older Teese inhabitants. They kept no kings and ordered their lives through village councils, initiation rites and village shrines, which made them difficult subjects for the cavalry states on their borders. In 1815 Bakary Ouattara, brother of the founder of Gwiriko, raided the country and burned several villages before a Lobi archer killed him with a poisoned arrow. The village leagues survived the raid, and the Lobi war bands of the early nineteenth century were known to their neighbors for their bows, their field earthworks and their defense of the shrines.
zh:
洛比是黑沃尔特河上游以南的一片地方，没有单一王都，到处是农田和猎场。南部洛罗佩尼的石墙围着一座要塞聚落，是当地十处同类围城中保存最好的一处；洛龙人和库兰戈人占据此地，靠把黄金运往跨撒哈拉商路致富，14至17世纪最为兴旺，到19世纪初被废弃。1444年，甘人、洛龙人、库兰戈人等说古尔语的村社占据此地大部，后来统称洛比人的诸族群当时还主要住在河以东。

约1770年，洛比诸群体从瓦城一带开始渡过黑沃尔特河，迁入甘人、库兰戈人和更古老的泰塞人中间。他们没有国王，按村社会议、成丁仪式和各村神龛安排生活，周边的骑兵强国很难把他们变成顺民。1815年，格维里科建立者的兄弟巴卡里·瓦塔拉来袭，焚毁数座村庄，被一名洛比弓箭手用毒箭射死。各村的联盟熬过了这场袭击；到19世纪初，邻邦提起洛比战士，想到的就是弓箭、野战土工和他们死守的神龛。

en:
Gwiriko was the Dyula name for the lands at the far end of the caravan road, in the upper Mouhoun bend beyond the reach of the Niger trading cities. The word means 'at the end of the long stage', or 'beyond the forest'. Its chief town was Sya, now the Dioulassoba quarter of Bobo-Dioulasso; local tradition traces it to Kibidoué, a Bobo farming village founded around 1050 where Mande Dyula traders later settled. Sya dealt mainly in horses brought south from Djenné and the Inner Niger Delta on their way to Kong, Begho and the Gold Coast, while Bobo-Oulé farms around it sold grain to the caravans. In 1444 Muslim Dyula merchants lived there among farming clans who kept their own rites, and the town was ruled by its own chiefs.

Its kings came from Kong. After Seku Ouattara founded the Kong empire in 1710, his brother Famagan Ouattara established Gwiriko in the Mouhoun bend in 1714 as his deputy, and the Wattara took Sya itself only in 1737–38 during Kong's push north. When Seku died in 1745 Famagan refused homage to his sons, seized Tiefo, Dafin and Bwamu and ruled Sya as the head of a nearly independent branch. His successors joined Dyula merchant wealth, Bobo grain and cavalry, and crushed repeated village revolts by force. Gwiriko never became a centralized state; around 1800 it was still a Sya-centred web of markets, war leaders and tributary villages.
zh:
圭里科是朱拉语对商路尽头之地的称呼，地处穆洪河上游河湾，超出尼日尔河商埠势力所及；名字意为「长途驿站的尽头」，一说意为「森林之外」。它的首镇是萨城，即后来博博迪乌拉索的迪乌拉索巴老城区。当地传说把萨城追溯到约1050年博博农民建立的基比杜埃村，曼德朱拉商人后来在此定居。萨城主要做马匹生意：马匹从杰内和内尼日尔河三角洲南下，经此运往孔、贝戈和黄金海岸，周围博博—乌莱人的农田则把谷物卖给商队。1444年，穆斯林朱拉商人住在保留本地仪轨的农耕氏族中间，城镇由本地酋长治理。

后来的君主出自孔。1710年塞库·瓦塔拉建立孔帝国，其弟法马甘·瓦塔拉于1714年作为他的代理人在穆洪河河湾建立圭里科，瓦塔拉家族到1737—1738年孔向北扩张时才取得萨城。1745年塞库死后，法马甘拒绝向塞库之子称臣，夺取蒂埃福、达凡和布瓦穆，以近乎独立的支系之首统治萨城。他的继承者把朱拉商人的财富、博博人的谷物和骑兵结合起来，以武力镇压村落的反复起事。圭里科始终没有成为集权国家：到1800年前后，它仍是以萨城为中心，由市场、军头和朝贡村落组成的网络。

en:
Bono Manso stood on the fringe where the Akan forest thins into savanna, south of the Black Volta, the capital of Bono, the earliest of the Akan states. The town took shape around the year 1000, and its Dwabirem market was the southern end of the caravan road from Djenné and Timbuktu: donkeys and horses could not live in the dense forest farther south, so Wangara and Juula merchants unloaded Saharan salt, cloth and brassware here and packed up gold dust, kola nuts and ivory. In 1444 the Bonohene at Bono Manso ruled the leading power of the northern Akan lands, his wealth drawn from the goldfields and the caravans.

Kings Ameyaw and Obunumankoma enlarged the state in the later fifteenth century. Drought and succession disputes weakened it in the seventeenth, and the European trading posts on the coast drew the gold trade south to Akan states armed with firearms. The last Bonohene, Ameyaw Kwakye I, raised taxes and let the royal rites lapse; when the Asante came, his people refused to defend the capital, saying that if the king had his war he could fight it himself. In 1722-1723 the Asantehene Opoku Ware I stormed Bono Manso and carried the king and queen off to Kumasi; Bono craftsmen were put to work in Asante workshops, and the surviving royal line settled at Techiman under Kumasi's overlordship.
zh:
博诺曼索坐落在阿肯森林没入草原的边缘、黑沃尔特河以南，是阿肯诸邦中最早的博诺王国的都城。城镇约在1000年成形，城中的德瓦比伦市场是杰内、廷巴克图商路的南端：驴马进不了南方的密林，万加拉和朱乌拉商人便在这里卸下撒哈拉的盐、布匹和铜器，装走金砂、柯拉果和象牙。1444年，坐镇博诺曼索的博诺赫内统治着北阿肯最强大的政权，财富来自金矿和商队。

15世纪后期，阿梅尧和奥布努曼科马两位国王开疆拓土。17世纪的干旱和王位纷争削弱了王国，欧洲人在沿海的商站又把黄金贸易引向掌握火器的南方阿肯诸邦。末代博诺赫内阿梅尧·夸基一世加征赋税、荒废王家祭仪；阿散蒂人打来时，国人拒绝据守都城，说「国王既要打仗，就让他自己打」。1722至1723年，阿散蒂赫内奥坡库·瓦雷一世攻陷博诺曼索，把国王和王后掳回库马西；博诺工匠被送进阿散蒂的作坊效力，残存的王族则在库马西的宗主权下定居泰奇曼。

en:
West of Bono Manso the Akan forest opens into grassland cut by the Black Volta, the corridor the northern caravans followed. Its great market was Begho, also called Nsoko, a town founded in the eleventh century where Soninke Wangara merchants from Mali traded Saharan salt, cloth and brassware for Akan gold and kola; its quarters held Brong farmers and Mande Muslim families side by side, and three roads ran south from the town, among them the road through Dormaa to Elmina on the coast. In 1444 this was Akan country on the western fringe of the Bono state, living on the trade that passed through Begho.

In the seventeenth century Aduana Akan from Dormaa moved into the Black Volta basin, brought the Kulango, Nafana and Ligbi peoples under their rule, and made Amanvi the seat of the kingdom of Gyaman, with the old Dyula town of Bondoukou as its commercial hub. The Asantehene Opoku Ware I destroyed the capital in 1740-1741 and reduced Gyaman to tribute; Begho was sacked around the same years and its merchants dispersed to Bondoukou and Kong. Around 1800 Kwadwo Adinkra took power, and in 1818 he withheld tribute and rose against the Asantehene Osei Tutu Kwamina. He was killed in the war that followed, some said by his own hand to escape capture, and an effigy of his head entered the Asantehene's stool regalia; in 1819 Asante turned Gyaman into an occupied province and barred it from trading direct with the coast. The stamped and printed cloths of Adinkra's court were taken up by the Asante and survive as the Adinkra symbols of the Akan.
zh:
博诺曼索以西，阿肯森林让位于黑沃尔特河穿过的草原，这条地带正是北方商队往来的走廊。当地的大市场叫贝戈，又名恩索科，是11世纪兴起的城镇：来自马里的索宁克万加拉商人用撒哈拉的盐、布匹和铜器交换阿肯人的黄金和柯拉果；城里各街区中，布龙农民与曼德穆斯林家庭比邻而居，三条商路南通海岸，其中一条经多尔马抵达埃尔米纳。1444年，这里是博诺西缘的阿肯人之地，靠途经贝戈的贸易为生。

17世纪，来自多尔马的阿杜阿纳氏族阿肯人迁入黑沃尔特河流域，将库兰戈人、纳法纳人和利格比人纳入治下，以阿曼维为都建立贾曼王国，古老的朱乌拉城邦邦杜库成为商业中心。阿散蒂赫内奥坡库·瓦雷一世于1740至1741年摧毁其都城，迫使贾曼称臣纳贡；贝戈也在同一时期被洗劫，商人四散逃往邦杜库和孔城。1800年前后夸德沃·阿丁克拉即位，1818年他停止纳贡，起兵反抗阿散蒂赫内奥塞·图图·夸米纳，在随后的战争中丧命，有说法称他为免被俘而自尽，他首级的模拟像还被收入阿散蒂赫内的王权法器；1819年阿散蒂将贾曼改为军管行省，禁止它与海岸直接通商。阿丁克拉宫廷使用的戳印花布被阿散蒂人沿用，流传为阿肯人的阿丁克拉符号。

en:
Dagbon is the kingdom of the Dagomba, spread over the open grassland of the White Volta basin. The Gbewaa dynasty united the villages of the Tindaamba, the local earth-priests, and Naa Nyagsi, who reigned from 1416 to 1432, overthrew them one by one, set his capital at Yani Dabari near modern Tamale, and placed his own sons over the conquered towns. Its plains yielded grain, cattle and iron, and Dyula caravans between the Niger bend and Hausaland passed through its markets. Dagbon tradition also claims the neighbouring Mossi dynasties as kin: it tells of the princess Yennenga, a warrior who fled her father the king disguised as a man on her stallion, met a hunter far to the north, and bore Ouedraogo, founder of the royal lines of Wagadugu, Tenkodogo and Yatenga. In 1444 the Yaa Naa at Yani Dabari ruled the strongest power of the northern Volta basin, his people still keeping their ancestral earth cults.

In the seventeenth century the rising Gonja kingdom struck from the west and seized Daboya, the salt town on the road from Yendi to Bouna. After years of war Yaa Naa Luro moved the court east to Yendi, and late in the century Naa Zanjina defeated the Gonja near the new capital and killed their chief Kumpatia. He was the first Muslim Yaa Naa, and Dyula and Hausa scholars settled by the palace to say the king's protective prayers; around 1700 the Moliyili house of learning made Dagbon a centre of Arabic letters, its scholars writing chronicles and works of law in an Ajami hand. Kola and salt linked Yendi with Salaga, Kumasi and the Hausa cities, and by 1788 travellers called the town larger than Kumasi. In the 1740s Asante armies reached Yendi, and Dagbon paid tribute to Kumasi for a time.
zh:
达格邦是达贡巴人的王国，疆域铺展在白沃尔特河流域开阔的草原上。格贝瓦王朝兼并了本地土地祭司廷达姆巴所辖的村落；1416至1432年在位的纳·尼亚克西逐次推翻他们，定都亚尼·达巴里（在今塔马利附近），把诸子分封为各征服城镇的统治者。平原出产谷物、牲畜和铁器，往返于尼日尔河河曲与豪萨兰之间的朱乌拉商队途经这里的市场。达格邦传说还把相邻的莫西诸王朝视为亲族：公主耶内加是员女将，因父王不许嫁人而女扮男装，骑一匹种马出逃，在遥远的北方遇见一位猎人，生下韦德拉奥果，即瓦加杜古、滕科多戈和亚滕加诸王族的始祖。1444年，坐镇亚尼·达巴里的亚阿·纳是北沃尔特河流域最强大的君主，他的人民仍信奉祖传的土地崇拜。

17世纪，兴起的贡贾王国从西方攻入，夺取了耶恩迪通往布纳商路上的盐镇达博亚。多年战争后，亚阿·纳·卢罗把宫廷东迁耶恩迪；17世纪末，纳·赞吉纳在新都附近击败贡贾人，斩杀其首领昆帕蒂亚。他是第一位信奉伊斯兰教的亚阿·纳，朱乌拉和豪萨学者在宫旁定居，为国王诵念祈福的祷文；约1700年创立的莫利伊利学馆使达格邦成为阿拉伯学术的中心，学者们用阿贾米文撰写编年史和律法著作。柯拉果和盐把耶恩迪与萨拉加、库马西和豪萨诸城连在一起，到1788年，过路客商称这座城比库马西还大。18世纪40年代阿散蒂军队进抵耶恩迪，达格邦一度向库马西纳贡。

en:
The forest between the Ofin and the Pra, around Dunkwa-on-Offin, was in 1444 a country of Akan village-clans. The Agona and other Akani families washed gold in the Ofin and Oda valleys and looked to Adanse, the oldest of the forest Akan states, for ritual leadership. Their gold dust went two ways: south through Akani broker-towns to a coast where no European fort yet stood, and north to the marts of Begho and Bono Manso. No paramount king ruled the district; the men who would build an empire here were still one clan among many.

By the mid-seventeenth century the Agona had built the kingdom of Denkyira and turned Abankeseso into an imperial capital. Adanse, Sefwi, Wassa, Aowin and Assin paid tribute, and their gold filled the Sikadan, the royal treasury. Denkyira's armies kept the roads to the coastal forts open, and in 1692 Dutch, English and Brandenburg envoys travelled inland to Abankeseso to treat with Denkyirahene Boamponsem, whose country the European factors called the richest in gold on the coast.

Boamponsem died two years later, and his successor Ntim Gyakari drove the subject states to rebellion with his tribute demands. One by one they turned to Osei Tutu of Kwaaman and his priest Okomfo Anokye, who were forging the Asante union. In 1701 Ntim Gyakari marched north with two or three Dutch cannons and chased Osei Tutu's men out of three towns, straight into an ambush prepared at Feyiase. The full Asante army fell on his force, killed the king and captured the cannons; Abankeseso was sacked. A revolt in 1706 was crushed, and for the rest of the eighteenth century Denkyira took its orders from Kumasi, its goldfields feeding the Asante empire.
zh:
奥芬河与普拉河之间、奥芬河畔敦夸周围的林区，1444年还是阿肯氏族村落的乡土。阿戈纳等阿卡尼家族在奥芬河与奥达河谷淘金，礼制上尊奉林中阿肯诸邦里最古老的阿丹斯。金沙分两路外运：向南经阿卡尼掮客的集镇，送到还没有欧洲商堡的海岸；向北送往贝戈和博诺曼索的市集。此时这里没有一统各部的大王，后来建起帝国的人此刻还只是众多氏族中的一支。

到17世纪中叶，阿戈纳人建起登基拉王国，把阿班克塞索经营成帝都。阿丹斯、塞夫维、瓦萨、奥温、阿辛等邦纷纷纳贡，黄金堆满王室的西卡丹宝库。登基拉军队维持着通往海岸商堡的道路；1692年，荷兰、英国和勃兰登堡的使节深入内地，到阿班克塞索觐见登基拉赫内博阿蓬塞姆，欧洲商馆管事称他的国家是海岸上最富金的国度。

两年后博阿蓬塞姆去世，继任的恩蒂姆·贾卡里索贡无度，逼反属邦。各邦陆续投向正在缔造阿散蒂联盟的库马曼首领奥塞·图图和他的祭司奥科姆福·阿诺基耶。1701年，恩蒂姆·贾卡里带着两三门荷兰大炮北上，把奥塞·图图的人马连逐三城，径直钻进了费亚斯的埋伏。阿散蒂大军合围，击杀国王，缴获大炮，阿班克塞索也被洗劫。1706年的反叛再遭镇压，此后整个18世纪登基拉都听命于库马西，金矿区转而供养阿散蒂帝国。

en:
The western Gold Coast runs from the Nzima country around Axim east to the Fante headlands, a surf-bound shore backed by gold-bearing hills. In 1444 Akan towns held the beaches and lagoons: Nzima fishermen at the mouth of the Ankobra, the old kingdom of Eguafo above the village of Mina, and Fetu further east. Gold washed in the forest rivers came down to the coast to be bartered for salt and fish, while Akani brokers carried the dust on to the northern marts. No European had yet appeared on the shore.

The Portuguese reached it in 1471. Eleven years later Diogo de Azambuja treated with the Eguafo lord Caramansa and raised São Jorge da Mina at Elmina, the first European stronghold in sub-Saharan Africa, and Fort Santo António was later built at Axim. The Dutch took Elmina in 1637 and Axim five years on. At Cabo Corso the Swedes put up a timber fort, Carolusborg, in 1653; it passed between Swedes, Danes, Dutchmen and the king of Fetu before Robert Holmes seized it for England in 1664 and rebuilt it as Cape Coast Castle, the English headquarters on this stretch of coast. As captives overtook gold as the staple trade, its underground dungeons held as many as a thousand men and women awaiting shipment. The Brandenburgers raised Groß Friedrichsburg at Pokesu in 1682; after they withdrew, the local chief John Konny held the abandoned fort against Dutch arms for seven years. Fante brokers mediated between the castles and the interior until the Ashanti-Fante wars of 1806-1807 broke their power, and by 1816 the Fante states were tributary to Kumasi.
zh:
黄金海岸西部，西起阿克西姆一带的恩济马人之地，东到芳蒂人的岬角，拍岸浪后面是含金的丘陵。1444年，阿肯人的城镇据有海滩和潟湖：安科布拉河口是恩济马渔民，米纳村之上是古老的埃瓜福王国，更东边是费图。森林河川里淘出的黄金南运海岸，换取食盐和咸鱼，阿卡尼掮客再把金沙转往北方的市集。此时海岸上还没有欧洲人。

葡萄牙人1471年抵达。十一年后，第奥古·德阿赞布雅与埃瓜福首领卡拉曼萨缔约，在埃尔米纳筑起圣若热·达米纳堡，这是撒哈拉以南欧洲人的第一座要塞；阿克西姆后来也建起圣安东尼奥堡。荷兰人1637年攻下埃尔米纳，五年后取得阿克西姆。在科博科索，瑞典人1653年建起木堡卡尔斯堡，它在瑞典人、丹麦人、荷兰人和费图国王之间几度易手，1664年罗伯特·霍姆斯为英国夺占，扩建成海岸角城堡，作为英国人在这段海岸的总部。奴隶取代黄金成为主要贸易后，城堡的地下地牢能关押上千名等待运出的男女。勃兰登堡人1682年在波克苏筑起大腓特烈堡；他们撤离后，当地酋长约翰·康尼据守这座废堡，力抗荷兰军队达七年之久。芳蒂掮客在城堡与内地之间居间撮合，直到1806至1807年的阿散蒂—芳蒂战争击垮他们，到1816年芳蒂各邦都向库马西纳贡。

en:
Sah stands on the right bank of the Bara-Issa, the branch that drains the northern end of Lake Débo, the wide seasonal lake midway between Jenné and Timbuktu. Arab geographers and later European mapmakers drew this 'Great Lake' on chart after chart: a study of nine centuries of maps of the region found it on 95 percent of them, and of all the features they drew only the Nile appeared more often. Each flood turned the channels around Sah into fishing grounds and left damp silt fields for millet and rice as the water fell. Somono canoemen, Bozo and Sorko fishermen, Bambara cultivators and Fulbe herders all lived by that rhythm. In 1444 Sah belonged to the river world of Jenné: its canoes worked the lane carrying grain and dried fish north to Timbuktu and bringing Saharan salt south, and most villagers kept the old water and ancestor rites rather than the Islam of the merchant cities.

Power on this lane belonged to war canoes, and Sonni Ali built Songhai's navy on Sorko crews. Jenné endured years of siege before it submitted in 1473, and Sah passed into the Songhai Empire with it. The river empire held until March 1591, when Judar Pasha's Saadi musketeers and cavalry broke Askia Ishaq II at Tondibi. Moroccan soldiers settled as the Arma, but after the last reinforcement crossed the desert in 1618 the Timbuktu pashalik broke into garrison towns that answered to no one, and in the eighteenth century Bambara power from Ségou reached the delta. In 1818 Seku Amadu defeated the Bambara coalition at Noukouma, took Jenné in 1819 and built Hamdullahi in 1820 as the capital of his Fulbe Diina. Under its judges and land-masters, Sah's fisheries, flood fields and cattle tracks were ruled like the rest of Massina, by the calendar of the river.
zh:
萨位于巴拉-伊萨河右岸，这条河汊从代博湖北端排水；代博湖是杰内与廷巴克图之间随季节涨落的大湖。阿拉伯地理学者和后来的欧洲制图者把这片「大湖」画进一张又一张地图：有人研究过九个世纪里的本区地图，95%都画了它，在所画的各种地物里，出现得比它更多的只有尼罗河。每年汛期，萨周围的水道变成渔场，水退之后，湿润的淤泥地种上粟和稻。索莫诺船夫、博若和索尔科渔民、班巴拉农夫与富拉尼牧民都按这个水令生活。1444年，萨属于杰内的河水世界：独木舟沿杰内至廷巴克图的水路把谷物和鱼干北运，再把撒哈拉的食盐南运，多数村民仍守河水与祖灵仪式，不信商城里的伊斯兰教。

控制这条水路靠的是战船，桑尼·阿里正是以索尔科人为桨手建立桑海船队。杰内被围数年后于1473年投降，萨随之并入桑海帝国。河上帝国维持到1591年3月，朱达尔帕夏的萨阿德火枪兵和骑兵在通迪比击溃阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世。摩洛哥士兵留驻成为阿尔马人，但1618年最后一批援军穿过沙漠后，廷巴克图帕夏领分裂成各自为政的军镇；18世纪，塞古的班巴拉势力伸入三角洲。1818年，塞库·阿马杜在努库马击败班巴拉联军，1819年夺取杰内，1820年建起哈姆杜拉希，作为富拉尼迪纳的都城。在它的法官与土地主人治下，萨的渔场、洪泛田和牧道同马西纳其他地方一样，按河水的时令管理。

en:
Méma is the alluvial country west of Lake Debo and the Inner Niger Delta, flooded every year by the Niger and planted with millet and rice; canoes carried its grain north to Timbuktu, and the river towns counted it among their granaries. It was an old Soninke kingdom and once a province of Ghana, and the Epic of Sundiata gives it a named part: when Sundiata fled the Manding country, the Tunkara of Méma sheltered him and sent the cavalry that helped him defeat Soumaoro Kanté. The mansas of Mali let Méma keep more freedom than their ordinary provinces in return. The kingdom broke away in 1433, and in 1444 the Tunkara ruled on his own again, pressed for allegiance by both the Tuareg who held Timbuktu and the Songhai kings of Gao.

Independence lasted one generation: Méma fell to Sonni Ali's Songhai. Its eastern town of Tindirma was founded in 1496 by Sephardic Jews expelled from Spain and Portugal, and grew into the seat of the Kurmina-fari, governor of the western provinces; Jewish graves from those years still stand in the village. Askia Ishaq II sacked Tindirma in 1588 after a revolt, and after Tondibi in 1591 the Moroccans put one of their river kasbahs there. When the Arma garrisons weakened, the Bambara of Ségou moved into the gap: Bitòn Coulibaly, who ruled from 1712 to 1755, took Djenné and raided Timbuktu, and Méma's grain fields became part of the Bambara empire.
zh:
梅玛在德博湖和内尼日尔三角洲以西，是一片年年被尼日尔河泛滥浸润的冲积地，种粟和稻；粮船顺河北上廷巴克图，河滨诸城把它当作自己的粮仓之一。这里本是古老的索宁克人王国，曾为加纳的行省，在《松迪亚塔史诗》里也有一号：松迪亚塔逃离曼丁故地时，梅玛的通卡拉收留了他，又派骑兵助他击败苏毛洛·坎特；马里的曼萨们因此让梅玛保留了比普通行省更大的自主权。1433年梅玛脱离马里，1444年通卡拉再度独自治国，占据廷巴克图的图阿雷格人与加奥的桑海人都来逼他归附。

独立只维持了一代人，梅玛便落入桑尼·阿里的桑海之手。境东的廷迪尔马城1496年由被逐出西班牙和葡萄牙的塞法迪犹太人建立，后来成为桑海西部行省长官库尔米纳法里的驻所，早年的犹太墓葬仍在村中。1588年，阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世在一场叛乱后洗劫该城；1591年通迪比之战后，摩洛哥人又在这里设了一座河畔卡斯巴。阿尔马戍军衰弱后，塞古的班巴拉人填上空缺：1712至1755年在位的比顿·库利巴利夺取杰内、攻掠廷巴克图，梅玛的粮田也被并入班巴拉帝国。

en:
Kala was the river province immediately above the Inner Niger Delta, holding both banks of the Niger north of Bendugu. Under Mali its governor, the Fala Faren, kept his seat at Kokry, while Sama, Niono, Sansanding and Sibila each commanded a channel, a fishing ground or a stretch of flood plain. Bozo and Sorko families paddled the pirogues and cast the nets, trading river fish to Jenné's merchants for grain, cloth and salt. Jenné lay close by, yet in 1444 Kala still answered to the mansa of Mali; its river people prayed as Muslims and kept the older water rites as well.

Sonni Ali's Songhai took Kala in the 1470s and renamed its governor the Cha'a. After Tondibi in 1591 the province rebelled and Askia Ishaq II had to march against it himself; in 1599, at the battle of Jenné, the Kala-sha Bukar brought his canoes over to the Timbuktu pashalik, and Mansa Mahmud IV's defeat ended Mali's last attempt to rebuild an empire. A Bambara rising in 1645 swept away the old chiefdoms, leaving only Traoré petty kings, and after Biton Coulibaly built Ségou's Somono war fleet Kala followed the new Bambara power on the middle Niger. Its town Sansanding grew into the great market port of the Bamana age. When Mungo Park reached it in 1796 he counted eight to ten thousand people: stalls sold indigo balls and Jenné and Hausa cloth, a slab of salt fetched eight thousand cowries, and wholesale crowds packed the Tuesday market. Park passed through again in 1805 on his last journey downstream, from which he did not return. In time the old provincial name survived mainly on the north bank, in Ségou's shadow, while Seku Amadu held the delta to the south.
zh:
卡拉是紧接在内尼日尔三角洲上游的河省，据有本杜古以北的尼日尔河两岸。马里统治时，行省长官法拉·法兰驻在科克里，萨马、尼奥诺、桑桑丁和西比拉各控一条水道、一片渔场或一段洪泛平原。博若和索尔科家族划独木舟、撒渔网，把河鱼卖给杰内商人，换回谷物、布匹和食盐。杰内城虽近，1444年的卡拉却仍奉曼萨号令；河居者既按伊斯兰教礼拜，也守更古老的河水仪式。

15世纪70年代，桑尼·阿里的桑海夺取卡拉，把长官改称「恰阿」。1591年通迪比之战后卡拉反叛，阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世只得亲自出征；1599年杰内之战，卡拉-恰·布卡尔率独木舟倒向廷巴克图帕夏，曼萨·马哈茂德四世战败，马里重建帝国的最后努力告终。1645年班巴拉起事扫平旧酋长领地，只留下特拉奥雷系小王；比顿·库利巴利建起塞古的索莫诺战船队之后，卡拉便追随尼日尔河中游新起的班巴拉强权。境内的桑桑丁成长为班巴拉时代的大市场港埠。1796年蒙哥·帕克抵达时，估其人口有八千到一万：摊上摆着靛蓝团、杰内布和豪萨布，一板盐卖到八千枚贝币，周二的大集挤满趸货的人潮。1805年，帕克在最后一次顺流而下的途中再次经过，再也没有回来。旧省名后来主要留在北岸，在塞古的威势下存续，南面的三角洲则归塞库·阿马杜。

en:
The middle Niger runs straight here between Timbuktu and Gao, narrowing at Bamba between banks of fishing villages. Their people are the Sorko, the oldest rivermen of the Songhai country: they hollowed canoes out of cailcedrat trunks, netted fish from the river, ferried goods for the kings and pulled oars in the imperial fleet, paying their tribute in dried fish. Sorko tales tell of Nana Miriam, who used her wits and magic to kill a giant hippopotamus harrying the riverside settlements. In 1444 the reach belonged to the Songhai kings of Gao, who kept Bamba and the village of Karabara as stations on the river road to Timbuktu, while Tuareg herds grazed the desert edge to the north.

This bank is where the Moroccan invasion first reached the Niger: in February 1591 Judar Pasha, a commander of Spanish origin, led his musketeers across the Sahara to the river at Karabara, and the following month their firearms destroyed Askia Ishaq II's army at Tondibi. The Moroccans built a chain of kasbahs on the river ports and placed one at Bamba; in 1599 boats sent from Timbuktu carried the reinforcements that broke the mansa of Mali's attack on Djenné. After 1618 the soldiers, by then called the Arma, named their own pashas and ignored Marrakesh, and in 1630 they made peace with the Songhai holding out in Dendi. Their rule splintered through the next century, and around 1770 the Tuareg took Gao; the riverside villages answered to whichever cavalry reached the bank.
zh:
廷巴克图与加奥之间，尼日尔河在这一段笔直流过，到班巴附近收窄，两岸尽是渔村。村民是索尔科人，桑海故地最老的河上人：他们凿木做成独木舟，在河里撒网捕鱼，替国王运送货物，也到帝国舰队上划桨，缴纳的贡赋是干鱼。索尔科人的故事里有一位娜娜·米丽亚姆，相传她凭机智和法术杀死了一头祸害河畔村落的巨型河马。1444年，这一段河岸属于加奥的桑海国王，班巴和卡拉巴拉村是通往廷巴克图的水路上的驿站，北侧沙漠边缘有图阿雷格人的牧群。

摩洛哥入侵军正是在这段河岸第一次踏上尼日尔河畔：1591年2月，西班牙裔将领朱达尔帕夏率火枪手越过撒哈拉，在卡拉巴拉抵达河边，次月便用火器在通迪比击溃阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世的大军。摩洛哥人在沿河港口连筑卡斯巴，班巴也设了一座；1599年马里曼萨攻打杰内，廷巴克图派船运来援军将其击退。1618年后，被称为阿尔马的戍兵自行任命帕夏，不再理会马拉喀什，1630年又与据守登迪的桑海人议和。此后一个世纪里阿尔马的统治四分五裂，约1770年图阿雷格人夺取加奥，河畔渔村谁家骑兵到了岸边，就向谁纳贡。

en:
The Haayre is the broken rock country around Douentza, east of the Inner Niger Delta; its name means 'rocky place' in Fulfulde. Granite outcrops rise from a dry Sahelian plain, holding rainwater in their pools long after the flats have dried and giving villagers a wall of stone to climb when horsemen appear. Between roughly 700 and 1200, at the height of Wagadu, the same country carried dense villages and iron-workings on an industrial scale. In 1444 it was the open northern march of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga, whose horsemen were the feared raiders of the century: chronicles report Mossi bands taking Timbuktu and sacking Walata, though some historians put those raids down to other peoples. Farmers here sowed uncertain fields, kept cattle and retreated into the rocks at the first alarm.

Sonni Ali campaigned against the Mossi for six years, and his victory at Kubi, south of Lake Débo in 1483, brought the Haayre chiefs under Songhai. Askia Muhammad carried a holy war down the same frontier in 1497 and defeated the Mossi without converting them. After the Songhai army broke at Tondibi in March 1591 no outside power held the rocks, and through the seventeenth century Tuareg bands and Fulbe moving out of the delta fought over the same villages, wells and cattle herds, the plateaus sheltering whichever side lost. In the 1810s Fulbe chiefs followed the example of Seku Amadu, who founded Massina in 1818 and built Hamdullahi in 1820, turning their raiding parties into a Fulbe-led kingdom with Douentza its leading town, fed with grain and labour from conquered villages. The Haayre became the stony eastern edge of the new Massina state.
zh:
海雷是杜安扎周围、内尼日尔三角洲以东的破碎岩地，其名在富拉语中意为「多岩之地」。花岗岩丘从干旱的萨赫勒平原隆起，岩间水潭在平原干透后仍存着雨水，骑兵出现时，村民也能翻入石壁据守。约700年至1200年的瓦加杜时期，这片土地村落稠密，冶铁已具工业规模。1444年，它是莫西人雅滕加王国敞开的北路边地；莫西骑兵是那个世纪令人生畏的袭掠者，史籍记载他们攻下廷巴克图、洗劫瓦拉塔，但也有学者把这些袭掠归于别的族群。此地的农夫在收成难料的田里耕作、牧牛，警报一来便退进岩丘。

桑尼·阿里对莫西作战六年，1483年在代博湖以南的库比取胜，海雷诸首领归入桑海。1497年，阿斯基亚·穆罕默德沿同一条边地发动圣战，打败莫西人，却没能使他们改宗。1591年3月桑海军在通迪比溃败后，再没有外部政权守住这些岩石；整个17世纪，图阿雷格队伍和迁出三角洲的富拉尼人反复争夺同样的村落、水井和牛群，谁打输了就上高原躲避。1810年代，富拉尼首领效法塞库·阿马杜（1818年建马西纳、1820年筑哈姆杜拉希），把掠袭队伍整合成富拉尼人主导的王国，以杜安扎为首要城镇，由被征服的村落供给谷物和劳力。海雷成了新兴马西纳国家多石的东缘。

en:
South of the Niger bend the Gourma steppe runs into a wall of sandstone mesas, and the highest of them, Hombori Tondo, climbs to 1,155 metres, the tallest peak in Mali. Dogon farmers built their villages on the terraces and in the narrow valleys, keeping to the old cults after the river towns turned to Islam, and Songhay-speaking hunters lived among them; Hombori was already an old Dogon town before its age was recorded. In 1444 the escarpment was the northern march of the Mossi kingdom of Yatenga, whose horsemen raided between the hills and the Niger, and no army from Gao had yet marched this far south.

The mesas were drawn into the wars of the river empires. In 1483 Sonni Ali broke off his canal works toward Walata and turned back to throw a Mossi invasion out of Songhai. After Tondibi in 1591 a branch of the Askia royal house fled from Gao to Hombori, with Songhai refugees following, and the chiefs who raided south into Mali in the old empire's name rode out from these valleys. Villages deeper in the crags answered to no one: Tabi, thirty kilometres into the hills, was never taken, and its people kept their traditional rites through the years of Moroccan and Arma power on the river.
zh:
尼日尔河套以南，古尔马草原的尽头耸起一道砂岩台地峭壁，其中最高的洪博里通多山海拔1155米，是马里全境的最高点。多贡农夫在台地和狭谷里建村，河滨城镇改奉伊斯兰之后，山里人仍守着古老的信仰，讲桑海语的猎人和他们同住；洪博里早就是一座古老的多贡城镇，何时建城已不可考。1444年，这片崖地是莫西人雅滕加王国的北疆，骑兵在群山与尼日尔河之间往来劫掠，加奥还没有派军队远征到这么靠南的地方。

台地也被卷进河畔诸帝国的战事。1483年，桑尼·阿里中断通往瓦拉塔的运河工程，回师把入侵的莫西人赶出桑海。1591年通迪比战败后，阿斯基亚王室的一支从加奥逃到洪博里，桑海难民随之而来，后来以旧帝国之名南侵马里的酋长们就从这些谷地出师。更深藏在岩壑里的村落谁也不臣服：深入山中30公里的塔比从未被攻下，摩洛哥人与阿尔马人在河上称雄的那些年，村民一直守着自己的传统祭仪。

en:
Liptako is the hot hill pasture north of Gourma, between the Niger bend and the upper Volta country, a land where cattle mattered more than towns. Its seasonal ponds, above all the Wendu water later called Dori, drew Gourmantché farmers, Songhai traders from the river, Tuareg caravans and Mossi raiders to the same grazing grounds; Dori is Gourmantché for the banks beyond the pond. Cattle, salt and grain moved along the tracks toward the Niger, much of it through the bargaining of the herder camps. In 1444 this was a loose frontier country under Gourmantché chiefs, not a kingdom with a walled capital.

Fula clans from Macina and Gourma began settling in Liptako in the seventeenth century, accepting Gourmantché rule at first and rising against it later. Brahima Seydou Birmali sent to Usman dan Fodio at Sokoto and came back with the caliph's battle banner, which turned the Fula revolt into a jihad; his men defeated the Gourmantché on the banks of the Yayré, the seasonal watercourse that fed the Dori pond, and founded the Emirate of Liptako in 1809-1810. Dan Fodio is said to have named the country himself: Liptako, 'the untamable'. Dori became the capital and livestock market of the westernmost Sokoto emirate, its caravans trading down the road to Say on the Niger, and in 1821 a Fula Muslim elite ruled this pastoral borderland.
zh:
利普塔科是古尔马以北炎热的丘陵牧地，处在尼日尔河河湾与沃尔特河上游之间；在这片地方，牛比城镇更要紧。季节性水塘，尤其是后来称作温杜、又称多里的水域，把古尔曼切农人、河上来的桑海商人、图阿雷格商队和莫西抄掠者引向同一片草场；「多里」在古尔曼切语里意为水塘彼岸的岸边。牛、盐和谷物沿旱道运往尼日尔河，大半经牧民营地间的讨价还价成交。1444年，这里是古尔曼切首领治下的松散边地，不是据有城墙都城的王国。

17世纪，来自马西纳和古尔马的富尔贝氏族开始在利普塔科定居，起初接受古尔曼切人统治，后来起兵反抗。布拉希马·赛义杜·比尔马利派人到索科托求见乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥，带回哈里发的战旗，富尔贝人的反抗随之变成圣战；他的部众在亚伊雷（Yayre，注入多里塘的季节水道）岸边击败古尔曼切人，于1809至1810年建立利普塔科埃米尔国。相传「利普塔科」这个名字就是丹·福迪奥亲自取的，意为「不可驯服者」。多里成为索科托体系最西端埃米尔国的都城和牲畜市场，商队沿旱道去往尼日尔河畔的萨伊；1821年，统治这片畜牧边地的已是富尔贝穆斯林精英。

en:
Bilanga is the open grain country east of the Mossi plateau, where the land rolls east into the Gourma savanna: scattered villages of Gurma and Mossi farmers, with nothing on the scale of the Niger-side cities. Its chief town gave its name to one of the small Gurma-Mossi polities counted among the Mossi kingdoms, whose ruler bore the title bilanbedo, and it is remembered as a one-time capital of the Gourma. Horsemen from Wogodogo, Yatenga and Gourma crossed its fields, and its own men had once marched against the Songhai Empire. In 1444 Bilanga was a chiefly village on a fought-over march, living on grain, cattle tribute and the ancestral earth cults.

The last emperor of Songhai came here as a fugitive. Askia Ishaq II lost the battle of Tondibi in March 1591, when Judar Pasha's four thousand Saadian troops broke his cavalry with arquebus fire and eight cannons just north of Gao. The empire fell apart and Ishaq was deposed; he fled toward Gourma and sought shelter in a town he had once raided. On his first night in Bilanga, in April 1592, the townspeople stormed his lodging and killed him. After that Bilanga slipped back into the rivalries of the Volta chiefdoms. The Fula jihad founded the Emirate of Liptako to its northwest in 1809–1810, but the old chiefly line kept its villages on the eastern savanna, and in 1821 Bilanga was still a small grain market served by its earth shrines.
zh:
比朗加位于莫西高原以东，地势向东铺入古尔马草原，是一片开阔的谷物地带：古尔曼人和莫西人农户聚成散落的村落，没有尼日尔河沿岸那样的大城市。当地的中心集镇为古尔曼-莫西诸小酋邦之一得名，统治者称号为「比兰贝多」，相传这座集镇还一度是古尔马地区的都城。沃戈多戈、雅滕加和古尔马的骑兵穿过这里的田野，当地人自己也曾出兵攻打过桑海帝国。1444年的比朗加是争夺边地上的一个酋长村落，靠谷物、牲口贡赋和土地祖灵祭祀过活。

桑海的末代皇帝是作为逃犯来到这里的。1591年3月，阿斯基亚·伊沙克二世在通迪比之战中溃败：加奥以北，朱达尔帕夏的四千萨阿德军队以火绳枪和八门火炮冲垮了他的骑兵。帝国瓦解，伊沙克被废，他逃往古尔马，到一座自己曾劫掠的城镇寻求庇护。1592年4月，他抵达比朗加的第一夜，镇上的人冲进住处将他杀死。此后比朗加重回沃尔特诸酋邦的纷争。1809至1810年，富尔贝圣战在西北方建立利普塔科埃米尔国，但旧酋长家族仍守着东部草原上的村落；到1821年，比朗加依旧是个靠祖灵祠庙维系的小型谷物集市。

en:
Tenkodogo, 'the old land' in Mooré, stands on the upper White Volta in the south-eastern Mossi country, and Mossi tradition honours it as the eldest of the Mossi dynasties. The founding story belongs to this stretch of river: the Dagbon princess Yennenga, the tale runs, fled her father's court disguised as a man on a white stallion and reached the upper Volta, where she met Rialé, a Bissa elephant hunter; their son was Ouédraogo, 'the male horse', who built Tenkodogo. His sons and their kin later founded Yatenga and Fada N'Gourma, while the line at Tenkodogo stayed. Its villages grew millet and sorghum, Peul herders tended the cattle, and Bissa farmers of Rialé's people cultivated the riverside fields; iron and pottery were worked and the market met every three days. In 1444 the Tenkodogo-naaba ruled his own people, joined by kinship and ritual to the other Mossi kings, while Wogodogo to the north-west under its Mogho Naaba was growing into the strongest of the Mossi powers.

Caravans carried kola north through the kingdom and salt south, and Muslim merchants kept their houses of prayer in the towns while the court went on with its ancestral sacrifices; the Mogho Naaba at Wogodogo took no tribute here and could not command the Tenkodogo-naaba. In the early nineteenth century the Fulbe jihads of Sokoto and Masina pressed the Volta basin, yet the Mossi of Tenkodogo kept their old rites and answered to no foreign ruler.
zh:
滕科多戈在莫雷语中意为「古老的土地」，地处莫西地区东南部的白沃尔特河上游，莫西传统把它尊为各莫西王朝中最古老的一个。建国传说就发生在这段河畔：相传达格邦公主耶内加女扮男装，骑一匹白色种马逃离父王宫廷，来到沃尔特河上游，遇见比萨族猎象人里亚莱；两人的儿子便是韦德拉奥果（意为「公马」），他修筑了滕科多戈。他的子孙后来另建亚滕加和法达恩古尔马，滕科多戈的王统则留在本地。四乡种植黍和高粱，颇尔牧人照看牛群，与里亚莱同族的比萨农民耕种河畔田地；人们冶铁制陶，集市每三天一次。1444年，滕科多戈纳巴统治自己的人民，与其他莫西诸王以血缘和祭仪相联，西北方莫戈霍·纳巴治下的瓦加杜古则是莫西诸地中最强的政权。

商队经王国北上贩运柯拉果、南下运盐，穆斯林商人在城中自有礼拜之所，宫廷却照常举行祖传祭祀；瓦加杜古的莫戈霍·纳巴从这里收不到贡物，也号令不了滕科多戈纳巴。19世纪初，索科托和马西纳的富尔贝圣战势力进逼沃尔特河流域，滕科多戈的莫西人仍守旧礼，不奉外来的统治者。

en:
Aribanda is the right bank of the Niger below Gao, dry grassland cut by floodplain and broken up by islands. Its chief place, Kukiya, lies on an island about 150 kilometres downstream from Gao, between two rapids and hard by the modern border with Niger. It is the oldest seat of the Songhai kings: the Za rulers held court here before moving upstream to Gao early in the tenth century, and when Mali seized Gao at the end of the thirteenth, the old royal line withdrew downstream again. The island commanded a stopping point on the trade road from Borgu and Hausaland toward North Africa.
