Arabic tombstone inscriptions in the cemeteries at nearby Bentia run from the late 1200s into Songhai times, yet the Timbuktu chronicle Tarikh al-Sudan still calls Kukiya 'the center of paganism'. In 1444 the bank belonged to the Songhai state of the Sonni dynasty, its villages growing grain and fishing under Muslim rulers whose people largely kept the old cults.

Sonni Ali Ber, who came to power in 1464 and built his empire on Gao, had grown up in this downstream country among his Dendi mother's people, and the Kukiya reaches stayed the river core of his state. In March 1591 the Saadian army destroyed the Songhai host at Tondibi, and the last Askias fled down the Niger through these islands on their way to Dendi and their new capital at Lulami. The Moroccans made Timbuktu, not Gao, their seat, so the upstream cities withered; the Aribanda bank fell back to its river chiefs and to the askias downstream, and Kukiya itself shrank into an ordinary riverside village.
zh:
阿里班达是加奥以下尼日尔河右岸之地，干燥草原间夹着漫滩与河洲。首镇库基亚坐落在加奥下游约150公里的一座河洲上，夹在两处急流之间，紧贴今尼日尔边境。这里是桑海诸王最古老的驻地：扎王朝10世纪初迁往上游加奥之前在此设朝，13世纪末马里夺取加奥后，旧王裔又退守下游。河洲扼住博尔古、豪萨兰通往北非商路上的停泊处。附近本提亚的墓地里，阿拉伯文墓碑从13世纪末一直立到桑海时代，廷巴克图编年史却仍把库基亚称作「异教的中心」。1444年，这片河岸属松尼王朝的桑海国家，村人种粮捕鱼，统治者是穆斯林，百姓大多仍守旧俗。

1464年即位、以加奥为根基建立帝国的松尼·阿里，幼年就在这片下游乡野由登迪籍母亲抚养长大，库基亚一带始终是其国家的河上腹地。1591年3月，萨阿德军队在通迪比歼灭桑海大军，末代阿斯基亚们经这些河洲顺河南逃，退往登迪和新都卢拉米。摩洛哥人以廷巴克图而非加奥为驻地，上游诸城随之凋敝，阿里班达河岸重归本地河酋与下游诸阿斯基亚之手，库基亚也缩成一座普通的河畔村落。

en:
Zarmaganda is the 'land of the Zarma', a sandy Sahel plateau between the Niger valley and the Azawagh, cut through by seasonal wadis; its chief market, Ouallam, lies north of the later site of Niamey. The Zarma are Songhai kin who claim descent from the Za, the ancient kings of Kukiya and Gao, and their traditions bring them southeast off the Niger bend onto this plateau in the Songhai centuries, in clans under chiefs titled zarmakoy. They herd cattle, sheep, goats and camels, farm the wadi bottoms and follow the Sunni Islam of the Maliki school; their herds and wool already fed the Sahel caravan trade. In 1444 the plateau was the southwestern march of the Songhai state.

Zarma horsemen stood in the thick of the dynasty change of 1493, when Askia Muhammad overthrew Sonni Baru with their help. The Za line never recovered a throne, and its descendants ruled only small Zarma chiefdoms. Through the next two centuries the Zarma pushed south into the Dallol Bosso and the country around Dosso, fighting Tuareg and Fulani for the bottom land; around 1750 the zarmakoy Aboubacar founded the Dosso state in the valley, while Ouallam stayed the head town of the northern Zarma.
zh:
扎尔马甘达意为「扎尔马人的土地」，是尼日尔河谷与阿扎瓦格之间的沙质萨赫勒高原，季节性旱谷穿行其间，首镇瓦拉姆在后来的尼亚美城址以北。扎尔马人与桑海人同源，自称库基亚和加奥古老扎王的后裔；按其口传，桑海时代各部在称「扎尔马科伊」的酋长率领下从尼日尔河曲东南迁上这片高原。他们牧养牛、绵羊、山羊和骆驼，在旱谷底部耕作，奉马立克学派的逊尼伊斯兰，畜群和羊毛早已供应萨赫勒商队。1444年，高原是桑海国家的西南边地。

1493年王朝更迭时，扎尔马骑兵身处其中：阿斯基亚·穆罕默德借他们之力推翻松尼·巴鲁。扎王朝旧裔再未能重登王位，后人只领有若干扎尔马小酋长国。此后两百年间，扎尔马人向南推进到达洛尔博索和多索一带，与图阿雷格人、富拉尼人争夺谷底田地；约1750年，扎尔马科伊阿布巴卡尔在谷中建立多索国，瓦拉姆则一直是北方扎尔马人的首镇。

en:
The Dallol country takes its name from its broad dry valleys, the dallols of the Songhai: they carry the wet-season rains south from the Azawagh and the Ader hills to the Niger and turn into watercourses and gardens where they meet the river. At that meeting point stands Say, the province's river town. Eastward runs the Dallol Maouri, home of the Hausa-speaking Maouri, whom their Zarma neighbours call Arawa. They kept to the old gods of this country, sacrificing to the Doguwa spirits under a priesthood seated at Bagaji; their small state of Arewa, ruled from the twin capitals Matankari and Lougou, was an animist holdout on the edge of the Muslim world. The flood-retreat fields grew grain for the river trade. In 1444 the valleys were the southeastern march of Songhai, with Gobir and Kebbi just beyond.

After Tondibi in 1591, Songhai refugees crowded the river towns, and the last Dendi askias kept a capital, Lulami, somewhere in the bush south of Say; its site has never been found. The Maouri held to their rites through the wars of the Songhai successor states, then faced a sterner test after 1804, when the Fula jihad built the Sokoto Caliphate and overran the Hausa kingdoms around them. Matankari and Lougou refused forced conversion and kept the Doguwa shrines with jihad states on every side.
zh:
达洛尔得名于宽阔的旱谷，桑海语称「达洛尔」：雨季时，阿扎瓦格和阿德尔山地的降水沿旱谷南流，在注入尼日尔河处化为水网与园田，本省河埠赛就坐落在汇流处。向东延伸的是达洛尔毛里谷地，住着讲豪萨语的毛里人，扎尔马邻族称他们为阿拉瓦人。他们守着这片地方的旧神，在巴加吉的祭司统辖下祭祀多瓜精灵；他们的小国阿雷瓦由马坦卡里和卢古两座都城分治，是穆斯林世界边缘的一处异教据点。退水田里出产谷物，供河上贸易。1444年，达洛尔诸谷是桑海的东南边地，再往外就是戈比尔和凯比。

1591年通迪比之战后，桑海遗民涌进沿河小镇，登迪末代阿斯基亚们把都城卢拉米设在赛以南的某处荒野，其址从未被找到。在桑海后继诸国的纷争中，毛里人一直守着旧礼；1804年后更严峻的考验到来，富拉尼圣战建起索科托哈里发国，踏平了周围的豪萨王国。马坦卡里和卢古拒绝被强迫改宗，在四周圣战国家环伺之下保住了多瓜神龛。

en:
The Azawagh is the basin of a river that ran dry after the last wet age, a flat plain of grass and thornscrub about 420,000 square kilometres in extent between the Adrar des Ifoghas, the Aïr and the Hoggar. Wells along the old wadi watered the herds that moved between the desert and the Sahel, and the Tuareg word azawagh means 'savannah'. Islam reached the western flank of the Aïr in the eighth century. In 1444 the camps of the Iwellemmeden Tuareg grazed these steppes as far south as the gates of Gao, and their clans heeded the kings of Songhai only when a royal army drew near enough to punish them.

Songhai's defeat at Tondibi in 1591 opened the country east of Gao to the confederation. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its western arm, the Kel Ataram based around Ménaka, harried the Moroccan Arma garrisons on the Niger and made the river towns pay tribute from the inland delta down to Say. The eastern arm, the Kel Dinnik of the Azawagh proper around Tchin-Tabaraden, filled the office of paramount chief, the amenokal, from the noble Kel Nan clan. By the later eighteenth century the two arms had drawn apart, with Ménaka remaining the seat of the Kel Ataram while the Kel Dinnik kept the Azawagh.
zh:
阿扎瓦格是一个古河水系干涸后留下的盆地，草原与灌丛平坦铺开，夹在伊福加斯山地、阿伊尔高原与霍加尔山之间，面积约四十二万平方公里。古干谷沿线的水井为往来于沙漠与萨赫勒之间的畜群供水；其名在塔马舍克语中意为「稀树草原」。8世纪时伊斯兰教已传到阿伊尔山西麓。1444年，伊韦勒梅登部图阿雷格人的营帐遍布这片干草原，向南一直扎到加奥城下；各部只有在桑海国王大军压境、足以兴师问罪时，才听其号令。

1591年桑海在通迪比战败，加奥以东之地对这个联盟门户洞开。17至18世纪间，其西支凯尔·阿塔拉姆人以梅纳卡一带为基地，不断袭扰尼日尔河上摩洛哥人的阿尔马戍兵，迫使沿岸城镇从内河三角洲到萨伊一路纳贡。东支是盘踞阿扎瓦格本土、以钦塔巴拉登一带为中心的凯尔·丁尼克人，联盟的最高首领阿梅诺卡尔按例出自显贵的凯尔·南氏族。到18世纪末，两支已经分道扬镳，梅纳卡一直是凯尔·阿塔拉姆人的驻地，凯尔·丁尼克人则保有阿扎瓦格。

en:
Azbin, also called Asben, is the Tuareg and Hausa name for the western Aïr: granite hills running out into the Azawagh plain, where the rains feed the salt pans. The oasis gardens of In-Gall grow dates and vegetables, and fifteen kilometres to the north the salt of Teguidda-n-Tessoumt is scraped from evaporated pans. West of them lie the ruins of Takedda at Azelik, a Sanhaja Berber kingdom whose copper mines made its name across the Sahel in the fourteenth century; Mansa Sakoura of Mali conquered it on campaign, and Ibn Battuta stopped there in 1353 on his way home from Mali. By 1444 the mines were spent, but the wells and provisions of In-Gall made it a fixed stage on the road between the Aïr towns and the Niger bend, ruled from Agadez by the Tuareg amenukal.

In the sixteenth century In-Gall was the easternmost post of Songhai power. The Hausa captain Muhammadu Kanta led the Songhai army that reduced Agadez around 1516, then quarrelled over his share of the spoils, revolted and made himself ruler of Kebbi, and his men held Agadez for a time. After Tondibi in 1591 the sultanate stood on its own again, and In-Gall kept supplying salt and dates to the caravans for Kano. In 1740 the Kel Owey confederation moved south out of the Algerian desert, destroyed Assodé and sacked Agadez, keeping the sultan as their client. Under them the Azalai salt caravans ran as before, and each year after the rains the Tuareg drove their herds down to the pans round In-Gall to graze on the salt pasture.
zh:
阿兹宾又作阿斯本，是图阿雷格人与豪萨人对阿伊尔西缘的称呼：花岗岩丘陵向西没入阿扎瓦格平原，雨水在洼地汇成盐滩。因加尔的绿洲菜园出产椰枣和蔬菜，北面15公里的泰吉达因泰苏姆靠晒蒸取盐。再往西是阿泽利克的塔凯达遗址，这个桑哈贾柏柏尔人的王国凭铜矿在14世纪闻名萨赫勒；马里曼萨萨库拉东征时将它征服，1353年伊本·白图泰从马里归国途中也曾在此停留。到1444年，铜矿已经采尽，但因加尔的水井和补给使它成为阿伊尔诸城通往尼日尔河河曲商路上的固定驿站，受阿加德兹的图阿雷格阿梅努卡尔管辖。

16世纪，因加尔是桑海势力最东边的据点。豪萨籍将领穆罕默杜·坎塔率领桑海军队在约1516年迫降阿加德兹，随后因分赏不均起兵反叛，自立为凯比之主，他的人马还一度占领阿加德兹。1591年通迪比之战后，苏丹国重新独立，因加尔继续向前往卡诺的商队供应盐和椰枣。1740年，凯尔·奥韦联盟从阿尔及利亚方向的沙漠南下，摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹，把苏丹留作傀儡。他们治下，跑盐和椰枣的阿扎莱驼队照旧往来；每年雨后，图阿雷格人仍把畜群赶到因加尔四周的盐滩牧放，让牲畜补充盐分。

en:
The Ader is the broken Sahelian margin where the granite ranges of the Aïr sink into the plains of Hausaland: bare rock outcrops, thorn scrub and valleys that carry water for a few weeks after the rains. Hausa villagers, many of them the animist Azna of Gobir stock, farmed the valley floors, while Kel Geres and Kel Itesen drum-groups drove their camels and cattle down from the massif each dry season to winter at its wells. Neither the amenukal at Agadez nor the Hausa king at Gobir did more than loosely claim the country. In 1444 its only real wealth was grass and water, shared between the villagers and the nomad camps that came down with the dry season.

Tahoua grew from two villages, Bilbis and Fakoua, and filled out only after the seventeenth century, when Fulani herders, Tuareg pushed south by the troubles in the Aïr and Azna families fleeing Muslim rulers settled about its wells. The Kel Owey made themselves masters of the massif around 1740 and forced the Kel Geres and Kel Itesen permanently into the Ader. When Usman dan Fodio proclaimed his jihad against the Hausa kings in 1804, the Tuareg of the valleys rode with Yunfa of Gobir, who had once been dan Fodio's own pupil. At Tsuntua that December they caught a jihadist army scattered in search of food and killed between two and three thousand of its men, two hundred of them said to be hafiz who knew the Quran by heart. The victory saved Gobir for only a few years: Alkalawa fell in 1808, the Sokoto Caliphate swallowed the kingdom, and Hausa and Tuareg refugees streamed through the Ader toward Maradi and Damagaram.
zh:
艾德尔是阿伊尔花岗岩山地倾入豪萨平原处的破碎萨赫勒边缘：裸岩孤丘、荆棘灌丛，雨后的谷地里只有几周流水。谷底耕田的是豪萨村民，其中多为戈比尔系、信奉旧神的阿兹纳人；凯尔·格雷斯、凯尔·伊特桑等部族联盟则每逢旱季赶着驼牛下山，到这里的水井边过冬。阿加德兹的阿梅努卡尔和戈比尔的豪萨君主对这片地方都只有松散的名义。1444年，这里真正的财富只有牧草和井水，由村民和旱季南下的游牧营帐分享。

塔瓦起于比尔比斯、法库瓦两村，17世纪后才扩展开来：富拉尼牧人、被阿伊尔动乱逼到南方的图阿雷格人、逃避穆斯林统治者的阿兹纳家族，陆续在井畔安家。约1740年凯尔·奥韦成为山地之主，把凯尔·格雷斯人和凯尔·伊特桑人永久压进艾德尔。1804年乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥向豪萨诸王发起圣战，谷地的图阿雷格人却随戈比尔君主云法出战，而云法本是丹·福迪奥的学生。同年12月的聪图阿之战，他们趁一支圣战军四散觅食发起攻击，斩杀两三千人，据说其中两百人是能背诵整部《古兰经》的哈菲兹。这场胜利只给戈比尔争得几年时间：1808年阿尔卡拉瓦陷落，索科托哈里发国吞并戈比尔，豪萨与图阿雷格难民成批穿过艾德尔，逃往马拉迪和达马加兰姆。

en:
The Aïr is a wedge of granite peaks rising from the central Sahara, whose high valleys catch enough rain to make an island of pasture, date gardens and seasonal fields in the desert. Tuareg kels have held the mountains since at least the twelfth century. Their oldest town, Assodé, was founded around 880 by the Isandalen clan and long served as the seat of the Tuareg chiefs, but it was overtaken by Agadez, which lay on the caravan road from the Hausa cities of Kano and Katsina to Ghat, Ghadames and Tripoli on the Mediterranean. Worn down by feuding, the clans chose a neutral outsider, Yunus, as their amenukal around 1405; by the middle of the fifteenth century the court was settled in Agadez, where Katsina merchants ran the first indigo dyeworks. In 1444 the two towns lived off the caravans that carried Hausa cloth and leather north and brought Bilma salt and Kaouar dates south to Kano.

A Songhai army from the Niger bend took Agadez around 1500, and the Hausa captain Kanta held the mountains first in Songhai's service and later, as lord of Kebbi, on his own account. The conquest gave the city its best-known landmark: the Grand Mosque was built in 1515 by Imam Bakhili, a scholar from Algeria, with a mud-brick minaret twenty-seven metres tall, which local tradition says he raised in a single night. Agadez then held perhaps 30,000 people and won back its independence late in the century with help from Kano and Katsina, but civil wars thinned the caravans. In 1740 the Kel Owey swept down from the north, destroyed Assodé and sacked Agadez, keeping the sultan as their client. Assodé was never rebuilt. Under their chief the anastafidet the Kel Owey ran the mountains and the azalai salt caravans, while Agadez shrank to a fraction of its old size.
zh:
阿伊尔是撒哈拉腹地拔起的楔形花岗岩山地，高谷截留雨水，在沙漠中托出一片由牧场、椰枣园和季节性农田组成的孤岛。至迟12世纪，图阿雷格各部已是群山之主。最古老的城镇阿索代约880年由伊桑达伦氏族建立，长期是图阿雷格酋长的驻地，后来却被阿加德兹超过：后者坐落在卡诺、卡齐纳等豪萨诸城通往加特、古达米斯和地中海沿岸的黎波里的商道上。约1405年，内争不休的各氏族推举身份中立的外人尤努斯为阿梅努卡尔；15世纪中叶苏丹廷已设在阿加德兹，卡齐纳商人在那里经营最早的靛蓝染坊。1444年，两座城镇靠商队为生：豪萨布匹和皮革北上，比尔马的盐和卡瓦尔绿洲的椰枣南运卡诺。

约1500年，尼日尔河河曲的桑海军队攻占阿加德兹；豪萨籍将领坎塔先替桑海镇守群山，后来自立为凯比之主，凭自己的力量据有其地。这场征服给这座城留下了最显眼的地标：大清真寺建于1515年，出自来自阿尔及利亚的学者伊玛目巴赫利之手，泥砖宣礼塔高27米，相传他在一夜之间便将塔建成。当时阿加德兹约有三万人口，16世纪后期靠卡诺和卡齐纳相助恢复独立，但内讧使商队日渐稀少。1740年，凯尔·奥韦自北方席卷而来，摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹，把苏丹留作傀儡。阿索代再未复兴。凯尔·奥韦在其首领阿纳斯塔菲德特统率下据有群山，经营阿扎莱盐队，阿加德兹则缩成旧日规模的零头。

en:
The Ténéré is the sand sea east of the Aïr, the Erg of Bilma running from the mountains toward the Kawar escarpment. Across it runs the Taghlamt, the salt-caravan road from Agadez to Bilma, whose sure stage is Agram, better known as Fachi: an oasis at the foot of a small rocky outcrop 160 kilometres west of Bilma. Wells, date gardens and salt pans are its whole living, traded to the passing caravans. Its Kanuri and Toubou people, who gave the place its older name of Agram, built a high ksar of banco salt blocks against Tuareg and Bedouin raiders. In 1444 the Tuareg Sultanate of Aïr held the mountains to the west, while Fachi also looked east to Kanem-Bornu and the Kawar oases.

The wars of the empires reached the desert road around 1516-17, when the Hausa captain Muhammadu Kanta led a Songhai army against Agadez and, denied his share of the plunder, broke away to found Kebbi; the oases passed between Songhai and Kebbi until Agadez went its own way after the Songhai collapse of 1591. Clan war emptied much of the Aïr in the seventeenth century, and in 1740 the Kel Owey confederation came south out of the desert, destroyed Assodé and sacked Agadez, reducing the sultanate to a vassal. Under them the Taghlamt caravans carried salt and dates south to Zinder and Kano, and hides, gold, ostrich feathers and captives north to Ghat and Ghadames.
zh:
泰内雷是阿伊尔高原以东的沙海，比尔马沙海从高原朝卡瓦尔崖壁延伸。塔格拉姆特盐队商路横穿沙海，从阿加德兹通往比尔马，路上最可靠的一站是阿格拉姆，即更广为人知的法奇：比尔马以西160公里处、一座小岩丘脚下的绿洲。水井、椰枣园和晒盐池就是它的全部生计，靠与过路商队交易维持。居民以卡努里人和图布人为主，阿格拉姆正是他们语言里的旧名；他们用盐坯土砖砌起一座高堡，防备图阿雷格人和贝都因人劫掠。1444年，西侧高原归图阿雷格人的阿伊尔苏丹国统治，法奇则同时朝向东边的加涅姆-博尔努和卡瓦尔绿洲。

约1516至1517年，帝国之间的战事打到了这条沙漠商路上：豪萨将领穆罕默杜·坎塔率桑海军队进攻阿加德兹，因分不到战利品而反叛，另建凯比；绿洲在桑海与凯比之间几度易手，直到1591年桑海崩溃，阿加德兹自立。17世纪的氏族战争使阿伊尔大半空虚，1740年，凯尔·奥韦联盟从北方沙漠南下，摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹，把苏丹国降为附庸。在他们治下，塔格拉姆特商队把盐和椰枣南运津德尔和卡诺，把兽皮、黄金、鸵鸟羽和人口北运加特和古达米斯。

en:
Itesan is named after the Kel Itesen, the strongest of the Tuareg drum-groups of the Aïr in the fourteenth century. Their country is the grassy steppe between the southern foot of the mountains and the Hausa kingdom of Gobir: wells and flats of thorn scrub that turn green for a few weeks after the rains and made winter grazing for herds that summered in the high valleys. When the Itesen leader failed to win recognition from the other groups, the feuding clans settled their quarrel around 1405 by creating the office of amenukal and choosing the neutral Yunus, after which the Kel Itesen became one of the chief pillars of the Sultanate of Agadez. In 1444 their herdsmen still made the yearly round from the wells of the Aïr to the valleys of Gobir, selling livestock and salt at Agadez and the Hausa markets.

The confederacy declined with the sultanate. Caravan troubles in the seventeenth century narrowed its living, and around 1740 the Kel Owey came down from the north, beat the older drum-groups and shut the Kel Itesen and Kel Geres out of the best mountain valleys, pushing them south and west. The Kel Itesen then made the Gobir borderlands their winter ground, which put them in the path of Usman dan Fodio's jihad. In December 1804 they rode with Yunfa of Gobir at Tsuntua, and accounts of the war name their horsemen as decisive both there and at Alwassa, the battles that checked the jihadists for the moment. The successes bought Gobir only four years; after Alkalawa fell in 1808 the Kel Itesen were left on the open steppe between the Sokoto Caliphate and the Kel Owey mountains, owing dues to both.
zh:
伊特桑得名于凯尔·伊特桑，14世纪阿伊尔图阿雷格诸鼓群中最强大的一支。其地是山脉南麓与豪萨人的戈比尔王国之间的草甸草原：散布水井和荆棘平地，雨后几周遍体泛青，是夏季在高山谷地放牧的畜群过冬的地方。伊特桑首领得不到其他各部承认，相互仇杀的氏族约1405年找到平息争端的办法：设立阿梅努卡尔之位，推举中立的尤努斯，凯尔·伊特桑随之成为阿加德兹苏丹国的主要支柱之一。1444年，其牧民仍年年从阿伊尔的水井转到戈比尔的谷地，在阿加德兹和豪萨集市上出售牲畜和盐。

这个联盟随苏丹国一同衰落。17世纪商路多艰，生计变窄；约1740年凯尔·奥韦自北方南下，击败旧有诸鼓群，把凯尔·伊特桑人和凯尔·格雷斯人逐出最丰美的山谷，压向南方和西方。凯尔·伊特桑人改以戈比尔边地为冬牧场，正挡在乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥圣战的路上。1804年12月，他们随戈比尔君主云法战于聪图阿；据记载，图阿雷格骑兵在聪图阿和此后的阿尔瓦萨两战中都是制胜的关键，圣战军一时被挡住。这些胜仗只给戈比尔争得四年时间；1808年阿尔卡拉瓦陷落后，凯尔·伊特桑人留在索科托哈里发国与凯尔·奥韦群山之间的开阔草原上，两头纳贡。

en:
Kawar is a string of palm oases at the foot of a north-south escarpment on the eastern edge of the Ténéré, where winds dropping over the cliffs bring groundwater close to the surface. Its chief settlements are Bilma and Dirkou, whose wells are the only sure water on the caravan road between Bornu and Fezzan; no camel train crossing between the Lake Chad country and the Mediterranean could avoid them. The oases draw their own wealth from the same ground: brine is run into evaporation pans for salt and natron, and date palms grow in gardens under the cliffs. Bilma was the birthplace, in the twelfth century, of the poet Abu Ishaq Ibrahim al-Kanemi. In 1444 Kanuri villagers worked the gardens and pans while Tuareg and Toubou nomads pastured camels around them and collected protection dues from passing caravans. Kanem-Bornu and the Tuareg confederacies facing Aïr both claimed the oases, and neither held a fixed desert border.

For most of the following centuries Kawar stayed inside the Bornu-to-Fezzan trading world, its salt and dates exchanged for grain, cloth and metal goods brought from the Lake Chad side. In the eighteenth century Tuareg confederations took the oases from Kanem-Bornu. After the Kel Owey destroyed Assodé and sacked Agadez in 1740, their great Taghlamt caravan travelled each year from Agadez through Fachi to Bilma, loaded salt and dates for Zinder and Kano, and carried hides, ostrich feathers and captives of the central Sudan north toward the markets of Ghat and Ghadames.
zh:
卡瓦尔是泰内雷东缘一道南北向崖壁下的成串椰枣绿洲；东风越过崖壁下沉，使地下水贴近地表。最大的两处聚落是比尔马和迪尔库，它们的水井是博尔努至费赞商道上唯一可靠的水源，往返乍得湖地区与地中海之间的骆驼商队无法绕开。绿洲自己的财富也出自这片土地：卤水被引入蒸发池晒制盐和泡碱，崖下园圃里种着椰枣。12世纪的诗人阿布·伊斯哈格·易卜拉欣·阿尔-卡奈米就出生在比尔马。1444年，在园圃和盐池里劳作的是卡努里村民，图阿雷格与图布牧人在周围放牧骆驼，向过往商队收取保护费；加涅姆-博尔努和面向阿伊尔的图阿雷格联盟都声称拥有这些绿洲，沙漠中没有固定边界。

此后几个世纪的大部分时间里，卡瓦尔处在博尔努—费赞贸易圈中，以盐和椰枣交换乍得湖地区运来的谷物、布匹和金属器。18世纪，图阿雷格联盟从加涅姆-博尔努手中夺取绿洲。1740年凯尔·奥韦人摧毁阿索代、洗劫阿加德兹后，他们的塔格拉姆特大商队每年从阿加德兹出发，经法奇抵达比尔马，把盐和椰枣运往津德尔和卡诺，再把兽皮、鸵鸟羽和掳来的人口北运向加特与古达米斯的市场。

en:
Kebbi fills the lower Rima valley where the river bends west to meet the Niger, floodplain farms and fishing waters on the western edge of Hausaland. In 1444 there was no Kingdom of Kebbi, no walled Surame, no fortress at Birnin Kebbi: clan chiefs ruled the lower valley, Hausa immigrants had begun to settle it, and under Sunni Ali the land had just passed to Songhai. Tradition counts the Kebbawa among the Banza Bakwai, the seven 'later' Hausa states, and Muhammadu Kanta himself was a soldier from Kuyambana in Katsina who came to rule Songhai's province of Kebbi by force of arms.

In 1516–17 Kanta Kuta, lord of Leka, rose against the dendi fari after being cheated of his share of the booty from a campaign against Air, and a Songhai army sent in 1517–18 failed to put him down. Muhammad Kanta, ruling from about 1523, made Kebbi a power in the central Sudan. He ringed his capital at Surame with massive ramparts and made a fortress of Birnin Kebbi, then scattered the army of Askia Muhammad Bunkan so thoroughly that the Askia barely escaped with his life and no Askia ever marched against Kebbi again. Kanta took Agadez from Songhai, overran Yauri and Nupe, routed a Bornu invasion, and drew tribute from much of Hausaland. He died in 1556; his son Ahmadu let the tribute lapse, Agadez was lost with Kano and Katsina backing a rival claimant, and by 1600 Kebbi was a minor kingdom. Early in the 18th century its tributaries Gobir and Zamfara revolted together and carried off King Muhammadu dan Giwa. In 1808 Abdullahi dan Fodio, Usman's brother, took Birnin Kebbi and founded the Gwandu emirate under Sokoto, yet the Kebbawa never fully submitted: the deposed Muhammadu Hodi, and then Karari, kept fighting from the Zamfara valley and the new stronghold of Argungu.
zh:
克比地处里马河下游河谷，河水西折注入尼日尔河，是豪萨兰西缘一片河滩农田与渔场交错的地方。1444年还没有克比王国，没有筑城的苏拉梅，比尔宁克比也还不是要塞：里马河下游由氏族首领治理，豪萨移民刚开始迁入，在孙尼·阿里治下，这片土地刚被桑海取得。传说把克比人列入「班扎巴夸伊」，即七个「后来的」豪萨邦国；穆罕默德·坎塔本人是来自卡齐纳库扬巴纳的军人，凭战功成了桑海克比省的实际统治者。

1516至1517年，莱卡之主坎塔·库塔因被登迪法里克扣征讨阿伊尔的战利品份额而起兵，桑海1517至1518年派来讨伐的军队也没能压服他。约1523年起执政的穆罕默德·坎塔把克比变成中苏丹的一方强国：他给都城苏拉梅筑起厚重高大的城墙，把比尔宁克比修成要塞，将阿斯基亚·穆罕默德·本坎的军队杀得四散，阿斯基亚本人仅以身免，此后再没有哪位阿斯基亚敢来征讨。他从桑海手中夺取阿加德兹，征服亚武里和努佩，击溃博尔努的入侵，向豪萨兰大部索取贡赋。坎塔1556年去世，其子艾哈迈杜放任贡赋中断，卡诺和卡齐纳又支持觊觎者夺走阿加德兹，到1600年克比已沦为小邦。18世纪初，属国戈比尔与扎姆法拉联手反叛，掳走克比王穆罕默杜·丹·吉瓦。1808年，奥斯曼之弟阿卜杜拉希·丹·福迪奥攻占比尔宁克比，在索科托之下建立关杜埃米尔国，但克比人始终没有完全屈服：被废的穆罕默杜·霍迪、继之而起的卡拉里先后以扎姆法拉河谷和新据点阿尔贡古为基地坚持作战。

en:
Daura is one of the seven true Hausa states, and Hausa tradition calls it the spiritual home of the Hausa people. Their founding legend says that Bayajidda, a stranger who had crossed the Sahara from the east, reached the town to find its well held by a great serpent named Sarki, which let no one draw water; he killed it, and Queen Daurama married him. The rulers of the seven Hausa states, the story runs, all descend from that marriage, and Daura's Kusugu well is named as the spot where Sarki died. Daura was also, with Katsina, one of the two great market kingships of Hausaland. Its merchants moved salt, henna and dyed cloth, leather and kola nuts between Kanem-Bornu, the Niger bend and the Hausa cities. In 1444 it was a Sunni Hausa town in the commercial world of nearby Katsina, and Bornu's western reach extended to its caravan roads.

When Bornu pressed westward in the fifteenth century, tribute from the Hausa rulers passed along Daura's roads, but the town kept its markets and its place as a seat of Islamic learning until the Fulani War. In 1805 Malam Ishaku, a follower of Usman dan Fodio, took Daura after the Hausa ruler Abdullahi, also called Gwari Abdu, had withdrawn with his people. Ishaku became its first Fulani emir and brought the town into the Sokoto order. The old Hausa dynasty withdrew to Murya, Yekuwa and other nearby settlements and kept a rival court, so that early in the nineteenth century an emir's Daura and a Hausa Daura lay a short distance apart.
zh:
达乌拉是豪萨七邦之一，豪萨人把它当作整个民族的精神祖地。相传巴亚吉达从东方穿越撒哈拉来到这里时，城中的水井被一条名叫「萨尔基」（意为「王」）的巨蛇盘踞，谁也取不到水；他杀死巨蛇，女王道拉玛因此嫁给他。豪萨人的说法是，七个豪萨邦的统治者都出自这桩婚姻，城中的库苏古井就是斩蛇的地方。达乌拉还与卡齐纳并称豪萨地区两大市场政权，商人把食盐、散沫花、染色布匹、皮革和柯拉果在卡涅姆—博尔努、尼日尔河湾与豪萨诸城之间转运。1444年，它是邻近卡齐纳商业圈里的一座逊尼派豪萨城镇，博尔努向西的势力也延伸到它的商路上。

15世纪博尔努向西扩张时，豪萨统治者的贡赋取道达乌拉的道路，而直到富拉尼战争前，这座城镇的市集和伊斯兰学务都还保持着。1805年，奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的追随者马拉姆·伊沙库攻占达乌拉，豪萨统治者阿卜杜拉（又称瓜里·阿卜杜）此前已带着民众撤离。伊沙库成为第一位富拉尼埃米尔，把城镇纳入索科托的秩序。旧豪萨王朝退到穆里亚、耶库瓦等邻近聚落，另立王廷；到19世纪初，埃米尔的达乌拉和豪萨人的达乌拉相隔不远并存着。

en:
Biram, also called Garun Gabas, was the easternmost of the seven true Hausa states, the Hausa Bakwai of the Bayajidda legend. In that story the hero comes to Daura from Baghdad by way of Borno, kills the snake that keeps the townspeople from their well and marries Queen Daurama; her son Bawo fathers six sons who rule Daura, Katsina, Zazzau, Gobir, Kano and Rano, while the seventh city, Biram, goes to the son of his Borno princess, which ties the easternmost state by kinship to the Kanem court. Its towns stood on the Hadejia River along the caravan track between Kano and Kanem-Bornu, where Kanuri merchants and, from the fifteenth century, Fulbe herders lived among Hausa farmers and craftsmen. In 1444 Biram was a small Habe chiefdom in Kano's shadow, and on one reading of the sources already a tribute-payer to Bornu; Islam belonged mostly to the traders' quarters, and the villages kept their old rites.

In the following centuries Hadejia became the chief town of the district. Usman dan Fodio's Fulani jihad reached it in 1808, when Hadejia was made a Fulani emirate; by 1810 the Habe rulers of the seven states had all been overcome and Biram's lands entered the Sokoto Caliphate.
zh:
比拉姆又称加伦加巴斯，是豪萨七邦中位置最东的一个，七邦之名来自巴亚吉达传说。相传英雄巴亚吉达从巴格达经博尔努来到达乌拉，杀死霸占水井的巨蛇，娶了道拉玛女王；道拉玛所生的巴沃有六个儿子，分领达乌拉、卡齐纳、扎造、戈比尔、卡诺和兰诺六邦，第七邦比拉姆则归他与博尔努公主所生的儿子统领，传说便把这个最东的城邦同卡涅姆宫廷连在一起。它的城镇位于哈代贾河畔，正当卡诺通往卡涅姆—博尔努的商队道上，卡努里商人与15世纪起进入的富拉尼牧人，同豪萨农夫和工匠混居。1444年，比拉姆是卡诺威势之下的小型哈贝酋长邦，按一种史料解读已在向博尔努纳贡；伊斯兰教主要行于商人区，乡间仍守旧礼。

此后几个世纪，哈代贾成为这一带的首镇。1808年，奥斯曼·丹·福迪奥的富拉尼圣战波及此地，哈代贾被立为富拉尼埃米尔国；到1810年，七邦的哈贝统治者全部败亡，比拉姆之地并入索科托哈里发国。

en:
Rano lies in the open farm country south of Kano, one of the seven true Hausa states. Hausa tradition gives each of the seven states its own trade, and Rano's was cloth: with Kano it held the cotton fields and indigo pits of Hausaland, and the two rulers were called the 'kings of indigo'. Local tradition names Zamna Kogi, a descendant of Bayajidda, as founder, and remembers an early Kwararrafawa line before the Habe took over around 1000. Kano's Yaji I, in whose reign Islam came to Kano, conquered Rano for two years between 1349 and 1385; the town kept its chiefs afterwards but never recovered its sovereignty. In 1444 its Hausa weavers, dyers and traders, by then Muslim, lived under Habe rulers inside Kano's political and commercial orbit.

Bales of Rano indigo cloth, with leather, kola nuts and henna, went out with the Hausa caravans for the next three and a half centuries. The Fulani jihad broke the old order in the Kano region: Hausa tradition dates Rano's change of dynasty to 1819, when a Fulani line replaced the Habe chiefs and their district entered the Kano emirate within the Sokoto Caliphate.
zh:
兰诺位于卡诺以南开阔的农耕地带，是豪萨七真邦之一。豪萨传统给七邦各分一行生计，兰诺的一行是织布：它和卡诺据有豪萨地区的棉田和靛蓝染坑，两地统治者因此并称「靛蓝之王」。当地传说称建城者是巴亚吉达的后裔扎姆纳·科吉，约1000年哈贝人掌权之前，这里还经历过早期的夸拉拉法王世系。伊斯兰教在卡诺王亚吉一世在位时传入卡诺；1349年至1385年间，他攻占兰诺两年，兰诺后来保住了自己的首领，却再没恢复主权。1444年，城里已改信伊斯兰教的豪萨织工、染匠和商人处在哈贝统治者治下，政治与商业都听卡诺号令。

此后三个半世纪，成捆的兰诺靛蓝布连同皮革、柯拉果和散沫花随豪萨商队外运。富拉尼圣战打破了卡诺地区的旧秩序：按豪萨传统，兰诺在1819年改朝换代，富拉尼世系取代哈贝首领，其地并入索科托哈里发国治下的卡诺埃米尔国。

en:
Muniyo, also spelled Mounio, is the dry Sahelian country below the Koutous massif in south-eastern Niger, west of the Bornu heartland. Tuareg from the Koutous hills raided down onto the plain, whose villages looked west toward the Hausa trading lands; Birni N'Gafata and, later, Bouné were the chief places. In 1444 there was no province of Muniyo, only a scatter of farming villages on the western approaches of Kanem-Bornu, with no walled capital and no dynasty of their own.

The land entered Bornu in the late sixteenth century, when the mai Idris Alooma pushed the empire west. Early in the seventeenth century Tuareg from Koutous sacked Birni N'Gafata, and its chief Dagalama called on the mai for help. He sent Saémi, a Mandara ruler who lived in exile at his court. Saémi beat off the raiders and kept the village for himself, fortifying it as the seat of a newly unified Muniyo, while Dagalama had to content himself with a smaller district to the west. Around 1700 the province ran from the Koutous to the shore of Lake Chad, Machina and Guidimouni. Saémi's son and grandson ruled only briefly, but his great-grandson Kiari held power for forty-four years. After Kiari's death his kinsmen carved the province into small domains, until Ibrahim of Bouné won most of it back, moved the seat to Bouné, and died in a failed attack on Machina.
zh:
梅诺约（又拼作穆尼约）是今尼日尔东南部库图山以南一片干旱的萨赫勒土地，位于博尔努核心地带以西。库图山的图阿雷格人常下山袭掠，平原上的村落向西对着豪萨商路；比尔尼·恩加法塔和后来的布内是这一带的主要居地。1444年还没有梅诺约省这个建制，只有卡奈姆-博尔努西通路上一串分散的农耕村落，既无城墙围护的都城，也没有自己的王朝。

16世纪末，伊德里斯·阿劳马担任马伊时把帝国边界向西推进，梅诺约被纳入博尔努。17世纪初，库图山的图阿雷格人洗劫比尔尼·恩加法塔，村长达加拉马向马伊求援。马伊派来流亡在宫廷中的曼达拉统治者萨埃米。萨埃米击退袭掠者后把村子据为己有，筑墙固守，作为新统一的梅诺约的统治中心，达加拉马只得到西边一块较小的辖区。约1700年，这个省北起库图山，东抵乍得湖岸，南接马希纳，西达吉迪穆尼。萨埃米的儿子和孙子在位时间都不长，曾孙基亚里却掌权四十四年。基亚里死后，亲族把全省割成许多小领地，直到布内的易卜拉欣重新夺回大部，把治所迁到布内，最后在攻打马希纳失败时死去。

en:
Bedde, also spelled Bade, is the floodplain country of the lower Yobe and Hadejia rivers, around Tagali and later Gashua. The Bade speak a West-Chadic language close to Ngizim and reckon themselves settled here from about 1300; their own traditions derive the clans from four brothers who separated at Dadigar. They farmed the seasonally flooded land and fished the two rivers. In 1444 the Bade lived in autonomous clans under local chiefs called dugums, on the western fringe of the Muslim Bornu state, with no single ruler and no town of any size.

By 1750 the clans had their own dugum leaders, and Dugum Bugia of the Gidgid clan is remembered as the founder of the Bedde state about 1759. The Bedde polity was forged in the shadow of the Fulani jihad: Kanuri pressure and Fulani raids drove Lawan Babuje of Gidgid to bring the Dumbari, Dagilwa, Tagali and the other clan chiefs into one confederation. Raiders struck Bedde in 1808, while it still owed obedience to Bornu. In 1818 Lawan threw off that obedience, walled Gorgorum as his capital, and ruled an independent Bedde from the Yobe marshes on the edge of the Sokoto wars.
zh:
贝代（又拼作巴德）是约贝河下游与哈代贾河之间的洪泛平原，在塔加利和后来的加舒阿一带。贝代人讲属西乍得语支的贝代语，和恩吉津语相近，自认约1300年已定居于此；他们自己的传说把各氏族溯到在达迪加尔分手的四兄弟。他们耕种随水涨落的土地，也在两河捕鱼。1444年，贝代人仍以氏族自治，由称杜古姆的本地首领统领，处在伊斯兰国家博尔努的西缘，没有统一的首领，也没有像样的城镇。

到1750年，各氏族已有自己的杜古姆首领，吉德-吉德氏族的杜古姆·布贾被认为约在1759年建立贝代政权。贝代政权是在富拉尼圣战的阴影下逼出来的：卡努里人的压力和富拉尼人的袭掠，迫使吉德-吉德的拉万·巴布杰把敦巴里、达吉尔瓦、塔加利等氏族首领联合成一个同盟。1808年袭掠者打来时，贝代仍向博尔努称臣。1818年，拉万不再臣服，在戈戈拉姆筑墙为都，从约贝河沼泽地带统治独立的贝代，置身索科托战争的边缘。

en:
Manga is the dry Kanuri grassland that runs east from Damagaram and Zinder toward the Lake Chad approaches, between the Bornu farmlands and the desert roads to Kawar. Its people speak Manga Kanuri, a caravan trade tongue of the Zinder and Diffa country, with its Dagara dialect around Diffa. Pastures and wells joined Hausa traders to Tubu and Tuareg nomads, and the frontier lived on natron, millet and cattle. In 1444, with the Sayfawa mai withdrawn from Kanem to Ngazargamu, Manga guarded the north-western roads of Bornu; it had no single capital.

The wars of Idris Alooma in the later sixteenth century brought the Tuareg of Aïr and the Tubu of Bilma under Bornu and put the Sahara salt roads in its hand. Manga and Tubu diggers worked the western natron deposits, and mixed frontier camps such as Nguru and Mashina supplied soldiers and caravans. Early in the seventeenth century the mai set a galadima over Nguru to hold the western edge and used Muniyo and Machina as buffers against the Tuareg. In 1736 Kanuri aristocrats built the walled Birni quarter at Zinder and made the town the seat of Damagaram, nominally under Bornu; Zinder pulled the caravan trade south toward Kano and east toward Bornu. When Sokoto forces sacked Ngazargamu in 1808, the Manga pastures became Bornu's recruiting ground and first line of defence.
zh:
芒加是一片干旱的卡努里草原，从达马加姆和津德尔向东伸向乍得湖方向，夹在博尔努农耕地带与通往卡瓦尔的沙漠道路之间。这里的人讲芒加卡努里语，它是津德尔、迪法一带商队通用的贸易语言，迪法附近通行达加拉方言。牧场和水井把豪萨商人与图布、图阿雷格游牧民连到一起，这片边地靠碱盐、小米和牲畜为生。1444年，赛义夫王朝的马伊已从卡奈姆退到恩加扎尔加穆，芒加为博尔努看守西北方的道路，本身没有统一的都城。

16世纪后期，伊德里斯·阿劳马征战，把阿伊尔的图阿雷格人和比尔马的图布人收入博尔努，撒哈拉盐路也落入其手。芒加人和图布人开采西部的碱盐矿，恩古鲁、马希纳等混居据点为军队和商队提供补给。17世纪初，马伊在恩古鲁设置加拉迪马镇守西疆，并以梅诺约、马希纳作为抵御图阿雷格人的缓冲。1736年，卡努里贵族在津德尔筑起有城墙的比尔尼城区，把该城作为达马加姆的治所，名义上仍臣服博尔努；津德尔把商队贸易向南引向卡诺、向东引向博尔努。1808年索科托军队洗劫恩加扎尔加穆后，芒加牧场成了博尔努的募兵地和第一道防线。

en:
The Marghi country lies between the Mandara Mountains and the Adamawa highlands, in grain-growing valleys around Uba and Madagali. Marghi-speaking clans, called fal, drifted from the Mandara highlands in scattered movements; some built their villages within Bornu while others pushed south into Adamawa. They kept their own Chadic speech and their ancestral rites, though Kanuri power and trade reached up the valleys from Bornu. In 1444 their villages stood on Kanem-Bornu's southern march, and Fulbe herders had already begun to camp on the plateau pastures, paying the farmers in milk, cattle and hides for grain.

That border life ended in 1809, when Modibo Adama carried the jihad of Usman dan Fodio into Fombina, the lands south of Bornu, and fighting spread through Uba and Bazza. Marghi villages found themselves on a contested frontier between Bornu and the new Adamawa emirate, whose lamidos answered to Sokoto; raids carried off cattle and captives, and tribute went to whichever side could enforce it.
zh:
马尔格希地处曼达拉山脉与阿达马瓦高地之间，乌巴和马达加利一带宜粮的谷地是其核心。讲马尔吉语的氏族（当地称fal）分批从曼达拉高地迁来，一部分在博尔努境内建村定居，另一部分继续南入阿达马瓦。他们保留着自己的乍得语和祖灵仪式，卡努里人的势力和商路则沿谷地从博尔努延伸过来。1444年，这些村落处在卡奈姆-博尔努的南部边地，富拉尼牧民已开始在高原牧场扎营，用乳品、牛只和皮革向农民换取谷物。

这种边地生活在1809年终结：莫迪博·阿达马瓦把乌斯曼·丹·福迪奥的圣战带入丰比纳，即博尔努以南的土地，战火蔓延到乌巴和巴扎。马尔格希人的村落就此处在博尔努与新兴阿达马瓦酋长国的拉锯前线，后者的拉米多向索科托称臣；无论哪一方得势，村庄都要缴纳贡赋，牛群和人口还常被掳走。

en:
The Logone rises in the Mandara Mountains and runs north through wide floodplains to Lake Chad, giving this country both its name and its chief town. In 1444 its banks were lined with Kotoko towns, heirs of the old Sao civilization, each ringed with earthen ramparts and ruled by its own mra. Millet farmers, fishermen and ironworkers traded iron brought down from Mandara and ivory gathered in the south, and canoes carried fish and goods along the river. Islam had reached the courts of the river towns through Kanem, but most people still made offerings to the spirits of the water.

When Idris Alooma led Bornu's musketeers against the Kotoko city-states at the end of the sixteenth century, the northern towns submitted, while the southern ones closed ranks behind the ruler of Logone and stood clear of the wars between Bornu and Bagirmi. Tradition dates the walled town of Logone-Birni, the 'fort of Logone', to about 1700, when Prince Bruha is said to have founded it: its wide main street ran between uniform courtyard houses with strong doors hasped with iron. Logone-Birni has also been put forward, though the claim is disputed, as the birthplace of Abram Gannibal, a boy carried off to the Ottoman court and then to Russia who became a tsarist general and the great-grandfather of Alexander Pushkin. Through the eighteenth century, as Bornu tightened its hold on the northern cities and Fulani armies rose in the west, Logone kept its independence.
zh:
洛贡河发源于曼达拉山脉，穿过广阔的洪泛平原北流注入乍得湖，这片地方因河及其河畔重镇得名。1444年，河两岸分布着科托科人的城镇，它们是古老萨奥文明的继承者，每座都环以土墙，由一位姆拉统治。种小米的农夫、渔民和铁匠在此交易从曼达拉贩来的铁和南方采集的象牙，独木舟载着鱼获和货物往来河上。伊斯兰教已随加奈姆的影响传到河畔诸城的宫廷，多数人仍向水中的神灵献祭。

16世纪末，伊德里斯·阿卢马率博尔努的火绳枪手征伐科托科城邦，北方诸城臣服，南方诸城则拥戴洛贡的统治者抱团自保，不卷入博尔努与巴吉尔米之间的战争。相传设防城洛贡-比尔尼（意为「洛贡堡」）建于约1700年，为布鲁哈王子所建：宽阔的大街两侧是整齐的带院宅屋，屋门坚固、以铁扣加固。也有人考证洛贡-比尔尼是阿布拉姆·加尼巴尔的出生地，此说仍有争议：他幼年被掳往奥斯曼宫廷，后又到了俄国，成为沙皇麾下的将军，是亚历山大·普希金的外曾祖父。整个18世纪，博尔努对北方诸城的控制日益收紧，富拉尼大军在西方崛起，洛贡却始终保持独立。

en:
South of Lake Chad the Logone and Chari spill across green floodlands, the country of the Kotoko, a Chadic people who hold themselves descendants of the Sao. By 1444 some twenty walled city-states stood on the riverbanks and muddy islands, among them Makari, Afade, Goulfey, Kousséri and Houlouf, each ruled by a king titled mra and served by tribute collectors and captains of horsemen and archers. Houlouf filled sixteen hectares inside its ramparts, its six quarters entered through gates named after past rulers, with a royal palace and a royal cemetery. At Goulfey rose a twelve-metre tower that served both defence and ritual. Iron from Mandara passed through the markets, and the northern towns had lain in Kanem's sphere since the days of the old empire; Islam was spreading from the courts while the common people kept the cults of the water.

The mais of Bornu campaigned against the Kotoko cities through the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries. Soon after 1570 Idris Alooma sent in musketeers drilled in the Turkish fashion, captured the king of Kousséri and bound the northern towns to Bornu by treaty. Two leagues came out of these wars: a northern one led from Makari under Bornu's suzerainty, and a southern one led from Logone that kept its freedom, and Islam followed Bornu's influence from the courts into the villages. In 1808 Fulani raiders from the jihad of Usman dan Fodio reached the Logone, but Muhammad al-Amin al-Kanemi broke them in the country of Ngala and shielded the river towns, which stayed Bornu's southern flank.
zh:
乍得湖以南，洛贡河与沙里河漫成翠绿的洪泛平原，这里是科托科人的土地。科托科人操乍得语族语言，自认是萨奥人的后裔。到1444年，河畔与泥岛上已建起约二十座带城墙的城邦，马卡里、阿法德、古勒费、库塞里、胡卢夫等都在其中，各由一位称姆拉的王统治，王下设征税官和统领骑兵、弓箭手的将领。胡卢夫城垣之内占地十六公顷，分为六个坊区，各门以历代统治者命名，还有王宫和王陵。古勒费矗立着一座十二米高的塔楼，兼用于防御和祭祀。曼达拉贩来的铁在这些市场转售；北方诸城自旧帝国时代起便处在加奈姆的势力范围内，伊斯兰教正从宫廷向外传播，平民仍守着河水崇拜。

15至16世纪，博尔努历代马伊不断征伐科托科诸城。1570年后不久，伊德里斯·阿卢马派出按土耳其方式操练的火绳枪手，俘获库塞里之王，以条约使北方诸城臣服博尔努。战乱中形成两个同盟：以马卡里为首的北盟奉博尔努为宗主，以洛贡为首的南盟保持自由；伊斯兰教也随博尔努的影响从宫廷传入村庄。1808年，奥斯曼·登·福迪奥发动圣战，富拉尼袭掠者打到洛贡河，穆罕默德·阿尔-阿明·阿尔-卡奈米在恩加拉一带将其击溃，护住河畔诸城，它们始终是博尔努的南翼。

en:
Some three hundred kilometres east of Lake Chad the shallow Lake Fitri spreads across the Sahel, ringed by the villages of the Lisi: the Bilala, Kuka and Medogo, Nilo-Saharan farmers and herdsmen who sow millet and keep cattle on the lake's seasonal pastures. The Bilala were the people who undid old Kanem. In the fourteenth century they rose against its Sayfawa dynasty, killed one mai after another and took the capital Njimi around 1380; the surviving mai Umar carried the dynasty across the lake and built it anew in Bornu. The Muslim kingdom the Bilala set up in Kanem grew rich on the trans-Saharan caravan roads. In 1444 its horsemen held both Kanem and the Fitri country and still matched the Sayfawa west of the lake.

Early in the sixteenth century mai Idris Katakarmabe of Bornu defeated the Bilala at Garni Kiyala and won back Kanem, then sealed the peace with a dynastic marriage and left them governing the country as his vassals. Around 1530 their chief Djil Essa Tubo led them back to Lake Fitri and founded the sultanate of Yao. In those same years Leo Africanus had heard the Bilala country described as richer than Bornu. For more than two centuries the sultans of Yao held the Fitri shore, its millet fields, cattle herds and fishing grounds, on the roads between Kanem and Wadai. At the end of the eighteenth century the Baguirmians killed sultan Djourab el-Kabir in fighting at Kabara, and Yao had to accept Wadai's suzerainty.
zh:
乍得湖以东约三百公里，菲特里湖的浅水面铺展在萨赫勒上，湖岸环居着利斯人：比拉拉人、库卡人和梅多戈人操尼罗-撒哈拉语，种植小米、牧养牛群，随湖周季节性牧场迁居。拖垮旧加奈姆的正是比拉拉人。14世纪他们起兵反抗赛法瓦王朝，接连击杀马伊，约1380年攻占都城恩吉米；幸存的马伊奥马尔携王朝渡湖西走，在博尔努重建国家。比拉拉人在加奈姆建立的穆斯林王国靠跨撒哈拉商道致富。1444年，其骑兵据有加奈姆和菲特里之地，仍可与湖西的赛法瓦王朝匹敌。

16世纪初，博尔努马伊伊德里斯·卡塔卡尔马贝在加尼-基亚拉击败比拉拉人、收复加奈姆，随后以一桩王室联姻缔和，仍让他们作为封臣统治该地。约1530年，首领吉勒·埃萨·图博率部回到菲特里湖畔，建立亚奥苏丹国。就在那些年，利奥·阿非利加努斯曾听说比拉拉人的国家比博尔努更富庶。此后两个多世纪，亚奥历代苏丹据守湖岸的小米田、牛群和渔场，地当加奈姆与瓦达伊之间的往来道路。18世纪末，巴吉尔米人在卡巴拉一战中杀死苏丹朱拉卜·卡比尔，亚奥只得承认瓦达伊的宗主权。

en:
Ondo is rolling forest country between Ife and the Benin empire, where the Yoruba and Edo worlds meet. Its farmers grew yams and cotton and wove aso oke, the prestigious strip-cloth worn by Yoruba elites, and the roads linking the Yoruba interior with the Bight of Benin passed through its markets. Benin's power ran deep into these marches in the fifteenth century, and in 1444 the country answered to the Oba, with no dynasty of its own.

The kingdom was founded around 1510 by Pupupu, traditionally one of the twin daughters of Alaafin Oluaso of Oyo. Twins were then held to be an abomination, and the tradition sends her into exile with her two infants, south through the forests to the place that became Ondo, where she ruled as the first Osemawe. The title is popularly derived from ese omo re, 'these children are an abomination', the cry said to have greeted the twins' birth. Her son Airo built the royal palace, and his sons founded the houses from which later Osemawes were chosen. Under them Ondo grew into the chief market town on the road between the Yoruba interior and the coast, its cotton cloth and farm produce feeding the trade of the Benin bight.
zh:
翁多是伊费与贝宁帝国之间一片起伏的林地，约鲁巴与埃多两个世界在这里相接。农人种植甘薯和棉花，织作约鲁巴上层珍重的条带布「阿索奥凯」；连接约鲁巴内陆与贝宁湾的道路经过这里的市集。15世纪时贝宁的势力深入这片边地，1444年的翁多臣属于贝宁的奥巴，还没有自己的王朝。

翁多王国约建于1510年，开国君主普普普相传是奥约阿拉芬奥卢阿索的双胞胎女儿之一。当时双生被视为不祥，传说她带着两个孩子被逐南行，穿过森林来到后来的翁多城，成为第一位以「奥塞马韦」为号的统治者。这个王号据说来自双胞胎降生时的惊呼「埃塞奥莫雷」，意为「这两个孩子是不祥之物」。她的儿子艾罗修建了王宫，艾罗的儿子们分别创立王室支系，此后的奥塞马韦便从各支系中选出。在他们治下，翁多发展为约鲁巴内陆通往沿海道路上的首要集镇，棉布与农产品供应着贝宁湾的贸易。

en:
Ijebu lies behind the creeks and lagoons of the coast east of Lagos, a Yoruba kingdom raised above the waterways on forest farmland. Its dynasty is credited to Obanta, a prince who came from Ile-Ife, and the capital at Ijebu-Ode was ringed by Sungbo's Eredo, walls and ditches raised from around 800, whose builders moved some 3.5 million cubic metres of earth, more than went into the Great Pyramid at Giza. The rampart bound scattered forest communities under one ruler; tradition names it for Bilikisu Sungbo, a wealthy widow of the court whom local legend identifies with the Queen of Sheba, and her shrine at Oke-Eiri was a place of pilgrimage. The Awujale reigned at Ijebu-Ode, checked by the Osugbo, a council of titled elders led by the Oliwa, the second man in the kingdom, and Edo influence from Benin ran through the court. In 1444 Ijebu stood within the Benin sphere and held the road from the interior to the lagoon.

Portuguese ships already knew the ditch-girt city: an account of 1508 calls it Geebu, 'a great city surrounded by a great ditch', and names its ruler the Agusale, and in 1620 a trader called Xabu 'a kingdom small but very warlike'. In the eighteenth century the Awujale's men closed their roads to outsiders and made every load between the Lagos lagoon and the interior pass through Ijebu merchants. The monopoly turned Ijebu-Ode into one of the richest markets on the Slave Coast; the same barriers wore at the patience of European traders.
zh:
伊杰布位于拉各斯以东沿海的河汊与潟湖内侧，是一座立于水乡林地上的约鲁巴王国。相传王朝由来自伊费的王公奥班塔开创；都城伊杰布奥德被「松博埃雷多」环绕，这道长墙深沟约自公元800年起兴筑，搬动的沙土约有350万立方米，比吉萨大金字塔的土石方还多，把分散的林中聚落统一在一位统治者治下。相传工事为纪念宫廷中的富有寡妇比利基苏·松博而建，当地传说把她指认为示巴女王，她在奥凯埃里的神龛是朝圣之地。奥乌贾莱在伊杰布奥德治国，由显贵长老组成的奥苏格博会议制衡，会议之首奥利瓦是国中第二号人物；来自贝宁的埃多影响也深入宫廷。1444年的伊杰布处在贝宁势力范围内，扼守内陆通往潟湖的道路。

沿海贸易的葡萄牙船只早知道这座深沟环绕的城市：1508年的一份记载把它记作吉布，称其为「被一道大沟环绕的大城」，君主称阿古萨莱；1620年又有商人把哈布称作「很小但十分好战的王国」。18世纪，奥乌贾莱的人对外人封锁道路，规定拉各斯潟湖与内陆之间的每件货物都须经伊杰布商人转手。垄断使伊杰布奥德成为奴隶海岸最富庶的市集之一；同样的层层限制，也让欧洲商人越来越难以忍受。

en:
Ketu is the rolling farm country on the western marches of the Yoruba world, between Oyo and the Fon plains. Its walled capital, Ketou, was counted one of the oldest Yoruba towns; tradition says Sopasan, a descendant of Oduduwa who came from Ife, founded the settlement, and its kings, the Alaketu, kept a dynasty tied by blood to Ife. In 1444 the kingdom kept its own gods and festivals, close to Oyo in speech and custom, its market towns set among yam fields and the sacred groves of the mask societies. Oyo counted it a dependency: the Alaketu paid annual tribute and came in person to the Bere festival.

As Dahomey grew into a slave-raiding power on the western flank, Ketu became a frontier stronghold, its walls pierced by a single great gate, the Akaba Idena. The town was famed across Yorubaland for its masked ceremonies, the Gelede. At the king's festivals, dancers wearing carved wooden masks performed for 'our mothers', the living and dead women of the community, and for the orisha; their songs celebrated women's fertility and power and taught right conduct. Ketu's Gelede was counted among the oldest and most elaborate of the Yoruba masked traditions.
zh:
科图是约鲁巴世界西境起伏的农乡，夹在奥约与丰人平原之间。城墙环绕的都城科图（Kétou，今译凯图）被视为最古老的约鲁巴城镇之一：相传建城者索帕桑是出自伊费的奥杜杜瓦后裔，历代国王称「阿拉凯图」（Alákétu），王统与伊费血脉相连。1444年的科图守着本族神祇与祭典，语言风俗与奥约相近，集镇散布在薯蓣田和面具会社的圣林之间。奥约把它视作属邦：阿拉凯图每年纳贡，还要亲赴贝雷（Bere）大典。

达荷美在西侧崛起为掳掠奴隶的强权后，科图成了边境要塞，城墙只开一座大门，名唤阿卡巴·伊德纳（Akaba Idéna）。这座城还以热莱德（Gèlèdé）面具祭典闻名整个约鲁巴兰。国王举行节庆时，舞者戴上木雕面具，为社群中「我们的母亲」（包括在世和已故的女性）与众神起舞，歌声赞颂女性的生育与力量，也劝人守规矩；科图的热莱德被视为最古老、仪轨最繁复的约鲁巴面具传统之一。

en: South of Bussa lies the wooded savanna between the Niger and the Nupe plains, home of the Kambari and other Kainji-speaking farmers and fishermen. In 1444 their scattered villages were pagan borderland communities, growing grain and working timber between the Bussa rapids and the middle Niger, paying tribute when the horsemen of Borgu or the kings of Nupe came to collect it. The wars of the empires marched straight through this country: Askia Muhammad's army passed through on its way to take Bussa in 1505, and Askia Daoud's raids laid it waste in 1558 and 1563. After Songhai collapsed in 1591, Oyo's cavalry made the kings of Borgu tributary too. When Etsu Ma'azu of Nupe died in 1818, the wars of succession ended with the old kingdom under Gwandu's control, and Borgu's eastern march lay open to the raiding years that followed.
zh: 莫希位于布萨以南、尼日尔河与努佩平原之间的林木稀树草原，居民是坎巴里等操卡因吉语支诸语的农人与渔民。1444年，他们星散的村落还是边境上信奉本土神祇的村社，在布萨急流与尼日尔河中游之间种粮伐木，博尔古骑兵或努佩国王来索贡时便照例缴纳。帝国的战争径直从这片土地上碾过：1505年阿斯基亚·穆罕默德的大军穿过此地去攻占布萨，阿斯基亚·达乌德的抄掠又在1558和1563年两度把这里洗劫一空。1591年桑海崩溃后，奥约骑兵也迫使博尔古诸王纳贡。1818年努佩王埃祖·马阿祖死后，继承战争以古国落入甘杜控制告终，博尔古东境随之暴露在随后的劫掠年代里。

en:
Yawuri lies where the Niger runs out of the gorges above its great bend, a country of river islands, fishing creeks and fertile banks. The Kamberi, a Benue-Congo farming people, settled it from around the year 1000; by the 15th century the Gungawa who lived on the Niger islands were overtaking them, with Sorko fishermen working the channels. In 1444 there was no walled capital yet. The Gungawa chieftaincy of Gungu Kafa was only taking shape, the river villages kept their old spirit cults, and no Hausa king ruled the country.

Early in the 16th century Garba, the fifth chief of Gungu Kafa, founded the walled town of Birnin Yawuri and made the Gungawa kingdom supreme over the Kamberi; local tradition also remembers the place as conquered and fortified by Queen Amina of Zazzau, whose great earthen walls long marked the site. Stronger neighbors soon fixed its bounds: Kanta of Kebbi overran it in his wars with Songhai, and Zamfara raided down to its borders without staying to hold them. Slave-raiding wore the country through the 18th century as Gungawa and immigrant Hausa merged into one people, and after the Fulani jihad of 1808 Yawuri became a tributary of the Gwandu emirate.
zh:
亚武里位于尼日尔河流出大峡谷、转入大河曲的地方，河洲、渔汊与肥沃河岸交错。坎贝里人属贝努埃-刚果语族的农耕部族，约从1000年起在此定居；到15世纪，住在尼日尔河河洲上的贡加瓦人已盖过他们，索尔科渔民则在各条水道上操舟打鱼。1444年时还没有城墙环绕的都城：贡加瓦人的贡古法酋邦刚在成形，河滨村寨守着旧有的精灵崇拜，也没有哪位豪萨王统治这片地方。

16世纪初，贡古法第五代首领加尔巴筑起有城墙的比尔宁亚武里，使贡加瓦人的王国压过坎贝里人；当地传说还称扎造女王阿米娜曾攻占并设防此地，她留下的高大土墙多年后仍标示着城址。强邻很快替它划定了边界：克比的坎塔在对桑海的战争中将它征服，扎姆法拉南下劫掠也只打到边境，未能久占。整个18世纪，奴隶掳掠不断消耗着这片地方，贡加瓦人与迁入的豪萨人渐趋融合；1808年富拉尼圣战之后，亚武里成为关杜埃米尔国的属国。

en:
Warri is the mangrove country of the western Niger Delta, a maze of creeks where the Benin, Escravos and Forcados rivers meet the Atlantic. Ijaw and Urhobo fishing villages shared its waterways with Yoruba-speaking settlers from the Ijebu waterside, all within Benin's trading orbit, for this was the Oba's outlet to the sea. In 1444 his power ran down these channels, and the Portuguese captains who arrived soon afterwards described the place as a port of Benin. At the riverside barter grounds their ships took slaves, cotton cloth, panther skins and palm oil, paying in brass and copper bracelets.

The reigning dynasty came from Benin itself. About 1480 Ginuwa, a son of Oba Olua, left the Benin court after a succession quarrel; tradition says he was carried out hidden in a wooden box, with the sons of seventy chiefs for company. He married an Ijaw woman and died at Ijala, and his son Ijijen led the party on to Okotomu, where a man named Itsekiri acknowledged him as ruler and gave him land. On it Ijijen built Ode-Itsekiri, capital of the mixed river peoples under the Olu of Iwere.

Missionaries from Sao Tome made Ode-Itsekiri one of the earliest Christian courts on this coast. An Augustinian mission sat in the town the Portuguese called Cidade de Santo Agostinho, and a prince baptised Sebastian was Olu by 1597. Around 1600 he sent his son Dom Domingos to school in Coimbra and Lisbon; the young man came home in 1611 with a Portuguese wife, Maria Pereira, a chaplain and ten servants, and later reigned as Olu Atuwatse I. His son Antonio Domingo, Olu in the 1640s, wrote to Pope Innocent X in 1652 asking for Capuchins, saying no priest had been seen in the kingdom for seven years. Warri's armies moved by water, in war canoes carrying up to a hundred men who fought with muskets and swivel guns behind shields. Olu Erejuwa, reigning from about 1760 to 1800, used his Portuguese ties to master the river trade and the dues paid by European ships, and the kingdom reached its widest bounds.
zh:
瓦里是尼日尔河三角洲西部的红树林之乡，贝宁河、埃斯克拉沃斯河与福卡多斯河在此汇入大西洋，河汊纵横如迷宫。伊乔人和乌尔霍博人的渔村，与来自伊杰布水网地带的约鲁巴语移民共居水畔；这里正是奥巴通向大海的河口，处处都在贝宁的贸易圈内。1444年，他的势力沿水道延伸至此，此后不久到来的葡萄牙船长把这里称作贝宁的一个港口。在河畔的易货地，他们用铜镯和黄铜镯换取奴隶、棉布、豹皮和棕榈油。

统治瓦里的王朝本身也出自贝宁。约1480年，奥巴奥卢阿之子吉努瓦因王位之争离开贝宁宫廷；相传他藏在木箱中被运出，同行的还有七十名酋长的儿子。他在途中娶了一位伊乔女子，最后死于伊贾拉。其子伊吉坚率众人继续前行，抵达奥科托穆，当地一个名叫伊策基里的人奉他为主、献给他土地。伊吉坚在这片土地上建起奥代伊策基里，作为水边诸族的都城，统治者是伊韦雷的奥卢。

来自圣多美岛的传教士使奥代伊策基里成为这片海岸最早的基督教宫廷之一。奥斯定会传教团驻在城中，葡萄牙人称之为圣奥古斯丁城，一位受洗取名塞巴斯蒂安的王储在1597年已是奥卢。约1600年，他把儿子唐·多明戈斯送往科英布拉和里斯本求学；多明戈斯1611年携葡萄牙妻子玛丽亚·佩雷拉、一名神父和十名仆从归国，后来即位为奥卢·阿图瓦特塞一世。他的儿子安东尼奥·多明戈于1640年代任奥卢，1652年致书教皇英诺森十世，请求派遣嘉布遣会教士，因为国中已七年不见神父。瓦里的军队在水上行动，战用独木舟每艘可载百人，士兵在盾障后使用火绳枪和旋转炮座上的火器。奥卢埃雷朱阿约于1760年至1800年在位，他借葡萄牙关系掌控河道贸易和欧洲船只缴纳的税费，使王国达到最大版图。

en:
The Oti River winds through wooded savanna between the Atakora hills and Gambaga, a country of Gur-speaking villagers: Konkomba farmers along the river and Moba clans in the grass plains to the north, who had drifted south after the fall of the Fada-Gurma kingdom around 1420. In 1444 Dagomba horsemen from Yendi kept a loose overlordship and outposts on the Oti, while the villages held to their ancestor shrines and paid tribute in grain and cattle.

For centuries this was a corridor rather than a kingdom. Caravans out of the Ashanti country passed through Salaga, the great kola and slave market, and turned up the Oti valley on their way to the Hausa cities. About 1751 a mercenary band of Akan soldiers from Anou on the Komoe, hired for the wars of Gonja, settled on the river instead of marching home; Anufo tradition gives two reasons, that they were still waiting for their pay, or that their leader had died at Gambaga. They built Sansanne-Mango, and the Anufo, also called Chokossi, held it as a small warrior state, with Mande horsemen, Akan musketeers and Muslim amulet-makers ranked as separate classes among them. Their town became a market for kola, salt and captives on the road between Salaga and Hausaland.
zh:
奥蒂河蜿蜒流过阿塔科拉丘陵与甘巴加之间的林木稀树草原，居民都是操古尔语族语言的村社：沿河是孔孔巴农人，北方草原上是莫巴人诸氏族，他们约在1420年法达-古尔马王国崩溃后向南迁来。1444年，达格邦的骑兵从延迪维持着松散的宗主权，在奥蒂河畔设有据点；各村社守着祖先神龛，以谷物和牛只纳贡。

数百年来这里是一条通道而非一个王国。阿散蒂方向来的商队先经过柯拉果与奴隶的大市场萨拉加，再转入奥蒂河谷，前往豪萨诸城。约1751年，一队阿坎族雇佣兵从科莫埃河畔的阿努出发，受雇参加贡贾的战事，却没有返乡，而是在河畔落脚；阿努福人的口传有两种解释，一说是在等酬劳，一说是首领死在了甘巴加。他们建起桑萨内-曼戈，阿努福人又称乔科西人，以此为中心形成一个小小的军人政权，曼德骑兵、阿坎火枪手和制作护符的穆斯林学者在其中分属不同阶层。他们的城镇成了柯拉果、食盐和俘虏的集市，坐落在萨拉加通往豪萨诸城的商路上。

en:
Karasi lies behind the Asian shore of the Dardanelles, from the castles at the narrows back to the Biga plain on the Granicus river. This was the heartland of the Karasid Turkoman beylik. Karasi Bey's successors kept their fleet at Karabiga, and Demirhan Bey's ships cruised the Sea of Marmara and raided the Balkans, more than a match for the small early Ottoman navy, until he signed a truce with Andronikos III at Pegae in 1328. Orhan took over the beylik in the 1340s with the help of the claimant Dursun Bey. His son Süleyman Paşa used Karasi ships and crews for the first Ottoman crossing to Gallipoli and secured the Biga interior in 1353; Murad I later reduced its sea-castle. The old shore town, sacked in the wars, was rebuilt inland as Biga, seat of an Ottoman sanjak. In 1444 its broad plain was the usual muster ground where Anatolian armies embarked for Rumeli.

Mehmed II closed the strait with a pair of castles facing each other across the water. In 1462 he raised Kale-i Sultaniye on this shore, opposite Kilitbahir on the European side. Its thirty guns were ranged to cover the 1,250-metre passage, so no fleet could force the narrows without the sultan's leave. Suleiman strengthened and enlarged the fortress in 1551, and it was renewed again during the Cretan War with Venice. Biga itself stayed a small market town, just over a thousand people in 1516 and about two thousand by 1575, living by the troops and warlike stores passing between the two continents. Selim III rebuilt the strait fortresses during the Napoleonic wars, and the works were updated again in 1808, the guns at the narrows still covering the channel.
zh:
卡拉西位于达达尼尔海峡亚洲海岸后方，从最窄处的城堡一直延伸到格拉尼库斯河（今比加河）畔的比加平原。这里曾是卡莱西突厥蛮贝伊国的腹地，卡莱西贝伊的后继者把舰队设在卡拉比加。德米尔汗贝伊的船只游弋马尔马拉海、袭掠巴尔干，实力在弱小的奥斯曼早期海军之上，直到他1328年在佩盖与安德洛尼卡三世订立和约。奥尔汗于14世纪40年代借争位者杜尔孙贝伊之力吞并贝伊国，其子苏莱曼帕夏动用卡莱西的船只和船员完成奥斯曼人对加里波利的首次渡海，并于1353年拿下比加内陆，海岸城堡后来也被穆拉德一世攻克。战争中遭劫的海滨旧城在内地重建为比加，成为奥斯曼桑贾克的治所。1444年时，这片开阔平原是安纳托利亚军队渡海前往鲁米利亚的惯常集结地。

穆罕默德二世用隔海相对的一对城堡封锁海峡。1462年，他在这一岸筑起苏丹尼耶城堡，与欧洲岸上的基利特巴希尔隔海相望。三十门大炮次第排列，覆盖1250米宽的水道，未经苏丹许可，任何舰队都无法强渡窄口。苏莱曼一世1551年加固扩建这座要塞，与威尼斯进行克里特战争期间又加以修缮。比加本身始终是座小商埠，1516年人口刚过一千，1575年约有两千，靠往来于两洲之间的军队与军需物资为生。塞利姆三世在拿破仑战争时期重修海峡要塞，1808年工事又经更新，窄口的炮群仍然封锁着航道。

en:
Manisa, the Roman and Byzantine Magnesia ad Sipylum, lies beneath Mount Sipylus where the hills open onto the Gediz plain. During the Empire of Nicaea it kept the imperial mint and treasury and operated as a working capital while the Latins held Constantinople. After Michael IX failed to stop Turkish raiders in 1302, much of the population fled and the city fell into ruin. Saruhan Bey took it in 1313 and made Manisa the seat of his beylik; his dynasty built ships, raided the Greek and Thracian coasts with the Aydınids, and completed the Great Mosque in 1366. The Ottomans absorbed the principality in 1412, according to Turkish sources, and from 1437 Murad II sent princes here to learn provincial government. In 1444 Manisa was the leading princely seat of western Anatolia and its plain was being settled again.

Sixteen Ottoman princes governed Manisa before the practice ended in 1595. Two of them later ruled as Mehmed II and Süleyman I; Süleyman held the city from 1513 to 1520 with his mother Hafsa Sultan. Murad III, who had also been governor here, replaced his small princely mosque with the Muradiye Mosque of 1583 to 1586. Mimar Sinan designed it, Mahmud Halife began the building, and Sedefkar Mehmed Aga, later the architect of Istanbul's Sultan Ahmed Mosque, finished the work.

The princely governorship ended in 1595, the same year a severe earthquake damaged Manisa. Jelali disorders then filled the surrounding countryside; in the 1620s the warlord Cennetoğlu controlled much of the fertile land around the city, and Kalenderoğlu's rebels later plundered the same villages. By about 1700 Manisa had recovered as a caravan terminus with cotton markets and a leather trade named after the city, while Greek and Jewish merchants were already moving down to the rising port of İzmir.
zh:
马尼萨在罗马和拜占庭时代称西皮洛斯山下的马格内西亚，位于西皮洛斯山与盖迪兹平原相接处。尼西亚帝国时期，这里存放帝国铸币厂和国库，在拉丁人占据君士坦丁堡期间实际承担行都功能。1302年米哈伊尔九世未能挡住土耳其袭掠者后，大量居民逃离，城市残破。1313年，萨鲁汗贝伊夺取此地，定为自己侯国的都城；他的王朝建造船只，与艾登侯国联手袭掠希腊和色雷斯海岸，并在1366年建成乌鲁清真寺。据土耳其文资料，奥斯曼人于1412年吞并这个侯国；1437年起，穆拉德二世派遣皇子到这里学习地方治理。1444年，马尼萨已是西安纳托利亚最重要的皇子驻地，周围平原有了重新定居的迹象。

皇子出镇制度在1595年结束前，先后有十六位奥斯曼皇子治理马尼萨。其中两人后来成为穆罕默德二世和苏莱曼一世；苏莱曼在1513至1520年出镇此地，母亲哈芙莎苏丹随他在此主事。也曾担任马尼萨总督的穆拉德三世，把自己做皇子时的小清真寺扩换成1583至1586年修建的穆拉迪耶清真寺。米马尔·锡南负责设计，马哈茂德·哈利法开工，后来设计伊斯坦布尔苏丹艾哈迈德清真寺的塞德夫卡尔·穆罕默德阿加完成工程。

皇子出镇制度于1595年结束，同年一场强震破坏了马尼萨。杰拉里动乱随后席卷乡间；1620年代，军阀詹奈特奥卢控制了城周大量肥沃土地，卡伦代尔奥卢率领的叛乱者后来也劫掠了这些村庄。到1700年前后，马尼萨已恢复为商队终点站，有棉花市集和以城名命名的皮革贸易，希腊与犹太商人则已经陆续迁往山下正在兴起的伊兹密尔港。

en:
Antalya, called Adalia by Latin sailors, lies on a sheltered bay of the Pamphylian coast where the Taurus Mountains meet the sea. Attalus II of Pergamon founded Attaleia around 150 BC as a naval base. Under Byzantium it became the chief station of the Cibyrrhaeot fleet and the best harbour between the Aegean and Cyprus. Kaykhusraw I's Seljuks took it in 1207 and used its dockyard for Mediterranean ships. From 1321 the Teke Turcomans made the port their capital. Ibn Battuta found Christian merchants locked into the walled Mina quarter at night, while Greeks, Jews and the emir's court occupied separate quarters; orchards around the town supplied apricots dried for Egypt. Peter I of Cyprus stormed the city in 1361, and the Teke ruler recovered it in 1373. Ottoman annexation, Timur's restoration of the old dynasty and a second Ottoman conquest followed before 1423. In 1444 Teke was an Ottoman sanjak: ships used the old harbour, and cotton and fruit came down from the coastal plain for the voyage to Syria and Egypt.

The hills behind Antalya produced one of the most dangerous revolts of Bayezid II's reign. In 1511 Şahkulu, a dervish from the Teke country, led a Kızılbaş rising among Turcoman highlanders, and the rebels marched inland before Ottoman forces suppressed it. The port remained a busy mixed town. When Evliya Çelebi visited in the later seventeenth century, he counted 3,000 houses in twenty Turkish and four Greek quarters, with room in the harbour for about two hundred boats. Imperial power along this coast weakened during the derebey period. The Tekkeoğlu lords around Perge kept their own estates and armed followings until Mahmud II's government broke their power in 1812.
zh:
阿塔利亚（安塔利亚）位于潘菲利亚海岸的避风湾，托罗斯山脉直逼海边。帕加马国王阿塔罗斯二世约在公元前150年建立阿塔利亚，把它作为海军基地。拜占庭时期，它是基比拉奥特舰队的主要驻港，也是爱琴海与塞浦路斯之间条件最好的港湾。1207年，凯霍斯鲁一世的塞尔柱军队攻下此城，并利用船坞修造地中海船只。1321年起，泰凯土库曼人以这座港口为都。伊本·白图泰看到，基督徒商人夜间被关在有城墙的米纳港区，希腊人、犹太人和埃米尔的宫廷各住一区；周围果园出产的杏子制成杏干，运往埃及。1361年，塞浦路斯国王皮埃尔一世攻陷城市，泰凯统治者又在1373年将其收复。此后它经历奥斯曼吞并、帖木儿恢复旧侯国和奥斯曼再次征服，1423年起稳定归入奥斯曼。1444年，泰凯是奥斯曼的桑贾克，船只停泊在老港，棉花和水果从海岸平原运下，再经海路运往叙利亚和埃及。

阿塔利亚后方的山地，孕育了巴耶济德二世晚年最危险的叛乱之一。1511年，出身泰凯的托钵僧沙赫库鲁率领土库曼山民中的克孜勒巴什信徒起兵，叛军向内陆挺进，最后被奥斯曼军队镇压。港口城市本身保持着繁忙和族群杂居的面貌。17世纪后期爱维亚·瑟勒布到访时，城中有二十个土耳其街区和四个希腊街区，共三千户人家，港湾可容约两百艘船。到德雷贝伊时期，中央对这段海岸的控制减弱。佩尔格一带的泰凯奥卢领主拥有自己的地产和武装随从，直到1812年马哈茂德二世政府压服他们。

en:
Bolu is the forested saddle between the Sakarya and Filyos rivers, where the road from Constantinople climbs into inner Anatolia; to the north the hills run down to a short strip of Black Sea shore. Its Greek city, Bithynium or Claudiopolis, was known in Strabo's time for its pastures and cheese, and it was the birthplace of Antinous, the Bithynian companion of the emperor Hadrian, who was deified after dying in Egypt and whose name Hadrian added to the city's coinage. As a Byzantine frontier fortress it came under Turkish siege in 1179, until Manuel I arrived by forced marches and the besiegers fled; Seljuk forces took the city before 1214. Orhan's commander Konur Alp secured it in the mid-1320s. After Timur's victory at Ankara the Candarids held Bolu from 1402 to 1423, and Mehmed Çelebi sheltered on the Kızık highland here before restoring Ottoman unity. In 1444 Bolu was a settled Sunni Turkish sanjak centre on the road into Anatolia, its shore hamlets carrying fish up to the inland markets.

In the sixteenth century Bolu ranked among the second-tier sanjaks assigned to Ottoman princes, and Bayezid II posted the young Şehzade Süleyman (the future Suleiman I) there to learn provincial government. The old bishopric of Claudiopolis had lost its resident bishop in the previous century, and after 1692 military governors called voyvodas ran the sanjak in place of the princely governors.
zh:
博卢是萨卡里亚河与菲利约斯河之间森林密布的鞍形地带，从君士坦丁堡通往安纳托利亚内陆的道路在此翻山，北面的丘陵一直延伸到一段黑海海岸。希腊人的城市比提尼翁，即克劳狄奥波利斯，在斯特拉波的时代就以牧场和乳酪闻名；这里也是安提诺乌斯的出生地：这位比提尼亚少年是罗马皇帝哈德良的宠臣，在埃及死后被奉为神，哈德良还把他的名字加铸在城市钱币上。作为拜占庭边境要塞，它在1179年遭到突厥人围攻，曼努埃尔一世急行军赶到，围城者才四散退走；塞尔柱军队在1214年前占据该城。14世纪20年代中期，奥尔汗的将领科努尔·阿尔普将其拿下。帖木儿安卡拉获胜后，詹达尔人于1402年至1423年占据博卢，穆罕默德·切莱比在恢复奥斯曼统一前也曾在克孜克高原避居。1444年时，博卢是通往安纳托利亚大路上一座安定的逊尼派土耳其人桑贾克城镇，海滨渔村把鱼货送进内陆市集。

16世纪，博卢被列为分派给奥斯曼皇子的第二等桑贾克之一，巴耶济德二世曾把年轻的皇子苏莱曼（日后的苏莱曼一世）派来学习行省治理。古老的克劳狄奥波利斯主教区在上一个世纪已没有驻地主教；1692年后，称为沃伊沃达的军事长官取代皇子总督管理桑贾克。

en:
Bozok is a high grain plateau in the middle of Anatolia, crossed by the roads between Amasya, Tokat, Sivas and Kayseri. The Galatian stronghold of Tavium had once been its chief place, but only Turkmen villages and summer pastures remained around the hamlet of Yozgat. The district took its name from the Bozok Oghuz Turks, and its horses, flocks and wheat made it useful recruiting country: the tribes put mounted men into the Ottoman armies. Çelebi Mehmed brought it under Ottoman rule in 1408 after Timur's withdrawal. In 1444 Bozok was therefore an inland sanjak without a walled capital, a province of herds and soldiery in the shadow of greater Amasya and Sivas.

In 1519 a Bozok Turkmen named Şeyh Celal raised a revolt around Tokat, and the suppression was so bloody that the great Celali uprisings of later years took their name from him. In 1526 the Mamalu Turkmen of the Aleppo Bozulus confederation were settled on the plateau, and from those herdsmen rose the Çapanoğlu, the family that built Yozgat. Ahmed Ağa became voivode of Bozok in 1732, turned the hamlet into a market town, built a mosque at Saray in 1749 and a madrasa in Yozgat in 1753; his son Mustafa added eighty shops, an inn and the domed Çapanoğlu Mosque, begun in 1779. Whoever held the formal governorship, the tax farms stayed in the family. They provisioned Istanbul and sent grain and soldiers to the Russian wars, and in 1790 Süleyman Bey led 4,000 of his men to the Rumelian front. The rival Canikli family had his brother Mustafa murdered in the spring of 1782, after which Süleyman became the strongest magnate in central Anatolia; he signed the Sened-i İttifak charter with the sultan in 1808 and died in 1813. Mahmud II then reclaimed Bozok for the imperial treasury.
zh:
博佐克是安纳托利亚中部的谷物高原，阿马西亚、托卡特、锡瓦斯和开塞利之间的道路穿行而过。加拉太人的要塞塔维乌姆曾是这一带的首邑，到约兹加特这个小村周围只剩土库曼村庄和夏季牧场。地区得名于乌古斯人的博佐克部，马匹、羊群和小麦使这里成为上好的兵源地，各部落为奥斯曼军队提供骑兵。帖木儿撤离后，切莱比·穆罕默德于1408年将其纳入奥斯曼统治。1444年的博佐克因此是一个没有城墙首府的内陆桑贾克，在阿马西亚和锡瓦斯这些大城的近旁出产牲畜、输送士兵。

1519年，名叫谢赫·贾拉尔的博佐克土库曼人在托卡特一带起事，镇压极为血腥，后来大规模的杰拉里叛乱便以他的名字命名。1526年，阿勒颇博祖卢斯联盟的马马卢土库曼人被安置到高原上，恰潘奥卢家族就从这些牧户中崛起，约兹加特城也由他们建成。艾哈迈德阿迦1732年成为博佐克长官，把小村经营成市镇，1749年在萨拉伊建清真寺，1753年在约兹加特办伊斯兰学校；其子穆斯塔法添了八十间商铺、一家客栈，1779年又动工修建带穹顶的恰潘奥卢清真寺。无论正式长官换成谁，包税权始终握在这个家族手里。他们向伊斯坦布尔供应物资，为俄土战争输送粮食和士兵，1790年苏莱曼贝伊亲率四千人开赴鲁米利亚战线。敌对的贾尼克利家族1782年春派人暗杀了他的兄长穆斯塔法，苏莱曼此后成为安纳托利亚中部最有势力的豪强，1808年与苏丹签署《同盟宪章》，1813年去世，马哈茂德二世随即把博佐克收归国库。

en:
Kayseri lies beneath Mount Erciyes, the 3,917-metre dormant volcano of Cappadocia. As Mazaca it was the residence of the kings of Cappadocia, where the road from Sinope to the Euphrates crossed the Persian Royal Road; as Roman Caesarea it was the see of Basil the Great, who built his hospital and monastery complex outside the walls in the fourth century. Alp Arslan's Seljuk army sacked the city in 1067, and the Danishmendids rebuilt it in 1134; from 1178 to 1243 it was the second capital of the Sultanate of Rum, which left the Gevher Nesibe hospital, the Hunat Hatun complex and the grand mosque inside Justinian's old basalt walls. Mongol rule followed, then the Eretnids and Kadi Burhan al-Din, and the Karamanid Ibrahim II took it from the Dulkadirids in 1435. In 1444 it was the northern stronghold of the Karamanid beylik, its walled streets crowded with Seljuk and Turkmen monuments.

In 1508 Shah Ismail's Safavid followers swept into Kayseri but soon withdrew, and after Selim I's eastern wars it became in 1515 the seat of a sanjak, first of the Rûm province and then of Karaman. Caravanserais and bazaars served the road between Sivas and Konya, and building inside the old walls went on through the sixteenth century. The city's best-known son of the age was born just before the conquest: Koca Mimar Sinan of the village of Agirnas rose as a Janissary military engineer to be chief architect to Suleiman the Magnificent, Selim II and Murad III, responsible for more than 300 major structures including the Selimiye Mosque at Edirne; in 1573 he obtained orders from Selim II exempting his Kayseri relatives from the deportation of Orthodox families to repopulate Cyprus.
zh:
开塞利坐落在卡帕多奇亚的埃尔吉耶斯山下，这座休眠火山海拔3917米。古称马扎卡，曾是卡帕多奇亚诸王的驻地，锡诺普通往幼发拉底河的道路与波斯御道在此相汇；罗马时代名凯撒里亚，4世纪时主教大圣巴西略在城外建起医院与修道院综合体。1067年阿尔普·阿尔斯兰的塞尔柱军队洗劫该城，达尼什曼德王朝1134年将其重建；1178至1243年它是鲁姆苏丹国的第二都城，格夫赫尔·内西比医院、胡娜特哈屯建筑群和大清真寺都建在查士丁尼时代留下的玄武岩旧城墙之内。此后历经蒙古人、埃尔特纳侯国和卡迪·布尔汉丁，1435年卡拉曼君主易卜拉欣二世从杜尔卡迪尔王朝手中夺得此城。1444年，这座城墙之内塞尔柱与土库曼建筑林立的坚城，是卡拉曼侯国北方的重镇。

1508年，沙阿·伊斯玛仪的萨法维部众曾席卷开塞利，又很快撤走；塞利姆一世东征之后，开塞利1515年成为桑贾克治所，先属鲁姆省，后归卡拉曼省。商馆和巴扎为锡瓦斯与科尼亚之间的道路服务，旧城墙内的营建延续了整个16世纪。这个时代最出名的本地人出生在征服前不久：开塞利近郊阿厄尔纳斯（Agirnas）村的米马尔·希南从近卫军军工工程师做起，最终成为苏莱曼大帝、塞利姆二世和穆拉德三世三代苏丹的首席建筑师，主持三百多项重大工程，包括埃迪尔内的塞利米耶清真寺；1573年，他还从塞利姆二世那里取得敕令，使自己在开塞利的亲属免于随东正教家庭被迁往塞浦路斯补充人口。

en:
İçel stretches from the rugged western Taurus to the Mediterranean, where Silifke, Mut and Anamur look out over the sea lanes to Cyprus. Its chief town, Ermenek, lies inland above the passes between the Anatolian plateau and this coast. The Karamanid Turkmen built their power around castles at Ermenek, Mut, Gülnar and Silifke, and Ermenek was one of their earliest centres before their rulers settled at Larende and Konya. Karamanid patrons gave the town its Grand Mosque in 1302, the Tol Medrese in 1339 and the Meydan Mosque around 1435. Down at Silifke, a citadel above the Göksu River had guarded the coastal route since Byzantine times; in 1210 Leo I of Armenian Cilicia granted it to the Knights Hospitaller, who left much of the surviving Crusader stonework. In 1444 the country belonged to the Karamanid beylik. İbrahim Bey had used the Balkan crusade to raid Ankara and Kütahya, but Murad II turned against him, drove him back into these mountains, and imposed Ottoman peace terms in August.

The beylik's last wars began over an inheritance. When İbrahim died in 1464, İshak Bey received İçel, Ermenek and Mut and kept his seat at Silifke, while Pir Ahmed held Konya. Mehmed II backed Pir Ahmed, who defeated İshak in 1465; Ottoman troops took Konya in 1468 and forced the Taurus highlands and coast in 1474. After Kasım Bey died in 1483, Karamanid lords in İçel raised Turgutoğlu Mahmud II and sought Mamluk help. The Ottoman campaign of 1487 extinguished the beylik. Registers in 1523 list İçel as a sanjak of Karaman with Silifke, Ermenek, Gülnar and Mut; after the conquest of Cyprus it passed to the new Cyprus provincial government in 1571.
zh:
伊切尔从崎岖的西托罗斯山地一直延伸到地中海，锡利夫凯、穆特和阿纳穆尔等城镇面向通往塞浦路斯的海路。首府埃尔梅内克地处内陆，高踞在安纳托利亚高原通往南部海岸的山口之上。卡拉曼土库曼人围绕埃尔梅内克、穆特、居尔纳尔和锡利夫凯的城堡扩张势力，埃尔梅内克也是他们最早的据点之一；后来王朝宫廷才迁往拉伦德和科尼亚。卡拉曼统治者在这里留下了1302年的大清真寺、1339年的托尔伊斯兰学校，以及约1435年的迈丹清真寺。海边的锡利夫凯城堡位于格克苏河上方，自拜占庭时代起便控扼沿海道路；1210年，奇里乞亚亚美尼亚国王列奥一世把它交给医院骑士团，现存城堡有相当部分出自十字军时期的工程。1444年，这片土地仍属卡拉曼贝伊国。易卜拉欣贝伊趁巴尔干十字军战争袭掠安卡拉和屈塔希亚，穆拉德二世却回师相向，把他逼回群山，并在8月迫使他接受奥斯曼的议和条件。

贝伊国最后的战争起于继承纠纷。易卜拉欣1464年死后，伊沙克贝伊分得伊切尔、埃尔梅内克和穆特，驻在锡利夫凯；皮尔·艾哈迈德则占有科尼亚。穆罕默德二世支持皮尔·艾哈迈德，后者于1465年击败伊沙克；奥斯曼军队1468年攻占科尼亚，1474年又压服托罗斯山区和海岸。卡西姆贝伊1483年死后，伊切尔的卡拉曼旧臣拥立图尔古特奥卢·马哈茂德二世，并向马穆鲁克求援。奥斯曼1487年的远征终结了这个贝伊国。1523年的登记簿把伊切尔列为卡拉曼下辖的桑贾克，辖区包括锡利夫凯、埃尔梅内克、居尔纳尔和穆特；塞浦路斯征服后，它又在1571年划归新设的塞浦路斯行省。

en:
Malatya, known in older records as Melitene, lies on a fertile Taurus plain where roads from Sivas and Kayseri continue toward Aleppo and the upper Euphrates. The Roman army made Melitene a frontier legionary base. In the ninth century it was a Muslim emirate, and Umar al-Aqta used it as a base for raids on Byzantine Asia Minor until he was killed at Lalakaon in 863; John Kourkouas recovered the city for Constantinople in 934. Its merchants later dealt in brocades, pearls and gold. A Syriac Christian merchant named Abu Salim was said to have ransomed 15,000 captives from Turkish raiders at five dinars a person. The Seljuks sacked the city in 1058, after which it passed through Danishmend, Seljuk, Ilkhanid, Mamluk and Eretnid hands. By the later fourteenth century Cairo and the Dulkadir beys were contesting it. In 1444 Malatya was a walled Dulkadir border town facing Mamluk Syria, with cloth bazaars and a Seljuk great mosque built around 1224.

The town entered the Ottoman Empire with the rest of Dulkadir in 1515, during Selim I's eastern campaigns, and later registers placed it under Harput. Without the old Mamluk frontier wars, its garrison role shrank while its markets continued to handle woven cloth and caravan provisions. The Great Mosque, dated to about 1224 and attributed to the architect Yakub bin Ebubekir, stood inside the walls of old Malatya; Seljuk and Mamluk tombs around it served travellers and dervishes on the Aleppo road. Repeated rebellions disturbed the district between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries, but the old town kept its bazaars, caravan traffic and weaving. By the early nineteenth century it was a provincial market town within its medieval walls, with no frontier army to support.
zh:
马拉蒂亚旧称梅利泰内，坐落在托罗斯山脉的肥沃平原上，锡瓦斯和开塞利通往阿勒颇与幼发拉底河上游的道路经过这里。罗马军队曾把梅利泰内设为边疆军团驻地。9世纪时，这里是穆斯林埃米尔国，奥马尔·阿克塔曾从这里出兵袭掠拜占庭的小亚细亚，直到863年在拉拉卡翁之战中被杀；934年，约翰·库尔库阿斯替君士坦丁堡收复此城。后来，这里的商人经营锦缎、珍珠和黄金。据说一位名叫阿布·萨利姆的叙利亚基督徒商人，曾以每人五第纳尔的价钱，从土耳其袭掠者手中赎出一万五千名俘虏。1058年塞尔柱人洗劫城市，此后它历经达尼什曼德、塞尔柱、伊儿汗、马穆鲁克和埃雷特纳统治。到14世纪后期，开罗和杜勒卡迪尔贝伊反复争夺此地。1444年，马拉蒂亚是杜勒卡迪尔一座有城墙的边城，面向马穆鲁克控制的叙利亚，城内有布料市集和约1224年修建的塞尔柱大清真寺。

1515年，塞利姆一世东征期间，马拉蒂亚随杜勒卡迪尔其余领土并入奥斯曼帝国，后来的册籍将它划归哈尔普特管辖。过去同马穆鲁克对峙的边塞战争结束后，它的驻军作用下降，市场仍经营织物和商队给养。约1224年建成、归在建筑师雅各布·本·阿布·贝克尔名下的大清真寺立在旧马拉蒂亚城墙内，周围的塞尔柱和马穆鲁克墓冢接待前往阿勒颇路上的旅客与托钵僧。16至18世纪，多次叛乱惊扰这一地区，但旧城保留了市集、商队贸易和织造业。到19世纪初，它已是一座围在中世纪城墙中的行省集镇，不再需要供养边塞大军。

en:
Canik is the Black Sea coastal belt between Sinop and Trebizond, with Samsun its harbour beneath the Canik Mountains. Ionian Greeks from Miletus founded Amisos around 760 BC on a shallow bay, and because the shortest road from the sea to Amaseia and inner Anatolia climbed from its quay, it became the commercial capital of Roman Pontus, outranking Sinope. Genoese merchants held a walled trading quarter here in the thirteenth century. The Danishmendids, unable to storm the Greek town, built a second, Muslim settlement named Isamisos beside it, and the two Samsuns coexisted until Ottoman troops took Amisos from its Genoese garrison while a fire burned in the streets and united the two towns. In the fourteenth century the coast was parcelled among the Canik beyliks; Bayezid I first took Samsun in 1398, lost it after Ankara, and the last local house, the Taşanoğulları, was subdued only in 1430. In 1444 Canik was a newly pacified Ottoman sancak, its hills grazed by Turkmen and its ports still largely Greek and Orthodox.

In 1461 Mehmed II's army and fleet moved along this coast to force Sinop's surrender and then extinguish Trebizond, the last Byzantine successor state on Canik's eastern flank. For most of the Ottoman centuries Samsun stayed a modest pier: the coastal marshes produced hemp cordage, and in wartime the town shipped grain to the army. During the Celali rising Abdülhalim Karayazıcı, defeated by Sokolluzade Hasan Pasha at Sepedlü on 12 August 1601, withdrew into the district and died in the Canik mountains in 1602; his brother Deli Hasan kept the revolt alive. Cossack raids from the sea added to the damage, and the tax registers of 1642 and 1643 found the town reduced to a village. Its later fame came from tobacco, as the small, aromatic Samsun-Bafra leaf grown along this coast fetched high prices in the Istanbul market by the eighteenth century.
zh:
贾尼克是锡诺普与特拉布宗之间的黑海海岸带，治所萨姆松是贾尼克山麓的港口。公元前760年前后，米利都的爱奥尼亚希腊人在一处浅水湾边建立阿米索斯；由这座港口登岸，取道阿马西亚深入安纳托利亚内陆最为近便，它也因此成为罗马本都的商业首府，地位压过锡诺普。13世纪时，热那亚商人在此据有一座筑墙商站。达尼什曼德人久攻希腊城镇不下，便在紧贴它的地方另建穆斯林城镇伊萨米索斯，两座萨姆松长期并存，直到奥斯曼军队趁城中起火攻下阿米索斯的热那亚守军，才把两城合为一体。14世纪，海岸被各个卡尼克贝伊国瓜分：巴耶济德一世1398年首取萨姆松，安卡拉战役后得而复失，最后一个地方王公塔尚奥卢家族到1430年才臣服。1444年的贾尼克是刚平定的奥斯曼桑贾克，山地是土库曼人的牧场，港口居民仍以希腊东正教徒为主。

1461年，穆罕默德二世的陆海军沿海岸东进，迫降锡诺普，随即攻灭特拉布宗，拔掉了贾尼克东侧最后一个拜占庭继承国。奥斯曼统治的几百年里，萨姆松多半只是个不起眼的码头：沿海沼泽出产大麻绳索，战时还要为军队输送军粮。杰拉勒叛乱中，阿卜杜勒哈利姆·卡拉亚泽吉1601年8月12日在塞佩德卢被索科卢扎德·哈桑帕夏击败，退入这一带，1602年死于贾尼克山中，其弟德利·哈桑继续举事。哥萨克人又从海上来袭，雪上加霜，到1642和1643年的税册里，萨姆松已衰败成村庄规模。它后来的名声靠的是烟草：沿海种植的萨姆松—巴夫拉烟叶叶片小、香气浓，到18世纪在伊斯坦布尔市场上能卖出高价。

en:
Erzincan lies on the upper Karasu, the western arm of the Euphrates, where the river opens into a broad fertile plain. Armenian Yerznka was an archbishop's seat and a town of monasteries. After Manzikert the Mengujekid Turkmen made it one of their capitals, and under Behram Shah in the twelfth century its markets and crafts drew traders from the surrounding country; Marco Polo, passing through, called it the noblest city of those parts and noted that its people were Armenians. The Seljuk sultan Alaeddin Keykubad I annexed it in 1228 and two years later defeated the Khwarazmshah Jalal al-Din at Yassıçemen nearby. Mongol armies wrecked the town before the battle of Köse Dağ, and in the disorders after the Ilkhanids its lord Mutahharten sought Timur's protection, which drew Bayezid I's siege of 1401. The Black Sheep chief Kara Yusuf seized it in 1419, so that in 1444 Erzincan was a Black Sheep frontier town whose people were still largely Armenian.

The White Sheep sultan Uzun Hasan took Erzincan and repaired its citadel, and on 11 August 1473 Mehmed II met him in person at Otlukbeli on the town's own plain. Hasan's son Zeynel Mirza was killed in the fighting; Hasan got away only by leaving a lookalike to hold his standard, and Erzincan passed to the Ottomans. In the summer of 1500 about 7,000 Qizilbash warriors of eight tribes mustered here to join the young Ismail at the outset of his Safavid venture, and after Chaldiran in 1514 Selim I brought the town firmly under Ottoman rule. The first census, in 1516–18, counted twenty quarters, seven Muslim and thirteen Christian, and Suleiman twice stopped here on his Tabriz campaigns. When Evliya Çelebi came in 1647 he found the citadel standing alone in the open plain, with about 2,000 houses and forty-eight quarters around it and eleven bathhouses serving the caravan trade.
zh:
埃尔津詹位于幼发拉底河西支卡拉苏河上，河道在此铺展成一片开阔肥沃的平原。亚美尼亚语中的耶尔兹恩卡是大主教驻地，也是修道院林立的城镇。曼齐刻尔特战役后，门居切克突厥蛮把它立为都城之一；12世纪贝赫拉姆沙在位时，城市的市集和手工业吸引着四乡客商，后来路过的马可·波罗称它是这一带最华贵的城市，并注意到居民都是亚美尼亚人。罗姆苏丹阿拉丁·凯库巴德一世1228年吞并此城，两年后又在附近的亚瑟切门击败花剌子模沙札兰丁。蒙古大军在克塞山战役前毁城而过，伊儿汗国崩溃后的纷乱中，领主穆塔哈尔滕投靠帖木儿，招来巴耶济德一世1401年的围攻。黑羊首领卡拉·优素福1419年夺城，因此1444年时埃尔津詹是黑羊治下的边镇，居民仍以亚美尼亚人为主。

白羊苏丹乌尊哈桑攻占埃尔津詹后重修了城堡。1473年8月11日，穆罕默德二世亲率大军，在城边平原的奥特卢克贝利迎战乌尊哈桑：哈桑之子泽伊内勒·米尔扎战死，哈桑本人靠让一个相貌相似的人替他掌旗才得以脱身，埃尔津詹随后归入奥斯曼。1500年夏，约七千名分属八个部族的奇兹尔巴什战士在此集结，前去投奔起兵之初的伊斯玛仪；1514年查尔迪兰战役后，塞利姆一世稳固领有此城。1516—1518年的首次人口调查记下二十个街区，七个穆斯林区、十三个基督徒区；苏莱曼一世远征大不里士时也曾两度在此停留。1647年埃夫利亚·切莱比到访时，城堡孤悬在旷野平川上，周围约有两千户人家、四十八个街区，十一座浴室迎送着往来商队。

en:
Mush lies on the high Armenian plain of Taron, beneath the northeastern slopes of Çavuş Mountain at about 1,250 metres; winters are long and the plain lies under morning fog for much of the year, and Armenian writers derive the town's name from mshush, the word for fog. Between the tenth and thirteenth centuries it was an Armenian town of 20,000 people or more. Thirty kilometres to the northwest stood Surb Karapet, the Holy Precursor, founded in tradition by Gregory the Illuminator over relics of John the Baptist; from the twelfth century it was the seat of the bishops of Taron and was counted the foremost monastery of western Armenia, second only to Etchmiadzin. Mongol wars in the 1340s left Mush half ruined and Timur's forces plundered the district around 1387. In 1444 a small fortress stood above the town: its Armenian townspeople and villagers lived under local beys within the Aq Qoyunlu border orbit, while Muslim pastoral camps grazed the surrounding plain.

The Venetian Giosafat Barbaro, passing through in the 1470s, saw a crowded town of some three miles' circuit beneath a strong little castle. Mush later followed Bitlis into the Safavid orbit and, after Selim I's victory at Chaldiran in 1514, passed to the Ottomans; its government then moved back and forth between the Kurdish beys of Bitlis and Ottoman officials. In the eighteenth century Alaaddin Bey ruled Mush on behalf of Bitlis but defeated the troops Bitlis sent against him, until the governor of Erzurum, Çeteci Abdullah Pasha, intervened in 1754. In 1821 Qajar troops under Abbas Mirza captured and damaged the town.
zh:
穆什位于亚美尼亚塔龙高原、恰武什山东北坡下，海拔约1250米，冬季漫长，一年中很多清晨平原都笼罩在雾气里，亚美尼亚学者把城名与意为「雾」的mshush一词联系起来。10至13世纪间，这里已是一座有两万以上人口的亚美尼亚城镇。城西北三十公里处的圣卡拉佩特修道院（Surb Karapet，意为圣先驱），相传由启蒙者格列高利所建，用以安置施洗约翰的遗骨；12世纪起它是塔龙主教的座堂，被视为西亚美尼亚最重要的修道院，地位仅次于埃奇米阿津。14世纪40年代蒙古诸埃米尔的争战使穆什大半残破，1387年前后帖木儿的军队又劫掠这一带。1444年，城镇上方仍有一座小要塞：亚美尼亚居民在地方贝伊治下处于白羊王朝边境势力范围，平原四周则是穆斯林游牧营地。

15世纪70年代，威尼斯人巴尔巴罗路过此地，见到坚固小堡下一座周长约三英里、人烟稠密的城镇。穆什后来随比特利斯进入萨法维势力范围，1514年塞利姆一世在恰尔德兰获胜后转入奥斯曼之手，此后治权长期在比特利斯库尔德贝伊与奥斯曼直辖官员之间来回。18世纪，阿拉丁贝伊代比特利斯管辖穆什，却击败了比特利斯派来的军队，埃尔祖鲁姆总督切特吉·阿卜杜拉帕夏只得于1754年出兵介入。1821年，阿巴斯·米尔扎率领的卡扎尔军队攻占并破坏了穆什。

en:
Van stands on the eastern shore of Lake Van, beneath the long rock ridge that carries Van Castle. The lake is the great saline soda lake of the Armenian highlands, 1,640 metres above the sea and with no outlet. The rock was ancient Tushpa, capital of Urartu; on a smoothed face above the fortress the Achaemenid king Xerxes had a trilingual inscription cut in Old Persian, Babylonian and Elamite, twenty-seven lines in each column and still legible. Van later became the centre of the Armenian kingdom of Vaspurakan, and in 915-921 King Gagik I Artsruni built the Cathedral of the Holy Cross on the island of Aghtamar of pink volcanic tufa; it became the seat of the catholicos of Aghtamar. The last Artsruni king ceded Vaspurakan to Byzantium in 1021, and Seljuk, Ahlatshah, Ayyubid and Hakkari rule followed before Timur besieged the town in 1387. In 1444 Cihan Shah's Kara Koyunlu held the upper hand around the lake, while the walled old town below the rock was a highland frontier market where Armenian traders lived under Kurdish lords and Turcoman garrisons.

The Safavids took Van from the Hakkari Kurds in 1507 and lost it to Ottoman troops after Chaldiran in 1515, only to win it back. A ten-day Ottoman siege in 1548 retook the town and the Van eyalet was formed that year; the Peace of Amasya confirmed the conquest in 1555. A Safavid army besieged the fortress again in 1633 and withdrew after defeat in a battle outside the walls, and the Treaty of Zuhab in 1639 fixed the frontier and left Van to the Ottomans. It did not change hands again: until 1821 the rock remained the seat of an eastern frontier governor, a garrison on the road into Iran.
zh:
凡城位于凡湖东岸，城堡坐落在一道狭长的岩山上。凡湖是亚美尼亚高地上的咸水碱湖，湖面海拔1640米，没有出口。岩山古称图什帕，曾是乌拉尔图王国的都城；要塞上方一块削平的岩壁上刻着波斯王薛西斯的三语铭文，用古波斯文、巴比伦文和埃兰文各刻二十七行，字迹仍可辨认。凡城后来成为亚美尼亚瓦斯普拉坎王国的中心，915至921年，加吉克一世·阿尔茨鲁尼在阿赫塔马尔岛上以粉红色火山凝灰岩建起圣十字教堂，这里后来成为阿赫塔马尔卡托利科斯的驻地。末代阿尔茨鲁尼国王1021年把瓦斯普拉坎割让给拜占庭，之后历经塞尔柱、阿赫拉特沙赫、阿尤布和哈卡里统治，1387年帖木儿曾围攻凡城。1444年，吉汉沙的黑羊王朝在凡湖一带占优，岩山下有城墙的旧城是高地边境市场，亚美尼亚商人处在库尔德贝伊和土库曼驻军之间。

1507年，萨法维人从哈卡里库尔德人手中夺取凡城，1515年恰尔德兰战役后被奥斯曼军队攻占，后又被萨法维收回。1548年，奥斯曼军队经十天围城再度攻取，同年设立凡城埃亚莱特，1555年的《阿马西亚和约》确认了这次征服。1633年，萨法维军队再度围城，在城外战败后撤围；1639年的《席林堡条约》划定边界，凡城归奥斯曼。此后凡城再未易手，直到1821年，岩山要塞始终是东部边境总督的治所，也是通往伊朗道路上的驻军重镇。

en:
Urfa, the ancient Edessa, stands on a plain about eighty kilometres east of the Euphrates, where the roads from Diyarbakır, Mardin and Raqqa lead on to Aleppo. The crusaders made it their first state, the County of Edessa, in 1098; when Imad al-Din Zengi of Mosul stormed the walls in December 1144 the news brought on the Second Crusade, and the Christian town never recovered from the second siege two years later. Below the citadel lies the fish pool of Balıklıgöl, where Jewish and Muslim tradition says Nimrod cast Abraham into a fire and God turned the flames into the pool and the logs into carp; a cave beside it is shown as Abraham's birthplace. In 1444 the town was a Sunni Aq Qoyunlu garrison on the confederation's western frontier, its walls and the Aleppo road worth more than its market.

Uzun Hasan beat his Aq Qoyunlu rivals near Urfa and had the citadel repaired before a Mamluk army under Yashbak min Mahdi bombarded the walls during Ramadan in 1480; the besiegers were destroyed outside the town and their commander was later executed. Urfa passed to Selim I after Marj Dabiq in 1516 and was soon entered in the Ottoman tax registers, becoming the exchange between Iran and Aleppo; mid-sixteenth-century registers counted 13,000 to 14,000 inhabitants. In 1599 the rebel Karayazıcı Abdulhalim seized the citadel, declared himself sultan and had coins melted into bullets before imperial troops retook the inner fortress in street fighting. Murad IV restored the citadel on his march against Baghdad in 1638. When Evliya Çelebi came in 1646 he counted twenty-two mosques and four hundred shops, and noted the town's yellow morocco leather and cotton cloth, wares the French traveller Tavernier also praised.
zh:
