乌尔法古称埃德萨，位于幼发拉底河以东约八十公里的平原，迪亚巴克尔、马尔丁和拉卡通往阿勒颇的道路都在此会合。1098年，十字军把这里建成最早的十字军国家埃德萨伯国；1144年12月，摩苏尔的伊马德丁·赞吉攻破城墙，消息传回欧洲，直接引出第二次十字军东征，而两年后的第二次围城使这座基督教古城再未恢复元气。城堡脚下是鱼湖（Balıklıgöl），相传宁录把亚伯拉罕投入火堆，真主使火焰化成池水、木柴化成鲤鱼，湖畔一个洞穴被指为亚伯拉罕的出生地。1444年，乌尔法是白羊部落联盟西境的逊尼派戍城，城墙和阿勒颇商路比市集更要紧。

乌尊·哈桑在乌尔法附近击败白羊各部对手，下令修缮城堡。1480年，马穆鲁克将领亚什巴克（Yashbak）在斋月间以重炮轰击城墙，结果围城军在城外被歼，他后来被处死。1516年达比克草原战役后，乌尔法并入谢里姆一世的版图，很快进入奥斯曼税册，成为伊朗与阿勒颇之间的转运市场，十六世纪中叶的税册所记人口已有1.3万至1.4万。1599年，起事者卡拉亚泽哲·阿卜杜勒哈利姆占据城堡，自称苏丹，还把钱币熔成弹丸，官军最后经巷战才夺回内城。穆拉德四世1638年进军巴格达时下令修缮城堡。1646年埃夫利亚·切莱比到访，数出二十二座清真寺和四百家店铺，还记下当地的黄色山羊皮革与棉布，法国旅行家塔韦尼耶也称赞过这些物产。

en:
Sinjar is the market town just south of the Sinjar Mountains, a hundred-kilometre ridge that rises alone out of the steppe between Mosul, Rakka and the Khabur. The mountains are sacred to the Yazidis, who hold that Noah's ark came to rest on their highest peak after the Flood, and the ridge has given them refuge in every persecution. The town below entered its best centuries after 1107 under Turkmen atabegs and a junior line of the Zengids. A double wall ringed mosques, six madrasas, Sufi lodges and bathhouses whose mosaic floors and octagonal stone pools moved the geographer al-Qazwini to call the town 'little Damascus'; the minaret of its congregational mosque was raised in 1201, and Ibn Battuta later found the people to be Kurds, 'brave and generous', with a perennial stream running around the Friday mosque. The Mongols broke both walls and the shrine of Ali in 1262, and Badr al-Din Lu'lu' of Mosul had earlier campaigned against the Yazidis of the ridge. In 1444 Sinjar stood on the Qara Qoyunlu frontier below highlands that no lowland ruler fully controlled.

The Safavids took Sinjar in 1507 or 1508, and Ottoman forces captured it in 1534 during the war with Shah Tahmasp; it became the seat of a sanjak in Diyarbekir province, though the tax registers ran only to the foot of the hills. When Evliya Celebi visited in the seventeenth century, Kurds and Arabs of the Banu Tayy lived in the town, while he put the Yazidi and Baburi Kurds of the mountains at 45,000, ruled by their own chiefs. Those chiefs kept the ridge outside regular state control for centuries, and even the troops of Dawud Pasha of Baghdad, sent against the highlanders in the early nineteenth century, failed to subdue them.
zh:
辛贾尔是辛贾尔山正南的一座商镇，那道山岭长约百公里，孤零零隆起在摩苏尔、拉卡和哈布尔河之间的草原上。山岭是雅兹迪人的圣地，他们相信洪水之后诺亚方舟就停在最高的峰顶；每逢迫害，山脊就是他们的避难地。1107年以后，山下的城镇在土库曼阿塔贝格和赞吉王朝支系统治下进入最兴盛的几个世纪。双层城墙之内有清真寺、六座伊斯兰学校、苏菲道堂和澡堂，澡堂铺着镶嵌画地面、砌着八角石池，地理学家卡兹维尼因而把这里称作「小大马士革」。聚礼清真寺的宣礼塔建于1201年；伊本·白图泰后来见到城中居民是库尔德人，称他们「勇敢而慷慨」，还有一条四季不涸的溪水绕着聚礼清真寺流过。1262年，蒙古人攻破双层城墙，毁掉了阿里圣祠；更早的时候，摩苏尔的巴德尔丁·鲁卢还亲自带兵攻打过山里的雅兹迪人。1444年，辛贾尔是黑羊王朝边疆上的城镇，城后是没有任何低地君主真正控制的山岭。

1507或1508年，辛贾尔被萨法维王朝攻取；1534年，奥斯曼军队在与塔赫玛斯普沙阿的战争中拿下该城，它成为迪亚巴克尔省一个桑贾克的治所，但税册只能管到山脚。17世纪埃夫利亚·切莱比到访时，城里住着库尔德人和巴努·塔伊部的阿拉伯人，他估计山中的雅兹迪库尔德人与巴布里库尔德人有四万五千之众，由各自的首领管辖。这些首领让山岭长期游离在国家的常规控制之外，19世纪初巴格达的达乌德帕夏派兵进山，也没能征服这些山民。

en:
Tikrit is a walled citadel-town on the west bank of the Tigris, guarding the river road and the crossing between Mosul and Baghdad. From the sixth century it was one of the great cities of Miaphysite Christianity: the maphrian had his seat here, with an authority reaching as far as Central Asia, and the Green Church was the see's great cathedral. A Muslim governor had the cathedral pulled down in 1089; it was rebuilt, but in 1156 the maphrian withdrew to Mosul. The town kept its place in Muslim history as the birthplace of Saladin, born here around 1138. Ibn Jubayr, passing in 1188, found a large town of markets and mosques with the Tigris running beneath its walls, until Timur's army stormed and wrecked it in 1393. In 1444 it was a half-ruined fortress town of Sunni Arabs under the Qara Qoyunlu, living by passing river trade and by herds in the dry country behind it.

It passed with Iraq to the Aq Qoyunlu in 1469 and to Shah Ismail's Safavids in 1508, and in 1534 it fell to Suleiman the Magnificent's Ottoman army marching down the Tigris to Baghdad. Under Ottoman rule it shrank to a small settlement, counted for a time within the Rakka Eyalet, its population never rising above four or five thousand. The old Christian community, which had supplied the Syriac Orthodox Church with patriarchs, theologians and translators, had vanished altogether by the seventeenth century. Tikrit lived on as a small fortified crossing-place between Baghdad and Mosul.
zh:
提克里特是底格里斯河西岸的城墙要塞城，扼守摩苏尔与巴格达之间的河路与渡口。6世纪起，它是基督一性论派的重镇：马弗里安总主教驻跸于此，教权所及远至中亚，城中的绿教堂是教座的大堂。1089年，穆斯林总督下令拆毁绿教堂；大堂后来虽得重建，马弗里安还是在1156年迁往摩苏尔。萨拉丁约于1138年出生在这里，是这座城最著名的人物。1188年伊本·朱拜尔路过时，见到的仍是一座市场与清真寺众多的大城，底格里斯河从城下流过；1393年帖木儿的军队攻破并摧毁了它。1444年，这里是黑羊王朝治下一座半毁的逊尼派阿拉伯要塞城镇，居民靠过境河运和城外旱地的牧群为生。

此后它随伊拉克先后于1469年归入白羊王朝、1508年归入沙阿·伊斯玛仪的萨法维王朝；1534年，苏莱曼一世的奥斯曼大军沿底格里斯河南征巴格达，提克里特随之易手。奥斯曼时期，它萎缩成一座小聚落，曾一度被划入拉卡行省，人口从未超过四五千。这个曾为叙利亚正教会贡献宗主教、神学家和翻译家的古老基督徒社群，到17世纪已完全消失。此后的提克里特只是底格里斯河上一个筑有城堡的小渡口，夹在巴格达与摩苏尔之间。

en:
This mid-Euphrates province holds Najaf, on the desert rim west of Kufa, and Samawah downriver among the palm groves. Najaf grew around the tomb of Ali ibn Abi Talib, the first Shia imam; Shia tradition holds that Adam and Noah lie buried at his side, and the town ranks with Mecca, Medina and Jerusalem among the four holy places of Shia Islam. Harun al-Rashid raised the first mausoleum over the tomb around 790, and in 979 the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla walled the town and brought it Euphrates water by a qanat. Ibn Battuta in 1326 saw silk carpets, gold and silver candelabra, and dishes of rose-water and musk for pilgrims to bless themselves with. A fire destroyed the shrine in 1354 and the Jalairid sultan Shaikh Awais rebuilt it. Beside the town stretched Wadi al-Salaam, the greatest burial ground of the Shia world, where families brought their dead to lie near Ali, and its seminary was already one of the oldest schools of Shia law. At Samawah, caravans and river craft crossed the Euphrates through the date palms and carried Basra's Indian spices north. In 1444 the country belonged to the Black Sheep (Qara Qoyunlu) Turkomans, who ruled Iraq from Tabriz under Jahan Shah.

The Black Sheep confederation fell to Uzun Hasan's White Sheep (Aq Qoyunlu), and in 1508 Shah Ismail swept into Iraq, prayed at Ali's tomb and made the land Safavid. Suleiman came in person after his first Persian campaign and sent rich gifts to the shrine. Its present form is the work of Shah Abbas I, who visited Najaf twice and in 1623 set five hundred men to rebuilding the sanctuary; the work was finished under his grandson Shah Safi in 1632, with a new dome, a hospital, kitchens and pilgrim hospices around the courtyard. Sultan Murad IV's capture of Baghdad in 1638 and the peace that followed left Iraq in Ottoman hands. The gilding came a century later from Nader Shah, who had the dome and minarets covered in gold in 1742 while his wife paid for the walls and courtyard; three years on, the great iwan was rebuilt in nine tiers of gilded muqarnas. Carsten Niebuhr passed through in 1765, the first European to leave an account of Najaf, while Samawah's covered Suq al-Masgoof kept serving the river traders through these centuries.
zh:
这片幼发拉底河中游省份有两处要地：库法以西沙漠边缘的纳杰夫，和下游椰枣林中的塞马沃。纳杰夫围绕阿里·伊本·阿比·塔利卜的陵墓兴起，阿里是什叶派第一位伊玛目；按什叶派说法，阿丹和努哈也安葬在他身旁，纳杰夫与麦加、麦地那和耶路撒冷并称什叶派四大圣地。哈伦·拉希德约在790年在墓上建起第一座陵殿；979年，白益埃米尔阿杜德·道拉为城镇筑墙，并用坎儿井引来幼发拉底河水。伊本·白图泰1326年到此，看到丝毯铺地、金银烛台环绕灵位，还有盛着玫瑰水和麝香的盘盏供朝圣者沾抹祈福。1354年圣陵毁于大火，贾拉伊尔王朝苏丹谢赫·奥韦斯将其重建。城边铺展着和平谷，这是什叶派世界最大的墓地，信徒把家人送来安葬在阿里身旁；这里的经学院也是什叶派最古老的教法学校之一。塞马沃一带，商队和河船在椰枣林间横渡幼发拉底河，把巴士拉的印度香料运往北方。1444年，这片土地属于黑羊（喀拉衮鲁）土库曼人，贾汉·沙在大不里士统辖伊拉克。

黑羊王朝败于乌尊·哈桑的白羊（阿克衮鲁）王朝；1508年，沙阿伊斯玛仪攻入伊拉克，到阿里墓前祈祷，此地归入萨法维。苏莱曼一世第一次波斯战役后亲临圣陵，送来厚礼。圣陵现存的格局成于沙阿阿拔斯一世：他两度到访纳杰夫，1623年派出五百人重修圣所，工程在其孙沙阿萨菲治下的1632年完工，庭院周围新增穹顶、医院、厨房和接待朝圣者的客栈。1638年穆拉德四世攻占巴格达，随后的和约确认伊拉克归奥斯曼所有。贴金在一个世纪后由纳迪尔沙完成：1742年他下令为穹顶和宣礼塔包金，他的妻子出资重修围墙和庭院；三年后，大伊万又改建成九层镀金钟乳拱。1765年，卡斯滕·尼布尔途经纳杰夫，成为首位留下文字记载的欧洲人；塞马沃带顶棚的马斯古夫市场则在这些世纪里继续接待往来河商。

en:
Wasit means 'middle', for the site its founder chose halfway between Kufa and Basra on the Tigris. The Umayyad viceroy al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf built it around 702 as the garrison capital of Iraq, and even the doors of its citadel and Friday mosque were carried off from the conquered town of Zanzaward; al-Hajjaj himself died there in 714. In 1327 Ibn Battuta still found fine quarters and abundant orchards, but the old canals were silting and the Tigris was shifting west, and by the sixteenth century the city, a brick-built circuit sixteen kilometres around, stood empty. Its countryside lived on. Black-earth villages along the Shatt al-Gharraf grew wheat and barley for Baghdad and Basra, carpet dealers traded at the bend where the canal leaves the Tigris, and farther south boat-dwelling Arab tribes kept to their reed marshes and answered to no outside master. In 1444 the plain was held for the Black Sheep Turkomans from Tabriz.

The Black Sheep gave way to the White Sheep, and in 1508 to the Safavids of Shah Ismail. Suleiman's army came down the Tigris in 1534 and made the district an Ottoman march of Baghdad province, its grain barges feeding the garrisons; tax collectors and soldiers repeatedly pushed into the marshes after tribes that raided the river road and vanished among the reeds. Sultan Murad IV retook Baghdad in 1638, and the frontier fixed by the next year's peace left the grain barges and the carpet market at the Gharraf bend to trade on without further war.
zh:
瓦西特意为「中间」，得名于建城者选定的位置：底格里斯河上库法与巴士拉之间的中点。倭马亚朝的伊拉克总督哈查只·伊本·优素福约在702年把它建为伊拉克的驻军首府，连城堡和主麻清真寺的大门都是从一座被征服的城市拆运来的，哈查只本人也于714年死在这座城里。1327年伊本·白图泰到此，仍见整洁的街区和丰饶的果园，但古渠已经淤塞，底格里斯河也在向西改道；到16世纪，这座周长十六公里的砖筑之城终告荒废。它的乡野却延续了下来：盖拉夫渠两岸的黑土村庄为巴格达和巴士拉种植小麦和大麦，渠口分出的河湾边有地毯商交易，更南边栖身舟中的阿拉伯部落守着芦苇沼泽，不承认外来的主人。1444年，这片平原由大不里士的黑羊土库曼人统治。

黑羊之后是白羊，1508年又归沙阿伊斯玛仪的萨法维王朝。1534年苏莱曼的大军沿底格里斯河南下，把这里变成奥斯曼巴格达省的边地，粮船为各处要塞供粮；税吏和士兵一再进入沼泽，追剿那些劫掠河路、随即隐没在芦苇间的部落。1638年穆拉德四世收复巴格达，次年和约划定边界，盖拉夫河湾的粮船和地毯市集在余下的奥斯曼岁月里未再遭兵燹。

en:
Antioch on the Orontes fills the south-western corner of the fertile Amuq plain, where the road down from Anatolia enters Syria. Seleucus I founded it in 300 BC as a capital of his Seleucid empire, and at its Roman peak perhaps half a million people lived here, third only to Rome and Alexandria. It was one of the five patriarchal cities of the early Church: the book of Acts says the disciples were first called Christians here, and a cliff-cut cave church where Peter was said to have preached drew pilgrims from the fourth century. Earthquakes, above all the one in 526, and long frontier wars broke its power. The First Crusade took it after an eight-month siege in 1098 and set up the Latin Principality of Antioch; when the Emperor Frederick Barbarossa drowned on the Third Crusade, his son Frederick had his remains buried in the cathedral of St Peter. The Mamluk sultan Baybars stormed the city on 18 May 1268, promised its people quarter and then killed or enslaved most of its Christians, and the Mongol-era Black Sea trade route carried off its commerce. In 1432 a visitor counted only about three hundred inhabited houses inside the walls. In 1444 Antioch was a small Mamluk market town living among its own ruins, with most of its traffic gone to the newer harbour of Alexandretta; pilgrims still came to the Habib-i Nejjar mosque, said to hold the tomb of the carpenter Habib named in the Quran's surah Ya-Sin.

The Ottomans took Antioch after Marj Dabiq in 1516 and made it a sanjak under Aleppo. Its one great battlefield of these centuries lay on the Amuq plain below the walls: in October 1607 the grand vizier Kuyucu Murad Pasha routed the rebel army of Ali Janbulad, the Kurdish governor of Aleppo, who had sworn a secret alliance with the Grand Duke of Tuscany against the sultan and for a time commanded all of northern Syria. Janbulad escaped the field, was pardoned the next year, and was arrested at Belgrade and executed there in 1610. An English naval chaplain riding out from Aleppo in 1675 found a quiet, half-ruined place of patched walls and tumbled columns, its bazaars selling soap and the farm produce of the surrounding plain. From the middle of the eighteenth century Alawite settlers from the hills around Latakia began moving into the district.
zh:
奥龙特斯河畔的安条克位于肥沃的阿米克平原西南角，安纳托利亚南下入叙的大道从这里经过。塞琉古一世公元前300年建城，作为塞琉古帝国的都城；罗马鼎盛时城中约有五十万人，规模仅次于罗马和亚历山大。它是早期基督教五大牧首驻地之一：《使徒行传》记载，「基督徒」这一称呼最早就出现在安条克；崖壁中凿出的圣彼得洞窟教堂，相传彼得曾在此讲道，从4世纪起便有朝圣者前来。526年的大地震和数百年边境战事耗尽了它的国力。第一次十字军围攻八个月，于1098年拿下此城，建立拉丁人的安条克亲王国；皇帝腓特烈一世（巴巴罗萨）在第三次十字军途中溺亡后，其子腓特烈将他的遗骸葬入圣彼得主教座堂。1268年5月18日，马穆鲁克苏丹拜巴尔斯破城，他先前许诺饶命，随后却把城中基督徒大部杀死或掳为奴；蒙古时代通往黑海的商路又带走了它的生意。1432年一位访客数过，城墙之内仅余约三百户有人居住的房屋。1444年的安条克是马穆鲁克治下一座寄居在废墟间的小集镇，商贸大多流向较新的亚历山大勒塔港；仍有朝圣者前来哈比卜·内贾尔清真寺，相传《古兰经》雅辛章提到的木匠哈比卜就安葬在那里。

1516年达比克草原战役后，奥斯曼人取得安条克，设为阿勒颇省下的一个桑贾克。这一时期这里唯一的一场大战就在城下的阿米克平原：1607年10月，大维齐尔库尤朱·穆拉德帕夏击溃阿里·詹布拉德的叛军。这位库尔德出身的阿勒颇总督曾与托斯卡纳大公秘密结盟反对苏丹，一度号令整个叙利亚北部。詹布拉德兵败逃脱，次年获赦，最终在贝尔格莱德被捕，1610年就地处决。1675年，一名从阿勒颇骑马前来的英国海军牧师看到的是一座安静的半废城镇，城墙经过修补，断柱散落各处，市集上出售肥皂和四乡的农产品。18世纪中叶起，拉塔基亚一带山区的阿拉维派信徒开始迁入这一地区。

en:
The Rahba country is the stretch of the middle Euphrates below the Sinjar steppe: Deir ez-Zor sits at the river crossing, and the citadel of al-Rahba rises on a mound in the desert a day's march downstream near Mayadin. Ibn Battuta called it 'the end of Iraq and the beginning of Syria'; caravans out of Iraq made it their first halt on the road to Aleppo or Damascus, and its masters held what one historian called the key to Syria and sometimes to Iraq. The Abbasid general Malik ibn Tawk founded the fortress in the ninth century as Rahbat Malik ibn Tawk. After the earthquake of 1157 Shirkuh built a new castle on the desert edge, and his grandson Shirkuh II rebuilt it in 1207. From the 1260s the Mamluks kept al-Rahba as their chief bulwark on the Euphrates against the Mongols, an administrative centre where the postal road from Egypt ended; the Ilkhan Oljaitu's month-long siege of 1312-13 failed, and the Mongols never tested that frontier again. In 1444 the garrison watched the Mamluk eastern marches while the Al Fadl Bedouin ran the caravans, flocks and raids along the desert edge.

Sultan Selim I entered al-Rahba in 1516. Under Ottoman rule the desert wars ended and the Palmyra road lost its traffic, so the fortress decayed; when the Venetian Gasparo Balbi saw it in 1588 the walls were dilapidated and Rahabi villagers lived below them. The Ottomans nevertheless kept the district as the sanjak of Deyr-Rahbe, which included Deir ez-Zor, and for most of the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries they named emirs of the Al Abu Risha, descendants of the Al Fadl, as both governors and desert emirs to guard the Aleppo-Baghdad road. When Guillaume-Antoine Olivier passed in 1797 the citadel was a ruin used by shepherds, while small riverine settlements such as Deir ez-Zor lived by the crossing, the grain fields and the caravan trade.
zh:
拉巴地方是辛贾尔草原下方的一段幼发拉底河中游：代尔祖尔在河的渡口上，拉赫巴堡则在下游约一天路程的沙漠土丘上，靠近马亚丁。伊本·白图泰说这里是「伊拉克的尽头、叙利亚的开端」；从伊拉克往阿勒颇或大马士革去的商队把这里当作第一站，它的主人握着一位史家所说的「叙利亚的钥匙，有时也是伊拉克的钥匙」。9世纪，阿拔斯将领马利克·本·陶格修建这座要塞，人称「马利克·本·陶格的拉赫巴」。1157年地震后，希尔库在沙漠边缘另筑新堡，他的孙子希尔库二世1207年又加以重建。1260年代起，马穆鲁克把拉赫巴作为幼发拉底河上抵御蒙古人的首要壁垒和行政中心，从埃及伸来的驿路以此为终点；1312至1313年，伊儿汗完者都围攻一个月未能得手，蒙古人此后再没有试探这条边防线。1444年，驻军守望着马穆鲁克的东部边疆，阿勒法德勒部贝都因人则经营着沙漠边缘的商队、羊群和袭掠。

1516年，塞利姆一世进入拉赫巴。奥斯曼治下沙漠里的战争结束，巴尔米拉道路失去了商队，要塞随之败落；1588年威尼斯人加斯帕罗·巴尔比见到它时，城墙已经残破，拉赫比村民住在墙下。奥斯曼人仍把这一带设为代尔-拉赫巴桑贾克，把代尔祖尔也划在其中；16到18世纪的大部分时间里，他们任命出自阿勒法德勒后裔的阿布·里沙家族埃米尔为总督兼沙漠埃米尔，守护阿勒颇至巴格达的商路。1797年纪尧姆-安托万·奥利维耶经过时，要塞已成牧羊人栖身的废墟；代尔祖尔这类河滨小聚落则靠渡口、粮田和商队贸易过活。

en:
Suez sits at the head of the Gulf of Suez, where the road from Cairo ends at the Red Sea. Just to the north stood Qulzum, the Roman Clysma and the eastern end of the canal dug by Amr ibn al-As to link the Nile with the Red Sea. The caliph al-Mansur closed it in 770 to cut supplies reaching his enemies in Arabia, and the town's trade withered. Saladin later fortified Qulzum and Suez after Raynald of Chatillon brought ships into the Red Sea in 1183-84 and tried to deny the garrison its water; a fleet built for Saladin's brother al-Adil sailed to Aydhab and put an end to the venture. By the thirteenth century Qulzum was a ruin and the smaller settlement of Suez had taken its place. In 1444, under the Mamluk sultans, Egyptian shipwrights still used the roadstead, caravans carried Sinai acacia timber to Cairo, and the port joined Egypt to Arabia and the Indian Ocean trade for all its lack of fresh water.

The Portuguese in the Indian Ocean turned Suez into a front-line base. A Qulzum merchant fleet sailed against them off western India in 1505, and in 1507 Sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri posted Selman Reis there with 6,000 men, a commitment that weakened the Mamluk fleet facing the Ottomans in the Mediterranean. After 1517 the Ottomans made Suez a naval arsenal, and in 1541 Estevao and Cristovao da Gama entered the Red Sea with 80 ships and 2,300 soldiers, sacked Suakin, and sent 16 light galleys with 250 picked men against the port; Davud Pasha's forewarned gunners drove them off. The Portuguese spent seven months cruising the Red Sea while Muslim shipping stayed in port, then sailed back to India. In the eighteenth century about twenty ships still left each year for Jeddah, but by the French invasion of 1798 Suez had shrunk to a backwater, and the fighting of 1800 left most of the town in ruins.
zh:
苏伊士坐落在苏伊士湾顶端，是从开罗通往红海的道路入海之处。城北不远处曾是古勒祖姆，即罗马时代的克利斯马，也是阿姆鲁·本·阿斯开凿的尼罗河—红海运河东端。770年，哈里发曼苏尔为切断阿拉伯半岛上的敌人从埃及取得补给，关闭了运河，城镇贸易随之凋敝。1183—1184年，沙蒂永的雷纳德将战舰驶入红海，企图断绝古勒祖姆守军的水源，萨拉丁于是加固古勒祖姆和苏伊士的工事；他兄弟阿迪勒下令建造的舰队后来驶往阿伊扎卜，终结了这场袭掠。到13世纪，古勒祖姆已成废墟，较小的苏伊士聚落取而代之。1444年，在马穆鲁克苏丹治下，埃及造船工匠仍使用这片锚地，商队把西奈的相思树木材运往开罗；尽管淡水匮乏，这个港口仍把埃及同阿拉伯半岛和印度洋贸易连在一起。

葡萄牙人进入印度洋后，苏伊士成了前沿军港。1505年，一支古勒祖姆商船队驶往印度西海岸对葡萄牙人作战；1507年，苏丹甘萨维·古里派塞尔曼·赖斯率6000人驻守此地，这笔投入也削弱了马穆鲁克在地中海上对抗奥斯曼的舰队。1517年以后，奥斯曼人把苏伊士建成海军兵工厂和军港。1541年，埃斯特旺·达伽马和克里斯托旺·达伽马率80艘船、2300名士兵进入红海，洗劫萨瓦金后派出16艘轻快桨船、250名精兵进攻港口，却被达乌德帕夏早有准备的炮火击退。葡萄牙人在红海游弋七个月，穆斯林商船只得停在港内，舰队随后返回印度。18世纪时，每年仍有约20艘船驶往吉达，但到1798年法国入侵时，苏伊士已缩为一座偏僻小港，1800年的战事更使全城大半化为废墟。

en:
Al-Gharbiyya, 'the western land,' fills the middle of the Nile Delta between the Rosetta and Damietta branches. Its canals carried wheat, rice and flax from hundreds of tax villages toward Cairo, and the river town of al-Mahalla al-Kubra was made the provincial seat by the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad in 1320. The place that outgrew them all was Tanta. Ahmad al-Badawi, a Sufi born in Fez, settled there about 1237 and gathered forty disciples, who were said to dwell on the city's rooftops; his Badawiyya order spread across Egypt, and after his death in 1276 his tomb became one of the country's most visited shrines. His birthday festival drew merchants, dervishes and villagers by the thousand, turning Tanta into one of the great Delta fairs. In 1444 Gharbiyya was a rich Mamluk granary run through cavalry fiefs and tax farmers, with no single ruling city.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517 the old Mamluk fief-holders kept much of their power and the festival ran on. Ali Bey al-Kabir, the Mamluk strongman who ruled Egypt in the 1760s, built the Ahmadi shrine mosque over the tomb, paid its teachers and students, and endowed shops and caravanserais where Indian cloth and Yemeni coffee were sold; the Ottoman traveller Evliya Celebi counted seven caravanserais and forty mosques in the town. On 7 October 1798 a French battalion under General Le Fevre entered Tanta while the festival was under way; the governor Salim al-Shurbagi called the pilgrims to arms and the townspeople drove the French out. The battalion returned three days later, shelled and occupied the town, and laid heavy fines on the shrine and its people. The French left Egypt in 1801, and Muhammad Ali's Delta reorganization of 1813 kept Tanta within Gharbiyya.
zh:
西部省意为「西方之地」，地处尼罗河三角洲中部，夹在罗塞塔河与杜姆亚特河之间。省内运河把数百座税村的小麦、稻米和亚麻运往开罗；1320年，马穆鲁克苏丹纳绥尔·穆罕默德把河畔城镇大迈哈莱定为行省治所。但最兴旺的地方是坦塔。苏非行者艾哈迈德·巴达维生于非斯，约1237年定居于此，收了四十名弟子，据说他们都在城中屋顶上栖身修行；他创立的巴达维教团传遍埃及，1276年他去世后，其陵墓成为埃及香火最盛的圣墓之一。他的圣纪节庆吸引成千上万的商人、托钵僧和乡民，坦塔借此成为三角洲最大的集市之一。1444年，西部省是马穆鲁克治下富庶的粮仓，由骑兵封地和包税人分掌，没有一座统辖全境的城市。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，旧马穆鲁克封地的主人仍保有大量权力，节庆也照办不误。18世纪60年代主政埃及的马穆鲁克强人阿里贝伊·卡比尔在圣墓上主持修建了艾哈迈迪圣寺，供养寺中师生，又出资开设商铺和商队客栈，市上能买到印度布匹和也门咖啡；奥斯曼旅行家艾弗里雅·切莱比在城中数出七座客栈和四十座清真寺。1798年10月7日，勒费弗尔将军率一营法军在节庆期间进入坦塔，地方长官萨利姆·舒尔巴吉号召朝觐者拿起武器，市民把法军逐出城外。三天后该营折返，炮击并占领坦塔，向圣寺和居民课以重罚。1801年法军撤出埃及；1813年穆罕默德·阿里重整三角洲，坦塔仍属西部省。

en:
Minya lies on the west bank of the Nile in Middle Egypt, the chief river landing between Cairo and the towns of Upper Egypt. Its older name, Munyat ibn Khasib, commemorates the Abbasid governor who enlarged the village in the early ninth century and retired to die there. Under the Fatimids it acquired bazaars, baths and the Amrawy and Lamaty mosques, and Ibn Battuta, stopping in 1326, wrote that Minya 'excels all the other towns of Upper Egypt'. Near Samalut the monastery of Gebel el-Teir holds a rock-cut church that Coptic tradition credits to the Empress Helena and numbers among the halts of the Holy Family in Egypt. Sugarcane was the cash crop of the district: Mamluk sources list Bahnasa, Ashmunayn and Mallawi among the cane villages of Upper Egypt, local presses boiled the harvest, and conical loaves of raw sugar went down the Nile to the refineries at Fustat; Burji sultans at times reserved the right to buy the crop. In 1444 Minya was a Burji Mamluk market town, living on Nile traffic, sugar and grain.

The last Mamluk sultan came this way in the Ottoman conquest of 1517. After his army broke at Ridanieh outside Cairo, Tuman Bay withdrew to Bahnasa in the Minya countryside, returned to fight his final battle by the Pyramids of Giza, and was betrayed to the Ottomans; he was hanged at Cairo's Bab Zuweila on 15 April 1517. Mamluk households kept much of their provincial power under Ottoman sovereignty. In 1798 and 1799 General Desaix pursued Murad Bey up the Nile through Middle Egypt and on into Upper Egypt, and the French withdrew after 1801. Muhammad Ali destroyed the remaining Mamluk chiefs in 1811.
zh:
明亚位于中埃及尼罗河西岸，是开罗与上埃及诸城之间最主要的河埠。它的旧称「穆尼亚特·伊本·哈西卜」得自9世纪初的阿拔斯王朝总督伊本·哈西卜，他把旧村扩建成城，晚年又退隐终老于此。法蒂玛王朝时期，明亚有了巴扎、公共浴室和阿姆拉维、拉马提两座清真寺；1326年伊本·白图泰途经此地，说明亚「胜过其他所有上埃及城镇」。塞马鲁特附近的泰尔山修道院有一座凿岩教堂，科普特传统认为它由海伦娜皇后下令开凿，也是圣家族逃埃途中停留过的地方。甘蔗是这一带的经济作物：马穆鲁克文献把拜哈纳萨、赫尔莫波利斯和迈莱维列为上埃及的甘蔗村，蔗坊就地榨煮，圆锥形的粗糖饼顺尼罗河运到福斯塔特的糖坊精炼；布尔吉王朝的苏丹有时还包买甘蔗。1444年，明亚是布尔吉马穆鲁克治下的集镇，靠尼罗河航运、蔗糖和粮食立足。

1517年奥斯曼入侵时，末代马穆鲁克苏丹曾途经此地。里达尼耶兵败开罗城外后，图曼贝伊二世退守明亚乡间的拜哈纳萨，后来又回到吉萨金字塔旁打了最后一仗，被人出卖给奥斯曼人，1517年4月15日在开罗的祖韦拉门被绞死。奥斯曼统治下，马穆鲁克家族仍保有大量地方势力。1798至1799年，德塞将军沿尼罗河追击穆拉德贝伊，穿过中埃及直入上埃及，法军则在1801年后撤离。1811年，穆罕默德·阿里诛灭了余下的马穆鲁克首领。

en:
Bahariya, the Northern Oasis, is a mountain-rimmed depression in the Western Desert southwest of the Fayyum, with about 400 cold and thermal, mineral and sulphur springs feeding date palms, olives and orchards around the villages of Bawiti and el-Qasr. The oasis was once famed for its wine: its oldest attested name, Djesdjes, also meant its celebrated vintage, and Theban tomb paintings show its people bringing wine, hides and mats as tribute while donkey caravans carried the casks to the Nile by two desert tracks. Greco-Roman rule put a garrison here, supplied from Oxyrhynchus on the Nile, the town later called Bahnasa, and the large fort at Qarat el-Toub guarded the oasis's northern edge. Coptic tradition recorded by Abu Salih sends the apostle Bartholomew to Bahariya to preach and even places his martyrdom there, though other accounts put his death on the coast; the oasis had its own bishop and kept a substantial Christian community into the sixteenth or seventeenth century. In 1444 it was a remote Mamluk possession, joined to the Nile through Bahnasa and to Farafra by a desert road, sending out dates and olive oil.

Ottoman sovereignty in 1517 changed the oasis little. Muhammad Ali laid claim to Bahariya together with Farafra and Hayz as early as 1813, exacted an annual tribute, and found he needed between 400 and 500 men to keep order there, a far larger garrison than Kharga required. In May 1819 Giovanni Belzoni, an Italian former circus strongman turned explorer, crossed from the Fayyum and became the first modern European known to reach the oasis; for a while he believed he had reached Siwa.
zh:
拜哈里耶意为「北方绿洲」，是西部沙漠中一处山岭环抱的洼地，位于法尤姆西南；约400处冷泉与温泉、矿泉与硫泉滋养着巴维提、盖斯尔等村周围的椰枣、橄榄和果园。葡萄酒曾是它最出名的出产：它最早见于记载的名字「杰斯杰斯」同时指当地的名酒，底比斯的墓画里还有绿洲居民进献葡萄酒、兽皮和席子的场面，驴队顺着两条沙漠道把成桶的酒运往尼罗河谷。希腊罗马时期，这里驻扎了军队，补给由尼罗河畔的俄克喜林库斯（即后来的拜哈纳萨）接应，卡拉特图卜的大军堡扼守绿洲北缘。据阿布·萨利赫记载，科普特相传使徒巴多罗买曾被派到拜哈里耶传教，甚至说他在此殉道，不过另一些记载称他死于海滨；当地有自己的主教，规模不小的基督徒社群一直延续到16或17世纪。1444年，它是马穆鲁克治下的遥远属地，经拜哈纳萨连通尼罗河谷，另有沙漠道通往费拉菲拉，外运椰枣和橄榄油。

1517年奥斯曼的宗主权覆盖到拜哈里耶，但绿洲没有多少变化。穆罕默德·阿里早在1813年就把拜哈里耶连同费拉菲拉和海兹收入版图，征收年贡，却要派驻四五百人才能维持秩序，所需驻军远比哈里杰为多。1819年5月，早年以马戏团大力士为生、后来成为探险家的意大利人乔瓦尼·贝尔佐尼从法尤姆穿越沙漠而来，是有记载的第一个抵达拜哈里耶的近代欧洲人，却一度以为自己到的是锡瓦。

en:
This stretch of the Nile valley runs from Manfalut and Asyut on the west bank to Akhmim on the east. Asyut was the Nile end of the Darb al-Arba'in, the Forty Days Road that came up from Darfur by way of the Kharga Oasis; in the fourteenth century a single caravan could bring 12,000 camels, with cattle, ivory, gold, ostrich feathers and slaves, out of the Sudan. Its weavers made crimson carpets fit to compare with Armenian work; Manfalut grew cotton and pomegranates; Akhmim kept the linen trade already noted by Strabo, and its covered bazaars and caravanserais served merchants and monks alike, for this was early monastic country: Pachomius founded a monastery near Akhmim in the fourth century, and Nestorius, the deposed patriarch of Constantinople, died in exile nearby. In 1444 the district belonged to the Mamluk sultan, and its river landings were busy with grain, carpets and linen bound for Cairo.

The Ottoman conquest of 1517 put a Cairo-appointed governor over the district without ending the rivalry of Mamluk beys and Bedouin houses for the caravan tolls. The Hawwara chief Humam ibn Yusuf counted these villages in the Upper Egyptian domain he held from Minya to Aswan in the 1760s, until Ali Bey al-Kabir's men burned Farshut and broke his power in 1769. The old road still carried traffic: the French physician Jacques-Charles Poncet travelled it in 1698, and William George Browne rode with a great Darfur caravan in 1793. After 1798 Desaix's French division passed up the Nile in pursuit of Murad Bey, and when the French withdrew in 1801 the river towns and caravan wells fell under the government of Muhammad Ali.
zh:
这一段尼罗河谷西起曼费卢特和艾斯尤特，东到艾赫米姆。艾斯尤特是四十日商路（Darb al-Arba'in）的尼罗河终点：商路从达尔富尔经哈里杰绿洲北上，14世纪时，一支商队最多能把一万二千峰骆驼连同牲畜、象牙、黄金、鸵鸟羽和奴隶从苏丹带到这里。当地织工织造足以媲美亚美尼亚货的绯红地毯；曼费卢特种棉花和石榴；艾赫米姆则延续着斯特拉波时代就已知名的亚麻织造，有顶市场和商队客栈同时接待商人与修士。这里是早期基督教修道的中心：4世纪帕科缪在艾赫米姆附近创立修道院，被废黜的君士坦丁堡牧首聂斯脱里也在流放中死于此地附近。1444年，这一地区归属马穆鲁克苏丹，河码头忙于把谷物、地毯和亚麻运往开罗。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，开罗派来的总督统辖此地，但马穆鲁克贝伊与贝都因家族对商路税卡的争夺并未停止。18世纪60年代，哈瓦拉首领胡马姆·伊本·优素福把这些村庄算作他从明亚到阿斯旺领地的一部分；1769年，阿里贝伊·卡比尔的部下焚毁法尔舒特，瓦解了他的势力。老路仍有旅人经过：法国医生雅克-夏尔·庞塞1698年取道于此，威廉·乔治·布朗1793年随一支达尔富尔大商队同行。1798年后，德塞的法国师溯尼罗河追击穆拉德贝伊，经过此地；1801年法军撤出后，这些河港城镇和商路水井都落入穆罕默德·阿里政府治下。

en: The shore around Ras Gharib runs along the African side of the Gulf of Suez, with the Red Sea Hills rising between the coast and the Nile. Inland, at Gebel Dokhan, the Romans worked the quarries of Mons Porphyrites from the first to the fifth century: discovered in AD 18 by Caius Cominus Leugas, they were the empire's only source of purple imperial porphyry. The highest workings lay more than 1,400 metres up the mountain, and cut blocks were dropped down slipways to five workers' villages in the wadi below, where a fort, cisterns, temples of Isis and Sarapis and a signal tower kept the settlement alive. The stone was hauled along a fortified road from Qena on the Nile to the coast fort of Abu Sha'ar, and went on to Rome and Constantinople for imperial buildings and sarcophagi before the quarries were abandoned in Byzantine times. In 1444 this was a remote Mamluk shore of fishing boats and passing Red Sea shipping rather than towns. It passed to the Ottomans with Egypt in 1517, and Estevao da Gama's Portuguese fleet sailed these waters on the way to its repulse at Suez in 1541 without leaving a garrison.
zh: 拉斯加里卜沿岸是苏伊士湾的非洲一侧海岸，红海山脉在海与尼罗河之间隆起。内陆的杰贝勒杜赫坎山中，罗马人从1世纪到5世纪开采波菲利特斯采石场：采石场于公元18年由盖乌斯·科米努斯·柳加斯发现，是罗马帝国境内唯一出产紫色帝王斑岩的地方。最高的矿点开在海拔1400多米处，切下的石块沿滑道溜到山下干河谷里的五处工人村落，村落靠堡垒、蓄水池、伊西斯与塞拉皮斯神庙和一座信号塔维持运转。石材经一条设防道路，从尼罗河畔的基纳运到海岸上的阿布沙阿尔（Abu Shaar）堡，再送往罗马和君士坦丁堡，用于皇家建筑和石棺；拜占庭时代，采石场终遭废弃。1444年，这里是马穆鲁克治下的偏远海岸，只有渔船和途经的红海船只，谈不上城镇。1517年，海岸随埃及归入奥斯曼；1541年，埃斯特旺·达伽马的葡萄牙舰队曾沿这片水域驶往苏伊士并在那里被击退，却没有留下驻军。

en:
Quseir lies where the Wadi Hammamat road comes down from the Red Sea Hills to the shore, joining the Nile valley near Qus to Arabia, East Africa and India. Eight kilometres north of the town, at Old Quseir, lies Myos Hormos, the Ptolemies' harbour for the Indian trade. Ptolemy II Philadelphus chose it over Arsinoe, at the head of the same gulf, because the long sail down from that harbour was difficult and slow, and Strabo records that as many as 120 ships a year left for India under Augustus. Inscriptions in Tamil, Nabataean, Palmyrene and Greek have been read on the site, its ships traded as far as Muziris on the Malabar coast, and the Greeks probably called it the Harbour of the Mussel for the pearl mussels gathered on this coast. Busy in the first century, the port was abandoned by the third. The road revived under Islam, and when Qus became the Nile terminus of Red Sea commerce in the thirteenth century, Ayyubid and Mamluk Quseir shipped goods and embarked pilgrims for Mecca. In 1444 it was a small but useful Mamluk port rather than a great city.

The Ottoman conquest of 1517 kept pilgrimage and Indian Ocean traffic moving through it. The square fortress the townspeople call the Tabiya was built by order of Sinan Pasha, governor of Egypt, under Sultan Selim II and finished in 1571, its four corner towers and cannon covering the harbour, the trade caravans and the pilgrim boats crossing to the Hijaz. During the French campaign of 1798-1801 French and Ottoman troops fought over the fort and the desert crossing behind it. The French withdrew in 1801, the coast returned to Ottoman rule, and the Tabiya remained the port's chief landmark.
zh:
古赛尔位于瓦迪哈马马特道路从红海山脉通往海岸的出口，把库斯附近的尼罗河河谷同阿拉伯半岛、东非和印度连在一起。城镇以北8公里处的古港遗址，是托勒密王朝经营印度贸易的米奥斯·霍尔莫斯。托勒密二世选中它而冷落同一海湾顶端的阿尔西诺，因为从那个港口出湾的航程又难又慢；斯特拉波记载，奥古斯都时代每年有多达120艘船从这里驶往印度。遗址中可以读到泰米尔文、纳巴泰文、帕尔米拉文和希腊文题记，商船远航到马拉巴尔海岸的穆吉里斯（Muziris）；希腊人大概因这一带海岸出产珍珠蚌，称它为「贻贝港」。港口在1世纪最繁忙，3世纪便遭废弃。伊斯兰时代这条道路复兴，13世纪库斯成为红海商路在尼罗河上的端点后，阿尤布和马穆鲁克时期的古赛尔转运货物，也送朝圣者从海路前往麦加。1444年，它是一座小而有用的马穆鲁克港口，算不上大城。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，朝圣和印度洋贸易仍从此经过。当地人称「塔比耶」的方形城堡奉埃及总督锡南帕夏之命、在塞利姆二世治下修建，1571年完工，四角塔楼和大炮俯守港口、商队以及开往汉志的朝圣船。1798—1801年法国战役期间，法军与奥斯曼军围绕城堡和它身后的沙漠通道交战。1801年法军撤走，海岸重归奥斯曼统治，塔比耶仍是这座港口最主要的标志。

en:
Wadi Halfa lies at the Second Cataract of the Nile, on the northern edge of Sudan, where the river breaks into miles of rocky channels between desert cliffs and through-navigation ends, cargoes being ported past the rocks on land. Just below the cataract the Egyptians held Buhen, a copper-working settlement in the Old Kingdom and one of the great walled fortresses of the Middle Kingdom. Upriver stood Pakhoras, now Faras, the capital of Silko, king of Nobatia, and later the seat of Nobatia's eparchs. When the Makurian court abandoned Dongola in the later fourteenth century, the Christian kingdom that remained, Dotawo in its own Nubian tongue, held the river from the castles of Gebel Adda and Qasr Ibrim as far as Meinarti at the Second Cataract. In 1444 Nubian kings and castle-lords still ruled the valley, and their villagers grew grain, kept livestock and tended date palms.

Around 1500 a Syrian traveller named John found the Nubians still calling themselves Christians but without a king, obeying roughly a hundred and fifty lords in their castles. The Funj of Sennar took Dongola by 1523, while Ottoman garrisons pushed south from Egypt and by the middle of the century held the Nile as far as the Third Cataract, with a fort on the island of Sai; the Wadi Halfa reach became the march between the two powers, left to small Nubian chiefs. The Shaykiyya Arabs seized Dongola around 1782, and in 1820 Ismail Pasha, son of Muhammad Ali, led an army through the Second Cataract up the Nile, and the last Funj sultan, Badi VII, submitted at Sennar the following year.
zh:
瓦迪哈勒法地处尼罗河第二瀑布、苏丹最北端：河水在沙漠崖壁间散入绵延数里的礁石汊道，直航到此为止，货物须起旱绕过礁石。瀑布下游不远处是布亨，古王国时期埃及人的炼铜据点，到中王国又建成尼罗河畔最坚固的围城之一。更往上游是帕霍拉斯，即今法拉司，曾是诺巴蒂亚国王西尔科的都城，后来成为诺巴蒂亚都督的驻地。14世纪末马库里亚朝廷弃守董古拉后，残存的基督教王国以努比亚语自称「多塔沃」，凭盖贝勒阿代和伊布里姆堡等城堡据守大河，据点沿河南下一直到第二瀑布的迈纳尔提。1444年，努比亚的国王和城堡领主仍统治着这段河谷，村民种谷物、养牲畜、照料椰枣林。

约1500年，一位名叫约翰的叙利亚旅人来到此地，发现努比亚人仍自称基督徒，却已没有国王，只听令于约一百五十名据堡自守的领主。森纳尔的丰吉人在1523年以前攻取董古拉；奥斯曼驻军则从埃及南进，到16世纪中叶已把势力推到第三瀑布，在萨伊岛上筑堡驻守。瓦迪哈勒法一带成为两大政权之间的边地，交给努比亚小酋领分治。1782年前后，沙伊吉亚阿拉伯人夺取董古拉；1820年，穆罕默德·阿里之子伊斯梅尔帕夏率军穿过第二瀑布溯河南征，次年丰吉末代苏丹巴迪七世在森纳尔归降。

en:
The Nubian Desert fills the 400,000 square kilometres between the Nile and the Red Sea with bare hills, dunes and wadis that run dry before they reach the river. Its people are the Beja, Cushitic-speaking nomads, the Medjay and Blemmyes of pharaonic and Roman texts, who move camels, sheep and goats between the Nile wells and the Red Sea hills. Egyptians crossed the sand after gold: the pharaohs built the fortresses of Quban and Ikkur at the mouth of Wadi Allaqi, and between the ninth and thirteenth centuries that wadi's gold and emerald mines were worked by gangs of chattel slaves. Arab tribes of the Rabi'a and Juhayna married into the Beja clans and brought Islam, while caravans used the Korosko road, running straight across the desert from Korosko on the Nile to Abu Hamed, avoiding the long Dongola bend and its cataracts, carrying gold and slaves north into Egypt. In 1444 the Bisharin, Ababda and Amarar pastured their herds along these tracks, and most Beja had become Muslim.

After the mines gave out, the desert lived on its roads and the tolls charged on them. The Hedareb Beja held the Red Sea port of Suakin as their chief town, and when Özdemir Pasha occupied it in the 1550s and the Ottoman province of Habesh was formed, Suakin became the place where desert caravans met sea-going ships. Ivory, gold and slaves from the Funj kingdom of Sennar crossed the sands under Beja escort, and the clans took dues at every well; by the eighteenth century the Hadendoa were the strongest Beja power of the eastern desert. In 1820–1821 the Ababda supplied camels and guides to Muhammad Ali's army invading Sudan, and in return Egypt confirmed their hold on the desert road and their right to a tenth of every cargo.
zh:
努比亚沙漠横亘在尼罗河与红海之间，方圆约四十万平方公里，荒山、沙丘和尚未流到尼罗河便已干涸的干谷交错其间。这里的主人是贝扎人：讲库希特语的游牧民，古埃及和罗马文献里的梅德杰伊人与布莱米伊人，赶着骆驼和羊群往返于尼罗河沿岸水井与红海丘陵之间。埃及人穿过沙海来此淘金：法老在瓦迪阿拉基干谷的谷口修建库班、伊库尔两座要塞，9至13世纪，干谷中的金矿和绿宝石矿由成群的奴隶开采。拉比阿、朱海奈等阿拉伯部落与贝扎诸部通婚，带来伊斯兰教；商队走科罗斯科道，从尼罗河畔的科罗斯科径直横穿沙漠到艾布哈米德，绕开董古拉大河曲和重重瀑布，把黄金和奴隶运往北方的埃及。1444年，比沙林、阿巴卜达、阿马拉尔等部沿古道放牧，贝扎人多已改奉伊斯兰教。

矿坑枯竭后，沙漠靠商道和过境税为生。贝扎人的一支赫达里卜人以红海港口萨瓦金为首邑；1550年代厄兹代米尔帕夏占领该城、奥斯曼哈贝什行省设立后，萨瓦金成了沙漠商队与海船交接货物的港口。来自森纳尔丰吉王国的象牙、黄金和奴隶由贝扎人护送穿过沙海，各部落在沿途水井抽税；到18世纪，哈丹杜瓦人已成为东部沙漠最强的贝扎势力。1820至1821年，阿巴卜达人为穆罕默德·阿里入侵苏丹的军队提供骆驼和向导，换来的回报是埃及承认他们对沙漠商道的控制，并准许他们抽取每批货物的十分之一。

en:
Halaib is a small Red Sea anchorage on the Beja coast; its Beja name refers to the mangroves along the shore, and older charts call it Mersa Ooleyeb. Twenty kilometres to the northwest stood Aydhab, the great port of this coast. The Wadi Allaqi gold rush from the tenth century, Fatimid trade with Yemen and the steady southerly winds that kept large ships from climbing the sea to Suez all drew shipping here. A regular ferry carried African pilgrims across to Jiddah, and caravans ran from the town to Aswan on the Nile. Its customs were shared between Indian Banyan merchants and Beja nomads, who protected the trade; Ibn Battuta was told that one-third of Aydhab belonged to the Mamluk sultan in Cairo and two-thirds to the king of the Beja. Both Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Battuta passed through, and David, the brother of Maimonides, drowned sailing from here to India. A Crusader force under Raynald of Chatillon sacked the town in 1182, and around 1270 David I of Makuria sacked it again; Baybars answered by sacking Dongola, and Makuria became a short-lived Egyptian vassal. In 1426 Sultan Barsbay destroyed Aydhab in reprisal for the plunder of pilgrim goods, and its people fled to Dongola and Suakin, where the Suakinis slaughtered them. By 1444 the site was deserted, and nearby Halaib served only Muslim Beja pastoralists and small coastal craft under loose Mamluk authority.

After the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 this coast became the ill-defined southern edge of Ottoman Egypt, with no border drawn against the Red Sea province of Habesh. Ababda and Bisharin clans kept the wells, grazing grounds and tracks into the Eastern Desert in their own hands while Arabic kinship networks and Islam spread among the Beja. By the eighteenth century the Hadendoa dominated much of the country behind the coast, but Halaib remained a minor anchorage and never recovered Aydhab's pilgrim and Indian trade.
zh:
哈拉伊卜是贝扎海岸上的小红海锚地，贝扎语地名来自岸边的红树林，旧称奥莱布港。它西北20公里处就是这条海岸上的大港口阿伊扎布。10世纪起瓦迪阿拉基的淘金热、法蒂玛与也门的贸易，再加上常年南风使大船难以驶近苏伊士，都把船只吸引到这里。班船把非洲朝觐者送往对岸的吉达，商队又把这座城与尼罗河畔的阿斯旺连在一起。关税由印度商人和贝扎游牧民分享，后者负责保护商路；伊本·白图泰听说，阿伊扎布三分之一归开罗的马穆鲁克苏丹，三分之二归贝扎人的国王。伊本·朱拜尔和伊本·白图泰都曾路过此地，迈蒙尼德的兄弟大卫就是从这里启航前往印度时溺亡的。1182年，十字军首领沙蒂永的雷纳德率军洗劫该城；约1270年，马库里亚国王大卫一世再度洗劫阿伊扎布，拜巴尔斯随即回师溯尼罗河攻破栋古拉，马库里亚就此一度沦为埃及附庸。1426年，苏丹巴尔斯拜为报复朝觐货物遭劫而摧毁阿伊扎布，居民逃往栋古拉和萨瓦金，却在萨瓦金尽遭屠戮。到1444年，城址已经荒废，邻近的哈拉伊卜只供穆斯林贝扎牧人和零星小船使用，处在马穆鲁克的松散权威之下。

1517年奥斯曼征服埃及后，这片海岸成为奥斯曼埃及界定模糊的南缘，与红海的哈贝什省之间没有划定边界。阿巴卜达和比夏林部落继续把水井、牧场和通往东部沙漠的道路掌握在自己手中，阿拉伯亲属网络和伊斯兰教也在贝扎人中扩展。到18世纪，哈登多亚人已主导海岸后方的大片土地，但哈拉伊卜始终只是个小锚地，再没有恢复阿伊扎布当年的朝觐与印度贸易。

en:
Marsa Matruh, Paraetonium to the Greeks and al-Baritun after the Islamic conquest, is the only sheltered anchorage on the desert shore west of Alexandria; rocks guard the mouth of its bay and leave a narrow passage for small ships. It began as a fishing village and grew as the port for the oracle of Amun at Siwa, whose priests pronounced Alexander the Great a son of Amun and the rightful pharaoh of Egypt. Under the Ptolemies and Rome its ships carried Egyptian grain across the Mediterranean, and Ovid wrote that Isis was its patron goddess. Cairo's Mamluks claimed this coast in the late thirteenth century, but daily life belonged to Bedouin groups, fishermen and caravan men moving between the Delta, Siwa and the Libyan ports. In 1444 it was a remote frontier valued for its water, fish and safe roadstead.

The coast passed to the Ottomans with Egypt in 1517 and lay lightly governed between Ottoman Egypt and the regency of Tripoli. The desert behind it stayed almost unknown to Europeans; when the English traveller William George Browne reached Siwa in 1792, he was the first documented European visitor to the oasis since Roman times. In 1820 Muhammad Ali's troops marched into the Western Desert and annexed Siwa, pulling the caravan track and its fishing roadstead into the Egyptian state. At the close of the period Marsa Matruh was still a small anchorage, valued more as a link between Alexandria, Barqa and the oases than as a city.
zh:
塔拉纳一带的马特鲁港，希腊人称之为帕莱托尼翁，伊斯兰征服后称巴利通，是亚历山大以西荒漠海岸上唯一可避风浪的锚地；礁石护住湾口，只留一道窄缝供小船进出。起初这里是渔村，后来成为从海上前往西瓦阿蒙神谕所的登岸港；神谕所的祭司曾宣布亚历山大大帝为阿蒙之子、埃及合法的法老。托勒密和罗马统治时期，港中船只把埃及谷物运往地中海，奥维德还记下伊西斯是此城的守护神。13世纪末，开罗的马穆鲁克人对这条海岸提出主权主张，但日常事务由贝都因群体、渔民和往来三角洲、西瓦与利比亚港口的商队做主。1444年，这里是偏远的边疆，所重的是淡水、渔产和安全锚地。

1517年这片海岸随埃及转入奥斯曼之手，夹在奥斯曼埃及与的黎波里摄政国之间，治理向来松弛。后方的沙漠几乎不为欧洲人所知；1792年英国旅行家威廉·乔治·布朗抵达西瓦时，是罗马时代以后首位有记载到访该绿洲的欧洲人。1820年，穆罕默德·阿里的军队开进西部沙漠，兼并西瓦，把商路和路边的渔业锚地纳入埃及国家。本时期末，马特鲁港仍是一座小锚地，其价值更多在于连接亚历山大、巴尔卡与绿洲，而不在于城市本身。

en:
Bardia (al-Bardiyya) is a small natural roadstead on the Mediterranean coast at the eastern edge of Cyrenaica, east of Tobruk and a short distance from the Egyptian frontier. Its cliff-bound cove is one of the few anchorages on a shore where the desert runs to the sea. The Romans knew it as Petras Maior. After the Banu Sulaym Arabs settled Barqa in the eleventh century the country belonged to its Bedouin tribes; the Mamluk sultans in Cairo could uphold their claim over it only by alliance with the tribes and payments to them. In 1444 Bardia was Mamluk in name, a roadstead where coasting vessels called, with no garrison of its own.

Ottoman armies took Egypt in 1517 and Tripoli in 1551, and Bardia fell within the loose frontier zone of the regency of Tripoli. In 1711 Ahmed Karamanli made himself pasha at Tripoli and founded a hereditary dynasty; Bardia stood at the remote eastern edge of his domains, nearer to the Egyptian border than to his capital.
zh:
拜尔迪耶是地中海沿岸一座天然小港，在昔兰尼加的最东端，位于图卜鲁格以东，离埃及边界不远。崖壁环抱的小湾是这段沙漠直抵大海的海岸上少有的锚地，罗马人称它大佩特拉斯。11世纪，巴努苏莱姆阿拉伯人在巴尔卡定居，此后这片土地归贝都因部落所有；开罗的马穆鲁克苏丹只能靠与部落结盟、向他们纳贡来维持宗主权。1444年的拜尔迪耶名义上臣属马穆鲁克，实际上只是沿岸航船停靠的锚地，本地没有驻军。

奥斯曼军队1517年取下埃及，1551年又攻占的黎波里，拜尔迪耶被划入的黎波里摄政政权松散的边疆地带。1711年，艾哈迈德·卡拉曼利在的黎波里自立为帕夏，建立世袭王朝，拜尔迪耶处在其疆域偏远的东缘，离埃及边界比离都城还近。

en:
Ma'an lies on the desert edge where the old King's Highway leaves the Transjordanian highlands and becomes the Hajj road to western Arabia. Minaean traders from Yemen founded a station here before Roman times, and in 951 the geographer al-Istakhri found a small desert-border fortress where travellers were received and pilgrims stored goods they did not need for the road. Yaqut al-Hamawi in the early thirteenth century found the place largely ruined, but its pilgrim station survived, and by the end of the century the Bahri Mamluks had made Ma'an one of the four districts of Karak province. Al-Dimashqi knew a small city with a caravanserai, a provision market and a hostel, and Ibn Battuta called it the last settlement in Syria before the Hejaz. In 1444 Ma'an was a Mamluk watering and provisioning town, valued less for its size than for its wells and gardens and its command of the desert crossing.

The Ottomans annexed Transjordan in 1517 and in 1566 built Qal'at al-Ma'an to guard the pilgrims, store water and house troops. The governor of Damascus put down a rising here in 1656, but when the Banu Tamim rebelled soon afterward the imperial troops were routed, and Ottoman control stayed weak for generations. Long split into a Syrian and a Hijazi quarter, Ma'an al-Shamiyya and Ma'an al-Hijaziyya, the town lived almost entirely by the Hajj. Supplies came from Gaza and Hebron, the outward caravan bought camels for transport and sheep for sacrifice, and the returning caravan turned the market into a sale of goods from across the Islamic world. Many townsmen were literate and served the surrounding Bedouin as imams and scribes; with the Anizzah and Huwaytat they kept closer terms than most desert towns, bargaining down the usual tribute in lean years. Burckhardt, visiting early in the nineteenth century, recorded that the people of Ma'an regarded their town as an advanced post on the road to Medina.
zh:
马安位于沙漠边缘，古老王道在这里离开外约旦高地，化为通往阿拉伯半岛西部的朝觐大道。罗马时代之前，来自也门的米奈商人已在此设立驿站；951年，地理学家伊斯塔赫里见到一座沙漠边缘的小要塞，旅客在那里受招待，朝觐者也可寄存路上不必随身携带的货物。13世纪初雅古特·哈马维记载此地大半荒废，但朝觐驿站仍然保留；该世纪末，巴赫里马穆鲁克把马安划为卡拉克省的四个区之一。迪马什基笔下的马安是座小城，有商队客栈、粮食市场和旅舍；伊本·白图泰则称这里是进入汉志之前叙利亚的最后一处定居点。1444年的马安是马穆鲁克的补水和补给镇，价值不在城邑大小，而在水井、园圃和对沙漠通道的控制。

1517年奥斯曼吞并外约旦，1566年修建马安堡，保护朝觐者、蓄水并驻扎军队。1656年，大马士革总督镇压了这里的起事，但巴努·塔米姆部落随后反叛，击败奥斯曼军队，此后几代人时间里帝国对这里的控制都很薄弱。城市很早便分为沙姆马安和汉志马安两区，生计几乎全靠朝觐。补给从加沙和希伯伦运来，出发的商队购买驮运的骆驼和献祭的绵羊，返程商队则让市集摆满伊斯兰世界各地的货物。许多居民识字，在周围贝都因人中间充当伊玛目和文书；他们同安纳扎、胡韦塔特等部落的关系比多数沙漠城镇都亲近，年成不好时还能把照例缴纳的贡赋讨价还价压下来。19世纪初布尔克哈特到访时记载，马安人把本城看作通往麦地那道路上的前沿据点。

en:
Al-Ula is the chief oasis of Wadi al-Qura, the 'Valley of Villages', a fertile cleft in bare mountains on the road from Syria to Medina. Before Islam it was Dedan, seat of the Dedanite and Lihyanite kings, and in the 13th century a walled town, al-Dirah, rose beside the palm groves, its houses built from the stones of the older ruins. Twenty kilometres north the Nabataean city of Hegra stood abandoned: the kingdom's second city after Petra, with more than a hundred tombs cut into the red sandstone. Muslims knew it as the dwellings of the Thamud of the prophet Salih, and caravans hurried past for fear of the cursed ground; when Ibn Battuta passed in the 14th century he saw the red tombs and no inhabitants. The tenth-century geographer al-Istakhri still counted Wadi al-Qura among the most populous and productive valleys in Arabia. In 1444 the date gardens belonged in practice to the Bedouin of the wadi, above all the Anizah, and the Syrian pilgrim caravan bought dates and watered here on the march to Medina.

After the Ottoman conquest of 1517 the Damascus caravan became the sultan's charge, yet for two centuries the road past al-Ula had no garrison. Between 1744 and 1757 As'ad Pasha al-Azm, governor of Damascus, raised a fort at al-Hijr among the Nabataean tombs, with a great well and a cistern, where pilgrims rested a day and bought dates, lemons and oranges. It was finished just in time for the road's worst disaster: in 1757 the Banu Sakhr and their allies swept down on the caravan at al-Ula and the stations to the north on its way back to Damascus, and thousands of pilgrims died by the sword or of thirst. The fort was repaired and regarrisoned; As'ad Pasha himself was executed in the aftermath, accused of negligence or a hand in the catastrophe. Al-Ula went on as a watering stage of the Syrian pilgrim road.
zh:
欧拉是瓦迪·古拉（意为「村庄之谷」）的首要绿洲，坐落在叙利亚通往麦地那的大道上，是童山之间一道土地肥沃的峡谷。伊斯兰兴起以前，这里是德丹，德丹人和利哈彦人的王城；13世纪，一座有城墙的城镇迪拉在椰枣林旁建起，房屋大量取用古城废墟的石料。城以北二十公里是废弃的纳巴泰城市黑格拉，它曾是纳巴泰王国仅次于佩特拉的第二大城，红砂岩中凿有一百多座墓窟。穆斯林把这里看作先知撒立哈时代赛莫德人的居地，畏惧这片受咒之地，驼队都匆匆经过；14世纪伊本·白图泰路过时，只见到红色墓窟，没有见到居民。10世纪的地理学家伊斯塔赫里仍把瓦迪·古拉列为阿拉伯人口最密、出产最丰的谷地之一。1444年，谷地的椰枣园实际掌握在贝都因人、尤其是阿尼扎人手中，走叙利亚路的朝觐驼队在前往麦地那途中，在这里买椰枣、补饮水。

1517年奥斯曼征服后，大马士革驼队改由苏丹负责，但此后两百年，欧拉附近的道路一直没有驻军。1744年至1757年间，大马士革总督艾斯阿德·阿兹姆帕夏在黑格拉的纳巴泰墓窟间修起一座要塞，内置大井和蓄水池，供朝觐者歇脚一日，购买椰枣、柠檬和柑橘。要塞刚落成，这条路上最惨的劫难就发生了：1757年，巴努·萨赫尔部落及其盟友趁驼队返回大马士革，在欧拉和北面各驿站冲下袭击，数千名朝觐者死于刀剑或干渴。要塞事后得到修复和重派驻军；艾斯阿德帕夏本人也在事后的整肃中被处死，罪名是疏于职守或牵涉其中。欧拉继续作为叙利亚朝觐路上的补水驿站。

en:
Yanbu means 'spring', after the freshwater wells behind a flat Red Sea shore. In early Arab geography the name usually meant Yanbu al-Nakhl, a palm oasis in a wadi on the Quraysh caravan road to Syria, and the Egyptian pilgrimage route from Aqaba down to Mecca passed the same settlements. Yanbu al-Bahr, the harbour a few days' ride from Medina, was the nearest landing place for the holy city, where Egyptian grain, pilgrims and trade goods came ashore before going inland. When the Mamluks built up Jeddah as the main port of the Hejaz, Yanbu kept only the Medina traffic and became a quiet secondary roadstead. In 1444 the oasis and its port belonged to the Sharifate of Medina, inside the Mamluk-backed order of the Hejaz.

Ottoman sovereignty followed in 1517 and changed little; pilgrims and supply caravans kept using the harbour. Its one turn as an army base came in the Ottoman-Wahhabi war. In 1811 Tusun Pasha, the teenage son of Muhammad Ali of Egypt, seized Yanbu as the bridgehead for his march on Medina, but Abdullah bin Saud caught his column in the Wadi al-Safra and routed it in January 1812; the survivors fell back to their ships. Reinforced from Egypt, Tusun used Yanbu again for the counterstroke that retook Medina later in 1812, and the harbour supplied his army by sea until the Saudi capital Diriyah fell in 1818. In 1821 Yanbu was held by Muhammad Ali's Egyptian administration.
zh:
延布意为「泉水」，得名于平坦红海海岸背后的淡水井。早期阿拉伯地理书中的延布，通常指延布枣园：干河谷里的一片枣椰绿洲，在古莱什人前往叙利亚的商队路上；埃及朝觐队伍从亚喀巴南下麦加，也经过这片聚落。延布港离麦地那只有几天路程，是圣城最近的登陆地，埃及粮食、朝觐者和商货在此上岸，再转往内陆。马穆鲁克王朝把吉达经营成汉志首要港口后，延布只剩下通往麦地那的生意，成了冷清的次级锚地。1444年，绿洲和港口属于麦地那谢里夫国，处在马穆鲁克支持的汉志秩序之中。

1517年奥斯曼接管汉志，这里没有多少变化，朝觐者和补给商队照旧使用港口。延布唯一一次充当大军基地，是在奥斯曼—瓦哈比战争中。1811年，埃及穆罕默德·阿里十几岁的儿子图松帕夏夺取延布，作为进军麦地那的桥头堡；阿卜杜拉·本·沙特在萨夫拉谷截住他的队伍，1812年1月将其击溃，残部退回船上。得到埃及增援后，图松再以延布为基地反攻，同年晚些时候夺回麦地那；直到沙特都城德里耶耶1818年陷落，这座港口一直从海上供应他的军队。1821年，延布归穆罕默德·阿里的埃及政权管辖。

en:
Ma'din Sulaym, the Mine of the Banu Sulaym, lies on the desert road southeast of Medina toward Najd, and Arabs later called the place Mahd al-Dhahab, the golden cradle. Gold was washed here before Islam, and the Banu Sulaym were still working the deposits in the Prophet's lifetime. Under the Umayyads their gold went to the mints Caliph Abd al-Malik opened for the first Islamic dinars, and Abbasid records claim about forty tons of it between 750 and 1258. The district also carried the Darb Zubayda, the pilgrim road from Kufa to Mecca, whose wells, cisterns and stations were endowed by Zubayda, granddaughter of Caliph al-Mansur and wife of Harun al-Rashid; travellers crossing the lava plain and its wadis watered there for centuries. Sulaym clans that stayed in Arabia were absorbed from the ninth century by the incoming Banu Harb. By 1444 the mines had long been quiet, and the wells and pastures mattered as the tribal hinterland of the Sharifate of Medina.

Ottoman sovereignty reached the district with the rest of the Hejaz in 1517, and nobody reopened the old workings. The armies of the Wahhabi war then passed over it: Diriyah's men entered the Hejaz in 1803 and took Medina in 1805, Tusun Pasha retook the city in 1812, and Ibrahim Pasha's march on Najd ended with the fall of Diriyah in 1818. In 1821 the old mining district lay within the Egyptian-Ottoman frontier posts run from Medina.
zh:
曼丁苏莱姆意为「苏莱姆之子的矿」，在麦地那东南、通往内志的沙漠道路上，阿拉伯人后来称这里为马赫德宰海卜，意思是黄金的摇篮。伊斯兰教以前已有人在此淘金，先知穆罕默德在世时，苏莱姆部落仍在开采矿脉。倭马亚时代，这里的黄金运进哈里发阿卜杜勒·马利克为铸造最早的伊斯兰第纳尔开设的造币厂；阿拔斯史料记载，750年至1258年间共产金约四十吨。境内还有祖拜达道经过，那是库法通往麦加的朝觐大路，沿途水井、蓄水池和驿站都由曼苏尔哈里发的孙女、哈伦·拉希德的妻子祖拜达捐建，几个世纪里穿越熔岩原和干河谷的旅人都在此取水。留在阿拉伯的苏莱姆支派，从9世纪起逐渐被迁来的哈尔卜部落吸收。到1444年，金矿早已停工，水井和牧场只是麦地那谢里夫国的部落腹地。

1517年，这一地区随汉志并入奥斯曼版图，古矿坑再没有人重新开采。瓦哈比战争的军队随后从这里往来：德里耶耶的人马1803年进入汉志，1805年拿下麦地那；图松帕夏1812年夺回该城，易卜拉欣帕夏进军内志，1818年德里耶耶陷落。1821年，这片古矿区处在麦地那派出的埃及—奥斯曼戍所一线之内。

en:
Jeddah is the port of Mecca on the Red Sea shore, a day's travel from the Holy City. It began as a fishing hamlet, and in 647 the Caliph Uthman made it Mecca's harbour in place of the older al-Shu'ayba; thereafter most pilgrims who came to the Hajj by sea landed on its beach, and Indian merchants brought spices and textiles to its customs house. Local tradition held that Eve, the mother of mankind, was buried here, and the city's name was explained from the Arabic jaddah, 'grandmother'. The Mamluks of Egypt cut Jeddah's duties to draw the Indian trade away from Aden, and Ibn Battuta found a thriving town when he passed through around 1330; the al-Shafi'i Mosque, whose minaret went up in the thirteenth century, was already the oldest mosque in town. In 1444 the city and the coastal plain around it were held, under loose Mamluk suzerainty, by Barakat ibn Hasan, the Hashemite Sharif of Mecca, whose income rested largely on Jeddah's customs and the pilgrim fleets.

After Vasco da Gama reached the Indian Ocean the Portuguese carried the war into the Red Sea, and the Mamluk sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri ordered his amir Husain al-Kurdi to ring Jeddah with a wall and shore batteries, a work Arab sources date to 1509. It served the town in April 1517, when Selman Reis's gunners drove off the armada of Lopo Soares de Albergaria. Later that year the Ottoman conquest of Egypt made Jeddah an Ottoman port, and in 1525 the Turks rebuilt the walls with six towers and six gates; Sharif Barakat II of Mecca submitted to the sultan in the same year. A second Portuguese assault was beaten back in 1541. As the Cape route and Dutch and English ships drew the Indian trade elsewhere, Jeddah lived increasingly on the Hajj alone. In 1802 the Wahhabi forces of the First Saudi State seized Mecca and Jeddah, but in January 1813 the city opened its gates without a fight to Muhammad Ali Pasha's Egyptians under his kinsman Mustafa Bey; Muhammad Ali landed there in September and made Jeddah his base for reconquering Arabia.
zh:
吉达是红海岸边的麦加外港，距圣城只有一天路程。它本是一处渔村，647年哈里发奥斯曼把它定为麦加的港口，取代更古老的舒艾巴港；此后由海路前来朝觐的香客多在吉达登岸，印度商人也把香料和布匹运进这里的海关。当地相传人类之母夏娃就葬在城中，城名也被解释为阿拉伯语里「祖母」一词。埃及的马穆鲁克人降低吉达关税，把印度贸易从亚丁吸引过来；伊本·白图泰约在1330年路过时，见到的已是一座繁荣城镇，城里最古老的沙斐仪清真寺，其宣礼塔在13世纪便已建起。1444年，吉达及周围沿海平原处在松散的马穆鲁克宗主权之下，由麦加的哈希姆系谢里夫巴拉卡特·伊本·哈桑统治，他的收入主要靠吉达的关税和朝觐船队。

瓦斯科·达·伽马驶入印度洋后，葡萄牙人把战火烧进红海，马穆鲁克苏丹坎苏·戈里命埃米尔侯赛因·库尔迪为吉达环筑城墙和海岸炮台，阿拉伯史料把这项工程系于1509年。1517年4月，城墙派上用场：塞尔曼·雷斯的炮火击退了洛波·苏亚雷斯·德·阿尔贝加里亚的舰队。同年晚些时候奥斯曼征服埃及，吉达成为奥斯曼港口，1525年土耳其人重修城墙，设六塔六门，麦加谢里夫巴拉卡特二世也在同年向苏丹称臣。1541年，葡萄牙人的第二次进攻再被击退。随着好望角航路和荷兰、英国商船把印度贸易引走，吉达越来越只靠朝觐维持。1802年，第一沙特国的瓦哈比军队攻占麦加和吉达；1813年1月，吉达不战开城，向穆罕默德·阿里帕夏的姻亲穆斯塔法贝伊所率埃及军队投降，穆罕默德·阿里本人9月登陆，把吉达作为重新征服阿拉伯的基地。

en:
Turbah is a palm-watered oasis in the wadi of the same name, one of Arabia's longest valleys, which runs down from the Sarat highlands past Jebel Hadhn, the mountain between Hejaz and Najd, to the edge of the Najd desert. Medieval Arab geographers counted it among the districts of Mecca, and its people are the Buqum, a tribe that had held the wadi since before Islam. Springs and a stream running all year fed gardens and date groves along the banks, and local accounts put the palms at around 300,000; the unwalled farms were famed for feasting passing travellers at harvest. In 1444 the valley lies within the loose lordship of the Sharif of Mecca, backed by Mamluk power, and supplies the highland road between Mecca and the interior with dates and livestock.

In 1797 the Buqum swore allegiance to Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad, the Saudi imam of Diriyah, and Turbah became a strongpoint on the Wahhabi flank facing the Hejaz. Its defence in the Ottoman-Wahhabi war made the name of Ghaliya, widow of Hamd ibn Abdallah, the Saudi amir of Turbah, who armed her household, rallied the tribesmen and was acknowledged by the garrison as their amira. When Muhammad Ali Pasha of Egypt campaigned for the Ottomans, his son Tusun Pasha stormed the oasis in 1813 and was beaten back with heavy loss; bedouin raiders struck at Tusun's supply trains, and the Egyptian soldiers blamed the rout on Ghaliya's sorcery, for rumour said she could make her men invisible. In 1814 a second assault led by Tusun and Abidin Bey collapsed after eight days of fighting. After the Saudi defeat at Busal in 1815 a peace settlement ceded the Hejaz, and Ghaliya withdrew to Diriyah, where by the local account she died when the Egyptian army stormed the Saudi capital in 1818.
zh:
图赖拜是同名干河谷中的椰枣绿洲。图赖拜干河是阿拉伯半岛最长的河谷之一，自塞拉特高地蜿蜒而下，经汉志与内志的界山哈杜恩山麓，延伸至内志沙漠边缘。中世纪的阿拉伯地理学家把它算作麦加的属地之一，居民是伊斯兰教兴起前便定居此谷的巴古姆部落。泉眼和常年不涸的河水滋养着两岸田园与椰枣林，当地记载称椰枣树约有三十万株；不设围墙的农庄还以收获季款待过路旅客闻名。1444年的图赖拜处于麦加谢里夫松散的统治之下，背后是马穆鲁克的权势，沿麦加通往内陆的山路供应椰枣和牲畜。

1797年，巴古姆人向德拉伊耶的沙特伊玛目阿卜杜勒·阿齐兹·伊本·穆罕默德宣誓效忠，图赖拜成为瓦哈比派面向汉志一侧的要塞。让这里名传一时的是女子加利亚：她是图赖拜沙特埃米尔哈姆德·伊本·阿卜杜拉的遗孀，在奥斯曼与沙特的战争中武装家中人丁、鼓动族人上阵，被守军奉为女埃米尔。埃及的穆罕默德·阿里帕夏奉素丹之命讨伐沙特人时，其子图松帕夏1813年猛攻绿洲，损兵折将而退；贝都因袭扰者又打击图松的补给线，埃及士兵便把惨败推到加利亚的妖术上，传言她能让自己的人马隐身。1814年，图松与阿比丁·贝伊再度来攻，连打八天仍告溃败。1815年沙特人在拜苏勒战败后签订和约、放弃汉志；加利亚随后撤往德拉伊耶，按当地记载，1818年埃军攻破这座沙特首都时她死在城中。

en:
Zufra is the empty western reach of the Gulf coast, the shore later known as Al Dhafra, running from the Qatar borderlands towards Liwa. Its small anchorage of Sila looks over fishing beaches, with grazing around scattered wells inland between the sea and the dunes. Arab geographers called the whole coast from Basra towards Oman the Khatt Abd al-Qays, after the tribe whose camps reached this far west. In 1444 Hormuz commanded the shipping lanes offshore, while the mainland felt the weight of the Jabrid rulers of al-Hasa, who had taken Qatif in 1439. Fish, camels, date caravans and well-water counted for more here than any walled town.

The coast's overlords changed within a few years. In 1521 the Jabrid sultan Miqrin ibn Zamil was killed in Bahrain trying to throw back a Portuguese landing, and in 1526 Rashid ibn Mughamis al-Shabib, sheikh of the Muntafiq in Iraq, seized al-Hasa and the dynasty collapsed. In the centuries after, Manasir Bedouin moved between Qatar, Buraimi, Liwa and this shore, breeding camels, leading camel trains, working date plots and diving for pearls in summer. When the Bani Yas settled Liwa about 1700 and built up Abu Dhabi in the 1790s, Sila became the far, thinly peopled western edge of their orbit; in January 1820 Abu Dhabi's acceptance of the General Maritime Treaty with Britain drew these beaches and wells into the new coastal order.
zh:
萨夫拉是海湾沿岸空旷的西陲，即后来所称的达法拉海岸，从卡塔尔边境地带延伸向利瓦。小停泊点锡拉面向渔村滩涂，往内陆去，沙丘间散布着水井，井周有牧场。阿拉伯地理学家把从巴士拉伸向阿曼的整条海岸称作「阿卜杜勒·盖斯之线」，名字来自营地远及这片西陲的阿卜杜勒·盖斯部。1444年，外海航路归霍尔木兹掌控，大陆上则承受哈萨的贾布里德统治者的压力，他们已于1439年夺取盖提夫。在这里，鱼获、骆驼、椰枣商队和井水比任何设防城池都要紧。

海岸的宗主没几年就换了。1521年，贾布里德苏丹米克林·本·扎米勒在巴林抵御葡萄牙人登陆时战死；1526年，伊拉克蒙塔菲格部的谢赫拉希德·本·穆加米斯·谢比卜夺取哈萨，王朝灭亡。此后几个世纪，马纳西尔贝都因人在卡塔尔、布赖米、利瓦和这片海岸之间转场，养骆驼、赶驼队、种椰枣地，夏天出海采珠。巴尼·亚斯人约1700年定居利瓦、1790年代建起阿布扎比后，锡拉成为其势力范围最西端人烟稀少的边地；1820年1月阿布扎比接受与英国的《总航海条约》，这些滩涂和水井也被纳入新的海岸秩序。

en:
Dawasir is the long oasis valley of Wadi ad-Dawasir in southern Najd, called al-Aqiq by older Arab geographers. Watercourses running down from the western highlands feed its wells and palm groves before the wadi loses itself in the sands east of as-Sulayyil. The Dawasir tribe made the valley its home seat: the Al Zayed and Taghlib branches both herded camels and worked the palm gardens, and the number of its wells and fighting men kept outside rulers at a distance. In 1444 this Sunni Bedouin country was run by its own shaykhs, beyond the firm reach of any court in the Najdi towns.

A tribe this strong had to be courted rather than commanded. In 1785 Rabi ibn Zayd al-Mukharim al-Dawasir and his brother Badan travelled to Diriyah and pledged obedience to Abdulaziz ibn Muhammad, then returned with money and arms to gather fighting men around the new alliance; Rabi's palace in the oasis later housed the local Saudi garrison. Wadi ad-Dawasir became one of the southern pillars of the First Saudi State and stayed tied to Diriyah until 1818, when Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army captured and destroyed the Saudi capital and Saudi power collapsed across Najd. The wells and palm groves then went back to the shaykhs and the tribe.
zh:
代瓦西尔的核心是内志南部狭长的绿洲干河瓦迪达瓦西，阿拉伯古籍称之为阿吉格。西部高地流下的径流补给井水和椰枣林，干河最终消失在塞利勒以东的沙海里。代瓦西尔部落把这条河谷当作根本之地：阿勒·扎伊德与塔格莱卜两大支既牧放骆驼，也耕作椰枣园；水井之众、战士之多，使外来统治者难以涉足。1444年时，这片逊尼派贝都因土地由自己的谢赫治理，内志各城镇的宫廷都够不到这里。

对这样强的部落，只能争取，不能号令。1785年，代瓦西尔人拉比·本·扎伊德·穆哈里姆与兄弟巴丹前往德拉伊耶，向阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·本·穆罕默德宣誓归顺，又带着钱帛和武器返回，在这层新盟约下集结战士；拉比在绿洲中的宫殿后来驻扎了沙特的当地守军。瓦迪达瓦西成为第一沙特国南方的支柱之一，与德拉伊耶的联系一直维持到1818年，易卜拉欣帕夏的埃及军队在这一年攻陷并摧毁沙特都城，沙特势力在内志全面瓦解，水井和椰枣林重归谢赫和部族之手。

en:
Aflaj is a string of oasis villages spread across the southern Tuwaiq upland, about 300 kilometres southeast of Riyadh, with Layla the largest of them. The villages live from the falaj, channels that carry spring water out to palm groves, grain fields and grazing; at al-Kharaz a single natural spring feeds a web of small linked canals. Dawasir clans held the oasis as one of their southern seats in Najd, shifting their herds between the settled strip and the desert around it. In 1444 dates, grain and livestock supported a small population whose mud forts answered to local elders rather than to any court in the Najdi towns.

Arab tradition makes this the country of Layla and Majnun. The town of Layla bears the name of Layla of the Banu Amir, cousin and beloved of Qays ibn al-Mulawwah, the seventh-century poet whom his people called Majnun, the possessed, after her father married her to another; Jabal Toubad above the oasis is linked with the pair. Nizami of Ganja turned the tale into a Persian narrative poem in 1188, and the versions of Jami in 1484 and Fuzuli in 1535 carried it through the Persian- and Turkish-speaking lands, while the oasis itself kept to its springs, palms and herds.
zh:
阿夫拉季是散布在图韦克山地南段的一连串绿洲村落，在利雅得东南约300公里，莱拉是其中最大的一处。各村落依靠坎儿井和明渠引出泉水，浇灌椰枣林、粮田和牧场；海拉兹渠系便由一条天然泉水分出彼此相连的小渠。代瓦西尔各部把这片绿洲当作内志南部的根基之一，赶着畜群在定居地带与周围沙漠之间转场。1444年时，椰枣、谷物和牲畜养活着不多的人口，土筑堡垒听命于本地长老，内志各城镇的宫廷都管不到这里。

相传这里就是莱拉与玛吉努故事的故乡。莱拉镇得名于阿米尔部落的莱拉：她是7世纪诗人凯斯·伊本·穆劳瓦的表妹和心上人，她的父亲把她另嫁他人后，族人便称凯斯为「玛吉努」，意为被精灵附了体的痴人；绿洲旁的图拜德山也与这对情侣联系在一起。1188年，甘贾的尼扎米把这段故事写成波斯语叙事诗，1484年贾米、1535年富祖里又各有同名之作，把它带到波斯语和突厥语世界；而这片绿洲依旧守着泉水、椰枣和畜群。

en:
Buraydah stands on the eastern rim of the Wadi al-Rummah, the long watercourse that crosses the Qasim highlands of northern Najd. Its wells watered some of the best grazing in the peninsula, used in 1444 by the Anazzah Bedouin. Nearby Unayzah was already a watering place on the Darb Zubaydah, the pilgrim road from Kufa to Mecca laid out under Harun al-Rashid. No town yet stood here, only a well called Buraydah where camel and sheep herds drank and caravans put in between the Shammar pastures and the markets of Najd and the Hijaz.

Najdi tradition has the town begin with a purchase. In 1577 Rashid ibn Abdullah al-Duraybi, chief of the Al Abu Alian clan of the Banu Tamim, bought the Buraydah well from its Anazzah owners and built around it the seat of his family's emirs, soon the chief town of Qasim and rival to Unayzah. A wall went up against Bedouin raids, then a second under Hujaylan ibn Hamd, the emir who brought Buraydah under the First Saudi State and ruled all Qasim but Unayzah. Two armies came against the walls in the 1780s, Saadun ibn Arar of the Banu Khalid in 1782 and Thuwaini al-Saadun of the Muntafiq in 1786, and both broke off their sieges. In the Ottoman-Wahhabi war the town could not hold out. After Abdullah ibn Saud's attack on the Egyptian vanguard failed at Mawiyah in May 1817, Ibrahim Pasha took Rass that October following a three-and-a-half-month siege, Unayzah surrendered, and Buraydah submitted. Its leading men went off as hostages with the army that marched south to destroy Diriyah in 1818, and an Egyptian garrison stayed behind in Qasim.
zh:
布赖代坐落在鲁迈干河东缘，这条长河谷横亘内志北部的卡西姆高地。这里的井泉滋养着阿拉伯半岛最好的几处牧场，1444年的主人是安宰部落的贝都因人。附近的欧奈宰已是祖拜黛大道上的饮水点，这条从库法通往麦加的朝觐路铺筑于哈伦·拉希德时代。此时此地还没有城镇，只有一口名叫布赖代的水井供驼羊饮水，商队往返于舍迈尔牧场与内志、汉志的市集之间时在此歇脚。

据内志志书的传承，这座城始于一笔买卖。1577年，贝尼塔米姆部落阿布·阿里扬氏族的首领拉希德·本·阿卜杜拉·德里比从安宰人手中买下布赖代井，在井边建起本家族埃米尔的驻地，这里很快成为卡西姆首镇，与欧奈宰争雄。城镇先筑一道墙抵御贝都因袭掠，侯吉兰·本·哈姆德任埃米尔时又修了第二道；他率布赖代归附第一沙特国，统辖除欧奈宰外的整个卡西姆。1780年代，两支大军先后兵临城下：1782年贝尼哈立德的萨阿敦·本·阿拉尔、1786年蒙塔菲格的苏韦尼·萨阿敦都没能破城。奥斯曼－瓦哈卜战争中，布赖代未能幸免。1817年5月，阿卜杜拉·本·沙特在穆维叶截击埃及前锋失败，易卜拉欣帕夏围攻拉斯三个半月后于10月破城，欧奈宰投降，布赖代也归顺。城中头面人物被作为人质随军押走，那支军队在1818年南下毁灭了德拉伊耶，卡西姆则留下了埃及驻军。

en: Hafar is a line of desert wells in the broad, usually dry bed of Wadi al-Batin, the lower course of Wadi al-Rummah. After rain, its pastures are among the best in this part of northern Arabia, although the channel can fill with dangerous speed. During Caliph Uthman's reign, Abu Musa al-Asha'ari dug wells here after pilgrims complained about the dry road from Iraq to Mecca; the place became known as Hafar Abu Musa and served pilgrims leaving Basra. In 1444 Shammar, Anaza and neighboring Bedouin clans watered camels, sheep and goats there, while caravans followed the wadi track. No walled town stood at Hafar. Its value lay in wells, grazing and a reliable stopping place for groups crossing the desert.
zh: 哈费尔是巴廷干河宽阔而多半干涸的河床上的一串沙漠水井，巴廷干河也是鲁迈干河的下游河段。雨后，这一带的牧场属于阿拉伯北部最好的牧区之一，但干河河道也可能迅速涨水。哈里发奥斯曼在位时，朝觐者抱怨伊拉克通往麦加的道路缺水，阿布·穆萨·阿沙里于是在此开凿水井；这里被称为「阿布·穆萨之井」，供从巴士拉出发的朝觐者使用。1444年，舍迈尔、阿奈扎及邻近贝都因部族在此给骆驼、绵羊和山羊饮水，商队也沿干河道路前行。哈费尔没有城墙环绕的城镇，它的重要性全在水井、牧场和穿越沙漠者可以依靠的停脚处。

en:
Yabrin is a watered hollow at the northern rim of the Rub' al Khali, about 210 kilometres south of Riyadh, the last oasis on the road out of Najd towards Oman. Its wells and date palms made it a caravan crossing of long standing, and travellers counted it the southernmost habitable ground before the sands of the Empty Quarter. The old walled town was already counted a ruin in the early modern centuries, its wells kept open for passing herdsmen and caravans. In 1444 camel nomads from the southern desert watered their herds here, and no town-based ruler claimed the oasis.

The nomads who used those wells were the Al Murrah, camel breeders who ranged between eastern Arabia and the edges of the Empty Quarter, and they handed the expanding Saudis one of their rare checks. In 1776 Abdulaziz ibn Muhammad of Diriyah raided south against them, and at Mukhayriq al-Safa the Murrah drove his men into a narrow defile and killed about sixty, among them Abdullah ibn Hasan, emir of Qasim, and Hudhul ibn Nasir Al Saud. Diriyah kept pressing south anyway, and as al-Hasa and Qatar came under its influence the Yabrin wells passed into the First Saudi State's loose tribal sphere. That lasted until 1818, when Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptians destroyed Diriyah and the oasis returned to Murrah hands.
zh:
耶卜林是鲁卜哈利沙漠北缘一片有水的洼地，在利雅得以南约210公里，是内志通往阿曼的道路上最后一片绿洲。水井和椰枣林使它久为商队中转之地，旅人把它看作进入空白之地沙海前最靠南的可居之处。古城在近代几个世纪里已被视为废墟，只有水井仍为过路的牧民和商队保留。1444年，南方沙漠的骆驼游牧人在此饮畜，没有哪个以城镇为根基的统治者领有这片绿洲。

用这些水井的是穆拉部落，他们牧放骆驼，游牧于阿拉伯东部与空白之地边缘之间，也曾让扩张中的沙特人少见地受挫。1776年，德拉伊耶的阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹·本·穆罕默德南征穆拉人，在穆海里格·萨法被穆拉人逼入狭窄隘口，折兵约六十人，死者中包括盖西姆埃米尔阿卜杜拉·本·哈桑和赫祖勒·本·纳赛尔·阿勒沙特。德拉伊耶并未止步，随着哈萨和卡塔尔先后落入其势力范围，耶卜林的水井也归入第一沙特国松散的部族势力圈。这一局面维持到1818年，易卜拉欣帕夏的埃及军队摧毁德拉伊耶，绿洲重归穆拉人之手。

en:
Grane, the old al-Qurayn, is a sheltered bay at the head of the Persian Gulf, where the wells of Kazima watered caravans and pilgrims travelling from Iraq into Arabia. It was at Kazima in April 633 that Khalid ibn al-Walid, in the first battle the caliph's army fought outside Arabia, routed the Sasanian army under Hormozd, remembered as the Battle of the Chains; and Kazima was the birthplace of the poet al-Farazdaq, one of the great satirical voices of the Umayyad age, whose verses later critics said preserved a third of the Arabic language. The port afterwards served the merchants of the Bahrayn coast before fading into tribal rule under the distant sway of Hormuz. Early in the fifteenth century the Banu Jabr made themselves masters of the whole western shore of the Gulf, and in 1444 the fishing and pearling hamlets of Grane lay on the northern edge of their amirate of al-Hasa.

Visitors to al-Qurayn in the following centuries found a bare fishing village, too stony for palms or grain, fed by wheat shipped from Basra. The Portuguese took the coast with Hormuz in 1507, and Ottoman governors and the Muntafiq chiefs of Basra disputed it after them, until the Bani Khalid drove the Turkish garrisons out of eastern Arabia about 1670. In 1716 the Utub clans, the Al Sabah, Al Khalifa and Al Jalahimah, settled the bay with Bani Khalid leave and divided its rule among their sheikhs, and in 1752 Sabah I ibn Jaber became the first independent sheikh of Kuwait. The Persian siege of Basra from 1775 to 1779 sent its merchants fleeing here with the India and Aleppo trade, and Kuwait grew into the busiest boatbuilding port on the Gulf, its ships known across the Indian Ocean; the East India Company moved its Gulf shipping there in 1792.
zh:
格雷恩古称古拉因，是波斯湾顶端一处避风海湾，岸边卡济马的水井曾供从伊拉克进入阿拉伯的商队和朝觐者歇脚。633年4月，哈立德·伊本·瓦利德正是在卡济马击溃霍尔木兹率领的萨珊军队，那是哈里发军队在阿拉伯之外打的第一仗，史称链条之战；卡济马还是诗人法拉兹达格的出生地，他是倭马亚时代最伟大的讽刺诗人之一，后世评家说，若无他的诗，阿拉伯语将失去三分之一的词汇。这个港口后来为巴林沿岸的商人效劳，随后湮没于部落自治，只在名义上远奉霍尔木兹。15世纪初，巴努·贾布尔成为整个海湾西岸的主人，1444年，格雷恩这些捕鱼采珠的村落正处在他们哈萨埃米尔国的北缘。

此后几百年，旅人见到的古拉因是个不毛的渔村，地上多石，长不出椰枣和粮食，每日靠从巴士拉海运小麦糊口。1507年，葡萄牙人随征服霍尔木兹一并拿下这段海岸；之后奥斯曼总督与巴士拉的蒙塔菲克首领反复争夺，直到约1670年巴尼·哈立德部落把土耳其驻军逐出阿拉伯东部。1716年，乌图布人的萨巴赫、哈利法、贾拉希马三族经巴尼·哈立德准许在海湾定居，三分其政；1752年，萨巴赫一世·伊本·贾比尔成为科威特第一位独立的谢赫。1775至1779年波斯围攻巴士拉，商人带着通往印度和阿勒颇的贸易逃来此地，科威特也成为海湾最繁忙的造船港，所造船只闻名整个印度洋；1792年，东印度公司也把海湾航运转到这里。

en:
Masirah is a long, narrow, arid island in the Arabian Sea, sixty miles from north to south and only eight or nine wide, separated from the Omani coast by a shallow channel. Its interior is empty desert and its villages cluster in the north. Copper was mined here around 1500 BC, when the land of Magan traded across the Gulf, and shards of Indus pottery have been found at the workings. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, written in the first century, calls it the Isle of Sarapis: three villages of fish-eating holy men who spoke Arabic, wore loincloths of palm leaves and sold fine tortoiseshell to passing merchants. Medieval dhows watered at its wells, and the geographer Yaqut al-Hamawi knew it as 'a great island in the sea of Oman, with several villages'. Its people were fishermen, boatbuilders and weavers, Ibadi Omanis sailing within the loose maritime empire of Hormuz; in 1444 the island answered to Hormuz and lived from its boats and looms.

Portuguese warships occupied Masirah in the 1500s. In 1650, when the Ya'rubi imams drove the Portuguese from Muscat, the island returned to Omani allegiance, but power stayed with its own sheikhs and headmen: their sailors built their own craft, fished the surrounding banks and sold dried fish and woven cloth on the Sharqiyah mainland. Few wars or courts disturbed it under the Busaid sultans, and Masirah remained a remote, self-sufficient island under the loose rule of Muscat.
zh:
马西拉是阿拉伯海中一座狭长干旱的岛屿，南北长约六十英里，宽仅八九英里，与阿曼本土隔着一道浅海海峡。岛的内陆是空旷的沙漠，村庄多集中在北部。约公元前1500年，岛上已有铜矿开采，当时马干的商船往来于海湾之上，矿址还出土过印度河流域的陶片。成书于1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》称这里为「萨拉皮斯岛」：岛上有三个村落，住着以鱼为食的圣者，他们说阿拉伯语，腰系棕榈叶，向来往的商人出售优质玳瑁。中世纪的帆船常到岛上的水井补给淡水，地理学家雅古特·哈马维称它是「阿曼海中一座大岛，岛上有数个村庄」。岛民是渔民、造船匠和织工，这些伊巴德派的阿曼人往来于霍尔木兹松散的海洋势力范围内；1444年，马西拉名义上臣服霍尔木兹，生计全靠自家的渔船和织机。

16世纪，葡萄牙舰队占领马西拉。1650年，叶阿里卜王朝的伊玛目把葡萄牙人逐出马斯喀特，马西拉随之重归阿曼，但实权仍在岛上的谢赫和头人手中：岛民自造船只，在周围渔场捕鱼，把鱼干和布匹销往东部地区本土。在赛义德王朝治下，少有战事和权贵打扰这座岛屿，马西拉始终是马斯喀特松散统治下一座偏远、自给自足的海岛。

en: Wusta is the empty middle of Oman's southern shore, where the stony plain of Jiddat al-Harasis runs back from the sea into waterless desert. Off the coast lie the five Khuriya Muriya islands, the Isles of Zenobios to the Greek sailors of the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea. Sheltered coves at Hasik and Sadah collected frankincense from the Qara country in antiquity, and the ruins of an old town stand beside Hasik's harbor. In 1444 this was remote Mahri ground, visited by little besides incense dhows and fishing boats. In May 1503 a storm caught the first Portuguese patrol in the Indian Ocean off these islands: two ships left behind by Vasco da Gama to prey on Red Sea trade were torn from their moorings and driven onto the rocks of Al-Hallaniyah, and their commander Vicente Sodré, da Gama's uncle, drowned on his carrack Esmeralda.
zh: 中部省是阿曼南岸中段一片空旷的海岸，哈拉西斯砾石平原从海边一直伸向没有水源的内陆沙漠。海岸外的五座哈拉尼亚特群岛，成书于1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》已经记载。古代，哈西克和塞代赫两处有天然遮蔽的港湾集散盖拉山地的乳香，哈西克港边留有古城废墟。1444年，这里是迈赫拉人偏远的土地，除了运乳香的帆船和渔船，少有来客。1503年5月，一场风暴在群岛外海袭击了葡萄牙人在印度洋的第一支巡逻舰队：瓦斯科·达·伽马留下袭扰红海贸易的两艘船被扯离锚地、推上哈拉尼亚岛的礁石，指挥官、达·伽马的舅父维森特·索德雷随他的克拉克帆船「埃斯梅拉达号」一同溺亡。

en:
The province covers the middle of Wadi Hadhramaut, a long valley cut through an arid plateau, whose spate floods and wells sustain palm gardens and mud-brick towns. Bedouin of the surrounding jol graze camels and goats on the plateau, and caravan roads climb from the incense ports of Shihr and Mukalla to the valley markets. Three towns lie a short ride apart. Shibam, twelve kilometres west of Say'un, is enclosed by a wall and packed with about five hundred mud-brick towers five to eleven storeys high, raised against Bedouin raiders, and the present town dates from its rebuilding in 1533. Sayun lies midway of the wadi, and Tarim, thirty-five kilometres east, is its seat of religious learning, crowded with sayyid families and scholars. The Al Kathir, a Bedouin clan turned dynasty, founded their sultanate in 1379, and in 1414 their sultan Ali bin Omar, backed by the scholars of the Hadhramaut, conquered Dhofar. In 1444 his state ran from the wadi to the Arabian Sea, and was fighting the Mahra for Shihr while the walled towns harvested dates and grain.

The Kathiri took Shihr from the Tahirids in 1462 and kept it after 1495, when Sultan Jafar bin 'Amr backed the winning Zwedi faction in the Mahri civil war. In 1501 Badr Abu Tuwairq made Sayun his capital, and under his long rule the sultanate stretched from Ain Bamabd in the west to the approaches of Dhofar in the east. In 1545 his kinsmen took Qishn with Ottoman guns, but a Portuguese fleet bombarded the town and returned it to the Mahra. Portuguese raids burned several coastal ports, while the wadi itself kept its mosques, scholars and date gardens. In the eighteenth century Yafa'i tribes from the southwestern highlands overran the valley towns, and by 1821 the Kathiri sultan held little beyond his palaces at Sayun, while rival Yafa'i houses held Shibam and the coast.
zh:
本省占据哈德拉毛干谷中段：干旱高原上裂开一条长谷，季节性洪水和井水滋养着谷中的椰枣园与土坯城镇。周围高原的贝都因人放牧骆驼和山羊，商队从希赫尔、穆卡拉等乳香港口翻山进入谷地集市。谷中三大城相距不远：赛云以西十二公里的希巴姆城墙环绕，城内挤着约五百座五至十一层高的土坯塔楼，为抵御贝都因袭扰而建，现存城建自1533年的重建；赛云地处干谷中段；东行三十五公里的塔里姆是谷地的宗教学术中心，聚居着大批圣裔家族和学者。卡西部落本是贝都因部族，1379年建立苏丹国；1414年，苏丹阿里·本·奥马尔在哈德拉毛学者支持下征服佐法尔。1444年，其国家从干谷延伸到阿拉伯海，正为争夺希赫尔与迈赫拉人交战，谷中诸城则凭城墙守护椰枣和谷物的收成。

卡西里人1462年从塔希尔王朝手中夺取希赫尔；1495年，苏丹贾法尔·本·阿慕尔在迈赫拉内战中支持获胜的兹韦迪一派，此后长期占有该港。1501年，巴德尔·艾布·图韦里格定都赛云，在他长期统治下，苏丹国疆域西起艾因巴曼卜德、东抵佐法尔边地。1545年，他的族人借奥斯曼火炮攻占基什恩，但葡萄牙舰队随即炮轰该城，把它交还迈赫拉人。葡萄牙人的袭扰焚毁了几座沿海港口，干谷里的清真寺、学者和椰枣园却安然无恙。18世纪，来自西南高原的亚法伊部落席卷谷地诸城；到1821年，卡西里苏丹的号令已不出赛云的宫殿，希巴姆与海岸都掌握在敌对的亚法伊家族手中。

en: Marib was the capital of Saba, wealthiest of the old South Arabian kingdoms, which many scholars identify with the Sheba of the Bible. Across Wadi Adhanah its kings raised the Great Dam from the eighth century BC, watering the palm groves and fields around the temples of the moon god Almaqah at Awwam and Barran while caravans carried frankincense and myrrh north into the desert. In 25 BC a Roman army under Aelius Gallus reached the city and failed to take it. Breaches scattered the oasis farmers across the centuries; the last, left unrepaired after the dam was overtopped in the 570s, is remembered in the Quran as the Flood of Arim, after which tens of thousands moved north and Marib became a small town amid its own ruins. In 1444 its people lived from date gardens and flocks under tribes loosely tied to the Zaydi imams of Sanaa, and Ottoman rule never reached the arid east; under the Qasimid imam al-Mutawakkil Isma'il (1644-1676) its pastoral clans were counted among the tribes of the imamate.
zh: 马里卜是古代南阿拉伯诸王国中最富庶的塞巴王国之都，不少学者认为塞巴就是《圣经》中的示巴。公元前8世纪起，塞巴诸王在宰奈河上筑起大马里卜水坝，灌溉月神阿穆格的阿瓦姆、巴兰两座神庙周围的椰枣园与农田，商队则载着乳香、没药向北深入沙漠。公元前25年，埃利乌斯·加卢斯率罗马军队兵临城下，却未能破城。此后数百年间水坝多次溃决，绿洲农户一次次流散；最后一次在570年代漫坝后再未修复，《古兰经》称之为「阿里姆洪水」，数万人口随后北迁，马里卜沦为栖身废墟之间的小镇。1444年，居民以椰枣园和畜群为生，所属部落松散地依附于萨那的扎伊迪派伊玛目，奥斯曼人的统治始终没有深入干旱的东部；卡西姆王朝的穆塔瓦基勒·伊斯玛仪（1644—1676年在位）时，这里的游牧部落被算作伊玛目治下的部众。

en:
Beihan, also called Bayhan al-Qasab, is the market town of Wadi Bayhan, whose seasonal floods water fields along the desert edge. In antiquity this was Qataban, one of the six kingdoms of ancient South Arabia: its kings bore the title mukarrib and ruled from Timna, where camel caravans carrying frankincense stopped on the road from Shabwa to Gaza and Petra. Strabo and Pliny both recorded the Qatabanians, whom they called the Gebbanitae, and the kingdom ended in the late first century when Hadhramaut and Himyar divided its lands. By the fifteenth century the wadi was livestock country on the inland fringe of Rasulid Yemen, run by its own tribes, among them the Fuqara, Masabin and Banu Harith. In 1444 the Rasulid sultans at Zabid and Taiz were weakened by plague and succession wars and had little hold over Beihan.

The Rasulid realm passed to the Tahirid clan in 1454. Around 1500, in the reign of Sultan Amir ibn Abd al-Wahhab, a Jewish messianic movement arose near Bayhan and organized its followers into a fighting force before the sultan's troops crushed it. Ottoman armies reached inland Yemen after 1538, but Imam al-Mansur al-Qasim raised the Qasimid revolt in 1597, and tribal forces drove the Ottomans out of Yemen by 1638. As the imamate broke apart in the following century, the tribes of Wadi Bayhan ran their own affairs.
zh:
拜汉又称拜汉·盖萨卜，是拜汉干谷的集镇，季节性洪水浇灌着沙漠边缘的田地。古时这里是卡塔班，古代南阿拉伯六国之一：国王称「穆卡里布」，定都提姆纳；运送乳香的驼队从沙布瓦前往加沙和佩特拉，途中在提姆纳歇脚。斯特拉波和老普林尼都记载过卡塔班人，称之为格巴尼特人；王国在1世纪末灭亡，土地被哈德拉毛和希木叶尔瓜分。到15世纪，干谷已成拉苏勒也门内陆边缘的畜牧之地，由富卡拉、马斯阿宾、拜尼·哈里斯等本地部落自行治理。1444年，驻在扎比德和塔伊兹的拉苏勒苏丹们饱受瘟疫和继承战争削弱，对拜汉已鞭长莫及。

1454年，拉苏勒疆域转入塔希尔家族之手。约1500年，在苏丹阿米尔·伊本·阿卜杜勒·瓦哈卜统治期间，拜汉附近兴起一场犹太弥赛亚运动，追随者被编成武装，最终遭到苏丹军队镇压。1538年后奥斯曼军队深入也门内陆，但伊玛目曼苏尔·卡西姆于1597年发动卡西姆派起事，部落武装到1638年把奥斯曼人逐出也门。此后一个世纪伊玛目国家分裂，拜汉干谷诸部自行其是。

en:
Jazan is the Red Sea anchorage of the historical al-Mikhlaf al-Sulaymani, the coastal plain and hill country between the Hijaz and Yemen, with the Farasan Islands some forty-five kilometres out to sea. The Quraysh of Mecca knew the coastal road, using it on their journeys to Yemen and Abyssinia, and caravans linked the anchorage with Abu Arish inland, once called Darb al-Naja, a pilgrim station and former capital of the Mikhlaf. The town stands on a bed of rock salt, and salt dug from the hill behind it and fish from the shallows of the wadi mouth were the place's trade. In 1444 the Sulaymani sharifs still ruled its villages and forts, and Bandar Jizan served chiefly as the modest sea outlet of Wadi Jizan.

Ottoman power reached the coast after Hadım Suleiman Pasha stormed Aden in 1538 and took Zabid in 1539, and Jazan became the port of the Abu Arish sanjak on the new Yemeni frontier. During the 1620s and 1630s the Qasimid imams drove the Ottoman garrisons out of Yemen, and the weight of affairs shifted back to Abu Arish. In 1728-29 the descendants of Sharif Khayrat bin Shubayr set up a state of their own there; under the Al Khayrat rulers Jizan remained a small fishing anchorage guarded by coastal forts.
zh:
贾赞是历史上苏莱曼米赫莱夫在红海上的泊口，这片地区地处汉志与也门之间，兼有沿海平原和山地，法尔桑群岛就在外海约四十五公里处。麦加的古莱什人走熟了这条沿海道路，往返也门和阿比西尼亚都取道于此；商队把泊地与内陆的阿布阿里什连在一起，那里旧称德尔卜·纳贾，曾是朝圣驿站和米赫莱夫的都城。城镇坐落在岩盐层上，背后山中采出的食盐和河口浅滩捕来的鱼货是当地的贸易物产。1444年，苏莱曼系谢里夫仍统治着这里的村落与堡寨，贾赞港主要只是贾赞干谷规模不大的出海口。

1538年哈迪姆·苏莱曼帕夏攻陷亚丁、1539年夺取扎比德后，奥斯曼势力抵达这段海岸，贾赞成为新征服的也门边地上阿布阿里什桑贾克的港口。1620至1630年代，卡西姆伊玛目把奥斯曼守军逐出也门，事务的重心重新转回阿布阿里什。1728—1729年，谢里夫·海拉特·本·舒拜尔的后裔在那里建立了自己的政权；在海拉特家族统治者治下，贾赞仍是一座由海岸堡寨护卫的小型渔业泊口。

en:
Al-Ahsa is the great oasis of eastern Arabia, lying some forty miles inland from the Persian Gulf, where more than thirty fresh-water springs feed a wide ring of date gardens in the desert. The cities of Hofuf and al-Mubarraz stand there, on the ground of old Hajar. In 899 the Qarmatians, a millenarian Ismaili sect, seized the oasis and made it their capital. Abu Tahir al-Jannabi led his followers out from it against Mecca in 930, threw the dead into the Zamzam well and carried the Black Stone back to Hajar; the Abbasid caliphs ransomed it only in 951. When the Persian traveller Nasir Khusraw visited in 1051, he found a city where some 30,000 Ethiopian slaves worked the fruit estates, the people paid no taxes and trade ran on lead tokens. After the Qarmatians fell, the Uyunids, Usfurids and Jarwanids ruled in turn, until the Bedouin Banu Jabr stormed the oasis in 1417. In 1444 their Jabrids ruled al-Hasa and Qatif from Hofuf, their power stretching from the Iraqi border toward Oman, and their riders guarded the pilgrim road from Iraq to Mecca.

The last decades of the house turned on Bahrain. Muqrin ibn Zamil, who held al-Hasa, Qatif and the islands, fell fighting the Portuguese there in 1521, and five years later Rashid ibn Mughamis of the Muntafiq marched in from Basra and ended the dynasty. In 1550 the people of the oasis, preferring the Ottomans of Süleyman I to a Portuguese landing, accepted an imperial garrison. The new province of Lahsa built the Qasr Ibrahim in Hofuf from 1555, a fortress enclosing a domed mosque, a prison and a bathhouse; in 1559 its governor Mustafa Pasha sailed from it to besiege Bahrain and failed. Ottoman rule never ran deep among the palm groves. The Bani Khalid rose against the garrisons, and in 1670 they expelled the last Turks and made al-Mubarraz their capital. The Wahhabi army of Diriyah took the oasis in 1795, and in 1818 the Egyptian forces of Muhammad Ali, sent against the Saudis, retook it and restored the Bani Khalid under Ottoman overlordship.
zh:
哈萨绿洲是阿拉伯东部最大的绿洲，在波斯湾以南约六十公里的内陆，三十多处清泉在沙漠中滋养出大片椰枣园，胡富夫和穆巴拉斯两座城就坐落在古城哈贾尔的故地。899年，信奉救世思想的伊斯玛仪支派卡尔马特派夺取绿洲，在此定都。930年，卡尔马特派从这里奔袭麦加，把死者投入渗渗泉，并将天房黑石劫回哈贾尔；阿拔斯王朝的哈里发直到951年才付赎金将其迎回。波斯旅行家纳赛尔·霍斯鲁1051年到访时，看到城里的果园由约三万名埃塞俄比亚奴隶耕作，居民不纳赋税，买卖用铅铸的代币。卡尔马特政权灭亡后，乌尤尼、欧斯福尔、贾尔万三个王朝相继统治，1417年贝都因巴努·贾布尔部攻陷绿洲。1444年，贾布里德政权以胡富夫为都城，领有哈萨和盖提夫，势力从伊拉克边境伸展到阿曼一带，其骑兵还护卫着从伊拉克前往麦加的朝觐道路。

这个王朝最后几十年的命运系于巴林。领有哈萨、盖提夫和巴林诸岛的穆克林·伊本·扎米勒1521年在巴林与葡萄牙人作战时阵亡；五年后，蒙塔菲克部落的拉希德·伊本·穆加米斯从巴士拉进军绿洲，终结了贾布里德王朝。1550年，绿洲居民宁可接受苏莱曼一世的奥斯曼驻军，也不愿葡萄牙人登陆；新设的拉赫萨省1555年起在胡富夫修筑易卜拉欣宫，这是一座围有穹顶清真寺、监狱和浴室的要塞。1559年，省长穆斯塔法帕夏从这里出师围攻巴林，兵败而归。奥斯曼的统治在椰枣园间始终不深，巴尼·哈立德部起兵反抗，1670年逐出最后一批土耳其人，以穆巴拉斯为都城。1795年，德拉伊耶的瓦哈比军队夺取绿洲；1818年，穆罕默德·阿里派来讨伐沙特的埃及军队将其攻占，在奥斯曼宗主权下恢复了巴尼·哈立德的统治。

en:
Chios lies only a few miles from the Anatolian shore, and its most profitable ground is the dry south, where the mastic villages tend lentisk trees. Farmers cut the bark and collected the scented resin that Genoese warehouses shipped across the Mediterranean. A Greek Orthodox majority worked the fields, vineyards and port, while Latin merchants held the castle and accounts.
