The Zenata chief Ziri ibn Atiyya founded it as a garrison town in 994, after his Maghrawa tribesmen had been settled at Fez and he moved back east to be nearer their homeland. Its history was set by that road: the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub razed the town in 1271 after defeating the Zayyanid Yaghmorasan, and when Marinid forces came back in 1296 they rebuilt the walls, a palace and the Great Mosque. In 1444 Oujda was a contested Muslim frontier market on the western edge of the Zayyanid kingdom of Tlemcen, living on overland traffic and the wool and flocks of its Berber hinterland, with Marinid Fez still pressing from the west.

From the sixteenth century the town stood between the Saadi and Alaouite sultans of Morocco and the Ottoman Regency of Algiers, and its allegiance followed the fighting around Tlemcen. Moulay Isma'il, who ruled Morocco from 1672 to 1727, made it a fortified Alaouite march, adding walls and garrisons to secure his eastern border. After his death succession crises loosened the court's hold on this distant frontier, until Alaouite forces retook the town in 1795 and kept Oujda inside the Moroccan realm.
zh:
乌季达坐落在贝尼·伊兹纳桑山下的安加德平原，正当非斯通往特莱姆森的大道，西马格里布与中马格里布在这里相接。泽纳塔马格拉瓦部首领齐里·伊本·阿提耶于994年建城驻军：他的部众曾被安置在非斯，他却东返故土，在靠近本乡的地方立起这座城。这座城的命运也系于这条大道：1271年，马林苏丹阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白击败扎扬王朝的叶格穆拉辛后将乌季达夷平；1296年马林军队再占此地，重修城墙、宫殿和大清真寺。1444年，乌季达是特莱姆森扎扬王国西缘反复易手的穆斯林边境集市，靠陆路商队和柏柏尔腹地的羊群、羊毛维生，西方马林王朝治下的非斯仍在步步进逼。

16世纪起，乌季达夹在摩洛哥的萨阿德、阿拉维两朝苏丹与奥斯曼阿尔及尔摄政政权之间，归属随特莱姆森一带的战局变化。1672年至1727年在位的穆莱·伊斯梅尔把它改造成设防的阿拉维边镇，增筑城墙、驻扎守军以拱卫东部边界。他死后继承危机不断，朝廷对这片遥远边地的控制松弛下来，直到1795年阿拉维军队收复乌季达，才把它稳稳压在摩洛哥境内。

en:
The Draa is Morocco's longest river, running 1,100 kilometres from the High Atlas to the Atlantic. Its valley is a chain of palm oases and walled ksour fed by irrigation canals, whose caravan stations joined the Atlas crossings to the great western road to Timbuktu. Salt from the Sahara and gold from the Niger bend moved north through them. At the valley's centre lay the district of Tagmadert, where a family of sharifs claiming origin at Yanbu had settled early in the fourteenth century. By the mid-fifteenth century the Marinid sultans in Fez had little hold on the south, and in 1444 the Draa oases managed their affairs through local chiefs and Sufi brotherhoods while caravans still passed north to Marrakesh and the Sous and south into the desert.

In 1510 the Tagmadert sharif Muhammad al-Qa'im was called to the Sous to lead its tribes against the Portuguese, and his sons Ahmad al-Araj and Muhammad al-Shaykh became the founders of the Saadian dynasty. In the 1540s Tuareg raiders sent by Askia Ishaq I of Songhai swept through the valley when the two powers quarrelled over the salt mines of Taghaza. Muhammad al-Shaykh, who called himself al-Drawi, 'the man of the Draa', founded the town of Tagmadert in 1550. Forty years later Ahmad al-Mansur's invasion army gathered in these oases before crossing the desert. Judar Pasha, a Spanish-born commander, led about four thousand musketeers and horsemen to the Niger; their firearms broke the Songhai host at Tondibi in 1591 and opened Gao and Timbuktu to the Moroccans, and the soldiers left behind ruled Timbuktu as the Arma pashalik. Under Moulay Ismail the valley became an appanage governed by the sultan's sons with the title khalifa. Tagmadert never recovered from the troubles of the early nineteenth century. The Aït Atta Berbers probably sacked it, as they did Sijilmasa in 1818, and only an irrigation canal kept the name alive.
zh:
德拉河是摩洛哥最长的河流，从大阿特拉斯山奔流1100公里注入大西洋。河谷中是一连串靠灌溉渠滋养的椰枣绿洲和设防城堡村，村里的商站把阿特拉斯山区的各山口与通往通布图的西路干道连在一起，撒哈拉的盐、尼日尔河湾的黄金经此北运。河谷中心是塔格马德特地区，14世纪初便有一支自称源自延布的圣裔家族定居于此。15世纪中期，非斯的马林苏丹对南方已无力掌控，1444年的德拉绿洲由本地首领和苏菲教团自行治理，商队仍北往马拉喀什和苏斯、南入撒哈拉。

1510年，塔格马德特圣裔穆罕默德·卡伊姆被请往苏斯，领导各部族抵抗葡萄牙人，他的儿子艾哈迈德·阿拉杰和穆罕默德·谢赫成为萨阿德王朝的开创者。1540年代，双方为塔加扎盐矿反目，桑海的阿斯基亚·伊沙克一世派图阿雷格骑手袭掠河谷。自称「德拉人」的穆罕默德·谢赫于1550年建起塔格马德特城。四十年后，艾哈迈德·曼苏尔的西征大军在这些绿洲集结，随后穿越沙漠。西班牙裔将领朱达尔·帕夏率约四千火绳枪兵和骑兵进抵尼日尔河，火枪在1591年的通迪比战役击溃桑海大军，为摩洛哥人打开加奥和通布图；留守的士兵形成阿尔马人集团，以帕夏的名义统治通布图。穆莱·伊斯梅尔在位时，河谷成为封邑，由苏丹众子以哈里发的头衔统辖。塔格马德特没能从19世纪初的动乱中恢复，艾特阿塔柏柏尔人可能洗劫了它，一如他们1818年对待西吉勒马萨那样，只剩一条灌溉渠还留着这个名字。

en:
Meknes began as Miknasa Berber villages on the Saïss plain, country so planted with olives that Arab writers called it the Meknes of the olives. The Almoravids placed a garrison fortress, Tagrart, beside the settlements; the Nejjarine Mosque comes from that early military town. Almohad troops destroyed it in the twelfth century, and Muhammad al-Nasir later rebuilt its walls, mosque and aqueduct. Marinid rulers took Meknes in 1244, added a kasbah in 1276 and founded the Bou Inania Madrasa in 1336. By 1444 it was a prosperous market town for olive oil, grain and cloth, a frequent residence for princes and viziers, with Fez a day's ride to the east.

The town's imperial turn came under Moulay Ismail. His brother Moulay Rashid made him governor of Fez and the north, and when Rashid died in 1672 Ismail chose Meknes rather than Fez as his capital, outside the influence of Fez's scholars. During his fifty-five-year reign he raised a palace-city beside the old medina behind more than forty kilometres of walls. Its works included the Dar al-Kebira finished in 1679, the Bab Berda'in Mosque, vast granaries and the House of the Ten Norias, whose water wheels supplied the palaces through pipes. The Black Guard and tribal garrisons held the gates. The ceremonial Bab al-Mansur was designed by a former Christian slave who had converted to Islam; it was still unfinished at Ismail's death and was completed by Moulay Abdallah in 1732.

After Ismail died in 1727, the Black Guard and his rival sons made and unmade sultans, and Meknes lost the court. The Lisbon earthquake of 1755 shattered much of the palace quarter. Later 'Alawi rulers kept a residence here and were buried near Ismail, but by 1821 the great gates and granaries overlooked the market centre of some of Morocco's richest farmland.
zh:
梅克内斯起于赛斯平原上的米克纳萨柏柏尔村落；这里橄榄树密布，阿拉伯作者称它为「橄榄的米克纳萨」。穆拉比特人在村旁设下塔格拉尔特驻军要塞，纳贾林清真寺就出自这座早期军镇。12世纪穆瓦希德军队摧毁该城，后来穆罕默德·纳赛尔重修城墙、清真寺和引水渠。马林王朝1244年攻取梅克内斯，1276年添建城堡，1336年创办布伊纳尼亚学院。到1444年，它已是橄榄油、谷物和布匹贸易兴盛的集镇，常有王公和维齐尔驻留，都城非斯则在东面一日骑程之外。

梅克内斯的帝王转折来自穆莱·伊斯梅尔。其兄穆莱·拉希德任命他管辖非斯和北方；1672年拉希德死后，伊斯梅尔没有选择非斯，而是把都城定在梅克内斯，以避开非斯学者的牵制。在位55年间，他在老麦地那旁筑起一座宫城，城墙绵延40多公里。工程包括1679年完工的大达尔宫、巴布·贝尔达因清真寺、巨型粮仓和十架水车房；水车把水送入管道，供应各处宫殿。黑奴禁军和部落驻军把守城门。典礼正门曼苏尔门由一名改信伊斯兰教的前基督徒奴隶设计，伊斯梅尔去世时仍未完工，1732年由穆莱·阿卜杜拉主持建成。

1727年伊斯梅尔去世后，黑奴禁军和争位诸子废立苏丹，梅克内斯随即失去都城地位。1755年里斯本大地震震毁大片宫区。后来的阿拉维君主仍在此保留住所，并葬在伊斯梅尔附近；到1821年，宏伟的城门和粮仓俯瞰着这座服务摩洛哥最肥沃农田之一的集贸中心。

en:
Tadla is the grain plain between the High and Middle Atlas, crossed by the Oum Er-Rbia. Its Amazigh name means 'the sheaf', after the wheat grown in the river valley. The crossing at Kasba Tadla mattered because armies and caravans moving between Fez and Marrakesh had to pass there; the Almohads kept a fortress on the site and a son of Abd al-Mu'min governed the district from it. Later Marinid rule let the old fort decay while rebels used the nearby hills. In 1444 Tadla was border country between the Marinid sultan in Fez to the north and the Hintata emirs of Marrakesh to the south, where Tadla tribes pastured cattle and raised wheat between the Atlas slopes and the river.

The plain became a dynastic frontier in the Saadi-Wattasid wars. After fighting at Wadi al-'Abid, the Treaty of Tadla in 1527 recognised Saadi rule over the Sus and Marrakesh while the Wattasids kept Fez. The settlement allowed the Saadis to turn against the Portuguese and take Agadir in 1541. When war resumed, Mohammed al-Shaykh defeated the remaining Wattasid army at the Battle of Tadla in 1554 and retook Fez, opening the road from southern Morocco to a reunited sultanate.

Moulay Ismail later turned the crossing back into a garrison. He settled Guettaya, Samguet and Ait Ma'dane Arabs with the local Tadla people as the Ait Rob'a, a guich confederation that held land in return for military service. On the old Almohad ruin rose the rectangular Kasbah Tadla, with granaries, a mosque and hidden stairways; his son Ahmad ad-Dhahabi added houses and the bridge over the Oum Er-Rbia later credited to the Portuguese. In 1821 the fort and its tribal camps still guarded the road for wheat and cattle.
zh:
塔德莱是大阿特拉斯山与中阿特拉斯山之间的谷物平原，乌姆赖比阿河横穿其间。它的柏柏尔语名字意为「麦穗」，说的是河谷里种植的小麦。今塔德莱堡所在的渡口扼守非斯与马拉喀什之间的通道，军队和商队都要经过；穆瓦希德王朝在此驻军，阿卜杜勒·穆明的一个儿子曾由这里统辖地方。马林王朝后期，旧堡失修，叛乱者也借附近山地藏身。1444年，这里是南北两强之间的边地：北面是非斯的马林苏丹，南面是马拉喀什的欣塔塔埃米尔；塔德莱诸部在阿特拉斯山坡与河谷之间牧牛、种麦。

萨阿德王朝与瓦塔斯王朝开战时，这片平原成了王朝边界。瓦迪阿比德之战后，双方在1527年签订《塔德莱条约》，承认萨阿德人统治苏斯和马拉喀什，瓦塔斯王朝则保有非斯。休战使萨阿德人能转而对付葡萄牙人，并在1541年夺取阿加迪尔。战火重开后，穆罕默德·谢赫1554年在塔德莱之战击溃瓦塔斯残军，随后收复非斯，从南方打通了重建统一苏丹国的道路。

穆莱·伊斯梅尔后来把渡口重新变成军镇。他把盖塔亚、萨姆古特和艾特·迈丹三支阿拉伯人迁来，与当地塔德莱人合编为艾特·鲁巴阿军屯同盟，以土地换取兵役。穆瓦希德旧堡遗址上建起长方形的塔德莱堡，内有粮仓、清真寺和暗道；其子艾哈迈德·宰海比又添建民居和乌姆赖比阿河大桥，这座桥后来被误传为葡萄牙人所造。1821年，城堡和周围的军屯部落仍守着这条运送小麦与牲畜的道路。

en:
Dukkala is the broad coastal plain between the Oum Er-Rbia and the Tensift, the grain country south of Anfa. Its people, the Doukkala, were a Masmuda Berber confederation; they took the Almoravid side when the Almohads took Marrakesh in 1147 and rose under the Sufi preacher Yaddar al-Dukkali. Caliph Abd al-Mu'min crushed the revolt, sold off women and children, and settled defeated Banu Hilal Arabs on the land, so that by 1500 Arabs made up most of the plain. The roadstead off its shore was called Mazighan, where an old tower, al-Burayja, stood above the anchorage. In 1444 the tribes sowed their grain and ran their own affairs under the failing Marinids, and no town yet stood at Mazighan.

The Portuguese came to the anchorage in 1502, when Captain Jorge de Mello, driven in by a storm, held the old tower against the locals. In summer 1514 the brothers Diogo and Francisco de Arruda built a four-towered citadel there, and the place became Mazagão. After John III gave up Safi and Azemmour in 1541, Mazagão received stronger walls the next year, and the garrisons and settlers of the abandoned towns moved in, making it Portugal's last Moroccan possession; behind the walls stood a Manueline church and a great vaulted cistern. It held out until 1769, when Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah's army closed around it. The garrison marched out on terms and blew up the governor's bastion, and most of the inhabitants were shipped to Brazil, where they founded Nova Mazagão. The empty town was called al-Mahdouma, 'the Ruined'. In May 1815 the Doukkala joined the Abda in revolt and drove out their governor, in the troubles of Moulay Slimane's last years.
zh:
杜卡拉是乌姆赖比阿河与坦西夫特河之间的广阔沿海平原，即安法以南的谷物之乡。当地的杜卡拉人本是马斯穆达系柏柏尔人的部落联盟，1147年穆瓦希德王朝攻取马拉喀什时，他们站在穆拉比特王朝一边，又在苏菲传道者亚达尔·杜卡利率领下起兵。哈里发阿卜杜勒·穆敏镇压叛乱，掠卖妇孺，并把降服的希拉勒系阿拉伯部落安置到这片土地上，到1500年阿拉伯人已占平原人口的多数。海岸外的锚地叫马齐甘，岸上立着旧塔布雷贾。1444年，马林王朝衰微，各部落自行种粮、各自为政，马齐甘还没有城镇。

葡萄牙人1502年来到这片锚地，船长若热·德·梅洛的船被风暴逼入港中，他率人据守旧塔，抵挡当地人。1514年夏，迪奥戈·德·阿鲁达与弗朗西斯科·德·阿鲁达兄弟在塔旁筑起四角带城楼的城堡，此地得名马扎甘。若昂三世1541年放弃萨菲和艾宰穆尔后，次年给马扎甘环筑更厚的城墙，弃守各据点的驻军和居民纷纷迁入，使它成为葡萄牙在摩洛哥的最后领地；城墙之内有曼努埃尔式教堂和宏大的拱顶蓄水池。马扎甘一直守到1769年，穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉苏丹的大军将它合围，守军依约撤出并引爆总督棱堡，居民大多被送往巴西，在那里建起新马扎甘。空城得名迈赫杜马，意为「被毁者」。1815年5月，杜卡拉人联合阿卜达人起事，驱逐了自己的总督，时当穆莱·苏莱曼晚年的乱局。

en:
The Haha, Iḥaḥan in their own Shilha tongue, are a Masmuda Berber confederation on the Atlantic flank of the western High Atlas, holding the coast from the bay of Mogador south toward the Sous. Leo Africanus, who visited in the early sixteenth century, found a hard land of crags, forests and narrow streams, crowded with goats and donkeys; the clans grew barley and millet, kept bees for honey, and pressed cooking oil from the argan trees on the dry slopes. In 1444 this country answered to Marrakesh. On the shore there was as yet no town, only an anchorage sheltered by the island of Mogador, named after Sidi Mogdoul, a Muslim saint buried nearby.

European powers kept testing that bay. In 1506 King Manuel I of Portugal put up Castelo Real de Mogador on the shore, and the local Regraga brotherhood stormed it four years later. Spanish, English, Dutch and French ships contested the anchorage through the rest of the century, for it shipped out Sous sugar and molasses and gave corsairs a base. In 1629 Isaac de Razilly, acting for Richelieu, landed a hundred Frenchmen and building stores on Mogador island and withdrew within days. The port that lasted was built from scratch: in 1760 the Alawid sultan Mohammed bin Abdallah set Théodore Cornut and the Englishman Ahmed al-Inglizi to lay out Essaouira, a walled town made for foreign merchants and the caravans coming up from Marrakesh, part of the work done by French captives taken at Larache in 1765. The sultan settled Jewish trading families in their own mellah, and by the end of the century Mogador had overtaken every other port in Morocco.
zh:
哈哈，什卢赫语中称伊哈哈恩，是马斯穆达系柏柏尔人的部落联盟，住在西阿特拉斯山面向大西洋的坡地上，海岸北起摩加多尔湾，南抵苏斯方向。16世纪初游历此地的利奥·阿非利加努斯写道，这是一片山崖、森林与细流交错的粗粝山地，遍地山羊和驴；各氏族种大麦和黍，养蜂取蜜，还用干旱坡地上阿甘树的果仁榨油食用。1444年，此地听命于马拉喀什。海边还没有城镇，只有摩加多尔岛屏障下的一处锚地，名字来自葬在附近的穆斯林圣徒西迪·莫格杜勒。

欧洲列强反复试探这座海湾。1506年，葡萄牙国王曼努埃尔一世在岸边修筑摩加多尔王家城堡，四年后就被当地雷格拉加兄弟会攻下。此后大半个世纪，西班牙、英格兰、尼德兰和法国船只反复争夺这处锚地：苏斯的蔗糖和糖蜜从这里装船，海盗也在此落脚。1629年，为黎塞留效力的伊萨克·德·拉齐利率一百名法国人带着建材登上摩加多尔岛，没几天便撤走。真正扎下根的港口是另起炉灶建成的：1760年，阿拉维苏丹穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉命泰奥多尔·科尔尼和英格兰人艾哈迈德·因吉利齐规划索维拉，一座为外国商人和从马拉喀什北上的商队修造的设防新城，部分劳役由1765年拉腊什一役俘获的法国人承担。苏丹安置犹太商贸家族，让他们住在自己的梅拉（犹太坊）内；到18世纪末，摩加多尔已超过摩洛哥其他所有港口。

en:
Ouargla is the great palm oasis of the Wadi Mya basin in the central Sahara, watered by underground courses and once the largest palm grove in Algeria. The Banu Wargla, a Zenata Berber clan that had migrated from the Tlemcen country, built the old ksar in the eighth century and adopted Ibadi doctrines. When the Fatimids destroyed Tahert in 909, Rustamid exiles made nearby Sedrata their capital; a Hammadid raid at the end of the eleventh century drove the people to build the present walled town, with seven gates and two Friday mosques, the Ibadi Lalla Azza and the Maliki Lalla Malkia. After Sedrata was destroyed in the thirteenth century, Ouargla was left the only city of the region; a Hafsid sultan of Tunis entered it and raised its great mosque, and Ibn Khaldun called it 'the gate of the desert', through which Mzab merchants carried their goods to the land of the blacks. In 1444 the oasis was still mostly independent under its own Ibadi lords, living on the caravan trade in gold and slaves.

In 1552 Salah Raïs of Algiers marched past Touggourt against Ouargla, and its sultan fled with four thousand horsemen to El Golea, leaving the town to its merchants and marabouts. The oasis submitted and promised tribute, was attached to the Beylik of the East at Constantine, and the Friday prayer was said in the name of the Ottoman caliph; the Said Atba became its makhzen tribe, holding the country for the regency. The Sudan caravans were soon diverted to Touggourt, and the old 'gate of the desert' faded into a quiet oasis, while the ruins of Sedrata, out in the desert, remained a place of Ibadi pilgrimage.
zh:
瓦尔格拉是撒哈拉腹地米耶河盆地中的大绿洲，靠地下暗河供水，椰枣林曾为阿尔及利亚之冠。8世纪时，从特莱姆森一带来的扎纳塔柏柏尔人巴努·瓦尔格拉部建起旧堡寨，改奉伊巴德派。909年法蒂玛王朝摧毁塔赫尔特后，罗斯图姆遗民在附近的塞德拉塔定都；11世纪末哈马德王朝的一次袭掠迫使居民修筑今城，新城开有七座城门，建有两座聚礼清真寺，伊巴德派的称拉拉·阿扎，马立克派的称拉拉·马尔基。13世纪塞德拉塔被毁，瓦尔格拉成为这一带唯一的城市；突尼斯的哈夫斯苏丹曾入城并敕建大清真寺，伊本·赫勒敦称它为「沙漠之门」，姆扎卜商人带货南下黑非洲都要取道于此。1444年，绿洲仍由本地伊巴德派首领统治，大半独立，靠黄金和奴隶的商队贸易为生。

1552年，阿尔及尔的萨拉赫·拉伊斯越过图古尔特进兵瓦尔格拉，当地苏丹率四千骑兵逃往古莱阿，城中只剩商人与隐士。绿洲称臣纳贡，被划归君士坦丁的东部贝伊辖区，周五聚礼改以奥斯曼哈里发的名义诵读，赛义德·阿特巴部成为替摄政国镇守此地的麦赫赞部落。通往黑非洲的商队不久改走图古尔特，这座老「沙漠之门」冷清下来，沙漠深处的塞德拉塔废墟则仍是伊巴德派的朝谒之地。

en:
The port of Susa (Arabic Sūsa, French Sousse), on the Gulf of Hammamet, covers the ruins of Hadrumetum, a Tyrian foundation older than Carthage which grew to be the second city of Roman Africa and capital of Byzacena. Roman writers tell that Julius Caesar, landing here in 46 BC in pursuit of his rivals, tripped on the shore and turned the bad omen into a boast by gripping the sand and crying 'I hold you, Africa'; the jurist Salvius Julianus, who gave Roman law its permanent praetorian edict under Hadrian, was a native son. The Vandals sacked the city in 434, the Byzantines retook and refortified it in 534, and the conquest of Uqba ibn Nafi left it in ruins.

The Aghlabids built Susa beside those ruins and made it their chief port. In 827 their fleet sailed from this roadstead to begin the conquest of Sicily, and when Malta fell in 870 marble from its churches was shipped here for the Ribat, a fortress whose tower served at once as watchtower and as the minaret of its mosque; an inscription of 821 names the emir Ziyadat Allah I. A Sicilian-Norman fleet under George of Antioch stormed the town in 1148. In 1444 Susa was the first port of the Hafsid Sahel, its weavers famous for Sūsī silk and linen and for the ready-made shuqqa robes sold across the Mediterranean.

After Mahdia declined, Susa led the towns of the Sahel with some 15,000 inhabitants. A joint Spanish-Maltese assault was beaten back with heavy loss in 1537, and with the Ottoman conquest of 1574 its seamen joined the Barbary corso. The old Ribat was restored in 1722. Angelo Emo's Venetian fleet bombarded Susa in 1784 and again in 1785, during a four-year campaign meant to force Hammuda Pasha to rein in his pirates; the walls held, and the bombardment settled nothing.
zh:
苏塞（阿拉伯语称苏萨）位于哈马马特湾，港城建在哈德鲁梅图姆的废墟之上。这座推罗人建立的古城比迦太基还要古老，后来成为罗马阿非利加的第二大城、拜扎凯纳行省的首府。罗马作家记载，公元前46年尤利乌斯·凯撒追击政敌在此登陆，失足跌上海滩，便抓起一把沙子高喊「阿非利加，我抓住你了」，把凶兆变成了豪言；在哈德良皇帝治下主持编定裁判官永久敕令的法学家萨尔维乌斯·尤利安努斯，就出生在这里。汪达尔人434年洗劫此城，拜占庭人534年收复并重修工事，欧格白·伊本·纳菲的征服则把它夷为废墟。

阿格拉布王朝在废墟旁营建苏萨，定为首要军港。827年，舰队从这片锚地启航，开启征服西西里之战；870年马耳他陷落，岛上教堂的大理石被运到这里修建里巴特修道堡，这座要塞的塔楼兼作瞭望塔和清真寺的宣礼塔，堡中821年的铭文记下了埃米尔齐亚达特·安拉一世。1148年，安条克的乔治率领西西里诺曼舰队攻破城池。1444年，苏萨是哈夫斯王朝萨赫勒地区的第一大港，织工以「苏西」丝绸、亚麻织物和远销地中海各地的成衣「舒卡」袍闻名。

马赫迪叶衰落后，苏萨成为萨赫勒诸城之首，居民约一万五千人。1537年，西班牙与马耳他联军的进攻被击退，损失惨重；1574年奥斯曼征服后，本地水手加入柏柏尔海盗的行列。旧里巴特1722年得到修缮。1784年和1785年，安杰洛·埃莫率威尼斯舰队两度炮轰苏塞，这场持续四年的战事意在逼迫哈穆达帕夏约束海盗，城墙守住了，炮击终归徒劳。

en:
Tajarhi is the southernmost oasis of Fezzan, on the edge of the Idehan Murzuq dune sea. The desert roads from Tripoli and Sirte meet here and divide for the Niger River, Lake Chad and the Sudan: it is the last watering place before the long empty crossing south along the old Garamantean Road, later called the Bilma Trail. Kanem and Bornu had held the Fezzan oases in earlier centuries, and by the later fifteenth century they looked toward Tunis and the Hafsids. In 1444 Tajarhi had no court of its own, only wells, date palms and brackish pools where Muslim camel caravans stocked up before entering the central Sahara.

From Murzuk the Awlad Muhammad dynasty ruled the oases through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, taxing the gold, slaves, cloth and ostrich feathers moving between the Sudan and the Mediterranean. Its founder, Muhammad al-Fasi, was traditionally a Moroccan sharif; he had come south as a caravan leader, and the men of Murzuk invited him to take command of their fortress against Tuareg raids. An Ottoman army under Mahmut Bey conquered Fezzan in 1574, though the settlement of about 1626 left the local dynasty its hereditary internal affairs under Tripoli's overlordship. Tripoli's Karamanli government took direct control in 1813. When the British officer George Francis Lyon passed through in 1819, he found groves of date palms and wild duck on the brackish lakes.
zh:
泰杰尔希是费赞最南端的绿洲，坐落在迈尔祖格沙漠边缘。从的黎波里和苏尔特南下的沙漠道路在此会合，再分道通往尼日尔河、乍得湖和苏丹地区；沿古老的加拉曼特之路（后来称比尔马商路）南行，这里是进入漫长无人沙路前最后一处补水地。更早的世纪里，卡涅姆和博尔努曾统治费赞诸绿洲，到15世纪后期它们转而向突尼斯的哈夫斯王朝称臣。1444年的泰杰尔希没有自己的王庭，只有水井、椰枣林和咸水湖，供穆斯林驼队进入撒哈拉腹地前补足给养。

16至17世纪，奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝以迈尔祖格为都统治诸绿洲，向往来苏丹地区与地中海之间的黄金、奴隶、布匹和鸵鸟羽毛征税。王朝开创者穆罕默德·法西相传是摩洛哥圣裔，他本是率驼队南下的商队首领，迈尔祖格人为抵御图阿雷格人的袭扰，把他请来主持要塞。1574年，马赫穆特贝伊率奥斯曼军队征服费赞，但约1626年达成的安排把内部事务留给本地王朝世袭，只须臣服的黎波里。1813年，的黎波里的卡拉曼利政权改为直接统治。1819年，英国军官乔治·弗朗西斯·莱昂路过此地，见到成片椰枣林和咸水湖上的野鸭。

en:
Djado is an oasis and a ksar on the stony plateau of the same name, north-east of the Aïr, on the desert road that runs from the Fezzan south to the Kaouar oases and Bornu. Caravans crossed the Ténéré for weeks without finding water, so its wells made it a fixed halt between the Mediterranean coast and Lake Chad. Its Kanuri townspeople tended date groves and salt pans. Kanuri tradition says the Sao people founded the town; another account makes it a colony of Ibadi merchants from Jadu in the Jabal Nafusa, south-west of Tripoli, who named it after their home. The mais of Kanem-Bornu counted Djado among their subjects from the reign of Dunama Dibalemi in the thirteenth century, but the desert between the two made the tie a loose one, and the oasis often acted for itself. In 1444 it was a self-governing Kanuri town under the distant lordship of the Sayfawa.

In the later sixteenth century Mai Idris Alauma marched an army across the desert from Fachi as far as Bilma, and Djado again acknowledged the Sayfawa. As Bornu weakened during the eighteenth century, Tuareg raiders fell on the oasis again and again; families packed up and drifted south to the Kaouar, and by the early nineteenth century the old ksar, remembered locally as Brao, was slipping into the sand.
zh:
贾多是阿伊尔山东北方同名石质高原上的绿洲堡寨，坐落在费赞南下卡瓦尔绿洲群、再往博尔努的沙漠商路上。商队横穿泰内雷沙漠，常常数周找不到水，这里的水井因此成了地中海沿岸与乍得湖之间固定的补水站。城中的卡努里人种植椰枣、经营盐池。卡努里人的传说称萨奥人最早建城；另一种说法认为，建城的是来自的黎波里西南奈富塞山贾杜的伊巴德派商人，他们以故乡的名字称呼新城。至少从13世纪杜纳马·迪巴勒米在位时起，加涅姆-博尔努的国王便把贾多算作臣属，但相隔的沙漠使这层联系十分松散，绿洲常常自行其是。1444年，它是赛法瓦王朝远疆之内一座自治的卡努里城镇。

16世纪后期，国王伊德里斯·阿劳马率军从法奇穿越沙漠，直抵比尔马，贾多再度听命于赛法瓦王朝。18世纪博尔努国势衰落，图阿雷格人的袭掠一次接一次降临绿洲；住户陆续举家南迁卡瓦尔，到19世纪初，当地人称作布拉奥的旧堡寨已渐渐没入黄沙。

en:
Kuumeyay is the land of the Kumeyaay, who in 1444 held the coast from Oceanside south beyond the bay of Ensenada and east as far as the Colorado River. The San Diego River parted the Ipai clans to the north from the Tipai to the south, while the Kamia lived in the desert valleys beyond the mountains. Thirty patrilineal clans made up autonomous bands speaking a Yuman tongue: they took fish, shellfish and sea mammals from the kelp beds, gathered acorns in the oak canyons, and their waterside villages held one of the densest native populations on the Pacific coast. At Cosoy, their village on San Diego Bay, no European had yet landed.

Juan Rodriguez Cabrillo sailed the San Salvador and Victoria into that bay on 28 September 1542, named it San Miguel and did not stay. Sebastian Vizcaino returned in November 1602 during the feast of San Diego de Alcala and gave the bay that saint's name; no Spanish ship followed him until the Portola expedition raised a presidio on the site of Cosoy in July 1769. On 16 July Junipero Serra founded Mission San Diego de Alcala, the first mission in Alta California. Kumeyaay warriors attacked it within weeks, and the friars soon moved the buildings up the San Diego River.

Presidio soldiers took native women and flogged mission Indians with metal-tipped whips. On the night of 4 November 1775 more than six hundred Tipai and their allies surrounded the moved mission, burned it to the ground and killed three men: Father Luis Jayme, California's first Christian martyr, a blacksmith and a carpenter. Serra rebuilt the mission as a walled and fortified settlement, consecrated in October 1776. An earthquake threw the church down in 1803, and it stood rebuilt by 1813. Eight years later the land passed from Spain with Mexican independence.
zh:
库米艾（库梅雅）是库梅雅人的土地。1444年，他们据有从欧申赛德向南越过恩塞纳达湾、东抵科罗拉多河的海岸。圣迭戈河把北方的伊派氏族与南方的蒂派氏族分开，卡米亚人住在山脉以东的荒漠谷地里。三十个父系氏族组成互不统属的群体，操尤曼语支的语言：他们在海藻林中捕鱼、采贝、猎取海兽，在橡树峡谷采拾橡子，水畔村庄构成太平洋沿岸人口最稠密的原住民地区之一。在圣迭戈湾畔的科索伊村，此时还没有欧洲人登陆。

1542年9月28日，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略率「圣萨尔瓦多号」和「维多利亚号」驶入海湾，将其命名为圣米格尔，没有久留。1602年11月，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯卡伊诺在圣徒圣迭戈·德·阿尔卡拉的瞻礼日重返此湾，便以这位圣徒的名字为海湾命名；此后再无西班牙船前来，直到1769年7月波尔托拉远征队在科索伊村旧址筑起要塞。7月16日，胡尼佩罗·塞拉创立上加利福尼亚的第一座传教所圣迭戈·德·阿尔卡拉。几周后库梅雅战士便发起进攻，修士们不久把房舍溯圣迭戈河迁走。

要塞士兵奸占原住民妇女，传教所用金属头皮鞭拷打印第安人。1775年11月4日夜，六百多名蒂派人及其盟友包围迁址后的传教所，把它夷为平地，杀死三人：路易斯·海梅神父、一名铁匠和一名木匠；海梅是加利福尼亚第一位基督教殉道者。塞拉把传教所按有围墙的设防聚落重建，1776年10月重新祝圣。教堂在1803年的地震中倒塌，到1813年重建完成。八年后，这片土地随墨西哥独立脱离西班牙。

en: In the forested ridges north of Pomo country, the Yukian peoples held Round Valley and the mountains about it, with their own stretch of Pacific shore. They went by three names: the Ukomno'om, the Valley People of Round Valley; the Huchnom, 'outside the valley'; and the Ocean People of the coast. Their neighbours called them Yuki, a Wintu word for foreigner or enemy. Their tongue, with Wappo, made up the small Yukian family, and they counted by eights, numbering the spaces between the fingers. The bands lived on deer, salmon and acorn mush and met in the iwil-han, the cone-roofed, half-sunken dance house whose name meant 'powerful house'; their stories told of Taikomol, 'he who travels alone', and his companion Coyote. In 1444, and still in 1821, no road or mission crossed the ranges, and the valley and the coast belonged to them alone.
zh: 在波莫之地以北林木丛生的山岭间，尤基语诸族据有圆谷及周围山地，还拥有一段自己的太平洋海岸。他们按住地分三支自称：圆谷的乌科姆诺姆意为「谷地之民」，胡奇诺姆意为「谷地之外的人」，海边一支意为「大洋之民」。邻族称呼他们的「尤基」一名来自温图语，意为外人或敌人。他们的语言与瓦波语同属很小的尤基语系，计数采用八进制，数的是手指之间的空隙。各群体以鹿肉、鲑鱼和橡子糊为食，在锥形顶、半地穴式的舞屋中聚会，舞屋名字意为「有力量的屋子」；他们的故事讲独自旅行的神泰科莫尔和他的伙伴郊狼。1444年如此，到1821年依然如此，没有道路或传教团越过分水岭，圆谷与海岸只属于他们自己。

en:
The Tachi, a Southern Valley Yokuts people, lived along the north and west shores of Tulare Lake, among reed marshes, sloughs and the dry Kettleman Hills. Fed by the Kings, Kaweah, Tule and Kern rivers, Tulare was the largest freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, thick with fish and waterfowl, dotted with islands and flooded seasonally, and the Yokuts around it lived at one of the highest native population densities in North America. The Tachi called the water Pa'ashi, 'big water'. They fished from canoes of bundled tules, dug tule roots, gathered acorns and hunted tule elk and pronghorn, trading valley salt, steatite and obsidian to the Chumash of the coast and taking shell beads as money. At contact three Yokuts nations held the lake: the Tachi on the north and west, the Wowol to the south and the Chunut to the east. In 1444 the Tachi drew their living from the lake the year round.

Pedro Fages crossed the country south of the lake in the 1770s and described the plain as a labyrinth of lakes and reed beds the Spaniards called tulares, from Nahuatl tollin, a rush. In 1805 Father Juan Martín, three days out from the coast, became the first European to see the lake itself, in Wowol country. Father José María de Zalvidea rode with the Ruiz expedition of 1806 in search of mission sites, and Gabriel Moraga's expeditions of 1806-1808 mapped the rivers and chased mission runaways who had carried off horses, cattle and weapons. No mission or pueblo was ever founded on the Tachi shore, so when Mexico became independent in 1821 the lake and its reed maze were still entirely Yokuts country.
zh:
塔奇人是南谷约库特人的一支，住在图莱里湖的北岸和西岸，出入于芦苇沼泽、水道与干燥的凯特尔曼丘陵之间。图莱里湖由金斯河、卡威亚河、图莱河和克恩河注入，是密西西比河以西最大的淡水湖，鱼和水鸟繁盛，湖中多岛，湖水随季节涨落；湖畔约库特人的人口密度在北美原住民中居于最高之列。塔奇人称这片大水为帕阿希，意思就是「大水」。他们坐着芦苇扎成的小舟捕鱼，挖香蒲根，采橡子，猎马鹿和叉角羚，把谷地的盐、皂石和黑曜石卖给海岸的丘马什人，收进贝壳珠作货币。接触之初，湖畔有三个约库特族群：北面和西面是塔奇人，南面是沃沃尔人，东面是丘努特人。1444年，塔奇人一年四季靠湖为生。

佩德罗·法赫斯1770年代从湖以南穿过，把这片平原形容为湖泊与芦苇荡的迷宫；西班牙人把这种芦苇荡叫作图拉尔，此词来自纳瓦特尔语的托林，即芦苇。1805年，胡安·马丁神父从海岸走了三天，在沃沃尔人的土地上成为第一个亲眼见到这座湖的欧洲人。1806年，何塞·玛丽亚·德·萨尔维德亚神父随鲁伊斯远征队寻找传教站选址；加夫列尔·莫拉加1806至1808年的远征测绘了谷地诸河，也追捕带走马匹、牛只和武器的传教站逃亡者。塔奇人的湖畔始终没有建起传教站或村镇，因此1821年墨西哥独立时，图莱里湖和它的芦苇荡仍是完全属于约库特人的土地。

en: East of the Wintun plains the land climbs from the Sacramento Valley into the pine-clad Sierra Nevada, cut by the Feather and American Rivers: Maidu country. In their tongue maidu means 'person'. Three branches held the slope in 1444: the Nisenan on the American, Bear and Yuba drainages, the Konkow along the north fork of the Feather, and the Mountain Maidu on its high forks, each valley running its own affairs with no chief above the village. They wintered in round earth lodges dug into the ground and lived on leached acorn meal kept in woven granaries, salmon taken on the upstream run and deer from the hills. The women coiled baskets from fern root and redbud bark, some small as thimbles and others ten feet across, the finest strands needing a magnifying glass. The men ran the Kuksu cult, a secret society that met in underground dance houses for the 'big head' dances; the spring Bear Dance opened the year, and their stories turned on the World-maker and trickster Coyote. The three branches may have numbered 9,000 in 1770. No mission rose in the foothills, and through 1821 the ranges shut out nearly all outsiders.
zh: 温图人的平原以东，地势从萨克拉门托河谷攀上松林覆盖的内华达山脉，羽毛河与亚美利加河穿行其间，这就是迈杜人的土地。在他们的语言里，「迈杜」就是「人」的意思。1444年，三个支系分据山坡：南方支系据有亚美利加河、贝尔河与尤巴河流域，西北支系住在羽毛河北支流沿岸，山地迈杜人住在上游各汊流，每条河谷各理各的事，村落之上没有更高的首领。他们冬天住挖入地下的圆形土屋，以去涩后存入编织粮仓的橡子粉、洄游时捕取的鲑鱼和山中的鹿为食。妇女用蕨根和紫荆皮盘织篮子，小的如顶针，大的直径十英尺，最细的篾丝要借助放大镜才看得清。男子主持库克苏秘密社团，在半地穴舞屋中举行「大头舞」；春天的熊舞开启一年，故事里有创世者和爱施诡计的郊狼。三支人口在1770年约有九千。山麓始终没有建起传教团，直到1821年，山岭仍把几乎所有外来者挡在外面。

en: High in the Klamath Mountains, where the Klamath, Shasta and Scott Rivers cut through pine and oak, four kindred Shastan peoples lived beneath the snow peak that carries their name, the greatest of them the Kahosadi or Shasta proper, who called themselves 'plain speakers'. Their villages rarely held more than a family or two, and wealthy headmen settled disputes with gifts. The year turned on salmon taken at weirs and deer driven by fire into gaps in the oak scrub; women and children dived for mussels in the Klamath, and acorns were leached into meal. Downriver went buckskin garments, sinew-backed yew bows and obsidian arrowheads, and above all dentalium shells, which the Shasta passed on to the Wintu and the Pit River peoples as money; men wore lines tattooed on their arms to measure a shell's length, women vertical marks on the chin. War meant small raids in armour woven from serviceberry rods, and captives were kept as slaves rather than killed. The year's first salmon could not be eaten until the Karuk across the ridges had held their White Deerskin dance. Through 1821 no European crossed these ranges.
zh: 克拉马斯山脉高处，克拉马斯河、沙斯塔河与斯科特河切穿松林与橡林，四个同源的沙斯塔语族群住在后来以他们命名的雪峰之下，最大的一支是自称「言语平实之人」的沙斯塔本支卡霍萨迪人。村落往往只有一两户人家，富有的头人靠馈赠而非命令调停纷争。一年的生计围绕鱼梁上捕取的鲑鱼和被火赶入橡丛缺口的鹿；妇女和儿童潜入克拉马斯河捞蚌，橡子去涩磨成粉。顺河运出鹿皮衣、贴筋紫衫木弓和黑曜石箭头，最多的是角贝，沙斯塔人把它当货币转给温图人和皮特河流域各族；男子手臂纹有成排的线，用来量贝壳的长度，女子下巴纹竖道。打仗是穿唐棣木棍编甲的小规模突袭，俘虏不杀，留作奴隶。山那边卡洛克人的白鹿皮舞举行之前，谁也不吃当年的第一批鲑鱼。直到1821年，没有欧洲人越过这片山岭。

en:
'The people' is what maqlaqs means in Klamath. Maqlaqs is the lake country of the upper Klamath Basin, east of the Cascade Range: Klamath Marsh, Pelican Bay, the Link River and the Williamson and Sprague valleys. In 1444 its bands lived from the big lake and its marshes, taking fish, wocus seeds and roots. Each late March the c'waam sucker runs up the Williamson, Sprague and Lost Rivers, and the villages opened the year with the Return of C'waam ceremony. Dugout canoes crossed the marsh channels, and trails climbed through the Cascades to The Dalles on the Columbia, a trading ground whose camps had drawn Indian traders for ten thousand years; there the Klamath bartered with the Wasco and Wishram. The mountains and marshes kept the basin so shut off that the Klamath knew nothing of the Pacific, a few days' travel to the west.

Once horses reached the basin, Klamath parties rode south to raid the Achomawi of the Pit River, carrying off captives to keep or sell as slaves; scholars date these slave raids only after the horse arrived. In 1821 the marsh villages still lay beyond every route of the European fur brigades.
zh:
maqlaqs在克拉马特语中意为「人」，马克拉克斯就是上克拉马特盆地的湖乡，地处喀斯喀特山脉以东，领有克拉马特沼泽、鹈鹕湾、林克河以及威廉森河与斯普拉格河河谷。1444年，各群体靠大湖和沼泽为生，捕鱼、采沃库斯睡莲籽和根茎。每年三月末夸姆鱼溯威廉森河、斯普拉格河和洛斯特河而上，各村以夸姆鱼回归仪式开启一年。独木舟穿行沼泽水道，山路翻过喀斯喀特山通往哥伦比亚河畔的达尔斯，那里的营地吸引印第安商人已有上万年，克拉马特人在那里同沃斯科人和威什拉姆人以物易物。山岭和沼泽把盆地封得很死，往西不过几天路程就是太平洋，克拉马特人却对它一无所知。

马匹传入盆地后，克拉马特队伍南下袭掠皮特河的阿乔马维村落，掳走俘虏留作奴隶或转卖；学者认为这类掳奴行动始于马匹到来之后。到1821年，欧洲毛皮商队的所有路线仍未伸进这些沼泽村落。

en:
The Kalapuya were not one tribe but a scatter of independent bands, among them the Tualatin and Yamhill on the northern streams and the Santiam, Luckiamute and Chepenefa on the central and southern tributaries of the Willamette. In 1444 their winter villages, root grounds, hunting camps and fishing weirs filled the valley between the Cascade Range and the Coast Range. The bands burned the prairies every year to hold back the forest and keep open oak savanna where women dug camas. They also gathered wapato, hazelnuts, berries and acorns soaked to remove the tannin, while the men took salmon, deer and elk and chipped points from obsidian of the eastern mountains. Camas, hides and dried meat went north to Chinookan villages on the lower Willamette and Columbia, and came back as dried salmon and shell wealth.

William Broughton sighted the Willamette mouth in 1792 and put it on European charts, and in April 1806 William Clark paddled up the river after Native guides showed him the channel. In 1812 William Wallace and John Halsey built Wallace House north of the Chemeketa village, the first fur post in the valley, and its hunters brought in deer and elk for Fort Astoria. When the North West Company's Oregon posts passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821, the prairies were still burned every year and every village in the valley was still Kalapuya.
zh:
卡拉普亚包括一群互不统属的群体，北部溪流边是图拉丁、亚姆希尔等群体，威拉米特河中游和南部支流边则是桑蒂亚姆、勒基缪特和切佩内法等群体。1444年，喀斯喀特山脉与海岸山脉之间的谷地里满是他们的冬村、球根采地、猎营和鱼梁。各群体年年放火烧荒，压住林木，把草地维持成栎树疏林，妇女好在其中挖卡马斯球根。他们还采瓦帕托块根、榛子、浆果和泡去涩味的橡子，男子则捕鲑鱼、猎鹿和麋，用东部山地的黑曜石打制箭镞。卡马斯球根、兽皮和肉干北运到威拉米特河下游和哥伦比亚河畔的奇努克村落，换回干鲑鱼和贝饰。

1792年威廉·布劳顿望见威拉米特河口，把它绘入欧洲海图；1806年4月，威廉·克拉克经原住民向导指引，划独木舟溯河而上。1812年，威廉·华莱士和约翰·哈尔西在切梅克塔村以北建起华莱士屋，这是谷地第一个毛皮商站，站里的猎手为阿斯托里亚堡猎取鹿和麋。1821年西北公司的俄勒冈商站转归哈德逊湾公司时，谷地的草地仍年年烧荒，每一座村落也仍是卡拉普亚人的。

en:
Umatalum comes from Imatalamłáma, the people of Ímatalam, the village at the mouth of the Umatilla River; imatilam is said to mean an island in the Columbia. These Sahaptian speakers held villages and seasonal camps that followed the Umatilla up into the Blue Mountain foothills and spread along the nearby south bank of the Columbia in 1444. Their open country had few defences, and Bannock and Paiute raiders struck at them from the south. The year turned on salmon runs, spring camas digs, late-summer berries in the high country and winter deer and elk hunts. Much of the trade ran to Wyam, the Celilo Falls villages, where fifteen to twenty million salmon passed each year. Fishermen worked from wooden platforms over the rapids with long-handled dip nets, and the Wishram on the north bank and the Wasco on the south took in goods from as far as the Great Plains, the Southwest and Alaska.

Horses from Spanish New Mexico reached the Shoshone by 1700 and the neighbouring Nez Perce and Cayuse by about 1730; Umatilla bands later kept large herds without giving up their fishing stations. On 19 October 1805 Lewis and Clark entered their land, and the frightened villagers hid until councils with the chiefs and the presence of Sacagawea turned the meeting friendly. The North West Company built Fort Nez Percés upriver on Walla Walla land in 1818, and the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company in 1821, as British fur brigades reached the edge of Umatilla country.
zh:
乌马塔卢姆来自伊马塔兰拉马（Imatalamłáma），即伊马塔兰村人，村子坐落在乌马蒂拉河河口；据说伊马塔兰指的是哥伦比亚河里的一座岛。这些说萨哈普廷语的人，1444年时的村落和季节营地沿乌马蒂拉河伸入蓝山山麓，也排在附近的哥伦比亚河南岸。地界开阔、少险可守，班诺克和派尤特袭掠者常从南面打来。他们的年岁随鲑鱼汛、春天的卡马斯采挖、夏末的高地浆果和冬天的鹿麋围猎轮转。贸易多集中在怀阿姆，即塞利洛瀑布的渔村，每年有一千五百万至两千万尾鲑鱼经过。渔人站在急流上的木台，用长柄抄网捕鱼；北岸的威什拉姆人和南岸的沃斯科人收来的货物，远的来自大平原、北美西南和阿拉斯加。

西属新墨西哥的马到1700年已传到肖肖尼人手中，约1730年又传到邻近的内兹珀斯人和卡尤塞人；乌马蒂拉各群体后来养起大群马，却没有丢下旧渔场。1805年10月19日，刘易斯与克拉克进入他们的地界，受惊的村民躲了起来，直到与酋长会谈、萨卡加维亚在场，会面才转为友好。1818年西北公司在瓦拉瓦拉人的土地上兴建内兹珀斯堡；1821年商站转归哈德逊湾公司，英国毛皮商队也抵近了乌马蒂拉地界的边缘。

en:
Aqokulo, or Aqokúlo, was the Chemakums' own name; later settlers called them the Port Townsend Indians. Their villages stood on the northeastern Olympic Peninsula, between Discovery Bay and Hood Canal, chiefly around Port Townsend Bay and Port Ludlow Bay. Sheltered anchorages and the Kah Tai canoe portage gave them a hold on the entrance to Puget Sound, while their Chimakuan language, close to Quileute, marked them off from the Klallam and Coast Salish peoples around them. In 1444 they lived from the bays and salmon streams as a Chimakuan-speaking people of the sound's mouth.

Around 1789 about four hundred Chemakum lived on the Quimper Peninsula and along Hood Canal, caught up in raids and blood feuds with the Klallam, Makah, Snohomish, Snoqualmie and Ditidaht. In the summer of 1790 Manuel Quimper and Gonzalo López de Haro, sent by Francisco de Eliza to survey the Strait of Juan de Fuca, mapped Port Discovery as Puerto Quadra, the first European charting of the bay. George Vancouver followed in 1792, named the sheltered anchorage Port Townshend for his friend the Marquis of Townshend, and fixed Discovery Bay on his charts. Vancouver's surveys opened Puget Sound to European ships, but in 1821 no foreign fort or town yet stood among the Chemakum villages.
zh:
阿科库洛（Aqokúlo）是切马库姆人的自称，后来的移民管他们叫汤森港印第安人。他们的村落立在奥林匹克半岛东北端，介于发现湾与胡德水道之间，主要环绕汤森湾和勒德洛湾。避风锚地和卡泰独木舟转运道使他们扼住普吉特湾的入口；他们的奇马库安语与奎鲁特语相近，又使他们与周围的克拉勒姆人和海岸萨利什人区别开来。1444年，这支说奇马库安语的族群守在湾口，靠各湾和产鲑鱼的河流为生。

1789年前后，约四百名切马库姆人住在昆珀半岛和胡德水道沿岸，卷入了同克拉勒姆、马卡、斯诺霍米什、斯诺夸尔米和迪蒂达特等族的袭掠和血仇。1790年夏，弗朗西斯科·德·埃利萨派曼努埃尔·昆佩尔和贡萨洛·洛佩斯·德·阿罗测绘胡安·德富卡海峡，他们把发现港绘入图中、命名为夸德拉港，这是欧洲人首次测绘该湾。1792年乔治·温哥华继之而来，以友人汤森侯爵之名将这处避风锚地命名为汤森港，还把发现湾确定在自己的海图上。温哥华的勘测为欧洲船只打开了普吉特湾，但到1821年，切马库姆村落间仍没有外来的要塞或城镇。

en:
The Kwaiailk, q̓ʷay̓áyiɬq in their own language, were the Upper Chehalis, a Southwestern Coast Salish people of the upper Chehalis River. Chehalis is a downriver word meaning 'sand', from the Lower Chehalis head village by Grays Harbor; the Kwaiailk name itself comes from q̓ʷayáiɬ, Mud Bay on Puget Sound, pointing to an older footing on that shore. Their river runs down to the harbor and the Lower Chehalis country. In 1444 Kwaiailk families held the fisheries, prairies and canoe portages between the sound and the lower Columbia, the inland people of the Coast Salish world through whose hands coastal goods moved. Shells, dried fish and, later, European iron passed up the river, most of it handled by Chinookan and Lower Chehalis middlemen.

Robert Gray sailed into Grays Harbor in 1792 and handed weapons and tools to Lower Chehalis visitors, but no European is known to have pushed upriver to the Kwaiailk. Their iron and cloth came through Chinookan and Lower Chehalis middlemen, moving from village to village by canoe rather than arriving with a ship or a fort. When the Hudson's Bay Company took over the North West Company's posts in 1821, the fords, prairies and fishing grounds of the upper Chehalis were still entirely in Kwaiailk hands.
zh:
夸伊艾尔克人在本族语里称q̓ʷay̓áyiɬq，即上奇黑利斯人，是西南海岸萨利什人的一支，住在奇黑利斯河上游。「奇黑利斯」是下游语言里「沙」的意思，得名于下奇黑利斯人在格雷斯港畔的主村；夸伊艾尔克人的自称则来自q̓ʷayáiɬ，即普吉特湾的马德湾，说明他们更早时还据有那片海岸。河流下游通向格雷斯港和下奇黑利斯人的地界。1444年，夸伊艾尔克人掌握着海湾与哥伦比亚河下游之间的渔场、草原和独木舟陆运道，是海岸萨利什世界里的「内地人」，海岸的货物多经他们的手。贝壳、干鱼以及后来的欧洲铁料沿河而上，大多由奇努克人和下奇黑利斯中间商经手。

1792年罗伯特·格雷驶入格雷斯港，把武器和工具交给来访的下奇黑利斯人，但已知没有欧洲人溯河而上到过夸伊艾尔克。他们的铁料和布匹都经奇努克人和下奇黑利斯中间商，一村传一村地由独木舟运来，而不是随船或要塞到来。1821年哈德逊湾公司接管西北公司的商站时，奇黑利斯河上游的渡口、草原和渔场仍全在夸伊艾尔克人手中。

en:
The Lower Yakama, who call themselves Mámachatpam, hold the dry lower valley of the Yakima River east of the Cascade Range, where sagebrush plains are cut by well-watered streams coming off the mountains. In 1444 their winter houses stood along the Naches, Ahtanum, Toppenish and Satus watercourses, their chief village at the hill gap called Pa'kiut, and families moved in season to salmon weirs, camas meadows and upland hunting camps. Horses reached the plateau from the Great Basin around 1730 and widened their range, and dried salmon, hides and horses went down the Yakima to the Columbia for trade with Chinookan villages near the river's mouth.

Disease crossed the mountains before Europeans did: a smallpox epidemic swept the plateau in the 1770s and thinned its villages. The first white men the Lower Yakama saw were the Lewis and Clark party, who reached the mouth of the Yakima about 17 October 1805 on their way down the Columbia and noted the river as Tâpe têtt; they did not ascend the valley. Through 1821 the Mámachatpam still governed their own villages and fishing stations.
zh:
下亚基马人自称马马查特帕姆（Mamachatpam），居住在喀斯喀特山脉以东干燥的下亚基马河谷；艾灌平原之间，源自山间的溪流带来水草。1444年，人们在纳奇斯河、阿塔努姆溪、托彭尼什溪和萨图斯溪沿岸建有冬屋，主要村落在名叫帕基乌特（Pa'kiut）的两山间峡口，家户按季节前往鲑鱼鱼梁、卡马夏草地和高地狩猎营地。马大约在1730年从大盆地传入高原，扩大了他们的活动范围；鱼干、兽皮和马匹顺亚基马河运到哥伦比亚河，与河口一带的奇努克村落交易。

疫病比欧洲人先翻过山：1770年代，一场天花横扫高原，村落人口锐减。下亚基马人见到的第一批白人是刘易斯与克拉克的队伍，他们1805年10月17日前后沿哥伦比亚河下行时抵达亚基马河口，把河名记为塔佩泰特（Tape tett），但没有溯河进入谷地。直到1821年，马马查特帕姆仍由自己的村落和渔场首领管理。

en:
Sqeliz is the land of the Spokane, Interior Salish people of the Spokane, Little Spokane and Latah waterways. Their own name for themselves means 'steelhead', although early traders translated Spokane as 'children of the sun', from a chief called Illim-Spokanée, 'Son of the Sun'. The Lower, Middle and Upper bands kept permanent winter villages for three months of the year and moved for the other nine between salmon fisheries, camas grounds and upland hunting camps. Families gathered at the mouth of the Little Spokane to catch and dry salmon, and trade in fish, hides and, later, horses linked them with Nez Perce, Coeur d'Alene and Columbia River peoples.

The Lewis and Clark party met the Spokane in 1805. In the winter of 1810–1811 Jaco Finlay, building for David Thompson's North West Company, raised Spokane House on the peninsula where the Spokane meets the Little Spokane, the company's farthest post in the Columbia country. John Jacob Astor's Pacific Fur Company built Fort Spokane next to it, and the two rival stations faced each other over the old salmon fishery until the War of 1812 forced the American post to close. The North West Company held Spokane House until 1821, when it was merged into the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
斯凯利兹是斯波坎人的土地。斯波坎人是内陆萨利什人的一支，活动在斯波坎河、小斯波坎河和拉塔溪一带。他们的自称意为「硬头鳟」，早期商人却把斯波坎解释成「太阳的孩子」，这个说法来自一位名叫伊利姆—斯波坎尼的首领，意为「太阳之子」。下、中、上三个群体每年有三个月住在固定冬村，其余九个月往返于鲑鱼渔场、卡马夏采集地和高地猎营之间。各家族到小斯波坎河口聚首，捕捞、晾晒鲑鱼；鱼、兽皮和后来的马匹贸易，把他们与内兹珀斯、科达伦和哥伦比亚河各群联系在一起。

1805年，刘易斯与克拉克一行遇到斯波坎人。1810年至1811年冬，在戴维·汤普森主持下，雅科·芬利为西北公司在斯波坎河与小斯波坎河之间的半岛上建起斯波坎屋，这是西北公司深入哥伦比亚地区最远的商站。约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的太平洋毛皮公司在隔壁修起斯波坎堡，两座敌对商站隔老渔场相望，直到1812年战争迫使美国商站关闭。西北公司守着斯波坎屋直到1821年，是年公司并入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
Palus is the river country of the Palouse, a Sahaptin people of the Columbia Plateau. Three bands held the Palouse River, the lower Clearwater and the lower Snake, and the village of Pa-luš-sa near where the Palouse joins the Snake gave its name to the whole people. In 1444 families followed the salmon runs, the camas meadows and the upland game, gathering with Nez Perce, Yakama and Walla Walla relatives to feast, trade and race horses. Horses reached the Nez Perce from the Shoshone around 1730 and spread through the plateau; the spotted ponies raised in this region were later known to settlers as 'Palouse horses', possibly after the river, and that name gradually became Appaloosa.

In October 1805 the Lewis and Clark party met the Palouse while most of the people were away on autumn hunts, and gave their head chief Kepowhan one of the expedition's silver peace medals bearing Jefferson's image; the captains recorded the Palouse as a people distinct from the Nez Perce. In July 1818 the North West Company began Fort Nez Percés near the Snake's mouth, and that September Donald MacKenzie led a large trapping brigade up the Snake through Palus country. His rich catch in July 1819 made such brigades annual, and in 1821 fort and trade passed to the Hudson's Bay Company, with Palus villages still under their own chiefs.
zh:
帕卢斯是哥伦比亚高原上萨哈普廷语族群帕卢斯人的河谷之地。三个群体据有帕卢斯河、克利尔沃特河下游和斯内克河下游；帕卢斯河汇入斯内克河处附近的帕卢萨村（Pa-luš-sa），把名字给了整个族群。1444年，各家族随鲑鱼洄游、卡马夏草熟和高地猎期转徙，与内兹珀斯、雅卡马和沃拉沃拉亲属聚首宴饮、贸易、赛马。约1730年，内兹珀斯人从肖肖尼人那里得到马匹，马匹随后传遍高原；这一带培育的斑点矮马后来被移民叫作「帕卢斯马」，名字可能得自帕卢斯河，渐渐念成了阿帕卢萨马。

1805年10月，刘易斯与克拉克一行遇到帕卢斯人，当时多数人正外出秋猎；他们向大首领克波汉赠送了一枚铸有杰斐逊像的探险队银质和平纪念章，两位队长还在记录中把帕卢斯人与内兹珀斯人区分开来。1818年7月，西北公司在斯内克河口附近动工修建内兹珀斯堡；同年9月，唐纳德·麦肯齐率大型猎捕队溯斯内克河穿过帕卢斯地方，1819年7月带回的丰厚毛皮使这种猎队成为年度行动。1821年，商堡与贸易转入哈德逊湾公司，帕卢斯各村仍由本族首领管辖。

en:
Boho'inee, also called Pohogwe or Bohogue, took in the upper Snake River Plain around the river bottoms later known to Americans as the Fort Hall country. The Northern Shoshone who wintered there built sagebrush and willow lodges near water and split into small family parties when the weather warmed. They dug camas and other roots, hunted antelope and mountain game, fished the streams, and travelled toward the Wind River valleys. Bannock relatives camped and married among them, so many bands moved between Shoshone and Bannock speech. In 1444 dogs carried the loads, camp headmen had no authority over neighbouring bands, and horses had not yet reached the plain.

Horses arrived from the Plains or the Spanish Southwest by the late 1600s. Mounted Bohogue hunters rode east after bison and traded horses to Nez Perce and Flathead neighbours, until Blackfoot raiders pushed many Shoshone bands back toward the mountains in the middle 1700s. Andrew Henry's fur trappers put up rough huts on Henry's Fork in the autumn of 1810; the post later called Fort Henry was abandoned in the spring. Wilson Price Hunt's Astorians used the empty cabins in October 1811 before attempting the Snake River route. The visitors stayed only briefly. In 1821 the camas grounds and winter bottoms around Bohogue were still Shoshone and Bannock country.
zh:
博霍伊内又称波霍格维或博霍格，包括后来美国人所说霍尔堡一带的斯内克河上游平原。在此越冬的北肖肖尼人近水搭建山艾和柳枝棚屋；天气转暖后，各家族分成小队，挖取卡马夏球茎和其他根菜，猎捕羚羊与山间猎物，在溪流捕鱼，有时远行到温德河谷。班诺克亲族与他们同住通婚，许多队群兼用肖肖尼语和班诺克语。1444年，驮运行李的还是狗，营地首领管不到邻近队群，马也尚未进入这片平原。

马在十七世纪末从大平原或西班牙人控制的西南部传来。骑马的博霍格猎手东行猎野牛，并同尼米普人和弗拉塞德人交换马匹；到十八世纪中叶，黑脚袭扰者把许多肖肖尼队群逼回山地边缘。1810年秋，安德鲁·亨利的捕兽者在亨利支流搭起棚屋，这座后来被称为亨利堡的据点只维持了一冬。1811年10月，威尔逊·普赖斯·亨特率领的阿斯托远征队曾在空屋里避身，随后尝试沿斯内克河探路。外来者停留得很短。1821年，博霍格周围的卡马夏采集地和越冬河谷仍是肖肖尼人与班诺克人的地方。

en:
Kusiutta, the country usually called Goshute on later maps, covers the dry valleys west and southwest of Great Salt Lake: Skull and Tooele, Deep Creek, Snake Valley, and the broken ranges reaching into eastern Nevada. Springs set the route of every journey. In winter families built willow-framed wickiups near reliable water; in summer small camps climbed into cooler hills and lived on pine nuts, grass seeds, roots, rabbits, lizards, snakes, insects, and whatever antelope, deer, or bighorn sheep they could take. In 1444 no Goshute chief could call on all the camps. Family heads knew which seep held water in a dry year and when each seed or pine-nut crop ripened.

Goshute families kept few horses long after mounted raiders crossed the desert edge. A horse herd needed grass and water that people could scarcely spare, and horses offered little help in narrow canyons or rocky ranges. During the 1700s and early 1800s, mounted Ute and Navajo parties raided camps for captives sold on the borderlands slave market. Goshute families moved between hidden springs instead of building a similar mounted force. No mission, fur post, or permanent outside settlement stood in their valleys in 1821.
zh:
库休塔在后来的地图上常标作戈休特，位于大盐湖以西和西南的干谷：斯卡尔谷、图埃勒谷、迪普克里克、斯内克谷，以及延伸入内华达东部的破碎山脉。泉水决定每一条迁徙路线。冬天，各家族在可靠水源旁搭起柳骨棚屋；夏天，小队进入较凉爽的山地，以松子、草籽、根块、兔、蜥蜴、蛇和昆虫为食，有机会也猎取羚羊、鹿或大角羊。1444年，没有哪个戈休特首领能调动所有营地。家族长者记得枯水年哪处渗泉仍有水，也知道每种草籽和松子何时成熟。

在骑马袭扰者抵达荒漠边缘后很久，戈休特家族仍很少养马。马要吃草饮水，而这些东西连人都得仔细分配；在窄峡和乱石山坡间，马的用处也有限。十八世纪至十九世纪初，骑马的尤特人和纳瓦霍人小队袭击营地，掳走人口，卖到边疆奴隶市场。戈休特家族选择在隐蔽泉眼之间转移，而不是建立同样的骑马武力。1821年时，他们的谷地里还没有传教站、毛皮据点或外来者的永久定居点。

en:
The Hwalbay, or Hualapai, 'people of the tall pines', held a hundred-mile stretch of the Grand Canyon's pine-clad southern rim, from the Colorado River south to the Cerbat and Hualapai mountains. Their roots lay with the Patayan farming peoples of the river and its side canyons. Three subtribes, the Middle Mountain People of the northwest, the Plateau People of the eastern canyons and the Yavapai Fighters of the south, were divided into seven bands and some thirteen local groups, each a cluster of family villages camped near a spring. They planted maize, beans and squash in storm-water washes, hunted deer and bighorn sheep, gathered pine nuts, and carried trade along trails that ran west to the Mohave on the river and east to the Hopi mesas; the Havasupai of Cataract Canyon were their own kin, once a band of the Plateau People. In 1444 no European had yet entered their canyons.

In September 1540 a party of Coronado's soldiers under García López de Cárdenas, led by Hopi guides, became the first Europeans to see the Grand Canyon, but they reached the South Rim far to the east of Hwalbay land and, after days of searching for a way down, never got near the river. The Hwalbay canyons went unseen for more than two centuries after. The first European to cross them was the Franciscan Francisco Garcés, who in 1776 travelled from the Mohave villages through Hwalbay country to the Havasupai and on to the Hopi town of Oraibi, where the Hopi turned him back; his diary is the first written description of the Hwalbay. After the Quechan uprising of 1781 destroyed the Spanish missions on the lower Colorado, no friar or soldier came this way again. A few horses and metal goods filtered in through native trade, and when Mexico took over Spain's claims in 1821, the Hwalbay still moved freely among their springs, canyons and pine ridges.
zh:
瓦拉佩人自称瓦尔拜（Hwalbáy），意为「高大松树之人」，据有大峡谷南缘松林地带约一百英里长的一段土地，北起科罗拉多河，南抵塞尔巴特山和瓦拉佩群山。他们是科罗拉多河及其支峡古代帕塔扬农耕人群的后裔，分为三支：西北的中部山地人、东部峡谷的高原人和南方的亚瓦派战士，三支之下又分七个群体、约十三个地方小集团，各是泉眼附近几座家族小村的组合。他们在雨后涨水的旱谷里种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎鹿和大角羊，采集松子，沿小径西行与河畔的莫哈维人往来，东去霍皮人的台地贸易；卡特拉克特峡谷的哈瓦苏佩人本是他们的亲族，原属高原人中的一支。1444年时，还没有欧洲人走进过这些峡谷。

1540年9月，科罗纳多麾下加西亚·洛佩斯·德·卡德尼亚斯带着一队士兵，由霍皮向导引路，成为最早看见大峡谷的欧洲人，但他们到达的南源远在瓦拉佩土地以东，一连数日寻找下山的路，始终没能靠近河边。瓦拉佩人的峡谷此后又有两个多世纪不为外界所见。第一个穿经这里的欧洲人是方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯：1776年，他从莫哈维人的村落出发，穿过瓦拉佩土地到哈瓦苏佩人处，再东行至霍皮人的奥拉伊比镇，被霍皮人拒之门外后折返；他的日记是对瓦拉佩人最早的文字记载。1781年克尚人起义摧毁了科罗拉多河下游的西班牙传教站，此后再没有修士或士兵来到这一带。少量马匹和金属器经原住民贸易流入，1821年墨西哥接管西班牙的权利主张时，瓦拉佩人仍自由往来于泉眼、峡谷和松林山脊之间。

en:
The Chiricahua Mountains rise from the arid borderlands where Arizona, New Mexico, Sonora and Chihuahua meet, their pine ridges and deep canyons standing high above the desert valleys. The Opata called the range Chiwi Kawi, Turkey Mountain, for the wild turkeys in its woods. By 1444 small family groups related to the Chiricahua, the Bedonkohe among them, moved through these canyons on foot, hunting, gathering, trading with the farming peoples of the southern valleys or raiding them; Mogollon and Mimbres villagers had farmed and made pottery in those valleys centuries before. The people of the mountains kept no towns and knew every spring and pass, and caves and waterholes were sacred ground where hoddentin, ground cattail pollen, was offered to the sun and used in healing rites.

The first known Spanish mention of Apache people came with Juan de Onate's occupation of New Mexico in 1598. Horses changed the balance of the frontier: by the late 1600s Chiricahua raiders were riding south into Sonora to lift horses and cattle, and through the 1700s mounted raids met Spanish slave-catching expeditions and a chain of presidios. Official gifts and treaties bought spells of quiet, but no garrison ever held the Chiricahua canyons. When New Spain gave way to Mexico in 1821, the Bedonkohe still commanded the mountain roads.
zh:
奇里卡瓦山脉耸立于亚利桑那、新墨西哥、索诺拉和奇瓦瓦交界的干旱边地，松岭和深峡谷高出四周荒漠谷地。奥帕塔人称这片山脉为奇维卡维，即野火鸡山，名字来自林中的野火鸡。到1444年，与奇里卡瓦诸群体有亲属关系的小家族群（贝当科赫人是其中一支）已徒步穿行于这些峡谷，狩猎采集，与南方谷地的农耕居民贸易，或对他们发动袭掠；更早些时候，莫戈永人和明布雷斯农民已在那些河谷耕种制陶。山里人不定居建城，熟知每一处水泉和山口；洞穴和水潭是圣地，人们把磨细的香蒲花粉撒向太阳，也用于疗愈仪式。

西班牙人最早一次提到阿帕奇人，是胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年占领新墨西哥时。马匹改变了整条边地的力量对比：到17世纪末，奇里卡瓦袭掠者已骑马南下索诺拉夺取马匹和牛群；整个18世纪，骑马袭掠对上的是西班牙抓捕奴隶的远征队和一线要塞。官方赠礼与和约只换来短暂平静，没有任何驻军守得住奇里卡瓦的峡谷。1821年新西班牙变为墨西哥时，贝当科赫人仍控制着山中道路。

en:
Hopituh is the mesa country of the Hopi, whose name means the peaceable, mannered people. They descend from the Hisatsinom, the Ancestral Puebloan farmers, and after the great Pueblo centres of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries were abandoned their villages gathered around the scarce springs of Antelope Mesa and the First, Second and Third Mesas. Awatovi rose after about 1300 as the leading town on Antelope Mesa, while Old Oraibi, settled before 1100, was already one of the oldest continuously occupied villages in what later became the United States. The people lived in stone pueblos built around kivas, in matrilineal clans, and fed themselves by dry farming corn in the sand dunes below the mesas. In 1444 no European had yet reached Tusayan, as the Spaniards later called the province.

In 1540 Coronado sent Pedro de Tovar west from Zuni, and after a short skirmish at Awatovi the Hopi made peace and gave the strangers cotton cloth and presents; Hopi guides then led García López de Cárdenas to the Grand Canyon, the first Europeans to see it. Later Spanish visitors counted five villages and perhaps 12,000 people, but Spain placed no garrison in so remote a country. Franciscan friars arrived in 1629 and raised a church at Awatovi, the only pueblo where many converts were made; forced labour and the suppression of ceremonies followed, and in 1655 the friar Salvador de Guerra beat a Hopi man, Juan Cuna, to death. The mesas joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680: the friars were killed and the Awatovi church taken apart stone by stone, and through the seventeenth century the villages climbed from the mesa feet to the heights for defence. When Awatovi accepted a rebuilt church in 1700, its own chief asked the other villages to intervene; in the winter of 1700–01 their warriors destroyed the town, killed its men and carried off the women and children. No mission or garrison returned to the mesas before the end of Spanish rule.
zh:
霍皮图是霍皮人的台地之邦，「霍皮」意为平和、守礼之人。他们是古普韦布洛农民希萨齐诺姆的后裔；12至14世纪的大型普韦布洛中心被放弃后，村庄聚集到羚羊台地和第一、第二、第三台地上稀少的泉眼周围。阿瓦托维约1300年后兴起，成为羚羊台地的首镇；旧奥赖比在1100年以前已有人定居，是后来美国境内持续有人居住的最古老村庄之一。人们住在围着基瓦会堂修建的石砌普韦布洛中，按母系氏族生活，在台地下的沙丘里旱作玉米为生。1444年，欧洲人还没有进入西班牙人后来所称的图萨扬。

1540年，科罗纳多从祖尼派佩德罗·德·托瓦尔西行，在阿瓦托维短暂交火后议和，霍皮人送给这些陌生人棉布和礼物；霍皮向导随后把加西亚·洛佩斯·德·卡德纳斯带到大峡谷，他们是第一批看见大峡谷的欧洲人。后来的西班牙来访者数出五座村庄、约12000人，但西班牙没有在如此偏远的地方驻军。1629年方济各会修士抵达，在阿瓦托维修起教堂，这里也是唯一有大量人入教的普韦布洛；随之而来的是强迫劳役和对传统仪式的压制，1655年修士萨尔瓦多·德·格拉将名叫胡安·库纳的霍皮人殴打致死。各台地参加了1680年普韦布洛起义：修士被杀，阿瓦托维的教堂被一砖一石拆毁；整个17世纪，村庄为求防御陆续从台地脚下迁到高处。1700年阿瓦托维接纳重建的教堂后，正是本村酋长请其他村庄出面；1700年至1701年冬季，外村战士摧毁这座镇子，杀死男子，带走妇女和儿童。直到西班牙统治结束，再没有传教站或驻军回到台地上。

en:
Shiwinna is the provincial name for the Zuni River valley, homeland of the A:shiwi, who call their country Halona Idiwan'a, the Middle Place. By about 1400 their farming settlements had drawn together into six pueblos, among them Halona and Hawikku, above the river that runs toward the Little Colorado. They irrigated maize fields and carried salt, corn and turquoise to trade around Zuni Salt Lake. In 1444 the six towns lay alone, with no Spanish mission or garrison, between the Rio Grande pueblos, the Hopi mesas and the southern deserts.

The first outsider to reach them was Estevanico, a survivor of the Narváez expedition who had crossed most of the continent with Cabeza de Vaca. Sent ahead of Fray Marcos de Niza with trade goods in 1539, he entered Hawikku and was killed there, and Niza's report turned the town into one of the Seven Cities of Cibola. On 7 July 1540 Coronado stormed Hawikku: about two hundred Zuni held the pueblo for less than an hour, and the Spaniards found adobe houses three to five stories high instead of gold; the people who fled sheltered on the Dowa Yalanne mesa. The Franciscans established a mission at Hawikku in 1628, but in 1632 the Zuni killed its priest and burned the church, and Apache raiders burned it again in 1672. During the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 the whole people withdrew to Dowa Yalanne once more and Hawikku was abandoned for good. They came down from the mesa in 1692 and consolidated around Halona, the Zuni Pueblo. Spanish rule stayed thin: only seven Spaniards were recorded in the country in 1799, and the last Franciscans left in 1821.
zh:
希温纳是祖尼河谷地在本省的名称，是祖尼人（A:shiwi）的故土；他们称这片土地为中央之地（Halona Idiwan'a）。到1400年前后，他们的农业聚落聚合成六座普韦布洛，哈洛纳和哈维库即在其中，坐落在流向小科罗拉多河的祖尼河旁。他们引水浇灌玉米田，把盐、玉米和绿松石运到祖尼盐湖一带交易。1444年，这六座城镇独自处在格兰德河普韦布洛、霍皮方山和南方沙漠之间，没有传教站，也没有驻军。

第一个来到这里的外人是埃斯特万尼科。他是纳尔瓦埃斯远征的幸存者，曾随卡韦萨·德·巴卡横穿大半个大陆。1539年，他带着货物走在马科斯·德·尼萨修士的队伍前面，进入哈维库后被杀；尼萨的报告把这座城镇说成西博拉七城之一。1540年7月7日，科罗纳多猛攻哈维库，约二百名祖尼人守了不到一小时，西班牙人没有找到黄金，只见到三五层高的土坯房屋；逃出战火的人到多瓦·亚兰内方山上避难。方济各会1628年在哈维库建立传教站，1632年祖尼人杀死神父、烧毁教堂，1672年阿帕奇袭掠者再次焚毁教堂。1680年普韦布洛大起义中，全体祖尼人再次退守多瓦·亚兰内山，哈维库就此荒废。他们1692年下山，集中到哈洛纳，即祖尼普韦布洛。西班牙人的统治始终薄弱：1799年全境登记在册的西班牙人只有七名，最后一批方济各会士于1821年离开。

en:
Aa'ku is the mesa country of the Acoma, a Keres-speaking Pueblo people west of the Rio Grande. Their main village stood on top of a flat rock 365 feet above the plain, and the only way up was a stairway of roughly two hundred broad steps, followed by footholds cut into the last stretch of stone; at the summit the defenders kept loose stones to roll down on anyone climbing. Up there were cisterns for rain and snow, stored maize and ground enough to sow, while farming camps such as Acomita worked the valley below. Maize and cotton cloth, turkeys, buffalo hide and turquoise moved between the mesa and its neighbours, and Navajo and Apache raids made the height worth holding. In 1444 the Acoma governed the rock and its camps under their own elders, and no Spanish soldier had yet come near it.

The first outsider to reach it, Estevanico in 1539, reported an independent 'kingdom' whose people wore turquoise at nose and ears. Hernando de Alvarado of Coronado's force came in 1540 and called the rock one of the strongest places he had seen. Juan de Oñate was received peacefully in October 1598, but after his nephew Juan de Zaldívar was killed there that December, Vicente de Zaldívar returned with seventy soldiers and a cannon. In three days of January 1599 the assault destroyed the village, killed about 800 Acoma and took some 500 captive, at a cost of one Spanish soldier. Men over twenty-five who were sentenced lost their right foot and twenty years of freedom, and two Indians visiting from other pueblos had one hand cut off and were sent home as a warning. Survivors began rebuilding before the year ended, and Oñate was later exiled from New Mexico for cruelty. In 1623 the Franciscans ordered a great church raised: Acoma labourers carried about 20,000 tons of adobe and sandstone up the stairway and hauled its pine beams from Mount Taylor, more than forty miles away. The Acoma joined the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, sheltered refugees from other pueblos and kept Catholic rites alongside their own on the mesa.
zh:
阿库是阿科马人的台地家园，阿科马人是说凯雷斯语的普韦布洛族群，聚居于里奥格兰德河以西。主村落建在一块高出平原111米的平顶岩丘上，唯一的上岩之路先是约两百级宽阔石阶，末段还要踩着凿出的脚窝徒手攀援；岩顶守军备有零散石块，专等攀岩者靠近时推落。岩上有蓄水池、储存的玉米和可耕作的土地，阿科米塔等农耕营地则在下方河谷劳作。玉米、棉布、火鸡、野牛皮和绿松石在台地与邻近村镇之间往来，纳瓦霍人和阿帕契人的袭掠也让这座高岩值得死守。1444年，阿科马人仍由本族长老治理岩丘与营地，西班牙士兵尚未涉足此地。

1539年，第一个外来者埃斯特万尼科抵达阿库，报告说这里是一个独立的「王国」，居民耳鼻上佩戴绿松石；翌年，科罗纳多麾下的埃尔南多·德·阿尔瓦拉多到此，称这是他见过最坚固的地方。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年10月还受到和平接待，但他的侄子胡安·德·萨尔迪瓦尔同年12月在此被杀后，维森特·德·萨尔迪瓦尔带着七十名士兵和一门大炮返回。1599年1月，三天强攻摧毁了村落，约八百名阿科马人被杀、约五百人被俘，西班牙方面只死一人。被判刑的二十五岁以上男子被砍去右脚并服二十年苦役；两名来自其他普韦布洛的访客被砍去一只手，放回本族示众。幸存者当年12月便开始重建，奥尼亚特后来也因暴行被逐出新墨西哥。1623年，方济各会下令修建大教堂，阿科马劳工把约两万吨土坯和砂岩背上岩丘，又从六十多公里外的泰勒山拖来松木房梁。阿科马人参加了1680年的普韦布洛起义，收容其他普韦布洛的逃难者，并在台地上把天主教仪轨与本土信仰并行保留。

en:
Saldindé is the mountain-edge country between the Rio Grande pueblos and the western rise of the Great Plains, home to the Jicarilla Apache. In 1444 their bands moved with the seasons between river-bottom fields of corn, beans and squash, mountain camps and the bison grounds east of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, carrying pottery and baskets to trade at Taos, Picuris and Pecos. Neighbouring Apache called them the People of Fixed Houses because they farmed and built Pueblo-like villages; the Spaniards later named them Jicarilla, 'little basket', after their sealed drinking baskets. The mountain-valley band called itself Saidindê, the Sand People, which gives the province its name.

In 1724 Comanche and Ute raiders armed with French guns fell on the eastern Apache bands, forcing one Jicarilla group to surrender half its women and children, burning its villages and leaving only sixty-nine men, two women and three boys alive. Survivors fled into the Sangre de Cristo north of Taos or took shelter at Pecos, and turned to the Spaniards they had long kept at a distance: in 1779 Jicarilla warriors marched with Ute, Pueblo and Spanish troops against the Comanche, and after seven more years of campaigns the Comanche sued for peace in 1786, letting Jicarilla groups reoccupy parts of their old grounds in southern Colorado.
zh:
萨尔丁德是格兰德河诸普韦布洛与大平原西缘之间的山麓地带，希卡里利亚阿帕奇人世代居住于此。1444年时，他们的群体随季节在河谷田亩、山地营地和桑格雷·德克里斯托山以东的野牛猎场间迁移，田里种着玉米、豆子和南瓜，又带着陶器和篮筐到陶斯、皮库里斯、佩科斯交易。邻近的阿帕奇人见他们务农、建起类似普韦布洛的村落，称他们为「住固定房屋的人」；西班牙人后来照他们密封的小饮水篮叫他们希卡里利亚，意为「小篮子」。山谷一支自称萨伊丁德（Saidinde），意为「沙人」，本省省名就来自这个称呼。

1724年，持有法国火器的科曼奇与尤特袭掠者攻入东阿帕奇诸部，逼迫一支希卡里利亚人交出半数妇女儿童，焚毁村庄，最后只剩六十九名男子、两名妇女和三名男孩活着。幸存者逃入陶斯以北的桑格雷·德克里斯托山，或到佩科斯避难，并转而向一向疏远的西班牙人借兵：1779年，希卡里利亚战士与尤特人、普韦布洛人和西班牙军队联合出征攻打科曼奇人；又经七年战事，科曼奇人于1786年求和，希卡里利亚人才得以回到科罗拉多南部的部分故地。

en:
Tsès Sembai takes its name from the Lipan Apache band Tsés tsembai, the Heads of Wolves People, who hunted the grasslands above the Texas Colorado River on the eastern flank of the Llano Estacado, possibly around the site of later Lubbock. In 1444 these easternmost Apache followed the bison herds across open plains, camping in river breaks where they gathered wild plants and planted small seasonal fields. Another plains people, the Teyas, held nearby country and were probably absorbed into the Lipan in later generations.

Coronado crossed these grasslands in 1541 and met both Teyas and Apache hunters. By 1608 the Lipan had Spanish horses, and their mounted bands ranged far as raiders and traders; Spanish records first named them during raids on the new settlement of San Antonio in 1718. Lipan chiefs made peace there in 1749, and at their urging the Spaniards founded Mission San Sabá on the San Saba River in 1757, though no Lipan ever came to live in it. To the Comanche the mission looked like a Spanish alliance with their Lipan enemies, and on 16 March 1758 some two thousand Comanche, Wichita and allied warriors burned it down, the only Texas mission destroyed outright. The Spanish punitive expedition of 1759 lost two cannon at the fortified Twin Villages on the Red River; a painting of the burning, completed in 1765, was the first artwork to depict an event in Spanish Texas.

A smallpox epidemic in 1764 and Comanche attacks had emptied the Lipan missions by 1767, and the crown inspector Marqués de Rubí then called for the Lipan to be exterminated. Around 1780 the Pecos River bands united under the chief Picax-Ande-Ins-Tinsle, Strong Arm, as the Lipiyanes coalition. Spanish estimates in 1820 put all the Lipan left in Texas at about seven hundred people.
zh:
采斯森拜得名于利潘阿帕奇人的采斯·森拜（Tses tsembai）一支，意为「狼首人」。他们在埃斯塔卡多平原东缘、得州科罗拉多河以北的草原游猎，活动范围可能就在后来拉伯克一带。1444年时，这支阿帕奇最东支的猎人随野牛群穿行开阔平原，在河谷断裂处扎营，兼营采集和小块季节田。邻近的特亚人据有附近地带，后世学者多认为他们最终并入了利潘人。

1541年，科罗纳多穿过这片草原，同时遇到特亚人和阿帕奇猎人。到1608年，利潘人已从西班牙人手中得到马匹，骑马队伍此后远行千里，四处袭掠又贩运货物；西班牙文献第一次明确记下他们，是1718年圣安东尼奥新城遇袭的时候。1749年利潘首领在圣安东尼奥议和，又经他们劝说，西班牙人于1757年在圣萨瓦河畔建起圣萨瓦传教站，却始终没有一个利潘人入住。在科曼奇人看来，这座传教站等于西班牙与宿敌利潘人结盟；1758年3月16日，约两千名科曼奇、威奇托及盟部战士将它焚毁，这是得州唯一一座被彻底烧毁的传教站。1759年，西班牙报复远征在雷德河畔设防的双村折了两门火炮；有人出资绘下这场大火，画作1765年完成，是西班牙治下得州第一幅描绘历史事件的作品。

1764年天花大疫，加上科曼奇人连年进攻，到1767年利潘人的传教站已全部逃散，西班牙巡阅官鲁维侯爵随即提出剿灭利潘之策。约1780年，佩科斯河沿岸各支拥戴名号「铁臂」的酋长皮卡克斯-安德-因斯-廷斯勒，组成利皮亚内斯联盟。1820年西班牙人估计，得州全境剩下的利潘人只有约七百口。

en:
Tahuundé was the country of the Tá'huú'ndé, a Mescalero band whose mountains and desert reaches lay along both sides of the Pecos in south-western Texas. Its southern end opened onto La Junta de los Ríos, where the Conchos pours into the Rio Grande, one of the few well-watered crossings on that long desert river. In 1444 Jumano towns of permanent houses stood on the floodplain: their people farmed corn and beans, fished and gathered desert plants, and traded bison hides along routes reaching the Rio Grande pueblos and the Conchos valley, while hunters pursued buffalo across the plains between the river fields and the Pecos canyons.

Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca reached the crossing in 1535, planted a cross on the mountainside and called the place La Junta de las Cruces. Spanish expeditions began recording the Jumanos in 1581; scholars estimate that around 1580 between twenty and thirty thousand people lived along the two rivers as Jumano or in Jumano-associated groups. Antonio de Espejo named one of their towns San Juan Evangelista in December 1582. Franciscans visiting the Conchos camps in 1629 were told that a lady in blue had already instructed the Jumanos in the faith, a story later attached in Spain to the nun María de Jesús de Ágreda, said to have visited America only in ecstatic visions. Chief Juan Sabeata came in 1683 with another sign, a fiery cross seen on the mountain, and missions were founded the following year.

Drought, Apache raids, disease and slave-raiding wore the Jumanos down; by 1729 Spaniards already spoke of 'Apache Jumanos', and by 1750 the name had nearly vanished from the records, its people absorbed into Apache, Wichita and Caddo groups. From 1760 a garrison of sixty soldiers guarded La Junta, and Spain made peace with the nearby Lipan in 1790.
zh:
塔洪德是梅斯卡莱罗人一支塔洪德（Ta'huu'nde）的乡土，其山地与沙漠范围沿得克萨斯西南部的佩科斯河两岸展开，南端通向拉洪塔·德洛斯里奥斯，即孔乔斯河汇入格兰德河之处，也是这条干旱长河上少有的水源充足的渡口。1444年时，胡马诺人的土屋村镇坐落在河漫滩上：居民种玉米和豆子、捕鱼、采集沙漠植物，把野牛皮沿商路贩往格兰德河诸普韦布洛和孔乔斯河谷；猎人则在河滨农田与佩科斯峡谷之间的平原上追捕野牛。

1535年，阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡抵达这处渡口，在山坡上立起十字架，称这里为十字汇流之地。1581年起，西班牙远征开始记录胡马诺人；据学者估计，1580年前后两河沿岸作为胡马诺人或其近缘群体生活的人口有两三万之多。1582年12月，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍将他们的一座村镇命名为圣胡安·埃万赫利斯塔。1629年到访孔乔斯河畔营地的方济各会修士被告知，已有一位蓝衣女子向胡马诺人传过道；这个说法后来在西班牙被附会到修女阿格雷达的玛丽亚·德·赫苏斯身上，据说她只在出神的异象中到过美洲。1683年，酋长胡安·萨贝亚塔带着另一个征兆求见西班牙人，说山中出现火十字，次年各传教站便建立起来。

干旱、阿帕奇袭掠、疫病和捕奴消耗着胡马诺人，1729年时西班牙人已开始使用「阿帕奇胡马诺人」的称呼；到1750年，这个名字几乎从记载中消失，族人多被阿帕奇、威奇托和卡多群体吸收。1760年起，一支六十人的驻军戍守拉洪塔，1790年西班牙又与附近的利潘人议和。

en:
Coahuilteco covers the flat Gulf shore south of the Nueces River, a country of lagoons, barrier islands and brushy inland plains reaching down toward the Pánuco. In 1444 no town or chiefdom ruled it: small Coahuiltecan bands hunted deer and bison, fished the lagoons, and gathered mesquite beans and prickly pear, moving between southern Texas and the land later called Tamaulipas. Fresh water is scarce for more than a hundred miles along this coast, so few bands camped on the shore itself, while the canoe-using Karankawa held the longer stretch to the north.

Alonso Álvarez de Pineda's Spanish expedition mapped this empty coastline in 1519, yet the Crown planted nothing there for decades. The shore entered colonial records in 1554, when three Spanish ships were wrecked on Padre Island; about a hundred survivors, walking south to Pánuco, were killed by local bands, all but one. Raiders out of Nuevo León later seized inland people for slaves, epidemics thinned the bands, and Apache pressure from the north drove refugees toward the missions. In 1746 the viceroy created the colony of Nuevo Santander, and José de Escandón settled it from 1748 with families from the interior: within a generation the colony ran from the Pánuco to the Guadalupe, with two dozen new towns and more than a million cattle on the open range, the first cattle country of Texas. Most of the old coastal bands were absorbed into the ranching towns around the missions.
zh:
科阿韦尔特科是努埃塞斯河以南平坦的墨西哥湾沿岸，潟湖、堰洲岛和长满灌丛的内陆平原一直铺向帕努科方向。1444年，这里没有城镇也没有酋邦：科阿韦尔特坎小群体猎鹿和野牛、在潟湖捕鱼、采集牧豆和仙人掌果，在得州南部与后来称作塔毛利帕斯的土地间迁徙。这段海岸一百多英里内少有淡水，很少有群体在海边扎营，划独木舟的卡兰卡瓦人占着更北面的绵长海岸。

1519年，阿隆索·阿尔瓦雷斯·德·皮内达的西班牙探险队绘下这段荒凉海岸，但王室几十年里没有在那里建立任何据点。海岸再次进入记载是1554年：三艘西班牙船在帕德雷岛失事，约百名幸存者徒步南下巴努科，几乎全部被当地群体杀死，仅一人幸免。后来新莱昂方向的掳掠者深入内陆抓人贩卖，疫病使各群体人口锐减，北方阿帕切人的压力又把难民赶向传教站。1746年，总督下令设立新桑坦德殖民地，何塞·德·埃斯坎东从1748年率内地移民家族前来开拓；一代人之内，殖民地从帕努科河延伸到瓜达卢佩河，建起二十多座新城镇，野地牧场上放牧着上百万头牛，成为得克萨斯最早的牧牛区。旧日的沿岸群体大多融入了传教站周围的牧业城镇。

en:
The grasslands above the upper Colorado River were the range of the Teł kóndahä, the Wild Goose band of the Lipan Apache; the Lipan call themselves the Łibaį Ndé, the Light Gray People, and were the easternmost of the Apache groups. In 1444 the Wild Goose had no horses. They hunted bison on foot, dragged their skin lodges with dog travois between the river breaks and the high plains to the west, and dried meat in thin sheets for the winter. Spanish records later called Apaches of these plains Querechos, a name heard first at Pecos Pueblo.

Coronado's expedition met Querecho hunters on the Llano Estacado in 1541, the first European sighting of Plains Apache bison hunters. The Lipan had Spanish horses by 1608, and mounted raiding parties soon struck the roads and settlements of New Spain; two Lipan chiefs nonetheless made peace at San Antonio in 1749. A mission founded on the San Saba River in 1757 to draw the Lipan in was destroyed the following year, before any Apache had settled there, by some 2,000 Comanche, Wichita, Tonkawa and Hasinai warriors who read the Spanish post as an alliance with their Lipan enemies. The Spanish-Lipan counterstroke failed in 1759 at the Twin Villages on the Red River: the Taovaya had girded their town with a moat and wooden stockade, and after four hours' fighting Colonel Ortiz Parrilla drew off with 19 dead, leaving two cannon behind. Comanches burned the Lipan missions at Candelaria and San Lorenzo in 1767, when every band, the Wild Goose included, had already quit the missions; later band lists treat the Wild Goose as possibly merged into the Prairie Men.
zh:
科罗拉多河上游的草原是利潘阿帕奇人野鹅部（Teł kóndahä）的游猎之地；利潘人自称「浅灰之人」（Łibaį Ndé），是阿帕奇诸支中位置最靠东的一支。1444年，野鹅部还没有马，他们步行猎野牛，用狗拉拖橇搬运兽皮帐篷，在河谷断裂地带与西面的高平原之间往返，再把肉切成薄片晒干过冬。后来的西班牙文献把平原上的这类阿帕奇人称作克雷乔人，这个名字最初是在佩科斯普韦布洛听到的。

1541年，科罗纳多的探险队在埃斯塔卡多平原遇到克雷乔猎人，这是欧洲人第一次见到平原上的阿帕奇野牛猎人。到1608年，利潘人已从西班牙人那里得到马匹，骑马的袭击队伍很快频频袭扰新西班牙的道路和居点；尽管如此，仍有两名利潘首领于1749年在圣安东尼奥议和。1757年，西班牙人在圣萨瓦河上修建传教站招抚利潘人，次年它就被约两千名科曼奇、威奇托、通卡瓦和哈西奈战士摧毁，那时还没有一个阿帕奇人入站；在他们看来，这座西班牙据点就是西班牙人与利潘仇敌结盟的证据。1759年，西班牙与利潘人的反击在雷德河的双村失利：陶瓦亚人在村子周围挖了壕沟、竖起木栅，激战四小时后，奥尔蒂斯·帕里利亚上校带着十九名死者撤退，还丢下两门大炮。1767年，科曼奇人烧掉坎德拉里亚和圣洛伦索的利潘传教站，那时各部（包括野鹅部）都已弃传教站而去；后来的部族名录认为，野鹅部可能并入了草原人部。

en:
Piikani, or Piegan, was the westernmost and largest of the Blackfoot-speaking peoples. The land named for them follows the Rocky Mountain Front east to the shortgrass plains around Cut Bank, Two Medicine and the Marias, where bison were driven over jumps in the summer hunt and bands wintered in wooded creek valleys. The high ground above Two Medicine is sacred country in Blackfoot belief, the setting of their creation story. In 1444 the camps still moved on dog travois, and the Algonquian-speaking ancestors of the Piegan had not yet reached this Montana edge of the plains; Shoshone, Salish and Kutenai peoples kept the routes between the mountains and the grassland.

Horses and guns remade the Piikani in the first half of the eighteenth century. Around 1730 their bands moved southwest out of the Saskatchewan country as Shoshone raids intensified, and took horses from the Kutenai, Interior Salish and Nez Perce; mounted Piegan parties pushed south toward the Yellowstone and made themselves a power of the northern plains. In the winter of 1787-88 the fur trader James Gaddy and David Thompson of the Hudson's Bay Company camped with a Piegan band on the Bow River, the first whites recorded seeing that river. On 27 July 1806 Lewis's party of the Lewis and Clark Expedition met Piegan on Two Medicine Creek, and a scuffle over guns and horses left two Piegan dead, the expedition's only bloodshed. British traders coming from the Saskatchewan and American parties ascending the Missouri afterwards had to reckon with Piegan power.
zh:
皮卡尼又称皮根人，是黑脚语各族里位置最靠西、人数最多的一支。以其为名的土地顺着落基山前缘向东，铺到卡特班克、双梅迪辛和玛丽亚斯河一带的短草平原：夏季围猎把野牛赶下跳崖，各部落在林木溪谷里过冬。双梅迪辛上方的高地是黑脚人信仰中的圣地，他们的创世故事就设在这里。1444年，营地仍靠狗拉拖架迁移，皮根人的阿尔冈昆语先民还没有到达蒙大拿这片平原边缘；往来山地与草原之间的，是休休尼人、萨利什人和库特尼人。

18世纪上半叶，马匹和枪支重塑了皮卡尼人。约1730年休休尼人的袭扰加剧，他们从萨斯喀彻温故地向西南迁移，从库特尼人、内陆萨利什人和内兹珀斯人手里得到马匹；骑上马背的皮根队伍向南推向黄石河，成了北方平原上的一支强权。1787至1788年冬天，毛皮商詹姆斯·加迪和哈德逊湾公司的戴维·汤普森与一群皮根人在弓河畔扎营，他们是最早见到这条河的白人记录者。1806年7月27日，刘易斯—克拉克探险队的刘易斯分队在双梅迪辛溪遭遇皮根人，一场争夺枪支和马匹的扭斗造成两名皮根人死亡，这也是整支探险队唯一一次流血。此后，从萨斯喀彻温来的英国商人和溯密苏里河而上的美国队伍，都得掂量皮根人的力量。

en:
Haaninin means the White Clay people; French traders misread their sign-language gesture and called them Gros Ventre, 'big belly'. Their later homeland was the cold Milk River grassland between the Bear Paws and the Little Rockies, where bison herds crossed semi-arid flats and bands wintered along wooded watercourses. In 1444 the Haaninin were still one people with the Arapaho in the Red River country, east of the Upper Missouri; the Montana valleys that later took their name saw only dog-travois hunting camps passing through.

Ojibwe pressure set the Haaninin moving toward the Upper Missouri early in the eighteenth century. They and the Arapaho parted, possibly near Devils Lake, and the Haaninin continued into Montana, where they had horses by mid-century. Their first known meeting with white men came around 1754 between the forks of the Saskatchewan, and smallpox soon cut into their numbers; the Lewis and Clark account of 1806 lists a northern band of 260 tipis, about 2,500 people, trading with the North West Company on the upper Saskatchewan. Around 1793 they burned two Hudson's Bay Company posts there, because the guns sold at them were reaching Cree and Assiniboine raiders. The Haaninin then joined the Blackfoot Confederacy and ranged across north-central Montana and the Saskatchewan grasslands. Lewis and Clark named the clay-pale Milk River in 1805, and the Anglo-American treaty of 1818 drew the boundary through the watershed their hunting camps still crossed.
zh:
汉尼宁意为「白粘土人」；法国商人会错了他们的手语手势，叫他们格罗斯文特，意思是「大肚子」。他们后来的家园在熊爪山与小落基山之间寒冷的牛奶河草原：野牛群走过半干旱的平地，各部落在林木水畔过冬。1444年时，汉尼宁人还和阿拉帕霍人同属红河地区的一个族群，住在上密苏里以东；后来冠上他们名字的这些蒙大拿河谷，当时只有狗拉拖架的狩猎营地经过。

18世纪初，欧及布威人的压力把汉尼宁人推向上密苏里。他们与阿拉帕霍人可能在魔鬼湖附近分手，汉尼宁人继续进入蒙大拿，到18世纪中叶已有马匹。已知他们与白人最早的接触约在1754年，地点在萨斯喀彻温河两支流之间，天花很快削减了他们的人口；刘易斯与克拉克1806年的记录里，北面一支有260顶帐篷、约2500人，在萨斯喀彻温河上游与西北公司贸易。约1793年，他们焚毁了那里的两座哈德逊湾公司商站，因为站里卖出的枪支流到了克里人和阿西尼博因袭击者手里。汉尼宁人随后加入黑脚联盟，游猎于蒙大拿中北部和萨斯喀彻温草原。1805年刘易斯—克拉克探险队为水色泛白的牛奶河命名，1818年英美条约划出的边界，正穿过他们游猎营地往来的流域。

en:
Ashshipite is the broken grass country where the Yellowstone, the river the Crow called the Elk, and the Musselshell meet the Missouri. Eroded breaks and shortgrass plains run between the Powder and the Tongue, and the grass was black with buffalo in season. In 1444 it was the northern home of the Kiowa, the Cauigu; their own tradition places the making of their people in the northern Missouri basin around the Yellowstone. They had no horses yet. Dog travois dragged the lodge poles and baggage, hunters ran buffalo on foot in great communal surrounds, and their language, kin to the Tanoan speech of the Rio Grande pueblos far to the south, set them apart from every neighbour on the river.

About 1650 the Kiowa moved southeast to the Black Hills, where they lived at peace with the Crow; a century later the invading Cheyenne and Sioux pushed them on to the southern plains. In their place came the River Crow, kinsmen who had split from the Hidatsa on the Knife after a quarrel over a bison stomach, which left the Hidatsa calling the Crow 'Those Who Pout Over Tripe'. The Crow called this band Ashshipite, the Black Lodges, the name this land now bears. From about 1730 they built up great horse herds on the Yellowstone grasslands and fought off Blackfoot, Gros Ventre and Assiniboine raiders. The Lakota came next. The Crow killed at least thirty of them in 1800-01, and the next year Lakota and Cheyenne warriors wiped out a Crow camp of thirty tipis, killing every man. In 1806 Crow raiders quietly drove off horses from Lewis and Clark's detachment on the Yellowstone without ever showing themselves. In 1820 another allied war party destroyed a camp on the Tongue River, the severest blow the River Crow ever suffered.
zh:
阿什希皮特是黄石河与马瑟尔谢尔河汇入密苏里河一带起伏破碎的草地，克罗人把黄石河叫作「麋鹿河」。粉河与汤河之间遍布蚀沟和矮草平原，到了季节野牛遍地。1444年，这里是基奥瓦人（Cauigu）北方的家园，他们的口传把本民族成形之地记在黄石河附近的北密苏里盆地。那时他们还没有马，狗拉拖橇载着帐篷杆和家当迁徙，猎人们徒步大队合围野牛。他们的语言与遥远南方格兰德河畔普韦布洛人的塔诺安语同源，使他们在沿河各邻族中显得与众不同。

1650年前后，基奥瓦人向东南迁到黑山，与克罗人和平共处；一个世纪后，西进的夏安人和苏族人把他们继续赶向南部平原。取而代之的是河克罗人：他们与奈夫河畔的希达察人本是亲族，因争夺一只野牛肚反目西迁，希达察人因此把克罗人叫作「为牛肚噘嘴的人」。克罗语称这支人为阿什希皮特（Ashshipite），意为「黑棚屋」，这片土地便因他们得名。约1730年起，河克罗人在黄石草原上养起大群马匹，抗击黑脚人、格罗斯文特人和阿西尼博因人的袭掠。接下来压境的是拉科塔人。1800至1801年，克罗人至少杀死三十名拉科塔人，第二年拉科塔人与夏安人便屠灭一个有三十座帐篷的克罗营地，杀光营中男子。1806年，克罗骑手趁夜悄悄赶走刘易斯与克拉克队伍在黄石河畔的马匹，始终没有现身。1820年，又一支联军摧毁汤河畔的一处克罗营地，这是河克罗人遭受过的最沉重打击。

en:
Eelalapito, 'Kicked in the Bellies', was the name later borne by a Crow band whose home became the Bighorn Basin, a dry plateau about a hundred miles across that takes only 6 to 10 inches of rain a year. The Absaroka Range bounds it on the west and the Bighorn Mountains on the east; the Wind River enters through a gap between the southern ranges and changes its name to the Bighorn on the basin floor. In 1444 this was a pre-horse world: small bison-hunting camps moved on dog travois, wintered in wooded river valleys, and dried meat and berries into pemmican. The Crow themselves still lived in the upper-Missouri earth-lodge villages of the Hidatsa, from whom they had not yet split.

In the late seventeenth century the Crow parted from the Hidatsa and moved west onto the Yellowstone and its tributaries, fighting Shoshone bands for the new hunting grounds; the Eelalapito made the basin their own and ranged south past the Owl Creek and Bridger ranges. Horses reached them by the 1740s, enlarging camps and herds and drawing Blackfoot raiders. In 1805 François-Antoine Larocque travelled for two and a half months with a Crow camp toward the Bighorn Mountains and left the first detailed European account of their movements. John Colter crossed the basin itself in 1807 and came upon steaming, sulphurous ground at its western edge, the thermal spot later called Colter's Hell.
zh:
厄拉拉皮（Eelalapito）意为「被踢中腹部的人」，是后来克劳人一支的名称，他们的家园成为大角盆地。这片干旱高原宽约一百英里，一年只有六到十英寸雨水，西临阿布萨罗卡岭，东接大角山；温德河从南部山岭间的缺口流入，在盆地上改称大角河。1444年的这里还没有马：小型野牛狩猎营地靠狗拉橇迁移，在林木河谷过冬，把肉和浆果捶成肉糜饼。克劳人当时还住在密苏里河上游希达沙人的土屋村落中，尚未与之分离。

17世纪末，克劳人与希达沙人分道，西进黄石河及其支流，为争夺新猎场与休休尼诸支交战；厄拉拉皮人以大角盆地为家园，活动范围南逾猫头鹰溪山和布里杰山。马匹在1740年代传到他们手中，营地与马群随之扩大，也引来黑脚人袭掠。1805年，弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克随一处克劳营地向大角山行进两个半月，留下欧洲人对其迁徙活动最早的详细记述。1807年约翰·科尔特穿过盆地，在西缘发现喷吐蒸汽的硫磺地热地，那里后来被称为「科尔特地狱」。

en:
Tsetsehesahese renders Tsétsêhéstâhese, 'those who are like this', the name of the Cheyenne proper. Their later plains country ran from the Bighorn Mountains to the Black Hills, along the upper Powder, Tongue and Little Bighorn, where cottonwood bottoms gave shelter through hard winters and the short-grass uplands carried great bison herds. In 1444 this country was not yet theirs and horses had not reached the northern plains: the Tsitsistas lived far to the east in the Minnesota woodlands, on wild rice and village hunts. Their tradition holds that the prophet Sweet Medicine received the four Sacred Arrows at Bear Butte on the edge of the Black Hills, and the arrow bundle was carried before the tribe whenever it went to war.

Pressure from the Assiniboine, and later from Ojibwe armed with muskets, pushed the Cheyenne west: a band visited the French Fort Crevecoeur on the Illinois River in the mid-seventeenth century, the first written notice of them, and their villagers reached the Missouri in 1676, though some communities kept to the Minnesota lake country until the 1760s. West of the river they learned earth-lodge village life from the Mandan and Hidatsa, then traded lodges for tipis and horse herds, the first of the later plains peoples to enter the Black Hills and the Powder country. Around 1730 they passed horses to the Lakota; the Lakota in turn grew stronger, and by 1776 Lakota bands held much of the Cheyenne ground by the Black Hills. The Cheyenne camped and raided with Arapaho allies and fought the Crow above all; Lewis and Clark visited a surviving Cheyenne village in 1804, and the fur posts built afterward drew the horse bands into the Missouri trade.
zh:
采采赫萨赫塞（Tsétsêhéstâhese）意为「如此之人」，指夏延人本体。他们后来的草原家园从大角山延伸到黑山，沿保德河、汤河和小大角河上游展开，三角叶杨林河谷可供越冬，短草高原则养育着庞大的野牛群。1444年时这片土地还不属于他们，马匹也未传入北方平原：夏延人仍住在遥远东方的明尼苏达林地，以野米和村落周边的狩猎为生。按他们的传统，先知甜药在黑山边缘的熊丘领受四支神箭，此后部落出征，神箭束都要抬在队伍之前。

阿西尼博因人、以及后来持火枪的欧及布威人的压力，把夏延人逐步推向西方：17世纪中叶，一支夏延人访问伊利诺伊河畔的法国克雷沃克尔堡，这是关于他们最早的文字记载；1676年他们的村民抵达密苏里河，也有一些群体留在明尼苏达湖区直到1760年代。河的西岸，他们先向曼丹人和希达察人学会土屋村落的生活，随后又以土屋换取帐篷和马群，成为后来的草原诸族中最早进入黑山和保德河地区的一支。约1730年他们把马匹传给拉科塔人；拉科塔人反而更加强盛，到1776年已占去夏延人在黑山一带的许多土地。夏延人与阿拉帕霍盟友共同扎营、外出袭掠，主要的敌手是克劳人；1804年刘易斯和克拉克走访了一座留存下来的夏延村落，此后建起的毛皮商站把这些骑马群体纳入密苏里河贸易。

en:
Kuccuntikka, also written Guchundeka or Kuchun-deka, means 'Bison Eaters.' The name belonged to Eastern Shoshone bands whose valleys followed the Green River and Wind River beneath the Absaroka and Wind River ranges, with seasonal trails toward Yellowstone, Jackson Lake, and the Teton passes.
