Family camps wintered in sheltered bottoms, gathered in spring, separated to fish and dig roots, and met again for the autumn bison drive. In 1444 the people who called themselves Newe travelled on foot and used dogs to carry loads. Their trails linked Great Basin seed and pine-nut grounds, Plateau fishing rivers, and Plains bison country, but no outside ruler controlled the mountains.

After 1500, Shoshone bands crossed into the northwestern plains, first on foot and then with horses. The mounted Kuccuntikka made bison the centre of their seasonal round; in the 1700s bison supplied roughly half their diet. The Comanche split away on the southern edge of that expansion around 1700. Raids and rivalry from Blackfoot, Crow, Lakota, Cheyenne, and Arapaho bands later forced many Eastern Shoshone back toward the mountains, and David Thompson reported in 1787 that the Blackfoot held much of their former plains range. John Colter, a former Lewis and Clark man, left Manuel Lisa's Fort Raymond in October 1807 and travelled for months through Crow and Shoshone country, probably crossing the winter Yellowstone and Teton region by a northern Wind River pass on a journey of more than 500 miles. When he returned in 1808, his reports of geysers and hot springs struck many listeners as improbable. By 1821 beaver trappers were entering the Green and Wind River valleys, but the mountain camps and passes still belonged to the Eastern Shoshone.
zh:
库聪蒂卡又写作古聪德卡或库春德卡，意思是「食野牛者」。这个名称属于东肖肖尼人的若干队群，他们的河谷沿绿河与温德河展开，北面是阿布萨罗卡岭和温德岭，季节性山路通往黄石、杰克逊湖和提顿山口。家族营地在避风低地过冬，春天汇合，随后分开捕鱼、挖取根块，秋天再集合围猎野牛。1444年，自称「内韦」的人们徒步迁徙，用狗驮物。他们的山路连接大盆地的草籽和松子地、高原的产鱼河流，以及大平原的野牛场，但没有外来统治者控制这些山地。

1500年以后，肖肖尼队群已进入西北大平原，起初步行，后来骑马。骑马的库聪蒂卡人把野牛作为一年生计的中心；十八世纪时，野牛约占他们食物的一半。科曼奇人约在1700年从这片扩张区域的南缘分离出去。黑脚、克劳、拉科他、夏延和阿拉帕霍等队群的袭扰与争夺，后来迫使许多东肖肖尼人退回山地；戴维·汤普森1787年记载，黑脚人已占据他们旧日平原领地的大部。1807年10月，曾随刘易斯和克拉克远征的约翰·科尔特离开曼努埃尔·莉萨的雷蒙德堡，用数月时间穿过克劳人和肖肖尼人的土地，行程五百多英里，可能经温德岭北部山口越过冬季的黄石与提顿地区。他在1808年返回后讲述的间歇泉和温泉，被许多听者当作离奇之说。到1821年，海狸捕兽者已开始进入绿河与温德河谷，但山地营地和山口仍在东肖肖尼人手中。

en:
Baachinena, 'the red willow men', was what the Southern Arapaho called the Northern Arapaho, who named themselves the White Sage People and were counted the mother tribe of the whole nation. Their later camps followed the cold shortgrass plains and willow-lined river valleys of western Nebraska and eastern Wyoming, above the upper North Platte and the Loup. In 1444 small pedestrian hunting bands shared this country with the bison herds: they moved on foot behind dog travois and wintered in the sheltered river bottoms. The Arapaho were then far to the northeast, Algonquian farmers in the Red River valley, living beside the people later known as the Gros Ventre.

Ojibwe raiders armed by French traders pushed that people west before 1700 and on to the upper Missouri, where the Arapaho and Gros Ventre separated. The Arapaho turned south into Wyoming and Colorado, took to horses, and built a long alliance with the Cheyenne. The northern camps kept the Arapaho sacred pipe and tribal bundles, and their sign in Plains sign language read 'mother people'. About 1800 the camps split into northern and southern groups; the reports brought back by Lewis and Clark in 1806 placed the northerners near the Loup headwaters. In 1811 Wilson Price Hunt, travelling east from Astoria with the Astor party, followed the North Platte valley through these plains, the first written American account of the river road across them.
zh:
巴齐尼那（Baachinena）意为「红柳人」，是南阿拉帕霍人对北阿拉帕霍人的称呼；北支自称「白艾人」，被视为整个阿拉帕霍民族的母支。他们后来的营地顺着内布拉斯加西部、怀俄明东部寒冷的短草平原和柳林河谷分布，活动在北普拉特河上游与卢普河一带。1444年，这里是小型步行狩猎群体与野牛群共处之地：人们跟着狗拉橇步行迁移，在避风的河谷低地过冬。那时阿拉帕霍人还远在东北方，是雷德河谷的阿尔冈昆农耕者，邻着后来被称为格罗斯文特人的族群。

得到法国商人武装的欧及布威袭掠者在1700年以前把这支人群向西赶向密苏里河上游，阿拉帕霍人与格罗斯文特人在那里分离。阿拉帕霍人南下进入怀俄明和科罗拉多，改以马匹为生，同夏延人结成长期同盟。北方各营保管着阿拉帕霍人的圣管和部落圣物包，在平原手势语里，他们的手势意思是「母亲之民」。约1800年，各营分为南北两群；刘易斯与克拉克1806年带回的报告把北方这群人记在卢普河源头附近。1811年，阿斯托利亚远征队的威尔逊·普赖斯·亨特从阿斯托利亚东返，沿北普拉特河谷穿过这片平原，留下了美国人关于这条河谷通道最早的文字记载。

en:
Skiri, written Skidi in older records and called the Wolf band or Panimaha, is the northernmost of the four Pawnee bands and gives this province its name. Their Caddoan speech stood closer to the Arikara than to the three southern bands, and their own oral history kept them a separate people until the mid-eighteenth century. In 1444 their small rectangular earth-lodge villages stood mainly along the Republican River. Women grew maize, beans and squash, and the whole community went out on foot for communal bison hunts. Priests and hereditary chiefs directed the ceremonies, in a land where no horse and no European firearm had yet appeared.

Mounted Apache raiders pressed the Skiri hard after about 1670. The villages united about 1680, left the Republican for the upper Loup, and rebuilt as compact towns of large circular lodges behind ditch-and-wall defences. In 1720 Skiri and Otoe warriors fell on Pedro de Villasur's Spanish column near the Loup's mouth, killing thirty-six of its forty Spaniards, ten Indian allies and a French guide; Villasur died with them and the survivors fled back to New Mexico. Early French maps labelled the Platte the Panimaha River after these people. The Skiri kept the Morning Star rite, in which a captive woman was bound to a pyre at the spring ceremony, for they held that without the offering their crops and hunts would fail. About 1817 the young warrior Petalesharo cut a Comanche girl free from that pyre, gave her a horse and provisions and sent her home, and the next year he freed a Spanish boy whom a trader passed on to St Louis. In 1821 he joined the O'Fallon delegation to Washington, met President Monroe, and received from schoolgirls who had watched the chiefs dance a silver medal inscribed 'bravest of the brave'. Smallpox epidemics had by then reduced the eight Skiri villages of 1725 to one, and in 1818 the Pawnee made their first land cession to the United States.
zh:
斯基伊（史料通译斯基迪）又称「狼族」或帕尼马哈，是波尼四支中位置最北的一支，本省即以它为名。他们的卡多语比三支南部波尼更接近阿利卡拉人的语言，其口传历史也表明，直到18世纪中叶他们都是单独的族群。1444年，斯基迪人的长方形小土屋村主要坐落在共和河沿岸：妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，全村徒步出动，集体围猎野牛。祭司和世袭酋长主持各项仪式；这片土地上那时还没有马匹，也没有欧洲火器。

约1670年后，骑马的阿帕奇袭掠者把斯基迪人逼得很紧。各村约在1680年联合起来，离开共和河迁往上卢普河，改筑带壕沟和围墙的密集村庄，土屋也换成更大的圆形。1720年，斯基迪人与奥托武士在卢普河口突袭佩德罗·德·维拉尔苏尔的西班牙纵队，四十名西班牙人被杀三十六名，另有十名印第安盟友和一名法国向导毙命，维拉尔苏尔也死在其中，残部逃回新墨西哥。早期法国地图因此把普拉特河标作「帕尼马哈河」。斯基迪人奉行晨星祭：祭典在春天举行，掳来的女子被绑在柴堆上，他们认为不献这份祭，庄稼和猎获就会衰败。约1817年，年轻战士佩塔莱沙罗把一名科曼奇女子从柴堆上解下，给她备了马和干粮，送她返回本族；第二年他又救下一个西班牙男孩，由商人辗转送往圣路易斯。1821年，他随奥法伦使团前往华盛顿，见到门罗总统；看过酋长们跳舞的女学生送他一枚银奖章，上镌「勇者之勇」。那时天花已多次流行，1725年时的八座斯基迪大村只剩一座；1818年，波尼人首次向美国割让土地。

en:
The Utsehta were the second great division of the Osage, the Wazhazhe of the Middle Waters — 'Down-Below People', whose lodges stood just below the hilltop towns of the Pahatsi. French traders, misreading their signs for 'above' and 'below', rendered the two bands as the Great and the Little Osage. Their villages and hunts lay west of the Pahatsi, in the oak woods and prairies stretching toward the Kansa. Like the Great Osage they farmed the bottomlands in summer and trailed buffalo on foot far into the plains, and in 1444 no European could yet have named either band.

The Marquette and Jolliet map of 1673 first printed the Osage name, and by 1690 the horse had spread through the bands. French goods then pulled the two divisions apart: by 1720 the Utsehta had left the Pahatsi for new villages on the Missouri River terraces. Étienne de Bourgmont, a former French officer who had lived for years among the Missouri tribes, built Fort Orleans there in 1723 at the mouth of the Grand River, the first European post on the Missouri. Named for the Duke of Orléans, it was meant to anchor a French empire reaching from Montreal to New Mexico, and he held it with forty soldiers. In 1725 he escorted Utsehta and other Osage chiefs to France, where they toured Versailles, Marly and Fontainebleau, saw an opera and hunted with Louis XV; Bourgmont stayed in Normandy and never returned. The French abandoned the fort the next year, and one account says the last eight soldiers were killed and the palisade burned. The Little Osage grew strong on guns and horses, trading and raiding between the Missouri and the Arkansas. After France ceded Louisiana in 1763, the Spanish of St Louis dealt with them through the Chouteau brothers. A smallpox epidemic cost the nation perhaps 2,000 dead early in the new century; when Lewis and Clark passed up the Missouri in 1804 the Little Osage lay a short way upstream from the Great Osage, and the treaties of 1808 and 1818 steadily handed their Missouri grounds to the United States.
zh:
乌采塔是奥塞奇（瓦扎热人，「中游之水的儿女」）的另一大分支——「下方之民」，屋舍就在帕哈齐人山顶诸镇的下方。法国商人把他们手势中的「上」「下」误读成「大」「小」，两支便被叫作大奥塞奇与小奥塞奇。他们的村落和猎场位于帕哈齐以西，林莽与草原一直铺向堪萨人的地界。和大奥塞奇人一样，他们夏天在河滩种地，徒步远入大平原追猎野牛；1444年时，还没有任何欧洲人能叫出这两支的名字。

1673年，马凯特与若利埃绘制的地图首次记下奥塞奇之名，到1690年，马已传遍各支。把两支拆开的是法国货：1720年前后，乌采塔人脱离帕哈齐，迁到密苏里河畔的阶地上另建新村。曾在密苏里诸部落中生活多年的前法国军官艾蒂安·德·布格蒙，1723年在格兰德河口建起奥尔良堡，这是密苏里河上第一座欧洲人据点。堡垒以奥尔良公爵命名，为的是撑起一个从蒙特利尔伸向新墨西哥的法兰西帝国，由他率四十名士兵驻守。1725年，他护送乌采塔和其他奥塞奇首领前往法国，首领们游览了凡尔赛、马尔利和枫丹白露，看了歌剧，还随路易十五行猎；布格蒙却留在诺曼底，再也没有回去。第二年法国人放弃了堡垒，一说最后八名士兵全数被杀、木栅被烧。小奥塞奇靠着火枪与马匹壮大，在密苏里河与阿肯色河之间贸易、劫掠。1763年法国割让路易斯安那后，圣路易斯的西班牙人经舒托兄弟与他们交易。新世纪初的一场天花让全族损失约两千人；1804年刘易斯与克拉克沿密苏里河上溯时，小奥塞奇人住在大奥塞奇上游不远处，1808年和1818年的条约，则把他们在密苏里的土地陆续交到美国手中。

en:
The Knife River comes down to the Missouri here through a wide green valley, and at its mouth stood the towns of the Hiraaca, 'People of the Willows', the largest of the three Hidatsa village groups. The Hiraaca began as nomadic bands around Devils Lake to the northeast and settled on the Knife only after moving west among the Mandan and taking up farming. Their main town, Big Hidatsa, was founded around 1600. Its round earth lodges stood forty feet across, and a family's best horses were penned by the door. Women tended large gardens of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, and the surplus went out on a trade network that reached from Minnesota to the southern plains and the Gulf; Cree, Assiniboine, Crow, Cheyenne, Kiowa and Comanche parties all came to the Knife to barter. Hidatsa ancestors had farmed this valley since the thirteenth century, and in 1444 they and the Mandan held the river as neighbours and allies.

The first Europeans came in 1738, when La Verendrye's French party visited the Mandan towns nearby, then reckoned at about 15,000 people in nine fortified villages. Horses reached the Hidatsa soon afterwards. The smallpox epidemic that moved north out of Mexico in 1781-82 emptied whole villages, and the survivors closed ranks with the Mandan. About 1790 they beat off a great Sioux siege of Big Hidatsa, cutting down more than a hundred of the attackers as they retreated. North West Company traders such as David Thompson arrived in the 1790s. In 1800 a Hidatsa raiding party carried off the Shoshone girl Sacagawea from a camp far up the Missouri. She lived in the lower Hidatsa village until the winter of 1804-05, when Lewis and Clark built Fort Mandan beside the five allied towns and took her west with them as their interpreter.
zh:
奈夫河流经一片宽阔的绿谷注入密苏里河，河口一带坐落着希拉卡人的城镇。希拉卡（Hiraaca）意为「柳树之人」，是希达察三个村落群中最大的一支。他们原是东北方魔鬼湖一带的游猎群体，西迁到奈夫河、与曼丹人为邻后才定居务农；主村大希达察约在1600年建立。村里的圆形土屋直径达四十英尺，主人最珍爱的马就拴在门边的围栏里。妇女照管大片园圃，种玉米、豆子、南瓜和向日葵，剩余出产沿贸易网外销，远达明尼苏达、南方平原和墨西哥湾；克里、阿西尼博因、克劳、夏安、基奥瓦和科曼奇的队伍都到奈夫河来交易。希达察人的先民自13世纪起就在这条河谷耕种，1444年时，他们与曼丹人沿河比邻，互为盟邦。

第一批欧洲人于1738年到来，拉韦朗德里率领的法国队伍造访了附近的曼丹村镇，据估计当时曼丹人约有一万五千之众，分住九个设防村落。此后不久马传到希达察人手中。1781至1782年，自墨西哥北上的天花使整村整村地死空，幸存者便与曼丹人合居联防。约1790年，他们顶住苏族人对大希达察的大规模围攻，趁敌军撤退时击杀逾百人。1790年代，戴维·汤普森等西北公司商人来到村中。1800年，一支希达察战队在密苏里河上游远处的营地掳走肖肖尼少女萨卡加维亚；她住在希达察下村，直到1804至1805年冬，刘易斯与克拉克在五个结盟村镇旁建起曼丹堡，带她西行担任翻译。

en:
Itscheabine is the name of an Assiniboine band recorded in early fur-trade lists, where French accounts translate it as the Girls' band. Its grounds were the broken grassland of the upper Souris River and Missouri Coteau, between the Assiniboine parklands and the Mandan and Hidatsa earth-lodge towns on the Missouri. In 1444 Nakota families still moved on foot and hauled their lodges with dog travois. Hunters took bison in the wooded Souris valley and trapped beaver and wolves among the potholes, then carried furs, robes and pemmican south to trade for Mandan corn and crafted goods. Horses, muskets and Europeans had not yet reached the coteau.

La Vérendrye learned the overland route in the autumn of 1738, when he left the newly built Fort La Reine with a large Assiniboine party, crossed this prairie to a Mandan village in December, and returned in January 1739. Horses and muskets later changed Nakota hunting and made the band part of the carrying trade between Assiniboine posts, Hudson Bay and the Missouri towns. At the Assiniboine edge of the country, the North West Company built Fort Montagne à la Bosse in 1790. Its stockade, about 200 by 250 feet, stood on a high bank above the plain. The post handled more bison robes and wolf skins than beaver, and its pemmican fed voyageurs on routes farther north; it also exchanged messages with the Mandan. François-Antoine Larocque left the fort for the Yellowstone River in 1805, near the end of its recorded use, and by 1821 no European post remained on the Souris coteau.
zh:
伊茨切阿比内是早期毛皮贸易记录中的一支阿西尼博因队群，法国文献把它的名字解释为「女孩队群」。他们的土地在苏里斯河上游和密苏里高地起伏破碎的草原上，东北接阿西尼博因林缘，西南通曼丹人与希达察人在密苏里河畔的土屋村镇。1444年时，纳科塔人仍徒步迁徙，用狗拉拖橇搬运帐篷。猎人在苏里斯河林木河湾猎野牛，在锅形湖沼间捕河狸和狼，再把毛皮、皮袍和干肉饼带到南方，换取曼丹人的玉米和手工器物。马匹、火枪和欧洲人都还没有进入这片高地。

1738年秋，拉韦朗德里随一大队阿西尼博因人离开新建的拉雷讷堡，穿过这片草原，12月抵达一座曼丹村镇，1739年1月返回，摸清了这条陆路。后来马匹和火枪改变了纳科塔人的狩猎方式，也使这支队群参与阿西尼博因商栈、哈得孙湾与密苏里村镇之间的转运贸易。1790年，西北公司在这片土地边缘的阿西尼博因河畔修建蒙塔涅阿拉博斯堡。围栅圈出约200英尺乘250英尺的场地，立在俯瞰草原的高岸上；这里经手的皮袍和狼皮多于河狸皮，出产的干肉饼则供给更北航路上的船夫，商栈也与曼丹人互通消息。1805年，弗朗索瓦-安托万·拉罗克从这里出发前往黄石河，此时该堡已接近有记载使用期的尾声；到1821年，苏里斯高地上已没有欧洲商栈。

en:
The Wahpekute, 'Shooters among the Trees' or 'Leaf Archers' in Dakota, were one of the four Eastern Dakota bands and, with the Mdewakanton of Mille Lacs, made up the Upper Council of the Santee, 'dwellers at the knife flint'. Unlike the settled Mdewakanton, they kept no fixed villages, moving through the oak woods and lake country between Mille Lacs and the Minnesota River, gathering wild rice, taking deer in the coverts and pushing out on to the prairie edge for buffalo. In 1444 these hunting grounds were theirs alone.

The first French post came in 1700, when Pierre-Charles Le Sueur built Fort L'Huillier for about thirty men near the mouth of the Blue Earth River. He had mistaken a soft blue clay for copper ore; the clay proved worthless, and by 1702 the fort had been attacked and abandoned, its remaining men never heard of again. Through the eighteenth century Ojibwe war parties carrying French muskets pressed the Wahpekute off the woods and southward. Zebulon Pike made the first United States treaty with the Dakota in 1805, and in 1821 Wahpekute camps still moved along the fur trails of the Minnesota River country.
zh:
瓦佩库特（Wahpekute）在达科他语中意为「林间射手」，又称「叶间射手」，是东达科他四支之一，与米拉湖的梅德瓦坎顿人共同组成桑蒂达科他的上议事会，桑蒂意为「住在燧石之地的人」。与定居的梅德瓦坎顿人不同，他们不建固定村庄，在米拉湖与明尼苏达河之间的栎树林和湖群间游徙，采野米、在密林中猎鹿，又推进到草原边缘猎牛。1444年，这些猎场还只属于他们。

1700年，第一个法国商站到来：皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔在蓝土河口附近为约三十人修建利利耶堡。他把一种松软的蓝黏土当成了铜矿，结果黏土一文不值；到1702年，商站已遭袭击并废弃，留守的人再无音讯。整个18世纪，手持法国火枪的奥吉布瓦战队把瓦佩库特人赶离林地，不断向南压缩。1805年，泽布伦·派克与达科他人订立第一个美国条约；到1821年，瓦佩库特人的营地仍沿着明尼苏达河流域的毛皮小道迁移。

en:
In 1444 the lower Des Moines River and the Des Moines Rapids of the Mississippi were Illinois country. At the rapids the river broadened over shallow limestone and fell more than twenty feet in eleven miles, so canoe parties unloaded and followed a beaten portage road along the bank; the cartographers Schoolcraft and Nicollet derived the name Moingona from a Miami-Illinois word meaning 'at the road'. The band that carried it was closely tied to the Peoria. Its families planted corn, beans and squash in summer villages of longhouses and mat-covered wigwams, and hunted bison on the prairie beyond the woods.

Marquette and Jolliet walked that portage path in 1673 to reach three nearby Illinois villages, and a later Marquette map labels one of them Moingwena. The Beaver Wars had already reached the valley: an Iroquois army burned the Kaskaskia town in 1680 and carried off hundreds of captives. By 1700 the Moingwena had merged into the Peoria, whom Father Gravier then named together with them. French maps and travellers kept their name on the river, and Charlevoix, passing in 1721, saw the prairie beyond it filled with bison. After 1763 Peoria families crossed to the Spanish side of the Mississippi. The Americans built Fort Madison above the rapids in 1808; British-allied warriors burned it in 1813, and in 1818 the Peoria ceded their Illinois lands by the Treaty of Edwardsville.
zh:
1444年，得梅因河下游与密西西比河上的得梅因急流一带是伊利尼人的地方。急流处，河面在浅浅的石灰岩床上展宽，11英里内落差超过20英尺，独木舟队伍只能卸货上岸，沿一条踩踏出来的转运小路绕行；制图学者斯库克拉夫特和尼科莱认为，莫因圭纳一名来自迈阿密-伊利诺伊语，意思是「在路旁」。这支群体与佩奥利亚人关系密切。各家在夏季村落里种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，住长屋和草席覆顶的维格沃姆棚屋，又到林地外的草原猎野牛。

1673年，马凯特与乔利埃特正是沿这条转运小路走到附近三座伊利尼村落，后来归在马凯特名下的地图把其中一座标为莫因圭纳。海狸战争此时已打进河谷：1680年，一支易洛魁军队焚毁卡斯卡基亚人的城镇，掳走数百人。到1700年，莫因圭纳人已并入佩奥利亚人，格拉维耶神父把二者并称。法国人的地图和行记留下了这个名字，1721年路过的沙勒瓦看到河外草原上遍布野牛。1763年后，佩奥利亚家族渡密西西比河迁往西班牙控制的一侧。美国人1808年在急流上方修建麦迪逊堡；亲英的战士1813年放火烧掉它，1818年，佩奥利亚人又依《爱德华兹维尔条约》割让了他们在伊利诺伊的土地。

en:
The Michigamea, also spelled Mishigamaw, took their name from Algonquian words for 'great water' and were the southernmost band of the Illiniwek confederacy. In the fifteenth century their village lay among the lakes and bayous where the St Francis River joins the Mississippi, in what is now north-eastern Arkansas, a country of flooded bottomland forest and southern cane. French visitors later found the band hard to understand, since the Michigamea may have spoken a Siouan tongue rather than Illinois. They farmed the rich bottoms and took fish and waterfowl from the marshes. In 1444 they held the confederacy's southern edge, nearest to the Quapaw towns on the Arkansas.

Marquette and Jolliet reached the Michigamea village in 1673 while descending the Mississippi, and turned back only among the Quapaw beyond. By about 1700 the band had left Arkansas, possibly driven north by the Iroquois wars, and resettled beside the French towns near the mouth of the Kaskaskia River. Their chief Chicagou was sent to France in 1725 with five other Illinois chiefs. On 25 November they pledged allegiance to the young Louis XV and danced in Paris. Jean-Philippe Rameau wrote his harpsichord air Les Sauvages for the occasion and later used it in an opera-ballet. Chicagou afterwards campaigned beside the French in the Chickasaw Wars. A long feud followed, as the Sauk, Meskwaki and their allies pressed the shrinking Illinois, and in 1752 the Sauk overran the Michigamea village. Most survivors were taken in by the Quapaw and the Kaskaskia. By 1803 the Michigamea were no longer counted as a separate people.
zh:
米希加毛人（一译米奇加梅人，Michigamea）的族名在伊利尼人的阿尔冈昆语里意为「大水」，是伊利尼韦克联盟最靠南的一支。15世纪时，他们的村落坐落在圣弗朗西斯河注入密西西比河一带的湖泊与水网之间，即今阿肯色州东北部，是一片常遭水淹的河漫滩林和南方藤丛。后来的法国人发现很难与他们交谈，米希加毛人说的可能是一种与伊利尼语并不相通的苏语。他们在肥沃的低地耕作，从沼泽里捕鱼和水禽。1444年，他们守在联盟的南缘，与阿肯色河畔的夸帕人城镇相距最近。

1673年，马凯特与乔利埃特顺密西西比河南下时抵达米希加毛人的村落，直到更南方的夸帕人处才折返。到1700年前后，这支人已离开阿肯色，可能是被易洛魁战争逼向北方，在卡斯卡基亚河口附近的法国城镇边重新落脚。首领希卡古1725年与另外五名伊利尼首领被送往法国，11月25日向年轻的路易十五宣誓效忠，并在巴黎起舞；让-菲利普·拉莫为这次来访写下羽管键琴曲《野蛮人》，后来又把它用进一部歌剧芭蕾。希卡古此后随法国人参加奇克索战争。再往后是长年的仇杀，索克人、梅斯夸基人及其盟邦不断进逼日益衰微的伊利尼人；1752年，索克人攻陷米希加毛人的村落，幸存者大多由夸帕人和卡斯卡基亚人收留。到1803年，米希加毛人已不再被算作一个单独的部族。

en:
South of the Ozarks, the Arkansas River meets the Verdigris and the Neosho in a wooded country that opens on to prairie, a country the French later called the Three Forks. In 1444 the bottomlands held Caddoan-speaking villages, whose farmers raised corn, beans and squash, fired pottery and hunted buffalo where the woods gave way to grass; their trade paths ran from the Red River towards the Missouri, and no horse had yet entered the land. The country later took its name from the Santsukhdhin, the Arkansas band of the Osage.

The Osage call themselves the Wazhazhe, the People of the Middle Waters, in their own Siouan tongue. They had the horse by 1690 and traded with the French coming up from the Mississippi, and in the long wars that followed their raiders entered the Three Forks; by 1750 they had defeated the Caddoan villages there and made the bottoms their southern hunting ground, in a domain that ran from the Missouri to the Red. Around 1800 a quarrel between the bands sent the chief Big Track and roughly half the nation south from the Osage River to settle on the Verdigris. Lewis and Clark found this Arkansas band there in 1804, and the Chouteaus of St Louis traded in their towns; smallpox swept the Osage settlements in 1801 and 1802 and killed perhaps 2,000 of them.

Lovely's Purchase in 1816 had already opened the Verdigris valley to land-seekers when, in June 1817, Western Cherokee and their allies under Spring Frog surprised Pasuga, Chief Clermont's town below Claremore Mound, while its warriors were away on the summer hunt. The fight is also called the Battle of the Strawberry Moon; the attackers killed 38 of the people who remained and carried off 104. The Treaty of St Louis in 1818 surrendered more of the old Osage grounds.
zh:
欧扎克山以南，阿肯色河在一片林木渐次让位于草原的土地上汇入弗迪格里斯河与尼欧肖河，法国人后来把这一带称作「三汊口」。1444年，河滩上散布着卡多语村落：农人种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，烧制陶器，到林草相接之处猎杀野牛，商路从红河通向密苏里河，马还没有踏入这片土地。这片地方后来得名于奥塞奇人的阿肯色支——萨图斯赫丁人。

奥塞奇人在自己的苏语里自称瓦扎热，意为「中水之民」。他们到1690年已有马匹，同密西西比河方向来的法国人交易；此后的长期战乱中，奥塞奇袭击者攻入三汊口，到1750年已击败当地的卡多语村落，把河滩变成南部猎场，势力北起密苏里河、南抵红河。1800年前后，诸支内讧，首领大迹率约半数部众离开奥塞奇河南下，在弗迪格里斯河畔住下，是为阿肯色支。1804年刘易斯与克拉克在这条河上找到他们，圣路易斯的舒托家族也到他们的镇子交易；1801至1802年天花横扫奥塞奇村镇，死者约两千人。

1816年，名为「拉夫利购地」的割让已把弗迪格里斯谷地向拓地者打开。1817年6月，西部切罗基人及其盟友在春蛙率领下，趁克莱蒙酋长的帕苏加村武士外出夏猎，突袭了克莱尔芒丘下的这座镇子；此战又称「草莓月之战」，袭击者杀死留守者38人、掳走104人。1818年的《圣路易斯条约》又把更多奥塞奇故地交出。

en:
The Adai were a Caddoan people of the pine country between the Red and Sabine rivers, where Louisiana and Texas now meet, and members of the Caddo confederacy. They farmed corn, beans and squash beside thatched lodges, in villages strung along the Red from Louisiana west beyond the Sabine, and carried their engraved pottery between them. In 1444 their world was the Caddo world of maize fields, river crossings and clan villages, and no European had yet entered their forests.

A survivor of the Narváez expedition, Cabeza de Vaca, noted them as the 'Atayos' in 1530, and Iberville met them on the Red at the end of the century. The Europeans then came to stay. When the French founded Natchitoches in 1714, Spain answered with the mission of San Miguel de los Adaes two years later, in a strip of forest both crowns claimed. In June 1719 seven Frenchmen walked into the mission, told its lone Spanish defender that a hundred soldiers were behind them, and took it without a fight. The Marqués de Aguayo came back with five hundred men and in 1721 raised the presidio of Los Adaes, six cannon and a hundred soldiers strong, twelve miles from Natchitoches; it became the first capital of Spanish Texas. Spanish law made imported goods so scarce and dear that the garrison and the twenty-five ranching families nearby bought most of what they needed from the French, and after forty-six years the Franciscans had done, in their own report, little more than baptize a few of the dying. The missionaries were recalled in 1768, and once France ceded Louisiana the post had no purpose: in 1773 the Spanish closed it and gave the settlers five days to march for San Antonio, a three-month trek that killed many. Fourteen Adai families went with them while the rest merged with the Caddo, and in 1820 Morse counted only thirty survivors.
zh:
阿代人是卡多语族群，也是卡多联盟的一支，住在雷德河与萨宾河之间的松林地带，即后来路易斯安那与得克萨斯相接之处。他们在草顶木屋旁种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，村落沿雷德河排开，从路易斯安那向西一直越过萨宾河，刻纹陶器在各村之间往来贩运。1444年时，他们的世界就是卡多人的世界：玉米田、渡口和氏族村落，还没有一个欧洲人走进他们的森林。

纳瓦埃斯远征队的幸存者卡韦萨·德巴卡早在1530年就记下了「阿塔约人」这个名字，到该世纪末伊贝维尔又在雷德河畔见到他们。欧洲人随后在这里扎下根来。1714年法国人建起纳基托什，两年后西班牙针锋相对地设立圣米格尔·德洛斯阿代传教站，所在的林带两国都声称归己。1719年6月，七名法国人走进传教站，告诉唯一的西班牙守军身后还有一百名士兵，兵不血刃地拿下了它。阿瓜约侯爵率五百人卷土重来，1721年筑起洛斯阿代斯要塞，配六门炮、一百名守军，距纳基托什仅十二英里，这里就此成为西属得克萨斯的第一个首府。按西班牙的法律，舶来货物又少又贵，守军和附近二十五户牧场人家大多从法国人手里采买；四十六年后，方济各会士在报告里自称他们的成绩「至多是为几个垂死之人施了洗」。1768年传教士被召回；法国割让路易斯安那后，这座据点再无用处，1773年西班牙人将其关闭，限定居者五天内启程迁往圣安东尼奥，三个月的跋涉死者甚众。十四户阿代人随军同行，其余并入卡多人；1820年莫尔斯清点时，幸存者只剩三十人。

en:
Bdewekhantunwan was the lake country of the Bdewákhathuŋwaŋ, the Mdewakanton Dakota, whose name means the people of Mde Wákhaŋ, the Spirit Lake that the French later called Mille Lacs. The shallow water gave fish through the ice and in open season, while wild-rice beds, oak woods and hunting grounds ringed the shore, and the Rum River carried canoes south to the Mississippi. In 1444 Dakota camps and old mound sites dotted that shore; the Mdewakanton lived by woodland hunting, rice gathering, fishing and the fur of beaver, otter and deer.

French maps named the lake Lac Buade or Lac des Issatis. Daniel Greysolon du Lhut visited the Izatys country in 1679, and an account of 1687 described the large Dakota village on the southwestern shore; the name Kathio, later given to that shore, began as a misreading of 'Izatys' in du Lhut's handwriting. The lake became a meeting place for Canadian coureurs des bois and Native trappers. Through the eighteenth century Ojibwe groups moving west with French and British firearms pressed the Dakota back from the Lake Superior country; Ojibwe oral tradition remembered a battle at Kathio that opened Mille Lacs to them, and many Mdewakanton shifted toward the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers. In 1805 Zebulon Pike obtained a treaty from two Mdewakanton villages for military-post land on the upper Mississippi: of the seven Dakota men at the council only two signed, and Pike left the payment blank, so the United States Senate later fixed the price at $2,000. In the War of 1812 Mdewakanton warriors led by Wapasha II fought for the British, and by 1821 the old Spirit Lake shore had ceased to be the band's only centre.
zh:
布德韦坎通万是姆德瓦坎顿达科他人的湖地，族名来自他们奉为圣湖的灵湖，法国人后来把这座湖叫作米尔莱克斯湖。水浅的湖面在冰封季节和通航时都能捕鱼，湖岸环绕着野米床、橡树林和猎场，拉姆姆河则把独木舟向南送入密西西比河。1444年，达科他营地和古老坟丘散布湖岸；姆德瓦坎顿人在林地狩猎、采集野米、捕鱼，取河狸、水獭和鹿的毛皮。

法国地图把这座大湖标作比阿德湖或伊萨蒂湖。达尼埃尔·格雷索隆·迪吕1679年进入伊萨蒂人的地区，1687年的记述描绘了西南岸那座达科他大村；后来这处湖岸被叫作卡西奥，名字正是把迪吕手书的「伊萨蒂」误读而来。湖畔成为法裔加拿大林居者和原住民捕兽人交换毛皮的会合地。整个18世纪，携法国和英国火器西移的奥吉布瓦人把达科他人从苏必利尔湖方向压退；奥吉布瓦口述传统记得在卡西奥打过一仗，这一仗为他们打开了米尔莱克斯，许多姆德瓦坎顿人于是向密西西比河与明尼苏达河转移。1805年，泽布伦·派克从两个姆德瓦坎顿村落取得一份割让密西西比河上游军站土地的条约：在场的七名达科他人只有两人签字，补偿金一栏也被他留空，美国参议院后来把地价定为二千美元。1812年战争中，瓦帕沙二世率姆德瓦坎顿战士为英国作战；到1821年，灵湖湖岸已不再是这支人唯一的中心。

en:
La Pointe faces Chequamegon Bay from the western shore of Mooningwanekaaning, later called Madeline Island, the largest of the Apostle Islands. Its Anishinaabe name means the place of the golden-breasted flicker. Anishinaabe migration stories tell of people led west until they found food growing on the water, and the wild-rice marshes of Chequamegon gave that story a local home. In 1444 the island was a fishery, camp and canoe crossing; the lake supplied whitefish and trout, while mainland woods supplied beaver and otter. Dakota and other lake peoples also used the shore, and Noquet country lay east toward Bay de Noc.

French traders were the first Europeans to settle into the bay. Pierre-Esprit Radisson and Médard Chouart des Groseilliers built a rough hut around 1659-1660, and Jesuits including Claude Allouez and Jacques Marquette later established a mission there. Pierre-Charles Le Sueur put a French fort on the island in 1693. Louis Denis de la Ronde reopened the post as La Pointe in 1718, trading furs and exploring nearby copper deposits; the garrison remained until 1759. The Fox Wars farther south repeatedly changed the alliances that guarded canoe routes between Superior and the Mississippi country.

After the British conquest, Alexander Henry and Jean-Baptiste Cadotte made the island trade a permanent business. Cadotte's son Michel, known in Ojibwe as Kechemeshane, married Ikwesewe, daughter of the head of the White Crane clan, whose men supplied the hereditary chiefs of the Lake Superior Ojibwe. The marriage tied the Cadotte trading house to the band's leading family, and the island became known in French by Ikwesewe's Catholic name, Madeleine. John Jacob Astor's American Fur Company took over the post in 1808.
zh:
拉潘特位于莫宁瓦内卡宁西岸，隔谢夸梅贡湾相望；该岛后称马德琳岛，是阿波斯特尔群岛中最大的一座。阿尼什纳比语地名意为「金胸啄木鸟之地」。阿尼什纳比人的迁徙故事说，族人被引向西方，寻找「长在水上的食物」，谢夸梅贡湾的野米沼泽正对应这个故事。1444年，岛上有渔场、营地和独木舟渡口；湖中产白鱼和鳟鱼，大陆林地出产河狸与水獭。达科他和其他湖区民族也会使用这片湖岸，诺奎特人的地方则在东面的贝德纳克湾方向。

法国商人是最早在湾畔定居的欧洲人。约1659—1660年，皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松与梅达尔·舒阿尔·德·格罗塞耶搭起简陋棚屋；后来克洛德·阿卢埃、雅克·马凯特等耶稣会士又在此设立传教站。1693年，皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔在岛上修建法国堡垒。1718年，路易·德尼·德·拉龙德重开据点，命名为拉潘特，经营毛皮并探察附近铜矿；驻军一直维持到1759年。南方的福克斯战争多次改变原住民联盟，也影响着苏必利尔湖通往密西西比地区的独木舟路线。

英国征服后，亚历山大·亨利与让-巴蒂斯特·卡多特把岛上贸易做成长期事业。卡多特之子米歇尔的奥吉布瓦名为凯切梅尚，他娶了白鹤氏族首领之女伊克韦塞韦；该氏族的男子担任苏必利尔奥吉布瓦人的世袭首领。这场婚姻使卡多特商馆与奥吉布瓦首领家族结盟，岛屿也以伊克韦塞韦的教名马德琳闻名。1808年，约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的美国毛皮公司接掌这座商站。

en:
The Kilatika were a band of the Miami (Myaamiaki), Algonquian-speaking villagers of the tallgrass prairies southwest of Lake Michigan. Their main town stood where the Kankakee and Des Plaines meet to form the Illinois River, on the canoe route between Lake Michigan and the Mississippi by way of the Chicago portage, and their country reached east toward the Wabash. Women grew maize, beans and squash in river-bottom fields while men hunted the prairie bison, a way of life going back to the Mississippian Fisher tradition. In 1444 no European had reached these prairies, and the Kilatika shared them with the Illiniwek and the other Miami bands.

French traders wrote down the name of the western Miami bands in the 1650s, the first Europeans to meet them. The Beaver Wars then broke over the prairies: Iroquois raiders carrying trade guns scattered the Miami westward, yet the Kilatika kept their town at the meeting of the two rivers through the French years. French firearms and fur trade let the Miami move back east around 1700, and the Kilatika settled on Indiana's Eel River, where the English later knew them as the Eel River band. Miami warriors seized the British garrison at Fort Miami in 1763, in Pontiac's rising. In the Northwest Indian War, Kentucky militia burned the Kilatika villages on the Eel in 1791, and their war with the United States ended with the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.
zh:
基拉提卡人是迈阿密人（Myaamiaki）的一支，说阿尔冈昆语系的迈阿密－伊利尼语，住在密歇根湖西南的高草草原上。他们的主镇设在坎卡基河与德斯普兰斯河汇成伊利诺伊河之处，正处在密歇根湖经芝加哥连水陆路通往密西西比河的独木舟航线上，乡土向东一直延伸到沃巴什河。妇女在河漫滩种玉米、豆子和南瓜，男子到草原上围猎野牛，这种生计承自密西西比文化的费希尔传统。1444年时还没有欧洲人到过这片草原，基拉提卡人与伊利尼维克人及迈阿密其他各支共享此地。

法国商人在1650年代记下偏西的迈阿密各支的名字，这是欧洲人与他们的首次接触。随后海狸战争席卷草原，拿着贸易火枪的易洛魁袭掠者把迈阿密人赶向西方；但在法国势力到来的岁月里，基拉提卡人的镇子始终守在两河交汇处。靠着法国火器和毛皮贸易，迈阿密人在1700年前后东返故土，基拉提卡人定居在印第安纳的鳗河畔，英国人后来称他们为鳗河支。1763年庞蒂亚克起事时，迈阿密武士拿下迈阿密堡的英国守军。西北印第安战争中，肯塔基民兵1791年焚毁基拉提卡人在鳗河畔的村落，他们与美国的战事到1795年签订《格林维尔条约》才结束。

en:
The Mengkonkia were Miami-Illinois-speaking villagers of the tallgrass prairies between the Illinois River and the Mississippi. Women tended fields of maize, beans and squash down in the river bottoms, while the men hunted the vast bison herds out on the grass; the missionary Charlevoix crossed this country in 1721 and called it le Moingona, 'an immense and magnificent prairie, all covered with Beef and other Hoofed Animals'. The bands moved, traded and feuded among the other Miami and Illinois villages, and in 1444 no European had entered the grasslands or written down their name.

That name first appears in French mission records. Jacques Marquette heard in 1672 of the Mengakonkia as one of the Illinois tribes who shared one language, and in 1673 he and Louis Jolliet visited three Illinois villages out on the prairie; a later map marked one as Moingwena. The band merged into the Peoria around 1700, and the Des Moines River, and later the town of Des Moines, kept a version of its name. Miami lists farther east remembered the Mengkonkia as the people of the war chief Little Turtle (Mihšihkinaahkwa). In 1790 and 1791 he led the Western Confederacy to break two American armies invading the Maumee valley, and St. Clair alone lost some 900 men, the heaviest defeat the United States ever suffered at Native hands. Little Turtle made peace at Greenville in 1795 and died in 1812.
zh:
蒙康基人说迈阿密－伊利尼语，村落散布在伊利诺伊河与密西西比河之间的高草草原上。妇女在河漫滩照料玉米、豆子和南瓜田，男子到旷野猎捕庞大的野牛群。传教士沙勒瓦1721年经过这片地方，把它称作莫因戈纳（le Moingona），说是一片「辽阔壮观、遍布野牛和其他有蹄兽类的大草原」。各支族人与迈阿密、伊利诺伊人的其他村落迁徙、贸易、仇杀；1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这片草原，也没人记下他们的名字。

这个名字最早见于法国传教记录。雅克·马凯特1672年听说孟加孔基亚（Mengakonkia）是说同一种语言的伊利诺伊诸部之一；1673年，他与路易斯·若利埃走访草原上的三个伊利诺伊村落，后来的地图把其中一村标作莫因圭纳。这支人约在1700年并入皮奥里亚人，德梅因河以及后来的德梅因城的名字都来自这个族名的变体。东边的迈阿密谱系则把蒙康基记作战酋小海龟（Mihšihkinaahkwa）的族人：1790和1791年，他率西部联盟接连击破两支入侵莫米河谷的美军，仅圣克莱尔一部就损兵约九百人，是美国对原住民作战败得最惨重的一次。小海龟1795年在格林维尔议和，1812年去世。

en:
Saginawe is a form of Zaagiinaang, an Ojibwe name for water flowing out into Saginaw Bay. The Tittabawassee and Shiawassee rivers meet inland and form the short Saginaw River, which carries an extensive watershed into Lake Huron; the bay shore, marshes and canoe routes make up the country around it. Those marshes supplied fish, waterfowl and wild rice, while inland woods gave maple sugar, deer and beaver. Ojibwe bands later remembered as the Saginaw, Black River and Swan Creek people had used the country since at least the fourteenth century, and Odawa and Potawatomi parties crossed it. In 1444 the river mouth was a fishing place and fur rendezvous without a European post.

Jacques Marquette was the first European known to visit the bay, in 1668. Jean Enjalran tried a mission in the valley in 1686, but it failed, and French and later British traders continued to meet Ojibwe trappers at the mouth without founding a permanent town. The country became part of Michigan Territory in 1805. After the War of 1812 Louis Campau opened a trading post on the Saginaw, and on 24 September 1819 Lewis Cass met Ojibwe leaders Mash Kee Yosh, Okemos and Wasso, together with Odawa and Potawatomi representatives, for the Treaty of Saginaw. They ceded more than six million acres of the central Lower Peninsula, while reserving smaller tracts for Native use within the ceded country.
zh:
萨吉纳韦是奥吉布瓦语地名扎吉纳昂的转写，指河水注入萨吉诺湾之处。蒂塔巴瓦西河与夏厄沃西河在内陆汇合，形成短短的萨吉诺河，把广阔流域的水量送入休伦湖；湾岸、沼泽和独木舟水路构成了这一带。沼泽出产鱼、水禽和野米，内陆林地提供枫糖、鹿和河狸。后来被称为萨吉诺、黑河与斯旺克里克人的奥吉布瓦诸部至少自14世纪起便使用这片地方，奥达瓦和波塔瓦托米队伍也会经过。1444年，河口是渔场和毛皮会合点，还没有欧洲人据点。

1668年，雅克·马凯特成为已知最早到访海湾的欧洲人。1686年，让·昂雅尔朗试图在谷地建立传教站，但没有成功；法国商人及后来的英国商人继续在河口与奥吉布瓦捕兽人交易，却未建立永久城镇。1805年，这里成为密歇根领地的一部分。1812年战争后，路易·康波在萨吉诺河畔开设贸易站。1819年9月24日，刘易斯·卡斯与马什基约什、奥基莫斯、沃索等奥吉布瓦首领，以及奥达瓦和波塔瓦托米代表签订《萨吉诺条约》。他们割让密歇根下半岛中部六百多万英亩土地，同时在割让地区内保留若干较小的原住民用地。

en:
Mascouten is the old prairie country of the southern Lower Michigan interior, a patchwork of oak openings, grassy clearings, beech-maple woods and marshes between the Saginaw lands and the Potawatomi and Miami country farther south. French missionaries, the first Europeans to meet its Algonquian speakers, called them the Fire Nation, though a Fox word gives their name as Little Prairie People; the same missionaries wrote that the Mascouten outnumbered the Neutral, Huron and Iroquois put together. Families moved with the seasons between river crossings, deer drives, maple groves and beaver ponds. In 1444 no mission or European fort stood here, only Mascouten villages, trails and the older Native commerce of the lakes.

The Beaver Wars emptied the country. Neutral and Five Nations raiders struck the Lower Peninsula in the mid-seventeenth century, and by the 1660s Mascouten families were moving west of Lake Michigan among Sauk, Fox, Kickapoo, Miami and Potawatomi refugees, leaving much of the ground between Lakes Huron and Michigan thinly held. French traders and missionaries followed the displaced bands into the upper lakes, and in 1701 Cadillac founded Detroit at the eastern end of the old southern trails. In 1712 the Mascouten joined the Fox and Kickapoo against the French at Detroit; French troops and their Potawatomi allies nearly destroyed them, and the survivors merged with the Fox and Kickapoo. A record of 1779 still names a Mascouten band on the Wabash, living with the Kickapoo and Piankeshaw; after that the records show them only as part of the Kickapoo.
zh:
马斯古顿本是密歇根下半岛南部内陆的草原之地，橡树疏林、草甸、山毛榉与枫树林和沼泽交错，北接萨吉纳韦人的土地，南连波塔瓦托米人与迈阿密人。最先接触这支阿尔冈昆语族群的法国传教士称他们为「火族」，但按梅斯夸基语（福克斯语）的一个词，其族名意为「小草原人」；这些传教士还写道，马斯古顿人比中立联盟、休伦人和易洛魁人加起来还多。各家随季节在河流渡口、围鹿场、枫树林和河狸塘之间迁移。1444年，这里没有传教站，也没有欧洲人的堡垒，只有马斯古顿人的村庄、步道和湖区原住民旧日的贸易往来。

河狸战争使这片土地为之一空。17世纪中叶，中立联盟与五族易洛魁的战士袭入下半岛；到1660年代，马斯古顿人随索克、梅斯夸基、基卡普、迈阿密和波塔瓦托米的难民陆续西渡密歇根湖，休伦湖与密歇根湖之间大片土地人烟稀疏。法国商人与传教士跟着这些流离的部族深入上游湖区，1701年卡迪亚克在南部古道的东端建立底特律。1712年，马斯古顿人与梅斯夸基人、基卡普人联手在底特律进攻法国人；法军及其波塔瓦托米盟友几乎将他们消灭，幸存者并入梅斯夸基与基卡普两部。1779年的一份记载还提到沃巴什河畔有一支马斯古顿群体，与基卡普人同住；此后的记录中，他们只作为基卡普人的一部分出现。

en:
Piankeshaw is the lower Wabash country of the Peeyankihsiaki, the Miami people whose name means those who split off. In 1444 their homeland centered on wooded bottoms above the Embarras River, the place later called Chippekawkay, 'place of edible roots', where Vincennes now stands. The Wabash and the old Buffalo Trace carried canoe parties and hunters between the Ohio valley, the prairies and the Wea country upstream, while cornfields and summer camps occupied the fertile flats. Closely related to the Wea, the Piankeshaw lived beyond European maps or trade routes.

Europeans came up the Wabash for its game. In 1702 Charles Juchereau opened a post to buy bison hides, and more than 13,000 reached his traders in two years before his death left the station abandoned. In 1732 Francois-Marie Bissot, Sieur de Vincennes, built a second post among the Piankeshaw and persuaded them to settle beside it, founding the town that later took his name; four years later the Chickasaw captured him and burned him alive. The British took over in 1763 and renamed the post Fort Sackville. During the War of Independence the Piankeshaw took the American side, and in December 1778 Henry Hamilton reoccupied the fort for the Crown with a force from Detroit. George Rogers Clark answered with a midwinter march from Kaskaskia, his men wading across the flooded Wabash bottoms in February 1779; they surprised Fort Sackville and forced Hamilton to surrender without losing a soldier. The post-war frontier was bloodier for the Piankeshaw: in 1786 Kentucky militia destroyed one of their towns and Wabash war parties came against Vincennes in forty-seven canoes, after which many families fled to the Wea at Terre Haute or to Kaskaskia. In 1818 Chief Chekommia signed away the last of the Piankeshaw land rights to the United States.
zh:
皮安克肖是佩扬基赫夏基人在下沃巴什河的土地；这个迈阿密群体的名称意为「分离出去的人」。1444年，他们的家园以埃姆巴拉斯河以上林木繁茂的河漫滩为中心，即后来称作奇佩科凯、意为「可食根茎之地」的地方，温森斯就坐落在这一带。沃巴什河与古老的野牛小道把独木舟队伍和猎人引向俄亥俄河谷、草原以及上游的韦阿人土地，肥沃低地上则分布着玉米田和夏季营地。皮安克肖人与韦阿人关系密切，那时仍处在欧洲人的地图和商路之外。

欧洲人沿沃巴什河而来，为的是沿岸的猎物。1702年，夏尔·朱什罗设站收购野牛皮，两年内收进一万三千多张，他一死据点便遭废弃。1732年，弗朗索瓦—马里·比索·德·万塞讷在皮安克肖人中再修一堡，劝他们在堡旁定居，后来的城镇便以他为名；四年后他被奇克索人俘获，活活烧死。1763年英国人接管，将据点改名萨克维尔堡。独立战争中皮安克肖人站在美国一边，1778年12月，亨利·汉密尔顿却率底特律的部队替英王重占该堡。乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克随即从卡斯卡斯基亚发动严冬行军，士兵们在1779年2月涉过沃巴什河泛滥的冰水，出其不意地逼近萨克维尔堡，迫使汉密尔顿投降，美军无一阵亡。战后的边疆对皮安克肖人更为凶险：1786年肯塔基民团毁了他们一座城镇，沃巴什各部又乘四十七艘战舟来攻温森斯，许多家庭只得逃往特雷霍特投奔韦阿人，或迁往卡斯卡斯基亚。1818年，酋长切科米亚签约，把最后的皮安克肖土地权利让给美国。

en:
Waapi-nipi is the Miami-Illinois name for the upper Wabash, the shining white water that runs over a bed of pale limestone. The Mississinewa and other creeks feed it, and canoes launching at the Maumee portage could travel down this river all the way to the Ohio. In 1444 Miami-speaking villagers held the fertile bottoms, planting maize, beans and squash and hunting through the prairies and oak woods. The river was their road and larder, and no European post yet stood anywhere on the Wabash.

Iroquois raiding emptied much of the valley during the Beaver Wars, and Miami-speaking bands, among them the Wea, came back only as French trade reopened the route from Canada to the Mississippi. The French built Fort Ouiatenon on the Wea stretch of the river in 1717, and it became one of the busiest fur posts in the region. The wars of the new American republic followed upriver. On 17 December 1812 John B. Campbell led about six hundred mounted men against Miami and Delaware towns on the Mississinewa and burned several villages before some three hundred warriors struck his camp at dawn. Eight Americans were killed and four more died of wounds; Campbell claimed at least 38 Native dead and then withdrew. The Treaty of St Marys with the Miami in 1818 opened the 'New Purchase', roughly a third of Indiana, and the open Wabash country was cut into reservations and American survey ranges.
zh:
瓦皮尼皮是迈阿密—伊利诺伊语对沃巴什河上游的称呼，说的是淡色石灰岩河床上白色闪光的河水。米西沙尼瓦河等支流汇入这条河，独木舟从莫米陆运道下水，可顺流一直划到俄亥俄河。1444年，说迈阿密语的村民占据着肥沃低地，种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在草原和橡树林中狩猎。这条河是他们的通路和粮仓，沃巴什河上还没有任何欧洲人的据点。

海狸战争期间，易洛魁人的袭击使河谷大半空弃，直到法国贸易重新打通加拿大到密西西比河的路线，迈阿密语诸部（包括韦阿人）才陆续返回。1717年，法国人在韦阿人那段河畔修建瓦亚塔农堡，它后来成为这一带最繁忙的毛皮据点之一。新生美国的战争随后向河上游推进。1812年12月17日，约翰·B·坎贝尔率约六百名骑兵进攻米西沙尼瓦河畔的迈阿密与特拉华村镇，烧毁数座村庄，约三百名战士随即在黎明袭击他的营地。美军八人阵亡、四人伤重不治；坎贝尔自称杀死至少38名原住民，之后撤退。1818年与迈阿密人签订的《圣玛丽斯条约》开放了「新购地」，约占印第安纳三分之一，开阔的沃巴什土地随即被划为保留地和美国人的测量区。

en:
Chalahgawtha was one of the five Shawnee divisions and the one traditionally charged with the nation's political leadership. Its principal chief lived in a town called Chillicothe, so whenever that town moved in war or migration, the name moved with it. In 1444 the Scioto and Paint Creek valleys lay in the southern Ohio homeland of the Shawnee, an Algonquian country of bark-covered villages, river-bottom maize fields, deer drives and beaver trails running south toward the Ohio. No European post yet stood in the valley; power rested in village councils and in the exchange of furs and native trade goods among neighbouring peoples.

Iroquois raids during the Beaver Wars scattered the Shawnee as far as Pennsylvania, the Illinois country and the Savannah River, and large towns formed again only after bands returned to the Ohio Country in the 1730s. In 1758 the people of Lower Shawnee Town withdrew up the Scioto together with Shawnee from Logstown and built the next Chillicothe near Paint Creek. In 1762 the town could field about 300 warriors, and Tecumseh was born there in 1768. Dunmore's Virginia army marched to the Scioto in 1774. Under the war chief Blackfish, Chillicothe raiders struck Kentucky, and in 1778 they brought Daniel Boone back to the town; tradition says Blackfish adopted him under a Shawnee name meaning Big Turtle, and Boone escaped after several months. Blackfish died of a wound in 1779, and George Rogers Clark burned the relocated Old Chillicothe the following year. After the Treaty of Greenville opened the Scioto country in 1795, Nathaniel Massie laid out a settler town of Chillicothe in 1796, and it became the first capital of Ohio in 1803.
zh:
查拉高萨是肖尼人的五大分支之一，按传统为全族提供政治领袖。分支大酋长所在的主村称奇利科西；每逢战乱或迁徙，村名也随人迁走。1444年，赛欧托河谷与佩恩特溪一带位于肖尼人记忆中的南俄亥俄故土，树皮屋村落、河畔玉米地、鹿群猎道和通向俄亥俄河的河狸小径构成了这片阿尔冈昆土地。当时河谷中还没有欧洲人的商站或堡垒，权力属于村落议事会，毛皮与土产交易也仍在相邻族群之间流转。

河狸战争中，易洛魁人的攻掠把肖尼人驱散到宾夕法尼亚、伊利诺伊乃至萨凡纳河一带；直到18世纪30年代各支派返回俄亥俄地区，大村镇才重新形成。1758年，下肖尼镇的居民与洛格斯敦来的肖尼人一起沿赛欧托河北上，在佩恩特溪旁建起新的奇利科西。1762年，这座村能出动约三百名战士，特库姆塞1768年出生在这里。1774年，邓莫尔麾下的弗吉尼亚军队进抵赛欧托河。在战酋黑鱼率领下，奇利科西战士袭掠肯塔基，1778年把丹尼尔·布恩本人带回了村子；相传黑鱼收他为养子，给他取了一个意为「大龟」的肖尼名字，几个月后布恩逃走。黑鱼1779年伤重而死，第二年乔治·罗杰斯·克拉克焚毁迁走后的旧奇利科西。1795年《格林维尔条约》开放赛欧托地区后，纳撒尼尔·梅西1796年规划了定居者的奇利科西，1803年它成为俄亥俄州第一个首府。

en:
Shatteras keeps the name of a mountain Siouan people whom early seventeenth-century maps placed in the Ouasioto, the Cumberland ridges. The forests between the Ohio Valley and the Kentucky headwaters had no fixed border: Tutelo and Moneton canoe trails crossed the portages, Shawnee bands hunted the ridges, and Iroquoian-speaking middlemen carried the furs east. In 1444 the country was a shared hunting ground on the edge of the Shawnee world. The Kispoko, smallest of the five Shawnee divisions, were the sept from which the hereditary war chiefs came.

In 1671 the first English party to cross these western waters, Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam, sent by Abraham Wood, met Mohetan and Moneton communities near the New and Kanawha rivers. The Beaver Wars then emptied the ridges: the Haudenosaunee broke the Tutelo around 1670 and claimed the Ohio's southern hunting grounds, while the Kispoko were driven as far as the Creek country and did not return to Ohio until about 1759. On 10 October 1774 the Shawnee chief Cornstalk, with 300 to 500 warriors, attacked Andrew Lewis's thousand Virginia militiamen at the Kanawha's mouth in the Battle of Point Pleasant. The fighting went hand to hand and the Shawnee withdrew at nightfall; their dead included the Kispoko war chief Pucksinwah, father of Tecumseh. The Treaty of Camp Charlotte surrendered Shawnee hunting rights south of the Ohio, and the wars that followed, through the Revolution and the Northwest Indian War, ended for the Shawnee only with the Treaty of Greenville in 1795, three years after Kentucky became a state.
zh:
查特里斯保留着一支山地苏语人群的名字，17世纪早期的地图把他们标在奥瓦西奥托，即坎伯兰山岭中。俄亥俄河谷与肯塔基河源之间的森林没有固定边界：图特洛人和莫内顿人的独木舟路线穿过水陆转运道，肖尼游群在山岭行猎，讲易洛魁语的中间商把毛皮运往东方。1444年，这里是肖尼世界边缘一片共有的猎场。基斯波科是肖尼五大分支中最小的一支，肖尼的世袭战酋长便出自这一分支。

1671年，受亚伯拉罕·伍德派遣，托马斯·巴茨和罗伯特·法拉姆率领第一支英国人队伍越过这些西流河水域，在新河与卡诺瓦河附近遇到摩赫坦和莫内顿社群。随后的海狸战争使山岭为之一空：霍德诺索尼人约在1670年击溃图特洛人，索取俄亥俄河南岸猎场；基斯波科人则被逐到远至克里克人之地，直到约1759年才回到俄亥俄。1774年10月10日，肖尼酋长康姆斯托克率300至500名战士，在卡诺瓦河口的波因特普莱森特战役中进攻安德鲁·刘易斯的一千名弗吉尼亚民兵。战斗演为白刃相接，肖尼人在入夜后撤退，战死者中包括基斯波科战酋长、特库姆塞的父亲。《坎普夏洛特条约》放弃了俄亥俄河南岸的肖尼狩猎权；此后的独立战争和西北印第安战争，对肖尼人而言直到1795年《格林维尔条约》才告结束，此时距肯塔基建州已有三年。

en:
The lower Little Tennessee, where the Great Smoky Mountains fall away toward the Tennessee, is the country of Atali. Dallas-culture farmers built platform-mound towns on its maize bottoms: Coste on Bussell Island at the river mouth, Tali upstream with a mound 25 feet high, and Satapo beyond. The Tennessee carried trade and war parties south to Coosa, and the towns lay on the northern edge of that chiefdom's orbit. In 1444 their mound centres still flourished, and no European had yet entered the valley.

De Soto's army left Coste on 9 July 1540 and marched up the Little Tennessee to Tali, where the townspeople were already piling into canoes to flee downstream; his soldiers drove them back, and the chief gave him four women and two porters and sent sofkee, a maize gruel, after the column until it reached Coosa on 16 July. Juan Pardo reached Satapo in October 1567, but a friendly warning of a plot against him hurried the expedition back to Chiaha. Disease emptied the Muskogean towns within two generations. Cherokee families moved into the valley and kept the old names: Satapo became Citico and Tali probably survived as Toqua, Cherokee for 'fish place', after a great fish said to haunt the mouth of its creek. By the eighteenth century the river was the chain of Overhill towns.

Citico was the largest, with about a thousand people and 204 warriors. The British built Fort Loudoun there in 1756-57, one of their first outposts beyond the Appalachians; after Cherokee hostages were killed at Fort Prince George, the Cherokee besieged the fort through the summer of 1760 and took its surrender in August, then attacked the retreating garrison and killed or captured most of the men. Henry Timberlake came upriver on the peace mission of 1761-62 and smoked so many pipes at Citico's townhouse that he could not stir for hours. In 1776 William Christian burned five Overhill towns, already deserted for the war chief Dragging Canoe, who led his people down the Tennessee in 1777 to found eleven towns on Chickamauga Creek and fought the Americans until 1794. John Sevier burned Toqua in 1788, and the Calhoun Treaty ceded the valley to the United States in 1819.
zh:
小田纳西河下游、大雾山向田纳西河低伏展开的这一带，就是阿塔利。达拉斯文化的农人在玉米滩地上建起一座座墩台市镇：河口布塞尔岛上是科斯特，溯河不远是土墩高25英尺的塔利，再往上是萨塔波。田纳西河把他们的商队和战队送往南方的库萨，这些市镇正处在那个最高酋邦势力范围的北缘。1444年，各处墩台中心依旧繁荣，欧洲人尚未进入这条河谷。

1540年7月9日，德·索托的队伍离开科斯特，沿小田纳西河上溯到塔利，镇民正纷纷登上独木舟准备顺流逃散，被士兵逼回；酋长献上四名女子和两名脚夫，又沿途送去玉米粥索夫基，直到远征队在7月16日抵达库萨。1567年10月，胡安·帕尔多进抵萨塔波，却因得到有人密谋加害的密报，匆忙退回奇亚哈。两代人之间，疫病使这些讲穆斯科格语的市镇人口断绝。切罗基人家族迁入空谷并沿用旧名：萨塔波变成西蒂科，塔利很可能就是后来的托夸；托夸在切罗基语里意为「鱼之地」，得名于相传栖居在其溪口的一条大鱼。到18世纪，这条河上已是山外切罗基城镇连成的链条。

西蒂科是其中最大的一座，约有一千居民、204名战士。1756至1757年，英国人在此修筑劳登堡，这是他们翻过大雾山以西最早的据点之一；切罗基人质在普林斯乔治堡被杀后，切罗基人于1760年夏围攻劳登堡，8月接受守军投降，随即袭击撤退的队伍，大部分英军被杀或被俘。1761至1762年，亨利·廷伯莱克奉命沿河上来议和，在西蒂科议事堂里连抽和平烟管，事后几个小时动弹不得。1776年，威廉·克里斯蒂安烧毁五座山外城镇，居民早已随战酋拖独木舟离去；次年他率部顺田纳西河而下，在奇卡莫加溪建立十一座城镇，与美国人一直打到1794年。托夸于1788年被约翰·塞维尔烧毁；1819年，《卡尔霍恩条约》把这条河谷割让给美国。

en:
Yazoo covers the lower Yazoo River and the bluffs where it approaches the Mississippi. In 1444 this was Tunica-speaking ground, shared by village peoples later documented as the Yazoo and Koroa and by Plaquemine farming towns built above the floods. Maize, beans and squash grew in the bottomlands, while canoes carried skins and shells between villages and chiefdoms upstream. Quizquiz, the chiefdom recorded in Hernando de Soto's narratives, was one of the powers on this stretch of the river; its exact site remains debated.

In the spring of 1541 de Soto's battered army reached Quizquiz, seized a town and took more than three hundred women; Spanish accounts say the aged chief rose from his sickbed with a battle-axe before the expedition moved on and crossed the Mississippi by night. Epidemics and raiding had thinned the river towns before French missionaries found the Yazoo and Koroa in the 1690s. France built Fort St. Pierre on the bluffs in 1719, a palisaded and moated northern post intended to check English trade from Carolina. After the Natchez destroyed Fort Rosalie, the Yazoo and Koroa killed the Jesuit Jean Rouel on 11 December 1729 and wiped out the St. Pierre garrison the next day. French and Choctaw retaliation ended the Yazoo as a tribe, with survivors sold into slavery or absorbed by neighbours. Spain later raised Fort Nogales on the bluffs in 1790, the United States took over in 1798, and the Choctaw cession at Fort Adams in 1801 opened the bottomlands to cotton planters.
zh:
亚祖包括亚祖河下游及其接近密西西比河处的陡崖地带。1444年，这里是图尼卡语族群的土地，后来被记载为亚祖人和科罗阿人的村落族群，与建在洪水线以上的普拉克明农耕城镇共同生活。河滩地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，独木舟载着兽皮与贝壳，往来于各村落和上游酋邦之间。德·索托远征记中提到的基斯基斯是这一段大河上的强权之一，但其确切位置仍有争议。

1541年春，疲惫不堪的德·索托队伍到达基斯基斯，夺取一座城镇并掳走三百多名妇女；西班牙记载称，年迈的酋长抱病持战斧起身，远征队随后继续前行，趁夜渡过密西西比河。法国传教士在17世纪90年代见到亚祖人和科罗阿人之前，疫病和袭扰已使沿河村镇人口大减。1719年，法国在陡崖上修建圣皮埃尔堡，这座带栅栏和壕沟的北方据点用以遏制卡罗来纳的英国贸易。纳奇兹人摧毁罗萨莉堡后，亚祖人与科罗阿人于1729年12月11日杀死耶稣会士让·鲁埃尔，次日又全歼圣皮埃尔堡守军。法国与乔克托联军的报复使亚祖人作为一个部族不复存在，幸存者被卖为奴或并入邻族。1790年，西班牙人在陡崖上修建诺加莱斯堡；1798年美国人接管，1801年《亚当斯堡条约》带来的乔克托割地使河滩地向棉花种植园主开放。

en:
The Natchez Bluffs rise where the lower Mississippi bends south across its floodplain, and they held the strongest chiefdom left in the valley. Plaquemine farmers had raised platform mounds here since about 700, and around 1500 their lands ran from the Big Black River to the Homochitto, centred on Emerald Mound, the second-largest pre-Columbian earthwork north of Mexico. By 1444 the paramount chief had his seat at the Grand Village of the Natchez and bore the title Great Sun. He inherited through his mother's line over Suns, Honored men and commoners who worked the maize fields, and when a Sun died retainers were sent to follow him to the grave.

The first Europeans on the bluffs were the survivors of Hernando de Soto's expedition. In 1542 and 1543 war canoes sent by a chief called Quigualtam harried them on the river for three days; many scholars take that chiefdom for the Natchez. La Salle passed through in 1682 and claimed the valley for France, and in 1716 Bienville built Fort Rosalie below the Grand Village after the first French war; the town beside it became Natchez, surrounded by tobacco concessions. On 28 November 1729 the Natchez burned the fort and killed about 230 colonists after the commandant Chépart tried to seize White Apple village for his own plantation, though most of the women and enslaved Africans were spared. French troops and Choctaw allies destroyed the chiefdom in reply: the Great Sun was captured in January 1731 and sold into slavery in Saint-Domingue, and the last refugees fled first to the Chickasaw and then to the Creek. The bluffs passed from France to Britain in 1763, to Spain in 1779 and to the United States in 1798; Natchez became capital of the Mississippi Territory and in 1817 the first capital of the state of Mississippi, its wharves loading cotton floated down from the plantations upriver.
zh:
纳奇兹陡崖矗立在密西西比河下游折流向南之处，崖下是河水流过的洪泛平原，下游最强大的酋邦就坐落在这片崖上。普拉克明农民约从公元700年起在此堆筑台丘，1500年前后其疆土北起大黑河、南抵霍莫奇托河，以翡翠丘为中心，那是墨西哥以北第二大的史前土建工程。1444年时，最高酋长坐镇纳奇兹大村庄，号称「大太阳」。他按母系继承，统治「太阳」贵族、「受敬者」和耕作玉米田的平民；一位「太阳」去世，便有随从被送去殉葬同行。

最早来到陡崖的欧洲人是德·索托远征队的残部。1542至1543年，一位叫基瓜尔塔姆的酋长派出独木战船，在河上截击他们三日；多数学者认为这个酋邦就是纳奇兹人。1682年拉萨尔经过此地，为法国宣称整个河谷；1716年第一次法国战争后，比安维尔在大村庄下方建起罗莎莉堡，堡旁长成的城镇便是纳奇兹，四周都是烟草租让地。1729年11月28日，要塞司令要强征白苹果村开辟私人种植园，纳奇兹人放火焚堡、杀死约230名殖民者，只放过了大部分妇女和非洲黑奴。法军和乔克托盟友反手摧毁了整个酋邦：1731年1月大太阳被俘，卖到圣多明戈为奴，最后的残部先投奇克索人，再投奔克里克人。陡崖之地1763年归英国，1779年归西班牙，1798年归美国；纳奇兹先为密西西比准州首府，1817年又成为密西西比州的第一个州府，码头上装运的是上游种植园顺河而下的棉花。

en:
Biloxi Bay opens behind the barrier sands of the Mississippi Sound, with Ship Island offshore as the safest roadstead between Mobile Bay and the Mississippi delta. In 1444 the shores of Taneks-Haya belonged to the Tanêks, a Siouan-speaking farming people descended from Mississippian mound-builders, whom French writers later called Biloxi; French accounts glossed their own name for themselves as 'the first people'. Women grew maize, beans and squash, while men fished the sound all year and hunted deer, bear and bison. When a chief died his body was dried over fire and smoke and set upright on a red pole in the temple, where visitors brought it food.

Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville sailed into the sound in 1699 and found the nation much reduced, for smallpox had emptied an entire village a few years before. With provisions running out, his men chose a rise on the northeast shore and raised Fort Maurepas in three weeks, twelve guns and four bastions, naming it the first capital of French Louisiana; about a hundred men stayed under Sauvolle and Iberville's teenaged brother Bienville, with orders to breed buffalo, seek pearls and look for mines. Fever killed Sauvolle, and Bienville moved the colony to the Mobile River in 1702. A new town, New Biloxi, went up across the bay after 1717 with Fort Louis beside it, and the government of Louisiana returned to Biloxi for two years before Bienville moved it down to New Orleans in 1722. The coast passed to Britain in 1763 and to Spain during the American war, and United States rule reached it in 1811. The surviving Tanêks drifted west to the Red River and the Louisiana prairies, where they merged with the Tunica.
zh:
比洛克西湾在密西西比湾的障沙岛后方展开，外海的船岛是莫比尔湾到密西西比河口之间最稳妥的锚地。1444年，塔内克斯哈亚的湾岸属于塔内克斯人：他们操苏语族语言，是密西西比土丘建造者的后裔，后来的法国作者称他们为比洛克西人，法国文献还把他们的自称解释为「最初的人」。妇女种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，男子常年在海湾捕鱼，猎取鹿、熊和野牛。首领死后，遗体会用烟火熏干，直立安放在神庙里的红柱上，访客每日为他献上食物。

1699年，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔驶入海湾，发现这个族群已经大为衰落，几年前的一场天花让整座村落空无一人。由于给养将尽，部下选中湾东北岸的一处高地，三周内筑起有四座棱堡、十二门炮的莫勒帕堡，定为法属路易斯安那的第一个首府；约一百人留守，归索沃尔和伊贝维尔十几岁的弟弟边维尔统领，领到的差事包括驯养野牛、寻觅珍珠和勘探矿藏。索沃尔后来死于热病，边维尔在1702年把殖民地迁往莫比尔河。1717年后，海湾对岸建起新城新比洛克西，旁边是圣路易堡，路易斯安那的治所回到比洛克西两年，1722年边维尔又把它迁往新奥尔良。海岸1763年转入英国之手，美国独立战争期间归属西班牙，1811年美国的统治延伸到此。幸存的塔内克斯人逐渐西迁到雷德河和路易斯安那草原，最终并入图尼卡人。

en:
Abihka is the upper country of the Coosa and Tallapoosa, where the rivers come down out of the southern Appalachians onto the coastal plain. In 1444 its towns stood within the reach of the Coosa chiefdom, whose core lay upstream and whose alliances ran into central Alabama. They worked wide maize fields in the Mississippian manner, while a people the later Spanish chronicles call the Napochi held the western tributaries on the Black Warrior.

Hernando de Soto entered Coosa in July 1540 and let the chief receive him in state, then chained the chief and his headmen and dragged them south as hostages as far as Talisi. In the summer of 1560 a two-hundred-man detachment from Tristan de Luna's colony marched with Coosa warriors against the rebellious Napochi, found their towns abandoned, and accepted their leaders' renewed submission and tribute. Epidemics then emptied the old chiefdom, and its survivors gathered into the Upper Creek towns; Abihka became one of the four mother towns of the Muscogee confederacy.

The forks of the Coosa and Tallapoosa became an imperial frontier. In 1717 the French built Fort Toulouse there, its twenty to fifty marines trading muskets and blankets for deerskins to hold the Upper Creeks against Carolina and Georgia; the British answered with Fort Okfuskee up the Tallapoosa in 1735. By tradition the French captain Marchand married the Creek woman Sehoy, whose descendants later included Alexander McGillivray and William Weatherford, the Upper Creek warrior called Red Eagle. The French spiked their cannon and left in 1763, and the naturalist William Bartram visited the ruined post in 1776. After Tecumseh's visit of 1811 the Upper Towns led the Red Stick rising. At Tohopeka, on a horseshoe bend of the Tallapoosa, Menawa's thousand warriors had raised a four-hundred-yard log breastwork across the neck of land; on 27 March 1814 Andrew Jackson stormed it with 2,700 men and Cherokee and Lower Creek allies, the young Sam Houston among the first over the logs. About 800 Red Sticks died, and Menawa escaped wounded. Jackson raised Fort Jackson on the old French site, and there on 9 August 1814 the Creeks ceded 22 million acres, the whole Abihka country among it.
zh:
阿比卡是库萨河与塔拉普萨河上游之地，河水从阿巴拉契亚山南麓奔流而下，进入滨海平原。1444年，这里的诸镇处于库萨邦国的势力范围内：邦国核心在更靠上游的地方，同盟则延伸到阿拉巴马中部。各镇按密西西比式的耕作开辟大片玉米田；西边黑沃里尔河支流上的一支居民，后来被西班牙史家称作纳波奇人。

1540年7月德索托进入库萨，先受酋长隆重接见，随即将他和头人锁拿，一路南押到塔利西为质。1560年夏，德卢纳殖民队伍的两百人分队随库萨战士出征黑沃里尔河畔叛离的纳波奇人，见其城镇已弃守，便接受纳波奇首领重新称臣纳贡。疫病随后掏空了旧邦国，幸存者汇聚成上克里克诸城，阿比卡便是克里克联盟四大母镇之一。

库萨河与塔拉普萨河的汇流处后来成了帝国对峙的前沿。1717年法国人在此建起图卢兹堡，常驻二三十名到50名海军陆战队员，用火枪和毛毯交换鹿皮，把上克里克人拉向法国一边，对抗卡罗来纳与佐治亚；英国人则于1735年在塔拉普萨河上游建起奥克富斯基堡应对。相传法国军官马尚娶了克里克女子塞霍伊，她的后人中后来有麦吉利夫雷和被称为「红鹰」的上克里克战士威廉·韦瑟福德。1763年法国人钉死大炮撤离，1776年博物学家威廉·巴特兰探访过这座荒废的堡垒。特库姆塞1811年来访后，上镇成为红棍起事的骨干。在塔拉普萨河一个马蹄形大河弯的托霍佩卡，梅纳瓦的1000名战士在河弯瓶颈处筑起400码长的原木胸墙；1814年3月27日，安德鲁·杰克逊率2700人及切罗基、下克里克盟军强攻，五小时破阵，年轻的山姆·休斯顿是最先翻过原木墙的人之一。约800名红棍战士战死，梅纳瓦负伤逃脱。杰克逊在法国旧堡址上建起杰克逊堡，1814年8月9日克里克人在此割让2200万英亩土地，阿比卡故土尽在其中。

en:
Mabila is the lower Alabama and Tombigbee country, where the rivers leave the fall-line hills and wind through maize-rich bottoms toward Mobile Bay. In 1444 it lay on the southern edge of the Mississippian world, among its farming settlements; Choctaw-speaking peoples lived west of the Alabama, while the Tohome and Mobile held the lower Tombigbee and Tensaw near the delta.

In October 1540 Hernando de Soto came down from Coosa. At Atahachi, a newly built fortified town with a mound and plaza above the Alabama River, he took the paramount chief Tuskaloosa hostage; the chroniclers describe a chief so tall he stood head and shoulders above the Spaniards, and his Muskogean name means Black Warrior. Tuskaloosa directed the expedition to Mabila, a palisaded town on a cleared plain where more than 2,500 warriors waited in the houses. On 18 October the trap closed. The fighting ran eight or nine hours, the town was fired, and the Mabilians carried off the Spanish baggage; almost no one inside survived. The chronicler Biedma puts the dead above 5,000, Tuskaloosa's son was among them, and the chief himself disappeared. The chiefdom never recovered, and within a century its people had been drawn into the forming Choctaw and Creek confederacies.

In 1702 the French raised Fort Louis de la Louisiane on a Mobile River bluff, the first capital of their Louisiana colony. The Tohome and Mobile settled beside it about 1709, and in 1711 Bienville moved the town down to Mobile Bay; the brick Fort Conde went up from 1723. Mobile passed to Britain in 1763, was taken by Bernardo de Galvez's Spaniards in 1780, and was seized for the United States by James Wilkinson in 1813. That summer the Creek War reached the Tensaw: on 30 August Red Sticks stormed Fort Mims and killed perhaps 250 to 500 people, and after Horseshoe Bend the district passed to the United States in the Creek cession of 1814.
zh:
马比拉地处阿拉巴马河下游与汤比格比河流域，河水越过瀑布线丘陵，穿过盛产玉米的滩地流向莫比尔湾。1444年，这里位于密西西比文化世界的南境，分布着农耕聚落；阿拉巴马河以西住着操乔克托语的族群，三角洲附近的汤比格比河与坦索河下游则在托霍梅人和莫比尔人手中。

1540年10月，德索托自库萨南下。德索托抵达阿拉巴马河畔的阿塔哈奇，这是一座带土墩和广场的新建设防城镇，他在此挟制了大君塔斯卡卢萨；编年史家称这位酋长身材极高，比西班牙人高出一头有余，其名在马斯科吉语中意为「黑武士」。塔斯卡卢萨把远征队引向马比拉，那是平原上一片砍净草木的木栅城镇，2500多名战士藏在屋中。10月18日伏兵杀出，战斗持续八九个小时，城镇被焚毁，马比拉人还夺走了西班牙人的辎重，寨中几乎无人幸免。编年史家别德马称死者超过5000人，塔斯卡卢萨之子陈尸其间，他本人则不知所终。邦国再未恢复，不到一个世纪，其民众便被卷入正在形成的乔克托联盟和克里克联盟。

1702年，法国人在莫比尔河畔高崖上建起路易斯堡，作为路易斯安那殖民地的第一个首府。托霍梅人和莫比尔人约1709年获准迁居堡旁，1711年边维尔把城镇迁到莫比尔湾畔，1723年起砖石结构的孔代堡拔地而起。莫比尔1763年归英国，1780年被贝尔纳多·德·加尔维斯的西班牙军队攻占，1813年又被詹姆斯·威尔金逊为美国夺取。同年夏天克里克战争烧到坦索：8月30日红棍战士攻破米姆斯堡，杀死约250至500人；蹄铁湾之战后，这片地区随1814年克里克人的割地归入美国。

en:
The Chipola and Choctawhatchee rivers wind through pine hills and fertile bottoms between Choctawhatchee Bay and the Apalachicola, the richest corner of the Florida panhandle. In 1444 Chatot belonged to a Muskogean farming people whom Spanish records later wrote down as Chacato and English writers as Chatot; their pottery and ways of farming matched those of the Apalachee to the east. At Waddells Mill Pond, two mounds inside a circular rampart mark a fortified town in the heart of their later homeland. No mission bell or Spanish garrison had yet reached them.

Two Franciscan missions, San Carlos Borromeo and San Nicolás de Tolentino, opened in Chacato villages in June 1674. The conversion went badly. The next summer Juan Fernández de Diocsale and two companions swore to kill Fray Barreda after the friar forced mass attendance and Christian marriage on the village; they ambushed and wounded him, he escaped, many families fled to Tawasa, and Diocsale was exiled to Mexico. In January 1704 James Moore, the former governor of Carolina, led his militia and Muscogee riders through the Apalachee missions, burning the chain of towns and killing or carrying off their people. Between 200 and 250 Chacato got away through Pensacola to French Mobile, some driving their cattle ahead of them; the French counted about 250 Chacato men there at first, forty in 1725 and thirty in 1817. The empty homeland passed to Britain with West Florida in 1763 and back to Spain twenty years later, while the last Chacato families merged into the peoples of French Louisiana.
zh:
奇波拉河和乔克塔哈奇河蜿蜒穿过松林丘陵与肥沃低地，这片土地位于乔克塔哈奇湾和阿巴拉奇科拉河之间，是佛罗里达狭长地带最富庶的一角。1444年，沙托属于一支说穆斯科格语的农耕人群，西班牙文献后来把他们记作查卡托，英国文献记作沙托；他们的陶器和农作方式与东边的阿巴拉奇人如出一辙。沃德尔磨坊池有两座土墩围在一圈环形壁垒之内，标示出他们后来祖地中心的一座设防村镇。此时传教士的钟声和西班牙驻军都还没有到来。

1674年6月，方济各会在沙托人的村落开设圣卡洛斯·博罗梅奥和圣尼古拉斯·德·托伦蒂诺两座传教站。皈依进行得很不顺利。次年夏天，胡安·费尔南德斯·德·迪奥克萨莱和两名同伴立誓要杀巴雷达修士，起因是修士强令村民参加弥撒、遵守基督教婚姻；他们伏击并打伤了修士，修士脱身逃走，许多家庭逃往塔瓦萨，迪奥克萨莱被流放墨西哥。1704年1月，前卡罗来纳总督詹姆斯·穆尔率领民兵和穆斯科格骑兵横扫阿巴拉奇传教区，焚毁连成一线的村镇，居民或遭杀戮，或被掳走。二百至二百五十名沙托人经彭萨科拉逃到法属莫比尔，有些人还一路赶着牛群；法国人起初清点约有二百五十名沙托男子，1725年只剩四十，1817年只剩三十。空置的祖地1763年随西佛罗里达归入英国，二十年后又转回西班牙，最后的沙托家庭则融入了法属路易斯安那的各族群。

en:
In 1444 Yustaga was the westernmost Timucua country, filling the Suwannee Valley between the Aucilla and Suwannee rivers next to Apalachee. As many as eight local chiefdoms shared the same pottery and perhaps the Potano dialect, kept stores of maize, beans and pumpkins, and looked to Potohiriba as the leading town. Across the Suwannee, marriage ties and raids alike linked them to the Northern Utina without making the two peoples one.

De Soto entered an evacuated Uzachile on 25 September 1539, and a chronicler counted two hundred houses and stacks of maize, beans and pumpkins; French visitors from Fort Caroline in 1564 put the local chief's strength at three or four thousand warriors. A missionary later left a description of their ball game, and Yustaga teams were still playing it in the 1680s, after the Apalachee had given theirs up.

The Yustaga kept Franciscans out until about 1623, when the chief of Potohiriba accepted two friars, and San Pedro de Potohiriba became the head of a mission province put at some 12,000 people. Chief Diego of Potohiriba led the Yustaga into the Timucua Rebellion of 1656 and was executed after it failed, with other rebel chiefs. Four missions still served 330 families in 1689, but the Carolinian and Creek raids of 1704 destroyed the province, and the surviving Yustaga withdrew toward St. Augustine and merged with the other mission peoples.
zh:
1444年的尤斯塔加是蒂穆夸语人群中最西的一支，占据奥西拉河与萨旺尼河之间的萨旺尼河谷，与阿巴拉契为邻。约八个地方酋邦共用同一种陶器，所说可能是波塔诺方言，各村储存玉米、豆类和南瓜，尊波托伊里巴为诸镇之首。萨旺尼河对岸，联姻和袭掠都把他们同北乌蒂纳人连在一起，却没有让两族人合成一家。

1539年9月25日，德·索托进入已经撤空的乌萨奇莱，一名随行军士清点出两百座房屋和成堆的玉米、豆子与南瓜；1564年卡罗琳堡来的法国人估计，当地酋长能出动三四千名战士。后来一名传教士记下了他们的球赛，阿巴拉契人放弃这种球赛后，尤斯塔加的球队到1680年代仍在比赛。

尤斯塔加人把方济各会挡在门外，直到约1623年波托伊里巴酋长接纳两名修士，圣佩德罗·德·波托伊里巴随后成为一个传教教区之首，据估教区约有一万二千人。波托伊里巴酋长迭戈率尤斯塔加人参加1656年蒂穆夸叛乱，失败后与其他叛乱酋长一同被处死。到1689年，四座传教站仍统辖三百三十户人家；1704年卡罗来纳人和克里克人的袭掠摧毁了教区，幸存的尤斯塔加人撤往圣奥古斯丁方向，同其他传教区人群融合。

en:
The Calusa ruled the mangrove-lined sounds and estuaries of southwest Florida, from Charlotte Harbor to Marco Island. Calos, the capital probably raised on Mound Key in Estero Bay, stood on shell works built from the lagoon's oysters and conchs; later Spanish accounts described a royal hall large enough for two thousand people. Fish, oysters, turtles and waterfowl supported nobles, priests, a war captain and perhaps 20,000 people around 1500. Dugout war canoes carried the king's demands to the Mayaimi at Lake Okeechobee and to the Tequesta and Jaega on the Atlantic side. In 1444 the Calusa king ruled the densest society in South Florida, and its wealth came from fishing weirs and shell mounds rather than maize fields.

Juan Ponce de León careened his ships at the Caloosahatchee in 1513 and fought twenty war canoes; when he returned to plant a colony in 1521, a Calusa arrow wounded him and he died in Cuba. Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, shipwrecked as a boy and held for seventeen years, later wrote one of Spain's fullest accounts of Florida's peoples. The main Spanish attempt at a foothold used marriage as well as force: in 1566 Pedro Menéndez de Avilés married King Carlos's baptized sister, Doña Antonia, and built San Antón de Carlos at Calos. The alliance did not last. The Spaniards killed Carlos and then his successor Felipe, and withdrew after three years. A Franciscan mission in 1697 lasted only months, and the Calusa kept their own ceremonies and chiefly line. Epidemics and slave raiders from Carolina then broke the kingdom. In 1711 the Spaniards shipped 270 survivors to Cuba, where nearly 200 soon died. The last Calusa exiles left with the Spaniards in 1763, two centuries after their arrows stopped Ponce de León's colony.
zh:
卡卢萨人统治着佛罗里达西南红树林环绕的海湾与河口，疆域从夏洛特港延伸到马科岛。都城卡洛斯可能建在埃斯特罗湾的芒德礁上，坐落在用潟湖牡蛎壳和海螺壳堆成的贝冢高地；后来的西班牙记载称，王宫中的大殿足以容纳两千人。鱼、牡蛎、海龟和水禽供养着贵族、祭司、军事首领以及1500年前后约两万人。作战独木舟把国王的命令送往奥基乔比湖畔的马亚依米人，也送往大西洋沿岸的特克斯塔人和哈埃加人。1444年，卡卢萨国王统治着南佛罗里达人口最稠密的社会，其财富来自鱼梁和贝冢，而不是玉米田。

1513年，胡安·庞塞·德莱昂在卡卢萨哈奇河口修船，与二十艘作战独木舟交战；1521年他再次前来建立殖民地，被卡卢萨人的箭射伤，死在古巴。少年时遇海难、被扣押十七年的埃尔南多·德·埃斯卡兰特·丰特内达，后来写成西班牙人记述佛罗里达诸族最详尽的文献之一。西班牙人一次主要的立足尝试同时借助婚姻和武力：1566年，佩德罗·梅嫩德斯·德·阿维莱斯娶国王卡洛斯受洗的妹妹安东尼娅女士为妻，并在卡洛斯修建圣安东·德·卡洛斯。同盟并未维持多久。西班牙人杀死卡洛斯，又杀死继立者费利佩，三年后撤兵。1697年设立的方济各会传教站只维持数月，卡卢萨人仍保留自己的仪式和酋长世系。疫病和来自卡罗来纳的奴隶贩子随后击垮了王国。1711年，西班牙人把270名幸存者送往古巴，近200人很快死去。最后的卡卢萨流亡者在1763年随西班牙人离开，距他们用箭挡住庞塞·德莱昂的殖民已有两百年。

en:
The Mayaimi lived around Lake Mayaimi, the 'big water' now called Okeechobee, in the marshy plain of southern Florida. Their villages stood on earthen mounds above flood level, joined by canals that carried shovel-ended dugout canoes between fishing grounds. Fort Center, northwest of the lake, was a complex of mounds, ditches, middens and an artificial pond, and one of the region's major ceremonial works. The lake supplied bass, eels, turtles and alligator, while coontie root was processed into flour; when high water covered the low ground, the mound villages lived largely on fish. Fontaneda described many small towns of thirty or forty people. In 1444 these lake towns paid tribute to the Calusa kings on the Gulf coast.

For more than a century after Juan Ponce de León's voyage, Europeans knew the Mayaimi chiefly through Hernando de Escalante Fontaneda, who lived among the peoples of southern Florida for seventeen years and visited their lake towns. No Spanish mission or fort secured the lake, and its communities were broken by the slave trade. Early in the eighteenth century, Creek and Yamasee raiders armed by Carolina crossed the peninsula, burned villages and sold captives in ports from Boston to Barbados. A refugee party of 280 Florida people that reached Cuba in 1710 included the cacique of 'Maimi'. Some survivors regrouped on the coast south of Cape Canaveral, where the Maymi still held a fortified place in 1738. Five years later missionaries found about a hundred Mayaimi, Santaluzo and Mayaca people living four days north of the Miami River. Any Mayaimi who remained were thought to have been evacuated to Cuba with the Spaniards in 1763.
zh:
马亚依米人住在马亚依米湖畔；「马亚依米」意为「大水」，此湖即今奥基乔比湖，位于南佛罗里达的沼泽平原。他们的村镇建在土筑高台上以避洪水，高台之间有运河相通，两端如铲的独木舟沿运河往来渔场。湖西北的森特堡由土台、沟渠、贝丘和人工池塘组成，是这一地带最重要的仪式工程之一。湖中出产黑鲈、鳗、龟和短吻鳄，泽米蕨根则被加工成粉；大水淹没低地时，高台上的村镇主要靠鱼为生。丰特内达记载，这里有许多三四十人的小镇。1444年，这些湖畔村镇向墨西哥湾沿岸的卡卢萨国王纳贡。

胡安·庞塞·德莱昂航行后的一个多世纪里，欧洲人主要通过埃尔南多·德·埃斯卡兰特·丰特内达知道马亚依米人；他在南佛罗里达诸族中生活了十七年，曾到过湖畔村镇。西班牙人的传教站或要塞始终没有控制大湖，真正瓦解湖镇的是奴隶贸易。18世纪初，得到卡罗来纳武装的克里克和亚马西袭击者横穿半岛，焚毁村镇，把俘虏卖到从波士顿到巴巴多斯的港口。1710年抵达古巴的280名佛罗里达难民中，有一位「迈米」首领。一些幸存者在卡纳维拉尔角以南海岸重新聚集，1738年马亚依米人仍在那里据有一处设防地点。五年后，传教士发现约一百名马亚依米人、圣卢索人和玛亚卡人，住在迈阿密河以北四天路程处。1763年，仍存的马亚依米人据信都随西班牙人撤往了古巴。

en:
Ichisi was a Muskogean chiefdom of the Ocmulgee floodplain, its principal town usually identified with the Lamar mounds a few miles southeast of the older Ocmulgee mound center, where two earthen mounds give their name to the late Lamar phase. Maize fields and bottomland hunting grounds supported a hierarchical town linked by trails to Ocute and the other chiefdoms of central Georgia. In 1444 priests held ceremony on the mounds, women cooked corn cakes and venison, and no European had yet entered the valley.

Hernando de Soto's army reached Ichisi in March 1540 and met no fight. The chief received the Spaniards in peace, supplied corn cakes, wild onions and venison, and told them of the paramount chief at Ocute; de Soto set up a wooden cross on a mound before marching on. Within a century disease and political collapse had undone the Ocmulgee chiefdoms. The people of Ichisi later appear in Spanish records as Chechessee, one of the Lower Towns of the Yamasee confederacy, while Hitchiti-speaking towns held Ocmulgee Fields near Macon until they withdrew toward the Chattahoochee after the Yamasee War of 1715. The United States built Fort Benjamin Hawkins on the bluff in 1806, and the Creek cession of Ocmulgee Fields in 1821 opened the bottomlands to short-staple cotton planters.
zh:
伊奇西是奥克马尔吉河洪泛平原上的马斯科吉酋长领地，主城通常比定为拉马尔土丘遗址，它在更古老的奥克马尔吉土丘中心东南数英里，遗址内的两座土墩是拉马尔晚期文化的命名地。玉米田和滩地猎场养着一个等级分明的城镇，有小径通往奥库特和佐治亚中部其他酋邦。1444年，祭司在土墩上主持仪式，妇女制作玉米饼、烹烤鹿肉，欧洲人尚未进入这片河谷。

1540年3月，埃尔南多·德·索托的队伍抵达伊奇西，没有遭遇战斗。酋长和平接待这些西班牙人，送来玉米饼、野洋葱和鹿肉，还向他们指点奥库特的大酋长；德·索托在一座土墩上竖起木十字架后继续北上。此后不到一个世纪，疫病和政治动荡瓦解了奥克马尔吉诸酋邦。伊奇西人后来以「切切西」之名出现在西班牙记录中，是亚马西联盟的下镇之一；希奇蒂语诸镇则据守梅肯附近的奥克马尔吉原野，1715年亚马西战争后向查特胡奇河方向退去。1806年，美国在河畔高地上建起本杰明·霍金斯堡；1821年克里克人割让奥克马尔吉原野，滩地随之对短绒棉种植园主开放。

en:
Ocute was the paramount chiefdom of the Oconee River valley, a loose league of mound towns under a mico whose own center stood at Shoulderbone, founded about 1325 halfway between the towns of Altamaha and Cofaqui-Patofa. The towns lived on maize and the river, and their fifteenth century was one long war with Cofitachequi, the great chiefdom to the east. Raiding emptied the Savannah, Saluda and Broad river basins and left a no-man's-land later called the Wilderness of Ocute. In 1444 the province was populous but heavily armed, and no European had entered it.

De Soto came through in April 1540 on his way to Cofitachequi. Zamuno, chief of Altamaha, came to meet him in arms, exchanged gifts, and asked whether his tribute should now go to the Spaniard instead of his overlord at Ocute; de Soto told him to keep his old allegiance, raised a wooden cross on the mound, and marched on with porters the Ocute towns gave him for the crossing of the wilderness. A Franciscan mission in 1597 was welcomed at Altamaha but warned off at Ocute, where the 1540 raid was still remembered. In the 1660s the Westo, armed with flintlocks by the English and deep in the Indian slave trade, raided the Oconee and shattered the province. Its refugees made for the coast, where Altamaha, Ocute and Ichisi re-formed as the Lower Towns of the Yamasee, the later refugee confederacy that gave this country its name. The Yamasee served Carolina as mercenary raiders until their defeat in the Yamasee War of 1715. Milledgeville was laid out on the old Oconee lands in 1803 and became Georgia's capital in 1804, and cotton fields spread where the mound towns had stood.
zh:
奥库特是奥科尼河流域的等级酋长联盟，各土丘城镇共奉一位米科大酋长，其驻地在肩骨遗址，约1325年建于奥尔塔马霍镇与科法基—帕托法镇之间，距两边各半程。诸镇以玉米和河运为生，整个15世纪都在同东方的强大酋邦科菲塔切基交战。袭掠使萨凡纳河、萨卢达河和布罗德河流域人烟断绝，留下一片后来被称作「奥库特荒野」的无人区。1444年的奥库特人口稠密却刀枪不离身，欧洲人尚未涉足。

1540年4月，德·索托在前往科菲塔切基途中经过此地。奥尔塔马霍首领萨穆诺武装出迎，与他互换礼物，询问自己今后是否该向西班牙人而非奥库特的宗主纳贡；德·索托让他照旧效忠，在土墩上竖起一座木十字架，带着奥库特诸镇提供的脚夫继续向荒野进发。1597年一支方济各会传教团在奥尔塔马霍受到欢迎，在奥库特却被勒令止步，当地人还记着1540年的那次入境。17世纪60年代，由英国人供给燧发枪、深度卷入印第安奴隶贸易的韦斯托人袭掠奥科尼河，打碎了这个酋邦。难民逃往海岸，奥尔塔马霍、奥库特和伊奇西在那里重组为亚马西联盟的下镇，这个后来的难民联盟把名字留给了这个地方。亚马西人替卡罗来纳充当雇佣袭掠者，直到1715年在亚马西战争中战败。1803年，米利奇维尔在旧日的奥科尼土地上建成，次年成为佐治亚首府，土丘城镇的故地改种棉花。

en:
The tidal sounds and Sea Islands between the Altamaha River and the mouth of the St. Johns were Mocama country, whose people spoke the Mocama dialect of Timucua. Two chiefdoms met the first Europeans on this coast: the Saturiwa, whose main town stood on Fort George Island and whose chief, the French leader Laudonniere was told, counted thirty villages under him, ten of their chiefs his 'brothers'; and the Tacatacuru on Cumberland Island. Villages moved through the salt-marsh channels by canoe to trade and to raid, and Mocama potters made the grog-tempered San Pedro ware found all along these waterways. In 1444 the chiefdoms had the coast to themselves.

French Huguenots reached it in 1562 and raised Fort Caroline in Saturiwa territory in 1564 with the chief's eager help, but Spanish troops out of St. Augustine destroyed the fort the following year and drew Mocama into their mission province. Three friary stations served the islands: San Juan del Puerto on Fort George Island, San Pedro de Mocama on Cumberland, and Santa Maria de Sena on Amelia. At San Juan the friar Francisco Pareja learned Timucua, worked out a way to write it, and printed a Spanish and Timucua catechism in 1612, the first book published in an Indian language in what is now the United States; a grammar and confessionals followed. Disease and slave raids emptied the islands nonetheless, English-backed Westo raiders wrecked the three stations in the 1670s, and South Carolina's invasion of 1702 overran the last refugee missions. The survivors gathered near St. Augustine, and in 1763, when Spain ceded Florida to Britain, eighty-nine mission Indians, Mocama and Guale among them, were shipped to Cuba with the garrisons.
zh:
阿尔塔马哈河与圣约翰斯河口之间的潮湾和海群岛，是莫卡马人的土地，他们讲蒂穆夸语的莫卡马方言。最早来到这段海岸的欧洲人遇到两个酋邦：萨图里瓦人的主镇在乔治堡岛，法国首领拉尔博尼耶尔听说，他们的酋长统辖三十个村庄，其中十个村长是他的「兄弟」；塔卡塔库鲁人则据有坎伯兰岛。各村乘独木舟穿行盐沼水道，做买卖也互相袭掠，莫卡马陶工烧制掺碎陶胎的圣佩德罗式陶器，整条水道沿岸都有出土。1444年，这片海岸还只有这两个酋邦。

1562年法国胡格诺派到此，1564年在萨图里瓦酋长的热心相助下，于其领地建起卡罗琳堡，第二年圣奥古斯丁派出的西班牙军队便拆毁堡垒，把莫卡马纳入自己的传教省。三座修士站分驻海岛：乔治堡岛的圣胡安·德尔·普埃尔托、坎伯兰岛的圣佩德罗·德·莫卡马和阿米莉亚岛的圣玛丽亚·德·塞纳。修士弗朗西斯科·帕雷哈在圣胡安站学会蒂穆夸语，摸索出它的写法，于1612年印出西班牙语和蒂穆夸语双语教义问答，这是今美国境内第一部以印第安语言出版的书，后来又有语法书和告解手册问世。尽管如此，疫病和掳奴仍使各岛人口流散；1670年代，得到英国人支持的韦斯托人摧毁三座站点，1702年南卡罗来纳入侵，踏平最后的避难传教站。幸存者聚到圣奥古斯丁附近；1763年西班牙把佛罗里达割让给英国时，八十九名传教区印第安人随守军被送往古巴，其中就有莫卡马人和瓜莱人。

en:
Etowah takes its name from italwa, the Muscogee word for a town. It stands on the north bank of the Etowah River, in the valley where the Piedmont meets the first Appalachian ridges. Around 1000 Mississippian farmers built the first town there, and at its peak in 1325 to 1375 a semicircular palisade and a moat ten feet deep ringed its plazas, some 140 buildings and three flat-topped mounds, the tallest sixty-three feet high. The dead in the burial mound went to the grave wearing embossed copper plates of a winged Birdman figure, some of the plates made as far away as Cahokia on the Mississippi; conch shells reached the town from the Gulf, and mica and copper from the Cumberland plateau. Etowah was one of the cycling chiefdoms under Coosa. In 1444 it had passed its peak and held the valley within Coosa's paramountcy.

Hernando de Soto's expedition crossed the valley in 1540 and heard of a town called Itaba between Coosa and Ulibahali, likely Etowah; within a generation epidemics and the collapse of the chiefdoms emptied the site. The Muscogee Creek kept the overgrown mounds sacred as Italwa, their foremost ancestral town. Coweta, leading town of the Lower Creeks, carried that Muskogean inheritance into the deerskin trade after Henry Woodward first reached it in the 1670s. Late in the eighteenth century the Cherokee, giving ground before settlers from the east, took the Etowah valley from the Creek, and Andrew Jackson's defeat of the Creeks in 1814 opened the old mound lands to the American frontier.
zh:
埃托瓦的名字来自穆斯科格语，伊塔尔瓦就是「镇」的意思。它坐落在埃托瓦河北岸、皮德蒙特与阿巴拉契亚山前缘相接的河谷。约1000年，密西西比文化的农人在此建起最早的城镇；1325至1375年全盛时，半圆形木栅和十英尺深的壕沟环护着广场、约140座房屋和三座平顶大土丘，最高的一座有63英尺。墓葬丘中的死者佩戴压花铜片，上铸带翼的鸟人形象，其中部分铜片产自远在密西西比河畔的卡霍基亚；海螺壳来自墨西哥湾，云母和铜料来自坎伯兰高原。埃托瓦本是库萨之下此消彼长的酋邦之一。1444年它已过鼎盛期，在库萨的宗主权下据守河谷。

1540年，埃尔南多·德索托的探险队穿过河谷，听说库萨与乌利巴哈利之间有座叫伊塔巴的城镇，很可能就是埃托瓦；此后不到一代人，疫病和酋邦体系的崩溃便使这里沦为空城。穆斯科格克里克人把野树丛生的土丘奉为圣地伊塔尔瓦，也就是他们最重要的祖居之城。下克里克人的首镇考维塔承下这份穆斯科格遗产，1670年代亨利·伍德沃德首次到访后，考维塔带着它进入鹿皮贸易的时代。18世纪末，切罗基人在东面移民的压力下节节西退，从克里克人手中夺占埃托瓦河谷；1814年安德鲁·杰克逊击败克里克人，古老的土丘之地向美国边疆敞开。

en:
Saluda is the piedmont valley of the Saluda River, which runs some two hundred miles to meet the Broad and become the Congaree on the way to the Santee and the Atlantic. At Saluda Old Town a low mound, a plaza and stamped pottery mark a farming village of the Temple Mound period, occupied from about AD 950 to 1550. In 1444 the valley was late Mississippian maize country, its fords linked by trails that the Carolina trade turned into the Cherokee Path.

By the late seventeenth century a people recorded as the Saluda, possibly a Shawnee band, held the Old Town, but they had moved north by 1712. George Hunter's 1730 survey marked the Cherokee Path through the valley, the road Charles Town packhorsemen followed back from the Lower Cherokee towns with deerskins. The abandoned town hosted its one great council on 2 July 1755, when Governor James Glen met Old Hop, the lame First Beloved Man of Chota, and Attakullakulla, called the Little Carpenter and counted the finest Cherokee orator of his day; the two chiefs acknowledged British sovereignty over the Cherokee lands in South Carolina, then put at 360,000 square miles. The concession drew lasting anger from Cherokee traditionalists, and within three years the Lower Towns were at war. In 1769 the valley was included in the new Ninety-Six District. Thomas Chappell then ran a ferry on the Saluda and built a bridge there in 1792; when the bridge was lost in 1800, the crossing went back to a ferry.
zh:
萨卢达地处萨卢达河的皮德蒙特河谷；河水奔流约二百英里，与布罗德河汇成康加里河，再经桑蒂河注入大西洋。萨卢达旧城留有低矮土丘、广场和压纹陶器，是约950年至1550年间庙丘时期的农业村落。1444年，这片河谷还是密西西比后期的玉米之乡，浅滩之间由小路相连，卡罗来纳商人后来把这些小路走成了切罗基商道。

17世纪末，一支被记作萨卢达的人占据旧城，可能是肖尼人的一支，但到1712年前已北迁。1730年，乔治·亨特的测绘标出穿谷而过的切罗基商道，查尔斯顿马帮沿这条路从切罗基下镇运回鹿皮。1755年7月2日，这座废城迎来唯一一次重要会盟：詹姆斯·格伦总督会见乔塔镇跛足的「第一受敬人」老霍普，和人称「小木匠」、被推为当时第一演说家的阿塔库拉；两位酋长承认英国对南卡罗来纳境内切罗基土地的主权，当时估计有36万平方英里。这一让步长期激起切罗基守旧派的愤怒，不出三年下镇便卷入战火。1769年，河谷划入新设的九十六司法区。此后托马斯·查普尔在萨卢达河上经营渡口，1792年又在河上修桥；桥1800年被毁后，渡河重新改用渡船。

en:
Cusabo is the low-country coast around Charleston Harbor, where the Ashley, Cooper and Wando meet the Atlantic behind a chain of sea islands. In 1444 the inlets and islands belonged to the Kiawah, Etiwan, Kussoe, Stono and their kin, villages later grouped together as the Cusabo. Five of them shared a language that matched none of the Algonquian, Iroquoian, Muskogean or Siouan tongues around them.

Early wars with the Kussoe and the Stono ended in land cessions and a token tribute of deerskins. The English founded Charles Town at Albemarle Point in 1670 and moved it in 1680 to the defensible peninsula between the Ashley and Cooper; by the 1690s it was one of the largest towns in North America. The Cusabo fought for the colony in the Tuscarora War of 1711, and after the Yamasee War of 1715 most survivors joined the Catawba or the Muscogee. Rice and indigo and the Atlantic slave trade made Charles Town rich: by 1770 its 11,000 people, half of them enslaved, made it the fourth-largest colonial port after Boston, New York and Philadelphia, and roughly four in ten of the enslaved Africans entering North America between 1700 and 1775 came through its harbor.
