Blackbeard blockaded the harbor for several days in May 1718 to obtain medicine for his crew. On 9 September 1739 the enslaved leader Jemmy led a band south from the Stono River for Spanish Florida, killing more than twenty whites before militia ran them down near the Edisto; the assembly answered with the harsh Negro Act of 1740.

On 28 June 1776 William Moultrie's palmetto-log fort on Sullivan's Island survived a day of British naval bombardment, the spongy logs absorbing the shot, while his gunners badly cut up Peter Parker's squadron; the blue flag his men flew became the basis of South Carolina's colors. The British returned in force in 1780, and from 29 March to 12 May Benjamin Lincoln was besieged in the town; his surrender with some 5,500 men was the heaviest American defeat of the war. Charles Town remained the British base in the South until the garrison sailed out in December 1782, and on 13 August 1783 the town was incorporated as Charleston.
zh:
库萨博是查尔斯顿湾周围的低地海岸，阿什利河、库珀河与万多河在一列海岛的屏护下汇入大西洋。1444年，各处海湾和岛屿属于基亚瓦、埃蒂万、库索、斯托诺等相互联姻的村落，后来被统称为库萨博人。其中五个族群共用一种语言，却与周边的阿尔冈昆、易洛魁、马斯科吉和苏语都不相属。

早期与库索人、斯托诺人的交战，以割地和缴纳象征性的鹿皮贡赋告终。英国人1670年在阿尔伯马尔角建立查尔斯镇，1680年迁至阿什利河与库珀河之间易守难攻的半岛，到1690年代已是北美最大的城镇之一。库萨博人1711年替殖民地出征图斯卡罗拉人，1715年亚马西战争之后，多数幸存者投奔卡托巴人或马斯科吉人。稻米、靛蓝和奴隶贸易堆起查尔斯镇的财富：1770年全城11000名居民中半数为奴，港口规模在殖民地中仅次于波士顿、纽约和费城，居第四位；1700至1775年间进入北美的黑奴约有四成从这里上岸。1718年5月，黑胡子封锁海湾数日，为的是给他的手下弄到药品。1739年9月9日，黑奴领袖杰米率众从斯托诺河南下，逃往西属佛罗里达，沿途杀死二十多名白人，后在埃迪斯托附近被民兵剿灭；随后便是严苛的1740年《黑人法》。

1776年6月28日，威廉·穆尔特里在沙利文岛用棕榈木筑起的要塞顶住了整整一天的英军舰队炮击，松软的木料吸住炮弹，守军的炮火反而重创彼得·帕克的舰队；穆尔特里部下所竖的蓝旗，后来成为南卡罗来纳旗帜的底本。1780年英军大举重来，自3月29日围城至5月12日，本杰明·林肯率城及约5500人投降，这是整场战争中美军最惨重的失败。查尔斯镇一直作为英军在南方的基地，直到1782年12月守军登船撤离；1783年8月13日城镇设市，定名查尔斯顿。

en:
Waccamaw is the blackwater coast behind Winyah Bay, where the Waccamaw and Great Pee Dee rivers draw near the channels of the Sampit and Black before all four enter the bay. Waccamaw towns stood on both the Waccamaw and the Pee Dee, with maize fields beyond the canoe landings; Mississippian farmers had brought maize to the coast around 1150-1200. Their trails and canoe routes met those of the Winyah, Sampit, Sewee, Santee and Pedee. In 1444 no European sail had entered Winyah Bay, and this river world belonged to its canoe towns.

A Spanish expedition under Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón reached the coast in 1526 and tried to plant a settlement, but fever and a revolt of its enslaved Africans ended it within months. Epidemic disease thinned the Waccamaw before the English recorded them; a Carolina census counted 610 in 1715. The Cheraw drew them into the Yamasee War that year, a small war in 1720 left sixty of them dead or captured, and in 1755 the Waccamaw joined the Catawba of King Haigler. Elisha Screven platted Georgetown on Winyah Bay in 1729, and its river lands became indigo and rice plantations worked by enslaved Africans; the Winyah Indigo Society ran a school from 1757 on dues paid in indigo, and the Georgetown planter Thomas Lynch Jr. signed the Declaration of Independence. The Revolution made the district Francis Marion's ground. From Snow's Island in the Pee Dee swamps the 'Swamp Fox' led four attacks on Georgetown, and Banastre Tarleton pursued him twenty-six miles through a swamp only to give up, saying the devil himself could not catch that old fox. While Marion's men raided British supply lines, the port shipped rice and stores to Nathanael Greene's army.
zh:
沃卡莫是温亚湾后方的黑水河滨海岸，沃卡莫河、大皮迪河与桑皮特河、布莱克河的水道在入海前彼此逼近，最终一同注入湾中。沃卡莫人的城镇分布在沃卡莫河与皮迪河两岸，独木舟码头之外是玉米田；约1150至1200年，密西西比文化的农民把玉米带到沿海。他们的林间路和独木舟航路与温亚人、桑皮特人、西维人、桑蒂人和皮迪人相接。1444年，还没有欧洲船帆进入温亚湾，这片河流世界属于驾独木舟的村镇。

1526年，卢卡斯·巴斯克斯·德·艾永率西班牙远征队抵达这段海岸，试图建立殖民地，但热病和随行非洲奴隶的起事几个月内便终结了它。疫病使沃卡莫人口锐减，此后英国人才留下他们的记录：1715年卡罗来纳人口调查记有610人。同年切罗人把他们拖进亚马西战争，1720年的一场小仗又使六十人被杀或被俘，1755年沃卡莫人加入海格勒王为首的卡托巴人。1729年，伊莱沙·斯克里文在温亚湾畔规划乔治敦，河畔土地变成由非洲奴隶劳作的靛蓝和水稻种植园；温亚靛蓝协会从1757年起用以靛蓝缴纳的会费办学，乔治敦种植园主小托马斯·林奇后来在《独立宣言》上签字。独立战争中，这一带成了弗朗西斯·马里恩的战场。这位「沼泽之狐」以皮迪河沼泽中的斯诺岛为营地，四次进攻乔治敦；巴纳斯特·塔尔顿追他穿过二十六英里沼泽仍无功而返，说连魔鬼也抓不住这只老狐狸。在马里昂所部袭扰英军补给线的同时，乔治敦港把大米和军需运往纳撒内尔·格林的军队。

en:
The Yadkin rises in the Blue Ridge and winds more than two hundred miles through the Carolina Piedmont to join the Pee Dee, its valley a broad run of oak woods and canebreaks between the mountains and the coastal plain. The river's name is a Siouan word, perhaps meaning 'place of big trees'. At the Trading Ford the shallows let the Great Indian Trading Path cross between the Appalachians and the Chesapeake, and in 1444 the banks above it held the palisaded corn towns of the Saura and other Catawban-speaking peoples, with the Tutelo and Keyauwee nearby.

Two Virginians, James Needham and Gabriel Arthur, crossed the upper Yadkin in 1673 on their way to the Tomahittans beyond the Occaneechi middlemen. Seneca raids soon drove the Saura south to the Pee Dee, and the survivors were adopted into the Catawba. Scots-Irish and German farmers followed down the Great Wagon Road: Rowan County was formed in 1753 and Salisbury was laid out at the old ford as its seat. The same year twelve Moravian brethren arrived to open their Wachovia tract, building Bethabara and stockading it in 1756; the planned town of Salem followed in 1766. The provincials' own post, Fort Dobbs, named for Governor Arthur Dobbs, went up on the frontier in 1756, and its garrison beat off a Cherokee attack on 27 February 1760.

The valley's best-known settler was Daniel Boone, whose family brought him to a farm near Mocksville in 1750. He married Rebecca Bryan of the Yadkin on 14 August 1756 and earned his keep as a market hunter, leaving each autumn on the long hunts that carried him farther west. When Cherokee raids swept the valley in 1759, his family fled with their neighbours to the Bethabara stockade. In May 1769 he set out from the Yadkin for Kentucky, and in 1775 he blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap and founded Boonesborough; by the end of the century more than 200,000 settlers had followed his trace over the mountains.
zh:
亚德金河发源于蓝岭山脉，蜿蜒二百多英里穿过卡罗来纳皮德蒙特，汇入皮迪河，河谷是群山与沿海平原之间一片遍布橡树林和芦苇荡的宽阔低地。河名来自苏语，一说意为「大树之地」。河上的贸易浅滩水浅可涉，「大印第安商路」从这里过河，连接阿巴拉契亚山区与切萨皮克；1444年，浅滩上游两岸分布着绍拉人等卡托巴语族居民设有栅栏的玉米镇，附近还住着图特罗人和基奥维人。

1673年，弗吉尼亚人詹姆斯·尼达姆和加布里埃尔·阿瑟穿过亚德金河上游，去寻找奥卡内基中间商背后的托马希坦人。塞内卡人的袭击很快把绍拉人南逼到皮迪河畔，幸存者并入卡托巴人。苏格兰—爱尔兰裔和德意志农户随后沿大篷车道而来：1753年设立罗安县，索尔兹伯里就建在旧日浅滩旁，充任县治。同年，十二名摩拉维亚弟兄会成员抵达，开辟瓦霍维亚居留地，建起贝塔巴拉并于1756年围上木栅；1766年又建成规划整齐的塞勒姆镇。殖民地方面在边疆筑起名叫多布斯堡的据点，以总督阿瑟·多布斯命名，1756年动工，1760年2月27日守军击退了切罗基人的进攻。

谷中最出名的居民是丹尼尔·布恩。1750年，全家带着他迁居莫克斯维尔附近的农庄；1756年8月14日，他在亚德金娶了丽贝卡·布赖恩，以打猎卖皮货为生，每年秋天加入一次比一次深入西方的「长猎」。1759年切罗基人袭扰河谷时，他一家和邻居一起躲进贝塔巴拉的木栅。1769年5月，他从亚德金出发前往肯塔基；1775年，他率人开辟穿过坎伯兰隘口的荒野之路，建立布恩斯伯勒。到18世纪末，已有二十多万人沿他标出的小路翻山进入肯塔基。

en:
The Waxhaws are a rolling stretch of piedmont meadow and canebrake on the upper Catawba, around the creek bottoms that now form the border between the two Carolinas. They take their name from the Waxhaw, a small Siouan people called the Wysacky by some writers, kin in language and marriage to the Catawba and Wateree; their women worked the cornfields in the bottoms and their hunters took deer on the oak savanna. In 1444 this was unvisited border country, and when the Spaniard Juan Pardo passed through on his inland marches in the 1560s the villages were still in place.

The Waxhaw sent twenty-seven warriors under their own Captain Jack with John Barnwell against the Tuscarora in 1711, wading through a swamp to storm Fort Narhontes before slipping away to sell the slaves they had taken. Four years later they joined the Yamasee rising against Carolina, and when it failed the Catawba made their own peace and fell on their kinsmen, breaking the Waxhaw as a people; the survivors drifted to the Cheraw or south with the Yamasee. Scots-Irish farmers moving down the Great Wagon Road took up the empty land, and on 15 March 1767 a couple newly arrived from Ulster had a son here, Andrew Jackson; just which side of the future state line he was born on was argued for decades.

The Revolutionary War reached the Waxhaws on 29 May 1780, when Banastre Tarleton's British Legion rode down Abraham Buford's Virginia regiment on the march and kept killing after the first calls to surrender; 113 of Buford's 420 men died in the field. 'Tarleton's quarter' became the backcountry name for no quarter, and the fight swelled the patriot militia. Jackson, then thirteen, served as a courier with his brother Robert, and the British captured both boys in April 1781; when he refused to polish an officer's boots, the officer cut his head and hand with a sword. His mother died nursing American prisoners in Charleston harbor later that year, leaving him an orphan at fourteen, and in 1784 he left the Waxhaws to read law in Salisbury.
zh:
瓦克斯霍是卡托巴河上游一片起伏的皮德蒙特草甸与芦苇地，地处今南北卡罗来纳州界一带的溪边低地。地名来自苏语小部落瓦克斯霍人，有些文献写作维萨基人，他们在语言和姻亲上都与卡托巴人、沃特里人相近；妇女在低地里种玉米，猎人到橡树稀树草原上猎鹿。1444年，这里还是外人未至的边地；到1560年代西班牙人胡安·帕尔多内陆远征经过时，各村落仍在原处。

1711年，瓦克斯霍人派出27名战士，在自己的杰克上尉率领下随约翰·巴恩韦尔出征图斯卡罗拉人；他们涉过沼泽攻下纳洪茨堡，随后不辞而别，去卖掉掳来的奴隶。四年后，他们加入雅马西人对卡罗来纳的起义；起义失败后，卡托巴人单独议和，反过来攻打这支亲族，把瓦克斯霍部落打散，幸存者或投奔绍拉人，或随雅马西人南迁。沿大篷车道南下的苏格兰—爱尔兰裔农户占下空置的土地。1767年3月15日，一对刚从阿尔斯特迁来的夫妇在这里生下儿子安德鲁·杰克逊；他究竟出生在后来的州界哪一边，争论了几十年。

独立战争在1780年5月29日打到瓦克斯霍：巴纳斯特·塔尔顿的英军军团追上行军中的亚伯拉罕·布福德弗吉尼亚团，在对方初次请降之后仍不停手，布福德麾下420人中有113人死在战场上。「塔尔顿的饶命」成了山乡对杀降的说法，这一仗让爱国者民兵的队伍迅速壮大。当时13岁的杰克逊和哥哥罗伯特当起了信使，1781年4月兄弟二人被英军俘获；他拒绝给一名军官擦靴，被那军官用军刀砍伤头部和手。同年晚些时候，母亲在查尔斯顿港护理美军战俘时病故，14岁的杰克逊成了孤儿。1784年，他离开瓦克斯霍，前往索尔兹伯里学习法律。

en:
The lower Cape Fear River opens to the Atlantic under the treacherous Frying Pan Shoals, and the country round its mouth was known to its native people as Chicora. The small Cape Fear Indians, whose language was probably Siouan, planted riverside fields round Necoes, their only named village, about twenty miles above the mouth, took fish and oysters from the estuary, and carried deerskins through the longleaf-pine forests that met the coast. Once perhaps a thousand strong, they had no European neighbours in 1444; Giovanni da Verrazzano, sailing for France, became the first European known to sight the headland in 1524.

In 1585 Richard Grenville's fleet, bound for Roanoke, was embayed behind the headland, and the crew's fear of wrecking gave Cape Fear its English name. Barbadian planters planted Charles Towne on the west bank in 1664, but war with the Indians over the English slave trade and a great hurricane emptied it within a few years; the same colonists' next venture was Charleston, far to the south. A count in 1715 found only 206 Cape Fear left. Some had marched with South Carolina militia against the Tuscarora three years earlier, and the survivors now drifted up the Pee Dee to settle inland from Charleston. Brunswick Town, founded in 1726, was the first lasting settlement and housed two provincial governors; Wilmington, laid out at the river fork in the 1730s and named for the Earl of Wilmington, shipped out the pine woods' pitch, tar and turpentine, and by 1767 enslaved Africans made up more than three fifths of the lower river's people. In 1765 Stamp Act crowds made the stamp agent resign and stopped river shipping rather than clear vessels on stamped paper, and on 27 February 1776 patriot militia scattered a loyalist Highland charge at Moore's Creek Bridge, eighteen miles above Wilmington. A British raid burned Brunswick later that year, leaving its St Philip's Church and the governors' mansion Russellborough in ruins, and the town was never rebuilt.
zh:
开普菲尔河下游在凶险的煎锅浅滩旁注入大西洋，河口一带在当地原住民口中叫奇科拉。人数不多的开普菲尔印第安人语言可能属苏语族，在河口以上约二十英里处唯一有名可考的村落尼科兹周围耕种河畔田地，在河口湾捕鱼采蚝，又穿过与海岸相连的长叶松林贩运鹿皮。他们一度可能有上千之众，1444年时四周还没有欧洲邻居；为法兰西效力的乔瓦尼·达·韦拉扎诺1524年成为已知第一个望见这座岬角的欧洲人。

1585年，前往罗阿诺克的理查德·格伦维尔船队被困在岬角内侧，船员惧怕沉船，海角便有了菲尔角（Cape Fear，意为「恐惧角」）这个英文名。巴巴多斯种植园主1664年在西岸建起查尔斯城，却因英国人贩卖印第安奴隶而与当地人开战，又逢一场大飓风，几年之内定居点便空无一人；这批殖民者再往南，建起了远处的查尔斯顿。1715年的人口调查只点到206名开普菲尔人。此前三年，他们中还有人随南卡罗来纳民兵出征图斯卡罗拉人；幸存者这时沿皮迪河而上，最终在查尔斯顿以北的内陆落脚。1726年建立的布伦瑞克镇是第一处存续下来的定居点，住过两任殖民地总督；威尔明顿1730年代在河汊处开辟，以威尔明顿伯爵的封号得名，输出松林出产的沥青、焦油和松节油，到1767年，被奴役的非洲人已占下游人口的五分之三以上。1765年，抗议印花税的人群逼印花税官辞职，宁可让河上航运停摆，也不用贴了印花的文件为船只清关；1776年2月27日，爱国者民兵在威尔明顿以北十八英里的穆尔溪桥击溃效忠派高地人的冲锋。同年的英军突袭烧毁布伦瑞克镇，圣腓力教堂和总督府拉塞尔伯勒只剩残垣，镇子再未重建。

en:
Roanoke Island lies between the Albemarle and Croatan sounds behind the Outer Banks, the centre of a Carolina Algonquian world: the Roanoke on the island, the Chowanoke and Weapemeoc on the mainland rivers. Their palisaded towns of cedar-bark houses stood by cornfields and fish weirs, canoes linked the sounds in trade, and kinship and occasional war tied the villages to the Tuscarora inland. In 1444 nothing on these shores foreshadowed the coming of the English.

Walter Raleigh's captains Philip Amadas and Arthur Barlowe landed in 1584 and claimed the island for England. Two Croatans, Manteo and Wanchese, sailed to England with them; Manteo crossed again with Governor John White and was christened on Roanoke in 1587, the first Native American received into the Church of England. An earlier fort, raised by Ralph Lane in 1585, had lasted a year before short supplies and fighting with the Roanoke drove him out with Francis Drake. White's settlers were bound for Chesapeake Bay, but their pilot Simon Fernandes put them ashore on Roanoke and left them there. On 18 August White's granddaughter Virginia Dare was born, the first English child in an English American colony. White sailed home for supplies, and the war with Spain kept him away until 1590, when he found the palisade standing empty with 'CROATOAN' carved on a post. Rough seas cut short the search, and the settlers were never found.

Virginians began settling the Albemarle shore in the 1650s, and in 1677 the colonists drove out the proprietors' customs officers in Culpeper's Rebellion. The Tuscarora War of 1711-13 made the sounds a battleground, with the Chowanoke and Tom Blount's northern Tuscarora on the English side; the peace of 1718 settled the remaining Tuscarora on a reserve on the Roanoke River. Edenton, on Queen Anne's Creek, was the young province's capital until the 1740s, and in 1774 fifty-one of its women, led by Penelope Barker, signed the tea boycott remembered as the Edenton Tea Party.
zh:
罗阿诺克岛在外滩群岛后方，扼守阿尔伯马尔湾与克罗阿坦湾之间，是卡罗来纳阿尔冈昆世界的中心：岛上住着罗阿诺克人，大陆各河畔住着乔瓦诺克人和维佩米奥克人。他们的城镇围以栅栏、以雪松树皮盖屋，旁边就是玉米地和鱼梁；独木舟在各海湾间往来贸易，姻亲与断断续续的战事又把这些村落同内陆的图斯卡罗拉人连在一起。1444年的海岸上，还没有任何英格兰人将至的迹象。

沃尔特·雷利派出的船长菲利普·阿马达斯和阿瑟·巴洛1584年登岛，以英格兰名义将其领有。两名克罗阿坦人曼蒂奥和万切斯随船前往英格兰；曼蒂奥后来又随总督约翰·怀特再渡大西洋，1587年在罗阿诺克受洗，成为第一个加入英格兰国教会的美洲原住民。更早时拉尔夫·莱恩在1585年筑起要塞，只维持了一年，便因补给不足和与罗阿诺克人交战而随弗朗西斯·德雷克撤走。怀特这批移民本要前往切萨皮克湾，领航员西芒·费尔南德斯却把他们送上罗阿诺克岛，自己扬帆离去。8月18日，怀特的外孙女弗吉尼亚·戴尔出生，是英格兰人美洲殖民地出生的第一个英格兰婴儿。怀特回英格兰筹办补给，对西班牙的战争使他直到1590年才得以返回，却只见栅栏仍在、村落已空，一根木桩上刻着「克罗阿坦」（CROATOAN）。风浪迫使搜寻草草结束，移民再也没有被找到。

1650年代起，弗吉尼亚人陆续到阿尔伯马尔湾岸定居；1677年，殖民者起事赶走业主政府的海关官员，史称卡尔佩珀暴动。1711至1713年的图斯卡罗拉战争把各海湾变成战场，乔瓦诺克人和汤姆·布朗特率领的北部图斯卡罗拉人站在英格兰一边；1718年的和约把余下的图斯卡罗拉人安置在罗阿诺克河畔的保留地。安妮女王溪畔的伊登顿是这个年轻省份的首府，直到1740年代；1774年，镇上51名妇女在佩内洛普·巴克带领下签署抵制英茶的倡议书，即「伊登顿茶会」。

en:
Tutelo country is the mountain headwater land of southwest Virginia: the upper Roanoke where the Staunton and Dan rivers join, the gorges of the New River, and the Big Sandy, which the Tutelo called the Totteroy, beyond the Allegheny ridges. They spoke an eastern Siouan tongue close to those of their Monacan and Manahoac kinsmen, built their towns on river terraces, and buried their dead in earthen mounds. In 1444 mountain Indian roads threaded these high valleys, with the Monacan to the east and the closely related Saponi beside them.

Englishmen first crossed these mountains in 1671. The Batts and Fallam expedition, sent out by Abraham Wood, noted 'Totero Town' on the upper Roanoke near where Salem later stood and crossed the divide to the New River. Iroquois raiders were already driving the Tutelo out of their valleys: they took refuge on islands at the Roanoke forks above the Occaneechi, joined the Saponi, and later withdrew as far as the Yadkin headwaters in North Carolina. Governor Spotswood of Virginia settled them with the Saponi beside Fort Christanna, his Indian mission school, and the 1722 Treaty of Albany ended the Iroquois attacks. In the 1730s they moved north to Shamokin in Pennsylvania under the Oneida overseer Shickellamy, whose wife was Tutelo, and in 1753 the Cayuga formally adopted them. They built Coreorgonel below Cayuga Lake, near later Ithaca, and lived there until Sullivan's expedition burned the town in 1779. The survivors followed the Cayuga to the Grand River in Canada.
zh:
图特洛人的家园是弗吉尼亚西南部的山地河源地带：斯汤顿河与丹河在此汇合成罗阿诺克河上游，新河切出深峡，阿勒格尼山脊以西的大桑迪河被他们称作「托特罗伊河」。图特洛人操一支东苏语方言，与亲族莫纳坎人和马纳霍克人的语言相近；他们把村镇建在河流阶地上，将死者葬入土丘坟冢。1444年，山间印第安小路穿行在这些高山河谷之间，莫纳坎人居于其东，语言相通的萨波尼人紧邻其侧。

英格兰人最早在1671年越过这些山岭。受亚伯拉罕·伍德派遣的巴茨与法勒姆远征队在罗阿诺克河上游、后来塞勒姆兴起之处记下「托特罗镇」，并西行抵达新河。这时易洛魁袭击者已在把图特洛人逐出河谷：他们先避居罗阿诺克河汇流处的岛上，住在奥卡尼奇人之地的北缘，与萨波尼人合居，后来又远退到北卡罗来纳的亚德金河源头。弗吉尼亚总督斯波茨伍德把他们和萨波尼人一同安置在克里斯蒂安娜堡旁他兴办的印第安传教学校附近，1722年的《奥尔巴尼条约》结束了易洛魁人的攻击。1730年代，他们北迁宾夕法尼亚的沙莫金，归附奥奈达管理人希基拉米，他的妻子就是图特洛人；1753年卡尤加人正式接纳他们。他们在卡尤加湖下游、后来的伊萨卡附近建起科雷奥戈内尔村，直到1779年沙利文远征军焚毁该村。幸存者随卡尤加人前往加拿大的格兰德河。

en:
The Moratuc, for whom the middle Roanoke River was also named, are usually counted as Algonquian speakers. They farmed its bottomlands and kept fishing weirs in the current. In 1444 their villages stood among the Chowanoke, Mangoak and Weapemeoc on the coastal plain south of the Chesapeake, joined by river travel and the diplomacy of neighbouring peoples; no European had yet entered the valley.

The first English force to see it came from Roanoke Island in 1586. After Ralph Lane's men seized the Chowanoke chief Menatonon at Choanoac, Menatonon's son Skiko described metal at Chaunis Temoatan to the west. Lane took forty men up the Moratuc for roughly a hundred miles, but Pemisapan had warned the river villages. The English found empty houses and stripped stores, ran out of food and turned back; Lane abandoned Roanoke Island later that year. Planters moved up the Roanoke after the Tuscarora War and founded Halifax at the head of navigation in 1757. On 12 April 1776 North Carolina's provincial congress met there and adopted the Halifax Resolves, the first official call by an American colony for independence.
zh:
莫拉托克（莫拉图克）人通常被认为操阿尔冈昆语，住在罗阿诺克河中游，这段河道也曾以他们为名。他们在河畔低地耕作，在水流中设置鱼堰。1444年，他们的村庄位于切萨皮克湾以南的沿海平原，处在乔瓦诺克人、曼戈阿克人和韦阿佩梅奥克人之间，靠河道往来和邻部外交彼此联系；欧洲人还没有进入这条河谷。

第一支见到这里的英格兰队伍来自罗阿诺克岛。1586年，拉尔夫·莱恩的人在乔阿诺阿克掳走乔瓦诺克首领梅纳托农，梅纳托农之子斯基科向掳走父亲的英格兰人谈到西方乔尼斯·特莫阿坦的金属。莱恩带四十人溯莫拉托克河上行约一百英里，佩米萨潘却已向河畔各村示警。英格兰人只见到空屋和被搬空的粮仓，断粮后折返；莱恩同年放弃罗阿诺克岛。塔斯卡洛拉战争后，种植园主沿罗阿诺克河上迁，1757年在通航起点建立哈利法克斯。1776年4月12日，北卡罗来纳省议会在此通过《哈利法克斯决议》，这是英属北美殖民地第一份正式要求独立的文件。

en:
The peninsula between the Rappahannock and Potomac rivers held two Algonquian peoples in 1444. The Rappahannock had thirteen villages along their river, with their chief town Topahanocke; the Doeg lived higher up the Potomac around Tauxenent and kept a hamlet at the place later called Quantico. Both groups planted corn, worked tidal fishing grounds and used shell beads in exchanges among the coastal villages.

English contact produced a striking early Virginia scene. In May 1607 the Rappahannock weroance met English explorers, and George Percy saw him come to the shore playing a flute, his face painted blue and sprinkled with silver, with a red deer-hair crown and bird-claw earrings. After John Smith's capture that December, the Rappahannock brought him to Topahanocke to learn whether he came from the earlier people who had attacked them. Colonial patents opened the Northern Neck in the 1650s: the Rappahannock deeded river land, lost Taweeren in a colonial brawl, had their reserve narrowed and by 1669 had withdrawn to the Mattaponi headwaters. In July 1675 Doeg men took hogs from the planter Thomas Mathew in a payment dispute. The colonists' pursuit killed Doeg and Susquehannock alike, Nathaniel Bacon's militia marched into Maryland, and the conflict became Bacon's Rebellion in 1676.
zh:
1444年，拉帕汉诺克河与波托马克河之间的半岛上住着两支阿尔冈昆人。拉帕汉诺克人沿河有十三座村庄，首镇是托帕哈诺克；多格人住在波托马克河更上游，以托克塞嫩为中心，在后来得名匡蒂科的地方还有小村。两族都种玉米，在潮汐水域捕鱼，并用贝珠同滨海村落交易。

英格兰人到来后，拉帕汉诺克人留下了弗吉尼亚早期很有画面感的一幕。1607年5月，他们的首领会见英格兰探险者，乔治·珀西看到他吹着笛走到岸边，脸涂蓝色并撒有银色饰物，头戴红鹿毛冠，耳挂鸟爪耳饰。同年12月约翰·史密斯被俘后，拉帕汉诺克人把他带到托帕哈诺克，辨认他是不是早先袭击者的同族。1650年代，殖民者开始在北内克半岛申领土地，拉帕汉诺克人立约让出河畔土地，新任首领在一场殖民者斗殴中丧命，保留地也被压缩，到1669年已退往马塔波尼河源头。1675年7月，多格人因债务纠纷赶走种植园主托马斯·马修的猪；殖民者追击时连多格人和萨斯奎汉诺克人一起杀，纳撒尼尔·培根的民团随即攻入马里兰，冲突在1676年演变为培根起义。

en:
Calicula covers the upper Monongahela, where the West Fork and Tygart Valley rivers join and the water runs north between forested ridges toward the forks at Pittsburgh. Its Lenape name describes a bank that slips and falls into the river. Around 1050, Monongahela farmers began laying out ordered villages, often ringed with palisades, some holding fifty to a hundred houses; they grew maize and beans in the bottoms and traded stone and shell through networks that reached toward the Ohio. In 1444 their villages still filled the hill valleys, untouched by direct European contact. By the 1620s or 1630s every one of them was gone. Disease, the droughts of 1587-1589 and 1607-1612, and Haudenosaunee and Lenape raids over fur-country hunting grounds emptied the upper valley, which became a march between Native warriors, French claim and Virginia.

The first cabins went up after Britain's 1763 victory. Zackquill and David Morgan entered the country about 1767, and Zackquill built Fort Morgan at the mouth of Decker's Creek in 1772; Forts Pierpont, Coburn, Dinwiddie and Martin rose on the same stretch of river within five years. War soon followed the surveyors. After Daniel Greathouse's band carried out the Yellow Creek massacre in 1774 and opened Dunmore's War, frightened families 'forted up': at least a hundred blockhouses and palisaded stations stood across the Monongahela valley, and as many as eighty families crowded into Prickett's Fort during the worst alarms. The fort was never attacked, though militiamen who had left it were killed elsewhere. Virginia formed Monongalia County in 1776, and in October 1785 the assembly marked out fifty acres of Zackquill Morgan's land at Decker's Creek as Morgan's Town. Flatboats carried the valley's grain and timber north, and in 1817 Pennsylvania chartered the Monongahela Navigation Company to lock and dam the river.
zh:
卡利库拉覆盖莫农加希拉河上游：西支流与泰加特谷支流在此汇合，河水穿过林木覆盖的山脊，向北流向匹兹堡河口。河名来自莱纳佩语，形容河岸不断塌落入水。约1050年起，莫农加希拉文化的农人在此建起布局齐整、常以木栅环绕的村落，最大的有五十到上百座房屋；他们在河洲上种玉米和豆类，用石器、贝壳通过通往俄亥俄方向的商网交换。1444年，他们的村落仍遍布丘陵河谷，未与欧洲人直接接触。到1620至1630年代，这些村落已无一留存。疫病、1587至1589年和1607至1612年的大旱，再加上易洛魁人与莱纳佩人为争夺毛皮猎场发动的袭扰，把上游河谷腾空，使它变成原住民战士、法国领属主张与弗吉尼亚之间的边地。

英国1763年获胜后，第一批木屋才建起来。扎奎尔·摩根与戴维·摩根约在1767年进入此地，扎奎尔1772年在德克斯溪口建起摩根堡；五年之间，皮尔庞特堡、科本堡、丁威迪堡和马丁堡也在同一段河岸相继立起。测量员身后很快跟着战争。1774年，丹尼尔·格雷特豪斯一伙制造耶洛克里克惨案，引爆邓莫尔战争，受惊的家庭纷纷「入堡」：莫农加希拉河谷中竖起至少一百座碉堡和木栅据点，最紧张时仅普里基特堡就挤进八十户人家。这座要塞本身从未受到攻击，从堡中应调外出的民兵却有死在别处的。弗吉尼亚1776年设立莫农加利亚县，1785年10月，议会在扎奎尔·摩根位于德克斯溪的土地上划出五十英亩建立摩根镇。河谷出产的粮食和木材搭平底船北运，1817年宾夕法尼亚又特许成立莫农加希拉航运公司，在河上修闸筑坝。

en:
The Manahoac country is the northern Virginia piedmont above the falls of the Rappahannock, the wooded upland between the Fall Line and the Blue Ridge through which the Rappahannock and its Rapidan branch run. Its people were a loose confederacy of Siouan-speaking bands, perhaps a thousand strong in all: Mahaskahod below the meeting of the two rivers, Hassinunga at the forks, and Stegara farthest upstream on the Rapidan. They were leagued with their Monacan kinsmen to the south, at war with the Powhatan below the falls and with the Iroquois raiders who came from beyond the Potomac. In 1444 the falls still closed their hill country to every stranger from the coast.

John Smith met a large Manahoac party above the Rappahannock falls in 1608 and was told of seven villages inland. In 1656 their bowmen, with the Nahyssan and a mountain people called the Richahhecrian, defeated Virginia militia and their Pamunkey allies at the Battle of Bloody Run, where the Pamunkey leader Totopotomoi was killed. Beaver Wars raids and disease then broke the confederacy: a count in 1669 found only fifty bowmen left, and when John Lederer crossed the country in 1671 the villages were gone and the Seneca already claimed it as their hunting ground. Survivors joined the Monacan and then the Tutelo and Saponi. A Stegaraki band appeared at Fort Christanna, Governor Spotswood's Indian school south of the James, and the Ontponea were heard of for the last time a few years later. After 1728 the name Manahoac disappears from the records.
zh:
马纳霍克人的家园在拉帕汉诺克河瀑布线以上的弗吉尼亚北部皮德蒙特，即瀑布线与蓝岭山脉之间林木覆盖的丘陵，拉帕汉诺克河与其支流拉皮丹河穿流其间。他们是若干操苏语部落组成的松散联盟，总人口约有一千：两河汇流处下方的马哈斯卡霍德、住在汇流处附近的哈西宁加、拉皮丹河上位置最靠上游的斯特加拉。他们与南方的亲族莫纳坎人结盟，同瀑布以下的波瓦坦人交战，还要抵御波托马克河以北来袭的易洛魁人。1444年，瀑布仍把海岸方向的一切外来者挡在这片山地之外。

1608年，约翰·史密斯在拉帕汉诺克河瀑布上方遇到一大群马纳霍克人，得知内陆有他们的七座村镇。1656年，他们的弓箭手会同纳赫桑人和一支被称为里卡赫克里安的山地部族，在血溪之战中击败弗吉尼亚民兵及其帕蒙基盟军，帕蒙基首领托托波托莫伊战死。海狸战争的袭击和疫病随后击垮了这个联盟：1669年的一次人口清点只剩五十名弓箭手；1671年约翰·莱德勒穿过这片土地时，村镇已经不见，塞内卡人已把它称作自己的猎场。幸存者先后投奔莫纳坎人、图特洛人和萨波尼人。一支斯特加拉基人出现在詹姆斯河以南、斯波茨伍德总督兴办的印第安人学校克里斯蒂安娜堡，翁特波尼亚人最后一次露面则在数年之后。1728年以后，「马纳霍克」之名从记载中消失。

en:
Patawomac is the upper Potomac highland country. The North and South Branches wind between Allegheny ridges, and at Wills Creek the valley opens a gap toward the place later called Cumberland, where river fords meet trails across the mountains. The Great Indian Warpath and other Native paths carried hunters, traders and war parties from these valleys to the Susquehanna, Shenandoah, Monongahela and Ohio countries. In 1444 no colonial boundary crossed the ridges; Susquehannock, Piscataway, Delaware and other parties used the country as hunting ground and passage, and no European town stood above Wills Creek.

John Smith entered and mapped the Potomac in 1608, but the upper valley remained a Native corridor for another century and a half. Around 1750 Thomas Cresap opened a trading post at Wills Creek, and with the Delaware chief Nemacolin he cut a packhorse road across the Alleghenies to Redstone Creek on the Monongahela, known as Nemacolin's Path. Maryland militia built a stockade at the creek mouth in autumn 1754, renamed Fort Cumberland the next year; it became the westernmost British post in North America and the base for Edward Braddock's march against Fort Duquesne. Daniel Boone and Daniel Morgan drove supply wagons with the column. On 9 July 1755 the French and their Native allies destroyed Braddock's army on the Monongahela, more than 500 men were killed, and Braddock died of his wounds on the retreat; George Washington formed the rear guard and brought the survivors back to Cumberland. During the Revolutionary War the fort supplied the Continental Army's western department and held British prisoners from about 1778. In 1811 work began at Cumberland on the Cumberland Road, which carried wagon traffic west toward the Ohio.
zh:
波托马克是波托马克河上游高地。北支流与南支流的河谷穿行于阿利根尼群山之间，威尔斯溪一带的河谷打开一道山口，通向后来坎伯兰所在之地，河上徒涉点与翻山小径在这里相接。「大印第安战道」等原住民小路载着猎人、商人和征战队伍，从这些河谷通往萨斯奎汉纳、谢南多厄、莫农加希拉和俄亥俄方向。1444年时，还没有殖民地边界越过群山；萨斯奎汉诺克人、皮斯卡塔韦人、特拉华人及其他群体把这里当作猎场和通道，威尔斯溪以上没有欧洲人的城镇。

1608年，约翰·史密斯进入并测绘了波托马克河，但上游河谷在此后一个半世纪里仍是原住民通道。约1750年，托马斯·克雷萨普在威尔斯溪开设贸易站，并与特拉华酋长内马科林一起辟出一条驮马道，穿越阿利根尼山脉，通往莫农加希拉河上的雷德斯通溪，人称内马科林小道。1754年秋，马里兰民兵在溪口筑起木栅据点，次年改名坎伯兰堡；它成为英国在北美最西端的据点，也是爱德华·布雷多克进军迪凯纳堡的基地，丹尼尔·布恩和丹尼尔·摩根都在队伍里驾驶辎重车。1755年7月9日，法国人及其原住民盟军在莫农加希拉河畔击溃布雷多克的军队，五百余人战死，布雷多克本人在撤退途中伤重不治；乔治·华盛顿组织后卫，把幸存者带回坎伯兰。独立战争期间，这座堡垒为大陆军西部部门提供补给，约1778年起还关押英国战俘。1811年，通往西方俄亥俄方向的坎伯兰大道在坎伯兰动工。

en:
Nentego was the Nanticokes' own name, the 'Tidewater People'. The province is the lower reach of the river named for them, where marshy creeks open into Tangier Sound and Chesapeake Bay on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Algonquian-speaking chiefdoms, the Wicomoco, Monie and Manokin among them, kept riverside villages and traded through a network that reached peoples all around Chesapeake Bay. Chicacone, on the ground where Vienna later stood, was their largest town. In 1444 canoes moved between fishing weirs, cornfields and shellfish shallows, and the tidal river was the main road through the country.

John Smith sailed up the Nanticoke in 1608, mapped it and visited Chicacone, and beaver pelts soon drew the chiefdoms into alliance with the English of Maryland. Unnacokasimon, the Nanticoke ruler styled 'emperor' by the colonists, made peace in 1668, and in 1684 the colony marked out a reservation between Chicacoan Creek and the river; Vienna grew up beside it as a port for tobacco and shipbuilding. Settlement pressed harder, and the Nanticoke began a long staged withdrawal up the bay. After a multi-tribal gathering called to discuss a Shawnee plan against the settlers was surprised in 1742, the leaders were arrested, and in 1744 the Iroquois allowed the bands to settle along the Susquehanna and the Juniata. For years families kept walking their old path back to Delmarva to fish and gather fruit and nuts in season. The reserve was sold in 1768. In the Revolution the Nanticoke took the British side, and two hundred of them moved north to Fort Niagara in 1778; the British later settled them with the Iroquois on the Grand River in Ontario.
zh:
嫩特戈是楠蒂科克人的自称，意为「潮水之人」。本省即楠蒂科克河下游一带，马里兰东岸的沼泽河溪在这里汇入坦吉尔湾和切萨皮克湾。威科米科、莫尼、马诺金等说阿尔冈昆语的酋邦在河畔结村，贸易网络远及环切萨皮克湾的各个族群。最大的城镇奇卡科恩就在后来维也纳镇所在之处。1444年时，独木舟穿行于鱼梁、玉米田和盛产贝类的浅水之间，感潮河道就是穿越此地的主要道路。

约翰·史密斯1608年驶入楠蒂科克河，测绘河道并访问奇卡科恩；海狸皮很快把各酋邦带入与马里兰英人的同盟。被殖民地称作「皇帝」的首领乌纳科卡西蒙于1668年议和，1684年殖民地在奇卡科恩溪与楠蒂科克河之间划出保留地，维也纳就在旁边兴起，成为烟草和造船业的港口。定居者的挤压日甚，楠蒂科克人开始沿海湾一步步北迁。1742年，一场商议肖尼人攻英计划的跨部落集会遭查获，首领被捕；1744年易洛魁人允许他们到萨斯奎汉纳河与朱尼亚塔河一带居住。此后多年，各家仍沿古道走回德尔马瓦半岛，按时令捕鱼、采集果实和坚果。保留地于1768年售出。独立战争中楠蒂科克人站在英国一边，1778年两百人北迁尼亚加拉堡，后来英国人把他们和易洛魁人一起安置在安大略的格兰德河畔。

en: Honniasont is the name later French records gave to the forested upper Ohio country above the falls, across the ridges and river bottoms of eastern Ohio, western Pennsylvania and West Virginia. In 1444 the people called Oniasont or Honniasontkeronon lived among Fort Ancient and Monongahela villages of maize fields, palisades, hunting paths and ridge trails. Their language is uncertain, with Iroquoian and Ohio Valley Siouan links both proposed. European goods began reaching the valley by Native routes in the mid-1500s, before epidemics and the Beaver Wars emptied many settlements. During those wars of 1609 to 1701, Haudenosaunee campaigns dispersed neighboring nations and opened the Ohio valley to their hunters and raiders. The Honniasont name then dropped from French maps as Haudenosaunee, Lenape and Shawnee movements remade the upper Ohio country.
zh: 奥尼亚松特是后来法国记录给予俄亥俄瀑布以上林木河源地区的名称，地域横跨俄亥俄东部、宾夕法尼亚西部和西弗吉尼亚的山脊与河谷低地。1444年，被称作奥尼亚松特或奥尼亚松特克农的人生活在弗特安蒂恩文化和莫农加希拉文化的村落圈中，周围有玉米田、木栅、猎道和山路。他们的语言已无法确定，易洛魁语系和俄亥俄河谷苏语系两种联系都有人提出。16世纪中叶，欧洲货物已通过原住民商路进入河谷，随后疫病和海狸战争使许多聚落荒废。1609年至1701年的海狸战争中，豪德诺索尼诸部的征战打散邻近族群，也把俄亥俄河谷向他们的猎人和战队开放。此后奥尼亚松特之名从法国地图上消失，豪德诺索尼、莱纳佩和肖尼人的迁徙重塑了俄亥俄上游。

en:
Onojutta is the mountain valley of the Juniata, a shallow river that cuts the water gaps of Tuscarora and Jacks Mountain on its way to the Susquehanna. In 1444 the Onojutta-Haga, an Iroquoian people close to the Susquehannock, farmed the fertile bottomlands and hunted through the gaps; their river name, later written Onayutta, meant 'Standing Stone'.

Little is recorded of them before 1648, when they appear as forced auxiliaries of the Susquehannock, and after that power broke the Juniata bands were probably absorbed with it. Lenape families later used the valley, until Pennsylvania treaties opened it to colonial farmers. During the French and Indian War, warriors based at Kittanning on the Allegheny raided the new settlements and burned Fort Granville, a stockade on the Juniata, in August 1756. In September Lieutenant Colonel John Armstrong led a Pennsylvania column that surprised and destroyed Kittanning; gunpowder stored in the Lenape leader Captain Jacobs's house exploded in the fight, and the blast was heard forty-four miles away at Fort Duquesne. The Juniata stayed a hard military frontier for the rest of the war.
zh:
奥诺朱塔是朱尼亚塔河流经的山地河谷；这条水浅的河流切穿图斯卡罗拉山和杰克斯山的水口，汇入萨斯奎哈纳河。1444年，与萨斯奎汉诺克人关系密切、操易洛魁语的奥诺朱塔-哈加（Onojutta-Haga）人在肥沃低地上耕种，沿水口狩猎；他们的河名后来写作奥纳尤塔（Onayutta），意为「立石」。

1648年以前，奥诺朱塔-哈加人几乎不见记载，到这一年他们已是萨斯奎汉诺克人的被迫辅助者；萨斯奎汉诺克势力败亡后，朱尼亚塔诸部大概也随之被吸收。谷地后来为莱纳佩人所用，直到宾州的土地条约把它开放给殖民农民。法国-印第安人战争期间，以阿勒格尼河畔基坦宁为基地的战士袭扰新定居点，1756年8月焚毁朱尼亚塔河畔的栅栏堡格兰维尔堡。同年9月，约翰·阿姆斯特朗中校率领宾州部队奇袭并摧毁基坦宁；激战中，莱纳佩首领雅各布斯船长屋中储存的火药发生爆炸，四十四英里外的迪凯纳堡都听到了响声。整场战争期间，朱尼亚塔始终是严酷的军事边疆。

en:
Atrakwaye was the main town of the Akhrakouaeronon, a Susquehannock people whose palisaded villages stood on the east bank of the Susquehanna just below the meeting of its North and West branches, at a river junction later occupied by Sunbury. Susquehannock farmers raised maize, beans and squash on the flats and hunters crossed the surrounding ridges; canoes carried the valley's grain and pelts downriver toward the Chesapeake, while the Great Shamokin Path led west over the Allegheny. In 1444 no European trader had yet entered the valley. John Smith's map of 1608 later marked the town as Quadroque.

Smith met Susquehannock warriors on the Chesapeake in 1608 and opened the valley to written record. From the 1620s its beaver went to Virginia and New Netherland for kettles, axes and firearms, and Maryland made peace with the Susquehannock in 1652. Epidemics and Haudenosaunee wars broke the nation soon afterwards; after survivors were besieged on Piscataway Creek in 1675, the Susquehannock towns emptied and their people scattered or were absorbed.

The river junction lived on as Shamokin, 'the place of crawfish', a mixed trading town of Lenape, Seneca, Tutelo and Shawnee. In 1742 Shikellamy, the Oneida chief the Six Nations had placed over the Susquehanna villages, made it his seat; he guided the Pennsylvania envoy Conrad Weiser on his journeys to Onondaga and kept the border quiet until his death in 1748. The Lenape burned and abandoned Shamokin in May 1756, and Colonel William Clapham at once built Fort Augusta on the village site, the largest fort Pennsylvania ever raised: named for George III's mother, it had earthen walls two hundred feet long, twelve cannon and a garrison of over three hundred. A French and Indian force dragged two brass cannon down the West Branch to breach it, judged the walls out of range and turned back; the fort was never attacked. Pennsylvania laid out Sunbury here in 1772 and made it the seat of the new Northumberland County. After the defeat at Wyoming in July 1778, more than three thousand West Branch settlers crowded into the fort in the evacuation called the Great Runaway.
zh:
阿特拉夸耶是阿赫拉克瓦埃罗农人的主城。这支萨斯奎汉诺克人的木栅村镇位于萨斯奎哈纳河东岸、北支与西支汇口稍下之处，河汊要地后来由森伯里占据。萨斯奎汉诺克农人在低地上种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，猎人翻过往周围山岭；独木舟把河谷的谷物和皮毛顺流送往切萨皮克方向，大沙莫金小道（Great Shamokin Path）则向西翻过阿勒格尼山地。1444年，欧洲商人尚未进入这条河谷。约翰·史密斯1608年的地图后来把这座城镇标为「夸德罗克」。

1608年，史密斯在切萨皮克湾见到萨斯奎汉诺克战士，河谷开始有了文字记载。1620年代起，这里的河狸皮运往弗吉尼亚和新尼德兰，换回铜锅、斧头和火器；马里兰1652年同萨斯奎汉诺克人议和。此后不久，疫病和豪德诺索尼的战争压垮了这个族群；1675年残部在皮斯卡塔韦溪遭围困之后，萨斯奎汉诺克诸城为之一空，族人四散或被吸收。

河口要地作为沙莫金延续下来，其名意为「螯虾之地」，是特拉华、塞尼卡、图特洛和肖尼人杂处的贸易村镇。1742年，六族联盟派来统辖萨斯奎哈纳诸村的奥奈达酋长希克拉米把治所设在这里；他为宾夕法尼亚使者康拉德·魏瑟（Conrad Weiser）引路前往奥农达加议事，维持边境安宁，直到1748年去世。1756年5月，特拉华人焚毁并放弃沙莫金，威廉·克拉珀姆上校随即在村镇旧址建起奥古斯塔堡；这座以英王乔治三世之母命名的要塞是宾州历来所建最大的堡垒，土墙长达200英尺，配有12门大炮，驻军300余人。一支法国与原住民部队拖着两门铜炮顺西支而下准备破城，却发现距离超出火炮射程，只得折返；这座要塞终其使用也没有受到进攻。1772年，宾州在此规划森伯里，并作为新设诺森伯兰县的县治。1778年7月怀俄明战败后，3000多名西支居民在史称「大逃亡」的撤离中涌进这座要塞避难。

en:
Espachomy was the Esopus country on the west bank of the Hudson, where Rondout Creek meets the river and fertile flats run below high banks; the local Lenape word esepu means 'high bank'. Munsee Lenape villages, fishing places and cornfields stood along the flats, joined by trails to the hunting grounds in the woods and hills to the northwest. In 1444 the people here moved between planted valleys and hunting camps, and no Dutch post yet commanded the river landing.

Henry Hudson's voyage of 1609 opened the river to Dutch fur traders, who ran a post at the mouth of Rondout Creek from 1614 until the Esopus destroyed it. Settlers returned in 1652 and the first permanent farmer, Thomas Chambers, arrived the next year. In 1658 Peter Stuyvesant gathered the scattered homesteads into a stockaded village on the high ground, chartered as Wiltwyck in 1661. War broke out in 1659 after settlers shot Esopus labourers paid in brandy, and the uneasy peace lasted only until June 1663, when warriors entered Wiltwyck under cover of selling produce, burned much of it and carried off women and children while another band destroyed the new village of Nieu Dorp, later Hurley. Dutch troops reinforced from New Amsterdam and guided by Mohawk and Wappinger allies burned the Esopus fields and stormed their upland stronghold that September, killing the chief. English rule came in 1664; Richard Nicolls made peace with the Esopus the next year, and in 1669 Wiltwyck was renamed Kingston. The opened country later drew French Huguenots, who founded New Paltz.

In 1777 Kingston was the safest town left in rebel New York. The state constitution was completed there in April, George Clinton was inaugurated as first governor in July, and on 16 October a British force coming up the Hudson burned the town together with its stores of wheat, for the valley was the army's chief granary; the government had already withdrawn to Hurley. Kingston sloops carried Hudson Valley grain down to New York, and the town was incorporated as a village in 1805.
zh:
埃斯帕丘米是哈德逊河西岸埃索普斯人的地方，龙多特溪在此汇入大河，肥沃阶地横在高岸之下；当地莱纳佩语esepu意为「高岸」。阶地上分布着芒西-莱纳佩人的村落、渔场和玉米地，步道把它们同西北林地丘陵里的猎场连起来。1444年，这里的人往来于河谷农田和猎营之间，河畔渡口还没有荷兰人设立的商站。

1609年亨利·哈德逊的航行向荷兰皮货商人打开了这条河，他们从1614年起在龙多特溪口经营一处商站，直到埃索普斯人把它捣毁。1652年移民重返，第一位定居农户托马斯·钱伯斯次年到来。1658年，彼得·斯泰弗森特把分散的宅地集中到高地上一座栅栏围起的村庄，1661年获特许状，定名威尔特韦克。1659年，移民向以白兰地抵工酬的埃索普斯劳工开枪，战争爆发，脆弱的和局只维持到1663年6月：战士们以售卖农产品为掩护进入威尔特韦克，烧毁大片村舍、掳走妇女儿童，另一支部队同时摧毁新村，即后来的赫尔利。新阿姆斯特丹派来援军，在莫霍克人与瓦平格尔盟友引导下焚毁埃索普斯人的田地，于9月强攻其山地据点，杀死酋长。1664年英国接管，理查德·尼科尔斯次年同埃索普斯人讲和，1669年威尔特韦克改名金斯顿。开放的土地后来吸引法国胡格诺派信徒，他们建立了新帕尔茨。

1777年，金斯顿是起义的纽约州剩下的最安全的城镇。州宪法4月在这里制定完成，乔治·克林顿7月在此就任第一任州长；10月16日，一支沿哈德逊河溯流而上的英军烧毁城镇和屯粮，因为这一带正是大陆军的主要粮仓，而政府已提前撤往赫尔利。金斯顿的单桅帆船把哈德逊河谷的谷物运往纽约，1805年这里正式设村。

en:
The forested dome of the Adirondacks rises between the Mohawk valley and Lake Champlain, threaded with cold lakes and beaver streams. The Mohawk and Oneida hunted the high ground; Mahican and Algonquin bands hunted the eastern slopes. At the mountains' southern foot, Lake George pours into Lake Champlain through three and a half miles of rapids, and the short carry beside them was the only break in the canoe road from the St Lawrence to the Hudson. The Mohawk called the narrows tekontaró:ken, 'the junction of two waterways', which gives this province its name. In 1444 only native canoes and war parties used the carry, and the quarrels over these hunting grounds were already old.

On 30 July 1609, beside the narrows, Samuel de Champlain and two Frenchmen marched with an Algonquin and Huron war party against some two hundred Mohawks; his first arquebus shot killed two of their three chiefs, and France and the Iroquois fought for the next century and a half. In 1642 the Jesuit Isaac Jogues, taken by Mohawk raiders, was the first European carried over the portage; he later named Lake George the Lac du Saint-Sacrement and was killed by the Mohawk at Ossernenon in 1646. The French built Fort Carillon at the carry between 1755 and 1757. In July 1758 Abercromby hurled 16,000 men at Montcalm's 4,000, dug in behind a wall of sharpened felled trees, without bringing up cannon; his second-in-command Lord Howe had been killed in a skirmish the day before, and the attack failed with heavy losses. The British took the fort only in 1759, when Amherst advanced on a skeleton garrison and renamed it Ticonderoga.

On 10 May 1775, three weeks after Lexington, Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys and Benedict Arnold's volunteers surprised its forty-eight British soldiers; Allen demanded the surrender 'in the name of the Great Jehovah and the Continental Congress'. Henry Knox then hauled the captured cannon three hundred miles to the siege lines outside Boston, and the British evacuated the city in March 1776. In July 1777 Burgoyne dragged guns onto Mount Defiance above the fort, and Arthur St Clair abandoned the supposedly impregnable works without a fight, to the alarm of all the colonies; after Saratoga the British gave the place up.
zh:
林木覆盖的阿迪朗达克山地隆起于莫霍克河谷与尚普兰湖之间，寒冷的湖泊与河狸溪穿行于群山之中。莫霍克人和奥奈达人在高处游猎，莫希干人与阿尔冈昆人的队伍活动在东坡。山地南缘，乔治湖经五公里半的急流注入尚普兰湖，旁边的短陆运道是从圣劳伦斯河到哈得孙河的独木舟航道上唯一的断点。莫霍克人称这片狭窄水道为特康塔罗肯（tekontaró:ken），意为「两条水道相接之处」，省名便得自这个称呼。1444年时，只有印第安人的独木舟和战队取道这条陆运道，诸部争夺猎场的宿怨也已持续很久。

1609年7月30日，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰带着两名法国火枪手，随阿尔冈昆人与休伦人的战队在狭窄水道旁迎战约二百名莫霍克人；他的第一发火绳枪弹便击毙对方三名酋长中的两人，法国与易洛魁诸部此后交战了一个半世纪。1642年，被莫霍克袭掠者俘获的耶稣会士艾萨克·若格成为第一个被押过这段陆运道的欧洲人；他后来把乔治湖命名为「圣事湖」（Lac du Saint-Sacrement），1646年在莫霍克村镇奥塞尔农遇害。1755至1757年，法国人在陆运道旁修起卡里永堡。1758年7月，阿伯克龙比以一万六千人强攻蒙卡尔姆四千人据守的鹿砦，连野战炮都没有运上来；他的副将豪勋爵已在前一天的遭遇战中阵亡，强攻以惨重伤亡失败。直到1759年阿默斯特进军时，守军只剩寥寥数人，英军才拿下要塞，改名提康德罗加堡。

1775年5月10日，列克星顿交火三周之后，伊森·艾伦的绿山兄弟会同本尼迪克特·阿诺德的志愿民兵，突袭这座只驻有四十八名英军的要塞；艾伦要求守军「以伟大的耶和华和大陆会议的名义」投降。亨利·诺克斯随后把缴获的大炮拖运三百英里，送到波士顿围城阵地，英军于1776年3月撤出波士顿。1777年7月，伯戈因把火炮拖上俯瞰要塞的迪法恩斯山，阿瑟·圣克莱尔不战而弃这座号称坚不可摧的工事，各殖民地为之震动；萨拉托加战役之后，英军也放弃了此地。

en:
Quiripi was the Eastern Algonquian language of the Quinnipiac and nearby village clusters on the north shore of Long Island Sound. Their name is translated as 'long-water people', and their principal village, also called Quinnipiac, stood at New Haven harbor and the mouth of the Quinnipiac River. In 1444 families fished the harbor and river, dug shellfish from tidal flats, raised maize in coastal fields, and took beaver and deer in valley woods. Trails and canoe landings linked villages between the Pequot country to the east and communities closer to the Hudson in the west.

Adriaen Block, the first European known to enter Long Island Sound, visited the coast in 1614; Dutch traders later exchanged beaver pelts there but did not settle. In April 1638 John Davenport and Theophilus Eaton led 500 Puritans into the harbor. The Quinnipiac, under pressure from neighboring Pequots, sold land in return for protection, and the newcomers laid out the nine-square theocratic town named New Haven by 1640. The English also set apart 1,200 acres nearby as a supervised Quinnipiac reserve, the first Indian reserve established by English colonists. A loaded ship sent from New Haven to England in 1646 disappeared and hurt the port's early trade. Abraham Pierson preached near Branford from 1651 to 1669 and translated Christian texts into Quiripi, with little result.

New Haven kept its own colony until 1664, when pressure from England merged it into Connecticut. In 1661 Davenport sheltered Edward Whalley and William Goffe, two judges who had condemned Charles I, in the West Rock hills; John Dixwell, another regicide, later lived and died in the town. The Collegiate School moved to New Haven in 1716 and became Yale College in 1718 after Elihu Yale's gift. On 5 July 1779 General William Tryon landed 2,600 British troops and Loyalists in the harbor and raided the town, but did not burn it as neighboring coastal towns had been burned.
zh:
奎里皮是长岛湾北岸奎尼皮亚克（中文维基作昆尼帕）及邻近村群使用的东阿尔冈昆语。奎尼皮亚克名义为「长水之人」，他们的主要村镇同名，位于纽黑文港和奎尼皮亚克河口。1444年，各家族在港湾与河中捕鱼，在潮滩采贝，在沿海田地种植玉米，并到河谷林地猎取河狸和鹿。小径和独木舟渡口把村镇连接起来：其地东邻佩科特人的乡土，西接更靠近哈得孙河的社群。

已知最早驶入长岛湾的欧洲人阿德里安·布洛克于1614年到访这段海岸；后来荷兰商人在此交换河狸皮，但没有定居。1638年4月，约翰·达文波特和西奥菲勒斯·伊顿率领五百名清教徒驶入港湾。奎尼皮亚克人受到邻近佩科特人的压力，以土地换取保护；新来者规划九街方格的神权城镇，到1640年将其命名为纽黑文。英国人还在附近划出1200英亩受代理人监管的奎尼皮亚克保留地，这是英格兰殖民者设立的第一处印第安保留地。1646年，一艘从纽黑文载货驶往英格兰的船失踪，打击了该港早期贸易。1651年至1669年，亚伯拉罕·皮尔森在布兰福德附近向奎尼皮亚克人传教，并把基督教文本译成奎里皮语，但收效很小。

纽黑文曾维持独立殖民地，直到1664年在英国压力下并入康涅狄格。1661年，达文波特把曾判处查理一世死刑的两名法官爱德华·惠勒和威廉·戈夫藏在城西的西岩丘陵；另一名弑君者约翰·迪克斯韦尔后来也在纽黑文终老。1716年，联合教会学校迁至该城，1718年因伊莱休·耶鲁的捐赠更名耶鲁学院。1779年7月5日，威廉·特赖恩将军率二千六百名英军和效忠派在港湾登陆并袭掠城镇，但没有像焚毁邻近海岸城镇那样放火烧城。

en:
The hooked arm of Cape Cod and the islands beyond it, Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket, were the country of the Wampanoag, the 'eastern people' of the southern New England shore. Under many sachems their villages ran from the bay where Plymouth now stands eastward around the cape; women raised maize, beans and squash behind the shore settlements, men took herring and shellfish and pursued whale in dugout canoes, and their speech was the Massachusett language shared with the peoples around Boston. In 1444 every creek, planting ground and fishing place here bore a name fixed by long custom.

The Patuxet man Tisquantum knew Europe before he knew the Pilgrims. Seized at the cape by the English slaver Thomas Hunt in 1614 and sold in Spain, he was ransomed by friars, reached England, worked his way to Newfoundland as an interpreter, and came home in 1619 to find Patuxet emptied by the great epidemic. When the Mayflower's people settled those abandoned cornfields as Plymouth in December 1620, Samoset and then Tisquantum came to them the next spring; Tisquantum stayed in their village, taught them to plant the local corn and take fish, and acted as the go-between who brought the sachem Massasoit to a peace treaty in 1621. The harvest feast shared that autumn is the meal later remembered as the first Thanksgiving.

Massasoit kept the peace for forty years. His younger son Metacom, whom the English called Philip, led the rising of 1675 that became King Philip's War; he was killed in 1676, and hundreds of Wampanoag were sold into slavery in Bermuda and the West Indies. Survivors on the cape gathered in the Christian town of Mashpee, on lands deeded to them in 1660, and Plymouth Colony was later absorbed into the royal Province of Massachusetts Bay. A fever outbreak on Nantucket nearly put an end to the island band, and after independence Massachusetts ended Mashpee's self-rule in 1788 and set overseers over it.
zh:
弯钩般的科德角半岛和海外的玛莎葡萄园岛、南塔克特岛，是万帕诺亚格人的故土，他们是新英格兰南部海岸的「东方之人」。在众多酋长治下，村落从今日普利茅斯所在的海湾沿半岛向东分布；女人们在岸后种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，男人捕捞鲱鱼和贝类、乘独木舟追猎鲸鱼，他们的语言与波士顿一带诸族通用的马萨诸塞语相同。1444年时，这里的每一条溪涧、每一块耕地和渔场都有按古俗定下的名号。

帕图克塞特人蒂斯匡特姆认识欧洲，比认识清教徒移民更早。1614年他在半岛被英国奴隶贩子托马斯·亨特掳走、卖往西班牙，又被修士赎下；他辗转到了英国，以翻译身份随船前往纽芬兰，1619年返乡时，发现帕图克塞特已在大瘟疫中绝了人烟。1620年12月，「五月花号」上的移民在这片荒弃的玉米地上建起普利茅斯；第二年春天，萨莫塞特和蒂斯匡特姆先后来到他们中间，蒂斯匡特姆留了下来，教他们种植本地玉米、捕鱼，并作为中间人在1621年引酋长马萨索伊特与移民缔和。那年秋天双方共享的丰收宴，就是后世感恩节所本的那一餐。

马萨索伊特维持了四十年和平。他的幼子梅塔科姆（英人称菲利普）于1675年率众起义，即菲利普国王战争；他在1676年被杀，数百名万帕诺亚格人被卖到百慕大和西印度群岛为奴。半岛上的幸存者聚入基督徒村镇马什皮，土地是1660年立契划给他们的；普利茅斯殖民地后来并入王室治下的马萨诸塞湾省。南塔克特岛上的支族遭一场热病，几乎绝灭；独立之后，马萨诸塞州于1788年取消马什皮自治，派员监管其地。

en:
Pennacook stood at the broad bends of the upper Merrimack, where the river leaves the New Hampshire lakes and turns south toward the sea. It was the main village of the loose alliance of Algonquian bands that took its name from the place, usually glossed as 'at the foot of the hill'. Its people planted maize, beans and pumpkins on the floodplain, took salmon, sturgeon and alewife at the rapids, and travelled by birchbark canoe as far as the coast or Lake Winnipesaukee. Mohawk raiders pressed them from the west and Mi'kmaq from the east. In 1444 Pennacook was the upriver centre of the alliance, and its fishery and planting grounds drew the bands of the Merrimack country together.

The epidemics of 1616 to 1619 and a smallpox outbreak in 1633 emptied much of the valley. Passaconaway, the chief of chiefs, had force enough to fight the English settlers but chose peace, and in 1660 he handed his authority to his son Wonalancet. Wonalancet tried to keep his people out of King Philip's War and withdrew them to Pennacook in 1675; Captain Samuel Mosely's men followed and burned the village with its winter stores. His nephew Kancamagus, the last sachem of the alliance, led the raid on Dover in June 1689, remembered as the Cochecho Massacre, but after his wife and children were seized the next year he made peace and led the survivors north under French and Abenaki protection. Wonalancet died in 1697, kept in his old age by the settler Jonathan Tyng at Dunstable.

The upper valley lay largely empty until Massachusetts granted the Plantation of Penacook in 1725, and families from Haverhill led by Ebenezer Eastman settled it over the next two years. It was incorporated as Rumford in 1734, and after a long boundary dispute with the neighbouring grant of Bow, Governor Benning Wentworth renamed it Concord in 1765. Blodget's canal at Amoskeag, completed in 1807, opened a through water route to Boston. Concord became the permanent capital of New Hampshire the next year, and its State House was finished in 1819.
zh:
佩纳库克位于梅里马克河上游的宽阔河湾，河水在这里离开新罕布什尔的湖区、掉头向南入海。阿尔冈昆诸族那个以村为名的松散联盟以这里为主要村落，村名通常解释为「山脚之地」。人们在泛滥平原上种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，在急流中捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼和灰西鲱，乘桦皮船远行至海边或温尼珀索基湖。莫霍克人从西边、米克马克人从东边不断来袭。1444年，佩纳库克是联盟的上游中心，渔场和耕地把梅里马克一带的各支族人聚在这里。

1616至1619年的瘟疫和1633年的天花使河谷人口大减。联盟的大酋长帕萨科纳韦本有足够武力同英人开战，却选择讲和，1660年把权位交给儿子沃纳兰塞特。沃纳兰塞特力图让族人置身菲利普国王战争之外，1675年率部退回佩纳库克；塞缪尔·莫西上尉的队伍追来，烧毁村子和全部冬粮。他的外甥坎卡马格斯是联盟最后一位酋长，1689年6月率部袭击多佛，即史称科切乔大屠杀一役；次年妻儿被掳，他只得讲和，带幸存者北投法国人与阿布纳基人。沃纳兰塞特1697年去世，晚年由邓斯特布尔的移民乔纳森·廷供养。

上游河谷此后长期空旷，直到1725年马萨诸塞授予「佩纳库克种植园」，埃比尼泽·伊斯特曼带领黑弗里尔的几户人家在随后两年间到此定居。1734年设治为拉姆福德，又因与邻镇鲍长期争执边界，总督本宁·温特沃思1765年将其改名康科德。1807年阿莫斯凯格的布洛杰特运河完工，打通了前往波士顿的水路；次年康科德成为新罕布什尔的永久首府，州议会大厦1819年落成。

en:
The north-eastern arm of Lake Champlain, where the Missisquoi River opens into Missisquoi Bay, was the country of the Missisquoi band of the Western Abenaki. Their name mazipskoiak, 'people of the flint', came from a chert quarry near the present village of Swanton, and survives in this province's name of Missiasik. Their main village stood at the river mouth; the women raised maize in the intervals, the men fished the bay and the lake and hunted the western flanks of the Green Mountains. The lake was a war-road as much as a fishery, and its southern shores were a long frontier against the Mohawk. In 1444 no European had seen these waters.

Samuel de Champlain landed on Isle La Motte on 9 July 1609, gave the lake his own name and made its first map. In 1666 Captain Pierre La Motte, sent south with four companies of the Carignan-Salieres regiment to bar the lake against the Iroquois, built Fort Sainte Anne on the island, the first European settlement in what is now Vermont. About three hundred soldiers garrisoned it, and Bishop Laval crossed from Quebec in 1668 to baptise Iroquois converts there; four years later the French demolished the post and withdrew. Through the colonial wars the Missisquoi held the eastern shore as armed allies of France.

Benning Wentworth began granting townships here as early as 1749, though settlers came in numbers only after France ceded the lake country to Britain in 1763. New York sold the same townships again, and Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys drove off New York's surveyors before taking up arms against the Crown. In 1777 the settlers proclaimed the independent Vermont Republic at Windsor, whose constitution was the first in North America to abolish slavery and gave the vote to every adult man. Vermont governed itself for fourteen years and struck its own copper coins; on 4 March 1791 it entered the Union as the fourteenth state. By then the Missisquoi had withdrawn to the Abenaki mission village of Odanak on the St Francis and did not return in force.
zh:
尚普兰湖东北端、米西斯夸河注入米西斯夸湾的地方，是西阿布纳基人米西亚西克（Missisquoi，又译米西斯夸）部的土地；其族名mazipskoiak意为「燧石之人」，得自河口附近今斯旺顿一带的一处燧石矿，省名米西亚西克便是它的异拼。他们的主要村镇立在河口，妇女在河滨台地种植玉米，男子在湾中和湖里捕鱼，在绿山西坡游猎。这片湖既是渔场也是战道，湖南岸长期是与莫霍克人对峙的前沿。1444年时，还没有欧洲人见过这片水面。

1609年7月9日，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰登上拉莫特岛，以自己的名字为湖命名，绘下第一幅湖图。1666年，卡里尼昂-萨利埃团的皮埃尔·拉莫特上尉率四个连南下封锁湖道、防备易洛魁人，在岛上修建圣安娜堡，这是今佛蒙特境内最早的欧洲人定居点。要塞常驻约三百名士兵，1668年魁北克主教拉瓦勒专程前来，为皈依的易洛魁人施洗；四年后法军拆毁据点撤走。此后的殖民战争年代，米西斯夸人作为法兰西的武装盟友据守湖的东岸。

本宁·温特沃思早在1749年就开始在这里授地设镇，但移民大批涌入要等到1763年法国把湖区割让给英国；纽约把同样的乡镇又卖了一遍，伊森·艾伦的绿山兄弟先是赶走纽约的测量员，后来又拿起武器对抗英王。1777年，定居者在温莎宣布建立独立的佛蒙特共和国，其宪法是北美第一部废除奴隶制、并赋予全体成年男子选举权的宪法。佛蒙特自治了十四年，还铸造过自己的铜币，1791年3月4日加入联邦，成为第十四个州。到这时，米西斯夸人已北撤至圣弗朗西斯河畔的阿布纳基传教村奥达纳克，再没有成批返回。

en:
Sokoki was the western Abenaki country of the upper Connecticut, where river meadows and pine woods lay between the White Mountains and the Green Mountains. Sokoki families planted maize, beans and squash on the intervales and hunted moose and beaver; trails linked their camps to the Cowasuck upstream and the Pennacook to the south. In 1444 no European had yet seen the upper Connecticut, whose pelts moved only between Indigenous hands.

Abenaki raids and English retaliation swept the upper valley through the wars of 1675 to 1725, and many Sokoki withdrew to the French mission village of St. Francis on the St. Lawrence. Massachusetts nevertheless granted Plantation No. 4 here in 1735, the northernmost English settlement on the Connecticut; families arrived from 1740 and in 1744 joined six houses together into a stockade. The settlers had all but left when Captain Phineas Stevens reoccupied the post with 31 men in March 1747, and on 7 April a French and Abenaki force under Ensign Joseph Boucher de Niverville surrounded it. Reports reaching Boston put the besiegers above five hundred; French records say about fifty. Stevens held the gate for three days and the attackers withdrew to Canada. Commodore Charles Knowles sent him the finest sword Boston could buy, and when the township was rechartered in 1753 it took the name Charlestown in Knowles's honour. The frontier stayed armed through the French and Indian War: Susanna Willard Johnson and her family were seized here in August 1754 and carried to Canada, and in 1759 Robert Rogers came down the valley to fetch help for his starving rangers after destroying the Abenaki town of St. Francis.
zh:
索科基是西阿贝纳基人的土地，位于康涅狄格河上游，河畔草甸与松林夹在怀特山和绿山之间。索科基人家族在河滨低地上种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，捕猎驼鹿和河狸；营地小径把他们同上游的科瓦萨克人、南方的佩纳库科人连在一起。1444年，还没有欧洲人见过康涅狄格河上游，这里的毛皮只在原住民各部之间转手。

1675至1725年的历次战争中，阿贝纳基人的袭掠和英格兰人的报复席卷上游河谷，许多索科基人迁往圣劳伦斯河畔的法国传教村落圣弗朗索瓦。尽管如此，马萨诸塞1735年还是在此授出「第四号种植园」，这是康涅狄格河上位置最北的英格兰人定居点；1740年起有家庭迁来，1744年他们把六栋房屋连成一座木栅要塞。定居者几乎逃光之后，菲尼亚斯·史蒂文斯上尉1747年3月率31名民兵重新进驻据点，4月7日，法国海军陆战队少尉约瑟夫·布歇·德·尼韦维尔（Joseph Boucher de Niverville）率领的法国与阿贝纳基联军便将它包围。传到波士顿的消息称围攻者有五百多人，法国档案却说大约只有五十。史蒂文斯守住寨门三日，攻城者撤回加拿大。英国海军准将查尔斯·诺尔斯送给他一把在波士顿能买到的最考究的佩剑；1753年镇区重新获颁特许状时，便以诺尔斯之名称为查尔斯敦。法国印第安人战争期间边疆依然兵戈不断：1754年8月，苏珊娜·威拉德·约翰逊一家在这里被掳往加拿大；1759年，罗伯特·罗杰斯在摧毁阿贝纳基人的圣弗朗索瓦镇之后，沿河谷回来为他挨饿的游骑兵求援。

en:
Kinnipekw is the upper Kennebec country, running from the cold waters of Moosehead Lake down through rapids to a broad bend above the later English settlements. The Norridgewock band kept its chief village there, Nanrantsouak, the still water between the rapids, on a plateau inside the bend opposite the Sandy River. Families grew maize, beans and squash on the intervales, and twice a year moved to the coast for fish, seals and shellfish; parties also came to Mount Kineo on Moosehead Lake for its workable rhyolite, and portage trails led from the river toward the Penobscot country and Canada. In 1444 no European crown claimed the valley, and Eastern Abenaki bands moved through the lakes with the seasons.

The village became New France's forward post on the disputed Maine border. The Jesuit Sébastien Rale settled there in 1693, built a bark chapel and converted most of the band; by 1716 a nine-foot palisade enclosed 26 log cabins built after the English manner, two streets crossing at a central square, and a larger church went up outside the east gate in 1720. Rale spoke Abenaki fluently, compiled an Abenaki-French dictionary, and kept the band from agreeing terms with New England. Massachusetts put a price on his head, militia burned the chapel and village in 1705, and a raid in 1722 carried off his letters from Quebec. On 23 August 1724 two militia companies rowed up from Fort Richmond in whaleboats and surprised the village, killing Rale and as many as forty of his people and burning the cabins and fields. French accounts had him die at the foot of the great cross in the square, drawing the soldiers' fire to shield his flock; New England said he was shot while reloading his musket. The survivors buried him and withdrew to Canada.

In September 1775 Benedict Arnold led about 1,100 Continental soldiers up the Kennebec past the empty village, hauling flat-bottomed bateaux up the rapids and over the height of land toward the Chaudiere. Leaking boats, swampy portages, storms and inaccurate maps cut the column to about 600 starving men before it reached Quebec.
zh:
金尼佩库是肯纳贝克河上游地区，从寒冷的穆斯黑德湖顺流而下，穿过多处急流，直抵后来英国定居点以北的一道宽大河曲。诺里奇沃克人群的主村就在这里，阿布纳基语称南兰楚阿克，意为「急流之间的静水」，坐落在桑迪河对岸的河曲高地上。居民在河滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，一年两度迁往海边捕鱼、猎海豹、拾贝类；穆斯黑德湖畔的基尼奥山出产适于打制石器的流纹岩，也会吸引各方人群前来，水陆转运小径则从肯纳贝克河通往佩诺布斯科特人地区和加拿大。1444年时，还没有任何欧洲王权领有这条河谷，东阿布纳基各群体随季节穿行于湖群之间。

这座村落后来成了法国在有争议的缅因边界上的前哨。耶稣会士塞巴斯蒂安·拉勒1693年定居于此，建起一座树皮礼拜堂，使多数村民皈依；到1716年，一道九英尺高的栅栏围着二十六座按英国式样建造的木屋，两条街在中央广场交叉，1720年东门外又建起一座更大的教堂。拉勒阿布纳基语流利，编成一部阿布纳基语与法语对照词典，并阻止村落同新英格兰达成协议。马萨诸塞悬赏他的人头，民兵1705年焚毁了教堂和村落，1722年的一次袭击又搜走他与魁北克往来的信件。1724年8月23日，两连民兵乘捕鲸船从里士满堡溯河而上，突袭村落，杀死拉勒和多达四十名村民，焚毁木屋和田地。法国方面记载，他死在广场的大十字架下，为掩护教民而把火力引向自己；新英格兰方面则说他是在给火枪装弹时被击毙的。幸存者将他安葬后撤往加拿大。

1775年9月，本尼迪克特·阿诺德率约一千一百名大陆军士兵沿肯纳贝克河北上，经过已成废墟的村落，拖着平底船越过急流和分水高地，前往肖迪耶尔河。漏船、沼泽转运路、风暴和粗糙地图使队伍抵达魁北克前只剩约六百名饥疲交加的士兵。

en:
The foggy, island-strewn mouth of the St. Croix and the waters of Passamaquoddy Bay, churned by the great tides of the Bay of Fundy, are the country of the Peskotomuhkatiyik, 'those of the place where pollock are plentiful', the Passamaquoddy. Each summer their bands gathered on the bay shores and islands to spear pollock and herring, take seals and dig clams, then scattered inland for the winter moose hunt, travelling the lakes by birchbark canoe; their chief camp of Qonasqamkuk stood at the head of the bay. Kinsmen of the Maliseet and Mi'kmaq, they were one of the nations of the Wabanaki league of the Dawnland, and in 1444 no European ship had yet wintered among them.

Europe arrived in June 1604, when the French nobleman Pierre Dugua de Mons, with Samuel de Champlain, put a wintering party on Sainte-Croix Island in the river mouth; scurvy killed 35 of the 79 men before spring, and the survivors moved across to Port Royal. French traders and Jesuits made the Passamaquoddy, whom they called the Etchemins, into allies and converts, and their warriors raided the New England frontier through the long Wabanaki wars of the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries. Settlers came only after the fall of New France: fishermen occupied Moose Island in 1772, and Machias, granted a few years earlier, became a hotbed of rebellion. In June 1775 its men rowed out in a lumber sloop under Jeremiah O'Brien, armed mostly with muskets, axes and pitchforks, and captured the armed schooner Margaretta, the first British warship taken in the Revolution; James Fenimore Cooper later called the fight 'the Lexington of the Seas'. In August 1777 forty Passamaquoddy warriors under Joseph Neeala helped drive Sir George Collier's squadron back from the town. An Anglo-American commission later fixed the St. Croix as the border, cutting the old homeland in two. War returned in 1814, when the British seized Eastport and Machias and held the bay until the Treaty of Ghent, and Eastport itself until 1818.
zh:
圣克罗伊河口雾气弥漫、岛屿散布，帕萨马科迪湾的海水受芬迪湾大潮吞吐，这里是帕萨马科迪人的故土，他们自称帕萨马科迪人（Peskotomuhkatiyik），意为「狭鳕丰饶之地的人」。每年夏天，各部群聚到湾岸和岛屿，用鱼叉捕捞狭鳕与鲱鱼、猎海豹、挖蛤蜊，冬天则分散到内陆猎驼鹿，乘桦皮独木舟往来于湖沼之间；他们的主要营地科纳斯卡姆库克就位于湾顶。作为马勒西特人和米克马克人的亲族，他们是「黎明之地」瓦巴纳基联盟的成员之一；1444年时，还没有一艘欧洲船在他们中间过冬。

欧洲人在1604年6月到来：法国贵族皮埃尔·迪加·德蒙与尚普兰率一队人在河口的圣克罗伊岛设营过冬，春天之前79人中有35人死于坏血病，幸存者后来迁往对岸的皇家港。法国商人与耶稣会士把他们所称的「埃切明人」发展为盟友和信徒，在17世纪后期至18世纪初漫长的瓦巴纳基战争中，帕萨马科迪战士不断袭扰新英格兰边疆。直到新法兰西陷落后，移民才真正到来：渔民1772年占据穆斯岛，早几年获颁建镇的马柴厄斯则成了反叛的温床。1775年6月，镇民在杰里迈亚·奥布赖恩带领下乘一艘运木帆船出港，武器多是火枪、斧头和干草叉，夺下武装帆船「玛格丽塔号」，这是独立战争中缴获的第一艘英国军舰；詹姆斯·费尼莫尔·库珀后来称此战为「海上莱克星顿」。1777年8月，约瑟夫·尼阿拉率领四十名帕萨马科迪战士，协助击退了乔治·科利尔爵士舰队的进攻。后来英美联合委员会划定以圣克罗伊河为界，把旧日故土一分为二。1814年战火又至，英军夺取东港和马柴厄斯，占据海湾直到《根特和约》签订，东港一地更是迟至1818年才归还。

en:
Inland from Passamaquoddy Bay the land climbs into a cold, forested interior cut by the upper tributaries of the Saint John, among them the Aroostook, whose Wolastoqey name Wool-ahs-took means 'good river for everything', and the Tobique. The Wolastoqiyik, the 'People of the Bright River', used these waters as winter hunting grounds: families paddled and snowshoed up them after moose and caribou, trapped beaver, took salmon at the rapids and made maple sugar when the thaw came. Their palisaded, maize-growing villages stood downriver at Meductic, the largest of them all, and at the Saint John's mouth, and raids from the Haudenosaunee far to the west were an old danger. In 1444 no European had yet ascended these streams.

French ships charting the Bay of Fundy met the Wolastoqiyik at the Saint John's mouth in 1604, and both Champlain and Lescarbot left descriptions of the large village there. A century of fur trade, Jesuit missions and military alliance followed, and Wolastoqey warriors fought beside the French in every war against New England. When the St. John River campaign of 1758 burned Meductic and the Acadian expulsion emptied the lower valley, the survivors withdrew upstream; Maliseet and Acadian refugees together made Madawaska, at the head of the river, one of the largest Wolastoqey villages of the later eighteenth century. In 1801 the colonial government, acting on the band's own petition, granted a reserve of nearly 20,000 acres at the mouth of the Tobique. In 1821 the Aroostook interior was still unceded forest, with no permanent settler town and no agreed international boundary.
zh:
从帕萨马科迪湾向内陆去，地势抬升为寒冷多林的高地，圣约翰河的上游支流纵横其间，阿鲁斯图克河与托比克河都在其中；阿鲁斯图克的马勒西特语原名沃拉斯图克（Wool-ahs-took），意为「百物皆宜之河」。沃拉斯托奎伊克人，即「亮河之民」，把这些水道当作冬季猎场：家户划独木舟、踏雪鞋溯河而上，猎驼鹿和驯鹿，诱捕海狸，在急流捕鲑鱼，开春转暖时熬制枫糖。他们种植玉米、设栅据守的村落位于下游，其中最大的梅达克蒂克和圣约翰河口；西面远方豪德诺索尼人的袭扰是由来已久的威胁。1444年，还没有欧洲人溯这些溪流而上。

1604年，测绘芬迪湾的法国船只在圣约翰河口与沃拉斯托奎伊克人相遇，尚普兰和莱斯卡博都记述过当地那座大村。此后是约一个世纪的毛皮贸易、耶稣会传教与军事同盟，历次对新英格兰的战争中都有沃拉斯托奎伊克战士与法国人并肩作战。1758年的圣约翰河战役烧毁梅达克蒂克，阿卡迪亚大驱逐又使下游河谷为之一空，幸存者便向上游转移；马勒西特难民与阿卡迪亚难民在河首的马达瓦斯卡合居，使这里成为18世纪后期最大的沃拉斯托奎伊克村落之一。1801年，殖民政府根据部落自己的请愿，在托比克河口划给他们一片近两万英亩的保留地。到1821年，阿鲁斯图克内陆仍是未割让的森林，没有固定的移民城镇，也没有议定的国际边界。

en:
Gespogoitnag is Kespukwitk, 'Land's End', the southwestern arm of Nova Scotia, where the great tides of the Bay of Fundy meet the Atlantic shore among inlets, rivers, lakes and canoe portages. The Annapolis Basin, called Nme'juaqnek for its abundant fish, drew Mi'kmaq chiefs to its weirs and camps, while routes through Kejimkujik carried canoes from the basin to the South Shore. The district saqamaw sat in the wider councils of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444, fishing weirs and seasonal camps, not European walls or seigneuries, marked control of this land.

Membertou, saqamaw of Kespukwitk and later grand chief of the seven districts, claimed to have been a grown man when he met Jacques Cartier in 1534, and he became the French ally at Port Royal. Pierre Dugua's party built its habitation on the Annapolis Basin in 1605, the first year-round European settlement in what became Canada, earlier than Jamestown or Quebec. In 1606 Samuel de Champlain set up the Order of Good Cheer there, a table society whose members took turns bringing moose, caribou, beaver, geese and partridge to the common feast, counted in France as the first social club in America. Samuel Argall's raiders, sailing from Virginia, burned the habitation in 1613. Scottish settlers built Charles Fort on the basin in 1629 and held it until France recovered the place three years later.

A British siege took Port Royal in 1710 and the town became Annapolis Royal. Between the French, Scots and English it had changed hands seven times and withstood thirteen sieges, more than any other place in North America. Four French and Mi'kmaq armies came against it between 1744 and 1746, Le Loutre leading three hundred Mi'kmaq warriors in the first, but none took Fort Anne, and the town stayed capital of Nova Scotia until Halifax was founded in 1749. In December 1755 the British cleared the basin of its Acadians, putting more than sixteen hundred men, women and children aboard seven ships at the Fort Anne wharf and carrying them to the American colonies. After the American Revolution, Loyalists, among them Black Loyalists, settled the emptied garrison town.
zh:
格斯波戈伊特纳格是凯斯普库维特克，意为「陆地尽头」，即新斯科舍伸向西南的半岛。芬迪湾的大潮在港湾、河流、湖泊和独木舟搬运道之间汇入大西洋南岸。安纳波利斯盆地的米克马克语名为恩梅朱阿克内克（Nme'juaqnek，意为鱼群丰饶之地），鱼梁和营地把各路酋长吸引到此，经凯吉姆库吉克的水路又能从盆地通往南岸，本地区酋长参加米克马克基的大议事会。1444年，标示这片土地归属的是鱼梁和季节性营地，而不是欧洲人的城墙或领主庄园。

凯斯普库维特克酋长梅姆伯图后来成为七个地区的大酋长，自称1534年遇见雅克·卡特尔时已是成年人；他在皇家港与法国人结盟，也以此闻名。1605年，皮埃尔·迪加一行在安纳波利斯盆地建起居留地，这是后来加拿大境内第一个欧洲人常年定居点，比詹姆斯敦和魁北克都早。1606年，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在此发起「好时光会」（l'Ordre de Bon Temps），入会者轮流把驼鹿、驯鹿、河狸、野雁和山鹑端上公共餐桌，在法国它被视作美洲第一个社交会社。1613年，从弗吉尼亚驾船而来的英国人塞缪尔·阿高尔率众烧毁了居留地。1629年，苏格兰移民在盆地上修建查尔斯堡，据守三年后被法国收回。

1710年，英军在围攻中拿下皇家港，城镇改名安纳波利斯罗亚尔。在法、苏、英三方之间，这里七次易主，承受十三次围攻，次数为北美之最。1744年至1746年，四支法国与米克马克联军先后打来，第一支里就有勒卢特尔率领的三百名战士，但没有人能攻下安妮堡；直到1749年哈利法克斯建立，这里始终是新斯科舍首府。1755年12月，英国人清空盆地里的阿卡迪亚人，在安妮堡码头把一千六百多名男女老幼押上七艘船，运往北美各殖民地。美国独立战争后，效忠派，其中包括黑人效忠派，来到这座被清空的旧要塞城镇定居。

en:
Eskikeogag is Eskikewa'kik, the 'skin-dressing place' of the Mi'kmaq, at the eastern tip of mainland Nova Scotia. Its coast runs from the St. Mary's River to the headlands of Chedabucto Bay and the Canso islands, facing Cape Breton across the Strait of Canso. The harbour called Gamso'q, ringed by islands and beaches, gave the Mi'kmaq a seasonal place for fishing, sealing, hide work and meetings, and canoe routes led from its camps to the other districts of Mi'kma'ki. In 1444 no European fish flakes or forts stood on these shores.

European fishing ships began watering at Canso in the early 1500s, and from the 1630s the French worked a fishery on Chedabucto Bay, where La Rochelle merchants built the fortified post of Fort St. Louis; about fifty fishers lived there in 1686. The Treaty of Utrecht assigned the bay to Britain in 1713, yet the French station held on until September 1718, when the New England privateer Cyprian Southack brought HMS Squirrel into the bay, wrecked the fishery, took the fort from its Acadian garrison and put the prisoners ashore on the Canso islands without food or clothing.

New Englanders raised their own garrison, Fort William Augustus, at Canso in 1720. A permanent fort broke the old agreement between the Mi'kmaq and the seasonal fishermen, and Mi'kmaq raids on the works helped open Father Rale's War, called Dummer's War in New England; the French sacked the fishing village again when war resumed in 1744. In April 1745 William Pepperell's 4,070 New England troops mustered at Canso and were joined there by Commodore Warren's four warships before the fleet sailed against Louisbourg. The Acadian deportation ship Duke William lay in the harbour for almost a month in 1758, narrowly escaping a Mi'kmaq raid. John Paul Jones brought USS Providence into Canso in September 1776 and burned, sank or captured fifteen vessels. Loyalists, Black Loyalists among them, founded Guysborough on the ruined French shore in 1784.
zh:
埃斯基凯奥加格即埃斯基凯瓦基克，米克马克语意为「鞣皮之地」，地处新斯科舍大陆部分的最东端。海岸从圣玛丽斯河延展到沙达巴克托湾的岬角与坎索诸岛，隔坎索海峡与布雷顿角相望。名为加姆索克（Gamso'q）的港湾外有岛屿和滩涂环绕，是米克马克人季节性捕鱼、捕海豹、加工兽皮和聚会的地方，独木舟路线从这里的营地通向米克马克基其他地区。1444年，这些岸上还没有欧洲人的晒鱼架和堡垒。

欧洲渔船16世纪初就开始在坎索补给淡水，1630年代起法国人在沙达巴克托湾经营渔场，拉罗谢尔商人在那里建起设防的圣路易堡，1686年约有五十名渔民在此居住。1713年《乌得勒支和约》把海湾划归英国，法国据点却一直撑到1718年9月：新英格兰私掠船长西普里安·索萨克率「松鼠号」战舰驶入海湾，摧毁渔场，从阿卡迪亚守军手中攻下堡垒，又把俘虏丢在坎索诸岛上，不给食物和衣物。

1720年，新英格兰人在坎索建起自己的威廉·奥古斯都堡。常驻堡垒打破了米克马克人与季节性渔民之间的旧约定，米克马克人屡次袭击工事，是勒莱神父战争（新英格兰称达默战争）的起因之一；1744年战事再起，法军又洗劫了这座渔村。1745年4月，威廉·佩珀雷尔率四千零七十名新英格兰士兵在坎索集结，沃伦海军准将的四艘战舰前来会合，随后合兵进攻路易斯堡。1758年，阿卡迪亚大驱逐的运输船「威廉公爵号」在港中停泊近一个月，险些遭到米克马克人袭击。1776年9月，约翰·保罗·琼斯驾「普罗维登斯号」进入坎索，烧毁、击沉或俘获十五艘船只。1784年，效忠派（其中包括黑人效忠派）在这片被毁的法国旧渔岸上建立盖斯伯勒。

en:
The Wolastoq, the ‘shining river’ the French named the Saint John, runs from the forests south of the St. Lawrence to a fall on the Bay of Fundy where every rising tide shoves the river backward. The Wolastoqiyik, People of the Bright River, held its whole valley in palisaded villages, grew corn, beans and squash on the intervales and took salmon, sturgeon and bass from the water. At Menahkwesk, the harbour where the river meets the bay, stood one of their largest villages, used by Mi'kmaq sealing parties too. The Mi'kmaq were kinsmen to the east, the Passamaquoddy held the bay and the Penobscot the country to the west, while the river stockades were raised against the old enemy, Haudenosaunee raiders far inland. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered the bay.

Samuel de Champlain landed at the harbour on 24 June 1604, the feast of St John the Baptist, and gave the river its name. In 1631 Charles de Saint-Étienne de la Tour built Fort Sainte-Marie at Portland Point, and the river mouth became his base in the Acadian civil war against Charles de Menou d'Aulnay, who held Port Royal across the bay. In 1645, while la Tour was in Boston seeking help from Massachusetts merchants, d'Aulnay stormed the fort against the defence of la Tour's wife, Françoise-Marie Jacquelin; she died within weeks of the surrender. When d'Aulnay died, la Tour married his widow in 1653 and recovered his standing in Acadia.

The Wolastoqiyik traded furs to the French and, from their upriver headquarters at Meductic, raided the New England frontier as allies of France, until France ceded Acadia to Britain at Utrecht in 1713 without consulting them. Forts rose and burned at the river mouth: Boishébert fired his own Fort Menagoueche in 1755 after Beauséjour fell, the British replaced it with Fort Frederick in 1758, American privateers sacked that in 1775, and Major Studholme built Fort Howe in 1777. Loyalist fleets began landing refugees in May 1783, more than ten thousand within months, and on 18 May 1785 Parrtown and Carleton were joined by royal charter as Saint John, the first incorporated city in what is now Canada and the chief port of the new colony of New Brunswick.
zh:
沃拉斯托克意为「闪光之河」，法国人称之为圣约翰河，发源于圣劳伦斯河以南的森林，在芬迪湾口形成一道瀑布，潮水上涨时甚至把河水顶得倒流。沃拉斯托基伊克人（意为「闪光河上的人」）在整条河谷居住，村落以木栅设防，在河畔滩地种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在河中捕捞鲑鱼、鲟鱼和鲈鱼。河海相接处、他们称作梅纳赫奎斯克的港湾旁，有他们最大的村落之一，米克马克人的海豹捕猎队也常来此地。他们的东邻是同族的米克马克人，湾畔住着帕萨马科迪人，西邻佩诺布斯科特人；远在内陆的霍德诺索尼人则是世仇，沿河村落筑栅正是为了抵御他们的袭击。1444年，还没有任何欧洲船只驶入过这座海湾。

1604年6月24日施洗者圣约翰节，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在港湾登陆，为河流取了圣约翰这个名字。1631年，夏尔·德·圣艾蒂安·德·拉图尔在波特兰角修筑圣玛丽堡，河口成为他与据守海湾对岸罗亚尔港的夏尔·德·梅努·多尔奈打阿卡迪亚内战的大本营。1645年，拉图尔正在波士顿向马萨诸塞商人借船贷款，多尔奈攻破堡垒，拉图尔之妻弗朗索瓦丝-玛丽·雅克兰率众死守，城破后数周便死去。多尔奈本人死后，拉图尔在1653年娶了他的遗孀，重新获得在阿卡迪亚的地位。

沃拉斯托基伊克人以毛皮与法国人交易，并以中游的梅杜克蒂克为大本营，作为法国盟友袭掠新英格兰边疆；直到1713年法国在《乌得勒支和约》中未与他们商议便把阿卡迪亚割让给英国。此后的战争里，河口的堡垒筑了又烧：法国的梅纳古埃什堡由守将布瓦埃贝尔在1755年博塞茹尔陷落后亲自焚毁；英国人1758年在原址建起弗雷德里克堡，1775年又遭美国武装民船洗劫；斯塔多姆少校1777年另筑豪堡。1783年5月起，效忠派船队载着难民源源登陆，数月内超过一万人；1785年5月18日，帕尔敦与卡尔顿两个居民点凭皇家特许状合并为圣约翰，成为今加拿大境内第一座获特许状建制的城市，也是新设的新不伦瑞克殖民地的首要港口。

en:
Madawaska is the cold upper valley of the Saint John River around the mouth of the Madawaska River, a country of river terraces, woods and canoe routes below the high ground of the watershed. In 1444 it was Wolastoqey country. The people took their name from Wolastoq, the 'bright river' or Saint John, and belonged to the Algonquian-speaking Wabanaki peoples. Family bands moved between fields of corn, beans, squash and tobacco, fishing stations, berry and nut grounds, and winter hunting camps. Canoes used the main river to reach the downstream villages and the tributaries meeting Mi'kmaq, Passamaquoddy and Penobscot lands.

French fur traders entered the Saint John early in the seventeenth century. The Wolastoqiyik traded pelts for metal tools and weapons, received Jesuit missionaries, and served as French allies when colonial raiding reached the lower river. During the Acadian expulsions of 1755-1764, families moved upstream beyond British patrols and found shelter in Wolastoqey camps. In 1785 Joseph Daigle led twenty Acadian families from Fredericton to the upper valley; local tradition places their landing on the south bank, where they raised a wooden cross. Farms spread on both banks, and French Canadians later joined the settlement. The Treaty of Paris of 1783 did not survey the headwaters, so in 1821 Madawaska remained a French-speaking Wolastoqey borderland claimed by Britain and the United States.
zh:
马达沃斯卡是圣约翰河寒冷的上游河谷，位于马达沃斯卡河汇入圣约翰河一带，由河流阶地、林地和分水岭高处以下的独木舟水路组成。1444年，这里是沃拉斯托奇人的土地。他们因沃拉斯托克河，即「明亮之河」圣约翰河得名，属于说阿尔冈昆语的瓦巴纳基诸族。各个家族群在玉米、菜豆、南瓜和烟草田、捕鱼点、浆果与坚果采集地以及冬季猎营之间往返。独木舟沿圣约翰河通向下游村落，也可进入各条支流，邻近米克马克人、帕萨马科迪人和佩诺布斯科特人的土地。

17世纪初，法兰西毛皮商人进入圣约翰河。沃拉斯托奇人用毛皮交换金属工具和武器，接待耶稣会传教士；殖民袭扰延及下游时，他们作为法兰西同盟作战。1755年至1764年阿卡迪亚人大流放期间，许多家庭溯河而上，避开英军巡逻队，在沃拉斯托奇人的营地中得到庇护。1785年，约瑟夫·戴格尔率领二十个阿卡迪亚家庭从弗雷德里克顿来到上游；当地传统把他们的登陆点定在南岸，据说他们在那里竖起了一个木十字架。农场随后扩展到圣约翰河两岸，法裔加拿大人也加入这一定居点。1783年《巴黎条约》没有勘定河源边界，因此到1821年，马达沃斯卡仍是法语居民与沃拉斯托奇人共处、英国和美国均提出声索的边境地带。

en:
Siknikt, ‘the drainage place’, is the Mi'kmaq name for the narrow neck joining the Nova Scotia peninsula to the continent: at its tightest, twenty-four kilometres of ridge and marsh separate the Fundy tides of Chignecto Bay from Baie Verte, which opens on the Gulf of St Lawrence. The short carry across that neck was the quickest road between two coasts, used for centuries by Mi'kmaq families who netted salmon and waterfowl on the Tantramar salt marshes. As Signigtewa'gi the isthmus was the south-eastern district of Mi'kma'ki, its villages governed by their own saqamaq under the Grand Council of the Wabanaki confederacy. In 1444 no European sail had yet entered the Bay of Fundy.

Acadians from Port-Royal settled the ridge above the Missaguash from 1671 as Beaubassin, dyking the Tantramar with aboiteaux into cattle ranges; by 1715 its fifty families ran a thousand cattle and traded in two directions, to Louisbourg through Baie Verte and to New England through the Bay of Fundy. New England raiders under Benjamin Church sacked the village in 1696 and again in 1704. After Utrecht the disputed Anglo-French frontier came to rest on the Missaguash, and in May 1750, as Major Charles Lawrence arrived with 800 men to claim it, the French burned their own town and withdrew across the river. Lawrence raised Fort Lawrence on the ashes; the French answered from the next ridge with the five-bastioned Fort Beauséjour, finished in 1752, and Fort Gaspareaux on Baie Verte, the two peacetime garrisons watching each other across one small river. Beauséjour was sold from within: Thomas Pichon, a fort clerk later called ‘the Judas of Acadia’, took British pay, sent the plans of the works to the commandant at Fort Lawrence and talked his own side out of strengthening the walls. In June 1755 Robert Monckton landed with about two thousand New England troops carried from Boston in thirty-one transports. On the thirteenth day of the siege a bomb crashed through a casemate roof and the commandant, Vergor, surrendered; he faced a court martial at Quebec two years later and was acquitted. Fort Gaspareaux was abandoned the same day, Beauséjour was renamed Fort Cumberland, and the round-ups of the Acadian deportation began from its gates. In the autumn of 1776 Jonathan Eddy's rebel band of Yankees, Acadians, Maliseet and Mi'kmaq besieged the fort for the American cause, until troops sent from Halifax drove them off.
zh:
锡格尼格泰奥加格（希格尼克特）意为「排水之地」，是米克马克人对这条连接新斯科舍半岛与北美大陆的狭窄地峡的称呼：最窄处只有24公里的丘陵与沼泽，一边是希格内克托湾的芬迪涌潮，一边是通向圣劳伦斯湾的贝尔特湾。横跨地峡的短联运道是两大海岸间最便捷的路，米克马克氏族多少个世纪沿这条路往来，在坦特拉马盐沼上张网捕捞鲑鱼、猎取水鸟。此地米克马克语称西尼克特瓦吉，是米克马克基东南一区，各村由酋长在瓦巴纳基联盟大议事会下自行治理。1444年，还没有欧洲船帆驶入芬迪湾。

1671年起，罗亚尔港来的阿卡迪亚人在米萨瓜什河畔的高地上建起博巴桑村，用水闸海塘把坦特拉马沼泽围成牧场；到1715年，村里的五十户人家养着上千头牛，贸易分走两头：经贝尔特湾通往路易斯堡，经芬迪湾通往新英格兰。1696年和1704年，本杰明·丘奇率领的新英格兰武装两度洗劫此地。《乌得勒支和约》后，争执不下的英法边界落在米萨瓜什河上。1750年5月，查尔斯·劳伦斯少校带八百人前来占地，法国人放火烧掉自己的城镇退过对岸；劳伦斯在废墟上筑起劳伦斯堡，法国人则在相邻山脊上修起五棱的博塞茹尔堡（1752年完工），又在贝尔特湾修了加斯帕罗堡，两国驻军在和平年代隔着一条小河互相盯防。博塞茹尔堡其实是从内部被卖掉的：书吏托马·皮雄收受英方银两，把工事图纸送给劳伦斯堡的指挥官，还劝自己这边不要加固城墙，后来有人称他为「阿卡迪亚的犹大」。1755年6月，罗伯特·蒙克顿率约两千名新英格兰兵，乘31艘运输船从波士顿而来；围城第十三天，一发炸弹砸穿一处掩蔽部的屋顶，守将韦尔戈尔投降，两年后他在魁北克受军法审判并被宣告无罪。加斯帕罗堡同日弃守，博塞茹尔堡更名坎伯兰堡，驱逐阿卡迪亚人的搜捕就从这座堡垒的大门开始。1776年秋，乔纳森·埃迪带着由新英格兰人、阿卡迪亚人、马勒西特人和米克马克人组成的叛军，为美国独立事业围攻此堡，直到哈利法克斯派来的军队把他们赶走。

en:
The broad, ice-free roadstead at Placentia is ringed by wide rocky beaches where cod can be salted and dried straight on the stones, without the wooden fishing stages other harbours required. In 1444 Beothuk bands, heirs of the island's Little Passage hunting tradition, still camped along the shore in season, taking salmon and seal and fishing the offshore grounds, and no European sail had yet rounded the headland. Within a century Basque fishermen from Biscay were using the bay as a seasonal base. They called it Plazençia, probably after Placencia de las Armas in Gipuzkoa, and a Basque seaman's will of 1563, asking that his body be buried in this port, is believed to be the oldest original civil document written in Canada.

France made Plaisance the capital of its Terre-Neuve colony in 1655 and fortified the hills above the roadstead, where Fort Plaisance and the Castle Hill works guarded the only French town on the island. English raiders sacked it in 1690, and in the winter of 1696-97 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville and Governor de Brouillan took the offensive from the bay: in three months their Canadians, Mi'kmaq and Abenakis destroyed twenty-three English settlements and burned St. John's, leaving only Bonavista and Carbonear in English hands. The Treaty of Utrecht ended the French colony in 1713. The settlers were shipped to the fortress then being built at Louisbourg, 116 men with their women and children, and their Mi'kmaq allies left with them. British soldiers held the Castle Hill works for the rest of the century. In 1786 Prince William Henry, the future William IV, commanded a frigate out of the harbour and spent the summer sitting as a surrogate judge; the town then held 1,500 to 2,000 people and still ranked with St. John's.
zh:
普拉森舍湾锚地开阔、终年不冻，湾内多宽阔岩滩，鳕鱼可以直接摊在石头上盐腌晾晒，不必像其他港口那样耗费木料搭建晒鱼台。1444年，贝奥图克人是岛上小通道狩猎传统的继承者，仍按季节在岸边扎营，在鲑鱼河和海豹场取获，到外海渔场捕鱼，海岬外还没有出现欧洲船帆。不出一个世纪，比斯开的巴斯克渔民已把这里当作季节性基地。他们称此地为普拉森西亚，名字大概取自吉普斯夸的普拉森西亚-德拉斯阿尔马斯；1563年一份巴斯克水手的遗嘱请求把自己葬在这个港口，这份文书被认为是加拿大现存最早的民间原件。

法国1655年将普莱桑斯定为纽芬兰殖民地的首府，在锚地上方的山丘层层设防，普莱桑斯堡和城堡山诸工事拱卫着岛上这座唯一的法国城镇。1690年英国劫掠者洗劫了它；1696至1697年冬，皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德伊贝维尔与布鲁扬总督从海湾出兵反攻，三个月间，麾下的加拿大移民、米克马克人和阿贝纳基人连毁二十三处英国人定居点，烧掉圣约翰斯，英国人只剩博纳维斯塔和卡博尼尔两处。1713年《乌得勒支条约》终结了这个法国殖民地，居民被迁往正在修建的路易斯堡，116名男子带着妻儿同行，结盟的米克马克人也一同离去。英军在城堡山工事驻守到该世纪末。1786年，后来成为威廉四世的威廉·亨利亲王率护卫舰驻泊港中，整夏代理审判；当时全城有一千五百至两千人，仍与圣约翰斯不相上下。

en:
Sikumiut means 'people of the sea ice', the name the Labrador Inuit gave their country of island chains, tide-split fjords and winter ice north of Hamilton Inlet. Finds on Okak Bay trace their settlement there to about 1200. In 1444 families moved with the ice and the animal migrations: they wintered in sod houses on the shore, raised skin tents in summer, and put out in kayaks and open umiaks after seal, whale and Arctic char while inland caribou herds supplied hides and winter food. No European mission or permanent trading post stood on the coast, and exchange still ran between Inuit families and neighboring peoples.

Basque whalers met Labrador Inuit in the 1500s, but a lasting European presence came only after Britain took the coast from France in 1763. Jens Haven, a Danish Moravian, founded Nain in 1771; the first Inuk baptized there, Kingminguse, took the name Petrus. Okak followed in 1776, its mission house cut and framed at Nain and freighted north, and the Brethren set up Hopedale at the Inuit settlement of Agvituk in 1782. Mikak, the daughter of an Inuit chief and one of the few Inuit of her day who had been to Europe and returned, ended her life at Nain. The stations drew families into settled villages and the Newfoundland trade, and in 1821 the northern coast was still a sparse chain of Inuit camps and Moravian stations, tied to sea ice and the annual mission boat rather than roads.
zh:
锡库缪特意为「海冰上的人」，是拉布拉多因纽特人对自己乡土的称呼；这片土地在哈密尔顿湾以北，岛链、受潮水切割的峡湾与冬季海冰交错。奥卡克湾的出土遗存显示，他们约1200年已在此居住。1444年，各个家庭随海冰和动物迁徙转换营地：冬天住在岸边草泥屋，夏天支起兽皮帐篷，乘皮艇和敞篷乌米亚克捕猎海豹、鲸和红点鲑，内陆驯鹿群则提供皮革和冬粮。海岸上没有欧洲传教站或固定贸易栈，物物交换仍在因纽特家庭与邻近族群之间进行。

16世纪，巴斯克捕鲸者已与拉布拉多因纽特人相遇，但欧洲人的持续存在要到1763年英国从法国手中取得海岸之后。丹麦籍摩拉维亚传教士延斯·黑文1771年建立内恩，第一名在此受洗的因纽特人金明古塞（Kingminguse）取教名彼得。1776年奥卡克随之建立，传教站房屋在内恩预制构件后海运北上；1782年，又在因纽特居点阿格维图克设立霍普代尔。因纽特酋长之女米卡克（Mikak）是那个时代少有的去过欧洲又活着回来的因纽特人，她最终在内恩度过晚年。这些站点把各个家庭吸引到定居村落，纳入纽芬兰贸易；1821年的北岸仍是一条稀疏的因纽特营地与摩拉维亚站点链，把它们连起来的是海冰和一年一度的传教船，而不是道路。

en:
The name Naskapi, 'people beyond the horizon', was used in the seventeenth century for the Innu groups living beyond missionary reach, the nomadic northern kin of the Montagnais of the St Lawrence shore. Their country, St'aschinuw, 'our land', stretched between Ungava Bay, Hudson Bay and the Torngat Mountains, its heart the barrens and lake crossings of southern Labrador, above all Ashuanipi, whose name means 'a place to cross'; routes led from there down the Moisie to the St Lawrence North Shore or north toward Okak. In 1444 small bands followed the caribou herds, took lake trout and char, pitched skin tents at sheltered crossings, and moved between Innu and Inuit neighbours. No mission, fur post or fixed settlement stood in the interior.

Europeans knew this country only from reports carried south.
