Around 1643 the Jesuit André Richard noted the Ounackkapiouek among the small nations north of Tadoussac, and in 1733 the name Naskapi appeared for the first time, in accounts placing about forty families at Ashuanipi; later fur-trade and Moravian reports from Okak used variants such as Annes-carps and Nascopies for the same inland people. Anglo-French claims shifted after 1763 and Labrador passed to Newfoundland in 1809, yet no colonial administration reached the barrens. In 1820 the Hudson's Bay Company man James Clouston descended the Caniapiscau, and a year later the interior still had no permanent company trading post.
zh:
纳斯卡皮意为「地平线之外的人」，17世纪时用来称呼生活在传教影响之外的因努群体，他们是圣劳伦斯海岸蒙塔格奈人偏北的游牧亲族。其故土斯塔希努（St'aschinuw）意为「我们的土地」，伸展于昂加瓦湾、哈德逊湾与通戈山脉之间，核心是拉布拉多南部的冻原与湖上渡口，首推阿舒阿尼皮湖，湖名意为「可以横渡之地」；从这里可顺穆瓦西河通往圣劳伦斯河北岸，也可向北前往奥卡克。1444年，小队人群跟随驯鹿群迁徙，捕捞湖鳟和红点鲑，在避风渡口支起兽皮帐篷，往来于因努与因纽特邻人之间。腹地中没有传教站、毛皮栈或固定聚落。

欧洲人很久只能通过南来的传闻知道这片土地。约1643年，耶稣会士安德烈·里夏尔记下了塔杜萨克以北诸小族中的乌纳卡皮乌埃克人（Ounackkapiouek）；1733年，纳斯卡皮一名首次见于记载，称约四十个家庭在阿舒阿尼皮湖一带有重要营地。后来的毛皮商人和奥卡克的摩拉维亚传教士又以安内斯卡普（Annes-carps）、纳斯科皮（Nascopies）等名字称呼这支腹地居民。英法间的主权归属在1763年后改变，拉布拉多又于1809年划归纽芬兰，但没有殖民行政力量进入冻原。1820年，哈德逊湾公司职员詹姆斯·克拉克斯顿沿卡尼亚皮斯科河下行；一年之后，内陆仍没有固定的公司贸易站。

en:
The Mingan River comes out of the spruce forest into the Gulf of St Lawrence beside a long chain of low limestone islands, and the Innu called the river-mouth Ekuanitshit, 'the place where something is washed ashore', perhaps for the whales that stranded among the islands. It was one of their principal summer camps. Families who had wintered far inland on caribou came down to spear salmon, hunt whale and seal and meet the other bands in trade, then paddled back upriver before freeze-up. In 1444 nothing European stood on this shore, and the islands were empty of people through the winter.

In 1661 the French crown granted the Mingan seignory, the first holding on this stretch of coast, and a fur post went up at the river-mouth. In 1680 Louis XIV gave the archipelago, together with Anticosti Island, to Louis Jolliet as the reward for his journeys: Jolliet had traced the Mississippi and reconnoitred the shores of Hudson Bay. From his seignory he traded muskets, powder and trade goods to the Montagnais and the Papinachois of the upper rivers for sealskins. The Innu never settled beside the post, but came in each summer with their furs and left again for the caribou season. The North West Company ran the post for a time, and in 1807 it passed to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
明根河穿出云杉林注入圣劳伦斯湾，河口外横着一长串低矮的石灰岩岛屿。因努人称河口为埃夸尼楚（Ekuanitshit），意即「有东西被冲上岸的地方」，大概指常在群岛间搁浅的鲸。这里是他们主要的夏日营地之一：在远方内陆猎驯鹿越冬的各家来到海边，叉鲑鱼、捕鲸和海豹、与其他部族聚会交易，封冻前再划着独木舟溯河而返。1444年时，岸上没有任何欧洲人造物，群岛在冬天也荒无人踪。

1661年，法国王室封授明根领地，这是这段海岸上的第一处法国产业，河口随之建起毛皮站。1680年，路易十四把明根群岛连同安蒂科斯蒂岛一并赐给路易·若列，酬报他的远行：若列曾溯密西西比河探察，又踏勘过哈德逊湾沿岸。他在领地内向蒙塔涅人和上游各河的帕皮纳舒瓦人出售火枪、火药和杂货，换取海豹皮。因努人从不在贸易站旁定居，每年夏天携毛皮而来，驯鹿季一到便走。贸易站一度由西北公司经营，1807年转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Two broad rivers break this coast, the Manicouagan and the Betsiamites. The band that held the shore between their mouths was the Bersimis, the Pessamit Innu, for Pessamit means 'the place of lampreys'; the Papinachois lived up the Betsiamites and the Ouchestigouetch at the head of the Manicouagan. Summer brought the families down to the river-mouths for salmon, seal and the lamprey runs, and winter scattered them far inland after caribou. Samuel de Champlain marked the Bersimis on his map of 1632 as the Sauvages Bersiamiste, their first appearance in a French record. In 1444 no European ship had yet traded on either river.

Jacques Cartier noted the Manicouagan mouth without naming it as he sailed past in 1535. After the French opened the trade at Tadoussac, down the coast to the west, the Bersimis became among their earliest native allies. In June 1664 the Jesuit Henri Nouvel became the first European to ascend the Manicouagan, the river the Innu called Manikouaganistikou and the French later named the Rivière Noire; other missionaries followed him to the summer gatherings. The Innu of the coast signed the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. In 1733 Intendant Gilles Hocquart had a fur post built at Pointe-des-Bersimites on the Betsiamites. The post was later leased to the North West Company, and in 1821 it passed with that company to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
这段海岸有两条大河入海：马尼夸根河与贝齐亚米特河。据有两河之间海岸的是贝尔西米人，即佩萨穆因努人，佩萨米特意为「七鳃鳗之地」；帕皮纳舒瓦人住在贝齐亚米特河上游，乌谢斯蒂古埃奇人住在马尼夸根河源头。夏天，各家来到河口捕鲑鱼、海豹，趁七鳃鳗洄游时捕捞七鳃鳗；冬天则四散深入内陆追猎驯鹿。尚普兰1632年的地图把他们标作贝尔西亚米斯特人，这是法国人对这支人的最早记载。1444年时，还没有欧洲船只到这两条河上贸易。

1535年卡蒂亚驶过这段海岸，记下马尼夸根河口却没有为它命名。法国人在西边海岸的塔杜萨克开埠贸易后，贝尔西米人成为他们最早的土著盟友之一。1664年6月，耶稣会士亨利·努韦尔成为第一个溯马尼夸根河而上的欧洲人；因努人称这条河为马尼夸加尼斯蒂库，法国人后来称它为黑河。其他传教士也循着他的足迹来到夏日聚点。1701年，海岸上的因努人签署《蒙特利尔大和约》。1733年，新法兰西行政长官吉勒·奥卡尔下令在贝齐亚米特河畔的贝尔西米特角修建毛皮站。该站后来租给西北公司，1821年随该公司并入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
Anticosti is a long, forested island lying across the mouth of the St Lawrence where the gulf narrows into the Jacques Cartier and Honguedo straits. The Innu called it Notiskuan, 'where bears are hunted'. For thousands of years mainland parties crossed the narrow water in summer to hunt bear and net salmon in its rivers, but no one wintered on it. In 1444 it lay uninhabited, a fog-bound hunting ground that mainland bands still crossed to each summer and left again before the ice.

Jacques Cartier made the first European report of the island in 1534, and on 15 August 1535, sailing past on the feast of the Assumption, he named it Île de l'Assomption. In 1680 Louis XIV granted it, with the Mingan Archipelago, to Louis Jolliet in payment for his reconnoitring of the Mississippi and Hudson Bay. Jolliet raised a fortified post against Inuit raiders and the following spring settled on the island with his wife, four children and six servants, bartering arms and goods to Montagnais hunters for sealskins. In the winter of 1690 Massachusetts troops under William Phips, retreating from their failed attack on Quebec, seized the fort. When Jolliet died, a lawsuit among his heirs left the island to his three sons, who held it until the Treaty of Paris gave it to Britain in 1763. Its owners then changed twice more, Newfoundland in 1774 returning it to Quebec and Newfoundland taking it again in 1809. The island stayed a remote timber seigneurie whose few inhabitants lived by cod fishing and the fur trade.
zh:
安蒂科斯蒂是一座狭长的森林大岛，横在圣劳伦斯河口，海湾在岛的两侧收窄为雅克·卡蒂亚海峡与翁格多海峡。因努人称它为诺蒂斯宽（Notiskuan），意即「猎熊之地」。几千年来，大陆上的人夏天渡过狭窄的海面上岛猎熊、在岛河中网鲑鱼，却从没有人在岛上过冬。1444年时，岛上无人居住，只是一座雾中的猎场，大陆各部仍每年夏天渡海而来、封冻前离去。

1534年，卡蒂亚首次向欧洲记载此岛；1535年8月15日圣母升天节，他再次绕过该岛，将它命名为圣母升天岛。1680年，路易十四把此岛连同明根群岛封给路易·若列，作为他探察密西西比河与哈德逊湾的酬报。若列筑起设防据点防备因纽特人袭掠，第二年春天带着妻子、四个孩子和六名仆人上岛定居，用武器和杂货向蒙塔涅猎人换取海豹皮。1690年冬，威廉·菲普斯麾下攻打魁北克失利的马萨诸塞部队在撤退途中占领了这座堡垒。若列去世后，继承人为遗产打了一场官司，岛屿最终归他的三个儿子，一直保有到1763年《巴黎条约》把它让给英国。此后归属又两度变更：1774年由纽芬兰交还魁北克，1809年再度并入纽芬兰。这座偏远的林木封地居民寥寥，几户人家靠捕鳕鱼和毛皮贸易为生。

en:
Pekuakami is the Innu name of the broad, shallow lake the French called Lac Saint-Jean, set in the Laurentian highlands and drained by the Saguenay River on its way to the Saint Lawrence. Its people are the Pekuakamiulnuatsh, 'the people of Pekuakami', the Innu band the French knew as the Montagnais. They followed the shoreline and the surrounding boreal forest, hunting caribou and moose, fishing through the ice and taking beaver, and in summer families gathered at river-mouth points such as Métabetchouane to meet and trade. In 1444 no European had yet seen the lake, deep in the Innu country called Nitassinan.

The Montagnais became France's first allies on the Saint Lawrence once trade opened at Tadoussac: Champlain sealed the alliance in 1603, and their warriors went with him on his 1609 campaign against the Iroquois. On 17 July 1647 the Jesuit Jean de Quen came up the Saguenay and became the first European to reach Pekuakami, where he said mass on the shore. In 1652 Governor Jean de Lauson raised a fur post at Métabetchouane, inside the king's own domain, land kept back from private settlement; a Jesuit mission joined the post in 1676, but in 1697 it was closed and its trade moved to Chicoutimi. Iroquois war parties raided the lake country through those decades, until the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701. After the British conquest the post reopened, and between 1760 and 1778 its traders put up a stone powder magazine. The North West Company ran the post from 1802, and in 1821 it passed with the company into Hudson's Bay Company hands.
zh:
佩夸卡米是因努语对这片宽阔浅水湖的称呼，法国人后来叫它圣让湖。湖坐落在劳伦琴高原之间，湖水经萨格奈河流向圣劳伦斯河。湖畔居民是佩夸卡米乌尔努阿奇，意为「佩夸卡米人」，属因努人的一支，法国人称之为蒙塔涅人。他们循着湖岸和周围的针叶林迁徙，猎驯鹿与驼鹿、冰下捕鱼、诱捕海狸；夏天各家聚到梅塔贝楚安等河流入湖处相会交易。1444年时还没有欧洲人见过这座湖，它深藏在因努人称作尼塔希南的土地腹地。

圣劳伦斯河上的贸易在塔杜萨克开场后，蒙塔涅人成为法国人在这条河上最早的盟友。尚普兰1603年与他们缔盟，1609年他们的战士随他出征易洛魁人。1647年7月17日，耶稣会士让·德康溯萨格奈河而上，成为第一个抵达佩夸卡米的欧洲人，并在湖边做了弥撒。1652年，总督让·德洛松在梅塔贝楚安建起毛皮贸易站，站点位于国王直辖领地内，这片土地不授予私人开垦；1676年站内增设耶稣会传教所，但1697年贸易站关闭，生意并入希库蒂米。那些年里易洛魁战团屡屡深入湖区劫掠，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和约》才告平息。英国征服后贸易站重开，1760至1778年间商人们修起一座石砌火药库。西北公司自1802年起经营此站，1821年贸易站随公司一并转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Atikamekw is the upper Saint-Maurice country that its people call Nitaskinan, 'our land': a boreal stretch of lakes, spruce forest and family hunting grounds above the later French town of Trois-Rivières. In 1444 its people gathered at riverside places such as Wemotaci in summer, then split into small winter camps to fish under the ice, hunt moose and trap beaver. Birchbark canoes carried them through the open-water months and snowshoes through the snow, and no European had yet reached the territory.

French documents first mention the Atikamekw early in the seventeenth century, writing their name as Atikamegouékhi and describing them as a nation of five or six hundred people. As the fur trade moved in, beaver pelts went down the Saint-Maurice to Trois-Rivières and metal tools came back, but French seigneurial farms never passed the river mouth, so the upper country stayed with Atikamekw hunters rather than habitants. Wemotaci first appears in a written source in 1724. Jean-Baptiste Perrault built the first confirmed trading post there in 1806, and the Hudson's Bay Company took it over in 1821.
zh:
阿蒂卡梅库是阿蒂卡梅库人称作尼塔斯基南（意为「我们的土地」）的地方，位于圣莫里斯河上游、后来的三河城以北，是一片由湖泊、云杉林和家族猎场组成的北方土地。1444年，人们夏季在韦莫塔奇等河畔地点聚集，入冬后分成小群营地，在冰下捕鱼、猎取驼鹿并诱捕河狸。开水时节桦皮舟载着他们往来，雪季则靠雪鞋穿行，当时还没有欧洲人到过这片土地。

法国文献在17世纪初首次提到阿蒂卡梅库人，把他们的名字记作阿蒂卡梅古埃基，称这是一个五六百人的部族。毛皮贸易进入后，河狸皮沿圣莫里斯河运往三河城，金属工具溯流而回，但法国人的领主农庄始终没有越过河口，河流上游依旧是阿蒂卡梅库猎人的天地，没有出现农户。韦莫塔奇一名最早见于1724年的文字记载。1806年，让-巴蒂斯特·佩罗建起第一座可确认的商站，1821年该站转入哈德逊湾公司之手。

en:
Timiskaming is a long, deep lake on the Ottawa River, at the corner where the water turns from its northwestern course toward Montreal. It runs 110 kilometres and drops in places to 216 metres, and its Algonquin name was Temi Kami. At Obadjiwan, the narrows where the two shores come within 250 metres of each other, Algonquin families kept a summer camp, fishing the lake and hunting beaver and moose in the surrounding forest. In 1444 the country was Anishinaabe land, and the lake lay about halfway along the forty-day canoe route between Montreal and James Bay by way of Lake Abitibi.

The Chevalier de Troyes led the first Europeans over the whole route in 1686, while France and England were still at peace. His canoes carried a raiding party north to seize the Hudson's Bay Company posts at Moose Factory, Rupert House and Fort Albany and to take the company ship Craven; Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville, later the founder of the French colony of Louisiana, was one of his junior officers. A Montreal merchants' post built on the west shore about 1679 had been destroyed by the Iroquois in 1688, and in 1720 French traders raised Fort Témiscamingue at the Obadjiwan narrows, on the old Algonquin campground. For forty years the post traded guns, brandy and ironware for furs. After the fall of New France it passed to independent traders and then to the North West Company in 1788, whose brigades carried the northern furs down the Ottawa to Montreal.
zh:
蒂米斯卡明是渥太华河上一道又长又深的湖，正处在河水由西北流向折向蒙特利尔的拐角处。湖长110公里，最深处达216米，阿尔冈昆语名作特米卡米。两岸相距不足250米的奥巴吉万（Obadjiwan，意为「水流湍急的狭口」）设有阿尔冈昆家族的夏季营地，他们在湖中捕鱼，到周围森林猎取河狸与驼鹿。1444年，这片土地属于阿尼希纳贝人，湖的位置大约在蒙特利尔至詹姆斯湾四十天独木舟航程的中点，中途经阿比蒂比湖。

1686年，法国军官德·特鲁瓦（de Troyes）率队在英法两国尚未开战之时取道此湖北上，成为首批走完整条航路的欧洲人。这支奇兵突袭哈得孙湾公司，连夺穆斯法克特里、鲁珀特堡和奥尔巴尼堡三处商站，还俘获了公司的「克雷文号」商船；后来创建法属路易斯安那的皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·迪贝维尔当时还是他手下的年轻军官。约1679年蒙特利尔商人在湖西岸建起的商栈，1688年被易洛魁人摧毁；1720年，法国商人在奥巴吉万狭口、旧日的阿尔冈昆营地处筑起蒂米斯卡明堡，四十年来以枪支、白兰地和铁器交换毛皮。新法兰西陷落后，商栈先由独立商人接手，1788年转入西北公司之手，北方的毛皮仍由成队独木舟沿渥太华河南运蒙特利尔。

en:
Animouski is the Algonquian name the French wrote as Rimouski, a river that enters the lower St. Lawrence estuary on this forested south shore between the Bic headland and Matane. In 1444 Wolastoqiyik, the Maliseet bands of the Wabanaki confederacy, moved with the seasons between these river mouths and the inland lakes, taking salmon, seal and moose, while Mi'kmaq parties from the east used the same coast. Two carrying places ran from here toward Chaleur Bay and the Saint John River, the Matapédia and the Témiscouata. Before any European settled, Basque whalers occupied Île aux Basques off Trois-Pistoles from 1584 to about 1637, rendering blubber in four stone ovens along the shore; a Jesuit visiting in 1664 found the great ribs of their whales still lying beside the ruined ovens.

Early in the seventeenth century La Rochelle merchants ran a fur post at Matane, trading European goods with the Mi'kmaq. The French granted more than twenty seigneuries along this coast, but settlers came slowly: the seigneury of Rimouski was granted in 1688 and occupied only in 1696, when René Lepage brought his family over from the Île d'Orléans. At the British conquest of 1760 a few dozen families held just four seigneuries between Rivière-du-Loup and Matane. A road over the Témiscouata portage opened toward British New Brunswick around 1783, and migrants from the older parishes then filled the river mouths; even so, in 1790 the whole shore held only about 1,250 people. The lighthouse raised on Île Verte between 1806 and 1809 was the first on the St. Lawrence.
zh:
阿尼莫斯基是阿尔冈昆语地名，法国人后来写作「里穆斯基」；里穆斯基河在这片森林南岸注入圣劳伦斯河口湾，海岸介于比克海岬与马塔纳之间。1444年，瓦巴纳基联盟的沃拉斯托奇人（马勒西特诸游群）随季节往返于这些河口和内陆湖泊之间，捕鲑鱼、猎海豹与驼鹿，东方来的米克马克游群也使用同一片海岸。马塔佩迪亚和塔米斯库塔两条搬运道从这里通向沙勒尔湾和圣约翰河。欧洲人尚未定居的年代，巴斯克捕鲸人在1584年至约1637年间占据特鲁瓦皮斯托勒外海的巴斯克岛，在岸边四座石炉里熬炼鲸油；1664年一位耶稣会士到访时，废炉旁还堆着巨大的鲸肋。

17世纪初，拉罗谢尔商人在马塔纳经营毛皮商站，用欧洲货与米克马克人交易。法国在这一带沿海封出二十多个领地，定居者却来得很慢：里穆斯基领地1688年封出，直到1696年勒内·勒帕热率全家从奥尔良岛迁来才有人常住。1760年英国征服时，从里维耶尔迪卢到马塔纳之间只有数十户人家、四个领地。1783年前后，一条翻越塔米斯库塔搬运道、通往英属新不伦瑞克的道路开通，来自老教区的移民这才陆续充实各个河口；即便如此，1790年整条海岸也只有约1250人。1806至1809年，绿岛上建起圣劳伦斯河上的第一座灯塔。

en:
Kikonteku is Kik8ntekw, 'River of the Fields' in Abenaki, the Chaudière that runs north from the Appalachian lakes and drops into the St. Lawrence over a churning fall opposite the rock of Quebec. In 1444 Abenaki and Etchemin bands paddled its length as a canoe road between the St. Lawrence, the Kennebec and the Atlantic, while St. Lawrence Iroquoian villagers of Stadacona fished and farmed the bank near the mouth. Cartier passed this shore on his way to Stadacona in 1535, Champlain later charted the water as the Etchemin River, and in 1629 he named the cape facing the city Cap de Lévy.

The cape became the seigneury of Lauzon in 1636, though its first settler, the former Jesuit interpreter Guillaume Couture, did not arrive until 1647. When Phips attacked Quebec in October 1690, English raiders burned the Pointe-Lévy settlements, and Couture, seventy-two years old, led the militia against them. The height was turned against Quebec in the summer of 1759: Wolfe's troops under Monckton seized the point, made it their main camp, and for about seventy days shelled the city from the cliffs before it fell. A grimmer local fame came in 1763, when the British hanged Marie-Josephte Corriveau for killing her husband and hung her body for weeks in an iron cage at Pointe-Lévy, the first gibbeting in British North America. In November 1775 Benedict Arnold's six hundred survivors, having marched through the Maine wilderness and down the Chaudière, crossed from this point on their way to their failed New Year's Eve assault on the city.
zh:
基康特库（Kik8ntekw）在阿布纳基语中意为「田野之河」，即肖迪耶尔河。它从阿巴拉契亚湖群向北流，在魁北克巨岩对岸越过翻滚的瀑布注入圣劳伦斯河。1444年，阿布纳基和埃切明游群把它当作独木舟通道，往来于圣劳伦斯河、肯纳贝克河与大西洋之间，圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的斯塔达科纳村民则在河口附近捕鱼种田。1535年卡蒂亚驶往斯塔达科纳时经过此岸；尚普兰后来把这条水道标作「埃切明河」，1629年又将魁北克对岸的海角命名为莱维角。

海角上的土地1636年封作洛宗领地，但第一个定居者、当过耶稣会翻译的纪尧姆·库蒂尔直到1647年才到来。1690年10月菲普斯攻打魁北克，英军焚毁莱维角的房舍，七十二岁的库蒂尔率民兵迎击。1759年夏，这片高地被用来对付对岸的魁北克：沃尔夫麾下孟克顿的部队夺取该角，把主营设在这里，崖上炮台隔河轰城约七十天，魁北克最终陷落。1763年，这里又出了一桩骇人的名案：英国人以杀夫罪绞死玛丽约瑟夫·科里沃（习称拉科里沃），把她的尸体装在铁笼里吊在莱维角示众数周，这是英属北美第一次以这种方式悬尸示众。1775年11月，本尼迪克特·阿诺德的六百名残兵穿过缅因荒原、顺肖迪耶尔河抵达此地，从这里渡河北上，新年前夜的攻城以失败告终。

en:
The Masoliantekw, an Abenaki name meaning 'the water where there is plenty of food', is the river the French first called the Rivière aux Iroquois and later the Richelieu. It runs north from Lake Champlain to the St. Lawrence through fertile bottoms and the Chambly rapids, the easiest canoe route into Canada from the south. In 1444 its lower valley held the maize fields and longhouses of the St. Lawrence Iroquoians, and the river carried traffic between their villages, Lake Champlain and the Mohawk country, while Abenaki bands ranged the eastern bank.

Jacques Cartier sighted the mouth in the 1530s, and when Samuel de Champlain came up the river in 1603 the Iroquoian villages had vanished. In 1609 Champlain joined a Huron, Algonquin and Montagnais war party through the river into Lake Champlain, opening the long French quarrel with the Mohawk; on 19 June 1610 the same allies caught and destroyed a Mohawk band at the mouth in the battle of Sorel. The French raised Fort Richelieu there in 1641 and lost it to fire six years later, and in 1665 the Carignan-Salières regiment rebuilt the post and ran up a chain of forts along the banks: Fort Saint-Louis at the Chambly rapids, Fort Sainte-Therese, and Fort Saint-Jean, finished in 1666.

Settlers then took up the fertile river lots. After the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701 the forts no longer faced the Iroquois, and Governor Vaudreuil had Fort Chambly rebuilt in stone between 1709 and 1711; the line of strongholds gave the Richelieu valley its nickname of the valley of forts. The whole chain passed to Britain in August 1760. American troops took Fort Chambly on 20 October 1775 during the invasion of Canada, wintered there and burned it in the spring of 1776 as they fell back on Ticonderoga, after which Loyalists settled the river lots.
zh:
马索利安特库（Masoliantekw）是阿布纳基语河名，意为「食物丰足之水」；法国人起初叫它易洛魁河，后来改称黎塞留河。河水自尚普兰湖北流，穿过肥沃低地和尚布利急滩注入圣劳伦斯河，也是从南方进入加拿大最便捷的独木舟通道。1444年，下游谷地分布着圣劳伦斯易洛魁人的玉米地和长屋，河上往来着他们的村寨、尚普兰湖与莫霍克之地之间的交通，河东一带有阿布纳基人游猎。

1530年代，雅克·卡蒂埃望见它的河口；塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1603年溯河而上时，易洛魁人的村寨已经消失。1609年，尚普兰随休伦人、阿尔冈昆人和蒙塔涅人（Montagnais）的战队经此河北上尚普兰湖，开启了法国与莫霍克人的长期敌对；1610年6月19日，还是这些盟军在河口的索莱尔之战围住并歼灭一支莫霍克队伍。1641年法国人在河口兴建黎塞留堡，六年后堡垒被焚；1665年卡里尼昂-萨利埃团被派到这里，重建黎塞留堡，又沿河谷筑起一串据点：尚布利急滩畔的圣路易堡、圣泰蕾兹堡，以及1666年落成的圣让堡。

移民随后到肥沃的河岸领垦。1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》之后，各堡失去了防备易洛魁人的用途，沃德勒伊总督下令在1709至1711年间以石材重建尚布利堡，这串要塞也使黎塞留河谷得了「要塞之谷」的别称。1760年8月，整条要塞链落入英国之手。1775年10月20日，美军在入侵加拿大之役攻占尚布利堡，在那里过了一冬，1776年春退回提康德罗加时将堡焚毁，此后效忠派在沿河授地上定居。

en:
Arendaronon is the country between Coldwater and Orillia, where the trails from the Huron ridges descend to the narrow channel joining Lake Couchiching and Lake Simcoe. In the channel stood the Mnjikaning weirs, fences of cedar and maple stakes that Wendat fishermen had kept up for thousands of years, funnelling the spawning runs into enclosures where they could be speared or netted; the Mohawk called them tkaronto, and that name travelled south with the canoe portage to Lake Ontario and settled on the city of Toronto. Palisaded longhouse villages with cornfields stood on the light soils near Hawkestone, and the carrying place from Lake Ontario ended at the narrows, bringing southern traders to the fisheries. In 1444 this was the exposed eastern flank of Wendake, facing Algonquin neighbours and raiders from across the lakes; the Rock People who gave the province its name entered the Wendat confederacy only around 1590 and made Cahiagué their chief town.

When Samuel de Champlain reached Cahiagué in 1615 he counted about 200 longhouses in the Rock capital, the chief town of the confederacy, and on 1 September he passed the weirs with a Wendat-Algonquin war party bound for a Haudenosaunee village south of Lake Ontario. The Rock chief Atironta, already known to the French, travelled to Quebec as Champlain's guest the next year. The Jesuits founded the mission of Saint-Jean-Baptiste at Cahiagué in 1639-1640, and when the missionaries met hostility a chief who had taken the name Atironta sheltered Antoine Daniel and Simon Le Moyne. The easternmost of the Wendat nations took the first shock of the Beaver Wars: epidemics and the Haudenosaunee invasion of 1649 shattered their towns, and the survivors fled toward Quebec or were absorbed into the Five Nations. The old weirs were still fished in the early 1700s. Ojibwe bands afterwards used the trail and the lakeshore, and the British treaties of 1798, 1815 and 1818, followed by the Penetanguishene Road, opened the country between Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay to settlement.
zh:
阿伦达罗嫩地处科尔德沃特与奥里利亚之间，休伦人山岭上的小路在此下降，通向连接库钦钦湖与锡姆科湖的狭窄水道。水道里立着姆尼吉卡宁（Mnjikaning）鱼梁：白雪杉和糖枫木桩编成的栅栏，温达特渔人数千年来持续维护，把洄游鱼群赶入围栏，再用鱼叉或渔网捞取；莫霍克人称鱼梁为特卡龙托（tkaronto），这个名字随独木舟联运线南传到安大略湖，最后落在了湖畔的多伦多城。霍克斯通附近疏松的土地上分布着木栅围护的长屋村和玉米田，从安大略湖北上的水陆联运道止于窄水道，南方商人因此来到渔场。1444年时，这里是温达克朝东敞开的一翼，面向阿尔冈昆邻族和湖对岸的袭掠者；赋予本省名称的岩族约1590年才加入温达特联盟，并以卡希亚盖（Cahiagué）为主村。

1615年塞缪尔·德·尚普兰抵达卡希亚盖时，点数这座岩族首府约有两百座长屋，为联盟首镇；9月1日，他随一支温达特—阿尔冈昆战队经过鱼梁，去攻安大略湖以南的一座豪德诺索尼村落。岩族首领阿蒂龙塔（Atironta）此前已与法人相识，次年作为尚普兰的客人前往魁北克。1639至1640年，耶稣会在卡希亚盖设立圣让巴蒂斯特传教站；传教士遭到敌视时，一位承袭阿蒂龙塔之名的首领庇护了安托万·达尼埃尔和西蒙·勒穆瓦纳。作为温达特最东面的族群，岩族最先承受海狸战争的打击：疫病和1649年豪德诺索尼人的入侵摧毁其村镇，幸存者逃往魁北克，或被五族联盟吸纳。老鱼梁一直使用到18世纪初。此后奥吉布瓦游群往来于旧道与湖岸，1798年、1815年和1818年的英国条约及随后修通的佩内唐吉申路，把锡姆科湖与乔治亚湾之间的土地开放给移民。

en:
Tionontate covers the cold south-western shore of Georgian Bay, where the limestone ridge of the Niagara Escarpment meets the inlets and low shore around Nottawasaga Bay. In 1444 the country belonged to the Tionontati, an Iroquoian confederacy related to but separate from the Wendat. French visitors later called them the Petun or Tobacco Nation after the crop grown in their fields and carried to neighbouring markets; their own name referred to people of the standing mountain. Eight to ten palisaded longhouse villages stood above the bay, divided between the Wolf and Deer groups. Cornfields, fishing stations and hunting camps supported the villagers, and trails ran about a day's journey to Wendat country while canoes carried tobacco and skins through the upper Great Lakes.

Samuel de Champlain reached Georgian Bay in 1615-1616 and listed about eight Petun villages. Epidemics after 1634 cut the population heavily, and French trade drew the Petun closer to their Wendat neighbours during the Beaver Wars. In March 1649 Wendat refugees crossed frozen Nottawasaga Bay after Haudenosaunee forces overran Huronia. By the end of the year those forces had destroyed most Petun villages; survivors fled with Odawa canoe parties and joined Wendat refugees in the people later called the Wyandot. The Ojibwe name used for the Nottawasaga River meant the Iroquois river-mouth, a warning rooted in raids through that approach.

The river mouth still mattered in 1814, when the former fur-trade schooner Nancy carried British supplies to Michilimackinac. An American squadron trapped her there on 14 August, and her crew set Nancy on fire rather than surrender the ship and stores. Lieutenant Miller Worsley escaped by canoe, returned with a small party, and captured the American schooners Tigress and Scorpion in the channels leading to Michilimackinac.
zh:
提奥嫩塔特位于乔治亚湾寒冷的西南岸，尼亚加拉陡崖的石灰岩山脊在这里接上诺塔瓦萨加湾周围的水湾与低岸。1444年，这片土地属于提奥嫩塔提人；他们是与温达特人亲缘相近、政治上各自独立的易洛魁语族群联盟。法兰西访客后来因他们种植并卖到邻族市场的烟草，称他们为佩琴人或烟草民族；他们的自称则指山陵矗立之地的人。八至十座设有栅栏的长屋村落俯瞰海湾，分属狼部与鹿部。玉米田、捕鱼点和猎营供养村民，小路约走一日可到温达特人的地域，独木舟则载着烟草和兽皮穿行五大湖上游。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在1615年至1616年抵达乔治亚湾，列出约八座佩琴村落。1634年后疫病使人口大减，海狸战争期间的法兰西贸易又让佩琴人与温达特邻邦走得更近。1649年3月，豪德诺索尼军队攻灭休伦尼亚，温达特难民越过冰封的诺塔瓦萨加湾。同年年底，这支军队摧毁了大部分佩琴村落；幸存者随奥达人的独木舟队离开，与温达特难民汇合，成为后来所称怀安多特人的一部分。诺塔瓦萨加河的奥吉布瓦语名称意为「易洛魁河口」，警示就来自沿这条水道袭来的劫掠。

到1814年，河口仍有军事价值。原为毛皮贸易船的纵帆船「南希号」当时负责向米希利马基诺运送英军补给。8月14日，一支美国分舰队在河口困住该船，船员纵火焚毁「南希号」，以免船和物资落入美方手中。米勒·沃斯利中尉乘独木舟脱身，随后率小队折返，在通往米希利马基诺的水道上夺取美国纵帆船「蒂格雷斯号」和「斯科皮恩号」。

en:
Odawa is the lake country of the Bruce Peninsula and Manitoulin Island, where the wooded Niagara Escarpment runs into Lake Huron and breaks into islands, straits and sheltered anchorages along the North Channel. In 1444 it was the original homeland of the Odawa, Anishinaabe members of the Council of Three Fires. Their name came from adaawe, 'to trade', and birchbark canoes linked Georgian Bay, the North Channel, Sault Ste. Marie and Green Bay. They carried cornmeal, sunflower oil, furs and skins, mats, tobacco and medicinal roots. Manitoulin took its name from an underwater cave where a powerful spirit was said to live; its fishing rivers and lee shores gave the trading families camps and meeting places.

Samuel de Champlain met about 300 Odawa warriors near the French River in 1615. He called them the Cheveux Relevés for their dressed hair, noted their bows, boiled-leather shields, clubs, tattoos and face paint, and visited their country west of the Wendat in 1616. The Odawa became the principal middlemen for New France in the upper-lakes fur trade. For much of the mid-seventeenth century they controlled most of the fur traffic through Green Bay and Sault Ste. Marie, sending beaver, deer, marten, raccoon, fox, otter and muskrat pelts east and receiving metal goods, blankets and firearms.

The Jesuit Joseph Poncet founded a mission near Wiikwemkoong on Manitoulin in 1648, naming the island Isle de Sainte-Marie. Disease and Haudenosaunee raids shattered the settlement, and in 1650 surviving Anishinaabe burned their villages as they withdrew; Odawa oral tradition links the fires to purification after disease. Many families made for Michilimackinac and the upper lakes. French traders still used the channels while Manitoulin remained mostly uninhabited for about 150 years. After the War of 1812, Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi families began returning to the island, and by 1821 the old homeland was being reoccupied.
zh:
渥太华是布鲁斯半岛与马尼图林岛一带的湖乡，林木覆盖的尼亚加拉陡崖在这里伸入休伦湖，散成岛屿、海峡和北海峡沿岸的避风锚地。1444年，这里是渥太华人原本的故地，他们是阿尼什纳比人三火议会的成员。族名来自意为「贸易」的词，桦皮独木舟把乔治亚湾、北海峡、苏圣玛丽和格林贝连接起来，运送玉米粉、葵花油、毛皮、席子、烟草和药根。马尼图林的名字来自一个水下洞穴，相传其中住着强大精灵；岛上的渔河和避风岸为贸易家族提供营地与会合点。

1615年，塞缪尔·德·尚普兰在弗伦奇河附近见到约三百名渥太华战士。他因他们的发式称之为「高发髻人」，记下他们的弓、煮皮盾牌、棍棒、文身和面饰，并在1616年走访了温达特人以西的渥太华地域。渥太华人后来成为新法兰西五大湖上游毛皮贸易的主要中介。17世纪中期的大部分时间里，他们控制着经格林贝和苏圣玛丽流通的大部分毛皮，把海狸、鹿、貂、浣熊、狐、水獭和麝鼠皮运往东方，换回金属器具、毛毯和火器。

1648年，耶稣会士约瑟夫·庞塞在马尼图林的威奎米孔附近设立传教站，把该岛命名为圣玛丽岛。疫病和豪德诺索尼人的袭击摧毁了这一定居点。1650年，幸存的阿尼什纳比人撤离时焚毁村落；渥太华口述传统把这些火与疫病后的净化联系在一起。许多家庭前往米希利马基诺和五大湖上游。此后约一百五十年间，马尼图林几乎无人长期居住，法兰西商人仍继续穿行其海峡。1812年战争结束后，渥太华、奥吉布瓦和波塔瓦托米家庭开始返回岛上，到1821年，这片旧地正重新有人定居。

en:
The Piscatang country centres on Night Hawk Lake, the old Piscoutagamy; its water drains through the Frederick House River into the Abitibi and on to James Bay. Cree and Ojibwe bands fished from its islands and hunted the surrounding Shield forest, linking the lake by birchbark canoe to the Moose River routes. In 1444 no European post stood on these waters, and beaver pelts moved only along the seasonal canoe rounds of Indigenous families.

The Hudson's Bay Company pushed inland in 1785, when Philip Turnor came up from Moose Factory and built Frederick House to keep Montreal traders from drawing the region's beaver pelts away from James Bay. Turnor was the Company's first inland surveyor, and he taught surveying to David Thompson and Peter Fidler, who went on to map much of the Canadian west. His own post fared badly: supply canoes struggled up the shallow Frederick House and Abitibi rivers, and a rival North West Company station on nearby Devil's Island fought it for the local Cree trade. In the winter of 1812-13 the manager, two labourers and several Indigenous people were murdered at the post, which was never permanently staffed again. It closed in 1821, when the two companies merged.
zh:
皮斯卡唐一带以夜鹰湖（旧称皮斯库塔加米）为中心，湖水经弗雷德里克豪斯河汇入阿比蒂比河，再通往詹姆斯湾。克里和奥吉布瓦诸部在湖岛捕鱼，在周围的地盾森林狩猎，乘桦皮独木舟把湖区与穆斯河诸水道相连。1444年，这些水面上还没有欧洲商站，河狸皮只随原住民家庭的季节舟路流转。

1785年，哈得孙湾公司向内陆推进，菲利普·特纳尔从穆斯法克特里溯流而来，建起弗雷德里克豪斯商站，以防蒙特利尔商人把这一带的河狸皮引离詹姆斯湾。特纳尔是公司第一位内陆测量师，曾向戴维·汤普森和彼得·菲德勒传授测绘术，这两人后来绘制了北美西部的大片土地。他这座商站却经营惨淡：补给独木舟难溯水浅的弗雷德里克豪斯河与阿比蒂比河，西北公司又在附近的魔鬼岛设站，与它争夺克里人的生意。1812年至1813年冬，商站主管、两名劳工和数名原住民在站中遇害，此后这里再无常驻人员。1821年两家公司合并，商站随即关闭。

en:
The Cree knew the shallow, fish-rich lake between the Moose and Harricana rivers as Kesagami, later recorded as Mesackamee. Around it stretch the swamps and muskeg of the James Bay lowland, the winter country of the Moose Cree. Each summer they paddled down to the bay coast to net fish and hunt waterfowl, and each autumn brought their traps back inland for the cold months. In 1444 no European had yet entered that round.

Their pelts later went to Moose Fort, which the Hudson's Bay Company raised at the mouth of the Moose in 1673, only its second post in North America. French raiders under the Chevalier de Troyes seized it in 1686 on their march against the bay factories, and the contest for the upcountry trade outlasted that war. In 1777 the Company sent George Atkinson, Peter Liske, William Thomas and William Robinson up from the fort with two Cree families, and they built Mesackamee House on the lakeshore to keep the Abitibi trade from Montreal pedlars. The post never covered its costs and stood empty by October 1779, leaving the lake to the Cree traplines.
zh:
克沙加米湖（一译凯萨加米湖，旧称梅萨卡米湖）水浅鱼丰，位于麋河与哈里卡纳河之间，四周是詹姆斯湾低地的大片沼泽，也是驼鹿克里人的冬季家园。每到夏天，他们划独木舟下到海湾沿岸捕鱼猎禽，秋天再带着陷阱返回内陆，度过寒冷的月份。1444年，还没有欧洲人走进这种随季节流转的生活。

后来，他们的毛皮运往麋河堡：哈得孙湾公司1673年在麋河口建起这座商馆，那是公司在北美的第二座据点。1686年，德·特鲁瓦骑士率法国突击队北上袭取海湾诸商馆，麋河堡也被攻占，而对内陆毛皮生意的争夺此后多年未歇。1777年，公司从麋河堡派乔治·阿特金森、彼得·利斯克、威廉·托马斯和威廉·罗宾逊四人，偕两户克里人上行，在湖畔建起梅萨卡米屋，以防阿比蒂比的生意落入蒙特利尔行商之手。商馆始终入不敷出，到1779年10月已空无一人，湖区重归克里人的猎道。

en:
The Shaggami country is the boreal upland between the Night Hawk lake country, Kesagami and the upper Moose River, whose streams all run north toward James Bay. In 1444 it was Cree hunting ground: families fished the lakes in summer and scattered to winter traplines for beaver, moose and caribou. The pelts moved along their own canoe rounds, and no European post stood anywhere in the inland behind the bay.

The forts those pelts went to stood downstream at the mouth of the Moose. The Hudson's Bay Company built Moose Fort there in 1673, its second post after Fort Rupert and the first English settlement in what is now Ontario. In 1686 the Chevalier de Troyes led about a hundred Frenchmen up the Abitibi and Moose routes and caught the garrison by surprise; the post became Fort St Louis, and Rupert House and Fort Albany fell to the same expedition. The English retook it ten years later and burned it to the ground, and the Company rebuilt on a site a mile upstream in 1730. The trade war reached the edges of Shaggami in 1785 with Frederick House, planted inland to keep Cree trappers in the bay trade, until the Hudson's Bay and North West companies merged in 1821.
zh:
沙加米一带是夜鹰湖地区、克沙加米与穆斯河上游之间的北方林地，境内溪流都向北汇入詹姆斯湾。1444年，这里是克里人的猎场：各家族夏季在湖上捕鱼，入冬分散到各自猎径，捕猎河狸、驼鹿和驯鹿。毛皮只沿他们自己的独木舟路线外运，湾岸后方的内陆深处还没有一座欧洲商站。

这些毛皮最终运到下游穆斯河口的堡垒。哈得孙湾公司1673年在那里修建穆斯堡，是公司继鲁珀特堡之后的第二座商站，也是今安大略境内最早的英格兰人定居点。1686年，特鲁瓦骑士率约百名法国人沿阿比蒂比河与穆斯河路线北上，守军猝不及防；堡垒改名圣路易堡，鲁珀特堡和奥尔巴尼堡也在同一次远征中陷落。十年后英国人夺回穆斯堡，将其付之一炬，1730年公司在旧址上游一英里处另筑新站。1785年，这场商战逼近沙加米的边缘：弗雷德里克豪斯商站深入内陆而设，为的是把克里猎人留在詹姆斯湾贸易圈内，直到1821年哈得孙湾公司与西北公司合并。

en:
The Outoulibi country is the Missinaibi watershed, the canoe road between James Bay and Lake Superior. From Moose Factory boats went up the Moose and the Missinaibi, past Thunderhouse Falls, where the river drops forty metres from the Shield through a chain of falls and violent rapids, to Missinaibi Lake; a portage over the height of land then carried them to the Michipicoten and Lake Superior. Its Cree name means 'pictured waters', after the paintings on the rock faces along the banks. In 1444 Cree families held the lakes and rapids, fishing in summer and trapping beaver through the winter, and no European post had yet been built behind the James Bay coast.

Once the English were established on the bay and the French on Lake Superior, the river became a frontier pressed from both ends. When the Hudson's Bay Company began building posts up the Missinaibi, it sent Philip Turnor, its first inland surveyor, who mapped the route in 1781. Macabanish House, built in 1788 and renamed New Brunswick House in 1799, became its chief station, while the North West Company kept a rival post less than a kilometre downstream of Wapiscogamy House for six years after 1800. When the two companies merged in 1821, the competing posts along the river were combined under one owner.
zh:
欧托利比一带是米西奈比河流域，也是詹姆斯湾与苏必利尔湖之间的独木舟河路。舟队从穆斯法克特里出发，溯穆斯河与米西奈比河而上，经过一道由瀑布和汹涌急流连成的险滩，河水在这里从地盾跌落四十米，抵达米西奈比湖；再搬过分水岭，经另一条河进入苏必利尔湖。克里语河名意为「绘有图像的水」，得自河岸岩壁上的图画。1444年，克里诸家族据有湖泊与急流，夏季捕鱼，冬季设套捕猎河狸，詹姆斯湾海岸后方还没有欧洲商站。

英国人在湾畔立足、法国人在苏必利尔湖南侧落脚后，这条河便成了两头受挤的交界。哈得孙湾公司着手沿米西奈比河修筑商站时，派来公司第一位内陆测量师菲利普·特纳尔，他于1781年测绘了这条路线。1788年建的马卡巴尼什屋1799年改名新不伦瑞克屋，是公司在河上的主站；1800年起的六年里，西北公司又在瓦皮斯科加米屋下游不到一公里处开设对垒商站。1821年两家公司合并，沿河互不相让的两排商站归了同一个东家。

en:
The western shore of James Bay is a drowned flat of muskeg and goose-marshes, where the Moose and Albany rivers wind out of the boreal forest to the tides. Its people, the Omushkego, are the eastern Swampy Cree, with the Moose Cree at the bay's head; they kept an exact seasonal round, summer fishing and berrying by canoe, autumn goose-hunting along the shore, winter trapping at inland camps. In 1444 no European sail crossed their bay, and the coastal camps lay seasons away from any European frontier.

Henry Hudson, ice-bound, wintered in the bay in 1610-11 and in June 1611 was cast adrift in an open boat by his mutineers, never to be seen again. After Pierre-Esprit Radisson explored the Moose River for the company, the Hudson's Bay Company raised Moose Fort in 1673 and Fort Albany in 1679, both wooden forts with cannon. In 1686, while France and England were at peace, the Chevalier de Troyes led a hundred French regulars and Canadian volunteers out of Montreal, paddled and portaged 800 miles in 82 days up the Ottawa and down the Abitibi and Moose, and took Moose Fort in a pre-dawn rush on its sixteen sleeping men, the Le Moyne brothers first tying down its three guns. Rupert House and Fort Albany fell in the same summer; Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville, later the victor of the naval Battle of Hudson Bay, served in the column and stayed to hold the captured posts, and the French renamed Moose Fort Fort St. Louis. The English retook and burned it ten years later; the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 gave the bay to Britain, and the company rebuilt Moose Fort in 1730.

Trade then pushed inland up the Albany. Henley House, built 160 miles upriver in 1743, was sacked in December 1754 by Cree under Wappisis, who was hanged at Fort Albany on 21 June 1755. Gloucester House and Osnaburgh House later carried the company's trade still deeper into the Shield.
zh:
马什凯科瓦克所在的詹姆斯湾西岸是一片被海水浸透的泥炭沼与雁沼低地，穆斯河与奥尔巴尼河在其中蜿蜒穿过北方针叶林，奔流入海。此地居民是奥马什凯戈人，即东部沼泽克里人，海湾南端的一支又称穆斯克里人；他们严守季节的节律：夏天划独木舟捕鱼采莓，秋天到岸边猎雁，冬天到内陆营地捕猎毛皮兽。1444年的詹姆斯湾上没有一片欧洲帆影，海岸营地离任何欧洲人的边疆都还隔着好几个季节的路程。

亨利·哈德逊的船被海冰封在湾中，于1610至1611年在此过冬；1611年6月，他被哗变船员放进一条敞篷小艇放逐，再无音讯。皮埃尔-埃斯普里·拉迪松为公司探察穆斯河之后，哈得孙湾公司于1673年建起穆斯堡，1679年又设奥尔巴尼堡，两座都是配有火炮的木堡。1686年英法尚在和平时期，德·特鲁瓦骑士率一百名法国正规军和加拿大志愿兵离开蒙特利尔，沿渥太华河上溯，再顺阿比蒂比河和穆斯河而下，82天里水陆兼行800英里，在黎明前突袭睡梦中的16名守军，勒穆瓦纳兄弟先把三门大炮绑死，拿下穆斯堡。鲁珀特堡和奥尔巴尼堡也在同年夏天陷落；日后在哈得孙湾海战中获胜的皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔当时也在军中，留守夺来的商栈。法国人把穆斯堡改名圣路易堡。英军十年后夺回并焚毁此堡；1713年《乌得勒支和约》将海湾划归英国，公司1730年重建穆斯堡。

此后贸易沿奥尔巴尼河深入内陆。1743年，公司在河上160英里处建起亨利屋商栈；1754年12月，瓦皮西斯率克里人攻陷该栈，他本人1755年6月21日在奥尔巴尼堡被处绞。格洛斯特屋、奥斯纳堡屋等后来设立的商栈，又把公司的贸易推向地盾更深处。

en:
The Winnipeg River, whose Cree name means 'murky water', drops from Lake of the Woods to Lake Winnipeg through a staircase of rapids: Portage de l'Isle, the seven white-water climbs of La Rivière Blanche, then Manitou Rapids at the approach to the mouth. It was the only easy canoe road between the Great Lakes and the inland northwest, and at midcourse the English River branched off toward James Bay. In 1444 Anishinaabe-speaking Nakawe bands and Cree worked that road, fishing the pools and hunting moose in the woods, their camps moving with the seasons.

The French were the first to fortify it. Pierre Gaultier de La Vérendrye built Fort St. Charles on Lake of the Woods in 1732, sent his sons down the river in 1733, and about 1739 raised Fort Maurepas at Bas de la Rivière near the mouth, where a large Cree village stood by the time Alexander Henry the elder traded through in 1775. In 1792 Toussaint Le Sieur built the North West Company's Fort Bas de la Rivière, with a fishery, farms and warehouses that after 1810 stocked pemmican for the Athabasca canoe brigades; the Hudson's Bay Company put Fort Alexander across the way before 1800. At the merger of 1821 the Company kept the North West post under the Fort Alexander name, and as the brigades switched to the York Factory route the river fell quiet.
zh:
瓦普斯一带的温尼伯河，克里语名意为「浑水」，自森林湖向温尼伯湖逐级跌落，一路是重重急流和搬运道：岛屿搬运道、白河的七连跌水，河口前还有马尼图急流。它是五大湖与西北内陆之间唯一便于独木舟通行的水道，行至半途，英格兰河又岔向詹姆斯湾。1444年，往来这条水路的是说阿尼什纳比语的纳卡韦氏族和克里人，他们在水潭捕鱼、在林中猎驼鹿，营地随季节搬迁。

法国人最先在河上设防。皮埃尔·戈蒂埃·德·拉韦朗德里1732年在森林湖建起圣夏尔堡，1733年派几个儿子顺河下行，约1739年又在河口附近的巴德拉里维耶尔筑起莫尔帕堡；1775年老亚历山大·亨利路过贸易时，当地已有一座不小的克里人村庄。1792年，图桑·勒西厄尔为西北公司建起巴德拉里维耶尔堡，配有渔场、农田和仓库，1810年后专门储存肉糜饼，供给开往阿萨巴斯卡的独木舟大队；哈得孙湾公司则在1800年前于对面设立亚历山大堡。1821年两公司合并，公司保留西北公司的货栈，改名亚历山大堡。后来独木舟队改走约克堡一线，温尼伯河便冷落下来。

en:
Between Lake Winnipeg and Hudson Bay lies a labyrinth of taiga lakes, Playgreen and Cross among them, and the upper Nelson and Hayes rivers, the canoe road from the bay into the Saskatchewan country. Its Cree bands lived on whitefish and sturgeon, moose and woodland caribou, moving camp with the seasons, while Chipewyan hunting grounds pressed in from the north-west. In 1444 these were exclusively native waterways, where no axe had ever sounded.

On 12 June 1690 Henry Kelsey left York Factory by canoe with a party of Cree, carrying the company's hatchets, beads and tobacco, sent to invite the distant nations to trade. Up the Nelson he crossed five lakes and made thirty-three portages, six hundred miles to Deering's Point near the later The Pas, and in 1691 crossed into the Saskatchewan country, the first recorded European there; on 20 August he saw great herds of bison and grizzly bears on the plains, and returned to York Factory in 1692 with Cree and Assiniboine eager to trade.

Cree armed through the bay trade barred the Chipewyan from the coast, and the company at York Factory wanted the two peoples reconciled. The woman who brought the peace was Thanadelthur, a Chipewyan captured by Cree raiders in 1713. She escaped and reached York Factory in November 1714, and on 27 June 1715 set out again with the Englishman William Stuart and 150 Cree to make the peace. She succeeded, but the post promised to her people was delayed, and on 5 February 1717 she died of fever at the factory before she could lead them home. Governor James Knight, who called her his 'Slave Woman Joan' after Joan of Arc, wrote in his journal that her burial day was his most melancholy there. The peace she made opened the way north for the bay trade. The Hayes–Nelson waterway stayed the main road west, and in 1817 the Hudson's Bay Company built Norway House where the Nelson flows out of Lake Winnipeg.
zh:
温尼伯湖与哈得孙湾之间，是泰加林中的湖泊迷宫，普莱格林湖、克罗斯湖等大大小小的水面，与纳尔逊河、海斯河的上游交错，构成从海湾进入萨斯喀彻温腹地的独木舟之路。这里的克里人部落以白鱼、鲟鱼、驼鹿和林地驯鹿为生，营地随季节迁徙；奇佩瓦恩人的猎场从西北方向逼近。1444年，这些水道完全属于原住民，还从未响起过斧头的声音。

1690年6月12日，亨利·凯尔西带着公司的斧头、珠子和烟草，随一队克里人乘独木舟离开约克堡，奉命去邀请远方的部族前来贸易。他沿纳尔逊河穿过五个湖泊、三十三处搬运道，上行600英里抵达后来帕斯附近的迪尔林角；1691年又进入今萨斯喀彻温省境，是有记录以来第一个到过那里的欧洲人。同年8月20日，他在草原上见到大群美洲野牛和灰熊，1692年带着急欲通商的克里人和阿西尼博因人返回约克堡。

得到海湾火器的克里人把守海岸，不许奇佩瓦恩人前来交易，约克堡的公司却盼着两族议和。办成这件事的是奇佩瓦恩女子塔纳德尔图尔：她1713年被克里掠走为奴，逃脱后于1714年11月抵达约克堡。1715年6月27日，她随英国人威廉·斯图尔特和一百五十名克里人离堡北上，促成两族和解。许给她族人的商栈迟迟未建，她还没来得及带族人返乡，便在1717年2月5日染热病殁于约克堡。曾以圣女贞德相比、称她为「女奴让娜」的总督詹姆斯·奈特在日记里写道，她下葬那天是他在任上最伤感的一天。她换来的和平为海湾贸易打开了北上之路。海斯—纳尔逊水道始终是西行正路，1817年哈得孙湾公司在纳尔逊河出温尼伯湖处建起挪威之家。

en:
The upper Churchill drains a chain of rapids and long island-strewn lakes toward Lac Île-à-la-Crosse, whose Cree name means the great opening where the waters meet. Twelve miles beyond the lake, the Methye Portage crosses the divide between Hudson Bay and the Arctic. In 1444 this was Dene country, travelled by small Chipewyan camps that followed barren-ground caribou, hunted moose in the northern woods and took whitefish at lake narrows. A band later recorded as the K'ësyëhót'ı̨ne, or aspen-house people, ranged from the Churchill toward Lac La Loche, Cold Lake and the approaches to the Athabasca. Cree war parties to the southeast made the route to the bay coast dangerous.

Thanadelthur, a Chipewyan woman who had escaped Cree captivity, spoke Cree, Chipewyan and English while serving the Hudson's Bay Company. In 1715 she helped company men broker peace between the Cree and Chipewyan, and she died of fever before the mission ended in 1717. The agreement let Chipewyan furs move toward Churchill. Thomas Frobisher recognised the value of Lac Île-à-la-Crosse while travelling with a Dene hunting party and built the first post there in the winter of 1776. Two years later Dene guides showed Peter Pond the Methye Portage. Canoes could then pass to the Clearwater, the Athabasca and the Mackenzie, and the lake became a provisioning and exchange stop for fur brigades bound for the northwest. Alexander Mackenzie used the route on his 1793 crossing to the Pacific. Montreal traders and the Hudson's Bay Company both maintained posts, the company from 1791, and Cree, Dene, French, Scots and English families formed a district Métis community. Smallpox travelled the same water road a few years after Pond's crossing and thinned many camps; the rival companies united in 1821.
zh:
丘吉尔河上游连接着一连串急流和岛屿散布的长湖，西端通向拉克罗斯湖；克里语称此湖为众水相会的大开口。湖以西12英里，梅蒂转运站越过哈得孙湾与北冰洋之间的分水岭。1444年，这里是德内人的土地，奇帕维安人的家族小队追逐荒地驯鹿，在北方林中猎驼鹿，在湖峡捕白鱼。后来被记作凯斯耶霍廷内（K'ësyëhót'ı̨ne）的一支，即「白杨屋人」，活动范围从丘吉尔河延伸到拉洛什湖、冷湖和阿萨巴斯卡方向。东南方的克里人战队使前往海湾沿岸的路途充满危险。

奇帕维安女子塔纳德尔图尔曾逃出克里人的拘押，后来为哈得孙湾公司效力，能说克里语、奇帕维安语和英语。1715年，她帮助公司人员促成克里人与奇帕维安人和谈，又在1717年使团结束前死于热病。和议使奇帕维安人的毛皮能够运往丘吉尔。托马斯·弗罗比舍随一支德内狩猎队出行时看出拉克罗斯湖的价值，于1776年冬在湖畔建起第一座商站。两年后，德内向导把梅蒂转运站指给彼得·庞德；独木舟从这里可进入克利尔沃特河、阿萨巴斯卡河和马更些河，拉克罗斯湖也成为西北毛皮船队的补给与交换地。亚历山大·麦肯齐1793年横越至太平洋时走的就是这条路线。蒙特利尔商人和哈得孙湾公司都在湖畔设站，公司站始于1791年；克里人、德内人、法国人、苏格兰人和英格兰人通婚，形成地方性的梅蒂社群。庞德越过转运站几年后，天花沿同一条水路传入，许多营地人口锐减；互相竞争的两家公司最终于1821年合并。

en:
Here the Saskatchewan leaves the prairies and enters the boreal forest, widening through Cedar Lake and the Cumberland marshes where the Carrot and Pasquia come in. Cree bands fished the lakes, took moose and beaver in the woods, and stalked the bison herds on foot at the parkland edge; their canoes could run downstream all the way to Hudson Bay. In 1444 those waterways carried only native hunters.

Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company paddled up from York Factory in 1690, wintered near The Pas, and went up the Carrot in 1691 as the first European to see bison and grizzlies on the northern plains, returning in 1692 with Cree and Assiniboine hunters. The French answered from Montreal: the La Vérendryes built Fort Paskoya on Cedar Lake in 1741 to turn western furs away from the bay, and a second post at The Pas about 1752 struck Anthony Henday in 1754 as a 'hogstye'; it closed with New France in 1759. Montreal pedlars were back by 1772, when Joseph Frobisher wintered on Cumberland Lake, and Samuel Hearne built Cumberland House there for the Company in 1774, a depot forty paddling days from York Factory against nearly five months from Montreal. Its stores fed the Athabasca canoe brigades, the North West Company built opposite in 1793, and the rival houses merged in 1821.
zh:
马米基维尼一带，萨斯喀彻温河流出草原、进入北方针叶林，在雪松湖与坎伯兰沼泽间展宽，卡罗特河与帕斯基瓦河在此汇入。克里诸氏族在湖中捕鱼，在林中猎驼鹿、捕河狸，又在林缘草原徒步潜猎野牛；他们的独木舟顺流而下，可一直划到哈得孙湾。1444年，这些水道上往来的还只有原住民猎人。

哈得孙湾公司的亨利·凯尔西1690年从约克堡划舟上行，在今帕斯附近过冬，1691年溯卡罗特河深入，成为头一个在北部平原见到野牛和灰熊的欧洲人，1692年随克里和阿西尼博因猎人返回。法国人从蒙特利尔出手应对：拉韦朗德里父子1741年在雪松湖畔建起帕斯科亚堡，要把西部毛皮从哈得孙湾引开；约1752年又在今帕斯设第二座商栈，1754年安东尼·亨德见了，说它活像个「猪圈」，该栈1759年随新法兰西一同关闭。1772年蒙特利尔行商已卷土重来，约瑟夫·弗罗比舍在坎伯兰湖过冬；1774年塞缪尔·赫恩为公司在当地建起坎伯兰豪斯。从约克堡划舟到这里只需四十天，从蒙特利尔却要将近五个月。货栈为开往阿萨巴斯卡的独木舟队供粮，西北公司1793年在对岸设栈，两强于1821年合并。

en:
The North and South Saskatchewan meet in a broad wooded valley east of the later Prince Albert, where boreal forest gives way to aspen parkland and open plains. In 1444 the Cree speakers of this stretch of river were the Sipiwininiwak, the 'river people'. They took sturgeon from the eddies, hunted moose in the woods to the north and drove buffalo into pounds on the grass to the south, where Blackfoot and Gros Ventre camps also ranged. Dogs pulled travois along the valley trails; horses had not yet reached the Saskatchewan, and the forks brought forest people and plains people into the same camps.

France tried to secure the river with Fort St. Louis, built by Louis de la Corne in 1753 below the forks and usually called Fort de la Corne. It was the westernmost link in a chain of French posts meant to draw furs away from Hudson Bay and to support the search for a route toward the Pacific. Anthony Henday travelled through the Saskatchewan valley soon afterward with Cree and Assiniboine companions, going for the Hudson's Bay Company to winter among the Blackfoot; he returned along the North Saskatchewan after learning that the western plains nations were unwilling to make the long, exposed journey to the bay. Traders returned after the French withdrawal and used posts at Nipawin and Fort Sturgeon. The smallpox epidemic of 1781 to 1782 emptied many camps while mounted, armed river Cree took their place beside the Assiniboine on the plains. Gros Ventre raiders burned South Branch House and Manchester House in 1793 and 1794, and the Hudson's Bay Company raised the first Carlton House near the old French site in 1796. Its rivalry with the North West Company lasted until the two companies united in 1821.
zh:
北萨斯喀彻温河与南萨斯喀彻温河在后来的艾伯特亲王城以东汇入一条宽阔林木河谷，北方针叶林也在那里转为杨树林草原和开阔草地。1444年，住在这一河段的克里语群体自称斯匹维尼瓦（Sipiwininiwak），意为「河人」。他们在漩流中捕鲟，到北面林中猎驼鹿，在南面草原把野牛赶入围栏；黑脚人和格罗斯文特人的队伍也在同一片草地上活动。狗拉拖架沿河谷小路运载物资，马匹尚未传到萨斯喀彻温，汇流处的营地中同时可见森林民族和草原民族。

1753年，路易·德·拉科尔讷在汇流处下游修建圣路易堡，后来通常称拉科尔讷堡，法国试图以此控制这条河。它是法国商站链最西端的一环，作用是把毛皮引离哈得孙湾，并支持寻找通往太平洋的水路。不久后，为哈得孙湾公司效力的安东尼·亨迪随克里人和阿西尼博因人穿行萨斯喀彻温河谷，到黑脚人中间越冬；他沿北萨斯喀彻温河返回，也得知西部草原各族不愿走那条漫长且易遭袭击的路去海湾。法国势力退出后，商人重新到来，使用尼帕温和斯特金堡等商站。1781至1782年的天花使许多营地空虚；此时骑马持枪的河克里人已在草原上与阿西尼博因人并肩行动。1793和1794年，格罗斯文特袭掠者先后焚毁南岔屋和曼彻斯特屋；哈得孙湾公司1796年在法国旧站附近建起第一座卡尔顿屋。它与西北公司的竞争持续到1821年两家合并。

en:
Ye Xa Yabine is Hebina, the 'Rock Mountain People' of the Nakoda, though in 1444 that division had not yet formed and the plains belonged to foot-borne bands. Their ground is the Cypress Hills, a wooded plateau rising about 600 metres out of the short-grass plains on the divide between the Saskatchewan and the Missouri: water falling on the summit runs north-east to Hudson Bay and south to the Gulf of Mexico. Springs, aspen groves and lodgepole pine on the north-facing slopes gave shelter in the coulees, with elk and moose in the woods and buffalo on the grass below, so hunting parties from the Blackfoot, Gros Ventre, Crow, Cree and Assiniboine all came and went. Nakoda-speaking relatives of the Assiniboine were moving north-west through this country; the Hebina name would appear later, as a southern branch.

That branch, the Mountain Stoney, broke from the Assiniboine about the middle of the 18th century and moved into the hill forests to get away from smallpox epidemics; once horses and muskets reached the plains, mounted parties raided through the hills between rival grounds. The fur posts only reached the northern approaches, and badly. Gros Ventre warriors burned Manchester House in 1793, and in July 1794 a force of one or two hundred stormed the Hudson's Bay post at South Branch House, killing the two officers caught outside and everyone sheltering within except one man who hid eight hours in a cellar and escaped by canoe. Across the river a rider warned the North West Company fort in time, and its first volley drove the attackers off. In 1800 the Siksika chief Feathers, who had taken his late father's name Old Swan, let Peter Fidler build Chesterfield House at the mouth of the Red Deer River. Working from maps the chief drew, Fidler charted the upper Missouri and the Rockies, peak names in Blackfoot and notes on thirty-two tribes, and the drawings went into Aaron Arrowsmith's printed map of North America. The post was abandoned within a few years, and in 1821 no trader had yet put down roots in the Cypress Hills themselves.
zh:
耶哈亚比内即纳科达人中的赫比纳人，意为「岩山人」，不过1444年时这支人尚未形成，平原上往来的是徒步的游猎队伍。他们的地方是赛普里斯山，一座林木覆盖的高地从短草平原中拔起约六百米，正处在萨斯喀彻温河与密苏里河的分水岭上：落在山顶的水，一路向东北入哈得孙湾，另一路向南入墨西哥湾。泉眼、白杨林和北坡上的扭叶松为冲沟里的营地提供遮蔽，林中有马鹿和驼鹿，山下草场有野牛，黑脚、格罗斯文特、克劳、克里和阿西尼博因的猎队都在此来去。与阿西尼博因人同源、说纳科达语的人正穿过这片地方向西北移动，「赫比纳」作为南支的名字要到后来才出现。

这支南支就是山地斯托尼人，约在18世纪中叶脱离阿西尼博因人，躲进山林以避天花；马匹和火枪传到平原后，骑马队伍便在各部地界之间的山区往来劫掠。毛皮商栈只触及此地北缘，而且站不稳脚跟。1793年，格罗斯文特战士焚毁曼彻斯特商栈；1794年7月，一两百名战士猛攻哈得孙湾公司的南支商栈，在商栈外的两名职员当场被杀，躲进栈内的人几乎无一幸免，只有一人在地窖藏了八小时后乘独木舟逃脱。河对岸，一名骑手及时给西北公司的商栈报信，第一轮排枪便把进攻者打退。1800年，锡克锡卡酋长「羽毛」承袭亡父「老天鹅」之名，允许彼得·菲德勒在雷德迪尔河口修建切斯特菲尔德商栈。菲德勒照着这位酋长亲手绘制的地图，测绘上密苏里与落基山脉，记下山峰的黑脚语名称和三十二个部族的情况，这些图后来进入阿罗史密斯刊行的北美地图。商栈没几年便遭废弃，到1821年，还没有商人在赛普里斯山中真正扎下根。

en:
Lake Athabasca is the great shallow lake of the boreal forest. The Athabasca River feeds it and the Slave River drains it north toward the Arctic Ocean, and its Woods Cree name, aðapaskāw, 'where the reeds grow one after another', later gave its name to the whole Athabasca country and to its family of languages. In 1444 the shores belonged to Dënesųłiné bands, the people the Cree called Chipewyan, 'pointed hides', after the cut of their parkas. They moved between winter and summer camps after caribou and moose, fished the lake, and bore the raids of Cree war parties from the southeast.

The first peacemaker known by name in this country was a Chipewyan woman. In 1715 Thanadelthur guided Hudson's Bay Company men out from Churchill and, speaking English, Cree and her own language, talked her people and the Cree into ending their feud. Traders followed the road she had opened. Peter Pond built Pond House on the lower Athabasca River in 1778, the first post in the country, and smallpox swept the lake bands three years later. In 1788 Roderick Mackenzie of the North West Company founded Fort Chipewyan on Old Fort Point, where furs gathered from the Peace, Slave, Athabasca and Mackenzie river basins were collected for Montreal. He assembled a library of more than 2,000 volumes, famous among traders across Rupert's Land, which he liked to call 'the little Athens of the Arctic regions'. His cousin Alexander Mackenzie set out from the fort, reached the Arctic in 1789 down the river later named for him, and crossed the mountains to the Pacific in 1793, the first European to cross the continent north of Mexico. Hudson's Bay men kept rival posts on the same lake until the two companies merged in 1821 and the trade of the lake settled on Fort Chipewyan.
zh:
阿亚巴斯卡维尼瓦克一带的阿萨巴斯卡湖，是北方针叶林中一座广阔的浅水湖。阿萨巴斯卡河注入湖中，湖水北经斯拉维河流向北冰洋。伍兹克里语称它阿达帕斯卡乌（aðapaskāw），意为「芦苇一株接一株生长之地」，后来整个阿萨巴斯卡地区乃至阿萨巴斯卡语族都借它得名。1444年，湖岸属于德内苏林各游群，克里人叫他们奇佩维安人，意为「尖皮」，出自他们皮袍的裁式。他们在冬营与夏营之间迁徙，追猎驯鹿与驼鹿，下湖捕鱼，还要抵挡东南方克里战团的袭扰。

这片土地上第一位留下姓名的调停者，是一位奇佩维安女子。1715年，塔纳德尔图尔领着丘吉尔堡的哈德逊湾公司人员出行，凭着通晓英语、克里语和本族语言，说动本族与克里人结束世仇。商人沿着她打开的路而来：彼得·庞德1778年在阿萨巴斯卡河下游建起庞德屋，是本地第一座商站；三年后天花席卷湖畔各游群。1788年，西北公司的罗德里克·麦肯齐在旧堡角建立奇佩维安堡，皮斯河、斯拉维河、阿萨巴斯卡河与马更些河流域的毛皮都汇集到这里，再运往蒙特利尔。他在堡中攒起两千余册藏书，名声传遍鲁珀特领地的商人圈子，他还爱把这座图书馆叫作「北极地区的小雅典」。堂弟亚历山大·麦肯齐以奇佩维安堡为起点，1789年沿后来以他命名的河流抵达北冰洋，1793年翻越山脉抵达太平洋，成为第一个在墨西哥以北横跨北美大陆的欧洲人。哈德逊湾公司在同一座湖上另设商站相争，直到两公司1821年合并，全湖贸易统归奇佩维安堡。

en:
Between Lake Athabasca and the Peace River lies a maze of boreal forest, muskeg and water: the lower Athabasca and Wabasca rivers, and Lesser Slave Lake, which drains east into the Athabasca. In 1444 this was Dene country, where Beaver and Chipewyan bands tracked moose and woodland caribou, fished the lakes and snared hare through the hard winters. The land bears a later name, Nihithawak, from Nîhithaw, 'the people', as the Woods Cree call themselves. In those years they still lived nearer Hudson Bay, selling the furs of inland nations on to the English ships there as middlemen.

During the 18th century Cree bands carrying trade muskets moved northwest into this country and the Dene gave ground before them. The smallpox epidemic of 1781 devastated both sides, and the peace that followed set the Peace River as the line between Cree and Dane-zaa. Traders came close behind the hunters. In 1802 the North West Company built its post at Buffalo Bay on Lesser Slave Lake, the first non-Indigenous settlement in these parts, and Cree hunters kept the posts supplied with bison meat and pemmican through the winters. By the time the North West and Hudson's Bay Companies merged in 1821, the Woods Cree were the people of the lake country that carried their name.
zh:
阿萨巴斯卡湖与皮斯河之间，是一片针叶林、泥炭沼与水网交织的土地：阿萨巴斯卡河下游、瓦巴斯卡河，以及向东泄入阿萨巴斯卡河的小奴湖。1444年时这里是德内人的家园，比弗人和奇佩维安人的游群在林中追踪驼鹿与林地驯鹿，下湖捕鱼，靠套野兔熬过严冬。这片土地后来的名字来自另一个民族，尼希塔瓦克出自伍兹克里人的自称尼希塔乌（Nîhithaw），意为「族人」。那时他们还住在更靠近哈德逊湾的地方，把内陆各族的毛皮转卖给湾边的英国船，做的是中间人生意。

18世纪，带着贸易火枪的克里游群向西北迁入，德内人步步退让。1781年的天花让交战双方都折损惨重，随后的和约把皮斯河定为克里人与达内扎人的界线。商人紧随猎人而至：1802年西北公司在小奴湖的布法罗湾设站，是这一带最早的外来定居点；克里猎手在严冬里为各商站供应野牛肉和干肉饼。到1821年西北公司与哈德逊湾公司合并时，伍兹克里人已是这片湖区的主人，地方也用了他们的名字。

en:
The Peace River runs nearly 2,000 kilometres from the Rocky Mountains to the Peace–Athabasca Delta, cutting prairie-bottomed valleys through the boreal forest. In 1444 its banks were the country of the Dane-zaa, 'the real people', whom Cree neighbours and later the European traders called the Beaver. They knew the river as Saaghii Naachii, 'big river', hunted bison on its valley prairies and moose in the surrounding woods, and carried on a long feud with the Cree over all the country to the southeast.

Trade muskets in Cree hands pushed the Dane-zaa northwest up the valley, until the smallpox epidemic of 1781 broke Cree power and the two nations smoked a peace pipe together. They fixed the river as their border, Dane-zaa to the north and Cree to the south, and the river has carried the name of that peace ever since. Traders had already found the way in. Peter Pond visited in 1785, and in 1788 Charles Boyer of the North West Company built a post on the Boyer River above the impassable Vermilion Chutes, among the vermilion-coloured clays that gave Fort Vermilion its name; with Fort Chipewyan it ranks as one of the oldest European settlements in Alberta. Alexander Mackenzie wintered at Fort Fork in 1792–93 on his way up the Peace to the Pacific, and in 1794 the company raised Rocky Mountain Fort at the mouth of the Moberly River, the first European post on the British Columbia mainland. The Dane-zaa kept the forts supplied with bison meat and grease until the rival companies merged in 1821.
zh:
皮斯河出落基山脉，奔流近两千公里，注入皮斯河—阿萨巴斯卡三角洲，在北方针叶林中切出一道道谷底铺着草原的河谷。1444年，河两岸是达内扎人的土地，他们自称「真正的人」，克里邻族和后来的欧洲商人则称他们为比弗人。他们把这条河叫作萨吉纳奇（Saaghii Naachii），意为「大河」，在河谷草原猎野牛，在四周林间猎驼鹿，还为东南方整片土地与克里人长期结怨。

克里人手里的贸易火枪把达内扎人顺着河谷逼向西北，直到1781年天花重创克里人，两个民族才坐到一起共吸和平烟斗。他们约定以河为界，达内扎人在北、克里人在南，河名就来自这次议和。商人此前已经摸到了门路：彼得·庞德1785年到过此河；1788年，西北公司的夏尔·布瓦耶在布瓦耶河口设站，位置在船只无法通过的弗米利恩急流上方，河岸一带的朱红色黏土给了弗米利恩堡这个名字，它和奇佩维安堡并列艾伯塔最早的欧洲人定居点。亚历山大·麦肯齐1792至1793年在福克堡过冬，随后溯皮斯河前往太平洋；1794年，公司在莫伯利河口筑起落基山堡，是不列颠哥伦比亚大陆上第一座欧洲人商站。达内扎人为各商站供应野牛肉和油脂，直到两家竞争公司1821年合并。

en:
The Siksikawa, Siksikáwa or the Blackfoot People, hold the short-grass prairie of south-central Alberta between the Red Deer River and the North Saskatchewan. They were the northernmost of the four Blackfoot nations, with the woods at their backs and open plains before them, and their name told of moccasins blackened by prairie ash. In 1444 they were foot hunters: bands of ten to thirty lodges followed the herds on foot, drove buffalo into pounds and over the jumps along the foothill edge, and wintered in wooded river valleys with dogs pulling the travois. Each summer the scattered bands gathered for the Okan, the sun ceremony, when warrior societies danced and men rose in rank by feats of courage against an enemy.

Horses and trade guns reached the Blackfoot in the first half of the 18th century, and mounted war parties pushed the Shoshone back towards the mountains; by 1787 David Thompson recorded Blackfoot country running from the North Saskatchewan to the Missouri. Anthony Henday of the Hudson's Bay Company was the first European known to enter it, wintering in Blackfoot camps near the Red Deer in 1754–1755 and, it is said, glimpsing the Rockies from afar, but his invitation to trade at Hudson Bay came to nothing. The journey was too long for a people without river canoes, and Cree and Assiniboine bands barred the way. Smallpox ran through every camp in 1781, yet the confederacy kept the upper hand. Fort Augustus and Edmonton House went up on the North Saskatchewan in 1795 and Rocky Mountain House soon after, all on the Blackfoot northern border, and traders still called them the 'Lords of the Plains' in 1821.
zh:
西西卡瓦即黑脚语所说的锡克锡卡瓦，意为「黑脚人」，据有艾伯塔中南部雷德迪尔河与北萨斯喀彻温河之间的短草平原。他们是黑脚四族中最北的一支，背后是林地，面前是开阔草场，族名来自被草原灰烬染黑的软皮鞋底。1444年的锡克锡卡人还是步猎者：十到三十座帐篷结成一队，徒步尾随牛群，把野牛赶入围栏、逼下麓缘的跳崖，冬季在林木河谷扎营，由狗只拉动拖橇。每年夏天，分散的队伍聚在一处举行「奥坎」太阳仪式，战士会社起舞，男人靠对敌的勇武之举挣取地位。

18世纪上半叶，马匹和商队火枪传到黑脚人手里，骑马战队把肖肖尼人逐回山区；到1787年戴维·汤普森记录地理时，黑脚人的疆土已从北萨斯喀彻温河伸展到密苏里河。哈得孙湾公司的安东尼·亨德代是已知第一个走进这片土地的欧洲人，1754至1755年随黑脚队伍在雷德迪尔附近过冬，据说还远远望见落基山脉；他邀请黑脚人前往哈得孙湾交易，却没有结果。对不会使用河上独木舟的人来说，这条路太远，克里和阿西尼博因队伍又卡着去路。1781年天花扫过每一支队伍，黑脚联盟仍占上风。1795年，奥古斯都堡和埃德蒙顿屋在北萨斯喀彻温河畔建起，落基山屋随后也设立，都在黑脚人的北境；到1821年，商人嘴里的他们仍是「平原之王」。

en:
Beyond the last ramparts of the Peace River canyon rise the northern Rocky Mountains, where the Finlay and Parsnip rivers gather in the Rocky Mountain Trench to form the headwaters of the Peace. In 1444 this high country belonged to the Tsek'ene, 'the people on the rocks', whom traders later wrote down as Sekani. Kin to the Dane-zaa and the Dakelh, they ranged in small nomadic bands through mountains and trench, living by moose and caribou where their western neighbours lived by fish, and they cremated their dead on the trail.

Toward 1800 Plains Cree raiders drove the Sekani deeper into the mountains. Alexander Mackenzie's canoes worked up the Parsnip in 1793 on his crossing of the continent to the Pacific. In 1805 Simon Fraser of the North West Company, put in charge of every company post west of the Rockies, built two in this country. One was Rocky Mountain Portage House below the Peace canyon; the other, Trout Lake Fort on McLeod Lake, was soon renamed Fort McLeod and became the first European settlement to endure west of the Rockies in present-day Canada. The Sekani brought furs, meat and grease to the forts, which grew into the kernel of the company's New Caledonia district. In 1808 Fraser descended the river later named for him to the sea, while his clerks kept the mountain trade going until the Hudson's Bay Company took over all the company's posts in the merger of 1821.
zh:
越过皮斯河峡谷最后的陡岸，便是落基山北段，芬利河与帕斯尼普河在落基山地堑中汇聚，构成皮斯河的源头。1444年，这片高地属于采凯内人，意为「岩石上的人」，后来的商人把这个名字译作塞卡尼。他们是达内扎人和卡尔克人的亲族，结成小股游群在山岭与地堑间游猎；西边的邻族以鱼为生，他们则靠驼鹿和驯鹿过活，行旅途中就把死者火化。

1800年前后，平原克里人的袭扰把塞卡尼人更深地赶进山里。1793年，亚历山大·麦肯齐的独木舟溯帕斯尼普河而上，横跨北美大陆前往太平洋。1805年，主管西北公司落基山脉以西全部商站的西蒙·弗雷泽，在这片地方建起两座：一座是皮斯峡谷下方的落基山运输屋，另一座是麦克劳德湖畔的鳟鱼湖堡，不久改称麦克劳德堡，成为今加拿大落基山脉以西第一座存留下来的欧洲人定居点。塞卡尼人把毛皮、兽肉和油脂送到堡中，这几座商站后来长成公司「新喀里多尼亚」辖区的根基。1808年，弗雷泽又顺后来以他命名的河南下入海；他手下的店员则维持着山里的生意，直到1821年哈德逊湾公司随两公司合并接走全部商站。

en:
The Dakelh, whom French traders called the Carrier, live in the lake country of the central interior, around Stuart, Fraser and Babine Lakes, the Nechako River and the upper Fraser. Their own name means roughly 'people who travel by boat', and their Athabascan tongue belongs to the Dene family. Each family holds its keyoh, its hunting and fishing grounds, under a hereditary chief. The year follows the salmon runs and the moose and caribou hunt: smoked fish, hides, dried meat and berry cakes go out along the 'grease trails' to the coast and come back as eulachon oil packed in bentwood boxes. In 1444 no European goods travel those trails.

Alexander Mackenzie followed one of the trails to the Pacific in 1793. In the winter of 1805-06 James McDougall, one of Simon Fraser's men, reached the lake the traders called Carrier's Lake, later renamed Stuart Lake for Fraser's assistant John Stuart. Fraser built Fort St. James on its shore in 1806, one of the first permanent European posts in British Columbia, and in 1808 descended the Fraser to its mouth. The trade grew slowly among a people whose living came from the fishery, and customary and ceremonial rules also stood in the way of a fur economy. In 1821 the post passed to the Hudson's Bay Company and became the headquarters of its New Caledonia district.
zh:
达凯尔人被法国商人称作卡列尔人（Carrier，意为搬运者），住在中部内陆的湖乡，斯图尔特湖、弗雷泽湖、巴宾湖、内查科河与弗雷泽河上游一带。他们的自称大意是「驾船出行的人」，语言属阿萨巴斯卡语系的德内语支。每个家族在自己世袭首领的掌管下保有传统狩猎捕鱼地（keyoh）。一年生计跟着鲑鱼汛期和猎驼鹿、驯鹿的季节走：熏鱼、兽皮、肉干和果饼沿「油脂小道」驮往海岸，换回弯木盒装的蜡鱼油。1444年，这些小道上还没有欧洲货物。

1793年，亚历山大·麦肯齐沿其中一条小道抵达太平洋。1805至1806年冬，西蒙·弗雷泽的部下詹姆斯·麦克杜格尔到达商人所称的「卡里尔湖」，湖后来以弗雷泽的助手约翰·斯图尔特改称斯图尔特湖。1806年，弗雷泽在湖畔建起圣詹姆斯堡，这是不列颠哥伦比亚最早的欧洲人常设商站之一；1808年，他又顺后来以他命名的弗雷泽河直下河口。达凯尔人以渔为生，习俗和仪式上的规矩也妨碍毛皮增产，生意起初起色很慢。1821年，商站转归哈德逊湾公司，成为其新喀里多尼亚区的总部。

en:
The Secwepemc, called Shuswap by the early fur traders, hold the largest country of any people in the southern interior, about 145,000 square kilometres of plateau running from the Chilcotin and Cariboo down the two Thompson rivers to their meeting at Kamloops and across the great bend of the Columbia. Their language is Interior Salish. Bands took salmon at the runs and dried it for winter, hunted the plateau and traded roots, hides and dried fish with their neighbours. Raids brought captives as well, and rather than keep slaves the Secwepemc sold most captives back to their own people for dried salmon. Kamloops is their word for the 'meeting of the waters'. In 1444 the confluence is a Secwepemc fishing camp and gathering ground.

Europeans first wintered there in 1811, when David Stuart of the Pacific Fur Company stayed with the Kamloops band. Alexander Ross raised Fort Cumcloups at the confluence in May 1812, and the rival North West Company built Fort Shuswap beside it before buying its competitor in 1813. Kwa'lila, chief of the main village, moved his people up to the fort gates to control the trade; his nephew and foster son Nicola, who inherited his place, built an alliance of Okanagan and lower Thompson peoples that traders had to take seriously. After 1821 the post, by then called Thompson's River Post, passed to the Hudson's Bay Company and became a station on the brigade road from the Columbia to New Caledonia.
zh:
赛克维派克人被早期毛皮商人称作舒什瓦普人，据有南部内陆最大的一片地界：约14.5万平方公里的高原，从奇尔科廷、卡里布一带沿北、南汤普森河而下，到两河合流的坎卢普斯，再越过哥伦比亚河大拐弯。他们的语言属内陆萨利什语支。各部在鲑鱼汛期捕鱼熏制过冬，在高原狩猎，用根茎、兽皮和干鱼与邻族交易。他们也会袭掳人口，但很少留作奴隶，多半把俘虏卖还其本族，换取干鲑鱼。坎卢普斯之名就来自他们的语言，意为「两水相会」。1444年，两河合流处还只是赛克维派克人的渔营地和聚会场。

1811年，欧洲人第一次在此过冬：太平洋毛皮公司的戴维·斯图亚特住在坎卢普斯部。1812年5月，亚历山大·罗斯在合流处筑起库姆克鲁普斯堡，对手西北公司在旁边另建舒什瓦普堡，并于1813年买下了太平洋毛皮公司。主村首领夸利拉把族人迁到堡门旁，把交易攥在自己手里；继任的外甥兼养子尼古拉把奥卡诺根人和汤普森河下游诸部结成同盟，商人都需认真应付。1821年后，这座当时已称汤普森河商站的据点转归哈德逊湾公司，成为哥伦比亚河通往新喀里多尼亚的毛皮队大道上的一站。

en:
The Tsilhqot'in take their name from the Chilko River, the 'red ochre river', and live on the dry plateau between the Coast Mountains and the Fraser, holding most of the Chilcotin basin and the headwaters of the Homathko and Dean. They are the southernmost Athabascan-speaking people in British Columbia and call their country Tsilhqot'in Nen. Before Europeans came they had a name as a fighting people, with war parties ranging south to the Similkameen, east to the Rockies and west to the Pacific coast, and they stood within a wide trade in obsidian, the black volcanic glass knappers valued for arrowheads. In 1444 a band's standing rests on its warriors and its hold on the obsidian trails.

European goods first climbed onto the plateau in the 1780s and 1790s, passed inland from the British and American sea-otter ships on the coast. Alexander Mackenzie canoed down the Fraser in 1793 as far as the village later called Alexandria, at the eastern edge of Tsilhqot'in country; warned of falls and rapids below, he turned north and then west along the West Road River to the Pacific. By 1808 the North West Company had posts among the Dakelh immediately to the north, so Tsilhqot'in furs moved north directly or through Dakelh middlemen. In 1821 the Hudson's Bay Company opened Fort Alexandria on the Fraser, named for Mackenzie, which became the people's main source of European goods.
zh:
奇尔科廷人的族名来自奇尔科河，河名意为「红赭石河」。他们住在海岸山脉与弗雷泽河之间的干燥高原上，据有奇尔科廷河流域大部及霍马斯科河、迪恩河的源头，是不列颠哥伦比亚分布最南的阿萨巴斯卡语族群，称自己的故土为「奇尔科廷嫩」。欧洲人到来之前，他们以善战闻名，队伍南起西密卡米恩，东抵落基山，西达太平洋海岸；他们还处在一个广阔的黑曜石贸易网中，这种黑色火山玻璃岩是打制箭头最受看重的材料。1444年，一个部落的地位系于其武士的名头和对黑曜石小道的掌握。

1780和1790年代，欧洲货先由海岸上做海獭皮生意的英美船只传入内陆高原。1793年，亚历山大·麦肯齐沿弗雷泽河下到奇尔科廷地界东缘、后来称亚历山德里亚的村落，因听人警告下游尽是险滩瀑布而折返北上，再沿西路河（West Road River）向西抵达太平洋。到1808年，西北公司已在北面紧邻的达凯尔人地界设站，奇尔科廷人的毛皮便或直接北上，或经达凯尔人转手。1821年，哈德逊湾公司在弗雷泽河畔开设亚历山德里亚堡，堡名取自麦肯齐，这里成为奇尔科廷人获取欧洲货物的主要去处。

en:
The Syilx, whom early traders called the Okanagan, hold a string of long lakes and dry grasslands running from Okanagan Lake down the Okanagan River to the Columbia, together with the Similkameen country to the west, about 69,000 square kilometres in all. Their language is an Interior Salish tongue akin to the Secwepemc. Each band wintered in a village of kekuli, pit houses dug into the ground and roofed with timber and earth, then spent the open months moving between salmon stations, root grounds and deer ranges. Lakes and rivers joined the bands and carried their canoes to the Columbia. In 1444 no European had yet crossed the mountains to the east.

In autumn 1811 men of John Jacob Astor's Pacific Fur Company, coming up the Columbia, met Okanagan headmen in council and on 31 October raised Fort Okanogan at the mouth of the Okanagan River, the first American-built post in what became Washington. The North West Company bought it with Astor's other inland posts in 1813, and fur brigades used the Okanagan valley as their road north to Thompson's River and the New Caledonia forts. In 1821 the post passed with the company to the Hudson's Bay Company. It yielded few furs of its own, but its boats and horses kept the northern posts supplied.
zh:
锡尔克赫人被早期商人称作奥卡诺根人，据有一串长湖和干草原：从奥卡诺根湖沿奥卡诺根河南下到哥伦比亚河，加上西面的西密卡米恩一带，共约6.9万平方公里。他们的语言属内陆萨利什语支，与赛克维派克人相近。各部冬天住在克库里半地穴屋的村落里，屋子掘地而成，以木梁和泥土盖顶；天暖后便辗转于渔场、根茎地和猎鹿场之间。湖与河把各部连在一起，独木舟顺水路可入哥伦比亚河。1444年，东面的群山还不曾有欧洲人翻越。

1811年秋，约翰·雅各布·阿斯特的太平洋毛皮公司的人沿哥伦比亚河而上，与奥卡诺根诸首领会盟，10月31日在奥卡诺根河口筑起奥卡诺根堡，这是后来的华盛顿州境内第一座美国人所建商站。1813年，西北公司随收购阿斯特的内陆各站取得此堡，毛皮队便取道奥卡诺根河谷北上，往返汤普森河与新喀里多尼亚诸堡。1821年，商站随西北公司并入哈德逊湾公司。当地出的毛皮一直不多，但这里的船只和马匹维持着北方各堡的补给。

en:
The Nisga'a are the 'people of the Nass River', a name borrowed from Tongass Tlingit. Their territory follows the Nass for 380 kilometres from the Coast Mountains to Nass Bay and Portland Inlet on Hecate Strait, the last 40 kilometres open to canoes. Two fish runs fed the lower villages: summer salmon and the late-winter run of oolichan, a smelt so fatty, with up to fifteen percent of its weight in fat, that a dried fish threaded on a wick burns like a candle. The oolichan were rendered into grease and carried from the Nass along native trade routes into the interior. In 1444 clan villages stood along the lower river, and Nass canoes carried trade and diplomacy between Tsimshian and Tlingit neighbours.

Nisga'a oral history records a volcanic catastrophe. In the eighteenth century, perhaps around 1775, Tseax Cone in the mountains above the river sent out fumes and lava: the smoke killed people before the flow reached them, a lava stream about 22 kilometres long dammed the Nass, and the villages of Lax Ksiluux, Lax Ksiwihlgest and Wii Lax K'abit were destroyed, with about 2,000 dead. On 23 July 1793 HMS Discovery and HMS Chatham anchored in Salmon Cove on Observatory Inlet, at the edge of Nisga'a waters; George Vancouver set up an observatory and mapped Portland Inlet before the ships left on 17 August. Every Nass village was still in Nisga'a hands in 1821.
zh:
尼斯加（又译尼斯迦）的名字借自汤加斯特林吉特语，意为「纳斯河的人」。他们的土地沿380千米长的纳斯河，从海岸山脉延伸到赫卡特海峡的纳斯湾和波特兰湾，下游最后40千米可以行船。两大渔汛供养着河下游的村落：夏天是鲑鱼，冬末是蜡鱼；蜡鱼是一种油脂极丰的胡瓜鱼，脂肪可占体重的一成五，晒干后穿根灯芯就能当蜡烛点。蜡鱼熬成的鱼油，由纳斯河沿原住民商路运往内陆。1444年，各氏族村落分布在下游河畔，独木舟在钦西安和特林吉特邻族之间往返贸易、交涉。

尼斯加口传中记下了一场火山浩劫。18世纪（一说约1775年），群山高处的齐阿克斯火山喷出烟气与熔岩：烟焰先于熔岩夺人性命，约22千米长的熔岩流截断纳斯河，拉克斯克西卢克斯（Lax Ksiluux）、拉克斯克西威尔盖斯特（Lax Ksiwihlgest）和维拉克斯卡比特（Wii Lax K'abit）三村被毁，约两千人丧生。1793年7月23日，「发现号」与「查塔姆号」停泊在尼斯加水域边缘观测湾的鲑鱼湾；乔治·温哥华架设观测仪器、测绘波特兰湾，船队于8月17日离去。1821年时，纳斯河上每座村落仍归尼斯加人所有。

en:
The Heiltsuk country of island channels and permanent winter villages centred on Milbanke Sound and the waters around Campbell Island and Lama Passage, the site of later Bella Bella. Five Heiltsuk-speaking divisions made their seasonal rounds from those villages, taking salmon, herring roe and shellfish and tending clam gardens built of stone along the shore. Rank and inherited privilege ordered the villages, and potlatches made status public. Heiltsuk artisans were known up and down the coast for bentwood boxes, horn spoons, canoes and the carved and painted work of the ceremonials, and neighbouring nations rated their warriors as highly as their carvers. In 1444 no European ship had entered these channels.

Charles Duncan brought Princess Royal into the uncharted sound in late June 1788, traded for several days with the Heiltsuk, and named the water after Vice Admiral Mark Milbanke; George Vancouver sailed through a few years later. In 1805 the Boston trading ship Atahualpa was attacked by Tlingit in the sound, and her captain and part of the crew were killed. The Heiltsuk entered the fur trade as suppliers and middlemen: their canoe makers learned to build western-style trading schooners, early guns gave them weight in every bargain, and shipmasters complained that they passed land-otter skins off as sea otter and cut oversized blankets down to sell the pieces separately. Introduced diseases and the long reciprocal war with the Haida cost them dearly. Through 1821 no European post stood in the sound, and its trade moved in Heiltsuk canoes and schooners.
zh:
黑尔楚克人的家园岛径纵横、冬村临海，以米尔班克湾以及坎贝尔岛、拉马水道一带为中心，后来的贝拉贝拉就在这片水域。五个说黑尔楚克语的部族从冬村出发随季节移动，捕捞鲑鱼，采集鲱鱼子和贝类，在岸边石埂围出的蛤蜊养殖地里劳作。等级与世袭特权维系村落秩序，夸富宴把身份摆给众人看。黑尔楚克工匠做的弯木盒、角勺、独木舟和仪式雕绘闻名沿海，邻族对他们战士的评价不亚于对他们雕工的评价。1444年，还没有欧洲船只驶入这些水道。

1788年6月底，查尔斯·邓肯率「皇家公主号」进入当时尚未标上海图的米尔班克湾，与黑尔楚克人交易数日，并以海军中将马克·米尔班克之名为海湾命名；几年后乔治·温哥华也驶过这里。1805年，波士顿商船「阿塔瓦尔帕号」在湾内遭特林吉特人攻击，船长和部分船员被杀。黑尔楚克人以供货者和中间人的身份进入毛皮贸易：独木舟工匠学会造西式贸易纵帆船，较早到手的火器让他们在每笔交易里都有分量；船长们则抱怨他们拿陆獭皮冒充海獭皮，还把偏大的毯子裁开分次卖掉。传入的疫病和与海达人长期互相攻伐让他们损失惨重。到1821年，湾内没有欧洲商站，往来贸易靠的是黑尔楚克人的独木舟和纵帆船。

en:
Kodiak (Alutiiq Qikertaq) is the largest island of the Kodiak Archipelago in the Gulf of Alaska, a mountainous land of deep ice-free bays and fjords, with open treeless coast in the south. The Karluk River has one of the richest salmon runs on the Pacific, and the island is the sole range of the Kodiak bear, the giant brown bear that gathers at the same rivers as the fishermen. Its people were the Koniag Sugpiaq, the Kodiak branch of the Alutiiq, who lived in large coastal villages of semi-subterranean houses, took salmon from the rivers, hunted sea lions and seals from skin kayaks on the open water, and gathered shellfish on the tides. In 1444 the many villages were linked by kayak along the shore, trading and raiding under local chiefs, and no European had yet landed there.

The first Russian to land was the fur trader Stepan Glotov, who wintered on Kodiak in 1762-64 under repeated attack. In 1784 Grigory Shelikhov arrived with 130 men to conquer the island. Islanders had taken shelter on Awa'uq, a sheer sea stack off Sitkalidak long used as a refuge; Shelikhov ringed it with cannon fire and killed an estimated 200 to 500 men, women and children, then held hostages to subdue the rest. In Alutiiq the rock's name means 'to become numb'. Three Saints Bay, founded that year, was the first permanent Russian settlement in Alaska; in 1792 the post moved to St Paul harbour, the nucleus of the town of Kodiak, which became the emporium of Russian America, its sea-otter pelts shipped on to Siberia and China. Monks from Valaam brought Orthodoxy in 1794. The Russian-American Company then set quotas of otter pelts and bird skins, conscripting island men for ever-longer voyages farther from home, and the archipelago's sixty-odd villages, some 13,000 people at first contact, shrank as families went hungry without their hunters.
zh:
科迪亚克（阿留特克语称基克尔塔克）是科迪亚克群岛中最大的岛屿，横卧阿拉斯加湾中；岛上多山，深水不冻湾与峡湾切过海岸，南部则是开阔无树的海滨。岛上的卡鲁克河是太平洋鲑鱼洄游最盛的河流之一，科迪亚克棕熊这种巨型棕熊只生活在这座岛上，和捕鱼人一样聚到河边。岛上的主人是科尼亚格苏克皮阿克人，即阿留特克人的科迪亚克支系。他们聚成大型海岸村落，住半地穴式房屋，从河中捕捞鲑鱼，乘兽皮小艇到外海猎取海狮和海豹，在潮间带采集贝类。1444年时，众多村落靠沿岸水路往来，在地方首领治下贸易、攻掠，还没有欧洲人登上过这座岛。

第一个登岛的俄国人是毛皮商人斯捷潘·格洛托夫，他于1762至1764年在岛上过冬，期间不断遭到岛民攻击。1784年，格里戈里·舍利霍夫率一百三十人前来征服此岛。岛民退守西特卡利达克岛外的阿瓦乌克，那是一座自古用作避难所的陡峭海蚀柱；舍利霍夫以炮火合围，估计有二百至五百名男女老幼遇害，又靠人质制服其余各部。阿留特克语中，阿瓦乌克意为「变得麻木」。同年建立的三圣湾是俄罗斯人在阿拉斯加的第一个永久定居点；1792年据点迁到圣保罗港，即后来科迪亚克城的雏形，并成为俄属美洲的贸易中心，海獭皮从这里转运西伯利亚和中国。1794年，瓦拉姆修道院的修士带来东正教。此后俄美公司摊派獭皮和鸟皮份额，强征岛民远赴越来越远的外海长期行猎；群岛上六十余座村落、接触之初共约一万三千人，因猎人长期离家、族人乏食而不断凋敝。

en:
The coast between Prince William Sound and the Copper River delta is a tangle of glacier-carved fjords, islands and forested shore, lashed by Gulf of Alaska storms. In the island-studded sound lived the Chugach, an Alutiiq people who hunted seal, sea otter and whale from skin baidarkas and traded or fought the Eyak, Ahtna and Tlingit. At the Copper River mouths, among the richest salmon grounds on the coast, lived the small Eyak nation in a handful of villages such as Alaganik. In 1444 these were among the northernmost peoples of the Northwest Coast, living richly by fish, furs and raids, untouched by Europeans.

On 20 July 1741 the first European foot was set on Alaskan soil here, when the naturalist Georg Steller went ashore from Bering's St Peter on Kayak Island; Bering himself stayed aboard. James Cook's ships entered the sound in May 1778, and he named it first Sandwich Sound and then Prince William, for Prince William Henry, George III's third son, a thirteen-year-old midshipman in the Royal Navy who later reigned as William IV. Spanish expeditions sailed in to claim the sound in 1779 and 1790 but left no settlement. The Russians came to trade: their first contact with the Chugach in 1783 ended with nine Russian sentries dead within a month, yet in 1793 they raised the Saints Constantine and Helen redoubt at Nuchek on Hinchinbrook Island, where Chugach paddled in with dried fish and sea-otter pelts. The far smaller Eyak nation, caught between Chugach and Tlingit raids and the newcomers' diseases, kept dwindling.
zh:
威廉王子湾与铜河口之间的海岸，是冰川刻出的峡湾、岛屿和林木海岸交织之地，常年受阿拉斯加湾风暴拍击。岛礁密布的湾中住着楚加奇人，他们是阿留特克人的一支，驾兽皮小艇「拜达卡」猎捕海豹、海獭和鲸，与埃雅克人、阿特纳人和特林吉特人或贸易或交战。铜河口是沿岸最富饶的鲑鱼场之一，小小的埃雅克部族就住在阿拉加尼克等寥寥几座村落里。1444年时，他们是西北海岸最北的族群之一，靠鱼产、毛皮和劫掠为生，欧洲人尚未涉足。

1741年7月20日，欧洲人第一次踏上阿拉斯加的土地：博物学家格奥尔格·斯特勒从白令的「圣彼得号」登上卡亚克岛，白令本人则留在船上。1778年5月，库克的船队驶入海湾；他先按恩主桑威奇伯爵称之为桑威奇湾，后来改名威廉王子湾，取名自英王乔治三世的第三子威廉·亨利，这位时年十三岁的皇家海军见习军官，就是后来的英王威廉四世。西班牙远征队又在1779年和1790年两度驶入湾中宣布占领，却没有留下定居点。真正扎下根的是做毛皮生意的俄国人：1783年他们首次与楚加奇人接触，一个月内就有九名俄军哨兵送命；尽管如此，1793年他们仍在欣钦布鲁克岛的努切克建起圣君士坦丁与圣海伦娜堡，楚加奇人划着小艇前来，用鱼干和海獭皮交易。小得多的埃雅克部族夹在楚加奇人与特林吉特人的袭掠和新来者的疾病之间，人口不断流失。

en:
Sitka Sound opens on the western side of Baranof Island, Shee in Tlingit, where rainforest mountains drop into one of the richest sea-otter and salmon grounds of the Alexander Archipelago. In 1444 the Kiks.ádi clan of the Sheetʼká Ḵwáan kept plank-house villages around the sound. Inheritance ran through the mother's line, clan houses owned the fishing stations and stored salmon, and their large canoes traded and raided as far as the other islands of the panhandle.

The sea otters brought Alexander Baranov, governor of the Russian-American Company, who surveyed the sound in 1795 and in 1799 built the Fort of Archangel Michael with the Kiks.ádi's leave. Demands for allegiance and labour broke the bargain: in June 1802 Tlingit warriors burned the fort and killed many of its men, and Baranov had to pay 10,000 rubles to Captain Barber of the British ship Unicorn to ransom the few survivors. He returned in 1804 with the warship Neva under Yuri Lisyansky. Naval gunfire failed to crack the Tlingit fort of saplings and a Russian assault was beaten off; after two more days of bombardment the Kiks.ádi hung out a white flag and left the fort by night. On the cleared ground the Russians raised New Archangel, which became the capital of Russian America in 1808.

The Kiks.ádi did not submit. They rebuilt their fort on the far side of Peril Strait and cut all trade with the Russians, keeping the embargo through 1821, so New Archangel drew its food and furs from friendly clans and company ships while the clan kept its independence across the water.
zh:
锡特卡湾在巴拉诺夫岛西岸敞开，特林吉特人称该岛为希岛（Shee）；雨林覆盖的群山直插入海，湾口是亚历山大群岛海獭和鲑鱼最丰足的水域之一。1444年，锡特卡群体（Sheet'ka Kwaan）的基克萨迪氏族在湾畔建有木板房屋村落。继承沿母系进行，氏族家族掌有渔场和鲑鱼储备，大型独木舟贸易和袭掠的范围远达狭地其他岛屿。

海獭把俄美公司总管亚历山大·巴拉诺夫引来：他1795年考察海湾，1799年经基克萨迪人许可建起大天使米迦勒堡。效忠和服劳役的要求打破了约定，1802年6月，特林吉特战士焚毁堡垒，杀死许多守军；为赎回少数幸存者，巴拉诺夫只得向英国船「独角兽号」船长巴伯支付一万卢布。1804年，他带着尤里·利相斯基指挥的战舰「涅瓦号」返回。舰炮轰不开特林吉特人的幼树堡垒，强攻也被击退；又炮击两天之后，基克萨迪人挂出白旗，乘夜撤离。俄国人在清出的土地上建起新阿尔汉格尔斯克，1808年成为俄属美洲的首府。

基克萨迪人没有屈服。他们撤到佩里尔海峡对岸重建堡垒，断绝与俄国人的一切贸易，禁运一直维持到1821年；新阿尔汉格尔斯克只能从友好氏族和公司船只取得食物和毛皮，这个氏族则在海峡对岸保持独立。

en:
Cotoname is the lower Rio Grande valley, where the river winds through flat, brushy plains and breaks into delta lagoons before reaching the Gulf. In 1444 small Cotoname-speaking bands, part of the wider Coahuiltecan world, moved between both banks of the river, hunting deer, fishing the lagoons and gathering mesquite beans and prickly pear; Spanish expeditions later came on large camps of several bands together in the delta. No town, mission or presidio then stood between the river mouth and the mines of Nuevo León.

Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca and the other survivors of the Florida expedition crossed neighboring Coahuiltecan country in the early 1530s, the first Europeans seen in these parts. From 1580 Luis de Carvajal, governor of Nuevo León, sent slaving parties down the Rio Grande, and Juan Bautista Chapa, a chronicler of Monterrey, counted 161 bands once named around the city that had since vanished. The smallpox and measles epidemic of 1636–1639 opened a collapse that later outbreaks kept deepening. Escandón's settlers reached the lower valley in 1748, and Spanish officers counted fourteen bands in the delta in 1757; missions, ranchos and the new river towns absorbed most of their people within a generation. By 1800 few delta bands still answered to their old names, and their families lived on as labourers and herders in the river towns.
zh:
科托纳梅地处里奥格兰德河下游：河水蜿蜒穿过平坦多灌丛的平原，在入海前散成三角洲潟湖。1444年，说科托纳梅语的小群体属于更大范围的科阿韦尔特坎世界，在河两岸往来，猎鹿、在潟湖捕鱼、采集牧豆和仙人掌果；后来的西班牙探险队在三角洲见到多个群体合住的大营帐。此时从河口到新莱昂的矿区之间，没有城镇、传教站或要塞。

1530年代初，佛罗里达远征的幸存者阿尔瓦·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡一行穿过邻近的科阿韦尔特坎土地，是这里见到的第一批欧洲人。1580年起，新莱昂总督路易斯·德·卡瓦哈尔派掳奴队沿里奥格兰德南下；蒙特雷编年史家胡安·包蒂斯塔·查帕统计，蒙特雷一带曾有名字记载的群体中，161个已经消失。1636至1639年的天花和麻疹疫情开启了人口崩溃，此后的疫病又一再加深。埃斯坎东的移民1748年进入下游河谷，1757年西班牙官员在三角洲点出十四个群体；传教站、牧场和新建的河滨城镇在一代人之内吸纳了他们的大多数人。到1800年，三角洲上仍以旧名相称的群体已寥寥无几，他们的家族作为雇工和牧人留在河滨城镇里。

en:
The dry plains and ridges of the Bajío were Guamare country. They were one of the nations the Spanish lumped together as Chichimecas, and they called themselves the Children of the Wind: nomadic hunters and gatherers who cremated their dead and scattered the ashes to give them back to the earth. Around 1400, pressed by the Aztec Empire to the east and the Purépecha to the south, the peoples of Guanajuato joined a league the Nahuas called Pechichitane Altepetlatskostli, whose tribal chiefs settled common action in a council. It was a mixed league, for the Guaxabanes were Guachichiles and the Xiconaques were Zacatecos; only groups such as the Copuces counted as Guamares proper, and the Spanish later labelled all of them Ixtlachichimecas or Guamares. In 1444 no empire reached them.

Silver ended that isolation. After the strikes at Zacatecas and then Guanajuato from 1543, Spanish roads, supply caravans and mining towns cut into Guamare land to feed the mines, opening the Chichimeca War, a guerrilla campaign that ran on into the early seventeenth century. In 1563 league fighters destroyed Pénjamo and overran the Spanish settlement at Comanja de Jaso, where only two Spaniards came out alive.
