In 1569 they sacked El Robledal near Guanajuato and pushed as far as Jilotepec before Pedro de Ahumada Sámano defeated them. Patrols and forts could not stop the raids on the silver caravans, so the Crown bought peace instead: by the early 1600s gifts, tools, land grants and mission towns had settled Guamare families into the mining society of New Spain.
zh:
巴希奥的干旱平原和丘陵是瓜马尔人的土地。他们是西班牙人统称奇奇梅卡人的诸族之一，自称风之子：以狩猎采集为生，火化死者，把骨灰撒出，送归大地。约1400年，在东面阿兹特克帝国与南面普雷佩查的压力下，瓜纳华托的诸族群结成纳瓦人所称的佩奇奇塔内·阿尔特佩特拉斯科斯特利联盟，各族酋长在议事会上决定共同行动。联盟由多个族群组成：瓜克萨班人是瓜奇奇尔人，西科纳克人是萨卡特卡人，只有科普塞斯等几支算真正的瓜马尔人，西班牙人后来把他们统统称作伊斯特拉奇奇梅卡人或瓜马尔人。1444年时，还没有任何帝国的势力到达这里。

银矿打破了这种孤立。1543年起，萨卡特卡斯、继而是瓜纳华托发现银矿，为了给矿场补给，西班牙人的道路、运输车队和矿镇直接切入瓜马尔人的土地，奇奇梅卡战争就此爆发，这场游击战一直延续到17世纪初。1563年，联盟战士摧毁彭哈莫，攻破科曼哈-德哈索的西班牙人据点，那里只有两名西班牙人生还。1569年，他们洗劫瓜纳华托附近的罗夫莱达尔，一直打到希洛特佩克，才被佩德罗·德·阿乌马达·萨马诺击败。巡逻队和要塞拦不住对运银车队的袭击，西班牙王室转而花钱买和：到17世纪初，靠礼物、工具、土地授予和传教城镇，瓜马尔人陆续定居下来，进入新西班牙的矿业社会。

en:
The Seri, who call themselves the Comcaac, held the arid coast of Sonora between the Encinas Desert, the inland mountains and the Gulf of California, with Tiburón and San Esteban Islands as the western edge of their range. Their tongue has no proven kinship with any other language. Six nomadic bands moved between desert hunting grounds, fishing shores and island camps, from the Altar Desert in the north to the Yaqui River in the south, and a leader was named only for war or an unusually hard season. They took sea turtles from the gulf and each spring gathered the rice-like seeds of the eelgrass growing under its waters, the only people known to have used that sea grass as grain. The Spaniards came to rank them, with the Apache and the Yaqui, among the fiercest fighters of the northwest.

Spanish expeditions touched Sonora in the sixteenth century, but no lasting settlement was planted in Seri country. The Jesuits made the steadiest attempt, gathering the bands into agricultural missions; in the 1660s a slaving posse killed most of one band and distributed its children through the towns of Sonora, and the Seri rose against that pressure in 1725, again and again returning to their desert rounds with Tiburón Island as a refuge no column could take. When Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767, the mission system collapsed. By Mexican independence in 1821 the Seri had lost people and ground, but Spanish accounts admitted that they had never been formally conquered, pacified, or evangelized.
zh:
塞里人自称孔卡阿克，据有索诺拉的干旱海岸，夹在恩西纳斯沙漠、内陆山地与加利福尼亚湾之间，蒂布龙岛和圣埃斯特万岛是其活动范围的西缘。他们的语言与其他语言都查不到亲缘关系，被视为孤立语言。六个游居群体往来于沙漠猎场、捕鱼海岸和岛屿营地之间，领地北起阿尔塔沙漠，南至亚基河一带；只在战时或渔猎异常艰难的季节临时推举首领。他们从湾中捕海龟，每年春天采集水下大叶草结出的米粒状草籽，已知把这种海草当作谷物食用的民族只有他们。西班牙人后来把他们与阿帕奇人、亚基人并列为西北最强悍的战士。

西班牙探险队在16世纪已抵达索诺拉，但没有在塞里人的土地上建立持久定居点。最持续的尝试来自耶稣会士，他们把各群体集中到农业传教区；17世纪60年代，一支捕奴武装杀尽一个群体的大部分成人，把孩子分卖到索诺拉各镇，塞里人在这种压力下于1725年起事，又一再回到沙漠游居生活，蒂布龙岛是任何讨伐队都攻不下的避难所。卡洛斯三世1767年驱逐耶稣会士后，传教体系瓦解。到1821年墨西哥独立时，塞里人虽人口锐减、领地收缩，但西班牙方面的记载也承认，他们从未被正式征服、平定或改宗。

en:
Huichol covers the broken southern ridges of the Sierra Madre Occidental, where the Bolaños River cuts steep canyons through northern Jalisco. Before the Spanish conquest, Tepecano and other Uto-Aztecan farming families lived in scattered rancherías on the slopes, tended maize in the narrow bottoms and exchanged salt with peoples from the valleys and lake shore. The highlands also bordered the arid Guachichil routes leading toward Wirikuta, later central to Wixárika peyote pilgrimages. In 1444 no single city ruled the canyons; difficult paths kept their villages apart from the richer chiefdoms near Lake Chapala.

After Nuño de Guzmán's campaign through Nueva Galicia in 1531, encomiendas and mining labour pushed native refugees into the mountains. Groups related to the Guachichiles settled among Tepecano communities, intermarried and took shape as Wixárika villages; Alonso Ponce's account of 1587 already placed them in the province of Tepeque. During the Mixtón War of 1540–1542, Caxcanes and other peoples of Nueva Galicia attacked Spanish outposts, and fighting in the sierra later merged with the Chichimeca wars. Wixárika and Tepecano forces rose together at El Teúl in 1592 and again at Nostic in 1702. The canyons let their rancherías, shared rites and language remain beyond direct Spanish control for long periods.
zh:
维乔地处西马德雷山脉南段的破碎山脊，博拉尼奥斯河在哈利斯科北部切出深谷。西班牙人到来前，特佩卡诺人和其他使用犹他—阿兹特克语的农耕家族散居坡地牧场，在狭窄河谷种植玉米，并用食盐同湖滨和谷地族群交换。山地东北邻接瓜奇奇尔人的干旱地域，通往维里库塔的路线后来在维夏里卡人的佩奥特朝圣中占有重要位置。1444年，峡谷中没有统辖全境的大城，陡峭山路使各村社同查帕拉湖附近较富庶的酋邦保持距离。

1531年努尼奥·德·古斯曼攻入新加利西亚后，委托监护制和矿山劳役把原住民难民逼入山区。与瓜奇奇尔人有关的群体进入博拉尼奥斯峡谷，同特佩卡诺人通婚共居，逐渐形成维夏里卡诸社区；阿隆索·庞塞1587年的记载已把他们列入特佩克省。1540—1542年的米克斯通战争中，卡斯坎人及新加利西亚诸族群联合进攻西班牙前哨，山地战事后来又同奇奇梅卡战争相接。维夏里卡人和特佩卡诺人1592年在埃尔特乌尔联手起事，1702年又在诺斯提克起兵。深谷使这些山间村社、共同仪典和语言在很长时间里没有被西班牙政权直接控制。

en:
The Toboso lived in the northern Bolsón de Mapimí, a belt of dry basins between the Rio Grande and the silver country of Nueva Vizcaya. They hunted with sling and spear, camped where water and mesquite allowed, and traded or fought with the Jumano of La Junta de los Ríos to the north and the Irritila bands of the lake valleys to the east. In 1444 no Spaniard had yet crossed their deserts, and a dozen autonomous bands answered to no outside lord.

Their southern lands took the first slaving raids out of New Spain, which set their response to Europeans: when Antonio de Espejo reached the Jumano in 1583 and was welcomed, the Toboso fled into the desert. From the 1640s they raided the missions and Tarahumara mines on their western flank. Many were later rounded up into missions around Monterrey, but numbers walked out and kept fighting; the Spanish called them ladinos, Indians who had learned the Spanish language and frontier habits the better to turn them against the settlements. The Spanish counted twelve Toboso bands in the 1680s and only four by 1693. By 1800 the bands left in Mexico had merged into mestizo society; a few refugees appear in the baptismal books of the Refugio mission on the Texas coast after 1807, and eighteenth-century Spanish maps mark Matagorda Island as Toboso Island.
zh:
托沃索人住在马皮米洼地北部，一片横在里奥格兰德河与新比斯开银矿区之间的干旱盆地地带。他们以投石索和长矛狩猎，在有水和豆灌木的地方扎营，与北方两河汇流处的胡马诺人、东方湖谷地带的伊里蒂拉诸部或贸易或交战。1444年，还没有西班牙人穿过他们的沙漠，十余个自主游群不奉任何外来的君主。

他们靠南的土地最先承受新西班牙派出的奴隶劫掠，这造就了他们对欧洲人的态度：1583年安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍受到胡马诺人迎接时，托沃索人却逃进了沙漠。从1640年代起，他们不断袭扰西侧的传教站和塔拉乌马拉矿山。后来许多人被圈进蒙特雷一带的传教站，但大批人又走了出来继续作战；西班牙人称他们为「拉迪诺人」，说这些印第安人学会了西班牙语和边疆的生存手段，再转手用来对付定居点。西班牙人在1680年代数出十二个托沃索游群，到1693年只剩四个。到1800年，留在墨西哥的部众已融入梅斯蒂索社会；1807年后，得克萨斯海岸雷富希奥传教站的洗礼册上出现过几名托沃索难民，18世纪的西班牙人地图则把马塔戈达岛标作「托沃索岛」。

en:
The Laguneros, whose name the Spanish usually wrote down as Irritila, lived on the shores of a chain of shallow lakes in the Bolsón de Mapimí, where the Nazas and Aguanaval rivers ended in the desert. The largest was the Laguna de Mayrán, the 'Great Lake of Nueva Vizcaya', with Viesca, Tlahualilo and Álamo strung out beside it. They were not one people but more than a dozen bands of different languages, using Nahuatl among themselves, and they kept their villages on the shores. They sowed nothing and kept no herds, living on lagoon fish, game and the mesquite, prickly pear and maguey of the banks, and moving as the waters rose and fell. In 1444 these lakes lay far beyond any Spanish road.

Expeditions pushing north from the new silver mines at Zacatecas and Durango found populous shore villages but no ore, so the crown left the lagoons to missionaries: in 1594 Philip II named the country the Provincia de La Laguna and gave it to the Jesuits. Their annual reports describe naked fishermen without houses or seed, so wary that the priests feared being killed and eaten; the same reports grumble that in New Spain the Gospel only travelled where silver had opened the road. The missions never took hold. Around 1687 the Jesuits were expelled from the region, the mission villages were abandoned, and the surviving Irritila drifted back into the desert and ceased to appear as a distinct people.
zh:
拉古内罗斯人（西班牙文献通常把他们的名字记作伊里蒂拉人）住在马皮米洼地一串浅湖的湖岸上，纳萨斯河与阿瓜纳瓦尔河流进沙漠后汇出这些湖泊。最大的是马伊兰潟湖，即「新比斯开大湖」，旁边还连着别斯卡、特拉瓦利洛和阿拉莫几个小湖。他们由十余个语言各异的游群组成，彼此以纳瓦特尔语往来，村落就设在湖边。他们不种地、不养牲畜，靠潟湖的鱼、猎物和湖岸的豆灌木、仙人掌、龙舌兰为生，随湖水涨落迁居。1444年，这些湖泊还远在任何西班牙人的道路之外。

西班牙人从新建的萨卡特卡斯、杜兰戈银矿向北派出远征队，发现湖岸上村落稠密却没有矿藏，王室便把湖区留给传教士：1594年，腓力二世把此地定名「潟湖省」，交给耶稣会。神父们的年度报告描写这些赤身裸体、没有房屋也不播种的渔民，说他们警惕到作者担心自己被杀掉吃掉；同一份报告还抱怨，在新西班牙，福音只肯沿着白银开出的路走。传教事业始终没能站住。1687年前后耶稣会被逐离此地，传教村废弃，幸存的伊里蒂拉人退回沙漠，此后再没有作为一个独立族群出现。

en:
The Nyakipa held the Pacific corner behind San Quintín Bay, the southwestern edge of the Kiliwa country that crossed the peninsula to San Felipe on the Gulf of California. They spoke the same Yuman language as the eastern Kiliwa, and life followed the same round of water and season. Pit-roasted agave was the staple; families climbed into the hills for acorns and pine nuts in autumn; jackrabbits and quail were driven into agave-fibre nets in communal hunts; and parties trekked to the Gulf shore for fish, shellfish and salt. Their houses were half underground, framed in willow poles and thatched. In 1444 these were autonomous bands, with neither towns, fields nor overlords.

Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo's ships reached San Quintín in 1542, the first Europeans the Kiliwa saw, and only brief expeditions came for the next two centuries: the Jesuit Wenceslaus Linck crossed the eastern approaches in 1766, and the Portolá-Serra march passed west of them in 1769. Settlement began in 1775, when Dominicans Miguel Hidalgo and Manuel García founded Santo Domingo northeast of the bay among the Kiliwa. The first site, thirteen kilometres inland, had too little water, and in 1793 the mission moved four kilometres further east. Epidemics and mission congregations thinned the people, and from Mexican independence in 1821 Santo Domingo had no resident priest.
zh:
尼亚基帕人住在圣金廷湾后方的太平洋一角，即基利瓦地区的西南缘；基利瓦人的土地横跨半岛，东抵加利福尼亚湾畔的圣费利佩。尼亚基帕人与东基利瓦人使用同一种尤曼语，生活也同样随水源和季节轮转。坑烤龙舌兰是主食，秋天各家上山地采收橡子和松子，集体围猎时把长耳兔和鹌鹑赶进龙舌兰纤维织成的网，还成群走到海湾东岸捕鱼、拾贝、取盐。他们的住房半在地下，用柳木杆和茅草搭成。1444年，这些都是自治的小队，没有城镇、农田或宗主。

1542年，胡安·罗德里格斯·卡布里略的船队抵达圣金廷，这是基利瓦人见到的第一批欧洲人；此后两个世纪只有零星远征队到来：耶稣会士文策斯劳斯·林克1766年穿过基利瓦地区东缘，波尔塔拉与塞拉的队伍1769年从其西边经过。定居始于1775年，多明我会士米格尔·伊达尔戈和曼努埃尔·加西亚在海湾东北的基利瓦人中建起圣多明各传教站。第一处站址在距海岸十三公里的内陆，水源不足，1793年传教站再向东迁四公里。疫病和传教集居使人口锐减，1821年墨西哥独立后，圣多明各不再有常驻神父。

en:
Tizapan occupies the southeastern shore of Lake Chapala, where Jalisco lake country meets the Purépecha approaches from Michoacán. Its Nahuatl name refers to chalk or to the white-trunked tizate bush, and Chichimec villages farmed the flats watered by the La Pasión River, fished the shallows and gathered mineral deposits along the bank. Raiding parties from Michoacán repeatedly crossed this exposed shore. In 1444 Tizapan was a borderland of scattered lakeside villages, close to Purépecha armies but without a strong lakeside court of its own.

Spanish captains sent by Hernán Cortés conquered the district late in 1521. Alonso de Ávalos later passed through with the friars Miguel de Bolonia and Juan de Padilla, and native families and Spanish settlers were grouped into the Estancia de Tizapán, later called San Francisco Tizapán. Its grain, fish and lake-shore land were tied to Sayula and the royal province of Ávalos. Tizapan never became a fortress or royal capital; it remained a farming and fishing settlement on the shore where Jalisco and Michoacán meet.
zh:
蒂萨潘位于查帕拉湖东南岸，正是哈利斯科湖滨地带与米却肯普雷佩查方向相接的边地。纳瓦特尔语地名一说指白垩，一说指白干的蒂萨特灌木；奇奇梅卡村社在拉帕西翁河灌溉的平地耕作，在浅水区捕鱼，并采集岸边的矿物沉积。来自米却肯的袭扰队伍一再进入这段开阔湖岸。1444年，蒂萨潘是分散湖滨村社组成的边地，邻近普雷佩查军队的活动范围，却没有自己的强大湖滨王城。

1521年底，埃尔南·科尔特斯派出的西班牙队长征服这一地区。阿隆索·德·阿瓦洛斯后来同修士米格尔·德·博洛尼亚、胡安·德·帕迪利亚到此，原住民家庭和西班牙移民被编入蒂萨潘牧场，后称圣弗朗西斯科·蒂萨潘。这里的谷物、渔获和湖滨土地同萨尤拉与阿瓦洛斯皇家省相连。蒂萨潘没有成为要塞或王城，而是哈利斯科与米却肯交界处一座靠农耕和捕鱼立足的湖滨聚落。

en:
Cuitzeo takes its name from the broad, shallow lake at the northeastern edge of the Purépecha highlands, the name meaning a place of water jars. East of the lake, the Ucareo valley held one of the largest obsidian quarries worked anywhere in pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica: Ucareo obsidian was the principal supply of Tula and Xochicalco, and its blades have been found as far away as Chichen Itza. The Purépecha took the district in the fifteenth century under Hiripan, drew Zinapécuaro and its villages into the tribute network run from Tzintzuntzan, and kept a temple to the mother goddess Cuerauáperi. In 1444 fishermen, maize farmers and obsidian workers lived on a prosperous inland frontier of the Purépecha realm.

The district was assigned as an encomienda to Gonzalo López in 1528, and around 1530 Luis Montañez founded the Spanish settlement of Zinapécuaro, where Franciscans led the evangelization. In 1550 the Augustinians began the monastery of Santa María Magdalena on the lakeshore, raising its church over a temple of the Purépecha sun god Curicaueri with stone from the old building. Its Plateresque facade was carved by a Purépecha craftsman, Juan Metl, who signed his name on a plaque beside the main doorway, the only indigenous signature known on an early colonial church; the open chapel preserves a sixteenth-century fresco of the Last Judgment. The native communities were reorganized as a republic of Indians under the government of Michoacán. In October 1810 Miguel Hidalgo's insurgents entered Zinapécuaro, carrying the independence rising into this corner of Michoacán.
zh:
奎采奥得名于普雷佩查高地东北缘宽阔水浅的湖泊，地名在普雷佩查语里意为盛水器皿之地。湖东的乌卡雷奥谷地有一处采石场，是前西班牙时代中美洲已知规模最大的黑曜石矿之一：乌卡雷奥黑曜石曾是图拉和霍奇卡尔科的主要货源，打制的石叶行销甚广，远至奇琴伊察都有出土。15世纪伊里潘向外扩张时，普雷佩查人取得这一地区，把锡纳佩夸罗及其村落纳入以钦聪灿为中心的贡赋网络，当地还保有祭祀母神库埃拉瓦佩里的神庙。1444年，渔民、玉米农和黑曜石工匠居住在此，是普雷佩查王国富庶的内陆边地。

1528年，奎采奥被封给贡萨洛·洛佩斯作委托监护地；约1530年，路易斯·蒙塔涅斯建立锡纳佩夸罗西班牙人定居点，方济各会士在当地主持传教。1550年，奥斯定会会士在湖滨动工修建圣玛利亚·马格达莱纳修道院，教堂建在普雷佩查太阳神（Curicaueri）的神庙旧址上，用的是旧庙的石料。银匠风格的正门出自普雷佩查工匠胡安·梅特尔（Juan Metl）之手，他在大门旁的饰板上刻下自己的名字，这是殖民早期教堂上仅见的土著工匠签名；露天礼拜堂里保存着一幅16世纪的《最后的审判》壁画。土著村社被整编为印第安人共和国，归米却肯政府管辖。1810年10月，米格尔·伊达尔戈的起义军进入锡纳佩夸罗，把独立起事带到米却肯的这一角。

en:
Cutzamala lies in the hot Tierra Caliente country where streams run down toward the Balsas. Its Nahuatl name means a place of weasels, and before the Purépecha took the town around 1410 a weasel-like idol was worshipped here. They renamed it Apatzingani and made it a southeastern frontier garrison looking toward the valley of Mexico. In 1444 its Matlatzinca and Nahua farmers lived on this armed edge of the realm ruled from Tzintzuntzan; the garrison faced the Aztec fortress of Oztuma, and Purépecha tradition remembered the warriors of Apatzingani serving the death god Apatzi.

In the 1470s Aztec armies under Axayacatl took a string of frontier towns, and the Purépecha answered by fortifying Cutzamala and settling Otomi and Matlatzinca refugees along the border on condition they helped defend it. The frontier only quieted after the Spanish conquest: Cortés held Cutzamala as an encomienda by 1528. Silver from the Alba de Liste mines paid for the church of the Assumption and its cloister, raised from 1555 in Plateresque style under Juan Bautista Moya. In December 1813 the old border town became the muster of José María Morelos, who gathered Mariano Matamoros, Hermenegildo Galeana, Nicolás Bravo and some 6,900 men with thirty cannon and then marched on Valladolid, where he was repulsed; it was the first in a run of defeats that broke his campaign. Agustín de Iturbide was lodged in the town in 1821, the year Spanish rule in Mexico ended.
zh:
库察马拉坐落在炎热的火地，河溪顺着山地流向巴尔萨斯河。它的纳瓦特尔语地名意为「鼬鼠之地」，普雷佩查人约1410年攻取此镇之前，当地供奉着一尊形似鼬鼠的偶像。普雷佩查人把它改名阿帕钦加尼，设为面向墨西哥谷地的东南边境据点。1444年，这里的马特拉钦卡和纳瓦农民住在钦聪灿治下这条驻有军队的边境上；驻军与阿兹特克人的奥斯图马要塞遥遥相对，普雷佩查传说也记得阿帕钦加尼战士侍奉死神阿帕齐。

15世纪70年代，阿萨亚卡特尔麾下的阿兹特克军队连夺边境城镇，普雷佩查人一面加固库察马拉的城防，一面把被阿兹特克人逐出家园的奥托米和马特拉钦卡难民安置到边境，条件是替王国守边。这条边境直到西班牙征服后才平静：1528年，库察马拉已是埃尔南·科尔特斯名下的委托监护地。阿尔瓦·德·利斯特诸矿出产的白银资助了圣母升天教堂及修道院，胡安·包蒂斯塔·莫亚主持工程，1555年起按银匠风格建造。1813年12月，这座边镇成为何塞·玛丽亚·莫雷洛斯的集结地：他会合马里亚诺·马塔莫罗斯、埃梅内希尔多·加莱阿纳、尼古拉斯·布拉沃，聚起约6900人和30门火炮，随后进军巴利亚多利德却遭击退，开始了他的连串败绩。1821年，阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德驻跸此镇，就在西班牙对墨西哥的统治终结的这一年。

en:
The Pátzcuaro basin is a volcanic lake district in the Michoacán highlands and the home ground of Purépecha power. Pátzcuaro, Ihuatzio and Tzintzuntzan stood on the shore as the kingdom's three principal seats, and around the middle of the fifteenth century the cazonci's tribute administration was consolidated at Tzintzuntzan. Its court drew fish and maize from the lake villages, copper weapons and tools from highland mines, and feathers, cacao and cotton cloth from long-distance trade. Tzintzuntzan, 'place of hummingbirds', raised five rounded yácatas on a grand platform above the water. Purépecha armies kept the Aztec Empire out of Michoacán through long frontier wars, and in 1444 it was the capital of a highland state that had checked Mexica expansion, while the older town of Pátzcuaro remained a retreat for nobles and priests.

Tangáxoan Tzíntzicha submitted to Cristóbal de Olid in 1522 without a siege, hoping to spare his capital the fate of Tenochtitlan, but the men of Nuño de Guzmán tortured and executed the last cazonci in 1530 and stripped the lake towns. Vasco de Quiroga, a judge of the second Audiencia, reached the district in 1533 and gathered the scattered population into hospital-towns organised on the plan of Thomas More's Utopia, founding Santa Fé de la Laguna nearby; as the first bishop of Michoacán he moved the civil capital and the episcopal see from Tzintzuntzan to Pátzcuaro in 1539, and Charles V granted the city arms in 1553. Franciscan, Augustinian and Jesuit colleges and the houses of encomenderos and native nobles filled its prosperous decades, until the civil government moved to Valladolid in 1575 and the diocese followed in 1579 and 1580.

Pátzcuaro kept a native government of its own. In 1766 and 1767 its indigenous governor Pedro de Soria Villarroel led a rising against new militias, heavier taxes and the expulsion of the Jesuits, and José de Gálvez put it down. Its best-known insurgent was Gertrudis Bocanegra, born in the town in 1765. She carried messages and gathered intelligence for the rebels, was taken and tortured in 1817 and named no one, and on 11 October she was shot in the main square.
zh:
帕茨夸罗盆地是米却肯高地的火山湖区，也是普雷佩查势力的根据地。帕茨夸罗、伊瓦齐奥和钦聪灿是湖滨三个主要王都；约15世纪中期，国王的贡赋机构集中到钦聪灿，朝廷从湖村征收鱼产和玉米，从高地矿场取得铜制武器和工具，又经长途贸易获得羽毛、可可和棉布。钦聪灿意为「蜂鸟之地」，五座圆顶亚卡塔金字塔排列在俯临湖面的大台地上。普雷佩查军队在连年边境战争中把阿兹特克帝国挡在米却肯之外；1444年，钦聪灿是这个遏止墨西卡扩张的高地国家的都城，较早的帕茨夸罗则仍是贵族和祭司的退居地。

1522年，坦加苏安·特辛特查未经围城便向克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德臣服，想让都城免遭特诺奇蒂特兰的命运；努尼奥·德·古斯曼的部下却在1530年拷打并处死末代国王，洗劫湖滨诸城。第二检审庭法官瓦斯科·德·基罗加1533年来到湖区，把流散的居民聚拢到按托马斯·莫尔《乌托邦》设想组织的医院村镇，并在附近建起圣费德拉拉古纳；他出任米却肯首任主教后，于1539年把行政首都和主教驻地从钦聪灿迁至帕茨夸罗，1553年查理五世颁赐城市纹章。方济各会、奥斯定会和耶稣会的学院，加上监护主和土著贵族的宅邸，填满了它数十年的兴旺日子；1575年行政政府迁往巴利亚多利德，教区在1579年至1580年随之迁走。

帕茨夸罗长期保留着土著自治政府。1766年至1767年，土著总督佩德罗·索里亚·比利亚罗埃尔领导起义，反对新设民兵、加重赋税和驱逐耶稣会，被何塞·德·加尔韦斯镇压。城中最出名的起义者是1765年生于本地的赫特鲁迪斯·博卡内格拉。她为起义军传递消息、搜集情报，1817年被捕后遭受酷刑，始终没有招供，10月11日在主广场被枪决。

en:
Hinonoeino is Hinono'eino, 'our people', first the self-name of the Arapaho proper and, once the divisions merged, of the whole Arapaho nation. Their country was the cold High Plains east of the Rocky Mountain front, where short grass, hard winters and great bison herds set the terms of camp life. In 1444 the Arapaho were far to the northeast, Algonquian farmers of the western Great Lakes who lived with their Gros Ventre kin in the Red River valley; the hunters trailing these plains herds on foot, with dog teams and travois, are unnamed in any record.

French guns gave the Ojibwe the upper hand around the Red River, and before 1700 the Arapaho were moving west, still pedestrian hunters until horses reached them on the Missouri in the early eighteenth century. Five cognate divisions then ranged from south to north, the Hinono'eino speaking Arapaho proper in the middle rank and the Gros Ventre standing farthest north; by the late eighteenth century the four divisions south of the Gros Ventre had fused, and their shared name, Hinono'eino, covered them all. Mounted, they worked the plains as traders, swapping meat and hides for maize and beans at the Arikara, Mandan and Hidatsa towns, and eight age-graded warrior societies kept order in camp and led the raids. Around 1811 they allied with the Cheyenne to hold the Wyoming and Colorado hunting grounds. In 1812 the fur trader Stuart reckoned the Arapaho at 3,050 warriors, about fifteen thousand people.
zh:
希诺诺埃诺（Hinono'eino）意为「我们的人」，起初是阿拉帕霍本体的自称，诸支融合之后又成为整个阿拉帕霍民族的名字。他们的家园在落基山东麓以东寒冷的高地平原，短草、严冬和庞大的野牛群决定了营地生活的面貌。1444年，阿拉帕霍人还远在东北方，是五大湖以西的阿尔冈昆农耕者，和同族的格罗斯文特人一起住在雷德河谷；这时在这片平原上带着狗队和拉橇徒步追随牛群的猎人，没有在任何记载里留下名字。

法国火枪让欧及布威人在雷德河一带占了上风，1700年以前阿拉帕霍人已开始西迁，直到18世纪初马匹在密苏里河流域传入之前，他们仍是步行猎人。当时五支同源的分支由南向北排列，希诺诺埃诺人居中，使用阿拉帕霍本体语言，格罗斯文特人在最北；到18世纪末，格罗斯文特人以南的四支融为一体，共同的名字希诺诺埃诺便涵盖了所有人。骑上马后，他们以贸易立足草原，到阿利卡拉、曼丹和希达察人的村镇用肉和皮革换取玉米和豆类；营中秩序和外出袭掠则由八个按年龄分级的战士会主持。约1811年，他们与夏延人结盟，共保怀俄明和科罗拉多的猎场。1812年，毛皮商人斯图尔特估计阿拉帕霍人有战士三千零五十名，总人口约一万五千。

en:
The Toluca Valley, called Matlatzinco in Nahuatl, is a high maize-growing basin on the upper Lerma River between the Basin of Mexico and Purépecha country. Matlatzinca, Otomi, Mazahua and Nahua communities shared its fields and hill towns. Calixtlahuaca, whose original Matlatzinca name was Pintanbati, was the strongest capital in the valley, while Tollocan remained a smaller rival. Its rulers drew maize and other supplies from broad farmlands, and Mexica and Purépecha armies both watched the routes crossing the upper Lerma. In 1444 Matlatzinco remained independent between the expanding Mexica and Purépecha empires.

Axayácatl's Mexica army conquered the valley in the mid-1470s, removed Calixtlahuaca's ruling dynasty and made Tollocan the tribute capital. Maize, warrior costumes, and cotton and maguey mantles passed through Tollocan toward Tenochtitlan. During the Spanish war against Tenochtitlan, Matlatzinca forces joined the Malinalca and Cohuixca against the Mexica, but Gonzalo de Sandoval and Andrés de Tapia defeated them and brought the valley under Spanish control in 1521. Franciscans arrived the next year; Andrés Castro learned Matlatzinca and tried to shield its people from early colonial abuses. A Spanish town was laid out in 1530. In 1810 Miguel Hidalgo's insurgent army crossed the valley on the way to the Sierra de las Cruces, defeated royalist troops at Monte de las Cruces, and then turned back toward Guadalajara instead of advancing on Mexico City.
zh:
图柳坎所在的托卢卡河谷在纳瓦语中称马特拉钦科，是莱尔马河上游的高寒玉米盆地，处在墨西哥盆地与普雷佩查之地之间。马特拉钦卡、奥托米、马萨瓦和纳瓦诸社群共享农田和山间村镇。卡利斯特拉瓦卡原名平坦巴蒂，是河谷最强的都城，托洛坎则是较小的对手。其统治者凭借广阔农田收取玉米等物资，墨西哥和普雷佩查的军队也都注视着穿过莱尔马河上游的道路。1444年，马特拉钦科仍保持独立，处在扩张中的墨西哥与普雷佩查两强之间。

15世纪70年代中期，阿萨亚卡特尔率墨西哥军队征服河谷，废黜卡利斯特拉瓦卡的王朝，把托洛坎设为贡赋中心。玉米、战装以及棉布和龙舌兰布斗篷经托洛坎送往特诺奇蒂特兰。西班牙人攻打特诺奇蒂特兰期间，马特拉钦卡人与马里纳尔卡人、科维克斯卡人联合反对墨西哥人，但贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔和安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚将其击败，于1521年控制河谷。方济各会次年抵达，安德烈斯·卡斯特罗学会马特拉钦卡语，并设法保护当地人免受早期殖民侵夺。1530年，西班牙人在此设镇。1810年，米格尔·伊达尔戈的起义军穿过河谷进入十字山，在蒙特德拉斯克鲁塞斯击败王党军队，却没有进逼墨西哥城，而是转回瓜达拉哈拉。

en:
Cihuatlan was the Mexica name for a long Pacific shoreline, from the mouth of the Balsas to the approaches to Acapulco, with the Sierra Madre del Sur pressing close behind the beaches. The name means the place of women, the western paradise of the Nahuatl world where the spirits of women who died in childbirth dwelled; the sheltered bay at Zihuatanejo was remembered as a sanctuary of the goddess Cihuateotl. In 1444 the scattered villages belonged chiefly to the Cuitlatecs, whose tongue was a language isolate, with no kin to any other speech, and whose country was called Cuitlatecapan. Their coastal seats were Cuitlatepan near Zihuatanejo and Petatlan, while Chumbia, Panteca and Nahua communities shared the rest of the coast and panned salt in the lagoons by Ixtapa. Purépecha and Mexica power was already pressing in, but no tributary province of Cihuatlan yet existed.

The Mexica emperor Ahuitzotl took Cuitlatepan in 1497, a conquest recorded in the Codex Mendoza, and by 1504 the coast was organized as the tributary province of Cihuatlan, whose tribute included cotton cloth and decorated conch shells. Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte and Simón de Cuenca occupied it with nearly all the Costa Grande in 1523; the Cuitlatec population fell fast, and survivors kept up resistance in the mountains for sixty years. Cortés turned Zihuatanejo Bay into a Pacific shipyard, building three ships of local cedar, the Florida, Espiritu Santo and Santiago, which Álvaro de Saavedra sailed on 31 October 1527 in search of a route to Asia; only the Florida reached Asian waters, and neither the captain nor his crew returned to Mexico. Friars gathered the remaining people into new towns at Tecpan in 1538, Atoyac in 1541 and Petatlan in 1550, and encomiendas and later haciendas shipped cedar, cotton, cacao and coconuts, while gold was found in the Sierra Madre del Sur behind the coast. In 1810 José María Izazaga rose here with 130 men, and José María Morelos made the coast part of his province of Tecpan the following year.
zh:
锡瓦特兰是墨西加人给这条漫长太平洋海岸的称呼，其地北起巴尔萨斯河口，南至阿卡普尔科附近，南马德雷山脉紧逼海滩。其名意为「女人之地」，在纳瓦人的观念里，那是西方的天堂、死于分娩的女子灵魂所居之处；锡瓦塔内霍的避风海湾相传是祭祀女神西瓦泰奥特尔的圣地。1444年时，沿岸分散的村落主要属于库伊特拉特克人，他们的语言是与其他语言都不沾亲的孤立语言，其地称库伊特拉特卡潘。沿海中心是锡瓦塔内霍附近的奎特拉特潘和佩塔特兰，琼比亚、潘特卡和纳瓦人群分住海岸其余各处，并在伊斯塔帕附近的潟湖晒盐。普雷佩查和墨西加的势力已经向这里施压，但锡瓦特兰纳贡省尚未建立。

1497年，墨西加君主阿维索特尔攻占奎特拉特潘，这次征服记在《门多萨手抄本》里；到1504年，整条海岸被编成锡瓦特兰纳贡省，贡物包括棉布和装饰过的海螺壳。1523年，胡安·罗德里格斯·德·比利亚富埃尔特与西蒙·德·昆卡占领此地和科斯塔格兰德大部；库伊特拉特克人口锐减，幸存者在山里坚持抵抗了六十年。科尔特斯把锡瓦塔内霍湾辟为太平洋造船地，用当地雪松造了「佛罗里达号」「圣灵号」和「圣地亚哥号」三艘船。1527年10月31日，阿尔瓦罗·德·萨维德拉率三船起航，寻找通往亚洲的航路；只有「佛罗里达号」抵达亚洲海域，船长和船员都没有回到墨西哥。修士把幸存的原住民聚居于1538年的特克潘、1541年的阿托亚克和1550年的佩塔特兰；委托监护地产和后来的大庄园输出雪松、棉花、可可和椰子，海岸背后的南马德雷山里还发现了金子。1810年，何塞·马里亚·伊萨萨加率一百三十人在这一带起事，次年何塞·马里亚·莫雷洛斯将此地纳入他设立的特克潘省。

en:
Tepeyacac, 'the nose of the hill' in Nahuatl, was a Nahua altepetl in the Tepeaca valley, ruled by three related tlatoque and devoted to Camaxtli, the god its Chichimec settlers had brought with them. It sat on the main road between the Valley of Mexico and the Gulf hot lands, and its market drew merchants from the surrounding country. After the Aztec conquest it was run as a tribute-collecting centre, required to keep luxury goods on sale in its market, with Acatzingo, Tecamachalco and Quecholac subject to it. Tlatelolco took the town in 1438 and the Mexica in 1446, so in 1444 it was a recently subjugated market town on the road between highlands and coast.

In 1520, after the Noche Triste, Cortes learned at Tlaxcala that the townspeople had killed several Spaniards making their way up from Veracruz. His punitive expedition stormed Tepeyacac, and on 4 September 1520 he founded on its site the Villa de Segura de la Frontera, securing the principal inland road for his renewed campaign against Tenochtitlan. In 1543 Franciscan friars moved the settlement to the foot of the hill and raised the monastery of San Francisco; the royal arms granted six years later showed an eagle with open wings on a hill, matching the Nahuatl name. The native population fell from about 25,000 in 1570 to little more than 4,000 by 1626. It entered independent Mexico in 1821 as part of the Puebla district.
zh:
特佩亚卡克在纳瓦语中意为「山鼻」，是特佩阿卡谷地中的一个纳瓦人城邦，由三位同族的特拉托阿尼共治，供奉奇奇梅克先民带来的神祇卡马斯特利。它地处墨西哥谷通往墨西哥湾炎热低地的主要道路上，市集吸引着周边乡野的商人。被阿兹特克征服后，它作为贡赋征集中心经营，市上必须常备珍奇货物，阿卡钦戈、特卡马查尔科和克乔拉克都受它统辖。特拉特洛尔科1438年攻取此地，墨西加人1446年再取之，所以1444年的它是一座新近臣服的商业城镇，坐落在高原通往海岸的路上。

1520年「悲痛之夜」过后，科尔特斯在特拉斯卡拉得知，本地居民杀了数名从韦拉克鲁斯北上的西班牙人。他率军讨伐攻陷特佩亚卡克，于1520年9月4日在原址建立塞古拉-德拉弗龙特拉镇，把这条内陆大道控制在手，作为重新进攻特诺奇蒂特兰的依托。1543年，方济各会士把城镇迁到山脚下，建起圣方济各修道院；六年后王家颁下城徽，上绘山巅展翼雄鹰，正合其纳瓦语名字的含义。土著人口从1570年的约两万五千人降到1626年的四千余人。1821年，它作为普埃布拉辖区的一部分加入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Coyolapan, the Cuilapan of the Spanish, began as Sahayuca, 'at the foot of the mountain', a Zapotec settlement in the western arm of the central valleys of Oaxaca. Farming families had lived here by 500 BC, and it grew into a city-state in Monte Albán's orbit before winning back its independence when that capital collapsed. Mixtec rulers overran the valley afterwards, and by 1444 Cuilapan was a Mixtec-ruled town: its nobles were Mixtec caciques, its macehuales mostly Zapotec, one of the prizes in the long struggle between the Mixtec kings and the Zapotec rulers of Zaachila. Mexica tribute collectors reached it through the garrison at Huaxyácac and took maize, cloth, gold and cochineal, but they left the town's Mixtec rulers in place.

When Francisco de Orozco entered the valleys in 1521 Cuilapan submitted with the other towns, a place of some 43,000 people. Cortés claimed it as Marquis of the Valley of Oaxaca, and his long quarrel with the Spanish city of Antequera ended in 1533 with a royal settlement that left him only four towns, the Cuatro Villas; Cuilapan was one of them and became a district seat in its own right. In 1551 the Dominican Domingo de Aguinaga refounded the town around the monastery of St James, raising a vast open chapel and painted walls to explain the Christian faith to Mixtec and Zapotec congregations; work stopped in the 1570s and the great basilica was never finished. Epidemics had cut the town to 7,000 people by 1600, and in the mid-eighteenth century the Dominicans surrendered the crumbling monastery to the secular clergy.
zh:
科约拉潘在西班牙人笔下作奎拉潘，其前身是瓦哈卡中央谷地西支的萨波特克村落萨哈尤卡，意为「山脚之地」。公元前500年这里已有定居农家，后来成为阿尔班山势力范围内的城邦，阿尔班山崩溃后重获独立。此后米斯特克君主席卷谷地，到1444年，奎拉潘已是一座米斯特克人统治的城镇：贵族是米斯特克酋长，平民多为萨波特克人，是米斯特克诸王与萨奇拉萨波特克君主长期争夺的一块要地。纳瓦收税官经瓦基亚卡克的驻军取走玉米、布匹、黄金和胭脂虫，却留用当地的米斯特克统治者。

1521年弗朗西斯科·德·奥罗斯科进入谷地时，这座约四万三千人的城镇随诸城归降。科尔特斯以瓦哈卡谷地侯爵的身份将它据为己有，同安特克拉城长期争执；1533年的王室裁定了结纠纷，侯爵只保留四座城镇，即「四镇」，奎拉潘为其中之一，并自成一处治所。1551年，多明我会修士多明戈·德·阿吉纳加在圣雅各修道院周围重建此镇，建起巨大的露天礼拜堂和绘满壁画的墙壁，向米斯特克和萨波特克会众讲解基督教义；工程在1570年代停工，宏伟的大教堂始终没有建成。到1600年，疫病已使人口降至七千；18世纪中叶，多明我会把倾颓的修道院交给世俗教士。

en:
Tochtepec, 'rabbit hill' in Nahuatl, later Tuxtepec, lies on the lower Papaloapan river, where the Oaxaca highlands give way to the Gulf coastal plain. Popoluca speakers of the Mixe-Zoque family first settled it, but by the fifteenth century Nahuatl is the language of its markets. The town is the river emporium where highland goods meet canoes bound for the Gulf, and Aztec pochteca merchants keep permanent houses there and use it as a base for the whole region. In 1444 it is still an independent trading town, outside the Mexica empire.

Around 1450 some three thousand settlers from Tenochtitlan and Tlatelolco arrived, and in 1463 the armies of Moctezuma I made Tochtepec a tributary province. Cacao, rubber, liquidambar, tropical feathers, gold ornaments and lip-plugs of amber and crystal went up to the highland capitals, and a Mexica governor, garrison and tribute collector took up residence; Mexica judges also sat there to hear the important lawsuits of the region. After 1521 a Spanish garrison held the river road from the coast to Antequera, but the hot wet lowlands drew few Spanish settlers, and the old town lived on among cattle ranches, canefields and river fisheries. At Amapa lived descendants of cimarrones, slaves who had fled from Yanga and San Juan de la Punta. In 1811, during the war of independence, the Spanish town of San Juan Bautista Tuxtepec was formally laid out on the ancient site.
zh:
托奇特佩克在纳瓦特尔语中意为「兔子山」，即今图斯特佩克，坐落于帕帕洛阿潘河下游，瓦哈卡高地在此倾入墨西哥湾沿岸平原。最早定居的是操米赫-佐克语系语言的波波卢卡人，到15世纪，镇上市场已通用纳瓦特尔语。高地货物在此换上进发海湾的独木舟，阿兹特克长途商人波奇特卡常年在此设馆，把这里当作经营整个地区的基地。1444年，它还是一座独立商镇，不在纳瓦帝国版图之内。

1450年前后，约三千名来自特诺奇蒂特兰和特拉特洛尔科的移民到此；1463年，蒙特祖马一世的军队把托奇特佩克变为纳贡行省。可可、橡胶、枫香脂、热带鸟羽、金饰、琥珀和水晶唇饰运往高原都城，纳瓦长官、驻军和贡赋官驻节镇上，墨西卡法官还在此审理地区要案。1521年后，西班牙驻军把守沿海通往安特克拉的河路，但低地湿热，少有西班牙移民定居，古镇在牧场、蔗田和河鲜之间延续。阿马帕村住的是西马隆人的后代，即从扬加和圣胡安-德拉蓬塔逃出的黑奴。1811年独立战争期间，圣胡安包蒂斯塔·图斯特佩克西班牙城镇在旧址正式辟建。

en:
The province runs from the fishing coast east of the Papaloapan to the Coatzacoalcos river and the forests below the Sierra Mixe. The Olmec city of Tres Zapotes had lain in ruins for centuries by 1444, but the land was far from empty. Popoluca villagers farmed the volcanic Tuxtla hills, while at the river mouth Nahuatl-speaking traders held Coatzacoalcos, the richest emporium on the southern gulf and seat of a polity that stretched towards Tabasco. Its people had fought the Mexica garrison at Tochtepec, and never paid tribute to Tenochtitlan. Far inland the Mixe, who call themselves the Ayuujk, 'the people of the mountain language', lived in mountain señoríos about the sacred peak of Cempoaltepetl, where their legendary king Condoy founded their kingdom; neither the Zapotecs of Zaachila nor the Aztec Triple Alliance fully subdued them.

In the reign of Axayácatl the Coatzacoalcos army destroyed a Mexica force at Cuilonimiquiztlan. The woman the Spanish called La Malinche was born around 1500 in this polity, at Olutla on the Coatzacoalcos; while still a girl she was carried to Xicalango and sold to Chontal Maya, and in 1519 she was among the twenty women given to Cortés at Potonchán, and became his interpreter in Nahuatl and Maya. Diego de Ordaz later sounded the river, and in 1522 Gonzalo de Sandoval founded the Villa del Espíritu Santo on its banks as the Spanish base on the isthmian coast. Spanish columns sent against the Sierra Mixe were beaten back more than once, and Cortés wrote to Charles V that the Zapotecs and Mixes were the only two provinces left unconquered, their country too rocky to cross on foot and their warriors fierce and well armed. The Mixe first admitted Spaniards peacefully in 1555, when Dominicans opened missions at Totontepec and Quetzaltepec.

A royal shipyard and salt-pans worked the lower river. In 1599 the Indians were gathered into new towns, but corsair raids and epidemics so emptied the coast that the district seat moved inland to Acayucan. The San Martín volcano buried the Tuxtlas in ash in 1664 and 1793, and in 1771 royal engineers began surveying a canal across the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.
zh:
本省从帕帕洛阿潘河以东的渔业海岸，延伸到夸察夸尔科斯河与米赫山脉脚下的丛林。1444年，奥尔梅克古城特雷斯萨波特斯已荒废数百年，这片土地却并不空旷：波波卢卡人在火山起伏的图斯特拉山地耕作；河口处，说纳瓦特尔语的商人据有墨西哥湾南岸最富庶的商港夸察夸尔科斯，以此为都的政权势力一直伸向塔瓦斯科。他们曾与驻托奇特佩克的纳瓦驻军交战，这座商港从未向特诺奇蒂特兰纳贡。深入内陆，自称阿尤克（意为「说山语的人」）的米赫人在圣山森波阿尔特佩特峰周围的山林酋邦中生活，传说中的君王孔多伊曾在此建国；萨奇拉的萨波特克人和阿兹特克三邦同盟都没能完全征服他们。

阿克萨亚卡特在位时，夸察夸尔科斯的军队在奎洛尼米基斯特兰歼灭一支纳瓦大军。西班牙人称作马林切的女子约1500年出生在这个政权境内的夸察夸尔科斯河畔奥卢特拉，年幼时被带到西卡兰科，卖给琼塔尔玛雅商人；1519年，她作为波通昌人献给科尔特斯的二十名女子之一，凭纳瓦特尔语和玛雅语做了他的译员。迭戈·德·奥达斯后来探测了这条河，1522年贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔在河畔建立圣灵镇，作为西班牙人在地峡海岸的据点。远征米赫山脉的部队一再被击退，科尔特斯在给卡洛斯五世的信中承认，萨波特克人和米赫人是仅剩的两个未被征服的省份，那里土地崎岖，徒步都难通过，战士又凶悍、装备精良。米赫人和平接纳的第一批西班牙人是多明我会士，他们1555年在托通特佩克和克察尔特佩克开设传教点。

夸察夸尔科斯河下游设有王家造船厂和盐场。1599年，原住民被集中迁入新的村镇，但海盗袭扰和疫病使海岸人口流失，地区治所只得内迁阿卡尤坎。1664年和1793年，圣马丁火山两度以火山灰覆盖图斯特拉；1771年，王家工程师开始勘测特万特佩克地峡的运河线路。

en:
Behind the long sandbar of Isla del Carmen, the Laguna de Términos opens into a maze of rivers and mangrove coast at the western edge of the Maya world, and the spit of Punta Xicalango was long counted as the boundary itself. This was the country of the Putún, the Chontal Maya of Tabasco, canoe-borne traders whose sea routes ran from the Grijalva delta round Yucatán as far as the Sula coast in Honduras. On the shore between the San Pedro river and the lagoon stood Xicallanco, a Nahuatl-speaking merchant town, one of three Nahuatl enclaves in Chontal country whose people the Aztec emperors backed against their Maya neighbours. Aztec pochteca kept storehouses here for the cacao of Tabasco, which served both as cargo and as money, and the town's markets drew Maya and Mexican merchants together. After the league of Mayapán broke up in 1441 the Chontal towns governed themselves, and in 1444 Xicallanco was among the richest emporia on the Gulf coast, trading and warring with its neighbours by turns.

Juan de Grijalva's four ships first charted the Boca de Términos in May 1518. In 1525 the port destroyed Cortés's supply ships and killed their crews, and Francisco de Montejo took it only in 1529, naming the town Salamanca; when he left for Campeche in 1531 the place slipped from Spanish control and his son had to retake it five years later. By 1550 Xicallanco was largely abandoned and its people had been moved to Jonuta. The lagoon then passed to the logwood cutters. English buccaneers held Isla de Tris from 1558 as a raiding base and shipped dyewood to Europe, and repeated expeditions out of Veracruz and Campeche dislodged them only briefly. In December 1716 Alonso Felipe de Andrade's flotilla seized the island, and on 16 July 1717 his garrison beat off the last pirate counter-attack and founded the presidio of El Carmen, which grew into the Spanish timber port of the lagoon.
zh:
卡门岛长沙坝的背后，特尔米诺斯潟湖通向一片河网纵横、红树林密布的水乡，这里是玛雅世界的西缘，希卡兰戈角向来被当作这条边界的标志。这片土地属于普顿人，即塔瓦斯科的琼塔尔玛雅人；他们操舟为业，海路从格里哈尔瓦河三角洲绕过尤卡坦，远达洪都拉斯的苏拉海岸。圣佩德罗河与潟湖之间的海岸上矗立着希拉兰科（西班牙文献写作希卡兰戈），一座说纳瓦语的商人城镇，是琼塔尔人土地上三处纳瓦人飞地之一，阿兹特克君主支持这些纳瓦人同玛雅邻居争斗。阿兹特克的长途商人波奇特卡在此设有货栈，囤积塔瓦斯科的可可，可可既是货物，也是当时的货币，城中的市集把玛雅和墨西哥商人聚到一处。1441年玛雅潘联盟瓦解后，琼塔尔诸城各自为政；1444年的希拉兰科是墨西哥湾沿岸最富庶的商埠之一，与邻邦时而通商，时而交战。

1518年5月，胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦的四艘船首次测绘了特尔米诺斯水道。1525年，希拉兰科人摧毁了科尔特斯的补给船并杀死船员；弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍直到1529年才攻下此地，将城镇命名为萨拉曼卡。他1531年转往坎佩切后，此地脱离西班牙控制，其子五年后再度夺回。到1550年，希拉兰科已基本被废弃，遗民被迁往霍努塔。潟湖随后落入伐木者之手。英国海盗从1558年起占据特里斯岛，既以之为劫掠基地，也把染料洋苏木运往欧洲，西班牙人从韦拉克鲁斯和坎佩切屡次出兵，都只能短暂将他们赶走。1716年12月，阿隆索·费利佩·德·安德拉德率舰队夺取该岛，1717年7月16日守军击退海盗最后一次反扑，建起卡尔门要塞，日后发展为潟湖地区西班牙人的木材港。

en:
Ceh Pech took in the northern Yucatec towns around Motul, with Chicxulub and Chuburná on the coast and Conkal, Yaxkukul and other settlements inland. The Maya name joins ceh, or deer, with Pech, the lineage that ruled the kuchkabal after Mayapan broke apart. Motul had stood empty for years when Nohcabá Pech, a kinsman of Mayapan's Cocom lords, settled there after the city's fall. In 1444 his family was still drawing old towns into a new jurisdiction; the Tutul-Xiu of Maní held the stronger power in western Yucatán.

The Pech cooperated with the Spaniards early and at times sent auxiliaries against rival Maya provinces, but Spanish forces took Motul in 1538 and ended the jurisdiction's independent rule. The Crown nevertheless recognized the Pech as native nobility and allowed family heads to use the title Don. In 1544 Pech lords wrote to Charles V explaining their cooperation and position; by 1567 Pech batabs governed 21 of the province's 25 towns. Motul was granted in encomienda to Francisco de Bracamontes, while Pech governors continued to hold office in Motul, Chicxulub, Chuburná and neighboring towns through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
zh:
克佩奇统辖莫图尔周围的尤卡坦北部城镇，沿海有奇克苏鲁布和丘布尔纳，内陆则有孔卡尔、亚什库库尔等定居点。其玛雅名称由意为「鹿」的ceh和家族名「佩奇」组成；玛雅潘解体后，佩奇家族统治这个辖区。莫图尔曾荒废多年，与玛雅潘科科姆统治者有亲族关系的诺卡瓦·佩奇在城陷后迁居此地。1444年，他的家族仍在把各旧城镇整合成新辖区，马尼的图图尔-休则在西尤卡坦势力更强。

佩奇人很早就与西班牙人合作，有时还派辅兵攻打敌对的玛雅辖区，但西班牙军队仍于1538年攻占莫图尔，结束这里的独立统治。西班牙王室承认佩奇家族为土著贵族，允许家族首领使用「唐」的称号。1544年，佩奇首领致信卡洛斯五世，说明自己的合作与处境；到1567年，克佩奇25座城镇中有21座由佩奇家族的巴塔布治理。莫图尔被作为监护地授予弗朗西斯科·德·布拉卡蒙特，而佩奇家族的地方长官在17至18世纪仍任职于莫图尔、奇克苏鲁布、丘布尔纳及邻近城镇。

en:
Uaymil was the lagoon-strewn eastern country of Yucatan, between Ekab and Chactemal: a large province whose wetlands left long stretches barely settled. Its principal place was Bakhalal, on a great freshwater lagoon; the Mayan name means 'surrounded by reeds'. Chontal-speaking settlers from the south called the Chanes founded it in the fifth century as Sian Ka'an Bakhalal. When the League of Mayapan tore apart between 1441 and 1461, Bakhalal became the chief town of one of the independent Maya kuchkabalob. In 1444 the breakup was still under way, and the canoe channels, milpa maize fields and cacao groves of Uaymil answered to local Maya lords.

Alonso Davila entered for Francisco de Montejo in 1531, reached Tulum and Bakhalal and founded Villa Real, but Maya attacks drove him out. The Pacheco entrada returned in 1543, and Melchor Pacheco laid out Salamanca de Bacalar in 1544, the seat from which the Spanish ruled the southern half of Quintana Roo. The villa never grew: in 1630 about thirty Spaniards held the east coast's main settlement, a staging point on the routes toward Guatemala and Honduras. Pirates then learned to come through the lagoon channels. The Scot Peter Wallace settled south of the Hondo River in 1640 to cut dyewood, the first English camp on that coast, which later grew into Belize; in 1652 the Cuban Diego el Mulato sacked Bacalar and the shore was almost abandoned. The Spanish answered with Fort San Felipe on the lagoon bank, finished in 1729, and brought in a hundred and forty-nine Canary Islanders between 1733 and 1735 to refill the town. Safe behind its walls, Bacalar shipped mahogany, dyewood, sugar, fruit and livestock.
zh:
瓦伊米尔是尤卡坦东部、埃卡布与查克特马尔之间一片潟湖纵横的土地；辖区广阔，但大片沼泽使许多地带人烟稀少。首要聚落巴克哈拉尔坐落在淡水大潟湖畔，玛雅语意为「芦苇环绕之地」。5世纪时，来自南方、讲琼塔尔语的查内人在此建城，名西安卡安·巴克哈拉尔。1441年至1461年马亚潘联盟崩解后，巴克哈拉尔成为独立的玛雅库奇卡巴尔辖区之一的首镇。1444年这场分裂仍在进行，瓦伊米尔的独木舟水道、米尔帕玉米地和可可园都归本地玛雅首领管辖。

1531年，阿隆索·达维拉奉弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍之命进入此地，抵达图卢姆和巴克哈拉尔并建立比亚雷亚尔城，却在玛雅人攻击下撤出。1543年帕切科父子的远征军重返，1544年梅尔乔·帕切科建起萨拉曼卡·德·巴卡拉尔，西班牙人以此为中心统治今金塔纳罗奥南部。这座城镇始终没有壮大：1630年，东海岸这座最大的定居点只有约三十名西班牙人，是通往危地马拉和洪都拉斯路线上的中转站。后来海盗摸清了潟湖水道：1640年，苏格兰人彼得·华莱士在翁多河以南落脚砍伐染木，那是英国人在这片海岸的第一个据点，后来发展成伯利兹；1652年，古巴人迭戈·埃尔穆拉托洗劫巴卡拉尔，海岸几乎被弃守。西班牙人的对策是在湖畔修筑圣费利佩堡，1729年完工，又在1733年至1735年迁来一百四十九名加那利岛民充实城镇。有了城墙护卫，巴卡拉尔向外输出桃花心木、染木、糖、水果和牲畜。

en:
East of the Chiapas highlands the land drops into the Selva Lacandona, rainforest threaded by the Lacantún river and closed at its heart by the great Laguna Miramar. In the fifteenth century a warlike Ch'ol-speaking Maya people, whom the Spanish later called the Lacandones, ruled it from Lakam-Tún, a town built on the Peñón rock, an island at the southern end of the lagoon. Neither the Aztecs nor the highland cities reached them. They grew cacao in forest clearings and carried it south to the towns of Verapaz, and baptised Maya who fled the colonial towns later slipped into the same forest to live among them. In 1444 Lakam-Tún held the woods without a rival.

Hernán Cortés heard of the Lacandones while crossing neighboring Kejache country in 1524, yet no Spaniard reached them for decades. Lakam-Tún was sacked in 1585, and its people withdrew up the Lacantún and about 1586 built Sac Balam, the 'white jaguar', in a wide bend of the river. From there they raided the Cuchumatanes frontier for a century, and the Spanish garrisons at San Mateo Ixtatán and Santa Eulalia never made the road safe; at Cobán and Cahabón they traded cacao and achiote for salt, cotton and Spanish iron tools. Franciscans who entered the forest in 1692 were chased out. The great expeditions of 1685 and 1695 ended in the city's fall, when it was refounded as Nuestra Señora de los Dolores. In 1712 the survivors were marched away to Huehuetenango and absorbed into the highland towns, and by the middle of the century the Lacandones had vanished as a people. Yucatec-speaking refugees later moved into the empty forest and inherited their name.
zh:
恰帕斯高地以东，地势倾入拉坎东雨林，拉坎通河穿行林莽，辽阔的米拉马尔湖卧在密林中央。15世纪，一支说乔尔语的好战玛雅人称雄于此，西班牙人后来叫他们拉坎东人；他们的都城拉坎敦建在湖南端佩尼翁岩的岛上，阿兹特克和高原城邦都到不了这里。他们在林间空地种植可可，南运到韦拉帕斯的城镇出售；后来连不堪殖民统治、逃出城镇的受洗玛雅人也躲进这片林子，投奔他们。1444年，拉坎敦是雨林中没有对手的主人。

1524年，科尔特斯途经相邻的凯哈切人之地时听说了拉坎东人，但此后数十年没有西班牙人到过这里。1585年拉坎敦被攻破洗劫，拉坎东人溯拉坎通河退入密林深处，约1586年在大河湾处建起新都萨克巴兰，意为「白美洲豹」。此后一百年，他们不断袭扰库丘马塔内斯边境，圣马特奥-伊斯塔坦和圣欧拉利娅的西班牙驻军始终无法保障道路安全；在科万和卡阿翁，他们用可可和胭脂树籽换取盐、棉布和西班牙铁制工具。1692年进入丛林的方济各会修士被赶走，1685年和1695年的两次大征伐终于攻陷萨克巴兰，旧城被改建为多洛雷斯圣母镇。1712年，幸存的拉坎东人被强行迁往韦韦特南戈，散入高原城镇，到18世纪中叶，拉坎东人作为一个族群已经消失。后来操尤卡坦语的难民进入空寂的丛林，接过了他们的名字。

en:
Chacujal was the principal Maya city of the lower Polochic River, which here
enters Lake Izabal before its water reaches the Caribbean through the Dulce
River and Amatique Bay. Its ruins have never been identified, and scholars
know it as the unnamed city on the Polochic. The river-bottom heat grew
cacao, and canoes carried the lowland's goods down to Nito, the seaport on
Amatique Bay, where cargoes changed hands for the coastal run to Yucatán.
Above this hot country rose the highland kingdoms of the K'iche' and
Kaqchikel, whose traders and raiding parties came down to the lake. In 1444
the towns of the Polochic and Izabal made a rich lowland between those
kingdoms and the Caribbean sea lanes.

Spanish ships found the lake from the sea. Gil González Dávila took Nito by
a night assault in March 1524 and renamed it San Gil de Buena Vista.
Cortés, marching overland to Honduras, reached it in April 1525, had small
vessels built, and worked his way up the Dulce and across Izabal. At
Chacujal he found ordered plazas and planned streets, but the inhabitants
had carried their goods away and fled before him. The Spanish never fought
a highland-style campaign here. The forest country from the Rabinal valley
to Nito was called the Tierra de Guerra, the Land of War. Bartolomé de las
Casas and his Dominicans offered to subdue it by preaching alone and began
in 1537, and the country took the name Verapaz, True Peace. Scattered towns
were gathered into new settlements nearer the colonial centres, and the old
lake cities were abandoned to the bush.

Izabal still carried the colony's trade: Guatemala's indigo went out by
lake and river to Spain, and pirates learned to follow the same channel in.
A first tower at the narrowest of the Dulce had a chain stretched across
the river at nightfall, but English, Dutch and Portuguese raiders burned it
in 1604. A proper fort rose in 1644 under Governor Diego de Avendaño,
called Fuerte Bustamante; the judge Lara y Mogrovejo redesigned its walls
and rebuilt it in 1651, when it took the name Castillo de San Felipe de
Lara, and engineers gave it Vauban-style bastions by 1697. It guarded the
port of San Antonio de las Bodegas, served as prison and customs house, and
was abandoned in 1817. Constant slave-raiding, much of it by Mosquito
raiders, had left the lake shores largely deserted long before that.
zh:
查库哈尔是波洛奇克河下游的玛雅大城，波洛奇克河在此注入伊萨瓦尔湖，湖水再
经杜尔塞河穿过阿马蒂克湾流入加勒比海。城址已不可考，学者称之为「波洛奇克
河上的无名之城」。谷底湿热，宜于可可生长，独木舟把低地产物运到阿马蒂克湾
畔的海港尼托，在那里换装大船，沿海岸驶往尤卡坦。湿热低地的上方是基切人
和卡克奇克尔人的高地王国，商人与武装队伍常下到湖畔。1444年，波洛奇克河
与伊萨瓦尔湖畔的城镇构成一片富庶低地，夹在高地王国和加勒比海路之间。

西班牙人从海上找到这片湖区。1524年3月，希尔·冈萨雷斯·达维拉夜袭夺取尼
托，改名为圣希尔·德·布埃纳维斯塔。1525年4月，科尔特斯从陆路进军洪都拉
斯途中抵达尼托，命人打造小船，沿杜尔塞河驶入伊萨瓦尔湖。他在查库哈尔看
到齐整的广场和规划过的街道，居民却已搬空财物、弃城而走。西班牙人没有在
这里进行高地式的武力征服。这片从拉维纳尔谷地延伸到尼托的林地名叫「战争
之地」，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯和他的多明我会修士提出单凭讲道将其降服，
于1537年开始，此地后来得名韦拉帕斯，意为「真正的和平」。分散的村镇被集
中到靠近殖民中心的新聚居点，湖畔诸城就此荒废，重新长起丛林。

伊萨瓦尔湖仍承担着殖民地的运输：危地马拉的蓝靛经湖、河出海运往西班牙，
海盗也顺着同一条水道摸进来。杜尔塞河最窄处最初立有一座塔楼，入夜后拉起
横江铁索封锁河面，但英、荷、葡海盗还是在1604年把它烧毁。1644年，总督迭
戈·德·阿文达诺主持建起正规要塞，名布斯塔曼特堡；王室法官拉腊·莫格罗韦
霍改建墙式并于1651年重建，要塞也改名为圣费利佩·德·拉腊堡，工程师又在
1697年以前为它添上沃邦式棱堡。它护卫着圣安东尼奥·德·拉斯·博德加斯港，
兼作监狱和海关，1817年被废弃。而在这以前很久，莫斯基托掠奴者持续不断的
袭扰，已让湖岸大部分地方荒无人烟。

en:
Chortli takes its name from the Ch'orti' Maya, whose villages in north-western Honduras linked the old Copán country with the hot Ulúa and Sula lowlands behind the Gulf of Honduras. In 1444 the highland Ch'orti' belonged to the network the Spanish later called Payaquí, while Tolupán, or Xicaque, groups farmed and fished around the lower Ulúa and the lagoon anchorage between Omoa and the future Puerto Caballos. Maize, cochineal, cacao and forest goods moved along native canoe routes, and no European had yet touched the coast.

Columbus claimed Honduras for Castile here in 1502, on his fourth voyage. A conquest expedition under Gil González Dávila landed in 1524, and Hernán Cortés reached the lagoon in 1526 after a storm drowned seventeen of his horses, which gave the place the name Puerto Caballos. In 1536 the Tolupán leader Cicumba fought Pedro de Alvarado in the Sula lowlands and lost; on 27 June that year Alvarado founded San Pedro de Puerto Caballos, the seed of San Pedro Sula. The open roadsteads drew raiders for two centuries: French pirates burned Puerto Caballos in 1592, Christopher Newport held it briefly in 1603, and in 1667 François l'Olonnais, the buccaneer called the Bane of Spain, sacked the port and marched on San Pedro. Spain answered from Omoa, refounded in 1752 and fortified to guard the silver shipped out from the Tegucigalpa mines. The great fort of San Fernando was finished in 1774 and stormed on 16 October 1779 by 150 British soldiers and seamen, who took its 365-man garrison; fever and a Spanish counter-attack drove them out within weeks.
zh:
卓特利因乔尔蒂玛雅人得名，他们在洪都拉斯西北部的村社连接着古老的科潘地区与洪都拉斯湾后方炎热的乌卢阿、苏拉低地。1444年，高地的乔尔蒂人属于西班牙人后来称作帕亚基的联盟网络；托卢潘人（又称希卡克人）在乌卢阿河下游、奥莫阿与日后的卡瓦略斯港之间的潟湖锚地一带农耕渔捞。玉米、胭脂虫、可可和林产品沿本土独木舟商路流通，此时还没有欧洲人到过这片海岸。

1502年哥伦布第四次航行时，在此代表卡斯蒂利亚宣布占有洪都拉斯。1524年，吉尔·冈萨雷斯·达维拉率征服队登陆；1526年，科尔特斯抵达这片潟湖，此前一场风暴淹死了他的17匹马，他便把这里命名为卡瓦略斯港（意为马港）。1536年，托卢潘首领西昆巴在苏拉低地迎战佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多，兵败；同年6月27日，阿尔瓦拉多建立圣佩德罗·德·卡瓦略斯，即圣佩德罗苏拉的前身。此后两个世纪，无遮无拦的港口不断引来袭击者：法国海盗1592年焚毁卡瓦略斯港，克里斯托弗·纽波特1603年短暂占港，1667年，有「西班牙之祸」之称的弗朗索瓦·洛洛奈洗劫港口，继而向圣佩德罗进军。西班牙的对策是奥莫阿：1752年重建该城并修筑要塞，护卫从特古西加尔巴银矿运出的白银。巨大的圣费尔南多堡1774年竣工，1779年10月16日即被150名英军士兵和水手强攻拿下，365人的守军全数被俘；但热病和西班牙反攻迫使英军在几周内撤离。

en:
Xoconochco, 'the place of the sour prickly pear' in Nahuatl, which the Spaniards wrote as Soconusco, is the hot coastal plain squeezed between the Pacific and the forested wall of the Sierra Madre de Chiapas, a country of wet rivers, volcanic earth and cacao groves. Before the strangers came it was shared among rival Mixe-Zoque towns, Mapastepec, Huehuetán, Mazatán and Ayutla among them, whose merchants carried cacao and achiote up the long coast road to the Mexican highlands. The Aztecs had not crossed the mountains, and the K'iche' kingdom of Q'umarkaj coveted the same groves. In 1444 Xoconochco was still free, and its cacao already passed for the finest known.

Ahuitzotl conquered the coast in 1486 and made it a tribute province, posting two governors and probably a garrison over levies of cacao, cotton mantles, feathers and jaguar skins; Moctezuma II had to send troops back in 1502 and 1505. Pedro de Alvarado passed through on his march to Guatemala in 1524, and the Crown declared Soconusco a province two years later under Pedro de Montejo, its first governor, while its people were already dying of the new diseases. Bartolomé de las Casas sent Dominicans in 1545, who divided the land into six parishes, and from 1568 the coast belonged to the Captaincy General of Guatemala. Its cacao was famous enough that Miguel de Cervantes himself asked the king for its governorship. The province was absorbed into Chiapas in 1790, and the hurricane of 1794 drove the district capital from Escuintla to Tapachula; in 1821 the coastal towns declared with the highlands for independence.
zh:
索科诺齐科在纳瓦特尔语里意为「酸仙人掌之地」，西班牙人写作索科努斯科。这片炎热沿海平原夹在太平洋与恰帕斯马德雷山脉的林墙之间，河川纵横、火山土肥沃，到处是可可林。外来者到来之前，这里分属马帕斯特佩克、韦韦坦、马萨特兰、阿尤特拉等互相争战的米塞-索克语城邦，商人沿漫长的滨海大道把可可和胭脂树籽运往墨西哥高地。阿兹特克人还没有翻过山岭，基切人的库马尔卡赫王国也觊觎着同一片可可林。1444年的索科诺齐科仍是自由之地，出产的可可已被视为天下第一。

1486年，阿维索特尔征服海岸，把它变成贡赋行省，留下两名总督、可能还有一支驻军，征收可可、棉披风、鸟羽和美洲豹皮；1502年和1505年，蒙特苏马二世还得两度派兵平叛。1524年，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多进军危地马拉时途经海岸，两年后王室宣布索科努斯科为行省，任命佩德罗·德·蒙特霍为首任总督，而此时当地人已在旧大陆传来的疫病下成批死去。1545年，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯派来多明我会修士，把土地分为六个教区；1568年起，海岸隶属危地马拉都督辖区。这里的可可名声太大，连米格尔·德·塞万提斯都亲自向国王求任总督。行省1790年被并入恰帕斯，1794年的飓风又把治所从埃斯昆特拉赶到塔帕丘拉；1821年，沿海诸城与高地一同宣布独立。

en:
Raritan is the low country at the mouth of the Raritan River, where tidal marshes and inlets open into Raritan Bay behind Staten Island. The Sanhican Lenape fished, gathered shellfish and planted corn and beans on the western shore, and their canoes and trails joined the bay to hunting grounds upstream. Their name for the river is read either as 'river beyond the island' or as 'forked river'. In 1444 no Dutch chart yet showed the anchorage, and the shore followed Lenape usage, not a European land patent.

A quarrel over stolen pigs and an attempt to make off with a Dutch yacht brought the colony's revenge on the band in the 1640s. Cornelis van Tienhoven led more than a hundred men against them, killed several and tortured the chief's brother held as a hostage; the Raritans answered by killing Dutch settlers, and Director Willem Kieft, who had planned an extermination campaign, folded the feud into Kieft's War of 1643 to 1645. The Sanhicans withdrew inland, and after a peace conference in 1649 a Lenape band from across the Hudson, the Wisquaskecks, moved onto the empty ground and inherited the name Raritan. English rule followed the seizure of New Netherland in 1664.

Scottish proprietors laid out Perth Amboy in 1683 on the point the Lenape called Ompoge, 'level ground'; named New Perth for the Earl of Perth, it became the capital of East Jersey in 1686 and afterwards alternated with Burlington as a capital of New Jersey until Trenton took the role in 1790. A ferry to Staten Island ran from 1684 and made the town a halt on the road between New York and Philadelphia, while Raritan Landing and New Brunswick shipped the valley's grain and timber. In the War of Independence the British used the Raritan as a route across New Jersey and raided the American outpost at Bound Brook in 1777, while militia harried their patrols along the river.
zh:
拉里坦是拉里坦河口的低地，潮汐沼泽与水汊在斯塔滕岛后方汇入拉里坦湾。萨尼坎莱纳佩人在西岸捕鱼、采贝，种植玉米和豆类，独木舟和步道把海湾同上游猎场连起来。河名在莱纳佩语里一说意为「岛后的河」，一说意为「分汊的河」。1444年，荷兰人的海图上还没有这个锚地，海岸依照莱纳佩人的习惯使用，并无欧洲人的土地特许状。

1640年代，一场围绕偷猪和盗走荷兰游艇未遂的争端，把殖民地的报复引到这里。科内利斯·范廷霍芬率一百多人袭击该支系，杀死数人，又酷刑折磨被扣为人质的酋长之弟；拉里坦人袭杀移民作为回答，而早已筹划剿灭行动的总督威廉·基夫特便把这场仇怨并入1643至1645年的基夫特战争。萨尼坎人退往内陆，1649年和谈之后，一支来自哈德逊河对岸的莱纳佩人维斯奎斯克克人迁到空地，也接过了拉里坦之名。1664年英国夺取新尼德兰，这里随之转入英国统治。

1683年，苏格兰业主在莱纳佩人称作奥姆波吉（Ompoge，意为「平地」）的角上规划珀斯安博伊；新城为纪念珀斯伯爵而称新珀斯，1686年成为东泽西首府，此后又与伯灵顿轮替担任新泽西首府，直到1790年特伦顿接掌此位。1684年开通的斯塔滕岛渡口使这里成为纽约与费城之间通道上的一站，拉里坦码头和新不伦瑞克则输出河谷的谷物与木材。独立战争期间，英军把拉里坦河一线当作横穿新泽西的通道，1777年突袭大陆军在邦德溪的前哨，民兵则在沿河不断袭扰其巡逻队。

en:
Lenca is the Lenca mountain country of southwestern Honduras, its valleys running down to the Pacific shore of the Gulf of Fonseca. In 1444 the land was divided among rival confederacies. Noble rulers governed each town with four assistants, commoners grew maize, beans, manioc, cotton and cacao, and tribute was paid in honey and cotton mantles. Markets drew Nahuat, Ch'orti' and Xinca traders, and the guancasco ceremony bound even hostile towns in a truce of processions and exchanged gifts. In the hot lowlands by the gulf, Lenca villagers lived beside Chorotega and Nahua settlements where Nacaome and Choluteca later stood, and no European ship had yet entered the bay.

The first Spaniard to enter the gulf was Andrés Niño, pilot of Gil González Dávila, who sailed in from the Pacific in 1522 and named it for Juan Rodríguez de Fonseca, the bishop who oversaw Spain's Indies voyages. Conquest reached the mountains within fifteen years: Cristóbal de la Cueva planted Xerez de la Frontera de Choluteca in the southern lowlands in 1535, and Gonzalo de Alvarado founded Gracias a Dios at Opoa in 1536; his men are said to have named it when, reaching level ground at last, they thanked God for flat land. In 1537 the Lenca rose under Lempira, a war captain whose name means 'lord of the mountains'. He fortified the Peñol de Cerquín, a rock stronghold above the valleys, and the chronicler Herrera puts his host at more than 30,000 men from over 200 towns. Montejo's troops forced the stronghold only after months of fighting; Lempira was killed before the year ended and the rising collapsed. On 16 May 1544 Gracias became the seat of the Royal Audiencia of Los Confines, high court for Guatemala and Nicaragua; the court sat there only five years before removing to Santiago de Guatemala.

Choluteca's wealth came from the southern mines, above all the silver works at El Corpus. In 1692 its council won leave to move the town across the river, away from the floods and closer to the mining road, and its cathedral was built in 1785. The towns and valleys of the Lenca country passed out of Spanish rule with Central American independence in 1821.
zh:
莱安卡是洪都拉斯西南部的伦卡人山地，一道道山谷向南延伸到太平洋岸的丰塞卡湾。1444年，这片土地分属几个互不相让的联盟：贵族首领在四名辅佐者协助下治理城镇，平民种植玉米、菜豆、木薯、棉花和可可，贡赋缴纳蜂蜜和棉斗篷。市集吸引来纳瓦特语、乔尔蒂语和辛卡语商人，「瓜纳卡斯科」仪式甚至能让敌对城镇停战，以游行和互赠礼物相会。海湾边的炎热低地上，伦卡村社与乔罗特加人、纳瓦人的聚落相邻而居，西班牙人后来在那里建起纳卡奥梅和乔卢特卡；此时还没有欧洲船只进入湾内。

第一个驶入海湾的西班牙人是吉尔·冈萨雷斯·达维拉的领航员安德烈斯·尼尼奥。1522年，他从太平洋驶入湾中，以主持西班牙海外航行事务的主教胡安·罗德里格斯·德·丰塞卡之名将海湾命名。十五年内，征服就推进到山地：1535年，克里斯托瓦尔·德·拉·奎瓦在南部低地建立乔卢特卡边境赫雷斯；1536年，贡萨洛·德·阿尔瓦拉多在奥波阿建立格拉西亚斯-阿迪奥斯，据说部众终于踏上平地，感谢上帝，城名便取自这句感谢的话。1537年，伦卡人在战时首领伦皮拉率领下起事，他的名字意为「山之主」。他扼守山谷间的岩山要塞塞尔金岩山，据编年史家埃雷拉记载，从200多个城镇聚起三万多人。蒙特霍的军队打了好几个月才攻克要塞；伦皮拉在当年被杀，起事随之瓦解。1544年5月16日，格拉西亚斯成为洛斯孔菲内斯王家检审法院驻地，统辖危地马拉和尼加拉瓜的诉讼；法院只在此驻了五年，便迁往圣地亚哥-德危地马拉。

乔卢特卡的财富来自南部矿山，尤其是埃尔科尔普斯的银矿。1692年，市议会获准把城镇迁到河对岸，以避洪水并靠近矿道；城中大教堂建于1785年。1821年中美洲独立，伦卡山地的城镇与河谷随之脱离西班牙统治。

en:
Tziccoac was a Tének or Huastec stronghold in the southern Huasteca, its name read as 'place of the precious serpent'. Its core lay on Mesa de Cacahuatenco, a long ridge between the Vinazco and Pantepec rivers on the Veracruz and Puebla border. Ravines protected the settlement, while trails from the ridge ran to Metztitlán, the Tuxpan coast and the Totonac lowlands. In 1444 Tziccoac was still independent, but Triple Alliance soldiers were already pressing the frontier and the nearby strongpoint of Metlaltoyuca was being fortified.

The rulers of Tziccoac submitted to the Triple Alliance in 1458 and later joined the Tetzapotitlan rising of 1476. After Ahuitzotl's reconquest in 1486, Mexica governors, colonists and state cults secured the routes toward Ixhuatlán, Tuxpan and Papantla; many Tziccoac men were carried off to build the Templo Mayor and were sacrificed at its dedication in 1487. Spanish forces took the Huasteca between 1519 and the 1530s, and Nuño de Guzmán's slaving raids from Pánuco emptied stretches of this old frontier. In 1592 Spanish officials gathered the survivors into congregations such as Chicontepec and San Cristóbal Ixhuatlán. The church and parish records at Chicontepec were burned during the independence war.
zh:
齐科瓦克是南瓦斯特克的特内克人要塞，地名意为「宝蛇之地」。其核心位于卡瓦滕科台地，即韦拉克鲁斯与普埃布拉边界、维纳斯科河和潘特佩克河之间的一道长岭。峡谷护卫着聚落，岭上山路通往梅斯特特兰、图克斯潘海岸和托托纳克低地。1444年，齐科瓦克仍保持独立，但三方同盟士兵已经进逼边疆，附近的梅特拉尔托尤卡据点也在修筑防御。

齐科瓦克统治者于1458年向三方同盟臣服，后来又参加1476年的特特萨波蒂特兰起义。1486年阿维索特尔重新征服后，墨西加官吏、移民和官方崇拜控制了通往伊斯瓦特兰、图克斯潘和帕潘特拉的道路；许多齐科瓦克男子被掳去修建大神庙，并在1487年神庙落成礼上被献祭。1519年至1530年代，西班牙军队征服瓦斯特克，努尼奥·德·古斯曼从帕努科发动的奴隶掳掠使旧边疆大片地区人口流散。1592年，西班牙官员把幸存者并入奇孔特佩克、圣克里斯托瓦尔·伊斯瓦特兰等聚居地。独立战争期间，奇孔特佩克的教堂和教区档案被焚毁。

en:
Metztitlan, the place of or among the moon, occupied a lake basin and the deep barranca cut through Hidalgo's Sierra Baja by the Venados River. Its Otomi rulers traced their independent state to refugees from Xaltocan after that city fell in 1395. By 1444 a priest-ruler, or tlatoani, governed from Metztitlan, with Molango as the second town; colonial accounts give the capital about 20,000 people and Molango 10,000. Aztec armies took Tulancingo, the northern Mezquital Valley and parts of the Sierra Alta, boxing the kingdom between the Amajac River and the Barranca de Metztitlan, but cliffs and ravines kept it outside the Aztec Empire. The moon deity Zäna had a temple in the capital, and the Metzca calendar kept its own day names alongside forms close to Aztec practice.

Tenochtitlan's fall exposed the mountain kingdom. In 1522 Hernán Cortés sent Tlaxcalan warriors with a Spanish captain to subjugate Metztitlan, ending its independent rule. The Augustinians reached the town in 1536 and used it as a mission station on their route toward the Sierra Alta and Huasteca. Tradition assigns their first low convent, La Comunidad, to Juan de Sevilla in 1537; work moved to higher ground after the flood of 1539, though later scholars have questioned that explanation. The Convento de los Santos Reyes rose above the former lunar sanctuary, built chiefly from 1540 to 1560, with its church completed in 1569. In 1700 the indigenous artist Salvador Ocampo finished its fifteen-metre main altarpiece, five tiers of sculpture and painting. During Miguel Hidalgo's rising, indigenous revolts broke out at Metztitlan in April and September 1811.
zh:
梅茨蒂特兰意为「月之地」或「月间之地」，据有伊达尔戈州低山脉中的湖泊盆地，以及贝纳多斯河切出的深谷。奥托米统治者把独立国家的渊源追溯到1395年哈尔托坎陷落后的避难者。到1444年，一位兼具祭司身份的特拉托阿尼以梅茨蒂特兰为都，莫兰戈是第二重镇；殖民记载称都城约有2万人，莫兰戈约有1万人。阿兹特克军队夺取图兰辛戈、梅斯基塔尔谷北部和高山脉部分地区，把王国压缩在阿马哈克河与梅茨蒂特兰峡谷之间，但悬崖和深谷使它没有落入阿兹特克帝国。月亮神萨纳在都城中有神庙，梅茨卡人的历法接近阿兹特克历，却保留自己的日名。

特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，这个山地王国也暴露在西班牙人面前。1522年，埃尔南·科尔特斯派特拉斯卡拉战士随同一个西班牙队长前去征服，梅茨蒂特兰的独立统治就此结束。1536年，奥斯定会会士抵达此城，把它作为前往高山脉和瓦斯特卡途中的传教据点。传统说法认为，胡安·德·塞维利亚于1537年建立首座低地修道院拉科穆尼达；1539年洪水后，工程转往高处，不过后世学者对迁建是否因洪水有疑问。三王修道院建在旧日月亮圣所上方，主要工程在1540年至1560年间，教堂于1569年完工。1700年，土著艺术家萨尔瓦多·奥坎波完成十五米高的主祭坛，五层结构上布置雕刻与绘画。米格尔·伊达尔戈起义期间，梅茨蒂特兰在1811年4月和9月两度爆发土著起事。

en:
Apatzingán sits in the hottest basin of the Tierra Caliente, where the Tepalcatepec and Balsas rivers run between the volcanic highlands and the Sierra Madre del Sur. Heat and river water made it cotton country: in the fourteenth century Purépecha lords from Lake Pátzcuaro drew the Balsas valley into their tribute system, settling Purépecha farmers beside Nahuas, Matlatzincas and Otomíes, and the irrigated fields sent maize and cotton up to the cazonci's cities on the lake. In 1444 its villages answered to Tzintzuntzan, and the marches towards Colima were the Purépecha kingdom's restless western frontier.

The kingdom ended within a decade of the Spaniards' arrival. Cristóbal de Olid entered Michoacán in 1522 and the last cazonci, Tangáxuan II, submitted; in 1530 Nuño de Guzmán had him tried, tortured and burned alive, and his ashes were thrown into the Lerma River. The valley was split into encomiendas, and Franciscan and Augustinian friars gathered the scattered hamlets into congregaciones and founded the town of Apatzingán in 1617. Ranches and haciendas then took over the watered plain, growing cotton, sugar, cacao and indigo for the highland trade. The town earned its name in Mexican history in 1814: harried by Félix Calleja's royalist armies, Morelos's insurgent Congress of Anáhuac abandoned Chilpancingo and withdrew here, and on 22 October Morelos and his deputies sanctioned the Constitutional Decree for the Liberty of Mexican America, Mexico's first constitution. Morelos was captured a year later and shot, but the congress he had convened gave the insurgency a republican program.
zh:
阿帕钦甘地处铁拉卡连特最炎热的盆地，特帕尔卡特佩克河与巴尔萨斯河在火山高原和南马德雷山脉之间流过。酷热加上河水灌溉，使这里成为棉花之乡：14世纪，帕茨库罗湖畔的普雷佩查王公把巴尔萨斯河谷纳入贡赋体系，迁来普雷佩查农民与纳瓦人、马特拉钦卡人、奥托米人杂居，灌溉田出产的玉米和棉花输往湖畔卡松西的诸城。1444年，这一带的村落向钦聪灿纳贡，朝向科利马的边境是普雷佩查王国动荡的西部门户。

西班牙人到来不到十年，这个王国便告终结。1522年克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德进入米却肯，末代卡松西坦加轩二世投降；1530年努尼奥·德·古斯曼将他审判、酷刑后烧死，骨灰撒进莱尔马河。河谷被划为委托监护地，方济各会和奥斯定会的修道士把散落的村舍归并为集居村，1617年建立阿帕钦甘镇。牧场和庄园随后占住这片有灌溉的平原，种植棉花、甘蔗、可可和靛蓝，运往高地贸易。这座小镇在墨西哥史上留名是在1814年：莫雷洛斯的起义国会阿纳瓦克国会在费利克斯·卡列哈所率王军的追击下放弃奇尔潘辛戈退守于此，10月22日莫雷洛斯与代表们批准《墨西哥美洲自由制宪法令》，即墨西哥第一部宪法。莫雷洛斯一年后被俘并遭枪决，但他召集的国会已为起义事业定下共和纲领。

en:
Cholula grew on the Puebla plain around Tlachihualtepetl, the 'hand-made mountain', a pyramid enlarged stage by stage over more than a thousand years and the largest anywhere by volume. By the late fifteenth century it was the holiest city of the Nahua highlands: priests were trained and initiated at the temple of Quetzalcoatl, pilgrims came from every neighbouring people, and Cortes later counted 430 temples in the city. Its permanent market was one of the greatest in Mesoamerica, where pochteca brought cacao, quetzal feathers and obsidian and Cholula's Mixteca-Puebla polychrome pottery sold across central Mexico and Oaxaca. The Triple Alliance never conquered it; its own lords kept it neutral between Tenochtitlan and the Tlaxcalans, and in 1444 it was a crowded priestly and merchant city on the roads joining the Valley of Mexico, Oaxaca and the Gulf coast.

In October 1519, marching on Tenochtitlan, Cortes and his Tlaxcalan allies called the city's lords to the central square and fell on the crowd. As many as 6,000 Chololtecs died in the massacre and much of the city burned; Spanish accounts say La Malinche had warned Cortes of an ambush, while indigenous accounts say there was none. In those same days Captain Diego de Ordaz climbed Popocatepetl and brought back sulphur for gunpowder. Franciscans arrived in 1529, pulled down the Quetzalcoatl temple and raised the San Gabriel friary on its base. The Capilla Real, begun in 1540 for indigenous congregations, stands under forty-nine domes in seven naves, and forty-seven churches went up across the barrios in the colonial years. The Great Pyramid was crowned with the sanctuary of the Virgin of the Remedies. Epidemics and the rise of nearby Puebla stripped the city of its old importance; in 1714 its indigenous San Andres quarter won standing as a separate Indian republic, and in 1821 Cholula entered independent Mexico.
zh:
乔卢拉崛起于普埃布拉平原，城畔便是特拉奇瓦尔特佩特尔，意为「人造之山」；这座金字塔千余年间一层接一层加高，论体积为世界之最。到15世纪末，它已是纳瓦高原最神圣的城市：羽蛇神神庙是祭司受训与受职之地，朝圣者来自周边各族，科尔特斯后来数出城中有430座神庙。这里的常设市集是中美洲最大的市集之一，波奇特卡商人运来可可、格查尔鸟羽和黑曜石，乔卢拉产的米斯特卡-普埃布拉彩陶远销墨西哥中部和瓦哈卡。三国同盟始终没能征服它：乔卢拉由自己的首领统治，在特诺奇蒂特兰与特拉斯卡拉之间保持中立，1444年时是一座人烟稠密的祭司与商人之城，位于连接墨西哥谷、瓦哈卡和墨西哥湾沿岸的道路上。

1519年10月，在进军特诺奇蒂特兰途中，科尔特斯和特拉斯卡拉盟友把城中首领召到中央广场，随即向人群动手：乔卢拉大屠杀中多达六千人遇害，城邑大半被焚。西班牙方面的记载称拉·马林奇事先警告科尔特斯有伏兵，土著记载则说根本没有伏击。就在这几天，迭戈·德·奥达斯上尉攀上波波卡特佩特火山，带回硫磺配制火药。方济各会士1529年抵达，拆毁羽蛇神神庙，在其台基上建起圣加百列修道院；1540年动工的王家礼拜堂为土著信众而建，七个中厅上覆四十九座穹顶。殖民年代里，各个街区共建起四十七座教堂，大金字塔顶也盖上了雷梅迪奥斯圣母圣殿。瘟疫加上邻近普埃布拉的兴起，使乔卢拉不复重要；1714年土著聚居的圣安德烈斯街区获准成为单独的土著共和国，1821年乔卢拉并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Teloloapan, a Nahuatl name usually read as 'round stone over the water', sits about 1,860 metres high in the Sierra Madre del Sur, on the mountain road between Iguala and the Balsas lowlands. Chontal, Izcuca and Nahua Coixca communities occupied its valleys before Tepanec and Mexica forces pushed in during the 1410s and 1430s. In 1444 the district paid tribute to the Mexica, but it remained hard border country facing the Purépecha Empire. The mountains yielded minerals, villages grew cotton and maize, and soldiers moved through high passes between the two powers.

That border drew large garrisons after the Templo Mayor dedication. In 1487 Ahuitzotl punished Teloloapan, Oztuma and Alahuixtlán for staying away from the ceremony, then moved about nine thousand settlers from the Valley of Mexico to hold the cotton lands and watch the Purépecha frontier. After 1521 Spanish encomenderos took the same tribute towns, and Teloloapan later became a royal corregimiento. Waldo Hernández led a native revolt against that order in 1804 and 1805. During the independence war the town changed hands four times in 1810 and 1811; José Gabriel de Armijo made it his southern headquarters until Vicente Guerrero captured him there in December 1818. Two years later Pedro Ascencio Alquisiras defeated Agustín de Iturbide nearby. Local tradition recalls Guerrero and Iturbide meeting at Acatempan on 10 January 1821, opening the alliance that issued the Plan de Iguala.
zh:
特洛洛瓦潘是纳瓦特尔语地名，通常解释为「水上的圆石」，位于南马德雷山脉近两千米的高处，扼守伊瓜拉通往巴尔萨斯低地的山路。琼塔尔人、伊斯库卡人和科伊克斯卡纳瓦人曾先后居住在这些山谷，特帕内克与墨西加军队则在1410年代至1430年代逼入此地。1444年，这一带已向墨西加纳贡，却仍是面对普雷佩查帝国的艰苦边地。山地出产矿物，村落种植棉花和玉米，两支强权的军队穿行于高处山口之间。

大神庙落成前后，这条边地派驻了大批屯守者。1487年，特洛洛瓦潘、奥斯图马和阿拉维斯特兰没有参加典礼，阿维索特尔随即出兵惩罚，并从墨西哥谷迁来约九千人，控制棉田、监视普雷佩查边境。1521年后，西班牙委托监护主接管这些纳贡城镇，特洛洛瓦潘后来成为王室科雷希米恩托。1804年至1805年，瓦尔迪·埃尔南德斯领导原住民反抗这一统治秩序。独立战争期间，城镇在1810年至1811年间四次易手；何塞·加夫列尔·德·阿米霍把这里设为南方司令部，直到比森特·格雷罗在1818年12月将其攻占。两年后，佩德罗·阿森西奥·阿尔基西拉斯在附近击败阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德。当地传说称，格雷罗与伊图尔维德于1821年1月10日在阿卡特潘会面，双方随后结成发表伊瓜拉计划的联盟。

en:
Coixtlahuaca, the Nahuatl 'plain of snakes', lies in a high valley between the Pueblan plains and the Mixtec mountains, on the merchant road that joined the Valley of Mexico to Oaxaca and the Pacific coast. Its capital, Inguiteria, was a market town of Chochos and Mixtecs where Nahuatl served as the traders' tongue, and the lords of Coixtlahuaca also ruled Cuicatec communities to the east. Merchants from Mexico, Cholula and the Oaxaca Valley dealt there in gold dust, quetzal feathers, cacao, cochineal, dyed rabbit fur and cotton cloth, and the town's dyes were known across central Mexico. In 1444, under Atonaltzin, it was one of the four great Mixtec lordships and paid tribute to no one.

That wealth brought the Mexica down on it. Atonaltzin had the central Mexican merchants in the town killed and seized their goods, breaking the rules that kept Mesoamerican trade routes open; Moctezuma I marched in in 1458, and after several years of war Atonaltzin was defeated and killed and Coixtlahuaca became a Mexica garrison town, sending warrior costumes, shields, quetzal feathers, cochineal and gold dust to Tenochtitlan. Its envoys submitted to Hernán Cortés in September 1520, but the valley rose again after Moctezuma II's death and Andrés de Tapia reconquered it in 1522. It entered New Spain as San Juan Bautista Coixtlahuaca. Native painters drew the new colonial boundaries on the Lienzo de Coixtlahuaca between 1527 and 1552, and Dominicans raised one of the large mission churches on the Oaxacan route, its altarpiece finished in 1584.
zh:
科伊斯特拉瓦坎在纳瓦特尔语中意为「蛇之平原」，坐落在普埃布拉平原与米斯特克山地之间的高谷，位于连接墨西哥谷、瓦哈卡和太平洋海岸的商路上。都城因吉特里亚是乔乔人与米斯特克人交易的市场城镇，纳瓦特尔语是商人的通用语，科伊斯特拉瓦坎的君主还统治着东边的奎卡特克社群。来自墨西哥谷、乔卢拉和瓦哈卡谷的商人在此买卖金砂、格查尔鸟羽、可可、胭脂虫红、染色兔皮和棉布，这里的染料在中部墨西哥远近闻名。1444年，阿托纳尔钦治下的科伊斯特拉瓦坎是米斯特克四大政权之一，不向任何人纳贡。

这笔财富把墨西卡人招来了。阿托纳尔钦处死城中的中部墨西哥商人并没收货物，破坏了维系中美洲商路通行的规矩；蒙特苏马一世1458年发兵，数年后阿托纳尔钦战败被杀，科伊斯特拉瓦坎变成墨西卡驻军城镇，向特诺奇蒂特兰输送战装、盾牌、格查尔鸟羽、胭脂虫红和金砂。1520年9月，它的使者向埃尔南·科尔特斯投降，但蒙特苏马二世死后山谷再度起事，安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚1522年重新将其征服。它以圣胡安·包蒂斯塔·科伊斯特拉瓦坎之名并入新西班牙。1527年至1552年间，本地画师在《科伊斯特拉瓦坎画布》上绘出殖民当局划定的新界；多明我会在瓦哈卡传教路线上建起一座大教堂，祭坛装饰1584年完成。

en:
Cuetlaxtlan, 'the place of skins' in Nahuatl, which the Spaniards later wrote
as Cotaxtla, lay on the hot Sotavento plain, where the rivers of central
Veracruz reach the Gulf through lagoons and a string of offshore sand islands.
Its Totonac towns grew maize and cotton, fished the river mouths and traded
cacao, amber and tropical bird feathers along the coast road to Cempoala.
Through the first half of the fifteenth century it was one of the free Totonac
lordships, courted by Tlaxcala and eyed across the mountains by the Mexica; in
1444 its lords still took no orders from Tenochtitlan.

Later in the century Moctezuma I's armies conquered the coast and levied
tribute in cacao, quetzal feathers and warrior costumes, and Axayacatl put
down its revolt with a Mexica garrison. In April 1519 Cortes landed on the
beach facing the islet of San Juan de Ulua and founded Villa Rica de la Vera
Cruz, the first Spanish municipality on the American mainland. The Totonac
lords of the region answered the call of Cempoala's ruler, whom the Spaniards
called the Fat Chief: they seized the Aztec tribute collectors and sent
warriors and porters with Cortes on his march to Tenochtitlan. The anchorage
became Veracruz, the one port in New Spain licensed to load Mexican silver
onto the annual treasure fleets, while sugar-cane haciendas spread across the
Sotavento.

Silver made the roadstead worth defending. In 1568 the viceroy's galleons
trapped John Hawkins and Francis Drake at San Juan de Ulua and attacked in
breach of a truce, sinking or capturing four of their six ships; the island
citadel was fortified from the 1590s. Even so the Dutch pirate Laurens de
Graaf sacked the city in 1683. Walls went up around Veracruz in the
eighteenth century, and during the independence wars the coast saw years of
guerrilla fighting. On the night of 26 October 1821 the last Spanish troops
abandoned the city and shut themselves in the island fortress.
zh:
奎特拉斯特兰，纳瓦语意为「兽皮之地」，西班牙人后来写作科塔斯特拉，地处炎热
的索塔文托平原：韦拉克鲁斯中部的河流穿过潟湖与一连串近海沙洲，在此注入墨
西哥湾。当地的托托纳克村镇种植玉米和棉花，在河口捕鱼，沿通往森波阿拉的海
岸大道交易可可、琥珀和热带禽羽。15世纪上半叶，这里是自由的托托纳克小邦之
一，特拉斯卡拉多方拉拢，山外的墨西卡人虎视眈眈；1444年，它的首领还不听命
于特诺奇蒂特兰。

15世纪后期，蒙特苏马一世的军队征服这片海岸，征取可可、格查尔鸟羽和武士戎
装，阿克萨亚卡尔又以墨西卡驻军镇压了当地的起义。1519年4月，科尔特斯在圣胡
安·德·乌卢阿小岛对面的海滩登陆，建立「比利亚里卡·德·拉·韦拉克鲁斯」，
这是美洲大陆上第一个西班牙人市镇。沿海的托托纳克首领响应森波阿拉首领（西班牙人称他「胖酋长」）的号
召，拿下阿兹特克贡官，派出武士和脚夫随科尔特斯进军特诺奇蒂特兰。这片锚地后来发展成韦拉克鲁斯，是新西班牙唯一获准
把墨西哥白银装上一年一度宝船队的港口，甘蔗庄园也随之遍布索塔文托平原。

白银使这片锚地值得死守。1568年，新西班牙总督的舰队在圣胡安·德·乌卢阿堵
住约翰·霍金斯和弗朗西斯·德雷克，撕毁休战之约发起攻击，六艘英船被击沉或俘
获四艘；岛上要塞自1590年代起修筑。1683年，荷兰海盗劳伦斯·德·格拉夫仍攻破
并洗劫了城市。18世纪，韦拉克鲁斯筑起城墙；独立战争期间，海岸一带游击战连年
不断。1821年10月26日夜，最后一支西班牙军队弃城退入岛上要塞。

en:
Yopitzinco was the Mexica name for Yope country, the Pacific slope of the Méphaa or Tlapanec people southeast of Acapulco. Fishing villages faced the Costa Chica, while paths climbed the Qmitlán valley into mountains divided among Cacahuatepec, Pochotitlan, Xocotlan and Xochitepec. No single capital ruled all those towns. In 1444 Mexica armies and client towns pressed in from the north, yet the Yope villages kept their independence; the fortress of Quecholtenanco watched the frontier. Fish, cotton and mountain food moved along narrow trails.

The northern Méphaa kingdom of Tlapa submitted to Ahuitzotl in 1486 and was entered in the Mexica tribute rolls, but Yopitzinco did not. Spanish encomenderos reached the coast in 1521 and met the same resistance. After people from Cuautepec killed Spaniards and their native allies in 1531, a Spanish campaign scattered the Yopes into the mountains and drove some refugees as far as Nicaragua; the fighting continued until 1535. Franciscan missionaries made little progress. Augustinian friars founded a convent at Chilapa in 1534 and promoted cotton, indigo and rebozo weaving around the mission. Land disputes kept Méphaa communities under arms from 1716 onward, and in 1810 mountain villages joined the independence rising to recover their communal lands.
zh:
约皮钦科是墨西加人对约皮人之地的称呼，指阿卡普尔科东南、梅法阿人（也称特拉帕内克人）居住的太平洋坡地。沿海渔村面朝开阔海岸，山路沿克米特兰河谷伸入山地，卡夸瓦特佩克、波乔蒂特兰、索科特兰和索奇特佩克各据一方，没有一座统辖全部城镇的都城。1444年，墨西加军队和附庸城镇从北方压来，约皮人的村落仍保持独立，克乔尔特纳南科要塞监视着这条边疆。鱼、棉花和山地粮食沿狭窄山路运送。

1486年，北方的梅法阿王国特拉帕向阿维索特尔臣服，并被载入墨西加贡赋名册，约皮钦科却没有屈服。1521年，西班牙委托监护主抵达海岸，遇到同样顽强的抵抗。1531年，夸乌特佩克人杀死西班牙人及其原住民盟友，西班牙远征军随后把约皮人驱散进山中，部分难民远至尼加拉瓜；战事一直持续到1535年。方济各会传教士没有多少进展。奥斯定会修士于1534年在奇拉帕建立修院，并在传教区推广棉花、靛蓝和雷博索披巾织造。土地争端使梅法阿社群从1716年起持续武装；1810年，山地村落加入独立起义，要求收回共有土地。

en:
Tehuantepec guards the narrowest waist of the Mexican land bridge, where the Pacific shore opens below the southern sierra into a maze of lagoons, salt pans and fishing grounds. The road across the isthmus carried trade between the Mexican plateau and Xoconochco, and the coast's salt, goldsmiths' work and cochineal dye were prized far inland. First Zoque and Huave country, it was taken in the fifteenth century by the Zapotec kings of Zaachila, who built the fortress-city of Guiengola on a hill above the Tehuantepec river, walled and terraced, with two pyramids, a ball court and a palace, and pushed the Huave fishermen back onto the sandspits. In 1444 Tehuantepec was the forward edge of the Zaachila kingdom, bracing for the Aztec advance.

War came in 1497, after King Cosijoeza, whose name means 'storm of obsidian knives', had Aztec spies in his country put to death. Ahuitzotl's armies burned Huaxyacac and Mitla on their march, and his general sat seven months before Guiengola; Cosijoeza held out with a Zapotec and Mixtec host of sixty thousand men and ended the siege by marrying the tlatoani's daughter, the princess Xilabela. Her son Cosijopii was the last Zapotec king, and in 1523 he offered his vassalage to Charles V, so the isthmus passed to Spain without a battle. Guiengola was abandoned, and the baptized king, now Juan Cortés Sicasibí, made his seat in the Spanish villa of Tehuantepec and raised the great Dominican monastery of Santo Domingo between 1543 and 1555. On 21 March 1660 the Tehuano Indians, ground down by the tribute and forced labour of alcalde mayor Juan de Avellano, stoned him to death and burned the royal houses; they ruled themselves for a year under Marcos de Figueroa, a descendant of the old kings, until a Crown judge tricked the leaders into surrender and had them put to death.
zh:
特万特佩克扼守墨西哥地峡最窄的腰部，南部群山脚下，太平洋岸展开成潟湖、盐田与渔场交错的水网。穿越地峡的大道连接墨西哥高原与索科诺齐科，海岸出产的食盐、金银细工和胭脂虫红深受内陆珍视。这里最初是索克人和瓦韦人的土地，15世纪被萨奇拉的萨波特克诸王夺取，他们在特万特佩克河畔的山丘上筑起要塞城市吉恩戈拉，城墙绕山、台地层叠，城内有两座金字塔、一处球场和一座宫殿，又把瓦韦渔民逼退到沙嘴之上。1444年的特万特佩克是萨奇拉王国的前哨，正对着阿兹特克扩张的方向。

1497年战火终于烧到地峡。此前国王科西霍埃萨（名字意为「黑曜石刀之风暴」）处死了潜入境内的阿兹特克间谍，阿维索特尔的大军在进军途中焚毁米特拉等高原诸城，麾下大将把吉恩戈拉围困了七个月。科西霍埃萨据城坚守，手下是萨波特克与米斯特克联军六万人，最后以迎娶特拉托阿尼的女儿解围。公主之子科西霍皮是末代萨波特克王，1523年向查理五世称臣，地峡未经一战归入西班牙。吉恩戈拉就此废弃，受洗后改名胡安·科尔特斯·西卡西维的国王以西班牙人建立的特万特佩克镇为治所，在1543至1555年间建起宏伟的圣多明各修道院。1660年3月21日，特瓦诺印第安人不堪市长胡安·德·阿韦利亚诺的贡赋与劳役，用石头将他砸死，焚毁王室官署；他们在老王后裔马科斯·德·菲格罗亚治下自治一年，最终王室法官诱降首领，将他们处死。

en:
Champutun is the river mouth where a small river enters the Gulf of Mexico, the site of the Maya port of Chakán Putum, inhabited since at least the tenth century by Putún, or Chontal Maya, fishermen and traders. When the League of Mayapán broke up in 1441 the coast split into rival lordships, and Chakán Putum held the shore from Seybaplaya to Laguna de Términos. Conquistadors who later saw the town counted more than 8,000 houses and a fleet of more than 2,000 fishing and trading canoes. In 1444 it was an independent Yucatec coast lordship, and no Spaniard had yet touched its shore.

The first meeting was a rout. In 1517 Francisco Hernández de Córdoba put his men ashore for water, and a thousand armed Maya met them on the beach under the one-armed chief Moch; Bernal Díaz del Castillo, who fought there, remembered the warriors shouting calachuni, 'the captain', so that their arrows and spears would find the leaders. Fifty-seven Spaniards were killed and Córdoba, wounded thirty-three times, died of his hurts after reaching Cuba, and the bay became Puerto de Mala Pelea, the Port of the Bad Fight. Juan de Grijalva came back in 1518 to avenge it: he took three arrows and lost two teeth, seven of his men died, but the Maya chief fell with some two hundred warriors.

Spain's first lasting foothold on the peninsula was built on that same river mouth. In 1538 Lorenzo de Godoy moved the settlement of San Pedro Tanoche to Champutun, and when the local chiefs plotted against the thin garrison Montejo's nephew seized them by surprise and renamed the post Salamanca de Champotón. Franciscans arrived in 1546, the year Montejo introduced sugarcane, and the district became a sugar country worked by Spaniards, Maya and enslaved Africans. English pirates sacked the town three times between 1644 and 1748.
zh:
坎普敦位于一条小河注入墨西哥湾的河口，是玛雅港口查坎·普图姆的故地：至迟10世纪起，普图恩人（又称琼塔尔玛雅人）已在这里打鱼、经商。1441年马亚潘联盟瓦解，沿海分裂为彼此争战的政权，查坎·普图姆据有从塞瓦普拉亚到特尔米诺斯潟湖的海岸。后来见到这座城镇的征服者清点出八千多座房屋、两千多艘渔用和商用独木舟。1444年，它是一个独立的尤卡坦沿海政权，还没有西班牙人踏上这里的海岸。

双方的第一次相遇以西班牙人溃败告终。1517年，弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦率部登岸补充淡水，独臂酋长莫奇带着上千名全副武装的玛雅人在滩头迎战；随军士兵贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯·德尔·卡斯蒂略后来回忆，玛雅战士齐声高喊他们语言里的「头领」，好让箭矢和长矛专找带队的人。五十七名西班牙人被杀，科尔多瓦身中三十三处伤，撤回古巴后伤重而死，这片海湾遂得名「恶战港」。1518年，胡安·德·格里哈尔瓦重返此地复仇，自己中了三箭、掉了两颗牙，七名部下丧命，但玛雅酋长与约两百名战士战死。

西班牙人在尤卡坦半岛的第一个持久据点就设在这个河口。1538年，洛伦索·德·戈多伊把圣佩德罗·塔诺切定居点迁到坎普敦；当地酋长密谋对付这支薄弱的驻军时，蒙特霍的侄子先发制人，将他们一网成擒，据点改名萨拉曼卡·德·坎普敦。1546年方济各会修士到来，同年蒙特霍下令引种甘蔗，这一带成为由西班牙人、玛雅人和非洲黑奴劳作的蔗糖之乡。1644至1748年间，英国海盗三次洗劫这座城镇。

en:
Ah Canul covered the northwestern Yucatán plain later called the Camino Real, a large jurisdiction reaching from Punta Kipté on the coast toward the Río Homtún near Campeche. Its name can be read as protector: the Canul lineage had guarded the approaches to walled Mayapan for the Cocomes against the Tutul-Xiu. When Mayapan fell in 1441-43, eight Canul batabs moved west and founded Calkiní, throat of the sun, beside the Halim well and a ceiba. In 1443 they made Ah Tzab Canul, their eldest, halach uinic. In 1444 the new confederation contained eight districts; after Ah Tzab died, its batabs ruled through a council rather than appoint another supreme lord.

Ah Canul offered stiff resistance during Montejo's third campaign. In 1540 Francisco de Montejo y León, the Younger, summoned the regional batabs to Campeche; most Canul leaders refused, above all the batab of Calkiní. He advanced with native allies and forty Spanish soldiers. Canul watchers posted in high trees signalled with conchs, and the heir of Tzab Canul met the column with archers before Spanish firearms and cavalry broke the resistance and killed him. Calkiní submitted beneath the same ceiba that had marked the confederation's foundation, then passed in encomienda to Gaspar Pacheco. Franciscans led by Luis de Villalpando and Juan de Herrera arrived in 1544; when Alonso Ponce visited in 1588, twenty-three friars were working from Calkiní among the neighboring towns.
zh:
阿卡努尔位于尤卡坦半岛西北部平原，即后来的皇家大道一带，辖区从海岸的基普泰角延伸到坎佩切附近的翁通河，是当时面积最大的玛雅辖区之一。其名可解作「保护者」：卡努尔家族曾替科科姆人戍守有城墙的玛雅潘，防备图图尔-休人。1441—1443年玛雅潘陷落后，八名卡努尔巴塔布西迁，在哈利姆井和一棵木棉树旁建立卡尔基尼，地名意为「太阳之喉」。1443年，他们推举最年长的阿·察布·卡努尔为哈拉奇·维尼克。1444年，这个新联盟分为八个辖区；阿·察布死后，诸巴塔布不再拥立最高首领，改用议事会共治。

阿卡努尔在蒙特霍第三次征伐中顽强抵抗。1540年，弗朗西斯科·德·蒙特霍-莱昂「小蒙特霍」命各地巴塔布前往坎佩切，多数卡努尔首领拒绝从命，卡尔基尼的巴塔布态度最坚决。小蒙特霍率原住民盟军和四十名西班牙士兵推进。卡努尔哨兵爬上高树，用海螺通报消息；察布·卡努尔的继承人率弓箭手迎击，却被火枪和骑兵击溃，本人战死。卡尔基尼在当年联盟成立的那棵木棉树下投降，随后被作为监护地授予加斯帕尔·帕切科。1544年，路易斯·德·比利亚尔潘多和胡安·德·埃雷拉率方济各会士抵达；到1588年阿隆索·庞塞到访时，已有二十三名修士从卡尔基尼向邻近城镇传教。

en:
Ecab covered the northeast corner of Yucatán: a flat limestone coast running
south from Cabo Catoche, with the islands of Isla Mujeres and Cozumel just
offshore. When the league of Mayapán broke up around 1441 the peninsula
split into some sixteen kuchkabals, but Ecab alone had no halach uinik over
it. Its coastal towns were ruled by rival batabs, and the batabs of Cozumel
carried the most weight. Cozumel, the Maya Kùutsmil or 'island of swallows',
was the busiest place in the province. Pilgrims crossed to its shrines at
San Gervasio to consult Ixchel, goddess of childbirth, weaving and the moon,
and merchant canoes on the coastal route from Honduras to Tabasco put in
there for honey and wax. Mainland villages lived by fishing and salt. The
