He led Mataram troops in the Madura campaigns and sent rice for Agung's 1628-1629 sieges of Batavia; the Sumedang-Ukur revolt that followed was put down by 1636, and Sumedang became a Mataram regency before passing to the Dutch East India Company with Pakubuwana I's concessions. In 1808 and 1809 Daendels drove the Great Post Road through a limestone cliff west of the town; thousands of laborers died in the cutting and the regent Pangeran Kornel rode out to confront the governor-general over it. Sundanese legend adds that he drove his keris into the rock, which has been called Cadas Pangeran, the Prince's Rock.
zh:
双木丹·拉朗是帕拉扬甘东部坦波马斯山区的巽他小邦，从帕匡·帕查查兰和加卢通往井里汶海岸与爪哇海的山路经过这里。它早期的治所在西特邦吉朗，数百年间统治者都是巽他和加卢君主座下的地方领主。1444年的双木丹还是帕查查兰世界边缘的印度教内陆政权，三代人之后伊斯兰教才进入它的宫廷。

伊斯兰教随桑特里亲王而来，他1530年至1578年在位，使双木丹与井里汶结盟。1578年，他的儿子昂卡维查亚得到帕查查兰旧将查亚·佩尔科萨在王国倾覆之际带出的王冠和王权信物，经四十四名帕拉扬甘领主拥立，加冕为帕布·格乌桑·乌伦；1579年万丹的莫拉纳·优素福灭掉帕查查兰后，双木丹以巽他王统的继承者自居，《双木丹编年史》称其疆土北起爪哇海、南抵印度洋。格乌桑·乌伦1585年与井里汶反目，但其继任者朗加·根波尔一世夹在万丹、井里汶和马打兰之间，于1620年归附阿贡苏丹。他率马打兰军队参加马都拉战役，又为1628年至1629年围攻巴达维亚输送军粮；随后爆发的双木丹—乌库尔叛乱到1636年被镇压，双木丹成为马打兰摄政区，帕库布沃诺一世作出让步后转入荷兰东印度公司之手。1808年至1809年，丹德尔斯修筑大邮路，公路从镇西的石灰岩绝壁间劈开，数千役夫死在工地上，摄政库苏马迪纳塔九世（人称科内尔亲王）当面质问这位总督；巽他传说称他把克里斯短剑插进岩壁，那处石崖后来得名「查达斯·庞格尔」，意为「亲王岩」。

en:
Pekalongan lies on the flat north Javanese shore, behind mangroves and wet-rice fields. Chinese traders used the anchorage early. The Song account Lingwai Daida, completed in 1178, calls the port Pukalong, a month's fair-wind voyage from Guangzhou. It describes Javanese with short hair and colourful woven cloth, coconut wine, red and white sugar, copper coinage, pepper, cloves, sandalwood, eaglewood and white cardamom. The seventh-century Sojomerto inscription found nearby links this coast with the older kingdom of Kalingga. In 1444 Pekalongan was still a Majapahit port in name, but Chinese, Arab and Malay Muslim merchants already handled much of its shipping, and the rising Muslim port of Demak lay farther east along the coast.

In the century after Majapahit's collapse, Pekalongan followed Demak and then Pajang. Treaties and marriage alliances brought it to Mataram in the early seventeenth century. Although the Mataram court lay inland, rice, sugar and port dues made Pekalongan one of its richest appanages by the end of the century. Amangkurat I's closure of coastal ports disrupted the Muslim merchant networks that carried that wealth. The Chinese-Javanese rising of 1741–1743 swept across the north coast, and in 1743 Pakubuwana II ceded the Pasisir to the VOC. Pekalongan then passed under Company rule. In 1753 the Dutch built a fort in the town to watch the harbour and the loading of rice and sugar.
zh:
北加浪岸位于爪哇海北岸，港岸后方是红树林和连片水田。中国商人很早便来此停泊。1178年成书的《岭外代答》称这里为莆加龙，说从广州顺风航行一月可达；书中记当地人剪短发、以花布裹身，用椰子酿酒，铸造铜钱，出产红白蔗糖、胡椒、丁香、檀香、沉香和白豆蔻。邻近出土的7世纪索佐梅尔托石碑，又把这片海岸与诃陵古国联系起来。1444年，北加浪岸名义上仍是满者伯夷的港口，但华人和阿拉伯、马来穆斯林商人已掌握大量航运，海岸以东的淡目也正在兴起。

满者伯夷崩溃后的一个世纪里，北加浪岸先后从属于淡目和巴章。17世纪初，条约与联姻把它纳入马打兰。马打兰王都虽在内陆，到17世纪末，稻米、蔗糖和港口税已使北加浪岸成为它最富庶的封邑之一。阿莽古拉特一世关闭沿海港口，打断了输送这些财富的穆斯林商人网络。1741至1743年华人与爪哇人起事席卷北海岸，1743年帕库布沃诺二世把北海岸割让给荷兰东印度公司，北加浪岸随之归入公司治下。1753年，荷兰人在城中筑堡，监视港口以及稻米、蔗糖装船。

en:
Kotagede lies on open ground east of the Gajah Wong river, south-east of Yogyakarta, between Mount Merapi and the sea, on the roads that link the towns of the Mataram heartland. In 1444 it was Mentaok, a tract of hunting forest and rice villages in the fading inland domains of Majapahit, and later it passed to the kingdom of Pajang. In the 1570s the ruler of Pajang granted the forest to his courtier Ki Ageng Pemanahan for putting down a rebellion; Pemanahan and his son Danang Sutawijaya cleared it and settled, naming the place Mataram.

After Pemanahan's death Sutawijaya took the title Panembahan Senopati and made the settlement his base. Javanese tradition, in the Babad Mangkubumi, tells how he meditated on a stone in a river until a giant fish carried him to the court of Ratu Kidul, the queen who rules the spirits of the southern ocean; she pledged him her support and became the consort of his line. In 1586 he took Pajang itself, and the walled town became the first capital of the Mataram Sultanate, called Kotagede, the 'Great City': its walls ran along the Gajah Wong, whose water was diverted to fill the moats on the other three sides, and the royal mosque and cemetery went up beside the palace. Senopati died in 1601 and was entombed here. His successor Mas Jolang kept building at the court until, tradition says, a stag killed him while he hunted in his own enclosed forest; Sultan Agung, reigning from 1613, moved the capital south to Karta and then Plered. When Trunajaya's rebels sacked Plered in 1677 the court moved on to Kartasura and later Surakarta, leaving Kotagede as a pilgrimage town around Senopati's mausoleum, its ancestral ground held indivisible and guarded by both the Surakarta and Yogyakarta courts. The treaty of Giyanti in 1755 gave it to the new Sultanate of Yogyakarta, whose kraton nearby was stormed and looted by Gillespie's British troops in June 1812.
zh:
哥打格德位于日惹东南、加约旺河以东的开阔地带，在默拉皮火山与海洋之间，地当马打兰腹地各镇往来的通道。1444年时这里还叫门陶克，是满者伯夷日渐衰微的内陆疆土上一片猎场与稻米村落，后来又归属巴章王国。16世纪70年代，巴章君主把这片林地封给平定叛乱有功的廷臣基·阿贡·帕马纳汉；帕马纳汉与儿子达南·苏达威查雅拓土定居，将此地命名为马打兰。

帕马纳汉死后，苏达威查雅上帕南巴汉·塞纳帕蒂尊号，以此为基业。爪哇编年史《芒库布米》（Babad Mangkubumi）记载，塞纳帕蒂曾在河心一块石头上苦修，一条巨鱼驮他入海，觐见统御南海诸灵的女王拉杜·基杜尔；女王许以助力，并做了他王朝世代君王的配偶。1586年，他攻下巴章本土，这座设防城邑成为马打兰苏丹国的第一个首都，得名哥打格德，意为「大城」：城墙沿加约旺河而筑，河水被引入其余三面的壕沟，王宫旁建起了王室清真寺与陵寝。塞纳帕蒂1601年去世，安葬于此。继位的玛斯·佐朗继续营建宫室，据说在自己的围苑中猎鹿时被鹿撞死；1613年即位的苏丹阿贡则把首都南迁卡尔塔，再迁普莱雷德。1677年杜鲁诺佐约的起义者洗劫普莱雷德后，王廷再迁卡尔塔苏拉、后迁梭罗，哥打格德便成为围绕塞纳帕蒂陵寝的朝圣地，这片祖地被认为不可分割，由梭罗与日惹两朝共同守护。1755年《吉安蒂条约》将它划归新立的日惹苏丹国；1812年6月，吉莱斯皮率领的英军攻破并劫掠了近旁的日惹王宫。

en:
Kediri, the old Daha, lies in the upper valley of the Brantas, the river that carries the rice of inland East Java down to the sea. Airlangga founded Dahanapura in 1042, and as the capital of Panjalu it headed a kingdom that held the eastern interior until Ken Arok overthrew it in 1222. Its best-remembered king is Jayabaya of the mid-twelfth century, when Kediri's power was at its height; Javanese tradition holds him an incarnation of Vishnu and the archetype of the Ratu Adil, the just king who returns in an age of madness to put the world right, and in old age he abdicated to meditate at Menang. This was the age of the poet Mpu Sedah, whose Kakawin Bharatayuddha retells the great Bharata war in Javanese verse. Under Majapahit, Daha stayed a royal appanage held by the king's kin, and in 1444 it was a wealthy Hindu-Javanese river town of merchants, fishermen and temple estates while the empire around it slipped into factional wars.

In 1478 the prince of Daha, Girindrawardhana, rose against Trowulan and made Kediri the seat of the last Majapahit kings, until Sultan Trenggana of Demak stormed the city in 1527 and its last ruler fled to Blambangan. Demak, Pajang and Mataram held it in turn after that. In 1677 the Madurese rebel Trunajaya, fresh from sacking Mataram's capital, made Kediri his court and piled his plunder there; on 25 November 1678 a VOC army under Anthonio Hurdt, marching with Amangkurat II's troops, stormed the town, and in 1680 the king killed Trunajaya with his own hands. When Cakraningrat IV of Madura defied the Company from East Java in the 1740s, his defeat left Kediri, with the rest of the Oosthoek, under Dutch rule.
zh:
谏义里古称达哈，地处布兰塔斯河上游河谷，这条河把东爪哇内陆的稻米运往大海。1042年，埃尔朗加建达哈纳普拉城；作为潘贾卢的都城，它所统领的王国曾掌握东爪哇内陆，直到1222年被肯·阿罗克推翻。谏义里最有名的国王是12世纪中叶的查亚巴亚，当时国势正值全盛；爪哇传统认为他是毗湿奴的化身、公正之王拉杜·阿迪尔的原型，这位公正之王将在疯狂之世重回人间、拨乱反正，他晚年退位，到默南村苦修。诗人穆普·塞达写下《婆罗多战争》正是在这一时代，把婆罗多大战搬入爪哇诗章。满者伯夷时代，达哈一直是王族领有的亲王封邑；1444年时，它是一座富庶的印度教爪哇河城，商人、渔户与寺院庄园辐辏其间，而周围的帝国正陷入党争内战。

1478年，达哈王公吉林德拉瓦尔达纳起兵反对特罗武兰，使谏义里成为满者伯夷末代君主的朝廷所在地；1527年淡目的特林卡纳苏丹攻破此城，末代统治者逃往布兰邦岸，此后淡目、巴章、马打蓝相继领有其地。1677年，马都拉起义者杜鲁诺佐约洗劫马打蓝首都之后，以谏义里为王廷，将劫得的财货囤积于此；1678年11月25日，安东尼奥·赫尔特麾下的荷兰东印度公司军队会同阿莽古拉特二世的部队攻破城池，1680年国王亲手杀死了杜鲁诺佐约。1740年代，马都拉的查克拉宁格拉特四世据东爪哇与公司对抗，他败亡之后，谏义里便与整个东角一起落入荷兰统治。

en:
Madura is a long, narrow island set across the Madura Strait from Surabaya, guarding the sea approaches to northeastern Java. Its plains are drier than Java's, and the Madurese lived by farming, fishing and trade with the ports on the far side of the strait. Javanese kingdoms drew the island into their politics early: the Nagarakretagama of 1365 already names Madurese lords within the Majapahit order. In 1444 Madura still belonged to the Majapahit world, but the declining empire could not shield it from the Muslim sultanates rising on Java's north coast.

The island's princely line began in 1624, when Sultan Agung conquered Madura and installed Raden Prasena, titled Cakraningrat I, to govern the west from Sampang and Bangkalan. Half a century later a Madurese prince nearly overturned Mataram. Trunajaya of Arosbaya in Bangkalan led Madurese and Makassarese rebels across the strait in 1674, overran Java's north coast and in 1677 sacked Mataram's court at Plered; Amangkurat I died during the flight. His son called in the Dutch East India Company, whose troops drove Trunajaya out of Surabaya, stormed his capital at Kediri in 1678 and seized him the next year, and Amangkurat II put him to death in 1680.

The Cakraningrats then sided with the Dutch in the Javanese wars of succession. Cakraningrat II backed Puger, who as Pakubuwana I granted the Company East Madura by treaty in 1705. Cakraningrat IV helped retake Kartasura in 1742, only for Pakubuwana II to cede the whole island to the Company in 1743. He rose in revolt, was hunted down at Banjarmasin and exiled to the Cape of Good Hope, where he died. The Dutch then ruled through the island's four regencies and drew heavily on Madurese levies, who served in Company wars across the archipelago.
zh:
马都拉是一座狭长岛屿，与苏腊巴亚隔着马都拉海峡相望，扼守通往爪哇东北的海路。岛上平原比爪哇干燥，马都拉人以农耕、捕鱼为生，并同海峡对岸的港口通商。爪哇诸王国很早就把这座岛拉进自己的政治圈，1365年的《爪哇史颂》已提到身处满者伯夷秩序中的马都拉领主。1444年，马都拉仍属于满者伯夷世界，但日趋衰落的帝国已挡不住爪哇北岸兴起的穆斯林苏丹国。

岛上的王公世系始于1624年：阿贡苏丹征服马都拉后，封罗登·普拉塞纳为查克拉宁格拉特一世，以三邦和邦卡兰为中心治理西马都拉。半个世纪后，一位马都拉王子险些掀翻马打兰。出身邦卡兰阿罗斯巴亚（Arosbaya）的杜鲁诺佐约率马都拉人和望加锡人于1674年渡过海峡，席卷爪哇北岸，1677年洗劫马打兰在普莱雷德的宫廷，阿莽古拉特一世死于逃亡途中。新君阿莽古拉特二世向荷兰东印度公司求援，公司军队把杜鲁诺佐约逐出苏腊巴亚，1678年攻陷他设在谏义里的都城，次年将他擒获；1680年，阿莽古拉特二世亲手将他处死。

此后查克拉宁格拉特家族在爪哇继承战争中站在荷兰一方。查克拉宁格拉特二世支持普格尔，后者成为帕库布沃诺一世后，在1705年依约把东马都拉交给荷兰东印度公司。查克拉宁格拉特四世1742年协助公司夺回卡尔塔苏拉，帕库布沃诺二世却在1743年把全岛主权割让给公司。他随即起兵，在马辰被追捕擒获，流放好望角并死在那里。荷兰人随后通过岛上的四个摄政进行统治，并大量征募马都拉士兵，派往群岛各地为公司作战。

en:
Lombok lies across the narrow Lombok Strait east of Bali, with Sumbawa beyond the Alas Strait on its other side, and the cone of Mount Rinjani dominates its northern half. In 1257 Samalas, a volcano in the Rinjani massif, collapsed in one of the largest eruptions of the last several thousand years. Pyroclastic flows buried much of Lombok, destroyed Pamatan, the capital of the island's kingdom, and crossed the sea to Sumbawa; ash fell as far as Java, 340 kilometres away. The palm-leaf Babad Lombok describes the disaster, and the collapsed peak became the caldera lake of Segara Anak; Bali and Lombok may have stood depopulated for generations afterwards. The Nagarakretagama later counted the island among Majapahit's conquests as Lombok Mirah, but Majapahit's rule ran shallow, and by 1444 Lombok was divided among many small, quarrelling Sasak principalities whose people still kept their old animist rites.

The Balinese kingdom of Gelgel first conquered Lombok early in the sixteenth century and settled its western side. Islam, carried there by traders, spread widely only around 1600 through the preaching of Sunan Prapen of Gresik, son of Sunan Giri, and the new faith mingled with the old cults in the Wetu Telu way. Early in the seventeenth century Balinese princes seized the west while Makassarese invaders from Sumbawa took the east. The Dutch East India Company made its first treaty on the island in 1674 with the Sasak princess who then ruled part of it. In 1740 the Balinese kingdom of Karangasem destroyed the old Sasak kingdom of Selaparang, and by 1750 all Lombok was in Balinese hands, soon split between four rival Balinese kingdoms. In the east the lords held garrisoned forts and the Sasak village head became little more than a tax collector, and that was how the Sasak majority still lived in 1821.
zh:
龙目位于巴厘岛以东，与巴厘只隔一道狭窄的龙目海峡，东面再隔阿拉斯海峡与松巴哇相望，林贾尼火山的锥体雄踞岛的北半部。1257年，林贾尼群峰中的萨马拉斯火山崩塌，是几千年来最大规模的火山喷发之一。火山碎屑流掩埋了龙目大部，摧毁了岛上王国的都城帕马坦，还越过海峡扑上松巴哇；火山灰一直飘到三百四十公里外的爪哇。棕榈叶文献《龙目纪事》（Babad Lombok）记下了这场灾难，崩塌的峰顶后来形成塞加拉阿纳克湖；巴厘和龙目可能因此荒疏了好几代人。后来的《爪哇史颂》把此岛算作满者伯夷的征服地，称龙目米拉（Lombok Mirah），但满者伯夷的统治始终浮于表面，到1444年，龙目已分裂为众多互相争战的萨萨克小邦，百姓仍守着旧有的泛灵祭祀。

16世纪初，巴厘的格尔格尔王国首次征服龙目，并在西部定居。伊斯兰教早已随商人上岛，但直到1600年前后，才因苏南·吉里之子、爪哇锦石的苏南·普拉彭传教而广为传播，新信仰与旧俗融合为韦图特鲁（Wetu Telu）之道。17世纪初，巴厘诸王公夺取龙目西部，来自松巴哇的望加锡人则侵入东部。1674年，荷兰东印度公司与当时统治岛上一部分的萨萨克女亲王订立第一份契约。1740年，巴厘的卡朗阿森王国攻灭萨萨克古国塞拉帕朗，到1750年整个龙目都落入巴厘人手中，不久又分裂为四个互相敌对的巴厘王国。在岛的东部，巴厘王公据守设防要塞，萨萨克人的村长沦为替他们收税的人；1821年，占人口多数的萨萨克人仍过着这样的日子。

en:
Gangneung lies on Korea's eastern coast beneath the Taebaek Mountains, the chief town of the Yeongdong region, where cold and warm currents meet offshore and the fishing is rich. The country once belonged to the Ye people and was called Haseulla; Silla took it in 639 and made it a secondary capital, and Goryeo guarded its north-eastern frontier from the town it called Myeongju. In 1423 King Sejong's reorganization named the surrounding province Gangwon, from Gangneung and Wonju. In 1444 Gangneung is a small Confucian prefectural town, ranked a grand protectorate over the neighbouring hyeon, whose shoreline markets live by fishing.

Late in the fifteenth century the scholar's house Ojukheon was built here; it was the home of the painter and calligrapher Shin Saimdang and the birthplace, in 1536, of her son Yi I, the Confucian thinker known as Yulgok. Gangneung also produced the poet Heo Nanseolheon, whose collected verse was printed in Ming China after her death in 1589 and later in Japan, and her younger brother Heo Gyun, who raised a righteous army during the 1592 invasion, rose to high office in Seoul, and wrote the early Korean novel Hong Gildong jeon before he was executed in 1618. By Lake Gyeongpo stood the pavilion Gyeongpodae, counted among the eight scenic views of the Gwandong country. Every fifth lunar month the town held its dano festival, honouring the mountain god with sacrifices, shaman rites and folk plays.
zh:
江陵位于太白山脉东麓的朝鲜东海岸，是岭东地方的中心；外海寒暖流交错，鱼群繁盛。这里原为濊人居地，名为河瑟罗，639年新罗攻取后设为小京，高丽又以溟州为号，在此经略东北边防。1423年朝鲜世宗调整区划，取江陵与原州首字，命名江原道。1444年的江陵是一座儒教朝鲜的小型府城，以大都护府统辖附近属县，海岸市镇多以渔业为生。

15世纪末建成的乌竹轩，是画家、书法家申师任堂的故居，她的儿子、号栗谷的儒学家李珥也于1536年出生于此。江陵还养育了女诗人许兰雪轩，她1589年去世后，诗集经弟弟许筠刊行于明朝，后来又传到日本；许筠在壬辰倭乱中举起义兵，仕至高位，所作《洪吉童传》是朝鲜早期小说，1618年被处斩。镜浦湖畔的镜浦台，是关东八景之一。每逢农历五月，江陵举行端午祭，祭祀山神，巫祭与民间戏乐同时上演。

en:
East Timor is the mountainous eastern half of Timor, the sandalwood island at the southern end of the Moluccan trade routes. Its southern shore is wet and forested; its northern coast opens on the sheltered roadsteads of the Banda Sea. Tetum, Kemak and Galoli peoples lived in the fifty or so small kingdoms the Portuguese later called Belos, and their lords acknowledged the ruler of Wehale in the island's centre as their ritual overlord. Coastal rajas sold white sandalwood, beeswax and honey to junks from Java, Malacca and China. In 1444 no European ship had yet entered these waters, and the hill kingdoms kept their ancestor cults and their feuds to themselves.

Sandalwood brought the Portuguese. The first landing was near Pante Macassar in 1515, and Dominican friars built their post at Lifau in 1556, running a trade that did much to keep Macau prosperous. Lisbon's grip was weak, and for a century and a half the real masters were the Topasses, mestiço traders led by the da Costa and Hornay families, who held off both the Dutch at Kupang and the governors sent from Goa. A governor only reached Lifau in 1702, António Coelho Guerreiro, and his authority scarcely ran beyond the settlement. Fifteen kingdoms rose against him in the 1720s; a Portuguese army stormed their hill stronghold at Cailaco in 1726 after a six-week siege, yet the interior was never pacified. The Dutch pressed from Kupang, and a fort they backed at Maubara pulled the western kingdoms into the rivalry. In 1766 the Topasses killed Governor Dionísio Galvão at Lifau, and three years later his successor abandoned the place and founded Dili in the kingdom of Motael, the first solid European footing in the east. Dili shipped sandalwood to Macau, but the hill rajas let the groves die and the trade withered; coffee was tried from 1815 with little success. In 1821 the colony still amounted to little more than Dili, its priests, and a string of rajas loyal in name only.
zh:
东帝汶是帝汶岛多山的东半部，这座檀香木之岛处在摩鹿加商路的南端。南岸湿润多林，北岸掩着班达海的几处避风锚地。德顿、克马克、加洛利等族群生活在后来被葡萄牙人统称为贝卢的约五十个小王国里，各国首领奉岛中部韦哈莱之主为礼仪上的共主。沿海拉惹把白檀、蜂蜡和蜂蜜卖给来自爪哇、马六甲和中国的商船。1444年时，还没有欧洲船进入这片水域，山地诸邦守着祖先祭祀，也守着彼此的世仇。

引来葡萄牙人的正是檀香木：1515年首批葡萄牙人在潘特马卡萨附近登陆，1556年多明我会修士在利福设立据点，他们经营的檀香贸易是澳门富庶的重要财源。里斯本的控制力薄弱，此后一个半世纪里真正的主人是托帕塞人；这些混血商人以达科斯塔和奥尔奈两大家族为首，既抗拒盘踞古邦的荷兰人，也不买果阿派来的总督的账。直到1702年，安东尼奥·科埃略·格雷罗才作为首任总督抵达利福，其权势几乎出不了这座据点。1720年代，十五个王国起兵反抗，葡萄牙军队围攻六周，于1726年攻破他们的山地要塞凯拉科，内陆却始终未被驯服。荷兰人从古邦步步进逼，在其支持下修建的毛巴拉堡把西部诸王国也卷进两强之争。1766年，托帕塞人在利福杀死总督迪奥尼西奥·加尔旺；三年后，继任者放弃利福，在莫塔埃尔王国境内兴建帝力，这是欧洲人在岛东第一个稳固的立足点。帝力向澳门输出檀香木，山地拉惹却任檀林荒弃，贸易日渐凋敝；1815年起又试种咖啡，收效甚微。1821年时，这块殖民地仍不过是帝力一城、几名教士和一串名义效忠的拉惹。

en:
Yamdena is the largest island of the Tanimbar group, about sixty-five islands set between the Banda and Arafura seas where Austronesian and Melanesian peoples meet. Forested hills run along its eastern shore; the western coast is low and reef-fringed, and wild water buffalo roam the inland woods. Some forty villages lived by gardens, fishing and inter-island barter, and their craftsmen did fine woodcarving and goldwork while nearby Selaru wove ikat cloth. At Sangliat Dol a stone stairway climbs from the beach to a boat-shaped stone platform, raised for the canoes that carried the ancestors to the island. In 1444 no chief above the villages was obeyed here, and the spice fleets sailing between Malacca and the Moluccas passed these waters by.

Portuguese pilots sighted and possibly landed on the islands between 1522 and 1526, and Portuguese charts marked Tanimbar from the 1560s; Petrus Plancius put the group on his Insulae Moluccae map of 1594. A Dutch ship first called in 1629, and in 1639 the VOC claimed Tanimbar by right of discovery, then did nothing with it: no fort was built, no garrison posted, no treaty enforced. Through 1821 the villages of Yamdena kept their own councils, their feuds and their ancestor stones, visited now and then by a passing trader.
zh:
延德纳是塔宁巴尔群岛的第一大岛；这群约六十五个岛屿夹在班达海与阿拉弗拉海之间，南岛人与美拉尼西亚人在此相接。岛东是林木覆盖的丘陵，西岸低平、珊瑚礁环绕，野水牛在内陆林间出没。沿岸约四十个村落以园圃、渔捞和岛际易物为生，工匠擅木雕与金工，邻近的塞拉鲁岛出产扎染花布。在桑利亚特多尔，一条石阶从海滩通向一座船形石坛，为运载祖先登岛的独木舟而建。1444年时，村落之上没有更高的首领，往来马六甲与摩鹿加的香料船队也径直驶过塔宁巴尔的海面。

1522至1526年间，葡萄牙领航员望见并可能登上过这组岛屿，1560年代起的葡萄牙海图已标出塔宁巴尔，普兰修斯1594年的《摩鹿加群岛图》也将其绘入。1629年荷兰船只首次到访，1639年荷兰东印度公司凭发现权宣布领有群岛，之后便再无下文：不筑要塞，不派驻军，也没有真正执行的条约。直至1821年，延德纳各村依旧自行议事、自相攻伐、自守祖先的石坛，只有过路商人偶尔停靠。

en:
Tondo occupied the north bank of the Pasig River delta, with Maynila facing it across the water. The two bayan divided the China trade between them: Fujian junks unloaded silk, porcelain and iron at the river mouth, and Tondo's merchants carried the goods from island to island, bringing back honey, wax and gold piloncitos. Its barangays were led by datus under a paramount lakan, and the Laguna Copperplate of 900, the oldest Philippine document, already mentions Tundun among its places. Trade with Brunei and Majapahit gave the ruling families Malay and Indian titles. In 1444 the junks still came each year, and the lakan of Tondo stood first among the chiefs around Manila Bay.

Martín de Goiti sailed into the bay in 1570 and burned Maynila after a parley broke down, while Lakandula of Tondo held back. When Miguel López de Legazpi returned in 1571, Lakandula was the first chief to meet him; a Kapampangan fleet from Macabebe chose to fight instead, and on 3 June Legazpi's ships destroyed it in Bangkusay Channel and killed its chief Tarik Sulayman, the last open resistance on the bay. Tondo's datus became tribute collectors under a Spanish governor, and in 1587 a group of them plotted to throw the Spaniards out. The leaders were Magat Salamat, a son of Lakandula, and his cousin Agustín de Legazpi, grandson of the conquistador and son-in-law of Sultan Bolkiah of Brunei. A chief from Calamianes, Antonio Surabao, betrayed the plot, and the leaders were put to death in 1588. Tondo became a mission town governed from Manila, its shore still crowded with Chinese junks and traders. During the Seven Years War the British seized Manila in 1762 and held the bay until 1764.
zh:
汤都地处巴石河三角洲北岸，与南岸的马尼拉隔河相望。两座巴彦分据对华贸易：福建帆船在河口卸下丝绸、瓷器和铁器，汤都商人再把货运往一座座岛屿，换回蜂蜜、蜂蜡和皮隆西托金币。它的巴朗盖由达图统领，共尊一位拉干；900年的拉古纳铜版铭文是菲律宾现存最古的文献，其中已提到「汤敦」之名。与文莱、满者伯夷的贸易给统治家族带来马来和印度式的称号。1444年，中国商船仍年年前来，汤都的拉干在马尼拉湾诸首领中位居首座。

1570年，马丁·德·戈伊蒂驶入马尼拉湾，谈判破裂后焚毁马尼拉，汤都的拉坎杜拉则按兵未动。1571年米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮再至，拉坎杜拉是第一个出迎的首领；马卡贝贝的邦板牙舰队却选择开战，6月3日，莱加斯皮的舰队在班库赛海峡将其歼灭，击毙首领塔里克·苏莱曼，这是马尼拉湾最后一次公开抵抗。汤都的达图们沦为西班牙总督治下的包税人，1587年，其中数人密谋驱逐西班牙人。主谋是拉坎杜拉之子马加特·萨拉马特和他的表亲阿古斯丁·德·莱加斯皮，后者是征服者莱加斯皮之孙，也是文莱苏丹博尔基亚的女婿。卡拉棉群岛首领安东尼奥·苏拉豪出卖了密谋，首领们于1588年被处死。汤都此后成为受马尼拉管辖的传教城镇，岸边仍挤满中国帆船和商人。七年战争期间，英军于1762年夺取马尼拉，占据马尼拉湾直到1764年。

en:
Pangasinan curves along the eastern shore of Lingayen Gulf, and its coastal villages lived from the salt pans that gave the land its name, 'place of salt'. Up the Agno River delta lay Caboloan, 'place of bolo bamboo', whose chief town Binalatongan was said to hold more than two thousand houses, the largest settlement in the region. Ming annals called the country Fengjiashilan, and embassies from its rulers reached the Yongle Emperor in 1406 and 1408; Chinese and Japanese merchants sailed in with silk and porcelain and sailed out with gold, slaves, deerskins and civet, so that the Spaniards later called the roadstead the 'Port of Japan'. In 1444 Binalatongan still governed itself under its own ari, or king, and its people were animists whom neither Islam nor Christianity had reached.

Juan de Salcedo sailed into the gulf and landed at the Agno's mouth in 1572, after which the encomienda of Pangasinan was formed. Two years later the Chinese pirate Limahong, twice beaten back from Manila with a fleet of nearly seventy ships and four hundred Japanese soldiers in his crews, sailed north and seized the Agno delta to found a kingdom of his own; Salcedo landed behind him in March 1575 and besieged his fort for seven months, until Limahong slipped away with the last of his men and was never heard of again. Dominican friars made Binalatongan their first mission town in the Philippines, and in 1611 the colonial government merged the coastal salt villages with the inland settlements into the province of Pangasinan. In December 1660 Andres Malong, a chief of Binalatongan, drove out the Spanish and was proclaimed Ari na Pangasinan, King of Pangasinan; his kingdom fell before the spring. When word came that the British had taken Manila in 1762, Juan de la Cruz Palaris raised the country against Spain and held it until he was captured in 1765.
zh:
邦阿西楠位于林加延湾东岸，沿海村落靠盐田为生，地名本意就是「盐之地」。阿格诺河三角洲上游是「竹子之地」卡布洛安，首镇比纳拉图干（Binalatongan，今圣卡洛斯市）据说有两千多户人家，是整个邦阿西楠地区最大的聚落。明代史籍称此地为冯嘉施兰，其统治者的使者于1406年和1408年两度到永乐朝廷朝贡；中国和日本商人载来丝绸、瓷器，换走黄金、奴隶、鹿皮和灵猫香，西班牙人后来因此把这个锚地称作「日本港」。1444年，比纳拉图干仍由本地的阿里（ari，即王）统治，居民信奉泛灵信仰，伊斯兰教和基督教都还没有传来。

1572年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多驶入林加延湾，在阿格诺河口登陆，邦阿西楠随后被划为西班牙人的监护征赋地。两年后，中国海盗林凤两度攻打马尼拉受挫，带着近七十艘船、部众中还有四百名日本士兵北上，占领阿格诺河口打算自立王国；萨尔塞多1575年3月在他后方登陆，围困他的寨堡七个月，最后林凤率残部逃脱，此后再无音讯。多明我会修士把比纳拉图干建成他们在菲律宾的第一个传教城镇；1611年，殖民当局把沿海盐村与内陆聚落合并为邦阿西楠省。1660年12月，比纳拉图干首领安德烈斯·马隆驱逐西班牙人，被拥戴为「邦阿西楠之王」，他的王国没撑过第二年春天。1762年英军攻占马尼拉的消息传来，胡安·德拉克鲁斯·帕拉里斯举兵抗西，一直坚持到1765年被俘。

en:
The Bicol peninsula, called Ibalon by its people, reaches from southeastern Luzon into the Philippine and Sibuyan seas. Its barangays followed datus rather than a king or sultan, and the settlement on the Naga River handled gold from Paracale and rice from the Yraya lowlands; Chinese junks brought iron armour and firearms to exchange for them. Streams from Mount Isarog watered rice fields and abaca plots. In 1444 Bicol's datus still kept animist rites, while their villages lived from the trade passing along the river and coast.

Juan de Salcedo's soldiers crossed Bicol in 1573, and Pedro de Chavez secured the Naga settlement after fighting on the river banks. The Spanish town there became Nueva Caceres, and Franciscan friars built its churches and made the see one of the oldest diocesan centres in the Philippines. Bicol's hardwoods also fed royal shipyards, above all Pasacao, whose carpenters built vessels for the Manila trade; abaca remained the peninsula's main export. Dutch raiders burned Cagsawa's Franciscan church in 1636. When the British took Manila in 1762, the Camarines rose and Spanish troops needed two years to defeat them. The Mayon Volcano erupted on 1 February 1814, burying Cagsawa and about 2,000 people. Survivors moved to Daraga, and the church belfry rose above the ash.
zh:
比科尔半岛被当地人称作伊巴隆，从吕宋东南部伸入菲律宾海与锡布延海。岛上居民以巴朗圭为单位，首领是达图，没有更高的国王或苏丹。那牙河畔的聚落转运帕拉卡莱的黄金和伊拉亚低地的稻米，中国帆船则运来铁甲、火器交换。伊萨罗格山的溪流灌溉稻田和蕉麻地。1444年，比科尔的达图们仍奉行泛灵仪式，各村依靠河海往来贸易为生。

1573年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多的军队进入比科尔，佩德罗·德·查韦斯经过河畔战斗后控制那牙聚落。西班牙人在那里建立的城镇成为新卡塞雷斯，方济各会修士修建教堂，使这里成为菲律宾最早的教区中心之一。比科尔的硬木供养王家船厂，尤其是帕萨考，船匠在那里为马尼拉贸易建造船只；蕉麻长期是半岛的主要出口物产。1636年，荷兰袭掠者焚毁卡格萨瓦的方济各会教堂。1762年英军占领马尼拉后，甘马仁人起兵，西班牙军队用了两年才将其击败。1814年2月1日，马荣火山喷发，掩埋卡格萨瓦和约两千人。幸存者迁往达拉加，教堂钟楼露出火山灰。

en:
Panay is the broad triangular island at the western end of the Visayas, with the Panay River and shorter streams running from the central highlands to the Sibuyan Sea. The northeast coast, where the old settlement of Bamban became the Spanish town of Panay, had wide rice plains and easy landing places. Visayan datus ruled its coastal barangays before Spanish contact. Yuan Chinese records knew a Visayan trading polity in these islands as Oton, called Yachen, and islanders bartered rice, gold and sea produce for Chinese porcelain, metal gongs and bells. A later written tradition, the Maragtas, remembered the chiefs as the confederacy of Madja-as, though historians treat the story of the ten datus as legend. In 1444 Panay was an animist island of rival chiefs and productive river plains.

The Spaniards reached Panay town in 1566 and made it their second settlement after Cebu. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi moved his whole camp there in 1569 because the island could feed his men and offered more shelter from Portuguese pressure on Cebu; the expedition that conquered Luzon sailed from Panay on 8 May 1570. Juan de la Isla built a fortress at the town later that year. For two centuries Panay shipped rice and meat to Manila, while the shipyards at Arevalo built galleys for the colonial government. Panay town remained a provincial capital and in the 18th century produced suerte cloth for export, before Capiz took its place as the seat of provincial administration in 1716.
zh:
班乃岛是米沙鄢西端的三角形大岛，班乃河和较短的河川从中部高地流向锡布延海。东北海岸的班班旧址后来成为西班牙人的班乃镇，这一带有开阔的稻米平原和便于登陆的海岸。西班牙人到来前，沿海的巴朗圭由米沙鄢达图统治。元代中国记载把群岛上的米沙鄢贸易政体称为奥通，记作哑陈；岛民以米粮、黄金和海产交换中国瓷器、金属钟锣。后世文献《马拉格塔斯》把诸首领称作马迪亚斯联盟，但学界将十达图的故事视为传说。1444年的班乃仍是诸首领并立的泛灵信仰岛屿，河畔平原出产丰足。

1566年，西班牙人抵达班乃镇，把这里建为宿务之后的第二个定居点。1569年，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮把整个营地迁来，因为岛上能够供应军粮，也比受葡萄牙威胁的宿务更安全；1570年5月8日，征服吕宋的远征军正是从班乃出发。同年晚些时候，胡安·德·拉·伊斯拉在镇上筑起要塞。此后两百年间，班乃向马尼拉运送米粮和肉类，阿雷瓦洛船场则为殖民政府建造桨帆战船。班乃镇长期担任省城，18世纪还出产供出口的苏埃尔特布，到1716年卡皮斯才取代它成为行政中心。

en:
Tagloc was the shore of the great gulf then called the Gulf of Tagloc, now Davao Gulf, where the Tagloc River enters the sea beneath Mount Apo, the highest peak in the Philippines. To the Bagobo, Matigsalug and other Lumad peoples of its foothills the mountain was Apo Sandawa, Grandfather Sandawa, the ancestor spirit for whom their shamans performed rites on the slopes. The Lumad farmed the interior valleys, while Islamized Kagan and Maguindanaon settlers clustered at the river mouth and Maguindanaon and Tausug traders sailed the gulf, carrying out wax, honey and forest produce and bringing in salt, metal goods and Chinese porcelain. In 1444 no European had yet entered these waters, and Lumad datus ruled their own valleys, though their trade already bound them to the Muslim sultanates to the west.

When Ruy López de Villalobos surveyed Mindanao's eastern coast for Spain in 1543, he gave the Gulf of Tagloc a wide berth: Moro war fleets crowded its waters, and his pilots judged a landing suicidal. No Spaniard pressed a claim there for almost three centuries. Around 1800 Datu Mama Bago, a Maguindanaon chief granted these shores for his campaigns against the Spaniards, moved east from his homeland, drew the Bagobo and neighbouring peoples to his side, and spent the following years conquering the gulf shore by shore until he ruled all of Tagloc.
zh:
塔格洛克是塔格洛克湾（即今达沃湾）的沿岸之地，塔格洛克河（今达沃河）在菲律宾最高峰阿波火山下注入湾中。在山麓的巴戈博人、马蒂格萨卢格人等卢马德族群看来，这座山是「阿波·桑达瓦」，意为「桑达瓦老翁」，是护佑他们的祖灵，由巫师在山坡上主持祭祀。卢马德人在山谷中耕作，归信伊斯兰教的卡甘人和马京达瑙人聚居河口，马京达瑙与陶苏格商人往来湾上，运出蜂蜡、蜂蜜和山林物产，运入盐、金属器和中国瓷器。1444年时还没有欧洲人进入这片水域，卢马德的达图们仍统治着各自的山谷，只是贸易早已把他们同西边的穆斯林苏丹国连在一起。

1543年，为西班牙勘测棉兰老东海岸的鲁伊·洛佩斯·德比利亚洛沃斯有意绕开塔格洛克湾：湾中密布摩洛人的战舰，引水员认定登陆无异于送死。此后近三百年，再没有西班牙人来此主张主权。1800年前后，马京达瑙的达图·马马·巴戈因对西班牙人作战有功而受封这片海岸，他从故土东迁，争取到巴戈博等邻近族群归附，随后数年逐岸攻战，最终统治了整个塔格洛克。

en:
Butuan lies at the mouth of the Agusan River on Mindanao's north-eastern coast, where gold washed out of the river gravel made its smiths famous, and its shipwrights built the balangay, the great ocean-going outriggers whose planked remains have been dug up at Libertad. A mission reached Song China as early as 1001, and the Chinese annals called the rajahnate Puduan. One rajah asked the Song for standing equal with Champa and was refused; a later envoy startled Emperor Zhenzong by arriving on the eve of a great state sacrifice with a memorial engraved on a gold tablet, white camphor, Moluccan cloves and a slave. Gold jewellery, cloves and camphor sailed from here to Champa, Majapahit, Brunei and the Bengali coast. A Chinese annal records Brunei conquering Butuan in 1304, before the port won its freedom back. In 1444 it was a rajah's town of fishermen and gold-panners, who kept the old animist rites beneath the Indian-style titles of their court.

On 31 March 1521 Rajah Siagu of Butuan was among the chiefs who met Ferdinand Magellan at Mazaua and stood at the first Catholic mass said in the Philippines. Real submission came only with the Jesuits: Father Valerio de Ledesma landed with a mission in 1596, sent to make a Spanish foothold in Mindanao against the Moro slave-raiders out of the southern seas, and the first church opened on 8 September 1597; Augustinian Recollects later carried the work on. Reinforcements from Mexico strengthened the Caraga garrison in 1635 and again in the 1670s, yet the sea-raiding never quite stopped. A Spanish census in 1818 counted 3,703 native families in Butuan.
zh:
武端位于棉兰老岛东北岸的阿古桑河口，河沙里淘出的黄金让当地金匠闻名远近，船匠则在这里建造大型远洋舷外支架船「巴朗盖」，利伯塔德已出土这种船的木板残骸。早在1001年，武端便有使团抵达北宋，中国史书称这个拉惹国为「蒲端」。一位拉惹曾请求宋朝给予与占城同等的地位，遭到回绝；后来的使者在一场隆重国祭的前夜谒见真宗，奉上刻在金板上的国书、白龙脑、摩鹿加丁香和一名奴隶，令满朝惊异。黄金首饰、丁香和龙脑从这里销往占城、满者伯夷、渤泥和孟加拉海岸。中国方志记载渤泥于1304年征服武端，港口后来才重获自由。1444年的武端是拉惹治下的渔村兼淘金之地，宫廷用着印度式的名号，百姓仍守着古老的泛灵仪式。

1521年3月31日，武端拉惹西亚古在马绍阿（今利马萨瓦）迎接麦哲伦，参加了菲律宾土地上的第一场天主教弥撒。西班牙人真正立足，要等到耶稣会前来：1596年巴莱里奥·德·莱德斯马神父率传教团登陆，要在棉兰老建立据点，抵御南方海域来的摩洛掠奴者；第一座教堂于1597年9月8日开放，传教事业后来由重整奥斯定会接续。墨西哥派来的援军于1635年和1670年代两度加强卡拉加驻军，海上的掳掠仍未止息。1818年的西班牙人口普查在武端录得三千七百零三户土著家庭。

en:
Lehad Datu is the coast facing Darvel Bay, where the Dent Peninsula runs out into the Sulawesi Sea. Its best-known harvest came from the limestone hills behind the shore, where for centuries the Ida'an held hereditary rights to take edible birds' nests from the caves at Madai and sold them into the trade with China. A Jawi account of 1408 records an Ida'an ruler, Raja Abdullah, accepting Islam on this coast, and Ming porcelain dug up around Lahad Datu puts its traders in touch with China within the same century. In 1444 these villages and anchorages formed the eastern edge of Brunei, where Muslim chiefs met Ida'an, Bajau and river people to exchange cave nests, spices, sea produce and forest goods.

The Brunei civil war of 1665 to 1673 pulled the coast away from Brunei. Sultan Muhyiddin called in Sulu to win the war, and afterward Sulu claimed authority over eastern Sabah, whether or not a formal cession had ever been signed. Sulu datus then took leading places around the bay, and in Bajau-Sinama speech Lahad Datu means the place of such nobles. Through the eighteenth century the bay belonged to the Sulu maritime world, its cave nests and coastal produce freighted to the Sulu Archipelago and China, while sheltered island anchorages also drew slave-raiders and sea rovers. In 1821 the caves and landing places were still in the hands of Ida'an families, Bajau settlers and Sulu chiefs.
zh:
拿笃在达卫湾畔，登特半岛在此伸入苏拉威西海。这里最出名的物产来自岸后的石灰岩山丘：伊达安人世世代代独占马代溶洞的燕窝采集权，把燕窝销往中国。一份1408年的爪夷文记载记下了伊达安首领拉惹·阿卜杜拉在这一带海岸皈依伊斯兰教；拿笃出土的明代瓷器也说明，同一世纪里本地商人已同中国通商。1444年，这些村落和锚地处在文莱势力的东缘，穆斯林酋长同伊达安人、巴瑶人和河畔居民交换洞燕、香料、海产与山林货物。

1665年至1673年的文莱内战把这片海岸从文莱手中拉开。苏丹穆希丁借苏禄之助打赢战争，战后苏禄便主张对沙巴东部的主权，至于双方是否签过正式割让文书，并无定论。苏禄贵族随后在湾畔据有要位，在巴瑶-西纳马语里，拿笃的意思便是「贵族之地」。整个18世纪，达卫湾属于苏禄的海上世界，洞燕窝和沿岸物产转运苏禄群岛与中国，岛屿间隐蔽的锚地也招来掳奴者和海上武装。1821年时，把持溶洞和泊地的仍是伊达安家族、巴瑶移民和苏禄酋长。

en:
Sibu occupies the low, swampy ground where the Rajang, Borneo's greatest river, meets the Igan some sixty kilometres from the sea. Its people were the Melanau, who call themselves A-Likou, 'river people', among Sarawak's earliest inhabitants; they fished, grew sago and rice, built boats and lived in tall stilt houses along the banks. Chinese records of the Song and Yuan eras knew this coast as Malano, and the Majapahit court poem of 1365 named Malano among the foremost lands of Borneo. As Brunei became a Muslim sultanate in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, Bruneian nobles drew the Melanau river mouths under their rule and took in camphor, rattan, beeswax and sago through local chiefs. In 1444 Sibu was only a Melanau fishing and sago village in the Rajang delta, held by Sultan Sulaiman of Brunei.

Brunei's sea power peaked under Sultan Bolkiah, who reigned from 1485, and when Magellan's expedition called in July 1521 Pigafetta found the Brunei capital girdled with forts mounting heavy guns. The Spanish came as enemies in April 1578, when a fleet sent from Manila seized Kota Batu, but cholera broke out among the occupiers and they withdrew after 72 days; no Spanish force reached the Rajang, and the delta kept its Bruneian allegiance. A Dutch report of 1609 already counted the Melanau among the peoples rebelling against the sultan and looking to Johor. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries tribal wars ran through the Rajang basin: Iban migrants moving out of the Kapuas country since the mid-sixteenth century pressed up the rivers, at times joining Malay raiders to strike the Kayan and plunder Chinese and island trading craft, while Iranun slave-raiders haunted the coast. In 1821 Sibu remained a small Melanau and Malay riverside settlement under Brunei's loose and weakening rule.
zh:
诗巫所在是婆罗洲第一大河拉让江与伊干江交汇处的低洼泽国，距南海约六十公里。这里的居民是马兰诺人，他们自称「河上之民」（A-Likou），是砂拉越最古老的族群之一，以打鱼、种西谷和稻子、造船为生，在河岸搭起高高的桩上屋。宋元时期的中国载籍已把这一带海岸称作马兰诺，满者伯夷1365年的宫廷史诗《爪哇史颂》也把马兰诺列为婆罗洲最重要的地方之一。14至15世纪文莱成为伊斯兰苏丹国，文莱贵族把各马兰诺河口纳入治下，经本地头人收取樟脑、藤、蜂蜡和西谷。1444年的诗巫只是拉让江三角洲上一个打鱼、制西谷的马兰诺村落，归文莱苏丹苏莱曼管辖。

文莱的海上国势在1485年即位的苏丹博尔基亚治下达到极盛：1521年7月麦哲伦船队到访时，皮加费塔见到都城外围堡垒环列、配有重炮。1578年4月，西班牙舰队从马尼拉袭来，攻占文莱都城哥打巴都，可是霍乱在占领军中蔓延，72天后便撤走；没有一支西班牙队伍进入拉让江，三角洲仍奉文莱为主。1609年的一份荷兰报告已把马兰诺诸部列为反叛苏丹、转而指望柔佛的势力。17至18世纪，拉让江流域部落战事不断：16世纪中叶起从卡普阿斯河地区陆续迁来的伊班人沿江扩张，有时与马来劫掠者联手攻打加央人、洗劫华人与南洋群岛商船，掳人为奴的伊拉农海盗船也在海岸出没。1821年的诗巫，仍是文莱松散而日渐衰微的统治下一个马兰诺人与马来人的河畔小聚落。

en:
The rivers here divide a forested coastal plain between the Rajang delta and the Saribas flats. The Sarikei and Nyelong join the Rajang before it reaches the South China Sea, while farther west the Kalaka and Saribas open their own mouths. Malay and Melanau villages held the landing places, and Dayak longhouses upstream sent rice, beeswax, damar resin and jungle produce to Brunei traders. The Javanese poem Nagarakretagama of 1365 names Kalka and Sawaku among Bornean lands acknowledging Majapahit, but by 1444 Sultan Sulaiman of Brunei claimed the coast. His nobles worked through local datu, and the men they sent seldom went far above the river mouths.

The Spanish attack on Brunei's capital in 1578 put no garrisons on these rivers, though it weakened the court that confirmed local chiefs. A Dutch report in 1609 listed Calca, Saribas and Melano among coasts in revolt and seeking Johor's protection. In the early or mid-1600s a small Malay kingdom took shape at Debak, where the Saribas and Rimbas meet; the Silsilah Raja-Raja Brunei remembered it, and after its ruling line ended local datu carried on its offices. Brunei's dynastic war of the 1660s, which lasted until 1673, kept the sultan's ships and nobles occupied nearer the capital. Iban migrants from Kapuas Hulu began entering the Saribas in the 1750s, and within five generations their longhouses and war-boats lined the Layar and neighbouring rivers. On the Rajang side, the Sigalang community occupied the land between the Sarikei and Nyelong by the 1700s; its headman Sigalang was remembered as fair, and his people farmed, hunted and built longhouses. In 1821 Brunei still received professions of allegiance from the river mouths, while the interior followed its own chiefs.
zh:
这里的河流把拉让江三角洲与沙里拔平原之间的林沼海岸分成若干流域。泗里街河和尼隆河先汇入拉让江再注入南海，更西的加拉卡河与沙里拔河则各自入海。马来和马兰诺村落掌握河口泊地，上游达雅人的长屋向文莱商人提供稻米、蜂蜡、达玛脂和山货。1365年的爪哇史诗《爪哇史颂》曾把加尔卡和沙瓦库列入向满者伯夷朝贡的婆罗洲地名；到1444年，文莱苏丹苏莱曼已宣称领有这片海岸。他的贵族通过本地拿督交易，派来的人很少深入河口以上。

1578年西班牙进攻文莱都城，没有在这些河流留下驻军，却使册封本地首领的朝廷更加衰弱。1609年的荷兰报告把加尔卡、沙里拔和马兰诺列为起兵反抗、并寻求柔佛保护的海岸。17世纪前期或中叶，沙里拔河与林巴斯河汇合处的德巴克形成一个马来小王国，《文莱诸王谱系》记下了它；其王世断绝后，地方拿督继续执掌各类职事。1660年代的文莱王位战争一直打到1673年，苏丹的战船和贵族多被牵制在都城附近。1750年代，来自卡普阿斯河上游的伊班人进入沙里拔；五代人之内，他们的长屋和战船已分布到拉耶河及邻近河流。拉让江一侧，西加朗社群在18世纪已住在泗里街河与尼隆河之间，相传头人西加朗处事公正，族人善于农耕、狩猎和建造长屋。1821年，文莱仍能从河口得到臣属表示，内陆则听从各族自己的首领。

en:
Katapang, now spelled Ketapang, occupies the Pawan River delta on Borneo's south-western coast, the old Tanah Kayong. Its rulers were the Malay rajas of Tanjungpura, the oldest royal line in western Borneo, who kept their court first at Negeri Baru and later at Sukadana. Local tradition derives the line from a crown prince of Majapahit exiled by his brothers to Matan, who married a Dayak princess; their son Raja Baparung founded the Sukadana line about 1400. In 1444 his Hindu successors ruled Malay-speaking coastal villagers and upriver Dayak alike. Sukadana's port sent the gold and diamonds washed from the rivers inland, with timber and other forest goods, across the Java Sea to Java; European writers later spelled it Succadano and called it the diamond town of Borneo's west coast.

Islam reached the court with the preacher Syekh Husein in 1550, under Panembahan Giri Kesuma, whose widow Ratu Mas Jintan afterwards ruled as Queen of Sukadana. Dutch ships came in 1604 and warred on her until she was set aside, and English factors kept a trading post at Sukadana from 1611 to 1617. An expedition from Mataram under Adipati Kendal attacked Matan in 1622, sent by Sultan Agung. The dynasty outlasted these wars but not its own family quarrels: Pangeran Agung drove out his brother Sultan Muhammad Zainuddin, who won his throne back with Bugis fighters from Johor led by Daeng Menambun; Menambun married the sultan's daughter Ratu Kesumba and later made himself ruler of Mempawah. The Matan-Tanjungpura sultans kept their court on this coast through the eighteenth century.
zh:
吉打邦（今名Ketapang，华文亦译作道房）位于婆罗洲西南海岸的帕万河三角洲，是旧称「卡荣之地」。这里的统治者是丹戎布拉的马来拉惹，婆罗洲西部最古老的王统，王廷先在內格里巴鲁，后来迁到苏卡达纳。当地传说，其先祖是被兄弟放逐到马坦的一位满者伯夷太子，他娶了达雅公主为妻，儿子拉惹·巴帕龙约在1400年开创苏卡达纳王统。1444年，其后裔信奉印度教的朝廷同时统治沿海说马来语的村民和上游的达雅人。苏卡达纳港把内河淘洗出的黄金、钻石，连同木材和山货运过爪哇海卖到爪哇；后来的欧洲作者把它拼作Succadano，称它是婆罗洲西岸的钻石城。

1550年，传教士谢赫·侯赛因把伊斯兰教传入帕南巴汉·吉里·克苏马的宫廷；吉里·克苏马死后，王后拉图·马斯·金丹以苏卡达纳女王的身份执政。1604年荷兰船到来，与女王交战，直到她被废黜；1611至1617年，英国商人也在苏卡达纳设有商馆。1622年，苏丹阿贡治下的马打兰派阿迪帕蒂·肯德尔率军攻打马坦。王朝熬过了外敌的战争，却没躲过自家的内争：邦格兰·阿贡赶走其兄苏丹穆罕默德·扎因丁，后者从柔佛请来达英·曼本率领的布吉斯战士复位，曼本娶苏丹之女拉图·克松巴为妻，后来成为曼帕瓦的统治者。整个18世纪，马坦-丹戎布拉的苏丹们仍在这段海岸维持王廷。

en:
The Barito is Borneo's second-longest river, running 1,090 kilometres from the Muller Mountains south through forested lowlands to the sea at Banjarmasin; its upper course is called the Dusun, and at Marabahan it meets the Negara river coming down from old Daha. In 1444 the basin belonged to no king. Ngaju and Ma'anyan Dayaks lived in riverside longhouses, farmed swiddens and kept their ancestral kaharingan rites, their longboats the only road between village and coast. The Ma'anyan tongue spoken on this river is the closest living relative of Malagasy, the language of Madagascar; between the third and tenth centuries Malay and Javanese trading fleets carried Ma'anyan and related Barito peoples across the Indian Ocean to the island.

When Raden Samudra fled Negara Daha in the 1520s he took refuge in the Barito region before founding his new town of Banjarmasin downstream. From the later sixteenth century Banjar traders pushed upstream, and the sultanate numbered the interior Dayak lands, the Dayak Besar, among its tributaries. Banjarese became the lingua franca of the river markets, but upriver headmen kept their own customs and the sultan's writ never ran far beyond the landing stages.
zh:
巴里托河是婆罗洲第二长河，自穆勒山脉南流1090公里，穿过森林低地，在马辰入海；上游称杜顺河，到马拉巴汉与从尼加拉·达哈故地流来的尼加拉河相会。1444年的流域不属于任何国王。雅朱人和马安亚人等达雅克族群住在河畔长屋，耕种山田，守着祖传的卡哈林干仪式，长长的独木舟是村寨与海岸之间唯一的通路。这条河上的马安亚语，是马达加斯加岛马拉加斯语现存最近的亲属；3至10世纪，马来人和爪哇人的商船队曾把马安亚人及相近的巴里托族群带过印度洋，送到那座岛上。

1520年代，拉登·沙穆德拉逃出尼加拉·达哈后先在巴里托地区避难，后来才在下游的马辰建城。16世纪末起，班贾尔商人沿河上行，苏丹国把内陆的大达雅克（Dayak Besar）诸地列入朝贡之列。班查语成为河畔集市的通用语，但上游头人依旧各行其俗，苏丹的号令从来到不了码头之外多远。

en:
Sampit lies on the lower Mentaya, called the Sampit River near its mouth, which winds through the swampy south Borneo coast to the Ot Danum Dayak country upstream. Javanese ships knew the place early: the Nagarakretagama of 1365 counts it among the Borneo lands tributary to Majapahit, and the later Hikayat Banjar names it again. In 1444 the river mouth was a row of Dayak villages under their own chiefs, where traders from the Javanese ports bartered for the produce brought down from the interior; no sultan at Banjarmasin yet ruled this coast.

The chiefs submitted to the new Sultanate of Banjar early in the sixteenth century, after Raden Samudra took the throne as Sultan Surianshah in 1526. About 1615 Sultan Mustain Billah, in whose reign Banjar grew rich on pepper, first gave Kotawaringin, the coast west of the Barito, to the chief Dipati Ngganding and then enfeoffed it to his own son Pangeran Dipati Anta-Kasuma, who had married Ngganding's daughter; the principality seated at Kotawaringin Lama also ruled the Mentaya settlements. The Dutch East India Company made its first contract with Kotawaringin in 1637, and through the next two centuries the river mouth shared in Banjar's pepper trade while the upriver Dayak kept their own laws and customs.
zh:
桑皮特在门塔亚河下游，河口一段称桑皮特河；河水穿过婆罗洲南岸沼泽，通向上游奥特达努姆达雅人的地方。爪哇船只很早就知道这里：1365年的《爪哇史颂》把它列为向满者伯夷称臣的婆罗洲之地，后来的《班贾尔史记》也提到其名。1444年，河口是一串各有酋长的达雅村落，爪哇各港来的商人在此换取顺河而下的内陆物产；马辰的苏丹还没有统治这段海岸。

16世纪初，这里的酋长臣服于新生的班贾尔苏丹国，即拉登·沙穆德拉1526年称苏里安沙苏丹后建立的国家。约1615年，在任内班贾尔靠胡椒致富的苏丹慕斯泰因·比拉，先把巴里托河以西的哥打瓦林因交给酋长迪帕蒂·恩甘丁，随后改封给娶了恩甘丁女儿的亲子邦格兰·迪帕蒂·安塔卡苏马；这个定都旧哥打瓦林因的公国也管辖门塔亚河畔的聚落。1637年荷兰东印度公司首次与哥打瓦林因立约，此后两个世纪里，河口随班贾尔一同经营胡椒贸易，上游的达雅人则按自己的法律和习俗生活。

en:
Tarakan is a low, swampy island in the Sulawesi Sea, just beyond the river mouths of northeastern Borneo. No community lived there permanently. It was a fishermen's stop, where boats out of the Kayan, Sesayap and Malinau estuaries beached to cook their catch and trade it. The older Berau polity, whose rulers dated to the fourteenth century, claimed a long stretch of this coast together with the Tidung and Bulungan countries. In 1444 the island sat on the maritime fringe of a still Hindu Berau realm, valued for its fish, fresh water and shelter rather than for any court or town.

A new dynasty took the nearby coast in 1731, when Wira Amir converted to Islam and founded the Sultanate of Bulungan, at first as a Berau vassal. A Berau succession war in 1770 loosened that tie, and in 1789 Sulu raiders sacked Berau and Tarakan alike; Bulungan then broke away. Around 1810 what remained of Berau split into the two courts of Gunung Tabur and Sambaliung, and Raja Alam built his Sambaliung capital at Tanjung. By then Sulu vessels were sailing past Tarakan to trade directly with the Tidung communities up the rivers. In 1821 the island was still a fishing anchorage and a meeting ground for sea traders.
zh:
打拉根是苏拉威西海中的低洼沼泽岛，紧靠婆罗洲东北部的河口。岛上无人长期定居，只是渔民的停留地：卡扬河、塞萨亚普河和马利瑙河河口的船来此靠岸，炊煮渔获、转手交易。较古老的伯劳政权可追溯到14世纪，其沿海势力涵盖提东、布隆岸等地的一长段海岸。1444年，打拉根处在仍信印度教的伯劳政权海疆边缘，人们看重它的鱼类、淡水和避风处，而不是宫殿或城镇。

1731年邻近海岸换了新王朝：威拉·阿米尔改宗伊斯兰教，建立布隆岸苏丹国，起初向伯劳称臣。1770年伯劳继承战争使这层宗主权松动，1789年苏禄海上武装把伯劳和打拉根一同洗劫，布隆岸趁势脱离。1810年前后，残存的伯劳分成古农塔布尔和桑巴利翁两个王庭，拉贾·阿拉姆在丹绒建起桑巴利翁的都城。这时苏禄船只已绕过打拉根，直接同河上游的提东人贸易。1821年，打拉根仍是渔船锚地和海商的会合地。

en:
Sambaliung is a name from 1810, when the old kingdom of Berau split in two; the coast itself, between the Bulungan lands and Sangkulirang, had been Berau country for four centuries. Berau grew out of the banua, fishing and trading villages strung along the rivers behind the coast, which its first ruler united in the fourteenth century; local chronicles give his reign, as Aji Raden Suryanata Kesuma, from 1377 to 1426, with his court on the Lati River. The Nagarakretagama of 1365 does not number Berau among Majapahit's conquests. In 1444 his successors still ruled from those river villages, their people kept the ancestor cults, and coastal produce was already sold south to the Banjar lands.

In the sixteenth century Berau became a Banjar tributary, and in the next century the preacher Imam Sambuayan brought Islam to its court. Sultan Muhammad Hasanuddin threw off Banjar overlordship late in the 1600s. When Sultan Tamjidullah I of Banjar tried to win back his dependencies, his treaty of 20 October 1756 with the Dutch East India Company, signed under Governor-General Jacob Mossel, brought Berau, Kutai and Pasir back to obedience. The throne had long passed by turns between two royal branches, and after Sultan Zainal Abidin II died in 1810 their rivalry divided the country between Gunung Tabur and Sambaliung. The first Sambaliung sultan, Alimuddin, called Raja Alam and a grandson of Hasanuddin, built his seat at Tanjung Batu Putih on the coast.
zh:
「桑巴利翁」之名出自1810年——那年古老的贝劳王国一分为二；而它所辖的这段海岸，北接布隆岸、南至桑库利朗，做了四百年的贝劳之地。贝劳兴起于沿海各河上以渔贸为生、称为「巴努阿」的村落，第一代君主在14世纪把它们联合起来；据当地编年史，他王号阿吉·拉登·苏尔雅纳塔·克苏马，1377至1426年在位，王廷设在拉蒂河畔。1365年的《爪哇史颂》没有把贝劳列入满者伯夷的征服之地。1444年，他的继承者仍在这些河畔村落治国，百姓守着祖先崇拜，沿海物产已向南卖到班贾尔之地。

16世纪，贝劳沦为班贾尔的属国；下个世纪，传教士伊玛目·桑布安把伊斯兰教带进宫廷。17世纪末，苏丹穆罕默德·哈萨努丁摆脱了班贾尔的宗主权。班贾尔苏丹塔姆吉杜拉一世试图收复各属地时，于1756年10月20日与荷兰东印度公司签约（时在总督雅各布·莫塞尔任内），贝劳、古泰、帕塞尔被重新压服。贝劳的王位久在两支王族间交替传袭，1810年苏丹扎因·阿比丁二世死后，两支相争，把国土分成古农塔布尔与桑巴利翁。桑巴利翁第一代苏丹阿利姆丁，人称罗阇·阿拉姆，是哈萨努丁之孙，他在海边的丹戎巴都普蒂建立王都。

en:
Bulungan is the river country behind the northeast coast of Borneo, where the Kayan and Sekatak flow out of the Apo Kayan highlands toward the sea. In 1444 Kayan and other Dayak communities kept longhouse villages on the upper rivers, fishing, tending forest plots and floating hardwood and other jungle produce downstream. No local court yet stood on these streams: the shore itself belonged to Berau, the Hindu-ruled kingdom centred on the Lati River, and its outlying district of Nagri Marancang reached up the Bulungan rivers, linking the interior to the coast through Berau chiefs.

Kayan oral tradition tells how the Uma Apan Kayan moved down from the Apo Kayan in the 16th or 17th century, and how the Brunei nobleman Datuk Mencang could marry the princess Asung Luwan only by bringing her the head of the Kenyah raider Sumbang Lawing, who had killed her father; he proved his prowess by splitting a moving orange with a blade. The firmly dated history begins in 1731, when the ruler Wira Amir accepted Islam as Sultan Amiril Mukminin, founded the Sultanate of Bulungan and placed his capital at Salim Batu under Berau's overlordship. Berau's civil war after 1770 loosened that bond, and when Sulu forces sacked Berau and Tarakan in 1789 Bulungan broke away and passed into the Sulu sphere. Sultan Alimuddin moved the court to Tanjung Palas, and by the early 19th century Tausug vessels plied between its river mouths, Tarakan and the Sulu islands, while the Kayan communities upstream kept their own leaders.
zh:
布隆岸位于婆罗洲东北海岸后方的河川地带，卡扬河、塞卡塔克河从阿波卡扬高地流向大海。1444年，卡扬等达雅克社群在上游各河建有长屋村落，以捕鱼、经营林地和园地为生，把硬木和其他山林物产顺流放运。这些河上还没有本地王庭：海岸本身属于以拉蒂河为中心、印度教君主统治的伯劳王国，其边远辖区纳格里马兰让延伸到布隆岸诸河上游，内陆经由伯劳酋首与海岸相连。

卡扬人的口传讲述，乌马阿潘卡扬人于16或17世纪从阿波卡扬向下游迁徙；又说文莱贵族达图·门仓（Datuk Mencang）要娶公主阿松·卢万（Asung Luwan），必须先献上杀死她父亲的肯雅族酋长苏邦·拉温（Sumbang Lawing）的首级，他还挥刀劈开一只掷出的橘子，以此证明身手。有确切纪年的历史始于1731年：首领维拉·阿米尔皈依伊斯兰教，称苏丹阿米里尔·穆米宁，建立布隆岸苏丹国，定都萨利姆巴图，奉伯劳为宗主。1770年后伯劳内战削弱了这层关系；1789年苏禄军队洗劫伯劳和打拉根，布隆岸随之自立，转入苏禄势力范围。苏丹阿利穆丁把宫廷迁往丹戎帕拉斯；到19世纪初，陶苏格人的船往返于这里的河口、打拉根和苏禄群岛之间，而卡扬河上游社群仍由各自首领统辖。

en:
Samarinda fills the flat, island-braided lower course of the Mahakam, where the river nears its delta. Long before the name was used, six riverside villages had stood here since the 13th century: Pulau Atas, Karang Asam, Karang Mumus, Loa Bakung, Sambutan and Mangkupalas. Their people farmed the wet banks, fished the delta channels and carried their catch by boat to the court of Kutai Kartanegara, founded upstream at Kutai Lama in 1300. In 1444 the villages lay within that Hindu-ruled Mahakam polity, close enough to the river mouth to share in coastal commerce and in the raids that came up it from the sea.

Banjar settlers entered the Kutai lands in 1565, and the court turned Muslim in 1575. The town itself was built by refugees: after Gowa lost the Bungaya war of 1667, several thousand Bugis from Wajo under La Mohang Daeng Mangkona, the first Pua Ado, sailed to the Mahakam and were received by the sultan. Around 1668 they were granted the low ground by the Karang Mumus, to farm, fish, trade and help ward off pirates raiding down from the Philippines. The flood-level site was called Sama Rendah, 'equally low', which became Samarinda; the Bugis built their raft houses to one height, so that no household stood above its neighbours. In 1732 the growing town was made the kingdom's river port as the court moved upstream to Pemarangan-Jembayan, and its traffic held after the capital settled at Tenggarong in 1782.
zh:
三马林达地处马哈坎河下游低平、沙洲交错、临近三角洲的河段。「三马林达」之名出现以前，13世纪起这里已有普劳阿塔斯、卡朗阿萨姆、卡朗穆穆斯、洛阿巴孔、三布坦和芒库帕拉斯六个河畔村落。居民耕种湿软的河岸，在三角洲水道捕鱼，再乘船把渔获运往1300年建于古泰拉马的古泰卡塔内加拉宫廷。1444年，这些村落属于这个印度教君主统治的马哈坎政权；因靠近河口，它们既分享沿海贸易之利，也承受溯河而来的劫掠。

1565年，班查尔移民进入古泰地区，1575年宫廷改奉伊斯兰教。这座城镇本身由难民建起：1667年戈阿在布尼亚战争中战败后，拉·莫杭·达英·芒科纳（首位普阿·阿多）率数千瓦佐布吉斯人驶往马哈坎河，受到苏丹接纳。约1668年，他们获准在卡朗穆穆斯旁的低洼之地落脚，耕种、捕鱼、贸易，并协助抵御从菲律宾南下劫掠的海盗。这片与水面齐平的低地称「萨马伦达」，意为「同样低」，后来演变为三马林达；布吉斯人的筏屋也造得一样高，没有哪一户高出邻人。1732年，随着宫廷迁往上游的佩马兰根—占巴延，这座成长中的城镇被辟为王国的河港；1782年都城定都登加龙后，港中航运仍在继续。

en:
Gorontalo lies across the narrow waist of Sulawesi's northern arm, between the Sulawesi Sea and the deep Gulf of Tomini, a country of broad rice plains and gold-bearing hills. Its kingdom grew from Hulontalangi, a valley domain said to date from about 1300; in the fourteenth century Raja Ilahudu bound seventeen small chiefdoms (linula) into one realm, and the royal house kept kinship ties with the four neighbouring kingdoms of Limboto, Suwawa, Bolango and Atinggola through the pohala'a bond. Across the seas the Sultans of Ternate were drawing the whole coast into their tribute network, while Bugis and Malay traders threaded the two waters for gold, rice and coconut. In 1444 the court of Gorontalo still kept the old ancestral cults, though its fortunes were already bound to Ternate and the spice trade.

Islam came through marriage and commerce. In 1525 Raja Amai, who reigned from 1523 to 1550, wed a princess of Palase Gomonjolo, a house linked by blood to Ternate, accepted her faith and took the title sultan; under his son Matolodulakiki Islam became the religion of the kingdom, which grew into one of the chief centres of the faith in eastern Indonesia, known as the 'Porch of Medina'. The court moved downstream to Tuladenggi in 1615. The Dutch closed in soon after: Ternate ceded its Sulawesi fiefs to the VOC by a treaty of 11 May 1677, Governor Padtbrugge came to Kwandang the next year to receive Gorontalo and Limboto, and Fort Nassare rose in 1770 to guard the gold and rice trade. Sultans Eato and, in the next century, Botutihe kept their throne, but after the Company collapsed in 1799 the Dutch state inherited its treaties, and in 1821 the sultan at Biawu still reigned under ever closer Batavian oversight.
zh:
哥伦打洛横在苏拉威西北支半岛的蜂腰处，北濒苏拉威西海，南临深邃的托米尼湾，是一片平原广产稻米、山中蕴藏黄金的土地。这里的王国由约1300年的谷地小邦乌兰塔朗吉发展而来；14世纪，国王伊拉胡杜把十七个小酋长邦（利努拉）联合成一国，王室又通过波哈拉血缘之盟，与林博托、苏瓦瓦、博朗戈、阿廷戈拉四个邻邦王室互通声气。海那边的特尔纳特苏丹正把整片海岸纳入贡赋网络，布吉斯和马来商人穿行于两海之间，贩运黄金、稻米和椰产。1444年的哥伦打洛宫廷仍守着古老的祖灵崇拜，但它的命运已经系于特尔纳特和香料贸易。

伊斯兰教随联姻与贸易传入。1525年，1523至1550年在位的国王阿迈迎娶帕拉塞·戈蒙佐洛的公主，该家族与特尔纳特素有血缘之盟；阿迈皈依伊斯兰教，改称苏丹。其子马托洛杜拉基基在位时，伊斯兰成为王国国教，哥伦打洛也成长为印尼东部最重要的伊斯兰中心之一，得了「麦地那廊庑」的名号。1615年，王都迁往下游的图拉登吉。荷兰人随后步步紧逼：1677年5月11日，特尔纳特立约把在苏拉威西的属地割让给荷兰东印度公司，次年帕德特布鲁赫到宽当接收哥伦打洛和林博托；1770年纳萨雷堡筑起，看守黄金与稻米贸易。埃阿托和下一个世纪的博图图赫等苏丹保住了王位，但公司1799年垮台后，各项条约由荷兰国家接手；1821年，驻跸比亚武的苏丹仍在位上，巴达维亚的管束却日益收紧。

en:
Palu stands at the head of a narrow, almost landlocked bay, where the long Palu River valley opens a road deep into Sulawesi between the Makassar Strait coast and the highland interior. It is the country of the Kaili, whose riverside and hill villages lived by fishing, farming and the forest. Warrior headmen (Tomalanggai) ruled them in early days, before councils and an aristocracy of madika nobles took shape in the fifteenth century. The bay was already a place where traders put in: Makassar and Bugis praus called there for coconut oil and forest produce floated down from the interior, though the busiest anchorage remained Donggala, out at the bay's mouth. In 1444 the villages where Palu now stands were still small, pagan and unfortified, and no neighbouring power had yet proved strong enough to take them.

That power came from Makassar. In the mid-sixteenth century Karaeng Tunipalangga, who reigned from about 1546 to 1565, carried Gowa's arms along the whole west coast from Kaili to Tolitoli, and Portuguese ships were soon calling at the bay to trade. Gowa's grip loosened after its wars with the VOC ended in defeat in 1667 to 1669, and the Kaili shore broke back into a patchwork of small kingdoms, among them Sigi, Bangga, Banawa and Palu. In 1796 four riverside villages, Besusu, Tanggabanggo, Panggovia and Boyantongo, joined in the Patanggota council to found the kingdom of Palu, with its first royal seat at Pandapa. Its first magau, Pue Nggari, accepted Islam with his court from the Sumatran preacher Dato Karama. His daughter Labugulili ruled as the kingdom's first queen from 1805 to 1815, and Malasigi Bulupalo followed in 1815; in 1821 Palu was a young Muslim kingdom whose trade still passed chiefly through Donggala, untouched as yet by Dutch rule.
zh:
帕卢坐落在狭长而近乎封闭的海湾顶端，长长的帕卢河谷在此打开一条深入苏拉威西内陆的通道，把望加锡海峡沿岸与高地内陆连在一起。这里是凯利人的家园，河畔与山间村落以渔猎、农耕和山林物产为生，早期统辖各部的是尚武的首领托马朗盖，到15世纪，长老议事与名为马迪卡的贵族阶层才逐渐成形。海湾早就是商舶往来之地：望加锡和布吉斯人的帆船在此收购椰油，以及从内陆顺河而下的山货，不过最繁忙的锚地始终是湾口的东加拉。1444年，后来帕卢城所在的几处村落仍然狭小、信奉泛灵、不设城防，周围还没有哪个政权强大到能拿下它们。

这个强权来自望加锡。16世纪中叶，卡拉昂·图尼帕朗加（约1546至1565年在位）率戈瓦军队横扫整条西海岸，势力从凯利一直伸展到托利托利，不久葡萄牙商船也来湾内停泊贸易。1667至1669年戈瓦在与荷兰东印度公司的战争中战败，控制随之松动，凯利沿岸又回到锡吉、邦加、巴纳瓦、帕卢等小王国林立的局面。1796年，贝苏苏、唐加邦戈、潘戈维亚、博扬通戈四个滨河村落组成帕坦戈塔议事会，建立帕卢王国，第一个王都设在潘达帕。初代马高普·恩加里在苏门答腊传道者达托·卡拉马的劝说下率宫廷皈依伊斯兰教；其女拉布古利利在1805至1815年作为王国第一位女王执政，1815年马拉西吉·布卢帕洛继位。1821年的帕卢已是一个年轻的伊斯兰王国，贸易仍主要经由东加拉出入，荷兰人的统治尚未降临。

en:
Palopo lies on the Gulf of Bone at the foot of a steep, winding pass into the Toraja highlands. In 1444 it was a minor coastal settlement, and Luwu's palace centre stood nearby at Malangke, also called Amassangan. Bugis settlers had occupied the coast around 1300, and iron ore brought down through the Lemolang lands of Baebunta was smelted at Malangke into weapons and tools for the rice-growing south; by the mid-fourteenth century Luwu was the feared overlord of much of the peninsula. Its datu ruled a Bugis-led coalition of coastal traders and highland peoples, Pamona, Wotu and Lemolang among them, and the court still prayed to ancestral spirits.

Luwu's primacy faded as the southern agrarian kingdoms grew. Its earliest named ruler, Bataraguru, made peace with Bone in the mid-fifteenth century, and Dewaraja's attacks on Wajo and Sidenreng around 1495-1520 failed to reverse the decline. On 4 or 5 February 1605 the datu La Patiwareq became the first major South Sulawesi ruler to accept Islam, taking the name Sultan Muhammad Wali Mu'z'hir al-din; the white-coral Jami Mosque at Palopo, with its three-tiered roof laid out on the old Austronesian cosmos, is dated 1604. After a war between rival princes the court abandoned Malangke, a town that may have held 15,000 people in the sixteenth century, and around 1620 established itself at Palopo under Sultan Abdullah Muhiddin, close to the Seko-Rongkong valleys and their highland trade. The new town had a royal square and market at Lalebbata, and to the north at Lokkoe the rulers of Muslim Luwu were laid in pyramid-shaped stone mausolea.
zh:
帕洛波位于波尼湾畔，城后一条陡峭曲折的山道通向托拉查高地。1444年时这里还只是个普通滨海聚落，鲁乌的宫廷中心在附近的马朗凯（又称阿马桑甘）。约1300年布吉斯定居者进入这片海岸；铁矿石经莱莫朗人的巴埃本塔运到马朗凯，熔铸成武器和农具，卖给南方种稻的平原，到14世纪中叶，鲁乌已是半岛大部所畏惧的宗主。达图统治着一个以布吉斯为首的联盟，成员包括沿海商人与帕莫纳、沃图、莱莫朗等高地族群，宫廷仍祭祀祖灵。

随着南方农业诸国崛起，鲁乌的首强地位渐渐流失。可考的最早君主巴塔拉古鲁在15世纪中叶与波尼议和；1495年至1520年前后，德瓦拉查对瓦久和西登伦用兵，也没能扭转颓势。1605年2月4日或5日，达图拉·帕蒂瓦雷克成为南苏拉威西第一位接受伊斯兰教的主要统治者，改名苏丹穆罕默德·瓦利·穆扎希尔·丁；帕洛波白珊瑚石砌成的贾米清真寺建于1604年，三层屋顶沿袭古老的南岛宇宙观。在一场对立王子之间的战争之后，宫廷放弃了16世纪可能有一万五千人口的马朗凯，约1620年在苏丹阿卜杜拉·穆希丁治下定都帕洛波，以便经营塞科—龙孔谷地的高地贸易。新城在拉莱巴塔设有王宫广场和市场；城北的洛科有王室墓地，穆斯林鲁乌的历代君主葬在金字塔形的石椁中。

en:
Buton is a large island off southeast Sulawesi, and the Wolio harbor that grew into Baubau commands the strait between Sulawesi and the spice route running to Maluku. Tradition makes the polity a union of four districts, Gundu-gundu, Barangkatopa, Peropa and Baluwu, with neighboring chiefdoms, which elected a woman, Wa Kaa Kaa, as their first ruler around 1332; the district heads, the bonto, sat on the council that chose and checked later monarchs. The Majapahit court poem Nagarakretagama named Buton in 1365, and Gajah Mada's Palapa oath counts it among the islands claimed by Majapahit. Outsiders called the islanders tukang besi, blacksmiths, because iron tools were so common among them. In 1444 Buton was still an animist kingdom whose proas carried coastwise goods toward the Moluccas, its court balancing noble families and sea traders.

In 1541 the Patani scholars Sheikh Abdul Wahid bin Sharif Sulaiman al-Fathani and Imam Fathani converted the Wolio court, and Lakilaponto, also called Halu Oleo, took the throne as Sultan Murhum Kaimuddin Khalifatul Khamis. Through the sixteenth century Buton held the strait as a secondary ally of Ternate, policing regional trade and forwarding tribute from the spice traffic. Sultan La Sangaji began its fortress in 1591-1596, at first only a ring of heaped coral and limestone around his palace on the steep hill above Wolio; Sultan La Elangi turned it into a permanent wall 2,740 meters around, with twelve gates called lawa and sixteen gun platforms called baluara looking over the strait. In 1610 the sultanate adopted the Murtabat Tujuh, a written law code that fixed the offices and the legislative council of siolimbona, with the bonto keeping their check on the throne. Pressed by Gowa and Ternate, Buton accepted Dutch East India Company protection in the course of the seventeenth century. Sultan La Badaru still reigned at Wolio in 1821, having ruled since 1799.
zh:
布敦（又译布顿）是苏拉威西东南方的大岛，后来发展成巴务巴务的沃利奥港湾，扼守苏拉威西与摩鹿加香料航路之间的海峡。相传这个政权由贡杜—贡杜、巴朗加索帕、佩罗帕、巴卢武四个区联合邻近首领组成，约1332年选立女子瓦·卡卡为第一位统治者；各区首领邦托组成议事会，负责选立并约束后来的君主。1365年满者伯夷宫廷诗《爪哇史颂》提到布敦，加查·马达的帕拉帕誓言也把它列入满者伯夷宣示的岛屿。外人称岛民为「铁匠」（tukang besi），因为他们几乎人人使用铁器。1444年，布敦仍是泛灵王国，岛民的马来快船转运沿岸货物、加入通往摩鹿加的航路，宫廷在贵族家族与海商之间维持平衡。

1541年，来自北大年的谢赫·阿卜杜勒·瓦希德·本·谢里夫·苏莱曼·法塔尼与伊玛目·法塔尼使沃利奥宫廷改宗，拉基拉蓬托（又称哈卢·奥莱奥）即位为苏丹穆尔胡姆·凯穆丁·哈利法图尔·哈米斯。整个16世纪，布敦作为特尔纳特的次级盟友扼守海峡，维持区域贸易秩序，并经香料航路转输贡赋。1591年至1596年，苏丹拉·桑加吉开始修筑堡垒：起初只是在沃利奥上方陡峭山丘的王宫周围堆起一圈珊瑚和石灰岩，苏丹拉·埃兰吉时把它建成永久城墙，周长2740米，设12座名为拉瓦的城门和16座名为巴卢阿拉的炮台，俯瞰海峡。1610年，苏丹国颁行《穆尔塔巴特·图朱》法典，规定各项官职和西奥林博纳议事机构，各邦托对王权的约束也写入制度。在戈瓦与特尔纳特的压力下，布敦于17世纪接受荷兰东印度公司保护。1821年，自1799年在位的苏丹拉·巴达鲁仍在沃利奥统治。

en:
The Sula Islands are Taliabu, Mangole and Sulabesi ringed by scores of smaller islets, set where the Molucca, Seram and Banda seas meet, east of Sulawesi and southwest of Halmahera. Sula and Mangole clans lived by the sea and the forest, sailing out to trade damar resin, rattan and beeswax; on Sulabesi the four-soa confederacy of Soa Gareha ran local affairs by the harbor that became Sanana. In 1444 the islands kept their own councils. Sailors from Makassar, the Bugis lands and Java knew these waters, but the Sultans of Ternate had not yet reached them.

Sultan Bayanullah of Ternate brought the Sulas under his sultanate in 1511 as an outer maritime fief. He posted a Salahakan of the Tomaito clan and a Sangadji at Sanana to gather tribute of resin, rattan and beeswax. In 1652 the Dutch East India Company built the stone Fort De Verwachting on Sanana's shore, one of the oldest colonial forts in the western Moluccas, to close the straits to Bugis, Makassarese and English smugglers and guard its spice monopoly. The garrison stored the islands' produce and watched the sea lanes, fending off hongi raiders and bargaining with village elders who refused its levies. Sanana stayed a small outpost in Ternate's shadow and passed with the Company to the Dutch crown; in 1821 the stone fort of 1652 still mounted guard over the shore where three seas meet.
zh:
苏拉群岛由塔利阿布、曼戈莱、苏拉贝西三座大岛和环绕四周的众多小岛组成，位于马鲁古海、塞兰海与班达海相接之处，在苏拉威西以东、哈马黑拉西南。苏拉人和曼戈莱人诸部靠海与山林为生，驾船外出贸易达玛树脂、藤条和蜂蜡；苏拉贝西岛上，四个「索阿」结成的传统联盟「索阿·加雷哈」在后来成为萨纳纳的港湾旁处理公共事务。1444年的群岛仍由本地议事会自主治理，望加锡、布吉之地和爪哇的水手熟知这片海域，特尔纳特苏丹的权势却尚未延伸至此。

1511年，特尔纳特苏丹巴亚努拉把苏拉群岛收作苏丹国的海上外藩，派托迈托氏族的「萨腊坎」和驻萨纳纳的「桑阿吉」征收树脂、藤条和蜂蜡贡物。1652年，荷兰东印度公司在萨纳纳海岸建起石砌的德韦瓦赫廷要塞，意为「希望要塞」，是西摩鹿加最古老的殖民要塞之一，用以封锁海峡、阻挡布吉人、望加锡人和英国走私者，保卫香料专卖。驻军收储岛产、监视航道，既要抵御洪吉掠船，也要应付拒缴摊派的村社长老。萨纳纳始终是特尔纳特阴影下的小据点，后来随公司一同转归荷兰国家；1821年时，扼守这片海岸的仍是这座1652年的石堡。

en:
Fakfak is a harbour on the Onin coast, the western arm of the Bomberai Peninsula, with Seram across the Berau Strait. In 1444 its bays were held by Papuan Onin clans, shore and inland communities alike following ancestral cults. Their canoes met Moluccan praus and carried nutmeg with other sea and forest produce into the routes between Seram, Bacan and the clove sultanates. No European post stood on the coast, and a port's allegiance came down to loose ties between its local leaders and whichever rival Moluccan ruler could serve them.

The rivalry of the spice sultanates pulled the Onin coast into island wars. In 1521 Sultan al-Mansur of Tidore took the Spanish side against Ternate and Portugal; Spain abandoned the Moluccas in 1663, yet Tidore kept its claims over western Papua. Old manuscripts of the Onin peninsula date the arrival of Islam on this coast to 1606, carried along the chain of power from Bacan to Tidore. The old mosque at Patimburak in the Kokas district became the centre of the new faith, one of the earliest Islamic monuments in Papua; coastal leaders embraced it while inland clans kept their ancestral cults. Through the sixteenth to eighteenth centuries Fakfak remained a Papuan port under Tidore, and the Onin clans still held much of their power beside the mosques and the Moluccan shipping lanes.
zh:
法克法克是奥宁海岸上的港口，奥宁半岛是邦巴赖半岛向西伸出的臂膀，与斯兰岛隔贝劳海峡相望。1444年，沿岸各湾由巴布亚奥宁氏族分据，滨海和内陆社群都奉行祖灵崇拜。他们的独木舟同摩鹿加马来帆船交易，把肉豆蔻和其他海林物产带入斯兰、巴占与丁香诸苏丹国之间的商路。沿岸没有欧洲人的据点，一处港口向背与否，全看本地首领和摩鹿加争霸者之间时松时紧的盟属关系。

香料苏丹国的争霸把奥宁海岸拖入岛屿战争。1521年，蒂多雷苏丹曼苏尔联西班牙以抗特尔纳特和葡萄牙；1663年西班牙弃守摩鹿加，蒂多雷对西巴布亚的宗主权却保留下来。奥宁半岛的古手稿把伊斯兰教传入这一带的时间定在1606年，信仰随巴占到蒂多雷的权力链条而来。科卡斯区帕廷布拉克村的旧清真寺成了新信仰的中心，也是巴布亚最早的伊斯兰史迹之一；沿岸领袖归信，内陆氏族仍守祖灵崇拜。16至18世纪，法克法克始终是蒂多雷治下的巴布亚港口，在清真寺与摩鹿加航道之侧，奥宁氏族仍掌握着相当权力。

en:
Madang's shore follows a broad bay on New Guinea's north coast, with Karkar Island a day's paddle offshore and the smoking volcano of Manam farther out. In 1444 Bel-speaking Austronesian villages occupied the beaches. The Bilibil lived on a cramped islet that could not feed them, built deep-hulled seagoing canoes and fired clay pots. Their canoes carried those pots from Karkar to western Morobe and returned with sago, taro and timber. Behind the coast, fast rivers cut through the rainforested Rai Coast ranges, where Papuan-language villages kept gardens, fishing grounds and their own trade friendships and feuds.

European navigators learned the offshore route before they knew the bay. In August 1545 Iñigo Órtiz de Retez, sailing the carrack San Juan from Tidore toward New Spain, sighted Karkar and Long Island on the voyage that gave New Guinea its name. Willem Schouten and Jacob le Maire, Abel Tasman and William Dampier later saw or visited Karkar, but the volcanic island stood between their ships and the mainland anchorage. No European landing on this coast is known before 1821; Bilibil canoes still carried pots and food between the volcanoes, islands and Rai villages.
zh:
马当海岸位于新几内亚岛北海岸的一处宽阔海湾，乘独木舟划一天可到外海的卡尔卡尔岛，更远处是冒着烟的马纳姆火山岛。1444年，海滩上分布着说南岛语系贝尔语族的村落。比力比尔人住在一座狭小、产粮不足的岛上，建造深舷远洋独木舟并烧制陶罐。他们的独木舟把陶器从卡尔卡尔岛带到莫罗贝西部，回程载来西米、芋艿和木材。岸后，急流穿过雨林覆盖的莱伊岭山地，说巴布亚诸语的村落经营园圃和渔场，也各有贸易伙伴与世仇。

欧洲航海者先熟悉外海航路，却不了解内侧海湾。1545年8月，伊尼戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·雷特斯乘大帆船「圣胡安号」从蒂多雷前往新西班牙途中，望见卡尔卡尔岛和长岛；正是这次航行给新几内亚取了名字。后来威廉·斯豪滕、雅各布·勒梅尔、亚伯·塔斯曼和威廉·丹皮尔也曾望见或到访卡尔卡尔岛，但火山岛挡在船只与大陆停泊地之间。到1821年，这里仍没有欧洲人登陆的明确记录；比力比尔人的独木舟继续在火山、海岛和莱伊村落之间运送陶器与食物。

en:
At Lae the Markham River comes out of the Finisterre Range and breaks into mangrove channels at the head of Huon Gulf, the wide bight of the Solomon Sea bounded on the north by the Huon Peninsula. Beach ridges, swamps and lagoons line the shore, and behind them climb the folded, forested coast ranges, whose raised terraces hold some of the oldest traces of human life in Oceania: stone tools about 40,000 years old. In 1444 the shore was held by Austronesian villagers, the Ahi with Butibam among their villages above the river mouth, and the Labu on their coastal lagoons. They fished the gulf, worked gardens and paddled trading canoes along the coast and up the Markham, giving sea produce for taro, bananas and sago grown by the Papuan-speaking peoples of the valley. No chief stood above the villages; the gulf was the road that joined them.

European ships only crossed the edge of this world. In August 1545 the Spanish carrack San Juan, on the voyage that gave New Guinea its name, sighted Long Island out in the Vitiaz Strait but did not enter Huon Gulf. In 1793 Bruni d'Entrecasteaux's French squadron, searching for the vanished La Pérouse, kept well offshore and named the gulf and peninsula after his captain Jean-Michel Huon de Kermadec, without a landing. No foreign flag or factory followed, and in 1821 the canoes of the Ahi and the Labu still had these waters to themselves.
zh:
莱城一带位于休恩湾湾首：马卡姆河从菲尼斯特雷岭流出，在此散入红树林水道，注入休恩湾这片北面以休恩半岛为界的所罗门海大海湾。沿岸滩脊、沼泽与潟湖交错，后方是褶皱起伏、密林覆盖的海岸山岭，山岭抬升阶地上保存着大洋洲最古老的人类活动遗迹之一，约四万年前的石器。1444年时，岸边居住着说南岛语的村民：河口上方的阿希人（布提班村是其一）和守着海岸潟湖的拉布人。他们在湾中捕鱼、种植园圃，驾贸易独木舟往来沿岸、溯马卡姆河而上，用海产换谷地说巴布亚语居民出产的芋艿、香蕉和西米。村落之上没有共主，把各村连起来的路就是海湾。

欧洲船只只是从这片天地的边缘掠过。1545年8月，西班牙大帆船「圣胡安号」在那次为新几内亚命名的航行中望见维蒂亚兹海峡里的长岛，却没有驶入休恩湾。1793年，布吕尼·当特勒卡斯托的法国舰队搜寻失踪的拉佩鲁兹，从远海通过，以他的舰长让-米歇尔·于翁·德·凯尔马代克之名为海湾和半岛命名，未曾登陆。没有外来旗帜或商馆随之而来，到1821年，这片水域里往来的仍是阿希人和拉布人的独木舟。

en:
Kerema lies on the concave shore of the Gulf of Papua, where the Purari, the Vailala and other rivers off the central highlands spill into the sea through deltas of sago swamp and tidal forest. The people of this eastern stretch, Elema and Toaripi, speak Papuan languages and live in patrilineal clan villages with no chief above the clan. Their mark on the coast was the men's longhouse, raised on piles and hung with carved gope boards, masks and bullroarers painted in red ochre, lime and charcoal; in the Purari delta the longhouses fronted the river with carved facades eighty feet high. Boys were initiated in them, and rival villages set out from them on ritual headhunting raids. Sago and fish filled the larder, and each sailing season the Motu arrived from the east in lakatoi, two or three dugout hulls lashed together with a platform over them and a crab-claw sail, carrying thousands of clay cooking pots and leaving with Gulf sago and timber. In 1444 that hiri voyage, rough and dangerous, was the only road this coast had to the wider world.

In 1606 the Spanish ships of Luís Vaz de Torres, working their way along New Guinea's southern coast, charted the shore as far as the Gulf of Papua without a landing or a post. No outside power followed, and in 1821 the longhouses still stood untouched, the yearly arrival of the Motu canoes still the great event of the coast.
zh:
凯里马一带是巴布亚湾向内凹进的海岸，普鲁阿里河、瓦伊拉拉河等源自中央高地的河流穿过西米沼泽与潮汐林莽构成的三角洲入海。这一东段的居民是埃莱马人和托阿里皮人，说巴布亚语，按父系氏族聚居，没有凌驾氏族之上的首领。他们留在海岸上的标记是男子长屋：架在木桩上，屋内挂满戈佩祖灵板、面具和吼器，以红赭、石灰、炭黑绘彩；普鲁阿里三角洲的长屋以八十英尺高的雕立面朝向河面。少年在长屋里行入会礼，敌对村落的仪式性猎头也从这里出发。居民靠西米和鱼为生，每到航季，莫图人便乘拉卡托伊独木舟从东方而来，两三根挖空舟体捆连、上架平台、张着蟹螯帆，载来数以千计的陶锅，换走海湾的西米和木材。1444年时，这条风浪险恶的希里商航是这片海岸通往外部世界的唯一通路。

1606年，路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯率西班牙船队沿新几内亚南海岸摸索前行，把海岸测绘到巴布亚湾，但没有登陆，也未留下据点。没有外来势力随之而来，到1821年，长屋依旧未受触动，莫图独木舟一年一度的到来仍是沿岸一年中的大事。

en:
Daru is a low elliptical island, nowhere higher than 27 metres, set in the narrow waters between the mouth of New Guinea's Fly River and the reef-strewn Torres Strait. Seagrass shallows surround it, where dugong graze and turtles come to breed, and the islanders lived by harpooning both from sailing outrigger canoes and by fishing the island roads. They were traders as well as hunters, in a chain that ran two ways. To the north their canoes dealt with the Kiwai villages of the Fly delta; to the south they worked the strait's old exchange network, where trumpet shells, bailer shells and turtle-harpoon shafts bought Papuan canoe hulls, cassowary bone-tipped arrows and bamboo, and the line of trade ran on to the Aboriginal peoples of Cape York. In 1444 no outside power reached Daru, and clan custom and the tides ordered the island.

Its first European sighting came on 5 September 1606, from the Spanish expedition of Luís Vaz de Torres feeling its way along New Guinea's southern coast; weeks later the ships passed through the strait that now bears his name without landing on Daru or leaving a post. So few vessels used the passage that Europe learned of it only when Alexander Dalrymple published captured Spanish accounts in 1770-71. No foreign flag flew over the island before 1821, and the canoe trade between the Fly delta, the strait and Cape York ran on as before.
zh:
达鲁是一座低矮的椭圆形岛屿，最高处海拔27米，夹在新几内亚岛弗莱河口与礁群密布的托雷斯海峡之间的狭窄水域中。岛周浅海生满海草，儒艮在此觅食，海龟前来繁殖，岛民驾挂帆舷外支架独木舟镖猎二者，又在岛际水道捕鱼为生。他们既是猎手也是商人，身处一条双向运转的岛链：独木舟向北同弗莱河三角洲的基瓦伊村落交易，向南经营海峡古老的交换网络，用法螺、贝砵和捕龟镖杆换取巴布亚独木舟舟体、鹤鸵骨镞箭和竹器，贸易线还一直延伸到约克角的原住民那里。1444年时没有外来势力到过达鲁，岛上的秩序由氏族规矩和潮汐安排。

1606年9月5日，沿新几内亚南海岸摸索前行的路易斯·巴斯·德·托雷斯探险队最先望见达鲁岛；数周后船队穿过日后以他命名的海峡，但没有登岛，也未留下据点。这条水道极少再有船只通行，欧洲直到亚历山大·达尔林普尔1770至1771年公布缴获的西班牙文献才知晓它的存在。1821年以前，岛上没有升起过外来者的旗帜，弗莱河三角洲、海峡与约克角之间的独木舟贸易照旧运转。

en:
Yos Sudarso is a low, leaf-shaped island off southern New Guinea, separated from the mainland by the narrow muddy Muli Strait and from the smaller Komoran Island by the Buaya Strait. Europeans later called it Frederik Hendrik Island; its own people, the Kimaam, speak Kolopom tongues and count themselves among the Marind, and their names for the island are Kolepom and Dolok. Mangroves line the Arafura shore and run far inland over the swamps. In 1444 its villages lived by canoes, tidal channels and sago, and Kimaam, the main settlement facing the Buaya Strait, gave the island one of its names. Neither Moluccan traders nor any foreign factory had reached it.

The first European ship came from the south. About January 1606 Willem Jansz took the Duyfken through the bight between the island and New Guinea on the voyage that also made the first recorded European landing on the Australian coast; his chart marked the low mud shore as Tiuri and did not part it from New Guinea. Jan Carstensz rounded the south-western cape in 1623 and named it Valse Kaap, the False Cape, which Dutch maps kept. Neither visit left a fort or a trading post. As late as 1821 the island was still drawn as a corner of New Guinea, and the Kimaam kept their mangrove channels to themselves.
zh:
约斯苏达索是新几内亚南岸外一座低平、形似树叶的岛屿，北隔狭窄多泥的穆利海峡与本岛相望，东南隔布阿亚海峡与较小的科莫兰岛相邻。欧洲人后来称它弗雷德里克·亨德里克岛；岛上的基马姆人操科洛波姆诸语言，自认属于马林德人群，他们把本岛称作科洛波姆或多洛克。阿拉弗拉海沿岸红树林成带，顺着沼泽伸入内陆。1444年，岛上的村落以独木舟、潮沟和西谷椰为生，最大的聚落是面朝布阿亚海峡的基马姆，基马姆后来也成了岛名之一。摩鹿加商人和外国商馆都还没有到过这里。

第一艘欧洲船从南面来。约1606年1月，威廉·扬松驾「杜伊夫根号」穿过此岛与新几内亚之间的海湾；同一次航行中，欧洲人第一次有记载地登上澳大利亚海岸。他的海图把这片低平泥岸标作蒂乌里，没有把它和新几内亚分开。1623年，扬·卡斯滕斯绕过岛西南端的海角，取名假角（Valse Kaap），荷兰海图一直沿用。两次航行都没有留下要塞或商馆。直到1821年，海图上的这座岛仍被画成新几内亚的一角，基马姆人照旧守着自己的红树林水道。

en:
Asmat is a tide country on New Guinea's south-western coast, where Arafura Sea tides push into mangrove forest, tidal swamp, freshwater swamp and lowland rainforest. In 1444 the Asmat lived here in coastal and inland groups, differing in dialect, livelihood and ritual, with the Bisman and Simai among the coastal people. They were among the Pacific's finest woodcarvers: for funeral rites they raised mbis poles stacked with ancestral figures, cut wuramon spirit canoes to carry the dead to the ancestors, and carved war shields. Village feuds and headhunting raids went with the ancestor cult, and war canoes worked the mangrove channels. No outside ruler, mission or trader had reached them.

Europeans knew Asmat only from the sea for the rest of the period. In 1623 Jan Carstensz's Dutch ship made the first recorded sighting of Asmat people from its deck. On 3 September 1770 a party from James Cook's Endeavour went ashore near Pirimapun, met a group of Asmat warriors and, reading danger in the encounter, pulled back to the ship at once. No other landing followed, and the Asmat name as headhunters kept traders and missionaries away. In 1821 the swamps, the carving and the raids were all still entirely theirs.
zh:
阿斯马特是新几内亚西南岸的潮汐之乡，阿拉弗拉海的潮水涌入红树林、潮汐沼泽、淡水沼泽和低地雨林。1444年，阿斯马特人分为滨海与内陆两群，方言、生计和仪式各不相同，滨海一支又有比斯曼（Bisman）和西迈（Simai）等群。他们是太平洋上最好的雕木匠之一：为丧葬仪式刻出叠满祖先形象的mbis祖先柱、载亡魂归于先祖的wuramon灵舟，还有战盾。村落间的世仇和猎头袭掠与祖灵崇拜相伴，战舟穿行在红树林水道里。外来的统治者、传教士和商人都没有到过这里。

本时期余下的时间里，欧洲人只能从海上认识阿斯马特。1623年，扬·卡斯滕斯的荷兰船第一次有记载地从甲板上望见阿斯马特人。1770年9月3日，詹姆斯·库克「努力号」的一队人在皮里马蓬（Pirimapun）附近登岸，遇到一群阿斯马特战士，察觉情势危险后立刻撤回船上。此后再没有欧洲人登岸，阿斯马特人的猎头名声也使商人和传教士远避。到1821年，沼泽、雕刻和袭掠都还完全是他们自己的事。

en:
The Aru Islands are a scatter of about ninety-five low islands on the Sahul Shelf, between the Banda Sea and the Arafura, their fauna half Papuan and their people Austronesian. Long before any European came, Aru was a node of the eastern Indonesian trade: Banda, Bugis and Makassar merchants sailed here for pearl shell and pearls, tortoiseshell, trepang, sago, parrots and the plumes of birds of paradise. The islanders kept little hierarchy beyond their hospitality-bound clans, grouped in two ritual leagues, Ursia and Urlima, and obeyed no king. In 1444 this commerce moved entirely under native sail, and no outsider held a footing on the islands.

Portuguese ships sighted Aru in 1522-1524, when Martim Afonso de Melo wintered on one of the islands; the Spaniard Alvaro de Saavedra saw them in 1528, and the Dutch yacht Duyfken sailed these waters in 1606. The VOC made its first contract with west-coast villages in 1623 and put a trading post with a small fort on Wokam in 1659, drawing pearls, birds of paradise and slaves into the Bandanese market. A few islanders took Islam or Dutch Protestantism from the 1650s. The Company's monopoly galled, and when Nuku, prince of Tidore, rose against Dutch rule in 1780, Aru rose with him. In 1787 the Muslims of Ujir killed the Dutch garrison and set Nuku's brother Jou Mangofa over much of the archipelago, until a Bandanese expedition retook the islands in 1791. Nuku then allied with the British, and their campaigns in the Moluccas after 1795 undid what remained of Dutch control. In 1821 Aru was again in the hands of its own traders and clan councils.
zh:
阿鲁群岛是萨胡尔大陆架上散落的约九十五座低平岛屿，介于班达海与阿拉弗拉海之间，动物已带一半新几内亚色彩，岛民则属南岛人。早在欧洲人到来之前，阿鲁就是东印度尼西亚商路的一环：班达、布吉斯和望加锡商人来此采办珍珠和珍珠贝、玳瑁、海参、西谷米、鹦鹉和极乐鸟羽。岛民没有多少等级，只有以好客与互助维系的氏族，分属乌尔西亚、乌尔利马两个祭祀同盟，也不奉国王。1444年时，这桩贸易全靠本地商船运转，没有任何外人在岛上立足。

1522至1524年，葡萄牙船首次望见阿鲁，马丁·阿方索·德梅洛还在其中一座岛上过冬；1528年西班牙人萨阿韦德拉看到了群岛，1606年荷兰船「杜伊夫根号」也驶过这片水域。荷兰东印度公司1623年与西岸村落签下首份契约，1659年在沃坎岛设立商站和小要塞，把珍珠、极乐鸟羽和奴隶卷入班达市场；1650年代起，少数岛民改信伊斯兰教或荷兰新教。公司的垄断令人怨愤，1780年蒂多雷王子努库起兵反荷，阿鲁随即响应。1787年，乌吉尔岛的穆斯林消灭荷兰驻军，拥努库之弟焦·曼加法统治群岛大部；一支班达远征军于1791年重新夺回群岛。努库随后与英国结盟，1795年后英军在摩鹿加的攻势又瓦解了荷兰人残余的控制。1821年时，阿鲁重新掌握在本地商人与氏族议事会手中。

en:
Malgana country is Gathaagudu, the 'two waters' of Shark Bay, where an arid coast breaks into long peninsulas, tidal flats and islands that give shelter. Wulybidi, the Peron Peninsula, reaches toward Wirruwana, the long island later called Dirk Hartog Island. The Malgana spoke a Kartu language of the Pama–Nyungan family, and shell middens on the peninsula and the islands record the fish and shellfish taken from these warm shallows. In 1444 the wells, landing places and seasonal camps served that maritime round, and no European ship had yet reached the western edge of Australia.

The first to arrive was Dirk Hartog. On 25 October 1616 his Eendracht, bound from the Cape of Good Hope to Batavia, landed at Wirruwana, the first recorded European landing on Western Australian soil. Hartog spent three days examining coast and islands, nailed a pewter plate inscribed with the date and his officers' names to a post, and named the mainland Eendrachtsland after his ship. Willem de Vlamingh found the plate still on its post in 1697, left one of his own copying the inscription and carried Hartog's home to Amsterdam. In August 1699 William Dampier caught sharks in the bay and gave it their English name. In 1712 the Dutch East India Company ship Zuytdorp, carrying newly minted silver to Batavia, struck the cliffs south of the bay; none of her people ever reached Batavia, and Malgana oral tradition keeps stories of survivors coming ashore, building shelters and trading their stores for hunting tools. In March 1772 a French party under Louis Aleno de Saint-Aloüarn buried a bottle and a coin on Wirruwana and took the coast for Louis XV. A later French expedition found Vlamingh's plate half-buried in sand and re-erected it in 1801, then carried it off to Paris in 1818. None of these visits founded a settlement, and in 1821 Gathaagudu still belonged to the Malgana.
zh:
马尔加纳人的土地是鲨鱼湾的加塔古杜，意为「两片水域」。干旱海岸在这里分成长长的半岛、潮滩和多座可避风浪的岛屿，武利比迪即佩龙半岛，伸向维鲁瓦纳，这座长岛后来得名德克哈托格岛。马尔加纳人使用帕马—尼翁甘语系的卡尔图语，半岛和岛上的贝丘记录着他们从温暖浅水中获取鱼类、贝类的生活。1444年，水井、登陆处和季节性营地服务于这种依海为生的日子，还没有欧洲船抵达澳大利亚的西缘。

最先到来的是德克·哈托格。1616年10月25日，他的「恩德拉赫特号」从好望角驶往巴达维亚途中抵达维鲁瓦纳，这是欧洲人有记录的第一次西澳大利亚登陆。哈托格用三天考察海岸和岛群，把一块刻有日期和船员姓名的锡镴牌钉在木柱上，并以船名将大陆命名为恩德拉赫特地。1697年，威廉·德·弗拉明发现锡牌还钉在原处的柱上，便另立一块刻有同样铭文的新牌，把哈托格的原牌带回阿姆斯特丹。1699年8月，威廉·丹皮尔在湾中捕到鲨鱼，把海湾命名为鲨鱼湾。1712年，荷兰东印度公司的「祖伊特多普号」载着新铸的银币驶往巴达维亚，在湾南的悬崖失事，船员无一抵达巴达维亚；马尔加纳人的口述传统里，一直有幸存者上岸、搭棚栖身、用船上存粮交换狩猎器具的故事。1772年3月，法国人圣阿卢安率队在维鲁瓦纳埋下装着宣言文书和钱币的瓶子，以路易十五的名义占领这片海岸。后来的法国探险队在1801年发现弗拉明的锡牌半埋在沙中，将它重新立起，1818年又把它取走送往巴黎。这些访问无一带来定居点；1821年，加塔古杜仍属于马尔加纳人。

en:
Minang is the southernmost Noongar country, around King George Sound, called Mammang-Koort in Menang speech, on the south coast of Western Australia. Princess Royal Harbour and Oyster Harbour lie sheltered behind Breaksea and Michaelmas islands, and the Stirling Range stands on the northern skyline. In 1444 Minang families summered at Kinjarling, the Albany shore, fishing the harbours, gathering shellfish and maintaining stone fish traps at Emu Point and the mouth of the Kalgan River; peoples further north used the name Minang for these 'southern people'.

Europeans were equally late to arrive. In 1627 a Dutch East India Company ship carrying Pieter Nuyts sailed along this coast from offshore, the first recorded European sighting, but no ship entered the sound until George Vancouver in 1791, who named it for George III and claimed the shore for Britain. Two British whalers called soon afterwards, and one skipper, Dixson, left an inscribed copper plate on the beach which Matthew Flinders' men found when he lay in the sound from December 1801 to January 1802; his botanist Robert Brown collected more than 500 plant species there.
