Nicolas Baudin's French expedition followed in February 1803, and the naturalist Francois Peron gathered more than a thousand shellfish species; Phillip Parker King called in 1818. Minang oral tradition kept a dance that imitated the bearing of Flinders' landing party. In 1821 the sound was a well-known anchorage, but still had no permanent European settlement.
zh:
米南是农雅诸族最南的一支，住在西澳南岸的乔治王湾周围，米南语称这片海湾为马芒库特。皇家公主港和牡蛎港在布里克西岛、米迦勒节岛遮蔽下形成避风水面，北方天际横亘着斯特灵山脉。1444年，米南家族在金贾林，也就是奥尔巴尼海岸度夏，在港湾捕鱼、采贝，在伊米角和卡尔根河口维护石砌鱼梁；更北方的族群用「米南」称呼这些「南方人」。

欧洲人到得同样晚。1627年，一艘载着彼得·纳茨的荷兰东印度公司船只从外海驶过这段海岸，这是欧洲人有记载的第一次望见此地；直到1791年乔治·温哥华才驶入湾内，以英王乔治三世命名，并宣布海岸归英国所有。不久后两艘英国捕鲸船来访，船长之一狄克逊在海滩留下一块刻字铜牌，1801年12月至1802年1月马修·弗林德斯在此停泊时，他的水手找到了这块铜牌，随船植物学家罗伯特·布朗采集了500多种植物。1803年2月尼古拉·博丹率法国考察队继至，博物学家佩龙采集了上千种贝类；菲利普·帕克·金于1818年到访。米南人的口传里还保留了一段舞蹈，模仿弗林德斯一行登岸时的姿态。到1821年，乔治王湾已是知名锚地，却仍没有欧洲人永久定居。

en:
The Tiwi, who call themselves Tunuvivi, live on Ratuati Irara, 'the two islands': Bathurst and Melville, separated by Apsley Strait in the Timor Sea. Their language has no proven link with the languages of nearby Arnhem Land, and descent runs through the mother's line. The monsoon sets the annual round among forest, mangroves, beaches and fishing grounds; islanders take game and seafood, while song and painting carry clan and Dreaming knowledge. Traders from Makassar and possibly China are thought to have reached the islands from around 1600, but they did not occupy them. In 1444 the Tiwi controlled both shores of the strait.

The first recorded European landing met resistance and ended quickly. On 30 April 1705 Maarten van Delft brought the Dutch East India Company ships Nieuw Holland, Waijer and Vosschenbosch into Shark Bay on Melville Island. Tiwi skirmishes followed, and the Dutch withdrew without leaving a trading post or fort. Philip Parker King made the first recorded British contact in 1818. The meeting was tense, but his party exchanged iron tools for fish, fresh water and sago, and King put Melville Island, Bathurst Island and Apsley Strait on his charts. In 1821 no European garrison or mission stood on Ratuati Irara.
zh:
提维人自称图努维维，住在拉图阿蒂·伊拉拉，意为「两座岛」：巴瑟斯特岛和梅尔维尔岛隔阿普斯利海峡相望，地处帝汶海。提维语与附近阿纳姆地诸语言没有可证的亲缘关系，世系按母系传递。季风安排着岛民一年的行止，他们往来林地、红树林、海滩和渔场，猎取野味和海产；歌与绘画承载氏族和梦创知识。约自1600年起，望加锡商人以及可能到来的中国商人被认为曾抵达群岛，但没有占据土地。1444年，阿普斯利海峡两岸都由提维人掌控。

首次有记载的欧洲登陆很快遭到抵抗。1705年4月30日，马滕·范德尔夫特率三艘荷兰东印度公司船只驶入梅尔维尔岛鲨鱼湾并登陆。提维人与荷兰人发生小规模冲突，来者最终撤走，没有留下商馆或堡垒。1818年，菲利普·帕克·金完成首次有记载的英国接触。双方会面时气氛紧张，但英国人仍用铁器换到鱼、淡水和西米粉，金还把梅尔维尔岛、巴瑟斯特岛和阿普斯利海峡标入海图。1821年，拉图阿蒂·伊拉拉仍没有欧洲驻军或传教站。

en:
Yolngu means 'person' in the Yolngu languages and covers many clans in north-eastern Arnhem Land. Their estates run from Arafura Sea beaches and dunes to the paperbark country of the Arafura Swamp. Dhuwa and Yirritja are the two moieties that order kinship, ceremony and responsibility for country; the Rirratjingu are among the Dhuwa clans and the Gumatj among the Yirritja. The coast supplied fish and shellfish, the wetlands supplied game and plant foods, and message-stick routes and foot-messengers linked Yolngu with peoples far inland. Boomerangs reached Yolngu hands through those networks from Central Australia. In 1444 no foreign port stood on the coast, and each clan held its own estate.

In 1623 Willem Joosten van Colster's Dutch ship Arnhem gave Cape Arnhem its European name without opening a settlement. By the eighteenth century, Makassan and Sama-Bajau praus from Sulawesi sailed to Marege' with the monsoon, drying and smoking trepang for Chinese markets. Yolngu allowed anchorage and supplied labour, receiving cloth, knives, metal, tobacco, rice, canoes and pipes. Makassar pidgin spread along the coast, and the word Balanda for Europeans entered Yolngu speech before British settlers reached northern Australia. The praus built no fort, and through 1821 Yolngu country had no mission, garrison or colonial station.
zh:
雍古在雍古诸语中意为「人」，是阿纳姆地东北部众多氏族的统称。他们的土地从阿拉弗拉海的海滩与沙丘延伸到阿拉弗拉沼泽一带的白千层林地。杜瓦和伊里恰两大半族安排亲属、仪典和对土地的责任，里拉津古（Rirratjingu）氏族属杜瓦一边，古马奇（Gumatj）氏族属伊里恰一边。海岸提供鱼和贝类，湿地提供猎物和植物性食物，传信木杖路线和步行信使把雍古同远在内陆的人群相连，回旋镖就沿这些网络从中澳大利亚传来。1444年，海岸上没有外来港口，各氏族仍保有自己的土地。

1623年，威廉·约斯滕·范·科尔斯特乘坐荷兰船「阿纳姆号」航行到此，欧洲人随之为阿纳姆角命名，但没有建立定居点。到18世纪，来自苏拉威西的望加锡人和萨马-巴乔人乘帆船借季风来到他们称为马雷格的北方海岸，把海参晒干、熏制后供应中国市场。雍古人允许船队停泊并提供劳力，换取布料、刀、金属、烟草、稻米、独木舟和烟斗。望加锡皮钦语沿北岸传播，英国定居者到达澳大利亚北部以前，称呼欧洲人的「巴兰达」一词已进入雍古语言。船队没有修筑堡垒；到1821年，雍古之地仍没有传教站、驻军或殖民据点。

en:
Awngthim is Winduwinda country on the eastern shore of the Gulf of Carpentaria. The Mission River winds through monsoon woodland into Albatross Bay, and behind its mangrove flats the people of this western Cape York coast, whose Thaynakwith speech was also recorded as Awngthim, moved between rivers, wells and seasonal camps to fish, gather and hunt. Other Paman-speaking countries lay to the east and south. In 1444 no European chart marked the gulf; life on the shore followed the channels and landing places and the seasons that brought fish and turtle into the shallows.

The first recorded European landing in Australia happened on this coast. In 1606 Willem Janszoon's Duyfken, sailing for the Dutch East India Company out of Bantam, put in at a river mouth he named Rivier met het Bosch, 'the river with the forest', later charted as the Pennefather River. He had felt his way south from New Guinea along an unknown shore; shore parties met spears, and Janszoon turned back with a report of swamp and barren ground. Jan Carstenszoon followed in 1623: on 8 May his crew fought a skirmish with 200 local warriors near Cape Duyfken, and he named the gulf after the governor-general Pieter de Carpentier before sailing on to the Staaten River. Abel Tasman mapped more of the shore in 1644 and Matthew Flinders charted the bay in 1802 and 1803, yet by 1821 no fort, mission or trading post stood on Albatross Bay.
zh:
阿翁提姆是温杜温达人在卡奔塔利亚湾东岸的土地。米申河蜿蜒穿过季风林地，注入阿尔巴特罗斯湾；红树林潮滩之后，约克角半岛西岸的居民使用塔伊纳克维特语，这种语言也被记作阿翁提姆语，人们往来于河川、水井和季节性营地之间捕鱼、采集、狩猎，东面和南面则是其他帕马语族群的土地。1444年，还没有欧洲海图标出这座海湾，海岸生活依水道、登陆点和把鱼群、龟群带上浅滩的季节而走。

欧洲人有记录的第一次澳洲登陆就发生在这条海岸。1606年，威廉·扬松率领荷兰东印度公司的「杜伊夫肯号」从万丹驶来，在一条河口登陆，将它命名为「林中之河」，即后来的彭尼法瑟河。他从新几内亚一路南下，摸索着测绘这片陌生海岸；上岸的人遭到长矛袭击，扬松掉头返航，报告说沿途尽是沼泽和瘠地。1623年，扬·卡斯特斯松循路而来：5月8日，他的船员在杜伊夫肯角附近与二百名当地武士发生冲突；他又以总督彼得·德·卡彭蒂耶之名将海湾命名为卡奔塔利亚湾，随后南航至斯塔滕河。1644年，阿贝尔·塔斯曼补绘了更多岸线，1802至1803年马修·福林达斯测绘了整个海湾。但到1821年，阿尔巴特罗斯湾边仍没有要塞、传教站或商栈。

en:
The mouth of Wabalumbaal, the Endeavour River on later maps, opens on the wet tropical coast of Cape York Peninsula. Its coastal Guugu Yimithirr clans called themselves saltwater people, and the country around modern Cooktown was Gangaar, the place of rock crystals: quartz quarried for ceremony travelled exchange routes at least 300 kilometres to the south. The river mouth, the reef passages offshore and the inland scrub were all held and managed by Guugu Yimithirr clans, and in 1444 no outside power yet claimed the shore.

On 11 June 1770 the Endeavour, holed on the Endeavour Reef south of the river, limped to the river mouth and was beached there for seven weeks of repairs. From Grassy Hill above the camp James Cook worked out a passage back through the reefs, and the crew made the first recorded European sighting of a kangaroo there. Joseph Banks and Daniel Solander collected more than two hundred new plant species, the bulk of the plants the voyage brought home from Australia, and the artist Sydney Parkinson drew the specimens and the people themselves, the first British artist to portray Aboriginal Australians from direct observation. Banks also wrote down about fifty local words, among them gangurru, from which English took the name kangaroo; Guugu Yimithirr became the first Australian Aboriginal language recorded in writing. After a month of wary distance five men came forward and the two sides grew friendly, but on 19 July Cook refused to share the ship's turtles, and a clash over the duty to share food ended in burning grass and one man wounded by a musket. When Cook sailed he left a few pigs behind, which bred quickly in the bush and became a local food source. Philip Parker King surveyed the river in 1819 and again in 1820, noting large outrigger canoes, but no European settlement stood there in 1821.
zh:
瓦巴伦巴尔（Wabalumbaal，后来的奋进河）河口位于约克角半岛湿润的热带海岸。沿海的古古伊米吉尔氏族自称「咸水人」；后来库克敦一带叫甘加尔（Gangaar），意为水晶之地，山中采来供仪式使用的石英沿交换路线向南流通至少300公里。河口、外海的堡礁水道和内陆丛林都由古古伊米吉尔各氏族保有和管理，1444年时还没有外来势力索取这片海岸。

1770年6月11日，在奋进礁撞穿船底的「奋进号」带伤驶入河口，被拖上滩涂修理，前后停留七周。库克登上营地旁的草山摸清穿过堡礁的航路，船员也在这座上头一回记录下袋鼠。班克斯和索兰德采集了两百多种新植物，占这次航行从澳大利亚带回植物的大半；画师悉尼·帕金森一边绘制标本，一边画下当地人的样貌，成为第一位当面写生澳洲原住民的英国画家。班克斯还记下约50个当地词，其中就有gangurru，英语的kangaroo（袋鼠）一词就是从它来的，古古伊米吉尔语也成了第一种被文字记录的澳洲原住民语言。双方谨慎相持一个月后，五名男子主动走近，往来一度友好；但7月19日库克拒绝分让船上的海龟，对分享食物的不同理解引发冲突，草地被点燃，一名男子被火枪打伤。启航时库克留下几头猪，它们在野外迅速繁殖，成了当地的肉食来源。菲利普·帕克·金1819年、1820年两度到河口测量，记下更多词汇，还看到大型舷外架独木舟；但到1821年，这里仍没有欧洲定居点。

en:
The Wulgurukaba took their name from the wulgurru, a bark canoe: they were the canoe people of the dry-tropical coast around Cleveland Bay and Halifax Bay, on the shore where Townsville later stood. Their sea country ran out to the reefs and took in the Palm Islands and Yunbenun, the mountainous island eight kilometres offshore later named Magnetic Island. They crossed its channel in bark canoes, camped in its bays by season, and left shell middens and cave drawings in the rock shelters. Wulguru tradition recalled harder seasons, when raiding parties from the Torres Strait sailed south on the northern trade winds and the islanders withdrew to the mainland. In 1444 the bays, reefs and passages belonged entirely to these canoe-using clans.

On 6 June 1770 the Endeavour passed through Cleveland Bay without landing. Cook gave the bay its name and called the island Magnetic, because he suspected its rocks were drawing his compass needles aside; he also watched men crossing the shallows at low tide in eight-foot bark canoes. No ship came after it to plant a settlement, and in 1821 Wulgurukaba groups still held every passage between their mainland shores and island camps.
zh:
乌古鲁卡巴（Wulgurukaba）的名字来自wulgurru一词，即树皮独木舟，意为「独木舟人」。他们住在克利夫兰湾和哈利法克斯湾一带的干热带海岸，就是后来汤斯维尔所在的地方；海上领地一直延伸到堡礁，包括棕榈群岛和距岸八公里的多山岛屿云贝农（Yunbenun，后来的磁岛）。他们划树皮独木舟往来海峡，按季节在岛上各海湾扎营，在岩棚里留下贝冢和岩画。乌尔古鲁人的传说提到过更艰难的时令：托雷斯海峡的猎头者乘北信风沿海岸南下，岛民便撤回大陆躲避。1444年，这些海湾、礁区和水道完全属于使用独木舟的各氏族。

1770年6月6日，「奋进号」穿过克利夫兰湾，没有靠岸。库克为海湾命了名，又把那座岛叫做磁岛，因为他疑心岛上的岩石使罗盘磁针偏转；他还看见有人趁低潮划着八英尺长的树皮独木舟穿越浅滩。此后没有船来建立定居点，到1821年，乌古鲁卡巴各群体仍掌握着大陆海岸与岛屿营地之间的每一条水道。

en:
Baiali, also spelt Byellee, is the coast from the Fitzroy delta to the deep harbour between the Calliope and Boyne Rivers. The Fitzroy, called Toonooba by the peoples of its basin, gathers the drainage of a wide swathe of central Queensland and empties into Keppel Bay; on its lower reaches the Baiali and Jetimarala were clans connected with the Darumbal. Around the future Gladstone, Baiali groups shared the shore with Gooreng Gooreng, Toolooa and Meerooni people, and their Bayali language was later recorded along the coast between Rockhampton and Gladstone. In 1444 these estuaries, islands and harbour were known only through the speech and sea-lore of their Aboriginal clans, and no European chart showed them.

James Cook was the first European to reach these waters. He brought the Endeavour to anchor in Keppel Bay on 27 May 1770 and named the bay after Admiral Augustus Keppel, but he sailed past the narrow entrance of the harbour to the south-east in darkness and did not go in. Matthew Flinders, in the Investigator on his voyage round Australia, found the inlet on 1 August 1802 and named it Port Curtis after Vice-Admiral Roger Curtis, who had helped repair his ship at the Cape the previous October. Flinders put the sheltered water on European maps, yet in 1821 the Baiali coast had no British settlement.
zh:
拜阿里（也拼作Byellee）的海岸，从菲茨罗伊河口三角洲延伸到卡利奥佩河与博因河之间的深水港湾。菲茨罗伊河被流域各族称为图努巴河，汇集昆士兰中部广大地区的水系，注入凯珀尔湾；在下游一带，拜阿里人和杰蒂马拉拉人是与达伦巴尔人相连的氏族。在后来格拉德斯通所在的岸边，拜阿里人与古伦古伦人、图卢阿人和米鲁尼人共处，他们的拜阿里语后来在罗克汉普顿到格拉德斯通之间的海岸留下记录。1444年，这些河口、岛屿和港湾只存在于原住民氏族的语言与海路见闻里，欧洲人的海图上还没有它们。

第一个来到这片水域的欧洲人是詹姆斯·库克。1770年5月27日，他率「努力号」在凯珀尔湾停泊，以海军上将奥古斯都·凯珀尔之姓为海湾命名，但他在夜色中驶过东南方那道狭窄的港湾入口，没有驶入。1802年8月1日，马修·弗林德斯乘「勘察者号」环航澳大利亚时找到这座水口，将其命名为柯蒂斯港，以纪念前一年10月在好望角协助修船的罗杰·柯蒂斯海军中将。弗林德斯把这片避风水域标上欧洲海图，但到1821年，拜阿里海岸仍没有英国定居点。

en:
Between Batemans Bay and Cape Howe the Yuin hold a coast of rocky headlands, sea inlets and surf beaches backed by the forested scarp of the Great Dividing Range. They are many clans, Wandandian, Walbunja, Djiringanj, Thaua and others, living by fish, shellfish and the mullet runs and putting out through the surf in bark canoes. Above the shore at Tilba rises Gulaga, the mother mountain, the Yuin's place of origin and ground especially sacred to their women. Her elder son Barunguba was allowed to travel far out to sea and became Montague Island; the younger, Najanuka, was kept close at her side. Perhaps 11,000 Yuin lived along this coast on the eve of European arrival. In 1444 their canoes had these waters to themselves.

On 21 April 1770 Cook's Endeavour, passing 15 miles offshore, named Gulaga Mount Dromedary, and no boat put in. Disease reached the Yuin first: in 1789 smallpox spread south from Sydney through Aboriginal networks, years before most of them saw a European. Whaling ships out of Sydney were working these waters by 1791. George Bass, driving south in an open whaleboat, sheltered in Twofold Bay in February 1798 and gave it its name; returning that October with Matthew Flinders in the Norfolk, he surveyed the bay and made first contact with the Thaua. Sealing and whaling vessels followed, and in 1821 the Mary was wrecked sheltering there. No European station yet stood on Yuin ground, though disease had already thinned the clans along the coast.
zh:
在巴特曼斯湾与豪角之间，尤因人守着一条遍布岩岬、海湾与浪滩的海岸，背后是林木覆盖的大分水岭陡坡。他们分为万丹迪安、瓦尔本贾、吉林甘、陶阿等众多氏族，以鱼、贝类和鲻鱼渔汛为生，划着树皮独木舟穿过浪涛出海。蒂尔巴岸边矗立着母亲山古拉加，那里是尤因人的祖源之地，对尤因女子尤其神圣。她的长子巴伦古巴获准远游大海，化作蒙塔古岛；幼子纳贾努卡则被留在身边。欧洲人到来前夕，约有一万一千名尤因人生活在这条海岸上。1444年，这片水面上还只有他们的独木舟。

1770年4月21日，库克的「奋进号」在十五英里外的海面经过，将古拉加命名为单峰驼山，但没有放艇靠岸。先抵达尤因人的是疫病：1789年，天花沿原住民的往来网络从悉尼南下，比大多数尤因人见到欧洲人早了许多年。早在1791年，悉尼派出的捕鲸船已在这片海域作业。乔治·巴斯驾无甲板捕鲸艇南下，1798年2月在图福德湾避风并为海湾命名；同年10月他与马修·弗林德斯乘「诺福克号」重返，测绘海湾并首次与陶阿人接触。随后海豹猎船和捕鲸船接踵而来，1821年「玛丽号」在湾中避风时失事。尤因人的土地上这时还没有欧洲人的定居站，但疫病已使沿岸各氏族人口大减。

en:
The Gunditjmara, also called Dhauwurd Wurrung, hold south-western Victoria around Portland, Port Fairy, Warrnambool and the volcano Budj Bim, whose name means 'High Head'. Their tradition says Budj Bim was a creator being who showed himself in an eruption that sent lava fifty kilometres to the sea; geologists date the eruption around 37,000 years ago. The lava blocked Darlot Creek into chains of swamps and pools, and over more than a hundred square kilometres the Gunditjmara built channels, stone races, weirs, dams and holding ponds, setting large woven baskets in the weirs to take mature short-finned eels, or kooyang, which they smoked over burning blackwood leaves. One trap has been dated to 6,600 years ago. Clans raised stone huts with turf and branch roofs beside the works and lived in settled villages, the Kerrup Jmara around Lake Condah, the Koroitgundidj near Tower Hill; fifty-nine clans held named lakes, traps and grounds, and the dead were buried with their heads towards the sea island of Deen Maar. In 1444 this was a settled aquaculture country, held clan by clan.

European ships came only at the period's end. In December 1800 James Grant, in the Lady Nelson, surveyed this coast and named Portland Bay; Matthew Flinders in Investigator and Nicolas Baudin's French expedition recorded more of the shoreline in 1802. From about 1810 whalers and sealers used Portland Bay as a seasonal camp, bringing trade and new diseases but no permanent station. Through 1821 the eel channels, stone villages and clan estates remained in Gunditjmara hands.
zh:
贡迪杰马拉人（也称道伍德·武龙人）住在维多利亚州西南部，土地环绕波特兰、费里港、瓦南布尔和布吉必姆火山，布吉必姆意为「高首」。相传布吉必姆是一位创世先祖，在喷发中现出真身，熔岩一直流到五十公里外入海；地质学家测定这次喷发约在三万七千年前。熔岩把达洛特溪壅成串珠状的沼泽与水塘，贡迪杰马拉人在一百多平方公里的范围内开渠道、砌石堰、修水坝和蓄养池，用大型编织篓在堰口捕捞成熟的短鳍鳗（本地称库扬），再用燃烧的黑木树叶熏制；一处鱼梁经测定已有六千六百年历史。各氏族在工程旁建起玄武岩石屋，以草皮树枝覆顶，聚落成村，凯鲁普·杰马拉氏族住在康达湖周围，科罗伊特贡迪杰氏族靠近塔山。五十九个氏族各有命名的湖泊、鱼梁和场地，死者下葬时头朝向海上的丁马尔岛。1444年时，这里已是由氏族分管的定居水产养殖之地。

欧洲船只到这一时期末尾才出现。1800年12月，詹姆斯·格兰特乘「纳尔逊夫人号」测绘这段海岸，命名波特兰湾；1802年，马修·弗林德斯乘「考察者号」与尼古拉·博丹的法国探险队又记录了更多海岸线。约1810年起，捕鲸者和海豹猎者把波特兰湾当作季节性营地，带来贸易和新的疾病，但没有设立常驻据点。到1821年，鳗鱼渠、石屋村落和氏族领地仍在贡迪杰马拉人手中。

en:
The Nukunu hold the eastern shore of upper Spencer Gulf, some 5,700 square kilometres running from the Broughton River mouth and Crystal Brook to the head of the gulf near Port Augusta, and inland through Melrose, Mount Remarkable, Gladstone and Quorn. Coast, the southern Flinders Ranges and the plains meet here, and the country is dense with sacred places. Beside a great tree near Port Augusta, a tree that also stood for the Milky Way, begins the Urumbula songline, which follows the wanderings of a western quoll north across the desert all the way to the Gulf of Carpentaria. Nukunu is a Thura–Yura language, and its speakers took pride in being 'ritual purists': they were the southeasternmost people to keep the circumcision and subincision rites of male initiation and a matrilineal system of two marriage moieties. In 1444 no European ship had entered Spencer Gulf, and Nukunu families moved between its tidal shores, watercourses and hills on their own rounds.

Matthew Flinders made the first recorded European exploration of Spencer Gulf in February 1802, taking Investigator almost to the head of the gulf, and named it Spencer's Gulph on 20 March after the Earl Spencer. Nicolas Baudin's French ships surveyed the same waters soon after, and French charts briefly labelled the gulf Golfe Bonaparte. Neither voyage put a post ashore, and through 1821 the upper gulf and its nearby ranges remained Nukunu country.
zh:
努库努人住在斯潘塞湾上段东岸，约5700平方公里的土地从布劳顿河口和克里斯特尔布鲁克向北延伸到奥古斯塔港附近的湾头，向内陆经过梅尔罗斯、里马克布尔山、格拉德斯通和阔恩。海岸、南弗林德斯岭与平原在此相接，境内圣地遍布。在奥古斯塔港附近有一棵大树，它同时代表银河；乌伦布拉歌路就从树旁起头，循着一只西袋鼬的足迹，向北穿过沙漠，一直通到卡奔塔利亚湾。努库努语属图拉—尤拉语支，努库努人以恪守仪礼的「纯粹」自豪：他们是同时保留割礼与次切礼成年仪式、以及母系两偶族婚制最东南的族群。1444年时还没有欧洲船只进入斯潘塞湾，努库努各家族按自己的节律往来于潮汐岸、水道和山地之间。

1802年2月，马修·弗林德斯乘「考察者号」首次有记录地勘探斯潘塞湾，船只几乎一直探到湾头；3月20日他以斯潘塞伯爵之名将海湾命名为斯潘塞湾。尼古拉·博丹的法国船队随后也测绘了这片水域，法国海图还一度把这里标作波拿巴湾。这些航行都没有在岸上设立据点；到1821年，上海湾及附近山岭仍是努库努人的土地。

en:
Between the forested Remutaka and Tararua ranges and the sea runs the south-eastern coast of the North Island, from the great Ahuriri lagoon in Heretaunga, later called Hawke Bay, down to Lake Wairarapa, the 'glistening waters' that gave the region its name. The lagoon, shut off from the surf by a shingle bank, was ringed by pā and fishing villages, and the southern lakes and swamps supplied eels and waterfowl. In 1444 the shore belonged to Whatumamoa, Rangitāne and Ngāti Awa.

Ngāti Kahungunu came to this coast after a quarrel between brothers in Tauranga. Kahungunu, raised there, fell out with his elder brother Ranginui and left for the east coast; tradition says that at Māhia he set out to win Rongomaiwahine, a woman of rank who had challenged him to prove himself, killed her husband Tama-taku-tai, and after many trials married her. His descendant Taraia led the people south from Māhia into Heretaunga, displaced Whatumamoa, Rangitāne and Ngāti Awa, and made his followers the first Ngāti Kahungunu of the district; a chief named Te Ahuriri cut the lagoon outlet to the sea that still bears his name, and related hapū settled among the eel grounds of Wairarapa. Late in the eighteenth century Te Kahu-o-te-rangi and Te-O-Tane shattered a Te Whānau-ā-Apanui war party at Whāwhāpō and secured the northern approaches. James Cook reached this shore in October 1769, the first European to do so, and named Hawke Bay after Admiral Sir Edward Hawke. At its southern point Māori in a fishing canoe seized Taiata, the twelve-year-old Tahitian servant of his interpreter Tupaia; fire from the Endeavour killed two or three of the party and the boy swam back to the ship, which gave Cape Kidnappers its name. No European settlement followed, and in 1821 the coast was still entirely Ngāti Kahungunu land.
zh:
在林木茂密的雷穆塔卡山脉、塔拉鲁阿山脉与大海之间，是北岛东南海岸：北起黑雷陶加（后称霍克湾）畔的阿胡里里大潟湖，南至怀拉拉帕湖，湖名意为「闪光的水域」，地区便因湖得名。潟湖被一道砾石洲与海浪隔开，四周环布山寨和渔村，南方的湖沼出产鳗鱼和水鸟。1444年，这段海岸属于瓦图马莫阿、朗吉塔内和恩加蒂阿瓦诸部。

雅提卡胡伍努伊人来到这段海岸，缘起陶朗加的一场兄弟失和。卡胡伍努在陶朗加长大，与兄长朗吉努伊争执后出走东海岸；相传在马希亚，他决意赢得朗戈迈瓦希内：这位出身高贵的女子曾出言相激，要他证明自己；他杀了她的丈夫塔马塔库泰，历经周折后娶到了她。他的后人塔拉亚率部从马希亚南下黑雷陶加，逐走瓦图马莫阿、朗吉塔内和恩加蒂阿瓦，使部众成为当地最早的雅提卡胡伍努伊人；酋长特阿胡里里为潟湖开凿出海水道，这处地方便以他得名，同族支系在怀拉拉帕的鳗鱼产地间定居。18世纪末，特卡胡奥特朗吉与特奥塔内在法法波一战大破特瓦瑙阿阿帕努伊战阵，稳固了北面的门户。1769年10月，詹姆斯·库克第一个驶过这段海岸，以海军将领爱德华·霍克爵士之名命名霍克湾。在海湾南端，毛利人乘一艘渔船靠近，掳走了船上翻译图帕伊亚的侍童、十二岁的塔希提少年提亚塔；「努力号」开火，打死对方两三人，少年游回船上，库克便把这处海角命名为绑架角。此后没有欧洲人来此定居，到1821年，这段海岸仍完全是雅提卡胡伍努伊人的土地。

en:
Te Tau Ihu, 'the tip of the fish's nose', is the pointed top of Te Waipounamu, the South Island. Farewell Spit runs twenty-six kilometres out from Cape Farewell, the longest sandspit in the country, and behind it lie the shallow bay of Mohua, Tasman Bay and the drowned valleys of the Marlborough Sounds. The old peoples of the sounds, Waitaha, Ngāi Tara and Ngāti Wairangi, kept some of the oldest settlements in the land, their villages on the Mohua shore going back to at least 1450. Waitaha, descendants of Rākaihautū's Uruaokapuarangi canoe, tended the 400 hectares of the Waimea Gardens below Pikimai, above the anchorage later called Whakatū, or Nelson. They were the first to quarry pakohe argillite on Rangitoto ki te Tonga, D'Urville Island, their dark adzes traded through Tōtaranui as far as the North Island. In 1444 the kūmara gardens, eel weirs and seafood grounds of the tip belonged to these sound peoples, with Waitaha foremost.

Early in the 1600s Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri of the Kurahaupō canoe pushed west through the sounds and ruled the whole northwest, from Māwhera to the Marlborough Sounds, for two centuries. In December 1642 two strange ships entered Mohua, Abel Tasman's Heemskerck and Zeehaen, the first Europeans Māori had seen. Waka challenged them with conch trumpets and ritual calls; when the Dutch tried to land beside kūmara gardens, more than twenty waka swept out, rammed a cockboat and killed four seamen, while fire from the ships killed one warrior. Tasman sailed away without landing and named the bay Murderers' Bay. James Cook sheltered at Tōtaranui in 1770 and named it Queen Charlotte Sound; from a hill on Arapaoa Island he made out the passage between the two islands that now bears his name, and he returned twice more. The tribes fought long wars over the greenstone trail crossing Tūmatakōkiri land to the West Coast, until a great canoe attack on Kāpiti was broken by contrary winds that swamped the fleet. Around 1810 Tūmatakōkiri were beaten in the Paparoa Ranges; the Ngāi Tahu chief Tuhuru killed their paramount chiefs Te Pau and Te Kokihi, the survivors were enslaved, and the lands were divided among Ngāi Tahu, Ngāti Apa and Ngāti Kuia.
zh:
陶伊胡意为「鱼鼻尖」，是特怀波纳穆（南岛）最北端的尖角。告别角的沙嘴伸入海中26公里，为全国最长的沙嘴；沙嘴后方是水浅的莫胡阿湾、塔斯曼湾，以及马尔堡峡湾一片被海水淹没的山谷。峡湾旧部怀塔哈、恩加伊塔拉和恩加蒂怀朗吉保有全国最古老的一些居民点，他们在莫胡阿湾沿岸的村落可上溯至1450年。怀塔哈人是拉凯豪图所率乌鲁阿奥卡普阿朗吉号独木舟的后裔，在皮基迈山下经营四百公顷的怀梅阿园圃，皮基迈山俯瞰的港湾后来称华卡图，即尼尔森。他们最早在朗吉托托基东加（德于维尔岛）开采巴科赫泥岩，深色石斧经托塔拉努伊远销北岛。1444年，尖角上的库马拉园圃、鳗鱼堰和海场属于这些峡湾部族，以怀塔哈人为首。

17世纪初，乘库拉豪波号独木舟迁来的恩加蒂图马塔科基里人沿峡湾西进，西起马韦拉、东抵马尔堡峡湾的整个西北部都归其统治，前后二百年。1642年12月，两艘陌生大船驶入莫胡阿湾，那是阿贝尔·塔斯曼的「赫姆斯凯克号」与「泽哈恩号」，毛利人头一回见到欧洲人。毛利独木舟吹起螺号、念诵咒语叫阵，荷兰人回以号声和一炮；荷兰人试图在一片库马拉园圃旁登陆时，二十多艘独木舟冲出，撞沉一艘交通艇，杀死四名水手，一名战士中枪。塔斯曼未敢登陆便离去，把海湾命名为「杀人犯湾」。1770年，詹姆斯·库克泊入托塔拉努伊，将其命名为夏洛特女王湾；他在阿拉帕瓦岛的山丘上辨认出分隔两岛的海峡，海峡后来以他命名，此后他又两度重来。为争夺穿过图马塔科基里土地、通往西海岸的绿玉商路，诸部交战多年；图马塔科基人大举出动独木舟进攻卡皮蒂，逆风倾覆了船队，残兵也被歼灭。约1810年，图马塔科基里人在帕帕罗瓦山脉战败，纳塔胡酋长图胡鲁杀了他们的大酋长特保与特科基希，余众沦为奴隶，土地被纳塔胡、恩加蒂阿帕和恩加蒂库伊亚三部分占。

en:
The Waikato is the wide garden basin of New Zealand's longest river, which runs north from Lake Taupō to the sea. Its terraces and swamps grew kūmara, taro and yams, its lakes and backwaters yielded eels and waterfowl, and before European times it was the third most densely peopled part of the country. The Tainui, descendants of Hoturoa's Tainui waka, had held Kāwhia on the west coast since the fourteenth century and entered the basin around 1400, bringing kūmara with them. At Kirikiriroa, 'the long stretch of gravel' where Hamilton now stands, the villages of Te Parapara, Miropiko and Pukete lay among river gardens. In 1444 the river is a highway of canoes and fish catches, and Tainui hapū are still fighting their way up its reaches against the earlier peoples of the interior.

The upper basin was not secured until the siege of Pōhatu-roa at the end of the seventeenth century, and around 1807 came the great trial, at Hingakaka near Ōhaupō. It began at a fish feast: Pikauterangi, a Ngāti Toa chief, seized the largest kahawai and was dunked for it, and answered by killing his Ngāti Apakura hosts and raising a coalition of 7,000 to 10,000 warriors from Ngāti Toa, Ngāti Raukawa, the southern North Island and the East Cape. The Waikato chief Te Rauangaanga met them with perhaps 3,000 Waikato and Ngāti Maniapoto, joined by Ngāti Whātua and Hauraki. A chain of alarm pā from Kakepuku to Taupiri carried warning of the march, and at Te Mangeo ridge above Lake Ngaroto the defenders stuck bunches of feathers on fern stems to fake a hidden reserve, drew the invaders up a narrow spur and took them in the flank; Te Rauangaanga himself killed Pikauterangi. Thousands died in the lake and swamps, so many chiefs among them that the fight was named Hingakaka, 'the fall of the kākā parrots', the largest battle ever fought in New Zealand. The sacred carving Te Uenuku was lost in the carnage.

In 1821 Te Rauangaanga's son Pōtatau Te Wherowhero led the Waikato taua south on the Āmiowhenua raid. In the same year Hongi Hika's Ngāpuhi destroyed Mauinaina pā on the Auckland isthmus, and the musket war had reached the Waikato frontier.
zh:
怀卡托是新西兰第一长河怀卡托河冲积出的宽阔盆地，河水自陶波湖北流入海。河阶与沼泽种着库马拉、芋头和薯蓣，湖泊河汊盛产鳗鱼和水禽；欧洲人到来之前，这里是全国人口第三稠密的地区。泰努伊人自认是霍图罗阿所驾「泰努伊号」独木舟移民的后裔，14世纪起据有西海岸的卡菲亚，约1400年携库马拉进入盆地。在今哈密尔顿所在的基里基里罗阿（意为「长长的砾石滩」），蒂帕拉帕、米罗皮科、普凯蒂等村落散布在河畔园地之间。1444年，怀卡托河是独木舟与渔获往来的通道，泰努伊各部仍在沿河向上游推进，与内陆先住民争地。

直到17世纪末波哈图罗阿围城战后，泰努伊人才拿下上游盆地。约1807年，决定胜负的大战在奥豪波附近的欣加卡卡打响。战祸起于一场鱼宴：恩加蒂托阿酋长皮考特兰吉在宴上独取最大的卡哈韦鱼，被人按住浸水，他随即杀死做东的恩加蒂阿普库拉人，又从恩加蒂托阿、恩加蒂劳卡瓦、北岛南部和东角纠集起七千到一万联军。怀卡托酋长特·劳安甘甘加能集结的，只有约三千怀卡托与恩加蒂马尼亚波托武士，另有恩加蒂华图阿和豪拉基来援。从卡凯普库山到陶皮里山，一连串报警寨堡接力传警；在恩加罗托湖畔的特曼盖奥山脊，守军把羽簇插在蕨茎上伪装伏兵，诱联军沿窄山脊仰攻，再从侧翼突击，特·劳安甘甘加亲手斩杀皮考特兰吉。数千人毙命于湖沼之间，战死酋长之多使此役得名「欣加卡卡」，意为「卡卡鹦鹉纷纷坠地」；这也是新西兰有史以来规模最大的战役，圣物木雕「特乌恩努库」在乱军中遗失。

1821年，特·劳安甘甘加之子波塔陶·特·维罗维罗率怀卡托战团南下参加「环地」（Āmiowhenua）远征。同年，杭吉·希卡的雅普希攻破奥克兰地峡上的莫伊纳伊纳寨堡，火枪战争已经逼到怀卡托北境。

en:
Jeju is a volcanic island in the strait south of Korea, eighty kilometres from the mainland, with the volcano Hallasan at its centre. Its Tamna kingdom kept its own lords and traded with China, Japan and the Korean kingdoms. Island lore says three divine men climbed out of three holes in the ground at the foot of Hallasan, the Samseonghyeol, married princesses who sailed in from across the sea with five grains, cattle and horses, and so began the island's farming and horse raising. In 1273 Goryeo and Yuan troops destroyed the Sambyeolcho rebels on Jeju, and the Yuan afterwards ran great horse pastures there; the island returned to Goryeo in 1295. Joseon ended Tamna self-rule in 1404 and in 1416 divided it into Jeju-mok, Jeongui-hyeon and Daejeong-hyeon under Jeolla. In 1444 a magistrate at basalt-walled Jeju governed fishing villages, tribute tangerine orchards and horse ranches. The law code allowed only grave criminals to be exiled here, and islanders were forbidden to cross the sea.

One exile was a king: Gwanghaegun, deposed in 1623, was moved from Ganghwa to Jeju and died there in 1641. A Dutch East India Company clerk, Hendrick Hamel, was wrecked here in 1653 when his ship the Sperwer went down; Joseon held the survivors for thirteen years, and after Hamel escaped to Dejima in 1666 his printed journal of 1668 gave Europe its first detailed account of Korea. Around 1754 the three walled towns placed basalt images of grinning old men, dol hareubang, at their gates as guardians. In 1793 a famine killed more than six hundred islanders and five government grain ships were lost. Gim Man-deok, who had bought her way out of the gisaeng registry and made a fortune in the port trade, spent it on mainland rice for the hungry; in 1796 King Jeongjo made a rare exception to the sea ban and let her visit Hanyang, and she died back on Jeju in 1812.
zh:
济州是朝鲜半岛以南海峡中的一座火山岛，与陆地隔着八十公里海路，岛中央耸立着汉拿山。岛上的耽罗国保留本地君长，与中国、日本和朝鲜半岛诸政权通商往来。相传三位神人从汉拿山北麓的三个地穴中走出，那地穴便是三姓穴；他们娶了渡海而来的公主，公主带来五谷、牛和马，教岛人耕作养畜。1273年，高丽与元朝的军队在岛上剿灭三别抄，元朝随即在这里经营大片牧马场；1295年济州复归高丽。1404年朝鲜废除耽罗自治，1416年又把全岛划分为全罗道下属的济州牧、旌义县和大静县。1444年，济州牧使从玄武岩城墙环绕的济州城治理渔村、向朝廷进贡柑橘的果园和牧马场；法典规定只有重罪人才可流放此岛，岛民也不得渡海。

流放来岛的还有一位国王：1623年被废的光海君先囚于江华岛，后移济州，1641年死在岛上。1653年，荷兰东印度公司书记员亨德里克·哈梅尔在济州乘船遇险，朝鲜扣留幸存者十三年；哈梅尔1666年逃到出岛，他的游记1668年刊印，成为欧洲第一部详细记述朝鲜的著作。1754年前后，济州、旌义、大静三座城邑在城门口立起玄武岩石刻的笑面老人守门像，当地称作石爷。1793年岛上饥荒，六百余人饿死，五艘官府运粮船沉没。金万德本是妓生，赎身后做港口贸易致富；她散尽家财从陆地买米赈饥，1796年正祖破例准许她渡海前往汉阳，她于1812年在济州去世。

en:
Yukjin, the Six Garrisons, was the chain of Hoeryong, Jongseong, Onsong, Gyeongwon, Gyeongheung and Puryong below a bend of the Tumen River, the northeastern edge of Korea. The river country belonged to the Jurchen when the Joseon dynasty began, and the early Korean post at Gyeongwon, founded in 1398, was evacuated after a Jurchen attack and restored only years later. In 1433 the general Kim Jong-seo pushed the frontier up to the Tumen, and King Sejong moved 2,200 farming households from southern Hamgil to people the six new forts. By 1444 Gyeongwon headed a string of military settlements, Korean soldiers and relocated farmers living among Jurchen villages that still held most of the riverbank.

The mixed border never settled for long. In 1583 Nitanggae, a tributary Jurchen chief near Hoeryong, rose and held out from January to July; two officers who learned their trade putting him down, Yi Il and Sin Rip, later held Joseon's main commands in the Japanese war. In 1592 Katō Kiyomasa led 22,000 men through the six towns to Onsong, crossed the Tumen and skirmished with the Jurchen beyond it, while the rebel chief Guk Gyeong-in seized the princes Imhae and Sunhwa at Hoeryong and handed them to Katō. Jeong Mun-bu raised a Righteous Army farther south, and two students of the Hoeryong Confucian school, acting on his secret order, lured Guk Gyeong-in out and killed him; Jeong's battles around Gyeongseong and Kilju cleared the Japanese from the province early in 1593. Qing forces raided across the border in the winter war of 1636-1637, after which the Tumen garrisons belonged to a Joseon kingdom tributary to the Qing. The settlers kept their southern speech, and the 1693 provincial gazette Bukgwan-ji found the six towns far easier for a southerner to follow than the rest of Hamgyeong.
zh:
六镇是图们江一处大河弯以南的会宁、钟城、稳城、庆源、庆兴和富宁六座军镇，是朝鲜的东北尽头。朝鲜开国之初，江两岸还是女真人的土地；设在庆源的边镇1398年初设，遭女真进攻后一度迁空，多年后才恢复。1433年，金宗瑞把边界推进到图们江，世宗又从咸吉道南部迁移2200户农家充实六座新镇。到1444年，庆源统领着一串军屯，朝鲜军士和南迁来的农户与据有大半江岸的女真村落错杂而居。

这条混居边防线始终不得安宁。1583年，会宁一带的藩胡首领尼汤介起兵，从1月坚持到7月才被镇压；参与平乱的李镒、申砬，后来都成了壬辰战争中朝鲜军的主将。1592年，加藤清正率二万二千人穿过六镇直抵稳城，又渡过图们江与江外的女真人交战；会宁的叛首鞠景仁则把临海君、顺和君两位王子抓住，送交加藤。郑文孚在南边组织义兵，会宁乡校的儒生申世俊、吴允迪奉他密谕诱杀鞠景仁，郑文孚又在镜城、吉州一带连番作战，于1593年初把日军逐出咸镜道。1636年至1637年冬季清军越边攻掠，战后图们江诸镇仍属朝鲜，只是朝鲜已成清朝藩属。南迁的移民保留了南方口音，1693年的道志《北关志》就记载，六镇的话比咸镜道其他地方好懂得多，南方人也听得懂。

en:
Gyeongseong sits on the East Sea coastal plain beneath the Hamgyong Mountains, on ground the Jurchen knew as Urong'i or Mokranggo; it was disputed between Goryeo and the Jurchen for centuries and at times stood under Yuan authority. The Joseon dynasty planted itself here early: the place was named Gyeongseong in 1398, a military camp went up in 1400, a walled bu followed in 1410, and the post was raised to a protectorate office in 1432. In 1444 it was a garrison town on the cold edge of the kingdom, guarding Korean outposts and fishing villages scattered among Jurchen settlements.

In 1467 Yi Si-ae and the gentry of Kilju raised some 20,000 men against King Sejo's centrally appointed magistrates and killed the provincial governor before royal armies broke the revolt. Kilju was demoted, and Gyeongseong took its place as the seat of the North Military Camp; in 1468 the province took the name Hamgyeong from Hamheung and Gyeongseong. In 1592 Katō Kiyomasa's army occupied the far north, and in the ninth lunar month Jeong Mun-bu, the northern defense commissioner, raised a few hundred men outside the walls. He entered Gyeongseong by feigning submission to its collaborator commander Guk Se-pil, drilled his militia inside the town, then killed Guk Se-pil along with the Japanese officers he dealt with and made Gyeongseong the base for cavalry raids and ambushes around Kilju that wore the Japanese down until they withdrew early in 1593. Jeong was later framed for plotting against King Injo and died under torture in 1624; he was exonerated in 1665, and a shrine named Hyeonchungsa was built for him in Gyeongseong. Manchu raiders reached the coast in 1636-1637, and the garrison became the northeastern edge of Qing-tributary Joseon.
zh:
镜城位于咸镜山脉脚下、面朝东海的沿海平原，女真人旧称这一带为于笼耳或木郎古；数百年来它是高丽与女真反复争夺之地，还一度处在元朝势力之下。朝鲜王朝开国后很快在此立足：1398年命名为镜城，1400年设军营，1410年筑城设府，1432年升为都护府。1444年的镜城是朝鲜寒冷边缘上的军镇，守卫着散布在女真聚落之间的哨所和渔村。

1467年，吉州豪族李施爱不满世祖直接派来的郡守，聚众两万起兵，杀死咸吉道观察使，最后被官军击溃。事后吉州被降级，镜城取而代之，成为北兵营所在地；1468年道名取咸兴与镜城之首字，定为咸镜道。1592年加藤清正占据北方，同年农历九月，北评事郑文孚率数百人在城外起兵。他假意顺从据守镜城的叛将鞠世弼，借机入城，在城中日夜操练义兵，随后诛灭鞠世弼和他往来的日军将官，把镜城变成反攻基地；义兵的骑兵和伏兵在吉州一带不断袭扰，拖到1593年初日军南撤。郑文孚后来被诬陷参与反对仁祖的密谋，1624年受刑而死；1665年朝廷为他平反，镜城为他建了显忠祠。1636年至1637年满洲骑兵攻抵海岸，战后镜城成为清朝藩属朝鲜的东北边镇。

en:
Yeongbyeon lies in the hills between tributaries of the Ch'ongch'on River, commanding the road north from Pyongyang toward the Yalu. Under Goryeo the country was split between the two walled districts of Yeonju and Muju, and in 1429 King Sejong merged them into the Yeongbyeon Grand Protectorate. The decision followed a survey by the veteran minister Hwang Hui, who inspected Yaksan and told the court the hill was the right place for the northern command. The seat went inside the old Cheorongseong, the 'iron jar fortress', whose linked walls ran from the town up onto Yaksan; three streams and fifty wells inside let a garrison sit out a long siege. The Sejong sillok gazetteer counted 1,121 households, 50 guard troops, 532 wing soldiers and 208 boatmen. The regional command moved to Ganggye in 1442, so in 1444 Yeongbyeon was a heavily walled northern town that had briefly lost the headquarters it had been built around.

The command returned in 1446 and was moved and restored several times over the following century. The east terrace of Yaksan above the fortress was counted among the eight celebrated views of the western provinces. In 1592 the Jeonju copy of the Veritable Records of Joseon was carried to nearby Mount Myohyang for safekeeping, and the monk Hyujeong of Pohyon Temple on the mountain was put in charge of the sixteen monk sects of all eight provinces and sent out the letters that called the monk armies into the war. In 1624 the general Yi Gwal marched out of Yeongbyeon in revolt and briefly held Hanyang before royal troops killed him. In the Manchu invasions of 1627 and 1636, besieging armies sat before Cheorongseong for days without forcing the steep walls and marched on. During the Hong Gyeong-rae rebellion of 1811, eight towns north of the Ch'ongch'on fell, and the rebels hoped to make the fortress their own base; the magistrate Oh Yeon-sang seized and beheaded Nam Ik-hyeon and more than ten other plotters inside the walls, and Yeongbyeon joined Kusong and Uiju among the towns the rebels never took.
zh:
宁边位于清川江支流之间的山地，扼守从平壤北上鸭绿江的大路。高丽时期这一带分属延州、抚州两座城；1429年，世宗将两地合并为宁边大都护府。此前老臣黄喜以平安道都体察使的身份踏勘药山，向朝廷建议以此地作为北方统帅的本营，设府正是采纳他的主张。治所设在旧铁瓮城内：这座高丽古城由本城和药山城等几重城墙连成一体，城内有三道溪水、五十口井，足以支撑长期围困。《世宗实录地理志》载当地有1121户，军额含侍卫军50人、翼军532人、船军208人。1442年都节制使营移往江界，因此1444年的宁边虽是高墙重锁的北方重镇，却暂时没有了为它而设的统帅机构。

1446年节制使营迁回，此后一个世纪里又屡有迁复。城中药山上的药山东台，被列为关西八景之一。1592年壬辰战争时，全州史库所藏《朝鲜王朝实录》一度移存附近的妙香山；山中普贤寺的僧人休静被任为八道十六宗都总摄，发文号召各道僧兵起兵参战。1624年，将领李适从宁边发兵叛乱，一度攻占汉阳，最终被官军诛杀。1627年和1636年两次胡乱中，后金与清军在铁瓮城下围攻数日，终究无法突入险墙，只能绕城南下。1811年洪景来之乱时，清川江以北八邑尽陷，叛军本打算以铁瓮城为据点；府使吴渊常先在城内捕杀南益显等十余名内应，据城死守，宁边与龟城、义州同为叛军未能攻陷的城镇。

en:
Gyeongju, called Seorabeol or Geumseong, was for nearly a thousand years the royal capital of Silla. After the unification of 668 the kings and great houses of the peninsula lived here: the Cheomseongdae observatory was built in the 640s, the nine-storey wooden pagoda of Hwangnyongsa rose in 645, and in the eighth century the minister Kim Daeseong founded Bulguksa and the Seokguram grotto. The Samguk Yusa counts 178,936 households in the city at its height, and a ninth-century Arab geography carried reports of it as far as Persia. When Silla submitted to Goryeo in 935 the court departed, and the city, renamed Gyeongju, served briefly as Goryeo's 'Eastern Capital' from 987 until the title was withdrawn in 1012. Mongol invaders burned Hwangnyongsa's great pagoda in the thirteenth century, and in early Joseon Neo-Confucian zealots smashed Buddhist images on Namsan. In 1444 Gyeongju was a quiet prefectural town of Gyeongsang, its fields and lanes scattered with the monuments of a vanished dynasty.

During the Japanese invasion of 1592 the Gyeongju plain became a battlefield: Kim Ho's local righteous army defeated a Japanese force at Nogok in August, but the old capital fell. Government troops under Pak Jin and the militia leader Gwon Eung-su retook the city that year after two sieges, bombarding its walls with the newly devised flying-thunder bombs. In May 1593 the invaders burned Bulguksa, where close to two thousand bays of halls went up in smoke; state-sponsored repairs began in 1604. In 1601 the Gyeongsang provincial office was moved from Gyeongju to Daegu, and the town never recovered its old rank. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries it remained a country seat of the Southerners faction and of old Silla-descended lineages, their yangban villages such as Yangdong lying among the royal tombs while traffic moved past the broken pagoda of Hwangnyongsa.
zh:
庆州古称徐罗伐、金城，近千年间一直是新罗的王都。668年新罗统一之后，国王与贵族大多聚居于此：瞻星台建于640年代，皇龙寺九重木塔于645年落成，8世纪大臣金大城又主持修建佛国寺与石窟庵。据《三国遗事》记载，极盛时城中有十七万八千九百三十六户，9世纪的阿拉伯地理书也把它的声名传到了波斯。935年新罗归降高丽，朝廷不复存在；改称庆州后，它在987年被高丽定为「东京」，1012年这一称号又被废止。13世纪蒙古入侵，皇龙寺大塔毁于兵火；进入朝鲜时代初期，性理学者中的排佛激进者还砸毁了南山的佛教造像。1444年的庆州是庆尚道一座安静的府城，田野街巷间散落着旧王朝的遗迹。

1592年壬辰倭乱，庆州平原沦为战场：金虎率领的本地义兵8月在露谷击败一支日军，但旧都终归陷落。朴晋的官军与义兵首领权应铢当年两度围城，用新造的飞击震天雷轰开城墙，收复庆州。1593年5月日军放火焚烧佛国寺，近两千间殿宇化为灰烬；国家修复工程于1604年启动。1601年，庆尚道监营从庆州迁往大邱，庆州再未能恢复旧日的行政地位。17、18世纪里，它是南人派和新罗旧族后裔的乡居之地，两班村落如良洞村坐落于王陵之间，行人车马从皇龙寺残破的塔址旁经过。

en:
Vidin guards a broad Danube crossing in the fertile, wine-growing north-west of Bulgaria. Roman Bononia stood here on the Danube frontier, and the medieval Bulgarian stronghold of Bdin grew around the Baba Vida citadel, raised between the tenth and fourteenth centuries. Basil II took the town only after an eight-month siege in 1003, when the local bishop betrayed it to him, and under the Second Empire the local Shishman dynasty gave Bulgaria an emperor when Michael Shishman was chosen tsar in 1323. In 1356 Ivan Stratsimir inherited the town and ruled the surrounding Vidin Tsardom as an independent Bulgarian ruler; Hungarian crusaders held it from 1365 to 1369, until Vladislav I of Wallachia drove them out. The Ottomans annexed Vidin after Bayezid's victory at Nicopolis in 1396 and made it a sanjak, and King Vladislav III's crusaders besieged it in vain in 1444.

Vidin then spent three centuries in the Ottoman-Habsburg border belt, trading wine, furs and barrelled caviar from the Danube. Austrian troops stormed it in October 1689 and deported thousands of its Muslims to Nikopol; when the Ottomans returned nine months later, only two or three hundred of the town's three thousand buildings were still standing. The frontier disorders of the 1790s raised Osman Pazvantoğlu, a former Janissary who ruled the Vidin region as his own from 1795 until his death in 1807 and built a mosque, a library and barracks in the town. His wars and the rival campaigns of other Ottoman commanders scattered the villagers of the Danube flats, and between 1812 and 1820 the authorities brought Bulgarian families back from Wallachia to resettle abandoned estates. In 1821 Vidin was a fortified Ottoman river town on a slowly reviving frontier.
zh:
维丁扼守保加利亚西北肥沃产酒之地的一处宽阔多瑙河渡口。罗马的波诺尼亚曾在此守卫多瑙河边防，中世纪保加利亚要塞布丁围绕巴巴维达城堡发展，城堡建于10至14世纪。1003年，巴西尔二世围城八个月，才靠当地主教叛卖拿下此城。第二帝国时期，本地的希什曼家族还出了一位君主：米哈伊尔·希什曼1323年被拥立为沙皇。1356年伊凡·斯拉齐米尔继承此城，以独立君主身份统治周围的维丁沙皇国；1365至1369年匈牙利十字军占据这里，最后被瓦拉几亚的弗拉迪斯拉夫一世赶走。1396年巴耶济德在尼科波尔获胜后，奥斯曼吞并维丁并设为桑贾克；1444年瓦迪斯瓦夫三世的十字军又围攻此城不克。

此后三个世纪，维丁处在奥斯曼与哈布斯堡的边界地带，输出葡萄酒、毛皮和多瑙河的桶装鱼子酱。1689年10月奥地利军队破城，把数千名穆斯林押往尼科波尔；九个月后奥斯曼人返回时，全城三千座建筑只剩两三百座尚存。1790年代的边疆动乱把前禁卫军奥斯曼·帕兹万特奥卢推上台面，他从1795年起把维丁地区当作私产统治，直到1807年死去，还在城中修建清真寺、图书馆和兵营。他的战争和其他奥斯曼军队的来回攻伐使多瑙河平原的村民离散；1812至1820年，当局招引从瓦拉几亚返回的保加利亚家庭重新垦殖废弃庄园。1821年的维丁，是缓慢恢复的边疆上一座设防的奥斯曼河城。

en:
Khara Narin Ula, the Black Narrow Mountain, is the range the Chinese call Lang Shan, the Wolf Mountains, the westernmost spine of the Yin range, covering the north-west corner of the Yellow River's Ordos Loop. Its southern face drops in cliffs to the irrigated back-loop plain, and the gentler northern slope runs out into the stony Gobi plateau. A gorge in the range, Gaoque, the High Tower pass, carried the long wall of the kings of Zhao and let Han armies march out against the Xiongnu. In 1444 no Ming garrison or magistrate remained in the back loop; Tatar, Oirat and Uriankhai herdsmen roamed the mountains and the desert pastures under the loose lordship of the Northern Yuan.

Dayan Khan's victories around 1510 brought the loop into his reunited Mongol realm, and the Ordos tumen took these lands for their grazing. They were the guardians of the Eight White Tents, the eight white gers that held the portable shrine of Genghis Khan, and from those tents, the ordo, they took their name. For a century their horsemen filed through the Lang Shan gorges on their way to raid the Ming frontier. Ligdan Khan scattered the Ordos in 1628, and the survivors submitted to Hong Taiji in 1635. The eastern range and the steppe reaching north toward the Gobi then passed to the Urad, enfeoffed as three jasak banners in 1648 and moved to the north bank of the Yellow River in 1649, a quiet Qing frontier facing the Khalkha across the desert.
zh:
哈拉纳林乌拉，蒙古语意为「黑色的窄山」，汉人称之为狼山，是阴山山脉最西端的一道山脊，屏护着黄河河套的西北角。山南是直落后套灌溉平原的峭壁，北坡平缓，逐渐没入砾石遍布的戈壁高原。山间峡谷中的高阙塞，是赵武灵王长城所经的关口，汉军也由这里出塞攻击匈奴。1444年，后套已无明朝的卫所与官吏，鞑靼、瓦剌、兀良哈牧民在狼山与北面的荒漠牧场上游牧，只在名义上尊奉北元大汗。

1510年前后，达延汗连战胜出，河套并入他重新统一的蒙古，鄂尔多斯万户以此为牧场。他们是八白室的守护者：八顶白色毡帐供奉着成吉思汗的移动灵帐，部落的名字就来自「斡耳朵」，即宫帐。此后百年间，骑兵不断穿过狼山口南下，袭扰明朝边境。1628年林丹汗西进，打散了鄂尔多斯部，余众在1635年归附皇太极。狼山东段及向北通往戈壁的草原后来归了乌喇特：1648年封授三个札萨克旗，1649年移牧黄河北岸，成为清代与大漠以北喀尔喀相望的安静边地。

en:
Jianchang follows the Anning River valley between the Dadu and Jinsha rivers, the open corridor from Sichuan into Yunnan and the Daliangshan Yi country. The Qiongdu people lived here before the Han set up Qiongdu county, and a local lord later held the Song title King of the Qiongdu. Nanzhao made the valley Jianchang Prefecture in the ninth century, Dali kept the name, and Mongol armies subdued it between 1253 and 1256. In 1275 the Yuan created Jianchang Route, seated at Jian'an near present-day Xichang. Marco Polo knew the country as Jiandu and recorded rods of gold for larger payments and half-catty pieces of molded salt used as small change. Ming forces took over in 1382. From 1394 Jianchang Guard was the seat of the Sichuan Regional Military Commission, directing five guards, eight battalions and four native offices; Chengdu lay 1,480 li to the northeast. In 1444 soldiers and native chiefs shared this frontier.

The Ming garrison order survived the dynastic change, though Qing officials gradually brought it under civilian administration. In 1728 the court made Jianchang the seat of Ningyuan Prefecture and Xichang County, replacing the old guard hierarchy with regular prefectural government. During the eighteenth century, missionaries of the Paris Foreign Missions Society brought Roman Catholicism into Ningyuan. The old name Jianchang remained in use beside the new Qing name.
zh:
建昌在大渡河与金沙江之间的安宁河谷，是四川进入云南、通向大凉山彝区的开阔走廊。汉人在此设县以前，当地住着邛都人；后来还有地方首领受宋朝封为邛都王。9世纪时，南诏把这里设为建昌府，大理国沿用其名。蒙古军1253至1256年征服此地，元朝1275年置建昌路，治所在今西昌附近的建安州。马可·波罗称这一带为建都，记载当地人用金条支付大数目的交易，又把半斤重的模制盐块当作零钱。明军1382年接管；1394年起，建昌卫成为四川行都指挥使司治所，统辖五卫、八所、四长官司，东北距成都一千四百八十里。1444年，驻军和土著首领共同维持这片边地。

明代卫所格局经历了明清易代，之后逐渐纳入文官行政。1728年，朝廷以建昌为宁远府和西昌县治所，用常规府县体系取代旧卫军建制。18世纪，巴黎外方传教会的传教士把罗马天主教传入宁远。旧名建昌仍与清代的新府名并用。

en:
Tikhvin began as the Predtechensky pogost on the Tikhvinka, where boats and portages linked the Volga basin with Lake Ladoga and the Baltic. A chronicle first notices it in 1383, when a wooden Church of the Dormition stood there, and church tradition connects that year with the image later called the Theotokos of Tikhvin: said to have been painted by Luke the Evangelist, it was believed to have appeared hovering over a lake nearby. In 1444 the place was still only a Novgorodian parish and a calling point on the portage road, where traders and craftsmen stopped between the Volga and the Baltic.

Vasily III paid for a stone Dormition Cathedral, raised in 1507-1515 to house the icon. In 1560 Ivan IV ordered the Dormition Monastery built on the river bank, with the smaller Vvedensky Convent and two trading settlements, all in a single spring and summer; by the mid-seventeenth century two log walls packed with earth and stone and nine towers ringed the grounds. In 1613 Swedish troops burned the posad, but on 25 May Leonty Artsybashev roused the townspeople, who held the monastery through the siege and then drove the Swedes out; the war ended with the Peace of Stolbovo in 1617. Tikhvin blacksmiths sold their iron abroad and the Tikhvin Fair became one of the largest in Russia. The Tikhvin water system, opened in 1811, joined the Volga to Ladoga by canal and in busy years carried as many as 6,000 vessels.
zh:
季赫温起于季赫温卡河畔的普列杰琴斯基教区聚落，附近的船只拖运路线把伏尔加河流域同拉多加湖、波罗的海连在一起。编年史在1383年首次提到它，当时那里有一座木制圣母安息教堂；教会传说把这一年与后来称作「季赫温圣母」的圣像联系起来，相传此像为福音书作者路加所绘，曾显现于附近的湖面之上。1444年时，这里还只是诺夫哥罗德的一个教区和拖运道上的停靠点，往来伏尔加河与波罗的海之间的商人和工匠在此歇脚。

瓦西里三世出资修建石造圣母安息大教堂，1507至1515年建成，用以安放这幅圣像。1560年，伊凡四世下令在河岸修建圣母安息修道院，连同较小的圣母进堂女修道院和两个工商业聚落，全部在一个春夏之内建成；到17世纪中叶，修道院四周已有两道内部填实土石的原木墙和九座塔楼。1613年，瑞典军队焚毁城镇聚落，列昂季·阿尔齐巴舍夫在5月25日唤起市民，他们退入修道院顶住围城，随后把瑞典人赶走；战争以1617年的斯托尔博沃和约结束。季赫温铁匠打造的铁器销到海外，季赫温集市也成为俄国最大的集市之一。1811年开通的季赫温水系以运河连接伏尔加河与拉多加湖，繁忙年份通行船只多达六千艘。

en:
Plovdiv spreads over seven syenite hills beside the Maritsa in the fertile Upper Thracian plain. Philip II of Macedon founded Philippopolis there in 342 BC, and under Rome the town was capital of the province of Thracia, where the Via Militaris met roads running to the Danube, the Aegean and the Black Sea; a chronicler of the Fourth Crusade called it the third city of the Byzantine Empire after Constantinople and Thessalonica. It changed hands repeatedly in the Bulgarian-Byzantine wars, Kaloyan destroyed it in 1206, and it served for a time as the seat of the Latin Duchy of Philippopolis before Ivan Asen II took it in 1230. Ottoman forces under Lala Şahin Pasha seized it in 1364 and called it Filibe. The town was the early Ottoman centre of Rumelia before Sofia took that role, while remaining chief town of its own sanjak. In November 1444, after Varna, Filibe was a securely Ottoman road and caravan town in productive Bulgarian Orthodox country.

In the Ottoman centuries Filibe became one of the richest market towns of the inland Balkans. Caravans between Edirne, Istanbul, Sofia and Belgrade lodged in its khans, and the Maritsa valley carried out the grain, livestock and crafts of the Thracian plain. Soon after the conquest the Ottomans pulled down the cathedral of St Petka and built the nine-domed Dzhumaya Friday Mosque on its site in 1363-1364, the first of the mosques, madrasas, caravanserais, bazaars and hammams that filled the town; the Imaret Mosque followed in the 1440s. From the fifteenth century to the end of the seventeenth most of its people were Muslims, though Sephardic Jews, Armenians and Bulgarian and Greek Orthodox Christians traded there too. Evliya Çelebi, visiting in the seventeenth century, counted many mosques, minarets, khans, baths and schools and ranked the city among the notable towns of Rumelia. In 1821 Filibe remained the seat of a sanjak and a rich market on the empire's main Balkan road.
zh:
普罗夫迪夫位于肥沃的上色雷斯平原，城区铺展在马里查河畔的七座正长岩丘陵上。公元前342年，马其顿王腓力二世在此兴建菲利普波利斯；罗马时代它是色雷斯行省首府，军事大道在此与通往多瑙河、爱琴海和黑海的道路相接。第四次十字军的一位编年史家称它是拜占庭帝国第三大城，仅次于君士坦丁堡和塞萨洛尼基。它在拜占庭与保加利亚的战争中多次易手，1206年被卡洛扬摧毁，一度成为十字军建立的菲利普波利斯公国都城，1230年被伊凡·阿森二世攻占。1364年，拉拉·沙欣帕夏率奥斯曼军攻占此城，改称菲利贝。它是奥斯曼人在鲁米利亚最早的统治中心，后来这一地位让给索非亚，但始终是本桑贾克的首城。1444年11月瓦尔纳战役之后，菲利贝已稳在奥斯曼治下，是丰裕的保加利亚东正教土地上的道路与商队城镇。

奥斯曼世纪里，菲利贝成为巴尔干内陆最富庶的市场城镇之一。往返埃迪尔内、伊斯坦布尔、索非亚和贝尔格莱德的商队在它的客店投宿，马里查河谷运出色雷斯的谷物、牲畜和手工业品。征服之初，奥斯曼人拆毁圣佩特卡大教堂，于1363至1364年在原址建起九穹顶的朱马亚聚礼清真寺；此后清真寺、伊斯兰学校、商队旅馆、巴扎和浴室遍布全城，1440年代又建成伊马雷特清真寺。从15世纪到17世纪末，菲利贝居民以穆斯林为多，也有塞法迪犹太人、亚美尼亚人以及保加利亚和希腊的东正教徒在此经商。17世纪埃夫利亚·切莱比到访时，数出城中众多清真寺、宣礼塔、客店、浴室和学校，把它列为鲁米利亚的名城之一。1821年，菲利贝仍是桑贾克治所，也是帝国巴尔干干道上的富庶市场。

en:
Cuenca crowns a narrow rock ridge squeezed between the gorges of the Júcar and the Huécar in the Iberian System. Muslims built the fortress of Qunka there, ringed by about a kilometre of wall, and Alfonso VIII of Castile took it only after a siege that ran from Epiphany to 21 September 1177; the garrison held the citadel into October. The Fuero of Cuenca became one of the most admired town charters in Castile, a bishopric followed in 1183, and Alfonso X granted civic rank in 1257. French masons raised the cathedral in an Anglo-Norman Gothic new to Castile, and in the fifteenth century townsmen built the hanging houses, their balconies projecting out over the Huécar gorge. Flocks and woollen cloth paid for the building boom and pushed new quarters down the river slopes. In 1444 Cuenca was a prosperous Catholic Castilian wool town, its defence still tied to the citadel on its rock.

The southern town of Belmonte, in the same province, produced two famous Castilians: Juan Pacheco, born there in 1419, who as marquis of Villena and master of Santiago dominated the court of Henry IV and helped depose him in effigy at the Farce of Ávila, and the Augustinian poet and theologian Fray Luis de León, born there in 1527, who held a chair at Salamanca and spent four years in the prisons of the Inquisition before he was cleared. Cuenca's Jewish quarter ended with the expulsion of 1492, and its last large crypto-Jewish trials ran from 1718 to 1725. Woollen cloth and tapestries made the city famous in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries until the trade collapsed in the seventeenth and emptied its streets. In the War of the Spanish Succession Anglo-Portuguese troops took Cuenca for the Habsburg claimant in June 1706, lost it in August, and Archduke Charles held it again briefly in 1710; the town's loyalty to Philip V earned it the title 'Most Faithful and Heroic'. During the Peninsular War French forces sacked Cuenca more than nine times.
zh:
昆卡雄踞在伊比利亚山脉中一道狭窄的岩脊上，胡卡尔河与韦卡尔河在两侧切出深峡。穆斯林在这里筑起约一公里长城墙环绕的昆卡要塞，卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索八世从1177年主显节起围攻，直到9月21日才破城，守军又在城寨里守到10月。《昆卡法典》后来成为卡斯蒂利亚最受推崇的城市宪章之一，1183年设主教区，1257年阿方索十世授予城市地位。法国工匠把大教堂修造成卡斯蒂利亚人还很陌生的盎格鲁-诺曼哥特式；15世纪，居民又在韦卡尔峡谷上方造起悬屋，阳台直接探出峡谷之上。牧群和毛织业为这场营建热潮出资，也把新街区推向河谷坡地。1444年的昆卡是一座富庶的天主教卡斯蒂利亚毛织城镇，防务仍系于岩脊上的城寨。

省境南部的贝尔蒙特镇出过两位卡斯蒂利亚名人：1419年出生的胡安·帕切科，他受封比列纳侯爵、出任圣地亚哥骑士团首领，长期左右恩里克四世的朝政，也是「阿维拉闹剧」废立仪式的主谋之一；1527年出生的奥斯定会诗人、神学家路易斯·德·莱昂，他在萨拉曼卡大学任教席，被宗教裁判所关押四年才洗清罪名。昆卡的犹太区随1492年的驱逐令而消亡，当地最后一轮大规模隐秘犹太教徒审判发生在1718年至1725年。15至16世纪，毛料和挂毯让昆卡闻名，17世纪产业崩溃，街区为之一空。西班牙王位继承战争中，英葡联军1706年6月替哈布斯堡觊觎者拿下昆卡，8月即告失守，卡尔大公1710年又短暂占据；昆卡因效忠费利佩五世获「至信至勇」称号。半岛战争期间，法军先后九次以上洗劫昆卡。

en:
Romsdal is the fjord country of western Norway where the Romsdalsfjord meets the steep Romsdalen valley, through which the Rauma river runs down from the mountains to the sea; the valley has always been the road between the western fjords and the inland. In the Viking age the island of Veøya, where the inner sea lanes forked, held the district's first market and probably the seat of Jarl Ragnvald of Møre, and a small stone church was raised there over a heathen site at the end of the 1100s. On 7 July 1162 the fjord itself was the scene of the battle of Sekken: King Håkon Herdebrei was killed fighting Erling Skakke, and the crown passed to the young Magnus Erlingsson. In 1444 Romsdal belonged to the Norwegian crown within the Kalmar Union, a Catholic land of free fishermen and farmers under the diocese of Nidaros, with Veøya and the fishing haven of Bud as its main settlements.

By 1604 Molde had become a timber-and-herring harbour trading with Holland and was made a loading place under Trondheim. During the Kalmar War some 300 Scottish mercenaries landed at Isfjorden in 1612 and marched inland through the valley to join the Swedes; Norwegian peasants ambushed and nearly annihilated them at Kringen. The treaty of Roskilde in 1658 carried the Swedish frontier down to the Romsdalsfjord, but the farmers refused Swedish taxes and conscription, and the treaty of Copenhagen restored the old border two years later. Molde became the governor's seat, with the governor residing at Moldegård from 1705, and on 29 June 1742 Christian VI granted the town full market-town rights despite protests from Bergen and Trondheim. In 1814 the district followed Norway into the union with Sweden.
zh:
鲁姆斯达尔是挪威西部的峡湾之乡：鲁姆斯达尔峡湾与陡峻的鲁姆斯达尔山谷相接，劳马河穿山出谷、奔流入海，这条山谷自古就是西部峡湾通往内陆的要道。维京时代，扼守内海航道分岔口的韦于亚岛形成了本区最早的市集，很可能还是默勒伯爵拉格瓦尔德的驻地；12世纪末，岛上在异教圣地建起一座小石堂。1162年7月7日，峡湾中爆发塞肯海战，国王哈康二世与厄尔林·斯卡克交战时阵亡，王冠落入年轻的马格努斯五世手中。1444年的鲁姆斯达尔属卡尔马联盟中的挪威王冠，是尼达罗斯教区治下天主教自由渔民和农民的土地，韦于亚和渔港布德是主要聚落。

1604年，靠木材和鲱鱼与荷兰通商的莫尔德成为特隆赫姆管辖的装卸港。1612年卡尔马战争期间，约三百名苏格兰雇佣兵在伊斯菲尤伦登陆，沿山谷东进去投瑞典，在克林根遭挪威农民伏击，几乎被全歼。1658年《罗斯基勒条约》把瑞典边界推到鲁姆斯达尔峡湾，农民却拒缴瑞典赋税、拒服兵役，两年后《哥本哈根条约》恢复旧界。莫尔德成为鲁姆斯达尔长官驻地，1705年起长官住进莫尔德庄园；1742年6月29日，克里斯蒂安六世不顾卑尔根和特隆赫姆反对，授予莫尔德完整市镇权。1814年，鲁姆斯达尔随挪威并入与瑞典的联盟。

en:
Narbonne first grew powerful as a Roman road junction and Mediterranean port. Founded in 118 BC as the colony of Narbo Martius, it became the capital of Gallia Narbonensis, where the Via Domitia toward Spain branched from the Via Aquitania toward the Atlantic. After centuries as a centre of Visigothic Septimania, the Frankish conquest of 759 left the archbishop and viscount sharing rule. In the twelfth century Viscountess Ermengarde kept a court frequented by troubadours, and the city's Jewish exegetical school drew scholars from across Latin Christendom. Around 1300 Narbonne had perhaps 30,000 people and was the leading cloth-working town in Languedoc, sending woollens to Spain and the Levant. The Aude then turned against the port. A flood in 1320 destroyed the river dam, the harbour began to silt, and the Black Death, Free Companies and the Black Prince's raid of 1355 further reduced the city. In 1444 Narbonne was still one of France's oldest archiepiscopal sees, but it had become a half-empty former port whose viscounts lived elsewhere.

In 1447 the viscounty was sold to Gaston IV of Foix. The dynasty soon reached a royal marriage: Germaine of Foix, daughter of Viscount John and granddaughter of Gaston, married King Ferdinand II of Aragon in 1505. Cardinal Giulio de' Medici held the archbishopric from 1515 until he was elected Pope Clement VII in 1523. The unfinished Cathedral of Saints Justus and Pastor shows the city's contracted ambitions. Begun in 1272, it has a choir vault 41 metres high, among the highest in France, but the city walls blocked the planned nave and transept and the work stopped after 1354. From the sixteenth century Narbonne dredged and rebuilt its old channel as the Canal de la Robine; wine boats used the waterway, which finally joined the Canal du Midi in 1776.
zh:
纳博讷最早凭借罗马大道交会处和地中海港口兴起。它建于公元前118年，初名纳尔博·马提乌斯殖民地，后来成为纳尔博南西斯行省首府；通往西班牙的多弥提亚大道在这里与通往大西洋的阿基坦大道分岔。西哥特统治时期，这里是塞蒂马尼亚的中心；759年法兰克人收复后，城市由大主教与子爵共同治理。12世纪，女子爵埃芒加德的宫廷常有行吟诗人出入，城中的犹太解经学校也吸引着拉丁基督教世界的学者。1300年前后，纳博讷约有三万居民，是朗格多克首屈一指的呢绒织造城镇，毛料远销西班牙和黎凡特。后来奥德河毁了这座港口：1320年洪水冲毁河坝，港湾开始淤塞，黑死病、自由佣兵和黑太子1355年的劫掠又使城市进一步衰败。1444年，纳博讷仍保有法兰西最古老的总教区之一，却已是一座半空的旧港，子爵一家也久居外地。

1447年，子爵领被卖给富瓦伯爵加斯东四世。这个家族很快通过婚姻接近王位：子爵让的女儿、加斯东的孙女热尔梅娜于1505年嫁给阿拉贡国王斐迪南二世。1515年至1523年，枢机主教朱利奥·德·美第奇担任纳博讷大主教，随后当选教皇，称克雷芒七世。未完工的圣茹斯特与圣帕斯托尔大教堂显示出这座城市收缩后的抱负。大教堂1272年动工，歌坛拱顶高达41米，属于法兰西最高的一批拱顶，但城墙挡住了规划中的正殿和耳堂，1354年之后工程便停止。16世纪起，纳博讷人疏浚并重修旧河道，建成罗比讷运河，酒船沿河道出入；1776年，这条运河终于与米迪运河连通。

en:
La Mancha is the dry southern tableland of Castile, crossed by the Guadiana and bounded by the Montes de Toledo and the Sierra Morena, a country of grain fields, sheep walks and windmills. After the Reconquista its towns and pastures went chiefly to the military Orders of Santiago and Calatrava; the masters of Calatrava made Almagro their seat, where Alfonso X held the Cortes in 1273. Alfonso X also founded Villa Real in 1255, a royal town planted inside the order's lands, and John II raised it to Ciudad Real in 1420 after its militia fought for him against the orders. The order's mines at Almadén produced cinnabar and quicksilver. In 1444 Ciudad Real was still a small royal town overshadowed by Almagro, while the plains lived from grain and sheep.

In the succession crisis after 1474 the Pachecos of Villena and the two orders backed Juana la Beltraneja and her Portuguese husband, until the 1479 Treaty of Alcáçovas confirmed Isabella and Ferdinand. Ciudad Real's own hero of that age was Hernán Pérez del Pulgar, born there in 1451 and called el de las Hazañas, 'the man of deeds': a captain in the Granada war who slipped into Granada by night with fifteen horsemen in 1490, nailed an Ave María placard to the door of the Great Mosque and set fire to the silk bazaar before fighting his way back to the camp at Santa Fe. After the Comuneros' defeat the order estates, Almadén included, passed to the Crown in 1523 and were leased to the Fuggers; Almadén quicksilver went through Seville to the American silver mines for the amalgamation process, and from 1566 convicts worked its poisonous shafts, until the Crown took the mines back in 1645. Almagro kept the Fuggers' stone warehouses and built its corral de comedias in the seventeenth century, a courtyard theatre for Golden Age plays; the conquistador Diego de Almagro is traditionally said to have been born there, and the town served as provincial capital from 1750 to 1761. Cervantes set Don Quixote's adventures among La Mancha's windmills in 1605 and 1615, and Charles III founded Spain's first mining school at Almadén in 1777. French troops took Ciudad Real in 1809 and Almadén in 1810.
zh:
拉曼查是卡斯蒂利亚南部干燥的高原，瓜迪亚纳河流贯其间，北界托莱多山，南接莫雷纳山，乡野间是粮田、牧道和风车。再征服运动之后，这里的城镇和牧场主要封给圣地亚哥和卡拉特拉瓦两个骑士团；卡拉特拉瓦的首领把治所设在阿尔马格罗，阿方索十世1273年还在那里召开议会。1255年，阿方索十世在骑士团领地之中建起王室直辖的皇家镇，1420年该镇民兵在内战中支持胡安二世，国王升其为城市，改名雷阿尔城。骑士团在阿尔马登的矿山出产辰砂和水银。1444年，雷阿尔城还是一座被阿尔马格罗盖过锋芒的小王领城镇，高原靠谷物和绵羊为生。

1474年后的继承危机中，比列纳的帕切科家族和两个骑士团支持胡安娜·贝尔特拉内哈和她的葡萄牙丈夫，直到1479年《阿尔卡索瓦斯条约》确认伊莎贝尔与费尔南多获胜。雷阿尔城为这个朝代贡献的人物是1451年出生于此的埃尔南·佩雷斯·德尔·普尔加，绰号「建功者」：他是格拉纳达战争中的卡斯蒂利亚队长，1490年率十五名骑士夜入格拉纳达，把写有「万福玛利亚」的告示钉在大清真寺门上，又放火烧了丝绸市场，才杀出城去，退回圣菲的王军大营。公社起义失败后，包括阿尔马登在内的骑士团地产于1523年并入王室，租给富格尔家族经营；阿尔马登的水银经塞维利亚运往美洲银矿，供混汞法炼银之用，1566年起苦役犯被送进有毒的矿坑，1645年矿山收归王室。阿尔马格罗留有富格尔家族的石砌仓库，17世纪又建起喜剧剧场，演出黄金世纪的戏剧；相传征服者迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗就出生在这座镇子，1750年至1761年它还做过省会。塞万提斯在1605年和1615年的《堂吉诃德》里，把主人公的冒险放在拉曼查的风车之间；1777年，卡洛斯三世在阿尔马登创办西班牙第一所矿业学院。1809年法军攻占雷阿尔城，1810年阿尔马登失守。

en:
Soria sits high on the upper Douro, on the pasture country where the kingdoms of Castile, Aragon and Navarre met. Alfonso I of Aragon, the Battler, conquered and resettled it between 1109 and 1114, and it passed to Castile in 1134. Kings kept coming back: Alfonso VIII was born here in 1155, and in 1257 the offer of the crown of the Holy Roman Empire reached Alfonso X at his court here. In 1375 the deposed James IV of Majorca died and was buried here, and that same year the future John I of Castile married Eleanor of Aragon in the same church. Its fueros put the town in the hands of twelve noble lineages, the Doce Linajes, who grew rich on wool: Soria stood at the head of several royal drovers' roads, and after the Mesta was created in 1273 it organised the summer shearing of the transhumant flocks and sent the clip through Burgos to the northern ports. Its Jewish quarter, about a thousand strong in the census of 1290, handled much of the trade. In 1369 Henry II gave the town to Bertrand du Guesclin in payment for his mercenaries, and the Frenchman's troops had to storm it. In 1444 Soria was a wealthy wool town ruled by its noble lineages, though the frontier wars that fed it were already over.

The union of Castile and Aragon in 1479 stripped Soria of its border trade, and the expulsion of the Jews in 1492 dispersed its merchant houses. The town remained a lordship of royal princes until 1539, then shrank into a quiet provincial capital of Romanesque churches and Renaissance palaces: the Hospitallers' San Juan de Duero keeps a thirteenth-century cloister mixing several styles, and Santo Domingo a carved doorway with a rare image of the Trinity. In 1808 the city raised a Numantine Volunteers battalion; on 22 November Marshal Ney's troops occupied Soria and sacked it for three days. His 20,000 men lingered while the Battle of Tudela was fought nearby, and Castaños and his army slipped out of the trap.
zh:
索里亚雄踞杜罗河上游的高原牧场，正当卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡与纳瓦拉三国交界处。1109年至1114年间，阿拉贡国王阿方索一世（斗士）攻占并重新移民此地，1134年并入卡斯蒂利亚。君主们一次次回到这里：1155年阿方索八世出生于此；1257年，神圣罗马帝国帝位的推举送达在此驻跸的阿方索十世；1375年，被废黜的马略卡国王海梅四世客死并安葬于此，同年，未来的卡斯蒂利亚国王胡安一世也在当地的教堂迎娶阿拉贡的莱昂诺尔。索里亚的特许状把市政交给十二支贵族世家（「十二族」），他们的财富来自羊毛：城市扼守数条皇家牧道的起点，1273年梅斯塔荣誉会成立后，由它组织转场羊群的夏季剪毛，再把羊毛经布尔戈斯运往北方各港。本地犹太社区在1290年普查中约有千人，承担了其中大部分贸易。1369年卡斯蒂利亚内战中，恩里克二世把索里亚送给贝特朗·杜·盖克兰以抵雇佣兵的军饷，这位法国统帅的部队只得强攻入城。1444年的索里亚是一座由贵族世家治理的富庶羊毛城镇，只是养肥它的边境战争已成往事。

1479年卡斯蒂利亚与阿拉贡合一，索里亚失去了边镇之利；1492年驱逐犹太人，又散去了它的商人家族。城市作为王族封邑一直保留到1539年，之后缩成一座安静的省会，城中多的是罗曼式教堂和文艺复兴式宫邸：医院骑士团的圣胡安·德·杜埃罗修道院保留着一座13世纪回廊，混用了好几种风格；圣多明我教堂的雕花门楣上则有一幅罕见的三位一体圣像。1808年，城市组建努曼西亚志愿营起兵抗法；11月22日，内伊元帅的部队进占索里亚，在城中盘踞三日、大肆劫掠。他的两万人马在索里亚逗留不去，附近正进行图德拉战役，卡斯塔尼奥斯的军队反倒因此逃出了包围圈。

en:
The Welayta highlands fill the broken country between the Bilate and the Omo, where the rains turn the valleys to marsh and coffee runs wild in the mountain woods. Their Omotic-speaking Wolayta people were ruled by kings titled kawo. Local tradition carries the kingdom back to about 1251 and counts more than fifty kings across four dynasties; some scholars equate it with the medieval kingdom of Damot and its remembered Kawo Motolomi, named in the Life of Saint Tekle Haymanot as a raider of the Christian north to whom the saint's mother was surrendered, and some accounts make the saint Motolomi's own son. In 1444 the Malla kawo still reigned beyond the reach of Christian Ethiopia and the Muslim lowland lords, his people keeping their old rites among the coffee forests and cattle pastures.

Imam Ahmad Gragn's Adal army occupied the country for a time in the sixteenth century and then withdrew; the Adal chronicler Arab Faqih himself called the land too marshy and waterlogged to hold. The Oromo migrations that followed cost the kingdom its subject lands, and in the upheaval the Malla dynasty gave way to the Tigre Malla line. In the seventeenth century Kawo Gazenja fought back and won a string of battles against Oromo raiders. The Wolayta kept their kings and their old beliefs in the mountains long after the lowlands around them had changed hands.
zh:
瓦莱提（瓦莱塔）高地占据比拉特河与奥莫河之间的破碎地带，雨水把谷地泡成沼泽，咖啡在山林里野生。当地的瓦莱塔人说奥莫语族语言，统治者号称「卡沃」。按本地传统，王国始于约1251年，四个王朝相传五十多位君王；一些学者把它等同于中世纪的达莫特王国和传说中的卡沃·莫托洛米。《圣特克莱·海马诺特行传》把莫托洛米写成北上侵扰基督教地区的人，圣徒的母亲被送交给他，还有说法称圣徒就是他的儿子。1444年，马拉王朝的卡沃仍在这片基督教埃塞俄比亚和低地穆斯林领主都鞭长莫及的山乡在位，族人在咖啡林和牧场间守着旧有仪轨。

16世纪，伊玛目艾哈迈德·格兰的阿达尔军队一度占领此地，随后撤走；阿达尔编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫自己也说，这里过于泥泞多沼，难以立足。随之而来的奥罗莫迁徙使王国丢掉大片属地，动荡中马拉王朝被蒂格雷·马拉一系取代。17世纪，卡沃·加曾贾反攻，对奥罗莫袭掠者连战连捷。周围低地几度易主之后很久，瓦莱塔人仍在群山中保留着自己的国王和旧信仰。

en:
Kaffa lies on the wet, forested southern flank of the Ethiopian Highlands, bounded by the Gojeb River to the north and the Omo to the east; near Anderaccha the Guma flows into the Gichey. The shade forests of these mountains were the native home of the coffee tree, and Muslim traders carried the beans out along the Zeila and Berbera roads to Arabia, where roasting and brewing first took hold in the fifteenth century. The fertile highland valleys could yield three harvests a year. In 1444 the sacred king, the tato, ruled the Kefficho people from mountain forests that are hard to enter. Hunters, leatherworkers and blacksmiths held hereditary duties, and the hunters, the manjo, had a king of their own appointed by the tato to guard his compounds and the gates into the kingdom; Muslim traders and Ethiopian Christians already lived here before the court itself turned Christian.

Oral tradition dates the kingdom to about 1390, when Minjo replaced the earlier Mato dynasty and made Bonga his first royal seat; later kings ruled from Anderaccha. In the sixteenth century the Emperor Sarsa Dengel persuaded the court to accept Christianity, and the church of St George at Baha kept a tabot bearing his name, but the faith largely faded again in later centuries. From 1675, under Gali Ginocho, the tatos spent a century and a half pushing outward and annexing the Gimira lands of She, Benesho and Majango. The Mecha Oromo took everything north of the Gojeb in the eighteenth century, but the forested core held. Tato Shagi Sherocho then brought Welayta and Konta under control and pushed the frontier to the Omo and the Denchya, and under Hoti Gaocho, whose reign ran from 1798 to 1821, Kaffa reached its greatest extent.
zh:
咖法（亦译卡法）在埃塞俄比亚高原南部湿润多林的山坡上，北以戈杰布河为界，东接奥莫河；安德拉恰附近，古马河汇入吉切河。这里的遮阴林是咖啡树的原生地，穆斯林商人把咖啡豆经泽伊拉和柏培拉商路带到阿拉伯，15世纪时烘焙煮饮的做法正是在那里流行开来。高地谷地土壤肥沃，一年可三熟。1444年，具有宗教权威、称「塔托」的国王在这片难以进入的山地森林中治理卡菲乔人。猎户、皮匠和铁匠各有世袭职分；其中猎户曼乔人有自己的王，由塔托任命，负责守卫王宫和通往王国的各处关口。宫廷自己皈依基督教之前，穆斯林商人和埃塞俄比亚基督徒已经住在王国境内。

口述传统把王国的开端定在约1390年：明乔取代更早的马托王朝，以本加为第一个王都，后来的国王改在安德拉恰理政。16世纪，埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔说动咖法宫廷接受基督教，巴哈的圣乔治教堂供奉着刻有他名字的塔博特，但这种信仰在以后几个世纪里又大致衰落。从1675年在位的加利·吉诺乔起，历代塔托用一个半世纪向外扩张，吞并谢、贝内绍、马扬戈等吉米拉人的土地。18世纪梅查·奥罗莫人夺取戈杰布河以北的全部属地，密林核心却守住了。塔托·沙吉·谢罗乔随后控制瓦莱提和孔塔，把边界推到奥莫河与登奇亚河；到霍蒂·高乔在位时（1798—1821年），咖法的版图达到最大。

en:
Illubabor lies in the forested western Ethiopian highlands, where the headwaters of the Baro gather and run west towards the Nile. To the east, in the Gibe country, lay Ennarea, strongest of the Gonga kingdoms. It broke from Damot in the fourteenth century and became the leading power of the non-Muslim south, forcing Kaffa and Bosa to pay tribute and sending its own gold, slaves and cattle to the Ethiopian emperors; a song for the Emperor Yeshaq I already records those payments in the early fifteenth century. In 1444 the Hinnario court kept its own institutions while tied to the Christian empire to the north.

Between 1578 and 1586 the Borana Oromo overran most of Gibe and bound themselves into the Sadacha federation, which fought Ennarea for the next hundred and thirty years. After the Sadacha took the kingdom in 1588, the Ennarean elite accepted Christianity in the same year that the Emperor Sarsa Dengel campaigned south of the Nile; an attack in 1594 nevertheless cost them the land between the Gibe and the Gibe Ennarea. Cut off from the empire, the old dynasty weakened, and in the mid-seventeenth century a Kaffa royal clan seized power and Kaffa and Sheka broke away. The Emperor Iyasu I reached Ennarea on campaign in 1704, but about six years later the Sadacha overthrew King Shisafotchi. He led the survivors south across the Gojeb into Kaffa, where their exile kingdom was subdued early in the nineteenth century. The Oromo who stayed turned from cattle to the plough and built five new kingdoms on the old Ennarean lands, Limmu-Ennarea among them.
zh:
伊路巴博位于埃塞俄比亚西部林木茂密的高地，巴罗河源流在此汇聚，向西流向尼罗河。东面的吉贝地区有贡加人最强的王国伊那瑞亚。它在14世纪脱离达莫特，成为南方非穆斯林诸邦的头号强权，迫使咖法和博萨纳贡，又把黄金、奴隶和牛只送往埃塞俄比亚皇帝那里；15世纪初一首为耶沙克一世皇帝而作的歌已唱到这些贡物。1444年，伊那瑞亚的辛纳里奥宫廷保留着自己的制度，同时臣属于北方的基督教帝国。

1578至1586年，博尔纳奥罗莫人席卷吉贝大部，结成萨达查联盟，此后同伊那瑞亚打了130年。1588年萨达查攻占伊那瑞亚后，就在埃塞俄比亚皇帝萨尔·登格尔进兵青尼罗河以南的同一年，伊那瑞亚精英接受了基督教；1594年萨达查再攻，伊那瑞亚仍失去吉贝河与吉贝·伊那瑞亚河之间的土地。同帝国的联系被切断，旧王朝日益衰弱，17世纪中叶一个咖法王室氏族夺取政权，咖法和谢卡相继脱离。1704年，伊亚苏一世皇帝在征战中抵达伊那瑞亚，但约六年后萨达查人推翻国王希萨福奇。他率残部南越戈杰布河进入咖法，这个流亡王国在19世纪初被咖法征服。留下的奥罗莫人弃牧从耕，在旧伊那瑞亚土地上建起五个新王国，利穆-伊那瑞亚便是其中之一。

en: Gambela is the hot riverine lowland between the Openo-Baro and the Akobo, where streams from the Ethiopian Highlands drain toward the Upper Nile. Between the twelfth and fifteenth centuries the ancestors of the Anuak, a Luo Nilotic people, moved south and east from the Gezira between the Blue and White Niles and settled along the Baro and Gilo. Unlike their cattle-keeping Nilotic neighbours they were farmers as well as herdsmen, and lived in scattered riverside villages. In 1444 these villages held the country, which highland Ethiopian rulers knew chiefly as a hunting ground for slaves rather than a province they taxed directly. Raiders from the highlands kept coming down to the Baro for the rest of the period.
zh: 甘贝拉是奥佩诺-巴罗河与阿科博河之间炎热的河畔低地，埃塞俄比亚高地的河川从这里流向尼罗上游。阿努亚克人属尼罗特卢奥人群，12至15世纪，其祖先从青尼罗河与白尼罗河之间的杰济拉向南、向东迁徙，在巴罗河与吉洛河沿岸定居。同其他专事畜牧的尼罗特邻人不同，他们既放牧也耕种，住在分散的河畔村落里。1444年，正是这些村落据有这片土地；高地的埃塞俄比亚统治者主要把这里当作掠取奴隶的地方，而非直接征税的辖地。本时期余下的时间里，高地袭掠者仍不断下到巴罗河一带来。

en:
Hadiya is the fertile, well-watered plateau south of Shewa, its ridges around Angacha above the Rift Valley lakes given over to grain, orchards and horse pasture. Its people were Muslims like the lords of Zeila and Adal, Cushitic-speaking Hadiyya, Halaba and Kebena with the Semitic-speaking Silte among them, and their ruler bore the title garad. The Arab geographer al-Umari in the fourteenth century described a country rich in cereals, fruit and horses, whose people used pieces of iron as money and could raise forty thousand horsemen. It became an Ethiopian tributary after Amda Seyon ravaged it when King Amano, urged on by a Muslim preacher named Bel'am, refused to submit.

Hadiya and the empire came to blows again in the 1440s. Garad Mahiko refused tribute to Zara Yaqob, who deposed him through one of his own followers in favour of his uncle Bamo; fleeing towards Adal, Mahiko was killed by pursuing troops, and his head and limbs went back to the imperial camp. The princess Eleni, daughter of the king of Hadiya, was baptized and married to Zara Yaqob. She became empress, called the Queen of Zeila, took the title of queen mother under the next emperor, and from 1507 to 1516 held the regency for the young Lebna Dengel. It was she who sent Mateus the Armenian to Portugal and the Pope, seeking allies against Adal and the Ottomans; she died in 1522. Sultan Badlay of Adal tried to answer Hadiya's grievances by invasion and fell at Gomit in 1445.

When the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares passed through in the 1520s, Hadiya was still thickly wooded country, its roads cut through the trees, a quiet tributary paying cattle to Lebna Dengel. Ahmad Gragn's Muslim governor opened the land without a fight; the people told the imam the emperor's men forbade them swords and saddled horses and took a girl from them yearly. In 1569 Sarsa Dengel marched against the tribute-refusing Garad Aze; Harar sent five hundred armoured Malassay, but Aze's men, weakened in the Oromo migrations, refused to fight. The Oromo had overrun its eastern marches, whose Arsi later claimed Hadiya descent. Early in the seventeenth century Garad Sidi Muhammad routed Susenyos's troops and the forests kept Hadiya free: the Portuguese Fernandez was turned back in 1613, and the Czech traveller Remedius Prutky in 1751 still found an independent Muslim kingdom south of Abyssinia.
zh:
哈迪亚是绍阿以南肥沃湿润的高原，昂加查一带的丘陵俯瞰东非大裂谷湖群，坡地上谷田、果木和马场相连。居民多说库希特语，有哈迪亚人、哈拉巴人、克贝纳人，也有说闪米特语的西尔提人，和泽伊拉、阿达尔的统治者同为穆斯林，君主号称「加拉德」。14世纪的阿拉伯地理学家欧麦里记载，此地盛产五谷、果木和马匹，民间以铁片为通货，能出骑兵四万。后来国王阿马诺在穆斯林传道者贝拉姆鼓动下拒不屈服，阿姆达·塞约恩纵兵蹂躏，哈迪亚被收为藩属。

15世纪40年代，哈迪亚与帝国再次开战。加拉德·马希科拒绝向扎拉·雅各布纳贡，皇帝通过他的一名随从将他废黜，改立其叔巴莫；马希科逃往阿达尔，被追兵所杀，首级和四肢送回皇帝大营。哈迪亚国王的女儿埃莱尼公主受洗后嫁给扎拉·雅各布，成为皇后，时人称她为「泽伊拉女王」。新君在位时她得到太后称号，1507至1516年代年幼的勒布纳·丹格尔主持摄政。正是她派亚美尼亚人马特乌斯出使葡萄牙和罗马教皇，谋求对抗阿达尔和奥斯曼的盟友；她于1522年去世。阿达尔苏丹巴德莱兴兵为哈迪亚出头，1445年在戈米特兵败身亡。

16世纪20年代，葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯路过时，哈迪亚仍是林木茂密之地，道路要在树中砍出，作为安静的藩地向勒布纳·丹格尔贡纳牲畜。艾哈迈德·格兰的穆斯林长官不战而开放全境，百姓向伊玛目诉苦说，皇帝的人不许他们佩剑、不许骑备鞍的马，每年还要索走一名少女。1569年，萨尔萨·登格尔讨伐拒绝纳贡的加拉德·阿泽；哈勒尔派来五百名披甲的马拉赛战士，但阿泽的部众在奥罗莫迁徙中折损太重，不肯出战。奥罗莫人已席卷其东部边地，那里的阿尔西人后来自称有哈迪亚血统。17世纪初，加拉德·西迪·穆罕默德击溃苏森约斯的军队，密林替哈迪亚挡住了吞并：1613年葡萄牙人费尔南德斯被挡回；捷克旅人雷梅迪乌斯·普鲁特基1751年仍记述阿比西尼亚以南有一个独立的穆斯林王国。

en:
The Arsi country is the chain of fertile highlands southeast of Shewa, between the Awash basin and the lakes of the Rift Valley. Before the sixteenth century it belonged, with neighbouring Dawaro, to the Muslim polity of Hadiya. Its Cushitic farmers kept great herds of horses and cattle, used pieces of iron as money, and answered to a ruler titled garad; the fourteenth-century historian al-Umari credited Hadiya with forty thousand cavalry. The garad Mahiko refused tribute to the emperor Zara Yaqob, fled to Adal and was killed there by Adal riders, who sent his head and limbs to the emperor. Zara Yaqob then married a Hadiya princess, Eleni, and Adal went to war over the match, losing its sultan Badlay in the fighting. In 1444 these uplands were still Muslim Hadiya country, caught between Adal and the Christian empire.

Eleni's influence did not end with the marriage. She remained in the imperial palace under the emperors Baeda Maryam and Na'od, ran the government as empress, and from 1507 held the regency for the young Dawit II; she sent an Armenian, Mateus, to Lisbon and Rome in search of Christian allies, and his mission brought the Portuguese embassy that reached Ethiopia in 1520. When Ahmad Gran invaded in the 1530s the Muslims of Hadiya fed his army and joined it, telling the imam their Christian lords had forbidden them swords and saddled horses. After Gran's fall the Oromo expansion rolled over these hills: by the end of the sixteenth century the Arsi clans held the country and had given it their name, absorbing most of the older Hadiya communities. All the same the Hadiya chiefs kept their independence: the garad Sidi Mohammed destroyed an army of the emperor Susenyos, after which no imperial force crossed this frontier for three hundred years. The Arsi pastured cattle on the heights above Assela, lived under their own elders and customs, and sent coffee down the caravan road to Harar; no outside power subdued them before the nineteenth century.
zh:
阿尔西是绍阿东南一串肥沃高地，夹在阿瓦什河流域与裂谷湖群之间。16世纪以前，这里与邻近的达瓦罗同属穆斯林政权哈迪亚。操库希特语的农人牧养大批马匹和牛只，以铁块为货币，首领称「加拉德」；14世纪史家欧麦里记载，哈迪亚能出骑兵四万。加拉德马赫科拒绝向扎拉·雅各布皇帝纳贡，逃奔阿达尔，被阿达尔骑兵追杀，首级和四肢被送回皇帝面前。扎拉·雅各布随后迎娶哈迪亚公主埃莱妮，阿达尔为这桩婚事起兵来犯，苏丹巴德莱战死沙场。1444年的阿尔西仍是穆斯林哈迪亚之地，夹在阿达尔与基督教帝国之间。

埃莱妮的影响没有随婚事结束。她在巴达·马里亚姆和纳奥德两朝留在宫中，以皇后之尊主持朝政，1507年起又为年幼的达维特二世摄政；她派亚美尼亚人马特乌斯前往里斯本和罗马寻求基督教盟友，这次出使最终引来了1520年抵达埃塞俄比亚的葡萄牙使团。1530年代艾哈迈德·格兰入侵时，哈迪亚的穆斯林向他的军队供粮从军，还向伊玛目控诉基督教长官不许他们佩剑、不许骑配鞍的马。格兰败亡后，奥罗莫人的扩张漫过这片丘陵：到16世纪末，阿尔西诸氏族据有此地，以自己的部名命名它，早先的哈迪亚居民大多被同化。哈迪亚诸首领还是保住了独立：加拉德西迪·穆罕默德歼灭苏塞尼奥斯皇帝的一支军队，此后三百年没有帝国军队越过这条边界。阿尔西人在阿塞拉上方的高地牧牛，按本族长老和习俗生活，咖啡沿商道运到哈勒尔；直到19世纪，没有外来势力征服他们。

en:
Damot is the fertile highland south of the Blue Nile and west of Shewa, the country later called Welega. Its people once spoke Omotic tongues and kept a pagan kingdom of their own; tradition says the monk Tekle Haymanot converted its ruler, and the armies of Amda Seyon I annexed the land in 1316–17. The province paid its way in gold: the writer Ibn Sa'id records Damot gold carried as far as the markets of Zeila, while Damot spearmen and archers marched in the emperor's wars against Ifat and Adal. Muslim merchants also bought its slaves, and its wealth was counted in gold dust and cattle. In 1444 Christian lords held these highlands on the empire's remote south-western march.

Francisco Álvares, the Portuguese priest who came with the embassy of the 1520s, found Damot 'very big', growing ginger, grapes and peaches, with fat sheep and great cattle; its slaves were so prized 'by the Arabs' that they would not part with them at any price, and they were sold on to Arabia, Persia, India, Egypt and Greece. In 1531 the imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim of Adal overran the province and set Gasa Umar over it, one of his generals sneering that Damot men were only slaves, fit to till the land and carry wood. After the imam's death in 1543 the Emperor Galawdewos won the province back, and Sarsa Dengel led Damot warriors against the Oromo at Waj in 1572. The Oromo tide could not be held: under the luba Birmaje, between 1578 and 1586, the Boran surrounded the province and carried off its people and herds, while the Macha settled the vacated land. Many Christians fled across the Blue Nile and carried the name Damot to the Gojjam side, and the Macha markets that grew on the old highlands became the first towns of a new Welega.
zh:
达莫特是青尼罗河以南、绍阿以西的肥沃高地，即后来的沃莱加。当地人原说奥莫语族语言，保有自己的异教王国；相传僧侣特克莱·海马诺特使其统治者皈依，阿姆达·锡安一世的大军又于1316至1317年吞并此地。这个省份以黄金立身：作者伊本·赛义德记载，达莫特的黄金远运至泽拉的市集，当地的长矛兵和弓箭手还随阿姆达·锡安出征伊法特和阿达尔。穆斯林商人也购买此地出产的奴隶，财富则以砂金和牲畜计算。1444年，基督教诸侯据守着帝国西南边陲的这片高地。

随1520年代葡萄牙使节来访的神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯，见达莫特「地域辽阔」，出产姜、葡萄、桃，还有肥羊和大牛；当地奴隶深受「阿拉伯人」看重，出什么价钱都不肯脱手，被层层转卖到阿拉伯、波斯、印度、埃及和希腊。1531年，阿达尔伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣攻陷此地，以加萨·奥马尔为总督，他手下一名将领还讥笑达莫特人不过是只会耕地搬柴的奴隶。伊玛目1543年战死后，格拉德沃斯皇帝收复该省，萨尔萨·登格尔1572年率达莫特士兵在瓦季迎击奥罗莫人。迁徙大潮已无法阻挡：1578至1586年的比尔马杰轮值期，博兰部包围全省、掳走居民和牲畜，马查人则在空出的土地上定居。大批基督徒北渡青尼罗河，把达莫特之名带到戈贾姆一侧；旧高地上兴起的马查人市集，后来成为新沃莱加最早的城镇。

en:
West of Damot the highlands break into forested ravines that drop towards the White Nile basin, the country later called Benishangul. Its mountain streams carry gold, and the Gumuz and other Nilo-Saharan villagers whom Christian highlanders called the Shanqella had been raided for slaves since Aksumite times, with Sudanese merchants leading the captives away in caravans. In 1444 this was the furthest country within Damot's reach, valued for gold dust and for slaves, and after the rise of the Funj sultanate of Sennar in 1504 it lay as a buffer between that Muslim power on the Nile and the Christian provinces of the plateau.

During the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the Berta, kinsmen of the Funj, drifted in from Sennar. They called the land Bela Shangul, the 'Rock of Shangul', after a sacred stone in the hills where they first settled, and built their villages on craggy heights, raising houses and granaries on stone pillars to keep slave raiders at bay. The Emperor Susenyos marched an army through the country in 1617–18, but highland rule did not hold, and in 1685 it passed to the Funj of Sennar. As Funj power ebbed in the mid-eighteenth century, Oromo groups filtered in and settled among the Shangul villages. When the Ottoman Egyptian armies overthrew Sennar in 1821, this ravined borderland was left in the hands of its own small hill chiefs.
zh:
达莫特以西，高地裂作林木密布的深谷，俯向白尼罗河盆地，这便是后来所称的本尚古勒。山溪中出砂金，古穆兹等尼罗-撒哈拉语族群的村落被高原基督徒称作香克拉，早从阿克苏姆时代起就是掳掠奴隶的对象，俘虏由苏丹商人成队押走。1444年，这里是达莫特势力所及最远的地方，以砂金和奴隶见重；1504年森纳尔的丰吉苏丹国兴起后，它夹在尼罗河畔的穆斯林强国与高原基督教行省之间，充作缓冲。

16至17世纪，与丰吉人同源的贝尔塔人从森纳尔陆续迁入。他们把这片土地称作贝拉·尚古勒，意为「尚古勒之石」，得名于初到此地时山中的一块圣石；为防备掠奴者，他们把村舍建在险峻的高地上，房屋和粮仓都用石柱架起。1617至1618年，苏塞尼奥斯皇帝曾率军穿过此地，但高原的统治未能维持，1685年全境转归森纳尔的丰吉人。18世纪中叶丰吉势力衰退，奥罗莫群体趁势渗入，在尚古勒人的村落间落脚。1821年奥斯曼埃及的军队攻灭森纳尔后，这片沟壑纵横的边地便留在本地众多小山酋手中。

en:
Aussa is the inland delta of the Awash, whose water ends in the sands and salt lakes of the northern Afar country instead of reaching the sea. Its year-round pastures and gardens made the oasis a meeting ground for Afar camel-herders and caravans travelling between Zeila, Harar and the Ethiopian highlands, and older Harla and Doba peoples had long mingled with the Afar here. In the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries the oasis was the western march of the Muslim Adal sultanate, and in 1444 its clans rode with Sultan Badlay in the jihad that the Emperor Zara Yaqob broke at Gomit the following year.

In 1577, after Oromo raids and a great famine had undone Harar, Imam Muhammad Gasa moved Adal's capital to the oasis near Asaita. The amirs of Harar broke away in 1647, raiding wore the imamate down, and in 1672 the local Mudaito Afar destroyed it. In 1734 the Mudaito chief Data Kadafo took the title of sultan and founded a new dynasty; the sceptre of the sultans was a silver baton credited with magical power, and his son and grandson each reigned long enough to give the caravan roads years of peace. In the last years of the eighteenth century the Debne-Wemas Afar marched on the capital with several hundred Yemeni matchlockmen hired at Aden, who held a monopoly of the firearms.
