Sultan Yusuf ibn Idjahis met them with cannons and matchlocks of his own and his men caught the attackers asleep in their camp, but the Debne-Wemas came back with fresh allies from the coast, slew the sultan and sacked the town. Aussa never regained its old political weight, though the ground outside stayed a perpetual fair crowded with Afar and Somali caravans.
zh:
奥萨（阿法尔语称阿乌萨）是阿瓦什河的内陆三角洲，河水没有出海，最终消失在阿法尔北部的沙地与盐湖之间。绿洲上年年有牧草和园地，阿法尔驼户和往来于泽伊拉、哈拉尔与埃塞俄比亚高原之间的商队都在此会集，更早的哈拉人和多巴人也早已与阿法尔人混居。14、15世纪，这片绿洲是穆斯林阿达尔苏丹国的西部边地；1444年，这里的部族随苏丹巴德莱参加圣战，次年皇帝扎拉·雅各布在戈米特击破了这支大军。

1577年，奥罗莫人的袭扰和一场大饥荒把哈拉尔拖垮，伊玛目穆罕默德·加萨把阿达尔都城迁到阿萨伊塔附近的这片绿洲。1647年哈拉尔的埃米尔们分立，伊玛目国在连年袭扰中日渐衰弱，1672年被当地的穆代托阿法尔人攻灭。1734年，穆代托首领达塔·卡达福称苏丹，建立新王朝；苏丹的权杖是一根相传具有法力的银杖，其子其孙相继长期在位，商路多年安宁。18世纪最后几年，德布内-韦马斯阿法尔人向都城进军，随行的有数百名在亚丁雇来的也门火绳枪手，火器全操在他们手中。苏丹优素福·伊本·伊德贾希斯以自己的火炮和火绳枪迎敌，部下趁敌兵睡熟时偷袭得手；但德布内-韦马斯人从海岸带回援军再战，杀死苏丹并洗劫了城镇。奥萨再没恢复往日的政治分量，但城外的场地始终是常设集市，阿法尔和索马里商队往来不绝。

en: Assab is a wide bay on the arid Danakil coast, just north of the Bab-el-Mandeb; Hellenistic sailors knew a trading post nearby as Arsinoe Epidires. The shore belongs to the Afar, Muslim camel-herders who move between the sea and the burning inland desert. In 1444 the bay was the remote southern edge of the Adal sultanate, off the caravan routes that carried slaves and ivory up to Zeila and Tadjoura. After the Ottomans seized Massawa in 1557 their Habesh province ended far to the north. In 1577 what remained of Adal withdrew inland to Aussa, and in 1734 the Mudaito Afar founded their own sultanate there, the leading monarchy among the Afar; its authority reached down into the Danakil lowlands, while the bay itself stayed with local Afar chiefs.
zh: 阿萨布是干旱的达纳基尔海岸上一处宽阔海湾，就在曼德海峡以北，希腊化时代的水手知道附近有个叫阿尔西诺伊·埃皮迪雷斯的商站。海岸的主人是阿法尔人，这些穆斯林牧放骆驼，在大海与灼热的内陆沙漠之间迁徙。1444年，阿萨布湾是阿达尔苏丹国遥远的南缘，不在把奴隶和象牙运往泽伊拉、塔朱拉的商路上。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，哈贝什行省的管辖止于北面很远的海岸。1577年，阿达尔的残余势力退入内陆的奥萨；1734年，穆达伊托部阿法尔人在那里建立自己的苏丹国，在阿法尔诸政权中地位最高，其势力延伸到达纳基尔低地，海湾本身则一直留在当地阿法尔酋长手中。

en:
The grain country around Mendefera is the historic Seraye plateau, the southernmost of the Christian highland districts bound together in Medri Bahri. Rock inscriptions in the old South Arabian script at Sehuf Emni link the district to the Aksumite world of King Ezana's day. In the fourteenth century followers of the monk Ewostatewos founded Debre Mariam, which grew into a monastery and school drawing pupils from across the north; Emperor Zara Yaqob raised the Bahr Negash at Debarwa above the chiefs of Seraye and confirmed the monastery's lands by charter. In 1444 Tigrinya-speaking Orthodox villagers and monks farmed this fertile plateau on Medri Bahri's southern road, along which traders carried gold, ivory and slaves between the interior, Aksum and the Red Sea port of Massawa.

Seraye was overrun in the Ethiopian-Adal war of 1535. A local lord, Tasfa Le'ul, killed the Adalite governor Vizier Addole and sent his head to the emperor; he tried to bar Wazir Abbas's advance with men from Dembiya, was defeated and chased into the hills, and the chronicler claims not one of his band escaped. Imam Ahmad named Abbas Bahr Negash, until plague and famine drove the occupying army out. After the Ottomans seized Massawa in 1557 the road through Seraye became a fighting corridor, and in 1578 the rebel Bahr Negash Yeshaq was killed beside his Turkish allies against Emperor Sarsa Dengel at Addi Qarro. Through the seventeenth century Seraye passed to hereditary highland houses, above all the family of Hab Sellus, and in the eighteenth rival chiefs divided it as imperial power faded.
zh:
门德费拉周围的谷物之乡，是历史上的瑟拉耶高原，梅德里·巴赫里诸基督教高原区域中最靠南的一处。塞胡夫埃姆尼的古南阿拉伯字母岩刻，把这一地区和埃扎纳王时代的阿克苏姆世界联系起来。14世纪，修士埃沃斯塔特沃斯的追随者建立德布雷·马利亚姆修道院，它后来发展成一座学府，吸引北方各地的学生；扎拉·雅各布皇帝提高驻德巴尔瓦总督的地位，使他位在瑟拉耶诸首领之上，还以敕书确认了修院的地产。1444年，操提格雷尼亚语的正教村民和修士在梅德里·巴赫里南道旁这片肥沃高原上耕作，商人沿道把黄金、象牙和奴隶在内陆、阿克苏姆与红海港口马萨瓦之间转运。

1535年的埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争中，瑟拉耶被军队席卷。本地首领特斯法·莱乌勒杀死阿达尔总督维齐尔·阿多勒，把他的首级送给皇帝；他又带着登比亚的人马试图阻击瓦齐尔·阿巴斯进军，兵败后被追入山中，据当时的编年史家记述，他的部众无一人逃脱。伊玛目艾哈迈德任命阿巴斯为总督，后来瘟疫和饥荒迫使占领军撤走。1557年奥斯曼人夺取马萨瓦后，穿过瑟拉耶的道路成了厮杀的走廊；1578年，反叛的总督伊沙克与奥斯曼盟友一起，在阿迪卡罗对抗萨尔萨·丹格尔皇帝时战死。17世纪，瑟拉耶转入世袭高原家族之手，其中最显赫的是哈布·塞卢斯家族；18世纪帝国权威衰退，敌对首领瓜分了这里。

en:
Enderta covers the eastern escarpment of the Tigray highlands, above the Danakil and Afar desert flats. Its historic seat, Antalo or Hintalo, occupied a plateau just under the cliffs of Amba Aradam, a natural fortress that Tigrayan chiefs fought over from the seventeenth century on. The governor held the old title bäalgada, 'lord of the salt', and organised the caravans that carried rock salt up from the desert into the highlands and taxed the trade; Hintalo's weekly salt market outlasted every dynasty that ruled the town. Hereditary chiefs ran the province after the Solomonic restoration of 1270, until their bid for independence brought Emperor Amda Seyon north in the 1320s. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, Enderta was a Tigrinya Orthodox province of the Ethiopian empire, its cliffs guarding highland grain fields and pastures and the road down to the salt pans.

Enderta's lord Ras Robel was governing all Tigray when he was killed fighting Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi at Sambera Kware in 1529, early in the Adal war. The province fills a larger place in Ethiopian history through the Era of Princes, which opened when the Enderta noble Mikael Sehul, Ras of Tigray and regent at Gondar, had Emperor Iyoas killed in 1769. After Mikael's defeat at Sarbakusa in 1771, Enderta's governor Kefla Iyasus challenged him for Tigray and was killed. Kefla's son Wolde Selassie, born at Antalo, fled into exile; Nathaniel Pearce, the Englishman who later lived in his camp, tells how he cut down two of Mikael's chosen men, the brothers Abel and Cail, sent to murder him. Wolde Selassie returned to become Ras in 1790 and kept Hintalo as his capital, reviewing troops there and giving shelter to the fugitive Emperor Tekle Giyorgis. Muslim and Christian merchants traded at a market second in Tigray only to Adwa, and the British envoy Henry Salt came in 1805 to discuss friendship and trade; he found a small, quick-witted ruler who played chess from morning until night. Wolde Selassie remained the strongest Christian warlord in the north until his death in 1816, and Hintalo declined soon after.
zh:
恩德塔地处提格雷高原东缘，俯临达纳基勒和阿法尔沙漠低地。其历史首府安塔洛又称欣塔洛，坐落在安巴·阿拉达姆崖壁下的台地上，是天然要塞，17世纪以来提格雷首领多次为它兵戎相见。当地总督拥有「巴阿尔加达」的旧衔，意为「盐之主」，负责组织把岩盐从沙漠运上高原的商队并征收盐税；欣塔洛每周一次的盐市比统治这座城的历代政权都长久。1270年所罗门王朝复兴后，这里由世袭首领治理；14世纪20年代他们谋求独立，引来安达·塞永一世北上。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，恩德塔是埃塞俄比亚帝国一个操提格雷尼亚语的正教省份，崖壁拱卫着高原的农田牧场和通往沙漠盐田的道路。

恩德塔首领罗贝尔统领整个提格雷期间，在1529年阿达尔战争初期的桑贝拉夸雷之战中被艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队杀死。让这片地方在埃塞俄比亚历史上更出名的是「王侯时代」：出身恩德塔的提格雷拉斯、贡德尔朝廷摄政米卡埃尔·塞胡尔于1769年弑杀伊约阿斯皇帝，开启了这个时代。1771年米卡埃尔在萨尔巴库萨战败后，恩德塔总督凯夫莱·伊亚苏斯与他争夺提格雷，兵败被杀。凯夫莱之子沃尔德·塞拉西生于安塔洛，被迫流亡；后来在他营中生活多年的英国人纳萨尼尔·皮尔斯记载，他曾只身斩杀米卡埃尔派来行刺的两名心腹阿贝尔和卡伊尔兄弟。沃尔德·塞拉西1790年回到提格雷成为拉斯，仍以欣塔洛为都城，在此检阅军队，并收留避难的特克勒·乔治斯皇帝。穆斯林和基督教商人在城中的市集交易，其规模在提格雷仅次于阿杜瓦；英国使节亨利·索尔特1805年来此商谈友好与通商，见到的是一位身材不高、机敏善辩、能从早到晚下棋的统治者。沃尔德·塞拉西到1816年去世前，始终是北方最有实力的基督教军阀，他死后欣塔洛也随之一蹶不振。

en:
Angot, 'the Neck', is the broken ribbon of highland running south from Lake Ashenge along the rim of the Ethiopian plateau, where the escarpment drops to the Muslim Afar lowlands. Christian emperors kept churches and garrisons on the heights while Dobe'a pastoralists grazed great herds below and traded with the Adal coast. Their chief market, Manadeley, stood on the highland edge above the desert; when Francisco Álvares saw it in the 1520s he called it 'like a city or seaport', crowded with merchants from Jeddah, Cairo, Tunis, Fez, Ormus and India. In 1444 Angot obeyed the Christian Emperor Zara Yaqob, yet many of its people were Muslim, and caravans and marriage ties bound the province to Adal.

Baeda Maryam harried the Dobe'a for years at the start of his reign (1468–1478) until they submitted, took baptism and turned to farming; he built them a church of the Virgin and planted vines and orange groves in their country. The Ethiopian–Adal war then swept over the borderland: Angot was overrun and governed for Adal by Ali Ankarsah. On 28 August 1542 Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi scattered the Portuguese stockade at Wofla near Lake Ashenge. Cristóvão da Gama, his arm broken by a bullet, was caught that night in the bush, where an old woman led his pursuers; Ahmad killed him with his own hands over the protests of his Ottoman musketeers, who wanted the prisoners kept for bargaining and marched back to Yemen with their men. After the war the Yejju, converts of the imam, settled Angot under their sheikh Umar, and Raya and Wollo Oromo pressed in from the later sixteenth century. Out of this mixed frontier rose the Yejju Warra Sheik, Oromo ras lords who ran the Gondar court through the age of the princes; early in the nineteenth century Ras Gugsa of Yejju held the emperors as his puppets.
zh:
安戈意为「脖颈」，是从阿申盖湖向南、沿埃塞俄比亚高原边沿伸展的一条破碎高地，崖下便是穆斯林阿法尔人的低地。基督教皇帝们在高地上建堂驻军，多贝阿牧人在崖下放牧大群牲畜，与阿达尔海岸通商。他们最大的市场马纳德莱坐落在高原边缘、俯瞰荒漠；1520年代弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯见到它时，称这座集市「如同城市或海港」，挤满了来自吉达、开罗、突尼斯、非斯、霍尔木兹和印度的商人。1444年，安戈臣属于基督教皇帝扎拉·雅各布，但居民中穆斯林众多，商路和联姻把这方边地与阿达尔系在一起。

巴埃达·马里亚姆皇帝在位（1468—1478年）之初连年征讨多贝阿人，直到他们归降、受洗并改事务农；他在当地建起圣母教堂，还种下葡萄和橙子。随后埃塞俄比亚—阿达尔战争席卷边地：安戈被攻占，由阿达尔的阿里·安卡尔萨管辖。1542年8月28日，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐在阿申盖湖附近的沃夫拉攻破葡萄牙营寨。克里斯托旺·达伽马手臂中弹骨折，当夜藏在灌木丛中，一个老妇人把追兵领到他的藏身处；艾哈迈德不顾奥斯曼火枪手留俘谈判的主张，亲手将他处死，奥斯曼指挥官随即率部返回也门。战后，被这位伊玛目改宗的耶朱人在谢赫·奥马尔率领下定居安戈，拉亚和沃洛的奥罗莫人也从16世纪后期起涌入。这片混杂边地后来走出耶朱人的瓦拉·谢赫家族：在王子纷争时代，这些奥罗莫出身的「拉斯」把持贡德尔朝政，19世纪初的拉斯·古格萨更把皇帝攥在手中。

en:
Lasta is the mountain fastness of the Agaw, set between Wag and Bete Amhara. After losing Aksum the Zagwe dynasty kept its court at Roha and ruled Ethiopia from there from about 1150 to 1270. Local tradition says that before King Lalibela (r. c. 1181–1221) came to the throne, Christ led him through Jerusalem and bade him build a second one in his own country; the eleven churches carved down from the living rock were laid out as two Jerusalems, earthly and heavenly, with a trench for the Jordan, after Jerusalem fell to Saladin in 1187. The church of Saint George was the last and best known of the eleven, and Roha itself took Lalibela's name after he died. Yekuno Amlak restored the Solomonic line in 1270, but the Zagwe heirs kept Lasta and Wag, bore the title Wagshum and claimed Israelite descent. In 1444 Zara Yaqob ruled through these lords, and the rock churches already drew pilgrims.

Francisco Álvares visited twice in the 1520s and wrote that he wearied of describing the churches, since no one in Europe would believe him. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's soldiers wasted the district between July and September 1531; the Adal chronicle has him set fire to a rock church and tells of a nun who threw herself onto the flames before his men pulled her away, though the Ethiopian royal chronicles say nothing of burned churches. Miguel de Castanhoso, a Portuguese veteran of Cristóvão da Gama's expedition, found them intact soon afterward: locals attributed the churches to angels, and neither crowbars nor gunpowder had cracked them. From 1629 the Agaw of the Emekina mountains rose under Melka Krestos for the old Orthodox faith, beat the emperor's armies and forced Susenyos to abandon Catholicism in 1632. They routed Fasilides at Libo in 1637, when Melka Krestos briefly held the throne before he was killed, and another imperial army froze to death in the Lasta mountains in 1638. Gondarine emperors campaigned here for generations, and in the 1750s the Franciscan Remedius Prutky still counted Lasta among the six Ethiopian provinces worthy to be called kingdoms.
zh:
拉斯塔是阿高人的险峻山地，夹在瓦格与贝特阿姆哈拉之间。扎格维王朝失去阿克苏姆后以罗哈为廷，约1150至1270年间在此统治埃塞俄比亚。当地相传，拉利贝拉王（约1181—1221年在位）登基前，基督带他游历耶路撒冷，命他在故国再建一座；1187年耶路撒冷落入萨拉丁手中后，十一座从整块活岩中向下凿出的教堂按地上、天上两座耶路撒冷布局，还凿出一道壕沟象征约旦河。圣乔治教堂是十一座中最晚、也最有名的一座，拉利贝拉死后罗哈也改以他的名字为名。1270年耶库诺·阿姆拉克恢复所罗门王朝，但扎格维后裔仍保有拉斯塔和瓦格，头戴「瓦格舒姆」头衔，自称以色列后裔。1444年扎拉·雅各布通过这些领主施行统治，岩凿教堂已吸引朝圣者远道而来。

1520年代，弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯两度到访，写道自己已懒得再描摹这些教堂，因为说得再多欧洲人也不会信。1531年7月至9月，艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的军队蹂躏此地；阿达尔编年史称他放火烧毁一座岩教堂，还记下一名修女扑进火堆、被他的士兵拉出，而埃塞俄比亚皇家编年史对教堂被烧只字未提。曾随克里斯托旺·达伽马远征的葡萄牙老兵米格尔·德·卡斯塔尼奥索不久后见到教堂完好：当地人说教堂出自天使之手，撬棍和火药都奈何它们不得。1629年起，埃梅基纳山区的阿高人在梅尔卡·克里斯托斯率领下为旧正教起事，屡败皇军，迫使苏西约斯在1632年放弃天主教。1637年他们在利博击溃法西里德斯，梅尔卡·克里斯托斯一度登上皇位，随即被杀；1638年另一支皇军在拉斯塔山中冻毙。贡德尔历代皇帝在此连番用兵，1750年代方济各会士雷梅迪乌斯·普鲁特基仍把拉斯塔列为埃塞俄比亚六个配称王国的省份之一。

en:
Agawmeder, the 'Land of the Agaw', fills the rolling country between Gojjam, Lake Tana and the Sudanese lowlands, around the later town of Dangila. The Agaw are a Cushitic people among the oldest in the Ethiopian highlands, named in fourth-century Aksumite inscriptions; a Greek traveller of the sixth century heard of a gold road running through 'Agau', its caravans guarded by an officer of King Kaleb. From Agaw stock came the Zagwe dynasty, which ruled Ethiopia from about 1137 to 1270 and counted King Lalibela among its rulers, and after the Solomonic restoration the Zagwe kept their home lands of Wag and Lasta with the title of Wagshum. The Agaw of the western marches had long been Christian but kept their own tongue; they grew grain on the high plateaux, pastured great herds and ran markets where slaves and gold brought up from the lowlands changed hands. In 1444 Agaw lords held this frontier for the emperor.

In the wars of Ahmad Gran, Adal raiders harried the Agaw country through the 1530s, and from the later sixteenth century Oromo war-bands crossed the Blue Nile onto its southern flank, so the frontier knew little peace. Susenyos passed through Dangila in 1620 while making his power felt along the western marches; his turn to Rome brought civil war here as elsewhere, and his reign ended in abdication in 1632, when his son Fasilides restored the old faith. The Gondarine emperors reasserted the west: after putting down the pretender Yeshaq in 1685, Iyasu I marched the following year against his Agaw backers beyond southern Gojjam, pushed on through Metekel into the Shanqella country in 1688, burning Gisa and taking captives at Gorsi, and in 1704 settled the Christianized Gawe Oromo along the north bank of the Abbay as a frontier guard. Agawmeder never formed a strong polity of its own, and the lords of Gojjam gradually absorbed it.
zh:
奥格（阿高默德尔）意为「阿高人之地」，位于戈贾姆、塔纳湖与苏丹低地之间的起伏地带，丹吉拉城后来便兴起于这一带。阿高人属库希特语族，是埃塞俄比亚高原最古老的居民之一，4世纪的阿克苏姆铭文已有其名；6世纪一位希腊旅行家还记述，一条黄金商路经过「阿高」，卡莱布王的官员专司护卫路上的商队。统治埃塞俄比亚的扎格维王朝（约1137至1270年）便出自阿高人，拉利贝拉王即在其列王之中；所罗门王朝复辟后，扎格维王室保留了故乡瓦格与拉斯塔，领有「瓦格舒姆」之号。西陲的阿高人早已信奉基督教，仍说本族语言，在高原台地上种植谷物、牧放大群牲畜，市镇上转手着低地贩来的奴隶和黄金。1444年，阿高诸侯为皇帝扼守这边疆。

格兰战争期间，阿达尔骑兵在整个1530年代连年蹂躏阿高之地；16世纪后期起，奥罗莫武装又渡过青尼罗河压向南境，边疆少有宁日。1620年，苏塞尼奥斯在西陲用兵途中经过丹吉拉；他后来改宗罗马，内战也蔓延到此，统治于1632年以退位收场，其子法西利德斯恢复了旧信仰。贡德尔林诸帝重新确立了对西部的控制：1685年平定僭称者叶沙克后，伊亚苏一世次年便进军南戈贾姆之外，惩讨支持叶沙克的阿高人；1688年又取道梅特克尔攻入香克拉人之地，焚毁吉萨，在戈尔西掳走居民；1704年他把已改宗基督教的加韦部奥罗莫人安置在阿巴伊河北岸，充作边守。奥格从未形成强有力的政权，后来被戈贾姆诸侯逐步吞并。

en:
Semien is the highest mountain country in Ethiopia, a wall of tablelands and pinnacles north of Lake Tana cut by the Tekezé and crowned by Ras Dashen. An Aksumite inscription recorded in the sixth century describes peaks knee-deep in snow where the king sent exiles. Its high valleys held the villages of the Beta Israel, who kept a Judaism without the Talmud, farmed cold plots and lived as weavers and blacksmiths. Tradition called this the kingdom of the Gideons and even told of a Jewish queen, Gudit, burning Aksum's churches around 960. Early in the fifteenth century Emperor Yeshaq conquered Semien and Dembiya from Jewish governors and tied inherited land to baptism: 'He who is baptised may inherit the land of his father, otherwise let him be a Falasi', a decree that may have given the Falasha their name. In 1444, under Zara Yaqob, the Ethiopian crown claimed Semien, but Beta Israel villages kept their faith on fortified heights above the Christian estates and the Dabareq pass.

Zara Yaqob married Seyon Moges, daughter of the Beta Israel leader Gideon V; after a highland revolt she was executed for alleged espionage, and in 1465-1472 General Markos razed synagogues and beheaded the community's leaders. In the Adal war they joined Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi, who returned their lands and exempted them from tax, then fought for Gelawdewos after Dawit II died. Sarsa Dengel dragged cannon captured from the Ottomans into the mountains, stormed the Semien strongholds and executed the leader Gershom; many of his followers then killed themselves rather than be baptised. A revolt begun in 1614 against Susenyos was crushed by 1625, the Beta Israel losing their lands and autonomy, with Judaism forbidden. Susenyos made his son Fasilides governor with the title Aggafari; once emperor, Fasilides expelled the Jesuits, and Beta Israel craftsmen worked near the new court at Gondar. In the Era of Princes Ras Gebre held the province from his fortress at Amba Hay from 1771 to 1815. James Bruce passed Dabareq's high market in 1770, and Henry Salt noted its coarse wool carpets and the joke that Semien's soldiers carried shields of sheepskin.
zh:
塞米恩是埃塞俄比亚地势最高的山地，塔纳湖北岸一列台地与尖峰，被特克泽河切开，顶峰是拉斯达山。6世纪记录下来的一份阿克苏姆铭文说，这里雪峰没膝、难以攀近，是国王流放罪人的地方。高山河谷中散布着贝塔以色列人的村落：他们奉行没有《塔木德》的犹太教，在寒冷地块上耕作，靠织布和打铁为生。传说把这里称作吉迪恩诸王的王国，甚至讲到犹太女王古迪特约在960年焚毁阿克苏姆的教堂。15世纪初，伊沙克皇帝从犹太首领手中征服塞米恩与登比亚，把土地继承权和受洗绑在一起：「受洗者可继承父亲的土地，否则就让他做法拉西」，法拉沙之名可能就出自这条敕令。1444年扎拉·雅各布在位时，埃塞俄比亚皇室已声称领有塞米恩，但贝塔以色列人的村落仍在设防高地上守着自己的信仰，俯临低处的基督教地产和德巴尔格山口。

扎拉·雅各布娶了贝塔以色列首领吉迪恩五世之女锡永·莫格斯；一次高地叛乱后她以通敌罪名被处死，1465年至1472年间马科斯将军拆毁会堂，把犹太社团首领尽数斩首。阿达尔战争中，他们投奔艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐，后者发还土地、免除赋税；达维特二世死后他们又转而为格拉德沃斯作战。萨尔萨·丹格尔把从奥斯曼人手中缴获的火炮拖进群山，轰开塞米恩山寨，处死首领革顺，他的许多部众不愿受洗，纷纷自尽。1614年爆发的反苏斯尼约斯起义到1625年被镇压，贝塔以色列人失去土地和自治，犹太教遭到禁止。苏斯尼约斯封其子法西利德斯为塞米恩总督，称阿加法里；法西利德斯继位后驱逐耶稣会士，贝塔以色列工匠到新都贡德尔附近谋生。王侯时代里，拉斯·格布雷1771年至1815年据守安巴海要塞统辖此地。詹姆斯·布鲁斯1770年经过德巴尔格的高山市场，亨利·索尔特则记下了当地织的粗羊毛毯，以及「塞米恩兵的盾牌是羊皮做的」这一笑话。

en:
Dembiya is the warm lowland on the northern shore of Lake Tana, the lake once called Dembea, from which the Abbay, or Blue Nile, flows out. The dark soil of the Foggora plain grows cotton and grain for the lake markets, and just offshore stands the island monastery of Gelila Zakarias, one of the lake's island houses to which emperors and monks sent their books and treasure in time of war. Amhara farmers shared the plain with Beta Israel villages, the Falasha, whose communities ran from here towards Semien and who lived by weaving cloth and forging spears, ploughshares and ironware. In 1444, under the Emperor Zara Yaqob, Dembiya was a settled province of the Christian empire, its peasant villages and Falasha hamlets living side by side.

The Adal jihad of Ahmad Gran reached the lake. In March 1537 his men burned Gelila Zakarias, and on 21 February 1543 the Emperor Galawdewos, with a band of Portuguese musketeers, met him at Wayna Daga on the Dembiya shore. Gran was killed in the fighting and his army routed; the battle broke the jihad and left the Christian empire standing.

Half a century later the lake shore briefly held a Catholic court. In 1607 Susenyos granted the Jesuits land at Gorgora, where Pedro Páez raised a stone church between 1618 and 1621 and the emperor built a palace beside it; a seminary taught the sons of Portuguese settlers in Portuguese and Amharic, and between 1627 and 1629 the Jesuit João Martins built a second church of lime and stone. Susenyos declared for Rome, and perhaps 100,000 people of Dembiya and Wegera are said to have taken the Roman rite. Orthodox revolts forced his abdication in 1632; his son Fasilides expelled the Jesuits, abandoned Gorgora, founded a new capital inland at Gondar in 1636, and in 1665 ordered the Catholic 'books of the Franks' burned. In the Era of the Princes the dejazmachs of Dembiya held the lake plain and took tribute from Muslim Galabat on the Sudan road.
zh:
德姆比亚是塔纳湖北岸温暖的低地。塔纳湖旧称德姆贝亚，阿巴伊河（青尼罗河）就从湖中流出。福格拉平原的黑土种植棉花和谷物，供应湖畔集市；近岸水面上矗立着格利拉·扎卡利亚斯岛修道院，它是塔纳湖众多岛修院之一，战乱时皇帝和修士常把经书、财宝送进这类岛上的院落。阿姆哈拉农民与贝塔以色列人（法拉沙人）的村落共处在平原上，后者的社群从这一带延伸向瑟门，以织布和打铁为生，出产布匹、长矛、犁铧和各种铁器。1444年扎拉·雅各布皇帝在位时，德姆比亚是基督教帝国治下安居的一省，农夫的村庄与法拉沙人的村落比邻而居。

格兰的圣战波及湖区：1537年3月，他的部下焚毁格利拉·扎卡利亚斯修道院；1543年2月21日，格拉德沃斯皇帝带着一队葡萄牙火绳枪手，在德姆比亚湖畔的韦伊纳达加迎战格兰。格兰在混战中被杀，大军溃散；此役击碎了这场圣战，基督教帝国得以存续。

半个世纪后，湖畔一度出现了一座天主教宫廷。1607年，苏西约斯把戈尔戈拉的土地赐给耶稣会士，佩德罗·佩斯于1618至1621年在此建起石砌教堂，皇帝又在旁修造王宫；一所修院用葡萄牙语和阿姆哈拉语教授葡萄牙定居者的子弟，1627至1629年耶稣会士若昂·马丁斯又建成一座石灰石教堂。苏西约斯宣布皈依罗马，据说德姆比亚和沃格拉有十万人随之改奉罗马礼。正统教派的叛乱迫使他在1632年退位；其子法西里德斯驱逐耶稣会士、弃置戈尔戈拉，1636年在内陆另建新都贡德尔，1665年又下令焚毁「法兰克人的经书」。王子时代里，德姆比亚的德贾兹马奇们据守湖原，向通往苏丹道上的穆斯林城镇加拉巴特收取贡赋。

en:
Mora is the dry belt between the Harar plateau and the Gulf of Tadjoura, a country of granite hills, dry riverbeds and wells where Issa and other Somali clans pastured camels. Caravans out of Harar carrying coffee, ivory and slaves made their first camps here on the Zeila road, and settlements such as Ali Adde grew up under Ifat and Adal rule. In 1444 the sultan of Adal held this arid border, and the Somali lancers of his army mustered at its wells.

This frontier faced Christian Abyssinia, and raiding armies crossed it both ways. In the 1470s the emir Usman routed the columns of the Emperor Baeda Maryam here. Mahfuz, governor of Zeila, was called the Captain of Zeila in the medieval texts and came to wield more power than the sultan; for a generation he launched his raids through these lowlands until Lebna Dengel's ambush in Fatagar left him dead and Adal slid into a succession war. In 1520 the sultan Abu Bakr moved his capital from Dakkar to Harar, and the imam Ahmad Gragn later led his jihad down this same road, conquering most of Abyssinia with muskets and cannons until a Portuguese-assisted Ethiopian army killed him in 1543. The Oromo then overran the lowlands, and in 1577 the Adal court withdrew to Aussa. The camel clans stayed by their wells, and the Zeila road carried its coffee and ivory as before.
zh:
莫拉是哈勒尔高原与塔朱拉湾之间的干旱地带，花岗岩丘陵、干涸河床和水井散布其间。伊萨等索马里氏族在此放牧骆驼；从哈勒尔驮运咖啡、象牙和奴隶前往泽伊拉的商队，出城后第一批营地就扎在这里，阿里阿德等聚落在伊法特和阿达尔治下发展起来。1444年，阿达尔苏丹占据这条干旱边地，他军中的索马里长矛骑兵在各处水井集结。

这道边境对面是基督教的阿比西尼亚，袭掠的军队双向往来。15世纪70年代，埃米尔乌斯曼在此击溃巴德·玛利亚姆皇帝的讨伐纵队。泽伊拉长官马赫福兹在中世纪记载里被称作「泽伊拉队长」，权势压过苏丹本人；他在一代人的时间里不断经这些低地袭掠，最终在法塔加尔中了勒布纳·丹格尔的埋伏被杀，阿达尔随之陷入继承战争。1520年，苏丹阿布·贝克尔把都城从达卡尔迁往哈勒尔，伊玛目艾哈迈德·格兰后来率圣战军沿这条道路出征，凭火枪和火炮征服大半个阿比西尼亚，直到1543年被有葡萄牙人相助的埃塞俄比亚军队击杀。奥罗莫人随后涌入低地，阿达尔宫廷于1577年退守奥萨。骆驼氏族仍守着各自的水井，泽伊拉商路上的咖啡和象牙照旧往来。

en:
The Jubba River reaches the Indian Ocean behind a chain of low islands and reefs running south toward Pate. In the fifteenth century Bajuni fishermen, Swahili-speaking Muslims, lived on the islands in coral-stone hamlets and sailed lateen-rigged beden boats to take shark and dry fish for the coasting trade; on the mainland Somali clans watered their herds at stone wells and grazed them back toward the bush. Islands and mainland alike answered to the Ajuran sultans of the House of Garen, the strongest power in the Horn. Their engineers dammed the Jubba and the Shabelle, ringed the country with stone wells and turned the river valleys into grain and fruit plantations whose harvests went out through Barawa and Mogadishu to Arabia and India; Muslim families from Arabia, Persia, India and Spain settled in the coastal towns under their rule. In 1444 the fishing anchorage at the Jubba mouth, later Kismayo, was a quiet southern outpost of that empire.

Early in the sixteenth century Tristão da Cunha's Portuguese fleet stormed and burned Barawa, yet found it too strongly defended to hold and sailed away without daring Mogadishu. In the 1580s the coastal cities sent to the Ottoman corsair Mir Ali Bey, and a Somali fleet joined him in seizing Pate, Mombasa and Kilwa until a Portuguese armada out of India retook them; Mogadishu the Portuguese never attacked, and the Ajuran coast struck new coins on the Ottoman model as a gesture of independence. Oromo pressure from the west then mounted: in the mid-1600s the Garen sultans fought the long Gaal Madow campaigns against the Oromo and converted their captives to Islam, while Oromo raiders drove many Bajuni south toward Lamu and Kenya. As the empire weakened its rulers grew oppressive with heavy taxation, and at the century's end a former Ajuran general, Ibrahim Adeer, overthrew the Silcis vassals of the interior and founded the Gobroon state of Geledi. By 1821 Sultan Mahamud Ibrahim held the Jubba mouth and its fishing islands.
zh:
朱巴河注入印度洋处，海面散落着一长串低矮岛屿和礁群，向南一直延伸到帕泰。15世纪时，讲斯瓦希里语的穆斯林渔民巴琼尼人住在岛上的珊瑚石小村，驾驶挂斜帆的「贝登」船捕捞鲨鱼、晒制鱼干，沿海南北贩运；大陆上的索马里诸族在石井边饮畜，再把牧群赶回灌丛。海岛与大陆都臣服于加伦家族的阿朱兰苏丹——非洲之角最强的势力。其工匠在朱巴河与谢贝利河上筑坝修堰，在各地开凿石井，把河谷辟为出产谷物、瓜果的农庄，收成经巴拉韦和摩加迪沙运往阿拉伯与印度；阿拉伯、波斯、印度乃至西班牙的穆斯林家庭也迁居其治下的港城。1444年，朱巴河口这处后来发展成基斯马尤的渔船锚地，还是帝国南端一处安静的据点。

16世纪初，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚的葡萄牙舰队猛攻并焚毁巴拉韦，却因城防坚固无法久占，未敢进犯摩加迪沙便扬帆离去。1580年代，沿岸各城派人联络奥斯曼私掠首领米尔·阿里·贝伊，一支索马里舰队随他联手夺取帕泰、蒙巴萨和基尔瓦，直到葡萄牙从印度调来大舰队反攻夺回；葡萄牙人始终没有进攻摩加迪沙，阿朱兰海岸还仿奥斯曼式样铸造新币，宣示经济上的独立。此后西面的奥罗莫人压力日增：17世纪中叶，加伦苏丹连年发动加尔·马多战争，将俘虏尽数改宗伊斯兰教，奥罗莫袭扰者也把许多巴琼尼人向南赶往拉穆和肯尼亚一带。帝国在衰弱中课税日重、统治苛暴，世纪之末，出身阿朱兰将领的易卜拉欣·阿代尔推翻内陆的西尔西斯封臣，建立格布龙家族的格勒迪国家。到1821年，马赫穆德·易卜拉欣苏丹已经领有朱巴河口和这片渔岛。

en:
Merca is an old roadstead on the Banaadir coast, about a hundred kilometres southwest of Mogadishu, where the produce of the Shabelle lowlands comes down to the sea. The first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea already lists a trading emporium here called Essina, and Ibn Sa'id in the thirteenth century ranked Merca with Mogadishu and Barawa as one of the three chief Muslim cities of the East African coast; he called it the capital of the Hawiye, who lived in fifty villages on the banks of a river he named the Nile of Mogadishu, the Shabelle. Under the Ajuran sultans it was an administrative centre run by their naa'ibs, or deputies, and local tradition gives those governors the pillar tombs that stand around the town. The saint Sheikh Hussein was born here in the thirteenth century before he carried Islam into Bale, where the pilgrim town built around his tomb bears his name. The Ming treasure fleets knew the port as Molugan. In 1444 Merca was a prosperous Ajuran haven, shipping the produce of the Shabelle lowlands to Arabia.

The Portuguese burned Barawa in 1507, and later fleets bombarded Mogadishu, but neither blow reached Merca, and its merchants kept their place in the Indian Ocean trade. When Ajuran power fell apart at the end of the seventeenth century, a warlord called Amir gathered a following, the El Amir, and drove the Ajuran lords out of the town; they held it for thirty-four years until the Bimaal clan expelled them in turn. The Bimaal made Merca their stronghold and kept it independent for the next century, even after the Geledi sultans rose at Afgooye inland and sent armies against the port.
zh:
马尔卡是贝纳迪尔海岸的古老锚地，在摩加迪沙西南约一百公里，谢贝利河低地的物产从这里出海。公元1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》已记有此地商埠埃西纳；13世纪的伊本·赛义德把马尔卡与摩加迪沙、巴拉韦并列为东非海岸三座首要的穆斯林城市，称之为哈维耶人的都会，说他们在他所谓「摩加迪沙的尼罗河」两岸的五十个村落里居住，那条河就是谢贝利河。阿朱兰苏丹治下，马尔卡是总督纳伊卜管辖的行政中心，当地传说把城外的柱墓归于这些总督所建。13世纪的圣徒谢赫·侯赛因出生于此，后来他把伊斯兰教传入巴勒，他陵墓所在的朝圣城镇便以他为名。郑和的船队把这座港口记作「木鲁旰」。1444年，马尔卡是阿朱兰治下一座殷实港口，把谢贝利河低地的物产运往阿拉伯。

1507年葡萄牙人焚毁巴拉韦，后来的舰队又炮轰摩加迪沙，但两场兵火都没烧到马尔卡，城中商人得以保住他们在印度洋贸易中的位置。17世纪末阿朱兰国势瓦解，一个名叫埃米尔的首领聚集起名为「埃米尔人」的部众，赶走了阿朱兰统治者；他们盘踞马尔卡三十四年，最终被比马尔氏族逐出。比马尔人以马尔卡为据点，在接下来的一个世纪里自主掌控此港，即便盖莱迪苏丹在后方的阿弗戈耶兴起、发兵来攻也没能拿下。

en:
Afgooye lies on the lower Shebelle River, on routes linking Mogadishu and the Benadir ports with the grain lands of the interior. In 1444 its settlement was called Lama Jiidle, Somali for 'two roads', and served as the administrative seat of the Silcis, a governing dynasty within the Ajuran state. Silcis officials took a measure of grain each day from every Geledi household, loaded it on a camel or donkey, and charged herdsmen who watered stock at the river. The river farms and camel caravans made the town useful as a tribute centre, though the Silcis did not surround it with stone walls or palaces.

The town's later name came from the revolt against that tax. Oral accounts say that the daughter of Silcis ruler Umar Abukar Abroone came to collect grain with her slaves and was beaten by the Geledi; when she reported it, her father said 'waa la i afgooye', 'they have cut off my mouth', meaning his supply of food had been stopped. Late in the seventeenth century Ibrahim Adeer, a former Ajuran general, led the Geledi to drive out the Silcis and founded the Gobroon dynasty. Afgooye became the capital of the Geledi Sultanate, drawing caravans with ivory, leopard skins and aloe in exchange for cloth, sugar, dates and firearms. Sorghum, beans and cotton grew on the surrounding farms, while weavers, potters and jewellers worked inside a walled town with five gates. Early nineteenth-century estimates put its population above 80,000, and its mosques and palaces served the caravan business along the Shebelle.
zh:
阿夫戈耶（通行译名阿夫哥耶）位于谢贝利河下游，摩加迪沙和贝纳迪尔诸港通向内陆产粮区的道路从这里经过。1444年，这里的聚落叫拉马吉德莱，索马里语意为「两条路」，是阿朱兰政权下属希尔西斯王朝的行政驻地。希尔西斯官吏每天从格勒迪每户征收一量器谷物，用骆驼或驴子驮走，还向到河边饮畜的牧人收费。河畔农田和骆驼商队使这座城镇成为实用的贡赋中心，不过希尔西斯人并未在这里修筑石墙和宫殿。

城镇后来的名字就来自反抗这项税赋的行动。口述故事说，希尔西斯统治者奥马尔·阿布卡尔·阿夫罗内的女儿带着奴隶征收谷物，反遭格勒迪人殴打；她回报父亲后，他说自己的「嘴被割断了」，意思是食物来源已被截断。17世纪末，曾在阿朱兰麾下为将的易卜拉欣·阿代尔率领格勒迪人赶走希尔西斯人，建立戈布伦王朝。阿夫戈耶成为格勒迪苏丹国都城，商队带来象牙、豹皮和芦荟，换走布匹、糖、椰枣和火器。周围农田种植高粱、豆类和棉花，织工、陶匠和珠宝匠在城内做工；城墙设有五座城门。19世纪初的估计称城中人口超过八万，清真寺和宫殿沿着谢贝利河的商路兴建。

en:
Bardera lies on a high, fertile stretch of the Jubba, where palm groves line the banks and run into the farms; its Somali name Baardheere means 'the tall palm'. In 1444 it was among the foremost inland cities of the Ajuran Sultanate, whose dams and wells commanded the river's water and whose granaries supplied the Benadir ports. Ajuran roads carried the town's merchants down to Barawa and Mogadishu, its madrasas taught the Quran and Islamic law beside the grain markets, and caravans brought ivory and cloth up from the river landing.

Portuguese fleets sacked the Benadir cities in the 1500s and burned Barawa, but the Ajurans held the river line and Bardera's trade survived. When Ajuran power collapsed at the end of the seventeenth century, the Geledi sultans of the Gobroon dynasty took over the Jubba. Under them the town kept its walled citadel above the river and became the chief ivory market of the southern Horn, where caravans from the interior sold their tusks for forwarding to the coast. In 1819 a Bardera sheikh launched a puritan revival: his followers forbade tobacco and folk dances, required women to veil, and stopped the ivory trade, holding the elephant an unclean animal. Their reformist community inside the citadel was drawing followers from across the region before 1821.
zh:
巴尔代雷位于朱巴河一段高腴的河岸上，棕榈林沿河岸生长、伸入农田，索马里语名Baardheere意为「高棕榈」。1444年，它是阿朱兰苏丹国最重要的内陆城市之一：阿朱兰人的水坝和水井控制着朱巴河的水量，粮仓供给贝纳迪尔诸港，修筑的道路把商人送往巴拉韦和摩加迪沙；经学堂在谷物集市旁讲授《古兰经》和伊斯兰教法，商队把象牙和布匹运到河埠。

16世纪，葡萄牙舰队洗劫贝纳迪尔沿海诸城、焚毁巴拉韦，但阿朱兰人守住了河道防线，巴尔代雷的贸易延续下来。17世纪末阿朱兰帝国瓦解，戈布伦家族的盖莱迪苏丹接管朱巴河流域。在盖莱迪治下，该城保留了临河高地的城堡，成为非洲之角南部首要的象牙市场，内陆商队在此出售象牙，再转运出海。1819年，巴尔代雷一位谢赫发起清教式复兴：信徒禁止烟草和民间歌舞，要求妇女蒙面，还以大象为不洁之兽、停止象牙贸易。到1821年前，城堡中的改革派社群已吸引了来自整个地区的信徒。

en:
Werder, in Somali Wardheer, is the well-country of the eastern Ogaden, the dry Doollo plain of red and white sand between the Haud and the grazing grounds of the Darod clans. No permanent river crosses it, and the deep wells decide where men and camels can live. In the 15th century the wells belonged above all to the Marehan, Sunni Somalis who counted their wealth in camels and sheep and answered to their own clan chiefs rather than to any city sultan. Herders, and the caravans that bought their stock, moved between Wardheer, the upper Shebelle and the northern market of Berbera. In 1444 the Adal court on the Harar plateau was too far away to command these plains: Somali pastoral country, tied to the Muslim world of the interior by trade and faith alone.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's call to jihad reached the wells anyway. Arab Faqih, the chronicler of the conquest of Abyssinia, records the Marraihan, as he calls the Marehan, marching under their chief Hirabu in the Imam's armies. South of them the Ajuran Sultanate kept the wider order of the interior, its power running up the Shebelle as far as Qalafo, until it declined in the 17th century. From that same century the caravan trails across the Ogaden also carried slaves taken among the Arsi and other southern peoples, driven north toward Berbera and the Red Sea together with the livestock and hides that remained the plainsmen's wealth. No fort or garrison watched over Wardheer: the wells belonged to whichever clan could water its own herds there and keep rivals away.
zh:
韦尔德（索马里语名Wardheer）是东欧加登的水井之地：豪德与达鲁德诸族牧地之间的多洛干旱平原，白沙红沙交错，没有常流河，深井决定了人和骆驼能在哪里落脚。15世纪时，这些水井主要归马雷汉人所有，他们是逊尼派索马里人，以骆驼和羊群计富，听从本族酋长，不认任何城里的苏丹。牧人和收购牲畜的商队往来于韦尔德、上谢贝利河与北方的柏培拉市场之间。1444年，远在哈勒尔高原的阿达尔朝廷号令不及这片平原：这里是索马里游牧之地，与内陆穆斯林世界之间只靠商路和信仰连着。

艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的圣战号召还是传到了井边。记录征服阿比西尼亚之役的编年史家阿拉伯·法基赫写道，他笔下的「马拉伊汉」就是马雷汉人，在酋长希拉布率领下随伊玛目的大军开拔。南面的阿朱兰苏丹国维持着内陆大局，其势力沿谢贝利河上溯至卡拉福，直到17世纪才衰落。也正是从这个世纪起，穿过欧加登的商路上又多了被掳往北方的人：掳自阿尔西等南方民族的奴隶同牲畜、皮革一道被赶往柏培拉和红海，后者始终是平原人的家底。韦尔德没有要塞或驻军看守：哪个氏族能在井边饮上自己的畜群、把别族赶开，水井就归谁。

en:
Afder, in Somali Afdheer, is the southern grazing country of the Ogaden, the semi-arid plains beyond the upper Ganale Dorya, the river that here divides Somali rangeland from the Oromo lands to the west. Darod clans of the Ogaden and the Absame families move camels and sheep between its wells. In the 15th century these pastures fell inside the wide range of the Habr Maqdi, a confederacy of the Bartire and Yabarre whose chieftains are remembered as holding the grazing grounds from the Bakool country all the way to Afder between the 14th and 18th centuries. They were Sunnis, and their herds supplied Harar and the Shebelle valley. In 1444 the plains made up the quiet southern wing of the Muslim frontier, well behind the embattled provinces of Bale and Dawaro.

The Habr Maqdi answered Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi's jihad with the largest of all the Somali contingents, and the Futuh al-Habasha names both the Bartire and the Yabarre among his forces. Oromo migrants later spread over the flat plains of Bale to the north, while the Afder grazing grounds stayed in Somali hands and the Maqdi chieftainship endured here into the 18th century. The Bartire also kept their long tie with the emirs of Harar: after the emirate broke away in 1647, Harari caravans crossed Afder as they had before, buying livestock, hides and ivory for the Red Sea markets.
zh:
阿夫德（索马里语名Afdheer）是欧加登南部的牧地，加纳莱·多里亚河上游以外的半干旱平原；这条河在此把索马里牧场同西面的奥罗莫地区分开。欧加登人和阿布萨梅等达鲁德系氏族赶着骆驼和羊群往来于各处水井。15世纪时，这些牧场落在哈卜尔·马克迪联盟的广阔游域之内：这个由巴尔蒂雷、亚巴雷两支组成的联盟，相传14至18世纪间其酋长的辖地从巴科勒一直延伸到阿夫德。他们是逊尼派穆斯林，牧群供应哈勒尔和谢贝利河谷。1444年，在战火频仍的巴勒和达瓦罗两省身后，这片平原构成穆斯林边疆安静的南翼。

响应艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的圣战号召时，哈卜尔·马克迪出动的兵力为索马里诸部之冠，《Futuh al-Habasha》（征服阿比西尼亚）把巴尔蒂雷和亚巴雷两支都记在了他的军中。奥罗莫移民后来遍布北面巴勒的平坦原野，阿夫德的牧场却始终留在索马里人手中，马克迪酋长的势力在此延续到18世纪。巴尔蒂雷人同哈勒尔埃米尔的老关系也没有断：1647年哈勒尔酋长国自立后，哈勒尔商队照旧穿过阿夫德，收购牲畜、皮革和象牙，运往红海市场。

en:
Beledweyne is the chief crossing of the middle Shebelle in Hiran: the river cuts the town in two, and pastoral tracks from the Ogaden meet the caravan road running south to Mogadishu, some 345 kilometres away. In 1444 the valley belonged to the Ajuran Sultanate, the Somali power that dammed and diked the Shebelle and dug the great stone wells on which herds and caravans depended. Hold the wells and fords, and the Hawiye pastoralists and the river farmers paid tribute; livestock, hides and water counted for more here than the merchandise of the coastal cities.

Ajuran rule came to an end at one of those wells. The rulers had decreed that the Darandoolle and other Hiraab clans could water their herds only by night; the Darandoolle gathered instead, found the Ajuran imam seated on a rock beside the well of Ceel Cawl, and killed him. Tradition has it that the sword stroke split his body and the rock beneath him together. The Gaaljecel, Baadicade and Xawaadle of the upper and middle valley fought on for years before they joined forces and drove the Ajuran out. By 1700 the Hiraab confederation held the country from the Shebelle to Mudug and the Benadir coast, and the Beledweyne crossing passed to the pastoral clans and their caravans.
zh:
贝兰德文（通行译名贝莱德文）是希兰地区谢贝利河中游最重要的渡口：河水把城镇分成东西两半，来自欧加登的牧道在此接上南下摩加迪沙的商路，两地相距约345公里。1444年，这片河谷属于阿朱兰苏丹国。阿朱兰人在谢贝利河上修筑堤坝，又开凿巨大的石井，牧民和商队都靠这些水源；把持水井和渡口，就能向哈维耶游牧民和河畔农户征贡。在这里，牲畜、兽皮和用水权比海港城市的货物更要紧。

阿朱兰的统治正是在一口水井边终结的。统治者曾下令，达兰多莱和其他希拉布氏族只能在夜里饮牲口；达兰多莱人反而聚集起来，找到正坐在塞尔考勒井旁岩石上的阿朱兰伊玛目，把他杀死。相传这一剑连人带身下的岩石一同劈开。谢贝利河中上游的加勒杰勒、巴迪卡德和哈瓦德莱人又苦战多年，才合力把阿朱兰人赶走。到1700年，希拉布联盟的地盘已从谢贝利河延伸到穆杜格和贝纳迪尔海岸，贝兰德文渡口也转入游牧氏族和他们的商队手中。

en:
Gedo is the upper Jubba country above the Dawa confluence, where the river, here called the Ganane, swings around Luuq in a horseshoe bend. Digil and Mirifle clans farmed and grazed stock along its banks, and Luuq grew into the main emporium on the caravan road from the Benadir coast into southern Ethiopia. Bender-Luuq merchants drew coffee, gold, slaves and ivory out of the interior and sent the goods on to Bardera and the sea, some as far as the markets of Southeast Asia. In 1444 Ajuran governors kept that road open, the sultanate's wells and staging posts linking the river towns of the Jubba and the Shebelle.

Under the Geledi federation the Gasaaragude dynasty ruled the upper Jubba and made Luuq its garrison town, where recruits trained, weapons were made and state prisoners were held. Its merchants kept weights and measures, gave credit and signed written contracts. They sold Benadir cotton cloth to the Arsi and Borana Oromo for cattle, then traded the cattle to inland hunters for ivory, the most prized commodity of all. In 1811 Captain Thomas Smee, reporting to British India, found a heavily fortified town of more than two thousand stone houses, with mosques and roads, and palaces and castles at its centre.
zh:
盖多是达瓦河汇流处以上的朱巴河上游地区。当地称这段河道为加纳内河，河水绕着卢格兜出一个马蹄形大河弯。迪吉尔与米里弗莱诸氏族在河畔农耕放牧，卢格则发展成贝纳迪尔海岸通往埃塞俄比亚南部商路上最大的商埠。本德尔-卢格商人从内陆收来咖啡、黄金、奴隶和象牙，经巴尔代雷转运出海，有些货物一直远销东南亚市场。1444年，阿朱兰总督维持着这条商路，苏丹国的水井和驿站把朱巴河与谢贝利河上的城镇串在一起。

格勒迪联盟时期，加萨拉古德王朝统治朱巴河上游，把卢格经营成军镇：新兵在此训练，武器在此打造，国家囚犯也关押在此。城中商人使用度量衡、凭信用赊贷、签订书面契约。他们把贝纳迪尔棉布卖给阿尔西和博兰纳的奥罗莫人换取牛只，再用牛向内陆猎人换取象牙，而象牙是所有货物里最值钱的一种。1811年，向英属印度当局报告的托马斯·斯米船长看到一座设防坚固的城镇：两千多所石屋，清真寺和道路齐备，城中心还建有宫殿和堡楼。

en:
Warsheikh is a small coastal town on the arid Banaadir shore, about seventy kilometres north of Mogadishu, where camel and sheep herds from the dry inland are driven down for sale and export. Somali tradition identifies the place with Sarapion, the harbour named in the first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, though modern scholars place Sarapion somewhere between Warsheikh and Mogadishu. In the Middle Ages it was an early Muslim settlement of trade and learning and one of the chief towns of the Sultanate of Mogadishu, whose Fakhr al-Din rulers struck their own coin and sent ships to Egypt, Arabia and China; like the rest of the coast, it also lay within the Ajuran hegemony. In 1444 the sultan in Mogadishu held the town, which lived by its roadstead and its livestock trade.

The Portuguese sacked the Swahili cities farther south and burned Barawa in 1507, but they never forced Mogadishu or its ports, and Warsheikh went on shipping livestock under its old rulers. That order ended at the close of the seventeenth century, when the Hiraab clans rose against Ajuran rule and the Yacquubi imams took Mogadishu. Warsheikh passed to their new Hiraab Imamate and was governed locally by Abgaal chiefs, the lords of this shore through the eighteenth century.
zh:
瓦尔希赫是贝纳迪尔干旱海岸上的一座滨海小镇，在摩加迪沙以北约七十公里，干旱腹地的驼群和羊群被赶到这里出售、装船出海。索马里传统把此地认作公元1世纪《厄立特里亚海航行记》所记的古港萨拉皮翁，但现代学者多把萨拉皮翁的位置推定在瓦尔希赫与摩加迪沙之间。中世纪时，这里是最早的穆斯林商贸与学术据点之一，也是摩加迪沙苏丹国的首要城镇之一；统治该国的法赫尔丁王朝自铸钱币，商船远达埃及、阿拉伯和中国。与海岸其他地方一样，它也处在阿朱兰的霸权之下。1444年，城镇归属摩加迪沙的苏丹，靠锚地和牲畜贸易为生。

葡萄牙人劫掠了更南方的斯瓦希里诸城，1507年又焚毁巴拉韦，却始终没能迫降摩加迪沙及其属港，瓦尔希赫在旧主人治下继续做牲畜出海的生意。17世纪末，希拉布诸部起兵反抗阿朱兰，雅库比家族的伊玛目夺取摩加迪沙，这一秩序才告终结。瓦尔希赫随之转入希拉布伊玛目国，由当地的阿布加尔酋长治理；整个18世纪，这片海岸都在他们手中。

en:
Hobyo is an open anchorage on the arid Mudug coast, between low dunes and the interior pastures
and sorghum lands. It was founded in the thirteenth century as one of the Ajuran Sultanate's
coastal outposts, close to Mareeg. Herders brought camels, cattle, sheep and goats to its market,
while farming settlements such as El Dher and Harardhere supplied sorghum and beans. In 1444 the
Sunni Somali port belonged to Ajuran, whose governors watched the goods moving between the
Shabelle valley, the dry lands of Mudug and ships sailing down the Somali shore.

The Hiraab rising of the late seventeenth century ended Ajuran rule. Local tradition describes
the new order as an alliance of related groups: army leaders and advisers shared authority, a qadi
handled Islamic judgments, and the hereditary imam came from its senior line. By 1700 the Hiraab
Imamate ran from the Shabelle valley across Mudug to Hobyo, and the port remained in its hands in
1821. Hobyo exported livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins, imported rice, clothing and
textiles, and provisioned coasting ships. Merchants also came here seeking precious metals and
pearls.
zh:
霍比奥是干旱的穆杜格海岸上的开放锚地，位于低矮沙丘与内陆牧场、高粱地之间。它在13世纪
作为阿朱兰苏丹国的沿海据点建立，邻近马雷格。牧人把骆驼、牛、绵羊和山羊赶到它的市场，
埃勒德尔、哈拉尔代雷等农耕聚落则供应高粱和豆类。1444年，这座逊尼派索马里港口属于阿朱兰，
谢贝利河谷、穆杜格旱地与沿索马里海岸南下船只之间流转的货物，都在阿朱兰长官的监视之下。

17世纪末的希拉布起兵终结了阿朱兰统治。当地口传把新政权描述为有亲缘关系的诸部联盟：
军事首领和顾问分管权力，卡迪执掌伊斯兰审判，世袭伊玛目则出自长支。到1700年，希拉布
教长国的势力已从谢贝利河谷穿过穆杜格，抵达霍比奥；1821年，这座港口仍在它手中。
霍比奥输出牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干，输入稻米、衣服和织物，也为沿岸航行的船只补给。
商人还到此寻求贵金属和珍珠。

en:
Galkayo is a run of wells and pasture on the dry Mudug plains, the border ground where Darod clans pushing south met Hawiye clans coming up from the coast. Both sides watered camels, sheep and cattle at the wells in the dry season and fought over them when the rains failed. No town stood here in 1444. The herds and hides of Mudug moved instead through Hobyo on the coast, a harbour the Ajuran empire had founded as a northern outpost in the thirteenth century, where Ajuran governors and Somali caravan traders loaded them onto Indian Ocean ships. The grazers were Sunni Muslims, and the empire's hold on these dry marches ran through kinship and trade, not garrisons.

In the late seventeenth century the Hiraab, a Hawiye confederation, overthrew Ajuran rule and set up their own imamate, whose power through the next century ran from the Shabelle valley and the Benaadir coast to the arid edge of Mudug. Hobyo prospered under the new order: livestock, hides, aromatic woods and raisins went out, rice and cloth came in, merchants bought textiles, precious metals and pearls there, and coasting vessels stopped to provision before the run south to Mogadishu. Around Galkayo's wells the old feud between Darod and Hawiye ran on whichever dynasty ruled the coast, and in 1821 the place was still a nomads' meeting ground rather than a town.
zh:
加勒卡约是干旱的穆杜格平原上一串有水井和牧场的地方，南移的达鲁德氏族与从海岸北上的哈维耶人在这里交界。旱季双方都在井边给骆驼、羊和牛饮水，雨水不济时便为水井厮杀。1444年这里还没有城镇。穆杜格的畜群和兽皮改从海边的霍比奥出海：那是阿朱兰帝国13世纪设立的北方据点，阿朱兰官吏和索马里商队在那里把货物装上印度洋的船。牧民都是逊尼派穆斯林，帝国对这片干旱边地的控制靠姻亲和贸易维持，不设驻军。

17世纪末，哈维耶人的希拉布联盟推翻阿朱兰，建立自己的伊玛目政权，此后一个世纪，其势力从谢贝利河谷、贝纳迪尔海岸一直伸到穆杜格的干旱边缘。霍比奥在新秩序下兴盛起来：牲畜、兽皮、香木和葡萄干外运，大米和布匹输入，商人在此购买纺织品、贵金属和珍珠，沿岸南下摩加迪沙的船只也在此停泊补给。加勒卡约水井边达鲁德与哈维耶的旧怨，并不管海岸上是哪个王朝当家；1821年，这里仍是游牧者会聚之地，而不是一座城镇。

en:
El Buur, or Ceelbuur, lies among the low hills and wells of inland Galguduud, where tracks from Hiran, the Ogaden, Mudug and Warsheikh meet. The Murusade branch of the Hawiye have lived here since at least the thirteenth century, and in 1444 the town was a local market of the Ajuran Sultanate. Its particular trade was stone. The hills yield meerschaum, the pale, soft mineral also called sepiolite, and El Buur's carvers cut it into the dabqaad, the one- or two-handled incense burner whose Somali name means 'fire-raiser' and which is used in households across Somalia, Ethiopia and Djibouti; they also carve pipe bowls, and the caravans carry both out through the Benadir ports.

When Ajuran rule collapsed, the Habar Gidir and Duduble fought the sultanate's forces out of Galguduud and Mudug after a hard struggle, and by 1700 the country lay within the inland arc of the Hiraab Imamate, which ran from the Shebelle valley through the dry country toward Mudug and the coast between Mogadishu and Hobyo. El Buur stayed a Murusade caravan market: herdsmen brought livestock and hides down from the pastures, and the quarried burners and pipes went back with the caravans toward the coast.
zh:
埃勒布尔（Ceelbuur）位于加勒古杜德内陆的低丘与水井之间，希兰、欧加登、穆杜格和瓦尔谢赫方向的道路在此交会。哈维耶人的穆鲁萨德支系至迟在13世纪已定居于此；1444年，这座城镇是阿朱兰苏丹国的一处地方集市。它的独门生意是石头：周围丘陵出产海泡石，一种色浅质软的矿石，埃勒布尔的匠人把它雕成dabqaad香炉，这种香炉有单柄或双柄，索马里语名字意为「引火之物」，索马里、埃塞俄比亚和吉布提的人家普遍使用；匠人也雕刻烟斗。香炉和烟斗都由商队经贝纳迪尔诸港运出。

阿朱兰统治崩溃时，哈巴尔·吉迪尔人与杜杜布莱人经苦战把苏丹国的势力赶出加勒古杜德和穆杜格。到1700年，这一带已纳入希拉布伊玛目国的内陆势力圈，其地盘从谢贝利河谷穿过干旱地带，延伸到穆杜格以及摩加迪沙与霍比奥之间的海岸。埃勒布尔始终是穆鲁萨德人的商队集市：牧民从牧场赶来牲畜、送来兽皮，石料雕成的香炉和烟斗则随回程商队运往沿海。

en:
Bosaso, historically Bender Qassim, lies on the Bari coast at the mouth of the Baalade valley, on the stretch of shore the Greeks knew as Mosylon. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea calls Mosylon the great cinnamon market of these coasts, its 'Mosyllitic' bark carried away in large ships, and most scholars now place that lost emporium at or near Bosaso. The anchorage takes its name from Qasim, a trader said to have settled here in the fourteenth century, whose favourite camel was called Boosaas. The Kaptallah were its first settlers, and for centuries the Dishiishe and other Harti clans of the Darod family held the coast, shipping frankincense, dates, skins and livestock to Arabian ports. In 1444 it was a chain of small Muslim fishing and trading roadsteads under its own clan elders, within the loose orbit of Adal.

In 1520 the ships of the Portuguese embassy to Abyssinia watered along this coast between Cape Guardafui and Mount Felis. Francisco Álvares went ashore to buy goats and found a sterile land where thick cloth served as money and white gum was gathered for caulking hulls, under a local ruler who reigned subject to Adel. In the following centuries the Majeerteen, another Harti clan, built up a kingdom on the Guardafui peninsula: oral tradition places its first rulers in the late fifteenth or sixteenth century, and by the late eighteenth it was a centralised sultanate with a strong seafaring tradition. Bender Qassim remained a Dishiishe harbour within that Harti maritime world, its dhows carrying the frankincense of the interior hills to Arabian and Indian ports.
zh:
博萨索旧称班达尔·卡西姆，位于巴里海岸、巴拉代河谷入海处，古希腊人称作莫西隆的那段海岸就在这一带。《厄立特里亚海航行记》把莫西隆写成这一带最大的肉桂市场，「莫西隆肉桂」由大型商船运走；多数学者现在把这座失落的商港定在博萨索或其附近。这处锚地得名于商人卡西姆，据说他14世纪在此定居，最心爱的骆驼名叫博萨斯，后来的地名就从这峰骆驼而来。卡普塔拉人是最早的定居者，此后数百年间，达鲁德族系下的迪希谢等哈提氏族据有这片海岸，把乳香、椰枣、兽皮和牲畜运往阿拉伯港口。1444年，这里是一连串穆斯林小渔村和贸易锚地，由本地氏族长老自行治理，处在阿达尔势力松散的辐射之下。

1520年，出使阿比西尼亚的葡萄牙船队在瓜达富伊角与费利斯山之间的海岸补充淡水。弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯上岸买羊，发现这是一片贫瘠之地：厚布在这里充当货币，人们采集白色树胶填补船缝，当地统治者则「臣属于阿达尔」。此后数百年间，同为哈提氏族的马吉尔廷人在瓜达富伊半岛建起王国：口述传统把其早期统治者置于15世纪末或16世纪，到18世纪晚期它已是一个号令集中、以航海见长的苏丹国。班达尔·卡西姆则始终是迪希谢人的港口，属于这个哈提航海世界，独桅船把内地山丘的乳香运往阿拉伯和印度。

en:
Hamasien is the highland basin around Asmara, the central part of the Eritrean plateau between the Red Sea hills and the Mereb River. After the long movements of Beja and Agaw peoples that followed the fall of Aksum, its villages were Tigrinya-speaking Christian communities, each largely ruling itself through a kantiba chief and a council of elders. Emperor Zara Yaqob drew them together in the mid-fifteenth century under the Bahr Negash, the 'King of the Sea', who resided at Debarwa and controlled the tracks down to Massawa. Gold, ivory and enslaved people went seaward along them, and imported weapons came back up. In 1444 Hamasien was the Christian highland core of Medri Bahri, its chiefs tied through Debarwa to the emperor's tributary empire.

The Portuguese priest Francisco Alvares reached Debarwa in 1520 and described its court: the Bahr Negash Dori, an uncle of Emperor Lebna Dengel, received tribute of horses, textiles and carpets, claimed authority north as far as Suakin, supplied the churches of his land with all they needed, and was then fighting the Nubians of Taka, five or six days' march away, who had killed his son. The wars of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi later killed the local governor, and after the Ottomans took Massawa in 1557 their troops raided up into the basin in 1559 and were driven back. Bahr Negash Yeshaq later joined the Turks and fell with them at Addi Qarro in 1578. An Ottoman army seized Debarwa in 1587, but the local chief Aquba Michael harried its columns, Emperor Sarsa Dengel retook the town and killed the Turkish pasha, and by 1589 the Turks held only the coast. In the seventeenth century the hereditary Deki Teshim governors ruled from Tsazega and unified local customary law, before their descendants split into the rival houses of Tsazega and Hazega. When James Bruce came in 1770, Medri Bahri was still a power apart from the Abyssinian court, and often at war with it.
zh:
哈马森是阿斯马拉周围的高原盆地，地处厄立特里亚高地中部，位于红海山地与马雷布河之间。阿克苏姆衰落后，贝扎人和阿高人相继迁入，这里的村落成为说提格里尼亚语的基督教社群，大多由坎蒂巴酋长和长老会议自行治理。15世纪中期，皇帝扎拉·雅各布把他们整合到驻德巴尔瓦的巴赫勒·尼加什，即「海王」麾下；通往马萨瓦的山路也由其掌握，黄金、象牙和奴隶顺路南运，武器则反向输入。1444年，哈马森是梅德利巴赫里的基督教高地核心，本地首领经由德巴尔瓦臣属于皇帝的纳贡帝国。

葡萄牙神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯1520年抵达德巴尔瓦，记下了这座小城的宫廷：巴赫勒·尼加什多里是皇帝勒布纳·丹格尔的舅父，收受马匹、织物和地毯为贡，宣称威权北至萨瓦金，为境内教堂置办所需之物；当时他正出兵征讨塔卡的努比亚人，那里在五六天路程之外，对方杀了他的儿子。艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣·加齐的战争后来杀死了当地长官。奥斯曼人1557年夺取马萨瓦，1559年又派军突入盆地，被击退。巴赫勒·尼加什伊沙克后来倒向土耳其人，1578年一同战死于阿迪卡罗。1587年奥斯曼大军攻占德巴尔瓦，但本地首领阿库巴·米卡埃尔不断截击其队伍，皇帝萨尔萨·登格尔收复该城、阵斩土耳其帕夏，到1589年土耳其人只剩沿海据点。17世纪，世袭的德基·特希姆统治者以察泽加为中心统辖一方，统一了当地习惯法；其后人后来分裂为察泽加和哈泽加两个对立家族。詹姆斯·布鲁斯1770年到访时，梅德利巴赫里仍是独立于阿比西尼亚朝廷之外的政权，双方还时常交战。

en:
Hafun occupies a low headland joined to the mainland by a long sandspit, the easternmost inhabited point of Africa; a sheltered bay opens onto the Guardafui Channel, where the Indian Ocean current presses southbound ships toward the cape. It is the ancient Opone. A Greek pilot's guide of the first century CE, the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, calls Opone a market town that produced more cinnamon than anywhere else on the coast and tortoiseshell better than any other; tombs excavated at nearby Damo have yielded Mediterranean and Persian Gulf pottery, some pieces going back to Mycenaean Greece. By 1444 the old emporium was a Somali fishing and trading settlement of Sunni Muslims, who gathered frankincense in the hills and scraped salt from the shore pans.

From the mid-seventeenth century Hafun was counted a core land of the Majeerteen sultanate, the Migiurtinia of European maps, and the place its rulers guarded most: a fortress rose at Ras Hafun to watch the channel. The sultan's boats used the bay as a roadstead and carried gum, frankincense, dried fish and salt north to Aden and the Red Sea ports, returning with cloth and dates. Ships the current drove onto the headland were a regular hazard, and wrecked cargo, salvage and the ransom of crews joined the incense trade as the coast's living. In 1821 Hafun remained a small, wind-battered Majeerteen port.
zh:
哈丰是一座由长沙嘴与大陆相连的低矮岬角，为非洲有人居住的最东端；一处避风海湾对着瓜达富伊海峡，印度洋的海流把南下的船只往海角方向推。这里就是古代的奥波内。成书于公元1世纪的希腊航海指南《厄立特里亚海航行记》把奥波内记作一处商埠，产出的肉桂为沿岸之最，玳瑁也甲于他处；在附近达莫发掘的墓葬中，出土了地中海和波斯湾的陶器，最古的甚至可上溯到迈锡尼时代的希腊。到1444年，这座古商埠已成了索马里人的渔村和贸易点，居民是逊尼派穆斯林，在山间采乳香，从岸边盐池刮盐。

从17世纪中叶起，哈丰被算作马吉尔廷苏丹国（欧洲地图上的米朱提尼亚）的核心疆土，也是统治者最看重的地方：拉什哈丰角筑起要塞，监视海峡。苏丹的船以海湾为锚地，把树胶、乳香、鱼干和盐北运亚丁和红海港口，再载回布匹和椰枣。被海流推上岬角的沉船是常有的祸事，沉船货物、打捞救助和船员赎金，与熏香生意并列，成了沿岸的生计。1821年，哈丰仍是马吉尔廷治下一座常受海风扑打的小港。

en:
Las Khorey is an anchorage of the Maakhir coast, where the frankincense-bearing Cal Madow mountains come down to the Gulf of Aden. In the thirteenth century Dhidhin, chief of the Warsangali branch of the Darod, rose to power on this shore and took the title of Garaad, founding the line that ruled these mountains for centuries. His people pastured camels, grew dates in the coastal wadis and gathered frankincense and gum arabic for Arabian and Indian dhows; Las Khorey itself long remained little more than a well and a beach. In 1444 it lay in the Warsangali domain on the Sunni Muslim coast of northern Somalia, facing Arabia across the gulf.

The town dates to 1735, when the Warsangali merchant-shaykh Ali Mahmud Nuh dug a well, built a mosque and raised a fortress there. Its ships then opened trade with Arabia, India, the Swahili coast and Zanzibar, and the coasting vessels were built on the beach. Garaad Mohamed II, who ruled from 1721 to 1764, moved the Warsangali capital to the new harbour, one of nine fortified ports through which the Maakhir state ran the frankincense trade of the gulf; its merchants crossed to Arabia to lease rights to frankincense trees there, and their fleets sailed twice a monsoon in company with the merchants of Murcanyo. Mohamed's son Ali II took the title of sultan in 1764. In 1809 the British traveller Henry Salt mapped old towers and castles along the shore, some already ruined in local wars, and Sultan Mahmud II, enthroned in 1804, set about repairing them. By then Las Khorey was the chief harbour of the Warsangali state.
zh:
拉斯戈赖是马希尔海岸的一处锚地，盛产乳香的阿尔马多山脉在此俯临亚丁湾。13世纪，达鲁德族系瓦尔桑盖利分支的首领迪丁在这一带兴起，采用「加拉德」称号，开创了统治这片山区数百年的王统。他的部众放牧骆驼，在沿海涸谷里栽种椰枣，采集乳香和阿拉伯树胶，供阿拉伯和印度的独桅船收购；拉斯戈赖本身长期不过是一口井、一片海滩。1444年，它属于瓦尔桑盖利在索马里北部逊尼派穆斯林海岸上的领地，隔湾与阿拉伯相望。

城镇始于1735年，瓦尔桑盖利的商人谢赫·阿里·马哈茂德·努赫在此挖井，建起清真寺和堡垒。港中船只随即开通了与阿拉伯、印度、斯瓦希里海岸和桑给巴尔的贸易，跑沿海航线的船就在海滩上打造。1721至1764年在位的加拉德·穆罕默德二世把都城迁到这座新港；马希尔国家靠九处设防港口经营亚丁湾的乳香贸易，拉斯戈赖便是其中之一。商人渡海到阿拉伯，租下当地乳香树的采收权，船队还与穆尔卡尼奥的商人结伴，每个季风季同行两趟。穆罕默德之子阿里二世于1764年改称苏丹。1809年，英国旅人亨利·索尔特把沿岸的古堡碉楼绘入地图，有些已在地方混战中残破；1804年继位的苏丹马哈茂德二世着手修缮。此时拉斯戈赖已是瓦尔桑盖利国家的首要港口。

en:
Sanaag is the mountain country behind the Maakhir coast, where the frankincense woods of the Cal Madow run down to roadsteads on the Gulf of Aden. Its oldest harbour is Maydh, already marked on the maps of the medieval Egyptian Book of Curiosities. Tradition says Sheikh Isaaq ibn Ahmad al-Hashimi, an Arab scholar, crossed from Arabia and settled the town in the twelfth or thirteenth century; the great Isaaq clan family counts him its ancestor, and pilgrims came to pray at his domed tomb. Ahmad ibn Majid listed Maydh among the notable ports of the Somali coast, and Duarte Barbosa later found meat plentiful there but trade small, as at a town of pilgrims. In 1444 Sunni Somali herdsmen and sailors held the shore under their Warsangali garaads, and the port owed allegiance to the sultans of Adal.

In 1520 the Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares landed at Maydh with the embassy to Abyssinia. The townspeople had fled into the mountains; he counted fifty or sixty hearths, two mosques and a Quranic school, his ships dug fresh wells and filled more than a thousand casks in three days, and the crews burned the houses and small craft when they sailed away. At the Battle of Shimbra Kure in 1529 the Harti of Maydh held the left wing of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim's army, men the Futuh al-Habash calls 'a people not given to yielding'. In later centuries Habr Yunis clansmen cut frankincense in the mountains behind the town, Arab and Banyan merchants called for hides, and old Isaaq clansmen came to spend their last years beside Sheikh Isaaq's tomb, until the graveyard ran a mile in every direction. Inland stand the ruins of Maduna, a trading town whose mosque keeps walls three metres high, dated to the fifteenth to seventeenth centuries.
zh:
萨纳格是马希尔海岸背后的山乡，阿尔马多山脉的乳香林顺着山坡一直延到亚丁湾的各处锚地。这里最古老的港口是迈德，中世纪埃及地志《奇物志》的地图上已标出它的位置。相传12或13世纪，阿拉伯学者谢赫·伊萨克·伊本·艾哈迈德·哈希米渡海到此、定居建镇；庞大的艾萨克氏族体系奉他为始祖，信众前来拜谒他的圆顶陵墓。航海家艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德把迈德列入索马里海岸的名港，杜阿尔特·巴尔博扎后来则说这里肉食充足、生意冷清，正是朝圣地的模样。1444年，信奉逊尼派的索马里牧人与水手在瓦尔桑盖利加拉德们治下据有海岸，港口效忠于阿达尔苏丹。

1520年，随葡萄牙使团前往阿比西尼亚的神父弗朗西斯科·阿尔瓦雷斯在迈德登陆，居民已躲进山里；他点到五六十户人家、两座清真寺和一所古兰经学校。船队新挖水井，三天内注满一千多只水桶，离去时又放火烧毁民房和小船。1529年的辛卜拉库雷之战中，迈德的哈尔蒂人列在伊玛目艾哈迈德·伊本·易卜拉欣的军队左翼，《阿比西尼亚战记》称他们「是一群不肯屈服的人」。此后数百年，哈布尔尤尼斯人在城后山中割取乳香，阿拉伯和巴尼亚商人来此收购兽皮，年迈的艾萨克人纷纷到此度过余生、葬在谢赫·伊萨克身旁，墓园扩展到方圆一英里。内陆的马杜纳商镇遗址留有三米高的清真寺残墙，断代在15至17世纪之间。

en:
Ankober stands on the eastern escarpment of the Ethiopian Highlands, where the cool Amhara plateau of northern Shewa falls away to the arid lowlands of the Afar. Behind it lie Menz and Tegulet, the oldest Christian Amhara country, from which Yekuno Amlak set out to overthrow the Zagwe in 1270. The escarpment tracks carried caravans and armies between the plateau and the Muslim coastlands, and the surrounding grain fields and pastures fed the imperial camps. In 1444 this was royal demesne of Zara Yaqob's Christian empire, a guarded frontier facing Adal.

A dozen years later Zara Yaqob built Debre Birhan just west of the escarpment, after the celestial light of 1456; under his successors the court drifted away and the town shrank to a large village. During Ahmad Gran's wars it served first the emperor and then the imam as a mustering ground, and Gran harangued his troops there in 1535 before marching north. When the Oromo expansion cut Shewa off from Gondar, the Amhara of Menz kept their mountains and their faith, and Negasi Krestos built his power among them about 1682; later Shoans called Menz the source of the Amhara. In the mid-eighteenth century his descendant Amha Iyasus moved the Shewan capital from Doqaqit to Ankober, which crowns the escarpment and commands the road into the lowlands. The meridazmachs held their court on the hilltop through the Era of Princes, its palaces and churches ringing the summit, though one king, Wossen Seged, preferred his seat at Qundi.
zh:
安科伯尔位于埃塞俄比亚高地东缘的陡崖上，凉爽的北绍阿阿姆哈拉高原从这里俯临干燥的阿法尔低地。崖后的门兹和特古莱特是最古老的阿姆哈拉基督教之乡，叶库诺·阿姆拉克1270年从这里起兵推翻扎格维王朝。崖上山路往来着高原与穆斯林沿海低地之间的商队和军队，周围的粮田牧场供应皇家营帐。1444年，这里是扎拉·雅各布基督教帝国的王室领地，是面向阿达尔、处处设防的边疆。

十余年后，扎拉·雅各布在1456年天现异光之后，于陡崖以西建起德卜勒伯尔汉；后继诸君在位时朝廷渐渐离去，都城缩成一座大村庄。艾哈迈德·格兰战争期间，它先后被皇帝和伊玛目用作集结大军之地，1535年格兰北征前还在那里向军队誓师。奥罗莫扩张使绍阿与贡德尔隔绝之后，门兹的阿姆哈拉人据守山地、守住信仰，内加西·克雷斯托斯约于1682年在他们之中起家，绍阿人后来把门兹称作「阿姆哈拉之源」。18世纪中叶，他的后裔阿姆哈·伊亚苏斯把绍阿都城从多卡基特迁到安科伯尔；此城雄踞陡崖，扼守通往低地的道路。整个「王侯时代」，默里达兹马奇们在山顶设朝，宫殿和教堂环列四周，只有国王沃森·塞格德更愿意住在昆迪。

en: Togdheer takes its name from the Tug Dayr, the wide dry riverbed that carries the rains of the interior plateau down toward the Berbera coast. In 1444 it was pasture rather than a kingdom: Isaaq nomads drove camels and flocks from waterhole to waterhole, and caravans climbed from Berbera through the Sheikh pass into the Hawd and on to Harar, carrying cloth and dates and bringing back hides, ivory and slaves. In the late eighteenth century nomads began to gather at the Ceel-Gooni well on the dry valley, and the market that grew around it became Burao, the link between the port and the interior. Around the same time the Habr Yunis broke away from the Isaaq sultanate and set up their own line of sultans under Sugulle, son of the chieftain Ainanshe Hersi; Sugulle's son Deria held his court at Wadhan near the pass and taxed the caravans, and the wells and grazing of the Togdheer became the centre of Habr Yunis power.
zh: 托格代尔得名于图格达伊尔河，一条宽阔的干河床，雨季把内陆高原的雨水输向柏培拉海岸。1444年，这里是牧场而非王国：艾萨克族系的游牧民赶着驼群和羊群逐井而居，商队从柏培拉经谢赫山口登上高原，深入豪德草原、远抵哈勒尔，运去布匹和椰枣，带回兽皮、象牙和奴隶。18世纪晚期，游牧民开始聚集到干河谷上的埃勒戈尼井旁，井边长成的集市就是布拉奥，把海港与腹地连成一线。差不多同时，哈布尔尤尼斯人脱离艾萨克苏丹国，在首领艾南沙·赫尔西之子苏古勒之下建立自己的苏丹世系；苏古勒之子德里亚在山口附近的瓦丹设立驻地、向商队征税，托格代尔的水井与牧场成为哈布尔尤尼斯权力的中心。

en:
Hargeisa is the well-watered valley in the Ogo highlands behind Berbera, where the Aleyadera watercourse runs between grazing hills on the old road from the coast to Harar. Long before it was a town it was a watering stop for nomads and caravans. The Isaaq clans grazing these hills trace themselves to Sheikh Ishaaq, an Arabian scholar who settled at Maydh, and from the fifteenth century the Arap, Habr Yunis and Eidagale branches spread southwest to these wells. In 1444 the country belonged to the Adal sultanate. Caravans resting here carried ivory, coffee and slaves from the Harar and Ogaden interior down to Berbera, the busiest of the Muslim ports on this coast, whose merchants shipped much of the coffee on to Mocha in Arabia.

When the imam Ahmad Gragn conquered Abyssinia between 1529 and 1543, the Habr Magadle lancers marched with him, and the chronicle Futuh al-Habasha names two of their leaders, Ahmad Gerri and Dawid, at his battles. After Adal broke, its old inland cities fell into ruin while the Somali clans kept the wells and the caravan roads alive. In the mid-eighteenth century the Eidagale leader Abdi Eisa defeated the Absame tribes at Lafaruug near Berbera. The clan chiefs offered him the crown, but he passed it to his young son Guled, who was crowned the first sultan of the Isaaq in July 1750 with his father acting as regent. Under the Rer Guled line the sultanate taxed livestock and kept mounted raiders over the Hargeisa grazing lands, and Guled himself ruled until 1808.
zh:
哈尔格萨是柏培拉后方奥戈高原上水草丰足的谷地，阿莱亚德拉干河在牧场丘陵间流过，正处在海岸通往哈勒尔的古道上。在成为城镇之前很久，这里只是游牧民和商队歇脚补水的站点。在这一带放牧的伊萨克诸部把先祖追溯到定居迈德赫的阿拉伯学者谢赫·伊萨克，15世纪起，阿拉普、哈布尔·尤尼斯、埃达加勒等支向西南扩散，陆续来到这些水井旁。1444年，此地属于阿达尔苏丹国。在井边歇脚的商队把哈勒尔和欧加登内陆的象牙、咖啡和奴隶运往柏培拉；柏培拉是这一带穆斯林港口中最繁忙的一个，当地商人再把大批咖啡转运到阿拉伯的穆哈。

1529至1543年伊玛目艾哈迈德·格兰征服阿比西尼亚时，哈布尔·马加德勒的长矛骑兵随军出征，《丰陀哈·哈巴沙》记下他们的两位首领艾哈迈德·格里和达乌德参战。阿达尔战后崩解，内陆古城纷纷沦为废墟，索马里诸氏族却守住了水井和商道。18世纪中叶，埃达加勒首领阿卜迪·伊萨在柏培拉附近的拉法鲁格击败阿布萨梅诸部；诸部首领要推他为王，他却把位子让给年幼的儿子古莱德。1750年7月，古莱德加冕为第一位伊萨克苏丹，由父亲摄政。雷尔·古莱德一系向牲畜征税、蓄养骑马袭掠者，统治哈尔格萨的牧场，古莱德本人在位直到1808年。

en:
Barawa is a coral-stone port on the Banaadir coast south of Merca, set on a flat, briny shore facing the Indian Ocean. The Tunni Somali founded it under their saint Aw-Ali as the capital of their Tunni Sultanate, and as early as the tenth century they admitted Muslim families from Yemen and Syria. Ibn Sa'id called Barawa 'an Islamic island on the Somali coast' and named it with Mogadishu and Merca as one of the three chief cities of the shore, and students from across the Horn came to its ulama. Its craftsmen wove alindi cloth and the embroidered kufi baraawa caps, carved Qur'an rests and wedding beds, and built multi-storey coral houses whose rooftops were joined by metal-lined bridges, so that women and elders need not cross the crowded streets. Under Ajuran rule the port reached its peak: the Ming treasure fleets called there in the early fifteenth century, and Fei Xin noted its salt pans and its cargoes of frankincense, myrrh, ambergris and ivory. In 1444 Barawa was one of the richest Muslim harbours in the Ajuran realm.

Its wealth drew the Portuguese. In 1507 Tristão da Cunha and Afonso de Albuquerque brought sixteen ships before the town, which answered their summons from behind a strong wall with a reported garrison of four thousand. The Portuguese stormed the walls, gave Barawa over to sack and fire, and Tristão himself was wounded; then they sailed away without holding the port, and the townspeople who had fled inland came back and rebuilt. Barawa made its peace with the Portuguese and kept its trade. When Ajuran power collapsed at the end of the seventeenth century, the town became the chief port of the Geledi Sultanate, its wharves shared between Tunni townsmen and Swahili-speaking Bravanese merchants, who made up about a fifth of the population; harbour traffic grew with Geledi power through the eighteenth century.
zh:
巴拉韦是马尔卡以南贝纳迪尔海岸上的珊瑚石港口，坐落在低平多盐的滩涂，面朝印度洋。图尼族索马里人在圣徒奥-阿里带领下建城，作为图尼苏丹国的都城；早在10世纪，他们就接纳了来自也门和叙利亚的穆斯林家族。伊本·赛义德称巴拉韦为「索马里海岸上的伊斯兰之岛」，把它与摩加迪沙、马尔卡并列为此岸三都，非洲之角各地的学生都来投奔城中的乌理玛。工匠织造阿林迪布和绣帽「库菲·巴拉瓦」，雕制经架和婚床，还盖起多层珊瑚石屋，屋顶之间架有金属贴面的天桥，妇人和老者不必穿行拥挤的街道。阿朱兰治下，此港臻于极盛：15世纪初郑和船队曾来停泊，费信记下了这里的盐池，以及乳香、没药、龙涎香和象牙等货物。1444年，巴拉韦是阿朱兰版图内最富庶的穆斯林海港之一。

它的富庶引来了葡萄牙人。1507年，特里斯唐·达·库尼亚与阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克率十六艘船兵临城下，城方凭高墙拒答降书，据称守军有四千之众。葡萄牙人强攻登城，纵兵劫掠后纵火焚城，达·库尼亚本人也受了伤；但他们随即扬帆离去，并未占据港口，逃入内陆的居民陆续回来重建家园。巴拉韦随后与葡萄牙人议和，贸易照旧。17世纪末阿朱兰崩溃后，此城成为盖莱迪苏丹国的首要港口，码头上往来着图尼市民和讲斯瓦希里语的巴拉瓦尼商人，后者约占全城人口的五分之一；整个18世纪，盖莱迪越强，港中的船就越多。

en:
Mareeg is a sandy anchorage on the arid coast of central Somalia, on the long shore between Warsheikh and Hobyo. It was founded in the thirteenth century as a capital of the Ajuran Empire, whose Garen sultans ruled from Hobyo in the north to Kismayo in the south and west as far as Qelafo. Along this dry littoral they kept wells, garrisons and stone fortifications, and from ports like this Somali livestock and Banaadir goods were shipped to Arabia. In 1444 Mareeg was a fortified seat of Ajuran power on the northern stretch of the imperial coast.

At the end of the seventeenth century the empire crumbled under heavy taxation and clan revolt. The Hiraab imams who had taken Mogadishu extended their hold along the coast towards Hobyo, and Mareeg passed into their Hiraab Imamate. It stayed a small anchorage serving the pastoral clans of its dry hinterland through the eighteenth century, their livestock trade untouched by the European wars farther south, and in 1821 the clans around the port lived under loose Hiraab overlordship.
zh:
梅雷格是索马里中部干旱海岸上的一处沙岸锚地，在瓦尔希赫与霍比奥之间的漫长海岸线上。它建于13世纪，本是阿朱兰帝国的都城；加伦王朝的苏丹北起霍比奥、南至基斯马尤，向西一直管到克拉福。在这段干旱海岸上，他们经营水井、派驻守军、修筑石造工事，索马里牲畜和贝纳迪尔货物就从梅雷格这样的港口装船运往阿拉伯。1444年，梅雷格是阿朱兰在帝国北部海岸的一处设防治所。

17世纪末，帝国在重税和诸部反抗中瓦解。夺取了摩加迪沙的希拉布伊玛目沿海岸向霍比奥扩张，梅雷格并入他们的希拉布伊玛目国。整个18世纪，它仍是一座小锚地，为干旱腹地的游牧氏族效力，牲畜贸易没有被更南方的欧洲战事波及；到1821年，港口一带的氏族仍处在希拉布松散的宗主权之下。

en:
Pate is the largest island of the Lamu Archipelago, ringed by mangroves and cut near Siyu by a sea channel that dries into a path at low tide. Farming villages there had grown into a Muslim Swahili trading society before the fourteenth century, when Pate town became the seat of a sultanate. Pate, Siyu and Faza were coral stone towns that traded with Arab, Persian and Indian shipmasters, rivals of Lamu rather than any foreign colony. In 1444 a Nabahani sultan at Pate led the island's harbour politics, while Siyu in the north was already a substantial Muslim town.

When the Portuguese friar Gaspar de Santo Bernardino visited Siyu in 1606, he called it the largest town on the island. In the 1700s its Famao patricians shared rule with Somali shaykhs from a new wave of settlers, and under their schools Siyu became known along the coast for Islamic learning and copied books. Pate town remained the seat of the Nabahani sultans; Fumo Madi ibn Abi Bakr reigned there from 1776 to 1809, and succession quarrels after him weakened the court. Around 1812 the rulers of Pate and Mombasa sent a combined army against Lamu, and Lamu's men destroyed it on the dunes at Shela; after the defeat the towns of the northern coast fell increasingly under Oman. In 1821 a Nabahani ruler still sat at Pate, but the island towns no longer set the terms of Swahili commerce.
zh:
帕泰是拉穆群岛最大的岛屿，沿岸红树林环绕，西尤附近有一道海潮沟，退潮时沟底干涸成路。14世纪以前，岛上的农业村落已发展为穆斯林斯瓦希里商业社会，帕泰城此后成为苏丹国都。帕泰、西尤和法扎都是珊瑚石砌成的城邦，与阿拉伯、波斯和印度商船通商，是拉穆的对手，却不是外来者的殖民地。1444年，帕泰的纳卜汉苏丹主导岛上港湾事务，北部的西尤也已是颇具规模的穆斯林城镇。

1606年葡萄牙修士加斯帕尔·德·圣贝纳迪诺到访西尤，称它为岛上最大的城镇。18世纪，西尤的法茂望族与新迁入的索马里谢赫共主城邦；在这些谢赫的宗教学塾影响下，西尤沿整个海岸以伊斯兰学问和缮写书籍闻名。帕泰城始终是纳卜汉苏丹的王庭所在，富莫·马迪·伊本·阿比·贝克尔1776年至1809年在位，他死后的继承纷争削弱了宫廷。约1812年，帕泰与蒙巴萨合兵进攻拉穆，拉穆人在谢拉的沙丘间将其击溃；此战后北部海岸诸城镇日益落入阿曼掌控。1821年时帕泰仍坐着一位纳卜汉统治者，但岛上城邦已无力左右斯瓦希里商路的格局。

en:
Shendy lies on the east bank of the Nile, forty-five kilometres southwest of the ruins of Meroe, where the river road downstream to Egypt meets the caravan track across the Butana to the Red Sea. Its weekly market was one of the largest in northeast Africa: pilgrim caravans from West Africa passed through on the way to Mecca, goods arrived from Abyssinia and the southern Sudan, and Egyptian cotton, copper and sugar came upriver from the town of Berber. In 1444 Nubian villagers worked the irrigated fields along the bank, Arab tribes that would become the Ja'alin were taking over the carrying trade, and Shendy's lord gave only loose obedience to the Nubian kings of Dongola.

After the Funj victory of 1504 Shendy entered the Sennar system, ruled by its Ja'alin Sa'dab line with the title makk, at first through the Abdallabi viceroys at Qarri and in time paying Sennar little more than a yearly sum. When James Bruce passed through in 1772 he found the town ringed with orchards and watered fields and the greatest weekly market in Nubia, its ruler a woman named Sitna; cattle, horses, gum arabic, honey and coffee came from the interior through Sennar, and Indian spices and European glassware and sweets were brought in through Suakin. In 1814 Burckhardt joined a Shendy caravan for Suakin of more than two hundred camels and three hundred slaves, with horses bound for Yemen; the town wove its own cotton cloth. Its makk Nimr had a Ja'ali father and a mother of the Wad Ajeeb royal house of Sennar, and in March 1821 he submitted to the advancing Turco-Egyptian army of Ismail Pasha.
zh:
申迪位于尼罗河东岸，地处麦罗埃故城遗址西南45公里，顺河北去埃及的水路与东穿布塔纳、通往红海的商道在这里相接。它的周市是东北非最大的市集之一：西非前往麦加的朝圣商队从这里经过，来自阿比西尼亚和苏丹南部的货物在此集散，埃及的棉布、铜器和食糖则从柏柏尔城溯河运抵。1444年，努比亚农人耕种着河畔的水浇地，后来形成贾阿林人的阿拉伯部落正把持转运贸易，申迪的首领对栋古拉的努比亚国王只维持着松散的臣属。

1504年丰吉人取胜后，申迪被纳入森纳尔体系，由贾阿林人萨达卜家族以「马克」之衔统治，最初通过驻在盖里的阿卜杜拉布副王臣事森纳尔，后来每年只缴一笔贡金，其余事务皆自专。詹姆斯·布鲁斯1772年路过时，见到城镇四周果园与水浇地环绕，周市为努比亚之最，当政的是一位名叫西特纳的女性；牲畜、马匹、阿拉伯胶、蜂蜜和咖啡经森纳尔从内地贩来，印度香料和欧洲的玻璃器、糖果则经萨瓦金港上岸。1814年，布尔克哈特随一支申迪商队前往萨瓦金，队中有两百多峰骆驼、三百名奴隶，还有运往也门的马匹，城里也织造棉布。马克尼姆尔的父亲是贾阿林人，母亲出身森纳尔的瓦德阿吉卜王族；1821年3月，他向进抵此地的伊斯梅尔帕夏土埃军队投降。

en:
Soba stands on the Blue Nile some twenty kilometres upstream from the meeting of the two Niles. From the sixth century it was the capital of Alodia, or Alwa, southernmost and greatest of the three Christian Nubian kingdoms. The tenth-century envoy Ibn Selim el-Aswani called it a large and wealthy city of fine buildings; its churches rose in red brick, one of them converted from an older Meroitic temple, and the royal court drew traders from the Middle East, India and even China while Nubian and Greek were written in its schools. Droughts, raids from the south and the swing of trade towards the Red Sea wore the kingdom down after the twelfth century, and Arab bedouin who began moving in after 1324 steadily overran the Nile valley. In 1444 a Christian Nubian king still ruled at Soba, but his realm was reduced to the country around the capital, ringed by Muslim Arab tribes who increasingly withheld his tribute.

Around 1500 Abdallah Jammah's Arab federation, with Amara Dunqas and his Funj coming from the south, stormed and razed the Christian capital, though one tradition dates the sack to 1509. The Funj kings briefly held Soba before founding Sennar, and when the Jewish traveller David Reubeni passed by in 1523 the city was already in ruins. The surrounding country, the old Alodian heartland of the Gezira and the Butana, became the land of the Abdallab, the Arabised Nubian descendants of its people, who governed from Qarri as Funj vassals. Their shaykh Ajib al-Kafuta grew strong under Sultan Dakin, invaded the Funj heartland and for a time ruled from Dongola to the Ethiopian border, until the Funj killed him at Karkoj in 1611 or 1612; the peace that followed left the Abdallab everything north of the Nile confluence as vassal kings. In 1762 Muhammad Abu Likaylik, a Hamaj cavalry commander, seized Sennar and turned the Funj sultans into figureheads. Soba's own bricks were carried off for Sufi domed tombs, and when Ottoman Egypt founded Khartoum in 1821 the last ruins were stripped for building stone.
zh:
索巴位于青尼罗河畔，在两条尼罗河汇流处上游约二十公里。从6世纪起，它是努比亚三个基督教王国中位置最南、也最强大的阿洛迪亚（又称阿卢瓦）的都城。10世纪的使者伊本·塞利姆·阿斯瓦尼称它是一座建筑精美的富庶大城；城中教堂以红砖砌成，其中一座还是由更古老的麦罗埃神庙改建，王宫吸引着来自中东、印度乃至中国的商人，学堂里通行努比亚文和希腊文。12世纪以降，干旱、南方部族的袭扰和商路转向红海使王国日渐衰弱，1324年后迁入的阿拉伯贝都因人逐渐遍布尼罗河谷。1444年，一位信奉基督教的努比亚国王仍以索巴为都，但疆土只剩都城周围，四境尽是穆斯林阿拉伯部落，贡赋也越来越收不上来。

约1500年，阿卜杜拉·贾马的阿拉伯部落联盟，与南方阿马拉·敦卡斯率领的丰吉人一道，攻陷并夷平了这座基督教都城，另有传说把城破之日系于1509年。丰吉国王曾短暂驻留索巴，随后营建森纳尔；犹太旅人戴维·雷乌贝尼1523年途经时，城市已成废墟。都城周围的杰济拉和布塔纳本是阿洛迪亚故土，此后成为阿卜杜拉布人的地盘，他们是当地努比亚人阿拉伯化后的后裔，以凯里为中心替丰吉人治理此地。其酋长阿吉布·卡富塔在素丹达金朝内势力日盛，发兵攻入丰吉腹地，一度统辖着从栋古拉到埃塞俄比亚边境的广大地区，最终于1611或1612年在卡尔科杰被丰吉人攻杀；战后和约把两河汇流处以北全部封给阿卜杜拉布人，作为丰吉的附庸之王。1762年，哈马季骑兵将领穆罕默德·阿布·利卡伊利克夺取森纳尔，把丰吉素丹变成傀儡。索巴的砖石不断被拆去修筑苏菲圣徒的穹顶墓，1821年奥斯曼埃及营建喀土穆时，最后的遗迹也被搜刮一空充作建材。

en:
The Sennar district lies on the west bank of the Blue Nile, the southern heartland of Alodia, last of the Christian Nubian kingdoms. Its capital Soba stood downstream near the confluence of the two Niles, but royal power had long faded: by the fifteenth century the Gezira was divided among petty lords, Arab Bedouin had brought Islam and Arabic into the pastures, and the Abdallab federation of Abdallah Jammah destroyed what remained of the old kingdom. In 1444 Nubian villagers and Christian communities still lived along the river under weak local rulers.

In 1504 the Funj, pastoralists from the upper Blue Nile led by Amara Dunqas, overcame the Abdallab and built a new capital at Sennar, ruling as Muslim sultans. The Jewish traveller David Reubeni saw Amara there in 1523, moving ceaselessly about the country with great herds and mounted captains; an Ottoman admiral reported a few years later that the Funj paid the Ethiopian emperor a yearly tribute of 9,000 camels and sold him horses for his wars against Adal. When the Ottomans pushed south into Nubia the Funj destroyed their army at Hannik in 1585, and the ground just south of the Third Cataract became the border. The Abdallab sheikh Ajib made himself master of most of the kingdom before Sultan Adlan I defeated and killed him at Karkoj in 1612; Ajib's sons kept everything north of the Nile confluence as vassal kings. Sennar's wealth came from the royal caravans that carried the trade of the Ethiopian frontier to Egypt and the Hejaz, and from the gold of Fazughli, conquered under Badi II in 1665. In 1744 Badi IV routed the huge Ethiopian army of Iyasu II on the Dinder river. The sultans' slave armies then alienated the old aristocracy, and in 1762 the Hamaj cavalry commander Muhammad Abu Likaylik entered Sennar and reduced the monarchs to puppets. Civil war followed, and when the Egyptian army reached the city in June 1821 the last sultan, Badi VII, submitted in a town the invaders found reduced to heaps of ruins.
zh:
森纳尔地区位于青尼罗河西岸，是基督教努比亚古国阿勒底亚南部的腹地。阿勒底亚的都城索巴坐落在下游、靠近两河汇流处，但王权早已衰落：到15世纪，杰济拉分据于众多小首领之手，阿拉伯贝都因人把伊斯兰教和阿拉伯语带进牧场，阿卜杜拉·詹马的阿卜杜拉布联盟摧毁了古国仅存的残余。1444年时，沿河仍住着努比亚村民和基督教社群，统治他们的是弱小的地方首领。

1504年，来自青尼罗河上游的游牧民族丰吉人在阿马拉·敦卡斯率领下压服阿卜杜拉布人，在森纳尔建立新都，以穆斯林苏丹的身份统治。犹太旅行家大卫·鲁本尼1523年见到阿马拉带着大群牲畜和骑兵队长在国中不停巡行；几年后一位奥斯曼海军将领报告，丰吉人每年向埃塞俄比亚皇帝进贡九千峰骆驼，还向他出售对阿达尔苏丹国作战用的战马。奥斯曼军队南下努比亚时，丰吉人1585年在哈尼克将其击溃，第三瀑布以南的战场随之成为两国边界。阿卜杜拉布谢赫阿吉卜一度成为大半个王国的主人，直到1612年苏丹阿德兰一世在卡尔科季将他击败击杀；阿吉卜的儿子们保住了尼罗河汇流处以北的土地，作为藩属小王继续统治。森纳尔的财富来自皇家商队，它们经营着通往埃及和汉志的贸易，又有1665年巴迪二世征服法祖格利后源源而来的黄金。1744年，巴迪四世在丁德尔河畔击溃伊亚苏二世的埃塞俄比亚大军。后来苏丹的奴隶军队激怒了旧贵族，1762年哈马吉骑兵将领穆罕默德·阿布·利凯里克进入森纳尔，把苏丹降为傀儡。随后内战连绵，1821年6月埃及军队兵临城下时，末代苏丹巴迪七世出城投降；入城者看到，这座曾经富庶的名城只剩一堆堆废墟。

en:
The poet al-Harrani, writing at the end of the thirteenth century, called the capital of Alodia 'Waylula': the king's city, he wrote, stood on the west bank of the Nile and was 'very large'. Alodia was the southernmost and last of the Christian Nubian kingdoms, and its capital Soba, near the confluence of the two Niles, had once been described as a town of dwellings, gardens and churches full of gold. Drought, plague and Arab tribes moving up the river had broken the kingdom since. In 1444 Nubian farmers worked the White Nile's western bank with a half-remembered Christianity and no priests, Bedouin grazed their herds on the plain behind, and the king in Soba ruled little beyond his crumbling town.

Around 1500 Soba was destroyed, by the Arab chief Abdallah Jammah in some accounts and by the Funj in others, and in 1504–05 the Funj king Amara Dunqas founded the sultanate of Sennar. The river villages entered the Blue Sultanate, where Sufi holy men taught Islam and Arabic slowly displaced Nubian, still heard along the Nile into the nineteenth century. The west-bank crossing carried caravans and West African pilgrims bound for Mecca. After the Hamaj seized Sennar in 1762 the sultanate lapsed into civil war, and in June 1821 its last ruler, Badi VII, submitted to the Egyptian army of Muhammad Ali Pasha led by his son Ismail; the west bank passed to Egypt.
zh:
13世纪末的诗人哈拉尼把阿勒底亚的都城称作「瓦伊卢拉」：他写道，这座王城位于尼罗河西岸，「极其宏大」。阿勒底亚是努比亚基督教诸王国中最南、也是最后一个；都城索巴靠近尼罗河两河汇流处，曾被形容为满城宅邸、花园，教堂中满是黄金。此后旱灾、瘟疫和沿河迁入的阿拉伯部落瓦解了这个王国。1444年，努比亚农人在白尼罗河西岸耕作，守着没有祭司、只剩模糊记忆的基督教，贝都因人在身后的平原放牧，索巴的国王号令不出残破的城池。

约1500年索巴被毁，有说法归于阿拉伯首领阿卜杜拉·詹马，也有说法归于丰吉人；1504至1505年，丰吉国王奥马尔·冬卡建立森纳尔苏丹国。河畔村落并入「蓝苏丹国」，苏菲圣徒在此传教，阿拉伯语逐渐取代努比亚语，而直到19世纪，尼罗河畔仍听得到努比亚语。西岸渡口往来着商队，也载着取道前往麦加的西非朝圣者。1762年哈马吉人夺取森纳尔后，苏丹国陷入内战；1821年6月，末代君主巴迪七世向穆罕默德·阿里帕夏之子伊斯梅尔率领的埃军归降，西岸改属埃及。

en:
Medwa is the arid country north of Al-Fashir and east of the Kobbei caravan road, built around the Meidob volcanic field, where about 700 vents and craters are scattered across 100 by 50 kilometres of desert. The Malha crater holds springs and a salty lake, and the Midob who pasture and farm around the vents tell that fire poured from it many generations ago and the lake rose and fell with strange sounds. The Midob speak a Nubian language, while Zaghawa nomads move camels and sheep between Darfur, Kanem and the Nile. In 1444 these wells lay on the remote northern edge of Tunjur-ruled Darfur.

Around 1600 Sulayman Solong's wars brought the Zaghawa under the Keira sultans, and Medowa lay on the desert flank of a sultanate whose Kobbei caravans carried slaves, ivory, ostrich feathers and gum north to Egypt. Muhammad Tayrab's conquest of Kordofan around 1785 extended that power eastward, but the Turco-Egyptian victory near Bara in 1821 stopped short of the craters.
zh:
梅德瓦是法希尔以北、科贝商路以东的干旱之地，境内横亘着迈多布火山地，约700个喷口和火山口散布在100公里长、50公里宽的沙漠中。马勒哈火山口里有泉水和一个咸水湖，在火山口周围放牧耕作的米多布人相传，许多代以前火曾从口中喷出，湖水涨落时伴有奇怪的声响。米多布人说属努比亚语系的米多布语，扎加瓦牧民则驱赶骆驼和绵羊往来达尔富尔、卡涅姆与尼罗河之间。1444年，这些水井处在通朱尔人治下达尔富尔的遥远北缘。

1600年前后，苏莱曼·索龙的征战使扎加瓦人臣服凯拉苏丹，梅德瓦地处苏丹国的沙漠一侧，科贝商队把奴隶、象牙、鸵鸟羽和树胶北运埃及。穆罕默德·泰拉布约1785年征服科尔多凡，把势力推向东方；1821年土埃军队在巴拉附近取胜，却没有进抵这些火山口。

en:
The ruins of Kobbe line the Wadi Kobbei west of Al-Fashir, at the southern end of the Darb El Arba'in, the Forty Days Road that runs nearly 1,800 kilometres to Asyut in Egypt. Wells and stone cairns, the alamat, marked the stages across some of the driest country on earth, laid out so that water was never more than two or three days apart; Herodotus knew the road, the Romans posted a chain of guards along it, and the geographer Ibn Hawqal described it in the tenth century. In 1444, under Tunjur rule, Kobbe was the northern outlet of Darfur rather than the market it later became. Camels carried slaves, ivory, gold and salt up the road, and cloth and metals came south in exchange.

Under the Keira sultans the road grew busy from the seventeenth century, and Kobbe dealt directly with Asyut. Around 1700 arms brought from Egypt helped Sultan Ahmad Bukr repel a Wadai invasion that had reached Kabkabiya. The French traveller Charles-Jacques Poncet came down the road to Kobbe in 1698; the English edition of his voyage says arrival ended two months of travel across a thousand of the most barren miles in Africa. William George Browne was the first Englishman to ride with the caravan and write of it, in 1793, the year after Sultan Abd al-Rahman founded his new capital at Al-Fashir. By the early nineteenth century Kobbe was the largest town in Darfur, with perhaps 8,000 people, its merchants trading slaves, ostrich feathers, camels, ivory and gum arabic. The Turco-Egyptian conquest of Kordofan in 1821 stopped short of the Marrah Mountains, and Kobbe's caravans still served an independent sultanate.
zh:
科贝废墟沿科贝干河延伸，在法希尔以西，是「四十日路」的南端终点；这条路在沙漠中延伸近1800公里，直抵埃及的艾斯尤特。沿途是地球上最干旱的地带之一，水井和阿拉伯语称作阿拉马特的石堆路标标出每一段歇脚地，路上的人每隔两三天就能找到水。希罗多德已知道这条路，罗马人曾沿线设戍，地理学家伊本·豪盖勒10世纪也留下记载。1444年通朱尔人统治时，科贝是达尔富尔北方的出口，还不是后来那样的大市场。骆驼队把奴隶、象牙、黄金和盐北运，布匹和金属则南来交易。

凯拉苏丹治下，这条路从17世纪起繁忙起来，科贝与艾斯尤特直接通商。约1700年，苏丹艾哈迈德·巴克尔靠埃及运来的武器击退了一支打到卡卜卡比耶的瓦达伊大军。法国旅人夏尔-雅克·蓬塞1698年沿这条路抵达科贝，他游记的英译本写道，到达科贝时，旅人已在非洲最荒凉的土地上走了两个月、上千英里。1793年，威廉·乔治·布朗成为第一个随骆驼商队同行并写下见闻的英国人，那是阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼定都法希尔的第二年。19世纪初，科贝已有约8000人，是达尔富尔最大的城镇，商人买卖奴隶、鸵鸟羽、骆驼、象牙和阿拉伯树胶。1821年土埃军队对科尔多凡的征服止步于迈拉山，科贝的商队仍为一个独立的苏丹国效劳。

en:
The Orinoco ends in a maze of channels, low sediment islands, mangroves and palm swamps. Its brown fresh water pushes far into the Atlantic, and the first Spanish explorers took the flooded lowlands for a sea. In 1444 most of these waterlands belonged to the Warao, whose name means the boat people. Canoes carried families through the inner caños, stilt houses stood over the water, and fishing, hunting, gathering and the seasonal river rise set the pattern of village life. Warao tradition describes the delta as a refuge entered under pressure from more warlike mainland peoples; no European post yet watched the Boca de Navíos.

Christopher Columbus sighted the Paria coast in 1498 but did not enter the delta. Alonso de Ojeda recognized the Orinoco mouth in 1499, and Vicente Yáñez Pinzón explored it in 1500, calling the fresh water Río Dulce. Adventurers seeking El Dorado followed: Diego de Ordaz ascended the Orinoco in 1531, and Spanish sources place a short-lived Santo Tomás near the Caroní mouths in the following year. On 21 December 1595 Antonio de Berrío founded Santo Tomás de Guayana just above the delta approaches to guard the river route. Carib attacks and Dutch and English raids forced the settlers to move three times. Walter Raleigh's expeditions burned and plundered the town, including the raid of 1617, and its successor was fixed at Angostura in 1764.
