The first Warao mission opened in 1682, and the Jesuit Joseph Gumilla later recorded their canoes and stilt houses. During the eighteenth century Spanish governors and English officials in Trinidad tried to gather the Warao into fixed towns, but many settlements did not last and some families moved toward Suriname.
zh:
奥里诺科河在河口散成一片水网，其间分布着低平的泥沙岛、红树林和棕榈沼泽。褐色淡水远远推入大西洋，最早的西班牙探险者曾把这片泛滥低地看成海。1444年，这片水乡多数地方属于瓦劳人，他们的族名意为「船民」。独木舟载着族人穿行内部河汊，桩屋架在水面上，捕鱼、狩猎、采集和河水季节性涨落决定着村落生活。瓦劳人的口述传统把三角洲称为避难地，说他们是受大陆上更好战族群的压力才进入水网；此时还没有欧洲据点监视纳维奥斯河口。

1498年，克里斯托弗·哥伦布望见帕里亚海岸，但没有进入三角洲。1499年，阿隆索·德·奥赫达辨认出奥里诺科河口；1500年，文森特·亚涅斯·平松探查此地，把这片淡水称为「淡水河」。寻找黄金国的冒险者随后而至：1531年，迭戈·德·奥尔达斯溯奥里诺科河而上，西班牙资料称次年卡罗尼河口附近曾有一个短暂存在的圣托马斯。1595年12月21日，安东尼奥·德·贝里奥在三角洲通道稍上游建立圣托马斯·德·瓜亚纳，守卫这条河路。加勒比人的攻击以及荷兰、英格兰袭掠迫使居民三次迁移。沃尔特·雷利的远征队曾焚毁和洗劫此城，1617年的袭击便是其中一次；后继据点1764年才固定在安戈斯图拉。第一个瓦劳传教站1682年设立，耶稣会士何塞·古米利亚后来记下了他们的独木舟和水上桩屋。18世纪，西班牙总督和特立尼达的英国官员都曾试图把瓦劳人集中到固定城镇，但许多定居点未能维持，一些瓦劳家庭迁往苏里南。

en:
Guasipati, 'beautiful land' in the local Carib tongue, lies inland from the lower Orinoco, between the Caroní and the forested rise of the Guayana highlands, on rolling savanna cut by streams that run north to the great river. In 1444 Carib-speaking villagers planted cassava on the creek banks, fished and hunted, and traded by canoe with the Orinoco and the coast. No missionary or soldier had yet entered the country from Spanish Guayana.

Catalan Capuchins pushed up from the Caroní in 1724 and gathered the Caribs into mission towns. Guasipati, founded on 27 September 1757, was the eleventh town of the Missions of Caroní and El Dorado, the golden country the conquistadors had once sought on these rivers. Its own soil was thin and the other missions sent it meat and cassava, but the chain of towns around it became the granary and cattle range of Guayana Province: nineteen settlements with some 7,000 Indians by 1817, farming the best land in the province. The Capuchins opposed the revolution from 1810 and supplied the royalists with horses and provisions. In January 1817 Manuel Piar was repulsed at Angostura; he crossed the Caroní in February, took Upata on the 6th and on the 17th routed the troops of the royal governor, Lorenzo Fitzgerald. Hundreds of mission Indians marched with him as archers and spearmen, and at San Félix on 11 April, on the Chirica tableland, they helped break Miguel de la Torre's army. The victory opened the Orinoco to the republic and ended the Capuchin state. The mission warehouses, stocked with hides, tobacco, cotton and cacao, supplied the new government at Angostura, more than a thousand mission Indians were drafted into the patriot army, and the friars were carried off to confinement at Caruachi, where eighteen of them were later put to death.
zh:
瓜西帕蒂在当地加勒比语中意为「美丽的土地」，地处奥里诺科河下游内陆、卡罗尼河与圭亚那高原林坡之间，起伏的草原上溪涧北流，汇入大河。1444年，说加勒比语的村民在溪畔种植木薯，捕鱼打猎，乘独木舟与奥里诺科河和海岸通商。那时还没有传教士或军人从西班牙属圭亚那进入这片土地。

1724年，加泰罗尼亚嘉布遣会修士从卡罗尼河向上游推进，把加勒比人编入传教村镇。瓜西帕蒂建于1757年9月27日，是「卡罗尼与黄金国传教区」的第十一座村镇，所谓黄金国，就是西班牙征服者当年在这一带河流寻找的富庶国度。这里土壤瘠薄，肉食和木薯要靠别的传教村接济，但周围连成一串的村镇却是圭亚那省的粮仓和牧场：到1817年共有十九座村镇、约7000名印第安人，耕种全省最肥的土地。嘉布遣会从1810年起反对革命，向保王军供应马匹和粮食。1817年1月，曼努埃尔·皮亚尔在安戈斯图拉被击退；2月他渡过卡罗尼河，6日拿下乌帕塔，17日击溃保王派省督洛伦索·菲茨杰拉德的部队。数百名传教镇印第安人带着弓箭和长矛随他出征，4月11日在奇里卡台地的圣费利克斯助他打垮米格尔·德·拉·托雷的军队。此战为共和国打开奥里诺科河，也终结了嘉布遣会的基业：传教区仓里的皮革、烟草、棉花和可可供养了安戈斯图拉的新政府，千余名传教镇印第安人被招入爱国军，修士们则被押往卡鲁阿奇看管，其中十八人后来在那里被处死。

en:
The bluffs where the Orinoco begins to open into its delta were the site of Uyapari, later Barrancas del Orinoco. The ground above seasonal floods holds Barrancoid and Saladoid artifacts from about 1000 BCE, and the village had been occupied without a break since at least the eleventh century. In 1444 its bohíos stood on one of the great canoe routes between the llanos waterways, the delta channels and the Atlantic.

Diego de Ordaz entered through the Caño Manamo in August 1531 while searching for El Dorado. The size of Uyapari impressed him: he reported more than 400 bohíos and went ashore to meet Naricagua, the cacique whose lordship was associated with the place name. Juan de Castellanos later described a powerful town crowded along the ravines. Aragonese Capuchins reached the district late in the seventeenth century, and Fray Joaquín de Morata founded San Rafael Arcángel de Barrancas in 1790 with Warao help and built its church. Alexander von Humboldt visited in 1800. The friars withdrew during the independence wars, while the indigenous river settlement remained occupied.
zh:
奥里诺科河开始展宽进入三角洲的河岸高地上，坐落着乌亚帕里，后来的巴兰卡斯德尔奥里诺科。洪水线以上的土地出土了约公元前1000年的巴兰科伊德与萨拉多伊德文化器物，村落至少自11世纪起便持续有人居住。1444年，村中的茅屋位于亚诺斯水网、三角洲汊道与大西洋之间的重要独木舟航路上。

1531年8月，寻找黄金国的迭戈·德·奥达斯经马纳莫汊河进入此地。乌亚帕里的规模令他吃惊：他报告说有四百多座茅屋，并上岸会见首领纳里卡瓜，这位首领的领地与村名相连。胡安·德·卡斯特利亚诺斯后来也称这里是峡谷间人群密集的大镇。17世纪末，阿拉贡嘉布遣会士来到这一带；1790年，华金·德·莫拉塔修士在瓦劳人帮助下建立圣拉斐尔·阿尔坎赫尔·德·巴兰卡斯传教站，并修建教堂。亚历山大·冯·洪堡1800年到访。独立战争期间修士撤离，这座印第安河村仍有人居住。

en:
The Guajira Peninsula, Woumainpa'a in the Wayuu language, is the arid, wind-scoured northern tip of South America, running from the salt pans of Manaure to the Gulf of Venezuela. In 1444 it was Wayuu country. The Wayuu, Arawak-speakers organised in matrilineal clans across scattered villages, fished the reefs, gathered salt, kept goats and traded by canoe with the Antilles, and Cabo de la Vela, which they called Jepirra, was the sacred cape where the souls of the dead passed on. Kindred peoples such as the Añú fished the gulf, and no European had yet landed on the peninsula.

Pearls brought the Spaniards. Alonso de Ojeda sailed past in 1499 with Juan de la Cosa and Amerigo Vespucci and named the gulf Coquivacoa, and in 1535 Nikolaus Federmann, an agent of the Welser banking house which held the lease of Venezuela, founded the first Spanish settlement beside Cabo de la Vela. After a pirate raid it was moved in 1544-45 to the mouth of the Ranchería river as Riohacha. Divers from the ruined pearl island of Cubagua worked its oyster beds, and the pearl port drew English raiders in their turn: John Hawkins forced shiploads of African slaves on the townspeople in the 1560s, and Francis Drake sacked the town in 1596.

The Wayuu were never conquered. They adopted horses and bought English and Dutch muskets with pearls and cattle, and a long string of revolts culminated in 1769, when some 20,000 warriors burned the Spanish settlements and penned the survivors inside Riohacha; the Crown afterwards ruled the coast as a separate Province of Riohacha. Spanish rule on the peninsula effectively ended on 25 May 1820, when a patriot fleet under José Prudencio Padilla, a Riohacha-born admiral, won the battle of Laguna Salá. The Wayuu kept their arms and their autonomy.
zh:
瓜希拉半岛在瓦尤语中称沃温帕阿，是南美洲最北端一片干旱多风的土地，从马瑙雷盐沼延伸到委内瑞拉湾。1444年，这里是瓦尤人的家园。这支说阿拉瓦克语的民族按母系氏族散居各处，在礁湖中捕鱼、采盐、养羊，划独木舟与安的列斯群岛贸易；他们称贝拉角为杰皮拉，那是亡魂渡往彼岸的神圣海角。阿纽人等亲缘部落以湾边渔捞为生，此时还没有欧洲人登上半岛。

是珍珠把西班牙人引来的。1499年，阿隆索·德·奥赫达与胡安·德·拉·科萨、亚美利哥·韦斯普奇乘船经过这一带，把海湾命名为科基瓦科阿；1535年，持有委内瑞拉承租权的韦尔泽银行家族派代理人尼古劳斯·费德曼在贝拉角旁建起第一个西班牙人定居点。该地遭海盗洗劫后，于1544至1545年迁到兰切里亚河口，是为里奥阿查。从凋敝的采珠岛库巴瓜来的潜水夫在港外珠蚌床作业，这座珍珠港又引来英国袭掠者：1560年代，约翰·霍金斯把一船船非洲奴隶强卖给城中居民，1596年弗朗西斯·德雷克又将它洗劫一空。

瓦尤人始终未被征服。他们学会养马，用珍珠和牲畜向英、荷商人换购火枪，起义接连不断，以1769年为最：约两万名战士焚毁西班牙人的定居点，把幸存者困在里奥阿查城内，王室此后只得把这片海岸单列为里奥阿查省。1820年5月25日，出生于里奥阿查的舰队司令何塞·普鲁登西奥·帕迪利亚率爱国舰队赢得拉萨拉达湖海战，西班牙在半岛的统治实际终结。瓦尤人保住了武器，也保住了自治。

en:
The eastern shore of Lake Maracaibo runs low and hot behind a fringe of mangroves. In 1444 it belonged to the Caquetío, an Arawakan fishing people who built stilt villages over the shallows, moored their canoes under the houses and traded fish and salt toward the dry country around Coro; Lagunillas de Agua, Moporo and Tomoporo were the largest of these water-villages. No outside power yet touched the shore.

Charles V had leased the conquest of Venezuela to the Welser, the Augsburg banking house to whom he owed money, and their first governor, Ambrosius Ehinger, reached the lake in 1529. After beating down the resistance of the Coquivacoa he founded Neu-Nürnberg on the west shore at the lake narrows on 8 September. Local tradition, upheld by the Zulia Academy of History, places the Welsers' first post on this eastern shore on the same day, the beginning of Altagracia. Ehinger was killed by a poisoned arrow on an inland expedition four years later, and the east-shore post stayed a poor fishing anchorage until 1600, when it was raised to a villa and gained streets, a church and warehouses. Santa Rita and Cabimas took shape along the same coast in the colonial years.

The Maracaibo province stayed royalist after 1810, while Los Puertos de Altagracia produced the best-known local figure on the patriot side: Ana María Campos, born there in 1796, organised resistance from the port. Seized by royalist troops, she was lashed through the streets in public and refused to recant.
zh:
马拉开波湖东岸地势低平、气候湿热，沿岸是一道红树林。1444年，湖岸属于卡克蒂奥人：他们属阿拉瓦克语族，以渔为业，在浅水中架起桩屋，屋下系着独木舟，拿鱼和盐与科罗方向的干旱地带通商；拉古尼利亚斯德阿瓜、莫波罗、托莫波罗是其中最大的几座水村。此时没有任何外来政权触及这片湖岸。

查理五世因欠债，把委内瑞拉的征服特许权租给了奥格斯堡的银行家韦尔泽家族。家族任命的首任总督埃因格1529年进入湖区，在压服科基瓦科阿人的抵抗后，于9月8日在湖口西岸建起新纽伦堡。按苏利亚州历史学院采用的当地说法，韦尔泽人在湖口此岸设立的第一个据点也在同一天，即阿尔塔格拉西亚的开端。四年后，埃因格在一次深入内陆的远征中被毒箭射死，而东岸的据点长期只是个荒凉的渔船锚地，直到1600年才正式设镇，修起街道、教堂和仓库；殖民时期，圣丽塔和卡维马斯也在同一道湖岸上成形。

1810年后马拉开波省仍效忠西班牙王室，而洛斯普埃尔托斯·德·阿尔塔格拉西亚出了爱国阵营最有名的本地人：1796年生于此处的安娜·玛丽亚·坎波斯在港中组织抵抗。她被保王军逮捕，当众受鞭刑，仍不肯屈服。

en:
Coro (Santa Ana de Coro) lies on a flat, windy coastal plain south of the Paraguaná Peninsula, with its port of La Vela a few kilometres away on the Caribbean; local tradition derives its name from the Caquetio word curiana, 'place of winds'. In 1444 the country, called Curiana, belonged to the Caquetio, an Arawak people ruled by the cacique Manaure. Spaniards first sailed this coast in 1499 with Alonso de Ojeda, whose men saw villages raised on stilts above the water and, thinking of Venice, named the land Venezuela. Juan de Ampíes founded Santa Ana de Coro on 26 July 1527, promising to leave Manaure his authority.

Two years later Charles V granted the province to the Welser banking house of Augsburg. The family renamed the town Neu-Augsburg and ran the territory as Klein-Venedig, 'Little Venice', making Coro the first German colony in the Americas. Ambrosius Ehinger, its first governor, founded Maracaibo in 1529 and died on an inland gold search in 1533, and column after column left Coro for the Llanos, the Andes and the Orinoco after El Dorado. When the last Welser captain, Philipp von Hutten, returned in 1546, the Spanish governor Juan de Carvajal had him and young Bartholomeus Welser executed and the emperor revoked the charter. Coro nevertheless became the first capital of Venezuela Province and, from 1531, the seat of South America's first bishopric. Corsair raids, an English one under Preston and Somers in 1595 among them, and its harsh climate cost it the capital to Caracas in 1578 and the diocese in 1636; after hurricanes and sacks European charts marked the town 'destroyed', and the trade of its hinterland brought it slowly back.

Independence began early in the Sierra de Coro. On 10 May 1795 the free zambo José Leonardo Chirino raised the slaves there against the planters, demanding abolition under the rebels' 'French law'; he was hanged the next year. In August 1806 Francisco de Miranda landed at La Vela and raised his yellow, blue and red flag for the first time on Venezuelan soil, the colours later carried by Gran Colombia. The townspeople gave him no support, and after 1810 Coro was a royalist stronghold against the First Republic. The province changed sides only in 1821, when Josefa Camejo, born on the Paraguaná Peninsula in 1791, led the patriots who seized the town just before Rafael Urdaneta's army arrived.
zh:
科罗（圣安娜德科罗）位于帕拉瓜纳半岛以南平坦多风的沿海平原，几公里外的加勒比海岸是它的外港拉维拉；按当地传统，「科罗」来自卡克蒂奥语curiana，意为「多风之地」。1444年，这片被称为库里亚纳的土地属于卡克蒂奥人，即受酋长马瑙雷统辖的一支阿拉瓦克人。1499年，西班牙人随阿隆索·德·奥赫达首次航行这段海岸，水手看见木桩撑出水面的村落，想起威尼斯，便把这片土地命名为委内瑞拉。1527年7月26日，胡安·德·安普埃斯建立圣安娜德科罗，许诺保留马瑙雷的权位。

两年后，查理五世把委内瑞拉省特许给奥格斯堡的韦尔瑟银行家族。他们把城市改名新奥格斯堡，以「小威尼斯」之名统治全省，科罗成了美洲第一个德意志殖民地。首任总督安布罗修斯·埃因格1529年建立马拉开波，1533年死于深入内陆的寻金之旅；此后一支接一支队伍从科罗出发，进入亚诺斯草原、安第斯山区和奥里诺科河流域寻找黄金国。末任韦尔瑟队长菲利普·冯·胡滕1546年返回时，西班牙人胡安·德·卡瓦哈尔已就总督之位；卡瓦哈尔处死了他和年轻的巴托洛梅乌斯·韦尔瑟，皇帝随即收回特许。科罗仍是委内瑞拉省的第一个首府，1531年起又驻有南美洲的第一个主教区。海盗接连来袭，1595年英国人普雷斯顿和萨默斯的船队就是其中一路，加上气候恶劣，它在1578年把首府让给加拉加斯，1636年又失去主教区；飓风和几度洗劫之后，欧洲海图把这座城标作「已毁」，全靠腹地贸易才慢慢恢复。

独立运动在科罗山区开始得很早。1795年5月10日，自由的桑博人何塞·莱昂纳多·奇里诺带领山区奴隶起事，要求按起义者所称的「法国法」废除奴隶制，次年被绞死。1806年8月，弗朗西斯科·德·米兰达在拉维拉登陆，黄蓝红三色旗第一次在委内瑞拉土地上升起，后来成为大哥伦比亚的旗帜。市民没有响应他；1810年以后，科罗变成保王派堡垒，西班牙军队正是从这里出发扼杀了第一共和国。全省直到1821年才倒向共和：1791年生于帕拉瓜纳半岛的何塞法·卡梅霍率领爱国者拿下科罗，比拉斐尔·乌达内塔的大军早到几天。

en:
The Eastern Llanos around the Guárico are a wide tropical grassland east of the Andes, cut by gallery forests, seasonal streams and rivers that spill over their banks in the rains. In 1444 the peoples later recorded on these plains hunted, fished, gathered and planted small alluvial plots, moving camps as water and game moved. The Guárico's banks offered fish, game and dry ground, but the country later centred on Calabozo had no Spanish town, mission or cattle herd. Plains tracks linked camps and river crossings; roads to the coastal markets did not yet exist.

Andalusian Capuchins began missions near the Guárico in 1723, bringing people from several Orinoco and plains peoples into reductions, and Villa de Todos los Santos de Calabozo was formally founded on 1 February 1724. Cattle, horses and mules then became the basis of its wealth: ranchers occupied the savanna, and herds were driven along plains routes toward Caracas. By the later eighteenth century Calabozo had its own council, and Bishop Mariano Martí counted 428 houses and 3,448 people in 1780. In 1800 Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland stopped there to examine electrical instruments built by Carlos del Pozo y Sucre, a self-educated local experimenter. Calabozo joined the independence movement on 31 July 1811. José Tomás Boves, confined there before the war, later made it one of his operating bases. On 12 February 1818 Simón Bolívar and José Antonio Páez led about 3,500 patriots against Pablo Morillo; Páez's cavalry broke the royalist position, and Morillo evacuated the town two days later.
zh:
瓜里科河一带的东亚诺斯是安第斯山脉以东广阔的热带草原，林带沿水道伸展，雨季河水漫出河岸。1444年，后来见于记载的草原居民狩猎、捕鱼、采集，并在小片冲积地上耕作，随水源和猎场变化转移营地。瓜里科河畔有鱼、猎物和干地，但后来以卡拉沃索为中心的这片土地上，还没有西班牙城镇、传教区或牛群。草原小路连接营地和渡口，通往沿海市场的道路尚未出现。

1723年，安达卢西亚嘉布遣会修士开始在瓜里科河附近设立传教区，把若干奥里诺科与草原族群编入归化村；1724年2月1日，诸圣卡拉沃索镇正式建立。牛、马和骡随后成为当地财富的基础：牧场主占据稀树草原，牲畜沿草原道路被赶往加拉加斯。到18世纪后期，卡拉沃索已有自己的市政会，马里亚诺·马蒂主教1780年统计到428栋房屋、3448人。1800年，亚历山大·冯·洪堡和艾梅·邦普朗在此停留，查看自学成才的本地实验者卡洛斯·德尔·波索·伊·苏克雷制造的电学仪器。卡拉沃索于1811年7月31日加入独立运动。战前曾被拘禁在此的何塞·托马斯·博韦斯，后来把这里当作作战基地之一。1818年2月12日，西蒙·玻利瓦尔和何塞·安东尼奥·派斯率约3500名爱国者进攻巴勃罗·莫里略；派斯的骑兵击破保王军阵地，莫里略两天后撤出卡拉沃索。

en:
Apure is the flood-country of the western Venezuelan Llanos, where the Apure, Arauca and Capanaparo gather the Andes' drainage and carry it to the Orinoco. Each wet season the rivers spread over grasslands that run for weeks of travel, leaving only banks and low mounds above water. In 1444 no Spanish frontier reached the plains; Arawak and Carib groups lived along the banks and the higher ground and used the rivers as roads by canoe. The name Apure belonged first to the river, later explained either from a riverside shrub or from a chief called Apur.

Spanish expeditions probed the region from the mid-1600s, and Friar Jacinto de Carvajal used the name Apure in 1648, but occupation came a century later, when ranchers out of San Carlos de Austria and Andalusian Franciscans moved in with cattle herds and missions; most of the towns, Guasdualito and Achaguas among them, date from after 1760. The river port of San Fernando del Paso Real de Apure was founded on 28 February 1788 by order of Governor Fernando Miyares for the new Province of Barinas, and hides and heron feathers for quill pens went out down the river to the Orinoco. Alexander von Humboldt passed through in March 1800 on his way up the Apure by canoe. The plains became cavalry country in the independence wars under the llanero commander José Antonio Páez. At Las Queseras del Medio on 2 April 1819, his 153 mounted lancers feigned flight, turned at his shout of '¡Vuelvan caras!' ('about face'), and routed more than a thousand royalist cavalry. By 1821 the Apure plains lay within Gran Colombia.
zh:
阿普雷是委内瑞拉西部草原的洪水之乡，阿普雷河、阿劳卡河和卡帕纳帕罗河汇集安第斯山来水，注入奥里诺科河。雨季河水漫上绵延数周路程的草原，只有河岸和低矮土墩露出水面。1444年，西班牙人的势力还没到这里；阿拉瓦克人和加勒比人住在河岸和高地上，划独木舟以河道为路。阿普雷这个名字最初属于河流，后来有人说来自河畔的一种灌木，也有人说来自名叫阿普尔的酋长。

西班牙远征从17世纪中叶起试探此地，修士哈辛托·德·卡瓦哈尔1648年已使用阿普雷一名，但真正的占领晚了一个世纪：来自圣卡洛斯·德·奥地利的牧场主和安达卢西亚方济各会士带着牛群和传教站进入，瓜斯杜阿利托、阿查瓜斯等城镇大多在1760年以后形成。1788年2月28日，省长费尔南多·米亚雷斯为新设的巴里纳斯省下令建立河港圣费尔南多·德尔帕索雷亚尔·德·阿普雷，皮革和制笔用的鹭羽顺河运往奥里诺科河外销。1800年3月，亚历山大·冯·洪堡划独木舟溯阿普雷河考察，途中经过此港。独立战争中，草原骑手出身的将领何塞·安东尼奥·派斯把平原变成骑兵战场。1819年4月2日的拉斯克塞拉斯德尔梅迪奥一役，他的153名骑马枪骑兵先佯退，听到「转身！」的命令一齐回马，冲垮一千余名保王骑兵。到1821年，阿普雷草原已纳入大哥伦比亚。

en:
The Atabapo is a blackwater river that runs some 130 kilometres through rainforest, forming much of the border between Venezuela and Colombia. At San Fernando it meets the Guainía and the Guaviare, and from the confluence the river is called the Orinoco. In 1444 its dark, fish-rich banks belonged to Arawak speakers, the Baniva among them, who planted bitter cassava and paddled dugouts between the Orinoco below and the Guainía, which carries traffic towards the Amazon. Puinave villagers lived at the meeting of the waters, and their hamlet of Casuru stood on the ground the Spanish town later occupied.

Spain came to mark a frontier rather than plant a colony. Its Orinoco Boundary Expedition of 1754–1761 was fixing the line with Portuguese Brazil under the Treaty of Madrid when José Solano raised a fort beside Casuru on 31 July 1758 and, with the local chief Crucero named lieutenant and governor, founded San Fernando de Atabapo, the first Spanish settlement in what is now the state of Amazonas. The town was destroyed two years later, and a rebuilding attempt in 1765 left little behind it but a thin chain of mission stations along the blackwater creeks. Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland passed through in 1800 on their way from the Orinoco to the Casiquiare channel and the Río Negro. In 1817 the patriot officer Hipólito Cuebas took San Fernando with eighty men.
zh:
阿塔巴波（阿塔瓦波）是一条在热带雨林中穿行约130公里的黑河，大部分河道构成委内瑞拉与哥伦比亚的国界。它在圣费尔南多与瓜伊尼亚河、瓜维亚雷河相会，三河交汇之后河道始称奥里诺科河。1444年，黝黑多鱼的河岸属于说阿拉瓦克语的诸族，巴尼瓦人是其中一支：他们种植苦木薯，划独木舟往来于下游的奥里诺科河与通向亚马孙河的瓜伊尼亚河。普伊纳维人住在三河汇流处，他们的卡苏鲁村就坐落在后来西班牙城镇所在的地方。

西班牙人到这里是为了划界，而不是拓殖。按1750年《马德里条约》，1754至1761年的奥里诺科勘界远征队负责划定与葡属巴西的边界；1758年7月31日，何塞·索拉诺在卡苏鲁村旁筑起要塞，任命当地酋长克鲁塞罗为副长官兼地方首领，建立圣费尔南多·德·阿塔巴波——今委内瑞拉亚马孙州境内的第一座西班牙人城镇。两年后城镇被毁，1765年的一次重建尝试只在黑水溪涧间留下一串稀疏的传教站。1800年，洪堡与邦普朗途经此地，由奥里诺科河前往卡西基亚雷水道和内格罗河。1817年，爱国军军官伊波利托·奎瓦斯率八十人拿下圣费尔南多。

en:
The grasslands around Pore lie where the eastern Llanos climb into the Eastern Cordillera of the Andes. The wider region takes its name, Casanare, from the Sáliva word casanari, 'black-water river'. In 1444 Sáliva, Guahibo, Tunebo and Piapoco bands moved between seasonally flooded savanna, gallery forest and rivers, farming small clearings, fishing and hunting. Expeditions out of the Andes reached the plains early in the sixteenth century, and encomiendas soon put many of the people to forced labour, but no Spanish town stood here until 5 November 1644, when Adriano Vargas and Francisco Enciso founded Pore.

Jesuit haciendas turned the surrounding plains into cattle country whose herds and hides traded as far as Tunja and Venezuela; the walled prison the crown built at Pore was one of the few stone buildings the llanos ever saw. The expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 broke the ranch economy, and the plains gave the government trouble soon afterwards. In the Comunero rising of 1781 Javier de Mendoza raised Casanare against Spanish rule, claiming authority from Túpac Amaru and gathering more than five thousand indigenous followers. On 17 February 1810 three eighteen-year-olds, Carlos Salgar, José María Rosillo and Vicente Cadena, seized Pore and declared it free of Spanish rule, months before Bogotá. The town's officials laid a trap: Salgar and Cadena were executed on 30 April and their heads sent to Bogotá for display, until public anger stopped it.

In 1818 Pore became a provincial capital of the independence government. The next year Bolívar's troops joined Santander's llanero cavalry on these grasslands, and the combined army marched from Casanare over the cold heights of the Páramo de Pisba on its way to victory at Vargas Swamp and Boyacá.
zh:
颇雷周围的稀树草原，位于东部亚诺斯平原向安第斯山东科迪勒拉山脉爬升的地带；大区名「卡萨纳雷」来自萨利瓦语casanari，意为「黑河」。1444年，萨利瓦人、瓜希沃人、图内博人和皮亚波科人在季节性泛滥的草原、走廊林和河流之间迁徙，耕作小块空地，捕鱼狩猎。16世纪初，来自安第斯山区的远征队进入平原，监护征赋制很快把许多原住民逼去服劳役，但直到1644年11月5日，阿德里亚诺·巴尔加斯和弗朗西斯科·恩西索才建立颇雷，这是当地第一座西班牙城镇。

耶稣会的庄园把周围平原经营成牧牛地，牛群和皮革远联通哈与委内瑞拉；西班牙王室在颇雷修建的围墙监狱，是亚诺斯草原上少见的石造建筑。1767年耶稣会被驱逐，牧场经济随之衰败，这片草原不久就开始给当局制造麻烦。1781年市民起义期间，哈维尔·德·门多萨在卡萨纳雷举事，自称受图帕克·阿马鲁委派，聚拢了五千多名印第安人。1810年2月17日，三个十八岁的青年卡洛斯·萨尔加、何塞·玛丽亚·罗西略和维森特·卡德纳攻占颇雷，宣布脱离西班牙统治，比波哥大还早几个月。市政官员设下圈套：萨尔加和卡德纳于4月30日被处死，人头送往波哥大示众，终因民愤太大而作罢。

1818年，颇雷成为独立运动的省府。次年，玻利瓦尔的部队在这片草原上与桑坦德的亚诺斯骑兵会合，大军从卡萨纳雷出发，翻越高寒的皮斯巴荒原，随后赢得巴尔加斯沼泽之战和博亚卡之战。

en:
The Mérida country occupies the high valleys and shelves of the Venezuelan Andes, along the Chama river between the Sierra de la Culata and the snow peaks of the Sierra Nevada; the plateau where the city stands lies about 1,600 metres up. In 1444 the valleys belonged to the Timote and Cuica and their kinsmen the Mucuchíes and Tatey, held to be the most advanced farming peoples of Venezuela and related to the Chibcha of New Granada. They grew maize and roots on irrigated terraces, lived in round thatched houses, traded along mountain tracks, and honoured the sun, the lakes and the high peaks. No Spaniard had yet entered the sierra.

Captain Juan Rodríguez Suárez founded Mérida on 9 October 1558, naming it for his native Mérida in Extremadura. After fighting with neighbouring peoples, Juan de Maldonado moved the town to its present plateau a year later under the name Santiago de los Caballeros. The town answered to Tunja at first and was later attached to the Captaincy General of Venezuela. Tobacco taxes and Bourbon monopolies drew it into the comunero rising of 1781; four years later the new bishopric brought Bishop Juan Ramos de Lora, who founded the San Buenaventura seminary that became the University of the Andes in 1811. On 26 March 1812 an earthquake killed more than 800 people in the city. Bolívar entered in May 1813 on his Admirable Campaign, royalists retook it the next year and crushed a local rising called La Patriecita, and Bolívar freed Mérida again before it entered Gran Colombia in 1821.
zh:
梅里达地处委内瑞拉安第斯山的高谷与台地，位于查马河畔，夹在库拉塔山脉与积雪的内华达山脉之间；后来建城的高台海拔约1600米。1444年，谷地属于蒂莫特人和奎卡人，以及他们的亲族穆库奇人、塔泰人；他们被视为委内瑞拉境内最先进的农耕部族，与新格拉纳达的奇布查人同源。他们在灌溉梯田上种植玉米和块根作物，住圆形茅草屋，沿山路交换物产，敬拜太阳、湖泊和高峰。此时还没有西班牙人进入这片山地。

1558年10月9日，胡安·罗德里格斯·苏亚雷斯上尉建立梅里达，以故乡埃斯特雷马杜拉的梅里达命名；因与邻近部族交战，胡安·德·马尔多纳多一年后把城迁到现址所在的高台，改名圣地亚哥·德·洛斯·卡瓦列罗斯。此城最初受通哈管辖，后来划归委内瑞拉都督辖区。烟草税和波旁专卖把它卷入1781年的公社者起事；四年后主教区设立，首任主教胡安·拉莫斯·德·洛拉办起圣布埃纳文图拉神学院，神学院于1811年改为安第斯大学。1812年3月26日的地震使城中八百余人丧生。1813年5月，玻利瓦尔在可敬战役中进入梅里达；保王派次年夺回此城，还镇压了名为「小祖国」的本地起事。玻利瓦尔再次解放梅里达后，它于1821年并入大哥伦比亚。

en:
The lands named after the Meta, the great Orinoco tributary that carries the water of the Eastern Cordillera, run from wet Andean foothills out into the open eastern Llanos. In 1444 Guayupe, Guahibo, Huitoto and Piapoco communities were scattered across this country of seasonally flooded savanna, gallery forest and rivers, moving with the waters, hunting and fishing and planting small clearings. No Spanish town commanded the plains, and the outside world first heard of the Meta through men chasing rumours of gold.

Diego de Ordaz, sailing up the Orinoco, learned of the river around 1531; Alonso de Herrera followed him, and late in 1539 Alfonso de Heredia crossed the Llanos to the Meta's mouth. The same hunt carried the Welsers' German captains from Coro across these plains, Georg von Speyer and Nikolaus Federmann among them, before Federmann reached the new Spanish settlement at Bogotá in the Andes. By 1544 encomiendas were in place, the first held by Pedro Rodríguez de Salamanca. Jesuit and Augustinian missionaries later gathered the people into reductions, learned their languages and taught loom weaving, wood carving and European instruments; the mission harp became one of the instruments behind the llaneros' music. The plains long remained a mission frontier attached in part to the province of Bogotá.

In 1819 Francisco de Paula Santander raised and drilled the patriot army on the Casanare and Meta grasslands, the force with which Bolívar opened the New Granada campaign.
zh:
以梅塔河得名的这片土地，从湿润的安第斯山麓铺展到开阔的东部亚诺斯平原；梅塔河是奥里诺科河的大支流，承接着东科迪勒拉山脉的来水。1444年，瓜尤佩人、瓜希沃人、维托托人和皮亚波科人散居在季节性泛滥的草原、走廊林与河网之间，随水季迁徙，捕鱼狩猎，耕作小块空地。当时没有西班牙城镇控制平原，外界最初听说梅塔，全靠追逐黄金传闻的人。

迭戈·德·奥尔达斯溯奥里诺科河而上，约在1531年听说了这条河；阿隆索·德·埃雷拉继之而来，1539年末，阿方索·德·埃雷迪亚穿过亚诺斯，抵达梅塔河口。同一场寻金热也把韦尔瑟家族的德意志队长们从科罗带到这片草原，其中就有格奥尔格·冯·施派尔和尼古劳斯·费德曼；费德曼最后走到了安第斯山区新建的波哥大。到1544年，监护征赋制已经确立，第一块监护地属于佩德罗·罗德里格斯·德·萨拉曼卡。后来，耶稣会和奥古斯丁会的传教士把原住民聚入归化村，学习他们的语言，教他们织机织布、木雕和欧洲乐器；传教士带来的竖琴，后来成了亚诺斯牧人音乐里的乐器之一。这片草原长期是传教前沿，一部分隶属波哥大省。

1819年，弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·桑坦德在卡萨纳雷和梅塔的草原上招募、训练爱国军，玻利瓦尔正是率领这支军队打响了新格拉纳达战役。

en:
Puerto Carreño covers the wet savanna and gallery woods where the Meta River joins the Orinoco. In 1444 this was Achagua country. Their villages and fields stretched across the Casanare, Meta and Apure basins, and canoes linked family groups through a trade network in which strings of quiripa shells passed as money. Farm produce also changed hands with Carib groups for weapons. Seasonal floods set the limits on fishing, farming and travel; at the Meta's mouth there was neither mission nor fort.

Spanish entry came by river. In 1666 the Jesuit Alonso de Neira founded San Joaquín de Atanari for Achagua people on the south bank of the Meta, close to the Orinoco, but the mission was abandoned in 1669 after supplies failed and Carib raids continued. Missionaries later set up Santa Teresa de Jesús and the mission and stronghold of Carichana, which supported itself with crops and cattle. During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, smugglers also used the Meta and Orinoco to bring in goods more cheaply than the licensed markets at Santafé and Caracas. The missions and cattle holdings weakened during the independence wars.
zh:
卡雷尼奥港覆盖梅塔河汇入奥里诺科河一带的湿草原和走廊林。1444年，这里是阿查瓜人的土地。他们的村落和田地分布在卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河流域，独木舟把各家族群连进贸易网，成串的基里帕贝壳可作货币，农产品也用来同加勒比人群交换武器。季节性洪水限定了捕鱼、农耕和出行的范围；梅塔河口当时还没有传教站或堡垒。

西班牙人也是从河道进入这里。1666年，耶稣会士阿隆索·德·内拉在梅塔河南岸、靠近奥里诺科河处为阿查瓜人建立圣华金·德·阿塔纳里传教站；1669年，因补给断绝、加勒比人的袭扰持续，传教站废弃。传教士后来又设圣特雷莎·德·赫苏斯以及卡里查纳传教站和堡垒，后者靠作物和牧牛维持。17至18世纪，走私者也利用梅塔河与奥里诺科河运入货物，价格比圣菲和加拉加斯的特许市场更低。独立战争期间，传教站和牧牛产业走向衰落。

en: The Guaviare forms where the Guayabero and Ariari meet below the eastern Andes and runs east between gallery forest and open savanna to the Orinoco. For much of its course it divides the grassy Llanos from the Amazon rainforest, and shallow-draft boats can travel more than 600 kilometres of its lower channel; its coffee-coloured waters are rich in fish. In 1444 Guayabero, Tinigua, Sikuani, Nukak, Piapoco and Puinave communities fished the river and moved between its banks in canoes, with no Spanish road or post among them. Spain later drew the basin into the province of Popayán on paper, and in 1821 Gran Colombia assigned it to the department of Boyacá, but neither claim brought a town upriver, and the riverside peoples kept their own councils.
zh: 瓜维亚雷河在东安第斯山麓由瓜亚韦罗河与阿里亚里河汇合而成，东流经林带与开阔草原注入奥里诺科河。其河道大半是草原大平原与亚马逊雨林的分界，下游600多公里可通行吃水浅的船只；河水呈咖啡色，盛产鱼类。1444年，瓜亚韦罗、蒂尼瓜、西库阿尼、努卡克、皮亚波科和普伊纳韦诸族在河中捕鱼，乘独木舟往来两岸，其间没有一条西班牙道路或一个据点。西班牙后来在纸面上把流域划入波帕扬省，1821年大哥伦比亚又将它划归博亚卡省，但两次归属都没有在上游建起城镇，河畔诸族仍由各自的议事会管理。

en:
The upper Magdalena crosses a hot, fertile plain between the Cordillera Central and the Cordillera Oriental, the country later administered from Neiva. The Las Ceibas and del Oro rivers drain the eastern side of the basin, while the Saldaña brings gold-bearing gravels down from the mountains. In 1444 the peoples of the valley lived entirely outside Spanish rule. The northern plain was Pijao country, where the Coyaima and Natagaima were leading communities in loose war and trade federations; Tama peoples held the ground near the later town, and Páez, Andaquí and Yalcón communities lived around the neighbouring hills and southern plain. Villages traded tobacco and goldwork along the Magdalena and could send raiding parties against intruders. No European settlement yet stood on the riverbank where Neiva would be built.

The first Spanish towns did not hold. Juan de Cabrera founded Neiva in 1539 on the Río Neiva in Tama country, and Juan de Alonso y Arias moved the settlement about 1550 to the ground later called Villavieja. Pijao warriors destroyed it in 1560. Diego de Ospina y Medinilla founded the third Neiva on the present riverbank site on 24 May 1612, and it became capital of the Province of Páez, soon renamed Neiva, taking precedence over La Plata, Timaná and Purificación. Cattle haciendas then occupied the warm plain, miners washed gold in the Saldaña, and mule trains used the town on the route between Peru, Santafé and the Caribbean. Neiva later formed part of the Viceroyalty of New Granada. During the wars of independence it declared a free state on 8 February 1814, and Pablo Morillo's royalists retook it on 17 May 1816. Patriot forces recovered the upper Magdalena in 1819.
zh:
马格达莱纳河上游流经中部山脉与东部山脉之间一片炎热肥沃的平原，后来的内瓦就建在河畔。塞瓦斯河和奥罗河汇集盆地东侧的水流，萨尔达尼亚河则从山中带出含金砾石。1444年，河谷各族仍完全不受西班牙统治。北部平原是皮哈奥人的地盘，科亚伊马和纳塔盖马是松散作战与贸易联盟中的重要群落；塔马人占据后来城镇附近的土地，帕埃斯人、安达基人和亚尔孔人住在周围山地与南部平原。村落沿马格达莱纳河交易烟草和金器，也能派出队伍袭击入侵者。未来的内瓦河畔这时还没有欧洲人城镇。

西班牙人最初建立的城镇都没有守住。1539年，胡安·德·卡布雷拉在塔马人的内瓦河畔首建内瓦；约1550年，胡安·德·阿隆索·阿里亚斯把城镇迁到后来的比亚维哈，1560年又被皮哈奥战士摧毁。1612年5月24日，迭戈·德·奥斯皮纳·梅迪尼利亚在今日河畔第三次建城，内瓦随后成为帕埃斯省（不久改称内瓦省）省会，地位在拉普拉塔、蒂马纳和普里菲卡西翁之上。牧牛庄园占据温暖平原，淘金者在萨尔达尼亚河洗取沙金，骡队则把这里当作秘鲁、圣菲与加勒比海之间通道上的一站。内瓦后来划入新格拉纳达总督辖区。独立战争中，内瓦于1814年2月8日宣布成立自由邦，巴勃罗·莫里略的保王军在1816年5月17日夺回城市；1819年，爱国者收复上马格达莱纳。

en:
Popayán occupies the cool Pubenza Valley, 1,760 metres up between the Western and Central cordilleras. Before the Spanish conquest its village of Yauto was the seat of the Pubenza confederacy, which linked the Kokonuco, Guambía, Totoró, Timbío and other chiefdoms under rulers called yasgüenes. At El Morro del Tulcán they built an adobe pyramid between roughly 500 and 1600; sea shells and nonlocal stones in its graves show contacts with peoples far beyond the mountains. In 1444 the highland basins were farmed by these communities and their streams were panned for gold.

Juan de Ampudia seized the El Azafate ridge on Christmas Eve 1536, and Sebastián de Belalcázar proclaimed Asunción de Popayán on 13 January 1537, with the formal town charter on 15 August. In 1540 Belalcázar made it the seat of his governorship. The town stood on a route between Quito, Lima and Cartagena, and mine owners from the Chocó and Barbacoas kept houses there while their gold was shipped toward Spain. Cattle entered through Buenaventura after 1550, and enslaved Africans and Indian labour sustained the haciendas and mines. Wealthy families raised the baroque San Francisco and Santo Domingo churches and paid Payanesa goldsmiths. Their best-known work was the Crown of the Andes, made in stages for the cathedral's Virgin: its top cross and orb date to the sixteenth century, the diadem to about 1660 and the arches to about 1770, with 450 emeralds including the stone said to have come from Atahualpa. A royal mint opened in 1748, one of two in the Viceroyalty of New Granada, and struck gold escudos until 1820.

Independence fighting reached the town early. A junta met in 1810 and Popayán proclaimed independence in 1814; the country around it saw the battles of La Ladera, Calibío and La Cuchilla del Tambo. During Pablo Morillo's reconquest, two men from Popayán, the jurist Camilo Torres and the scientist Francisco José de Caldas, were executed in Santafé. Republican control followed Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819.
zh:
波帕扬坐落在西安第斯山与中科迪勒拉山之间、海拔1760米的普本萨河谷，气候凉爽。西班牙征服前，亚乌托村是普本萨联盟的中心，科科努科人、关比亚人、托托罗人、廷比奥人等酋邦在称亚斯古恩的首领下联合。图尔坎山岗上有一座约500年至1600年间修筑的土坯金字塔，墓中的海贝和外地石料说明他们与群山之外的人群有往来。1444年，这些族群耕作高原盆地，从溪涧里淘取砂金。

1536年圣诞夜，胡安·德·安普迪亚夺取埃尔阿萨特岭；1537年1月13日，塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔宣布建立亚松森·德·波帕扬，正式建城仪式在8月15日举行。1540年，贝拉尔卡萨尔把督军辖区治所设在这里。波帕扬位于基多、利马与卡塔赫纳之间的通道上，乔科和巴尔巴夸斯金矿的矿主在城中置宅，黄金再运往西班牙。1550年后，牛群经布埃纳文图拉输入，黑奴和印第安劳役支撑着种植园与矿区。富有的家族修建圣方济各、圣多明各等巴洛克教堂，也资助波帕扬金匠。他们最有名的作品是大教堂圣母像所用的「安第斯之冠」：顶部十字架与宝球为16世纪部件，冠圈约成于1660年，拱架约成于1770年，共嵌四百五十颗祖母绿，其中最大的宝石据说来自阿塔瓦尔帕。1748年王家铸币厂开设，是新格拉纳达总督区仅有的两家铸币厂之一，铸造金埃斯库多直到1820年。

独立战争很早波及这座城。1810年城中设立洪达，1814年波帕扬宣布独立；拉德拉、卡利维奥和坦博岭等战役在城周展开。巴勃罗·莫里略再征服期间，波帕扬出身的法学家卡米洛·托雷斯和科学家弗朗西斯科·何塞·德·卡尔达斯在圣菲被处死。1819年玻利瓦尔赢得博亚卡战役后，共和国接管了这里。

en:
Darién is the wet, forested neck at the east end of the Isthmus of Panama, between the Gulf of Urabá and the Bay of San Miguel. In 1444 its river villages belonged to the peoples the Spanish later called Cueva, who farmed forest clearings and hammered gold into ornaments; Guna communities lived along the Urabá shore. Swamp and rainforest put the lands beyond the canoe routes outside the reach of any outside empire.

Here Europeans made their first lasting footing on the American mainland. In September 1510 Martín Fernández de Enciso, on Balboa's advice, founded Santa María la Antigua del Darién after defeating the Cueva warriors of the chief Cémaco. From this town Vasco Núñez de Balboa marched out on 1 September 1513 with 190 Spaniards and about 1,000 indigenous auxiliaries, crossed the isthmus and on 25 September sighted the South Sea, claiming it for Castile four days later on the shore of the Bay of San Miguel. The discovery did not save him: soldiers under Francisco Pizarro arrested him on the orders of Governor Pedrarias Dávila, and he was tried and beheaded at Acla in January 1519, four friends dying with him. Pedrarias founded Panama City that August and moved the government of Castilla del Oro there; Santa María was abandoned and burned. Within those same years the Cueva themselves disappeared, dead in wars and epidemics or enslaved, the survivors fleeing or joining the Guna, who later spread into Darién.

The isthmus still drew men who wanted a road between the two seas. In 1698 William Paterson's Company of Scotland, which had raised roughly a fifth of all the money circulating in Scotland, landed colonists near Golden Island, made an alliance with a local Guna leader and built Fort St Andrew and the town of New Edinburgh, calling the colony New Caledonia. Fever and hunger emptied it and the survivors sailed away in June 1699; a second expedition of about 1,300 men returned that November to find a Spanish blockade and siege waiting, and surrendered on 28 March 1700. The ruin helped drive Scotland into the union with England in 1707. Darién itself stayed a frontier the Spanish never fully controlled.
zh:
达连是巴拿马地峡东端潮湿多雨的林颈，夹在乌拉瓦湾与圣米格尔湾之间。1444年，这里的河滨村落属于后来被西班牙人统称为库埃瓦人的诸族群；他们在林间空地耕作，把黄金锤成饰物，乌拉瓦湾沿岸则住着库纳人。沼泽和雨林使独木舟水路之外的土地不受任何外来帝国管辖。

欧洲人在美洲大陆的第一个长期立足点就在这里。1510年9月，马丁·费尔南德斯·德·恩西索采纳巴尔沃亚的建议，击败酋长塞马科的库埃瓦战士后，建立圣玛丽亚·拉·安提瓜·德尔·达连。1513年9月1日，瓦斯科·努涅斯·德·巴尔沃亚率190名西班牙人和约1000名原住民助战者从这座城镇出发，穿过地峡，于9月25日望见南海，四天后在圣米格尔湾岸边替卡斯蒂利亚宣布占有这片海洋。这一发现没能救他的命：弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗手下的士兵奉总督佩德拉里亚斯·达维瓦之命将他逮捕，1519年1月他在阿克拉受审后被斩首，四名友人同死。佩德拉里亚斯同年8月建立巴拿马城，把黄金卡斯蒂利亚的治所迁去，圣玛丽亚被废弃焚毁。也就在这些年里，库埃瓦人本身消亡了：或死于战争和瘟疫，或被奴役，幸存者逃散或并入库纳人，库纳人后来扩散到达连一带。

这条地峡仍吸引着想在两大洋之间开路的人。1698年，威廉·佩特森的苏格兰公司把移民送到金岛附近登陆，这家公司筹得的资金约占苏格兰流通货币的五分之一；移民与一位当地库纳首领结盟，筑起圣安德鲁堡和新爱丁堡镇，把殖民地命名为新喀里多尼亚。热病和饥饿使殖民地为之一空，幸存者1699年6月乘船撤离；约1300人的第二支远征队同年11月返回，等待他们的是西班牙人的封锁和围攻，1700年3月28日只得投降。这场破产推动苏格兰在1707年与英格兰合并。达连本身则始终是西班牙人未能完全控制的边疆。

en:
North of the Guayas the coast turns hot and rain-drenched, a line of mangrove channels and forested capes watered by the Santiago, Cayapas and Esmeraldas rivers. It had once been the country of the La Tolita goldworkers, whose gold travelled the Pacific shore, but by the fifteenth century it belonged to small peoples who answered to no outsider, the Cayapas, Campaces, Malabas and Niguas, lumped together by highlanders as Yumbos; no Inca road crossed their forests. In 1444 they lived by fishing, river trade and gold washing.

Pizarro's pilot Bartolomé Ruiz de Estrada was the first European on the coast: on 21 September 1526 he anchored in the bay he named San Mateo and found three towns dressed in gold. The Africans came next. In October 1553 a cargo of slaves bound from Panama to Lima seized their ship and beached it at Atacames. Their leader was Alonso de Illescas, a Cape Verdean who had lived in Seville and spoke Castilian; with firearms taken from the ship they married and allied with the Niguas and Cayapas, who called them juyungos, devils, and fought a rival band led by Juan Mangache and his son Francisco de Arobe. The two houses divided the shore, Arobe at San Mateo in the north and Illescas at Cabo Pasado in the south. Quito, which wanted an outlet to the Pacific, sent over thirty expeditions against them before 1583, all failures. Off Atacames in July 1594 Beltrán de Castro's galleons captured the English corsair Richard Hawkins and his ship the Dainty.

In 1599 Arobe came to Quito with his sons Pedro and Domingo to swear vassalage; the oidor Juan del Barrio had the mestizo painter Andrés Sánchez Gallque paint the three of them in oil, and the portrait was sent to Philip III. In 1602 the crown recognised both black houses as governors of the coast. Runaway slaves from the Barbacoas mines, who had heard of the free polity, swelled the zambo towns after 1640. From 1738 Pedro Vicente Maldonado drove the first mule road over the Andes to the sea and founded La Tola, and the gold rushes on the Cayapas and Santiago after 1780 brought a last wave of African-born settlers.
zh:
埃斯梅拉达斯位于瓜亚斯以北，海岸湿热多雨：红树林水道纵横，森林覆盖的海岬伸入太平洋，圣地亚哥河、卡亚帕斯河与埃斯梅拉达斯河在此入海。这里曾是拉托利塔金匠的故土，金器沿太平洋海岸辗转贸易；到15世纪，据有此地的是卡亚帕人、坎帕塞人、马拉瓦人和尼瓜人等小而强悍的族群，高原人笼统称他们为永博人。印加的道路从未伸入这片雨林。1444年时，他们以捕鱼、河上贸易和淘金为生，不臣服于任何外人。

第一个看到这片海岸的欧洲人是皮萨罗的领航员巴托洛梅·鲁伊斯·德·埃斯特拉达。1526年9月21日，他在自己命名为圣马特奥的海湾抛锚，见到三个城镇的人满身金饰。接踵而至的是非洲人：1553年10月，一船从巴拿马运往利马的奴隶夺取船只，在阿塔卡梅斯登岸。他们的首领是阿隆索·德·伊列斯卡斯，一个在佛得角出生、在塞维利亚生活过、会说西班牙语的人；部众带着从船上夺来的火器，与尼瓜人、卡亚帕人联姻结盟，卡亚帕人把他们叫作「juyungo」，意思是魔鬼，又同胡安·曼加切及其子弗朗西斯科·德·阿罗韦率领的另一伙黑人长年争战。两大家族最终瓜分海岸，阿罗韦据北方的圣马特奥，伊列斯卡斯据南方的卡博帕萨多。基多一心想要一个太平洋出海口，1583年之前派出三十多支远征队，无一成功。1594年7月，贝尔特兰·德·卡斯特罗的战舰在阿塔卡梅斯近海俘获英国海盗理查德·霍金斯和他的座舰「丹蒂号」。

1599年，阿罗韦带着两个儿子佩德罗和多明戈到基多宣誓效忠；检审法院法官胡安·德尔·巴里奥命混血画家安德烈斯·桑切斯·加尔克把父子三人画成一幅油画，送往西班牙进献费利佩三世。1602年，王室正式承认两大家族为这片海岸的首领。1640年后，听说有这个自由政权，从巴尔瓦科阿斯矿场逃出的奴隶纷纷前来，壮大了这些桑博人的城镇。1738年起，佩德罗·比森特·马尔多纳多主持修通第一条翻越安第斯山通往海边的骡道，并建立拉托拉；1780年后卡亚帕斯河与圣地亚哥河的淘金热，又带来最后一批非洲出生的移民。

en:
The lower Piura and Chira valleys run between the Pacific and the Sechura Desert. Seasonal rivers water fields of maize, cotton and fruit, and the shore yields fish and salt. Their Tallan inhabitants lived in scattered parcialidades, farming, fishing and trading by barter with the next valleys, and archaeologists group their older traditions under the Vicús name. The native word Pirhua, later Piura, is said to have meant 'granary'. In 1444 the valleys were being pulled into the Chimú kingdom, but no Inca army had yet reached the coast.

It was here that Francisco Pizarro, finding Tumbes a poor base, founded the first Spanish town in Peru. On 15 August 1532 he planted San Miguel de la Nueva Castilla at the Tallan settlement of Tangarara in the Chira valley. The town did not stay put: it moved to Piura la Vieja in October 1534 and to the harbour of Paita around 1578, and after Thomas Cavendish's men sacked Paita in 1587, carrying off twenty-five pounds of silver and five thousand five hundred pounds of other precious metal, the settlers moved for the last time in 1588 to Tacala beside the Piura River. Paita kept the sea trade: viceroys arriving from Spain landed there and went on to Lima overland, and the region shipped cordovan leather, Catacaos cotton, dried meat and tallow, salted shark, and salt from Colan and Sechura. On 4 January 1821 Piura proclaimed its independence in the atrium of the church of San Francisco.
zh:
皮乌拉河与奇拉河下游夹在太平洋与塞丘拉沙漠之间，季节性河水浇灌玉米、棉花和果园，海岸出产鱼和盐。塔拉人分作一个个零散社群，务农捕鱼，同邻近河谷以物易物，考古学家把他们更早的传统称作维库斯文化。土著语「皮尔瓦」即后来的皮乌拉，据说意为「粮仓」。1444年，这些河谷正被卷入奇穆王国，但印加军队还没有到达海岸。

弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗觉得通贝斯不适合做据点，便在这里建起西班牙人在秘鲁的第一座城镇：1532年8月15日，他在奇拉河谷的坦加拉拉立下「新卡斯蒂利亚的圣米格尔」。这座城一再迁移，1534年10月搬到旧皮乌拉，约1578年搬到海港派塔；1587年托马斯·卡文迪什的部下洗劫派塔，掠走25磅白银和5500磅其他贵金属，居民便在1588年最后一次迁到皮乌拉河畔的塔卡拉。海上贸易仍走派塔：从西班牙来的秘鲁总督多在此登岸，再走陆路前往利马；这一带输出科尔多瓦皮革、卡塔考斯棉花、肉干油脂、咸鲨鱼肉，以及科兰和塞丘拉的盐。1821年1月4日，皮乌拉在圣方济各教堂的廊前宣布独立。

en:
Tucume covers a plain south of the La Leche River, grouped around a bare rock hill called La Raya or Cerro Purgatorio. When the Sican centre of Batan Grande burned and was abandoned, the Lambayeque people built a new capital here from the eleventh century: more than two dozen major adobe pyramids and mounds spread across five hundred and forty acres. A tradition written down by the Spanish chronicler Miguel Cabello Valboa in 1586 makes the founder Naimlap, a hero who came from the sea and raised the town around La Raya with the help of local farmers. In 1444 the place belonged to the Chimú kings, who enlarged the old Huaca Larga and put a Chimú-style citadel on its summit. Across the Lambayeque plain, the largest valley of Peru's north coast, the eroded remains of about two hundred and fifty mud-brick pyramids line its waterways.

After the Chimú-Inca war of 1470 the Incas held Tucume, and the town was still in their hands when the Spaniards reached the north coast in 1532. The old capital did not survive the conquest as a living settlement. When Pedro Cieza de Leon came in 1547 he found the pyramids abandoned and ruined, while the canals and fields around them still fed the villages of the plain.
zh:
图库梅在拉莱切河以南的平原上，围一座名叫拉亚、又名炼狱山的光秃岩丘展开。西坎人的中心巴坦格兰焚毁废弃后，兰巴耶克人从11世纪起在这里另建都城：二十四座以上的大型土砖金字塔和土墩散布在五百四十英亩范围内。西班牙编年史家米格尔·卡韦略·巴尔沃亚1586年记下的一则传说称，建城者是从海上而来的英雄纳伊姆拉姆，他靠当地农人相助，绕拉亚山筑起此城。1444年，图库梅属于奇穆国王，他们扩建古老的长瓦卡，在其顶部修起一座奇穆式城寨。兰巴耶克平原是秘鲁北海岸最大的河谷，约二百五十座土砖金字塔的风蚀残迹沿水道排列在整片平原上。

1470年奇穆—印加战争后，图库梅转入印加手中，1532年西班牙人抵达北海岸时这座城镇仍归印加所有。古都没能作为有人居住的聚落熬过征服之年。佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂1547年来到时，金字塔已荒废倾颓，只有周围的沟渠农田还养着平原上的村落。

en:
The eight valleys of the upper Mayo run down from the cloud forests on the eastern flank of the Andes, each watered by its own tributary: the Yuracyacu, Negro, Tonchima, Indoche, Rumiyacu, Gera, Huascayacu and Juningue. Their people were the Muyupampas, kin of the Chachapoyas, whom the Incas called Sachapuyos, 'cloud-forest people'; their round plain gave the place its Quechua name, muyu pampa. In 1444 Inca power had not reached these forests. The Muyupampas kept to their own valleys, and the river jungle sheltered peoples beyond Inca rule; an Inca outpost on the red-clay plateau appeared only during the northern wars of Tupac Inca Yupanqui and his son Huayna Capac.

On 25 July 1540 Juan Perez de Guevara founded Santiago de los Ocho Valles de Moyobamba on that plateau with thirteen soldiers, after his captain Alonso de Alvarado gave up the jungle expedition and fell back to Chachapoyas. It was the first Spanish town in the Peruvian Amazon, and it grew into the 'metropolis of Maynas', the mustering point on the road between the Andes and Quito; from here missionaries, soldiers and traders pushed into the jungle to found missions and towns. Rivalry between the Jesuit and Franciscan mission fields was one reason the crown set up the General Commandancy of Maynas by royal decree in 1802, with Moyobamba its capital. An earthquake in 1746 had already moved the town four kilometres east from its old site at Ocsapampa, and in 1781 Mayoruna raiders killed its Spanish townsfolk. When San Martin sent Pedro Pascasio Noriega to raise the Mayo in 1821, Noriega told the plan to a Spanish officer who feigned sympathy and gave him away; he and the men he had named were shot in the main square on 11 April. The town proclaimed its independence on 19 August 1821.
zh:
上马约河的八条山谷从安第斯山东坡的云雾林中流出，每谷各有一条支流滋养：尤拉亚库河、内格罗河、通奇马河、因多切河、鲁米亚库河、赫拉河、瓦斯卡亚库河和胡宁格河。谷地的主人是莫尤潘帕人，与查查波亚人同源，印加人称他们为萨查普约人，意为「云雾林里的人」；他们的圆形平原给了这块地方克丘亚语名字「莫约班巴」（muyu圆，pampa平原）。1444年时印加势力还没有进入这片丛林，莫尤潘帕人安居在自己的谷中，河畔丛林里还住着不肯受印加管束的部族；直到图帕克·印卡·尤潘基及其子瓦伊纳·卡帕克发动北方战争，红土高地上才出现一座印加前哨。

1540年7月25日，胡安·佩雷斯·德·格瓦拉带着十三名士兵在这座高地上建立「莫约班巴八谷圣雅各镇」；此前他的长官阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多放弃丛林远征，退回了查查波亚斯。这是西班牙人在秘鲁亚马逊建立的第一座城镇，后来成为「迈纳斯都会」，是安第斯山区与基多之间道路上的必经集结地；传教士、士兵和商人从这里深入丛林，建立传教站和城镇。耶稣会与方济各会传教区争执不下，也是西班牙王室1802年颁布敕令设立迈纳斯总司令部辖区、以莫约班巴为首府的原因之一。早在1746年，一场地震已迫使城镇从旧址奥克萨潘帕向东迁移4公里；1781年，马约鲁纳人袭击此地，屠杀了西班牙裔市民。1821年，圣马丁派佩德罗·帕斯夸西奥·诺列加前来马约河策动起义，诺列加却把计划告诉了一名假装同情爱国派的西班牙军官，被对方出卖；他和他供出名字的人于4月11日在主广场被枪决。同年8月19日，莫约班巴宣布独立。

en:
Wankapampa, written Huancapampa or Huancabamba in Spanish sources, lies in a high Andean valley east of Piura and north of Cajamarca, on the river of the same name that drains toward the Marañón. Before the Incas its people farmed the mountain slopes, wove cloth and venerated jaguars, and their pasturelands carried llama and alpaca herds. In 1444 the valley was ruled by its own highland lords, beyond the Inca frontier.

Tupac Yupanqui's armies conquered it around 1480, put down the jaguar cult and moved mitma families into the valley. They laid out Caxas and Huancapampa on the Inca highway from Quito to Cuzco, with cut-stone buildings, aqueducts and storehouses for the armies. In October 1532, while Francisco Pizarro waited on the coast for news of Atahualpa, Hernando de Soto rode in with sixty horsemen to reconnoitre: at Caxas he found the highway, the supply depots and a house of chosen women said to hold five hundred maidens, and Huancapampa beyond it struck him as the larger and more populous town. After the conquest Pizarro granted its people in encomienda to Diego Palomino, and colonial Huancabamba formed part of the Piura corregimiento.
zh:
万卡班巴（西班牙文作Huancapampa或Huancabamba，通译宛卡班巴）地处皮乌拉以东、卡哈马卡以北的安第斯高山谷地，同名河流穿境而过，流向马拉尼翁河。印加到来之前，这里的人在山坡耕作、纺织布匹、崇拜美洲豹，牧场上放养着美洲驼和羊驼。1444年的谷地由本地山地首领统治，还在印加边界之外。

约1480年，图帕克·尤潘基的军队征服谷地，取缔美洲豹崇拜，把米特马人家迁来安置。他们在基多通往库斯科的印加大道上营建卡萨斯和万卡班巴，修起琢石房屋、水渠和军需仓库。1532年10月，皮萨罗在沿海等待阿塔瓦尔帕的消息，派埃尔南多·德·索托率六十名骑兵前来侦察：他在卡萨斯看到这条大道、补给仓库和一座据称住着五百名少女的选女之屋，再往前的万卡班巴在他看来更大、人口也更多。征服之后，皮萨罗把当地居民以监护征赋制封给迭戈·帕洛米诺，殖民时期的万卡班巴隶属皮乌拉辖区。

en:
Pisqupampa, written Piscobamba in Spanish, means 'plain of birds' in Quechua. It occupies a cold plain at roughly 3,300 metres in the Conchucos highlands, on the eastern flank of the Ancash Andes. After Chavín, Recuay and Wari power faded, independent ethnic lordships formed there between 1200 and 1480, and the Piscopampa were split among rival curacazgos that fought each other over mountain pasture. In 1444 their valleys answered to local chiefs, not to the court at Cuzco.

When the Inca general Capac Yupanqui pushed north towards the Yanamayo River around 1480, the united warriors of the Piscopampa, Conchucos and Siguas drove him back on Yauya, and he had to build the military tambo of Maraycalle at 4,260 metres before he could subdue the country. In April 1533 Hernando Pizarro and Miguel de Estete came this way back from sacking Pachacamac and were lodged by the curaca Tawani before riding on to Cajamarca. Pedro Cieza de León later saw a broad, long stone lodging for lords here, and wrote that Conchucos had always held rich gold and silver mines. The Spanish town of San Pedro y San Pablo de Piscobamba was founded in 1574. On 24 November 1594 Archbishop Toribio de Mogrovejo held his eighth diocesan synod there, when the town was capital of the Conchucos corregimiento.
zh:
皮斯科班巴（西班牙文作Piscobamba）在盖丘亚语中意为「鸟之平原」，地处安卡什山东侧孔丘科斯高地、海拔约3300米的寒冷平原。查文、雷夸伊和瓦里的势力消退后，1200至1480年间，这一带形成一批独立的族群领地；皮斯科班巴人分成几个相争的酋邦，为争夺山地牧场彼此交战。1444年，这些谷地听命于本地首领，而不是库斯科的宫廷。

约1480年，印加将领卡帕克·尤潘基向北推进到亚纳米约河，皮斯科班巴、孔丘科斯和西瓜的联军把他逼退到尧亚；他只得在海拔4260米处修筑马赖卡列军用驿站，才得以压服此地。1533年4月，埃尔南多·皮萨罗和米格尔·埃斯特特洗劫帕查卡马克后沿印加道路返回，途经这里时由酋长塔瓦尼安排食宿，随后继续前往卡哈马卡。佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂后来在此见过一座又宽又长的石造贵族驿馆，并称孔丘科斯一带向来盛产金银矿。1574年，圣佩德罗与圣巴勃罗·德·皮斯科班巴建城；1594年11月24日，大主教托里比奥·德·莫格罗韦霍在此举行第八次教区会议，当时此镇是孔丘科斯辖区的首府。

en: Chimbote is the cove of Ferrol Bay, where the Lacramarca River meets the sea beside the Santa valley, the corridor from the desert coast up into the Ancash highlands. Moche masons raised the adobe platforms and plazas of Huaca San Pedro between the second and seventh centuries, and Chimú pottery and burials have been found around the bay; in 1444 this coast marked the southern edge of the Chimú kingdom. It passed to the Incas around 1470 with the rest of Chimor, though no Inca building has been identified here. After 1532 the fishermen of the cove answered to the Spanish villa of Santa in the next valley, and no formal town was ever laid out. The name Chimbote appears for the first time in an official record in 1774, when Cosme Bueno listed it as a small fishing settlement attached to Santa, and a fishing cove was all it was when the period ended in 1821.
zh: 钦博特是费罗尔湾里的小港湾，拉克拉马卡河在此入海，旁边的圣塔河谷是从沙漠海岸登上安卡什高地的通路。莫切工匠在2至7世纪筑起圣佩德罗瓦卡的土砖台庙和广场，海湾一带还出土过奇穆陶器和墓葬；1444年，这段海岸正是奇穆王国的南缘。约1470年，它随奇穆其余疆土转入印加之手，不过这里没有发现过印加建筑。1532年以后，湾里的渔民归邻谷的西班牙人圣塔镇管辖，始终没有规划建城。「钦博特」这个名字最早见于1774年的官方记录，科斯梅·布埃诺把它记作隶属圣塔的小渔村；到1821年这一时期结束时，它仍然只是这样一个小港湾。

en:
The Callejón de Huaylas is the long valley of the Santa river, walled between the snows of the Cordillera Blanca and the dark ridge of the Cordillera Negra. Hunters had sheltered in the Guitarrero cave thousands of years earlier; the Chavín shrine of Pumacayán stood above the later town, and Recuay and Wari lords in their turn ruled the valley. The Huaylas polity that followed gave the province its name. In 1444 Guaraz, 'the dawn', was one of its chief towns, set among maize fields and llama pastures, and no Inca army had yet entered the valley.

The Huaylas fought hard to keep it so. Allied with the Conchucos and other neighbours, they held out until Huayna Capac campaigned in the valley himself; when they surrendered the wak'a of Pumacayán was thrown down and their country became an Inca province. Its curacas sent daughters to the court at Cuzco. Añas Colque's son by the Inca was Paullu Inca, later made Inca by the Spaniards and their principal native ally; Contarhuacho, a Huaylas curaca, became a secondary wife of Huayna Capac, and her daughter Quispe Sisa, baptized Inés Huaylas Yupanqui, was given to Francisco Pizarro and became his first wife.

Hernando Pizarro passed through in January 1533 on the road to Pachacámac and left the first Spanish account of the valley's fields and villages. In August 1536 Contarhuacho answered the siege of Lima by sending a large native contingent from Huaylas against Manco Inca's army, and her men helped Pizarro hold his new capital. Francisco Pizarro granted the valley to Sebastián de Torres in 1538, and by the 1570s silver, lead and tin had hundreds of Quechua villagers working Spanish mines. In January 1574 Alonso de Santoyo gathered the settlements into the reducción of San Sebastián de Huaraz, seat of the corregimiento two years later. An earthquake wrecked its churches in 1725, and in 1780 the town rose against the alcabala tax. Colonel Campino entered it with his men late in 1820 and proclaimed independence; in February 1821 San Martín made Huaraz the capital of the new department of Huaylas.
zh:
瓦伊拉斯走廊是圣河冲积出的一条长谷，夹在积雪的布兰卡山脉与黝黑的内格拉山脉之间。早在公元前数千年，猎人已在吉他雷罗洞穴栖身；查文时代的普马卡扬圣所立在后来瓦拉斯城上方的高地上，此后雷夸伊和瓦里的统治者先后主宰这条河谷，最后兴起的瓦伊拉斯人还把名字留给了这个省份。1444年时，意为「黎明」的瓜拉斯是该国的一座重镇，周围玉米田成片，高山牧场上羊驼成群，印加军队还没有踏入谷地。

瓦伊拉斯人为保住谷地苦战多年。他们与孔丘科等邻邦结盟，一直抵抗到瓦伊纳·卡帕克亲自出征；投降之后，普马卡扬的瓦卡被拆毁，故土沦为印加的一个行省，各族酋长把女儿送往库斯科王廷。阿尼亚斯·科尔克所生的儿子是保柳·印卡，后来被西班牙人立为印卡王，也是他们最主要的本地盟友；瓦伊拉斯女酋长孔塔尔瓦乔做了瓦伊纳·卡帕克的次妃，她的女儿伊内斯·尤潘基（Quispe Sisa）被送给弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗，成为他的第一个妻子。

1533年1月，埃尔南多·皮萨罗在前往帕查卡马克途中经过这里，留下了西班牙人对谷地农田和村落的最早记述。1536年8月利马被围，孔塔尔瓦乔从瓦伊拉斯派出一支庞大的本地队伍迎战曼科·印卡的大军，帮皮萨罗守住了他的新都。1538年，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗把整条谷地封给塞瓦斯蒂安·德·托雷斯；银、铅、锡矿随后引来西班牙矿主，到1570年代已有数以百计的克丘亚村民在矿上劳作。1574年1月20日，阿隆索·德·桑托约把四散的土著村落归并为归化镇圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·瓦拉斯，两年后瓦拉斯成为辖区治所。1725年的一场地震毁了城中教堂，1780年市民又因抗缴销售税起事。1820年末，坎皮诺上校率军入城宣布独立；1821年2月，圣马丁把瓦拉斯定为新设的瓦伊拉斯省首府。

en:
The Camaná River reaches the Pacific through a broad, fertile valley on one of Peru's driest coasts. Smaller desert valleys at Ocoña and Tambo and the sheltered roadstead of Quilca lie along the same shore. Spanish sources use the name Changos for the maritime villagers, a loose term for communities who fished from reed, plank and seal-skin rafts, gathered guano from offshore islands and used it to manure maize fields. They traded dried fish, shells and guano inland for wool, fruit, maize and coca. The people of Ocoña, Camaná and Tambo kept their independence after nearby highland groups came under Inca pressure, and Spanish chronicles credit Tupac Inca Yupanqui with their later conquest. In 1444 this shore was a coastal borderland outside direct Inca rule.

Spanish founders established Villa Hermosa in the valley on 9 November 1539, but within a year its council and settlers moved to the Chili Valley, and the displaced town became Arequipa. Camaná kept its value through Quilca. In 1540 Francisco Camargo landed there with goods bound for Charcas, Cuzco and Arequipa, and the roadstead became Arequipa's main seaport. Alonso Martínez de Rivera refounded the valley town on 29 September 1557 as San Miguel de Rivera. Under the late viceroyalty Quilca served royalist shipping, and when Lima proclaimed Peruvian independence in 1821, Camaná and its port remained on the royalist side.
zh:
卡马纳河在秘鲁最干旱的一段海岸上穿过宽阔肥沃的谷地，注入太平洋；同一岸线还有奥科尼亚、坦博等荒漠小谷和可避风浪的基尔卡锚地。西班牙文献把沿海村民称作昌戈人，这个泛称覆盖多个海洋群体。他们乘芦苇、木板和海豹皮筏捕鱼，从近海岛屿收集海鸟粪给玉米施肥，又把鱼干、贝壳和鸟粪带到内地，交换羊毛、水果、玉米和古柯。奥科尼亚、卡马纳和坦博居民在邻近高地群体受到印加压力之后仍长期保持自主，西班牙编年史把后来的征服归于图帕克·印卡·尤潘基。1444年，这片海岸仍是印加直接统治之外的边地。

1539年11月9日，西班牙殖民者在谷中建立美丽镇；不到一年，市政会和居民迁往奇利河谷，这座迁走的城镇后来成为阿雷基帕。卡马纳凭借基尔卡保留其价值。1540年，弗朗西斯科·卡马戈在此卸下运往查尔卡斯、库斯科和阿雷基帕的货物，基尔卡随后成为阿雷基帕的主要海港。1557年9月29日，阿隆索·马丁内斯·德·里韦拉重建谷地城镇，命名为圣米格尔·德·里韦拉。总督辖区末期，基尔卡为保王派船只服务；1821年利马宣布独立时，卡马纳和港口仍站在保王派一边。

en:
Ayaviri stands on the cold plains northwest of Lake Titicaca, where the Inca road from Cuzco runs south into the Collao. Aymara herders had run their flocks over these grasslands under Pucará, Tiwanaku and then Colla overlords before Sarmiento de Gamboa dated the Inca conquest to Pachacutec in 1430; the newcomers resettled the town and raised a temple of the Sun above its chief huaca. In 1444, therefore, Ayaviri was a newly secured road station, whose pastures and llama herds supplied the traffic moving south out of Cuzco.

Diego de Almagro's expedition to Chile drew food and stores from its tambos on the way through in 1534. Francisco Villacastín became its first encomendero in 1543, and the church of San Francisco was later raised on the foundations of the Sun temple; Reginaldo de Lizárraga, passing through, called the windy town large and rich in livestock, and estancias spread over its grazing lands. As part of Lampa it was assigned to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1777 and returned to Peru in 1796. Ayaviri joined the highland rising of 1771 and opened its gates to Túpac Amaru II on 6 December 1780. On 10 March 1815 the Angulo brothers and Mateo Pumacahua marched out of the town's barracks for Umachiri. Pumacahua had once been the royalist captain whose pursuit helped run Túpac Amaru II to ground; now he commanded the Cuzco junta's army, lost the battle on 11 March, and was captured and executed at Sicuani on 17 March.
zh:
阿亚维里位于的的喀喀湖西北的高寒平原，库斯科通往科利亚奥的印加大道从这里穿过。在这片艾马拉牧人的草场上，普卡拉、蒂亚瓦纳科和后来的科利亚势力曾先后称雄。据萨缅托·德·甘博记载，帕查库特克于1430年征服此地并重新安置居民，还在当地最重要的瓦卡上方建起太阳神庙。因此1444年时，阿亚维里是库斯科新近平定的道路驿站，高山草场和羊群为都城南下的人马提供补给。

1534年，迭戈·阿尔马格罗远征智利途中经过此地，从沿途坦博取走粮食和物资。弗朗西斯科·比利亚卡斯廷1543年成为首任监护主，圣方济各教堂后来就建在太阳神庙的旧基上；雷希纳尔多·德·利萨拉加路过时，称这座多风的城镇规模可观、牲畜繁盛，牧场庄园随之遍布周围的草场。作为兰帕的一部分，阿亚维里1777年被划给新设的拉普拉塔总督区，1796年又重归秘鲁。当地人参与了1771年的高原起义，1780年12月6日开门迎接图帕克·阿马鲁二世。1815年3月10日，安古洛兄弟和马特奥·普马卡瓦从城中兵营开赴乌马奇里。普马卡瓦本是保王派军官，当年追击图帕克·阿马鲁二世、促成其败亡；此时他却统率着库斯科政务会的军队，次日战败，被俘后于3月17日在锡夸尼被处死。

en:
Quero, also spelled Q'ero and Q'iru (q'iru means 'wood' in Quechua), names a Quechua people and their high valleys in Paucartambo, east of Cuzco, rather than a town the Spaniards founded. Their country climbs from warm maize slopes below 1,800 metres to puna pasture above 4,500 metres under the snows of Ausangate: potatoes in the high fields, llamas and alpacas on the grasslands, villages one to three days apart along mountain trails. The people break the thin soil with the chaki taklla foot-plough, keep temporary huts in the lower valleys for sowing time, and weave cloth in patterns traced to Inca times. In 1444 these valleys belonged to Antisuyu, the Inca quarter facing the forests of the Amazon.

The Spaniards never made much of this country. In 1565 they set up a corregimiento at Paucartambo, the market town below the valleys, where coca from the warm gorges, gold washed out of forest rivers and highland textiles passed between the Andes and the Amazon lowlands. Quero storytellers tell how their ancestors held off a Spanish force near Wiraquchapampa until the mountain spirit, the apu, shook the ground and sent a rockslide down upon the soldiers.
zh:
克罗（又拼Q'ero、Q'iru，克丘亚语q'iru意为「木材」）这个名字指的是库斯科以东、保卡坦博一带一个克丘亚人群及其高山谷地，这里没有西班牙式的城市。他们的土地从海拔1800米以下种玉米的温暖坡地，升到奥桑加特雪山脚下海拔4500米以上的普纳草原：高处种马铃薯，草场放美洲驼和羊驼，村落之间沿山路要走一到三天。人们用脚犁查基塔克亚翻耕贫瘠的土地，在低地谷地留有播种季暂住的茅屋，织出的布纹样可追溯到印加时代。1444年，这些山谷属于印加面向亚马孙森林的安蒂苏尤。

西班牙人始终没有经营这片山地。1565年，他们在谷地下方的集镇保卡坦博设立辖区，暖谷的古柯、林河淘出的黄金和高地织物经此往来于安第斯山与亚马孙低地之间。克罗人的口传故事讲，祖先在维拉科查潘帕附近挡住一支西班牙军队，最后是山神阿普摇动大地，一场山崩落在敌兵头上。

en:
The largest ruined city of the pre-Inca Andes lies 21 kilometres south-east of Lake Titicaca, on the cold Collao plain. Tiwanaku grew up around AD 110, and by 800 ten to twenty thousand people lived there, farming raised fields, herding llamas and trading across the lake. Its builders dressed andesite and sandstone into the stepped Akapana pyramid, the Kalasasaya enclosure and a sunken court. Their most famous work is the Gate of the Sun, a single ten-ton slab carved with a staff-bearing god above rows of winged figures, with the flat stone platforms of Pumapunku to the south. A long drought around 1000 helped empty the city. When its power dissolved, Aymara lordships divided the Collao, and the Pacajes, whose seat was Caquiaviri on the Desaguadero, held the lands around the ruins. In 1444 their farmers planted potatoes, quinoa and oca and pastured llamas among the fallen monoliths, and the lords of Caquiaviri still kept the Inca armies beyond their frontier.

The Pacajes held out until the campaigns of Tupac Inca Yupanqui late in the fifteenth century, when their country became part of Qullasuyu. The first Spaniard to leave an account of the ruins was Pedro Cieza de León, who reached them in 1549 while searching for the southern capital of Qullasuyu and wrote that they belonged to a people older than the Incas. The village beside the site belonged to the province of La Paz in Spanish Alto Peru, and early in the seventeenth century its church of San Pedro went up from dressed stone pulled from the adjoining ruins. After the patriot defeat at Huaqui, the Pacajes rose in 1811 with Omasuyos and Larecaja against Spanish rule.
zh:
前印加时代安第斯最大的废城坐落在的的喀喀湖东南21公里的科亚奥寒原上。蒂亚瓦纳科约公元110年兴起，到800年已有一两万居民；他们耕种高台式农田、牧养大羊驼，并在湖上贸易。营建者把安山岩和砂岩琢成阶梯状的阿卡帕纳金字塔、卡拉萨亚围院和一座下沉式神庙。最有名的作品是太阳门：一整块约十吨重的石板上雕着持杖神像，下方排列着带翼人像；城南则是普玛彭古的石砌平台。约1000年的长期大旱加速了城市的荒废。蒂亚瓦纳科政权解体后，艾马拉诸领地分割科亚奥，以德萨瓜德罗河畔卡基亚维里为治所的帕卡赫斯人据有遗址一带。1444年，他们的农民在倒伏的石碑之间种植马铃薯、藜麦和奥卡薯、牧养大羊驼，卡基亚维里的首领仍把印加军队挡在边外。

帕卡赫斯人一直坚守到15世纪后期图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的远征，其地才并入科利亚苏尤。第一个留下文字记录的西班牙人是佩德罗·谢萨·德·莱昂：1549年他为寻找科利亚苏尤的南部首府来到遗址，写道这是比印加更古老的民族留下的。遗址旁形成的村落归入西属上秘鲁拉巴斯省；17世纪初，圣佩德罗教堂用从相邻古迹拆下的琢石建起。爱国者在瓦基战败后，1811年帕卡赫斯人与奥马苏约斯、拉雷卡哈一同举事，反抗西班牙统治。

en:
San Joaquín and its later administrative seat Exaltación anchor the wet north-eastern edge of the Moxos plains, between the Mamoré and the Itenéz, the river also called the Guaporé. In 1444 no empire reached its seasonally flooded savannas, lakes and riverine forest. Cayubaba villages held the country near the Mamoré, while Baure communities lived toward the San Martín and Baures rivers; their people planted manioc and maize on raised ground, fished, hunted and travelled by canoe with the rise and fall of the waters.

The Jesuit Cipriano Barace met the Baure around 1690. Agustín Zapata entered Cayubaba country in 1693 and counted seven substantial villages, six of about 1,800 people and one of more than 2,000. Antonio Garriga gathered the Cayubaba into the Exaltación de la Santa Cruz mission in 1704, and Antonio de Orellana and Pedro de Rado founded San Joaquín among the Baure on 21 August 1708, one of nine Baure reductions. Each town was laid out around a church and plaza, with quarters for weavers, painters and musicians; cattle were new to the plains, and wild-cotton cloth was woven finely enough to be exported to Europe, along with cacao, rice, sugar and wax. The Hungarian Jesuit Francisco Eder lived fifteen years at the San Martín mission in the 1720s and 1730s and left the fullest contemporary account of Baure life, printed in 1770. The reductions held about 16,000 Baure by 1740, but their people had been disarmed and Portuguese bandeirantes crossed the rivers to seize slaves. After the Jesuit expulsion reached Moxos in 1768 the missions lost people, and late in the century the local leader Gabriel Ojeari moved San Joaquín to the Machupo River, away from the slavers' route.
zh:
圣华金及其后来的行政中心埃克萨尔塔西翁，坐落在莫克索斯平原湿润的东北缘，地处马莫雷河与伊特内斯河（又称瓜波雷河）之间。1444年，没有任何帝国的势力到达这里季节性泛滥的草原、湖泊和河岸林。卡尤瓦瓦人的村落据有马莫雷河附近地带，包雷人则生活在圣马丁河与包雷斯河方向；人们在高地种植木薯和玉米，捕鱼打猎，划独木舟随河水涨落往来。

耶稣会士西普里亚诺·巴拉塞约在1690年与包雷人接触。1693年，阿古斯丁·萨帕塔进入卡尤瓦瓦人的地方，数出七个人口稠密的村落：六个各约一千八百人，另一个超过两千人。1704年，安东尼奥·加里加把卡尤瓦瓦人聚入圣十字埃克萨尔塔西翁传教站；1708年8月21日，安东尼奥·德·奥雷利亚纳和佩德罗·德拉多在包雷人中建立圣华金，它是九座包雷人归化村镇之一。每座城镇都以教堂和广场为中心布局，分出织工、画匠和乐师的坊区；牛群是平原上的新东西，野棉花织出的布精细到能远销欧洲，一同外运的还有可可、稻米、糖和蜡。匈牙利籍耶稣会士弗朗西斯科·埃德尔1720至1730年代在圣马丁传教站住了十五年，写下关于包雷人生活最详尽的同时代记录，1770年付印。到1740年，这些归化村镇约有一万六千名包雷人，但居民已被解除武装，葡萄牙旗队不断渡河掳人为奴。1768年驱逐耶稣会的命令抵达莫克索斯后，传教村镇人口流散；18世纪末，本地首领加夫列尔·奥赫阿里把圣华金迁往马丘波河，避开奴贩子的水路。

en:
The Madre de Dios gathers the rains of the sub-Andean forests and carries them east to the Beni, the Madeira and the Amazon. In 1444 its banks and tributaries were an indigenous river world below the Apolobamba and Paucartambo ranges. Arawak-speaking Yine, also called Piro, lived along the Madre de Dios, Urubamba and Las Piedras; Tacana communities were scattered along the Beni, Madre de Dios and Orthon, and Araona groups held the forest paths nearer the mountains. Inca roads and a stone fortress at Ixiamas marked the edge of a border province the Incas called the Chunchos, but Inca power stopped in the foothills, maintained there with gifts and diplomacy rather than garrisons. The river, rather than any road, joined villages, fishing camps and garden clearings.

Spanish parties first tested the frontier through the Pelechuco and Charazani valleys, on old Inca trails. In June 1615 Pedro de Legui Urquiza left Larecaja with 165 men and three Augustinians and founded Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, the nucleus of Apolo, on 10 August. In 1670 Gabriel González led a party down the rivers in search of the legendary wealthy land of Paitití and returned without finding it. The Franciscans Bartolomé Zumeta, Francisco Corso, Andrés de Castro and Pedro de la Peña entered Araona country in 1680, lived there two years and founded Santa Bárbara; over the next four decades their outstations ran through Ixiamas to the Madidi and the Madre de Dios. Neophytes kept slipping back into the forest and stations were abandoned, so the chain never closed the frontier. In 1814 the priest Ildefonso de las Muñecas took refuge at the Atén mission, and a small local band under Santos Pariamo held it against royalist troops sent by Agustín Gamarra; many river communities still lived beyond Spanish control.
zh:
马德雷德迪奥斯河汇集安第斯山麓森林的雨水，向东带入贝尼河、马代拉河和亚马孙河。1444年，它的干流与支流是阿波洛班巴岭、保卡坦博岭下方的原住民河居世界。操阿拉瓦克语的伊内人（又称皮罗人）住在马德雷德迪奥斯河、乌鲁班巴河和彼德拉斯河沿岸，塔卡纳人散布在贝尼河、马德雷德迪奥斯河和奥尔顿河一带，阿劳纳人则据守更靠近大山的林间通路。印加道路和伊西亚马斯的一座石堡，标志着被印加人称作「琼乔斯」的边省的尽头；印加势力止于山麓，在那里靠馈赠和外交维系，没有驻军。村落、渔营和农地全靠河流水路往来相连。

西班牙人最初沿古老的印加山道，从佩莱丘科和查拉萨尼山谷试探这片边疆。1615年6月，佩德罗·德·莱吉·乌尔基萨率165人和三名奥斯定会士离开拉雷卡哈，8月10日建立瓜达卢佩圣母镇，即阿波洛的雏形。1670年，加夫列尔·冈萨雷斯率队顺河而下，寻找传说中的富庶之地帕提提，一无所获而返。1680年，方济各会士巴托洛梅·苏梅塔、弗朗西斯科·科尔索、安德烈斯·德·卡斯特罗和佩德罗·德拉佩尼亚进入阿劳纳人的地方，住了两年，建立圣巴巴拉；此后四十年间，传教点经伊西亚马斯一直延伸到马迪迪河与马德雷德迪奥斯河。新信徒不断逃回丛林，传教站屡遭废弃，这条链子始终没能锁住边疆。1814年，教士伊尔德方索·德·拉斯·穆涅卡斯避入阿滕传教站，桑托斯·帕里亚莫率一小队本地居民据守，挡住了阿古斯丁·加马拉派来的保王军；直到此时，许多河边社群仍在西班牙人的控制之外。

en:
Santa Cruz de la Sierra is the warm lowland of eastern Bolivia, where the Piraí and Guapay cross the Grigotá plains between the Andean foothills, the Chaco and the Amazon. The plains take their name from the title of the Chané leaders, Arawak-speaking villagers who farmed the grassland and left pottery and weapons across the region. In 1444 no Inca road or Spanish encomienda reached so far east, and the Chané still held the river crossings, though Guaraní-speaking war bands from the southeast would break into the country in the following century.

Domingo Martínez de Irala scouted the plains in 1549. On 26 February 1561 Ñuflo de Chaves marched in from Asunción with 158 soldiers and founded Santa Cruz de la Sierra at Santa Cruz la Vieja, naming it after his home town in Extremadura; he was killed fighting in Itatín in 1568. Indian raids pushed the settlers toward the Guapay, where San Lorenzo el Real arose in 1590, while the old town shifted by stages toward the Piraí, and the two populations were joined in one town on 9 November 1621. The frontier captaincy formed by these moves never knew the mining mita of the highlands. Its people lived by cattle and maize, supplied the Jesuit expeditions into Chiquitos and Moxos, and turned back Portuguese bandeirantes from the east.

When the independence wars reached the lowland, Antonio Vicente Seoane set up the first junta on 24 September 1810. The royalist comeback left the province to Ignacio Warnes, a soldier from Buenos Aires who had fought under Belgrano and ran Santa Cruz's small 'republiqueta' from 1813 to 1816; he freed the slaves who joined his ranks and held the frontier until 21 November 1816, when the royalist Francisco Javier de Aguilera attacked on the El Parí plain. Warnes's horse was killed under him by a cannon shot and he was bayoneted on the ground; his head was displayed on a pike. Aguilera's men were too cut up to advance into the Argentine provinces.
zh:
圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉地处玻利维亚东部暖热低地，皮赖河与瓜佩河流过格里戈塔平原，平原夹在安第斯山麓、大查科与亚马孙之间。「格里戈塔」原是查内人首领的称号；这些讲阿拉瓦克语的村民耕作草地，陶器和武器散见于这一带。1444年，印加的道路和西班牙的委托监护地都没有延伸到这么靠东的地方，查内人仍守着各处渡口；不过到下个世纪，东南方讲瓜拉尼语的武装队伍就会攻入这片地方。

1549年，多明戈·马丁内斯·德·伊拉拉踏勘了这片平原。1561年2月26日，纽夫洛·德·查维斯率一百五十八名士兵从亚松森开进此地，在圣克鲁斯拉维耶哈建立圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，以他在埃斯特雷马杜拉的故乡命名；1568年他在伊塔廷的战事中被杀。印第安人的袭扰迫使殖民者迁往瓜佩河畔，1590年在那里建起圣洛伦索埃尔雷亚尔，旧城人口也分批移向皮赖河，两镇居民最终于1621年11月9日合为一城。合并而成的边疆都督辖区没有高原那种矿山米塔：居民靠牧牛和种玉米过活，为深入奇基托斯和莫霍斯的耶稣会远征队补给物资，还击退过从东面来的葡萄牙旗兵。

独立战争蔓延到低地后，安东尼奥·维森特·塞奥内于1810年9月24日建起第一个洪达。保王军反扑时，出身布宜诺斯艾利斯、曾在贝尔格拉诺麾下作战的伊格纳西奥·瓦尔内斯主持圣克鲁斯的抗战小政权（republiqueta），从1813年守到1816年；他宣布加入队伍的奴隶获得自由，并守住了这条边疆。1816年11月21日，保王派将领弗朗西斯科·哈维尔·德·阿吉莱拉在城外的埃尔帕里平原发起进攻。瓦尔内斯的坐骑被炮弹击毙，他坠马后被刺刀杀害，首级被挑在长矛上示众；阿吉莱拉的部队也伤亡惨重，无力再把战事推向阿根廷诸省。

en:
The high valley of Sucre, called Chuquisaca in the Inca years and La Plata by the Spaniards, lies between the Churuquella and Sica Sica hills at nearly 2,800 metres. It was the country of the Charcas, warlike Aymara speakers who kept the hamlet of Choquechaca at the foot of the two hills, where their shrines stood. In 1444 Inca armies had not yet entered these southern valleys: the Charcas lived under their own lords and beat off Guarani-speaking Chiriguano raiders from the eastern lowlands. Conquest came at the end of the century with Tupac Inca Yupanqui, who made the land the province of Charca within Collasuyu, with Chuquisaca its capital, and settled Quechua speakers alongside the Aymara.

The Portuguese Aleixo Garcia, the first European known to cross the continent, passed through in 1525. In the late 1530s Gonzalo Pizarro's men camped here and local allies showed them the silver mines of Porco; on 16 April 1540 Pedro Anzures founded the Villa de la Plata on the old Choquechaca site. When the silver mountain of Potosi was found a few days' ride to the south in 1545, La Plata became the seat of law and government for the richest mining country in the Indies, home from 1559 to the Royal Audiencia of Charcas, whose courts and treasury answered for the whole of Upper Peru, and from 1624 to the University of St Francis Xavier, one of the first universities in the Americas. By 1639 about 14,000 people lived among its churches and colleges.

In 1776 the Audiencia passed from the Viceroyalty of Peru to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, and the Carolina Academy, founded the same year, trained a generation of lawyers. On 25 May 1809 a crowd led by those lawyers deposed the Audiencia's president and set up the first autonomous junta of the Spanish-American wars of independence. Troops sent from Peru retook La Plata before the year ended, and in the long war that followed the city changed hands again and again; its deputies signed the United Provinces' declaration of independence at Tucuman in 1816. In the hills around the city Juana Azurduy, born in La Plata in 1780, and her husband Manuel Ascencio Padilla led the guerrilla bands of the district they called the Republiqueta de La Laguna; she held a lieutenant-colonel's commission from 1816, and the bands were still fighting as the war entered 1821.
zh:
苏克雷（印加时期称丘基萨卡，西班牙人建城后名拉普拉塔）所在的高谷坐落在丘鲁克利亚山与西卡西卡山之间，海拔近2800米，本是查尔卡人的故土。这个好战的艾马拉语族群把乔克查卡村建在两座山下，山上有他们的祭拜地。1444年时印加军队尚未进入这些南方河谷，查尔卡人仍由自己的首领治理，抵御着东部低地讲瓜拉尼语的奇里瓜诺人袭扰。15世纪末，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基征服此地，设为科利亚苏尤的查尔卡省，以丘基萨卡为首府，又迁来克丘亚语居民与艾马拉人杂处。

已知最早横穿南美大陆的欧洲人、葡萄牙人阿莱霍·加西亚1525年经过此地。1530年代末，贡萨洛·皮萨罗的部下在此扎营，当地盟友向他们指明波尔科的银矿；1540年4月16日，佩德罗·安苏雷斯在乔克查卡旧址上建立拉普拉塔镇。1545年，南行数日路程之外的波托西银山被发现，拉普拉塔成了西印度最富庶银矿区的司法与行政中枢：1559年设查尔卡斯皇家检审庭，法庭与财政机构统管整个上秘鲁；1624年又创办圣弗朗西斯科·哈维尔大学，属美洲最早的大学之一。到1639年，城中教堂与学院之间已住有约1.4万人。

1776年，检审庭由秘鲁总督辖区划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区，同年创办的卡罗琳娜学院培养出一代法学家。1809年5月25日，这些法学家带领市民罢免检审庭庭长，建立西属美洲独立战争中的第一个自治政权。秘鲁派来的军队在年底前重新夺城，此后漫长的战争中拉普拉塔反复易手；1816年，当地代表在图库曼签署拉普拉塔联合省独立宣言。城周山间，1780年生于拉普拉塔的胡安娜·阿苏尔杜伊与丈夫帕迪利亚率领游击队作战，他们控制的地区被称为「拉古纳小共和国」；她从1816年起领中校军衔，直到1821年战争进入末期，这些武装仍在战斗。

en:
The Tucumán lowlands lie below the Aconquija ranges, where streams gather into the Salí River and the land opens east into the Chaco. In 1444 the western valleys were held by Pazioca, or Diaguita, peoples, Calchaquíes, Quilmes and Tolombones among them, who farmed terraces of maize, potatoes and quinoa and herded llamas, while Lule, Vilela and Tonocote groups held the central and eastern plains. The Quilmes' fortified hill town, a hundred hectares below Cerro Alto del Rey, was the largest pre-Columbian settlement in what is now Argentina, and its warriors had thrown back Inca attacks. Inca forces only reached that frontier around 1480, so in 1444 the chiefdoms answered to no outside governor.

Diego de Rojas passed through in 1543. The first lasting Spanish town was San Miguel de Tucumán, founded by Diego de Villarroel at Ibatín in 1565 for the new Governorate of Tucumán. Calchaquí warriors under the cacique Gualán nearly destroyed it in 1578. The Quilmes held out longest: in 1667 some four hundred Spaniards besieged their forts, blocked their fields by the Santa María River and poisoned the mountain water, and after a month the cacique Martín Iquín surrendered. About 2,600 survivors were force-marched a thousand kilometres to a reservation outside Buenos Aires; fewer than five hundred arrived, and the place took the name Quilmes. In 1685 San Miguel was moved to La Toma on the Salí, on the highway between Peru and the Río de la Plata, where the townsmen sold cattle, cloth and timber to the mule convoys carrying Andean silver to Buenos Aires.

The wars of independence made San Miguel a military and political centre. On 24 September 1812 Belgrano's Army of the North defeated a royalist army twice its size outside the town and stopped its advance into the interior. The Bazán y Laguna house, built in 1760, had billeted Belgrano's troops and then hosted the Congress of Tucumán; on 9 July 1816 delegates of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata declared independence there. In 1820 Governor Bernabé Aráoz proclaimed a Federal Republic of Tucumán, which lost Catamarca and Santiago del Estero within a year and collapsed.
zh:
图库曼低地位于阿孔基哈山脉脚下，溪涧汇成萨利河，地势向东开向查科平原。1444年，西部谷地属于帕西奥卡人（即迪亚吉塔人，有卡尔查基、基尔梅斯、托隆邦等支派），他们在梯田种植玉米、马铃薯和藜麦，牧养大羊驼；中部和东部平原住着卢莱人、比莱拉人和托诺科特人。基尔梅斯人设防的山城坐落在雷伊山（Cerro Alto del Rey）下，占地约一百公顷，是后来阿根廷境内最大的前哥伦布时期聚落，他们的战士还曾击退印加军队。印加军队约1480年才推进到这条边界，因此1444年各酋邦还不受外来总督管辖。

迭戈·德·罗哈斯1543年经过此地。第一座持久的西班牙城镇是圣米格尔-德图库曼，1565年由迭戈·德·比利亚罗埃尔在伊瓦廷为新设的图库曼督辖区建立。1578年，酋长瓜兰率领卡尔查基战士几乎将它摧毁。基尔梅斯人坚持最久：1667年，约四百名西班牙军围攻他们的堡垒，封锁他们在圣玛丽亚河畔的田地，又在山泉中投毒，一个月后酋长马丁·伊金投降。约二千六百名幸存者被徒步押解近一千公里，迁往布宜诺斯艾利斯郊外的居留地，抵达者不足五百，那个地方后来便以他们得名，即基尔梅斯。1685年，圣米格尔城迁到萨利河畔的拉托马，正当秘鲁与拉普拉塔之间的王道，居民向运送安第斯白银前往布宜诺斯艾利斯的骡队出售牛、布匹和木材。

独立战争使圣米格尔成为军事和政治中心。1812年9月24日，贝尔格拉诺的北方军在城外击败兵力两倍于己的保王军，挡住了它向内陆的推进。巴桑-拉古纳家1760年建成的宅邸曾驻扎贝尔格拉诺的部队，后来又成为图库曼议会的会址；1816年7月9日，拉普拉塔联合省的代表在这里宣布独立。1820年，省长贝尔纳韦·阿劳斯宣布成立图库曼联邦共和国，不到一年卡塔马卡和圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗相继脱离，共和国随之瓦解。

en:
Santa Catalina is the coldest corner of the Jujuy puna, a treeless tableland nearly 4,000 metres high between the Quebrada de Humahuaca and the Bolivian plateau. Atacameño herders of the Lipe division and Omaguaca clans, a mix of Calchaquí and Atacameño stock, pastured llamas and washed gold with sieves from the mountain streams. Their resistance slowed first the Incas and then the Spaniards; Quechua and Aymara forces overran the country only around 1470, and in 1444 its high valleys still answered to their own chiefs.

Diego de Almagro crossed this frozen plain in 1536 on his march to Chile. The gold-bearing streams and llama herds long remained the district's only wealth; the town's parish church went up in the seventeenth century, and from 1783 the puna formed part of the intendancy of Salta del Tucumán. During the independence wars the high road from Upper Peru carried royalist armies south, while the gaucho bands of Martín Miguel de Güemes, men who knew every path of the mountains, harried them for seven years in the Guerra Gaucha. In June 1821 the royalist general Olañeta sent 300 men under José María Valdez, called Barbarucho, from Yavi across this puna by the camino del despoblado and down the Quebrada del Toro to surprise Salta. Güemes was shot in the night attack and died of the wound on 17 June 1821.
zh:
圣卡塔利娜是胡胡伊普纳高原最寒冷的一角，这片不生树木的台地海拔近4000米，夹在乌马瓦卡峡谷与玻利维亚高原之间。利佩一支的阿塔卡梅诺牧人和兼有卡尔查基、阿塔卡梅诺血统的奥马瓜卡氏族在此放牧美洲驼，用筛子从山溪里淘洗金粒。他们的抵抗先拖慢了印加人、后拖慢了西班牙人；克丘亚和艾马拉军队直到1470年前后才攻下这片地方，1444年时各高山谷地仍归本地酋长管辖。

1536年，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗在进军智利途中穿过这片冰封高原。此后很长时间里，产金的溪流和驼群是这里唯一的财富；17世纪镇上建起教区教堂，1783年起普纳高原隶属萨尔塔-德尔图库曼行政区。独立战争期间，从上秘鲁南下的大道上不断有保王军开过，马丁·米格尔·德·格梅斯的高乔游击队都是熟悉山间每一条小路的本地人，七年里以「高乔战争」袭扰敌军。1821年6月，保王军将领奥拉涅塔派绰号「巴尔瓦鲁乔」的何塞·玛丽亚·巴尔德斯率300人，从亚维出发，取道「荒原道」穿过这片空旷的普纳高原，沿托罗峡谷下山突袭萨尔塔；格梅斯在夜袭中中弹，1821年6月17日伤重而死。

en:
The warm valley of Tarija lies between the high Andes and the eastern jungles at little over 1,800 metres, watered by the Guadalquivir. It was the land of the Churumatas, with the Moyos Moyos people to their north, and in 1444 it sat beyond the Inca frontier. Tupac Inca Yupanqui's Collasuyu wars of the 1470s broke the Churumatas: many were deported as mitma garrison-settlers to Chile and Argentina, and mitimaes brought from the Norte Chico of Chile, the Tomatas, were planted in their place. When Spaniards first saw the valley it was largely empty, and only old stone roads crossed its hills.

Pedro de Candia camped here with 200 men from September 1539 to February 1540, but the valley gained no permanent Spanish town until Viceroy Toledo's frontier war against the Chiriguanos. On 4 July 1574 the Sevillian captain Luis de Fuentes y Vargas, on Toledo's orders, founded the Villa de San Bernardo de la Frontera de Tarija and moved Tomata families from the San Juan del Oro valley to till its lands. The mild climate suited wheat, olives and vines; the friars planted vineyards, and through the seventeenth century Tarija wine and the muscat grape brandy called singani went to the mining cities of Upper Peru. In 1776 the district passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata and was administered from Salta.

On 25 July 1810 the town council declared for the Buenos Aires revolution and sent the lawyer Jose Julian Perez de Echalar as its deputy to the junta there. Royalist armies from Upper Peru answered by marching on the frontier town. The battle of Tarija opened on 14 April 1817, and the next day Gregorio Araoz de Lamadrid's United Provinces troops defeated the royalists. The district changed hands more than once afterwards, and its roads and haciendas became the country of the gaucho bands whose frontier skirmishing lasted as the wars entered 1821.
zh:
塔里哈所在的温暖谷地位于高耸的安第斯山与东部丛林之间，海拔1800米出头，瓜达尔基维尔河穿流其间，本是楚鲁马塔人的土地，莫约斯莫约斯人住在他们以北。1444年时这里还在印加边界之外。1470年代图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的科利亚苏尤战争击垮楚鲁马塔人：许多人被作为米特马克屯戍者迁往智利和阿根廷，又从智利北奇科迁来叫托马塔人的米特马克移民填补空地。等西班牙人见到谷地时，这里已大半荒芜，山丘间只有古老的石砌道路。

1539年9月至1540年2月，佩德罗·德·坎迪亚率200人在此驻扎，但直到托莱多总督征讨奇里瓜诺人的边境战争时期，谷地才有了永久的西班牙城镇。1574年7月4日，塞维利亚籍统领路易斯·德·富恩特斯·伊·巴尔加斯奉托莱多之命建立「塔里哈边境圣贝尔纳多镇」，并从圣胡安德尔奥罗谷地迁来托马塔人家族耕种。温和的气候宜于小麦、油橄榄和葡萄；修士们开辟葡萄园，整个17世纪，塔里哈葡萄酒和用麝香葡萄蒸馏的辛加尼白兰地都输往上秘鲁各矿业城镇。1776年，这一地区划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区，由萨尔塔管辖。

1810年7月25日，市议会宣布支持布宜诺斯艾利斯革命，并派律师何塞·胡利安·佩雷斯·德·埃查拉尔作为代表前往布宜诺斯艾利斯执政委员会。上秘鲁的保王军随即进兵这座边镇。1817年4月14日塔里哈战役打响，次日格雷戈里奥·阿劳斯·德·拉马德里率领的拉普拉塔联合省军队击败保王军。此后这一地区仍不止一次易手，道路和庄园成了边境高乔武装袭扰拉锯之地，战事一直延续到1821年战争末期。

en:
The Puna de Atacama is a cold, arid plateau of salt flats and volcanic ridges, where sheltered quebradas hold the only watered ground. Atacameño, or Likanantay, communities herded camelids and farmed the valley floors, and they guarded their oases early. The greatest of their strongholds, Quitor, fills a bend above the San Pedro River: a twelfth-century stone pukará of terraces and towers climbing eighty metres up the hillside over the road it guarded. In 1444 these fortresses were still in local hands, and Inca armies had not yet crossed the Salar de Atacama.

Topa Inca Yupanqui annexed the oases in the later fifteenth century and made Catarpe, five kilometres north of San Pedro de Atacama, the principal Inca administrative centre in what is now Chile; its governors directed Quitor and the other pukarás, while Inca roads ran from the Salar de Atacama into north-western Argentina. The first Spaniards reached the oases with Diego de Almagro in 1536, and Atacameño resistance lasted until a peace settlement in 1557. Colonial rule imposed encomiendas, gathered indigenous families into supervised pueblos de indios and pressed Catholic baptism, and the Kunza language lost ground. In the Andean revolts after 1780 the Atacameño leader Tomás Paniri brought the region into the uprisings of Túpac Amaru II and Túpac Katari.
zh:
阿塔卡马高原是片寒冷干旱的高地，遍布盐沼和火山脊，只有有遮蔽的峡谷里才有水浇地。阿塔卡马人（Likanantay）的社群放牧骆驼科牲畜，在谷底耕作，也很早就懂得守卫绿洲。他们最大的堡寨基托尔雄踞圣佩德罗河上方的河湾：这座12世纪的石砌要塞沿山坡垒出层层台地和敌楼，高出脚下看守的道路八十米。1444年，这些堡寨仍在当地人手中，印加军队还没有越过阿塔卡马盐沼。

15世纪后半叶，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基征服这些绿洲，把圣佩德罗德阿塔卡马以北5公里的卡塔佩（Catarpe）建成印加在今智利境内最重要的行政中心；官吏从那里统辖基托尔等堡寨，印加道路也从阿塔卡马盐沼通向阿根廷西北部。1536年，第一批西班牙人随迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗抵达绿洲，阿塔卡马人的武装抵抗持续到1557年议和。殖民当局推行委托监护制，把原住民家庭编入受监管的印第安人村镇，强迫受洗，昆萨语日渐衰微。1780年后的安第斯大起义中，阿塔卡马人首领托马斯·帕尼里率本地人加入图帕克·阿马鲁二世和图帕克·卡塔里的暴动。

en:
Calama is the oasis where the Loa River crosses the driest stretch of the Atacama. Its Kunza name Ckara-ama is explained as a town amid the waters, because the river, marshes and wet meadows nearly surrounded the settlement. In 1444 Lickan-antay farmers grew maize, worked copper and kept llamas on a route between the Pacific, the altiplano and the Argentine valleys. Dried fish came inland from Cobija, while llama caravans carried highland cloth, metals and crops toward the coast. The oasis was a desert stopping place on an older exchange network, and the Inca frontier was approaching from the east.

At Turi, above the upper Loa, Atacameno builders had raised a stone pucara from about 1250. Its four hectares and roughly 620 enclosures make it the largest architectural complex left by their culture. After the Incas took Atacama around the middle of the fifteenth century, they added Inca structures, including a 26-metre kallanka hall. Calama itself became the main tambo of the Despoblado, supplying chasquis and soldiers with maize and tempered copper for weapons; local people later gave Diego de Almagro's returning party copper horseshoes made with that technique. Spanish settlement stayed thin, although the Corregimiento of Atacama claimed the roads for the Royal Audiencia of Charcas and linked Cobija with Potosi, Salta and Tucuman. During the rising of Tupac Amaru II, Tomas Panire led the local movement and was executed.
