In 1793 Andres Baleato's map still placed Calama under Copiapo in the Captaincy General of Chile, a sign of how uncertain jurisdiction remained along the desert frontier.
zh:
卡拉马是洛阿河横穿阿塔卡马最干旱地带时形成的绿洲。孔萨语地名词根被解释为「水中央的城镇」，因为河流、沼泽和湿草甸几乎把定居点围在中间。1444年，利坎安塔伊农人在这里种植玉米、加工铜器、牧养羊驼；绿洲正处在太平洋、高原和阿根廷谷地之间的道路上。鱼干从科维哈进入内陆，羊驼商队则把高原织物、金属和作物带向海岸。在印加边疆自东面逼近以前，这里已是旧交换网络中的沙漠歇脚点。

在洛阿河上游的图里，阿塔卡马工匠约1250年起建起石砌堡垒。遗址占地约4公顷，留有约620个房间，是阿塔卡马文化规模最大的建筑群。15世纪中叶印加征服阿塔卡马后，对堡垒加以改建，并增建一座长26米的印加式长厅。卡拉马本身成为阿塔卡马无人区的主要坦博，向查斯基信使和士兵供应玉米以及可造兵器的韧铜；迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的队伍返程经过时，当地人还送给他们用这种工艺制成的铜马掌。西班牙人始终未能大规模定居，但阿塔卡马辖区代表查尔卡斯王家检审院控制这些道路，把科维哈同波托西、萨尔塔和图库曼连接起来。图帕克·阿马鲁二世起义时，托马斯·帕尼雷领导当地起事，后来被处死。1793年，安德烈斯·巴莱阿托的地图仍把卡拉马列入智利都督府的科皮亚波辖区，可见这条沙漠边疆的管辖界限仍旧含混。

en:
The Antofagasta coast is one of the driest faces of the Atacama, broken by fog-watered hills and a few springs that reach the sea. In 1444 its inhabited places were Chango fishing camps, above all Paposo, Cobija, Tocopilla and Taltal, rather than the future bay and town of Antofagasta. Fishing families drew fresh water from the ravines, put rafts into the cold Pacific and carried dried fish and shellfish across the desert to Lickan-antay oases. Inca expansion reached Atacama around the middle of the century, but its roads and resettlements affected the inland routes around San Pedro de Atacama more firmly than this shore.

Colonial settlement began with water and pasture rather than a city. On 4 July 1674 Francisco de Cisternas, corregidor of Copiapo, received the Paposo grant and turned the watered bay into cattle range; from 1679 the place was recorded as Nuestra Senora del Paposo under Copiapo. During Ambrosio O'Higgins's governorship, Copiapo militia were posted there against English privateers sailing the Atacama coast. In 1789 Gregorio Almendariz replaced the local deputy Jose Zuleta after abuses against the Changos. Four years later, Jose Joaquin Pinto's expedition reached Junquillar, counted 142 people between Pan de Azucar and Agua Salada, and proposed a town, parish and school, but the treasury could not pay for it. Governor Gabriel de Aviles authorized a chapel in 1797. A royal order of 1803, confirmed in 1805, moved Paposo toward the Viceroyalty of Peru; the Chilean census of 1813 nevertheless listed its port district under Copiapo with 570 inhabitants, and the future bay of Antofagasta still had no Spanish town.
zh:
安托法加斯塔一带是阿塔卡马沙漠最干旱的海岸之一，只有靠雾水滋养的丘陵和少数抵达海边的泉水打破荒漠。1444年，有人居住的是帕波索、科维哈、托科皮利亚和塔尔塔尔等昌戈渔民营地，而不是后来的安托法加斯塔湾和城镇。渔民家庭从沟谷汲取淡水，驾皮筏进入寒冷的太平洋，再把鱼干和贝类穿过沙漠带到利坎安塔伊人的绿洲。15世纪中叶印加扩张抵达阿塔卡马，但印加道路和移民安置对圣佩德罗·德·阿塔卡马一带的内陆通道影响更深，对这条海岸触及较少。

殖民定居点最初依靠的是水源和牧场，而不是城市。1674年7月4日，科皮亚波辖区长官弗朗西斯科·德·西斯特纳斯获得帕波索封地，把这片有水的海湾用作牧牛地；1679年后，该地以「帕波索圣母」之名归科皮亚波管辖。安布罗西奥·奥希金斯任都督期间，科皮亚波民兵驻守这里，防备在阿塔卡马海岸航行的英国私掠者。1789年，地方代表何塞·苏莱塔因虐待昌戈人被格雷戈里奥·阿尔门达里斯接替。四年后，何塞·华金·平托的队伍抵达洪基亚尔，在潘德阿苏卡尔至阿瓜萨拉达之间清点出142人，并提议设立城镇、堂区和学校，却因财政无款作罢。1797年，都督加夫列尔·德·阿维莱斯批准修建小堂。1803年的王室命令于1805年获确认，要把帕波索划归秘鲁总督辖区；但1813年智利人口普查仍把这个港区列入科皮亚波，记有570名居民，后来的安托法加斯塔海湾也还没有西班牙城镇。

en:
The country around Santiago del Estero is the wooded floodplain of the Dulce River, whose waters spill across the low ground in the wet season and return to a single channel in the dry. In 1444 the river banks were held by Tonocote villagers, whom the first Spaniards called Juríes: they grew maize and cotton, wove cotton cloth and fired painted pottery. Lule peoples lived to the north and west, Vilela and Mocoví groups to the east and Sanavirones to the south. Neither Inca rule nor Quechua had yet reached the Dulce.

Santiago del Estero is the oldest Spanish town in Argentina, though its first years were a long fight over jurisdiction. Juan Núñez de Prado, sent from Peru, founded El Barco on 29 June 1550 and named it for his birthplace in Spain; ordered about by the rival Chilean and Peruvian authorities, he moved the settlement twice. In 1553 Francisco de Aguirre came from Chile, arrested Prado, broke up the town council and destroyed its records, and on 25 July refounded the place as Santiago del Estero. Quechua-speaking yanaconas in Prado's party gave the region its Quechua dialect, quichua santiagueño. Expeditions sent from the town founded San Miguel de Tucumán, Córdoba, Salta and La Rioja, and Santiago became the first capital of the Governorate of Tucumán and seat of its first bishopric, later moved to Córdoba; the silver road in time bypassed the old town. An earthquake ruined the cathedral in 1817, and on 27 April 1820 the autonomist Juan Felipe Ibarra proclaimed provincial autonomy.
zh:
圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带是杜尔塞河林木覆盖的平原：雨季河水漫过低地，旱季又收回单一河道。1444年，河畔居住着托诺科特村民，最早的西班牙人把他们称作胡里人；他们种玉米和棉花，织棉布，烧制彩绘陶器。卢莱人居在北方和西方，比莱拉人和莫科维人在东方，萨纳维龙人在南方。此时印加统治和克丘亚语都还没有到达杜尔塞河。

圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗是阿根廷最古老的西班牙城镇，但最初几年纠缠在管辖权之争里。奉秘鲁之命而来的胡安·努涅斯·德·普拉多于1550年6月29日建立巴尔科，名字取自他在西班牙的故乡；在智利与秘鲁两方相争的当局命令下，他把定居点搬了两次。1553年，弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷从智利到来，逮捕普拉多，解散市议会，销毁档案，于7月25日重建此城，改名圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗。普拉多一行中讲克丘亚语的亚纳科纳人，带来了当地的克丘亚方言圣地亚哥克丘亚语。从这座城出发的远征队先后建立圣米格尔-德图库曼、科尔多瓦、萨尔塔和拉里奥贾，圣地亚哥也成为图库曼督辖区的第一个首府和最早主教区的驻地，主教区后来迁往科尔多瓦；白银道路日久也绕过了这座老城。1817年的地震毁了主教座堂；1820年4月27日，自治派胡安·费利佩·伊瓦拉宣布省自治。

en:
La Rioja occupies a chain of arid Andean ranges broken by narrow irrigated valleys, with the snow-capped Nevado de Famatina rising over the north of the province. In 1444 Diaguita, Capayan and Olongasta communities farmed the valley floors through their own canals and grazed llamas on the dry uplands; tracks over the ranges linked them with the plains toward Córdoba and the high country toward Chile. No European town yet stood here.

Juan Ramírez de Velasco, a conquistador from the Spanish Rioja, founded the City of All Saints of New Rioja on 20 May 1591 as a war seat on the Tucumán frontier, laying out a cabildo and grants for his soldiers. In 1592 he rode north into the Famatina range after its reported gold. Diaguita attacks nearly destroyed the new town in 1593, and a rising in 1630 was put down by Governor Felipe de Albornoz. La Rioja answered first to Peruvian and then to Córdoban authorities until 1776, when it passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata; its cabildo backed the May Revolution of 1810. Francisco Ortiz de Ocampo became the first provincial governor in 1820, and a year later Juan Facundo Quiroga's llanero militiamen from the southern plains fought their way into the capital and installed Nicolás Dávila as governor.
zh:
拉里奥哈地处一列干旱的安第斯山脉，山间夹着靠水渠灌溉的狭窄谷地，北部耸立着积雪的法马蒂纳峰。1444年，迪亚吉塔人、卡帕扬人和奥隆加斯塔人社群在谷底开渠务农，在干燥高地上牧放骆马；翻山的小路把他们与通往科尔多瓦的平原、通往智利的高地连在一起。此时这里还没有欧洲人的城镇。

来自西班牙拉里奥哈地区的征服者胡安·拉米雷斯·德·贝拉斯科，于1591年5月20日建立「新拉里奥哈诸圣城」，把它作为图库曼边境的作战据点，设立市政会、向士兵分地。1592年，他为寻找传闻中的金子北上进入法马蒂纳山地。1593年，迪亚吉塔人的进攻几乎摧毁新城，1630年的又一次起义被省长费利佩·德·阿尔沃诺斯镇压。拉里奥哈先后受秘鲁和科尔多瓦管辖，1776年转入新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区，市政会支持了1810年五月革命。1820年，弗朗西斯科·奥尔蒂斯·德·奥坎波成为首任省长；一年后，胡安·法昆多·基罗加率领南部草原民兵攻入首府，扶立尼古拉斯·达维拉为省长。

en:
Chepes covers the semi-arid southern plains of La Rioja province below the Sierra de los Llanos, where streams out of the ranges feed scattered pastures and vineyards. In 1444 the country sat between two indigenous worlds: Diaguita farmers worked the northern Riojan valleys, while Huarpe villages and grazing grounds ran across the plains toward San Juan and San Luis.

The villa began as a cattle ranch. Antonio Reynoso Tello held the tract under a Tucumán grant, built a house and a church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, planted vines and stocked herds; his will made at Tama in 1754 is the earliest surviving record of the place. The llanos around it were ranch country, and its ranch hands made hard-riding militia. Juan Facundo Quiroga was born at San Antonio de los Llanos in 1788, the son of a local rancher, and in the fighting after 1810 he led these llanero companies as the 'Tiger of the Llanos'. When La Rioja broke with Córdoban authority in 1820, his charges into the capital settled who governed the province.
zh:
切佩斯在拉里奥哈省南部半干旱平原上，背靠洛斯亚诺斯山脉，山溪在山前滋养出片片牧场和葡萄园。1444年，这里处在两个原住民世界之间：迪亚吉塔农人经营北部河谷，瓦尔佩人的村落和牧场越过平原，一直延伸向圣胡安和圣路易斯。

这座村镇起自一座牧牛庄园。安东尼奥·雷诺索·特略凭图库曼授地持有这片土地，盖起住宅和「切佩斯至净受孕圣母」教堂，栽种葡萄、牧放牲畜；1754年他在塔马立下的遗嘱，是关于此地现存最早的文字记载。周围的洛斯亚诺斯是牧牛区，牧人惯于骑射，组成剽悍的民兵。胡安·法昆多·基罗加1788年生于圣安东尼奥·德·洛斯亚诺斯，父亲是当地牧场主；1810年后的战事中，他率领这些草原民兵，人称「洛斯亚诺斯之虎」。1820年拉里奥哈脱离科尔多瓦当局，他的队伍几次攻入首府，决定省长的废立。

en:
San Juan lies in arid Andean foothills cut by the snowmelt San Juan River, whose water makes the Tulum Valley an oasis. In 1444 Huarpe farmers watered maize, quinoa, beans and squash through canals of their own digging and kept llamas, while Diaguita villages held the northern Jáchal and Iglesia districts. Inca roads and garrisons reached these valleys only late in the fifteenth century.

Juan Jufré founded San Juan de la Frontera on 13 June 1562 by order of the Chilean captain general Francisco de Villagra, set up a cabildo, and distributed about 1,500 Huarpe and Diaguita people in encomiendas; many were sent to work fields and mines in Chile. A flood of the San Juan River swept the fragile town away late in 1593, and the founder's son Luis Jufré y Meneses rebuilt it twenty-five blocks to the south around a new plaza. Vines went in between 1569 and 1589, and wine and aguardiente became the goods that mule carts carried east from the oasis. Long ruled from Mendoza under Chile, San Juan passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776, the year an earthquake badly damaged the town. When José de San Martín made neighbouring Mendoza his base in 1814, the cabildo raised soldiers and taxed outgoing wine to supply mules and provisions for the crossing of the Andes. Domingo Faustino Sarmiento, later the author of Facundo and president of Argentina, was born here in 1811. San Juan separated from Cuyo as an autonomous province in 1820.
zh:
圣胡安地处干旱的安第斯山麓，圣胡安河的融水在荒山之间浇灌出图卢姆谷地这片绿洲。1444年，瓦尔佩农人自开渠道灌溉玉米、藜麦、菜豆和南瓜，饲养骆马，迪亚吉塔人的村落分布在北部的哈查尔和伊格莱西亚一带；印加的道路和戍卒要到15世纪末才进入这些谷地。

1562年6月13日，胡安·胡弗雷奉智利都督弗朗西斯科·德·比亚格拉之命建立「边疆圣胡安」，设立市政会，把约1500名瓦尔佩人和迪亚吉塔人分到委托监护名下，其中许多人被送往智利的农庄和矿场做工。1593年末，圣胡安河洪水冲毁了这座简陋的城镇，建立者之子路易斯·胡弗雷·伊·梅内塞斯把城南迁25个街块，围绕新广场重建。1569至1589年间，这里开始栽种葡萄，葡萄酒和阿瓜尔丁特酒成为绿洲上骡车东运的货物。圣胡安长期在智利治下由门多萨管辖，1776年转入新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区，同年又遭地震重创。何塞·德·圣马丁1814年以邻近的门多萨为大本营后，市政会招募士兵、对出境的酒征税，为翻越安第斯山筹措骡子和军粮。1811年出生于此的多明戈·福斯蒂诺·萨米恩托后来写下《法昆多》，并成为阿根廷总统。1820年，圣胡安脱离库约，成为自治省份。

en:
The Suquía River cuts through the Sierras Chicas before running out onto the plains, and its valley was the natural route between the Río de la Plata and the highlands of Peru long before any Spanish road reached it. In 1444 it was Comechingón country: the Henia and Kamiare groups lived in ayllu communities that farmed maize, beans and quinoa on rain-fed plots, gathered algarrobo and chañar fruit, and built rectangular houses partly dug into the earth against the cold mountain wind. Their trails joined sierra camps to guanaco and pampas-deer hunting grounds, and the riverside ground the Spanish later called Quisquisacate, 'meeting of waters,' held no town.

Jerónimo Luis de Cabrera marched out of Potosí in 1572 with orders from the Viceroy of Peru to plant a Spanish town on that route, and on 6 July 1573 he founded Córdoba de la Nueva Andalucía at Quisquisacate, on the left bank of the Suquía; four years later the settlement was moved to the opposite bank, where seventy blocks were laid out around a plaza. From 1622 an inland customs house, the aduana seca, taxed the wagon and mule traffic between the estuary and Peru, and the town lived from provisioning it. The Jesuits arrived in 1599 and made Córdoba their center for missions across southern South America: their college, opened in 1610, became the University of Córdoba in 1613, the first university in what is now Argentina, beside the Compañía church and the cathedral, and it gave the city its nickname La Docta, 'the learned one.' When the British seized Buenos Aires in 1806, Viceroy Sobremonte withdrew to Córdoba and opened the viceroyalty's interim capital there, gathering troops for the counterattack. In 1810 the city became the royalist answer to the May Revolution: Santiago de Liniers, the officer who had reconquered Buenos Aires from the British, raised men here against the junta, was hunted down after his defeat and shot without trial that August, while Dean Gregorio Funes carried the university and the city over to the revolution.
zh:
苏基亚河切穿奇卡斯山后流入平原，早在西班牙道路到达之前，这条河谷就是拉普拉塔河口与秘鲁高原之间天然的通道。1444年，这里是科梅钦贡人的土地：埃尼亚和卡米亚雷群体以村社为单位，在雨养田地上种植玉米、菜豆和藜麦，采集角豆和刺果豆的果实，建造半埋入地下的长方形房屋抵挡山间寒风。小径把山间营地与原驼、潘帕斯鹿猎场相连；西班牙人后来称作奎奎萨卡特、意为「两水汇合」的河畔地方，此时还没有城镇。

1572年，赫罗尼莫·路易斯·德·卡夫雷拉奉秘鲁总督之命从波托西出发，要在这条通道上建立一座西班牙城镇；1573年7月6日，他在苏基亚河左岸的奎奎萨卡特建立「新安达卢西亚的科尔多瓦」。四年后，定居点迁到对岸，围绕广场铺成七十个街块。1622年起，王室在此设立内陆关卡，向河口与秘鲁之间往来的车队和骡队征税，城市就靠为过境商旅补给立足。耶稣会士1599年抵达，把科尔多瓦作为在南美洲南部传教的中心：他们的学院1610年开办，1613年发展为科尔多瓦大学，是今阿根廷境内第一所大学，耶稣会教堂和主教座堂就在旁边，城市也得到「学者城」（La Docta）的别称。1806年英军攻占布宜诺斯艾利斯，索布雷蒙特总督退到科尔多瓦，把总督辖区的临时首都设在这里，召集反攻的军队。1810年，这座城市成了保王派对五月革命的回应：曾从英军手中收复布宜诺斯艾利斯的圣地亚哥·德·利涅尔斯在此募兵对抗执政委员会，兵败后被追获，于8月未经审判即遭枪决；教长格雷戈里奥·富内斯则带领大学和城市倒向革命。

en:
San Luis lies between the wooded Comechingón sierras, the Guanacache lagoons and the dry grassland crossing called the Travesía Puntana, the last watered ground before the road runs out across the Pampas. In 1444 Comechingón farmers held the northeastern hills, Huanacache Huarpes lived around the lagoons, Olongasta Diaguitas reached the far north, and Taluhet Het hunters moved across eastern plains that then ran thick with pampas deer, the venados that gave the country its early name.

Spaniards from Chile planted a town here in 1594 as an outpost of the Cuyo jurisdiction, but the first site flooded and was abandoned; refounded in 1596 as San Luis de Loyola Nueva Medina de Rioseco, it was moved twice more and settled on its present ground in 1689, usually called La Punta after the tongue of land it occupied. Caravans from Buenos Aires joined the road to Mendoza here before the Andean crossing to Chile. By the eighteenth century the Taluhet had been thinned by epidemics and displaced or absorbed by mounted Ranquel and Pehuenche groups from the south. The cabildo recognized the Buenos Aires junta in June 1810, and a census in 1812 registered every man of military age in the partido. On 15 February 1820 an open cabildo deposed Lieutenant Governor Vicente Dupuy and proclaimed the province autonomous.
zh:
圣路易斯位于林木葱郁的科梅钦贡山地、瓜纳卡切湖群和被称为「特拉韦西亚·蓬塔纳」的干旱草场之间，是道路横穿潘帕斯之前最后一片有水源的地方。1444年，科梅钦贡农人据有东北部山地，瓜纳卡切分支的瓦尔佩人住在湖群周围，奥隆加斯塔系迪亚吉塔人分布在最北端，塔尔乌埃特系埃特猎人在东部平原游猎，那时平原上潘帕斯鹿成群，这片土地早期名字里的「鹿」说的就是它们。

1594年，来自智利的西班牙人在此设城，作为库约辖区的前哨；最初的城址遭水淹而废弃，1596年以「圣路易斯·德·洛约拉·新梅迪纳·德·里奥塞科」之名重建，此后又两度迁址，1689年才定于现址，日常多按所在的舌形高地称它「拉蓬塔」。从布宜诺斯艾利斯来的骡车队在这里并入通往门多萨的大路，再翻安第斯山前往智利。到18世纪，塔尔乌埃特人已被瘟疫削弱，被南方骑马的兰克尔人和佩文切人排挤或同化。市政会于1810年6月承认布宜诺斯艾利斯洪达，1812年的一次人口普查登记了境内所有适龄男子。1820年2月15日，公开市政会罢黜副省长比森特·迪皮伊，宣布省份自治。

en:
The Salado reaches the Paraná through lagoons, marshes and slow side rivers, and in 1444 this wet country was shared by river peoples. Charrúa bands ranged the grasslands that became Santa Fe, while the Timbú, Calchín and Quiloaza villages of the Chaná-Timbú family lined the Paraná, the Coronda and the Carcarañá. They fished from canoes that also tied the islands to the mainland camps, hunted rhea and deer with bolas and bows, planted maize, squash and beans in seasonal plots, and gathered honey; hereditary chiefs headed their communal longhouses.

The first Spanish post in the region went up in 1527, when Sebastián Gaboto built the Sancti Spiritus fort on the Carcarañá, Spain's first settlement anywhere in the Río de la Plata basin; native warriors burned it two years later. Juan de Garay came down from Asunción in 1573 and founded Santa Fe near Cayastá as a staging port for river traffic to the estuary, and seven years later he refounded Buenos Aires from the same Paraná route. Floods, locusts and attacks wore the first site out, and between 1650 and 1660 the townspeople carried the cabildo and the parish church south to the Vera Cruz ground. A royal decree of 1662 made Santa Fe a puerto preciso, a port every passing vessel had to call at, and the town lived from that river traffic. The cabildo recognized the May Revolutionary junta in June 1810, but anger at Buenos Aires's centralism soon carried the city into José Gervasio Artigas's federal camp; in 1816 the militia officer Estanislao López seized the town with help from Artigas and made it a federal stronghold.
zh:
萨拉多河穿过潟湖、沼泽和岔流汇入巴拉那河，1444年时，这片水乡由河畔诸族群分据。查鲁亚游群活动在后来成为圣菲的草原上，廷布、卡尔钦、基洛阿萨等查纳-廷布村落分布在巴拉那河、科龙达河与卡尔卡拉尼亚河沿岸。他们划独木舟捕鱼，舟楫还把岛屿与大陆营地相连，用投石索和弓箭猎取美洲鸵和鹿，在季节性田地上种植玉米、南瓜和菜豆，采集蜂蜜；村落在世袭首领之下居住在公共长屋里。

西班牙人在这一带的第一个据点建于1527年：塞瓦斯蒂安·加沃托在卡尔卡拉尼亚河畔筑起圣埃斯皮里图斯堡，这是西班牙人在整个拉普拉塔河流域最早的定居点，两年后即被原住民战士烧毁。1573年，胡安·德·加赖从亚松森南下，在卡亚斯塔附近建立圣菲，作为通往河口航运的中转港；七年后，他又沿同一条巴拉那河水路重建布宜诺斯艾利斯。洪水、蝗灾和袭扰耗尽了旧城址，1650年至1660年间，市民把市议会和本堂区教堂南迁到贝拉克鲁斯。1662年的王家诏令把圣菲定为「必泊港」，过往船只一律要在此停靠，城市就靠这项河运特权立足。1810年6月，市议会承认五月革命的执政委员会，但对布宜诺斯艾利斯集权的不满很快把圣菲带入何塞·赫尔瓦西奥·阿蒂加斯的联邦阵营；1816年，民兵军官埃斯塔尼斯劳·洛佩斯在阿蒂加斯援助下夺取城市，把它变成联邦派据点。

en:
Rosario's stretch of the Paraná is a flat bank cut by the Ludueña, Saladillo and smaller streams, with islands lying offshore. In 1444 there was no town here: Charrúa bands and Chaná-Timbú river people fished the islands and banks, crossed the grasslands after rhea and deer, and planted maize, squash and beans in seasonal plots; their canoes worked the crossings of the country the Spanish later called the Pago de los Arroyos, the 'country of the streams.'

The crossing became a wagon stop early in the seventeenth century on the royal road from Córdoba to the Paraguay river route, and it never received a founding charter. Around 1724 the settler Santiago Montenegro built a mill and a chapel to Our Lady of the Rosary here, and the growing place took its name from that chapel; a local magistrate followed by mid-century. Rosario entered the history of the United Provinces on 27 February 1812, when Manuel Belgrano, who had been building the Independencia and Libertad batteries to cover the river crossing, raised a new light-blue-and-white flag over the Independencia battery on Espinillo Island and made his gunners and infantry swear to it at dawn; local tradition names María Catalina Echevarría de Vidal as the woman who sewed the cloth and the sailor Cosme Maciel as the man who hauled it up. The First Triumvirate in Buenos Aires had not approved the flag and ordered it put away, but Belgrano's men carried it north and won the Battle of Tucumán under it that September, and the Congress of Tucumán adopted it as the national flag in 1816.
zh:
罗萨里奥所在的巴拉那河岸地势平坦，卢杜埃尼亚河、萨拉迪略河和多条小溪切岸而入，河中岛洲散布。1444年这里还没有城镇：查鲁亚游群和查纳-廷布河畔人群在岛屿与岸边捕鱼，穿过草原追逐美洲鸵和鹿，在季节性田地上种植玉米、南瓜和菜豆；他们的独木舟往来于各渡口，西班牙人后来把这一带称作「溪流地」。

17世纪初，这个渡口成为科尔多瓦通往巴拉圭河路的王家大道上的大车队停靠点，却始终没有领过建城文书。约1724年，定居者圣地亚哥·德·蒙特内格罗在这里修了磨坊和供奉玫瑰圣母的小堂，发展起来的居民点便从这所小堂得名，到18世纪中叶已有了本地行政官。罗萨里奥写进拉普拉塔联合省历史的日子是1812年2月27日：负责修筑「独立」「自由」炮台封锁渡口的曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺，在河中埃斯皮尼略岛的独立炮台上升起一面蓝白新旗，清晨令炮兵和步兵向旗帜宣誓。当地相传，旗子由玛丽亚·卡塔利娜·埃切瓦里亚·德·比达尔缝制，由水手科斯梅·马谢尔升上旗杆。布宜诺斯艾利斯的第一届三头执政并未批准这面旗，下令收起，但贝尔格拉诺的部下带着它北上，同年9月即在这面旗下赢得图库曼会战；1816年，图库曼议会把它定为国旗。

en:
The bay of Montevideo is a wide anchorage off the Rio de la Plata, sheltered on its landward side by the low cerro that gave the place its name. Ferdinand Magellan's fleet passed in January 1520, and the seaman Francisco Albo noted the headland as Monte Vidi; a popular account, which most scholars reject, has an unknown sailor cry monte vide eu, 'I saw a mountain', when the hill came into view. In 1444 Guenoa-Minuane hunters and fishers kept seasonal camps around the bay, and no chart yet marked a port there.

Montevideo was built to answer a Portuguese foothold. After Portugal planted Colonia do Sacramento across the river in 1680, a Portuguese redoubt went up on this bay in November 1723; Bruno Mauricio de Zabala crossed from Buenos Aires, drove its builders out in January 1724 and raised Fuerte San Jose with ten guns and about a thousand mission Guarani behind him. Families from the Canary Islands, Guarani and enslaved Bantu Africans settled the surveyed town of San Felipe y Santiago from 1726, behind walls and bastions facing the sea. When the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata was created in 1776, Montevideo became its chief naval port, the base from which Spain watched the river mouth, and its shipyards and garrison drew a constant traffic of troops and stores.

War reached the walls in 1807, when British troops under Samuel Auchmuty stormed the city on 3 February and held it until September, when John Whitelocke's surrender at Buenos Aires forced its evacuation. Francisco Javier de Elio made it the viceroyalty's last capital on 19 January 1811. Jose Artigas's Oriental forces blockaded it by land in 1811 and again from 1812, and an Argentine squadron under the Irish-born William Brown destroyed the Spanish fleet off Buceo in May 1814; the garrison surrendered in June. A Portuguese army invaded in 1816, entered Montevideo in 1817 and annexed the whole Banda Oriental to Brazil in 1821.
zh:
蒙得维的亚湾是拉普拉塔河畔一处开阔锚地，陆地一侧有座低矮山丘为它遮挡风浪，地名也来自这座山。1520年1月，斐迪南·麦哲伦的船队经过此地，水手弗朗西斯科·阿尔沃把海岬记作蒙特维迪；还有个流传很广的说法：一名无名水手望见山丘时喊出「蒙特维德乌」（monte vide eu，意为「我看见了山」），便有了这个地名，但多数学者不接受这个解释。1444年时，格诺阿—米努安人的狩猎和渔猎群体在海湾四周按季节扎营，还没有任何海图在这里标出港口。

蒙得维的亚是为了回应葡萄牙人的据点而建的。1680年葡萄牙在河对岸建起萨克拉门托殖民地后，1723年11月又在这个海湾修起棱堡；布鲁诺·毛里西奥·德·萨瓦拉从布宜诺斯艾利斯渡河，于1724年1月赶走修筑者，建起圣何塞堡，配备十门火炮，手下有大约一千名传教区瓜拉尼人。1726年起，加那利群岛的移民家庭、瓜拉尼人和被奴役的班图非洲人在测绘好的圣费利佩—圣地亚哥城里定居，城外筑起面向大海的城墙和棱堡。1776年拉普拉塔总督辖区成立，蒙得维的亚成为首要军港，是西班牙人监视河口的基地，船坞和驻军使军队与物资不断运到这里。

1807年战火烧到城墙下：塞缪尔·奥克穆蒂率英军于2月3日强攻得手，占领到9月，因约翰·怀特洛克在布宜诺斯艾利斯投降而被迫撤出。1811年1月19日，弗朗西斯科·哈维尔·德·埃利奥把总督辖区最后的首都设在这里。阿蒂加斯的东岸武装1811年、又于1812年起从陆路封锁城市；1814年5月，爱尔兰出生的威廉·布朗率领阿根廷舰队在布塞奥外海歼灭西班牙舰队，守军6月投降。1816年葡萄牙军队入侵，1817年进入蒙得维的亚，1821年把整个东部海岸并入巴西。

en:
Colonia sits on a low cape between the Punta de San Pedro and Punta de Santa Rita, the San Gabriel Islands just offshore and Buenos Aires fifty kilometres away across the Rio de la Plata. In 1444 Charrua hunters worked the open north bank and Chana-Timbu fishermen paddled canoes among the islands and shoals; the anchorage was empty of Europeans and no treaty line yet crossed the river.

Portugal planted the Nova Colonia do Santissimo Sacramento here between 20 and 28 January 1680: Manuel Lobo arrived with five ships, four hundred men and eighteen guns, sent from Rio de Janeiro to pry open Spain's silver trade. Jose de Garro answered from Buenos Aires, and Antonio de Vera y Mujica stormed the post that August; Lobo died a prisoner in Buenos Aires in 1683, the year Portugal reoccupied the site. The town lived by contraband. British and Portuguese merchants ran manufactured goods and slaves across the river and carried away Potosi silver, while cattle hides came in from the eastern grasslands, and after 1718 governors such as Antonio Pedro de Vasconcellos ringed it with sea bastions and laid out the narrow stone streets that bent with the uneven ground. Spain took it in 1705 and Utrecht gave it back; the 1750 Treaty of Madrid, which would have traded it to Spain for the Seven Jesuit Towns, was never carried out.

Pedro de Cevallos took Colonia on 11 October 1762 and handed it back after the 1763 peace, then returned in 1777 as viceroy of the new Rio de la Plata viceroyalty with more than eighty ships and 9,000 men; the Treaty of San Ildefonso kept it for Spain. British troops seized it on 5 March 1807, and Jose Artigas briefly commanded it for Spain that September. It joined the May Revolution in 1810, entered Artigas's Provincia Oriental in 1813, fell to a Portuguese army in 1818 and passed to Brazil with the rest of the Banda Oriental in 1821.
zh:
科洛尼亚位于圣佩德罗角与圣丽塔角之间一座低矮海角，近海有圣加夫列尔群岛，拉普拉塔河对岸五十公里就是布宜诺斯艾利斯。1444年时，查鲁亚猎人在北岸开阔地游猎，查纳—廷布渔民在岛屿和浅滩间划独木舟；锚地里没有欧洲船，河面上也还没有条约划出的界线。

1680年1月20日至28日，葡萄牙人在此建立「至圣圣事新殖民地」：曼努埃尔·洛博带着五艘船、四百名士兵和十八门炮从里约热内卢前来，为的是撬开西班牙的白银贸易。何塞·德·加罗从布宜诺斯艾利斯作出回应，安东尼奥·德·贝拉·穆希卡同年8月攻破据点；洛博被俘押往布宜诺斯艾利斯，1683年死在那里，同年葡萄牙重新占领此地。这座城镇靠走私立足：英国和葡萄牙商人把制成品和奴隶运过河，换走波托西白银，东部草原的牛皮也汇集到这里；1718年后，安东尼奥·佩德罗·德·瓦斯康塞洛斯等总督在海边筑起一圈棱堡，并顺着起伏的地面铺出狭窄弯曲的石板街。西班牙1705年攻占科洛尼亚，《乌得勒支和约》又把它还给葡萄牙；1750年《马德里条约》本要以七个耶稣会传教镇交换它、划归西班牙，最终没有执行。

佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯1762年10月11日攻占科洛尼亚，1763年和约后交还；1777年他已出任新设的拉普拉塔总督，率八十多艘船、九千人再来，《圣伊尔德方索条约》确认科洛尼亚归西班牙。1807年3月5日英军夺取该地，阿蒂加斯同年9月曾代表西班牙短暂接管。科洛尼亚1810年加入五月革命，1813年并入阿蒂加斯的东岸省，1818年被葡萄牙军队攻占，1821年随整个东部海岸并入巴西。

en:
At Salto the Uruguay River runs over a long ledge of rock, breaking into rapids the Guarani called Ytu and the Spanish named Salto Chico and Salto Grande. No boat could climb past them, so all traffic up or down river unloaded at the crossings below. In 1444 the east bank was Bohanes country, a people of the wider Charruan world, with Yaro bands farther south between the Negro and San Salvador rivers.

The Spanish first came to enforce a treaty. The 1750 Treaty of Madrid exchanged the Seven Jesuit Towns for Colonia, and Jose Joaquin de Viana marched four hundred men north during the Guarani War; his sheds at the Salto Chico in October 1756 began the settlement, officially dated 8 November. In 1757 Viana and Pedro de Cevallos built Fuerte San Antonio and left a hundred men at the head of navigation. On 16 June 1768 Francisco de Paula Bucareli reached it with 1,500 men to carry out Charles III's expulsion of the Jesuits: the fort held the arms seized from the missions and then their priests, before the prisoners were sent down to Buenos Aires or on to Spain. A flood later wrecked the works, which were rebuilt across the river at Concordia.

Salto entered the Oriental revolution in December 1811, when Jose Artigas's Exodus of the Eastern People camped on this bank for a month. His census counted some 6,000 fighters, 4,500 civilians and 846 carts, and the Buenos Aires junta named him lieutenant governor in the camp before the column crossed at the Paso de Salto. Portuguese troops reached the Salto Chico in 1817; a handful of women who had followed the army and stayed on when it marched away built the first huts of the permanent town. The annexation of 1821 put the region under Brazil.
zh:
乌拉圭河流到萨尔托，越过一条长长的岩脊，激起瓜拉尼人叫作伊图（Ytu）的急流，西班牙人则称之为小萨尔托和大萨尔托。船只无法继续上行，上下游往来的一切都要在险滩以下的渡口卸货转运。1444年时，东岸是博哈内斯人的土地，他们属于更大的查鲁亚族群，再往南的内格罗河与圣萨尔瓦多河之间住着亚罗人的游群。

西班牙人最初是为执行条约而来。1750年《马德里条约》约定以七个耶稣会传教镇交换科洛尼亚，瓜拉尼战争期间，何塞·华金·德·比亚纳率四百名士兵北上；1756年10月他的部队在小萨尔托搭起棚屋，定居点就此开始，官方把11月8日定为建城日。1757年，比亚纳和佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯修筑圣安东尼奥堡，在这个河运尽头留下一百名士兵。1768年6月16日，弗朗西斯科·德·保拉·布卡雷利率一千五百人抵达，执行卡洛斯三世驱逐耶稣会士的命令：堡垒先存放从传教区收缴的武器，又用来关押传教区的神父，这些囚徒后来被送往布宜诺斯艾利斯，再转往西班牙。一场洪水后来冲毁工事，设施改在对岸的康科迪亚重建。

1811年12月，萨尔托卷入东岸革命：阿蒂加斯率领的「东岸人民出亡」在这处河岸扎营一个月。他造册清点，约有六千名战士、四千五百名平民和846辆车；在队伍从萨尔托渡口过河之前，布宜诺斯艾利斯执政委员会在营中任命阿蒂加斯为副都督。1817年葡萄牙军队进抵小萨尔托；几个随军女人在军队开拔后留了下来，搭起永久城镇最早的棚屋。1821年东部海岸被吞并，这一地区并入巴西。

en:
Yapeyú, 'ripe fruit' in Guarani, was first the name of the Guaviraví, the small river that here cuts through soft green hills on its way to the Uruguay. In 1444 these banks were the southern march of the Guarani world: the farming villages of the Uruguay Guaraní lay between the Paraná and the Uruguay, and across the water ranged the Charrúa and the Yaro, neighbours they raided and feared. Juan Díaz de Solís's ships were the first Europeans in these waters when they entered the Río de la Plata in 1516. On 4 February 1627 three Jesuits, Roque González de Santa Cruz, Pedro Romero and Nicolás Mastrilli Durán, opened the reduction of Nuestra Señora de los Santos Reyes Magos de Yapeyú; González, a priest of Guarani and Spanish blood and the first missionary among the Paraguay Guaraní, was killed in 1628 while founding another mission.

Yapeyú grew rich on cattle. Its Guaraní rounded up feral herds between the two great rivers and ran the Gran Estancia, whose grazing lands a royal cedula of 1657 carried south to the Río Queguay; later estancias specialised in sheep, horses, pack mules and oxen. By the early eighteenth century the pueblo held some 10,000 people, Guaraní with Charrúa, Bohanes and Yaro, and the Jesuit superior over all the Paraguay missions kept his seat here. The expulsion ordered by Charles III reached the town in 1768, the missions were secularised and Yapeyú became the head of a civil department. Its lieutenant governor from 1774, Juan de San Martín, reopened the Salto road that carried the district's mate, cotton, tobacco and hides to Buenos Aires. His son José was born here on 25 February 1778 and left for Spain at seven; he returned to fight the crown in 1812, led the Army of the Andes across the mountains, freed Chile at Chacabuco and Maipú, and entered Lima in 1821 as Protector of Peru. Portuguese raiders stripped the eastern mission lands after 1801, and in 1817 Colonel Chagas's Luso-Brazilian troops sacked Yapeyú and levelled it after the defeats of Artigas and Andrés Guazurarí, leaving the liberator's birthplace in ruins.
zh:
「亚佩尤」在瓜拉尼语里意为「成熟的果实」，原是瓜维拉维河的名字；这条小河在这里穿过连绵和缓的青翠丘陵，汇入乌拉圭河。1444年，这片河岸是瓜拉尼世界的南疆：巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间散布着乌拉圭瓜拉尼人的务农村落，对岸草原上游猎着查鲁亚人和亚罗人，瓜拉尼人对这两个邻族既劫掠又畏惧。1516年，胡安·迪亚斯·德·索利斯的船队驶入拉普拉塔河口，是第一批来到这片水域的欧洲人。1627年2月4日，罗克·冈萨雷斯·德·圣克鲁斯、佩德罗·罗梅罗和尼古拉斯·马斯特里利·杜兰三位耶稣会士在此创立「亚佩尤圣王三贤圣母」传教村；有瓜拉尼与西班牙双重血统、最早向巴拉圭瓜拉尼人传教的冈萨雷斯，1628年在开辟另一处传教区时被杀。

亚佩尤靠牛群兴旺起来。瓜拉尼村民在两条大河之间围捕野牛，经营庞大的大牧场，1657年一道国王敕令把牧地南界定在克瓜伊河畔；后来的各分牧场还分别专养绵羊、马匹、驮骡和役牛。到18世纪初，镇上约有一万居民，除瓜拉尼人外还有查鲁亚人、博安人和亚罗人，统辖巴拉圭各传教区的耶稣会会长也驻节于此。驱逐耶稣会的命令1768年传到这里，传教区被世俗化，亚佩尤成为一个民政区的首镇。1774年出任副区长的胡安·德·圣马丁重整萨尔托商道，把辖区的马黛茶、棉花、烟草和皮革运往布宜诺斯艾利斯。1778年2月25日，他的儿子何塞出生在这里，七岁便随家人前往西班牙；1812年他返回美洲与王室作战，率安第斯军翻越安第斯山，在查卡布科和迈普解放智利，1821年以秘鲁护国公的身份进入利马。1801年后葡萄牙袭掠者夺走了乌拉圭河以东的传教区土地；1817年，阿蒂加斯和安德列斯·瓜苏拉利相继战败，查加斯上校的葡属巴西军队洗劫亚佩尤并将其夷平，这位解放者的出生地只剩断壁残垣。

en:
Chaco Central is the thorn-forest belt bounded on the north by the Pilcomayo-Araguay and on the south by the old Bermejo channel and the Teuco. In 1444 its camps and fishing grounds belonged to the Toba, Pilagá, Mocoví and other Guaycuru-speaking peoples, with Wichí groups toward the upper Bermejo and Pilcomayo. Bands followed game, fish, carob and honey through seasonal rounds, carried bows and built light branch shelters; the rivers linked one people to the next, but no state in the highlands or on the Paraguay commanded the interior.

Expeditions out of Asunción broke into this country in the 1580s, and on 14 April 1585 Alonso de Vera y Aragón founded Concepción de Nuestra Señora, later called Concepción de Buena Esperanza, on the macomita track that ran from Asunción to Talavera de Esteco. It served the trade through the Chaco and the encomiendas that forced Matará and Guacara people into labour; about 500 people lived there, and after 1617 it was one of only four towns in the Governorate of Buenos Aires. The forced labour wore the local nations down until a tribal coalition fell on Matará in 1631 and killed most of the Concepción garrison that marched to its defence. The town was abandoned, the survivors fled to Corrientes, three expeditions sent to resettle the site came to nothing, and its cabildo was dissolved in 1645. This was the first serious defeat the Chaco nations handed Spanish expansion, and the Paraguay-Tucumán trade road died with the town. Jesuit attempts fared no better: Nuestra Señora María de los Reyes, founded among the Guaycurú in 1610, and the Guazutinguá station of 1626 were both given up, and the eighteenth-century stations passed to the Franciscans after the expulsion of 1768. In 1821 the mounted Toba and Mocoví still barred the interior to every Spanish and creole army.
zh:
中查科是一片刺林地带，北以皮科马约河与阿拉瓜伊河为界，南以贝尔梅霍河旧道和特乌科河为界。1444年，这里的营地和渔场属于托巴人、皮拉加人、莫科维人等瓜伊库鲁语族群，维奇诸群活动在贝尔梅霍河与皮科马约河上游。各群体按季节追逐猎物、鱼群、角豆和蜂蜜，带着弓箭，搭起轻便的枝棚；河流把一个个族群连在一起，但无论高原还是巴拉圭河畔的政权都号令不了这片内陆。

1580年代，亚松森派出的远征队闯入此地；1585年4月14日，阿隆索·德·贝拉-阿拉贡在连接亚松森与塔莱韦拉-德埃斯特科的马科米塔小路上建立康塞普西翁-德努埃斯特拉-塞尼奥拉，后来又称布埃纳埃斯佩兰萨的康塞普西翁。它既作穿查科商路上的驿站，也靠委托监护制驱使马塔拉和瓜卡拉的原住民劳作；城中约有五百居民，1617年后是布宜诺斯艾利斯都督辖区仅有的四座城镇之一。强征的劳役把当地各族逼到忍无可忍，1631年，诸族联军进攻马塔拉，歼灭了赶来救援的大部分康塞普西翁守军。城镇随后废弃，幸存者逃往科连特斯，三次重占尝试都无功而返，市议会于1645年解散。这是查科诸族给予西班牙扩张的第一场重大挫败，巴拉圭通往图库曼的商路也随这座城镇断绝。耶稣会的尝试同样不顺利：1610年在瓜伊库鲁人中建立的努埃斯特拉·塞尼奥拉·玛丽亚·德·洛斯雷耶斯传教区和1626年的瓜苏廷瓜据点都先后放弃，18世纪设立的传教站则在1768年耶稣会被逐后转交方济各会。到1821年，已骑马作战的托巴人和莫科维人仍把所有西班牙和克里奥尔军队挡在内陆之外。

en:
Misiones is the red-earth country between the Upper Paraná and the Uruguay, a humid forest cut by a hundred rivers that ends northward at the Iguazú. There the river drops in a long wall of falls on the border with Brazil; a Guarani legend calls the water Iguazú, big water, and tells of the girl Naipí, who fled by canoe with her lover Tarobá to escape a jealous god, only for the god to split the river and hurl the pair over the falls. Around 1444 Guarani war bands were still pressing into these woods from the north, settling among older Kaingang and Xokleng hunters; they cleared maize and manioc fields round long-house villages, gathered the wild yerba mate of the forest and called themselves avá, men. Sebastian Cabot was turned back by the Apipé rapids in 1527, and Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca became the first European to see the great falls when he came overland from the Brazilian coast in 1541.

From 1610 the Jesuits gathered the Guaraní into the reductions, thirty pueblos whose churches of red sandstone were raised by Guarani masons and carpenters in the style called Guarani baroque; the church of San Ignacio Miní, seventy-four metres long, was among them. Slave-raiders from São Paulo, the bandeirantes, sacked the early towns, and at the end of 1631 some 12,000 Guaraní fled downriver on seven hundred rafts under Father Antonio Ruiz de Montoya; scarcely 4,000 lived to refound their towns, and a Guaraní force broke the raids at Mbororé in 1641. By the Treaty of Madrid in 1750 Spain handed the seven eastern towns to Portugal and ordered the Guaraní west across the Uruguay; they refused, and in the Guaraní War their leader Sepé Tiaraju was killed in February 1756, days before 1,511 of his people were cut down at Caibaté. The Jesuit expulsion of 1768 emptied the pueblos, and in January 1817 a Luso-Brazilian army under Francisco das Chagas Santos crossed the Uruguay, sacked the towns and carried off 1,800 Indians, leaving the thirty churches to the forest.
zh:
米西奥内斯是上巴拉那河与乌拉圭河之间的红土之乡，湿润丛林被上百条河流切开，北端止于伊瓜苏河。伊瓜苏河在与巴西交界处跌成一道瀑布长墙；瓜拉尼传说称此水为「伊瓜苏」，意为大水，讲的是少女纳伊皮与恋人塔罗巴乘独木舟逃离妒忌的神灵，神灵一怒劈开大河，把两人抛下瀑布。1444年前后，瓜拉尼人的战团仍在从北方渗入丛林，与更古老的卡因冈人、肖克伦猎人杂处而居；他们在长屋村落四周开辟玉米地和木薯地，采摘林中野生的马黛茶，自称「阿瓦」，意即人。1527年，塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特被阿皮皮急流挡住去路；1541年，阿尔瓦尔·努涅斯·卡韦萨·德·巴卡从巴西海岸陆路西行，成为第一个见到大瀑布的欧洲人。

1610年起，耶稣会士把瓜拉尼人聚入传教村，先后建起三十座村镇，红砂岩教堂由瓜拉尼石匠和木匠砌筑，即后来所称的「瓜拉尼巴洛克」风格，七十四米长的圣伊格纳西奥米尼教堂便是其中之一。圣保罗来的旗手不断掳人为奴、洗劫早期村镇；1631年底，安东尼奥·鲁伊斯·德·蒙托亚神父率约一万二千名瓜拉尼人乘七百只木筏顺河南逃，活下来的不到四千人，得以重建村镇。1641年，一支瓜拉尼武装在姆博罗雷击败旗手，袭掠才告终止。1750年《马德里条约》把河东七镇交给葡萄牙，西班牙勒令瓜拉尼人西迁；他们拒绝从命，瓜拉尼战争爆发，领袖塞佩·蒂阿拉茹1756年2月战死，几天后一千五百一十一名部众在凯巴特被杀。1768年耶稣会被逐，诸村人去屋空；1817年1月，弗朗西斯科·达斯·沙加斯·桑托斯率葡属巴西军队越过乌拉圭河洗劫村镇，掳走一千八百名印第安人，三十座教堂最终没入丛林。

en:
The Highveld around the future Bloemfontein is open grassland some 1,400 metres above the sea, swept by winter frost and sharp summer thunderstorms. Sotho-Tswana farmers and cattle keepers had broken away from their Tswana kin by the fourteenth century and settled among older San hunter-forager bands, mixing with them; their homesteads combined sorghum fields, ironwork, cattle kraals and springs. The spring below the later town was called Mangaung, 'the place of cheetahs', in Sesotho. One account derives the Dutch name Bloemfontein, 'Bloem's fountain', from Jan Bloem II, a Griqua leader. In 1444 no dynasty ruled a single state here, and power rested with local chiefs and elder lineages whose authority followed cattle, rainfall and the best grazing.

By at least the seventeenth century a string of small Basotho chiefdoms covered much of the southern plateau, including the country that became the Free State. Their kraals made loose confederations rather than one kingdom, trading cattle and iron and shifting when drought or raiding wore a valley out. During the eighteenth century mounted Korana and mixed Cape frontier bands moved up the Orange and Vaal corridors and joined the older Sotho-Tswana and Barolong networks around Mangaung. In 1821 those kraals still held the plateau, though the wars of Shaka's Zulu kingdom had begun to the east and the first displaced bands were moving towards the highveld.
zh:
后来布隆方丹所在的海维尔德是海拔约1400米的开阔草原，冬有严霜，夏季多猛烈雷阵雨。索托—茨瓦纳的农民和牧人到14世纪已与茨瓦纳亲部分开，在更古老的桑人游猎群体之间定居、融合；家园周围有高粱地、铁匠炉、牛栏和泉水。后来城址下方的泉水，塞索托语叫曼噶汪，意为「猎豹之地」；荷兰语名布隆方丹一说意为「布洛姆之泉」，得名于格里夸首领扬·布洛姆二世（Jan Bloem II）。1444年时没有哪个王朝在这里统治统一国家，权力属于各地酋长和世系长老，威望随牛群、雨量和最好的牧场升降。

至迟从17世纪起，一连串南索托小酋长辖地覆盖了南部高原的大部分，包括后来成为自由邦的土地。这些畜栏村寨结成松散联盟而非一个王国，用牛只和铁器与邻部交易，山谷遭旱灾或劫掠耗竭时便迁走。18世纪，骑马的科拉纳人和来自开普边疆的混血群体沿奥兰治河、法尔河走廊上溯，加入曼噶汪一带原有的索托—茨瓦纳和巴罗龙关系网。1821年，治理这片高原的仍是这些畜栏村寨；不过东边恰卡的祖鲁战争已经开打，第一批流离失所的队伍正朝高草原移动。

en:
Rio Grande faces the narrow channel that carries water from the Lagoa dos Patos and Lagoa Mirim toward the Atlantic. Dunes front the sea; behind them open pampa runs south toward the River Plate. In 1444 Guarani families fished, planted maize and manioc and kept villages on the lagoon shores, while Charrua and Minuano bands crossed the grasslands. No fort covered the passage, and no European cattle grazed there.

Portugal's push into the River Plate dispute turned the channel into a garrison. On 19 February 1737 Brigadier José da Silva Paes landed and began the Jesus-Maria-José fort; the colonial settlement was formally laid out that May. Azorean and Madeiran families enlarged the post, which received its town charter as Rio Grande de São Pedro and became the seat of a separate captaincy in 1760. A Spanish army under Pedro de Cevallos seized it in April 1763; refugees who fled toward Viamão helped build up Porto Alegre. Rafael Pinto Bandeira retook the town in 1776, and the Treaty of San Ildefonso left the coast in Portuguese hands. Near Pelotas, charqueadas began drying beef for northeastern buyers in 1780. By 1821 hides and salted meat from the southern herds moved through the old fortress port.
zh:
南里奥格兰德面对一道狭窄水道，帕图斯湖和米林湖的水经这里排入大西洋。海边是沙丘，后方开阔的潘帕草原一直伸向拉普拉塔方向。1444年，瓜拉尼人在湖岸建立村落，捕鱼并种植玉米、木薯；查鲁亚人和米努亚诺人群则穿行草原。水道上没有要塞，也还没有欧洲牛群吃草。

葡西争夺拉普拉塔河时，葡萄牙把这道水道变成驻军地。1737年2月19日，准将若泽·达席尔瓦·派斯登陆，开始修建耶稣-马利亚-若瑟要塞；同年5月，正式殖民点划定。亚速尔和马德拉移民扩充了据点，它后来取得里奥格兰德-德圣佩德罗的镇建制，并在1760年成为独立都督辖区治所。1763年4月，佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯率西班牙军队攻占此地，逃往维亚芒的难民也推动了阿雷格里港的发展。拉斐尔·平托·班德拉于1776年收复城镇，《圣伊尔德方索条约》随后确认海岸归葡萄牙所有。佩洛塔斯附近的腌肉场从1780年起为巴西东北部买家风干牛肉。到1821年，南方牧群出产的皮革和咸肉都经这座老要塞港外运。

en:
South of Asunción the Paraguay spreads into a watery wedge of esteros, lagoons and backwaters before meeting the Paraná: the Ñeembucú, 'the long spill of water' in Guarani. East of the marshes the land rises gently between the Tebicuary and the Paraná into grass and palm savannah. In 1444 Guarani farmers and fishermen held the banks and islands, their villages looking west across the river to the unmastered Chaco. Sebastian Cabot's ships were the first Europeans in these waters when they passed the confluence in 1528, and Asunción was founded upriver nine years later.

After the conquest the country was divided between two estates. From 1676 the Asunción elite were granted cattle runs south to the Tebicuary, while the Jesuits held everything between that river and the Paraná, their herds grazing to the northern edge of Ñeembucú. At Santiago Apóstol, a reduction first founded on the Apa river as San Ignacio de Caaguazú and refounded on its present hilltop in 1669, the Spanish officer and naturalist Félix de Azara counted only 1,215 people in 1784 where there had once been 3,151. The Jesuit expulsion of 1768 broke that world, and raids out of the Chaco were answered with a line of riverside forts and a new garrison port: Pedro Melo de Portugal founded Villa del Ñeembucú on the Paraguay in 1779 to watch traffic on the river, and it was soon renamed Pilar. When Paraguay broke with Spain in 1811 a detachment was waiting at Pilar and stopped the Spanish governor, Bernardo de Velasco, from escaping downstream by ship. Under Dr Francia from 1814 the southern forts, Humaitá among them, were strengthened, and Pilar became the only port in the republic allowed to trade with foreigners, its wharves shipping yerba mate; Santiago and the other old mission pueblos lived on as small country towns around the cattle ports.
zh:
亚松森以南，巴拉圭河在汇入巴拉那河之前漫成一片水乡楔子：浅滩、潟湖与回水道纵横交错，瓜拉尼语称其为涅恩布库，意为「长长的溢水道」。沼泽以东，特维夸里河与巴拉那河之间地势缓升，是草原与棕榈稀树草原。1444年，河畔和岛上住着务农捕鱼的瓜拉尼人，村落西望巴拉圭河对岸尚未被征服的查科。1528年，塞瓦斯蒂安·卡博特的船队经过两河汇合处，是第一批驶入这片水域的欧洲人，九年后亚松森在更上游的河畔建城。

征服之后，这片土地分属两种营生：1676年起，亚松森权贵获授南至特维夸里河的牧地，该河与巴拉那河之间则尽归耶稣会，牛群一直牧放到涅恩布库北缘。圣地亚哥使徒传教村最初建于阿帕河畔，名为圣伊格纳西奥·德卡瓜苏，1669年在今日所在的丘陵上重建；西班牙军官、博物学家费利克斯·德·阿萨拉1784年清点村中人口，只剩一千二百一十五人，而从前曾有三千一百五十一人。1768年驱逐耶稣会，旧秩序瓦解；为应对查科方向的袭扰，西班牙人沿河修起一串要塞，并新设驻兵河港：佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙1779年在巴拉圭河畔建立「涅恩布库镇」，监视河面往来，该镇不久改名皮拉尔。1811年巴拉圭脱离西班牙时，一支部队正守在皮拉尔，截住了打算顺流乘船出逃的西班牙都督贝尔纳多·德·贝拉斯科。弗朗西亚博士1814年执政后加固乌迈塔等南部要塞，并把皮拉尔定为全国唯一准允对外贸易的港口，码头外运的货物以马黛茶为主；圣地亚哥等传教故镇则作为乡间小镇，依傍牧牛港口延续下来。

en:
Itapúa is the steep red-earth right bank of the Upper Paraná, where the river bends south in a broad sweep opposite the forests of Argentine Misiones; inland the ground climbs through yerba mate woods to the San Rafael hills. At the crossing-place a pointed rock stood out in the water, and the Guarani called the spot Itá Púa, the pointed stone. In 1444 Guarani farmers kept villages on the arroyos cutting these slopes, hunted the dense selva and gathered wild mate, and the only craft on the Paraná were their canoes. The first Jesuit cross went up on 25 March 1615, when Roque González de Santa Cruz founded Nuestra Señora de la Encarnación de Itapúa on the eastern bank; plague, bandeirante raids and local resistance drove the whole pueblo across the river in three days to its permanent ground on the right bank. González himself, the first missionary among the Paraguay Guaraní, was killed in 1628 while opening another mission.

More pueblos followed along the shore. San Cosme y Damián, founded in 1632 and moved four times before settling at its last site in 1718, became the workshop of the Jesuit Buenaventura Suárez: with Guarani craftsmen he built telescopes, quadrants and sundials and wrote the Lunario de un Siglo, which predicted eclipses years ahead and was read with admiration in the universities of Europe. His confrere Taddaeus Enis led the mission Guaraní against Portuguese troops in the Guaraní War of 1754 to 1756. At Trinidad and Jesús the great stone churches were still rising when the expulsion order reached the towns in 1768; secular clergy took over and the pueblos slowly emptied. In 1810 and 1811 Belgrano's patriot army crossed here into Paraguay on its way to defeat at Paraguarí and Tacuarí, and Paraguay broke with Spain in 1811. By 1821 the old pueblo of Itapúa was a quiet riverside backwater of the young republic, its mate woods and ruined churches overgrown by the selva.
zh:
伊塔普阿是上巴拉那河陡峭的红土右岸，大河在这里拐出一道宽阔的南弯，对岸是阿根廷米西奥内斯的丛林；内陆地势沿溪谷抬升，穿过马黛茶林通向圣拉斐尔丘陵。渡口江中有一块尖石兀立，瓜拉尼人便把这里称作「伊塔普阿」，意为尖石。1444年，瓜拉尼农户在切过坡地的溪涧旁结村，入密林狩猎，采摘野马黛茶，巴拉那河上往来的只有他们的独木舟。1615年3月25日，罗克·冈萨雷斯·德·圣克鲁斯在河东创立「伊塔普阿道成肉身圣母」传教村，在这里竖起第一座耶稣会十字架；瘟疫、旗手袭扰和当地人的反抗，逼得全村用三天时间渡过大河，迁到右岸的永久址上。作为最早向巴拉圭瓜拉尼人传教的耶稣会士，冈萨雷斯本人1628年在开辟另一处传教区时被杀。

沿岸随后建起更多村镇。圣科斯姆和圣达米安1632年初建，历经四次迁徙，1718年才定于现址；耶稣会士布埃纳文图拉·苏亚雷斯把这里当成了作坊，在瓜拉尼工匠帮助下制造望远镜、象限仪和日晷，所著《世纪历算》能提前多年推算日食月食，欧洲大学读到后大为钦佩。1754至1756年瓜拉尼战争中，他的同会修士塔德乌斯·埃尼斯率领传教区的瓜拉尼人抗击葡萄牙军队。1768年驱逐令到达时，特立尼达和赫苏斯宏伟的石砌大教堂还在施工；诸村转交世俗神职人员，人口渐渐流散。1810至1811年，贝尔格拉诺的爱国军经这里攻入巴拉圭，随后在帕拉瓜里和塔夸里战败，巴拉圭于1811年脱离西班牙。到1821年，伊塔普阿故镇已是这个年轻共和国一处安静的河滨边地，马黛林和残破教堂正被丛林慢慢吞没。

en:
The tall-grass plains south and west of the Rio de la Plata, running to the Salado River, were the country of the Querandi, the easternmost of the Didiuhet bands of the Het peoples. Their Guarani neighbours named them for the animal fat in their diet, 'they who carry fat'. In 1444 they moved in leather-tented bands, wintering by the waterholes and riding the plains on summer raids. Their runners could overtake pampas deer, rheas and guanacos on foot. They threw the bolas and a more primitive weapon of a stone on a leather thong, made pottery, and ground dried fish into meal with stone mortars. To the Spaniards soon arriving, nomads such as these were simply 'Pampas'.

Sebastian Cabot met them peacefully in 1527. Nine years later Pedro de Mendoza planted Buenos Aires on the edge of their land. After a few weeks of trade the Querandi cut off the food supply, and in June 1536 Mendoza sent his brother Diego against them: bolas dragged the Spanish cavalry from their horses and the column was cut to pieces, the German soldier Ulrich Schmidl leaving the only eyewitness account. Allied bands then kept the starving town under siege until the Spaniards burned it and withdrew. The Querandi rounded up the horses left behind and became mounted hunters. Juan de Garay refounded Buenos Aires in 1580; three years later he was killed in a Querandi ambush on the Carcarana. After Rodrigo Ortiz de Zarate's reprisals of 1586 the name drops out of the records, and by the 1670s only ten Querandi appeared in the encomienda rolls. The survivors merged into the wider Pampas world, and in 1821 the plains south of the Salado were still an unconquered Indian frontier.
zh:
拉普拉塔河西南、高草一直铺到萨拉多河的平原，是克兰迪人的地盘。他们是海特人中迪迪乌维特一支最靠东的部落，瓜拉尼邻人因他们以动物油脂为食，称他们克兰迪，意为「带脂人」。1444年，他们以兽皮帐篷为单位迁徙，冬天聚在水源旁，夏天结队深入内陆袭掠。他们的猎手能徒步追垮潘帕斯鹿、美洲鸵和原驼。流星索之外，他们还使用皮绳拴石的原始猎具，会制陶，并用石臼把鱼干磨成粉。在不久后到来的西班牙人嘴里，这样的游牧者统统只有一个称呼：潘帕斯人。

1527年，塞巴斯蒂安·卡博特与他们和平相遇。九年后，佩德罗·德·门多萨在他们的土地边缘建起布宜诺斯艾利斯。交易了几周后，克兰迪人断了粮食供应，1536年6月，门多萨派弟弟迭戈前去征讨：流星索把西班牙骑兵纷纷拽下马，队伍几乎被全歼，队中的德国士兵乌尔里希·施米德尔留下了唯一一份亲历记述。随后诸部结盟围困这座饥饿的城，直到西班牙人自己放火烧城撤走。克兰迪人收拢遗下的马匹，成了骑马的猎人。胡安·德·加赖1580年重建布宜诺斯艾利斯，三年后就在卡尔卡拉尼亚河畔死于克兰迪人的伏击。1586年罗德里戈·奥尔蒂斯·德·萨拉特的征剿之后，克兰迪之名便从记载中消失，到17世纪70年代，委托监护征册上只剩十名克兰迪人。幸存者融入更广义的潘帕斯世界，1821年，萨拉多河以南仍是一片未曾被征服的印第安边疆。

en:
West of the Salado the wet grassland dries into open steppe broken by calden woods and the rocks of Lihue Calel. In 1444 the only tracks ran between waterholes, used by the western Het bands, the Diuuhet and the Taluhet, whom the Spaniards later lumped together as 'Pampas'. They camped in leather toldos along the Chadileuvu, hunted guanaco and rhea with the bolas, and answered to no outside chief. The nearest settled towns lay far away, at Cordoba and Cuyo.

After the Spanish founded Mendoza, Cordoba and San Luis between 1561 and 1594, displaced bands pushed south into these plains, and smallpox thinned them in the next century. Horses and feral cattle turned the survivors into formidable raiders: Spanish parties crossed the grass only in armed columns to fetch salt from the Salinas Grandes, while Indian malones swept down on frontier estancias. Around the middle of the eighteenth century Pehuenche families from the Andean Ranquil country settled among the local Tehuelches in the reed beds of the dry pampa; rankul means reed, and the mixed people became the Ranqueles. Their cacique Llanquitur was raiding Salado estancias by 1765. No Spanish army subdued them. The viceroy Pedro Melo de Portugal made peace with them in 1796, and when the British invaded the Rio de la Plata in 1806 and 1807 their principal cacique Carripilun offered the viceroy three thousand lancers for the defence of Buenos Aires; the offer was not taken. In 1821 the whole steppe was still Indian country.
zh:
萨拉多河以西，湿润的草原渐成开阔的干旱草原，间杂卡尔登树林和利韦尔卡莱尔岩山。1444年，这里唯一的路是连接各处水源的兽径，往来其上的是海特人中偏西的迪乌维特、塔卢维特等游群，西班牙人后来把他们统称潘帕斯人。他们在查迪莱乌武河畔张起兽皮帐篷，用流星索猎取原驼和美洲鸵，不受任何外来首领统属；最近的定居城镇远在科尔多瓦和库约。

1561年至1594年间，西班牙人先后建起门多萨、科尔多瓦和圣路易斯，被挤压的各部不断南迁，下一个世纪的天花又使人口锐减。马匹和野化牛群把幸存者变成可怕的骑手：西班牙人只有武装结队才敢穿过草原，前往萨利纳斯格兰德斯盐沼取盐，而印第安马队则频频扫过边境牧场。18世纪中叶，来自安第斯山兰基尔一带的佩文切家族迁入干草原的芦苇地，与当地特维尔切人合流；兰库尔意为芦苇，融合而成的部族便叫兰克尔人，即「芦苇人」。酋长兰基图尔到1765年已在袭掠萨拉多河畔的牧场。没有哪支西班牙军队征服过这片土地：总督佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙1796年与兰克尔人议和；1806年至1807年英国入侵拉普拉塔时，大酋长卡里皮伦还向总督提出三千长矛兵协防布宜诺斯艾利斯，未被接受。到1821年，整片草原仍是印第安人的天下。

en:
Coquimbo's sheltered bay opens below the Elqui valley, one of the transverse valleys cutting through the coastal desert hills of Chile's semi-arid Norte Chico. In 1444 the anchorage was an Indigenous fishing landing beneath bare hills, and the valley belonged to the farming chiefdoms later called Diaguitas: they watered maize and bean fields from mountain streams, fired pottery in red, black and white, and carried fish and shells from the coast up to the sierra to trade. Each valley followed its own chief and no single state joined them. Before the century ended Inca armies had pushed south over the desert, appointing their own kurakas and planting mitma colonies, and Cuzco designs entered the local pottery.

Pedro de Valdivia wanted a waystation where ships carrying men and provisions from Lima could call on the voyage to Santiago, and in 1544 his captain Juan Bohón founded Villanueva de la Serena on the site. The first town lasted less than five years: on the night of 11 January 1549 an Indigenous rising killed nearly every Spaniard and burned the place. Francisco de Aguirre rebuilt it that August as San Bartolomé de La Serena, on what became the Plaza de Armas, and the Crown granted it city status in 1552; Bohón and Valdivia had both marked Coquimbo Bay as the settlement's natural harbor. The open anchorage then drew English privateers: militiamen drove off Francis Drake at Guayacán in 1579; Bartholomew Sharp caught the town without guns or walls and sacked it in 1680; Edward Davis's men broke in in 1686, were trapped in the Santo Domingo convent and were chased back to their ships at dawn. The raids finally forced fortification in 1730, the year an earthquake leveled much of the town.
zh:
科金博的避风海湾开在埃尔基河谷下方，这道河谷横切智利半干旱小北地区滨海的荒漠丘陵。1444年，这片锚地还是秃山下的原住民渔港，谷地属于后来被称作迪亚吉塔人的农耕酋邦：他们引山溪浇灌玉米地和豆田，烧制红、黑、白三色彩陶，把海鱼和贝壳运往山地交换；各河谷自有酋长，没有统一的政权。到15世纪末，印加军队已越过沙漠南下，自行任命库拉卡、安置米特马克移民，库斯科风格的图案随之出现在当地陶器上。

佩德罗·德·巴尔迪维亚需要一个中途站，让从利马运送士兵和补给的船只在驶往圣地亚哥途中停靠休整，1544年，他的部将胡安·博翁在此建立塞雷纳新镇。新城只存在了不到五年：1549年1月11日夜，原住民起事，杀死几乎所有西班牙人并将镇子烧毁。同年8月，弗朗西斯科·德·阿吉雷将其重建为圣巴托洛梅·德·拉塞雷纳，城址就在后来的武器广场，1552年王室授予城市称号；博翁和巴尔迪维亚都早已看中科金博湾，把它当作这座定居点的天然港口。敞开的锚地随后招来英国私掠船：1579年，民兵在瓜亚坎击退弗朗西斯·德雷克；1680年，巴塞洛缪·夏普趁城防没有火炮、没有城墙，洗劫了拉塞雷纳；1686年，爱德华·戴维斯的人闯入城中，被困在圣多明各修道院，黎明时被逐回船上。连绵的袭击终于迫使城市在1730年修筑工事，同年又有一场地震把大半个镇子震毁。

en: The Río Negro runs east from the Limay–Neuquén junction across the northern Patagonian steppe to the Atlantic, its willow-lined islands and floodable bottomlands a strip of green in dry country. In 1444 the middle valley was the ground of the Gününa këna bands, whom Mapuche speakers called Puelche, 'people of the east.' They camped in branch-and-hide shelters, hunted guanaco and rhea, gathered wild fruit and moved in small family groups led by elders. Spanish power reached only the river mouth, where Carmen de Patagones was founded in 1779 and the royal pilot Basilio Villarino later set out in a small boat to reconnoitre the river upstream, the first European to penetrate this stretch of the valley. Epidemics late in the eighteenth century thinned the Puelche bands and drew the survivors into Mapuche speech and customs. No colonial town stood on the middle Río Negro through 1821.
zh: 内格罗河从利迈河与内乌肯河交汇处向东，穿过北巴塔哥尼亚草原注入大西洋；河中多柳林岛屿，两岸有受洪水浸润的低地，是干旱地带里一条绿色地带。1444年，中游谷地是古努纳凯纳诸群体的活动范围，说马普切语的邻居称他们为普埃尔切人，意为「东方之人」。他们以树枝兽皮搭棚，猎原驼和美洲鸵、采野果，以家庭为小群迁徙，由族中长者带领。西班牙人的势力只到河口：1779年卡门·德·帕塔戈内斯在那里建立，王家领航员巴西利奥·比亚里诺后来驾小船从那里出发，溯河侦察，是最早深入这段谷地的欧洲人。18世纪末的疫病使普埃尔切诸群体人口大减，幸存者逐渐改用马普切人的语言、随其习俗。直到1821年，内格罗河中游仍没有殖民城镇。

en:
Senqu is the river later renamed the Orange. Khoe speakers knew it as the black river and the great river, names settlers rendered as Gariep and translated as the Groote Rivier; Senqu is the name used where it rises in the Lesotho highlands, from where it runs some 2,400 kilometres to the Atlantic. The province covers the arid southern bank of its middle course, where the open plains and isolated koppies of Bushmanland slope toward the water. The soil is thin and the groundwater often saline, so San hunter-foragers and Khoekhoe herders moved between the river, seasonal pans, springs and the migrations of game. In 1444 no one could settle far from reliable water, and influence here meant knowing where the scattered water points lay.

During the eighteenth century Cape trekboers pushed into these dry parts, grazing cattle and sheep on enormous loan farms rather than laying out towns. Families moved between summer and winter pasture in wagons, tents or reed-and-clay hartbees houses, and San raids on their stock made the northern frontier dangerous. In 1779 Colonel Robert Jacob Gordon, commander of the Dutch East India Company garrison at the Cape and an explorer and naturalist, reached the river and named it the Orange for William V, Prince of Orange, and the Groote Rivier fell off colonial maps. By 1821 this stretch had no magistrate or fixed town; river camps, cattle posts and widely separated loan holdings were the only marks of settlement along the Senqu.
zh:
森库是一条河的名字，这条河后来被改名奥兰治河。科伊人称之为黑河、大河，移民把这些名字转写为加里普，又译作「大河」（Groote Rivier）；河流在莱索托高地的发源处则叫森库，从那里西行约2400公里注入大西洋。本省位于河流中段干旱的南岸，布什曼兰的开阔平原和孤立岩丘向水边倾斜。这里土层薄、地下水常带盐味，桑人猎民和科伊科伊牧人便在河流、季节性盐盘、泉水和猎物迁徙路线之间往返。1444年时，远离可靠水源便无法定居，在这里的势力取决于谁知道散落水点的位置。

18世纪，开普的游牧布尔人进入这片干旱地带，在面积广大的借地牧场上放牧牛羊，而没有建立城镇。各家在夏冬牧场之间迁徙，住在大车、帐篷或芦苇黏土搭的哈特比斯小屋里；桑人盗畜使北部边疆处处危险。1779年，荷兰东印度公司开普驻军司令罗伯特·雅各布·戈登上校抵达此河，他兼为探险家和博物学家，以奥兰治亲王威廉五世之名把河命名为奥兰治河，殖民地图上的「大河」一名随之退场。到1821年，这一河段仍没有法官驻地或固定城镇，河边营地、牲畜哨站和彼此远离的借地牧场，是森库沿岸仅有的定居痕迹。

en:
Between the southern slopes of the Tandil ranges and the Rio Negro lie the driest of the pampas, a country of river valleys and brackish lakes. Its people in 1444 called themselves Gununa Kune; Puelche, 'people of the east', was the Mapudungun name their Araucanian neighbours used, and Falkner later grouped them with the northern Tehuelches of his Het. Small bands followed guanaco and rhea, dressed in guanaco-hide cloaks and leather moccasins, painted their faces for war, and camped in skin toldos along the waters draining to the Rio Negro. They had never seen a European.

Two of their headmen went to Buenos Aires in 1739 to treat with Governor Salcedo, and treaties made at the Sierra de la Ventana three years later opened the country to Jesuits and to the poncho fairs at El Cayru and Chapaleofu. Contact brought epidemics that broke the bands at the end of the century, and the survivors were drawn into the Araucanian speech and customs spreading from the Andes, so that by 1800 'Puelche' meant a mixed, Mapuche-speaking equestrian people. In 1779 the Spanish built Fuerte del Carmen on the lower Rio Negro. The naval pilot Basilio Villarino, who had helped found it, took four sloops up the Negro, Limay and Collon Cura in 1782 with a native chieftain aboard as his guide; he was killed three years later on an expedition to the Sierra de la Ventana. In 1821 the Puelches still held the plains between the new fort line and the river.
zh:
坦迪尔群山南坡与内格罗河之间是潘帕斯最干旱的一段，河谷与咸水湖交错。1444年住在这里的人自称古努纳克讷；「普埃尔切」是阿劳卡诺邻人用马普切语给他们起的名字，意为「东方之人」，福克纳后来把他们归入自己所说海特人中的北特维尔切群。小股游群追逐原驼和美洲鸵，身披原驼皮披风，脚穿皮便鞋，战时在脸上涂彩，在通向内格罗河的水道沿岸张起兽皮帐篷。他们还从未见过欧洲人。

1739年，两名酋长前往布宜诺斯艾利斯与萨尔塞多总督议和，三年后在本塔纳山订立的和约向耶稣会士开放了这片土地，也开放了埃尔凯鲁和查帕莱奥富的篷乔集市。接触带来了瘟疫，在18世纪末打散了诸部；幸存者被卷入从安第斯山蔓延开来的阿劳卡诺人语言和习俗，到1800年前后，「普埃尔切」已指称一个讲马普切语的混血骑马民族。1779年，西班牙人在内格罗河下游建起卡尔门堡；曾参与建堡的海军领航员巴西利奥·比利亚里诺1782年率四艘小艇，在一位当地酋长引航下溯内格罗河、利迈河和科永库拉河而上，三年后他在远征本塔纳山时被杀。到1821年，普埃尔切人仍据守着新建堡垒线与大河之间的草原。

en:
West of Tandil the Tandilia hills flatten into the open pampas, cut by the Tapalqué and Chapaleofú streams. In 1444 nomadic Serrano bands, among the peoples later grouped together as the Het, hunted guanaco, rhea and deer with boleadoras in these glens and built dry-stone corrals for the livestock they traded. The westernmost end of the range held El Cayrú, one of the two great plains fairs the Jesuit chroniclers called the 'poncho fairs'; the other met at Chapaleofú. Plains Indians, northern Patagonians and peoples from both sides of the Andes gathered at El Cayrú to exchange ponchos, hides, cattle and farm produce, and upland bands used the same hills as a refuge when the open country was unsafe.

Araucanian traders came over the Andes first, and their language and customs followed, the change later called Araucanization; Mapuche speakers called these eastern neighbours puelches, 'people of the east'. The Catriel, a chiefly line of puelche origin, held the country between the headwaters of the Tapalqué and the western Tandilia ranges, and in 1741 a Spanish expedition reached the district and made peace with the 'sierra Indians' of that dynasty. No Spanish estancia then crossed the Salado far to the north, and the plains south of the river were known in Buenos Aires simply as the 'desert'. Patrols sent by Viceroy Vértiz reconnoitred as far as Tandil in the 1770s and noted the old dry-stone corrals, but no fort went up on the western ranges. In 1821 the Tapalqué country still belonged to its native riders.
zh:
坦迪尔以西，坦迪利亚山渐次没入坦荡的潘帕斯草原，塔帕尔凯河与查帕莱奥富河穿行其间。1444年，游牧的塞拉诺诸部（后来被归入海特人的一支）在这些山谷里用投石索猎取原驼、美洲鸵和鹿，并砌起干石畜栏关养用于交易的牲畜。山系最西端有埃尔凯鲁，是草原两大集市之一，耶稣会史家把这类集市称作「篷乔集市」，另一处在查帕莱奥富。草原印第安人、北巴塔哥尼亚人和安第斯山两侧的部族来埃尔凯鲁交换篷乔、兽皮、牛只和农产品；草原不太平的时候，山地部族也把这片山岭当作避身处。

安第斯山方向先来了阿劳卡诺商人，久而久之，阿劳卡诺的语言和习俗也传了过来，这一过程后来被称为阿劳卡诺化；操马普切语的人把这些东边的邻族叫作普埃尔切人，意为「东方之人」。卡特里尔是源出普埃尔切人的酋长世系，据有塔帕尔凯河源与坦迪利亚西山之间的土地。1741年，一支西班牙远征队抵达这一带，与该世系的「山印第安」议和。当时没有一家西班牙牧场越过北方远处的萨拉多河，河以南的草原在布宜诺斯艾利斯人口中只叫「荒漠」。1770年代，贝尔蒂斯总督派出的侦察队远至坦迪尔，记下了古老的干石畜栏，但西部山地上始终没有筑起堡垒。1821年，塔帕尔凯一带仍属于本地骑手。

en:
Chañar is the dry belt between the Cuyo uplands and the southern pampa, around western watercourses that feed the Desaguadero-Chadileuvú and Colorado rivers. In 1444 it was Diuihet country, one of the nomadic Het divisions later placed by Thomas Falkner between about 35° and 38° south, east of the Pehuenche. Bands followed guanaco, deer and rhea, gathered wild seeds and sweet chañar pods, and used boleadoras in open steppe and thorn scrub. Camps shifted with water and game, and no Spanish road, fort or mission controlled the country.

Spanish towns grew up in Cuyo without subduing this steppe, so its waterholes and tracks remained useful to raiders. Pehuenche and Huilliche fighters crossed it on their way to San Luis in 1712, and Cangapol's allied plains nations passed through during their 1740 raid toward Buenos Aires. From the late seventeenth century, eastward Pehuenche and Mapuche movement drew local Het bands into Araucanized trading and raiding networks; Falkner recorded the Diuihet division in 1774. The Ranquel, whose name meant 'reed people', later kept their independence between the Chadileuvú and Salinas Grandes. The Camino de los Chilenos began as a salt route from the Salinas Grandes toward Buenos Aires, then reached the Neuquén passes and Chile carrying cattle taken in malones. In 1821 no settled frontier government yet controlled Chañar.
zh:
查尼亚尔是库约山地与南方潘帕斯之间的干旱地带，西部溪流汇入德萨瓜德罗—查迪莱乌武河和科罗拉多河。1444年，迪维特人在此游牧；他们是海特人的一支，活动在佩温切人以东、南纬35度至38度之间。人们追猎原驼、鹿和美洲鸵，采集野籽与甜美的查尼亚尔豆，在开阔草原和荆棘灌丛中使用投石流星。营地随水源和猎物搬迁，西班牙人的道路、堡垒和传教站都还没有进入这里。

西班牙人在库约建起城镇，却没有征服这片草原，水洼和小路仍为突袭队伍所用。1712年，佩温切人和维利切人经此前往圣路易斯；1740年，坎加波尔联合草原诸部向布宜诺斯艾利斯进军时也穿过这一带。17世纪末以后，佩温切人和马普切人东移，把迪维特群体带入阿劳卡尼化的贸易与劫掠网络；福克纳在1774年记下这个分支。兰克尔人后来在查迪莱乌武河与大盐沼之间保持独立，族名意为「芦苇丛中的人」。「智利人之路」最初是大盐沼通向布宜诺斯艾利斯的盐路，后来延伸到内乌肯山口和智利，运送从潘帕斯掠走的牛。1821年，仍没有定居的边疆政府控制查尼亚尔。

en:
San Antonio covers the deep bite of Bahía San Antonio on the northwestern side of the San Matías Gulf. In 1444 mobile Het and northern Tehuelche bands followed the arid shore between the Río Negro and the gulf, hunting guanaco and rhea, gathering seeds and using boleadoras in open country. The inlet gave canoes and later ships sheltered water and a clear landmark, but it had no permanent Spanish post.

Ferdinand Magellan entered the larger gulf on St Matthias's day, 24 February 1520, and left the Spanish name used on later charts. For more than two and a half centuries ships mostly treated the bay as a coastal reference. Basilio Villarino, a pilot in the Spanish Royal Navy, surveyed this part of the Patagonian coast from the brig Nuestra Señora del Carmen between 25 October 1780 and 1 January 1781, mapping Bahía San Antonio and its anchorage for the new post at Carmen de Patagones. He had taken part in the Patagonian expeditions of 1779 and went on to chart the Río Negro and Limay before he was killed in the Ventania hills in 1785. No permanent Spanish settlement had been built on the bay by 1821.
zh:
圣安东尼奥覆盖圣马蒂亚斯湾西北侧凹入陆地的圣安东尼奥运湾。1444年，海特人与北特维尔切人的游群沿着内格罗河至海湾之间的干旱海岸移动，在旷野猎取原驼和美洲鸵、采集种子、使用投石索。海湾可为独木舟和后来的船只提供避风水域与明显方位，但这里没有西班牙常设据点。

1520年2月24日圣马蒂亚斯日，斐迪南·麦哲伦驶入外侧大海湾，后来的海图便使用这个西班牙语名称。此后两个半世纪，船只大多只把这处海湾当作辨认海岸的标志。西班牙王家海军领航员巴西利奥·比亚里诺乘「卡门圣母」号双桅船，在1780年10月25日至1781年1月1日间测绘这段巴塔哥尼亚海岸，为卡门-德帕塔戈内斯的新据点绘出圣安东尼奥运湾和锚地。他曾参加1779年的巴塔哥尼亚远征，随后又测绘内格罗河与利迈河，1785年在本塔纳山地被杀。到1821年，海湾边仍未建起西班牙人的常设居民点。

en:
San Julián Bay is a natural harbour on the arid Atlantic coast of Patagonia, the stretch of shore where Florida Blanca was later built. In 1444 the bay and the steppe behind it were Aónikenk Tehuelche country. Bands wintered near sheltered inlets, fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting seals, then followed guanaco and rhea inland in summer. They kept no permanent town for a seafaring power to seize; the bay offered visitors fresh water, anchorage and cliffs that broke the Patagonian wind.

Ferdinand Magellan brought his fleet into the anchorage on 31 March 1520 and stayed five months, the first European expedition to winter on the Patagonian coast. Antonio Pigafetta described the Aónikenk as giants, and Magellan, a reader of the chivalric romance Primaleon, named them after Patagon, the book's savage giant, which is how Patagonia got its name. At midnight on Easter Sunday his captains mutinied; Magellan crushed the rising, executed one of his captains and left another mutineer marooned on the shore. Francis Drake reached the same bay on 15 June 1578 and found the rotting remains of that gallows. There he tried his friend Thomas Doughty for inciting mutiny and had him beheaded, then used a sermon to assert sole command before sailing to the Strait of Magellan in August. Spain made its only attempt to settle the bay on 19 April 1780, when Antonio de Viedma founded Nueva Colonia y Fuerte de Floridablanca for Charles III, naming it for Jose Monino, Count of Floridablanca, the crown's chief minister. Under an Enlightenment plan the roughly 150 settlers were to live as farming families on assigned plots. Scurvy and the climate defeated them, and in 1784 the colony was evacuated and its buildings deliberately destroyed so no rival power could use the harbour.
zh:
圣胡利安湾是巴塔哥尼亚干旱大西洋海岸上的一处天然良港，佛罗里达布兰卡后来就建在这片岸边。1444年，海湾和背后的草原是阿奥尼肯克·特维尔切人的土地。各群体冬季在避风小湾附近捕鱼、拾贝、猎海豹，夏季进入内陆追逐原驼和美洲鸵。他们没有常设城镇，海上来的势力无城可取；海湾能给人的只有淡水、锚地和几面挡住巴塔哥尼亚强风的崖岸。

1520年3月31日，麦哲伦率舰队驶入锚地，停留五个月，这是第一支在巴塔哥尼亚海岸过冬的欧洲探险队。随队的皮加费塔把阿奥尼肯克人描写成巨人；麦哲伦爱读骑士小说《普里马莱翁》，便以书中蛮族巨人「巴塔贡」称呼他们，巴塔哥尼亚由此得名。复活节当夜，几名船长在午夜发动哗变，麦哲伦将其镇压，处死一名船长，把另一名哗变者遗弃岸上。1578年6月15日，弗朗西斯·德雷克来到同一个海湾，找到了那座绞架腐朽的残骸。他在这里以煽动哗变的罪名审判旧友托马斯·道蒂并将其斩首，又借一场布道确立独断的指挥权，8月才驶往麦哲伦海峡。西班牙人唯一一次在湾边殖民是1780年4月19日：安东尼奥·德·别德马奉卡洛斯三世之命建立「佛罗里达布兰卡新殖民地与要塞」，并以国王首席大臣佛罗里达布兰卡伯爵何塞·莫尼尼奥的姓氏命名。按启蒙时代的规划，约150名居民要作为务农家庭在份地上自给自足。坏血病和气候击垮了他们；1784年殖民地撤离，房屋被有意拆毁，免得敌对国家利用这座港湾。

en:
Tehuelmapu is the dry central Patagonian steppe between the Río Negro and the Chubut, a plain of stony mesetas, wet hollows and short rivers such as the Senguerr draining toward the Atlantic. In 1444 Tehuelche bands, the people Spaniards later called Patagones, crossed it on foot, following guanaco and rhea between winter lowlands and summer uplands. Their skin-tent camps and networks of kinship and exchange tied the interior to the Atlantic shore and the Andean valleys, but no chiefdom, and no outside power, commanded the grasslands.

The horse remade life on the steppe. Horses reached Tehuelche bands around 1570 and turned seasonal walking hunts into long-range mounted hunts and far-ranging raids. In the eighteenth century trade with the Pampas and Araucanía carried Mapuche speech and customs inland with the riders, the change later called Araucanization. Spain's only fortified foothold on this flank was San Jose de la Candelaria, built on Peninsula Valdes in 1779 and reduced to a fort in 1784; Tehuelche warriors burned it down on 7 August 1810. Around 1820 Patagones and Pehuenches fought on the Senguerr, and with the fort in ruins the interior remained entirely Tehuelche country.
zh:
特华马普是内格罗河与丘布特河之间干旱的巴塔哥尼亚中部草原，遍布石质台地、湿草甸和森格尔河这类短促的入海河流。1444年，被西班牙人称作巴塔戈内斯人的特维尔切诸群体徒步穿行其间，在冬季低地和夏季高原之间追逐原驼与美洲鸵。他们的兽皮帐篷营地，加上亲属和交换关系，把内陆同大西洋海岸、安第斯谷地连在一起；但无论本地首领还是外来势力，都没有统治这片草原。

马改变了草原上的生活。马匹约在1570年传到特维尔切诸群体手中，季节性的步行狩猎变成骑马长途出猎和远距离袭掠。18世纪，他们同潘帕斯、阿劳卡尼亚的贸易让马普切语言和习俗随骑手进入内陆，这一变化后来被称为阿劳卡诺化。西班牙在这一侧唯一的筑垒据点是圣何塞·德·拉坎德拉里亚：1779年建于瓦尔德斯半岛，1784年降为要塞，1810年8月7日被特维尔切战士焚毁。约1820年，巴塔戈内斯人与佩文切人在森格尔河畔交战；要塞已成废墟，内陆依旧完全是特维尔切人的天地。

en:
Poya is a country of cold lakes, volcanic cordillera and forested passes behind mainland Chiloé. The Poya, also called Ténesch, were a northern Tehuelche people living on both Andean slopes and around the eastern and southern shores of Nahuel Huapi. In 1444 family bands lived in skin tents under chosen chiefs, hunted guanaco and choique, and gathered roots, wild fruit and llao-llao fungus. Horses had not yet reached them, and the trails from the Chilean fjords toward the eastern steppe remained under the camps' own control.

Captain Juan Fernández found Puelche and Poya camps near Nahuel Huapi in 1620, but the Jesuits from Chiloé made the lake district their main field. Nicolás Mascardi brought freed Poya prisoners home and opened the Nahuel Huapi mission in February 1670. He planted the first apple trees there and in 1672 followed the Limay and Negro rivers to the Atlantic. Poya hostile to the mission killed him in 1674, and the station was abandoned. Later attempts ended the same way: Felipe Laguna reopened it in 1703 and was poisoned in 1707; after Juan José Guillelmo opened the Vuriloche route in 1715, Puelches burned the station for fear it would mark a slaving road, Guillelmo was killed in 1716, and Francisco Elguea and the rebuilt houses were destroyed in 1717. Franciscan expeditions from Chiloé visited the lakes between 1792 and 1795 without leaving a permanent mission. By the later colonial period horses had changed Poya hunting, while Mapuche-speaking neighbours called the mountain people Vuriloche.
zh:
波亚在奇洛埃大陆后方，由寒冷湖泊、火山山脉和林中山口组成。波亚人也称特内施人，属北巴塔哥尼亚人，活动在安第斯山两坡以及纳韦尔瓦皮湖东岸、南岸一带。1444年，家族队伍住兽皮帐篷，由酋长带领迁徙和狩猎，追逐原驼与小美洲鸵，采集块根、野果和利亚奥—利亚奥菌。马匹尚未传入，从智利峡湾通往东部草原的山路仍由这些营地自己掌握。

1620年，胡安·费尔南德斯在纳韦尔瓦皮附近见到普埃尔切和波亚营地；后来把湖区拉入西班牙边疆事务的，主要是奇洛埃的耶稣会士。1670年2月，尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪把获救的波亚囚徒送回故乡，并设立纳韦尔瓦皮传教站。他在当地种下最早的苹果树，1672年又沿利迈河和内格罗河抵达大西洋。反对传教的波亚人在1674年杀死他，传教站随即废弃。后来的尝试同样短命：费利佩·拉古纳1703年重开站点，1707年被毒杀；胡安·何塞·吉列尔莫1715年探通武里洛切山口后，普埃尔切人因害怕这里变成贩奴道路而焚毁站点，吉列尔莫1716年被杀，弗朗西斯科·埃尔格亚和重建房舍也在1717年被毁。1792年至1795年，方济各会从奇洛埃多次进入湖区，仍未能留下常驻传教站。到殖民时代后期，马匹改变了波亚人的狩猎方式，说马普敦贡语的邻人则称他们为武里洛切人。

en:
Chiquiyami covers the arid Andean edge south of Cuyo, where the Atuel, Diamante and Barrancas rivers descend from the Malargüe highlands toward the eastern plains. In 1444 its mobile bands belonged to the southern Huarpe kinship world and were later included among the people whom Mapudungun speakers called Puelche. They lived by hunting and gathering and traded with Huarpe villages farther north, where maize, quinoa and beans were grown. Their camps lay between the Pehuenche mountains and the Het steppe, with no Spanish town yet in the valleys.

Spanish control came late and stayed mostly to the north. Francisco de Villagra explored the district in December 1552 with seventy horsemen; after Pedro del Castillo founded Mendoza in 1561, Spanish estates and labour systems settled on the Cuyo oases rather than these southern ranges. The mountain trails kept their military value. The Pehuenche rising of 1769 carried malones to Mendoza, and Pehuenche who had withdrawn to Malargüe attacked the newly built Fort San Carlos in December 1770. The Parliament of Negrete calmed the Chilean frontier without ending indigenous control of the eastern valleys. In 1816 San Martín met Pehuenche chiefs at San Carlos to obtain passage and supplies for the Army of the Andes. After the Battle of the Biobío on 19 January 1819, the Pincheira royalists withdrew east of the cordillera and, with Pehuenche and Huilliche allies, used Atuel, Varvarco and Epulafquen as refuges and cattle routes. In 1821 independent Mendoza held the oases, while Chiquiyami remained beyond the settled frontier.
zh:
齐奎亚米位于库约以南的干旱安第斯边缘，阿图埃尔河、迪亚曼特河和巴兰卡斯河从马拉圭高地流向东部平原。1444年，这里的游动群体属于南瓦尔佩亲属圈，后来被说马普敦贡语者泛称为普埃尔切人。他们以狩猎采集为生，同北面种植玉米、藜麦和豆类的瓦尔佩村落交换物产。营地夹在佩温切山地与海特草原之间，河谷中还没有西班牙城镇。

西班牙人进入得很晚，控制区也主要留在北方。1552年12月，弗朗西斯科·德·比利亚格拉率七十名骑兵勘探这一带；佩德罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略1561年建立门多萨后，地产和劳役集中在北面的库约绿洲。南部山路仍有军事价值。1769年佩温切人起事，突袭蔓延到门多萨；次年，退到马拉圭的佩温切人攻打新建的圣卡洛斯堡。内格雷特议会平息了智利一侧的战事，却没有让原住民交出东坡山谷。1816年，圣马丁在圣卡洛斯与佩温切首领会谈，为安第斯军争取借道和补给。1819年1月19日比奥比奥战役后，平切拉保王派退到山脉东坡，联合佩温切人和维利切人，把阿图埃尔、瓦尔瓦尔科和埃普拉夫肯湖当作庇护所和贩牛路线。1821年，独立派的门多萨控制着绿洲，齐奎亚米仍是定居边界之外的山地。

en:
Chiloé is the large island at the centre of a rainy Pacific archipelago, separated from mainland Chile by the narrow Chacao Channel. The Piuchén and Pirulil highlands divide wet western forests and swamps from the quieter coves of the east and north, where Spanish towns were later built. In 1444 Chono canoe parties fished, hunted and gathered shellfish, while Huilliche and Cunco families grew potatoes, maize and beans and kept llamas. Their dalca boats linked coves and smaller islands. The island's later Huilliche name means the place of the chelles, a white gull with a black head.

Alonso de Camargo sighted the coast in 1540, and Francisco de Ulloa explored the Chacao Channel in 1553; Castro, founded in 1567, became the main Spanish town. The Dutch corsair Baltazar de Cordes and local Huilliches briefly captured Castro in 1600, before Spanish forces pushed him northward. Jesuit missionaries worked the archipelago as a boat circuit, travelling between hamlets and building native-timber chapels made for the rain. Seventy-nine chapels stood there when the Jesuits were expelled in 1767, and Franciscans took over the mission in 1771. Those chapels did not end forced labour under the encomienda. A Huilliche rising against Spanish encomenderos began in February 1712 and was crushed within a week, leaving several hundred Huilliches and several dozen Spaniards dead. Because Chiloé was governed directly by the Viceroyalty of Peru, it stayed outside the new Chilean state in the first wars of independence. A patriot attack failed in 1820, and in 1821 Castro remained under the Spanish Crown.
zh:
奇洛埃是多雨太平洋群岛中心的大岛，以狭窄的查考海峡与智利大陆相隔。皮乌琴和皮鲁利尔山地把湿润的西部森林沼泽，同东面、北面较平静的海湾分开；后来的西班牙城镇就建在这些湾畔。1444年，乔诺人的独木舟队伍捕鱼、狩猎、采集贝类，韦利切和昆科家族则种植马铃薯、玉米和菜豆，饲养美洲驼。他们的「达尔卡」舟往来各个海湾和小岛。岛名后来取自韦利切语，意为切莱斯鸥栖居之地；切莱斯鸥是一种黑头白身的鸥。

阿隆索·德·卡马戈1540年望见海岸，弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚1553年探查查考海峡；1567年建立的卡斯特罗成为西班牙人的主要城镇。1600年，荷兰私掠船长巴尔塔萨尔·德·科德斯和当地韦利切人短暂攻占卡斯特罗，随后被西班牙军队逼向北撤。耶稣会士把整片群岛作为乘船巡回的传教区，往来渔村之间，用当地木材修建适应多雨气候的小堂。1767年耶稣会被驱逐时，这里已有79座小堂；方济各会士1771年接办传教事务。这些小堂并没有终止委托监护制下的劳役。1712年2月，韦利切人起兵反抗西班牙委托监护主，起义一周内即遭镇压，数百名韦利切人和数十名西班牙人死亡。奇洛埃原由秘鲁总督辖区直接管辖，独立战争初期没有落入新智利政权控制。1820年独立派进攻失败，1821年卡斯特罗仍在西班牙王室治下。

en:
The Guaitecas and Chonos archipelagoes form the rainy seaward edge of Chilean Patagonia, a maze of wooded islands, glaciers and channels running south to the Taitao Peninsula and the Ofqui Isthmus, with the icefields of the Andes behind. In 1444 the channels between roughly 44 and 48 degrees south belonged to Chono canoe bands. They had no shore villages. Families moved by canoe, the men fishing and harpooning sea lions, the women diving in the cold water for shellfish and gathering seaweed. They kept dogs, wove cloaks from dog hair and planted small potato patches on sheltered ground. South of Taitao paddled the Kawesqar, whom outsiders later called the Alacaluf, while Aonikenk or Tehuelche hunters followed guanaco on the eastern steppe. No outside chiefdom claimed these crossings.

Magellan sailed past on his way through the strait in 1520, but the first Spaniard to meet the Chonos was Francisco de Ulloa, whose ships reached the archipelago in 1553. Expeditions from Chiloe then gave way to slave raids: a royal decree of 1608 permitted the enslavement of 'rebellious' Indians, and although the Chonos had never taken up arms, canoe people were carried north in bonds. Jesuits from Castro sailed these channels in turn; they gathered a band of Chonos on Guar Island for a mission that most soon abandoned for the sea. The wreck that fixed Spanish attention on the coast was HMS Wager, driven onto the Guayaneco Islands in 1741. Her captain, David Cheap, had been left on Wager Island by the mutineers, until a Chono party led by Martin Olleta found him, guided the survivors north to Chiloe in exchange for the longboat and muskets, and kept the salvaged metal for themselves. The crown answered the British wreck by emptying parts of the archipelago so corsairs could find no help there; a fort built on Taitao in 1749 was abandoned within a few years. In 1821 no Spanish town stood between Chiloe and Taitao, only seasonal sea-lion hunters and cypress cutters sailing south from Chiloe.
zh:
瓜伊特卡斯群岛与乔诺斯群岛是智利巴塔哥尼亚多雨的海上前缘，林木岛屿、冰川与水道交错如网，向南直抵泰陶半岛和奥夫基地峡，背后是安第斯山冰原。1444年，南纬约44度至48度的水道掌握在乔诺人的独木舟游群手里。他们没有岸上村落：一家人乘独木舟往来，男子捕鱼、用鱼叉猎海狮，妇女潜入冷水采捞贝类、收集海藻。他们养狗，用狗毛织披风，在避风处种小块马铃薯。泰陶半岛以南海面是卡韦斯卡尔人的天地，他们后来被外人称作阿拉卡卢夫；阿奥尼肯克人即特维尔切猎人则在东部草原上追逐原驼。没有任何外来酋邦占有这些水道。

1520年，麦哲伦在穿过海峡途中经过这片海岸，但第一个遇见乔诺人的西班牙人是弗朗西斯科·德·乌略亚，他的船队1553年驶入这片群岛。此后从奇洛埃来的探险渐渐变成掳掠：1608年的一道王令允许把「叛乱」的印第安人掳为奴隶，尽管乔诺人从未动过武，独木舟居民仍被成批绑往北方。卡斯特罗的耶稣会士随后也往来于这些水道，曾把一批乔诺人安置到瓜尔岛传教，但多数人很快又弃岸出海。真正让西班牙盯住这段海岸的是英国军舰「韦杰号」：1741年它在瓜亚内科群岛触礁，舰长戴维·奇普被哗变水手遗弃在韦格岛，直到马丁·奥列塔率领的一队乔诺人发现了他，以换取长艇和火枪为条件带领幸存者北上奇洛埃，从船上打捞的金属则被他们留下。王室对这起英国沉船的回应，是清空部分群岛，让私掠船得不到当地人的帮助；1749年又在泰陶半岛筑堡，几年后即遭废弃。到1821年，奇洛埃与泰陶之间仍没有一座西班牙城镇，只有季节性捕猎海狮和采伐柏木的人从奇洛埃驾船南来。

en:
The Chubut rises in the eastern foothills of the Andes and winds east across the dry Patagonian tablelands to the Atlantic; its Tehuelche name, chupat, means 'transparent.' In 1444 the shallow river, its floodable bottomlands and the nearby Río Chico were seasonal country for nomadic Tehuelche bands. They hunted guanaco and rhea from skin-tent camps and used the valleys as a corridor between winter lowlands, summer uplands and the Atlantic coast.

The first Spanish attempt to plant a town in Patagonia ended here. Simón de Alcazaba, a Portuguese navigator whom Charles V had named adelantado and governor of Nueva León, founded Puerto de los Leones near Camarones on 24 February 1535, the earliest European settlement in Patagonia. From there he marched inland up the Río Chico with Tehuelche guides, who led his men for ten days toward a rumoured city of gold; they found only empty steppe. Discontent turned to mutiny and Alcazaba was killed that May. The mutineers sailed away on 17 June, abandoning a group of exiled men who held out at the site until the end of the year. Missionaries later crossed parts of Chubut, and horses and trade with the Mapuche reshaped Tehuelche life in the eighteenth century, but no permanent Spanish town rose on the river through 1821.
zh:
丘布特河发源于安第斯山东麓，蜿蜒向东穿过干旱的巴塔哥尼亚台地入海；在特维尔切语里，河名「丘帕特」意为透明。1444年，水浅的河道、会被洪水漫过的低地和邻近的奇科河，是特维尔切游牧群体的季节性活动地。他们在兽皮帐篷营地周围猎原驼和美洲鸵，把这些河谷当作冬季低地、夏季高地与大西洋海岸之间的通道。

西班牙人在巴塔哥尼亚建立城镇的第一次尝试就终结于此。葡萄牙航海家西蒙·德·阿尔卡萨瓦是查理五世任命的新莱昂先行官兼总督，1535年2月24日，他在卡马罗内斯附近建立莱昂港，这是欧洲人在巴塔哥尼亚最早的定居点。他率人沿奇科河深入内陆，特维尔切向导带着队伍走了十天，去寻找一座传说中的金城，眼前却只有空旷草原。不满酿成哗变，阿尔卡萨瓦在当年5月被杀。哗变者6月17日乘船离去，留下一批被放逐的人在据点苦撑到年底。后来虽有传教士经过丘布特部分地区，18世纪马匹和与马普切人的贸易也改变了特维尔切人的生活，但直到1821年，河畔始终没有建起永久的西班牙城镇。

en:
Behind the harbours of Deseado and San Julián, stony canyons and semi-arid mesas climb from the Atlantic steppe toward the Chilean cordillera. The Teushen knew the waterholes and hunting tracks through this country. In 1444 it belonged to the Teushen or Tehues, foot nomads between the Puelche to the north and the Aónikenk Tehuelche to the south. Small camps followed guanaco and rhea, gathered seasonal plants and carried their few possessions from one camping place to the next. Their language was closest to Tehuelche, the speech of their southern neighbours.

European ships learned the outer coast long before anyone held the interior. Magellan wintered at San Julián in 1520, and Thomas Cavendish named Port Desire in 1586 before meeting arrow fire on the shore. Spanish clergy and travellers crossed later: Flores de León passed through in 1621, and Nicolás Mascardi travelled the same sparse country in 1671 and 1672, but neither left a lasting mission. The Spanish Crown tried a firmer footing at Floridablanca, near San Julián, in 1780. The Aónikenk leader Julián Grande showed the newcomers a freshwater valley, and settlers traded goods for guanaco meat; the post cost too much and was dismantled in 1784. In 1821 the inland tracks remained Teushen land.
zh:
德塞阿多港与圣胡利安港后方，石质峡谷和半干旱台地从大西洋草原向智利方向的安第斯山抬升。特乌申人熟悉这里的水源和猎道。1444年，这片土地属于特乌申人，又称特乌斯人；他们是徒步游猎者，北邻普埃尔切人，南接阿奥尼肯克特维尔切人。小群营地追逐原驼和美洲鸵，采集季节性植物，带着少量财物逐处迁移。他们的语言与南方邻人的特维尔切语最接近。

欧洲船只先熟悉外缘海岸，很久以后仍未控制内陆。1520年麦哲伦在圣胡利安过冬；1586年托马斯·卡文迪什把港口命名为德塞阿多，随后在岸边遭到弓箭射击。后来的西班牙神职人员和旅人也曾进入内地：弗洛雷斯·德·莱昂1621年穿过这里，尼古拉斯·马斯卡尔迪1671至1672年走过同一片荒凉土地，两人都没有留下持久传教点。1780年，西班牙王室在圣胡利安附近的佛罗里达布兰卡尝试建立较稳固的据点。阿奥尼肯克首领大胡利安为新来者指出一处淡水谷地，殖民者用货物交换原驼肉；但据点耗费过高，1784年被拆除。1821年，内陆猎道仍是特乌申人的土地。

en:
Mendoza spreads over the arid eastern foot of the Andes, where snowmelt rivers turn a strip of desert between the mountains and the Pampas into irrigated oases. In 1444 Huarpe farmers of the Agrelo tradition watered maize, beans, squash and quinoa from their own acequias in the Huentota valley, while Puelche hunter-gatherers moved between the Barrancas and Diamante rivers. Inca armies reached these oases only late in the fifteenth century, and they became the south-eastern edge of Tawantinsuyu.

Francisco de Villagra's column out of Chile wintered among the Huarpes at Huentota in 1551. On 2 March 1561 Pedro del Castillo founded Mendoza del Nuevo Valle de La Rioja, sent by the governor of Chile, García Hurtado de Mendoza, whose name the town took; the first muster counted 47 Spanish households, 30 encomenderos and about 2,500 indigenous tributaries. The town was sited for the mule road between the Río de la Plata and Santiago, the last wintering ground before the Andean passes. Juan Jufré moved it a few hundred metres to its present plaza in 1562 and briefly tried to rename it the City of the Resurrection, but Mendoza stuck. Vines went in from the 1560s, and Jesuit estancias together with the irrigation works of 1788 made wine and aguardiente the cargoes that mule carts hauled east to Buenos Aires. In the 1770s the forts of San Carlos and San Juan Nepomuceno went up against Mapuche raids, and in 1776 Cuyo was transferred from Chile to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata.

Independence turned Mendoza into a military capital. The intendancy of Cuyo was restored in 1813 with the town as its seat, and José de San Martín took over as governor in 1814. At El Plumerillo he built powder works, a foundry and cloth shops that equipped the Army of the Andes, about 4,000 men with 10,000 mules, which crossed the cordillera into Chile in January 1817. With the dissolution of the Cuyo government in March 1820, Mendoza became an autonomous province, and Tomás Godoy Cruz took office as its first governor that July.
zh:
门多萨位于安第斯山东麓的干旱地带，融水河流在荒山与潘帕斯之间冲出一片片灌溉绿洲。1444年，具有阿格雷洛文化传统的瓦尔佩农人在温托塔谷地自开灌渠，种植玉米、菜豆、南瓜和藜麦，普埃尔切狩猎采集者在巴兰卡斯河与迪亚曼特河之间游徙。印加军队要到15世纪末才进入这些绿洲，这里成了印加帝国的东南边地。

1551年，弗朗西斯科·德·比亚格拉从智利带出的队伍在温托塔的瓦尔佩人中间过冬。1561年3月2日，佩德罗·德尔·卡斯蒂略建立「新拉里奥哈谷地之门多萨」，他是智利都督加西亚·乌尔塔多·德·门多萨派来的，城名也取自这位都督；最初的清点为47户西班牙人、30名委托监护主和约2500名纳贡原住民。这座城为骡路而设，是拉普拉塔与圣地亚哥之间商路上翻过安第斯山前最后的越冬地。1562年，胡安·胡弗雷把城向西南移了几百米，还一度想改名为「复活城」，但门多萨的名字保留了下来。定居者从1560年代起栽种葡萄，靠着耶稣会的庄园和1788年的河渠工程，葡萄酒和阿瓜尔丁特酒成了骡车东运布宜诺斯艾利斯的大宗货物。1770年代，为抵御马普切人袭扰，城郊建起圣卡洛斯堡和圣胡安·内波穆塞诺堡；1776年，库约从智利划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。

独立战争把门多萨变成了军事首府。1813年库约监督区恢复，以门多萨为首府，何塞·德·圣马丁1814年接任省长。他在埃尔普卢梅里略设火药厂、铸炮厂和被服工场，为安第斯军团装备约4000名士兵和10000匹骡子，大军于1817年1月翻山进入智利。1820年3月库约政府解散，门多萨成为自治省份，托马斯·戈多伊·克鲁斯于同年7月就任首任省长。

en:
Matará takes its name from the Mataraes, a people counted among the Tonocoté, who held the dry plains south of the Bermejo River between the 61st and 63rd meridians west; their villages bordered the country of Vilela bands moving between the Bermejo and the Salado. In 1444 no outside lord ruled them. Families lived on game from the thorn forest, fish from the floodlands and seasonal lagoons, carob and small planted fields, and tracks ran south-west to the Tonocoté lands around Santiago del Estero.

The Spanish frontier reached the plains in the 1580s. Settlers from Talavera de Esteco held Matará and the neighbouring village of Guacara as encomiendas from 1584, and after Alonso de Vera y Aragón founded Concepción seven leagues, about fifty kilometres, to the east in 1585, he seized both villages for his city; the quarrel over their forced labour was carried all the way to the king of Spain. Matará's Indians were the economic base of Concepción, the only Spanish city in the Gran Chaco, built on an indigenous track that joined Asunción to the towns of north-western Argentina. A census in 1622 counted 638 Matará and Nogosna people in the encomienda.
