Resentment of the forced labour grew while Concepción's garrison shrank. In 1631 a coalition of Chaco tribes stormed Matará, and most of the city's soldiers died defending it; the survivors withdrew to Corrientes, every attempt to resettle failed, and the cabildo was dissolved in 1645. The ruins of Matará were later identified at Pampa de Tolosa. The Spanish crown planted no other town in the Chaco, and in 1821 the bush around the old encomienda was still held by its indigenous peoples.
zh:
马塔拉得名于马塔拉人。他们被算作托诺科特人的一支，占据贝尔梅霍河以南、西经61度至63度之间的干燥平原，村落毗邻在贝尔梅霍河与萨拉多河之间游动的维莱拉群体。1444年，还没有外来领主统治他们。居民靠刺林中的猎物、河泛地和季节湖的鱼产、角豆和小块农田过活，小路向西南通往圣地亚哥-德尔埃斯特罗一带的托诺科特人土地。

1580年代，西班牙人的边疆推进到这片平原。塔莱韦拉-德埃斯特科的殖民者从1584年起把马塔拉和邻近的瓜卡拉村当作委托监护地；1585年阿隆索·德·贝拉-阿拉贡在以东七里格、约五十公里处建立康塞普西翁后，硬把两座村落夺归新城，围绕劳役的争端一直上诉到西班牙国王那里。马塔拉的印第安人是康塞普西翁的经济根基。这座大查科唯一的西班牙城建在一条土著古道上，古道连接着亚松森和阿根廷西北部的城镇。1622年的人口清点记载，监护区里有六百三十八名马塔拉人和诺戈斯人。

对劳役的怨恨日积，康塞普西翁的驻军却日渐单薄。1631年，查科诸族联军强攻马塔拉，城里的大部分士兵战死在村防中；幸存者退往科连特斯，重建尝试全部失败，市议会于1645年解散。马塔拉的遗址后来在潘帕德托洛萨被辨认出来。西班牙王室再没有在大查科建立城镇，1821年时，旧监护地周围的丛林仍掌握在当地诸族手中。

en:
Santa Tecla covers rolling pampa around the Rio Negro and Piraízinho, ground later included in the district of Bagé. Waterholes and low ridges mark routes between the Uruguay valley, the Guarani missions and the overland approach to Montevideo. In 1444 Charrua and Guenoa bands hunted and camped across these grasslands; Guarani travellers from the Uruguay also crossed them. No European earthwork had yet interrupted the plain.

The Jesuit reduction of Santo André dos Guenoas was founded among the Guenoa in 1683. Feral cattle then drew Spanish and Portuguese raiders, and the Buenos Aires governor Juan José de Vértiz ordered Bernardo Lecocq to build a pentagonal Fort Santa Tecla in January 1774. Its walls were meant to block Portuguese moves toward the missions and the Banda Oriental. Rafael Pinto Bandeira's guerrillas and Rio Pardo dragoons besieged it in 1776, took it and pulled it down. The Treaty of San Ildefonso returned the post to Spain, but Spanish forces abandoned and destroyed the works in 1801 during the War of the Oranges, leaving the district with Portugal.

Bagé grew from the military life of that border. A Portuguese camp on the Cerros de Bagé in July 1811 became the nucleus of the town, and a chapel dedicated to Saint Sebastian was raised there in 1820. Horsemen, cattle raiders and ranchers used the same grassland that had made Santa Tecla worth fortifying. In 1821 the district was Portuguese frontier cattle country around the site of the demolished fort.
zh:
圣特克拉涵盖内格罗河与皮拉伊齐纽河周围起伏的潘帕草原，这片土地后来归入巴热地区。水源和低山脊标出几条道路，连接乌拉圭河谷、瓜拉尼传教区以及通往蒙得维的亚的陆路。1444年，查鲁亚人和格诺阿人群在草原上狩猎、扎营；乌拉圭河谷来的瓜拉尼旅人也会经过此地。平原上还没有欧洲人的土木工事。

1683年，耶稣会在格诺阿人中建立圣安德烈-杜斯格诺阿斯归化村。野牧牛群随后引来西班牙和葡萄牙掠牛者；1774年1月，布宜诺斯艾利斯总督胡安·何塞·德·贝尔蒂斯命令工程师贝尔纳多·勒科克修建五边形的圣特克拉要塞。城墙用于阻挡葡萄牙人进入传教区和东岸。1776年，拉斐尔·平托·班德拉的游击队与里奥帕尔多龙骑兵围攻要塞，攻克后将其拆除。《圣伊尔德方索条约》把边堡归还西班牙，但1801年橘子战争期间，西班牙军队放弃并摧毁工事，地区留给葡萄牙。

巴热正是在这条边境的军务中发展起来。1811年7月，葡萄牙人在巴热丘陵设立军营，成为城镇的雏形；1820年，军营旁建起献给圣塞巴斯蒂昂的小教堂。骑手、掠牛者和牧场主经营的仍是当初促使西班牙筑堡的草原。1821年，这里已是葡萄牙边境牧地，要塞只剩下遗址。

en:
The dry grassland between the Vaal and Orange rivers, around the ridge where Kimberley later stands, was Khoe-San country long before it was called Griqualand. Hunter-foragers and herders moved between its pans, springs and game routes, and at Wildebeest Kuil, a rock outcrop about sixteen kilometres from the future town, they pecked engravings of eland, elephant, rhinoceros and hippopotamus into the stone. Setswana-speaking cattle farmers later spread into the wider region from the north, organising their villages under chiefs, but the Kimberley ridge itself has no recorded permanent town. In 1444 the people who would give the country its name were still far to the south: the Griqua community had not yet formed.

During the eighteenth century mounted bands of mixed Khoe, slave and European descent, called Basters by the colonists, moved beyond the Cape frontier with their guns and cattle and settled along the Orange. In 1801 William Anderson and Cornelius Kramer of the London Missionary Society opened a station at Leeuwenkuil, then moved it up the valley to the Klaarwater spring, the first town founded north of the Orange River. In 1813 the missionary John Campbell persuaded the settlers to drop 'Baster' for 'Griqua', and Klaarwater became Griquatown. Its kaptein, Andries Waterboer, ruled the surrounding country as Waterboer's Land from a six-room house that his followers called the palace, while Adam Kok II quarrelled with him and led his own faction away to the south-east. In 1821 Mary Moffat, daughter of Robert and Mary Moffat and later the wife of David Livingstone, was born at the station.
zh:
法尔河与奥兰治河之间、金伯利后来所在的山脊周围，是一片干旱草原；在得名格里夸兰之前很久，这里是科伊桑人的土地。猎民和牧人循着盐盘、泉水和猎物通道往来；在距未来金伯利约十六公里的怀尔德比斯特奎尔（Wildebeest Kuil）岩丘上，他们把大羚羊、象、犀牛和河马的形象凿刻在岩石上。说茨瓦纳语的牧牛农民后来从北方扩散到更广阔的区域，在酋长之下组织村落，但金伯利山脊本身没有留下固定城镇的记载。1444年时，后来给这片土地命名的人还远在南方，格里夸共同体尚未形成。

18世纪，科伊人、奴隶和欧洲人混血的骑马群体被殖民者称作巴斯特人，带着火枪和牛群越过开普边疆，沿奥兰治河落脚。1801年，伦敦传道会的威廉·安德森和科内利斯·克拉默在莱乌恩奎尔（Leeuwenkuil）开设传教站，随后沿山谷迁到克拉尔瓦特（Klaarwater）泉边，这是奥兰治河以北建立的第一座城镇。1813年，传教士约翰·坎贝尔说服居民弃用「巴斯特」一名、改称「格里夸」，克拉尔瓦特随之改名格里夸镇。首领安德里斯·沃特布尔在一座六个房间的房子里统治周围的沃特布尔之地，追随者把那房子称作宫殿；亚当·科克二世与他反目，率自己的部众迁往东南。1821年，罗伯特·莫法特夫妇的女儿玛丽在传教站出生，她后来嫁给了戴维·利文斯通。

en:
Corumbá sits on the right bank of the Paraguay River, where the seasonally flooded plains of the Pantanal stretch west toward the Bolivian hills. Its lagoons belonged to the Guató, who lived in family bands aboard dugout canoes, fishing and taking birds with the bow, while the Paiaguá, whom the Portuguese called the canoe people, ranged the upper river in war canoes. In 1444 no European had entered this maze of water and marsh, and the only roads were the waterways between the river and the camps of the Mato Grosso plateau.

Spaniards founded Santiago de Xerez here in 1593, but the town and its Jesuit neighbours were destroyed by bandeirantes raiding upriver from São Paulo, and no European settlement remained in the floodplain. Portugal and Spain haggled over the Paraguay line for a century after. To pin the frontier and curb the Paiaguá, the governor of Mato Grosso, Luís de Albuquerque, sent Captain Mathias Ribeiro da Costa from Cuiabá in 1775 with 245 men in fifteen canoes. Ribeiro raised an earth-and-stake fort at the São Francisco Xavier narrows, the one reach where the river could be commanded, and its guns had been shipped all the way from Belém do Pará. In 1778 Sergeant-Major Marcelino Rois Camponês founded the Vila de Nossa Senhora da Conceição de Albuquerque on the last deep water below the Serra de Albuquerque, the nucleus of Corumbá.

The garrison had the Indians to fight as well as the Spanish. Guaicurú warriors stormed the fort in 1791 and killed fifty-four of its men, after which the old palisade was rebuilt in stone as the Forte Novo de Coimbra. In September 1801 the Paraguayan governor Lázaro de Ribera came against it with four schooners, two canoes and 600 men; the forty-two defenders held out for ten days and the Spaniards sailed away. In 1821 Corumbá was still a small garrison port serving the river traffic between Cuiabá and Cáceres.
zh:
科伦巴位于巴拉圭河右岸，潘塔纳尔季节性泛滥的平原从这里向西铺向玻利维亚的丘陵。潟湖之间是瓜托人的地方，他们以家族为单位住在独木舟上，捕鱼、用弓箭射鸟；被葡萄牙人叫作「独木舟人」的帕亚瓜人则驾着战舟游弋在巴拉圭河上游。1444年时，还没有欧洲人进入这片水与沼泽的迷宫，唯一的道路是连通巴拉圭河与马托格罗索高原营地的水道。

西班牙人1593年在这里建起圣地亚哥-德赫雷斯城，但这座城和邻近的耶稣会据点都被从圣保罗溯流劫掠的远征队摧毁，泛滥平原上再无欧洲人定居。此后葡萄牙和西班牙为巴拉圭河边界争执了一个世纪。为钉住边界、压制帕亚瓜人，马托格罗索都督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克于1775年派马蒂亚斯·里贝罗·达科斯塔上尉率245人、乘15艘独木舟从库亚巴出发，在圣弗朗西斯科·沙勿略狭道筑起土木要塞，那是整条河上唯一能用炮火封锁的河段；要塞的火炮还是从贝伦杜帕拉一路水运而来。1778年，军士长马塞利诺·罗伊斯·坎波内斯在阿尔布克尔克山以下最后一段深水河道旁建立「圣母受孕德阿尔布克尔克镇」，这就是科伦巴的雏形。

守军的敌人不止西班牙人。1791年，瓜伊库鲁武士猛攻堡垒，杀死54名守军，旧木栅此后改用石料重建，称新科英布拉堡。1801年9月，巴拉圭督军拉萨罗·德·里韦拉率4艘双桅纵帆船、2艘独木舟和600人来攻，42名守军坚守十天，西班牙人最终撤围。1821年时，科伦巴仍是一座小小的驻防河港，为库亚巴与卡塞雷斯之间的河运服务。

en:
In 1444 the steep bluffs above an upper Paraguay River bay, just below the Pantanal, were Mbayá and Guaná country. Mobile bands knew the channels, islands and seasonal floods, and the hills rising from the bank offered defensible ground in a land without towns. The river led from Asunción toward the northern wetlands and the country that Portuguese raiders and settlers later entered from Mato Grosso. No European garrison watched the channel then, and no treaty had fixed a border there.

Portugal built the New Coimbra Fort in 1775 to secure its claims after the Treaty of Madrid and to check Payaguá and Kadiwéu raids. On 17 October 1791 the Viceroy of the Río de la Plata ordered two Spanish posts, Fuerte Borbón and San Carlos del Apa. José Antonio Zavala y Delgadillo founded Borbón on 25 September 1792 on the steep hills above the bay, invited Mbayá chiefs to the ceremony and named the post for the Spanish Bourbon dynasty; José de Isasi became its first commander. Its garrison of about a hundred men depended on irregular convoys of salt meat from Concepción and Charcas. Mbayá and Guaná bands sold cattle stolen from Spanish ranches to the Portuguese in exchange for arms and brandy. After attacks on Concepción in 1796, settlers killed seventy-five Indigenous people from nearby camps, breaking the fragile peace. In September 1801 Lázaro de Rivera sent four schooners, two canoes and six hundred men against Coimbra; forty-two defenders, warned by Kadiwéu allies, held out for ten days and the expedition withdrew. Borbón troops fought Manuel Belgrano's forces in 1810, and prisoners from that campaign were held there. When the post was abandoned, Mbayá groups occupied it, then Portuguese troops from Coimbra displaced them before withdrawing and returning it. Around 1817 Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia added a stone wall three kilometres long and new buildings for the garrison.
zh:
1444年，后来建起波旁堡的陡峭丘陵位于上巴拉圭河一处河湾上方，潘塔纳尔就在上游不远处，四周是姆巴亚人和瓜纳人的土地。移动群体熟悉水道、岛屿和季节性洪水，河岸隆起的丘陵则在这片没有城镇的土地上提供了易守之处。巴拉圭河从亚松森通向北方湿地，也通向葡萄牙袭掠者和移民后来从马托格罗索进入的地区。那时还没有欧洲驻军监视河道，也没有哪份条约在这里划定边界。

1775年，葡萄牙修建新科英布拉堡，用以巩固《马德里条约》后的主张，并防备帕亚瓜人和卡迪韦乌人袭掠。1791年10月17日，拉普拉塔总督下令修建波旁堡和圣卡洛斯德尔阿帕堡两处西班牙据点。1792年9月25日，何塞·安东尼奥·萨瓦拉-德尔加迪略在河湾上方的陡丘上建立波旁堡，邀请姆巴亚酋长出席仪式，并以西班牙波旁王朝为要塞命名；何塞·德·伊萨西任首任指挥官。约一百名驻军依赖康塞普西翁和查尔卡斯不定期运来的腌肉补给。姆巴亚人和瓜纳人把从西班牙牧场偷来的牛卖给葡萄牙人，换取武器和白兰地。1796年他们袭击康塞普西翁后，当地定居者杀死附近营地中的75名原住民，脆弱的和平随之破裂。1801年9月，拉萨罗·德·里韦拉派出四艘双桅纵帆船、两艘独木舟和六百人攻打科英布拉堡；42名守军得到卡迪韦乌盟友示警，坚守十天，远征队撤退。1810年，波旁堡军队与曼努埃尔·贝尔格拉诺的部队作战，一些战俘也关押在堡中。据点弃守后，姆巴亚人群先占据此地，随后科英布拉的葡萄牙军队赶走他们，最终又撤军交还要塞。约1817年，加斯帕尔·罗德里格斯·德·弗朗西亚加修一道三公里长的石墙，并为驻军增建房屋。

en:
In 1444 the Paraguay River banks and islands northwest of Asunción were Payaguá country. The Payaguá called themselves Evueví, people of the river, and relied on large dugouts while other Guaycuruan peoples later took to horses. Families moved between the Pantanal and waters far downstream, fishing, gathering and raiding Guaraní maize fields on the eastern shore. Guaraní speakers called their enemies Payaguá; the river itself may carry that name, from a word meaning 'river of the Payaguá'. On this stretch of water, canoes gave Payaguá crews the advantage that horsemen held on the plains.

Juan de Ayolas founded the short-lived port of Candelaria on 2 February 1537 while passing through Payaguá lands; after his return from the Chaco, Payaguá warriors killed him and about eighty Spaniards, probably near the later Fuerte Borbón. After Asunción was founded, their canoes made Spanish crews call them river pirates. In 1613 the colony declared a 'war of fire and blood' against the Payaguá and their Mbayá allies, and seventeenth-century yerba mate traffic often moved overland to avoid their raids. The gold rush to Cuiabá after 1718 brought Portuguese canoe traffic through the northern waters; Payaguá attacks destroyed a party of about two hundred men in 1725 and killed most of a party of about four hundred in 1730. Spanish policy changed to trade and accommodation in that same year, and the southern Tacumbú bands were living near Asunción by about 1750. In 1786 Father Juan Francisco Amancio González y Escobar founded Reducción Melodía on this bank, naming it for Governor Pedro Melo de Portugal. His departure left the reduction abandoned, and the site was remembered as Amancio Cué. In 1821 the crossing still answered more to river people and passing canoes than to a settled town.
zh:
1444年，亚松森西北方的巴拉圭河岸与岛屿是帕亚瓜人的土地。他们自称埃武埃维，意为河上人；其他瓜伊库鲁人后来成为骑手，他们则依靠大型独木舟。各家庭在潘塔纳尔和远方下游水道之间往来，捕鱼、采集，也袭掠东岸的瓜拉尼玉米田。瓜拉尼语把这些敌人称作帕亚瓜人；巴拉圭河的名字可能就来自这个称呼，意思是「帕亚瓜人的河」。在这段水面上，独木舟带给帕亚瓜人的优势，如同马匹带给平原骑手。

1537年2月2日，胡安·德·阿约拉斯经过帕亚瓜人的土地时建立短命的坎德拉里亚港；他从查科返回后，帕亚瓜战士杀死他和约80名西班牙人，地点可能在后来的波旁堡附近。亚松森建立后，他们的独木舟使西班牙船员把他们称为河流海盗。1613年，殖民地对帕亚瓜人和姆巴亚盟友宣布「火与血之战」；17世纪的马黛茶贸易常改走陆路，以避开河上袭掠。1718年库亚巴发现黄金后，葡萄牙淘金者乘独木舟涌入北方水道。帕亚瓜人在1725年消灭一支约200人的队伍，1730年又杀死一支约400人队伍中的大多数。同年，西班牙政策转向贸易与安抚；约1750年，南部的塔昆布群体已在亚松森附近居住。1786年，神父胡安·弗朗西斯科·阿曼西奥·冈萨雷斯·伊·埃斯科瓦尔在这一岸建立摩罗蒂亚传教村，以总督佩德罗·梅洛·德·葡萄牙的姓氏命名。他后来离开，传教村荒废，旧址被称为阿曼西奥库埃。1821年，这里的渡口仍更多听命于河上居民和往来独木舟，而不是一座定居城镇。

en:
The grasslands east of the upper Uruguay, walled with gallery forest along the river bends, were Guarani country in 1444. Families moved between open campo and riverine villages, and canoes carried fish, maize and pottery along the waterway that the Spanish and Portuguese empires later made their frontier. The seven towns known as the Seven Peoples of the Missions did not yet exist; the Guarani of the future São Borja lived beyond the reach of either crown.

Paulist slave-raiders had destroyed the earlier Jesuit reductions in Guaíra and Tape when Spanish Jesuits returned in 1682. Francisco Garcia brought 195 Guarani from São Tomé and founded São Francisco de Borja, the first of the Seven Peoples, which held 2,814 people by 1707. Stone churches rose around planned plazas, cattle ran by the thousand on the campos, and the seven towns kept their own herds, workshops and militia. The Treaty of Madrid of 1750 handed this ground to Portugal in exchange for Colônia do Sacramento and ordered the Guarani to move west of the Uruguay. Led by Sepé Tiaraju, a war captain of São Luiz Gonzaga, they refused, and the Guarani War ran from 1753 to 1756. Sepé was killed in a skirmish on 7 February 1756; three days later at Caiboaté, 3,000 Spanish and Portuguese troops killed about 1,500 Guarani for the loss of four of their own and occupied the seven towns. Spain annulled the transfer in 1761 and recovered a district the troops had emptied, while the Jesuit expulsions of 1759 and 1767 broke the mission system altogether by 1768. In 1801 Manuel dos Santos Pedroso took the whole Seven Peoples for Portugal with forty men.
zh:
乌拉圭河上游东岸是片片草原，河湾处生着带状林，1444年时是瓜拉尼人的土地。家族在开阔草原和河畔村落间迁移，独木舟沿着河道运送鱼、玉米和陶器；西班牙和葡萄牙两个帝国后来把这条河变成边界，此时瓜拉尼人还不受任何一方王冠管辖。合称传教士城（七传道区）的七座村镇尚不存在，后来圣博尔哈一带的瓜拉尼人自行其是。

圣保罗的捕奴旗兵摧毁了瓜伊拉和塔佩较早的耶稣会传道村，西班牙耶稣会士于1682年重返此地。弗朗西斯科·加西亚带着从圣多梅迁出的一百九十五名瓜拉尼人建立圣方济各·德·博尔哈，这是七传道区中的第一座，到1707年已有二千八百一十四人。石砌教堂立在规划整齐的广场周围，草原上放养着数以千计的牛，七座村镇自营牧场、作坊和民兵。1750年的《马德里条约》把这片土地划给葡萄牙，以交换科洛尼亚-德尔萨克拉门托，并命令瓜拉尼人西迁到乌拉圭河对岸。圣路易斯-贡萨加的战将塞佩·蒂亚拉茹带领众人拒绝，1753至1756年瓜拉尼战争就此展开。1756年2月7日，塞佩在一场遭遇战中被杀；三天后的凯博阿特，三千名西葡军队杀死约一千五百名瓜拉尼人，己方仅亡四人，随即占领七座村镇。1761年，西班牙废除这次转让，收回的却是一片被军队清空的地区；1759年和1767年耶稣会接连被逐，到1768年整个传道体系已经瓦解。1801年，曼努埃尔·多斯桑托斯·佩德罗索带着四十个人，就把整片传教士城替葡萄牙拿了下来。

en:
Barra sits where the Rio Grande runs into the São Francisco, among seasonally flooded flats and gallery forests cut through the dry sertão of north-eastern Brazil. In 1444 the confluence was Xakriabá country; these Akwé-speaking Ge people ranged from the São Francisco to the Tocantins, moving between riverine woods, hunting grounds and inland trails.

The place was opened up by the Casa da Torre of Dias d'Ávila, the great cattle clan of Bahia, whose fortified seat on the coast was built like a medieval castle. The family opened a corral on the Rio Grande ravines in 1670, and Franciscans raised a chapel there ten years later. Cattle pens, ferries and boats plying the São Francisco turned the spot into an inland river station on the ranching frontier, and in 1752 it was raised to a town as Vila de São Francisco do Rio Grande.
zh:
巴拉位于格兰德河汇入圣弗朗西斯科河之处，季节性河滩与走廊林横切过巴西东北部干旱的内陆荒原。1444年，汇合处一带是舍克里厄巴人的土地；他们是说阿克温语的热依人，活动范围从圣弗朗西斯科河直到托坎廷斯河，往来于河畔林地、猎场和内陆小径之间。

打开这片地方的是迪亚斯·达维拉的卡萨达托雷，巴伊亚最大的畜牧家族，其在海岸的宅邸按中世纪城堡的样子修成堡垒。1670年，家族在格兰德河坡地开设牧栏，十年后方济各会在那里建起礼拜堂。牛栏、渡口和往来圣弗朗西斯科河的船只，把这里变成畜牧边疆上的内河驿站；1752年，此地升格为镇，称圣弗朗西斯科-杜里奥格兰德镇。

en:
Parnaíba covers the delta of the Parnaíba, the only delta in the Americas that opens directly into the sea; before the Atlantic the river splits into the Igaraçu and a web of mangrove channels and shoals. In 1444 the shores were the country of the Tremembé, who fished the banks from canoes and gathered shellfish along the dunes, and their Tupi name for the river means muddy-water river. Portuguese vessels reconnoitred the coast in the sixteenth century, and Jesuits began work among the Tremembé in 1607, but no settlement yet stood among the dunes.

Cattle brought war, then a port. As ranchers occupied the Parnaíba valley, a baptized Indian named Mandu Ladino rose in 1712 and led Tupi and Cariri bands through the sertões of Piauí, Maranhão and Ceará, burning fazendas. An expedition raised with Tabajara allies from the Serra da Ibiapaba ran him down in 1716; he died of his wounds in the river, and the rising lasted until 1719. In 1758 Domingos Dias da Silva set up a charqueada, a dried-beef works, at Porto das Barcas, and the Vila de São João da Parnaíba was installed beside it in 1762. It became the shipping point for the dried beef and leather of the Piauí sertão and took the name Parnaíba in 1801; one local account traces the word instead to the parnahiba, a rancher's knife for chopping dried beef, said to have been brought from Bahia. In 1821 its quays still shipped the cattle products of the sertão.
zh:
巴纳伊巴一带是巴纳伊巴河的三角洲，这是美洲唯一直接面向开阔大洋的河口三角洲：大河在入海前汊出伊加拉苏河，散成一片红树林水道和沙洲。1444年，两岸是特雷门贝人的地盘，他们划独木舟在浅滩捕鱼、沿沙丘采贝，大河的图皮语名字意为「浑水河」。16世纪有葡萄牙船只侦察这段海岸，耶稣会士从1607年起向特雷门贝人传教，但沙丘之间还没有聚落。

牛群先带来战争，再带来港口。牧人占据巴纳伊巴河谷后，受洗的印第安人曼杜·拉迪诺于1712年起事，率领图皮人和卡里里人转战皮奥伊、马拉尼翁和塞阿拉的荒原，焚毁牧场。1716年，一支得到伊比亚帕巴山塔巴哈拉人助战的讨伐队追上了他，他伤重死在河中，战事延续到1719年。1758年，多明戈斯·迪亚斯·达席尔瓦在巴尔卡斯港开办腌肉作坊，1762年圣若昂达巴纳伊巴镇在作坊旁设立，成为皮奥伊荒原腌肉和皮革的输出港，1801年定名巴纳伊巴。当地还有一种说法，把名字追溯到牧人切风干肉的刀「帕尔纳伊巴」，说这刀是最早的牧主从巴伊亚带来的。1821年时，码头上装船的仍是荒原出产的牧产品。

en:
Santa Catarina is a long Atlantic island separated from the southern Brazilian mainland by a sheltered strait. Bays on its landward side offered anchorage to ships sailing to the River Plate, while mainland bays and the Serra do Mar lay beyond the channel. In 1444 Carijó Tupi-Guarani villagers called the island Meiembipe and lived from maize and manioc gardens, fishing and shellfish. Their canoes crossed the same strait that later carried European garrisons and supply ships.

Portuguese navigators knew the island early in the sixteenth century, but settlers did not stay until Francisco Dias Velho founded a shore community in 1673; its chapel to Nossa Senhora do Desterro followed five years later. After the settlement became a town, the crown created the island captaincy on 11 August 1738 and appointed José da Silva Paes governor. From 1748 about six thousand Azorean and Madeiran settlers reached the coast, opening farms and producing cotton and linen beside the fishing villages.

Paes's garrison covered the northern anchorage with Santa Cruz de Anhatomirim, São José da Ponta Grossa and Santo Antônio de Ratones. The forts did not stop Pedro de Cevallos, whose Spanish expedition took the island in February 1777; the Treaty of San Ildefonso returned it to Portugal that October. In 1821 Desterro was a garrison, fishing and provisioning port on the route to the River Plate.
zh:
圣卡塔琳娜是大西洋中的狭长岛屿，与巴西南部大陆隔着一条遮蔽良好的海峡。朝向大陆的海湾可为前往拉普拉塔河的船只提供锚地，海峡对岸是大陆海湾和马尔山。1444年，讲图皮-瓜拉尼语的卡里若村民把此岛称为梅因比佩，靠种植玉米和木薯、捕鱼和采贝为生。他们的独木舟往来的海峡，后来也通行欧洲驻军和补给船。

葡萄牙航海者16世纪初就知道这座岛，但直到1673年，弗朗西斯科·迪亚斯·维略才在岸边建立持久定居点；五年后，这里建起献给流亡圣母的小教堂。聚落升为镇后，王室在1738年8月11日设立岛屿都督辖区，任命若泽·达席尔瓦·派斯为总督。1748年起，约六千名亚速尔和马德拉移民抵达海岸，在渔村旁开辟农庄，种植棉花、纺织麻布。

派斯的驻军在北方锚地周围布置阿尼亚托米林圣十字、蓬塔格罗萨圣若泽和拉托内斯圣安多尼三座要塞。这些工事没有挡住佩德罗·德·塞瓦略斯：1777年2月，他率西班牙远征队夺取岛屿；同年10月，《圣伊尔德方索条约》把它归还葡萄牙。1821年，德斯泰罗是通往拉普拉塔河航路上的驻军港、渔港和补给港。

en:
The Cuiabá country lies around the Cuiabá and Coxipó rivers, where tropical forest gives way to cerrado scrub and seasonal floodplain on the edge of the Paraguay basin. Its Bororo name is commonly read as the place of the ikuia, a barbed fishing arrow, and in 1444 Coxiponé villages held the riverbanks, their canoes and trails following waters that run south to the Paraguay. No Portuguese captaincy reached this far inland.

Gold brought the Portuguese. The São Paulo bandeirante Manoel de Campos Bicudo passed through in 1673 and 1682 and left a short-lived settlement at the mouth of the Coxipó. In 1718 Pascoal Moreira Cabral, a bandeirante from Sorocaba, went up the Coxipó to seize Indians, lost a fight with Coxiponé warriors, and on the retreat his men found gold. The founding act was signed at the Forquilha camp on 8 April 1719, and Cabral was elected guardian of the mines by a direct vote held in the forest. Thousands of prospectors then made their way west from the São Paulo captaincy. In October 1722 enslaved Indians working for another Sorocaba bandeirante, Miguel Sutil, struck a richer seam on the Prainha stream, and the whole camp moved there; the parish church of Bom Jesus went up on the new site in 1723. Rodrigo César de Menezes raised the settlement to a town, Vila Real do Senhor Bom Jesus de Cuiabá, on 1 January 1727. The gold ran thinner than hoped, and an earthquake in 1746 destroyed much of the town. When the Captaincy of Mato Grosso was created in 1748 its first governor, Antônio Rolim de Moura, founded Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade as his capital after arriving in 1751. Cuiabá stayed a remote riverside mining and supply town, made a city only on 17 September 1818.
zh:
库亚巴一带位于库亚巴河与科希波河沿岸，地处巴拉圭河流域边缘，热带雨林在此过渡为塞拉多灌丛和季节性洪泛平原。博罗罗语通常把这个地名解释为使用「伊库亚」（一种带刺渔箭）的地方；1444年，科希波内人的村社据有河畔，独木舟和小径顺着南流注入巴拉圭河的水路延伸，葡萄牙人的都督辖区还没有触及这么深的内陆。

是黄金把葡萄牙人引来的。圣保罗的内地拓荒者曼努埃尔·德·坎波斯·比库多1673年和1682年经过此地，在科希波河口留下一座不久荒废的聚落。1718年，来自索罗卡巴的拓荒者帕斯科阿尔·莫雷拉·卡布拉尔沿科希波河上溯猎捕印第安人，被科希波内武士击败，撤退途中他的人发现了黄金。1719年4月8日，众人在福基利亚营地签署建置文书，卡布拉尔还在丛林中经直接投票当选矿区监督。数以千计的淘金人随后从圣保罗都督辖区向西赶来。1722年10月，为另一位索罗卡巴拓荒者米格尔·苏蒂尔劳作的被奴役印第安人在普赖尼亚溪挖到更富的矿脉，整个营地随之迁去，邦热苏斯主教堂1723年在新址建起。1727年1月1日，罗德里戈·塞萨尔·德·梅内塞斯把聚落升为维拉·雷亚尔·杜·塞尼奥尔·邦热苏斯·德·库亚巴镇。金矿比预期稀薄，1746年的一场地震又摧毁了大半个城镇。1748年马托格罗索都督辖区设立，首任总督安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1751年到任后另建维拉贝拉达桑蒂西马特林达德为首府。库亚巴始终是一座偏远的河畔采矿与补给城镇，直到1818年9月17日才升为市。

en:
Rio Branco covers the upper Branco valley, where the Uraricoera and Tacutu meet and the river starts its run south to the Negro. Open savanna breaks the forest around the upper streams, with gallery woods along the banks. Carib-speaking Macushi lived beside those streams, and Arawak-speaking Wapishana held country to the east. High water let canoes ascend the lower Branco from the Negro, while rapids restricted travel farther upstream. In 1444 the valley belonged to river and savanna villages linked by manioc fields, fishing and regional trade.

Portuguese intervention came late and by force. Carmelite missionaries entered in 1725, and slave-raiding parties and troops pushed up the Branco in the 1730s while Dutch, English and Spanish rivals also probed the Guiana savanna. The Portuguese built São Joaquim Fort at the Uraricoera-Tacutu meeting point from 1775 to 1778, then tried to settle Macushi and other villagers in controlled missions. In 1790 that policy produced the rising remembered in Portuguese sources as Praia de Sangue: after a chief was seized at the fort, the villages withdrew to the hills and Portuguese reprisals broke up the settlements; old accounts say the slaughter in the river reddened the Branco. Manuel da Gama Lôbo d'Almada introduced cattle and horses in 1789, and the São Bento, São José and São Marcos ranches followed from 1793 to 1799, giving the Portuguese frontier a ranching economy. An English incursion in 1810 to 1811 was driven back.
zh:
里奥布朗库位于布朗库河上游，乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河在此汇合，河水随后南流注入内格罗河。上游地带森林间露出大片稀树草原，河岸则有林带。说加勒比语的马库希人沿水道居住，说阿拉瓦克语的瓦皮沙纳人据有东面土地。涨水时，独木舟可从内格罗河驶入布朗库河下游，急流又限制了更上游的航行。1444年，河谷属于这些滨河与草原村社，木薯田、渔业和区域贸易把各村落联系起来。

葡萄牙人很晚才以武力进入这里。1725年，加尔默罗会传教士先来；1730年代，掳奴队和军队沿布朗库河推进，荷兰、英格兰和西班牙的势力也在试探圭亚那草原。1775年至1778年，葡萄牙人在乌拉里奎拉河与塔库图河汇合处修建圣若阿金堡垒，随后试图把马库希人和其他原住民安置进受控制的传教村。1790年，这种做法引发「血滩」暴动：一名酋长在堡垒被抓后，各村社退入山地，葡萄牙人的报复摧毁了村社；旧记载称，河中的杀戮使布朗库河泛红。曼努埃尔·达·加马·洛博·德·阿尔马达在1789年引入牛和马，圣本图、圣若泽和圣马科斯牧场又在1793年至1799年间建立，河谷的稀树草原上出现牧场，也使葡萄牙人的边疆占据有了依托。1810年至1811年，一支进入河谷的英格兰武装被击退。

en:
Marajó is the large river-and-sea island between the Amazon mouth, the Pará channels and the Atlantic. Floodwater covers broad stretches of its savanna and forest every year, so its inhabitants raised villages on earthen mounds called tesos, planted manioc on the higher ground, fished the surrounding channels and moved by canoe. The mound-building Marajoara tradition also produced finely painted and incised pottery, with seated figures, urns and geometric decoration. In 1444 Aruã villages still occupied the island, and their fishermen and canoe-warriors knew the shoals and passages where fresh river water met the Atlantic tides.

European ships entering the estuary in the sixteenth century brought raids and new diseases, which sharply reduced the indigenous population. The Portuguese crown then turned the island into a noble grant, the captaincy of Ilha Grande de Joanes, in 1665; António de Sousa Macedo's proxy took possession two years later. The grantee held lands around some of the most useful channels out of the Amazon, while Marajó's natural grasslands carried cattle that supplied Belém with meat and hides. Capuchin friars received lands near the Arari River in 1696 and combined missions with cattle ranching. The crown bought the captaincy back in 1754 and placed Marajó under Grão-Pará, putting the river entrance under direct royal administration.
zh:
马拉若是亚马逊河口、帕拉河水道与大西洋之间的大河海岛。每年洪水会淹没大片热带草原和林地，岛上居民因此把村落建在名为特索的土丘上，在高地种木薯，在四周水道捕鱼，并乘独木舟往来。筑丘的马拉若文化还制作绘刻精美的陶器，包括坐像、葬瓮和几何纹饰。1444年，阿鲁昂人的村落仍住在岛上，渔民和独木舟战士熟悉河水与大西洋潮水相接处的浅滩和航道。

16世纪进入河口的欧洲船只带来袭掠和新的疾病，使印第安人口大幅减少。1665年，葡萄牙王室把全岛封给安东尼奥·德索萨·马塞多，设为大若阿内斯岛都督领；其代理人在两年后接管。受封者掌握着亚马逊出海通道周边的土地，马拉若的天然草场则牧放牛群，为贝伦供应肉类和皮革。1696年，嘉布遣会修士获得阿拉里河附近土地，把传教和养牛结合起来。1754年，王室购回都督领，将马拉若划归格劳帕拉，使这一河口进入王室直接管辖。

en:
Santo Antônio da Manga occupies a left-bank stretch of the middle São Francisco, between the mouths of the Urucuia and Paracatu and opposite a wooded island later called São Romão. In 1444 the river, its islands and the surrounding sertão were Kaiapó country. Villages planted and hunted along the banks, and Portuguese backwoodsmen and slave-raiding bands had not yet reached this bend.

The Portuguese arraial of Santo Antônio da Manga was founded on 23 October 1668. Its wharf became the main river port on the Minas stretch of the São Francisco and later a judicial seat; boats carried gold, coin and precious stones from Goiás and Mato Grosso toward the coast. Runaway slaves, fugitives, survivors of earlier expeditions and colonial patrols fought over the island opposite, and tradition places the destruction of the Kaiapó village there on a feast of Saint Romanus before 1712. In 1736 the Crown extended a per-capita gold levy to sertão households, including enslaved people, even though this river-and-ranch district had few mines. The arraial joined the backcountry risings in July. Its leaders included Pedro Cardoso de Oliveira and his mother Maria da Cruz, who had run a large ranch after her husband's death in 1734. The rebels discussed marching on Vila Rica against Governor Martinho de Mendonça, but colonial forces crushed the movement that year. Tried in Bahia, Maria was sentenced to a fine and six years' exile in Africa, then received a pardon from João V in April 1739.
zh:
圣安东尼奥-达曼加位于圣弗朗西斯科河中游左岸，地当乌鲁库亚河与帕拉卡图河河口一带，对岸是后来称为圣罗芒的林木岛屿。1444年，大河、岛屿和周围腹地都是卡亚波人的土地。村社沿岸耕作和狩猎，葡萄牙腹地开拓者与捕奴队还没有抵达这道河湾。

1668年10月23日，葡萄牙人建立圣安东尼奥-达曼加村。这里的码头成为圣弗朗西斯科河米纳斯河段主要河港，后来又设司法驻地；船只把来自戈亚斯和马托格罗索的黄金、钱币和宝石运往沿海。逃亡奴隶、逃犯、旧远征队残部和殖民巡逻队曾在对岸岛屿交战，相传卡亚波人村落就在1712年以前的一个圣罗芒日被摧毁。1736年，王室把按人缴纳的黄金税扩及腹地住户，连被奴役者也要计入，但这个靠河运和牧场为生的地区几乎没有矿山。7月，村落加入腹地起事，领袖包括佩德罗·卡多佐·德·奥利维拉和他的母亲玛丽亚·达克鲁斯；后者在丈夫1734年去世后经营一座大农庄。起事者曾商议进军维拉·里卡，反对总督马蒂纽·德·门东萨，但殖民军当年就将运动镇压。玛丽亚在巴伊亚受审，被判罚款并流放非洲六年，1739年4月获若昂五世赦免。

en:
The open plateau between the Serra da Canastra and the Rio Grande was known to colonial travellers as the country of the Araxás. Gallery forest followed its streams through high grassland, and the fords and camping grounds lay on the routes leading from São Paulo into the Goiás and Minas interior. In 1444 the Araxás lived in independent villages held together by kinship and dealings with their neighbours; no Portuguese farm, parish or road had yet marked this far western edge of the future Minas Gerais.

Europeans noted the Araxás from the late sixteenth century, but the frontier only reached them in the 1740s. In 1749 their leaders asked the governor of Goiás for Jesuit missionaries and a settled village under the protection of Antônio Pires de Campos, the Paulista commander of the inland frontier. A village was laid out on the Rio Claro near where it enters the Rio das Velhas in 1750 and 1751; while Pires de Campos was away on a northern campaign, Caiapó warriors struck, killed the Araxá men and carried off the surviving women and children, and official letters of early 1751 reported the people destroyed. Bandeira warfare then opened the grassland to cattle ranches, whose owners took up land from about 1770, and in 1791 the farming settlement became the parish of São Domingos de Araxá, the indigenous name carried into the Portuguese province that existed by 1821.
zh:
卡纳斯特拉山脉与格兰德河之间的开阔高原，在殖民时代旅行者口中是阿拉斯人的地方。林带河谷穿插在高原草场之间，渡口和营地正处在从圣保罗通往戈亚斯和米纳斯内陆的路上。1444年时，阿拉斯人靠亲属关系和与邻族的往来维系着各自独立的村落；在后来的米纳斯吉拉斯极西边地上，还没有葡萄牙人的农庄、堂区或道路。

欧洲人的记载从16世纪后期起提到阿拉斯人，但边地真正推进到他们身边要到18世纪40年代。1749年，阿拉斯首领请求戈亚斯总督派遣耶稣会士，并在圣保罗出身的内陆边地统领安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯保护下建一座定居村。1750至1751年，村子建在克拉鲁河汇入旧河处附近；皮雷斯·德·坎波斯北上征战期间，卡亚波战士袭来，杀死阿拉斯男子、掳走幸存的妇孺，1751年初的官员信函报告这一部群已经覆灭。随后的旗队战争把草场开放给牧牛场，牧场主约从1770年起占地定居；1791年，农业聚落成为圣多明我-迪阿拉沙堂区，到1821年，这个原住民名字已挂在葡萄牙人治下的行省堂区名下。

en:
Ofaie is named for the Ofaié, a Macro-Jê people of the Paraná bend in what is now eastern Mato Grosso do Sul. They camped along the great river near the mouth of the Sucuriú and by the headwaters of the Ivinhema and Vacaria, hunting and planting in the gallery forest in small bands; later estimates put their numbers before the colonists at perhaps five thousand. Around them stretched the cerrado and the sertão of the São Paulo backlands. In 1444 this was a world of rivers and villages no European had seen.

Europeans first passed here in numbers after gold was found on the Cuiabá in 1718. Every high-water season, from late March into June, the monções left Porto Feliz, fleets of great dugouts that went down the Tietê into the Paraná and past the Sucuriú mouth on a 3,500-kilometre pull to the mines. Year after year the Ofaié watched the canoes go by, and no post was raised on their bank. In 1821 the Sucuriú still had no Portuguese town or fort, and the convoys, past their greatest days, were the people's only regular tie to the world outside their rivers.
zh:
奥法耶得名于奥法耶人，这是住在巴拉那河大拐弯一带的大热依语族群，地在今南马托格罗索州东部。他们在苏库里乌河口附近的大河沿岸和伊维涅马河、瓦卡里亚河的源头扎营，以小群体在长廊林中狩猎、耕种；据后世估计，殖民者到来之前他们约有五千人。四周是塞拉多稀树草原和圣保罗方向的荒原。1444年，这里还是一片欧洲人未曾见过的河流与村落世界。

1718年库亚巴河发现黄金后，欧洲人才成批经过这里。每逢3月底到6月的涨水季，「季风船队」从波尔图费利斯出发，一队队大独木舟沿铁特河驶入巴拉那河，经过苏库里乌河口，走完3500公里水路前往金矿。奥法耶人年年看着独木舟驶过，他们的河岸上却没有建起一个据点。1821年时，苏库里乌河畔仍没有葡萄牙人的城镇或要塞，船队最繁忙的年月已经过去，过往的独木舟是他们与河外世界唯一的固定往来。

en:
The Rio das Mortes, the River of Deaths, runs through a corridor of hills between the Serra do Lenheiro and the Serra de São José, on the southern edge of the Minas country. Before the miners came, Macro-Jê villages farmed and hunted along its water meadows, and their tracks crossed the river at the fords on the way through the sertão. In 1444 no Portuguese trail yet entered the valley, and its gravel had never been panned for gold.

A Paulista party led by the Taubaté bandeirante Tomé Portes del-Rei opened the first lasting camps on the river around 1700; after he died, other miners built up the arraial of Nossa Senhora do Pilar. These diggings were among the districts fought over in the War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709, when the Paulista pioneers who had found the gold fought the emboabas, newcomers from Portugal and the other Brazilian captaincies. The newcomers won, and the crown used the peace to set up its own order: in 1713 the camps were chartered as the town of São João del-Rei, named for King John V, and it became seat of the Rio das Mortes comarca.

The town stood on the Estrada Real, the royal road that carried the gold of the mountains down to the coast at Paraty. Its merchants ranched cattle, supplied the interior and bought slaves from Africa alongside mining, and the lay brotherhoods raised the baroque churches of Pilar, Carmo, Mercês and Rosário; the sculptor Aleijadinho carved for São João as he did for the other mining towns. The gold gave out in the later eighteenth century, but cattle and trade kept the comarca town going, and in 1789 its officers and militia men were drawn into the Inconfidência Mineira, the conspiracy against Portuguese rule.
zh:
死亡河（Rio das Mortes）穿行在莱涅罗山与圣若泽山之间的丘陵走廊里，地当米纳斯金矿区的南缘。淘金者到来之前，大热依语族的村落沿河畔水草甸耕作、狩猎，他们的小路经各处渡口穿过荒原。1444年时，还没有葡萄牙人的小路进入这条河谷，河中的砾石也无人淘洗。

约1700年，陶巴特出身的圣保罗远征者托梅·波尔特斯·德尔雷伊率队在河畔开出最早的持久营地；他死后，其他矿工把圣母皮拉尔营地发展起来。1707—1709年的恩博阿巴斯战争就是为争夺这类金矿区而打：发现黄金的圣保罗拓殖者对阵「恩博阿巴斯」，即从葡萄牙和其他都督辖区涌来的新来者。新来者取胜，王室借战局安定建立自己的秩序：1713年各营地合组为圣若昂-德尔雷伊镇，以国王若昂五世命名，并成为死亡河司法辖区的驻地。

小镇位于皇家大道上，山里的黄金沿这条大道运往帕拉蒂海岸。商人在采金之外牧牛、为内陆供货、买进非洲奴隶，各在俗兄弟会建起皮拉尔、卡尔莫、梅尔塞斯和罗萨里奥等巴洛克教堂；雕刻家阿莱雅迪尼奥也曾为圣若昂创作雕刻，就像他为其他矿业城镇所做的那样。18世纪后期黄金枯竭，但牧牛和贸易让这座司法辖区城镇维持下去，1789年，这里的军官和民兵也卷入反抗葡萄牙统治的米纳斯密谋。

en:
Castro covers a stretch of the Campos Gerais, the open grasslands that run across Paraná between wooded ridges. The Iapó cuts through sandstone banks at Guartelá and provides water and fords on the way from the southern pastures toward São Paulo. In 1444 Guarapiaba people, a Tupi group recorded along the Iapó, used these crossings and camp sites, while Kaingang bands moved through the nearby forest edge. Native paths followed the driest ground, but no Portuguese ranch, chapel or toll post had yet been built.

Paulista cattlemen reached the Campos Gerais around 1700, and the Capão Alto land grant is dated to 1704. Pouso do Iapó became a watering and overnight camp on the Caminho de Sorocaba, where tropeiros rested mule and cattle herds travelling from Viamão to the Sorocaba fair. Families from Sorocaba, Santos and Itu took up ranches; a wattle-and-daub chapel appeared in 1751, and Carmelite friars built another church in 1769. The settlement became the parish of Sant'Ana do Iapó in 1771, and on 24 September 1788 it was separated from Curitiba and raised to a town as Vila Nova de Castro, named for the Portuguese overseas minister Martinho de Melo e Castro. In 1821 cattle, mules, ranches and the long road to market still set the pattern of local life.
zh:
卡斯特鲁位于坎波斯吉拉斯草原的一段，这片开阔草原穿过巴拉那，两侧是林木覆盖的山脊。亚波河在瓜尔特拉切过砂岩河岸，为南方牧场通往圣保罗方向的道路提供水源和渡口。1444年时，亚波河畔有记载的图皮语族群瓜拉皮亚巴人使用这些渡口和营地，卡因冈游群则在附近林缘活动。原住民小路沿最干燥的地面延伸，但这里还没有葡萄牙牧场、小教堂或税卡。

1700年前后，圣保罗牧人进入坎波斯吉拉斯，卡庞阿尔托授地的时间可追溯到1704年。亚波宿地成为索罗卡巴路上的饮水点和夜营处，赶畜人从维亚芒驱赶骡马和牛群前往索罗卡巴集市，常在那里歇脚。索罗卡巴、桑托斯和伊图的家族到此经营牧场；1751年当地建起一座泥栅小教堂，1769年加尔默罗会修士又建成另一座教堂。1771年，聚落成为圣安娜-杜亚波教区；1788年9月24日，它从库里蒂巴划出，升格为新卡斯特鲁镇，名称来自葡萄牙海外部大臣马蒂尼奥·德·梅洛·埃卡斯特罗。到1821年，牛、骡马、牧场和通往市场的长路仍决定着这里的生活。

en:
Inland beyond the Serra do Mar, wide natural clearings break the Atlantic forest of the plateau; the paulistas called these grassy flats campinas. Tupi-Guarani and Jê peoples grew manioc, maize and beans along the watercourses and hunted the intervening woods. In 1444 native trails crossed the area, and no European road ran through it for more than two centuries after ships reached Brazil.

The first regular colonial traffic followed the gold trails. In the 1720s bandeirantes from Piratininga opened routes toward the mines of Minas Gerais and Goiás, and Fernão de Camargo set up a tropeiro stopping post in a clearing called Campinas do Mato Grosso. Sesmarias were granted from 1728. A parish dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception was formed there in 1774, and in 1797 the settlement was detached from Jundiaí as Vila de São Carlos, later called Campinas. Roads built under Governor Morgado de Mateus helped sugarcane replace many provision farms. By the end of the century the district formed part of the paulista sugar country around Sorocaba, Piracicaba, Mogi-Guaçu and Jundiaí.
zh:
越过马尔山深入内陆，高原上的大西洋森林间分布着大片天然草甸，圣保罗人称之为「坎皮纳斯」。操图皮-瓜拉尼语和热语的族群沿水道种植木薯、玉米和豆类，也在相邻林地狩猎。1444年，这里只有土著小路；船只抵达巴西后的两百多年里，仍没有欧洲道路穿过。

最早稳定的殖民地往来随淘金山路出现。1720年代，皮拉蒂宁加的旗队开辟通往米纳斯吉拉斯和戈亚斯矿区的道路，费尔南·德·卡马戈在一处叫「马托格罗索草原」的草甸上设了赶骡人歇脚点。1728年起，王室开始在此分封授地。1774年，圣母无染原罪堂区成立；1797年，聚落脱离容迪亚伊设为圣卡洛斯镇，以后改名坎皮纳斯。莫尔加多·德·马特乌斯总督修筑的道路，帮助甘蔗取代了许多补给农庄。到18世纪末，这里已同索罗卡巴、皮拉西卡巴、莫日瓜苏和容迪亚伊连成一片圣保罗蔗糖产区。

en:
Araraquara covers the Campos de Aracoara, open tableland in central São Paulo where grassland and low hills rise above the gallery woods of the Tietê tributaries. In 1444 the country belonged to the Guaianás, Macro-Jê speakers whose southern farming groups are counted among the ancestors of the Kaingang. They kept gardens and hunted, fished and gathered across the campos. The name later read as Aracoara meant the dwelling place of daylight, though Portuguese writers also gave a second reading, 'lair of the macaws'. No Portuguese ranch or chapel stood between their villages and the Tietê valley.

Portuguese occupation came through cattle and one fugitive. Pedro José Neto, a settler at Itu sentenced to exile, fled with his sons into the grasslands, built a small chapel dedicated to Saint Benedict and marked out cattle claims around it. The chapel became the core of São Bento de Araraquara, which was made a parish under Piracicaba on 22 August 1817 and raised to a district on 30 October. Early estates planted sugarcane, maize, tobacco and cotton, and raised pigs and cattle. In 1821 Araraquara was only four years old as a settled parish, ranching country laid over old Guaianá land.
zh:
阿拉拉夸拉地处圣保罗中部高原的阿拉科阿拉草原，草地和低丘铺展在铁特河支流的河岸林上方。1444年时，这里属于瓜亚纳人；他们是大热语系族群，南方农耕支系被视为卡因冈人的祖先之一。瓜亚纳人经营田园，也在草原上狩猎、捕鱼和采集。这个名称后来被解释为阿拉科阿拉，意为「日光栖居之处」；葡萄牙写作者还给出另一说，即「金刚鹦鹉巢穴」。那时瓜亚纳村落与铁特河谷之间还没有葡萄牙牧场或小教堂。

葡萄牙人的占据由牧牛和一名逃亡者开始。佩德罗·若泽·内图原是伊图居民，被判处流放后带着儿子逃入草原。他建起一座供奉圣本托的小教堂，并在周围圈定牧地。小教堂后来成为圣本托-迪阿拉拉夸拉的核心；1817年8月22日，教区隶属皮拉西卡巴设立，同年10月30日聚落又成为辖区。早期庄园种植甘蔗、玉米、烟草和棉花，也饲养猪牛。1821年时，作为定居教区的阿拉拉夸拉只有四年历史，是铺在瓜亚纳故土上的牧牛边地。

en:
Serro occupies a cold, broken section of the Serra do Espinhaço near the headwaters of the Jequitinhonha. Tupi-Guarani speakers called the highlands Ivituruí, a windy, cold hill. In 1444 Macro-Jê and other indigenous groups used its ridges, creeks and upland camps; no Portuguese mine, foundry or royal road yet entered the country later called Serro Frio.

Antônio Soares Ferreira's expedition found gold along the Quatro Vinténs and Lucas streams in 1701, and the camps were formally recorded in 1702 as Arraial do Ribeirão das Minas de Santo Antônio do Bom Retiro do Serro do Frio. Governor Brás Baltasar da Silveira raised the settlement to a town as Vila do Príncipe in 1714. Diamonds later appeared around Milho Verde, São Gonçalo do Rio das Pedras and Tejuco, and in 1720 Vila do Príncipe became seat of the large Serro Frio comarca, covering northern and northeastern Minas and its diamond grounds. A crown foundry ordered in 1725 required regional gold to pass through official melting and taxation, while smugglers carried gold and stones around the guarded roads. Enslaved Africans and their descendants supplied much of the mining labour, and the African woman Jacinta de Siqueira was later named among the figures who helped found and people the town. After nearly a century of digging, mining gave way to cattle and subsistence farms. When the French naturalist Auguste de Saint-Hilaire visited in 1817, Vila do Príncipe had about 700 houses and 2,500 to 3,000 people, with churches standing above its steep slopes.
zh:
塞鲁位于埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉一段寒冷崎岖的山地，靠近热基蒂尼奥尼亚河源头。图皮-瓜拉尼语称这片高地为伊维图鲁伊，意思是多风的寒冷山丘。1444年，大热依语系及其他印第安族群使用这里的山脊、溪流和高地营地；后来得名塞鲁弗里乌的地方还没有葡萄牙矿山、熔铸厂或王室道路。

1701年，安东尼奥·苏亚雷斯·费雷拉的远征队在夸特罗温滕斯溪和卢卡斯溪一带发现黄金，营地1702年正式登记为「圣安多尼邦雷蒂鲁杜塞鲁弗里乌矿溪村」。1714年，总督布拉斯·巴尔塔萨·达西尔韦拉将其升格为太子镇。米尔霍韦尔德、圣贡萨洛杜里奥达什佩德拉斯和特茹科后来发现钻石，太子镇又在1720年成为塞鲁弗里乌大辖区治所，管辖米纳斯北部、东北部及钻石产地。1725年，王室下令设立熔铸厂，地区黄金必须经过官方熔铸和征税，走私者则绕开受监视的道路携带黄金和宝石。被奴役的非洲人及其后裔承担大量矿场劳动，非洲妇女雅辛塔·德·西凯拉也被认为是参与建城和移民的重要人物。开采近百年后，矿业让位于养牛和自给农业。1817年法国博物学者奥古斯特·德·圣伊莱尔到访时，太子镇约有700栋房屋、2500至3000人，几座教堂立在陡峭山坡上。

en:
Vila Rica, the present town of Ouro Preto, lies in a steep fold of the Serra do Espinhaço under Itacolomi Peak, where the Tripuí and other streams cut through ridges of dark, iron-stained gravel. Macro-Jê villagers farmed the valleys for generations before the gravel was found to hold gold of unusual richness. Parties including Antônio Dias de Oliveira and Father João de Faria Fialho made the first strikes in 1695–1696, and diggers poured into the hollows. These streams were prizes in the War of the Emboabas of 1707–1709, between the Paulista pioneers and the newcomers called emboabas, after which the crown merged the camps as Vila Rica in 1711. In 1720 a protest against the new smelter monopoly and the royal fifth grew into the Vila Rica Revolt; the Count of Assumar crushed it and executed Filipe dos Santos, and Minas Gerais became a captaincy of its own with Vila Rica as its capital.

The gold made Vila Rica the richest town in the colony: officially recorded exports ran to some 800 tons in the eighteenth century, and the town held about 40,000 people by 1730 and 80,000 by mid-century. Its slopes filled with baroque churches, and the Casa da Ópera opened in 1770 for opera seasons paid for out of mining wealth. The sculptor Aleijadinho was born in Vila Rica and carved its Church of Saint Francis before taking his chisels to the other mining towns, where the painter Manoel da Costa Ataíde worked in the same churches. Cláudio Manuel da Costa, author of the epic Vila Rica, and the magistrate Tomás António Gonzaga, who wrote as Dirceu, made the town the literary centre of colonial Brazil.

When the gold ran thin, the threatened derrama levy to make up the royal fifth drove officers, priests and poets into the Inconfidência Mineira of 1788–1789, a plot to break with Portugal. The plot was broken before it rose. Cláudio Manuel da Costa died in 1789, Gonzaga ended his days on Mozambique Island in 1810, and Tiradentes, the militiaman who had been its most enthusiastic propagandist, was hanged in Rio de Janeiro on 21 April 1792. In 1821 Vila Rica remained the mountain capital of Minas Gerais.
zh:
里卡镇（今欧鲁普雷图）藏在埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉一道陡峭的褶皱里，伊塔科洛米峰俯瞰全镇，特里普伊等山溪穿过发黑、裹着氧化铁的砾石山脊。大热依语族村民在这些山谷里耕种了许多代，后来才有人发现砾石中含金极富。1695—1696年，安东尼奥·迪亚斯·德·奥利维拉、神父若昂·德·法里亚·菲亚略等人的队伍首先找到矿脉，挖金者随即挤满各条山沟。这些溪涧也是1707—1709年恩博阿巴斯战争争夺的目标，圣保罗拓殖者与被称为「恩博阿巴斯」的新来者开战；战后王室于1711年把各营地合并为里卡镇。1720年，反对熔铸厂垄断和五分之一金税的抗议演成里卡镇暴动，阿苏马尔伯爵将其镇压并处决费利佩·多斯桑托斯，米纳斯吉拉斯随之分设为独立都督辖区，以里卡镇为首府。

黄金让里卡镇成为全殖民地最富的城镇：18世纪里仅官方登记的米纳斯黄金出口就有约800吨，1730年全镇约4万人，到18世纪中叶约有8万人。山坡上盖满巴洛克教堂，1770年歌剧院落成，上演靠矿业财富供养的歌剧季。雕刻家阿莱雅迪尼奥出生在里卡镇，他在这里雕成圣方济各堂，后来又带着凿子奔走于其他矿业城镇；画家曼努埃尔·达·科斯塔·阿塔伊德在同一批教堂作画。以本镇为名创作史诗《里卡镇》的克劳迪奥·曼努埃尔·达科斯塔，和以「迪尔塞乌」为笔名写诗的法官托马斯·安东尼奥·贡萨加，使里卡镇成为殖民地巴西的文学中心。

黄金渐稀后，总督为补足五分之一金税威胁征收「德拉马」摊派，把军官、神父和诗人逼进1788—1789年的米纳斯密谋，企图脱离葡萄牙独立。密谋还未举事就被破获。克劳迪奥·曼努埃尔·达科斯塔1789年死去，贡萨加在莫桑比克岛度过晚年、1810年死在那里；当过民兵的蒂拉登特斯是密谋中最卖力的鼓动者，1792年4月21日在里约热内卢被处绞刑。1821年时，里卡镇仍是米纳斯吉拉斯的山中首府。

en:
The Guaporé, called Iténez on the opposite bank, rises in the Parecis plateau and runs west through flooded savanna and gallery forest toward the Mamoré. Chapacura, Itenes, Torá and other Chapacuran villages kept gardens above the annual floods on its lower course, while Jê-related groups lived in the Branco, Mequens and Corumbiara valleys. They grew maize and peanuts, fished with arrows and fish poisons, and used canoes on the main river. In 1444 the crossings, fishing grounds and routes from the Guaporé to the Mamoré and Madeira were still controlled by those indigenous villages.

Gold and Spanish Jesuit missions later brought Portuguese soldiers to the river. Portugal created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748, and Antônio Rolim de Moura founded Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade on the upper Guaporé four years later as its capital. A small riverside post, Nossa Senhora da Conceição, went up in 1769 but could not secure the river against Spanish pressure and nearby missions. Luís de Albuquerque therefore began the stone Real Forte Príncipe da Beira in 1775, with indigenous and enslaved labour; work continued to 1783 on what Portuguese sources describe as the largest military building raised by Portugal outside Europe in colonial Brazil. Its walls covered the route by which gold and supplies moved between the Mato Grosso mines, the Mamoré and the Madeira. Fever, floods and long supply lines kept the garrison on a difficult frontier.
zh:
瓜波雷河在对岸称伊特内斯河，发源于帕雷西斯高原，向西穿过会被洪水淹没的热带草原和河岸林，流向马莫雷河。下游沿岸有查帕库拉人、伊特内斯人、托拉人等查帕库兰语族群，布兰库河、梅肯斯河和科伦比亚拉河流域则住着与热语族群相近的人群。他们在每年洪水线以上开辟田园，种植玉米和花生，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，在干流上乘独木舟往来。1444年，瓜波雷通往马莫雷河、马代拉河的渡口、渔场和航路，仍掌握在这些印第安村落手中。

后来，黄金和西班牙耶稣会传教站把葡萄牙士兵引到河边。1748年，葡萄牙设立马托格罗索都督辖区；四年后，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉在上瓜波雷建立维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪，作为都督辖区首府。1769年，河边建起小型的圣母受孕哨所，却不足以抵御西班牙人的进逼和附近传教活动。路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克于是在1775年动用印第安人和奴隶劳力，开始修建石砌的贝拉亲王皇家堡垒，工程持续到1783年。葡萄牙资料称，它是殖民时期葡萄牙在欧洲以外修建的最大军事建筑。堡垒掩护马托格罗索金矿与马莫雷河、马代拉河之间的黄金和物资航路，而热病、洪水和漫长补给线使驻军一直面对艰苦边地。

en:
Cerejeiras covers rolling ground about 45 kilometres north of the Guaporé, where the Corumbiara, Mequens and smaller streams drain south toward the border river. In 1444 Jê-related groups kept gardens and hunting grounds in those tributary valleys, while Chapacuran villagers lived closer to the Guaporé. They planted maize and peanuts, gathered Brazil nuts when they were in season, fished with arrows and poisons, and used canoes on the main river. No European post yet stood between their villages and the crossings.

The Spanish conquistador Ñuflo de Chávez, later the founder of Santa Cruz de la Sierra, crossed this side of the Guaporé valley in the 1540s; Portuguese bandeirantes entered around the 1650s. Gold on the river's right bank then drew Portuguese colonial government into the area, and the crown created the captaincy of Mato Grosso in 1748. Local history records a camp made by Antônio Rolim de Moura on this stretch of the river in 1750. Fugitive slaves from Vila Bela later occupied the place and supplied parties descending the Guaporé. The large stone Príncipe da Beira fortress went up downstream from 1775 to 1783, but it covered the main waterway and did not turn Cerejeiras's inland forests into a town.
zh:
塞雷热拉斯位于瓜波雷河以北约45公里的缓丘地带，科伦比亚拉河、梅肯斯河和较小溪流向南注入界河。1444年，这些支流河谷中的田园和猎场属于与热语族群相近的人群，靠近瓜波雷干流处则住着查帕库兰语村民。他们种植玉米和花生，按季采集巴西坚果，用箭和鱼药捕鱼，并在主要河道上使用独木舟。那时他们的村落与各渡口之间，还没有欧洲人的常设据点。

西班牙征服者努夫洛·德·查韦斯后来创建了圣克鲁斯-德拉谢拉，他在1540年代穿过瓜波雷河谷这一侧；约1650年代，葡萄牙旗队进入此地。瓜波雷右岸发现黄金后，葡萄牙殖民政府随之而来，王室于1748年设立马托格罗索都督辖区。当地史记载，安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉1750年曾在这段河畔扎营。后来，从维拉贝拉逃出的奴隶占据该地，为顺瓜波雷河下航的队伍提供补给。1775年至1783年，下游修建了大型石砌的贝拉亲王堡，但堡垒掩护的是干流航道，并没有把塞雷热拉斯的内陆林地变成城镇。

en:
Vila Bela covers the upper Guaporé, below the Parecis plateau and close to the ridges of the Serra de Ricardo Franco. Gallery woods line the river, cerrado opens around its headwaters, and fords lead from the savanna toward the Bolivian plains farther west. In 1444 Sararé, Kabixi and other Nambikwara bands moved between the Guaporé and Juruena headwaters, hunting, gathering and shifting camp through forest and grassland; Chiquitano peoples held the plains beyond the western ridges. The river carried canoes and supplied fish, but no Portuguese town, tax post or garrison controlled the valley.

Gold parties entered the valley in 1733-34. In 1742 Manuel Félix de Lima followed the Guaporé, Madeira and Amazon all the way to Belém, opening the long water route that supplied the remote mines. Diamonds were found in Mato Grosso in 1747, and the Portuguese Crown created a separate captaincy the next year. Its first governor, Antônio Rolim de Moura, founded Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade on 19 March 1752 as the seat of government. His officials collected the mining tax, treated with Indigenous groups, expelled Spanish missionaries and opened roads toward Bahia and Maranhão while treaties with Spain repeatedly redrew the border. Rolim later became viceroy of Brazil, but Vila Bela remained a frontier capital set among mines, rivers and ranchland. In 1821 Mato Grosso became a province; after Governor Magessi was deposed, Vila Bela and Cuiabá briefly ran separate juntas.
zh:
维拉贝拉位于上瓜波雷河一带，背靠帕雷西斯高原，邻近里卡多·佛朗哥山的山脊。河岸林沿河伸展，源头周围是热带稀树草原，渡口通向更西的玻利维亚平原。1444年时，萨拉拉、卡比希等南比夸拉游群在瓜波雷河与茹鲁埃纳河源头之间移营，在森林和草原间狩猎、采集；西山脊外的平原则属于奇基托斯人。瓜波雷河可供独木舟通行和捕鱼，但谷中还没有葡萄牙人的城镇、税卡或驻军。

1733年至1734年，寻金队伍进入河谷。1742年，曼努埃尔·费利克斯·德·利马顺瓜波雷河、马代拉河和亚马孙河一直下航到贝伦，开辟了为偏远矿区运送补给的漫长水路。1747年马托格罗索发现钻石，葡萄牙王室在次年另设马托格罗索都督辖区。首任都督安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉于1752年3月19日建立维拉贝拉-达桑蒂西马特林达迪，把它设为治所。他的官员征收矿税、与原住民群体谈判、驱逐西班牙传教士，并开辟通往巴伊亚和马拉尼昂的道路；葡萄牙与西班牙之间的条约则一再更改这条边界。罗林后来出任巴西副王，维拉贝拉却始终是矿山、河流和牧场之间的边疆首府。1821年马托格罗索改省，都督马热西被推翻后，维拉贝拉与库亚巴一度各自成立政务会。

en:
The future Cáceres lies on the upper Paraguay at the edge of the Pantanal, where the river's seasonal floods spread across the grassland and boats are the only way through for months each year. The Guató, whose language has no known relatives, were the masters of this water world: they built dugout canoes, shot with the bow, and could keep alive for weeks aboard a canoe when they had to, moving in small family groups rather than villages. In 1444 the Paraguay carried only their fishing parties between temporary camps, and no European post yet stood on its banks.

The river was also the artery that joined the gold towns of Cuiabá and Vila Bela to São Paulo by way of the Paraguay and Paraná, and the long voyage upstream was exposed to Spanish patrols and indigenous raids. After Spain and Portugal fixed their South American frontier in the Treaty of Madrid of 1750, a limestone marker carved in Lisbon was freighted out in pieces and planted on the bank of the Jauru, a Paraguay tributary, on 18 January 1754 by Antônio Rolim de Moura Tavares, first governor of Mato Grosso. The border still needed a garrison: on 6 October 1778 the dragoon Antônio Pinto Rego e Carvalho founded Vila Maria do Paraguai by order of Governor Luís de Albuquerque de Melo Pereira e Cáceres. Sixty Indians brought from the Spanish missions of Chiquitos were among the first settlers, and a chapel dedicated to Saint Louis faced the river. By 1809 the presidio held a royal warehouse of arms, tools and boat gear, serving Cuiabá and Vila Bela as a small armed river port.
zh:
后来的卡塞雷斯位于巴拉圭河上游、潘塔纳尔沼泽边缘；每年有好几个月，河水漫上草原，船只成了唯一能穿行的交通工具。瓜托人的语言与任何已知语言都没有亲缘关系，他们是这片水乡的主人：会造独木舟、射术精准，必要时能在船上生活数周，平时以小型家族群体活动，不聚居成大型村落。1444年时，巴拉圭河上只有他们往来渔场和临时营地的独木舟，河岸上还没有任何欧洲人的据点。

巴拉圭河也是库亚巴、维拉贝拉的金镇与圣保罗之间的通道，船队经巴拉圭河与巴拉那河往来，漫长的上航程要面对西班牙人的巡逻和原住民的袭扰。1750年《马德里条约》划定西葡两国在南美的边界后，一块在里斯本雕成的石灰岩界碑拆散运来，1754年1月18日由马托格罗索首任总督安东尼奥·罗林·德·莫拉·塔瓦雷斯竖在巴拉圭支流雅鲁河畔。边界还需要守军：1778年10月6日，龙骑兵军官安东尼奥·平托·雷戈·埃·卡瓦略奉总督路易斯·德·阿尔布克尔克·德·梅洛·佩雷拉·埃·卡塞雷斯之命，建立巴拉圭河畔玛丽亚镇。最早的居民中有从西班牙人管辖的奇基托斯传教区带来的六十名印第安人，河畔建起供奉圣路易的小堂。到1809年，这座要塞设有储存武器、工具和船具的皇家仓库，是库亚巴和维拉贝拉的一座小型武装河港。

en:
Diamantino lies on the broken southern edge of the Parecis plateau, on the line dividing two of South America's great river systems: its southern streams descend to the Paraguay and the Plate, while the Arinos carries the northern waters to the Amazon. Pareci (Haliti), Arino and neighbouring peoples moved through this cerrado and gallery-forest country by canoe, hunting and fishing along the watercourses. In 1444 the gravel of the streams had never been panned by a Portuguese miner, and the plateau was an indigenous borderland between the Amazon and Paraguay worlds.

Gold brought the Portuguese up from Cuiabá: on 18 September 1728 Gabriel Antunes Maciel struck it in the Ribeirão do Ouro and reported the find, and the camp of Arraial do Ouro, later called Félix, grew around the diggings. Diamonds then gave the district its name, and the Portuguese crown answered with a diamond monopoly: workings were closed and the Destacamento Diamantino do Paraguai patrolled the streams against clandestine prospectors. The stones proved fewer than hoped and the rush ebbed, but the camp lived on as a supply point, its boatmen, known as paranistas, running local goods north down the Arinos to Pará and the Amazon. In 1811 the parish of Our Lady of the Conception of Alto Paraguai Diamantino was created under a name that recorded a geographical mistake, the explorers believing they were near the Paraguay headwaters; a royal charter raised the settlement to vila rank in 1820.
zh:
迪亚曼蒂努位于帕雷西斯高原崎岖的南缘，正好在南美两大水系的分界线上：南部溪流向南汇入巴拉圭河、通向拉普拉塔河口，北部水流经阿里努斯河进入亚马孙流域。帕雷西人（自称哈利蒂人）、阿里努人及邻近族群划着独木舟穿行在塞拉多草原与林带河谷之间，沿水道狩猎捕鱼。1444年时，溪中的砂砾还没有被葡萄牙淘金者淘洗过，高原仍是亚马孙世界与巴拉圭世界之间的原住民边地。

黄金把葡萄牙人从库亚巴引来：1728年9月18日，加布里埃尔·安图内斯·马西埃尔在金溪找到金矿并报官，金溪营地（后称费利克斯）便在矿坑旁成形。后来发现的钻石给这一带取了名，葡萄牙王室的回应是实行钻石专卖：封闭矿坑，派迪亚曼蒂努·杜·巴拉圭支队在溪流间巡逻，缉捕私采者。钻石数量远不如预期，淘金热退去，但营地作为补给点延续下来，被称为「巴拉尼斯塔」的船工驾船把本地货物沿阿里努斯河北运帕拉和亚马孙。1811年设立的上巴拉圭·迪亚曼蒂努圣母受孕教区，名字记下了一个地理错误：探险者以为这里靠近巴拉圭河源头。1820年，王室特许状把定居点升格为镇。

en:
The Rio das Mortes, the River of Deaths, also called the Manso, rises in the Serra de São Lourenço and runs some 1,200 kilometres across the Mato Grosso cerrado to the Araguaia. In 1444 its valley was the northern edge of the Bororo world, whose villages and hunting grounds stretched from the Paraguay east toward the Araguaia. The river gave fish, fords and campsites; its banks were known to Bororo travellers, but no Portuguese had yet mapped them.

From the 1660s slaving bandeiras crossed this country, which fed one of the interior's most tenacious gold legends. In 1673 two boys, Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva and Antônio Pires de Campos, marched with their fathers' expeditions and afterwards told of Araés and the Serra dos Martírios, lands where gold lay so thick on the ground that a man could gather it by hand. In 1722 Bartolomeu, by then a veteran bandeirante, set out with 300 men to find it; three years later he came back with sixteen, having struck gold instead in Goiás. Real gold appeared on the Rio das Mortes in 1745, when Amaro Leite Moreira's party opened diggings and raised a camp named Araés, soon renamed Santo Antônio do Amarante. Poor communications with Cuiabá, failing gravel and indigenous attacks emptied it in 1789, and the other placer camps were deserted as the easy gold gave out, leaving no Portuguese town in the valley by 1821.
zh:
莫尔蒂斯河意为「死亡之河」，又称曼苏河，发源于圣洛伦索山，穿过马托格罗索的塞拉多草原约1200千米，注入阿拉瓜亚河。1444年时，河谷是博罗罗人地域的北缘，他们的村落与猎场西起巴拉圭河一带，东抵阿拉瓜亚河。河流提供鱼产、渡口和营地，博罗罗旅行者熟悉河岸，葡萄牙人却还不曾测绘这里。

从17世纪60年代起，捕奴旗队开始穿过这片地方，这里还流传着内陆最顽固的黄金传说之一。1673年，巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达·席尔瓦和安东尼奥·皮雷斯·德·坎波斯两个少年随父亲的远征队出行，回来后讲述阿赖埃斯和马蒂里奥斯山的故事，说那里地上的黄金多到可以随手拾取。1722年，已是老练旗队队员的巴托洛梅乌率三百人出发寻找，三年后只剩十六人归来，他倒是在戈亚斯找到了黄金。莫尔蒂斯河上真的出金是在1745年，阿马罗·莱特·莫雷拉的队伍开掘金坑，建起名为阿赖埃斯的营地，不久改称圣安东尼奥·杜·阿马兰蒂。与库亚巴交通困难、砂砾见了底，加上原住民不断袭击，营地在1789年走空；其他砂金营地也随易采黄金耗尽而荒废，到1821年，河谷里仍没有葡萄牙人的城镇。

en:
Iporá covers the western Goiás cerrado, the headwater country of the Rio Claro and the Caiapó, whose streams run south to the Paranaíba; its name is a later Tupi word meaning 'clear waters'. In 1444 it was Xavante country, villages of Jê-speaking hunters and gardeners set between the Araguaia and the Tocantins, with the Ofaié beyond the southern rivers. No mining camp or mule track had yet reached it.

The frontier arrived in the 1730s with two São Paulo entrepreneurs, the brothers Joaquim and Felisberto Caldeira Brant, who worked gold strikes across western Goiás. In 1748 a troop of dragoons was posted at the Arraial de Pilões on the right bank of the Rio Claro to guard the brothers' diamond workings, and the garrison ran up a barracks, the parish church of Senhor Jesus do Bom Fim and the miners' ranchos. The diamond beds were thin, and Pilões earned its keep instead as the trading post on the overland road linking Vila Boa with Cuiabá. The sertão around it stayed in Xavante hands until the 'pacification' campaigns of 1794-1798 broke the villages.
zh:
伊波拉是戈亚斯西部的塞拉多，克拉鲁河与卡亚波河发源于此，溪水南流汇入巴拉那伊巴河；「伊波拉」是后来的图皮语地名，意为「清水」。1444年这里是沙万特人的土地，说热依语的猎手和农人把村落建在阿拉瓜亚河与托坎廷斯河之间，河南更远则是奥法耶人。此时还没有采矿营地或骡道进入此地。

边疆在1730年代到来：圣保罗商人若阿金与费利斯贝托·卡尔德拉·布兰特兄弟在西戈亚斯各地开采金矿。1748年，一队龙骑兵驻守克拉鲁河右岸的皮隆伊斯营地，护卫兄弟俩的钻石矿，驻军建起营房、善终耶稣教区教堂和矿工棚屋。钻石层很薄，皮隆伊斯便改靠商站维持，扼守连接博阿镇与库亚巴的陆路通道。周围腹地仍在沙万特人手中，直到1794至1798年的「绥靖」征讨打散了各村落。

en:
Vila Boa sits in the Serra Dourada on the Rio Vermelho, a headwater that runs west to the Araguaia. The surrounding cerrado was the country of the Goiá, a Jê-speaking people who gave the whole inland region their name. They gardened maize and manioc in the gallery forest and hunted the savanna above streams that already carried the alluvial gold later comers would dig out, and in 1444 no Portuguese road had yet reached the Serra Dourada.

The town is the work of one bandeirante. Bartolomeu Bueno da Silva, the second Anhanguera (Tupi for 'old devil'), first crossed this sertão at twelve years old, riding with his father. In 1722, close to fifty, he left São Paulo to find the legendary Serra dos Martírios, the gold-bearing hills promised by that boyhood journey, and after nearly three years in the wilderness he struck rich gravels in the Rio Vermelho in 1725. Named captain-major of the mines, he laid out the Arraial de Sant'Anna in 1727; it became Vila Boa de Goiás in 1739, and he died there the following year. When the Crown created the Captaincy of Goiás on 9 May 1748, Vila Boa was made its capital. Every miner's gold went to the Casa de Fundição, the royal foundry built in 1750, to be melted into bars while the Crown took its fifth; the governor's Palácio Conde dos Arcos rose beside it in 1751, and the Casa de Câmara e Cadeia, the council house and jail, followed in 1761. As the gravels gave out late in the century, the governor Luís da Cunha Meneses planted avenues and aligned the streets, and the shrinking town settled into a quiet grid of adobe houses and baroque churches living from ranching. On 28 February 1821 the captaincy became a province, with Vila Boa still its seat.
zh:
博阿镇（Vila Boa de Goiás，今戈亚斯城）坐落在多拉达山中的红河畔，红河西流注入阿拉瓜亚河。四周的塞拉多本是热依语族群戈亚人的家园，整个内陆地区后来都因他们得名。戈亚人在林带里种玉米和木薯，在草原上狩猎，脚下河溪里早有沙金，只是要等后来者翻掘；1444年，还没有一条葡萄牙人的道路通到多拉达山。

这座城是一位旗手一手辟出的。第二位「阿年古埃拉」（图皮语意为「老魔鬼」）巴托洛梅乌·布埃诺·达席尔瓦十二岁就随父亲穿过这片腹地。1722年，年近五旬的他从圣保罗出发，去寻找传说中的马蒂留斯山，也就是少年远行时见过的藏金之山；在荒野里找了将近三年，1725年终于在红河挖到富矿。他被任命为矿区总兵，1727年辟建圣安娜营地，营地1739年成为戈亚斯的博阿镇，次年他在城中去世。1748年5月9日王室设立戈亚斯都督府，定博阿镇为首府。矿工的金子都要送进1750年建成的王家铸金局熔成金锭，王室在那里抽走五一税；都督的阿科斯伯爵宫1751年在旁边建成，市政暨监狱大厦1761年落成。18世纪末金沙渐尽，都督路易斯·达库尼亚·梅内塞斯沿街植树、裁齐道路，这座收缩中的小城便归于一片土屋与巴洛克教堂排列整齐的宁静街区，靠畜牧为生。1821年2月28日都督府改为行省，博阿镇仍为省会。

en:
Arraial dos Couros is the high cerrado on the eastern rim of the Goiás plateau, around the Lagoa Feia, whose streams feed the Paranã; close by, the Itiquira river drops off the plateau edge in a waterfall. In 1444 this was Jê country, Caiapó and Xavante bands moving through the gallery woods and grasslands between the Paranã headwaters and the São Francisco, and no Portuguese road had yet climbed onto the plateau.

It began as a toll post on the gold road. In February 1736 the Crown set up the Registro da Lagoa Feia, which taxed every load of gold carried from the Goiás mines toward Bahia and Minas Gerais. Settlers drifted up from the Arraial de Santo Antônio do Itiquira, a Paranã-valley camp thinned by killing fevers, and muleteers on the cool upland slept in leather shelters pitched beside the lagoon; the two groups formed the Arraial dos Couros in 1749, the 'leather camp', named perhaps for those tents and perhaps for the wild hides sold there. Put under the comarca of Santa Luzia, it became the chief station on the Bahia road, where tropeiros swapped leather and cattle for mining tools and salt. Through 1821 it stayed a rough waystation on the long haul between the mines and the coast.
zh:
阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯（Arraial dos Couros，意为「皮革营地」，即今福莫萨）坐落在戈亚斯高原东缘的高地，费亚湖一带的溪水汇入帕拉南河，伊蒂基拉河在附近从高原边缘跌落成瀑。1444年，这里是热依语族群的土地，卡亚波人与沙万特人的队伍穿行于帕拉南河源与圣弗朗西斯科河之间的林带和草原，葡萄牙人的道路还没有登上高原。

它起初是黄金路上的一座税卡。1736年2月，王室设立费亚湖税卡，对从戈亚斯矿区运往巴伊亚和米纳斯吉拉斯的每一票黄金抽税。居民从帕拉南河谷热病夺命的圣安东尼奥-杜伊蒂基拉旧营陆续迁来，骡夫们则在凉爽高地的湖边支起皮帐过夜；两批人在1749年聚成阿拉亚尔-杜斯科鲁斯，即「皮革营地」，得名一说来自这些皮帐，一说来自当地买卖的野皮。它隶属圣卢齐亚区，成了巴伊亚商路上的首要驿站，骡队在这里拿皮革和牲畜换取矿具和食盐。直到1821年，这里始终是矿区通往海岸的漫长驮路上一座粗粝的驿站。

en:
Conceição lies in the high cerrado of the Tocantins-Araguaia basin, above the valley of São João da Palma. In 1444 this was Jê country: small bands opened gardens in woodland clearings, hunted the grasslands and shifted camp with the seasons, while the Portuguese gold camps of Goiás still lay far to the south.

The Goiás gold rush reached the district in 1741, when the Portuguese settler Manoel Paes Andrade stopped beside a placer mine and had enslaved workers raise a house and a church dedicated to Our Lady of the Conception, which gave the place its name. The crown posted a contagem here, a counting station where travellers and pack trains bound for the northern mines were checked and taxed, and the settlement became a parish in 1755. Gold washing and cattle ranching filled its life until 1821.
zh:
康塞桑位于托坎廷斯-阿拉瓜亚流域的高位塞拉多草原，俯临圣若昂-达帕尔马河谷。1444年，这里是热依人的土地：小群人在林中空地开辟园圃、在草原狩猎、随季节迁移营地，而葡萄牙人在戈亚斯的淘金营地还远在南方。

1741年，戈亚斯淘金潮推进到这里：葡萄牙定居者曼努埃尔·派斯·安德拉德在一处砂金矿旁落脚，驱使被奴役者建起住宅和献给无玷始胎圣母的教堂，地方也得名康塞桑。王室在此设立税务站，检查前往北方矿区的行人和驮队、征收金税，1755年定居点升为堂区。直到1821年，淘洗砂金和牧牛就是这里的生计。

en:
Pontal takes its name from a point of land on the left bank of the Tocantins, in cerrado country later drawn into the mining frontier of northern Goiás. In 1444 the river and its hunting grounds belonged to the Akwẽ-Xerente and related Central Jê peoples, who kept riverside villages, fished, planted seasonal gardens and moved across ground that no Portuguese expedition had yet crossed.

Miners from Goiás opened the placers after Natividade was founded in 1734, and the Arraial de Bom Jesus do Pontal grew up as a gold camp about four years later. Mule trains carried its gold south, while the crown kept the Tocantins closed to river traffic in mining years to stop gold being smuggled out. Local tradition holds that Xerente warriors once surprised the camp and killed nearly everyone in it; the garrison post that guarded the nearby trails was named the Presídio da Matança, the Slaughter Fort, and the survivors settled at the crossing downstream that became the Porto Real. By the late eighteenth century the placers were thinning, cattle and crops mattered more, and in 1821 the old arraial was a small settlement beside the growing river port.
zh:
蓬塔尔得名于托坎廷斯河左岸的一块尖角地，所在的塞拉多后来被卷入北戈亚斯的淘金边疆。1444年，大河和沿岸猎场属于谢伦特人（自称Akwẽ）及相近的中央热依族群，他们在河畔结村、捕鱼、开辟季节园圃，往来于葡萄牙远征队尚未踏足的土地上。

纳蒂维达1734年建立后，戈亚斯的矿工来此开采砂金，约四年后邦热苏斯-杜蓬塔尔淘金营地兴起。黄金靠驮队南运，采金年代王室还禁止在托坎廷斯河通航，以防黄金走私。相传谢伦特武士曾突袭营地，几乎杀光了营中的人；守卫附近道路的兵营叫马唐萨要塞，葡语意为「屠杀堡」，幸存者在下游渡口定居，那里后来成为波尔图雷亚尔。18世纪末砂金日渐稀少，牧牛和农耕取而代之，1821年时，旧营地只是日益兴旺的河港旁一座小聚落。

en:
Natividade lies beneath the Serra da Natividade, in the southeastern Tocantins cerrado. Streams cut through the ridges on their way to the Tocantins basin, and high ground carries the driest trails between woodland, seasonal grassland and river valleys. In 1444 Xavante groups used this country for gardens, hunting camps and those ridge routes. Goiás gold seekers had not yet crossed their lands.

The gold frontier reached the serra in 1734, when Antônio Ferraz de Araújo founded Arraial de São Luiz, named for Governor Dom Luís de Mascarenhas; devotion to Our Lady of the Nativity later gave Natividade its name. Enslaved workers washed gold from the mountain streams, while mule caravans carried the metal toward Salvador. The camp became one of Goiás's largest mining settlements, behind only Pirenópolis. Enslaved builders later began the soapstone church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Pretos, and the work was still unfinished when Pohl saw it in 1819. A royal charter of 1809 made Natividade the provisional seat of the Comarca do Norte. By 1821 the richest gravel was gone, and cattle ranches were taking over the valleys.
zh:
纳蒂维达位于纳蒂维达山脚下，地处托坎廷斯东南部的塞拉多。溪流穿过山脊，流向托坎廷斯流域；高处则有较干燥的小路，连接林地、季节草地和河谷。1444年，沙万特人在这里经营园圃和狩猎营地，沿山脊小路往来，戈亚斯的淘金者还没有进入他们的土地。

1734年，淘金浪潮抵达这片山地，安东尼奥·费拉斯·德·阿劳若建立圣路易斯营地，名称取自总督唐·路易斯·德·马斯卡伦哈斯；后来对圣诞圣母的敬奉使这里改叫纳蒂维达。被奴役者在山溪中淘金，骡队把黄金运往萨尔瓦多。这个营地成为戈亚斯最大的采矿定居点之一，规模仅次于皮雷诺波利斯。被奴役的工匠后来动工修建皂石教堂黑人玫瑰圣母堂，1819年波尔见到它时仍未完工。1809年，王室敕令把纳蒂维达设为北方司法区临时驻地。到1821年，富矿砂已经淘尽，牧牛场开始接管各处河谷。

en:
Sergipe occupies the short coastal strip between the lower São Francisco and the river the Tupi called Siriîype, the river of crabs. In 1444 Tupinambá villages stood along its mangrove shores, planted manioc on the coastal flats, and controlled the beaches where French brazilwood ships later anchored. Lisbon counted the shore as part of Bahia, but Tupinambá warriors, supplied in part through French trade, kept Portuguese settlers out for most of the sixteenth century.

Cristóvão de Barros defeated the river villages and founded São Cristóvão on 1 January 1590 to secure traffic between Salvador and Pernambuco. The town took the usual Portuguese colonial form: an upper town held the parish, convents and officials, while the lower town by the water contained the warehouses and landing place. Sugar mills worked by enslaved Africans spread through the Cotinguiba and neighboring valleys, and inland ranches supplied cattle and leather. French buccaneers kept raiding for kingwood, a hardwood valued in Europe. Dutch troops destroyed São Cristóvão in 1637 and built the region's first fort during their occupation; Portuguese forces recovered the coast in 1645. Sergipe remained tied to Bahia until João VI restored its separate captaincy on 8 July 1820.
zh:
塞尔希培位于圣弗朗西斯科河下游与塞尔希培河之间，海岸线不长；塞尔希培河的古图皮语名「西里伊佩」意为「蟹河」。1444年，图皮南巴人的村落分布在红树林岸边，在滨海平地种植木薯，也控制着后来法国巴西木商船停泊的海滩。里斯本把这段海岸算作巴伊亚的一部分，但图皮南巴战士依靠同法国人的部分贸易获得物资，在16世纪大部分时间里把葡萄牙定居者挡在外面。

克里斯托旺·德·巴罗斯击败沿河村落后，于1590年1月1日建立圣克里斯托旺，用以保障萨尔瓦多与伯南布哥之间的往来。城镇采用葡萄牙殖民地常见格局：上城区安置教区、修院和官员，水边的下城区则是仓库和登陆点。使用非洲奴隶劳作的糖坊扩展到科廷吉巴等河谷，内陆牧场供应牛只和皮革。法国海盗继续来袭，掠夺欧洲人珍视的硬木王木。1637年，荷兰军队摧毁圣克里斯托旺，并在占领期间修建这一地区第一座要塞；葡萄牙军队1645年收复海岸。塞尔希培长期隶属巴伊亚，直到1820年7月8日若昂六世恢复其独立都督辖区地位。

en:
Jeremoabo lies in the dry sertão of northern Bahia, where caatinga scrub and the stony expanse of the Raso da Catarina are cut by the Vaza-Barris River. In 1444 this was Tupinambá country; its later recorded Tupi name, Yuru'mún-yba, meant the pumpkin place, the language of villagers who kept clearings, hunting grounds and trails through the backlands.

Cattle entered first, from the ranches tied to Garcia d'Ávila's Casa da Torre, the Bahian house whose herds opened up the sertão in the seventeenth century. The priests Jacob Roland and João de Barros followed in the 1660s and founded the Geremoabo mission, to catechise the villagers and protect them, and by 1698 the settlement had the standing of a julgado.
zh:
热雷莫阿布位于巴伊亚北部干旱的内陆荒原，卡廷加灌丛和卡塔里纳裸地的多石旷野被瓦扎巴里斯河切过。1444年，这里是图皮南巴人的土地；后来记载下来的图皮语名尤鲁蒙伊巴（Yuru'mún-yba）意为「南瓜之地」，出自在腹地中经营垦地、猎场和小径的村民之口。

最先进来的是牛群，它们来自依附于加西亚·达维拉的卡萨达托雷家族的牧场，这个巴伊亚家族靠畜群在17世纪打开了内陆荒原。1660年代，神父雅各布·罗兰和若昂·德巴罗斯随后而至，建立热雷莫阿布传教站，向村民传教，并为他们提供庇护；到1698年，这个定居点已取得司法辖区地位。

en:
Inhambupe lies inland of the Bay of All Saints, among rolling agreste woods between the sugar coast and the dry sertão. Its river has a Tupi name meaning 'among the waters of the inhambu', a forest tinamou. In 1444 the valleys were held by Tapuia bands, Jê-speaking hunters and gatherers called 'strangers' by the coastal Tupi peoples. They moved between riverside camps, hunting game and gathering wild fruits.

Cattle opened the country to Portuguese settlement. From the late 1500s, herds from Garcia d'Ávila's Casa da Torre, the great ranching house based near Salvador, were driven up these valleys and along the royal road into the sertão. The ranches supplied beef and leather to coastal sugar mills, while their vaqueiros traded, intermarried and took slaves among the Tapuia. Jesuits had already established a settlement at nearby Água Fria in 1562, so the early ranchers looked there for worship and justice.

A hermitage of the Holy Spirit became the nucleus of the future town. The parish of Divino Espírito Santo do Inhambupe de Cima was formed in 1718 and was serving three smaller chapels by 1757. Tobacco spread beside the cattle pastures in the 1780s, and Fernando José de Portugal, governor of Bahia, authorized a town in 1798; Vila do Inhambupe was formally installed in 1801.
zh:
伊尼扬布皮位于万圣湾内陆，地处沿海蔗区与干旱腹地之间的阿格雷斯特疏林丘陵间。贯穿此地的河名来自图皮语，意为「在伊尼扬布鸟的水畔」，伊尼扬布鸟是一种林栖鸟类。1444年，河谷属于塔普亚诸部；这些操热语的狩猎采集者被沿海图皮人称为「外族人」。他们在河畔营地间迁徙，猎取野味、采集野果。

牛群为葡萄牙人打开了这片乡野。16世纪末起，加西亚·德阿维拉设在萨尔瓦多附近的庞大牧业家族「塔楼庄园」把牧群赶入这些河谷，再沿王家大道进入腹地。牧场向沿海糖坊供应牛肉和皮革，牧人则同塔普亚人交易、通婚，也把他们掳为奴隶。耶稣会士已于1562年在附近的阿瓜弗里亚建立据点，早期牧人因此长期到那里参加宗教活动并处理司法事务。

一座圣灵小圣堂成为后来城镇的核心。1718年，「上伊尼扬布皮圣灵教区」成立，到1757年已服务于三座附属小堂。1780年代，烟草种植在牧场旁扩展；巴伊亚总督费尔南多·若泽·德·葡萄牙于1798年批准设镇，伊尼扬布皮镇在1801年正式设立。

en:
Pambu names a stretch of the northern Bahian sertão, where caatinga backlands run down to the islands and banks of the lower-middle São Francisco. In 1444 this country was held by the various Indigenous groups the Portuguese later lumped together as Tapuia. Its memory was kept by the Tumbalalá, a people historically linked to the Kariri and Procá, who trace their origin to the old mission aldeia of Pambu in the Rodelas sertão.

The bandeira of Belchior Dias founded Pambu as an Indigenous aldeia, and through the seventeenth century cattle ranges and river missions drew the Rodelas backlands into Bahia's colonial frontier. A new ranch chapel raised in 1809, Bom Jesus da Boa Morte, became one more nucleus in the same thinly peopled border country.
zh:
帕姆布指巴伊亚北部内陆荒原的一片土地，卡廷加旱地在这里延伸到圣弗朗西斯科河中下游的岛洲与河岸。1444年，这片地方由后来被葡萄牙人统称为塔普亚人的多个原住民族群占据。把它留在记忆里的是通巴拉拉人，这个族群历史上与卡里里人、普罗卡人关系密切，自认起源于罗德拉斯腹地中的旧帕姆布传教村。

贝尔希奥尔·迪亚斯的远征队建立帕姆布，把它作为原住民传教村；整个17世纪，牧牛场和河畔传教站把罗德拉斯腹地拉进巴伊亚的殖民边疆。1809年新建的邦热苏斯-达博阿莫尔特牧场礼拜堂，成为这个人烟稀少的边地里又一个定居核心。

en:
Rio de Contas occupies the upper valleys of the old Contas Pequeno, now the Brumado, where the cool ridges of the Chapada Diamantina rise above the Bahian sertão. In 1444 Pataxó bands of the Macro-Jê family moved through these mountains between the Contas and the Pardo, hunting in gallery forests and camping above the valley mists.

Cattle entered before miners. In the seventeenth century Antônio Guedes de Brito, a Bahian backwoodsman, drove herds into the high valleys. Around the middle of the century freed and runaway Africans established Pouso dos Crioulos on the Brumado, one of the quilombos beyond the reach of Portuguese landowners. By 1690 the clearing was also a stopping place on the trail carrying men and goods between Minas Gerais and Salvador.

Gold changed the district in 1710, when the Paulista bandeirante Sebastião Pinheiro Raposo found alluvial gold in the Brumado and its streams. Portuguese, Paulistas and Pernambucans rushed into the camps of Mato Grosso and Livramento. A royal charter of 27 November 1723 created Vila de Nossa Senhora do Livramento das Minas do Rio de Contas, installed the next year by Pedro Barbosa Leal; a road to Jacobina and a crown foundry for the royal fifth soon tied the mines tighter to Salvador. Fever drove the administration from its riverside seat, and in July 1746 the planned Vila Nova was laid out at Pouso dos Crioulos. Enslaved miners worked the washings until the gold gave out early in the next century, and the town returned to cattle, crops and road traffic.
zh:
里奥孔塔斯地处旧小孔塔斯河上游谷地，该河即今布鲁马杜河；迪亚曼蒂纳高原的清凉山脊在这里耸立于巴伊亚腹地之上。1444年，属大热语族的帕塔肖诸部在群山间活动，往来于孔塔斯河与帕尔多河之间，在长廊林中狩猎，在谷雾上方扎营。

矿工到来之前，先进入山谷的是牛群。17世纪，巴伊亚腹地开拓者安东尼奥·格德斯·德·布里托把牧群赶入高山谷地。约在17世纪中叶，获得自由的非洲人和逃亡者在布鲁马杜河畔建立「克里奥尔人驿站」，这是葡萄牙庄园势力之外的逃亡者聚落之一。到1690年，这片空地也成了米纳斯吉拉斯与萨尔瓦多之间人马和货物往来路线上的宿地。

1710年，圣保罗旗兵塞巴斯蒂昂·皮涅罗·拉波索在布鲁马杜河及其支流发现沙金，整个地区随之改变。葡萄牙人、圣保罗人和伯南布哥人涌入马托格罗索和利夫拉门托营地。1723年11月27日的王旨敕设「孔塔斯河金矿圣母利夫拉门托镇」，次年由佩德罗·巴尔博扎·莱阿尔主持建镇；通往雅科比纳的道路和征收五一税的王室熔金所很快把这些金矿同萨尔瓦多更紧地连在一起。热病迫使官署离开河畔镇址，1746年7月，经过规划的新镇在克里奥尔人驿站动工。黑奴矿工开采砂金，直到19世纪初金矿衰竭，城镇才转回畜牧、农耕和道路运输。

en:
Paratinga covers a stretch of the middle São Francisco, where a useful crossing cuts through the caatinga of western Bahia. Boats served riverside landings, while trails from the banks led inland through dry country; Tuxá people are thought to have predominated here, and other middle-river peoples used the islands, fishing grounds and trails. In 1444 there was no Portuguese settlement on the banks. The colonial town that later grew here was called Urubu; Paratinga is a later name.

Permanent colonization came with Antônio Guedes de Brito's Casa da Ponte, one of the largest landed estates in colonial Brazil. Cattle ranches took over the middle-river plains. The Santo Antônio do Urubu de Cima ranch became the local centre after a chapel of Saint Anthony was built in 1680, and herds rested there on drives between Bahia and the mines of Minas Gerais. The landing also handled enslaved Indigenous people and Africans brought to the estate. Its people included Luso-Brazilians, Indigenous people and Africans; the settlement became a parish in 1718 and was installed as Vila de Santo Antônio do Urubu in 1749. By the later eighteenth century it was the second-largest slave market in the Jacobina comarca.
zh:
帕拉廷加地处圣弗朗西斯科河中游，渡口穿过巴伊亚西部的卡廷加旱地。船只往来于河畔登陆点，岸上小径通向内陆；一般认为这一带以图沙人为主，中游的其他族群也使用河岛、渔场和小路。1444年，河畔还没有葡萄牙人的定居点。后来在这里长成的城镇叫乌鲁布，帕拉廷加是以后才采用的名称。

永久殖民随安东尼奥·格德斯·德布里托的蓬特庄园而来，这座庄园是殖民巴西最大的地产之一。牧场占去中游平原，圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布德西马牧场在1680年建起圣安东尼小堂后成为当地中心。往返巴伊亚与米纳斯吉拉斯矿区的牛群在此休整，登陆点也为庄园转运被奴役的印第安人和非洲人。居民包括葡裔巴西人、原住民和非洲人；聚落1718年成为教区，1749年正式设为圣安东尼奥-杜乌鲁布镇，到18世纪后期已是雅科比纳司法区第二大奴隶市场。

en:
Campo Largo, later renamed Cotegipe, was a stretch of open grassland and gallery forest on the Rio Grande in far western Bahia. The river plains were Acroá country in 1444. The Acroá spoke a Central Jê language of the Macro-Jê linguistic world, and no Portuguese town yet stood on the flats.

These lands were later included in the Casa da Ponte grant. Adventurers from Pernambuco settled the bank in the first half of the eighteenth century, planting crops and raising cattle. A flood drove them to higher ground at Alto do Umbuxeiro, where the church of Nossa Senhora Santana do Campo became the centre of Campo Largo. Ranching tied the small settlement to Vila da Barra, and in 1820 a royal charter of John VI included Campo Largo in the new Comarca do Rio de São Francisco.
zh:
坎普拉古是巴伊亚极西部格兰德河畔草原与走廊林地带的旧称，以后改称科特日皮。1444年，河畔平原是阿克罗阿人的土地。阿克罗阿人操大热依语世界中的中热依语，当时这里还没有葡萄牙人的城镇。

这片土地后来被划入蓬特庄园的授地。18世纪上半叶，来自伯南布哥的冒险者在河畔定居，种植作物、牧养牛群。一场洪水把他们逼到温布谢罗高地，圣安娜-杜坎波教堂在那里成为坎普拉古的中心。牧业把这个小聚落同巴拉镇联系起来；1820年，若昂六世颁布王室敕令，将坎普拉古划入新设的圣弗朗西斯科河司法区。

en:
Luziânia is the south-eastern corner of the Goiás plateau, the campo around the Rio São Bartolomeu where the cerrado begins its long descent toward the Paranaíba and the mines of Minas. In 1444 it held no settlements at all: Caiapó and Xavante bands of the Jê family moved through the grasslands and gallery forest, and the creek beds later turned over for gold ran untouched.

Gold came late and all at once. On 13 December 1746 the Paulista bandeirante Antônio Bueno de Azevedo, pushing northwest out of Paracatu, found nuggets in a creek and raised a cross at dawn, dedicating the diggings to Saint Lucy. The Arraial de Santa Luzia drew more than ten thousand people within a year, and Father Luiz da Gama Mendonça said the first mass there before some six thousand miners. Water was the bottleneck: in April 1758 thousands of enslaved Africans began the Saia Velha cut, a 42-kilometre canal finished two years later to feed the washings, and on 6 December 1758 the arraial became an ecclesiastical comarca. By the end of the century the gold was spent and the diggers had drifted out to cattle ranches and farms, leaving the eighteenth-century church of Nossa Senhora do Rosário above a quiet pastoral town on the Minas road.
zh:
卢齐亚纳（卢齐阿尼亚，殖民时期称圣卢齐亚）位于戈亚斯高原东南角，圣巴托洛梅乌河一带的原野上，塞拉多从这里向巴拉那伊巴河和米纳斯金矿区缓缓降低。1444年，这里没有一处定居点：热依语族的卡亚波人与沙万特人游猎于草原和林带之间，后来被翻遍淘金的溪床，当时还无人扰动。

黄金来得晚，却一下子涌来。1746年12月13日，圣保罗旗手安东尼奥·布埃诺·德阿泽维多从帕拉卡图向西北探矿，在一条溪里发现金块，天亮便竖起十字架，把矿区献给圣卢齐亚。圣卢齐亚营地一年内聚起上万人，路易斯·达伽马·门多萨神父主礼首场弥撒，在场矿工约六千人。水是瓶颈：1758年4月，数千名非洲黑奴开工开凿「旧裙」水渠，这条42公里长的水道两年修成，引水淘矿；同年12月6日，营地升为教务区。18世纪末金沙采尽，矿工散向牧场和农庄，只留下18世纪的玫瑰圣母教堂，守着米纳斯大道旁一座安静的牧业小镇。

en:
Coxim lies where the Coxim River joins the Taquari, at the line where the wooded cerrado opens into the flooded plains of the Pantanal. Caiapó and Bororó bands were its first lords; in the Bororó tongue cojim means fish, and both rivers ran full of them. In 1444 this was still Caiapó and Bororó country, known only to its own hunters and fishermen.

The place enters colonial history with the gold road to the Cuiabá. In 1719 the Lemes brothers, fleeing São Paulo, reached the new diggings by this route, and in 1729 Domingos Gomes Biliago and his partners raised the Arraial do Biliago on the bank to feed and repair the monções, the great canoe convoys from Porto Feliz. After a thirteen-kilometre portage at Camapuã the fleets launched into the Coxim and the Taquari and entered the Pantanal. Those waters belonged to the Paiaguá, and the canoe warriors destroyed convoy after convoy: they killed 400 men in 1730 and left one fleet with four survivors in 1733, until a punitive expedition destroyed one of their towns in 1734. The arraial never grew into a town; by 1821 it had dwindled to a provisioning stop for the few convoys still making the Cuiabá run.
zh:
科欣位于科欣河汇入塔夸里河之处，林木覆盖的塞拉多到这里让位于潘塔纳尔的泛滥平原。卡亚波人和博罗罗人的游群是这里最早的主人；博罗罗语中cojim一词意为鱼，而两条河都盛产鱼。1444年，这里还是卡亚波人与博罗罗人的土地，只有他们自己的猎人和渔人知晓。

此地随通往库亚巴的淘金水道进入殖民史。1719年，莱梅斯兄弟逃离圣保罗，沿这条路线抵达新发现的金矿区；1729年，多明戈斯·戈麦斯·比利亚戈和同伴在河畔建起比利亚戈村，为从波尔图费利斯来的季风船队补给、修船。船队在卡马庞经过13公里陆上搬运后，驶入科欣河与塔夸里河，进入潘塔纳尔。那一带水域是帕亚瓜人的天下，这些独木舟战士接连歼灭船队：1730年杀敌400人，1733年一支船队仅四人生还，直到1734年讨伐队摧毁了他们的一座城镇。营地始终没有发展成城镇，到1821年，它已缩成一个补给点，只接待仍走库亚巴线的少数船队。

en:
Alagoas takes its name from the chain of coastal lagoons between Pernambuco and the lower São Francisco. In 1444 Caeté villagers fished those shallow waters and planted manioc on the higher ground, while older Jê groups had been pushed inland toward the sertão. French brazilwood ships later anchored at Porto do Francês, and when Portuguese colonization moved south, this shore became the southern fringe of the Captaincy of Pernambuco.

The sugar frontier reached Alagoas along the São Francisco. Penedo commanded the wide estuary, while Cristóvão Lins founded Porto Calvo in 1570 with five engenhos. The frontier remained violent: Caeté people killed the shipwrecked bishop Pero Sardinha in 1556, and Dutch armies burned the towns after 1630 and raised Fort Maurits at Penedo. Domingos Fernandes Calabar, a mameluco who guided Dutch forces through the district, was hanged at Porto Calvo in 1635. Portuguese troops expelled the Dutch in September 1645.

Inland palm forests sheltered the quilombo of Palmares. Escaped Africans, later joined by Indians seeking refuge from the colonists, built fortified villages and exchanged goods with nearby settlers; Ganga Zumba ruled the main settlement, and his nephew Zumbi later led its defense. In January 1694 three columns of paulista and local troops under Domingos Jorge Velho overran the last stronghold with artillery. Zumbi fought on until he was killed on 20 November 1695. By 1730 the comarca of Alagoas held about fifty sugar mills, and on 16 September 1817 João VI raised it to a captaincy separate from Pernambuco.
zh:
阿拉戈斯得名于伯南布哥与圣弗朗西斯科河下游之间成串的海岸潟湖。1444年，卡埃特村民在浅水中捕鱼，在较高的地块种植木薯；更早的热依诸族则被逐向内陆旱源。后来，运载巴西木的法国船在「法国人港」停泊；葡萄牙殖民活动向南推进后，这段海岸成为伯南布哥都督辖区的南缘。

蔗糖拓殖沿圣弗朗西斯科河进入阿拉戈斯。佩内杜控制宽阔河口，克里斯托旺·林斯则于1570年建立波尔图卡尔沃和五座糖坊。这条边界长期充满暴力：1556年，卡埃特人杀死遇海难的主教佩罗·萨尔迪尼亚；1630年后，荷兰军队焚毁城镇，还在佩内杜修筑毛里茨要塞。为荷兰军引路的马梅卢科人多明戈斯·费尔南德斯·卡拉巴尔于1635年在波尔图卡尔沃被处绞。1645年9月，葡萄牙军队将荷兰人逐出。

内陆棕榈林庇护着帕尔马雷斯逃奴堡。逃出来的非洲人建起设防村落，后来又有躲避殖民者的印第安人加入；他们同附近定居者交换货物，冈加·尊巴统治主村，其侄祖比后来领导防御。1694年1月，多明戈斯·若热·韦柳率领圣保罗兵和当地军队三路并进，用火炮攻陷最后据点。祖比继续抵抗，1695年11月20日被杀。到1730年，阿拉戈斯司法区已有约五十座糖坊；1817年9月16日，若昂六世将它升为独立于伯南布哥的都督辖区。

en:
The Borborema Plateau is the rainy divide between the coastal forests of Paraíba and Pernambuco and the dry sertão. Its eastern escarpment catches Atlantic moisture and gives rise to more than a hundred rivers, including the Paraíba do Norte and Pajeú; west of the watershed the land drops into drought-prone caatinga. In 1444 Cariri, Tarairiú and Ariú bands occupied this agreste, the transitional country between forest and scrub. They farmed moist mountain hollows, hunted the drier slopes, and were old enemies of the coastal Tupi peoples. The Portuguese later grouped such non-Tupi peoples under the name tapuia.

Cattle ranches brought the colonial frontier into the highlands. During the seventeenth century vaqueiros drove herds up from the coast, and crown land grants followed the pasture.
