The French Capuchin Martin of Nantes worked among the Cariri from 1672, and around 1676 the Mission of Our Lady of the Mountains was founded among the Ararobá. Xukuru people joined it in the 1690s, and the settlement grew into Cimbres, chartered as a town on 3 April 1762. Cariri, Tarairiú and Janduí war bands resisted the ranches and punitive columns for decades in the broad cycle of conflicts later called the Barbarians' War, which lasted from the mid-seventeenth century into the early eighteenth rather than forming one coordinated confederation. In 1697 Captain Teodósio de Oliveira Ledo settled Ariú families at Campina Grande; the town became a cattle market and, in the later eighteenth century, a cotton market as well.
zh:
博尔博雷马高原是一道多雨分水岭，隔开帕拉伊巴、伯南布哥的沿海林地与干旱旱源。东麓截住大西洋水汽，北帕拉伊巴河、帕热乌河等一百多条河流发源于此；分水岭以西则转入易旱的卡廷加灌丛。1444年，卡里里、塔莱里乌和阿里乌等部落占据这片林地与灌丛之间的阿格雷斯特过渡带。他们在湿润山谷耕作，在较干旱的坡地狩猎，并与沿海图皮诸族世代为敌。葡萄牙人后来把这些非图皮人泛称为塔普亚人。

牧场把殖民边界带上高原。17世纪，牧牛人从沿海把畜群赶到山上，王室随后沿牧地封授土地。法国嘉布遣会士南特的马丁1672年起在卡里里人中传教；约1676年，阿拉罗巴人中间建立「山中圣母」传教站。舒库鲁人1690年代加入，聚落发展成辛布雷斯，1762年4月3日正式设镇。卡里里、塔莱里乌和扬杜伊战士在数十年间袭击牧场、抗击讨伐队；这些从17世纪中叶延续到18世纪初的一系列冲突后来被称作「野蛮人战争」，并非由一个统一联盟指挥。1697年，特奥多西奥·德·奥利维拉·莱多上尉把阿里乌人安置在大坎皮纳；这座城镇成为牲畜集镇，18世纪后期又兼作棉花市场。

en:
Pastos Bons occupies the chapadas of the upper Itapecuru, the dry southeastern corner of Maranhão, where open cerrado grassland runs into caatinga scrub. Its streams and gallery woods were held in 1444 by the Amanajó; the wider southern Maranhão interior belonged to Jê-speaking Timbira groups such as the Sakamekra, who moved between savannah, riverine woods and seasonal lagoons. No Portuguese land grant had yet been measured out on these grasslands.

The pastures were taken by cattlemen from Bahia and Pernambuco who crossed the Parnaíba. Around 1744 they founded a village at the Amanajó spring of Olho d'Água do Pinga and called it Pastos Bons, 'good pastures', a name which at first covered the whole sweep of open campos stretching west towards the Tocantins. The Amanajó fought the intruders. These ranches stood at the far end of a cattle frontier opened in the previous century by Domingos Afonso Mafrense, a Portuguese settler known as Domingos Sertão, who opened up the Piauí sertão and founded more than thirty cattle ranches; after he died his lands passed to the Jesuits, whose herds supplied Maranhão and the Brazilian northeast in the eighteenth century. The parish of São Bento das Balsas was created between 1743 and 1747 and its church went up in 1764, and a royal charter of 28 July 1770 raised Pastos Bons to a vila. Cattle and hides went north along the ranch trails to the coastal towns, while the General Trading Company of Grão-Pará and Maranhão, chartered in 1755, shipped enslaved Africans to the colony to work its cotton and rice.
zh:
帕斯图斯邦斯地处伊塔佩库鲁河上游台地，位于马拉尼昂东南的干燥一角，开阔的塞拉多草原在此没入卡廷加灌丛。1444年，溪涧与河畔林地为阿马纳若人所有；马拉尼昂南部内陆更广阔的地带属于萨卡梅克拉人等说热依语的廷比拉族群，他们在稀树草原、河岸林地和季节性湖泊之间往来。这些草原上还没有划出任何葡萄牙授地。

占下牧场的是从巴伊亚和伯南布哥渡过帕纳伊巴河而来的牧牛人。约1744年，他们在阿马纳若人的平加泉眼旁建村，取名帕斯图斯邦斯，意为「好牧场」；这个名字最初泛指向西一直延伸到托坎廷斯的整片旷野。阿马纳若人以武力抵抗这些闯入者。这些牧场处在一条牧牛边疆的尽头：上一个世纪，葡萄牙拓殖者多明戈斯·阿方索·马弗伦塞（人称「腹地多明戈斯」）开辟了皮奥伊腹地，建起三十多座牧牛场；他死后土地归耶稣会，会中的牧群在18世纪供给马拉尼昂和巴西东北。1743年至1747年间，这里设立圣本图-达斯巴尔萨斯教区，教堂1764年落成，1770年7月28日的王室特许状把帕斯图斯邦斯升为镇。牛只和皮革沿牧道北上沿海城镇；1755年获特许成立的大帕拉与马拉尼昂总贸易公司，则把非洲奴隶运入殖民地种植棉花和水稻。

en:
Timon lies on the Maranhão bank of the middle Parnaíba, the broad river dividing Maranhão from the lands that became Piauí. In 1444 its floodplain woods, fords and canoe crossings belonged to Timbira and Gamela villages, Jê-speaking peoples of the eastern Maranhão interior. Dugout canoes linked the villages along the river; no Portuguese ferry, road or customs point stood on the bank.

The first Europeans here were French. After Daniel de La Touche founded Saint-Louis on the coast in 1612, the Timbira and Gamela of the upper Itapecuru lived at peace with the French; when Portuguese troops from Pernambuco expelled the French in 1615, slave-raiding expeditions pushed into the interior and seized or scattered those villages. Portuguese land grants pushed cattle inland on purpose so the coast could be kept for sugar. The Fazenda Cabrobó ranch, the nucleus of Oeiras, took shape in the 1670s and became Vila da Mocha in 1712, and Piauí became a separate captaincy in 1718. In 1728 a large Timbira war party raided Oeiras itself, then the captaincy's capital. The cattle frontier kept advancing anyway, and by the later eighteenth century no Timbira groups remained east of the Parnaíba. A royal road linked Vila da Mocha with Aldeias Altas, later Caxias, and the Santo Antônio ferry, thirteen kilometres upstream from the future town, was the only settlement on this bank until 1779.
zh:
蒂蒙位于帕纳伊巴河中游的马拉尼昂一岸，这条大河把马拉尼昂同后来成为皮奥伊的土地隔开。1444年，洪泛林地、浅滩和独木舟渡口都属于廷比拉人与加梅拉人的村社，他们是马拉尼昂东部内陆说热依语的族群。独木舟沿河串联各村，岸上还没有葡萄牙人的渡口、道路或税卡。

最先到此的欧洲人是法国人。1612年达尼埃尔·德·拉图什在沿海建起圣路易斯后，伊塔佩库鲁河上游的廷比拉人和加梅拉人与法国人和平相处；1615年伯南布哥的葡萄牙军队赶走法国人，掳奴远征队随即深入内陆，把这些村社掳走或驱散。葡萄牙的授地刻意把牧牛业推向内地，好把沿海留给甘蔗种植。奥埃拉斯的前身卡布罗博牧场在1670年代成形，1712年成为莫沙镇，皮奥伊则在1718年成为单独的都督辖区。1728年，一支大规模廷比拉战队甚至袭击了已是辖区首府的奥埃拉斯。牧牛边疆照样向前推进，到18世纪后期，帕纳伊巴河以东已无廷比拉族群存留。一条王家大道从莫沙镇通往后来改称卡希亚斯的阿尔德亚斯阿尔塔斯；位于后来蒂蒙城上游十三公里的圣安东尼渡口，到1779年仍是此岸唯一的聚落。

en:
Parnaguá lies in the southern Piauí cerrado on the shore of the Lagoa de Parnaguá, the largest lake in Piauí; its Tupi name joins the words for a great river and a cove. In 1444 the camps and gardens around the lake belonged to Pimenteira, Xerente and Acroá bands of the Ge stock, far from any European frontier.

Cattle reached the lakeside after 1676, when the governor of Pernambuco granted the country out in sesmaria tracts, and the new fazendas were soon harried by Macoá and Rodelleiro raiders. The settlers answered with a fortified town in 1698, only the second founded in Piauí after Oeiras; a royal charter made it a vila in 1761. Its independence was short: a provincial law of 1816 suppressed the vila and attached its district to Corrente, so that in 1821 Parnaguá was a cattle parish on the shore of Piauí's largest lake, ruled from its neighbour.
zh:
帕纳瓜位于皮奥伊南部的塞拉多草原，滨临全州最大的帕纳瓜湖；地名来自图皮语，由「大河」和「河湾」两个词拼成。1444年，湖畔的营地和园地属于热依语群的皮门泰拉人、谢伦特人和阿克罗阿人，离任何欧洲人的边境都很遥远。

1676年之后，牛群随伯南布哥总督批出的份地来到湖边，新建的牧牛场很快遭到马夸人和罗德莱罗人袭扰。定居者的回应是1698年筑起一座设防城镇，这是皮奥伊继奥埃拉斯之后建起的第二座城镇，1761年王室诏令升为市镇。它独立的时间不长：1816年省法令将其撤销，辖区并入科伦蒂，因此1821年时，帕纳瓜是皮奥伊最大湖泊畔的一个牧牛堂区，归邻镇管辖。

en:
Grajaú sits on the river of the same name in south-central Maranhão; its Tupi name karaîá'y means 'river of the Carajás'. In 1444 its gallery woods and crossing places belonged to Timbira and Piocobjé groups, Jê-speaking peoples of the southern Maranhão interior, and the east-bank chapada later called Porto da Chapada held no Portuguese ranch or land grant. Cattle and horse ranches pushed into the region only in the early nineteenth century, and the river carried their hides to the markets of Maranhão and the neighbouring sertões.

Permanent Portuguese occupation began on 11 March 1811, when Ensign Antônio Francisco dos Reis settled his people on Manoel Valentim Fernandes's Fazenda Chapada, also called Porto da Chapada, on the east bank. The Timbira and Piocobjé across the river answered with war: in 1814 they wiped out the settlement, which then held forty people, and only six lived through it because they were away. The survivors returned in 1816, called the place São Paulo do Norte and kept a small military detachment. In 1817 the governor founded the nearby Colônia Leopoldina at Estrião Grande and posted forty line soldiers there under Francisco José Pinto Magalhães to hold the frontier. In 1821 Grajaú was still a fortified river-trade post rather than a chartered vila.
zh:
格拉雅乌位于马拉尼昂中南部的同名河畔，图皮语地名karaîá'y意为「卡拉雅人之河」。1444年，河畔林地与各处渡口属于廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人等说热依语的族群；东岸后来叫沙帕达港的台地上还没有葡萄牙牧场或授地。直到19世纪初，牧牛场和养马场才推进到这一带，河运把皮革送往马拉尼昂及周围腹地的市场。

葡萄牙人的永久占据始于1811年3月11日：少尉安东尼奥·弗朗西斯科·多斯·雷斯带人在东岸曼努埃尔·瓦伦丁·费尔南德斯的沙帕达牧场（又名沙帕达港）落脚。河对岸的廷比拉人和皮奥科贝人以战争回应：1814年他们屠灭了这座已有四十人的聚落，只有六人因外出而幸免。幸存者1816年返回，把这里命名为北圣保罗，并保留一支小型驻军。1817年，总督在附近的埃斯特里昂格兰德设立莱奥波尔迪纳殖民点，派弗朗西斯科·若泽·平托·马加良斯率领四十名线列步兵驻守边疆。1821年时，格拉雅乌仍是一座设防的河贸据点，还不是特许镇。

en:
Alcântara faces São Luís across the Bay of São Marcos, its mangrove shore and tidal channels lying between the mouths of the Mearim, Pindaré and Turiaçu. In 1444 the shore was held by a cluster of Tupinambá villages, the principal one called Tapuitapera, whose canoes fished the bay and traded along the river mouths. No European power had yet laid claim to the land.

The French were first. Daniel de La Touche made contact with the villages after founding Saint-Louis in 1612 and raised a chapel at Tapuitapera. Portuguese troops from Pernambuco under Alexandre de Moura defeated the French at the Battle of Guaxenduba, fought in the Bay of São José in November 1614, and expelled them from Maranhão the following year. Portuguese settlers occupied Tapuitapera between 1616 and 1618, and it became the seat of the Captaincy of Cumã, granted to Antônio Coelho de Carvalho and his grandson Francisco. A Dutch invasion in 1641 drove the Portuguese out and the town was abandoned. After the reconquest it was chartered in 1648 as the Vila de Santo Antônio de Alcântara, with a town hall, pillory and parish church, and the sugar mills and cotton fields went back to work. The Crown took the donated captaincy back by royal charter around 1754. By the late eighteenth century cotton grown by enslaved African labour and shipped through the bay had made Alcântara one of the richest towns in Maranhão, its planters and merchants facing São Luís across the water.
zh:
阿尔坎塔拉隔着圣马科斯湾与圣路易斯相望，红树林海岸和潮汐水道位于梅阿林河、平达雷河与图里亚苏河河口之间。1444年，海岸上散布着一串图皮南巴村落，主村名叫塔普伊塔佩拉，村人的独木舟在湾中捕鱼，沿各河口往来交易。还没有任何欧洲势力声索这片土地。

法国人最先到来。1612年达尼埃尔·德·拉图什建立圣路易斯后与这些村落往来，并在塔普伊塔佩拉建起一座小教堂。来自伯南布哥的葡萄牙军队由亚历山大·德·莫拉率领，1614年11月在圣若泽湾的瓜申杜巴战役中击败法国人，次年把他们逐出马拉尼昂。葡萄牙移民在1616年至1618年间占据塔普伊塔佩拉，这里成为库芒都督辖区的治所，封给安东尼奥·科埃略·德·卡瓦略和他的孙子弗朗西斯科。1641年荷兰入侵赶走葡萄牙人，聚落也遭废弃；收复后，1648年它获特许成为圣安多尼·德·阿尔坎塔拉镇，建起市政厅、鞭刑柱和教区教堂，糖坊与棉田重新开工。约1754年，王室凭特许状收回这座赠领辖区。到18世纪末，靠被奴役非洲劳工种植、经海湾运出的棉花，已使阿尔坎塔拉成为马拉尼昂最富庶的城镇之一，种植园主和商人隔湾与圣路易斯相望。

en:
Tucuruí covers a stretch of the lower Tocantins, above the river's final run through the Pará channels toward the Atlantic. Its Tupi name means green grasshoppers, from tukura and oby. In 1444 Asurini do Tocantins, Paracanã and Gavião groups moved through the forest, rapids and portages here; their camps and trails joined the lower river to its middle course. Whoever could use those crossings could move between the interior and the Pará delta without holding a large town.

French and Portuguese expeditions probed the Tocantins from the sixteenth century, but a fixed Portuguese post came only in 1779, when Governor Telo de Meneses founded the military colony of São Bernardo da Pederneira against the growing Itapocu confederation. The settlement was renamed Alcobaça in 1780, and work began two years later on the Fort of Nossa Senhora da Fachina, later called Nossa Senhora de Nazaré, using indigenous and enslaved labour. Its soldiers inspected river traffic, searched for gold smuggled from Goiás and Mato Grosso, and supported campaigns against nearby quilombos. Expeditions against runaway slaves and for indigenous captives also used this stretch of the Tocantins along with Baião and Cametá.
zh:
图库鲁伊位于托坎廷斯河下游，控制着河水经帕拉河水道流向大西洋前的一段河道。其名来自图皮语，由意为蚱蜢的图库拉和意为绿色的奥比组成，合指绿色蚱蜢。1444年，托坎廷斯阿苏里尼人、帕拉卡南人和加维翁人在这一带的森林、急流和陆路桥间活动；他们的营地和小路把下游与中游连接起来。掌握这些渡口，就能在内地和帕拉河三角洲之间调动人马，而不必占据大城。

16世纪起，法国和葡萄牙远征队先后探查托坎廷斯河，但葡萄牙人的固定据点到1779年才出现。为应对伊塔波库联盟的壮大，总督特卢·德梅内塞斯建立圣贝尔纳多-达佩德内拉军事殖民点，1780年改名阿尔科巴萨。两年后，法希纳圣母堡动工，后改称拿撒勒圣母堡，施工使用印第安人和奴隶劳力。守军检查河上往来，搜查从戈亚斯和马托格罗索偷运的黄金，并配合清剿附近逃奴堡。讨伐逃亡奴隶和抓捕印第安人的远征，也把这段河道与巴扬、卡梅塔一同当作出发地。

en:
Para is named after the wide tidal Pará channel south of Marajó. Portel, its chief settlement, sits among islands, igarapés and forest flats flooded by the seasonal river. In 1444 Tupinambá and other canoe peoples fished, planted gardens and carried goods between the Amazon and Tocantins systems. Their villages and landing places, rather than a European fort, controlled the route.

Portel began as Arucará, a Jesuit aldeia founded in the mid-seventeenth century by Father António Vieira, the Portuguese preacher, diplomat and defender of indigenous peoples. He settled Nhengaíba people brought from Ilha Grande de Joanes there, giving the Portuguese crown a fixed river village in waterways also claimed by Spain. On 24 January 1758 Mendonça Furtado, head of the captaincy of Grão-Pará, installed a municipal senate and raised the old mission to Vila de Portel. The post did not make the surrounding channels safe: Munduruku warriors reached the town in 1786 and killed several Luso-Brazilian residents.
zh:
帕拉因马拉若岛南侧宽阔的感潮水道帕拉河得名，首府波特尔坐落在岛屿、溪涧和会被季节性河水淹没的林地平滩之间。1444年，图皮南巴人和其他使用独木舟的族群在这里捕鱼、开辟田园，并在亚马逊水系与托坎廷斯水系之间运送货物。控制航路的是他们的村落和登陆点，而不是欧洲人的堡垒。

波特尔的前身是17世纪中叶建立的耶稣会传教村阿鲁卡拉，创建者安东尼奥·维埃拉是葡萄牙著名布道者、外交家，也曾为印第安人的权利辩护。他把从大若阿内斯岛迁来的年加伊巴人安置在这里，使葡萄牙王室在西班牙同样声索的水网中有了固定村落。1758年1月24日，格劳帕拉都督府长官门东萨·富尔塔多设立市参议会，把旧传教村升格为波特尔镇。但这个据点没有让周围水道安定下来：1786年，蒙杜鲁库战士攻到镇上，杀死若干葡裔巴西居民。

en:
Santarém occupies the high ground at the Tapajós mouth, where the river's clear water meets the sediment-laden Amazon. Long before European ships arrived, the Santarém or Tapajonic culture built riverside agricultural towns here, with populous villages and distinctive modelled ceramics. In the seventeenth century the Tapajó still controlled a long stretch of the south bank from around Juruti to Prainha. In 1444 their maize and manioc fields, fishing camps and canoe traffic made the mouth one of the stronger Indigenous positions on the lower Amazon.

The first Spaniards to pass were from Francisco de Orellana's expedition. In mid-1542 Chief Chipayo met them with Tapajó war canoes on this stretch of the river. Portuguese contact became permanent after Pedro Teixeira stopped at the Tupuliçus settlement in 1626 and opened trade. On 22 June 1661 João Filipe Bettendorff, a Jesuit missionary in Maranhão and Grão-Pará, founded Aldeia dos Tapajós and built its Chapel of Our Lady of Conception. The Portuguese added the Tapajós fortress between 1693 and 1697, placing a garrison and guns above the mouth. In 1698 the remaining Tapajó and Urucucú people were moved to the Cumaru mission, and in 1758 the Portuguese raised the settlement to town status and renamed it Santarém.
zh:
圣塔伦位于塔帕若斯河河口的高岸上，清澈的河水在此与挟带泥沙的亚马孙河相会。欧洲船只到来很久以前，圣塔伦文化（又称塔帕若尼卡文化）已在这一带建起滨河农业城镇，形成人口稠密的村落和造型独特的陶器。到17世纪，塔帕若斯人仍控制着从茹鲁蒂一带到普赖尼亚的漫长南岸。1444年，他们的玉米田、木薯田、渔场和独木舟交通，使这个河口成为下亚马孙较强的原住民据点之一。

最早经过这里的西班牙人属于弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳的远征队。1542年中，酋长奇帕约率塔帕若斯作战独木舟，在这段河道迎击他们。1626年，佩德罗·特谢拉在图普利苏斯聚落停靠并开启贸易，葡萄牙人的接触才固定下来。1661年6月22日，在马拉尼昂与大帕拉传教的耶稣会士若昂·菲利佩·贝滕多夫建立塔帕若斯村，并修建圣母受孕小堂。1693年至1697年，葡萄牙人又增建塔帕若斯堡垒，在河口高地上部署驻军和火炮。1698年，留下来的塔帕若斯人和乌鲁库库人被迁往库马鲁传教站；1758年，葡萄牙当局把该聚落升为镇并改名圣塔伦。

en:
Pirara is the Rupununi, open savanna ringed with forest at the head of the Essequibo. In the rains the rivers spread over the flat grassland and lie there as shallow lakes; a carry of a single day across the Pirara watershed joins the Essequibo to the Takutu and, through it, the Amazon. In 1444 the grassland belonged to the Macushi, Carib speakers who hunted the open country, fished the floodwaters and planted cassava on the ridges, with Arawak-speaking Wapishana neighbours to the south. Their canoes had long made the Pirara carry the road between two great river systems.

That road drew the hunters of El Dorado. Walter Raleigh, on the Orinoco in 1595, heard of a golden city called Manoa on the shore of a vast inland lake, and his lieutenant Lawrence Kemys brought back the Carib account in 1596: twenty days up the Essequibo and a day's portage led to a great water named Parime. Seasonal flooding of the Rupununi may be what the guides were describing. Jodocus Hondius put the lake and its city on his map of Guiana in 1598, and Europeans searched the savanna for both for two centuries. The country on either side of the divide began to fill in: the Dutch built Kyk-Over-Al on the Essequibo in 1616 and drew the interior trade down to the coast, while in 1789 the Portuguese officer Manuel da Gama Lobo d'Almada brought cattle and horses into the Rio Branco grasslands beyond the watershed. No fort or mission was ever raised on the Rupununi itself. In 1821 Pirara was still Macushi country, crossed by trade paths and by the remembered route to a lake that no one found.
zh:
皮拉拉地处鲁普努尼草原——埃塞奎博河源头一片被林海环抱的开阔草地。雨季时河水漫过平坦原野，积成大片浅水湖；只需在皮拉拉分水岭上陆运一天，就能从埃塞奎博河进入塔库图河，再转入亚马孙河。1444年，草原属于马库希人：这些说加勒比语的居民在旷野狩猎、在洪水里捕鱼、在高地上种木薯，南边住着说阿拉瓦克语的瓦皮沙纳人。他们的独木舟早把皮拉拉陆运道走成了沟通两大水系的大路。

正是这条路引来了寻找黄金国的人。1595年，沃尔特·雷利在奥里诺科河上听说金城马诺阿坐落在一个巨大的内陆湖畔；1596年，他的副官劳伦斯·凯米斯带回加勒比人的说法：沿埃塞奎博河上行二十天，再陆运一天，便有一片名叫帕里梅的大水。向导所说的，很可能只是鲁普努尼草原季节性的河水泛滥。1598年，约道库斯·洪迪乌斯把大湖和金城刻进他的圭亚那地图，此后两个世纪里欧洲人一直在草原上搜寻二者。分水岭两侧也渐渐有了经营：1616年荷兰人在埃塞奎博河上建起基克-奥弗阿尔堡，把内陆物产引向海岸；1789年，葡萄牙军官曼努埃尔·达·伽马·洛博·达尔马达把牛马赶入分水岭另一侧的里奥布兰科草原。鲁普努尼草原本身却始终没有立起一座要塞或传教站。1821年，皮拉拉仍是马库希人的土地，往来的只有商道，和那条通向一座无人找到的大湖的旧路。

en:
Wadai is highland country between the Lake Chad basin and Darfur: hills and dry watercourses, millet fields and cattle pastures, with water at the wells. In 1444 it was Maba, or Bargo, land, worked by clans who farmed and herded under the loose overrule of the Tunjur from Darfur. The Tunjur had swallowed the old Daju kingdom about a century before and still kept to their own cults; Islam sat at the court, while most villagers followed the older religions.

In 1635 Abd al-Karim, a Maba noble, raised the clans under an Islamic banner, overthrew the Tunjur king Daud, married the king's daughter, and built his walled capital at Ouara (Wara), founding the Kolak dynasty and tying the Masalit and Dajo to his house by marriage. For most of the seventeenth century Wadai paid tribute to Darfur, until Kolak Ya'qub Arus withheld it and defeated the invasion that followed, in a time of harsh drought. The state was at its strongest under Muhammad Sabun from 1804. His army took Bagirmi in 1805, killed its ruler and sold some 20,000 captives, then pushed south to Dar Sila and Dar Runga. About 1809 a traveller found a northern route through Ennedi and Kufra to Benghazi; Sabun filled it with royal caravans, minted his own coin, and brought in chain mail, firearms and military advisers from North Africa. When he died about 1815, rival claimants were already fighting over the wells of Ouara.
zh:
瓦达伊是乍得湖盆地与达尔富尔之间的高地，丘陵和干河床之间散布着粟田、牧场和水井。1444年，这里是马巴人（又称巴尔古人）的土地，各氏族兼营农耕和畜牧，松散地受达尔富尔通朱尔人统辖。通朱尔人约一个世纪前吞并了旧达朱王国，仍保留自己的信仰；伊斯兰教只在宫廷中流传，多数村民信奉更古老的宗教。

1635年，马巴贵族阿卜杜勒·卡里姆以伊斯兰教为号召集结诸氏族，推翻通朱尔国王达乌德，娶达乌德之女为妻，在瓦拉（Ouara）筑起有城墙的都城，开创科拉克王朝，并以联姻把马萨利特和达朱两族绑到自己的家族。17世纪大部分时间瓦达伊向达尔富尔纳贡，直到科拉克雅库布·阿鲁斯拒缴贡赋，在一场大旱中击退随之而来的入侵。瓦达伊在1804年穆罕默德·萨本掌权后最为强盛：1805年攻占巴吉尔米，杀其君主，把约两万人卖为奴隶，又向南扩张到达尔西拉和达尔龙加。约1809年，一位旅人探出取道恩内迪、库夫拉通往班加西的北路；萨本派出王室商队行走此路，自铸钱币，还从北非购入锁子甲、火器，聘请军事顾问。他约在1815年死去时，争夺瓦拉水井的各派已经打了起来。

en:
Barcelos covers a middle stretch of the Negro, a black-water river broken by islands and flooded forest on the canoe route between the Branco and the Amazon. Manau families held the right-bank landing called Mariuá, with Baré, Baniwa and other Negro peoples nearby. They fished, planted manioc and moved between riverside villages. In 1444 Portuguese soldiers and missionaries had not yet entered this stretch, and river travel remained in Manau hands.

Portuguese entry was decided by war with the Manau. In the 1720s their leader Ajuricaba used allied villages and river patrols against Portuguese shipping; after his capture he drowned on the voyage down to Belém rather than be taken there in chains. In 1728 Carmelite friar Matias de São Boaventura reached Mariuá and founded the Mission of Our Lady of Conception beside the Manau village of chief Camandri; Baré, Baniwa, Passé and Uerequena people later gathered there. Francisco Xavier de Mendonça Furtado, governor of Grão-Pará and the crown's plenipotentiary for the Treaty of Madrid boundary survey, arrived in 1754 and used Mariuá as a base for two years. The crown created the captaincy of São José do Rio Negro in 1755, and on 6 May 1758 the settlement became the town of Barcelos, first seat of the captaincy. The seat moved to Barra in 1791, returned late in the decade, and was fixed at Barra, the future Manaus, in 1808.
zh:
巴塞卢斯地处内格罗河中游一段；这条黑水河岛洲散布、洪泛林连绵，是布朗库河与亚马孙河之间的独木舟水路。马瑙人的家族据有右岸名为马里瓦的登陆地，附近还有巴雷人、巴尼瓦人和其他内格罗河族群。他们捕鱼、种植木薯，往来于滨河村落。1444年，葡萄牙士兵和传教士尚未进入这段河道，河上交通仍掌握在马瑙人手中。

葡萄牙人进入内格罗河，先同马瑙人交战。1720年代，马瑙人首领阿茹里卡巴联合邻近村社、布置河上巡哨，拦截葡萄牙船只；被俘后，他在押往贝伦受审途中跳入河中，宁死不入囚牢。1728年，加尔默罗会修士马蒂亚斯·德·圣博阿文图拉来到马里瓦，在酋长卡曼德里的马瑙村落旁建立圣母受孕传教站，巴雷人、巴尼瓦人、帕塞人和韦雷凯纳人后来也聚居于此。1754年，大帕拉总督、葡萄牙王室负责《马德里条约》划界的全权代表弗朗西斯科·沙维尔·德·门东萨·富尔塔多抵达马里瓦，并在此驻留两年督办工程。1755年，王室设立内格罗河圣若泽都督区；1758年5月6日，该聚落成为巴塞卢斯镇，也是都督区的首个治所。治所1791年迁往巴拉，1790年代末一度迁回，最终在1808年固定于后来发展为马瑙斯的巴拉。

en:
Manaus occupies the left bank at the mouth of the Negro, a little above the point where its black water meets the Solimões. Manaó and Baré villages held the banks and islands in 1444, fishing, planting manioc and passing between tributary rivers in canoes. The future Lugar da Barra had no wall or fort, but river chiefs already controlled the place where routes from the upper Negro and Solimões met the downstream channel.

Europeans first entered the Negro with Francisco de Orellana's expedition in 1542. Portugal secured the confluence more than a century later, when Francisco da Mota Falcão began the stone-and-clay Fort of São José da Barra do Rio Negro in 1669; its four guns were aimed at Dutch and Spanish rivals as much as at the river. Missionaries added the Chapel of Our Lady of the Conception in 1695, and cabins of indigenous workers and mestizos grew up beside the walls.

The fort also faced resistance upstream. From 1723 to 1728 the Manaó fought Portuguese slaving raids and conquest under Ajuricaba; after he was captured and chained for trial in Belém, he jumped into the Amazon and drowned. The captaincy of São José do Rio Negro was created in 1755, with its seat first at Mariuá, later Barcelos. Fear of Spain helped bring the administration to Barra in 1791, and after two further moves it was fixed there on 29 March 1808. In 1821 the place was still only Lugar da Barra, but its fort and governor's seat watched the main rivers of the upper Amazon.
zh:
马瑙斯位于内格罗河河口左岸，距深色河水与索利蒙伊斯河会合处不远。1444年，马瑙人和巴雷人的村落占据河岸与岛洲，居民捕鱼、种植木薯，乘独木舟往来于各支流之间。后来的巴拉地方还没有城墙或堡垒，但河上酋长已经控制着内格罗河上游、索利蒙伊斯河水路与下游通道相接之处。

1542年，弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷利亚纳的探险队率先进入内格罗河。一个多世纪后，葡萄牙为控制这处河口，由弗朗西斯科·达·莫塔·法尔康于1669年动工修筑石土结构的内格罗河河口圣若泽堡垒；堡上四门火炮既对着河面，也对着荷兰和西班牙竞争者。1695年，传教士在堡旁增建圣母受孕小堂，印第安劳工和混血居民的棚屋也在墙边发展起来。

堡垒还要面对上游的抵抗。1723年至1728年，马瑙人在阿茹里卡巴率领下抗击葡萄牙贩奴袭击和征服；他被俘并锁送贝伦受审时，投入亚马孙河而死。1755年，内格罗河圣若泽都督区设立，治所最初设在马里瓦，后来迁往巴塞卢斯。对西班牙势力的戒备促使行政机关于1791年迁至巴拉，又经两次迁移，最终在1808年3月29日定于此地。1821年，这里在名义上仍只是巴拉地方，但堡垒和都督长官驻所已经看守着上亚马孙的主要河道。

en:
Muturu covers the low channels and islands where the Xingu runs into the Amazon. Tupinambá villages used the floodplain for fishing and manioc fields, and their canoes carried forest produce between riverbank settlements and peoples farther up the Xingu or out on the main stream. In 1444 no European fort guarded the mouth, but ships entering the Amazon could use the anchorage and the sheltered routes beside the islands.

The first European post here was Dutch and known as Orange or Muturu. After 1599 its traders bartered for annatto and other inland goods, while sugar and tobacco were planted on nearby ground. Portuguese forces from Pará under Luís Aranha de Vasconcelos and Bento Maciel Parente moved against it in 1623 with more than a thousand allied native bowmen. The fort fell after two hours of fighting and was pulled down. Capuchins later gathered a native settlement at Muturu, traditionally dated to 1639; it became Porto de Moz, which the Portuguese crown raised to town status in 1758.
zh:
莫图鲁位于欣古河注入亚马孙河处，省内河汊纵横、岛洲散布。图皮南巴人的村社在泛滥平原捕鱼、种植木薯，独木舟载着林产品，往来于滨河村落、欣古河上游和亚马孙干流上的各族群。1444年，河口还没有欧洲人的堡垒，但从海上进入亚马孙河的船只可以利用这里的锚地和岛间避风水道。

这里最早的欧洲据点是荷兰人设立的，兼有奥兰治和莫图鲁两个名字。1599年后，据点商人收购胭脂树红和其他内陆物产，附近土地也种起甘蔗和烟草。1623年，路易斯·阿拉尼亚·德·瓦斯康塞洛斯与本托·马西埃尔·帕伦特率领帕拉的葡萄牙军队，在一千多名原住民同盟弓箭手支援下进攻该堡。战斗两小时后堡垒失守，随即被拆毁。后来嘉布遣会在莫图鲁聚集原住民建立村社，传统上定为1639年；它发展为莫兹港，葡萄牙王室在1758年将其升为城镇。

en:
The Suriname River rises in the rainforest and rapids of the interior and runs north across a flat coastal plain to the sea. In 1444 Arawak villages stood on its lower banks, among them the place later recorded as Torarica, while Kalina (Carib) groups grew cassava, fished and controlled the crossings and portages. Dugouts linked the river villages to the shore, and smaller Cariban-speaking peoples moved through the forest and savanna upstream. No European had yet seen the waterway.

The English entered the river in 1650 on the authority of Francis Willoughby, and a royal charter made the Arawak village of Torarica the capital of their short-lived Willoughbyland, though Paramaribo had outstripped it by the time Abraham Crijnssen's Zeelanders took the colony in 1667. Upstream, Sephardic Jews expelled from Brazil and Cayenne under David Cohen Nassy settled a savanna in 1664 and called it Jodensavanne. They built a synagogue and rebuilt it in imported brick in 1685, and the Dutch confirmed their rights to their own court and freedom of worship. Around 1700 some 500 Jewish planters on the sugar estates held roughly 9,000 enslaved people. The settlement suffered Kalina raids and slave revolts, and the French privateer Jacques Cassard extracted a heavy ransom from the colony in 1712; by the late eighteenth century barely twenty Jewish families remained. The runaways fared better upstream. After the Tempati revolt swelled the Ndyuka, the Society of Suriname made peace on 10 October 1760, recognizing Ndyuka freedom and a territory of their own deep in the forest, in return for handing over new runaways; the Saramaka took the same terms in 1762. The only earlier such peace in the Caribbean was Jamaica's, of 1738, and the Ndyuka negotiator was a literate Maroon who had himself been deported from Jamaica. Later British occupations of the coast never reached the treaty peoples' lands far upriver.
zh:
苏里南河发源于内陆雨林和急流，向北穿过低平的海岸平原入海。1444年，阿拉瓦克人的村落散布下游两岸，后来记作托拉里卡的地方便是其中之一；卡利纳（加勒比）人种植木薯、捕鱼，把持着渡口和转运道。独木舟把河畔村落与海岸连起来，更上游的森林和草原上还有较小的加勒比语族群活动。欧洲人此时还没见过这条水道。

1650年，弗朗西斯·威洛比手下的英国人进入苏里南河，后来的王室特许状把阿拉瓦克村落托拉里卡定为短命的威洛比兰首府；1667年亚伯拉罕·克莱因森的泽兰军队夺取殖民地时，帕拉马里博已经盖过了它。上游方向，1664年，大卫·科恩·纳西率领一批被逐出巴西和卡宴的塞法迪犹太人在一片草原落脚，取名尤登萨瓦内。他们建起会堂，1685年又用运来的砖石重建，荷兰当局承认他们自设法庭、自由信仰的特权。1700年前后，约500名犹太种植园主在甘蔗种植园里占有约9000名奴隶。这里遭到卡利纳人袭击和奴隶起义，法国私掠船长雅克·卡萨尔又在1712年勒索了巨额赎金；到18世纪末，只剩二十来户犹太人家。逃奴在上游的处境要好得多：滕帕蒂起义壮大了恩迪乌卡人之后，苏里南协会在1760年10月10日议和，承认恩迪乌卡人自由并在雨林深处保有自己的领地，条件是交回新逃出的奴隶；1762年，萨拉马卡人也获得同样的条款。这种和约在加勒比地区此前只有1738年的牙买加订立过，而恩迪乌卡人的谈判者本人就是一名被押送到苏里南、识字的牙买加逃奴。后来英军对海岸的占领也没有延伸到远上游缔约各族的土地。

en:
Oiapoque follows the lower course and estuary of the river once called Japoc, Wiapoco or Vicente Pinzón, along the coast between the Amazon delta and Cayenne. In 1444 Waiãpi, Galibi and Palikur families kept villages on the main stream and the Uaçá affluents, using canoes for fishing, floodplain farming and travel along the Guiana shore. The river was a route and fishing ground controlled by its peoples, not yet an imperial boundary.

European colonial attempts soon fixed on the river. Vicente Yáñez Pinzón reached the estuary early in 1500. Charles Leigh planted an English settlement named Oliveleighe in May 1604, after a voyage meant to find gold; thirty-five men and boys stayed when the Olive Plant sailed away, but mutiny and a Carib raid drove the survivors out on 31 May 1606. Robert Harcourt claimed the Guiana coast for England there in 1609, yet by 1623 the English river posts were gone. Jessé de Forest, a Walloon colonist connected with the settlers who went to Manhattan in 1623, died on the river the next year while reconnoitring for the Dutch West India Company. The 1713 Treaty of Utrecht named the Japoc or Vincent Pinzón as the Franco-Portuguese limit without settling which river that name described; Luso-Brazilian and British forces used this coast in their 1808 to 1809 campaign against Cayenne.
zh:
奥亚波基指旧称亚波克、维亚波科或维森特·平松河的下游及河口，地处亚马孙三角洲与卡宴之间的海岸。1444年，瓦亚皮人、加利比人和帕利库尔人的家族在干流和瓦萨河支流建立村落，乘独木舟捕鱼、耕作泛滥平原，并沿圭亚那海岸往来。这条河当时由沿岸族群掌握，是渔场和航路，还不是帝国边界。

欧洲人很快把殖民尝试投向这里。1500年初，维森特·亚涅斯·平松抵达河口。1604年5月，查尔斯·利建立名为奥利弗莱的英国殖民点；这次远航原本为了寻金，「橄榄树号」离开后留下三十五个男人和男孩，但哗变与来自卡宴河方向的加勒比人袭击迫使幸存者在1606年5月31日撤走。1609年，罗伯特·哈考特在此宣布圭亚那海岸归英国所有，到1623年，河畔英国据点已经消失。瓦隆殖民者杰西·德·福雷斯特曾参与组织1623年前往曼哈顿的移民，次年却在为荷兰西印度公司侦察时死在河畔。1713年《乌得勒支和约》把亚波克河或维森特·平松河定为法葡界线，却没有说明这个名称究竟指哪条河；1808年至1809年，葡属巴西与英国军队又利用这段海岸进攻卡宴。

en:
Zaraza lies where the Eastern Llanos slope into the Unare lowlands, a country of grassland, gallery woods and streams that rise in the rains. In 1444 it was Carib-speaking indigenous territory. Palenque and Cumanagoto communities later recorded near the Unare kept maize, manioc and sweet-potato fields, hunted in the woods and sometimes palisaded their villages. The meeting of the Unare and Quebrada Honda, later called El Batey, stood where plains tracks joined routes toward eastern Venezuela, but the ground then held camps and fields rather than a Spanish town.

Miguel de Urbés, a lieutenant of Joan Orpí, used that junction in 1645 when he founded San Miguel de la Nueva Tarragona del Batey, named for Tarragona in Catalonia. Governor Gregorio de Castellar authorized it on 22 April 1646, but the town lasted only a few years. Ranching brought the place back after Carlos del Peral bought the García lands in 1740 and formed the Chaguaramal del Batey estate. In May 1760 the Andalusian Capuchin Anselmo Isidro de Ardales founded nearby Santo Tomás de Tucupío for Palenque and Cumanagoto people. A parish followed in 1779, and Bishop Mariano Martí's 1783 visit recorded 1,607 people around estates producing cotton, rice, maize, plantains, wheat, cassava and cattle. During the independence war Chaguaramal supported the Crown until Pedro Zaraza's republicans occupied and burned it in 1816. On 2 December 1817 Miguel de la Torre marched by night against Zaraza near La Hogaza. The royalist line withstood three cavalry charges and then scattered the patriot infantry; Guillermo Palacios Bolívar, Simón Bolívar's nephew, was killed in the fight.
zh:
萨拉萨位于东亚诺斯草原向乌纳雷低地倾斜之处，草原、林带和雨季涨水的溪流交错。1444年，这里是加勒比语族群的土地。后来在乌纳雷河附近留下记载的帕伦克人和库马纳戈托人种植玉米、木薯和甘薯，在林中狩猎，有时还会给村落设置木栅。乌纳雷河与翁达溪交汇处后来称作巴特伊，草原小路在此接上通往委内瑞拉东部的道路，但当时这里只有营地和农田，没有西班牙城镇。

1645年，霍安·奥尔皮的副官米格尔·德·乌尔韦斯利用这个河口路口，建立圣米格尔·德拉新塔拉戈纳·德尔巴特伊，地名取自加泰罗尼亚的塔拉戈纳；总督格雷戈里奥·德·卡斯特利亚尔于1646年4月22日批准建城，但城镇只维持了几年。1740年，卡洛斯·德尔佩拉尔购有加西亚土地，建立查瓜拉马尔·德尔巴特伊庄园，畜牧业让此地重新发展。1760年5月，安达卢西亚嘉布遣会修士安塞尔莫·伊西德罗·德·阿达莱斯在附近为帕伦克人和库马纳戈托人建立图库皮奥的圣多马村。1779年堂区设立，马里亚诺·马蒂主教1783年巡访时记录周围有1607人，庄园出产棉花、稻米、玉米、香蕉、小麦、木薯和牛。独立战争中，查瓜拉马尔支持王室，1816年被佩德罗·萨拉萨的共和军占领并焚毁。1817年12月2日，米格尔·德拉托雷乘夜进军，在拉奥加萨附近袭击萨拉萨所部。保王军战线挡下三次骑兵冲锋，随后打散共和军步兵；西蒙·玻利瓦尔的外甥吉列尔莫·帕拉西奥斯·玻利瓦尔战死。

en:
Chichas is the rugged southern country of the Chicha people, where the Potosí highlands break into the dry red valleys of Tupiza, Talina and the Angostura river. Chicha farmers kept towns and high pastures along the Inca road, and Tupiza was remembered as their chief place. In 1444 these valleys stood just beyond the Inca frontier, on the southern edge of the Pacajes highland world, astride the road from Upper Peru to Tarija and the Puna de Atacama.

Inca armies under Túpac Inca Yupanqui conquered the valleys around 1478 and folded them into Qullasuyu. The state moved whole Chicha communities about as mitimaes: some were sent as far north as newly conquered Ecuador, others to the Calchaquí valleys, the Humahuaca gorge and the Loa river, to hold the frontier against the warlike Chiriguanos of the Gran Chaco. Diego de Almagro's expedition entered Tupiza late in 1535, regrouped in the Chicha settlements until January 1536, and then pushed on south toward Chile. The district entered the Viceroyalty of Peru in 1542 and passed to the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. On 7 November 1810, 25 kilometres south of Tupiza at Suipacha, the army sent from Buenos Aires under Balcarce and Castelli, together with the Chicha caudillo Pedro Arraya and his cavalry, beat a royalist force for the first patriot victory in Upper Peru; the Buenos Aires junta struck a badge for the men that read 'The Fatherland to the victors of Tupiza'. The road south stayed a battleground until the war ran beyond 1821.
zh:
奇查斯是奇查人崎岖多山的南部故土，波托西高原在这里跌入图皮萨、塔林纳和安戈斯图拉河一带干旱泛红的谷地。奇查农人沿印加大道经营城镇和高山牧场，图皮萨是他们留名的首要城镇。1444年时，这些谷地还在印加疆界之外，处在帕卡赫斯高原世界的南缘，压住上秘鲁通往塔里哈和阿塔卡马高原的道路。

图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的印加军队约在1478年征服这些谷地，将其并入科利亚苏尤。印加国家把整支整支的奇查群落当作米蒂马埃斯调走：一些人被北送到新征服的厄瓜多尔填补人口，另一些人被送往卡尔查基谷地、乌马瓦卡峡谷和洛阿河谷，镇守边疆，抵挡大查科好战的奇里瓜诺人。1535年末，迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗的远征队进入图皮萨，在奇查人的聚落里休整到1536年1月，随后继续南下前往智利。这一地区1542年划入秘鲁总督辖区，1776年改属新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。1810年11月7日，在图皮萨以南25公里的苏伊帕查，巴尔卡斯和卡斯特利率领的布宜诺斯艾利斯援军，会同奇查人首领佩德罗·阿腊亚和他的骑兵，击败一支保王军，赢得爱国者在上秘鲁的第一场胜仗；布宜诺斯艾利斯执政委员会为参战者颁发勋章，上刻「祖国属于图皮萨的胜利者」。通往南方的大道仍是战场，战事一直打到1821年以后。

en:
Choquechaca, the Spanish spelling of Colquechaca, 'silver bridge' in Quechua, is the cold mining country of the Chayanta, a spread of valleys and passes lying more than 4,000 metres up in the mountains north of Potosi. Aymara-speaking ayllus herded llamas there and worked small veins of metal. In 1444 the district lay beyond the Inca frontier: Tupac Inca Yupanqui's campaigns at the end of the century folded Chayanta into Collasuyu and its warriors marched in the Inca armies, while Guarani Chiriguanos kept raiding up from the eastern lowlands.

Under Spanish rule the Chayanta became one of the great silver districts of Upper Peru. The mines of Aullagas and Hankonasa were ranked with Porco and Potosi, worked by mita levies from the surrounding communities and by yanaconas, with Spanish, Portuguese and German miners among their owners and overseers. Around the San Miguel vein, held in the eighteenth century by a Portuguese named Francisco Amaral, grew the town of Colquechaca, whose houses climbed to more than 4,000 metres; records show the town in existence by 1746. In 1776 the province passed with the Audiencia of Charcas to the new Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata.

The province entered the Andean rebellions through one of its own caciques. Tomas Katari, born about 1740 in the ayllu of Macha, walked to Buenos Aires in 1778 to protest that a Spaniard had seized his office and his people's tribute; the corregidor jailed him on his return, and armed communities freed him by force. The rising he led overran Chayanta, and when a patrol took him near Aullagas and killed him at the Chataquilla pass on 15 January 1781, his brothers Damaso and Nicolas carried the revolt on to Challapata and Chuquisaca while his wife Kurusa Yawi led its fighters, in step with the risings of Tupac Amaru at Cuzco and Tupac Katari at La Paz. Royalist troops crushed the movement and executed its leaders. After 1809 the mining province changed hands again and again: Manuel Belgrano's defeat at Ayohuma on 14 November 1813 left Upper Peru to the royalist armies, though irregular bands in these mountains kept the war alive as it entered 1821.
zh:
卓奎查卡是西班牙人对科尔克查卡的拼法，克丘亚语意为「银桥」，指波托西北方海拔4000米以上查扬塔的高寒矿乡：山谷与山口之间，艾马拉语村社放牧美洲驼，开采零星矿脉。1444年时这一带还在印加边界之外：15世纪末图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的远征把查扬塔并入科利亚苏尤，当地战士随印加军队出征，瓜拉尼人的奇里瓜诺分支则不断从东部低地北上袭扰。

西班牙统治时期，查扬塔成为上秘鲁最重要的银矿区之一。奥亚加斯和安科纳萨的银矿被认为可与波尔科、波托西比肩，矿工既有周边村社摊派的米塔劳力，也有亚纳科纳人，矿主和监工里则有西班牙人、葡萄牙人和德意志人。科尔克查卡镇围绕圣米格尔矿脉发展，18世纪时这座矿为葡萄牙人弗朗西斯科·阿马拉尔所有，房舍一直建到海拔4000多米处，殖民档案1746年已有这个定居点的记载。1776年，查扬塔随查尔卡斯检审庭划归新设的拉普拉塔总督辖区。

把这个省卷进安第斯大起义的，是本地出身的酋长。托马斯·卡塔里约1740年生于马查村社，1778年为抗议西班牙人篡夺其酋长职位、侵吞村社贡赋，步行前往布宜诺斯艾利斯申诉；回乡后省督将他下狱，武装村社以武力把他救出。他领导的起义席卷查扬塔，1781年1月15日，巡逻队在奥亚加斯附近抓获他并在查塔基利亚山口将他杀害，其弟达马索和尼古拉斯把起义推进到查亚帕塔和丘基萨卡，妻子库鲁萨·亚维（Kurusa Yawi）也接过起义队伍的指挥，与库斯科的图帕克·阿马鲁二世、拉帕斯的图帕克·卡塔里大起义南北相应。保王军最终镇压了起义，处死领袖。1809年以后，这片矿区反复易手：1813年11月14日贝尔格拉诺在阿约乌马战败，上秘鲁重归保王军，但山间的非正规武装把战斗一直坚持到1821年战争末期。

en:
The broken highlands north of Potosi, cold valleys and plains lying between La Paz, Oruro and Cochabamba, were the homeland of the Charcas, who called themselves Qhara Qhara and kept the capital of their confederation at Sacaca. They were Aymara-speaking warriors, trading with their neighbours and beating off Chiriguano raiders from the eastern lowlands, and in 1444 they lived under their own lords, free of the Incas. Tupac Inca Yupanqui's armies invaded at the end of the century; the Charcas took arms and lost several battles before their elders and the chief Copacatiraca persuaded the people to submit. The Incas prized them as soldiers, and Wayna Capac levied great numbers for his northern campaigns.

The first European known to have reached them was the Portuguese Aleixo Garcia, who crossed the country about 1520 with a great band of Guarani in search of the Sierra de la Plata, a mountain said to be made of silver. In 1538 Gonzalo Pizarro entered the highlands and the Charca lord Consara made friends with the Spaniards and showed them the silver of Porco, the first step toward the riches of Potosi. The colonial district of Charcas then supplied the mita drafts that kept the Cerro Rico working; the Indian Juan Ayaviri of Sacaca later wrote to the king of Spain, asking to be acknowledged as a noble and to live as a hidalgo, reminding the crown that his family had never failed to send men to the mountain. Its mining camps were caught up in the long feud between the Basque Vascongados and the creole Vicunas, and in 1617 Jose Alonso de Ibanez led the Vicuna rising at Potosi and was executed. In 1776 the district passed to the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, and in the wars after 1809 royalist and patriot armies marched its roads between Oruro, Cochabamba and Potosi; as the war entered 1821 these highlands were still held by royalist troops.
zh:
波托西北方这片崎岖高地处在拉帕斯、奥鲁罗和科恰班巴之间，由寒冷的山谷与高原组成，是自称卡拉卡拉（Qhara Qhara）的查尔卡人的故土，联盟首府设在萨卡卡。他们是说艾马拉语的武士，既与邻族通商，也抵御东部低地奇里瓜诺人的袭扰；1444年时仍在自己的首领治理下，不受印加统治。15世纪末图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的大军入侵，查尔卡人拿起武器，连遭败绩之后，长老和首领科帕卡蒂拉卡才说服族人归附，此地被设为科利亚苏尤的一个省。印加人极为看重查尔卡士兵，瓦伊纳·卡帕克曾把他们大量征往北方战场。

已知最早到达这里的欧洲人是葡萄牙冒险家阿莱霍·加西亚：约1520年，他带着一大群瓜拉尼人穿越此地，寻找传说中由白银堆成的「白银山脉」。1538年贡萨洛·皮萨罗进入高地，查尔卡首领孔萨拉与西班牙人交好，向他们指明波尔科的银矿，这成了通往波托西财富的第一步。殖民时期的查尔卡斯辖区随后承担米塔摊派，持续为里科山输送劳力；萨卡卡的印第安人胡安·阿亚维里后来致信西班牙国王，要求承认他的贵族身份、准许他像西班牙绅士一样行事，并称他的家族从未少给里科山送过人。各矿营随后卷入巴斯克人的「巴斯孔加多斯」与克里奥尔人的「比库尼亚斯」之间漫长的派系仇杀；1617年，何塞·阿隆索·德·伊瓦涅斯在波托西领导比库尼亚派起事，事败被处死。1776年这一地区划归拉普拉塔总督辖区；1809年以后的战争中，保王军与爱国军反复在奥鲁罗、科恰班巴与波托西之间的道路上行军，到1821年战争进入末期，这片高地仍握在保王军手中。

en:
The Chachapoyas, whom the Incas called the 'warriors of the clouds', farmed the cloud-forest slopes above the Utcubamba River, terracing the hillsides and living in round stone houses. Their strongest place was Kuelap, on a limestone ridge above the valley: a walled settlement almost six hundred metres long, its outer walls reaching nineteen metres, with room for perhaps three thousand people and separate quarters for rites, storage and dwelling. Their dead lay in the cliffs of the same country. At Karajia human-shaped sarcophagi stand two and a half metres tall in the ravine face, and at Revash house-like mausoleums were built into the limestone of Cerro Carbon. No single king ruled the valleys; local chiefs governed on their own. In 1444 the land was still independent, a fortified farming country between the Andes and the Amazon.

Tupac Inca Yupanqui's armies took the country around 1470, campaigning through Pias and Levanto, where the Incas raised a military bastion. The Chachapoyas revolted twice under Huayna Capac, and the Incas answered by moving numbers of them away as mitma settlers and planting colonies of outsiders in their valleys. In the war between Huascar and Atahualpa their loyalties were split when the Spaniards reached them. Alonso de Alvarado entered the region in 1535, when epidemic and factional fighting had thinned the people, and founded San Juan de la Frontera de los Chachapoyas on 5 September 1538, later moved to its present site. The reductions gathered the survivors into new towns, and from about 1570 Kuelap stood empty, its walls overtaken by forest. Pedro Cieza de Leon, who saw the Chachapoyas in those years, wrote that they were the whitest and most handsome people he had met in the Indies, and that their women were taken to the Incas' Sun Temple at Cuzco. On 6 June 1821 a patriot force beat royalist troops from Moyobamba at Higos Urco and swore the land free.
zh:
查查波亚人被印加人叫作「云中武士」，在乌特库班巴河上游的云雾林坡地上开垦梯田，居住圆形石屋。他们最险要的据点是俯瞰河谷的库埃拉普：围城墙垣沿石灰岩山脊绵延近六百米，外墙最高达十九米，城中可容约三千人，分设祭祀、仓储和居住的房舍。死者安葬在同一片乡野的悬崖上：卡拉希亚的人形石棺高二米半，立在峡谷崖壁间；雷瓦什的屋形陵墓凿进卡尔邦山的石灰岩壁。这些谷地没有共主，各由地方首领分治。1444年，它仍是安第斯山脉与亚马孙雨林之间一片独立的高地农乡，凭垒寨自保。

约1470年，图帕克·印卡·尤潘基的军队经皮亚斯和莱万托征服此地，并在莱万托修筑军事据点。瓦伊纳·卡帕克在位时查查波亚人两度反叛，印加人把大批人作为米特马迁出，又把外来垦殖者安插进他们的谷地。瓦斯卡尔与阿塔瓦尔帕内战期间西班牙人到达，当地的效忠已经分裂。1535年阿隆索·德·阿尔瓦拉多进入这一地区，当时疫病和派系仇杀已使人口大减；1538年9月5日他建立圣胡安·德拉弗龙特拉·德·洛斯查查波亚斯，城址后来迁到今地。集居政策把幸存者并进新城镇，库埃拉普约自1570年起空无一人，城墙没入林莽。谢萨·德·莱昂在那些年里见过查查波亚人，写道他们是自己在西印度群岛所见过最白皙、最俊美的人，查查波亚女子还被送往库斯科的太阳神庙。1821年6月6日，爱国者在伊戈斯乌尔科击败来自莫约班巴的保王军，宣誓这片土地自由。

en:
The Ucayali begins where the Tambo and Urubamba rivers meet, then runs north through rainforest flooded for part of each year. Pano-speaking Shipibo, Conibo and Shetebo communities occupied its banks, oxbow lakes and tributaries, while Piro or Yine people of the Maipurean family lived on the upper reaches and along the Urubamba. Canoes linked garden clearings, fishing camps and hunting grounds used by villages that answered to no highland state. In 1444 Inca armies had not subdued this lowland forest. Ucayali was neither a province nor a town but a network of autonomous river settlements divided among Pano and Maipurean languages.

Spanish contact came mainly through missionaries. Franciscans and Jesuits entered from the mid-seventeenth century and built reductions between the Ucayali and the Perené, but epidemics, flight and armed resistance kept those villages fragile. The resistance found a leader in Juan Santos Atahualpa, a Jesuit-educated man from Cuzco who claimed to be Atahualpa returned. Beginning in 1742, Asháninka, Yanesha, Shipibo, Piro and Quechua fighters destroyed or forced the evacuation of 23 missions; in 1752 they held Andamarca for three days before withdrawing into the forest. Spanish expeditions failed to bring the central jungle back under control. The royal order of 15 July 1802 created the General Command of Maynas and directed garrisons toward the frontier with Portuguese Brazil, yet in 1821 most Ucayali villages still had little part in either viceregal or independent government.
zh:
乌卡亚利河由坦博河与乌鲁班巴河汇合而成，向北穿过每年定期泛滥的雨林。说帕诺语的希皮博、科尼博和谢特博群体住在河岸、牛轭湖和支流旁；属于马伊普雷语族的皮罗（又称伊内）人则活动于上游和乌鲁班巴河流域。独木舟把各村使用的林间农地、渔场和猎场连接起来，这些村落不听命于任何高地国家。1444年，印加军队尚未征服低地雨林。这里没有行省或城镇，只有由自治河畔聚落组成的网络，各群体分属帕诺语和马伊普雷语族。

西班牙人主要通过传教士进入这里。17世纪中叶以后，方济各会和耶稣会先后在乌卡亚利河与佩雷内河之间建立集居村，但疫病、逃亡和武装抵抗使这些村落一直脆弱。起义领袖胡安·桑托斯·阿塔瓦尔帕是库斯科人，曾受耶稣会教育，自称阿塔瓦尔帕转世。1742年起，阿沙宁卡、亚内沙、希皮博、皮罗和克丘亚战士摧毁或迫使西班牙人撤离23座传教站；1752年，他们攻占安塔马尔卡三天，随后退回丛林。西班牙远征军未能恢复对中央丛林的控制。1802年7月15日，国王诏令设立迈纳斯军政区，命令在朝向葡属巴西的边疆设置驻军；但到1821年，乌卡亚利大多数河畔村落仍同总督辖区和独立政府都没有多少关系。

en:
The future port of Yurimaguas lies in low rainforest around the lower Huallaga, where the Paranapura and Shanusi join its river system. In 1444 no town bore that name. Shawi or Chayahuita canoes used the Paranapura, Cahuapanas, Sillay, Supayacu and Shanusi, and Muniche communities lived on the lower Paranapura. Their villages combined fishing, hunting, riverside gardens and canoe-borne exchange beyond the Inca frontier. The Yurimagua people, whose migrants later gave the settlement its name, still lived far to the east between the Napo and Negro rivers.

The Jesuit Mainas missions began in 1638 and reached this river network in 1654, when Chayahuita, Jebero and Muniche people were gathered into a reduction where epidemics took a heavy toll. Samuel Fritz, a Bohemian Jesuit who worked among the Omagua and Yurimagua from 1686, founded 38 reductions between the Napo and Negro and in 1707 completed a map that traced the Amazon from the Marañón. Brazilian slave raiders had attacked those missions since the 1690s, so Fritz led surviving Yurimagua westward and founded Santa María de las Nieves de Yurimaguas at the Shanusi and Paranapura confluence on 8 December 1709. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 many residents dispersed, while Franciscans took over part of the mission network. In 1802 the territory was placed in the General Command of Maynas; by 1821 the river settlement remained a thinly held viceregal frontier post.
zh:
后来成为河港尤里马瓜斯的地方，位于瓦亚加河下游低地雨林，帕拉纳普拉河和沙努西河在这一带汇入河水网络。1444年还没有同名城镇。沙维（查亚维塔）人的独木舟往来于帕拉纳普拉、卡瓦帕纳斯、锡亚伊、苏帕亚库和沙努西等河，穆尼切人群体住在帕拉纳普拉河下游。各村落以捕鱼、狩猎、河畔园地和独木舟交换为生，远在印加边疆之外。后来把名称带给这座城镇的尤里马瓜人，当时仍住在东方遥远的纳波河与内格罗河之间。

耶稣会的迈纳斯传教事业始于1638年，并在1654年伸入这一河网；查亚维塔人、赫贝罗人和穆尼切人被集中到一座集居村，疫病使聚居人口大量死亡。波希米亚耶稣会士萨穆埃尔·弗里茨自1686年起在奥马瓜人和尤里马瓜人中传教。他在纳波河与内格罗河之间建立38座集居村，并于1707年完成一幅以马拉尼翁河为源头描绘亚马孙河的地图。自1690年代起，巴西捕奴者不断袭击这些传教村，弗里茨于是带领幸存的尤里马瓜人西迁，于1709年12月8日在沙努西河与帕拉纳普拉河汇合处建立圣玛利亚·德·拉斯·涅韦斯·德·尤里马瓜斯。1767年耶稣会被驱逐后，许多居民离散，部分传教网络交给方济各会。1802年，王室把该地划入迈纳斯军政区；到1821年，这座河畔聚落仍是总督辖区控制薄弱的边疆据点。

en:
Quillacas is the high Aymara plateau around the southern shore of Lake Poopo, where the pasturelands of the Oruro plateau run into the arid caravan country that falls away toward the Atacama desert. After Tiwanaku declined, the Quillacas and their Caranga neighbours were among the Aymara lordships of the altiplano, their communities ruled by two paired lords and their llama caravans working the mountain roads between the lake country, the Pacajes lands and the southern oases. In 1444 Inca armies had not yet reached the lake and the Quillacas lived under their own chiefs. The conquest came in the later fifteenth century, when Quillaca became a huamani, one of the twenty-eight provinces of Inca Collasuyu.

After 1545 the silver of Potosi fixed the province's lot. Its communities were assessed for the mita, and every year parties of Quillaca men walked the plateau roads to labour in the Cerro Rico; by 1581 Potosi had a church of San Sebastian set aside for Quillacas mitayos. Those same roads carried llama trains between Oruro, Potosi, Chichas and Atacama, and at Quillacas itself the Spaniards built a colonial church and sanctuary around which the settlement of Santuario de Quillacas grew.
zh:
基亚卡斯位于波波湖南缘的艾马拉高原，奥鲁罗高原的牧场在这里伸入通向阿塔卡马沙漠的干旱商队地带。蒂亚瓦纳科衰落之后，基亚卡人与相邻的卡兰加人同属高原上的艾马拉诸领地，村社由两位并立的首领治理，美洲驼队往来于湖区、帕卡赫斯之地与南部绿洲之间的山路。1444年时印加军队尚未到达湖畔，基亚卡人仍由自己的酋长管辖。15世纪后期印加征服此地，基亚卡斯成为瓦马尼，即印加科利亚苏尤二十八省之一。

1545年波托西发现银矿后，这个省的命运便系于里科山：各村社被摊派米塔徭役，每年都有一队队基亚卡男子沿高原山路前往矿场服役，到1581年，波托西已建有专门服务基亚卡米塔劳工的圣塞瓦斯蒂安教堂。同样这些路也走美洲驼队，连接奥鲁罗、波托西、奇查斯与阿塔卡马；西班牙人又在基亚卡建起殖民时期的教堂和圣所，定居点环绕圣所发展，这便是后来的基亚卡斯圣所镇。

en:
Macaya was a pascana, a travellers' halt, on the road between Cuzco and Alto Peru, six kilometres east of the town later called Azángaro, on the Collao plain at 3,859 metres. Llama caravans bartered at the halt so steadily that it earned the name Aswan Q'atu, the great market, and Colla chiefs drew wealth from the traffic crossing the cold plain north-west of Lake Titicaca. Farmers around it planted potatoes and quinoa and kept llama herds. In 1444 Macaya was a chief place of the Colla lords of Omasuyos, with the armies of Pachacuti already moving up into the Collao.

The Colla–Inca war of 1445–1450 put the market and its road under Cuzco; local memory says the defenders fought Pachacuti's men hard enough to earn the name aswan qharis, the strongest men. Captain Manuel Ortiz Aguilar reached the place in November 1535, and a priest reported an idol in the shape of a cat with eyes of precious stones. Dominicans set up the doctrine of Our Lady of the Rosary, but water was short and the old cult kept its hold, so the settlement moved. On 5 July 1586 the viceroy Count of Villar authorized Diego Chuquihuanca to found Spanish Azángaro, whose church of Nuestra Señora de la Asunción was begun that August. The district passed to the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata in 1776. In the Andean rising of 1780–1783 the town became a rebel headquarters: Pedro Vilca Apaza, born there in 1741, led the siege of Sorata with Andrés Túpac Amaru and was executed in the square on 8 April 1782. Its colonial church of San Bernardo was known for its gilded interior.
zh:
马卡亚是库斯科通往上秘鲁大道上的一处驿站（pascana），位于海拔3859米的科亚奥高原、后来的阿桑加罗镇以东6公里。大羊驼商队在驿站中频繁以物易物，使它得到「阿苏万卡图」之名，意为大市场，科拉首领靠的的喀喀湖西北寒冷高原上的往来贸易致富。四周的农民种植马铃薯和藜麦，牧养大羊驼。1444年，马卡亚是奥马苏约斯科拉首领的要地，帕查库特克的军队已经向科亚奥推进。

1445—1450年的科拉—印加战争使市场和大道归入库斯科治下；当地记忆称，居民抵抗帕查库特克的军队极为顽强，因而被称作「阿苏万卡里」，即最强壮的人。1535年11月，曼努埃尔·奥尔蒂斯·阿吉拉尔上尉抵达此地，一名神父报告供着一尊眼睛嵌宝石的猫形偶像。多明我会士建起玫瑰圣母传教区，但这里水源短缺，旧信仰又难以根除，聚落只得迁移。1586年7月5日，比利亚尔伯爵总督授权迭戈·丘基万卡建立西班牙式的阿桑加罗，圣母升天堂于同年8月动工。1776年，此地划归拉普拉塔总督辖区。1780—1783年的安第斯大起义中，此镇成为起义据点：1741年出生于此的佩德罗·比尔卡·阿帕萨与安德烈斯·图帕克·阿马鲁一同指挥索拉塔围城战，1782年4月8日在广场被处决。殖民时期修建的圣贝尔纳多教堂以镀金内堂闻名。

en:
Matamba is an Mbundu kingdom in the wooded savanna east of Ndongo, the Baixa de Cassanje country in Angola's Malanje Province. Its rulers bore the title ngola, from which the Portuguese took the name Angola, and its villages lived in the orbits of Ndongo and the greater kingdom of Kongo. In 1444 no European had come within hundreds of miles of it; the Portuguese founded Luanda only in 1575. Matamba first appears in writing in 1530, when its ruler sent tribute to Afonso I of Kongo, and Kongo's overlordship went no further than that tribute.

The country is known above all for Queen Njinga. She first dealt with Europeans as her brother's envoy to Luanda in 1622. A story has it that the Portuguese sat in chairs and offered her only a mat, so one of her attendants knelt on all fours and Njinga negotiated from her back, face to face with the governor; before leaving she took baptism as Ana de Sousa. Driven out of Ndongo in 1629, she defeated Matamba's queen Mwongo Matamba and made the town of Matamba her capital, joining the two kingdoms. When the Dutch seized Luanda she joined them, retook much of Ndongo and in 1647 routed a Portuguese army at Kombi, though the inland fort of Massangano held out. After the Dutch withdrew she made peace in 1656, let Italian Capuchins in to baptize thousands, and exchanged letters with Pope Alexander VII. She died in 1663 at about eighty; Cavazzi the Capuchin, who saw her review troops the year before, recorded her boast that in her youth twenty-five armed men could not best her, 'unless they had muskets'.

Matamba kept fighting. In 1681 Francisco Guterres fell on the largest army Portugal ever mobilized in Angola, over 40,000 men, at dawn in Katole; he and several kinsmen died in the fight and the Portuguese fell back to Ambaca. His sister Verónica I ruled for forty years, accepted only nominal vassalage by the treaty of 1683, and went to war with Portugal again in 1689 and 1692. A fresh invasion in 1744 ended the same way for Queen Ana II: her army mauled the Portuguese columns and she signed no more than another treaty of nominal vassalage.
zh:
马坦巴是姆本杜人的王国，位于恩东戈以东的林木稀树草原，在今安哥拉马兰热省的卡桑热低地一带。其君主称恩戈拉，葡萄牙人后来把这个称号叫成了国名「安哥拉」；诸村落的命运系于恩东戈与强国刚果之间的和战。1444年，还没有欧洲人走到这片内陆附近，葡萄牙人要到1575年才建立罗安达。马坦巴之名最早见于文字是1530年，其君主向刚果国王阿方索一世进贡，而刚果的宗主权也止于此，马坦巴最紧密的关系始终在恩东戈一边。

这个国家最出名的是女王恩津加。她最初替兄长出使罗安达是在1622年。据说葡萄牙官员都坐在椅子上，给她的只有一张席子，她的一名侍女便以手膝伏地，恩津加坐在侍女背上与总督平视谈判，离开前还受洗取名阿娜·德·索萨。1629年她被逐出恩东戈，随后击败马坦巴女王姆翁戈·马坦巴，以马坦巴城为都，把两国合为一体。荷兰人夺取罗安达后，她立刻与之结盟，收复恩东戈大片土地，1647年在科姆比击溃一支葡军，只是内陆要塞马桑加诺始终未下。荷兰人撤走后，她于1656年议和，允许意大利嘉布遣会士入境，数千臣民受洗，她还与教皇亚历山大七世互通书信。恩津加1663年去世，时年约八旬。曾在她宫中居住的嘉布遣会士卡瓦齐前一年看过她阅兵，记下她的话说，年轻时二十五个持兵器的男人她也抵挡得住，「除非他们有火枪」。

恩津加身后，马坦巴仍在战斗。1681年，弗朗西斯科·古特雷斯在卡托莱黎明突袭葡萄牙在安哥拉出动过的最大一支军队，据说兵力超过四万；他本人和几名亲属战死，受挫的葡军退回安巴卡。其妹韦罗妮卡一世在位四十年，依1683年条约只接受名义上的臣属，又在1689年和1692年两度与葡萄牙开战。1744年新的入侵轮到女王阿娜二世，结局如出一辙：马坦巴军队重创葡军，她签下的仍不过是一纸名义臣属的条约。

en:
Mbata was the eastern march of the Kingdom of Kongo and, in the country's memory, its oldest partner. Around 1375 its king Nsaku Lau gave his daughter in marriage to Nimi a Nzima of Mpemba Kasi, and from that union came Lukeni lua Nimi, the first manikongo. Mbata never let the debt be forgotten: it remained a kingdom within the kingdom, its ruler the mwene Mbata holding the title Nkaka andi Mwene Kongo, 'grandfather of the king of Kongo'. While other governors held office at the crown's pleasure, his passed by matrilineal inheritance, and Mbata's princes spoke for Kongo in all dealings with the interior. From Mbanza Mbata, on the plateau above the Inkisi near the later Angola border, the province led Kongo's eastward drive into the cloth-weaving lands of Kongo dia Nlaza, and its markets sent grain and raffia cloth west to the capital. In 1444 the grandfather of the king still governed in his own right, watching the eastern roads and the tribute coming down them.

After the court became Christian the Portuguese knew Mbata as the Duchy of Bambata. Mbanza Mbata was rebuilt on a new site from the late sixteenth century, and in the seventeenth it received a stone church, beside which the local elite were buried with clay pipes among their grave goods. By 1620, though, the grandfather's real power had shrunk to his ancient title. In 1665 António I fell at Mbwila, and for forty years Kongo tore itself apart between the Kimpanzu and Kinlaza; São Salvador was sacked in 1678 and rival kings held out in mountain strongholds in the eastern provinces. Only with the restoration of the kingship early in the eighteenth century did Mbata's roads and markets know peace again.
zh:
姆巴塔是刚果王国的东疆，在这个国家的记忆中也是最古老的盟友。约1375年，姆巴塔王恩萨库·劳将女儿嫁给姆潘巴·卡西的首领尼米·阿·恩齐马，二人生下的卢基尼·卢阿·尼米便是第一位马尼刚果。姆巴塔从未让人忘记这桩渊源：它始终是「王国中的王国」，长官姆韦内·姆巴塔保有「恩卡卡·安迪·姆韦内刚果」之号，意为「刚果王的祖父」；别的总督由国王任免，他的职位却按母系世代相承，对内陆的交涉也历来由姆巴塔的王公主持。从因基西河上游、靠近后来安哥拉边界的高原首府姆班扎姆巴塔出发，姆巴塔率领刚果向东进入「刚果·迪亚·恩拉扎」的织布之乡，市集上的谷物和拉菲草布源源西运，输往王都。1444年，这位「国王的祖父」仍在自主治事，掌管东方大道和沿道而来的贡赋。

王室皈依基督教后，葡萄牙人称姆巴塔为班巴塔公国。姆班扎姆巴塔在16世纪末另择新址重建，17世纪又建起一座石砌教堂，地方权贵的墓葬就在教堂近旁，随葬品中有许多陶土烟斗。然而到1620年，「祖父」的实权已缩水成那个古老头衔。1665年安东尼奥一世殒命姆布维拉，此后四十年间刚果在金潘祖与金拉扎两派之间自相残杀，圣萨尔瓦多于1678年遭洗劫，争位的国王们在东部诸省的山寨中固守。直到18世纪初王权重立，姆巴塔的商路与市集才重归太平。

en:
Buhera, or VuHera, 'the land of the Hera', is the country of the Hera Shona around Gombe Hill and the upper Save River, south of the Mutapa heartland. Its people are the VaHera of the Museyamwa totem, under the Nyashanu chiefly line; Shona tradition traces that line to a leader named Mbiru who came to Gombe Hill with five young followers, and derives the title Nyashanu from the Shona word for five. The VaHera kept cattle on the plateau grassland, hunted elephant in the Save woodlands and sent ivory along the road to Sofala. In 1444 their grazing and hunting country formed part of the southern tributary world of Mutapa, between the fading stone city of Great Zimbabwe and the gold streams of Manyika.

Portuguese fairs took root in neighbouring Manyika in the late sixteenth century, but Changamire Dombo's Rozvi armies overran that kingdom in the 1690s and drew the Hera hill chiefs into the Rozvi order; Hera genealogies also remember marriage ties with Rozvi rulers. The Changamire succession war of 1768 and the drought of 1795-1800 weakened the kings' hold on the tributary hill country.
zh:
布海拉原名武赫拉，意为「赫拉人的土地」，是穆塔帕腹地以南、贡贝山与萨韦河上游一带赫拉绍纳人的家园。居民是穆塞亚姆瓦图腾的瓦赫拉人，尊奉尼亚沙努酋长世系；按绍纳传统，这一世系始于一位名叫姆比鲁的首领，他带着五个年轻随从来到贡贝山，「尼亚沙努」的称号便来自绍纳语的「五」。瓦赫拉人在高原草地上牧牛，在萨韦林地猎象，把象牙沿商路送往索法拉。1444年时，他们的牧场与猎场属于穆塔帕南部纳贡圈，夹在渐衰的石城大津巴布韦和马尼卡的产金溪流之间。

16世纪后期，葡萄牙商站在邻近的马尼卡扎根，但昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维军队在17世纪90年代征服马尼卡，把赫拉山地酋长纳入罗兹维秩序；赫拉谱系中还保留着与罗兹维统治者联姻的记忆。1768年的昌加米雷继承战争和1795年至1800年的大旱，削弱了君王对这片纳贡山地的掌控。

en:
Manyika was the gold country of the Manyika Shona, a run of highland valleys between Mutapa's southern province of Guruuswa and the coast-facing kingdom of Uteve. Its streams carried alluvial gold, and long before any Portuguese reached the plateau, caravans washed the gold and carried it east with ivory to the Muslim merchants of Sofala. Its kings bore the title Chikanga, and mining camps and hill valleys made up their realm. In 1444 the Chikanga still governed his own country, but Mutapa's expansion and the trade rivalries around Sofala were already pulling Manyika into highland wars.

Around 1500, in the reign of Mwenemutapa Chikuyo, Makombe, king of Barue, sent his son Chikanga into the highlands; he occupied Manyika, checked Uteve and made the kingdom a Mutapa vassal, although Manyika tradition remembers rulers of its own before the conquest. After Portugal took Sofala in 1506, the road to these goldfields was a repeated cause of war, and in the late sixteenth century the Mwenemutapa allowed the Portuguese to open a feira in the kingdom. Manyika broke away during Mutapa's civil wars early in the seventeenth century, but a Portuguese army reconquered it in 1632. In 1695 Changamire Dombo's Rozvi overran Manyika, descended to the lowlands on its eastern edge and destroyed the Portuguese market town of Masikwesi; Dombo installed his own Chikanga, possibly the exiled Mwenemutapa Nyakunembire, founder of the Mutasa dynasty. Manyika remained under Rozvi overlordship until the mid-eighteenth century, when its kings again ruled on their own.
zh:
马尼卡是马尼卡绍纳人的黄金之地，为一连串高地山谷，夹在穆塔帕南方省古鲁乌斯瓦与面海的乌泰维王国之间。溪河中出产沙金，早在葡萄牙人抵达高原以前，商队就淘洗黄金，连同象牙一起东运，卖给索法拉的穆斯林商人。国王称奇坎加，境内遍布采金营地和山谷村落。1444年时，奇坎加仍统治着自己的国度，但穆塔帕的扩张和索法拉一带的贸易争夺，已经把马尼卡拖入高原纷争。

约1500年姆韦尼穆塔帕奇库约在位时，巴鲁埃王马孔贝派儿子奇坎加进入高地，占据马尼卡、遏制乌泰维，把这个王国变成穆塔帕属国；马尼卡传统则记得征服之前本地原有君王。1506年葡萄牙夺取索法拉后，通往这片金矿区的道路一再引发战争；16世纪后期，姆韦尼穆塔帕允许葡萄牙人在王国境内开设商站。17世纪初穆塔帕内战，马尼卡脱离，但葡萄牙军队在1632年将它重新征服。1695年，昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维大军攻灭马尼卡，直下东缘低地，摧毁葡萄牙人的集市城镇马西克韦西（Masikwesi）；敦布另立自己的奇坎加，此人可能就是流亡的姆韦尼穆塔帕尼亚库嫩比雷，即穆塔萨王朝的开创者。马尼卡此后一直臣服罗兹维，直到18世纪中叶，其君王才又自行统治。

en:
Madanda was the country of the Madanda, one of the five main groups of the Ndau, Shona-speakers of the hot lowlands between Sofala and the Manyika goldfields. Their villages lay along the inland road from the Muslim coast: cattle and grain supported them, elephant herds supplied ivory, and Muslim merchants paid in Indian cloth and beads. In 1444 Madanda stood on the south-eastern edge of the expanding Mutapa empire, still governed by its own chiefs but already trading in Sofala's shadow.

Mutapa tradition remembers the armies of Mwenemutapa Matope overrunning Teve and Madanda as the empire pushed towards the sea. In the early sixteenth century the Sachiteve of Uteve broke from Mutapa with Changamire II's help, conquered Madanda and placed his younger brother over it as the first Sedanda. Command of the road from Portuguese Sofala to Manyika's gold then dragged Madanda into the Mutapa-Teve wars, which continued into the 1540s. In the 1640s a Portuguese settler who had helped the Sachiteve hold power received northern Uteve as a prazo, which brought armed European clients to Madanda's border. A Portuguese coup against Uteve failed in the 1690s as Changamire Dombo's Rozvi overran the plateau, and a reduced Uteve regained its sovereignty.
zh:
马丹达是马丹达人的土地，他们是恩达人五大支系之一，属说绍纳语的人群，住在索法拉与马尼卡金矿区之间的炎热低地。村落在穆斯林海岸通往内陆的道路两侧：居民养牛种粮，象群供应象牙，穆斯林商人用印度布匹和珠子收购。1444年时，马丹达处在扩张中的穆塔帕帝国东南边缘，仍由本地酋长治理，生意却已笼罩在索法拉的影响之下。

穆塔帕的传统记得，姆韦尼穆塔帕马托佩的军队向海边推进时，攻灭了特维和马丹达。16世纪初，乌泰维的萨奇特韦借昌加米雷二世之助脱离穆塔帕，进而征服马丹达，立弟弟为首任塞丹达统治此地。从葡萄牙人占据的索法拉通往马尼卡黄金的道路握在谁手，随后把马丹达拖进穆塔帕与特维的战争，战祸一直延续到16世纪40年代。17世纪40年代，一名协助萨奇特韦保住权位的葡萄牙拓殖者获封乌泰维北部为普拉佐，武装的欧洲门客也随之来到马丹达边界。17世纪90年代，昌加米雷·敦布的罗兹维人席卷高原，葡萄牙人推翻萨奇特韦的图谋失败，疆域缩小的乌泰维恢复了主权。

en:
Djerba, at 514 square kilometres the largest island off North Africa, lies in the Gulf of Gabès, linked to the mainland near Zarzis by a Roman causeway seven kilometres long. Its roadsteads, olive groves and market ports gave it a place in Mediterranean trade before the Ottomans reached the Maghreb; the Phoenicians are said to have brought the olive, and oil stayed the island's staple. After Arab forces took Djerba in 665, Ibadi Islam took deep root: villagers built watch-towers that served as mosques, and an inner ring of fortified mosques answered by smoke by day and fire by night. Rain was scarce, so households caught it in paved yards and fed it into underground cisterns, denying their wells to invaders. A Jewish community had lived there since antiquity; tradition says its Ghriba synagogue holds a door and stones from Jerusalem's destroyed Temple. Normans stormed it in 1135 and carried women and children to Sicily; the Hafsids later made it part of Ifriqiya. Their castle above Houmt Souk, the Borj el-Kebir, rose in the late fourteenth century and was enlarged in 1450. In 1444 the Hafsids of Tunis ruled its Ibadi villagers, Jewish artisans, olive pressers and sailors.

The Ottoman-Spanish struggle over Hafsid Tunisia reached it in the 1530s; the corsair Dragut, later pasha of Tripoli, once held Djerba as bey. Early in 1560 a Christian coalition of Spain, the Papacy, Genoa, Malta and Naples seized the island and built a fortress facing Tripoli. In May Piali Pasha's Ottoman fleet, with Dragut in the fighting, caught the allied galleys and took 27 ships; the fortress fell within weeks, and more than 5,000 men were killed and as many carried into captivity. The victory marked the high point of Ottoman sea power, though Tunisia was secured only when Tunis and La Goulette fell in 1574. It then passed through pashas and deys, Muradid beys from 1628 to 1702, and Husainid beys after 1705; Hammuda Pasha gave Tunisia broad autonomy from 1782 to 1814. Djerban merchants and sailors kept moving through Ottoman ports, and in 1821 the island lived from Tunis, olive oil, shipping and its old Ibadi worship.
zh:
杰尔巴是加贝斯湾中一座面积514平方公里的岛屿，也是北非近海最大的岛屿，一条7公里长的海堤在杰尔吉斯附近把它与大陆相连，海堤最早由罗马人修筑。早在奥斯曼势力抵达马格里布之前，岛上隐蔽的锚地、橄榄园和小型商港就已使它进入地中海贸易；相传腓尼基人带来了油橄榄，橄榄油长期是岛上的头号出产。665年阿拉伯军队攻占杰尔巴，伊巴德派伊斯兰教在此扎下深根：岛民修筑兼作清真寺的海岸瞭望塔，第二圈防御是带堡垒的清真寺，各塔之间白天燃烟、夜里举火传讯。岛上雨水稀少，住户把雨水从铺砌的院落引入地下蓄水池贮存，外敌来犯时便以断绝水源应战。岛上还有自古与穆斯林相邻而居的犹太居民，相传他们携来耶路撒冷圣殿被毁时的门和石料，砌入格里巴会堂。1135年诺曼军队攻陷杰尔巴，把许多妇孺掳往西西里；哈夫斯王朝后来把它并入伊夫里奇亚，他们在胡姆特苏克高地上的城堡布尔吉·凯比尔建于14世纪末，1450年又加扩建。1444年，杰尔巴属于突尼斯的哈夫斯统治者，岛上住着伊巴德派村民、犹太匠人、榨油匠和水手。

16世纪30年代，奥斯曼与西班牙争夺衰落的哈夫斯突尼斯，战火烧到杰尔巴；后来官至的黎波里帕夏的海盗德拉古特，一度担任岛上的贝伊。1560年初，由西班牙、教皇国、热那亚、马耳他和那不勒斯组成的基督教联军夺取杰尔巴、修筑堡垒，作为进攻的黎波里的基地。5月，皮雅利帕夏的奥斯曼舰队发起攻击，德拉古特参战，联军桨帆船遭到突袭、27艘战船被缴；几周后堡垒失陷，五千余人战死，差不多同样数目的人被俘。这一战是奥斯曼地中海海权的顶点，而奥斯曼对突尼斯的统治直到1574年突尼斯城与拉古莱特陷落才稳固。此后杰尔巴先后经历帕夏与德伊统治、1628年至1702年的穆拉德贝伊政权，以及1705年后的侯赛因贝伊王朝；哈穆达帕夏1782年至1814年执政期间，突尼斯享有广泛自治。杰尔巴商人和水手仍往来于奥斯曼各港口；1821年，这座岛屿的生计仍系于突尼斯、橄榄油、航运和古老的伊巴德派信仰。

en:
Ingolstadt guards a Danube crossing on the road from Munich to Nuremberg. First recorded on 6 February 806 as the Carolingian royal estate Ingoldesstat, it became a planned Wittelsbach walled town and from 1392 the capital of the small Duchy of Bavaria-Ingolstadt. Duke Louis VII ringed it with walls of eighty-seven towers and began the New Castle and the Church of Our Lady. Upstream, Neuburg commanded the next Danube crossing: on 4 October 1443 Louis VIII took it after a four-month siege and handed over his own father, Louis VII, to Henry XVI of Bavaria-Landshut. In 1444 Ingolstadt was a Catholic ducal residence and a salt and wine market, its ruling line already broken; when Louis VII died in prison in 1447 the duchy passed to Landshut.

Louis IX founded Bavaria's first university here on 13 March 1472. The town's most famous document followed on 23 April 1516, when Dukes William IV and Louis X issued the Bavarian state ordinance containing the beer-purity rule since called the Reinheitsgebot. After the Landshut succession war Neuburg became the seat of the new Wittelsbach principality of Palatinate-Neuburg in 1505, and Count Palatine Ottheinrich introduced Lutheran teaching there in 1542; Ingolstadt became the Catholic answer, its state fortress built from 1537 to about 1565, its Jesuit college opened in 1549 and Johann Eck teaching at the university. In April 1632 Gustavus Adolphus failed to storm the fortress, the first in Germany to hold out through a whole Swedish siege; a cannon shot killed the king's horse under him, and the town had the animal preserved and showed the Schwedenschimmel for centuries. Tilly, wounded earlier against the Swedes, died here on 30 April 1632, and Swedish troops occupied Neuburg again and again until 1634. Adam Weishaupt, a professor at the university, founded the Order of the Illuminati in Ingolstadt on 1 May 1776, and Mary Shelley set Victor Frankenstein and his anatomy studies in the same town. The French razed the fortress after entering in July 1799 and moved the university to Landshut; Palatinate-Neuburg was absorbed into Bavarian administration in 1808.
zh:
英戈尔施塔特扼守多瑙河渡口，位于慕尼黑通往纽伦堡的大道上。806年2月6日，它首次以加洛林王室领地「英戈尔德施塔特」之名见于记载，后来成为维特尔斯巴赫家族规划营建的城墙城镇，1392年起是小巴伐利亚-英戈尔施塔特公国的都城。路德维希七世公爵为它修起有87座塔楼的城墙，又动工兴建新宫和圣母教堂。上游的诺伊堡控制着多瑙河上的下一处渡口：1443年10月4日，路德维希八世经四个月围城拿下该城，还把自己的父亲路德维希七世交给巴伐利亚-兰茨胡特的亨利十六世。1444年的英戈尔施塔特是天主教公爵驻地和盐、酒贸易城市，统治家族却已崩坏；路德维希七世1447年死于囚中后，公国并入兰茨胡特。

1472年3月13日，路德维希九世在此创办巴伐利亚第一所大学。本城最出名的一份文件在1516年4月23日颁布：威廉四世与路德维希十世发布巴伐利亚邦法，其中关于啤酒原料的规定后来被称为《纯酿法》。兰茨胡特继承战争结束后，诺伊堡于1505年成为维特尔斯巴赫新邦国普法尔茨-诺伊堡的驻地，行宫伯爵奥特海因里希1542年在此引入路德宗；英戈尔施塔特则成为天主教一方的回应：国家要塞1537年至约1565年修筑，耶稣会学院1549年开办，约翰·埃克在大学任教。1632年4月，古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫未能攻下这座要塞，它也是第一座顶住瑞典人全程围攻的德意志要塞；一发炮弹击毙了国王胯下的战马，城里人将马剥制后长期展出，称为「瑞典灰马」。此前与瑞典人作战受伤的蒂利于1632年4月30日在此死去，1634年前瑞典军队又反复占领诺伊堡。大学教授亚当·魏斯豪普特1776年5月1日在英戈尔施塔特创立光明会，玛丽·雪莱后来也把学生维克多·弗兰肯斯坦和他的解剖学业安排在这座城市。1799年7月法军入城后拆除要塞，大学迁往兰茨胡特；普法尔茨-诺伊堡于1808年并入巴伐利亚行政体系。

en:
Straubing holds the Danube crossing at the centre of the Gäuboden, the broad grain plain between Regensburg and Passau. The Romans kept the military post of Sorviodurum here, and Bavarian settlers later gathered round St Peter's. In 1218 Duke Louis I of Wittelsbach laid out a new town beside the old settlement, and after the Wittelsbach partitions the local dukes kept their seat here as dukes of Bavaria-Straubing; the same line also ruled the wealthy counties of Holland, Hainaut and Zeeland far down the Rhine. Their male line died with Duke John III in 1425, and the imperial award of 1429 assigned Straubing to Bavaria-Munich. Six years later Duke Ernest, unwilling to accept his son Albert's match with a barber's daughter, had Agnes Bernauer condemned for witchcraft and drowned in the Danube; the Bernauer Chapel he later raised in St Peter's churchyard was his penance. In 1444 Catholic Straubing served Munich as a Danube market and toll town, with the tall city tower and the Gothic basilica of St Jacob above its quays, while glass huts such as Rabenstein, already firing in 1421, drew on the woods toward the Bavarian Forest.

The town enlarged its walls in the 1470s and stayed a Bavarian administrative centre, seat of a ducal revenue office from 1507. It was among the first towns in Lower Bavaria to accept the Reformation, but the dukes forced it back to Catholicism and brought in Capuchins and, in 1631, Jesuits. Two years later the Swedes of Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar took it, and plague and the passage of armies killed about 1,800 of its 4,000 people. Austrian troops occupied Straubing in 1704 and came back to besiege it twice in the 1740s, and a fire swept the northern quarters in 1780. Napoleonic secularization closed the old ducal offices, but with the grain of the Gäuboden and Danube shipping Straubing stayed the chief market between Regensburg and Passau.
zh:
施特劳宾扼守多瑙河渡口，地处雷根斯堡与帕绍之间广阔的高博登粮仓中心。罗马人曾在此设有军事据点索尔维奥杜鲁姆，巴伐利亚人后来在圣彼得教堂一带定居。1218年，维特尔斯巴赫家族的路易一世公爵在旧聚落旁营建新城；维特尔斯巴赫家族分封后，本地公爵以巴伐利亚-施特劳宾之名在此开府，同一支公爵还远在莱茵河下游领有富庶的荷兰、埃诺和泽兰伯国。1425年末代公爵约翰三世去世，男嗣断绝，1429年皇帝的仲裁把施特劳宾判给巴伐利亚-慕尼黑。六年后，恩斯特公爵容不下儿子阿尔布雷希特与理发师之女的婚事，以巫术罪将阿格妮丝·贝尔瑙尔沉入多瑙河；他后来在圣彼得教堂墓园修建贝尔瑙尔小堂，以此赎罪。1444年，信奉天主教的施特劳宾是慕尼黑治下的多瑙河市集与税关，高耸的城市塔和哥特式圣雅各布宗座圣殿俯瞰码头，拉本施泰因等玻璃作坊1421年已在通往巴伐利亚森林的林地中开炉烧造。

1470年代城市扩建城墙，此后长期是巴伐利亚的行政中心，1507年起设有公爵税务公署。它是下巴伐利亚最早接受宗教改革的城市之一，但公爵们把它拉回天主教，先后引入嘉布遣会，又在1631年引入耶稣会。两年后萨克森-魏玛的伯恩哈德率领瑞典军队攻占此城，瘟疫和军队往来使全城四千居民中约一千八百人丧生。1704年奥地利军队占领施特劳宾，1740年代又两度围城，1780年大火席卷城北街区。拿破仑时代的世俗化裁撤了旧的公爵官署，但凭高博登的粮食和多瑙河航运，施特劳宾仍是雷根斯堡与帕绍之间最大的市集。

en:
Regensburg occupies the northernmost bend of the Danube, where the Regen and Naab enter the river. The Roman fortress Castra Regina became the core of a town that the Agilolfing dukes made their Bavarian capital, and bishops and monasteries kept large church estates within and around the walls. The Stone Bridge, built from 1135 to 1146, mattered more than any charter: for centuries it was the only Danube crossing between Ulm and Vienna, carrying traffic between northern Europe and Venice. Merchants and goldsmiths grew rich, mills used the current pressed through its piers, and the city became a Free Imperial City in 1245. By 1444 the eastern routes had shifted, debt had mounted, and Catholic Regensburg maintained a narrow self-rule between Bavaria and its own bishop.

The later city is best read through its assemblies and sieges. In 1519, after Emperor Maximilian I died, the council expelled about 500 Jews, destroyed the synagogue and much of the Jewish quarter, and removed or reused gravestones from the cemetery. The city adopted the Reformation in 1542 even though the Catholic bishopric and three imperial abbeys kept their own votes in imperial affairs. Swedish troops stormed Regensburg in 1633 and blew a span of the Stone Bridge; imperial and Bavarian forces retook it the next year. From 1663 the Imperial Diet sat there without dissolving, called first to discuss the Ottoman threat and later attended by roughly seventy foreign envoys. Princes of Thurn und Taxis served as the emperor's principal commissioners. French troops stormed the town in 1809, and Napoleon was wounded in the fighting; Regensburg passed to Bavaria in 1810.
zh:
雷根斯堡位于多瑙河最北的河湾，雷根河与纳布河在此汇入。罗马要塞卡斯特拉雷吉纳构成城市核心，阿吉洛尔芬公爵曾把这里作为巴伐利亚都城；主教和修道院又在城墙内外保有大片教会领地。1135至1146年建成的石桥比任何特许状都更关键：此后几百年间，它是乌尔姆与维也纳之间唯一的多瑙河渡河处，承载北欧与威尼斯之间的人流货运。商人和金匠借此致富，水磨利用桥墩束紧的水流作业，城市则在1245年成为帝国自由城市。到1444年，东方商路已经改道，城债日增，信奉天主教的雷根斯堡在巴伐利亚与本城主教之间维持着狭小的自治。

后来的雷根斯堡，可以从帝国会议和攻城战来看。1519年皇帝马克西米利安一世去世后，市议会驱逐约五百名犹太人，拆毁犹太会堂和大片犹太区，墓地的许多墓碑也被移走或再用。1542年城市接受宗教改革，但天主教主教区和三座帝国修道院仍在帝国事务中保有自己的席位。1633年瑞典军队攻陷雷根斯堡并炸断石桥一跨，皇帝与巴伐利亚联军次年收复城市。自1663年起，帝国议会在此持续召开而不解散；它最初为讨论奥斯曼威胁而召集，后来约有七十名外国使节常驻。图恩与塔克西斯亲王作为皇帝首席专员驻在城中。1809年法军强攻城市，拿破仑在战斗中受伤；1810年雷根斯堡并入巴伐利亚。

en:
Osterode began as a Teutonic watchtower on the islands where the Drwęca runs into its lake, in the Sasin lands of the Order's Oberland. Around 1270 the Knights raised a wooden tower and named it after Osterode am Harz, the home country of many of their Welf commanders. In 1329 Komtur Luther von Braunschweig, himself later grand master, granted Kulm town rights, and between 1349 and 1370 the commandery's granite-and-brick castle rose beside the old wooden fort. Kęstutis burned castle and town in 1381. The fields of this very commandery were where Grunwald was fought in July 1410: Polish troops cut down fugitive knights under the town walls, the knight Claus von Doringe handed castle and town to Władysław Jagiełło, and the king brought the body of the slain Grand Master Jungingen there before the Order retook the place a few months later. Osterode joined the Prussian Confederation in 1440, and in 1444 it was a commandery town grown restive under Order rule.

The peace of 1466 made it a Polish fief held by the Order, a standing it kept until 1657. Sigismund the Old's army took it in the war of 1519, and after the secularisation of 1525 the last komtur, Count Quirin Schlick, stayed on as the duchy's first captain; a Latin school opened in 1592. Gustavus Adolphus lodged in the town while the Swedes held it in 1628 and 1629. From 1633 John Christian of Brzeg, one of the last Silesian Piasts, governed Osterode by grant of the Polish king and died there in 1639, his wife buried in the town church. Tatar and Swedish raids laid it waste in 1656, plague came in 1708 and 1711, and Russian troops were quartered there for four years during the Seven Years' War. The fire of 1788 destroyed the old castle and most of the houses. In the spring of 1807, soon after the refugee King Frederick William III and Queen Louise had passed through, Napoleon himself lived in the castle from 21 February to 1 April, directing the East Prussian campaign; a medal struck for his stay and a painting of the burghers' homage are kept at Versailles.
zh:
奥斯特罗德起于德雷文察河注入湖泊处一片岛屿上的条顿哨塔，地处骑士团上普鲁士辖区的萨辛人之地。1270年前后骑士团筑起木塔，以许多出身韦尔夫家族的指挥官的故乡哈茨山奥斯特罗德命名。1329年，后来官至大团长的长官路德·冯·布伦瑞克授予库尔姆城市法；1349至1370年，长官辖区的花岗岩砖石城堡在旧木堡旁建成。1381年科斯图提斯焚毁了城堡和城镇。1410年7月的格伦瓦德战役就打在这片长官辖区的土地上：波兰军队在城墙下追杀逃散的骑士，骑士克劳斯·冯·多林根把城堡和城镇献给瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃，国王还把战死的大团长容金根的遗体运到这里；数月后骑士团夺回此城。1440年奥斯特罗德加入普鲁士联盟，1444年时已是一座对骑士团心怀不满的长官驻地。

1466年的和约把它定为骑士团领有、向波兰称臣的封邑，这一地位维持到1657年。1519年的战争中，「老国王」齐格蒙特一世的军队攻占此城；1525年世俗化后，末任长官奎林·施利克伯爵留任公国首任行政官，1592年城里开设了拉丁语学校。1628至1629年瑞典占领期间，古斯塔夫·阿道夫曾在此下榻。1633年起，经波兰国王同意，西里西亚末代皮亚特公爵之一、布热格的扬·赫雷斯特安以受封方式治理奥斯特罗德，1639年死于此地，他的妻子葬在城中教堂。1656年鞑靼人和瑞典军队先后把城镇劫掠一空，瘟疫在1708和1711年两度袭来，七年战争中俄军又在此驻留四年。1788年的大火烧毁了旧城堡和大半房屋。1807年春，出逃途中的弗里德里希·威廉三世与路易丝王后刚经过这里，拿破仑本人便在2月21日至4月1日住进城堡指挥东普鲁士战役；为他此行铸造的「拿破仑在奥斯特罗德」奖章和一幅市民献降图，都藏在凡尔赛宫的藏品中。

en:
Tarnow lies at the meeting of the Biala and the Dunajec, on the old road from Krakow into Ruthenia. A Slavic gord stood on St Martin's Mount from the mid-ninth century, and the name first appears in a papal document of 1124. In 1327 the knight Spycimir of the Leliwa clan bought the village, and in 1330 Wladyslaw the Elbow-high granted it Magdeburg rights; Spycimir raised his castle on the hill, and Tarnow stayed with his descendants, the Tarnowski magnates, for more than two centuries. They ringed the town with walls in the mid-fifteenth century and in 1467 piped water into the market square, where German settlers and craftsmen swelled the guilds. In 1444 Tarnow was a busy private town in Sandomierz Voivodeship, its river trade and workshops enriching one of the great families of the Crown.

The town's golden age belonged to Jan Amor Tarnowski, born there in 1488. He became Grand Crown Hetman, led the Crown army to victory over the Moldavians at Obertyn in 1531, had fought the Moors in Portuguese Africa and been made a knight of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, and became the first Imperial count in his family. In 1528 his castle sheltered the exiled Hungarian king Janos Szapolyai. The town below held up to twelve guilds, a school, a synagogue and a Calvinist prayer house among its Catholic churches. After the hetman died in 1561 the Italian sculptor Jan Maria Padovano built his tomb in the cathedral, a Renaissance monument almost fourteen metres high in St Anne's Chapel, finished in 1573; he also remodelled the town hall, whose twenty-eight niches carried portraits of the family. In 1570 Tarnow passed by marriage to the Ostrogski family, and after 1588 through several hands until the Sanguszko family bought it in 1723. Swedish troops sacked it in October 1655 during the Deluge, and the population fell from 2,000 to 768. With the First Partition of 1772 it went to Austria, becoming a Galician county seat and, in 1783, a bishop's see.
zh:
塔尔努夫位于比亚瓦河注入杜纳耶茨河之处，地处克拉科夫通往罗斯的古道上。9世纪中叶，圣马丁山上已矗立斯拉夫人的堡寨，塔尔努夫之名最早见于1124年的教皇文书。1327年，莱利瓦氏族的骑士斯皮齐米尔买下这座村落，1330年瓦迪斯瓦夫一世（矮子）授予它马格德堡法；斯皮齐米尔在山丘上筑起城堡，塔尔努夫此后二百多年一直属于他的后裔塔尔诺夫斯基世家。他们在15世纪中叶环筑城墙，1467年把自来水管铺进集市广场，德意志移民和工匠充实了各个行会。1444年的塔尔努夫是桑多梅日省一座繁忙的贵族私城，河运与作坊养富了波兰王国的一个世家大族。

城市的全盛时代属于1488年出生于此的扬·阿莫尔·塔尔诺夫斯基。他官至王军大盖特曼，1531年率王军在奥伯廷击败摩尔达维亚人，此前曾随葡萄牙人到非洲与摩尔人作战，并在耶路撒冷受封为圣墓骑士，后来成为家族中的第一位神圣罗马帝国伯爵。1528年，他的城堡接待流亡的匈牙利国王绍波尧伊·亚诺什。山下的城市有多达十二个行会，除天主教教堂外，还办有学校、犹太会堂和加尔文宗祈祷所。盖特曼1561年去世后，意大利雕塑家扬·马里亚·帕多瓦诺在大教堂的圣安娜礼拜堂为他修筑陵墓，这座近十四米高的文艺复兴式纪念碑1573年完工；他还改建市政厅，厅上二十八个壁龛安放着家族成员的肖像。1570年，塔尔努夫随联姻转入奥斯特罗格斯基家族，1588年后几经易主，1723年由桑古什科家族购得。大洪水时代，瑞典军队于1655年10月洗劫城市，人口从两千降至768人。1772年第一次瓜分中它归属奥地利，成为加利西亚的县治，1783年又成为主教驻地。

en:
Nowy Sącz sits in the Dunajec valley at the foot of the Beskids, where the road from Kraków climbs towards the Hungarian border. It was founded on 8 November 1292 by Wenceslaus II of Bohemia on the site of the village of Kamienica, at the request of its owner Bishop Paweł of Przemanków, and it was the only Polish town the Bohemian king ever chartered; it took its name from older Stary Sącz nearby. Granted Magdeburg rights, it grew rich on the Hungarian carrying trade, and in 1329 it struck a reciprocal staple treaty with Kraków, whose merchants had to halt here on their way south. Casimir the Great ringed it with walls and built a royal castle, the seat of a castellan and starosta on the southern frontier, and many royal meetings were held there; in 1409 Władysław Jagiełło and Vytautas met in the castle to plan their war on the Teutonic Order. In the fifteenth century the town's forges produced steel, its weavers woollen cloth, and its painters nearly rivalled those of Kraków. In 1444 Nowy Sącz was a royal city of the Kraków Voivodeship, still peopled largely by descendants of German colonists.

In 1448 Bishop Zbigniew Oleśnicki raised the parish church to a collegiate, and the town won the staple right in 1554. It became a centre of the Reformation, hosting a school and congregation of the Polish Brethren from 1556 to 1616. A great fire devastated it in 1611, and in the Deluge the Swedes seized and sacked it in late 1655. On 13 December 1655 the burghers, led by the Wąsowicz brothers with a detachment of Gabriel Wojniłłowicz's troops, drove the garrison out, one of the first towns of the Commonwealth to free itself; the Swedes abandoned the siege of Jasna Góra thirteen days later, and John II Casimir sent the town his thanks in January 1656. In 1683 John III Sobieski met his queen Maria Kazimiera at nearby Stary Sącz on his way back from Vienna. The Great Northern War and the Bar Confederation brought fresh destruction and the burning of the castle. In 1770, ahead of the First Partition, Austrian troops annexed the Sącz lands, which became part of Galicia.
zh:
新松奇坐落在贝斯基德山麓的杜纳耶茨河谷，是克拉科夫通往匈牙利边境道路的要冲。1292年11月8日，波希米亚国王瓦茨拉夫二世应卡缅尼察村的主人、克拉科夫主教普热梅努夫的帕韦尔请求，在该村旧址颁令建城，这也是这位国王在波兰建立的唯一一座城市，城名则取自附近更古老的旧松奇。城市获授马格德堡法，靠转运匈牙利货物致富，1329年与克拉科夫订立对等的货栈条约，规定克拉科夫商人南下匈牙利必须在此停驻。卡齐米日大帝为它修筑城墙和王家城堡，城堡是镇守南部边境的城主与行政长官驻地，历代君主多次在此会面，1409年瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃和维托尔德便在堡中筹划对条顿骑士团的战争。15世纪，城中锻炉出产钢材，织工织造毛呢，绘画几乎可与克拉科夫比肩。1444年的新松奇是克拉科夫省的一座王家城市，居民多为早期德意志移民的后裔。

1448年，兹比格涅夫·奥莱希尼茨基主教把当地教堂升格为协同教堂；1554年城市取得货栈特权。宗教改革时期，这里是波兰兄弟会的一个中心，1556至1616年间办有该会的学校和会堂。1611年一场大火重创全城；「大洪水」中瑞典人于1655年底攻占并洗劫城市。同年12月13日，市民在翁索维奇兄弟率领下，由加布里埃尔·沃伊尼沃维奇率部配合，驱逐了瑞典守军，是共和国最早自行解放的城市之一；瑞典人十三天后解除了对光明山的围攻，1656年1月扬·卡齐米日国王致信向全城致谢。1683年，扬三世·索别斯基在维也纳之捷后回国途中，在附近的旧松奇与王后玛丽亚·卡齐米埃拉团聚。大北方战争和巴尔联盟战争又带来破坏，城堡也遭焚毁。1770年，在第一次瓜分之前，奥地利军队即已吞并松奇地区，此地后来成为加利西亚的一部分。

en:
Lwów grew up below the High Castle on the roads that carried Black Sea and Crimean goods into central Europe. Daniel of Galicia is counted its founder, naming the stronghold for his son Leo; it is first documented in 1256 and became the capital of Galicia-Volhynia around 1272. Casimir III of Poland took the city in 1349 and granted Magdeburg rights in 1356, walling a new market town governed by German burghers while Ruthenian, Armenian and Jewish communities kept their own quarters; the Armenians had their own archbishop there by about 1280. From 1434 Lwów was the capital of the Ruthenian Voivodeship. In 1444 it was a royal city of the Polish Crown, whose merchants forwarded furs, wax and eastern goods to Kraków and the German towns.

Fires in 1527 and 1556 destroyed most of Gothic Lwów, and the rebuilt centre took on its Renaissance face around the Market Square, with the Black House, the Korniakt Palace and the Boim family chapel rising there in the next two generations. The Orthodox Dormition Church served the Ruthenian townspeople, its brotherhood ran a school, and Ivan Fedorovych, a printer who had fled Moscow, worked in the city. In 1648 Bohdan Khmelnytsky's Cossacks stormed the High Castle and withdrew only for a ransom, and the town's repeated defence won it the motto Semper fidelis, always faithful. John II Casimir made his Lwów Oath in the Latin cathedral in 1656, an Ottoman siege failed in 1672, and John III Sobieski defeated another Ottoman and Crimean army outside the walls in 1675. Lwów fell to a foreign army for the first time since the Middle Ages in 1704, when Charles XII of Sweden took and looted it. The First Partition of 1772 gave the city to the Habsburgs as Lemberg, capital of the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria; its old walls were dismantled from 1777, and a university opened in 1784.
zh:
利沃夫在高堡脚下兴起，地当黑海、克里米亚通往中欧的商路。传统上认为它由加利西亚王公丹尼尔兴建，并以其子列夫命名；现存最早的文字记载在1256年，约1272年成为加利西亚-沃里尼亚的都城。波兰国王卡齐米日三世1349年攻取此城，1356年授予马格德堡法，筑起一座由德意志市民治理的有墙市场新城，鲁塞尼亚人、亚美尼亚人和犹太人则各居自己的街区；约1280年，亚美尼亚人已在此设有自己的大主教。1434年起，利沃夫成为鲁塞尼亚省首府。1444年时，它是波兰王国的王室城市，商人把毛皮、蜂蜡和东方货物转销克拉科夫与德意志诸城。

1527年和1556年的大火烧毁了哥特式利沃夫的大部分城区，重建后的市中心在集市广场周围显出文艺复兴面貌，黑屋、科尔尼亚克特宫和博伊姆家族礼拜堂都在这一时期建起。东正教圣母安息教堂服务于鲁塞尼亚市民，附设的兄弟会开办学校，从莫斯科逃出的印刷匠伊万·费多罗维奇也曾在此工作。1648年，博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基的哥萨克攻下高堡，拿到赎金才撤兵；城市在连番围攻中坚守，得到「始终忠诚」的铭言。1656年，扬二世·卡齐米日在拉丁主教座堂发表利沃夫誓愿；1672年奥斯曼军队攻城不克；1675年，扬三世·索别斯基又在城外击败一支奥斯曼与克里米亚联军。1704年，卡尔十二世的瑞典军队攻破并劫掠利沃夫，这是中世纪以来它第一次落入外国军队手中。1772年第一次瓜分后，城市以「伦贝格」之名归属哈布斯堡，成为加利西亚和洛多梅里亚王国的首府；旧城墙自1777年起拆除，大学则于1784年开办。

en:
Rowne lies on the Ustia River, on the old road that carried traffic between Kyiv, Volodymyr and western Volhynia.
