The Uckermark is the fertile lakeland of the Uecker and the Ucker lakes, named after the Slavic Ukrani, whose gords at Drense and by the later Prenzlau guarded the routes through it. Pomeranian dukes opened the country to Christian missions and Low German settlers, and their trading place at Prenzlau was described in 1188 as a fortified settlement with a market, an inn and one of Pomerania's three mints; Duke Barnim I gave it German town law in 1234. The town stood on the busy Magdeburg-Stettin road, and Wolfram von Eschenbach names 'Ukerlant' and its 'Ukersee' in Parzival. By 1250 Prenzlau had walls, four parish churches and a monastery, and ranked with Berlin, Stendal and Frankfurt an der Oder among the largest towns of the March. The Treaty of Landin handed the whole Uckerland to Brandenburg in that same year, and after two centuries of war with Pomerania and Mecklenburg, Prenzlau returned to Hohenzollern rule in 1426 and the Peace of Wittstock secured the region for the elector in 1442. In 1444 it was a still-Catholic Brandenburg frontier province of rich farms and long-distance trade.

The Thirty Years' War reached it in 1626 and plague in 1630. When Gustavus Adolphus fell at Lützen, his body was carried north and lay for three days that December in Prenzlau's St Mary's, the first brick hall church built east of the Elbe. At the peace nearly two in five of the region's 222 villages lay destroyed or empty. In 1701 Dorothee Elisabeth Tretschlaff was executed there, the last person put to death for witchcraft in Brandenburg. Dutch settlers and a French Huguenot community founded in Prenzlau in 1687 brought new crafts, the Finow Canal, opened in the south in 1746, carried the region's timber and grain, and the Uckermark became the granary of Berlin. War returned in 1806: on 28 October General Hohenlohe surrendered about 12,000 Prussian troops to the French near Prenzlau, and occupation levies lasted until 1812.
zh:
乌克马克是于克河与乌克湖群一带的肥沃湖乡，得名于斯拉夫乌克拉尼人；他们在德伦瑟和后来的普伦茨劳设有堡寨，扼守湖沼间的通道。波美拉尼亚公爵把此地开放给基督教传教团和低地德意志移民，他们在普伦茨劳的贸易点1188年已被记作设防聚落，设有市场、酒肆和波美拉尼亚三座铸币厂之一；1234年，公爵巴尔尼姆一世授予它德意志城市法。普伦茨劳位于马格德堡至斯德丁的商路上，沃尔夫拉姆·冯·埃申巴赫在《帕西法尔》里提到过「乌克兰」和「乌克湖」，足见他熟知此地。到1250年，普伦茨劳已有城墙、四座教区教堂和一座修道院，与柏林、施滕达尔、奥得河畔法兰克福同属马克最大的几座城市。同年，《兰丁条约》把整个乌克兰划给勃兰登堡；在与波美拉尼亚、梅克伦堡打了两个世纪的仗之后，普伦茨劳1426年重归霍亨索伦家族，1442年的《维特施托克和约》最终确保选帝侯取得这一地区。1444年，这里是仍奉天主教的勃兰登堡边省，农田肥沃，远途贸易繁忙。

三十年战争1626年波及此地，1630年瘟疫接踵。古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫在吕岑战死后，遗体北运，同年12月在普伦茨劳圣母教堂停放三天；这座教堂是易北河以东第一座砖砌厅堂式教堂。战争结束时，全区222个村庄中近四成被毁或无人居住。1701年，多罗特娅·伊丽莎白·特雷奇拉夫被处死，这是勃兰登堡最后一起巫术死刑。荷兰移民和1687年在普伦茨劳建立的法国胡格诺教徒社区带来新手艺，1746年南部通航的菲诺运河运出木材和粮食，乌克马克也成了柏林的粮仓。1806年战火又起：10月28日，霍恩洛厄将军在普伦茨劳附近率约一万二千名普军向法军投降，占领摊派一直持续到1812年。

en:
Wolgast guards the Peenestrom, the sound between the Pomeranian mainland and the island of Usedom, where the ferries to the island put in. A Slavic trading and toll station stood here in the early twelfth century, with a shrine to the god Jarovit until Bishop Otto of Bamberg destroyed it on his second Pomeranian mission in 1128. During the German eastward settlement a planned town was laid out beside the old Wendish quarters. Wolgast joined the Hanseatic League but never carried weight in it, dwarfed by Stralsund down the coast. After the Pomeranian partition of 1295 it became the seat of the Griffin dukes of Pomerania-Wolgast; their castle on its island in the sound grew into one of the grandest Renaissance palaces of northern Germany, and the dukes were buried in St Peter's Church beside it. In 1444 Duke Wartislaw IX held a Catholic, modestly prosperous ducal town that lived from the shipping through the sound and the salt trade.

The Thirty Years War made the sound a battlefield. On 2 September 1628 Wallenstein's imperial army defeated Christian IV of Denmark outside the town, and in 1630 Gustavus Adolphus landed his Swedish army at Peenemuende, then part of Wolgast, opening Sweden's intervention in the war; after the king fell at Luetzen his body was brought here before being shipped home. From 1648 Wolgast belonged to Swedish Pomerania. In 1713, during the Great Northern War, Russian troops burned the town in reprisal for the Swedish burning of Altona, and the castle was destroyed with it, its stones later carted away for new buildings; St Peter's was among the few Gothic survivors, and a baroque town hall rose in the rebuilding. After 1720 Wolgast collected the customs at the Oder entrance, for the Swine channel had silted up. In 1815 the town passed to Prussia. Its native son the painter Philipp Otto Runge, born here in 1777 the child of a Wolgast merchant, ranks with Caspar David Friedrich among the leading figures of German Romanticism.
zh:
沃尔加斯特扼守波美拉尼亚大陆与乌泽多姆岛之间的佩讷海峡，渡海登岛的船只就在这里起航。12世纪初，这里是斯拉夫人的贸易和征税站，设有雅罗维特神庙，1128年班贝格的奥托第二次赴波美拉尼亚传教时将其摧毁。东向殖民时期，一座规划城镇在古老的文德聚落旁建成。沃尔加斯特加入了汉萨同盟，却在同盟中无足轻重，声势远不及沿海的施特拉尔松德。1295年波美拉尼亚分封后，它成为格里芬王朝波美拉尼亚-沃尔加斯特支系公爵的驻地；公爵们在海峡中的岛上修筑宫城，后来成为北德最宏伟的文艺复兴宫殿之一，历代公爵则葬在宫城旁的圣彼得教堂。1444年，瓦季斯瓦夫九世统治着这座信奉天主教、还算富庶的公爵驻城，生计靠海峡航运和食盐贸易。

三十年战争使海峡变成战场。1628年9月2日，华伦斯坦的帝国军队在城外击败丹麦国王克里斯蒂安四世；1630年，古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫在当时隶属沃尔加斯特的佩讷明德率瑞典军队登陆，瑞典就此参战。国王战死于吕岑后，灵柩先运抵这里，再装船送回本国。1648年起，沃尔加斯特属瑞典属波美拉尼亚。1713年大北方战争期间，俄军为报复瑞典人焚毁阿尔托纳而放火烧城，公爵宫城同毁，残存石料后来被拆去建造新房；圣彼得教堂是少数幸存的哥特式建筑之一，一座巴洛克式市政厅在重建中落成。1720年后希维纳水道淤塞，沃尔加斯特改在奥得河入河口征收关税。1815年，城市并入普鲁士。本地出生的画家菲利普·奥托·龙格是一位沃尔加斯特商人之子，他与卡斯帕·大卫·弗里德里希同为德国浪漫主义的代表人物。

en:
Stolp stands on the Słupia, between the lower Vistula and the lower Oder, at the only ford on the old road from Danzig to Stargard. Its first stronghold sat on a marshy islet in the river, whose branches served as a natural moat. The Samboride duke Swietopelk II granted Lübeck law in 1265, and Westphalian and Holstein merchants laid out a new ward on the bank in 1276. After Brandenburg rule and a spell pledged to the Teutonic Order, the town's knights, clergy and burghers raised the ransom themselves and brought it back to the Griffin dukes in 1341. They had already bought the downstream village of Stolpmünde in 1337, and through its harbour the fish, amber and cloth of the hinterland reached Baltic and North Sea buyers. From 1368 Stolp was the seat of the dukes of Pomerania-Stolp, who held their duchy as vassals of the kings of Poland: Kaźko, a grandson of Casimir III of Poland once favoured for the Polish crown, ruled there from 1374, and the later dukes Wartislaw VII and Bogislaw VIII paid homage to King Władysław II Jagiełło in 1390 and 1410. In 1444 it was a Catholic Hanse town under the Griffins.

Fire gutted most of the town in 1477, and Duke Bogislaw X raised his Renaissance ducal castle there from 1507. The townspeople went over to Lutheranism in the disturbances of 1524 and 1525, but plague, repeated fires and quarrels with the dukes ended its Hanse days. In the Thirty Years' War Swedish troops took it in 1630, imperial forces in 1637, and Banner's Swedes left the place in ruins; Brandenburg took actual possession in 1653. A tower of the old town walls, later called the Witches' Tower, served by then as the prison where women accused of witchcraft were tortured before burning, and the last such victim in Prussian Stolp was a Catholic woman named Trina Papisten. Huguenot settlers helped revive trade, Frederick the Great stationed cavalry here and opened a cadet school in 1769, and Polish troops in Napoleon's service briefly seized the town in February 1807. From 1816 Stolp was a district seat in the Prussian Province of Pomerania.
zh:
施托尔普（斯武普斯克）位于斯武皮亚河畔，地处维斯瓦河下游与奥得河下游之间、旧商道从但泽通往施塔加德的唯一渡口。最早的堡寨建在河中沼泽小岛上，河汊就是天然壕沟。1265年，桑博里德家族的希维托佩乌克二世授予此地吕贝克法；1276年，威斯特伐利亚和荷尔斯泰因商人在河岸建起新街区。此地先后经历勃兰登堡统治、又被抵押给条顿骑士团，1341年由城中骑士、教士和市民凑齐赎金，使它重回格里芬公爵治下。市民早在1337年就买下下游村落施托尔普明德，腹地出产的鱼、琥珀和布匹经这个港口销往波罗的海和北海。1368年起，施托尔普成为波美拉尼亚—施托尔普公爵的驻地，这一支以波兰国王封臣的身份领有公国：波兰国王卡齐米日三世的外孙卡兹科（Kaźko）曾被视为波兰王位继承人选，1374年起在此统治，后来的瓦尔齐斯瓦夫七世和博吉斯瓦夫八世又分别在1390年和1410年向国王瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃行臣服礼。1444年，它是格里芬家族治下的天主教汉萨城镇。

1477年大火烧毁大半个城镇，博吉斯瓦夫十世1507年起在此兴建文艺复兴式的公爵城堡。1524至1525年的动荡中，市民改宗路德宗，但瘟疫、接连的火灾和与公爵的争执终结了城市的汉萨岁月。三十年战争中，瑞典军队1630年占城，帝国军队1637年进驻，巴内尔所率瑞典军队撤离时只留下废墟；勃兰登堡1653年实际接管此城。旧城墙中的一座塔楼当时已被用作监狱，被控行巫的妇人在那里受刑，再被送上火刑柱，这座塔后来被称为女巫塔；普鲁士治下的施托尔普最后一名此类死者，是名叫特丽娜·帕皮斯滕（Trina Papisten）的天主教妇人。胡格诺移民帮助恢复了贸易，腓特烈大帝把骑兵驻在此城并于1769年创办幼军校，随拿破仑作战的波兰军队1807年2月短暂夺城。1816年起，施托尔普成为普鲁士波美拉尼亚省的县治。

en:
Wismar lies on a sheltered Baltic bay behind Poel island, where a natural harbour served land once held by the Obotrites. German colonists founded the town under Henry Borwin I around 1226; it is documented in 1229 and soon received Lübeck law. The dukes of Mecklenburg kept a residence there from 1257 to 1358. In 1259 Wismar's envoys met Lübeck and Rostock to make a piracy-protection treaty, one of the early agreements behind the Wendish Hanse network. Wool processing, cloth, beer and Baltic freight paid for the brick churches and gabled houses of St Mary's, St Nicholas' and St George's parishes. The Black Death killed about 2,000 inhabitants in 1350, and civic conflict ended on the market square in 1427 with the execution of Mayor Johann Bantzkow and a fleet commander. In 1444 Wismar remained a Catholic Hanse port under Mecklenburg lordship.

Later wars made the harbour a Swedish strongpoint. The Franciscan Heinrich Never carried Lutheran preaching into the friaries and parishes, and the Viechelner Fahrt canal linked the town with Lake Schwerin and the Elbe system in 1594. Imperial troops took Wismar in 1627, Sweden conquered it in 1632, and the Peace of Westphalia assigned it to the Swedish crown in 1648. After 1653 the Fürstenhof housed the supreme tribunal for Sweden's imperial fiefs, and Erik Dahlbergh strengthened the fortifications. Danish forces held the town from 1675 to 1680; coalition troops took it again in 1716, after which the elaborate defenses were dismantled. The 1803 Treaty of Malmö pledged Wismar to Mecklenburg-Schwerin for 99 years. Napoleonic troops occupied it from 1806 to 1813, and the port stayed with Mecklenburg-Schwerin after 1815.
zh:
维斯马位于珀尔岛遮蔽下的波罗的海海湾，天然港口服务着这片原属奥博特人的土地。约1226年，海因里希·博尔温一世招徕德意志殖民者建立城镇；1229年已有文献记载，不久后采用《吕贝克法》。1257年至1358年，梅克伦堡公爵以这里为驻地。1259年，维斯马使者与吕贝克、罗斯托克签订抵御海盗的互助条约，这是汉萨文德城市网络最早的协议之一。毛纺、布料、啤酒和波罗的海货运为圣马利亚、圣尼古拉和圣乔治堂区的砖砌教堂与山墙宅邸提供了财富。1350年黑死病造成约两千名居民死亡；1427年城市冲突在市集广场收场，市长约翰·班茨科和一名舰队指挥官被处死。1444年，维斯马仍是梅克伦堡治下的天主教汉萨港口。

后来的战争把这个港口变成瑞典据点。方济各会修士海因里希·内弗把路德宗讲道带入修院和堂区；1594年，维谢恩航道把城镇同什未林湖和易北河水系连接起来。1627年帝国军队攻占维斯马，1632年瑞典将其攻克，1648年《威斯特伐利亚和约》把它划给瑞典王室。1653年后，侯爵宫成为瑞典在神圣罗马帝国各封地的最高法院，埃里克·达尔贝里主持加固要塞。1675年至1680年，丹麦军队占据城市；1716年联军再次攻占，此后复杂的防御工事被拆除。1803年，《马尔默抵押条约》将维斯马抵押给梅克伦堡-什未林99年。1806年至1813年拿破仑军队占领此地，1815年后港口仍属梅克伦堡-什未林。

en:
Tuchola, German Tuchel, lies among rivers and lakes on the south-western edge of the great Tuchola Forest in Gdańsk Pomerania. It grew up as a trading settlement serving the old castellany at Raciąż, on the road that carried Gdańsk goods through Nakło to Greater Poland, Silesia and Bohemia. Archbishop Jakub Świnka consecrated its church in 1287. The Teutonic Order took the town in 1330 and made it the seat of a wide forest commandery, and on 22 July 1346 Grand Master Heinrich Dusemer confirmed its Chełmno town law at Malbork. Brick castle, walls, moats, town hall and St Bartholomew's church looked over a market in grain, timber and forest produce. After Grunwald in 1410 Polish garrisons and Teutonic-Brandenburg troops fought here for months; Długosz records that in the November battle more of the Order's men drowned in Zamkowe Lake and the marshes than fell to Polish swords, though the First Peace of Thorn in 1411 left Tuchola to the Order. It joined the Prussian Confederation in 1440, so in 1444 it was a Teutonic commandery in name, already leaning toward Poland.

In 1454, at the Confederation's call, Casimir IV proclaimed the region's reincorporation into Poland, and Mikołaj Szarlejski became Tuchola's first royal starosta. A Polish victory nearby in 1464 and the Second Peace of Thorn in 1466 made it a royal town and county seat in Royal Prussia. The Gdańsk trade filled the place, and by 1570 it had 123 houses in the town, seventy-three more in the suburbs and eight merchant warehouses. The Deluge ended that growth: the Swedes walked in unopposed in 1655 and left again in 1656, and their five assaults of 1656–1659 were beaten off amid plague and fire; by local report the castle powder magazine blew up, and the damage was not repaired for a century. At the First Partition of 1772 Tuchola passed to Prussia with only 108 houses and 490 inhabitants. On 17 May 1781 Johann Philipp Voigt fired the church outbuildings to steal their valuables; the flames took St Bartholomew's, the town hall and most of the wooden town. The burghers rejected a plan to move the town, rebuilt on the old site, and weaving revived it by 1804. French, Polish, Prussian and Russian troops passed through in 1806–1807.
zh:
图霍拉，德语称图赫尔，位于格但斯克波美拉尼亚的大图霍拉森林西南缘，河湖交错。它早年是为拉琼什旧城堡辖区服务的贸易聚落，扼守格但斯克货物经纳克沃运往大波兰、西里西亚和波希米亚的商路。1287年10月9日，大主教雅库布·希温卡为当地教堂祝圣。骑士团1330年攻取此镇，设立管辖大片森林的指挥官辖区；1346年7月22日，大团长海因里希·杜塞默在马尔堡确认其享有海乌姆诺法。砖堡、城墙、壕沟、市政厅和圣巴多罗买教堂，环护着谷物、木材和林产品市场。1410年格伦瓦尔德战役后，波兰守军与骑士团、勃兰登堡联军在此拉锯数月；据德乌戈什记载，11月一战中，骑士团一方溺毙于城堡湖和周围沼泽者多于死于波兰刀剑者，1411年《第一次托伦和约》仍把图霍拉留给骑士团。1440年它加入普鲁士联盟，所以1444年时图霍拉名义上还是骑士团指挥官驻地，归属之心已倒向波兰。

1454年，应普鲁士联盟之请，卡齐米日四世宣布将这一地区重新并入波兰，米科瓦伊·沙尔莱伊斯基成为第一任王室县尉。1464年波军在附近取胜，1466年《第二次托伦和约》把图霍拉定为皇家普鲁士的王室城镇和县治。格但斯克贸易养富了这座城，到1570年，城区有123栋房屋、郊区另有73栋，还有八座商人仓库。「大洪水」逆转了这段好景：瑞典人1655年不战而入、1656年不战而走，1656至1659年又五次来攻，均被击退，其间瘟疫、火灾相继；民间还传说城堡火药库被引爆，残损近百年未能修复。1772年第一次瓜分波兰时，图霍拉归属普鲁士，只剩108栋房屋、490名居民。1781年5月17日，约翰·菲利普·福格特为窃取教堂财物，纵火点燃教堂附属房屋，火势吞没圣巴多罗买教堂、市政厅和大半个木构城镇。迁镇他处的计划被放弃，市民在原址重建，靠纺织业到1804年重新站稳。1806至1807年的战事中，法国、波兰、普鲁士和俄国军队先后经过此地。

en:
Buzău sits on the right bank of its river, where the Buzău comes out of the Carpathian curvature into the Bărăgan Plain, and the roads from Wallachia into Moldavia and Transylvania meet there. A medieval fortress overlooked the place, but trade made the town: a charter of Prince Dan II, who reigned from 1420 to 1431, certified it as a market and customs point, and by 1431 merchants were already gathering the livestock and wool of the surrounding plains. In 1444 Wallachia was an Ottoman tributary, and Buzău lived by that traffic, as shepherds coming down from the mountains after the shearing sold their wool to merchants bound for the Danube and the passes.

That midsummer gathering was the origin of Drăgaica, the wool fair first held up in the Buzău valley and later moved into the town around 24 June. In 1778 Prince Alexandru Ipsilanti gave its organisation and all its tolls to the Orthodox bishopric, and in 1792 Mihai Șuțu ordered that no customs officer interfere with the bishop's collectors. The see had been founded early in the sixteenth century, and its bishops were the town's greatest builders: the Dormition cathedral and the merchants' 'Greeks' church' both went up in 1649, under Matei Basarab. War returned with every decade after that, from Michael the Brave's campaigns in the Long Turkish War to the Wallachian rising of 1821; raids, fires, plague and earthquakes emptied the town more than once, and its people rebuilt every time, putting the phoenix on the city seal in the early eighteenth century. In 1806 the Ottoman army burned Buzău during its war with Russia, the inhabitants fled into the hill villages, and the Drăgaica fair was suspended for many years.
zh:
布泽乌位于布泽乌河右岸，河水在此穿出喀尔巴阡山弯、流入伯勒甘平原，瓦拉几亚通往摩尔多瓦和特兰西瓦尼亚的道路也在这里会合。中世纪时高地上有一座要塞，但真正立城的是贸易：丹二世大公（1420至1431年在位）的一份文书确认这里为集镇和税关，到1431年，商人已在此大量收购周围平原的牲畜和羊毛。1444年的瓦拉几亚向奥斯曼称臣纳贡，布泽乌靠这宗往来为生：剪毛季后从山里下来的牧人把羊毛卖给前往多瑙河和各个山口的商人。

这场仲夏集会就是「德拉加伊卡」羊毛集市的由来。集市起初在布泽乌河谷上游举办，后来迁进城里，在6月24日前后开集。1778年，大公亚历山德鲁·伊普西兰蒂把集市的经办权和全部税入判给东正教教区，1792年米哈伊·舒图又下令税吏不得插手主教属下的征税。主教区设于16世纪初，历任主教是城里最大的营建者：安息大教堂和商人的「希腊人教堂」都建于1649年马泰伊·巴萨拉布在位时。此后战争几乎每十年一轮，从勇士米哈依在漫长土耳其战争中的征战，到1821年的瓦拉几亚起义；劫掠、火灾、瘟疫和地震一再使城市空无一人，居民又每次重建，并在18世纪初把不死鸟铸上市印。1806年俄土战争期间，奥斯曼军焚毁布泽乌，居民逃入丘陵村庄；「德拉加伊卡」也停办多年。

en:
Hormuz is a bare island of salt rock and red ochre, set in the narrow channel where ships leave the Persian Gulf for the Indian Ocean. It has no springs and little soil, but the sea protected it from the Mongol and Turkmen raiders who struck the mainland. The old port stood near Minab until 1301, when Baha ud-Din Ayaz moved the ruler's court and merchants to Jarun, the island that then took the name Hormuz. Boats brought drinking water from the shore, while Arab, Persian and Indian merchants brought spices, pearls, jewels and textiles to its roadstead. An Arabic proverb compared the world to a golden ring and Hormuz to the stone set in it. Zheng He's fourth Ming treasure voyage ended here, and Ma Huan and Fei Xin described handsome dress and wealthy commoners. In 1444 an Arab king ruled the island emporium and dependencies on both sides of the gulf.

The Portuguese agent Pero da Covilha scouted the port in 1488. Afonso de Albuquerque attacked in 1507, and after Portugal established lasting control the Fort of Our Lady of the Conception became the main strongpoint of its gulf position. The king of Hormuz ruled as a vassal largely controlled from Goa, and Hormuzi ships joined the Portuguese invasion of Bahrain in 1521. Piri Reis brought an Ottoman fleet against the fortress in 1552 and could not take it. In 1622 Shah Abbas I used an English fleet to join his own troops in the siege, captured the castle and ended the kingdom. He did not rebuild the island port; he developed Bandar Abbas on the mainland instead. Many families returned seasonally to fields and orchards around old Hormuz, while the permanent islanders were mostly fishermen shipping rock salt and red iron oxide for ballast. In 1794 Hormuz passed with Bandar Abbas under an Omani lease.
zh:
霍尔木兹是一座遍布盐岩和红赭石的荒岛，坐落在波斯湾船只驶入印度洋的狭窄水道上。岛上没有泉水，土壤也少，海水却使它避开了来自内陆的蒙古和土库曼劫掠者。旧港原在米纳布附近，1301年，巴哈乌丁·阿亚兹把王廷和商民迁到当时叫杰龙的岛上，海岛后来也改称霍尔木兹。饮水由船只从大陆运来，阿拉伯、波斯和印度商人则把香料、珍珠、宝石和织物带到锚地。阿拉伯谚语把世界比作一枚金戒指，把霍尔木兹比作戒指上的宝石。郑和第四次下西洋的终点就是这里，马欢和费信都记下当地人衣饰齐整、平民也富有的景象。1444年，一位阿拉伯国王统治着这座岛城和海湾两岸的属邦，这里是波斯湾入口最著名的商埠。

1488年，葡萄牙密使佩罗·达·科维良先到港中侦察。1507年，阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克来攻；葡萄牙站稳脚跟后，「圣母受孕堡」成为其控制海湾的主要据点。霍尔木兹国王沦为附庸，政令多受果阿方面牵制，霍尔木兹船只还参加了1521年葡萄牙人对巴林的进攻。1552年，皮里·雷斯率奥斯曼舰队围攻要塞，未能攻下。1622年，沙阿·阿拔斯一世借英国舰队配合陆军围城，夺取城堡，灭亡霍尔木兹王国。他没有重建岛上港口，转而经营大陆上的阿巴斯港。许多人家季节性地回到旧霍尔木兹周围的农田和果园，岛上的常住居民多为渔民，只能外运岩盐和可作压舱物的红氧化铁。1794年，霍尔木兹随阿巴斯港一并租给阿曼。

en:
Niš commands the Nišava valley on the old road between Belgrade, Sofia and Constantinople. The Roman town of Naissus was a garrison and market in Moesia and the birthplace of Constantine the Great; at Mediana, in its eastern suburbs, he kept a walled villa with baths and a granary where he often resided and issued laws, and later emperors used it on their journeys, among them Valentinian and Valens, who divided the empire there in 364. Attila's army sacked Naissus in 442. The town later passed between Byzantium, Bulgaria, Hungary and Serbia; Stefan Nemanja held it as his capital by 1188 and received Frederick Barbarossa's crusaders there the next year. After the Ottoman conquest of the late fourteenth century the road town changed hands again, and on 8 November 1443 a Hungarian and Serbian army under John Hunyadi defeated the Ottomans outside its walls and returned Niš to Serbian rule. In 1444 it was an Orthodox frontier market of the Despotate, crowded with soldiers and livestock on the road south.

The Ottomans retook Niš in 1448 and made it a military and administrative centre. Austrian troops held it from 1689 to 1690, and the present fortress went up on earlier ramparts between 1719 and 1723, among the best-preserved Ottoman works in the central Balkans; the Austrians came back briefly in 1737. During the First Serbian Uprising the insurgents attacked at Čegar near the town in 1809, and after their defeat the Ottomans built Skull Tower from the heads of the killed Serbs, to warn the surrounding villages. The repression did not ease: in 1821 Bishop Milentije and some two hundred local Serbs were seized while preparing a rising, and the bishop and his fellow leaders were hanged on 13 June.
zh:
尼什扼守尼沙瓦河谷，位于贝尔格莱德、索非亚和君士坦丁堡之间的古道上。罗马城镇纳伊苏斯是默西亚的驻军和集镇，也是君士坦丁大帝的出生地；他在东郊的梅迪亚纳建有带浴室和谷仓的围墙别墅，常在此驻跸、颁布法令，后来的皇帝途经时也在此停留，瓦伦提尼安和瓦伦斯364年就是在这里划分帝国疆土。442年，阿提拉的军队洗劫纳伊苏斯。此后城市在拜占庭、保加利亚、匈牙利和塞尔维亚之间数度易主；斯特凡·尼曼雅到1188年时已以此为都，次年在此接待腓特烈·巴巴罗萨的十字军。14世纪后期奥斯曼征服后，这座道路城镇再度易手，1443年11月8日，匈雅提·亚诺什率领匈牙利和塞尔维亚军队在城外击败奥斯曼人，尼什重归塞尔维亚。1444年，它是专制公国的东正教边贸城镇，南通的道路上挤满士兵和牲畜。

奥斯曼人1448年再取尼什，把它建成军政中心。奥地利军队1689年至1690年占据该城；现存要塞1719年至1723年在旧城墙基址上修筑，是巴尔干中部保存最完好的奥斯曼工事之一；1737年奥军曾短暂重返。第一次塞尔维亚起义期间，起义者1809年在城外的切加尔进攻，战败后，奥斯曼人用阵亡塞尔维亚人的头颅筑起骷髅塔，威吓四乡。高压并未松弛：1821年，米伦蒂耶主教和约二百名当地塞尔维亚人在准备起事时被捕，主教与其他领导人于6月13日被绞死。

en:
Skopje lies in a broad valley on the upper Vardar, where the road from the Danube to the Aegean crosses the river below a fortress hill. Roman Scupi, a colony of veterans of the Seventh Legion, was destroyed by the earthquake of 518, and Justinian I rebuilt the town on the rocky promontory that now holds the citadel. Under Tsar Samuel it was the Bulgarian capital from 972 to 992, and Basil II took it in 1004. The Serbian king Stefan Milutin took it in 1282, and under the Nemanjids merchants from Venice and Dubrovnik kept houses there. Stefan Dusan made Skopje his capital and was crowned emperor of the Serbs and Greeks there on 16 April 1346. After the battle of Maritsa in 1371 it passed to Vuk Brankovic, and the Ottomans took it on 19 January 1392. In 1444 Uskup, as its new rulers called it, was a Rumelian market town on the Vardar road, its bazaar full of passing caravans, its people mostly Orthodox Slavs with a growing Muslim quarter.

Sultan Mehmed II had the Stone Bridge thrown across the Vardar between 1451 and 1469, and the Old Bazaar spread around it with caravanserais, mosques and baths; the Mustafa Pasha Mosque of 1492 is one of the most resplendent Ottoman mosques in the Balkans. At Nerezi above the city, the monastery church of St Panteleimon, built in 1164, holds Komnenian frescoes of the Lamentation of Christ. In 1535 the governor had every town church pulled down, and in 1555 an earthquake wrecked much of Skopje, cracking the bridge columns and the Nerezi frescoes, but the town was soon rebuilt. Evliya Celebi in 1660-1661 counted 12,000 houses, some 60,000 people, 2,150 shops and 120 mosques, with caravans running to Salonika, Belgrade and Dubrovnik. In October 1689, during the Great Turkish War, the Habsburg general Silvio Piccolomini entered a town already weakened by cholera and set it on fire; it burned for two days, and Piccolomini himself died of the plague. The rebel Petar Karpos was impaled on the Stone Bridge. Skopje spent the eighteenth century half in ruins, plague-ridden and passed over by the trade caravans.
zh:
斯科普里坐落在瓦尔达尔河上游的宽阔河谷中，多瑙河通往爱琴海的大道在一座要塞山下渡河。罗马古城斯库皮离此不远，本是第七军团老兵为主的殖民市，518年毁于大地震，查士丁尼一世把城建在岩石岬角上，即今斯科普里城堡所在。972至992年这里是沙皇萨穆伊尔的保加利亚都城，1004年被巴西尔二世攻取；1282年塞尔维亚国王斯特凡·米卢廷夺得此城，尼曼雅王朝时期威尼斯和杜布罗夫尼克的商人在此开有商号。斯特凡·杜尚定斯科普里为都，1346年4月16日在此加冕为塞尔维亚人与希腊人的皇帝。1371年马里查河战役后城市归武克·布兰科维奇，1392年1月19日被奥斯曼人攻占。1444年，这座被新主人称作于斯屈普的城市是鲁米利亚的一处集镇，商队穿巴扎而过，居民以信奉东正教的斯拉夫人为主，旁边是不断扩大的穆斯林区。

穆罕默德二世下令在瓦尔达尔河上修建石桥，工程从1451年持续到1469年，旧巴扎在桥周铺开，商队旅馆、清真寺和浴池连片兴起，1492年的穆斯塔法帕夏清真寺是巴尔干最华丽的奥斯曼宗教建筑之一。城外高处的内雷齐有1164年所建的圣潘捷列伊蒙修道院教堂，保存着科穆宁王朝时期的《哀悼基督》湿壁画。1535年，总督下令拆毁城中所有教堂；1555年地震毁掉大半城区，桥柱与内雷齐壁画受损，城市很快重建。埃夫利亚·切莱比1660至1661年到访时，记下1.2万栋房屋、约6万居民、2150间店铺和120座清真寺，商队从巴扎出发往来于萨洛尼卡、贝尔格莱德和杜布罗夫尼克。1689年10月大土耳其战争期间，哈布斯堡将军西尔维奥·皮科洛米尼进入这座已被霍乱削弱的城市并纵火，大火连烧两天，他本人也死于瘟疫；起义者佩塔尔·卡尔波什被钉死在石桥上。整个18世纪，斯科普里大半残破、瘟疫横行，商队也绕开了它。

en:
Where the Fojnica joins the Bosna, the Visoko valley was the nucleus of the medieval Bosnian state and its coronation ground. On Visočica hill stood the fortress of Visoki, first named in a royal charter of 1355, guarding Podvisoki below, the kingdom's busiest market, where Ragusan merchants bought the grain and hides of the fertile plain. Nearby at Mile the nobles' assembly, the stanak, met and the state archives were kept; Tvrtko I was crowned king there in 1377 and later buried beside his uncle Stjepan II, and the churchyard held the carved tombs of kings and bans. At Moštre the Bosnian Church ran a school that Vatican records mention for medicine, theology, cosmogony and ethics, and at Biskupići a ruined church yielded Ban Kulin's inscribed plate of 1193. The last royal charter issued from Visoki is dated 1436. In 1444 the valley remained the kingdom's prosperous centre under its new king Tomaš, although the court had withdrawn to Bobovac and Ottoman armies were closing on the Drina.

When the kingdom collapsed in 1463 the old strongholds fell into ruin, and Visoki vanished from the records before 1503. A new Ottoman town grew below the hill under Ajas-beg, a local man converted from the Bosnian Church: by 1477 he had built a hammam, mekteb, madrasa, aqueduct and a bridge over the Bosna, and endowed a Naqshbandi tekke. Visoko became the seat of a nahiya and a centre of trade and leatherwork, while the medieval stećak graveyards around the valley slowly vanished under grass as the townspeople turned to Islam. Unlike the frontier lands on the Sava and the Una, this basin saw no great battle through the long Ottoman centuries, and Visoko entered the nineteenth century as a quiet provincial market town.
zh:
福伊尼察河注入波斯纳河处的维索科河谷，是中世纪波斯尼亚国家的发祥和加冕之地。维索齐察山上的维索基要塞首见于1355年的一份王家诏书，拱卫着山下的波德维索基，即王国最繁忙的集镇，拉古萨商人在此收购肥沃平原出产的谷物和皮革。附近的米莱是贵族会议召开和保存国家档案之处，特尔特科一世1377年在此加冕为王，身后与舅父斯捷潘二世同葬于此，墓园中还有历代国王和班的雕饰石墓。莫什特雷有波斯尼亚教会的学府，梵蒂冈的档案提到它兼修医学、神学、宇宙生成和伦理；比斯库皮奇的一座废教堂遗址出土了班·库林1193年的铭文石版。维索基颁出的最后一份王家诏书是在1436年。1444年，新王托马什治下的河谷仍是王国最富庶的中心，只是宫廷已退守博博瓦茨，奥斯曼大军正逼近德里纳河。

1463年王国覆灭，旧日堡垒沦为废墟，维索基在1503年之前便从记载中消失。山下兴起一座奥斯曼新城，营造者阿亚斯贝伊是本地人，出身波斯尼亚教会、后改奉伊斯兰：到1477年，他已建起公共浴室、经文小学、经学院、水道和波斯纳河桥，并捐建了一座纳克什班迪教团道堂。维索科成为一个纳希耶的治所，也是贸易和皮革业中心；随着居民渐渐改奉伊斯兰，河谷里中世纪的斯特恰克石墓慢慢荒没在草间。与萨瓦河、乌纳河畔的边地不同，这片盆地在漫长的奥斯曼数百年间没有经历大战，维索科作为一座安静的外省集镇走入19世纪。

en:
Euboea is a long island parallel to the Greek mainland, and at Chalcis the Euripus Strait narrows enough for a bridge to join the two shores. Western sailors turned the Greek name Euripos into the Italian form Negroponte, with its echo of a black bridge. After the Fourth Crusade Lombard barons divided the island among the triarchs, while Venice steadily tightened its hold on the port and took full sovereignty in 1390. The Republic brought in Albanian clans to repopulate villages thinned by raids, settling 10,000 people in 1425 alone, and fortified Chalcis as a staging port for galleys sailing between Venice, Crete and Constantinople. In 1444 Greek Orthodox farmers and fishermen, some of Albanian descent, lived under Latin garrisons, and Negroponte guarded Venice's route through the central Aegean.

Mehmed II struck that route in the summer of 1470. By Venetian and later Greek accounts, he came in person with 70,000 men and 400 ships; his galleys closed the Euripus with a chain while his army laid a bridge of boats to the island. After nearly a month of costly assaults, Negroponte was stormed on 12 July. Venetian reports said the bailo Paolo Erizzo was sawn in two after the fall. The Ottomans called the town Eğriboz and made it the seat of a sanjak reaching far into the Greek mainland; Ottoman families took the richer plains while Greek communities held the hills. Francesco Morosini besieged Eğriboz for three months in 1688 without taking it. On 8 May 1821 the island rose at Istiaia under Angelis Govios, and Kymi, Limni and Styra joined the revolt.
zh:
埃维亚是一座与希腊本土平行的长岛；在哈尔基斯，埃夫里普海峡收窄到可以架桥连通两岸。西方水手把希腊语名称埃夫里普斯读成意大利语的内格罗蓬特，词形里又带上了「黑桥」的联想。第四次十字军东征后，伦巴第男爵把岛屿分给三方领主，威尼斯则逐步控制港口，于1390年取得完整主权。共和国迁来阿尔巴尼亚部族，补充遭袭后人口稀少的村庄，仅1425年就安置了一万人；哈尔基斯也被筑成桨帆船往来威尼斯、克里特和君士坦丁堡的补给港。1444年，信奉东正教的希腊农夫和渔民（其中一些有阿尔巴尼亚血统）生活在拉丁守军治下，内格罗蓬特则扼守威尼斯穿过爱琴海中部的航路。

1470年夏，穆罕默德二世亲自动手切断这条航路。据威尼斯人和后世希腊记载，他带来七万陆军和四百艘战船；桨帆军用铁链封锁埃夫里普海峡，陆军则搭起浮桥直通岛上。经过近一个月伤亡惨重的强攻，内格罗蓬特于7月12日陷落。威尼斯记载称，驻节长官保罗·埃里佐在城破后被锯成两段。奥斯曼人称此城为埃格里博兹，把它设为桑贾克治所，辖地深入希腊本土；奥斯曼家庭占去较肥沃的平原，希腊社区则保有山地。1688年，弗朗切斯科·莫罗西尼围攻埃格里博兹三个月，仍未能破城。1821年5月8日，安盖利斯·戈维奥斯在伊斯蒂亚亚举事，库米、利姆尼和斯蒂拉随后响应。

en:
The Comoros, Ngazidja, Ndzuwani, Mwali and Mayotte, form a volcanic chain across the northern mouth of the Mozambique Channel. Bantu farmers from the Swahili coast, together with Malagasy and Austronesian seafarers, had settled the islands by the eighth century. From the eleventh century merchants of Kilwa, Sofala and Mombasa worked them into the monsoon trade, buying ivory, tortoiseshell, ambergris, gold and slaves and carrying them to Arabia, Persia and India, while Islam took root among the harbour towns. By 1444 Ndzuwani was a Muslim island of stone-built ports. Its oldest is Domoni on the east coast, a Swahili town of the twelfth century whose merchants traded with Africa, Persia and India; finds there have been traced as far as Japan, and the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid, who piloted Vasco da Gama to India, knew it as a major trading centre. Walls enclosed its mosques and the palaces of its Shirazi elite. The rest of the island was shared among local chiefs.

Mutsamudu, on the north coast, was probably founded in 1482 and by the eighteenth century was the busiest port in the archipelago; a European commissioner who landed there in 1773 noted stone houses whitewashed inside and out, public baths and two-storey villas. Before that, late in the fifteenth century, Sharif families from the Hadramawt married into Ndzuwani's ruling houses and established the Sultanate of Anjouan, the strongest power in the islands by 1500, while Ngazidja stayed split between rival sultans. Portuguese ships first called in 1503, and for much of the sixteenth century Ndzuwani provisioned Portugal's fort on Mozambique Island, though Portugal never attempted a conquest. English captains knew the island as Johanna and brought their India-bound ships in for water, cattle, coconuts and tortoiseshell; the same sea lanes later carried islanders away as slaves to the Mascarene plantations. From the 1790s Sakalava and Betsimisaraka fleets from Madagascar burned the coastal towns and carried off their people, and at the end of the century Sultan Abdallah I moved his court from Domoni to Mutsamudu. In 1812 Sultan Alawi bin Husain asked Britain for help against the raiders and was refused. In 1821 the islands were still in local hands, their villages thinned and their trade broken.
zh:
科摩罗是恩加济贾（大科摩罗）、恩祖瓦尼（昂儒昂）、姆瓦利（莫埃利）和马约特四座火山岛组成的岛链，横在莫桑比克海峡北口。至迟8世纪，来自斯瓦希里海岸的班图农民以及马尔加什和南岛水手已在各岛定居。11世纪起，基尔瓦、索法拉、蒙巴萨的商人把群岛纳入季风贸易，收购象牙、玳瑁、龙涎香、黄金和奴隶，运往阿拉伯、波斯和印度，伊斯兰教也在港镇中扎下根。到1444年，恩祖瓦尼已是一座以石砌港镇闻名的穆斯林岛屿。东岸的多莫尼最为古老，这座12世纪兴起的斯瓦希里商埠与非洲、波斯和印度通商，当地出土器物中甚至有远自日本辗转传来的物件；为瓦斯科·达·伽马引航到印度的航海家艾哈迈德·伊本·马吉德也称它是重要商港。城墙之内有清真寺和设拉子望族的王宫。岛的其余部分则由众多地方首领分治，没有共主。

北岸的穆察穆杜约建于1482年，到18世纪已是全群岛最繁忙的港口；1773年一位登岸的欧洲专员记下，这里的石屋内外都粉刷洁白，有公共浴室和两层高的宅邸。更早以前的15世纪末，哈德拉毛的谢里夫家族与恩祖瓦尼统治家族联姻，建立昂儒昂苏丹国，到1500年已凌驾各岛，恩加济贾则仍由几个互不相让的苏丹分治。葡萄牙船队1503年首次到访，16世纪大部分时间里，恩祖瓦尼为葡萄牙人在莫桑比克岛的要塞供应补给，里斯本却没有发兵征服。英国船长把此岛称作约翰娜，驶往印度的船进港补给淡水、牲畜、椰子和玳瑁；同一条海路后来也把岛民当奴隶运往马斯克林的种植园。1790年代起，马达加斯加的萨卡拉瓦人和贝齐米萨拉卡人的船队焚毁沿岸城镇、掳走人口，苏丹阿卜杜拉一世在18世纪末把宫廷从多莫尼迁往穆察穆杜。1812年，苏丹阿拉维·本·侯赛因请求英国出兵抵御劫掠者，遭到拒绝。1821年，各岛仍在本地统治者手中，只是村社凋零、商路残破。

en:
Antankara is the northern tip of Madagascar. The Ankarana massif cuts across it, a plateau of grey tsingy limestone that rain has eaten into jagged ridges, caves and underground rivers, with dry forest in the hollows; beyond it the great bay later called Diego-Suarez bites deep into the shore. In 1444 the Vohilava, Antambohitsy and other Malagasy clans of the tip fished from dugout canoes, herded zebu, boiled sea salt and sold tortoiseshell to the dhow captains who called along the coast. They answered to no king, for the Sakalava kingdoms were still gathering far to the south-west.

Early in the sixteenth century Portuguese captains gave the great bay its European name, Diego-Suarez, and foreign ships began to call there for tortoiseshell. The Antankarana kingdom grew out of a Sakalava succession feud: in the early seventeenth century the Zafin'i'fotsy, the 'children of silver', lost the kingship to the Zafin'i'mena, the 'children of gold', and moved north with their herds; their chief Kozobe claimed the whole tip and divided it among five sons. Hard pressed by the new Sakalava kingdom of Iboina, Andriantsirotso (r. 1692–1710) led his people into the Ankarana caves and then to refuge at Maroantsetra, and three years later came back with soldiers lent by his kinsman Raholo and drove the Sakalava out. The clans he united took their name from the rocks, Antankarana, 'the people of the tsingy'. Lamboeny, who followed him, ruled eighty years, and the kings kept their court near Ambatoharaña and traded tortoiseshell and slaves for guns with the ships in the bay. In the reign of Tsialana I, from 1809, the armies of expanding Imerina pushed up the northern trade routes, built garrisons and tax posts, and around 1818 forced the king to accept vassalage, the position in which the north stood in 1821.
zh:
安坦卡拉位于马达加斯加岛最北端。安卡拉纳山地横亘岛尖，灰色的钦吉石灰岩被雨水溶蚀成犬牙交错的石脊、溶洞与暗河，洼地里长着旱生林；山地之外，后来得名迪耶果-苏瓦雷斯的大海湾深深切入海岸。1444年，岛尖的沃希拉瓦、安坦博希齐等马尔加什氏族驾独木舟捕鱼、牧养瘤牛、煮晒海盐，把玳瑁壳卖给沿岸停靠的单桅帆船船长。他们不奉共主，萨卡拉瓦诸王国还在遥远的西南方成形。

16世纪初，葡萄牙船长为这座大海湾取了欧洲名字迪耶果-苏瓦雷斯，外国船开始来此收购玳瑁。安坦卡拉王国起于萨卡拉瓦人的王位之争：17世纪初，争位失败的「银系」扎菲尼夫齐不敌「金系」扎菲尼梅纳，带着部众北迁，其首领科佐贝宣称领有整个岛尖，分给五个儿子。面对萨卡拉瓦伊博伊纳王国的逼迫，安德里安齐罗措（1692—1710年在位）率众退入安卡拉纳溶洞，又避往马鲁安采特拉，三年后借亲族拉霍洛的兵回师，把萨卡拉瓦人赶了出去；他联合起来的诸氏族便以石林为名，称安坦卡拉，意为「钦吉之人」。继他而立的兰博埃尼统治长达八十年，历代国王在安巴托哈拉尼亚一带驻帐，用玳瑁和奴隶向湾内船只换购火枪。1809年齐亚拉纳一世即位后，扩张中的伊梅里纳沿北方商路推进，设立驻军和税卡，约在1818年迫使安坦卡拉王称臣，这正是1821年北方的处境。

en:
The shores of Boina Bay and the Betsiboka estuary were for centuries the busiest sea edge of western Madagascar. Muslim, Swahili-speaking Antalaotra had settled here from the tenth century, and by the late 1400s the Arab navigator Ibn Majid could count more than a dozen ports along this coast. In 1444 dhows from Mozambique, Arabia and the Comoros beached at its roadsteads to barter beads, cloth and metalware for cattle, rice and captives, and Mazalagem Nova was already the richest Muslim mart on the island's north-west. Inland, Sakalava-speaking clans grazed zebu on the plains and answered to no single ruler. No European ship had yet called, and the port of Mahajanga did not yet exist.

Portuguese ships reached Madagascar around 1500, and by the 1690s the island's northern coast sheltered about five hundred European pirates. Into this coast came Andriamandisoarivo, a son of the Menabe king Andriandahifotsy, driven out by his brother in 1685: with some eight hundred followers he fought his way north through Ambongo, overran the Antalaotra of Mahajamba Bay, stormed Mazalagem Nova and killed its sultan, and about 1690 founded the kingdom of Iboina, seat of the Volamena, or 'red gold', dynasty. He put the new port of Mahajanga in charge of the kingdom's trade and ruled from Tongay on Boina Bay. His successors were quasi-divine kings who interceded with the ancestors; the Antankarana of the far north paid them tribute, and in 1720 King Toakafo was accounted the mightiest ruler in Madagascar. Tom Similaho, the son of an English pirate and a Malagasy woman, served for a time as chief minister to a Boina king.

Mahajanga carried the kingdom's trade. An English captain who saw it in 1764 found stone houses and mosques built 'after the Indian fashion', with merchants from Surat, Anjouan, Mozambique and the Comoros striking deals under the king's trade officers; Muslims worshipped freely, and captives were the port's chief cargo while the Sakalava held Madagascar's slave trade in their hands until the end of the century. French probes in the 1770s were beaten off, and in the 1780s a French traveller counted some two hundred Indian Muslim traders settled at the Betsiboka mouth, in the long reign of Queen Ravahiny. In 1817 Radama I of Imerina promised Britain to end the slave trade in exchange for arms and turned his reformed armies against the Sakalava. The Boina court leaned on its Muslim councillors and on France, but in 1821 Merina troops had not yet crossed the Betsiboka.
zh:
博伊纳湾沿岸与贝齐布卡河口，几个世纪里一直是马达加斯加西部最繁忙的海岸。讲斯瓦希里语的穆斯林安塔劳特拉人自10世纪起在此定居，到15世纪末，阿拉伯航海家伊本·马吉德已能在这一带数出十几处港埠。1444年，来自莫桑比克、阿拉伯和科摩罗的独桅帆船在锚地靠岸，用珠子、布匹和金属器皿换取牛只、稻米和俘虏，马扎拉任诺瓦已是西北海岸最富庶的穆斯林商埠。内陆平原上，讲萨卡拉瓦语的诸氏族放牧瘤牛，不奉任何共主。此时还没有欧洲船只到访，马任加港也尚未出现。

约1500年，葡萄牙船只到达马达加斯加；到17世纪90年代，岛的北海岸聚集了约五百名欧洲海盗。就在这片海岸，梅纳贝国王安德里安达希富齐之子安德里亚曼迪苏阿里武在1685年被兄长逐出，率约八百部众北上，一路穿过安邦戈，攻陷马哈詹巴湾的安塔劳特拉人之地，攻克马扎拉任诺瓦、杀死其苏丹，于1690年前后建立伊博伊纳王国，开创意为「红金」的武拉梅纳王朝。他让新都马任加掌管全国贸易，自己定都博伊纳湾畔的通盖。继他而立的是介于人神之间、为祖先与世人传话的国王；极北之地的安塔卡拉纳人向他们纳贡，1720年时，托阿卡福国王被视为全岛最强大的统治者。英国海盗与马尔加什女子之子汤姆·西米拉霍，还曾一度出任博伊纳国王的首辅。

马任加承载着王国的贸易。1764年，一名英国船长见到城中石屋与清真寺皆「按印度样式」建造，来自苏拉特、昂儒昂、莫桑比克和科摩罗的商人在王室贸易官的监管下成交，穆斯林可以自由礼拜；俘虏是这座港口最大宗的货物，直到18世纪末，全岛的奴隶贸易都握在萨卡拉瓦人手中。1770年代法国人的试探被击退；1780年代，一名法国旅行者在贝齐布卡河口数到约两百名定居的印度穆斯林商人，时值拉瓦希尼女王漫长的统治。1817年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世以废除奴隶贸易为条件换取英国军火，把整编后的军队转向萨卡拉瓦人。博伊纳宫廷倚重穆斯林谋臣、向法国靠拢，但到1821年，梅里纳军队还没有越过贝齐布卡河。

en:
The Tsimihety country is the broken mountain land of north-central Madagascar, between the Merina highlands and the Sakalava plains, its valleys draining toward the Sofia river. Its people were farmers and zebu herders who lived in independent village clans; their society was strongly egalitarian, with no king or chiefs set above the villagers. In 1444, even while Muslim trading towns were taking shape on the coast, these remote valleys answered to no outside ruler.

Their name means 'those who never cut their hair', and it records that independence: when the Sakalava kingdom to the west claimed their obedience and demanded the mourning haircut after a ruler's death, they refused. They were still a warlike, kingless people at the end of the eighteenth century, when they fought the unifying armies of Andrianampoinimerina.
zh:
齐米赫蒂之地是马达加斯加中北部崎岖的山区，夹在梅里纳高地与萨卡拉瓦平原之间，山谷的水流汇入索非亚河。齐米赫蒂人以农为业、牧放瘤牛，散居在各自独立的村落氏族中；社会奉行强平等，没有国王，也没有凌驾于村民之上的首领。1444年，沿海虽在形成穆斯林贸易城镇，这些偏远山谷仍不臣服于任何外来统治者。

他们的族名意为「不剪头发的人」，这份独立也写在名字里：当西方的萨卡拉瓦王国对他们提出宗主要求、命他们在国王死后剪发服丧时，他们拒绝从命。到18世纪末，他们仍是尚武而无王的族群，迎战安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳的统一大军。

en:
Maroantsetra lies at the mouth of the Antainambalana River, where it enters the Bay of Antongil, the largest bay in Madagascar, ringed by the wettest rainforest on the island. In 1444 the people later called Betsimisaraka lived in small villages of fishermen and rice farmers, each under a filohany who ruled little more than a village or two; the chiefs about the bay kept regalia that set them above their neighbours, and their canoes carried rice, slaves and tortoiseshell to the dhows trading along the northern coast.

The first European ship stumbled in by accident: in August 1500 Diogo Dias, blown off course from Cabral's fleet bound for India, became the first European to sight Madagascar, and Portuguese captains soon learned the shelter of Antongil. From the 1680s British and American pirates gathered along this coast and married chiefs' daughters; their mixed descendants were the zana-malata. The most famous of them, Ratsimilaho, is said to have been the son of Queen Rahena and the English pirate Thomas Tew, and as a boy he sailed with his father to England and India. In 1710 southern clans under Ramanano of Vatomandry invaded the northern ports, burning villages and desecrating tombs; Ratsimilaho led the resistance, took Fenerive and drove the enemy south across fields of wet red clay that stuck to their feet, which earned them the name Betanimena, 'many of red earth'. Elected king at Foulpointe, he named his own people Betsimisaraka, 'the many inseparables', and over a reign of about fifty years built the confederation that stretched four hundred miles along the coast to Toamasina, marrying a daughter of the Sakalava king of Iboina to bind the west to him. The union loosened after he died. In February 1774 the Hungarian adventurer Maurice Benyovszky landed here to found the French colony of Louisbourg, with a hospital and a quarantine post on Nosy Mangabe island; he persuaded the local chiefs to acknowledge him as king of Madagascar, but the outpost was abandoned soon after he left. In 1817 the armies of Radama I of Imerina subdued the whole coast, and Maroantsetra entered the Merina empire.
zh:
马鲁安采特拉在安泰南巴兰纳河注入安通吉尔湾的河口上。安通吉尔湾是马达加斯加最大的海湾，环抱着全岛最湿润的雨林。1444年，后来被称作贝齐米萨拉卡人的居民住在一个个捕鱼种稻的小村里，各由一位菲卢哈尼统辖，权势通常不出一两座村落；湾边的酋长保留着高人一等的仪仗，他们的独木舟把稻米、奴隶和玳瑁壳运给北方海岸的单桅帆船。

第一艘欧洲船是误打误撞进来的：1500年8月，随卡布拉尔赴印度舰队失散的迪奥戈·迪亚斯成为第一个望见马达加斯加的欧洲人，葡萄牙船长们很快晓得了安通吉尔湾的避风良港。1680年代起，英美海盗聚集在这段海岸，娶酋长的女儿为妻，他们的混血后代称扎纳-马拉塔。其中最出名的拉齐米拉胡，相传是女王拉海娜与英国海盗托马斯·图之子，年少时还随父亲到过英格兰和印度。1710年，瓦图曼德里的拉马纳诺率南方氏族进犯北方港口，烧村掘墓；拉齐米拉胡率众抵抗，连克北方港口，把敌人赶过黏脚的湿红泥田，他们脚上沾满红泥，得了贝塔尼梅纳之名，意为「众多红土人」。获胜后他被推举为王，给自己人取名贝齐米萨拉卡，意为「密不可分的众人」；约五十年的统治把沿岸绵延四百英里直至图阿马西纳的氏族结成联盟，又娶萨卡拉瓦伊博伊纳国王之女，把西海岸也绑在自己一边。他死后联盟松散下来。1774年2月，匈牙利冒险家莫里斯·贝尼奥夫斯基在此登陆，建立法国殖民地路易堡，设有医院，并在诺西曼加贝岛上设立检疫站；他还说服当地酋长承认他为马达加斯加国王，但据点在他离开后不久便荒废。1817年，伊梅里纳的拉达马一世大军征服整个东岸，马鲁安采特拉并入梅里纳帝国。

en:
Vatomandry lies on Madagascar's rain-drenched eastern shore, where two dark rocks stand at the water's edge; its name means 'Sleeping Rocks'. Lacking the sheltered bays that made ports farther north, in the fifteenth century this stretch of coast held only small chiefdoms: Malagasy clans worked wet-rice fields and herded zebu under filohany headmen who ruled a village or two, honoured their ancestors and held tromba possession rites. No European ship had yet reached the island, and such trade as there was moved between coastal villages in canoes.

The first European sighting of Madagascar came off this coast on 10 August 1500, when the Portuguese captain Diogo Dias, blown off course for India, raised the island. From the 1680s British and American pirates settled the northern bays and married chiefs' daughters, fathering the mixed zana-malata, while rice, cattle and captives shipped out of Foulpointe and Tamatave to the French Mascarene Islands. Vatomandry enters the story in 1710, when its chief Ramanano was elected head of the southern Tsikoa league and sent a militia north from Vohimasina to burn villages, desecrate tombs and carry off women and children. A young zana-malata of Foulpointe, Ratsimilaho, held by tradition to be the son of the pirate Thomas Tew and to have sailed with him as far as England and India, led the northern resistance and took Fenerive in 1712. The Tsikoa fled over clay fields that clung red to their feet and were mocked as the Betanimena, the 'Many Red Earth'. Ratsimilaho was elected king at Foulpointe, gave his followers the name Betsimisaraka, and ruled until 1750, one of the strongest kings in Madagascar. His weak heirs let French traders and slavers take over the shore, and in 1817 the Merina king Radama I marched 25,000 men on Tamatave and planted garrisons across the east.
zh:
瓦图曼德里位于马达加斯加雨水丰沛的东岸，海边立着两块黑色巨石，地名意为「安睡的岩石」。这一带海岸没有北方那种可供停泊的海湾，15世纪时只有一些小酋邦：马尔加什诸氏族耕种水田、牧养瘤牛，菲卢哈尼酋长通常只统辖一两个村落，人们敬奉祖先，举行通巴降神仪式。当时还没有欧洲船到过这座岛，仅有的贸易靠独木舟在沿岸村落之间往来。

1500年8月10日，欧洲人第一次望见马达加斯加，地点就在这一带海面。驶往印度的葡萄牙船长迪奥戈·迪亚斯被风浪吹偏航线，远远看到这座岛。17世纪80年代起，英、美海盗在北方港湾落脚，与酋长的女儿通婚，生下混血的扎纳马拉塔人；稻米、牛和俘虏从富尔潘特、塔马塔夫装船，运往法国人的马斯克林群岛。瓦图曼德里在1710年卷入这段历史：本地酋长拉马纳诺被推举为南方齐科亚联盟的首领，从武希马西纳派出民军北上，焚烧村庄、亵渎坟墓、掳走妇女儿童。富尔潘特的扎纳马拉塔青年拉齐米拉霍率众抵抗，相传他是海盗托马斯·图的儿子，还曾随父亲远航英格兰和印度；1712年他攻克费内里夫，齐科亚人穿过粘脚的红泥田溃逃，被讥为「贝塔尼梅纳」，意为「众多红土之人」。拉齐米拉霍在富尔潘特被推举为王，给部众取名贝齐米萨拉卡，统治到1750年，是马达加斯加最强的国王之一。他的后继者软弱，法国商人和奴隶贩子逐步把持海岸；1817年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世率军两万五千攻打塔马塔夫，在东部各处驻扎守军。

en:
Vohipeno stands on the low, rain-soaked Matitanana coast, the country called Imoro, home of the Antemoro, the 'people of the shore'. Its villagers fished the Indian Ocean, grew rice on the coastal plain, and traded with ships crossing the Mozambique Channel. In 1444 the shore was divided among competing Malagasy clans, above all the high-status Zafiraminia, descendants of seafarers who alone performed the ritual sacrifice to the ancestors. Marrying in among them were Muslim families from overseas, the Anteony and the Antalaotra, who claimed Arab and Persian descent and held to Islam; among their descendants the ban on pork long outlasted the faith itself. They commanded a knowledge of writing no other Malagasy clan possessed, the Sorabe script that wrote Malagasy in Arabic letters, and their astrology and manuscripts gave them a standing no local family could match.

During the 1400s and 1500s the newcomers merged with the people of the plain and made Matitana the centre of Antemoro power. Around 1550, after its leader married a local woman, the Zafikasimambo family overthrew the Zafiraminia and founded a kingdom ruled through scribal learning, ritual and the ombiasy, their learned men. Antemoro ombiasy fanned out across Madagascar, casting horoscopes and selling charms, serving as advisers at courts from the central highlands to the Sakalava west, and some founded principalities of their own; their Sorabe manuscripts carried the Malagasy language into writing. By the early 1700s the Matitanana coast also shipped rice and captives overseas. Long wars with the Ikongo-Tanala later carried invasion into the plain, and in the late 1700s the Antemoro sought the friendship of Andrianampoinimerina of Imerina; under Radama I, Antemoro scholars served the highland court that was uniting the island.
zh:
武希佩努位于地势低平、雨水丰沛的马塔蒂塔纳海滨，这片称作伊莫罗的土地是安泰莫罗人，即「海岸之民」的家园。村民在印度洋捕鱼，在沿海平原种稻，同横渡莫桑比克海峡的船只贸易。1444年时，海岸由彼此竞争的马尔加什氏族分据，地位最高的是扎菲拉米尼亚人，这支海民后裔垄断着祭祀祖先的牲祭之礼。来自海外的穆斯林家族安泰奥尼和安塔劳特拉正通过联姻在他们中间扎根，他们自称有阿拉伯和波斯血统、信奉伊斯兰教；在其后人中间，不食猪肉的禁忌比信仰本身存留得更久。他们掌握着其他马尔加什氏族所没有的文字，即用阿拉伯字母拼写马尔加什语的苏拉贝文，星象之学和典籍为他们赢得了本地家族难以比肩的地位。

15至16世纪，这些新来者与平原上的居民融合，把马塔蒂塔纳变成安泰莫罗权力的中心。约1550年，扎菲卡西姆博家族的首领同本地女子联姻，随后推翻扎菲拉米尼亚人、建立王国，凭书写之学、祭祀和「翁比亚西」智者进行统治。安泰莫罗的翁比亚西游走马达加斯加全岛，占星、售卖护身符，在中部高地到西部萨卡拉瓦的各处王廷充当顾问，有的还自建小邦；他们的苏拉贝抄本让马尔加什语落成文字。到18世纪初，马塔蒂塔纳海岸也向海外输出稻米和俘虏。此后同伊孔古—塔纳拉人的长期战争把战火烧进平原，18世纪末安泰莫罗人谋求与伊麦里纳的安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳交好；到拉达马一世时代，安泰莫罗学者已在那个正在统一全岛的高地王廷效力。

en:
The Betsileo country fills the southern half of Madagascar's central highlands, from the Mania river in the north to the granite walls of the Andringitra massif in the south, shut in by the Bongolava hills and the eastern rainforest. Its people made the wet valleys into the island's most carefully worked rice land, terracing the hillsides and channelling water from one flooded field into the next, while zebu herds grazed the higher ground. In 1444 the country was a scatter of clan chiefdoms, none strong enough to rule the rest, and its rice and cattle went mostly unseen by the merchants of the coast.

In the seventeenth century the chiefdoms hardened into kingdoms, among them Isandra, Lalangina, Fandriana and Fisakana. Tradition gives their name, 'the many invincible ones', to a King Besilau who threw back a Sakalava invasion from Menabe in the 1670s. Isandra grew strongest, its rulers absorbing Lalangina and Vohibato and drawing wealth from trade that crossed the island to the port of Toliara. The kingdoms kept their independence through the wars of the eighteenth century, but the Merina armies of Andrianampoinimerina opened the way south and his son Radama I completed the conquest. Many Betsileo were sold into slavery, and the Merina built Fianarantsoa, Malagasy for 'good learning', as the new administrative capital over the conquered southern highlands.
zh:
贝齐略之地位于马达加斯加中部高地南半段，北起马尼亚河，南抵安德林吉特拉山地的花岗岩绝壁，西屏邦古拉瓦丘陵，东界热带雨林。贝齐略人把湿润山谷垦成岛上耕作最精细的稻田：山坡上层层梯田相接，渠水从一块蓄水田引入下一块，高处的坡地则牧放瘤牛群。1444年时，这里只是一片零散的氏族酋邦，谁也压服不了谁，稻米和牛群也大多不为沿海商人所知。

17世纪，诸酋邦演变为伊桑德拉、拉兰吉纳、凡德里亚纳、菲萨卡纳等王国。按口传传统，族名「众多不可战胜者」得自贝齐劳王，他在1670年代击退了来自梅纳伯的萨卡拉瓦人入侵。伊桑德拉最为强盛，其君主兼并拉兰吉纳和沃希巴图，靠横穿全岛、通往图利亚拉港的贸易致富。这些王国在18世纪的战乱中保持独立，但安德里亚南普伊奈梅里纳的梅里纳大军打开了南进之路，其子拉达马一世完成征服；许多贝齐略人被卖为奴，梅里纳人又修建菲亚纳兰楚阿（马拉加什语意为「良好的教化」），作为统治被征服南部高地的新行政首府。

en:
Mahafaly is the dry limestone and sand country of southwestern Madagascar between the Menarandra and Onilahy rivers, around Betioky, Ejeda and Ampanihy; its people, tradition says, came up from southeastern Africa in the twelfth century. Their name is read either as 'those who make happy' or, the reading linguists prefer, 'those who make holy'. Wealth and chiefly power ran on cattle, sheep and goats, with cassava and grain grown in the thinner coastal plains, and the Mahafaly spent that wealth on their dead: chiefs and kings lay under vast stone tombs ringed with the skulls of slaughtered zebu and set with aloalo, tall carved posts topped by figures and birds that recounted the dead person's life, the word alo meaning a messenger who carries the deceased among the ancestors. In 1444 the land was divided among the old ruling families called andriantsileliky.

In the 1500s the Maroserana noble Olembetsitoto defeated or displaced those families and founded the dynasty that gave the Mahafaly their political identity; when he later withdrew into seclusion his followers held he had grown holy, faly, and made his land and people maha-faly, with an ombiasy speaking between the hidden ruler and his people. In June 1649 twelve Mahafaly envoys travelled to the French settlement of Fort Dauphin and hired French mercenaries against the Masikoro, who had raided the king's cattle. The kingdom then split into Sakatovo and Menarandra around 1650, Linta some twenty years later, and Onilahy around 1750; the kings of Menarandra also seized the Antandroy province of Karimbola, and the Onilahy court took the Antemoro-style title andrianony for its ruler. These small kingdoms changed rulers often, but the highland armies of Imerina never reached them, and in 1821 Mahafaly still stood outside Merina rule.
zh:
马哈法利位于马达加斯加西南部，是门纳兰德拉河与奥尼拉希河之间干旱的石灰岩和沙土地带，贝蒂乌基、埃热达和安帕尼希一带；相传其先民在12世纪从非洲东南部迁来。族名一说是「使人快乐之人」，语言学家更倾向「使土地成圣之人」。财富和酋权都建立在牛、绵羊和山羊之上，居民也在较贫瘠的沿海平原种植木薯和谷物，而马哈法利人把大笔财富花在死者身上：酋长和国王葬在巨大的石墓中，墓周环绕献祭瘤牛的头骨，墓上竖立「阿罗阿罗」雕刻高柱，柱顶雕有人物和禽鸟，讲述死者的生平；「阿罗」意为使者，负责把死者引荐到祖先中间。1444年时，这片土地由称作「安德里安齐莱利基」的旧有统治家族分据。

16世纪，马拉塞拉纳贵族奥伦贝齐托托击败或取代这些家族，建立王朝，也塑造了马哈法利人的政治认同；他后来退居隐修，信众认为他已成圣，并使这片土地和人民随之成圣，由一名「翁比亚西」在隐居的统治者与民众之间传话。1649年6月，十二名马哈法利使者前往法国人的多凡堡殖民地，雇用法国雇佣兵攻打劫走国王牛群的马西科罗人。王国随后分裂：萨卡托沃和梅纳兰德拉约于1650年形成，林塔约二十年后分立，奥尼拉希则在1750年左右成形；梅纳兰德拉的国王还夺取了安坦德鲁伊人的卡里姆博拉地方，奥尼拉希王廷则仿照安泰莫罗人，以「安德里亚诺尼」作为君主称号。这些小王国统治者更替频繁，但伊麦里纳的高原军队始终没有到达；1821年时，马哈法利仍处在梅里纳王国的统治之外。

en:
Anosy is the wet southeastern tip of Madagascar, the coast and Efaho valley around Tolagnaro, between the Masianaka and Mandrare rivers. Its people fished the coastal lagoons, sailed the Indian Ocean, grew rice and sweet potatoes and herded zebu; blacksmiths worked local iron and carvers shaped chlorite schist, which went north by canoe in exchange for Chinese greenware. The name means 'islands' in Malagasy, after the flood plains and lagoons that break the shoreline. In 1444 its villages lay beyond the Antemoro trading states up the coast, though their worked stone and cattle already drew Muslim shipping down from the north.

European ships met Madagascar on this coast. On 10 August 1500 Diogo Dias, blown off course from the second Portuguese India Armada, sighted it here and named the island São Lourenço. At least five Portuguese ships were wrecked on the coast between 1504 and 1507, and survivors may have built Tranovato, a ten-metre square stone blockhouse on a hill west of Tolagnaro and probably the first European building on the island. In 1613 a Portuguese expedition met King Andriantsiambany at Manafiafy and left Jesuits to preach, but after the Portuguese carried the king's son off to Goa for his schooling, trade was cut off and the missionaries withdrew in 1617 with one baptism to show for their stay. In 1643 Jacques de Pronis founded Fort-Dauphin on the village of Taolankarana, naming it for the dauphin, the future Louis XIV, and married a local noblewoman. Étienne de Flacourt, governor from 1648, put what he learned into his 'History of the Great Isle of Madagascar', Europe's main book on the island for two centuries.

The colony paid its way with ebony, cattle and slaves, and its men joined local wars and lifted zebu until the Antanosy turned on them: in 1674 they killed most of the garrison and the survivors were evacuated. French ships kept coming back for cattle, and live zebu went to Réunion for nearly three hundred years, while slavers shipped Antanosy to the Mascarene Islands. Inland the Zafiraminia kept their capital at Fanjahira, and in 1821 the kingdoms of Anosy still lay outside the Merina kingdom of the highlands.
zh:
安塔诺西在马达加斯加湿润的东南端，包括陶拉纳鲁一带的海岸和埃法霍谷地，介于马西亚纳卡河与曼德拉雷河之间。居民在沿海潟湖捕鱼、在印度洋上航行，种植水稻和甘薯，牧养瘤牛；铁匠锻打本地的铁，工匠雕凿绿泥石，石件由独木舟北运，换回中国青瓷。安塔诺西在马尔加什语中意为「群岛」，得名于破碎海岸线上的河漫滩和潟湖。1444年，这里的村寨位于北方安泰莫罗诸商业政权之外，但本地雕石和牛群已经吸引穆斯林商船南下。

欧洲人正是在这处海岸第一次见到马达加斯加。1500年8月10日，迪奥戈·迪亚士的船在随第二次葡萄牙印度舰队航行时被风暴吹散，他在此望见岛屿，将其命名为圣劳伦斯。1504至1507年间至少五艘葡萄牙船在此失事，幸存者可能在陶拉纳鲁以西的小山上建起十米见方的石砌碉楼特拉诺瓦图，这大概是岛上第一座欧洲建筑。1613年，葡萄牙使团在马纳菲亚菲会见国王安德里安齐安巴尼，留下耶稣会士传教；后来葡萄牙人强携王世子赴果阿读书，贸易随即断绝，传教士也在1617年撤走，几年只施洗了一人。1643年，雅克·德·普罗尼斯在陶兰卡拉纳村建立多凡堡，以当时的法国王太子、后来的路易十四命名，并娶当地贵族女子为妻。1648年起出任总督的艾蒂安·德·弗拉古把见闻写成《大马达加斯加岛史》，此后两百年间这是欧洲人了解该岛的主要著作。

殖民地靠乌木、牛和奴隶牟利，法国人又介入本地战争、抢走瘤牛，终于激起安塔诺西人反抗：1674年他们袭杀大部分驻军，幸存者乘船撤离。后来法国船只仍不断回来买牛，向留尼汪输出活牛的贸易持续了近三百年，奴隶贩子则把安塔诺西人运往马斯克林群岛。在内地，扎菲拉米尼亚人以凡贾希拉为都；1821年，安塔诺西诸王国仍在高地伊麦里纳王国的版图之外。

en:
Ibara, the Bara country, is the grassland of the southern central plateau around Ihosy, between the Zomandao River, the Tanala forest and the Onilahy. The Bara are the island's great zebu people, semi-nomadic herders for whom cattle were wealth, the marriage price and a man's standing before the law; a young man had to carry off cattle in a sanctioned raid before he could take a wife. Grain and cassava filled the gaps, but the kraals set the rhythm of life. In 1444 no king ruled Ibara. Lineage groups and weak chiefly families moved across the plains with their herds, and the highland kingdom of Imerina lay far to the north.

A dynasty arrived from outside. Around 1640 a Mahafaly noble invaded Ibara and installed his family as the Zafimanely line; when he died in 1653 his kin fought over the country for a generation, keeping themselves by cattle raids and fines rather than tribute. Ibara knew one short spell of unity, when King Raikitroka issued rules around 1800 that settled the clan feuds, and after his death it split again into competing kingdoms. Cattle raids and the trade in cattle and slaves made the Bara richer through those years. In 1821 they were still fragmented, and still beyond Merina rule.
zh:
伊巴拉即巴拉人的土地，是中部高原南部伊胡西一带的草原，处在佐曼道河、塔纳拉森林和奥尼拉希河之间。巴拉人是马达加斯加首屈一指的牧牛民族，过着半游牧生活；牛是财富、聘礼，也是一个人在族法面前的身份，年轻人要先在被认可的盗牛行动中赶回过牛群，才能娶妻。谷物和木薯只是牧业之外的补充，日子围着牛栏转。1444年的伊巴拉没有王，各血缘群体和势力有限的酋长家族带着牛群在草原上游徙，北方高地的伊麦里纳王国还离得很远。

统治王朝来自外部。约1640年，一名马哈法利贵族入侵伊巴拉，把自家立为扎菲马内利世系；他1653年死后，族人争夺这片土地达一代人之久，不征贡赋，靠盗牛和罚金维持。伊巴拉只有过一次短暂统一：约1800年，国王赖基特罗卡立下规矩，平息了氏族仇杀；他死后，国土又分裂成几个相争的王国。那些年里，盗掠加上牛和奴隶贸易让巴拉人越来越富足。1821年，他们依旧四分五裂，也依旧不受伊麦里纳统治。

en:
Between the Manambolo and the Tsiribihina the dry western plain climbs eastward into the grey karst pinnacles, the tsingy, and the dry forest of the Bemaraha. Sakalava tradition places the earliest home of their ancestors at Sadia, by the Manambolo's mouth. In 1444 fishing villages stood behind the shore; clans herded zebu, farmed rice in the river valleys and sold tortoiseshell and cattle to dhows making for the Muslim marts of the north. No king yet ruled the coast, and the Menabe kingdom was only taking shape far to the south, around Morondava.

Tradition names Andriamandazoala, who reigned in the mid-sixteenth century, the founder of Menabe, and in that century the kingdom grew rich selling cattle and captives to European ships calling on the coast. Its great king was Andriandahifotsy, 'the White Prince', of the Maroserana dynasty: armed with muskets bought with slaves, he carried his power up the west coast as far as the Manambolo, kept the coasting trade in his own hands, and tried without success to bring all Madagascar under one rule. At his death his sons quarrelled, and about 1685 Andriamanetriarivo kept Menabe while Andriamandisoarivo marched north to found Iboina; Menabe stayed the senior Sakalava power through the 1700s. In 1820 and 1821 the British-trained armies of Radama I of Imerina invaded, but the Bemaraha country did not submit, and in 1821 Sakalava lords still held Antsalova and the Manambolo valley.
zh:
在马南布卢河与齐里比希纳河之间，西部干旱平原向东抬升，化作贝马拉哈灰色的石灰岩尖峰与旱生林。萨卡拉瓦人的传说把先祖最早的家园放在马南布卢河口附近的萨迪亚。1444年时，渔村散布在海岸后方，诸氏族牧放瘤牛、在河谷种植稻米，把玳瑁和牛只卖给驶往北方穆斯林商埠的独桅帆船。海岸上还没有国王，梅纳贝王国尚在遥远南方的穆龙达瓦一带成形。

传说把16世纪中叶在位的安德里亚曼达祖阿拉称为梅纳贝的建立者；那个世纪，梅纳贝靠向靠岸的欧洲船只出售牛只和俘虏致富。王国最强大的国王是马罗塞拉纳家族的安德里安达希富齐，绰号「白王子」：他用奴隶换得火枪，把势力沿西海岸向北扩张到马南布卢河，沿海贸易尽操其手，还试图统一全岛，但没有成功。他死后诸子争立，约1685年，安德里亚马内特里阿里武保住梅纳贝，安德里亚曼迪苏阿里武则北上建立伊博伊纳；整个18世纪，梅纳贝始终是萨卡拉瓦诸邦中的长者。1820年和1821年，梅里纳国王拉达马一世两度派英军训练的军队来攻，但贝马拉哈山区并未屈服，1821年时，安察卢瓦和马南布卢河谷仍在萨卡拉瓦领主手中。

en:
The Fiherenana is a short river that cuts through the arid southwestern plain and meets a coast of reefs, sandbars and spiny bush. In 1444 Vezo fishermen beached their outrigger canoes along the shore; their name means both 'the people who fish' and 'to struggle with the sea', and they lived from the reef rather than the land. Inland, Masikoro clans grazed zebu and raised rice, bartering cattle and dried fish to dhows sailing between the Muslim ports of the northwest and the southern bays. No king ruled the valley then, and its villages answered to clan elders alone.

Early in the seventeenth century the Andrevola dynasty founded the kingdom of Fiherenana, also called the Masikoro kingdom, ruling the coastlands between the Mangoky and the Onilahy rivers and growing rich on cattle, rice, maize and captives sold to other Malagasy rulers and European ships. Sakalava tradition traces the Maroserana princes who built the Sakalava kingdoms back to this valley; their name means 'those who owned many ports', and after 1610 Andriandahifotsy extended his power north past the Mangoky with guns bought through the slave trade, the first Sakalava kingdoms taking shape around the 1650s. On the bay of Saint Augustine the port of Toliara grew up under Andrevola suzerainty, where French buccaneers and other European ships put in for water and trade, and Vezo seafarers carried the coastal traffic. The Merina conquests of Radama I after 1817 broke the Sakalava monarchies further north but never reached the Fiherenana, and in 1821 the Andrevola still ruled their dry river kingdom.
zh:
费希拉那河不长，切开西南部的干旱平原，注入一片遍布礁岩、沙洲和多刺灌丛的海岸。1444年时，维佐渔民把独木舟停在岸边；他们的族名兼有「打鱼之人」和「与大海搏斗」两重意思，靠礁湖而非土地为生。内陆的马西科罗诸氏族牧放瘤牛、种植稻米，用牛只和鱼干同独桅帆船交易，这些船往返于西北的穆斯林港埠与南方海湾之间。河谷里还没有国王，村落只听命于氏族长老。

17世纪初，安德雷武拉王朝建立费希拉那王国，又称马西科罗王国，统辖曼戈基河与乌尼拉希河之间的沿海地带，靠向马尔加什诸统治者和欧洲船只出售牛只、稻米、玉米和俘虏致富。萨卡拉瓦人的传说把建立萨卡拉瓦诸王国的马罗塞拉纳诸王的故土追溯到这座河谷，他们的名号意为「拥有众多港口之人」；1610年后，安德里安达希福齐用奴隶贸易换来的枪械把势力向北扩展到曼戈基河以北，第一批萨卡拉瓦王国约在1650年代成形。圣奥古斯丁湾畔的图利亚拉港在安德雷武拉王朝的宗主权下兴起，法国海盗和其他欧洲船只入湾补水、贸易，维佐水手承担了沿海航运。1817年后拉达马一世的梅里纳征服战争打垮了更北方的萨卡拉瓦王国，却始终没有波及费希拉那；1821年时，安德雷武拉王朝仍统治着这个干旱的河畔王国。

en:
The Qadarif country is the southern Butana, the rolling plain between the Blue Nile, the Atbara and the Ethiopian hills. It was once the eastern march of the Christian kingdom of Alodia, but by 1444 Nubian-speaking villagers planting sorghum along the rainy-season wadis lived alongside Beja herders and Arab camel nomads, all slipping loose from the weak successors of Soba. Ivory from the Ethiopian foothills passed through the local markets on its way to the Nile.

After the Funj conquest of 1504 the southern Butana became a grazing and grain country of the Sultanate of Sennar, its markets drawing camels, cattle and slaves. The camel-owning Shukriya were its leading tribe, and their tribal market of Suq Abu Sinn, Abu Sinn's Market, grew into the town of Qadarif; an Arabic folk etymology derives the name from the crier who called at sunset, telling everyone who had finished buying and selling to leave. Armies crossed these marches in the Funj wars with Ethiopia. Ethiopian chronicles claim that in 1618-1619 the Bahr Negash Gebre Mariam, raiding for Emperor Susenyos, captured Fatima, queen of Mandara, whose town controlled the caravan road from Suakin. In 1744 Iyasu II's host marched through on its way to defeat on the Dinder. When James Bruce passed in 1772 he called the place Teawa and found its sheikh Fidele holding it as a vassal of Sennar. The Egyptian army of Muhammad Ali ended that allegiance in 1821 and put a garrison in the town.
zh:
加达里夫一带是布塔纳平原的南部，这片起伏的平原夹在青尼罗河、阿特巴拉河与埃塞俄比亚山地之间。这里曾是基督教阿勒底亚王国的东部边陲；到1444年，在季节性河谷边种植高粱的努比亚语村民，与贝扎牧人、阿拉伯骆驼游牧民杂处其间，索巴的衰弱继承者已无力约束他们。埃塞俄比亚山麓出产的象牙经当地市集运往尼罗河。

1504年丰吉人征服后，南布塔纳成为森纳尔苏丹国的畜牧和谷物之地，市集上汇聚着骆驼、牛只和奴隶。牧驼的舒克里亚人是当地最强大的部族，他们的部落市集「阿布·辛恩市场」后来发展为加达里夫城；按阿拉伯民间的说法，城名来自收市时差人的吆喝，叫买卖做完的人尽可离场。丰吉与埃塞俄比亚的战争中，军队多次穿过这片边地。据埃塞俄比亚方面的编年史记载，1618至1619年，巴赫勒·尼加什格布雷·马里亚姆为皇帝苏塞尼奥斯出征，俘获了曼达拉女王法蒂玛，她的城扼守着从萨瓦金延伸而来的商路。1744年，伊亚苏二世的大军经此开赴丁德尔河畔的败局。1772年詹姆斯·布鲁斯路过时把这里称作特阿瓦，见到城主谢赫菲德莱作为森纳尔的封臣据守此地。1821年，穆罕默德·阿里的埃及军队结束了这层臣属关系，并在城中屯驻军队。

en:
The Makua are the largest people of northern Mozambique, Bantu speakers who hold the broad country between the coast and Lake Malawi. Their oral tradition places their first home on Mount Namuli, where the first man and woman were born; other peoples, they say, came out of the neighbouring mountains. They lived in villages under local chiefs and councils of elders, tracing descent through the mother's line, farming and hunting and smelting iron in wood-burning hearths worked by the whole community, which turned out axes, hoes, knives and spearheads. Ivory, grain and ironwork went out along bush paths to the Swahili towns of Angoche and Mozambique, where Gujarati and Arab merchants paid in cloth and salt. In 1444 no outside king could call on the Makua.

Vasco da Gama's ships passed the coast in 1498, and for two and a half centuries the Portuguese dealt with the Makua mainly as traders, relations staying mostly peaceful into the mid-1700s. The eighteenth century brought an ivory boom that emptied the bush of elephants, and behind it came slave raiders. Yao caravans from the north carried Makua captives to Zanzibar for Arab buyers, and French planters on Reunion and the Isle de France added their own demand. From 1749 the Makua answered with a long war of raids and attrition against the coastal sultans, the Portuguese and the African chiefs allied with them, and the fighting ran on past the end of the century.
zh:
马库阿人是莫桑比克北部最大的族群，讲班图语，占据着海岸与马拉维湖之间的广阔土地。口传传统把最初的家园放在纳穆利山，说第一对男女便出生在那里，其余各族则出自邻近的群山。他们聚村而居，由本地首领和长老议事会治理，按母系计算世系；村民农耕、狩猎，全村合力在柴火炉中冶铁，打制斧头、锄头、小刀和矛头。象牙、谷物和铁器沿林间小路运往安戈谢、莫桑比克等斯瓦希里城镇，与古吉拉特和阿拉伯商人换取布匹和食盐。1444年时，没有任何外来的国王能向马库阿人发号施令。

1498年，达·伽马的船队驶过这片海岸；此后两个半世纪里，葡萄牙人主要以商人身份与马库阿人往来，到18世纪中叶关系大体和平。18世纪的象牙热潮把丛林里的大象捕杀殆尽，随之而来的是奴隶劫掠：北方尧族的商队把马库阿俘虏运往桑给巴尔卖与阿拉伯买家，留尼汪和法兰西岛的法国种植园也加入收购。1749年起，马库阿人以长期的袭扰消耗战回应沿海苏丹、葡萄牙人以及与他们结盟的非洲酋长，战火一直烧过世纪末。

en: Ngindo is the inland country of the Ngindo, a Bantu-speaking people who farm and hunt in small, scattered villages through the dry woods and plateaus around Liwale, between the caravan roads to Kilwa and Lindi and the lands of the Makua and Yao. They have no kings or paramount chiefs, and every village settles its own affairs. The woods held elephant herds, and Ngindo hunters carried ivory and other forest goods east to the Swahili coast, where in 1444 Kilwa was still the great market of the interior, its dhows sailing on to Arabia and India. Portuguese troops sacked Kilwa in July 1505 and the interior trade fell quiet, reviving only in the eighteenth century as Kilwa came under Omani rule. Through both changes the Ngindo kept their villages and their stateless ways.
zh: 恩金多是恩金多人的内陆家园。这个操班图语的族群在利瓦莱周围干燥林地和高原上耕种、狩猎，村落小而分散，地处通往基尔瓦、林迪的商路与马库阿人、尧人土地之间。他们没有君王或大酋长，每个村落自行处理事务。林中仍有象群，恩金多猎人把象牙和其他林产品东运斯瓦希里海岸；1444年的基尔瓦仍是内陆货物的大市场，当地独桅帆船再把货物运往阿拉伯和印度。1505年7月葡萄牙军队洗劫基尔瓦，内陆商路随之萧条，到18世纪基尔瓦受阿曼统治后才再度兴盛。两度变迁之间，恩金多的散村和无君长的旧制始终未改。

en:
The wooded Ruvuma country lies between the southern Tanganyikan coast and the Niassa interior, on the caravan routes that join Lake Nyasa with the ports of Lindi and Kilwa. In 1444 its villages belonged to the wider Makua world: Bantu farmers, hunters and ironworkers who smelted ore in wood-burning hearths and forged axes, knives, spears and rings, governed by local headmen and village councils. Makua caravans carried food, ivory and ironwork down to the coast for Swahili and Gujarati merchants and came back with cloth and salt. The Yao, or WaYao, for whom the province is named, then lived farther inland toward the Lugenda River and Lake Nyasa, still farming villagers rather than the Muslim caravan chiefs they later became.

Portuguese ships entered the Mozambique Channel before 1500, and coastal traders met Makua merchants soon after, but Portuguese power long stayed on the coast. Yao caravans grew on the ivory trade, exchanging tusks and grain with Arab and Swahili merchants for cloth and guns. Yao hunters called the greater honeyguide with a special note taught from father to son, followed the bird to bees' nests, and left it the wax. When Omani and French planters turned the traffic toward slaves in the eighteenth century, Yao raiders seized Makua and Lomwe villagers for the Zanzibar market. From 1749 the Makua fought a long war of attrition against the coastal sultans, the Portuguese and the traders allied with them. In 1821 most people around Wayao still followed ancestral rites and village headmen, and the mass turn to Islam had not begun, but guns and slave raiding had already reached the Ruvuma caravan country.
zh:
林木覆盖的鲁伍马地区位于坦噶尼喀南部沿海与尼亚萨内陆之间，地处连接尼亚萨湖与林迪、基尔瓦两港的商路上。1444年，这里的村落属于更广的马库阿世界：班图农民、猎人和铁匠以燃木炉冶炼矿石，打制斧头、刀、矛和指环，村社由地方头人和议事会管理。马库阿商队把粮食、象牙和铁器运到沿海，同斯瓦希里和古吉拉特商人交易，运回布匹和食盐。省名所指的瓦窑（WaYao，尧人）当时住得更靠内陆，在卢任达河和尼亚萨湖方向务农为生，还不是后来的穆斯林商队首领。

葡萄牙船只在1500年之前进入莫桑比克海峡，沿海商人很快接触到马库阿人，但葡萄牙势力长期停在沿海。瓦窑商队靠象牙贸易壮大，用象牙和粮食向阿拉伯和斯瓦希里商人换取布匹和枪支。瓦窑猎人还用父子相传的特殊叫声召唤导蜜鸟，跟着它找到蜂巢取蜜，把蜂蜡留给小鸟。18世纪，阿曼和法国种植园主把贸易转向奴隶，瓦窑劫掠者便掳走马库阿和隆韦村民，卖到桑给巴尔市场。1749年起，马库阿人对沿海苏丹、葡萄牙人及与其结盟的商人展开长期消耗战。1821年的瓦窑一带，多数人仍奉行祖灵仪礼、听命村社头人，大规模改宗伊斯兰教尚未开始，但枪支和奴隶劫掠已经进入鲁伍马商路地区。

en:
Katsekera covers the lowlands at the south-eastern end of Lake Malawi, where the lake narrows towards the sandbars of the Shire outlet and Nyanja fishermen beach their canoes. Its people are Chewa of the Maravi cluster, villagers who farmed and fished and paid their overlord tribute in ivory, carried south to be worked at the Kalonga's capital of Mankhamba. The Kalonga ruled from the country south of the lake and set his kinsmen over the outlying lands as his deputies; caravans carried Maravi cloth and iron hoes east to the coast and brought back glass beads and copper. Beyond the hills to the east lived the Yao, farming their own villages and driving ivory and grain down to the Muslim merchants of Kilwa. In 1444 this lake shore answered to the Kalonga through one of his kinsmen.

The Maravi order was at its strongest under Kalonga Muzura, a famous hunter who Portuguese reports say once led labourers on a settler's plantation. In 1608 he sent men to help the Portuguese against the rivals of the Mwenemutapa, Gatsi Rusere, and in 1616 he entertained Gaspar Bocarro, a Portuguese trader travelling overland from Tete to Kilwa, whose account left the first written description of the lake country. Muzura conquered the breakaway kingdom of the Lundu but could not dislodge the Portuguese from the Zambezi, and after his death in the 1640s the confederacy slowly came apart. In the 1700s succession to the Kalonga turned into armed quarrels, Mankhamba was abandoned, and territorial chiefs sold ivory straight to coastal caravans. Yao traders from the Chiconono hills in Niassa opened the roads west to the lake, bartering cloth, beads and muskets for ivory and, by the early 1800s, raiding for captives as well. By 1821 the Kalonga's old tribute network had given way to their caravan roads.
zh:
卡泽克拉位于马拉维湖东南端的湖岸低地，湖面在此收窄，通向希雷河出口处的沙洲，尼亚萨渔民把独木舟拖上滩头。这里的居民是马拉维族群中的切瓦人：村民耕种渔猎，以象牙向共主纳贡，象牙再南运，在卡隆加的都城曼坎巴加工。卡隆加居于湖南岸的国土，派亲族分镇边地；商队把马拉维布匹和铁锄东运海岸，带回玻璃珠与铜料。东面山地之外住着尧人，他们耕作自己的村寨，把象牙和粮食贩运给基尔瓦的穆斯林商人。1444年，这片湖岸由卡隆加的一位亲族代为管辖。

马拉维秩序在卡隆加·穆祖拉在位时最为强固：据葡萄牙人记载，他本是有名的猎人，曾在殖民者的种植园里领工。1608年，他派兵协助葡萄牙人攻打莫诺莫塔帕统治者的敌手；1616年，他款待了从太特走陆路前往基尔瓦的葡萄牙商人加斯帕尔·博卡罗，后者的记述留下了关于湖区最早的文字。穆祖拉征服了分裂自立的隆杜之国，却始终未能把葡萄牙人赶出赞比西；他在1640年代去世后，联盟渐渐瓦解。18世纪，卡隆加的继承陷入武力纷争，曼坎巴被废弃，各地酋长直接向沿海商队出售象牙。来自尼亚萨希科诺诺山地的尧人开辟了西通湖区的商路，以布匹、珠子和火枪换取象牙，到19世纪初又兼营掳掠人口的买卖。到1821年，卡隆加旧日的贡赋网络已让位于尧人的商队大道。

en:
Lolo is the inland plateau between the Shire valley and the harbour town of Quelimane, rolling miombo woodland watered by the Licungo and its sister rivers. The Lolo are the southern branch of the Makua, whom the Portuguese called the lower Makua; their own oral tradition makes them descendants of the first man and woman, born of Namuli, the mountain they call their first home. They were hoe farmers and iron smelters, working the ore in wood-burning hearths as a village and forging axes, knives and spear-blades. In 1444 their headmen ruled scattered villages, trading ivory, grain and ironware for cloth and salt with Muslim merchants on the Nampula coast.

The first Portuguese account, from the Zambezi expedition of 1569, finds the Lolo around Tete; by 1590 they had been driven east into the plateau they have occupied since, probably by Maravi war bands from the north. On the Shire the Maravi chief Lundu hired the Zimba mercenaries who destroyed two Portuguese armies in 1592 and 1593, before Lundu made peace in 1599. Through most of the 1600s and the mid-1700s the Lolo lived at peace with Quelimane, and the eighteenth-century ivory boom sent tusks out through its harbour. From 1749 a long Makua war of attrition against the coastal Muslim sultanates and the Portuguese cut the trade roads, while Yao raiders began pressing south for captives; in 1821 the Lolo villages lay in the path of a slave trade that fed Zanzibar and the French island colonies.
zh:
洛洛是希雷河谷与港镇克利马内之间的内陆高原，利昆戈河及其支流流过一片连绵的林地草原。洛洛人是马库阿人的南支，葡萄牙人称他们为「下马库阿人」；按他们自己的口传，人类第一对男女诞生在他们的原乡纳穆利山，洛洛人便是其后人。他们锄耕为业，也由全村人在燃木炉中冶铁，打制斧头、小刀和矛头。1444年，各地头人管辖着星散的村落，把象牙、粮食和铁器卖给楠普拉海岸的穆斯林商人，换取布匹和食盐。

1569年远征赞比西河的葡萄牙人留下第一份记载，当时洛洛人还住在河畔的太特一带；到1590年，他们已被来自北方的马拉维武装东逐到这片高原，此后一直居住于此。希雷河畔的马拉维酋长隆杜雇用津巴雇佣兵，后者于1592年和1593年连歼两支葡萄牙军队，隆杜则在1599年议和。17世纪大部分时间到18世纪中叶，洛洛人与克利马内相安无事，18世纪的象牙热潮使大批象牙经该港运出。1749年起，马库阿人对沿海穆斯林苏丹国和葡萄牙人展开长期消耗战，商路被切断，尧人又开始自北向南掳掠人口；1821年，洛洛诸村正处在奴隶贸易的路线上，俘虏被运往桑给巴尔以及法国人控制的科摩罗、留尼汪等印度洋岛屿。

en:
Lundu rules the Lower Shire valley, a hot and fertile floodplain where the Shire winds south through Nsanje to the Zambezi. Its people are the Mang'anja of the Maravi cluster, hoe farmers who grew cotton and wove it into cloth, dried fish on the riverbanks, and sent ivory down to the coast. Their chiefs held two sources of power: the tusks sold through the Muslim ports, and the Mbona rain shrine at Khulubvi, where a priestess served as the medium of a rain spirit said to have been killed by his own people and whose goodwill was held to bring the rains. The first Lundu, a kinsman of the Kalonga who broke away in a succession quarrel, set his seat at Mbewe near Chiromo; in 1444 his successor ruled the valley as a Maravi paramount, and village headmen sent him ivory.

In the later 1500s Lundu built a warrior power on the Zimba, a host of mercenaries, probably Shona-speakers from the south bank of the Zambezi, led by a chief called Tondo. They overran the Lolo and Makua country to the east, then in 1592 threw up a fort of two concentric palisades and a trench opposite Sena and destroyed the Portuguese army sent against it, ambushing its firearms relief on the road. A second Portuguese army with artillery came in 1593 and failed against new earthen walls; after two months it withdrew, and the Zimba captured its guns and raided Sena and Tete. Their bands reached the coast in 1595, but in 1599 Lundu offered peace and the Portuguese accepted. The title Lundu first appears in writing in Gaspar Bocarro's account of 1616. In 1622 Muzura, who had once worked for the Portuguese and ruled the Maravi chiefships with their support, crushed Lundu's revolt and made the valley part of his domains. The Maravi paramountcy withered through the 1700s, and by 1800 the old Lundu kingdom lay exposed to Portuguese slavers working up the Zambezi.
zh:
隆杜统治着希雷河下游谷地，这片炎热肥沃的冲积平原上，希雷河经恩桑杰南流汇入赞比西河。居民是马拉维集群南支的曼甘贾人，种棉织布，在河岸晒鱼干，把象牙运往海岸。酋长的权势有两个来源：经穆斯林港埠出售的象牙，以及库卢布维的姆博纳祈雨圣所，那里由一名女祭司充当雨神的灵媒；相传这位雨神被自己的族人所杀，安抚他的灵魂便能换来雨水。第一代隆杜本是卡隆加的亲族，在继承之争中率部出走，定都奇罗莫附近的姆贝韦；1444年，其继承者作为马拉维人的大君统治谷地，各村头人向他进献象牙。

16世纪后期，隆杜靠津巴人建立军事强权，这支雇佣兵多半是来自赞比西河南岸的绍纳语者，首领名叫通多。他们向东攻占洛洛和马库阿之地，1592年又在塞纳对岸筑起双重木栅、外挖壕沟的寨堡，歼灭来攻的葡萄牙军队，携火器驰援的队伍也在半路中伏。1593年，第二支葡萄牙军队携火炮再来，却拿新建的土墙无可奈何，围攻两个月后撤走，津巴人缴获其火炮，并袭掠塞纳和太特。1595年，这支武装已打到东海岸；1599年隆杜主动议和，为葡萄牙人接受。「隆杜」这个称号最早见于1616年加斯帕尔·博卡罗的记载。1622年，曾为葡萄牙人效力、在其支持下统领马拉维诸部的穆祖拉镇压了隆杜的反叛，把谷地并入自己的领地。18世纪间，马拉维人的宗主权日趋瓦解，到1800年前后，古老的隆杜王国已直接暴露在溯赞比西河而上的葡萄牙奴隶贩子面前。

en:
The Kalonga's country covers the rolling hills between Lake Malawi and the Shire valley, the land of the Chewa. Chewa farmers drifting south from Katanga began settling it in the 12th century, and the later Phiri clan brought kingship: its ruler took the title Kalonga and kept his court at Manthimba, the site archaeologists know as Mankhamba, near Kaphirintiwa Hill. The Kalonga held secular power, but the Makewana, a priestess of the older Banda clan, held the rain. Kaphirintiwa, whose rocks bear marks like human and animal footprints and which Chewa tradition calls the place of creation, was the 'mother' of the rain shrines, and the Makewana posted spirit wives to the lesser shrines on the hilltops. Subject chiefs sent ivory to the court, while smiths traded iron tools and cloth down the routes to the coast for glass beads and copper. In 1444, with the rain cult balancing the throne, the Kalonga already headed one of the great inland powers east of the Zambezi.

Kinsmen sent out to rule border lands grew into rivals. In the 16th century Lundu broke away to the lower Shire, grew rich on the Zambezi trade, patronised the Mbona rain shrine at Nsanje and allied with the warrior Zimba, who defeated Portuguese forces in 1592 and 1593. The Kalonga who overcame him, Muzura, comes straight from Portuguese reports: a noted hunter who had once led labourers on a Portuguese planter's estate. He had earlier fought beside the Portuguese against the enemies of the Mwenemutapa, and in 1616 he hosted Gaspar Bocarro, the first European to leave an account of the Maravi, at his southern court; with Portuguese backing he overthrew Lundu in 1622. In 1629 he marched against his former allies alongside Mwenemutapa Kapararidze, but his assault on Quelimane failed. In the 18th century succession disputes split the court, chiefs sold ivory to coastal merchants on their own account, and gun-carrying Yao traders opened new routes and raided Chewa villages for slaves. Manthimba was abandoned around the turn of the 19th century, and in 1821 the Kalonga's authority scarcely reached beyond his own settlement.
zh:
卡隆加之地是马拉维湖与希雷河谷之间的起伏丘陵，切瓦人的家园。12世纪起，自加丹加南迁的切瓦农民在此落户，较晚到来的菲里氏族带来了王权：首领号称卡隆加，王廷设在曼廷巴，即考古学家所称的曼坎巴遗址，邻近卡菲林蒂瓦山。卡隆加执掌世俗之权，祈雨之事却出自更古老的班达氏族的马克瓦纳女祭司。卡菲林蒂瓦山的岩石上有形似人畜脚印的痕迹，切瓦传说也把这里称作创世之地；此山是切瓦各祈雨圣所的「母所」，马克瓦纳再派「灵妻」分驻各处山丘上的小圣所。附庸酋长把象牙送往王廷，铁匠则把铁器和布匹沿商道运往海岸，换回玻璃珠和铜。1444年，王权与祈雨崇拜彼此制衡，卡隆加已是赞比西河以东的内陆强权之一。

派去镇守边地的亲族往往反成对手。16世纪，隆杜在下希雷河自立，靠赞比西河贸易致富，扶持恩桑杰的姆博纳祈雨圣所，并与尚武的津巴人结盟；津巴人在1592和1593年连破葡萄牙军队。最终压倒隆杜的卡隆加名叫穆祖拉，葡萄牙人的记载里留着他的来历：他本是有名的猎人，还曾替葡萄牙种植园主带领劳工。他早先曾协助葡萄牙人攻打穆韦内穆塔帕的敌人，1616年在南方的宫廷接待了最早留下马拉维记载的欧洲人加斯帕尔·博卡罗，1622年又借葡萄牙之力推翻隆杜。1629年，他与穆韦内穆塔帕·卡帕拉里泽联手，向旧日盟友开战，但攻打克利马内失败。18世纪，继承之争撕裂王廷，酋长们绕开卡隆加直接向海岸商人出售象牙，持枪的尧人商人另辟商路，掳掠切瓦村庄为奴。曼廷巴约在19世纪初被废弃；1821年时，卡隆加的号令已几乎不出自己的村寨。

en:
The Kinga, or Wakinga, farm the high country of the Kipengere Range, called the Livingstone Mountains where it rises above the northeastern shore of Lake Nyasa. Montane grasslands, forested stream valleys and steep escarpment paths divide the clan lands, and the Sanga clan is the largest of them and long held the leading place. Beside the clan heads stand the priests of Lwembe, the ancestor venerated as a divine king, whose shrine rites were older than any chiefly authority. In 1444 no king ruled these mountains: the Kinga lived in autonomous farming villages, and their smelters forged hoes and spear points for the Nyakyusa and Ngonde down by the lake, taking food, cattle and salt in return.

During the following centuries the lake-region trade kept moving Kinga iron, cloth, pottery and salt between the escarpment and the shore, and Ngonde ivory travelled the same routes on its way toward Kilwa and the coast. The steep paths kept the high villages out of the plains wars, and Swahili traders and coastal sultans never gained a footing above the escarpment. In 1821 the Kinga still lived by clans and Lwembe shrine rites, a mountain people of the lake country belonging to no coastal state.
zh:
金加人（Wakinga）在基彭盖雷岭的高地务农；山岭耸峙于尼亚萨湖东北岸，这一段又称利文斯通山。山地草场、溪谷森林和陡峭崖路把各氏族的土地分隔开来，桑加氏族最大，长期居于首位。与氏族首领并列的是卢恩贝的祭司：卢恩贝是被尊为神王的先祖，对他的神祠祭祀比任何首领权威都更古老。1444年，没有国王统治这片山地，金加人住在自治的农耕村落，铁匠为山下湖滨的尼亚库萨人和恩贡德人打制锄头和矛镞，换回粮食、牲畜和盐。

此后几个世纪，湖区贸易把金加铁器、布匹、陶器和盐不断运下崖地、送上湖滨，恩贡德象牙也沿同一条路转往基尔瓦和沿海方向。陡峭山路使高地村落置身平原战事之外，斯瓦希里商人和沿海苏丹始终未能在崖地以上立足。1821年，金加人仍按氏族和卢恩贝神祠祭仪生活，是湖区不属于任何海岸政权的山地居民。

en:
Makonde is the thicket-covered plateau west of Lindi, bounded by the Lukuledi River to the north and the steep Ruvuma escarpment to the south. In 1444 its scattered Bantu hamlets straddled the borderland of Makua and Yao speakers. The clans later called Makonde kept no king or chief: kin groups farmed the Newala and Mueda heights, descent ran through the mother's line, and a husband moved into his wife's village. Their men were already carvers, working the dense blackwood called mpingo and shaping masks from the soft njala wood for the mapiko dances of initiation and ancestor rites.

The eighteenth-century revival of Kilwa's ivory and slave trade pushed caravans and raiders toward the plateau. Makonde clans withdrew upward from the Ndonde lowlands of northern Mozambique into the Mueda and Newala heights, seeking healthier ground and shelter from slavers; dense bush and steep paths protected the scattered villages, which litawa kin groups and mwenyekaya elders ran without chiefs. African, Arab and European slavers all met resistance here, and by 1821 no power from the coast had crossed the escarpment to subdue the highland villages.
zh:
马孔德是林迪以西、灌木覆盖的高原，北以卢库莱迪河为界，南缘是鲁伍马河陡崖。1444年，散布其间的班图村落处在马库阿语和尧语族群的交界地带。后来被称作马孔德的诸氏族没有国王或酋长：血族在新瓦拉和穆埃达高地耕作，世系按母系计算，丈夫搬进妻子的村落。男子已是熟练的雕刻匠，用名为姆平戈的致密黑木雕刻，也用松软的恩贾拉木刻成面具，用于成年礼和祭祖仪式上的「马皮科」舞。

18世纪，基尔瓦的象牙和奴隶贸易再度兴盛，商队和劫掠者向高原逼近。马孔德诸氏族从莫桑比克北部的恩东代低地退上穆埃达、新瓦拉高地，既为寻找更宜居的地方，也为躲避奴隶贩子；密林和陡路护住了分散村落，「利塔瓦」血族和「姆文耶卡亚」长老在没有酋长的情况下协调村务。非洲人、阿拉伯人和欧洲奴隶贩子都在这里遇到抵抗，到1821年，仍没有哪股沿海势力越过陡崖征服这些高地村落。

en: The Phangwa, or Wapangwa, farm the eastern face of the Livingstone escarpment above Lake Nyasa, their villages clustered around Ludewa, Mlangali and Mawengi. In 1444 these steep ridges were clan country without a king: Pangwa households tilled the high valleys, Kinga neighbours held the heights to the north, Kisi and Manda fishermen kept the lakeshore, and Yao and Makonde country opened to the east. Local accounts say clans gathered in Ludewa after wars drove them from the Malawi and Mozambique direction. Through the following centuries the high valleys remained a stateless country of mountain kin groups, set between lakeshore fishing villages and the Ruvuma caravan routes.
zh: 庞瓦人（Wapangwa）在尼亚萨湖上方利文斯通崖地的东坡耕作，村落集中在卢代瓦、姆兰加利和马文吉一带。1444年，这些陡峭山脊是没有国王的氏族之地：庞瓦农户耕种高谷，金加人据有北面的高地，基西和曼达渔民守着湖滨，东面通向瓦窑和马孔德人的地方。地方记载称，来自马拉维、莫桑比克方向的战乱把一些氏族赶到卢代瓦，在此汇聚。此后几个世纪，高谷始终是山地血族组成的无国家之地，夹在湖滨渔村与鲁伍马商路之间。

en:
Ngonde lies along the north-western shore of Lake Malawi, a hot plain between the Songwe River in the north and the North Rukuru, cut by rivers, marshes and lakeside grassland. In the fifteenth century scattered Bantu farming villages held the plain, and digs at Mbande Hill, a rise above the lake, show a settled community there between 1410 and 1480. The villagers grew millet and bananas, kept a few cattle, netted fish and hunted elephant, each homestead answering to its own headman with no chief above him. In 1444 the ivory caravans that ran between the great lakes and the Indian Ocean had not yet reached this plain.

Around 1600 the Ngonde, a branch of the Nyakyusa who lived north of the Songwe, crossed the river and settled the Karonga plain in numbers, mingling with and absorbing the older villagers. Their banana groves and millet fields spread along the lakeshore, and over their chiefs they set a sacred king, the Kyungu, chosen from one of two royal lines and enthroned at Mbande Hill; his authority ran to ritual and religion rather than direct command. Behind its swamps and rivers Ngonde grew populous for two centuries, untroubled from outside, and elephant ivory left the plain only in the nineteenth century, when coastal traders arrived at last.
zh:
恩贡德地处马拉维湖西北岸，北起松圭河、南至北鲁库鲁河，是一片湿热的湖岸平原，河汊、沼泽与湖滨草地交错。15世纪时，这里散布着班图语农耕村落；湖边高地姆班德山上的发掘显示，1410至1480年间已有定居聚落。村民种粟和香蕉，养少量牛，下湖捕鱼，入林猎象，各田庄只听命于本族头人，上面没有更高的首领。1444年，往返于大湖与印度洋之间的象牙商队还没有踏上这片平原。

约1600年，原住松圭河以北的尼亚库萨人的一支恩贡德人渡河南下，在卡龙加平原密集定居，与早先的村民杂处融合。他们的香蕉园和粟田沿湖岸铺开，并在众酋长之上立了一位神圣君主「昆古」：昆古从两支王族世系中选出，在姆班德山登基，其权威在祭祀与宗教，不在直接的号令。凭着沼泽和河流为屏障，恩贡德人安稳生息了两个世纪，境外无人来犯；直到19世纪海岸商人才终于到来，平原上的象牙开始外运。

en:
