The Tumbuka plateau rolls between the Luangwa valley and the western shore of Lake Malawi, grassland broken by the Henga valley and the Nkhamanga plains. Tumbuka clans entered it from the Luba country in the early fifteenth century, drifting east with their goats and sheep, and by 1444 they were the people of the land: Henga in the northern valleys, Kamanga around Nkhamanga, Phoka below the Nyika plateau, Tonga by the lake. They farmed millet in scattered homesteads, each clan under its own head, with no king above them and no dues beyond the occasional gift of a leopard or lion skin. Elephant herds roamed across the plateau, but the Tumbuka set small value on ivory.

For three centuries the clans multiplied and spread, south to the Bua and west across the Luangwa, still without a single ruler. From the mid-eighteenth century long-distance traders from Unyamwezi appeared, dressed in Arab fashion and called Balowoka, 'the people who crossed over', buying ivory as far inland as the Luangwa and paying with cloth, beads, cowries and iron hoes. Around 1780 their leader Mulowoka crossed Lake Malawi, landed at Chilumba and made his way to Nkhamanga, giving away hoes and cloth and marrying into the leading Luhanga and Kumwenda clans; the clans made him their chief. His son, remembered as Gonapamuhanya for dozing in the sun after his midday meal, was the first holder of the kingship title Chikulamayembe, from the Swahili for 'pick up the hoes', the call Mulowoka gave as the tools were handed out. A loose federation under the dynasty reached from the Songwe to the Dwangwa, and by 1821 the trade-built kingship of Nkhamanga was at the height of its power.
zh:
通布卡高原横在卢安瓜河谷与马拉维湖西岸之间，草原上嵌着亨加河谷与恩卡马加平原。15世纪初，通布卡诸氏族从卢巴故地东迁，赶着山羊和绵羊一路东来，到1444年已成了这片土地的主人：亨加人居于北部河谷，卡曼加人在恩卡马加一带，福卡人住在尼伊卡高原南麓，通加人在湖岸。他们在分散的田庄种粟，各氏族由自己的头人管治，上面没有国王，也没有常赋，至多偶尔献上一张豹皮或狮皮。象群走遍高原，通布卡人却不把象牙当回事。

此后三百年，诸氏族生齿日繁、四处扩散，南抵布阿河，西越卢安瓜河，始终没有共主。18世纪中叶起，来自乌尼亚姆韦齐的长途商人出现了：他们一身阿拉伯装束，被称作巴洛沃卡，意为「渡水而来的人」，一路深入卢安瓜河谷收购象牙，以布匹、串珠、海贝和铁锄作价。约1780年，其首领穆洛沃卡渡过马拉维湖，在奇伦巴上岸，转入恩卡马加；他沿途散送锄头布匹，又与最有权势的卢汉加、库姆温达两氏族联姻，众氏族便拥戴他做了酋长。他的儿子戈纳帕穆哈尼亚（因午饭后爱晒太阳打盹而得名）是王号「奇库拉马延贝」的第一任持有者；王号来自斯瓦希里语，意为「拿起锄头」，是穆洛沃卡分发锄头时吩咐随从的话。该王朝下的松散联盟疆域北起松圭河、南至德万瓜河；到1821年，这个靠贸易建起来的恩卡马加王权正处于最强之时。

en:
Lala is the well-watered plateau around Serenje, where woodland streams cross fertile country and the Kaombe River goes over the lip of the Muchinga escarpment at Kundalila, a fall of about eighty metres whose name means 'crying dove' in Bemba. Its people speak Ilala, a Bantu language close to Bisa and Bemba, and their oral history traces the clans to the Luba-Lunda country farther north. In 1444 there was no royal capital here, only dispersed farming, hunting and fishing villages. Chiefs, district headmen called chilolos and village sulutani kept the chiefdoms' bounds; the senior chief bore the title Kankomba-we-Lala, the royal house was Bena Nyendwa, and the Insaka ye Lala council advised the chiefs and judged disputes between them.

Families burned woodland in chitemene gardens for finger millet and sorghum. Through the following centuries the harvests, traps, spears, fish weirs and hunting grounds supported these small highland chiefdoms, while the caravan routes from the Luangwa and the Zambezi passed well to the east. In 1821 the Lala still lived under their own chiefs and headmen, keeping to the plateau of millet gardens above the falls.
zh:
拉拉是塞伦杰周围水草丰沛的高原，林溪穿过肥沃乡野，卡翁贝河在昆达利拉越过穆钦加崖缘，形成约八十米高的瀑布，「昆达利拉」在本巴语中意为「哭泣的鸽子」。居民使用伊拉拉语，这是与比萨语、本巴语相近的班图语，口传历史把诸氏族的来历追溯到更北方的卢巴-隆达之地。1444年，这里没有王城，只有分散的农耕、狩猎和渔业村落。酋长、称「奇洛洛」的地区头人和称「苏卢塔尼」的村头维系各酋邦疆界；最高首领号「坎孔巴-韦-拉拉」，王室为「本纳·延杜瓦」，「因萨卡·耶·拉拉」议事会辅佐酋长并裁决酋邦争端。

各家在奇泰梅内烧出的林地里种植手指粟和高粱。此后几个世纪，收成、陷阱、长矛、鱼梁和猎场支撑着这些高原小酋邦，通往卢安瓜河与赞比西河的商路则远在东面。1821年，拉拉人仍生活在自己的酋长和头人治下，守着瀑布上方种满粟谷的高原。

en:
Nsenga is the Luangwa country, the broad valley where the river loops south between wooded escarpments to join the Zambezi, and the plateau above it. Cattle, goats and sheep graze the valley floors beside fields of millet, sorghum and groundnuts, and Nsenga villages are known for beadwork and basketry. Their name means 'the journey', after the long migration that brought their clans south out of the Luba country, probably in the fourteenth century; their traditions tell of running fights on the road with the Bemba of Chitimukulu. They had no kings, only clan heads called tumvi, and in 1444 self-ruling villages lay scattered along the river, far from the Maravi kingdoms of the Shire.

In the 1600s the Maravi chief Undi, ruling from Mano near Tete, carried his power west to the Luangwa, and the eastern Nsenga may have paid him tribute, though their own traditions remember no conquest. Early in the eighteenth century the Portuguese opened the feira of Zumbo where the Luangwa meets the Zambezi, and its traders paddled canoes up both rivers buying ivory as far inland as Lake Bangweulu; Nsenga ivory and provisions then flowed down to the coast. Around 1800 the Nsenga broke from Undi. In 1804 the chief Mburuma fell on Zumbo and drove the Portuguese out, and the fair stayed shut until 1820, when it reopened on the eve of the valley's nineteenth-century upheavals.
zh:
恩森加是卢安瓜河流域：大河在林木覆盖的崖壁间绕向南方，汇入赞比西河，河畔高原也在其地。河谷底部牧着牛、山羊和绵羊，田间种粟、高粱和花生，恩森加村寨以珠饰和编织出名。族名意为「旅途」，得名于诸氏族在14世纪前后从北方卢巴之地南迁的漫长路程；口述传统里，他们一路上还和奇蒂穆库卢率领的本巴人且战且行。恩森加人没有王，只有称「通比」的氏族长老。1444年，自治村寨沿河散布，希雷河流域的马拉维诸王国还远在南方。

17世纪，以太特附近马诺为都的马拉维酋长温迪把势力向西推到卢安瓜河，东部恩森加人可能曾向他纳贡，但他们自己的传统里没有被征服的记忆。18世纪初，葡萄牙人在卢安瓜河汇入赞比西河处开设宗博集市，商人划独木舟沿两条河上行，远至班韦乌卢湖收购象牙，恩森加的象牙和粮食随之顺流运往海岸。约1800年，恩森加人脱离温迪。1804年，酋长姆布鲁马攻破宗博、赶走葡萄牙人，集市一直关闭到1820年才重开，此时河谷19世纪的大变局已在眼前。

en:
The Lomwe speak eLomwe, a tongue close to Makua, and hold the well-watered highland belt that rises between the Shire valley and the coastal plains of northern Mozambique. They farmed the hillsides, smelted iron and gathered ivory, living in village clusters under their own headmen. In the fifteenth century the Maravi confederation grew up around Lake Malawi under its Kalonga kings, who sent kinsmen out to rule tributary chiefships and took their tribute in ivory. By 1444 the Lomwe lands lay on the eastern edge of this Maravi world, sending ivory toward the lake and taking beads and cloth in return.

The Portuguese who pushed up the Zambezi met the Maravi at their height under Kalonga Muzura. Portuguese records make him a man who had once led labourers on a settler's plantation and was famous as a hunter. In 1608 he helped the Portuguese defeat the rivals of the Mwenemutapa Gatsi Rusere, and in 1616 he received Gaspar Bocarro at another of his capitals near the Zambezi; Bocarro went on to write the first European account of Maravi. In 1622 Muzura overthrew his rival Lundu with Portuguese help, but in 1629 he allied with the new Mwenemutapa Kapararidze to drive the Portuguese out of Zambezia, and his attack on Quelimane failed. A Portuguese report of 1635 called him cunning and very powerful, and he died in the 1640s. From the mid-1700s the royal succession broke down, outlying chiefs made their own bargains with coastal merchants, and Yao caravans from the north turned the old ivory paths into slave routes. By 1800 the Lomwe headmen answered to no Kalonga and lived amid the raiding.
zh:
隆韦人讲与马库阿语相近的隆韦语，住在希雷河谷与莫桑比克北部沿海平原之间湿润的高地带上。他们在山坡耕种、冶铁、获取象牙，聚寨而居，各有首领。15世纪，奉卡龙加为共主的马拉维联盟在马拉维湖一带兴起；卡龙加派子弟四出统治纳贡的酋邦，贡物多为象牙，以此把各地维系在一起。1444年时，隆韦之地处在这个马拉维世界的东缘，象牙输往湖区，换回珠子和布匹。

沿赞比西河北上的葡萄牙人见到的，是卡龙加·穆祖拉治下最强盛时的马拉维。葡方记载说，他曾在殖民者的种植园里带领劳工，又是出名的猎手。1608年，他助葡萄牙人击败姆韦尼·马塔帕的对手；1616年，他在赞比西河附近的另一座都城接待加斯帕尔·博卡罗，博卡罗后来写下欧洲人对马拉维的第一份记述。1622年，穆祖拉靠葡萄牙相助推翻对手伦杜；1629年他又与新任姆韦尼·马塔帕结盟，要把葡萄牙人逐出赞比西亚，攻打克利马内却告失败。1635年的一份葡方报告称他狡诈而兵力强盛，穆祖拉于1640年代去世。18世纪中叶起，王位继承崩坏，边远酋长径自与沿海商人交易，北方尧族的商队把旧日的象牙之路变成贩奴路线。到1800年，隆韦首领已不再听命于任何卡龙加，在四境的劫掠中各自求存。

en:
The Quirimbas are a chain of some thirty coral islands running up the coast toward Cape Delgado. Makonde fishermen beached their canoes there first, and in the medieval centuries Swahili traders settled the better anchorages; the Portuguese later knew the group as the Islands of Saint Lazarus. Ibo lies a few miles off the mainland behind reefs and mangrove creeks and grew into one of the chief of these little stone towns. Its dhows carried ivory, tortoiseshell and ambergris south to Kilwa and brought back Indian cloth and beads, and in 1444 the sheikh of Ibo, like the sheikhs of the sister islands, looked to Kilwa.

Vasco da Gama is said to have put in at Ibo on his second voyage, in 1502. Within a generation Portuguese raiders were burning the Muslim towns: an expedition sacked Ibo, killed some sixty merchants and carried off its ivory, and in 1609 the Portuguese built a fort on the island. Many Swahili merchants simply withdrew to other islands of the archipelago and went on trading beyond Portuguese reach, while Ibo served the captains of Mozambique as a northern outpost, gathering ivory and, in time, captives for the island capital. Malagasy raiders harried the archipelago through much of the eighteenth century, and to hold Ibo the Portuguese raised the star-shaped Fort São João Baptista, completed in 1791. By 1821 Ibo was the second-busiest slave port in the colony after Mozambique Island, its dhows shipping captives to the Mascarene plantations.
zh:
基林巴是约三十座珊瑚岛连成的岛链，沿海岸向北铺向德尔加杜角。最早把独木舟划上这些岛的是马孔德渔民；中世纪的几个世纪里，斯瓦希里商人陆续在条件较好的锚地定居，葡萄牙人后来把这片群岛称作圣拉撒路群岛。伊博距大陆仅数公里，藏在礁群与红树林水道之后，渐渐长成这些小石城中最要紧的一个。岛上的独桅船把象牙、玳瑁和龙涎香南运基尔瓦，换回印度布匹和珠子；1444年时，伊博的谢赫和姊妹岛上的谢赫们一样，都听命于基尔瓦。

据说达·伽马1502年第二次远航时曾在伊博落脚。不出一代人，葡萄牙袭掠者便开始焚烧这些穆斯林城镇：一支远征队洗劫伊博，杀死约六十名商人，掠走岛上的象牙，又于1609年在岛上筑起要塞。许多斯瓦希里商人索性迁到群岛其他岛屿，在葡萄牙人管不到的地方继续贸易；伊博则成了莫桑比克岛驻防统领的北方前哨，为岛城收购象牙，后来又加上了人口。18世纪的大部分时间里，马达加斯加袭掠者不断骚扰群岛；为守住伊博，葡萄牙人建起星形的圣若昂·巴普蒂斯塔堡，1791年完工。到1821年，伊博已是殖民地仅次于莫桑比克岛的第二大奴隶港，独桅船把一船船俘虏运往马斯克林群岛的种植园。

en:
Luangwa is the lower Luangwa valley and the country around its meeting with the Zambezi. Seasonal floods open fishing channels and leave fields beside the water, while the steep Zambezi Escarpment cuts villages off from the plateaus but leaves them linked by canoes. Nsenga oral history traces a migration from the Luba world in about the fourteenth century. In 1444 Nsenga and related Bantu clans lived under clan heads, planting millet and sorghum, keeping cattle and hunting elephant; no European trader yet occupied the confluence.

The Portuguese reached it from the Mozambique coast in the early eighteenth century and built Zumbo on the Zambezi's north-east bank. By 1720 traders had crossed the Luangwa to Feira, opposite Zumbo. Zumbo became the most remote of the middle Zambezi's major fairs, buying ivory carried down the lower Luangwa and from lands as distant as Lake Bangweulu. Much of that traffic depended on African boatmen, hunters and Chikunda, the armed clients of Afro-Portuguese river estates. They lived in small fortified villages, served as soldiers and traders, and by the mid-eighteenth century some carried muskets. Canoes, tusks and these armed clients tied Mozambique to the lower Luangwa valley.
zh:
卢安瓜指卢安瓜河下游及其与赞比西河相汇的地带。季节性洪水带出捕鱼水道，也在河边留下可耕之地；陡峭的赞比西崖坡把村落与高原隔开，独木舟却把各河畔聚落连在一起。恩森加口传历史称，他们约在14世纪从卢巴世界迁来。1444年，恩森加及亲缘班图氏族在氏族首领管辖下种植粟和高粱、饲养牛只、猎捕大象；河口还没有欧洲商人占据。

18世纪初，葡萄牙人从莫桑比克海岸来到这里，在赞比西东北岸建立宗博。到1720年，商人已渡过卢安瓜河，在宗博对岸的费拉住下。宗博成为中赞比西最偏远的大集市，收购沿卢安瓜河下游运来、甚至远自班韦乌卢湖一带的象牙。这笔贸易大量依靠非洲船工、猎人和奇昆达人；奇昆达人是非裔葡萄牙人河畔领地的武装依附者，住在设防小村，充当士兵和商人，到18世纪中期已有一部分人使用火枪。独木舟、象牙和这些武装依附者把莫桑比克与卢安瓜河下游连在同一条贸易线上。

en: Ewaso Ngiro takes its name from the Ewaso Ng'iro, the river of 'brown or muddy water' in Maasai. It rises near Mount Kenya, crosses semi-arid plains and spreads into the Lorian Swamp, whose floodwaters occasionally run on down the intermittent Lagh Dera toward the Jubba. In such dry country wells and waterholes are the only fixed wealth. In 1444 these grazing lands lay under the Ajuran, a Somali Muslim sultanate that built great stone wells and river dykes, controlled the Jubba and Shabelle and taxed the herdsmen who watered their flocks here. Ajuran armies met expanding Oromo groups in the Gaal Madow Wars of the mid-seventeenth century; by the early eighteenth century Ajuran power had vanished from Banaadir, and the wells and pastures around the Lorian were held by clan right alone, disputed between Somali pastoral families and the Oromo newcomers.
zh: 埃瓦索恩吉罗得名于同名河流，河名在马赛语中意为「褐色或浑浊的水」。河源自肯尼亚山附近，穿过半干旱平原后漫入洛里安沼泽，沼泽涨水时，积水偶尔会顺着季节性的拉格代拉河道继续流向朱巴河。在这样干旱的地方，井泉和水坑是唯一靠得住的财富。1444年，这片牧场属于索马里人的穆斯林政权阿朱兰苏丹国；阿朱兰人开凿大石砌水井、修筑河堤，控制朱巴河与谢贝利河，向在此饮畜的牧民收税。17世纪中叶的加拉马多战争中，阿朱兰军队迎击不断扩张的奥罗莫人；到18世纪初，阿朱兰势力已退出贝纳迪尔，洛里安一带的井泉和牧场只按氏族权利占有，由索马里游牧家族和新来的奥罗莫人反复争夺。

en: Dawa is the dry grazing country along the lower Dawa, which runs southeast out of the Ethiopian highlands and joins the Ganale to form the Jubba. Wells and fords, rather than any title to land, decide who can stay here. In 1444 the camel-herding Somali Garre held the Dawa and Ganale basins ahead of the Borana and Warday Oromo groups pushing south, and their wells, pastures and fords were disputed between clans for generations. The Futuh al-Habasha, the Arabic chronicle of the Adal-Ethiopian war, names a Garre sultan, Imam Mataan, who led his tribesmen in the invasion of Ethiopia. By the eighteenth century Garre traders ran much of the caravan route from Luuq into Borana country and used Oromo as its language of trade, tying the Dawa crossings to the markets of the Jubba valley.
zh: 达瓦是达瓦河下游一带的干旱牧区。达瓦河从埃塞俄比亚高地向东南流来，与格纳莱河汇合成朱巴河；在这里，掌握井泉和渡口的人才能立足。1444年，放牧骆驼的索马里加雷人占据着达瓦河与格纳莱河流域，早于向南扩张的博尔纳、瓦尔代奥罗莫群体；他们的井泉、牧场和渡口多少代以来都是各氏族争夺的对象。记述阿达尔—埃塞俄比亚战争的阿拉伯文史书提到，一位名叫伊玛目·马坦的加雷苏丹曾率本族部众攻入埃塞俄比亚。到18世纪，加雷商人把持着从卢格通往博尔纳地区的大半商路，商路上通用奥罗莫语，达瓦河各渡口也因此与朱巴河谷的市集连在一起。

en:
Turkana is the sun-scorched basin beside the great jade-green lake its people call Anam Ka'alakol, 'the sea of many fish'. It is the largest permanent lake in any desert, an alkaline Rift Valley water with no outlet but the sun, fed by the Omo out of the Ethiopian highlands and by the Turkwel and Kerio from the south; sudden storms sweep its warm, brackish surface, crocodiles crowd the shore flats, and the crater of Central Island vents steam. In 1444 the fisheries and the dry plains around them belonged to older fishing and herding peoples, while a Nilotic section of the Ateker confederation was moving in from the north with its zebu herds. These newcomers, the Turkana, had broken away from their Ateker kin and were already at war with them.

The Turkana call themselves the people of the grey bull, after their zebu. They ran camels, wove baskets, carried spears and steel wrist knives, and every man kept a small wooden stool that did as his headrest at night. They took their guidance from the ngimurok, diviners who received dreams from the high god Akuj and named the sacrifice required for rain, sickness or a raid; tradition credits one of them, Lokerio, with parting the lake so that Turkana warriors could cross on foot and drive off the enemy's camels. Generations of fighting carried the Turkana and their allies across the whole basin by the 1600s: they defeated the peoples in their path with better tactics and weapons, folded the young of conquered groups into their own sections, and let elders rather than kings rule each territory. On the margins of their country they skirmished with Arab, Swahili and Abyssinian slavers and ivory traders. In 1821 no European had yet seen the lake, and the Turkana held it unchallenged.
zh:
图尔卡纳是骄阳炙烤的盆地，旁倚一汪碧绿色大湖，当地人称之为阿纳姆·卡阿拉科尔，意为「多鱼之海」。这是世界上最大的常年沙漠湖泊，东非大裂谷中一座没有出口的碱性内流湖，湖水靠北方奥莫河从埃塞俄比亚高地、南方特克韦尔河与凯里奥河补给，只能凭蒸发流去；微咸的暖湖面上风暴骤起，鳄鱼成群伏在岸边滩地，中央岛的火山口吐着蒸汽。1444年时，湖上渔场和周围干旱平原的主人还是更早的渔猎与游牧部族，而一支属于阿特克尔联盟的尼罗特人正赶着瘤牛从北方进入盆地。这些新来者就是图尔卡纳人，他们已与分裂出去的同族开战。

图尔卡纳人自称「灰牛之民」，名字来自他们的瘤牛。他们牧养骆驼、编织筐篓，手持长矛和钢制腕刀，每个男子还带着一只小木凳，夜里便当作枕头。指引他们的是占卜师恩吉姆罗克：他们从至高神阿库吉托领受梦示，指定为求雨、治病或出战当献的祭品。相传占卜师洛凯里奥曾分开湖水，让图尔卡纳武士步行过湖，赶走敌人的骆驼。经过几代人攻战，到17世纪，图尔卡纳人及其盟友已据有整个盆地：他们凭更出色的战术和武器击败沿途各部，把被征服者中的青年编入自己的支队，各领地由长老而非国王治理。在这片土地的边缘，他们与阿拉伯、斯瓦希里和阿比西尼亚的捕奴者、象牙商人零星交战。1821年时，还没有欧洲人见过这座湖，图尔卡纳人无可争议地据有它。

en:
Kuria land is the rolling grass country east of Lake Victoria, from the Migori river in the east to the Mara and its estuary in the west, where Kenya and Tanzania now meet. In 1444 its Bantu people, the AbaKuria, grazed cattle on the plains and planted millet and sorghum in the wetter valleys for porridge and beer, living in many independent clans whose tongue was close to that of their Gusii kinsmen in the highlands. Cattle were the measure of all wealth: the Kuria drank their milk and blood, paid them over as bride-price and slew them at the sacrifices, and boys were bound into warrior age-sets to guard the herds and the villages. A narrow Luo corridor lay between the Kuria and the lake; their other neighbours were the Suba and Ikoma, and Maa-speaking herdsmen held the grasslands far to the south-east.

The Kuria and the Gusii hold that they were once a single people, before fierce Maasai attacks in the early nineteenth century scattered them into separate countries. The same generations of Kuria warriors kept the Arab and Swahili slavers who worked the lake and the coast from establishing themselves in Kuria country. Their custom also let a woman pay bride-price in cattle and take a wife of her own; the children of that household bore her name and inherited from her, so that a line without a male heir could still be carried on.
zh:
库里亚之地是维多利亚湖以东起伏的草原，东起米戈里河，西抵马拉河及其河口，处在肯尼亚与坦桑尼亚相接之地。1444年，住在这里的阿巴库里亚人是一支班图人，在平原牧牛，在较湿润的谷地种植粟和高粱以煮粥酿酒，分成众多互不统属的氏族，语言与高地的近亲古西人相近。牛是衡量一切财富的尺度：人们饮牛奶和牛血，以牛作聘礼，也在祭祀中宰牛；男孩成年后编入武士年龄组，守护牛群和村落。库里亚人与大湖之间隔着一条卢奥人的走廊，其他邻人是苏巴人和伊科马人，东南远方的草原则属于讲马阿语的牧人。

库里亚人和古西人都认为两族本是一族，直到19世纪初马赛人的猛攻把他们打散，各自流落一方。同样是这几代库里亚武士，使在湖区和海岸活动的阿拉伯、斯瓦希里捕奴者无法在库里亚之地立足。他们的婚俗还允许女子自己以牛只支付聘礼、娶一位妻子；这户人家生下的孩子随她的姓、继承她的财产，没有男嗣的一支也能如此延续。

en:
The Shamba of the Usambara Mountains call their wet highland home Shambaai, 'where bananas thrive', above the dry nyika plains. In 1444 its clans lived in separate hill villages under their own elders, clearing forest and leading irrigation channels through banana groves. They traded iron tools, salt from the plains and shell ornaments from the coast; marriage ties linked neighbouring hills, and no one ruled the whole range.

The unifier came from outside. Early in the eighteenth century Maasai raiders from the northern steppe made the lower slopes unsafe, and refugee pastoralists followed them into the hills. Into this country came Mbegha, a hunter from the Ngulu hills, condemned at home after a quarrel and exiled again when a chief's son died beside him in a bush-pig hunt. Living in caves and camps, he was asked down by hill villages whose crops the pigs destroyed; he cleared them and killed a lion on the road to Vugha, the Shambaa chief town. The farmers made him their king, called him Simba Mwene, the Lion King, and gave him wives from each major clan; the firstborn sons were set over the clans, and the Kilindi dynasty tied the scattered hills to Vugha. His grandson Kinyashi Muanga Ike gave the court a harder military grip. Around 1815 Kimweri ye Nyumbai took power, and under him the kingdom reached its greatest extent, its arms and its ivory trade reaching down the Pangani toward the coast; firearms and the slave trade were already pulling at its edges by 1821.
zh:
乌桑巴拉山区的珊巴人把湿润的高地家乡称为尚巴伊，意为「香蕉繁盛之地」，山下便是干旱的尼伊卡平原。1444年时，各氏族在不同的山头上聚村而居，由本族长者主事，开垦森林，引水渠浇灌香蕉林。他们以铁制工具、平原的盐和来自海岸的贝饰互相交易，婚姻把相邻山头连在一起，整个山区还没有共主。

统一山区的人来自山外。18世纪初，北方草原的马赛袭掠者使低坡不再安全，避难的牧人也随之进入山地。就在这时，恩古鲁山地的猎人姆贝加来到这里：他在家乡因纷争获罪被逐，又在一次猎捕野猪时因酋长之子意外身亡而再次出逃，栖身山洞，靠打猎为生。受野猪毁害庄稼的山村请他下山除害，他清除了猪群，又在前往珊巴首邑武加的路上杀死一头狮子。山民拥他为王，称他为辛巴·姆韦内，意为「狮王」，并把各主要氏族的女子嫁给他；诸子被分遣到各氏族主事，基林迪王朝就此把分散的山头系于武加。他的孙子基尼亚希·穆安加·伊凯强化了王廷的军事控制。约1815年金韦里·耶·尼乌姆巴伊继位，在他治下王国达到最大版图，兵锋与象牙贸易沿潘加尼河伸向海岸；到1821年，火器和奴隶贸易已开始侵蚀它的边缘。

en: Gogo is the dry Ugogo plateau, the uncertain-rain country between the coastal hinterland and the western plateau of Tanzania. In 1444 Bantu-speaking homesteads lay scattered through the bush, their people growing millet and keeping cattle where pasture and waterholes held out, with authority in the hands of local elders and headmen. The country had no gold or ivory of its own, but it sat across the shortest line between the coast and the interior, and the road from Bagamoyo to Tabora ran straight through it. When the long-distance ivory caravan trade grew up in the early nineteenth century, Nyamwezi caravans crossed Ugogo and bought grain and water from Gogo homesteads; by 1821 every chief along the road expected hongo, tribute for passage, and no caravan could afford to refuse.
zh: 戈戈是干旱的乌戈戈高原，雨量无常，夹在沿海腹地与坦桑尼亚西部高原之间。1444年时，班图语居民的家户散布在灌丛中，种植黍类，在牧场和水坑能维持的地方养牛，权柄操在当地长者和头人手里。这里不产黄金和象牙，却正横在海岸通往内陆最便捷的路线上，巴加莫约到塔波拉的大路直穿全境。19世纪初长途象牙商队贸易兴起后，尼亚姆韦齐商队穿过乌戈戈，向戈戈家户购买粮食和水；到1821年，沿途每个首领都要收取「洪戈」，即过路贡赋，商队无从拒绝。

en: Nyatura is the dry Singida plateau of north-central Tanzania, country of the Arimi, a name that means farmers; their Bantu speech is Kinyaturu, which keeps words left by earlier Cushitic-speaking herders. In 1444 the Airwana, Vahi and Anyinganyi clans held to their own villages and lineage lands, growing millet and keeping cattle where pasture and water allowed. No king stood above the lineage elders, who settled disputes and arranged the marriages binding homesteads together. With the Nyiramba to the west and the Iraqw to the north they kept utani, formal joking partnerships that let farmers and cattle keepers meet and trade without feud.
zh: 尼亚图拉是干旱的辛吉达高原，在坦桑尼亚中北部，居民是阿里米人，族名意为「农人」。他们说班图语支的基尼亚图鲁语，语言里保留着更早的库希特语牧人留下的词汇。1444年时，艾尔瓦纳、瓦希和安宁加尼等氏族各守本村和世系土地，种植黍类，在水草允许的地方养牛。世系长者之上没有国王，争端由长者裁断，婚姻也由长者安排，把各家户连在一起。他们与西边的尼伊拉姆巴人和北边的伊拉库人保持着「乌塔尼」，即固定的戏谑伙伴关系，让农耕者和牧人这两种生计不同的人可以往来交易，而不结仇怨。

en:
Zigua is the hinterland country behind the Swahili coast, between the Pangani and Ruvu rivers. In 1444 its Bantu-speaking farming clans lived in palisaded villages, most of them between thirty and two hundred huts, entered through long narrow alleys built against the danger of raids. Villages on islands in the Ruvu needed no stockade; a light wooden or string bridge, sometimes strong enough for flocks, was the only way ashore. The land belonged to matriclans, and elders settled killings with bloodwealth and closed quarrels at communal ox feasts; no single chief ruled every village. At the coast stood Kaole, a Swahili trading town already old, with two coral-stone mosques and thirty pillar tombs; its merchants had shipped ivory, ebony, sandalwood and mangrove poles and kept Chinese porcelain in their houses. The smaller markets of Bagamoyo and Pangani now carried the trade with the hinterland.

The Zigua tell of a march from the north led by Seuta, a hero famed for his bow, and they count the Shambaa and Bondei as peoples who branched off from them; Mbegha, the hunter who made himself king of the Usambara hills, was born a Zigua. In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Bagamoyo grew from a fishing and farming market into a caravan stopping place, and Muslim families settling there late in the eighteenth century traded salt and taxed traffic going inland. Zigua war-leaders sent ivory, cattle and slaves to the coast in return for cloth and powder. Early in the nineteenth century Maasai and Baraguyu raids drove more villages behind palisades, and a leader's name rested on the cattle he took and the gifts he gave.
zh:
兹古阿是斯瓦希里海岸后方的腹地，在潘加尼河与鲁伏河之间。1444年时，说班图语的农耕氏族住在栅栏围护的村落里，大村小村从三十座到两百座茅屋不等，进村要穿过又长又窄的巷道，这是防备袭掠的设计。鲁伏河上的岛上村落无需栅栏，一座轻便木桥或藤桥是上岸的唯一通道，有的桥结实得能过羊群。土地归母系氏族所有，长者用偿命财了结命案，以共食牛肉的宴会平息争端；没有一个首领能统辖所有村落。海岸上的卡奥莱是一座早有年头的斯瓦希里商城，留有两座珊瑚石清真寺和三十座柱墓：那里的商人运出象牙、乌木、檀香和红树木材，家中藏过中国瓷器。与腹地往来的生意，这时由巴加莫约和潘加尼的小市场承接。

兹古阿人有自己的迁徙传说：善射的英雄塞乌塔率领他们自北方而来；他们把珊巴人和邦德伊人视为从本族分出的支系，后来在乌桑巴拉山区称王的猎人姆贝加，就生为兹古阿人。17至18世纪，巴加莫约从渔农小市场发展为商队停驻地；18世纪末定居当地的穆斯林家族经营食盐，对深入内陆的往来征税。兹古阿的军事首领把象牙、牛和奴隶送往海岸，换回布匹和火药。19世纪初，马赛人和巴拉古尤人的袭掠迫使更多村落筑起栅栏，首领的名望也取决于他夺来的牛和散出的礼物。

en:
Shaga is the old name for the Chagga country (Uchaga or Dschagga in early accounts) on the well-watered southern slopes of Kilimanjaro. Bantu farmers had climbed the mountain from about the eleventh century, terracing the wet ridges, cutting channels to carry mountain water into banana groves and keeping cattle above the hot plains. Each fenced homestead, a kihamba, held its banana grove and yams round a round grass-thatched house, ringed with the masale plant as a sign of peace. Families venerated their ancestors and Ruwa, the sun who fed them, whose shrines stood in the high forest. In 1444 the slopes were a scatter of self-ruling clan villages, the mitaa, with no king over them, while food, pots and iron passed down to Taveta, Taita and Pare.

The Chagga kingdoms hardened during the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, each ridge carrying its own mangi. Late in the eighteenth century Horombo (Orombo in English sources) ruled from Keni, raided east into Mwika and raised the great stone-walled enclosures whose ruins litter the upper ridges, his power overshadowing all of Vunjo. In the small state of Mamba, Queen Mashina kept the kingdom her husband Mafaluke had built, its smiths trading spears and necklaces for cattle; Rongoma of Kilema lured her there with a show of friendship, and she fell through the straw covering of a pit dug inside her hut and suffocated. After 1810 Rengua, whom his father Kiwaria had sent as a child to the Varoo of Mount Meru dressed as a girl, returned to Machame, overawed the Kikafu-valley clans with an iron spear and became their first mangi; his slaughter of Kibosho initiates at Kimbushi opened a feud that ran for generations. As the mountain's rulers armed after 1800, Pare and Taita smiths fed their hunger for spears, and coastal trade began to climb the Pangani basin.
zh:
沙嘎（查加，早期记载作乌查加、德查加）是乞力马扎罗山湿润南坡上查加之地的旧称。约从11世纪起，班图农民沿山而上，在湿润山脊修梯田，开渠把山水引入香蕉林，在炎热平原上方牧牛。每座围起的宅院「基汉巴」都有香蕉林和薯蓣，围着一座茅草圆屋，四周种着马萨雷树，作为和平与和解的表示。人们敬奉祖先和赐食的太阳神鲁瓦，高山密林里设有他的神龛。1444年时，山坡上是自治氏族村落「米塔」并立，没有统管全山的王；粮食、陶器和铁器往山下运到塔韦塔、泰塔和帕雷。

17至18世纪，查加诸王国成形，每道山脊各有自己的「曼吉」。18世纪末，霍龙博（英文资料作奥龙博）从凯尼发号施令，向东袭掠姆维卡，筑起巨大的石墙围寨，废址散落在高处山脊，权势盖过整个温乔。小国曼巴的女王玛希娜守着丈夫马法卢克创下的邦国，国内匠人以长矛和项链换取牲畜；基莱马的龙戈马佯称友好把她骗到基莱马，她跌入屋中铺着稻草的暗坑窒息而死。1810年后，幼年被父亲基瓦里亚男扮女装送到梅鲁山瓦鲁人那里的伦瓜回到马查姆，凭一支铁矛震慑基卡富河谷诸氏族，成为他们的第一位曼吉；他在金布希屠杀基博绍成年礼成员，结下延续数代的世仇。1800年以后，山上的诸首领纷纷置办武器，帕雷和泰塔的铁匠满足他们对战矛的渴求，海岸贸易也开始沿潘加尼河盆地深入山地。

en:
The Kikuyu country is the cool, fertile highland between the snowy pyramid of Mount Kenya, which the Agĩkũyũ call Kirinyaga, and the long ridge of the Aberdares, reaching south towards the Ngong hills and Ol Donyo Sabuk. Bantu farmers of the Thagicu branch reached the northern slopes of the mountain around the third century, and by the thirteenth century their descendants held a settled core at Murang'a, having mingled with the older hunter-gatherers of the forest; oral tradition names Gĩkũyũ and Mũmbi as the first parents, settled beneath a sacred fig tree at Mũkũrwe wa Nyagathanga. In 1444 the Agĩkũyũ were nine clans without a king, ruled by councils of elders. They tilled millet and the black njahi bean in valleys that gave two harvests a year, ran goats, sheep and cattle, and worked iron into wire and chain; sacrifices to Ngai were offered under the mugumo fig tree with the worshippers facing Kirinyaga. Years were counted by initiation sets, for the youths circumcised together were formed into regiments, and the ruling generation handed power to the next in the itwĩka ceremony roughly every thirty-five years.

The centuries that followed carried the nation steadily outward. By purchase, blood-brotherhood, intermarriage and adoption the Kikuyu drew forest hunter-gatherers into their clans and opened new ridges, and in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries a great southward movement took them from Murang'a into the Kiambu country. With the Maasai of the southern and northern plains they traded and fought by turns, while Kamba caravans brought the goods of the dry country into their markets. Arab and Swahili slavers coming up from the coast touched only the southern edge of the nation; those who pushed farther were killed, for the Kikuyu kept no slaves and answered to no overlord. When the Ndemi generation took power around 1792, the whole highland still lay in Kikuyu hands.
zh:
基库尤之地是凉爽肥沃的高地，夹在雪锥般的肯尼亚山（阿基库尤人称之为基里尼亚加）与阿伯德尔山脉的长岭之间，向南延伸到恩贡丘陵和奥尔东约奥萨布克山。属塔吉库分支的班图农民约在3世纪抵达肯尼亚山北坡，到13世纪，其后裔已在穆兰卡形成定居核心，并与林中更古老的采集狩猎者融合；口传传统把吉库尤与蒙比奉为始祖夫妇，相传他们最初住在穆库尔韦·瓦·尼亚加坦加的一棵神圣榕树下。1444年时，阿基库尤分为九大氏族，没有国王，由长老议事会治理。他们在一年两熟的谷地种植粟和黑色的恩贾希豆，饲养山羊、绵羊和牛，还把铁锻成铁丝和铁链；祭祀天神恩盖时，人们在穆古莫榕树下献祭，脸朝基里尼亚加。他们以成年礼年龄组纪年：一同割礼的青年编成连队，当政的一代约每三十五年举行「伊特维卡」礼，把权力交给下一代。

此后几个世纪，这个族群稳步向外扩展。基库尤人靠购买土地、结血盟、通婚和收养，把林中的采集狩猎者纳入氏族，开辟出新的山脊；18至19世纪，一场大南迁又把他们从穆兰卡带到基安布地方。对南北两线平原上的马赛人，他们时战时和；坎巴人的商队把干旱地区的货物运进他们的市集。从海岸北上的阿拉伯和斯瓦希里捕奴者只能擦着族群的南缘行走，再深入便会被处死，因为基库尤人不蓄奴隶，也不承认任何宗主。1792年前后恩代米一代当政时，整片高地仍完全掌握在基库尤人手中。

en: Buzinza is the south-western corner of Lake Victoria, the shore and offshore islands held by the Zinza, a Bantu people. They fish the lake, farm bananas and grain on the islands and the lake plain, and graze cattle on the grasslands behind. Hereditary smith-clans smelted local iron in charcoal furnaces and forged hoes, spears and knives, and weaving supplied a second trade good. Zinza iron, dried fish and cloth went by canoe to the Haya chiefdoms to the north and west into Karagwe. Even the rulers of Buzinza were said to come of Bunyoro stock, planted there by Bito princes moving along the lake, and the Zinza language is closest to those of the northern, Ugandan shore. In 1444 the Zinza lived under their own small chiefdoms, while the Hinda kingdom of Karagwe was rising on the hills to the east.
zh: 布津扎在维多利亚湖西南角，是班图人津扎人的湖岸和近岸岛屿。他们在湖中捕鱼，在岛屿和湖滨平原种植香蕉和谷物，在岸后草原牧牛。世袭铁匠氏族用木炭炉冶炼当地的铁，打造锄头、长矛和刀；纺织提供了第二种商货。津扎的铁器、鱼干和布匹乘独木舟销往北方的哈亚诸酋长国，并向西进入卡拉圭。据说连津扎的统治者也出自布尼奥罗世系，是沿湖南下的比托王子留下的；津扎语与湖北岸乌干达一侧各族的语言最接近。1444年，津扎人分属各自的小酋邦，欣达人的卡拉圭王国正在东边的丘陵上兴起。

en:
Busoga is the water-girt country east of the Victoria Nile, with Lake Kyoga to the north, the Mpologoma to the east and the broad reach of Lake Victoria to the south, where fishing villages such as Bukaleba worked the shallows. Its Soga people grew bananas and millet, herded cattle on the ridges and smoked fish for the inland trade. They had no common king: clan chiefs, each clan under its own totem, ruled their separate hills and answered to no overlord, though Bunyoro across the Nile was honoured as the wellspring of kingship. In 1444 every Soga chiefdom was independent.

The first Bito prince came from that same Bunyoro. Tradition says Mukama Namutukula of the Bunyoro royal house crossed Lake Kyoga in the sixteenth century with his wife Nawudo, a handful of servants, arms and a dog, and landed at Iyingo beneath Kagulu, the great rock that looks over northern Busoga. He liked the hunting, set up as a blacksmith making hoes and spears, and when he returned to Bunyoro he left the land to his five sons: Wakoli took Bukooli, Zibondo Bulamogi, Ngobi Kigulu, Tabingwa Luuka and the youngest, Kitimbo, Bugabula. He never came back, and the sons kept their chiefdoms; Bulamogi traced its line to about 1550. Bito principalities stood then beside older clan chiefdoms.

In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries the kabakas of Buganda reached in from across the Nile. Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi conquered stretches of Busoga, and the chiefs of the southern shore became Ganda clients. Rival Soga houses called Bunyoro or Buganda in by turns, paying cattle, goats and sometimes slaves to whichever court was stronger and taking their succession disputes there for judgment. In 1821 the chiefdoms still had no ruler in common.
zh:
布索加是一片四面环水之地，在维多利亚尼罗河以东：北临基奥加湖，东界姆波洛戈马河，南濒维多利亚湖浩阔的湖面，布卡莱巴等渔村在湖边浅滩捕鱼。索加人种植香蕉和黍子，在山脊牧牛，把鱼熏干后输往内陆。他们没有共主：各氏族各有图腾，酋长统治各自的丘陵，不奉宗主，只把尼罗河对岸的布尼奥罗奉为王权的源头。1444年，每个索加酋邦都是独立的。

第一位比托王子也正是来自布尼奥罗。相传16世纪，布尼奥罗王族的姆卡马·纳穆图库拉带着妻子纳武多、几名仆从、武器和一条狗渡过基奥加湖，在卡古卢巨岩脚下的伊英戈登陆；卡古卢岩俯瞰着北布索加。他喜欢此地的狩猎，又当起铁匠，打制锄头和长矛。后来返回布尼奥罗时，他把土地留给五个儿子：瓦科利领布科利，齐邦多领布拉莫吉，恩戈比领基古卢，塔宾瓜领卢卡，幼子基廷博领布加布拉。他再没有回来，儿子们便各自守住酋邦；布拉莫吉的世系可追溯到约1550年。比托系公国便与更古老的氏族酋邦并立。

17和18世纪，布干达的卡巴卡们从尼罗河对岸插手进来。金布圭、卡特雷加和穆特比征服了布索加大片土地，南岸的酋长沦为布干达的附庸。相互敌对的索加家族轮番把布尼奥罗或布干达请进来，向当时更强的王廷进贡牛、羊乃至奴隶，连继承纠纷也送去请对方裁断。到1821年，这些酋邦仍然没有共主。

en:
Karagwe, also called Bunyambo after its people the Abanyambo, is the high grassland between Rwanda and Lake Victoria. Its kings, titled Omugabe, came from the Hinda clan and claimed descent from Ruhinda, whom tradition makes a descendant of Wamara, the Chwezi ruler of Kitara. Tradition connects Ruhinda with the first politics here in 1430 to 1446 and dates the new dynasty to about 1450, with its capital at Bweranyange on the hills. Hima cattle-owning families stood above the farming clans and lent out stock to bind cultivators as clients, making Karagwe one of the most strictly ranked societies of the lake region. The Omugabes fought a long contest to bring the mediums of the Kubandwa cult under court control. The kingdom also rested on iron: closed hereditary smith-clans smelted with charcoal and forged symbolic iron cows and hammers that tied the king himself to iron-working, while their hoes and weapons sold across the lake country. In 1444 the Hinda rulers were newly settled on their hills at the head of a cattle-and-iron state.

For generations Karagwe stood inside the interlacustrine order overshadowed by Bunyoro, each clan holding an appointed role at the Bweranyange court. Late in the eighteenth century it turned against its overlord: Ntare Kiitabanyoro, Omugabe from about 1775 to 1795, destroyed a Nyoro army and carried the nickname Kitabanyoro, the Nyoro-slayer. The Bito kingdom of Kiziba then called in Buganda against its Hinda neighbours, and by 1800 Ganda arms were reaching into the Hinda chiefdoms. Ruhinda VI Orushongo ruled across the turn of the century, and about 1820 Ndagara I came to the throne; in his reign Karagwe's trade with the lake country and the coast grew large.
zh:
卡拉圭又称布尼扬博，得名于境内的尼扬博人，是卢旺达与维多利亚湖之间的高原草地。国王称奥穆加贝，出自欣达氏族，自称是齐韦兹统治者瓦马拉的后裔、英雄鲁欣达的子孙。传说鲁欣达在1430至1446年间已参与这里最早的政权，新王朝约于1450年建立，定都丘陵上的布韦拉尼扬盖。拥有牛群的希马家族高居农耕氏族之上，靠出借牲畜把农人束为依附者，使卡拉圭成为湖域等级最森严的社会之一。历代奥穆加贝长期经营，把库班德瓦神媒置于宫廷控制之下。国家的另一根支柱是铁：封闭的世袭铁匠氏族以木炭炼铁，还打制象征王权的铁牛和铁锤，把国王本人与冶锻连在一起；锄头和武器销往湖周各地。1444年，欣达统治者刚刚在丘陵上立足，统领着一个以牛群和铁器立国的政权。

此后几代人，卡拉圭处在布尼奥罗笼罩下的环大湖秩序中，各氏族在布韦拉尼扬盖宫廷各有当差。18世纪末它转而进攻宗主：约1775至1795年在位的奥穆加贝恩塔雷·基塔巴尼奥罗击溃一支尼奥罗军队，得到「基塔巴尼奥罗」（意为屠戮尼奥罗人者）的绰号。比托人的基济巴王国转而向布干达求援，对付欣达邻邦，到1800年，干达兵锋已伸入欣达诸酋邦。鲁欣达六世（号奥鲁雄戈）在世纪之交执政，约1820年恩达加拉一世即位，卡拉圭与湖域和海岸的贸易在他治下大为扩张。

en:
Buganda covers the green hills and swamps north of Lake Victoria, which the Ganda call Nalubaale. Bantu farmers making Urewe pottery had settled there by the sixth century, and Ganda tradition names Kintu the founder of the kings, who led the clans in, defeated the last indigenous ruler and then disappeared. The kingdom probably took shape between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries around the small counties of Kyadondo, Busiro and Mawokota. In 1444 the fifth kabaka, Kiggala, ruled from Kitala Hill, the capital he had founded about 1434, his power still shared with strong clan heads and hill chiefs. Their villages lived from banana gardens, and court and household dressed in barkcloth beaten from fig-tree bark.

A Bunyoro invasion in the sixteenth century killed Kabaka Nakinge, but Buganda kept its independence and grew as Bunyoro declined. Under Kimbugwe, Katerega and Mutebi in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its armies took Buddu and parts of Busoga and Karagwe, made Kooki tributary and replaced conquered rulers with royal appointees; blue beads became the state currency under Kyabaggu in the later eighteenth century, and ivory discs strung on cords followed under Junju. The kabakas ran a warfare state, sending armies out every dry season, feeding brave men at the king's own table while a coward might be burned on the field or put to women's work with a banana stem tied behind him. On the lake they built war canoes over seventy feet long carrying sixty to a hundred warriors. In 1800 Kabaka Kamanya had a hundred canoes carried overland through Busoga and reassembled on far waters to strike the Lango from the rear, while a second army marched by land. Appointed chiefs, dry-season campaigns and the war-canoe fleets made Buganda one of the strongest powers on the Great Lakes.
zh:
布干达位于维多利亚湖以北的青翠丘陵与沼泽之间，干达人称此湖为纳卢巴莱。早在6世纪，制作乌雷韦陶器的班图农民已在此定居；干达传说称诸王的始祖为金图，他率诸氏族迁入，击败土著人的末代首领，随后消失不见。王国大约在12至14世纪成形，最初只有基亚东多、布西罗和马沃科塔等小郡。1444年，第五任卡巴卡基加拉以基塔拉山为王都，这座都邑是他约1434年建立的；他的权力仍要与强势的氏族首领和山丘酋长分享。村社靠香蕉园过活，宫廷和家户穿着捶打无花果树皮制成的树皮布。

16世纪布尼奥罗入侵，杀死卡巴卡纳金格，但布干达保住独立，并趁布尼奥罗衰落而扩张。17至18世纪，在金布格韦、卡泰雷加和穆特比在位时，军队夺取布杜以及布索加、卡拉圭的部分土地，迫使库基纳贡，以国王任命的官员取代被征服者的首领；18世纪后期基亚巴古在位时，蓝珠成为国家通货，君朱时又通行穿绳的象牙圆片。历代卡巴卡维持着一个战争国家：每年旱季出兵，勇者可在国王的餐桌上受赏，临阵怯懦者则可能在战场被烧死，或在身后绑一段香蕉秆、罚做女人的活计。湖上的战船长逾七十英尺，可载六十至一百名战士。1800年，卡巴卡卡曼亚命人把一百艘战船经布索加抬过陆地，在远处水域重新组装，从后方突袭兰戈人，另一支军队同时由陆路开进。任命制酋长、旱季征战和战船队使布干达成为大湖地区最强的强权之一。

en:
This is the southern Bunyoro country around Mugenyi, on the Katonga River, the old heartland of the Chwezi rulers of Kitara before the Babiito kings. At Bigo bya Mugenyi, ditches and banks running for more than ten kilometres join the Katonga to the Kakinga swamps and wrap four central compounds on a rise above the river, with three mounds beside them. Excavators date the works to roughly 1300 to 1500 and call them the greatest ancient monument of the interlacustrine region. They found roulette-decorated pottery, iron arrowheads and a grain knife, the debris of rulers able to call out labour and keep large herds. Trade through these lands ran on salt won at Kibiro on Lake Albert, where women leached salty earth and boiled off the brine, as well as on iron and ivory. In 1444 the works marked the southern march of the old Chwezi world, which the incoming Bito dynasty was reshaping into Bunyoro; Buganda lay across the Katonga.

Bunyoro's kings took the title Omukama. Tradition makes the first of them, Rukidi Mpuga, the son of a Chwezi prince by a woman of the Luo country north of the Nile, called Bukidi; as the Chwezi order broke up he came south with his brothers and founded the Babiito line. Bito princes later carried the dynasty's power to Kiziba, the Busoga kingdoms, Buzinza and the lands west of the Rwenzoris. Duhaga ruled from 1731 to about 1782, and under his successors Bunyoro's primacy slipped: at the end of the century Buganda seized Kooki and Buddu on the southern border. Nyamutukura Kyebambe III came to the throne in 1786 and still ruled in 1821. His realm kept its wealth in salt, iron and ivory, but the Bigo earthworks lay on a frontier pressed hard by Buganda.
zh:
这是穆根伊一带、卡通加河畔的布尼奥罗南部，巴比托诸王兴起之前，这里曾是基塔拉齐韦兹统治者的旧腹地。比戈·比亚·穆根伊的壕沟与土堤绵延十多公里，把卡通加河与卡金卡沼泽连成一体，围住河畔高地上的四座中央围场，旁有三座土丘。考古学家把土垒年代定为约1300至1500年，称之为环大湖地区最宏大的古代遗址。出土物有绳纹陶、铁箭镞和一把谷刀，是能够征发劳役、保有大牛群的统治者留下的东西。这些土地上的贸易靠艾伯特湖畔基比罗出产的盐（妇女淋滤咸土、熬干卤水取盐），以及铁和象牙。1444年，土垒是旧齐韦兹世界的南部边障，新来的比托王朝正把它改造为布尼奥罗；卡通加河对岸就是布干达。

布尼奥罗的国王称奥穆卡马。相传初代国王鲁基迪·姆普加是齐韦兹王子与尼罗河北岸卢奥地方（名布基迪）一女子所生，齐韦兹秩序瓦解时，他与兄弟南来，开创巴比托王统。比托王子后来把王朝势力带到基济巴、布索加诸王国、布津扎和鲁文佐里山以西。杜哈加1731年至约1782年在位，他的后继者治下，布尼奥罗的优势渐渐丧失：18世纪末，布干达夺取了南境的科基和布杜。尼亚穆图库拉·基埃班贝三世1786年即位，1821年仍在位。他的国家仍靠盐、铁和象牙致富，但比戈土垒已处在布干达重压的边境上。

en:
Nkore, called Ankole only after the colonial conquest, is the rolling grass country east of Lake Edward between Buganda, Bunyoro, Karagwe and Rwanda. Its pastures let the herds water almost every day and the cows give milk nearly all year round, and herdsmen and neighbours alike called the land Kaaro Karungi, 'the good land'. Bahima herdsmen kept the long-horned Ankole cattle, whose horns could span more than two and a half metres, and stood above the Bairu, who grew finger millet and brewed. The mugabe ruled through cattle given in homage, war-bands called emitwe and the sacred royal drum Bagyendanwa: when a king died his sons fought, and the strongest took both the throne and the drum. Tradition calls Ruhinda, founder of the Hinda dynasty, a son of Wamara, last king of the Chwezi, and places his reign about 1430 to 1446; his son Nkuba firmed the kingship up from its core at Isingiro. In 1444 Nkore was still a small power in Bunyoro's shadow.

For two and a half centuries it stayed minor and at times owned Bunyoro's overlordship. Ntare IV, who reigned from 1699 to 1727, reversed that. Invaded by the Banyoro army of King Cwamali and beaten in the field, he sheltered first in the Nyamistindo caves and then on Kantsyore Island in the Kagera, gathered his men there, counter-attacked and killed Cwamali, earning himself the name Kiitabanyoro, 'slayer of the Banyoro'. He carried his northern border to the Katonga and took Kabula. Macwa, who followed him, kept the peace until 1755, and his death threw the succession open again. Wars with Rwanda and cattle-raids on every frontier filled the reigns after that, and in 1821 the Hinda kings still grazed their own pastures and answered to no overlord.
zh:
恩科莱在殖民征服之后才改称安科莱，是爱德华湖以东的起伏草原，夹在布干达、布尼奥罗、卡拉圭与卢旺达之间。这里牧场肥美，牛群几乎天天都能饮水，母牛终年有奶，牧人和四邻都把这片土地称为「卡鲁昆吉」，意为「好地方」。巴希马牧人放牧长角安科莱牛，牛角展幅可超过两米半，地位高于种黍子、酿酒的巴伊鲁农人。姆加贝国王靠三样东西治国：臣民进献的牛、叫做埃米特韦的战团，以及神圣王鼓巴吉丹瓦维；国王死后儿子们相争，最强者同时得到王位和王鼓。相传欣达王朝的开国君鲁欣达是奇韦齐末代国王瓦马拉之子，在位时间约为1430至1446年；他的儿子恩库巴在伊辛吉罗的核心之地巩固了王权。1444年，恩科莱还是布尼奥罗阴影下的一个小国。

此后两个半世纪里它一直是个小国，有时还向布尼奥罗称臣。1699至1727年在位的恩塔雷四世扭转了局面。茨瓦马利国王率布尼奥罗军队来犯，恩塔雷初战失利，先避入尼亚米斯廷多洞穴，又退守卡盖拉河中的坎乔雷岛；他在岛上收拢部众，反攻并杀死茨瓦马利，赢得「基塔巴尼奥罗」之名，意为「诛杀尼奥罗人者」。他把北界推进到卡通加河，夺取卡布拉。继他之后的马克瓦把和平维持到1755年，他一死，继承之争再起。其后诸王的岁月充斥着与卢旺达的战事和各条边境上的掠牛之行；到1821年，欣达诸王仍在自己的牧场上放牧，不向任何宗主称臣。

en:
Nduga is the hilly country of central Rwanda around old Gitarama, reaching south toward Nyanza and watered by the Nyabarongo. Banana groves and cattle pastures supported the Ababanda kingdom whose king ruled from Rwesero and displayed the royal drum Nyabahinda as his emblem. Twa hunters, Hutu farmers and incoming cattle-keeping lineages lived on the same hills. In 1444 Nduga still had its own king and army; the Nyiginya rulers at Gasabo, around Lake Muhazi, were the lords of a neighboring chiefdom rather than masters of the whole country.

In Rwandan oral tradition, the conquest turns on refuge, marriage and a feast. The Ababanda king Mashira was driven out and sheltered in Bugesera, then fought his way back to Nduga. Mibambwe Mutabazi accepted the restoration and gave Mashira his daughter Nyirantobwa. When Mibambwe later visited Nduga as a guest, Rwandan warriors seized Mashira at Nyamagana near Nyanza during the entertainment, killed him and his sons, and destroyed the Ababanda army. With the royal line cut off, Nduga was absorbed into the expanding Nyiginya kingdom during the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
zh:
恩杜加位于卢旺达中部丘陵，即旧吉塔拉马一带，向南延伸至尼安扎附近，尼亚巴隆戈河为这里供水。香蕉园和牧牛场支撑着阿班达王国；国王从鲁韦塞罗山实行统治，以圣鼓尼亚巴欣达为王权标志。特瓦猎人、胡图农民和迁入的牧牛氏族同住于这些丘陵。1444年，恩杜加仍有自己的国王和军队；驻在加萨博、环穆哈齐湖而治的尼金亚统治者只是邻近一个酋长国的君主，还不是整个地区的主人。

卢旺达口述传统中，这场征服围绕避难、联姻和一场宴会展开。阿班达国王马希拉被逐后在布格塞拉避难，随后反攻回到恩杜加。米班布韦·穆塔巴齐承认其复位，把女儿尼兰托布瓦嫁给他。后来米班布韦以宾客身份到访，卢旺达武士在尼安扎附近尼亚马加纳的宴饮间拿下马希拉，处死他和他的儿子，并歼灭阿班达军队。王统断绝后，恩杜加在16至17世纪被扩张中的尼金亚王国吞并。

en:
Bafuriru is the highland country above the northern end of Lake Tanganyika, where the mountains of Uvira look down on the Ruzizi plain, the open march along the borders of Rwanda and Burundi. Its clans hold the valleys of Mulenge, Luvungi and Lemera, keep cattle on the ridges, and make pottery and woven baskets, the baskets used even as musical instruments. The Bafuliru are unusual among the highland Bantu of the Great Lakes: the Bahamba clan drew the scattered settlements together into the Hamba kingdom, a small state whose court was more centralised than the autonomous village lands around it. In 1444 the mwami ruled from Lemera, while the plain below served mostly as pasture and hunting ground, the side on which Rwanda and Burundi pressed closest.

Tradition names Kahamba Kalingishi as the founder who united the clans at Lemera and began the royal line, though oral accounts date him anywhere between the sixteenth century and the start of the nineteenth. Their kinsmen the Vira hold the lakeside slopes, spread from Mount Munanira above Uvira and dividing the Uvira highlands with the Bafuliru. From the 1600s Bafuliru hunters and herders made their way down into the Ruzizi plain, the frontier between the mountains and the two royal kingdoms.
zh:
巴夫里鲁位于坦噶尼喀湖北端的高地，乌维拉山区在此俯临鲁济济平原，那是沿着卢旺达、布隆迪边界展开的开阔边地。当地诸氏族据有穆伦盖、卢温吉和莱梅拉的河谷，在山脊上牧牛，制作陶器和编织篮筐，篮筐甚至能当乐器使用。在大湖地区的高地班图人中，巴夫里鲁人是个异数：巴汉巴氏族把分散的聚落合并成汉巴王国，这个小国的王廷比周围自治的山村之地更为集权。1444年，姆瓦米在莱梅拉统辖全境，山下的平原主要用作牧场和猎场，卢旺达和布隆迪也正是从这一侧逼近。

相传卡汉巴·卡林吉希在莱梅拉统一诸氏族、开创王统，但口述传统给他的年代从16世纪到19世纪初说法不一。与他们相近的维拉人占据沿湖山坡，以乌维拉上方的穆纳尼拉山为中心散布开来，与巴夫里鲁人分据乌维拉高地。17世纪起，巴夫里鲁的猎人和牧人陆续进入鲁济济平原，那是山地与两个王权王国之间的前沿。

en: Bushubi is the highland country of the Washubi around Ngara, well-watered ridges in north-western Tanzania pressed between Rwanda, Burundi and the Karagwe and Buha kingdoms. The Shubi lived by hunting before turning mainly to farming; they grow grain and keep cattle, and their Bantu speech is close to Kinyarwanda and Kirundi. In 1444 the hill villages were ruled by their own kings, titled mwami, remembered by the royal names Magina, Kibogora, Nsoro and Kinanaira. Shubi tradition ties the line to Ruhinda, the ruler who led his followers south from Ankole to found Karagwe: one of his sons is said to have pushed on to Lusubi and set up a kingship without a fight, for the scattered farmers could not stop his well-armed, cattle-rich following. The Shubi kingdom then kept its place among the Great Lakes states, trading and intermarrying with Rwanda, Burundi and Buha and fighting its border wars.
zh: 布苏毕是瓦苏比人的山地，在今坦桑尼亚西北部恩加拉一带水源充足的山梁上，夹在卢旺达、布隆迪与卡拉圭、布哈诸王国之间。苏比人本以狩猎为生，后来主要转为农耕，种植谷物、牧养牛群，所说的班图语接近卢旺达语和布隆迪语。1444年，山村由苏比人自己的国王统治，国王称姆瓦米，流传下的王名有马吉纳、基博戈拉、恩索罗和基纳奈拉。按苏比传说，这一王统出自鲁欣达：这位首领率部从安科勒南迁，建立卡拉圭王国，据说他的一个儿子继续前行来到卢苏比，没经过多少战事便在那里称王，因为分散的农夫挡不住他那武装精良、牛羊成群的部众。苏比王国此后周旋于大湖诸邦之间，与卢旺达、布隆迪和布哈贸易、通婚，也打过边境战争。

en:
Nkoma is the ridge country of the Nkoma massif, which dominates the hot Moso depression and overlooks the Kumoso plain in what is now Rutana Province, southeastern Burundi. In 1444 no king held court here. Bantu farmers, Twa hunter-foragers and a few cattle-keeping families lived in scattered hill homesteads under local heads, their millet fields, herds and forges tying the ridge to both the Buha and Burundian worlds; they honoured the high god Imana and the Kiranga spirit cult.

The southern cycle of Burundian royal tradition is called the Nkoma cycle after these hills. It tells how the founder Ntare Rushatsi, raised as a cattle herder at the court of the Buha king Ruhaga, was fetched back across the Malagarasi River to end a famine in Burundi. At Mount Nkoma he slaughtered the bull he had brought with him and stretched its hide over a termite mound; when Inkoma, the serpent inside, struck the hide, the first royal drum was made from it and named Karyenda, the drum that became the sign of Burundian kingship. The first mwami known to history, Ntare I, reigned from about 1680 and united the northern and southern centres of the country, also setting up the Sentare, a panel of judges for property disputes between chiefs. From about 1795 Ntare IV Rugamba, whose regnal name means 'war', pushed Burundian power eastward against the small polities of Buha, and in 1821 Nkoma lay on the frontier his armies were pressing toward the old Ha courts.
zh:
恩科马是恩科马山体的山脊地带，这座山雄踞于干热的莫索洼地，俯临今布隆迪东南部鲁塔纳省境内的库莫索平原。1444年时，没有国王在此设朝。班图农民、特瓦族狩猎采集者和为数不多的牧牛家族散居各处山梁，受本地首领管辖，粟田、牛群和锻炉把这片山地同布哈与布隆迪两边的世界连在一起；人们敬奉至高神伊马纳，也崇奉基兰加神灵。

布隆迪王室口述传统中南方一系称「恩科马系」，名字就来自这片山梁。相传开国者恩塔雷·鲁沙齐幼年在布哈国王鲁哈加的宫廷里牧牛，后来被人渡过马拉加拉西河接回布隆迪，以消弭国中饥荒。他到恩科马山后杀了随行带来的公牛，把牛皮蒙在一个白蚁冢上；冢中毒蛇因科马撞上皮子，第一面王鼓就此制成，名为卡林达，后来成为布隆迪王权的标志。史上可考的第一位姆瓦米恩塔雷一世约1680年在位，统一了国土南北两个中心，还设立称森塔雷的法官庭，裁决首领之间的田产纷争。约1795年起，王号意为「战争」的恩塔雷四世·鲁加姆巴把布隆迪势力向东推向布哈诸小邦；1821年时，恩科马正处在他的军队向旧哈人王庭进逼的边境上。

en:
Buyogoma is the high eastern plateau between the Ruvubu valley and the Moso plains, where the grasslands of Buha run up against the Burundian hills. In 1444 its Ha farmers, the Abaha, lived in dispersed homesteads and spoke Kiha, a Bantu language close to Kirundi. They grew sorghum and millet, kept goats and cattle where the tsetse fly was light, and hunted and gathered honey in the lowland belts. Ancestor spirits and the high god Imana ordered their religious life, and at the hill markets their iron hoes, spears and salt changed hands against the goats, cattle and skins brought over from Urundi.

The plateau was a western march of Buha's small kingships, held at the end of the eighteenth century by the Buha mwami Ruhaga rather than by any town-based court. Across the border, Ntare IV Rugamba of Burundi, whose regnal name means 'war', conquered Bugesera between 1796 and 1801 and then marched against Ruhaga, coveting Buyogoma's granaries and open grazing. Buha began to break apart under the blows. In 1821 the plateau had still not been absorbed by Burundi: its villages answered to the Ha court while Burundian armies campaigned on the approaches.
zh:
布约戈马是鲁武布河谷与莫索平原之间的东部高原，布哈的草原在这里接上布隆迪的丘陵。1444年，这里的哈人农民（自称阿巴哈人）散居各家庄园，说与基隆迪语相近的班图语基哈语。他们种高粱和粟米，在采采蝇稀少处养山羊和牛，在低湿地带狩猎、采蜜。祖先神灵和至高神伊马纳主宰着信仰生活；山地集市上，铁锄、长矛和盐用来交换从布隆迪贩来的山羊、牛和兽皮。

这片高原是布哈诸小王国的西部边地，18世纪末由布哈姆瓦米鲁哈加掌握，并不存在以城镇为中心的朝廷。邻国的布隆迪国王恩塔雷四世·鲁加姆巴王号意为「战争」，他先在1796至1801年间征服布格塞拉，随后又觊觎布约戈马的粮仓和开阔牧场，发兵攻打鲁哈加。布哈在连番打击下逐渐瓦解。1821年时，高原尚未被布隆迪吞并：村落仍听命于哈人王庭，布隆迪军队已在邻近地区作战。

en:
Ruguru, also called Luguru or Nkanda-Luguru, was one of the small Ha chiefdoms of Buha, covering the country around Basanza, Murufyiti and Makere in the Kasulu hills. In 1444 Kiha-speaking clans lived in scattered homesteads on fertile grassland and open woodland under clan elders called muteko. Women grew millet and other food crops; men hunted, gathered honey and kept cattle where the tsetse fly allowed. Ha smelters forged hoes, knives and arrows, which went to highland markets such as Kwigarame and Mwibuye in exchange for goats, skins and the salt of Uvinza, a trade controlled by the neighbouring Nkalinzi chiefdom.

Around 1800, during Buha's succession wars, cattle-keeping Tutsi dynasties known as the Abhakimbiri imposed a new hierarchy on the chiefdoms. Their ubugabire bond tied a client to his lord through the gift of cattle: he built the lord's house, worked his fields and brought him honey and beer. A mwami and his appointed watwale officials rose above the muteko elders, who nevertheless kept the ritual tasks and alone installed a new mwami, while tribute in grain, salt, milk, honey and cattle flowed to the new courts. By 1821 Nkanda-Luguru was counted among Buha's six chiefdoms, its Ha clans folded into a cattle aristocracy that answered to the mwami of Heru, the senior chiefdom.
zh:
卢古鲁又称恩坎达-卢古鲁，是布哈的哈人小酋邦之一，据有卡苏卢丘陵中巴桑扎、穆鲁菲蒂和马凯雷一带。1444年，说基哈语的氏族散居在肥沃草地和开阔疏林中，由称穆特科的氏族长老统领。妇女种植粟米等粮食，男子狩猎、采蜜，并在采采蝇为害不重处养牛。哈人铁匠锻打锄头、刀和箭，送到奎加拉梅、姆维布耶等山地集市，交换山羊、兽皮和乌温扎盐；这宗盐的贸易由邻近的恩卡林齐酋邦把持。

约1800年布哈继承战争期间，称阿巴基姆比里的牧牛图西王朝在各酋邦之上建立起新的等级。他们以乌布加比雷关系约束部众：领主以牛相赐，受赐者为他建房、耕田，献上蜂蜜和酒。姆瓦米和他任命的瓦特瓦莱官员高踞穆特科长老之上，但长老仍掌管仪式，并且只有他们能为新姆瓦米行继位礼；谷物、盐、奶、蜜和牛等贡赋流入新王庭。到1821年，恩坎达-卢古鲁已是布哈六酋邦之一，哈人氏族被纳入牧牛贵族体系，尊赫鲁酋邦的姆瓦米为共主。

en: Hehe is the high southern plateau later called Uhehe, the grazing country around Iringa above the Great Ruaha River, northeast of Lake Nyasa. In 1444 no ruler held it as a single kingdom. Bantu villagers grew grain on the hillsides and kept cattle and goats where pasture allowed, under small chiefs whose chiefdoms rarely ran to more than a few thousand people. Local traditions remember the groups living there before the Hehe name existed: the Hafiwa in the Welu highland valleys, the Vanyategeta of Udzungwa who were skilled blacksmiths, the Vanyakilwa of Mufindi who traced their origin to Kilwa on the coast, and the Vasavila and Vadongwe of the Welu and Uhambingeto hills. Chiefs raided one another for cattle, married into each other's families and dropped the alliances when advantage turned. Through 1821 the plateau stayed a patchwork of rival homesteads and chiefdoms, with no court that could speak for all the people later called the Hehe.
zh: 赫赫是后来被称为乌赫赫的南方高原，位于大鲁阿哈河上游、尼亚萨湖东北的伊林加一带牧地。1444年时，没有任何统治者把它统一为一个王国。说班图语的村民在坡地上种谷，在有牧草的地方养牛和山羊；小酋长们的酋邦大多不过几千人。当地口传记得「赫赫」一名出现以前居住在此的诸群体：韦鲁高地谷地中的哈菲瓦人，在乌宗圭瓦以打铁闻名的瓦尼亚特盖塔人，发祥于沿海基尔瓦、住在穆芬迪的瓦尼亚基尔瓦人，以及韦鲁山和乌汉宾盖托山中的瓦萨维拉人与瓦东圭人。酋长们互相夺牛、彼此联姻，局势一变便撕毁盟约。直到1821年，这片高原仍是彼此争竞的牧人家户和酋邦拼成的地方，没有一个宫廷能号令后来所称的赫赫全体。

en:
Pubungo, called Pubungu in Luo tradition, was a crossing of the Albert Nile where the town of Pakwach later grew, set in short-grass country good for cattle. In 1444 it was a ferry and a grazing frontier rather than a walled town. Older Madi-, Okebo- and Lendu-speaking communities held the river banks and the surrounding savanna alongside incoming Luo clans; they fished the Nile, grew sorghum and millet, and kept sheep, goats and cattle. Village and kin elders settled disputes, and Bunyoro's power reached only the southern approaches.

Luo tradition remembers Pubungu as the point where migrants coming down the Nile divided, some staying by the river and others moving west or south into Bunyoro. The Babiito kings traced their own founder, Rukidi Mpuga, to the Luo country north of the Nile, so the fords here fed both the small river chiefdoms and the dynasty at Bunyoro. From the late seventeenth century chiefdoms arose under rulers called rwodi, who took royal drums and regalia from Bunyoro, redistributed tribute and called out large communal hunts. In 1821 the country remained a cattle frontier between the Bito monarchy and the Luo chiefdoms later named Acholi, a world of trade, marriage and raiding without fixed borders.
zh:
普布恩戈在卢奥传统中称普本古（Pubungu），地处阿尔伯特尼罗河上的渡口，即后来帕夸奇兴起的地方，周围是宜于牧牛的短草地。1444年时，这里只是渡口和畜牧边地，没有城墙。更早的马迪、奥凯博和伦杜语共同体占据河岸与周围稀树草原，迁入的卢奥氏族与他们共居；众人在尼罗河中捕鱼，种植高粱和粟米，饲养绵羊、山羊和牛。争端由村落和氏族长老裁断，布尼奥罗的势力只到其南缘。

卢奥传统把普本古记作沿尼罗河南下的迁徙者分路之处：一部分人留在河畔，另一部分向西或向南进入布尼奥罗。巴比托诸王也把开国先祖鲁基迪·姆普加的出身追溯到尼罗河北岸的卢奥地方，这一带的渡口因此既连着河畔小酋邦，也连着布尼奥罗王朝。17世纪末起，称为鲁奥迪（rwodi）的统治者建立酋邦，采用布尼奥罗的王鼓和王权仪仗，再分配贡物、召集大型围猎。1821年，这里仍是比托王朝与后来得名阿乔利的卢奥诸酋邦之间的牧牛边境，维系各方的是贸易、婚姻和袭掠，没有固定边界。

en:
Lango is the grass-and-papyrus country north of Lake Kyoga, where Lake Kwania and wide swamps run toward the borders of Bunyoro. The people who later took the name Lango belonged to the Ateker world of the Karamojong, Teso and Jie, cattle-keeping eastern Nilotes of the dry plains, and their speech gradually took a Luo form close to Acholi. In 1444 their ancestors still grazed herds far to the east among the Jie, and the Kyoga wetlands were merely a remote frontier on Bunyoro's edge. They kept no kings: clan elders settled land, marriage disputes, sacrifice and tribute, and when several clans had to fight together they chose a war leader whose command ended as soon as peace returned. A household won its fields by being the first to break unused ground, and Jok and the ancestral spirits guarded clan life.

Around 1780 Lango groups split from the Jie and moved west with Teso-related peoples, halting for a time around Mount Otuke before they entered the Kyoga lowlands. By 1821 their clans were settling the wetland frontier, still with no permanent chief or central court, their lives bound to cattle, cultivation, hunting and the favour of Jok.
zh:
兰戈是基奥加湖北方的草原与纸莎草之乡，夸尼亚湖和大片沼泽一直延伸到布尼奥罗边境。后来以兰戈为名的人群原属阿特克尔世界，与卡拉莫琼人、特索人、杰人同系，是干旱平原上牧牛的东尼罗特人，语言则逐渐变成与阿乔利语相近的卢奥形态。1444年时，他们的先民还在东方的杰人当中放牧，基奥加湿地只是布尼奥罗边缘一处遥远的边疆。他们不立国王：氏族长老裁断土地、婚姻争端、祭祀和贡纳；几个氏族需要联合作战时才选出一名战时首领，和平一回来，他的指挥权即告终止。一户人家最先开垦无主土地，便得到那块田；乔克神和祖灵护佑着氏族生活。

约1780年，兰戈各群体从杰人中分出，与同特索有关的人群一同西迁，在奥图凯山附近停留过一段时间，随后进入基奥加低地。到1821年，各氏族已在湿地边疆安顿下来，依旧没有常设首领和中央宫廷，生活系于牲畜、农耕、狩猎和乔克神的庇佑。

en:
Muhambwe is the ridge country of the Wahambwe, the Kibondo branch of the Ha, in the Buha highlands east of Lake Tanganyika, on the approaches to Burundi and Rwanda. Their Kiha speech is close to Kirundi and Kinyarwanda, and their clans took names from totems, a beast, bird or insect, or from the ground they settled: the Wayungu held the clay country around Kakonko, the Wanyaheru the high Heru ridges. Farmers grew sorghum and beans on the hillsides, fishermen worked Lake Tanganyika and the Malagarasi, and herdsmen kept cattle on the upper slopes. Men dressed in barkcloth and families lived in round mud-and-wood houses. Cattle-keeping Tutsi lineages, the same pastoral order that ruled Rwanda and Burundi, stood above the Ha cultivators as overlords.

In 1444 the highlands were a scatter of independent clans with no king over them. The Buha chiefdoms took shape only around 1800, as related Ha clans drew together under hereditary rulers; Muhambwe then stood alongside Heru, Bushingo, Ruguru and Buyungu as one of the small Ha states.
zh:
穆罕布韦是瓦汉布韦人的丘陵之乡，他们是哈人（阿巴哈）的基邦多支系，住在坦噶尼喀湖以东的布哈高地，邻近布隆迪和卢旺达。他们的基哈语与基隆迪语、卢旺达语相近；各氏族以图腾为名，取一种野兽、禽鸟或昆虫，或取所居的土地：瓦永古人占有卡孔科一带的黏土地，瓦尼亚赫鲁人住在赫鲁的高脊上。农民在坡地种高粱和豆子，渔民在坦噶尼喀湖和马拉加拉西河打鱼，牧人在高坡牧牛。男人穿树皮衣，一家人住在土木圆屋里。牧牛的图西人世系与统治卢旺达、布隆迪的是同一个游牧阶层，地位在哈人耕作者之上。

1444年时，高地上只是互不统属的独立氏族，没有统管他们的王。布哈诸酋邦到1800年前后才成形，彼此关联的哈人氏族聚合于世袭首领之下；穆罕布韦与赫鲁、布欣戈、鲁古鲁、布永古并列，是哈人的小邦之一。

en:
Rukwa takes its name from the long soda lake caught in the trough between Lake Tanganyika and Lake Nyasa, with no outlet and a shoreline that grows and shrinks with the rains. Above its western side rises the open, thinly wooded Ufipa Plateau, high ground between the two lakes on the way towards the Congo. Fipa, Wanda and Nyika clans farmed its ridges and kept cattle, but the plateau's prized wealth was iron: smelting needed rare skill, and the smiths guarded it so closely that whole clans became their subjects. In 1444 elected village headmen governed a scatter of plateau settlements, and smith clans already bartered hoes and iron for woven cloth; the foremost of them, Milanzi, was called 'the eternal village'.

During the seventeenth century Milanzi became the central Fipa chiefdom, but around 1700 an immigrant clan, the Twa, took power and divided the country into Nkansi and Lyangalile. The old smith dynasty kept its ritual standing and the right to install the new ruler, while the Twa governed the land through appointed officers down to elected village headmen. Nkansi carried this order furthest: its chief kept a prime minister and a court of at least nine titled officials, and the queen mother held her own palace, court and tribute estate. A female magistrate in each village judged brawls and breaches of public order; a murderer was handed over to the victim's family as compensation unless he became their slave, and only the chief could order death, carried out by poison, spearing or beheading. Iron, grain, cattle and cloth moved between the courts, villages and lake approaches, and the open plateau bore a tighter, more layered rule than its empty borders suggest.
zh:
鲁夸得名于夹在坦噶尼喀湖与尼亚萨湖之间凹陷地带的狭长苏打湖；湖泊没有出口，湖岸随降雨涨缩。湖西隆起开阔而林木稀疏的乌菲帕高原，是两湖之间、朝向刚果方向的高地。菲帕、旺达和尼伊卡氏族在脊地上农耕、牧牛，但高原上最贵重的财富是铁：冶铁需要稀罕手艺，铁匠把技术守得极严，整族整村的人都成了他们的属民。1444年时，民选的村落头人分管高原上散落的聚落，铁匠氏族已在用铁锄和铁料换取布匹，其中为首的米兰齐号称「永恒之村」。

17世纪，米兰齐成为菲帕人的中心酋邦；约1700年，外来的特瓦氏族夺取权力，把国土分为恩坎西和利扬加利莱两部。旧铁匠家族保留宗教地位和为新首领授职的权力，特瓦人则经由任命的官吏、直到民选的村落头人治理土地。恩坎西把这套秩序推得最远：首领之下设有首相和至少九名带头衔的官员，王太后拥有自己的宫殿、宫廷和纳贡庄园。每村有一名女法官，审理斗殴和扰乱公共秩序的案件；杀人犯交给死者家属抵偿，否则便成为其家奴；只有首领能判死刑，以毒药、长矛或斩首执行。铁器、粮食、牲畜和布匹在宫廷、村落与通往湖区的道路间流转，这片开阔高原上的统治，比它空旷的边界显得更严密、更有层次。

en:
Mayumba is the southern Gabonese coast of long sandspits cut off from the mainland by the Banio and Ndogo lagoons. Bantu villagers of the Lumbu and Vili peoples, both close kin of the Bakongo, fished the shallows, gathered the oysters for which the bay was known, and boiled sea salt to carry inland to the Punu; ivory and raffia cloth changed hands on the beach markets. In 1444 the lagoon mouths were a string of small Lumbu and Vili chiefdoms. Dutch records later named Mayumba among the tiny coastal states, each with its own leader, that 'made war on each other' before Loango grew up among them, and Portuguese ships first sailed this coast in the 1470s.

The founder Njimbe built Loango in the later 1500s, overcoming rivals such as Kilongo while the still more northerly districts of Docke and Sette gave in without a fight; at the kingdom's seventeenth-century strength the king at Bwali and his Vili governors held the coast all the way up to Cape St Catherine. Just north of Mayumba, Setté Cama shipped timber and ivory to Dutch and English vessels that anchored offshore and paid the mafouk, the royal officer who handled all trade with foreigners. Mayumba dealt in the same goods, and from the late 1600s Vili merchants brought captives down from the interior as well, to join ivory, raffia and salt among the exports. Through the eighteenth century the lagoon villages stayed small markets on the far northern edge of the Loango world.
zh:
马永巴所在的加蓬南部海岸是一列长沙嘴，巴尼奥、恩多戈等潟湖把沙嘴与陆地隔开。伦布人和维利人的班图村落散布其间，两支人都与巴刚果人相近。村民在浅海捕鱼，采摘这一带海湾出产的牡蛎，又熬煮海盐运往内地卖给蓬古人；象牙和拉菲亚布就在海滩市集上易手。1444年，这些潟湖口是一连串伦布、维利小酋邦。荷兰人的记载后来把马永巴列为卢安果兴起之前海岸上「各有首领、彼此攻战」的小国之一；到1470年代，葡萄牙船只第一次航行到这片海岸。

16世纪后期，创建者恩津贝建立卢安果，先后征服基隆古等对手，更北边的一些地区，包括塞泰，则不战而降；17世纪王国势力最强时，布瓦利的国王和维利长官管辖的海岸北达圣凯瑟琳角，马永巴也在其中。塞泰卡马在马永巴以北，是木材和象牙的输出港，荷兰、英国商船停泊外海，生意都要经王室贸易官马富克之手，外商由他统一接待。马永巴经营同类货物；17世纪末以后，维利商人还从内陆贩来俘虏，与象牙、拉菲亚布和海盐一同出口。整个18世纪，这些潟湖村落始终是卢安果世界北疆上的小市集。

en:
Ngoyo was the kingdom of the Woyo, a Bakongo people, on the coast immediately north of the Congo River, around the bay later called Cabinda; its capital was Mbanza Ngoyo. Its dynasties claimed the earliest roots in the soil, so its chiefs bore the title nfumu nsi, 'lords of the earth', and with Vungu and Kakongo the country had belonged to the old coastal confederations out of which the Kingdom of Kongo itself grew. In 1444 Ngoyo lay in Kongo's northern shadow, its boats carrying ivory, raffia cloth and red tukula dyewood along a coast no European ship had reached.

Diogo Cão opened the coast in 1482–83, and by 1535 Ngoyo was named in the titles of the Manikongo Afonso I. The small kingdom's later years were spent caught in Soyo's wars. A Soyo army set the ruler's son on the throne at Mbanza Ngoyo in the 1630s, and in 1670 Ngoyo answered Soyo's call for allies and sent men and arms to Kitombo, where the Portuguese army invading from Angola was destroyed and the commanders on both sides were killed. In 1682 an exile from Loango's Christian faction, Miguel da Silva, was elected ruler of Ngoyo; not long afterwards the prince of Soyo, António II Baretto da Silva, invaded again, and English traders who tried to shield Ngoyo were brushed aside. By 1700 Cabinda had become the leading slave port north of Luanda, and the kingdom lived by captives brought up from the interior. The kingship cost more than it repaid with every reign, and after a joint attack with Kakongo on a Portuguese fort was beaten off in 1783, the old kingdom slowly broke into chiefdoms.
zh:
恩戈约是沃约人的王国。沃约人属巴刚果一支，住在刚果河正北的海岸，即后来卡宾达湾一带，都城为姆班扎·恩戈约。王族自称是这片土地最早的主人，首领因此号称恩富姆·恩西，意为「大地之主」；它与温古、卡刚果同属古老的海岸邦联，刚果王国正是从这些邦联中兴起的。1444年，恩戈约处在刚果的北方阴影下，居民的船只沿欧洲人尚未到过的海岸贩运象牙、拉菲亚布和红色的图库拉染木。

迪奥戈·康在1482至1483年间打开了这片海岸，到1535年，恩戈约已列在马尼刚果阿方索一世的名号之中。这个小王国后来的岁月多被索约的战争牵动：1630年代，索约军队把索约统治者的儿子扶上姆班扎·恩戈约的王位；1670年，恩戈约应索约之请派出士兵和武器，在基通博合力歼灭从安哥拉来犯的葡萄牙军，双方主将双双战死。1682年，一个从卢安果基督教派系争斗中逃来的人米格尔·达席尔瓦被推举为恩戈约的统治者；此后不久，索约亲王安东尼奥二世·巴雷托·达席尔瓦再度入侵，想庇护恩戈约的英国商人也被击退。到1700年，卡宾达已成为罗安达以北最大的奴隶港，恩戈约靠从内陆贩来的俘虏为生。王位的耗费一任比一任沉重，1783年与卡刚果联手攻打葡萄牙要塞失败后，这个古老王国便渐渐碎成一个个酋邦。

en:
Soyo was the coastal province of the Kingdom of Kongo, running south from the mouth of the Congo River to the Loze and about a hundred kilometres inland. Its governor, the mwene Soyo or 'lord of Soyo', was usually a royal kinsman serving a limited term, and the river port of Mpinda handled the kingdom's Atlantic traffic. In 1444 Soyo was the seaward edge of the Bakongo world, and no European sailor had yet entered the estuary.

Diogo Cão sailed into the river in 1482 and set up a stone pillar to St George on the headland. In 1491 the lord of Soyo, baptised Manuel and said to be the king's own uncle, became the first Kongo ruler to accept Christianity. Portuguese traders settled at Mpinda and shipped ivory, copper and slaves; a royal inquest of 1548 counted as many as 4,000 captives a year passing through to São Tomé and on to Brazil. When European titles reached the Kongo court, Álvaro II made its ruler Miguel a count in the early 1590s.

The counts of Soyo soon stopped taking orders from São Salvador. From 1641 Count Daniel da Silva insisted that the county's nobles elected their own lord, and Garcia II's armies came to grief four times in the fortified forest of Nfinda Ngula. In 1670 a Portuguese army invaded from Angola to put an end to Soyo; on 18 October, at Kitombo, the Soyo host with Ngoyo's men and Dutch muskets and cannon destroyed it, leaving the Portuguese commander João Soares de Almeida and the Soyo commander Estêvão da Silva dead on the field. Its rulers afterwards called themselves grand princes and made and unmade kings during Kongo's civil wars, until after 1708 they took no further part in the royal elections.
zh:
索约是刚果王国的沿海省份，从刚果河口向南延伸到洛热河，深入内陆约一百公里。长官称「索约之主」，多由国王的亲族出任，任期有限；河港姆平达掌管王国通往大西洋的买卖。1444年，索约是刚果面向大洋的一面，欧洲航海者还从未驶入过这条河口。

1482年，迪奥戈·康驶进刚果河，在岬角立起献给圣乔治的石柱。1491年，受洗取名曼努埃尔、据说是国王舅父的索约之主，成为第一个皈依基督教的刚果统治者。葡萄牙商人在姆平达定居，运出象牙、铜和奴隶；1548年刚果王室的调查显示，每年经这里运往圣多美、再转巴西的俘虏多达四千名。后来欧洲式爵位传入刚果宫廷，16世纪90年代初，阿尔瓦罗二世封索约统治者米格尔为伯爵。

索约的伯爵们很快不再听命于圣萨尔瓦多。1641年起，达尼埃尔·达席尔瓦伯爵坚持索约领主由本地贵族推选，加西亚二世四度出兵，都在设防的恩芬达恩古拉森林中惨败。1670年，一支葡萄牙军队从安哥拉来犯，想一举消灭索约；10月18日的基通博一战，索约军在恩戈约援兵和荷兰人提供的火枪火炮支援下将其歼灭，葡萄牙主将若昂·苏亚雷斯·德阿尔梅达和索约主将埃斯特旺·达席尔瓦都战死阵中。此后索约统治者自称大亲王，在刚果的内战中废立国王；1708年以后，他们不再参加国王推选。

en:
Songo is the forest-and-savanna country east of Okanga, the district Portuguese records often spell Okanga. Its Kikongo-speaking villagers farmed the inland valleys and wove palm-fibre cloth that travelled west to the markets of Mbanza-Kongo. Their elders remembered the loose realm the Portuguese called the Seven Kingdoms of Kongo dia Nlaza, or the Momboares, which ran from the Kwale toward the Kwango and was drawn into Kongo through the eastern province of Mbata; Mbata's own lord held the honorific 'grandfather of the King of Kongo'. In 1444 Songo lay on Kongo's loosely held eastern approaches. Its headmen answered greater lords for tribute and war service, while the shrines, village councils and looms stayed in local hands.

The court at Mbanza-Kongo turned Catholic after Diogo Cão reached the coast in 1483 and the Manikongo was baptised in 1491, but the new faith changed little this far inland. Songo's real link to the Atlantic was cloth. After the Portuguese founded Luanda in 1575, their fiscal officer Pero Sardinha reported an average of 45,000 Songo cloths arriving there each year in 1611 and 1612. The Jaga raids of 1568 opened long years of border war, and on 29 October 1665 Portuguese forces killed the Manikongo António I at Mbwila and struck off his head. Kongo then split between the Kinlaza and Kimpanzu houses; São Salvador was sacked in 1678 and its people were carried off to the slave ports. When the crown was restored in the early eighteenth century, Songo remained largely with its own chiefs and merchant clans.
zh:
松戈是奥坎加（Okanga）以东林莽与稀树草原交错的地带，葡萄牙记载常把奥坎加写作Okanga。这里的居民说刚果语，在河谷间耕作，织出的棕榈纤维布沿商路西行，送往姆班扎刚果的市场。老人们还记得一个松散的故地，葡萄牙人称之为「刚果迪亚恩拉扎七王国」，又叫莫姆博阿雷斯，其地从夸莱河延伸到宽果河，后来通过东境省份姆巴塔被纳入刚果；姆巴塔的领主还保有「刚果国王的祖父」这一尊号。1444年的松戈处在刚果控制松散的东缘：村社首领向更强大的统治者纳贡、从征，但神龛、村落议事和织机仍在本地人手里。

迪奥戈·康1483年抵达海岸、马尼刚果1491年受洗后，姆班扎刚果的宫廷皈依了天主教，但这么深的内陆并未因新信仰改变多少。松戈与大西洋真正的联系是布匹：1575年葡萄牙人建立罗安达后，财政官佩罗·萨尔迪尼亚报告，1611和1612年平均每年有四万五千匹松戈布运抵该城。1568年的贾加袭掠开启了长年边患；1665年10月29日，葡萄牙军队在姆布维拉击杀马尼刚果安东尼奥一世，并割下他的首级。刚果随后分裂为金拉扎与金潘祖两派，圣萨尔瓦多1678年遭洗劫，城中人口被掳往奴隶港。18世纪初王权恢复时，松戈大半仍在本地酋长和商业氏族手中。

en:
Kasanje is the Baixa de Cassanje, the wooded savanna between the Kwanza and the upper Kwango. In 1444 its Mbundu villages knew nothing of Europeans: Luanda did not exist, no Portuguese trader had yet crossed the Kwanza, and the kingdom that gives the province its name was unborn. Its founders were an Imbangala war band, one of the mercenary companies that came out of the south early in the seventeenth century and hired their spears to the governors of Luanda. The English sailor Andrew Battell lived among such a band for sixteen months around 1600 and left the first written account of them. Their armed camp, the kilombo, had twelve gates for twelve fighting squadrons; a boy wore an iron collar until he had killed his man; children born in the camp were put to death and the ranks filled with captured teenagers. They sacrificed captives before battle and ate the flesh of enemies and of cowards, and their war clubs and their reputation for eating human flesh made them the most feared allies in Angola.

In 1618 the band led by a warlord named Kasanje marched with the Portuguese when they sacked Ndongo's capital, then slipped away and pillaged on through Matamba until about 1620, when it settled its followers on the upper Kwango. The new state kept his name; its elected king, the kinguri, was chosen from the three founding clans. Wars against Queen Njinga's Matamba, above all in 1634 and 1635, and against a string of smaller neighbours widened its borders, and by the 1650s six languages were spoken within them. Portuguese merchants had followed the armies, and the Feira de Cassange became the furthest inland market on the Luanda road, the end of the pombeiro caravan route, where slaves and ivory from the Lunda country changed hands for cloth, beads and firearms. In 1689 the chronicler Cadornega put its population at 300,000, 100,000 of them able to bear arms, figures perhaps inflated but a measure of the kingdom's scale. Slave caravans kept the kinguri and the feira rich for another century, until Ovimbundu routes from Benguela began to draw the trade south.
zh:
卡桑吉地处宽扎河与宽果河上游之间的林木稀树草原卡桑热低地。1444年，这里的姆本杜村落对欧洲人一无所知：罗安达尚不存在，没有葡萄牙商人越过宽扎河，日后赋予本省名字的王国也还没有建立。它的建立者是一支因班加拉战团，即十七世纪初从南方涌来、把武力雇给罗安达总督的雇佣武装之一。约1600年，英国水手安德鲁·巴特尔随这样一支战团生活了十六个月，留下了最早的文字记录。他们的武装营寨称基隆博，开十二座门，对应十二个战斗纵队；男孩颈戴铁环，直到阵前杀过一人才可摘下；营中生下的婴儿一律处死，兵源靠掳来的少年补充。他们战前杀俘献祭，分食敌人和懦夫的肉；凭着战棍和食人的名声，因班加拉人成了安哥拉最令人胆寒的盟友。

1618年，首领卡桑吉率战团随葡萄牙人洗劫恩东戈王都，随后脱离葡方，一路劫掠马坦巴，约1620年在宽果河上游安顿部众。新国家沿用了他的名字；国君称金古里，由三个开国氏族中选出。与恩津加女王的马坦巴交战，以1634至1635年最为激烈，又不断征伐周边小邦，到1650年代境内已通行六种语言。葡萄牙商人随军而来，卡桑吉集市成为罗安达商道最深入内陆的市场，也是庞贝罗商队路线的终点：隆达地方贩来的奴隶和象牙在此换取布匹、珠子和火器。1689年，编年史家卡多内加估计其人口有三十万，其中十万可执兵器，数字或有夸张，却也可见王国的规模。此后一个世纪，奴隶商队供养着金古里的王权与这座集市，直到本格拉方向的奥文本杜商路把生意逐渐引向南方。

en:
The Shinje are a Lunda-related people of the rolling savanna and gallery forests east of the upper Kwango. Yaka farmers lay to their north, Ruund villages around the Kalanyi to the east and Lwena country to the south. In 1444 headmen still governed their own millet fields, fishing camps and oil-palm groves; the state later Portuguese sources called Kasanje did not yet exist. Footpaths already carried ivory, salt and captives between the Kwango and Kasai basins, but no paramount ruled the frontier.

That trade drew in the Mbangala, mercenary war bands hardened in the Angolan wars who lived in palisaded camps and replenished their ranks by initiating captured boys rather than raising children. In 1620 one such band, led by Kasanje, broke from Portuguese service, settled the upper Kwango and founded the kingdom that took his name, its elected king bearing the title kinguri. Portuguese merchants followed, and the western approaches to Shinje became a slave market feeding Luanda and Brazil; in the 1650s Kasanje's wars reached Matamba, then ruled by Queen Njinga. During the same century Lunda power expanded from Musumba, and Lunda caravans tied Shinje into the Atlantic traffic in ivory and captives. Rivalry for tribute between the kinguri at Kasanje and the Mwata Yamvo kept the country a contested borderland through the eighteenth century.
zh:
欣杰人与隆达人有亲缘，住在宽果河上游以东起伏的稀树草原和廊林之间，北面是雅卡农人，东面是卡兰伊河一带的鲁恩德村社，南面是卢埃纳人的乡土。1444年，各村首领仍各自管理粟田、渔场和油棕林；后世葡萄牙资料所载的卡桑吉国家这时还不存在。小路已把象牙、盐和俘虏贩运于宽果河与开赛河流域之间，但这片边疆还没有共主。

这门生意把姆班加拉人引来：他们是在安哥拉战争中打磨出来的雇佣兵战团，住在木栅围起的营寨里，不靠生育、而靠为掳来的男孩行入会礼补充兵员。1620年，卡桑吉率领一支这样的队伍脱离葡萄牙军役，在宽果河上游定居，建立以他为名的王国，国王称「金古里」，由推举产生。葡萄牙商人接踵而至，欣杰西侧的通道成了向罗安达和巴西供货的奴隶市集；17世纪50年代，卡桑吉的兵锋抵达马坦巴，同恩津加女王治下的国家交战。同一世纪，隆达势力从穆松巴扩张而来，隆达商队把欣杰系进大西洋的象牙与俘虏贸易。整个18世纪，卡桑吉的金古里与姆瓦塔·扬沃为贡赋相争，欣杰始终是二者之间拉锯的边疆。

en:
Malem is the narrow belt of woodland and plateau between the Ndongo highlands and the Baixa de Cassanje, where the paths climbing from the Kwanza valley turn east toward the Kwango. In 1444 its Mbundu villages answered to local headmen, the sobas, within the loose lordship of the ngola of Ndongo, and nothing European had reached them; Portuguese raiders were still more than a century from the Kwanza.

Passing armies and trade gave the corridor its later history. Kasanje's Imbangala band came through it after helping to sack Ndongo in 1618, on the way to settle the upper Kwango around 1620, and once that kingdom took root the track became its western road and, in time, the caravan route between the Portuguese fortified country around Ambaca and the Feira de Cassange. The pombeiros, African agents buying for Luanda merchants, led long columns of porters along it; an expedition might be a year on the march and bring back four or five hundred slaves. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries its villages lived by feeding and housing those columns, or by taking to the bush when a raiding party passed.
zh:
马勒姆是恩东戈高地与卡桑热低地之间一条林木覆盖的高原狭地，从宽扎河谷攀来的道路在此折向东去宽果河。1444年，这里的姆本杜村落由本地索巴统辖，处在恩东戈恩戈拉松散的势力圈内，欧洲事物尚未传来，葡萄牙掠奴队进入宽扎河流域还要等一个多世纪。

后来的历史是过路军队和商队带来的。卡桑吉的因班加拉战团1618年参与洗劫恩东戈之后穿过这一带，约1620年去宽果河上游定居立国；这个国家扎下根后，这条小路成为它的西部门户，久而久之又成为安巴卡一带的葡属要塞区与卡桑吉集市之间的商队大道。庞贝罗是替罗安达商人深入内地收货的非洲代理人，他们率领长长的脚夫队伍走这条路，跑一趟可能要一年，带回四五百名奴隶。整个十七、十八世纪，沿途村落或靠供应和留宿这些队伍为生，或在掳掠队伍经过时逃入丛林。

en:
Yaka is the middle Kwango country between the Kwango and Wamba rivers, a belt of forest and savanna cut by fishing streams and hunting grounds. In 1444 its villages were run by local chiefs and clan elders under matrilineal rules of kinship and inheritance; farmers cleared the upland soils and hunters took game with dogs. The carvers' work was known across the region: heavy masks with upturned noses and globular eyes, mbwoolo figures and the mukoku, a hollowed slit drum beaten for dances that dealt with the ancestors. Mbanza-Kongo claimed no direct rule here, and the Bakongo used 'Yaka' as the name for their own frontier warriors.

In 1568 armed bands out of the east, whom the Portuguese lumped together as Jaga although they came from several peoples, overran Mbata and drove the Manikongo Álvaro I out of Mbanza-Kongo to an island in the Congo River. About 600 Portuguese matchlockmen from São Tomé under Francisco de Gouveia Sottomaior restored him to the throne, and the raiders were pushed back beyond the borders by the mid-1570s; the price of the rescue was Portuguese leave to found Luanda. During the seventeenth century Lunda lineages moving west under King Kabamba married local Kongo women, took to Kiyaka speech and merged with the older clans into the Yaka kingdom. Yaka companies later hired out as soldiers in Kongo's dynastic wars while captives from the frontier were sold toward the Atlantic, and after the civil war of 1665–1709 the restored Manikongo held little more than a loose claim on this armed border.
zh:
雅卡位于宽果河与万巴河之间的宽果河中游，林莽、稀树草原、渔场和猎场交错成一条带状地带。1444年，村落由地方酋长和氏族长老按母系亲属与继承规则掌管；农人开垦高地，猎人带着猎犬围猎。工匠的雕刻在这一带有名：翻鼻、圆球状眼睛的厚重面具，称姆沃洛的人像，还有叫穆科科的镂空缝鼓，用于祭祀祖先的舞蹈。姆班扎刚果对这里没有直接管辖权，而巴刚果人本来就用「雅卡」称呼他们的边地战士。

1568年，来自东部的武装群体冲垮姆巴塔，把马尼刚果阿尔瓦罗一世赶出姆班扎刚果，逼到刚果河中的一座岛上避难；这些人分属好几个族群，葡萄牙人却笼统称为贾加。约六百名来自圣多美的葡萄牙火枪手在弗朗西斯科·德戈韦亚·索托马约尔率领下帮助他复位，到1570年代中期，入侵者被逐出国境，而求援的代价是允许葡萄牙人建立罗安达。17世纪，在卡班巴王率领下西迁的隆达谱系首领与本地刚果氏族通婚，改用基亚卡语，与旧有诸族融合成雅卡王国。后来的刚果王朝战争常雇雅卡队伍当兵，边境上的战俘则被卖向大西洋；1665至1709年内战之后，复位的马尼刚果对这条武装边地只维持着松散的统属。

en:
Nunu is the watery forest below Lake Mai-Ndombe, where the Kasai meets the Fimi and the channels of the Lukenie, Kwilu and Wamba spread into a country of floodwater and canoe-landings, with Mushie as its river crossing. Its BaNunu people farmed the banks, fished the flooded channels and built the long canoes that carried war parties, toll-goods and fine cloth from one market village to the next. Oral king lists put the making of their river polity, Mwene Muji, just after 1400, under rulers titled ntote. In 1444 it was a young power of the Lower Kasai, which held its rivers by fleets of war canoes and market dues rather than garrisons; by its own account, the Jaga bands that fell on the kingdom of Kongo in the sixteenth century had set out from one of its provinces.

Europeans learned the name in 1591 from Filippo Pigafetta's book on Kongo, which located 'Monemugi' so vaguely that mapmakers set it far to the east, filling blank ground between Congo and Abyssinia. Mwene Muji's unity did not outlast that century: Boma, Yaka and Bozanga broke away in the early 1600s, and around 1625 Shyaam a-Mbul united the Kuba chiefdoms to the southeast into the Bushoong-led Kuba federation, whose power grew along the Kasai through the eighteenth century. Nunu stayed a world of fishermen and canoe-men. Its villages paid allegiance to whichever power commanded the water and kept their older rites under the rival claims of Mwene Muji and Kuba.
zh:
努努是迈恩东贝湖以下的水网森林，开赛河在此与菲米河相会，卢凯尼河、奎卢河和万巴河的河汊把这一带变成一片泛水与舟埠交织之地，穆希是其中的渡口。巴努努人在河岸耕作，在泛水河道捕鱼，建造修长的独木舟，把战队、税货和精细布匹从一个集市村落送到下一个。口传王表把他们的水上政权姆韦内·穆吉的形成系于1400年后不久，君主称恩托特。1444年，它是下开赛的年轻强权，靠一队队战舟和集市税赋而非驻军控制诸河；按它自己的说法，十六世纪杀向刚果王国的贾加战团就是从它的一个省份出发的。

欧洲人知道这个名字，是1591年从菲利波·皮加费塔记述刚果的书里；他把「莫内穆吉」的位置写得太含糊，制图师便把它放到遥远的东方，去填补刚果与阿比西尼亚之间的空白。姆韦内·穆吉的统一没能维持过那个世纪：十七世纪初，博马、雅卡和博赞加相继分立；约1625年，希亚姆·阿-姆布尔把东南方的库巴诸酋长国联合成布雄人主导的库巴联邦，其势力在十八世纪沿开赛河壮大。努努始终是渔夫和舟师的世界，哪一方的水上强权发号施令，村落便向哪一方臣服，在姆韦内·穆吉与库巴的争夺之间守着更古老的仪式。

en:
Kumbana lies between the Lutshiko and Loange rivers, southeast of the later town of Kikwit, in a broken country of forest, savanna, fishing waters and Bantu village fields. It takes its name from the title Mwata Kumbana, but in 1444 that office did not exist; no paramount ruled the land, and river tracks were the only roads, pointing toward the Kwilu, Kwango and Kasai. Pende groups had not yet entered the region, and Musumba's Lunda were still far to the southeast.

About 1650 Mukelenge Mutombo, a Lunda leader out of Musumba, settled his followers at the confluence of the Loange and Lutshiko, dislodged Pende groups then moving into the country and founded a chiefdom under the title Mwatha Kombana, 'one who gives generously'; positional succession made the title outlive its first holder. His Shakatwala clansmen continued westward to Mwe Nzila. The rise of the Yaka state under Mwene Putu Kasongo then turned Kombana from an offshoot of Musumba into a halt on a long caravan road. Slaves and ivory moved from the interior through the kiamfu's capital to the Portuguese at Ambriz on the Atlantic. Kombana's Lunda elite ran that trade while adopting the Gipende language and customs, and still held their authority as delegates of the Mwata Yamvo.
zh:
库巴纳位于卢奇科河与洛安盖河之间、后来基奎特城的东南方向，林莽与稀树草原交错，渔场和班图人的村社田地散落其间。地名得自姆瓦塔·库巴纳头衔，但1444年这个职位还不存在；这里没有高居各村之上的统治者，唯一的通路是河畔小径，通往奎卢河、宽果河和开赛河方向。巴彭德人此时尚未迁入，穆松巴的隆达人也还远在东南。

约1650年，来自穆松巴的隆达首领穆凯伦盖·穆通博率部在洛安盖河与卢奇科河汇流处定居，逐走当时正迁入此地的巴彭德人群，建立酋长国，采用姆瓦塔·孔巴纳头衔，意为「慷慨施予者」；凭借职位继承制，这个头衔在首任统治者身后延续下来。他的沙卡特瓦拉族人继续向西，抵达姆韦·恩齐拉。姆韦内·普图·卡松戈的雅卡国家兴起后，孔巴纳从穆松巴的分支变成一条漫长商路上的歇脚点，奴隶和象牙从内地经基阿姆富的都城，运往大西洋口岸安布里什的葡萄牙商人手中。孔巴纳的隆达上层改习吉彭德语和风俗、经营这门贸易，同时仍承认自己的权力受自姆瓦塔·扬沃。

en:
Munene covers the river corridor above the meeting of the Kasai and the Tshikapa, where falls and rapids forced canoe traffic to unload and cross the bank; the portages made meeting places long before any chiefs ruled here. In 1444 Tufia, Tupokoto, Kete and Bashilange villagers farmed the savanna edge, fished both rivers and hunted the gallery forest, and village heads and custodians of the land kept order at the crossings. The Lunda-founded chiefdom remembered as Mai Munene still lay in the future, and so did the Kuba federation.

The Lunda reach came after 1700, in the same long expansion that had earlier sent the founders of Kasanje and Shinje out from the court at Musumba. A commander named Mujinga was beaten by the Tufia, so the court sent Mai Munene with another lieutenant, Kombana Mutombo, to finish the campaign. Mai subdued the Tufia and brought some Tupokoto, Kete and Bashilange communities under his rule; his war against the Pende failed completely when their chief Kombo destroyed his forces; Kombo's bravery in the fight made his name among the Pende, who kept their autonomy. Mai set his seat beside the great falls of the Kasai, and the portage market there drew caravans from the Kwango, which bartered captives and forest produce for cloth and beads carried up from Angolan markets. Kombana crossed the Loange and founded Mwaka Kumbana on the other bank. The court later felt strong Luba influence, but in 1821 Mai Munene remained an interior river market under its own chiefs, with no European post above the falls.
zh:
穆内内是开赛河与奇卡帕河汇流处上游的河运走廊，瀑布和急流迫使独木舟在此卸货，行人货物上岸转运；早在首领立国之前，这些转运点就已是各方会聚之处。1444年，图菲亚、图波科托、克特和巴希兰格人的村社在稀树草原边缘耕作，在两条河里捕鱼，在走廊森林狩猎，各村首领和守护土地的长老维持着渡口的秩序。隆达人建立的迈伊穆内内酋长国尚在未来，库巴联邦也是一样。
