基希后来改称沙赫里萨布兹，坐落在撒马尔罕以南约80公里的卡什卡河谷。以粟特的标准看，它也算得上古城，学界多认为古城那乌塔卡就在此处；公元前328至前327年，亚历山大在此过冬，并结识了罗克珊娜。阿拉伯征服后，卡什卡河谷成为一场反阿拉伯起义的中心，首领是阿拉伯语所称的「蒙面者」，他的追随者「白衣人」在8世纪与哈里发的军队长年作战。基希周围的牧场后来归巴鲁剌思部所有，1336年帖木儿出生在城外的霍贾伊尔加尔。他虽以撒马尔罕为都，却把大量钱财花在出生地：1380年，从被征服的花剌子模掳来的工匠开始营建阿克萨赖宫，即「白宫」，规格要压过他所建的一切；两座门塔高65米，入口上方刻着铭文：「若要质疑我们的力量，就看看我们的建筑。」1437年，乌鲁伯格为纪念父亲沙哈鲁，建起蓝顶的库克贡巴兹聚礼清真寺。1444年，基希仍在帖木儿王朝境内，由撒马尔罕方面统辖。

清真寺附近是多尔·萨阿达特建筑群，里面葬着帖木儿的长子贾汉吉尔，旁边一座清真寺相传葬有这个家族的导师、伊玛目阿米尔·库拉尔。帖木儿本人1405年死后，被送往撒马尔罕安葬。1556年，布哈拉的阿卜杜拉汗二世攻下基希，把它并入新设的卡尔希省。18世纪中叶，乌兹别克克纳加斯部把这一地区经营成半独立的伯克领地；1785年曼吉特王朝取得布哈拉，但沙赫里萨布兹和基塔布的山地首领据守城寨，在汗国内保住了很大自治权。

en:
Saidabad, the later name of Sirjan, lies on a high plain west of Kerman, on the Kerman-Shiraz road where tracks branch south toward the Persian Gulf. Under the Abbasid caliphs Sirjan shared the status of capital of Kerman with the city of Kerman, and medieval geographers praised it highly: Ibn Hawqal and al-Muqaddasi called it the greatest city of the province, wider than Shiraz, with eight gates, two bazaars and tall walls, and a congregational mosque whose minaret was fitted by Adud al-Dawla with a curious wooden mechanism that partly turned. Its water ran from two qanats dug by Amr and Tahir, sons of Layth al-Saffar, and sugarcane, fruit and wealthy houses filled the town. The last Sasanian king, Yazdgerd III, lodged in its palace while fleeing the Arab conquest in the 640s. Nearby Sang Castle went back to Sasanian times, and an inscription there dated 1387 names the Muzaffarid ruler Imad al-Din Ahmad. In 1444 the district was a Persian-speaking Timurid frontier land, its flocks, wool and caravans linking the Kerman plateau with Fars and the Gulf.

The medieval town later shifted its site three times. Under the Qajars the settlement at Saidabad became the nucleus of the city of Sirjan, and a new bazaar served the caravan trade that returned to the old road.
zh:
赛伊达巴德是锡尔詹后来的名字，位于克尔曼以西的高原，地处克尔曼通往设拉子的大道，另有小路南通波斯湾。阿拔斯哈里发时期，锡尔甘与克尔曼城同为克尔曼地区的首府。中世纪地理学家对它称赞有加：伊本·豪盖勒和穆卡达西称它是全省最大的城市，比设拉子还开阔，有八座城门、两座巴扎和高耸的城墙；聚礼清真寺的宣礼塔上，阿杜德·道莱装了精巧的木制机关，有一部分能够转动。城里的水来自两条坎儿井，是萨法尔人莱伊斯的两个儿子阿慕尔和塔希尔开凿的；蔗糖、水果和富商宅邸充满城中。末代萨珊国王伊嗣俟三世在640年代躲避阿拉伯人时，曾在城中的宫殿落脚。附近的石堡始于萨珊时期，堡中一方1387年的铭文提到穆扎法尔王朝的伊马德丁·艾哈迈德。1444年，这片地区是帖木儿王朝治下说波斯语的边疆，羊群、羊毛和商队把克尔曼高原同法尔斯和波斯湾连在一起。

这座中世纪城市后来三次迁址。卡扎尔时期，赛伊达巴德的定居点成为锡尔詹城的核心，一座新巴扎为重回老路的商旅服务。

en:
Ifugao is the steepest country of the Cordillera, where rivers cut south through folded mountains toward the Magat and lowlanders seldom went. Its people call themselves the people of the hill, and in 1444 they farmed the slopes around villages such as Kiyyangan, growing taro, trading gold and beeswax down to the plains, and following wealthy kadangyan clans rather than kings. They set carved wooden bulol guardians in their granaries and chanted the hudhud epics at their feasts. No outside power had entered these mountains, and the Ifugao answered to no state.

The Spaniards who overran the coasts of Luzon found the Cordillera a harder country. Expeditions pushed up the Magat valley between 1591 and 1594 and brought back the first Spanish accounts of the Ygolote highlanders, and the loss of the lowlands drove the Ifugao deeper into the range. Between 1600 and 1700 they gave up taro for wet rice and carved the great terraced mountainsides, field walls climbing ridge after ridge, the largest earthworks in the Cordillera; the new fields fed a growing population and bound the villages together against the lowland government. Punitive columns in the 1770s and 1790s tried to force highlanders into reduccion settlements while forts watched the Magat below, but in 1821 the terraces and the villages that built them remained outside Spanish control.
zh:
伊富高是中科迪勒拉山最险峻的地方，河谷向南穿过层叠群山通向马加特河，低地人很少进去。他们自称「山上之民」。1444年，伊富高人在基扬甘等村落周围的坡地上种植芋薯，把黄金和蜂蜡运下平原交易；他们没有国王，由富有的卡丹阳氏族统领，谷仓里供着木雕的布洛尔守护神，宴会上传唱胡德胡德史诗。还没有外来政权进入这些大山，伊富高人不属于任何国家。

征服吕宋海岸的西班牙人发现，中科迪勒拉是一块更难啃的土地。1591至1594年，远征队沿马加特河谷上行，首次留下西班牙人对「伊戈洛特」山民的记载；低地失陷，把伊富高人更深地赶入群山。1600至1700年间，他们弃芋种稻，在山坡上凿出大片梯田，田埂顺着一道道山脊层层攀高，是中科迪勒拉规模最大的土方工程；新稻田养活了增长的人口，也把各村凝聚起来，对抗低地的殖民政权。1770和1790年代，西班牙又派出讨伐队，企图把山民强行迁入归并村，并在下游马加特河畔筑堡监视，但直到1821年，这些梯田和修筑它们的村落仍不在西班牙人治下。

en:
Laguna de Bay is the great freshwater lake southeast of Manila Bay, and its southern shore was Tagalog rice country. Boats carried the harvest across the lake and down the Pasig River to the markets of Tondo, and barangays such as Bay, Pila and Lumban fed the chiefs of Tondo and Maynila. The oldest document in the Philippines, the Laguna Copperplate of 900, was written here: it acquits a debtor before Jayadewa, Lord of Pailah, the place now called Pila. Later tradition makes Bay and its neighbours the domain of a chief named Gat Pangil. In 1444 the lakeside datus stood within the orbit of the lakan of Tondo.

Juan de Salcedo overran the district in 1571 with a hundred Spanish-Mexican soldiers, and Martín de Goiti received about 8,000 tribute-payers there, one of the largest encomiendas of the early conquest. The Franciscan Juan de Plasencia arrived in 1578, laid out Bay, Majayjay, Pila and Lumban as parish towns, baptised their people and wrote the Doctrina Cristiana, the first book printed in the Philippines. Twice the lakeside hills sheltered Chinese rebels from Manila: fugitives of the 1603 Sangley rising were run to ground in the San Pablo highlands, and in 1639 another band fortified the ridges above Cavinti and Lumban before surrendering at Pagsanjan the next year. Bay remained the provincial capital until 1688, when the seat moved to Pagsanjan. During the British occupation of Manila, Captain Thomas Backhouse's men sacked Pagsanjan hunting for the silver cargo of the galleon Filipina, but Francisco de San Juan carried the hoard through to Simón de Anda in Pampanga.
zh:
内湖湾是马尼拉湾东南的大淡水湖，湖南岸是他加禄人的稻米之乡。米船穿过湖面、沿巴石河下行，把收成运往汤都的市场，巴彦、皮拉、隆班等巴朗盖供养着汤都和马尼拉的首领。菲律宾最古的文献、900年的拉古纳铜版铭文就出自此地：铭文记载一名债务人在帕伊拉（今皮拉）领主阇耶提婆面前免除债务。后世传说把巴彦一带归在首领加特·邦吉尔名下。1444年，湖岸诸达图都处在汤都拉干的势力圈内。

1571年，胡安·德·萨尔塞多率一百名西属墨西哥士兵征服此地，马丁·德·戈伊蒂受封约八千名纳贡者，是征服初期最大的监护征赋区之一。方济各会士胡安·德·普拉森西亚1578年来此，把巴彦、马海海、皮拉、隆班建成堂区城镇，为居民施洗，并写成菲律宾最早付印的书籍《基督教义》。湖岸山地两次收容从马尼拉逃出的华人起事者：1603年「生理人」起事的残部被追剿至圣巴勃罗山区；1639年另一支队伍据守卡文蒂和隆班上方的山脊，次年在百胜滩投降。巴彦作为府治直到1688年，之后府治迁往百胜滩。英军占领马尼拉期间，托马斯·巴克豪斯上尉的部队洗劫百胜滩，搜求大帆船「菲律宾人号」上的白银，弗朗西斯科·德·圣胡安却把这批财宝送到了邦板牙的西蒙·德·安达手中。

en:
Mindoro faces Luzon across a narrow sea, and Chinese records knew it as Ma-i or Mait. The Song annals name it in 972, and Zhao Rugua's Zhu Fan Zhi of 1225 describes its trade in detail. When a junk entered the anchorage it registered at the official plaza and gave the local chiefs white parasols as gifts; island traders then carried the porcelain, iron pots and coloured beads away to other islands and came back in September or October with beeswax, cotton, pearls and tortoiseshell, and the Chinese author says none ever broke their bargain. The same account speaks of bronze Buddha images among the islanders. Mangyan clans farmed the interior, while the southern anchorages of Mangarin and Caminawit drew junks and Malay prahus. In 1444 Muslim settlers tied to Brunei and Maynila held stretches of the coast, Lubang to the north paid tribute to Rajah Sulayman, and the Mangyan kept to the highlands.

Spaniards first explored Mindoro in 1570 and found enough gold to call it Mina de Oro, 'gold mine', a name later compressed into Mindoro. In 1572 Juan de Salcedo sailed its west coast and burned the Muslim village on Lubang. The coastal villages were granted as encomiendas, but war and the slave trade emptied much of the island, and refugees crossed to Batangas. In 1602 Moro fleets sacked the Spanish towns and built a fort at Mamburao. Iranun raiders returned in force in 1757 with 74 prahus and carried islanders off to the slave market of Jolo, until a Spanish expedition of 1,200 men destroyed the Mamburao fort in 1766. Caminawit later became the seat of the southern presidencia.
zh:
民都洛与吕宋隔海相望，在中国载籍中称麻逸。《宋史》在972年已记其国，1225年赵汝适的《诸蕃志》更详述了它的贸易情形：中国帆船驶入锚地后，先在官市前登记，向当地首领赠送白伞；岛上商人随即把瓷器、铁锅和彩珠携往其他岛屿，到九、十月间带着蜂蜡、棉布、珍珠和玳瑁回来，书中说他们从不爽约。同书还提到岛民家中有铜佛像。芒扬人诸部在内地农耕，南部的曼加林、卡米纳维特锚地吸引着中国帆船和马来快船。1444年，与文莱和马尼拉有联系的穆斯林居民已占据沿海多处，北方的卢邦岛向拉惹·苏莱曼纳贡，芒扬人退居山地。

1570年西班牙人首次探查民都洛，因发现黄金而称之为「金矿」（Mina de Oro），后缩读为民都洛。1572年胡安·德·萨尔塞多沿西岸航行，焚毁卢邦岛上的穆斯林聚落。沿岸村落被封作监护征赋区，但战乱和奴隶贸易使岛上大半人口流失，难民渡海逃往八打雁。1602年，摩洛舰队洗劫西班牙人城镇，并在曼布劳修筑堡垒。1757年伊拉农人集结七十四艘快船大举重来，把岛民掳往霍洛的奴隶市场；1766年一支一千二百人的西班牙远征军摧毁了曼布劳堡垒。卡米纳维特后来成为南部行政长官的驻所。

en:
Buglas was the old Hiligaynon name of Negros, a long island lying across the Tañon Strait from Cebu; the word was understood to mean 'cut off', as though the island had once broken from a larger land. Dark-skinned Ata foragers of the Negrito peoples ranged its interior mountains, while Visayan villages lined the coasts. The shore settlement that became Silay was called Carobcob, 'to scratch', for the way its people raked tuway clams out of the sand at low tide. The western coast stood under the nominal sway of the Kedatuan of Madja-as in Panay, and the east looked to the rajahs of Cebu. Local legend tells of Princess Kansilay, who led her village against pirate raiders sword in hand and was killed in the fight; a kansilay tree grew from her grave and gave the later town its name. In 1444 the islanders sailed the Visayan seas in large outrigger boats and kept their old Visayan rites.

Legazpi's men reached the island in April 1565 and, seeing the Ata, named it Negros. Carobcob was granted as an encomienda in 1571 to Cristobal Nuñez Paroja, one of the seventeen soldiers who had come with Legazpi. Moro slave-raiders harried the coasts from the late 1500s, and the Spanish commander on the island answered with flight rather than resistance: in 1760 the people of Silay left their shore village and rebuilt it behind a palisade between the Matagoy and Panaogao rivers, at the place later called Estaca after the stockade. Negros was governed from Oton in Panay until 1734, when it became a military district with its capital at Ilog, later moved to Himamaylan. By 1818 the island counted about 200 Spanish-Filipino families, and Silay alone was a town of more than 200 houses.
zh:
布格拉斯是米沙鄢语对内格罗斯岛的旧称。这座长形大岛与宿务隔着塔尼翁海峡相望，旧名意为「割断」，仿佛它曾从一块更大的陆地断裂开来。肤色黝黑的阿塔人属于尼格利陀族群，在中部山地游猎，米沙鄢人的渔村则沿海岸散布。日后发展为锡莱的滨海聚落原名卡罗布科布，意为「刨挖」，得名于居民趁退潮在沙滩上刨挖蛤蜊的生计。西岸名义上臣属班乃岛的马加斯，东岸则受宿务诸位拉惹影响。当地相传，坎西莱公主曾持剑率领村民抵御海盗，战死之后坟头长出一棵坎西莱树，后来的城镇便以此为名。1444年，岛民驾着大型舷外支架船往来于米沙鄢诸海，奉行米沙鄢旧俗。

1565年4月，莱加斯皮的部下抵达此岛，因见到阿塔人而称之为内格罗斯。1571年，卡罗布科布被封作监护征赋区，受封者是随莱加斯皮远征的十七名士兵之一。16世纪末叶起，摩洛掳奴船队不断袭扰海岸，岛上的西班牙长官采取先躲避、不抵抗的方针：1760年锡莱居民离开海边旧村，在马塔戈伊河与帕纳奥高河之间树起木栅、另建新村，那一带也因这座栅寨得名埃斯塔卡。内格罗斯长期由班乃的奥通管辖，1734年成为军区，以伊洛格为首府，后来迁往希马马兰。到1818年，全岛约有二百个西班牙—菲裔家庭，仅锡莱一镇便有二百余栋房屋。

en:
Cebu, called Sugbu by its Visayan people, is a narrow island in the central Philippines, its east-coast harbour looking across the strait toward Bohol. The Zhufan Zhi of 1225 may describe the island as Suwu, a sea country whose beeswax, tortoiseshell, cotton, agarwood and sea produce drew Chinese porcelain, silk, salt, rice and trade gold. By the 15th century the harbour was a line of coastal houses around the rajah's palace and an open square at Singhapala. Its rulers used Sanskrit titles, and Visayan oral legend traces the dynasty to Sri Lumay, a half-Tamil, half-Malay prince from Sumatra. In 1444 Cebu was an Indianized rajahnate whose chiefs lived by the port traffic and had to defend it against raiders from Mindanao.

Ferdinand Magellan's ships entered Sugbu on 7 April 1521. Rajah Humabon welcomed the Spaniards and was baptized, but Magellan was killed on 27 April while fighting Lapulapu on Mactan, and the surviving fleet sailed away. Miguel Lopez de Legazpi returned on 27 April 1565, scattered Visayan boats with cannon and forced Rajah Tupas to terms. The wooden work begun on 8 May became Fort San Pedro, the core of the first permanent Spanish settlement in the Philippines. In a burned house a Spanish soldier found the Sto. Nino image given to Humabon's queen in 1521, and a church was later raised on the spot. Legazpi moved the colonial government to Manila in 1571, yet Cebu stayed the main Spanish town in the Visayas, with its own Chinese Parian and diocese. Raids from the Muslim south led the garrison to replace the wooden fort with stone; its gate bears the date 1738.
zh:
宿务，米沙鄢人称作苏格布，是菲律宾中部一座狭长岛屿，东岸港湾隔着海峡面向保和。1225年《诸蕃志》记载的束务国可能就是这里；岛上输出蜂蜡、玳瑁、棉布、沉香和海产，引来中国瓷器、丝绸、盐、米和贸易用黄金。到15世纪，港湾沿岸屋舍连绵，拉者宫殿和广场所在的辛格帕拉是统治中心。统治者使用梵语头衔，米沙鄢口述传说把王朝追溯为来自苏门答腊的半泰米尔、半马来王子斯里·卢迈的后裔。1444年的宿务是一个印度化拉让国，首领们依靠港市贸易为生，也要防备棉兰老来的袭掠者。

1521年4月7日，麦哲伦的船队驶入苏格布。拉者·胡玛邦欢迎西班牙人并接受洗礼，但麦哲伦在4月27日进攻马克坦岛时被拉普拉普所杀，幸存船队随后离去。1565年4月27日，米格尔·洛佩斯·德·莱加斯皮重返此地，用火炮驱散米沙鄢战船，并迫使拉者·图帕斯议和。5月8日动工的木构工事后来成为圣佩德罗堡，也是菲律宾第一个永久西班牙人定居点的核心。一名西班牙士兵在焚毁的屋舍中发现了1521年麦哲伦赠给胡玛邦王后的圣婴像，后来人们在发现地建起教堂。1571年莱加斯皮把殖民政府迁往马尼拉，但宿务仍是西班牙人在米沙鄢的首要城镇，拥有华人涧内和主教区。为防备南方穆斯林袭掠，守军把木堡改建为石堡；堡门所刻年份为1738年。

en:
Leyte lies between Samar and Mindanao, its eastern shore opening on Leyte Gulf and its western valleys shelving to the Camotes Sea. The Spaniards who came in the 1500s heard the island called Tandaya, after one of its lords; Warays lived in the east and other Visayan peoples in the west, in datu settlements such as Carigara and Mairete, the latter once ruled by Datu Ete. They farmed rice and millet on the coastal flats, fished and built boats in the sheltered gulfs, and shared the anito rites of the rest of the Visayas. In 1444 Leyte had no kingdom and no foreign flag, only rival datus, their balangay crews, and the island traffic south to Mindanao and north to Luzon.

Magellan's fleet reached little Limasawa, off Leyte's south coast, on 28 March 1521. Two rulers were there hunting with their balangays, Rajah Kolambu of Butuan and Rajah Siaui, and they feasted the crew for several days. On Easter Sunday, 31 March, Father Valderrama said the first mass in the islands at Mazaua, and Magellan had a cross raised on the island's highest hill before Kolambu piloted the ships on to Cebu. In 1543 Ruy Lopez de Villalobos gave Leyte and Samar the name Las Islas Filipinas, in honour of the prince who became Philip II. The datu Bankaw welcomed Legazpi at Carigara in 1565 with a blood pact and baptism, but in 1621 the old convert turned back to the old gods and, with his son Pagali, a babaylan priest, raised a diwata temple and six towns in revolt. Juan de Alcarazo sailed from Cebu with forty ships, burned the temple and crushed the rising in 1622, setting Bankaw's head on a stake. Jesuits had opened a mission at Carigara in 1595, and Palo, Ormoc and Alangalang followed, yet Spanish rule stayed light: Leyte and Samar became a single province in 1735 with Carigara as capital, and after they split in 1768 the 1818 census found only fifty-six Spanish families among more than sixteen thousand native households.
zh:
莱特位于萨马与棉兰老之间，东岸敞开为莱特湾，西部山谷缓斜入卡莫特斯海。16世纪到来的西班牙人听到此岛叫坦达亚，名字来自岛上的一位首领；瓦瑞人居于岛东，其他米沙鄢族群居于岛西，住在卡里加拉、迈雷特等达图聚落中，迈雷特曾由达图埃特统治。他们在沿海平原种稻粟，在避风海湾捕鱼、造船，奉行整个米沙鄢共同的阿尼托祭祀。1444年的莱特上既无王国，也无外邦旗帜，只有相互争雄的达图、他们的巴朗盖船队，以及南往棉兰老、北通吕宋的岛际航路。

1521年3月28日，麦哲伦船队抵达莱特南岸外的小岛利马萨瓦。岛上有两位首领正率巴朗盖船队行猎，即武端的拉惹科兰布和拉惹西亚乌伊，他们设宴款待船员数日。3月31日复活节，巴尔德拉马神父在马萨瓦主持菲律宾第一场弥撒，麦哲伦又命人在岛上最高的山丘竖起十字架，随后由科兰布领航前往宿务。1543年，鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·维拉洛沃斯把莱特和萨马命名为「菲律宾群岛」，以纪念后来成为腓力二世的王子。1565年，达图班考在卡里加拉歃血欢迎黎牙实比并受洗；但到1621年，这位老基督徒重奉旧神，与任巫师的儿子帕加利筑起迪瓦塔神庙，煽动六座城镇起事。胡安·德·阿尔卡拉索率四十艘船从宿务赶来，烧毁神庙，于1622年平定叛乱，班考的头颅被悬于竹竿示众。耶稣会早在1595年就在卡里加拉开教，帕洛、奥尔莫克、阿兰加兰相继设堂，但西班牙人的统治始终稀薄：1735年莱特与萨马合为一省，以卡里加拉为首府；1768年两省分置后，1818年普查在一万六千余户本地人之外，只数出五十六户西班牙裔家庭。

en:
Zamboanga guards the western tip of Mindanao, where the peninsula ends in a roadstead facing Basilan and the Sulu Sea. Its Sinama name, Samboangan, means a mooring place. The river valleys behind the coast were Subanen country; the Subanen had farmed them since the twelfth century and kept to their old spirits, while Sama and Yakan boat-dwellers fished the islands offshore. By the 1400s the Islamised Tausug of Sulu, then founding their sultanate, were the rising sea power of these straits and claimed suzerainty over the coast. In 1444 Zamboanga was still more anchorage than town: raiders and traders from Mindanao, Sulu and Borneo put in for wood and water.

Spain built its foothold here as a barrier to the Moro raiding fleets sailing out of Sulu and Maguindanao. A first post at La Caldera, used from 1569, was withdrawn to Cebu in 1599. On 23 June 1635 the Jesuit engineer Melchor de Vera laid the cornerstone of Fort San José at his order's request, a date counted as the city's founding; Spaniards, Mexicans and Peruvians worked beside labourers brought from Cebu, Bohol, Panay and Cavite, and the camp's mixed Spanish and Visayan speech grew into the Chavacano creole. The Dutch attacked the fort in 1646, and in 1662 the garrison was recalled to Manila against Koxinga, after which the Jesuits rebuilt the ruined works in 1669.

In 1718–1719 Juan Sicarra raised the present fortress and renamed it for Our Lady of the Pillar of Zaragoza. A year later King Dalasi of Bulig stormed it with three thousand Moro raiders and was beaten off, and a British naval bombardment of January 1798 was likewise repulsed. In 1734 a carved relief of the Virgin was set over the east gate; local tradition holds that she appeared there to a sentry, and the gate became an open-air shrine. In 1821 the fort was commanded for a year by Juan Fermín de San Martín, the Uruguayan elder brother of the liberator José de San Martín.
zh:
三宝颜扼守棉兰老岛西端，半岛尽头的锚地正对巴西兰岛和苏禄海。萨马语原名三宝安岸（Samboangan）意为抛锚之地。海岸后方的河谷是苏巴农人的乡土，他们自12世纪起在此耕作，信奉古老的祖灵；萨马人和雅坎人等船民则在外海岛屿以渔为生。到15世纪，正在创建苏丹国的苏禄陶苏格人已经伊斯兰化，是这片海峡崛起的海上强权，向海岸索取宗主权。1444年的三宝颜还只是锚地、不成城镇，棉兰老、苏禄和婆罗洲的劫掠者与商船在此停泊，补充柴水。

西班牙人在此立足，为的是阻挡从苏禄和马京达瑙出海的摩洛劫掠船队。1569年他们先在拉卡尔德拉设点，1599年撤回宿务。1635年6月23日，耶稣会士工程师梅尔乔·德·贝拉应修会之请为圣何塞堡奠基，这一天被算作三宝颜的建城之日；西班牙人、墨西哥人和秘鲁人，连同从宿务、保和、班乃和甲米地征来的劳工一同施工，营中西班牙语与米沙鄢语混杂，逐渐形成查瓦卡诺克里奥尔语。荷兰人1646年来攻，1662年驻军为防备国姓爷被召回马尼拉，1669年耶稣会士重修了被毁的工事。

1718至1719年，胡安·西卡拉筑起现存的要塞，以萨拉戈萨的皮拉尔圣母为之改名。次年，布利格王达拉西率三千摩洛劫掠者猛攻，被守军击退；1798年1月英国舰队的炮击同样无功而返。1734年，东门上方安放了圣母浮雕，当地人相传圣母曾在那里向一名哨兵显现，这座门就此成为露天祭坛。1821年，要塞由乌拉圭人胡安·费尔明·德·圣马丁出任了一年司令官，他是解放者何塞·德·圣马丁的兄长。

en:
Caraga is the rain-drenched eastern shoulder of Mindanao, a coast of river mouths and offshore islands facing the Pacific. Its people were the Kalagan, 'the spirited ones' from kalag, spirit or soul, in their own tongue; they kept the anito cult, dwelt in datu-led villages called banwa, and lived by shore fishing and farms of rice, abaca and coconut. In 1444 their chiefs ruled unchallenged, though the coast was already caught up in the commerce and wars of neighbouring Butuan, whose balangay fleets and goldsmiths traded with China and Champa and whose gold drew raiding fleets all the way from Ternate in the Moluccas.

The first Europeans to meet these shores were Magellan's men: at Limasawa in 1521 Antonio Pigafetta encountered Rajah Siawi of the Surigaonon, tattooed and loaded with gold ornaments, noted the balangay warships under him and recorded the coast as 'Calagan'. Ruy López de Villalobos attacked Surigao in 1543 and was fought off, and Spanish arms made no headway until an expedition took Tandag in 1609 and organised the district of Caraga. Recollect friars opened the permanent mission at Tandag in 1622 and named the land provincia de gente animosa, the province of spirited folk, after the Kalagan name. Parties of soldiers and settler families were shipped from Mexico in 1635 and again in 1670 and 1672 to hold the coast against Moro raiders, and the census of 1818 counted 2,475 native families and 25 Spanish households in Surigao.
zh:
卡拉加是棉兰老岛雨水丰沛的东翼，海岸河口纵横、岛礁散布，面向太平洋。住在这里的是卡拉甘人，族名出自kalag（魂灵、胆气），意为「有胆气的人」。他们信奉阿尼托泛灵信仰，住在达图统领的村社（banwa）里，靠海捕鱼，种植稻、蕉麻和椰子。1444年，酋长们仍是这片海岸无可争议的主人，但海岸早已被卷入西邻武端的商路与战事：武端的巴兰盖船队和金匠与中国、占城通商，它的黄金还招来摩鹿加特尔纳特的渡海袭掠。

最早见到这片海岸的欧洲人是麦哲伦的船队。1521年，皮加费塔在利马萨瓦见到文身披金的苏里高人拉惹·西亚威，记下他乘坐的巴兰盖战船，并把这一带记作「卡拉甘」。1543年鲁伊·洛佩斯·德·比利亚洛沃斯进攻苏里高，被当地人击退；西班牙人的武力长期无所作为，直到1609年远征军攻下坦达格、设立卡拉加区。1622年重整奥斯定会传教士在坦达格开设常驻传教站，并依照卡拉甘的族名把这里命名为「勇者之地」（provincia de gente animosa）。1635年及1670、1672年，西班牙从墨西哥分批运来士兵和移民户驻守海岸、抵御摩洛袭掠者；1818年的户口册载，苏里高有2,475户本地家庭和25户西班牙家庭。

en:
Taytay guards the northern neck of Palawan, where Malampaya Sound opens between the South China and Sulu seas. Chinese records of the thirteenth century counted these islands among Sandao, vassals of the trading polity of Ma-i on Mindoro. Before the Spaniards came, Taytay was the seat of a small kingdom whose king, Antonio Pigafetta later heard, was followed wherever he went by ten scribes. Its people fished the sound, farmed along its shores and kept the animist rites of anito, and in 1444 they answered to their own king.

In 1521 the survivors of Magellan's expedition, fleeing his death at Mactan, put in at Taytay and held the king and his queen hostage for provisions before sailing on to the Moluccas; the court paid, and sent more food than the strangers had asked. Spanish rule followed a century later: the town was formally founded in 1623 and given to Augustinian Recollect missionaries, who began the stone fortress of Fuerza de Santa Isabel in 1667 and finished its walls only in 1738. Its guns covered the anchorage against Moro raiders from the Sulu archipelago, whose war fleets repeatedly struck the settlements of northern Palawan, Cuyo and the Calamianes. In 1818 Taytay became capital of the province of Calamianes, covering all of Paragua, as the Spaniards then called Palawan.
zh:
泰泰扼守巴拉望岛北端的颈部，马拉帕亚湾在此连通南海与苏禄海。13世纪的中国载籍把这一带岛屿记作三屿，是民都洛岛上商贸政权麻逸的属国。西班牙人到来之前，泰泰是一个小王国的都城；安东尼奥·皮加费塔后来听人说，那里的国王无论走到何处都有十名书吏随行。岛民在海湾捕鱼、沿岸耕种，奉行泛灵的阿尼托信仰；1444年时，他们听命于自己的国王。

1521年，麦哲伦在麦克坦丧命后，残部逃到泰泰，扣押国王与王后勒索粮食，随后继续驶往摩鹿加；王廷交了赎金，送来的食物比这些陌生人索要的还多。一个世纪后西班牙人才建立统治：城镇于1623年正式设立，交给重整奥斯定会传教士；他们1667年动工修建圣伊莎贝尔石堡，城墙直到1738年才完工。要塞炮火覆盖锚地，抵御从苏禄群岛而来的摩洛掠奴者，他们的战船屡次袭扰巴拉望北部、库约和卡拉棉群岛的聚落。1818年，泰泰成为卡拉棉省省会，管辖西班牙人当时称作拉帕瓜的整个巴拉望。

en:
Ise opens on the deep bight of Ise Bay, its shore a string of fishing harbours and salt fields, and the Tokaido crosses its north on the road between Kyoto and the east. In the cedar country south of the Kushida River stands the Ise Grand Shrine, holiest site of the imperial cult and reputed home of Yata no Kagami, the sacred mirror; its halls are rebuilt every twenty years, with offerings from every province. During the Southern Court wars the courtier Kitabatake Akiyoshi came south as provincial governor, and his family made themselves lords of the five southern districts, ruling from Kiriyama Castle above the Taki valley. In 1444 his descendant Kitabatake Noritomo held Kiriyama as governor-lord of southern Ise.

The house peaked under Harutomo and his son Tomonori, a swordsman trained by Tsukahara Bokuden, their reach extending into Shima and the border marches. In 1568 Oda Nobunaga's armies entered northern Ise and the local lords submitted; in the eighth month of 1569 he besieged Tomonori in Okawachi Castle himself, until Ashikaga Yoshiaki mediated a peace whose price was Nobunaga's second son Nobukatsu, adopted as the Kitabatake heir. Nobukatsu took the succession in 1575, and in the eleventh month of 1576 his soldiers killed Tomonori and his sons at several places in a single night, the Mitsuse bloodbath that ended the governor's line.

Under the Tokugawa the province was split among several domains, the greatest being Tsu, granted in 1608 to the castle-builder Todo Takatora and rated in time at 323,000 koku. Pilgrimage did more for Ise than any lord: in the Tokugawa peace one Japanese in ten is thought to have walked to the Grand Shrine, and in 1625 the shrine counted 3.62 million pilgrims in fifty days, crowding Yamada and the northern Tokaido post stations. The province also bred traders. Matsusaka was a commercial centre from the Sengoku years, and in 1673 Mitsui Takatoshi, son of a Matsusaka shopkeeper, opened the Echigoya draper's in Edo's Nihonbashi, selling over the counter for cash at fixed prices instead of visiting clients for orders. In 1683 the shogunate licensed him to run exchange shops, moving daimyo tax money between Osaka and Edo, and the Mitsui money house grew from that trade.
zh:
伊势面向水深湾阔的伊势湾，沿岸渔村、盐田相连，东海道自北境穿过，连接京都与东国。内陆栉田川以南杉林幽深，伊势神宫坐落其间：这是朝廷祭祀最神圣的所在，相传藏着神器八咫镜；神殿每隔二十年依式年迁宫之制重建，各国都要送来奉纳。南北朝争乱时，公卿北畠显能以国司身份南下，北畠家便成为南伊势五郡的主人，居城是多气山谷上方的雾山城。1444年，其后人北畠教具在雾山城以国司兼领主的身份统治南伊势。

晴具、具教父子两代是北畠家最强盛之时，势力伸入志摩和周边边境，具教还曾随名剑客冢原卜传习剑，自己也以剑术闻名。1568年织田信长的大军攻入北伊势，当地豪族相继臣服；1569年8月，信长亲围具教于大河内城，最后由将军足利义昭斡旋议和，条件是信长次子信雄做北畠家的养子。信雄1575年继承家督，1576年11月便派兵在一夜之间分数处袭杀具教及其诸子，史称三濑之变，国司名门就此断绝。

德川时代，伊势被分为数藩，最大的是1608年封给筑城名家藤堂高虎的津藩，石高后来达三十二万三千石。让伊势繁盛的却是参拜客：太平年月里，据说每十个日本人就有一人步行前往伊势神宫，1625年神宫记下五十天内三百六十二万人参诣，门前町山田和北境的东海道宿场人头攒动。伊势也出商人：松阪自战国年间就是商业集镇，1673年，松阪商家之子三井高利在江户日本桥开出越后屋吴服店，不再登门接订单，而在店里按固定价格现钱售货；1683年他又获准经营两替店，为大名在大阪和江户之间调拨税款，三井的钱庄生意就是从这笔银两替买卖做起的。

en:
Mikawa, or Sanshū, lay on the Tōkaidō east of Owari, its coast indented by Mikawa and Atsumi bays and the Yahagi river crossing its rice plains. The province had long been split informally into east and west around the Yasaku, and the murder of its shugo Isshiki Yoshitsura on Shōgun Yoshinori's orders in 1440, followed by the grant of the office to the Hosokawa, threw it into civil war. In 1444 rival governors, ikki bands and local houses fought over the lowlands. Among the small lords gaining ground were the Matsudaira of the Kamo hills in the west, pushing south under Matsudaira Nobumitsu.

That obscure house produced the Tokugawa. Matsudaira Kiyoyasu held Okazaki and came close to taking the whole province before a retainer killed him in his Owari camp in 1535, an event remembered as the Moriyama collapse. His grandson Takechiyo, the future Tokugawa Ieyasu, was born in Okazaki Castle in January 1543; at five he was seized on the road by Oda Nobuhide while being delivered as a hostage to the Imagawa, and he grew up at Sunpu before reclaiming Okazaki after Imagawa Yoshimoto fell at Okehazama in 1560. He broke the armed True Pure Land leagues of the Mikawa Ikkō-ikki of 1563–64, fighting in the front line at Azukizaka in 1564 where several bullets struck his armour without piercing it, and in 1566 he won imperial leave to take the name Tokugawa. After he moved east to Hamamatsu and later to the Kantō, Okazaki passed through other hands until the new shogunate enfeoffed Honda Yasushige there at 50,000 koku in 1602, first of a line of fudai lords. Mikawa then supplied the shogunate in quieter ways: the Tōkaidō stations carried daimyō retinues over the Yahagi bridge, the regime concentrated its gunpowder works in the province, and from the mid-seventeenth century the Hatchō breweries west of Okazaki aged the dark soybean miso sold to Edo's warrior houses.
zh:
三河（简称三州）位于尾张以东的东海道上，海岸凹入为三河湾与渥美湾，矢作川流过平原上的稻田。国内长期以矢作川一线分东西，1440年守护一色义贯被将军足利义教下令杀害、守护之职转授细川氏，三河就此陷入内战。1444年，新旧守护、国人一揆与在地豪族在平原上混战；西部加茂郡的松平氏只是其中一家小领主，在松平信光带领下向南扩张。

正是这个不起眼的家门生出了德川家。松平清康据有冈崎，几乎拿下整个三河，1535年却在尾张阵中被家臣刺杀，史称森山崩。其孙竹千代（后来的德川家康）1543年1月生于冈崎城，五岁时在被送往今川氏为质的途中遭织田信秀劫持，后来在骏府长大，直到1560年今川义元战死桶狭间才夺回冈崎。1563至1564年，他打垮三河一向一揆的真宗门徒武装，1564年在小豆坂之战中亲临前线，身中数弹而铠甲未穿；1566年获朝廷敕许改姓德川。他后来东移滨松、再入关东，冈崎几经转手，幕府于1602年封本多康重五万石入城，开谱代大名世袭之先。此后三河以另一种方式支撑幕府：东海道宿场迎送跨过矢作桥的大名行列，国内集中了火药工场，17世纪中叶起，冈崎城西的八丁作坊陈酿深色豆味噌，卖给江户的武家。

en:
Roxburghshire is the middle march of Scotland, where the Teviot runs into the Tweed under Roxburgh Castle. David I made Roxburgh a royal burgh and a southern seat of his court, and planted two of the border's greatest abbeys at Kelso and Jedburgh. Few castles changed hands so often. It went to England with the captive William the Lion in 1174, and under Edward I Bruce's sister Mary spent four years in a cage hung outside its walls. Sir James Douglas retook it on a February night in 1314, his men in black cloaks mistaken for grazing cattle, and Bruce ordered the whole fortress pulled down. The English rebuilt it under Edward III and kept it after Neville's Cross in 1346; two later Scottish sieges failed, and in 1444 an English garrison still held the Tweed crossing. Up the Jed water, Jedburgh lived by its abbey, its horse and cattle fairs and the reiving trade under Douglas wardens. Border speech named 'Jethart justice' after the town: a man was hanged first and tried afterwards.

In 1460 James II brought his artillery to Roxburgh and was killed when one of his own bombards burst; his queen, Mary of Guelders, pressed the storm, and the Scots razed castle and town so completely that Roxburgh was never rebuilt, and Jedburgh became the county town. English armies burned Kelso, Melrose and Jedburgh abbeys in the Rough Wooing, although the Scots won at Ancrum Moor in 1545 and the fort the English had thrown up on the castle mound was demolished when the war ended. Mary, Queen of Scots, lay ill at Jedburgh in 1566. After the Union of the Crowns the reivers were curbed and the wool and knitting trades spread up the dales; Floors Castle, seat of the Dukes of Roxburghe, rose facing the castle mound in 1721–26, and Prince Charles's army passed through on 6 November 1745. In 1787 James Hutton examined the tilted rock beds capped by red sandstone near Jedburgh, one of the unconformities on which he built his case for an immensely old earth.
zh:
罗克斯堡郡是苏格兰的中部边疆，蒂维厄特河在罗克斯堡城堡下注入特威德河。大卫一世把罗克斯堡建成皇家自治镇和南方的王家居城，又在凯尔索和杰德堡建起边境上最宏大的两座修道院。没有几座城堡像它这样频繁易主。1174年，它随被俘的狮子王威廉交给英格兰；爱德华一世据守期间，布鲁斯的妹妹玛丽被关在吊于城墙外的木笼里四年。1314年2月的一个夜晚，詹姆斯·道格拉斯率身披黑袍的部下奇袭得手，守军把他们错当成吃草的牛群，布鲁斯随后下令把整座城堡拆毁。英格兰人在爱德华三世时将其重建，1346年内维尔十字之战后持续占据；之后苏格兰人两次围攻均告失败，1444年特威德河渡口仍在英格兰守军手中。杰德沃特河上游的杰德堡靠着修道院、马市牛市和边境劫掠为生，守臣出自道格拉斯家。边境俗语把先绞后审称作「杰德哈特式审判」，名字就来自这座镇子。

1460年，詹姆斯二世携炮兵围攻罗克斯堡，他自己的一门攻城炮炸裂，碎片将他打死；王后海尔德的玛丽继续督战破城，苏格兰人把城堡和城镇彻底夷平，罗克斯堡再未重建，郡治改设杰德堡。「粗暴求婚」战争中，英军焚毁凯尔索、梅尔罗斯和杰德堡的修道院，尽管苏格兰人1545年在安克勒姆荒原取胜，城堡土丘上的英军要塞也在战后拆除。1566年，苏格兰女王玛丽在杰德堡重病。两国王位合并后，边境流寇遭到整肃，羊毛和针织业沿河谷传播开来；1721至1726年，罗克斯堡公爵的弗洛斯城堡在城堡土丘对岸建成，1745年11月6日查理王子的军队穿镇而过。1787年，詹姆斯·赫顿在杰德堡附近考察上覆红砂岩的倾斜岩层，正是这类不整合面支撑了他关于地球极为古老的论证。

en:
Dumfries commands the lowest crossing of the Nith above the Solway Firth, port and market of Scotland's West March. William the Lion made it a royal burgh in 1186. Lincluden Abbey stood on the bank above the town, and eight miles to the south Sweetheart Abbey was founded in 1273 by Dervorguilla of Galloway, who carried her dead husband John Balliol's embalmed heart in a casket of ivory and silver and was buried with it; their son reigned in Scotland as John Balliol. Further south the Maxwells' moated, three-cornered Caerlaverock guarded the Nith mouth: in July 1300 sixty men held it for days against the army Edward I led north in person, until hunger forced surrender, and the heralds in the English host turned the siege into a roll of arms in French verse. In the Greyfriars' church at Dumfries Robert Bruce stabbed the Red Comyn on 10 February 1306, and his follower Kirkpatrick went in to 'mak siccar', to make sure; the killing put Bruce on the road to Bannockburn. Beyond the Dee, Archibald the Grim raised Threave Castle for the Douglases in the 1370s, and in 1444 his widowed daughter-in-law Princess Margaret ruled the Galloway lordship from its tower. The marches lived by wool, cattle and raiding.

James II ended Douglas power with his own knife, stabbing the eighth earl at Stirling on 22 February 1452; the rising that followed collapsed near Langholm on 1 May 1455, and Threave surrendered. In November 1542 the English routed a Scottish army on Solway Moss beside the Esk, a defeat said to have hastened the death of James V. Caerlaverock held for the Catholic earls of Nithsdale until a Covenanter army took it after thirteen weeks in 1640, and the Maxwells never lived there again. Late in 1745 the Young Pretender kept his headquarters in Dumfries for three days and mulcted the town of £1,000 on his retreat north. Robert Burns farmed at Ellisland from 1788, moved into Dumfries in 1791 and died there in 1796; in 1788, the year Burns took the farm, William Symington tried a steam engine in a boat on nearby Dalswinton Loch.
zh:
邓弗里斯扼守尼思河注入索尔韦湾前的最后渡口，是苏格兰西部边疆的港口与集镇。狮子王威廉1186年将其升为皇家自治镇。林克卢登修道院立在镇北河畔；再往南八英里，甜心修道院1273年由加洛韦的德沃尔吉拉创建，她把亡夫约翰·巴利奥尔经防腐处理的心脏盛在象牙白银匣中随身携带，死后与之合葬，修道院的拉丁名意为「甜心」；他们的儿子后来登上苏格兰王位，即国王约翰·巴利奥尔。更南边，马克斯韦尔家环水而建的三角形城堡扼守尼思河口：1300年7月，六十名守军在此抵挡爱德华一世亲率的大军多日，粮尽才降，英军中的传令官把这场围城写成法文韵文的纹章名册。1306年2月10日，罗伯特·布鲁斯在邓弗里斯的灰衣修士会教堂刺死「红科明」，随从柯克帕特里克进屋补刀，说是要「确保万无一失」，这桩血案把布鲁斯推上班诺克本的道路。迪河对岸，「冷面的」阿奇博尔德在14世纪70年代为道格拉斯家筑起特利维城堡；1444年，他守寡的儿媳玛格丽特公主仍在主塔里统治加洛韦领地。边疆上下以羊毛、牲畜和劫掠为生。

詹姆斯二世亲手了结道格拉斯家的权势：1452年2月22日他在斯特灵刺死第八代伯爵，随后的叛乱于1455年5月1日在兰霍姆附近溃败，特利维城堡开城投降。1542年11月，英军在埃斯克河畔的索维莫斯击溃苏格兰军，据说这场败仗加速了詹姆斯五世之死。三角水堡为天主教的尼思河谷伯爵们坚守到1640年，盟约派军队围攻十三周才将它拿下，马克斯韦尔家再没搬回堡中。1745年末，小王位觊觎者在邓弗里斯设了三天司令部，北撤时向镇上勒索了一千英镑。罗伯特·彭斯1788年起在埃利斯兰务农，1791年迁居邓弗里斯，1796年在此去世；同在1788年，威廉·赛明顿在附近的达斯温顿湖上试航了装有蒸汽机的小船。

en:
Argyll (Gaelic Earra-Ghàidheal, the 'coast of the Gaels') is the sea-loch coast and inner isles of western Scotland, the old country of Dál Riata. Its kings were enthroned on the rock of Dunadd, and from Iona, founded in 563, Columba's monks took Christianity to the Picts. Kintyre and Lorn fell under Norse rule and came back to Scotland only with the Treaty of Perth in 1266. Power then lay with the MacDonald Lords of the Isles, Norse-Gaelic heirs of Somerled who ruled from Finlaggan on Islay with fleets of galleys and answered to no king in practice; the Campbells rose beside them as hereditary sheriffs and the crown's men, building the first castle at Inveraray on Loch Fyne around 1432. In 1444 Sir Duncan Campbell of Lochawe held Loch Awe and the sea roads for the king from his tower-houses, though the Gaelic west still looked to Islay rather than Edinburgh, and cattle, timber and herring moved through the sea lochs.

Colin Campbell became the first Earl of Argyll in 1457. The Lordship of the Isles ended in 1493, when James IV seized John MacDonald's lands and titles, and the Campbells afterwards led the crown's expansion into the Hebrides; they embraced the Reformation and under James VI subdued the Catholic MacDonald lands of Islay and Jura. Civil war struck savagely in December 1644, when Montrose and Alasdair MacColla burned Inveraray, and on 2 February 1645 destroyed Argyll's army beneath Inverlochy Castle. On 13 February 1692 government troops under Campbell of Glenlyon killed about thirty MacDonalds of Glencoe who had fed and sheltered them for a fortnight, and Glencoe fed Jacobite anger for two generations. The Campbells became dukes in 1701. From 1744 the third duke rebuilt Inveraray as a planned town with a new castle by the Adam family, and in 1753 the Bonawe furnace on Loch Etive began smelting imported ore with Highland charcoal, turning the local oakwoods into cannon and tools.
zh:
阿盖尔（盖尔语Earra-Ghàidheal，意为「盖尔人的海岸」）是苏格兰西部的峡湾海岸与内群岛，古达尔里阿达王国的故地。国王在杜纳德堡的岩石上登基，563年创立的艾奥纳修道院里，哥伦巴的修士把基督教传给皮克特人。金泰尔和洛恩曾受诺斯人统治，直到1266年《珀斯条约》才归还苏格兰。此后实权在麦克唐纳家族的群岛之主手中：他们是萨默莱德的诺斯与盖尔后裔，率桨帆船队坐镇艾拉岛的芬拉根（Finlaggan），实际上不奉王命；坎贝尔家族则作为世袭郡长和王庭的代理人崛起，约1432年在法恩湖畔建起第一座因弗雷里堡。1444年，洛赫奥的邓肯·坎贝尔爵士凭塔楼扼守洛赫奥与各条海路为王庭效力，但盖尔语的西方更听命于艾拉岛而非爱丁堡，牛只、木材和鲱鱼在重重峡湾间往来。

科林·坎贝尔1457年成为第一代阿盖尔伯爵。1493年，詹姆斯四世剥夺约翰·麦克唐纳的土地与头衔，群岛之主时代结束，坎贝尔家族此后替王庭向赫布里底扩张；他们皈依新教，奉詹姆斯六世之命平定了艾拉、朱拉两岛信奉天主教的麦克唐纳领地。内战来得惨烈：1644年12月，蒙特罗斯与阿拉斯代尔·麦科拉焚毁因弗雷里，1645年2月2日又在因弗洛希堡下歼灭阿盖尔的军队。1692年2月13日，格伦里昂的坎贝尔率领的政府军杀害了供他们食宿两周的格伦科麦克唐纳族人约三十名，格伦科之事滋养了此后两代人的詹姆斯党怒火。坎贝尔家族1701年受封公爵。1744年起，第三代公爵把因弗雷里重建成规划新城，并由亚当家族修建新堡；1753年，埃蒂夫湖畔的博诺铁炉开炉，用高地木炭冶炼进口矿石，把当地的栎树林化作大炮和工具。

en:
The Inner Hebrides run from Skye through Mull to Islay on Scotland's western sea lanes. Norse-Scottish seafaring lords grew out of Somerled's twelfth-century realm, and the 1266 Treaty of Perth brought the islands from Norway to Scotland. Their seat was Finlaggan on Islay: on Eilean Mor in the loch stood the Lord's residence, and the smaller Isle of the Council held his meeting of chiefs, whose galleys linked Ireland with the Highlands. On Skye, Dunvegan Castle on a rock in its sea loch was already the seat of the MacLeod chiefs, and it kept the Fairy Flag, a torn square of eastern silk which tradition called a fairy's gift or a relic brought home from the Crusades, and which unfurled in battle was said to multiply the clan's fighting men. MacDonalds held Sleat in the south of the island. In 1444 these Catholic, Gaelic-speaking islands were the core of the maritime power of Alexander MacDonald, Lord of the Isles and Earl of Ross, not a distant edge of Scotland.

Alexander's son John signed the secret Treaty of Ardtornish with Edward IV of England in 1462; when it came to light James III stripped him of most of his power in 1476, and his own son Angus defeated him at the Bloody Bay off Mull in 1481. James IV ended the lordship altogether in 1493, and the isles became a patchwork of MacLean, MacLeod, MacDonald and MacKinnon estates held under the Crown. Islanders joined the Jacobite risings of 1715 and 1745. After Culloden the old clan order was recast as landed estates. Flora MacDonald, who helped Charles Edward Stuart escape through Skye in 1746, later lived on the island, where Samuel Johnson and James Boswell visited her in 1773; she was buried at Kilmuir. Cattle, fishing, kelp and Easdale slate tied the islands to southern markets, until the kelp trade collapsed after 1815.
zh:
内赫布里底群岛沿苏格兰西侧海路，从斯凯岛经马尔岛延伸到艾莱岛。12世纪萨默雷德的海上王国孕育出诺斯与苏格兰混血的航海领主，1266年《珀斯条约》又把群岛从挪威移交苏格兰。领主的统治中心在艾莱岛的芬拉冈：湖中的大岛上建有领主宅邸，旁边较小的「议事岛」召开氏族首领会议，他们的桨帆船把爱尔兰和高地之间的海路连成一气。斯凯岛上，邓韦根城堡立在海湾的礁石上，已是麦克劳德首领的世代驻地；堡中收藏着「仙旗」，那是一块残破的东方丝绸，相传为仙女所赠，或十字军从圣地带回的圣物，据说战斗中展开能让氏族战士凭空倍增。岛南的斯莱特归麦克唐纳家族。1444年，这些信奉天主教、使用盖尔语的岛屿是群岛领主兼罗斯伯爵亚历山大·麦克唐纳海洋势力的核心，而不是苏格兰偏远的边地。

亚历山大之子约翰1462年与英格兰国王爱德华四世秘密签订《阿德托尼什条约》；事情败露后，詹姆斯三世于1476年剥夺他的大部分权力，1481年他的亲生子安加斯又在马尔岛近海的血腥湾战役中将他击败。1493年詹姆斯四世彻底废除群岛领地，群岛此后成为麦克莱恩、麦克劳德、麦克唐纳和麦金农等家族在王权威名下交错的封地。岛民参加了1715年和1745年的詹姆斯党起事；卡洛登之后，旧氏族秩序被改造成地产制度。弗洛拉·麦克唐纳1746年帮助查理·爱德华·斯图亚特经斯凯岛脱身，后来长住岛上，1773年塞缪尔·约翰逊和詹姆斯·鲍斯韦尔曾登门拜访，她去世后葬在基尔缪尔。牲畜、渔业、海藻灰和伊斯代尔石板把群岛与南方市场连在一起，直到1815年后海藻灰贸易崩溃。

en:
Mann, the Isle of Man, lies in the middle of the Irish Sea, within sailing reach of England, Scotland, Ireland and Wales. Norse Vikings made it the seat of the Kingdom of Mann and the Isles, whose rulers established Tynwald, by tradition founded in 979 and the oldest continuous parliament in the British Isles; its twenty-four Keys sat as the island's court, and laws were proclaimed outdoors from the mound at St John's. The 1266 Treaty of Perth transferred the island from Norway to Scotland, but Mann changed hands repeatedly in the Scottish wars, and English rule became lasting only after 1346. Castletown grew beneath Castle Rushen, guarding its southern harbour, and the three running legs of the Manx coat of arms appeared in the thirteenth century. In 1405 Henry IV granted John Stanley the title King of Mann. In 1444 Catholic, Manx-speaking islanders lived by farming and fishing under the Stanley family, whose English feudal lordship left Tynwald and local customs in being.

The Stanleys kept Mann through the fifteenth century, and early in the sixteenth their royal-sounding title became Lord of Mann. During the Civil War James Stanley, seventh Earl of Derby, held a Royalist court at Castle Rushen; he sailed in 1651 with three hundred Manx Royalists, was captured after Worcester and executed at Bolton. His wife Charlotte held the castle until the Manx rising of Illiam Dhone and her garrison's mutiny delivered it to Parliament; Dhone was executed in 1663. Bishop Wilson helped secure the Act of Settlement in 1704, which gave Manx tenants permanent holdings and became known as their Magna Carta. Low duties then made the island a smugglers' haven, with cargoes run across to England and Ireland, and in 1765 Parliament paid £70,000 to buy the Atholl family's rights and take the customs into Crown hands. Smuggling lingered, and the Napoleonic wars made Mann a naval outpost. In 1821 it remained a separately governed fishing island under the British Crown, not part of Great Britain.
zh:
马恩（Isle of Man，常译曼岛）坐落在爱尔兰海中央，从英格兰、苏格兰、爱尔兰和威尔士都能扬帆抵达。诺斯维京人曾把这里作为「马恩与群岛王国」的中心，统治者设立了廷瓦尔德议会：按传统说法始于979年，是不列颠群岛最古老且未曾中断的议会，二十四名「钥匙」议员组成岛上的法庭，法令则在圣约翰斯的土丘上当众宣布。1266年《珀斯条约》把岛屿从挪威移交苏格兰，但马恩在苏格兰战争中多次易手，英格兰的统治到1346年后才稳固下来。卡斯尔敦在拉申城堡脚下发展，城堡守护着南部港湾，马恩纹章上三条奔跑的人腿图案13世纪已经出现。1405年，亨利四世把「马恩国王」的头衔授予约翰·斯坦利。1444年，信奉天主教、使用马恩语的岛民在斯坦利家族治下农耕捕鱼，这个英格兰封建领主仍保留了廷瓦尔德和本地旧俗。

斯坦利家族在15世纪一直领有马恩；到16世纪初，他们那个近似君王的头衔从「马恩国王」改成「马恩领主」。内战期间，第七代德比伯爵詹姆斯·斯坦利在拉申城堡维持王党宫廷；1651年他率三百名马恩王党人出援，伍斯特战败后被俘，在博尔顿被处决。妻子夏洛特继续据守城堡，直到伊利厄姆·多恩率马恩人起事、守军哗变，城堡才落入议会军之手；多恩本人于1663年被处死。1704年，威尔逊主教促成《定居法》，使佃农获得永久持有权，该法后来被称为马恩人的大宪章。低关税随后把岛屿变成走私者的天堂，私货被小船运往英格兰和爱尔兰；1765年，议会出资七万英镑买下阿索尔家族的封建权利，把关税收归王权。走私仍有余波，拿破仑战争又使马恩成为海军前哨。1821年，它仍是不列颠王权下单独治理、以渔业为生的岛屿，不属于大不列颠王国。

en:
Montgomery stands a mile inside Wales, where the border hills come down to a ford of the Severn; Offa's Dyke runs past the town. The Normans first raised a motte at Hen Domen to watch that ford, and a stone castle was begun on the crag above it in 1223, taking its name from Roger de Montgomery, the Conqueror's earl in these Marches. Here in 1267 Henry III signed the treaty that recognised Llywelyn ap Gruffudd as Prince of Wales. The lordship behind the castle ran south through the old Powys lands into the wooded country between Wye and Severn that later became Radnorshire, poor ground of drovers' roads and marcher fortresses. Owain Glyndwr's revolt burned through the district: the town was sacked, and on 22 June 1402 the Welsh destroyed a Herefordshire levy under Sir Edmund Mortimer at Bryn Glas above Pilleth, Glyndwr's greatest victory in the open field. Mortimer was captured, threw in his lot with the Welsh prince, and married his daughter Catrin. Royal power returned before the revolt ended, and by 1444 this thinly peopled Catholic March lived under royal and marcher castles on the roads to Shrewsbury.

After Bosworth the lordship passed to the Welsh Herbert family, and the poet George Herbert was born in the town in 1593. The Laws in Wales later turned the marcher lordships into shires, with New Radnor and then Presteigne as the Radnorshire assize towns. The Civil War gave Montgomery the largest battle fought on Welsh soil: on 18 September 1644 Sir John Meldrum's Parliamentarians routed Lord Byron's royalist army below the castle. Parliament had the castle itself demolished in 1649, and Radnor Castle was dismantled after a siege.
zh:
蒙哥马利在威尔士境内一英里处，边地丘陵在此俯临塞文河的一处渡口，奥法堤从镇旁经过。诺曼人先在亨多门筑起土岗堡监视渡口，1223年又在高处的巉岩上动工修建石堡，城镇得名于征服者威廉册封在此的边地伯爵罗杰·德·蒙哥马利。1267年，亨利三世在此签订条约，承认卢埃林·阿普·格鲁菲德为威尔士亲王。城堡后的领地向南穿过古老的波伊斯土地，一直延伸到怀河与塞文河之间的林地，即后来的拉德诺郡；这片贫瘠之地遍布赶牲畜的山道和边地贵族要塞。欧文·格林杜尔的叛乱席卷此地：城镇遭劫掠，1402年6月22日，威尔士军又在皮莱思上方的布林格拉斯歼灭埃德蒙·莫蒂默爵士率领的赫里福德民军，这是格林杜尔在野战中最大的胜利。莫蒂默被俘后归附这位威尔士亲王，并娶了他的女儿卡特琳。叛乱结束前王权已经恢复；到1444年，这片人烟稀少的天主教边地由王室和边地贵族的城堡统辖，守望着通往什鲁斯伯里的道路。

博斯沃思战役后，领地转入威尔士赫伯特家族手中，诗人乔治·赫伯特1593年出生在这座镇上。后来的《威尔士法律法令》把边地领地改为郡份，拉德诺郡的巡回审判先在纽拉德诺举行，后改在普雷斯泰因。内战在蒙哥马利打出了威尔士土地上规模最大的一仗：1644年9月18日，约翰·梅尔德伦爵士的议会军在城堡下击溃拜伦勋爵的王党军队。议会1649年下令拆毁蒙哥马利城堡，拉德诺城堡也在围攻后被拆除。

en:
Hull stands where the River Hull joins the Humber, twenty-five miles inland from the North Sea. The monks of Meaux Abbey laid out the haven of Wyke in the late twelfth century to ship their wool, and in 1293 Edward I bought the manor and renamed the town Kingston upon Hull by charter in 1299, using it as his supply port for the Scottish wars. Wool and cloth went out to the Hanse ports of the Baltic and timber and wine came back. The town's first mayor, William de la Pole, was called by a chronicler second to no merchant in England; he and his descendants financed Edward III's wars and rose to become Earls and Dukes of Suffolk. A charter of 1440 placed the town under a mayor and a sheriff. In 1444 Hull was Yorkshire's busiest port on the east coast, compact and prosperous behind its walls.

Hull mattered most at the start of the Civil War because of its arsenal, the second largest in England after the Tower of London, holding 120 guns and arms for 16,000 to 20,000 men. On 23 April 1642 Charles I came in person to Beverley Gate with his lords and Prince Rupert and demanded entry; Sir John Hotham stood on the wall above him and refused, offering the king twelve attendants where he wanted thirty, while provisions were lowered from the ramparts as the two sides argued. A royalist siege in July collapsed after Sir John Meldrum led a sally that destroyed the king's magazine outside the walls. The shut gate was the first open blow of the Civil War, but Hotham did not long survive it: he and his son were accused of bargaining to hand the town back, and both went to the block in January 1645. After the Restoration the walls came down and docks were dug along their line, the first in 1778 and Humber Dock in 1809, while Hull whalers sailed to Arctic waters. William Wilberforce, born here in 1759, led the parliamentary campaign that carried the Slave Trade Act of 1807.
zh:
赫尔位于赫尔河注入亨伯河处，距北海二十五英里。12世纪末，莫修道院的修士开辟威克港外运羊毛；1293年爱德华一世买下这片庄园，1299年颁赐特许状，改名赫尔河畔金斯顿，作为苏格兰战争的补给港。羊毛和呢绒运往波罗的海的汉萨城市，木材和葡萄酒随船而回。首任市长威廉·德拉波尔被编年史家称为「英格兰商人中无人能出其右」，他和后代为爱德华三世的战争筹款，家世累迁至萨福克伯爵与公爵。1440年的特许状确立了市长加治安官的治理体制。1444年的赫尔是约克郡东岸最繁忙的港口，城墙之内紧凑而富庶。

内战开打时各方都盯住赫尔，为的是城中的军火库：其规模在英格兰仅次于伦敦塔，存有120门火炮和可供一万六千至两万人使用的武器。1642年4月23日，查理一世带着众贵族和鲁珀特亲王亲临贝弗利门要求入城，约翰·霍瑟姆爵士站在城头回绝，只许国王带十二名随从，国王则要三十名；双方僵持时，食物从城墙上缒下。7月王党围攻该城，约翰·梅尔德勒姆爵士率军出击，毁掉了城外的王党火药库，围军这才撤走。闭门拒王是内战的第一记公开冲突，霍瑟姆却没能得意多久：他和儿子被指控与王党暗中交易、要献出该城，两人于1645年1月先后被斩首。王政复辟后城墙拆除，沿墙基开凿船坞，第一座1778年落成，亨伯船坞1809年启用，赫尔的捕鲸船也远航北极海域。1759年生于本城的威廉·威尔伯福斯在议会长期奔走，促成1807年《废除奴隶贸易法案》通过。

en:
Scarborough lies beneath a great headland castle on the North Sea coast of the North Riding. A wooden fortress went up in the 1130s, and from about 1157 Henry II rebuilt it in stone, raising his keep between 1159 and 1169 above the borough he had chartered in 1155. The king's peace served trade: in 1253 Henry III licensed a six-week fair, from 15 August to Michaelmas, where merchants from across Europe did business beside the herring fleets, the Scarborough Fair later remembered in the ballad of that name. The same walls drew the crown's quarrels to the town. In May 1312 Piers Gaveston, Edward II's favourite, held the castle while the king's enemies closed in; he surrendered on terms to the Earls of Pembroke and Warenne on 19 May, and on 19 June the Earl of Warwick and his allies had him beheaded on Blacklow Hill. The Scots under Sir James Douglas burned the town in 1318. In 1444 Scarborough was a fishing port and market town beneath one of England's strongest royal castles.

During the Pilgrimage of Grace Robert Aske failed to take the castle in 1536, and in 1557 Thomas Stafford's rebels got in disguised as peasants, held the castle for three days and went to their executions. In the Civil War a royalist garrison endured a five-month siege: Parliament's men stormed the town on 18 February 1645 and their commander Sir John Meldrum was killed below the keep, which did not surrender until 25 July; a second siege ended on 19 December 1648, after the stronghold had changed hands seven times, leaving it a roofless ruin. Peace brought the town a different living. In 1626 Thomasin Farrer found acidic springs in the cliffs, and after Dr Robert Wittie published a book on the waters in 1660 visitors began to arrive, making Scarborough Britain's first seaside resort; bathing machines stood on the sands by 1735 and the pier lighthouse went up in 1806.
zh:
斯卡布罗位于约克郡北赖丁的北海之滨，镇子贴着海岬上的巨堡而建。1130年代这里先筑起一座木堡，约1157年亨利二世改用石材重建，主楼在1159至1169年间落成，俯临他1155年特许设立的自治镇。王政安定利于通商：1253年亨利三世恩准举办为期六周的集市，自8月15日到米迦勒节，欧洲各地商人赶来与鲱鱼船队并排交易，这就是后来同名歌谣里传唱的「斯卡布罗集市」。坚固的城墙也把王权与贵族的争斗引到这里：1312年5月，爱德华二世的宠臣皮尔斯·加韦斯顿在众贵族进逼下据守堡中，5月19日有条件地向彭布罗克伯爵和瓦伦伯爵投降，6月19日便被沃里克伯爵及其同党押到布莱克洛山斩首。1318年，詹姆斯·道格拉斯爵士率苏格兰人焚毁全镇。1444年的斯卡布罗是一座渔港和集镇，坐落在英格兰最坚固的王室城堡之一脚下。

1536年求恩巡礼期间，罗伯特·阿斯克攻打城堡未果；1557年，托马斯·斯塔福德的党羽化装成农夫混入堡内，只据守三天就被擒获处死。内战中，王党守军熬过了长达五个月的围城：1645年2月18日议会军攻入镇区，主将约翰·梅尔德勒姆爵士战死于主楼下，城堡直到7月25日才投降；第二次围城于1648年12月19日结束，其间这座要塞七度易手，最终只剩没有屋顶的废墟。和平给镇子带来另一种生计：1626年托马辛·法勒在崖壁间发现酸性矿泉，1660年罗伯特·威蒂医生为泉水著书后访客陆续前来，斯卡布罗成为英国第一处海滨疗养地；1735年沙滩上已有更衣车，1806年码头灯塔建成。

en:
Carmarthen lies eight miles up the Towy from Carmarthen Bay, on the Roman town of Moridunum, the civitas of the Demetae, whose amphitheatre still stands beyond the streets; it has a claim to be the oldest town in Wales. Its Welsh name, Caerfyrddin, was read in the Middle Ages as 'Merlin's fort', and Geoffrey of Monmouth set Merlin's birth in a cave outside the town, though the name in fact runs back to Roman Moridunum. Medieval Carmarthen was two boroughs, one around the Augustinian priory and one around the castle rebuilt in 1223. The priory kept the Black Book of Carmarthen, written about 1250 and one of the oldest books written entirely in Welsh, with poems on Myrddin and Arthur. The wider province took in the Towy cattle pastures, the Cardiganshire coast, the pilgrim roads to St Davids and the old Flemish farmland of southern Pembrokeshire. Glyndwr's men took the town and sacked the castle in 1405, and by 1444 Carmarthen was again a Catholic royal garrison and market serving the bay trade.

About 1451 the town hosted one of the earliest recorded eisteddfodau, under Gruffudd ap Nicolas. In 1456 Edmund Tudor, Earl of Richmond, died of plague in the castle, three months before his son Henry Tudor, the future Henry VII, was born. Henry sailed from Pembroke to Bosworth in 1485 with south-west Welsh levies brought him by Sir Rhys ap Thomas, who was later buried in Carmarthen's Grey Friars beside Edmund. Under Henry VIII the priory and friary were dissolved, and in 1555 Bishop Ferrar of St Davids was burned at the stake in Carmarthen market. In the Civil War Parliament slighted the castle and Cromwell besieged Pembroke after a 1648 mutiny. The country roundabout fattened cattle and shipped herrings and corn, with lead and silver in the hills, and in the eighteenth century Daniel Rowland preached the Methodist revival at Llangeitho. On 24 February 1797 Colonel William Tate's French legion surrendered at Fishguard after a three-day landing, the last hostile landing on mainland Britain; local tradition keeps Jemima Nicholas, who herded a dozen French soldiers into the town at pitchfork point.
zh:
卡马森位于托威河上、距卡马森湾八英里处，建在罗马城镇莫里杜努姆的旧址上。这里曾是德梅泰人的城邦中心，城边就有罗马圆形竞技场的遗址，卡马森也被认为是威尔士最古老的城镇。它的威尔士语名Caerfyrddin在中世纪被解作「梅林的堡垒」，蒙茅斯的杰弗里还把梅林的出生地安排在城外的一个洞穴里，不过这个地名其实可追溯到罗马时代的莫里杜努姆。中世纪的卡马森分作两处自治聚落，分别围绕奥斯定会修道院和1223年重建的城堡。修道院保存着约1250年成书的《卡马森黑皮书》，它是最古老的全威尔士语写本之一，录有写梅尔丁和亚瑟的诗篇。这片广阔地区涵盖托威河畔牧场、卡迪根郡海岸、通往圣戴维兹的朝圣道路，以及彭布罗克郡南部早年有佛兰芒人定居的农田。1405年，格林杜尔的人马攻占城镇、洗劫城堡；到1444年，卡马森重新成为天主教王室驻军据点和市场，为海湾贸易效劳。

约1451年，在格鲁菲德·阿普·尼古拉斯主持下，卡马森举办了有记载的最早一批威尔士诗人赛会之一。1456年，里士满伯爵埃德蒙·都铎在城堡中染疫病故，三个月后他的儿子亨利·都铎，也就是后来的亨利七世出生。1485年，亨利从彭布罗克出征博斯沃思，里斯·阿普·托马斯为他带来西南威尔士的征召部队；里斯死后葬在卡马森的方济各会院，与埃德蒙为伴。亨利八世时期，修道院和方济各会院被解散；1555年，圣戴维兹主教费拉尔在卡马森市场被处以火刑。内战中，议会军拆毁卡马森城堡，1648年彭布罗克兵变后克伦威尔又围攻彭布罗克。这一带养牛外销，装运鲱鱼和谷物，山中出产铅银；18世纪，丹尼尔·罗兰在兰盖索布道，推动了循道宗复兴。1797年2月24日，威廉·泰特上校的法国军团登陆菲什加德，三天后即告投降，这是敌对军队最后一次在不列颠大陆登陆；当地传说里还留着杰迈玛·尼古拉斯的名字，据说她用干草叉押着十几个法国兵进了镇。

en:
Cambridge lies at the southern edge of the Fens, where the road from London crosses the Cam on the last firm ground before the marsh. A Roman small town stood on Castle Hill; the Vikings made it a fortified Danish borough after 875, and William the Conqueror raised the castle motte there in 1068. Scholars fleeing Oxford's hostile townsmen settled by the river in 1209, and their university took root: Peterhouse, the first college, was founded in 1284, and others followed over the next two centuries. Fen barges carried eels, fish, salt and grain to the town's hythes, while Stourbridge Fair, first authorised by King John in 1211 for a leper hospital, filled the common beyond the gates every September and grew into the largest fair in Europe. After townsmen burned the university records in the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, the Crown gave the university oversight of weights, measures and markets. In 1444 Henry VI's King's College, founded three years earlier, was about to raise its chapel, and out across the waterlogged fens the abbey at Ely ruled its island estates.

The chapel's fan vault and great windows were finished under Henry VIII after decades of interrupted work. Erasmus lodged at Queens' from 1506 to 1515, teaching Greek and preparing his printed edition of the Greek scriptures, and the English Reformation was led largely by Cambridge men, among them Tyndale, Cranmer, Latimer and Ridley. Henry VIII founded Trinity College in 1546 on the old King's Hall, where Isaac Newton later wrote the Principia, published in 1687. Early in the 1600s the carrier Thomas Hobson, who hired out only the horse nearest the stable door, gave English the phrase Hobson's choice, and the fresh-water conduit brought in from Nine Wells was named for him. In the Civil War Cambridge housed the Eastern Association's headquarters, and in 1643 Parliament gave the town to Cromwell, a Sidney Sussex man. Dutch engineers hired by the Earl of Bedford's syndicate cut the Old and New Bedford Rivers through the fens from the 1630s; Fen Tigers smashed the new drains as the work went on, until the Bedford Level Corporation took charge in 1663. Stourbridge Fair kept the quays busy for another century before it dwindled away.
zh:
贝德福德郡（此处以剑桥郡为中心）的剑桥位于沼泽区南缘，伦敦来的大道在进入沼泽前最后一片硬地上跨过剑河。罗马时期城堡山上设有小镇，875年维京人到来后把它建成设防的丹麦人自治镇，1068年征服者威廉又在山上堆起城堡土丘。1209年，与牛津市民起了冲突的学者到剑河畔落脚，他们办起的大学就此扎下根：第一所学院彼得豪斯1284年创立，此后两个世纪里其他学院陆续添设。沼泽的驳船把鳗鱼、鱼、盐和粮食运到剑桥各码头；斯陶尔布里奇集市最早是1211年约翰王特许给一所麻风病院开办的，每年九月占满城外公地，后来发展成欧洲最大的集市。1381年农民起义波及剑桥，市民焚毁大学档案，王室随即把度量衡与市场的监管权划给校方。1444年，亨利六世三年前创办的国王学院正要动工修建礼拜堂；在浸了水的沼泽深处，伊利修道院统治着它的岛地。

经过数十年时断时续的施工，礼拜堂的扇形拱顶和巨型彩色玻璃窗在亨利八世朝完工。1506至1515年，伊拉斯谟寓居王后学院，讲授希腊语，并促成希腊文《新约》付印；其后英格兰宗教改革的领头人多出自剑桥，廷代尔、克兰麦、拉蒂默和里德利都曾在此求学或任教。亨利八世1546年在旧国王学堂的基础上创办三一学院，艾萨克·牛顿后来在此写成1687年出版的《自然哲学的数学原理》。17世纪初，脚夫托马斯·霍布森只许顾客牵走离马厩门最近的那匹马，英语成语「霍布森的选择」（别无选择）即出自他；从九井引淡水入城的水渠也以他得名。内战期间，东部联盟的总部设在剑桥，1643年议会把全城交给曾在悉尼·萨塞克斯学院读书的克伦威尔掌管。1630年代起，受雇于贝德福德伯爵投资团的尼德兰工程师在沼泽中开凿旧贝德福德河与新贝德福德河，被称作「沼泽之虎」的当地人在施工中不断砸毁新修的排水沟，直到1663年贝德福德洼地公司接手全部工程。斯陶尔布里奇集市又让河埠热闹了一个世纪，才渐渐冷清。

en:
Sussex, the land of the South Saxons, runs along the Channel coast between Hampshire and Kent, with the wooded Weald behind its coastal plain. In September 1066 William of Normandy landed at Pevensey, and on 14 October Harold Godwinson was killed near Hastings. William founded Battle Abbey on the field, its high altar marking the spot where Harold fell, and when the church was consecrated in 1094 the Conqueror's sword and coronation robes were laid on the altar. The Normans divided the county into fortified rapes and raised castles at Arundel, Lewes, Pevensey and Hastings. Simon de Montfort captured the future Edward I at Lewes in 1264. During the Hundred Years' War French raiders burned Hastings, Rye and Winchelsea, and Sir Edward Dalyngrigge built the moated Bodiam Castle in 1385 under licence from Richard II, as much for display as for defence. After the Black Death killed about half the county's people, much economic life shifted into the Weald, whose timber, iron, cloth and glass helped Sussex recover. In 1444 it was a Catholic coastal frontier guarded by castles and Cinque Port towns.

Sussex men joined Jack Cade's rising in 1450, and local tradition places Cade's death near Heathfield. The first Wealden blast furnace arrived from the Low Countries in 1496, and Flemish and later Huguenot craftsmen worked the iron cast into guns for the Crown's ships and armies, the furnaces fed on Wealden timber. The Reformation pulled down Battle Abbey and Lewes Priory in 1538 and broke St Richard's shrine at Chichester, and under Mary I forty-one Protestants were burned in the county. In 1642 Parliamentarians routed Royalists at Haywards Heath, and the two sides fought over Chichester, Arundel and the Wealden works. After Worcester in 1651 Charles II was hunted for six weeks with a £1,000 price on his head, reached the fishing village of Brighthelmston, later Brighton, and sailed from Shoreham for France on 15 October aboard a collier. In 1681 about two hundred Sussex Quakers left to join William Penn's colony. By the later 18th century Brighton, Hastings and Worthing were turning this exposed coast into fashionable resorts.
zh:
萨塞克斯意为南撒克逊人的土地，地处汉普郡与肯特之间的海峡沿岸，沿海平原背后是林木茂密的威尔德。1066年9月，诺曼底的威廉在佩文西登陆；10月14日，哈罗德·戈德温森在黑斯廷斯战死。威廉在战场上修建巴特尔修道院，主祭坛正标着哈罗德倒下的地点；1094年教堂祝圣时，征服者的佩剑和加冕礼服被陈放在祭坛上。诺曼人把全郡划为一个个设防辖区，在阿伦德尔、刘易斯、佩文西和黑斯廷斯筑起城堡。1264年，西蒙·德·孟福尔在刘易斯俘获了后来的爱德华一世。百年战争期间，法国袭掠者焚毁黑斯廷斯、拉伊和温奇尔西；1385年，爱德华·达林格里奇爵士经理查二世许可修筑环水的博丁安城堡，防卫之外也为炫耀。黑死病夺去郡里约半数人口后，大量生计转入威尔德，当地的木材、铁器、布匹和玻璃帮萨塞克斯恢复过来。1444年，这是一处天主教海岸前沿，由城堡和五港城镇把守。

1450年，萨塞克斯人参加杰克·凯德起义，当地传说把凯德之死系于希思菲尔德附近。1496年，威尔德第一座高炉自低地国家引入，佛兰德工匠和后来的胡格诺工匠在此炼铁，为王室的舰船和军队铸炮，铁炉烧的木炭也取自威尔德山林。宗教改革中，巴特尔修道院和刘易斯修道院于1538年被拆毁，奇切斯特的圣理查德圣龛也被捣毁；玛丽一世治下，郡内有四十一名新教徒被火刑处死。1642年，议会派在海沃兹希思击溃王党军，双方又争夺奇切斯特、阿伦德尔和威尔德的铁工场。1651年伍斯特战役后，查理二世被悬赏一千英镑追捕，在西部辗转六周，最后抵达后来改名布莱顿的渔村布赖特尔姆斯顿，于10月15日在肖勒姆登上一艘运煤船前往法国。1681年，约二百名萨塞克斯贵格会信徒出航，加入威廉·佩恩的殖民地。到18世纪后期，布莱顿、黑斯廷斯和沃辛把这段直面海峡的海岸经营成时髦的疗养地。

en:
Coventry grew up on the River Sherbourne around the Benedictine abbey that Leofric, Earl of Mercia, and his wife Godiva founded in 1043. The town's name attached to Godiva early: a story first written down in the thirteenth century says she rode naked through its streets, covered only by her long hair, to force Leofric to lower his taxes, and later versions added the tailor Tom who peeped and gave English the figure of Peeping Tom. By the thirteenth century Coventry was a cloth town, its woad-dyed 'Coventry blue' known across the country, and the craft guilds staged the Corpus Christi pageants whose songs included the Coventry Carol. Work on the city wall began around 1355 and ran for 175 years; when finished in 1530 it ran two and a quarter miles with twelve gatehouses, and contemporaries counted it among the wonders of later medieval England. By the early fifteenth century Coventry held perhaps 10,000 people, one of the four largest cities in the land. In 1444 it was the richest city in the Midlands, its merchants lending money to the crown.

Coventry became a county of itself in 1451, and between 1456 and 1459 Margaret of Anjou moved Henry VI's court and parliament there from an unsafe London; the 1459 assembly that condemned the Yorkist lords was remembered as the Parliament of Devils, and the city served for a while as the seat of Lancastrian government. In the Dissolution of 1539 to 1542 the priory cathedral was pulled down, the only English cathedral destroyed in those years. Coventry was a parliamentarian bastion in the Civil War and beat off Charles I's assault on its walls in August 1642; the cold shoulder the townsfolk gave the Scottish royalist prisoners held there in 1648 is the likely source of the phrase 'sent to Coventry'. After the Restoration Charles II had the walls slighted in 1662. The Coventry Canal arrived in 1769, and by the 1780s silk ribbon weaving employed some 10,000 people in the town and its neighbourhood, while watch and clock making made Coventry one of Britain's three chief centres of the trade.
zh:
考文垂在舍本河畔发展起来，城中是麦西亚伯爵利奥弗里克与妻子戈黛娃1043年捐资修建的本笃会修道院。这座城很早就和戈黛娃的名字连在一起：一个13世纪才见诸文字的故事说，她为逼丈夫减轻征税，以长发遮体、裸体骑马穿过街市，后世版本又添了一个偷看的裁缝汤姆，英语里「偷窥者汤姆」的说法就出自这里。到13世纪，考文垂已是呢绒之城，菘蓝染成的「考文垂蓝」行销全国；各行会在基督圣体节上演连环剧，《考文垂颂歌》就是剧中的曲目。城墙约1355年动工，修了175年，到1530年才完工，周长两又四分之一英里，开有十二座城门楼，时人把它列为中世纪晚期英格兰的奇景之一。15世纪初全城人口约有一万，是英格兰四大城市之一。1444年的考文垂是米德兰兹最富庶的城市，商人常向王室放贷。

1451年考文垂自成一郡。1456至1459年，安茹的玛格丽特因伦敦不再安全，把亨利六世的宫廷和议会迁到这里；1459年宣判约克派贵族罪名的那次议会被称作「恶魔议会」，该城一度是兰开斯特政府的驻地。1539至1542年的解散修院运动中，修道院座堂被拆毁，这是当时唯一被毁的英格兰主教座堂。内战中考文垂是议会派堡垒，1642年8月击退了查理一世亲自指挥的攻城；1648年被俘的苏格兰王党官兵关押在此，镇民对他们冷脸相向、拒不来往，据说「送他去考文垂」这句俗话就是这么来的。王政复辟后，查理二世于1662年下令拆毁城墙。考文垂运河1769年通航；到1780年代，丝绦织造在本镇及周边雇工约一万人，钟表制造也使考文垂成为英国三大钟表业中心之一。

en:
Devon is the bulge of the south-western peninsula between Exmoor, Dartmoor and the Channel, brought into Wessex when King Aethelstan fixed the Cornish border on the Tamar in 936. Dartmoor tin kept the shire its own stannary law, while wool, fishing and shipbuilding fed a string of southern creeks. Exeter remained the old bishop's city, but the rising harbour was Sutton on Sutton Pool. Breton raiders burned it in 1403, and in 1439 Parliament made it a borough under the name Plymouth, the first town charter issued by act of Parliament rather than by the king alone; a castle went up beside the pool before the century ended. In 1444 Catholic, English-speaking Devon lived by tin, wool and the sea lanes out of the Sound.

The sea made the shire famous. Francis Drake grew up in a Plymouth seafaring household, sailed round the world in the Golden Hind between 1577 and 1580, and was vice-admiral against the Armada in 1588, when the English fleet lay in Plymouth Sound; legend has him insisting on finishing a game of bowls on the Hoe above the town before he would put out. His cousin John Hawkins, born in Plymouth, ran slaves to the Spanish Indies and, as Treasurer of the Navy, rebuilt the queen's ships into the faster, more heavily gunned fleet the Armada met. The Mayflower carried the Pilgrims from the Sound to North America in 1620, and in the Civil War the town held out through a royalist blockade from 1642 to 1646, supplied only by sea. In 1688 William of Orange landed unopposed at Brixham on his way to the throne, and a royal dockyard opened on the Tamar two years later.
zh:
德文是西南半岛上凸出的一块，夹在埃克斯穆尔、达特穆尔和英吉利海峡之间；936年艾塞尔斯坦把与康沃尔的边界划在泰马河，这里就此并入威塞克斯。达特穆尔的锡矿让全郡奉行自己的锡矿法，羊毛、渔业和造船业则养着南岸一连串溪湾。埃克塞特仍是古老的主教之城，但兴起中的港口是萨顿池畔的萨顿：1403年布列塔尼袭掠者将它焚毁，1439年议会以普利茅斯之名把它设为自治市镇，这是第一份由议会立法而非国王单独颁发的市镇特许状；世纪末，池畔又建起城堡。1444年，信奉天主教、说英语的德文靠锡、羊毛和普利茅斯湾外的海路为生。

大海让这个郡出了名。弗朗西斯·德雷克在普利茅斯的海员家庭长大，1577年至1580年乘「金鹿」号环球一周，1588年以副舰队司令迎击无敌舰队，当时英国舰队正驻泊普利茅斯湾；相传他非要在城旁高地（the Hoe）打完一局草地滚球，才肯出战。他的表亲约翰·霍金斯生在普利茅斯，经营贩运奴隶到西属西印度的生意，又以海军财务官的身份把女王的战舰改造得更快、炮火更重，无敌舰队碰上的就是这支舰队。1620年，「五月花」号载着清教徒前辈移民从普利茅斯湾驶往北美；内战期间，王党从1642年到1646年封锁全城，普利茅斯全靠海路补给坚守。1688年，奥兰治的威廉在布里克瑟姆无人阻挡地登陆，随后登上王位；两年后，泰马河畔开设了王家船坞。

en:
Dorset is a maritime county of chalk downs and clay vales between the Isle of Purbeck and the Channel, the Durotriges' country before the Romans came. Medieval Dorset lived from downland sheep, the Purbeck marble quarried along the coast, and a chain of small harbours. At the mouth of the Wey, Weymouth and Melcombe Regis, two towns on opposite banks, haggled over wine and wool for two centuries. Melcombe kept the darker name: the Black Death first reached England there in 1348, and in 1433 the crown moved the wool staple to Poole because French raiders kept finding the exposed anchorage. Corfe Castle, the crown fortress on its mound in the Purbeck chalk ridge, guarded the roads between the harbours. In 1444 this Catholic, English-speaking shire lived by pasture, stone and cross-Channel shipping.

Henry VIII covered the roadstead with Sandsfoot and Portland castles, and Elizabeth I united the rival ports in 1571. Dorset's fiercest fighting was around Corfe, which Lady Mary Bankes held for the king through years of siege until a treacherous officer let the Parliamentarians inside in 1646; they blew the castle apart with gunpowder and left the ruin on the hill. Lyme Regis beat off a royalist siege of eight weeks in the same war, and in 1685 the Duke of Monmouth landed there to open the rebellion that ended at Sedgemoor. Portland's white limestone made the coast rich in another way. Inigo Jones brought the stone to London, and after the Great Fire of 1666 Christopher Wren, Member of Parliament for Weymouth, shipped six million tons of it to rebuild St Paul's and the burned city. At Lyme Regis too, in 1811, a twelve-year-old girl called Mary Anning dug the first recognised ichthyosaur from the Blue Lias cliffs; her finds filled the new London museums and drew the first geologists to the coast.
zh:
多塞特是珀贝克半岛与英吉利海峡之间的滨海郡，白垩丘陵和黏土谷地相间，罗马人到来前是杜罗特里吉人的土地。中世纪的多塞特靠丘陵牧羊、滨海开采的珀贝克大理石和一串小港为生。韦伊河口两岸的韦茅斯和梅尔科姆雷吉斯，为葡萄酒和羊毛生意相争了两百年。梅尔科姆留下的名声更为凶险：1348年黑死病首次从这里传入英格兰；1433年，由于法国袭掠者屡屡攻入毫无遮蔽的锚地，王室把羊毛市场迁往普尔。科夫城堡是王冠设在珀贝克白垩山脊高地上的要塞，扼守各港之间的道路。1444年，这个信奉天主教、说英语的郡靠牧场、石料和海峡航运为生。

亨利八世用桑兹富特堡和波特兰堡掩护锚地，伊丽莎白一世在1571年把两个相争的港口合为一体。多塞特最惨烈的战事围绕科夫展开：玛丽·班克斯夫人据堡为国王坚守数年，直到1646年一名变节军官把议会军放进堡内；议会军用火药拆毁城堡，只留下山丘上的残垣。同一场战争里，莱姆里吉斯击退了王党八周的围攻；1685年，蒙茅斯公爵在这里登陆起事，叛乱最后败于塞奇穆尔。波特兰的白色石灰岩让海岸以另一种方式致富：伊尼戈·琼斯把这种石料引入伦敦，1666年伦敦大火后，身为韦茅斯议员的克里斯托弗·雷恩运去六百万吨石料，重建圣保罗座堂和焚毁的城区。同样在莱姆里吉斯，1811年，十二岁的女孩玛丽·安宁从蓝里阿斯崖壁中挖出第一具被辨认出的鱼龙骨架；她的发现填满了伦敦的新博物馆，也把最早的一批地质学者吸引到这段海岸。

en:
Chester guards the lowest crossing of the Dee on the road into Wales. The Romans planted the legionary fortress of Deva Victrix here in the AD 70s, with walls and an amphitheatre, and Æthelflæd, Lady of the Mercians, refounded the burh in 907. After the Normans sacked the town in 1070 Hugh d'Avranches received the Earldom of Chester the next year and raised its castle; Cheshire became a marcher county palatine against Wales, and from 1237 the earldom went to the heir to the English throne. The harbour drew ships from Aquitaine, Spain and Ireland with wine and goods, and the town was known for furs. Its citizens also built the Rows, long first-floor galleries that ran above the four main streets behind shops and stalls, the only covered walks of their kind in Britain. Inland, Nantwich, Middlewich and Northwich boiled brine into salt, while Manchester to the east gathered Flemish wool and linen weavers. On the feast of Corpus Christi the guilds acted the Chester mystery cycle on pageant wagons. In 1444 this Catholic palatine province lived by the Dee trade, Cheshire salt, cheese and the eastern textile towns.

When the Benedictine abbey of St Werburgh was dissolved under Henry VIII its church became the cathedral of the new diocese and Chester was made a city in 1541; the mystery plays, the last cycle still performed in England, were stopped in 1578. The Cheshire gentry tried to keep the shire out of the civil wars with the Bunbury Agreement, but fighting reached it at Middlewich in 1643 and Chester became the King's last port. On 24 September 1645 the Royalists were beaten at Rowton Heath outside the walls while Charles I was inside the city; the wall tower from which he watched the fight is called King Charles' Tower, and after a long siege Chester surrendered on 3 February 1646. Rock salt was found again near Northwich in the 1670s. The industrial current then ran east: the Irwell and Mersey were made navigable, the Bridgewater Canal reached Manchester in 1761, Richard Arkwright opened Manchester's first cotton mill in 1780, and the Trent and Mersey Canal of 1777 carried Cheshire salt and cheese.
zh:
切斯特扼守迪河下游通往威尔士的渡口。罗马人在1世纪70年代建起军团要塞德瓦·维克特里斯，筑有城墙和圆形竞技场；907年，麦西亚女领主埃塞尔弗莱德重建这座堡镇。诺曼人1070年洗劫切斯特后，休·达夫朗什次年受封切斯特伯爵、修筑城堡，柴郡成为防备威尔士的巴拉丁边郡，1237年起伯爵衔归入英格兰王储名下。港口接待阿基坦、西班牙和爱尔兰来的商船，输入葡萄酒，切斯特也以毛皮生意闻名。市民还建起「廊街」：四条大街上方连绵不绝的二层有顶走廊，廊后开店设摊，这种有顶商廊在不列颠独此一处。内陆的楠特威奇、米德尔威奇和诺斯威奇煎煮卤水制盐，东边的曼彻斯特则聚来从事毛纺和麻纺的佛兰德织工。基督圣体节时，各行会在彩车上演出切斯特神秘剧连台戏。1444年，这个信天主教的巴拉丁省份靠迪河贸易、柴郡食盐、奶酪和东部纺织城镇为生。

圣韦尔伯格本笃会修道院在亨利八世治下被解散，教堂改为新教区的主教座堂，切斯特也在1541年正式设市；神秘剧连台戏是英格兰最后还在上演的一组，1578年终于停演。柴郡乡绅本想靠《本伯里协议》置身内战之外，但1643年战火烧到米德尔威奇，切斯特成了国王手里最后的港口。1645年9月24日，王军在城外罗顿荒原战败，查理一世当时就在城中；他观战的那座城墙塔楼名叫「查理王塔」，城市经长期围困后于1646年2月3日投降。17世纪70年代，诺斯威奇附近重新发现岩盐。工业的潮流此后转向东部：厄韦尔河与默西河疏浚通航，布里奇沃特运河1761年通达曼彻斯特，理查·阿克莱特1780年开办曼彻斯特第一座棉纺厂，1777年的特伦特—默西运河则外运柴郡盐和奶酪。

en:
Leicester grew up where the Fosse Way forded the River Soar, on the site of the Roman town of Ratae; the wall of its public bath-house still stands at the Jewry Wall. The Vikings made it one of the Five Boroughs of the Danelaw, and after the Norman Conquest the earldom came to Simon de Montfort, who ran his revolt against Henry III from the castle before his death at Evesham in 1265. His lands passed to the House of Lancaster: John of Gaunt kept a household at Leicester and died there in 1399, the year his son took the crown as Henry IV, and parliaments met at the castle in 1414 and 1450. In 1444 Leicester was a firmly Lancastrian crown town on the Midlands roads, living by its Saturday market and the wool and cloth trade of the Soar valley.

In August 1485 Richard III marched out from Leicester to Bosworth Field, and after his death there his body was brought back to the town and buried at Greyfriars. Other court figures ended their stories in Leicester: Cardinal Wolsey, on his way south to the Tower under arrest for treason, died at Leicester Abbey on 29 November 1530, and Lady Jane Grey, queen for nine days in 1553, had been born at Bradgate Park in the Charnwood hills about 1536; Elizabeth I gave the earldom of Leicester to her favourite Robert Dudley. Puritan preaching won the town to Parliament, and on 30 May 1645 Charles I and Prince Rupert stormed it with about 10,000 men. Some 2,000 defenders held out for a day, after which Rupert's cavalry sacked the streets and carried off 140 wagon-loads of plunder to the royalist garrison at Newark. Parliament retook Leicester on 18 June, four days after Naseby.
zh:
莱斯特的前身是罗马大道福斯路在索尔河的渡口上发展起来的城镇拉塔埃，罗马公共浴室的残墙立在犹太墙遗址。维京人把它列为丹法区五镇之一；诺曼征服后，伯爵封号落到西蒙·德·孟福尔手中，他以莱斯特城堡为大本营反抗亨利三世，1265年战死于伊夫舍姆。他的领地转入兰开斯特家族：冈特的约翰长期在莱斯特起居，1399年卒于城堡中，同年其子即位为亨利四世；议会也曾于1414年和1450年在城堡召开。1444年的莱斯特是米德兰兹道路上一座坚定效忠兰开斯特王室的城镇，靠周六集市和索尔河谷的羊毛、布匹生意为生。

1485年8月，理查三世从莱斯特出兵博斯沃思原野，战败身亡后遗体被运回城里，葬在格雷夫莱尔教堂。还有几位宫廷人物的故事在莱斯特收尾：1530年11月29日，被控叛国、押解伦敦塔途中的沃尔西枢机病死在莱斯特修道院；1553年做了九天女王的简·格雷，约1536年出生在查恩伍德林间的布拉德盖特庄园；伊丽莎白一世则把莱斯特伯爵封号赐给宠臣罗伯特·达德利。清教布道使全城倒向议会。1645年5月30日，查理一世与鲁珀特亲王率约一万人攻城，约两千名守军撑了一天，城破后鲁珀特的骑兵纵兵洗劫，把一百四十车赃物运往王党据守的纽瓦克。纳西比战役四天后，议会军于6月18日收复莱斯特。

en:
Ormond is the pasture country of the upper Nore, and Kilkenny is its capital, standing over a ford of the river in the old kingdom of Ossory. The Normans came with Strongbow and raised a castle by the crossing; William Marshal walled the borough, and the stone keep looked down on the English trading town of Hightown while the older Irish quarter, Irishtown, kept to the rise around St Canice's and its round tower. This was no quiet market town. In 1324 the bishop of Ossory tried the wealthy, four-times-widowed Alice Kyteler for witchcraft; she fled to England or Flanders, but her maidservant was flogged and burned at the stake, the first person recorded burned in Ireland on such a charge, and Kyteler's house still stands in the town. In 1366 the parliament of Ireland met in Kilkenny and passed the Statutes of Kilkenny, forbidding the colonists to speak Irish or follow Irish customs, without stopping either. James Butler, third earl of Ormond, bought the castle in 1391, and in 1444 his son the 'White Earl', a scholar and patron of Irish scribes, held the Butler lordship with its great cattle and wool wealth, while his long feud with the Talbots dragged the Dublin government into the quarrels of Ormond.

James I made Kilkenny a city in 1609. After the rising of 1641 it became the capital of Confederate Ireland: the Catholic General Assembly and Supreme Council sat in the castle from 1642, coining money, running a printing press and sending ambassadors to France, Spain and the papacy. Cromwell came in person and forced the garrison's surrender on 28 March 1650 after a six-day siege, his guns wrecking the castle's east wall. The Duke of Ormond rebuilt it as a modern chateau from 1661, and James II held court in the castle through the winter of 1689–90. Brewing made Kilkenny prosperous from the late seventeenth century, its ale later sold as Smithwick's.
zh:
奥蒙德是诺尔河上游的牧地，首镇基尔肯尼踞守河上渡口，旧属奥索里王国。诺曼人随「强弓」而来，在渡口旁筑起城堡；威廉·马修尔给集镇筑起城墙，石砌主堡俯瞰英裔商人聚居的「高镇」，爱尔兰人旧城「爱尔兰镇」则守在圣卡尼斯座堂和圆塔所在的高地上。这座集镇并不平静。1324年，奥索里主教以巫术罪名审判四度丧夫的富孀爱丽丝·吉蒂勒，她逃去了英格兰或佛兰德，女仆却受鞭刑后被烧死在火刑柱上，是爱尔兰见于记载的第一个以此罪名被焚的人。1366年，爱尔兰议会在基尔肯尼通过《基尔肯尼法令》，禁止殖民者说爱尔兰语、遵从爱尔兰风俗，两样都没禁住。第三代奥蒙德伯爵詹姆斯·巴特勒1391年买下城堡；1444年，他的儿子、学者兼爱尔兰抄写人赞助者「白伯爵」执掌巴特勒家的领地，拥有大群牲畜和大宗羊毛收入，他与塔尔博特家的多年世仇还把都柏林政权卷进奥蒙德的纷争。

1609年，詹姆斯一世将基尔肯尼升格为市。1641年起义后，这里成为爱尔兰邦联的都城：1642年起，天主教徒的全体大会和最高委员会在城堡中议事，自行铸币、开设印刷所，并向法国、西班牙和教宗派遣使节。克伦威尔亲至，围城六天，于1650年3月28日迫使守军投降，炮火轰毁了城堡东墙。奥蒙德公爵1661年起把城堡改建为新式宅邸；1689至1690年冬天，詹姆斯二世在城堡中驻跸理政。从17世纪末起，酿酒业让基尔肯尼富庶起来，所产麦酒后来得名史密斯威克。

en:
Desmond is the Atlantic south-western corner of Ireland: the Dingle and Iveragh peninsulas and the Killarney lakes, the part of the old kingdom that never submitted to the Normans. When Munster was split in 1118 Tadhg Mac Carthaigh became the first king of Desmond; the Fitzgeralds overran its eastern half as earls of Desmond, but Fínghin Mac Carthaigh's victory at Callann in 1261 kept the Kerry country Gaelic under the MacCarthy Mór and his O'Sullivan and O'Donoghue clans. Its door to the sea was Dingle, which by the thirteenth century shipped more goods than Limerick, sending out fish and hides for the wines of France and Spain. On an island in Lough Leane the monks of Innisfallen, founded in 640, kept the annals of Munster. In 1444 Donal MacCarthy Mór ruled these glens and peninsulas while the Fitzgerald earls held the plains to the east.

Donal MacCarthy Mór founded the Franciscan friary of Muckross by the Killarney lakes. In July 1579 James FitzMaurice FitzGerald landed at Dingle to raise the Second Desmond Rebellion, and in November 1580 the Spanish and Italian papal troops who had come to his aid were cornered at Smerwick and put to the sword after they surrendered. When the rebellion ended in 1583 Munster was opened to plantation and the last monks of Innisfallen were driven from their island. After Kinsale the conquest reached the peninsulas: at Dunboy in June 1602 George Carew brought up to 5,000 men against 143 followers of Donal Cam O'Sullivan Beare, took the castle after eleven days and hanged most of those who survived, while Irish accounts put at around 300 the Gaelic Irish, many of them civilians, killed by his men on nearby Dursey Island; O'Sullivan led his remaining people north to Leitrim. Lord Broghill scattered a Confederate force at Macroom on 10 May 1650, and in 1652 Ross Castle on Lough Leane surrendered to Ludlow only after cannon were brought in by water, with Muckross burned soon afterwards. From the 1750s the fourth Viscount Kenmare drew travellers to the lakes and ruins, making Killarney Ireland's first celebrated resort.
zh:
德斯蒙德在爱尔兰的大西洋西南端，由丁格尔、伊弗拉两半岛和基拉尼湖群组成，是旧德斯蒙德王国从未臣服于诺曼人的那一部分。1118年芒斯特分裂，泰格·麦卡锡成为第一代德斯蒙德国王；菲茨杰拉德家以德斯蒙德伯爵之名吞并了王国东半部，但菲因·麦卡锡1261年在卡伦取胜，使凯里的山湖之地留在麦卡锡·莫尔及其奥沙利文、奥多诺霍诸氏族手中。丁格尔是这里通往海上的港口：早在13世纪，它吞吐的货物已比利默里克还多，运出鱼和兽皮，换回法兰西和西班牙的葡萄酒。利恩湖的因尼斯法伦岛上，建于640年的修道院修士世代编修芒斯特编年史。1444年，多纳尔·麦卡锡·莫尔在湖山与半岛间统治这片山地，菲茨杰拉德伯爵们则盘踞东面的平原。

多纳尔·麦卡锡·莫尔在基拉尼湖畔创建方济各会的马克罗斯修道院。1579年7月，詹姆斯·菲茨莫里斯·菲茨杰拉德在丁格尔登陆，掀起第二次德斯蒙德叛乱；1580年11月，前来助战的西班牙、意大利籍教宗士兵在斯梅里克被围困，投降后被悉数处死。1583年叛乱平息，芒斯特开放为种植园，因尼斯法伦最后的修士也被逐离岛屿。金塞尔战役之后，兵锋抵达各半岛：1602年6月，乔治·卡鲁率多达五千人围攻邓博伊城堡，守军只有多纳尔·奥沙利文·比尔的一百四十三名部下，坚守十一天后城堡陷落，大部分生还者被绞死；据爱尔兰方面记载，卡鲁的部队还在附近一座海岛杀死约三百名盖尔爱尔兰人，其中多为平民，奥沙利文只得率残部北撤利特里姆。1650年5月10日，布罗希尔勋爵在麦克鲁姆击溃一支邦联军队；1652年，利恩湖畔的罗斯城堡直到英军经水路运来大炮才向勒德洛投降，马克罗斯修道院不久后被焚。从18世纪50年代起，第四代肯梅尔子爵招揽游人来看湖光与废墟，基拉尼成为爱尔兰第一个闻名的观光胜地。

en:
The Midlands run from the Pale's western edge to the Shannon, a country of pasture, bog and loughs crossed by the Esker Riada, the glacial ridge that carries the old east-west road down to the river. Where that road meets the Shannon, Saint Ciarán founded Clonmacnoise in 544; high kings of Tara and Connacht were buried there, its monks produced the Book of the Dun Cow, and the carved Cross of the Scriptures marks the ruins. By the thirteenth century the monastery had lost people and trade to Athlone a few miles downstream. Athlone's ford and bridge carried the road on into Connacht, and John de Gray's twelve-sided stone castle of 1210 guarded the crossing. The Normans never settled the whole region: the O'Farrells recovered Annaly and built up Longford, the O'Mores held Laois, the O'Conor Falys ruled Uí Failghe, and Edward Bruce sacked Granard in 1315. In 1444 these Catholic cattle lands were a patchwork of Gaelic lordships and Gaelicised marches, with only the eastern approaches firmly tied to the Pale.

The Tudors redrew the midlands by force. Westmeath was split from Meath in 1543, an English fort went up in Laois in 1548, and Mary I's act of 1556 created Queen's County and King's County for plantation on O'More and O'Conor land; the Athlone garrison sacked what remained of Clonmacnoise in 1552. Annaly became Longford county in 1564 and was planted in 1620. Athlone stayed the Shannon bridgehead through every seventeenth-century war: Confederate troops held it until Charles Coote took it late in 1650, Richard Grace's Jacobites beat off an attack by ten thousand men in 1690, and in 1691 Ginkel's Williamite army stormed the town, broke the bridge defences and left almost two thousand defenders dead inside the walls. The Cromwellian plantations of the 1650s moved most of the land to new owners, and Huguenot refugees made Portarlington a French Protestant town. On 8 September 1798 Cornwallis defeated Humbert's Franco-Irish army at Ballinamuck and ended the French landing of the rebellion year.
zh:
中爱尔兰从佩尔西缘延伸到香农河，是一片牧场、沼泽与湖泊之地；冰碛垄脊埃斯克·里亚达横贯其间，古老的东西大道沿这条垄脊通往河边。大道与香农河交汇处，圣徒西亚兰（Ciarán）于544年建立克朗麦克诺伊斯修道院，塔拉与康诺特的至高王多葬于此，修道僧在此写下《褐牛之书》，刻满纹饰的圣经十字立在遗址间。到13世纪，修道院的人口和生意已被下游不远的阿斯隆夺走。阿斯隆的渡口和桥梁把大道继续引向康诺特，约翰·德·格雷1210年修筑的十二面石堡扼守渡口。诺曼人始终没能占住整片地区：奥法雷尔家族收复安纳利、发展朗福德，奥莫尔家族据有莱伊什，奥康纳·法利家族统治奥法利故地，爱德华·布鲁斯又在1315年洗劫格拉纳德。1444年，这片天主教畜牧地带是盖尔领地与盖尔化边区交错的地方，只有通往东部的道路牢牢系于佩尔。

都铎王朝以武力重划中爱尔兰。1543年韦斯特米斯从米斯分出，1548年英军在莱伊什筑起堡垒，1556年玛丽一世的法案设立女王郡和国王郡，在奥莫尔与奥康纳家族的土地上推行种植；1552年，阿斯隆驻军又把残存的克朗麦克诺伊斯洗劫一空。安纳利1564年成为朗福德郡，1620年接受种植。整个17世纪的战争里，阿斯隆都是香农河上的桥头堡：爱尔兰邦联军队据守到1650年末，被查尔斯·库特攻占；1690年理查德·格雷斯的詹姆斯党守军击退一万人的进攻；1691年，威廉派大军强攻破城，摧毁桥防，城墙内陈尸近两千。1650年代的克伦威尔种植把大部分土地转给新主人，胡格诺难民把波塔灵顿建成一座法国新教徒城镇。1798年9月8日，康沃利斯在巴利纳马克击败亨伯特的法爱联军，为起义之年的法国登陆画上句号。

en:
Donegal, Dun na nGall, the 'fort of the foreigners', sits where the River Eske runs into Donegal Bay beneath the Blue Stack Mountains, on the western edge of Ulster. From the fifteenth century it was the seat of the O'Donnells, kings of Tyrconnell, Irish Tir Chonaill, the 'land of Conall', formed from the breakup of the old kingdom of Ailech. The O'Donnells and the O'Neills of Tyrone were kinsmen and permanent rivals for mastery of the north. In 1444 this Catholic, Irish-speaking coast belonged to the O'Donnell lordship, which took cattle tribute from the hills and shipped fish and hides out of the bay. Hugh Roe O'Donnell built the tower house on the Eske in the 1460s and, with his wife Nuala, founded a Franciscan friary beside the water in 1474; a century later the Lord Deputy Henry Sidney called it the greatest fortress he had seen in Irish hands.

The castle's story belongs above all to Red Hugh O'Donnell. In 1587 government agents had him kidnapped aboard a wine ship at Rathmullan and locked in Dublin Castle; he escaped four years later and was inaugurated chief at Kilmacrennan. With his father-in-law Hugh O'Neill he led the Irish lords of the Nine Years' War, raiding into Connacht and destroying an English army at Curlew Pass. In 1601 he besieged a Crown garrison in Donegal itself, commanded by his cousin Niall Garve O'Donnell, who had defected to the English. The abbey was wrecked when its powder store exploded, and Red Hugh broke off the siege for the march to Kinsale. After the defeat there he sailed to Spain to fetch reinforcements and died of fever at Simancas in 1602, aged twenty-nine. The northern lords sailed into exile from Rathmullan in 1607, and the Crown granted the castle to Captain Basil Brooke, who rebuilt it in Jacobean style and laid out the Diamond. The friars driven from the ruined abbey kept their house at Bundrowes, where Micheal O Cleirigh and his companions compiled the Annals of the Four Masters between 1632 and 1636. The last Catholic field army of the north was cut to pieces at Scarrifholis in 1650.
zh:
多尼戈尔的爱尔兰语名意为「外国人的堡垒」，城镇坐落在埃斯克河流入多尼戈尔湾的河口，背后是蓝斯塔克山，地处阿尔斯特西缘。从15世纪起，这里是奥唐奈家族的驻地；他们统治的蒂康奈尔，爱尔兰语作「科纳尔之地」（Tir Chonaill），是从古老的阿莱克王国分裂出来的盖尔王国。奥唐奈家族与蒂龙的奥尼尔家族同宗，却又是争夺北爱尔兰霸权的世仇。1444年，这片讲爱尔兰语的天主教海岸属于奥唐奈领地：山乡缴纳牛只贡赋，鱼和皮革从港湾装船外运。休·罗·奥唐奈在1460年代建起埃斯克河畔的塔楼宅邸，又在1474年与妻子努阿拉在水边创建方济各会院；一个世纪后，爱尔兰总督亨利·西德尼称这座城堡是他见过的爱尔兰人手中最大的要塞。

城堡的故事多半属于「红休」奥唐奈。1587年，官府派人在拉斯穆兰把他骗上一艘酒船绑架，关进都柏林城堡；四年后他逃脱，在基尔麦克雷南就任首领。九年战争中，他与岳父休·奥尼尔联合各路爱尔兰领主，攻入康诺特，并在柯卢山口歼灭一支英军。1601年，他回师围攻据守多尼戈尔的王军，守军将领正是投奔英格兰的堂兄尼尔·加夫·奥唐奈。战中修道院的火药库爆炸，会院被毁，红休撤围南下，向金塞尔进军。金塞尔战败后他渡海赴西班牙求援，1602年在锡曼卡斯染病去世，年仅二十九岁。1607年，北方诸领主从拉斯穆兰渡海流亡，王室把城堡授予巴兹尔·布鲁克船长；他按詹姆斯风格重建城堡，并规划了钻石广场。修士们离开被毁的修道院，在本德罗威斯另立会院，米凯尔·奥克莱里和同伴于1632至1636年间在此编成《四大师年鉴》。1650年，北方最后一支天主教野战军队在斯卡里夫霍利斯被击溃。

en:
The Oversticht was the northern lordship of the prince-bishop of Utrecht beyond the IJssel: Salland, Twente and Vollenhove, with a looser claim over Drenthe. Three river towns carried its Hanse trade. Deventer, the oldest, was founded by the English missionary Lebuinus and held the common mint where the three IJssel towns struck their coin; its shippers brought dried cod and haddock from Norway, which gave Deventer people their 'Stokvis' nickname. Kampen commanded the passage from the Zuider Zee toward the Rhine, and Zwolle, which held staple rights, won a trading post in Scania after the Hansa's war with Denmark.
