色姆尔是旁遮普山邦中最靠南的一个，据有吉里河与亚穆纳河之间俯临锡尔欣德平原的山岭。从平焦尔进山的军队必须面对一连串山寨，低地农民则种植棉花，供应平原市集。早先的帕马尔都城锡尔毛尔-塔尔位于吉里河畔，1195年洪水毁城，拉杰乌加尔·昌德溺死。杰伊瑟尔默拉杰之子索巴趁乱建立巴蒂王朝，统治者以「普拉卡什」为号；旁遮普首领贾斯拉特的袭掠军后来也穿过这些河谷。1444年，印度教帕哈里拉杰仍靠群堡控制吉里河谷，马劳恩则是山道上方最坚固的据点。

1616年，卡拉姆·普拉卡什在旧堡下方修建纳亨并迁都于此。后来的统治者靠参加莫卧儿对加瓦尔的战事维持地位：曼达塔·普拉卡什派兵随沙贾汗的将领哈利勒-乌拉出征，索巴格·普拉卡什两度跟随奥朗则布，得到包括科塔哈在内的封地。色姆尔也在锡克历史中留下一笔：1685年，马特·普拉卡什收容古鲁·戈宾德·辛格。古鲁在保恩塔修筑工事，1688年率部在邦加尼击败卡赫卢尔和加瓦尔的山邦联军。1750年，基拉特·普拉卡什夺取平焦尔和纳拉因加尔，后来又迫使廓尔喀人接受以恒河为界；但1793年，达姆·普拉卡什在同冈格拉的桑萨尔·昌德单骑决斗时被杀。继承争端把廓尔喀人引入色姆尔，其大将阿马尔·辛格·塔帕把马劳恩建成主营。1815年，戴维·奥克特洛尼迫使马劳恩投降，随后立幼主法塔赫·普拉卡什为英国保护下的拉杰，同时保留了部分低地。

en:
Khairabad lies in the level Awadh country between the Gomti and the Ghaghra, about eighty kilometres north of Lucknow. It was once Masi Chitra, a Hindu pilgrimage place with a tank, the Maswasi Talao, whose waters were said to heal the sick. Local tradition names the Pasi chief Khaira as its founder: when Turkish armies raided Awadh he refused to submit and lost his kingdom, but the town kept his name. It passed to the Sharqi sultans of Jaunpur in 1394, and in 1444 it was a small market qasba of Mahmud Shah Sharqi, its weavers and bazaars quite overshadowed by the sultan's capital downstream.

The Mughals turned the qasba into a seat of learning. Rent-free grants under Babur and Akbar brought learned Muslim families to Khairabad, and in Akbar's administration it became the seat of one of the sarkars of the Awadh subah; its madrasas and Urdu poets kept its name alive through the seventeenth century. Pilgrims visited the tombs of the two Makhdoom saints, and the bazaars dealt in Kashmir shawls, Assamese elephants and jewels brought from Birmingham, while the East India Company shipped out the handwoven cloth made here and in Dariyabagh. Under the nawabs Khairabad was a faujdar's seat and then one of Asaf-ud-Daula's chaklas, though the posting was counted an undistinguished one. In the early 1800s the Nawab of Awadh resumed the old rent-free grants, and his flag still flew over the town in 1821.
zh:
凯拉巴德位于戈默蒂河与加格拉河之间平坦的阿瓦德原野，勒克瑙以北约八十公里。这里旧名马西奇特罗，是印度教朝圣地，有一座叫马斯瓦西池的水塘，据说池水能治病。本地传说以帕斯首领凯拉为建城者：突厥军队袭掠阿瓦德时他拒绝臣服，战败亡国，城镇却留下了他的名字。1394年它归入章普尔的沙尔基苏丹国；1444年，这里是马哈茂德沙·沙尔基治下的一座小集镇（qasba），织工和集市的声势远不及苏丹下游的都城。

莫卧儿时代，这座集镇成了学问之地。巴布尔和阿克巴时期的免租赐地把穆斯林学人之家吸引到凯拉巴德，阿克巴的行政区划又把它定为阿瓦德苏巴下辖一个萨尔卡尔的治所；经学院和乌尔都语诗人让它的声名维持到17世纪。香客拜谒两位马克杜姆圣徒之墓，集市上交易着克什米尔披巾、阿萨姆大象，甚至伯明翰运来的珠宝，东印度公司则把这里和达里亚巴格织造的土布收购出口。纳瓦卜时代，凯拉巴德先是统兵官（faujdar）的驻地，后被阿萨夫·乌德·道拉划为一个查克拉（chakla），只是这个职任被认为无足轻重。19世纪初，阿瓦德纳瓦卜收回了旧日的免租赐地；1821年，城头飘扬的仍是他的旗帜。

en:
The Feyzabad country lies on the lower Saryu east of Lucknow, and its old heart is Ayodhya, the Saketa of ancient times, one of the chief cities of Kosala, known to Buddhist and Jain travellers. The Gahadavala kings of the eleventh century filled it with Vishnu shrines, and in 1226 the Turks made it the seat of their new province of Awadh; Muslim writers found the town half deserted, and Hindu pilgrims were tolerated but taxed. In 1394 it passed with the province to the Sharqi sultans of Jaunpur, and in 1444 the governor of Awadh still kept his headquarters in the old fort there under Mahmud Shah Sharqi, while pilgrims bathed at the river tirtha. The town of Faizabad did not yet exist.

The Sharqi kingdom went down to the Lodi Afghans after 1478 and the country passed to the Mughals in 1526; in 1528-29 Mir Baqi, a commander of Babur, built at Ayodhya the mosque later called the Babri Masjid. Ayodhya remained the provincial seat until 1730, when Saadat Khan Burhan-ul-Mulk built a hunting lodge four miles to the west and laid gardens around it, and under his successor Safdar Jang the new town took the name Faizabad. After his defeat at Buxar in 1764, Shuja-ud-Daula withdrew here, fortified the place and built a capital of palaces, treasury and arsenal. He died early in 1775 and was buried in the Gulab Bari, and within the year his son Asaf-ud-Daula had moved the court to Lucknow. Faizabad then became the town of the dowager begams: Shuja's widow Bahu Begum and the older Nawab Begam kept small courts in the Moti Mahal, and their treatment at the Company's hands became one of the charges brought against Warren Hastings. Bahu Begum died in 1816 and was laid in a marble maqbara built by Darab Ali Khan for three lakh rupees, counted among the finest tombs in Awadh; after her death the town decayed further.
zh:
法扎巴德这片地方位于勒克瑙以东的萨拉尤河下游，古老的核心是阿约提亚，即古时的萨羯陀，曾是拘萨罗的首要城市之一，为佛教和耆那教行旅所知。11世纪的加哈达瓦拉诸王在城中修建了许多毗湿奴神庙；1226年，突厥人把新设阿瓦德省的治所放在这里，穆斯林史家笔下的城镇近乎半废，印度教朝圣虽被容忍却要课税。1394年，它随全省归入章普尔的沙尔基苏丹国；1444年，马哈茂德沙·沙尔基治下的阿瓦德长官仍把官署设在旧城，旧堡里驻扎着苏丹的骑兵，朝圣者在河边的圣渡沐浴。那时还没有法扎巴德这座城。

1478年后，沙尔基王国亡于洛迪阿富汗人，1526年这片土地转入莫卧儿之手；1528至1529年，巴布尔的将领米尔·巴基在阿约提亚修建了后来称为巴布里清真寺的礼拜寺。阿约提亚作为省治延续到1730年：这一年，萨阿达特汗·布尔汉·穆勒克在城西四英里处建起一座猎舍，周围辟出园林，到继任者萨夫达尔·姜格时，新城得名法扎巴德。1764年布克萨尔战败后，舒贾·乌德·道拉退居于此，加固城防，建起宫殿、国库与兵工厂齐备的都城。他1775年初去世，葬入古拉巴里陵园；不出一年，其子阿萨夫·乌德·道拉已把宫廷迁往勒克瑙。法扎巴德此后成为寡居太后们的城镇：舒贾的遗孀巴胡·贝古姆和更长一辈的纳瓦卜贝古姆在莫蒂宫各自维持小朝廷，东印度公司对待两位太后的方式后来成为弹劾沃伦·黑斯廷斯的罪状之一。巴胡·贝古姆1816年去世，葬入达拉卜·阿里汗耗资三十万卢比修建的大理石陵园，这座墓被视为阿瓦德最精美的陵墓之一；她死后，法扎巴德进一步衰败。

en:
Kora (Kora Jahanabad) stands in the Lower Doab between the Ganga and the Yamuna, level farming country on the old road from Delhi to Bihar. After the Muslim conquest the region was governed from nearby Kara, seat of one of the great iqtas of the Delhi sultans. The eunuch Malik Sarwar, sent against rebels in these lands, was granted the country from Kannauj to Bihar and from it founded the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur. Through most of the fifteenth century Kora followed the Sharqi court, its villages held by Bachgoti Rajput landholders. In 1444 it is the western march of Jaunpur, watched from the forts at Kara and Kora.

The Lodis won the country back for Delhi, and at the Mughal coming it was held independently by Jalal Khan, brother of Ibrahim Lodi. Akbar's forces conquered Awadh in 1559, and in 1567 the rebel Ali Quli Khan Zaman was defeated and killed in this district. Kora became a sarkar of the new Allahabad subah, divided into three dasturs, as the Grand Trunk Road and the Allahabad fort pulled the region's trade east. The district's great Mughal battle was fought on 5 January 1659 at the tank of Khajwa, between the Ganga and the Yamuna a few miles from Kora. Shah Shuja, who had claimed the throne from Bengal, met the newly crowned Aurangzeb there and was beaten and driven east, and the throne was Aurangzeb's.

After 1707 the district changed hands among the Barha Sayyids, the Bangash Afghans of Farrukhabad, the Nawabs of Awadh and Maratha raiders, who sacked it in 1736. Bhagwant Singh of Asothar killed the faujdar of Kora and Kara and held out with Maratha help until Awadh brought him down. After Buxar the Company handed Kora to the Emperor Shah Alam II, and when the Marathas took the emperor and his lands into their keeping, it sold Kora back to Awadh in 1773 for fifty lakh rupees. Almas Khan governed it from Kora for the next twenty-eight years, until the Lower Doab was ceded to the Company in 1801.
zh:
戈拉（今科拉贾哈纳巴德）位于恒河与亚穆纳河之间的下河间地，地势平坦，旧德里通往比哈尔的大道穿境而过。穆斯林征服之后，这一地区由附近的卡拉统辖，那里是德里苏丹大伊克塔之一的治所。宦官马利克·萨尔瓦尔受命到这一带平叛，受封从卡瑙杰到比哈尔的土地，并以此为根基建立章普尔沙尔基王国。15世纪的大部分时间里，戈拉臣属沙尔基朝廷，村社土地握在巴赫戈特拉杰普特地主手中。1444年时，它是章普尔的西部边陲，由卡拉与戈拉的堡寨在此弹压。

洛迪王朝为德里收复此地，莫卧儿人初来时，割据自守的是易卜拉欣·洛迪之弟贾拉尔汗。阿克巴的军队1559年征服阿瓦德，1567年又在此地击败并击杀叛将阿里·库里汗·扎曼。戈拉成为新安拉阿巴德省下辖的萨卡尔，分为三个达斯图尔；大干道穿过这一地区，安拉阿巴德堡也把商旅重心向东拉去。1659年1月5日，距戈拉不远的卡杰瓦水塘爆发了这一带在莫卧儿时代最大的会战，战场在恒河与亚穆纳河之间。在孟加拉自行称帝的沙·舒贾在此迎战刚刚加冕的奥朗则布，战败东逃，皇位就此落入奥朗则布之手。

1707年以后，此地在巴尔哈的赛义德家族、法鲁卡巴德的班加什阿富汗人、阿瓦德纳瓦布和马拉塔袭掠者之间几度易手，1736年遭马拉塔人洗劫。阿斯塔尔的巴格万特·辛格袭杀戈拉与卡拉的军政长官，借马拉塔之力割据，最终被阿瓦德平定。布克萨尔之战后，东印度公司把戈拉交给皇帝沙·阿拉姆二世；马拉塔人挟皇帝、占其地之后，公司又在1773年以五百万卢比的代价把戈拉卖回阿瓦德。此后二十八年，阿尔马斯汗以戈拉为治所统辖此地，直到1801年下河间地割让给东印度公司。

en:
Kannauj stands on a bluff above the Ganges at the eastern edge of the Doab, the granary between the Ganges and Jumna. Ancient Kanyakubja was already the chief city of the Panchalas, and under Harsha, who reigned from 606 to 647, it was the greatest city in northern India; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang found it crowded with Buddhist monasteries. For three centuries afterwards the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas fought over the city, until the Pratiharas kept it as their imperial capital. Mahmud of Ghazni sacked it in 1018, the Gahadavala kings raised it again, and in 1193 Muhammad of Ghor killed their raja Jayachandra at Chandawar, after which Iltutmish drew it into the Delhi sultanate. With Delhi enfeebled after Timur, the Sharqi sultans of Jaunpur pushed west to the Ganges: in 1444 Kannauj is their western fortress, a frontier garrison against the Lodis and a grain mart where the Doab harvest is gathered.

The fortress lay on the fighting edge of the Sharqi decline: Sultan Mahmud's siege of Delhi failed against Bahlul Lodi in 1452, and Bahlul's advance swallowed the Jaunpur frontier within a generation, the last Sharqi inscription in the city dating to 1476. On 17 May 1540 Sher Shah Suri routed Humayun at the Battle of Kannauj and seized the Mughal throne. Under the restored Mughals it became the seat of the sarkar of Kannauj in the subah of Agra; its parganas paid grain into the treasury while its perfumers, heirs to a craft centuries old, distilled flower attars and rose water for the markets of the empire, and Kannauj was known as the perfume capital of India. With Mughal power collapsing the city passed to the Nawabs of Awadh, and in 1801 it was ceded with the Lower Doab to the East India Company.
zh:
卡瑙杰耸峙在恒河畔一处高崖上，地处恒河与亚穆纳河之间多阿布大粮仓的东缘。古称羯若鞠阇，早为般阇罗人的首邑；606至647年戒日王在位时，它是北印度最伟大的城市，中国求法僧玄奘到此，见城中佛寺林立。此后三百年间，波罗提诃罗、波罗与拉喜特拉库塔三朝在此反复争夺，最后波罗提诃罗人留据此城，以之为帝国之都。1018年伽色尼的马哈茂德洗劫卡瑙杰，伽诃达瓦罗诸王使它复兴；1193年古尔的穆罕默德在昌达瓦尔击杀其王阇耶旃陀罗，此后伊勒杜迷失把它纳入德里苏丹国。帖木儿之后德里衰弱，章普尔的沙尔基苏丹向西推进到恒河；1444年，卡瑙杰是他们的西陲要塞，既是防洛迪人的边境驻军重镇，也是汇集多阿布粮产的商埠。

这座要塞正处在沙尔基王朝衰亡的战线上：1452年马哈茂德沙阿围攻德里，败于巴赫鲁尔·洛迪；不出一代人，巴赫鲁尔的推进便吞并了章普尔边疆，城中最晚一方沙尔基铭文止于1476年。1540年5月17日，舍尔沙·苏尔在卡瑙杰之战击溃胡马雍，夺占莫卧儿皇位。莫卧儿统治恢复后，此地成为阿格拉苏巴下辖卡瑙杰萨尔卡尔的治所，各帕尔加纳向国库输纳米赋，城中香匠则承袭数百年的手艺，蒸馏花卉精油和玫瑰香水供应帝国各市场，卡瑙杰也以印度的香水之都闻名。莫卧儿政权瓦解后，此城转归奥德的纳瓦布；1801年随下多阿布割让给东印度公司。

en:
Sambhal is a market town on the western edge of Katehar, on the level road between Delhi, Agra and the Rohilkhand plain. Hindu tradition identifies it with Shambhala, where Vishnu's future tenth avatar, Kalki, is to be born, and Tibetan Buddhists borrowed the same name for the hidden kingdom beyond the Himalayas. Ibn Battuta writes that the town drew pilgrims from Tibet in his day, and that the last Yuan emperor of China sent an embassy to Muhammad bin Tughluq asking leave to rebuild its Buddhist temple. Under the Delhi sultans it was a Muslim military centre, and Ibrahim Shah Sharqi of Jaunpur established his authority there in 1407. In 1444, therefore, Sambhal is a north-western garrison of Mahmud Shah Sharqi's kingdom, hard against the contested frontier with Delhi.

When the Lodis overcame the Sharqis, Bahlul Lodi granted Sambhal to his son Sikandar, who kept his court there for four years after becoming sultan. Babur's victory at Panipat in 1526 carried the town into the Mughal domains; he gave the jagir to Humayun and is credited with building the town's mosque, and after Babur's death it passed to Askari Mirza and later to Sher Shah Suri's son-in-law Mubariz Khan. The town prospered under Akbar, but when Shah Jahan held the district its local headquarters was moved to Moradabad. As part of Rohilkhand it was drawn into the Rohilla Wars, passed to Awadh after 1774 and was ceded to the East India Company in 1801.
zh:
森珀尔是卡特哈尔西缘的集镇，地处德里、阿格拉与罗希尔坎德平原之间的坦途。印度教传统把它认作香巴拉，即毗湿奴未来的第十化身迦乐季的降生地，藏传佛教也借用了这个名字，指喜马拉雅山外的隐秘王国。据伊本·白图泰记载，当时这里吸引西藏香客，元朝末代皇帝还遣使觐见穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克，请求获准重建城中的佛寺。德里苏丹时代，这里是穆斯林军事据点；章普尔的易卜拉欣·沙·沙尔基1407年在此建立统治。因此1444年时，森珀尔是马哈茂德·沙·沙尔基王国西北的驻军要地，紧挨着与德里相争的边界。

洛迪王朝击败沙尔基王朝后，巴赫鲁尔·洛迪把森珀尔封给儿子锡坎达尔；锡坎达尔称苏丹后曾在此驻跸四年。1526年巴布尔在帕尼帕特获胜，森珀尔并入莫卧儿；他把这块封地授予胡马雍，相传还在城中修建了清真寺，巴布尔死后森珀尔先归阿斯卡里·米尔扎，后转封谢尔沙·苏利的女婿穆巴里兹汗。阿克巴时代城镇富庶，到沙贾汗掌有此地时，地方治所被迁往莫拉达巴德。作为罗希尔坎德的一部分，它被卷入罗希拉战争，1774年后归属阿瓦德，1801年割让给东印度公司。

en:
Bareily, now Bareilly, stands on the Ramganga in the Katehar plain. The older power in these parts was Ahichchhatra, capital of northern Panchala, whose mounds and ruins lie near Aonla; they have yielded coins and terracotta figures from the centuries before the Delhi sultans. By the fifteenth century the countryside was held by Katehriya Rajput clans within reach of the Sharqi sultans of Jaunpur. In 1444 there is no town called Bareilly yet: this is cotton-growing frontier country of Mahmud Shah Sharqi, governed through local chiefs and watched from the garrisons at Budaun and Sambhal.

The settlement of Bans-Bareli was founded in 1537 by the Katehriya chief Jagat Singh, who named it after his sons Bansaldev and Bareldev, and the historian Bada'uni already mentions it. Mughal rule reached the district in 1569, and Mukrand Rai laid out the new town of Bareilly in 1657, the year before it became the governor's seat for Budaun. Mughal governors had planted Pashtun soldiers in Katehar to overawe the Rajput clans, and from 1719 Ali Muhammad Khan made Bareilly the capital of the Rohilla state. Its best-known chief, Hafiz Rahmat Khan, fought at the Third Battle of Panipat and in 1772 beat off a Maratha invasion with Awadh's help; when he refused the price Awadh demanded for that help, the nawab and the East India Company marched together and killed him at Miranpur Katra in 1774. The district passed to Awadh and then to the Company in 1801, which built a military station south of the town in 1811 and a fort there in 1816.
zh:
婆雷利（今译巴雷利）位于卡特哈尔平原的兰甘加河畔。这一带早先的权力中心是阿希查特罗，北般阇罗的都城，其土丘遗址在奥恩拉附近，出土过德里苏丹时代之前数百年的钱币和赤陶像。15世纪，乡野由卡特赫里亚拉杰普特诸氏族掌握，处在章普尔沙尔基苏丹的势力范围内。1444年还没有巴雷利这座城：这里是马哈茂德·沙·沙尔基出产棉花的边地，由本地首领治理，布道恩和森珀尔的驻军负责监视。

1537年，卡特赫里亚首领贾格特·辛格建立班斯-巴雷利，以两个儿子班萨尔代夫、巴雷尔代夫的名字合称命名，史家拜达欧尼的著作已提到此地。莫卧儿势力1569年到达这一地区；1657年穆克兰德·莱营建巴雷利新城，次年这里成为布道恩总督的驻地。莫卧儿历代总督把普什图士兵安置在卡特哈尔，以震慑拉杰普特诸氏族；1719年起，阿里·穆罕默德汗以巴雷利为罗希拉国家的都城。最知名的罗希拉首领哈菲兹·拉赫马特汗曾参加第三次帕尼帕特战役，1772年借阿瓦德之助击退马拉塔入侵；他拒绝支付阿瓦德索要的酬金后，纳瓦布与东印度公司联合进军，1774年将他攻杀于米兰布尔·卡特拉。该地区先归阿瓦德，1801年转交东印度公司；公司1811年在城南设立军站，1816年在那里筑堡。

en:
Bharatpur is the open grazing and farming plain east of the Mewat hills, in the marchland between Agra, Mathura and Delhi, where Hindu Jat clans kept large cattle herds and filled the village headmanships. In 1444 the country formed the eastern fringe of the Khanzada kingdom of Mewat, its Jat and Gujar peasants subjects of the Muslim Rajput court at Alwar. It had no towns or rulers of its own, and for two centuries its history was the doings of turbulent village zamindars on the Delhi frontier.

The Jat rising of 1669 turned those village headmen into kings. Gokula, a Jat zamindar of Tilpat, led the Mathura farmers against Aurangzeb's tax collectors and was captured and executed in 1670; Rajaram of Sinsini carried on the revolt, plundered Akbar's tomb at Sikandra, and fell in 1688, after which Aurangzeb granted Mathura as a faujdari to the Kachwaha raja of Amber. Churaman used the Mughal civil wars to make the Jat forts at Sinsini and Thun independent, and in 1722 Badan Singh founded a regular state with his capital at Deeg. His son Suraj Mal began the Lohagarh, the Iron Fort, in 1732 and founded the city of Bharatpur; at the height of his power, on 12 June 1761, he took Agra itself and melted down the silver doors of the Taj Mahal. In 1805 Lord Lake battered the Lohagarh for three months and four assaults failed; the defenders raised the Fateh Burj tower to mark the fight, and the siege ended by treaty.
zh:
婆罗多布尔是梅瓦特丘陵以东一片开阔的农牧平原，地处阿格拉、马图拉与德里之间的边疆地带，印度教贾特人在这里牧养大批牛群，各村头人也多由他们充任。1444年，这里是梅瓦特汗扎达王国的东缘，贾特与古贾尔农夫都是阿尔瓦尔穆斯林拉杰普特宫廷的属民；本地没有自己的城镇和君主，此后两百年，这片土地的历史就是德里边疆上一众不安分的村庄柴明达尔的活动。

1669年的贾特人起义把这些村庄头人送上了王位。蒂尔帕特的贾特地主戈库拉率领马图拉农民反抗奥朗则布的税吏，1670年被俘处死；辛西尼的拉贾拉姆接过反旗，洗劫锡坎德拉的阿克巴陵，1688年战死，奥朗则布随即将马图拉作为法吉达尔辖区封给安贝尔的卡奇瓦哈拉贾。丘拉曼乘莫卧儿内战，凭辛西尼和通两座堡垒使贾特人自立；1722年，巴丹·辛格正式建国，定都迪格。其子苏拉杰·马尔1732年动工修建洛哈加尔堡，意即「铁堡」，并建立婆罗多布尔城；权势最盛时，他在1761年6月12日攻克阿格拉，熔取泰姬陵的银门。1805年，莱克勋爵围攻洛哈加尔堡三个月，四次强攻均告失败；守军筑起法泰赫布尔吉塔纪念这场守御，围城最终以缔约收场。

en:
Bhilwara is the open grain plain east of the Aravallis, where routes from Mewar run toward Ajmer and Bundi. Bhil farmers gave the district its name, and local tradition mentions Bhiladi coins said to come from a mint here. The oldest part of Bhilwara grew around the Krishna temple called Bada Mandir in the mid-eleventh century. The military anchor of the plain was Mandalgarh, a hill fort first held by local Rajput chiefs and taken for Mewar by Rana Kshetra Singh in the fourteenth century. In 1444 the pargana answered to Maharana Kumbha and covered the north-eastern approach from Malwa.

Mahmud Khalji of Malwa twice stormed Mandalgarh in the mid-fifteenth century, and the garrison then changed repeatedly between Mewar, Malwa and later Mughal commanders. Bahadur Shah's Gujarat army crossed Bhilwara in 1534 on its march to Chittor, and Mandalgarh was sacked after it fell the next year. Akbar also used the plain as a military base: when he moved against Chittor in 1567, his army camped at Mandal. Around 1650 Shah Jahan granted Mandalgarh to Raja Roop Singh of Kishangarh, who began a palace there; Rana Raj Singh retook the fort in 1660. Aurangzeb's men seized the palace in 1680, and Rana Amar Singh recovered Mandalgarh in 1706. It then remained with Mewar.
zh:
皮尔瓦拉是阿拉瓦利山脉以东开阔的谷物平原，梅瓦尔通往阿杰梅尔和本迪的道路从这里穿过。比尔农民赋予地区名字，当地口传还提到名为「比拉迪」的钱币，说它们出自这里的铸币厂。皮尔瓦拉最早的街区在11世纪中叶围绕奎师那神庙巴达曼迪尔发展起来。平原上的军事支点是曼达尔加尔：这座山堡最初由本地拉杰普特首领掌握，14世纪被梅瓦尔的拉那·谢特拉·辛格夺取。1444年，这片帕尔加纳听命于马哈拉那·贡波，遮护梅瓦尔朝向马尔瓦的东北通道。

15世纪中叶，马尔瓦的马哈茂德·卡尔吉两次攻破曼达尔加尔，此后这座堡垒长期在梅瓦尔、马尔瓦和后来的莫卧儿将领之间换防。1534年，古吉拉特巴哈杜尔沙的军队穿过皮尔瓦拉开往奇托尔，曼达尔加尔于次年失陷并遭劫掠。阿克巴也把这片平原当作进兵基地：1567年攻打奇托尔时，他的军队在曼达尔镇扎营。约1650年，沙贾汗把曼达尔加尔封给基尚加尔的罗阇·鲁普·辛格，后者开始在堡中修建宫殿；拉那·拉杰·辛格1660年将其夺回。1680年，奥朗则布的军队占入宫城，拉那·阿马尔·辛格1706年收复堡垒，此后它属于梅瓦尔。

en:
Merta, called Medantaka in older records, lies on the open plain between Nagaur and Ajmer. Cattle herds, village carts and caravans used its flat ground, and the town supplied the surrounding parched country. A Pratihara chief of Mandore had once made it his seat, and Alauddin Khalji's conquests in the thirteenth century left a governor here. In 1444 Merta was held from Nagaur, while the Rathores of Mandore and the rising state of Marwar pressed close on its western side.

The town gave its name to the Mertiya Rathores after Rao Jodha of Marwar enfeoffed his son Rao Duda with the estate. Duda built the first palace, the Chaturbhuj temple and the Dudasar tank. His successor Rao Viramdeo fought at Khanwa in 1527, and Viramdeo's niece Mira Bai became the Bhakti poet whose hymns to Krishna spread through northern India. Rao Maldev of Marwar later seized Merta and raised the Malkot fort, although the town went briefly to Sher Shah after the Battle of Sammel in 1544 and then returned to Marwar. Viramdeo's son Jaimal, lord of Merta, commanded the Chittor garrison against Akbar and was killed there in 1568; Akbar afterwards divided Merta between Jaimal's sons Surtan Singh and Keshavdas. At the Battle of Merta in 1790, Mertiya horsemen charged Benoit de Boigne's trained battalions serving Mahadji Scindia and were nearly destroyed.
zh:
梅尔达古籍作梅丹塔卡，位于纳高尔与阿杰梅尔之间的开阔平原。牛群、村车和商队都利用这片平坦地面通行，城镇也为周围干旱地区供给货物。曼多尔的一名普拉蒂哈拉首领曾以此为治所，13世纪阿拉乌丁·卡尔吉征服后又派官员驻守。1444年，梅尔达在纳高尔治下，西面曼多尔的拉索尔人与新兴的马尔瓦尔已经逼近。

马尔瓦尔的拉奥·乔达把梅尔达封给儿子拉奥·杜达后，杜达的后裔便称梅尔蒂亚·拉索尔。杜达修建了最早的王府、查图尔布吉神庙和杜达萨尔水塘。继他统治的拉奥·维拉姆迪奥1527年参加坎瓦之战；维拉姆迪奥的侄女米拉拜是虔诚派诗人，献给黑天的赞歌传遍北印度。马尔瓦尔的拉奥·马尔德奥后来夺取梅尔达，修筑马尔科特堡。1544年萨梅尔之战后，此地短暂归舍尔沙所有，随后又回到马尔瓦尔手中。维拉姆迪奥之子、梅尔达领主贾伊马尔率奇托尔守军抵御阿克巴，1568年战死；阿克巴随后把梅尔达分给贾伊马尔的两个儿子苏尔坦辛格和凯沙夫达斯。1790年梅尔达之战，梅尔蒂亚骑兵向玛哈德吉·辛迪亚麾下贝努瓦·德布瓦涅训练的步兵营冲锋，几乎全军覆没。

en:
The flat country between the Indus and the Thar holds the ruins of al-Mansura, later also called Brahmanabad, the first capital founded by Muslims in South Asia. Arab armies under Muhammad ibn Qasim seized the region early in the eighth century, governors planted a garrison town, and under the Abbasids it grew into a metropolis said to outshine Multan and Debal. Its merchants dressed in the Baghdad fashion and shipped spices, textiles, ivory and mirrors to Baghdad. Its scholars included Abu Mashar Sindhi, an early compiler of hadith, and Abu Raja Sindhi, who in Baghdad translated Indian works of mathematics, astronomy and medicine into Arabic, and the town produced the first Sindhi translation of the Quran. An earthquake in 893 weakened the city, and Mahmud of Ghazni sacked it after the townsmen refused to open their gates; the Indus later shifted course, leaving the courtyard of its great mosque among the fields. In 1444 the district was farmland of the Samma rulers of Sindh, governed from their capital at Thatta.

The Sammas' best years came under Jam Nizamuddin II, who ruled from 1461 to 1508. Shah Beg Arghun overthrew the last Jam in 1519-1520, and after decades in which Arghun and Tarkhan princes contested lower Sindh, Mughal forces took the region in 1592. In 1713 Mir Shahdad Khan Talpur founded Shahdadpur beside the old ruins, and in 1783 the Talpurs overthrew the Kalhoras at the Battle of Halani and divided Sindh among their branches, which still held the Mansura country in 1821.
zh:
印度河与塔尔沙漠之间的平原上有阿拉伯古都曼苏拉的遗址，它在后世也叫布拉赫曼纳巴德，是穆斯林在南亚建立的第一座都城。8世纪初，穆罕默德·伊本·卡西姆率军夺取这一带，阿拉伯总督建起驻军城镇，到阿拔斯时代它发展成大都会，富庶据说超过北方的木尔坦和南方的德巴尔。当地商人一身巴格达装束，把香料、纺织品、象牙和镜子运往巴格达；学者中有早期汇编圣训的阿布·马沙尔·信迪，也有在巴格达把印度数学、天文、医学典籍译成阿拉伯文的阿布·拉贾·信迪，城里还完成了第一部信德语古兰经译本。893年的地震削弱了城市，加兹尼的马哈茂德又因市民拒不开门而纵兵洗劫；印度河后来改道，大清真寺的庭院便荒在田间。1444年，这一带是信德萨马王朝的农田，由王都特达统辖。

1461年至1508年贾姆·尼扎姆丁二世在位，是萨马王朝的全盛期。1519年至1520年，沙赫·贝格·阿尔浑推翻末代贾姆·菲鲁兹；阿尔浑与塔尔汗王公争夺下信德数十年后，莫卧儿军队于1592年攻取此地。1713年，米尔·沙达德·汗·塔尔普尔在古城遗址旁建起沙达德布尔；1783年，塔尔普尔人在哈拉尼战役推翻卡尔霍拉王朝，把信德分封给各支系，1821年曼苏拉一带仍在他们手中。

en: Nasirpur lies in the flat alluvial country between Mansura and the Thar approaches, its watered fields supporting a town long given over to weaving. Local tradition counts it among the chief cities of medieval Sindh with Thatta, Sehwan and Umarkot; an Arabic tradition dates its founding to 132 AH, when the governor Nasr ibn Muhammad al-Khuzai established it, and the town is said to have borne the older name of Mata Lui. In 1444 it was a Muslim textile town of the Samma kingdom. The Arghuns ended Samma rule there in 1523, Tarkhan lords followed, and Akbar's forces took lower Sindh in 1592. Under the Mughals Nasirpur was a sarkar of the Thatta province, and English merchants kept an office there and bought locally woven bafta cloth for export; old mosques, tombs and Sufi shrines faced with glazed tilework stood among the weavers' quarters. In the eighteenth century Kalhora rule gave way to the Talpur amirs.
zh: 纳西尔布尔位于曼苏拉与塔尔沙漠边缘之间平坦的冲积地带，良田环绕，城中世代以织造为业。当地传统把它与特达、塞赫万、欧迈尔果德并列为中世纪信德的主要城市；据阿拉伯文献的说法，此城由总督纳斯尔·本·穆罕默德·胡扎伊建于伊斯兰历132年，旧称马塔卢伊。1444年，它是萨姆马王国治下一座穆斯林纺织城镇。1523年阿尔洪人终结萨姆马统治，随后是塔尔汗首领，1592年阿克巴的军队夺取下信德。莫卧儿时期，纳西尔布尔是特达省的一个萨尔卡尔，英国商人在此开设商馆，收购当地织造的巴夫塔布外销；织工街区之间，矗立着古清真寺、陵墓和饰有琉璃砖的苏菲圣祠。十八世纪，卡尔霍拉人的统治又让位于塔尔普尔埃米尔。

en:
East of the Indus the land rises slowly out of the river plain into the Nara flats and the first dunes of the Thar, a country of wells, grazing herds and villages strung along the water. It was the open eastern march of upper Sindh, facing Jaisalmer and the desert track to Umarkot, where no strong town stood before the eighteenth century. In 1444 Sindhi Muslim herders pastured their flocks here for the Samma Jam at Thatta, and the district paid its dues in livestock rather than coin.

Rule over the march followed the dynasties of upper Sindh, Samma, Arghun and Tarkhan, until Jani Beg Tarkhan submitted to the Mughals in 1593 and governors took over, followed by the Kalhoras. The town that now names the province began with the Talpur Mirs, who overthrew the Kalhoras at the Battle of Halani in 1783 and divided Sindh among their chiefs. Mir Sohrab Khan took the upper country as his share, set his seat at Khairpur, and between 1785 and 1795 built Kot Diji on a ridge at the desert edge, twenty-five miles east of the river; the citadel was formally called Fort Ahmadabad, and its name means the Fort of the Daughter. In 1811 he handed the country to his eldest son, Mir Rustam Ali Khan.
zh:
印度河以东，地势从河滨平原缓缓抬升，进入纳拉低地和塔尔沙漠的头几道沙丘，地上散布着水井、牧群与依水而建的村庄。这里曾是上信德敞开的东部边陲，对着杰伊瑟尔梅尔和通往乌默科特的沙漠道，18世纪以前没有一座坚固的城镇。1444年，信德穆斯林牧民在此为特达的萨姆马贾姆放牧，这片地方缴纳的贡赋是牲畜，而不是钱币。

边陲的归属随上信德的王朝更替，萨姆马、阿尔浑、塔尔汗相继而过，1593年贾尼·贝克·塔尔汗归降莫卧儿后换为总督统治，此后又是卡尔霍拉家族。后来赋予本省名字的城镇是塔尔普尔人建立的：1783年他们在哈拉尼战役击败卡尔霍拉家族，把信德分给各米尔。米尔·索赫拉布汗分得北信德，驻帐海尔布尔，并在1785至1795年间于沙漠边缘、印度河以东25英里处的山脊上筑起科特迪吉堡；城堡正式名称为艾哈迈达巴德堡，科特迪吉的意思是「女儿之堡」。1811年，他把这片土地交给长子米尔·鲁斯塔姆·阿里汗。

en:
The Mallani country around Barmer covers the driest flank of the Thar, where the Luni's shallow channels and scattered wells decide where herds can graze. Cattle, camels and Marwari horses matter more than town trade here. At Kiradu, the old Kiratakupa, vassals of the Solanki kings built a group of Hindu temples between the eleventh and twelfth centuries; the Someshvara temple is the best preserved of the ruins, and an inscription of 1178 records repairs after a Turkic raid. Bahada Rao, a Paramara chief, founded Juna and called his hill settlement Bahadamer, the name that later became Barmer. The wider country took its name from Rawal Mallinath of Mehwanagar, born in 1358 and honoured with his wife Rupade as a folk saint in western Rajasthan. He defeated the army of Nizamuddin, governor of Malwa, in 1378, helped his nephew Rao Chunda take Mandore and Nagaur, and his descendants, the Mahecha Rathores, kept their chief seat at Jasol. His shrine at Tilwara on the Luni drew breeders to a cattle fair for Tharparkar cows, camels and horses. In 1444 the sandy estates of Mallani belonged to Rana Kumbha's Mewar, six years after Rao Ranmal's murder pulled Marwar into war.

Mallinath's grandson Rawat Luka drove the Paramaras out of Juna and made the town his capital. In 1552 his descendant Rawat Bhima founded the town of Barmer and moved the seat there. The district later followed Jodhpur into the kingdom of Marwar: Aurangzeb's armies pillaged it during the Rajput war of 1679, and local chiefs expelled the Mughal garrisons in 1707. As part of Jodhpur, Mallani entered a British subsidiary alliance in January 1818.
zh:
巴尔梅尔一带的马拉尼是塔尔沙漠最干旱的边缘，卢尼河的浅河道和零散水井决定牧群能在哪里放牧。对这里来说，牛、骆驼和马尔瓦里马比城镇贸易更要紧。在古称基拉塔库帕的基拉杜，索兰基国王的封臣于11至12世纪建起一组印度教神庙；索梅什瓦尔庙是废墟中保存最完整的一座，1178年的铭文还记下了突厥人袭扰后的修缮。波罗马拉首领巴哈达·拉奥建立朱纳，把山城命名为巴哈达梅尔，这个名字后来变成巴尔梅尔。整个地区得名于梅赫瓦纳格尔的拉瓦尔·马林纳特。他生于1358年，与妻子鲁帕德同受西拉贾斯坦民间奉祀；1378年击败马尔瓦总督尼扎姆丁的军队，又帮助侄子拉奥·春达攻取曼多尔和纳高尔。他的后裔马赫查·拉索尔人以贾索尔为宗座；卢尼河畔蒂尔瓦拉的马林纳特神庙吸引牧人前来集市，交易塔尔帕卡尔牛、骆驼和马匹。1444年，马拉尼的沙地领地属于拉那·贡波的梅瓦尔；六年前拉奥·兰马尔遇害，马尔瓦尔被拖入战争。

马林纳特之孙拉瓦特·卢卡逐出朱纳的波罗马拉人，并把朱纳立为治所。1552年，其后裔拉瓦特·比马建立巴尔梅尔城，将首领驻地迁来。这一地区后来随焦特布尔归入马尔瓦尔：1679年拉杰普特战争期间遭奥朗则布军队劫掠，1707年各地首领驱逐莫卧儿驻军。1818年1月，马拉尼作为焦特布尔的一部分接受英国的附属同盟。

en:
Churu covers the thorn scrub and first sand dunes on the eastern side of the Thar, where tracks from Jangladesh run toward Shekhawati, Bhatner and the later Bikaner country. In 1444 there was still no walled town here. Kaler and other Jat pastoral clans lived in scattered villages, grazing herds on scrubland under their own headmen, while Muslim Bhattis and Johiyas held country to the north around Bhatner. Wells and cattle mattered more than fortresses in this thinly peopled borderland.

Rao Bika's Rathore conquest at the end of the fifteenth century drew the area into Bikaner. During the sixteenth century Chuhru Singh, a Jat headman of the Kaler clan, founded Churu and built its fort, and the settlement became one of Bikaner's eastern thikanas. Maharaja Zorawar Singh removed its restive thakur Sangram Singh between 1735 and 1746, and Bikaner and Jodhpur spent the rest of the century raiding across this border. In 1798 Maharaja Surat Singh founded nearby Ratangarh while returning from Churu; its fort was completed in 1812 and Prithvi Singh, thakur of Churu, attacked it twice in 1815 and 1816 with help from Sikar. Bikaner accepted British protection in 1818.
zh:
久鲁一带是塔尔沙漠东侧最先出现沙丘和荆棘灌丛的地方，小路从禅伽罗通向谢卡瓦蒂、珀特纳以及后来的比卡内尔地区。1444年，这里还没有城墙环绕的城镇，卡拉尔等贾特游牧氏族住在分散村落里，由本族头人管束，在灌丛地上放牧；北面珀特纳周边则由穆斯林巴蒂人和乔希亚人占据。在这个人烟稀少的边地，水井和牛群比堡垒更重要。

15世纪末，拉奥·比卡率领拉索尔人征服此地，把这一带纳入比卡内尔。16世纪，卡拉尔氏族的贾特头人楚鲁辛格建立久鲁并修筑堡垒，这里后来成为比卡内尔东部封邑之一。1735至1746年间，摩诃罗阇佐拉瓦尔辛格逐走不安分的领主桑格拉姆辛格；此后到该世纪末，比卡内尔与焦特布尔不断在这条边界袭掠。1798年，摩诃罗阇苏拉特辛格从久鲁返回时在附近建立拉坦加尔，城堡1812年落成；久鲁领主普里特维辛格得到西卡尔援助，于1815和1816年两次进攻该堡。1818年，比卡内尔接受英国保护。

en:
The Sutlej runs through the north of this tract, and south of its riverine woods the Cholistan dunes run for a hundred miles. Saraiki graziers raised herds between the river and the desert, and the road from Multan towards Rajputana crossed the sands under the protection of a chain of Bhati forts. The strongest was Derawar, raised in 858 by Rai Jajja Bhati of the Bhati clan, its forty bastions standing thirty metres high over a walled circuit of fifteen hundred metres; caravans travelling between India and Central Asia, and pilgrims making for Mecca, watered there. In 1444 the country belonged to the Langah sultans of Multan, who ruled it through local chiefs; its wealth was in livestock and road tolls rather than towns, and the chief city of the region was still Uch, further west. Mughal rule later made it a quiet district of the Multan subah.

In the eighteenth century the Daudpotra, an Abbasi family from Shikarpur in Sindh, settled kinsmen on newly watered canal lands along the Sutlej. Nawab Sadeq Muhammad rebuilt Derawar in 1732, though the fort was lost fifteen years later, and Nawab Bahawal Khan I founded the town named after him in 1748; it grew into an emporium on the caravan road between Afghanistan and central India. In 1785 a Durrani army, called in by the Kalhoras of Sindh, sacked the town; Bahawal Khan II took shelter first in Derawar and later among the Rajputs, then came back by way of Uch to recover it. He proclaimed the state of Bahawalpur in 1802, Nawab Mubarak Khan retook Derawar in 1804, and when Ranjit Singh's army besieged Multan in 1807, families fleeing the siege filled the new city.
zh:
萨特莱杰河流经这片土地的北缘，河滨林地以南便是绵延上百英里的焦利斯坦沙丘。讲萨拉基语的牧人在河流与沙漠之间放养牲畜，从木尔坦通向拉杰普塔纳的商路横穿沙海，沿途靠一连串巴蒂人的要塞庇护。其中最坚固的是德拉沃尔堡：858年由巴蒂部的拉伊·贾贾·巴蒂修建，四十座棱堡高过三十米，堡墙周长一千五百米；往返印度与中亚的商队、前往麦加的朝觐者都在此补水歇脚。1444年时，此地归属木尔坦的朗伽苏丹，由地方首领松散管辖，财富出在牲畜和过路商税上，没有什么大城，一带首城仍是西边的乌奇。莫卧儿时代，这里成为木尔坦苏巴中一处平静的地方。

18世纪，来自信德希卡布尔的阿巴西家族达乌德波特拉部，把同族部众安置在萨特莱杰河畔新开渠水浇灌的土地上。纳瓦卜萨迪克·穆罕默德1732年重修德拉沃尔堡，但堡垒十五年后得而复失；纳瓦卜巴哈瓦尔汗一世1748年建立以自己名字命名的城镇，后来发展为阿富汗与印度中部之间商路上的商埠。1785年，应信德卡尔霍拉人之请而来的杜兰尼军队洗劫了此城，巴哈瓦尔汗二世先避入德拉沃尔，再投奔拉杰普特诸邦，最后经乌奇回师收复。他于1802年建立巴哈瓦尔布尔邦，纳瓦卜穆巴拉克汗1804年夺回德拉沃尔堡；1807年兰吉特·辛格的军队围攻木尔坦，逃离围城的家眷塞满了这座新城。

en:
Karor lies on the eastern bank of the Indus, and in the fifteenth century the river ran past the walls of the old fort, Kot Karor. Its first name was Depal Garh, the stronghold of a Hindu raja, Deopal, until Mahmud of Ghazni stormed it in 1004; a Qurayshi scholar in his army, Sultan Husain Khwarizmi, settled in the fort, built its first mosque and gave it its Muslim name. The same Qurayshi family had made its home here when Baha al-Haq Bahauddin Zakariya was born about 1170, and local tradition counts Kot Karor as his birthplace; he later made Multan a seat of the Suhrawardiyya order. Mongol raids left the fort waste. In 1444 it was a half-ruined Indus crossing in the domains of the Langah sultans of Multan, its ferry trade and grazing grounds in the hands of local chiefs.

Sultan Husayn Langah restored the place as a provincial seat, first granting it to his brother and then, after the brother rebelled, to Baloch jagirdars; it passed to Malik Sohrab Dodai, and the feuds of Ghazi Khan and Ismail Khan over the grant tore the town apart. In 1545 the Sufi Lal Esan came to Kot Karor. Tradition says he stood on the bank of the Indus and recited the Surah Muzammil one crore times, ten million, and a crore is what karor means in the local tongue; under the Mirani chief Ghazi Khan IV, who ruled from 1590 to 1614 and venerated the saint, the town took the name Karor Lal Esan. The Jaskani Baloch held the country until 1787, when Timur Shah Durrani appointed his own governors. In 1794 the Kabul pretender Humayun Shah was caught near Layyah and blinded at Zaman Shah's command, and with the fall of Mankera to Ranjit Singh in 1821 the whole tract passed to the Sikhs.
zh:
格罗尔地处印度河东岸，15世纪时河水就从古城堡科特格罗尔的墙下流过。它最早叫迪帕尔加尔，是印度教拉杰·迪奥帕尔的要塞，1004年被加兹尼的马哈茂德攻破；随军的古莱氏学者苏丹·侯赛因·花剌子米住进堡中，建起第一座清真寺，给它改了穆斯林名字。大苏菲巴哈乌丁·扎卡里亚约1170年出生时，他的古莱氏家族已经定居于此，当地传统把科特格罗尔算作他的出生地；他后来在木尔坦传道，使该城成为苏赫拉瓦迪教团的中心。蒙古人的侵袭把城堡荒废。1444年时，它是木尔坦朗伽苏丹辖境内一处半废的印度河渡口，摆渡生意和牧场都握在地方首领手里。

侯赛因·朗伽苏丹恢复了此地的省治，先封给弟弟，其弟称乱后又改封给俾路支采邑主，最后落到马利克·苏赫拉布·多多伊手中；加齐汗与伊斯梅尔汗为这份封地长期仇杀，把城镇打得四分五裂。1545年，苏菲修士拉勒·伊桑来到科特格罗尔，相传他站在印度河边把《穆赞米勒章》诵念了一千万遍，「克罗尔」在当地话里就是一千万的意思；在虔敬他的米拉尼首领加齐汗四世（1590至1614年在位）治下，城镇改称格罗尔·拉尔伊桑。贾斯卡尼俾路支人领有此地到1787年，帖木儿沙·杜兰尼随后另派总督。1794年，喀布尔的王位觊觎者胡马云沙在莱亚附近被俘，遵扎曼沙之命刺瞎双目；1821年曼克拉陷落后，整片地区归入兰吉特·辛格的锡克政权。

en:
Shorkot lies east of the Chenab, on the edge of the Sandal Bar, the open grazing lands of central Punjab. Its old fort-mound looks over river villages and the camps of pastoral clans, and among them the Nauls long overshadowed the Sials, then a small tributary tribe. Delhi's writ in the bar ran loose, and in 1444 the clansmen answered to whichever governor held Lahore or Multan. Cattle and cloth moved from the pastures through Shorkot market to the river towns; the Sials did not found nearby Jhang until 1462.

The town's one famous son is Sultan Bahu, born here in 1630 into a Mughal officer's family of the Awan tribe. A Qadiri Sufi, he wrote more than forty Persian treatises, but it was his Punjabi verses, sung as qawwali and kafi, that carried his name through the Punjab. After he died in 1691 his tomb at Garh Maharaja drew pilgrims, and it was moved twice whenever the Chenab shifted its bed. In the 1510s Babur, raiding these tracts, names Bhera and Chiniot, and perhaps Shorkot itself, in his memoirs. The Sials, grown powerful around Jhang, were united into a kingdom by Walidad Khan early in the eighteenth century, until Hari Singh of the Bhangi Misl sacked Jhang in 1760 and made their chiefs his tributaries. Ranjit Singh had absorbed the country by 1810, and in 1821 governors sent from Lahore farmed its revenues.
zh:
绍尔果德位于奇纳布河以东，紧邻旁遮普中部的开阔牧地桑德尔巴尔。古老的堡寨踞在土丘上，俯瞰河畔村落与游牧部族的营地；诸部之中，瑙尔人长期压过还是纳贡小部的锡亚尔人。德里朝廷对这片牧地的号令松弛，1444年时各部听命于占据拉合尔或木尔坦的总督。牲畜和布匹从牧场经绍尔果德市集运往沿河城镇；锡亚尔人要到1462年才在附近建起章城。

此地最出名的人物是苏丹·巴胡，1630年生于绍尔果德，出身阿万部一个莫卧儿军官家庭。他是卡迪里教团的苏菲行者，写过四十余部波斯文论著，真正传遍旁遮普的却是他的旁遮普语诗篇，后人谱成卡瓦里和卡菲演唱。1691年他去世后，在格尔赫·默哈拉杰的陵墓引来朝圣者；奇纳布河几次改道，陵墓也两度随之迁移。巴布尔1510年代攻略这一带时，回忆录提到贝赫拉、吉尼奥德，或许也包括绍尔果德。锡亚尔人以章城为中心坐大，18世纪初瓦利达德汗统一诸部建国，1760年班吉米斯尔的哈里·辛格攻破章城，迫其首领称臣纳贡。兰吉特·辛格到1810年已吞并此地，1821年由拉合尔派来的总督包收赋税。

en:
Bhera stands on the old Kabul road, just north of the Jhelum and below the southern face of the Salt Range, the hills Muslim writers called Koh-i-Jud. The Khewra, Kalabagh and Warcha mines yield the range's rock salt, and Bhera was the town where that salt changed hands with the Kabul caravans. Mahmud of Ghazni sacked the first settlement here, and two centuries later Mongol generals plundered it again. Its clans were older than any conqueror: Babur recorded that the Janjua and the Jud had from old times ruled the hills between the Indus and Bhera. In 1444 the Khokhar chief Jasrat had been dead two years and the confederacy he built across the upper Punjab had fallen apart, so Sirhind's governors barely reached the road while armed clans held the passes and the Jhelum crossings.

The walled old town opened through eight gates onto mohallas of traders, weavers and cutlers; its smiths made serpentine, the false jade hauled from Afghanistan, into pesh-kabz dagger handles. Babur held Bhera to ransom in 1519. In 1540 Sher Shah Suri refounded the town, and its congregational mosque was completed in 1541 with a dated inscription. Work began the same year on Rohtas Fort to the northeast, entrusted to Todar Mal, with great sandstone walls thrown across a gorge to pin down the Gakhars and shut Humayun out of India. The Gakhars refused to work on the site, Sher Shah died in 1545 before it was finished, and the walls were never stormed: the garrison ceded them to Humayun in 1555. Jahangir stopped a night on his way to Kashmir and thought the fort's strength past imagining. Under Akbar, Bhera became the seat of a subdivision of the Lahore subah. In the reign of Muhammad Shah, Abbas Khan Khattak of Pind Dadan Khan murdered its Khukhrain governor Salamat Rai and seized the town, which Salamat's nephew Fateh Anand soon recovered. Nader Shah and Ahmad Shah Durrani both used Rohtas on their campaigns, and in 1767 Charat Singh, grandfather of Ranjit Singh, took it from its Durrani governor. Bhera went on trading along the Kabul road, and under Ranjit Singh it ran a Sikh mint.
zh:
佩拉位于杰赫勒姆河以北、盐岭南麓之下，坐落在喀布尔古道上，穆斯林文献把这片山岭称作「贾德山」。盐岭的凯沃拉、卡拉巴赫和瓦尔恰盐矿出产岩盐，佩拉正是岩盐与喀布尔商队交易的城镇。最早的聚落遭马哈茂德·伽色尼洗劫，两百年后又被蒙古将领掠夺。这里的氏族比任何征服者都古老：巴布尔记载，詹朱阿人与贾德人同出一父，自古以来统治印度河至佩拉之间的山地，两族分据山岭两侧。1444年，霍哈尔首领贾斯拉特已去世两年，他在上旁遮普建立的联盟已经解体，西尔欣德的总督几乎管不到这条道路，把守山口和杰赫勒姆渡口的是盐岭上的武装氏族。

带城墙的老城开有八座城门，门内街坊里聚居着商人、织工和刀匠；铁匠把阿富汗运来的蛇纹石（假玉）做成佩什卡布兹匕首的刀柄。1519年，巴布尔迫使佩拉缴纳赎金。1540年，舍尔沙·苏利另建新城，城中聚礼清真寺1541年完工，寺内留有纪年铭文。同年，东北方的罗赫塔斯堡开工，由托达尔·马尔督造：巨大的砂岩城墙横过山峡，用以压制加哈尔人、把胡马雍挡在印度之外。加哈尔部众拒绝应役筑城，舍尔沙1545年去世时工程仍未完工，而这道城墙最终也没被强攻攻破，守兵在1555年开城交给胡马雍。贾汉吉尔赴克什米尔途中在此驻跸一夜，写道建于这般峡谷裂隙中的堡垒，坚固难以想象。阿克巴时期，佩拉成为拉合尔苏巴一个分区的治所。穆罕默德沙在位时，霍赫兰出身的长官萨拉马特·拉伊管辖此城，被据守平德·达丹汗的阿巴斯·汗·哈塔克谋害夺城，萨拉马特的外甥法塔赫·阿南德不久将其收复。纳迪尔沙和艾哈迈德沙·杜兰尼用兵时都曾利用罗赫塔斯；1767年，兰季德·辛格的祖父恰拉特·辛格从杜兰尼总督手中夺取此堡。佩拉继续在喀布尔商路上做买卖，兰季德·辛格时期还设有锡克人的造币厂。

en:
Bharuch, entered on British maps as Broach, stands where the Narmada opens into the Gulf of Khambhat. The first-century Periplus of the Erythraean Sea knew it as Barygaza, the greatest port of these coasts: its estuary was so thick with shoals and racing tides that the king sent pilots out to sea to meet incoming ships and guide them to the anchorage, while cotton cloth, silk, agate and long pepper sailed for the Red Sea and the Roman world. The Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang found the town still flourishing, and in 1345 Muhammad bin Tughluq defeated his rebel Afghan amirs beneath its walls. Under the Gujarat sultans it stayed one of the busiest harbours on the gulf, a town of Gujarati shipowners and Bhargava Brahmins, and in 1444 its customs houses and shipyards served the court at Ahmadabad.

Between 1500 and 1700 Bharuch was above all a textile town, its bafta calico shipped to Europe and Southeast Asia. In the late fifteenth century the Sikh guru Nanak is said to have crossed the Narmada here on a cloth sheet after a boatman refused him passage. In 1547 a Portuguese squadron under Jorge de Meneses entered the estuary by night and sacked the city, a heavy blow to Gujarat's sea trade; its Jami Masjid was built in 1644, under Shah Jahan. After Akbar's conquest the port passed to Mughal governors and then to local nawabs, who accepted Maratha suzerainty in 1685 and made themselves independent in 1736. The East India Company wanted its cotton, attacked in 1771 and took the city's surrender on 18 November 1772, leaving the dispossessed nawab a hereditary pension.
zh:
布罗奇（英国地图上写作Broach，今译珀鲁杰）位于讷尔默达河注入坎贝湾处。公元1世纪的《厄立特里亚海航行记》称它为巴里加扎，是这一带海岸最大的港口：河口浅滩密布、潮水湍急，国王要派出领航员出海迎接来船、引到锚地，棉布、丝绸、玛瑙和长胡椒则从这里运往红海和罗马世界。中国求法僧玄奘见到的城镇依旧繁盛；1345年，穆罕默德·伊本·图格鲁克在城下击败叛乱的阿富汗埃米尔。古吉拉特苏丹时期，布罗奇始终是湾内最繁忙的港口之一，城中多古吉拉特船主和巴尔加夫婆罗门；1444年，它的海关和船坞为艾哈迈达巴德的宫廷效力。

1500至1700年间，布罗奇首先是座纺织城，出产的巴夫塔棉布远销欧洲和东南亚。相传15世纪后期，锡克教祖师那纳克被船夫拒绝渡河，便乘一块布片渡过讷尔默达河。1547年，若热·德·梅内塞斯率葡萄牙分舰队趁夜驶入河口、洗劫城市，重创古吉拉特的海上贸易；城中的大清真寺建于1644年沙贾汗在位时。阿克巴征服后，港口先归莫卧儿总督，后落入本地纳瓦布手中，他们1685年接受马拉塔宗主权，1736年自立。东印度公司看中了当地的棉花，1771年发兵来攻，1772年11月18日城市投降，被废的纳瓦布得到一笔世袭年金。

en:
Dipalpur stands on an old bed of the Ravi in the Bari Doab, on the road an invader from the north-west took on the way to Delhi. Its earthen walls, already old when Timur came, made it one of the fortified towns, with Uch, Samana and Hansi, where the Delhi sultans met invasion. In 1285 the Mongols of Pir Muhammad Khan broke against these walls; Balban's son Muhammad Khan beat them in the field and was killed riding after the retreat. Local tradition points to his small tomb west of the town's Badshahi Mosque, though no authentic source confirms the grave. Firuz Shah Tughlaq, who came here often, raised a large mosque outside the walls, which later vanished. When Timur sacked Dipalpur in 1398 it ranked second only to Multan, and when the old Beas ran dry soon afterwards the town was left half deserted. In 1444 it is a weathered border fortress held for Delhi by the Afghan lords of Sirhind.

Babur writes plainly in his memoirs that in 1524 he defeated Pahar Khan and took Lahore and Dipalpur. Under the Mughals it became a sarkar of the Lahore subah, and the Ain-i-Akbari rates its militia at 5,210 horse and 53,300 foot. In 1578 Akbar and Prince Salim halted here on their way to Baba Farid's shrine at Pakpattan, and the emperor coined the name Bari Doab from the Beas and the Ravi. A Qalandar from Baghdad, Bahawal Sher, settled in a village near the town, built a cell and a mosque, and lies buried there; his tomb-shrine and his grandson Shah Muqeem, who carried on his mission, gave the village its later name of Hujra Shah Muqeem. Punjabi oral tradition places the prayers of Sahiban, in the romance of Mirza Sahiban, at the same village, with no record to bear it out.

As Mughal power ebbed, the Sandhu Jat chieftain Heera Singh founded the Nakai Misl across the Ravi-Sutlej country in 1748, and Dipalpur became one of its forts. In 1810 Ranjit Singh's general Mohkam Chand stormed it together with Chunian and Satghara. In 1821 it is a garrison town of the Sikh Empire.
zh:
迪巴尔布尔在巴里河间地的拉维河故道旁，西北入侵者进军德里的大路正从这里经过。土墙在帖木儿到来之前早已筑成，使它与乌奇、萨马纳、汉西同属德里苏丹迎击外敌的一线要塞。1285年，皮尔·穆罕默德汗的蒙古军在这道墙前溃败，巴勒班之子穆罕默德汗打赢野战，却在追击中战死；当地传说他的小墓就在城中皇家清真寺西侧，只是没有可靠凭据。常来此地的菲鲁兹沙·图格鲁克在城外修过一座大清真寺，后来也已不存。1398年帖木儿洗劫此城时，它的规模仅次于木尔坦；老比亚斯河随后干涸，城池半废。1444年的迪巴尔布尔是一座饱经风霜的边镇，由西尔欣德的阿富汗诸酋代德里据守。

巴布尔在回忆录里直写：1524年他击败帕哈尔汗，拿下拉合尔与迪巴尔布尔。莫卧儿时期它成为拉合尔省的萨卡尔，《阿克巴则例》记其民兵有5,210名骑兵、53,300名步兵。1578年，阿克巴与皇子萨利姆前往帕克帕坦拜谒巴巴·法里德圣陵，途中在此驻跸；「巴里河间地」之名，就是阿克巴取比亚斯河与拉维河之名拼合而成。来自巴格达的卡兰达尔行者巴哈瓦尔·希尔在城附近的村落定居，修起静室与清真寺，死后葬在那里；他的圣祠和继承其事业的孙子沙·穆基姆，使村子后来得名胡吉拉·沙·穆基姆。旁遮普口头传说还把民间故事《米尔扎与萨希班》中萨希班祈祷之处安在这个村子，却没有记载可作凭据。

莫卧儿权势衰退后，桑杜贾特首领希拉·辛格于1748年在拉维河与萨特莱杰河之间建立纳卡伊米斯尔，迪巴尔布尔成为其堡寨之一。1810年，兰吉特·辛格的大将莫哈姆·昌德连克迪巴尔布尔、楚尼安和萨特加拉。1821年时，它是锡克帝国的驻防城。

en:
Sakya lies in a high valley about 130 kilometres west of Shigatse and takes its name from the pale grey earth of Ponpori Hill. In 1073 Khon Konchog Gyalpo of the old Khon clan founded a monastery beneath the hill, and under the Five Supreme Masters, above all Sakya Pandita and his nephew Phagpa, its lamas became the rulers of Tibet. Sakya Pandita, already an old man, reached the camp of Godan Khan at Liangzhou in 1246 with the young Phagpa and settled the terms of Tibet's submission to the Mongols; he died there five years later, and Phagpa became imperial preceptor to Kublai Khan. In 1268 the dpon-chen Sakya Sangpo raised the walled southern monastery and its great Lhakhang Chenmo, the hall from which Tibet was governed under the Yuan, and Kublai sent the library giant volumes written in gold letters and bound in iron. After the Phagmodrupa leader Changchub Gyaltsen overthrew Sakya's rule in the mid-fourteenth century, the Khon lamas kept only a small monastic domain. In 1444 the Tsang around it was held by the Rinpungpa lord Norzang, who administered the great hall himself as its dpon-chen.

Sakya's scholarship still flourished in these years. Sonam Senge, known as Gorampa, was the foremost master of its teachings in the fifteenth century, and later in the century the Khon line, its other branches extinct, divided into the Phuntsok and Dolma palaces, whose eldest sons held the Sakya throne in turn. The Tsangpa kings who seized Tsang from the Rinpungpa in 1565 favoured the Karmapas but spared Sakya, and the Lhakhang Chenmo was restored during that century. In 1642 the Mongol army of Gushi Khan overthrew the Tsangpa and installed the Fifth Dalai Lama. Sakya lost its last temporal claims but kept its palaces, its rites and its famous library under the Ganden Podrang and later Qing protection, and the two palaces kept supplying throne-holders without interruption down to the end of the eighteenth century.
zh:
萨迦在日喀则以西约一百三十公里的高山谷地里，得名于本波山灰白色的山土。1073年，古老昆氏家族的昆·贡却杰布在山下首建寺院；到萨迦五祖、尤其是萨迦班智达与其侄八思巴的时代，萨迦喇嘛成了西藏的统治者。萨迦班智达以年迈之身，于1246年带着年少的八思巴抵达凉州蒙古阔端的营地，谈定吐蕃归附蒙古的条件，五年后圆寂于凉州；八思巴后来成为忽必烈的帝师。1268年，萨迦本钦释迦桑布主持筑起城墙环绕的南寺，宏伟的拉康钦莫大殿成为元代治理西藏的政厅所在，忽必烈还赐给寺中一批金汁书写、铁箍装订的巨型经卷。14世纪中叶，帕木竹巴的绛曲坚赞推翻萨迦政权，昆氏喇嘛只保住一处小小的教权领地。1444年，后藏已在仁蚌巴领袖诺布桑波手中，他还以本钦身份亲自兼管这座大殿。

这一时期萨迦的佛学仍然兴盛，索南僧格是15世纪最杰出的萨迦义理大师。15世纪后期，昆氏其余各支先后绝嗣，仅存的一支分出彭措颇章与卓玛颇章两房，由两房长子轮流出任萨迦法王。1565年取代仁蚌巴据有后藏的藏巴汗崇信噶玛噶举，却没有为难萨迦，拉康钦莫也在这一世纪得到修缮。1642年，固始汗的蒙古大军攻灭藏巴汗、拥立五世达赖喇嘛，萨迦失去最后的世俗权力，却在甘丹颇章政权及后来清朝的护持下保留了宫殿、法事和闻名全藏的藏书，两房也继续轮值法王，直到18世纪末年都未曾中断。

en:
Gyirong, the 'happy valley', lies on the Gyirong Tsangpo, the headwater stream of Nepal's Trishuli River, at little more than 2,700 metres: a warm, wooded corridor through the Himalayas and the shortest road between Tsang and the Kathmandu valley, which Newar traders knew as Kerung. After the Tibetan empire collapsed, princes of the old Yarlung royal line founded the kingdom of Mangyul Gungthang here, with its citadel at Dzongka, the 'White Fortress', and under the Mongol Yuan it counted among Tibet's thirteen myriarchies. The yogin-poet Milarepa, Marpa's disciple and the Kagyu order's best-loved singer of meditation songs, was born into a Gungthang family in this valley in 1052. The little kingdom lived on the trans-Himalayan pack trade, its markets taking in gold from the western Tibetan goldfields and cloth and rice from the Newar towns. In 1444 King Thri Lhawang Gyaltsen still ruled from Dzongka; his daughter Chokyi Dronma, married to a prince of Lato in 1438, later left him to follow the bridge-building yogin Thang Tong Gyalpo, who recognised her as the first Samding Dorje Phagmo and began Tibet's highest line of female incarnations.

Gungthang outlasted a string of overlords until 1620, when the king of Tsang destroyed the kingdom and ended its royal line, and Gyirong became a frontier dzong under the Dalai Lamas' government, its pass crowded each trading season with Newar caravans climbing out of the Nepalese hills. In 1788 the Gorkha rulers of Nepal marched an army up this same corridor and seized Kyirong and Kuti; Tibetan officials bought a hasty peace, and in 1791 the Gurkhas came back, stormed Kyirong, Tingri and Shigatse and sacked Tashilhunpo. In 1792 the Qing army under Fuk'anggan retook Kyirong and forced its way down the Trishuli to the outskirts of Kathmandu, until the Gurkhas submitted and entered tributary relations with Beijing. The Twenty-Nine Article Ordinance that followed remade Tibet's administration, and after it the Kyirong road carried only merchants and pilgrims.
zh:
吉隆，藏语意为「快乐舒适之地」，坐落于吉隆藏布河畔；这条河是尼泊尔特里苏利河的上游，谷地海拔仅两千七百余米，是喜马拉雅山中一条温暖湿润、林木葱郁的走廊，也是后藏通往加德满都谷地最近的商道，尼瓦尔商人称之为「基隆」。吐蕃王朝崩溃后，雅砻旧王的后裔在此建立芒域贡塘王国，王城建在宗嘎堡寨，宗嘎意为「白色的堡垒」；元代时，这里是西藏十三万户之一。瑜伽行者、诗人密勒日巴是玛尔巴的弟子、噶举派最受爱戴的修道歌者，1052年就生在谷地中一户贡塘人家。小国靠跨喜马拉雅的驮运贸易谋生，市上既有西藏西部金矿的砂金，也有尼瓦尔城镇贩来的布匹和大米。1444年，国王拉旺坚赞仍在宗嘎治国；公主曲吉卓美1438年嫁给拉堆的王子，后来离开夫家，师从以修建铁索桥闻名的瑜伽师唐东杰布，唐东杰布认定她是桑顶·多吉帕姆的第一世，这也是西藏地位最高的女活佛转世世系。

贡塘在一个又一个宗主之间存续到1620年，终为藏巴汗攻灭，王统断绝，吉隆成为达赖喇嘛政权治下的边境宗；每到通商季节，山口挤满了从尼泊尔山地攀援而上的尼瓦尔商队。1788年，尼泊尔的廓尔喀统治者沿这条走廊进军，攻占吉隆和聂拉木；西藏官员仓促以银赎地，1791年廓尔喀人却卷土重来，连下吉隆、定日、日喀则，洗劫扎什伦布寺。1792年，福康安统率清军收复吉隆，沿特里苏利河直逼加德满都近郊，廓尔喀被迫归降，向北京称臣入贡。战后颁行《钦定藏内善后章程》重整西藏政务，吉隆商道上便只剩行商与朝圣者往来。

en:
Purang, called Taklakot by its Nepali neighbours, is the broad valley south of Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar, where the Karnali rises and the high passes drop into Humla and Kumaon. Kailash is sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, Bonpo and Jains alike, and pilgrims of all four pass through the valley on their way to circle the mountain and bathe in the lake. Above the town rises Tegla Kar, the Lying Tiger, a cliff fort first raised by the kings of Zhangzhung; after 910 the fugitive Tibetan prince Kyide Nyimagon made it his first foothold, and the lands he gathered later split into the kingdoms of Guge and Purang. A Purang line ruled on its own from about 1100 until a resurgent Guge reabsorbed the valley in 1378. The town lived by pack trains: thousands of sheep carried salt, wool and barley south into Nepal and brought rice and cloth back. In 1444 Purang was the southern march of the Guge kingdom, its old fort above the market road.

War reached the valley only as Guge itself was failing. Early in the seventeenth century the Balti ruler Ali Sher Khan Anchan raided east as far as Purang, and in 1635 Ladakh overran Guge and kept the valley for Leh. In 1679–80 the Fifth Dalai Lama's general Galdan Chhewang conquered Ngari at the head of a Mongol-Tibetan army and attached Purang to Lhasa. Officials sent out from Lhasa then ran the district, and the town saw few soldiers but many travellers: each summer Purangpa caravans crossed the passes and pilgrims climbed toward Kailash, until the first snows sealed the valley for the winter.
zh:
普兰，尼泊尔邻人称之为塔克拉果特，位于冈仁波齐峰与玛旁雍错以南的宽阔谷地，格尔纳利河发源于此，山口向南下到胡姆拉和库马盎。冈仁波齐是印度教徒、佛教徒、苯教徒和耆那教徒共同的圣山，四众朝圣都要路经这片谷地，前去绕山转经、在圣湖沐浴。镇上方的山崖上立着特格拉卡堡，意为「卧虎堡」，最早为象雄诸王所筑；910年后西逃的吐蕃王子吉德尼玛衮以这里为第一个立足点，他收拢的土地后来分出古格与普兰两个王国。约1100年普兰王系自成一国，1378年复兴的古格将其重新吞并。城镇靠驮队为生：成千上万只羊驮着盐、羊毛和青稞南下尼泊尔，换回大米和布匹。1444年的普兰是古格王国的南边要塞，古堡俯临着通市的商道。

战火烧进谷地时，古格自身已在倾覆。17世纪初，巴尔蒂王阿里·谢尔汗·安詹东征，兵锋远及普兰；1635年拉达克攻灭古格，谷地转归列城统治。1679至1680年，五世达赖的将领噶丹泽旺率蒙藏联军攻取阿里，普兰划归拉萨。此后当地由拉萨派来的官员治理，兵戈稀少而旅人不断：每年夏天普兰人的商队翻过山口，朝圣者也结伴走向冈仁波齐，直到初雪封山，谷地才安静一冬。

en:
Nedong lies in the grain-rich Yarlung Valley above Tsetang, the oldest royal country in Tibet. On a ridge to the south stands Yumbulakang, said to be the first building raised in Tibet, palace of the legendary first king Nyatri Tsenpo; after Songtsen Gampo moved his court to Lhasa it became a shrine. Nearby Tradruk, founded in the seventh century as one of the kingdom's earliest geomantic temples, was later counted among the three royal monasteries. A cave in the hillside east of Tsetang is shown as the place where the Tibetan people were born to a monkey and a mountain ogress, and the Tsetang monastery Ganden Chokhorling was founded beside the town in 1351. The valley became a seat of living power in the fourteenth century: Tai Situ Changchub Gyaltsen overthrew Sakya overlordship and after 1354 governed the whole of Tibet from his palace at Nedong, at the head of the Phagmodrupa regime. In 1444 his descendant Drakpa Jungne, invested by the Ming court as Chanhuawang, still ruled there, but the succession war of a decade before had broken the court's strength and feudatories such as the Rinpungpa now overshadowed it.

After Drakpa Jungne's death the next year Rinpungpa pressure tightened year by year, until Kunga Lekpa was deposed in 1481. Ngawang Tashi Drakpa won back the Lhasa area in 1517 and 1518, the last Phagmodrupa king with real authority; after him the dynasty shrank to its home valley. The kings of Tsang defeated it in 1613 and again seven years later, and Gushi Khan's Mongol victory of 1642 gave Tibet to the Fifth Dalai Lama and his Ganden Phodrang government. The old royal shrines then changed schools: Yumbulakang became a Gelug monastery, Tradruk took a golden roof under the Fifth Dalai Lama and was enlarged under the Seventh, so that by the late eighteenth century it was said to hold twenty-one temples, and the old Kagyu house at Tsetang, Ganden Chokhorling, passed to the Gelug order during the eighteenth century.
zh:
乃东位于泽当以上盛产谷物的雅砻河谷，这里是西藏最古老的王都之地。南面山脊上的雍布拉康相传是西藏的第一座建筑，为传说中第一代赞普聂赤赞普的宫殿；松赞干布迁都拉萨后，它成了一座神殿。附近的昌珠寺建于7世纪，是吐蕃最早的镇寺神庙之一，后来位列三大皇家寺院。泽当以东的山坡上有一处山洞，相传藏族先民就出生在那里，是一只猕猴与岩魔女的后代；1351年，泽当寺甘丹曲科林在城边建成。14世纪，雅砻河谷重新成为权力中心：大司徒绛曲坚赞推翻萨迦的统治，1354年以后以乃东宫殿统辖全藏，建立帕木竹巴政权。1444年，他的后人、被明朝封为阐化王的札巴迥乃仍在此执政，但十年前的继承纷争已经耗尽宫廷的力量，仁蚌巴等强藩的声势盖过了它。

札巴迥乃次年去世后，仁蚌巴的压力一年紧过一年，贡噶勒巴最终在1481年被废。阿旺札西札巴在1517和1518年恢复了拉萨地区，他是最后一位仍有实权的帕竹第悉；在他之后，王朝势力缩回雅砻河谷。藏巴汗在1613年和七年后两度击败帕竹，1642年固始汗的蒙古大军获胜，西藏归于五世达赖喇嘛的甘丹颇章政权。古老的王统圣迹随后改换教派：雍布拉康被改为格鲁派寺院，昌珠寺在五世达赖喇嘛时期铺上金顶，七世达赖喇嘛时期继续扩建，到18世纪后期据说已有21座佛殿；泽当的噶举古寺甘丹曲科林也在18世纪转归格鲁派。

en:
Tsurphu Monastery lies high in the Tolung valley, on the upper reaches of the Tsurphu river some seventy kilometres upstream from Lhasa, at about 4,300 metres. Walls four metres thick enclosed a complex that once held a thousand monks. The First Karmapa, Dusum Khyenpa, founded it in 1187 and made it the head monastery of the Karma Kagyu order and the home of every Karmapa after him; his line was the oldest of Tibet's great reincarnating successions, each holder leaving instructions for his own next birth. Its most famous relic was the Black Crown: legend says the dakinis wove the original from their own hair, and the jewelled crown topped with a ruby was made for the Fifth Karmapa after the Yongle Emperor of Ming saw it above his head in a vision at court and asked for a copy that others could be blessed by. In 1444 the Sixth Karmapa, Thongwa Donden, held the throne: a scholar and organiser rather than a fighter, he composed new rituals, expanded the copying and printing of scriptures and founded a monastic college. Beyond the valley the order's military patrons were the Rinpungpa lords of Tsang, whose troops already held Shigatse.

Under the Seventh Karmapa, Chodrak Gyatso, a master of Buddhist logic, the order reached its height: Rinpungpa troops kept Gelugpa monks out of Lhasa's Monlam prayer festival from 1498 to 1517, and in 1613 the kings of Tsang styled the Karmapa 'lord of U-Tsang'. That patronage ended when Gushi Khan's Mongols overthrew the Tsangpa in 1642. Kagyu monasteries across Tsang were converted to the Gelug order or emptied, and the Tenth Karmapa, Choying Dorje, fled into exile and wandered for years through Bhutan, Kham and Nepal. He returned to central Tibet in 1672 and met the Fifth Dalai Lama at the Potala the next year; by the end of the century the Eleventh Karmapa had been raised and ordained at Tsurphu. The monastery kept its monks and its crown ceremony, but its lamas no longer commanded armies.
sources: https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/第十世噶瑪巴·確映多傑
zh:
楚布寺坐落在堆龙河谷高处的楚布河上游，海拔约4300米，距拉萨约七十公里；四米厚的围墙之内，寺群最盛时住有上千名僧人。1187年，第一世噶玛巴杜松虔巴创建此寺，使它成为噶玛噶举派的主寺和历代噶玛巴的驻锡地。噶玛巴转世是藏传佛教各大活佛体系中最早的一支，历代转世都留下了认定下一世的嘱托。寺中最有名的圣物是黑宝冠：相传这顶宝冠本为空行母以头发织成，第五世噶玛巴得银协巴赴南京觐见永乐帝时，皇帝在定中看见他头上的黑冠，便命工匠仿制一顶镶满宝石、顶上嵌一颗红宝石的宝冠，使世人也能领受加持，黑冠法会便由历代噶玛巴传续下来。1444年，第六世噶玛巴通瓦敦殿住持法座，他是学者和组织者而非战将，编订新仪轨，组织经书的抄写与刊印，还创办了佛学院；山谷之外，噶玛噶举的军事护法是已据有日喀则的仁蚌巴。

第七世噶玛巴确札嘉措是因明学大师，在他的时代噶玛噶举声势达到顶点：仁蚌巴的军队在1498至1517年间禁止格鲁派僧人参加拉萨的传昭大法会，1613年藏巴汗又尊噶玛巴为「卫藏之主」。1642年固始汗的蒙古军攻灭藏巴汗，这段世俗护持随之结束：后藏的噶举寺院多被改宗格鲁派，或僧众逃散，第十世噶玛巴秋英多杰出亡，在不丹、康区和尼泊尔辗转多年。1672年他返回卫藏，次年在布达拉宫与五世达赖喇嘛会面；到17世纪末，第十一世噶玛巴已在楚布寺长大、受戒。寺院仍有僧人和黑冠法会，但这里的喇嘛已不再统兵。

en:
Damxung, or Dam in Qing records, means the chosen pasture. Its steppe lies southeast of Namtso, the Heavenly Lake, below the Nyenchen Tanglha range, whose highest peak rises to 7,111 metres on the direct northern approach to Lhasa. In 1444 there was no fortress here, only high grazing worked by Tibetan herders: the sheep supplied wool, and yaks and horses carried traffic between Lhasa and the northern lake country. The weather over the passes could break an army before it ever reached central Tibet.

In the southern valley the Fourth Shamarpa, the Red Hat Karmapa, founded Yangpachen Monastery around 1490 with money from the prince of Rinpung, and the house remained the Shamarpas' seat for three hundred years. Later in the same century the Fifth Dalai Lama granted the Damxung steppe to Gushi Khan, whose Khoshut cavalry settled there as the Eight Banners of Dam; after Gushi Khan's death the grazing passed to Sera Monastery's Ngakpa Tratsang. In 1717 the Dzungar commander Tsering Dondub marched some six thousand men through Nagchu and past Namtso, surprised Lhasa and killed Lhabzang Khan, ending the Khoshut khanate; Qing forces drove the Dzungars out three years later, and Khoshut clansmen fleeing the failed Qinghai rising of 1723 swelled the camps at Dam. In 1750 the Eight Banners were placed directly under the Qing ambans in Lhasa. Yangpachen fell in 1792, after the Gurkha war: the Tenth Shamarpa was blamed for siding with Nepal, the Gelug government confiscated the monastery, the red hat was buried and recognition of further Shamarpa incarnations was forbidden.
zh:
当雄在清代史料中多称达木，藏语意为「挑选的草场」。草原位于纳木错东南、念青唐古拉山下，山脉主峰海拔7111米，草原正处在从北面直通拉萨的要道上。1444年，这里没有堡寨，只有藏族牧民经营的高寒牧场：羊群出产羊毛，牦牛和马匹支撑着拉萨与藏北湖群之间的往来。山口上的天气，能让一支军队在抵达西藏中枢之前就垮在半路。

谷地南部，红帽噶玛巴第四世夏玛巴约在1490年靠仁蚌巴首领的资助建起羊八井寺，此后三百年间这里都是夏玛巴的驻锡地。同一个世纪稍后，五世达赖喇嘛把当雄草原赐给固始汗，定居于此的和硕特骑兵编为达木蒙古八旗；固始汗死后，牧场转归色拉寺的阿巴扎仓占有。1717年，准噶尔将领大策零敦多布率约六千人经那曲、纳木错一线突袭拉萨，杀死拉藏汗，灭亡和硕特汗国；清军三年后将准噶尔人逐出西藏，1723年罗卜藏丹津在青海反清失败，又有和硕特部众逃来，壮大了达木的营地。1750年，达木八旗改由拉萨的驻藏大臣直接管辖。羊八井寺则在1792年廓尔喀之役后倾覆：第十世夏玛巴被指责勾结尼泊尔，格鲁派政府没收寺院、埋藏红帽，并禁止再认定夏玛巴转世。

en:
Rutog is the high country beyond the Trans-Himalaya, a windswept plateau of salt lakes and pastures around 4,500 metres, where the eastern arm of Pangong Lake reaches toward Ladakh. The old dzong crowned a hilltop above the caravan track, with a fort and several monasteries, and rock carvings in the district go back to Zhangzhung times. After the Tibetan empire broke up, Rutog passed to Maryul, the Ladakhi kingdom whose lands ran from the Zoji La to Demchok and the Gogpo goldfields; with Guge's rise in the fourteenth century the frontier swung back and forth, and in 1444 the district was the western march of the Guge kings. Nomad flocks supplied coarse wool and the fine pashmina that Ladakhi caravans carried west toward Kashmir.

Ties to Leh stayed close, as one odd episode shows. The Jesuit António de Andrade, welcomed at the Guge court in 1626, was even allowed to open a second chapel at remote Rudok, but a few years later Sengge Namgyal of Ladakh reclaimed the district when his armies overran Guge. Ladakhi rule ended in 1679 before the Fifth Dalai Lama's general Galdan Chhewang, who invaded at the head of a Mongol-Tibetan army. The peace sealed at Tingmosgang in 1684 fixed Rutog under Lhasa yet kept it the hinge of the Himalayan wool trade: only Ladakh's royal trader might enter from the west, two hundred horse-loads of Lhasa tea went to Leh each year, and a triennial mission carried gold dust, saffron and Yarkand cotton the other way. Those guarded terms kept Rutog's caravans moving through the eighteenth century.
zh:
日土在喜马拉雅山以北，是海拔约4500米的高原，盐湖散布、牧场开阔，狭长的班公错经此伸向拉达克。旧日土宗雄踞商道旁的山巅，堡寨与数座寺院并立，境内的岩画可上溯到象雄时代。吐蕃崩溃后，日土归入麻域，这个拉达克王国的疆域从佐吉山口一直延伸到典角和果普金矿；14世纪古格崛起，边界几经进退，到1444年，日土是古格国王的西部边地。牧民的羊群出产粗羊毛和细软的羊绒，由拉达克商队一路西运往克什米尔。

日土与列城关系密切，有一桩事很能说明。1626年耶稣会士安德拉德在古格宫廷受到礼遇，甚至获准在偏远的日土也设一座小教堂；不过数年，拉达克王僧格南嘉攻灭古格，把这片地区重新收回。拉达克的统治止于1679年，五世达赖的将领噶丹泽旺率蒙藏联军西征到此。1684年在丁莫岗订立的和约把日土划归拉萨，却保留了它在喜马拉雅羊毛贸易中的枢纽地位：从拉达克来的人中，只有王廷官商可以进入日土；每年有两百驮拉萨茶叶西运列城，列城则每三年遣使，带着金砂、藏红花和叶尔羌棉布东来。凭着这些管束森严的条款，日土的商队在整个18世纪往来不断。

en:
Skardu opens the broad valley where the Shigar River runs into the Indus, the centre of the Balti country the Mughals called Little Tibet. The Balti speak a Tibetan tongue, and their valleys were Buddhist lands under the Tibetan kings until that power collapsed; the local Maqpon dynasty then ruled them for some seven hundred years. Disciples of Mir Sayyid Ali Hamadani crossed the passes from Kashmir in the fourteenth century, and Balti tradition points to their Chaqchan mosque at Khaplu; Nurbakhshiya missionaries carried the new faith further. In 1444 the Maqpon raja rules the river junction from Skardu, his family turning to Islam while lamas and Buddhist villagers still people most of the valleys, and caravans carry mountain wool, dried fruit and river gold toward Kashmir and Yarkand.

About 1500 Maqpon Bokha made Skardu his capital and raised above the town the fort later called Kharphocho, 'the king of forts', bringing craftsmen from Kashmir and Chilas to set its trades going. Early in the sixteenth century Sultan Said Khan of Yarkand raided the valleys, and Sikh tradition also dates Guru Nanak's visit to these years. After Akbar conquered Kashmir in 1586 the Maqpons acknowledged Mughal suzerainty, and Mughal historians called their kings rulers of Little Tibet. The greatest of the line, Ali Sher Khan Anchan, ruled from 1580 to 1633. When the Ladakhis overran Kargil and put his garrison to the sword, he marched round them by way of Marol and seized Leh about 1594, carrying King Jamyang Namgyal prisoner; the peace was sealed by marriage to a Ladakhi princess, for whom the Mendoq Khar palace was built beside the fort. Anchan then made Astore, Gilgit, Hunza, Chilas and Chitral his tributaries. His death opened a war among his sons, and a Mughal army under Zafar Khan crossed the passes in 1634–1636 to settle the succession, after which the Maqpons ruled within the Mughal orbit; a Mughal chronicler counted twenty-two parganas and thirty-seven forts in this poor, fruit-growing land. The Nurbakhshiya taught on, and by the end of the century nearly all Baltis were Muslim, most of them Shia. As Mughal power ebbed the Maqpons kept their mountain kingdom behind its passes, still independent in 1821.
zh:
斯卡都位于什加尔河汇入印度河处的宽谷，是巴尔蒂人的中心，莫卧儿人称这片土地为「小西藏」。巴尔蒂人操藏语支的巴尔蒂语，这些河谷原是吐蕃诸王治下的佛国；吐蕃崩溃后，本地的默格本王朝在此统治了约七百年。14世纪，米尔·赛义德·阿里·哈马丹尼的门徒从克什米尔翻山而来，巴尔蒂人相传赫布利的恰克钦清真寺即为他们所建，努尔巴赫希亚教团的传教士随后继续传教。1444年，默格本拉杰在斯卡都据守印度河汇流处，王族正在改奉伊斯兰教，而多数河谷仍是喇嘛和佛教村民的天下，商队把山羊毛绒、干果和沙金运往克什米尔与叶尔羌。

约1500年，默格本·博哈定都斯卡都，在镇外高地上建起后来称作卡尔福乔的堡垒，巴尔蒂语意为「万堡之王」，又从克什米尔和吉拉斯招来工匠，振兴新都城的百工。16世纪初，叶尔羌的赛义德汗曾入掠各河谷；锡克教传说也把古鲁·那纳克到访斯卡都系于这几年。1586年阿克巴征服克什米尔后，默格本君主加齐·米尔承认莫卧儿宗主权，莫卧儿史官笔下的斯卡都诸王也成了「小西藏之主」。王朝最伟大的君主阿里·谢尔·汗·安钦1580至1633年在位：拉达克人攻陷卡尔吉尔、屠戮当地驻军后，他绕道马罗尔，约1594年直下列城，俘获拉达克拉杰甲央南嘉，以联姻缔和，堡垒旁为嫁来的拉达克公主建有门多克卡尔宫。其后他又使阿斯托尔、吉尔吉特、罕萨、吉拉斯和奇特拉尔俯首纳贡。他死后诸子争位，1634至1636年扎法尔汗率莫卧儿大军翻山而来裁定继承，此后默格本诸王在莫卧儿势力范围内执政；一位莫卧儿史官统计，这片贫瘠的果乡有22个帕尔加纳、37座堡垒。努尔巴赫希亚教团持续传教，到17世纪末几乎全体巴尔蒂人都成了穆斯林，多数为什叶派。莫卧儿衰落后，默格本诸王在山口之后保住了山地王国，到1821年仍独立。

en:
Inowrocław lies on a brine-rich plain in western Kuyavia, where salt has been boiled from the ground since the eleventh century. The settlement first appears in a document of 1185 as Novus Wladislaw, planted by townsfolk who had left flood-stricken Włocławek, and it was laid out under a Silesian-style charter around 1238. Under the Piast dukes of the fragmentation it was a princely seat, capital first of the Duchy of Kuyavia and then of the Duchy of Inowrocław from 1267 to 1364; Władysław Łokietek, who reunited the kingdom and was crowned in 1320, was one of its dukes. The town sat on the quarrelsome Teutonic frontier: a Polish–Teutonic tribunal judged the Order's seizure of Gdańsk Pomerania here in 1321, the Knights held the town themselves from 1332 to 1337, and Jagiełło ran the closing stages of the 1410 war from its castle after Grunwald. In 1444 Inowrocław was a royal town living by its salt, with further brine deposits discovered nearby in the following decades.

The first Jews settled in 1447, and from 1466 the town was the seat of the Inowrocław Voivodeship covering north-western Kuyavia. The Deluge broke its prosperity: the Swedes took it in the autumn of 1655, and of nearly 250 houses counted in the late sixteenth century only 23 remained in 1659, with about 500 inhabitants; Stefan Czarniecki's troops killed many of the town's Jews in 1656, and John III Sobieski restored their rights in 1680. The Great Northern War brought fresh ruin. In the First Partition of 1772 Inowrocław passed to Prussia, in 1807 to the Duchy of Warsaw, and Napoleon made the town his headquarters during the 1812 march on Russia. After 1815 it returned to Prussian rule in the Grand Duchy of Posen, where its people later took part in the Polish risings against Germanisation.
zh:
伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫坐落在库亚维西部一片富盐的平原上，当地人从11世纪便煮卤取盐。1185年的一份文献首次提到这座聚落，称之为「新瓦迪斯瓦夫」，居民是从遭水灾的弗沃茨瓦韦克迁来，城市约在1238年按西里西亚模式规划建成。分裂割据时期，这里是皮亚斯特公爵的驻地，先后为库亚维公国都城和1267至1364年间伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫公国的都城；重新统一波兰、1320年加冕的瓦迪斯瓦夫·沃凯太克就曾任伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫公爵。此城地处与条顿骑士团纷争不断的边境：1321年波兰与骑士团的仲裁法庭在此审理格但斯克波美拉尼亚归属一案，骑士团1332至1337年一度占据此城，1410年雅盖沃在格伦瓦德战后又坐镇城中城堡指挥战争收尾。1444年，伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫是一座靠盐为生的王家城市，此后几十年间附近还发现了更多盐泉。

1447年首批犹太人来此定居，1466年起城市成为管辖库亚维西北部的伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫省首府。「大洪水」毁了它的繁荣：瑞典人1655年秋攻占此城，16世纪末登记在册的近二百五十栋房屋到1659年只剩二十三栋，居民约五百人；同一场战争中，斯特凡·恰尔涅茨基的部队1656年杀害了城中许多犹太人，扬三世·索别斯基于1680年恢复了他们的权利。大北方战争又添新创。1772年第一次瓜分时伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫划归普鲁士，1807年转入华沙公国，1812年拿破仑征俄途中以此为大本营。1815年后它重归普鲁士治下的波森大公国，当地居民后来投身波兰人的历次起义，抵制德意志化。

en:
Dobrzyń guards a Vistula crossing in the Dobrzyń Land, the region that takes its name from the town. A stronghold stood on its castle hill from the tenth century, and the castellan's gord is named as Dobrin in a document of 1065. In 1228 Konrad of Masovia enfeoffed the place to the Brothers of Dobrzyń, a brotherhood founded by Bishop Christian of Oliva to fight the pagan Prussians and confirmed by Pope Gregory IX the same year; it was the only military order created on Polish soil, and it never numbered more than about thirty-five knights before most of them joined the Teutonic Order around 1235. A town laid out under Lübeck law grew up below the castle. Between 1288 and 1352 Dobrzyń was, with interruptions, the seat of the dukes of Dobrzyń, and it changed hands almost as often: Lithuanians burned it on 14 September 1323 and killed or carried off some 2,000 people, the Teutonic Knights took the castle in 1329, and after Władysław Opolczyk pawned it to the Order it was stormed with artillery on 20 August 1409, when the defender Starosta Jan Chełmicki was beheaded. The First Peace of Toruń returned it to Poland in 1411. In 1444 it was a small royal town of the Inowrocław Voivodeship with a land court, and the nobility of the Dobrzyń Land held their sejmiks here.

Legend makes Dobrzyń the birthplace of Nawojka, the girl who disguised herself as a boy to study at the University of Kraków in the fifteenth century and later became a nun, remembered as Poland's first female student. The town's later history was harsher: Swedish troops burned castle and town in 1657 during the Deluge, and of some 600 houses standing before the wars a survey of 1661 found only 30 inhabited. Dobrzyń never recovered. It passed to Prussia in the Second Partition of 1793, to the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807, and after 1815 to Russian-ruled Congress Poland.
zh:
多布任扼守维斯瓦河的一处渡口，多布任地区便因这座城镇得名。10世纪时城堡山上已有据点，1065年的一份文献已以「多布林」之名记载这座城堡长官府邸。1228年，马佐夫舍公爵康拉德把此地封给多布任骑士会；这个武装修会由奥利瓦的克里斯蒂安创立，专门对付信奉异教的普鲁士人，同年获教皇格列高利九世批准，是唯一在波兰土地上建立的军事修会，人数最多时也只有约三十五名骑士，多数成员约在1235年并入条顿骑士团。城堡脚下，一座按吕贝克法建立的城镇发展起来。1288至1352年间，多布任几度成为多布任公爵的驻地，也同样频繁地易手：1323年9月14日立陶宛人焚城，约两千人被杀或掳走；1329年条顿骑士夺取城堡；奥波莱的瓦迪斯瓦夫后来把它典当给骑士团，1409年8月20日城堡在炮火下陷落，守将扬·海乌米茨基被斩首。1411年第一次托伦和约把它归还波兰。1444年，多布任是伊诺弗罗茨瓦夫省一座设有地区法庭的小王家城市，多布任贵族也在此召开地方议会。

相传纳沃伊卡就出生在多布任：这位15世纪的少女女扮男装进入克拉科夫大学求学，后来成为修女，被视为波兰第一位女学生。城镇此后的命运严酷得多：1657年「大洪水」期间瑞典军队烧毁城堡和全城，战前约六百栋房屋，1661年普查时仅剩三十栋有人居住，多布任再未恢复元气。1793年第二次瓜分中它归属普鲁士，1807年并入华沙公国，1815年后落入俄国治下的波兰会议王国。

en:
Rawa stands on the Rawka River in the southern Mazovian plain. First mentioned in 1228, it became the seat of a castellany in 1313 and received town rights in 1321, as the capital of the Duchy of Rawa. Between 1355 and 1370 Duke Siemowit III ringed the town with walls and built a brick castle, a square moated fortress nearly seventy metres across, set into Casimir the Great's chain of strongholds on Mazovia's southern border. Under Siemowit, who reunited most of Mazovia, Rawa was for a time the capital of the whole duchy. The wars of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries passed it by, and in 1444 it was a prosperous walled seat of the Masovian Piasts on busy inland trade routes.

In 1462 Casimir Jagiellon incorporated the duchy into the Crown and made Rawa the capital of a new voivodeship. From 1562 the castle held the Rawa Treasury, money voted at the Piotrków sejm to pay the Commonwealth's standing army. Its tower also served as a state prison: Carl Carlsson Gyllenhielm, the Swedish commander taken at Kokenhausen in 1601, an illegitimate son of Charles IX of Sweden, wore chains there for six and a half years before he was exchanged for Prince Karol Korecki. The Jesuits ran a collegium in the town, where the memoirist Jan Chryzostom Pasek studied as a boy. Swedish troops seized Rawa during the Deluge, and in April 1656 Charles X Gustav's men burned the town and wrecked the castle; a survey of 1676 found only about a hundred inhabitants. John Casimir lodged in the damaged castle during Lubomirski's rebellion, and the fire of 1766 gutted most of the town. After the Third Partition of 1795 Prussian authorities pulled the castle ruins down except for the tower, and its bricks went into nearby houses. Rawa passed through the Duchy of Warsaw to Congress Poland in 1815.
zh:
雷瓦位于马佐夫舍南部平原的拉夫卡河畔。1228年首见记载，1313年设立城主辖区，1321年获得城市特许，成为雷瓦公国的都城。1355至1370年间，谢莫维特三世公爵环城筑墙，修起一座砖造城堡：方形、围有护城河，边长近七十米，是卡齐米日大帝马佐夫舍南部边境要塞链上的一环。谢莫维特三世重新统一了马佐夫舍的大部分土地，雷瓦一度是整个公国的首都。14、15世纪的战火没有波及这里，1444年的雷瓦是马佐夫舍皮雅斯特王公治下一座繁荣的设防城市，地处繁忙的内陆商路。

1462年，卡齐米日·雅盖隆把公国并入王国，以雷瓦为新置行省的省会。1562年起，城堡中存放「雷瓦金库」，那是彼得库夫议会拨给共和国常备军的税款。城堡主塔还兼作国家监狱：1601年在科肯豪森被俘的瑞典司令卡尔·卡尔松·于伦赫尔姆是瑞典国王卡尔九世的私生子，他戴着镣铐在此关了六年半，后来才被用来交换波兰亲王卡罗尔·科雷茨基。耶稣会在城里办有学院，回忆录作家扬·赫里佐斯托姆·帕塞克年轻时在此求学。大洪水时期瑞典军队占领雷瓦，1656年4月卡尔十世·古斯塔夫的部下焚毁城市、破坏城堡，1676年的调查发现居民只剩约一百人。卢博米尔斯基叛乱期间，扬·卡齐米日曾住进这座残破的城堡；1766年的大火又烧掉大半个城。1795年第三次瓜分后，普鲁士当局拆毁城堡废墟，只留下主塔，拆下的砖石盖了附近的民房。雷瓦后来经过华沙公国，于1815年并入波兰王国。

en:
Gniezno lies among the hills and lakes east of Poznań, on the earliest ground of the Polish state. Polish legend makes it the home of Lech, who travelled north when the three brothers Lech, Czech and Rus went their separate ways: he saw a white eagle guarding its nest against a red sunset, took the sight for an omen, and named his settlement Gniezno, 'the nest'; the white eagle became Poland's arms. A Piast stronghold rose on Lech Hill around 940, and the town served the first Polish dukes as their capital. In 1444 it was a royal county seat of the Polish crown, drawing merchants to four annual fairs, but it mattered most as the seat of Poland's oldest archdiocese.

The cathedral on Lech Hill kept the relics of Saint Adalbert, the Prague bishop killed while preaching to the Prussians in 997; tradition holds that Bolesław the Brave ransomed the body for its weight in gold. In 1000 Bolesław met Emperor Otto III there at the Congress of Gniezno, which founded Poland's first ecclesiastical province, and in 1025 he was crowned king in the cathedral. Mieszko II, Bolesław II in 1076, Przemysł II in 1295 and Wenceslaus II of Bohemia in 1300 were crowned there after him. The Bohemian sack of 1038 drove the court to Kraków. Around 1175 the cathedral received the bronze Gniezno Doors, eighteen Romanesque reliefs of Adalbert's life and one of the major works of its kind in Poland. The Teutonic Knights burned the town again in 1331, and Casimir the Great rebuilt it; in 1419 its archbishop took the title of Primate of Poland, the first prelate of the kingdom.

Fires in 1515 and 1613 and the Swedish invasions of the Deluge emptied and impoverished the town, though Primate Jan Łaski built a brick castle by Lake Jelonek in 1518. The Second Partition of 1793 gave Gniezno to Prussia. Jan Henryk Dąbrowski operated here during the 1794 rising, and in 1806 the townsmen joined his return to Greater Poland, opening the way to the Duchy of Warsaw. Gniezno belonged to that Duchy from 1807 until 1815, when it reverted to Prussia.
zh:
格涅兹诺位于波兹南以东的丘陵湖泊之间，是波兰国家最早的根基之地。波兰传说中，莱赫、捷克、罗斯三兄弟各奔一方，北上的莱赫看见一只白鹰在红色晚霞中守着巢，视为吉兆，便在此定居，以波兰语的「巢」（gniazdo）命名为格涅兹诺，白鹰后来成为波兰的纹章。约940年，皮雅斯特王公在莱赫山上筑起要塞，这里成为波兰最早的都城。1444年时，格涅兹诺是波兰王冠治下的王家县城，每年四场市集吸引各地商人，而它最重要的身份是波兰最古老总主教区的座堂所在地。

莱赫山大教堂供奉着圣阿德尔伯特的遗骨：这位布拉格主教997年向普鲁士人传教时被杀，相传博莱斯瓦夫一世以与遗体等重的黄金将他赎回安葬。1000年，博莱斯瓦夫在此会见神圣罗马帝国皇帝奥托三世，是为格涅兹诺会议，会上设立了波兰第一个教会省；1025年他在大教堂加冕为王，梅什科二世、1076年的博莱斯瓦夫二世、1295年的普热梅斯尔二世和1300年的捷克国王瓦茨拉夫二世也先后在此加冕。1038年捷克军队洗劫城市，王廷随后迁往克拉科夫。约1175年，大教堂装上青铜铸造的格涅兹诺门，十八幅浮雕讲述阿德尔伯特的一生，是波兰最重要的罗曼式艺术品之一。1331年条顿骑士团再焚此城，卡齐米日大帝予以重建；1419年，格涅兹诺总主教领波兰首席大主教衔，位列王国教界之首。

1515年和1613年的大火、大洪水时代的瑞典入侵使城市人口流失、民生凋敝，首席大主教扬·瓦斯基曾在1518年于耶洛内克湖畔修建砖石城堡。1793年第二次瓜分波兰，格涅兹诺划归普鲁士。1794年起义中，扬·亨利克·东布罗夫斯基在此活动；1806年他返回大波兰，市民起而响应，为华沙公国打开道路。格涅兹诺1807年起归入华沙公国，1815年重回普鲁士。

en:
Chęciny lies in the limestone uplands of northern Lesser Poland, pressed against a steep Castle Hill where lead was already being mined in the thirteenth century. First recorded in 1275, it grew up beneath a royal castle raised around 1300, one of the fortresses of Władysław the Short. In May 1331 the king gathered the nobility of Lesser and Greater Poland in the castle to plan the war with the Teutonic Knights, and the keep later served as a state prison: in 1387 Władysław Jagiełło locked up his own brother Andrzej the Hunchback there, and after the Battle of Koronowo in 1410 the Poles held Michael Küchmeister von Sternberg, the future Grand Master of the Order, within its walls. Queens also kept court at Chęciny, among them Adelaide of Hesse, Sophia of Halshany with her young son Władysław of Varna, and Bona Sforza. In 1444 it was a royal town of the Sandomierz Voivodeship, seat of noble courts and of the local lead mines.

The sixteenth century was Chęciny's mining age. Its marble went to churches and royal building sites across the kingdom, and its workings also yielded silver, copper and lead, while weavers ran a busy cloth trade. John Albert gave the miners Olkusz-style rights in 1494, and a Calvinist congregation and a Polish Brethren church made the town a Reformation centre. War ended that. The castle was damaged during the Zebrzydowski rebellion, and on 1 April 1657 George II Rákóczi's Transylvanians sacked and burned Chęciny; plague followed, and the survey of 1660 counted only 48 houses, down from 341 five years earlier. In 1666 John Casimir granted five yearly fairs to draw trade back. A Swedish garrison wrecked the castle again in 1707, its last inhabitants left, and over the next century villagers carried its stones away for building. In the Third Partition of 1795 the town passed to Austria, and in 1815 it passed with Congress Poland to Russia.
zh:
亨齐内位于小波兰北部的石灰岩高地，紧贴一座陡峭的城堡山，13世纪时山上已在开采铅矿。亨齐内1275年首见记载，城在1300年前后修建的王家城堡脚下发展，那是瓦迪斯瓦夫一世的要塞之一。1331年5月，国王在城堡召集小波兰和大波兰的贵族，筹划对条顿骑士团的战争；这座城堡后来又被当作国家监狱：1387年瓦迪斯瓦夫·雅盖沃把自己的弟弟「驼背」安德烈关在这里，1410年科罗诺沃战役之后，波兰人又把后来的骑士团大团长米夏埃尔·屈希迈斯特·冯·施特恩贝格关进城堡。先后也有王后在此驻跸，如黑森的阿德海德、带着幼子瓦迪斯瓦夫（后来的瓦尔纳之王）的霍尔尚斯卡的索菲亚，以及博娜·斯福尔扎。1444年的亨齐内是桑多梅日省的王家城市，贵族法庭和铅矿事务都设在这里。

16世纪是亨齐内的矿业年代：当地大理石运往王国各地的教堂和王家工地，矿场还出产白银、铜和铅，织工们经营着兴旺的呢绒生意。1494年，扬·奥尔布拉赫特授予矿工奥尔库什式采矿权；加尔文宗教堂和波兰兄弟会会堂又使这里成为新教的据点。战乱结束了这一切：泽布日多夫叛乱中城堡受损，1657年4月1日拉科齐·哲尔吉二世的特兰西瓦尼亚军队洗劫并焚毁亨齐内，随后又是瘟疫，1660年的清查只数出48栋房屋，而五年前还有341栋。1666年扬·卡齐米日准许一年开五次集市，想把商路拉回来。1707年瑞典驻军再度毁坏城堡，最后的居民离去后，村民在此后一个世纪里不断拆走城堡的石料。1795年第三次瓜分中亨齐内划归奥地利，1815年随波兰王国并入俄国。

en:
Brześć Kujawski lies on the Zgłowiączka in the middle of Kuyavia, the oldest ducal seat in the region. At the old gord of Stary Brześć, on 23 April 1228, Konrad of Masovia granted the Teutonic Order its first Polish holding, four villages as a temporary endowment. Duke Casimir of Kuyavia chartered the town nearby around 1250, and from 1267 it was the capital of the Duchy of Brześć and the seat of Władysław Łokietek, who set out from here to reunite the Polish lands and was crowned king in 1320. The quarrel with the Order was fought out beneath these walls: in 1321 a papal verdict ordering the Knights to return Gdańsk Pomerania was read out in the town and rejected, their assaults failed in 1327, 1329 and 1331, and an eleven-day siege in 1332 gave them Brześć for eleven years until the Treaty of Kalisz returned it in 1343. Casimir the Great enlarged the castle and granted Bydgoszcz its charter here in 1346. The Knights' last siege, in 1431, failed, and in December 1435 the Peace of Brześć Kujawski ended the war. In 1444 Brześć was a fortified royal city and capital of the Brześć Voivodeship, with the frontier wars at last over.

Casimir IV often stayed in the castle during the Thirteen Years' War, and from 1496 the voivodeship sejmik met in the town. In the sixteenth century Brześć lived by the grain trade, and the 1565 register counted 192 house plots, 115 craftsmen and 108 merchants within its walls. The Deluge undid all this, as the Swedes burned the town hall, the parish church and the castle between 1655 and 1657 and killed every inhabitant of neighbouring Stary Brześć; in 1661 three craftsmen remained, and about 350 people were counted in 1662. The wars of the early eighteenth century and the plague of 1707–09 left three householders. In 1782 Stanisław August allowed the town's Jews to build on a street of their own. Brześć was annexed by Prussia in 1793, passed to the Duchy of Warsaw in 1807, and in 1815 to Russian-ruled Congress Poland.
zh:
库亚维省的首府布热希奇·库亚夫斯基位于库亚维中部的兹格沃维翁奇卡河畔，是这一地区最古老的公爵驻地。1228年4月23日，马佐夫舍公爵康拉德在旧布热希奇的城堡把条顿骑士团在波兰的第一块封地交给骑士团，那只是包括四个村庄的临时封赐。约1250年，库亚维公爵卡齐米日在附近为城市颁下特许状；1267年起，这里成为布热希奇公国都城，也是瓦迪斯瓦夫·沃凯太克的驻地，他从这里出发重新统一波兰诸地，1320年加冕为王。与骑士团的纷争就在这道城墙下展开：1321年，要求骑士团归还格但斯克波美拉尼亚的教皇判词在城中宣读，被骑士团拒绝；他们1327、1329和1331年的三次进攻均告失败，1332年历时十一天的围攻才拿下布热希奇，统治十一年后由1343年的卡利什和约归还波兰。卡齐米日大王扩建了城堡，1346年还在此向比得哥什颁发城市特许状。骑士团1431年最后一次围攻仍告失败，1435年12月，《布热希奇·库亚夫斯基和约》在此终结了战争。1444年，布热希奇是设防的王家城市、布热希奇省首府，边境战火终于远去。

十三年战争期间，卡齐米日四世常住在这座城堡；1496年起，全省地方议会固定在此召开。16世纪的布热希奇靠粮食贸易为生，1565年的登记册载有192处宅地、115名工匠和108名商人。「大洪水」毁了这一切：1655至1657年间瑞典人烧毁市政厅、教区教堂和城堡，还把附近旧布热希奇村的居民全部杀光；1661年全城只剩三名工匠，1662年登记人口约三百五十人。18世纪初的战争和1707至1709年的瘟疫过后，全城仅余三户人家。1782年，斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特准许城中犹太人在专门的街道建房。1793年布热希奇被普鲁士吞并，1807年并入华沙公国，1815年转归俄国治下的波兰会议王国。

en:
Iași lies on the Bahlui stream in the wooded hills of central Moldavia, where the road from Lviv crosses the country on its way to the Black Sea ports. Lviv waggons and steppe caravans made it one of Moldavia's busiest inland markets: Armenian merchants had a church there from 1395, and Prince Alexandru cel Bun's charter of 1408 granting the Lviv merchants their privileges is the town's first written mention. Moldavian wine and cattle went north through its fairs to Poland. In 1444 Iași was a prosperous trading town of Orthodox Moldavia, though the prince's court still sat at Suceava.

The court came to Iași around 1564, when Alexandru Lăpușneanu moved the capital from Suceava, and the city stayed Moldavia's princely seat for nearly three centuries. Its great builder was Vasile Lupu, who raised the Trei Ierarhi Monastery in 1635–1639, founded the Vasilian school and a Romanian-language printing press in 1640, and printed the first Moldavian book in 1643; the Orthodox synod that met here in 1642 answered the Calvinist teaching spreading from Transylvania. Raids were the price of its exposed position, as Tatars, Ottomans, Cossacks and Poles each sacked the wooden town, and fires and plague returned for generations. The scholar-prince Dimitrie Cantemir wrote the first Romanian philosophical work, the Divanul of 1698, and later, in Russian exile, a history of the Ottoman court that long served Europe as its standard book on the Turks; his 1711 alliance with Peter the Great failed and put the Phanariot princes of Constantinople on the Moldavian throne. The peace ending the Russo-Turkish war of 1787–1792 was signed at Iași, and on 24 February 1821 Alexander Ypsilantis proclaimed the Greek rising outside Trei Ierarhi, the act that opened the Greek War of Independence.
zh:
雅西位于摩尔达维亚中部林木葱郁的冈峦间，巴赫卢伊河穿城而过，利沃夫通往黑海诸港的大路在此横贯国土。利沃夫的货车与草原商队使它成为摩尔达维亚最繁忙的内陆市场之一：亚美尼亚商人1395年便在此建有教堂，1408年善人亚历山德鲁颁赐利沃夫商人特权的诏书，则是此城最早的文字记载。摩尔达维亚的葡萄酒和牲畜经这里的集市运往北方的波兰。1444年的雅西是东正教摩尔达维亚一座富庶的商业城镇，不过大公的宫廷当时还设在苏恰瓦。

1564年前后，亚历山德鲁·勒普什内亚努把都城从苏恰瓦迁至雅西，此后近三百年这里都是摩尔达维亚的公国都座。最热心营造的大公是瓦西里·卢普：他在1635至1639年建起三圣修道院，1640年创办瓦西里安学院和罗马尼亚语印刷所，1643年印出摩尔达维亚第一部书；1642年东正教雅西会议在此召开，回应从特兰西瓦尼亚传来的加尔文宗主张。地势暴露，兵祸便成了常事，鞑靼人、奥斯曼人、哥萨克和波兰人都曾洗劫这座木构城市，火灾与瘟疫也一代接一代地重来。学者型大公德米特里·坎泰米尔1698年写成罗马尼亚语第一部哲学著作《迪万》，流亡俄国期间又写出一部奥斯曼宫廷史，长期是欧洲人了解土耳其人的标准读物；他1711年与彼得大帝结盟失败，君士坦丁堡的法纳尔王公就此入主大公之位。结束1787至1792年俄土战争的和约在雅西签订；1821年2月24日，亚历山大·伊普西兰蒂斯在三圣修道院外宣布希腊起义，希腊独立战争由此爆发。

en:
Bârlad sits on the river of the same name in the plains of Moldavia's Lower Country, on the road that runs south from Iași to Galați and the Danube. The great route from Lviv to the Black Sea passed this way, through Iași, Bârlad, Chilia and Cetatea Albă, carrying northern goods toward the Levant, and Byzantine and papal papers called the country around it Terra Berladensis. Prince Alexandru cel Bun gave the town's customs to Bistrița Monastery, and Bârlad merchants appear in the chronicle of the Council of Constance in 1418. The same open ground that made it a market also let raiders reach it: Tatar armies burned the town in 1440 and again in 1444. In November 1444 Bârlad was a frontier fair rebuilding among ashes.

Under Stephen the Great the vornic of the Lower Country kept his seat at Bârlad, and the prince's chancellery sometimes worked from the town; after his victory at Vaslui in 1475 he threw up an earthwork in the river meadow to bar an Ottoman march on central Moldavia.
