The Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453 had already choked the old eastern road, and Tatars, Turks, Cossacks and Poles raided in turn. In 1758 a Tatar host put by the contemporary writer Daponte at more than 100,000 men burned Bârlad to the ground; the great earthquake of 1802 threw down what old buildings had risen again. On 20 March 1820 Alexandru Ioan Cuza, the future first prince of the united Romanian principalities, was born in the rebuilt lower town.
zh:
伯尔拉德位于摩尔达维亚下国平原上的同名河畔，在雅西南下加拉茨与多瑙河的道路上。利沃夫通往黑海的大商路取道于此，经雅西、伯尔拉德、基利亚和白堡，把北方货物运往黎凡特，拜占庭和教廷文书把这一带称为伯尔拉德尼克之地。善人亚历山德鲁曾把此城的关税赐给比斯特里察修道院，1418年康斯坦茨宗教会议的纪事里也有伯尔拉德商人的名字。开阔的平原既养出了市集，也方便敌军长驱直入：鞑靼军队1440年焚毁此城，1444年又来一次。1444年11月的伯尔拉德是一座在灰烬中重建的边地市集。

斯特凡大公时代，摩尔达维亚下国总管驻节伯尔拉德，大公的掌玺厅有时也在此办公；1475年瓦斯卢伊大捷之后，他在河漫滩上筑起一座土木工事，阻挡奥斯曼军队进扑摩尔达维亚腹地。1453年奥斯曼攻占君士坦丁堡，旧的东方商路受阻，鞑靼人、土耳其人、哥萨克和波兰人又轮番来袭。1758年，据时人作家达蓬特记载，一支十多万人的鞑靼大军把伯尔拉德烧成白地；1802年的大地震又震塌了劫后重建的老屋。1820年3月20日，后来成为罗马尼亚联合诸邦第一位大公的亚历山德鲁·伊万·库扎，出生在这座重建之城的下区。

en:
Giurgiu lies among the marshes and mudflats on the Wallachian bank of the Danube, facing the Bulgarian shore and the fortress of Rusçuk; small islands screen its harbour. Its first certain mention is in the Codex Latinus Parisinus, which calls the place Zorio and marks it as waste, probably after the Ottoman raid of 1394 against Mircea the Old. An old story that Genoese merchants founded the town and named it San Giorgio after their patron saint has been discarded by historians. The Ottomans took Giurgiu in 1417 to command the Danube crossing, and as Yergöğü it became a raia, a sultan's fortress on Wallachian soil, its garrison supplied from across the river. In 1444 the stronghold facing Rusçuk was Turkish, while the countryside around it belonged to Wallachia.

The fortress had its most famous night in the winter of 1461–62. Mehmed II had sent Hamza Bey of Nicopolis, with a thousand cavalry, to seize Vlad the Impaler at a sham parley near the town; Vlad ambushed the party in a narrow pass, and Hamza and the sultan's Greek envoy were taken and put to death. He then rode to the gates and, in fluent Turkish, ordered the garrison commander to open them; his men broke in and plundered the stronghold before his winter campaign across the Danube. Enlarged in 1560 and made a kaza, Giurgiu was the Ottomans' nearest bridgehead to Bucharest. In October 1595 Michael the Brave and his Transylvanian allies caught Grand Vizier Sinan Pasha's retreating army at the crossing and cut it to pieces; the Turks remembered the day as the Bridge Disaster, and Michael held the fortress for two years. The town was burned in 1659 during Mihnea III's attempt to retake it. In 1771 the Ottomans raised a clocktower above the river to watch the boat traffic, and after further sieges in the Russo-Turkish wars that followed, Giurgiu remained the sultan's garrison and munitions store in 1821.
zh:
久尔久位于多瑙河瓦拉几亚一岸的沼泽与滩涂之间，几座小岛遮着港口，与保加利亚岸上的鲁斯楚克要塞隔江相望。它现存最早的确凿记载见于《巴黎拉丁抄本》，书中称此地为佐里奥，标作废墟，大概是1394年奥斯曼进犯老米尔恰之后的样子。热那亚商人在此建城、并以其主保圣人圣乔治（San Giorgio）命名的旧说，已被学界放弃。1417年，奥斯曼人攻占久尔久以控制多瑙河渡口，土耳其语称之为耶尔格于，把它设为拉亚，即苏丹设在瓦拉几亚土地上的直属要塞，守军给养由南岸补给。1444年，对着鲁斯楚克的这座要塞在土耳其人手中，周围乡野则属于瓦拉几亚。

这座要塞最出名的一夜在1461至1462年冬天。穆罕默德二世派尼科波利斯长官哈姆扎贝伊率一千骑兵，借假谈判在久尔久附近擒拿穿刺公弗拉德；弗拉德在一道狭谷里设下埋伏，哈姆扎和苏丹的希腊籍使者被俘处死。随后他驰到要塞门前，用流利的土耳其语喝令守将开门，瓦拉几亚人冲入城内劫掠，然后渡河南征。1560年要塞扩建并升为卡扎，成为奥斯曼距布加勒斯特最近的桥头堡。1595年10月，勇士米哈依和特兰西瓦尼亚盟军在渡口截住大维齐尔锡南帕夏撤退的大军，将其杀得大败；土耳其人把这一天称作「桥梁之灾」，米哈依据守要塞两年。1659年，城市在米赫内亚三世试图收复它的战事中被焚。1771年，奥斯曼人在江边建起钟楼监视舟楫；此后的俄土战争中它又屡遭围攻，到1821年仍是苏丹的驻军要塞和军火库。

en:
Severin guards the Danube where the river leaves the Iron Gates gorges, at the narrow crossing between the Hungarian plain and the Balkans. The Romans built Drobeta here, below Trajan's Bridge of AD 103–105, thrown across the river by Apollodorus of Damascus, and the medieval fortress rose on the Roman stones long after the bridge was gone. In 1233 King Andrew II of Hungary organised the Banate of Severin, a march stretching on both sides of the mountains, and the Knights of St John briefly took over its defence a few years later. Litovoi, an early Wallachian voivode, fell beneath its walls in 1272, and Basarab I lost the fortress in 1330 only to win it back after Posada. Mircea the Old, himself a former ban of Severin, signed his alliance with King Sigismund here. The Turks took the fortress in 1417 and burned it ten years later; by 1444 it was Hungarian again, held for the king by John Hunyadi. That September part of the Varna crusade forded into Bulgaria at this crossing, and seven weeks later the crusader army was destroyed at Varna.

Suleiman's army took the fortress in October 1524, and in 1526 it was systematically dismantled: its dressed stone was ferried across to strengthen Ottoman forts on the Bulgarian bank, and only a fragment of the keep was left, the Tower of Severin that later gave the place its name of Turnu. The townspeople moved six kilometres inland to Cerneți, which became the market, customs seat and district capital of the Mehedinți country, while the banate's Oltenian lands went to the bans of Craiova. Michael the Brave's Wallachians held the riverside from 1594 to 1599. After the Peace of Passarowitz in 1718 the Austrians occupied the ground and even planned a new town called Carolina, but the Turks returned in the late 1730s and the old site became a crossing watched from the southern bank. Through the wars of the eighteenth century Russian and Austrian armies used Cerneți in turn, and the town kept the district trade in livestock, hides and grain. In 1821 the Tower of Severin still stood on the Ottoman bank.
zh:
塞韦林扼守多瑙河出铁门峡谷之处，是匈牙利平原与巴尔干之间最狭窄的渡口。罗马人曾在此建德罗贝塔城；公元103至105年，大马士革的阿波罗多罗斯主持修建的图拉真桥横跨江面，桥毁多年之后，中世纪的城堡又取用罗马旧石建起。1233年，匈牙利国王安德拉什二世设立塞韦林巴纳特，这片边地横跨山脉两侧，医院骑士团数年后曾短暂接防。瓦拉几亚早期王公利托沃伊于1272年战死在城墙之下，巴萨拉布一世1330年失守城堡，波萨达战役得胜后又将其收复。老米尔恰本人做过塞韦林班，他与匈牙利国王西吉斯孟德的盟约就在此签订。1417年土耳其人攻陷城堡，十年后将其焚毁；到1444年它已重归匈牙利，由亚诺什·匈雅提为国王镇守。这一年9月，瓦尔纳十字军一部在此涉水进入保加利亚，七周后，十字军在瓦尔纳覆灭。

1524年10月，苏莱曼的大军攻陷城堡；1526年城堡被有系统地拆除，凿下的石料运到南岸加固奥斯曼要塞，只留下主堡的一段残墙，人称「塞韦林之塔」，后来图尔努（意为「塔」）的地名也得自这座残塔。居民迁往内地六公里的切尔内齐，那里成为梅赫丁茨一带的集镇、税关和地区中心，巴纳特在奥尔特尼亚的土地则归克拉约瓦的各班所有。勇士米哈依的瓦拉几亚军于1594至1599年据守河畔。1718年《波扎雷瓦茨和约》后，奥地利人占领此地，还规划过一座名为卡罗利纳的新城；1730年代末土耳其人卷土重来，古堡旧址成了一个受南岸监视的渡口。18世纪的战争中，切尔内齐先后为俄军和奥军所用，当地牲畜、皮革和粮食的贸易则一直维持。1821年，奥斯曼一侧的河岸上只剩塞韦林之塔。

en:
Wieluń is the chief town of the Wieluń Land, a march in the Warta basin facing Czech-ruled Silesia. The district was first run from the castellan's gord at nearby Ruda, already named in the Bull of Gniezno of 1136; the seat moved to Wieluń in 1281, and in 1283 Przemysł II granted the settlement rights modeled on Kalisz. Casimir the Great raised a stone castle here to guard the frontier, and after his death Louis I gave the land to Władysław Opolczyk, who made Wieluń the capital of his duchy from 1370 to 1391 and founded the Paulist abbey. Jagiełło retook the castle in 1391, and in 1424 he issued the Edict of Wieluń here, outlawing the Hussite movement in Poland under pressure from the Church. In 1444 the town held a freshly granted staple right, but its border location kept it exposed, as Silesian dukes' raiders sacked it repeatedly through the 1440s and 1450s.

In the sixteenth century the starosty formed part of Queen Bona Sforza's estates and the castle lodged royal women: Isabella, queen of Hungary, spent the autumn of 1553 here receiving envoys, and Catherine Habsburg, third wife of Sigismund II Augustus, stayed nine months in 1566 before leaving Poland. In the succession war of 1587–88 the town opened its gates to the Habsburg claimant Maximilian; he lodged here in January 1588, and within days Jan Zamoyski routed his army and took him prisoner at Byczyna in Silesia. A fire of 1631 consumed nearly all the town, and during the Deluge a Swedish garrison held the castle from November 1655 to May 1656, even after Polish troops retook the town in January 1656, and burned it when they withdrew. Wieluń never recovered its standing. It was annexed by Prussia in 1793 and passed to Russian-ruled Congress Poland in 1815.
zh:
维隆是维隆地区的首城，地处瓦尔塔河流域，与捷克治下的西里西亚接壤，是一片边防要地。这一带最早的统治中心在附近鲁达的城堡长官据点，1136年的格涅兹诺诏书已有其名；1281年城堡长官驻地迁至维隆，1283年普热梅斯瓦夫二世颁令，让它参照卡利什的权利立市。卡齐米日大王在此修筑石砌城堡镇守边境，他死后路易一世把这片土地封给奥波莱的瓦迪斯瓦夫，后者在1370至1391年间以维隆为自己公国的都城，并创立保罗会修道院。1391年雅盖沃武力收复城堡，1424年又在此颁布《维隆敕令》，应教会要求在波兰取缔胡斯派。1444年，维隆刚取得仓储特权，但边城始终难得安宁，1440至1450年代西里西亚诸公爵的袭掠者一再洗劫此城。

16世纪，维隆城堡辖区成为博娜·斯福尔扎王后御用地产的一部分，城堡也专门接待王室女眷：匈牙利王后伊莎贝拉1553年秋天在此驻跸、接见使节，齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特的第三任王后卡塔日娜·哈布斯堡1566年在此住了九个月，随后离开波兰。1587至1588年王位继承战争中，城市向哈布斯堡家族的争位者马克西米利安开城，他1588年1月在此下榻；不过几天之后，扬·扎莫伊斯基就在西里西亚的贝奇纳击溃并生俘了他。1631年的大火几乎吞没全城；「大洪水」期间，瑞典守军在1655年11月至1656年5月间占据城堡，1656年1月波兰军队收复城区也未能迫使他们撤出，瑞军撤离时又把城堡付之一炬。维隆再未恢复往日地位，1793年被普鲁士吞并，1815年转归俄国治下的波兰会议王国。

en:
Upytė, 'the little river', was the northernmost Baltic land of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, a lowland of the Nevėžis facing Semigallia and the Livonian frontier. Its island castle stood in Lake Vešeta, and between 1353 and 1379 it beat off ten Livonian Order assaults; the Order overran it in 1398 and gave it back only with the Melno peace. In 1444 Upytė was a powiat of Trakai Voivodeship, a country of forests, cattle and cavalry service whose starosts sat in the island castle. Its starosts included Konstanty Ostrogski, victor of the battle of Orsha in 1514, and the small town of Biržai nearby already appears in Riga border records of 1416.

The land's later fame came from Biržai. After Barbara Radziwiłł married King Sigismund II Augustus in 1547, the Radziwiłłs made the town the seat of their duchy and built it into a Lithuanian centre of Calvinism, with Protestant churches and schools and a Jewish community that ran an international linen trade. A dam on the local rivers in 1587 created Lake Širvėna, the brick water-castle rose on its shore in 1586–1589, and Magdeburg law followed in 1589. Gustavus Adolphus took the castle at the head of 8,000 men in 1625, and after a second sack in 1657 it was rebuilt in Renaissance form from 1662. In 1652 the Upytė deputy Władysław Siciński broke up the Warsaw Sejm with the first liberum veto in the Commonwealth's history; he was said to have been put up to it by Janusz Radziwiłł, and a later folk legend had the thunder god Perkūnas strike him down for it. On 9 March 1701 Augustus II met Peter the Great in the castle and allied with him against Sweden, and in 1704 the Swedes blew the castle up and burned the town. During the Kościuszko rising of 1794 Giedroyć defeated a Russian army at Saločiai, but the third partition of 1795 gave the land to Russia, and in 1812 MacDonald's Prussian corps marched through on the road to Riga.
zh:
乌皮塔意为「小河」，是立陶宛大公国最北边的波罗的人土地，即涅韦日斯河流域面向泽姆加利亚和利沃尼亚边境的低地。韦谢塔湖中的岛堡曾在1353至1379年间击退利沃尼亚骑士团的十次进攻；1398年骑士团一度攻占此地，梅尔诺议和后才归还。1444年，乌皮塔是特拉凯省的一个县，境内遍布森林、牧场和骑兵役户，县尉驻在岛上城堡；历任县尉中包括1514年奥尔沙之战的胜者康斯坦丁·奥斯特罗格斯基，附近的小镇比尔扎伊也已出现在1416年的里加边地文书中。

这片土地后来的名气全在比尔扎伊。1547年芭芭拉·拉齐维乌嫁给国王齐格蒙特二世·奥古斯特后，拉齐维乌家族把该镇立为本支公国的中心，经营成立陶宛加尔文宗的重镇，建起新教教堂和学校，16世纪末定居于此的犹太人还经营着一笔跨国亚麻生意。1587年，当地两河被拦腰筑坝，汇成希尔维纳湖；砖石水堡于1586至1589年在湖畔建起，1589年城镇又获马格德堡法。1625年，古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫率兵八千攻下城堡；1657年再遭洗劫后，城堡自1662年起按文艺复兴风格重建。1652年，本县议员瓦迪斯瓦夫·西钦斯基动用自由否决权解散华沙议会，为联邦史上头一回；据传他受雅努什·拉齐维乌指使，后世民间传说更讲雷神佩尔孔纳斯将他劈死。1701年3月9日，奥古斯特二世在城堡中会见彼得大帝，缔盟共抗瑞典；瑞典人1704年炸毁城堡、焚毁城镇作为回应。1794年柯斯丘什科起义中，盖德劳伊茨在萨洛奇艾击败俄军，但1795年第三次瓜分把这片土地划给俄国，1812年麦克唐纳的普鲁士军团经此开往里加。

en:
Wilkimierz, called Vilkmerge by Lithuanians, stands in the old Lithuanian land of Deltuva, where a wooden hill castle overlooked the Šventoji River. That castle first appears in a Livonian chronicle in 1333, when the Order's raiders reached its walls. Teutonic and Livonian armies returned in 1365, 1378 and 1386, and burned the castle in 1391. After Lithuania's conversion in 1387, St Peter and St Paul became one of the country's earliest Catholic parish churches. The fields beside the river then decided a Lithuanian civil war. On 1 September 1435 Grand Duke Sigismund Kęstutaitis and his Polish allies routed Švitrigaila and the Livonian Order at Pabaiskas; the defeat ended the Order's major part in Lithuanian politics. Sigismund built the Church of the Holy Trinity on the battlefield between 1436 and 1440. In 1444 a rebuilt brick castle stood above a town tied to the Catholic grand duchy.

Wilkimierz never became a large city, but the Vilnius road and county administration kept it active as a market town. It held municipal rights by 1486 and after 1566 became a county centre in Vilnius Voivodeship. Swedish and Russian troops plundered it during the Deluge in 1655; Jewish families settled in the following decades, and plague cut through the population in 1711-12. Stanisław August renewed the town rights and granted a coat of arms in 1792, only three years before the Third Partition placed Wilkimierz, under the Russian name Vilkomir, in the Russian Empire. In 1812 the Battle of Deltuva was fought nearby, and French troops raided the town during the invasion of Russia.
zh:
乌克梅尔盖（波兰语旧称维尔基米日，立陶宛语旧称维尔克梅尔盖）位于古老的立陶宛代尔图瓦地区，一座山丘木堡俯临什文托伊河。1333年，立窝尼亚编年史第一次记载这个定居点，当时骑士团袭扰者已兵临城下。条顿和立窝尼亚军队又在1365、1378和1386年来袭，并在1391年烧毁木堡。1387年立陶宛皈依基督教后，圣彼得与圣保罗堂成为全国最早的天主堂区教堂之一。河畔原野随后决定了一场立陶宛内战的走向。1435年9月1日，西吉斯蒙德·科斯图泰提斯大公率波兰盟军在帕巴伊斯卡斯击溃斯维特里盖拉和立窝尼亚骑士团；此役后，骑士团不再能左右立陶宛大局。1436至1440年，西吉斯蒙德在战场修建圣三教堂。1444年，重建的砖堡俯临这座已归入天主教立陶宛大公国的城镇。

乌克梅尔盖没有发展成大城市，但维尔纽斯大道和县治机构让它保持着市镇规模。它在1486年已被文献称为城市，1566年后成为维尔纽斯省的县治。1655年大洪水期间，瑞典和俄国军队先后劫掠全镇；此后几十年犹太家族迁入，1711至1712年的瘟疫又使人口大减。1792年，斯坦尼斯瓦夫·奥古斯特更新城市权并赐下纹章；仅三年后，第三次瓜分便把俄语称维尔科米尔的此地划入俄罗斯帝国。1812年，代尔图瓦之战在附近打响，法军在进军俄国途中洗劫此镇。

en:
Lida grew up below a brick castle that Gediminas began in 1323 on rising ground between the Kamenka and Lida rivers. The citadel belonged to a chain of strongholds covering Vilnius and Trakai against the Teutonic Knights, with two angle towers and boulder walls faced in red brick. After Gediminas died it became an appanage centre for Algirdas, and later served Kęstutis, Jogaila and Vytautas. Crusaders raided repeatedly after 1384 and took the place at times. In 1396-99 Vytautas sheltered his ally Tokhtamysh, the fugitive khan of the Golden Horde, who camped near the walls after losing power. Jogaila founded the Catholic parish after the Union of Krewo and visited Lida in 1415 and 1422. In 1444 merchants and craftsmen occupied four streets around a market square beneath the grand-ducal castle, on roads to Vilnius, Minsk and Navahrudak.

The castle remained a useful mobilisation point. In 1506, while Crimean Tatars raided Lithuania, Alexander Jagiellon convened a sejm at Lida; the army mustered there and marched under Michael Glinski to Kletsk, where it defeated the khan's sons on 5 August. Lida became a county centre in 1568 and received Magdeburg rights, a coat of arms and two yearly fairs from Sigismund III in 1590. War undid the small town: Cossacks sacked it in 1655, Russians stormed it in 1659, Swedes plundered it in 1702, and the old castle burned in 1710. A tax privilege in 1676 brought settlers back, but only 514 people remained in 1786. The Third Partition assigned Lida to Russia in 1795, and Napoleonic troops destroyed much of the rebuilt town in 1812.
zh:
利达的城镇围绕砖堡发展。1323年起，格迪米纳斯大公在卡缅卡河与利达河之间的高地上修建这座城堡，作为掩护维尔纽斯和特拉凯、抵御条顿骑士的要塞链一环；城堡有两座角楼，巨石墙外砌红砖。格迪米纳斯死后，利达成为阿尔吉尔达斯的封地中心，后来又供科斯图泰提斯、约盖拉和维陶塔斯使用。1384年后十字军屡次来犯并曾攻占此地。1396至1399年，维陶塔斯收留败逃的金帐汗脱脱迷失；这位失去权位的盟友曾在城墙附近的毡帐中驻留。克列沃联合后，约盖拉建立天主教堂区，并在1415和1422年两度到利达。1444年，商人和手工业者住在大公城堡下的集市广场和四条街道旁，道路通向维尔纽斯、明斯克和新格鲁多克。

城堡仍是实用的动员据点。1506年克里木鞑靼人袭扰立陶宛时，亚历山大·雅盖隆契克在利达召集议会；军队在此集结，由米哈伊尔·格林斯基率领开赴克列茨克，在8月5日击败汗王的儿子们。1568年利达成为县治，1590年齐格蒙特三世授予马格德堡法、纹章和每年两次市集。战争随后拖垮这座小镇：1655年哥萨克洗劫，1659年俄军强攻，1702年瑞典人劫掠，古堡也在1710年焚毁。1676年的免税特权招回部分居民，但到1786年全城只剩514人。1795年第三次瓜分把利达划归俄国，1812年拿破仑军队又摧毁了重建后城镇的大部。

en:
Navahrudak, called Nowogródek in Polish, occupies a ridge in Black Ruthenia, west of the Pripyat marshes. Its hilltop ramparts looked over craft quarters, where archaeologists have found jewellery workshops and imported Baltic amber, Byzantine glass and Iranian faience. The Hypatian Codex gives its first reliable mention in 1252, as Novogorodok, the 'new little town'. Mindaugas soon used it as one of his chief seats, his son Vaišvilkas ruled there, and tradition places Mindaugas's coronation as king of Lithuania in 1253 in a field below the town. Teutonic armies repeatedly attacked the hill castle between 1314 and 1394. In 1415 Orthodox bishops meeting there elected Gregory Tsamblak as their metropolitan, and in 1422 Jogaila married Sophia of Halshany in the town; their children continued the Jagiellonian line. Vytautas settled Lipka Tatars in the district. In 1444 Navahrudak was a grand-ducal demesne town, largely Orthodox Ruthenian, with wool as its principal trade.

In 1507 Navahrudak became the capital of the Nowogródek Voivodeship. The Reformation won many followers there, and from 1581 the Lithuanian Tribunal held its Ruthenian sessions in the town. After the Union of Brest, its metropolitan see turned Uniate. Russian forces held it from 1655 to 1661, Swedish troops blew up the old castle in 1706, and the fire of 1751 destroyed 167 houses, four churches and the town hall. It passed to Russia in the Third Partition of 1795. The poet Adam Mickiewicz was born on a nearby estate in 1798, was baptised in the town's Transfiguration Church and spent his childhood in Navahrudak. When Napoleon's army occupied the district in 1812, local infantry and uhlan regiments were raised there for his campaign.
zh:
新格鲁多克（波兰语称诺沃格鲁代克）位于普里皮亚季沼泽以西、黑鲁塞尼亚的一道高岗上。山顶城垒下方是手工业街区，考古曾发现珠宝作坊，以及波罗的海琥珀、拜占庭玻璃和伊朗彩陶等外来器物。《伊帕季耶夫编年史》在1252年首次可靠地提到它，称其为「诺沃戈罗多克」，意为「小新城」。明道加斯很快把这里作为主要驻地之一，其子瓦伊什维尔卡斯在此统治；相传明道加斯1253年加冕立陶宛国王的地点就在城下郊野。1314至1394年间，条顿军队反复攻打山堡。1415年，东正教主教会在此选出格里戈里·察姆布拉克为都主教；1422年，雅盖沃在此迎娶索菲娅，两人的子嗣延续了雅盖隆王朝。维陶塔斯还把利普卡鞑靼人安置在这一带。1444年，新格鲁多克是大公直辖领地的重镇，居民多为信奉东正教的鲁塞尼亚人，羊毛是主要贸易品。

1507年，新格鲁多克成为新格鲁多克省首府。宗教改革在此吸引了许多信徒，1581年起，立陶宛法庭的鲁塞尼亚庭期在此开庭。布列斯特联合后，当地都主教区并入东仪天主教会。1655年至1661年俄军占领此城；1706年瑞典军队炸毁古堡，1751年大火又烧毁167所房屋、4座教堂和市政厅。1795年第三次瓜分后，新格鲁多克并入俄国。诗人亚当·密茨凯维奇1798年出生在附近庄园，在城中教堂受洗，并在新格鲁多克度过童年。1812年拿破仑军队占领这一带时，当地还为其战事组建了步兵和枪骑兵团。

en:
Chełm crowns a chalk hill above the Uherka, a tributary of the Western Bug, in the old land of the Cherven Towns. A gord on Wysoka Górka first served as a pagan cult centre, and the stronghold passed back and forth between early Poland and Kyivan Rus. Daniel of Galicia granted the town a charter in 1235 and moved his capital here after the Mongols destroyed Halych; his new castle on the hill was one of the few Ruthenian fortresses that withstood the Mongol assault, and the Orthodox eparchy he founded drew Ruthenian, Polish and German settlers and refugees from the steppe. Casimir III of Poland took the region in 1366, and after nine years under Hungarian rule Chełm returned to Poland and was relocated under Magdeburg law in 1392. In 1444 it is a royal Polish border town, where Ruthenian townsmen and Orthodox clergy live beside Catholic settlers and Jewish merchants on the roads between Lublin, Belz and Volhynia.

Chełm prospered in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries as the seat of noble courts and, from 1541, a staple town; chalk mined beneath it from the sixteenth to the eighteenth centuries left kilometres of tunnels under the old town. Its Jews made it famous across rabbinic Europe: Elijah Ba'al Shem, chief rabbi of Chełm until his death in 1583, was a kabbalist of such repute that legend credited him with fashioning a golem. After the 1596 Union of Brest the old Orthodox bishopric passed to the Greek Catholics. In 1648 Khmelnytsky's Cossacks burned Chełm and killed nearly its entire Jewish community, and the town recovered only slowly as Catholic, Orthodox and Jewish settlers returned in the eighteenth century. It was among the first towns to join Kościuszko's rising in 1794, but on 8 June General Zajączek's force was defeated outside it by the Russians and the town was sacked. The Third Partition gave Chełm to Austria in 1795, the Napoleonic wars briefly carried it to the Duchy of Warsaw, and from 1815 it belonged to Russian-ruled Congress Poland.
zh:
海乌姆雄踞西布格河支流乌赫尔卡河畔的白垩山丘，属古老的切尔文诸城之地。维索卡山上的堡寨最初是异教崇拜中心，这座要塞早年在波兰与基辅罗斯之间反复易手。丹尼尔·加利茨基1235年授予城镇特许状，蒙古人摧毁加利奇后把都城迁到这里；他在山上新建的城堡是少数顶住蒙古进攻的罗斯要塞之一，他设立的东正教区又引来鲁塞尼亚人、波兰人、德意志移民和躲避草原战祸的难民。波兰国王卡齐米日三世1366年取得此地，海乌姆在匈牙利治下过了九年后复归波兰，1392年依马格德堡法重新设城。1444年的海乌姆是波兰王室的边境城镇，在卢布林、贝尔兹与沃里尼亚之间往来的道路上，鲁塞尼亚市民、东正教神职人员与天主教移民、犹太商人比邻而居。

15至16世纪，海乌姆作为贵族法庭所在地而兴盛，1541年又取得货物集散权；16至18世纪在城下开采白垩，老城区地下留下纵横数公里的坑道。城中的犹太人更让它闻名于拉比的欧洲：埃利亚·巴阿尔·谢姆1583年去世前一直担任海乌姆首席拉比，这位卡巴拉学者声名之盛，相传他曾造出一个戈仑。1596年布列斯特联合后，旧东正主教区转入希腊天主教徒手中。1648年，赫梅利尼茨基的哥萨克焚毁海乌姆，几乎杀光犹太居民；直到18世纪天主教徒、东正教徒和犹太人重新迁入，城镇才慢慢恢复。1794年，它是最早响应柯斯丘什科起义的城镇之一，但6月8日扎扬切克将军的部队就在城外被俄军击败，城镇再遭洗劫。1795年第三次瓜分波兰后海乌姆归属奥地利，拿破仑战争中一度并入华沙公国，1815年起成为俄国治下波兰王国的城市。

en:
Kremenets guards a rocky height at the northern edge of the Kremenets Mountains, where the little Irva stream runs toward the Ikva on the road between Volhynia and Podolia. Its fortress is first reliably mentioned in 1227, a year after Prince Mstislav the Bold defeated the Hungarian army of King Andrew II nearby, and in 1241 it was one of the few Ruthenian strongholds Batu Khan failed to storm. After the collapse of Galicia–Volhynia the hill passed through Hungarian, Polish and Lithuanian hands; Liubartas took it from Hungary in 1382, and later in the fourteenth century a stone castle replaced the older earth-and-timber works. Svidrigailo, who had once been imprisoned in the castle, granted the town Magdeburg rights in 1438. In 1444 Kremenets is a small Orthodox Ruthenian garrison town on Lithuania's exposed southern frontier, its towers watching the roads toward Podolia and the steppe.

Tatar raids emptied the town later in the fifteenth century, but in the 1530s King Sigismund I gave the castle to his wife Bona Sforza. She rebuilt it with three towers, high walls, guns and barracks, and in her twenty years as mistress Kremenets revived into one of the leading markets of the region; one account derives the name of the castle hill from her. The Union of Lublin transferred it to the Polish Crown in 1569. In autumn 1648 Colonel Maksym Kryvonos besieged the castle for six weeks, and when it fell in October the royal garrison was carried off and the fortress was demolished, never to be rebuilt. After the Third Partition of 1795 Kremenets entered the Russian Empire and, a year later, the Volhynian Governorate. Its later fame came from books: the Higher Volhynian Gymnasium, founded by Tadeusz Czacki, opened in 1805 and was reorganised as the Volhynian Lyceum, whose library held more than 50,000 volumes, among them 1,500 incunabula printed before 1500, and contemporaries called the town the Volhynian Athens. The poet Juliusz Słowacki, one of the Three Bards of Polish literature, was born here in 1809.
zh:
克列梅涅茨扼守克列梅涅茨山脉北缘的岩丘，伊尔瓦小溪从此流向伊克瓦河，正当沃里尼亚通往波多利亚的道路。城堡在1227年首次有可靠记载，此前一年姆斯季斯拉夫·勇猛王公就在附近击败匈牙利国王安德烈二世的军队；1241年，它又是拔都汗未能攻下的少数罗斯要塞之一。加利西亚-沃里尼亚崩溃后，山堡在匈牙利、波兰和立陶宛之间易手；1382年柳巴尔塔斯从匈牙利手中夺取此地，14世纪后期石堡取代了旧有土木工事。曾被囚禁在城堡中的斯维特里盖拉1438年授予城镇马格德堡权利。1444年的克列梅涅茨是立陶宛暴露的南方边境上一座小型东正教鲁塞尼亚军镇，塔楼监视着通往波多利亚和草原的道路。

15世纪后期，鞑靼袭掠使城镇人口流散；16世纪30年代，波兰国王齐格蒙特一世把城堡赐给妻子博娜·斯福尔扎。她重修城堡，建起三座塔楼、高墙、火炮和营房，在她领有的二十年间，克列梅涅茨复苏为当地首屈一指的市场之一；有一种说法认为城堡山即以她命名。1569年卢布林联合后，克列梅涅茨划归波兰王冠领。1648年秋，马克西姆·克里沃尼斯上校围攻城堡六周；10月城陷后王室守军被俘，要塞被拆毁，再未重建。1795年第三次瓜分波兰后克列梅涅茨并入俄国，次年划入沃里尼亚省。它后来的名声来自书卷：塔德乌什·恰茨基创办的沃里尼亚高级中学1805年开学，后改组为沃里尼亚学园，藏书超过五万卷，其中包括1500册摇篮本，即1500年以前刊印的早期书籍，时人因而称此城为「沃里尼亚雅典」。波兰文学三大诗人之一尤利乌什·斯沃瓦茨基1809年出生于此。

en:
Vinnytsia lies on the Southern Boh below Bratslav, where the forest thins into the Podolian steppe. The Lithuanian princes Koriatovychi built a wooden fortress there from the 1360s to the 1380s, and the town appears in their charters of 1391 and 1392; Vytautas enfeoffed it together with Bratslav to Dmytro Korybut in 1395. A Tatar raid burned the place in 1430. In 1444 Vinnytsia is a small Lithuanian frontier post under a starosta, held by Orthodox Ruthenian townsmen and a garrison who watch the Black Tatar Trail and rebuild when the raiders have passed.

A stone castle went up around 1512; a later one raised by Kostiantyn Ostrozky burned in 1580, and crown charters of 1580, 1593 and 1634 granted the town yearly fairs. The courts and sejmiks moved from Bratslav to Vinnytsia in 1554. Jesuits arrived in 1611 and opened a college in 1642, two years after the town received Magdeburg rights. Khmelnytsky's Cossacks entered Vinnytsia in July 1648, and the Treaty of Zboriv assigned it to the Hetmanate the next year. From 11 to 21 March 1651 Colonel Ivan Bohun, with 3,000 Cossacks and townsmen, held the town against Marcin Kalinowski's 12,000-strong Crown army and routed it. Vinnytsia remained a Cossack regimental seat until the Andrusovo truce returned it to Poland in 1667. The Ottomans claimed it after Buchach in 1672, but Crown troops reoccupied the town in 1674, and Jan Sobieski restored the Cossack regiment there in 1685. Haidamakas sacked it in 1750, and plague took 1,330 lives in 1770 and 1771. Antoni Protazy Potocki opened his Polish Trade Company in Vinnytsia in 1783, and the Second Partition assigned the town to Russia in 1793.
zh:
温尼察位于南布格河畔、布拉茨拉夫下游，处在林地渐稀、没入波多里亚草原的过渡带上。1360至1380年代，立陶宛的科里亚特维奇王公修建木堡，1391至1392年的王公文书已提到这座城镇；1395年维陶塔斯把它与布拉茨拉夫一同封给德米特罗·科里布特。1430年一次鞑靼来袭把此地烧毁。1444年的温尼察是长官治下的小边塞，信奉东正教的鲁塞尼亚市民和守军盯着「鞑靼黑路」，掠奴者退走后再重新盖房。

约1512年石堡落成；康斯坦丁·奥斯特罗兹基后来修建的另一座城堡1580年失火，王室又在1580、1593和1634年特许该城举办年集。地方法庭和地方议会1554年从布拉茨拉夫迁到温尼察。耶稣会士1611年来此，1642年开办学院，比该城获得马格德堡法晚两年。1648年7月赫梅利尼茨基的哥萨克入城，次年《兹博里夫条约》把它划给盖特曼政权。1651年3月11日至21日，伊万·博亨上校率三千名哥萨克和市民守城，击溃马尔钦·卡利诺夫斯基麾下一万二千人的王军。温尼察作为哥萨克团区驻地，直到1667年《安德鲁索沃停战协定》把它归还波兰。1672年《布恰奇条约》后奥斯曼名义上领有此地，王军1674年重新进驻，扬·索别斯基1685年恢复这里的哥萨克编制。1750年海达马克人洗劫城市，1770至1771年瘟疫夺去一千三百三十条人命。1783年安东尼·普罗塔齐·波托茨基在温尼察开办波兰贸易公司，1793年第二次瓜分把该城划给俄国。

en:
Drohobych sits on the Tysmenytsia stream in the Beskid foothills, on the salt road that carried Galician brine salt west through the Carpathian passes. A trading settlement grew beside its brine springs at the end of the eleventh century, and the town first appears in Lviv records in 1387. Its royal saltworks were leased to merchants from across Europe, Italians among them. Up in the mountains to the south the cliff fortress of Tustan, cut into sandstone crags, guarded the same road: its garrison escorted the salt caravans and took customs duty from merchants crossing toward Hungary, until the fortress fell out of use in the mid-sixteenth century. Jogaila founded the Catholic parish church in 1392, and Drohobych received Magdeburg rights in 1422. In 1444 it was a Ruthenian market town of the Polish-ruled Ruthenian Voivodeship, living almost entirely from salt, with Jewish settlers first recorded in 1404.

A Turkish-Tatar raid burned much of the town in 1498, and sixteenth-century burghers ringed it with ramparts, gates and a fortified church. The salt town's best-known native was Yuriy Drohobych, called Kotermak, born around 1450. He taught medicine and astronomy, served as rector of the University of Bologna in 1481 and 1482 and later as professor at the Krakow Academy, and in 1483 printed an astronomical prognostication in Rome, the first published work by a writer from Rus. In 1578 the town won a privilege barring Jews from residence, and only in 1616 were they allowed to settle in the suburbs. During the Khmelnytsky Uprising of 1648 Cossacks stormed Drohobych and killed many townspeople who had sheltered in the parish church; a handful held out in the bell tower, and the breach by which the attackers entered was afterwards walled shut. Drohobych passed to Austria in the partition of 1772 and became a Galician district seat.
zh:
德罗霍贝奇位于贝斯基德山麓的蒂什梅尼察河畔，加利西亚的井盐沿盐路向西翻过喀尔巴阡山口外运，这座城镇就处在这条路上。11世纪末，盐泉旁形成了贸易定居点；1387年，它的名字首次出现在利沃夫的文献记录中。当地的王室盐场租给欧洲各地商人经营，其中也有意大利人。南面山里的图斯坦要塞凿在砂岩崖壁上，看守着同一条路：驻军护送运盐商队，向翻山前往匈牙利的商人收取关税，要塞到16世纪中叶废弃。1392年雅盖沃修建天主教教区教堂，1422年德罗霍贝奇获得马格德堡法。1444年时，它是波兰治下鲁塞尼亚省的鲁塞尼亚集镇，生计几乎全靠食盐，犹太人定居者最早见于1404年记载。

1498年，土耳其与鞑靼人的入侵烧毁大半个城镇；16世纪的市民环筑土墙、城门和一座设防教堂。这座盐镇最有名的人物是约1450年出生的尤里·德罗霍贝奇，人称科特尔马克。他教授医学与天文学，1481至1482年任博洛尼亚大学校长，后来在克拉科夫学院任教，1483年在罗马印行一部天文预言，这是罗斯出身者出版的第一部印刷著作。1578年，城镇取得禁止犹太人居住的特权，直到1616年犹太人才获准在城郊定居。1648年赫梅利尼茨基起义期间，哥萨克攻破德罗霍贝奇，杀害许多躲进教区教堂的居民，少数人在钟楼里支撑到最后，进攻者打开的缺口事后被砌死。1772年瓜分波兰后德罗霍贝奇归属奥地利，成为加利西亚的一个区治。

en:
Lubny stands above the Sula River, on the old fortified line that covered Kyiv from raiders moving out of the steppe. Ukrainian tradition identifies it with a wooden fortress founded by Grand Prince Vladimir in 988; its first clear written notice comes from 1107, when Sviatopolk II and Vladimir Monomakh defeated the Cumans of Boniak and Sharukan nearby. Mongol forces destroyed the settlement in 1239, but the river crossing, woods and marshes kept the place alive. In 1444 Lubny was a small Orthodox Ruthenian outpost of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, set in grain country and close to the steppe road.

The Wiśniowiecki family revived Lubny late in the sixteenth century. Prince Alexander Wiśniowiecki built a new castle in 1589, and the town received Magdeburg rights and a coat of arms two years later. From 26 May to 7 June 1596 the meadows at nearby Solonytsia were the scene of the Battle of Lubny, the last major fight of Severyn Nalyvaiko's Cossack uprising against the Polish Crown. The Mhar Saviour-Transfiguration Monastery was founded on the Sula in 1619 with money from Princess Raina Wiśniowiecka, as an Orthodox brotherhouse in the eastern Commonwealth; in the 1680s Hetmans Ivan Samoylovych and Ivan Mazepa helped pay for its Ukrainian Baroque katholikon. During the Khmelnytsky Uprising, in 1648, Lubny became the headquarters of its own Cossack regiment and remained so until 1781. Peter I ordered a field pharmacy and medicinal herb garden here in 1709. Local bakers were known for korovai and paska, and the breads earned a mention in Ivan Kotliarevsky's Eneida.
zh:
卢布内位于苏拉河畔高地，处在古代掩护基辅、防备草原袭掠者的筑防线上。乌克兰传说把它与弗拉基米尔大公988年建立的一座木堡联系起来；第一条明确文字记载见于1107年，斯维亚托波尔克二世和弗拉基米尔·莫诺马赫在附近击败博尼亚克与沙鲁坎率领的库曼人。1239年，蒙古军队摧毁聚落，但渡口、森林和沼泽使此地没有荒废。1444年，卢布内是立陶宛大公国一座信奉东正教的鲁塞尼亚小据点，位于粮田之中，离草原道路不远。

维希涅维茨基家族在16世纪后期重振卢布内。1589年，王公亚历山大·维希涅维茨基修建新城堡，两年后城镇获得马格德堡权利和城徽。1596年5月26日至6月7日，附近索洛尼齐亚的草甸上爆发卢布内战役，这是塞韦林·纳利瓦伊科领导的哥萨克起义对抗波兰王权的最后一场大规模战斗。1619年，马加尔救主显圣容修道院在苏拉河畔建立，资金来自拉伊娜·维希涅维茨卡公主，目的是在联邦东部设立东正教兄弟会据点；17世纪80年代，盖特曼伊万·萨莫伊洛维奇和伊万·马泽帕资助修建了乌克兰巴洛克式大教堂。1648年赫梅利尼茨基起义期间，卢布内成为独立哥萨克团的总部，并一直保持到1781年。1709年，彼得一世下令在这里设立野战药房和药草园。当地面包师以科罗瓦伊面包和帕斯卡面包闻名，这些面包还在伊万·科特利亚列夫斯基的《埃涅伊达》中被提到。

en:
Rylsk stands on the Seym, in the black-earth country once held by the Siverians. The Hypatian Chronicle first names it in 1152, when it was a town subject to Novhorod-Siverskyi and the second settlement of the Kursk district; in the 1160s it became the seat of a small appanage principality. Batu's invasion probably damaged the town, but its hinterland was unusual for the region: Russian sources describe it as the one part of the Central Black Earth belt where settled farming continued from the Mongol campaigns into the 16th century. The Grand Duchy of Lithuania took Rylsk in the 14th century. In 1444 it was a small Orthodox frontier town, valuable more for its grain fields and river access than for strong walls.

Its ruling princes tied the town to Moscow's civil wars. Casimir IV enfeoffed Rylsk to Ivan Shemyachich, son of the exiled Moscow prince Dmitry Shemyaka; Ivan's son Vasily later entered Ivan III's service in 1500, although Lithuanian claims and garrisons kept the border disputed until 1522. Through the 16th century Rylsk formed part of the chain of southern fortress towns that screened Muscovy from Crimean Tatar raids. The townspeople were among the first to admit False Dmitry I in 1604, and the next year they held out against an army sent by Tsar Boris Godunov's government. Once the Left Bank came under the tsar, Rylsk merchants profited from overland traffic between Little Russia and Great Russia.
zh:
雷利斯克位于谢伊姆河畔，地处古谢韦里安人占据过的黑土地带。《伊帕季耶夫编年史》在1152年首次提到它，当时它隶属诺夫霍罗德-锡韦尔斯基，是库尔斯克辖区的第二处聚落；12世纪60年代，这里成为一个小封邑公国的驻地。拔都入侵可能破坏了城镇，但它的腹地在这一带相当特殊：俄文资料称，中央黑土区中只有这一带从蒙古入侵到16世纪始终没有中断定居农耕。14世纪，雷利斯克归入立陶宛大公国。1444年，它是一座信奉东正教的边疆小城，价值主要在谷地粮田和河道交通，而不在坚固城墙。

统治这里的王公把城镇卷进了莫斯科的王公纷争。卡西米尔四世把雷利斯克封给流亡莫斯科王公德米特里·舍米亚卡之子伊万·舍米亚奇奇；伊万的儿子瓦西里后来在1500年转投伊凡三世，不过立陶宛的主权要求和驻军仍使边界争执持续到1522年。整个16世纪，雷利斯克都是南方要塞城镇链的一环，为莫斯科阻挡克里米亚鞑靼人袭扰。1604年，雷利斯克市民最早向伪德米特里一世开门，次年又顶住了鲍里斯·戈东诺夫政府所派军队的围攻。第聂伯河左岸归入沙皇统治后，雷利斯克商人靠小俄罗斯与大俄罗斯之间的陆路贩运获利。

en:
Babruysk stands on the Berezina, on the old water route between the Dnieper and the Western Dvina. Its name recalls the beavers once trapped by local fishermen, and it first appears in a charter of Grand Duke Jogaila on 28 April 1387 granting the place to his brother Skirgaila. In the Grand Duchy of Lithuania a grand-ducal volost kept its wooden castle on the hill, while timber-and-earth walls with about ten towers guarded a ferry crossing toward Mogilev. In 1444 Babruysk was an Orthodox Ruthenian customs and trading town, living by river traffic, the surrounding forests and grain country.

Crimean Tatars ravaged the district in 1503–1505, and the town withstood a siege by Mikhail Glinski's rebels in 1506. Its customs post supported the recovery that followed: an inventory of 1620 recorded 409 households and seventy-five shops. Janusz Radziwiłł stormed Babruysk in January 1649 to dislodge Cossack rebels, and Zolotarenko's Cossacks burned it in 1655; later wars reduced the town to a much smaller place. After the Second Partition of 1793 it passed to Russia, and its coat of arms of 1796 bore a ship's mast, for the mast timber floated down the Berezina to the imperial fleets. In 1810 the military engineer Teodor Narbutt chose the old castle ground for a Russian fortress. The works were still unfinished in 1812, when Ignatiev's garrison supplied the retreating Second Russian Army, ferried out its wounded and held for four months against Jan Henryk Dąbrowski's Polish corps.
zh:
博布鲁伊斯克位于别列津纳河畔，地处第聂伯河与西德维纳河之间的旧水路上。城名来自当地渔民曾捕猎的河狸，最早见于1387年4月28日大公约盖拉把此地封给弟弟斯基尔盖拉的特许状。立陶宛大公国时期，这里是大公直辖乡的中心，山岗上立着木城堡；约十座塔楼的木土城墙护卫着通往莫吉廖夫的渡口。1444年时，博布鲁伊斯克是东正教鲁塞尼亚人的税关和商镇，靠河运、周围林地与谷物产地为生。

1503至1505年，克里米亚鞑靼人蹂躏这一带，1506年城镇又顶住米哈伊尔·格林斯基叛军的围攻。税关支撑了后来的恢复，1620年的清册记载有四百零九户人家和七十五家店铺。1649年1月，雅努什·拉齐维乌破城赶走哥萨克起义者；1655年佐洛塔连科的哥萨克军焚毁城镇，连番战争后博布鲁伊斯克沦为小邑。1793年第二次瓜分波兰后它划归俄国，1796年城徽采用一根船桅，因为造舰桅木沿别列津纳河漂运，供帝国舰队使用。1810年，军事工程师特奥多尔·纳尔布特选中旧城堡一带修建俄国要塞。1812年要塞尚未完工，伊格纳季耶夫的守军仍为撤退的俄国第二军团补给粮食、运出伤兵，并顶住扬·亨里克·东布罗夫斯基所部波兰军团长达四个月的围攻。

en:
Slutsk stands on the Sluch, a tributary of the Pripyat, in Dregovichi country. The chronicles first name it in 1116, when Gleb of Minsk burned it during a campaign in the district, and from 1160 it was the seat of its own princes, a branch of the princes of Turov. It entered Lithuania in the 1320s, and in 1395 passed to Olelko, founder of the Olelkovich line. An upper and a lower castle rose above the river in the early fifteenth century, a Slutsk levy fought at Grunwald in 1410, and the town received limited self-government and a coat of arms in 1441. In 1444 Slutsk was an Orthodox princely seat behind strong timber walls, dealing in cloth and river-borne goods.

In 1481 Prince Mikhail Olelkovich was executed after a conspiracy against Casimir IV, and his widow kept the inheritance for their young heir. Crimean Tatars began raiding the district in 1502; Princess Anastasia led the defence that saved Slutsk in 1506, and the castles held out against Michael Glinski's rebels two years later. When the Olelkovich princess Sophia died in 1612, her husband Janusz Radziwiłł inherited the town and opened a Calvinist gymnasium there in 1617. Bogusław Radziwiłł later rebuilt the castles as a bastioned fortress, which withstood a Russian siege in 1655. Slutsk's best-known product was the kontusz sash: a Radziwiłł silk manufactory opened in 1740, and its silk sashes with gold and silver thread were three to four metres long and could be folded to show different patterns, making them favoured wear among Commonwealth nobles. A Radziwiłł court theatre opened in 1751, and Protestant and Orthodox nobles formed the Slutsk Confederation there in 1767. Slutsk passed to Russia in 1793 and held French troops in 1812.
zh:
斯卢茨克位于普里皮亚季河支流斯卢奇河畔，地处德列戈维奇人的土地。编年史在1116年首次提到它，当时明斯克王公格列布出征这一带时焚毁了斯卢茨克。1160年起，这里成为支系王公的驻地，统治者出自图罗夫王公家族。1320年代它并入立陶宛，1395年封给奥列尔科，后者开创了奥列尔科维奇支系。15世纪初，河边先后建起上、下两座城堡；1410年，斯卢茨克民军参加格伦瓦德之战；1441年，城市获得有限自治权和城徽。1444年的斯卢茨克是一座东正教王公驻地，木墙坚固，经营布料和河运货物。

1481年，米哈伊尔·奥列尔科维奇因卷入反对卡齐米日四世的密谋被处死，他的遗孀为年幼继承人保住了产业。1502年起，克里米亚鞑靼人开始连年入寇；1506年，阿纳斯塔西娅王妃主持城防，保住斯卢茨克；两年后，城堡又顶住米哈伊尔·格林斯基叛军的围攻。奥列尔科维奇家族的索菲娅1612年去世后，她的丈夫亚努什·拉齐维乌继承城市，并于1617年开办加尔文宗书院。博格斯拉夫·拉齐维乌后来把城堡改造成棱堡要塞，1655年抵挡住俄军围攻。斯卢茨克最出名的物产是孔图什腰带：拉齐维乌家族的丝织工坊于1740年开办，所产腰带以丝绸和金银线织成，长三至四米，折叠后可露出不同纹样，是联邦贵族看重的服饰。1751年，拉齐维乌宫廷剧院开办；1767年，新教与东正教贵族在此组成斯卢茨克联盟。1793年斯卢茨克并入俄国，1812年曾驻有法国军队。

en:
Málaga fills a broad Mediterranean bay between the Gibralfaro hill and the Guadalmedina river. Phoenicians from Tyre founded Malaka there around 770 BC, and Roman Malaca grew rich on the fish sauce called garum and on harbour trade. Under Muslim rule the walled town climbed from the port to the Alcazaba and the Gibralfaro castle. The tenth-century chronicler al-Razi already praised its vineyards and raisins, and Ibn Battuta, passing through around 1325, found its grapes, figs, almonds and pomegranates without equal, along with fine gilded pottery. Under the Nasrids it was Granada's chief western port and second city: Genoese merchants shipped silk, raisins, the Rayya figs reportedly carried as far as China, wine, cutlery, leather and lustreware along the routes between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic. In 1444 about 15,000 people lived here, and its wharves and Genoese warehouses made it the richest port in the Muslim kingdom.

The Catholic Monarchs' armies invested Málaga in 1487 and fought the hardest operation of the Granada War: after about four months of assault, bombardment and hunger, the city surrendered in August, in the first siege on record where dedicated wagons were used to carry the wounded away. Its fall cost Granada its main sea gate. Almost all surviving inhabitants were enslaved or led away, and only twenty-five families, among them the merchant Ali Dordux's group, were allowed to remain as Mudéjars; Christian settlers from across the peninsula then repopulated the town, which kept up its trade with the interior through Antequera and Córdoba. Málaga chafed under the jurisdiction of the Admiral of Castile, rose against it in 1516 and freed itself only in 1530, and by 1625 it held some 36,000 people. On 24 August 1704 the sea off the city saw the largest fleet action of the War of the Spanish Succession, the indecisive Battle of Málaga, fought three weeks after the same Anglo-Dutch fleet had taken Gibraltar.
zh:
马拉加坐落在希布拉尔法罗山与瓜达尔梅迪纳河之间的广阔地中海海湾。约公元前770年，推罗的腓尼基商人在此建立马拉卡，罗马时代的马拉加靠鱼酱和港口贸易富庶起来。穆斯林统治时期，带城墙的城区从港口一路铺到阿尔卡萨瓦要塞和希布拉尔法罗城堡。10世纪的编年史家拉齐已经盛赞这里的葡萄园和葡萄干；伊本·白图泰约1325年路过时，看到的是天下无双的葡萄、无花果、杏仁和石榴，以及精美的鎏金陶器。纳斯里德王朝治下，它是格拉纳达首要的西部海港和王国第二大城：热那亚商人把丝绸、葡萄干、据说远销中国的拉亚无花果，还有葡萄酒、刀具、皮革和光泽陶器装上船，往来于地中海与大西洋之间的航路。1444年城中约有一万五千人，码头和热那亚人的货栈使它成为这个穆斯林王国最富庶的港口。

1487年，天主教君主的军队兵临城下，打了格拉纳达战争中最艰难的一仗。经过约四个月的强攻、炮击和饥馑，马拉加在8月投降，这次围城还第一次使用了专门运送伤兵的车辆。城市陷落使格拉纳达失去主要海上门户，幸存者几乎全部被罚为奴或押走，只有以商人阿里·杜尔杜克斯为首的二十五户获准作为穆德哈尔人留下；随后伊比利亚半岛各地的基督教定居者迁入此城，马拉加则继续经安特克拉和科尔多瓦同内陆贸易。它不甘受卡斯蒂利亚海军上将管辖，1516年起兵反抗，直到1530年才彻底摆脱，到1625年居民已有约三万六千人。1704年8月24日，城外海面爆发西班牙王位继承战争中规模最大的舰队交战，胜负未决的马拉加海战，此时距同一支英荷舰队夺取直布罗陀才过去三周。

en:
Albacete lies on Los Llanos, the wide wheat plains where La Mancha opens towards Murcia and the Valencian coast. Its Muslim village of Al-Basit, Arabic for 'the plain', sat below the fortified hill of Chinchilla, whose castle commanded the roads across the flat country. Castilian troops took it in 1241, and for two centuries the hamlet remained in Chinchilla's shadow, becoming a separate villa of the lords of Villena only with its town charter in 1375. In 1444 it was a small grain town on the road linking the Castilian Meseta with Murcia and Valencia, and Chinchilla's castle still overshadowed it.

Knife-making took root in the fifteenth century, inherited from Muslim smiths; by the seventeenth, workshops along the Calle Zapateros made knives, daggers, swords, scissors and the folding navaja, and the eighteenth was the trade's golden age, when Albacete blades sold across Spain and abroad. The town had held an annual fair since its charter, and the Catholic Monarchs added a weekly market in 1476. On 25 April 1707, on the plains at Almansa east of the town, the Duke of Berwick, illegitimate son of James II of England, led Philip V's Bourbon army against an allied force under the Earl of Galway, a French Huguenot exile in English service, prompting the joke that the English were commanded by a Frenchman and the French by an Englishman. Berwick's victory opened Valencia to the Bourbons, and Frederick the Great later called it the best-fought battle of the century. Philip V made the Albacete fair tax-free in 1710, and in 1783 a permanent fairground opened, a pan-shaped ring of stalls built in thirty-three days; the fair became one of the great stock fairs of inland Spain. During the Peninsular War French troops sacked the town and later blew up the keep of Chinchilla's castle.
zh:
阿尔瓦塞特位于利亚诺斯平原，拉曼查的广阔麦田在这里向穆尔西亚和巴伦西亚海岸方向展开。穆斯林村庄阿尔-巴西特（阿拉伯语意为「平原」）坐落在钦奇利亚设防山丘下方，山上的城堡扼守着穿越旷野的道路。1241年卡斯蒂利亚军队攻取此地，此后两百年间村落一直掩在钦奇利亚的阴影里，直到1375年凭市镇特许状成为比列纳领主治下的独立市镇。1444年，它是卡斯蒂利亚高原通往穆尔西亚和巴伦西亚路上的一座谷物小镇，仍处在钦奇利亚城堡的俯瞰之下。

制刀业在15世纪从穆斯林工匠手中接续而来；到17世纪，鞋匠街一带的作坊已在打制刀具、匕首、剑、剪刀和名叫纳瓦哈的折叠刀，18世纪更是这门手艺的黄金年代，阿尔瓦塞特出产的刀剑行销西班牙内外。小镇自立镇起便有年市，天主教双王又在1476年赐它每周开市。1707年4月25日，城东阿尔曼萨的平原上打响了西班牙王位继承战争中具有决定意义的一仗：费利佩五世的波旁军由英王詹姆斯二世的私生子贝里克公爵指挥，对面的联军主帅却是流亡英国的法国胡格诺派加尔韦伯爵，当时有人打趣说，这是唯一一场英军由法国人率领、法军由英国人率领的战斗。贝里克获胜，为波旁王朝打开巴伦西亚的大门，后来腓特烈大帝还称赞这是本世纪指挥得最好的一仗。费利佩五世1710年赐这里的集市免税特权；1783年，一座煎锅形的环形集市场在33天内建成开市，阿尔瓦塞特年市也成为西班牙内陆最有名的牲畜集市之一。半岛战争期间，法军洗劫城镇，后来又炸毁钦奇利亚城堡的主塔。

en:
Huelva sits on the sheltered ría where the Odiel and Tinto flow into the Gulf of Cádiz, with low copper-bearing hills a short way upstream. As Phoenician Onoba it shipped copper and silver, purple dye and salted fish, and Roman Onoba kept a mint on the same estuary; the Rio Tinto diggings upriver were already a major mining district under Roman rule. Muslim Walba passed to Castile when Alfonso X took the town in 1262, and for the rest of the Middle Ages it was mostly a noble lordship on the Portuguese border. In 1444 it was a Catholic Castilian fishing and trading harbour, while the little ports strung along the same estuary, Palos and Moguer among them, already made their living from the Atlantic.

Palos held the sailors who knew the Guinea run, and in the Castilian-Portuguese war of 1475-1479 they used that knowledge to raid Portuguese shipping, until the Treaty of Alcáçovas in 1479 left the Atlantic and African routes to Portugal apart from the Canaries. Columbus spent months at the Franciscan monastery of La Rábida and won over the Pinzón brothers, the leading shipmasters of Palos, who helped him raise crews and money. On 3 August 1492 the Pinta, Niña and Santa María put out from Palos with about ninety men. The Santa María was wrecked in the Caribbean, and the two caravels returned to the same roadstead on 15 March 1493. The youngest Pinzón, Vicente Yáñez, who had captained the Niña, sighted the Brazilian coast in 1500. When the Casa de Contratación opened at Seville in 1503 the Atlantic trade moved up the river, Palos emptied, and Huelva grew on sardine and tuna fishing.

The 1755 Lisbon earthquake wrecked much of the town. In 1810 French troops under the Duke of Aremberg attacked Huelva and Moguer, but the harbour stayed open and went on landing men and supplies for Cádiz, which the French had under siege.
zh:
韦尔瓦位于奥迭尔河与廷托河注入加的斯湾的避风河口，上游不远就是产铜的低缓丘陵。腓尼基时代的奥诺巴输出铜、银、紫染料和咸鱼，罗马时代的奥诺巴还在同一河口设有铸币厂，廷托河矿区在罗马治下已是重要的铜银矿区。穆斯林称此地为韦勒巴，1262年阿方索十世攻占后它归入卡斯蒂利亚，整个中世纪后期基本是葡萄牙边境上的一处贵族领地。1444年，这里是卡斯蒂利亚天主教徒的渔业与贸易港口；同一河口还串着帕洛斯、莫格尔这些小港，它们的生计早已系于大西洋。

帕洛斯有的是熟悉几内亚航路的水手。1475年至1479年卡斯蒂利亚与葡萄牙交战，他们凭着这套本事劫掠葡萄牙船只，直到1479年《阿尔卡索瓦斯条约》把大西洋和非洲航路划归葡萄牙，只把加那利群岛留给卡斯蒂利亚。哥伦布在拉维达的方济各会修道院盘桓数月，说动了帕洛斯首屈一指的船主平松兄弟，由他们帮着招募水手、筹措费用。1492年8月3日，「平塔号」「尼尼亚号」和「圣马利亚号」率约九十人从帕洛斯起航；「圣马利亚号」在加勒比海域失事，两艘卡拉维尔船于1493年3月15日返回同一锚地。曾任「尼尼亚号」船长的平松家幼子比森特·亚涅斯，1500年又望见了巴西海岸。1503年塞维利亚设立贸易署，大西洋贸易随之移往上游，帕洛斯为之一空，韦尔瓦则靠沙丁鱼和金枪鱼渔业发展起来。

1755年里斯本大地震摧毁了城中大片房屋。1810年，阿朗贝格公爵麾下法军进攻韦尔瓦和莫格尔，但港口始终未失，继续为遭法军围困的加的斯运送兵员和补给。

en:
Xàtiva climbs a hill above the Albaida river, and its castle was held to be the strongest in the Kingdom of Valencia. Roman Saetabis sold fine linen across the Mediterranean, and Catullus names its linen handkerchiefs among the presents his friends brought back from Spain. Under Muslim rule Shāṭiba learned paper-making from Arab craftsmen and became one of the first paper towns in western Europe; the geographer al-Idrisi praised its mills and its schools in the twelfth century. James I of Aragon took the city in May 1244 after an earlier siege had failed, kept its mosque and made it seat of the governorship beyond the Júcar; its fair was licensed in 1250 and Peter IV granted city status in 1347. As the second city of the kingdom, dealing in paper and linen, it was the birthplace of the House of Borgia: Alfonso de Borja, the future Pope Callixtus III, was born here in 1378, and his nephew Rodrigo de Borja, the future Alexander VI, around 1431. In 1444 Xàtiva was a walled royal city of some 8,000 people.

The Germanías revolt turned the city into a battlefield: the agermanat leader Vicent Peris made it his stronghold and held out until he was killed in 1522. The painter José de Ribera, called Lo Spagnoletto, was born here in 1591. The Morisco expulsion of 1609-1614 emptied more than a hundred villages of its governorship and cost it nearly half its people, and the plagues of the seventeenth century thinned them further. In the War of the Spanish Succession Xàtiva declared for the Habsburg claimant, and after the Bourbon victory at Almansa d'Asfeld's army laid siege; the English garrison in the castle marched out on 12 June 1707. The town was then looted and put to the torch; tradition says it burned for a year, and its people were deported to La Mancha. Philip V renamed the blackened ruins the Colonia de San Felipe and dissolved the ancient governorship, and the fire gave Xativans their nickname of socarrats, the scorched ones. The Cortes of Cádiz gave the city its old name back in 1811.
zh:
沙蒂瓦坐落在阿尔瓦伊达河畔的山丘上，城中城堡号称巴伦西亚王国最坚固的要塞。罗马时代的萨埃塔比斯出产上等亚麻布，行销地中海各地；卡图卢斯就写到朋友从西班牙带回的萨埃塔比斯亚麻手帕。穆斯林治下的沙提巴从阿拉伯工匠那里学会造纸，是西欧最早的造纸城镇之一，12世纪的地理学家伊德里西称赞过它的磨坊和学堂。阿拉贡的海梅一世早先一次围攻无功而返，1244年5月终于拿下此城；他保留了城里的清真寺，把沙蒂瓦设为胡卡尔河外辖区的首府，1250年准许开设集市，1347年佩德罗四世授予城市称号。作为王国第二大城，它靠纸张和亚麻立足，也是博尔吉亚家族的桑梓：未来的教皇加里斯都三世阿方索·德·博尔哈1378年出生于此，他的外甥罗德里戈·德·博尔哈，即后来的亚历山大六世，生于1431年前后。1444年的沙蒂瓦城墙环绕，约有八千居民。

兄弟会起义把这座城变成了战场：起义领袖维森特·佩里斯以沙蒂瓦为据点坚守，1522年被杀。画家何塞·德·里韦拉（绰号「小西班牙人」）1591年出生于此。1609至1614年驱逐摩里斯科人，使辖区内一百多处村落荒无人烟，人口损失近半，17世纪的瘟疫又使人口进一步减少。西班牙王位继承战争中，沙蒂瓦支持哈布斯堡觊觎者，波旁军队在阿尔曼萨获胜后，达斯费尔德率军围城，城堡里的英国守军1707年6月12日开出城外。城市随即遭到洗劫和纵火，相传大火烧了一年，居民被流放至拉曼查；腓力五世把这片焦黑的废墟命名为圣费利佩新殖民地，废除了古老的辖区，而这场大火也给沙蒂瓦人送来了「烧焦的人」（socarrats）的绰号。1811年，加的斯议会恢复了城市的旧名。

en:
Castelló lies on the flat coastal plain north of Valencia, the Plana crossed and watered by the Mijares, and the wheat of its irrigated fields made the district one of the granaries of the Kingdom of Valencia. Its people began on the Magdalena height, in the Muslim hill-fort of Fadrell, which capitulated to James I of Aragon in 1233. After the Mudéjar revolt of 1247 the Muslim population was expelled, and on 8 September 1251 the king authorised Ximén Pérez d'Arenós to bring the settlement down from the hill onto the plain; local tradition dates the move to the third Sunday of Lent 1252. The new town was ringed with moats, walls and towers, and its grain and fruit were loaded at the Grau, its beach landing on the shore. In 1366 a farmer called Perot de Granyana found a buried image of the Virgin, Our Lady of Lledó, who became the town's patron. During the succession crisis of 1410-1412 Castelló withstood the governor Bellera and, on 24 April 1412, defeated an attacking army at its gates, leaving more than five hundred assailants dead; two months later the Compromise of Caspe gave the crown to Ferdinand of Trastámara. In 1444 Castelló was a small royal town living off its fields and its beach trade.

In the Germanías revolt Castelló rose against Charles I and was one of the guildsmen's last strongholds until the Duke of Segorbe took and sacked it in 1521. The Crown afterwards kept clipping its old privileges; in 1616 its justicia and jurats were carried off to Valencia as prisoners. Plague ran through the town from 1647 to 1653. In the War of the Spanish Succession Castelló backed the Habsburg claimant, and in May 1707 Berwick entered it, exacted a forced payment of 8,840 Valencian pounds and had the medieval walls demolished. The Nueva Planta decree of that year abolished the Valencian furs, and in February 1708 a Castilian-style town council took over. A hemp industry grew up from 1747, and the last stretches of wall were cleared in 1796 to let the town spread.
zh:
卡斯特略位于巴伦西亚北面平坦的沿海平原上，米哈雷斯河纵贯并灌溉着这片名叫「普拉纳」的平原，灌溉田里的小麦使这一带成为巴伦西亚王国的粮仓之一。居民最初住在马格达莱纳高地上的穆斯林山堡法德雷尔，1233年山堡向阿拉贡的海梅一世投降。1247年穆德哈尔起义后，当地穆斯林遭到驱逐；1251年9月8日国王特许希门·佩雷斯·德·阿雷诺斯把定居点从山上迁到平原，相传迁城在1252年大斋期第三个星期日完成。新城外有壕沟、城墙和塔楼，粮食和果品在海滨滩岸格劳装船外运。1366年，农夫佩罗特·德·格拉尼亚纳挖出一尊被掩埋的圣母像，即利多圣母，后来成为城镇的主保。1410至1412年王位空缺期间，卡斯特略抵挡住总督贝列拉，1412年4月24日又在城下击败来犯军队，攻方死者逾五百；两个月后卡斯佩妥协把王冠交给特拉斯塔马拉家族的费尔南多。1444年的卡斯特略是一座靠田地和滨海贸易为生的皇家小镇。

兄弟会起义中卡斯特略起兵反对卡洛斯一世，是起义行会最后的据点之一，1521年被塞戈尔韦公爵攻破洗劫。此后王室不断裁削它的旧有特权，1616年甚至把市政法官和陪审官作为囚犯押往巴伦西亚。1647至1653年瘟疫肆虐。西班牙王位继承战争中它支持哈布斯堡觊觎者，1707年5月贝里克入城，强征8840巴伦西亚镑，并下令拆毁中世纪城墙；同年颁布的《新基本法令》废除巴伦西亚地方特许状，1708年2月按卡斯蒂利亚模式组建的新市府开始运作。1747年起大麻产业兴起，1796年残存的城墙也被拆除，好让城镇向外扩展。

en:
Ávila lies on the high meseta beside the Adaja, over 1,100 metres up and the highest city in Castile. It was a Visigothic bishopric, then a Muslim frontier fortress and an almost deserted no man's land, until Raymond of Burgundy repopulated it for Alfonso VI after 1088. Its walls, begun then and rebuilt through the twelfth century, ring the old town: about 2,500 metres of rampart with 88 semicircular towers and nine gates, one of the most complete medieval circuits in Europe. The cathedral was built into the wall, and its apse forms one of the towers. Frontier council militias raided as far south as Seville and Córdoba; by the late thirteenth century the town held one of Castile's largest Jewish communities, a vote in the Cortes, great herds on its pastures and a cloth industry that never matched Flemish or Italian wares. In 1444 Ávila was a quiet walled town of herdsmen and weavers, its frontier days long past.

On 5 June 1465 rebel nobles staged the ceremony later called the Farce of Ávila on open ground outside the walls. They set a wooden statue of Henry IV on a platform, dressed in mourning and wearing the crown, with his sword and staff beside it; after reading their charges they stripped the effigy of crown, sword and staff in turn and threw it to the ground, then proclaimed the king's half-brother Alfonso, not yet eleven. The Jewish quarter ended with the expulsion of 1492. When the Comuneros rose in 1520 their Holy Junta met first at Ávila, on 1 August, and drafted its perpetual-law project inside the cathedral. The town's most famous child is Teresa de Jesús, born here in 1515: in 1562 she founded San José, the first convent of her Discalced Carmelites, and she was canonized in 1622. Its walls and its mystics gave Ávila the name of the 'City of Stones and Saints'. French troops under Marshal Lefebvre sacked it from 4 to 7 January 1809 and looted its churches.
zh:
阿维拉位于阿达哈河畔的高原台地，海拔逾1100米，是卡斯蒂利亚地势最高的城市。这里先是西哥特人的主教驻地，穆斯林时期成为边塞要塞，后来沦为几近荒弃的无人地带，直到1088年后勃艮第的雷蒙奉阿方索六世之命重新移民屯垦。环城城墙此时动工，12世纪又经历重修，环抱着老城：墙身周长约2500米，立着88座半圆形塔楼，开有九座城门，是欧洲最完整的中世纪城墙之一。大教堂直接修进墙体，它的半圆形后殿就是墙上一座塔楼。边塞年代，市政民兵曾南下远掠塞维利亚和科尔多瓦；到13世纪末，阿维拉拥有卡斯蒂利亚最大的犹太社区之一、议会中的一票、四野的大群牛羊，还有一门始终敌不过佛兰德和意大利货的呢绒业。1444年的阿维拉是一座安静的城墙之城，居民以牧人和织工为主，边塞岁月早已远去。

1465年6月5日，叛乱贵族在城外举行后来被称作「阿维拉闹剧」的仪式。他们把恩里克四世的木像安在高台上，木像身着丧服、头戴王冠，旁边摆着国王的剑和权杖；宣读罪状之后，众人依次摘去塑像的王冠、剑和杖，将它掀翻在地，随即拥立国王尚未满十一岁的异母弟阿方索。1492年的驱逐令终结了犹太区。1520年公社起义爆发，起事者的「神圣委员会」于8月1日首先在阿维拉集会，在大教堂内起草《永久法律草案》。阿维拉最有名的孩子是1515年出生于此的特雷莎·德·赫苏斯：1562年她创立圣何塞修道院，即赤脚加尔默罗会的第一座修院，1622年被封圣。城墙与圣徒为阿维拉赢来「石头与圣徒之城」的称号。1809年1月4日至7日，勒菲弗尔元帅麾下的法军洗劫全城，抢掠各教堂。

en:
Palencia stands on the Carrión River in Tierra de Campos, the wheat country medieval writers called the Campos Góticos. The Vaccaei knew the settlement as Pallantia, and under the Visigoths it held a Christian bishopric that vanished after the Muslim conquest until Sancho III of Navarre restored it in 1035. Its schools became the first university in Castile: the studium Alfonso VIII and Bishop Tello Téllez de Meneses founded between 1208 and 1212 was confirmed by Pope Honorius III in 1221, and Domingo de Guzmán, later Saint Dominic, read the arts there for six years and theology for four. The Gothic cathedral was begun in 1321, and the road to Santiago crossed the north of the province past the Romanesque San Martín at Frómista and the pilgrim town of Carrión de los Condes. In 1444 Palencia was an episcopal city under one of Castile's richest dioceses, ringed by the wheat fields that paid for it.

Most of Palencia's Jews chose exile in Portugal in 1492, and their synagogue was a slaughterhouse by 1495. The city threw itself into the Comunero revolt of 1520: Antonio de Acuña, the fighting bishop of Zamora, raised troops at Dueñas and the city ran a war council, until the royal victory at Villalar on 23 April 1521; in 1524 it bought its pardon for 925,000 maravedís, which paid for repairs to the episcopal tower and palace. The province also produced the poet and courtier Íñigo López de Mendoza, Marqués de Santillana, born at Carrión de los Condes in 1398, and the painters Pedro Berruguete and his son Alonso, the leading sculptor of the Spanish Renaissance, both from Paredes de Nava. After the decline of the 17th century, engineers began the Canal of Castile at Calahorra de Ribas on 16 July 1753 and joined its branches in August 1791, to carry Tierra de Campos wheat to the northern ports. French troops were quartered on the city in 1808; the rising of 5 June brought battalions two days later, and the town escaped sack only through the council's and bishop's pleas.
zh:
帕伦西亚位于卡尔皮翁河畔，地处田野坎波斯的广阔小麦平原，中世纪作家称这片平原为「哥特田野」。瓦凯伊人曾称此地为帕兰提亚，西哥特时代这里设有基督教主教座，穆斯林征服后一度中断，直到1035年纳瓦拉的桑乔三世恢复主教区。当地的学堂发展成卡斯蒂利亚的第一所大学：阿方索八世与特略·特列斯·德·梅内塞斯主教在1208年至1212年间创办学堂，教皇洪诺留三世1221年予以批准；日后创立多明我会的多明戈·德·古斯曼曾在此攻读六年艺学、四年神学。宏大的哥特式主教座堂1321年动工，通往圣地亚哥德孔波斯特拉的朝圣路穿过省境北部，沿途有弗罗米斯塔的罗曼式圣马丁教堂和朝圣重镇卡里翁德洛斯孔德斯。1444年的帕伦西亚是一座主教城市，隶属于卡斯蒂利亚最富有的教区之一，供养它的是四周的麦田。

1492年，城中大多数犹太人不愿受洗，选择流亡葡萄牙；到1495年，他们的会堂已经被当作屠宰场。1520年，帕伦西亚全力投入公社起义：善战的萨莫拉主教安东尼奥·德·阿库尼亚在杜埃尼亚斯募兵，城中自设战争议事会，直到王军1521年4月23日在维拉拉尔取胜；1524年，城市缴纳92.5万马拉维迪才换来赦免，这笔钱用于修缮主教塔楼和宫邸。这片地方也出过文人和艺术家：诗人兼廷臣、桑蒂利亚纳侯爵伊尼戈·洛佩斯·德·门多萨1398年生于卡里翁德洛斯孔德斯，帕雷德斯德纳瓦则出了西班牙-佛兰德斯画派的佩德罗·贝鲁格特，以及他的儿子、西班牙文艺复兴最重要的雕塑家阿隆索·贝鲁格特。17世纪的衰落之后，工程师们1753年7月16日在卡拉奥拉德里瓦斯开工修建卡斯蒂利亚运河，各支段于1791年8月合流，把田野坎波斯的小麦运往北方港口。1808年法军驻扎城中；6月5日的起义在两天后招来法军营队，全靠市政当局和主教出面求情，城市才免遭洗劫。

en:
Zamora sits on a rocky bluff above the Duero, and for three centuries it was the great fortress of the Christian north, the 'well-walled city', la bien cercada, of the romances. Alfonso III of León repopulated it in 893 with Mozarab builders from Toledo, and its walls held the frontier until Almanzor sacked the city in 981 and again in 997. Ferdinand I rebuilt the fortifications in 1055 and left the city to his daughter Urraca. In 1072 her brother Sancho II of Castile, besieging the walls with El Cid at his side, was lured out and killed by the Zamoran noble Bellido Dolfos; the Portillo de la Traición, the Treason Gate, takes its name from the deed. Castile passed to the deposed Alfonso VI, and on 5 October 1143 Alfonso VII concluded here the Treaty of Zamora, recognising Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal. Bishops and princes ringed the city with Romanesque churches, twenty-four in all, more than any other city in Europe. Zamora cast one of the seventeen votes in the Cortes of Castile and even spoke there for all Galicia. In 1444 it was a Leonese-speaking city of grain and wine on the road into Portugal.

That road turned the district into a battlefield in the War of the Castilian Succession, when Afonso V's Portuguese held nearby Toro; the battle fought there on 1 March 1476 left Isabella and Ferdinand the political masters of Castile. The long sieges gave Spanish the saying that Zamora was not won in an hour. In 1492 the expelled Jews crossed here into Portugal, some 30,000 passing by way of Miranda do Douro; the crown gave their Great Synagogue to the city as a church and a hospital for the poor, and the busy frontier made Zamora a smugglers' town. On 6 January 1809 the townsmen fought the French at the Villagodio bridge before giving ground, and the French occupation lasted until the campaign that ended at Salamanca in 1812.
zh:
萨莫拉雄踞杜罗河畔的岩石高岗，在三百年里是基督教北方最坚固的要塞，即歌谣里「城墙环绕之城」（la bien cercada）。893年，莱昂国王阿方索三世把托莱多的莫萨拉布工匠迁来定居，城防一直支撑着边境战事，直到981年和997年两度遭曼苏尔洗劫。费尔南多一世1055年重修城防，把城市留给女儿乌拉卡。1072年，她的兄长卡斯蒂利亚国王桑乔二世在熙德陪同下围城，被萨莫拉贵族贝利多·多尔福斯诱出杀害，「叛国门」即因此事得名。卡斯蒂利亚王位随之落入被废的阿方索六世之手；1143年10月5日，阿方索七世在此缔结《萨莫拉条约》，承认阿丰索·恩里克斯为葡萄牙国王。主教和王公在城中建起24座罗曼式教堂，数量为欧洲城市之最。萨莫拉在卡斯蒂利亚议会十七张表决票中占其一，甚至代表整个加利西亚发言。1444年，它是通往葡萄牙大道上一座说莱昂语、产粮产酒的城市。

卡斯蒂利亚王位继承战争中，这条大道把这一带变成战场：阿丰索五世的葡萄牙军队占据附近的托罗，1476年3月1日的托罗之战在政治上让伊莎贝尔和费尔南多成为卡斯蒂利亚的主人。长年的围城还给西班牙语留下一句谚语：萨莫拉不是一个时辰打下来的。1492年，被逐的犹太人经此进入葡萄牙，约三万人取道米兰达杜罗过境；王室把他们的大会堂赐给城里，改作教堂和济贫医院，繁忙的边境也使萨莫拉成了走私客的城镇。1809年1月6日，市民在比亚戈迪奥桥迎战法军后撤退，法国人的占领一直持续到1812年以萨拉曼卡之战告终的那场战役。

en:
Lugo stands inland on a hill above the upper Miño, the oldest town in Galicia. The Romans founded Lucus Augusti in the age of Augustus as the seat of one of the three judicial districts of Gallaecia, in busy gold-mining country, and between about 260 and 325 they girdled it with a wall two kilometres round whose full circuit of gates and towers still rings the old town. The Suevi made it an archbishop's see in 460; after the Visigothic conquest of 585 it withered, and when Alfonso I entered unopposed in 741 Bishop Odoario found it half in ruins and rebuilt it. The Galician army gathered here in 842 to enthrone Ramiro I, and in 1088 Alfonso VI made the bishop lord of the city. Lugo lay on the Camino Primitivo, the early pilgrim road to Santiago: pilgrims entered by the Porta Miña to visit the cathedral begun in 1129, where the host was perpetually exposed, a rare privilege. In 1312 the townspeople drove out their bishop, and the crown prince Philip built a fortress there against him four years later. In 1444 Lugo was an old, church-ruled Castilian town inside its Roman walls, overshadowed by Santiago and the feuding Galician nobles.

When the Great Irmandiño War broke out in 1467 Lugo sent representatives to the brotherhood, and baronial strongholds went down across the region before the lords crushed the rising in 1469. Early in the sixteenth century Charles V could still name Lugo one of the capitals of the Kingdom of Galicia, but the city then declined while Santiago prospered. In 1669 the Kingdom of Galicia instituted its annual offering to the Sacrament in the cathedral, honouring the city's perpetual host. The eighteenth century brought the St Froilán cattle fairs, confirmed by royal privilege in 1754, which sold horses and mules to León and Castile; the Lisbon earthquake of 1755 cracked the cathedral's vault and the altarpiece was dismantled. War returned on 9 January 1809, when Soult's vanguard clashed with Moore's retreating British army at Conturiz outside the walls and the French occupied Lugo, until a Galician rising and the defeat at Puentesampayo drove them out that summer.
zh:
卢戈地处内陆，坐落在上米尼奥河畔的一座山丘上，是加利西亚最古老的城镇。罗马人在奥古斯都时代建立卢库斯·奥古斯塔，作为加拉西亚三个司法辖区之一的治所，地处繁忙的金矿区，约260至325年间环以两公里长的城墙，整道墙垣连同各门和塔楼完整地围在老城四周。460年苏维汇人将卢戈升为大主教驻地；585年西哥特征服后城市凋敝，741年阿方索一世兵不血刃入城时，奥多阿里奥主教见城池半毁，着手重建。842年，加利西亚军队在此集结，拥立拉米罗一世；1088年阿方索六世把城市封给主教。卢戈在通往圣地亚哥的原始朝圣路上，朝圣者经米尼亚门前往1129年动工的主教座堂，城中的教士团享有永久供奉圣体这一少见的特权。1312年市民驱逐主教，四年后王子费利佩为对抗主教在此修筑城堡。1444年的卢戈是一座围在罗马城墙内、由教会统治的卡斯蒂利亚古城，声势为圣地亚哥和混战不休的加利西亚贵族所掩。

1467年伊尔曼迪尼奥战争爆发，卢戈派出代表加入兄弟会，在领主们1469年镇压起义之前，这一带的贵族堡垒纷纷被拆毁。16世纪初，卡洛斯一世还能把卢戈列为加利西亚王国的首府之一，但城市此后陷入长期衰落，圣地亚哥则日益繁荣。1669年，加利西亚王国在主教座堂设立一年一度向圣体奉献的仪式，致敬此城永久供奉的圣体。18世纪，圣弗罗伊兰牛市带来复苏，集市1754年获王家特许，马匹和骡子远销莱昂和卡斯蒂利亚；1755年里斯本大地震震裂主教座堂的拱顶，大祭坛被拆除。1809年1月9日，苏尔特的先头部队在城外孔图里斯与撤退中的穆尔所部英军交战，法军随即占领卢戈，直到当年夏天加利西亚起义和蓬特桑帕约之战才把他们逐出该省。

en:
Pontevedra sits at the head of its ria, where the Lérez runs into the sea among the Rías Baixas. It takes its name from an old Roman bridge over the river, and its quays grew up beside the Burgo bridge on the Portuguese road to Santiago, whose arches are carved with pilgrim scallop shells. Fishing and shipbuilding made the town: in 1229 the crown gave its townsmen the monopoly of sardine oil and fish curing across Galicia, and its yards built the fleet that Payo Gómez Chariño, a son of Pontevedra, led to help Ferdinand III take Seville in 1248. By the fifteenth century it was the leading town of Galicia, with the busiest harbour on the coast; the French chronicler Froissart called it the good city. In 1444 it was a thriving Castilian port, living off the catch, the yards and the sea trade.

The crown made Pontevedra Galicia's sole port for loading and unloading cargo, and in 1467 Henry IV granted it the thirty-day free fair, the Feira Franca, for which the walls were extended. Townsmen had joined the first of the Galician brotherhoods in the rias of Pontevedra and Arousa in 1451, and the town sent its men to the Great Irmandiño War of 1467-1469 against the Galician nobles. The yards are traditionally said to have built Columbus's carrack Santa María, 'La Gallega'. The mariners' brotherhood, the oldest sea guild in Spain, paid for the basilica of Santa María la Mayor, whose plateresque facade was finished in 1541. Then the Lérez began to silt up so that large ships could no longer reach the quays, and war and plague cut the population by half. In October 1719 a British expedition under Lord Cobham held the town for ten days. In 1809 a French army occupied the coast until the Galician División del Miño, mustered around Pontevedra, checked it at Puentesampayo on 7-9 June and drove the French out of Galicia.
zh:
蓬特韦德拉位于下海湾地区莱雷斯河入海的河口顶端，城名来自河上一座古罗马桥。码头沿布尔戈桥发展起来，此桥在通往圣地亚哥的葡萄牙朝圣道上，桥拱上刻着朝圣用的扇贝壳。这座城镇靠渔业和造船立足：1229年，王室把全加利西亚沙丁鱼油和咸鱼加工的专营权授予镇民，船坞打造的舰队由本镇子弟帕约·戈麦斯·查里尼奥率领，1248年协助费尔南多三世攻取塞维利亚。到15世纪，它已是加利西亚首屈一指的城镇，港口为全海岸最繁忙，法国编年史家傅华萨称它为「良城」。1444年的它是卡斯蒂利亚治下一座兴旺的港口，靠渔获、船坞和海贸为生。

王室把加利西亚唯一的货物装卸港资格授予蓬特韦德拉；1467年恩里克四世又准其举办为期三十天的自由集市，为此扩建了城墙。早在1451年，镇民就加入了蓬特韦德拉湾与阿罗萨湾一带加利西亚的第一个兄弟会，后来又投身1467至1469年反抗加利西亚贵族的伊尔曼迪尼奥大战。相传哥伦布的克拉克帆船「圣马利亚号」（又名「加利西亚人号」）就出自这里的船坞。西班牙最古老的海员行会出资修建大圣马利亚圣殿，银匠式立面于1541年完工。后来莱雷斯河日渐淤塞，大船无法再驶到码头，战乱和瘟疫又使人口减半。1719年10月，科巴姆勋爵率领的英国远征军占领此城十天。1809年法军占据沿海，在蓬特韦德拉一带编组的加利西亚「米尼奥师」于6月7日至9日在蓬特桑帕约阻击得手，把法国人逐出了加利西亚。

en:
Aveiro sits behind the sandbars of a shallow Atlantic lagoon, at the mouth of the Vouga, where salt pans, fishing grounds and coastal sea lanes meet. The Romans already worked the salt here, and the will Countess Mumadona Dias left in 959 named her lands Alauario et Salinas, the 'bird preserve and salt pans'. John I had walls raised on the advice of his son Peter, the town's lord, and in 1434 Edward I granted an annual duty-free fair, the Feira de Março. In 1444 Aveiro was a walled Catholic salt town and small port held by Peter, Duke of Coimbra and regent of Portugal; its households lived from salt, fish and the coasting trade.

Royal favour came to Aveiro above all through Afonso V's daughter Joanna. She ruled Portugal as regent in 1471 while her father campaigned in Morocco, then entered the Dominican Convent of Jesus in the town and stayed until her death on 12 May 1490, venerated in Portugal as the Holy Princess, Santa Joana Princesa. Manuel I granted the first charter on 4 August 1515, and in 1547 John III created the Duchy of Aveiro for John of Lencastre. Between the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries the lagoon's outlet to the ocean shifted and closed. The port died, the waters stagnated and many fishermen emigrated, and the Misericórdia church was built in those hard years. In 1759 Duke José Mascarenhas was condemned and executed in the Távora affair; the ducal title was extinguished, Joseph I raised Aveiro to city rank, and for a time it was called Nova Bragança. An artificial channel cut through the bar in 1808 gave the lagoon a sea entrance again and brought trade back.
zh:
阿威罗在大西洋浅水潟湖的沙洲背后、沃加河入海处，盐田、渔场和沿海航路在此相接。罗马人已在这里煮盐，959年穆马多娜·迪亚斯伯爵夫人的遗嘱把她的领地记作「鸟类栖地与盐田」（Alauario et Salinas）。若昂一世听取领有此地的儿子佩德罗的建议修筑城墙，1434年杜阿尔特一世又恩准一年一度的免税集市，即后来的三月集市。1444年的阿威罗是一座有城墙的天主教盐业小镇和小港，属科英布拉公爵、葡萄牙摄政佩德罗，居民靠盐、鱼和沿海航运为生。

让王室眷顾阿威罗的，主要是阿方索五世的女儿若阿纳。1471年父亲在摩洛哥作战期间，她以公主身份摄政，随后进入城中的多明我会耶稣修道院，一直住到1490年5月12日去世，葡萄牙人敬称她「圣公主」若阿纳。1515年8月4日曼努埃尔一世颁下第一道特许状，1547年若昂三世为若昂·德·伦卡斯特尔设立阿威罗公爵衔。16世纪末至17世纪初，潟湖入海的水口移动后封闭，港口荒废，积水污浊，许多渔民外迁，仁慈堂教堂就建于这艰难的年月。1759年，公爵若泽·马斯卡雷尼亚斯在塔沃拉事件中被定罪处决，公爵衔遭革除，若泽一世把阿威罗升为城市，还一度改称新布拉干萨。1808年，人们凿开沙洲开出人工水道，潟湖重获入海口，贸易也跟着恢复。

en:
Calatayud commands the Jalón gap, the pass linking the Castilian meseta with the Ebro valley and carrying the road from Zaragoza to Castile. Four kilometres to the north stand the ruins of Augusta Bilbilis, capital of the Celtiberian Lusones and a town already famous for its metalwork; it was the birthplace of the poet Martial about AD 40, who praised its hills and the sulphur springs twenty-four kilometres away, the spas still used at Alhama de Aragón. After Bilbilis declined, the Muslims founded the present town around 716 beside the castle of Ayyub, Qal'at Ayyub in Arabic, from which Calatayud takes its name. Alfonso I of Aragon stormed it on 24 June 1120, consecrated the chief mosque as Santa María and granted fueros to the settlers, and from 1131 the town ruled a wide community of villages. In 1444 it was a prosperous Catholic Aragonese market town on the Castile road, with one of the largest Jewish quarters in the kingdom below the old castle and brick Mudéjar towers rebuilt after the war between Aragon and Castile.

The Jewish aljama, almost as large as Zaragoza's, ended with the expulsion of 1492. Santa María stayed a collegiate church: the town council tried once more to unite its three chapters and win a bishopric in 1592, without success. The Jesuits opened a college late in the sixteenth century, and Baltasar Gracián, born at nearby Belmonte in 1601, taught humanities there in 1627; he later wrote The Art of Worldly Wisdom and the allegorical novel El Criticón. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 their church became San Juan el Real in 1771. Calatayud followed Aragon into the Austrian cause in the War of the Spanish Succession, and came under Bourbon rule after the defeat at Almansa and the Nueva Planta decrees. French troops clashed here in November 1808 and held the town through most of the Peninsular War, until Pedro Villacampa drove them out on 2 October 1812.
zh:
卡拉塔尤德扼守哈隆河谷山口，这里是卡斯蒂利亚高原通往埃布罗河谷的孔道，萨拉戈萨至卡斯蒂利亚的大路从这里穿过。城北四公里是奥古斯塔·比尔比利斯遗址，原为凯尔特伊比利亚卢松人的都城，古时便以金属工艺闻名；约公元40年，诗人马提亚尔出生于此，他在诗中称赞故乡的山野和二十四公里外的硫磺温泉，那里就是后来的阿拉马-德阿拉贡温泉。比尔比利斯衰落后，穆斯林约在716年依阿尤布城堡建起新城，阿拉伯语称「阿尤布堡」，卡拉塔尤德的名字便来自这座城堡。1120年6月24日，阿拉贡国王阿方索一世破城，将大清真寺祝圣为圣马利亚教堂，向居民授予特许状；1131年起，这座城镇统辖广阔的村庄共同体。1444年的卡拉塔尤德是一座繁荣的天主教阿拉贡集镇，位于通往卡斯蒂利亚的大路上，旧城堡下有王国最大的犹太区之一，阿拉贡与卡斯蒂利亚战争后重建的砖造穆德哈尔塔楼矗立城中。

规模几乎仅次于萨拉戈萨的犹太社区在1492年驱逐令后终结。圣马利亚始终只是协同教堂：市政会1592年再次试图合并三个教士团、争取设立主教区，仍未成功。耶稣会在16世纪末创办学院，1601年出生于附近贝尔蒙特的巴尔塔萨尔·格拉西安于1627年在此讲授人文学，他后来写成《智慧书》和寓言小说《批评家》。1767年耶稣会被逐后，其教堂于1771年改为圣胡安·埃尔雷亚尔堂。西班牙王位继承战争中，卡拉塔尤德随阿拉贡支持奥地利阵营，阿尔曼萨之战和《新基本法令》后转入波旁统治。1808年11月法军曾在此交战，半岛战争大部分时间占据城镇，直到1812年10月2日佩德罗·比利亚坎帕将其收复。

en:
Ourense lies inland in a warm valley of the upper Miño, and two things have always defined it: hot water and a bridge. The Burgas springs, channelled since Roman times, run at 60 to 68 degrees; one reading of the town's Roman name Auriense makes it the city of gold, for the gold panned in the Miño. The Romans founded the town to guard the crossing on the road from Braga to Astorga, and the piers of the great bridge over the river are still Roman work. Suevic kings are said to have kept a court here, and after the Moorish capture in 716 and the later raids of Norse fleets and Al-Mansur, the town was rebuilt and resettled in the eleventh century. In 1122 Teresa of Portugal made the bishops lords of the city, and they ruled it for five centuries from Castelo Ramiro, their fortress on the hill, while they consolidated the bridge and drew wealth from the Ribeiro vineyards downstream. The Romanesque cathedral, consecrated in 1188, keeps the Pórtico del Paraíso and the much-venerated Santo Cristo. In 1444 Ourense was a quiet Castilian cathedral town on the Sanabrés road to Santiago.

In 1386 John of Gaunt occupied Ourense and had himself proclaimed king of Castile there by right of his wife, until the Treaty of Bayonne ended his claim two years later; in 1501 Philip the Handsome and Juana met Cardinal Cisneros in the city. During the Irmandiño rising of 1468, rebels stormed the baronial castles of the district and partly pulled down the Count of Lemos's fortress at Castro Caldelas, whose lords later made the villagers rebuild it. The Catholic Monarchs had the bishops' own Castelo Ramiro demolished, and the Jewish quarter was emptied in the expulsion of 1492. Ribeiro wine went down the Miño to the sea and on to England and the Indies, and the old bridge took its present form around 1660. In 1809 French troops overran the district and General Loison burned Castro Caldelas in reprisal for the guerrilla war, before the Galician rising and the victory at Puentesampayo drove the French out that June.
zh:
奥伦塞深居内陆，坐落在上米尼奥河一处温暖的河谷，两样东西自古决定了它的面貌：热水和桥梁。布尔加斯温泉自罗马时代起就被引作浴用，水温高达60至68摄氏度；关于城名的一种解释是罗马名Auriense，意为「金城」，因米尼奥河里可以淘金。罗马人在此建城，扼守布拉加至阿斯托加大道上的渡口，跨河大桥的桥墩仍是罗马旧物。据说苏维汇国王曾在此设宫廷；716年城市被穆斯林攻占，后来又屡遭诺曼舰队和曼苏尔蹂躏，11世纪才得以重建和重新安置。1122年，葡萄牙的特蕾莎把城市管辖权授予主教，此后主教们从山上的卡拉米罗堡统治此城五百年，同时主持加固大桥、从下游的里贝罗葡萄园取得财富。现存罗曼式主教座堂1188年祝圣，堂内有天堂门廊和备受敬奉的圣基督像。1444年的奥伦塞，是萨纳夫雷斯圣地亚哥朝圣道上一座宁静的卡斯蒂利亚主教城。

1386年，冈特的约翰占领奥伦塞，凭妻子的权利在此自立为卡斯蒂利亚国王，两年后《巴约讷条约》终结了他的继承权；1501年，美男子费利佩与胡安娜在此会见希斯内罗斯枢机。1468年伊尔曼迪尼奥起义期间，起事者攻打全区的贵族城堡，拆毁了莱莫斯伯爵在卡斯特罗卡尔德拉斯要塞的一部分，领主回来后又强迫村民将其重建。天主教双王后来下令拆毁主教名下的卡拉米罗堡，1492年犹太区也随驱逐令人去屋空。里贝罗葡萄酒顺米尼奥河运到海边，再远销英格兰和西印度，古桥则在1660年前后完成最后一次大修。1809年法军席卷此地，卢瓦松将军为报复游击战焚毁卡斯特罗卡尔德拉斯，直到当年6月加利西亚起义和蓬特桑帕约之战才把法国人赶走。

en:
Menorca is the smaller and more northerly of the two Gymnesian Islands, a dry country of farms and fishing anchorages. Its prehistoric people left boat-shaped navetes, taules and talaiot towers, which still dot its fields. After James I of Aragon took Mallorca, the Muslim island became his tributary in 1231 and kept its own rulers until Alfonso III invaded in January 1287; much of the population was then enslaved and Catalans settled the island, which in 1343 passed with the Kingdom of Mallorca to the Crown of Aragon. In 1444 it was a thinly peopled Catalan Catholic land, governed from western Ciutadella with Mahón at its eastern end. Mahón's inlet runs five kilometres inland, among the finest natural harbours in the western Mediterranean, on the sea lanes between Iberia, Sardinia and North Africa; mayonnaise is said to take its name from the town.

The sixteenth century brought the island its worst raids. In 1535, after the Spanish capture of Tunis, Hayreddin Barbarossa sacked Mahón and carried off about 600 captives to Algiers. In July 1558 an Ottoman fleet burned Ciutadella and took thousands of its people; the year is still remembered as Any de sa Desgràcia, the Year of Misfortune. Philip II then set his engineer Giovanni Battista Calvi to build Fort Sant Felip across the harbour mouth.

That harbour made Menorca a naval prize in the wars of the next century. An Anglo-Dutch force took the island in 1708 and the Treaty of Utrecht assigned it to Britain five years later. The British moved the capital from Ciutadella to Mahón, opened a Royal Navy dockyard there in 1715 and enlarged Sant Felip into a Mediterranean base. In May 1756 a French fleet beat off Admiral John Byng's relief squadron off the island and the fort surrendered; Byng was court-martialled and shot in 1757 for failing to do his utmost. France returned Menorca in 1763, a Franco-Spanish siege of nearly five months took it in 1782, and the Peace of Paris gave it back to Spain.
zh:
梅诺卡是吉姆内西亚两岛中较小、也更靠北的一座，气候干燥，乡间分布着农庄和渔船锚地。史前岛民留下船形石墓、石桌祭台和圆形石塔，仍散布岛上田野。阿拉贡国王海梅一世攻占马略卡后，这座穆斯林岛屿于1231年称臣纳贡，仍保留自己的统治者；1287年1月阿方索三世发兵入侵，投降之后居民多被鬻为奴隶，加泰罗尼亚移民迁来填补，1343年该岛随马略卡王国并入阿拉贡。1444年的梅诺卡人烟稀少，是操加泰罗尼亚语的天主教之地，岛西的休达德拉为统治中心，岛东端是马翁。马翁港湾深入陆地五公里，是西地中海最好的天然良港之一，扼伊比利亚、撒丁岛与北非之间的海路；据说西文里蛋黄酱一词就得名于马翁。

16世纪是梅诺卡遭劫最重的时期。1535年西班牙攻占突尼斯后，海雷丁·巴尔巴罗萨洗劫马翁，把约六百名俘虏押往阿尔及尔。1558年7月，奥斯曼舰队焚毁休达德拉，掳走数千居民，梅诺卡人把这一年称作「不幸之年」。腓力二世随后命工程师乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·卡尔维主持修筑，在马翁港入口建起圣费利佩堡。

正是这座港湾，让梅诺卡在18世纪的战争中成了各国争夺的海军据点。1708年英荷联军攻占该岛，五年后《乌得勒支条约》把它划归英国。英国人把首府从休达德拉迁往马翁，1715年在港内开设皇家海军船坞，把圣费利佩堡扩建成地中海基地。1756年5月，法国舰队在岛外击退约翰·拜恩率领的救援舰队，堡垒随后投降；拜恩经军事法庭审判，1757年以未尽全力为由被枪决。法国1763年归还梅诺卡，1782年法西联军近五个月的围攻再下该岛，《巴黎条约》又把它交还西班牙。

en:
Ibiza and Formentera, the Pine Islands, are the Balearics closest to the Iberian coast, 150 kilometres from Valencia. Phoenician settlers founded a port here in 654 BC, and Punic Ebusus traded salt, dye, fish sauce and wool; its people honoured the goddess Tanit at the Es Cuieram cave, and in 205 BC the fleeing Carthaginian general Mago called there for men and supplies. Muslim Yabisah looked across the water to Dénia, its nearest market. The Norwegian king Sigurd the Crusader sacked the island in 1110 on his way to Jerusalem, and a Sicilian Norman fleet sacked it again in 1159. In August 1235 Guillem de Montgrí, Archbishop of Tarragona, took Ibiza for James I of Aragon; most of the Muslim population was deported and settlers came from the Girona country. In 1444 it was a Catalan Catholic island run from the walled Vila above the harbour, and the southern salt pans filled the island council's treasury.

Salt was the island's fortune. Seawater was trapped in shallow pools along the southern shore, evaporated, and carried to ships beside the pans, and the Universitat, the island council created in 1299, lived on the trade. Repeated Barbary and Ottoman raids moved Philip II to rebuild the defences in Renaissance form: Giovanni Battista Calvi laid out bastions around the Vila from 1555, and Giacomo Fratín revised the works after 1575, giving Ibiza Town its walled upper city, Dalt Vila.

The island kept its own government until the War of the Spanish Succession. Its elite split, but Ibiza held to the Austrian claimant until Bourbon troops completed the conquest of the Balearics in July 1715. Philip V's Nueva Planta decree that November abolished the Universitat and gave the salt pans to the Crown, so the island's old income flowed to Madrid; the replacement town council was not settled until 1724.
zh:
伊维萨与福门特拉合称松树群岛，是巴利阿里群岛中最靠近伊比利亚海岸的两座，距瓦伦西亚仅一百五十公里。公元前654年，腓尼基商人在此建港，布匿时代的埃布苏斯经营盐、染料、鱼酱和羊毛；岛民在埃斯库埃拉姆洞供奉塔尼特女神，公元前205年败逃的迦太基将领马戈还曾到此征集人马和给养。穆斯林统治时城镇称亚比萨，与隔海相望的德尼亚往来最密。1110年，率军前往耶路撒冷的挪威国王西居尔洗劫该岛，1159年西西里的诺曼舰队又劫掠一次。1235年8月，塔拉戈纳大主教吉列姆·德·蒙特格里替阿拉贡国王海梅一世攻占伊维萨，穆斯林居民多被驱逐，移民主要来自赫罗纳一带。1444年的伊维萨是操加泰罗尼亚语的天主教岛屿，由港湾上方城墙环绕的维拉城治理，南岸盐田的收入供岛务机构开支。

盐是这座岛的财源。海水引入南岸的浅池晒成盐，再从盐田旁装船运走，设立于1299年的岛务自治会就靠这笔收入维持。柏柏尔与奥斯曼海盗反复袭扰，促使腓力二世按文艺复兴样式重修防务：1555年起，乔瓦尼·巴蒂斯塔·卡尔维沿维拉城设计棱堡，1575年后贾科莫·弗拉廷又改造工事，伊维萨城便有了城墙环绕的上维拉。

岛上的自治一直维持到西班牙王位继承战争。岛上精英虽有分歧，伊维萨仍支持奥地利阵营，直到1715年7月波旁军队完成对巴利阿里群岛的征服。同年11月，腓力五世颁布《新基本法令》，废除岛务自治会，把盐田收归王室，岛屿旧日的收入改由马德里支配；取代自治会的市政议会直到1724年才确立。

en:
Tétouan sits in the Martil valley a few miles inland from the Mediterranean, just south of the Strait of Gibraltar, below the ridges of the Rif. The Marinids built a casbah here, and in 1307 Sultan Abu Thabit fortified the town as a base against Ceuta. Its corsairs drew Castile down on it: an army of Henry III razed Tétouan in 1399, and in 1436 the Portuguese garrison of Ceuta sent Duarte de Menezes to raid the ruins before they recovered. In 1444 the valley belonged to the Kingdom of Fez and held little more than a half-ruined settlement among grain fields and orchards.

Its second founding came from Granada. In the 1480s Ali al-Mandri, a captain of Boabdil, the last Nasrid king, led Andalusian Muslims to the ruined town: they raised the walls and then packed the enclosure with houses. After fighting the Beni Hozmar of the hills they paid the Wattasid sultan a heavy sum in gold for his protection and eighty soldiers, and kept the town's autonomy. Jewish refugees from Spain settled here as well, and Tétouan grew into the leading Andalusian city of northern Morocco, called 'Granada's Daughter'; families long kept the keys of houses left behind in Granada. From the 1530s the harbour was one of the chief corsair ports of the western Mediterranean. Captives waited out their ransoms in the mazmorras, a warren of linked underground caves, where Spanish Franciscans came to negotiate; Cervantes, himself a captive in Algiers, lets one of his characters in The Divorce Judge compare marriage to 'captivity in Tétouan's caves', and Leo Africanus reported thousands of Christian prisoners in the town. A Castilian fleet destroyed the harbour in 1565. In the next century the wealthy al-Naksi family ruled Tétouan and held out against Sultan Moulay Ismail, whose troops took it only after hard fighting; an Alaouite governor afterwards raised the Meshwar palace and the Pasha mosque.
zh:
得土安位于马尔蒂勒河谷，距地中海仅数里，在直布罗陀海峡以南，背靠里夫山脊。马林王朝在此筑有城堡，1307年阿布·萨比特苏丹加固城防，作为攻打休达的据点。城中海盗招来卡斯蒂利亚的报复：恩里克三世的军队1399年将得土安夷为平地，1436年葡萄牙据守的休达又派杜阿尔特·德·梅内塞斯，趁城市尚未恢复再洗劫一次。1444年，这片河谷属于非斯王国，谷田和果园之间只剩一处半毁的聚落。

得土安的第二次建城来自格拉纳达。1480年代，末代纳斯里德国王博阿布迪尔的将领阿里·曼德里率安达卢西亚穆斯林来到废城：他们先筑起城墙，再在墙内密密建起宅院。与山里的贝尼·霍兹马尔部交手之后，他们向瓦塔斯苏丹献上重金，换来八十名士兵和庇护，也保住了城市自治。来自西班牙的犹太难民同样在此安家，得土安成长为摩洛哥北部首屈一指的安达卢西亚城市，人称「格拉纳达之女」，许多家族长年保存着格拉纳达旧居的钥匙。从1530年代起，这个港口成为西地中海最主要的海盗港之一。俘虏在彼此连通的地下洞窟「马兹莫拉」里等待赎金，西班牙方济各会修士会入洞洽谈；曾在阿尔及尔为俘的塞万提斯，在《离婚法官》里让人物把婚姻比作「囚禁在得土安的洞窟中」，莱奥·阿菲利加努斯则记载城中关着数千名基督徒囚徒。1565年，一支卡斯蒂利亚舰队摧毁了港口。下个世纪，富有的纳克西家族统治得土安，抗拒穆莱·伊斯梅尔苏丹，后者的军队经苦战才攻下此城；后来一位阿拉维总督建起梅什瓦尔宫和帕夏清真寺。

en:
Mers El Kébir, the Great Harbour, is a roadstead sheltered by hills a few miles northwest of Oran, on the shortest crossing to Iberia. The Almohads built a naval arsenal there in the twelfth century, and in the thirteenth it passed to the Zayyanid sultans of Tlemcen, an inland dynasty that needed a safe anchorage for its trade with Spain. In 1444 merchants moved cloth and other goods between the port, Oran and the caravan road to Tlemcen, and the place mattered as a defensible harbour rather than a large town.

Around 1492 the anchorage became a corsair base, and Iberian expeditions followed. Zayyanid troops beat off a Portuguese force in 1501 and a Spanish one in 1507, but a Castilian fleet took the port in 1505 and renamed it Mazalquivir; from there Cardinal Cisneros's army sailed to conquer neighbouring Oran in 1509. Spain held the twin fortresses for the next two centuries. In 1708 Mustafa Bouchelaghem, bey of Mascara, forced the garrison to surrender, and the Spanish returned only in 1732, when the Duke of Montemar's armada won the battle of Aïn-el-Turk. In 1792 Madrid handed the two ports to the Dey of Algiers, and Mers El Kébir became part of the western beylik.
zh:
凯比尔港意为「大港」，是奥兰西北几英里外被山丘环抱的一处锚地，与伊比利亚半岛隔海相望，航程最短。12世纪，穆瓦希德人在这里建起海军军械库；13世纪它转归特莱姆森的扎扬苏丹，这个王朝深居内陆，需要一处安全锚地维系对西班牙的贸易。1444年，商人把布料等货物在港口、奥兰和通往特莱姆森的商队路之间转运，这里的分量不在城镇大小，而在这座易守难攻的港湾。

1492年前后，这片锚地成了私掠船基地，伊比利亚人的远征随之而来。扎扬军队1501年击退一支葡萄牙部队，1507年又击败一支西班牙部队，但卡斯蒂利亚舰队仍在1505年夺取港口，改名马萨尔基维尔；1509年，西斯内罗斯枢机的军队就是从这里启航去征服邻近的奥兰。此后西班牙据守这对要塞近两百年。1708年，穆阿斯凯尔贝伊穆斯塔法·布歇拉格姆迫降守军，西班牙人迟至1732年才靠蒙特马尔公爵的舰队在艾因图尔克取胜后重返。1792年，马德里宫廷把两港交给阿尔及尔德伊，凯比尔港并入西部贝伊辖区。

en:
Salé faces the Atlantic at the mouth of the Bou Regreg, across the water from the citadel of Rabat. The Romans kept the older settlement of Sala Colonia upstream at Chellah, but Salé itself was founded in the eleventh century by Andalusian families, chief among them the Banu 'Ashara, who supplied its judges and rulers. The Almohad caliph Yaqub al-Mansur built the Great Mosque in 1196, laid out Rabat on the opposite bank, and is said to have joined the two with the first bridge over the river. In September 1260 a Castilian fleet sent by Alfonso X sacked the town during Eid al-Fitr and carried off its people; the Marinid sultan Abu Yusuf Yaqub retook it after a fourteen-day siege, rebuilt the walls, and raised Bab el-Mrisa, a sea gate tall enough for galleys to pass into the harbour. Later Marinid building added the Madrasa of Abu al-Hasan and a maristan, and the Sufi Ibn 'Ashir (d. 1363), the city's patron saint, lies in a domed tomb by the seaside cemetery. In 1444 Salé was the chief Atlantic port of the Kingdom of Fez, its quays filled with merchants and jurists.
