The expulsion of the Moriscos from Spain after 1609 remade the town. Some 3,000 wealthy refugees from Hornachos in Extremadura made the kasbah across the river their stronghold and put to sea as corsairs; English sailors called that bank 'New Salé'. In 1624 they gave their fleet to Jan Janszoon, a Dutchman captured off the Canaries who had turned Muslim as Murad Reis, and made him grand admiral. In April 1627 the Hornacheros expelled the Saadi governor and set up a republic modelled on Genoa and Venice, with a yearly elected Diwan of a dozen notables keeping its papers in Spanish. Murad Reis's corsairs swept the Atlantic, raiding as far as Iceland in 1627 and the Irish fishing town of Baltimore in 1631, where they seized 108 people for the slave markets. Spanish, French and English bombardments could not clear them from the river. The Dila'iya brotherhood made Salé its vassal in 1641, and in June 1668 Sultan Moulay al-Rashid brought the port to the Alaouite dynasty.
zh:
塞拉濒临大西洋，地处阿布·赖格赖格河口，与拉巴特要塞隔水相望。罗马人的萨拉殖民地在更上游的舍拉，塞拉城本身则建于11世纪，建城者是来自安达卢西亚的几大家族，其中以出任法官、执掌市政的巴努·阿沙拉家族最显要。穆瓦希德哈里发雅各布·曼苏尔1196年敕建大清真寺，在对岸营建拉巴特，据说还修起河上第一座桥连接两城。1260年9月，阿方索十世派出的卡斯蒂利亚舰队趁开斋节突袭，洗劫城市、掳走居民；马林苏丹阿布·优素福·叶尔孤白围城十四天才收复，随后重修城墙，建起高得可让桨帆船直驶港内的海上城门迈里萨门。后来的马林苏丹又添建阿布·哈桑经学院和一所马里斯坦病院；塞拉的主保圣人、1363年去世的苏菲修士伊本·阿希尔，就葬在海滨墓园旁的圆顶墓里。1444年的塞拉是非斯王国首要的大西洋港口，码头和经学院里满是商人与法学家。

1609年后西班牙驱逐摩里斯科人，重塑了这座城市。约三千名来自埃斯特雷马杜拉奥尔纳乔斯的殷实难民据有对岸城堡，以此为基地出海为盗，英国水手把那片河岸称作「新塞拉」。1624年，他们把舰队交给荷兰人扬·扬松统领：他在加那利群岛外海被俘，改宗伊斯兰教后取名穆拉德·雷斯，被推举为大统领。1627年4月，奥尔纳乔斯人驱逐萨阿德王朝总督，仿热那亚和威尼斯之制建立共和国，由每年改选的十余名显贵组成迪万议事会治理，公文一律用西班牙语书写。穆拉德·雷斯的海盗船横行大西洋，1627年远袭冰岛，1631年又攻入爱尔兰渔港巴尔的摩，掳走一百零八人卖为奴隶。西班牙、法国和英国的舰队先后炮轰河口，都未能肃清这批海盗。直到1641年迪拉兄弟会迫使塞拉臣服，共和国才走向瓦解，1668年6月穆莱·拉希德苏丹把这座港口并入阿拉维王朝。

en:
Anfa stood on a rise of the Chaouia coast, its Berber name meaning 'the hill', the Atlantic harbour that al-Idrisi counted among the chief ports of the Maghreb al-Aqsa. It grew up in the eighth century in the Berber kingdom of the Barghawata and grew rich on trade with al-Andalus; when the Almohads broke that kingdom they settled Hilalian Arabs across the Tamesna, and the country became the Arabised Chaouia. Under the Marinids the town kept its prosperity: Abu Inan Faris founded a madrasa there between 1348 and 1358, Ibn al-Khatib visited from Granada, and Leo Africanus later wrote of fine houses whose gardens sent fruit as far as Fez. By 1444, with the Marinid state collapsing, Anfa ran its own affairs, a wealthy merchant town whose corsairs raided up to the mouth of the Tagus.

Those pirates drew Portuguese revenge. In 1468 a fleet sent by Afonso V and commanded by the Infante Ferdinand stormed the city and left it in ruins, and for three generations only Salé corsairs and local tribes used its anchorage. Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah rebuilt it from 1760, girdling the new town with walls and the fortified sqala, placing it under a pasha and stocking a sultanic grain silo at Mers-Sultan with Chaouia wheat. He named it Dar al-Bayda, after a whitewashed ruin that Iberian sailors had long used as a seamark and called Casa Branca. Venetian shippers took out the first grain cargoes in 1781, and a Spanish company held the wheat export monopoly from 1788 and carried the name Casablanca into foreign ports. It stayed a modest grain harbour, overshadowed by Mazagan and Mogador.
zh:
安法坐落在沙维耶海岸的一处高地上，柏柏尔语地名意为「山丘」，伊德里西曾把这座大西洋港口列为马格里布最西端的主要港口之一。它于8世纪兴起于柏柏尔人的巴尔加瓦塔王国，因与安达卢西亚通商而富庶；穆瓦希德王朝攻灭该王国后，把希拉勒系阿拉伯部落迁入塔马斯纳，这片地方逐渐阿拉伯化，成为沙维耶。马林王朝治下城市保持繁荣，阿布·伊南·法里斯在1348至1358年间于此兴建伊斯兰学校，格拉纳达的伊本·哈提卜也曾到访；利奥·阿非利加努斯后来记述，这里屋宇华美，园圃出产的水果一直卖到非斯。1444年马林国家土崩瓦解，安法人自行其是，既是富商之城，也是海盗巢穴，寇掠远至塔霍河口。

海盗招来了葡萄牙的报复。1468年，阿方索五世派出、费尔南多亲王统率的舰队攻破安法，将城市夷为废墟；此后近一个世纪，只有萨累海盗和当地部落间或使用这片锚地。穆罕默德·本·阿卜杜拉苏丹1760年起重建新城，环筑城墙与炮台斯卡拉，派帕夏治理，又在米尔苏丹设立苏丹粮仓，收储沙维耶的小麦。他把新城命名为达尔贝达，名字来自一座刷白的废墟：伊比利亚水手早把它当作航标，葡语称之为卡萨布兰卡（Casa Branca）。1781年，威尼斯商人运出了第一批谷物；1788年起一家西班牙公司取得小麦出口专营权，把卡萨布兰卡之名带进各国港口。它始终只是一座不大的谷物港，声势不及马扎甘和摩加多尔。

en:
Tenerife is the largest Canary Island, with Teide rising above its high ravines and pine-covered ridges. The Guanches had herded goats and sheep, farmed coastal plots and fished there for many centuries. By the fifteenth century the island was split into chiefdoms called menceyatos, each under a mencey; traditional accounts traced the division to the descendants of its last common ruler, and Taoro in the fertile north was the strongest. European ships knew the island and raided its coasts, but no foreign garrison held ground there. In 1444 all nine chiefdoms were independent, and the pastures, cave shelters and mountain shrines around Teide were still outside the Castilian conquest reshaping the smaller Canaries.

Diego García de Herrera made a symbolic Castilian claim in 1464 and built a short-lived tower in Anaga. The Catholic Monarchs granted the conquest to Alonso Fernández de Lugo in December 1493. He landed near the future Santa Cruz in April 1494 with about 2,000 infantry and 200 cavalry, but the Guanches defeated him at Acentejo on 31 May by using the steep broken ground. On 14-15 November they lost the open battle of Aguere near La Laguna; another defeat at Acentejo followed, and the remaining menceys submitted by September 1496. Lugo then founded San Cristóbal de La Laguna as the island's first capital. Sugar cane, Malvasia vines and cochineal later tied its estates to Atlantic trade, while Santa Cruz became a centre for corsair expeditions. The 1706 Trevejo eruption buried the north-coast port of Garachico. On 22 July 1797 Horatio Nelson launched an amphibious attack on Santa Cruz; Spanish fire wounded his right arm, which was partly amputated, and the survivors withdrew under a truce on 25 July.
zh:
特内里费是加那利群岛最大的岛屿，泰德峰耸立于高耸沟壑和松林覆盖的山脊之间。许多世纪以来，关切人在这里牧放山羊和绵羊，在沿海地块耕作，也捕鱼采贝。15世纪时，全岛分为若干称为门塞亚托的酋邦，各由门塞统治；传统说法把这种分治归于末代共主的后裔，北部沃土上的塔奥罗最为强大。欧洲船只已经知道此岛，也曾上岸袭扰，却没有外来驻军守住土地。1444年，九个酋邦全部独立，泰德峰周围的牧场、岩洞居所和山间圣所仍在卡斯蒂利亚征服范围之外，而较小的加那利岛屿已被这场征服改变。

迭戈·加西亚·德·埃雷拉1464年代表卡斯蒂利亚作象征性占领，并在阿纳加修建一座短命塔楼。1493年12月，天主教双王把征服权授予阿隆索·费尔南德斯·德·卢戈。1494年4月，他率约两千步兵和两百骑兵，在后来的圣克鲁斯附近登陆；5月31日，关切人凭崎岖地形在阿森特霍将其击败。11月14日至15日，他们在拉古纳附近的阿格雷平原作战失利，随后又在阿森特霍战败，残余门塞到1496年9月相继臣服。卢戈建立圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉拉古纳，作为岛上第一个首府。甘蔗、玛尔维萨葡萄和胭脂虫后来把岛上庄园接入大西洋贸易，圣克鲁斯则发展为海盗活动中心。1706年，特雷韦霍火山喷发，掩埋了北岸港口加拉奇科。1797年7月22日，霍雷肖·纳尔逊向圣克鲁斯发动两栖进攻；西班牙守军的火力击伤他的右臂，手臂随后被部分截去，残部于7月25日在停火协议下撤退。

en:
Kairouan rises in the inland plains fifty kilometres west of Susa, the first Arab city founded in North Africa. Around 670 the general Uqba ibn Nafi camped his army in a forest far from the sea and raised the Great Mosque that bears his name, as a base for the conquest of the Maghreb. Under the Aghlabids it was the capital of Ifriqiya, where jurists such as Sahnun taught Maliki law and the great Aghlabid cisterns were built beyond the walls. The Fatimids withdrew to Mahdia, the Zirids brought the city a second bloom, and in 1057 the Hilali bedouin sacked it and left it in ruins for two centuries; the Hafsids began its revival in the thirteenth century. In 1444 Kairouan was the first holy city of the Maghreb and, in common esteem, the fourth in Islam, a town of pilgrims and grain merchants slowly rising from its ruins.

Outside the walls stands the zawiya of Sidi Sahab, over the tomb of Abu Zama'a al-Balawi, a companion and barber of the Prophet who, tradition says, was buried with three hairs of Muhammad's beard; pilgrim caravans from across the Maghreb gathered there before taking the road to Mecca. The Muradid beys rebuilt the shrine during the seventeenth century and repaired the Great Mosque in 1618. Kairouan also gave the Husainid dynasty its end: Hussein ibn Ali, who restored its walls and founded a madrasa, was defeated by his nephew Ali Pasha at Smendja in 1735, run to earth here and beheaded beneath the ramparts in 1740.
zh:
凯鲁万矗立在苏萨以西五十公里的内陆平原上，是北非第一座阿拉伯人建立的城市。约670年，名将欧格白·伊本·纳菲把军营设在远离海岸的林地中，筑起以他之名命名的大清真寺，作为经略马格里布的据点。阿格拉布王朝时期，它是伊夫里奇亚的都城，塞赫农等法学家在此讲授马立克学派教法，城外修起宏大的阿格拉布蓄水池。法蒂玛王朝迁都马赫迪叶，齐尔王朝一度带来中兴；1057年希拉尔贝都因人洗劫全城，城市荒废了两个世纪，直到13世纪哈夫斯王朝才着手复兴。1444年的凯鲁万是马格里布第一圣城，在通行的说法中也是伊斯兰教第四圣城，朝圣者与粮商往来其间，城市正缓慢走出废墟。

城外的西迪·萨哈布道堂安葬着先知的伙伴兼理发师阿布·宰迈阿·拜莱维，相传他入葬时随身带着先知胡须中的三根，全马格里布的朝觐者先在此会集，再结伴前往麦加。17世纪穆拉德王朝的贝伊们重建圣陵，1618年又整建大清真寺。凯鲁万也成了侯赛因王朝开创者的丧命之地：侯赛因·伊本·阿里曾修复此城城墙、创办经学院，1735年在斯门贾被侄子阿里帕夏击败，逃回这里后被擒，1740年在城墙下斩首。

en:
Sabha is the chief oasis of central Fezzan, on the desert road from the Tripolitanian coast through Hun and Waddan to Murzuk and Bornu. Springs water its palms and the villages of Wadi al-Bawanis. A prominent hill holds the remains of a fortress built over a Garamantian stronghold more than 2,500 years old. Al-Bakri marked Sabha in the eleventh century as a station five days' march south of Hun, where caravans changed guides and took on dates before the long crossing. Kanem and Bornu successively claimed the oases between the thirteenth and fifteenth centuries, while Arab tribes pastured flocks around them. In 1444 Sabha was a caravan town under the lords of Fezzan, supplied with slaves and ivory moving north and horses and cloth moving south.

The Awlad Muhammad included Sabha in their sultanate, and the Ottoman southern campaigns soon reached the oasis. Mahmut Bey led Ottoman expeditions through Fezzan as far as Kawar and Lake Chad, then died in 1583 putting down a revolt backed by Bornu. Ottoman authority stayed loose; Tripoli asserted it only through campaigns in 1679–1682, 1690 and 1718. From 1622 to 1626 Ahmad ibn Huwaydi al-Kharmani, a local chief who claimed Garamantian descent, rebuilt the old hill fortress, later called Fort Elena. When Tripoli absorbed the Murzuk sultanate in 1813, Sabha's caravans and fortress passed under its pashas.
zh:
塞卜哈是费赞中部的主要绿洲，位于的黎波里塔尼亚海岸经洪、瓦丹通往穆尔祖克和博尔努的沙漠路上。泉水滋养着椰枣林和布瓦尼斯河谷的村庄，一处显眼山冈上有座堡垒，建在有2500多年历史的加拉曼特要塞旧址上。11世纪的白克里把塞卜哈记作洪以南五日路程的驿站，商队会在此更换向导、装载椰枣，再开始漫长穿行。13至15世纪，卡涅姆和博尔努先后宣称领有这些绿洲，阿拉伯部落则在周围放牧。1444年，塞卜哈是费赞首领治下的商队城镇，北上货物有奴隶和象牙，南来货物有马匹和布匹。

奥拉德·穆罕默德王朝将塞卜哈划入苏丹国，奥斯曼人的南征很快抵达这片绿洲。马哈茂德贝伊率远征军穿过费赞，远达卡瓦尔和乍得湖，1583年在镇压博尔努支持的叛乱时身亡。奥斯曼的统治仍然松散，的黎波里只通过1679至1682年、1690年和1718年的远征宣示权力。1622至1626年，自称加拉曼特人后裔的本地首领艾哈迈德·本·胡韦迪·海尔马尼重建山冈古堡，即后来的埃莱娜堡。1813年的黎波里吞并穆尔祖克苏丹国，塞卜哈的商队和堡垒也转入当地帕夏治下。

en: Demnate is a Berber market town in the Tassaout valley on the northern foot of the High Atlas, about a hundred kilometres east of Marrakesh; in Tachelhit its name means fertile lands. Local tradition dates the settlement to about 998, when the Inoultan and Infedouak clans made it a meeting place for trade and common defence. A Jewish community established itself there in the early twelfth century, living by wine, leatherwork and crafts, and its mellah became one of the town's quarters. In 1444 Demnate was a market of the Moroccan realm, where Atlas herders and southern caravans dealt in wool, hides, dates, olive oil and grain, and under the Saadians and Alawids it remained a provisioning stop on the tracks from Marrakesh toward the Draa and Tafilalt. Near the town the Imi n'Ifri, a natural rock arch over a cave mouth, stands at the foot of the Atlas.
zh: 代姆纳特是大阿特拉斯山北麓塔萨沃特河谷中的柏柏尔集镇，在马拉喀什以东约一百公里；其名在塔切拉特语中意为肥沃之地。当地传统把定居史追溯到998年前后，伊努尔坦和因费杜瓦克两个氏族当时把这里辟为交易与共同防御的集会地。12世纪初，一个犹太社区在此落脚，以酿酒、皮革和手工业为生，梅拉犹太坊后来成为城区的一部分。1444年，代姆纳特是摩洛哥政权治下的集镇，阿特拉斯山民与南方商队在此买卖羊毛、兽皮、椰枣、橄榄油和谷物；萨阿德与阿拉维时期，它始终是从马拉喀什通往德拉和塔菲拉勒特道路上的补给站。城旁的阿特拉斯山脚下有伊米尼弗里，一座架在洞口上的天然岩拱。

en:
Texcoco was the Acolhua capital on the eastern shore of Lake Texcoco. Its king Nezahualcoyotl was sixteen when Tepanec warriors killed his father, and he fled into exile in Tlaxcala and Tenochtitlan before coming back with Itzcoatl, overthrowing Azcapotzalco and taking his throne in 1431. The Triple Alliance born of that war made Texcoco the second city of the Aztec world, taking two-fifths of the tribute from joint campaigns. By 1444 his court drew the poets and scholars of the valley: he is credited with eighty laws, with aqueducts and flood dikes, and with the songs on 'flower and song' attributed to him. Above the city he laid out the hill of Texcotzingo as royal gardens of medicinal and rare plants, where baths and pools were cut from the living rock and fed by his watercourses; one pool was flanked by three carved frogs, for Texcoco, Tenochtitlan and Tlacopan.

Nezahualcoyotl died in 1472 and his son Nezahualpilli succeeded him. When Hernán Cortés reached the lake in 1519, Cacamatzin ruled Texcoco, and in 1521 the Spaniards made the city the base for their siege of Tenochtitlan, assembling and launching the lake brigantines there. The Franciscan Pedro de Gante learned Nahuatl, wrote a Nahuatl catechism and opened a school where local boys learned Spanish, Latin and crafts. Charles V recognised Texcoco as a city in 1551. It never rivalled the new Mexico City beside it, and through the colonial centuries the lakeshore lived mostly from fishing, farming and country estates.
zh:
特斯科科是特斯科科湖东岸的阿科瓦人都城。国王内萨瓦尔科约特尔十六岁时父亲被特帕内克武士杀害，他流亡特拉斯卡拉和特诺奇蒂特兰，后来随伊斯科阿特尔归国，推翻阿斯卡波特萨尔科，于1431年登上王位。这场战争中结成的三方同盟让特斯科科成为阿兹特克世界的第二大城，分得联合作战全部贡物的五分之二。到1444年，他的宫廷已聚起谷地的诗人和学者：相传他制定八十条律法，主持修筑水渠和防洪堤；传世的「花与歌」诗篇也多托名于他。他又把城后的特斯科钦科山经营成王家园林，种植药草和远方搜罗来的奇木，浴池与池沼从整幅岩石中凿出，由修来的水道引水；其中一座池子边雕着三只青蛙，分别代表特斯科科、特诺奇蒂特兰和特拉科潘。

内萨瓦尔科约特尔1472年去世，其子内萨瓦尔皮利继位。埃尔南·科尔特斯1519年抵达湖畔时，在位的是卡卡马辛；1521年，西班牙人把特斯科科当作围攻特诺奇蒂特兰的大本营，用于湖上作战的双桅船也在此拼装下水。方济各会士佩德罗·德·甘特学会纳瓦语，编写纳瓦语教义问答，并开办学校，向本地男孩教授西班牙语、拉丁语和手工技艺。查理五世1551年正式承认特斯科科为城市。它始终没能比肩身旁新建的墨西哥城，整个殖民时期，湖滨主要靠渔业、农业和庄园维持。

en:
Tlacopan, later called Tacuba, was a Tepanec city on the fertile western shore of Lake Texcoco, once subject to Azcapotzalco. Its ruler Totoquihuaztli joined Itzcoatl of Tenochtitlan and the exiled Nezahualcoyotl to overthrow the Tepanecs in 1428, but in the Triple Alliance they founded Tlacopan remained the junior partner, keeping only one-fifth of the tribute from joint campaigns. The long Mexico-Tacuba causeway ran from the city straight into the island capital of Tenochtitlan. The chronicler Cervantes de Salazar counted six languages spoken in its streets, among them Nahuatl, Otomi, Mazahua and Matlatzinca.

That causeway was the road of La Noche Triste. On the rainy night of 30 June 1520 Cortés led his men out of Tenochtitlan by the shortest route, west towards Tlacopan; soldiers overloaded with gold drowned at the broken gaps in the road, and the survivors who reached Tacuba had lost every cannon. Later tradition placed the tears of Cortés beneath an ahuehuete cypress at Popotla, on this edge of the city. When the Spaniards returned in 1521 the siege of Tenochtitlan ended the alliance. Tlacopan's last ruler, Tetlepanquetzal, was tortured on suspicion of hiding treasure and in 1525 was hanged beside Cuauhtémoc on the Honduras march. A decree of 1526 made the town the encomienda of Isabel Moctezuma, daughter of Moctezuma II, whose households paid fowl, eggs, maize, tortillas and cacao. The Franciscans raised the church of San Gabriel over the old ceremonial precinct, and in later colonial times dozens of haciendas around Tacuba supplied the growing Mexico City with grain, lumber and stone.
zh:
特拉科潘后称塔库巴，是特斯科科湖肥沃西岸的特帕内克城邦，原臣属于阿斯卡波特萨尔科。1428年，君主托托基瓦斯特利与特诺奇蒂特兰的伊斯科阿特尔、流亡归国的内萨瓦尔科约特尔联手推翻特帕内克霸权；但在新生的三方同盟里，特拉科潘始终是小盟友，联合作战所得贡物只分得五分之一。长长的墨西哥城—塔库巴堤道从城中直通岛上都城特诺奇蒂特兰。编年史家塞万提斯·德·萨拉萨尔记载，塔库巴街上能听到六种语言，包括纳瓦语、奥托米语、马萨瓦语和马特拉钦卡语。

这条堤道后来成了「悲痛之夜」的逃路。1520年6月30日雨夜，科尔特斯率军选最短的西路撤出特诺奇蒂特兰，直奔特拉科潘；背负黄金的士兵在堤道缺口处落水溺亡，残部退进塔库巴时火炮尽失。后世传说，科尔特斯就是在城郊波波特拉的一棵墨西哥落羽松下落泪。1521年西班牙人卷土重来，特诺奇蒂特兰围城战终结了三方同盟。特拉科潘末代君主特特莱潘克察尔先因被疑藏匿宝藏而受刑，1525年又在洪都拉斯行军途中与夸乌特莫克一同被绞死。1526年的敕令把此镇封给蒙特祖马二世之女伊莎贝尔·蒙特祖马作委托监护地，辖下民户缴纳禽鸟、禽蛋、玉米、薄饼和可可豆。方济各会在旧祭祀中心上建起圣加百列教堂；殖民时代后期，塔库巴周围数十处庄园为日益扩大的墨西哥城供应粮食、木材和石材。

en:
Malinalco lies in the rugged hills south of Toluca, where paths from the high plateau drop toward the warm country of Cuernavaca and Guerrero. Its valleys were settled by Culhua, Matlatzinca, Ocuilteco and Otomi communities, and by 1444 a Matlatzinca elite ruled a populous town below the Cerro de los Ídolos, whose terraces and shrines had served as a ceremonial centre long before the Aztecs. Malinalco fought wars with Cuauhnahuac and traded with the Basin of Mexico and the Puebla-Tlaxcala valleys, but still kept out of the Mexica Empire.

Axayacatl conquered it in 1476 and made it a tributary town assessed in maguey mantles, grain and stone. Around 1486-1490 Ahuízotl sent carvers from Tenochtitlan to hollow the Cuauhcalli, the House of the Eagle, out of the living rock of the hill: a sanctuary where Eagle and Jaguar warriors were initiated, entered through the gaping jaws of a serpent with fangs and a red-painted forked tongue. Inside, a horseshoe bench was carved with eagles and a jaguar whose hide was spread like a hunting trophy, facing the stone vessel made to receive the hearts of sacrificial captives. The work was still unfinished when the Spanish came. After La Noche Triste the people of Malinalco rose against the newcomers, and Andrés de Tapia subdued them together with Ocuilán. In 1533 the Augustinians took charge of the town and raised the monastery of the Divino Salvador below the hill, building with stone quarried for the abandoned sanctuary.
zh:
马利纳尔科坐落在托卢卡以南的崎岖山地，中部高原的小路从这里下坡，通向夸尔纳瓦卡和格雷罗的暖地。库尔瓦、马特拉钦卡、奥奎尔特克和奥托米社群定居在它的谷地；到1444年，马特拉钦卡上层统治着一座人口稠密的城邦，城后的偶像山上早有层层台地和神庙，是远比阿兹特克人古老的祭祀场所。马利纳尔科曾与夸尔纳瓦克交战，也同墨西哥盆地和普埃布拉至特拉斯卡拉一带有商贸往来，但始终没有并入墨西哥帝国。

阿萨亚卡特尔1476年征服马利纳尔科，把它变成缴纳龙舌兰布、粮食和石材的贡赋城邦。约1486至1490年，阿维索特尔从特诺奇蒂特兰派来石匠，在偶像山的整幅岩体中凿出「鹰屋」：这是鹰战士与豹战士行入会礼的圣所，入口是一条巨蛇张开的大口，露出獠牙和涂红的分叉长舌。内部一圈马蹄形石台上雕着几只雄鹰和一头豹，豹皮像猎获的战利品般摊开；石台对面是石容器，用来盛放献祭俘虏的心脏。西班牙人到来时工程仍未完工。「悲痛之夜」后，马利纳尔科人起兵反抗新来者，安德烈斯·德·塔皮亚将他们与奥基兰人一同平定。1533年，奥斯定会接管此镇，在山下建起圣救主修院，用的正是为废弃圣所采下的石料。

en:
Acámbaro lies on the Lerma at the northeastern edge of the Purépecha state, where the road from Tzintzuntzan runs out toward the Bajío. Farmers of the Chupícuaro culture, among the oldest in Mesoamerica, had worked this riverbank since about 1200 BC and left distinctive painted ceramics. In the fifteenth century Purépecha rulers settled Otomi lineages allied to the Uacúsecha on this stretch of the river to guard the frontier, then posted their own officials over them. The Purépecha name Ak'amparhu referred to the maguey and was also linked to a woman named Ak'amba, and the Otomi called the place Mauadá. In 1444 Otomi farmers and frontier warriors held the Lerma crossing with its maguey and maize fields for the cazonci in Tzintzuntzan.

On 19 September 1526 the cacique Nicolás de San Luis Montañés founded San Francisco de Acámbaro, the first Spanish-ordered town in what is now Guanajuato. Franciscans built the Hospital Temple and, from 1527, a Mudéjar aqueduct under Antonio de Bermul that carried spring water from Tócuaro; the stone bridge over the Lerma followed in 1750, and the town also held the first bullfights recorded in New Spain. The native head town became a republic of Indians, administered together with Yuririapúndaro under the mayor of Celaya. On 22 October 1810 Miguel Hidalgo made Acámbaro the quarters of his Grand Army of America and took the title Generalísimo of the Americas; eighty thousand insurgents paraded that day, against the eight hundred who had answered the Grito de Dolores a month earlier.
zh:
阿坎巴罗位于莱尔马河畔、普雷佩查国家东北缘，从钦聪灿通往巴希奥的道路在此离开高原、进入低地。丘皮库阿罗是中美洲最古老的文化之一，约公元前1200年起就在这段河岸耕作，留下了独具风格的彩陶。15世纪，普雷佩查君主把与瓦库塞查结盟的奥托米氏族安置在这段河畔守卫边境，随后又派来自己的官员统辖。普雷佩查语地名阿坎帕鲁（Ak'amparhu）既指龙舌兰，也关联一位名叫阿坎巴（Ak'amba）的女性；奥托米语则称这里为马瓦达（Mauadá）。1444年，奥托米农民和边境战士为钦聪灿的国王扼守莱尔马河渡口及河畔的龙舌兰田和玉米地。

1526年9月19日，酋长尼古拉斯·德·圣路易斯·蒙塔涅斯建立圣方济各·德·阿坎巴罗，这是今瓜纳华托境内第一座按西班牙殖民秩序建立的城镇。方济各会修建医院教堂，又从1527年起在安东尼奥·德·贝尔穆尔主持下建造穆德哈尔风格输水道，引来托夸罗的泉水；莱尔马河上的石桥1750年建成，新西班牙有记载的第一场斗牛也在此举行。土著首镇成为一个印第安人共和国，与尤里里亚彭达罗一同归塞拉亚长官管辖。1810年10月22日，米格尔·伊达尔戈把阿坎巴罗定为「美洲大军」的驻地，受称「美洲大元帅」；当天受阅的起义者有八万人，而一个月前在多洛雷斯响应呼声起事的不过八百人。

en:
Ihuatzio, the Purépecha 'place of coyotes', lies on the southeastern shore of Lake Pátzcuaro on the slopes below Cerro Tariaqueri. Nahua-speaking farmers held it from about 900 to 1200 and called it Coyoacán, and after 1200 the Purépecha built it up as one of the three heads of their growing kingdom. The Relación de Michoacán tells how, after Tariácuri died, his nephews divided his lands: Hiripan took Ihuatzio, Tangaxoan took Tzintzuntzan and Hiquingaje took Pátzcuaro. Hiripan built a shrine at Ihuatzio for the god Curicaueri and kept the conquest treasure there; later cazoncis moved both god and treasure to Tzintzuntzan, though the lord of Ihuatzio still harangued the army before battle and sat on the council that chose a new king. In 1444, with the court gone, Ihuatzio remained a walled ceremonial centre of raised causeways and rounded yácatas above the lake farms and fishing villages.

The ruins hold three yácatas, temples to Curicaueri and the goddess Xaratanga, a circular observatory and a chac-mool sculpture of the kind associated with Toltec central Mexico. Court life ended with the Spanish conquest after 1530, when the lake district fell to the men of Nuño de Guzmán, yet the community outlasted it as an indigenous town; in 1593 Ihuatzio still counted among the principal settlements governed through the native governors at Tzintzuntzan.
zh:
伊瓦齐奥在普雷佩查语中意为「郊狼之地」，位于帕茨夸罗湖东南岸、塔里亚克里山南坡。约900年至1200年，纳瓦语农民居住于此，称之为科约阿坎；1200年以后，普雷佩查人把它建成兴起中王国的三大首府之一。据《米却肯记述》，塔里亚库里死后，他的几个侄子瓜分领地：伊里潘得到伊瓦齐奥，坦加苏安得到钦聪灿，伊金加赫得到帕茨夸罗。伊里潘在伊瓦齐奥为库里考埃里神建庙，把征战财宝存放在那里；后来的国王把神像和财宝都迁到钦聪灿，但伊瓦齐奥领主仍在战前向全军训话，并参加推选新国王的会议。1444年，王廷虽已迁走，伊瓦齐奥仍是一座有围墙的礼仪中心，高台堤道和圆顶亚卡塔金字塔俯临湖滨农田与渔村。

遗址有三座亚卡塔金字塔、库里考埃里与女神沙拉坦加的神庙、一座圆形观象台，还有一尊与中部墨西哥托尔特克文化同类的恰克莫尔石像。1530年后，西班牙征服终结了这里的王廷生活，湖区落入努尼奥·德·古斯曼的军队之手；但伊瓦齐奥作为土著村镇存续下来，1593年仍是经钦聪灿土著长官治理的主要村镇之一。

en:
Puruarán lies in the well-watered hot lowlands of southern Michoacán, where the ground slopes toward the Balsas River; its Purépecha name means 'place of the steaming springs'. Springs and maize made it the granary of the Purépecha kingdom. The Relación de Michoacán records that the cazonci granted the lands running from Puruarán south to Guerrero to the lord of Tacámbaro, and the maize grown here fed the royal cities around Lake Pátzcuaro. In 1444 the district was governed through that frontier lord, and the country beyond the Balsas belonged to peoples the cazonci never subdued.

Spanish rule arrived with the end of the Purépecha dynasty: after Cristóbal de Olid's men reached Tzintzuntzan the last cazonci, Tangáxuan II, submitted, and in 1530 Nuño de Guzmán had him tortured and burned alive. The hot country was parcelled into encomiendas and later covered with sugar-cane haciendas. The parish church of San José served friars carrying the Gospel through the Tierra Caliente, and a papal bull in 1721 confirmed the feast of the Señor del Huerto, the crucified image venerated in the town. Puruarán saw heavy fighting in the independence war. Early in the revolt the Rayón brothers made it their headquarters, and on 5 January 1814 Agustín de Iturbide, the royalist officer later crowned emperor of Mexico, fell on Morelos's rearguard at the bridge of Puruarán together with Ciriaco del Llano, routed it after a short fight and captured the priest-general Mariano Matamoros, who was executed at Valladolid on 3 February. Morelos's wandering Congress took shelter at the hacienda here in July 1815, a few months before he too was captured and shot.
zh:
普鲁阿兰位于米却肯南部泉水丰沛的炎热低地，地势向巴尔萨斯河倾斜，普雷佩查语地名意为「沸腾泉水之地」。泉水和玉米使它成为普雷佩查王国的粮仓。《米却肯纪事》记载，卡松西把从普鲁阿兰向南直到格雷罗的土地封给塔坎巴罗的首领，这里出产的玉米供应帕茨库罗湖一带的王城。1444年，这片地方由这位边疆首领管辖，巴尔萨斯河对岸是卡松西始终未能征服的族群。

西班牙人的统治伴随着普雷佩查王朝的终结：克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德的人马抵达钦聪灿后，末代卡松西坦加轩二世投降，1530年努尼奥·德·古斯曼将他酷刑后烧死。炎热低地被划为委托监护地，日后遍布甘蔗庄园。圣何塞堂区教堂成为修道士向整个铁拉卡连特传教的据点，1721年教廷下诏，确立镇中供奉的「菜园基督」苦像的节庆。独立战争期间普鲁阿兰战事频繁：起义之初拉永兄弟以该镇为司令部；1814年1月5日，日后加冕为墨西哥皇帝的保王军军官阿古斯丁·德·伊图尔维德与西里亚科·德·利亚诺在普鲁阿兰桥突袭莫雷洛斯的后卫，短战后将其击溃，俘获神父出身的将领马里亚诺·马塔莫罗斯，后者于2月3日在巴利亚多利德被处死。1815年7月，莫雷洛斯辗转各地的国会在当地庄园避难，几个月后莫雷洛斯本人也被俘遭枪决。

en:
Amaxocotlan, later called Mascota, occupied the pine ridges and high meadows of western Jalisco above the rivers that descend toward the Pacific. Its Nahuatl name, Amaxacotlán Mazacotla, describes a place of deer and snakes, and Tecos hunters and farmers worked the mountain valleys around the chief's town. This cacicazgo was not confined to the sierra: Talpa, El Tuito and coastal Chacala all answered to its ruler, opening paths from the highlands to salt, fish and coastal goods. In 1444 it was one of the stronger Tecos polities between the Colima lowlands and the forested Pacific slope.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura reached the town early in 1525, sent north from Colima by Hernán Cortés; the Spaniards called the country Valle de los Venados, the Valley of Deer, and also Valle de Banderas. The district was granted in encomienda to Pedro Gómez and Martín Monje, and Nuño de Guzmán's western campaign subdued Mascota in 1530. Most of the land later passed to the Augustinian college, whose religious steward lived near Mal Paso. At Talpa, within the old chiefdom, Spanish families settled beside the Aranjuez silver workings in 1599; Mascota remained a stopping place between those mountain workings and the coastal lowlands.
zh:
阿马索科特兰后称马斯科塔，地处哈利斯科西部的松林山脊和高山草场，脚下溪河流向太平洋坡地。其纳瓦特尔语全名阿马萨克特兰·马萨克特拉意为「鹿与蛇之地」，特科斯猎人和农人在酋长大镇周围的山谷活动。这个酋邦并不限于山区：塔尔帕、埃尔图伊托和滨海的查卡拉都受其首领统辖，高地因此有路取得食盐、鱼和海货。1444年，它是科利马低地与林木茂密的太平洋坡地之间较强的特科斯人政权之一。

1525年初，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉奉埃尔南·科尔特斯之命从科利马北上，抵达这座山镇；西班牙人把这一带称为「鹿谷」，也称巴耶德班德拉斯。这一地区先被委托给佩德罗·戈麦斯和马丁·蒙赫，努尼奥·德·古斯曼西征时又在1530年压服马斯科塔。后来大部分土地归奥斯定会会院管理，宗教事务管家住在马尔帕索附近。旧酋邦境内的塔尔帕在1599年因阿兰胡埃斯银矿引来第一批西班牙家庭，马斯科塔则继续作为银矿山地同沿海低地之间的停留地。

en:
Tohono means 'desert people', and the driest edge of their country lay on the Gulf of California. This coast belonged to the Hia C-eḍ O'odham, the 'sand dune people', whom the Spanish later called Areneños. Their camps moved between rainwater pools and springs around the Pinacate volcanoes and the Gran Desierto de Altar, whose dunes are the largest in the Americas. Black cinder cones and broad steam-blast craters break the sand, and the Spanish took the name Pinacate from the Nahuatl word for the desert stink beetle. Bands ran down jackrabbits on foot, hunted bighorn sheep and pronghorn with bows, fished and gathered salt on the gulf, and carried shell to the Cocopah and other Yuman peoples near the Colorado Delta; their own ways were closer to those neighbours than to the Piman villages far to the east. In 1444 no road, mission or encomienda reached this shore.

The first European to cross the dune country was the Jesuit Eusebio Kino, who climbed Cerro del Pinacate in 1698 with O'odham guides. The head of the gulf he sighted from the summit helped him argue that Baja California was a peninsula rather than an island, and his map of 1701 carried the conclusion to Europe. Missions and presidios only took root farther east, in the Pimería Alta, where revolt flared in 1695 and again in 1751, and the expulsion of the Jesuits in 1767 withdrew the missionaries most active on the frontier. Those changes touched the river valleys more than the sand sea, and when Mexican independence reached Sonora in 1821 the coastal bands still lived beyond mission control.
zh:
「托霍诺」意为沙漠之人，他们的土地最干旱的一角就在加利福尼亚湾畔。这片海岸属于希亚塞德·奥奥德姆人，族名意为「沙丘之人」，西班牙人后来称他们阿雷尼奥人。他们的营地随着雨水洼和泉眼，在皮纳卡特火山群与阿尔塔大沙漠周围迁徙；这里有美洲最大的沙丘，黑色火山渣锥和巨大的蒸汽喷发口散落在沙海里，皮纳卡特这个名字则得自纳瓦特尔语中的沙漠臭甲虫。各群体徒步追猎野兔，用弓箭捕猎大角羊和叉角羚，到海湾捕鱼、采盐，再把贝壳带到科罗拉多河三角洲的科科帕人及其他尤曼群体那里；他们的习俗更接近这些邻人，而不是远在东方的皮马村落。1444年时，还没有道路、传教站或监护征赋区延伸到这条海岸。

第一个穿过沙丘地带的欧洲人是耶稣会士欧塞维奥·基诺。1698年，他在奥奥德姆向导带领下登上皮纳卡特峰，从山顶望见的海湾尽头成为他论证下加利福尼亚是半岛而非岛屿的依据之一，他1701年的地图把这一结论带到了欧洲。传教站和要塞只在更东边的皮梅里亚阿尔塔扎下根，1695年和1751年两度爆发起事，1767年耶稣会被逐，这边疆上最活跃的传教士也就撤走。这些变动影响的是河谷而不是沙海，1821年墨西哥独立的消息传到索诺拉时，沿海群体仍在传教控制之外。

en:
Tzapotzingo was one of three Totorame-speaking chiefdoms on the Nayarit coastal plain, alongside Aztatlán and Senticpac. Its subject towns were Tepehuacan, Guaristemba, Mecatlan and Xalxocotan, and Mecatlan stood on the shoreline later chosen for the port of San Blas. Farmers grew maize, beans and chile; fishing boats brought in fish and shrimp, and salt made along the shore was carried up to the Cora and Huichol mountains to trade. By the fifteenth century the old Aztatlán network had broken into rival chiefdoms. In 1444 Tzapotzingo governed itself, bordering the inland sphere of Xalisco and lying well beyond the reach of Tenochtitlan.

Francisco Cortés de San Buenaventura entered Nayarit in 1526 and some chiefs submitted without fighting, but the conquest that held was carried out by Nuño de Guzmán from 1530; his Villa del Espíritu Santo, founded in November 1531, became Tepic. During the Mixtón War of 1540-1542 Francisco Pantecatl, cacique of Tzapotzingo, described the prophets' ceremony in the Huasamota valley that called on the peoples of Nueva Galicia to drive out the Spaniards, before Viceroy Mendoza's army broke the rising. In 1768 José de Gálvez made San Blas a royal naval base and shipyard for expeditions to Sonora and California. Juan Pérez sailed north from the port in 1774 and became the first European to chart the islands off British Columbia, and in 1775 Juan Francisco de la Bodega y Quadra reached Alaska in the Sonora, a schooner built in the San Blas yard. The insurgent priest José María Mercado seized Tepic and San Blas in 1810 and was killed in the royalist counterattack the following January.
zh:
察波钦戈是纳亚里特沿海平原上三个讲托托拉姆语的酋邦之一，与阿斯特兰、森蒂克帕克并列。属村有特佩瓦坎、瓜里斯滕巴、梅卡特兰和哈尔尔索科坦，梅卡特兰所在的海岸后来被选为圣布拉斯港址。农家种植玉米、豆类和辣椒，渔船捕回鱼和虾，海滨出产的盐被运进科拉人和惠乔尔人的山地交易。到15世纪，旧阿斯特兰网络已分裂为彼此争战的酋邦。1444年，察波钦戈由自己的首领统治，毗邻内陆的哈利斯科势力范围，远在特诺奇蒂特兰的势力之外。

1526年，弗朗西斯科·科尔特斯·德·圣布埃纳文图拉进入纳亚里特，一些酋长不战而降；真正站住脚的征服由努尼奥·德·古斯曼从1530年开始，他1531年11月建立的圣灵镇后来发展为特皮克。1540至1542年米克特战争期间，察波钦戈酋长弗朗西斯科·潘特卡特记述了瓦萨莫塔谷的先知仪式，仪式号召新加利西亚各族驱逐西班牙人，最后门多萨总督的军队镇压了起义。1768年，何塞·德·加尔韦斯把圣布拉斯建成皇家海军基地和船厂，作为远征索诺拉和加利福尼亚的跳板。胡安·佩雷斯于1774年由圣布拉斯北航，成为最早绘制不列颠哥伦比亚外海岛屿的欧洲人；1775年，胡安·弗朗西斯科·德·拉·博德加·伊·夸德拉驾驶圣布拉斯船厂建造的「索诺拉号」纵帆船抵达阿拉斯加。1810年，起义神父何塞·马里亚·梅尔卡多夺取特皮克和圣布拉斯，次年1月在保王派反攻中被杀。

en:
Sayula occupies a wide inland basin south of Lake Chapala, where shallow briny lagoons evaporate into salt. Its people were Tecos, Nahuatl speakers who called the town Tzaulan, 'the place where flies abound'. In 1444 it was a chiefdom inside the Tecos kingdom of Colimán, and its salt and saltpeter drew traders along the western Mexican roads. Those same beds drew a Purépecha invasion: between 1480 and 1510 the cazonci marched west to seize the saltpeter workings, and Colímotl of Colima led the lords of Sayula, Zapotlán and Amula against him, fought him at Zacoalco, and threw the Purépecha armies out of Colima and Jalisco. The peace cost the cazonci a quarter of his lands, which passed to Colima.

Spaniards reached Tzaulan in 1523 with Alonso de Ávalos, a cousin of Cortés, who made the town the seat of his encomienda and the capital of the Provincia de Ávalos. In the 1570s Franciscans built the Convent of San Francisco and opened an Indian hospital beside it, and the Saturday market grew large enough for Sayula to join the twelve towns allowed to send deputies to the merchants' tribunal of the Guadalajara consulado; pack trains carried out salt and soap and brought back cloth and knives. In 1742 clay pipes led spring water to a new stone fountain in the main square. When news of Hidalgo's rising arrived in October 1810 the Spanish merchants fled, and José Antonio Torres entered on 28 October with five thousand men. Among the local men who rode out to join him was the priest José Guadalupe Montenegro, whose own conspiracy had been uncovered seventeen years earlier.
zh:
萨尤拉位于查帕拉湖以南一片开阔的内陆盆地，水浅味咸的潟湖经日晒蒸发产出食盐。居民是说纳瓦特尔语的特科斯人，他们把镇子叫作察乌兰，意为「苍蝇成群之地」。1444年，萨尤拉是特科斯科利曼王国境内的一个酋邦，所产食盐和硝石吸引商人沿西墨西哥的道路前来。正是这些盐滩引来普雷佩查的入侵：1480至1510年，卡松西为夺取硝石产地西征，科利马的科利莫特尔率领萨尤拉、萨波特兰和阿穆拉的首领迎战，在萨科阿尔科与普雷佩查人交战，将其军队逐出科利马和哈利斯科；停战的代价是卡松西四分之一的土地并入科利马。

1523年，科尔特斯的表亲阿隆索·德·阿瓦洛斯抵达察乌兰，把镇子设为自己委托监护地的治所和阿瓦洛斯省的省会。1570年代，方济各会建起圣方济各修道院，并在旁边开设印第安人医院；每周六的集市规模日大，萨尤拉也成为获准向瓜达拉哈拉商会商事法庭选派代表的十二座城镇之一，驮队运出食盐和肥皂，换回布匹和刀具。1742年，陶土管道把泉水引入主广场新建的石砌喷泉。1810年10月，伊达尔戈起义的消息传来，西班牙商人纷纷出逃，何塞·安东尼奥·托雷斯于10月28日率五千人入城；本地人中策马投奔他的还有神父何塞·瓜达卢佩·蒙特内格罗，此人自己的密谋早在十七年前就已败露。

en:
Tecomán occupies the hot coastal plain of Colima, where the mountains run down to lagoons and the Pacific. Its Tecos people, Nahuatl speakers, farmed and fished the valley and kept their ruler's seat at Caxitlán; in 1444 Colimán was the strongest power on the western shore. Fishermen worked the lagoons and the salt pans sent salt inland, and those same beds were coveted across the eastern hills by the Purépecha cazonci. His invasion went badly: in the Saltpeter War of 1480–1510 the Tecos king Colímotl defeated the Purépecha at Zacoalco, brought the lords of Sayula, Zapotlán and Amula under tribute, and took a quarter of the cazonci's lands.

Colímotl then handed Cortés's captains their worst set of reverses in western Mexico. His warriors beat Juan Rodríguez de Villafuerte at Trojes, killed Juan Álvarez Chico in a mountain defile, and drove Cristóbal de Olid back from the Paso de Alima, until Gonzalo de Sandoval arrived with Spaniards and Purépecha, Tlaxcalan and Mexica allies, feigned a retreat at Alima in 1523, and routed the Tecos; Colímotl was probably killed in the fight. On 25 July 1523 Sandoval founded the Villa de Colima at Caxitlán, the first Spanish town council in western New Spain, and the Indian town of Santiago de Tecomán was laid two leagues away, with a hospital of Saint James recorded there by the middle of the century. The Spanish town was moved to an inland site in 1527, and Caxitlán dwindled until a fire in October 1800 burned down its parish church. In 1812 the insurgent captains Pedro and Manuel Regalado took Tecomán and Caxitlán and sacked the royal salt works of San Pantaleón.
zh:
特科曼位于科利马炎热的沿海平原，群山在此降至潟湖与太平洋。特科斯人说纳瓦特尔语，在这片河谷耕种捕鱼，首领的驻地设在卡希特兰；1444年，科利曼是西部海岸最强大的势力。渔民在潟湖中捕捞，盐田出产的盐输往内陆，东山之外的普雷佩查卡松西也觊觎着这些盐滩。他的入侵却以惨败收场：1480至1510年的硝石战争中，特科斯人的国王科利莫特尔在萨科阿尔科击败普雷佩查军队，迫使萨尤拉、萨波特兰和阿穆拉的首领向他纳贡，并夺占卡松西四分之一的土地。

科利莫特尔随后让科尔特斯麾下的统领们在西墨西哥连吃败仗。他的战士在特罗赫斯击败胡安·罗德里格斯·德比利亚富埃尔特，在山隘中杀死胡安·阿尔瓦雷斯·奇科，又把克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德从阿利马山口击退；直到贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔率西班牙人及普雷佩查、特拉斯卡拉和墨西卡盟军前来，1523年在阿利马佯退设伏，击溃特科斯人，科利莫特尔可能战死阵中。1523年7月25日，桑多瓦尔在卡希特兰建立科利马镇，这是新西班牙西部第一个西班牙市镇议会；两里格外另设印第安人城镇圣地亚哥·德·特科曼，到16世纪中叶，那里已有一座供奉圣地亚哥的医院。1527年西班牙人的城镇迁往内陆新址，卡希特兰日渐凋零，1800年10月的一场大火烧毁了它的堂区教堂。1812年，起义军首领佩德罗和曼努埃尔·雷加拉多攻占特科曼和卡希特兰，洗劫了王家的圣潘塔莱昂盐场。

en:
Yohualtepec was the Nahuatl name for the broken mountain country where Guerrero's La Montaña highlands meet the Mixteca and the edge of Puebla. Its paths linked Coixtlahuaca with Tlapa, and Tlapanec farmers, whom the Mexica called Yope, shared the valleys with Mixtec and Nahua communities. Huamuxtitlán, the western town whose history can be traced, was founded around 1200 as Cuamuztitlán and kept ties with the Mixtec head town of Alcozauca. In 1444 no imperial road ran through these hills and no garrison collected tribute for Tenochtitlan.

In the later fifteenth century Triple Alliance armies subdued the Tlapanec towns and made Huamuxtitlán a strongpoint; the archaeologists of Mexico's National Institute of Anthropology and History attribute the campaign to Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco, the poet-king who helped found the Alliance. The district became part of the tribute province of Yohualtepec, which the Codex Mendoza assesses at forty gold disks the size of communion wafers. After the Spanish conquest Bernardino Vázquez de Tapia held Huamuxtitlán as an encomienda from 1531. Augustinians began the convent of Santa María de la Asunción in 1534 with dressed stone from the old temple, and the central pyramid of the native town stands directly behind its church.
zh:
约瓦尔特佩克是纳瓦特尔语对一片崎岖山地的称呼，位于格雷罗的拉蒙塔尼亚山区、米斯特克和普埃布拉边缘相接之处。山中的小路连接科伊斯特拉瓦卡和特拉帕，被纳瓦人称作约佩人的特拉帕内克农夫，与米斯特克人、纳瓦人共居各条山谷。瓦穆斯特特兰是这一带历史可考的西部城镇，约1200年以夸穆斯特特兰之名建立，同米斯特克首领城镇阿尔科绍卡保持着联系。1444年，还没有帝国大道穿过这些山岭，也没有驻军替特诺奇蒂特兰征收贡赋。

15世纪后期，三方同盟军队征服特拉帕内克诸镇，把瓦穆斯特特兰建成堡垒；墨西哥国立人类学和历史研究所的考古学者认为，率军出征的是特斯科科的「诗人国王」内萨瓦尔科约特尔，他也是三方同盟的缔造者之一。这一地区被纳入约瓦尔特佩克贡赋省，《门多萨手抄本》登记的贡物是四十个圣饼大小的金盘。西班牙征服后，贝尔纳迪诺·巴斯克斯·德·塔皮亚自1531年起领有瓦穆斯特特兰的监护权。1534年，奥斯定会修士拆用旧神庙的修凿石料动工修建圣母升天修道院，旧城的中央金字塔就在教堂背后。

en:
Teotitlan, 'between the houses of the gods' in Nahuatl, stands at the mouth of the Oaxacan Canada, the steep corridor that drops from the Puebla highlands to the tropical lowlands. The town was Nahua, home of the Nonoalca among Mazatec and Cuicatec villagers, with Huautla, Nanahuatipam and Mazatlan subject to it. Three priest-lords ruled, the chief called Teuctlamacaz, serving Cihuacoatl and a local form of Xipe Totec; they kept strict abstinence rites and lit the new fire every four years. Its weavers made cloth carried as far as Guatemala. Whether the Aztec Empire ever ruled it is uncertain. A report drawn up here in 1581 remembered Teotitlan as an independent republic, allied to Moctezuma but paying no tribute; other accounts say Moctezuma I rebuilt the town in 1430, or that Axayacatl stormed it after a revolt, killed the old Cuicatec population and settled Mexica in their place. In 1444 it was in any case the strongest town at the head of the Canada.

Under the viceroys it became Teotitlan del Camino, named for the royal road that ran from Tehuacan and Puebla down to Antequera: it was the first Oaxacan town on that road, where travellers stopped before entering the Canada. It served as a district seat under the Intendancy of Oaxaca and entered independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
特奥蒂特兰在纳瓦语中意为「众神之屋之间」，地处瓦哈卡卡尼亚达峡谷的入口，这条险峻通道从普埃布拉高原直下热带低地。城本身是纳瓦人诺诺阿尔卡人的居所，周围是马萨特克人与奎卡特克人的村寨，瓦乌特兰、纳纳瓦蒂潘和马萨特兰等镇都受它统属。三位祭司首领共治此城，为首者称特乌克拉马卡斯，供奉西瓦科亚特尔和当地化身的希佩托特克；他们恪守严苛的斋戒仪轨，每四年举行一次新火典礼。织工出产的布匹远销至危地马拉。阿兹特克帝国是否曾统治它并无定论：1581年在此写成的一份记述回忆，特奥蒂特兰是独立共和国，与蒙特苏马结盟而不纳贡；另一些记载则说蒙特苏马一世1430年重建此城，或说阿萨亚卡特尔在一场反叛后攻破它、屠戮旧奎卡特克居民、迁入墨西加移民。无论如何，1444年的它是卡尼亚达北口最强的城镇。

总督时期，它得名特奥蒂特兰-德尔卡米诺，即「大道上的特奥蒂特兰」；在从特瓦坎、普埃布拉通往安特克拉的王家大道上，它是进入瓦哈卡后的第一座城镇，旅人入峡谷前在此歇脚。它作为瓦哈卡行政区下的区治，于1821年并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
The rainy eastern slope of Citlaltepetl, the snow peak the Cuauhtochca Totonacs called Poyauhtecatl after the Chichimec town their people had left, was the country of Cuauhtochco. Its villagers had come down from the Puebla sierra around 1325 and grouped their settlements into chiefdoms, with the old village of Tetlalpa among them. They did not practise human sacrifice: they burned incense with offerings of flowers and birds, danced and sang mournful chants before their gods, and their priests taught the village children and held office under the chiefs. The road between the central plateau and the Gulf coast crossed their maize lands and cloud-forest hamlets. In 1444 these valleys still answered to their own lords, but the armies of Moctezuma I were already closing on the region.

About 1454 a son of Netzahualcoyotl, leading the forces of the Triple Alliance, conquered Cuauhtochco and bound it under heavy tribute, leaving its customs otherwise untouched. In 1520, when news of the Noche Triste reached the mountains, the towns rose and killed more than a hundred passing Spaniards. In November 1521, after the fall of Tenochtitlan, Gonzalo de Sandoval marched through and subdued them, and under the encomienda the survivors paid tribute in cotton and cacao. In 1597 fifteen Spanish families were settled here as San Juan Coscomatepec, and four of their heads of household later joined the founders of the nearby city of Cordoba. In October 1813 Nicolas Bravo and six hundred insurgents broke the royalist siege that had pinned the town for thirty-three days. The district joined independent Mexico in 1821.
zh:
索科特拉群山坐落在奥里萨巴山多雨的东坡。这座雪峰当地夸赫托奇科托托纳克人称之为波亚乌特卡特尔，得名于他们先民迁出的奇奇梅克城波亚乌特兰。这一带是夸赫托奇科之地：约1325年，他们从普埃布拉山地迁来，把聚落组成若干酋邦，特拉拉尔帕旧寨便是其中之一。他们不行人祭：向神祇焚香时献上鲜花和飞鸟，在神像前起舞、唱起哀歌，祭司兼任村塾教师，并在首领手下任职。一条连接中央高原与墨西哥湾沿岸的道路穿过玉米地和云雾林中的村寨。1444年，这些山谷仍听命于本地首领，而蒙特苏马一世的军队已在步步逼近。

约1454年，内萨瓦尔科约特尔之子率三国同盟军队征服夸赫托奇科，科以沉重贡赋，其余习俗一仍其旧。1520年「悲痛之夜」的消息传入山区后，诸镇起事，杀死一百多名路过的西班牙人；1521年11月特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔进军此地将其平定，在委托监护制下幸存者改以棉花和可可纳贡。1597年，十五户西班牙家庭在此定居，建立圣胡安·科斯科马特佩克，其中四户的家长后来参与了邻近科尔多瓦城的创建。1813年10月，尼古拉斯·布拉沃率六百名起义军打破了王党军围困该镇三十三天的封锁。1821年，此地并入独立后的墨西哥。

en:
Mitla lies at the upper end of the Tlacolula valley, the eastern arm of the central valleys of Oaxaca. The Zapotecs called it Lyobaa, the 'place of rest'; the Mexica knew it as Mictlan, the place of the dead, from whose name the Spanish form Mitla comes. It began as a fortified village and, as Monte Albán lost power, became the Zapotec world's main religious centre, a burial city for nobles who were expected to become 'cloud people' and intercede for the living. Mixtec rulers took it around 1000, yet its Zapotec priests kept their authority. In 1444 Mitla was a largely autonomous holy city under the kings of Zaachila, its palace walls faced in mosaic fretwork of small polished stones cut and fitted without mortar, decorative work found nowhere else in Mexico.

The high priest Uija-tào still held the sanctuary when the Spaniards entered the valley in 1521, and the friar Motolinía described its temples within a generation, taking the city's name to mean hell. Later in the sixteenth century Bishop Bernardo de Albuquerque had the palaces dismantled and sacked, to dissolve the power the sacred site still held over the region; Spanish clergy then moved into its rooms. Monolithic lintels and dressed blocks from the Zapotec halls went into the church of San Pablo, raised on one of the sacred quadrangles. Diego García de Palacio wrote his description of the ruins in 1576, and the pueblo of San Pablo Villa de Mitla grew around the church on the road from Antequera to Tehuantepec.
zh:
米特拉位于瓦哈卡中央谷地东支特拉科卢拉谷的上游。萨波特克人称它为略奥瓦，意为「安息之地」；纳瓦人叫它米克特兰，意为亡者之地，西班牙文名称米特拉就是这个名字的转写。它起初是一处设防村落，阿尔班山失势后成为萨波特克世界最重要的宗教中心，是安葬贵族的葬城：人们相信葬在这里的贵族会化作「云之人」，为活着的人代祷。约1000年米斯特克君主夺取此城，萨波特克祭司却仍保有权威。1444年，米特拉是萨奇拉诸王治下一座高度自治的圣城，宫殿墙面布满用细小磨光石块切割拼合、不用灰浆的回纹镶嵌，这种装饰工艺在墨西哥别处见不到。

1521年西班牙人进入谷地时，大祭司乌伊哈-塔奥仍主持着圣所，修士莫托利尼亚在一代人之内就记述了这里的庙宇，并把城名理解为地狱。16世纪后期，主教贝尔纳多·德·阿尔武尔克尔克下令拆毁、洗劫古宫殿，以消解这座圣所对当地仍保有的影响力；西班牙教士随后住进其中的房间。萨波特克殿堂的整石横梁和修凿石块被用于修建圣巴勃罗教堂，教堂就建在一处神圣庭院之上。迭戈·加西亚·德·帕拉西奥1576年写下对废墟的记述，圣巴勃罗·米特拉村则在教堂周围、安特克拉通往特万特佩克的大道旁发展起来。

en:
The Tzotzil, whose name means the 'people of the bat', occupy the cold pine-clad ridges and valleys of Los Altos, the highlands of Chiapas, where their ancestors had settled by the early centuries of the first millennium. On the eve of the conquest their country was divided among at least seven small lordships; Zinacantán was the strongest, with Chamula and Huixtán beside it, each lord enthroned in a fortified hilltop town. They wove cotton, worked amber, drew salt from wells near Ixtapa and sent quetzal feathers and amber north to Tenochtitlan. In 1444 the highland towns were free, quarrelsome and rich by the measure of the sierra.

The first Spaniards entered as allies rather than conquerors: in December 1522 Cuzcácuatl, lord of Zinacantán, travelled down to the Spanish town of Espíritu Santo on the Gulf coast to offer an alliance, and at Easter 1524 Luis Marín's expedition, guided and fed by Zinacantec warriors, subdued the rival lordships; the people of Chamula and Huixtán abandoned their towns and fled into the mountains rather than serve. Encomiendas soon parcelled out the survivors, and on 31 March 1528 Diego de Mazariegos founded Villa Real de Chiapa, raised in 1536 to Ciudad Real de Chiapa, the seat of Spanish power over the highland towns. Bartolomé de las Casas arrived there in 1543 as the first bishop of Chiapa.

Heavy tribute and a new cult at Cancuc brought the highlands out in revolt in June 1712. A Tzeltal girl, María de la Candelaria, said the Virgin had appeared to her, and when the clergy refused to recognise the shrine the rebels proclaimed there was no longer a king, ordained their own priests and named their own bishops; thirty-two Tzeltal, Tzotzil and Ch'ol towns joined, their fighting men calling themselves 'soldiers of the Virgin', and held most of the highlands for three months. Royal troops retook Cancuc on 21 November and crushed the rising with great severity.
zh:
索西人的族名意为「蝙蝠人」，世居恰帕斯中部高寒的松林山脊与谷地，他们的祖先早在公元后最初几个世纪已在此定居。征服前夕，这片土地分裂为至少七个小邦，齐纳坎坦最强，查穆拉、维斯坦等次之，各邦君主坐镇筑垒的山头城镇。他们织棉布、制琥珀，从伊斯塔帕附近的盐井取盐，又把格查尔鸟羽毛和琥珀北销特诺奇蒂特兰。1444年，这些高原城镇自由、好斗，以山地的标准算得上富庶。

第一批西班牙人是以盟友身份进山的。1522年12月，齐纳坎坦首领库斯卡夸特尔南下墨西哥湾沿岸的西班牙人城镇圣灵镇求盟；1524年复活节，路易斯·马林的远征队靠齐纳坎坦战士引路供粮，征服了敌对各邦，查穆拉和维斯坦的居民则弃城逃入深山，不愿臣服。幸存者很快被编进监护征赋制分给征服者。1528年3月31日，迭戈·德·马萨列戈斯建立恰帕皇家镇，1536年升格为恰帕王城，成为西班牙人统辖高原诸城的中心。1543年，巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯到此就任恰帕首任主教。

沉重的贡赋和坎库克兴起的新崇拜，终于在1712年6月激起高原大暴动。特塞尔塔尔女孩玛丽亚·德·拉·坎德拉里亚自称见到圣母显灵，教士拒绝承认这座圣所后，起义者宣布世上已无国王，自行任命神父、册封主教；三十二个特塞尔塔尔、索西和乔尔人城镇参与起事，战士自称「圣母的士兵」，控制高原大部三个多月。王家军队在11月21日攻陷坎库克，残酷镇压了暴动。

en:
The Jacaltenango plateau sits on the high north-western shelf of the Cuchumatanes, above the river frontier with Chiapas. The Jakaltek Maya, who call themselves Popti', know their chief town as Xajlaj, 'the place of the great white rock slabs'; the Nahuatl-speaking auxiliaries in Alvarado's army later rendered it as Xacatenango, 'the wall of huts'. Jacaltenango was the first and principal town of the Huista country, whose market drew together trails from the Petén lowlands and paths climbing from the Pacific coast. Jakaltek oral tradition names B'alunh Q'ana as its founder, a fugitive from the northern land of Yichkanh. The sierra kept the highland empires at arm's length, though local memory holds that K'iche' war parties reached this far under K'iq'ab the Great (1425-1475). In 1444 the Jakaltek towns kept their own lords and their own Q'anjob'alan tongue.

Spanish troops overran the Guatemalan highlands in 1524, but rule here stayed distant. In 1529 Jacaltenango, together with San Mateo Ixtatán and Santa Eulalia, was granted in encomienda to Gonzalo de Ovalle, one of Alvarado's companions, and a town of some two thousand Indians became his estate. Dominicans carried out the first reducción there in 1549, gathering scattered hamlets into a Spanish-style town. The Mercedarians later swapped their parishes near the new capital for the Cuchumatanes doctrines, formed their Guatemalan province in 1565 and raised the convent of Nuestra Señora de la Purificación in 1567. Beyond those parishes the forest frontier stayed unsafe: independent Lacandones raided all through the seventeenth century, and the Spanish kept garrisons in the northern towns. Around 1690 the chronicler Fuentes y Guzmán found a town shrunk to eight hundred people, which he called 'an ancient and principal place, the court of some cacique'. In 1754 the Bourbon reforms took the doctrine from the Mercedarians and handed it to the secular clergy.
zh:
哈卡尔特克人自称波普蒂人，他们的台地坐落在库丘马塔内斯山西北缘，脚下就是与恰帕斯分界的河谷。首镇在哈卡尔特克语里称哈伊拉赫，意为「巨大白石板之地」；随阿尔瓦拉多军队而来的纳瓦语援军后来把它读作哈卡特南戈，意思是「茅屋之墙」。哈卡尔特南戈是维斯塔地区最早、最大的城镇，佩滕低地的山道与从太平洋岸攀上来的小路都会聚到镇集。哈卡尔特克口述传统把建镇者记作巴尔温·卡纳，说他是从北方的伊奇坎之地逃来的人。群山把高原帝国挡在远处，不过当地人记得，在基卡布大王（1425—1475年在位）治下，基切人的战阵曾推进到这里。1444年，哈卡尔特克诸城仍奉自己的首领、说自己的坎霍瓦尔兰语。

1524年西班牙军队席卷危地马拉高地，但对此地的统治一直疏阔。1529年，哈卡尔特南戈连同圣马特奥-伊斯塔坦、圣欧拉利娅一起被作为监护地封给阿尔瓦拉多的部将贡萨洛·德·奥瓦列，这座约有两千印第安人的城镇成了他的私产。1549年，多明我会首次在此集村归化，把分散的村舍并入西班牙式城镇。仁慈圣母会后来用新都附近的牧区换来库丘马塔内斯的教区，1565年成立其危地马拉会省，1567年建起净礼圣母修道院。教区之外的林缘始终不太平：整个17世纪，独立的拉坎东人不断入袭，西班牙人在北部诸城驻军。1690年前后，编年史家富恩特斯-古斯曼见到的城镇已缩至八百人，他称之为「古老而首要之地，曾为某位酋长的宫廷」。1754年，波旁改革把这一教区从仁慈圣母会手中收归世俗教士。

en:
Q'umarkaj, called Utatlán by the Nahuatl-speaking allies of the Spanish, was the capital of the K'iche' Maya and the strongest city of the Guatemalan highlands. It was founded around 1400 on a flat plateau beside the older K'iche' center of Pismachi', ringed by ravines that made it hard to storm. Four temples stood around the main plaza, to the jaguar god Tohil, patron of the city, and to Awilix, Jakawitz and the feathered serpent Q'uq'umatz; the palaces of the Kaweq, Nijaib and other ruling houses crowded nearby, with the ballcourt between them. In 1444 K'iq'ab ruled there at the head of the K'iche'-Kaqchikel alliance. His wars had carried K'iche' arms to Rabinal, Cobán and Quetzaltenango, east to the Motagua River and south to the Pacific cacao lands around Escuintla, while subject towns sent tribute to the plateau.

The expansion ended with a palace coup in 1470: two of K'iq'ab's sons rose during a great assembly, killed Kaqchikel warriors and Kaweq nobles, and forced the old king to hand over power. The new lords turned on the Kaqchikel, who walked out and founded Iximché; after K'iq'ab died in 1475, a K'iche' attack on the new city ended in disaster, and another son, Tekum, was killed fighting the Tz'utujil by Lake Atitlán. In March 1524 Alvarado's cavalry broke a K'iche' army in the Quetzaltenango valley, and Tecún Umán fell in the campaign. Legend later said he fought in quetzal plumes with a quetzal as his spirit-guide, that he killed Alvarado's horse with his spear before he himself was cut down, and that the grieving bird flew to his body, after which male quetzals carried a scarlet breast and never sang again. The surviving lords invited the Spanish into Q'umarkaj; Alvarado camped outside the walls, afraid the narrow streets would trap his horsemen, seized the two kings when they visited his camp, burned them alive and set fire to the city. The Spanish built Santa Cruz del Quiché nearby and carried off the ruined stones for their churches. In the 1550s K'iche' nobles of Santa Cruz set down their people's creation stories and king-lists in a Latin-letter manuscript, the Popol Vuh.
zh:
库马尔卡赫在西班牙人的纳瓦语盟友口中称乌塔特兰，是基切玛雅人的都城，也是危地马拉高地最强的城市。它约1400年建在一座平坦高原上，紧邻更古老的基切中心皮斯马奇，四周深谷环绕，难以强攻。主广场周围立着四座神庙，分别供奉城市守护神、美洲豹神托希尔，以及阿维利什、贾卡维茨和羽蛇神库库马茨；卡韦克、尼哈伊布等统治氏族的宫殿环列近旁，球场夹在宫殿之间。1444年，基克阿布以基切-卡克奇克尔同盟首领的身份在此统治。他连年征战，把基切势力推向拉比纳尔、科万和克萨尔特南戈，东抵莫塔瓜河，南达埃斯昆特拉一带的太平洋可可产地，臣服的城镇向高原纳贡。

扩张终结于1470年的宫廷政变：基克阿布的两个儿子趁大集会举事，杀死卡克奇克尔战士和卡韦克贵族，逼迫老王交权。得势的首领转而对付卡克奇克尔人，后者出走另建伊希姆契；1475年基克阿布死后，基切军队攻打新城惨败，他的另一个儿子特库姆又在阿蒂特兰湖畔与楚图希尔人作战时被杀。1524年3月，阿尔瓦拉多的骑兵在克萨尔特南戈谷地击溃基切大军，特昆·乌曼也死于这一战役。相传他头插格查尔鸟羽出战，护身神灵是一只格查尔鸟；他先刺死阿尔瓦拉多的战马，自己随即被杀，悲痛的神鸟落在他身上，后来的雄性格查尔鸟都有绯红胸羽，也不再啼鸣。幸存的首领邀请西班牙人入库马尔卡赫，阿尔瓦拉多却担心狭窄街巷困住骑兵，只在城外扎营；两位国王到营中拜访时被他拿下，活活烧死，整座城市随之被焚。西班牙人在附近建起圣克鲁斯-德尔基切，拆走遗址的石材修筑教堂。1550年代，圣克鲁斯的基切贵族用拉丁字母把本族的创世神话和王世系写成一部手稿，即《波波尔·乌》。

en:
Between the Yucatan plain and the Petén lakes runs a broad corridor of karst hills and rainforest, held at Spanish contact by kindred Maya groups. The Kejache lived in its northern half; their name means 'land of deer' in Yucatec, from kej, deer, and Aztec merchants knew the country as Mazatlán. The Kob'ox, also written Couoh and kin to the Itzá, had moved south from Mayapan around 1300 and settled nearer the lakes. Kejache and Itzá were often at war, with a deserted no-man's-land between them. The Kejache answered with walls: their trading towns stood on defensible ground, one on a rocky outcrop above a lake behind a palisade and a moat, and Tiac, the largest, had walls, watchtowers, earthworks and three separately fortified wards. In 1444, as the League of Mayapan broke apart, these woods held fortified villages and refugee kin groups linking the Yucatec chiefdoms to the independent Itzá kingdom on Lake Petén Itzá.

Hernán Cortés crossed the corridor in 1525 on his march to Honduras and left the first European account of those forts; Alonso Dávila crossed its northern edge in 1531, and part of the northern Kejache country was granted in encomienda in 1543. By about 1600 the Kejache numbered perhaps 7,000 in ten to twenty towns, sheltering Yucatec refugees and moving goods between Spanish Yucatan and the still-independent Petén Maya. Franciscans pushed a road south from Campeche, opened missions at Ichbalche and Tzuktok, and in 1695 the army built a stockaded base at Chuntuki, about sixty-five miles north of the lake. In December 1696 Itzá raiders sacked the mission town of Pak'ek'em, burned its church and drove the Chuntuki garrison back toward Campeche. Martín de Ursúa y Arizmendi reopened the road regardless, had an oared galley carrying 114 men and artillery built on the lakeshore, and on 13 March 1697 rowed through an arc of Itzá war canoes to storm Nojpetén. The island capital was the last independent native kingdom in the Americas; many surviving Kejache, Itzá and Kob'ox withdrew deeper into the Lacandon forest.
zh:
尤卡坦平原与佩滕湖群之间横亘着一条石灰岩丘陵和雨林构成的宽阔走廊，西班牙人到来时，这里住着几支有亲缘关系的玛雅群体。北部是克哈切人：其族名在尤卡特克语里意为「鹿之乡」（kej即鹿），阿兹特克商人则把这片地方叫作马萨特兰。科博赫人（又写作Couoh）与伊察人同源，约1300年从马亚潘南迁，定居在更靠近湖群的地带。克哈切人与伊察人交战频繁，两地之间隔着一片荒无人烟的中间地带。克哈切人的对策是筑墙：贸易城镇都建在易守难攻之处，一座城镇在湖边的岩丘上以木栅和壕沟环绕，最大的蒂亚克则有城墙、望楼、土工工事和三个各自设防的城区。1444年，马亚潘联盟正走向瓦解，森林里散布着设防村社和避难亲族，把尤卡特克诸政权同佩滕伊察湖畔独立的伊察王国连接起来。

1525年，埃尔南·科尔特斯进军洪都拉斯时穿过这条走廊，留下了欧洲人对这些要塞的第一手记述；1531年阿隆索·达维拉穿过其北缘，1543年克哈切北部的一部分被封作监护地。到1600年前后，克哈切人约有七千，分布在十至二十座城镇里，他们收留尤卡坦难民，在西班牙治下的尤卡坦与仍独立的佩滕玛雅人之间转运货物。方济各会沿从坎佩切向南开辟的道路推进，在伊奇巴尔切和楚克托克开设传教站；1695年，军队在湖北约六十五英里处的琼图基建起栅栏营地。1696年12月，伊察人袭破传教城镇帕克埃肯、烧毁教堂，琼图基的驻军退回坎佩切方向。马丁·德·乌尔苏亚·阿里斯门迪仍重新打通这条路，让人在湖边造出一艘载有一百一十四人和火炮的桨帆快船；1697年3月13日，快船划开排成弧形的伊察独木舟战阵强攻诺赫佩滕。这座岛城是美洲最后一个独立的原住民王国；幸存的克哈切人、伊察人和科博赫人大多退入拉坎东森林深处。

en:
Moran is the wet Caribbean slope between Chetumal, the Petén lakes and the Polochic-Izabal lowlands, cut by the New, Belize, Sibun and Macal rivers. Canoe traffic along those waterways linked the coast with Lamanai, the 'submerged crocodile' town occupied for three thousand years, and with Tipu, chief town of the Postclassic province of Dzuluinicob, whose ways were closer to Petén than to northern Yucatán and which grew after Mayapan fell. Its Putún-connected Maya towns kept cacao orchards and river trade on the frontier between Chactemal and the Itza, and in 1444 no European had yet reached them.

Cortés crossed the Mopan and Manche lowlands in 1525. Then came the Pacheco entrada of 1543–1544, which dragged Dzuluinicob into the new Bacalar district; its mass killings were judged excessive even in its own time, and the Pachecos were later convicted of crimes against the Indians. Franciscans made Lamanai and Tipu mission towns, but by 1619 Tipu had returned to its old gods, and in 1638 it rose. Maya priests had foretold that the new k'atun would bring war, and within a few years Spanish power collapsed across the district: Bacalar itself was abandoned in 1652, and Tipu ruled a revived Dzuluinicob until 1695. Its men served the Spanish against the Itza in 1696 and saw Nojpetén fall in 1697; in 1707 the survivors were forcibly moved to Lake Petén Itzá. English Baymen had meanwhile made the Belize River a logwood and mahogany frontier, regularised by treaties in 1783 and 1786, and on 10 September 1798 their victory off St George's Caye ended Spain's last attempt to dislodge them.
zh:
莫兰是查克特马尔、佩滕湖区与波洛奇克—伊萨瓦尔低地之间一片潮湿的加勒比坡地，纽河、伯利兹河、西本河和马卡尔河穿流其间。独木舟沿这些水路往来，把海岸同拉马奈和蒂普连在一起：拉马奈意为「水中的鳄鱼」，已有人居住三千年；蒂普是后古典期政区祖卢伊尼科布的首要城镇，风俗更近佩滕而非北尤卡坦，在马亚潘瓦解后兴起。这里与普屯人有关的马雅村镇经营可可园和河上贸易，地处查克特马尔与伊察之间的边地，1444年时欧洲人尚未到来。

1525年，科尔特斯穿过莫潘与曼切低地。随后是1543—1544年帕切科家族的远征，祖卢伊尼科布被拖入新设的巴卡拉尔辖区；这场征服中的大规模杀戮在当时即被视为过分，帕切科家族后来被判犯有侵害印第安人罪。方济各会把拉马奈和蒂普变成传教城镇，但到1619年蒂普已重新信奉旧神，1638年正式起事。马雅祭司曾预言新的卡顿周期将带来战乱；数年间西班牙权力在整个辖区崩溃，巴卡拉尔本身也于1652年废弃，蒂普统治着复兴的祖卢伊尼科布直到1695年。1696年蒂普人为西班牙进攻伊察人效力，1697年目睹诺赫佩滕陷落，幸存者于1707年被强行迁往佩滕湖畔。与此同时，英国「湾民」把伯利兹河变成染木和桃花心木的采伐边疆，其地位经1783年和1786年的条约确认；1798年9月10日，他们在圣乔治岛外海取胜，终结了西班牙驱逐他们的最后尝试。

en:
Xiu was the inland province west of the Sotuta country, with Maní as its capital. The land has few surface rivers, and its towns depended on rainwater pools and cenotes. The Xiu lineage had held first rank in the League of Mayapan from Uxmal and Maní before the Cocomes, helped by Canul guards, tightened their hold on the city and drove many Xiu out around 1400. Ah Xupan Xiu opened war in 1441, and the twenty-year conflict destroyed Mayapan and the Cocom royal house. In 1444 Maní was therefore becoming the seat of the strongest western Yucatec polity, with Na, Ku, Dzul, Tun and other lineages settled across the province.

The Cocom feud shaped the province's part in the Spanish conquest. In 1535 a Xiu party given leave to sacrifice at the sacred cenote of Chichén Itzá was ambushed, and in 1541-42 the Xiu lord of Maní submitted to Montejo and became Catholic; neighboring western provinces followed. Maní then became the place most closely linked with Diego de Landa's campaign against native rites. After a hidden shrine was discovered, the Franciscan held an auto de fe on 12 July 1562 beside the monastery of San Miguel Arcángel, burning Maya codices and cult images and using torture to press conversion. The Crown recalled him to answer for the violence, cleared him, and sent him back as bishop of Yucatán in 1572. Maní remained a colonial head town around its Franciscan monastery.
zh:
休是索图塔以西的内陆辖区，以马尼为首府。这里地表河流稀少，城镇依赖雨水池和天然井。休家族曾凭借乌斯马尔和马尼在玛雅潘联盟中居首，后来科科姆人在卡努尔戍卫支持下控制玛雅潘，并在约1400年驱逐许多休人。1441年，阿·苏潘·休发动战争；这场持续二十年的冲突摧毁玛雅潘和科科姆王室。到1444年，马尼正成为西尤卡坦最强大政权的治所，纳、库、祖尔、通等家族分布在休人辖区内。

与科科姆人的旧怨决定了休人在西班牙征服中的选择。1535年，一队获得许可前往奇琴伊察圣井祭祀的休人遭到伏击；1541—1542年，马尼的休人首领向蒙特霍归附并改奉天主教，邻近的西部各辖区也随之接受西班牙统治。马尼后来与迭戈·德·兰达打击本土仪式的行动联系最深。一处秘密祭坛被发现后，这名方济各会士于1562年7月12日在圣米格尔修道院旁举行信仰判决，焚毁玛雅抄本和神像，并用酷刑逼迫改宗。西班牙王室将他召回调查，随后又为他洗清，1572年派他以尤卡坦主教身份返回。马尼则围绕方济各会修道院，继续作为殖民时期的首镇。

en:
Chikinchel, or Chauaca after its chief town, was the salt country of north-eastern Yucatán, a flat shore of lagoons, marshes and estuaries between Ah Kin Chel, Cupul, Tases and Ekab. When Mayapan fell between 1441 and 1461 the coast became one of the sixteen Maya kuchkabalob, and a loose one: Chauaca fought often with Sinsimato and Dzonotake. Salt held the rivals together. The estuaries later called Ría Lagartos and El Cuyo yielded game, fish and the peninsula's best salt, and the towns kept outsiders from Ah Kin Chel and the south away from the pans. The coast was too unhealthy for the lords, who lived in villages set back from the water; the Spanish later found the people here refined in their manners and speech. In 1444 the salt beds and hunting grounds were still in Maya hands.

The first Spaniards seen here were Francisco Hernández de Córdoba's men, who put into an estuary in 1517 to look for fresh water and named it for the many large alligators, los lagartos. The conquest government founded Valladolid at Chauac-Há, on the lagoon by Chauaca, on 28 May 1543, laid out the Spanish town and granted encomiendas to forty-five conquistadors. Mosquitoes, humidity and marsh fever drove the settlers out, and on 24 March 1545 the villa was moved inland to the Cupul town of Zaci, whose stones were taken for the new buildings. A Maya revolt swept the east the following year and was put down with reinforcements from Mérida. The old town never recovered: its people were gathered into Tizimín, and by about 1579 only twenty families remained where Chauaca had stood.
zh:
奇金切尔又称乔阿卡，后者是其首镇的名字。这是尤卡坦东北部的盐乡，阿金切尔、库普尔、塔塞斯和埃卡布之间一片遍布潟湖、沼泽和河口的平坦海岸。1441年至1461年马亚潘陷落后，这片海岸成为十六个玛雅库奇卡巴尔辖区之一，而且是其中松散的一个：乔阿卡常与辛西马托、佐诺塔凯交战。把这些对头拢在一起的是盐。后来称作里奥拉加托斯和埃尔库约的河口出产猎物、鱼和全半岛最好的盐，诸城合力把阿金切尔和南方来的外人挡在盐池之外。海岸瘴疠太重，首领们都住在远离潮水的村落里；西班牙人后来评价此地居民举止谈吐都很文雅。1444年，盐场和猎场仍在玛雅人手中。

最先到此的西班牙人是弗朗西斯科·埃尔南德斯·德·科尔多瓦的部下：1517年，他们驶进一处河口寻找淡水，因水中有许多大型短吻鳄，将其命名为里奥拉加托斯，意为「鳄鱼河口」。1543年5月28日，征服政权在乔阿卡旁潟湖边的乔阿克-阿建立巴利亚多利德，规划西班牙式城镇，向四十五名征服者分封监护征赋权。蚊虫、湿热和沼泽热病逼走了定居者：1545年3月24日，城镇迁往内陆的库普尔城镇萨西，拆用其石材建造新房。次年，一场玛雅起事席卷东部，梅里达派来援军才将其镇压。旧城再未恢复：居民被集中到蒂西明，到1579年前后，乔阿卡故地只剩二十户人家。

en:
In 1444 the rainy eastern slope of Nicaragua was the river country of the Ulwa, the southernmost of the Mayangna, or Sumu, peoples. Their villages followed the Río Grande de Matagalpa and the Río Escondido, along with the Tuma, Siquia and Mico tributaries that run from the central highlands into Caribbean lagoons. Ulwa families fished, hunted and cleared riverside fields, moving by dugout canoe; their lands were a web of river basins rather than a fixed border. Miskito communities lived to the north, Matagalpa-speaking highlanders to the west, and Kukra and Rama groups around the southern bays, and no European post had yet touched that world.

In the early seventeenth century Dutch and English privateers began anchoring in the Escondido mouth and at Bluefields, the lagoon named after the Dutch privateer Abraham Blauvelt. British traders gave the coastal Miskito firearms, and in 1660 the English recognised a chief they called Oldman as king of the Mosquito Coast. Armed Miskito raiders then pushed up the rivers after captives: Ulwa men were sold on to Jamaica for its plantations, the women kept, and the dugouts that carried the raiders were built from tropical hardwoods the Mayangna themselves felled and sold. The Ulwa withdrew to remoter headwaters. Spanish missionaries and officials only reached the western basins in the eighteenth century, where villages switched alliances as their interests shifted. Yarrince, an Ulwa leader from Olama, took Spanish rank as a captain-governor after dealing with the British, was imprisoned in 1780 and died in Guatemala the same year. The 1786 Convention of London pulled the British settlers out without making Spanish rule firm; Miskito forces drove the Spanish out in 1800, and in 1821 the river basins still answered to their own people.
zh:
1444年，尼加拉瓜湿润的东部坡地是乌尔瓦人的河网之乡。乌尔瓦人是马扬格纳人（又称苏穆人）最南的一支，村落沿马塔加尔帕大河与埃斯孔迪多河展开，也散布在图马河、西基亚河、米科河等从中部高地注入加勒比潟湖的支流沿岸。乌尔瓦家庭捕鱼、狩猎、开垦河畔田地，乘独木舟往来；他们的土地是一张河流水系织成的网，没有固定边界。北方是米斯基托社群，西方是说马塔加尔帕语的高地人，南部港湾一带住着库克拉人和拉马人，当时还没有欧洲人据点闯入这个世界。

17世纪初，荷兰和英格兰私掠者开始在埃斯孔迪多河口和布卢菲尔兹潟湖停泊，后者得名于荷兰私掠者亚伯拉罕·布劳维尔特。英国商人把火器交给沿海的米斯基托人，并于1660年承认他们所称的首领奥德曼为莫斯基托海岸之王。有了火枪的米斯基托袭掠队随即溯河捉拿俘虏：乌尔瓦男子被转卖到牙买加的种植园，女子则被留下；而载着袭掠者往来的独木舟，正是用马扬格纳人自己采伐出售的热带硬木造成的。乌尔瓦人一步步退向更偏远的河源。直到18世纪，西班牙传教士和官吏才进入西部各河流盆地，而各个村庄随利害改换同盟。奥拉马的乌尔瓦首领亚林塞先与英国人往来，后接受西班牙授予的军政长官职衔，1780年入狱，同年死于危地马拉。1786年《伦敦公约》撤走英国移民，却没有稳固西班牙的统治；1800年米斯基托军队把西班牙人赶走，到1821年，这些河流盆地仍听命于本地人。

en:
Xicaque is the Spanish name for the Tolupan country on the central Honduran coast. Its beaches, lagoons and river mouths run from the Ulúa toward Puerto Castilla, and the forested ridges of Yoro climb inland to the Sulaco headwaters. In 1444 Tolupan villages and mobile bands planted bitter manioc and maize, hunted, fished and carried maize and cochineal cactus by dugout canoe between Tela Bay, the rivers and the interior. Each settlement followed its own headman, there was no single capital, and no European ship had yet anchored off the shore. The bay's name, some writers suggest, is a Spanish shortening of the Nahuat tetla, a land of hills.

On 3 May 1524 Cristóbal de Olid landed beside the native town of Tehuacán in Tela Bay, whose headman the Spaniards called Cucumba, and set up one of the first Spanish settlements in Honduras. He came ashore on the feast of the Cross, and the promontory above the bay kept the name Triunfo de la Cruz; the little municipality lasted only months before it was dissolved and the district put under Trujillo. Spanish rule stayed thin. Independent Tolupan groups held the forest frontier the Spaniards called Taguzgalpa, and by the end of the sixteenth century buccaneers lay in Tela Bay to seize the schooners carrying precious metal out of Trujillo and Puerto Caballos. Franciscan reductions began upriver after 1600, and by 1609 some Tolupans had settled as far inland as the Guayape and Guayambre valleys. The last newcomers were the Garifuna: after Britain deported the Black Caribs defeated on St Vincent to Roatán in 1797, families spread along the coast and in 1808 founded the villages of Triunfo de la Cruz and San Juan by Tela. In 1821 the shore was still a frontier of Tolupan, Garifuna and a thin scatter of Spaniards.
zh:
希卡克是西班牙人对洪都拉斯中北部海岸托卢潘人土地的称呼。海滩、潟湖和河口从乌卢阿河一带延伸向卡斯蒂利亚港，内陆则是约罗的林脊和苏拉克河源头。1444年，托卢潘人的村社和流动群体种植苦木薯与玉米，兼营狩猎和渔捞，乘独木舟在特拉湾、河流与内陆之间运送玉米和胭脂虫仙人掌。各聚落只听本聚落首领的，没有统一都城，也还没有欧洲船只在近海停泊。有学者认为，特拉湾的名字是西班牙人把纳瓦语 tetla（山丘之地）缩写而来。

1524年5月3日，克里斯托瓦尔·德·奥利德在特拉湾的原住民城镇特瓦坎旁上岸，建立洪都拉斯最早的西班牙据点之一；西班牙人把当地首领称作库库姆巴。这一天是十字架节日，湾畔海岬便留下特里温福·德拉鲁斯之名。这个小市镇只存在了几个月就被撤销，地区划归特鲁希略管辖。西班牙人的统治一直薄弱，独立的托卢潘群体守着被称作塔古斯加尔帕的森林前沿；到16世纪末，巴克尼尔海盗已在特拉湾守候，截击从特鲁希略和卡瓦略斯港运出贵金属的纵帆船。1600年后，方济各会深入河上游建立集居传教区，到1609年，已有托卢潘人深入内陆，定居到瓜亚佩河与瓜亚姆布雷河谷。最后到来的是加里富纳人：1797年英国把在圣文森特岛战败的黑加勒比人流放罗阿坦岛后，他们的家庭沿海岸扩散，1808年在特拉旁建立特里温福·德拉鲁斯和圣胡安两个村落。1821年时，这片海岸仍是托卢潘人、加里富纳人和零星西班牙人共处的边疆。

en:
Tzul covers the rainforest and foothills between Lake Petén Itzá, the Lacandón forest and the Guatemalan highlands, the country Spanish records called Tute. Its rivers carried canoes between the Itza lake world and Cahabón and Cobán, where Lakandon traders exchanged cacao and achiote for quetzal feathers, copal, salt and Spanish iron tools; maize fields stood beside vanilla and cotton groves. The Tute and the Lakandon Ch'ol were warlike forest nations on the edge of Kan Ek's orbit, sometimes paying tribute, more often raiding the Cuchumatanes foothills until the Spanish put garrisons at San Mateo Ixtatán and Santa Eulalia. In 1444 their forest country lay between Nojpetén and the highlands, untouched.

Spanish expeditions penetrated this forest for a century and a half without holding it. Cortés crossed neighbouring Manche Ch'ol country in 1525, and Pedro Ramírez de Quiñones led the first expedition against the Lakandon in 1559. Around 1586 the Ch'ol abandoned their island capital of Lakam-Tun and built Sac Balam, the 'white jaguar', hidden in a bend of the Lacantún, where they stayed free for more than a century. Franciscans Antonio Margil and Melchor López were expelled in 1694, and the great Guatemalan campaign of 1695 opened the forest, baptised more than six hundred families around the new Dolores settlements and took Sac Balam. After Nojpetén fell on 13 March 1697, the Tute fled the troops and joined the postwar rising; Spanish prisoners named them among those who killed soldiers and looted missionary goods. In 1712 the surviving Lakandon Ch'ol were marched off to Huehuetenango and absorbed into the local Maya, and the Tute then disappear from colonial records as a separate people. The last three Lakandon Ch'ol on record were living at Retalhuleu in 1769.
zh:
楚尔（Tzul）是佩滕湖、拉坎东丛林与危地马拉高地之间的雨林和山麓地带，西班牙文献称之为图特。各条河川上的独木舟把伊察人的湖区世界同卡瓦翁、科万连接起来：拉坎东商人用可可和胭脂树交换格查尔鸟羽、柯巴脂、盐和西班牙铁工具；玉米地旁还种着香荚兰和棉花。图特人与拉坎东乔尔人是善战的森林族群，处在卡内克势力的外圈，有时纳贡，更多时候则南下劫掠库丘马塔内斯山麓，西班牙人最后不得不在圣马特奥伊斯塔坦和圣欧拉利娅驻军。1444年，他们的森林之地夹在诺赫佩滕与高地之间，外人尚未踏入。

一个半世纪里，西班牙远征队多次深入这片森林却无法立足。1525年，科尔特斯穿过相邻的曼切乔尔地区；1559年，佩德罗·拉米雷斯·德·基尼奥内斯率队首次征讨拉坎东人。1586年前后，乔尔人放弃岛上都城拉坎-通，在拉坎通河一处河曲深处建起隐秘新城萨克巴兰（意为「白虎」），在那里自由生活了一百多年。方济各会士安东尼奥·马希尔和梅尔乔·洛佩斯1694年被驱逐；1695年危地马拉大军打开森林，在新建的多洛雷斯聚居点为六百多个家庭施洗，并攻占萨克巴兰。1697年3月13日诺赫佩滕陷落后，图特人逃散并加入战后的起事，西班牙俘虏称他们参与杀害士兵、劫掠传教士器物。1712年，幸存的拉坎东乔尔人被强行迁往韦韦特南戈，逐渐融入当地马雅人，图特人也随之不再作为独立群体见于记载。有案可查的最后三个拉坎东乔尔人，1769年住在雷塔卢莱乌。

en:
Guaymi covers the island-dotted waters of Almirante Bay and Chiriquí Lagoon and the rain-soaked mountains behind them. In 1444 Atlantic Ngäbe villages occupied the shores and river valleys, led by chiefs and influential families rather than by one court. Their country reached across the isthmus between the Caribbean and Pacific, but it had no imperial capital. They called themselves Ngäbe, meaning 'people' in Ngäbere; Guaymí was a later outsider form taken from Buglere.

Christopher Columbus entered these waters in October 1502 while looking for a passage to the Pacific, and the leader Quibían helped drive his ships away. The longest resistance came from Urracá. He united nearby communities that had often fought one another and forced Captain Diego de Albites to make peace in 1522. The Spanish seized him at talks and sent him in chains toward Nombre de Dios, but he escaped and spent the next eleven years raiding from the hills; when he died in 1531 he had never submitted. Spanish posts on this coast fared poorly: Castillo de Austria on Almirante Bay and Artieda del Nuevo Reino de Navarra on the Cricamola were both soon abandoned. English pirates and Miskito raiders later used the lagoons, and an attack in 1758 destroyed the Tojar community, with Spanish records reporting about two thousand people killed or enslaved. In 1821 the isthmus joined Gran Colombia, while Ngäbe communities kept their autonomy in the mountains.
zh:
瓜伊米包括岛礁散布的阿尔米兰特湾、奇里基潟湖，以及后方潮湿多雨的雨林山地。1444年，靠大西洋的恩戈贝村落住在海岸和河谷中，由酋长和望族统领，没有统一的王廷。他们的活动范围横越加勒比海与太平洋之间的地峡，却没有帝国都城。他们自称恩戈贝，在恩戈贝雷语中意为「人」；瓜伊米是后来外来者根据布格雷语使用的称呼。

1502年10月，哥伦布为寻找通往太平洋的水道驶入这片海域，首领基维安带人把他的船队赶走。抵抗时间最久的是乌拉卡。他联合了彼此常有冲突的邻近社群，在1522年迫使迭戈·德·阿尔比特斯队长议和。西班牙人借谈判抓住他，把他锁缚着押往农布雷-德迪奥斯，但他成功逃脱，此后十一年从山地出击，1531年去世时仍未屈服。西班牙人在这海岸建立的据点也站不住脚：阿尔米兰特湾的奥地利堡和克里卡莫拉河畔的新纳瓦拉王国阿尔铁达都很快废弃。英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者后来利用潟湖出入；1758年的一次袭击摧毁托哈尔社群，西班牙记载称约两千人被杀或沦为奴隶。1821年地峡加入大哥伦比亚时，恩戈贝社群仍在山中保持自主。

en:
The province covers the eastern shore of the Gulf of Urabá and the lower, mangrove-lined Atrato, where rainforest and lagoon country mark the start of the Darién isthmus. In 1444 the people here were Guna, who call themselves Dule, or people. They lived in autonomous villages, raised maize and yuca, fished the lagoons and hunted in the forest behind the coast. Dugouts carried them between river mouths and sea villages. They answered to no single paramount chief, and no European settlement had yet been planted on the gulf.

Rodrigo de Bastidas explored the gulf in 1501. On 20 January 1510 Alonso de Ojeda brought about 300 men ashore near the later Necoclí and built the fort of San Sebastián de Urabá, the first Spanish settlement attempted on the American mainland. The Guna refused to supply it and met sorties with poisoned arrows; one arrow wounded Ojeda himself. He sailed for Hispaniola and left the young Francisco Pizarro in command, promising relief within fifty days. No help came in that time, and when Martín Fernández de Enciso's ship finally reached the fort, only 42 Spaniards remained. Vasco Núñez de Balboa was aboard that ship, and he persuaded the survivors to cross to the gulf's western shore and found Santa María del Darién. San Sebastián was abandoned and quickly disappeared. The gulf never gained a permanent Spanish town in these centuries; under pressure from colonists and warring neighbours, Guna communities gradually shifted west toward the San Blas coast.
zh:
库纳这片地方包括乌拉瓦湾东岸和红树林夹岸的阿特拉托河下游，雨林与潟湖地带从这里进入达连地峡。1444年，这里的居民是库纳人，他们自称杜雷，意思是「人」。他们住在自治村落里，种植玉米和木薯，在潟湖捕鱼，到海岸后方的雨林狩猎，乘独木舟往来河口与海边村落。他们没有统一的至高首领，乌拉瓦湾边也还没有欧洲人的定居点。

1501年，罗德里戈·德·巴斯蒂达斯勘察海湾。1510年1月20日，阿隆索·德·奥赫达率约三百人在后来的内科克利附近上岸，修筑圣塞瓦斯蒂安·德·乌拉瓦堡，这是西班牙人在美洲大陆尝试建立的第一个定居点。库纳人拒绝供粮，并以毒箭迎击出击者，奥赫达本人也中箭受伤。他乘船前往伊斯帕尼奥拉，把年轻的弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗留下指挥，答应五十天内带援军回来。期限过去后援军未至，等马丁·费尔南德斯·德·恩西索的船终于抵达，堡中只剩四十二名西班牙人。巴尔沃亚也在恩西索船上，他劝说幸存者渡海到海湾西岸，另建圣玛利亚·拉安提瓜·德尔达连。圣塞瓦斯蒂安随即被弃，很快从地图上消失。此后几个世纪里，海湾始终没有形成稳固的西班牙城镇；在殖民者和敌对邻族的压力下，库纳社群陆续向西迁往圣布拉斯海岸。

en:
Talamanca is the wet Caribbean slope below the Talamanca mountains, running from Tariaca toward the Changuinola and Sixaola rivers. In 1444 Bribri and Cabécar communities shared the forests with Térraba, Viceita, Terbi and neighbouring peoples. Autonomous villages and chiefdoms, rather than one empire, governed the country; the Cabécar polity was the strongest on Costa Rica's Atlantic side. Steep ridges, heavy rainfall and many separate nations meant that Spanish expeditions later had to subdue one community after another.

Christopher Columbus reached Cariay on 25 September 1502 and anchored off Quiribrí, now Isla Uvita, during his fourth voyage, but the mountains long prevented occupation. Cartago sent expeditions into Talamanca after 1660. Some communities accepted Spanish authority as protection against English pirates and Miskito raiders, then rebelled when officials attacked polygamy and shamanic practice. Raids in 1665 and 1666 burned villages and crops and seized more than a hundred people for colonial plantations. Franciscans built missions after 1670. On 29 September 1709 Pablo Presbere, a chief from Suinse, led peoples from Chirripó to Almirante Bay in revolt; fourteen mission churches burned and several friars and soldiers were killed. Presbere was captured and put to death in 1710, but Spanish forces withdrew and Talamanca remained an indigenous refuge. New missions and military attempts after 1740 produced little. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, Bribri and Cabécar leaders still held most of the mountains.
zh:
塔拉曼卡位于塔拉曼卡山脉下方潮湿的加勒比坡地，从塔里亚卡延伸到昌吉诺拉河与锡克绍拉河一带。1444年，布里布里人、卡韦卡尔人与特拉瓦人、维塞塔人、特尔维人及邻近族群共居山林。这里没有统一帝国，而是由自治村落和酋长领分治；卡韦卡尔人的政体是哥斯达黎加大西洋岸最强大的势力。陡峭山脊、充沛雨量和众多彼此独立的族群，使后来的西班牙远征队必须逐一压服各个社区。

1502年9月25日，哥伦布第四次航行时抵达卡里亚伊，停泊在基里布里岛（今乌维塔岛）外，但这片山地长期阻碍西班牙人占领。1660年后，卡塔戈不断向塔拉曼卡派出远征队。一些社区为抵御英国海盗和米斯基托袭掠者而接受西班牙权威，后来又因官方禁止多偶制和萨满习俗而起兵。1665年和1666年的捕奴袭击烧毁村落与庄稼，把一百多人掳往殖民地种植园。1670年后，方济各会修建传教站。1709年9月29日，苏因塞首领巴勃罗·普雷斯贝雷率领从奇里波到阿尔米兰特湾的诸族群起义，焚毁十四座传教教堂，杀死多名修士和士兵。1710年，普雷斯贝雷被俘处死，但西班牙军队撤出，塔拉曼卡仍是原住民的避难地。1740年后新的传教和军事行动成效很小。1821年西班牙统治终结时，布里布里和卡韦卡尔首领仍控制着大部分山地。

en:
Cuauhtochco was a small fortified lordship in the broken hills above the Gulf plain, where tracks from Veracruz climbed toward Puebla and the Valley of Mexico. The Nahuatl name refers to a tree squirrel or 'place of the rabbit tree'. Its land had belonged to Totonacapan before a Teochichimeca group with Tlaxcalan ties founded the ruling line in 1327. Its chief places were Cuauhtochco, the later Santiago Huatusco near Carrillo Puerto, Otlaquiquixtla and Tototlán. In 1444 the lordship had fewer than five thousand people, but its towns controlled traffic moving inland from the Gulf.

Moctezuma Ilhuicamina conquered it in 1457 and turned Cuauhtochco into a Nahuatl-speaking Mexica garrison. Gonzalo de Sandoval stormed that post in November 1521, after Tenochtitlan had fallen. Severe depopulation left its old pyramid almost untouched as colonial administration shifted toward San Antonio Otlaquiquixtla, called San Antonio Huatusco after 1670. In the Atoyac lowlands, Indian and African labour worked estates and sugar trapiches. During the independence war, enslaved workers and sugar labourers around Atoyac rose after Miguel Hidalgo's call. Mariano Mota made Cerro del Chiquihuite an insurgent base in 1812, and in 1813 the Congress of Chilpancingo named Huatusco the insurgent capital of Veracruz.
zh:
夸赫托奇科是墨西哥湾平原上方崎岖山地中的小要塞领主国，韦拉克鲁斯方向来的道路从这里爬向普埃布拉和墨西哥谷。纳瓦特尔语地名与树栖松鼠有关，也可解释为「兔树之地」。这里原属托托纳克潘，1327年，一支与特拉斯卡拉有联系的特奥奇奇梅卡人群建立了统治家族。主要据点包括夸赫托奇科、后来卡里略港附近的圣地亚哥·瓦图斯科、奥特拉基基斯特兰和托托特兰。1444年，这个领主国人口不足五千，却控制着从海湾进入内陆的往来道路。

1457年，蒙特苏马·伊尔维卡米纳征服此地，把夸赫托奇科变成说纳瓦特尔语的墨西加驻军要塞。1521年11月，特诺奇蒂特兰陷落后，贡萨洛·德·桑多瓦尔攻占这座据点。人口急剧减少，旧金字塔几乎无人惊扰；殖民行政中心则转向圣安东尼奥·奥特拉基基斯特兰，1670年后称圣安东尼奥·瓦图斯科。阿托亚克低地的庄园和蔗糖作坊役使原住民与非洲劳力。独立战争期间，阿托亚克一带被奴役的工人和蔗糖劳工响应米格尔·伊达尔戈号召起事。1812年，马里亚诺·莫塔把奇基维特山建成起义基地；1813年，奇尔潘辛戈议会将瓦图斯科命名为韦拉克鲁斯的起义首都。

en:
The Sinú river runs from forested highlands to the Caribbean beside the wetlands of the San Jorge, and in 1444 its valley was Zenú country. For centuries Zenú farmers had grown maize and cotton on raised fields laced with drainage canals, and their craftsmen made pottery and hammered the gold dust the river washed down from the hills. Spanish chroniclers later described three chief towns: Finzenú, where the great female chief of the Zenú lands held court, Yapel the potters' town and Mexión the weavers' town. Around the Gulf of Morrosquillo people fished and traded salt, and the gold buried in their ancestors' burial mounds was still undisturbed.

That gold undid them. Between 1510 and 1535 disease and warfare broke the chiefdoms, and after Cartagena was founded in 1533 Pedro de Heredia's men marched up the Sinú and dug the gold from the royal tombs. Survivors were gathered into encomienda pueblos such as San Andrés de Mexión, whose people rowed timber, maize and manatee oil downriver to Cartagena. In 1773 the Crown set aside 83,000 hectares at San Andrés de Sotavento as a Zenú reserve, which kept their communities intact through the rest of the colonial period. Antonio de la Torre y Miranda founded Montería on the Sinú in 1777, and it became the market town for the cattle ranches spreading along the river. After Bolívar's victory at Boyacá in 1819 the Sinú lands entered Gran Colombia with the reserve still standing.
zh:
锡努河（省名「西努」即由此而来）从林木茂密的高地流入加勒比海，与圣豪尔赫河的湿地相连；1444年，它的河谷是塞努人的家园。数百年来，塞努农人在排灌渠网纵横的台地上种植玉米和棉花，工匠制陶，并把河水从山中带下的金砂锻打成金器。后来的西班牙编年史家记下了塞努人的三座重镇：女大酋长坐镇的芬塞努、制陶之城亚佩尔和纺织之城梅希翁。莫罗斯基约湾一带的居民捕鱼、贩盐，祖先墓丘中的黄金此时还无人惊扰。

正是这些黄金给他们招来大祸。1510至1535年间，疾病和战争瓦解了诸酋邦；卡塔赫纳1533年建立后，佩德罗·德·埃雷迪亚的部下沿锡努河而上，掘开王陵取金。幸存者被并入监护征赋制下的圣安德烈斯-德梅希翁等村镇，村民把木材、玉米和海牛脂撑船运往卡塔赫纳。1773年，王室在圣安德烈斯-德索塔文托划出8.3万公顷土地作为塞努人保留地，使他们的社群在整个殖民年代得以存续。1777年，安东尼奥·德拉托雷·米兰达在锡努河畔建立蒙特里亚，后来成为沿河牧牛场的集镇。玻利瓦尔1819年赢得博亚卡战役后，锡努河流域并入大哥伦比亚，保留地也依然存续。

en:
The Cauca and San Jorge reach the Magdalena through a low, flooded country of ciénagas, caños and natural levees around the future site of Magangué. Water routes linked Maguey, Yati, Tacaloa and Guazo, the river communities of these wetlands. The Maguey were a Chimila people whose language was related to Carib; they planted maize and cassava on raised banks, took fish from the lagoons and hunted in woodland flooded during the rains. Their villages had long mixed with Zenú people from the lower Cauca and with the Malibú, another river people of the lower Magdalena. In 1444 canoes carried travellers and goods through the waters, and no European had yet entered the main river.

Diego de Carvajal founded a Spanish town at Magangué in 1610, but it long remained a quiet riverside settlement. Antonio de la Torre y Miranda changed its scale on 28 October 1776, when he refounded it as Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Magangué and established Cascajal, Tacaloa, Madrid, El Retiro and Tacasaluma in the adjoining caños. The wars of independence reached these waterways in 1815, when royalists seized the town. Five years later José María Córdova captured Magangué and placed his general staff there, using its canoes and landing places to operate on the lower Magdalena.
zh:
考卡河和圣豪尔赫河在一片低洼多水的地方汇入马格达莱纳河，潟湖、河汊和天然堤岸环绕着后来的马甘格。水路连接马圭、亚蒂、塔卡洛阿和瓜索等河畔群落。马圭人是奇米拉人的一支，语言与加勒比语相近，在高岸上种植玉米和木薯，在潟湖中捕鱼，雨季进入淹水的林中狩猎。他们的村落很早就与下考卡的塞努人、下马格达莱纳的河畔居民马利布人通婚杂处。1444年，独木舟载着旅客和货物穿行水面，欧洲人还没有进入这条大河。

1610年，迭戈·德·卡瓦哈尔建立西班牙人的马甘格，但它长期只是安静的河畔聚落。1776年10月28日，安东尼奥·德·拉托雷·米兰达把它重建为坎德拉里亚圣母马甘格，又在相邻河汊一带设立卡斯卡哈尔、塔卡洛阿、马德里、埃尔雷蒂罗和塔卡萨卢马等新村。独立战争在1815年打进这片水道，保王派占领马甘格。五年后，何塞·马里亚·科尔多瓦攻占此地，把总司令部设在这里，凭借独木舟和停泊点在下马格达莱纳机动作战。

en:
Between the snow-capped Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the forested Serranía del Perijá lies the hot, landlocked valley of the Cesar river, watered by the Ariguaní and the Guatapurí, 'cold water' in the Chimila tongue. In 1444 it belonged to the Chimila, who call themselves Ette Ennaka and speak a Chibcha language. Their lands ran west to the Ciénaga de Zapatosa and the Magdalena, and the Yukpa of the Perijá hills belonged to their confederation. Their two districts, Upar and Pocabuy, obeyed a supreme sacred chief, and the people of Upar farmed the riverbanks, kept bees, made pottery and played flutes at their festivals.

Raiders from Santa Marta forced their way into the valley in the 1530s, and on 6 January 1550, the feast of the Three Kings, Hernando de Santana and Juan de Castellanos founded the Ciudad de los Santos Reyes del Valle de Upar on the Guatapurí, naming the valley after the local chief Upar. Castellanos later became a parish priest in Tunja and wrote the Elegías de varones ilustres de Indias, a verse chronicle of the conquest. Encomiendas parcelled out the Chimila, and many fled death and enslavement into the mountains as the valley turned into cattle ranges. Through the eighteenth century haciendas kept pressing on their villages, and during the wars of independence the Chimila abandoned the reduction towns and slipped back into the forests of the Ariguaní; on 4 February 1813 Valledupar rose against the Spanish Crown.
zh:
圣玛尔塔内华达山脉与林木茂密的佩里哈山脉之间，是炎热闭塞的塞萨尔河谷，阿利瓜尼河与瓜塔普里河穿流其间，「瓜塔普里」在奇米拉语中意为「冷水」。1444年，这里属于奇米拉人。他们自称埃特恩纳卡，说奇布查语，土地向西直到萨帕托萨沼泽和马格达莱纳河，佩里哈山中的尤克帕人也属于他们的部落联盟。全境分乌帕尔和波卡布伊两区，尊一位具有神圣地位的大酋长；乌帕尔人在河畔耕作、养蜂、制陶，在节庆上吹奏长笛。

1530年代，从圣玛尔塔出发的征服者闯入谷地。1550年1月6日三王节，埃尔南多·德·桑塔纳与胡安·德·卡斯特利亚诺斯在瓜塔普里河畔建立「乌帕尔谷地圣王城」，地名取自当地酋长乌帕尔。卡斯特利亚诺斯后来在通哈任神父，写下记述征服经过的长诗《印第安名人哀歌》。监护征赋制把奇米拉人层层瓜分，许多人为躲避死亡和奴役逃入深山，谷地变成牧牛场。整个18世纪，大庄园不断侵占他们的村落；独立战争期间，奇米拉人离开归化集镇，退回阿利瓜尼河丛林。1813年2月4日，巴耶杜帕尔起兵反抗西班牙王权。

en:
The Catatumbo drains the wet forests between the eastern Cordillera and the Maracaibo lowlands, country held in 1444 by the Barí, whom Spanish-speakers later called the Motilones. Their autonomous villages centred on large roundhouses in forest clearings, with maize and manioc fields cut from the bush and hunting and fishing on the rivers; the people spoke a Chibchan language, and no European road or mission had yet reached the basin. In the Barí tongue the river's name is read as 'house of thunder': over the marshes where the Catatumbo enters Lake Maracaibo, storm clouds gather on most nights and lightning flashes for hours, the densest concentration of lightning anywhere on earth.

The first intruders came from the Welsers' concession, after Charles V granted the province of Venezuela to the Augsburg banking house. In 1530 its governor Ambrosius Ehinger led a gold-seeking column through the Bobalí highlands, and Barí warriors ambushed it and scattered its treasure; Ehinger himself was killed on another expedition three years later. The forest then kept out Spanish raids and Capuchin missionaries for two centuries, and only after 1730 did the friars learn Barí and draw some families into mission villages. In 1772 the government at Maracaibo made peace with twenty-one communities, offering metal tools and cacao planting, and trading families settled round the missions.
