The peace broke in the wars of independence, when the Capuchins stood by the Spanish king: after patriot troops defeated them in 1813, most Barí left the villages and went back into the forest, so that in 1821 the new republic controlled little beyond the old mission sites.
zh:
卡塔通博河汇集东安第斯山脉与马拉开波低地之间湿林的来水，1444年这片流域属于巴雷人，说西班牙语的人后来叫他们莫蒂洛内斯（莫蒂隆人）。他们的自治村落以林间空地上的大圆屋为中心，在灌木中辟出玉米和木薯地，在河中捕鱼、在林中狩猎；巴雷人操奇布查语系语言，此时还没有欧洲人的道路或传教站进入流域。巴雷语中这条河的名字通常解释为「雷霆之家」：卡塔通博河注入马拉开波湖的沼泽上空，大多数夜晚都堆起雷雨云，闪电持续数小时，是全球闪电最密集的地方。

最早的闯入者来自韦尔塞家族的特许领地：卡洛斯五世把委内瑞拉省特许给奥格斯堡的韦尔塞银行家族。1530年，其总督安布罗修斯·埃因格率寻金队伍取道博巴利高地，巴雷战士设伏袭击，使其财宝散落丛林；埃因格本人三年后死于另一次远征。此后两百年间，这片丛林挡住了西班牙讨伐队和嘉布遣会传教士，直到1730年以后修士学会巴雷语，才把一些家庭迁入传教村。1772年，马拉开波政府同21个社群议和，以金属工具和可可种植招揽，从事贸易的家庭在传教点周围定居。独立战争打破了和平：嘉布遣会站在西班牙国王一边，1813年爱国军击败他们后，大多数巴雷人弃村退回丛林，到1821年新共和国实际控制的不过是几处旧传教点。

en: Moniquirá, recorded in the sixteenth century as Ubaza, sits on the wooded north-western slope of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense, where the Moniquirá, Pómeca and Suárez rivers cut through the Eastern Cordillera; its Chibcha name is read as 'place of the bath'. In 1444 it was a Muisca community under the cacique Susa. Its farmers worked maize fields in the temperate and cold ground, and the village traded salt and cloth with the highland towns. Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada passed through Ubaza on 16 March 1537. In 1755 the visitador Andrés Verdugo y Oquendo sold the indigenous town and attached its people to Chitaraque, and a parish was founded there in 1788.
zh: 莫尼基拉在16世纪文献中称乌瓦萨，坐落在昆迪博亚卡高原西北缘的林坡上，莫尼基拉河、波梅卡河和苏亚雷斯河在这里切开东部山脉；在奇布查语里，其地名一说意为「沐浴之地」。1444年，这里是臣服于酋长苏萨的穆伊斯卡社群，农民在温带和寒带土地上种植玉米，村子与高原各镇交换盐和织物。1537年3月16日，贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达途经乌瓦萨。1755年，巡视官安德烈斯·贝尔杜戈·伊·奥肯多出售这座印第安村镇，居民被并入奇塔拉克；1788年，这里设立堂区。

en:
The province rises from the mangrove channels of the Pacific coast, where the Telembí and Patía drain rain-soaked forests, to the cold Atriz Valley beneath the Galeras volcano. Coastal groups later called Barbacoas lived along those rivers with the Awá and related peoples, while the Quillacingas farmed the highland basin that took the broader name Pastos. They grew maize and potatoes and washed gold from mountain streams. In 1444 Inca armies had not yet reached the valley; their conquest of these southern mountains came only shortly before the Spanish arrival.

Sebastián de Belalcázar made the first Spanish foundation near Yacuanquer in 1537, and Lorenzo de Aldana moved the town to the Atriz Valley in 1539 as San Juan de Pasto. The crown granted it arms in 1559, and the town became the administrative and religious centre of the southern highlands. Down on the coastal rivers, Francisco de la Parada founded a settlement in 1600 and Pedro Martín Navarro formalised it in 1612 as Santa María del Puerto de los Barbacoas. Its goldfields were worked by enslaved Africans for families based in Popayán, and Barbacoas grew into the region's richest mining town and river port.

Few New Granadan towns supported the Spanish crown as firmly as Pasto. Troops from the short-lived Quito junta entered the town in September 1811, but royalist forces recovered it in 1812 and 1813 and defeated Antonio Nariño's patriot army outside Pasto in 1814. After Boyacá in 1819 the wars moved south again, and Pasto resisted under Agustín Agualongo, a mestizo royalist commander born in the town. At the end of 1821 it had still not submitted, the last major royalist centre in southern New Granada.
zh:
帕斯托斯从太平洋沿岸的红树林水道向上抬升，特莱姆比河和帕蒂亚河排走雨林中的积水，高地尽头是加莱拉斯火山脚下寒冷的阿特里斯河谷。沿海河流住着后来被称为巴尔巴夸斯人的族群，以及阿瓦人和亲缘相近的各部；高地上的阿特里斯盆地则是基利亚辛加人的农田，整个地区后来以帕斯托斯人得名。他们种植玉米和马铃薯，从山溪中淘金。1444年，印加军队尚未进入这个河谷；他们征服南部群山，只比西班牙人到来早了不久。

1537年，塞瓦斯蒂安·德·贝拉尔卡萨尔首先在亚昆克尔附近建立西班牙城镇；1539年，洛伦索·德·阿尔达纳把城镇迁入阿特里斯河谷，定名圣胡安·德·帕斯托。王室1559年颁赐城徽，这里成为南部高原的行政和宗教中心。沿海河流地带，弗朗西斯科·德·拉·帕拉达1600年建立定居点，佩德罗·马丁·纳瓦罗1612年正式定名为圣玛利亚·德尔普埃尔托·德·洛斯·巴尔巴夸斯。黑奴为定居波帕扬的家族开采当地金矿，巴尔巴夸斯因此成为全区最富庶的矿业城镇和河港。

新格拉纳达各城中，少有像帕斯托这样坚定支持西班牙王室。1811年9月，短命的基多洪达派军队入城，但保王军在1812年至1813年夺回此地，又于1814年在城外击败安东尼奥·纳里尼奥的爱国军。1819年博亚卡战役后，战事再度南移；出生于帕斯托的梅斯蒂索保王将领阿古斯丁·阿瓜隆戈继续率部抵抗。到1821年底，这座城仍未屈服，是新格拉纳达南部最后一个主要保王据点。

en:
The Putumayo rises in the Nudo de los Pastos and cuts through forested Andean gorges on its way to the Amazon; long stretches of it are navigable, and canoes carried trade between the riverside communities. In 1444 its upper basin belonged to no empire. Cofán peoples held the southwest, Kamëntšá the northwest, Siona and other Tucano-speaking villages the central and southern waters, and Witoto-speaking peoples the eastern forest. The Inca armies had not yet crossed the foothills.

Within a lifetime they did. In 1492 the Sapa Inca Huayna Cápac marched through Cofán land, subdued part of the Kamëntšá country and planted a Quechua-speaking colony in the Sibundoy valley, the forebears of the Inga people and their Quechua tongue. After the Inca collapse of 1533 Spanish expeditions entered the Putumayo from 1542, and Catholic missions of one order after another ran much of the frontier from 1547, answering for government to distant Popayán. Distance, forest and the great river left the Cofán, Kamëntšá, Siona and Witoto room to keep their own chiefs and customs, and in 1821 the old mission country was still attached to Popayán rather than ruled as a province of its own.
zh:
普图马约河发源于帕斯托斯山结，穿过林木覆盖的安第斯峡谷流向亚马逊河；干流多段可通航，独木舟载着河畔诸族往来贸易。1444年，上游流域不属于任何帝国：西南部是科方人，西北部是卡门查人，中部和南部水道住着西奥纳人和其他图卡诺语族群，东部雨林则是维托托语族群的土地。印加军队此时还没有越过山麓。

没过一代人，印加人便到了。1492年，萨帕·印卡瓦伊纳·卡帕克率军穿过科方土地，征服部分卡门查地区，并在锡本多伊谷地安置一支说克丘亚语的移民，他们是因加人的先祖，因加人说的克丘亚语就是那时带来的。1533年印加崩溃后，西班牙远征队从1542年起进入普图马约，1547年起由历代修会的天主教传教团管理这条边疆的大部分事务，政务上听命于遥远的波帕扬。距离、雨林和大河给科方、卡门查、西奥纳和维托托人留下余地，让他们保留自己的首领和习俗；到1821年，这片旧日传教地仍依附波帕扬，没有成为单独治理的行省。

en:
The Chichitames were a desert band of the Bolsón de Mapimí, the closed basin between the sierras of Nueva Vizcaya where the Nazas River runs out into the sands. With several kindred nomad peoples they were grouped by the Spanish as Tobosos, hereditary enemies of the Irritila who fished the lakes to their south. They had no fields or towns: they hunted with sling and lance, gathered mesquite and mescal, moved their rancherías from waterhole to waterhole, and raided the settled valleys to the south and west. In 1444 no road entered the bolsón and no lord claimed it; the silver under Mapimí still lay untouched.

Antonio de Espejo's expedition crossed the basin in 1583 and the Tobosos simply vanished into the desert. Silver is what brought the Spanish back in force: on 25 July 1598 Antón Martín de Zapata and the Jesuit Juan Agustín de Espinoza founded Santiago de Mapimí at the foot of the Sierra de la India, and its mines grew into one of the richest silver districts of New Spain. Slave-raiding against the desert bands drove them to war, and within a generation they were fighting on horseback. Risings swept Mapimí in 1616-17 and flared again and again into the 1710s, and the Spanish answered with a presidio and campaigns of extermination. Of the twelve bands counted in the 1680s, a Spanish tally in 1693 found only four: the Osatayogliglas, Guazapayogliglas, Sisimbles and Chichitames. By 1800 the survivors had merged into the mestizo frontier population. In 1811 the priest Miguel Hidalgo, who a year earlier had raised the cry of revolt at Dolores, passed through Mapimí as a prisoner on his way to Chihuahua, where he was shot on 30 July.
zh:
奇奇塔梅斯人是马皮米盆地的一个沙漠游群。这个封闭盆地位于新比斯开的群山之间，纳萨斯河流入其中、消失在沙地里。他们与几个亲缘游牧族群同被西班牙人归为托博索人，世代与在南方湖畔渔猎的伊里蒂拉人为敌。他们没有田地和城镇：以投石器和长矛狩猎，采集豆灌木和龙舌兰，在水源地之间迁徙营地，向南、向西劫掠定居的山谷。1444年时没有一条道路通向盆地，也没有君主领有此地，马皮米地下的银矿还无人触碰。

1583年安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍的探险队穿过盆地，托博索人直接遁入沙漠。真正把西班牙人大批引来的是银子：1598年7月25日，安顿·马丁·德·萨帕塔与耶稣会士胡安·阿古斯丁·德·埃斯皮诺萨在印度山脚下建立圣地亚哥·德·马皮米，这里的矿区后来成为新西班牙最富庶的银矿区之一。西班牙人猎捕荒漠族群为奴，把他们逼上战场，只用一代人的时间，这些游群便骑上了马。起义在1616至1617年席卷马皮米，此后到1710年代又反复爆发，西班牙人则以要塞和剿灭战役回应。1680年代清点出的十二个游群，到1693年西班牙人重新统计时只剩四个：奥萨塔约格利格拉斯、瓜萨帕约格利格拉斯、西辛布雷斯和奇奇塔梅斯。到1800年，幸存者已融入边境的混血居民之中。1811年，一年前在多洛雷斯发出起义呼声的神父米格尔·伊达尔戈作为囚犯经过马皮米，被押往奇瓦瓦，于7月30日被处决。

en:
Pijaos is the mountain-and-river country between the snow peaks of the Cordillera Central and the hot upper Magdalena valley. In 1444 it belonged to a series of Pijao chiefdoms: Coyaima, Natagaima, Guauro and Tamagale on the plains, and smaller federated communities in the mountains above the Saldaña, Amoya and Coello. No single ruler commanded all of them. Families grew the tobacco they called tenú, prepared it as medicine or rolled it into cigars, and Pijao traders carried it far beyond the Magdalena. Their raiders also made the warm valleys feared by neighbouring peoples, and no Spanish fort yet stood beside the rivers.

Spanish invaders spent about eighty years trying to force the country. Diego Bocanegra built Fuerte de Palenque and Santiago de la Frontera in Amoya territory in 1572 and won Chief Tala's alliance, but Pijao fighters drove the settlers out. The commander Chequera answered later outposts with raids, and Medina de las Torres, founded near Chaparral in 1586, was destroyed in its turn. Juan de Borja y Armendia, president of the Audiencia of Santafé, finally broke the federations by exploiting divisions among their peoples. After heavy fighting near Chaparral, the Spanish founded Natagaima about 1608 and Nuestra Señora del Carmen de Coyaima in the same year. Survivors were concentrated in resguardos. Coyaima, its formal foundation recorded in 1621, became a market where produce from the cold highlands met goods from the warm valley, and the village was moved to the Saldaña bank in 1778. Repeated floods forced Natagaima to its final site in 1801.
zh:
皮豪斯（皮哈奥人之地）位于中部山脉雪峰与上马格达莱纳炎热河谷之间。1444年，这里属于一系列皮哈奥酋邦：科亚伊马、纳塔盖马、瓜罗和塔马加莱在平原上，更小的联盟群落则住在萨尔达尼亚河、阿莫亚河和科埃约河上方的山里。他们没有共同的统治者。各家种植称作「特努」的烟草，把它制成药剂或卷成雪茄，皮哈奥商人还将烟草带到马格达莱纳河以外很远的地方。他们的袭击队伍也让邻近族群忌惮这些温暖河谷；这时河畔还没有西班牙堡垒。

西班牙入侵者花了约八十年才压服这片土地。1572年，迭戈·博卡内格拉在阿莫亚地区修建帕伦克堡和圣地亚哥-德拉弗龙特拉堡，并争取到酋长塔拉结盟，皮哈奥战士后来仍把定居者赶走。统帅切克拉以后来的据点为目标不断发动袭击，1586年在查帕拉尔附近建立的梅迪纳-德拉斯托雷斯也被摧毁。圣菲王家检审庭主席胡安·德·博尔哈·阿门迪亚利用各部矛盾，才拆散这些联盟。经过查帕拉尔附近的苦战后，西班牙人约在1608年建立纳塔盖马，同年又建立卡门圣母科亚伊马。幸存者被集中到保留地。科亚伊马在1621年补办正式建城手续，成为寒冷高原与炎热河谷物产交换的市集，1778年迁至萨尔达尼亚河畔。屡次洪水则迫使纳塔盖马在1801年迁到最后一处城址。

en:
Achaguas lies in the wet llanos of Apure, where rivers spread across open savanna during the rains and shrink into channels in the dry season. In 1444 the land around the future town belonged to the Achagua, the most numerous people of the Orinoco plains. Their villages in the Casanare, Meta and Apure basins kept up trade by river and overland, using strings of quiripa shells as money. The same country later produced the llanero horsemen of Venezuela's independence wars.

The town began as a Capuchin mission. On 4 December 1774 Fray Alonso de Castro founded Santa Bárbara de la Isla de los Achaguas and brought together Achagua, Taparita and Otomaco families with three Spanish households. On 2 April 1819 the plains nearby became the battlefield of Las Queseras del Medio, when José Antonio Páez's llanero cavalry met a larger royalist mounted force. Páez drew the royalists forward with a feigned retreat, turned his lancers back for a sudden charge, and the order 'Vuelvan, caras!' became attached to the action.
zh:
阿查瓜斯位于阿普雷州湿润的亚诺斯草原；雨季河水漫上开阔草原，旱季又缩回河道。1444年，未来城镇周围是阿查瓜人的土地。他们是奥里诺科草原人数最多的族群，在卡萨纳雷河、梅塔河与阿普雷河流域的村落依靠河道和陆路贸易，以成串基里帕贝壳作货币。同一片草原后来也走出委内瑞拉独立战争中的亚诺斯骑手。

城镇始于嘉布遣会传教站。1774年12月4日，修士阿隆索·德·卡斯特罗建立圣巴巴拉·德·拉·伊斯拉·德·洛斯·阿查瓜斯，把阿查瓜、塔帕里塔、奥托马科家族和三户西班牙人家聚到一起。1819年4月2日，附近草原成为拉斯克塞拉斯德尔梅迪奥战场，何塞·安东尼奥·派斯的亚诺斯骑兵对上兵力更多的保王派骑兵。派斯佯退诱敌，再令长矛骑兵回身急冲，「转身！」这道命令也随此战传开。

en:
The valley of the Turbio was called Variquicimeto, the 'ash-coloured river', by its villagers. In 1444 its maize lands and hunting grounds belonged to the Caquetío and their neighbours the Gayón, Ayamán and Jirajara, Arawakan-speaking peoples who carried cotton, salt and dye along the tracks from the Caribbean coast to the inland plains. No stranger yet ruled the valley.

Gold in the Buría river brought the captain Juan de Villegas up from El Tocuyo, and in 1552 he founded Nueva Segovia de Buría beside the new mines. The enslaved Africans working the mines rose that same year under Miguel, a slave from San Juan de Puerto Rico: other slaves and the local Indians joined him, they set up a forest kingdom with Miguel as king and his wife Guiomar as queen, named a former slave their bishop and raided the mines. Within a few years Diego de Losada's troops had killed Miguel and broken the kingdom, the first African revolt on Venezuelan soil. The Spanish town fared no better: unhealthy ground and indigenous attacks drove the settlers to El Carabalí in 1556, where it became Nueva Segovia de Barquisimeto.

Lope de Aguirre, the rebel conquistador who styled himself the Wrath of God, reached Venezuela after his mutiny on the Amazon and had Nueva Segovia burned as he passed in 1561; at Barquisimeto his own soldiers turned on him and killed him on 27 October. Rebuilt at the meeting of the Turbio and the Claro, then moved again to escape harsh winds, the town settled in 1563 on the plateau north of the Turbio, its native name worn down by Spanish tongues to Barquisimeto. It lived from farm trade and the roads joining western to central Venezuela. In 1811 its deputy José Ángel Álamo signed the Independence Act, and in 1813 patriot and royalist armies fought the battle of Los Horcones nearby.
zh:
图尔维奥河谷的土著地名叫巴里基西梅托，意为「灰色的河」。1444年，谷地的玉米地和猎场属于卡克蒂奥人及其邻族加永人、阿亚曼人和希拉哈拉人；他们都说阿拉瓦克语，沿加勒比海岸通往内陆平原的商路贩运棉花、盐和染料。此时还没有外来者统治这片谷地。

布里亚河的黄金把西班牙队长胡安·德·维列加斯从埃尔托库约引来，1552年他在新办的金矿旁建起「布里亚的新塞戈维亚」。同年，在矿上劳作的黑奴在来自波多黎各圣胡安的奴隶米格尔带领下起事，其他奴隶和附近的印第安人陆续投到他麾下。他们在林中建立自己的王国，立米格尔为王、妻子吉奥马尔为后，又从奴隶中指名一人当主教，并不断下山袭扰金矿。几年后，后来建立加拉加斯的迭戈·德·洛萨达率部杀死米格尔、剿灭了这个王国；这是委内瑞拉土地上第一次非洲人起义。西班牙人的城镇也没站住脚：水土恶劣加上土著袭击，殖民者1556年迁往埃尔卡拉瓦利，改名「巴里基西梅托的新塞戈维亚」。

自称「上帝之怒」的叛征服者洛普·德·阿基尔在亚马孙河上哗变后转战到委内瑞拉，1561年路经此地时让部下烧毁了新塞戈维亚；同年10月27日，他在巴基西梅托被自己的士兵所杀。城镇先在图尔维奥河与克拉罗河汇流处重建，又为躲避烈风再次迁址，1563年终于在图尔维奥河北岸的台地定居下来，土著地名在西班牙人口中讹变成巴基西梅托。此后它靠农产品贸易和连接委内瑞拉东西部的道路立足。1811年，本地代表何塞·安赫尔·阿拉莫签署独立法案；1813年，爱国军与保王军在城外接战，是为洛斯奥尔科内斯之战。

en:
The forested ridges of the Serranía del Perijá rise west of Lake Maracaibo, their eastern streams feeding the Catatumbo. In 1444 the high valleys belonged to the Yukpa, a Carib-speaking people who lived in autonomous clan villages above the hot plains, planted maize and manioc on burned mountain slopes and hunted in the cloud forest. Spaniards later called them Motilones, 'the shaved heads', a loose name they shared with the Barí beyond the ridges. No road or tribute reached these valleys.

The Yukpa kept their mountains for nearly three centuries. Expeditions out of Maracaibo and the new Venezuelan towns climbed into the sierra after gold and captives and won no lasting foothold; the first Spanish town below it, Concepción, founded at the Palmar's mouth in 1717, was burned by its indigenous neighbours three years later. Juan de Chourio, a Navarrese holding a royal licence of 1722, came back to Maracaibo with about 150 men and families from the Canary Islands, hacked a road through to the Palmar and from 1724 built La Villa de Perijá behind a palisade. In 1729 he moved the town upriver to the healthier site it kept. Concepción was burned again in 1752 and rebuilt for the last time. Capuchin missionaries and cattle ranches then worked their way up the valleys, but the high sierra was still Yukpa country in 1821.
zh:
佩里哈山在马拉开波湖以西隆起，东坡的溪水汇入卡塔通博河。1444年，高山中的谷地属于尤克帕人：他们说加勒比语，在炎热平原之上按氏族聚村而居，在烧出的山坡上种玉米和木薯，在云雾林中狩猎。后来的西班牙人叫他们莫蒂隆人，意为「剃光头的人」；山那边的巴里人也被笼统地冠以这个名字。那时没有道路或赋税伸进这些山谷。

尤克帕人据守大山近三百年。从马拉开波和委内瑞拉各新城出发的远征队为黄金和掳口多次进山，都没能久留。山脚下第一座西班牙城镇康塞普西翁1717年建于帕尔马河口，三年后就被邻近的土著烧毁。纳瓦拉人胡安·德·乔里奥持1722年的王室特许，带着约一百五十人和加那利群岛的移民家庭回到马拉开波，挥刀开路推进到帕尔马河，1724年起在木栅后面建起佩里哈镇。1729年，他把镇子迁到上游更宜居住的地点，此后再未搬迁。康塞普西翁1752年再度被焚，同年最后一次重建。这以后嘉布遣会传教士和牧牛场才沿山谷慢慢推进，但直到1821年，高山之上仍是尤克帕人的地盘。

en:
Wayuu covers the southeastern shore of Lake Maracaibo and the hot plains below the Venezuelan Andes. In 1444 Arawakan- and Cariban-speaking villagers lived along the southern shore, fishing the lake, hunting the gallery forest and planting maize and manioc; the rivers running down from Mérida carried their traffic into the water. No European settlement stood anywhere on the lake.

In February 1592 Gonzalo Piña Ludueña founded San Antonio de Gibraltar on this shore, naming it after his hometown across the Atlantic. Gibraltar became the lake port of Mérida: cacao, worked by enslaved African labour on estates the Jesuits helped develop, was gathered in its warehouses and freighted across the lake for Spain. Its wealth drew the buccaneers. François l'Olonnais sacked the town on his sweep through the lake, and in March 1669 Henry Morgan, coming back from plundering Maracaibo, found three Spanish warships waiting at the lake mouth: he burned the San Luis with a fireship, destroyed the Magdalena and captured the Soledad before sailing out with his loot. Michel de Grammont came with six ships in 1678, sacked Gibraltar and pushed on overland as far as Trujillo. By 1680 the repeated raids had left the port nearly abandoned.
zh:
瓦尤据有马拉开波湖东南岸，以及委内瑞拉安第斯山下的炎热平原。1444年，湖南岸一带住着说阿拉瓦克语和加勒比语的村落，人们下湖捕鱼、在河岸林中狩猎，种植玉米和木薯；从梅里达方向流来的河川把他们的水路带进大湖。此时湖岸上还没有任何欧洲人的定居点。

1592年2月，贡萨洛·皮尼亚·卢杜埃尼亚在这段湖岸建立圣安东尼奥·德·直布罗陀，以他大西洋彼岸的故乡命名。直布罗陀成了梅里达的湖港：可可由黑奴在庄园中劳作产出、耶稣会士帮助推广种植，在港中的仓库里集中，再穿过大湖运往西班牙。财富引来了加勒比海的海盗。法国海盗弗朗索瓦·罗罗内在席卷湖区时洗劫了此城；1669年3月，亨利·摩根在劫完马拉开波后返航，发现三艘西班牙战舰守在湖口，便用火船烧毁「圣路易斯号」、击毁「马格达莱纳号」、俘获「索莱达号」，带着战利品驶出大湖。1678年，米歇尔·德·格拉蒙率六艘船前来，洗劫直布罗陀后又沿陆路一直打到特鲁希略。到1680年，连番袭击已使这座港口近乎荒废。

en:
The broad basin of Lake Tacarigua, later called Lake Valencia, fills a valley between the coastal cordillera and the hot lowlands that slope down toward the Llanos. In 1444 the Tacarigua and other Arawak peoples farmed its shores, growing maize and cotton, fishing the reed-fringed water and raising their houses on artificial mounds against the floods. Spaniards first settled the cove of Borburata on the nearby coast, but corsairs sacked it so often that the survivors moved inland, and on 25 March 1555 Captain Alonso Díaz Moreno founded Nueva Valencia del Rey by the lake, the first Spanish town in north-central Venezuela. The encomienda put the lake villages to work for the settlers, and the district sent wheat, cattle and cotton down to the coast.

In its first centuries Valencia was repeatedly caught in other men's wars. In 1561 Lope de Aguirre, the Basque conquistador who called himself the Wrath of God, passed through after the mutiny on the Amazon that killed his commander Pedro de Ursúa; he had written to Philip II renouncing his vassalage and seized the island of Margarita, and royalist forces ran him down and killed him at Barquisimeto later that year. French raiders burned the town hall and the province's early records in 1677. When Alexander von Humboldt visited in 1800 he counted six or seven thousand inhabitants and noted that clearing the shores was shrinking the lake, which has no outlet to the sea. The revolutionary congress met at Valencia in 1812, and in 1814 José Tomás Boves's royalists took the town after a long siege and sacked it. On 24 June 1821 Bolívar defeated the Spanish marshal Miguel de la Torre on the Carabobo plain west of the lake, and Venezuela's independence was settled.
zh:
塔卡里瓜湖（后称巴伦西亚湖）的宽阔湖盆，夹在海岸山脉和向亚诺斯草原倾斜的炎热低地之间。1444年，塔卡里瓜人和其他阿拉瓦克部族在湖畔耕作，种植玉米和棉花，在芦苇丛生的湖面捕鱼，把房屋建在人工土台上躲避泛滥。西班牙人最初在附近海岸的博尔布拉塔海湾落脚，那里屡遭海盗洗劫，幸存者只得内迁。1555年3月25日，阿隆索·迪亚斯·莫雷诺上尉在湖畔建起新巴伦西亚德尔雷伊，这是委内瑞拉中北部的第一座西班牙城镇。委托监护制把湖畔村落交给移民役使，这一带出产的小麦、牲畜和棉花沿陆路运往海岸。

建城后的头几个世纪，巴伦西亚几度被卷入别人的战争。1561年，自称「上帝之怒」的巴斯克征服者洛佩·德·阿吉雷途经此地：此前亚马逊河上发生哗变，队长佩德罗·德·乌尔苏阿被杀，他又写信给腓力二世宣布不再效忠，并占领了马加里塔岛；同年晚些时候，他在巴基西梅托被保王军追杀毙命。1677年，法国海盗烧毁市政厅和全省的早期档案。1800年亚历山大·冯·洪堡到访时，城里有六七千居民；他注意到湖畔伐林开垦后，这座没有出海口的湖正在缩小。1812年革命议会在巴伦西亚召开；1814年，何塞·托马斯·博韦斯的保王军经长期围困攻陷并洗劫了城市。1821年6月24日，玻利瓦尔在湖西的卡拉博博平原击败西班牙元帅米格尔·德·拉·托雷，委内瑞拉的独立就此定局。

en:
The Guanaguanare country lies where the south-western Llanos meet the Andean piedmont, between the Portuguesa and Guanare rivers. In 1444 Cuiba, Caquetío and Guamo groups farmed, fished and gathered across the savanna and left mounds and causeways that probably served as flood refuges, drainage works or burial places; the wooded country north of the future town belonged to the Cospes. The indigenous name was glossed as 'place of seagulls' or 'land between the rivers', and no Spanish town yet stood in the valley.

The first Europeans were Welser men hunting El Dorado: Nikolaus Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed the plain for the Augsburg company in 1534, and Philipp von Hutten was wounded there by Omagua warriors in 1542. The town itself was founded on 3 November 1591 by the Portuguese captain Juan Fernández de León as Espíritu Santo del Valle de Guanaguanare, later shortened to Guanare, and cattle ranches and maize farms spread around it. The valley's best-known story began in 1651, when the Cospes chief Coromoto said a beautiful lady appeared to him by a stream and bade him seek baptism; she appeared again the next year and, as the tale was told, left a tiny parchment bearing her image, which was carried to the parish church and brought Capuchin missionaries to the Cospes. On 5 December 1813, during the Second Republic, Bolívar defeated José Ceballos's larger royalist army at Araure nearby and captured the standard of the Numancia battalion, reputed invincible. The next day he gave that flag to a battalion that had fought without a name and dubbed it Vencedor de Araure, the Victor of Araure.
zh:
瓜纳瓜纳雷位于西南草原与安第斯山麓交会处，地处波图格萨河与瓜纳雷河之间。1444年，奎瓦人、卡克蒂奥人和瓜莫人在稀树草原上农耕、捕鱼、采集，他们留下的土墩与堤道可能用于洪水期避难、排水或安葬；后来城镇北面的林地属于科斯佩人。这个印第安语地名被解释为「海鸥之地」或「两河之间的土地」，当时山谷中还没有西班牙城镇。

最早到来的欧洲人是寻找黄金国的韦尔塞公司人马：1534年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔代表这家奥格斯堡公司穿过平原；1542年，菲利普·冯·胡滕在此被奥马瓜战士打伤。城镇本身迟至1591年11月3日才由葡萄牙籍上尉胡安·费尔南德斯·德·莱昂建立，取名埃斯皮里图·桑托·德尔巴列·德·瓜纳瓜纳雷，后来简称瓜纳雷，牧牛场和玉米地随即在城周铺开。谷地最有名的故事始于1651年：科斯佩酋长科罗莫托说，一位美丽的妇人在溪边显现，要他去求洗礼；据说她次年再次显现，留下一小幅绘有圣像的羊皮纸，圣像被送往教区教堂，嘉布遣会士也因此来向科斯佩人传教。1813年12月5日第二共和国期间，玻利瓦尔在附近的阿劳雷击败何塞·塞瓦略斯兵力更强的保王军，夺获号称无敌的努曼西亚营军旗；次日他把这面旗授予一个没有番号、却奋勇作战的营，将其命名为「阿劳雷胜利者营」。

en:
Tuneo covers the eastern approaches to the Sierra Nevada del Cocuy, where the Cobaría and Arauca rivers drop from cloud-forest ridges toward the Llanos. In 1444 the Tunebo, who call themselves U'wa, 'the people', held these slopes and spoke a Chibchan language; neighbouring peoples knew them as the people who speak well. They farmed highland clearings, hunted and fished in the valleys, and kept kin ties across the massif, while the gold-working Muisca around Tunja stayed beyond the steep passes.

The first Europeans to climb these approaches were German adventurers hired by the Welser banking house of Augsburg, to which the emperor Charles V had leased Venezuela. Nikolaus Federmann and Georg von Speyer crossed into Arauca in 1536, and Hernán Pérez de Quesada's gold expedition later pushed up toward Güicán. Tunebo families withdrew behind the snowy crest rather than submit.

Missionaries followed the soldiers. Jesuits reached the Tunebo and their neighbours in 1659, and Miguel Blasco founded the reduction of Güicán on the west flank of the massif in 1756; it held 310 people eight years later. When Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767 the Arauca missions passed to Augustinian Recollects, who founded San Fernando de Arauca. The Comunero revolt of 1781 found supporters in Tame, and on 24 February 1814 Güicán declared independence from Spain, one of the first free towns in the New Granada. In June 1819 Bolívar passed through Arauca and Tame, joined Santander's forces there, crossed the Andes by the Vargas swamp and won at Boyacá.
zh:
图内奥位于科库伊雪山东麓，科瓦里亚河与阿劳卡河从云雾林山脊下注东部草原。1444年，自称乌瓦人（意为「人」）的图内博人居住在这些坡地上，操奇布查语；邻近族群称他们为善于言辞的人。他们在高地开荒耕种，在河谷渔猎，亲属网络跨过山地往来，而通哈一带制作金器的穆伊斯卡人始终被险峻山口隔在另一侧。

最早登上这一带的欧洲人，是受雇于奥格斯堡韦尔泽银行家族的德意志冒险家。皇帝查理五世把委内瑞拉租给了这家银行商。1536年，尼古劳斯·费德曼和格奥尔格·冯·施派尔进入阿劳卡，埃尔南·佩雷斯·德·克萨达的寻金队伍随后逼近圭坎，图内博人举族退到雪线另一侧，不肯臣服。

传教士继士兵之后到来。耶稣会士1659年起进入图内博人和邻族的土地，米格尔·布拉斯科1756年在山地西侧建立圭坎归化村，八年后村中有310人。1767年查理三世驱逐耶稣会，阿劳卡的传教站改由重整奥斯定会接管，他们后来建立阿劳卡的圣费尔南多。1781年公社者起义，塔梅起而响应；1814年2月24日，圭坎宣布脱离西班牙独立，是新格拉纳达最早的自由市镇之一。1819年6月，玻利瓦尔途经阿劳卡和塔梅，与桑坦德尔的部队会师，经巴尔加斯沼泽翻越安第斯，在博亚卡取胜。

en:
Guanipa takes in the western edge of the mesa named after it, a belt of open tableland, gallery woods and swampy streams south of the Unare plains. The Guanipa River rises at about 260 metres on the plateau and runs roughly 340 kilometres through dense wetlands to the Gulf of Paria, just north of the Orinoco Delta. In 1444 this was Kali'na, or mainland Carib, country; families moved between the rivers and coast to fish, plant, trade and visit kin, and later local tradition named the district for Guanipa, a Kali'na cacique said to have led his people on the mesas above the Orinoco.

Christopher Columbus's third voyage entered the adjacent Gulf of Paria in 1498, after his ships found Orinoco fresh water far out at sea, but Spanish control of the mesas came slowly. In 1717 Cristóbal de Molina, commissioner of the Píritu missions, reported foreign smugglers on the Tigre River trading weapons to Carib and other indigenous groups and proposed two Spanish towns there. The plan shows Guanipa as a loosely guarded mission and smuggling frontier, without the fortified towns built in older Venezuelan provinces.
zh:
瓜尼帕包括同名台原西缘，是乌纳雷平原以南一片由开阔台地、林带和多沼泽溪流组成的土地。瓜尼帕河发源于台原上海拔约260米处，流经约340公里的茂密湿地，在奥里诺科河三角洲以北注入帕里亚湾。1444年，这里是卡利纳人（大陆加勒比人）的活动范围；族人往来于河流与海岸之间捕鱼、耕作、贸易和探访亲属，后来的地方传统以酋长瓜尼帕命名此地，据说他曾统领奥里诺科河上游台原上的卡利纳人。

1498年，克里斯托弗·哥伦布第三次航行进入邻近的帕里亚湾，此前船队已在远海发现奥里诺科河冲下的淡水，但西班牙人很久以后才试图控制台原。1717年，皮里图传教区专员克里斯托瓦尔·德·莫利纳报告，蒂格雷河上有外国走私者向加勒比人和其他原住民贩运武器，他因此提议在当地修建两座西班牙城镇。这份计划显示，瓜尼帕当时是防守松散的传教和走私边界，没有委内瑞拉较早省份那种设防城镇。

en:
The hot coastal plain between the Unare River and the Guanipa plateau, with the low country stretching behind it toward the Orinoco, belonged in 1444 to Cariban peoples: the Cumanagoto held the Neverí valley and the shore, while the Píritu, Chacopata and Palenque fished and farmed maize and cotton among the Unare lagoons. The first Europeans they saw were provisioning parties from the pearl island of Cubagua, who began landing below the Maracapana hill in 1499 to stock their boats.

The Cumanagoto kept the Spanish out of their valley for decades after that. A first Spanish town, San Cristóbal de la Nueva Écija, went up in 1586, after Captain Cristóbal Cobos defeated the cacique Cayaurima, but the fighting ran on until Joan Orpí, sent to finish the conquest, founded Nueva Barcelona del Cerro Santo in 1638; in 1671 Governor Sancho Fernández de Angulo moved the settlement two kilometres south and it became Barcelona. Cattle ranches, cotton and sugar spread through its district, and Franciscan missions at Clarines and Píritu gathered indigenous people around the Church. On 27 April 1810 Barcelona's junta declared against French rule in Spain.

The province bears the name of a son of the town: José Antonio Anzoátegui, born in Barcelona in 1789, fought through the republic's campaigns and commanded a division at Boyacá, then died at Pamplona in 1819, aged thirty. Before that, the independence cause nearly ended on these plains. On 17 August 1814 eight thousand royalists routed Bolívar's three thousand republicans at Aragua de Barcelona, and on 7 April 1817 they stormed the town itself. Bolívar had fortified the old Franciscan convent of the Casa Fuerte as a refuge for the garrison and townspeople and left it to the Irishman Charles Chamberlain and the local officer Pedro María Freites; when the royalists under Aldama and Morales broke in, Chamberlain killed himself, and the wounded Freites was carried to Caracas and shot in the main square on the orders of Captain General Moxó.
zh:
乌纳雷河与瓜尼帕台地之间是炎热的沿海平原，背后是伸向奥里诺科河的低地。1444年住在这里的是加勒比语族各部：库马纳戈托人据有内韦里河谷和海岸，皮里图人、查科帕塔人和帕伦克人在乌纳雷河的潟湖之间捕鱼，种植玉米和棉花。他们最先见到的欧洲人，是采珠岛库瓦瓜派出的补给队；这些人从1499年起在马拉卡帕纳山下登岸，为船只采办给养。

此后几十年，库马纳戈托人一直把西班牙人挡在河谷外。1586年，克里斯托瓦尔·科沃斯上尉击败酋长卡尧里马之后，第一座西班牙城镇圣克里斯托瓦尔-德拉新埃西哈建了起来，但战事一直持续，直到受命收尾这场征服的霍安·奥尔皮于1638年建立圣山新巴塞罗那；1671年，省长桑乔·费尔南德斯·德·安古洛把居民点南移两公里，改名巴塞罗那。牧牛场、棉花和甘蔗铺满辖区，克拉里内斯和皮里图的方济各会传教站把原住民聚到教会周围。1810年4月27日，巴塞罗那的执政委员会宣布起兵，反对法国控制下的西班牙。

这个省的名字，出自城里出生的一个人：何塞·安东尼奥·安索阿特吉1789年生于巴塞罗那，参加过共和国历次战役，在博亚卡战役中指挥一个师，1819年在潘普洛纳去世，年仅三十岁。在此之前，独立事业险些在这片平原上断送。1814年8月17日，八千保王军在阿拉瓜-德巴塞罗那击溃玻利瓦尔的三千人；1817年4月7日，保王军又攻破巴塞罗那城。玻利瓦尔已把旧方济各会修道院卡萨富埃特加固成守军和市民的避难所，托付给爱尔兰人查尔斯·张伯伦和本地军官佩德罗·玛丽亚·弗雷特斯；阿尔达马和莫拉莱斯率部破门而入，张伯伦自尽，负伤的弗雷特斯被押往加拉加斯，经都督莫克索下令枪决在主广场上。

en:
Guaju is the deep forest between the upper Orinoco and the Rio Branco, a country of blackwater creeks and flat-topped heights such as the Duida. Its singular feature is the Casiquiare: below the Duida a natural arm leaves the upper Orinoco and winds more than 300 kilometres south to the Río Negro, carrying Orinoco water into the Amazon. No other natural channel on earth links two river systems of this size. In 1444 Arawak speakers, the Baré and Baniva among them, farmed and fished along the Casiquiare and the Guainía, while Ye'kuana villages held the Ventuari and its rapids; their canoes already used the channel and the short Pimichín portage to pass between the two river worlds.

Europeans learned of the waterway from the Jesuit Manuel Román, who in 1744 met Portuguese slavers at La Esmeralda and went with them through from the Río Negro to the Orinoco, the first recorded crossing. La Condamine carried the report to the Académie française, and the Royal Orinoco Expedition confirmed it in 1755, after which Spain tried to make the country its own. A patrol found cacao groves on the Ocamo and Padamo, a fort named Buena Guardia went up at the channel's mouth in 1759, and from 1760 officers and friars gathered Ye'kuana families into a town formally founded in 1767 as San Francisco de la Esmeralda, named for an emerald said to have been found beneath Cerro Duida. From there a party pushed up the Orinoco to its source, still looking for Lake Parime and the golden city of Manoa. A native rising put an end to the road planned from La Esmeralda down to Angostura. In 1800 Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland navigated the full length of the Casiquiare and fixed its course, but Spanish rule never ran past a handful of forest posts, and in 1821 the interior was still the rivers and villages of its native peoples.
zh:
瓜胡在上奥里诺科河与里奥布朗库河之间的密林深处，到处是黑水溪涧和杜伊达这样的平顶山。这里最不寻常的是卡西基亚雷河：在杜伊达峰下方，一条天然汊流从上奥里诺科河分出，蜿蜒三百多公里向南注入内格罗河，把奥里诺科河的水送入亚马孙河；以如此规模连通两大水系的天然河道，世上再无第二处。1444年，说阿拉瓦克语的巴雷人、巴尼瓦人在卡西基亚雷河和瓜伊尼亚河沿岸耕渔，叶库纳人的村落据守着本图阿里河及其急流；他们的独木舟已经借这条水道和短短的皮米钦陆运道，往来于两个大河世界之间。

外界得知这条水道，靠的是耶稣会士曼努埃尔·罗曼。1744年，他在拉埃斯梅拉达遇到从内格罗河上来的葡萄牙奴隶贩子，随他们穿水道从内格罗河进入奥里诺科河，这是有记载的第一次欧洲人通行。拉孔达明把此事报告给法兰西科学院，1755年皇家奥里诺科远征队证实了水道的存在，西班牙随后试图把这片土地据为己有。一支巡逻队在奥卡莫河和帕达莫河一带发现可可林，1759年水道河口修起布埃纳瓜迪亚要塞；1760年起，军官和修士把叶库纳人家族聚入一座新城，1767年正式定名圣弗朗西斯科·德拉埃斯梅拉达，名字来自据说在杜伊达山下找到的一颗祖母绿。又有一队人从这里溯奥里诺科河直抵源头，仍在寻找帕里梅湖和金城马诺阿。一场原住民起事终结了从拉埃斯梅拉达通往安戈斯图拉的筑路计划。1800年，洪堡与邦普朗走完全部卡西基亚雷水道，勘定了河道走向，但西班牙人的统治始终只及密林里的寥寥据点；1821年，内陆仍是原住民的河流与村落。

en:
The bay and river mouths that later became Jacmel were Yaquimo, a Taíno coastal district on the eastern side of Hispaniola's Tiburon Peninsula. Fishing villages, cassava fields and canoe landings lay between the Caribbean shore and the steep hills behind it. Spanish accounts placed the district inside Jaragua, the chiefdom of Bohechío, and remembered Zui and Yáquimo as its two constituent parts. In 1444 local caciques still governed the bay, untouched by European conquest.

Spanish settlers founded a town there in 1504, but after the Devastations of Osorio in 1605 the Crown uprooted the western settlements and the coast was emptied. The Compagnie de Saint-Domingue built a French town at the river mouth in 1698, and the authorities in France designated it a colonial town in 1720; sugar paid at first, and coffee introduced in 1770 drew merchants to the port. In 1791 and 1792 Romaine-la-Prophétesse led around 13,000 rebels out of the hills; they occupied and burned Jacmel, raided plantations from Marigot to Bainet and freed the enslaved. During the War of the South, Alexandre Pétion held the port until Toussaint Louverture's troops took it in February 1800. On 12 March 1806, lying in Jacmel bay aboard the corvette Leander, Francisco de Miranda raised the first flag of Venezuela, the yellow, blue and red 'mother flag' later copied by Colombia and Ecuador.
zh:
后来成为雅克梅勒的海湾和河口，原是泰诺人的沿海地区亚基莫，位于伊斯帕尼奥拉岛蒂伯朗半岛东侧。加勒比海岸与后方陡山之间，分布着渔村、木薯地和独木舟泊岸。后来的西班牙记载把这里归入博埃奇奥的哈拉瓜酋长国，并称祖伊和亚基莫是哈拉瓜的两个组成部分。1444年，地方酋长仍统治着海湾，欧洲人的征服尚未到来。

1504年，西班牙殖民者在此建城；1605年奥索里奥荒毁之后，王室强拆西部居民点，这片海岸为之一空。1698年，圣多明各公司在河口建起法国城镇，1720年被定为殖民城镇；起初靠蔗糖，1770年引入咖啡后，商人随之而来。1791年至1792年，罗曼·拉·普罗费特斯率约一万三千名起义者出山，占领并焚毁雅克梅勒，袭击从马里戈特到拜内一带的种植园，解放奴隶。南方战争期间，亚历山大·佩蒂翁据守港口，直到1800年2月被杜桑·卢维杜尔的军队攻占。1806年3月12日，弗朗西斯科·德·米兰达在雅克梅勒湾内的「莱安德号」护卫舰上升起委内瑞拉第一面旗帜；这面黄蓝红三色的「母旗」，后来为哥伦比亚和厄瓜多尔所仿效。

en:
Marien was the north-westernmost of the five Taíno chiefdoms of Hispaniola, facing the Atlantic and the Windward Passage, with Tortuga riding offshore and borders with Maguá, Maguana and Jaragua. Its chief town, El Guarico, stood near the later Cap-Français, and fourteen nitaíno districts answered to the cacique, whose people farmed the northern plains and fished the river mouths. In 1444 Taíno caciques still held these shores, plains and valleys; Guacanagaríx, the ruler Columbus met here in 1492, already occupied the northern chiefly seat.

At Christmas 1492 the Santa María grounded on a reef off this coast. Guacanagaríx lent men to unload her and allowed Columbus to build a fort, La Navidad, from her timbers; when he returned eleven months later the stockade was burned and the garrison dead, destroyed by a rival chiefdom. Spain founded Puerto Real nearby in 1503, moved the townspeople to Bayajá in 1578 and evacuated the north in the Osorio devastations after 1605, leaving the coast open to buccaneers. French settlers under Bertrand d'Ogeron founded Cap-Français in 1670; chartered in 1711, it was the capital of Saint-Domingue until 1770 and the colony's richest port, nicknamed the Paris of the Antilles for its merchants, theatres and sugar shipments. By 1790 it held 15,000 people, two-thirds of them enslaved.

On 14 August 1791 two hundred enslaved delegates gathered in the woods of Bois Caïman outside the city, where the enslaved leader Dutty Boukman led the ceremony that bound them to revolt; the plantations of the northern plain were burning within a week, and after Boukman was killed the French displayed his head in the city square. On 18 November 1803 Jean-Jacques Dessalines defeated Rochambeau at Vertières below Cap-Français, and Haiti proclaimed independence on 1 January 1804. Henri Christophe made the north a separate state in 1807 and a kingdom in 1811, renaming the city Cap-Henri. At Milot he built the Sans-Souci palace and raised the Citadelle Laferrière on a 900-metre summit nearby: tens of thousands of labourers worked on it between 1805 and 1820, and its walls mounted 365 cannon against a French return that never came. In 1820 Christophe suffered a stroke, his troops mutinied, and according to legend he shot himself with a silver bullet; his death ended the northern kingdom.
zh:
马里安（Marién，也译马列恩）是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛五大泰诺酋长国中最靠西北的一个，北临大西洋，与托尔图加岛隔海相望，东接马瓜和马瓜纳，南连哈拉瓜。首府埃尔瓜里科位于后来的法兰西角附近，酋长之下设十四个小区，居民耕种北部平原、在河口捕鱼。1444年，这些海岸、平原和河谷仍在泰诺酋长手中；1492年哥伦布在这里见到的统治者瓜卡纳加里克斯，正是这一北方酋邦的首领。

1492年圣诞节，圣玛利亚号在这一带海岸触礁。瓜卡纳加里克斯派人帮助卸货，并允许哥伦布用船木修建纳维达德堡；十一个月后哥伦布返回时，木寨已被敌对酋长国焚毁，驻军全部丧命。1503年，西班牙人在附近建立雷亚尔港，1578年把居民迁往巴亚哈；1605年后的奥索里奥荒毁撤空了北岸，布坎尼尔海盗乘虚而入。1670年，贝特朗·多热龙带领法国移民建立法兰西角，1711年正式设城。到1770年首府迁往太子港之前，这里一直是法属圣多明各的都城和殖民地最富的港口，凭商人、剧院和蔗糖船运被称为「安的列斯群岛的巴黎」。1790年，城中有一万五千人，三分之二是奴隶。

1791年8月14日，两百名奴隶代表在城外的凯门森林集会，奴隶领袖杜蒂·布克曼主持仪式，约定起义；一周之内，北部平原的种植园燃起大火。布克曼被杀后，法国人把他的头颅挂在城中广场示众。1803年11月18日，让-雅克·德萨林在法兰西角城下的韦尔蒂埃尔击败罗尚博；1804年1月1日，海地宣布独立。亨利·克里斯托夫1807年在北方另立政权，1811年改称王国，把城市改名亨利角。他在米洛修建圣苏西宫，又在附近海拔九百米的山顶筑起拉费里埃城堡：1805年至1820年间，数以万计的劳工参与施工，城墙架设三百六十五门大炮，防备法国人卷土重来，而法军始终没有来。1820年克里斯托夫中风，军队哗变，相传他用一颗银弹自尽；他一死，北方王国便告终结。

en:
The Ciguayos held the Samaná Peninsula, the Nagua shore and the lower Yuna, a northeastern edge of Hispaniola where hills, mangroves and a broad bay meet. They were older inhabitants than the agricultural Taíno and kept their own language; Spanish accounts describe long-haired archers who used poisoned arrows and made no pottery. Taíno expansion brought them within Maguá's orbit, but in 1444 their villages still commanded the hills and shores of Samaná Bay.

The bay entered written history on 13 January 1493, when Columbus's landing party met Ciguayo archers at Rincón Beach. The islanders refused to sell their bows, two were wounded in the fight, and Columbus named the anchorage the Bay of Arrows. He carried four Ciguayos to Spain, and only one survived the voyage. Spanish authorities left Samaná lightly occupied for generations, so runaways and privateers used its coves. The bay also sheltered Guarionex: Mayobanex refused Bartholomew Columbus's demand to return the fugitive cacique, and both chiefs were captured. In 1756 Governor Francisco Rubio y Peñaranda settled Canary Islander families at Santa Bárbara de Samaná and Sabana de la Mar. Under the Peace of Basel the colony passed to France in 1796; a British naval raid took Samaná in 1807 and gave the town to Spanish creoles fighting French rule.
zh:
锡瓜约人占据萨马纳半岛、纳瓜海岸和尤纳河下游，也就是伊斯帕尼奥拉岛东北山丘、红树林与宽阔海湾相接的一侧。他们比从事农业的泰诺人更早住在这里，保留自己的语言；西班牙记载把他们写成留长发、使用毒箭且不制陶的弓箭手。泰诺人的扩张使他们受马瓜势力影响，但到1444年，他们的村落仍控制着萨马纳湾的山丘和岸线。

1493年1月13日，哥伦布的登陆队在林孔海滩遇到锡瓜约弓箭手，萨马纳湾也在这一年进入文字记载。岛民拒绝出售弓箭，冲突中有两人受伤，哥伦布把锚地命名为箭头湾。他带走四名锡瓜约人前往西班牙，航行结束时只有一人生还。西班牙当局此后几代都没有认真经营萨马纳，逃亡者和私掠者便使用这里的小海湾。这里也曾收留瓜里奥内克斯：马约瓦内克斯拒绝巴尔托洛梅·哥伦布交回逃亡首领的要求，最后两名首领都被俘。1756年，弗朗西斯科·鲁维奥-佩纳兰达总督把加那利群岛移民家庭安置到圣巴巴拉-德萨马纳和滨海萨瓦纳。根据《巴塞尔和约》，殖民地于1796年转交法国；1807年英国海军袭取萨马纳，把城镇交给反抗法国统治的西班牙裔克里奥尔人。

en:
Higüey filled the eastern end of Hispaniola, from the Haina River across the Yuma plain to Cape Engaño, Saona Island and the Mona Passage. Its principal village stood on the Yuma River, and 21 nitaínos governed its districts. Contact-period accounts name the caciques Cayacoa and Cotubanamá and the female ruler Higuanamá. In 1444 these forests, cassava fields and canoe crossings still belonged to an independent Taíno chiefdom.

Saona supplied much of Santo Domingo's cassava in 1502 when a Spanish crew stopped there to load bread. A crewman set a mastiff on a local cacique, and the dog killed him. Cotubanamá's followers then killed eight Spaniards, giving Governor Nicolás de Ovando reason to send Juan de Esquivel's soldiers in 1503; Bartolomé de las Casas marched with them and later wrote about the campaign. Las Casas described Cotubanamá as a large, powerful man who could draw a bow farther than any of his warriors. At the first peace settlement, Esquivel and Cotubanamá exchanged names in the guatiao ceremony. Fighting resumed, the Spanish fort was attacked, and eight of its nine soldiers died. Juan López tracked Cotubanamá to a cave on Saona, overpowered him and took him alive. The cacique was carried in chains to Santo Domingo and hanged in 1504. Defeated Taínos were forced into plantation labor, and colonists brought in African slaves as their numbers collapsed. Higüey received a royal privilege and coat of arms in 1508; sugar cane, ginger, cacao and cattle later became the Spanish town's sources of wealth.
zh:
伊圭位于伊斯帕尼奥拉岛最东端，疆土从艾纳河越过尤马平原，延伸到恩加尼奥角、绍纳岛和莫纳海峡。主要村落坐落在尤马河畔，21名尼塔伊诺分管各区。接触时代的记载提到卡亚科阿、科图瓦纳马等首领和女统治者伊瓜纳马。1444年，这里的森林、木薯田和独木舟航道仍属于一个独立的泰诺酋长领地。

1502年，绍纳岛已向圣多明各供应大部分木薯。一艘西班牙船靠岸装载木薯饼时，船员放出一条大獒犬，当地首领被咬死。科图瓦纳马的部下随后杀死八名西班牙人，总督尼古拉斯·德·奥万多便在1503年派胡安·德·埃斯基维尔出兵；巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯也在军中，后来记述了这场战争。他称科图瓦纳马身材高大、力气过人，开弓胜过部下所有战士。初次议和时，埃斯基维尔与科图瓦纳马按瓜蒂奥仪式交换名字。战事再起后，西班牙要塞遭到进攻，九名守军中八人丧命。胡安·洛佩斯追到绍纳岛一处洞穴，制住科图瓦纳马并将他生擒。这位首领被锁送圣多明各，1504年被绞死。战败的泰诺人被迫从事种植园劳役，人口锐减后，殖民者又输入非洲奴隶。1508年，伊圭获得王室特权和纹章；甘蔗、生姜、可可和养牛业后来成为西班牙城镇的财源。

en:
East of Havana the Bay of Matanzas bites deep into Cuba's north coast, where the Yumuri, San Juan and Canimar rivers come down to the sea. In 1444 Taino villages farmed those river valleys and paddled the wide, quiet bay in canoes; fishing people had camped at the mouth of the Canimar since far older times.

Columbus only sighted this coast on his second voyage in 1494, and the first Spaniard to survey it was Sebastian de Ocampo during his circumnavigation of Cuba in 1508. The bay's name comes from an act of resistance before the conquest of the island had begun. In 1510 a party of armed Spaniards, stranded without boats, asked native fishermen to ferry them across a river; midstream the fishermen overturned the canoes, and the armoured Spaniards drowned. Bernal Diaz del Castillo recorded the tale, and the place was called Matanzas, 'the slaughter'. Between 1514 and 1518 the Spanish laid out the Indian pueblo of Canimar on the eastern shore. For a century and a half the deep anchorage had no Spanish town and became a lair of smugglers and corsairs, until a royal order of 25 September 1690 brought thirty families from the Canary Islands. San Carlos y San Severino de Matanzas was founded in October 1693 under the guard of the Castillo de San Severino, and its cabildo met from 1695.

Sugar then made the district's fortune. By 1792 the town held some 1,900 enslaved Africans, nearly a third of its people, and by 1817 more than 10,000, close to half the population; Matanzas had become one of the richest sugar regions of Cuba. A printing press arrived in 1813.
zh:
哈瓦那以东，马坦萨斯湾深深切入古巴北海岸，尤穆里河、圣胡安河和卡尼马尔河在此入海。1444年，泰诺人的村落耕种这几条河的河谷，划独木舟往来于宽阔平静的湾面；更古远的年代，卡尼马尔河口就有渔猎部族栖居。

哥伦布1494年第二次航行时只是望见这片海岸，第一个前来勘察的西班牙人是1508年环航古巴的塞瓦斯蒂安·奥坎波。海湾的名字来自征服古巴开始前的一次反抗。1510年，一队无船可用的西班牙武装人员让当地渔民渡他们过河，行至中流渔民掀翻独木舟，披甲的西班牙人溺水而亡。贝尔纳尔·迪亚斯·德尔·卡斯蒂略记下此事，此地便被称作马坦萨斯，意为「杀戮」。1514至1518年间，西班牙人在湾东岸设立原住民村镇卡尼马尔。此后一个半世纪，这个深水锚地旁没有西班牙城镇，成了走私者和海盗的巢穴，直到1690年9月25日王室下令从加那利群岛迁来三十户人家。1693年10月，圣卡洛斯和圣塞韦里诺·德·马坦萨斯在圣塞韦里诺城堡护卫下建城，市政会自1695年起运作。

蔗糖随后造就了这片地区的财富。到1792年，城中约有一千九百名被奴役的非洲人，接近人口的三分之一；到1817年已超过一万人、将近居民半数，马坦萨斯成了古巴最富庶的蔗糖产区之一。1813年，城里有了印刷机。

en:
The Escambray, called Guamuhaya in the Taíno tongue, is the mountain knot of central Cuba, forested ridges running from the Caribbean coast up to the 1,140-metre Pico San Juan. In 1444 Taíno villages kept conucos in the foothills and fished the coves of Jagua Bay, a broad sound opening to the sea through a narrow mouth. The valleys belonged to them, and no European had yet seen the range.

Early in 1514 Diego Velázquez founded the Villa de la Santísima Trinidad beneath the sierra, the third Spanish town in Cuba. Hernán Cortés mustered his Mexico expedition there in 1518; Pedro de Alvarado and his five brothers joined him, and the town alcalde could not stop the ships sailing against Velázquez's orders. In 1527 Pánfilo de Narváez's Florida fleet was caught by a hurricane in the roadstead and lost two ships, twenty horses and sixty men. For two centuries Trinidad lived on cattle and small farms, while Jagua Bay became a smugglers' and pirates' anchorage; the Castillo de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles de Jagua was raised to close its mouth and was finished in 1742. Sugar then moved into the valleys behind the town, later called the Valle de los Ingenios, where at the trade's height more than fifty mills worked three valleys and over 30,000 enslaved Africans laboured in the canefields. On 22 April 1819 French settlers under Luis de Clouet founded Fernandina de Jagua on the great bay, the town later renamed Cienfuegos. In 1821 the Escambray was sugar country, and Trinidad's merchants had grown rich on the mills behind the coast.
zh:
埃斯坎夫雷山，泰诺语称瓜穆哈亚，是古巴中部的山岳枢纽，林木覆盖的山岭从加勒比海岸隆起，最高峰圣胡安峰海拔1140米。1444年，泰诺人的村落在山麓经营田园，在哈瓜湾的小湾里捕鱼；哈瓜湾是一道经狭窄水口通向大海的宽阔潟湖。这些山谷完全属于他们，欧洲人还不曾见过这片群山。

1514年初，迭戈·贝拉斯克斯在山麓建立至圣特里尼达镇，是西班牙人在古巴的第三座城镇。1518年，埃尔南·科尔特斯在此集结远征墨西哥的人手，佩德罗·德·阿尔瓦拉多五兄弟也在其中；镇长奉贝拉斯克斯之命阻拦，却没能挡住船队出航。1527年，潘菲洛·德·纳尔瓦埃斯的佛罗里达舰队在港中遭遇飓风，两艘船、二十匹马和六十人葬身风浪。此后两个世纪，特里尼达靠畜牧和小农为生，哈瓜湾则成了走私者和海盗的锚地；为封锁湾口而建的天使圣母哈瓜城堡于1742年完工。随后甘蔗进入镇后的谷地，那里后来得名因赫尼奥斯谷，极盛时三条山谷里有五十多座糖厂，三万多名非洲黑奴在蔗田里劳作。1819年4月22日，路易斯·德·克卢埃率法兰西移民在大海湾畔建立费尔南迪纳德哈瓜，后来更名为西恩富戈斯。1821年，埃斯坎夫雷已是蔗糖之乡，海岸后方的糖厂养肥了特里尼达的商人。

en:
Guane is the far west of Cuba, the rolling country beyond the Sierra de los Órganos that runs out to Cape San Antonio. In 1444 it belonged to the Guanahatabey, a people older than the Taíno. They moved in small bands rather than villages, made no pottery and kept no cemís, living on fish and shellfish; even the Taíno knew the western tip as another people's country.

Columbus reached this end of the island in April 1494, on his second voyage, and the Taíno interpreters with him could not understand a word the locals said. Diego Velázquez mentioned the Guanahatabey again in 1514 and Bartolomé de las Casas in 1516, but after the conquest they vanish from the record as Cuba's indigenous world collapsed. The Spanish town of Guane was founded in 1602, one of the few settlements in a district long left to itself. Canary Islanders arriving from the later sixteenth century planted the riverside vegas with tobacco, and the leaf went to the royal cigar factories in Havana. When the crown set up a tobacco estanco in 1717, fixing both price and the amount each grower had to sell, the vegueros rose three times between that year and 1723; the last revolt ended with twelve men shot and their bodies hung from trees along the road. By the later eighteenth century the far west was run as the Pinar del Río tobacco district, and in 1821 Guane remained a small town among the tobacco fields.
zh:
瓜内是古巴的最西端，奥尔加诺斯山脉之外，起伏的原野一直延伸到圣安东尼奥角。1444年，这里属于瓜纳哈塔贝伊人，一个比泰诺人更古老的族群。他们以小群体游徙，不建村落，不制陶器，也不拜塞米神像，靠鱼和贝类过活；在泰诺人看来，岛屿西头本就是另一族人的地方。

1494年4月，哥伦布第二次远航抵达岛的这一端，随队的泰诺译员却听不懂当地人的话。迭戈·贝拉斯克斯1514年、巴托洛梅·德·拉斯卡萨斯1516年还分别提到过瓜纳哈塔贝伊人，但征服之后，随着古巴原住民世界的崩溃，他们从记载中消失了。1602年建立的瓜内镇，是这片长期被放任自流的地区少有的定居点。16世纪末起迁来的加那利移民在河畔低地种烟，烟叶运往哈瓦那的王家雪茄烟厂。1717年王室设立烟草专卖，定死售价和收购数量，烟农在1717年至1723年间三次起事；最后一次有十二人被枪决，尸体挂在路边的树上示众。到18世纪后期，远西地区被划为比那尔德里奥烟草辖区；1821年时，瓜内仍是烟草田间的一座小镇。

en:
The Mayaca occupied the lakes and marshes of the upper St. Johns River south of Lake George, where villages stood on high ground and canoes moved through seasonally flooded woods and prairies. Their pottery belonged to the St. Johns culture shared with the Freshwater Timucua to the north, but Fontaneda reported that their language resembled that of the Ais on the Indian River. They lived by hunting, fishing and gathering rather than the maize fields worked by Timucua chiefs. The chief at Mayaca spoke for several towns, including places reported near the Atlantic coast, and his relations with the Freshwater Timucua set the local balance of power. In 1444 those canoe routes and lake villages still lay outside European maps.

Europeans entered the marshes through the rivalry between French Fort Caroline and Spanish St. Augustine. The Spaniards first met the Mayaca in 1566 while ransoming French captives; the next year the Mayaca joined Saturiwa and the Potano against the Freshwater Timucua. Franciscans reached the chief before 1600, and San Salvador de Mayaca later became the chief church of a mission province. By the 1690s the missions at Mayaca and Jororo served a changed population, because Yamasee refugees had become the majority and Spanish ranches occupied nearby ground. Unrest at the end of the century killed a friar and several converts. Carolina-backed raids in 1708 split the people: some fled to St. Augustine, while others moved to the eastern shore of Lake Okeechobee. There they fought the Calusa and their allies in 1738 and 1739, and the combined battles killed roughly 300 people. A few Mayaca were still living with Mayaimi and Santaluzo survivors in 1743; that mixed band is presumed to have left for Cuba with the Spaniards in 1763.
zh:
玛亚卡人占据圣约翰斯河上游、乔治湖以南的湖泊与沼泽；村镇建在高地上，洪水季节，独木舟穿行于被水淹没的林地和草泽。他们的陶器属于圣约翰斯文化，和北方「淡水蒂穆夸」诸部相同；但丰特内达记载，玛亚卡语与印第安河沿岸艾斯人的语言相近。他们以狩猎、捕鱼和采集为生，不像蒂穆夸诸酋那样经营玉米田。玛亚卡镇的首领能代表数个村镇，其中一些远在大西洋沿岸；他与淡水蒂穆夸人的关系决定着当地势力的消长。1444年，这些独木舟水路和湖畔村镇还完全没有出现在欧洲人的地图上。

欧洲人是随着法国卡洛琳堡与西班牙圣奥古斯丁的争夺进入这片沼泽的。1566年，西班牙人在赎回法国俘虏时首次遇到玛亚卡人；次年，玛亚卡人与萨土里瓦部、波塔诺部联合，攻打淡水蒂穆夸人。方济各会修士在1600年前已接触到大酋，圣萨尔瓦多·德·玛亚卡后来成为传教区的主要教堂。到17世纪90年代，玛亚卡和霍罗罗的传教站所服务的人口已经改变：亚马西难民占了多数，西班牙牧场也占用了附近土地。17世纪末的骚乱造成一名修士和数名信徒被杀。1708年，得到卡罗来纳支持的袭击者打散玛亚卡人，一部分逃往圣奥古斯丁，另一部分迁至奥基乔比湖东岸。1738至1739年，他们在那里同卡卢萨人及其盟友交战，各场战斗共造成约300人死亡。1743年，少数玛亚卡人仍和马亚依米人、圣卢索人的孑遗生活在一起；这支混居群体据信于1763年随西班牙人前往古巴。

en:
The Potano farmed the Alachua savanna, the oak-dotted prairies and fertile uplands of north-central Florida where the Alachua culture had raised villages and burial mounds since about 700. Potano, their chief town, led a string of settlements, and maize, beans and squash filled chiefly storehouses. Later Spanish officials ranked the Potano among the strongest Timucua-speaking chiefdoms. In 1444 their rivals were other Timucua chiefs, especially the Freshwater Utina to the east, and no European army had yet crossed the prairie.

Pánfilo de Narváez passed west of Potano before Hernando de Soto's army crossed the prairie in 1539 and seized stored maize. French soldiers from Fort Caroline and later Spaniards backed the Utina against Potano, and a Spanish expedition burned the chief town in 1584 after a Spanish captain was killed. Franciscans then made the defeated province one of Florida's busiest mission fields. San Francisco de Potano, founded in 1606, was the first mission with a resident priest west of the St. Johns; with Santa Ana, San Miguel and San Buenaventura nearby, the Potano missions first served about 1,200 people. Epidemics closed two missions and concentrated survivors around San Francisco and Santa Ana, while Spanish cattle ranches spread over former Potano fields. The Potano joined the Timucuan revolt in 1656, and by the 1670s only 160 people remained at the two missions. During Queen Anne's War, San Francisco was fortified after nearby Santa Fé was destroyed. The remaining Potano abandoned the prairie and moved east of the St. Johns in 1706.
zh:
波塔诺人在阿拉楚阿稀树草原务农。这片北佛罗里达中部的草原点缀着橡树林地，土壤肥沃；约自700年起，阿拉楚阿文化已在此营建村镇和墓葬土垒。酋镇波塔诺统领着一连串聚落，玉米、豆类和南瓜充实着首领的仓廪。后来的西班牙官员把波塔诺人列为最强的说蒂穆夸语酋邦之一。1444年，他们的对手是其他蒂穆夸首领，尤其是东方的淡水乌蒂纳人，当时还没有欧洲军队越过这片草原。

潘菲洛·德·纳瓦埃斯曾从波塔诺以西经过，随后埃尔南多·德·索托的军队在1539年穿越草原，夺走储存的玉米。卡洛琳堡的法国士兵以及后来的西班牙人都支持乌蒂纳人对抗波塔诺人；1584年，一名西班牙队长被杀后，讨伐军焚毁了波塔诺酋镇。方济各会随后把这个战败地区变成佛罗里达传教站最密集的地方之一。1606年设立的圣弗朗西斯科·德·波塔诺，是圣约翰斯河以西第一座有常驻教士的传教站；加上附近的圣安娜、圣米格尔和圣布埃纳文图拉，波塔诺诸传教站最初约为1200人服务。疫病迫使两座传教站关闭，幸存者集中到圣弗朗西斯科和圣安娜，西班牙牧牛场则扩展到波塔诺人原有的田地上。1656年，波塔诺人参加蒂穆夸起义；到17世纪70年代，两座传教站只剩160人。安妮女王战争期间，附近的圣菲被毁后，圣弗朗西斯科被加固设防。1706年，幸存的波塔诺人放弃草原，迁往圣约翰斯河以东。

en:
The wooded lowlands bearing the name Tanu run from the Brazos to the Neches, around Bedias Creek and the middle Trinity on the edge of the Big Thicket. In 1444 this was Bidai country; the people called themselves Quasmigdo, and Bidai is a Caddo word for 'brushwood', after the thickets they lived among. Their villages farmed the river bottoms and hunting parties worked the pine and oak woods. Three bands shared the country, the northernmost called Deadose, while the Akokisa fished Galveston Bay to the south and Hasinai towns stood beyond the Neches.

Europeans learned of the Bidai through a castaway. In 1722 the French officer François Simars de Bellisle was wrecked on the Bolivar peninsula and taken by the Akokisa; his journal, the first written account of the bay people, describes the Bidai as farmers allied to his captors. French traders were soon carrying goods up the Trinity, and after a French trading post on the river was broken up, Spain answered in 1756 with Presidio San Agustín de Ahumada and a Franciscan mission at El Orcoquisac, meant to draw Akokisa and Bidai families together. The Bidai kept to the old trade: in 1770 Spanish officials found them passing French guns to the Lipan Apache, when all three parties were enemies of Spain. After the Marqués de Rubí's frontier inspection the presidio was abandoned in 1771. The epidemics of 1776 and 1777 cut the Bidai by half; survivors joined the Akokisa and Koasati, and by 1821 no separate Bidai polity remained in the old Tanu country.
zh:
得名塔努的林地低地从布拉索斯河延伸到内奇斯河，环抱着贝迪亚斯溪与特里尼蒂河中游，紧挨着大丛林的边缘。1444年，这里是比代人的土地：他们自称夸斯米格多，而「比代」是卡多语里「灌柴」的意思，得自他们栖身的密林。村落在河滩上耕作，狩猎队伍出入松林与橡树林。这片土地上分作三个群体，最北的一支叫德阿德人；南面加尔维斯顿湾畔打渔的是阿科基萨人，内奇斯河以东则是哈西奈人的城镇。

欧洲人知道比代人，是从一个落难者开始的。1722年，法国军官弗朗索瓦·西马尔·德·贝利斯勒在玻利瓦尔半岛遇海难，被阿科基萨人掳走；他的日记是关于湾畔诸族最早的文字记录，其中写到比代人务农，并与俘获他的阿科基萨人结盟。法国商人很快沿特里尼蒂河上溯贩运货物，在河上一处法国贸易站被捣毁后，西班牙于1756年在奥科基萨克建起圣阿古斯丁·德·阿乌马达要塞和一座方济各会传教站，想把阿科基萨和比代的家庭聚拢过来。比代人更中意旧日的买卖：1770年西班牙官员发现他们把法国火器转卖给利潘阿帕奇人，那时三方都是西班牙的敌人。鲁维侯爵巡边之后，这座要塞于1771年废弃。1776和1777年的瘟疫使比代人减少一半，幸存者投奔阿科基萨人和科阿萨蒂人；到1821年，旧日的塔努之地上已没有独立的比代政体。

en:
Nitahendé reproduces the Mescalero name Nit'ahéndé, 'people who live against the mountains'; from about 1550 Spaniards called these Ndé bands Mescalero, after the agave they roasted in pit ovens and stored against famine. Their seasonal country took in the Sacramento Mountains of southern New Mexico and the Guadalupe Mountains above the west Texas desert, with canyons reaching toward the Pecos. In 1444 families moved between high pine forest, pinyon-juniper slopes, desert basins and buffalo plains, hunting deer and bighorn in the ranges and following buffalo east toward the Pecos and Llano Estacado. Springs, caves and mountain passes made this rough country both refuge and highway.

Spanish entradas first crossed the Guadalupe country in the sixteenth century, but no town or mission was planted there. The horse herds of New Mexico, occupied by Juan de Oñate in 1598, gave Apache raiders a far wider reach: bands along the frontier traded at the pueblos one season and swept off Spanish livestock the next, while colonial patrols answered in kind and took captives. Comanche expansion after 1700 pushed many Mescalero groups back into the Sacramento, Guadalupe and Trans-Pecos ranges. In the 1790s Spanish commanders negotiated limited peace settlements with the mountain rancherías, but the Mexican independence struggle after 1810 drained the frontier presidios and raiding resumed. When Spanish rule ended in 1821, the Nitahendé mountains were still an unconquered Mescalero stronghold on the edge of independent Mexico.
zh:
尼塔恩德一名来自梅斯卡莱罗人的称呼Nit'ahéndé，意为「住在山边的人」；约1550年起，西班牙人把这些恩代群体称作梅斯卡莱罗，名字得自他们在坑炉里烘烤、储藏起来度荒的龙舌兰。他们按季节往来的故土包括新墨西哥南部的萨克拉门托山和耸立在得克萨斯西部沙漠上的瓜达卢佩山，峡谷向佩科斯河方向延伸。1444年，各家族在高山松林、矮松刺柏坡、沙漠盆地和野牛草原之间迁移，在山里猎鹿和大角羊，又东赴佩科斯河与埃斯塔卡多平原追猎野牛。泉水、洞穴和山口让这片崎岖山地既是避难所，也是往来通道。

16世纪已有西班牙探险队穿过瓜达卢佩山区，但没人在那里建城镇或传教站。胡安·德·奥尼亚特1598年据有新墨西哥后，那里的马群让阿帕切骑手走得更远：边境群体这个季节在普埃布洛村落贸易，下个季节就卷走西班牙牲畜，殖民巡逻队也以同样的手段报复，掳走人质。1700年后科曼奇人扩张，把许多梅斯卡莱罗群体逼回萨克拉门托山、瓜达卢佩山和佩科斯以西山地。1790年代，西班牙指挥官与山里的牧场群落谈成有限的和平；1810年后墨西哥独立战争抽空了边境要塞，劫掠重新开始。1821年西班牙统治结束时，尼塔恩德群山仍是独立墨西哥边缘一处未被征服的梅斯卡莱罗据点。

en:
Ndawe Qoha is the lower Pecos borderland, where the river turns southeast out of the Trans-Pecos mountains and cuts arid canyons on its way to the Rio Grande. Waterholes and arroyos break the dry country where the cedar breaks of the Edwards Plateau meet the Chihuahuan Desert. In 1444 this was Ndé hunting ground: Lipan families moved with bison and white-tailed deer, roasted agave, gathered mesquite beans, and used the fords to meet Jumano travellers, whose trails ran west by Toyah Creek to La Junta de los Ríos. No Spanish town or mission yet stood on the lower river.

Antonio de Espejo followed this river on his return in 1582–1583 and named it Río de las Vacas for the buffalo herds, with Jumano guides showing him the way by Toyah Creek to La Junta. The Lipan had Spanish horses by 1608, and mounted rancherías turned the lower fords into links between west Texas, Coahuila and the southern plains; before long their riders were raiding the supply road from Coahuila to the new settlement of San Antonio. Comanche and Wichita pressure told next: the mission built for the Lipan on the San Sabá River in 1757 was destroyed within two years, and a Spanish and Lipan force was beaten at the Twin Villages in 1759. In 1778 Juan de Ugalde, governor of Coahuila, found a Lipan ranchería of about forty people led by Zapato Bordado on the Rio Grande, a Mescalero camp beside it, and opened the campaigns that followed. When Mexico became independent in 1821, the sparse frontier presidios had still not pinned the lower Pecos Lipan into a settled colonial district.
zh:
恩达韦科哈是佩科斯河下游边地：河水从佩科斯以西山地折向东南，切出一道道干旱峡谷，奔向里奥格兰德。水洼和旱谷散布在爱德华兹高原的雪松坡地与奇瓦瓦沙漠相接的干旱地带。1444年，这里是恩代人的猎场，利潘家族随野牛和白尾鹿迁移，烤龙舌兰、采牧豆，借各处渡口同胡马诺旅人往来；胡马诺人的小路向西经托亚溪通到拉洪塔。此时下游河畔还没有西班牙城镇或传教站。

1582至1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍沿这条河返程，因野牛成群而称其为「母牛河」，胡马诺向导带他经托亚溪前往拉洪塔。到1608年利潘人已有西班牙马，骑马的营地群落把下游渡口变成连接得克萨斯西部、科阿韦拉和南部平原的纽带，骑手们很快开始劫掠从科阿韦拉通往新建圣安东尼奥的补给道。接着是科曼奇人和威奇塔人的压力：1757年在萨巴河为利潘人修建的传教站不到两年就被毁，一支西班牙与利潘联军又在1759年的双子村之战中战败。1778年，科阿韦拉总督胡安·德·乌加尔德在里奥格兰德河畔找到利潘首领萨帕托·博达多（意为「绣花鞋」）约四十人的营地，旁边还扎着一处梅斯卡莱罗营地，他随后发动了连年讨伐。1821年墨西哥独立时，稀疏的边境要塞仍未能把佩科斯河下游的利潘人约束进固定的殖民辖区。

en:
Natahéndé is the middle Pecos River country of the Naa'dahéńdé, the Mescal People, whom Spanish records wrote down as Natagés. The Pecos rises on the eastern slope of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and runs south-east through dry grassland to the Rio Grande. In 1444 Apache bands pitched skin lodges along its valley and side arroyos, planting seasonal fields and hunting deer and bison; their staple was mescal, the desert agave whose roasted hearts fed them through lean seasons. No mission or presidio yet stood on the river, and horses had not reached these camps.

Antonio de Espejo followed the Pecos downstream on his return in 1582-1583 and named it the Río de las Vacas, River of Cows, after six days of travel through country thick with bison. Mounted raiding later tied the Natagés to the Texas frontier: in 1731 they joined Lipan, Teya and Jumano allies in raiding San Antonio, and on 9 December 1732 Governor Juan Antonio Bustillo y Ceballos fell on a camp of about four hundred tipis on the San Sabá River and fought for five hours without stopping the raids. Natagé and Lipan chiefs made peace with Spain at San Antonio in 1749. Comanche pressure then drove Lipan survivors south to join Natagé bands, and around 1780 the Natagés entered the Lipiyán coalition under Picax-Ande-Ins-Tinsle, Strong Arm.
zh:
纳塔恩德是佩科斯河中游地带，住在这里的是梅斯卡尔人，西班牙文献记作纳塔赫斯（Natages）。佩科斯河发源于桑格雷·德克里斯托山东坡，向东南穿过干旱草原，汇入格兰德河。1444年时，阿帕奇群体在河谷和支谷中搭起兽皮帐篷，种季节田，猎鹿和野牛；他们最要紧的口粮是梅斯卡尔龙舌兰，这种沙漠龙舌兰烤熟的心能在缺粮季节充饥。河畔那时还没有传教站和要塞，马匹也没有传到这些营地。

1582至1583年，安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍返程时顺佩科斯河下行，因连续六日穿行在野牛成群的地带，把河命名为「母牛河」。后来的骑马袭掠把纳塔赫斯人与得州边疆缠在一起：1731年，他们与利潘、特亚、胡马诺盟友联手袭掠圣安东尼奥；1732年12月9日，总督胡安·安东尼奥·布斯蒂略·伊·塞瓦略斯突袭圣萨瓦河畔一座约四百座帐篷的营地，激战五小时，仍未能止住阿帕奇人的袭掠。1749年，纳塔赫斯与利潘首领在圣安东尼奥同西班牙议和。科曼奇人的攻势随后把利潘残部向南驱赶，与纳塔赫斯各支合流；约1780年，纳塔赫斯人加入名号「铁臂」的皮卡克斯-安德-因斯-廷斯勒领导的利皮亚内斯联盟。

en:
Naflat is the Rio Grande country around Cochiti, one of the eastern Keres pueblos; its Keres name Kotyit means 'stone kiva'. Its people came from cliff-dwelling farmers of the Pajarito canyons, above all Rito de los Frijoles, and had lived in turn at Potrero Viejo and Hanut Cochiti before the historic town took shape. River water carried maize and cotton fields, and the finger mesas above the valley offered refuge in war. In 1444 Cochiti was an independent Keres town, bound by language, marriage and trade to the other pueblos strung along the river.

Juan de Oñate's men, who in 1598 gave Kotyit the Spanish form 'Cochiti', first opened trade; colonial rule then hardened into tribute in crops, cotton and labour. Franciscans put down the old rites and built the San Buenaventura mission. Cochiti took its part in the coordinated rising of August 1680, when about 400 Spaniards died and some 2,000 survivors abandoned the colony at Santa Fe. When Governor Otermín fought back to the river, the Cochiti withdrew with the people of San Felipe and Kewa to the Potrero Viejo mesa and held it until 1693, when Diego de Vargas's reconquest drove them off.
zh:
纳夫拉特是科奇蒂周围的里奥格兰德河谷地带，科奇蒂是东部凯雷斯语诸普韦布洛之一，其凯雷斯语本名科蒂伊特意为「石头基瓦」。科奇蒂人的先民是帕哈里托高原峡谷（以弗里霍莱斯河谷为中心）的崖居农民，在历史时期的城镇形成前先后住过波特雷罗维耶霍和哈努特科奇蒂。河水浇灌玉米和棉田，谷地上方的指状台地可在战乱时避难。1444年，科奇蒂是独立的凯雷斯人城镇，靠语言、通婚和贸易与沿河其他普韦布洛连在一起。

1598年，胡安·德·奥尼亚特的手下把「科蒂伊特」改写成西班牙式的「科奇蒂」；他们起初与当地人通商，殖民统治随后收紧，转为征收作物、棉布和劳役。方济各会压制传统仪式，建起圣布埃纳文图拉传教站。科奇蒂参加了1680年8月的联合起义，约四百名西班牙人在起义中丧命，约两千名幸存者放弃圣菲殖民地南逃。奥特尔明总督反攻回河畔时，科奇蒂人与圣费利佩、克瓦的部众弃城退往波特雷罗维耶霍台地，一直据守到1693年，才被迭戈·德·巴尔加斯的再征服军逐走。

en:
Tsi'ya is the Jemez River valley home of the Zia, Eastern Keres speakers who came south from the Four Corners country and settled beside the stream in the thirteenth century. They watered maize fields from the river, raised an adobe pueblo and became known for their pottery, above all the sacred sun sign: a circle ringed by four groups of four rays, because the number four bound together the four directions, the four times of day, the four stages of life and the four seasons. In 1444 the Zia kept their own fields and ceremonies, with no Spaniard yet inside the valley.

Antonio de Espejo first wrote down the name Tsi'ya in 1583, noting the largest pueblo on the Jemez. After Oñate's entry in 1598 Fray Alonso de Lugo set up the San Pedro y San Pablo mission, and Zia labourers had raised its church and convent by 1613. When the colonial government outlawed the old rites, the Zia joined Popé's revolt of 1680 and helped drive the Spanish south, leaving their horses in Pueblo hands for trade onto the plains. Governor Cruzate stormed the pueblo in 1689, killed 600 Zia and carried off seventy captives. The survivors moved a little north, and when wars between the pueblos turned against them they sided with Diego de Vargas; their leader Antonio Malacate brought them home to a town of about 120 people in 1692. The mission church was rebuilt in 1694 and remodelled in 1707 as Nuestra Señora de la Asunción.
zh:
齐亚是齐亚人在赫梅斯河谷的家园；齐亚人说东部凯雷斯语，13世纪从四角地区南迁到河畔定居。他们引河水灌溉玉米田，筑起土坯普韦布洛，并以制陶闻名，陶器上最受尊崇的是神圣的太阳符号：一个圆环外围着四组、每组四道光芒，因为四这个圣数把四方、一天四时、人生四阶段和四季统合在一起。1444年，齐亚人自行管理田地与仪式，河谷里还没有西班牙人。

安东尼奥·德·埃斯佩霍1583年首先记下「齐亚」这个名字，称它是赫梅斯河畔最大的普韦布洛。奥尼亚特1598年进入后，修士阿隆索·德·卢戈设立圣佩德罗与圣巴勃罗传教站，到1613年，齐亚劳工已建起教堂和修道院。殖民当局禁止传统仪式后，齐亚人参加了波佩1680年领导的起义，协助把西班牙人逐往南方，西班牙人的马匹也经普韦布洛人之手流入大平原贸易。1689年，总督克鲁萨特攻陷普韦布洛，六百名齐亚人被杀，七十人被俘。幸存者稍向北迁，后来普韦布洛诸部交战、处境不利，他们便倒向迭戈·德·巴尔加斯；首领安东尼奥·马拉卡特率众返乡时，1692年全镇只剩约一百二十人。传教教堂1694年重建，1707年整修后定名圣母升天教堂。

en:
The Sobaipuri were an O'odham people who farmed the well-watered valleys of the San Pedro and Santa Cruz rivers in the Pimería Alta. Their compact, carefully laid-out villages stood on river terraces, where maize, beans and squash grew in fields watered by flood ditches, and the settlements later recorded as Tumacácori and Guevavi had occupied the two valleys for many generations before Europeans reached the Southwest. With the Apache, Jocome and Jano on their eastern flank they traded, intermarried and at times rode out raiding, and they spoke the same Piman tongue as the Akimel and Tohono O'odham around them. In 1444 no friar or soldier had yet entered their valleys.

Fray Marcos de Niza may have passed Sobaipuri rancherías on the San Pedro in 1539, and Coronado's men entered the region soon after, but no Spaniard came back for roughly 150 years. In 1691 Sobaipuri headmen walked south to Sáric to invite the Jesuit Eusebio Francisco Kino, a Tyrolean who spent his last 24 years in the Pimería Alta; he visited Tumacácori and Guevavi, brought in cattle and wheat, and raised a church at Guevavi. On Easter Day 1698 the Sobaipuri leader Coro beat off a much larger force of Apache, Jocome and Jano that fell on his village of Gaybanipitea on the San Pedro, and his people became Spain's firm allies on the Sonora frontier and its buffer against the raiders. The Pima revolt of 1751 brought a presidio to Tubac in the following year, and as Apache raids worsened the Sobaipuri gave up the San Pedro valley around 1762. After the Jesuit expulsion of 1767 the Franciscans moved the mission headquarters from Guevavi to Tumacácori in 1771, and by 1775, the year a presidio was planted at Tucson, Guevavi stood empty. When New Spain's rule ended in 1821, the surviving Sobaipuri had merged into the O'odham communities at San Xavier del Bac and Tumacácori.
zh:
索巴伊普里人是奥奥德姆人的一支，在皮梅里亚阿尔塔境内圣佩德罗河与圣克鲁斯河水源充足的河谷务农。他们布局齐整的密集村落坐落在河流阶地上，用引洪水的沟渠浇灌玉米、豆类和南瓜；后来被记作图马卡科里和格瓦维的那些村落，在欧洲人来到西南之前的许多世代里就已住在这两条河谷。他们与东侧的阿帕奇人、霍科梅人和哈诺人贸易、通婚，有时还一同骑马外出劫掠，所说的皮曼语与周围的阿基梅尔人和托霍诺·奥奥德姆人相同。1444年时，还没有修士或士兵进入过他们的河谷。

1539年，修士马科斯·德·尼萨可能在圣佩德罗河畔经过索巴伊普里人的村落，科罗纳多的部下不久也进入这一带，但此后约一百五十年间再没有西班牙人来。1691年，索巴伊普里诸首领南行至萨里克，邀请耶稣会士尤塞维奥·弗朗西斯科·基诺；这位蒂罗尔人把人生最后24年都花在皮梅里亚阿尔塔，他走访了图马卡科里和格瓦维，带去牛和小麦，还在格瓦维主持建起教堂。1698年复活节，阿帕奇、霍科梅和哈诺人的大军围攻首领科罗在圣佩德罗河畔的盖巴尼皮特亚村，科罗率众以少胜多；此后他的部族成为西班牙在索诺拉边疆坚定的盟友，也是抵御袭扰的屏障。1751年皮马人起义后，西班牙人于次年在图巴克设立要塞；随着阿帕奇袭扰加剧，索巴伊普里人约在1762年放弃圣佩德罗河谷。1767年耶稣会被逐后，方济各会于1771年把传教中心从格瓦维迁往图马卡科里；到1775年图森设立要塞时，格瓦维已无人居住。1821年新西班牙统治结束时，幸存的索巴伊普里人已并入圣哈维尔·德尔·巴克和图马卡科里的奥奥德姆社群。

en:
The Pinaleño Mountains are the pine-bearing sky island of this upper Gila countryside, rising above Sonoran and Chihuahuan desert valleys to Mount Graham, which the Western Apache call Dził Nchaa Si'an, Big Seated Mountain, one of their four holiest peaks and a sacred mountain to the other peoples around it. Its streams run all year. The Tsékʼáádn, the Metate People, were the San Carlos and Pinaleño bands, who gathered pine nuts, hunted and farmed along those creeks. In 1444 their Ndee family groups moved between the ridges and the Gila watercourses, near the old farming lands of the Mogollon and Hohokam and neighbours who spoke Yavapai and O'odham.

Spanish knowledge entered the Gila watershed soon after the conquest of Mexico: Juan de la Asunción may have reached the river in 1538, and Hernando de Alarcón sailed to its mouth on the Colorado in 1540. Spanish maps long called the waterway the Río Grande de los Apóstoles or Río del Nombre de Jesús before writers fixed the name Gila in the early 1700s. By then horses had remade Apache raiding, and through that century raiders and Spanish reprisals swept the upper Gila valleys without a mission or presidio being planted in these mountains. In 1821 the Ndee still held every spring and trail.
zh:
皮纳莱尼奥山脉是希拉河上游一座长满松林的天空岛，耸立于索诺兰沙漠与奇瓦瓦沙漠的谷地之间，主峰格雷厄姆山被西阿帕奇人称为「安坐的大山」（Dził Nchaa Sí'an），是他们的四大圣山之一，也是周围各族共同的圣地，山间溪水终年不断。采卡登人（Tsékʼáádn，意为石磨盘人）即圣卡洛斯与皮纳莱尼奥诸群体，他们采集松果、狩猎，沿山溪耕作。1444年，他们的恩迪家族群体往来于这些山脊和希拉河水道之间，邻近莫戈永人和霍霍坎人的古老农地，也与亚瓦派人和奥奥德姆人为邻。

征服墨西哥后不久，西班牙人的地理知识进入希拉河流域：胡安·德·拉·亚松森可能在1538年抵达这条河，埃尔南多·德·阿拉尔孔1540年航行到希拉河注入科罗拉多河之处。在那以后的两百年里，西班牙地图长期把这条水道写作阿波斯托莱斯大河或耶稣之名河，直到18世纪初才固定使用希拉一名。那时马匹已经改变了阿帕奇人的袭掠方式；整个18世纪，袭掠者与西班牙人的报复往复于希拉河上游谷地，这群山里没有建起一座传教站或要塞。1821年，每一处水泉和山道都还在恩迪人手中。

en:
Taaqtam means 'people' in their own Takic tongue; the Spaniards later called these mountaineers Serranos, highlanders. In 1444 the Yuhaaviatam, the People of the Pines, held villages and oak groves high in the San Bernardino range, while the Desert Serrano, among them the Vanyume, lived along the Mojave River on the desert floor. The river runs underground for most of its course from the Cajon Pass toward Soda Lake, surfacing at gorges and oases where the people built their villages; at Wá'peat, mesquite, yucca, pine nuts and acorns, deer and bighorn sheep carried the bands through the year. The Mojave trail followed this chain of water from the Colorado River to the coast: coastal shell beads and asphaltum went east, Southwestern pottery and textiles came west, and Desert Serrano villagers supplied the caravans.

No European reached the country until 1771, when Mission San Gabriel Arcángel was founded and began claiming Serrano land and labour. Five years later the Franciscan Francisco Garcés travelled up the Mojave River, the first European known to do so, and named it Arroyo de los Mártires. In 1812 the Serrano joined the Cahuilla and Quechan in revolt against the missions' forced resettlement. In 1819 San Gabriel opened its San Bernardino de Sena estancia inland, a cattle station to which Serrano families were moved; they dug the Mill Creek Zanja, the ditch that carried mountain water to its fields. That same year Mojave warriors killed many Serrano in the desert. At Mexican independence in 1821 the estancia was still only a thin edge of settlement, and Taaqtam communities still held the mountains and the desert road.
zh:
「塔克塔姆」在他们自己的塔基克语里就是「人」的意思，是圣贝纳迪诺山脉的山居部族，西班牙人后来称他们为塞拉诺人，即山里人。1444年，「松林之人」尤哈维亚塔姆在高山上经营村落和橡树林；瓦尼乌姆等沙漠塞拉诺群体则住在沙漠地带的莫哈韦河沿岸。这条河从卡洪山口流向苏打湖，大部分河道在地下，只在峡谷和绿洲涌出地面，村落就建在这些地方；在瓦佩阿特，人们靠牧豆、丝兰、松子、橡实、鹿和大角羊度过一年。莫哈韦商路顺着这串水源从科罗拉多河通向海岸：沿海的贝壳珠和沥青向东运去，西南地区的陶器和织物向西流来，沿途的沙漠塞拉诺村民为商队补给饮水和食物。

欧洲人迟至1771年才进入此地：圣加百列大天使传教站就在这一年建立，随后开始征用塞拉诺人的土地和劳力。五年后，方济各会修士弗朗西斯科·加尔塞斯沿莫哈韦河上溯，成为有记载的第一个走过这条河的欧洲人，他把河命名为殉道者溪。1812年，塞拉诺人联合卡维拉人和克昌人起义，反抗传教站强迫集居。1819年，圣加百列传教站在内陆谷地开设圣贝纳迪诺·德·塞纳牧场站养牛，塞拉诺家庭被迁往那里；他们挖成米尔溪灌溉渠，把山泉水引到牧场站的田里。同年，莫哈韦战士在沙漠中杀死许多塞拉诺人。1821年墨西哥独立时，这座牧场站仍只是定居区伸向内陆的前沿，塔克塔姆诸群体仍占据着山地和沙漠商路。

en:
The Choinumni were a Kings River people, one of dozens of autonomous Yokuts tribes in the San Joaquin Valley. In 1444 their villages stood along a stretch of the upper Kings River, in country of oak hills and reedy sloughs. The oaks supplied acorns ground into meal, the waterways gave fish, waterfowl and roots, and tule rushes roofed pit houses and were lashed into rafts. Yokuts stories tell of a duck that brought mud up through a covering flood, the mud becoming the Sierra Nevada and the Coast Ranges. Trails over the Sierra carried trade with the Mono and other Paiute bands on the east side, and each Yokuts tribe ran to several hundred people. No mission or garrison stood anywhere near the river.

The first non-Indian recorded in the southern valley was Pedro Fages, who crossed it in 1772 while travelling from San Diego to San Luis Obispo. In 1805 Gabriel Moraga's expedition camped on the Kings and named it Río de los Santos Reyes in honour of the Three Kings; a friar in the party thought the populous, well-watered valley fit for a mission and a presidio, and Moraga's later journeys fixed the Spanish names of the San Joaquin and the valley's other rivers. No mission was ever built on the Kings. When New Spain became Mexico in 1821, the Choinumni still held all their river villages.
zh:
乔伊努姆尼人是金斯河居民，也是圣华金谷数十个自治约库特部族之一。1444年，他们的村落坐落在金斯河上游一段河畔，周围是橡树坡和芦苇荡：橡树提供可磨粉的橡实，河汊出产鱼、水禽与根茎，香蒲既能铺半地穴房屋的顶，也能扎成木筏。约库特人的故事讲，洪水覆盖大地时，一只鸭子衔泥出水，泥堆成了内华达山脉和海岸山脉。翻山的小路通向山脉东侧，同莫诺人及其他派尤特队群贸易。每个约库特部族有几百人，河畔附近没有传教站，也没有驻军。

有记载第一个进入圣华金谷南部的外人是佩德罗·法赫斯，他1772年从圣迭戈前往圣路易斯奥维斯波途中穿过谷地。1805年，加夫列尔·莫拉加的远征队在金斯河畔扎营，为纪念三王将河命名为三王河（Río de los Santos Reyes）；随行修士认为这片人烟稠密、水源充足的河谷适合建传教站和要塞，莫拉加后来的几次出行又给圣华金河等谷地河流定下西班牙名字。金斯河上始终没有建起传教站。1821年新西班牙变为墨西哥时，乔伊努姆尼人仍占有着他们全部的河畔村落。

en:
Ohlone is the country around San Francisco Bay, a great inland sea whose narrow opening to the Pacific let even Cabrillo's ships sail past unseen. In 1444 more than fifty autonomous tribelets lived between the bay's marshes and Monterey in the south, among them the Ramaytush at the peninsula tip, where the village of Chutchui stood, and the Tamyen of the Santa Clara valley. They spoke related Utian languages, followed the Kuksu cult and raised shellmounds beside their waterside villages. Tule rafts carried them across the bay to trade and feud, and salmon, acorns and clouds of waterfowl made this one of the most thickly peopled lands north of Mexico.

Europeans found the bay by mistake. Gaspar de Portola marched north in 1769 to rediscover the port of Monterey, failed to recognise Monterey when he passed it, and pushed on with his men falling sick of scurvy. On 4 November his sergeant Jose Francisco Ortega, scouting ahead with a party over the coast ridges, found their northward path barred by an enormous bay no chart showed. Portola led the whole expedition up into the hills to look at it, and Friar Juan Crespi wrote in his diary that all the navies of Europe could lie sheltered there.

Six years later Juan de Ayala took the San Carlos through the Golden Gate, and in March 1776 Juan Bautista de Anza laid out the sites for Mission San Francisco de Asis, soon called Dolores, and the Royal Presidio; Mission Santa Clara and the pueblo of San Jose followed the next year. Hundreds of Ohlone entered the missions in 1794 and 1795, when a deadly epidemic swept the bay. In 1807 and again in 1810-11 Russian-led Aleut otter hunters raided in kayaks and carried thousands of skins away to Canton. Dolores came to hold about 1,100 neophytes, while more than 5,000 had died there by the time Mexico took the province in 1821.
zh:
奥洛内是旧金山湾这片巨大内海四周的土地，海湾通向太平洋的入口太窄，连卡布里略的船都驶了过去，没有发现它。1444年，五十多个互不统属的部落小群住在湾边沼泽到南方蒙特雷之间：半岛尖端是拉马伊图什人，楚特奎伊村就在这里，圣克拉拉谷里住着塔米恩人。他们操亲属相近的乌蒂安语系语言，奉行库克苏信仰，在水畔村庄旁堆起贝丘。人们乘香蒲筏渡湾去贸易和械斗，鲑鱼、橡子和遮天蔽日的水鸟，使这里成为墨西哥以北人口最稠密的地区之一。

欧洲人是误打误撞发现这片海湾的。1769年，加斯帕尔·德·波尔托拉为重新找到蒙特雷港沿海岸北上，路过蒙特雷却没有认出来，只好继续前行，士兵纷纷染上坏血病。11月4日，他手下的军士何塞·弗朗西斯科·奥尔特加率侦察队翻上海岸山脊，发现向北的去路被一片地图上没有的巨大海湾挡住。波尔托拉把全队带上高地远望，修士胡安·克雷斯皮在日记里写道，全欧洲的海军都能在这片湾中停泊。

六年后，胡安·德·阿亚拉驾「圣卡洛斯号」穿过金门；1776年3月，胡安·包蒂斯塔·德·安萨选定城址，建起圣弗朗西斯科·德·阿西斯传教所（不久即以「多洛雷斯」闻名）和王家要塞，第二年又建了圣克拉拉传教所和圣何塞镇。1794至1795年，数百名奥洛内人进入传教所，一场致命疫病恰在此时席卷湾区。1807年以及1810至1811年，为俄国人效力的阿留申海獭猎手两度乘皮艇闯入湾中，把数千张海獭皮运往广州。多洛雷斯最多时约有一千一百名新信徒，而到1821年墨西哥接掌这片土地时，已有五千多人死在那里。

en: In 1444 the Wintun held the Sacramento Valley on the river's west side, from Mount Shasta down to San Francisco Bay, between the water and the Coast Range. They were three kindred peoples: the Wintu on the upper Sacramento and McCloud, the Nomlaki on the central tributaries, and the Patwin of the lower valley, perhaps 12,000 strong in 1770. Domed earth lodges lined the streams, and life turned on salmon runs, acorn meal, manzanita cider and tight-woven baskets. The Patwin kept the Kuksu religion: its men danced in disguise in underground dance houses, and in the Hesi ceremony women joined the rites the Maidu and Pomo also held. Wintu canoes carried Tan-oak acorns and abalone beads up to the Shasta and brought dentalium shells back. By 1800 Spanish missions and soldiers had broken the southern Patwin into small bands pressed toward San Francisco Bay, and in 1808 Gabriel Moraga's expedition entered the lower valley and named the river the Rio de los Sacramentos, the name the Sacramento still bears.
zh: 1444年，温图诸族据有萨克拉门托河西侧的河谷，北起沙斯塔山，南到旧金山湾，夹在大河与海岸山脉之间。他们分三支：北支温图人住在河上游与麦克劳德河，中支据有中部各支流，南支是下游的帕特温人；1770年三支人口合计约一万二千。圆顶土屋沿河排开，生计围绕鲑鱼汛、橡子粉、熊果酒和细密的编织篮筐。帕特温人奉行库克苏信仰：男子在半地穴舞屋中化装跳舞，赫西仪式还允许女子参加，迈杜人和波莫人也行同样的礼。温图人的独木舟载着石栎橡子和鲍鱼贝珠北上沙斯塔，换回角贝。到1800年，西班牙传教团和军人已把南方帕特温人拆成小股，逼向旧金山湾；1808年，加布里埃尔·莫拉加的远征队进入下游河谷，将河命名为「圣事之河」，萨克拉门托河的名字即从这一西班牙语名而来。

en:
The Paipai, also called Akwa'ala, held the widest corridor of northern Baja California: their trails ran from San Vicente on the Pacific between Kiliwa country to the south and Kumeyaay and Cocopa lands to the north, almost to the Colorado River delta. They spoke a Yuman language close to that of the Yavapai across the Colorado, and lived without towns or fields, moving between agave and mesquite harvests, acorns and pine nuts in the high hills, and fish and shellfish on both coasts. In 1444 autonomous bands held the whole corridor.

Sebastián Vizcaíno mapped the Pacific shore in 1602, but sustained contact only began with the Portolá-Serra expedition of 1769. Dominicans Miguel Hidalgo and Joaquín Valero founded San Vicente on 2 August 1780, on the red-earth Llano Colorado. It grew into the largest Dominican establishment in Baja: a church thirty metres long, granaries and neophyte dormitories inside a wall with watchtowers, and a barracks for twelve to twenty-five soldiers detached from the Loreto presidio. As the order's frontier headquarters it guarded the mission road between San Fernando de Velicatá and San Diego and faced the warlike peoples of the lower Colorado. The Dominican Luis Sales served there from 1781 and left one of the few accounts of the Paipai; the baptized population rose from 83 in 1782 to 317 in 1787, then fell to 246 by 1800 as disease ran through it. A second station, Santa Catarina, was opened on 12 November 1797 at a Paipai place called Jactobjol, 'where the water falls on the stones', near the Kumeyaay border; dams and stone-lined ditches watered wheat, maize and vegetables over sixty hectares. Two soldiers were killed on the road between the missions in 1804 and a fight followed at Santa Catarina; a wider rising broke out there in 1808 over the abuse of native women. Neither mission ever prospered, and when Mexico became independent in 1821 the Spanish frontier here rested on those two hard-pressed stations alone.
zh:
派派人又称阿克瓦阿拉，据有下加利福尼亚北部最宽的一条走廊：他们的活动路线西起太平洋畔的圣维森特，南接基利瓦人的土地，北邻库梅亚伊人与科科帕人，东端几乎到达科罗拉多河三角洲。他们的尤曼语与科罗拉多河对岸亚瓦派人的语言相近；他们没有城镇和农田，随龙舌兰、牧豆、橡子和山地松子的采收季节迁徙，也在两岸捕鱼拾贝。1444年，自治的小队据有整条走廊。

1602年，塞瓦斯蒂安·比斯开诺测绘了太平洋海岸，但持续接触要到1769年波尔塔拉与塞拉的远征队才开始。1780年8月2日，多明我会士米格尔·伊达尔戈和华金·巴莱罗在红土的科罗拉多平原建立圣维森特传教站。它后来成为下加利福尼亚规模最大的多明我会据点：三十米长的教堂、粮仓和新信徒宿舍围在带瞭望塔的墙内，另有兵营驻扎从洛雷托要塞调来的十二至二十五名士兵。作为多明我会的边疆指挥中心，它扼守圣费尔南多·德·贝利卡塔与圣迭戈之间的传教干道，正对科罗拉多河下游好战的诸族。会士路易斯·萨莱斯1781年起驻在此地，留下了为数不多的派派记述之一；受洗人口1782年为八十三人，1787年增至三百一十七人，到1800年因疫病又降到二百四十六人。第二座传教站圣卡塔琳娜于1797年11月12日开设，站址在库梅亚伊边界附近一个派派人称为 Jactobjol 的地方，意为「水落在石头上的地方」；水坝和石砌沟渠灌溉着六十公顷的小麦、玉米和蔬菜。1804年，两站之间的路上有两名士兵被杀，随后圣卡塔琳娜发生战斗；1808年，因原住民妇女受虐待，那里又爆发更大规模的起事。两座传教站始终没有兴盛，1821年墨西哥独立时，西班牙人在这里的边疆只靠着这两座苦苦支撑的传教站。

en:
Tecpatitlan, the older spelling of the Tepatitlán district, lay in the Tecuexe highlands of Jalisco, on the tracks between Tonala and the drier Guamare country to the east. The Tecuexes, whose name is read as stone terraces, were Uto-Aztecan speakers split among independent lordships; Tecpatitlan, Acatic, Xalostotitlan and Yahualican were among their seats. Their strongest neighbour was Tonala, Tonallan in Nahuatl, the kingdom of the place through which the sun rises, whose subject towns included Tlaquepaque and Tlajomulco. In 1444 its ruler was a woman, Cihualpilli Tzapotzinco, and the lordship bordered the Caxcanes and Guachichiles to the north, the Guamares to the east and the Purépecha Empire to the south. Its villagers were already potters, shaping burnished ware for the local markets.

The Purépecha brought the lordship its great war. From 1480 to 1510 the irecha Tangaxoan sent armies out of Tzintzuntzan to seize the saltpeter beds along Lake Chapala; the force that marched on Tonala was beaten at Tlajomulco by Cihualpilli's captain Coyotl, fighting beside the kingdom of Colliman. Spaniards came in 1530 with Nuño de Guzmán's rapid and brutal sweep through western Mexico. Cihualpilli sent gifts, Guzmán demanded submission, and when some 3,000 of her people attacked his column they were routed on 25 March; she was baptized Juana Bautista and Tonala was renamed Santiago de Tonala. Pedro Almíndez Chirino passed through Tecpatitlan on the same campaign, and Franciscans who raised its first church named the settlement San Francisco de Tecpatitlan. Tonala remained the leading Spanish town of the area only until Guadalajara was founded nearby in 1535; the Mixtón War of 1541–1542, epidemics and the Chichimeca War then broke Tecuexe power. Friars taught the local potters the wheel and the glaze kiln, and Tonala polychrome ware was shipped to Spain and Italy in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. The parish church of San Francisco at Tecpatitlan was begun in 1742.
zh:
特克帕蒂特兰是特帕蒂特兰地区的旧拼法，地处哈利斯科的特库埃克塞高地，位于托纳拉与东面更干旱的瓜马尔人之地之间的往来通道上。特库埃克塞一名可解为石梯田，他们使用犹他—阿兹特克语系语言，分成若干互不统属的领主政权，特克帕蒂特兰、阿卡特克、哈洛斯托蒂特兰和亚瓦利坎都是其据点。它们最强的邻邦是托纳拉，纳瓦特尔语作托纳兰，意为「太阳升起之地的王国」，辖有特拉凯帕克、特拉霍穆尔科等属城。1444年，其统治者是一位女性，名西瓦皮尔皮·察波钦科；领地北接卡斯坎人和瓜奇奇尔人，东邻瓜马尔人，南与普雷佩查帝国接壤。这里的村民已是制陶匠，为附近市集制作磨光陶器。

普雷佩查人给这个领主政权带来一场大战。1480至1510年，国王坦加克索安从钦聪灿派出军队，要夺取查帕拉湖畔的硝石带；进攻托纳拉的一支在特拉霍穆尔科被西瓦皮尔皮的将领科约特尔击败，与他们并肩作战的还有科利曼王国的军队。1530年，西班牙人随努尼奥·德·古斯曼扫荡墨西哥西部的迅猛残酷之师而来。西瓦皮尔皮送去礼物，古斯曼却要求臣服；她手下约三千人进攻西班牙纵队，于3月25日被击溃，她本人受洗取名胡安娜·包蒂斯塔，托纳拉改名圣地亚哥·德·托纳拉。佩德罗·阿尔门德斯·奇里诺在同一次征战中经过特克帕蒂特兰，方济各会修士建起当地第一座教堂，定居地遂称圣弗朗西斯科·德·特克帕蒂特兰。托纳拉作为当地首要西班牙城镇的地位只维持到1535年瓜达拉哈拉在附近建立；1541—1542年的米克斯顿战争、疫病和奇奇梅卡战争随后瓦解了特库埃克塞人的力量。修士向本地陶匠传授陶轮和釉窑技术，17、18世纪时托纳拉彩陶已远销西班牙和意大利。特克帕蒂特兰的圣弗朗西斯科教区教堂于1742年动工。

en:
Xilotepec, whose Nahuatl name means the hill of the young maize ear, rises in the wooded ranges north of the Valley of Mexico. It was the seat of an Otomi lordship, with subject towns running from Soyaniquilpan and Huichapan to Nopala, and trade and kinship ties reaching the Huasteca, Michoacan and the Guanajuato frontier. Acamapichtli of Tenochtitlan overran it in 1379, but the people of the district fought their way back to self-rule, and the later campaigns of Axayacatl against Xiquipilco, Xocotitlan and Xilotepec found them hard to subdue. In 1444 Xilotepec was still an Otomi realm, its villages growing maize and making pottery and cloth, while Chichimeca peoples held the dry country farther north.

Ahuitzotl brought the lordship back under Tenochtitlan: the campaign waged for his coronation in 1487 destroyed Chiapa, and hundreds of Otomi were brought to the ceremonies. Spanish colonization began in 1526 with a Franciscan mission, and the farmland was granted out as encomiendas. Its most famous holder was Juan Jaramillo, husband of Cortés's interpreter Doña Marina, known as Malintzin or La Malinche; after her death he married Beatriz de Andrada, and the suit between Beatriz and María, his daughter by Marina, over the Xilotepec lands went as far as the Council of the Indies.
