Its late Gothic and Renaissance houses show the commerce of around 1500, when Görlitz held some 10,000 people; about 600 woad carts a year were still being taxed there around 1560. Protestant preaching began in 1521, and the city introduced an evangelical church order in 1539. Ferdinand I imposed the Upper Lusatian Pönfall in 1547, fining Görlitz and stripping it of rights and estates. After the Peace of Prague moved Upper Lusatia to Saxony in 1635, Swedish forces occupied the city in 1639 and besieged it in 1641. Fighting returned to nearby Moys in 1757, when an Austrian army twice the size of the Prussian force defeated the Prussians and killed their commander. The Upper Lusatian Society of Sciences was founded in Görlitz in 1779, and the Congress of Vienna assigned the city to Prussian Silesia in 1815.
zh:
格尔利茨（上索布语称佐尔耶尔茨）占据卢萨蒂亚尼斯河渡口，国王大道上的西方商人经此前往西里西亚和波兰。斯拉夫人聚落戈雷利茨见于1071年记载；1126年至1131年，波希米亚公爵索别斯拉夫一世在后来圣彼得与圣保罗教堂附近修建边境城堡。城市商人靠呢绒和菘蓝致富：1339年，格尔利茨取得这种蓝色染料的强制中转权，到中世纪晚期，来自图林根的菘蓝车在前往布雷斯劳途中于此纳税。1346年，它与包岑等城市加入卢萨蒂亚同盟，1377年至1396年又是短暂的格尔利茨公国都城。1348年，一位名叫阿达斯的犹太女性取得市民身份，这在中世纪德意志城市中很少见。1429年，胡斯袭掠者烧毁外城郊区，但城墙内的城市守住了。1444年，格尔利茨是一座富裕的天主教波希米亚边城，附近村庄仍有人说索布语。

1469年至1490年波希米亚继承冲突期间，城市接受马加什·科尔温统治，随后重归波希米亚。城中的晚哥特式和文艺复兴宅邸显示出1500年前后的商业规模，当时格尔利茨约有一万居民；1560年前后，每年仍约有六百辆菘蓝车在此纳税。新教讲道始于1521年，城市在1539年颁行新教教会规章。1547年，斐迪南一世发动上卢萨蒂亚惩罚，格尔利茨被罚以重金，并被剥夺权利和地产。1635年《布拉格和约》将上卢萨蒂亚划归萨克森后，瑞典军队于1639年占领城市，又在1641年围城。1757年，战事再抵附近的莫伊斯：兵力两倍于普军的奥军击败普鲁士人，击毙其指挥官。1779年，上卢萨蒂亚科学学会在格尔利茨成立；1815年维也纳会议将城市划归普鲁士的西里西亚。

en:
Gallipoli stands on the southern shore of the Thracian peninsula that still bears its name, only three kilometres across the Dardanelles from Lapseki. That short crossing made it a ferry town and naval base long before the Ottomans arrived. The Macedonian foundation of Kallipolis was fortified by Justinian I, who stocked it with grain and wine for his armies. Venice held it after 1204; the Catalan Company occupied the town in 1306, killed most of the townspeople, and pulled down the works when it left. The earthquake of March 1354 shattered the walls, and the Ottomans crossed into the ruins a month later, gaining their first durable stronghold in Europe. A Savoyard crusade restored it to Byzantium in 1366, but Ottoman troops returned in September 1376 and kept the crossing. In 1416 Pietro Loredan burned the Ottoman fleet off the quays. In 1444 Gallipoli was the ferry and arsenal for Ottoman armies moving between Anatolia and the Balkans, with Greek Orthodox fishermen and sailors living under a Turkish captain.

The Ottomans turned the narrows into a defended naval frontier. Gallipoli became the chief town of a sanjak and the first centre of the Kapudan Pasha's naval province. In 1463 Mehmed II built Kilitbahir on the western shore and Kale-i Sultaniye opposite it, siting the two forts at the narrowest stretch to lock the passage. The town also produced Piri Reis: born there around 1470, he sailed with his uncle Kemal Reis, drew the 1513 world map, and compiled the Kitab-i Bahriye for Suleiman. Sephardic families later joined the Greek, Turkish and Jewish population. During the Cretan War a Venetian fleet broke the Ottoman galleys outside the Dardanelles in June 1656 and blockaded Istanbul, until Koprulu Mehmed Pasha forced a passage in July 1657. The forts again fired on a passing fleet in February 1807, when a British squadron under John Duckworth broke through and returned damaged. In 1821 Gallipoli remained a fortified sanjak town, ferry port and naval station.
zh:
加里波利位于仍以它得名的色雷斯半岛南岸，与对岸的拉普塞基相隔仅三公里。这段狭窄海路使它早在奥斯曼人到来前就是渡口和海军基地。马其顿人建立的卡利波利斯由查士丁尼一世加固，城中储存军粮和酒。1204年后威尼斯控制此城；1306年加泰罗尼亚佣兵团占据该镇，杀害大部分市民，撤走时又拆毁防御工事。1354年3月地震摧毁城墙，奥斯曼人一个月后进入废墟，得到他们在欧洲第一处持久据点。1366年萨伏依十字军把它交回拜占庭，但奥斯曼军队1376年9月重返渡口并长期据守。1416年，彼得罗·洛雷达安在码头外焚毁奥斯曼舰队。1444年的加里波利是奥斯曼军队往返安纳托利亚与巴尔干的渡口和军械港；希腊东正教渔民、水手在一名土耳其长官治下生活。

奥斯曼人把这段窄海经营成设防的海军边疆。加里波利成为桑贾克首城，也是海军元帅行省最初的中心。1463年，穆罕默德二世在西岸修建基利特巴希尔堡，又在对岸修建苏丹尼耶堡，把两座要塞设在海峡最窄处，以锁住航道。加里波利还与皮里·雷斯联系在一起：他约1470年出生于此，早年随叔父凯末尔·雷斯出海，后来绘制1513年世界地图，并为苏莱曼编成《海洋志》。塞法迪犹太人家族后来也迁入此城。克里特战争期间，威尼斯舰队1656年6月在达达尼尔海峡外击溃奥斯曼桨帆船队并封锁伊斯坦布尔，科普鲁律·穆罕默德帕沙直到1657年7月才强行打开航道。1807年2月，约翰·达克沃思率领的英国分舰队强闯海峡又带伤撤回，两岸要塞再次向过路舰队开火。1821年，加里波利仍是设防的桑贾克城镇、渡口和海军站。

en:
Ohrid spreads along the shore of the great lake that bears its name, in the mountains of south-western Macedonia. The Romans knew it as Lychnidos, a station on the Via Egnatia between Dyrrachion and Constantinople, and Slavs of the Berziti tribe settled there before it passed to Bulgaria around 840. In 886 Clement, a disciple of Cyril and Methodius soon joined by Naum, founded the Ohrid Literary School to train Slavic priests in their own tongue; his name is linked to the Cyrillic alphabet, and Ohrid became one of the foremost centres of Slavic letters. From 990 it was Tsar Samuel's capital and patriarchal seat; after taking it in 1018 Basil II reduced the patriarchate to an autocephalous archbishopric, with the new church of St Sophia as its cathedral. Normans, the Despotate of Epirus, Stefan Dusan's Serbs in 1334 and the Albanian Gropa lords followed. The Ottomans took Ohrid in 1408 and made it a sanjak seat. In 1444 it was a largely Orthodox Slavic town of monasteries and churches; later tradition counted 365 chapels, one for each day of the year.

The archbishopric outlived its new masters. In the early sixteenth century it held sway over the eparchies of Sofia and Vidin, the churches of Wallachia and Moldavia and of the Patriarchate of Pec, and even the Orthodox districts of Italy. Ohrid was drawn into Skanderbeg's wars: his troops, with Gjergj Arianiti and Zaharia Gropa, took the town, and on 14-15 September 1464 the 12,000 men of the League of Lezhe with 1,000 Venetians routed a 14,000-strong Ottoman army outside its walls. In 1466 Mehmed II, on his return from Albania, deported Archbishop Dorotheos with his clergy and many citizens to Istanbul for supporting the revolt. The Christian town then shrank: in 1529-1536 the registers counted 337 Christian households against 93 Muslim ones, and by 1664 only 142 Christian hearths remained. Evliya Celebi in 1670 found seventeen quarters and about 150 shops. A trade revival in the eighteenth century brought the town back to some 5,000 people, and in 1767 the Sultan abolished the archbishopric that Basil II had set up in 1018.
zh:
奥赫里德沿同名大湖的湖岸展开，坐落在马其顿西南部的群山间。罗马人称此地为吕克尼多斯，是都拉基乌姆通往君士坦丁堡的埃格纳提亚大道上的一站；斯拉夫人贝尔扎提部落在此定居，约840年并入保加利亚。886年，西里尔与美多德的弟子克莱门特在此创办奥赫里德文学学派，瑙姆不久也前来共事，学塾用斯拉夫语培养本地教士，克莱门特的名字也与西里尔字母的创制连在一起，奥赫里德成为斯拉夫文字最重要的中心之一。990年起，这里是沙皇萨穆伊尔的都城和保加利亚牧首驻地；1018年巴西尔二世攻取此城，把牧首区降为自治的奥赫里德大主教区，以新建的圣索菲亚教堂为座堂。此后诺曼人、伊庇鲁斯专制国、1334年斯特凡·杜尚的塞尔维亚帝国和阿尔巴尼亚格罗帕家族先后入主。1408年奥斯曼人攻占奥赫里德，设为桑贾克治所。1444年时，它是一座以东正教斯拉夫人为主的城镇，修道院和教堂林立，相传城中教堂曾多至365座，一年每日各有一座。

大主教区在新主人治下延续下来，16世纪初势力达到顶峰，下辖索非亚、维丁教区，瓦拉几亚、摩尔多瓦和佩奇牧首区的教会，甚至意大利的东正教教区。奥赫里德卷入了斯坎德培的战争：他的部队联合乔治·阿里安尼提和扎哈里亚·格罗帕攻取此城；1464年9月14至15日，莱什联盟的1.2万人与1000名威尼斯士兵在城外击溃一支1.4万人的奥斯曼军队。1466年，穆罕默德二世从阿尔巴尼亚回师，以支持起义为由，把多罗泰奥斯大主教连同教士和大批市民放逐到君士坦丁堡。基督徒的小城随即衰败：1529至1536年税册中有337户基督徒、93户穆斯林，到1664年基督徒住户只剩142户；1670年切莱比到访时记下17个街区和约150间店铺。18世纪商路复兴，人口恢复到约五千人；1767年，苏丹废除了巴西尔二世1018年设立的大主教区。

en:
Transvaal is the high grassland beyond the Vaal River, its centre lying between the Apies River and the long quartzite ridge of the Magaliesberg, which the Tswana below it called Dithaba, the Mountains. By the fifteenth century Sotho-Tswana clans held its watered valleys in homesteads of conical-roofed huts, keeping cattle, smelting iron and hunting the highveld game. Each chiefdom took a totem animal, lion, crocodile or porcupine, and the ruling house bound its outlying villages by taking wives from them; a man's standing was counted in cattle. In 1444 no European frontier crossed these plateaus. Related clans traded and feuded between the Magaliesberg and the Steelpoort valley; the Bahurutshe were the strong lineage to the west and the Maroteng Pedi to the east.

Towards 1780 the Maroteng ruler Thulare brought the smaller chiefdoms under his house and built the first Pedi paramountcy, holding country from the Magaliesberg east to the lowveld and south to the Vaal. He died about 1820, and his death let in the Mfecane. Ndwandwe regiments raiding from the south-east broke his outlying districts and swept off the cattle; clans abandoned the open valleys and held out on fortified hills. By 1821 raiding parties and migrant columns were crossing the highveld, Thulare's polity had split back into its component chiefdoms, and his Maroteng heirs kept only the Pedi heartland in the Steelpoort mountains.
zh:
德兰士瓦是瓦尔河以北的高原草原，中心在阿皮斯河与绵长的马加利斯堡石英岩山脊之间；住在山下的茨瓦纳人把这条山脊称作迪萨巴（Dithaba），意思就是「群山」。15世纪时，索托-茨瓦纳诸氏族已在水草丰美的谷地里建起圆锥形顶茅屋的聚落，牧牛、冶铁，在高原上狩猎。每个酋邦各奉一种图腾，狮子、鳄鱼或豪猪；统治氏族靠与边远村落联姻来约束它们，人的名望以牛只多少来计。1444年，还没有欧洲人的边疆横过这片高原，彼此亲缘的诸氏族在马加利斯堡与斯蒂尔普特河（Steelpoort）谷地之间通商、交战；西方最强的谱系是巴胡鲁策人，东方是马罗滕佩迪人。

约1780年，马罗滕首领图拉雷把小酋邦们收归本族，建立第一个佩迪最高酋邦，疆域从马加利斯堡向东直到低地草原、向南抵达瓦尔河。他约在1820年去世，身后的局面正撞上「姆费卡内」大动荡：恩敦德韦人的军团从东南袭来，攻破他的外围地区、卷走牛群，诸氏族弃守开阔谷地，在设防的山头上苦撑。到1821年，袭掠队伍和迁徙的人潮正穿过高原，图拉雷的政权已散回一个个独立酋邦，他的马罗滕后人只保住斯蒂尔普特山区的佩迪腹地。

en:
The Tswana country is a dry plateau between the upper Vaal and the Kalahari thirstland. Its Setswana-speaking merafe, chiefdoms of clans gathered around a ruling house, lived in large stone-walled towns. A kgosi ruled through council and court, and his wealth lay in cattle kraals, iron and copper work, ivory and long-distance trade. In 1444 the Bahurutshe, one of the principal Tswana lineages, held the watered valleys of the Marico and the grazing runs that opened toward the desert edge.

In the late 1400s the Bahurutshe founded Kaditshwene in the Tshwenyane Hills, beside the iron and copper deposits that fed its smelting houses, and its workshops made it one of the chief Tswana towns. Its name is said to mean 'what an incredible number of baboons'. When the missionary John Campbell reached it in 1820 he found a stone-walled city of roughly 20,000 people, larger than Cape Town in those years. The city fell in 1821, during the Mfecane. Mmanthatisi, regent of the Batlokwa while her son Sekonyela was a minor, led her people into the Marico ahead of the wars; her followers called her Mosanyane, the tiny one, and her regiments stormed and sacked Kaditshwene. The survivors fled west to the Bakwena and other Tswana chiefdoms. Stone walls, foundations and ash middens are all that remains of the town.
zh:
茨瓦纳之地是瓦尔河上游与卡拉哈里荒原之间的干旱高原。说茨瓦纳语的「梅拉斐」是围绕统治氏族聚合的诸酋邦，住在石墙环绕的大城镇里；「科戈西」首领靠议事会和断事治理，财富来自牛栏、铁器铜器、象牙和长途贸易。1444年，作为茨瓦纳主要谱系之一的巴胡鲁策人据有马里科河谷的水草之地，以及伸向沙漠边缘的各条牧场。

15世纪末，巴胡鲁策人在奇韦尼亚内丘陵的铁矿和铜矿旁建起卡迪奇韦内，矿脉养着各处炼炉，作坊使它成为茨瓦纳数一数二的大城。据说城名的意思是「哪来这么多狒狒」。1820年传教士约翰·坎贝尔抵达时，这座石墙城镇约有二万人，比当时的开普敦还多。1821年，城在「姆费卡内」动荡中陷落：巴特洛夸人的摄政曼塔提西在儿子塞科涅拉（Sekonyela）年幼期间掌权，为避战乱率部涌入马里科，部众称她为「小个子」莫萨尼亚内（Mosanyane）；她的军团攻破并洗劫了卡迪奇韦内，幸存者西逃，投奔巴奎纳等茨瓦纳酋邦。石墙、屋基和灰烬堆，就是这座城剩下的全部东西。

en:
The Swazi highlands climb from the Pongola valley and the Lubombo escarpment to the Mdzimba range, where the Mbabane and Polinjane rivers meet; wet valleys and broken mountain country made the kind of ground on which a small kingdom could defend itself. Farmers and ironworkers speaking the ancestral Nguni and Sotho tongues had settled there by the eleventh century, and San hunters still kept the remoter heights. In 1444 small Nguni and Sotho clans grazed cattle and tilled the wet valleys. The Dlamini, an Embo-Nguni lineage, then lived under the Tembe chiefs near Delagoa Bay, east of the Lubombo; the kingdom that would carry their name into these hills had not begun.

A Dlamini king ruled with a queen mother at his side, and a queen regent held the kingdom during a minority. In the eighteenth century the lineage crossed the Pongola. Ngwane III, counted as the first Swazi king, called his state kaNgwane and, pressed by the Ndwandwe king Zwide, planted his royal kraal Zombodze below the Mhlosheni hills in Shiselweni. His praise name remembered him as the mamba that lays twelve eggs and eats them, for he put his sons to death; only Ndvungunye was spared to follow him. Ndvungunye ruled from the same kraal until 1815, when lightning killed him. His son Sobhuza, called Somhlolo, 'man of mysteries', then took the throne. He ended the Ndwandwe wars by marrying Zwide's daughter Tsandzile and moved his capital north to a new Zombodze in the central highlands, drawing the older Nguni and Sotho clans of the Emakhandzambili into his kingdom. When the Mfecane swept the lowlands after 1815, Sobhuza kept out of it with embassies, tribute and timely alliances with Shaka, and the highland ridges screened his people from the worst of the fighting. By 1821 a mixed kingdom of Nguni, Sotho and surviving San was forming around the northern strongholds.
zh:
斯威士高地从蓬戈拉河谷和卢邦博崖坡抬升到姆津巴山脉，姆巴巴内河与波林贾内河在山中汇流；湿润谷地和崎岖山地，正适合一个小王国凭险自守。说恩古尼语、索托语先祖语言的农民和铁匠至迟在11世纪已在此定居，桑人猎手仍占着更高的山岭。1444年，若干恩古尼和索托小氏族在湿谷中养牛耕作；德拉米尼这支恩博-恩古尼氏族当时还住在卢邦博以东、德拉戈阿湾附近的滕贝首领治下，把他们的名字带进这片山地的王国尚未开始。

德拉米尼国王由王母在侧共同治国，王储年幼时则由女王摄政守住国家。18世纪，这一氏族渡过蓬戈拉河。被视为斯威士第一代国王的恩瓦内三世把自己的国家称作「卡恩圭内」；在恩敦德韦国王兹维德（Zwide）的压力下，他把王室牛克拉尔宗博泽设在希塞卢韦尼的姆洛谢尼山下。他的赞歌称号把他比作「下了十二个蛋又把它们吃掉的曼巴蛇」，因为他处死了自己的儿子，只有恩德温贡耶活下来继位。恩德温贡耶在同一座王帐统治到1815年，被雷击身亡；其子索布扎，绰号索姆赫洛洛，意为「神秘之人」，随后即位。他迎娶兹维德之女灿齐莱（Tsandzile）结束了与恩敦德韦的战争，又把都城北迁到中部高地的新宗博泽，把早先在此的恩古尼、索托氏族恩马汉赞比利（Emakhandzambili）纳入王国。1815年后「姆费卡内」动荡席卷低地，索布扎靠使节、贡赋和在时机合适时与沙加结盟置身战外，高地山脊替他的族人挡住了最猛烈的兵锋。到1821年，一个由恩古尼人、索托人和残存桑人组成的复合王国正在北方山寨周围成形。

en:
Upper Limpopo covers the country between the Limpopo's southern tributaries and the salt-bearing Soutpansberg, or 'Salt Pan Mountain', with the high basin around Polokwane at its southern edge. The old kingdom of Mapungubwe broke up around 1300 and its gold and ivory trade moved north to Great Zimbabwe, leaving Vhangona clans in the mountains and Sotho-Tswana villagers on the plateau. Around 1400 contacts with Kalanga groups crossing the river shaped Venda speech and chiefship; Venda tradition names Thoho-ya-Ndou, 'head of the elephant', as its first ruler and his royal kraal Dzata in the mountains as the first Venda capital. In 1444 the Venda strongholds around the Soutpansberg and the Pedi homesteads of the southern highveld exchanged cattle, iron, copper and salt from the pan at the mountain's western end, and answered to no single ruler.

The Venda kept their independence in the broken ridges and defiles of the Soutpansberg, while Pedi lineages coalesced on the highveld to the south; around 1780 their Maroteng chief Thulare built the Pedi power that overshadowed the Transvaal. By about 1820 the Mfecane reached even these valleys, as raiding parties crossed the plateau hunting cattle and refuge. In 1820 Coenraad de Buys came into this country, a fugitive from the Cape frontier nearly seven feet tall who had fought on the Xhosa side in the frontier wars and counselled the chief Ngqika. He made his camp near the Soutpansberg with his mixed following of Khoi, Oorlam, Baster and Xhosa kin, the clan afterwards called the Buys people, meaning to trade ivory for gunpowder with Tsonga and Afro-Portuguese merchants from the coast. In 1821, old and ailing, he set off down the Limpopo towards the Portuguese settlements, telling his sons to wait for him at the river; he never returned, and his body was never found. The Venda ridges stayed in African hands.
zh:
上林波波地区覆盖林波波河以南各支流与产盐的索特潘斯山（意为「盐盘山」）之间的土地，南缘是波洛夸内周围的高原盆地。古老的马蓬古布韦王国约1300年瓦解，黄金和象牙贸易北移到大津巴布韦，山地里留下凡戈纳诸氏族，高原上住着索托-茨瓦纳村民。约1400年，与渡河南下的卡兰加人群接触，塑造了文达语和文达酋邦；文达传统把最早的王称作托霍-亚恩杜，意为「象首」，把他在山中的王室牛克拉尔扎塔奉为第一个文达王都。1444年，索特潘斯山周围的文达山寨与南部高原的佩迪聚落交换牛只、铁、铜和山西端盐盘所产的盐，不奉任何共主。

文达人在索特潘斯崎岖的山岭和隘口中保持独立，佩迪各谱系则在南方高原联合；约1780年，马罗滕首领图拉雷建立起威震德兰士瓦的佩迪政权。约1820年，连这些谷地也逼近了「姆费卡内」动荡，袭掠队伍为搜掠牛群、寻找容身之地而穿过高原。1820年，科恩拉德·德·拜斯进入此地：这个从开普边疆逃出的人身高近七英尺，曾在边疆战争中站在科萨人一边，还做过恩格基卡（Ngqika）首领的谋士。他带着科伊、奥拉姆、巴斯特和科萨姻亲组成的混合部众在索特潘斯山附近扎营，这一氏族后来称作拜斯人；他打算用象牙向沿海来的聪加人和非裔葡萄牙商人换取火药。1821年，年迈多病的德·拜斯沿林波波河向葡萄牙人的居留地出发，让儿子们在河边等他，却一去不返，遗体也始终没有找到。文达人据守的山岭仍在非洲首领手中。

en:
Sheffield grew up where the River Sheaf joins the Don, in the Yorkshire South Riding, among hills thick with coal and iron. After the Harrying of the North a Norman motte-and-bailey castle guarded the ruined settlement, and the stone castle was begun in 1270 above a market fixed there by 1296. The ground suited edge-tools: fast becks turned grindstones cut from the local gritstone, and by the fourteenth century Sheffield knives were known well enough for Chaucer to arm his miller in the Canterbury Tales with a 'Sheffield thwitel' stuck in his hose. In 1444 it was still a small market town of Hallamshire, living by its cutlers.

Two famous state prisoners knew the place under the Tudors. Cardinal Wolsey lodged at Sheffield Manor for some eighteen days in 1530, travelling south under arrest for high treason as the guest of the fourth Earl of Shrewsbury; he died at Leicester before he reached London. From 1570 to 1584 Mary, Queen of Scots, was held in the castle and manor by George Talbot, sixth Earl of Shrewsbury, and his wife Bess of Hardwick, fourteen of her nineteen years in English captivity. By the early 1600s Sheffield was England's chief cutlery town outside London, and the Company of Cutlers in Hallamshire was incorporated by act of Parliament in 1624. Its royalist garrison surrendered the castle after a short siege in 1644, and the stronghold was then razed. In the 1740s Benjamin Huntsman perfected crucible steel at Handsworth and Thomas Boulsover devised the silver-fused Sheffield plate, drawing metalworkers to the town, which held just over 60,000 people by 1801.
zh:
谢菲尔德兴起于雪菲河汇入顿河之处，地处约克郡南赖丁煤铁富藏的丘陵之间。「北方浩劫」之后，一座诺曼式土岗城堡镇守着这片残破之地；石砌城堡于1270年动工，山下到1296年已辟有固定集市。这里的地利适合打造利器：湍急的山溪推动以当地砂岩凿成的砂轮，到14世纪，谢菲尔德刀已相当出名，乔叟在《坎特伯雷故事集》里让磨坊主的袜筒里插着一把「谢菲尔德短刀」。1444年的谢菲尔德还是哈伦郡的一座小集镇，靠刀匠手艺为生。

都铎时期，两位要犯来过这里。1530年，被控叛国的枢机主教托马斯·沃尔西被押解南下，在第四代谢鲁斯伯里伯爵作东的谢菲尔德庄园住了约十八天，未到伦敦便病死在莱斯特。1570至1584年，苏格兰女王玛丽被第六代谢鲁斯伯里伯爵乔治·塔尔博特和他的妻子哈德威克的贝丝囚禁在城堡与庄园之中；她在英格兰被囚十九年，其中十四年在谢菲尔德。17世纪初，谢菲尔德已是伦敦以外英格兰首屈一指的刀具之城，哈伦郡刀匠公会于1624年获议会立法成立。内战中据守城堡的王党守军在短暂围城后于1644年投降，城堡随即被夷为平地。1740年代，本杰明·亨茨曼在汉兹沃思完善坩埚炼钢法，托马斯·博尔索弗又发明银铜贴合的「谢菲尔德镀银」，大批工匠随之而来；到1801年，全镇人口已逾六万。

en:
Prignitz is a country of heath, pastures and river crossings between the Elbe, Havel and Stepenitz; its name comes from an old Polabian word for difficult woodland. Slavic villagers lived along its rivers before the Wendish Crusade of 1147 opened the way for German settlers, and the land was divided between the Margraves of Brandenburg and the bishops of Havelberg. Noble houses such as the Plothos, the Gans zu Putlitz and the Quitzows held its castles; Dietrich and Johann von Quitzow were robber-barons feared across Brandenburg, living off feuds and plundered merchants. Perleberg, chartered in 1239, joined the Hanse in 1358 and sent the region's cattle and wool north to the sea. In 1444 Prignitz was a Catholic Brandenburg border country of livestock estates, restless knightly families and crowded pilgrimage roads.

Those roads led to Wilsnack. On 15 August 1383 the knight Heinrich von Buelow, feuding with the bishop of Havelberg, burned the village and its church; in the ruins the priest found three hosts on the altar, unburned and stained with blood. They became one of the great shrines of Latin Christendom, called the Santiago of the North, and penitents came from the British Isles, Scandinavia, Hungary and the Baltic lands. Their offerings rebuilt the church as the great St Nicholas's, the Holy Blood Church. Jan Hus denounced the cult in 1403, and when the Synod of Magdeburg tried to ban the pilgrimages in 1443, the bishop of Havelberg and Elector Frederick II kept them open with the pope's support. Wilsnack's first Protestant clergyman burned the hosts in 1552 and was imprisoned and expelled for it; the pilgrim trade ended and the town shrank, though the mid-fifteenth-century blood shrine survived.

After 1627 armies of every party crossed the heath in the Thirty Years' War. At Perleberg fire and plague cut 3,500 inhabitants to about 300, and barely 127 of 300 houses were still habitable at the peace. Friedrich Ludwig Jahn, the 'Turnvater' who founded the German gymnastics movement, was born at Lanz in the Prignitz in 1778. French troops plundered Perleberg in October 1806 and levied contributions through the years of occupation; in 1812 the towns raised a citizen guard, and about a thousand Prignitz volunteers served against Napoleon until 1815.
zh:
普里格尼茨是易北河、哈弗尔河与施特珀尼茨河之间的荒野、牧场和渡口地带，名字来自古波拉布语，意为难以通行的林地。1147年文德十字军为德意志移民打开通路之前，斯拉夫村民已沿河而居；后来这片土地分属勃兰登堡藩侯和哈弗尔贝格主教。普洛托、甘斯·楚·普特利茨、奎措等贵族家族在此据有城堡，迪特里希·冯·奎措和约翰·冯·奎措两兄弟更是出了名的强盗骑士，令整个勃兰登堡忌惮，靠家族仇杀和劫掠商队为生。佩勒贝格1239年获得城市特许状，1358年加入汉萨，把本地的牲畜和羊毛运往北方海边。1444年的普里格尼茨是勃兰登堡边境上的天主教畜牧之乡，骑士家族不安分，朝圣路上人来人往。

朝圣者去的是维尔斯纳克。1383年8月15日，与哈弗尔贝格主教结仇的骑士海因里希·冯·比洛焚毁村庄和教堂；神父在废墟中的祭坛上找到三块圣体，既没有烧坏，又沾着血迹。它们后来成为拉丁基督教世界最重要的圣物之一，被称为「北方的圣地亚哥」，从不列颠群岛、斯堪的纳维亚、匈牙利和波罗的海沿岸都有人前来。朝圣者的布施把教堂重建成宏伟的圣尼古拉堂，又称圣血教堂。扬·胡斯1403年就痛斥过这一崇拜；1443年马格德堡宗教会议试图禁止朝圣，哈弗尔贝格主教和选帝侯腓特烈二世又在教宗支持下保住了它。1552年，维尔斯纳克第一位新教牧师烧掉圣体，本人也因此下狱、被逐；朝圣生意就此断绝，城市随之萎缩，只有15世纪中叶的圣血龛保留下来。

1627年后，三十年战争中各方军队轮番穿过这片荒野。佩勒贝格遭火灾和瘟疫夹击，三千五百名居民只剩下约三百人，战争结束时三百栋房屋里仅一百二十七栋还能住人。后来人称「体操之父」、创立德国体操运动的弗里德里希·路德维希·雅恩，1778年出生在普里格尼茨的兰茨。1806年10月法军洗劫佩勒贝格，占领年间一直征收贡赋；1812年各城镇组建市民卫队，约一千名普里格尼茨志愿者对法作战，直到1815年。

en:
The Ribatejo is the Tagus floodplain above Lisbon, its name meaning 'up the Tagus'. Winter rains spread the river over the lezíria marshes, whose grazing fattened the cattle, bulls and horses that supplied most of the animals used in Portuguese bullfighting; grain and cattle moved downriver to the capital. The chief town, Santarém, began as the Roman Scalabis, where Julius Caesar set a military camp in 61 BC. Its later name comes, by tradition, from Saint Irene, a Christian maiden martyred at Tomar whose body the Tagus carried to its walls. Under the Moors it was Shantarin, a frontier fortress and seat of learning that gave birth to the poet and historian Ibn Bassam. On 15 March 1147 Afonso Henriques took it when a handful of men climbed the walls by night and opened a gate, an exploit told in the chronicle De expugnatione Scalabis; in 1184 the Almohad caliph Abu Yaqub Yusuf died beneath the walls while trying to retake it. The kings of Portugal held cortes in its palace, Fernando I chose a convent in the city for his burial, and the 1415 expedition against Ceuta was planned in the same halls. In 1444 Santarém, crowded with Gothic churches and monasteries, was called the capital of Portuguese Gothic, and John I's palace at nearby Almeirim, already known as the 'Sintra of winter', drew the Aviz court for the cold season.

In 1491 João II's heir Afonso died in a riding fall on the Tagus banks, and the crown passed in 1495 to his cousin Manuel, who enlarged the Almeirim palace. Gil Vicente staged plays there for the wintering court, among them a tragicomedy at the marriage of the Infanta Isabel to the Emperor Charles V, and Garcia de Resende began printing his Cancioneiro Geral within the palace. Pedro Álvares Cabral died in Santarém after his voyage to Brazil and lies in the Graça church, beside Pedro de Meneses, the first Portuguese governor of Ceuta. When Sebastian vanished in Morocco, Cardinal Henry opened the Cortes of Almeirim in January 1580 to settle the succession; it failed, and Philip II of Spain took the kingdom. Earthquakes damaged the city in 1531 and 1755. French troops occupied it in 1807, and in the winter of 1810–11 Masséna's army held the Santarém–Rio Maior line after failing against the Lines of Torres Vedras, then fell back into Spain.
zh:
里巴特茹是里斯本上游的塔霍河冲积平原，地名意为「塔霍河上游」。冬季河水漫过莱齐里亚沼泽，牧场养肥牛群、公牛和马匹，葡萄牙式斗牛所用的牲畜大多产自这里；谷物和牲畜顺河运往首都。首府圣塔伦的前身是罗马人的斯卡拉比斯，公元前61年尤利乌斯·凯撒在此设立军营。相传其名来自圣女伊雷妮：她在托马尔殉道，遗体随塔霍河漂到城下。摩尔人统治时名作尚塔林，这座边境要塞也是学术中心，诗人兼史家伊本·巴萨姆出生于此。1147年3月15日，阿方索·恩里克斯派少数勇士趁夜攀上城墙、打开城门夺城，事迹载入《斯卡拉比斯攻克记》；1184年，穆瓦希德哈里发阿布·叶尔孤白·优素福试图夺回该城时死于城下。葡萄牙列王常在圣塔伦王宫召开议会，费尔南多一世安葬在城内修道院，1415年远征休达也在这些殿堂中筹划。1444年的圣塔伦哥特教堂与修道院林立，被称为葡萄牙哥特式之都；若昂一世在邻近阿尔梅林的行宫已有「冬季辛特拉」之名，阿维什宫廷常来此避寒。

1491年，若昂二世的太子阿方索在塔霍河畔坠马身亡，1495年王位传给堂弟曼努埃尔，他扩建了阿尔梅林行宫。吉尔·维森特为在此过冬的宫廷献演戏剧，其中包括在伊莎贝尔公主与皇帝查理五世婚礼上演出的悲喜剧；加西亚·德·雷森迪也在宫中开始印行他的《诗歌总集》。佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔从巴西归来后在圣塔伦终老，葬于恩典教堂，身旁是休达首任葡萄牙总督佩德罗·德·梅内塞斯。塞巴斯蒂安在摩洛哥失踪后，红衣主教恩里克于1580年1月召开阿尔梅林议会议决王位继承，议会无果而终，西班牙国王腓力二世取得葡萄牙。1531和1755年两次地震使城市受损。1807年法军占领此地；1810至1811年冬，马塞纳的军队攻托里什韦德拉什防线不克，退守圣塔伦至里奥马约尔一线，随后撤回西班牙。

en:
Plasencia guards the entrance to the Jerte valley in northern Extremadura, where the Silver Road ran between the kingdom of Leon to the west and al-Andalus to the south. Alfonso VIII of Castile founded it as a planned frontier city in 1186, with the motto 'to please God and men', and Clement III made it a bishop's see in 1189. The Almohads took it after Alarcos in 1196 and lost it again on 15 August, after which Castile ringed the town with walls. Its late-thirteenth-century charter protected Christians, Muslims and Jews, and Plasencia held the largest Jewish community in Extremadura; Alfonso X's Cantigas de Santa Maria sing of a bull run in the town square, one of the earliest bullfights on record. Plasencia sent proctors to the Cortes of 1391, but in 1442 John II granted the town to Pedro de Zuniga, first Count of Plasencia, and the vote was lost. Four years later Bishop Juan de Carvajal opened university-level humanities courses, the first in Extremadura. In 1444 it was a livestock town on the Silver Road, lately become the seat of the Zuniga counts.

Two episodes of the Castilian succession quarrel took place in Plasencia. On 27 April 1465 the count joined the nobles who symbolically deposed Henry IV here, snatching the sword of justice from the king's wooden effigy on the way to the Farce of Avila, and on 29 May 1475 Juana la Beltraneja married Afonso V of Portugal in the Casa de las Argollas, the pair claiming Castile. In 1488 the townsmen rose against the Zuniga, and Ferdinand the Catholic confirmed their fueros at the cathedral gate on 20 October. The abdicated Charles V withdrew in 1557 to the Hieronymite monastery of Yuste in the Vera hills and died there on 21 September 1558. Plasencia helped buy Extremadura its own vote in the Cortes when the province was formed in 1653. French troops took the town on 28 December 1808, occupied it twelve times during the Peninsular War, and burned Yuste in 1809.
zh:
普拉森西亚扼守埃斯特雷马杜拉北部赫尔特河谷的入口，银之路在这一段夹在西边的莱昂王国与南边的安达卢斯之间。1186年卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索八世建立这座计划性边境城市，城铭意为「取悦上帝与众人」，1189年教皇克雷芒三世将其设为主教驻地。1196年穆瓦希德人乘阿拉尔科斯之战攻占此城，同年8月15日卡斯蒂利亚将其收复，随后环城筑起城墙。13世纪末的特许状保护基督徒、穆斯林和犹太人，普拉森西亚拥有埃斯特雷马杜拉最大的犹太社群；阿方索十世的《圣玛利亚之歌》里有一首写城中广场的奔牛，是最早见于记载的斗牛活动之一。此城曾向1391年的议会派出代表，1442年胡安二世却把它封给首任普拉森西亚伯爵佩德罗·德·苏尼加，表决权随之丧失。四年后，主教胡安·德·卡瓦哈尔开办大学级别的人文学科，是埃斯特雷马杜拉最早的高等教育。1444年的普拉森西亚是银之路上的畜牧城，新近成为苏尼加伯爵家族的治所。

卡斯蒂利亚王位之争有两件大事发生在普拉森西亚。1465年4月27日，贵族在此象征性废黜恩里克四世，伯爵从国王木像身上夺下象征司法的剑，随后便是阿维拉闹剧；1475年5月29日，胡安娜·拉·贝尔特拉内哈在阿尔戈利亚斯宅邸嫁给葡萄牙国王阿丰索五世，二人宣称拥有卡斯蒂利亚。1488年市民起兵反抗苏尼加家族，费尔南多于10月20日在主教座堂门前确认城市特权。退位的查理五世1557年退居拉贝拉山区的耶罗尼姆派尤斯特修道院，1558年9月21日在那里去世。1653年埃斯特雷马杜拉设省，普拉森西亚出资为其购得议会席位。法军1808年12月28日攻占该城，半岛战争中十二次占领此地，1809年焚毁尤斯特修道院。

en:
Segovia perches on a rocky ridge above the Eresma, with its alcázar at one end and the Roman aqueduct crossing the Plaza del Azoguejo at the other. The aqueduct was built late in the first century AD and runs for over 800 metres on 167 arches of granite blocks laid without mortar, the tallest arcade nearly 29 metres high, carrying water from springs 17 kilometres away in the Sierra de Guadarrama. Local legend says a girl tired of climbing the hill for water bargained with the Devil, who promised to finish the bridge before the cock crowed in exchange for her soul; one stone was still missing at cockcrow, and the gap later held a statue of the Virgin. The Moors destroyed 36 arches in 1072, and they were rebuilt under the Catholic Monarchs by Pedro Mesa, prior of the Jerónimos del Parral. After Alfonso VI took Toledo, Raymond of Burgundy and Bishop Pedro de Agén brought settlers from northern Spain and beyond the Pyrenees from 1088. On the transhumance roads the town grew rich on wool and its segovienne flannel, with a large Jewish quarter and an alcázar favoured by Alfonso X and Henry IV. In 1444 Segovia was one of the wealthiest towns in Castile.

On 13 December 1474, after Henry IV's death, Isabella was proclaimed queen of Castile in the church of San Miguel. In 1520 the town joined the Comuneros under Juan Bravo, head of its militia, while a royalist garrison held the alcázar throughout the revolt. Bravo was captured at Villalar and beheaded there on 24 April 1521 with Padilla and Maldonado; when his body was brought back to Segovia in June, his funeral nearly turned into a rising. The late-Gothic cathedral, one of Europe's last great Gothic churches, went up in those years, and the town held about 27,000 people by 1594 before plague carried off some 12,000 in 1599; by 1694 only 8,000 remained. In June 1706 the council bowed to an imperial army and recognized the Habsburg claimant, but a popular rising declared for Philip V on 31 July and the Portuguese garrison in the alcázar surrendered three days later. Spain's first military academy, the Royal School of Artillery, opened in 1764, and French troops occupied the town from December 1808 to May 1813.
zh:
塞哥维亚坐落在埃雷斯马河上方的岩脊上，岩脊一端是王宫，另一端的阿索格霍广场上横跨着罗马高架渠。高架渠建于1世纪末，全长逾800米，由167道无灰浆砌筑的花岗岩拱券组成，最高处近29米，把17公里外瓜达拉马山的泉水引入城中。相传有个厌倦了天天背水上山的姑娘和魔鬼做交易：魔鬼答应鸡鸣前架好水渠，代价是她的灵魂；鸡鸣时还差一块石头没有放上，姑娘保住了灵魂，那个缺口后来安放了圣母像。1072年穆斯林摧毁了36道拱券，天主教双王时代由帕拉尔修道院的佩德罗·梅萨院长主持重建。1085年阿方索六世攻占托莱多后，勃艮第的雷蒙和主教佩德罗·德·阿亨自1088年起从西班牙北方和比利牛斯山以北招募移民。扼守转场牧道的塞哥维亚靠羊毛和本地的塞哥维亚法兰绒致富，犹太社区规模庞大，王宫则是阿方索十世和恩里克四世喜爱的驻跸之地。1444年的塞哥维亚是卡斯蒂利亚最富庶的城镇之一。

1474年12月13日，恩里克四世去世后，伊莎贝尔在圣米格尔教堂被拥立为卡斯蒂利亚女王。1520年，城市在民兵统领胡安·布拉沃带领下加入公社起义，而保王派守军在整个起义期间一直占据着王宫。布拉沃在比利亚拉尔被俘，1521年4月24日与帕迪利亚、马尔多纳多一同被斩首；6月他的遗体运回塞哥维亚，葬礼险些演成民变。晚期哥特式大教堂在这些年间动工，是欧洲最后一批建成的宏伟哥特教堂之一。到1594年全城约有27000人，1599年瘟疫又夺去约12000人的性命，到1694年只剩8000人。1706年6月，市政会迫于帝国大军承认哈布斯堡家族的觊觎者，但民众起事，于7月31日宣布拥戴费利佩五世，王宫里的葡萄牙驻军三天后投降。西班牙第一所军事学院皇家炮兵学校于1764年开学，1808年12月至1813年5月塞哥维亚被法军占领。

en:
The southern flank of the Parahyangan highlands falls steeply to the Indian Ocean, where forested headlands frame a horseshoe bay of rough surf, later marked on Dutch charts as Wijnkoopsbaai. Sundanese farmers cut wet-rice terraces into the mountain slopes. The high country was holy ground in the old Sunda faith, the abode of the hyangs, and the southern ocean was held to be the realm of the sea queen Nyai Loro Kidul. In 1444 these rainy southern reaches were outlands of the Hindu Sunda kingdom of Pajajaran, governed through local lords, and such trade as there was went out through the northern port of Kalapa.

After Banten sacked Pakuan in 1579 the sultan's writ ran weakly this far south, and the upland lords of Cianjur, Sumedang and Ciamis, who claimed descent from King Siliwangi, largely did as they pleased. Sultan Agung of Mataram ended that independence when he conquered Sumedang in 1618, and after revolts he deported much of the highland population in 1630. The south coast remained unknown to Europeans until 1687, when a VOC expedition under Pieter Scipio van Oostende crossed the wilderness from Batavia, passed the ruins of Pakuan and reached the bay. Under the treaty made with Banten in 1684 the Priangan, as the Dutch called the highlands, came under the Company, whose planters turned its cool hills into coffee gardens early in the eighteenth century; Preanger coffee became the most prized crop shipped out of Java.
zh:
勃良安高地的南坡陡峭直落入印度洋，林木掩映的海岬环抱着一道浪涛险恶的马蹄形海湾，荷兰海图后来把它标作韦恩库普斯拜。巽他农人在山坡上开出层层水田。在巽他古老信仰中，高地是神灵栖居的圣地，南方大洋则被视为南海女王（Nyai Loro Kidul）的领域。1444年时，这片多雨的南边之地是印度教巽他王国帕查查兰的边远疆土，由地方头人治理，少量贸易都经北方的港口格拉巴出入。

1579年万丹洗劫帕库安之后，苏丹的号令到不了这么远的南方，展玉、双木丹、尖米士的山地王公自称承续西里旺义王的血脉，大半自行其是。1618年，马打蓝苏丹阿贡攻灭双木丹，终结了他们的独立；平定叛乱后，他又在1630年强迁了大批高地居民。南海岸长期不为欧洲人所知，直到1687年，彼得·斯基皮奥·范·奥斯滕德率荷兰东印度公司考察队从巴达维亚穿越荒野，经过帕库安废墟抵达这道海湾。依据1684年与万丹签订的条约，被荷兰人称作普里安的勃良安归入公司治下；18世纪初，种植园主把凉爽的丘陵开辟成咖啡园，普里安咖啡成为从爪哇外运的最受珍视的物产。

en:
Cirebon sits on the Java Sea plain beneath Mount Ceremai, where the shipping lanes of Sundanese and Javanese Java meet. Its fifteenth-century harbor was Muara Jati, a fishing village turned port under Galuh's loose hand; the port master Ki Gedeng Alang-Alang moved the settlers south to Lemahwungkuk and took the title Kuwu Cerbon. The name comes from cai rebon, the water left from boiling the tiny rebon shrimp for shrimp paste, and the town lived by fish, paste, petis and salt. Javanese, Sundanese, Chinese and Arab settlers crowded in, and a Pajajaran prince, Walangsungsang, had become a Muslim under Sheikh Datuk Kahfi. In 1444 Cirebon still sent tribute to the Hindu court at Kawali, but its coast was already passing into Muslim hands.

Walangsungsang, titled Cakrabuana, stopped the tribute and built his court at Pakungwati, on the site of the later Kasepuhan kraton. The court became an Islamic sultanate under his nephew Syarif Hidayatullah, the Sunan Gunungjati (1448-1568), son of a Champa sultan and a Pajajaran princess and one of the nine saints, the Wali Songo, who carried Islam across Java. In 1480 he founded the Great Mosque Sang Cipta Rasa, and Cirebon tradition gives him a Chinese bride, Ong Tien Nio, said to be a Ming princess; his tomb at Gunung Sembung draws Muslim pilgrims. A Portuguese-Sundanese treaty signed at Sunda Kelapa in 1522 was meant to hold Demak in check, yet in 1527 Cirebonese and Demak troops under Fatahillah seized that same harbor and named it Jayakarta, the future Jakarta. Cirebon's ships exported teak, rice, sugar and pepper. When Panembahan Ratu II died a captive in Mataram in 1677, his sons divided the realm into the Kasepuhan, Kanoman and minor courts, and on 7 January 1681 their rulers signed the treaty that made Cirebon a Dutch East India Company protectorate. The courts kept their Chinese-porcelain pavilions and the nearby Sunyaragi water caves through 1821.
zh:
井里汶位于泽雷迈山以北的爪哇海沿海平原，爪哇岛巽他一侧与爪哇一侧的海路在此相接。15世纪时，这里的穆阿拉贾蒂先是渔村，后成港口，只在名义上受加卢约束；港务长基·格登·阿朗阿朗把居民南迁到勒马旺库，自称库武·切尔邦。井里汶之名来自「采雷邦」，即煮雷邦小虾制虾酱时剩下的水，当地人以鱼、虾酱、虾膏和盐为业，爪哇人、巽他人、华人和阿拉伯人聚居于此；帕查查兰王子瓦朗松桑已随谢赫·达图克·卡赫菲皈依伊斯兰教。1444年，井里汶仍向卡瓦利的印度教宫廷纳贡，但这段海岸已经在转入穆斯林之手。

瓦朗松桑后称查克拉布阿纳，停止纳贡，在帕贡瓦蒂建立宫廷，即后来卡塞普汉王宫的所在。宫廷在他的外甥沙里夫·希达亚图拉治下成为伊斯兰苏丹国，他就是苏南·古农·查提（1448—1568）：父亲是占婆苏丹，母亲是帕查查兰公主，他本人是向全爪哇传播伊斯兰教的九圣瓦利松戈之一。1480年，他创建桑吉普塔·罗萨大清真寺；井里汶传说还称他娶了中国女子翁天娘（Ong Tien Nio），说是明朝公主；他在古农松姆邦的陵墓朝觐者络绎不绝。1522年葡萄牙与巽他在巽他格拉巴签约，意在遏制淡目，但1527年法塔希拉就率井里汶与淡目军队夺取同一港口，改名查雅卡尔塔，即雅加达的前身。井里汶的海船输出柚木、稻米、蔗糖和胡椒。帕能巴罕·拉图二世1677年死于马打兰拘押后，诸子把国家分为卡塞普汉、卡诺曼等宫廷，1681年1月7日各方签约，井里汶成为荷兰东印度公司的保护国。这些宫廷保留着嵌满中国瓷盘的殿宇和附近的苏尼亚拉吉水洞，一直延续到1821年。

en:
Kendal lies on Java's north coast between Pekalongan and Semarang, a flat shore of fishing villages and rice fields with wooded hills behind. In 1444 its villages still answered to Majapahit and sent rice and fish along the coastal trade, but the empire's hold on the Pasisir was loosening and Muslim merchants and preachers had settled in the ports on either side. Demak brought the coast under its rule around the turn of the century, and under Sultan Trenggana, from 1521, Kendal became one of the earliest seats of Javanese Islam; the teachers' quarter at Kaliwungu took shape in those years, and the shrine of Sunan Katong there drew pilgrims.

The district remembers the Mataram commander it sent to the first great siege of Batavia. On 28 July 1605 the court appointed Joko Bahu, with the title Tumenggung Bahurekso, as Kendal's first regent, and under Sultan Agung he commanded Mataram's armies; on 26 August 1628 he led tens of thousands of troops against the VOC in Batavia and was killed there on 21 October with his two sons. Kaliwungu was the regency's first seat before the regent moved to the town of Kendal. The Chinese-Javanese rising of 1741 against the Dutch reached Kaliwungu, and the treaty that ended the war in 1743 transferred the whole north coast, Kendal included, from Mataram to the Company.
zh:
肯德尔位于爪哇北海岸，在北加浪岸与三宝垄之间，沿岸是渔村与稻田，背后是林木覆盖的丘陵。1444年时，这里的村落仍臣属满者伯夷，沿近岸航路运出稻米与渔获，但帝国对北海岸的控制正在松动，穆斯林商人与教士已定居在东西两面的港口。15世纪末淡目兴起，将这片海岸纳入版图；自1521年特林加纳苏丹在位时起，肯德尔成为爪哇伊斯兰教最早扎根的地方之一，卡利翁古的经师聚居区在那些年成形，当地苏南·卡通的陵墓也引来朝圣者。

这片地方最记得的，是它送出去攻打巴达维亚的那位马打兰统帅。1605年7月28日，宫廷任命佐科·巴胡为首任肯德尔县长，封号图孟贡·巴胡雷克索；苏丹阿贡时，他升任马打兰军队统帅，1628年8月26日率数万大军进攻巴达维亚的荷兰东印度公司，10月21日与两个儿子一同战死城下。卡利翁古本是该县最初的治所，后来县长才移驻肯德尔镇。1741年反抗荷兰人的华人与爪哇人起事波及卡利翁古；结束战争的1743年条约把整个北海岸连同肯德尔一起，从马打兰划归荷兰东印度公司。

en:
Pajang was an inland rice district of Central Java, around Boyolali, Klaten and Salatiga, the country later Javanese chronicles call Pengging. The Nagarakretagama of 1365 already lists it as a Majapahit appanage: Dyah Nertaja, sister of King Hayam Wuruk, ruled it with the title Bhre Pajang. In 1444 its rice villages still lay inside the crumbling Majapahit order, while wealth and Islam were moving to the trading ports on Java's northern coast.

Pajang became a kingdom through Jaka Tingkir, better known as Adiwijaya. His father Ki Ageng Pengging had been executed by Demak, yet the young man served Sultan Trenggana so well in the field that he became the sultan's son-in-law and regent of Pajang. After Trenggana died in 1546 and Sunan Prawata was murdered by his cousin Arya Penangsang of Jipang, Adiwijaya defeated the claimant with help from Ratu Kalinyamat, queen of Jepara, and from his vassals Ki Ageng Pamanahan and Sutawijaya, and made Pajang the inland successor to Demak. He rewarded father and son with the forest of Alas Mentaok, where they cleared the ground for Kotagede, the future seat of Mataram; Javanese tradition adds that he raised Sutawijaya at court as his own heir's companion. When Adiwijaya died in 1582 his heir Prince Benawa was driven out by the rebel Ario Pangiri and took shelter with Sutawijaya. Sutawijaya defeated Pangiri, Benawa submitted his crown in 1586, and the new ruler took the title Panembahan Senopati. Pajang rose against Mataram in 1617 and was put down. After the Trunajaya war Mataram moved its court to Kartasura, in Pajang, in 1680; the palace burned in the Chinese-Javanese war of 1743, and the Treaty of Giyanti partitioned Mataram in 1755.
zh:
帕章是爪哇中部的内陆稻米地区，在博约拉利、克拉滕和沙拉笛加一带，后世爪哇编年史称这片地方为彭京。1365年的《爪哇史颂》已把它列为满者伯夷的封邑：国王哈奄·武禄的妹妹迪娅·内尔塔查以「帕章布雷」之衔统治此地。1444年，这里的稻作村落仍处在日趋瓦解的满者伯夷秩序中，而财富和伊斯兰教正转向爪哇北岸的贸易港口。

帕章成为一个王国，靠的是贾卡·廷基尔，即后来的阿迪维查亚。他的父亲基·阿贡·彭京被淡目处死，他却凭战功成为苏丹特伦加纳的女婿，受封帕章摄政。特伦加纳1546年去世、苏南·普拉瓦塔被堂兄吉庞的阿里亚·彭昂桑杀害后，阿迪维查亚在哲帕拉女王加理雅末、家臣基·阿贡·帕马纳汉和苏塔维查亚的帮助下击杀彭昂桑，使帕章在内陆继承了淡目的权位。他把阿拉斯·门塔奥克森林封给帕马纳汉父子，二人在那里辟出科特格德，即后来马打兰的根基之地；爪哇相传，阿迪维查亚十分喜爱苏塔维查亚，把他养在宫中与王子贝纳瓦作伴。阿迪维查亚1582年去世后，继承人贝纳瓦王子被叛臣阿里奥·潘吉里逐出，投奔苏塔维查亚。苏塔维查亚击败潘吉里，贝纳瓦于1586年献出王冠，新君上号帕能巴罕·森纳帕提。帕章1617年起兵反抗马打兰，被镇压下去。杜鲁诺佐约战争后，马打兰于1680年把宫廷迁至帕章境内的卡尔塔苏拉；王宫在1743年华人与爪哇人的战火中焚毁，1755年的《吉安蒂条约》瓜分了马打兰。

en:
The Malang basin is a cool highland ringed by volcanoes at the headwaters of the Brantas, old country long before Majapahit: the Kanjuruhan kings ruled it in the eighth century, and in 1222 Ken Arok rose at Tumapel, north of the later city, to found the Singhasari empire. Javanese tradition, in the Pararaton, sets a famous scene at the Watugede spring near Tumapel, where Ken Arok saw light radiating from Ken Dedes as she bathed and knew her for a woman of destiny; the dynasty he founded made the valley royal ground. Above its wet-rice terraces stand the temples of his line, Kidal for King Anusapati, Jago for Wisnuwardhana and Singhasari for Kertanegara, and Hayam Wuruk of Majapahit came on pilgrimage to them in 1359. In 1444 Tumapel was a crown province of Majapahit, governed by a bhre prince under Queen Suhita, a quiet Hindu-Javanese interior of temples, rice fields and mountain streams.

When Demak stormed Daha in 1527 a son of the last Majapahit king, Raden Pramana, fled into the southern mountains, where the lord Arya Terung set up a Hindu realm at Sengguruh. Its attack on Gresik in 1535 failed, and Arya Terung turned to Islam; when partisans of the old court rose against him, Sultan Trenggana of Demak marched in and crushed them in 1545, and Pramana fled on to Blambangan. The Javanese called the ruined country Kutho Bedah, the Broken City. Sultan Agung of Mataram conquered it in 1614 against stiff local resistance, and with the treaty of 1743 Mataram ceded its claims over the Oosthoek and the old Singhasari country passed under the Company's rule.
zh:
玛琅盆地是一处群山环峙的凉爽高地，正当布兰塔斯河的源头，在满者伯夷之前很久便已是古老之地：8世纪甘朱尔汉诸王立国于此，1222年肯·阿罗克又在后来玛琅城以北的图马佩尔崛起，建立信诃沙里帝国。爪哇古书《君王传》（Pararaton）在图马佩尔附近的瓦图格德泉边记下有名的一幕：肯·阿罗克看见正在沐浴的肯·德德斯身上放出光芒，知道她是身负天命的女子；他所建立的王朝也使这片河谷成为王土。稻梯田上方矗立着这个王朝的庙宇：奉祀阿努沙巴迪王的基达尔寺、奉祀威斯努瓦尔达纳王的查戈寺，以及奉祀克尔塔纳加腊王的信诃沙里寺，1359年满者伯夷的哈奄·武禄还曾前来拜谒。1444年时，图马佩尔是满者伯夷的直隶省，由女王苏希塔治下的一位「巴莱」（亲王）统辖，是一片宁静的印度教爪哇腹地，寺院、水田与山溪错落其间。

1527年淡目攻破达哈，末代满者伯夷国王之子拉登·普拉马纳逃入南部群山，首领阿里亚·特龙在此建立印度教政权森古鲁。1535年森古鲁进攻锦石失败，阿里亚·特龙改宗伊斯兰教；旧朝党羽起兵反对他时，淡目的特林卡纳苏丹于1545年进军镇压，普拉马纳再逃往布兰邦岸。爪哇人把这片残破之地称为「库托·贝达」，意为「破城」。1614年，马打兰的苏丹阿贡在当地人顽强抵抗下将其征服；1743年的条约中，马打兰割让了对东角的权利，这片信诃沙里旧土遂转入荷兰东印度公司治下。

en:
Bone faces the Gulf of Bone on the eastern side of South Sulawesi, a land of wet-rice plains and fishing ports centred on Watampone. Its people are the Bugis. The Bone chronicle makes Manurung ri Matajang the founder who united seven village communities in the early fourteenth century, and by the time of La Umasa, early in the fifteenth, the realm still amounted to little more than a ring of settlements around Watampone. In 1444 Bone was an adat kingdom of farmers and traders who honoured ancestor spirits, overshadowed by Gowa-Tallo, the twin Makassarese kingdom near Makassar, and by Luwu to the north.

Bone's first wars pushed north against Luwu for the mouth of the Cenrana River, the outlet of the east-coast trade. In 1582 its rulers buried stones with Wajo and Soppeng at Timurung, swearing the Tellumpocco'e pact of the Three Summits against Gowa-Tallo. Muslim teachers had reached Bone by 1605, and the Gowa invasion of 1611 forced its court to accept Islam. The prince who raised Bone above all its neighbours was La Tenritatta, called Arung Palakka. Born about 1634, he rose against Gowa and sailed with Cornelis Speelman's VOC fleet; his summons brought the Bugis of Bone and Soppeng into the Makassar War of 1666-1669. In June 1669 he led the final assault on Fort Somba Opu, Gowa's citadel outside Makassar. Mines opened a breach in the wall, and after six days of rain his Bugis charged through it and took the fort. The Treaty of Bungaya left Bone the overlord of South Sulawesi. Palakka ruled Bone as its sultan from 1672 until his death in 1696, and under him and his successors the Bugis became a maritime power whose traders and soldiers ranged across the archipelago for nearly a century. Bone kept that supremacy until the British took the region in 1814; the Dutch returned in 1816 and set about reducing the kingdom from ally to vassal.
zh:
波尼临南苏拉威西东侧的波尼湾，是以瓦坦波尼为中心的水稻平原与渔港之境，居民为布吉人。波尼编年史把马努隆·里·马塔姜奉为建国者，称他在14世纪初联合七个村落社群；到15世纪初拉·乌马萨之时，波尼仍不过是瓦坦波尼周围一圈聚落。1444年，波尼是依风俗法治理的农民和商人之国，敬奉祖先神灵，西面受望加锡附近的戈瓦-塔洛孪生王国压制，北面则有卢武。

波尼最早的战事是向北攻打卢武，争夺东海岸贸易的出口森拉纳河口。1582年，波尼统治者与瓦久、索彭在蒂穆隆埋石为誓，订立共抗戈瓦-塔洛的「三峰」特伦波科埃之约。到1605年，穆斯林教师已进入波尼，1611年戈瓦入侵，宫廷被迫接受伊斯兰教。把波尼抬到诸邻之上的王子是拉·滕里塔塔，人称阿隆·帕拉卡。他约1634年出生，起兵反抗戈瓦，随科内利斯·斯皮尔曼的荷兰东印度公司舰队出海；他一召唤，波尼和索彭的布吉人便投入1666年至1669年的望加锡战争。1669年6月，他指挥了对戈瓦在望加锡城外的核心堡垒松巴乌普的最后强攻。地雷在墙上炸开缺口，连雨六天后，他的布吉兵冲入缺口夺下堡垒。依《邦加亚条约》，波尼成为南苏拉威西的宗主。帕拉卡1672年成为波尼苏丹，统治至1696年去世；在他和后继者手中，布吉人成为一大海上势力，商人和士兵纵横群岛近百年。波尼的优势维持到1814年英国人夺取该地区；荷兰人1816年返回，着手把这个王国从盟友降为附庸。

en:
Kendari occupies a sheltered deepwater bay on Sulawesi's southeastern arm. The shore villages belonged to Konawe, a Tolaki kingdom whose mokole ruled from inland Unaaha. Farmers raised rice and cempedak, herders kept buffalo, and boats fished the bay. Custom turned on the Kalo Sara, three rattan pieces laid on a white cloth to express kinship, law and good conduct. Portuguese charts later marked the anchorage as the City of the Bay and called the water Tivora Bay. In 1444 the people around Kendari still followed animist and dynamist rites.

Bugis merchants from Makassar and trade with nearby Buton brought Islam to the coast in the fifteenth century, but Konawe's court changed only under Lakidende. After studying the faith in Bone, he reigned from 1724 to 1786, forbade pork, required mosques and Muslim marriages, and reinterpreted the Kalo Sara within Islamic teaching. Javanese, Makassarese and Moluccan traders then settled along the shore. Succession quarrels weakened Konawe after his long reign, though in 1821 the bay still had no European fort or trading post.
zh:
肯达里坐落在苏拉威西东南半岛一处隐蔽的深水湾畔。沿岸村庄属于托拉基人的科纳韦王国，国王称「莫科莱」，驻地在腹地的乌纳阿哈。居民种植水稻和小菠萝蜜、牧养水牛，也在海湾捕鱼。当地习惯法以「卡洛萨拉」为标志，把三段藤条放在白布上，表示亲属关系、法律和善行。后来的葡萄牙海图把这处锚地标作「海湾之城」，又称这片水域为蒂沃拉湾。1444年，肯达里一带的人仍奉行泛灵论和物力论仪式。

15世纪，望加锡的布吉商人以及同邻近布顿的贸易把伊斯兰教带到海岸，但科纳韦宫廷要到拉基登德时才改宗。他曾在波尼学习教义，1724年至1786年在位期间禁食猪肉，要求修建清真寺、按伊斯兰教法成婚，又把「卡洛萨拉」纳入伊斯兰教义解释。爪哇、望加锡和摩鹿加商人随后到岸边定居。他长期统治之后，继承纷争削弱了科纳韦；到1821年，海湾边仍没有欧洲人的堡垒或商站。

en:
Soppeng lies inland from Makassar, up the Walanae River in wet-rice country that runs north toward Lake Tempe; its chief town is Watansoppeng. Early Bugis Soppeng was sixty village communities, each following its own matoa leader under loose custom, and for a time they were subject to Luwu. A revolt around 1300 produced two separate realms, Soppeng Riaja and Soppeng Rilauq, with rulers seated at Tinco, and the two stayed apart through the fifteenth century. In 1444 this was an animist rice-growing Bugis land, not the single sultanate later centred on Watansoppeng.

The two realms were joined only around 1550. In December 1582 Soppeng stood with Bone and Wajo at Timurung, burying stones in the Tellumpocco'e pact against Gowa-Tallo, and in the wars that followed it took Lamuru and shared control of Cenrana. The preacher Sheikh Abdul Madjid arrived in 1606, but Islam came with conquest as well as teaching. After Soppeng rejected Gowa's call to convert, Watansoppeng fell in October 1609 and its ruler submitted as a Muslim vassal. The Atappang raft agreement of 1660 bound Soppeng to Bone and Arung Palakka; Gowa exiled the Datu La Tenribali that December, yet Soppeng troops fought through the entire Makassar War. When Fort Somba Opu fell in June 1669, among the last people left in the citadel's mosque were the Malay wife of the Datu of Soppeng, her children and eighty of her retinue. Soppeng renewed the old alliance in 1708.
zh:
索彭在望加锡内陆，溯瓦拉奈河而上，是向北通往坦佩湖的水稻之乡，重镇是瓦坦索彭。早期布吉人的索彭是六十个村落社群，各推马托阿首领，靠松散的风俗维系，一度臣属于卢武。约1300年的一场反抗催生了两个分立的政权：索彭里阿查和索彭里劳，统治者驻在廷科，整个15世纪两地都未合并。1444年的索彭是布吉人种稻的泛灵之地，还不是后来以瓦坦索彭为中心的统一苏丹国。

两地约1550年才合为一体。1582年12月，索彭与波尼、瓦久会于蒂穆隆，埋石订立共抗戈瓦-塔洛的特伦波科埃之约；此后的战事中，索彭攻取拉穆鲁，并与盟国分掌森拉纳。讲经师谢赫·阿卜杜勒·马吉德1606年抵达，但伊斯兰教既随教义而来，也随征服而至。索彭拒绝戈瓦的改宗号召后，瓦坦索彭于1609年10月陷落，统治者成为穆斯林附庸。1660年的阿塔庞木筏之约把索彭绑在波尼和阿隆·帕拉卡一边；同年12月戈瓦流放了达图·拉·滕里巴利，索彭军队却打满了整场望加锡战争。1669年6月松巴乌普陷落时，堡垒清真寺里留下的最后一批人，正是索彭达图的马来妻子、她的孩子和八十名随从。旧盟1708年续订。

en:
Wajoq occupied the eastern shore of Lake Tempe, on the route from the south Sulawesi lakes to the sea at the Cenrana river. The Wajo chronicle makes a hunting Bugis noble its founder, who found wide rice fields, game-filled forests and fish-crowded lakes and settled his followers at Cinnotabiq. Its name is said to come from the bajoq tree where the ruler La Tenribali bargained with the three chiefs of Boliq. Its kings first bore the title batara; after the third was driven out and killed by his own people, notables chose each ruler as arung matoa, 'senior lord'. In 1444 it was an animist rice country of wet fields and lake boats, overshadowed by Luwu, master of the lakes and the northern coast.

Under its fourth arung matoa, La Tadampareq (r. c.1491-1521), Wajoq helped Luwu defeat Sidenreng, absorbed the remnants of Cina and joined the major Bugis states. In 1582 Bone drew Wajoq and Soppeng into the Treaty of Timurung: the three called one another brothers, Bone the elder, and the Tellumpocco ('Three Peaks') beat back every Gowa attack of that decade. Gowa returned stronger, and in 1610 Wajoq accepted Islam, handed its foreign affairs to Makassar and kept its home rule. Wajoq held to that loyalty through the Makassar War of 1666-1669 and fought on after Gowa surrendered, until Arung Palakka's Bone-led troops stormed walled Tosora in December 1670 and killed the arung matoa La Tenrilai To Sengngeng. The peace limited Wajorese arms and trade, and Bone took the Cenrana mouth, its only outlet to the sea. Wajorese merchants then scattered to Makassar, Borneo, the Lesser Sundas and the Strait of Malacca, their houses abroad tied by family and trade to the homeland.

Later rulers used those ties to rearm. La Tenriwerrung taught that Wajorese 'could not stand upright' without riches; La Salewangeng (r. 1713-1736) dredged the river to Tosora, created a trade office and funded commerce and farming from a public purse. In 1736 La Maddukelleng, back from exile, took power, defeated Bone and by mid-1737 led the Three Peaks from Wajoq. Diaspora merchants kept it prosperous and independent for the rest of the century.
zh:
瓦久地处坦佩湖东岸，南苏拉威西湖泊的水经森拉纳河排入大海。《瓦久通史》把开国溯源记成这样：一位布吉贵族出猎时，见到连片的稻田、满是猎物的森林和盛产鱼的湖泊，便率随从在钦诺塔比克定居；相传国名来自一棵巴乔克树，首领拉·滕里巴利就在树下与博利克三部首领立约。早期君主称巴塔拉，第三代巴塔拉被国人驱逐后杀死，此后君主由贵族议事会选立，称号阿隆·马托阿，意为「年长之主」。1444年的瓦久是稻田与湖船之地，信奉泛灵，仍处在湖泊与北海岸强权卢武的威势之下。

第四任阿隆·马托阿拉·塔丹帕雷克（约1491年至1521年在位）时，瓦久与卢武联手击败西登伦，吸收奇纳残余，跻身布吉主要政权。1582年，波尼促成瓦久与索彭签订蒂穆隆盟约：三国以兄弟相称，波尼为长，号称「三峰」的同盟击退了戈瓦在这十年间的历次进攻。17世纪初戈瓦卷土重来，1610年瓦久接受伊斯兰教，外交权交给望加锡，内政仍由自己掌管。1666年至1669年望加锡战争中，瓦久忠于戈瓦，甚至在戈瓦投降后继续作战，直到1670年12月阿隆·帕拉卡率领的波尼联军攻陷有城墙的都城托索拉，阿隆·马托阿拉·滕里莱·托·森恩根战死。胜利者限制瓦久的军备与贸易，波尼还夺走瓦久唯一的出海口森拉纳河口。瓦久商人此后散居望加锡、婆罗洲、小巽他和马六甲海峡，海外商馆与故土保持着家族和生意上的联系。

18世纪的历任君主靠这些海外联系重整武备。拉·滕里韦伦主张，瓦久人不寻求财富就「站不直腰」；拉·萨莱旺恩（1713年至1736年在位）疏浚通往托索拉的河道以便海船通行，又设置贸易官职，用公共基金资助商贸和农耕。1736年，流亡归来的冒险家拉·马杜克伦掌权，击败波尼，到1737年中使瓦久成为三峰之首。整个18世纪后半叶，离散商人维持着这个选举制小国的富足与自主。

en: Sangkulirang is the bay where the Karangan River breaks through a mangrove coast at the southern foot of the Mangkalihat Peninsula. Behind the shore stand the steep limestone cliffs and caves of the Sangkulirang-Mangkalihat karst, where the Basap Dayak hunted, worked small forest plots and moved from river to river. Berau tradition fixed Tanjung Mangkaliat as the limit of its coastal mandala and the border with Kutai; in 1444 the southern shore was therefore Kutai's exposed northeastern edge, ruled from the Mahakam court under Hindu titles while the inland Basap kept their own rites. The court's conversion in 1575 and the absorption of Martapura in 1635 carried Muslim trade and teaching farther along this coast, and when Berau split into Gunung Tabur and Sambaliung around 1810 the bay became a quiet border between Sambaliung and the Kutai sultanate, its people living still by fish, boats and forest produce.
zh: 桑库利朗是卡兰甘河在孟卡利哈特半岛南缘穿过红树林海岸注入的海湾。岸后矗立着桑库利朗—孟卡利哈特喀斯特的石灰岩陡崖与洞穴，巴刹夫达雅克人在此狩猎、经营小片林地、沿河迁徙。伯劳传统把丹戎孟卡利亚特定为其沿海势力圈的尽头、与古泰的分界；因此1444年时，这片南岸是古泰面向东北的边境，马哈坎宫廷以印度教尊号遥领，内陆的巴刹夫人则保留自有仪礼。1575年宫廷改宗、1635年吞并马尔塔普拉后，穆斯林贸易与传道沿海岸进一步传入；约1810年伯劳分裂为古农塔布尔和桑巴利昂，海湾成为桑巴利昂与古泰苏丹国之间平静的边地，居民仍以捕鱼、舟船和林产为生。

en:
Paser faces the Makassar Strait on Borneo's south-eastern coast, where the Kendilo and Telake rivers run out of forested hills past Mount Lumut, a mountain held sacred by the Paser people, and cut through a low, muddy shore. The Javanese court poem Nagarakertagama named Pasir among the trading lands tributary to Majapahit in 1365, and Malay and Bugis sailors logged the anchorage on their charts as Passir, Passeir or Pasir. In 1444 the river mouths were the country of the Paser Dayaks, fishermen and collectors of forest and sea produce which they carried south by prau to Banjarmasin. No royal court is recorded there in these years, and the coast stood on the edge of the Banjar world.

The river settlements united in 1516 under a woman ruler, Ratu Aji Putri Petong, who founded the kingdom of Sadurengas. Islam reached the court with the Kendilo river trade and with her husband Abu Mansyur Indra Jaya, leader of an Islamic mission from Giri in Java, and in time the rulers took the title of sultan as the Sultanate of Paser Darul Aman. Banjar counted Pasir among its tributary coasts, and Dutch treaties wrote it into 'Greater Banjar'. Its Bugis ties later brought Paser an unusual ruler. La Maddukelleng, the warlike raja of Wajo in Sulawesi, married a Paser princess, and when her claim to the throne was rejected he conquered the kingdom and reigned over it from 1726 to 1736, before sailing back to Sulawesi with war fleets from Kutai, Pagatan and Johor to make war on Bone and the VOC. Paser was also dragged into Banjar's succession wars: in 1757 the fugitive Prince Amir raised a Bugis and Paser force here through his uncle Arung Tarawe and marched on Banjarmasin, until VOC troops broke the invasion. In 1817 the Sultan of Banjar ceded Pasir to the Netherlands in the Treaty of Karang Intan.
zh:
巴塞尔（Pasir，海图上又拼作Passir、Passeir）位于婆罗洲东南海岸，面朝望加锡海峡；肯迪洛河与特拉克河自林木覆盖的丘陵流出，途经巴塞尔人尊为圣山的卢穆特山，在低平多泥的海岸入海。爪哇宫廷史诗《爪哇史颂》在1365年已把帕塞尔列入向满者伯夷朝贡的通商之地，马来和布吉水手也在海图上把这片锚地标作Passir或Pasir。1444年时，各河口是巴塞尔达雅克人的地方，百姓打鱼、采集海产与林产，用帆船南运马辰；此时还没有留下名号的王庭，海岸处在班贾尔世界的边缘。

1516年，沿河诸部在一位女王治下统一，拉杜·阿吉·普特里·佩东建立萨杜伦加斯王国。伊斯兰教随肯迪洛河的商路而来，也随她的丈夫、自爪哇吉里率领传教团前来的阿布·曼苏尔·因德拉·查亚进入宫廷，后来的统治者改称苏丹，是为帕塞尔达尔阿曼苏丹国。班贾尔把帕塞尔列为称臣的海岸，荷兰人与班贾尔订约时也把它写入「大班贾尔」。与布吉人的渊源还给帕塞尔带来一位奇特的君主：苏拉威西瓦乔的好战王公拉·马杜克伦（La Maddukelleng）娶了帕塞尔公主，她的王位诉求遭拒后，他起兵攻下帕塞尔，在1726至1736年为其国王；随后他率库泰、帕加坦和柔佛相助的战船返回苏拉威西，进攻波尼与荷兰东印度公司。帕塞尔还被卷入班贾尔的继承战争：1757年，亡命的阿米尔王子经舅父阿隆·塔拉韦在此召集布吉与帕塞尔联军，回攻马辰，被荷兰东印度公司军队击溃。1817年，班贾尔苏丹在卡朗因坦条约中把帕塞尔割让给荷兰。

en:
Batulican lies on the south-eastern shoulder of Borneo, where the Batulicin, Cantung and Bangkalaan run short courses out of forested hills into the Makassar Strait. In 1444 these river mouths were the country of the Bangkalaan Dayaks, fishermen and cave collectors whose most valued harvest was the swiftlet nest taken from the limestone Gua Temualuang; the cave also supplied the water used in their chiefs' rites. Village traders carried cave harvests and forest produce by prau on the long coastal run west to Banjarmasin. The shore had no king's court of its own in these years and stood on the edge of the Banjar world.

In the seventeenth century the coast received a dynasty. Raiders from the sea had sacked Pamukan at the Cengal river mouth, and the local Dayaks asked Banjarmasin for help; Dipati Tuha, a son of Sultan Saidullah of Banjar, came overland with his following, settled on the Bumbu river and founded the vassal kingdom of Tanah Bumbu, which ruled the five streams of the shore from Batu Licin to Bangkalaan. One of its chiefs, Raja Batu Ganting, accepted Islam and his people became known as the Bangkalaan Malays, while Gua Temualuang was left to Dayaks who kept the old rites. Bugis settlers followed. Puana Dekke, a rich trader from Wajo in Sulawesi, coasted past Paser without finding ground that suited him and, with the Banjar sultan's leave, opened a Bugis settlement at Pagatan in the neighbouring Kusan country. His commander La Pangewa cleared the coast of the pretender Amir's Bugis and Paser forces, and around 1784 was installed as its first ruler with the title Kapitan Laut Pulo. In 1817 the Treaty of Karang Intan handed the Tanah Bumbu coasts, with Paser, to the Netherlands.
zh:
巴都利金（Batulicin）位于婆罗洲东南肩部，巴都利金河、詹通河、邦卡兰河等短河自林木覆盖的丘陵奔流入望加锡海峡。1444年时，这些河口是邦卡兰达雅克人的地方，百姓打鱼、采洞，最珍贵的收获是特穆隆石灰岩洞出产的燕窝，洞中所取的水还用于首领的仪式。村人把燕窝和林产装上帆船，沿漫长海路西运马辰。这片海岸当时没有自己的王庭，处在班贾尔世界的边缘。

17世纪，这片海岸迎来了自己的王朝：海上袭来的武装洗劫了Cengal河口的帕穆坎，当地达雅克人向马辰求援，班贾尔赛义杜拉苏丹之子迪帕蒂·图哈（Dipati Tuha）率众从陆路而来，在布姆布河畔定居，建立藩属的塔纳布姆布王国，统辖自巴都利金到邦卡兰的五条河川。其中一位首领巴都·甘廷王皈依伊斯兰教，部众成为邦卡兰马来人，特穆隆洞则留给仍守旧俗的达雅克人。布吉移民随后而至：苏拉威西瓦乔的富商普瓦纳·德克沿海岸南下，在帕塞尔没找到合意的落脚地，得到班贾尔苏丹准许后，在邻近的库桑地区开辟帕加坦布吉定居点。他的将领拉·庞厄瓦把觊觎王位者阿米尔的布吉—帕塞尔联军逐出海岸，约1784年受封为首任统治者，号「海岛甲必丹」（Kapitan Laut Pulo）。1817年的卡朗因坦条约把塔纳布姆布沿岸与帕塞尔一并割让给荷兰。

en:
The Pontianak lands lie in the waterlogged delta where the Kapuas, Borneo's great inland highway, meets the sea on the equator. In 1444 only a few Malay fishing villages clung to the river mouths, within the loose orbit of Mempawah and the older Tanjungpura world of south-western Borneo. Dayaks of the Landak and Mandor rivers panned alluvial gold and floated it down to the coast with rattan, beeswax and camphor gathered in the forests behind.

Gold drew Chinese miners from the mid-eighteenth century, brought in by the rulers of Sambas, and their self-governing mining companies, the kongsi, soon ran the upriver fields. In 1771 Syarif Abdurrahman, an Arab sayyid who had left Mempawah, cleared a settlement where the Kapuas Kecil meets the Landak and founded the Pontianak Sultanate. Tradition says the ground was a haunt of the pontianak, the ferocious female ghost of Malay belief, until he and his men drove the spirits off with cannon fire; he built his mosque and Kadriah palace there and named the town after the ghost. In 1777 the Hakka miners upriver at Mandor proclaimed the Lanfang Republic under Luo Fangbo, a kongsi state that kept its own militia and courts, swore fealty to the Qing throne and allied itself with the new sultanate. The Dutch recognised Abdurrahman as sultan in 1778 and by treaty in 1779 set up a factory facing the palace. By 1821 the delta was a three-cornered world of Malay palace, Chinese mining towns and Dutch traders.
zh:
坤甸地处婆罗洲内河大动脉卡普阿斯河入海口的沼泽三角洲，正压在赤道线上。1444年，河口一带只有几个马来渔村，处在喃吧哇和婆罗洲西南部更古老的丹戎布拉势力圈的松散影响之下。兰达河、东万律河一带的达雅克人淘洗沙金，连同在后方森林里采来的藤条、蜂蜡和樟脑，顺流运到海口。

18世纪中叶起，黄金引来大批华工，他们由三发的统治者招募而来，自治的采矿结社「公司」很快掌控了上游各矿区。1771年，离开喃吧哇的阿拉伯圣裔沙里夫·阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼在卡普阿斯小河与兰达河相汇处辟地建埠，创立坤甸苏丹国。相传那一带本是马来人传说中厉鬼庞蒂雅娜出没之地，他命部下开炮驱走鬼魂，在原址建起清真寺和卡德里亚赫王宫，城也因鬼得名。1777年，东万律上游的客家矿工推举罗芳伯建立兰芳共和国，这个公司之邦自养民兵、自设公堂，向清朝称臣，并与新生的苏丹国结盟。荷兰人于1778年承认拉赫曼的苏丹称号，又在1779年立约，在王宫对岸设立商馆。到1821年，三角洲已是马来宫廷、华人矿镇与荷兰商人三足鼎立的世界。

en:
Meliau lies inland on the middle Kapuas, among the first broad rice plains met after pushing up from the Borneo coast. Its riverbanks were Dayak country, with Malay traders settled among the villages, and the river carried rice and forest produce downstream to the Sukadana coast, where the old Malay kingdom of Tanjungpura had stood since the eighth century. Local tradition traces the upriver courts to sons of an exiled prince of Majapahit who took a Dayak princess for wife; the wars of Tanjungpura later drove those princes up the Kapuas with their followings. In 1444 Meliau was a scatter of river villages, shipping rice and resin to the coast and keeping the old Hindu and ancestral customs of the inland courts.

Islam reached Sukadana in 1550 and crept up the Kapuas only gradually. The Kerajaan Meliau enters the records in 1762, when a prince claiming Majapahit descent set up a Malay-style river kingdom here; in time its rulers bore the Muslim title of panembahan over Dayak subjects who kept their own ways. Meliau stayed a small upriver polity, marrying and warring with its neighbours Tayan and Sanggau, and in 1821 it was still a self-ruling little court while Dutch power gathered along the West Borneo coast.
zh:
默利奥深居卡普阿斯河中游内陆，是从婆罗洲海岸溯河而上最先遇到的开阔稻作平原之一。河两岸本是达雅克人的土地，马来商人定居在村寨之间，稻米和林产顺流运到苏卡丹纳海岸，古老的马来王国丹戎布拉自8世纪起立国于此。当地传说把上游各小邦的王室追溯到一位流亡的满者伯夷王子，他娶了达雅克公主，诸子各有封地；后来丹戎布拉征战不断，这些王公率众溯卡普阿斯河而上。1444年的默利奥是一串沿河村寨，把稻米和树脂运往海口，保留着内陆宫廷古老的印度教与祖先崇拜习俗。

伊斯兰教1550年传到苏卡丹纳，沿卡普阿斯河而上却十分缓慢。默利奥王国见于记载始于1762年，一位自称满者伯夷后裔的王子在此建立马来式的河上王国；后来的统治者使用穆斯林的「潘嫩巴汉」称号，治下的达雅克人则保留自己的风俗。默利奥始终是个小小的上游政权，与邻国戴燕、上侯时战时婚；1821年它仍是一座自治的小河宫廷，而荷兰人的势力已在西婆罗洲沿海集结。

en:
Kuching is the country of the Sarawak River, a muddy coast of mangroves and fishing villages beneath the forested ridges of south-western Borneo. At its mouth Santubong was already a trading port where Chinese junks called between the eighth and thirteenth centuries, and the ceramics they left are still dug from its earth. The coast passed under Brunei as that sultanate spread from the reign of its first ruler, Muhammad Shah. In 1444 it was a Sunni Muslim frontier of the Bruneian empire, run through local Malay datus and Land Dayak chiefs, who sent beeswax, camphor, rattan and inland gold downriver to exchange for Chinese goods and salt.

In 1578, during the Castilian War, a Spanish fleet out of Manila stormed Brunei's own capital, Kota Batu, and held it seventy-two days before disease drove it out; Sarawak itself never fell. After Brunei subdued the old Santubong kingdom, the new sultan Abdul Jalilul Akbar in 1599 settled his younger brother Pengiran Muda Tengah's claim to the Brunei throne by sending him to rule Sarawak. Tengah went with a thousand Sakai, Kedayan and Bunut followers, built a fortified palace at Sungai Bedil by Santubong and reigned as Sultan Ibrahim Ali Omar Shah, the first and only sultan of Sarawak. A journey to Johor ended in a quarrel at court and he was ordered out of the kingdom; a storm on the voyage home blew his ship to Sukadana, where he married the ruler's sister Ratu Surya Kesuma and studied under Sheikh Shamsuddin, a teacher from Mecca. He later married a princess of Matan as well. His son by the Sukadana marriage, Radin Sulaiman, carried Islam to the throne of Sambas. In 1641 a traitor stabbed him with a spear at Batu Buaya in Santubong, and Sarawak reverted to governors appointed from Brunei. The Bruneian civil war of 1661–1673 drained the empire, and by 1821 the Sarawak River was a quiet backwater under local datus and Bruneian nobles, its small trading villages not yet grown into the town later called Kuching.
zh:
古晋是砂拉越河流域之地，乃婆罗洲西南角一片泥泞海岸，渔村散布于红树林间，背后是覆满森林的丘陵。河口的山都望早为贸易港口，8至13世纪间中国帆船常来停泊，留下的瓷片后世仍不断从土中出土。随着文莱苏丹国自初代苏丹穆罕默德·沙阿时代向外扩张，这片海岸归入文莱。1444年的砂拉越是文莱帝国的逊尼派穆斯林边疆，由当地马来拿督与陆上达雅克酋长分头治理，蜂蜡、樟脑、藤条和内陆黄金顺河而下，换取中国货物和食盐。

1578年卡斯蒂利亚战争期间，一支来自马尼拉的西班牙舰队猛攻文莱本国都城哥打巴鲁，占领七十二天后因疫病撤走；砂拉越本身并未陷落。文莱攻灭古老的山都望王国后，新苏丹阿卜杜勒·贾利鲁·阿巴尔于1599年把与自己争位的弟弟彭吉兰·穆达·登加分封至砂拉越，了结这场继位之争。登加带着上千名战士和随从赴任，在山都望筑起带城墙的王宫，称苏丹易卜拉欣·阿里·奥马尔·沙阿，是砂拉越第一位也是唯一一位苏丹。他出使柔佛，却在柔佛宫廷起衅，被令离境；归国途中遇风暴，船被吹到苏卡丹纳，他在那里娶了苏卡丹纳统治者的姊妹，又跟随麦加来的传教师研习教义，后来还在马丹娶了一位公主。他与这位苏卡丹纳妻子所生之子拉登·苏莱曼，后来把伊斯兰教带上三发的王位。1641年，一名叛臣在山都望的峇都布阿亚（Batu Buaya）用长矛将他刺死，砂拉越重新由文莱任命的总督治理。1661至1673年的文莱继位内战耗尽了帝国国力，到1821年，砂拉越河已是安静的偏僻角落，由当地拿督和文莱贵族统辖；那些小小的贸易村落，此时还未长成日后名为古晋的城市。

en:
Bintulu sits at the mouth of the Kemena River, on the exposed coast between Brunei Bay and the Rajang delta. The Kemena linked Melanau stilt villages with their fishing grounds, sago groves and the sea. Its name is said to come from a Melanau phrase meaning 'picking heads', referring to headtaking remembered along this shore. Chinese geographical works of the Song and Yuan eras list Wen Du Ling, together with Igan, among places under Fo-ni. The Melanau villages had their own headmen before Brunei's expansion drew them into the sultanate in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries. In 1444 Bintulu belonged to Sultan Sulaiman's Brunei, and its trade was modest: fish, sago, damar resin and sea produce changed hands at the river landing.

The Castilian War reached Brunei Bay rather than the Kemena. Spanish troops took Kota Batu in April 1578 and withdrew after 72 days; no garrison came here, but Brunei's fleets could no longer patrol these river mouths as securely. Dutch intelligence in 1609 counted the Melano coast among the Bruneian lands growing restive. Through the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries Brunei merchants still came for sago, resin and sea produce, while Melanau headmen managed the villages. Iranun war-boats raided the coast for captives, so the Melanau kept their main settlements up the Kemena and went down to the mouth in parties. In 1821 Bintulu still had no fort, bazaar or foreign trading post, only fishing and sago villages on a shore Brunei claimed more often than it governed.
zh:
民都鲁位于格盟纳河口，地处文莱湾与拉让江三角洲之间无遮拦的海岸。格盟纳河把马兰诺人的高脚村落同渔场、西谷林和大海连在一起。据说地名来自一个意为「拾取人头」的马兰诺语词，指向沿海流传的猎头习俗。宋元时期的地理著作把温都灵与伊干并列，记作浡泥属下之地。14至15世纪文莱势力扩张到这里以前，各渔村由马兰诺头人自理。1444年，民都鲁属苏丹苏莱曼治下的文莱，贸易规模不大，渔获、西谷、达玛脂和海产在河畔泊地交易。

卡斯蒂利亚战争打到文莱湾，没有打到格盟纳河。1578年4月，西班牙军队攻占哥打巴都，72天后撤走；这里没有来过驻军，但文莱战船已不能像从前那样安稳巡防各河口。1609年的荷兰情报把马兰诺海岸列入渐生反意的文莱属地。17至18世纪，文莱商人仍来收购西谷、树脂和海产，村落事务则由马兰诺头人处理。伊拉农战船到沿海掳人，马兰诺人便把主要村落设在格盟纳河上游，只结队下到河口。1821年的民都鲁仍没有堡垒、市集或外商商馆，只有渔村和西谷村，落在文莱声称拥有、却很少实际管辖的海岸上。

en:
Kapit is the middle Rajang country above the Pelagus Rapids, where the Balleh, Katibas and other forest streams enter the main river. The rapids made the upriver journey dangerous and gave the longhouse peoples a strong defence. Kejaman, Sekapan, Tanjung and Kanowit communities lived in Kajang-speaking longhouses, Punan families occupied smaller streams, and Kayan war parties moved through the upper country. They cleared hill-rice fields, gathered camphor and beeswax, and fought feuds in which heads and captives were taken. Brunei claimed the whole Rajang basin, and its traders came upriver for jungle produce, but in 1444 the sultan had no fort, tax post or appointed chief above the lower reaches. Kapit was governed by its own longhouse councils.

Migration changed that balance. Kayan groups had been pressing into Sarawak from the upper Kayan, Kapuas and Mahakam country when Iban expansion began from the Kapuas basin in the mid-sixteenth century. Iban settlers moved first into the Batang Lupar and Saribas, then into the Katibas and other southern Rajang tributaries by the early 1800s in search of fresh rice land. Their longhouse fleets fought the older Kajang and Kayan communities in feuds that lasted for generations. Brunei's civil war of the 1660s was fought far downriver and ended in 1673 without bringing a sultan's garrison to Kapit. In 1821 no town yet stood above the Pelagus Rapids, and older upriver peoples still held much of the upper Rajang against advancing Iban war-boats.
zh:
加帛是彼拉古斯急滩以上的拉让江中游地带，巴拉河、卡提巴斯河等森林支流在这里汇入大江。急滩使上行航程危险，也给长屋诸族提供了可靠屏障。格察曼、色卡班、丹戎和加拿逸等说卡章语的社群住在长屋中，普南人散布较小支流，加央战队往来上游。他们开辟旱稻田，采集樟脑和蜂蜡，也在争夺人头与俘虏的世仇战事中出战。文莱名义领有整个拉让江流域，商人沿河上溯收购山货，但1444年时，苏丹在下游以上没有堡垒、税站或任命的首领。加帛由各长屋议事会自行管理。

族群迁徙改变了这种势力分布。加央人从加央河、卡普阿斯河和马哈坎河上游一带进入砂拉越；16世纪中叶，伊班人也从卡普阿斯河流域向外扩张。伊班移民先到巴当鲁巴河与沙里拔河，19世纪初又沿卡提巴斯河等拉让江南部支流上溯，寻找新的稻田。他们的长屋船队同更早居住的卡章、加央诸族交战，世仇延续数代。1660年代的文莱内战发生在很远的下游，到1673年结束时也没有把苏丹驻军带到加帛。1821年，彼拉古斯急滩以上仍没有城镇，上游各族还据守着拉让江上游大部，抵御不断推进的伊班船队。

en:
Langkat is the low, river-drained coast of northeastern Sumatra, facing the Strait of Malacca around the mouth of the Batang Serangan; the later court sat upriver at Tanjung Pura. In the fifteenth century this shore belonged to the maritime kingdom of Aru, whose fleets controlled the northern entrance of the strait and whose ports loaded camphor, benzoin, lignaloes, rattan, honey, gold and slaves brought down by Karo and Batak highlanders. Tomé Pires called Aru a prosperous land of rice, fish and wine, and heard that a great slave market was held for several months each year at a town upcountry, where dealers bought captives and kinsmen came to ransom them. The pagan interior had another name in foreign reports: the Portuguese in Malacca wrote that the sultans kept cannibal executioners from a country they called Aru for particular punishments. Pasai claimed this coast in 1444, but Aru's chiefs and war-boats made it a fought-over border rather than a quiet subject land.

Aceh broke Aru in a long run of wars. It took the port-capital of Kota Rentang in 1539 and drove the court inland to the walled Benteng Putri Hijau; an Ottoman fleet sailing to Aceh's aid defeated Aru in 1564, and Sultan Iskandar Muda stormed the last stronghold in 1613. In 1568, amid the Acehnese advance, an Aru commander named Dewa Shahdan fled east with his followers and founded the river polity that became Langkat. His line continued under Raja Kahar and a succession of bendahara rajas, who kept the river mouth and the traffic in forest produce. Raja Kejuruan Hitam ruled from 1750 to 1818 through constant wars with his neighbours, and at the end of the period Langkat remained an autonomous Malay kingdom on Aceh's southeastern flank.
zh:
冷吉是苏门答腊东北部地势低洼、河网密布的海岸，在巴唐塞兰甘河河口一带临马六甲海峡，后来的王廷设在河上游的丹戎布拉。15世纪时，这片海岸属于海上强国阿鲁，阿鲁的船队控制着海峡北口，港中装运的是卡罗和巴塔克山民背下来的樟脑、安息香、沉香、藤条、蜂蜜、黄金和奴隶。托梅·皮莱资称阿鲁富庶，出产稻米、鱼和酒，还听说内陆有座城镇每年开市数月，商人在此购买奴隶，亲属也可到场赎人。阿鲁的异教内陆在外国记载里另有恶名：马六甲的葡萄牙人写道，苏丹们专用来自阿鲁的食人者充当行刑手，处置特殊罪名的犯人。1444年，八昔声称领有这片海岸，但阿鲁的首领和战船使这里成为反复争夺的边地，而非恭顺的属土。

亚齐在一连串战争中击垮了阿鲁。1539年亚齐攻陷阿鲁的港口都城哥打冷坦，王廷退守内陆有城墙环绕的普特里希乔堡；1564年，一支驰援亚齐的奥斯曼舰队击败阿鲁，1613年苏丹伊斯坎达尔·穆达又攻克其最后据点。1568年，在亚齐攻势中，阿鲁将领德瓦·沙赫丹率部众东逃，建立了后来冷吉的河上政权。他的后裔在拉惹·卡哈尔和此后历任盘陀诃罗拉阇治下延续，守住河口和山林物产贸易。拉惹·基朱兰·希坦于1750年至1818年在位，常年与邻邦交战；到这一时期末，冷吉仍是亚齐东南侧一个自治的马来王国。

en:
The low coast around the Deli River and Belawan faces the northern entrance to the Strait of Malacca. In the fifteenth century this was the heartland of Aru, a Muslim Malay sea power whose prestige the Malay Annals set beside that of Pasai and Malacca. Its port capital, Kota Rentang, has yielded Jawi headstones, Arab coins and ceramics from China, Siam and Sri Lanka, with the timbers of a wrecked ship still buried in the river mud. Inland rises Benteng Putri Hijau, the Green Princess Fort, a walled and moated stronghold in the Karo Batak manner. Ma Huan, chronicler of Zheng He's voyages, wrote in 1416 of a Muslim king whose people farmed and fished between the mountains and the sea; the kingdom sent tribute to the Ming court in 1411 and shipped rice, camphor, benzoin, gold and aromatic woods. Pires later found it prosperous, with a slave market held at Arqat in fixed months. In 1444 Aru's fleets watched over the northern end of the strait, while the animist Karo highlands behind the coast kept their own gods.

Rivalry with Portuguese Malacca and a rising Aceh wore Aru down. Kota Rentang probably fell to Acehnese attack in 1539, and the court withdrew to the Green Princess Fort; in 1564 an Ottoman fleet campaigning alongside Aceh defeated Aru, and in early 1613 Sultan Iskandar Muda put an end to the kingdom. In 1632 he granted its lands to his commander Gocah Pahlawan, called the Horse of Bintan, veteran of the campaigns against Pahang, Kedah and the Portuguese. The general married a daughter of the Karo ruler of Sunggal, and the four Karo chiefs accepted him as their single overlord. His son threw off Aceh in 1669, set his capital at Labuhan and opened trade with Dutch Malacca. After a succession feud in 1720, the dispossessed prince Tuanku Umar founded the separate Sultanate of Serdang in 1723. Deli then passed back and forth between Aceh and Siak, until Siak conquered it in 1814.
zh:
碟里（Deli，中国载籍多称日里）一带的低海岸临马六甲海峡北口，15世纪时是哑鲁国的核心。《马来纪年》把哑鲁的声势与帕赛、马六甲并列。港口都城哥打伦唐出土过爪夷文墓碑、阿拉伯钱币和中国、暹罗、锡兰的瓷器，河泥中还埋着沉船的木构件。内陆耸立着绿公主堡（Putri Hijau），是按卡罗巴塔克人的形制筑成的围墙深壕要塞。随郑和下西洋的马欢1416年记载，哑鲁国王是穆斯林，百姓在大山与大海之间耕渔为业；哑鲁1411年曾向明朝进贡，输出稻米、樟脑、安息香、黄金和香木。皮莱资后来见到的哑鲁仍然富庶，阿尔卡特有隔几个月开市一次的奴隶市场。1444年，哑鲁的船队扼守海峡北口，海岸后方信泛灵信仰的卡罗人高地自行其是。

与葡萄牙人的马六甲和崛起的亚齐相争，耗尽了哑鲁的国力。哥打伦唐约在1539年被亚齐攻破，王廷退入绿公主堡；1564年，一支与亚齐协同作战的奥斯曼舰队击败哑鲁，1613年初苏丹伊斯干达·穆达攻灭了这个王国。1632年，他把旧哑鲁土地封给将领哥查·帕拉万。此将绰号「民丹之马」，曾参加征讨彭亨、吉打和对葡萄牙人的战事。他娶松加尔卡罗族首领之女，卡罗四部共奉他为唯一的宗主。其子1669年摆脱亚齐，定都拉布汉，并与荷兰人的马六甲通商。1720年王位内争之后，被夺位的王子端古·乌马尔于1723年另建雪冷苏丹国。此后碟里在亚齐与锡亚之间反复易手，1814年为锡亚所灭。

en:
Barus, also called Fansur or Pansur, was the camphor port of western Sumatra, a string of harbour sites on the coast below the forested Batak highlands; when one anchorage silted up, its people moved to the next, and a Batak chronicle mentions three such moves. Resin from the highland trees was sold abroad as kapur barus, 'Barus chalk', and Arabs, Persians, Tamils and Chinese all came to buy it. Sulaiman wrote in 851 of gold mines and the superior camphor of Fansur; al-Mas'udi noted that fansuri camphor was plentiful in years of storms and earthquakes; Marco Polo judged Fansur camphor the finest in the world, fetching its own weight in gold. A Tamil inscription of 1088 at Lobu Tua records the foreign merchants settled in the port and names the local people Zabedj, the word Arab writers used for the Batak. Muslim tombstones at Bukit Hasang show an Islamic community by 1370. In 1444 Barus was still a rich trading kingdom with a crowded harbour, ruled by a court that, like the highlands behind it, kept Hindu-Batak rites.

In the early sixteenth century Tomé Pires heard of the 'very rich kingdom of Baros', known to many nations as Panchur. The port's best-known writer may be Hamzah Fansuri, who took his name from the town: the first known poet to write Sufi mysticism in Malay and one of the makers of the syair form, he may have been born or raised here and died around 1590. Aceh absorbed Barus around the middle of the century and stationed a panglima over its trade, and in 1668 the Dutch East India Company drove him out. The old camphor market never recovered, and west Sumatran commerce moved to newer ports.
zh:
巴鲁斯又称凡苏尔或班苏尔，是苏门答腊西岸的樟脑港：林木茂密的巴塔克高地下方海岸上分布着一连串港址，一处港湾淤塞，居民就迁往下一处，一部巴塔克编年史提到这样迁了三次。高地树木产的树脂外销时叫「巴鲁斯樟脑」，阿拉伯人、波斯人、泰米尔人和中国人都来购买。851年，苏莱曼记载凡苏尔有金矿、出产上等樟脑；麦斯欧迪注意到凡苏里樟脑在多风暴和地震的年份产量尤丰；马可·波罗称凡苏尔樟脑为世界之最，能卖出与自身等重的黄金价钱。1088年洛布图阿的泰米尔碑文记载了定居港中的外商，并把当地居民称作扎贝吉，阿拉伯作家正是用这个名字称呼巴塔克人。武吉哈桑的穆斯林墓碑说明1370年时当地已有穆斯林社群。1444年，巴鲁斯仍是富庶的贸易王国，港中停满各国商船，而宫廷和身后的高地一样，保留着印度教—巴塔克仪式。

16世纪初，托梅·皮莱资听人说起「非常富庶的巴鲁斯王国」，许多民族都知道它叫班苏尔。这座港口最著名的文人或许是哈姆扎·凡苏里，名字里的凡苏尔指的就是巴鲁斯：他是已知最早用马来语撰写苏菲神秘主义作品的诗人，也是马来沙依尔诗体的奠基人之一，相传出生或成长于此，约1590年去世。约16世纪中叶，亚齐吞并巴鲁斯，派庞利马管制贸易；1668年荷兰东印度公司将他逐走。老樟脑市场再未复兴，苏门答腊西岸的贸易转向了更新的港口。

en:
Gerik fills the forested trough between the Bintang and Titiwangsa ranges, where the upper streams of the Perak River gather beneath the old Belum rainforest. The deep woods belonged to Semang bands, who hunted and gathered there as their people had for millennia; Malay villagers kept to the river banks, growing hill rice and fishing. In 1444 this was the remote southern hinterland of the Patani sultanate, joined to the capital by jungle tracks and canoe routes, and its march with Perak had no fixed line.

The upriver settlements get their first named leader from the fall of Malacca. Early in the 1500s Tun Saban, son of the Malaccan bendahara Tun Perak and himself the fallen sultanate's treasurer, led his followers through upper Patani to Belum and became the headman there. The hills stayed a quiet borderland until outsiders came for their tin. After Siam reconquered Patani in 1785, refugees filled the Kroh plateau, and in 1790 the tin-bearing country around Klian Intan and Kroh passed to Tuan Mansor, a Patani noble set over the mines. He broke with Patani in 1808, and when Siam divided Patani into seven semi-autonomous chiefdoms in 1810 he was confirmed as king of Reman, the largest of them, reaching south as far as Lenggong. In 1818 John Bannerman, governor of Penang, met Tuan Mansor at Kroh and signed an agreement, the first treaty between the forest kingdom and a European power.
zh:
宜力位于宾当山脉与蒂蒂旺沙山脉之间的林谷，霹雳河上游的支流在古老的柏隆雨林间汇集。密林深处是塞芒人的天地，各部族千百年来在此游猎采集；马来村民傍河而居，种旱稻、捕鱼。1444年，这里是北大年苏丹国僻远的南部腹地，靠林径和舟路与都城相通，与霹雳之间也没有明确的界线。

上游各聚落第一个留下名字的首领，来自马六甲亡国之余：16世纪初，马六甲名相敦霹雳之子、苏丹国财务大臣敦沙班在国破后率追随者经上北大年到柏隆落脚，做了这些聚落的头人。山地长期是寂静的边地，直到外面的世界为锡砂而来。1785年暹罗重新征服北大年后，难民涌入高乌高原；1790年，吉连旦和高乌一带富藏锡砂的地区落入受命管矿的北大年贵族端·曼梳手中。他于1808年与北大年决裂，1810年暹罗把北大年分为七个半自治土邦时受封为拉曼（Reman）之王；七邦之中拉曼最大，疆域南至玲珑。1818年，槟榔屿总督约翰·班纳曼在高乌会晤端·曼梳并签订协议，这是这个森林王国与欧洲势力之间的第一项条约。

en:
Across a narrow strait from the Kedah rice coast lies a hilly island the Malays call Pulau Pinang, the areca-nut isle, fringed with good anchorage and springs of fresh water; the Ming sailing charts used by Zheng He's fleets already mark it as Binglang Yu. Semang foragers and a handful of Malay fishing families lived there, and the chiefs across the water counted it part of Kedah. In 1444, as for centuries before, traders beating between Kedah and Malacca put into its coves for water, while the opposite shore was quiet rice country under the Sultan of Kedah.

An English ship first watered there in 1592. Francis Light, a country trader acting for the East India Company, called the island 'a convenient magazine for trade' from which to check the Dutch and French, and on 17 July 1786 he landed with a small party. He took formal possession on 11 August, renamed the island Prince of Wales Island and laid out George Town as a free port, with Fort Cornwallis rising on the cape. Sultan Abdullah of Kedah had ceded the island against a promise of military aid that Light had no authority to give, and his attempt to take it back in 1791 was beaten off; a treaty fixed the rent at 6,000 Spanish dollars a year. Light died of malaria in 1794 (his son William Light later founded Adelaide), yet settlers had already flocked in, Chinese, Indians, Bugis and Malays among them, and the population neared ten thousand by 1792. In 1800 the Company acquired the mainland strip named Province Wellesley and raised the rent to 10,000 dollars; in 1805 Penang became a presidency of British India on a footing with Bombay and Madras, and its spice trade drew shipping away from Dutch Malacca. By 1821 George Town was a flourishing free port on the flank of Dutch-held Malacca.
zh:
与吉打稻米海岸隔一道窄峡相望的，是一座丘陵起伏的岛屿，马来人称之为槟榔屿，因岛上遍生槟榔树而得名，沿岸锚地良好，又多甘泉；郑和船队所用的明代航海图已把它标作「槟榔屿」。岛上住着塞芒游猎者和寥寥几户马来渔家，对岸的酋长把它算作吉打的一部分。1444年时，和此前几百年一样，往来吉打与马六甲之间的商船常驶入岛边海湾取水，对岸则是吉打苏丹治下宁静的稻作乡野。

1592年，第一艘英国船曾在此取水。受东印度公司委派的散商法兰西斯·莱特称此岛是「便利的商货仓库」，可用来牵制荷兰和法国，遂于1786年7月17日率一小队人登岸，8月11日正式占领，将岛屿改名威尔士亲王岛，辟建自由港乔治市，并在海角筑起康华丽堡。吉打苏丹阿都拉以岛换取军事援助，而莱特根本无权许下这种承诺；1791年苏丹试图夺回岛屿，攻势被击退，条约定下年租6000西班牙元。莱特1794年死于疟疾（其子威廉·莱特后来创建了阿德莱德），但华人、印度人、武吉斯人和马来人已纷纷涌入，到1792年人口已近一万。1800年，公司取得名为威斯利省的对岸狭长地带，年租增至10000元；1805年槟榔屿成为英属印度的一个辖区，与孟买、马德拉斯地位相当，香料贸易把商船从荷属马六甲吸引过来。到1821年，乔治市已是荷占马六甲侧翼一座兴旺的自由港。

en: Semantan is the forested interior of the Pahang basin, where hill streams such as the Semantan and Tembeling join the upper Pahang around Temerloh, and the highest mountain of the peninsula, Mount Tahan, rises on the eastern watershed. The Tembeling valley was the old road between the Pahang estuary and the lands towards Siam, and gold workings along its rivers go back to the early Iron Age. Jakun and other Orang Asli gathered camphor, aromatic woods and rattan here, the same forest goods that Wang Dayuan in the fourteenth century saw shipped out through the Pahang river mouth. In 1444 these upriver valleys still kept the older Hindu-Buddhist and indigenous beliefs, ruled loosely from Pekan by the chiefs of Dewa Sura, the last of the old maharaja line. A Ligor army marched this river route against Malacca, and Tun Perak's conquest of Pahang in 1454 brought the valleys under Malaccan rule; Dewa Sura's grandson, raised as a Malaccan prince, returned as the first sultan of Pahang. When Aceh overran the coast in 1615 the Pahang sultan fled up the Tembeling into these forests, and the upriver chiefs later answered to Pahang's bendaharas, autonomous under Tun Abdul Majid after 1770.
zh: 士曼丹是彭亨河流域的森林内陆，士曼丹河、淡美岭河等山溪在淡马鲁一带汇入彭亨河上游，半岛最高峰大汉山耸立于东侧分水岭。淡美岭河谷是彭亨河口通往暹罗方向的古老通道，沿河淘金遗迹可追溯到早期铁器时代。贾昆人及其他原住民在这里采办龙脑、香木和藤条，14世纪汪大渊在彭亨河口见到装船外运的，正是这些山林物产。1444年，上游诸河谷仍保持印度教-佛教与本土旧信仰，由旧摩诃罗阇世系末代君主提婆素罗的酋长们从北干松散管辖。洛坤攻打马六甲的军队曾沿这条河南下；1454年敦霹雳征服彭亨，诸河谷纳入马六甲治下，提婆素罗之孙以马六甲王子的身份归来，成为彭亨首任苏丹。1615年亚齐攻陷沿海，彭亨苏丹溯淡美岭河逃入这片丛林。后来上游酋长听命于彭亨的宰相，1770年以后归自治的敦阿都·马吉德管辖。

en:
Singapore, then called Temasek, is a low island off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula, separated from Johor by a narrow tidal strait. The Chinese mariner Wang Dayuan found a trading port here when he visited about 1330: he described the Long Ya Men passage at Keppel and a town that a Sukhothai fleet of more than seventy ships had failed to storm after a month's siege, and Siam and Majapahit long disputed its allegiance. Around 1400 its ruler Parameswara withdrew north to found Malacca, and the old hill settlement on Fort Canning was abandoned. In 1444 a small Sunni Malay fishing and trading village remains at the mouth of the Singapore River, a quiet backwater of the Malacca Sultanate whose Orang Laut fishermen know every shoal in the strait.

After Malacca fell in 1511 Singapore passed to the new Johor Sultanate, but in 1613 Portuguese raiders burned the Malay outpost at the river mouth, and for two centuries the island lay almost deserted, a haunt of Orang Laut and passing pirates while its strait traffic came under Dutch control. On 29 January 1819 Stamford Raffles landed in search of a British port beyond Dutch reach; he found barely a thousand inhabitants, mostly Malays with a handful of Chinese. The Temenggong Abdul Rahman governed the island for Johor, whose reigning sultan leaned on the Dutch and the Bugis; Raffles therefore brought back the exiled elder prince Tengku Hussein from Penyengat and, on 6 February 1819, signed a treaty recognising him as sultan in exchange for leave to build a factory. Declared a free port, Singapore at once drew Malay, Bugis, Chinese and Indian shipping, and pepper and gambier plantations spread inland. In 1821, barely two years later, the fishing village has become the straits' fastest-growing emporium under the East India Company's flag.
zh:
新加坡在14世纪称淡马锡，是马来半岛南端外海一座低平岛屿，与柔佛仅隔一条狭窄的潮汐海峡。中国航海家汪大渊约1330年到访时，这里已是商埠：他记下了岌巴港的「龙牙门」水道，还记下素可泰七十余艘兵船来攻、围城一月不下；当时暹罗与满者伯夷长期争夺该岛。1400年前后，岛上君主拜里米苏拉北撤另立马六甲，福康宁山上的旧城随之废弃。1444年的新加坡河口只剩一座小小的逊尼派马来人渔村兼商埠，是马六甲苏丹国治下安静的角落，唯有海人渔民熟悉海峡中的每一处浅滩。
