Clans fished the estuaries, gathered on the beaches and moved through coastal woods and red cedar stands by season and kinship. In 1444 every inlet and offshore island was in Aboriginal hands.

On 29 April 1770 the Endeavour anchored in the bay and Cook made his first landing on the Australian east coast. Two Gweagal men came down to the boats shouting 'Warra warra wai', 'you are all dead', and levelling their spears; Cook threw beads and nails ashore, then fired small shot and wounded one of them. His men took forty to fifty spears from the abandoned camp, and Cook gave some to his patron Lord Sandwich, who presented them to his old college, Trinity College at Cambridge. Cook first called the place Stingrays Harbour for the catch, then renamed it Botany Bay for the plants Joseph Banks and Daniel Solander collected there. In January 1788 the First Fleet sailed in to found a penal colony, but Arthur Phillip found no sure fresh water, poor soil and an open roadstead; as his ships were moving out, the French expedition of the Comte de Lapérouse appeared beyond the heads, and the British founded their settlement at Sydney Cove instead. The Illawarra stayed shut behind its escarpment until George Bass and Matthew Flinders explored it in 1796. Red cedar drew cutters from the early 1800s, and in 1815 Dharawal guides led cattle down the ranges for Sydney graziers pushed south by drought.
zh:
达拉瓦尔海岸从博塔尼湾（他们的语言里叫卡迈）南岸，经哈金港和伊拉瓦拉陡崖延向肖尔黑文。格韦加尔氏族据有湾南，瓦迪瓦迪氏族的土地在伊拉瓦拉湖周围。各氏族在河口捕鱼、在海滩采集，按季节和亲族往来于海岸林地与红杉林之间。1444年，每一处小湾和近海岛屿都在原住民手中。

1770年4月29日，「努力号」在湾中下锚，库克在澳大利亚东海岸第一次登陆。两名格韦加尔男子走到滩前，高喊「瓦拉瓦拉外」，意为「你们都是死人」，举矛相对；库克把珠子和铁钉抛到岸上，随即开枪，用霰弹击伤一人。部下从被弃的营地取走四五十支长矛，库克把其中一些赠给赞助人桑威奇伯爵，伯爵又转赠母校剑桥大学三一学院。库克起初因渔获丰盛把这里叫做黄貂鱼港，后来因约瑟夫·班克斯和丹尼尔·索兰德在此采得大量植物，改名博塔尼湾，湾名取自植物。1788年1月，第一舰队驶入湾中，打算建流放犯殖民地，但阿瑟·菲利普发现这里没有可靠的淡水、土壤贫瘠、港湾敞开无险可守；英舰正要撤出时，拉彼鲁兹伯爵率领的法国探险队出现在湾外，英国人于是改在悉尼湾建城。伊拉瓦拉被陡崖隔绝，直到1796年乔治·巴斯和马修·弗林德斯才进入探查。19世纪初红杉引来伐木者；1815年干旱把悉尼牧人逼向南方，达拉瓦尔向导把牛群领下了山岭。

en:
The Gundungurra, also recorded as the Gandangara, held the sandstone tablelands and river valleys southwest of Sydney: the Nattai and Wollondilly catchments, the Burragorang Valley, the Southern Highlands and the country toward Goulburn. Their clans moved between highland woods and river flats thick with yam vines, and the steep scarps of the tableland kept outsiders out. In 1444 Gundungurra life ran through valleys, ceremonial grounds and kin paths that no European had yet seen.

On the Cumberland Plain below the tableland, cattle that had strayed from the new settlement at Sydney Cove were found running wild in 1795; the British called the grazing ground the Cowpastures and kept settlers off it for years to protect the herd. In 1802 Francis Barrallier crossed the Nattai to the Wollondilly and was welcomed in Gundungurra camps; his journal notes that the people built huts for strangers they chose to receive as friends. The Gundungurra later asked Governor King to protect their river yam beds, and the promise held until King left in 1807. Land grants around Appin from 1811, together with drought, brought war in 1814: the Gundungurra joined Dharawal bands and surviving Dharug to raid cornfields, timing their spear attacks to the long pause while muskets were reloaded. On the night of 17 April 1816 Captain James Wallis led the 46th Regiment onto a camp by the Cataract River. In the moonlight people were shot or driven over the cliffs; at least fourteen men, women and children died in the Appin massacre, the mountain chief Cannabaygal among them. Sixteen Gundungurra were taken and four children removed to the Native Institution at Parramatta. In 1819 Charles Throsby and Hamilton Hume pushed into the valleys with Gundungurra guides, opening the country to the grazing grants that followed.
zh:
贡东古拉人（也记作甘丹加拉人）据有悉尼西南的砂岩台地与河谷：纳泰河和沃隆迪利河流域、伯勒戈兰山谷、南部高地，以及通往古尔本的地带。各氏族往来于高地林地和长满薯蓣藤的河畔平地之间，台地陡峭的崖壁使外人难以进入。1444年，贡东古拉人的生活沿着山谷、仪典场地和亲族小路展开，欧洲人还从未踏足这里。

在台地下方的坎伯兰平原，1795年有人发现一群从悉尼湾新殖民地走失的牛在野外繁衍；英国人把这片牧地叫做牧牛原，多年禁止移民进入，以保护牛群。1802年，弗朗西斯·巴拉利耶穿过纳泰抵达沃隆迪利，在贡东古拉人的营地受到款待；他在日记里写道，主人会为愿意接纳为友的外人造屋。后来他们请求金总督保护河畔的薯蓣地，这项承诺维持到1807年金总督离任。1811年起阿平一带的土地被陆续封赐，再加上干旱，战争在1814年爆发：贡东古拉人联合达拉瓦尔氏族和残余的达鲁格人袭击玉米田，专门趁火枪装填的漫长间隙投标进攻。1816年4月17日夜，詹姆斯·沃利斯上尉率第四十六团逼近卡特拉克特河畔的营地。月光下，人们被枪击或被逼下悬崖，至少十四名男女和儿童死于阿平屠杀，山居首领坎纳巴伊加尔也在其中。十六名贡东古拉人被俘，四个孩子被送往帕拉马塔的原住民学校。1819年，查尔斯·斯罗比和汉密尔顿·休姆由贡东古拉向导带路进入山谷，为随后的牧场授地打开了门路。

en:
Dharug country lay inland of the Eora coast, along Dyarubbin, the Hawkesbury-Nepean river system, and across the Cumberland Plain to the lower Blue Mountains. River clans fished the channels and planted the alluvial flats, meeting neighbours to trade at fixed places; inland clans moved through eucalyptus woods and sandstone ridges, and the high mountains walled off the plains to the west. In 1444 the rivers, fords and ridges were divided between clans by kinship, without a European house among them.

British boats explored the Hawkesbury and Nepean in 1789, and Governor Phillip named the Hawkesbury that June. Smallpox came with the colonists and in some river districts killed up to nine in ten Dharug that year. From 1794 settlers were granted the river flats, and raids and troop patrols began at once. The Bidjigal warrior Pemulwuy, a Dharug carradhy, or cleverman, marked from childhood by a blemish on his eye, fought the colony for twelve years from 1790, burning crops and raiding outlying farms between the Hawkesbury and Parramatta. In 1797 he led about a hundred warriors on Parramatta itself, was shot seven times and carried to the hospital in a leg-iron, and escaped; his people afterwards held that British bullets could not kill him. A price was set on his head and settlers shot him in 1802; the head was preserved in spirits and Governor King sent it to Sir Joseph Banks in London. In 1813 Blaxland, Wentworth and Lawson crossed the Blue Mountains, and Macquarie's 1816 weapons bans and new military posts tightened the colony's hold along Dyarubbin.
zh:
达鲁格之地位于埃奥拉海岸地带内侧，沿迪亚鲁宾，即霍克斯伯里-尼皮恩河水系展开，跨过坎伯兰平原直至蓝山低岭。河畔氏族在河道捕鱼、在冲积平地上种植，在固定地点与邻族交易；内陆氏族穿行于桉树林和砂岩山脊之间，西面的高山把更远处的平原隔开。1444年，河流、浅滩和山脊按亲属关系分属各氏族，其间没有一座欧洲人的房屋。

1789年，英国人的小船探查了霍克斯伯里河与尼皮恩河，菲利普总督于同年6月将大河命名为霍克斯伯里河。天花随殖民者而来，那一年部分河畔地区多达九成达鲁格人病死。1794年起，移民在河畔平地获得授地，袭击和军队巡逻随即开始。比迪加尔战士佩姆乌（Pemulwuy）是达鲁格人的卡拉吉，即通晓法术的智者，自幼一目带有异斑；他从1790年起与殖民地作战十二年，烧毁作物，在霍克斯伯里和帕拉马塔之间袭击偏远农庄。1797年，他率领约一百名战士直攻帕拉马塔，身中七弹，戴着脚镣被送进医院，却成功逃走；族人于是相信英国子弹杀不死他。后来官府悬赏他的首级，定居者在1802年将他枪杀；他的头颅被用酒保存，金总督把它送往伦敦献给约瑟夫·班克斯爵士。1813年，布拉克斯兰、温特沃思和劳森翻越蓝山；1816年麦夸里颁布武器禁令、增设军营，殖民地对迪亚鲁宾河畔的控制随之收紧。

en: The Ovens and King rivers meet below the north-western slopes of the Victorian Alps and run north through open forest to the Murray. This upper Murray country belongs to the Pallanganmiddang, also called Waveroo or Waywurru, whose tongue was unlike the Kulin speech of the tribes to their south-west. Above the Kiewa valley rises Warkwoolowler, Mount Bogong, highest peak of the Victorian Alps; in Waywurru and Dhudhuroa the name means the mountain where people collected the bugung, the brown bogong moth that sleeps out the summer in granite crevices. The high country was held by the Yiatmathong of the Kiewa and Mitta Mitta valleys, and other tribes had to ask their leave before climbing to the feast. First they gathered at Mungabarreena on the Murray near Albury for ceremonies, initiations, trade and the settling of quarrels, then walked into the mountains to feed on the fat, protein-rich moths; bands came from as far as the coast and the south-western slopes. In 1444, and for nearly four centuries after, no European had entered these valleys.
zh: 奥文斯河与金河在维多利亚阿尔卑斯山西北坡下汇合，向北穿过疏林原野注入墨累河。这片上墨累之地属于帕兰甘米当人，也称瓦弗鲁人或韦武鲁人，他们的语言与西南方诸部的库林话迥然不同。基瓦河谷之上矗立着瓦库武勒（Warkwoolowler），即博贡山，维多利亚阿尔卑斯山的最高峰；在韦武鲁语和杜杜罗阿语里，山名的意思是「人们采集布贡的山」，布贡（bugung）就是褐色的博贡蛾，夏天躲在花岗岩缝中夏眠。高山属于掌握基瓦河与米塔米塔河谷的亚特马通人，别部上山赴宴前须先征得他们同意。各部落先在墨累河畔奥尔伯里附近的蒙加巴利纳（Mungabarreena）集会，举行仪式和成年礼、互通贸易、了结争端，再结伴走进山地，捕食肥美而富含养分的蛾群；远至海岸和西南坡的部族都会赶来。1444年，以及此后近四百年里，还没有欧洲人进入这些山谷。

en: The Ngadjuri are the Mid North people of South Australia, whose country covered roughly 30,000 square kilometres of peppermint gum woodland from Gawler and Clare through Burra north to Orroroo at the foot of the Flinders Ranges. Their name means 'we men'; the neighbouring Kaurna called them Wirameju, 'peppermint gum forest people', after the trees that marked their bounds. Bands such as the Burra Burra and the northern Mimbara kept camps around Clare, Auburn and Kapunda, and large parties of men hunted possums together in the wooded hills. In 1444 the country lay beyond European reach, and so it still was in 1802, when Matthew Flinders in the Investigator surveyed upper Spencer Gulf. He named the 964-metre peak above the shore Mount Brown after his botanist Robert Brown; on 10 and 11 March Brown climbed it with the botanical artist Ferdinand Bauer and the landscape painter William Westall and looked east over the southern Flinders Ranges. No party from the ships pushed inland, and no European entered the Ngadjuri woodlands before 1821.
zh: 雅朱里人是南澳大利亚中北部的原住民，传统土地约三万平方公里，几乎全是薄荷桉林地：南起高勒和克莱尔，经布拉向北延伸到弗林德斯山脉脚下的奥鲁鲁。他们的族名意为「我们这些人」；相邻的考尔纳人按划定地界的桉树称他们为维拉梅朱，意为「薄荷桉林之人」。布拉布拉和北部的明巴拉等游群在克莱尔、奥本和卡潘达一带扎营，大群男子会在林木山丘中集体猎捕负鼠。1444年，这里还远在欧洲人所能到达之外，1802年仍是如此：马修·弗林德斯乘「考察者号」测绘斯潘塞湾上段，把岸边一座964米高的山峰以随队植物学家罗伯特·布朗之姓命名为布朗山；3月10日至11日，布朗与两位随船画师登顶，东望弗林德斯山脉南段。船上没有人分队进入内陆，到1821年为止，也没有欧洲人踏入雅朱里人的林地。

en: Nyaki-Nyaki is the Njakinjaki country of the dry eastern Wheatbelt east of Lake Grace, about 31,000 square kilometres of mallee scrub, salt lakes and bare granite rises around Hyden Rock. In 1444 small bands moved between seasonal camps and granite gnammas, the rock holes that hold water long after the rains end, hunting and gathering around Katter Kich, Wave Rock, the curved granite wall 15 metres high and 110 metres long that forms the north face of Hyden Rock. A neighbouring Noongar group, the Ballardong, tell how the Wagyl, the great serpent of the Dreaming, shaped the wave as it dragged itself across the land. Njakinjaki speech was counted by some as a Noongar dialect and by others as a dialect of the neighbouring Kalaamaya language. Dutch and English ships touched only the far western coast, and in 1821 these inland rocks and waterholes had never been mapped by Europeans.
zh: 尼亚基-尼亚基是尼亚金贾基人的土地，位于格雷斯湖以东干旱的小麦带东部，约3.1万平方公里，海登岩周围遍布马洛桉灌丛、盐湖和光秃的花岗岩丘。1444年，小型族群往返于季节性营地与花岗岩水塘之间，这种岩坑在雨季结束后仍能长期存水；他们在卡特基奇，也就是波浪岩周围狩猎采集，那是海登岩北侧一道15米高、110米长的弧形花岗岩壁。邻近的巴拉栋农雅人传说，梦创时代的巨蛇瓦吉尔拖行过大地，塑出了这道波浪。尼亚金贾基话有人算作农雅语方言，也有人归入邻近的卡拉马亚语。荷兰和英国船只只到过遥远的西海岸，到1821年，这些内陆岩丘和水塘还从未被欧洲人测绘过。

en:
Yuat is the Yued country at the northern edge of Noongar lands, taking in the Indian Ocean coast between Ledge Point and Jurien Bay and running inland along Garban, the Moore River, to Gingin and New Norcia, nearly 17,000 square kilometres of coastal dunes, estuaries and inland woodland. In 1444 Yued families moved with the six Noongar seasons, camping in spring at the swamps and estuaries where turtles and frogs were plentiful and meeting in summer with the peoples to the north, where their craftsmen traded the hardwood fighting clubs and cutting tools they were known for. The deep pools of the Moore River were sacred, made in the Dreaming by the Wagyl serpent; northern neighbours called the Yued Minnalyungar, 'southern people'.

This coast holds the best-known Dutch wreck in Western Australia. On the night of 28 April 1656 the Dutch East India Company ship Vergulde Draeck, the Gilt Dragon, bound for Batavia with eight chests of silver coin, struck a reef between Seabird and Ledge Point. Of her 193 crew, 118 were lost and 75 reached the shore. Nine days later her under-steersman and six sailors put to sea in the ship's boat and reached Batavia after 41 days, crossing some 1,400 nautical miles with almost no water. Four rescue voyages between 1656 and 1659 lost more men in the coastal bush and found no survivor; a shore party in 1658 came upon only a circle of planks set upright in the sand, and another boat crew, cut off by storms and given up for dead, sailed its own small boat back to Batavia. A party from Emeloordt also met three Aboriginal people who spoke with them peacefully by signs, probably Yued. Nicolas Baudin's French survey passed the coast in 1801-1803 and named Jurien Bay, and in 1821 there was still no European settlement.
zh:
尤阿特是尤阿德人在农雅诸族北缘的土地，涵盖莱奇角至朱里恩湾之间的印度洋海岸，并沿古称加尔班的穆尔河向内陆延伸到金金和新诺尔恰，近1.7万平方公里，沿岸是沙丘与河口，内陆是林地。1444年，尤阿德家族按农雅人的六个物候季节迁徙：春天在沼泽和河口扎营，捕食龟、蛙，夏天与北方诸族聚会，族中匠人带去他们擅长制作的硬木格斗棍和切削工具交易。穆尔河的深潭是圣地，相传为梦创时代的彩虹蛇所开辟；北方邻族称他们为明纳利扬加，意为「南方人」。

这片海岸沉下了西澳最有名的荷兰沉船。1656年4月28日夜，荷兰东印度公司商船「镀金龙号」载着八箱银币驶往巴达维亚，在西博德与莱奇角之间触礁。全船193人中118人丧生，75人上岸。9天后，二副带6名水手驾小艇赴巴达维亚求救，在几乎断水的情况下横渡约1400海里，历时41天抵达。1656年至1659年，四支救援船队先后出发，又有人在海岸丛林中失踪，却没有找到一名幸存者；1658年的一支岸队只在沙滩上发现一圈竖立的木板，另有一艘小艇的船员被风浪隔断、以为必死，竟也驾船自行回到巴达维亚。「埃默洛德特号」的一支岸队还遇到三名原住民，双方以手势和平交谈，这些人很可能就是尤阿德人。1801年至1803年，尼古拉·博丹的法国考察队沿海岸测绘并命名朱里恩湾，到1821年这里仍没有欧洲定居点。

en:
The Kurrama are a Pilbara people whose country takes in the high plateaux and gorges of the Hamersley Range, running from Mount McCrae in the east to the headwaters of Duck Creek and the upper Hardey River in the south. The Hamersley is one of the oldest ranges on earth, its banded-iron rock folded into deep gorges whose pools hold water through the dry season, and gorge shelters here were lived in right through the last Ice Age. Norman Tindale estimated Kurrama lands at about 9,600 square kilometres. Their language is close to Yindjibarndi, though kept as a separate tongue, and the Kurrama share laws, country and waters with the neighbouring Pinikura. In 1444 only their own people knew these uplands.

Europe touched only the sea off the coast. In 1699 William Dampier, an English buccaneer turned hydrographer, brought the Roebuck along the Pilbara shore and named the islands he reached the Dampier Archipelago, calling one of them Rosemary Island after a scented shrub. No European party crossed the Hamersley before 1821, and Kurrama life kept to the gorges, waters and meeting grounds of its own country.
zh:
库拉玛人是皮尔布拉的原住民，家园在哈默斯利岭的高原与峡谷之间，东起麦克雷山，南抵达克溪源头和哈代河上游。哈默斯利岭是地球上最古老的山岭之一，带状铁岩被褶皱深切出峡谷，谷中水潭旱季仍有蓄水；这里的峡谷岩荫从上一个冰期起就一直有人居住。廷代尔估计库拉玛人的土地约9600平方公里。他们的语言与殷吉巴恩迪语十分接近，但使用者仍把它当作独立的语言；库拉玛人与相邻的皮尼库拉人共享律法、土地和水源。1444年时，熟悉这片高地的只有他们自己。

欧洲人只到过这片土地外海。1699年，由海盗改做水文测量师的英国人威廉·丹皮尔驾「罗巴克号」沿皮尔布拉海岸航行，把到达的岛群命名为丹皮尔群岛，又因一种气味芬芳的灌木把其中一岛称作迷迭香岛。1821年以前没有欧洲人进入哈默斯利岭，库拉玛人的生活仍守着自己土地上的峡谷、水潭与会合地。

en: The Mangarla, also written Mangala, hold some 40,000 square kilometres of the north-western Great Sandy Desert, country of long parallel dunes and spinifex around the McLarty Hills and reaching north to Geegully Creek and the head of the Edgar Range. Karajarri coast country lies to their west and Walmajarri country to their east. Their language belongs to the Marrngu group of the Pama–Nyungan family, and Mangala families travel and intermarry with Karajarri and Nyangumarta neighbours. Rain comes with summer thunderstorms and the occasional cyclone, and water lies hidden in soaks among the dunes; knowing those waters fixed the round of camps and meeting grounds. Perenties and thorny devils forage the sand, and the summer heat ranks among the fiercest in Australia. In 1444 the desert was known only to its own peoples, and no European crossing is recorded before 1821; Mangala life followed the seasons and waters of the inland.
zh: 曼加拉人（也拼作曼加拉尔拉）住在大沙沙漠西北缘，约四万平方公里的土地上遍布平行长沙丘和三齿稃，麦克拉蒂丘陵横亘其中，地界北到吉古利溪和埃德加岭。西面是卡拉贾里人的海岸之地，东面是瓦尔马贾里人的土地。他们的语言属帕马—尼永甘语系的马伦古语支，曼加拉家族与卡拉贾里、尼扬古马塔邻族往来通婚。雨水只随夏季雷暴和偶尔到来的气旋降下，水藏在沙丘间的渗坑里；认准这些水源，才排定了营地与会合地的迁徙次序。眼斑巨蜥和魔蜥在沙地上觅食，这里的夏天也是澳大利亚最酷热的地方之一。1444年时，这片沙漠仍只有本地族群熟知，1821年以前没有欧洲人穿越的记录，曼加拉人的生活只随内陆的季节和水源安排。

en:
The Wunambal are a saltwater people of the northern Kimberley. With the Gaambera they care for Uunguu, their land-and-sea country around York Sound, which runs from Brunswick Bay north to Admiralty Gulf and the Osborne Islands and inland to the divide of the King Edward River. Life here follows Wanjina-Wunggurr law, taught by cloud and rain spirits whose faces are painted on shelter walls: mouthless heads ringed with lightning, repainted each wet season to bring on the monsoon, alongside the older Gwion Gwion figures. Tides on this coast can rise twelve metres, and Tindale called the Wunambal among the most venturesome of Australian coastal peoples; the Laiau and Wardana bands sailed rafts out to sea reefs and the Cassini and Montalivet islands as far as Long Reef. Named clan estates took in Prince Frederick Harbour, Port Warrender and Cape Wellington. In 1444 the coast, its islands and its fresh water were all Wunambal country.

Makassan trepang fishermen from Sulawesi later worked these shores on the monsoon, leaving stone cooking hearths and a prayer alcove cut into a boab at Wunbung-gu, and dugout canoe-building spread from them along the coast. In September 1820 Lieutenant Phillip Parker King beached his survey cutter Mermaid at Wunbung-gu, now Careening Bay on Coronation Island, for eighteen days of repairs and had the carpenter carve 'Mermaid 1820' into a boab. His men saw bark shelters on the beach and larger huts on the hill and found the leavings of sago palm nuts, but met no one. No garrison followed, and in 1821 the Wunambal still held their island and mainland estates.
zh:
伍南布尔人是金伯利北部的海洋族群，与甘贝拉人共同守护称为乌恩古的土地与海域：其地以约克湾为中心，北从不伦瑞克湾延伸到阿德默勒尔蒂湾和奥斯本群岛，向内陆直抵金爱德华河分水岭。他们的生活遵循万吉纳—翁古尔律法；万吉纳是云和雨的精灵，脸绘在岩荫石壁上，没有嘴的头四周环绕闪电纹，人们每个雨季重新描彩以唤来季风，旁边还有更古老的吉温吉温岩画。这一带潮差可达十二米，廷代尔称伍南布尔人是澳大利亚最大胆的沿海族群之一；莱奥和瓦尔达纳两个氏族的人驾木筏出海，远航到卡西尼群岛、蒙塔利韦群岛以至长礁一带的海上礁石。弗雷德里克亲王港、沃伦德港和威灵顿角都是有名字传世的氏族领地。1444年时，海岸、海岛和岛上的淡水全是伍南布尔人的土地。

此后，来自苏拉威西的望加锡海参渔民乘季风来这些海岸作业，留下石砌煮参灶；在乌本古，一株猴面包树中还凿有祈祷壁龛，独木舟制造技术也随他们传到沿海各族群。1820年9月，海军上尉菲利普·帕克·金把测绘艇「美人鱼号」拖上乌本古（今科罗内申岛修船湾）的海滩修理十八天，让船匠在一株猴面包树上刻下「美人鱼号1820」。他的部下看见海滩上有树皮棚子、山丘上有更大的茅屋，还捡到西米椰子的残核，却没有遇见一个人。此后没有守军留下；1821年，伍南布尔人仍保有自己的海岛与大陆领地。

en:
Pyemmairrener country forms Tasmania's north-eastern corner. Cape Portland, called Tebrakunna, points across Ringarooma Bay to Banks Strait, where Clarke Island of the Furneaux Group lies about fifteen miles offshore; the strait's rocks and islands carried great colonies of fur seals. From the cape the coast runs west by Pipers River toward the Tamar estuary, while inland the Ben Lomond plateau rises as the country of the Plangermaireener. Pyemmairre was the language of Cape Portland, and later word lists were taken down there, at Pipers River and around Ben Lomond. In 1444, long after Bass Strait had parted Tasmania from the mainland, the headlands, rivers and offshore rocks belonged to this distinct north-eastern Palawa world.

The first European ship was the Norfolk, on the voyage that settled whether Van Diemen's Land was an island. In 1798 George Bass and Matthew Flinders took her through the strait and into the Tamar, then called Port Dalrymple; Flinders named the cape after the Duke of Portland and noted the seals thick on Clarke Island. Once those seals were reported, the Furneaux Group became the hardest-worked sealing ground in Bass Strait. In November 1804 Colonel William Paterson arrived with four ships and 181 soldiers, convicts and settlers to found the north's first British post at Outer Cove, later George Town. The camp soon shifted to York Town and then up the Tamar, becoming Launceston by March 1806, and Ensign H. Piper gave his name to the river east of the estuary. From 1810 sealing gangs lived on Clarke Island with Aboriginal women they had seized from the northern beaches; the sealer George Briggs had carried two such women off to the Furneaux Islands, and one of the children born there was Dolly Dalrymple. In 1821 the Tamar was a settled colonial district, while Tebrakunna still lay on the sealers' edge.
zh:
皮耶迈雷纳人的土地构成塔斯马尼亚的东北角。本名特布拉昆纳（Tebrakunna）的波特兰角隔着林加鲁马湾与班克斯海峡相望，外海约十五英里处是弗诺群岛中的克拉克岛；海峡的岩礁和海岛上栖息着大群毛皮海豹。海岸从岬角向西经派珀斯河通向泰马河口，内陆则耸起本洛蒙德高原，那里是普兰格迈雷纳人（Plangermaireener）的高地乡野。皮耶迈雷语（Pyemmairre）曾通行于波特兰角，后世的语言词表分别采录于当地、派珀斯河和本洛蒙德一带。1444年，在巴斯海峡把塔斯马尼亚与大陆分隔很久以后，这些岬角、河流和近海岩礁仍属于这个独立的东北部帕拉瓦世界。

第一艘欧洲船是「诺福克号」，这趟航行要回答范迪门斯地是不是一座岛屿。1798年，乔治·贝斯与马修·弗林德斯驾船穿过海峡，进入当时称达尔林普尔港的泰马河口；弗林德斯以波特兰公爵之名为岬角命名，还记下克拉克岛上海豹成群。海豹的消息一经传出，弗诺群岛便成了巴斯海峡上开发最烈的捕海豹场。1804年11月，威廉·帕特森上校率四艘船、181名士兵、罪犯和移民抵达，在后来成为乔治敦的外湾建立塔斯马尼亚北部第一个英国据点。营地不久迁往约克镇，再沿泰马河上移，1806年3月形成朗塞斯顿；H·派珀少尉也把河口以东的河流冠以自己的姓氏。1810年起，捕海豹帮伙带着从北部海滩掳走的原住民妇女在克拉克岛上常住；海豹帮乔治·布里格斯此前把两名这样的女子掳到弗诺群岛，多利·达尔林普尔（Dolly Dalrymple）就是岛上出生的孩子之一。1821年，泰马河已是稳固的殖民地区，特布拉昆纳则仍处在捕海豹者的边疆边缘。

en:
Peerapper sea country runs along Tasmania's far north-western coast, from Kennaook, the headland Europeans later named Cape Grim, to Circular Head, Robbins Passage and Robbins Island. The Parperloihener band lived on Robbins Island, while other Peerapper families moved with the seasons among wallaby grasslands kept open by fire, seal rocks, short-tailed shearwater burrows, shellfish beds and fishing places. The coast lies open to the Roaring Forties, and Bass Strait had long separated these Tasmanian communities from mainland Australia. In 1444 the headlands, tidal channels and islands belonged to north-western Palawa clans, with no foreign sealers or garrison.

Abel Tasman put Tasmania on European charts in 1642, but his landfall was on the eastern side. On 7 December 1798 Matthew Flinders reached this coast in the Norfolk during his circumnavigation of Van Diemen's Land and named Circular Head and Cape Grim. The long swell rolling in from the south-west showed open sea west of the coast, confirming that a strait separated Van Diemen's Land from mainland Australia. Sealers and whalers began to work nearby islands soon afterward, and British convict posts were founded on the Derwent in 1803 and the Tamar in 1804. Those posts lay far from Kennaook; in 1821 Peerapper country still had no European settlement.
zh:
皮拉佩尔人的海洋之地沿塔斯马尼亚西北角海岸延伸，从欧洲人后来称格里姆角的肯纳乌克，一直到瑟丘勒黑德、罗宾斯水道和罗宾斯岛。罗宾斯岛上的氏族在岛上居住，其他皮拉佩尔家族则按季节往来于烧荒维持的沙袋鼠草地、海豹岩礁、短尾鹱洞穴、贝滩和渔场。海岸直迎咆哮西风带，巴斯海峡早已把这些塔斯马尼亚社群与澳大利亚大陆隔开。1444年，岬角、潮汐水道和岛屿属于西北部帕拉瓦氏族，没有外来猎海豹者或驻军。

阿贝尔·塔斯曼1642年把塔斯马尼亚标上欧洲海图，但登陆点在岛东。1798年12月7日，马修·弗林德斯乘「诺福克号」环绕范迪门地航行时到达这处海岸，命名瑟丘勒黑德和格里姆角。西南方涌来的长浪说明海岸以西是开阔海洋，确认范迪门地与澳大利亚大陆之间隔有海峡。猎海豹者和捕鲸者很快开始在附近岛屿作业；英国流放据点于1803年设在德文特河畔，1804年设在塔马尔河畔。这些据点离肯纳乌克很远，1821年的皮拉佩尔之地仍没有欧洲定居点。

en:
High on the Connecticut, the Kwenitekw or Long River, the current sweeps round a great oxbow below the White Mountains, enclosing broad intervales of deep alluvial soil where salmon ran thick. Here stood Cowass, the chief village of the Cowasuck band of the Western Abenaki. Their name Goasek means 'white pines place', and the tall pines gave the whole upper valley its later name of Coos; women grew maize and squash on the meadows and men hunted the hills. Paths from the headwaters that feed the St Lawrence met those that run down to the sea, so war parties and envoys passed through Cowass in both directions. In 1444 no European had yet reached the upper Connecticut.

The long colonial wars reached Cowass early. In 1704 its chiefs travelled down to Quebec to meet Governor-General Vaudreuil, who offered them land nearer the French settlements, and they refused. The same year raiders brought captives from the sack of Deerfield up the river to Cowass, among them the boy Stephen Williams, who was kept with the sachem George Tahanto. By 1712 Mohegan raids had made the village unsafe and it was deserted, although the Abenaki reoccupied it after peace returned. They harried the English frontier as allies of France through the French and Indian War of 1754 to 1763.

The first English family at the oxbow, Samuel Sleeper's, arrived in 1762, and on 18 March 1763 Governor Benning Wentworth chartered the town as Newbury to Jacob Bayley and seventy-four associates. During the Revolutionary War Bayley and Colonel Moses Hazen drove a military road north from Newbury toward St John's near Montreal, clearing fifty-four miles between 1776 and 1779 for an invasion of Canada that was never launched. By 1798 most of the Cowasuck had withdrawn to the Abenaki mission village of St Francis (Odanak) in Quebec.
zh:
原住民称康涅狄格河为奎尼特库（Kwenitekw），意为「长河」。在它的上游，河水在怀特山下绕出一个大河湾，环抱着土层深厚的冲积滩地，河里鲑鱼成群。西阿布纳基人科瓦苏克部的主要村镇科瓦斯就坐落在这里。其名Goasek意为「白松之地」，高大的白松使整个上游谷地后来得名「库斯」；妇女在滩地上种植玉米和南瓜，男子在周围山地狩猎。注入圣劳伦斯河的诸水源头与顺流奔海的水路在这一带相接，战队和使臣取道科瓦斯往来南北。1444年时，还没有欧洲人到过康涅狄格河上游。

漫长的殖民战争很早就波及科瓦斯。1704年，村里的酋长前往魁北克会见总督沃德勒伊，对方拨出土地请他们迁近法兰西定居点，他们没有接受。同年，袭掠者把洗劫迪尔菲尔德得来的俘虏沿河押到科瓦斯，其中有少年斯蒂芬·威廉斯，他被留在酋长乔治·塔汉托身边。到1712年，莫黑根人的袭掠使村镇不再安全，村民弃村他去，和平恢复后又重返故地。在1754至1763年的法国—印第安人战争中，他们作为法兰西的盟友不断袭扰英格兰人的边疆。

1762年，塞缪尔·斯利珀一家成为头一个到河湾定居的英格兰家庭；1763年3月18日，总督本宁·温特沃思把这片地方特许给雅各布·贝利及其七十四名同伙，设镇纽伯里。独立战争期间，贝利与摩西·黑森上校从纽伯里向北朝蒙特利尔附近的圣约翰斯修筑军用道路，1776至1779年开辟出五十四英里，为的是进军加拿大，这场进攻最终没有发动。到1798年，多数科瓦苏克人已北撤至魁北克的阿布纳基传教村圣弗朗西斯（奥达纳克）。

en:
The Wenro (Wenrohronon, 'people at the place of the floating scum') were a small Iroquoian nation wedged between the Neutral towns near Niagara and the Seneca, the westernmost people of the Haudenosaunee. Their name came from the dark film of petroleum on a spring in the upper Allegheny oil country, the first recorded source of petroleum in what is now the United States; Wenro families gathered its oil and used it as medicine. In 1444 they farmed maize, beans and squash around bark longhouses and hunted beaver in forests whose pelts fed the northern trade, while Neutral protection kept the Seneca at a distance.

The French interpreter Étienne Brûlé may have crossed Wenro country in 1615 while scouting the nations south of the Wendat, and the Récollet Joseph de La Roche Daillon reached the oil spring in 1627 and wrote down how the Wenro used the black oil. Their shelter ended in the late 1630s, when the Neutral withdrew their protection for reasons the French missionaries could not explain and Seneca raids began. Rather than wait to be destroyed, the Wenro asked the Wendat for land: in the summer of 1638 more than six hundred men, women and children walked some 240 miles through Neutral territory to the Wendat town of Ossossané on Nottawasaga Bay, many arriving sick. A few families stayed among the Neutral or were taken by the Seneca. Those who reached Ossossané fled west with the Wendat a decade later, when Haudenosaunee armies destroyed the Wendat towns, and their descendants merged into the people later called the Wyandot. The old hunting grounds became Seneca borderland through the Beaver Wars. Most Seneca fought for Britain in the American Revolution, and the 1794 Treaty of Canandaigua kept the oil-spring country in Seneca hands as the Oil Spring Reservation.
zh:
温罗人（Wenrohronon，省名作文罗霍嫩）是一支人口不多的易洛魁语族群，夹在尼亚加拉一带的中立人村镇与豪德诺索尼最西端的塞尼卡人之间。族名意为「浮膜之地的人」，得名于阿勒格尼河上游油乡一处泉面上黑色的原油薄膜；这处油泉是今美国境内最早见诸记载的石油产地，温罗人采集泉中的油当作药物。1444年，温罗人在树皮长屋周围种植玉米、菜豆和南瓜，在森林里捕猎供给北方贸易的河狸；中立人的庇护使塞尼卡人一时难以逼近。

法国译员艾蒂安·布吕莱1615年替温达特人探查南方部族时，可能曾穿过温罗人的土地。1627年，重整派修士约瑟夫·德·拉罗什·达永走到油泉，记下了温罗人使用这种黑油的方法。1630年代末，温罗人的庇护消失了：中立人收回保护，法国传教士也说不清缘由，塞尼卡人的袭掠随之而来。温罗人不愿坐以待毙，向温达特人求取容身之地；1638年夏，六百多名男女老幼穿过中立人的土地，步行约240英里，抵达诺塔瓦萨加湾畔的温达特村镇奥索萨内，许多人到达时已身患疾病。也有几户人家留在中立人那里，或被塞尼卡人收留。十年后豪德诺索尼军队摧毁温达特诸城，来到奥索萨内的温罗人又随温达特人西逃，后人最终汇入怀恩多特人。旧日猎场在海狸战争中成了塞尼卡人的边地。美国独立战争中多数塞尼卡人站在英国一方作战，1794年的《卡南代瓜条约》把油泉一带留给塞尼卡人，设为油泉保留地。

en:
Pegwaki is the upper Saco country, where the river loops out of the White Mountains foothills through broad intervales at Pequawket, the sharp bend where Fryeburg later stands. The Saco gave the village fish, fertile bottomland and a canoe route down to Saco Bay, and kinship and river trails linked its people with the other Wabanaki bands. They were a Sokoki-related Eastern Abenaki community. In 1444 the bend was an Indigenous village ground, with no European post above the river mouth.

Around 1700 the village hired English carpenters to raise a fourteen-foot palisade against Mohawk raids, and its sachems signed the 1713 Treaty of Portsmouth with the English colonies. The peace did not hold. On 9 May 1725, in Dummer's War, John Lovewell led 47 volunteer scalp hunters to a pond beside the village, 34 of them fighting after a garrison was left on the march. Morning prayer had just ended when the firing began. Lovewell and the Abenaki chief Paugus were both killed, while the rangers were pinned between the lake, a swollen brook and fallen trees; barely 20 of them lived through the day. The Pequawket survivors abandoned the bend, withdrew to the Connecticut River and later moved to French Canada, and the fight, called Lovewell's Fight, was sung in New England ballads for generations. The Pequawket healer Molly Ockett, born about 1740, later worked as a midwife and herbalist among settlers across northern New England. Massachusetts granted the empty intervales to Joseph Frye in 1762, and the town was incorporated as Fryeburg in 1777.
zh:
佩瓜基地处萨科河上游，河水从怀特山山麓绕出，在佩阔克特的宽阔滩地上转出一道急弯，弗赖堡后来就建在这道河曲上。萨科河为村落提供鱼获、肥沃的低地，以及顺流直下萨科湾的独木舟水路，亲属关系和河路又把村民同其他瓦巴纳基群体连在一起。他们是与索科基人关系密切的一支东阿布纳基人。1444年时，河曲上还是原住民的村落之地，河口以上没有欧洲人的据点。

1700年前后，村落雇用英国木匠筑起十四英尺高的栅栏，以抵御莫霍克人的袭击；1713年，村中首领又与英国殖民地签订《朴次茅斯条约》。和平没有维持住。1725年5月9日达默战争期间，约翰·洛夫韦尔率四十七名志愿猎取头皮者来到村边一座池塘旁，途中留下守军后，参战的只剩三十四人。晨祷刚结束，战斗便打响了。洛夫韦尔和阿布纳基首领保古斯双双战死，英国人被湖泊、涨水的溪流和倒伏的树木困在中间，只有约二十人活过当天的战斗。幸存的佩阔克特人放弃河曲，先退到康涅狄格河一带，后来又迁往法属加拿大；这场被称为「洛夫韦尔之战」的战斗，此后几代都在新英格兰的歌谣里传唱。佩阔克特草药医妇莫莉·奥基特约1740年出生，后来在新英格兰北部的定居者中间以助产和草药行医。1762年，马萨诸塞把空下来的滩地授予约瑟夫·弗莱，1777年这里正式设镇，定名弗赖堡。

en:
In the upper valley of the Housatonic, where the Berkshires and the Taconic highlands face each other across meadow and forest, lay Westenhuck, 'beyond the mountains' in the Algonquian tongue. Its people, often called the Housatonic Indians, were one of the five divisions of the Mahican confederacy; their chief village stood near Mahaiwe, the 'place downstream', now Great Barrington. They raised maize, beans and squash, took fish at their weirs and traded the furs of the western woods. In 1444 the valley villages lay on the quiet eastern flank of the Mahican world, though the long feud with the Mohawk beyond the Hudson was never far away.

That feud went against the Mahicans, and after Henry Hudson's men drew the nation into the Dutch fur trade in 1609, defeated bands drifted east across the Taconics; from the 1680s refugees joined the Westenhuck villages. In 1724 the sachem Konkapot sold the lower Housatonic township to Massachusetts men, and Sheffield, settled the next year and incorporated in 1733, became the first English town in the Berkshires. John Sergeant opened a mission nearby in 1734, incorporated as Stockbridge in 1739, where Mahican and Wappinger families learned English, settled farming and Christianity; the theologian Jonathan Edwards later served its church.

Among the Wappinger who settled there was Daniel Nimham, who kept house at Westenhuck from 1746 and went to law again and again over the lands his people had lost. In 1766 he sailed to London with three Mahican chiefs and carried the case to the crown's Lords of Trade, who found grounds to investigate the New York manor lords; the inquiry came to nothing. In the Revolution Nimham and his son Abraham led the Stockbridge warriors on the American side, serving before Boston and at Valley Forge, and on 31 August 1778 Simcoe's Queen's Rangers caught their company at Kingsbridge in what is now the Bronx; Nimham fell with most of his men. In 1781 Elizabeth Freeman, a woman held as a slave in the county, sued for her liberty at the Great Barrington court and won, a ruling that helped put an end to slavery in Massachusetts. The last fight of Shays' Rebellion was waged at Sheffield in February 1787, and by the end of the decade the Stockbridge families had left the valley to settle among the Oneida in New York.
zh:
胡萨托尼克河上游的河谷里，伯克希尔丘陵与塔科尼克高地隔著林野草甸相望，韦斯滕胡克就在这里，阿尔冈昆语意为「山那边」。这里的人常被称为胡萨托尼克印第安人，是莫希干联盟五大分支之一；主村邻近一个叫马海韦（意为「下游之地」）的地方，即后来的大巴灵顿。他们种植玉米、豆子和南瓜，在鱼堰捕鱼，用西部山林的毛皮进行贸易。1444年时，河谷村落处在莫希干世界僻静的东翼，但与哈得孙河以西莫霍克人的世仇从未真正远去。

这场世仇以莫希干人失利告终。1609年亨利·哈得孙的船队把整个部族带入荷兰人的毛皮贸易之后，战败的群体陆续东渡塔科尼克山，1680年代起一批批难民投奔韦斯滕胡克诸村。1724年，酋长孔卡波特把胡萨托尼克下游的镇区卖给马萨诸塞人；谢菲尔德次年即有人定居，1733年设治，成为伯克希尔第一个英裔城镇。约翰·萨金特1734年在附近开设传教站，1739年设为斯托克布里奇镇，莫希干和瓦平杰家族在这里学英语、学定居农耕，也皈依基督教；神学家乔纳森·爱德华兹后来在此牧会。

迁来的瓦平杰人中有一位丹尼尔·尼纳姆，他1746年起在韦斯滕胡克安家，为族人失去的土地一再打官司。1766年，他偕同三名莫希干酋长渡海赴伦敦，把案子递到英王的贸易委员会面前，委员会认为确有理由查究纽约庄园主，调查最终却不了了之。独立战争中，尼纳姆和儿子亚伯拉罕率斯托克布里奇战士站在美利坚一边，曾在波士顿城外和瓦利福奇作战；1778年8月31日，西姆科的女王游骑兵在今日布朗克斯境内的金斯布里奇突袭他们的连队，尼纳姆与大多数部下战死。1781年，在本县为奴的伊丽莎白·弗里曼在大巴灵顿法院起诉争取自由并胜诉，这一判决推动了马萨诸塞奴隶制的终结。1787年2月，谢斯起义的最后一战在谢菲尔德打响；到1780年代末，斯托克布里奇的家族已离开河谷，迁往纽约州，依附奥奈达人而居。

en:
Welhikhane is the Lenape river name preserved in the later word Allegheny. The upper watercourse rises in the Pennsylvania hills, makes its New York bend above Cattaraugus country, and turns southwest through wooded gorges toward the Ohio. In 1444 this was the southern edge of an Iroquoian world: Wenro and Erie communities held nearby upper-valley lands, while Seneca and Cayuga towns lay beyond the northern plateau. Bark longhouses stood by maize, bean and squash fields, and the river and ridge paths carried beaver pelts, deerskins and war parties between the Ohio headwaters and the Great Lakes.

The Beaver Wars changed that map. Haudenosaunee forces defeated the Wenro and Erie and, by the later seventeenth century, ranged far down the Allegheny. Lenape families founded Kittanning in 1724 at the western end of the Kittanning Path, and the river town soon drew Shawnee, Seneca, Cayuga and other displaced families; by 1756 it had 300 to 400 people and served as a staging point for French-allied Lenape and Shawnee raids on Pennsylvania. Pennsylvania traders and French envoys had both used the town, and a captive's report described more than a hundred English prisoners there. On 8 September 1756 Lieutenant Colonel John Armstrong led 300 provincial troops through the forest and burned Kittanning. Powder stored in the houses exploded in the fire; Lenape chief Captain Jacobs was killed, and many survivors withdrew west toward Fort Duquesne.
zh:
韦尔希卡内是保存在后来「阿勒格尼」一名中的莱纳佩语河名。上游水道从宾夕法尼亚丘陵出发，绕过纽约州南部卡塔拉格斯地带旁的河曲，再向西南穿过林木峡谷，流向俄亥俄河。1444年，这里处在易洛魁世界南缘：温罗人和伊利人的社群据有附近的上游谷地，塞尼卡与卡尤加村镇则位于北方高原之外。树皮长屋旁种着玉米、菜豆和南瓜；河流与山脊小径在俄亥俄河源和五大湖之间运送河狸皮、鹿皮，也通行战队。

海狸战争改变了这幅格局。豪德诺索尼军队击垮温罗人和伊利人，到17世纪后期，其猎人和战队已深入阿勒格尼河下游。1724年，莱纳佩家族在基坦宁小径西端建立基坦宁；这座河畔村镇很快吸引肖尼、塞尼卡、卡尤加和其他流离者，到1756年约有三百至四百居民，并成为与法国结盟的莱纳佩、肖尼战队袭击宾夕法尼亚的出发地。宾夕法尼亚商人和法国使者都曾利用这里，一名被俘者的报告称镇中有一百多名英格兰囚犯。1756年9月8日，约翰·阿姆斯特朗中校率三百名省军穿过森林焚毁基坦宁。屋中储存的火药在大火中爆炸，莱纳佩酋长雅各布战死，许多幸存者向西撤往迪凯纳堡。

en:
Scahentowanen, 'a very great plain', was the Iroquoian name for the Wyoming Flats, the bottomland where the Lackawanna joins the North Branch of the Susquehanna above later Wilkes-Barre. In 1444 the people later called Scahentoarrhonon farmed maize by the river, fished the channels with weirs and hunted the surrounding ridges, and their trails ran north to Cayuga and Onondaga, downriver to the Susquehannock towns and east through the Poconos to Lenape country.

Written records reach the flats only in the next century: Champlain sent an embassy here in 1615, and a Jesuit Relation of 1635 located three towns, by then trading with the Dutch. In the winter of 1652 a Haudenosaunee war party reportedly surprised about a thousand Scahentoarrhonon and carried off five or six hundred for adoption into the Five Nations; the survivors were absorbed as well.

Settlers sent by Connecticut's Susquehanna Company arrived in 1762 and fought Pennsylvania for the valley through the Pennamite land wars, holding the upper hand by 1771. On 3 July 1778 John Butler's Loyalists and Seneca warriors routed the valley's Patriot militia, killing about three hundred men in what became known as the Wyoming Massacre. Settlers fled across the Poconos or down the Susquehanna, and a newspaper falsely reported the killing of hundreds of women and children. John Sullivan made the plain his staging base the next year, and in 1782 a Continental Congress commission awarded the valley to Pennsylvania.
zh:
斯卡恩托瓦嫩（Scahentowanen）意为「很大的平原」，是易洛魁语对怀俄明平原的称呼；拉克万纳河在后来的威尔克斯-巴里上方，于这片低地汇入萨斯奎哈纳河北支。1444年，后来被称为斯卡亨托阿罗农（Scahentoarrhonon）的族群在河畔种玉米，在水道里设鱼梁捕鱼，在周围山岭狩猎；他们的小径向北通往卡尤加和奥农多加，向下游通往萨斯奎汉诺克诸镇，向东穿过波科诺山地进入莱纳佩人地区。

这片平原直到下一世纪才进入文字记载：1615年尚普兰派人出使到此，1635年的一份《耶稣会报道》记载当地有三座城镇，那时他们已经同荷兰人贸易。1652年冬，豪德诺索尼的战队据记载奇袭约一千名斯卡亨托阿罗农人，带走五六百人收进五族各部落，幸存者也同样被吸收。

1762年，康涅狄格萨斯奎哈纳公司派来的移民进入谷地，为争夺土地同宾州打了多年佩纳米特战争，到1771年已占上风。1778年7月3日，约翰·巴特勒率领的效忠派和塞内卡战士击溃谷地的爱国者民兵，约三百人被杀，这就是后来所称的怀俄明大屠杀。移民们翻过波科诺山或顺萨斯奎哈纳河逃走，而一家报纸虚报有数百名妇孺遇害。次年约翰·沙利文把这片平原作为进军集结地；1782年，大陆会议委员会把谷地判归宾夕法尼亚。

en:
The Nottoway call themselves Cheroenhaka, and their Iroquoian language was close to that of the Meherrin and Tuscarora. Their three towns lay west of the Fall Line, on the Nottoway River, Stony Creek and the Rowantee Branch, where cornfields met pine hunting grounds. Algonquian neighbours knew them as dealers in shell beads, deerskins and otter skins, and one reading of the name Nottoway is 'traders'. In 1444 no European had reached their valley.

Edward Bland reached them from Fort Henry on 27 August 1650 and found 400 to 500 people under two brother chiefs, Oyeocker and Chounerounte. A Nottoway representative signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation in 1680, making the tribe tributary to Virginia, but squatters still crossed its bounds. Warfare forced the Nottoway south twice, while newly introduced diseases reduced the towns, and survivors of the Weyanoke and Nansemond joined them. In 1711 two Nottoway boys entered the College of William and Mary. A treaty of 1713 confirmed two small tracts, yet piecemeal sales over the next forty years removed most of the land. A count in 1772 found 35 Nottoway on the reserve; the land sale of 1794 named only seventeen men, women and children.
zh:
诺托韦人自称切罗恩哈卡，所操易洛魁语与梅赫林人、塔斯卡洛拉人的语言相近。他们的三座城镇位于瀑布线以西，分别在诺托韦河、斯托尼克里克和罗万蒂支流一带，镇外是玉米地和可供狩猎的松林。阿尔冈昆邻族把他们看作贝珠、鹿皮和水獭皮的交易者，还有一种解释把「诺托韦」这个他称理解为「商人」。1444年，还没有欧洲人到达这条河谷。

1650年8月27日，爱德华·布兰德从亨利堡西行至此，见到两位兄弟首领治下的四五百人。1680年，诺托韦代表签署《中种植园条约》，部落成为弗吉尼亚的纳贡者，但占地者仍越过边界。战乱迫使他们两度南迁，新传入的疾病又削弱了城镇，韦亚诺科人和楠西蒙德人的残部也陆续加入。1711年，两名诺托韦男孩进入威廉与玛丽学院。1713年的条约确认了两块小土地，随后四十多年间的分次售地却拿走了大部分土地。1772年，保留地上只剩三十五名诺托韦人；1794年售地时，在册的男女老幼只有十七人。

en:
The Eno is a short river of the eastern Piedmont, named for the Siouan farmers who worked its valley. Their chief town, Œnock, stood on the Great Indian Trading Path, over which deerskins and shell beads moved from the mountains toward Virginia. The Eno gathered three grain crops in a summer, kept granaries that supplied neighbouring towns, and hired themselves out as carriers along the path. They lived in round, mud-plastered houses under the judgments of their elders, and in 1444 no European had yet entered the valley.

John Lederer walked into Œnock in 1670, and James Needham and Gabriel Arthur passed 'Aeno' in 1673. When Nathaniel Bacon destroyed the Occaneechi trading island in the Roanoke in 1676, the survivors rebuilt on the Eno near the later Hillsborough; John Lawson found them there in 1701, living beside the Eno, Shakori and Adshusheer under a chief called Enoe Will. The Eno themselves merged into the Catawba around 1715.

Settlers laid out Hillsborough at the old river ford in 1754, and the farmers' Regulation made the little courthouse town its centre: they shut the courts and dragged officials through the streets until Governor William Tryon's militia scattered them on Alamance Creek on 16 May 1771 and hanged six of their leaders in the town on 19 June. The Provincial Congress met at Hillsborough in 1775 to put the colony on a war footing, and the first convention called to consider the federal Constitution sat there in 1788; in between, the Loyalist raider David Fanning took the town in 1781 and threw the market-house bell into the Eno. In 1789 the assembly chartered the University of North Carolina, which opened its doors at Chapel Hill in 1795.
zh:
埃诺是皮德蒙特东部一条不长的河，河名来自在河谷里耕作的苏语部落埃诺人。他们的主城奥诺克坐落在「大印第安商路」旁，鹿皮和贝壳珠沿这条路从山区运往弗吉尼亚。埃诺人一个夏天收三茬谷物，谷仓充实，时常接济邻近城镇，还受雇在商路上替人搬运货物。他们住圆形的灰泥房屋，听从族中老者裁断；1444年，还没有欧洲人走进这座谷地。

约翰·莱德勒1670年走进奥诺克，詹姆斯·尼达姆和加布里埃尔·阿瑟1673年途经「埃诺」。1676年，纳撒尼尔·培根摧毁了奥卡内基人在罗阿诺克河上的贸易岛，幸存者迁到埃诺河畔、后来希尔斯伯勒附近的地方重建；1701年约翰·劳森在那里见到他们，与埃诺人、沙科里人、阿德舒希尔人比邻而居，首领叫「埃诺的威尔」。埃诺人自己在1715年前后并入卡托巴人。

1754年，移民在旧日河渡口开辟希尔斯伯勒，农民的规约运动把这座小县城当成大本营：他们关闭法庭、把官吏拖到街上，直到1771年5月16日威廉·特赖恩总督的民兵在阿拉曼斯溪将他们驱散，并于6月19日在城中绞死六名首领。1775年，省议会在希尔斯伯勒开会，为殖民地参战做准备；审查联邦宪法的第一次全州会议1788年也在此召开。其间1781年，效忠派头目大卫·范宁袭占城镇，把市场大楼的钟扔进了埃诺河。1789年，议会特许设立北卡罗来纳大学，学校1795年在教堂山开学。

en:
Kituwa lies on the upper Tuckasegee in the Great Smoky Mountains, a short way above where the Oconaluftee joins it. Around AD 1000 South Appalachian Mississippian farmers raised the earthen platform mound that marks the town, and the Cherokee built their townhouse on its flat top and rebuilt it again and again; inside, the sacred flame was kept burning while the Ani-kitu-hwagi gathered for counsel. They called Kituwa the first of their seven mother towns and the head of the Out Towns strung along the Tuckasegee and Oconaluftee, whose warriors held the northern border against Iroquois and Algonquian raiders. In time the people of these mountains called themselves by the town's name: Kituwah, the Cherokee. In 1444 no European had yet seen the mound in its valley.

De Soto's chroniclers first heard of the Cherokee from east of the mountains, at Joara in 1540, and wrote the name down as Chalaque. The Cherokee took the British side in the American Revolution, and after they struck the Watauga settlements in July 1776 General Griffith Rutherford led 2,400 North Carolina militiamen through the Oconaluftee and Tuckasegee valleys, burning the Middle Towns with Kituwa among them. Some of its people drifted back after the peace and rebuilt on the old ground, but treaties then stripped the mother town away; by 1819 the Kituwa country had been ceded to the United States.
zh:
基图瓦位于大雾山中的塔卡塞吉河上游，距奥科纳卢夫提河汇入口不远。约公元1000年，南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化的农人堆起这座土筑墩台，切罗基人在平顶上建起议事堂，又一次次将它翻建；堂中圣火常年不熄，阿尼基图赫瓦吉人在此聚会议事。他们把基图瓦奉为七大母镇之首，统领塔卡塞吉河与奥科纳卢夫提河沿岸的外镇，其战士镇守北境，抵御易洛魁人和阿尔冈昆人的袭掠。后来山里人干脆以镇名称呼自己：基图瓦，也就是切罗基人。1444年，没有一个欧洲人见过这座河谷里的土墩。

1540年，德·索托的书记官在山以东的乔阿拉首次听说切罗基人，把名字记作「查拉克」。独立战争中切罗基人站在英国一边；1776年7月他们袭掠沃托加定居点后，格里菲思·拉瑟福德将军率两千四百名北卡罗来纳民兵开进奥科纳卢夫提与塔卡塞吉河谷，焚毁中部诸镇，基图瓦也在其中。和平之后，部分居民陆续返回旧地重建，母镇却在随后的条约中被一步步夺去：到1819年，基图瓦一带已割让给美国。

en:
The Combahee is a blackwater Lowcountry river, born where the Salkehatchie and its Little branch meet, winding through marsh and live-oak forest to Saint Helena Sound near Beaufort. It took its name from the Combahee, one of the Cusabo tribes whose villages shared the coast between the later sites of Charleston and Savannah. Settlers recorded five of these tribes speaking one language, unrelated to Algonquian, Iroquoian, Siouan or Muskogean. In 1444 their river crossings, hunting grounds and villages still made up part of that loose Cusabo web.

English colonists founded Charles Town on Cusabo land in 1670 and made war on the Kussoe and Stono before the nearby tribes submitted. The Westo, slave raiders armed by the new colony, harried every people around them until Carolina turned on the Westo and destroyed them in 1679 and 1680. The Cusabo who stayed became the colony's Settlement Indians, paid in trade goods to bring in game, kill wolves and cougars, and hunt down runaway enslaved people; lands along several rivers, the Combahee among them, were granted to incoming Yamasee. In the Yamasee War of 1715 the Cusabo fought for Carolina, and afterwards most moved off to join the Catawba or the Muscogee. Their river then watered rice fields diked out of the tidal swamp. On 27 August 1782 a British foraging party on the bank met American fire in one of the last skirmishes before Charleston was evacuated. John Laurens, the 27-year-old abolitionist who had been an aide-de-camp to Washington, was killed there.
zh:
卡姆比河是低地南部的一条黑水河，由索尔克哈奇河与小索尔克哈奇河汇流而成，穿过沼泽和长满活栎的海岸林，在博福特附近注入圣赫勒拿湾。河名来自卡姆比人，他们是库萨博诸部之一，村镇分布在日后查尔斯顿与萨凡纳之间的沿岸；殖民者记录说其中五部共用一种语言，与阿尔冈昆、易洛魁、苏语、穆斯科格各语系都不相干。1444年，河畔的渡口、猎场和村庄还都属于这张松散的库萨博网络。

1670年，英国殖民者在库萨博人的土地上建起查尔斯镇，先与库索部、斯托诺部交战，附近各部才告屈服。韦斯托人仗着新殖民地供给的武器四处掳人为奴，袭扰四周所有部族，后来卡罗来纳反目，在1679年至1680年将其消灭。留下来的库萨博人成了殖民地的「定居印第安人」：缴纳猎物、捕杀狼和美洲狮、追拿逃亡奴隶，以此换取货物；卡姆比河等几条河的沿岸土地则被划给迁入的亚马西人。1715年亚马西战争中，库萨博人为卡罗来纳作战，战后多数人迁走，投奔卡托巴人或穆斯科吉人。他们的河后来浇灌着从潮汐沼泽围堤开出的稻田。1782年8月27日，在查尔斯顿撤守前的最后几场小战之一中，岸上一支英军征粮队与美军交火；曾在华盛顿身边任副官的27岁废奴主义者约翰·劳伦斯中弹身亡。

en:
Sabacola, named Sawokli in English records, was the southernmost of the Apalachicola towns, which stood in a line along the lower Chattahoochee above its meeting with the Flint. Its people were usually described as Hitchiti speakers, and the Hitchiti reading of the name is sawi, 'raccoon', plus ukli, 'town'. Its trail ran straight south to Apalachee, so in 1444 the town already sat between two Indian worlds, its maize fields and square ground untouched by Europeans.

It became the only Apalachicola town to accept Spanish friars. Bishop Calderon dedicated the mission Santa Cruz de Sabacola in 1675 at Sabacola el Menor near the river junction, and Chief Baltazar marched with the Spanish against the Chisca in 1677 before leading his people north to the other Chattahoochee towns. When friars came again in 1679 at the Christians' request, the chief of Coweta, the strongest town and a friend of the English-allied Westos, arrived and turned them out within three days; another attempt in 1681 failed the same way. English trade goods then drew the Chattahoochee towns east to the Ocmulgee in 1690-91, and Sawokli joined the raids that destroyed the Apalachee missions. After the Yamasee War the town returned to the Chattahoochee, where Diego Pena counted 84 warriors in 1716. When Spain ceded Florida in 1763, its Christian families sailed with the other evacuees from San Marcos to Havana.
zh:
萨巴科拉（英文记录中作萨沃克利）是阿巴拉契科拉诸镇中最靠南的一座，诸镇沿查特胡奇河下游、与弗林特河汇流处以北一字排开。其居民通常被认为操希奇蒂语，镇名按希奇蒂语解作「浣熊」（sawi）加「城镇」（ukli）。镇中小路直通南方的阿巴拉契，所以早在1444年，这座城镇就夹在两个印第安世界之间，玉米地和广场上还没有欧洲人的踪影。

它后来成为唯一接纳西班牙修道士的阿巴拉契科拉城镇。1675年，卡尔德龙主教在汇流处附近的小萨巴科拉为圣克鲁斯·德萨巴科拉传教站祝圣；首领巴尔塔萨尔1677年随西班牙人出征奇斯卡人，随后率部北投查特胡奇诸镇。1679年修道士应信教居民之请再来，最强的考维塔镇与英国人支持的韦斯托人交好，其首领赶到后不出三天就把修道士赶走；1681年的再次尝试同样收场。此后英国货在1690至1691年把查特胡奇诸镇吸引东迁奥克马尔吉河，萨沃克利也加入了摧毁阿巴拉契传教站的袭击。亚马西战争后，该镇迁回查特胡奇河，迭戈·佩尼亚1716年在那里清点出八十四名战士。1763年西班牙割让佛罗里达，镇中信教家庭随其他撤离者从圣马科斯乘船前往哈瓦那。

en:
Etali is the Blue Ridge foothill country of the Keowee, Tugaloo and Chauga rivers, the head-streams of the Savannah. South Appalachian Mississippian farmers raised Chauga's platform mound and village in the twelfth century; by 1444 these valleys were the eastern edge of the Cherokee world, its Lower Towns. Iroquoian-speaking and self-governing, each town kept a plaza and a townhouse, and Keowee on the river of that name was the leading one. Maize, beans and squash fields, deer hunts and river trails tied the foothill towns to the higher mountain towns, and no European post yet stood on the upper Savannah.

After Charles Town was founded in 1670 the Lower Cherokee Traders' Path carried deerskins east from Keowee, and traders early in the next century counted about 2,100 Cherokee in sixteen towns east of the Blue Ridge. The Yamasee War settled the towns' English alignment: Maurice Moore's column reached Tugaloo on 29 December 1715, and eleven Lower Creek ambassadors killed there in 1716 threw the Cherokee into the English camp. South Carolina built Fort Prince George across the river from Keowee in 1753, an earth-and-timber square that became its chief trade post among the Lower Towns. The Anglo-Cherokee War grew out of that fort: after Governor Lyttelton seized thirty-eight Cherokee chiefs as hostages there, a rescue attempt in February 1760 failed and the garrison killed every hostage. Archibald Montgomerie then burned ten Lower Towns, Keowee among them, until the Cherokee stopped him at Echoee Pass; a second army under James Grant forced peace in 1761. During the War of Independence Andrew Williamson's militia returned in 1776 and destroyed Seneca and most towns east of the mountains, and the Treaty of DeWitt's Corner on 20 May 1777 ceded nearly all Cherokee land in South Carolina. At Hopewell, Andrew Pickens's plantation on the Keowee, the United States signed another treaty with the Cherokee in the winter of 1785-86.
zh:
埃塔利是基奥维河、图加卢河和乔加河流经的蓝岭山麓，三河都是萨凡纳河的上游源流。12世纪，南阿巴拉契亚密西西比文化的农民筑起乔加的台基土丘和村落；到1444年，这些河谷已是切罗基世界的东缘，即下镇地带。各镇说易洛魁语、各自为政，都有广场和镇屋，基奥维河畔的基奥维镇是首镇。玉米、豆类、南瓜田，加上猎鹿道和河路，把山麓各镇与更高处的山地城镇连在一起；萨凡纳河上游还没有欧洲人的据点。

1670年查尔斯镇建立后，下切罗基商路把鹿皮从基奥维东运；18世纪初的商人统计，蓝岭以东的十六座切罗基城镇约有2100人。亚马西战争定下了各镇的亲英立场：1715年12月29日莫里斯·穆尔的纵队抵达图加卢，十一名下克里克使节1716年在那里被杀，切罗基人就此倒向英国一边。1753年，南卡罗来纳在基奥维镇对岸建起乔治亲王堡，这座土木方堡成为英国在下镇的首要商馆。英切战争就因这座要塞而起：利特尔顿总督把三十八名切罗基酋长扣作人质关进堡内，1760年2月切罗基人营救失败，守军杀了全部人质。阿奇博尔德·蒙哥马利随后焚毁包括基奥维在内的十座下镇，直到在埃科伊山口被切罗基人挡住；詹姆斯·格兰特率第二支军队在1761年迫和。独立战争期间，安德鲁·威廉森的民兵1776年再入河谷，摧毁塞内卡和蓝岭以东的大多数城镇，1777年5月20日的《德威特角条约》割走切罗基人在南卡罗来纳的几乎全部土地。1785至1786年冬，美国又在安德鲁·皮肯斯位于基奥维河畔的种植园霍普韦尔同切罗基人缔约。

en:
The Tennessee sweeps south through a broad bend broken by the long Muscle Shoals, rock bars and islands where fish ran thick. Maize fields covered the bottomlands beside Mississippian platform-mound towns. By 1444 many of those towns had fragmented, leaving cleared terraces and old earthworks. Chickasaw villages in the Yazoo and Tombigbee country used the bend as a hunting ground and a path for raids. The Napochi towns named in later Spanish accounts lay farther up the Tennessee. Along the shoals themselves, no single chiefdom ruled in 1444; Chickasaw hunters and war parties passed through from the south.

Hernando de Soto wintered among the Chickasaw south of the bend in 1540 and 1541. Chickasaw warriors attacked his camp at night, burned much of his baggage and quarters and nearly broke the expedition. Firearms obtained from Carolina traders later let Chickasaw raiders range deep into the valley. The French governor Bienville launched two major campaigns to subdue them. His attack on Ackia was repulsed in 1736, and in 1739 he built Fort de l'Assomption on the fourth Chickasaw Bluff and gathered about 3,600 French, Black and Indigenous troops. Disease, weather and desertion wore the army down before it withdrew in the spring of 1740. Chickasaw families settled the bend around 1765 at the place later called Chickasaw Old Fields, but they withdrew after a bloody battle with the Cherokee in 1769. In 1816 they sold their claims along the bend to the United States.
zh:
田纳西河向南绕出宽阔河湾，河道被马斯尔肖尔斯的长列岩滩和岛屿切分，鱼群在浅水中聚集。河滩上遍布玉米地，旁边是密西西比文化的台墩城镇。到1444年，许多城镇已经瓦解，只留下开垦过的阶地和旧土墩。亚祖河与汤比格比河一带的奇克索村落把河湾当作猎场和袭掠通道。西班牙后来记载的纳波奇城镇位于田纳西河更上游。1444年，急流沿岸没有统辖全境的单一酋邦，奇克索猎人和战队则不断从南方经过。

1540至1541年，德·索托在河湾以南的奇克索人处越冬。奇克索武士夜袭营地，烧毁大量辎重和营舍，几乎击溃这支远征队。后来，奇克索人从卡罗来纳商人手中获得火枪，袭掠队伍得以深入河谷。法国总督比安维尔两次大举进攻：1736年，法军在阿基亚被击退；1739年，他在第四奇克索崖修建阿松雄堡，集结约3600名法国、黑人和印第安人士兵。疾病、天气和逃兵拖垮了军队，法军于1740年春撤退。约1765年，奇克索家庭到后来称作「奇克索旧田」的河湾地定居，1769年与切罗基人血战后撤离。1816年，他们把河湾一带的土地要求权卖给美国。

en:
The Houma were a Muskogean-speaking people whose name means 'red' in Choctaw, after the red clay of the Red River country above the Mississippi's east bank. Their main town, eighty cabins of six or seven hundred people in French reckonings, stood on the great river not far above where the Red runs in, with the Bayogoula for neighbours. They raised corn, squash and chickens, played chunkey before a temple of carved and painted figures, and kept a fire-keeper watching over the bones of a dead female chief. Men went in breechcloths with copper ornaments and feathers, women in robes of turkey feathers or muskrat skin, and both tattooed their faces and blackened their teeth. In 1444 the lower Mississippi below the Natchez bluffs was Houma water, and no European had yet sounded it.

La Salle passed the village of the 'Oumas' in 1682, and Henri de Tonti made an alliance with them four years later. Iberville was welcomed with song, tobacco and a dance, and when he returned in 1700 he found half the people dead of disease and a French-built church already standing. About that time the Houma and Bayogoula raised a tall red pole on the east bank, hung with sacred animal carcasses and feathers, to mark the border of their hunting grounds; they called it Istrouma, and the French called the spot Baton Rouge, the Red Stick. In 1706 or 1709 the Tunica, whom they had sheltered, massacred them, and the survivors fled downriver to the Ascension country, where they kept two villages, the Great and the Little Houmas. Bayogoula and Acolapissa refugees joined them, but the decline ran on: sixty warriors were counted in 1758 and twenty-five in 1784. After the Louisiana Purchase, President Jefferson read that some sixty 'Houmas or Red Men' lived twenty-five leagues above New Orleans, and in 1805 John Sibley found only a few families east of the river, intermarried with Tunica and Atakapa, who 'scarcely existed as a nation'.
zh:
霍马人说穆斯科格语，族名在乔克托语里意为「红」，得自密西西比河东岸雷德河故土的红黏土。他们的主镇有八十座木屋，法国人的估算是六七百人，立在大河畔、雷德河河口上游不远处，邻族是巴尤古拉人。他们种玉米和南瓜、养鸡，在供着彩绘雕刻神像的神庙前玩春克戏，庙里有守火人照看一位已故女酋长的遗骨。男子围腰布，佩戴铜饰和羽毛，女子披野火鸡羽或麝鼠皮的袍子，男女都在脸上文身、把牙齿染黑。1444年时，纳奇兹陡崖以下的密西西比下游还是霍马人的水面，还没有欧洲人到过这里。

1682年，拉萨尔经过「乌马人」的村落，四年后亨利·德·通蒂与他们结盟。伊贝维尔到访时，霍马人以歌声、烟草和舞蹈相迎；他1700年再来，半数人已死于疫病，一座法国人主持修建的教堂已经立在村里。约在此时，霍马人与巴尤古拉人在东岸竖起一根高大的红柱，柱上挂着献祭的兽尸和羽毛，作为猎场分界；他们称之为伊斯特鲁马，法国人则把这个地方唤作巴吞鲁日，意为红棍。1706或1709年，被他们收留的图尼卡人反戈屠戮，幸存者顺河南逃到阿森松地方，建起大霍马、小霍马两座村落。巴尤古拉人和阿科拉皮萨难民先后投奔他们，但衰败仍在继续：1758年尚有六十名战士，1784年只剩二十五名。美国购得路易斯安那后，杰斐逊总统看到的报告说，新奥尔良上游二十五里格处还住着约六十名「霍马人或红人」；1805年，约翰·西布利只在河东找到几户人家，他们与图尼卡人、阿塔卡帕人通婚，「作为一个民族已几乎不复存在」。

en:
The Avoyel held the lower Red River near where its waters join the Black, the Atchafalaya and the Mississippi. From palisaded villages, the largest close to the later site of Marksville, they controlled the back channels that dugouts used between the interior and the Gulf. Neighbours called them the Flint People or Stone-Arrow-Point People, because Avoyel crews carried flint from Caddo country to the Atakapa and Chitimacha of the coast, who had little workable stone. In 1444 this canoe traffic gave a small nation real weight at the river junction.

French records counted 280 Avoyel in 1698. When Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville visited the next year he called them the little Taensas, but the name confused them with the Natchez-speaking Taensa higher on the Mississippi, whom the French called the great Taensas. Introduced diseases reduced the Avoyel rapidly. In the late 1780s and 1790s Tunica, Ofo and Biloxi families moved into the district, and Avoyel survivors married among them. About 1794 Marc Eliche, a Sephardic Jewish trader believed to have come from Venice, opened a post after his wagon broke down on an old Indian meeting ground; the settlement became Marksville. In 1805 the Indian agent John Sibley reported that only two or three Avoyel women remained, living along the Ouachita.
zh:
阿沃耶尔人占据雷德河下游，地点靠近雷德河接入布莱克河、阿查法拉亚河和密西西比河的地方。他们以栅栏村落控制内地与墨西哥湾之间的支汊航路，最大的栅寨邻近后来马克斯维尔的位置。邻族称他们为「燧石人」或「石箭镞人」：阿沃耶尔人的独木舟把卡多地方的燧石运给海边的阿塔卡帕人和奇蒂马查人，后两者的土地缺少可用石材。1444年，这种独木舟转运贸易使这个小族群在河流汇合处拥有实际分量。

法国文献在1698年统计有280名阿沃耶尔人。次年皮埃尔·勒穆瓦纳·德·伊贝维尔到访，把他们称为「小坦萨人」；这个叫法容易把他们与密西西比河上游说纳奇兹语的坦萨人混淆，法国人把后者称作「大坦萨人」。欧洲传入的疫病使阿沃耶尔人口迅速减少。1780年代末至1790年代，图尼卡人、奥福人和比洛克西人的家庭迁入此地，幸存的阿沃耶尔人与他们通婚。约1794年，据信来自威尼斯的塞法迪犹太商人马克·埃利切的马车在一处旧印第安集会地损坏，他随后在那里开设贸易站，聚落后来发展成马克斯维尔。1805年，印第安事务官约翰·西布利记载，沃希托河畔只剩下两三名阿沃耶尔妇女。

en:
At the Great Bend of the Red River, in the country where Texas, Arkansas and Oklahoma meet, the Upper Nasoni built their thatched temple-towns as members of the Kadohadacho circle of the Caddo. Their farmers worked the bottoms for corn, beans and squash and gathered pecans from the groves, and their bows and pottery moved along Caddo trails as far as the Mississippi; their kinsmen the Lower Nasoni lived farther south, between the Sabine and the Angelina. In 1444 no European had reached the bend, and the horse was still unknown on the Red River.

The first Europeans to reach them were Spaniards of the Hernando de Soto entrada, who met the Lower Nasoni in 1541; in 1686 men of La Salle's Texas expedition were carried into a Nasoni town and feasted by its people. Within a generation France and Spain were bidding for Caddo friendship along the river. Spanish friars opened Mission San José de los Nazones among the Lower Nasoni in 1716. Three years later Jean-Baptiste de La Harpe raised a small fort beside the principal Upper Nasoni village, the Poste des Cadodaquious, named for the Kadohadacho; French traders sent out guns, powder, metal tools and beads and took back hides and horses. Louis Juchereau de Saint-Denis, founder of the post at Natchitoches, had the garrison sent there, and French expeditions into the west set out from it. The Upper Nasoni held to the French alliance until Louisiana passed to Spain in 1762. Warfare and smallpox thinned the Caddo towns in the decades after, and when the United States bought Louisiana the surviving Nasoni had already drawn in among the Kadohadacho; the old French post was abandoned at the transfer.
zh:
红河大拐弯处，在得克萨斯、阿肯色与俄克拉荷马相接的那片地方，上纳索尼人作为卡多人卡多达乔同盟的一员，建起茅草覆顶的神庙村镇。他们在河滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在林中采收山核桃，所制的弓和陶器沿卡多商路远销密西西比河；亲族下纳索尼人住在更南边的萨宾河与安杰利纳河之间。1444年，还没有欧洲人到过这道河弯，红河畔也没有马。

最早到来的欧洲人是埃尔南多·德·索托远征队的西班牙人，1541年遇上了下纳索尼人；1686年，拉萨尔得克萨斯远征队的几名队员被迎进一座纳索尼镇子赴宴。不过一代人光景，法国与西班牙已在红河两岸争取卡多诸部的亲善。1716年，西班牙修士在下纳索尼人中间开设圣何塞·德·洛斯·纳索内斯传教站；三年后，让-巴蒂斯特·德·拉阿尔普在上纳索尼主村旁筑起小堡卡多达库斯堡，名字取自卡多达乔人，法国商人从堡中运出火枪、火药、金属器具和珠子，换回兽皮与马匹。纳基托什商站的创建者圣但尼派来了驻防兵士，法国人向西的探险队也从这座小堡出发。上纳索尼人恪守法国同盟，直到1762年路易斯安那转交西班牙。此后数十年间，战事与天花使村镇凋零；美国购得路易斯安那时，幸存的纳索尼人已在卡多诸部联合中并入卡多达乔人，那座法国旧堡也在易手之际废弃。

en:
Cochati covers the east bank of the Mississippi below the Ohio: the Kentucky Bend, the cypress bottoms of the Reelfoot country, and then the first rise of the Chickasaw Bluffs. Late Mississippian farmers had built mound villages on these heights, and the walled town at Chucalissa, a few miles downstream, still belonged to that river world in the fifteenth century. In 1444 the high landings, cane brakes and ridge paths were used by Chickasaw hunters and war parties, who could watch and stop every canoe moving between the Ohio and the lower Mississippi.

La Salle's canoes reached the bluffs in February 1682. When his armorer Pierre Prudhomme vanished on a hunt and was feared taken by the Chickasaw, the party threw up a stockade on one of the bluffs and named it Fort Prudhomme after him; ten days later the man stumbled back, starving but unhurt. It was the first French structure recorded in Tennessee, and La Salle, who spent forty ill days there on his return, went on to the river mouth and claimed the whole Mississippi valley for France. The bluffs kept giving Chickasaw fighters the high ground against French river traffic in the wars of the following century. A survey of 1785 still maps a Reelfoot River flowing into the Mississippi, but the New Madrid earthquakes of December 1811 to February 1812 shook whole banks into the water, made the current seem to run backwards, and drowned the cypress woods that became Reelfoot Lake. In 1818 the Treaty of Tuscaloosa ended Chickasaw rule over the lands east of the river, and by 1821 surveyors were running their lines along the bluffs.
zh:
科查蒂位于俄亥俄河口以南的密西西比河东岸，包括肯塔基湾、里尔富特一带柏树成林的低洼地，再往前就是奇克索崖的第一道隆起。晚期密西西比文化的农民曾在这些高地上修建土墩村落；下游几英里处带围墙的楚卡利萨镇，在15世纪仍属于这个河上世界。1444年，高处的登陆点、藤丛和山脊小路为奇克索猎人和战队所用，他们能监视并截住往返于俄亥俄河与密西西比河下游之间的每一条独木舟。

1682年2月，拉萨尔的独木舟队抵达陡崖。军械匠皮埃尔·普吕多姆打猎时失踪，众人以为他被奇克索人掳走，便在其中一座崖上赶筑栅栏，以他的名字命名为普吕多姆堡；十天后他踉跄着走回营地，饿得发慌却没有受伤。这是田纳西有记载的第一座法国建筑，拉萨尔返程时还在堡中养病四十天，随后下到河口，为法国领有整个密西西比河流域。在随后一个世纪的战争里，这些陡崖一直让奇克索战士对法国河运占着居高临下的地利。1785年的测量地图上，里尔富特河仍注入密西西比河；但1811年12月至1812年2月的新马德里大地震把整段河岸震入水中，河水看似倒流，柏树林被水淹没，成了后来的里尔富特湖。1818年的《塔斯卡卢萨条约》结束了奇克索人对河东土地的统治，到1821年，测量员已沿着陡崖拉线划界。

en:
Tatteroa is one of the old Native names for the Big Sandy, a short Ohio tributary whose Tug and Levisa forks drain the wooded Kentucky and Virginia hills. For only about 29 miles the river cuts a natural road from the Cumberland ridges to the Ohio, with sandbars giving the later colonial name Big Sandy. The Tutelo knew the valley as Totteroy and hunted through its gaps, while Shawnee bands traveled the same creek bottoms; in 1444 the Hathawekela and other Shawnee divisions used it as fur country and a route for raids, not as a fixed border.

The valley drew soldiers because that route could carry an army away from the Ohio. In February and March 1756, Virginia Regiment troops and Cherokee allies marched upstream in the Sandy Creek Expedition, Virginia's only offensive of the French and Indian War and its first joint campaign with the Cherokee. Deep snow, flooded streams and short rations turned the column back before it met the Shawnee. George Washington later surveyed land at the river mouth between 1768 and 1772, when Virginia speculators were pressing into the Ohio Valley. Cornstalk's Shawnee and Mingo warriors fought the Virginia militia at Point Pleasant on 10 October 1774; their defeat and the Treaty of Camp Charlotte cleared the way for Virginia claims south of the Ohio, and maps were using Big Sandy by 1789.
zh:
塔特罗阿是大桑迪河的原住民旧称之一。塔格河与莱维萨河排去肯塔基和弗吉尼亚山林的水，汇成这条注入俄亥俄河的短河，全长约29英里，河道中大片沙洲后来给它带来「大桑迪」之名。这条河谷像一条天然通道，从坎伯兰山岭通向俄亥俄河。图特洛人称这里为托特罗伊，在各山口间狩猎；肖尼群体也沿同一片溪谷往来。1444年，哈萨韦凯拉等肖尼分支把这里当作毛皮产地和袭扰通道，而不是一条固定边界。

正因这条通道能让军队离开俄亥俄河深入内陆，河谷后来引来了军队。1756年2月至3月，弗吉尼亚军团与切罗基盟友沿桑迪河上游进军，发动桑迪溪远征。这是弗吉尼亚在法国—印第安人战争中唯一的攻势，也是它与切罗基人的首次联合军事行动；深雪、暴涨的溪流和粮草短缺迫使队伍在遭遇肖尼人之前折返。1768年至1772年，乔治·华盛顿在河口一带测量土地，当时弗吉尼亚的土地投机者正涌向俄亥俄河谷。1774年10月10日，康姆斯托克率领肖尼与明戈战士在波因特普莱森特迎战弗吉尼亚民兵；战败和《坎普夏洛特条约》为弗吉尼亚取得俄亥俄河南岸的主张扫清道路，到1789年，地图上已经使用大桑迪这个名称。

en:
Mohetan is the high country of the central Alleghenies, where the ridges part the Potomac, Monongahela and Kanawha watersheds and the mountain streams either run west to the Ohio or east toward the Virginia tidewater. The Greenbrier valley carried the Seneca Trail, the warpath that joined the Ohio country to the Virginia Piedmont; small Montaine and other Late Woodland groups gardened the bottoms, hunted the oak forests and moved along those paths. In 1444 no European had seen these valleys. The first Virginian party, Thomas Batts and Robert Fallam in September 1671, met a Mohetan runner on a New River tributary and spoke with him through a Siouan interpreter, and scholars count the Mohetans among the Eastern Siouan peoples. The runner carried a European gun and accepted powder and shot as gifts, so colonial arms already reached the highlands through intertribal trade. War and disease scattered the small band before any colonist settled its valleys.

The first whites over the ridge supplied the Greenbrier's best-remembered frontier story. In 1749 Jacob Marlin and Stephen Sewell built a cabin on what became the site of Marlinton, the first permanent Europeans west of the Allegheny crest, where every stream runs west toward the Gulf. After a religious quarrel Sewell moved out of the cabin and into a hollowed sycamore, and surveyor John Lewis found the pair living this way in 1751. Four years later David Tygart and Robert Files tried the Tygart Valley with their families; a raiding party travelling the Shawnee Trail found the Files cabin and killed seven of its people, and the one son who escaped warned the Tygarts in time to flee. The valley stood empty of settlers until the 1770s. John Stuart surveyed the Greenbrier in 1769 and built its first mill at Frankford the next year, led its militia to Point Pleasant in 1774, and became Greenbrier County's first clerk in 1780.
zh:
莫赫坦是阿勒格尼山脉中段的高地，山脊分开波托马克、莫农加希拉和卡诺瓦三个水系，山溪或向西流入俄亥俄河，或向东流向弗吉尼亚滨海。格林布赖尔谷是塞内卡小道的一段，这条征战之路连接着俄亥俄地区与弗吉尼亚皮埃蒙特；蒙泰恩等晚期林地文化的小群体在河洲园作、在橡树林狩猎，沿这些山路往来。1444年，还没有欧洲人见过这些山谷。1671年9月，托马斯·巴茨与罗伯特·法伦姆的小队成为第一批进入此地的弗吉尼亚人，他们在纽河一条支流上遇到一名莫赫坦跑者，靠苏语译员交谈，学者多把莫赫坦人算作东苏语族群。这名跑者带着一支欧洲火枪，还收下火药和铅弹作为礼物，可见殖民地武器已通过部族贸易进入深山。后来战争与疫病流散了这个小群体，那时还没有殖民者在这些山谷定居。

翻过山脊的第一批白人，给格林布赖尔留下了流传最广的边地旧事。1749年，雅各布·马林与斯蒂芬·休厄尔在后来的马林顿一带搭起木屋，成为阿勒格尼分水岭以西、河水一律西向墨西哥湾的最早欧洲常住者。两人因宗教争执闹翻后，休厄尔搬出木屋，住进一棵掏空的美国梧桐；测量员约翰·刘易斯1751年发现他们时，二人仍是这般光景。四年后，戴维·泰加特和罗伯特·法尔斯带着家小尝试定居泰加特谷，一伙沿肖尼小道行进的袭击者发现法尔斯家的木屋，杀死七口，唯一逃脱的儿子及时报信，泰加特一家才得以逃走。此后直到1770年代，谷中再无定居者。约翰·斯图尔特1769年测量格林布赖尔，次年在弗兰克福德建起当地第一座磨坊，1774年率本地民兵开赴波因特普莱森特，1780年成为格林布赖尔县首任书记官。

en:
The Kichesipirini, the People of the Great River, lived on the islands where the Ottawa narrows through Allumette Lake. In 1444 their villages occupied Allumette and Morrison islands, with Grand Calumet farther downstream, and every canoe moving between the St. Lawrence, the upper Ottawa and the Great Lakes had to pass their landing places. The nation lived by that choke point: families fished the eddies and camped along the carries, while guards made the portages a toll gate, and Algonquin, Wendat and Odawa parties alike paid to move through. French memoirs later called the chief's island the Isle du Borgne, the One-Eyed Man's Island.

That chief was Tessouat, blind in one eye, who first met Champlain in 1603 and kept the Kichesipirini the middlemen of the river for thirty years. When Champlain reached the islands in 1613, Tessouat feasted him but refused passage toward the northern sea, and he worked to stop his French, Wendat and Odawa allies trading with one another direct, so that furs kept passing through Kichesipirini hands. In 1633 his people turned the Jesuits back from Huronia. Epidemics and the Beaver Wars undid that order. A peace made with the Haudenosaunee did not hold, and in 1650 Haudenosaunee war parties overran the island villages and nearly destroyed the nation. The narrows stayed a fighting ground, empty and unsafe, until the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701 reopened the canoe route. European families only settled Allumette Island in 1818, most of them loggers or hands at the Hudson's Bay post upstream at Fort William.
zh:
基切西比里尼人意为「大河之人」，世居渥太华河在阿吕梅特湖收窄处的群岛。1444年，他们的村庄占据阿吕梅特岛和莫里森岛，下游还有大卡吕梅特岛；往来圣劳伦斯河、渥太华河上游与五大湖之间的独木舟，都必须经过他们的渡口。这个族群靠这个河上狭口过活：族人在回水湾捕鱼，沿搬运道扎营，看守的人把陆路变成税关，阿尔贡昆、温达特和渥太华的队伍经过都要交费。法国人的回忆录后来把这位首领所在的岛称作「独眼人之岛」。

这位首领就是独眼的泰苏阿特。他1603年初遇尚普兰，此后三十年把基切西比里尼人维持成河上的中间商。1613年尚普兰抵达群岛，泰苏阿特设宴款待，却拒绝放他前往北方海洋；他还设法阻止法国人、温达特人和渥太华人彼此直接交易，好让毛皮始终经基切西比里尼人之手。1633年，族人又把前往休伦尼亚的耶稣会士挡了回去。疫病和海狸战争瓦解了这套秩序。与霍德诺索尼人达成的和平没能维持多久，1650年，霍德诺索尼人的战队攻陷岛上村庄，几乎消灭这个族群。这片狭口此后沦为战场，荒凉而危险，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》重新打开独木舟航路。欧洲裔家庭迟至1818年才到阿吕梅特岛定居，大多做伐木工人，或在上游威廉堡的哈德逊湾贸易站干活。

en:
Piktuk, the Mi'kmaq name Europeans wrote as Pictou, means the 'explosive place', for the gas bubbling out of the coal seams beneath a deep harbour on the Northumberland Strait, or for the river of pitch the Mi'kmaq knew there. The harbour was an annual summer station of the Mi'kmaq, who came to fish, take seals and dry shellfish on the shore, and the country belonged to Epekwitk aq Piktuk, one of the seven districts of Mi'kma'ki, which also held the island across the strait. In 1444 the only keels in these waters were Mi'kmaq canoes, and the place was valued for its fishing rather than for the black stone under the bay.

France counted the coast as part of Acadia in the early seventeenth century, and Nicolas Denys recorded the harbour in the 1660s; a few Acadian hamlets lasted nearby until the expulsion and the British conquest of 1763. The Mi'kmaq had made their peace in the Halifax treaties of 1760 and 1761, and in June 1767 the Philadelphia Company landed its first families on the empty shore. The landing that made the port famous followed on 15 September 1773, when the Hector put in, an old Dutch fluyt carrying 189 Highland crofters from the Loch Broom country who had been promised a farm and a year's provisions. Eleven weeks at sea, a fortnight's gale off Newfoundland, dysentery and smallpox killed eighteen of them, and on shore no provisions awaited the survivors, who threw up huts before their first winter closed in. She was the first emigrant ship to sail directly from Scotland to Canada, and Pictou became the chief receiving port of the Highland Clearances. Squared timber went out to Britain from 1777, though American privateers raided the harbour that November and carried off the ship Molly. Coal was struck in 1798, and by 1803 fifty ships a year loaded in the roads. The Presbyterian minister Thomas McCulloch opened a grammar school at his house in 1808, chartered as Pictou Academy in 1816, which taught without religious tests while King's College at Windsor admitted Anglicans alone.
zh:
皮克图克是米克马克语地名，欧洲人后来写作皮克图（Pictou），意为「爆发之地」：诺森伯兰海峡边这座深水港下的煤层直往外冒瓦斯，也有人说得名自米克马克人所知的一条沥青河。这里是米克马克人每年夏季的营地，他们来捕鱼、猎海豹、在岸边晒制贝类；此地属于米克马克七区之一的「埃佩克维特克与皮克图克」区，海峡对岸的岛屿也在同一区内。1444年时，这片水面上只有米克马克人的独木舟，此地为人看重的是渔场，而不是海湾底下的黑石。

17世纪初法国把这段海岸算作阿卡迪亚的一部分，尼古拉·德尼在1660年代记载了这座港口；附近一度有几处阿卡迪亚人小村，直到大驱逐和1763年英国征服才告终结。米克马克人已在1760至1761年的哈利法克斯条约中与英国人议和；1767年6月，费城公司招募的第一批家庭在空旷的海岸登岸。让港口闻名的登陆发生在1773年9月15日：老旧的荷兰平底快船「赫克托号」进港，船上是189名来自布鲁姆湖一带的高地佃农，招募时许给他们一座农场和一年口粮。海上走了十一个星期，纽芬兰外海的一场风暴又耽误了十四天，痢疾和天花夺去十八条人命；岸上并没有口粮等着幸存者，他们赶在第一个冬天到来前搭起茅屋。这是第一艘从苏格兰直接驶往加拿大的移民船，皮克图也成为高地大驱逐中移民进入新斯科舍的主要港口。方材自1777年起输往英国，同年11月美国私掠船却袭掠港口，劫走「莫莉号」。1798年这里挖到煤炭，到1803年每年有五十艘船在锚地装货。长老会牧师托马斯·麦卡洛1808年在自己家中开办文法学校，1816年获特许为皮克图学院，入学不设宗教门槛，而当时温莎的国王学院只收圣公会信徒。

en:
Iroquet country covered the flat South Nation watershed, where white-pine forest and marsh drain northeast from the country above Brockville to the Ottawa near Plantagenet. In 1444 a small Algonquian-speaking band lived by the river, taking fish from its weirs and beaver from its ponds and carrying canoes across the short portages into the upper St. Lawrence, the road toward the Great Lakes. French records called these people the Iroquet or Ononchataronon, and Iroquet was also the name of the chief who dealt with the first French expeditions.

Chief Iroquet was among France's first allies in the interior. In June 1609 he and a Huron chief met Champlain near Quebec to make war on the Haudenosaunee, and within weeks Champlain fought in their war party on the lake that now bears his name: near the future site of Fort Ticonderoga, a single arquebus shot from him killed two Haudenosaunee chiefs. At the council on Île Saint-Ignace the next year, Iroquet took a French youth, probably Étienne Brûlé, eighty leagues above the Lachine Rapids to live with the band and learn its language and waterways; Brûlé became the first European to make his life beyond the St. Lawrence. In 1615 Iroquet led his Algonquins on Champlain's raid south of Lake Ontario. The Beaver Wars later broke Algonquian power on this ground. Loyalists began taking up the river townships in 1785, and on 11 November 1813 John Crysler's fields beside the St. Lawrence saw a battle in which a British and Upper Canadian force threw back an American army several times its size and ended the campaign against Montreal.
zh:
伊罗奎特之地是南纳申河流域的低平原野：白松林和沼泽间的水道从布罗克维尔以北向东北汇流，在普朗塔热内附近注入渥太华河。1444年，一支说阿尔贡昆语的小族群傍河而居，在鱼梁捕鱼，在海狸塘捕猎，再沿短途搬运道把独木舟抬进圣劳伦斯河上游，取道前往五大湖。法国记录称他们为伊罗奎特人或奥农查塔罗农人，而伊罗奎特也是最早同法国探险队打交道的那位首领的名字。

首领伊罗奎特是法国人在内陆最早的盟友之一。1609年6月，他和一名休伦首领在魁北克附近会见尚普兰，约定共同对霍德诺索尼人开战；几周后，尚普兰便加入他们的战队，在后来以他命名的湖泊作战，双方在日后的提康德罗加堡附近相遇时，他一枪打死两名霍德诺索尼首领。次年在圣伊尼亚斯岛议事时，伊罗奎特收下一名法国青年，很可能就是艾蒂安·布吕莱，带他到莱克欣急流上游八十里格处与族群共同生活，学习语言和水路，布吕莱成了第一个在圣劳伦斯河以外扎根的欧洲人。1615年，伊罗奎特率阿尔贡昆人参加尚普兰深入安大略湖以南的远征。海狸战争后来摧毁了阿尔贡昆人在这片土地上的势力。效忠派1785年开始进入沿河诸镇区；1813年11月11日，圣劳伦斯河畔约翰·克莱斯勒的田地上爆发战斗，英国与上加拿大部队击退数倍于己的美军，美方攻打蒙特利尔的战役就此告终。

en:
Nebesek is the Western Abenaki name for the shallow, marsh-fringed widening of the St. Lawrence that the French called Lake Saint-Pierre, lying between Sorel and Trois-Rivières where the Saint-François and Bécancour rivers come in. In 1444 its islands, reed beds and floodplain woods were fishing, fowling and trapping ground for the Laurentian peoples of the St. Lawrence valley; canoes crossed the open water in summer, and the ice joined the two shores in winter.

Cartier called the water Angoulême when he passed in 1535, and Champlain, reaching it in June 1603, named it for Saint Peter. A French seigneury later took root on the south shore at Bécancour, and around 1680 Abenaki and Sokoki families settled at the mouth of its river; in 1708 the Baron de Portneuf, Pierre Robineau, granted them the land that became Wôlinak, one of the seven Catholic communities of the Seven Nations of Canada. Those Abenaki fought for the French in the colonial wars and, after the British conquest, served the British Crown in the American Revolution and the War of 1812. British rule did not change the lake's old uses: ferries crossed it in open water and sleighs took the winter ice road between Montreal and Quebec, while the marshes supplied fish and wildfowl to the farms gathering on both shores.
zh:
内贝塞克是西阿贝纳基人对圣劳伦斯河上一片浅阔水域的称呼，法国人后来称之为圣皮埃尔湖。它位于索雷尔与三河城之间，圣弗朗索瓦河、贝坎库尔河在此汇入。1444年，湖中岛屿、芦苇荡和泛滥平原林地，是圣劳伦斯河谷劳伦提亚人捕鱼、猎禽和设陷阱的场地；夏季独木舟横渡开阔水面，冬季冰面又把两岸连成一片。

1535年卡蒂埃经过时把这片水域称作昂古莱姆，1603年6月尚普兰抵达后以圣皮埃尔为它命名。南岸后来建起法国人的贝坎库尔领主地；约1680年，阿贝纳基和索科基家庭在贝坎库尔河口定居，1708年波特纳夫男爵皮埃尔·罗比诺把土地授予他们，后来形成沃利纳克，也是「加拿大七族」七个天主教社区之一。这些阿贝纳基人在殖民战争中为法国作战，英国征服后又在独立战争和1812年战争中为英国王冠效力。英国统治没有改变这片湖的用途：夏季渡船往来，冬季雪橇走冰路，连接蒙特利尔与魁北克，湖沼则向两岸越聚越多的农庄供应鱼和野禽。

en:
Here the Ottawa, called Kitchissippi by the Algonquin, widens into lake-like reaches threaded by the great islands of Allumette, Morrison and Grand Calumet. The chain was the natural choke point on the river road from the St Lawrence to the upper Great Lakes and to Hudson Bay. Beside the Otaguottouemin lived the Kichesipirini, the 'men of the great river', also called the Island Indians, whose main village stood on Morrison Island. Too far north for maize, the two bands lived by fishing, hunting and trade, and their canoes decided who might pass up or down the river. In 1444 the islands were the busiest meeting place on the upper Ottawa.

Their one-eyed chief Tessouat, known to the French as le Borgne de l'Isle, first met Samuel de Champlain in 1603 and received him again in 1613. Champlain had come upstream on the word of the young Nicolas de Vignau, who had wintered on the islands and in Paris talked of a northern sea and an English shipwreck; Tessouat's council showed the route he described was impossible, and Vignau confessed. Tessouat charged every French convoy a toll, kept French, Huron and Odawa business moving through Algonquin middlemen, and in 1633 refused the Jesuits passage to Huronia. He died not long afterward. The peace his people made with the Haudenosaunee in 1645 did not hold, and by 1650 the island bands had fled, most of them probably joining the Odawa. War parties and fur brigades then had the river to themselves until the Great Peace of Montreal of 1701 reopened it.
zh:
渥太华河在阿尔冈昆语中称基奇西比（Kitchissippi，意为「大河」），到此展宽成湖泊般的河面，阿卢梅特岛、莫里森岛和大卡吕梅特岛罗列其间。这串岛屿是圣劳伦斯河通往五大湖上游和哈得孙湾的水路咽喉。奥塔戈托埃明人的邻族是基切西皮里尼人（Kichesipirini，意为「大河之人」），又称「岛民」，主寨就在莫里森岛上。这里过于寒冷，不宜玉米，两族人都靠渔猎和贸易为生，谁能在河上往返，要由他们的独木舟说了算。1444年，这群岛屿是渥太华河上游最繁忙的会聚之地。

独眼首领泰苏阿（Tessouat）被法国人称为「岛上的独眼人」，1603年第一次见到塞缪尔·德·尚普兰，1613年又在岛上接待他。尚普兰此来，是听信了曾在岛上过冬的年轻人尼古拉·德·维尼奥的话：此人在巴黎声称北方有一片海，还有一艘英国沉船。泰苏阿的议事会指出，维尼奥所说的航路根本走不通，他只得招认。泰苏阿向每支法国船队收过路费，让法国、休伦和渥太华之间的买卖都经阿尔冈昆中间人转手，1633年又不许耶稣会士经此前往休伦尼亚，不久后去世。1645年岛民与易洛魁联盟订立的和平没有维持，到1650年各岛族群已弃地逃亡，多数人大概投奔了渥太华人。此后这条河只剩战队和毛皮独木舟穿行，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》签订后才重新开放。

en:
The Batiscan comes down from the forested Laurentian highlands to the St. Lawrence, through country that in 1444 belonged to Algonquian-speaking hunters, the Attikamekw of the upper river among them. They took moose and beaver in its woods and eel and sturgeon at the wide, misty mouth, camping there on the way between the inland forests and the native trading rendezvous at Trois-Rivières. No European had yet been seen, but the river already lay on the canoe route between the upper country and the gulf.

Samuel de Champlain recorded the river's name in 1603, met a chief called Batiscan in 1611 and marked the 'region of bastisquan' on his map the following year. The country first lay within the huge Madeleine seigneury, granted to Jacques Laferté over the land between the Chevrotière and Saint-Maurice rivers and a hundred kilometres inland; on 13 March 1639 the Batiscan fief inside it was given to the Jesuits for the evangelization of the native bands and the planting of a settlement. Colonists came in 1666 and laid out long narrow river lots, about ten times longer than wide, so that every family had water frontage; the parish the Jesuits organised took its name from Francis Xavier, co-founder of their order. Men trapped up the Batiscan and sold their furs at Trois-Rivières, and sawmills worked its timber. After 1712 Fox captives brought from the west were held here as slaves. By the end of French rule a ribbon of farms and the Chemin du Roy linked Batiscan with Champlain and Sainte-Anne-de-la-Pérade, and British troops marched that road against Montreal in 1760.
zh:
巴蒂斯坎河自森林覆盖的劳伦琴山脉奔流而下，注入圣劳伦斯河。1444年，这片土地属于说阿尔冈昆语的猎民，上游林中有阿蒂卡梅库人（Atikamekw）。他们在林中猎驼鹿与河狸，在宽阔多雾的河口捕鳗鱼和鲟鱼，往来于内陆森林与三河城原住民贸易聚地之间时在此扎营。此时欧洲人尚未出现，巴蒂斯坎河已是连接上游腹地与海湾的独木舟路线。

塞缪尔·德·尚普兰1603年首次记下河名，1611年会见一位名叫巴蒂斯坎的首领，次年又在地图上把这一带标为巴斯蒂斯坎地区（bastisquan）。这片地方最初属于封给雅克·拉费尔泰的马德莱娜大领地，领地东到圣莫里斯河、向内陆延伸一百公里；1639年3月13日，领地中的巴蒂斯坎封邑被授予耶稣会，用于向原住民传教和建立定居点。1666年移民到来，开出一条条狭长的临河授地，长宽约为一比十，好让每户都临着水面；耶稣会设立的堂区以修会创始人之一方济各·沙勿略命名，即圣方济各·沙勿略堂区。居民沿巴蒂斯坎河深入内陆设阱捕猎，把毛皮卖到三河城，锯木厂也加工河运的木材。1712年后，从西部押来的福克斯人俘虏在此为奴。到法国统治末期，成串的农庄和国王大道把巴蒂斯坎与尚普兰村、圣安娜-德拉佩拉德连成一线，1760年英军正是循此路进逼蒙特利尔。

en:
Mehtawtik, ‘the end of the path’, stood where the Eel River joins the middle Saint John, at the head of the portage that carried canoe traffic between the Wolastoq valley and the rivers of Maine. It was the chief town of the Wolastoqiyik: longhouses and cornfields lay within a stout palisade raised in the seventeenth century against Mohawk war parties raiding from the west, and Fort Meductic was remembered as the first fort in Acadia. Salmon runs and the furs of the interior made the town wealthy, and from here the People of the Bright River commanded the carrying place between Acadia and New England. In 1444 it was their headquarters, greater than any of their other villages.

The French knew the place as Medoctec. In August 1689 a Wolastoqiyik war party brought the nine-year-old John Gyles up the rivers after sacking Pemaquid; he spent six years here as a captive before being sold to the French seigneur Louis D'Amours de Chauffours at Jemseg, and in 1736 he published the memoirs that describe the stockaded town and its life. When the French made nearby Fort Nashwaak the capital of Acadia in 1692, Meductic warriors joined Governor de Villebon's raids on New England and helped him hold the fort against the English siege of 1696. The Jesuit Joseph Aubéry reopened the mission at the turn of the century, and in 1717 Jean-Baptiste Loyard built the chapel of Saint-Jean-Baptiste, its bell a gift of Louis XV. Through Dummer's War of the 1720s and the colonial conflicts after it, the town remained a base for raids on the English frontier; it then lost ground to the French village of Sainte-Anne and the upriver settlement of Aukpaque. After the St. John River campaigns of the Seven Years' War its people removed to Aukpaque in 1767, and the old site was used only as a seasonal camp.
zh:
梅杜克蒂克又称梅赫陶提克，意为「小径的尽头」，地处鳗鱼河汇入圣约翰河中游之处，是一条水陆联运道的起点，独木舟经此往来于沃拉斯托克河谷与缅因诸河之间。这里是沃拉斯托基伊克人的首镇：17世纪筑起的坚固木栅围着长屋与玉米地，抵御从西边来袭的莫霍克战队，梅杜克蒂克堡后来被追记为阿卡迪亚的第一座堡垒。洄游的鲑鱼和内陆的毛皮养着这座镇子，「闪光河上的人」据此掌控连接阿卡迪亚与新英格兰的转运道。1444年，这里是他们的大本营，比其他任何村落都大。

法国人把此地称作梅多克泰克。1689年8月，一支沃拉斯托基伊克战队攻陷佩马奎德后，沿着河川把九岁的约翰·盖尔斯带到梅杜克蒂克；他在此为奴六年，后被转卖给在热姆塞格领有庄园的法国领主路易·达穆尔·德·肖富尔，1736年他出版回忆录，记下这座栅寨的样貌与生活。1692年，法国人把附近的纳什瓦克堡定为阿卡迪亚首府，梅杜克蒂克战士加入维尔邦总督对新英格兰的袭掠，并在1696年帮他顶住了英军对该堡的围攻。耶稣会士约瑟夫·奥贝里在世纪之初重开传教站，让-巴蒂斯特·卢瓦亚尔1717年建起圣让-巴蒂斯特小堂，教堂的钟还是路易十五所赐。在1720年代的达默战争及此后的殖民地冲突中，这座镇子始终是袭扰英国边疆的基地；后来它被法国人的圣安娜村和上游的奥克帕克聚居点比了下去。七年战争中的圣约翰河诸役过后，居民于1767年迁往奥克帕克，旧址此后只作季节性营地使用。

en:
The Keinouche, the People of the Pickerel Waters, held the lower Ottawa around Pontiac Bay and Chats Falls, where the river dropped thirty-five feet through a long run of chutes. In 1444 their seasonal bands took fish from the eddies below the rapids, hunted moose and beaver in the pine woods, and carried canoes around the falls on the route between the upper river and the St. Lawrence. The valley was poorly suited to farming, so camps, weirs and portage landings, not permanent towns, marked the country.

French canoes appeared in Champlain's time, but for decades only trading parties followed them. The Beaver Wars ended that: in 1650 Father Paul Ragueneau found the Algonquian communities along the Ottawa dispersed or destroyed, and for the rest of the century the river was a Haudenosaunee war road, too dangerous for canoe fleets until the Great Peace of Montreal in 1701 reopened it. The French then kept this shore largely unsettled to preserve the fur route; the only winterer on record was Nicolas d'Ailleboust de Manthet, who camped at the mouth of the Coulonge in 1694. Trade came back with the British conquest. The North West Company built Fort Coulonge at that river mouth in 1784 and ran it as the chief post on the Ottawa, and two years later Joseph Mondion built a homestead at Indian Point below Chats Falls. His post passed to the XY Company, then to the North West Company, and in 1821 to the Hudson's Bay Company.
zh:
凯诺切人意为「狗鱼水域之人」，据有渥太华河下游庞蒂亚克湾和沙茨瀑布一带，河水在这里穿过一长串陡槽，落差三十五英尺。1444年，季节性的族群在急流下的回水湾捕鱼，在松林里猎捕驼鹿和海狸，沿瀑布旁的搬运道抬舟而过，往来于河之上游与圣劳伦斯河之间。谷地不宜农耕，这里没有固定村镇，标出这片土地的是营地、鱼梁和搬运渡口。
