尚普兰时代法国独木舟开始出现，但几十年来跟来的只有商队。海狸战争终结了这种局面：1650年，保罗·拉格诺神父发现渥太华河沿岸的阿尔贡昆社群已经离散或被毁；该世纪余下的时间里，这条河成了霍德诺索尼人的战争通道，独木舟船队不敢通行，直到1701年《蒙特利尔大和平》才将其重新打开。此后法国人为保住毛皮航路，长期不让这一岸出现定居点；留有记载的唯一过冬者是尼古拉·达耶布·德·芒泰，他1694年在库隆日河口扎营。贸易随英国征服恢复：西北公司1784年在河口修建库隆日堡，作为渥太华河上的首要商站；两年后，约瑟夫·蒙迪翁在沙茨瀑布下的印第安角建起家园。他的商站先转入XY公司，再归西北公司，1821年并入哈德逊湾公司。

en:
The Noquet country was the strip of Upper Peninsula land between Lake Superior's southern shore and the two bays at the head of Green Bay. A trail joined their summer camps on the cold lake to the winter grounds at Big and Little Bay de Noc, a route later marked as one of the most important on the peninsula. In summer families fished, gathered wild blueberries and harvested wild rice; in winter they travelled by canoe and snowshoe into the pine woods to take beaver and otter. Their endonym, which the French wrote down as Noquet, meant bear paw. Closely related to the Menominee, in 1444 they were still among the foremost nations of the Upper Peninsula, and they also kept camps on the islands off the Garden Peninsula that once bore their name. On the rocky neck of land dividing their two bays, Spider Cave held ancient pictographs, one of them a man joined to a sixteen-legged spider by a spiral line.

Jean Nicolet met Noquet bands near Green Bay in 1634-1638, and French missionaries called their winter bays the Baie des Noquets. At the mission of Saint Michael they lived beside Menominee and Potawatomi families, and Jacques Marquette counted the whole people at about 150 people, a small Algonquian clan. The missionary Saint-Cosme still listed them among Green Bay's peoples in 1698; when Charlevoix passed through in 1721, only a few families remained. Epidemics, the Beaver Wars, mission life and marriage into Menominee, Potawatomi and Ojibwe villages dissolved the separate band, and by the early nineteenth century Noquet families lived on within those neighbouring nations. Big and Little Bay de Noc still carry their name.
zh:
诺奎特人的地方是上半岛上的一条长条地带，夹在苏必利尔湖南岸与格林湾湾头的两个海湾之间。一条步道把寒凉湖畔的夏季营地和大诺克湾、小诺克湾的冬季营地连起来，后来被标为上半岛最重要的步道之一。夏天，各家捕鱼、采野蓝莓、收野米；冬天乘独木舟、踏雪鞋进入松林，猎取河狸和水獭。他们的自称被法国人记作诺奎特，意为熊掌。诺奎特人与梅诺米尼人关系最近，1444年时仍是上半岛最主要的族群之一；加登半岛外海的一组岛屿曾以他们为名，岛上也有他们的营地。分隔两个海湾的石质岬角上有蜘蛛洞，洞中古老岩画里有一幅画着人形以螺旋线与一只十六条腿的蜘蛛相连。

让·尼克莱在1634—1638年的格林湾航行中遇到诺奎特游群，法国传教士把他们过冬的海湾称作诺奎特湾。在圣弥额尔传教站，他们与梅诺米尼人、波塔瓦托米人比邻而居，雅克·马凯特统计全族约一百五十人，只是一个小小的阿尔冈昆氏族。1698年，传教士圣科姆仍把他们列为格林湾诸族之一；沙勒瓦1721年经过时，只剩几个家族。疫病、海狸战争、传教站生活，加上与梅诺米尼、波塔瓦托米、奥吉布瓦各村的通婚，消解了这支独立的群体；到19世纪初，诺奎特各家族已生活在这些邻近民族中间。大诺克湾和小诺克湾的名字仍然来自他们。

en:
The Mamaceqtaw are the Menominee, an Algonquian people of the rivers and lakeshores around Green Bay. Their own name means 'the people'; the Ojibwe called them the Wild Rice People, and French traders took the term over as Folles-Avoines. Wild rice and sturgeon ordered their year, and five clans, Bear, Eagle, Wolf, Crane and Moose, ordered the village; their own tradition places the nation's birth at the mouth of the Menominee River. In 1444 they shared the northern forests and waters with the Ojibwe and Noquet, whom they counted as kin in language and origin.

They watched the first European landing in Wisconsin: in 1634 Jean Nicolet, still hoping to reach China, came through Green Bay in a Chinese silk robe and fired two pistols from his canoe at Red Banks. After 1667 French coureurs de bois drew the Menominee into the fur trade, yet when Charlevoix visited in 1721 the whole nation still lived in a single riverside village; he called them the finest and handsomest men in all Canada, taller even than the Potawatomi. The French defeat of the Iroquois in 1701 opened hunting grounds to the south and west, and Menominee camps spread over central Wisconsin to Milwaukee across some ten million acres. They took the French side in the colonial wars and later the British, helping hold Mackinac Island against an American assault in 1814.
zh:
马马切陶人即梅诺米尼人，是格林贝周边河湖地带的阿尔冈昆民族。自称只意为「人」；奥吉布瓦人称他们「野米人」，法国商人把这个叫法转写为「野麦人」（Folles-Avoines）。野米和鲟鱼安排着一年的生计，熊、鹰、狼、鹤、驼鹿五个氏族维系着村落；按他们自己的传统，民族诞生于梅诺米尼河河口。1444年时，他们与语言源流相近的奥吉布瓦人、诺奎人共享着北方的森林与水域。

他们亲眼看见了欧洲人在威斯康星的第一次登岸：1634年，仍一心想找到中国的让·尼科莱身着中国绸袍，在红岸附近的独木舟上鸣放两把手枪。1667年以后，法国林中人把梅诺米尼人带入毛皮贸易；而1721年沙勒瓦到访时，整个民族仍住在唯一一座河畔村落里，他称他们是全加拿大最英武俊美的人，身材比波塔瓦托米人还要高大。1701年法国战胜易洛魁后，南方和西方的猎场打开，梅诺米尼人的营地扩展到威斯康星中部、远达密尔沃基，活动范围约一千万英亩。殖民战争中他们先站在法国一边，后来又依附英国，1814年协助守住麦基诺岛，击退了美国人的进攻。

en:
In 1444 the grasslands between the upper Iowa, Des Moines and Missouri rivers were late Oneota country, where river villages tended gardens of corn, beans and squash and seasonal camps followed bison on foot. The people later called Otoe, Jiwére in their own Chiwere speech, were then still part of the Ho-Chunk world west of the Great Lakes. In the sixteenth century they split off with the Ioway and Missouria and moved south-west, in time taking to elm-bark lodges for the farming season and tipis when the bands rode out to hunt.

Marquette's 1673 map already places the Otoe near the Des Moines and upper Iowa rivers. In 1700 d'Iberville found them living with the Omaha west of the Mississippi, and through the eighteenth century their earth-lodge villages edged toward the Platte. Around 1760 Otoe and Missouria families shared a village near the Elkhorn, where horses made the summer bison hunt the centre of the year. Disease and tribal warfare thinned both groups, and eighty surviving Missouria joined the Otoe in 1796. When Lewis and Clark ascended the Missouri in 1804, the Otoe were the first tribe they met; the council of 2 August at Council Bluff put their combined population at about 500. The Americans built Fort Atkinson above the bluff in 1820, the first army post west of the Missouri, and garrisoned it on the edge of Otoe country.
zh:
1444年，上艾奥瓦河、得梅因河与密苏里河之间的草原是晚期奥内奥塔人的土地：河畔村落种着玉米、豆类和南瓜，季节性营地则徒步追踪野牛。后来被称作奥托埃、自称吉韦雷的人，此时仍属于五大湖以西的霍楚克-奇维雷世界。16世纪，他们与艾奥瓦人、密苏里人分出，向西南迁移，逐渐过上农耕季住榆皮屋、出猎时住梯皮帐篷的生活。

马凯特1673年的地图已把奥托埃人标在得梅因河与上艾奥瓦河附近。1700年，德伊贝尔维尔发现他们与奥马哈人同住于密西西比河以西；整个18世纪，他们的土屋村落一点点移向普拉特河。约1760年，奥托埃与密苏里家族共居于埃尔克霍恩河附近，马匹使夏季野牛猎成为一年中最重要的事。疫病和部落战争使两族人口锐减，1796年，八十名幸存的密苏里人并入奥托埃人。1804年刘易斯与克拉克溯密苏里河而上，遇到的第一个部落就是奥托埃人；8月2日在议事崖举行的会谈估算，两族合计约五百人。1820年，美国人在崖上修建阿特金森堡，这是密苏里河以西第一座美军哨所，驻兵于奥托埃土地的边缘。

en:
Saone covers the southwestern headwaters of the Minnesota, where river woods give way to the long grass of the Coteau des Prairies. In 1444 it was Yankton country. The Yankton were the Ihanktunwan, 'Village at the End', who with the Yanktonai called themselves the Wichiyena, one of the seven council fires of the Oceti Sakowin. No horses had yet reached them: families left the wooded lakes on foot for the summer buffalo drive, penning the herds in pounds or stampeding them over jumps, and netted fish and gathered wild rice in the northern waters. On the coteau rose the thin seam of red catlinite the Dakota called inyansha. The quarries were neutral ground, where every nation laid down its arms to cut pipe-bowls; the red stone has turned up in ancient burial mounds across the plains, and the Yankton kept the quarry for the seven fires.

The first French post came in 1700. Pierre-Charles Le Sueur built Fort L'Huillier at the mouth of the Blue Earth River, the stream the Dakota called the river where blue earth is gathered, and shipped boatloads of its blue-green clay down the Mississippi as copper ore, though the Dakota dug the same earth for body paint and it held no metal at all. A Meskwaki attack forced the garrison to abandon the fort in 1701. Through the rest of the eighteenth century Ojibwe war parties carrying French muskets pressed the Yankton and Yanktonai southwest out of the Minnesota woods onto the open plains, where horses and guns recast their lives. In 1815 the Yankton signed their first treaty with the United States, a peace and friendship agreement at Portage des Sioux on the Mississippi.
zh:
萨奥内位于明尼苏达河上游西南，河畔林地在此让位于草原台地的长草。1444年，这里是扬克顿人的地方。扬克顿人自称伊汉克顿万（Ihanktunwan），意为「尽头的村落」，与扬克顿奈人合称维奇耶纳，是奥切蒂-沙科温七堆营火之一。那时他们还没有马：夏季人们徒步离开林间湖沼围猎野牛，把牛群赶入围栏或逼下断崖，又在北方水域撒网捕鱼、采集野米。台地上出露一层薄薄的红色烟斗石，达科他语叫伊扬沙（inyansha）。采石场是中立之地，各部落都放下武器来取石刻制烟斗；远在各地的古墓中都发现过这种红石，扬克顿人为七堆营火世代看守采石场。

第一座法国据点出现于1700年。皮埃尔-夏尔·勒叙厄尔在布卢厄斯河口建起吕利耶堡，达科他人把这条河叫作「采蓝土的河」；他把一船船蓝绿色黏土当作铜矿沿密西西比河运走，而达科他人挖这种土只是用来涂身，土里根本没有铜。1701年梅斯克瓦基人来袭，守军被迫弃堡。此后整个18世纪，装备法国火枪的奥吉布瓦战队不断进逼，把扬克顿人和扬克顿奈人向西南赶出明尼苏达林地，推上开阔草原，马和火器在那里重塑了他们的生活。1815年，扬克顿人在密西西比河畔的波蒂奇德苏与美国签订第一个和平友好条约。

en:
The Sheyenne River swings eastward in a great bend across the prairie to join the Red, its wooded banks cutting through open bison grassland. In 1444 this was the western edge of the Cheyenne world. The Tsitsistas lived east of here, between the upper Mississippi and Mille Lacs, gathering wild rice and hunting bison on foot, their camps hauled by dogs; they had no horses and had never seen European goods. Only the long summer hunts brought their bands to the Sheyenne, and pressure from the Assiniboine was already pushing them west. The river woods held beaver, and the plains around them carried the herds that would one day draw the fur companies.

The best-known Cheyenne farming village stood on a terrace above an old channel of the lower Sheyenne. From about 1724 an independent band held Biesterfeldt, where a ditch and probably a palisade enclosed about seventy circular earth lodges around a plaza. Its farmers worked with bison-scapula hoes and made pottery in the manner of the Mandan and Arikara; horse bones and a few glass beads turned up among the finds. It is the only earthlodge village ever found in the Red River watershed, and it lasted barely two generations. Excavators found the lodges burned, and by about 1780 the site was empty: Lakota and Ojibwe pressure and the smallpox years had driven the band on. The Cheyenne gave up fields and earth lodges for tipis and horses and moved toward the Missouri and the Black Hills. Their old Sheyenne country became open hunting ground, crossed by the summer buffalo hunts of Assiniboine and Red River Métis brigades, and by 1821 fur caravans were using it as a road west.
zh:
马坎德韦温一带，夏延河在草原上绕出一个大弯，折而向东汇入红河；两岸林木成带，切开开阔的野牛草原。1444年，这里是夏延人世界的西缘。自称齐齐斯塔斯的夏延人住在更东边，介于密西西比河上游与米尔湖之间，采集野米、徒步猎牛，营地全靠狗拖拽；他们没有马，也没见过欧洲货物。只有夏季的长途猎队才会来到夏延河，而阿西尼博因人的逼迫已在把他们逐步推向西方。河畔林地多河狸，四周草原上野牛成群，日后正是这些引来了毛皮公司。

夏延人最有名的一座农耕村落，坐落在夏延河下游一条故河道旁的阶地上。约1724年起，一支独立的夏延人据有比斯特费尔特村，围壕之内可能还树有栅栏，约七十座圆形土屋环着广场而建。村人以野牛肩胛骨为锄，烧造近于曼丹人和阿里卡拉人风格的陶器，遗存中还见有马骨和少量玻璃珠。这是红河流域迄今发现的唯一一座土屋村落，只存在了不到两代人的时间。发掘时土屋都有焚烧痕迹，约1780年遗址已经空无一人，拉科塔人、奥吉布瓦人的逼迫和天花流行的岁月把这支夏延人赶向西方。他们舍弃农田和土屋，改用帐篷与马匹，迁往密苏里河和布莱克山。夏延河故土就此成为开放猎场，阿西尼博因人和红河梅蒂人的夏季猎牛队穿行其间，到1821年，毛皮商队已把这里当作西进的通道。

en:
Chinko is the tallgrass country between the Illinois River valley and the Wabash watershed, where prairie is broken by oak groves and the wooded valleys of the Kankakee, Iroquois and Vermilion rivers. In 1444 it was Illini range, shared by the small Chinkoa band that French writers recorded as Chinko. Villages moved with the seasons: women tended corn, beans and squash in the river bottoms, and hunting parties followed bison across the open grass. Miami-speaking Wea and Piankeshaw lived to the east, and no European had yet seen the prairie.

War reached Chinko in the second half of the seventeenth century, when Iroquois Five Nations parties armed through Dutch and English trade raided far south for pelts and captives, scattering Illini bands toward the Mississippi at the height of the Beaver Wars. The little Chinkoa band vanishes from the records in those years, one of the Illini tribes that did not survive the century as a separate people. Louis Jolliet and Jacques Marquette crossed the Illinois Country in 1673, and La Salle's expedition followed in 1682, opening the French fur trade and drawing the remaining villages into the French alliance. That claim ended in 1763, when all land east of the Mississippi passed to Britain; Kickapoo and Potawatomi bands were already moving into the empty prairie. After the American Revolution the country entered the Northwest Territory, and the Kickapoo ceded their claims here in the 1819 Treaty of Edwardsville.
zh:
钦科位于伊利诺伊河谷与沃巴什水系之间，高草草原上散布着橡树林，以及坎卡基河、伊罗夸伊河和弗米利恩河林木丛生的河谷。1444年，这里是伊利尼人的活动范围，法国文献记作「钦科」（Chinko）的小支钦科阿人也在这片土地上游居。村落随季节迁徙：妇女在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，猎队穿过开阔草地追逐野牛。东面住着说迈阿密语的韦阿人和皮安克肖人，那时还没有欧洲人见过这片草原。

战争在17世纪下半叶打到钦科：易洛魁五族的战队靠荷兰与英国贸易得来的火器远征南方，在海狸战争中为毛皮和俘虏扫荡草原，把伊利尼各支驱向密西西比河。小小的钦科阿支在这些年里从记载中消失，成了未能作为独立部族熬过那个世纪的伊利尼分支之一。1673年，路易·若利埃和雅克·马凯特穿过伊利尼地区，拉萨尔远征队1682年继至，毛皮贸易随之展开，残存村落被拉入法国同盟。法国的宣称在1763年终结，密西西比河以东土地全部转归英国；基卡普人和波塔瓦托米人早已进入空旷的草原。美国独立战争后，这片土地归入西北领地，基卡普人又在1819年《爱德华兹维尔条约》中割让了他们在这里的权利。

en:
The Espeminkia were one of the twelve tribes of the Illinois, the loose Illiniwek confederacy of Miami-Illinois-speaking villagers in the Mississippi and Illinois river valleys. Their lodges of rush mats and bark stood beside fertile bottomlands where women grew maize, beans and squash; on the northern prairies the men joined bison hunts several hundred strong, drying the meat and dressing robes for trade. In 1444 the Illinois were still among the masters of the middle Mississippi, far from any European.

Jolliet and Marquette canoed through in 1673 and visited the Kaskaskia Grand Village on the Illinois River; after a Jesuit mission was founded there in 1675 it grew to perhaps 6,000 people in about 460 houses, likely the largest Native town north of Mexico, and La Salle built Fort Saint Louis on the great rock across the river. In 1680 an Iroquois army sacked the Grand Village and carried off hundreds of captives, and the site was abandoned around 1691. War and epidemic thinned the twelve tribes to five by 1700, and the Espeminkia no longer survived as a separate tribe. The remnant Illinois raided beside the French through the Fox Wars, until a Fox stronghold on the Sangamon was stormed in 1730. They lost their French patrons in 1763, the British took Fort de Chartres in 1765, and by 1778 the whole confederacy numbered only about 300 people. Local tradition says the last Illinois starved under siege on the rock called Starved Rock, but no record of the event survives.
zh:
埃斯佩明基亚人是伊利诺伊人十二支之一。伊利诺伊人又称伊利尼维克，是说迈阿密－伊利尼语的松散联盟，散居在密西西比河与伊利诺伊河流域。他们的草席和树皮小屋建在肥沃的河漫滩旁，妇女种玉米、豆子和南瓜；男子到北方草原参加数百人规模的围猎，猎牛晒肉、鞣制皮袍用来交易。1444年时，伊利诺伊人仍是密西西比河中游的主人之一，欧洲人还远在天边。

若利埃和马凯特1673年泛舟经过此地，走访伊利诺伊河畔的卡斯卡斯基亚大村；1675年耶稣会传教站在村里建起后，大村发展到约六千人和四百六十座房屋，可能是墨西哥以北最大的原住民城镇，拉萨尔还在河对岸的巨岩上筑起圣路易堡（Fort Saint Louis）。1680年，易洛魁军队洗劫大村，掳走数百人，村址约在1691年废弃。战乱和疫病使十二支到1700年只剩五支，埃斯佩明基亚人不再作为独立一支存续。残存的伊利诺伊人在福克斯战争中随法国人出征，直到1730年福克斯人在桑加蒙河畔的据点被攻破。1763年法国战败，他们失去庇护，英军1765年接管沙特尔堡；到1778年，整个联盟只剩约三百人。当地传说最后一批伊利诺伊人被围困在饥饿岩（Starved Rock）上饿死，但此事没有任何记载流传下来。

en:
In 1444 the Illinois River crossed the meeting line of eastern woodland and western prairie below a steep sandstone butte later called Le Rocher by the French. Illini villages planted corn, beans and squash in the alluvial soil, gathered wetland roots, and hunted deer and elk between river and grassland. The Tapouaro were one of the small Miami-Illinois divisions that shared the settlement the French knew as the Grand Village of the Illinois; set between forest and prairie, the town let its people mediate exchange between the two worlds.

Louis Jolliet and Jacques Marquette reached that village in 1673 and counted about seventy-three cabins and 1,000 people. Marquette came back in 1675, already dying, to found the Mission of the Immaculate Conception. French guns, trade and refuge drew so many bands that reports of the 1680s list about 400 cabins and as many as 6,000 people, for a time the largest Native settlement north of Mexico. An Iroquois army burned the village in the autumn of 1680, at the height of the Beaver Wars. In the winter of 1682 La Salle built Fort Saint-Louis du Rocher on top of the butte, its timbers hauled up the only climbable slope, and gave the command to Henri de Tonti, who had lost a hand to a grenade in Sicily and wore an iron hook under a glove. Illinois, Miami, Shawnee and Mahican families camped beneath the walls. Iroquois pressure never eased: Tonti pulled the garrison back to Fort Pimiteoui near Peoria in 1691, and by 1700 the Tapouaro no longer appeared as a separate people, their descendants absorbed among the Peoria and Kaskaskia.
zh:
1444年，伊利诺伊河在一座陡峭砂岩崖下流过，这里是东部林地与西部草原的交界；法国人后来把这座崖称作岩石。伊利尼村落在冲积土上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，采集湿地根茎，在河与草原之间猎鹿和美洲马鹿。塔波阿罗是迈阿密-伊利诺伊语的小群体之一，和其他伊利尼群体共用法国人所称的伊利诺伊大村落；村子卡在林地与草原之间，村民得以居间往来于两个世界之间。

1673年，路易·乔利埃特与雅克·马凯特来到这座村落，数出约七十三座棚屋、一千人。1675年，已在病中的马凯特重返此地，建立圣母无原罪传教站。法国火枪、贸易和庇护吸引众多群体投奔，1680年代的记载已有约四百座棚屋、多达六千人，一度是墨西哥以北最大的原住民聚落。1680年秋，海狸战争正酣，一支易洛魁军队焚毁了村落。1682年冬，拉萨尔在崖顶修建圣路易堡，木料全靠人沿唯一可登的斜坡拖上去，守将是亨利·德·通蒂：他在西西里被手榴弹炸掉一只手，手套里戴着一只铁钩。伊利尼、迈阿密、肖尼和莫希干家族在堡墙下扎营。易洛魁的压力始终未减，1691年通蒂把守军撤往皮奥里亚附近的皮米特乌堡；到1700年，塔波阿罗不再作为独立群体见于记载，后裔并入佩奥利亚人和卡斯卡基亚人。

en:
This stretch of the Mississippi runs from the Des Moines Rapids, where the water spills over eleven miles of shallow limestone ledges, down to the wooded bluffs above the mouth of the Illinois. On both banks Illini villages planted corn, beans and squash in the bottoms and left for the prairie on the winter bison hunt. The Coiracoentanon were one of the twelve or thirteen small divisions of the Illiniwek counted by the French, kinsmen of the Peoria and the Tapouaro. High on a limestone bluff at the lower end of the corridor native painters had set two great monsters, antlered and scaled, their long tails curling round their bodies; passing boatmen offered tobacco smoke to the manitou of the rock. In 1444 the whole river was Illinois country.

Jolliet and Marquette came downstream in 1673, and Marquette left the first written description of the painted bluff. The Coiracoentanon were among the Illinois groups attached to the Grand Village up the Illinois River, and when the Iroquois wars scattered its people they drifted down to Cahokia and Kaskaskia. Sauk and Meskwaki bands then took up the empty country, and a Sauk village led by Quashquame stood at the head of the rapids. The peace of 1763 divided the river, Britain taking the east bank and Spain the west. After the Louisiana Purchase the Americans built Fort Madison beside the rapids in 1808, their first permanent post on the upper Mississippi. British-allied Sauk besieged it during the War of 1812, the young warrior Black Hawk fighting before its walls and claiming he shot down its flag, and the garrison burned and abandoned it in 1813.
zh:
这一段密西西比河北起得梅因急流，河水在十一英里长的浅水石灰岩岩脊上漫过，南至伊利诺伊河口上方林木覆盖的崖岸。两岸的伊利尼村落在河漫滩种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，冬季则出发到草原围猎野牛。科伊拉科恩塔农是法国人清点出的伊利尼韦克十二三个小分支之一，与佩奥利亚人、塔波阿罗人同源。在走廊南端的石灰岩高崖上，原住民画师绘有两头巨兽，头上长角、身覆鳞片、长尾盘绕身躯；过往的船工向崖上的「马尼图」献上烟草的烟。1444年，整条大河都是伊利尼人的土地。

1673年，乔利埃特与马凯特顺水南下，马凯特为这座画崖留下了最早的文字记载。科伊拉科恩塔农人是与伊利诺伊河上游大村落有关的伊利尼群体之一，易洛魁战争打散村民后，他们顺流而下，流落卡霍基亚和卡斯卡基亚。索克人和梅斯夸基人随即进入空出的土地，夸什夸梅率领的索克村落就设在急流北端。1763年的和约把大河两岸分归英国与西班牙，东岸属英、西岸属西。路易斯安那购地之后，美国人于1808年在急流旁修筑麦迪逊堡，这是他们在密西西比河上游的第一座常驻据点；1812年战争中，与英国结盟的索克人围攻此堡，年轻的武士黑鹰在墙下作战，自称曾击落堡上的旗帜；1813年，守军焚毁堡垒并撤离。

en:
Mosopelea is the Siouan-speaking country between the Muskingum and Scioto rivers on the Ohio's north bank, a land of older Hopewell mounds, Fort Ancient fields and steep wooded valley walls. Women grew maize, beans and squash on the fertile bottoms, and canoe parties used the Ohio and the two tributaries as highways. The Miami-Illinois name for the great river was Mosopeleacipi, river of the Mosopelea, later shortened by the Shawnee to Pelisipi and carried south to the Clinch. In 1444 Europeans were still beyond the Alleghenies, and village councils held the paths, fields and fishing waters.

The villages did not last the century. Seneca and other Haudenosaunee warriors overran them in the Beaver Wars of the early 1670s, and when Jean-Baptiste-Louis Franquelin mapped the Ohio valley in 1684 he marked all eight as destroyed; Marquette and Joliet, travelling the Mississippi in 1673, had already heard that the people had probably moved south. They did, and became known as the Ofo, living briefly with the Quapaw and then among the French-allied Tunica on the lower Mississippi. The old country served mainly as a Haudenosaunee hunting ground until France and Britain began their contest for it. On 15 August 1749 a French party under Céloron de Blainville stopped at the Muskingum's mouth and set one of its inscribed lead plates into the earth, claiming the whole valley for France; Wyandot and Lenape towns stood there when American settlers arrived after the Revolutionary War. Marietta, founded at the mouth in 1788, was the first permanent American settlement in the Northwest Territory. On 2 January 1791 Lenape and Wyandot fighters struck the Big Bottom outpost thirty miles up the Muskingum, stormed its half-built blockhouse and killed fourteen settlers, eleven men, a woman and two children. The Treaty of Greenville closed that war in 1795 and opened the valley to surveyors.
zh:
莫索佩莱阿是俄亥俄河北岸、马斯金格姆河与赛欧托河之间的苏语人群之地，境内散布着更古老的霍普韦尔土丘、堡古文化农田和林木陡峭的谷壁。妇女在肥沃低地上种玉米、豆类和南瓜，独木舟队伍借俄亥俄河与两条支流往来。迈阿密—伊利诺伊语把这条大河叫作莫索佩莱阿西皮（Mosopeleacipi），意为「莫索佩莱阿人之河」；肖尼人后来把它简称为佩利西皮（Pelisipi），这个名字又被带到南方的克林奇河。1444年时欧洲人仍远在阿勒格尼山脉之外，村社议事会掌握着小路、农田和渔场。

这些村镇没有存留到那个世纪末。17世纪70年代初，塞内卡及其他豪德诺索尼战士在河狸战争中攻陷它们；1684年弗兰克兰绘制俄亥俄河谷地图时，已把八座村镇全部标为已毁。早在1673年，沿密西西比河旅行的马凯特和若利埃就听说莫索佩莱阿人很可能已经南迁。他们确实走了，后来被称为奥福人，曾短暂与夸保人同住，最后投到密西西比河下游与法国结盟的蒂尼卡人中间。故土主要成为豪德诺索尼人的猎场，直到法国和英国开始争夺。1749年8月15日，塞洛隆·德·布兰维尔率领的法国队伍在马斯金格姆河口停下，把一块刻字铅牌埋入土中，为法国宣称整个河谷；美国定居者独立战争后抵达时，那里已有怀安多特和莱纳佩人的村镇。1788年在河口建立的玛丽埃塔，是西北领地第一个永久美国定居点。1791年1月2日，莱纳佩与怀安多特战士袭击马斯金格姆河上游三十英里处的大底部据点，攻入尚未修成的木堡，杀死十四名定居者，其中有十一名男子、一名妇女和两名儿童。1795年《格林维尔条约》结束这场战争，向测量者开放了河谷。

en:
Tawehash preserves Taovaya, the name of a powerful Wichita people. Their later stronghold was the middle Red River, where grassy bottoms and oak groves meet the plains west of the Caddo towns. In 1444 Caddoan-speaking families here combined limited river-bottom farming with seasonal bison hunts; dogs pulled the travois before horses reached the southern plains, and this stretch of the river was Wichita and Tonkawa country. The Taovaya themselves then lived farther north, in the Wichita world of Kansas.

Osage and Apache pressure helped push the Taovaya south during the 1720s, and they built twin towns facing each other across the Oklahoma and Texas banks of the Red River. After France brokered their peace with the Comanche in 1746, the crossing became one of the busiest markets on the southern plains. Comanche parties brought horses, mules and Apache captives and took French powder, shot, knives and textiles; the Taovaya sold maize, melons, pumpkins, squash and tobacco from their fields. Spanish officers who later approached the towns found entrenchments, a wooden stockade and a moat, with a French flag flying over the lodges.

In March 1758 a Comanche-led coalition of Norteño peoples burned the San Sabá mission beyond the Texas settlements. That August Colonel Diego Ortiz Parrilla marched about five hundred Spaniards and Lipan Apaches against the Red River towns, but his column walked into an ambush and fell back, leaving two bronze cannon behind. The Taovaya made peace with Spain in 1771 and handed the guns back in 1778, when Athanase de Mézières, the lieutenant governor at Natchitoches, came to settle the horse thefts and named the place San Teodoro; the twin towns then held 160 houses, six hundred men and perhaps 2,500 people. Smallpox in 1777-78 killed about a third of the Wichita, and another epidemic in 1801 thinned them again, so that in 1805 John Sibley counted only four hundred Taovaya men. When Chief Awahakei died at Natchitoches in 1811, the band chose no successor and broke apart, some families joining the Tawakoni. In 1821 the Adams-Onís Treaty made the Red River the frontier with Mexico, and the survivors were counted simply as Wichita.
zh:
塔韦哈什保存着塔瓦亚人（Taovaya）这支强大威奇塔群体的名字。他们后来的重镇在雷德河中游：多草的河滩与橡树林在此相接，东边就是卡多人的城镇。1444年，说卡多语族语言的家庭在河滩经营有限的农耕，又按季节出猎野牛；马匹传入南部平原以前，迁营靠狗拉拖架，雷德河中游这一段是威奇塔人与通卡瓦人的地盘。塔瓦亚人本支当时还住在更北边，属于堪萨斯的威奇塔世界。

18世纪20年代，在奥塞奇人与阿帕奇人的压力下，塔瓦亚人向南迁移，在雷德河今俄克拉荷马与得克萨斯两岸建起隔河相望的双子村。1746年法国撮合他们与科曼奇人议和后，这个渡口成了南部平原最热闹的市集之一：科曼奇人赶来马匹、骡子和阿帕奇俘虏，换走法国火药、铅弹、刀和布匹；塔瓦亚人则卖出田里出产的玉米、甜瓜、南瓜、倭瓜和烟草。后来开到村前的西班牙军官看到的，是壕沟、木栅和一道护城河，营帐上方还飘着法国旗。

1758年3月，科曼奇人主导的「北方人」联盟焚毁了得克萨斯定居点以西的圣萨瓦传教站。同年8月，迭戈·奥尔蒂斯·帕里利亚上校率约五百名西班牙士兵和利潘阿帕奇人进攻雷德河双子村，却中了埋伏败退，丢下两门青铜炮。塔瓦亚人1771年与西班牙议和，1778年交还火炮；纳基托什的副省长阿塔纳斯·德·梅齐埃这一年为盗马纠纷前来，把此地命名为圣特奥多罗。当时双子村共有一百六十座房屋、六百名男子，总人口可能约二千五百。1777至1778年的天花夺走约三分之一威奇塔人的性命，1801年疫病再起，1805年约翰·西布利只点到四百名塔瓦亚男子。1811年酋长阿瓦哈凯在纳基托什去世，部众没有再选首领，群体就此离散，一部分家庭并入塔瓦科尼人。1821年《亚当斯-奥尼斯条约》把雷德河定为与墨西哥之间的边界，幸存者此后只被笼统算作威奇塔人。

en:
Kitsash preserves K'itsäsh, the name of the Kichai, a Caddoan people of the southern plains. In 1444 their villages and camps lay in the grassy river country of north-central Texas and southern Oklahoma, along the upper Red and Trinity rivers, west of the better-known Caddo towns. They farmed the river bottoms and set out on foot, with dogs carrying the camp gear, for seasonal bison hunts on the plains.

French travellers came upon Kichai bands on the upper Red River and the Trinity headwaters in 1701. They were fighting the Hasinai down the Trinity in 1712, and in 1719 the trader La Harpe found them near the Canadian River and drew them into his campaigns against the Apache; the Kichai took to horses about then and kept the French alliance for a time. The people later split, one branch joining the Wichita and the other marrying into the Kadohadacho. A Spanish count in 1772 found their main village east of the Trinity, thirty houses and eighty warriors; another village stood to the south in 1778, when Spanish records put all their warriors at about a hundred. Disease and the French-Spanish rivalry had cut their numbers hard by 1821.
zh:
基察什保留着基蔡人的自称K'itsäsh，他们是南部大平原上的卡多语族人群。1444年，他们的村落和营地分布在得州中北部与俄克拉荷马南部多水草的河谷，雷德河与特里尼蒂河上游一带，位于名气更大的卡多诸镇以西。他们在河滩耕作，出猎时步行，由狗驮着营地家当，按季到大平原上猎野牛。

1701年，法国旅行者在雷德河上游和特里尼蒂河源头遇到基蔡人的群体。1712年，他们沿特里尼蒂河下同哈西奈人交战；1719年，商人拉阿尔普在加拿大河附近找到他们，把他们拉进对抗阿帕奇人的战事，基蔡人约在此时开始养马，并一度维持与法国的同盟。这个部族后来分裂，一支投奔威奇托人，另一支与卡多哈达乔人通婚。1772年西班牙人清点时，他们位于特里尼蒂河以东的主村有三十座房屋、八十名战士；1778年南面又有一座村子，西班牙记录估计全部战士约一百人。到1821年，疫病和法国与西班牙的争夺已使他们人口大减。

en:
Tawakoni means 'river bend among red sand hills' in the Wichita tongue, and the name fit the river country the tribe held along the southern edge of the plains, the bottomlands of the Arkansas and the Cimarron. They were one of the Wichita-speaking Caddoan peoples, farming villagers set between the Plains Apaches to their west and the stockaded Caddo towns of the east. In 1444 Tawakoni families planted maize, pumpkins and peas on the floodplain and fired pottery for exchange with neighbouring bands. They lived in domed grass lodges, and each winter broke camp to follow the bison herds, moving over the open plains in skin tipis.

The first European to reach them was Jean-Baptiste Bénard de La Harpe, who in 1719 found a Tawakoni village in what is now Muskogee County, Oklahoma, surrounded by fields of maize and tobacco, and mediated a peace between France and the Tawakoni and eight other tribes. Osage raids, together with French and Spanish pressure, carried the tribe south; Spanish records place them on the Brazos alongside the Waco by 1730. For the next forty years they kept the French as friends and the Spanish as enemies. In 1772 Chief Quiscat travelled to San Antonio to settle peace with the Spaniards, but the agreement did not hold. By the early nineteenth century disease and warfare had thinned the Tawakoni, whose future lay with the Waco and the wider Wichita confederacy.
zh:
塔瓦科尼在威奇托语里意为「红沙丘陵间的河曲」，这个名字正合他们居住的平原南缘，即阿肯色河与锡马龙河的滩地。他们是说威奇托语的卡多安语族之一，务农而居，夹在西边的平原阿帕奇人与东边设栅的卡多城镇之间。1444年，塔瓦科尼各家在河滩种植玉米、南瓜和豌豆，烧制陶器与邻近部族交换。他们住在干草搭成的圆顶草屋里，每年冬季拔营，跟着野牛群在开阔平原上迁徙，住进兽皮帐篷。

第一个找到他们的欧洲人是让-巴蒂斯特·贝纳尔·德·拉阿尔普。1719年，他在今俄克拉荷马州马斯科吉县境内见到一座塔瓦科尼村落，四周是玉米田和烟草田，并促成法国与塔瓦科尼及另外八个部族议和。奥塞奇人的袭击，加上法国和西班牙的压力，把这支人推向南方；西班牙文献记载，到1730年他们已与韦科人同住在布拉索斯河畔。此后四十年，他们以法国为友、以西班牙为敌。1772年，首领奎斯卡特亲赴圣安东尼奥与西班牙人议和，但协议没有维持住。到19世纪初，疾病和战争使塔瓦科尼人大为减少，他们的前途系于韦科人和更广泛的威奇托联盟。

en:
Nabaydacu, Nabáydácu in Caddo and often written Nabedache, means 'blackberry place'. The country lay between the Neches and Trinity rivers, the westernmost Hasinai land on the edge of the Caddo world. In 1444 permanent villages grew maize, beans and squash in the Piney Woods, and priests kept the ceremonies that fixed planting and harvest. Plains peoples came from the west with Jumano trade goods, and Kadohadacho towns lay to the north.

The French contest with Spain put the Nabedache on European maps. Henri Joutel, left in command of La Salle's Fort Saint-Louis colony on the Texas coast, reached their villages near the Neches headwaters in 1686, and his journal gives the first European description of them. Spain answered the French intrusion with a mission among the Caddo: San Francisco de los Tejas was dedicated among the Nabedache in 1690, staffed by three friars and three soldiers. Smallpox swept the country that winter and killed about 3,300 people, and the Nabedache blamed the newcomers; after two summers of drought the friars burned their own church in 1693 and retreated to Monclova. The Ramón–St. Denis expedition, a Spanish column guided by the French trader Louis de Saint-Denis, reopened the mission in 1716, but it was abandoned and reoccupied twice in the Franco-Spanish wars before being withdrawn to San Antonio in 1731 and renamed San Francisco de la Espada. The Nabedache stayed on their river lands and traded with the Jumano at their western town, moving higher up the Neches late in the century. Epidemics and the failed missions had thinned them by 1821, but they remained the westernmost Hasinai people.
zh:
纳拜达库（卡多语作Nabáydácu，欧洲文献常拼作Nabedache）意为「黑莓之地」。这片土地位于内奇斯河与特里尼蒂河之间，是哈西奈联盟最西端的地盘，处在卡多世界的边缘。1444年，这里的永久村落在松林地中种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，祭司掌管着规定播种与收获的仪式。西面，大平原上的人群带着胡马诺人的商货前来，北方则是卡多哈达乔人的城镇。

法国与西班牙的争夺把纳拜达库人带上了欧洲人的地图。探险家拉萨尔在得州海岸留下圣路易堡，由亨利·茹泰勒据守；1686年，茹泰勒抵达内奇斯河源头附近的纳拜达库村落，他的日记留下了欧洲人对他们最早的描述。为回应法国人的闯入，西班牙在卡多人中开设传教站：圣方济各·德·洛斯·特哈斯于1690年在纳拜达库人中间祝圣，随站的只有三名修士和三名士兵。那年冬天天花席卷此地，约三千三百人病死，纳拜达库人怪罪新来的西班牙人；连着两个夏天干旱之后，修士们在1693年亲手烧掉教堂，撤回蒙克洛瓦。拉蒙与法国商人圣但尼联合率领的探险队于1716年重开传教站，但它在法国与西班牙的战事中两度弃守又重开，最终于1731年迁往圣安东尼奥，改名圣方济各·德·拉埃斯帕达。纳拜达库人始终留在自己的河地，在西部村镇与胡马诺人交易，又在18世纪后期迁向内奇斯河更上游。到1821年，疫病和一次次失败的传教使他们人口大减，但他们仍是哈西奈联盟最西端的人群。

en:
The Mohawk call the St Lawrence Kaniatarowanenneh, the great waterway. Above Lake St. Francis the river braids among wooded islands and rapids, where eel run thick and migrating waterfowl gather. In 1444 both banks were held by St. Lawrence Iroquoians, Laurentian speakers, who lived in palisaded towns of bark longhouses, planted maize, beans and squash on the river flats and took eel at weirs below the falls. Their towns answered to no one: they were independent of each other and of the Iroquois leagues to the south, from whose side Mohawk war parties were already pushing up the river.

Jacques Cartier was feasted in towns of these people in 1535, but when Champlain reached the river seventy-five years later every one of them had gone, destroyed or driven out in the Mohawk wars for the fur trade and the hunting. The valley became an empty hunting ground and a war-road between the Great Lakes and the French settlements. In the mid-1750s about thirty Catholic Mohawk families from Kahnawake moved twenty leagues upriver to settle it. Their chiefs included the brothers John and Zachariah Tarbell, English boys of twelve and eight carried off from Groton in 1707, adopted by Mohawk families and later married to chiefs' daughters. The village took the name Akwesasne, 'the land where the partridge drums'; French Jesuits opened the St Regis mission there in 1755, the French paid for a sawmill, and in 1795 the Mohawk finished a stone church that served as a landmark for boats running the rapids. It became one of the Seven Nations of Canada.

Most Mohawk fought for the British in the Revolutionary War, and the peace that followed drew a new international border straight through the villages, leaving families on both sides; the Jay Treaty of 1794 nonetheless left them free to cross. On 11 November 1813, at Crysler's Farm a few miles downstream, a small British and Canadian force routed a much larger American army marching on Montreal, and the United States abandoned its St Lawrence campaign.
zh:
莫霍克人称圣劳伦斯河为卡尼亚塔罗瓦嫩（Kaniatarowanenneh），意为「大水之道」。圣弗朗西斯湖上游这一段，河汊在林木葱郁的岛屿与急流间分合，鳗鱼成群，候鸟迁徙时在此聚集。1444年时，两岸居住着说劳伦提亚语的圣劳伦斯易洛魁人：他们住在树皮长屋组成的栅栏村镇里，在滩地上种植玉米、豆类和南瓜，在瀑布下的鱼堰中捕捞鳗鱼。这些村镇谁也不属，彼此互不统属，也不归附南方的易洛魁联盟，而莫霍克战队已从那一侧沿河向上进逼。

1535年，雅克·卡蒂亚还在这些人的村镇里受到宴饮款待；七十五年后尚普兰再来时，村镇已全部消失——为控制毛皮贸易和猎场，莫霍克人在战争中摧毁或驱逐了他们。河谷成了空旷的猎场，以及五大湖与法兰西定居点之间的战道。18世纪50年代中期，约三十户信奉天主教的莫霍克家庭从卡纳瓦克溯河而上约二十里格，到此定居。为首的酋长中有约翰·塔尔贝尔与扎卡赖亚斯·塔尔贝尔兄弟：1707年他们一个十二岁、一个八岁，被从马萨诸塞的格罗顿掳走，由莫霍克家庭收养，后来都娶了酋长的女儿。新村取名阿克威萨斯尼（Akwesasne），意为「松鸡振翅之地」；法国耶稣会士1755年在此开设圣雷吉斯传教站，法国人出资建起锯木厂，1795年莫霍克人建成石砌教堂，成为行船闯滩时的航标。这里后来是加拿大七部族之一。

独立战争中多数莫霍克人站在英国一边；战后划定的新国界径直穿过村落，把一家人分在两侧，而1794年《杰伊条约》仍允许他们自由越界。1813年11月11日，在下游不远的克莱斯勒农场，一支人数不多的英军与加拿大民兵击溃了远征蒙特利尔的庞大美军，美国就此放弃圣劳伦斯河战役。

en:
The Cumberland River curves through the Nashville Basin, a rolling downland cupped inside the wooded ridge of the Highland Rim. Brine springs break out along its banks, and their salt licks drew such herds of bison and deer that animal paths wore roads through the canebrake. In 1444 palisaded villages of the Middle Cumberland Mississippian culture farmed the bottoms; their platform mounds had risen at river bends such as Mound Bottom since about AD 1000. The Yuchi of the Tennessee valley, whom the Cherokee called Aniyutsi, hunted north as far as these licks.

By about 1500 the mound towns had collapsed under drought, disease and warfare, and for nearly two centuries the basin held no permanent villages. Shawnee bands moved in late in the 1600s, until Cherokee and Chickasaw raiders pressed them out. French fur men came for the same salt. Martin Chartier set up a post on the Cumberland in 1689, Jean du Charleville built beside a sulphur spring in 1710 at the place called French Lick, and from 1769 the French-Canadian trapper Timothy DeMonbreun kept a cabin there between hunts.

Long hunters' reports of the empty, fertile bottoms brought settlers from North Carolina. James Robertson's overland party and John Donelson's river fleet reached French Lick in 1779–80 and raised Fort Nashborough, a two-acre log stockade, and 256 settlers signed the Cumberland Compact in May 1780. Its frontier government paid its governor a thousand deerskins a year and its clerks in raccoon skins. Andrew Jackson, newly arrived from the Carolinas, was admitted to the bar at Nashville's first court in 1788. Chickamauga Cherokee raided the outlying stations for fourteen years, until the Nickajack campaign of September 1794, known to the settlers as the last battle of the Cherokee, broke their resistance and opened the basin to safe settlement. North Carolina had chartered the town as Nashville in 1784.
zh:
坎伯兰河蜿蜒穿过纳什维尔盆地，盆地是一片起伏低地，卧在林木覆盖的高地边缘台地环抱之中。河畔多处涌出盐泉，形成舔盐的盐滩，野牛和鹿群成群来此，兽群踏出的小径在藤丛间踩成了道路。1444年，中坎伯兰密西西比文化的栅栏村镇在河漫滩上耕作；约自公元1000年起，他们的台庙土丘已立在芒德博顿这样的河湾处。田纳西河谷的尤奇人（切罗基人称其为「阿尼尤齐」）北上游猎，足迹远达这些盐滩。

约1500年前后，土丘城镇在干旱、疫病和战争的压力下崩溃，此后近两百年盆地内没有常住的村落。17世纪末肖尼人一度进入，后来被切罗基和奇克索的袭掠者逼走。法国毛皮商人同样为盐而来。1689年，马丹·沙尔捷在坎伯兰河畔设立贸易站；1710年，让·迪·沙勒维尔在一处硫磺泉边建起商站，那地方得名法国盐滩；1769年起，法裔加拿大捕兽人蒂莫西·德蒙布勒安又在泉边留了一间小屋，供狩猎间隙落脚。

长猎人带回的消息说，这片空出来的肥沃低地适于开垦，北卡罗来纳的移民于是远道而来。1779至1780年，詹姆斯·罗伯逊的陆路队伍与约翰·多纳尔森的船队抵达法国盐滩，筑起占地两英亩的圆木寨堡纳什伯勒堡；1780年5月，256名移民签订《坎伯兰契约》，这套边疆政体规定总督年俸为一千张鹿皮，文书的薪给用浣熊皮支付。1788年，刚从卡罗来纳迁来的安德鲁·杰克逊在纳什维尔的首次庭审上获准执业律师。此后十四年，奇克莫加切罗基人不断袭掠外围据点，直到1794年9月的尼卡杰克远征粉碎其抵抗，移民称之为切罗基人的「最后一战」，盆地这才安定下来。城镇则早在1784年已由北卡罗来纳特许建为纳什维尔。

en:
Neozho takes its name from an Osage word for clear water. The province covers the upper Neosho and Verdigris rivers, prairie broken by wooded stream valleys southeast of the Arkansas bend. In 1444 Wichita villagers of the Caddoan speech family lived here in round, thatched-roof lodges, raised maize, beans, squash and sunflowers on the bottoms, and rode out on communal bison hunts. Their streams carried their trade toward the Arkansas towns the Spanish later heard of as Quivira.

Coronado reached those towns in 1541 and counted about twenty-five settlements of as many as two hundred houses each, well fed and well lodged but holding neither gold nor silver. The first official French party came in 1719: Claude Charles du Tisné crossed 250 miles of Ozark hills and plain from the Osage country, whose chiefs tried to keep him from going farther, and reached two Wichita towns four days apart on the Verdigris. The French guns that followed did the Wichitas little good. Apache raids from the west, Osage pressure from the east and epidemic disease pushed the whole people south toward the Red River by 1757. Osage hunters then worked the empty valleys; Lewis and Clark met an Arkansas Osage band on the Verdigris in 1804, and in 1821 no European settlement yet stood on either river.
zh:
尼欧肖得名于欧塞奇语，意思是清水。这片地方在尼欧肖河与弗迪格里斯河上游、阿肯色河大拐弯东南，是草原与林地交错之地。1444年，说卡多语的威奇托村民住在圆形茅草顶屋里，在低地种玉米、豆子、南瓜和向日葵，按季节集体出猎野牛。河川把他们的交换带向阿肯色河畔的城镇，西班牙人后来把那里称作基维拉。

1541年科罗纳多抵达这些城镇，数到约25座聚落，每座多至200所房屋，居民吃得饱、住得好，却没有金银。1719年法国首个正式使团到来：克洛德·沙尔·迪蒂斯内从欧塞奇地区出发，穿越250英里的欧扎克山地与草原，欧塞奇首领曾试图拦阻，他仍走到弗迪格里斯河畔两座相距四日路程的威奇托城镇。随法国火器而来的并没有给威奇托人带来好处。西边阿帕奇人的袭掠、东边欧塞奇人的逼迫，加上疫病，到1757年把整个族群逼向南方的雷德河。欧塞奇猎人随后进入空下来的河谷；1804年刘易斯与克拉克在弗迪格里斯河遇到一支阿肯色欧塞奇人；到1821年，两条河上还没有欧洲人的定居点。

en:
Pitahawirata is one of the three southern Pawnee bands, whom the French called the Tappage, the Noisy Pawnee. Their river country lies between the Republican and the Platte, where Nebraska's plains tilt down toward Kansas. In 1444 the Caddoan villagers ancestral to those bands lived in earth lodges on this grassland: women tended maize, beans and squash, and the camps walked out together on communal bison hunts. Priests and hereditary chiefs led the rites, and neither horses nor European guns had reached the plains. Their kin and trade ran to the Chaui and Kitkehahki and to the Wichita farther south, not to the Skiri on the Loup.

By 1750 the southern Pawnee and their Wichita allies held firm grounds on the Arkansas, kept supplied with French arms through New Orleans. France's cession of Louisiana in 1763 put Spanish officials across that trade, and their restrictions cut off the gun supply; Osage war parties, armed through French and British channels, drove between the allies and pushed the Wichita south to the Red River. The Pawnee pulled north into Nebraska, the Chaui leading the move and the Pitahawirata following, and a Spanish report placed them there by 1777. A short war with the Skiri ended in the Wolf band's defeat around 1775, after which the four bands dealt with one another as a single people. The villages planted in spring, rode out on the summer buffalo hunt, and came back for the autumn harvest feast. In 1806 Facundo Melgares carried Spanish gifts and a Spanish flag to the Kitkehahki town on the Republican, just east of this country; Zebulon Pike arrived soon after and talked the Pawnee into hauling that flag down and raising the American one. War with the Kanza in 1809–1811 drew more lodges toward the Platte, and the first land cession to the United States followed in 1818.
zh:
皮塔哈维拉塔是三支南部波尼之一，法国人称之为塔帕日（Tappage），即「喧哗的波尼人」。他们的河畔地方在共和河与普拉特河之间，内布拉斯加平原在这里向堪萨斯方向倾斜。1444年，后来组成南部诸支的卡多语先民已在这片草原的土屋中生活：妇女照料玉米、豆类和南瓜，营地众人结队徒步，集体猎捕野牛；祭司和世袭酋长主持仪式，马匹和欧洲火器都还没有进入草原。他们的亲族与贸易通向查维人、基特克哈基人和更南方的威奇托人，而不是卢普河上的斯基迪人。

到1750年，南部波尼人与威奇托盟友已在阿肯色河站稳脚跟，经新奥尔良不断获得法国武器。1763年法国割让路易斯安那，接管贸易的西班牙官员加以限制，枪支供给随之中断；从法国和英国渠道取得武器的奥塞奇战团插入同盟各部之间，把威奇托人南逼到雷德河。波尼人向北撤回内布拉斯加，查维人领头迁移，皮塔哈维拉塔人随行，1777年的西班牙报告已把他们记在当地。他们与斯基迪人的一场短战约在1775年以狼族失败告终，此后四支便以同一个民族相待。各村春天播种，夏天倾巢出猎野牛，秋天再回来办丰收宴。1806年，法昆多·梅尔加雷斯带着西班牙礼物和旗帜来到共和河畔、本省以东的基特克哈基镇；泽布伦·派克随后也到，说服波尼人降下那面旗，升起美国旗。1809—1811年与堪萨人的战争把更多土屋引向普拉特河，1818年波尼人首次向美国割让土地。

en:
The Niobrara runs out of the Sand Hills and meets the Missouri through wooded bottomland at the southeastern edge of the South Dakota plains. In 1444 its terraces held earth-lodge villages of Caddoan-speaking farmers, kin to the Pawnee and Arikara. Women tended fields of corn, beans, squash and sunflowers, seasonal parties went out after the bison herds, and dugout canoes carried grain and hides along the Missouri. The settled river country ended where the short-grass bison plains began.

Late in the 17th century the Siouan-speaking Ponca, moving west with the Omaha, reached the river and fought the Arikara before peace was made; Arikara women taught the newcomers to raise earth lodges. Pierre-Charles Le Sueur's map of 1701 already marks the Ponca on the upper Missouri, and by the end of the century they were settled at the Niobrara's mouth. In 1789 the fur trader Juan Baptiste Munier held an exclusive license for their trade and built a post at the confluence, where he counted about eight hundred Ponca. Smallpox swept them soon after: when Lewis and Clark came upriver in 1804 barely two hundred remained. The survivors kept their maize fields and gardens even as the mounted life of the plains closed around them.
zh:
奈厄布拉勒河从沙丘地带流出，在南达科他平原东南缘穿过林木茂盛的低地汇入密苏里河。1444年，河畔阶地上是卡多语系农耕者的土屋村庄，他们是波尼人和阿里卡拉人的亲族。妇女照料玉米、豆类、南瓜和向日葵田，季节性队伍出猎野牛，独木舟载着粮食和兽皮往来于密苏里河上。定居的河畔世界到此为止，再往前便是短草覆盖的猎牛平原。

17世纪末，说苏语的潘卡人（篷卡人）随奥马哈人西迁到这条河边，先与阿里卡拉人交战，议和之后，阿里卡拉妇女教新来者建造土屋。勒叙厄尔1701年的地图已把潘卡人标在上密苏里河畔；到18世纪末，他们已定居奈厄布拉勒河口。1789年，皮货商胡安·巴蒂斯特·米尼埃取得对潘卡人贸易的专营许可，在两河交汇处建起贸易站，清点出约八百名潘卡人。天花随即袭来：1804年刘易斯与克拉克溯河到来时，幸存者仅剩约二百人。即使马背平原生活已将他们包围，幸存者仍守着玉米田和菜园。

en:
Selis is the Séliš name of the people outsiders later called Flathead. This province is their old Upper Missouri country, where the Jefferson, Madison and Gallatin join to form the Missouri and the Big Hole and Beaverhead valleys run beneath the Continental Divide. In 1444 Séliš bands wintered in sheltered camps near the later Helena and Butte country and in the Big Hole, crossed the divide on seasonal hunts, and before horses moved their camps with dogs and lived in tule-mat lodges; Shoshone neighbours held the mountains to the south and Blackfoot rivals the plains to the east.

Horses from the Shoshone opened long bison drives, but guns from the Saskatchewan traders gave the Blackfoot the upper hand. Between 1700 and 1750 foot-borne Blackfoot parties carrying firearms drove the Séliš off their eastern hunting grounds, and war and smallpox broke neighboring bands; Séliš families wintered more often in the Bitterroot Valley, though they still crossed the divide once or twice a year to run buffalo. On 4 September 1805, at Ross Hole, Lewis and Clark came on a Séliš camp of about 400 people; the band gave the expedition food and traded it pack horses. The party had already named the Jefferson, Madison and Gallatin at the Three Forks, and after resting at Travelers' Rest from 9 to 11 September it took the Lolo Trail over the mountains. From about 1810 North West Company, Hudson's Bay Company and American Fur Company trappers worked the beaver streams of the Big Hole.
zh:
塞利斯来自萨利什人的自称塞利什（Séliš），「平头」是外人后来给的称呼。这一省是他们在密苏里河上游的故地：杰斐逊河、麦迪逊河与加勒廷河在此汇成密苏里河，比格霍尔河谷与比弗黑德河谷沿大陆分水岭延伸。1444年，塞利什各部在后来的赫勒拿、比尤特一带和比格霍尔河谷的避风雪营地过冬，按季翻山打猎；马匹到来之前，迁营靠狗，住的是香蒲草席营帐。南面山地在休休尼邻人手中，东面平原由黑脚对手控制。

从休休尼人那里得到马匹后，长途赶野牛成为可能，但萨斯喀彻温商人的火枪让黑脚人占了上风。1700年至1750年间，徒步持枪的黑脚队伍把塞利什人赶出东部猎场，战争和天花又击散了相邻部落；塞利什家庭越来越多地到比特鲁特谷过冬，但每年仍翻一两次分水岭去猎野牛。1805年9月4日，刘易斯—克拉克探险队在罗斯洼地遇到约四百人的塞利什营地，部落给了他们食物，又换给他们驮马。此前探险队已在三河汇流处为杰斐逊河、麦迪逊河和加勒廷河命了名；9月9日至11日在旅人休憩地休整后，他们沿洛洛小道向西翻越。约1810年起，西北公司、哈德逊湾公司和美国毛皮公司的捕兽者开始进入比格霍尔河的河狸溪流。

en:
The Hunkpapha, 'Head of the Circle' in Lakota, were one of the seven Lakota bands; when the Sioux met in great council, tradition put their tipis at the opening of the camp circle. In 1444 none of them were here yet. The short-grass plains between the Missouri and the Grand and Cannonball rivers were pedestrian bison-hunting country, and the Saone Lakota who carried Hunkpapa descent still lived far to the east, kept on that side of the river by the great fortified villages of the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara. The Saone reached Lake Traverse only after 1720 and the Missouri's east bank in about 1750.

Horses came to them through Cheyenne traders around 1730; the Lakota called the animal sunka wakan, the mysterious dog, and a mounted hunter could run buffalo on the open plains. The smallpox that swept the Missouri villages in 1781 broke the river barrier, and the Lakota crossed into the short-grass country. Lewis and Clark's armed confrontation with Teton Lakota on the Missouri in 1804 was the first clash with Americans on this frontier, and a trader's count the next year put the Hunkpapa at roughly 1,600 people in 160 tipis. By 1821 their mounted camps were spreading through the grazing grounds between the Grand and the Cannonball.
zh:
洪克帕帕（Hunkpapha）在拉科塔语中意为「营圈之首」，是拉科塔七支之一；苏族举行大会时，按传统洪克帕帕人的梯皮就扎在营圈的入口处。1444年，他们还没有到这里。密苏里河与格兰德河、坎农博尔河之间的短草草原是徒步猎牛者的地方，承载洪克帕帕源流的索恩拉科塔人还远在东边，被曼丹人、希达察人和阿里卡拉人设防的大村庄挡在河对岸。索恩人1720年后才抵达特拉弗斯湖，约1750年才到达密苏里河东岸。

约1730年，马匹经夏安商人传入；拉科塔人称马为「神犬」，有了马，猎人就能在开阔草原上追猎野牛。1781年席卷密苏里河各村庄的天花打破了大河屏障，拉科塔人渡河进入短草之地。1804年，刘易斯与克拉克在密苏里河上与梯顿拉科塔人武装对峙，这是美国在这道边疆的第一次冲突；次年一个商人清点，洪克帕帕约有1600人、160座梯皮。到1821年，他们的骑马营地正散布到格兰德河与坎农博尔河之间的牧场。

en:
Sihabi covers the open grassland of southwestern Manitoba, where the Assiniboine River and its tributary the Souris cut wooded valleys through the northern bison plains. Its people were the Nakota, whom neighbouring nations called the Assiniboine. Before horses reached the northern plains, their camps followed the herds on foot, hunters drove bison into communal pounds, and the Nakota pounded dried meat, fat and berries into pemmican for winter food and trade. Trails ran north to Cree camps on the lake chain and south toward the earth-lodge towns on the Missouri. In 1444 those trails carried Nakota hunters, dogs and bundles of provisions, but no European had crossed the grass.

Bison provisions and the overland road to the Mandan towns drew European traders into the country. Henry Kelsey of the Hudson's Bay Company travelled with Assiniboine parties in the 1690s, the first European known to have described the Nakota and the plains herds. In 1738 La Vérendrye built Fort La Reine on the Assiniboine and set out from it with Assiniboine guides for the Mandan villages on the upper Missouri. Horses and muskets later made the Assiniboine mounted hunters and important middlemen in the Iron Confederacy with the Cree, while smallpox struck their camps in the early 1780s. Two rival posts opened near the Souris mouth in 1793: the North West Company's Fort Assiniboine and the Hudson's Bay Company's Brandon House, which sent horse trains and dog sleds south to the Missouri. Cuthbert Grant's men sacked Brandon House during the Pemmican War in May 1816; the rivalry ended when the two companies merged in 1821.
zh:
锡哈比是马尼托巴西南部的开阔草原，阿西尼博因河和支流苏里斯河在北部野牛草原上切出林木茂盛的河谷。住在这里的是纳科塔人，邻族称他们为阿西尼博因人。马匹传到北部草原以前，他们的营地徒步跟随兽群，猎人把野牛赶入集体围场，再把肉干、油脂和浆果舂成干肉饼，供过冬和交易。小路向北通往湖链上的克里人营地，向南则通向密苏里河畔的土屋村镇。1444年时，这些道路上往来的是纳科塔猎人、狗和一捆捆食物，欧洲人尚未穿过这片草原。

野牛食物和通往曼丹村镇的陆路把欧洲商人引到此地。1690年代，哈德逊湾公司的亨利·凯尔西随阿西尼博因队伍出行，是已知最早记述纳科塔人和草原野牛群的欧洲人。1738年，拉韦朗德里在阿西尼博因河畔修建拉雷讷堡，并由阿西尼博因向导带路，从堡前出发前往密苏里河上游的曼丹人村落。后来马匹和火枪使阿西尼博因人成为骑马猎手，也使他们在与克里人结成的铁器联盟中担当重要中间人；1780年代初，天花袭击了他们的营地。1793年，苏里斯河口附近开了两座对头商栈：西北公司的阿西尼博因堡和哈德逊湾公司的布兰登馆；后者派出马队和狗拉雪橇南下密苏里河。1816年5月，卡斯伯特·格兰特的人在干肉饼战争中洗劫布兰登馆。1821年两家公司合并，这场商栈相争才结束。

en:
Wadopabina is the Assiniboine, or Nakota, name of the Canoe Paddlers; their Cree neighbours called them the Paddling Assiniboine. Their country is the canoe road from the Saskatchewan lowlands to the upper Assiniboine: the Swan River comes out of the Porcupine Hills, runs between those hills and the Duck Mountains into Swan Lake, and the short Shoal River carries on to Lake Winnipegosis, while an easy portage at the Swan's bend reaches the upper Assiniboine. The upper river itself is shallow, twisting and barred with sandbanks, so this lake chain was the way in. In 1444 Nakota bands moving north-west paddled it to fish, hunt moose and beaver, and reach the summer buffalo hunts on the parkland edge; canoes carried their trade before horses or European goods arrived.

Henry Kelsey reached the upper Assiniboine from Hudson Bay in 1691, the first European known in this country, and French traders entered the lake chain soon afterwards. In 1741 Pierre Gaultier de La Verendrye, a son of the elder La Verendrye, built Fort Dauphin at the mouth of the Mossy River on Lake Winnipegosis and named it for the heir to the French throne; a second fort of the same name later went up on Dauphin Lake. The rivals crowded in fast: the North West Company built Swan River Fort in 1787, and the Hudson's Bay Company answered with Swan River House half a mile upstream; by the middle 1790s Marlboro House, Bird Mountain House, Somerset House, Carlton House and Fort Alexandria were strung along the upper river. Somerset House stood in a buffalo wintering ground and took so much trade that Swan River House was reduced to its outpost. The beaver were soon trapped out. The Hudson's Bay posts closed and Peter Fidler reopened them for a single season in 1807–1808; the North West Company held on until the merger of 1821, when every Swan River post was shut and the first generation of the trade came to an end.
zh:
瓦多帕比纳是阿西尼博因人（纳科塔人）对「划独木舟者」的称呼，邻近的克里人叫他们「划桨的阿西尼博因人」。他们的土地是萨斯喀彻温低地通往上阿西尼博因河的独木舟路：斯旺河发源于豪猪丘陵，在豪猪丘陵与鸭山之间流入斯旺湖，再经短短的肖尔河进入温尼伯戈西斯湖；在斯旺河转弯处有一段省力的陆运，接上阿西尼博因河上游。上游河道本身水浅、弯曲、多沙洲，这串湖泊便成了出入的门户。1444年，向西北迁徙的纳科塔队伍沿水路捕鱼，猎驼鹿和海狸，再到林缘草原参加夏季野牛围猎；那时马和欧洲货物都还没到，贸易全靠独木舟装载。

1691年，亨利·凯尔西从哈得孙湾抵达阿西尼博因河上游，是已知最早来到这一带的欧洲人，法国商人随后也进入湖群。1741年，老拉韦朗德里之子皮埃尔·戈蒂埃·德·拉韦朗德里在温尼伯戈西斯湖的莫西河口建起多凡堡，以法国王太子命名，后来又在多凡湖畔建起第二座同名商栈。对手们很快蜂拥而至：西北公司1787年建斯旺河堡，哈得孙湾公司在它上游半英里处回敬以斯旺河商栈；到18世纪90年代中期，马尔伯勒商栈、鸟山商栈、萨默塞特商栈、卡尔顿商栈和亚历山德里亚堡已沿上游河道一字排开。萨默塞特商栈地处野牛越冬地，生意太好，斯旺河商栈反倒降成它的分站。海狸很快被捕绝。哈得孙湾公司各处商栈关闭，彼得·菲德勒1807至1808年又主持重开了一个贸易季；西北公司一直撑到1821年两家公司合并，斯旺河诸栈全部关闭，这一带最早一代毛皮贸易就此收场。

en:
Kuttawa is the wooded lower Cumberland country, where the river crosses the narrow ridge-and-bottomland strip between the Cumberland and Tennessee shortly before it reaches the Ohio. The old Tolu mound center stood in this part of western Kentucky from about 1200 to 1450, with a burial mound, a platform mound and a plaza in the Angel-Kincaid Mississippian network. A fluorite statue from the Tolu area shows a beaded forelock and is one of the most detailed Mississippian stone figures known from the region. By 1444 those mound towns had faded, and Shawnee farmers, hunters and canoe parties used the river they called Wasioto. The name later recorded as Kuttawa preserved a Cherokee village name; sources translate it variously as 'beautiful', 'city in the woods' and 'great wilderness'.

French traders knew the waterway as the River of the Shawnee before Thomas Walker of Virginia gave it the English name Cumberland in 1758. Bison traces and ridge paths already ran through the Between the Rivers woods, and hunters, war parties and settlers used them to move among the Cumberland, Tennessee and Ohio. After colonial settlement reached the lower river, keelboats and flatboats carried frontier produce north into the Ohio and Mississippi.
zh:
库塔瓦是林木覆盖的坎伯兰河下游地区。河水在汇入俄亥俄河前不久，穿过坎伯兰河与田纳西河之间狭长的山脊和低地。约1200年至1450年，古老的托卢土墩中心位于西肯塔基这一带，墓葬墩、台墩和广场属于密西西比文化的安吉尔—金凯德网络。托卢一带的一尊萤石雕像刻有串珠额发，是这一带已知雕刻最精细的密西西比石像之一。1444年，这些土墩城镇已经衰落，肖尼农民、猎人和独木舟队伍仍使用他们称作瓦西奥托的河流。后来记为库塔瓦的名称保存了一个切罗基村名，资料对其含义有「美丽」「林中城」「大荒野」等解释。

弗吉尼亚人托马斯·沃克于1758年将这条河定名为坎伯兰；在此之前，法国商人称它为「肖尼人之河」。野牛踏出的小径和山路早已穿过「两河之间」的林地，猎人、战队和定居者沿这些道路往来于坎伯兰河、田纳西河与俄亥俄河之间。殖民地定居点推进到下游后，龙骨船和平底船把边疆农产品北运俄亥俄河与密西西比河。

en:
Pepikokia covers the Tippecanoe watershed, whose Miami-Illinois name refers to the buffalo fish taken in its quiet water. The river gathers itself from kettle lakes and marshes before crossing wooded country and wet prairie to the Wabash. In 1444 Miami families planted corn in the bottoms, set fishing weirs for buffalo fish and pike, and followed trails southwest to Ouiatenon and northeast to Kekionga. Their main village, Kithtippecanuck, stood at different times near the headwaters or closer to the mouth.

The French built the nearest European post at Ouiatenon in 1717, a palisaded fur station on the Wabash where Tippecanoe families traded. French records commonly grouped the Tepicon band with the Wea after 1742, but its villages kept their own chiefs. Smallpox killed the pro-French chief Le Gris in 1752. His younger namesake, Nagohquangogh, joined Henry Hamilton's Wabash expedition in 1778 and raided with the British; after the Western Confederacy lost Fallen Timbers, he signed the Treaty of Greenville in 1795.

The river mouth was also the site of Prophetstown, the village Tenskwatawa, the Shawnee Prophet, founded and Tecumseh used as a headquarters for resistance to American settlement. William Henry Harrison marched there with about 1,000 men and on 7 November 1811 drove off a dawn attack while Tecumseh was away recruiting allies. His troops burned the abandoned town and its winter food stores. The defeat broke much of Tecumseh's confederacy and gave Harrison the nickname 'Tippecanoe'.
zh:
佩皮科基亚是蒂珀卡讷河流域；河名来自迈阿密—伊利诺伊语，指静水中捕得的牛胭脂鱼。河水从冰蚀湖和沼泽间汇集，穿过林地与湿草原，汇入沃巴什河。1444年，迈阿密人在低地种玉米，设鱼梁捕捉牛胭脂鱼和狗鱼，沿小路向西南到乌亚塔农、向东北到凯基翁加。主村基斯蒂佩卡努克有时设在河源附近，有时更靠近河口。

1717年，法国人在乌亚塔农建起最近的欧洲人据点，这座沃巴什河畔的木栅毛皮站也是蒂珀卡讷诸村交易的地方。1742年后，法国记载常把特皮孔部归入韦阿人，但各村落仍保留自己的首领。1752年，亲法酋长勒格里死于天花。年轻的同名酋长纳戈匡戈1778年参加亨利·汉密尔顿的沃巴什远征，随英军袭扰；西部联盟在福伦廷伯斯战败后，他于1795年签署《格林维尔条约》。

河口一带有先知镇。它由肖尼先知滕斯夸塔瓦建立，特库姆塞把这里作为抵抗美国定居的总部。1811年11月7日，威廉·亨利·哈里森率约一千人进军至此，在特库姆塞外出联络盟友时击退拂晓进攻，随后焚毁空镇和冬季储粮。此战重创特库姆塞联盟，也让哈里森得到「蒂珀卡讷」的绰号。

en:
Pacaha ruled the Mississippi bends of northeastern Arkansas, a string of Nodena-phase villages running from the Missouri Bootheel south to Wapanocca Lake. The Bradley site near Turrell is the leading candidate for the paramount town. The Nodena site itself, fifteen acres behind a bastioned palisade cut with archer slots, held two large substructure mounds, ordered plazas and a chunkey field behind its main mound; de Soto's chroniclers called these the best-planned towns they had seen in all of La Florida. In 1444 maize fields and river fisheries fed a dense population, chert and whelk shells arrived through the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex, and a perpetual war with Casqui kept every large village walled.

The Spaniards came in 1541 and stayed about forty days. Casqui followers trailing the army fell on the town while its people fled toward a river island; some drowned, the houses were looted and the shrines desecrated. De Soto won the chief over with gifts and a promise to punish Casqui, then accepted the return of the plunder and made the two enemies eat at one table. That visit is the only written record of Pacaha. The Nodena villages ended around 1650, and by the 1670s Dhegiha Siouan-speaking Quapaw held this bank of the river; scholars have wondered whether their town Kappa kept the old name Capaha, but the link has never been proved.
zh:
帕卡哈统辖阿肯色东北部的密西西比河曲，诺德纳阶段村落沿河成串分布，北起密苏里靴跟地带，南至瓦帕诺卡湖。蒂雷尔附近的布拉德利遗址是其主邑的首要候选；诺德纳遗址本身是一座15英亩的重镇，木栅上设有棱堡和箭眼，镇内有两座大台墩、排列齐整的广场，主墩背后还有一处舂克伊球场。德索托麾下的编年史家说，这是他们在整个「拉佛罗里达」见过规划最严整的城镇。1444年，玉米田与河渔养活着稠密人口，燧石和海螺壳经仪礼性交换网络流通，而与卡斯基无休止的战争让每座大村镇都圈着木墙。

1541年西班牙人到来，停留约40天。尾随军队的卡斯基人趁帕卡哈人逃向河中岛屿时袭破城镇，有人溺亡，房屋遭劫，神庙被亵渎。德索托以礼物和惩罚卡斯基的许诺争取到帕卡哈酋长，随后接受归还的战利品，让两个仇敌同席而食。这次造访是关于帕卡哈仅有的文字记载。诺德纳诸村约在1650年消亡，到1670年代，这段河岸已由使用德吉哈语支苏语的夸帕人占据；有学者猜测夸帕人的卡帕村保留了卡帕哈（Capaha）旧名，但这一关联始终未获证实。

en:
Maui, the Valley Isle, joins the West Maui Mountains to the great volcano Haleakalā with a broad isthmus. In 1444 the wet windward east around Hāna and the dry western coast around Lahaina were two separate chiefly worlds; Lahaina, then called Lele, was a royal village set among breadfruit and coconut groves. Chiefs drew their wealth from taro gardens, reef fishing grounds, temple lands and fleets of large canoes, and they governed rank, fishing and war through the kapu. Two works remain from those centuries. At Kihei the Koʻieʻie fishpond, walled with lava and coral between 1400 and 1500, fattened mullet and milkfish behind its walls, and above Hāna stood Piʻilanihale, the largest heiau in the Hawaiian islands, whose terraces were first raised in the fourteenth century.

Late in the fifteenth century Piʻilani, chief of western Maui, conquered Hāna and joined the two halves of the island under one ruler for the first time; the coastal road he began was wide enough for eight men to walk abreast, and the great temple at Hāna was enlarged under his line and named Piʻilanihale, the house of Piʻilani. James Cook sighted Maui on 26 November 1778 but did not land, and war canoes met his ships off Lahaina. The first European ashore was the French navigator Lapérouse, on 29 May 1786, in the bay that bears his name. In 1790 Kamehameha of Hawaiʻi invaded while Maui's king Kahekili was away on Oʻahu. His army met Kahekili's son Kalanikūpule in ʻĪao Valley at Kepaniwai; after two even days John Young and Isaac Davis brought up two cannons, and the dead so choked the stream that the fight was named Kepaniwai, 'the damming of the waters'. The victory did not hold, for Kahekili retook the island, and Maui passed to Kamehameha only in 1795. He stationed his peleleu war-canoe fleet at Lahaina in 1802–03, and his son Kamehameha II resided there over the winter of 1819–20.
zh:
毛伊（Maui）又称「峡谷之岛」，西毛伊山脉与哈雷阿卡拉大火山由一条宽阔地峡相连。1444年，以哈纳为中心的湿润迎风东部和以拉海纳为中心的干燥西海岸分属两个酋长世界；拉海纳当时称莱莱，是面包果树与椰林间的王族聚落。酋长的财富来自芋田、礁海渔场、神庙属地和大型独木舟舰队，身份、渔捞与战争都由卡普禁忌规范。那一时期留下两处大工程：基黑的科伊埃伊埃鱼塘在1400至1500年间以熔岩和珊瑚筑墙，在墙后养肥鲻鱼和遮目鱼；哈纳上方矗立着皮伊拉尼哈雷，全夏威夷最大的神庙，台基最早垒于14世纪。

15世纪后期，西毛伊首领皮伊拉尼征服哈纳，首次把岛屿东西两半置于一人治下；他开工修筑的环岛道路宽得可让八人并行，哈纳的大庙也在他的家族治下扩建，并得名皮伊拉尼哈雷，意为「皮伊拉尼之屋」。1778年11月26日，库克望见毛伊却未能登陆，夏威夷战独木舟曾在拉海纳外迎上他的船队。1786年5月29日，法国航海家拉佩鲁兹在后来以他命名的海湾登岸，成为第一个踏上毛伊的欧洲人。1790年，夏威夷岛的卡美哈梅哈趁毛伊国王卡赫基利远在欧胡之际入侵，在伊奥河谷的可帕尼瓦伊迎战卡赫基利之子卡拉尼库普莱；双方相持两日后，约翰·扬和艾萨克·戴维斯推来两门大炮，战死者堵塞了河道，此役遂名「可帕尼瓦伊」，意为「壅水之战」。这场胜利没有保住，卡赫基利收复毛伊，直到1795年该岛才归入卡美哈梅哈。1802至1803年，他把佩莱莱乌战独木舟舰队驻扎在拉海纳；1819至1820年冬天，其子卡美哈梅哈二世也曾驻跸于此。

en:
Oʻahu is two extinct volcanoes, the Waiʻanae and Koʻolau Ranges, with a wide central plain between them and sheltered anchorages on the southern shore. Polynesian households worked valleys and reefs as one estate of agroforestry, irrigated taro patches, fishponds and fishing grounds, and women beat decorated kapa bark cloth. An aliʻi nui ruled the island from his court and heiau, and on the central plain stood Kūkaniloko, the piko, the navel of Oʻahu: the birthstones where the island's highest-ranking children were delivered among chiefly witnesses, its name meaning 'to anchor the cry from within'. Around 1480 the lawmaker Maʻilikūkahi founded the chiefly house that ruled Oʻahu for the next three centuries. In 1444 the island was a chiefdom apart, and no European ship had entered its waters.

James Cook sighted Oʻahu in January 1778, the first Hawaiian island seen by Europeans, but sailed on to Kauaʻi; Charles Clerke took the ships into Waimea Bay the year after, following Cook's death. Kahekili II of Maui conquered the island in 1783, made Waikīkī his own residence and set his son Kalanikūpule over it. In February 1795 Kamehameha of Hawaiʻi assembled some 12,000 men and 1,200 war canoes, his troops drilled in muskets and cannon by the English sailor John Young, stranded in the islands years before, and landed on Oʻahu that May. Kalanikūpule's lines broke in the Nuʻuanu valley, where the chief Kaʻiana, who had deserted Kamehameha on the voyage over, was killed. Cornered at the valley head against a thousand-foot pali, more than seven hundred Oʻahu warriors were driven over the cliff; Hawaiians called the fight Kalelekaʻanae, the leaping mullet. Kalanikūpule fled but was later taken, and Kauaʻi's submission in 1810 completed Kamehameha's kingdom. Foreign ships had used Honolulu Harbor from 1794, and the king kept court at Waikīkī from 1804. When Kamehameha died in 1819, his son Kamehameha II ate with the women at the ʻAi Noa and broke the old kapu; by 1821 traders, whalers and missionaries were coming ashore.
zh:
瓦胡（Oʻahu，中文也译欧胡）岛由怀厄奈和柯欧劳两列死火山山脉构成，中间是宽阔平原，南岸有可避风浪的锚地。波利尼西亚人家户把山谷和礁岸经营成农林、灌溉芋头地、鱼塘与渔场相连的生计，妇女捶打制作带纹饰的卡帕树皮布。全岛由一位阿利伊努伊在宫廷和神庙（heiau）统治；中央平原上的库卡尼洛科是瓦胡的「皮科」（piko，肚脐）：出身高贵的孩子要在这块诞生石上、众酋长环立之下降生，地名意为「系住发自内心的哭声」。约1480年，立法者马伊利库卡希开创的王族，在此后三百年间统治瓦胡。1444年，它仍是一个自成一体的酋邦，欧洲船只还没有进入过它的水域。

1778年1月，詹姆斯·库克最先望见瓦胡，这也是欧洲人见到的第一个夏威夷岛屿，但船队继续驶往考爱；库克死后，查尔斯·克拉克于次年率船进入怀梅阿湾。1783年，茂伊岛的卡赫基利二世征服瓦胡，以威基基为自己的驻地，立其子卡拉尼库普莱为岛主。1795年2月，夏威夷岛的卡美哈梅哈集结约一万二千人、一千二百艘战独木舟，部下由多年前流落群岛的英国水手约翰·扬训练火枪和火炮，5月在瓦胡登陆。卡拉尼库普莱的防线在努阿努谷被突破，出征途中叛离卡美哈梅哈的酋长卡伊阿纳（Kaʻiana）被击毙。守军在谷头被堵在近千英尺高的帕利悬崖前，七百多名战士被逼落崖下；夏威夷人称这场厮杀为卡莱莱卡阿奈（Kalelekaʻanae），意为「惊跳的鲻鱼」。卡拉尼库普莱逃走后仍被擒获，1810年考爱归服，卡美哈梅哈的王国就此告成。外国船只自1794年起使用檀香山港，国王自1804年起在威基基驻跸。1819年卡美哈梅哈去世后，其子卡美哈梅哈二世在「艾诺亚」宴上与女性共食，打破旧卡普戒律；到1821年，商人、捕鲸者和传教士已纷纷上岸。

en:
Kauaʻi is the oldest and north-westernmost of the main Hawaiian islands, lying 117 kilometres across the Kauaʻi Channel from Oʻahu. Trade-wind rain keeps its volcanic highlands wet: the Waimea River has cut a deep red-walled canyon into the western plateau, while on the rainy east coast the Wailua, the island's only navigable river, opens onto a flat shore. At its mouth stood Wailua, a chiefly seat whose heiau and royal birthing stones served the aliʻi of the island's largest ahupuaʻa; the anchorage nearby was Tapaʻa, the Kauaʻi dialect form of Kapaʻa. In 1444 Kauaʻi and Niʻihau form an independent high chiefship under their own aliʻi nui, ruling through the kapu order. Taro patches and sweet-potato plots, pigs and fowl, reef fishing and brackish fishponds feed the island; at the Hulēʻia River the 270-metre wall of the Alekoko fishpond was raised in the fifteenth century, a work tradition attributes to the Menehune, the little people of Hawaiian legend.

European ships reached Kauaʻi before any other Hawaiian island. On 20 January 1778 Cook's Resolution and Discovery anchored at Waimea to take water, trading iron nails for pigs and vegetables in the first recorded meeting between Europeans and Hawaiians; one Kauaian had been shot dead on the shore the day before when a landing party was jostled. Kauaʻi also became the one main island Kamehameha never took: a fleet sent from Oʻahu in 1796 broke up in rough seas while rebellion broke out at home, and the army assembled for a second attempt in 1803 was wasted by epidemic. Kaumualiʻi kept his court at Waimea until 1810, when he acknowledged Kamehameha as overlord and went on ruling the island. The 1815 wreck of the Russian-American Company ship Bering brought the German agent Georg Anton Schäffer, who turned a salvage claim into a treaty for a Russian protectorate; a star fort and the Russian flag went up at Waimea in 1817, until American traders and Kamehameha's pressure led Kaumualiʻi to expel him. On 16 September 1821 Kamehameha II invited Kaumualiʻi aboard his ship and sailed with him to Honolulu, and the last independent chief of Kauaʻi never returned to power.
zh:
考爱（Kauaʻi）是夏威夷主要岛屿中最古老、位置最西北的火山岛，与瓦胡岛隔着117公里宽的考爱海峡。信风给火山高地带来丰沛雨水：韦梅阿河在西部高原切出红崖壁立的深峡谷，湿润的东海岸则有全岛唯一可通航的怀卢阿河。河口的怀卢阿是酋长驻地，岛上最大阿胡普阿的神庙与王族诞生石都在这里，附近的塔帕阿（Tapaʻa，即标准夏威夷语中的Kapaʻa）是东岸锚地。1444年，考爱与尼豪同属一位阿利伊努伊治下的独立最高酋长国，按卡普秩序施治。芋田、甜薯园、猪禽、礁海捕捞和咸淡水鱼塘供养着全岛；胡莱阿河畔270米长的阿莱科科鱼塘石墙筑于15世纪，相传为夏威夷传说中的小个子民族梅内胡内人所建。

欧洲船只最先抵达的夏威夷岛屿就是考爱。1778年1月20日，库克的「决心号」与「发现号」在韦梅阿湾停泊取水，用铁钉换取猪只和菜蔬，这是欧洲人与夏威夷人有记录的首次接触；前一天岸上人群拥挤混乱，已有一名考爱人中枪身亡。考爱也是卡美哈梅哈唯一未能以武力征服的大岛：1796年从瓦胡派出的舰队遇风浪瓦解，后方又爆发叛乱；1803年为第二次远征集结的军队被疫病拖垮。考穆阿利伊在韦梅阿保有宫廷，直到1810年承认卡美哈梅哈为宗主，本人仍继续执政。1815年俄美公司商船「白令号」失事，德国籍代理人格奥尔格·安东·舍费尔借索赔之机搞出一份俄国保护国条约，1817年韦梅阿竖起星形要塞和俄国国旗，最终在美国商人和卡美哈梅哈的压力下被考穆阿利伊驱逐。1821年9月16日，卡美哈梅哈二世邀考穆阿利伊登船，随即载着他驶往檀香山，考爱最后一位独立酋长再没有回来执政。

en:
Lau is the chain of islands thrown out across the sea east of Fiji. The northern islands are volcanic and high; the southern line is reef and raised limestone. Lakeba, fertile and well watered, is the chiefly island of the south: at Tubou the Vuanirewa clan holds the title Tui Nayau, 'Lord of Nayau', and its canoe routes and marriages tied Lau to Tonga, whose speech, rounded house forms and dances entered the islands along the same sea roads. A fortress raised on Lakeba around the tenth century against Tongan raiders had room for 2,500 people, and a clan at Nasaqalau kept the ritual office of calling sharks from the sea. In 1444 no single chief ruled all Lau; northern Lau, southern Lau and the Moala group followed separate chiefs and tribute networks.

European ships came late to this edge of Fiji. James Cook sighted Vatoa on 2 July 1774, and his master went ashore with a boat's crew the next day, the only Fijian landing of his voyage. In June 1791 the Matavy, tender to HMS Pandora, called at Ono-i-Lau, where William Oliver and his men held the first recorded talk between Europeans and Fijians. When the Ono reefs were charted in 1820, Lau was the best-known corner of Fiji to European navigators, though the islands still had no European settlement and every island followed its own chief.
zh:
劳（Lau）是斐济向东撒入大海的一串岛屿。北部岛屿多火山高地，南部一线则是礁盘和隆起的石灰岩。拉肯巴岛土地肥沃、水源充足，是南劳的酋长岛：图布的瓦尼雷瓦氏族持有「奈尧之主」图伊纳尧头衔，岛上的独木舟航线和联姻把劳与汤加连在一起，汤加语、圆端房屋形制和舞蹈也随这些海路传入。拉肯巴有一座约10世纪为抵御汤加入侵者修筑的要塞，可容纳2500人；纳萨卡劳村还有一个氏族世袭从海中唤鲨的仪式职分。1444年的劳没有统一的酋长，北劳、南劳和莫阿拉群岛各随其主，各有贡赋网络。

欧洲船只很晚才抵达斐济这一东缘。1774年7月2日，詹姆斯·库克的船队望见瓦托阿，次日船长率一艘小艇的船员登岸，这是他那次航行中唯一一次踏上斐济土地。1791年6月，英国军舰「潘多拉号」的补给船「马塔维号」停靠奥诺劳，威廉·奥利弗一行在那里留下了欧洲人与斐济人交谈的最早记录。1820年奥诺礁群绘入海图时，劳已是欧洲航海者最熟悉的斐济一角，但岛上仍没有欧洲人定居点，各岛依旧听命于本地酋长。

en:
Vanua Levu ('Big Land') is Fiji's second-largest island, 64 kilometres north of Viti Levu. Rugged ridges run most of its length and divide one coast from another; in the north-east three rivers build the Labasa delta, a spread of gardens and fishing grounds behind the reef, and Bua Bay opens on the south coast. Between 1250 and 1350 the Pacific level fell by about 30 centimetres, reef catches shrank and fighting grew, and the villagers moved into fortified hilltops above the landings and river mouths. In 1444 the island was shared among rival chiefs, elders and warriors, none strong enough to rule the whole of it.

Abel Tasman sighted the island in 1643, William Bligh passed its waters in 1789 after the Bounty mutiny, and James Wilson surveyed them in the Duff in 1797. What brought Europeans to stay was sandalwood. In January 1800 the American schooner Argo was wrecked south-east of Fiji; a survivor, Oliver Slater, lived two years on Vanua Levu and carried word of the sandalwood thickets behind Bua Bay to the China trade. Ships were cutting there from about 1805 and had stripped the woods by 1815. The cutting ended in bloodshed: in 1813 a fight at a Bua camp killed most of the European party, and third mate Peter Dillon with a handful held out on a rock later called Dillon's Rock while Fijians prepared a cannibal feast of the dead. After that only whalers and bêche-de-mer ships called, and the chiefs kept their power.
zh:
瓦努阿（Vanua Levu，意为「大地」）是斐济第二大岛，位于维提岛以北64公里。崎岖山脊纵贯全岛，把各侧海岸隔开；东北部三河汇成兰巴萨三角洲，礁后是成片园圃和渔场，南海岸则敞开着布阿湾。1250至1350年间太平洋海面下降约30厘米，礁盘出产减少、冲突增多，村民陆续迁上俯临登陆点和河口的设防山顶。1444年，全岛由彼此敌对的酋长、长老和武士分据，无人能统辖全岛。

1643年阿贝尔·塔斯曼望见瓦努阿岛，1789年「邦蒂号」哗变后的威廉·布莱经过岛边水域，1797年詹姆斯·威尔逊又乘「达夫号」前来勘测。真正把欧洲人留住的是檀香木。1800年1月，美国双桅纵帆船「阿尔戈号」在斐济东南失事，幸存水手奥利弗·斯莱特在瓦努阿岛住了两年，把布阿湾后大片檀香林的消息带到了对华贸易线上。约1805年起商船入湾伐木，到1815年林已被砍光。伐木终于酿成血战：1813年，布阿一处伐木营发生冲突，欧洲人大多被杀，三副彼得·狄龙带着几个人死守在一块岩石上，此岩后来得名狄龙岩，斐济人则在为死者准备食人宴。此后只有捕鲸船和海参船偶尔到访，岛上权力仍在酋长手中。

en:
Te Urewera is the wall of steep, misty forest between the Bay of Plenty and Hawke Bay, a country of narrow ridges, the long lake of Waikaremoana and the sacred peak of Maungapōhatu. In its deep valleys live Tūhoe, the 'children of the mist', who trace their descent both from Toi-te-huatahi and Pōtiki, remembered among the first peoples of the island, and from Toroa's crew of the Mātaatua canoe; a tribal saying holds that the land is from Toi and Pōtiki and the mana is from Tūhoe. Neighbouring iwi knew the forest as a graveyard for invading war parties. Along the northern edge, on the Rangitaiki mouths and the coast at Whakatāne and Matatā, dwelt their Mātaatua kin Ngāti Awa, descendants of Awanuiarangi. In 1444 the coast and the plains belonged to Ngāti Awa, while Tūhoe held the forest behind them and lived on its birds and timber.

The two peoples often fought each other, yet the hills were their common shield. In 1818 Te Morenga and Korokoro of Ngāpuhi swept south with muskets to raid Ngāti Pūkeko; Ngāti Awa and their allies fell back into the Urewera ranges and held Okahukura pā until reinforcements came up, then drove the northerners off with heavy loss, a rare reverse for the raiders of the early Musket Wars. The victory bought only a short breathing space. By 1821 the Ngāpuhi chiefs Pōmare and Te Wera Hauraki were arming a war party to avenge it, and no European had yet ventured into the mist.
zh:
乌雷韦拉是横亘在丰盛湾与霍克湾之间的一道崇山峻岭，重雾密林、山脊逼窄，山中躺着长长的怀卡雷莫阿纳湖，腹地耸立着圣山毛阿波哈图。深谷中住着图霍埃人，即「雾之子」：他们既奉岛上最早先民托伊特胡阿塔希与波蒂基为祖，也承继托罗阿所率马塔阿图阿号独木舟乘员的血脉，族中谚语说，土地得自托伊与波蒂基，威望得自图霍埃。邻部都把这片密林看作来犯战阵的坟场。北缘的朗伊塔伊基河口及华卡塔尼、马塔塔海岸，住着与他们同出马塔阿图阿的雅提阿瓦人，奉阿瓦努伊阿朗吉为始祖。1444年，海岸与平原属于雅提阿瓦人，身后的密林归图霍埃人，靠林中的飞禽和木材为生。

两族虽屡有争战，群山却是共同的屏障。1818年，恩加普希人的特莫伦加与科罗科罗携火枪南下，袭击恩加蒂普凯科人；雅提阿瓦与盟友退入乌雷韦拉山区，坚守奥卡胡库拉山寨直至援兵到来，随即重创北来的劫掠者，这是火枪战争初期劫掠者少有的一场挫败。这场胜利只换来短暂喘息。到1821年，恩加普希酋长波马雷与特韦拉·豪拉基已在武装战阵图谋复仇，而还没有欧洲人走进这片雾中。
